name: Hotel Beacon
title: “Pretty average when things get tough”
text:
We experienced the Beacon for three weeks, before and after Hurricane Sandy. The hotel was fully booked when we arrived and the attitude showed. Management did a great job of keeping guests informed immediately after the storm. 
My major criticism is the front desk attitude towards guests when they know they have so many wanting a room. Prices were jacked up by $50 a night after the storm (supposedly because of the Marathon). The TV system throughout the hotel was brushed off and our problems were only addressed when we pointed out that we were not 1 or two night guests but in fact there for weeks. I understand this will be completely fixed mid November.
I agree with all the positive comments most reviewers have made, this is why we had chosen the Beacon as a return visit. Location could not be better. A real positive also is free WiFi throughout the hotel. Would we stay again? Yes.

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “Great Hotel - Fantastic location”
text: Stayed at the Beacon on our honeymoon/around the world trip. From the time we arrived we were made to feel welcome. The staff were accommodating and friendly. Were assigned a room on the 10th floor overlooking Broadway. Had a great view and no street noise. The room was ideal for us as we wanted something nice without being over the top. Hotel rooms in NYC can be quite expensive but the Beacon was reasonably priced - cheaper than many similar standard hotels. The room was clean and well appointed. The bed was comfortable. Having a kitchenette was also useful for making small meals/snacks. We found the location to be absolutely perfect. Coming from Australia, we found that the hotel was within easy reach of the subway which in turn made visiting the main sites of NYC a breeze. Although there was no restaurant in the hotel, the diner next door was fine. The Fairways across the road was a revelation. We were over there every day!! There are hundreds of other food options available - all within an easy subway ride. I would definitley stay here again and would recommend The Beacon to others. Great hotel + Great location + great service = great experience!

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “So Perfect”
text:
I've been to NYC many times, but had never stayed in the Upper Westside area before. I found out about Hotel Beacon while going over other TripAdvisor reviews, which rate it very high also.
At first, when I booked I had some doubts about location, I thought that this could be too far from Midtown. But after my recent stay, I am quite sure that this has got to be one of the best places to stay in NYC. 
First of all, it is very conveniently located: The neighbourhood is very pleasant and well kept, with mostly local newyorkers passing by. There are also many great bars, restaurants, cafés and stores. Central Park is just a few blocks away and a good supermarket can be found just across the street. A subway station is only 2 blocks away, where you can ride the express train all the way to downtown after only a few stops. 
The hotel itself is very well mantained and comfortable, with spacious, clean and tidy rooms that among other things include a desk, a small sofa, a flat screen tv and a nice little kitchen (stove, microwave, coffe machine refilled daily, fridge and sink). All the hotel staff was also quite nice and very helpful.
On top of it all, the rates are very reasonable considering NYC standards. Overall, I have to strongly recommend this place.

name: Andaz 5th Avenue
title: “Excellent Stay, even though there was a hurricane!”
text:
We were originally supposed to stay at Andaz 5th Ave for 4nts from 27 Oct, but due to hurricane Sandy, ended up having to extend our stay until 04 Nov. 
Upon our arrival we were greeted by Ramone who offered us wine/refreshments while he checked us in. The lobby area was quite large with a seating area/library off to one side and restaurant to the other. A few minutes later we were taken to our allocated room and shown all the amenities the room had to offer. Our room was on the 7th floor, (an XL King with view) and we had a lovely view of the library and 42nd Street. The bed was really comfortable, our son had a rollaway bed which was also comfortable. The bedroom was a good size and had a large 42inch flatscreen TV, sofa, mini fridge with complimentary snacks and non alcoholic drinks, safety deposit box, a small glass wardrobe, bedside drawers, iron & ironing board and desk with a telephone. There was a touchpad control for the lights and window blind, which was straight forward to use. It would have been handy if there was a mirror over the desk as the only other mirror in the room was next to the glass wardrobe in the entrance. It was mentioned in previous reviews about noise from the road outside, the only thing we could just about hear was the sound of police/fire engine sirens.
The bathroom was lovely, it had twin sinks, the shower area had a rain shower, normal shower and footbath. We managed to work out the controls for each one after a couple of goes. There was also a hairdryer and toiletries. The only thing I would suggest to change in the bathroom is the lighting, it was rather dim. Other than that the bathroom was very modern, clean and towels changed every day.
Because of hurricane Sandy the hotel issued us with a torch and glow sticks and offered us complimentary pay per view films/TV. We were expecting the power to fail, but fortunately the hotel was not affected (1 block away was in complete darkness)We were kept informed at all times by staff. When we were told our return flight was cancelled I contacted reception who extended our stay straight away and offered assistance contacting my airline. We met with other guests in the seating/library area of an evening, swapping stories over our glasses of complimentary wine (Ramone was the best 'host'). It is a nice touch that the hotel offers this between 6pm and 9pm each evening.
We used the restaurant for breakfast as everywhere else was closed due to Sandy. The eggs, bacon and hash brown was very nice and staff very attentive.
The Andaz 5th Ave is right in the middle of all the tourist areas, 5 mins in each direction to Grand Central Station, Time Square, Empire State Building and shopping on 5th Ave.
This was our 2nd trip to New York, 1st time at Andaz. When we do return there is only one hotel we shall chose and that is Andaz 5th Avenue. The staff are exceptionally friendly and helpful, the hotel is modern with a warm atmosphere and in an excellent location.

name: The Setai Fifth Avenue, a Capella managed Hotel
title: “The Setai Fifth Avenue is a fabulous addition to NYC luxury hotels!”
text: My friends and I had a "spa weekend" at The Setai Fifth Avenue and it was simply amazing! The rooms were awesome (spacious, modern with fabulous bathrooms & great products!), the spa treatments were terrific & the spa itself was huge for NYC with plenty of space to lounge around, pools, saunas & steam rooms ...and very friendly & accommodating staff. We had dinner right in the hotel at Ai Fiori, which was beyond delicious and an exquisite dining experience! All in all, it was an amazing experience and the 4 of us highly recommend this luxurious hotel!

name: The Setai Fifth Avenue, a Capella managed Hotel
title: “Fabulous!”
text:
Just got back from a one night girls trip at the Setai. Got a promotional deal on a studio suite with two of the most comfortable queen beds. The flexible check in was perfect. Checked in at 3pm and out at 6pm the following day. It enabled us to take our time, shop and get a massage, in the Ariuga hotel spa on the day of departure. Why dont other hotels do this????
We were also able to secure the house car "an awesome Mazerati" to take us to Time square for our Broadway show. Honestly, for two amatuer city travelers it made us feel pretty special. Valet and the Setai door men were warm and polite. Front desk and consierge was top notch. The hotel itself is gorgeous and chic. The Huge Macys and Lord and tailor are within blocks. I am usually one who wants to try a different hotel at each visit... but not in NYC I cannot say enough about this hotel. We absolutely loved it. For a girls shopping and pampering trip this is perfect. My girlfriend and I plan on making the setai a definate tradition. When we go back we will absolutely stay at the Setai!!

name: The Setai Fifth Avenue, a Capella managed Hotel
title: “The Crown Jewel Of Manhattan!”
text: Let me just throw it out here. I am a "spoiled" traveler! Our approach toward travel is that our lives are so incredibly busy that the few too many precious times we are able to get away and relax, we are going all out, period... Thus, I have stayed in some of the most acclaimed hotels across the world. All too often to be disappointed. On our most recent trip to NYC (November 2011), we decided we were going to look for a new hotel in the city that had great reviews without a "great" price tag. I chose the Setai and what a great choice I made! The Setai was absolute perfection! The staff is incredible. BRAVO to Yvonne, Norma, the wonderful door men, housekeepers, concierge, etc. Within a few hours upon arrival, it appears everyone knows your name! AND it's not in a stuffy & cold manner. This staff has accomplished making you feel warm and welcomed each and every time you encounter them. They are the most gracious, accommodating, EAGER TO PLEASE staff that I have ever experienced. The rooms... So NOT typical of New York hotel rooms! They are spacious and the bathrooms are amongst the best i've been in. VERY large with double sinks, large soaking tub, separate dual head shower, enclosed and private toilet area. Plenty of counter space for your belongings, plenty of under the counter storage space, etc. I am a bathroom junkie! The bathroom is certainly high up on my criteria list in a hotel room and I promise you the Setai delivers. I should add that we had the entire family with us, in total 4 rooms. We were in the Apartment Avenue Suite and the other categories ranged from Studio Suite to Premier King. Each and every room/bathroom was spacious and well appointed. I would love to see the hotel add some more drawer space to the rooms. Two big dressers on each side of the bed opposed to night stands was the ONLY change I would prefer. Bottom line, this is truly a 5 star hotel. I frequent NYC often. I have stayed in The Ritz, The Mandarin Oriental, The Four Seasons and St. Regis. The Setai is a boutique hotel but for me it rivals if not surpasses them all! It's my new hotel of choice when visiting NYC and I cannot wait to get back!

name: The Setai Fifth Avenue, a Capella managed Hotel
title: “The best hotel I have ever stayed in!!”
text: I stay in 120 hotels a year. Over 30% of the hotels I stay in for business are high end hotels, Ritz and Four Seasons. This is the nicest hotel I have stayed in. Rooms are incredible and HUGE for NYC. Espresso maker and complimentary wifi, water, and sodas- NICE TOUCH. People are friendly and it is in a great location. HIGHLY RECOMMENED!!

name: The Chatwal
title: “Nice Hotel - Good Location”
text:
My husband and I stayed there recently for 5 nights. We liked the hotel very much and everyone was very nice towards us. The chief concierge (Nick) was extremely helpful. He not only made reservations for dinner every single night but got us tickets to a show with 24 hours notice. 
 I realized that we were lucky to be given a junior suite on the 4th floor and thus we were not bothered with the noise from the bar. The bar was always packed with people until very late and the music was always very loud. 
The only thing that went wrong was the sophisticated telephone/room control system that was not working properly. We informed the people at the main desk a couple of times about it and they promised to get it fixed but never did. For the price (and it was really pricey) they should have fixed it immediately. We could not use the phone and thus we had to come to the main desk to ask for wake up calls, and room service.
Otherwise we had a positive experience. We liked the decor and enjoyed the location.

name: The Chatwal
title: “Amazing!!”
text: Been to hundreds of hotels and this one is definitely top shelf. Can't say enough. Service, attitude, location, ambiance, food and drink. No detail is overlooked.

name: The Sherry-Netherland Hotel
title: “Good Location”
text: Good location close to Central park and in easy walking distance of most attractions. We were upgraded to a beautiful suite overlooking Central park,which helped to make our stay special.Warm welcome,friendly staff and good service. The only downside was the small lobby with no "common area" where you could easily get a drink or cup of coffee. The restaurant (Harry Cipriani's) which was attached to the hotel was a bit fromal and stuffy if you just wanted a cool drink,as we did in the recent heat wave- no shorts allowed,not even late afternoon before dining starts.Other than that, lovely stay.

name: San Carlos Hotel
title: “Great family room set up!”
text: We stayed in one of the suite rooms with 2 Queen beds and a Queen sofa bed in a separate room (4 people - 2 adults and 2 teens). We were surprised by the size of the bedroom and the additional room with the sofa bed. Everything was really nice - the bathrooms, the beds, and the kitchenette. There were nice bathroom fixtures and also a good size countertop space in the bathroom for us to share. We asked for a quiet room and got one - you would have never known you were in New York from the lack of street sounds - our room was completely quiet. We were impressed with the staff - when we asked for extra blankets and towels, they were immediately brought to our room. The staff was also helpful with restaurant suggestions. All in all, we could not have asked for more. This is a great hotel in a great spot in the city - blocks from Rockefeller Center and many other attractions and activities. We loved it and will definitely go back!

name: San Carlos Hotel
title: “Great hotel, and we're picky!”
text: My wife and two younger children stayed here for three nights. The room was spacious, clean, and the most well-lit I've ever been to. There were power outlets EVERYWHERE! There was a refrigerator as well. The pull-out sleep sofa mattress was comfortable, and the service was outstanding. Free wireless is another plus. When we return to NYC, we will definitely stay here again.

name: San Carlos Hotel
title: “Excellent stay”
text:
We stayed for Thanksgiving this year with our two children. Facilities were excellent. Location was great - short walk to many attractions and great shopping nearby. Room was plenty large with a nice kitchen area and two bathrooms. Staff was excellent. On the first day, the cleaning staff was not very efficient, but this was remedied on the following days of our stay, when their services improved.
We will stay again and recommend this hotel to our friends staying in NYC. Thank you, especially to Matthew, who was a great ambassador of the hotel.

name: San Carlos Hotel
title: “Very good location”
text:
This was my fifth trip to NYC and I have stayed in some large hotels and one that was small but more famous. Truthfully, this hotel topped them all and was a very good experience. The entire staff seemed to want to make our visit a success and they surely did. We had reserved four rooms for a small wedding party and they were quiet and clean , though not exceptionally large they were adequate. I loved the locatiion and found it extremely easy to get around to all the major attractions. I liked the speed of the elevators as the last boutique hotel where I stayed had very slow ones. We were on the 15th floor on the front of the building and we still could hear noise down below but that is NYC. I have always been able to hear sirens and horns no matter where I have stayed. 
The free breakfast was a real bonus with lots of choices for a continental style.
I would highly recommend this hotel and their staff.

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “overall a decent room/bathroom/location”
text:
Bathroom was perfect, shower was great (good pressure, temperature control and a ledge for toiletries), mirror didn’t steam up and had a low light for night time usage. 
Bedroom was fine, bit of an odd layout which included a mirror behind the bathroom door which couldn’t really be used, a badly lit mirror in the hall and no other mirror or sufficient lighting in the bedroom. 
Housekeeping didn’t bother to service our room on the first day as we got up late, although on the second day they did at least leave a card informing us we needed to ask for the room to be made up at a later time. Also, they took the towels for washing even though we hung them up and let us run out of shower gel and toilet tissue by not replacing them regularly enough. 
Location was good in the sense that most of the areas were walkable and close to Penn station and subway, but bear in mind the area it’s in is nothing special and nowhere particularly close for brunch or drinks. 
We were looking forward to the excellent service they publicise, especially as it was our wedding anniversary and first time in New York, but the girl who checked us in was uninterested in our excitement and we got no thoughtful freebies. The doorman Doug gave us a welcome greeting every night as if he’d never seen us before which was funny at first and then annoying. 
Let down by the service, but would still stay there again though as overall a decent room/bathroom/location.

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Kimpton never seems to fail me. Eventi NYC is delightful.”
text:
Just got back from a weekend trip at the Eventi with my partner and another couple and found the hotel to be charming, chic, elegant, and accommodating. All of the things I've grown used to from Kimpton. We stayed in a suite (pricey) and it was everything I was hoping for. The bedroom was well appointed, perfectly lit, amazing bed. The bathroom was the highlight...this is not your normal NYC bathroom or room for that matter. It was spacious and the shower was simply perfect. We were in a high enough floor that I didn't hear any noise. This is a real treat as anyone whose ever stayed in NY know that the traffic noise can be annoying while you try to sleep.
I also loved my yoga bag, being able to use their gym and the great products in the bathroom. I wish I had taken photos as the room was just as attractive as the photos on their site. My only issue was that the hotel is not really in Chelsea (or if it is it's on the border) but closer to Herald Square. I was looking to walk to great restaurants and bars but really they weren't in that area. Chelsea's best spots are south of 24th and this was at 30th St. Still you are close to the subway which was great and walking in NYC is part of the fun. Kimpton...please keep up the great work. I don't want you guys to loose your mojo.

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A little pricey, but ...”
text: If the price were a little lower, I'd probably rate this property "excellent" but it's often somewhat steep - which is why I've only stayed here once. That said, it's a super cool joint - very modern and nice rooms (though smaller than expected) with comfy beds. Slept better here (noise level) than other hotels in the vicinity. Staff is friendly and very helpful. Location is excellent, especially if you are going to MSG (and/or traveling into Penn Station). Good subway access. If you need wireless, be sure to join Kimpton's guest program and you'll be comped. Would definitely return if the rate is reasonable.

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Wonderful!”
text: Just returned from a 5 night stay. This surpassed all my previous hotel experiences. The entire staff makes you feel special. The hotel and room was extremely clean. Loved the walk-in shower instead of a tub.

name: The Iroquois
title: “Great Location!”
text: My husband and I stayed here for NYE 2012. It was kind of a last minute trip and I was looking for a four star hotel close enough to Times Square and still available two weeks before NYE. I read some great reviews on Trip Advisor of the Iroquois and we decided to stay here. The room was clean, but extremely small, even by NYC standards, but I think we had the smallest room on our floor when looking at the evacuation routes and floor plan posted to our door. I had requested a king sized bed and a room facing the street, and while I was advised those requests would be considered, neither was fulfilled. The room was clean, but the queen bed was small - both mine and my husbands' feet dangled off the edge. Since we only stayed the weekend, it wasn't that big of a deal, but if our trip was longer it would have become a problem. They served complimentary hot apple cider every afternoon in the lobby, which was delicious. It is a small, boutique hotel, but reasonably priced in an amazing location - we did not have to cab or take the subway our whole weekend and we went to Central Park, Times Square, Broadway, 5th Avenue, Rockefellar Center and the Meat Packing District. I would consider it again for a weekend stay.

name: The Iroquois
title: “Great hotel in a good location”
text: Nice boutique hotel in Midtown. Smallish rooms but that is what you expect in Manhattan. The rooms are very comfortable and the bedding was lovely and crisp. All in all a great place to stay in NY. The only down sides worth commenting on are the room service menu is rather limited but there is a diner next door that delivers. And the German receptionist is not the friendliest person that I have ever come across but the rest of the staff make up for her shortcomings.

name: Holiday Inn Hotel-Houston Westchase
title: “Exceling (new) hotel, recommend”
text:
As a European I reserve "excellent" grade for events that go beyond expectations or limits. Therefore I rate only "very good". A American would call experience as an excellent.
Hotel is located 33 miles from Houston International (IAH) airport, so I guess you have business at this Westchase area, if you are considering this hotel. Neighborhood is industrial/office like the closest blocks (3 directions) or highway (1). This of course made morning running not so fun, as I prefer outside, real life neighborhood learning to inside running machine.
Rooms, like hotel, are new, even though there is not anymore this "new car smell", but nothing is worn out. Cleaning is good, though slow. One day I visited room at 3pm to change for dinner and it had not been cleaned (was later w/o rqst). Check-in is from 3pm onwards. Beds were good with options for pillows (soft/hard). In bathroom there were amenities like shampoo & conditioner. I'm not sure if one bottle should have been moisturizer, now I had one shampoo and two conditioner bottles. Toilet paper location is design flaw as it is extremely far from the seat.
Hotel premises included Sporting News Grill, which also was breakfast room. Breakfast was not a gourmet experience, but very good value for money. There are option between buffet and menu. Buffet has some bacon, eggs, potato wedges, sausages and oatmeal as warm component. Fresh fruits (salad) was nice touch. Packed Danish was a disappointing, orange juice was excellent. Breakfast buffet takes you long. Atmosphere and service were both very good. At evening bar/grill was quite empty, probably same lot Cheddar's takes some clientale.
WiFi was strong at entire hotel area, which is an unexceptional experience, giving a strong + for the hotel. Hotel also has a pool and a gym, which neither I tested. Parking is free.
Service from employees were excellent, real dedicated team there.
As a summary, I can really recommend this hotel for Houston area. Car is essential, GPS is highly recommendable.

name: Crowne Plaza Houston - Brookhollow
title: “Comfortable place to stay”
text: I thought this was anice place to stay. Overall it was comfortable, and the front desk staff was the most friendly I've ever met. They continually joked with us and recognized us as we came in the front door each day. The only thing I didn't like about this hotel is the bathroom wasn't very clean. You can tell it had been mopped, but they must not have vacuumed before the mopped, because it smeared hair around on the tile. There was even hair stuck to the back of the door. Gross.

name: The Westin Houston Memorial City
title: “Very nice, new Westin”
text:
I love staying at Westin's and this was a good stay. This is not an excellent place for Platinum recognition, but the stay was very good.
The hotel is new and everything works. As with all Westin's that I have been in, the bed was excellent and the shower was superb. The bathroom lighting was very nice. I got a room that was on the diagonal end, so my bath was very long -- that was a nice touch.
I had to pay for parking, so was not happy about that.
Will surely stay again here.

name: Hilton University of Houston
title: “Unbelievable Value”
text: I found this hotel while searching for a place to stay near the University of Houston for a football game. What I found was an absolutely beautifully appointed hotel and rooms. The motif is Asian and it is carried through to the room appointments. It was very reasonalbly priced and has free internet in the rooms. It is a great bargain for location to the University of Houston.

name: Hotel Sorella CITYCENTRE
title: “New, Crisp with attention to detail”
text:
I found a great deal at this hotel and it is brand new and the staff really wants to be helpful, which is nice to see. I have family that lives nearby and it is great that there is finally a nice hotel in the area to stay at when I come to visit. The room was spacious and well appointed. Housekeeping did an outstanding job, even putting my shoes in a row neatly in the closet.
The only negative I have, and this did not bother me, but there are a few bars directly below the hotel so you can hear the music and some of the crowds at night. It did not bother me, but if you are a light sleeper, just ask for a room on a higher floor or away from the bars.
The positives very much outweigh any negatives. Free WiFi in the room, free self parking in the garage, walking distance to shopping and restaurants, overall a great hotel.

name: Hotel Sorella CITYCENTRE
title: “The unique atmosephere finaly in Houston”
text: The Hotel is very crisp, elegant and modern with a hint of European class. The lounge/Bar is absoutly devine. I was very impressed with the professionalism of the staff, and the precise cleanliness of my room. Top star and great price. I will stay again and again.

name: Hotel Icon, Autograph Collection
title: “Think Twice Before You Book for a Special Occassion”
text: We booked a suite on the Pent House floor on our wedding night. Although the room was clean and the view was nice overlooking the city, this hotel left a lot to be desired. Apparently on the pent house floor there are also hospitality suites directly across the hall from the guest suites. By design this is a very poor choice by the hotel as hospitality suites are typically for parties. Yes, we were staying across the hall from a loud drunken open house party! The music was loud, the people were in and out of the suite causing a big disturbance in our suite. A note was slipped under our door by the Party Hostess suggesting that she knew it was loud and that we should join them. This is not at all what we had in mind for our wedding night. At 12:30am when we couldn't take anymore we checked out and found another hotel. The attendant at the front desk was considerate and understanding as we conveyed the issues and didn't charge us for the room. I can only think that the rental price for the Hospitality Suite was much more than our guest suite as no additional solutions to the problem were offered. The whole experience was frustrating. Absent that,the hotel appeared to be clean and nice.

name: Hotel Icon, Autograph Collection
title: “One of the best hotels you'll ever stay in”
text:
Seriously, every time we have to travel through Houston we make a point of staying the night just to stay at the Icon. Sad isn't it but I'm a bit addicted to this hotel. From the red and gold valet parking station, the stunning lobby, beautiful bar and colonial style lifts your greeted with an excellently inviting opening design statement. 
We stay in the delux rooms (the are great deals to be had on this hotel on a weekend as its in the business district) which features a huge king sized bed and my favourite feature, the connected bathroom with louvre doors over the tub into the bedroom.
Every single feature has been thought out to perfection and the general style: European boutique meets cowboy burlesque is just the right side of delux and cosy. I've always found the staff to be more than helpful. never used the gym but I'm told it's lovely. Beer prices in the bar are a bit insane.
WARNING/TIP: don't think that because the Icon is smack dab in the middle of Houston's boring business district that thes nothing going on around here. An observant walk round the surrounding streets will reveal a buzzing little scene of cool cafes, cutting edge bars, a fabulous Mexican fast food joint just up the road, galleries, etc etc. If youre really stuck and want a quick bite to eat, there's also the tired looking Italian place on the corner that does a great early bird menu and has friendly staff.

name: Hotel Icon, Autograph Collection
title: “Great Place to Stay.....”
text: We stayed here for a long weekend....great accomidations, wonderful room and very clean and well appointed, excellent bar in the lobby; service was superior and very friendly.....can't tell you if the dining was good, we ate out.......we'll go back for sure.....

name: Hotel Icon, Autograph Collection
title: “Pleasantly surprised, will stay with them again.”
text: On June 9th and 10th three of my friends and I traveled to Houston to see our favorite baseball team, the St. Louis Cardinals, play the Houston Astros. I used TripAdvisor to locate hotels that were close to the downtown ballpark. The Icon Hotel was recommended and was eight blocks from Minute Maid Park. I booked two rooms for two nights and we were very pleased with our stay. The staff was very friendly and the rooms were clean, spacious and comfortable. The central air conditioning was quite and keep the room nice and cool even with the outside temperature in the high nineties. We did not see any children during our stay, mostly young professionals in the bar area and lobby. We requested the hotel suttle us to the ballpark before the game and we walked back to the hotel after the game when the temperature had cooled down. We walked two blocks to The Spaghetti Warehouse for an excellent pregame meal. The Icon Hotel is located in an old bank building and has the feel of an expensive downtown hotel. Vallet parking is $28.00 per day with suttle service offered for in town trips.

name: Hotel Icon, Autograph Collection
title: “Great stay!”
text: Check-in was a breeze. Check out was even smoother. The hotel makes you feel fancy from the moment you walk in, and the longer you stay the more at-home you feel. It's a throw-back hotel with a nod to the 20's with classy touches and a warm feel. The rooms are elegant, though admittedly a little dated. The bed was uncomfortable, as I could feel the springs when siting or lying on it, but I got a good night's sleep regardless. Even with all the busy traffic and noise outside, you can't hear much once you're inside your room. It's in a great location, walkable to my destination. The staff were wonderful, and always answered the phone in a timely manner. They went above and beyond to make sure I was well cared for during my stay, and I felt like a VIP (even though I wasn't). I ordered room service in the morning; it arrived promptly and had a very nice presentation. The complimentary Wi-Fi was a HUGE plus! I have my February stay already booked at Hotel Icon and look forward to another wonderful stay!

name: Hotel Icon, Autograph Collection
title: “One of the best in Houston”
text: What can I say about ICON it was great. It's downtown Houston great location.They have valet parking about 20 something a day.We got they our room was nice but we prefer a bigger bed,they upgraded our room it was great. The showers and bathroom is great. The scenery from the room are wonderful. There's a bar downstairs pretty pricy but therea many bars and resturants near. The hotels also gives free rides in the downtown area pickup ,drop- off. The decor of the hotel is very nice.Overall next trip I will stay at the ICON.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Houston
title: “Anniversary Get Away”
text: My husband and I chose Four Seasons for a night away from our children for our anniversary. I was very pleased with the friendliness and professionalism of the staff. Our room was very nice, and the bed was very comfortable. We even recieved a plate of assorted chocolates as an "anniversary gift". The only things that concerned me with our short stay is that we checked in at about 7 or 8 o'clock and night and checked out around 10 the next morning and we recieved two $15 dollar charges for the valet as the price is $15 dollars per day. We used the valet a total of 2 times so this didn't really seem very reasonable to me but I understand the policy. Also when we left I called for valey 15 minutes before hand. After about half an hour of waiting I ask the valet manager what the hold up was. Turns out they brought the wrong car down.... Wasn't happy about that but overall we had a good night there. I would recommend to a friend.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Houston
title: “Old Hotel, still maintained the prestigious level”
text:
The four seasons are a luxury chain hotels that thrive to maintain their level every where in the world. There will be some discrepancies from one hotel to another depends on the area, state, country, management and establishment, but overall they do not deviate from the main target… luxury.
This particular hotel in Houston is in the middle level between all the Four Seasons Hotels, mainly because the building is old (although well-kept) and the amenities are limited (only one restaurant), but still provides high class service.
If you are loyal to the four seasons, you will find the minor imperfections well tolerated. 
Just a quick point of notice, if I have to pick one hotel to stay at for business between the “Fairmont”, the “Ritz”, and the “Four Seasons”… I most probably pick the four seasons.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Houston
title: “Nice stay at an expensive hotel.”
text: We were in and out of Houston for one night to attend an event at the Four Seasons Houston. Our stay very brief but we enjoyed the hotel. It was quiet, the staff was accommodating, and the rooms were very clean. The property is a little older, but pretty well maintained. Our rate was discounted by my company, so I don't know about the value. The hotel only has valet parking although I think there is a parking garage next door. Valet was $30. The hotel is downtown near all the local attractions. We didn't use the pool with the poolside bar, but it looked nice. This is a fun hotel for a weekend get away. We have seen fancier hotels that provide more gilts and glam but this was a very nice hotel. The food and drink is expensive at this hotel. Its the Four Seasons, you pay for luxury. We enjoyed our stay and were very comfortable.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Houston
title: “Superb Service”
text: My husband and I had a wonderful stay at The Four Seasons Houston. The service was first class and the amenities were endless. We will be back here soon!!! Try the chocolate truffle martini. It was so yummy!

name: Hampton Inn and Suites Houston Medical Center - Reliant Park
title: “Good choice when visiting Rice University”
text: We stayed three days while visiting our daughter at Rice University. The hotel is one of a number that are within a short drive of Rice. We have previously stayed at the nearby Springhill Suites but thought we'd try the Hampton this time, and we did think that it was a better choice than Springhill: better rooms, newer appearance, air conditioners aren't noisy. We were a bit disappointed that the one bedroom suite is not really a suite here. We had just stayed in a Hampton earlier in the week that had a completely separate bedroom plus asmall kitchen. The bedroom here is open to the small living room and instead of a kitchen, there's a small refrig and microwave. On a positive note the furniture, carpets, beddding, etc., are all in good shape and appear to be fairly new. The housekeeping was average. The room appeared to be clean but I did notice that the coffee pot was not cleaned or changed when the room was cleaned. The breakfast was typical for a Hampton and the breakfast area is pleasant and clean. We were here on a Saturday morning and it was absolutely packed at 9 a..m. The weekday mornings were much less frantic. The hotel is located next to a Luby's Cafeteria, which would be convenient if you didn't have a car. Overall a good hotel choice.

name: La Quinta Inn Houston Northwest
title: “Excelente hotel”
text: Lo mejor es el desayuno, puedes preparte hasta unos wafles. La habitación tiene frigobar y horno de microondas. Todo con mucha limpieza y amabilidad del personal que labora ahi. Cuenta con alberca, ah y las camas muy cómodas.

name: Alden-Houston
title: “Attorney's Dream”
text: In town for a court case. 3 blocks to the court house and close to all kinds of food. I stayed for 3 nights and got excellent dinner advice each time, including the in house restaurant which was delicious. Keep up the good work......

name: Alden-Houston
title: “Boutique hotel run by people who don't know how to run a hotel”
text:
I recently stayed at the Alden Hotel during a conference. We had block booked a number of rooms and held three events in the hotel. While the hotel lobby is funky and the location is good for downtown Houston (but across the road from the Salvation Army soup kitchen), I found the staff at the hotel to be very unhelpful if not rude. I called down for a wake up call and was put on hold for so long that I gave up. I asked for the restaurant menu during a business meeting event and was told that the manager had to authorise giving us a menu. I spent 10 minutes on the phone arguing about the menu which we ended up collecting ourselves from the restaurant. Staff also kept coming in to the meeting room throughout the day which was very disruptive. On check out, the hotel refused to give us room receipts because we had block booked even though we explained that one person's credit card did not have an adequate limit to pay for 9 rooms and the card would be rejected. The only person with any customer service skills was the shuttle driver would went out of his way to be helpful.
In terms of the room, the lighting in my room could generously be called 'mood' lighting but in fact, the lightbulbs were burnt out. Every morning I showered in the near dark and it was hard to do work in the evenings due to the low lighting. The free wireless Internet in my room did not work and I ended up using a cable connection. Everyone in my group had issues with the Internet. Either they had to stand with laptop in hand by the window, use a cable or use a neighbouring hotel's wireless connection instead. One colleague couldn't get on at all.
In all, it was a bad stay not because the hotel is bad but because the people who run it don't know how to cater to the business traveller. I will never stay here again.

name: Carefree Inn Medical Center
title: “A pleasant surprise for me when all 5 stars were booked solid for the OTC!!”
text: I got to Houston a whole lot discouraged that I missed the chance to book into a 5 star hotel. A search on the Internet led me to Carefree Inn Medical Centre and I was so glad of the quality that I extended my stay a few more nights. Clean, quality rooms, complimentary breakfast and free internet were among the best parts. Also, I found the staff and management courteous and helpful, and their service prompt. On one occassion, one of them offered me a lift to my conference venue when the taxi I booked was running late. I recommend this hotel and would use it again while in Houston.

name: Hyatt Place Houston/Greenspoint/IAH Airport
title: “Nice lobby; rooms not so much”
text: The lobby is attractive as you walk in, but service and cleanliness has some to be desired. They had no hotel room keys when we checked in, so they had to escort us up to our rooms to be let in. Received room keys the next day. Room smelled like it needed a good cleaning. Breakfast the next morning was barely ok. A few of the staff were kind and helpful, but overall, wouldn't recommend it.

name: Marriott Houston Airport at George Bush Intercontinental
title: “Convenient”
text: I stayed here on business, i just had about 12hrs there. I liked that its at the airport. Theres a little tram that takes you there. The hotel seems huge. The rooms were clean & a good size. The beds are great. The only down fall, to get to my room i had a very short walk from one building to the next, which is kind of a hassle because i have my bags im trying to open the glass door, then get shoved by the door on my way out..i little pain but i survived. I then found out if you stay in the newer tower u dont have to be bothered with this hassle.. The staff was friendly, but i feel they should save rooms for there weeker smaller female, or elderly guest in the newer section. If your a guy you wouldnt care but when your tired shlepping your bags last thing you want to deal with is struggleing to open a door with one arm. Just an f.y.i. Other than that i would stay here again i think it was still worth it.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Houston
title: “Enjoyed The Four Seasons Houston”
text:
Spent a long weekend at Four Seasons Houston in the dead of summer. 
Excellent, large, clean room with outstanding service from all hotel employees. Very professional and courteous, attentive to your needs without being overbearing. Nice gift shop with newspapers, snacks, sundries, etc...Big outdoor pool with staff providing you with large plastic cups of ice water. Real good health club for serious workout enthusiasts. Cybex equipment -about a dozen different stations, plus treadmills, bikes with tv monitors. Nice whirlpool right off health club. Ten-minute walk to Minute Maid Park for Astros baseball, although be alerted that there seems to be an inordinate amount of construction work going on around Houston downtown streets, making it somewhat hazardous for pedestrians. Am looking forward to going back to the Four Seasons Houston - Very clean, nice, elegant, but no pretense. Not at all stuffy.

name: The Chatwal
title: “Don Draper move over!”
text: This hotel is like something out of a movie set - its beautiful and gleaming and just visually enticing in every way. The service was outstanding, the staff helped our family at every turn and couldn't have been more welcoming. The guest rooms are beautiful, lots of references to Broadway (think old movie posters from the 1950's) and Hollywood-esque vanity desks. Our favorite thing without a doubt was the breakfast though. Nectarine smoothies to die for. A real treat all round.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Houston
title: “Hohe Erwartung absolut erfüllt !”
text: Four Seasons erweckt nicht zuletzt aufgrund des Preisniveaus eine sehr hohe Erwartung, die in Houston absolut erfüllt wurde. Die grosszügige Juniorsuite war sehr geschmackvoll eingerichtet, hatte ein sehr gutes Sofabett, das guten Schlafkomfort bot und ein gediegenes Bad. Einzig der Lift vermittelt den Eindruck in einem alten Hotel zu sein, die restliche Ausstattung ist sehr klassisch und in einem ausgezeichneten Zustand. Room Service nachts nach später Anreise erstklassig - Küche und Service ! Kleiner aber sehr feiner Outdoor-Pool im ca. 5 Stock, sehr gepflegt und aufmerksam serviciert. Alle Mitarbeiter sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit. An den Pool grenzen Zimmer mit kleiner Terrasse und direkten Poolzugang, was für Familien sicherlich eine angenehme Lage ist. Das Hotel kann man absolut empfehlen - elegant und sehr persönlicher Service !

name: Andaz 5th Avenue
title: “Wonderful hotel”
text:
I just got back from my honeymoon in New York, and I absolutely loved our stay at the Andaz. The staff was incredibly professional and friendly, going so far as to remember our names for the entire week we were there! The man who showed us to our rooms, Dana, was helpful all week long, constantly inquiring about our stay and making great recommendations of things to see and do. 
And the hotel itself was fantastic. It's *so cool* looking that you feel like you're in a movie or something. I e-mailed Connie, the manager, and she gave us a complimentary room upgrade for our honeymoon! We had gorgeous views of the public library and a very large room. Plus, the free minibar stuff was delicious! There's a million cool hotels I'd love to stay at in New York, but I enjoyed the Andaz so much that I'm not really sure that I'll ever bother staying anywhere else.

name: San Carlos Hotel
title: “Fabulous as always”
text:
After flying up from Florida with great expectations for a cheaper hotel on the West side (in which we fled in horror), we found ourselves struggling to find a place to stay with no time to spare. Fortunately for us the fabulous San Carlos was able to give us a suite immediately and turn a horrible day into a wonderful stay. We had stayed at the San Carlos before with a positive experience but looked for a less expensive hotel as we were also paying for our two student family members. But as we found out, you get what you pay for. After the disappointment of another hotel, the San Carlos was worth paying for. The service as always was swift, efficient, pleasant and professional. Now if they would only give discounts for frequent guests I would feel complete...
Would definitely stay again.

name: La Quinta Inn Houston Medical / Reliant Center
title: “Good value”
text: The rooms were well-equipped and very clean. The only negative is that the doors open to the outside (motel-style). The free breakfast was very nice.

name: Marriott Houston Airport at George Bush Intercontinental
title: “The only hotel within the Airport and expensive.”
text:
The only hotel within the Airport, walking distance from any Terminal.
Very Good front desk.
Expensive but convenient.
Very Good break-fast with a cook-in station.
Worth the extra $$$ if you consider the time savings in getting the shuttle (or a car) to your out of airport hotel, tips, extra costs. etc.

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “Great Hotel”
text: I stayed at the Beacon in October 2011 with some girlfriends on a trip to NYC and it was the perfect hotel for our needs. We had 2 suites with a little kitchenette which came in very handy for the morning cup of tea, compliments of Mr Barry!! The suites were very spacious spotless and the beds very comfortable. The location was perfect, a little away from the main touristy parts of town but that was one of the main reasons why I chose this hotel. It is only a hop, skip and jump away from Central Park and the subway is just down the street where you can get a train to anywhere you wish to go. The staff were typical New Yorkers, not in your face over friendly but when I asked reception if they could recommend some nice places to eat, they couldn't have been more helpful. I personally love New Yorkers and their wonderful City...I will be back and would have no hesitation staying at the Beacon yet again.

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “Fantastic Location ~ 7th Floor View of Broadway ~ Excellent Room”
text:
This is a fantastic location on Broadway with a 24/7 deli / supermarket across the street. Downtown bus stop across street and only a few blocks either way to subway stations.
Excellent self contained room with full kitchen and views down onto Broadway
Easy early morning walk downtown for 40+ blocks. A few blocks from Central Park and Riverside Drive. Great walking area.
Ideal location for local business meeting.
First visit was in October 2001. Recommend it.

name: The Iroquois
title: “Excellent midtown hotel experience!”
text:
My wife and I stayed at The Iroquois for five nights to celebrate our anniversary, and enjoy some time in New York. When we first arrived at the hotel one of the doormen greeted us at the car, unloaded our bags, and proceeded to guide us into the hotel. Check-in was a breeze, and even though we arrived a bit early our room was ready for us. Chocolate covered strawberries and a bottle of sparkling water awaited us in the room, which was refreshing after we had had a bit of a stressful day prior to our arrival. 
The concierge desk was very helpful and friendly when assisting with reservations, tickets for shows, and great even just to talk to. All the staff in general were friendly, genuine and attentive, and always seemed to ask if there was anything they could do for us. We did not eat at Triumph, but we did visit the cocktail bar Lantern's Keep three nights we were at the hotel (they are closed Sunday and Monday). Quite simply some of the best cocktails we've ever had. 
We stayed in a suite, which we felt was necessary considering we would be there five nights. This gave us some breathing room, and a calm place to escape the hustle and bustle of the city for a little while in the afternoon. The living room was well appointed, with a mini-bar, Bose i-Pod dock, sofa/love seat, desk, etc... The bedroom had ample space, and the king size bed was great. Only thing I would change would be to get a duvet for the bed in the summer time that is a little lighter as it got a bit warm for me at night. The air-conditioning worked very well, and it was in the 90s the whole time we were there. Noise from the street was inaudible most of the time. Housekeeping was great, the room/bathroom was always clean. 
Overall, The Iroquois is a great hotel in midtown. If you want to have an "old" New York experience, with quality service, amenities, and well appointed rooms - stay at The Iroquois.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Houston Hwy 59S/Hillcroft
title: “a meeting with an out of town friend”
text: Easy access to the freeway and several restaurants in the area, room was clean and so was the hotel, the parking was free, Friendly staff, good breakfast. even though this hotel supposedly smoke free i still smelled cigarette smoke in the hallways, and the Ice machine is missing on the 5th floor.

name: Sun Suites Of Westchase
title: “great services”
text: Booked a room throught hotels.com at the gulf freeway location and was told they where booked and the front desk worker " mariticia" just told me they where booked and didnt help at all trying to relocate to another location she just informed me that they where full and said call hotels.com.So I called hotels.com and they found me another location on w sam houston location and Caroline was very helpful with everything. Her customer servies was excellent she made our stay there great.Thanks Caroline

name: The Iroquois
title: “Nothing too much trouble”
text: We stayed for a long weekend with our 17-yr old daughter to celebrate her school graduation. The staff were excellent, especially Alan the Concierge, who helped us with all our restaurant bookings and sundry other advise. We had a suite, which worked really well, as it was a proper suite (ie the bedroom was in a second room, not just an open-plan mini suite). The room was spacious enough and the bed extremely comfortable. The rate represented very good value indeed, given the excellent location and service.

name: Sun Suites Of Westchase
title: “Great location and value”
text: This is a great extended stay hotel. Its the most adorable area Comfortable beds and clean rooms.

name: Sheraton North Houston at George Bush Intercontinental
title: “Good Airport Hotel”
text:
I stayed here on two seperate occations in August, Priceline has it rated at 3 1/2 stars and I feel it is rated correctly. Some parts of the property seemed a bit dated and aside from very comfortable bedding, the room ammenitys were a bit sparce with no fridge or microwave, but it is a full service facility and has everything you need in an airport hotel. The Shuttle runs every 20 min to and from the airport and was very efficient, and I found the entire staff at every level to be very friendly and professional.
 Pros - In addition to free airport transportation, they have a full service resturaunt, lounge, 24 hr fitness center,and both indoor and outdoor pools as well as a business center with printer and fax service and also free Wi Fi in the rooms so all of your basic needs are covered here.
Cons - I felt the food and drink prices in the resturaunt and lounge were on the high side for the area, and I also felt that the rooms lacked a some common amenitys for a hotel at this star level (No fridge or microwave)
Overall though the friendly professional staff makes up for whatever shortfalls there are, and your needs are well taken care of here, I would not hesitate to stay again..

name: Baymont Inn & Suites Houston
title: “A convient roadside hotel”
text: A good value for the price. The decor is a bit dated , but the rooms are clean. The staff is very friendly. The free shuttle to and from the airport is a valuable perk.

name: The Iroquois
title: “A wonderful little gem”
text: This was our second stay at this property. All of the hotel staff were welcoming and helpful. The concierge went out of her way to accommodate our requests ranging from limo service to tickets, dinner reservations, champagne and flowers, and recommendations for sighseeing. The hotel is small, intimate, and beautifully appointed - a wonderful, quiet space to come home to! Location is great for easy access to galleries, museums, shopping, and theatre.

name: Hampton Inn Houston Hobby Airport
title: “Why are airport hotels always disappointing???”
text:
Here is the good -
Friendly staff
Great location
Good parking
Nice TV with lots of channels
Here is the not so good-
The room was dirty. I dropped my glasses in a corner off of the bed and had to dig under years of accumulated dirt. I looked around and found every corner to be dirty. 
Long black hairs in the bathroom. Not mine! 
Bathroom needs re-caulking.
The mattress slides off of the box spring.
The carpet is getting worn. Acceptable but worn.
So......your typical airport hotel.

name: Baymont Inn & Suites Houston
title: “missed our connecting flight to Europe and ended up here . . . it was fine”
text: A clean, average hotel. Other reviews stated that the shuttle driver was willing to take them to a store (Walmart), this was not the case for us. Shares a parking lot with Sonic and Waffle House where we used our airline food vouchers (no restaurant at the hotel). Very clean. Friendly staff. It was fine.

name: The Setai Fifth Avenue, a Capella managed Hotel
title: “Top Hotel”
text:
Nicht BILLIG aber preisWERT! Eines der besten Hotel in welchem ich je zu Gast war! Beste Lage, wunderschönes Zimmer mit bester Aussicht, freundliches und zuvorkommendes Personal, top Qualität in allen Bereichen! Minibar wird jeden Tag gefüllt und ist inbegriffen. 2x täglich Zimmerservice, und abends immer eine kleine Aufmerksamkeit runden das positive Gesamtbild ab.
Wir kommen beim nächsten New York Besuch sicher wieder ins The Setai!

name: Andaz 5th Avenue
title: “Will be back - great experience - not typical hotel in a good way”
text:
Reading some reviews about this hotel (mostly positive) I have to offer my perpective as a mid 30's business traveler and why I really like it. 
First - this hotel is in a great location and a new building, a good start for any hotel. It is well decorated in a modern/stylish look and feel, a stodgy Ritz Carlton this is not. The staff is on the younger side and very friendly - not old and formal like many 5 star hotels. During my stay they were professional and one woman went above and beyond to make sure a last minute request I made was done. I had room service and ate in the restaurant and both were high quality and worth the price. The shower in the room I had was huge and nice - all glass and stone, nice shower head etc. 
Beyond this what hit me was that they are not nickle and diming - internet is included in the rate, the water and basic snacks in the minibar were complimentary. While it seems small - this matters to me and says they are in tune with what people want. I will pay for a nice room service dinner - but don't charge for internet and a bottle of water. 
My complaints were really minor: the lights in the room were controlled by a fancy pad that was a bit tricky to use and the desk chair was a bit uncomfortable (looked nice). 
I will be staying there again on a future stay. As a frequent and global business traveler - this place is a solid hotel on all fronts. If you can afford the rate - try it. 
The NYTimes review which I read after seeing others on this board mention it is off track and probably written by an oldster for whom this hotel is not designed. Plus aren't the WWII generation they only people that subscribe to papers anymore?

name: Andaz 5th Avenue
title: “Really good experience”
text:
The location is perfect. So handy. Could walk to so many places.
The property is very good. Service is excellent. I was impressed by the versatility of the staff. Very efficient and responsive service. Booked restaurants, rearranged travel, loaded luggage on taxis, all with a smile. 
A laptop in the lobby was available for guests. Free wi-fi all through.
Room was great, large and comfortable. Bathroom was great, and huge.
Enjoyed the room very much.
Unfortunately the room had some dirty spots that were obviously routinely overlooked (the headboards were visibly dusty, the window panes absolutely filthy on the outside).
Air Conditioning wasn't very accurate, it was either too hot or too cold.
Room Service was ok, but food was not as good as Andaz Wall Street.
Restaurant was very good, both for breakfast and dinner. Good service. Great food. Nice mood. 
Really enjoyed my stay.

name: Studio 6 Houston Northwest
title: “Great for extended stay..”
text:
Before I begin, I agree with a previous reviewer "westoverroad" on all things about inside of the room itself.
I have been staying there for 10 days nows and would like to add my below thoughts - 
1. They have separate buildings for smoking and non-smoking rooms.
2. Front office staff is very cordial and caring. They assured me that, they will never remove our belongings for 24 hours (or something) unless we check out (or extend).
3. There is a security patrol at night, and the place is very safe, quiet and well lit. I saw couple of families with young kid living here.
4. Towels are clean and fresh. No smoke smell or stains.
5. Kitchen came with clean - cutting board, vessels, silver ware, dish drainer, kitchen towels, plates and bowls.
6. Kitchen has coffee maker, toaster, microwave, fridge and a small sink. There is a neat breakfast nook, which can be used for office work and reading too.
7. There is a love seat, lots of storage, ironing board and iron.
8. Very close to restaurants and other stores.
9. Reasonable laundry room.
If you're noise sensitive, you may want to choose your rooms carefully as this place sits right next to 290 fwy.
Things needing improvement - 
1. Bed linen smelt musty and felt ragged.
2. Pillows were too soft and old.
3. Wifi connection is very slow.
I used to stay at a nearby InnTown Suites and that place sucked.

name: Interstate Motor Lodge
title: “Nice motel”
text: Don't be fouled by the outside of the motel. The rooms were clean and the bed was comfortable. The breakfast was not to good. There was no milk for cereal and nobody around to help.

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Our favorite NYC Kimpton!”
text:
We've stayed at three of the four Kimptons in Manhattan and we won't need to stay at the other because this is our favorite. Clean, comfortable, modern rooms; welcoming and helpful staff as one might expect from Kimpton; and a perfect location. This is Manhattan so rooms are small and can be expensive, but we found the Eventi to be a great value, too.
We had an Executive One Bedroom Suite which gave us a little extra room to stretch out and relax without feeling like we had to spend all our time on the bed. If you can afford the extra expense, I would recommend doing the same.
The location couldn't make it any easier as a base for exploring the city. Just one cross-town block and two street blocks from Penn Station makes taking the train a breeze. A similar distance to the 28th Street Stations at Broadway or 7th Ave give you access to the 1, 2, N or R subway lines in five minutes.
The attached restaurant, Bar Basque, is also very modern and probably more of a bar than restaurant. A great patio area with a view of the GIANT TV screen on the wall of an adjacent building made for a great way to watch the NFL playoffs.
Overall, it is easy for us to recommend this fine hotel and we plan to stay there on our next visit to NYC.

name: The Iroquois
title: “Perfect place for Mother/Daughter weekend!”
text: My 12 year-old daughter and I returned to the Iroquois for our 2nd annual mother/daughter weekend, and had a wonderful time. You couldn't ask for a more friendly and helpful staff! Upon arrival we were informed that they selected a larger room for us knowing that we weren't 100% thrilled with our smaller room last year. The concierge was wonderful! I sent an email a week before our arrival asking for suggestions on places to visit and information on where to find my daughter's favorite ice cream. He responded within 12 hours and even followed up with more suggestions a day later. The doormen were always smiling when we ran into or out from the cold, and offering to get us transportation or sending us off in the correct direction when hoofing it down the street. Yes, the rooms are boutique in size, but they are spotless and the bedding is luxurious. My 12 year-old did not want to leave the cozy bed with it comforter and huge pillows. Location is awesome, easy to get to everything! As for price, it allowed this mom/daughter to enjoy NYC without breaking the bank. Coming back next year!!!

name: The Iroquois
title: “They wow'd us!”
text:
Check into one of their suites and enjoy all that New York has to offer! 
Let Alan and Venessa take care of threstaurants and theatres. 
Rooms are large and luxurious.
Staff is attentive and courteous! 
All together they helped make our January break-ation very special!

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Brilliant Manhattan Hotel”
text:
We've stayed in New York a number of times, usually in the Soho/Tribeca area, but this time we were looking to stay in a different area. The Eventi is a really lovely hotel and the staff were exceptionally helpful and friendly. 
The hotel itself is very trendy looking and the rooms are not huge but then again it is New York! We found our room was spacious enough, but we don't spend much time in our rooms. We were on the 14th floor so had no issues with any music as mentioned by some previous posters. 
The wine hour was delightful and tea and coffee in the morning was great. These small touches made you feel more at home, which as we were there for 9 nights made it for a really pleasant stay. 
In terms of location it was really great, its a short walk to most of the subway lines and it made for an easy commute to all manhattan destinations, it was also super convenient to drop things back to the hotel and keep going. The proximity to Macy's is a plus as well! 
The area immeditely around the hotel is not as touristy as other places, which we actually like and it is close to Koreatown so there is no shortage of restaurants near by. But you walk a couple of blocks across west 30th street and you end up near penn station or on 5th avenue where there is plenty to see and do. 
My only negative was that housekeeping comes very early and so if we were not out of our room early enough chances were we wouldn't get housekeeping that day, but this did not worry us, and we could have mentioned it to the front desk (but we kept forgetting!) 
We did note the party atmosphere at the hotel and on the weekends it was very crowded and noisy (which can mean you have to wait for a lift) but we were never affected by noise in our room. If anything our room was an oasis of quiet. 
The gym is also well equipped and clean.

name: San Carlos Hotel
title: “Semplicemente ideale”
text:
Ho soggiornato presso l'hotel San Carlos di NY dal 01/09 al 06/09/2010. Fam. composta da 2 adulti e 2 bambini di 9 e 13 anni. Il mio giudizio è più che positivo. Camere spaziose, silenziose, curate, pulite (cambio giornaliero delle lenzuola e degli asciugamani), colazione deliziosa ed abbondante (compresa nel prezzo che per NY è veramente un lusso) ideale per iniziare nel modo migliore la giornata. Posizione strategica sia per i collegamenti della Metro (fermata sulla 51^strada ad 1 blocco di distanza) che per passeggiate a piedi sino alla 5th Avenue - Cattedrale di St.Patrick, Rockefeller Center ecc. e per i volenterosi sino a Central Park. Il personale è gentile e disponibilissimo. Grazie alla Reception. Al secondo piano disponibilità di computer compreso accesso ad internet free. Al terzo piano piccolo ma sufficiente reparto fitness. 
NB. All'uscita della metro (fermata 51^strada sulla Lexington Avenue) piccolo punto di ristoro Metro Caffè ideale per un pranzo/cena veloce. Dai panini imbottiti, pizze, pasta con vari condimenti, frullati, yogurt ecc. sino alle squisite insalate da poter comporre a scelta del cliente... Ci ha risolto più di un pasto.

name: InTown Suites Houston Northwest / Cy-Fair (XHW) - Houston
title: “Gross, dirty,uncomfortable, but cheap”
text:
Checked in rather late at night (like 2:00 AM) after driving into town for a funeral. It's the only hotel that has a room available for less than $150. I should have known there was a problem when it was only $59, but I figured since it was the last room, they were offering a special on it.
 The guy at the checkin booth took his time processing the check-in. I asked if he could make sure my rewards card was noted on the reservation and he said okay. A few quiet minutes later, he was still staring at the screen. I asked if there was a problem, he said no and printed out a receipt for me to sign. I asked again about the rewards card (he never asked for it, so he couldn't have added it), and he said I would have to call. Fine. 
I find my room, walk in, close the door and the door barely shuts or locks. Someone could barely push the door and it would open. At this point, I am tired and since it's literally the last room they had, I wasn't going to get another one anyway. 
Main problems:
-The "non smoking room" reeked of cigarettes
-The floors were fillthy - made the bottom of my feet black
-There was soap scum in the shower, like someone had a bar of soap that got stuck to the side and no one bothered to clean it
-Someone elses hair (what appeared to be facial hair from someone who had shaved) all over the sink, and the shower
-The beds were concave in the middle, like they were 20 years old, even though the hotel isn't that old
-The blankets were knotty
-The sheets we itchy and rough
- The towels looked like they were washed on cold and left to dry by air
When I checked out in the morning, the day person couldn't find my reservation. She asked if I was SURE I stayed there last night. Um, YES!!!!!! Finally she found me and turns out the night guy had listed me as a no show. Well, he took my credit cards and I signed the receipt so I would have to argue I was there!!!!
When I tried to call the rewards line to have the night added, they said I was a no show too. They called the hotel who also confirmed I was a no show, but said they had a record of me staying there in Feb 07. NOPE, not me! I had to fax in a copy of my receipt and 3 days later the points still haven't been added. 
Considering the quality of the room, I deserve my points for it!!!!
Would NOT stay there again, even with the cheap price.

name: San Carlos Hotel
title: “Un lujo.”
text: Mejor imposible. En el centro. A un paso de todo. Con personal muy atento. La habitación impecable todos los días. Para repetir.

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Check your credit card statement when you get home!”
text: I stayed at the Eventi in June and December 2011 and overall enjoyed it (which is why I went back the second time). The rooms are quite nice, especially the bathrooms, they have lovely views (for an additional cost), and for the most part the staff are very friendly and helpful. Unfortunately, both times after I got home I discovered extra charges added to my credit card for additional nights of valet parking and also numerous items from the mini bar, none of which we had consumed. Both times I called the hotel the charges were reversed immediately; however, since I don't live in the US I ended up out of pocket due to fluctuating exchange rates both times. After I explained this the last time I called, the staff member I spoke to was very apologetic and said he would have someone from management contact me to discuss this, but sadly I never heard from anyone. Sorry Eventi (and Kimpton), but there are lots of fantastic hotels in NYC and I will be staying at one of them on my next visit,

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Nice location, decent service at this hotel”
text:
I seemed to run into quite a few issues on my business trip to NYC, two of them relating to the hotel. However, Kimpton hotels are known for their friendly service, and this hotel is no exception. I just wish that I wouldn't have had the problems in the first place! 
First, my co-worker and I arrived at the hotel and they had lost her reservation. She had a confirmation number and everything, but there was nothing they could do because the hotel was at 100% occupancy that night. She ended up staying on the pull-out sofa in my room, and the hotel generously waived the charge for that night. 
Second, my office shipped several boxes for an event that we were holding on the hotel's terrace, and one of our boxes was lost. It was a huge ordeal to prove to the hotel that we had shipped to the correct location, they signed for the package, and then it was misplaced. It was a big waste of time, but they ended up replacing what we lost in the box.
On to the other aspects of the hotel:
-The rooms are lovely and the bathrooms are very spacious. The quality of their bath products was appreciated.
-If you sign up to be a Kimpton member, you can receive free wifi and $10 free to the mini bar
-The downstairs restaurant had a fun wine sampling bar - pay by the ounce instead of glass
-Room service was very slow

name: The Setai Fifth Avenue, a Capella managed Hotel
title: “Luxus in Top Lage”
text: Neues Hotel in Top Lage an der 5th Avenue, mitten im Shopping Paradies. Ähnlich wie das Schwester Hotel in Miami sehr reduzierter Luxus, schlichtes Design, sehr edel. Die einfachste Zimmerkategorie ist eher klein mit wenig Stauraum, besser Deluxe Zimmer buchen: sehr geräumig mit traumhaftem Marmorbad und großer Dusche + Badewanne. Nespresso Maschine im Zimmer und die Minibar ist complimentary. Sehr hervorzuheben und nahezu einzigartig in Manhattan ist der SPA Bereich mit Sauna und Vitality Pool, der für Hotelgäste kostenfrei nutzbar ist. Vitality Pool und Hammam sind sogar für Männer und Frauen gemeinsam nutzbar. Nette Hotelbar.

name: Northgate Inn and Suites Houston
title: “Disgusting and flea infested-NASTY !!!”
text: the first room they gave me smelled so bad, like mold and sour milk and the carpet was soaking wet from the a/c leaking. i went to front desk and told them and had to argue with them for 2 hours before they would give me a different room. The second room was even worse than the first, it was completely flea infested BAD. i was told they had no other rooms available and they refused to refund my money so i went to store and bought 8 bug bombs with my own money and set them off in there. Even after that i was getting bitten so bad by fleas that i couldnt even stay there one night(and i had paid for a weeks stay). They still would not refund my money so i was out over $230 and still had to go pay to stay someplace else for the week. I cannot beleive this place is still open. I would definately NOT recommend staying here EVER for any reason

name: Days Inn West Houston
title: “Convenient location - small, I mean "small", bathrooms”
text:
Stayed 3 days in July 2010 at this Motel. 
ROOMS: We reserved 2 rooms since we were traveling with extended family (5 total). We had rooms next to each other but they were not connected rooms. There was a fridge in the room with the king size bed. Overall, the beds were comfortable and we felt it was relatively clean. 
BATHROOMS: Well, I can honestly say I have never seen a bathroom so small. It was about the size of a powder room with a toilet on one side and what can be descibed as a half tub on the other (half the height/half the length). Some might describe it as a shower. It was difficult to get around in the bathroom due to the size and the door swinging inward towards the small room.
POOL: We all really enjoyed the pool. It was in decent shape albeit somewhat aged. It was clean but did not have an overwhelming smell of clorine like some hotel/motel pools. We spent hours each day enjoying the pool. 
FOOD: The Days Inn breakfast was just cold breakfast. No waffles for the kids to make (which they enjoy making as much as eating). Bagles, toast, cereal, muffins as well as orange and apple juice. They had a small assortment of fruit each day as well.
SECURITY: This was the only real concern I had based on the area and the type of accomodations. The hotel was rather empty on our trip so we were able to park right up to the room (1st floor room). No problems though, quiet nights.
BONUS: I have to mention this. We left a t-shirt and my daughters "special pillow" she had since she was 3 or 4 (currently 9) in the room. After approximately 2 hours on the road heading north we realized it and called the hotel and had them check. They found the pillow and t-shirt and put it at the front desk for my brother (who lives close) to pick it up. Any complaints I might have (small bathroom) about the motel were changed by the kindness of the staff to help us when we needed it.
OVERALL: Good trip, decent motel. If you are just looking for a place to lay your head, this works for convenience. The breakfast is ok, but simple. The staff was kind - not great, but kind.

name: Hotel 31 Houston Near the Galleria
title: “Fraudulent charges, unhelpful staff, fraud claim filed”
text:
Booked through Hotwire.com on the company travel card, provided personal card at the front desk for incidentals. No restaurant, no parking charges, but was fraudulently charged the following week. Staff gave me erroneous explanations, would not send copy of bill, refund the charges, follow up on fax or return calls. Filed fraud claim. 
Avoid at all cost.

name: Sheraton North Houston at George Bush Intercontinental
title: “Great location, neat and clean, outdated”
text:
We stayed here before an early morning flight out of IAH. The location is perfect for the airport (don't be mistaken, Downtown Houston is quite a drive from the airport).
The hotel has clearly been built in the 80s. It has features like an indoor, but open-to-the-lobby pool on the ground level that are outdated. However, as old as the design and features maybe, they are kept very nicely and mostly everything is clean and neat.
Rooms are of average size and quiet with an updated design. The bathrooms are clean but could use a renovation. 
There is free WiFi in the lobby and also computers for customer use. Parking is free right outside the hotel. 
We paid 60$ per room via Priceline. For this money the hotel is a steal. If I had to pay rack rate, I would probably consider one of the nearby hotels of the Courtyard class, since on a short layover most of the services of a Sheraton are not needed.

name: Venetian Inn & Suites Houston Airport
title: “RED BUMPS all over my body”
text:
OMG, NEVER again. Three mosquitoes in the sink area, a spider in the bathroom and a dead fly in the refrigerator. Everything that everyone else said plus. I have bumps down my arms, legs and right side of neck & face. WTH!!! We called for towels three times to be told "People steal and we sorry." Unacceptable!! I believe this is a city hotel for shelter folks. Clothes hanging out the window and hillbilly folk sitting out as if they no longer had their trailor.
Other then that the lady at the front desk was very nice and took pics of us as we left out for dinner and the breakfast was ok.

name: Hotel 31 Houston Near the Galleria
title: “Under a new franchise, but just as good as a regular holiday inn.”
text: We arrived at 12:15 am, but service was exceptional, and the rooms were beautiful. The hotel has been bought over and renamed to Hotel 31, but you could never tell just looking at it. Literally. They haven't gotten around to taking down the Holiday Inn sign. :)

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “Best value Hotel!”
text: Stayed for 1 week end of June/start of July with family of 4, 1 bedroom with kitchenette, the sofa bed was ok for kids, but 2 adults would not have lasted a week. Everything else about this place staff & facilities is fantastic. Clean rooms, no bed bugs, exceptional beds- comfort, Wireless Internet. Even room maids were very accomodating with our long morning sleep ins (jet lagged kids), providing 3pm room service, or just towells as required. We really got to appreciate the location, a bit out of the noise/action, quiet, and only a $10 taxi to Times Square etc. Family made the observation that the street looked like a movie set! Fairways grocery across the street (fruit, veg etc), a deli also, Nicks Pizza a 10 min walk North on Broadway was excellent, Cafe Viand next door was tops also (we did a few 1am breakfasts!). 71st subway station street a 10 min walk, I even found "real" coffee - for an Aussie in Aromas coffee on 72nd street, 10 min walk in the mornings. Hotel do-your-own Laundry facilities were the best (clean, and dryers were fast -no shrink) we found in our whole 5 week holiday through West & East coast USA- all other laundries after were compared to the Beacon benchmark! (There is a couple of wash & folds about 1 block walk to Amsterdam St, $1.50 per pound, we used these when too tired to do laundry!). If you stay, do the museum of Natural History, a 15-20 min walk, get to the Dinosaur section, kids were wide eyed, and I have never seen anything like it. Also worth the walk down 72nd street to see J Lennon appt, & Central Park strawberry fields memorial, very pretty.

name: The Iroquois
title: “Exceptional, can't wait to return”
text: Perfect location, central to all the main sights yet quiet enough to ensure a good nights sleep which is essential after all the sightseeing and walking. We had a family room which was ideal for a family including 2 teenagers. The hotel staff were friendly and helpful at all times. Our package included buffet breakfast which set us up for the day. Good facilities including gym (if you have enough energy after all the walking!), free internet access and enough information to help you get around this amazing city.

name: San Carlos Hotel
title: “Encantado de conocer el hotel”
text:
