Me encanto, tranquilo, personal amable, de veras ningun prolema. Solo que es un poco caro, pero merece la pena. Repito sinceramente excelente.
Madrid. España.

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Hotel/Great Service”
text: This was my first time staying at this hotel during a business trip in late October. The hotel was centrally located to other destination spots in NYC. My room was very clean, the bed was very comfortable and the bathroom was beautiful. Another highlight of my visit was Omar at the front desk. He was so incredibly helpful and made sure that my stay at the Eventi was a great experience. I was so impressed with this hotel that I am coming back again next week!

name: Sheraton North Houston at George Bush Intercontinental
title: “Update (Year Four)”
text:
Attending a yearly conference here, I cautiously watched for negative items in other T.A. reviews. Shopping carefully, I got a great rate and stayed four nights. The only room issue was the a/c blew just hot air, however it was repaired immediately on my reporting it. The bed couldn't have been more comfortable. Perhaps the room was small but I was solo and got a great rate & room. As a final test, I ordered breakfast via door hanger on the last day, requesting delivery from 6:30-6:45 a.m. It was promptly, pleasantly delivered at 6:30 a.m., fresh and hot.
Usually critical in hotel reviews, I feel this year the Sheraton IAH did very well. No room-switching or problems described in other review(s). Perhaps they have adjusted from the storm last year.

name: Americas Best Value Classic Inn & Suites- Downtown
title: “bang for buck”
text: This is a great hotel to stay at for the price of the rooms. It's a convenient location very close to downtown. Not too much traffic around the area. The desk clerk was very friendly and the rooms were clean and tidy.

name: Andaz 5th Avenue
title: “A great find :)”
text: Great designed hotel in a good location. Service were friendly always and genuinely helpful. Having free wifi throughout was a big plus. And a nice place for coffee and breakfast on the ground flood was convenient and good. Even better ad it's free for Diamond members.

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “Great hotel, location and staff”
text: This hotel is fantastic! We stayed here for 5 nights and didn't want to leave. We got there early and the room wasn't ready so we left the bags in the hotel and had a walk around. The rooms are big for New York standards. We got two double beds, a flat screen t.v and a kitchenette (which came in very useful). The maids were extremely nice every morning we left and they were in the hall they would make sure to say 'good morning' and 'have a nice day'. You also get a newspaper everyday which is nice. There's a market straight across the street called fairway's and it's brilliant. They sell everything you would need and upstairs they have a cafe that has the most amazing breakfast! And in the evening they sell steak etc. There's loads of shops around the hotel, central park is only a short walk away and the subway is only a block and half from the hotel. The staff at reception give you a map when you check in which comes in really handy as the subway lines and hotel are all marked on it! It's only 10 minutes from Times Square (or 3 stops on the express train) on the subway. Overall we had a great experience and will most likely stay in this hotel again.

name: Sheraton North Houston at George Bush Intercontinental
title: “Loved the Sheraton!”
text: We stayed April 22 the night before an early morning flight out of Houston Intercontinental. . We arrived at noon and were pleased to get into our room! Having just come off a cruise ship in Galveston, it was great to check in so early. The entire hotel staff was the most accomodating of any hotel we have ever stayed at, especially the desk staff and the housekeeping staff. The business room and internet access were so helpful . We were able to print off 5 boarding passes and book last minute tickets to an Astros game. The best part was the outdoor pool-very large and clean and refreshing. The king bed was so comfortable , however, my daughter said the sofa bed was uncomfortable. The room and bathroom were very clean. We had complimentary airport shuttle the next morning at 5 am and again, a very friendly driver! All in all, if we ever need a hotel in Houston again we will definitely stay here again!

name: La Quinta Inn Houston Wilcrest
title: “strong smell of smoke in non-smoking room, road noise”
text:
Quite disappointed by smell of smoke in room. There was much road noise with room facing I-10. Noise was drowned out by ac, but there was no fan only setting or switch to keep it on constantly, so it was either too cold or too noisy. The birds in the trees outside my room made it difficult to sleep past 6am. Very much a motel.
On the positive side, the hotel was much less expensive that others in the area and it was close to I-10 and 8.

name: Rodeway Inn Houston
title: “Totally Surprised :)”
text: I was in north side of houston to visit my relatives and found this hotel. The price was $50 plus tax and i didn't expect much from the room. but i was totally surprised when i get into the room, It was super clean.Staff was very friendly and free breakfast in morning. Best fit for the price. Recommended

name: Sheraton North Houston at George Bush Intercontinental
title: “Nahe am Airport”
text:
Das Hotel liegt in der Nähe des Flughafens, der Shuttel hat ungefähr 5min gedauert.
Das Hotel hat einen kleinen Innen- sowie Außenpool. Es gibt eine Frühstücksbuffet, es ist mit $10 zu empfehlen, aber eher amerikanisch. Die Zimmer sind schon etwas in die Jahre gekommen, aber trotzdem sauber und gut eingerichtet. Es gibt einen öffentlichen Bus auf der anderen Strassenseite der ca. 1 Stunde bis Downtown braucht. (oneway $1,25)

name: Candlewood Suites Houston West
title: “Pleasant place to stay with hospitable staff”
text:
I was stayed here (Studio suite, ground floor, just behind the pool gazebo) 2 weeks for business purpose and I loved it. Despite that they don't clean the room everyday (every 2-3 days or so as I remember), the place is actually quite enjoyable.
Things you need to know;
- No breakfast served. But Waffle House & Sonic are just a stone's throw away. There's also a small mini-market called "cupboard" near the receptionist with variety of foods and drinks to choose from. If you want halal food, there's an Iranian run restaurant called "Hafez", just across the hotels on your right.
- They clean the room every 2-3 days or so. Couldn't remembered exactly, but for sure not everyday. This be the main cons. Not sure if this is part of corporate deal, but other reviews stated daily cleaning. Better check your deal first.
- Gym was more than OK.
- Laundromat is free!
- Kitchenette inside the room is quite small but beyond my expectations. Fridge is big, everything working fine.
- Free internet/Wifi !! :)
- Free local calls
- Pool was OK, there's a fire up grill and gazebo to hanging around.
- I love the bed and pillows so much.
- The receptionist (forgot the name, 3 of them I think) were all very hospitable and very friendly. They took care everything we need and provide reliable information for places around the hotel.
- Complete amenities; Irons, hairdryer, etc
- Flat screen and DVD in the room! :D.. love it! Aside from hundreds of good (HD) movie channel, you can borrow a collection of DVD titles available at receptionist for free!
- Parking slot is ample and we felt security is OK.
- There's a small but reliable business corner with online desktop PC and a printer.
- Location is in Westheimer Rd where you could go to a lot of places to eat.
Overall I would recommend this place to anyone and definitely will stay here again.

name: Red Carpet Inn Hobby Airport
title: “Lowest Bidder - There's a Reason”
text:
I booked this place sight-unseen through Travelocity. Big mistake. The grounds looked awful when I arrived. The lobby had several people just hanging around, smoking, watching TV, eyeing me when I turned my back. (I'm a bodyguard, so I watch people in reflections.) The clerk said my room number aloud.
My first "nonsmoking" room smelled of cigarettes and antiseptic. It had no smoke alarm. I went back for another room. It had the same conditions, plus a sink plugged with butts. I tried to get used to the place and took a shower. When I turned the TV on, I got hardcore porn, no warnings.
The bed sagged in the middle. The sheets and mattress bore cigarette burns.
I spent the night at a friend's house. I complained to Travelocity, but they haven't done anything but assure me they're working on a refund.

name: Comfort Suites
title: “It was very good”
text: The staff went out of there way to make my stay a very good one if we needed any thing they made sure we got what we needed.

name: Andaz 5th Avenue
title: “OFF THE HOOK”
text: This hotels is outstanding. The staff, room, bar, & restaurant all five star. Andaz gives new meaning to the word "boutique". For those that gave any negative reviews two words "stay home".

name: Scottish Inns & Suites Timber
title: “Good value for money”
text: Clean and large rooms, but thin walls, so we could hear our neighbours arguing. Breakfast not impressing, but ok concidering the price for the hotel

name: Microtel Inn & Suites by Wyndham Houston
title: “Weird evening - strange response from management”
text:
I left this establishment disturbed and very surprised at management's response to strange noises, doors slamming. I had a room on the first floor with a connecting door to another room. The guests in the next room were constantly playing with the door in what I assumed was an attempt to enter my room. I went to the front desk and asked if there was a problem. Their response was "they felt the room was too small" and decided to move. However, throughout the night the "guests" continued to fidget with the door, slam doors and knock on my walls. 
I decided to leave and was told that no one has been in my neighboring room at all. Very strange. They also told me the hotel was full and had no other available room. It was far from the truth as the parking lot was completely empty. 
It was the strangest hotel experience I've ever had. I would never recommend this place to anyone.

name: The Iroquois
title: “We could not have been more pleased...”
text: My new bride and I (both 59 years of age) had the most incredible honeymoon in New York, staying at the Hotel Iroquois. From check-in, to the quality of the room, to the helpfulness of the concierges, to the level of service - we could not have been more pleased with our stay. The decor of the room was great. The amenities in the room were thoughtful. The staff was attentive and extremely helpful. The recommendations by the concierge were terrific.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Houston Southwest
title: “Very Clean and Friendly”
text: We came to Houston so my husband could go into the Methodist Hospital for a surgical procedure. The Clerk at check in gave us an even better Hospital discount. They are the nicest people. The breakfast area is very clean ant the pool is great. An all around great hotel.

name: La Quinta Inn Houston Cy-Fair
title: “Great Stay”
text: Just got home from a stay here. It was great staff VERY friendly. I gave the room the sock test and they were still white. Lots of pillows very soft bed. The only sleep issue I had was when the room reached its temp the air conditioner stopped and the room got too quite. The breakfast was good we got there at 9:40 and they refilled so we could eat

name: La Quinta Inn Houston Cy-Fair
title: “fine accomodation in decent location”
text: Stayed here for 3 weeks in June 09. Place is very clean and quiet despite close proximity to the highway. Staff are very friendly, breakfast is basic and does the trick. Next to a bar but no real disturbance heard from there. Very handy for local restaurants. Would be happy to stay here again. PS Houston is very very HOT in June.

name: America's Inn
title: “A pretty average motel in a rather seedy location”
text: OK, so this is one of the few motels in Houston where you can stay get a room for the night, with continental breakfast and free Wi-Fi, for under fifty bucks. But I can honestly say that I have stayed in nice places than this. The motel is located between car lots on the access road to Highway 59, just about where it joins Beltway 8 (it could be a good setting for a vice movie, for sure). The motel itself is pretty OK, with a pool tacked on the side. My room was large, with everything I would expect at this price range. However, when I checked in in the early afternoon I noticed my next door neighbors sitting on their bed with the door wide open, smoking. And there was a wheelbarrow outide the door with a TV set perched on top. The reception staff were friendly, and the morning breakfast was OK, but somehow I could not get the location or the seedy clientelle out of my head. Conclusion: Try somewhere else if you can.

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Good service, nice rooms and good price”
text:
We went in June 2010 with a 6 months old baby and had a very pleasant stay. We were upgraded free to a better room as there were empty rooms. Did not see the room we initially booked, but the upgraded one was very nice and comfortable, with views of the Empire State Building.
My only complaints: We found a lost t-shirt behind a chair, from the previous guests, and we were charged from the mini-bar and we haven't take anything, but they solved it immediately I must say.
The rest was just about perfect, also the size of the room (beeing a NY hotel).
Would return to that place, that's for sure.

name: Candlewood Suites Houston Medical Center
title: “Very Disappointed, NEVER AGAIN!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this Candlewood hotel near Reliant Stadium for 5 nights for the Final Four. We have stayed at many Candlewood properties in the past and this was definitely not up to par! Some might not notice, but the first thing I saw when I walked into the room was a comforter on the bed that was so wrinkled that it looked like it had been in a dryer for about a week. It looked horrible and NEVER got any better for the entire stay. This is an extended stay hotel and we never got any service for the entire 
5 days we were there....no extra bars of soap, shampoo, fresh towels, etc. I asked for the suite to be vacuumed midway through our stay and was told it would cost an extra $10! Puleeze!
The one thing that really drove me crazy was the overhead "kitchen area" light that was always on if ANY lights were on in the suite. You couldn't lie in bed and read without the glaring light in the kitchen being on. We checked with the desk, thinking we were doing something wrong, but no, we weren't. My husband had to climb up on a chair to remove the light fixture and unscrew the two lightbulbs for our entire stay. Ridiculous. There are also only lights on one side of the bed, so if there are two travellers, one of them cannot lie in bed and read because there is no light!
Their shuttle only goes to the Medical Center and back on the hour. Want to dropped off somewhere in between? Too bad. No can do. There is no way you can stay at this hotel without renting a car.
There is no smoking allowed in the hotel (good!) and as a result there are always several people right outside the front door smoking up a storm. Frequently these are Candlewood employees. UGH! The front desk people were pleasant enough, but not one of them knew anything about the area, had maps, or had any info about the Final Four! There is no business center and there was no way to print anything off of a computer. Lastly, I bought a couple of things from the little convenience area by the front desk, which were fairlly priced BTW, but the area reeked so strongly of curry that I could hardly stand to go in there. This hotel has rooms for nearly $250 a night! I would never stay here again. EVER!
days!

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “This is the best place to stay for getting the feel of NYC neighborhood!”
text: I can't recommend this hotel enough. I have stayed there easily 6 or 7 times in the last 12 years. The suites are spacious and simply perfect for a middle of the road hotel experience. Lots of shopping and a good place for foodies. The rooms are always quiet. Nice view of the streets from whatever room you end up with. Shop around for price on this hotel and make sure you go to their website for pricing. If you call the hotel directly you can end up with a good deal or getting scalped! Beware of the laundry situation, in other words, don't send out your laundry. The only thing is, the location isn't great if you are going to Midtown every night for shows. But, it is a great location for Lincoln Center events.

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Houston- Medical Center
title: “Stay away !”
text: Besides the fact that it is so over priced for what it is, the rooms smell and aren't clean they also have roaches. The shuttle is anything but dependable we were left strainded several times and forced to pay for a taxi. I can go on but I think I've said enough to warn people from staying here.

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “beacon hotel great venue for NYC”
text:
Hotel Beacon Upper West Side NYC- Dec 2010. great location.
Arrived 17.12.2010 travelled with wife and 14 year old daughter, leisure trip. Stayed for 12 nights over Xmas, so we had a good deal of time there to assess just what type of
place this is.
Location adjacent, (100 metres from 72nd st metro stop) great location, this is 4 or 5 stops from times square centre of town, ie 42nd st for all theatres etc. Metro is $2.25 per ride per person regardless of distance, so get a card which you can place $ value on and then use it all over the system. Also can be used on buses. So 3 people going all over metro system per trip is really cheap. Super convenient safe clean system.
But the Beacon..... clean, safe, opposite fairway, i think, super market, 24/7 place with everything and anything you can imagine, also rooms are equipped with kitchenette ie micro wave, stove, fridge & sink etc . coffee making, haridryers, full bathroom including a tub king bed in main room. We got a jnr suit for a very reasonable rate but there are the following taxes applicable to all NYC hotel stays; state tax, city tax, occupancy tax and hotel unit fee so you have to factor that in to all accommodation. Sone of the rooms on our floor, 11th overlooking Broadway, are occupied/owned by fulltime residents. So i suppose it is almost like a serviced apartment block. 
The Beacon is worth every cent, great housekeeping, polite reception even assisted when we got hit with a Blizzard in getting us onto our airline to get out of NYC to Vegas. Free internet room off foyer, we had a couple of housekeeping malfunctions, we notified hotel and literally within 5 minutes people were at our door who actually fixed the problem. The room had movies on demand if you got sick of the 100 plus channels. 24/7 security and they are able to get you tickets to shows, tours etc if you like. 
We cant speak highly enough of this place and would not hesitate to recommend it to
others, regardless of age or trip reason. The hotel is 3 or 4 blocks walk from Central Park which is itself amazing, 3 or 4 blocks from Lincoln Centre which houses opera, ballet and movies etc. You can walk to 5th Ave or just down Broadway as a tourist.
Columbus and Amsterdam are 1 or 2 blocks East of the hotel and they are crammed with restaurants. Beacon has cafe Viand in the building, didnt try it. But the supermarket opposite has a breakfast floor which is great for brekky and reasonable if you dont want to use the kitchen.
The prices in Midtown are substantially more for similar quality of that offered by the Beacon we had friends there asnd saw there rooms. We stayed at the Woolcott Hotel on 34th Street for 5 nights also and though nice it was not a patch on the Beacon, more expensive BUT you could walk to 42 Street and Madison Square Garden. 
Tips for Beacon use the free internet, walk to metro and use it to go both downtown and also uptown to Harlem directly. Walk to Central Park, walk to the Dakota Building where tragically John LENNON was murdered and Strawberry Fields rememberance area. Get all your groceries at the supermarket opposite Beacon which also has barb B Q chooks hot off the rotisserie for lunch, which are great for sandwiches for kids and pre packed salads very reasonably priced. Walk down to Lincoln centre and checkout movies playing if you want a quiet night in. Go out the hotel turn right heard uptown cross Broadway for 2 blocks and there is Nicks Hamburger joint which has huge menu and great burgers, pasta, fries shakes etc and all reasonable, open 24/7 dinner for 3 of us @ $40. Also chilli and peppers pizza joint in street behind hotel which is really cheap and sells pie by the slice with a nice salad, dinner for 3 of us was @ $25.
Also if you are looking to shop, get the metro up to Harlem. There is Marshalls store there which has heaps of sport gear like Nike, Reebok, And 1, etc etc all cheap and lots of street wear shops stocking levis etc. I priced a pair of nikeair max s in midtown and Macys then went to harlem and got the same shoes for $50 USD less!!!!!!! Also at Macys take your passport in and get a discount card for 10% on all purchases. There are lots of branded clothes and shoes discounted throughout NYC, (according to my 14 year old daughter and lots of nice boutiques in Amsterdam and Columbus near Beacon), also a great flea market on Sunday on West 78 St (I think), which has great jewellery and furs etc, also vintage clothes.
In our opinion if you are visiting NYC and you want safe,clean,friendly and competitively priced accommodation you cant go past the Beacon Hotel.

name: Courtyard Houston Intercontinental Airport
title: “Nice stay”
text: Stayed here for one night, nice hotel, clean room, clean bathroom and that's all im asking for. Only downside?... location, not a single restaurant close by and at nite when your you are starving its disappointing. but other than that everything was good.

name: La Quinta Inn Houston Medical / Reliant Center
title: “Not the quality I expected”
text:
We stayed during the HLSR the March 15 and 16, 2007. It was definitely not the quality we expected. The room was to be non-smoking but it wasn't. I bought a can of lysol to help correct which it did some. Also it was definitely not as clean as it should have been. Hair in the sink, we also found a small pill on the floor (looked to be a cold medicine type pill but who knows). We then sprayed everything in sight with lysol. We only slept there as our days were completely consumed with our HLSR activities. We were scheduled to stay a third night but gave up our reservation and moved to another hotel. Parking is a real problem if there during a busy time as we were. Not enough parking spaces for all the vehicles.
People were parking in the fire zone as no where to park. I definitely wouldn't stay there again. Between cleanliness, the parking, and the smoking room I wouldn't give this hotel a chance again.

name: BEST WESTERN Fountainview Inn & Suites Near Galleria
title: “gute Lage um Houston zu erkunden”
text: Hotel in einem guten sauberen Zustand. Guter und freundlicher Service. Liegt verkehrsguenstig in unmittelbarer Naehe zu einem der Haupt Entertainment und Shoppinggebiete von Houston. Guter Ausgangspunkt um Houston zu entdecken.

name: Hotel Derek Houston Galleria
title: “Perfect!”
text: My friend and I were bridesmaids in our friends wedding and got the bride and groom a room here for $99. We thought it would be a great spot for them to retreat to after the fabulous wedding and house full of family. Someone else also arranged for them to have a car service. We arrived to check in for them and it was awesome! Check in was easy with no line. We go to the elevators and they have infused water which was great to have considering it was summertime. The room was exactly what we reserved - city view. It was awesome. We decorated it for the newly weds and went back to our car. We did call down to the front desk asking for scissors but no one came up as they were too busy to help us. We ended up down there to cut what we needed. We had the valet staff just hold the car out front as we weren't going to be long. It didn't cost anything thank goodness. The newly weds enjoyed the room tremendously and we couldn't be happier. I will definitely book more rooms here.

name: Extended Stay America - Houston - Galleria - Uptown
title: “Awesome service!”
text: Employees Zeba and Ashly at check-in were so helpful and they were so nice the whole time. Room was really clean and the bed was comfy as well. The hotel was very very clean and well presented. Long story short, I was so satisfied with staying here.

name: Residence Inn Houston by The Galleria
title: “Excellent consistent Service & great Location.”
text:
If you are looking out for long stay options in Houston’s; this is the place to leave. I am staying here for past 6 months & do not have any single major complaint. 
 Very friendly, helpful front desk & housekeeping staff makes your stay joyful. Complimentary breakfast has got just enough you need for your daily needs. They have Happy Hour every working day & it’s really refreshing after long office day. They always keep Vegetarian option menu in Breakfast & evening Snacks which is great thing. Rooms are specious & recently they have installed wireless internet to your rooms which makes it very convenient. Internet does get slow at times when you have number of users. 
Only couple of minor points which they can work on is design of Bathrooms (they are old fashioned) & A.C. performance.
For me In all its HOME away from HOME.

name: Andaz 5th Avenue
title: “Hotel agreable”
text: Hotel agréable dans l'ensemble. Le seul gros problème est l'insonorisation extérieur. le double vitrage n'insonorise pas assez les bruits extérieur. En dehors de ce problème, les chambres sont très bien, le service est excellent. Autre bémol le cout du petit déjeuner.

name: Marriott Houston Airport at George Bush Intercontinental
title: “Okay when it's your only option”
text: Arriving 7 hours llate and missing a connection it did the job clean room but some what dated

name: Four Points by Sheraton Houston Southwest
title: “very good location!”
text: this hotel is located in a good area and it is very close to downtown. There was a good price deal and parking is free so it was excellent for us. The hotel offers a pricey breakfast so we didnt eat there. overall it was a good stay and since there are so many places and bakeries in houston we didnt mind having our breakfast out of the hotel.

name: Hilton Houston Plaza/Medical Center
title: “Good, but not Great”
text:
This was the largest hotel room I have ever stayed in. It was a bedroom-living room suite with a bathroom, powder room, and bar.
The good: It was very clean and spacious. Very Hilton. I felt like I needed more people to help me populate all the space I had. The view was spectacular, and I was less than 2 miles from Rice Village.
The bad: The self-parking is a nightmare--the deck is very tight, and may the travel gods have mercy on you if an SUV is barreling down the other way. There is very little of interest to walk to around the hotel. I didn't want to pay for hotel food (and I could find no vending machines), so my options were a rough looking chinese place across the street, or a 3-block walk to the Burger King and Wingstop. Finally, the staff was not particularly friendly or outgoing to me, possibly because I look too young to be a CEO.
In looking at the above, I had to drop my initial rating from 4 to 3 stars. My company paid for my hotel, and after seeing the bill, I would choose another hotel if that money was coming out of my pocket. It was a nice stay, but there were too many holes to recommend them without seeing what else is out there.

name: HYATT house Houston/Energy Corridor
title: “Poor Internet Connectivity”
text: Stayed for about a month... Everything is great except internet connectivity (i give 1 out of 5 rating), the Sleep quality is poor (2 out of 5) and electronic stove does not work properly (2 out of 5). I suggest this place for those who are looking for economical and decent accomdation and for short term. But if you are on a business trip and the need for internet is high..may not be a best choice.

name: Hilton Houston Plaza/Medical Center
title: “5 Stars but almost 4, Hilton Houston Plaza-Houston Medical Center”
text:
Tripadvisor calls this the Hilton Houston Plaza hotel, which is probably the official name. It could also be titled the Hilton Houston Medical Center. It is the closest Hilton to all the large Houston hospitals, including the following: Texas Childrens Hosp, Methodist, U.T. and Herman, Baylor Coll., TIRR/UT Dental, M.D. Anderson Clinic/Hosp, St. Luke's, MDAnderson Mays/ CPB Clinic, Proton Clinic, VA Hosp., and Shriner Hosp. I've probably inadvertently ommitted a few. I asked and the front desk said they had a shuttle that took guests almost anywhere within a two mile radius. If so, that would include all these hospitals. This Hilton is a 20 story tower a few miles southwest of downtown Houston. It has a multi-story parking garage which seems about as safe as any parking garage can be.
 I had an upper floor room with one king bed. The room was beautifully decorated and very clean, as you would expect at a Hilton. Furnishings in the room and fixtures in the bathroom appeared to be new. The bed had 5 fluffy pillows and was very comfortable. The view from my upper floor northwest room was delightful, overlooking Rice University. The digitally controlled heat worked perfectly. (I've included photos for those who want more details.) (Sorry, apparently my photos are in the wrong format. I'll try to add them later.) Other than room service, I had very little time to use the many amenities, so I won't comment on most of them. They have everything you would rxpect in a large Hilton Hotel. I did notice that they had a 1/12th mile outdoor running track on one of the roofs. (See photo.) One Hilton bathrobe was provided for use. The room was $120.00 US. This may have been an off season price. The room service breakfast was about $20.00. It was tasty, delivered hot, and exactly on time. The room key card must be used in the elevator in order for it to function. Although slightly annoying, this is a good safety feature. You can get to the ground floor without your key card.
 Now, why did I almost give 4 stars? I was given my key card at the front desk and went to my upper floor room. The key card did not open my door after repeated tries. I hauled my luggage back down the elevator. While I was at the front desk, two other guests also complained that their cards did not work. Also, I was with a group. We had a total of four rooms. The rooms were separated by 8 floors. This seemed odd and inconvenient because one person reserved all four rooms. Other than these two problems, this was a great experience.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Houston / Bush Intercontinental Airport
title: “Great Service, nice rooms and decent food”
text: stayed here after a long trip and did not want to go out again so ate at the hotel, the food was decent and fairly priced as were the beverages. The room was very nice, clean, well-equipped and comfortable. The shuttle started running at 4:30AM and i caught the first one - the driver was courteous and efficient. Will most likely be staying here for my last night on Houston trips!

name: Courtyard by Marriott Houston Downtown
title: “Downtown Houston Hotel”
text: The hotel is only about 5-6 blocks from the Convention Center and Minute Maid Park. It is an older hotel on the outside but they have updated the exterior. It is a little tight entering and exiting the valet area at the front door because the whole driveway consists of a loop. There are only two individual stations to check in and out at and no counter space for the customer to even set their purse down which made getting my driver’s license and credit card out challenging. The restaurant hours are only in the morning and evening and there is a limit menu and very pricy. However, you can order from the surrounding restaurants to be delivered. Our room was ok, a little outdated. It would have been nice to have something in the room, which most hotels do, describing restaurants or attractions in the area. There was no pen and paper to write on and not even the yellow pages in our room. You are downtown so some of the "fast food" type restaurants close early and the more upscale restaurants are open late. Every restaurant in downtown has good food. My absolute favorite is Sambuca's!!! We didn't have any problems during our stay and overall it wasn't a negative experience. I just think they should manage the room’s contents and updated information for guest better. One cool thing, they have a BIG touch screen in the lobby that you can check weather, find destinations in downtown plus some other goodies.

name: Hilton Houston Southwest
title: “Never Again!!!”
text: We had the worst experienced from this hotel! It was bad that i couldn't wait to share this to all of u planning to visit Texas.I've been to diffrnt hotels ... and Hilton hotels, but boy to my surprise,this hotel is the worst of the worst. On the day of our check-in,i found left over candies,coins & candy wrappers in the drawers,the bedside phone can't even dial-out,and i let that go but the next day,.. it gets worst,HOUSEKEEPING didn't even came to service our room and we we're out from 9:30am till 10pm!! Can u believe that?! I'm a housekeeping supervisor on one of the prestigious hotels and i know a good housekeeping when i see one and boy this hotel diffinitely dont even categorized as 1 star hotel.I even tested the housekeeper on our 3rd day if they will change the sheets, and guess what? They didnt! Even to our last day in the hotel,sheets wasn't change,and we we're there for 5 days.Never again,and never recommend this hotel to any travelers.

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “Great hotel, friendly staff, great location”
text: This is a great new York hotel in a great location. Short walk from central park, quick cab ride from downtown, with lots of great, cheap and authentic eating opportunities nearby. Highly recommended.

name: HYATT house Houston/Energy Corridor
title: “Great staff and accommodations”
text: Just returned from a stay at Hyatt Summerfield, and it was great!! We had 27 rooms booked for my dance team members and families, and everyone enjoyed the stay. The rooms were clean and well-kept, the staff was very accommodating, and everyone got the type room they had booked. That's unusual!! Breakfast was good and cheap! If we return to Katy, TX, we won't hesitate to stay there.

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great hotel, great staff. Can't wait to return.”
text:
We spent 3 nights at the Eventi in a King Deluxe room.
We booked through Magellan Travel and will use this service again! Great rates!
Arrived at hotel in cab. 
Greeted immediately by a porter who showed us to the front desk, offered us water etc.
Check-in was very quick. The man who did the check-in took the time to give us info about the hotel, where things were located. The front desk staff is very knowledgeable. Give them a bit of info on what you want, what type of meal you are looking for and you won't be disappointed with their suggestions.
We called the concierge a few weeks in advance to get some top NYC restaurant ideas and we are so happy we did. The suggestions met our needs and wishes perfectly.
Room is lovely. Modern but comfortable decor. The only thing that needs to be looked at is the lighting in the bathroom. It is terrible for putting on makeup! 
The bed was so comfortable! 
Great view.
Loved the in-room robes!
Only ate breakfast at the hotel restaurant, but it was very good.
I will definitely stay at this hotel again!

name: Courtyard by Marriott Houston Downtown
title: “Houston we have a problem”
text:
I have to start off by saying Houston is a weird place. If you already know this then you will probably have no issues with this hotel. The staff was friendly enough but totally unprofessional, the rooms large enough but starting to show their age, the location is in the only area downtown with something supposedly going on at night but Houston is strange. 
We arrived late in the evening around 8pm and wanted to grab some grub. No-one seems to know anything about this city. The staff told us to go down main street and that there are restaurants all over. All we found were a couple of greasy diners. So then we were told to go to Washington ave, the only nightlife area in the city. No-one knew anything about this area other than it was open late. The hotel was unable to get ahold of a cab and when I managed to flag one down on the street, he didn't know where this area was. Again, there were supposed to be bars all up and down the street but instead there were banks, furniture stores, drycleaners etc. with the odd bar scattered here and there. For the fourth largest city in the US, there is nothing going on! 
If you're a tourist staying in Houston, I'd recommend staying on the outskirts and avoid the city. Another shocker was that there are only 2 country bars in Houston and the one that we tried was not a real country bar. It looks like a great place to live but a horrible place to be entertained.

name: Hilton Houston Plaza/Medical Center
title: “Reasonable but not perfect”
text:
Great staff, clean rooms, but the rooms are not very sound proof. I could hear the guests in the surrounding rooms having conversations. Also, any noise from the hall could be easily heard.
You need to have your hotel key to use the elevator, access the pool and gym. This is a bit of a hassle.
They have a shuttle that will drive and pick you up within a 2 mile radius which is great as it is not very easy to pick up cabs in Houston.
There is nothing nearby if you want to run out for a quick cup of coffee. And beware....coffee in the hotel restaurant is $5.00 per cup!!! While there is a coffee maker in the room, it is pretty weak.

name: BEST WESTERN Plaza Hotel & Suites at Medical Center Houston
title: “Hated the Best Western due to exceptionally poor management.”
text: The management uses the cheapest of the cheap to appoint the hotel. Kitchen had no utinsels, no paper towels. I was told by the hotel manager that if I needed paper towels, I could use kleenex that was provided in the bathroom. The breakfast was the almost non-existent. They have a large dining room with almost no food provided. Their shuttle service is the poorest I've even used in the Houston area. I ended up using the shuttle service from the next door Holiday Inn hotel. The rooms were way overpriced for the service. The hotel could be a very nice place to stay due to its' location and the configuration of the rooms, but the management is so cheap that it makes the stay almost unbearable.

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “Outstanding”
text: My family travelled to NYC in November 2009. We loved everything about the Hotel Beacon. The staff were friendly and helpful, the location is fantastic and in easy access to the subway, restaurants, Central Park and all that the Upper West Side has to offer. We stayed in the 2 bedroom apartment and it felt like a 'home-away-from-home'. The kitchenette is fabulous and you can make good use of both Fairway's and Citarella's located just across the street. There is internet access in the foyer of the hotel and a laundry for longer stays (we were there for 2 weeks). Nobody wanted to leave and we will definitely stay there when we return.

name: John F. Kennedy Inn and Suites
title: “Second Stay as great as first!!!!!”
text: Stayed for a second time upon my return to Houston. Great customer service. Chris Martin, the manager, went out of his way to make sure all was well! Saw him give the same time and concern to other guest. He is the reason we will return, and tell others about our great stay!

name: HYATT house Houston/Galleria
title: “Could Have Been 4 Stars”
text:
Overall the Hyatt House has a lot to like. The rooms were generally clean, a lot of space and a good value. The TV was new, and the WIFI worked well. I had my kids with me this time and the pool was a nice size, and well maintained. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful and the woman who handled the free breakfast was very nice and helpful.
The free breakfast was very good and they also had a cocktail hour with free beer both big pluses. 
The location is near the Galleria and also a couple of highway exit ramps so a pretty good spot. Also lots of restaurant choices nearby. 
My only issue was the house keeping. I had two rooms and when I arrived one of my rooms wasn't ready until after 6pm. The manager ended up cleaning that room. Twice the same room wasn't made up. The staff did make amends are were very apologetic about the problem. My guess was that they were having some kind of problem with the staff on my floor, because overall the hotel was spotless and the staff did a good job on the one room they I had that they did clean. 
In conclusion, I do think that my experience was probably just one of those things that happens sometimes and not a major problem with this particular hotel; nonetheless, I did dock the Hyatt House a star because of it for this trip.

name: Extended Stay America - Houston - Willowbrook - HWY 249
title: “Not the Residence Inn, but I wasn't expecting it to be”
text: Without a doubt, you generally DO get what you pay for. I spent two weeks at this hotel while on a business trip. My choice was driven by price. The front desk staff was courteous, and was attentive to my needs. The room was clean, as were the public areas of the property. The location is nothing special, and lower prices do sometimes attract people that you might not choose to be your neighbors. That said, I never feared for my safety, and I never saw any of the "partying" that another reviewer recently claimed. For what I paid, it was a great stay. It cost me a fraction of what I would have paid at any other hotel in the area. For that, I'm grateful.

name: Sheraton Suites Houston Near The Galleria
title: “Average hotel in a great location!”
text:
I was able to get a great rate for this hotel & I enjoyed my stay. 
Although...in my opinion, this is not a 4 star hotel (as other sites may suggest) Yet, it was still sufficient for my one night stay. The location of this hotel is great if you're looking for a hotel near the galleria mall. It's within walking distance to a Starbucks and has an onsite restaurant. However, I learned the hard way that room service is not 24 hours.
Note: Valet parking is $20.00 & the mini refrigerator is not stocked for (pay per use). This is an older hotel, which the room furniture & decor will show. But, the room is clean & very spacious. I like that the room is separated from the sitting area & hallway (I slept well). Overall, the pros outweigh the cons. In closing..I would stay here again.

name: Days Inn Houston - Galleria Mall
title: “New Management, New Rooms, What a nice place”
text: The hotel rooms are clean and freshly painted, the hotel seems to be completely remodeled. We stayed in three other hotels on our road trip to Houston, and this was by far the nicest. The front desk staff is friendly and hospitable and the location is great. I would reccomend this hotel to anyone.

name: Sheraton Suites Houston Near The Galleria
title: “Great location, OK suites and OK pricing”
text: I stayed in this hotel for 8 nights for a business trip since it was close to were all my team members were staying. The hotel is very well placed, 5 minutes walking distance from The Galleria. There are loads of restaurants around this area as well. The breakfast in the hotel is pretty alright, but the pool is very very small. The rooms are suites and they have a small living area and a bed room. The one TV each in the living area and the bedroom which is pretty good. But the whole hotel has a old feel and really needs renovation. The bar is quite nice as well. They even have a free pick up and drop service in 3 mile radius. Over all a decent stay might stay here again if I get a good deal.

name: Super 8 IAH West / Greenspoint
title: “TripAdvisor works again - another perfect choice”
text:
As part of our recent early November 3-destination trip to Texas (Houston, Dallas and Austin) this hotel was yet another selected with the aid of TripAdvisor reviews. And you know what, it was another perfect choice!
Handy location just 10-12 minutes from Bush Int. Airport, the very nice Greenspoint Mall about the same driving time in the other direction, easy trip to Downton Houston on I45 (about 20-30 minutes, depending on time of day).
Attractive, well-kept building, plenty of free parking, nice pool in sunny spot at the back, and friendly welcome from pleasant staff. Add in the spacious, spotless and perfectly-equipped room, the very useful free business room with no-charge internet and printing, the plentiful free breakfast (just help yourself to whatever you fancy) and you've got yourself the perfect hotel package. 
When you consider the bargain rate (we paid less than $200 all-included for 3 nights) would you really want to consider anywhere else in Houston? Thanks again, TripAdvisor. You've not let me down once yet!

name: Westin Galleria Houston Hotel
title: “Thanksgiving Holiday”
text: This was our first holiday away from home, so the hotel made us feel like we were home. Staff treated us on first name basis and the rates were perfect. I am always looking for specials with this hotel chain and when they do, we always to advantage of it.

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton Houston by the Galleria
title: “Mediocre hotel at best”
text: I found this hotel to be be average. The rooms are huge, but the water pressure was bad in the shower. Room service was bad as well. I received hash browns with my hamburger instead of french fries. The biggest upset was that I think they may have bedbugs. I was bitten all down the leg and arm of the side I was sleeping on. I will not be going back.

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Fantastic nights sleep - Bed and sheets extremely comfortable - Only criticism is that I couldn't buy the comforter.”
text:
The hotel was booked at v short notice (eg the night before arriving) without doing a lot of research and I was pleasantly surprised. Check in was smooth and quick and room service efficient (had ordered a delicious breakfast). The room size is average but adequate for a long weekend. One drawback is that the room doesn't have enough lighting which makes it rather dark. The bathroom is huge but no bath. This didn't bother me as I prefer showers anyway. There are 2 shower heads in the shower, the main, overhead rain shower head had very poor power so one could only use the nozzle shower head. 
The bed (American king size, 6 ft) and bedding were absolutely amazing. So much so that I wanted to buy the comforter (which is available on their website for purchase). Because of time constraints, there was no way that a new comforter could've been delivered in time. I offered to buy the comforter which was on my bed but was told I would have to pay full price for a second hand, used comforter! Bit of an insult to say the least. I declined. 
Apart from that, the service was generally very good. 
The room was relatively clean - dusty in some places, but the bathroom was spotless. 
I would return to this hotel without hesitation due to the comfort of the bed. Lets face it, when one is on holiday in NYC, most of the time is spent either shopping, dining or sightseeing. To come back to a hotel when one can be guaranteed a good nights sleep is second to none in my opinion.

name: Comfort Suites
title: “Great getaway”
text: We stayed for a night here as a getaway as a couple. It was hidden behind the great trees near IAH (Bush Airport). The hotel was clean, staff was pleasant, the bedding was nice and room was clean. Lots of good parking and convenient to the airport in a secure area.

name: Westin Galleria Houston Hotel
title: “Perfect”
text: Location is perfect. Can have a roof over your head. Then shop till you drop. Westin delivers as always.....Will come back again once in Houston...

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “Loved the room and location.”
text:
This hotel was just a few blocks from the subway and Central Park. Amsterdam street is just the next block over and is filled with great shopping and restaurants. Our room had a small kitchenette and across the street was an amazing grocery store so we had the option to eat a few meals in the room to save money. 
The staff was helpful and friendly and the room was clean and attractive.
The only thing to note is that it was crowded with a number of tour groups when we were there.

name: Comfort Suites
title: “Wonderfull welcome”
text: I stayed at this location while going to a class for my work. I was greeted by the courtious staff and made to feel welcome. The rooms were clean and had been recently updated. I got there late and left early but it was a restfull stay. Except for the time I spent studying.

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Well located, great hotel”
text: The Eventi Hotel offers standard excellent service and is well located as most Kimpton Hotels. Located at 6th and W. 30th Street, the hotel is centrally located to lower Manhatten. A subway station is located two blocks away. Reservations were easy online with upgrade offered for a higher floor and a corner room. The front desk staff was efficient and courteous although at times only one person was available to answer guest questions as well as check-in or check-out guests. The room was well appointed. The shower and bathroom were spacious. Management responded to our only concern when the AC was not cooling the room. The staff responded quickly and corrected the problem. Will definitely return to the Eventi.

name: Courtyard Houston Medical Center
title: “Fairly new property, clean and good choice for Medical Center area”
text: I have stayed at the Courtyard in mid March while in town for workshops at MD Anderson. This is a fairly new property (less than 3 years old I believe) across from the Residence Inn. I prefer to be outside the immediate vecinity of the UT Medical Center /MD Anderson etc. because of the bad traffic situation during rush-hour. The hotel is in a quiet area and convenient to several freeways. There is a pharmacy across the street which has a decent convenience food selection. The hotel is standard Courtyard fare/food with good service and new rooms.

name: Houston Marriott Medical Center
title: “Nice hotel for work”
text: Good place to stay for work but i wouldnt vacation here... It's clean, nice staff and i'll be here again weekly for the next year!!

name: Eventi - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Hotel - Great Location”
text: Just stayed here with my Wife and 2 dogs. We spent 3 nights and were treated well the whole time. Nice restaurant. Nice room. Nice staff. Great Location. My wife enjoyed the spa.

name: MainStay Suites Texas Medical Center/Reliant Park
title: “Great combination of price, location and amenities”
text: Good value for the Houston Medical Center location. Within ten minutes or less to MD Anderson Cancer Center. Frequent shuttle to/from MDA and other locations, i.e. grocery stores, airports, etc. Many MDA patients stay here so the hotel is very tuned in to their needs from clean rooms, shuttle, quiet rooms, attentive staff, etc. Ask for medical discount if you are getting treatment. It is lower than other discounts such as AAA, AARP, etc. Washer/dryer on premises is handy for long stays. Hot breakfasts are good tasting. No plastic hockey puck eggs, etc. Lobby and breakfast area is small but adequate. When compared to Staybridge, there are minuses such as floor space of rooms, quality of bkfst, no evening meals. There is no Staybridge close to MDA.

name: Houston Marriott North
title: “NOT a Marriott quality”
text: We stayed here recently as we were attending a wedding and this was the hotel of choice for the event. We are Marriott Rewards members and do stay at Marriotts all over the country. We will NEVER stay at this one again. From the moment we checked in to the moment we left, we never encountered a friendly staff member with the exception of the bartender. The front desk personnel needs either MUCH better training at customer service or be replaced. Frankly, I think replacement would be the better choice. I've never had such a lackluster welcome and each time we passed the front desk the young women were standing together talking with their backs to the lobby and never greeted us (or any other guest)! The rooms were average quality. However, the window tinting was done either by poorly craftsmen or with poor materials or both. It gave the hotel a very cheap impression and caused us to wonder about the rest of the property.

name: Holiday Inn Houston West Energy Corridor
title: “Nice hotel”
text: I've stayed at this hotel for long stays. I think it is a good value option. Very clean and tidy rooms with a modern minimalistic design that have everything. Staff very helpful. The gym and pool are rather tiny though. In general a good option. The restaurant is not so good.

name: JW Marriott Houston
title: “reasonable for business trips”
text: Was there for a conference. The hotel has perfect location for organizing small meetings. The staff was professional. The main advantage is in value for money. The price is quite reasonable (apart from parking) for the amenities.

name: SpringHill Suites Houston Brookhollow
title: “Recently Remodeled”
text: Very nice hotel. We checked our moms in for a retreat night. They really enjoyed their stay. It was recently remodeled and the color scheme is green (nice in my opinion). I really did enjoy the room layout. The front desk was very nice, accomodating and professional (lots of special requests from us to make the night special for our moms). Front desk also allowed a very late checkout which was fabulous. I was very satified and relieved that the stay turned out well.

name: Houston Marriott Medical Center
title: “Fabulous Final Four in Houston”
text: I had the pleasure of staying at the Marriott Medical Center for the Final Four weekend. The staff was extremely courteous and out going to ensure every guest had a positive experience. Check in and Check out was seamless. The room service wa very timely. Hot food was Hot and Cold Food was cold. The bar stayed open late to accomodate the guests after both games. i have already suggested this location for co workers and will be reserving rooms for upcoming Houston Texans football games. This location is only 40 miles from my house, however you feel like you are on vacation and not business when you stay there. Keep up the great service. I am a Marriott Platinum member and this property provides better than Platinum service.

name: Doubletree Houston Intercontinental Airport
title: “The Best DoubleTree Hilton Hotel in Hotel”
text: This DoubleTree Hotel is one of the Best in the United States. They welcome you to the hotel by offering you chocolate chip cookies which is one of their welcoming you to the Doubletree Hilton Hotel in Houston, TX. The staff makes you feel welcome right off the bat. The rooms are superb and comfortable especially with their King Size Pillows on the bed also the furniture is very comfortable and very relaxing. The restaurants in the hotel has everything that you would want. Thanks for a great stay!

name: Doubletree Houston Intercontinental Airport
title: “Mind blowing service”
text: The rooms were clean and nice which we expected from a double tree. We stayed here for a week and the staff met all of our requests. The personnel at the front desk were very sweet. The servers in the restaurant were very nice too. The restaurant has a good menu, there is something for everyone. Although the room service menu was wanting. They never had what we wanted from the menu. The hotel shoppe is well stocked too.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Houston by the Galleria
title: “No issues!!”
text: Stayed here on a business trip September 18 - 22. Clean, very modern room. Well laid out and all the usual amenities. Staff was nice and quite helpful. As the previous post indicated, $15/night parking. My only hitch was that there multiple times my parking pass didn't work... but a quick buzz to the desk (button right at the card reader) and I was in/out in a flash.

name: Crestwood Suites Houston 290-Galleria
title: “Worst Experience ever”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 5 nights and I had such a bad experience with this hotel. It was the worst hotel I have ever visited because no one came to clean the room for 5 nights we stayed at the place. Although Coffee was available in the morning, for 5 nights we were without any person cleaning up our room. We had to go to the Service Counter in the front of the hotel for Shampoos, Coffee for the room. Hope you fix this in the near future.

name: Holiday Inn Houston Northwest Willowbrook
title: “Texas hospitality”
text: I'm here for 1 week and it is now my second day. My luggage has been lost by the airline. There is a clerk by the name of Gary that does a great job at welcoming you. He has gone the extra mile to provide me with extra toiletries until my bags arrive. The room is nice and clean. The only negative is that the turn into the Hotel comes up quick and if you miss it, you will have to circle around always due to the one way.

name: Hilton Houston NASA Clear Lake
title: “A little far out...but very nice all the same”
text:
We booked this hotel for the night before we left out of Houston Hobby Airport. I got a great deal through through Expedia, but we ended up driving a lot farther than we intended to. However the hotel was very nice and we got what we wanted--which was a good night's sleep in a clean hotel. The decor is pretty cool...kind of space age which befits the hotel's location next to NASA. The rooms were clean and comfortable, albeit a bit tired. Of course, "tired" at Hilton is much different than "tired" at a lower ranked hotel chain. I'd pick this hotel over a brand new lower ranked chain any day.
It was very tranquil around the hotel even though it sits on a main thoroughfare. We had some difficulty finding the hotel as the roads were under construction and re-naming! We had to make a couple of calls to the front desk in order to get going in the right direction, but they were very patient with us. The morning commute to Hobby was quick though, but it was a Saturday. I wouldn't recommend staying here if you have a M-F morning flight.
All in all, I would definitely recommend this hotel.

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “Great hotel in a great Manhattan location!”
text:
I really enjoyed my stayed there! 
The hotel has oversized room and suites that are perfect to travel with a family. I was travelling with my family (2 adults and 2 young kids) and I reserved a suite who was perfect for us. The suite was large with a kitchenette. 
The hotel location (Upper West side) is great with many restaurants, central parks, natural history museum and stores at walking distance. It's a one minute walk to the subway station who go directly to Times Square (express line). 
I personally prefer this location where real New-Yorker leave. I’m not a fan of Times Square area hotels; too crowdy and noisy with expensive restaurants (and not good!) dedicated to serve mainly tourists visiting Time Square. 
The restaurant of the hotel is OK for a quick meal or breakfast (you will need to go out the hotel to access the restaurant - no direct access from the hotel lobby). 
The hotel have no parking; in this area the cost for parking is $47/day; it’s NYC….

name: Hilton Houston NASA Clear Lake
title: “So Not Worth The Money”
text:
We didn't mind paying more money in order to stay at a nicer hotel, but we feel like we didn't get our money's worth at the Hilton NASA Clear Lake.
You think in this day and age guests would receive free WI-FI, but that's not the case at the Hilton! Talk about getting nickel & dimed. They wanted $11 per day for internet access. How cheap and tacky is that? The lobby looks like something from the 1970's and there's a shop that practices the worst kind of price gouging you've ever seen.
GUEST ROOM: We ordered a lake view room with a King size bed. The view out the window was the parking lot and bridge, but the river was visible if you positioned your body against the window and looked out to your right.
The room had no microwave or little refrigerator. The bathroom was so small two adults couldn't be in there at the same time. The door hit the shower curtain rod preventing it from fully opening and creating a roadblock by the toilet. The trash cans were tiny and heavy. The mirrors had hand prints on them and the carpets were stained and soiled. The air conditioning worked but not very well and the room was always warm.
LUNA RESTAURANT: Overpriced menu. If you order an item, you get that item: no garnish, no frills, nothing for free. The wait staff didn't speak English and brought me a soda when I ordered a beer. When I pointed that out I was made to feel like a jerk in my own country. My wife found a hair in her salad. The took that off that bill.
POOL: It's only five feet deep. And it's not very big either. No outside food or drinks allowed; its all about selling you their overpriced food and drinks. Beware of locals crashing the pool party and attempting to charge drinks to your room. 
HOTEL STAFF: The English speaking ones were somewhat friendly. We requested a wake-up call but never got it. Had to argue at check out time over a bar tab that was no way mine; we ordered 4 or 5 drinks, but not 16 of them. They removed the charge but only after much protest. I have no proof but my gut tells me the staff is letting family and friends drop by and party. Hallways didn't feel safe at night with non- English speaking drunk people roaming around.
Beware of the "fitness center" which is a few treadmills in a hot room and the "business center" which are two slow computers that are pay per per use-again no free internet. and no free printer. How cheap can you be Hilton? The money we paid for the rooms and we don't even get sugar packets for our room coffee machine. 
Oh, and the TV was a joke too. The remote didn't work well and there was a delay between making a selection and input on the screen. So putting on a channel took 3 or 4 tries because by the time you clicked 1-6 the set would go to channel 1. And the picture quality was dark and could not be corrected with the remote. Its almost like they turned it down in order to preserve the life of the TV.
The hotel is not smoker friendly and there are no ashtrays anywhere.

name: The Iroquois
title: “Quiet and Close to everything”
text:
We just returned from 5 days in New York City during the Thanksgiving holiday. My husband and an 18 year old daughter, and 21 year old son. 
We all loved the cozy, quiet hotel. It is close to everything we needed and not a large loud chain hotel. The staff was very helpful and friendly. We had two adjoining rooms and they were all we hoped for. We will stay there on our next visit!

name: Hilton Houston NASA Clear Lake
title: “Great view”
text: Lake view is wonderful. The room was large but dated. The hotel is beng remodeled so should be much nicer soon.

name: Houston Marriott North
title: “not worth the money”
text:
I thought I'd written a lengthy review (complaint) about this hotel but I see it's not here.
Don't order the room service late at night and if you do (and they don't bring it....and don't really care or apologize for that), make SURE they don't charge you for the food THEY DIDN'T bring!!!
There are so many rip-offs about this motel, I can't even remember them all. It's the most overpriced place I've ever stayed and they nickel and dime you for EVERYthing.
I have to say the cleaning staff was very nice and did their job well but everything else about the place is a bunch of overpriced pomp!!!

name: The Iroquois
title: “hotel nel cuore di manhattan”
text: Sono appena tornato da new york e devo dire che the iroquois è veramente un ottimo hotel. è situato a soli 2 isolati da times square e il rumore non si sente per nulla. Alloggiavamo nella suite da 4 persone ( prezzo non esorbitante ma abbordabile se da dividere) e non posso trovare alcun difetto. Il personale era disponibilissimo e nel prezzo della camera è incluso 1 new york pass ( per camera) per accedere gratis a empire, rockfeller, ellis island, moma e metropolitan. E' bellissimo la sera girare per times square e , quando si è veramente stanchi dopo decine di chilometri a piedi, sapere di avere l'hotel a pochi passi. Consiglio di andare a new york e consiglio the iroquois. Complimenti..

name: Doubletree Houston Intercontinental Airport
title: “Great place to stay or have an event.”
text:
This is a great hotel to stay in or plan an event. The staff helped me replan my entire wedding in less than a month and were there every step of the way.
I have to say the staff went above and beyond to make sure my wedding was nothing less than perfect. Words are still not enough to express the way I feel. I will recommend the Double-tree Hotel to everyone I know that is planning an event and to stay. The rooms were very nice and the entire staff service was excellent. 
I look forward to staying there again.

Address: '5011 Westheimer Road at Post Oak Blvd.'
name: Westin Oaks Houston at the Galleria
title: “Loved the visit to the Westin and the Galleria.”
text: Took my two grandkids on a shopping trip. The stay was pleasant and enjoyable. I felt safe in the hotel and pool area and the staff was wonderful. We went down to the Galleria for shopping and when we got tired, came back to the room for a rest. The rooms were clean, and the view was wonderful. Had a great time and the grandkids are asking me when I am taking them to Houston again. Thanks for a wonderful visit. Norma L. Castellano

name: Inn at the Ballpark
title: “Not very kid friendly~”
text: There isn't a pool on the property. Nice decor for business trips, very bland. Love the shuttle service and free tickets to the aquarium. Nice getaway for grownups only. Not a bad place to stay, just isn't somewhere I will bring my family again.

name: Inn at the Ballpark
title: “Fantastic place for a baseball weekend”
text: My son and I travel each year to a different city for a baseball weekend. This was the best hotel for this sort of thing we have ever stayed at. The hotel is one block from Minute Maid stadium, and it has completely embraced the team. The entire decore is centered on baseball right from the statue of a pitcher in full wind up at the entrance to the details in the rooms. The food is good, and the service excellent. Highly recommended for a baseball trip.

name: JW Marriott Houston
title: “Great Location in Houston”
text: Great Location, Great food in the hotel and a nice staff. The only negative is the traffice around the hotel, but you do not need a car because tou can walk to a ton of restaurants and shops.

name: Crowne Plaza Houston Downtown
title: “Enjoyed our stay”
text: Staff are very courteous and helpful, front desk, valets, bellmen, etc. Never had to wait to get our vehicle out of valet. Even when we didn't call ahead it only took a minute or two for staff to bring our vehicle. Beds are comfy and hotel is clean and well maintained. Pool area is nice but only complaint is that the water in the pool was very cloudy and didn't look too clean. Overall we enjoyed our stay and I would stay here again.

name: The Lancaster
title: “Wonderful Boutique Hotel in the middle of Houston's best sights”
text: Although in the middle of the "city" here is a tucked away interlude from the hustle and bustle outside the walls of the Lancaster. Lovely accommodations, clubby restaurant with deliciously prepared foods and attentive, but not too, waitstaff. All with friendly and helpful staff all around. The shuttle was a godsend to get us to and from (in our case) church with no waiting or hassle. The theater was just a walk down the block. Many sights easily accessible for sightseers. You will not be disappointed with your stay! PS: We have stayed many times before, this time it was with a girlfriend. She can't wait to come back with her husband.

name: Hyatt Regency Houston
title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: The hotel was beautiful. Staff were friendly and helpful. The room was comfortble and clean. There was a safe in the room that was locked by the previous guest. I called about it and someone came to take care of it within 10 minutes. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone.

name: Holiday Inn Hotel & Suites Houston Medical Center
title: “Good as any other Holiday Inn”
text: The whole family stayed here coming from abroad for a cousin wedding celebration. We got a great price, and the hotel was perfect for our needs. Helpful staff, good rooms with flat TV and FREE internet. Some got a mini kitchen even. Kids went to the pool, mamas to Galleria, so everybody was happy. Overall a great stay.

name: Doubletree Houston Intercontinental Airport
title: “Nice Hotel - enjoyed our stay”
text: The hotel was very nice, a 3.5 star at minimum. The rooms were clean and up to date. The beds, sheets and pillows were wonderful! Check in went well. We were able to check in 3 hours early and were given hot cookies at check in. We got a good deal booking directly on Doubletree's website. I was impressed with the business center. It was located in a room with glass walls overlooking the pool area. There were 3 computers, a printer, paper and pens. The washer and dryer came in handy also. The only thing I noticed that I though could use improvement was the carpet in the hallway on our floor seemed a little old. I would stay here again and recommend it to anyone.

name: Comfort Suites Hobby Airport Houston
title: “Very nice and a bargain for the $$”
text: Although the area around the hotel is not the best, I did not feel unsafe staying here. The staff were very friendly and helpful and the hotel is well maintained and comfortable. Although it was close to the airport, I recall only hearing one plane and so the room was quiet. The breakfast is nice and tasty.

name: The Setai Fifth Avenue, a Capella managed Hotel
title: “This place will ruin you for other hotels.”
text:
There are plenty of nice hotels in New York; what sets the Setai apart is the service. The fact that things like in-room refreshments and internet are free really make you feel like a real guest. Yes, I know nothing is "free" - you pay for it one way or another. But I appreciate the honesty of including the details in the price of the room instead of charging $5 for water like many other hotels. 
They really go out of there way to make your stay special. I was there for my birthday, and they surprised me with Champagne and treats in my room one afternoon when we got back from lunch!

name: The Iroquois
title: “L hotel dei puffi”
text: Io e mia moglie siamo stati in quest hotel per 3 giorni pagando tariffa intera. Al momento Dell arrivo tutti cordiali e simpatici e ci informano che avendo prenotato attraverso american express ci spettava un upgrade della stanza. Considerate che l upgrade si traduceva con una stanza dove non era neppure possibile aprire le valigie. Un letto piccolo in uno spazio che forse arrivava a 12 -15 mq. Compreso il bagno. Certo tutto pulito ma per il resto meglio guardarsi intorno. Il concierge ci ha dato dei consigli (su ns richiesta) ma anche in questo caso la scelta e' stata pessima. Al ristorante ci hanno addirittura addebitato la "gratuity" due volte. Accortomi della cosa si sono scusati in mille lingue ma la volonta' era evidente così come la conoscenza del cameriere con il concierge...abbiamo speso circa 400 usd a notte ma, credo che l hotel sia ben lontano dagli standard che ci si aspetta vedendo il sito. Infine la ciliegina: dovendoci recare la mattina presto all aeroporto, ho chiesto se secondo loro era un problema trovare un taxi alle 6 di mattina. Mi hanno ovviamente proposto un limousine service dicendo che la mattina così presto non e' facile trovare taxi. Sono uscito alle 5.45 e davanti l hotel ce n erano una decina.. La trovo una caduta di stile. Non lo consiglierei nel senso che il rapporto qualità prezzo e' pessimo.

name: Omni Houston Hotel
title: “Excellent”
text: My husband and I stayed here last Saturday evening. Upon check in the desk clerk had inquired about our visit. Was there anything special, business trip or pleasure? I stated we are celebrating our 11th wedding anniversary. He said he would like to send to our room at bottle of wine and a fruit platter compliments of the hotel. Asked when I would like it delivered. We went to dinner and when we returned the wine and fruit were there waiting on us. Such a lovely surprise.

name: Hilton Americas - Houston
title: “Great location next to convention center, but Executive Lounge is lacking.”
text:
This was a weekend trip to see some music, so I wasn't expecting much in terms of the hotel. When I checked in, I was not given the executive room that I originally booked. Thankfully, I remembered that I should have access to the lounge and they quickly corrected the mistake. No worries. The room was big and comfortable and I had a slight view of the Toyota Center.
Wanting a pre-show snack, I went to the Executive Lounge and was amazed at the space - it was huge! However, it was empty. No body was up there and there was a plate of 4 cookies, some snack mix and a box full of sodas and water. There was a bartender, but there was a charge for alcoholic drinks?!
It seems I missed the evening reception from 5p-7p where they serve complimentary hors d'oeuvres, snacks & sodas. Perhaps I've been spoiled by other executive lounges, but my assumption was free beer and decent nibbles into the evening. My mistake. At least I thought the breakfast would be worthwhile. Nope. Continental Breakfast in every sense of the word. Hard boiled eggs, grits/oatmeal, cereal, juices, soda, and fruit. 
Suffice it to say that I was not impressed by the executive lounge. Otherwise, this is a decent hotel with the level of service you would expect from the Hilton brand.

name: The Iroquois
title: “Perfektes kleineres Haus mit großen Zimmern”
text: Rundrum empfehlenswert - ein riesiges sauberes, geräumiges Zimmer (Flachbildfernseher, Bügelbrett, Bügeleisen, Safe, kleiner Sekretär, tolle Matratze, Kühlschrank, WLan kostenlos), toller Service, Super Concierge, sauber, 1 Block vom Time Square entfernt, die 44 th Strasse ist eine ruhige Nebenstrasse zwischen der 5 th Ave. und 6 th Ave. U-Bahn ca. 300 m am Bryant-Park! Gerne wieder!"

name: Holiday Inn Hotel & Suites Houston Medical Center
title: “Holiday Inn, my choice of hotels in M.D. Anderson medical center area”
text: The Holiday Inn and Suites, Houston Medical Centre, is my first choice hotel in the MD Anderson Medical Center area. We have stayed at three hotels in the area: the Best Western, the Rotary Hotel ( owned by the Marriott), and the Holiday Inn. I prefer the atmosphere of the Holiday Inn--friendly, but not intrusive. The physical surroundings are fine, the shuttle convenient (plus one could walk to the MD Anderson main campus), the restaurant very acceptable, and the parking--super easy. No need to park in a parking garage. If you are an MD Anderson patient, be sure to give them your patient number to obtain a discount. We'll stay there again instead of begging for a reservation at the Rotary Hotel.

name: Holiday Inn Hotel & Suites Houston Medical Center
title: “Very friendly staff!”
text: Good proximity to Medical Center. Staff very helpful and friendly, especially Maria, Vilma Chano and Don at the cafeteria. Thanks for such a wonderful stay!

name: The Iroquois
title: “Ein perfekter Stützpunkt für Manhattan-Urlauber”
text:
Um es vorwegzunehmen: Der einzige Nachteil am Iroquois ist der Name - praktisch jeder (Taxifahrer, Bus-Chauffeure, Portiers, etc.) spricht es anders aus. Das kann kurz zu babylonischer Sprachverwirrung führen, daher lohnt es sich, den Namen ggf. schriftlich mit sich zu führen.
Im Übrigen lässt sich über das Iroquois nur Positives berichten: in der 44. Straße West gelegen befindet man sich fußläufig zum Times Square, zur Union Station, zum Central Park und zu den sonstigen Sehenswürdigkeiten in Mid Town. Dabei sind die Zimmer (für New Yorker Verhältnisse) groß genug und komfortabel eingerichtet. Insbesondere für den Sommerurlauber erweist es sich dabei als Vorteil, dass jedes Zimmer eine individuell einstellbare Klimaanlage hat. Und in New York ist es ein zusätzlicher Vorteil, dass die meisten Zimmer zu (eher ruhigeren) Hinterhöfen Fenster haben als zur unruhigen Vorderfront.
Alles in allem: Sehr empfehlenswert

name: The Iroquois
title: “Iroquois Toplage in New York”
text:
Das Iroquois liegt in Top Lage in New York, innerhalb von wenigen Minuten ist man am Times Square oder auch am Rockefeller Center.
Wir waren 11 Tage dort und vollkommen zufrieden.
Es ist ein kleines, beschauliches Haus in einer nicht so viel befahrenen Staße in New York. Netter Service und ein sehr freundliches Team sind im Hotel jederzeit sehr bemüht.
Top Preis- Leistungsverhältnis, die Zimmer sind nicht sehr groß, aber das ist halt typisch für New York.
Werden gerne wieder in diesem Hotel absteigen wenn wir in New York sind.

name: The Iroquois
title: “Iroquois”
text: Het iroquois hotel is een mooi hotel in een relatief rustige straat in het Theatre district, twee blokken vanaf Times Square; zeecentraal gelegen, dus. De kamer was wat klein, maar zag er goed uit, evenals de badkamer, hoewel het gebruik van de douche nogal onduidelijk was door de vreemde kraan, die men erg hard uit de muur moest trekken. De kamer werd goed schoongehouden en 's avonds lag er meestal (!) een chocolaatje op ons kussen. Al met al een goed adres, behalve dan de enorme geluidsoverlast van (waarschijnlijk) het ventilatiesysteem, dat de hele nacht doorronkte als een goederentrein. Een ander systeem, misschien was het de lift, deed het meubilair schudden als het geactiveerd werd. Gelukkig had ik oordoppen bij me, anders had ik geen oog dicht gedaan! Maar misschien zijn niet alle kamers zo rumoerig. We hadden ook geen uitizcht: we keken uit op een zwarte muur!

name: Hilton Americas - Houston
title: “Great Hotel Experience”
text: My stay at the Hilton Americas Houston was an absolute pleasure. The entire staff of this property really seems to understand how to treat its guests. With its great location, excellent restaurants and staff, I was very happy with my stay. The rooms are newly renovated and the beds are so comfortable. I would place it my "Top Ten" places to stay.

name: JW Marriott Houston
title: “Awesome!”
text: This is an awesome hotel, right across the street from the Galeria mall. The room was nice, clean and the bed very comfortable. The fitness center rivals that of any health club and the pool is indoor/outdoor. Overall, great hotel in a nice area. I highly recommend it.

name: Hilton Americas - Houston
title: “It's average.....”
text: This is in a good location for the downtown, convention centre and sports arenas.
