But otherwise it is pretty average in all respects, the rooms, the decor etc. there is a pool hidden on the top floor with views over Houston. I probably would not choose to stay here unless it was convenient for an event, which seems to be the key purpose for the hotel

name: Omni Houston Hotel
title: “Excellent!!!”
text:
Stopped in Houston for a family wedding which was at the Omni Hotel. We stayed for 3 nights and the hotel was outstanding. The parking is a bit tricky as the Valet is expensive and the close self parking garage is over 16 a night, however, there is a free garage in the back of the hotel and the front desk advised me of the free parking at check-in and gave time to move my car without charging me which was nice. The garage in the back is much closer then it appears.
We got a corner room which was very spacious and the bathroom was very big which allowed for both me and my wife to get ready at the same time.
The staff was very friendly and the cleaning service was outstanding.
The hotel has a nice breakfast/lunch restaurant however, it is a bit pricy. The bar is small but very friendly and fairly fast service. The Black Swan is a night club/bar on the lower level opened on friday and saturday nights which is a lot of fun.
The pool area is nice with two large pools and it stays open till 11 at night which is a nice bonus.
Every weekday morning I had a copy of USA TODAY waiting at my door.

name: JW Marriott Houston
title: “Very comfortable!!”
text: For my first visit to Houston, I couldn't have picked a better hotel. Don't pay for valet or garage parking, park in their free parking next to the Walgreens on Sage Road, which is on the side of the hotel. The hotel staff was friendly, and the king guest room was spacious and beautifully decorated. I was on the 14th floor which gave a beautiful view. I was able to actually see my car in the parking lot outside of my window. There is an A/V jack on the side of the television just in case you would like to bring a DVD player, or you can pay $12.99 for a pay per view movie. The toiletries are upscale, and the large spa like shower head gives a wonderful shower. The best thing about the room is the bed, the bed, the bed!!! I know there are about 8 pillows already on the bed, and two more in the closet.

Address: '5011 Westheimer Road at Post Oak Blvd.'
name: Westin Oaks Houston at the Galleria
title: “Shame on Westin II”
text:
Originally I was thrilled knowing I was staying at the Westin connected to the Galleria. Must be wonderful, right? Wrong. I went with my husband who attended a 2 day education seminar, and my plan was to retail my way around the mall. I absolutely loved it that I never had to go outside in the heat to make it back to my hotel, nor did I have to worry about parking. That was all I was really happy about.
The first night, I attempted to sleep in the "Heavenly" "pillow-top" bed and I must say it was the opposite of heavenly and the pillow top wore off long before we were there. It was extremely hard which I probably could have handled on its own, but the air conditioning was what really kept me awake. It was nice and cool in the room, but it was so very loud. I probably could have slept better in my car with the window down, with the car going 90 mph. I had never heard anything like it. I could barely hear the person on the other end of the phone or watch TV while the a/c was running. I dealt with it the next night with the same results. The next morning I called "service express" which is the front desk and I asked him if we could possibly obtain another mattress as the one we had was very hard. He said, "That is the only kind of mattress we have." I chose not to argue and endure it one more night.
If we ever have the need to go to this facility again for education hours, I will have to pass. Very sad.

name: Hyatt Regency Houston
title: “Wish I'd stayed at the Hilton”
text: Just checked out of the Houston Hyatt Regency Hotel. We stayed three nights, flying in from New Hampshire to see Constantine Maroulis starring in the Toxic Avenger at the Alley Theatre. The show was fabulous. Our hotel room was clean where it really mattered to me which is the bed and the bathroom. however there was a significant build up of dust on the furniture and the coffeemaker. We were awakened this morning at 9:00 by the maid asking when we'd be leaving. I found that to be quite rude. The structure of the hotel is pleasing to the eye, but not condusiveto sound absorption. The noise in the lobby traveled and was audible until way after midnight. Wifi is not free and bottled water is available in the rooms at 2:50 for for 12 ounces. Would think that a reputable hotel chain would include wifi in the price of the room (not cheap) and make bottled water available at a reasonable price to it's patrons. Also, there is absolutelynothing to do in Houston. I will not be returning.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Houston Galleria Area
title: “Value Destination in Upscale Location”
text: I stayed here in early April for 2 nights because all the other hotels in the Galleria area were $200 and up. $130 got me a nice room, the usual ok La Quinta breakfast, and a nice pool area. Computer with free internet access in lobby. There was no hot water one morning because the boiler wasn't working. Overall, a good stay for the price.

name: Club Quarters in Houston
title: “Club Quarters”
text:
Very good value for the money. May want to bring your own pillow; theirs provide no support. Room was just big enough to include double bed that you could walk around, small desk to work on and a side chair. Bathroom was very compact as well. May not be ideal for larger people (I'm small). Irons and ironing boards available upon request.
Instead of ice machines, they offer bottles with caps for you to fill at the chilled water station located on each floor.

name: Omni Houston Hotel
title: “Gem near everything.”
text: We visit Houston to see our daughter frequently and we always stay here. The hotel is an oasis of quiet and nature in the middle of the busiest part of town. Our room overlooks memorial park. the service is great and the room is dark, cool and comfortable. We invariably sleep well. Try it.

name: Embassy Suites Houston - Near the Galleria
title: “Swans - what else can I say”
text: This is a great property for Embassy Suits, all the normal things you have come to expect from this Hilton Brand but with a twist... SWANS IN THE LOBBY. The rooms clean very comfortable two very large led tvs. Chair and pull out couch one of the best in comfort. Cooked to order breakfast, etc in mornings. This is a perfect hotel for business or family on a short getaway and did I mention the Swans - you just have to go and see - another added plus, lots of resturants near hotel and oh yes the GALERIA. Go shopping. A great overal hotel in a great location. The staff, the best!

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Houston Energy Corridor
title: “Feb - March”
text: Complaints: hot water sporadic in the mornings, internet slow, sound and smells travel between rooms. But overall great stay. I'd definitely stay there again. Thanks!!

name: Homewood Suites Houston near the Galleria
title: “Nice amenities, Staff went out of their way”
text: THe rooms are very comfortable two-room suites. The outer room has a decent, serviceable kitchen (full-size fridge, garbage disposer, dishwasher, silverware, plates, glasses, basic cooking pots, a corkscrew even), fold-out sofa, table and chairs, tv and dresser. The inner room has a comfortable bed, large bathroom, vanity area, tv and dresser. Lots of electrical outlets, lots of storage space. Clean comfortable rooms, minimal noise passed between rooms. Very quiet. But what made this place really special was the staff. We were here for a family event and had about 7 or 8 rooms total (not enough for the hotel to think we were big-time guests or anything). Everybody went out of their way to accommodate every request. I was really impressed. At times the front desk ca be a little slow; but that's only because they are making sure that the person in front of them is completely satisfied before they move on to you and your request. The location is fantastic. There is little to no public transportation in Houston, but since there is lots of shopping, etc. close by, this is a place you could stay without a car.

name: Hotel ZaZa Houston
title: “Always love the Zaza”
text:
I've stayed at the Zaza in Dallas a few times, so it was nice to add the Houston location to my Zaza list (apparently I have a Zaza list). What excited me about this Zaza was the balconies - fresh air in a hotel is always a big plus. My only issue is that if you have a room on the lower floors (4th and below) most of your view is of the roof and the AC units. Also, there is noise, so it's not as lovely as I expected.
Otherwise, awesome hotel. Clean, modern, and quirky. Restaurant was pretty good and room service was speedy. The bed was comfortable - so comfortable, that I slept for ten hours straight. Woot.

name: Homewood Suites Houston near the Galleria
title: “Top Notch, Great Staff”
text:
My first time staying at a Homewood in many years of travel. It is great hotel, with a very friendly staff and nice clean rooms. As a business traveler that travels to the same location a number of times it is nice when the staff recognizes you and calls you by name. 
There are many other advantages: 
1. Happy hour in the lounge from 5:30 - 7:30 with food and drink. 
2. Good restaurants with in walking distance
3. Free parking for Hilton Honors Gold and Platinum members
4. Free WiFi
5. Walk to mall
6. Offer free gym passes to a full gym about .5 miles away
Recommend highly for business or personal.

name: Homewood Suites Houston near the Galleria
title: “Great value for your money”
text:
We stayed 5 nights for New Years Eve in the Homewood Suites by Hilton near the Galleria. We were 5 in one suite and we fit really comfortable. We had 2 rooms with 2 bathrooms and a living room with one sofa bed. Also you have a kitchenette in the room with refrigerator, toaster and cutlery, that you can use if you can’t catch the cheap but fair breakfast or the light dinner that they offer for free, with the always funny and kind Mr. Evaristo looking the way to make you fell comfortable. 
The location couldn’t be better. Walking distance to the Galleria, really easy way to take the highways and lots of restaurants around. 
I would definitely say there again.

name: Hilton Houston North
title: “hilton houston north”
text: i am a hilton diamond memeber and i have been staying at the hitlon houston north, greenspoint dr in houston tx every 2 weeks for approxiamtely 15 months. i have to say that i have stayed in many properties, hilton, marriott and starwood. but the hilton houston north far exceeds any expectations. i met the guest services manager over a year ago, gino quintana who assured me when i had a few special requests that they would all be fulfilled. well he wasn't wrong. everything he said they would do they did. since then i have become friends withn a mjarotiy of the staff and gino makes sure they take very good care of me. the restaurant is a#1 and the vino bar is a great place to hang out, whether for drinks or for dinner. the restaurant and wait staff are fantastic. my room is always ready on time, no matter when my arrival and the concierge loung is one of the best. i would not think of staying at another property in hosuton, even if i was on the other side of town. gino is by far the best i have met in the business and his staff and he should be recognized for their efforts.

name: Hyatt Regency Houston
title: “Some good, some bad”
text:
Stayed here for 5 nights for business in November 2009. Overall, I'd rate the hotel as average... 
The Good:
1) Room appeared to be recently upgraded. Lots of space, flat screen TV, good sized bathroom. 
2) Location: Working downtown, this hotel was very conveniently located for getting to work. It is tunnel-connected so you do not need to go outside if the weather is not good.
3) Staff were all very friendly and pleasant to deal with
The Bad:
1) Noise level: The hotel is designed with an "open concept", so the hallways all open to the center and look down to the lobby. This makes for a interesting look, but it is definitely not helpful for noise levels in the rooms. I was on the 16th floor, and every night I could clearly hear noise from the lobby-bar on the 1st floor. It wasn't horrible, but it was still a bit annoying and I imagine it would be worse on lower floors.
2) Elevators seemed unreliable. On the night I checked in, none of the elevators were working, which meant using the freight elevator to get my bags up and then walking down the stairs to get down for dinner. They were fixed by the next day, but it still wasn't great to see them down and have to use a dingy freight elevator to get upstairs.
3) Service in the lobby-bar - On my first night, I decided to go for a "quick" dinner in the lobby-bar. For whatever reason, my food took almost 1.5 hours to get to me, and the restaurant/bar were half empty (it was a Sunday). However, in the hotel's favour, the waitress gave me the whole meal for free without me even asking/complaining which was nice.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Houston Channelview
title: “Great Road Trip Break”
text:
We stayed in Room 303 for one night on 03/10/2001, 2 adults and our 6 yr old daughter.
This hotel is completely non-smoking which put a big smile on our faces. It is new, clean and bright. We got a fantastic rate from hotwire and even had free internet and a decent breakfast. Employees were courteous and attentive to our needs.
Overall, it was a nice place to break journey on our way to Baton Rouge. If you are a family looking for a long term stay to explore Houston, I have to say that it is far from city center. We did not mind the "refinery view" and the highway as we just needed a basic, clean place to rest for one night. Overall, I would recommend this hotel for road warriors.

name: Omni Houston Hotel Westside
title: “Fine for business”
text:
Room a little dated - could do with all-round renovation. Sleep not helped by aircon that was either hurricane or tornado strength and loudness. Staff friendly and efiicient and a pleasant bar.
Feel a bit mean - but really no better than average for this type of hotel.

name: Club Quarters in Houston
title: “Mixed bag”
text: Booked this property at what I thought was a good rate - should have shopped more as there were 4 star properties for less in nicer neighborhoods. The lobby is charming, rooms are small but nicely appointed. Surprised to find my king bed room was actually two twins shoved together without anything to hold them together to make a good sleeping surface -- this was definitely not a king bed, so don't book room 618. The walk to the convention center takes you through some dicey areas, but they do have a car service available. WiFi in the lobby only, not in the rooms - not good.

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “We will be back!”
text:
Just returned from 6 nights at the Beacon (May 1-7, 2004). Our room was a GIGANTIC deluxe king room with kitchenette. It was very handy to have fridge and microwave for restaurant leftovers. The stove burners shorted out at times, but worked well enough for our purposes. No view, but they offered to move us to a view room when it came available next day. The room was very clean and quiet except during concerts at the Beacon Theater directly underneath us.
The price was 1/3 less than a kitchenette suite in the Doubletree Times Square, with a much nicer neighborhood and ambience. Friendly concierge, outstanding location with museums, shops, Central Park, and cafes in walking distance. The rest of New York easily reached by subway. We got 7 Day Unlimited Metro Cards for $21 and rode all over. We have visited the city many times before, but never overnight. We did a lot, but missed a lot and will be back to the Beacon for more.

name: Omni Houston Hotel
title: “Just what we needed”
text: I stayed at the Omni Houston in July for my cousin's birthday getaway--gotaway from our husbands, jobs and kids. Since we were inducted into the world of "SPA" last year, we have tried to make it a point to always book our leisure trips based on the spa review. Omni Houston and the Mokara Spa were exactly what we needed to relax, relate and release. The staff was wonderful at the hotel. THe amenities including complimentary champagne and Starbucks coffee were a plus. (I love when I get extra stuff that wasn't mentioned on the webpage--makes me feel like I got over:)) We booked a package which included the breakfast buffet each morning. The buffet was LOADED! The grounds are so relaxing. The Mokara Spa was overall a good experience. There was an issue with my appointment when I arrived. I scheduled the 3 Express Package for an AWESOME price which includes 3 30-50 minute treatments. I selected body scrub, oxygen facial and reflexology. Someone didn't book the reflexologist so they had to figure out how to get me worked in. What I wound up with was having my facial and reflexology done simultaneously--OMG--it was awesome and I felt like I was floating when it was over. To make up for the delay and error (I had to wait about 20 minutes while things were sorted out) they added on the Chardonnay which is usually part of another package (more extras:)). If you add in the TO DIE FOR chocolatepecanoatmealsomethingelseorother cookielikething and the assortment of fruit, nuts and teas available while you are in the relax room, it was okay that I had to chill in there for a while. I could have eaten the whole plate. The only suggestion I have is that there be separate relax areas for men and women and couples. That part kind of freaked me out. Most of the guys there were part of couples but I knew that if all they had on under the robe was the disposable thong like me, I did NOT want that robe to accidentally fall off. There were a couple of uncomfortable moments for the guys as well as at one point there was quite a bit of "girl talk". Basically, the relaxation area just needs to be bigger. I did like the netted cabana like "nests". If I go again by myself I'm going to sit in one of those with a good book. Also, didn't like that the whirlpool has no door. What's up with that? Sauna has door, showers have door, whirlpool is in the middle of the pass through from the lockers to the relax room. I guess I'm spoiled. Still haven't found anyone to top Watermark in San Antonio yet. I'll be traveling to check out the Couples San Souci and reviewing their spa in November. Let's see what they have. Overall, still a great experience. Close to home so I'm sure I'll be visiting again. Back to the hotel...the food at the restaurant was expensive...but good. There is also bar food available at the lounge which was very pretty and tasty at a reasonable price for a 4-5 star hotel. Oh yeah..if you go on a weekend to Omni...YOU MUST go to the Black Swan lounge. I'm not even going to tell you, but if you like to partying with people who drive expensive a-- vehicles, GO!

name: The NoMad Hotel
title: “Classy... try their Intelligentsia capuccino”
text:
Enjoyed staying in this boutique hotel. A convenient location. I enjoyed their breakfast, and their coffee was delicious. 
Room lights difficult to figure out so I thought initially the room was dimly lit. But once I found out how to turn up the lights, it was fine.

name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park
title: “Sinking Service”
text: For the steep prices of the Ritz Carlton, the service would be acceptable at a low tier marriott, not when you're paying a thousand dollars a night. The Ritz Carlton Central Park used to be our favorite hotel in New York City. It was very disappointing to see how much the service had declined. The room was clean and the bathrooms were nice, but the overall service was below average, especially for a Ritz. Prior to checking in to our hotel, we had special requests that were unfulfilled when we arrived. In the past for special anniversaries/birthdays, the staff had always made the experience more special. We are hoping that these issues are resolved.

name: Club Quarters in Houston
title: “preiswert, aber nichts besonderes”
text: Das Hotel ist preiswert. Kaffee, Tee und vor allem Trinkwasser sind kostenlos im Zimmer verfügbar! Essen ist im Hotel nicht erhältlich, doch besteht die Möglichkeit vergünstigt Essen aus ausgewälten Restaurants direkt ins Zimmer liefern zu lassen. Da das Hotel direkt im CBD liegt, ist vor allem Nachts und am Wochenende viel "Gesindel" auf den Strassen, so dass man sich nicht sonderlich sicher fühlt. Bars sind in unmittelbarer Nähe und der Theater District ist zu Fuß leicht zu erreichen.

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “Suveränt hotell”
text: Min man och jag bodde fem nätter på detta underbara hotell i oktober 2012. Vi hade varit i mailkontakt med hotellet innan och bett om att få bo högt uppe. När vi anlände till hotellet hade vi blivit uppgraderade till ett större hörnrum på 19 våningen. Helt underbart. Rum 1912, utsikt mot både Broadway och en glimt av Central park. Rent, snyggt och bra gratis kaffe. Skulle absolut bo här igen om vi kommer tillbaka.

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “No nos decepcionó!!!!!”
text:
Hemos estado en octubre 4 personas en una habitación tipo suite, con dos camas grandes (caben dos personas en cada una) y un sofá cama en otra habitación con una cocina.
El sofá cama bastante incómodo, pero se puede pedir una cama supletoria y te la traen sin ningún problema. No es tan cómoda como las otras pero se puede dormir bien.
La cocina muy útil, sobre todo para desayunar.
Justo al lado del hotel hay un Fairway, una especie de mercado donde hay de todo. Es algo caro pero para comprar las cosas del desayuno e incluso algo de cena es perfecto.
La ubicación también muy buena, zona tranquila, perfectamente conectada con la linea roja del metro, y cerca de Central Park.
En resumen, muy contentos con la relación calidad-precio. Y como para repetir!!!!!

name: Hyatt Regency Houston
title: “On the plus side of "neutral"”
text:
I was a guest at the Hyatt Regency Houston for a convention of my nonprofit in March 2006. 
Being a Gold Passport member faciltated a no-delay check-in, and I was quickly in my 16th floor room. I found it to be clean and of average size. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom was spotless. Air conditioning worked quite well. The in-room coffeemaker came supplied with two packets of grounds, a nice touch if you want some extra "joe". High-speed wireless internet access was available for $9.95/day, and worked quite well.
Have to agree with previous comments about noise, though. My room was right by the elevator and people talking while waiting for the lift could be clearly heard in the room. Noise from the atrium was not a problem for me during my stay. 
I only ate breakfast in the restaurant downstairs, and was well satisfied. Their omelette station is impressive. We had some meals in the hotel as part of our convention package, and they, too, were good.
Hotel staff were friendly and helpful. They made my stay pleasant.

name: Indigo Houston at the Galleria
title: “What a great place to stay!”
text: The staff was super nice, the room was immaculate, and the decor was just beautiful. All that and we got priority club points. It is a little hard to find, but well worth the trouble. (Located behind another property but with a drive beside the other one and with an address on the same street.) My only caveat is that they could use a slightly better thread count for the sheets. Thanks for a great 2 nights.

name: The NoMad Hotel
title: “Great place to stay”
text:
Loved this hotel! I always try to stay in boutique hotels and this one is well located, has great decor, great ambiance and a good restaurant. We stayed in a salon room which was a good size but very well laid out. The bathroom is tastefully done with adequate room for toiletries.
The front desk was extremely helpful with booking car service and making reservations on our behalf. Unfortunately, we missed out on dining on the Rooftop due to uncooperative weather but still enjoyed cocktails there that were very fresh and tasty. The only negative point to the Rooftop is the extra service charge....
Will definitely return

name: The Michelangelo Hotel
title: “Fabulous stay!”
text: We love this hotel! We have stayed there before and were updated to a huge suite this time since it was our anniversary! Nice bedding, 1 1/2 bathrooms beautifully decorated rooms, terrific staff and great location. Highly recommend.

name: Hilton Houston North
title: “I was stolen $461 dollars in Front Desk!”
text:
I stayed for 5 days at Hilton Houston North (formerly Wyndham Greenspoint), from July 26 to July 31, 2008. I was attending a conference and it was the hosting hotel. I booked my stay through Hilton's website using my credit card, on the note that no charges would be made until the end of my stay.
On Thursday July 31, when doing check-out, I was billed $485.28 dlls, from which $461.46 where due to lodging and $23.82 were spent at the hotel's cafe. I asked the front-desk lady to split my account in two accounts: one for the $461.46 and the other for $23.82. She agreed and gave me two new bills. I asked her if I could pay the $461.46 in cash, and charge the $23.82 bill on my credit card. She said it was ok. So, I counted the money and I handled it to her in order to close the $461.46 bill. I GAVE HER $461.46 DOLLARS CASH! I HAVE NO DOUBTS I DID! It is a lot of money!!
Once she said it was fine, I asked about the $23.82 bill on my credit card. She said it was fine. I asked her -Do I need to show you my credit card?-. She said -No, we already have it in system through your booking-.I asked again - Do I need to sign anything?- She answered: - No, is fine. Everything's fine.
Days later, I found out that I have been charged $461.46 dollars in my credit card!! WHICH I HAD ALREADY PAID IN CASH!! I called Hilton Houston North front desk to clear the matter, and they told me they did not had the money. On their records it appeared as if I had paid $23.82 dollars in cash, which I did not. I paid $461.46. It is a big difference.
They found the lady who checked-me out and asked her about the money. She said she remembered me, and she remembered that I had asked her to split my account in two parts, but that I had paid $23.82 in cash and had requested $461.46 in my credit card...WHICH IS ABSOLUTELY NOT TRUE!!!
However, since she gave me no receipt, or anything for the matters, only my bill; and since they checked her cash-box and there was no spare money...They just told me that they were sorry and there was nothing they can do! 
And the money I cash-paid, where is it?
How is this possible? It is unthinkable! I am extremely mad and disappointed! There are no words to what just happened there! Only, IT WAS STEAL!!!!

name: Omni Houston Hotel
title: “Very Disappointed”
text: The only good thing I have to say is that the property was clean inside and out. Our room rate was $130 and I expected a 4 Star quality hotel (of which they are rated). The room looked just like a $70 per night Holiday Inn. We were there for a weekend away and I spent extra on a room expecting a very nice hotel. The bath tub was very small with all old water fixures and had an electrical outlet that was falling out of the wall. It was just nothing fancy about the place at all. Maybe my expectations were high since the photos on the internet were all beautiful - But in the end we were not impressed at all.

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “Excellent séjour !”
text:
Hotel bien situé au coin de la 74ème et Broadway proche de Central Park mais aussi d'une station de métro ce qui est très pratique ! Le personnel est très accueillant. La chambre pour 4 personnes est très spacieuse et dispose d'un petit coin cuisine et d'une table pour manger ce qui permet de prendre un petit déjeuner tranquillement (un supermarché se trouve juste en face de l’hôtel et est ouvert quasiment 24h/24 ! La chambre et la salle de bain sont très propres, bonne insonorisation et système de climatisation/chauffage agréable ! Petit plus: la chambre dispose de 2 télés.
A recommander vivement !

name: Hilton Houston North
title: “Very Pleasant Stay”
text: I stayed at this hotel 8/16/05- 8/19/05 on a business trip. I found the staff to be very friendly, courteous, and helpful. My king bed room was very spacious, and the bed was heavenly. If you are not a Wyndham by request member, you should join . it's free. On arrival they greeted me with a very nice welcome gift, (Cheese, crackers, a chilled bottle of wine, water and juice) You also receive free internet access, and free local telephone calls The breakfast buffet is standard fare, but the pasta bar at lunch is delicious, you select all the ingredients and the chefs make your lunch as you watch. This is a good hotel for a business trip; they also have an indoor pool. Starbucks and a great little bar are located in the atrium style lobby.

name: Hyatt Regency Houston
title: “Bewertung”
text: Das Hotel ist sicher ein guter Tipp für Houston. Wer sehr gute Zimmer mag, ist hier gut aufgehoben. Die Lage in Downtown Houston ist zwar nicht optimal zu den Flughäfen, jedoch entschädigt die Qualität der Zimmer dies auf jeden Fall. Der Service im Hotel ist von hohem Niveau. Leider konnten wir die Küche aus oben genannten Gründen nicht testen.

name: Omni Houston Hotel Westside
title: “Beautiful hotel...”
text:
Omni Houston Westside is a beautiful hotel. I got a great rate through Hotels.com so I chose it over other hotels I am familiar with in Houston. I was in town for Thanksgiving and the passing of a relative (four nights). I had lived in Houston for about 28 years so I am very familiar with what level of service to expect from this type of hotel.
I was not disappointed. The decor of the hotel was simply tranquil. As others have said, the lobby really creates a peaceful mood. The service from the the desk at check in was very efficient and friendly. 
My room was spacious and looked very pretty. I agree with another reviewer that the sheets on the beds were not what I expected. A higher thread count would have been more in line with this type of hotel. I also found the bathroom to be very nice but a pocket door would make you feel less restricted. 
All the little amenities, mini bar, water, high speed internet costs were way out of line for this hotel. The Omni Galleria can command these prices not Westside. Self park was complimentary. 
Overall, I liked the place and would definitely stay again. If you know and understand Houston, traffic is a way of life so complaining about it has nothing to do with a review of any hotel in the Houston area.

name: Houston Marriott West Loop by the Galleria
title: “Best Hotel for biz travelers”
text:
Excellent staff manners. Warm, friendly and attentive. Get the sense they have been properly schooled to greet and cater to business travelers, especially, MR members. 
Mr. Fidel Caballero, Rooms Ops Mgr., is very cordial and always greets me gladly. Will make this my primary destination hotel when in Houston. Right in the heart of the Galleria area.
Cocktail hour every Tues. to all guests hosted by hotel management. I highly recommend this Marriott facility to everyone.

name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park
title: “The BEST!!”
text: My friends and I stayed at the Ritz from Jan 12-15 and we could not have been happier!! The room, the service, and the location could not have been better. Book the concierge level, it's worth the money!! We can't wait to stay there again next January.

name: Hotel Mulberry
title: “Nice stay”
text: We thoroughly enjoyed our stay! We have been going the friday after Thanksgiving for 15 years. The last few years we stayed in Times Square but wanted to try something else. Our only complaint would be the noise level between rooms. The walls are thin. We stayed in room 702 with a terrace, which was awesome! The front desk was very helpful and stored our luggage when we arrived early. We never felt uneasy about the area and we were 2 women that did not come in until after 11pm almost every night. We enjoyed looking over at the park everyday and seeing the older people playing cards and doing Tai Chi. One day it rained and the hotel provided complimentary umbrellas. The breakfast is provided by a restaurant a few doors down. It is a set menu of about 7 items. It is a decent breakfast with quick service. Not many hotels provide complimentary breakfast much less a warm one. The beds were extremely comfortable and room was clean and spacious. We went to several good restaurants this year. Always good, New Green Bo in Chinatown just around the corner. Another good restaurant is Lasagne Ristaurante. DeGarrno in Little Italy is a good restaurant as well. We would definitely stay there again.

name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park
title: “If you can, ignore the room rate and enjoy”
text: This is an incredible property. From the location, to the staff, to the ways the rooms are appointed, everything was perfect. If you are not offended by the price, there is probably no better place to stay in NYC. Enjoy a drink at the lobby bar, where you are sure to see a celebrity, and for another $150 a night, you can enjoy the spectacular concierge level, serving incredible drinks and light food.

name: Affinia Gardens
title: “Sizeable in good condition rooms, cons: no free internet in room, the kitchenette and dining facilities are insufficient”
text:
We stayed in the Affinia Gardens in New York, from 20th of August until 27th of August with a family of 5. It was a reasonable good stay, staff professional, kind and helpful. 
Positive aspects -
- relatively more space for the same bucks than hotels in the region
- 5 blocks away from central park
Negative aspects -
- very noisy airconditioning, to the level that it can influence the sensitive sleeper's nightrest.
- the kitchenette was very disappointing - it had only 2 small picknick level pans, no dishwasher in junior suite (the lack of a dishwasher is not mentioned on the websites!).
- basically we did not use it at all, and went to restaurants all the time and treated this place as a hotel in stead of an appartment. 
- the area of upper east is under major reconstruction for the subways. be aware of some disruptance while walking to and from.
- the food emporium (grocery store) closeby sells bread for 5 dollars each, as hard as stone , you could knock someone out with that bread.

name: Sheraton Houston Brookhollow Hotel
title: “Back again in Houston”
text: I hadn't stayed here in a few years and I am pleased to say the hotel has not gone downhill in the least. The full service restaurant is nice and the bartender is helpful. My room on the 7th floor was clean and quiet and the expressway noise was minimal . . . and after all, the hotel is between two expressways, but is has nice grounds and an appealing pool. If you need convenience and don't mind full service rates, this is a fine place to stay.

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “A great retreat in the city”
text:
This is my second time staying at the Shelbourne, and I think I have found my new go-to spot. My daughter and I were visiting, this time to look at colleges in NYC. We stayed at another hotel the first night, but it was not acceptable, so I called the Shelbourne, hoping they had a room. They did, thankfully. I requested a quiet room because my daughter and I both appreciate a good night's sleep. The room had zero street noise, though it was between the two elevator banks on the hall and there were noisy guests walking by late at night. That was my only disappointment.
Our room had two queen beds and was not not huge but we had plenty of room to walk around the beds to get to the bathroom, etc. The bathroom, similarly, was small but nicely finished, with plenty of counter space and a nice shower.
There is a tiny coffee shop next door to the hotel that has good coffee and pastries. The subway is a few blocks away, and there is a drugstore nearby.
The staff is not super-friendly, and, even though this is New York, they could do a better job with that. And wifi in the rooms would be nice -- this is the 21st century, after all. But, all in all, when I need to be in midtown, this is a good spot.

name: Affinia Gardens
title: “Perfect for families”
text:
We stayed in a one bed apartment here in July 2012. Our party consisted of 3 adults and 2 children. From the outset the service was perfect. We were offered a baby cot, humidifier, new kettle and toaster within the first few hours of checking in.
There is ample room in these apartments. Everything works fine. Beds are comfortable. Kitchens include a dishwasher a huge fridge freezer. There is an iron plus ironing board.
The hotel also provides a walking tour of NY which is a box of guidebooks, guide walks and other useful items which we thought were great. The choice of pillows is also fantastic. All the staff are very friendly and helpful.
Maid service is daily, this includes bathroom, kitchen and arranging the beds. It didn't include a daily vacuum clean and tidy up which we thought was strange but not a deal breaker for us.
Wifi is exortionate, and this would be my main complaint. The trip was part business and part vacation and although I was paying for wifi, the connection was very poor. I had to end up going to the business center downstairs to get the full bars on wifi.
Despite this, if I was doing a vacation trip again with the kids, I would stay here again and really try and get a ground floor suite that has a garden.
Location was great for us. 10minute walk to central Park which was perfect for the kids. the metro is a 5min walk, and most evenings we walked it to Times Square, 5th Avenue and the museums.
Overall a great stay.

name: Houston Marriott West Loop by the Galleria
title: “Excellent Long Term Stay”
text: I've been at this hotel for 4 weeks now as I was working locally. Staff are friendly and polite. Food is excellent with a good bar menu. Rooms are spacious with fresh linen and good bathroom. Would stay at this hotel if I was paying for the room instead of my company.

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Nice hotel”
text:
Stayed here on business for a few nights. Room was clean, spacious and modern. 
Unfortunately I didnt' even have the time to look out my window or spend enough time at the hotel to appreciate it fully.
Staff was friendly and helpful, and service was quick and efficient.

name: Candlewood Suites New York City Times Square
title: “Perfect Location”
text: We just returned from a wonderful weekend in New York City. We stayed at the Candlewood Suites and it is a perfect location if you want to be near Times Square. It is 3 avenues over and 3 streets which is a 5 minute walk. The suite we had was clean, spacious and fully equiped with microwave, large refrigerator, dishwasher, and 2 burners. Coffee maker, toaster and all utensils were there was our use. The rooms are a bit more expensive but because of the location walking everywhere is so easy. The people at the front desk were very polite and friendly and the elevators were super fast. Absolutely the place to stay when in New York City.

name: Gansevoort Park Avenue NYC
title: “Perfect hotel for Girl's Weekend!”
text: I just spent a long holiday weekend at the Gansevoort on Park Ave. My best friend and I were celebrating our 40th birthdays:) I have nothing negative to say about our experience. The hotel is perfectly located in Midtown, just a block from the nearest subway station and directly across the street from Starbucks. There are also several restaurants and shops within a block of the hotel. It was incredibly convenient!! We enjoyed our spacious room with a balcony. And, it was so clean that it felt like home to me. I was also impressed with the housekeeping and turn-down service! The staff could not have been more friendly and helpful. I would definitely stay at the Gansevoort again!!!

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Lovely convenient and very clean location”
text: We travelled and stayed here prior to our daughters wedding. The suite was comfortable and the staff friendly and helpful. The hotel needs to publish its individual website details as messages to the Affinia site are not forwarded which is most annoying.Otherwise our stay was good and will stay here again on our next visit.

name: Aloft Harlem
title: “a very good stay in a very good atmosphere”
text:
The hotel maintains its promises: cleanliness, good atmosphere, design, very welcoming services at any hours. 
The rooms are not so big as advertised but in anyway larger than usual manhattan hotels: I loved the shower room!
it's a good place both for Harlem and Manhattan (10 mins from Columbus Circle, through express train).
I'll suggest it to anyone who'd like to be a little bit out of Manhattan

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan / Times Square South
title: “Best kept secret!”
text: My husband booked a surprise trip to New York, United Airlines direct from Glasgow, good flight, but my suitcase got trashed! The staff at the Hampton Inn couldn't have been friendlier. Small room but clean and a comfy bed. Surprised at the quality of the complimentary FREE breakfast. Have already recommended to friends. Would definitely stay there again. Half a block away from Hells Kitchen. ate there most nights after going to shows, good food, good bars, good value for money. Also make time to go to Eatily across from the Flat Iron Building, food to die for and great waiting staff. Don't be afraid to ask a New York cop for help / directions, they were fabulous. New Yorkers get bad press about being rude, not at all, we found them friendly.

name: The Carlyle, A Rosewood Hotel
title: “The Carlyle...Class, Service, and Cost”
text: The Carlyle is one of a quickly vanishing breed...a hotel which lives up to its reputation for high quality service, accommodations, and ambiance. From the moment you step into the lobby, you know this is not the Marriott Marquis or the "W". From the marble floors to the art to the impeccable service, it is first class. The 'superior suite' was just that with large living room and large bedroom. The bathroom, although very modern and totally mirrored, was miniscule even by NY standards. The decor in the Carlyle Gallery (restaurant) is Moorish and lovely, not over the top like a lot of 'Bogart-wanna-be's. Serving lighter fare, the Gallery is the better place to eat at the Carlyle. The main restaurant's decor is also marvelous; however, the seating is crowded and there is no way to not be involved in the conversation next to you. The food is fairly over-priced and not that good. Location, Location, Location..that is the major problem. Unless you plan to go to Central Park and that is it, brace yourself for lots of taxi expense and long travel time to the theaters. This is not a hotel for a taste of Broadway.

name: Candlewood Suites New York City Times Square
title: “Good”
text: Its a nice hotel to stay its near everything metro, restaurants, time square , broadway etc... The people working there are very helpful and friendly . The rooms are good size and include a fridge and micro oven , the beds are comfortable and very clean .

name: Gansevoort Park Avenue NYC
title: “Beautiful hotel, would definitely stay here again”
text:
This hotel made our trip! It is such a lovely hotel:
ROOM: We had a room at the back of the hotel, a 4 poster bed, sofa/seating area and large bathroom. I'd read reviews about noise but our room was so quiet, there was no noise at all. The bed was very comfortable and we had blackout curtains which made for a great sleep.
POOL/SUNDECK: We got lucky with the weather and spent 3 afternoons lying by the pool with the Empire State building as our backdrop. Towels are provided and they have waiter service to your sunbed. The pool was cold but refreshing.
LOUNGE AREAS: on the top levels there are plenty of areas to have meetings. Comfortable sofas and again, table service. It was a pleasure to bring our business colleagues to meet us here.
OVERALL: Free Wi-Fi, Ideally placed, very luxurious (everything felt new) and we were very well looked after. It's not cheap but we would definitely stay again.

name: Aloft Harlem
title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
I have to agree with all of the previous 5 star reviews. The reviews are accurate as well as the photos that others have attached to this hotel's overview. I have to add the hotel's free WiFi is very good since I haven't noticed many others mentioning it. 
Probably the chief concern with most people is the hotel's location. Harlem was a pretty bad place in the '70s and '80s but it is fine now. As one reviewer mentioned, there seems to be a gentrification process going on. Gentrification can mean bad things to some people because it means poorer folks can no longer afford to live in the neighborhood. There's a NYPD precinct just a half block away from the hotel's front door. The neighborhood folks seem cool. As with any urban environment, it helps to walk with a purpose and not like you are a lost tourist.
The 125th St. subway stop is one block away and with the A express train running days and evenings, you are only minutes away from Midtown or the Financial district. For any grocery needs, the Best Yet Market is your best bet - heh - and is about 5 blocks south of the hotel. Rite-Aid is another block further south. The Harlem Tavern is yet another block south from there. They have a pretty good beer selection, plenty of TVs for sporting events and live entertainment. Popular place too.
A special mention goes to the Paris Blues Bar about a block and a half southeast of the hotel. The bar is small - a Greyhound busload of people could fill it up. Beers are relatively cheap and they had some free food on Weds. night which is apparently amateur night. All of the performers were decent to very good. And they all seemed to be regulars since they all seem to know the drill. Many showed up to do their thing and then left within an hours time. My favorite was a guy who sauntered in late, clearly had had a few elsewhere and looked like the actor Sam Rockwell. A short time later, he gave a brief RatPack-esque performance that would have left Frank, Deano and Sammy proud. The old guy sitting behind me, who had been pretty quiet much of the evening, starting clapping and cackled, "Give 'em another drink!" Indeed.

name: Fitzpatrick Manhattan
title: “Great Staff- Professional with Charm”
text: Great place, staff makes one feel welcome. Stayed at hotel for work (booked thur my work)and was unfamiliar with the hotel. It was much better than I thought it would be. Staff is precise, and helpful without being overly familiar. Few minute walk to central park, 5th ave. St. Patricks. I would happily stay here again.

name: The Kimberly Hotel
title: “Absolutely satisfied”
text:
Got a good deal for this hotel through hotels.com and we were not disappointed.
On arrival we were put in a gorgeous 1 bedroom suite with a full kitchen and a balcony on the 3rd floor.
The staff is friendly and helpful, especially the charming lady concierge (Datsy -sorry if I am misspelling the name).
Would definitely stay there again.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Wonderful hotel in Manhattan and great staff/ service”
text: Sofitel is a wonderful luxury hotel in Manhattan within walking distance to shopping and theaters. The staff are professional and helpful. Rooms are clean and large. Bathrooms are very large. Great workout room. Would not stay anywhere else!

name: Hotel Mulberry
title: “Wonderful place”
text: We had a very nice stay at Hotel Mulberry in New York's Chinatown. It is a clean, nicely decorated and quiet hotel. The bed was very comfortable. We were impressed with the very friendly staff. As others have said the breakfast each morning is delicious and included. Make sure you know the names of nearby streets as we had cab drivers who were not aware of where Mulberry Street is.

name: Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden
title: “Great Staff, Very Good Value ... for NYC”
text: Stayed for three nights, four people in two rooms. If arriving by bus or train you cannot beat the location. Good for touring NYC as well. It's a short walk to Times Square and enjoys convenient access to subway. Most of the staff, including the General Manager who was very present and available from Breakfast to early evening, were very helpful. One of the front desk people seemed reluctant to provide anything above the minimum, but there was always someone else who would do their best to honor requests. The rooms, as noted elsewhere, are small. Trying to move around in the room with more than two people is difficult. The limited space between the bed and the wall and the bed and the tiny desk and chair are also a bit of a challenge. The free breakfast is above the normal Hampton Inn standard, and the free internet is decent. Highly recommended for a budget visit to NYC and would get 5/5 if the rooms were a little larger.

name: Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden
title: “Great stay in The Big Apple.”
text: Very sorry for the late review but still wanted to leave one as we had a great stay, Location was great and very close to Empire state building, Time square, Maddison square gardens etc. Breaskfast was included and was very nice, get there as early as you can because the seating is very limited so if you stay at a busy time of year be prepared to stand. Loved the fact you could make tea/coffee/hot chocolate at any time of day, we stayed in February and it was pretty cold getting back in the evenings so it was a welcome touch. The Hotel was very clean and staff were friendly....I will point out that the rooms are fairly small, especially by Americas standards but it wasn't a huge problem for us(Husband and I and a 12 year old and 9 year old) and it wouldn't put us off from staying here again. After all you don't go to New York and spend much time in the room. I have to mention that the lighting in the bathroom and shower were one of the best i've had on any holiday and i've been on a few so that was a bonus for me, the beds were pretty comfortable too. We didn't get much of a view from our room but we requested a quiete room so it was out of the way. All in all we thoroughly enjoyed our trip to New York and look forward to going back :)

name: Hotel Mulberry
title: “Great find! Wish I could keep it a secret.”
text: The other reviewers were spot on. This hotel is a gem in the heart of Chinatown and only 2 blocks to little Italy. Beds super comfortable, marble bathroom with strong shower pressure to ease away the pains of a long day sightseeing. Staff could not have been more helpful....especially Jackie, Kelly, and the young man on at night. We are in NYC frequenlt and will return to the Mulberry again and again.

name: Gansevoort Park Avenue NYC
title: “Nice but loud”
text:
I’m usually in NYC 2-3 times a month on business and decided to try a new hotel. On arrival and throughout my stay the staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The room was nice, clean and stylish. The bed had nice crisp linens. As others have mentioned the bathtub is huge. It was nice to soak in it after a long day at work. The minibar is well stocked. The entire hotel has a “club” vibe. 
Unfortunately that also includes the “club” noise level. Drunks were running up and down the hallway and screaming most of the night (on a Thursday) and doors were constantly slamming until about 3 am. It felt more like a freshman dorm during the first week of college than a luxury NYC hotel. I guess the take-home message is that this hotel is more appropriate for a young party crowd than it is for business people or families. It’s a shame because the staff and rooms are very nice and the price point is extremely reasonable for NYC. 
I’d stay here again if I was in town and wanted to party until 4 am every night, but not if I’m there on business.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Great Hotel”
text:
We stayed for a week over Easter, the hotel was clean and tidy and the staff were very friendly and helpful. We didn't dine in the hotel as there are so many delis and diners around the area and they seemed too good to avoid.
The hotel is in a great location just off 5th Avenue and a very short walk to Times Square and Broadway.
If we ever go back to NYC we'll be sure to stay here again.

name: Aloft Harlem
title: “Love the Harlem Aloft”
text: Stayed here with my wife for a conference at Columbia college she was at and like all Alofts the staff was very friendly and helpful. The place smells great and was always lively. Although we didnt do much in Harlem we found it very convenient to get wherever we were going by foot, subway or cab. If you are a walker like we are then going to Columbia everyday is no big deal. I think the price was pretty reasonable for being so close to Manhattan. I would definitly go back to this hotel.

name: Fitzpatrick Manhattan
title: “The Fitzpatrick, A wonderful hotel”
text: In a city of grand hotels, The Fitzpatrick Manhattan, should count as one of the grandest. What can i say, the staff is OUTSTANDING in particular Caroline Walls. She goes out of her way to make sure the guest are happy and satisfied. My wife and I were in the "PUB" having dinner when an un expected graduation party literally took over the place along iwth part of the resturant. Many employees would have allowed this to get them upset and a bit testy. NOT Caroline, she continued smiling with that Irish twinkle in her eye and made sure everyone was happy. The hotel is in a perfect location, and the beds among the best I have ever slept in. The rooms are large for NYC and very very confortable. Overall outstanding. My wife and I plan on returning to NYC several times and we will always stay at Ireland on this side of the Atlantic, THE FITZPATRICK

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan / Times Square South
title: “Exceptional customer service!”
text: We stayed here or four consecutive nights. You couldn't ask for a more accommodating staff than the workers at this hotel! Polite, efficient, catering to your requests, always wearing smiles, they are a well trained group. From the front desk, to the breakfast kitchen staff, to the young men who were there to carry luggage, etc, -- all were great! The hotel is well situated for a brief 15 minute walk to Times Square. The facility itself is clean and neat but sometimes getting up and down on two elevators may require a wait. But overall this is a nice place for the price and we would stay there gain.

name: Hotel Mulberry
title: “Une belle surprise pour un merveilleux séjour!”
text:
L'hotel est très propre. les chambres sont spacieuses. Nous étions 3 dans une chambre Luxe Queen. Situé en plein coeur de Chinatown et proche de little Italy nous nous rendions à times square en 10-15 minutes grâce à la ligne Q Broadway express. De plus nous nous sommes rendu au pont de Brooklyn à pieds. Ce fut une très belle surprise car nous n'avions pas imaginé l'hotel d'une si bonne qualité! Serviette, gel douche... Changés chaque jour. Ménage fait chaque jour. Et avant de partir appelé l'hotel qui est partenaire avec une compagnie de voiture pour vous conduire à l'aéroport!! 
Si nous devions repartir, ce serait notre premier choix!

name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park
title: “Wonderful Experience”
text: Everything was perfect. I have nothing but great memories of my stay. The view, the service, the bed, the bath, the food, the location.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Seaport Inn Downtown
title: “You get what you pay for”
text:
I stayed at this hotel while attending a conference in the financial district November 5-7. Given that this hotel is not that much cheaper than many other better hotels in the area, I was pretty dissapointed with my stay. 
When I arrived, I was asked to sign a document agreeing that this was a non-smoking hotel. Great!! I dont smoke and am allergic to it. Upon entering my room, it reiked of smoke. I was moved to another room, which did not smell of smoke until the second night. Someone might as well have been smoking in my room it was so bad. This is an old hotel and if someone is smoking in a room with a vent connected to yours, you might as well light up yourself. So if you are sensitive so smoke or dont want to stay in a hotel that smells of smoke, this is not the hotel for you.
The staff was also pretty rude and unhelpful. On my first night at the hotel, it was later in the evening, I didnt want to venture very far and was looking for a place to eat. I asked at the front desk for a recommendation to which the woman working the desk replied "I dont know, I dont eat down here." So I then proceeded to just ask for directions to some restaurants listed on the hotel's website that it states are nearby, to which I was pointed to a map of NYC! I dont really care if the front desk staff doesnt eat in the area, but I at least expect them to be helpful. 
Lastly, dont plan on eating the breakfast unless you like stale pastries and a box of Cheerios or like your waffle mix to come out of a machine that is not refrigerated. There are plenty of places nearby to get breakfast.
If you do stay here, I highly recommend eating at Salud, a Brazillian tapas restaurant a couple of blocks away. Excellent!!

name: Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden
title: “Great New York Hotel”
text: I am so glad I went against my travel agent, she had us staying at the Hotel Pennyslyvania, but I insisted after reading TA that I would choose my own, I am happy to write rave revues about Hampton Inn. All the little touches made our stay great, including breakfast, coffee in the room, breakfast bags, all day coffee, free internet and as we found out too late into our 4 night stay the beautiful hot soup in the afternoon. What hotels offer this?? Hilton the general manager spoke to us numerous times and got his ipad out to show us where to go or what to do that day, I appreciate the friendliness. The rooms were a tad small but what can you expect in NY, but were exceptionally cleaned daily.The hotel was close to everything and you could hail a cab easily from the front door. Choosing this hotel made our stay in New york a joy. Thankyou Hilton for caring about how you treat guest.

name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park
title: “A disappointing stay”
text:
We love the Ritz-Carlton hotels......we've stayed in Orlando twice this year, St Thomas and New York a few times. I'm starting to wonder if the Central Park location is either too busy or just don't care anymore.
Last night we went to dinner...( we were out of our room by 5pm ) and returned at 9:30. When we walked into our room, we realized that turn down and towel service had not occured. It was very disappointing. We called the front desk and asked if they changed their policy on turn down service, they replied that they have till 10pm to complete that service. I'm not sure that answered our question and is not typical of Ritz-Carlton hotels. We then asked for towels in order to shower in the morning(there was only 2 upon our arrival)....after waiting over half and hour (we were getting tired and wanted to sleep) we called again and the front desk said she sent them up and she has no idea what happened. Does that sound like Ritz-Carlton to you? After a call back by the front desk a woman brought towels to our room and told us of her woes on how busy she is and they just couldn't get to our room tonight. I can get that kind of response at any hotel.....not at $700 a night.
Needless to say, I was very disappopinted in the service. No one apologized or showed any remorse for inconviencing us at 10pm on a Saturday night. I'm used to a different Ritz-Carlton. It's too bad.

name: The Kimberly Hotel
title: “Good Location in NYC”
text:
This hotel is located in a good location, closed to the Lexington Ave subway station. It is also within walking distances to Park Ave, Central Park South, Grand Central Station etc.
The hotel have a lovley roof top terrace bar offering a nice view of the Manhattan skyline.
The rooms were clean and we had a nice stay. 
Unfortunately, our rates didn't include free wifi. However, there is a business centre (with computers & printer) which guests are welcome to use.

name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park
title: “Absolutely impeccable!”
text:
Just spent three nights here with my mother and my daughter (age 8). It was my second stay at this hotel and I enjoyed it even more than last year. The location is wonderful. We walked to MoMA, American Girl Place, Barney's, the theatre and much more!
 The level of service is excellent and traveling with my daughter seemed to get me even BETTER service than without. Upon arrival one of the staff members gave my daughter a Lizzie Maguire DVD to watch in the room. Our first morning, on the way out the door, the doorman greeted my daughter by name! Our bellman was very grateful for his tips...everyone was fantastic!
 Our room was at the back of the hotel. We needed two double beds so we booked the lowest room category, which is the only way to GET 2 doubles. It was exquisite! And we still had three large windows, including one in the spacious bathroom.
 We had breakfast every morning at the hotel's restaurant, Atelier.Again, the service is unparalleled. Dinner at Atelier our last night was divine (and now prix fixe); the Master Sommelier was very kind.
 Although I love shopping and exploring downtown...I will never be able to stay anywhere but the Ritz Carlton on central Park - as long as I can afford it. It is absolutely a dream hotel! I'm hoping to take my daughter again this summer.

name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park
title: “A perfect Hotel”
text: We spent 3 nights at the Ritz Carlton and have to say that it was the most beautiful and perfect hotel we have ever stayed in. We found all the staff very friendly, efficient and helpful and always courteous. We especially liked the juice and apples laid out for returning morning joggers every morning! The room was very spacious which is a real plus in New York. It was also very quiet - we had a back room - and although we didn't have a view of Central Park, we didn't feel at all disappointed. The bed was the most comfortable I have ever slept in - I am now busy changing all my bedding - and the bathroom was simply luxurious. A hotel which could not be faulted and to be recommended to all.

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Times Square New York
title: “Location Location in NYC”
text:
Great location - close to Empire State Building, Times Square, Bryant Park, NY Public Library, Subway, Theater District - 
Clean and stylish 
Our room had a view of the Empire State Building 
Breakfast buffet was good way to start our days
You can walk just about anywhere you want to 
Definitely a good location for visitng NYC
Would stay here again

name: The Kimberly Hotel
title: “Great, safe location with comfort.”
text: Friendly, efficient check in ~ good vaue for money, particulary for the area. Large, clean and well appointed rooms. Decor is traditional but in very good condition no shabby scuff marks, stains or scratches. Nice touches with a microwave (plastic cutlery and paper plates would be helpful), robes, slippers and quality toiletries. Lovely bedding on high sumptious bed, though perhaps a bit too soft! One minor drawback, felt like there was an electric blanket under the sheet as we tended to heat up, could this be due to a latex topper on the matress? No breakfast is worth $25 so we didn't try it, however there is a great place round the corner which will do a full fry up, coffee and juice for $10

name: Fitzpatrick Manhattan
title: “just love fitzpatricks”
text: i stay here at least once a year on annual shopping trips. it always feels like a home from home. service is excellant, rooms lovely with the most comfortable beds in the world! very convenient for bloomingdales and 5th avenue shoppong. good irish breakfast every morning.

name: The Kimberly Hotel
title: “Lovely rooms at a good price”
text: I have stayed at the Kimberley many times now, and just decided to write a review as they can be a useful guide when checking out where to stay. The Kimberley is a pretty low frills hotel of luxury suites. In New York, you can pay a pretty high price for a spacious high quality suite, but I have found the Kimberley to offer pretty good value in this regard. It is in mid town, so fairly well located but depends where you want to be. If you want to be downtown or spend most of your visit downtown, then this is not the place to stay, but if you want to be close to most of Manhatten and visit all over, this is a good location. The suites are very well appointed, very comfortable and very clean. There is an adequate gym and the roof terrace is a very good spot to have a cocktail, but definately expect the usual New York prices to apply there. Worth it though in my view. To be honest, I was teetering between a 4 and 5 star review here as it is not amazing, but the suites are really very nice at good value, and as I have been several times it does get the top rating for value for money and overall quality.

name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Midtown East
title: “Central location for a NYC stay”
text: I enjoyed my four-night stay at this hotel. We took the train from Newark to Penn station. If you have light luggage coming to NYC, jump on the red 1 line to Houston. The subway is right in front and next to the hotel building, super convenient. Take the same line to uptown Times Square (or further) or downtown South Ferry (view of statue of Liberty). We walked downtown since it is not that far to experience the city (Tribeca). Room is clean and the concierge is very friendly with any questions you may have about the city. Just a few blocks east is the Flatiron District with shopping and great food...on foot! Great place to stay all around. I received an email from the GM of this hotel with my confirmation a few days prior. Since I booked it on a Queen bed, I asked if he could change my reservation to two twin beds. Instead of the usual, I can't do it since I pre-booked, he replied with done - now that is first class service, yes I can attitude! Thank you Paul.

name: Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden
title: “Excellent location, very clean & modern”
text:
We had the chance that our room was very recently renovated. My (standard) room was comfortable, spacious, very tidy, and looked very modern. Beds are very comfortable with very nice pillows! Each room has individual heating. Bathroom was very nice and tidy. Rooms are cleaned daily. All staff was very friendly.
Breakfast was included: bagels, toasted bread, jam, philadelphia cheese, fresh fruits, yoghurt, fresh waffles, assortiment of pastries (muffins etc.), scambled eggs, ham, coffee, thee, orange juice ... Personel was constantly refilling food items and keeping things clean. Breakfast area was very nice.
WiFi is for free and there are 2 pc's at the reception which can also be used for free (to surf the www).
Great location since it is close to Penn Station. From JFK airport: take AirTrain to Jamaica and continue to Penn Station using LIRR.

name: Fitzpatrick Manhattan
title: “Great for families”
text:
So, there is good and bad about the Fitzpatrick Manhattan
On the good side: 
You can get a two room suite with kitchenette for the price of most hotel rooms in NY. We have stayed there twice with a young child. If you stay for a good number of nights in a row, you get a good discount. So, for a week this past July, it cost around $250 a night for a REAL two room suite- (not a fake suite that just has an alcove) It was really like a decent sized apartment. That is unbeatable in New York. This is a great option for a family where you want to put the kids to bed before you have to go to bed.
The staff is very nice. Many employees from Ireland. It is a nice small hotel feel. 
The location is great. Right in midtown- a bit more of an upscale area. And, away from the lunacy of Times Square. If you are brining kids to NY- this is a great option- don't stay in Times Square!
and the bad:
Two visits in a row we got to the hotel late at night and they gave us a key. We opened the door only to find the room not ready for us. First time we opened the door to find someone else's clothes still in the closet. I closed the door quickly- they may have been in there. On the second visit, we opened the door to find dirty wine glasses and garbage on the table, and a used shower with wet towels on the floor.
The housekeeping and front desk staff REALLY need to get their act together to know if people have indeed really checked out.
Both of these were shocking and unforgivable for any hotel.
On both ocassions we had this problem only on checkin. The housekeeping was fine for the rest of the time.
So, overall, I recommend this hotel, but the problem above should be noted.

name: Gansevoort Park Avenue NYC
title: “Too much like South Beach”
text: A great new hotel if you like the non-stop beat of club music in the lobby. The room is stayed in was extremely comfortable, well designed and very quiet. 24 hrs. access to the gym is a great plus. Food, service and staff were all excellent and I would return on my next visit to NYC.

name: Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden
title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: Highly recommend like most of the other reviews. Great location. We came in to NYC at Penn Station and only a block away. Subway and taxis at both corners. Very good breakfast. Wifi in room. Street front room a little noisy but its ok to us to hear city noise. Room and bath size adequate.

name: The Kimberly Hotel
title: “great value”
text: The Kimberly is a great little hotel in mid-town. The staff is very friendly and helpful. It is an all suites hotel. Traveling with 3 other women, this hotel worked the best. There is a lot of room with a nice size bathroom, and many mirrors. The new rooftop bar is nice, but pricey. We love The Kimberly.

name: Candlewood Suites New York City Times Square
title: “Great Location, Friendly Staff”
text: We stayed at this hotel for five nights in October. The price was reasonable for NYC and all the rooms have a small kitchen, a desk and a comfortable chair. The location is great. One block from a subway entrance, walking distance to Time Square and the Theater District. The entire staff were friendly and helpful. Michael, the front desk manager even emailed me after returning home, to make sure that a small problem had been resolved. We definately plan on staying here again.

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan / Times Square South
title: “satisyfying stay”
text: The hotel overall was great. A great breakfast was available both mornings. The front desk agent (i believe it was kelvin? Calvin?) was very nice and polite. We needed to check our bags when we arrived and when we were leaving and they were more than happy to do so. That was a great touch. The only problem I had was the small rooms. Nothing you can do about that in New York though. The hotel is also within walking distance of the times square and everything else.

name: Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden
title: “Excellent customer service”
text: I can't say I've experienced customer service like this in any other hotel in NYC. On our last day, "Coty" offered to get a cab for us because with all the construction on 31st St., cabs were few and far between. It was POURING rain. He got on his raincoat, disappeared for about 5-10 minutes and came back with a cab. Thanks Coty.

name: Candlewood Suites New York City Times Square
title: “Great location, suite and staff!”
text:
Stayed here with my mum for nearly two weeks whilst visiting friends in June 2011. The hotel staff were friendly and professional and our suite was just what we needed for our stay. 
You get a nice size bed, TV, drawers, desk, closet and very handy kitchen area - large fridge/freezer with ice maker, sink, dishwasher, stove for pans with microwave oven, cutlery, pans etc... we could cook our own food, store cool water and snacks - this was good as we enjoyed grocery shopping in the city too - this is NYC though and there are also loads of tempting diners and Restaurant Row isn't too far away!
When we needed help with a problem with the dishwasher this was sorted out almost right away and the engineer who was sent up to fix the dishwasher was efficient.
The laundry is free which is a huge bonus for us as we stayed for a couple of weeks and finding/going to a launderette was not on the agenda! There were enough machines/dryers for our laundry and we didn't have to wait around in order to get a machine. 
The lifts (elevators!) are nice and fast (this is especially good if you're on a higher floor like we were) and the sweets (candy!) and freshly baked cookies at reception could not be ignored either! :)
The location is great for Times Square and the Fashion District. Port Authority is nearby. All areas within walking distance. The area is ok, very busy at all times, and as anyone knows in a large city you have to be street wise, not look like a tourist and take a taxi when travelling late at night.
The rooms are clean, well decorated, have great air-con for those humid summer months, a handy kitchen, good shower, and the staff also add something extra to the place. Good prices for NYC too may I add!

name: The Kimberly Hotel
title: “Best hotel in NYC I've stayed at”
text:
The location (mid-town) was convenient. The room was clean, and had all sorts of amenities. There was an iPod dock (and radio alarm clock in one), a coffee-maker (and also tea available), a small refrigerator, a microwave, a bathroom scale, two white terry bathrobes and slippers, two umbrellas, a small safe, and even an electronic shoe-shiner. They had the usual shampoo and lotion (Neutrogena brand), but also had conditioner (which I’ve noticed a lot of hotels don’t have) and mouthwash. So, more than you usually see in a hotel room. 
By New York City standards, the room was definitely large, and that was a nice surprise. The bathtub was also quite large, great for a bath. The shower pressure was good. They used Neutrogena shampoo, conditioner, and lotion, which I liked—I like nothing too perfumed or fancy. 
The bed was extremely comfortable for me—not too soft and not too hard. Lots of pillows. There were also two nice chairs and a table, a desk and a chair, and an enormous widescreen TV on the wall. 
The front desk and lobby people were very helpful and pleasant. I was very happy with the hotel and would definitely come to the Kimberly again.

name: The Gotham Hotel
title: “What a great find!”
text: I, like many others found my way to The Gotham Hotel by way of Living Social, but I would love to find my way back again. My cousin and I have talked about spending a weekend in Manhattan and this deal was too good to pass up. I loved the quirky nature of the hotel. I loved the greeting process, that there wasn't a "desk" but a personalized greeting, an offered glass of wine, books to peruse (since the Hotel took over the Gotham Bookstore real estate and built upwards, they give their roots a nod with books in the rooms and the lobby!) Our upgrade gave us a great view from the balcony on the 17th floor. The amenities were fun as well - sparkling wine, oranges, and cookies. Thanks for a great place to lauch our daily adventures. And the Tenpenny was great. Again, breakfasts were so good there was no need to start the day elsewhere and our dinner was great both service and food!!

name: The Kimberly Hotel
title: “Extremely Efficient, Comfortable, Convenient Hotel”
text:
I attended a regional conference at the Kimberly's new board room and stayed at the property. The one thing that struck me about my first stay here was the extreme efficiency of the staff. As a customer, I was not only recognized but valued. This showed through at the front desk, at the bell stand, by housekeeping and by the meetings staff.
The rooms are extremely well appointed, luxurious and comfortable and geared towards both business and leisure guests. The bathroom was extremely impressive (large space) as well as a rain shower, a weighing scale and great soap products.
The bed has multiple feather pillows and is extremely comfortable. The closet is a walk-in, fully closable closet with a safe that fits a laptop, which I greatly appreciated.

name: Comfort Inn Lower East Side
title: “Great Location, Great Hotel Staff”
text:
GREAT location on LES. 7 nights here. Rooms are small but clean. Hotel staff is excellent. Coffee maker and fridge in room. Flat screen TV with HBO and fast highspeed internet. Breakfast is offered each morning but not a great selection if you aren't carb loading. (waffles, bagels, toast, pastry etc). If you want to stay on LES, the location could not be better. Fantastic food nearby Stanton Social, Beauty and Essex, Meatball Shop, WD 50, and casual food landmark Katz Deli etc. Also great people watching and bars and cool dive bars all around. Transit accessible. Service is as good as the 5 star place we have stayed at in the past. Housekeeping could be a bit more thourough and come a little earlier. They usually were coming when we had been gone all day and we were coming back to rest and change again to go out again. 
Use Quick Ride Corporation you can find on yelp, instead of taxis to and from the airport and during traffic times it will be cheaper than a taxi.

name: The Marcel at Gramercy
title: “Cool vibe with intimate feel”
text: I would recommend this hotel to those who are seeking a chic hotel with an intimate feel, who insist on a comfortable, quiet room with hip decor. The professionals at the front desk are very helpful. I extended my stay at the Marcel instead of going to the Hilton where I get reward points. I stayed nine days and was delighted with every aspect of the hotel. Jacquelin, the front office manager, always answered my smart phone 'texts' quickly when I was out and about and had a few questions during my stay. All the employees are top notch, from those at the front door to those who make sure the top floor sitting area and rooftop patio is 'just right'. The Marcel has an intimate, calm feel to it but when you walk out the door, you are only minutes from everything that you will need in NYC!

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “New York”
text: Hotel was beautiful. The room was bigger than most New York hotel rooms. Which made the stay that much better. Very clean and the staff was so friendly and helpful!! The gym is HUGE and the spa is fantastic

name: Hilton Club New York
title: “Definitely should consider over regular Hilton”
text:
Stayed at the Hilton Club for a couple of nights on business. As others have noted, this is like a "hotel within a hotel" -- occupying only the 37th and 38th floors of the massive New York Hilton Hotel towers. There is a separate check in on the 37th floor, at the entrance to the lounge area where breakfast is served in the morning and an early evening cocktail hour is featured. This helps remove the hotel from the usual "convention crowd" feel of the Hilton.
I stayed in a studio suite, which was surprisingly large with updated furnishings and bedding. Quite handsome. Flat screen TV, iPod dock, mini-fridge, coffee maker, bathrobes, safe, etc. I would have preferred a desk over the small round table but it was adequate.
