Breakfast, afternoon cocktails and WiFi are included in the rate. The breakfast was decent considering the rather small lounge area -- nothing hot other than drinks, but there is a Nespresso machine, juices, cereals, pastries, fresh fruit and hard boiled eggs.
If you are a Diamond Hilton Honors member, you might get a better upgrade staying at the regular part of the Hilton, but I found the Club to be a good value and it was extremely convenient for me.

name: Mondrian Soho
title: “What a amazing hotel”
text:
We were in New York for a friends wedding and the this hotel was very close to the church where the wedding was taking place. When we arrived at the hotel at noon the door staff were very helpful and attentive. You are greeted with the most refreshing fresh aroma driffting through the lobby. Our cases were taken to our rooms without any request. 
The room is a little on the small size and may have been better with a queen bed rather than a king.
All the staff are very very helpful nothing is too much trouble from cabs, hair salons, places to eat and directions. 
Big thanks go to the bar tender Ruben, lobby manager Alex and all the reception staff.
I had a problem with the sink plug which was replaced, the in room iPad did not charge and was not rectified in the time we were there but no big problem.
This is a great hotel I will stay here again away from the hussle of mid town, in the center of the Island and easy to get anywhere. This is a must for your sight seeing stay in NY.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Unacceptable At This Price”
text:
for $500 a night, i should be able to set the room temperature to anything I want. But no. I walk in at 1am and the thermostat is set to 80 degrees. I lower it to 67, but warm air is still coming out of the unit.
The front desk's response - we don't have air conditioning. Instead they tell me to turn off the thermostat and open the window. BUT the window doesn't open.
SO I wait for the engineer to come help. He takes forever. 
So now I have the EXTREMELY LOUD noises from the street cooling my room. 
My choices are either NOT SLEEPING because it's too loud in the room, or NOT SLEEPING because it's 80 degrees in the room.
Don't stay here if you want to sleep.

name: The Marcel at Gramercy
title: “Great overnight stay”
text:
Really a four-and-a-half overall. Nicely located between our midtown and Soho destinations. We took the middle-size room, it was "Superior room, king bed". The 180 square foot room + small bath was large enough, and was reasonably priced. Very clean and comfortable, the room felt larger because of modern decor and a high ceiling. It was very quiet in our room. Dim lighting reminiscent of Europe and Montreal.
Nice lounge (and outer patio) on top floor where breakfast was served and for free internet access. We would certainly return to this hotel.

name: Comfort Inn Lower East Side
title: “The Price is Right!”
text: For New York City LES close to SoHo this hotel was awesome. Clean, friendly and great location. For the price this place was outstanding. Highly recommend if you don't have a lot of $$$ but want to stay in the city in a real hotel.

name: AKA United Nations
title: “Love it here”
text: This AKA is very conveniently located for me. Very near Grand Central for subway access. Even though they have no restaurant or room service, the area has many good restaurants, diners, and groceries with prepared foods. The staff is very nice and the rooms are great.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Very convenient!”
text:
So far, I think this is one of the best hotels in the city, modern and classy lobby, I got a nice room and good service. 
Another point is Burger place, located on ground floor... Very convenient.
This place is just south of central park (3blocks-big bonus) and easily walkable to times square, and had several subway lines minutes away. Definitely consider if its in your budget!

name: New York Marriott East Side
title: “Another Disappointng Stay”
text: We've have stayed in the New York Marriott East Side the second week-end of December for the past 8 or 9 years. One would hope the hotel would make an effort to reach the minimum services Marriott offers its best customers. Not this hotel. Front desk is very patronizing and, inspite of the "Oh we're so glad you're here and thanks for being so loyal to Marriott' assigns run of the house room on a lower floor where there's lots of street noise. Housekeep is non-repsopnsive to requests - heck, even in New York they should be able to deliver a towel in less than 3 hours. The music is unbearably loud in the gym and the lower floor elevators stop once every 3 days. It goes on and on. Breaking up is always hard to do but next year when we return we'll stay around the corner at the Hyatt where the rooms and service have to be better than this.

name: Wyndham Garden Hotel Manhattan, Chelsea West
title: “Clean Hotel, Good Service, Great Location”
text:
My husband and I stayed here during a 3 day trip to NYC. The staff is VERY friendly and accomodating. We also thought that the location was great with easy Subway access. There are a lot of nice bars and restaurants on the block and we felt very safe in this area.
We would recommend this for travelors who don't intend to be in the room very much. It is very small and provides just the basics. The decor is lacking, but we found the king size bed to be very comfortable. The shower was OK - no bath tub. We had a pleasant experience at this hotel, and I only gave it an "Average" rating because I have stayed at much larger hotels that provided more ammenities. 
In the end, we were looking for an affordable, clean hotel with a good location and the Wyndham provided us with that experience!

name: Wyndham Garden Hotel Manhattan, Chelsea West
title: “Just a clean bed and bathroom”
text:
Don't expect a lot from this hotel besides a clean bed, room and bathroom. Rooms are TINY even by Manhattan standards. Bathroom is basic shower. No services, reception or facities to speak anything of. Area is a little quiet with not much to do, but go a little further and there's tons.
PS: the Italian retaurant opposite the hotel was fabulous!

name: Comfort Inn Manhattan Bridge
title: “Couldn't be better, unless it was cheapter”
text:
It's expensive to stay in Manhattan. That's my only complaint. 
The hotel is pretty new, very clean and everything is in good shape. We had a loft (a queen bed and a bathroom on the first floor and a second bed on a second floor). It had two new remote controlled AC units, 2 flat screen TVs.
The breakfast room was small, but the breakfast was about the same as what you see at other hotels.
It is two blocks from a subway station, it was pretty easy to get to the statue of liberty (from Battery Park), central park and times square from this train station, although there were a few transfers. The hotel is on the edge of Chinatown, which we enjoyed. We had a great view of the Manhattan Bridge from our room. The hotel was attached to an underground parking garage ($30/day) and we just left our car there for 3 days.
The staff was awesome, happy to give us directions and advice, very friendly and professional... not at all what I would expect in NY. I believe the woman who dealt with us the most was named Kirsten. 
Wireless internet was fast enough.
We had 3 adults and a baby, even with the two stories, we felt a little cramped, but in NY, what can you expect. 
Overall we enjoyed the stay, and if we go to NY again, we will definitely consider this hotel first.

name: The Gotham Hotel
title: “Nice, but pricey”
text:
Nice boutique hotel. Though in the heart of midtown only little noise, and mostly from the ac. Turndown service was... A big apple!
However, almost 400 dollars a night is a bit pricey...

name: Excelsior Hotel
title: “GREAT HOTEL”
text: This is a small quiet upper east side hotel . It is close to a subway stop, and with in 2 blocks of several great resturants . The staff , including the desk people were very friendly . The room is quite large for NY style .The bath room/shower is VERY large .

name: The Manhattan Club
title: “Great Night in the City”
text: We stayed here with our two adult children for one night. The room was clean and the check-in and out was easy. Valet parking was very convenient. Location was great for the places we wanted to visit. I would stay here again.

name: Doubletree Hotel New York City-Financial District
title: “Worst service ever”
text: I showed up last night to check into the hotel after a work dinner. I left my luggage in the morning. The manager, George, said someone had cancelled my reservation and the hotel was sold out. He, then, said I could wait until 2:30 am for a potential room (if a guest does not show up). He tried to blame me for the cancellation. When I said I would complain to Hilton Honors, he said to go ahead and complain. I stay at hotels every week, and this is the worst service I have had. Definitely love SPG for their service and hospitality. I don't know if I will book at a Hilton again after this. Hilton Honors was not helpful. In the end, I moved to the Sheraton, which easily gave me a room. This morning, I talked to the Director and she was kind enough to compensate me with enough points for one night, but I do not think this makes up for the terrinle service and having to go cross town to another hotel in the middle of the night.

name: The Manhattan Club
title: “Abysmal Sales Pitch Experience”
text:
This story starts a year and a half ago. I booked a couple of nights for our family of four at the Manhattan Club -- using the hotel's own website to do so. We were in what is called a "Junior Executive Suite," which was a bedroom, 1 bath, a partially separate small living area with a pullout couch and a little kitchenette. The room was fine. It was not particularly memorable --- the room was fine but ready for refurbishment; the shower fixture was pulled out from the wall and leaky, a small pedestal sink with no place in the bath to put stuff, and more than a normal layer of dust on baseboards, etc. A room like you would find in any aging 3 star airport hotel is pretty much what comes to mind. Our teenage kids put up with the terrible mattress on the couch, but it was just as bad as other reviews of the sofabed indicate. Our overall assessment was that the location was terrific and the hotel completely forgettable.
Soon after returning home, I received a call from the sales department, inviting us back to stay again for a reduced rate, and to "take a tour." I said that we are not interested in sales pitches, but would be willing to learn more about ownership, but that we certainly would not purchase on the spot. She said that was all they wanted was a chance to "impress us" with the wonderful opportunities of ownership at the Manhattan Club. I agreed to it, my card was charged, and then at the confirmation I learned that the accommodations would be "in our sister deluxe hotel right around the corner, with which we would be delighted." We then needed to reschedule several times due to various family circumstances, and finally made the trip, staying August 15-17.
When we checked into the "Sister Hotel" -- The Park Central -- we discovered the Trip Advisor reviews are spot on. It's a 2-3 star hotel, with a high turnover and occupancy due to location. We had the teenagers, so 4 of us were crammed in a small room. The staff was very pleasant, and it was fine for what it was. Not a place you would pick to stay for any reason but where it sits. Ironically, since we'd first been moved there from the promise of the Manhattan Club, and then had to pay extra to bring the kids and to pay a rescheduling fee, we were only paying about $15 less a night for the room than we would have if we'd simply booked the Park Central on Expedia.
But a deal's a deal. My husband and I showed up on time for the "tour" of the Manhattan Club. We were assigned a salesperson named Arnie, who proceeded with a classic timeshare sales pitch, the gist of which was that this was only a same day offer. If we did not sign on the spot, it would go away and never come back.
He began by learning that we had previously stayed at the Manhattan Club, and said, "you can never stay there again." I explained several times that I'd booked it as a hotel, not as part of a stay connected with a tour, and that we'd never been offered a tour, nor were we particularly clear about the timeshare angle when we stayed there. The offer of the tour came after we left. He said again that we could never stay there again, and when it was evident we found that odd, he said that the MC "used" to sell unused rooms to the general public, but that they quit doing that, in order to save the rooms for owners. The only way to stay at the Manhattan Club is to be an owner. Which was why, he said, that we were staying at the Park Central, which he would guess we were not enjoying, and that it is like a Holiday Inn or something, and they didn't put us there to punish us, but that only owners or potential owners can stay at the Manhattan Club, and we had already had our opportunity, and shouldn't think we could get back in.
I pointed out again that our stay was the result of booking with the MC's own website. He said that had stopped, and went on to tout why people would come to NYC on a regular basis. And how little the money is compared to the advantages. When it was evident that price points needed to be talked about, he explained a complicated scheme of ownership, depending upon whether one wishes weekend stays, and whether one wants to split a week between 2 years or take one week per year. The week per year basically fell into a $45K to $50K range for purchase, plus more than 2K per year in maintenance fees. When it was evident we weren't even going to talk about that much money, he moved further down the food chain with other options.
When he left to give us a chance to talk it over, I pulled up the hotel website on my iPad, plus several of the other booking websites. Many of which offer the Manhattan Club as a hotel room for non owners, making his vehement start off statements false. As I was staring at this on the iPad, he came back in and said, nastily, "What? You're texting someone?" I actually, at that point, thought he might be unaware that he wasn't telling the truth about the availability of the MC to non-owners. He cut me off and went on to describe their lowest options of ownership, on the "second floor," and splitting one week between 3 years (which still costs you 10K to buy into, plus maintenance fees." 
We reiterated that we had said when booking that we would never make a same day decision, and that we hadn't suddenly changed our minds about that. He then snarled, "I'm done here. I'm through with you." and went slamming out of his office, threw our paperwork at the receptionist so she could produce a dining certificate, and stomped away without thanking us for our time, or closing the conversation in any civil way.
All of this was most interesting, which caused me to look up the actual experiences of owners trying to book stays, and being unable to secure availability due to overbooking with non owner guests.
So, the stay at the Manhattan Club was fine. Not special. But fine as long as the pullout couch wasn't involved. The Park Central was an adequate place to say with a terrible mattress. And the sales experience meant we definitely earned the $100 dining certificate, which still did not remove the bad taste of the experience. If a reasonable rate is available at the MC, and you can be sure of not being moved to the Park Central, I'd stay there again. But I'd skip the "tour."

name: New York Marriott East Side
title: “Nice option in Midtown Center/East”
text: My wife and I stayed here for one night while in town for a party. Definitely more of a business/tourist location than true neighborhood, but certainly a solid option, and at a decent price. Old building with small elevators and rooms but lobby, hallways, and rooms are fairly updated. As is usually the case, Marriott comes through with a reliable and clean property.

name: Mondrian Soho
title: “Great place to stay”
text:
We spent a long weekend here and found the place to be a hidden gem.
I have stayed at a lot of the hotels around this area and I think I have now found
My place to stay in NYC.
All of the staff were fantastic and nothing was too much trouble.
Rooms are great lots of natural sunlight and an opening window.
I will be returning in August 2012 with a group.

name: The Manhattan Club
title: “Delighted with our Lodging in Manhatten.”
text: The Manhatten club is a time share. Everyone was so nice and VERY helpful for someone that has never been to New York. It was a GREAT location, we could walk to almost everything we wanted to visit. We took a five hour tour the first day we got there so we knew what we wanted to go back to see. We did take a Taxi to and from the airport and WOW those gentlemen know how to drive. They can get through anything. Do try Manhatten Club, you won't be sorry.

name: Comfort Inn Manhattan Bridge
title: “Lo consiglierei”
text:
Allora per dirla in pochi termini. 
Quello di positivo è:
1) camere relativamente grandi per NY
2) buona location a 2 minuti dalla metro
3) OTTIMA LA COLAZIONE A BUFFET!!!!!!!
4) NON CI SONO BEDBUGS NEL LETTO!!
Quello di negativo è:
1) muri sottili
2) porta del bagno scorrevole che non scorreva
3) cambiano le lenzuola poco (1 volta a sett)
Il prezzo è alto per l'Italia (ad un prezzo così da noi si prende un hotel superlusso) ma buono per Nyc. In media 200 a notte

name: Excelsior Hotel
title: “Nice quiet location on UWS”
text: Stayed here 4 nights on a family vacation. The hotel is conveniently located, just 1/2 block from the subway and the American Museum of Natural History, bus stops close by too. Central Park is 1./2 block away, and Roosevelt Park across the street (surrounding the AMNH). The hotel has a small but elegant lobby, and helpful staff. Fast check-in and check-out. Our double room was small by most US hotel standards, but not by NYC (or London) standards. Bath was also small, and outdated decor, but this is not important to us. Did not eat in the hotel restaurant. There are several restaurants within 2 blocks, including fast-food (Shake Shack), chain (Uno's), deli, diner, coffee shops (including Starbuck's), and local mid-priced places. Our room faced the back, so no view but very quiet.

name: The Mercer Hotel
title: “Fabulous NYC experience!”
text: We just loved this hotel! Everything was better than expected - from the location right in the heart of Soho, to the chic decor, to the ambiance, to the attentiveness of the staff (not too little or too much) to all the room extras - no charge for most of the honor bar items (except the alcohol of course). And that's saying a lot as our expectations were pretty high given the room prices. We felt like we were treated just as well and made to feel just as welcome as the couple of celebrities that we saw staying there as well. That was one complaint I had heard about the hotel before our stay but we had no such poor attitudes from the staff. It had a very exclusive feel to the whole experience. And The Kitchen (the hotel's restaurant) was also fabulous. I would stay there again in a heartbeat.

name: Doubletree Hotel New York City-Financial District
title: “Had a great 7 day stay”
text:
Stayed on 44th floor. Had a nice (partial) view of the bay. No problem with the elevators. . Room service was excellent,and the room was cleaned thoroughly every day. As we eat only Kosher food, had to turn down the cookies we were offered. We were able to purchase Kosher food snacks at around-the-corner Duanereade drugstore, coffee at Starbucks on different corner and t/a Kosher sandwiches on the corner of Broad and William streets nearby. 
Visited nearby attractions on foot such as the NYSE, South Ferry,South Street Seaport, Brooklyn Bridge and the Twin Towers area.
The hotel is situated near various subway lines and bus lines too, so that we had freedom of motion in all directions
Unfortunately - no nearby synagogues , made other arrangements for Sabbath.
Before we checked out , the concierge arranged a shuttle for us to JFK and saved us some money, as we planned to take a regular cab.
It would be nice if the hotel would have had a scale to weigh our suitcases before we left, to be sure we weren't overweight. ( We continued to JFK ). Instead we took them to the post-office nearby , so it was no big deal.
Would definitely recommend the hotel to others.

name: Comfort Inn Manhattan Bridge
title: “Komfortabel in schöner Lage”
text: Das Hotel liegt im Süden Manhattans direkt an der Manhattan Bridge und bietet aus den höheren Etagen grossartige Blicke über Downtown und auf den East River. Der Empfang war ausgesprochen freundlich, das Zimmer ausreichend groß, sehr sauber und mit TV, Klimaanlage, Safe und Kaffemaschine gut ausgestattet, lediglich eine Minibar war nicht vorhanden. Ein kostenloses Frühstück ist inbegriffen, ungewöhnlich für New York. Angeboten wurden neben Kaffee und Säften Cornflakes, Muffins, Toast, frische Waffeln, Butter Marmelade und Joghurt, also völlig ausreichend. Auch stehen in der Lobby zwei Rechner mit kostenlosem Internetzugang, sogar das Drucken war umsonst. Das Hotel befindet sich am Rande Chinatowns, südlich der Lower East Side, die in den letzten Jahren "hip" geworden ist. Wall Street, Soho, die Piers und Brooklyn liegen in entspannter Laufnähe, die U-Bahn ist ums Eck, so dass man in guten 10 Minuten auch Midtown erreicht. Mit der U-Bahn kann man auch direkt für etwa 7 Dollar in einer Stunde JFK erreichen, ich war vollends zufrieden, eine Empfehlung!

name: Washington Square Hotel
title: “"Inexpensive" typical non-chain NYC Hotel”
text:
New York City hotel rooms are small. Unless you get a suite, it doesn't matter if you pay $650 or $250 night. Of course, "usually" the more you pay the more amenities are available at the hotel.
The Washington Square Hotel is one of those non-chain hotels that can be found on many streets in NYC and which can be a real find or a real disaster. I consider the WSH a find. It was recommended to me by the company I was visiting in the area when all other hotels, even the "economy" brands were asking $550+ for one night.
As noted, the room was small, but updated and clean. The bathroom was fine for one or two persons. The only downside was in an effort to keep it very clean, it had a faint smell of bleach which must be used to keep the old style tile floor clean. There was a window AC unit which work very well, but was kind of loud. I finally turned it off in the middle of the night so it wouldn't wake me as it cycled on and off. But I am a light sleeper.
Check in was easy and very pleasant. Without asking I was offered a map and directions (which I didn't need). I had a drink in the small bar. A generous drink for a fair (NYC) price was provided by a pleasant server. It was a welcome respite after a long day of travel to the city. I did not partake of the free continental breakfast.
Free WIFI was available throughout the hotel.
This is a fine hotel if you're looking for a less expensive, less frills hotel near the village (and NYU). Many subway lines have stations within two or three blocks. I will stay here again when business brings me back to this area.

name: Comfort Inn Manhattan Bridge
title: “bon hotel tres agreable”
text: j'ai choisi cette hotel car en regardant ls commentaire, son prix pour le sejour sachant quil y avait le petit dej, je trouvais le tout tres bien et je confirme tout cela, l hotel est tres agrable, le personnel tres serviable et les chambre super confortable avec une grande salle de bain beignoire douche. Il y a une bouche de metro a 100m de l'hotel ce qui a new york est indispensable surtout que la ligne de metro traverse manhattan du sud au nord donc tres pratique!!!! Le seul probleme de cette hotel c'est le lieu ou il se trouve, on se demande meme d'ou il sort car chinatown c'est un peu pourri mais bon on se reconforte vite car on reste pas non plus dans ce quatier tellement que new york est grandiose!!!!!

name: Hotel 373
title: “Location location”
text:
We stayed here for eight nights over st patricks wk. We'er seasoned travelers n have stayed in many hotels in USA n Europe. Rooms are very small but very clean n modern, ensuite was nice. I'm over six foot n slept in the bed fine, street noise doesn't bother us but remember it's on 5th ave! We were in ny to sight 
see n shop so didn't spend any time
 in hotel only at night, which is good cause there's only the small room n starbucks to hang out in but we knew this when booking. Location is fantastic, we looked out on empire state from bedrm window! Macys n time sq 5 min walk, central park 10/15 min walk n hop on off bus tours pass across the st! Hardly used underground n only taxi twice! Staff were friendly n helpful. If your looking for large reception area, restuarant etc stay elsewhere. But for great location n very clean rooms for little money then 373 is the place. Ps not easy find the building for the first time even standing ar the street corner, small sign on glass door. traveled from Ireland n would defo stay here again n recommend.

name: The Mercer Hotel
title: “Immerse yourself in NY Mercer-style”
text: Mercer lived up to all expectations. Understated cool, superb location and far enough away from the business world to let you really relax and enjoy the shopping and village atmosphere unique to this part of Manhattan. Rooms are large (we had a Mercer room), bright, airy (and not noisy with the window open - Mercer St is hardly busy by NY standards) with white walls and high ceilings. Emphasis is on simple lines, comfort and space. And let's not forget that cool edge that seems to come naturally . Will just have to upgrade to the loft rooms next time!

name: Mondrian Soho
title: “Great boutique hotel in SOHO”
text: The Mondrian hotel was an oasis of calm, quality, and service in the middle of soho. The food was seriously the best prepared and presented and of course the best tasting ! The rooms are spotles and ver funkyly decorated and yea the are reall small, I mean closet size small but they are very nice, comfortable and unheard of in New York they were not noisy at all.

name: The Manhattan Club
title: “Great location”
text: The Manhattan Club is located just below Central Park, across the street from Carnegie Hall. The staff is friendly and helpful. The rooms are spacious for NYC. It's any easy walk to Times Square or any Broadway show.

name: The Marcel at Gramercy
title: “Great staff and location”
text: Just returned from a business/leisure trip. On first arrival, we were put in a room the size of a closet- do not let pictures fool you. However, we were promised an upgrade from the "standard" room the next day. Patience proved worthy. New room was much better and roomy. Staff was exceptional. To note: Raoul and Dan the doormen. Raoul knew us by name and made the big city feel small and quaint-which is the feel you get staying here. Front desk helpful so make sure you talk to them. Because of that, any hotel lack was forgivable. Place is clean and contemporary chic. Great location- central from everything. easy to get to subway and times-square and local eateries. Do not compare to your big chains but you will get a decent boutique hotel. Would return just for Raoul ,Dan and front desk staff.

name: Hotel 373
title: “Great Value/Location/Property”
text:
I stayed one night...called from the airport and booked the room. Friendly staff, very clean room, standard room perfect for solo traveler. Noise not a problem...comfortable bed and linens. Staff was prompt in delivering forgotten toiletries/iron, etc. Lobby is adjacent to Starbucks open until midnight. 
Would definitely return.

name: The Milburn Hotel
title: “Nice hotel”
text: Stayed there 2-3 weeks last summer, nice rooms, good service and houskeeping. It had also free internet, the breakfast was okay.

name: Mondrian Soho
title: “Cool, convenient hotel which will appeal to many”
text:
My partner and I stayed at the Mondrian SoHo for 2 nights, while we were working in NYC. We found an excellent deal on a discount hotel website, and ended up with a small but nice room on the 7th floor of the hotel. Our taxi driver was confused about where the entrance was, as there is no name on the hotel (typical for Ian Shrager hotels). But we found a lovely garden and walked through to see the entrance to the hotel. There is quite a lively bar/restaurant in the lobby, with gorgeous décor and even more gorgeous people. (We later stopped down for a drink and found it to be pricey but exciting to watch).
The front desk is one floor up from the ground. The staff were friendly and efficient, and were diligent about security procedures (verifying our identity). The elevators were a bit slow to take us to our floor. Our room was white-themed with a slightly whimsical design. We had a very comfortable queen sized bed with a fluffy white comforter, and drawers under the bed. There was an ample closet to both hold our suitcase and hang clothing, as well as having a safe. The room also had a desk area with ipad with lots of interesting selections/controls for the room. The TV was a flat screen with great quality – only issue is that it seemed to be on some sort of timer, where it would switch off at 10:30pm, switch back on at 12:30am and again at 6:30am. Never could figure out how to turn it off! Our room had a window which opened, and a broad view of the street with a peek at some buildings on the skyline.
The bathroom had an external sink (outside the bathroom door, with mini bar underneath. The bathroom itself had a toilet and shower/tub combination. We were impressed to see a handheld shower as well as an overhead one, and a deep tub as well. It would have been perfect if only there wasn’t a small leak from the central control area. The toiletries were super interesting, e.g. mint shampoo and rum shower gel. And the towels were wonderful.
 The neighborhood is typical SoHo, quite industrial on the nearby blocks but quickly changing to shopping to the north and Canal Street to the south. The cab ride to downtown was quick and cheap, definitely a convenient location for Wall Street, etc. We would definitely consider staying again.

name: Mondrian Soho
title: “Trendy Hotel. Great Location!”
text: Keeping to our theme of NYC weekends for birthday get aways, we decided to experience another Morgan Group Hotel. We had the best time in Miami at the Delano and looked forward to our stay in NYC. The service was great. The concierge was helpful in providing things in the area to do as well as restaurant reservation. Their recommendation for The Darby was a perfect fit for what we were looking for. If I were to provide any feedback in this regard I'd simply ask to be informed of any unique charges a restaurant would charge. The Darby provided live music which was FANTASTIC, but I was a bit surprised with the $50 "Entertainment" charge. The room was trendy and neat, equipped with an I pad, Ipod doc, great use of space. The walls were a bit thin so we heard the elevator as well as the pepople walking through the halls. But overall we had a great stay. The hotel in general was very fashionably decorated, so much so that I took pictures to add some style to my own home. The location of the Mondrian was ideal. We walked for hours and just loved the surrounding area. I'd recommend a stay at the Mondrian, along with any Morgans Group Hotel. I am looking forward to trying the next hotel from the group.

name: Excelsior Hotel
title: “A fine hotel, excellent location”
text: The Excelsior Hotel in Upper West side of Manhattan has one superb qualification: it's location! On W 81st street, it is a few buildings from Central Park, across the street from the Museum of Natural History, right near subway entrance, and near some shops and restaurants I enjoy: e.g. Schweitzer's Linens. Otherwise, it is pleasant, well appointed, with comfortable beds. The rooms are small but the furnishings are good quality. I had an uncertain, unconfirmed encounter with a bed bug, as I woke up with a few bites on my neck. They could have arisen from a walk through central park the previous day or from a close encounter with a bed bug while asleep. Unless confirmed by another stay, I cannot attribute the welts to the hotel. The staff at the front desk needs some additional training in welcoming guests, but all in all, a good experience.

name: New York Marriott East Side
title: “A great location and a nice place to stay”
text: I've stayed here about five times in total. I love the ease of access to the rest of Manhattan and the central location, with Grand Central station and the Chrysler building around the corner. The rooms are fine and the beds very comfortable. The gym is located at the top of the building , accessible via a quirky lift that just goes from the top room floor upwards. THe views from the gym are fantastic and the gym room itself has all the equipment you need. It's an old world type hotel with many unusual hotel features such as the oddly shaped lifts and passageways. I never use the hotel restaurant as it is far too expensive and there are great places to eat around town. I would definitely recommend this place if your budget allows.

name: The Manhattan Club
title: “Convenient location”
text: Stayed here with my family of four. Master bedroom and bathroom were very nice. Sofa bed in living area was uncomfortable and squeaked with every move. Elevators were very slow. Bellman was very friendly and helpful, especially in getting us cabs. It was a very convenient place to stay near everything...Times Square, Broadway shows, shopping, Central Park!

name: New York Marriott East Side
title: “Very Clean, Nice Room, Curteous Staff”
text: I had a standard room with 1 large double bed. The bed itself was very comfortable, room was compact but you can still be comfortable for 2 people. Room was VERY clean, nice contemporary decor..looked fresh....nice size bathroom too. Wasn't much of a view but if you're there just for a nite or few, you're not there to be looking our your window anyway. The staff was very polite and curteous. I would recommend this hotel for anyone on business, visiting friends in the area, or similar.

name: The Milburn Hotel
title: “Convenient, friendly, affordable hotel”
text: The Milburn Hotel is in a great neighborhood, is really affordable and has a friendly staff. Also, they offer a continental breakfast, which allows you to relax a bit before the day begins. I have stayed here three times when I am in NY for work and have turned co-workers on to it as well. Having a refrigerator and microwave in the room also allows you to buy food in the shops nearby or bring back your leftovers from dinner to have later.

name: Roger Smith Hotel
title: “Fabulous hotel, wonderful staff”
text:
Love staying at the Roger Smith Hotel. The staff are so friendly and warm, and the service is excellent. Especially love the artwork. 
Great location, close to everything - will definitely be back. And the wireless is free!

name: Doubletree Hotel New York City-Financial District
title: “I don't know what everyone is complaining about, I loved it!”
text: The location was great, the elevator was HARDLY a problem, the staff were wonderful and the room was NOT tiny, in fact, it was a great size. You've gotta love the warm chocolate chip cookie at check-in, and the rooms have all the amenities you'll ever need, including a STARBUCKS coffeemaker. That's what I call top notch, none of that bitter hotel stock coffee. And the beds are wonderful. I didn't try the restaurants, but hotel restaurants are rarely very good unless they employ some exceptional chef. Don't worry yourself about the elevators, I don't know why everyone makes such a big deal about that, the longest I waited was about a minute and a half. It's a big building people, what's the rush to go up and down??

name: Roger Smith Hotel
title: “This was one of our best picks in nyc hotels!!”
text: We were so happy with our choice of hotel! The staff was friendly, the room was spacious and clean, and the location was great. We'll definitely return! The only negative was that the rooftop bar is not open on the weekends. The accommodating staff did let us take drinks from the bar onto the rooftop, though!! We LOVE Roger Smith Hotel and we'll definitely return!!

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “Good spot for families on Upper West Side”
text:
Great location, right near the Natural History Museum, Central Park & 2 blocks from a nice little playground. 
We booked a family suite, which had 2 rooms & 3 beds -- pretty decent-sized room by my experience with NYC hotels. Rooms are very clean and a good value, too.
My only complaint -- when we first arrived, with a car full of luggage, the bell team were nowhere to be found so I had to unload & bring all the stuff into the lobby myself. Once we found them, they were happy to help. This was really the only concern we had the whole weekend.

name: Mondrian Soho
title: “Put the hotel to the test”
text:
After reading the Tripadivsor reviews I expected the worst from the Mondrian. I expected the business cards I sent, via FedEx, to be lost (but they weren't. Instead, I picked them up from the front desk right on time). I expected the staff to be inattentive (but they were very quick to meet my needs). I expected it to be difficult to hail a cab (but it wasn't - in fact, the doorman actually ran a block and a half up the street to hail a cab). I expected poor service from the concierge (but it was absolutely stellar - in fact, Rachel, the concierge at the time, recommended a fantastic little neighborhood gem of a burger joint just perfect for a quiet, cozy dinner.). I expected room service to be slow (but it was perfectly timed). 
I really can't think of any other tests to put the Mondrian through. It looks like they've incorporated their learnings from previous responses and are well on their way of becoming a fantastic hotel. Will I be back? Yep - absolutely.

name: Soho Grand Hotel
title: “grand and industrial combined”
text:
I loved staying here
through the combination of luxury hotel with some industrial architecture was great, service was good and my room was very comfortable, esp compared to other hotels in NY i have stayed in

name: Washington Square Hotel
title: “Pleasant stay at the Washington Square Hotel”
text:
We came to New York to visit in June, this being our third visit to the city. We decided we wanted to stay in Greenwich Village and hotel choice in this area was pretty limited so we opted for the Washington Square after reading reviews on tripadvisor.
Although the hotel is a bit tired in places, this is a charming little hotel with some lovely art deco touches. Our room was one of the interior rooms as we preferred to have "quiet" over a view. It certainly was quiet as well, we did not hear a peep from outside or from anyone else in the hotel.
Our room was very small and I would have liked to have a little more closet space but this was a small price to pay for being located in Greenwich Village. So much to see and do just on the hotels doorstep. The staff were also friendly and welcoming, always a goodbye or hello when leaving or entrering the hotel.
With regards food, we only ate breakfast at the hotel, this was plentiful and you could also order cooked extras should you prefer. There are simply hundreds of places to eat nearby - I am a vegetarian and had a fantastic meal at a place called "Gobo", just around the corner from the hotel. We also went on one of the many food tours of the area - this was a great way to spend the day.
Overall, a great stay at the Washington Square hotel - I would certainly stay here again.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Location, location, location”
text: Fairly large sized room for NYC, was able to fit the whole family in a double with the fold out couch. Went to the pool on the top for the kids and since it was during a snow storm, was pretty cool to watch the snow fall while they were swimming. Also used the gym and had a nice work out. Starbucks across the street, diners on every corner and Central Park around the corner. Plus if we really had a desire to get to time square, a quick walk down a few blocks. Quite enjoyed.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Would stay again.”
text: Friendly staff, great location. Used SPG points. Offered high room and very late checkout. Great bed, pillows, and towels. The burger smell in the lobby gets old. Would stay again.

name: Club Quarters Wall Street
title: “Club quarters”
text:
Hotel is very clean and staff are very friendly and helpful, rooms are on the small side but they have everything you need. Get a room over looking the memorial park, Nice bar on top floor.
I would stay there again

name: Hotel 373
title: “Great place to stay!”
text: This hotel was amazing for the price. Location was great. We booked the smallest room b/c we knew we would not be in there at all and could have cared less about how small it was-and it was small. Hotel staff was VERY friendly and helpful. Room and hotel was VERY clean. What a great place we will go back again!

name: New York Marriott East Side
title: “Great Location & Comfy Beds”
text: I love NY and have stayed in several places and other than Park Plaza (which is $$$$) this has been my favorite. The location is really close to Grand Central and a fast walk to many other sites. The rooms are on the small side as with many hotel rooms in NY but the beds are great, nice baths and a well maintained property....also had a small fridge in the room.

name: Soho Grand Hotel
title: “Downtown Chic”
text: Just enjoyed four fantastic nights here with my 16 year old daughter and we can't wait to stay here again on our next visit. I don't understand some of the recent negative reviews as we had a great experience on all levels - the entire staff couldn't have been nicer or more friendly, the hotel itself is beautifully outfitted with a very cool, retro, downtown chic decor and the room was spacious, comfortable and very nicely appointed. The concierge members here were some of the best in the business, so helpful with restaurant reservations and assisting with all of our inquiries. The doormen and especially everyone at the front desk were super friendly and welcoming. Special thanks go to Rina with reservations who helped make our stay a most memorable and fantastic experience. She couldn't have been nicer or more helpful. Our corner room on the 15th floor was super quiet with stunning views of the city and more than enough room and closet space for two. The bed was incredibly comfortable and the bathroom nicely appointed and tiled. We loved the decor of the lobby lounge areas - so comfortable and a nice way to start our days with the continental breakfast that serves probably the best croissants we've ever tasted. The only negative I can say was that the breakfast service was too slow. But other than that, we had a top notch experience. Also, I normally stay in midtown but i wanted my daughter to experience the fun and excitement of staying in the heart Soho with all its great restaurants and shops, plus we wanted to be walking distance to the Village. We couldn't have been happier with our choice of hotels as it offered us that great downtown experience with all the luxuries of a top NYC hotel. I will most definitely stay here again.

name: Wyndham Garden Hotel Manhattan, Chelsea West
title: “Great stay!”
text:
Location: within walking distance of Times Square and Rockefeller Center. A vareity of subway stations nearby. We took the subway to the Statue of Liberty and then took our time walking back to the hotel and checking out the downtown neighborhoods of Soho, Tribeca, the Village, Chinatown, etc. Lots of great restaurants and bar in the area.
Staff: very friendly and helpful. I'm very surprised at the reviews claiming the staff was unhelpful. We arrived early and they checked us in and had a room ready. They answered questions about the area, how to get around, and good places to eat.
Quality: I was impressed when we first entered the room. The hallway was warm, but the room was perfectly air conditioned. The room was very clean and comfortable. Yes, it's a bit small - that's what you get in Manhattan. But my boyfriend and I had enough room for the two of us and our bags.
I would definitely stay here again!

name: The Manhattan Club
title: “Great location, good amenities, but beware of the shower water temp.”
text: I love where this hotel is located. It is across the street from Carnegie Hall, and a few blocks from Central Park, two subway stations, and easy walking distance to Times Square. The rooms are nice, and the beds are very comfortable. The elevator issue seemed to be fixed, and we didn't get hounded to purchase a timeshare. We attended the presentation, said "no" and received our gift cards to the restaurants. The things to beware of--if you book for a presentation and they drop the price, you will not get your rate adjusted. Also, and this was the biggest headache--the water temperature was absolutely horrible. It would go from scalding to freezing, and scalding again. Finally, even though it was only a three dollar charge, we were told when we made our initial reservation that our room was completely paid for and yet we still had a three dollar bill (it wasn't for any incidentals--it was the room charge balance).

name: Doubletree Hotel New York City-Financial District
title: “Nice hotel with great location”
text:
Stayed for a week in April 2011. hotel is very clean and in good condition. We were given a non-smoking when asked, even though we had booked smoking. Asked for high floor too, which was not a problem. Good service!
Room was very new and in great condition. Bed was very comfy, as written in here earlier too. Room didn't have any spare space, but was acceptable. Our stuff fitted in and there was enough room for 2 person for 7 days. Can't be that small then. View was nice facing the Wall Street area. 32" flat TV with huge free selection.
Had breakfast every morning which was basic with eggs & bacon and pancakes. Bread and yogurt with fruits was available too. Didn't eat or drink outside breakfast time so can't comment on that.
Location was great. Subway R is 50 meters from hotel door and lines 4 & 5 around 100 meters. Cab fare to anywhere in Downtown shouldn't be more than 10 USD. South Ferry terminal to Staten Island is around 200 meters away.

name: Washington Square Hotel
title: “Wonderful stay”
text: Hotel is in lovely, quiet area yet only one block from major subway station. You are also near 24 hour drugstore, coffee, restaurants and bus lines. Cabs run down street often. Our room was fairly large, by NY standards, and comfortable. It was a little dark, no view, but that's OK if it's quiet. Our main complaint is tiny one -- the (free) breakfast area was so tight that you felt overwhelmed if a loud,annoying person happened to be braying at the next table. We plan to come back to NY and stay here again, no question.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Easy Come, Easy Go”
text:
Just wrapped up a quick business trip in NYC where I stayed at the Le Parker Meridien for one night. Overall, it was a pleasant experience. Front Desk attendant, Laurence, was personable and professional upon check in; he upgraded me to a junior suite based on my Gold status. 
Check in was easy although I'd recommend additional representatives during peak times to get things moving faster. Check out was fine. No issues with elevator wait times. Very clean, location was great (close to Central Park and shopping), and the bellmen were pleasant to deal with. Also, when I noticed that there were no complimentary bottles of water in my room for Starwood Preferred Guests, I inquired about it to the front desk and was told to have an Evian from the mini-bar on the house... that was a nice gesture and is something that shows me that the hotel is focused on delivery quality customer service. I would stay here again.
BTW, although I didn't dine hear this time, earlier in the month my wife and I enjoyed a great brunch at Norma's which is located in the hotel... it's a quite popular higher end brunch venue which is a hotspot for the locals... portions are gigantic but also healthy... quality is excellent.

name: Washington Square Hotel
title: “Nice breakfast and good location, but poor rooms and rude staff”
text: I will give WSH its due--the breakfast was great and the security man was excellent--friendly and attentive. After that and the location, not much I can say to recommend this hotel. I booked and confirmed (two days prior) a room with one queen-sized bed. When I checked in and went to the room, it had two double beds. I went back to the front desk and the clerk told me that they were queen beds, which obviously was not true. Then they tried to appease me and told me that this room with two double beds was an "upgrade" that I should be happy. I told them that since we were planning to only sleep in one bed, this was actually a downgrade for me. In response to my concerns, another staff member literally said to me that there were "plenty of hotels in NY" and to go find another one! When I asked why my confirmed room was not available, the manager said that they allow people to stay in their rooms if they decide to extend their time at the hotel. I can't imagine a hotel adopting this policy as this could confuse all the reservations that were made. In my experience, if I want to extend my stay at other hotels and the room is not available, I have to either leave or change rooms. Hard to believe that this really isn't their policy. OK--enough about the staff, let's focus on the rooms. The beds are not comfortable and the rooms are basic, to say the least. However, I could put up with this if the staff hadn't been so rude. As I said, I couldn't recommend this hotel unless there wasn't much left in the area.

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “We loved it and we'll be back”
text:
Pros:
Hotel staff was very nice
Rooms clean and comfortable, maybe a little too small
The location is awesome, just near two subway stops and a few blocks from Central Park.
Cons:
Air conditioning in the room was absolutely noisy!
One elevator was broken all the 9 days
The other one was broken for at least three days and in a 9 floor building this could be annoying. It must be said that a third (service?) elevator was available anytime.

name: Washington Square Hotel
title: “Fantastic Locatation, Great Interior...”
text:
Whilst this hotel is in a fantastic location and is generally a great place to stay, I did find some of the front desk staff rather sullen and unwelcoming. Only 2 of the 6 or so staff were actually friendly.
Make sure you book a deluxe room with a view otherwise you'll end up with a brick wall outside your window making the room very hot and the noise of the ac unit unbearable.
Other than that....highly recommended!

name: The Milburn Hotel
title: “The Milburn Delivers Again”
text: We won't stay anywhere else when we visit New York. However, this is NOT a luxury hotel. If you like new shiny Hiltons or Sheratons and don't know New York, you may not like this hotel. But it is a REAL bargain in Manhattan. In an Upper West Side neighborhood, close to restaurants and grocery shopping--and all kinds of other shopping. Three blocks from the cross-town bus or the subway. About 10 blocks from Lincoln Center (if you're a walker, Times Square is only 35 blocks away, but the express subway from 72nd street will take you there with no stops). Two blocks from the park. Quieter than the Times Square hotels and cleaner. The continental breakfast is a nice addition. It's also handy to have a kitchenette, however small. Although there is no restaurant, there is room service through the front desk from local restaurants--and the prices are reasonable. This time, we had a king suite (usually stay in a junior suite) and the space was wonderful. Except for the bathroom. The bathrooms here are infinitesimal. You can barely turn around, no matter what the size of the room. It's an old building, the carpeting is worn, but it's clean. The bed was very comfortable. Staff was friendly and helpful as ever. The swimming pool and fitness center are not on the premises. Although they say they have laundry facilities, they are industrial-size washers that cost $4 to wash and $2 to dry. If you have a huge amount of stuff to wash, that might be a deal, but if you pack light, there's a laundromat a block away on 75th where a wash is $2 and dry is .25 for each 7.5 minutes.

name: Doubletree Hotel New York City-Financial District
title: “Très agréable, je recommande vivement”
text:
Je suis restée 4 nuits à cet hôtel. Très bel accueil, avec un cookie Tout chaud! la chambre était très propre, un peu petite pour circuler mais pour le prix on ne peut demander mieux. Nous étions logé au 32me. Le ménage fait chaque matin, les parties communes également. Le personnel très disponible et agréable et efficace. Le Wifi est disponible à l'accueil (au Lobby) ou bien en chambre mais en supplément. 
Le restaurant est un peu petit pour les petits déjeuners, mais le buffet est bien copieux, nous mangions vraiment à notre faim pour des petits déjeuners typique Américain (saucisse, omelette, Pancake, Jus d'orange pressé,etc...) 
mes prochaines escales à New York se feront à cet Hôtel, c'est sur. Car très franchement, le prix est très intéressant pour la qualité proposée. 
Facilement accessible par Métro qui est au coin de la Rue (ce qui est rare à NY, contrairement à Paris, les bouches de Métro sont plus rares) et qui nous emmène directement dans le Coeur de la ville en 10/15mn. 
Le quartier est relativement calme le soir, et c'est plutôt sympa! cela dit, on peut trouver des petits bars et restos sympa à Stone Street, côté rue piétonne!
Proche de ground Zero, Wall Street, brodway à 2 pas, change de devise possible 1 rue derrière
Bref, je conseille cet hôtel si comme moi vous souhaitez partir pour un long weekend, marcher longuement pour découvrir et vous reposer le soir.

name: Soho Grand Hotel
title: “Plush”
text: The Soho Grand had the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in. The staff was top of the line and extremely friendly. Best of all they put a goldfish in my room so I wouldn't miss my fish at home.

name: Soho Grand Hotel
title: “Nice, but not fabulous”
text: This is a very nice hotel. It's very VERY soho. The vibe is downtown chic. The decor is very industrial. When my sister and I arrived we were greeted warmly and offered glasses of champagne. Not a bad way to start a vacation! The room was nice, but quite small. We were on the fourth floor and overlooking a lot of other buildings! It was a Soho view. It was pouring down rain when we arrived so we decided to watch some dvds we brought with us until the rain let up.The television was top of the line and when my sister and I couldn't figure out how to work the dvd player, someone knocked on our door and set it up for us. Apparently if you are messing around with the television, the IT guys downstairs are alerted automatically b/c we hadn't called for anyone! Over all, we had a pleasant stay. I don't think it was anything all that spectacular, but the rooms are clean, the beds are comfy and the location is great. If you can get a good rate and want a central to Soho location give it a go. I wouldn't pay the overly inflated rates for this place though. The regular rooms aren't worth the price. The celebrities that gush about this place are staying in the celebrity rooms...nothing like the rest of the hotel. keep that in mind!

name: Soho Grand Hotel
title: “Still itching”
text: Great location, close to everything. Beautiful hotel. But they have bedbugs, just saying.

name: New York Marriott East Side
title: “Noisy, very busy and aged but right area........”
text: Sorry I did not really like this hotel (or the city). I did arrive late on a very hot night from a long flight and jet lagged only to find my room was not ready! The Front Desk did not handle this very well, but was resolved with Concierge Lounge access (am a Platinum member) and then they found a room shortly afterwards. The Lounge is excellent here. The room we had was an average size with an ancient and very noisy air con unit - it was 88 degrees outside. The area is convenient for shopping. The downstairs Concierge was not very helpful for tour suggestions and only promotes one idea. But we were only here for 2 nights. I choose this hotel as my husband does not like heights so the fact it was a not a high rise hotel was excellent.

name: Wyndham Garden Hotel Manhattan, Chelsea West
title: “Hotel correcto”
text: Buen hotel par alojarse en Nueva York, centrico, bien cominicado por el Subway, y a un paso del Empire State.Lo unico que no me gusto, no cambiaron las sabanas de las camas en los 10 dias que estuvimos alojados y en el cuarto de baño estaban los pelos que nos encontramos al llegar. Por lo demas lo recomiendo totalmente

name: Doubletree Hotel New York City-Financial District
title: “Fantastisk!”
text:
Jeg og en venninne skulle være i NY i 12 dager og fant dette hotellet. Det var egentlig ingen tvil. Vi valgte det, og angret ikke et sekund. Personalet var utrolig hyggelige mot oss, og oppgraderte oss siden vi valgte å bo der så lenge. Sengen var fantastisk god og rommet generelt var rent og ryddig.
Sikkerheten på hotellet er også veldig bra, ettersom de har en som står nede og hilser på alle som kommer inn. Vi bestilte takeout og ble ringt opp av dørmannen for å få bekreftelse på at dette var riktig.
Ellers er rommet kanskje litt lite når man etter hvert shopper mye osv, men det var aldri noe stort problem for oss. Badet var også utrolig flott.
Kan virkelig anbefale dette hotellet.
Ikke å glemme. Doubletree her kjente for sine gode cookies. Og ja, de er helt fantastiske!

name: Wyndham Garden Hotel Manhattan, Chelsea West
title: “Séjour Audrey & Arnaud (France)”
text: Hôtel avec petit hall d'entrée sans prétention. La situation est parfaite à 2 pas du Madison square et au centre de Manhatan. Lit king size très conformable et appréciable. L'entretien de la salle de bain laisse à désirer. Nous recommandons cet hôtel à tout ceux qui souhaitent découvrir New York (1 semaine minimum) pour son confort et sa situation centrale.

name: The GEM Hotel-SoHo, an Ascend Collection hotel
title: “Meh...”
text: I stayed with a friend for one night of "girls night out." When we arrived we were greated by Anthony, and may I say, he was helpful and extremely friendly. I was disappointed with the room. It was very small and smelled like a boys locker room...combination musty. We were on the 6th floor so I guess it doesn't matter what floor you're on, I read various reviews repeating the latter. Luckily I travel with Lysol wipes and disinfecting spray. The sheets were a bit shakey as well. I wouldn't recommend this hotel to anyone unless they completely revamped the housekeeping practices. A real shame because it is so centrally located to great bars, eateries, and venues. I expected a lot more for $230.

name: W New York
title: “Nice people and service, but small rooms”
text:
Everyone from the bellmen to the security guards to the front desk agents were friendly and helpful. Nice hotel, comfortable lobby to meet friends or do business with a quieter upstairs to talk, sit, read or work. Unfortunately, the only downside is the rooms are small, but that's it.
The hot cider is delicious, too!

name: King & Grove New York
title: “Gem of a hotel”
text:
What a gem of a little hotel. Great location on East 29th street, very pleasant staff, comfortable beds, and immaculately clean. The lobby is welcomming and the doorman/porter extremely friendly. Free WiFi in the rooms and lobby. No noise from the street nor from the halls. Good restaurants nearby for breakfast, lunch or dinner. Nice pub on 28th street the Crooked Knife. We booked through Jet Setters and their price was excellent. 
Close to Macy's and a $5 to $10 cab ride to anywhere else, very conveniently located.
When I do go back to NY, I will deffinitively stay there again.

name: Hotel St. James
title: “get a room at the back ;)”
text:
Good value for the location - a few steps away from the hubbub of Times Sq. First room I go was 2nd floor at the front. Newbie error I am sure. Room was tiny and smelled of cigarettes. But when I called the next morning and asked to swap the guy couldnt have been nicer and gave me 2 rooms to choose between. One at the back - 7th floor was fab. No view at ALL, but twice the size.
Rooms were clean but sparse. Air con woke me up a few times doing som clanking. I had a bath which made me very happy - but hot water seemed a bit unreliable in the bath and the plug didnt work - so you got out quick before it seeped away ;) No inroom amenities beyond bed and TV really, but the deli next door was great for morning coffee, juice etc. And I certainly had more channels than I've had in other hotels which was welcome
A bit scruffy around the edges, but if you want to be in the centre, with a quiet room for good value then its definitely possible at St James. 
As for the staff - it varied HUGELY - had a couple of guys who were wonderful, really great and helpful, then sometimes I got a couple of guys who just were totally stand offish. Happily the nicer guys seemed to work the most :)

name: Wolcott Hotel
title: “Great location”
text: Took my son here for his 21st and it was one of the few hotels that offered 2 beds without silly charges. Fantastic location for all new York attractions. Spotlessly clean with small but adequate rooms with large bathrooms towels changed daily.. Cannot fault this hotel with complimentary muffins and fresh coffee in the lobby for breakfast each morning until 10.30. Small gym available free along with ice machine and free availability to pc for printing boarding passes. Only criticism was no wifi without charge, but there is a lovely starbucks around the corner with free wifi. Would not hesitate to stay here again.

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Awesome on a budget”
text:
Stayed for 8 days with my sister. room was big with a nice comfy bed, bathroom was clean and had a good shower. 
Location was incredible, a minute away for times sq. on 45 st., just no time from all major location and close to the 42 st. or the one on Rockefeller center.
Staff was very nice and they even let us check-out late since our flight wasn't until 7pm, they also gave great recommendations when asked. The hotel has a 20-something$ shuttle to the airports which is very convenient (we took the airtrain just because it's cheaper). 
Got a great deal on the room that made the whole stay even better, only thing i would've liked to have is a mini-fridge and coffee station, but we knew in advanced we wouldn't have one. 
Maid service was ok, we planned on tipping before we left and could feel the quality of cleaning going down when we didn't tip everyday.

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Good hotel in great location”
text:
For the money we paid my husband and I were very pleased with this hotel. It really is just two blocks away from Times Square and has good cheap restaurants, cafes and bars right on it's doorstep. The room was clean, the bed comfy and the room very quiet which meant it was a relaxing haven after the hustle and bustle of Manhattan! The staff were pleasant and were very helpful when I felt I was ripped off by the small technical shop next door who overcharged me considerably for a USB cable by checking prices on the internet so I could compare and confront him with the comparisons, 
We pretty much walked everywhere and saw all the usual sites without having to use the tube system much at all (which was probably a good thing as we found it very confusing to use even though we use the underground in London regularly).
Overall we would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone wanting a reasonable standard of hotel right in the heart of NYC!

name: Holiday Inn NYC - Manhattan 6th Avenue
title: “Good stay”
text: Good stay . No complaints. Pretty small of course but overall we really enjoyed our 4 days here.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Springtime in New York”
text: My boyfriend and I met in NYC for a getaway weekend. We had a great stay at the Roosevelt which is an older charming hotel in an ideal location. Room was sparsely decorated but had lovely linens and a very comforable bed. The room was not huge but hey it's NYC. The Roosevelt provides good value for the location and ambiance. Cocktails, especially the mojitos, were lots of fun in the bar. Good crowd and lively but cozy atmosphere.

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “Staff without doubt among the most friendliest and accommodating”
text: A very good hotel suited our needs perfectly. Was slightly apprehensive as like many we had been reading all the reviews over the last few weeks. We spent 7 nights and the room was always clean. Beds made daily with frequent changes. There were no bugs etc. the staff were very friendly and it was a pleasure to return each evening after full days activities and the bed was very very comfortable. Good value for money.

name: Doubletree By Hilton - Times Square South
title: “Great location, standard NYC size”
text:
Tiny, NYC-sized rooms, but that's to be expected. Clean, quiet-- exactly what we needed. All personnel were extremely pleasant and effective.
We loved the location: we could walk (with luggage) the two blocks from Penn Sta. Entrance to the subway was one block from hotel. We're not massively into the touristy stuff, but if you are, it's an easy walk to Times Square/BWay/42nd St. We're big noshers, and there were some fun local places nearby in Hell's Kitchen. Just a few blocks to the High Line.

name: Flatotel
title: “Great central location to explore the Big Apple!”
text:
Flatotel was a comfortable hotel, very centrally located. The room was a decent size and the bathroom was big, the reception and bar / restaurant area looks good and the staff were lovely. They really helped us out too as we'd had some baseball game tickets delivered to the hotel and looked after them for us until we arrived.
Let's face it if you're staying in NY all you need is a base to crash after a hard day's sightseeing and this did the trick. It was reasonably priced for what you got and the compimentary breakfasts were a nice touch we weren't expecting! The decor in places is now looking a little dated but I really wasn't going to NY from the UK to sit in my hotel.
Overall a good place to stay at a reasonable price and the staff were very helpful!
Enjoy x

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “The perfect location”
text:
We stayed there for 5 nights last October and we really enjoyed the location (at the corner between Madison Av. and the 45th east) at walkable distance to Rockfeller Center, St. Patrick Church, Times Square and of course the 5th. Just in front the Central Station, you can easily reach all Manhattan and NY places. We were asked to leave 100 dollars as caution, but that's normal in the USA, especially in NY. We had what promised, a double room with 2 queen size beds in a welcoming ambient and at the 12th floor. A little bit expensive for our standard but not so much if combined with the flight. The check in employee wasn't so friendly but we really appreciated the helping concierge staff that organized a tour for us with full informations and directions, they also booked for us a night at the blue note.
Even if the hall is so big and magnificient, as the room in itself, I have to say that the bathroom is very old and no restructured but very well cleaned.
I won't be there for my next time in NYC but only because I'd like to change block, I was fascinated by Greenwich and its neighbourhood... plenty of NY styled thinghs!

name: Hotel Deauville
title: “really nice hotel”
text:
My sister-in-law and i just stayed at the hotel deauville for 4 nights. On arriving at the hotel the person on duty at check in was Edward, we asked could we have a room with 2 beds and private facilities, thankfully Edward did this for us. 
The room was clean and we had clean towels everyday. The only drawback was the view, which was a brick wall, but we were out all day so the room was basically somewhere to put your head on a night and to have a clean bathroom. 
We were so grateful the air conditioning was good because New York was going through a heatwave at the time with temps hitting 100 degrees so coming back to a lovely cool room was a godsend.
The hotel has a free safety deposit box, free hairdryers and tea/coffee making facilities.
The staff at the hotel were really friendly and helpful especially Emily who organised our trip on a helicopter for us and was always happy to answer any questions.
We booked a car to take us back to jfk through the hotel and couldnt believe it when a limo turned up and it only cost 65 dollars.
So all in all if you are going to NY on a budget i would thoroughly recommend this hotel as being clean and having friendly staff.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Find another hotel”
text: We arrived dropped our bags off in our room and didn't return until late that evening. Once I laid on the bed I notice candy wrappers stuffed under the air conditioner. I reported that as well as the ice machine not working,missing tile in RR, carpet not cleaned and a light was out in our room. The person at the front desk wrote everything down but gave no apology. We returned later that night expecting everything to be fixed. The bed was made but the carpet was still dirty and the wrapper still under the air conditioner. Then during breakfast service we saw the chef come out with a flashlight looking under all the cabinets and shelves behind the bar. Not a good sign. we complained again when we left. Once again not even a sorry was given just an okay. We would have been better off at the Holiday Express!

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Great location!”
text: We stayed here for the theatres and was our best choice ever!!! Great security. It's perfectly located, near Time Square and Broadway. We had our perfect Anniversary. The room is tiny but cozy. It's a very fashion hotel, with low lights, black halls, red lights, really nice. Being in NYC who wants to saty in a room?! So, the room was just for the nights. We were @ the 18th floor with an excellent view to all those NY buildings, awesome!! We will stay again. Thanks paramount.

name: W New York
title: “In need of a total overhaul to live up to past standards”
text:
I have been staying at W on Lexington for a decade. It's become a bit of a dump and management appears to be putting it head in the sand so to speak. I will find a new NYC hotel to stay at.
The rooms have been redone and now look like something you'd see in Austin Powers movie with shag rugs and lots of metallic objects.
The service was never a strong suit but has gotten worse. Many of the folks feel like they are beneath the job they are doing and don't really try. I called Whatever Whenever multiple times and no one even bothered answering the phone.
Neither the TV nor the phone worked in my room so I had to have engineering come up.
The gym (aka Sweat) is really quite bad for a hotel at this price point. I think a new gym may be under construction as it is sorely needed.
Net net the hotel needs a real face lift.

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Great location and atmosphere!”
text: Everyone was pleasant and professional. Decor was chic and clean with cool New Age music pumped in. Library bar was classy, yet comfy. Food and drink delicious and reasonable. Fantastic, yet simple buffet breakfast. In the heart of the theatre district right by Times Square. Restaurant row down the block. Bring comfortable walking shoes and enjoy!

name: Doubletree By Hilton - Times Square South
title: “Above-average property that totally met expectations.”
text:
Location... It's a 3 to 4 block walk to Penn Station/Madison Square Garden, easily covered in 5 to 10 minutes (depending on the crowds, and what you're carrying!). Also, there are several subway lines within quick walking distance. So while it's not the "nicest" area of town, it's definitely near the transportation hub. Otherwise, there's a decent (and inexpensive) breakfast spot just around the corner, as well as a White Castle for a late night snack. 
Room... Small, but in NY, I suppose it was almost normal. For a weekend stay for 1 or 2, it's absolutely not a problem, as there is room to walk around the bed, and the bath is actually as large as many not located in NY. Shower only, though, for those who care.
Amenities... Everything seemed fresh and spotlessly clean. No issues whatsoever with this! And the bed was comfortable, the shower was hot, with good water pressure, and the flat screen tv was just fine. Also, there were 3 computers set up just outside the cafe for easy internet usage, at no charge. 
Service... excellent... they even gave me cookies on the way out!

name: The GEM Hotel-SoHo, an Ascend Collection hotel
title: “best location”
text: Small but nice affordable hotel, and the location is perfect. Right by the f train, with knishes and katz's practically next door. The staff is friendly and getting a late checkout was no problem which helps when you didn't get there until 4am. Would stay again.

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “Definitely seen better days”
text:
Let me start by saying, to be fair, there are signs posted around this slowly decaying hotel promising an upgrade. I hope so as it is in need of an overhaul. Obviously, this hotel was once new, modern and in good shape but the years are beginning to show.
First impressions weren't helped by the surly reception from the woman at the desk. Hey, if you don't like your job or you're having a bad day, take a chill pill but act professionally, be friendly and polite. 30 minutes later and a different staff member (aldi?) restored my confidence.
A couple of things to note. Wifi is free (as it should be) but they charge an outrageous fee to use the so called business centre - really just a couple of computers in the bar area. Certainly not conducive to working. The outrageous part is the gall to charge 25cents per MINUTE! If you want to use the pool. Get there after 10am and before 6pm as it is closed outside those times.
Very slow lifts, dirty floors, shabby furniture, smoking rooms (awful for non smokers) and an only average location well down 57th Street. Overall, many better choices in this amazing city. Didn't dine here so won't comment. 
Bring on the overhaul!

name: W New York
title: “Whatever, whenever.... ?????”
text:
Stayed here for the first 5 days of our honeymoon in November 2011. The room at the time was thought to be terrific, large corner suite. However the furniture was ridiculous. The couch was the most uncomfortable, spaceship looking thing that could not accommodate more than one person. And no space to put your toiletries in the bathroom. 
The check in staff were terrible. The only staff members to assist us where the concierge desk. The lovely Lady with white blonde hair (perhaps Maude?) another gentlemen who helped us with dinner recommendations. And of course the awesome night foyer security man who often kept my husband company as he worked early into the morning on the free WIFI in the foyer only, as he manages his business in another time zone. He was especially nice to me the morning of black Friday sales where I left for Macy's at 12am for the super sales and returned at 6am to his watchful eye! He had organized to wake my husband up at 6am if I had not returned in a taxi by then to ensure I was safe. Very nice. 
The service theme of whatever whenever works well at the W hotel in LA (Westwood) and I was horrified that this does not translate to this hotel. On check in, even though I could see "honeymoon" on her screen, the girl never congratulated us. It's just one of those nice things to do. The worst was when we left to stay at the Plaza Hotel and I found a wallet in the taxi that we had taken and I assumed that maybe it was from a guest who had just got out. I spent 20 minutes and 3 phone calls trying to reach the front desk. No one wanted to help. When I finally demanded flat out to be put through to the front desk, the owner of the wallet was indeed there and in tears. 
I wrote a significant letter to the manager and never received a response which I think is beyond rude, especially as an SPG member. 
I recommend skipping this one, and for your money, find a special at the Waldorf Towers across the road. I highly recommend using a service called Magellan travel as they booked all our New York hotels at great prices including this one. They only manage luxury properties and have some great packages with excellent cancellation terms. The more luxurious neighbour to this property is the same location,with giant luxury rooms, and talk about Whatever, Whenever! Because of the service failures and no follow up, I would give this one a miss.

name: Doubletree By Hilton - Times Square South
title: “Pleasant surprise!!!”
text:
We will definitely stay here again when we come back to New York City. The staff were all very courteous and pleasant and would walk that extra mile to help you. We arrived early and they found a way to check us in, enabling us to get an early start on our exploring the city. The hot breakfast was great! Free internet access was indeed an added bonus, even had a printer to print your boarding passes and such.
Thanks for making our New York stay hassle-free accommodation-wise!

name: Park 79 Hotel
title: “A more accurate Review...”
text: Let me first start out by saying that i am a 29yr old male being accompanied by a 29 yr old female architect. I must say that both of us were pleasantly suprised by the hotel after reading the mixed reviews online. So i wanted to take the time to right an honest review of the place so that like minded travelers will share the same experience my friend and i had. The Park 79 Hotel located in West Manhatten inbetween mid town and up town is an old building, but renovated to a more modern style. The location is only a block away from the Metro and only two blocks from a bar and fantastic coffee house. I like many others hopped on trip advisor and other travel review sites and discovered that the hotel was rated only 3 stars. I read several good reviews and several bad reviews of the place. Being my first time in New York City i was really concerned with finding a safe area and the few bad reviews i had read about park 79 was enough to make me nervous upon arrival. Well within the first 10 minutes of arriving at the hotel all of my worries were sent sailing. The Hotel staff was extremely courtious. ( I never opened the lobby door once! ) the room yet small was perfectly clean with a nice flat screen television and a very modern black tiled bathroom and shower. My friend and I shared a single bed and we did not have any problems at all sleeping. We paid roughly 150$ per night during the week and for Manhatten prices for a hotel with a private bathroom im not sure it can be beat. Ok so obviously im a fan of this hotel and would definetly stay there again.
