The only reason i will not give it 5 stars is because the elevator in the building is old and it does a take a while to reach the 7th floor and also the walls are thin and you can hear your neighbor pretty easily, but rarely did it bother me. But like i said im not the type of person who freaks out if my pillow is not fluffed correctly... or if the door guy doesnt completely kiss my butt everytime i walk in the door... So i would like to tell all of the travelers out there.. That you honestly can not go wrong with this hotel and it's very close location to the metro line. I talked to a groupd of travelers staying in a hostel in brooklyn for only 20$ cheaper than this place in manhatten with a private bath! And for those who rated this hotel in a negative way may i suggest quit being so nit picky and scaring off potential travelers just because the hotel is not as fancy as there $250,000 garden home. Im glad i took a chance on this hotel and would certaintly stay here again.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Stunning lobby, great location, historic building”
text: Wow. The Roosevelt hotel lobby is stunning. I know, I know, you can't sleep in the lobby (at least for too long). I was fresh off Amtrak from Penn Station so I was easily impressed with the grandeur and scale of this lobby. Our room was typically sized for Manhattan, no surprises there. The beds were very comfortable and I'd easily stay at the Roosevelt again. Great location.

name: Wolcott Hotel
title: “Old and out dated”
text:
only good thing about hotel was location. general feeling that the hotel was old and musty, although room was cleaned well every day. Beds ok. Could hear the neighbours shouting. Towels and bathroom had seen better days..... as had the carpets and walls. The coffee in the morning was a nice touch but undrinkable. 
A budget hotel at best.

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “THE PLACE TO STAY!!!”
text:
My daughter and I visited NY for New Year's and enjoyed it so much that we wanted to return soon. We did not stay here during our first visit so I do have another hotel (on the same block) that I can compare to. Actually, there is no comparison b/w the 2. The Paramount was better in every aspect possible. Being from the south and working with a northerner I was warned that people in NY do not seem as friendly as people in the south b/c NY is much larger than where we are and they are focused on their mission of getting to and from work as quickly as possible. The hotel staff from the "other hotel" lived up to the un-friendly description and I'm happy to say it was much different at this hotel. I was very pleasantly surprised to be greeted with wonderful smiles and generious kind personalities willing to help every time I entered the lobby of the Paramount. We arrived early and our room wasn't ready so the clerk offered to place us in another room that was ready. It was very nice of him to do that so we could get our luggage put away and hit the streets for shopping :) Our room had a pleasant scent and was very very clean. The bathroom was much larger than at the other hotel which was nice and allowed my daughter and I to get dressed at the same time with plenty of extra room for a couple more people. Our previous bathroom felt crowded when occupied by yourself alone, it was so small. These beds were extremely comfortable!!! That is important after a day out in the hot sun, walking miles that you're not used to walking and feeling really worn out. We didn't consume any of the hotel's food or drinks so I can't comment on that.
It is located in an excellent location, in the middle of Times Square and only 1 block from Broadway. Not only was I totally pleased with the hotel conditions but the rate was much cheaper than the other hotel for these same dates. If I ever return to NY I will not have to shop for a hotel....I "WILL" STAY HERE!

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Only for sleeping in, so it's OK”
text:
Anybody complaining about the facilities or the furniture in the room etc have missed the point of visiting NYC.
Just spent 5 days at this hotel and whilst it is very very basic and in need of an update, it was clean and the bed comfortable. Bathroom was very good. 
The staff on reception were very helpful.
Cranberry Deli next door is fantastic and very cheap. 
 Location of this hotel is it's best feature.

name: Park 79 Hotel
title: “Okay but noisy!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for 5 days. Like others have said, the rooms are quite tiny! (Especially the bathroom, you can't even sit comfortably on the toilet! But the shower is okay and the interior is amazing, like the tiling) But they are very clean and quite nicely decorated (I had a mirror and a picture of Central Park in mine). Hotel is close to the 79th Str. subway, and the 81th Str. subway, so excellent connections all over Manhattan and close to restaurants, museums and Central Park. The only thing that really annoyed me is the noise. The walls seems to be very thin, which means you can hear everything going on with your neighbours. Two nights were absolutely horrible for me, one night there was a guy who was being very loud in the middle of the night, flushing his toilet all the time and throwing up (and yes, I could hear all of it very clearly!!), then another time a drunk couple came to their room, put on the tv very loud, were being loud themselves and then put music on in the middle of the night. The cleaning staff was pretty loud as well, them shouting to eachother from across the hallway was pretty much what I woke up from every morning. Also, I hung the "Do not disturb" sign on my door, to get a good rest, yet they called me on the phone to ask if I wanted fresh towels. All in all, it was an okay stay. Most of the staff at the front desk were very friendly and helpful and helped me on my way more than once. (The men were a lot more helpful than the women though, they seemed to be bothered by my questions..) Internet worked really well (got a quite quick connection, even being on the 7th floor) and it being free is definitely a big plus!
To put it in short: if you're looking to stay at a great location for an okay price, this the place to be. If you are looking for a quiet, comfortable environment, I would recommend you try another hotel.

name: Flatotel
title: “just "okay"”
text:
I arrived at 3:35 hoping to check in a bit early (4 pm posted check in)on a Sat. The clerk said no rooms were available yet. This was despite the sign in the window advertising a vacany rate for that very weekend! There was a baggage hold and so that worked out fine for us. 
Upon seeing the room, I had a disappointing experience. While the room seemed mostly clean, it was VERY run down. Paint was scuffed and chipping off in places, the carpet was dirty, bed platforms were chipped, furniture legs wre chipped and bent, the sheer curtains that were under the EXTREMELY dusty drapes (i mean major fuzz at the top) had holes in them. The lamps in the room were very loose and very dim (presumable so you wouldn't notice the paint!) A very old tube style TV, which normally I wouldn't care about in NYC - who has time for TV? But we did watch the golden globes one evening and the TV picture and sound was not too good. 
One of the most unsafe of the run down features was the large mirror that was just resting against the wall. - The cable to hang it to the wall at some point snapped I guess. Also, the window - on the 25th floor that opened a good 11-12 inches and had no screen! You could drop anything (or anyone!) out of it!! Beds were comfortable and bug free, and the water pressure was good although the half shower door allowed watehr to spill all over the bathroom tiles. 
I clerk for checkout at 11:00, on a holiday Monday (Jan 16th MLK day)the other woman present was on the phone and then left altogether. 
Good location and for 115 a night prepaid, I got what I paid for!

name: Buckingham Hotel
title: “Great Staff! Great Location! Fun Time!”
text:
We just got back to California after a great trip to New York! We were very apprehensive about picking a hotel off the internet - especially after reading some of the less complimentary reviews - but, after contacting the hotel by e-mail, we decided to give it a try. The Buckingham Hotel was perfect for us. 
We were greeted at the door by a friendly, helpful staff member (Marvin) who helped us unload all of our luggage and took it up to our room which was a wonderful start to our New York adventure. Then, we were welcomed by a friendly front desk staff including Sandra Arrias who I had been corresponding with by e-mail. Sandra and other staff members gave us restaurant suggestions, parking information, and directions several times throughout our visit which really helped us. 
We were 5 women traveling together - most of us visiting New York for the first time - and we wanted a comfortable, safe, convenient and economical place to stay and THIS WAS IT!! We had two rooms (16H & 14C) and they were both perfect - lots of room to spread out and relax when we had the chance. We didn't do much cooking but having the refrigerator and microwave available for quick breakfasts was wonderful. The rooms are certainly not modern or "glitzy" but they are comfortable and clean which is what we wanted and the beds were the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in at a hotel. 
In addition, the location of the hotel can not be beat. It is steps to the subway, a block from Central Park, a couple of blocks from the tour bus stops and a short walk to Rockefeller Center and Times Square. We were out several nights past midnight and always felt safe and comfortable coming to and from the hotel. 
If and when we ever have the opportunity to return to New York, we will definitely be staying at The Buckingham.

name: Buckingham Hotel
title: “OK... if you know what you are getting”
text:
The Buckingham is a former apartment building consequently it is not your typical hotel and if you go in knowing that, you may well enjoy it.
The pros: great location at 57th and 6th, close to Carnegie Hall (the hotel has a music theme to its decor), Central Park, subways, MOMA and lots of restaurants. Also if you get a deluxe suite you are getting your own apartment with large living room and a kitchen (a small typical NYC kitchen.) That's great if you're there for multiple days.
The cons: really, really noisy location because 57th is a cross-town thoroughfare plus has bus service on it and has a lots of construction going on. (They were jack hammering at midnight one night.) Very limited technical infrastructure for computers (don't bother getting the modem unit; it's useless) and very few electrical outlets in the room. No tech knowledge or support from staff. 
Pokey bathroom with disintegrating tile, and a bad mattress on the bed. TV reception was all screwed up ( we got a weird selection of speciality stations but no mainstream stations.) 
Oddly, despite all these problems, we had a good time and enjoyed the location. The rooms vary significantly. We had friends staying there too so saw 3 rooms altogether and they were all very different in layout, comfort and condition. 
My advice, book only a deluxe room. Make them move you if you don't like the room. Leave your computer at home. And bring ear plugs.

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “Best value in New York City!”
text: I like most people had no idea where the best place to stay is in NYC. Coming from overseas we had no idea. On a budget and very overwhelmed by so many hotels the Holiday Inn was everything we wanted - a comfy bed, great service, close to subway and great value! If you just need some where to lay your head after a big day sight seeing this place is the go!

name: Mayfair Hotel
title: “Horrible horrible service!”
text:
This was some of the worst customer service I have ever experienced. One front desk staff member in particular was so rude and so disrespectful that we considered walking out and losing whatever cancellation fees would have applied. 
The rooms are small and nothing special; I would definitely recommend taking your business elsewhere, the staff obviously doesn't care if you do.

name: Mayfair Hotel
title: “$4.00 Fuel Charge?”
text: We booked the Mayfair through Expedia and paid $751 for 3 nights. We were surprised to be told at check-in that we would have to pay an additional $4.00 per night which was termed a "Fuel Charge." That brought the charge to $763. We laughed it off and gave them the extra $12, but we thought that was quite an arbitrary policy. We have often stayed in NYC, and this was the smallest room we have ever booked. It is shaped like an angle iron, and the double bed had perhaps a 7-inch clearance on each side. The bed shifted downward during the night so you would have to reposition the bed before you could open the door to exit the room. That was ironically good because there is no dead-bolt lock on the door. The bed was too soft and had no support.Now, the room was immaculate, and that's a biggie. The staff was most pleasant. Still, there are a lot of hotels in the area, and I believe you can get a bigger room, a clean room, and one that does not slap you with a "fuel" charge when you arrive.

name: the Lexington
title: “central and easy”
text: The hotel was pricey at $250 a night (but hey this was NYC) and it was a great location AND we wanted easy access by being in Midtown - which we got. The room was comfortable except for a slight irritating air conditioner whir sound, staff was excellent and efficient and the lobby was a great place to sit and wait for friends. The only downside was the wireless internet was slow and kept getting cut off. There is a free internet on five computers open in the business office except from 2am-5am. The room card opens the door. I was not charged for my room internet due to the poor quality so the alternative was fine. For a splurge on price, the was a good choice. We were able to catch the airport shuttle 43rd and Park, only six blocks away. This was easy as well as the easy access to the subway. It didn't hurt having a Starbucks by the lobby for the early morning java fix!

name: the Lexington
title: “GREAT PLACE TO STAY AND VERY CENTRAL!!!”
text:
My family and I stayed at the Radisson on Lexington in April of 2012. The hotel is near Grand Central Station and also near the Subway. Times Square is accessible by Subway although a taxi is probably a better choice!! An amazing breakfast place was just across the street named Avra!! We thoroughly enjoyed the breakfast service there immensely. 
The hotel room was small but, comfortable but, a little bit dated. We did not spend a lot of time in our hotel so the rooms were just a place to sleep, shower and dress!! The rooms were clean and Housekeeping did a great job in replacing towels and making our beds everyday!! It's always nice to come "home" to your room and find your beds are made!!
The concierge was very helpful in helping us plan our site seeing trip. They helped us map all the places we wanted to see and the best way to see them!! They were full of information and suggestions. 
We would definitely stay here again!!

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Great location”
text: Easy to find, Times Square location and excellent value for money if you book in advance. I had a single room which is very compact, but clean and comfortable for a night or two in Manhattan. The staff were friendly and the hotel offers a convenient express check-out to aovid the rush at the front desk. I would definitely recommend staying here if you want to be in the centre of the action and not pay the price.

name: Flatotel
title: “Spacious and Quiet”
text: The Flatotel was very clean with nice comfy beds. The rooms were spacious but simple.It was centrally located without being on a super busy street- short walk to Times Square- Lincoln Center and Central Park.

name: Park 79 Hotel
title: “Slamming Doors and No Hot Water”
text:
We stayed at Park 79 for 3 nights in May, 2007 knowing from the price that it was not going to be a luxurious stay. Our expectation was met. Upon arrival, the front desk was very polite and courteous. The room was extremely small, but we were somewhat prepared for that, as we also were prepared for the shared bathroom (you can have your own bathroom but will pay extra).
However, there are some areas which the hotel could improve upon. First, the doors slam. This would not normally be a huge problem in a hotel, except that it is exacerbated by the fact that the walls are paper thin. It is quite annoying. Secondly, the hot water was lukewarm for about 2 days of our stay. In fact, I could not get ANY warm water on Saturday morning at around 11 am. I politely but firmly explained this fact to reception, and also a security guard/ maintenance worker who was at the front desk. Incredibly, they questioned whether I had mastered the technique of turning on the shower. I had used the showers the previous day, so I knew I was turning it on the right way. I told them that, not only did the two showers on my floor not have hot water, neither did the floor above. I specifically asked whether this was a problem they had encountered before. I got a sweet smile, and an incredulous "no!" but I suspect that the hotel is overloaded and not properly equipped for all of the guests staying in the miniscule rooms. Anyways, I kind of half expected some sort of response -- even a slight discount? a free coffee coupon? -- but none was forthcoming.
Also housekeeping started cleaning at 9 am. Again, if this was a normal sized hotel with thicker walls this wouldn't be much of a problem, but you could hear EVERYTHING.
That's the negative part. The positive part is that the hotel is in a nice area, very good access to the subway, and there's a cute little deli across the street that sells great chicken sandwiches.

name: Mayfair Hotel
title: “Great Stay in the Mayfair Hotel New York”
text:
I found my stay in the Mayfair Hotel New York great the staff are soo helpful and the location is excellent its soo close to Times Square and everything else. Even though it was close we didnt hear anything rooms are nice and quiet. Rooms are a bit small but bathroom is a good size but its everything you need in a hotel which is so central.
Loved it thank you

name: W New York
title: “Service, service and service”
text: The W is a nice hotel with a great location. The staff is warm and friendly. Although the rooms are small they are definitely upscale.

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “royally disappointed”
text:
I very much wanted to stay at a boutique hotel near Times Square in lieu of a Hilton or Marriott type. After some research, hubby and I compromised on The Paramount after seeing the price of their modern chic rooms on the website. When we checked in we were both excited about the impressive lobby. Very us. BUT we were royally disappointed when we entered our King Deluxe room. Womp womp womp...
I'm normally a very flexible/laid back, go with the flow gal but this just wasn't what I was expecting at all.
The pictures seemed to be photo shopped bright and welcoming on the website. In reality, the room was entirely too small and the bathroom lacked a lot of luster. The room just seemed so dark and small. Just NOT what we had in mind for our 5 night NYC experience. The money spent renovating this hotel was obviously poured into the more public areas of the hotel. The closet would better be described as a compartment to store ~3 jackets so our suitcases took up the little floor space we had.
We headed downstairs and explained our concerns and requested upgrade options. I inquired about their Entertainment and Couture suites displayed on their website as they are the only ones displayed. Do you know what they told me?! The available suites displayed on their website are only used for corporate events and fashion shoots. I was dumbfounded. I encouraged them to provide keys to the suite that they DO have available for purchase so that I can see it before we accept the upgrade for an additional $110 for our 5 nights in NYC. We saw it and it was another womp womp womp. They had simply take a wall and corned off 2 rooms at the end of the hallway. Even the rooms still had the heavy secure hotel door separating the bedroom from the living room AND the exit sign still existed in the cornered off wasted space in the entrance of the suite. The bedroom in the suite had a double bed. My husband and I are very tall and we by no means intend to share a double bed while paying for a suite. Desperately trying to see the positive, I looked out the window to see if our view had been upgraded. View from Times Square? It had been a bit but a partial view of lights from Times Square and the back of a billboard just wasn't worth it to me. Womp womp womp.
We headed back downstairs, handed them the suite key and stated that we will only be spending 1 night at The Paramount and would be checking out the following day. (Obviously, it was too late to cancel our room that night and not pay a fee, etc.) The customer service was very kind so I hadn’t the heart to share my disappointment. I'm sure it was obvious by our actions at that point.
I've attached a picture of my hubby stretching out his hands so that you get an idea of just how small the King Deluxe room is. Note our luggage covering the entire opposite side of the bed. No point in showing you the view out the window, it was the back of a building.
If you care to know:
NYC was insanely booked everywhere last week. We did manage to secure 2 nights at The Bowery (LOVED it, 100% guarantee that we will return) and the 2 other nights of our trip were spent at the Marriott on Times Square with an incredible view of Times Square.

name: the Lexington
title: “Good location, not the best Radisson”
text: I stayed in this hotel from friday-sunday. I have stayed in a lot of Radisson Hotels, and this was certainly not the best one, but it was clean and in a good location with subways close by, and in new york, everything is really in walking distance! There was free Wi-fi in the lobby which also was a plus, compared to other hotels trying to charge 14 dollars a day even though you can walk over to your closest starbucks or Mcdonalds and get it for free!

name: Americana Inn
title: “Pratique, économique, très bien situé”
text:
Hôtel très bien situé, à seulement 5 minutes à pieds de Times Square, donc forcément un peu bruyant mais nous n'avions pas de mal à nous endormir après des journées bien chargées! Notre chambre était suffisamment grande pour deux personnes et pour le temps que nous y passions. Le chauffage était parfois un peu trop élevé. Nous n'avons jamais attendu pour nous doucher car 4 salles de bain à notre étage et nous y allions toujours le soir car c'était en plus propre. Personnel sympathique.
Nous recommandons cet hôtel pour les personnes qui cherchent le côté pratique et économique!

name: Skyline Hotel
title: “Most pleasantly surprised.”
text:
When a client in the hotel industry suggested I stay at the Skyline, I paused. As a former New York City dweller and frequent traveller, I was familiar with the fact that it was "way over on 10th Avenue." But the price was right, so I booked. The 10th Avenue location was actually welcome, for it was a soothing distance from the hustle-bustle of the tourist-jammed Times Square area. It was the only hotel in an otherwise residential neighborhood, with neighbor-hoody shops and delis to poke one's nose in. 
It is very accessible-- in good weather it is walking distance to TS, and all train stops are on 8th or B'way between 51st & 49th. In inclement weather or if you are less inclined to walking, the crosstown bus can be picked up at the corner of 50th & 10th to head east into midtown, and it will deliver you right back at 49th and 10th. If you have a car, there is an affordable garage on premises. One block over, 9th avenue is brimming with restaurants, between 8th & 9th avenues the Worldwide Plaza has a Starbucks to stop in on the way to or from the hotel from the subway, a burger joint and Bann, delightful Korean restaurant.
The Hotel itself is Holiday Inn-ish. It has been recently renovated and the rooms are spacious, with double queen beds (firm and comfortable mattresses!), flat screen TV, big bathroom and internet service (for a fee). There is no mini bar, but better than that, a fridge in which to create one's won custom mini-bar. Ther is no laundry service, but each room is equipped with and a "Gentleman's Valet" - that you can plug in to press your slacks (in addition to the standard iron).
The only thing I missed was the little coffeemaker many hotels have, as there is no room service currently, owing to their restaurant being under renovation. They did have some breakfast service available downstairs for $18, but we skipped this in favor of the myriad choices in the neighborhood.
The staff was attentive and helpful. Oh, I almost forgot, bring a swimsuit for a dip in the pool which is on the top floor. There is also a gym.

name: Park 79 Hotel
title: “Rennovated....but not fixed”
text:
We (2 couples) stayed at the newly "rennovated" park 79 in June taking two seperate single rooms. We stayed three nights, and over our stay we paid $245 per night on average. My first impression is that they "rennovated" it to raise room rates, but didn't quite fix everything. We saw both rooms (one on 5th floor, and the other on 6th) so my comments reflect the condition of both. Mind you, there were no pests visable, but if that is your benchmark for a quality establishment then you should really consider raising your expectations. In short, the hotel was "rennovated" simply because there were too many complaints of duct-tape repairs and critters roaming the floors; but they stopped short of making the rooms as good as the rate commands. They have cleaned up the property...there's no doubt of that, it's just that they only cleaned and could have (and still can) really improve the existing space. 
The good:
-great location in quiet neighborhood (close to park and subway)
-fresh paint, linen, and some other newer elements to the rooms
-newly done washrooms* (see below)
-new T.V. but it should be on wall-mounted bracket
-coffee in lobby in the A.M. but no pastry
-free wireless internet in rooms
The rest:
-Walls & Ceilings so thin you can hear phone rings, conversations, TV and see the light in some cases without making any effort at all.
-Elevator is guest & service in one, so you may have to wait 10 minutes plus while linen and luggage is transported through the day
-"closet" is a small bar behind the door with no closet door
-Carpet in rooms is thinner than astroturf on a mini-putt putt course and might as well have been just a paper towel. Floors in halls are chipped and chunks are missing in places
-No desk or work space at all...not even for a laptop
-couples have to decide who sleeps against the wall as the room size is barely wider than the "full" bed plus 3 or 4 feet on one side, and shoved into a corner on the other
-LADIES BEWARE all mirrors are at shoulder/chest height so you have to stand on the bed to check your outfit
-Bathroom is new, but no soapdish at sink or shower, no light in shower stall, no tub, no clearance to fully open shower door, and no towel rack makes you wonder why they bothered to begin with. The dark tile with no light makes it look like a cave, and impossible for wives to apply make-up without guessing. Could be solved with a sconce or two.
-No plugs in room. Charge your laptop and phone(s)?....unplug a lamp to do it.
-Window AC unit are signaling "filter replace" and are noisier than a lawnmover though the night.
-no amenities (soda/vending/ice/etc.) although there are a hairdryer and safe in rooms
IN CLOSING:
All in all, the hotel provides little more than a bed and TV with a dark bathroom, a paper thin room, and no room to do any business including meeting anyone in the "lobby" (only 2 chairs). I know there are better hotels for the money, but there are also worse....just do your homework, and maybe this review will help. I would be hard pressed to stay at this hotel again, which is too bad as I loved the location and access to area.

name: Buckingham Hotel
title: “New favorite hotel in NYC!!!”
text: I have lived in NYC for many years, visited numerous times and stayed at several of its upscale hotels. The Buckingham is now my favorite.. The size of our room, including large living room, large bedroom both with entertainment systems and wet bar with small refrigerator was a welcome relief after hours of walking, touring etc..the location couldn't be better for the arts (Carnegie, Lincoln Center) and for outdoor enthusiasts (runners, etc) as Central Park is 2 blocks away. Next visit..the Buckingham!!

name: Holiday Inn NYC - Manhattan 6th Avenue
title: “Holiday Inn NYC : chambre pour 4 très étroite”
text:
Emplacement très pratique, dans une rue pas trop passante, avec plein de petits restos à proximité.
Nous avions réservé une chambre pour 4 (2 adultes + 2 enfants), mais double déception : uniquement disponible en fumeurs (avec une pénible odeur de tabac froid partout), et la chambre est une chambre classique, mais avec 2 lits doubles au lieu d'un seul : résultat, c'est très serré... très très serré même !
Pas de frigo de bar non plus.
Par contre, Internet fonctionne vite et bien.
Nous avons échappé au porteur qui a cherché par tous les moyens à nous faire voyager vers l'aéroport avec une des voitures "complice" garée devant l'hôtel pour aller à JFK. Le taxi nous est revenu bien moins cher !
Nous n'avons pas essayé le restaurant de l'hôtel, ni ses autres prestations.
Donc, OK pour une famille, mais seulement en escale d'une ou 2 nuits.

name: Mayfair Hotel
title: “Stop Complaining, You get exactly what you pay for.”
text: The hotel itself is small, 78 rooms total. The entrance and lobby are both decorated with wood paneling. A very beautiful and unique look. The rooms are small; but this is New York and in a building dating back to the early 1900's. If you travel to NY to stay in a hotel room your incredibly stupid. I stayed at the Milford Plaza near by and encountered similar sized rooms. The rooms are clean and the beds are very comfortable. Maintenance is needed in the building, small things such as minor cracks in some mirrors and maybe an occasional leaking faucet. Although; maintenance seems to be on duty almost always and assisted me with these minor details. The staff was willing to go out of their way to help me. The concierge literally walked me down the block to my destination. In addition he fixed the wifi connection on my laptop; which is definitely out of his way. If you want to save some money at the expense of a small room, and lack of luxury, this is the place. The place has everything a human needs to survive pleasurably and more. If your picky and dwell on insignificant details such as lavash furnishings, gold plated chandeliers and room service go elsewhere. If you want a place to stay at a clean hotel with Victorian decorated rooms with a warm and friendly desk staff and concierge, near by parking, wifi internet with Ethernet connections in the rooms and very very comfortable beds; stay at the Mayfair. Well worth the inexpensive price to stay in the heart of one of the most expensive cities in the world. Oh and there are no bugs, myself and a business associate stay here a couple times a month. Also we never had a problem with the billing. Enjoy!

name: Astor on the Park
title: “excellent value for money”
text:
me and my husband stayed here for 3 nights last december, i had read the reviews and was really worried about some of them and even concidered changing hotel, but once we arrived at the hotel i thought it was fab, pretty basic really but excellent value if u are on a budget.
i was worried about the location but dont be the subway is a few minutes walk away and its so cheap to use and once you get used to it its fab and will save u loads on taxis.
i would def stay at this hotel again!!!

name: Flatotel
title: “Great Location - Disappointing Hotel”
text:
The Flatotel is in a great Midtown location. Within walking distance of Times Square and 5th Ave. Although, the rooms are very disappointing. 
 The room is clean, aside from the carpets they could use a good scrubbing. The furniture is much older than shown in the pictures. The hotel only offers 2 elevators, and it is a bit of a wait to use one. 
The staff was very friendly and accomodating. I would not rate this as a 4 star hotel as professed. More like a 3 star. I had gotten a special and paid approximately $180 per night. Prices have now increase to $300 on most websites, I would not pay this.
As a bonus.. we did get to see Americas Next Top Model filming in the lobby. So, the penthouse suites are remodeled as seen on tv.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “The reviews are right: perfect for some and not for others”
text:
Our comments are fairly consistent with the majority of previous reviews, in my estimation. This is a large hotel (1000 rooms) that hosts a lot of conferences. People wanting luxury accommodation or a large bathroom, for example, will be disappointed but for our purposes, we found the room to be perfectly acceptable. In our case, our family of four was on a mission to take in all the touristy sights, so we needed nothing more than a clean, decent place to sleep for 4 nights. Additionally, we booked the room through an online travel website for a “song” so cannot complain about value for money. 
Other reviews have commented on interactions with hotel staff, which appear to be hit and miss. Our experience with the hotel staff, especially the room maids, couldn’t have been more friendly and pleasant. We had two small issues (burnt out bathroom light and inoperable room safe) that were resolved with lightening speed by maintenance and security staff.
We weren’t thrilled having to pay $15/day for WiFi to appease our teenage daughters, but we were braced for it thanks to other tripadvisor reviewers. (Long live tripadvisor!!)
We’d stay again if only because of the location. It was a manageable walk to Times Square, or to the UN if that’s your cup of tea. Otherwise we took the subway daily to visit other attractions since The Roosevelt is very near Grand Central Station where the subway is easily accessible.
We loved the proximity to a little café right across the street called Cosi (a chain) where we had our coffee and a quick, inexpensive breakfast every morning of our stay (delicious breakfast sandwiches and wraps, yogurt parfaits and steel-cut oats). Anyone wanting a big, leisurely breakfast of eggs, pancakes, sausage, homefries etc. would want to go elsewhere. 
Yes, we would book there again due to the price point and plough the savings into sight-seeing and fabulous dinners.

name: Americana Inn
title: “Gut gelegen aber minimalster Komfort”
text: Das Americana ist sehr zentral. Die Zimmer sind aber spartanisch eingerichtet und winzig - kein Charme, null Atmosphäre!

name: Manhattan Broadway Hotel
title: “Great location”
text:
and clean place
Stayed here for a week with family. Not as bad as I thought with all the bad reviews. It was actually really convenient. Not much amenities, but who cares, didn't spend much time in the hotel. Shopped and toured nyc, so why not.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Queens Court Hotel
title: “Location is good”
text: The hotel was located in Flushing Chinatown and only 2 -3 blocks to the subway and the Long Island Railroad and close to LaGuardia airport. Good food in Flushing chinatown and also safe to walk around even late at night. Room was clean but there was a lot of noise in the mornings from the construction across the street. Also, the TV was old and the reception was bad. The heater in the room was not adjustable -either it was on and the room became very hot or we had to turn it off and the room got cold. What was really strange was that when it came time to check out, we were told we had to leave with all our luggage or we could not check out and we would be charge extra money after noon. As my brother had one of the rooms and was staying an extra night, we had planned to check out, leave our luggage in his room and get lunch around the corner and come back to take our luggage to the car after lunch. They did not offer to keep our luggage for us when I explained the situation so we decided to check out with all our bags, put them in the car and then go to lunch. I have never heard of this rule in any other hotel. Will probably still go back just because of the location and the price was reasonable and hopefully, the construction will be done next time.

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Great hotel in fab location for budget-conscious travellers”
text:
My mum and I went to NYC for a bit of shopping and sightseeing. St James' was chosen as it was in a central location and competetively priced... In fact couldn't find a better deal, even in an East Village hotel I had stayed before!
This is a standard, basic to mid-range, hotel with no extras as such (eg. no restaurant), but they're not needed as Times Square is around the corner, as well as cafes, shops etc.
Staff were friendly, helpful and efficient. The lifts were reaaally slow and a bit dodgy, but we took stairs most of the time anyway. 
The rooms are unfashionably decorated but tidy. Our room was cleaned on a daily basis, with fresh towels and beds made. What else do you need, when you only sleep there and spend the rest of the time exploring NYC? We certainly didn't.
If you have no problem with being in a basic hotel and rather spend you hard-earned cash on shopping and other entertainments, choose this hotel. Also a perfect choice for NYC 'first-timers' as it is right in the middle of Manhattan, so safe to walk around any time of day and always easy to find.

name: Central Park House
title: “Wild Party House - Unsafe”
text: Too bad as this place has a lot of potential but has clearly word has spread that this is the place to throw wild parties. This place has no staff, building management or security (yes, no security) on site. Proved to be a big problem as one of the nights we were there two rowdy and extremely loud parties were roaring till the wee hours of the morning. At one point a large and rather scary brawl spilled over into the hallway. Good luck finding someone at the management company to call (we had to read the fine print on our intinerary...doesn't matter as we ended up calling the police. If you have kids, looking for a good night sleep, want to feel safe in your room I would not recommend staying here.

name: Hotel St. James
title: “You just can't beat the St. James Hotel”
text: I have just read a recent review for the St. Jame's hotel and I also give it the thumbs up! It is the ideal spot for a shopping trip or indeed sightseeing as it is so central to everything. While the hotel does not have a restaurant (who cares) as there are 2 great diners right next door!! I stayed there Dec 06 also and the only complaint I have is the heat as it cannot be regulated and the rooms get very hot. The beds though are very comfy and the room and bathroom was spotless. It is a great little find for the price and location and I will most definitely stay there again next year.

name: La Semana Hotel
title: “völlig inakzeptabel und grausam - nicht buchen!”
text: La Semana verdient nicht den Begriff Hotel, es scheint eher ein abgewracktes Bordell zu sein. Unser erstes Zimmer im Keller ohne echtes Fenster stank nach jahrelangem Rauch, Muff und anderen Körperausdünstungen. Wir haben sofort ein neues Zimmer verlangt und das andere Zimmer im ersten Stock war nur vom Geruch besser. Größe des Zimmers kaum mehr als das Bett breit aber mit verdreckter alter Rundbadewanne im Zimmer. Alles verspiegelt, zT schwarz lackierte Fliesen und rote bemalte Wände. Die Wände scheinen nur aus Holz zu sein, denn wir konnten mit den Nachbarn quasi reden. Das Fenster verhangen führte ohnehin nur zu einem verdreckten Abluftschacht. Die Elektroinstallation konnte gut in allen Entwicklungsstadien nachvollzogen werden, da teilweise auf Putz und zT einfach nicht zu Ende geführt und unfertig. Das Klo und die Dusche: unterste Kategorie und sicher seit etlichen Jahren nicht mehr renoviert. Handtuchhalter abgerissen, Ablagen Fehlanzeige. Wir haben nach der zweiten Nacht - nachdem auch noch im Nachbarzimmer offensichtlich nicht ganz legale Geschäfte die ganze Nacht über abgewickelt wurden!! - das Hotel zum Glück verlassen können und sind nebenan in einem echten Hotel zum gleichen Preis untergekommen.

name: New York Inn
title: “Grotty & overpriced”
text:
Should have known by the locations & low price that the place would be awful.
Rundown, grotty - my door did not lock. Shower was a drip and cold but honestly didn't feel the bathroom was clean enough to shower in.
The roof was falling in.
Only positive was that the staff were friendly & helpful but really don't go there

name: Woogo Apartments - Times Square
title: “No Go to the WooGo!”
text:
I would definitely not recommend this hotel. We had booked 2x 2 bedroom rooms and when we got there we had to wait for a long time because there was a double booking with our rooms. The whole hotel looked old and was of very poor quality and in need of a lot of renovations. The kitchen had unusable filthy crockery and the suite was dusty and smelly. The beds were extremely uncomfortable too. The doors jammed often, electrical plugs hung from sockets, the bathroom taps came off in your hand, the shower curtain was filthy and we saw a huge rat run across the room - we tried to trap it under the filthy oven in the kitchen, but the manager wasn’t interested and didn’t even own any mouse traps, although other people complained about them as well. 
It was such a shame because it is in a great location in Times Square but the accommodation was almost unbearable. Let’s just say No Go to the Woogo Hotel, it’s as bad as it’s name sounds. Had there been any other beds in New York for the 2 nights we needed, we would definitely have moved.

name: Wolcott Hotel
title: “Excellent for the price....”
text: I have stayed in many hotels in NYC - some lower end and some higher end and more often than not disappointing because the hotel ads were misleading or omitted important flaws - like no elevator, old beds, etc. The Wolcott delivered! The room (a triple for 3 women) was clean, roomy and quite comfortable. The beds (3 twin beds) appeared to be new and were very comfortable!! No problems with the shower, lights, etc. Overall we were very happy with the room and the the price. The staff was wonderful and very accomodating! We arrived at noon and were able to go to our room even though check-in was at 3:00. Checkout was at 12:30 and there was no problem storing our luggage until we left town at 5:30 pm. I would definitely stay there again.

name: Manhattan Broadway Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text: If you are looking for a budget hotel with a great location I would recommend this hotel. It would be wrong to say that it isn't in need of a refurbishment, however the room was clean and the beds were comfy with clean sheets. We had a power shower and clean bathroom. There was no light from the windows but as we only used the room as a base for sleeping this was not a problem. Please ignore the negative reviews as they are unfounded. If you are looking for a luxury hotel then don't stay here, if you would rather save your money for shopping and sight seeing then this is a great place to stay, Staff are friendly and really helpful. Wi-fi was an added bonus and only cost $3 a day. We stayed for 3 nights and would definitely stay again.

name: Wolcott Hotel
title: “location, location, location”
text: Great service.....really nice staff....water pressure in the shower a bit dodgy so we had baths but that's not such a trial!!...room and sheets cleaned properly and regularly and great room safe.....You can see the Empire State Building out of the window!....Beautiful, old-world reception.... if you're looking for a budget hotel in New York I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this one!...I think we paid just £60 a night for our stay..

name: Wolcott Hotel
title: “Worst Hotel in the world”
text: I've been to NYC many times before and I never had an experiance like this. The hotel was terrible...it is worst then a hostal. I did not take my shoes off once....I even considered taking a shower with them on....the floors were gross the hotel smelled awful. The staff were very rude. There was hair in the bed....and was scared to sleep with the lights off. This was the worst experiance of my life. I will never stay at this hotel again. I do not recommend this hotel.

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Great Location-Nice Room”
text:
We stayed at the St. James Dec. 8-10, 2006. Great Location. Some rooms on the 8th Floor have been upgraded and ours was very nice. Large rooms for New York. Bathroom was very small but usable. Rooms were clean. Elevators are troublesome and have a mind of their own. If you have a lot of luggage, you may want to stay on a lower floor, in case you must carry it down the stairs. 
Front desk would not call us a cab. Cabs do not run past the hotel much. Husband had to flag one down on Broadway and have it come by and pick up the luggage and me.
Overall, I would stay at the St.James again anytime.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Old, very old”
text:
This is supposed to be a historic hotel. It probably is, but they forgot historic hotels can be renovated. The rooms are big. They could easily fit 5 by NYC standards. Our room windows allowed some cold wind through and the heater would not heat. The doors are an attraction on themselves: they tried to fit "modern" card-based locks but the old doors have strange shapes and they do not fit well together, making it difficult to open or close the doors.
The hotel is well located, just across the street from NY Penn Station, which is convenient for public transportation, shopping (Macy's) and some dining (specially Koreatown, a couple of blocks away).
One thing that we noticed is that there seems to be a constant line for the reception desk. So expect some waiting while arriving.

name: Manhattan Broadway Hotel
title: “Excellent Location, Good Budget Hotel”
text: The hotel is only blocks from Broadway and Times Square. It is obviously a budget hotel at this price and it was fine if you keep that in mind. The bathroom wasn't incredibly clean and there wasn't enough hot water, but it wasn't too bad either. For the price, I think it was fine to stay there.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “OK but nothing more....”
text:
We stayed here back in 2004 and have stayed at other hotels in the city on our other visits prior to this one. i thought we would give it a try again to be honest it hadn't improved, the bathroom and the room itself were ok we were on the 10th floor and you could here the street noise. 
There was no free wifi as was advertised on the website and we were only able to get online on our last night (as I am writing this review) in the room before then we had to go to Starbucks.
It's an old tired hotel that needs a complete refurbishment and more room amenities, we had a fridge but no tea or coffee making facilities and an old CRT TV in a cupboard.
There are other hotels at a similar price range, but when we come back to New York in another couple of years I won't be staying here.

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Adequate with no frills”
text:
At first glance the hotel and our room made us wish we'd stay somewhere else but once we got past the initial feelings, I'd have to say that the accommodations, although spartan, were adequate. There was no alarm clock in the room, one of the overhead light bulbs was burned, a plastic fixture in the elevator was broken and the TV remote did not work. The heating system and the A/C both worked fine. The cafeteria next door was good and the location could not be beat. They provided wake-up service and secured car service for us to the airport. We stayed 5 night and since we basically only stayed in the room to sleep, everything worked out OK.
If you are looking for a "no frills" hotel with a great location, I'd recommend it.

name: West Side Inn
title: “Unsanitary, dangerous, unfriendly”
text: No-one expects luxury from a lower-priced hotel, but the West Side Inn lies about the ameneties it offers, posts misleading pictures on its web site, and ultimately is NOT all that cheap (I paid nearly $100 a night). I've stayed in plenty of budget hotels and hostels, most of which offered basic ameneties but were clean and friendly. The WSI is filthy, smells like stale sweat and urine throughout, unsafe (doors don't close properly, no emergency lighting, no fire detection, one stairway, poor lighting, mentally unstable permanent guests, etc.). It presumably makes its money through non-refunded cancellations. Please look at my pictures to see what it really looks like.

name: Chocolat Hostel
title: “Hotel From Hell”
text: I booked a weekend stay in NYC through Orbitz at the West End Studio based on the beautiful pictures they have on their web site. What I encountered when we got there was a complete nightmare. The clerk gave us a room on the 6th floor and told us that the elevator was broken, but the repairman was on his way to fix it. Since coming home and reading these reviews I know that was a lie and that it's an on going problem that the hotel has no intention of fixing. After climbing 6 flights of stairs I noticed that the doors on the rooms didn't hang straight. Then as I opened the door to our room we nearly passed out from the stench. The sight that greeted us was of unmade beds with dirty sheets and blankets with nasty, dirty, towels laying everywhere. There were two department store shopping bags full of trash from the previous guest. What looked like pubic hairs were on the bedsheets. Black and white TV, no phone, broken air conditioner, and no working clock. I called Orbitz to complain and was told I could get another hotel on Time Square for a litte more money and when I agreed to take the room at the other hotel I was disconnected. I then called Orbitz back and got another operator who told me that the hotel I was told about did not exist. Yet Orbitz advertises that exact hotel on their website and we passed by it several times while at Time Square. Something is not right with this hotel being in business and Orbitz protecting the hotels business. I would not recommend anyone booking through Orbitz and advise staying as far away from West End Studios as possible. Spend the extra money and get a good hotel.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Hotel bad location good”
text: Room 683- room was dingy and dark. Television did not turn off and was stuck on for the 4 nights we stayed. On the last night we found a mouse in the room...the rooms are in need of refurbishment BIG TIME!!The reception was very poor... Upon check in we were treated poorly ( after a long haul flight this is not what you need) no free wifi anywhere, in nyc this is not acceptable! If you arent looking for comfort this place is o.k but the standard is very poor

name: W New York
title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
We checked into the W on Lexington. We were celebrating an anniversary so I said I was willing to pay a little more for a room with a view. The woman at the front desk said she would be happy to accommodate my request and upgraded us to a larger queen room "with a view". The view was the A/C unit on the building next door and the back end of other nearby high-rises...but, there was light. If this was "larger" than the room we were previously scheduled for then that other room would have been a disaster. We had to keep our shoes lined up in the room because there was no space for them in the closet. I've had larger rooms in Paris. 
The housekeeping was good, but I never received any new "plastic wrapped" glasses. I'm a little nervous drinking out of the regular glasses...I'm never sure if they are clean. The bathroom amenities were pretty tragic. I would think for a $400 per night room they'd have at least had a brand of shampoo that I'd heard of.
The hotel put out a very nice cooler with ice and fresh fruits in the lobby. Just a little sip of something cool after our shopping excursions. It was a nice touch.
The bar is packed every night and they have a DJ several nights a week I guess everyone was on expense account because our 2 drinks, Sprite and Grey Goose Martini were $22. YIKES!
The hotel is in a good location and just 2 blocks from a Metro stop. Their restaurant only serves breakfast and there is no coffee maker in the room (probably because there is no place to put it). Overall I'd say it's a typical "nice" hotel for New York City.

name: Hotel Riverside Studios
title: “Yikes....very scary”
text:
When I walked into this dump I immediately recognized it from an episode of Law & Order SVU. It truly looks like one of those hotels that would end up in a show about killers and rapists. It was awful. Half the deadbolt was missing, the mattresses were covered in plastic, there was no water in the shower and the sign for the elevator was written on a US Postal Service label.
The front desk people were unfriendly and dirty as was the hotel. The shared bathroom had a sink that was falling out of the wall.
Scary!!!!!
We actually ended up staying out as late as possible to avoid sleeping 
here.
Let's just say this place will never see me again.

name: Wolcott Hotel
title: “Ottima base d'appoggio!”
text:
Siamo stati al wolcott 3/4 giorni, c siamo trovati molto bene x l'ottima posizione, la pulizia e anche la colazione nn é male ;)
Essendo in una posizione centrale (a 2 passi dall'empire!) abbiamo visitato la città a piedi, MOLTO CONSIGLIATO!
Le camere sono comode e abbastanza spaziose, l'arredo é tipico anni 20.. se non avete troppe pretese questo hotel é perfetto, noi c siamo trovati molto bene e in caso di ritorno a NY sicuramente penseremo al wolcott!!

name: Hotel Riverside Studios
title: “Great if you like hard beds and disgusting bathrooms.”
text:
After reading all the mixed reviews of this place, me and my sister were a little wary of staying here. For the price, its great, a nice neighborhood and quick walk to the 72nd and Broadways station.
When we first checked in, we were told to go to the "elevator" at the end of the hallway. After walking around, we finally noticed what looked like a closet door with elevator buttons on the outside. This was the elevator. Our room looked pretty decent and was exactly as it had been described by other travelers as a dorm room. The shared bathroom was right next to our room. However, my sister noticed a pubic hair on the "clean" towel that was supplied in our room, the bathtub was disgusting and I showered in my flip flops. There was rust on the drain and all we got was a bar of soap and one towel and washcloth.
If you are looking for something in a nice, quiet neighborhood, quick walk to the subway and a great little cafe on the corner, this is your place. If you're looking for paper thin walls, a shared bathroom, and hard beds, this is also your place. It was good for a weekend stay, but not quite worth the 133 bucks we paid for an overnight stay.

name: Hotel Carter
title: “Never ever ever”
text:
this hotel was terrible, the image above needs changing, they now have plastic barrier in place (probably as protection against the clients staying)
it was like a back pack hostel in a 3rd world country. our room on the 9th floor was dirty, the original beds i think from when the hotel was built, our bathroom was disgusting, and the basin cracked, and the bathroom cabinet - painted over so many times, and again the mirror was damaged, water was warm at best, toilet was old. flat screen tv on the wall looked so out of place it was the only new thing in the room - no chair to sit on.
the worst part was waking up early in the morning, and feeling the lumps on my face arms and shoulders, legs from the BED BUGS !!!! my son was covered too. we came down to the lobby and asked them what they would do and the receptionist blamed me as a tourist for bringing them into her hotel !!! we cancelled our 2nd night stay and left, as she would only offer to spray the bed and we would have to re-use the same room.
Yes its close to Times Square - but so is a blanket and a box - and i would have preferred that to staying there again

name: Hotel Riverside Studios
title: “I'd go back again”
text: I wanted to take my two daughters (aged 10 and 6) to see some of the main sites in NYC (eg, Statue of Liberty, MOMA, Brooklyn Bridge) on a budget. The Hotel Riverside Studios met my needs almost perfectly. The shared bathrooms were marginally inconvenient in that I don't like my daughters being unsupervised in a strange place. However, the rooms were clean, the TV worked, and it was easy to get around Manhattan from the hotel. In addition, there were two decent cafes a couple of blocks away that served good food, and a Barnes & Noble in walking distance down by the Lincoln Center. I'd go back again with pleasure, at the price I paid for a Manhattan room. I might not stay in summer, though. I imagine the rooms might get hot during a warm spell.

name: Morningside Inn
title: “I agree - best value in NYC”
text: Just spent another night in Morningside Inn (been there at least 6+ times) and again I agree with an earlier reviewer - it is an excellent value. No, the rooms are not enormous and the toiletries are meager - but the hotel and rooms are clean and it feels safe and the beds are decent. What else you need for the price I don't know. If so, go pay 3-5 times the price elsewhere for a place that gives you fancier soap....but for my money and NYC experience the place always fits the bill and I have never had an issue with the front desk or any of the staff. In my trips in NYC about 4 times a year I always hope they have a room left and am delighted when they do.

name: St. Marks Hotel
title: “great location good deal”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed there last month.
 It is exactly what I expected for the price. 
It is a budget hotel, absolutely no frills. But who wants to stay in the room?!!
We stayed in a double room and it was perfectly clean; it appeats basic, but it had a TV, bathroom and bed, which is all we wanted
 The staff are young, friendly - and helpful

name: Morningside Inn
title: “Plenty of space and close to metro”
text: The Morningside Inn was a good place for our family to stay while seeing the NY sights - near the metro, a grocery store, and enough room for us to get a good night's sleep. Not a luxery suite, but very adquate for us.

name: Morningside Inn
title: “Bearable in an attractive part of New York”
text: Budget spartan room with nothing moveable and unnecessary stern warning not to steal the furnishings. No TV, hence the bonus that there's no TV noise next door. Quiet street. Peaceful ambience inside, and the few guests seemed largely budget-conscious young travellers. Lifts and loos erratic. However, close by is Upper Broadway, a cheerful area with almost Parisian ambience, good eating, drinking and excellent bus/metro communications .

name: Hotel Carter
title: “Perfect location!”
text:
We had a group of 8 book two rooms at Hotel Carter because we were on a serious budget. Had really low expectations and were pleansantly surprised upon arriving. Clean beds, NO BED BUGS, a bit of a dingy bathroom (little mold in the ceiling) so we wore flip flops when we showered, but honestly, you can't beat this place when it comes to location. 
We felt safe and clean and were central to EVERYTHING the big apple has to offer. Would stay here again in a heartbeat!

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Fantastic Location”
text: My friends (5 in all) stayed at the St. James November 23rd to November 30th. Like everyone, after reading the reviews I was nervous. When we checked in we were given a room on the 12th floor. The room was awful, it was dirty and very old. We went down to reception and asked for a renovated room (like someone advised in another review) and we were given a room on the 5th floor. This room was much better. It was a good size with 2 double beds and plenty of room for the roll away bed we needed. The bathroom was a decent size and there were clean towels daily. Housekeeping staff were very friendly and visited daily. There are 2 deli stores right outside the hotel which are great. Breakfast is especially good at Cranberrys and very inexpensive. Connollys restaurant is also really good. The location of the St. James is fantastic. Right between Times Square and 5th Avenue. We had less than a 5 minute walk to the parade. My 2 bits of advice to anyone would be 1. Ask for a renovated room and 2. call the hotel directly for a quote. We were quoted $189 plus tax and roll away bed per room at hotels and paid $125.00 plus tax and roll away bed when we called the hotel directly. This is a basic hotel, no frills. It definitely served our purpose and we had a wonderful time. I would stay there again.

name: the Lexington
title: “Worried about mixed reviews so I checked this out in advance but...”
text:
DID NOT STAY! I had booked a reservation in June through a special deal at travel ticker. The price was excellent under $215 per night for a stay in October of this year which is the middle of high season in the city. The price since then has been averaging about $269 per night. I stayed with a friend for a few days in June because her roommate was traveling and went there in person to check it out. If I had not I probably would have stayed and been upset.
You would think it was fine from the street view and because it was a Radisson and on Lexington Avenue but I was disappointed almost immediately when I walked in. The condition of the lobby was old and worn looking. I was still trying to keep an open mind and proceeded to the front desk and told them I had a reservation in October but was concerned because of some bad reviews and asked to see a room . I waited for over a half an hour for someone to come out and show me and nobody came out until I asked what was taking so long despite the fact I told them I posted regular reviews on Trip Advisor. I think they were hoping I would leave. I watched the front desk and while there were lots of people checking in I was not impressed with the attention paid to patrons at the front desk by the staff.
When someone did come out she was very pleasant and we took the elevator to a room. The condition of the hallways and the carpeting on the way to the room was disgusting and filthy. The room much to my surprise was very small but lovely. It was a standard queen. It turned out I was told the room I booked was even smaller, a petite room. Now I have stayed in small rooms in NYC before but this was already pretty small. I was told all the rooms were in similar condition but the overall condition of the hotel was dilapidated and not for me. I canceled my reservation.The only good thing I can say about my experience and the hotel is that it is in a great location.

name: W New York
title: “Pretty standard, would stay again”
text:
We had a late check in and were up graded to a spectacular room. The upgraded room was nice, and had enough room to be comfortable. I don't want to know how much smaller the "cozy" room is though. I feel like smaller rooms are pretty standard in NY, we were just there to change, shower and sleep so it was good. The staff were helpful and the room was clean. 
The hotel was in a good location, easy to find, and not overly far from anything.

name: Royal Park Hotel
title: “Cheap, clean excellent location”
text:
We travelled to new york for 7 nights and were surprised just how close the hotel is to the subway (a 2 minute walk if that). We had a double en suite room. ok so we had a view of a brick wall but thats not why we went to new york! it was lovely and clean, and the bed and towels were made/changed daily. The bathroom had recently been refurbished so everything was brand new!
The tube stop around the corner is 2 express stops from time square so you can be right in the action in about 10 minutes. Ideally situated the hotel is surrounded by supermarkets, pharmacy's and restaurants so everything you need is close to hand. The staff were nice and pleasant although we didnt really need to deal with them much.
A $2 fee for them to look after your bags on check out day but they are kept in a locked room so you know they are safe.
For the money you pay, dont expect a fancy posh hotel.... you get a bed, bathroom and towels, if your wanting a tv or glasses by the sink then this isnt the place for you. HOWEVER if you want somewhere nice clean and safe to rest after a busy day in new york then its ideal.
Highly Reccommend! :D

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “A average hotel for an average budget”
text:
You pay for what you get at this hotel.
We visited New York for the first time last year and had an amazing couple of days. We booked an airport transfer bus which took us straight to our hotel. 
When we entered the check in hall we were quite surprised at the cleanness and we later discovered this is probably where they have spent most of their money.
We got our room and went up to the room. When we stepped off the elevator it was like we had transported back to 1920. And then we came to our room.
We were quite shocked. It was smell, and not particularly the cleanest of rooms. It needed a lot of work to fit in to the 21st century. 
The hotel staff were very generous and helpful, but on the whole a budget hotel like this is fine if your only planning to take in the sights on New York. 
We still had an amazing trip and it didn't bother us too much.

name: the Lexington
title: “"Hidden" gem, low cost, great value!”
text: I am always surprised about how great this place is. Almost always the cheapest brand-name hotel within blocks, and the service is great and the rooms are nice, clean, and sizable. If you want to say in midtown for 30% less than average prices at a nice hotel that is great for business travelers, then this is your place. I would recommend it.

name: St. Marks Hotel
title: “Great Location and perfect for our needs”
text: My friends and I stayed at St. Marks hotel during the last weekend in August and encountered no problems at all with the hotel. The location was excellent as it was very close to the subway station (Astor Place) about a 2mins walk and is a short subway ride from all you need to see in the city. The hotel is also within walking distance to SOHO, China Town, Canal St, etc...Our room had 2 double beds, air conditioning that worked well and wasn't loud as others have said and also had a flat panel tv with a bunch of channels. Washroom was clean and tidy although it was quite small. I would recommend this hotel for students or young singles as the area has a vibrant nightlife and is located close to NYU. Overall this hotel exceeded our expectation for the price we paid ($170/night) when compared to other accommodations in one of the most expensive cities in the world. The staff was very helpful and friendly and assisted you with any needs you might have. I would definitely go back again and will recommend this hotel to people visiting NYC.

name: New York Inn
title: “Ottimo per la posizione”
text: L'albergo è in una posizione veramente comoda, a un isolato da Times Square! La struttura è modesta, ma non abbiamo avuto problemi di sporcizia (la polvere della moquette, ma quello è un problema frequente negli hotel!!). Il personale è veramente simpatico e gentile, in reception facevamo sempre lunghe e piacevoli chiacchierate. Prezzo basso, in rapporto alle cifre di Midtown Manhattan.

name: Manhattan Broadway Hotel
title: “Freezing in the City”
text: We stayed here because 6 girls were on a shopping trip and moved from another not-so-friendly NYC hotel because of the # of people. Anyway - the MB would accomodate 6 to a room. Luckily we had an air mattress with us (remember - we were here to shop!). One of the beds was a broken futon thingy, and the other 2 beds had linens that came from a charity organization. The bathroom was disgusting with a horrible blue light. It was December and snowy, and the heat didn't work - one of those old boiler heaters. They had to come and tape blankets around the windows to keep the cold out. We slept in our coats, gloves, scarves, you name it, we used it for warmth. The maids cart is a shopping cart mind you. And the elevator is the scariest thing ever. Needless to say, we really slummed it and would gladly pay a little more for a nicer hotel the next time we hit the Big Apple. Enter at your own risk!!

name: New York Inn
title: “Experiencia terrivel”
text: Estive em NY por diversas vezes e na primeira vez fiquei neste hotel. Como tinha reservado aqui no Brasil e ja pago, quando cheguei lá não tive como cancelar a reserva e fui obrigada a permanecer por quase 10 dias. O recepcionista que nos atendeu ao chegar era indiano e mal conseguia entender o que ele dizia, so entendi que não devolveria o dinheiro ja pago. Logo na entrada do hotel da pra perceber a sujeira, mal cabia nossa bagagem para fazer o chek in. O quarto era horrivel, sujo, embaixo da cama descobri uma armadilha de rato e mal conseguia dormir imaginando um andando pelo quarto. Os corredores eram imundos, a escada parecia nunca ter sido lavada,carpetes horriveis e encardidos.O lugar é bom, procurava então andar o dia inteiro e so chegar bem tarde , bem cansada , somente para dormir. Não aconselho ao amigos, pessima experiencia.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Absolutely Disgusting”
text: Walked into the foyer and thought it looked OK but upon opening the prison door to our room were appalled by what confronted us. Were expecting basic for the cost and location but this was something else! Dark, dingy, dirty and very cramped. My husband tried to turn on the air con and it fell apart, there were clothes and blankets from past inhabitants in the wardrobe and under the bed, holes in the carpet, wires hanging out of the wall from the telephone and many more things beside. I dread to think what was sharing the most uncomfortable bed I have ever slept in with us! We could not wait to get out of there. Avoid at all costs, there must be better hotels for the same price in NY, location is not everything!

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Great value hotel in a brilliant location for a tourist”
text: The Paramount is impressive upon entrance to the foyer. Service is efficient and welcoming. There is a nice bar at the front for a quick drink before heading out, complete with friendly bar staff. Rooms are decent, if not on the small side - but this is NYC, its par for course. The biggest downside to the rooms is that the walls seem paper thin and a fair bit of noise travels from your neighbours' rooms, although really not a major issue in the greater scheme. The furnishings are decent but far from special however the room is still very pleasant to come back to after a long day of seeing NYC. Times Square is a stone's throw away making it an excellent hotel for its price. Would highly recommend to anyone looking for value in a fantastic location.

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Good location but rooms very small”
text: max 2 adults per room, there is hardly enough room with luggage, otherwise good location for a short break. bar and restaurant poor

name: New York Inn
title: “Super bien ubicado y el staff...”
text: Super bien ubicado y el staff muy, muy amable! La habitación pequeña y las terminaciones descuidadas;pero las sábanas y toallas limpias y el tele más grande que la pieza. Microondas en la habitación y acceso a internet gratis... Volvería!

name: Royal Park Hotel
title: “Relativ gute Lage, sehr unsauber, nicht wie im Internet dargestellt”
text: Wir hatten 2 Zimmer mit einem gemeinsamen Bad reserviert. Das gab es gar nicht, obwohl wir dafür einen Aufpreis gezahlt hatten. Die Zimmer wurden nur aufgeräumt aber nicht gereinigt. Das Bad war sehr schmutzig und wurde anscheinend überhaupt nicht gereinigt. Nur das Bad im Erdgeschoß (beim Eingang) schien ordendlich zu sein. Es fehlte der normale Hotelstandard (Fön...) Man konnte die Heizung nicht einstellen. Dieses Hotel kann ich nicht empfehlen. Es gibt bessere Jugendherbergen.

name: Manhattan Broadway Hotel
title: “Pleasantly surprised”
text:
After reading all of the negative reviews for this place, my boyfriend and I were pretty scared about staying at this hotel. 
The lobby really isn't terribly impressive, I must admit. It's more like a hallway with a desk and a vending machines and two available computers for internet access at the end. A bit more like a college dorm than a hotel, but if you consider that the hotel has "Budget" in the name, then it's really not surprising that the lobby isn't all fancy and sparkling like the Ritz Carlton or something. Plus the staff at the desk is always very friendly and helpful, which is a definite plus.
Elevator was a bit cramped going up; two people with luggage is almost a tight fit -- with one more random person in there it's quite tight. 
Once we got to our actual room, we both breathed a sigh of relief and even laughed a little, because it was much, MUCH better than what we were expecting after all of the bad reviews. We had two double beds (we only used one -- we weren't the ones who booked the room, so that isn't the hotel's fault), which were fairly comfortable and the sheets were clean. The lighting in the room was particularly nice, and there were no bulky lamps or anything taking up space; everything was creatively wall mounted, and it created a very nice atmosphere in the room, especially with the addition of the one wall that was painted bright red...you will see this in the pictures. The bathroom was clean and there were towels, which were a bit on the thin side...we brought our own towels, however, so that was not a problem (I recommend that you bring your own toiletries as well). I think the bathtub may have actually been a jacuzzi at one point, but the jets were sealed over... Shower worked nicely. We saw absolutely NO bugs or rodents of any kind while we were there. The only noise we heard was in the hallways when housekeeping was out making rounds, or when there were people in the hallways making a lot of loud noises....so a bit more like a college dorm or an apartment in terms of hallway noise as well. We were on the 3rd floor, and I didn't really hear any street noise from where we were. Our room was also well-heated.
The only problem we had was shortly before we left, when the toilet got clogged, and the plunger that was provided with the bathroom (which I think is a good idea; I see few hotels that do this, and I would really rather plunge my own toilet and save the embarrassment of calling someone else to do it for me) didn't work as well as it should have... But we let them know about it on checkout, and the lady at the desk made a note about it in the logs and thanked us for telling her, so I assume they sent someone to fix the toilet and maybe replace the plunger. Kudos to them for being on top of things.
I would totally stay here again, though. The location is FANTASTIC -- we walked everywhere we went, no need to take any taxis at all. :)
(Not sure if I would recommend for business travelers though, since our room did not include a desk. This did not affect us at all, however, since we were just tourists who needed a comfortable place to sleep at night.)

name: Manhattan Broadway Hotel
title: “Do not stay here, mice!”
text: I stayed here for one week, what an experience. Just pay the extra few quid to stay up the road in the New Yorker for a cheap break. I was there with my partner and parents. We both had to change rooms three times each due to mice and overflowing toilets. Woke up one morning with a mouse running across the bed and shelf. No wardrobes in any of the three rooms I moved too. We didn't feel safe or secure in hotel. We wondered if this hotel rented rooms out by the hour... On my return I have contacted hotels.com to complain, This hotel should not be listed on their website, it is a health hazard. Only thing this hotel (really a hostel) has going for it is the location. Never again.

name: West Side Inn
title: “Abominable, horrible, répugnant!!!”
text:
J'avais réservé par internet une chambre pour deux personnes. Nous arrivons et là, le patron visiblement, souhaite nous mettre avec deux autres personnes dans une chambre à 4. Après plusieurs négociations, j'obtiens ce qui nous servira de "todi" pour une nuit (au lieu de 4 puisque nous avons changé d'hôtel).
Un ascenseur d'un 1m² grand maximum, donc nous décidons de prendre les escaliers... Insectes morts sur les marches, une odeur de moisie à vomir et vue sur des bouteilles, mouchoirs et autres débris jetés sur le toit du bâtiment voisin. 
Nous arrivons non sans peine à notre étage et là, magnifique couloir sombre (une vraie prison) éclairé par la lumière des sanitaires restés ouverts et une pauvre lampe. Nous ouvrons notre minuscule chambre et découvrons les planches de bois qui servent de sommier à notre lit superposé, une énorme trou dans le plafond, des rideaux répugnants, une fenêtre qui ne ferme pas (le bois se décompose), et un loquet de porte presque aussi efficace que s'il n'y avait rien! Et l'odeur, toujours l'odeur!!
Les points positifs: un ventilateur, un miroir et 3 cintres accrochés sous l'étagère de la TV (dont le fil est trop court pour être branché à l'unique prise de la pièce et qui de toute façon ne marche pas puisque nous l'avons descendue de son étagère pour la tester).
Les sanitaires sont relativement propres (du moins sur la demi-journée que nous avons passé là-bas), mais il y a toujours cette odeur nauséabonde.
Bref, à éviter!! Je n'ai pas réussi à me faire rembourser sur place, mais le site internet par lequel j'avais réservé, après envoie de photo et échange de mail, m'a intégralement restitué mon argent.

name: New York Inn
title: “Kein 2. Mal”
text:
Der Urlaub war super, sobald ich das Hotel Morgens verlassen habe. Die Lage ist gut, aber für den Preis den ich bezahlt habe der absolute Reinfall. Das Hotel ist in einem sehr schlechten Zustand und hat uns den Urlaub etwas kaputt gemacht.
Niemals ein Hotel unter 3 Sterne buchen. Selbst wenn man nur im Hotel schläft, es kann zu qual werden.

name: Skyline Hotel
title: “Not a great location, but a decent hotel.”
text:
Well I had never been to NYC before, so it was hard to do research. I chose this hotel based on its cheap price (around 100 bucks) and its multiple great reviews. However when I got there I noticed a few problems. For one - the location isn't really all that great. Its about a 15 minute walk to something worth visiting... even the subway... 
downtown, central park and the upper side are all quite a ways away. 
You'd be better off stayin' near times square... or in downtown. The neighborhood appeared safe, but it isn't that interesting. The staff was friendly and helpful for the most part, but not terribly knowledgeable of the city. The rooms are huge however, much larger than most in NYC. The room is well furnished and the bed is not uncomfortable (but not amazing either). The bathroom is pretty and it has a tub and shower (i had the king room - i'd recommend it). The room smelled of smoke however (I requested a non-smoking room) and the A/C + Heating unit rattled rather loudly.
