The view is nothing spectacular actually... so don't be fooled by the advertisements. But it isn't the ugliest thing in the world. I wouldn't stay here again, I'd rather be in a different location... but the experience was not a bad one.

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Fantastic hotel”
text:
Our compliments to Leonardo, receptionist , he delivered a fantastic service.
W.E. van der Sluis, from Holland

name: the Lexington
title: “The only Radisson in the world that is not worth the brand”
text:
The presentation on the website and the reality of the hotel in reality vastly different from one another. We are a party of 6 people.
1. Hotel appears dirty
2. Rooms are smelly
3. Rooms are small
4. No fridge in rooms
5. No water(bottle) in room
6. Room temperature controls broken in 3 rooms.
7. Cold water throughout hotel this morning.
8. Wifi in lobby extremely slow
9. No kettle and coffee in rooms.
There are definitely better hotels around. We will never stay at this hotel or recommend this hotel to anyone.

name: Skyline Hotel
title: “nice hotel, good concierge service,”
text:
This hotel is quite nice, we enjoyed our stay. Although we did have to ask 4 times to get the tv fixed, in the end they moved us to another room which was an upgrade but think this was because we had just got engaged otherwise they probably would of moved us to a room similar to the one we had already. The upgraded room was so much nicer. It had a huge king size bed which was fantastic, we had a great sleep and had a great view of the Empire State building. There was some noise (5th floor) from the street especially sirens from fire engines etc, but when we upgraded it wasn't as bad. (8th floor) It is very close to a train track to which was very loud but I only heard that once.
The conciege desk in the lobby of the hotel was a great help. We booked all our tours through them and got cheaper theatre tickets too which meant no queues at the TKTS booth.(Although it probably would nave been even cheaper to get them from TKTS).
The hotel does feel a bit far from the main action but then there's less noise. Takes about 10 minutes to walk into Times Square. 
The restaurant was great for food and reasonably priced. The staff aren't great but my fiance said it's the best salmon he's had. Breakfast was ok but not great, you have to pay extra for this. 
Overall a good stay and I would return to this hotel.

name: Hotel Riverside Studios
title: “Lo peor de lo peor”
text:
Ha sido el peor alojamiento que estado nunca. Sucio, mal olor, obras por todas partes, los baños asquerosos..... Me imagino que las fotos de las habitaciones y baños que hay en internet de este hotel existirán, pero la que me tocó a mí...... Nada más llegar a la habitación, me senté en la camá y el colchón se hundió totalmente. Nos dimos cuenta que el somier estaba dado la vuelta con las patas hacia arriba. Otra curiosidad, la habitación tenía una labavo el cual tenía un chicle pegado que no fuimoscapaces de despegar y nos acompañó toda la semana. 
el personal de la recepción antipáticos y parecía que les molestara que le preguntaras, etc..
Lo único a su favor, es la ubicación.

name: Hotel Riverside Studios
title: “Miteux... :(”
text:
Nous avons bénéficié du tarif avantageux de 78 euros par nuit... non-remboursable, chose à ne pas faire à moins d'être sûr du coup.
Sûr qu'il est bien placé, à 10 minutes à pied de Central Park, et la devanture a bel aspect, mais une fois les portes franchies, l'office laisse à désirer, une hotesse parlant français en quittant les lieux (c'est mieux que rien), chambre crasseuse et viellotte, lit sommaire, climatisation bruyante, télévision avec cinq chaînes, porte portant des traces d'effraction n'isolant aucunement des bruits du couloir (certains voisins jugeant certainement agréable de claquer les portes à chaque entrée/sortie), salle de bain commune avec wc pas très engageante et portant quelque coup de peinture pour cacher la misère.
Bref, à peine arrivés, nous avons cherché un autre hôtel, quitte à perdre notre reservation. Apparemment, un hôtel à moins de 80 euros correspond à un hôtel à moins de 20 euros en France, et encore, j'ai eu des chambres plutôt correctes à ce prix là.

name: Manhattan Broadway Hotel
title: “Perfekt beliggenhed, men...”
text: Hotellet lå super centralt og personalet var rigtig søde og hjælpsomme. Der lugtede lidt mærkeligt når man kom ind på hotellet og fra vores badeværelse turde vi ikke åbne vinduet, fordi der var SÅ klamt bag hotellet. Det kan slet ikke beskrives. Der var også meget larm på hotellet hele natten.. Ellers godt :-) og kan anbefales hvis man tager til NY for at opleve stedet og ikke sidde på hotellet :-)

name: Manhattan Broadway Hotel
title: “Horrible Experience”
text:
When looking for this hotel, make sure you are looking hard because it is very easy to miss! The lobby is not very welcoming and the entire place seems cramped. 
Now, first of all, this hotel says that it is for tourists and will work with them to make sure their stay is comfortable -- WRONG!! We made a reservation for a one-night stay and were told everything was fine. When we showed up at noon on Saturday we knew it was too early to get our room key, so we left our bags in a room and they checked us in and charged the credit card without giving us our key. We came back at 8pm to get our room key so we could freshen up and head out on the town. That is when the problems started!
We got our bags and asked for our key and the people at the front desk said they had no idea what we were talking about. They finally found our reservation again and said that there was a problem. Apparently it had rained on Friday morning and there was a leak in the roof and our room had water damage. So they said that they would refund our money so that we could go find some other place to stay. When asked why they didn't call us to let us know, or why we weren't told this at noon, all they came up with was "I don't know" and "the guy that was here at that time is new, so he probably didn't know either." This hotel has a 72 hour cancellation policy, yet they could not call their customers to let them know that they didn't have a room for them. They said that they probably did call, but when we told them that we did not have a message, they said that whoever noticed it probably forgot to call us to let us know.
When we told them that it was their responsibility to find us a place to stay, they said it wasn't their concern. they told us that they could refer us to some other hotels throughout the city that we could go and check to see if they had any vacancies! They actually wanted us to walk around the city at night with our luggage and look for a place to stay. Apparently the manager to this hotel is off on the weekends and does not answer his phone (BEWARE -- make sure not to have any "emergencies" on the weekend, because there is no manager). After having 5 of us saying that they had to do something, they found us a hotel for $300 more than we were going to pay there. Seriously, if we had $450 to spend in a room for one night, we wouldn't be staying at the "Manhattan Broadway" in the first place! 
Finally, when we told them to give us back our money, since that was what hey had been saying all along we had even more problems. Apparently the people that work at night don't have a "code" for refunds. So they expected us to trust them that they would refund us the money the next day when the person with the code came in. RIGHT!! When we asked for them to call that person to see if they could come help us, we were told that he didn't work on weekends either. Then, when we said to just give us the refund in cash they did not want to do that either. Finally, an assistant manager was reached and she was able to cancel the transaction from home.
We also had friends that stayed there the same weekend as us and they said they were glad to have taken their own sheets because the rooms look nothing like the pictures -- they are small, dark and dirty. This has got to be the absolute worst experience I have ever had at a hotel! Definitely BEWARE!!!

name: W New York
title: “Chic and comfortable”
text:
I was in NY for business and enjoyed a comfortable stay at the W. The hotel is chic and trendy with very lovely bar and lounge areas, and well-appointed (though small) rooms and beds. The linens were excellent -- I'm picky with that. Room service was also top-tier: prompt and courteous, and the food was delicious.
The service was generally excellent... They really go above and beyond to try to accommodate every request. In one case, the less professional night guy at the front desk fell short of the rest of the staff: waking me up at 5 am for something I had been assured would be no problem (I had left equipment with their Whenever/ Whatever office for a photographer to pick up... the front desk guy insisted it wasn't there and I had to come down at 5 am to argue that they most definitely did have it... Finally they found it). That was the single exception, though. Everyone else at the hotel - from their front desk, to their bell service, to their doormen, bar tenders and waiters - provided truly best-in-class service.
One final note... the cocktails are rather pricey at $15 and $17 per. But I forgave it when I tasted the incredible hummus & flat bread served in front of the fire in their lounge...
When in NY again, I look forward to returning to the W.

name: Envoy Club Suites
title: “a disappointment”
text:
the envoy club suites was recommended to us by friends . on arriving, it was a terrible disappointment!! our one bedroom self contained suite, was rather old. the carpet stained, windows dirty. bath plug broken.thankfully, however, to their credit, they fixed us a plug when requested on the second day. the springs in the sofa bed, stuck into my daughter's back, giving a very uncomfortable first night. the cleaning maid was very accommodating and put an extra comfort on top to improve things a little. the bathroom and kitchen, though old, was clean.
i had booked a few months early, and specially requested a rollaway to be added for when my 23 year old son arrived, and confirmed this several times with reservations., and also on arrival. to which, no-one ever said, they were subject to the day!! so, we found, that the night my son was to arrive, there was no rollaway available!!
i definitely would not recommend this hotel, unless you desperately need to be next door to the hospital. this part of town is not as pleasant as staying on the west side, especially upper west. true, you are not far from centre of town and the 15 bus is close by to catch to and from lower manhattan. however, if you are looking for somewhere with a nicer view and surroundings or pleasant area to walk, don't book here.

name: Skyline Hotel
title: “Qualité en baisse.”
text: Pour les équipements, il est dommage qu'internet ne soit pas gratuit. Il y a un Starbuck café pas loin qui vous permettra de vous connecter gratuitement. Pour l'emplacement, il est à la limite des quartiers un peu sales et chauds... mais c'est encore correct et time square accessible en 10 minutes à pieds. Pour la propreté c'est limite malgré le tip chaque jour. L'année dernière il était plus propre. Confort de la chambre côté rue très mal insonorisé. L'autre côté testé l'année dernière est correct. Personnel de l'hôtel assez aimable dans l'ensemble. Piscine à l'étage pas très propre ainsi que les pieds des surveillants qui sont assis en bout de bassin... ATTENTION le côté rue de l'hôtel est en rénovation totale. Le travaux commencent à 8 heures donc pas de grasses matinées...

name: Manhattan Broadway Hotel
title: “Manhattan Broadway Budget Hotel - meget Budget!!”
text:
Vi fik et værelse uden vinduer!! Jo, der var et vindue, men det var "blændet af" så man ikke kunne se ud.
Værelset var mere end nusset da vi overtog det, og særdeles skrabet. Jeg slog et insekt ihjel som jeg dårligt turde se nærmere på ... er dog ikke sikker på om det VAR en kakerlak.
Beliggenheden var fin nok, men standarden var simpelthen for ussel.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “sol65”
text: first impressions when checking in seemed fine until you got to the rooms corridors where bleak and filthy rooms where 3rd world standard putting it mildly the only conselation and saving grace is location wise times sqaure empire st building macys a stones through away and if you enjoy a drink and watching sport theres blarneys rock bar just oppisite also if you can pay cash do so as i was nearly spammed 4 paying 4 tickets to cats fortunality i hade left 3 days before it happened

name: Riverside Tower
title: “Very small ... but has everything you need”
text: A big group of us went to New York for new year's eve 2010. I found this hotel and booked everyone here because the price couldn't be beat. I had read that the rooms were small but that was New York, so what are you going to do. We booked two separate 'suites' for 8 of us. Each suite was made up of two rooms with trundle beds (bed with a roll out bed underneath) and a teeny bathroom between the rooms. It literally was all we needed as we were all there for fun and exploring. We didn't find it as dirty as some of the reviews would suggest, and no one could really complain, we all had a nice comfy enough bed to go back to (and quiet nights for sleeping), and the fridges were a plus - good for leftovers. The location is amazing, we walked to a lot of places (bars, restaurants, quick bites, central park, etc) but it was also convenient to the subway. If I were going back with my husband we would probably stay somewhere else, but we were with a big group of friends & totally did the trick.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “New York New York I can understand why they named it twice!”
text: Fantastic Hotel. Room is very basic but if its only a place to lay your head at the end of a long exciting day this is the place to stay.Very Clean Very Very helpful staff excellent location,beautiful building. Cannot recommend it enough. Will definatly stay again.

name: Skyline Hotel
title: “Buono a poco dal centro”
text:
Buon Hotel situato sulla 50th all' incrocio con lan 10^ av .Molto comodo per raggiungere TIMES SQUARE.Quattro blocchi come dicono loro(4 isolati) Con 15 minuti di passeggiata si raggiunge il cuore di Manhattan .Hotel non molto grande ma pulito con camere spaziose ,ottima prima colazione 
ed anche la cena. Personale molto cordiale ,sempre pronto a chiederti se tutto ok.L'unico neo per me è il ristorante con molti televisori che trasmettono partite di okey su ghiaccio ed incontri di Boxe ecc. con musica ad un livello adatta a persone di giovane età.
Rapporto qualità prezzo sicuramente più che buono dato che siamo a New York e ripeto in ottima posizione .La metro è a 2 isolati 300mt,ma i taxi sono abbastanza economici(quelli gialli).

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Roosevelt "grand renovation"”
text:
Actually it's not as pretty as the professional pictures:
1. unfriendly service
2. very poor "grand renovation"
3. room poor condition
4. standard rooms are very small
5. same days don´t clen the room
Only positive things that the hotel was located in a good location.
I was in this hotel 6 nights in February. I will not go back anymore.

name: BEST WESTERN Convention Center Hotel
title: “Loved it”
text:
Previous reviews are right - the room is small, but this is probably the best you could get from $80 per night...in Manhattan! i agree that their bathroom is clean and tasteful!
i had a great experience with the front desk. When my fiance an i arrived, it was about 10:30 a.m. i asked the front desk if we could store the luggage somewhere, and that we probably won't be able to make it back before 4 (the check-in time). You know what she did? She checked us in! 10:30 in the morning!! So we were able to refresh a bit and then start our city adventure!
Forgot to check her name, but she was a pregnant (i think so) African American lady.
Complimentary breakfast is cool. i stayed at one Best Western in upper Michigan, but don't remember if they had the same breakfast. At Best Western Convention Center Hotel, there was a toaster that we could warm up bagels and bread. All kinds of herbal tea, fresh apple juice, whole milk, different kinds of corn flakes and fruit loops, and muffins. Whenever something ran short, the hotel staff came back with more. 
It is indeed an iffy neighborhood. A few blocks from subway, but if you do not mind taking bus, the hotel is on 38th St between Amsterdam and Broadway. If you walk to Amsterdam, there is M11 going up Amsterdam; if you walk to Broadway, there is M42 going to Time Square, where you can transfer to a few of subway trains and buses. If you walk alone and are hesitant to, do not walk on 38th street. Instead, try get off the bus on 40th, and walk major blocks down (like Amsterdam).
If you come in New York by plane (either LGA or JFK), you will probably have to pay at least one bus fare ($2 or $4). Then try to get a Metro Card at a subway station ($7/per day, $21/per week), then you can tranfer unlimited buses and subway trains in NYC.
When we checked in, i did not specify we wanted a non-smoking room, so when we stepped on the eighth floor, we could smell some smoke. So if you want to stay there, make sure you specify you want a non-smoking room.
Overall i had a great experience with Best Western Convention Center Hotel. By the way, i got the deal from Priceline.

name: the Lexington
title: “Adequate hotel for the price”
text:
Stayed September for a business meeting. Location good but not exactly lively.
Very nice staff: very helpful and smiley.
Room was quite small (despite being upgraded, apparently). Room needed some updating and a bit of tlc. Bathroom quite old and dated and stank of mildew. It was very clean but I could not get rid of the smell (think the extractor fan in the bathroom wasn't working). Had to leave the window open for the first day until it got better. Would have changed it on the first day had it not been for the jet-lag etc. 
Okay lobby bar. There's a diner and a Starbucks attached. Diner had excellent breakfasts. Wifi was not free in rooms but was free in the lobby.
Overall, it was okay. Probably wouldn't stay here again unless I couldn't find anything else and was really stuck. In Europe, the Radisson is usually pretty plush. This was certainly not plush.

name: Envoy Club Suites
title: “Fabulous!”
text:
Thoroughly enjoyed my stay at the Envoy Club. Myself and my family booked a 2 bedroom suite for 7 nights at the end of September, and from other trip advisor reviews figured this place would be just what we required. How right we were!
We were given a corner suite with 2 good sized bedrooms and bathrooms, a well equipped kitchen, and a great living room area with a view down 1st Avenue. All furnishings were comfortable and good quality and we didn't want for anything. 
All staff were helpful and rooms cleaned every day.
Some comments have been made re the location of the Envoy Club. It's not in the midst of the hustle and bustle but it's a ten minute walk to the Empire State building or subway station, where the 6 train (@ every 2 minutes) takes you uptown to 5th Ave shopping and Central Park or downtown to Lower Manhattan. There's also many bars and restaurants in the immediate area.
With my 3 year old son in tow, this was an excellent place to call home for a week. When I return to New York I'll definitely stay here again. For about the same cost as a hotel room you get so much more. Book now! You won't be disappointed!

name: Envoy Club Suites
title: “Good apartment feel”
text:
Like the Sydney visitor, I was upgraded to a 'single' which really is like a decent one-bedroom apartment. Decoration and furnishing is a little on the drab side but everything was decent quality. That said, the living room tv (there was also one in the bedroom!) had poor reception and the cd player, though welcome, seemed to cause a lot of skips. The kitchen is good and well furnished with crockery, cutlery and glassware. Good bathroom too, not the world's most brilliant shower, but ok, and plenty of towels and a bathrobe.
Good size bedroom with big bed and adequate storage.
Distance from the subway is a little irritating but not terrible - it's only ten minutes walk.
Overall, for the money this was excellent value, but I don't know if I'd've been as pleased without the upgrade. If you like a hotel 'buzz' the Envoy will probbaly prove a little isolated, but if you prefer the apartment feel and like the self-catering aspect (and don't want to be in the heart of things geographically) you'll probably find it ideal.

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Buon albergo..centralissimo”
text:
Il punto di forza dell'albergo è la posizione, praticamente a 2 minuti da time square, ed il rapporto qualità prezzo...abbastanza vantaggioso. Le camere sono piccoline ma ben disposte ed arredate, il bagno è troppo piccolo ma per 2 persone che si adattano un pò si puo gestire, avevamo ben tre finestre in camera che davano su un cortile interno...ma comunque davano una buona luminosita alla stanza. L'aria condizionata è rumorosa !!
Il presonale è ok, disponibile alla reception e disponibile quello delle pulizie....ma la sua posizione è strepitosa...hai tutto a portata di mano ed a qualsiasi ora...e appena fuori l'albergo c'è il pub irlandese per la classica Guinnes notturna.

name: Astor on the Park
title: “what a dump”
text:
We had two double rooms or thats what it said on the paperwork.
One room was so small you had to climb over a bed to enter into the room and then climb back to visit the bathroom,the other was a better size but still small and the radiator leaked hot water obviously for a long time as the carpet was soaked to the middle of the room.The plumbing was so noisy in both rooms that it was impossible to sleep.We had views of the rubbish tip.After one night we demanded a room change ,which we got. The next rooms were slightly better, thank goodness we were only there for two nights.This is without doubt the worst hotel I have ever been in,in fact hotel is not the way I would describe this place, my pets are left in better accommodation. This is a dump do not stay here .This place ruined our stay in New York as we were so tired .

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Could Be So Much Better”
text:
When there was a problem with our original hotel reservation my sister booked us into the Hotel Pennsylvania at the last minute, and she didn’t first check Trip Advisor. 
Although the neighborhood seemed a bit dodgy, when we arrived at the beautiful hotel lobby I felt somewhat less concerned about her choice. Sadly me relief was short lived. 
After standing in a slow line we went to the available clerk and began the check-in process. My sister gave a credit card which the clerk said was declined, which was very odd. She gave them a second credit card and was told it was also declined, third card same thing. Finally she gave them her Credit/Debit card which was approved. More on this below.
We were given keys and headed for the elevators. There is a person stationed at the elevators who we were told would ask to see our key as a security measure, he never looked up or asked us any of the three times we went upstairs. 
When we arrived at our floor and stepped off the elevator we looked at each other and rolled our eyes. The long hallway was quite dark, but not dark enough to hide the filthy carpet or the holes and patches on the walls. Our assigned room was at the very end of the hallway and in a small recessed alcove. It appeared the door to our room had been damaged and patched, but not repainted.
The room had the faint smell of mildew. When I tried to open a drawer the handle and drawer front came off in my hand. The bathroom had several more unpainted patches. There was a small refrigerator in the room which was turned off, when my sister opened it there was mold. We were being charged $500 a night for this room!
We both reached for our phones and started looking for another hotel. After checking on Trip Advisor my sister called Park Central Hotel, they didn’t have a room for that night, but did have a room the next day and for the rest of out stay.
During the night paint from the ceiling molding fell on to my sister’s pillow. We checked out first thing in the morning and when we checked-in at Park Central there was no problem with the credit card going through. Later that day she discovered that Hotel Pennsylvania had not only charged our entire planned stay on her card, but had also placed an additional $1500 hold on her account. It took them five days to reverse the charges.
To their credit, Hotel Pennsylvania did adjust the rate from $500 to $250 for the night we stayed.
Hotel Pennsylvania could be a first-rate hotel. It’s a Historical Building with good size rooms and high ceilings with crown molding. I hope when the economy improves the owners will restore it to it’s former glory. 
I gave them three stars as encouragement.

name: Park 79 Hotel
title: “OTTIMO HOTEL SITUATO IN UPPER...”
text: OTTIMO HOTEL SITUATO IN UPPER WEST SIDE IN ZONA TRANQUILLA E MOLTO GRADEVOLE CON DUE FERMATE METRO NELLE VICINANZE. CAMERA PICCOLA MA MOLTO PULITA COSI' COME IL BAGNO. PERSONALE GENTILE E DISPONIBILE. HOTEL SICURAMENTE DA CONSIGLIARE.

name: Flatotel
title: “Start spreading the news!”
text:
This hotel room was a little dark; could have done with a few more lights!
Apart from that it was great...comfortable, clean, great location, trendy/nicely decorated, good toiletries (Molton Brown)
What more can I say?

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Location excellent but anything else HORRIBLE!”
text: The only thing great abt this hotel is the location, besides that I didnt know how I endured the dirty rooms, daunting corridor, rats n roaches n mouldy stale smell.Please do not ever stay in this hotel!!

name: W New York
title: “Hip Style, Great Music, Prescient Service”
text:
This trip centered around the Thanksgiving Day parade and also included Cirque du Soleil's Wintuk at the Madison Square Garden and American Idiot at the St. Jimmy on Broadway. The W's location was close to all the attractions we came for, while being nicely tucked away in a less frenetic locale. 
From the moment that we arrived to the moment we left, the service was prescient. We arrived by car, and though things were busy, we were immediately greeted by one of the bellhops (Nam?) who with a smile orchestrated a spot for us curbside by helping a cab that was trying to leave. He asked us about our trip as he loaded our luggage onto the cart and came with us into the hotel. Our car was whisked away to the W's parking facilities. 
We arrived around 10:30am, wanting to enjoy the city to the fullest. Being Starwood Preferred Guest Gold members, we were treated to a huge upgrade from our Cozy Room to a Marvelous Suite. When we first arrived, Mario advised us that a suite would be available at 3pm, should we wish to upgrade. For us, this presented no difficulty, since we had much to do around town. A bellhop stored our luggage for us and we were on our way to take a bite out of the Big Apple. 
Upon our return around 3pm, Cindy C. pleasantly and deftly handled our check-in. Our suite was not quite ready, so to ease the wait she treated us to a handful of vouchers for Oasis, the lounge bar serving the Living Room. Lounging on a comfy sofa in the Living Room after walking around town felt great. Alana took our drink orders sofa-side, returning to mix our complimentary drinks before our eyes with studied skill. A fruit and cheese plate meshed nicely with our drinks. Whenever we needed something Alana was there - a recurring theme for every visit to Oasis. Next, we stepped over to Cindy at the front desk, where we found she had upgraded us to a Marvelous Suite with private terrace since the other suite was still unavailable. 
The room lived up to its name. Spacious, and modernly styled, full of light, and sporting panoramic views of the city, the room felt like a home away from home. Even the standard amenities had visual appeal, from an interesting swiveling dual level glass-topped desk with Brazo LED work light, to a whimsical fuchsia cutout light fixture in the living room, to the wobbly chess set. The bathroom sported a separate shower and bath, as well as neat textured wallpaper rising from a handsome slate tile floor. One of my favorite W perks is the iPod dock and radio combo next to the bed. No need to worry about charging adapters or audio cables: I just plop in my iPhone and the room fills with my music, making the room truly mine. Everywhere in the hotel, there are trays of green granny smith apples available for consumption - in our room they added a splash of color to the glass dining table in the living room. Healthy and visually striking - awesome. Surrounding three sides of our suite, our terrace offered an open sort of privacy with great views and plenty of seating areas - definitely a space that begs for an after-party. The living room was also quite spacious and offered plenty of seating options, from sofas and ottomans to dining table chairs to the work chair by the desk. 
As we settled in, Cindy called to ask how we liked the suite - to which our reply was, “marvelous - thanks!”
We also spent some time in the Living Room at different times during our stay. There was always a refreshing playlist on at a comfortable volume, conspiring with the comfortable, eclectic mix of sofas and chairs, Oasis, and other guests to make the Living Room a pleasant time warp. There were one or two non-waiting staff members who kept watch over the Living Room guests to make sure absolutely nothing fell through the cracks. Everywhere there was something of interest to look at. There were art installations hanging from the ceiling. Abstract images and videos were projected onto some of the walls. Columns were draped in loosely pleated fabric and lit from inside, yielding a modern neoclassical look. The bathrooms on the second floor were also quite a visual treat, wrapped in stone. Vibrant green wheatgrass in stone-gray planters throughout the hotel look quite striking, while keeping the air fresh. The Living Room looks out onto 49th street through a kaleidoscope of randomly-shaped stained glass sections and clear sections, giving guests inside privacy while still offering a voyeuristic view of the street. While at Oasis, do try the sexy fries - they are drizzled with truffle oil and sprinkled with parmesan cheese. The pizza looked good too, but I didn’t get a chance to try it. The coffee martini was tasty, as were the kobe sliders. 
One morning, while having breakfast in the Living Room, I forgot my sunglasses on a table. By the time I remembered, we were already at the Thanksgiving Day Parade. I called the W to let them know what had happened. When we got back, I went to the concierge desk to fetch my sunglasses; the concierge told me to speak with the W security team member a few steps behind me near the reception desk. As I walked towards him, he held out my sunglasses to me. I was surprised and delighted. That was fast! It also gave me a great sense of security. Losing my sunglasses could have tainted my holiday - instead, I felt taken care of, safe. After that, I began to take notice of and appreciate the security personnel. At night, in addition to the usual requirement of an active keycard to use the lifts, security in the lobby makes sure only guests and their guests have access to the non-public areas of the hotel. There is also security posted around the Living Room and everywhere in the lobby. They scope out who brings what. A security team member discreetly looked at my laptop bag and SLR bag when I took them into the Living Room one night; I’m fairly certain no one but me would have been able to leave with that gear. I love that. That level of safety left me very relaxed and happy. I don’t think I’m alone, either. Observe the sea of Macbook Pros in the Living Room on any given weekday afternoon. 
Our stay was excellent. We loved the modern style and great service, and we felt right at home, thanks to the friendly staff. Every time we left or arrived, Cindy or another staff member would greet us. We are already planning our next stay at the W New York, sometime in mid-January. It will be nice to see familiar faces.

name: Park Savoy
title: “Always as expected!”
text: Yes, the rooms can be small, though we had a two double bed room, (roomier than the single bedrooms), with a nice size bathroom, a full walkin closet & a small fridge! Always very clean, and the location is the best! And continental breakkfast is included every day, plus a one time complimentary drink, at the Italian restaurant next door(which by the way had great food, reasonably priced too). We were half a block from where we watched the Macy's Thanksgiving Parade, which was the reason for our visit this year. We always stay here because of the reliable, clean, & convenient location this hotel has to offer.

name: Park Savoy
title: “You get what you pay for”
text: I have a couple complaints first the BED! one of the most uncomfortable hotel beds I have ever slept in. Lets just say I spent 3 days in NYC and got no sleep. After spending the day/night out all you wanna do is get some good sleep so you can be rested to do it all over again, not the case with this place. My 2nd complaint, having guests... I go out there to spend time with friends, would be nice if 1 was allowed to come up hang out before heading out for awhile but no, I think if the guest thing is an issue then the front desk should have a sign in sheet so they know no extra people are sleeping there. It makes sense for the people traveling from another state just to see people there. Overall its convenient to Central Park and Times SQ. I liked the fact that I could walk to and from Times Sq without taking the subway. Will I stay there again? Maybe in the future, and pay for 2 double beds just so i can have a guest!

name: Days Inn Hotel New York City - Broadway
title: “Overpriced , but clean..”
text:
We stayed here for a week in November.
Get room 1230, view to the Broadway..
Room clean, bathroom very nice but we didnt had hot water so they have to fix it , which they did immediately.
No breakfast, and you have to pay for internet and printing which should be included if they charge so much per night.
Also when we payed to use the pc and try to print out they just tell us sorry but the internet doesnt work at the moment.
We had a package delivered to the hotel a day later we left and asked to please send it to our address, they send it back instead of send it to me.
Overal nice room , unfriendly stuff, ok location, overpriced.

name: Windsor Hotel
title: “Excellent for budget travellers, can't fault the hotel!!!”
text:
Three of us (Early 20's) were over at end September for 6 nights, we had a very enjoyable stay at the Hotel, no bed bugs or anything like that, room was very clean, serviced every day, lots of toiletries in bathroom (toothpaste, soap and shower gel)
The beds were comfy enough and the shower was excellent, plus our room had a view of the Empire State Building (Think you will need to get a room on the corner, number *02 dependant on what floor you're on (We had 2 double beds)
Anybody saying that the room was too small is talking nonsense. Three of us were in one room and there was more than enough room for us.
If I come back to NY, I will definitely consider to staying here, as will my friends. The staff were very courteous and polite and there are 2 subways stations within the area (Grand St is 1 minute walk, yes, 1 minute! and Bowery is 2-3 minutes.
Fantastic budget hotel that gets all the basics right.

name: Days Inn Hotel New York City - Broadway
title: “WOW”
text:
I was wowed by the super efficient, friendly reception at the the front desk when I checked in early evening, November 18. I forget her name (Alaysa?) but not her keen attention to my requests. Wonderful customer service!
My room was recently renovated, clean, good use of space and color, clean with lovely presentation of amenities. Housekeeping had obviously been well trained - Clean, Clean Clean. Room size was typical NYC cozy.
Hotel location was great! Only 2 blocks from 96 st. subway *accessible subway stop*. Good area of the city. Bakery/Pizza place on corner good for breakfast/late night snack. Indian restaurant midway up the block had tasty food with good service. Nail salon 2 blocks from hotel had mani/pedi for only 20 dollars,
It almost seems as if Anthony Melchiorri from Hotel Impossible had visited this hotel and worked his magic for I have no complaints. Definitely look forward to returning to this hotel.

name: Windsor Hotel
title: “basic, clean no bed bugs or other critters”
text: Stayed here 3 nights, the first night I had a really hard bed and would have done better sleeping on the floor. The night shift clerk "starting at midnight" is a real jerk and does not help or know anything. had message light on the phone and he said there are no messages "written" for you. asked how I listen to my phone messages and all he could say is call back in the morning to talk to the manager. The room is very clean, it does not have a fridge as stated by write up and are very small. The price is right for $70.00 per night but I would not pay any more for it. It is in china town which is very run down, I never had any problems walking around even late at night when returning at 2am. There is a corner store across the street which is open til 12am and the hotel is close by to little italy and is in china town. It is right on the Grand street subway D line with access to anywhere you want to go. There is an excellent cafe about 3 blocks away called the cup and saucer which has 2 greek cooks. It is a small place with limited seating but the food and prices are awesome. You can easily get filled up for breakfast for about 7.00 here including your coffee "remember I said greek so it is thick and strong coffee". Over on allen st there is an excellent bar that has live country/folk music nightly with each band playing for about 1 hr sets. Over all for my first time to NY it was a clean, safe and comfortable room with really good front desk staff in the morning and afternoon who are quite knowledgeable and helpful with directions.

name: Windsor Hotel
title: “Basic, clean – and easy to get away from!”
text:
We stayed 4 nights at this hotel first week of December. 
I don’t have anything to complain about. Rooms was clean, free wifi, very quit a night and the best thing – only 1 min walk from Grand Street Subway that has excellent connection both up- and down town. 
However didn’t expect the hotel to e in the middle of China town and if I ever come to NY again I will look for a hotel where I get more value for money.

name: Days Inn Hotel New York City - Broadway
title: “No cell reception or Internet in rooms”
text:
We paid $249 a night for 2 beds, 2 adults&1child. Subway location great! Shower great! Bed super comfy! Look beyond that, my daughter lost a part to a toy so I was under the bed and dresser FILTHY!!!
Manhattan Diner just down the street amazing food And service!
Room very outdated, a/c worked ! 
One ice machine on 11 th floor . 
A little pricy for me, especially since we just needed it to sleep and shower. Neighbor hood very safe feeling , staff very friendly , bed comfy and very refreshing shower! My cellphone did not work in the room and no wifi in the room , ok in lobby, hotels computers you pay to use.

name: Eurostars Wall Street
title: “Don't cash travelers checks”
text:
The level of customer service is sub standard. There seems to be the arrogance of the European waiter here. I have cashed Amex travelers checks throughout he world. Not here! Why, we do not have the software!!!!!! Fortunately this is the banking district and a bank is nearby.
If you want convenience to meetings this works but it is overpriced and is not customer centric.

name: Windsor Hotel
title: “AVOID AT ALL COST”
text: Terrible location, in the Chinatown. Not a very safe area. Expedia had it listed as in SoHo (they have since corrected). The bedroom was small, smelly, had a TV that was at least 20 yrs old. The water in the shower was intermediate at best with no pressure. Towels were not provided in the room. We had to go down to the desk to get some. We will never go back!

name: Park Central
title: “Location is not everything”
text: Noisy. No individual control of room temperature. No bathmats. $55.00 per day to park the car. Extremely slow elevator service. The staff was nice and the hotel was convenient but not worth the money.

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “Potentially a good budget hotel if they had bothered to renovate with any sort of care”
text:
Positives: 
Close to Times Square/Subway
Cheaper end of NYC
Negatives: 
Shabby attempt at renovation (I'd hate to think what state it was in originally) 
Pokey barely livable rooms - we were in a two double room and literally had to step over each other and that was with just 3! 
Mould and hair all over the bathroom
Dingy lighting in the rooms and the hallways 
Lifts - if you are willing to waste half your day waiting to go up in the lift or brave 19 flights. 
Poor AC/Heating system with a mind of its own. 
It seems with the Milford that instead of taking the time and effort to create a well needed value option in the heart of Times Square they have decided to cut corners and costs to charge as little as possible in the hopes that the price will draw people in.

name: Park Central
title: “Great room”
text: This hotel served my purpose. Needed this area, and the location at 7th and 55th can't be beat. Close to shops, food, and subway. I was with another couple so room became reasonably priced when we split the cost. We were able to get a great room with a fantastic view thanks to Jessica. They only have a gym, no spa or extra perks.

name: Best Western PLUS President Hotel at Times Square
title: “Perfect location, quiet, reasonable price but attention to detail lacking”
text: I stayed at this hotel for a couple of nights in June and it really is the most fantastic location, particularly if you want to go to shows as it is so close to Times Square. Despite the fact that I booked a Deluxe room so that I could have more space and a bit more luxury, the room was a little cramped and while the bathroom was clean, the room itself was a bit tired and needed a more thorough clean. The staff on the front desk were inconsistent, some were helpful but for the most part seemed a little disinterested. NYC is a very expensive place to stay and while I didn't think hotel was great, it was reasonably priced. I didn't eat at the hotel at all so can't comment on the meals. The thing that was a real annoyance for me was the WiFi connection which was incredibly unreliable and despite the hotel advertising that there is free WiFI in all rooms, I was not able to connect and maintain the connection while in my room. Standing on one leg in a particular part of the lobby while whistling Dixie produced results sometimes but take a deep breath and you'd lose the connection, it was extremely annoying since having free WiFi was one of the reasons I'd chosen the hotel. Despite the very central location of the hotel, it was very quiet which was good.

name: Windsor Hotel
title: “Super hotel til prisen”
text: Billigt hotel midt i mellem Soho, Chinatown og Lower East Side med kun 2 minutter til metro B, D og F, der kører til næsten alle centrale stationer. Kvarteret bag hotellet omkring Ludlow Street er pakket med hyggelige restauranter og barer. Værelserne er rene og pæne og hotellets service er god, men svinger lidt alt efter hvem, der sidder i receptionen. Der var meget stille på hotellet, ingen billarm eller støj fra de andre værelser. Perfekt budgethotel.

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Lovely boutique hotel in fantastic location!”
text:
On looking for a hotel to stay at in NYC, our main concern at first was location and secondly comfort and value for money. We stayed over thanks giving weekend so were aware finding a decent value hotel in a good location might be tricky but then we happened about the Paramount Hotel. It is just round the corner from Times Square - no more than a 30 second walk out of the hotel and you can see the bright lights from the windows so we couldn't have asked for better. From Times Square you can get to everything you would want to within walking distance and nothing really takes more than half an hour apart from The Statue of Liberty, Ground Zero etc which we caught a subway to but walked back from. 
The hotel itself from the pictures looked just as lovely in real life. I was a little apprehensive before I went about room size as this seemed to be something a lot of people commented on but it was perfect! The bed was absolutely huge (we had a standard kingsize room) and the space around the bed vast and more than enough room for all our many purchases! The bathroom was small but adequate and perfectly equipped with a showe/bath, wash basin, toilet and lots of towels (something a lot of hotels cannot seem to get right). A flat screen tv with many channels adorned the wall and the decor was simple, clean yet modern and warm. 
We used concierge once to ask about posting mail to the UK and they were most helpful. They seemed to know a lot about shows and the local area! The lobby was striking and one of the more unusual ones I have seen. It was quirky and eclectic in its decor so probably not to everyones taste but I liked it and enjoyed eating breakfast one morning on the mezzanine floor over looking the lobby. Breakfast was nice (we opted for the buffet) albeit a little expensive for what we actually ate. Unfortunately we never made it to the bar but it looked great. 
The only bad experience we had was with the elevators - one broke on the second day and was never replaced and out of the remaining three, another broke leaving two on the last day which, when we were trying to get our luggage down, made it very difficult as every elevator that arrived was full of people! Oh and the fact we had to pay to leave our luggage once we had checked out I think was a little cheeky as we would have left the money as a tip anyway!
Overall a lovely hotel and would definately go back there if and when we make it back to NYC!

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Buen Hotel”
text:
Muy buen hotel, es sencillo, de lso mas baratos y muy cnetrico, esta en pleno times square! sinceramente una de las mejores opciones para alojarse en Nueva York, Claro que si es lujo lo que buscan este NO es su hotel, no es gran cosa en cuanto a decoración, pero tiene lo basico y fundamental: LIMPIO; PERSONAL MUY AMABLE!, CENTRICO.
Cuando vuelva a Nueva York: VOLVERE AL ST JAMES!
En cuanto a la calidad del sueño... en nueva york si quieres dormir sin tapones y antifaz, busquense un hotel en uno de lso otros barrios (queens, staten island) porque no encontraran un hotel apto para el sueño, aunque los ultimos dias depues de patear toda al ciudad ni sentiran el trafico ni les molestaran las luces. 
ANIMO Y A VISITAR NUEVA YORK! la ciudad perfecta para algunos^^

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Poor service in great location...”
text: Arrived at 5pm after long flight to be told only room left was not ready as it smelt of smoke. Being non smokers we were told of we waited two hours the room could be ironised and we could check in. Having booked the room 9 months earlier this was fustrating. We came back at 7pm and were given the room only to find when we opened the door two guests were already in it! Reception had made a mistake and magically another room was now free for us to use. I complained about this and we were given free breakfast vouchers for the delay and mix up which we were then charged for when we checked out! Not happy at all. Hotel in central location and fab for exploring! Rooms very small but clean and modern. No tea or coffee on rooms and signal on tv bad. Despite good location would not use again because of rubbish service, lack of communication and ownership.

name: Jolly Hotel Madison Towers
title: “Reasonable hotel, great location”
text: We booked on a deal so no great expectations, but our room was clean and more than adequate. The location is super because you are in easy reach of everything midtown - and Grand Central subway links. Staff were fine but breakfast very expensive when you can eat very well in several diners within a block's walk.

name: BEST WESTERN Convention Center Hotel
title: “Zentral und sauber”
text: Das Hotel liegt sehr zentral, nur ein paar Blocks vom Times Square und Macy's. Das Zimmer war sehr sauber und das Hotelpersonal war immer hilfsbereit. Wir hatten allerdings ein Zimmer zur 38th Street raus und genau gegenüber ist eine Taxiwerkstatt, die 24 Std. geöffnet hat; weiterhin läuft eine Bahnlinie direkt am Hotel vorbei. Aber beides hat uns nicht um den Schlaf gebracht, weil wir abends immer k.o. vom Sightseeing und shoppen waren.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Basic but convenient and clean”
text: Came into Penn station from Boston and were searching for a hotel overnight to catch an AM train to Montreal. The property is old, built at the beginning of the last century, but clean and the restaurant/steakhouse was great. Double bed- which wouldn't suit everyone - but we were fine. Good value for a very low price!

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “Good Value - Great Location”
text:
As a first time vistor to NYC I was not sure what to expect after finding this hotel at $150 per night - which seemed a great deal compared to most other Manhattan hotels I researched. I was there for a 5 night stay with my wife and 2 young kids. On arrival staff were friendly and we were pleased with the room which was spacious enough and clean. 
As other reviews have highlighted, the decor is faded and a little tired, but at this price in Manhattan I would have no hesitation in recommending this hotel as long as you're not looking for luxury - and if you are then pay the (significant) extra $$$'s so you won't be disappointed. On reading some reviews it seems to me that some are expecting more than what they paid for - it's a Holiday Inn at a discount price after all. In our experience, even with young kids, you'll be out exploring NYC most of your time and the hotel is for crashing in at the end of a tiring day.
We did not use the restaurant at all during our stay, so I cannot comment on the service or the food. There are too many options for eating out in this city so staying in a hotel to eat did not appeal to us. 
The location has to be the best thing about staying in this hotel, we loved the fact that we could walk to Columbus Circle subway station in a few minutes and hop on to get anywhere in the city. Central Park is also within a short walking distance, and the Times Square and Theatre District is only a 10-15 min walk away. There are also restaurants, pubs and diners nearby when you want to stay close. The neighbourhood is pleasant and safe and not too noisy. We were out with the kids after dark many times and did not feel at all threatened here.
To sum things up, this is a good value hotel situated in a great location for tourists. If I ever come back to NYC, I would definately book this hotel again. Just don't expect luxury for this price in Manhattan.

name: Flatotel
title: “Flatotel in New York - close to Times Square”
text:
Very central hotel in New York - close to shopping, restaurant (Restaurant Row with good dinning possibilities) and Times Square.
The hotel is a little worn, included breakfast is non existing, the service is okay but everything is compensated by good location.
New York - a fantastic experience

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Very elegant- great price”
text: We loved this hotel. After looking over the options on trip advisor we decided on the Roosevelt for the price and the location. The rooms were more than adequate, the location was spot on. We walked a ton and took the subway (got lost for one hour) but we were close to Time Square. DO NOT stay in a hotel at Time Square, it is very bright and you will be sorry - so busy. We purchased show tickets when we got there at Time Square but if there is something you must see I advise you purchase them ahead of time, well before your departure date. New York was fabulous and we plan to go back very soon. Very safe, cop on every corner. Not that they need it, people are very helpful and with common sense you will have an amazing trip.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Cant wait to Return”
text:
What can I say about the Roosevelt?
Great hotel, Great location 5 minutes walk one way to Grand Central And 5th Avenue, the other way 5 minutes walk to Times Square.
Ok so you pay a premium to stay in a great location but everything about trhis hotel was Great.
Unbelievable Bar Staff, the 2 Tony's were just Priceless, thats the reception bar then there is a roof bar which is great too.
The hotel is pretty plush, the breakfast was excellent, rooms were spacious although a bit Tired in places but that could account for the traffic as I am sure the hotel enjoys full occupancy 7 days a week.
All in all Great Hotel and Great location, would recommend to any traveller going to New York

name: Marrakech Hotel on Broadway
title: “Perfect perfect perfect !. Just what we were looking for”
text: This hotel was just what we were looking for. It was our first trip to New York on a low bugget and I spent over a week picking out the perfect hotel on the perfect location so we could have a good time. It was a short trip of three days and two nights in New York, so we wanted to enjoy it as much as we can and I have to say this hotels, the staff, the servies, the door men, the front desk and the concierge are just giving everything to the their guest and visitors. You guys ROCK . I have been working in the hotel industry all my life and I was so surprise to find a place like this. We had a GREAT TIME, the room was small but perfect, nice big windows, our room was just beside the staircase and I thought it will be noise at night, but it was pefect, I sleap better than in my house. We are coming back to New York in summer and we will stay there again for sure. The subway is just at the doors steps, it is easy to find nice littler restaurants all around, one block, two blocks and three blocks away from the hotel, all very nice, sabrosos and unspensive, again for our surprise.

name: Flatotel
title: “Un hotel pràctico”
text:
Aparthotel ubicado cerca de Times Square, perfecto para visitar el centro andando.
Las habitaciones disponen de cocina completa.
No és hotel de lujo, pero tiene todo lo necesario. Lo unico que me molestó un poco és la moqueta en la habitación, ya que da un poco de "asquito" caminar encima puesto que no està del todo limpia...
Por lo demàs todo muy bien, ademàs el hotel tiene un bar-restaurante que està muy bien, és caríssimo, pero ideal para tomar una copa.

name: Best Western PLUS President Hotel at Times Square
title: “THANK YOU SUNY!”
text: We traveled from Cincinnati Ohio to New Jersey, and stayed overnight in New Jersey about an hour away from New York City. We then headed out the next day to New York City. The traffic was overwhelming, then we went through the Lincoln Tunnel which was long and traffic stopped many times. It almost felt as though we were being herded towards something. Being from a smaller city, we really did not have an idea how overwhelming the drive into New York City would be, and by the time we arrived to the hotel, we were completely overwhelmed. Then I met Suny...she reminded me how ungrateful I was being, she gave me hope..she comforted me. By the time I got to the hotel I couldn't even remember how I had booked the room, I couldn't find the reservation number.. I was in every way overwhelmed. I went to the restroom and just sat to get myself together. Suny was amazing. She was so kind to me. Just kind to me. She recognized I was overwhelmed. By the way Suny is bilingual so she was helping both Spanish speaking guests and myself. Suny did this with ease. Suny transitioned from spanish speaking guests to myself with ease. Suny gave me hope. She recognized I was overwhelmed. She gave us a room when others had to wait. She told me the hotel was sold out, and gave me the peace and time to find my reservation number. New York City kicked my tail. I have traveled to Europe and traveled from Rome to Milan by train with no tourguide and with my 13 yr old son in tow. I had an easier time in Italy where noone spoke my language than I did in New York City. People like Suny make everything better. Thank you Suny!

name: Park Central
title: “Excellent hotel management”
text:
We recently visited NYC and were booked at another hotel. That hotel was over-booked so they moved us to the Park Central. The front desk manager-Elizabeth- was so nice to us and helped us out. It was a FANTASTIC weekend! 
They also have an airport shuttle for a flat $50- which was nice because cabs were tough to catch!

name: Park Central
title: “If you can make here, you can make it anywhere!”
text: Ok, the title is kind of harsh but I had high expectations for this hotel. My visit was July 12 - 15, it was a Girls Getaway. Let me get right to it. The Front Desk girl was rude and argumentative. I got her name but have forgotten it. She was obnoxious and has no idea about the relationship between the hotel and the Customer. She doesn't get it. Next, the hotel was a mess! Wait, that's not fair. The lobby looked great but once we got to our floor, it was a mess. I chose the hotel for the group, so perhaps I was more sensitive, however, there were cleaning carts, dirty towels and sheets in the hallway 24 hours a day. I thought there was a Hotel Workers strike going on! Maybe there was. It was an absolute mess. BUT, the location is perfect! You will be a short walk from Whole Foods, Central Park, Times Square, the Apple store, et. al, Carnegie Hall is across the street and subway stations are a short walk away. We loved the location! You can actually consider this hotel AVERAGE but the mess and the hallways and the mess at the Front Desk made it a bad experience for me. I will not return. Oh! We wanted to get a drinks but the lobby bar was always closed.

name: Park Central
title: “Good location with excelent service”
text:
Great location with excellent service just a few steps away from times square
As we stay a lot in hotels, we have been surprised by the excellent service in this hotel
Especially Elizabeth from the front desk is taking care of every single customer request
Nice lobby, nice bar, professional and friendly staff
All amenities are provided in the spaceful rooms
For sure wecwill stay there again

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Empfehlenswert”
text: sehr nettes, familiaeres Hotel fast direkt am Times Square. Zimmer nicht uebermaessig gross, aber sauber und stilvoll eingerichtet. Bus / U-Bahnnaehe und viele Delis in unmittelbarer Umgebung. Wuerden direkt wieder buchen. Sehr empfehlenswert.

name: Hotel Alexander
title: “Good Hotel for a Budget traveller”
text: We stayed there for 4 nights. Hotel was clean and nice. We had a shared bedroom and it was most of the time spotlessly clean. All I have to complain is that the room doors and walls are quite thin, so you hear almost everything. If it´s cold weather you´d better know that there was only linen on bed not blancket.

name: Skyline Hotel
title: “Brutto fuori, bello dentro”
text:
Era l'hotel meno costoso disponibile in occasione della maratona, da fuori si presenta in maniera abbastanza anonima, ma le camere sono spaziose, pulite e confortevoli.
Si trova all'incrocio tra la 10 avenue e la 49 street, Times Square è raggiungibile in 10 minuti di cammino.

name: Jolly Hotel Madison Towers
title: “Great location but not worth the price and would not stay there again”
text:
Really good location but that's probably the only positive. Rooms small, which wasn't too much of a problem but not worth the price paid. We had TV problems and had to call the front desk 3 times before they sent an engineer. Then the shower made a terrible knocking noise (pipes) so we had to move rooms (as they had to turn off the water supply to that floor to fix the problem). We went to a nicer and bigger room but once packed up had to wait at least 40 mins to move when they told us it would be 5 mins and that the porter would help with bags etc. We had to call the front desk and were told a couple of times that the porter had gone to the wrong room!
Biggest complaint was that under the facilities this hotel offered a sauna and steam room, which was a big factor in us choosing this hotel, but on arrival found out that you had to have a $90 massage to get a sauna! We offered to pay just to have a sauna but they said no - talking about cutting your nose off to spite your face! When we challened reception they said the Spa wasn't connected to the hotel, but after asking why was the facilities advertised as part of the hotel the duty manager laughed in my husbands face! We couldn't believe it! We've been to the states a lot and never experienced such service. We found the front desk staff very rude, whereas the other staff expecially the porters were fantastic, they really went our of their way to help us- the Italians on the front desk were not nice. 
We visit New York every year but there's no way we'd stay there again!

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Don't believe the horror stories”
text:
So it's a little old, a little shabby and pretty strange.... you'll see what I mean when you get there, but overall it was excellent! We went in winter and it was warm, and really spacious (we had a family room). The heater looked old and grubby but worked fine and warmed the room up really quickly. The shower was hot and really powerful (maybe too powerful!), and the beds were comfy. The bed linen, bathroom and towels were clean and room service were great.
The carpet was pretty worn, the skirting boards chipped and a little shabby, but for the money, in central NY, it was PERFECT! If you want luxury, then I guess you'll have to pay for it. This place is excellent on a budget, generally clean and in a great location. 
The only real downside for us was no wifi in the hotel - rooms have an ethernet cable, which was useless for our kindles, iphones, ipods and notebook laptop. But hey - there's a Starbucks on every corner with free wifi, so we got over it.

name: Jolly Hotel Madison Towers
title: “Amazing Location!!!!”
text: JOLLY HOTEL, Great staff very helpfull! Standard room Very small so we upgraded and the room was very nice and lots space! Bathroom was extremly nice... Location was fantastic in the heart of new york right around the corner from empire state building! I stayed over new year and i must say the whole experience was AMAZING!! Thankyou Jolly Hotel... only slight niggle getting a taxi from the hotel was way too expensive to the airport to avoid like the plague!!!!

name: Skyline Hotel
title: “Hotel Skyline New York”
text:
Hotel in buona posizione: a 5 minuti a piedi dalla metro e 10 da Time Square e Rockfeller Centre.
Camere comode e spaziose, bagni recentemente rinnovati (noi avevamo una exclusive con one queen bed).
Personale cordiale e disponobile, insomma un hotel da consigliare

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Super Lage, freudliches Personal”
text: Dieses Hotel ist sehr zu empfehlen. Es hat eine tolle Lage, das Personal ist sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit, wussten bereits am zweiten Tag welche Zimmernummer wir hatten. Die meisten Sehenswürdigkeiten sind schnell erreicht und die U-Bahn Station ist auch in unmittelbarere Nähe.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Cheap cheap hotel - you get what you pay for, but you're asleep most of the time”
text:
My wife and I were in NYC for one night to visit our son, so we wanted a cheap hotel in a midtown location. Hotel Pennsylvania was the cheapest available, and was priced below many hotels in less popular destinations, so it was a real bargain at $130. And the location is one of the best in NYC.
This grand old lady has a huge old fashioned lobby with the largest reception desk I have ever seen. Despite the large crowd and long line at check in, we were processed promptly and professionally. Unfortunately, that was the highlight of our stay.
The room was tiny (although comparable to other budget tourist hotels in NYC) and the king sized bed took up most of the floor space. The walls and carpet were not clean. Electrical outlets were old and worn out, and some wires were exposed. The bathroom was out of date, very small (could only fit one person at a time), and had mold on the walls. Climate control was not effective - on this cold rainy late autumn day we had to open our windows to moderate the heat. Because of the room temperature, we had to keep the window open a crack at night, which enabled us to hear street noise. Unfortunately, we did not sleep well.
The continental breakfast included in our room charge was served in a very small over-crowded room with too many people to be comfortable. We skipped it and went out to eat.
I have stayed at much worse hotels in small towns along the highway as I have travelled around the country. This hotel is very cheap relative to the NYC market. If you are not coming for a romantic vacation and can forgive the substandard room and amenities, this is a bargain and worth it for the location.

name: Hotel Carter
title: “What others said about this hotel is true.”
text: A $5,000-per-room renovation is not enough for this hotel. The walls and doors were all just painted over, even the wires were painted into the wall. The king size bed is in the way of everything, that you don't have space to move around the room. You don't know whether the toilet's clean or not, because it still looks dirty after being cleaned. I've been to old buildings that have been successfully turned into hotels, and Carter Hotel will have to do a better job of renovating for its guests to be able to say that they have really renovated. Suggestion to hotel: get smaller beds, or break down a few walls to convert 3 rooms into 2. The staff, while friendly, can't say anything else but 'just doing their jobs'. If you're on a budget, don't get a room in the Times Square area. If it has to be Times Square and you can spend a little over twice more than Carter's rate on a room, get at least a 4-star room.

name: Park Central
title: “Unclean & Unorganized”
text:
I recently stayed in Manhattan for 2 weeks, staying at a numb of different hotels. My last 4 days were spent at the Park Central Hotel. This is my first rating on trip advisor, and i felt i had to let people know of my experience at this hotel. 
Hotel room: Tidy, well laid out, quite spacious. A lower floor room, designed for wheel chair access. No problem, or so i thought until i opened the bathroom door... Floor tiles loose, rocking back and forth when i walked on them. Stains on the floor. Bath tub moldy, bathroom sink cracked, and falling off the wall. The sink was filthy, and I was loathe to clean my teeth using the basin. During my last day, the toilet broke down, and upon flushing sprayed me with raw sewerage. - always close the lid before flushing! 
Valet Parking: Problematic. As the hotel is situated on a busy street, you are unable to order your car to be bought up by valet parking earlier. This is understandable given Manhattan traffic conditions. Problem is that the hotel valet requests you stand outside and wait for your car but that does necessarily mean that collection of your car is a priority. On my last day i waited 26 minutes on the side walk for my car to be bought up by valet. 
Breakfast: reasonable
Gym: quite well equipped. 
Hotel front office staff: service level average.
All in all, based on my experience, i would not recommend this hotel to a potential visitor as a 4 star property
Thank you.

name: Best Western PLUS President Hotel at Times Square
title: “4* hotel?!?!?!?!?!?”
text:
This is more like a 2* .... And that's being generous!! The rooms are small but we expected this. However we did not expect the room to be dirty and the bathroom even worse.
 We did not get one good night's sleep because of the temperature in the room. It was impossible to regulate it. The room was stifling hot in general and when we turned on the air con it was absolutely freezing. So basically we spent our time getting up to turn on or off the air con all through the night instead of sleeping!! 
We had 2 hand towels when we got there but these were taken away by the cleaning staff the following day and we didn't get any replacement for the duration of our stay... Apart from one day when she left just one hand towel. 
The Internet was absolutely useless. Had to enter the wifi code every time you used it and it was so slow it was painful... That's if it worked at all.
The location was excellent. The price ok. But would certainly not go back. Expected way more for a 4*. Obviously stars mean nothing in NY!

name: Park Central
title: “Great service and excellent localization”
text:
Great Service excellent place. Near the Central Park and Times square.
I want to register the courtesy of Elizabeth at the front desk.
She was very nice and helped me to find a delivery.
The staff in general is very polite.
I also want to thank Ernesto in the package room

name: W New York
title: “Nice people work there, but nothing gets done. Street noise all night in Lex Ave rooms.”
text:
What appears as a bargain hotel rate of $209 at the W Hotel chain's Lexington Avenue location is most certainly no bargain. My three colleagues and I booked 4 rooms, each of us expressed disappionted and will never stay there again. And we are not fussy people, all of us are frequent world travellers, we spend dozens of nights each year in NYC, staying at varoius mid-priced hotels or University clubs. 
Here is a summary of my experience at the W Lexington Avenue.
This very busy section of Lexington Avenue - the sirens and horns blared well after midnight (luckily I had my earplugs with me). The windows are not soundproof as at other hotels. - you will need earplugs if your room faces the street.
The rooms are small, which is expected in NYC, but the W's rooms are especially small, more like large closets, with no place other than the bed to set a suitcase, barely any room to get around the bed. And I had the deluxe corner room. 
- I am no fan of "form over function" and the W's rooms reek of form, with little practicality (for example the light switches are fussy push buttons with skinny slide dimmers, cutesy little signs on them, etc., closet light is built into the rack rather than overhead, etc.). And, to boot, many of the floor and table lights were UNPLUGGED in my room, really frustrating when I tried the wall switches, buttons on the lamps, etc. just to get a light to turn on! I finally realized the maid or prior guest must had unplugged them. Understandable - but someone from the hotel needs to pay attention to these things.
As I walked to my room after check in, there were three room service trays, in front of three different rooms - with BREAKFAST DISHES (this was at 5pm). And, just in front of my room a big unattended hotel valet luggage cart was completely blocking the hall. I moved it aside and it was in the same location hours later. At check in I encountered an cheery front desk staff, and I was provided a card with a name and invitation to call with any questions or problems. When I left for dinner around 6pm I informed the person identified on the card that they should ask someone to remove the breakfast dishes. They expressed great shock over this and said they were "soooooo sorry." When I returned from dinner at 10pm the dishes were still in the hallway. This is a perfect example of the "friendliness with no follow through" that is often evidenct in poorly run establishments. 
After returning from dinner I noted that the "turndown" maid service left a printed note inviting me for coffee and a danish in the front lobby the following morning. I thought that was a nice touch, offered as token of goodwill for my less than perfect experience at the hotel thus far. The following morning I poured a coffee from the urn in the lobby, took a danish and presented the note to person watching me from behind the bar. She took the note, went to a cash register and presented me with a tab for around $10! I said there must be a misunderstanding, since had I given her the note inviting me for coffee and a danish. Her reply "no, that is only an invitation - nothing here is free for our guests". I gulped down my breakfast and vowed to never again set foot in the W Hotel, Lexington Ave. You would be wise to do so as well. Its management appears to be full of clueless amateurs.

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Modern hotel, but you wont sleep!”
text: Just got back today from this hotel, i was there from 5th jan 2011 and allthough it was a modern hotel near times square, the rooms were soooooo small we couldnt open our suit cases in them, without putting them on the bag first. We complained and got a upgraded room, which wasnt much bigger, but they agreed we would only have to pay for 2nights upgrade instead of 4. But the problems didnt finish there, every half hour the heating kicks in and the raditors make a bad banging noise, so we havent slept for 4 nights right through! My sister and her husband also came with us and they had the same problems with the room size, so were upgraded, but there heating kept going off in the middle of the night, they called the maintenence man out twice to fix it (which they were charged for!!!!) But we complained and got this charge scrapped. Their tv also didnt work, but knowone fixed that. Over all it was an ok hotel and near everything, so if you dont think your going to be in the room for long then this would be ok to book, but just be prepared that you wont be sleeping very well. Plus just a tip - if u wish to store ur suitcases downstairs with them because u have to check out, they charged us $16 and then wanted a tip for putting them in!

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “Milford Hotel = Fraudsters!”
text:
I booked this hotel online for a client and I filled the credit authorisation form for them to charge my account to a particular amount, i was charged extra and i only noticed when i saw the transaction notification rom the bank, i sent them an e-mail asking why i was charged so and i got a reply saying they deducted new york javit and occupancy tax, this was already included in my previous bill and i sent a mail back informing them of this, and i got a "we would look into this" reply, and i have not heard from them ever since, i sent my credit card details and believed the authorisation form would have effect in the amount they would charge my card but No, they charged extra, the milford is so badly managed, they are a rip-off and i hope they get burnt very soon!
I am taking steps to report this to a fraud unit!!! Duping customers of their money plus rendering bad service should not be condoned!!!!

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Basic and Central”
text:
Here are the pros and cons of this Hotel in a nutshell: -
Pros
1 Central location
2 Clean towels every day
Cons
1 Basic rooms in need of decoration
2 Rude and extremely unhelpful reception staff
3 Fittings and fixtures not working

name: Marrakech Hotel on Broadway
title: “Great hotel, great location, great price”
text: After reading the reviews on this site among others, as previous travellers have said before, I was a little apprehensive as I embarked on my stay at the hotel. However I was very pleasantly suprised. The staff at the check in desk were very polite and as my bag had not yet arrived in New York said that they'd deliver it to the room when it did arrive and joked about a certain airline always loosing bags. We were allocated a room on the forth floor which was not a problem for myself and my partner as we are young and used to living on the top floor but I can see how it could pose a problem for some. The room was clean and very warm which was wonderfull as when we were in New York, the worst snow storms of the season decided to arrive too. The only problem with the room was that there was no wardrobe, although this was a very minor problem. There was some renovation work going on during my stay but this caused no inconvience whatsoever. The bar is a nice place to have a quiet drink before heading out for the evening. The decor of the hotel is beautiful and interesting, especially in the bar. The door staff are very friendly and very strong, one impressively carried our two heavy cases down to the street as well as flagging us down a taxi. The hotel is ideally located next to the 103rd street subway which connects you to all the major attractions and Central Park is only a few blocks away. There are lots of nice places for breakfast within walking distance also. Great hotel, great location, great price :D

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “Comfortable rooms, good location”
text:
I stayed in this hotel twice in August 2008. Once on the 8th floor of the A tower, second time on 3rd floor. Hotel is centrally located, close to Central Park and subway. 
Rooms were spacious, ok equiped and beds comfortable. Bathrooms somewhat small and without good lighting, but also ok. Both times my rooms were facing the street and it was pretty loud diring the night. Earplugs solved that problem. 
During my second stay I discovered that my bathroom was not cleaned (don't ask me what I found there..). They appologized and quickly gave me other room and breakfast voucher. 
They said there is nice swimming pool on the roof of the hotel. However, opened only between 10a.m and 6p.m. so I didn't have chance to see it. 
Overall, this hotel represents good quality for the money I paid.

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “I am in agreement with every negative review here”
text:
No need to spend alot of time typing................I just agree with every negative review here, and the positive reviews sure don't sound like the hotel where we stayed.
I stayed here in 2004 and had a beautifully remodeled room. I even complained about the room and mentioned that prior experience. I was told all the rooms were like the one we were in. Also told there was NO A/C...............No A/C?!!!! Sure..........with the hot summers???????????? Will NEVER stay there again!!!!!
OK............one positive...........the bed was comfortable..................

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “The place is a complete dump and so dirty!”
text:
Honestly this hotel was a dump, I wouldn't of let me dog stay there to be honest.
The hotel was dirty and so tired. Anyone that rates this hotel as good must have very low standards is all I can say.
I wouldn't touch this place with a barge pole. The first room they put us in was the size of a shoebox and dirty, I refused to even put my bag down on the floor! The next room wasn't much better just bigger - it would seem this was the best it was going to get in this shocking hotel. Don't get me wrong I know hotel rooms in NY aren't big but they should at least be clean! I went to NY the previous year and didn't experience a hotel that was like this so I wouldn't recommend staying there to anyone
