If you stay there be warned the place is really dirty, decor completely dated, bar staff are pretty rude and reception staff seemed pretty uninterested when we complained as well. It was that bad that we almost checked into another hotel - we were only there for four nights.

name: Marrakech Hotel on Broadway
title: “very good bargain”
text:
Our stay here was great. The staff were professional and friendly.
The rooms were a bit small, but were clean and offered the latest in flat panel TVs and good channel selection. Although the city was noisy, the rooms were quiet. There was no elevator that we saw. The staff helped us get our bags to our rooms. Towels were plentiful, but there were no washcloths. Our room would have benefitted from a bedside lamp. We liked the neighborhood around the hotel. Central park was nearby. The restaurants were very good and other services we needed were close by. Convenient subways took us everywhere with ease.
Overall, my experience was great. I would stay here again. We are already talking about returning next year.

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “Good value for money, but don't expect to feel special”
text: The Milford Plaza offers good value for money with modestly sized, but clean and modern, rooms, in a very good location in New York. Staff was generally helpful, but not extraordinary and the booking, chek-in and check-out were efficiently done. The quality of the linen, mattress, towels, shower gel and moisturizer was good. The air conditioner is incredibly noisy, but helps masking the street noise. The hotel offers no breakfast, and has a very small bar. What lets the hotel down, and makes me give it 3 stars, is that it is too big and too busy. You fell like you are in a bus station, and everytime I was waiting for the lift in the lobby, I had at least another than 10 people, some times 20 people, in the same situation - I had never seen such a busy hotel in my life. That does raise some concerns with respect to security, as it must be impossible for staff to screen everyone that comes through the doors, but I think the risk is probably low. If you are on a budget, and want a good location in New York, you can do much worse than the Milford, but the hotel will not be one of the highlights of your trip.

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Goed hotel, dichtbij Time Square”
text: Het hotel zit 2 minuten lopen van Time Square. Maar op de kamer is het heerlijk rustig. Het is er behoorlijk schoon en je kan ook nog om je bed heen lopen. Voor New Yorkse begrippen is dit behoorlijk ruim. Ernaast zitten 2 Deli's waar je lekker kunt ontbijten. De bedden liggen ook nog eens heerlijk en in het hotel heb je gratis internet als je dit op je telefoon hebt, dus een echte aanrader om maximaal te profiteren van deze geweldige stad.

name: W New York
title: “Flashy”
text: Small rooms backing onto brick walls and Indifferent service.

name: Park Central
title: “Wonderful hotel all around”
text: Excellent service, this is the only hotel we stay at when we come to the city. Great location! Rooms are always clean, never had a bad experience yet in over 30 years. The front desk is always polite & helpful, this time brought very young kids & they were so nice to the kids!

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Not good for children”
text:
First the good things - Convenient location and a very helpful and cooperative staff in coffee shop. That's about it!
This hotel is an absolute no-no if you are traveling with kids. When I called up room service to request for warming up of milk, chap first refused stating that he was too busy attending other orders, and then said the hotel doesn't allow use of microwave to warm milk, and recommending going to the pasta shop next door to use their microwave!! In this tour of 20 days, I have stayed in 6 hotels, and not one ever refused to warm up milk (or provide a microwave in the room). Housekeeping was also not upto the mark. Bathroom sink has leaky taps, making everyday use a mess.

name: Hotel Alexander
title: “Très bon rapport qualité prix”
text: Nous y retournerons à notre prochain séjour car c'est un très bon rapport qualité prix. Le fait que les sanitaires soient communs ne pose pas de problème car le nettoyage y est fait régulièrement et nous n'avons pas eu de mauvaise surprise

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Nothing to Write Home About”
text:
I stayed at The Roosevelt in May for a very quick three night trip. I arrived late at the hotel and the first impression of the hotel is a beautiful hotel lobby as you would expect from a grand dame of the roaring 20's. The hotel is in a fabulous location that puts you central to all of the areas you want to go to, but that is where the pros end.
When I got into my room it smelled of Urine. So I called the front desk and was told that they were completely booked and could not move me. They sent up an employee who sprayed the room with Fabreeze and left. I was told that I could check back and they could see about moving me. They were able to move me the next night to another room in the hotel, which was much nicer as it was an upgraded room.
The rooms are small, and I expect this in major cities. Those that complain about room size have probably not traveled much outside of the US or in major cities as that tends to be the norm.
The pictures on the travel sites look nothing like the room you are given. Come to find out the rooms pictured are an upgraded room not the standard house room. My biggest complaint is that they did not have anything to do in the room. There was no internet, they didn't have Lodgenet or OnDemand so you could not watch movies, all you got was whatever was on TV.
The bathrooms are small, something else that is typical in historical buildings, but they should consider remodeling to give guests a place to place their vanity items as there is no room to place the items you need to get ready in the morning.
Overall the public spaces of the hotel were nice, but the rooms were not a 3 or 4 star because of the amenities offered. You can do better in New York.

name: Days Inn Hotel New York City - Broadway
title: “Much better than expected”
text:
Having read some of the not-so-choice reviews of this hotel, I was somewhat concerned about what to expect. However, I was pleasantly surprised. 
Ok, so it isn't the Waldorf Astoria, but how much can one expect for such a reasonable price, in NYC terms at least. 
I arrived earlier than planned at 2pm, but my room was ready and I was able to check in straight away. The room was a reasonable size by NYC standards, but small of course by other standards, but as a seasoned NYC traveller I was impressed by the larger-than-expected size of the room. 
The good: clean, easy location (subway on the corner) so felt safe as a single woman, nice enough rooms, not too noisy even though I was facing out to the street. 
The bad: Only one small radiator under the window didn't really provide enough warmth for NYC in December. The lift really was an experience to behold - I walked every time after trying it once!

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Good for the money”
text:
Stayed here for a few days in April, after a night at the Andaz, and before one night at a terrible airport hotel (see other reviews...). 
Overall, this is a good hotel for the money paid. Four nights at an average of US$200/night, including breakfast and taxes. When you consider that even the most basic of hotels in New York can be $300/night minimum, this place is fairly good value. 
Location-wise, you're only one minute away from the 24 hour electric daylight of Times Square. You're also close to the Port Authority, and three metro stations. 
Rooms
These are small, which is to be expected for New York, I guess. I stayed in a king, but as I was by myself, had more than enough room. What I noticed, though, was that when the hotel was renovated, the owners didn't bother changing certain things - so the doors, for example, look like they're from the hotel first time round, and the ceiling still has its original artexed finish. No big deal, really, except when it comes to the air conditioning unit - not ceiling mounted as in most hotels, but a very old fashioned below window unit, which was INCREDIBLY noisy. I found the best thing to do was to leave it on full blast when I went out, and then turn it off when I came back. Also, the soundproofing isn't great - could hear next door's mobile phone ring and part of their conversation. Though I guess you could turn on the aircon to drown out the sound...
Service
Front desk and the concierge were very helpful - can't fault them at all! Doorman presence was a little minimal when I was there...
Food
Quite a good breakfast spread in the restaurant - good service there too. Interesting that in 2010 they still use breakfast coupons! Worth noting that if you book a B&B rate, the tax and service are added on separately. Also worth noting to get there early or very late - I saw some unfortunate people who came down at peak hours, and had to sit at tables next to the lift...
Gym
As usual, limited selection of free weights, and the ceiling is so low that it almost skims the top of the cable station - meaning if you want to do pull ups, you hit your head. If you really want a proper workout, I'd suggest buying a day pass somewhere local - there's a well equipped gym on the corner of W 55th St and 8th Ave. 
Other
This place has the typical boutique hotel vibe - low lights in the lobby, artfully arranged furniture, lounge music soundtrack etc. I wonder if this isn't starting to feel a little old now. You get the feeling that when it was put together, the designers wanted the lobby to be filled with beautiful young things lounging on designer furniture. Unfortunately, the reality is a bit sadder....
Noticed that the lighting was so low that in the evening, it was very hard to use the internet terminals on the mezzanine floor. 
Overall, this was decent value for the money - a good choice for tourists and holidaymakers who want to be in the thinck of things.

name: Skyline Hotel
title: “Över förväntan”
text: Trevlig och hjälpsam personal och förhållandevis stora rum. Helt, rent och funktionellt men inte direkt modernt. Inte det roligaste området på Manhattan men ganska nära till Times Square och teaterdistriktet.

name: Hotel St. James
title: “tres bien pour ce tarif ,l'essentiel y est : propre et confortable”
text: situation parfaite a 2 pas de times square et du metro hotel un peu vieillot mais confortable et propre : parfait pour visiter la ville pour pas trop cher chambre assez grande pour new york : bon rapport qualité prix : ainsi qu'un delis juste en sortant de l'hotel pour les ptit dej avec pancake et omelette

name: Hotel Carter
title: “YUK - GROSS HOTEL - please clean up as the location is great.”
text:
DON'T stay here - it is so disgusting. Carpet in a really bad state, hairs all over the bathroom, blood on the wall, a nipple clamp under the bedside table, no bedside light. Noisy - kept up all night. 
Only good things were warm shower - in a dirty bath - and the location which was very central. Huge beds for a single room too. Had internet and Wifi which was useful.

name: The GEM Hotel Midtown West
title: “NOT a "gem"”
text:
Chose this hotel for proximity to a trade show. The staff was pleasant. The room tiny ,but seemed OK. Remote control unit was haphazardly taped together. A portent of things to come. Had my first experience with bedbugs. Shower control fell off in my hand the next AM The kindly person at check-out credited my account $50.00 for the shower dysfunction.
Upon returning home sent off an outline of problems encountered on my 2 night stay. Their only response - - - adding my email to their advertising spam list

name: Days Inn Hotel New York City - Broadway
title: “if you booked through pre-paid service, beware!!!”
text:
We used a housing booking service to book rooms at this hotel. So it is pre paid ahead of time. As my flight was landing late, I called the hotel to give them notification that it will be a very late check in. I believe the night receptionist gave the worst room the hotel have to me and to my colleague which are Room 401 and 402. There is the hotel sign outside the window but the rooms only have one layer of window blinds! So our rooms were lit up by the neon sign all night long. It was impossible to sleep! We requested to change room but the night reception would not do anything and tell us to wait until the morning when the Day shift manager comes in.
I have to pay a $25 to upgrade my room to King size bed room which I did not hesitate as the double size bed room is really way to small for a couple to stay in for 5 days.
So I strongly recemmend you insisting on NOT having the room on the fourth floor, especially 401 and 402!
The rest is pretty decent with free wireless internet. The other negative thing is the carpet. It is pretty used and worn out.
The hotel is located next to the metro station so it is very convenient to go around the city.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Beautiful Hotel, Comfy bed, Great location”
text:
This was our first trip to New York City and we stayed for 4 nights. The lobby looks so grand; it was really nice walking in to the hotel and seeing the chandelier and old fashioned decor. The room was small but enough for us and the bed was sooooo comfortable. Even with bands practicing right outside the hotel for the parade, the street noise was not bothersome at all. We walked over to Grand Central Station, Times Square, Fifth Avenue, Museum of Modern Art and Central Park. We took the subway for other locations. Great location! We would stay out late at night and felt very safe walking back to the hotel at 1-2 am. 
The lobby seemed to be a popular spot on St. Patrick's day. The parade was a block away so that was pretty nice! Patzeria Perfect Pizza delivers to the hotel in case you want seconds after visiting them on Times Square/Broadway!! 
My only disappointment was that the front desk responsible for luggage was not very helpful when it came to our lost luggage delivery inquiries. They acted like it was an annoyance each time we spoke to them. They kept telling us they would let us know as soon as they received our luggage from the airport. In the evening, we passed by the front desk and saw our luggage behind the desk and it was a few minutes before we could get the bell boy to pay attention to us. We had received no notice our luggage had arrived and we had been waiting in our room for hours since the airport had said it was on its way. 
But other than those men at the luggage desk, our hotel stay at The Roosevelt was very enjoyable. The ladies checking us in and out and the doorman who hailed our cab to the airport were very courteous.

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “Worst Hotel Experience I have ever had”
text: I do not even know where to begin to go on about the problems I have had with this hotel. 1. The first room I was in had grass stains and urine stains on the sheets. We were moved to another room after the manager looked at the sheets and right away was shocked and offered us a suit. 2. We called the front desk for extra towels and they never came. 3. We called the maid manager to get new sheets before we had our room moved and were told she would be right up and she never came. 4. There was yellow sheets in our second room but we decided to not make any more fuss. 5. We then had a maid come into our room without knocking and turned on the lights. We told her to come back later and she did not even appologize and walked out and shut the door. 6. They were nice enough to take off all chargers on the hotel (they said), and we went to the crowne plaza down the road ($70 more per night but WELLLLLL worth $300 more). 7. I had called back five days later because my card was charged for 2 nights (we had only stayed one and the one night was reversed). I spoke to a lady on the phone by the name of Jackie Ilbersonso that night and she raised her voice, hung up multiple times on me, interrupted me multiple times and was in no way understanding or in no way tried to solve the situation. This hotel had no positive qualities at all. The hallways were absolutly gross, they looked like a jail cell. The doors were barley made of metal, they were very thin/light doors. The service/people who work there/rooms were horrific and if it were possible I would personally pay every person $70 more per night to not stay here and to stay at the Crowne Plaza down the road. WORST HOTEL EXPERIENCE I HAVE EVER HAD BY FAR DOOOOO NOTTTT STAYYYYY HERE.

name: Days Inn Hotel New York City - Broadway
title: “The Quality hotel :) Days Inn”
text:
OK firstly, I gotta say for the price we received we weren't expecting a whole lot. And I gotta say the place delivered :) We got a far better hotel right on Time Square for a lot less than this place. 
I'll take you through it as we experienced it. As we checked in, the lobby looked presentable and there were a load of "please forgive our appearance the hotel is being refurbished". The staff were polite and seemed nice. It kinda suited us as we were tired and just wanted to drop our bags. One of the lads hopped on the lift and it nearly jammed when he stepped in. When the door opened on our floor the halls stank... that was before we even walked into our rooms. 
Now the rooms, they were a decent enough size but they looked like they hadn't been cleaned since the place was built. The toilet didn't flush and we had to jimmy it up just to make it work. The shower was blocked and the water flooded whenever someone took one. the inside of the cabinets had "hotel from hell 2005" written by previous occupants... so u could tell the cleaning was right up to scratch.
It sounds like I am being a tad negative here, so I'll jump to put some positive. We did have a real fun experience as we left to go out. The lift jammed between floors and we got to see New york's finest called in (while the hotel owner told them the occupants of the stuck lift were "not distressed"). Was even cool getting a few snapshots of the fire engine as it rescued the people stuck in the lift :).
All in all the place stank, the TV only worked if you wanted to listen to the radio... Then we had a lovely surprise the next morning when we awoke with bites of some kind all over our backs from whatever infested the beds. But again... the staff were friendly :) Stay in this place if u don't mind risking getting the plague or getting mugged.
The cheery message in your room "please ensure all doors are deadbolted" said it all. I can't say it enough to ring around as this place is miles off then beaten track.

name: W New York
title: “W Hotel Main”
text: Overall fantastic hotel, great location and superb bar.

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “Just average hotel”
text:
I returned from a stay at this hotel with my 2 teenage daughters for an Easter Spring Break trip. It's just far enough off the beaten path to be relatively quiet, especially if your rooms are on the back side of the hotel. We never heard the horns and sirens from the streets. There were, however, a fair number of rowdy teens in the hall yelling and slamming doors at all hours. I never saw security. The acoustics were lacking in that respect, as I was also awakened early in the morning by slamming doors. The room was clean, but the hotel is rather dreary with beige and green walls, old stained carpet and dark drapes and bedspreads. It is definitely in need of renovation. The 3 computers are in the lobby and charge for services. I had a house drink in the bar and it was $10.50. Ouch! Plus, they tack on a $4 fee for accessing movies in the room, which are steep to begin with. There is a small TV unit with 3 small drawers, that's it. No drawer in the desk. There is a tiny closet with one shelf, no storage in the bathroom except on the sink.No room safe or frig. There was an iron/board and a small hairdryer as well as a 4 cup coffee pot. All cups were plastic., one chair in room. We had 2 rather hard double beds with stiff linens. The shower head in the bathroom was fixed in one position. They provided a shower cap and a tiny bottle of cheap combination shampoo and conditioner. 
 We stored our luggage on the last day for $2 a bag and they had a cab for us. That was the extent of service we used, but they were very polite. We had an average breakfast in the dining room- not bad, but there are so many better options near the hotel. 
 They have 3 elevators, but they are very tiny and we had trouble at times catching one. The stairs lead to the back outside of the hotel and aren't well marked, but that's an option. Overall, this is a pretty good option for a reasonably priced hotel. I wouldn't choose it for a romantic or special trip, but for a clean and safe place, it's fine. I rated it 3 stars, but in reality it's about a 2.5.

name: Jolly Hotel Madison Towers
title: “Made to feel like pests not guests”
text: Arrived at the Jolly Madison ecstatic to be in New York for our Engagement.After a long flight tired but excited things soon went down hill! we showed reception our booking confirmation which the Girl on the desk dismissed & said "we have'nt got any confirmation of this booking" she then offered us a standard room instead of the deluxe room we booked until they sorted it with the company(Lets go 2).This was fair enough until we later found out our credit card was blocked for $1,200 $300per night for a standard room!!!!!!! subsequently meaning if we wanted to purchase anything we could'nt!!!!!!!! saving grace was we are'nt married yet so we have seperate cards not joint names.Whenever we asked the staff for anything we felt like we had just taken there months wages,they were very unhelpful.besides the hotel being 99% bad the porters(Eduardo especialy)& 1 male receptionist who told us the attractions of New York were the only thing that will help tourists.we were made to feel like we came off the street to sneak a room for a few nights.rooms were clean,towels changed regular but would avoid hotel at all costs.

name: The GEM Hotel Midtown West
title: “Terrible Location, please don't stay here!”
text:
Two first time experiences with this hotel- first time I have ever written a truly awful review for a hotel and the first time I ever walked into a hotel, looked around the lobby, went to my room, and walked out of the hotel without a word to anyone. I really didnt care about the money lost. There is no way I could have stayed here.
Booked online thru Quikbook. We decided to stay in NYC after being in the city for the day on business; we originally planned to take the train back to Albany but thought it might be nice to stay the night , see a show, have a few drinks, etc. and we Needed a last - minute hotel for just one night.
The rates were high overall for this night, but the GEM was affordable and I THOUGHT I knew the area where it is located and THOUGHT the reviews here on TA had been pretty much ok. It was also close to Penn station, where we needed to catch a train early in the morning. So we booked.
This hotel is an uncomfortable distance (in psychological terms) from the outskirts of Chelsea and the OK areas of 36th and 6,7,8th Aves in Midtown. You must cross the very busy highway (Dryers?) , it is a very, very dirty, gritty, dusty, trashy, area with little pedestrian traffic.
There is no eating or drinking establishment nearby and no place to comfortably linger outside the hotel. No Duane Reades or anything like that. 
I was having trouble with the location, but seeing our room sealed it. I didnt bother to examine the room to see how clean, etc. , it may have been very clean but the window looked out to the boarded up window of the crumbling building next door and the room was very, very dark.
I was also concerned about security- no doorman, no key card entry to the hotel OR the elevators OR the stairways. 
I felt so sorry for the the family with 3 children checking in behind us- international travelers, struggling to push and pull their bags thru the door with no offers of assistance, and probably no choice but to stay here for at least this one night.
The hotel itself was not "a dump", as in filthy dirty and bugs and stuff (at least didnt seem so from a quick glance around) but the location in the city and the neighbooring buildings and immediate area make it very undesirable.

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Nära till allt”
text: 150 från Broadway. Nära till Sightseingbussar, restauranger, affärer. Två Deli utanför hotelporten. Trevlig personal. Helt ok rum, rent & snyggt. Finns en liten lounge vid lobbyn med tv. Går att beställa airshuttel från hotellet, 54 dollar för tre pers till Newark.

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “I can't imagine staying anywhere else in NYC than The Paramount!”
text: I love The Paramount! The location is great; Times Sq is right around the corner but you're not in the thick of it. Rooms are small, but well outfitted & tidy. Be sure to stop next door and get pizza from Patzeria! Restaurant Row is just down the street (out the door & to the right). Brian the doorman is the BEST!

name: Jolly Hotel Madison Towers
title: “Great hotel!!”
text:
I was concerned by the comments which i had read before our trip however could not find fault with this hotel.
The rooms were clean with daily towel change and were an average size for a New York hotel. All staff were helpful and friendly.
A good location, close to Empire State Building and other major attractions. We stayed here in Dec 04 and would return again!!

name: The GEM Hotel Midtown West
title: “Nice hotel in a great location”
text: We just returned from a 3 night stay at the Gem Hotel in NYC. Although the room was very small, it was in a great location. We were four blocks from Macy's/Times Square. There is a soup kitchen/shelter across the street. If that bothers you, you might want to stay elsewhere. We never had any problems. They put us in a nice king size room at the back and it was very quiet. The hotel is extremely clean and upkept. We had a plasma tv, armoir and an Ipod ready radio. The bathroom was quite large and had all the toiletries you would need. The staff were the nicest I've ever found in New York. There is a subway stop around the corner so you can be anywhere in minutes. All in all, I would definitely stay there again.

name: Days Inn Hotel New York City - Broadway
title: “A cheap hotel, what you pay is what you get”
text:
I stayed here on a year 12 school trip and when we arrived at the hotel it took up to 2 hours for us all to be assigned rooms, although we were "lucky" in that we got a room straight away, only to walk into it and smell the strongest, most stale cigarette smell despite it supposedly being a non-smoking room.
Fortunately after complaining the staff were very polite and helpful and did in fact move us to another room although much better we found the lamp, hairdryer and toilet didn't work properly (the toilets actually became blocked in several people's rooms including ours.)
All in all I would say that for what you pay and the location the hotel isn't bad but I certainly wouldn't stay there again.

name: Park Central
title: “Great location, no serious problems”
text:
Just stayed at the Park Central for 3 nights during a trip to NYC to see shows. The location is just great. It is north of Times Square, but not far at all. You can see the lights of Times Square clearly from the front of the hotel. It's close to Carnegie Hall and maybe 2 blocks south of Central Park. There is a subway stop right next to the hotel. We found this incredibly convenient, especially for anyone who wants to go to Broadway shows yet does not want to be located in Times Square. By the way, Lincoln Center is also part of Broadway, and that is a few blocks northwest of this hotel. Another bonus: many, many delis and restaurants are located right around the hotel. The Carnegie Deli and Stage Deli are within one block. Ninth Avenue is lined with restaurants (we liked the Thai restaurant called Siam something, a lot).
The lobby has a bar that is decent, and also has a breakfast bar, which is handy. There is Starbucks coffee for sale in the lobby, but in case that's not enough, there is a Starbucks store located in one corner of the hotel, facing 7th Avenue. 
Our room was nondescript but OK. We were on about the 9th floor facing the inner courtyard, not the street (we wanted it quiet). It was very, very dark, although we didn't care very much. No refrigerator, no coffee maker. But otherwise pretty good, and clean.
The elevators are not slow, which is great, but you have to learn their "system" for using the elevators. It's not too bad, but was a surprise to me at first.

name: Hotel Carter
title: “this place should be condemed”
text: My sister and I and some of her friends wanted a weekend in New York as their annual trip. We took the advise from one of the girls in the group as to where to stay for less money and we were sooooo wrong. When we got thier the people were rude short with my sister who made the reservations. We got to our rooms and they were on seperate floors, it looked like the building had not been cleaned or updated since it was built and I found a map in our room that said the hotel dixie so you know that they don't go through the rooms very well. our room was cleaner then the other girls room but we had a revolting bathroom and the coax cable for the tv was broken the tv was unplugged and all the outlets looked like a fire hazard from the turn of the century. The other girls room had a nicer bathroom but the toilet was behind the door and was not only hard to get to but the door did not close all the way. They had a nice whole in the celling with mold and falling plaster. We we arrived we saw one of the bell boys drinking out of a paper bag. We left the second day but didn't get any of our money back.

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “ick ick ick!!!!”
text:
I stayed here last weekend with my two children. We were given a room on the 2nd floor, and as soon as we got off the elvator, there was a disgusting, rotting smell. Turned out it was someone's room service food in the hallway (meat with a sauce? coffee with milk?), super ripe, with a film on top. Called front desk, assured they would remove. The bathroom was disgusting: dirty, one towel, water on the floor, strange sewage marks, etc. We came back from dinner that night; the food was till there; called again.
The next morning food was still there and the smell had pervaded the room itself. I have travelled a lot, and generally budget and hostel level, and this was grosser than anything I have seen since the hostel in New Orleans during a heat wave when I was a teenager. In other words, my standards are not super picky. 
So I called again, was offered free breakfast ( kids eat free anyway, so whatever). Went out for the day, came back and the food was still there, now with flies and strange colorings. The room was stinky as hell and the air conditioning was not great (this was during a 90-plus days, even into 100 degree, btw).
So I went to the front desk and had some sharp words, which I have never done before. I offered to clear the food myself and the front desk person yelled at me...
Talked to the manager, very calmly, and she was wonderful. She swapped my room for a lux 9th floor corner room, tra la. That was great!
However, when we left the next evening, I stopped in on the 2nd floor (this is perhaps a 3-minute walk from the front desk) just to see...it was still there.
So there's some pretty serious internal and sanitation issues there.
I go to NY at least once a year...lemme tell ya, my friends' sofa beds will be fine from now on. Gross!!!!

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “Never Again!”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel for a week in May 2006. We had been to New York several times previously and we chose this hotel because of its proximity to the Lincoln Centre as we had booked to go to three operas. The location is fine - not the best bit of town, but quite acceptable and safe and the room was very spacious. However, the price was far too high and I felt that the room was dingy and unappealing. The bathroom was even darker and very old fashioned and the lobby doesn't have a welcoming feel about it at all. While we were there various groups of young people were staying and so the entrance area always seemed to be full of luggage, people and noise. I did not think it was up to what I would consider to be Holiday Inn standards and I would never stay there again. I did try to change hotels after a couple of nights, as we hadn't paid in advance, but unfortunately it was around graduation time and most hotels were full.

name: Days Inn Hotel New York City - Broadway
title: “Scene from a horror film”
text:
I visited with some friends on a 6th form college trip, our total number being 29, so we had alot of rooms, but the group were spread out over all floors.
When we first arrived our eyes were immediatly drawn to the 'danger' tape in the corner of the lobby where the plaster was falling off the ceiling. I hoped that things would get better, unfortunatly they did not. One of the lifts was out of order, so rather then wait around i choose to use the main stairs. These were fine till we reached 5th floor where there was all kinds of rubbish and cigarette ash along with flammable liquids with lids of ect.
My room was shared with 3 others yet only 3 keys were provided and only 3 sets f towels ect. The bed was not terrible but when i first arrived we had to remove the top cover and shake the dust off. The shower was also a cause for concern, it would not keep a stable temperature and when my friend had finished, the hot water tap would not turn off and the bath was filling up as the plug stuck. it took 3 people to turn the tap off. None of the showers in friends rooms kept a temperature either.
We were the lucky ones, we had a kitchenette part in our room, but many people had small cramped rooms which with 2 double beds can cause problems in moving about and storage of suitcases ect. In one bedroom a mousetrap was found set under the bed, and in another cockroches were living.
The staff on a whole were not friendly or helpful. When my friends and I ordered Chinease takeaway, and had it in our room, we did not wish to keep the left overs in the room, given findings elsewhere we did not want to encourage insects in our room. When we took down the rubbish they glared at us for daring to disturb them and snapped that there was a bin in the lobby. 
The back stairway was even worse then the front. It had doors and curtain poles on the stairs. These did not seem a very health and safety way about things.
Overall my stay in New York was good, but i spent as little time as possible in the hotel. We hope to return there again sometime, but will not be staying in the same hotel. If you are considering a stay in this hotel, i urge you to reconsider immediatly!

name: Days Inn Hotel New York City - Broadway
title: “Quality, no... Hotel, yes... on broadway, no...”
text: We stayed here for a long weekend in December of 2004. Upon our arrival we were greeted with a wonderful aroma of curry mixed with cigarette smoke which lingered through the entire building. I was not impressed with the lobby area which scared me as typically what lies beyond that area isn't usually any more impressive. We checked in (which was somewhat of a challenge since they had no record of our reservation which was confirmed twice prior to arrival) and entered the refrigerator sized elevator. Once we got to our floor, we tried to make our way through the labyrinth of narrow hallways and misleading signs that led us in circles on the way to our room. Our room was cramped to say the least, and looking out our window we were delighted to find an old sock sitting on our window sill. The radiator was loud and archaic and the room temperature fluctuated between 50 and 90 degrees F, and any tinkering with the thermostat was futile. On the morning of our second day we were forced to brush our teeth with bottled water and go without showering de to the fact that there was no water in the building. After arguing with the concierge for what seemed to be an eternity, I was led to the conclusion that they beleived running water was a luxury I didn't request. Shame on me for not asking that question. The only reason we stayed in this hotel was due to some last minute planning for a quick weekend away. Next time I'm bringing my tent and sleeping in Central Park. Then at least I won't be able to complain about not having any running water.

name: Clarion Hotel Park Avenue
title: “Vale o preço que custa.”
text:
Se vc levar em consideração o valor da tarifa, o valor é adequado (se for comparar com outros hotéis na região). Só não espere grande coisa do café da manhã, pois como é comum nos hotéis americanos, é bem fraco, ou melhor é quase nada.
Pesando os prós e os contras, valeu a pena!

name: Murray Hill Inn
title: “Bed & Bath in mid-Manhattan”
text: We stayed almost one week at Murray Hill Inn. The location is great; near many sights & shopping, safe neighbourhood and many restaurants. Rooms are clean but small, bathrooms are clean. The staff isn't so friendly. Breakfast (bagel & coffee/juice) is included which is a nice extra. Prices are very reasonable. I recommend that hotel for the budget-minded travelers, who likes private bathrooms

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Wonderful”
text: I had a wonderful stay at the Paramount Hotel. The hotel was very clean and everyone was very helpful. Brian the doorman was great. He helped bring in mine and my fiances luggage and helped us load it. He also had a cab waiting for us whenever we needed one. My stay at the Paramount was very pleasant! The concierge did wonderful job helping us to pick what we wanted to do in the time we had and helped book all the tickets and reservations.

name: The GEM Hotel Midtown West
title: “Fine hotel”
text:
This hotel is about 10-15mins walk from penn station/macys, and is quite OK. Service was excellent, and the rooms are nice and clean. The rooms are not very big, but I assume you get what you pay for. A/C in rooms but is very noisy. Flatscreen TV and Safe.
Overall a good hotel.

name: Hotel St. James
title: “Für den Preis völlig in Ordnung”
text: Das Hotel liegt in einer Seitenstraße vom Timesquare, der gute 100 Meter entfernt ist. Nächste U-Bahn Stationen sind Rockefeller-Center und Timesquare. Neben dem Hotel ist ein Deli und in der Straße sind neben einem Broadway-Theater noch zwei Irish-Pubs. Zentraler gehts kaum. Das Hotel sieht von außen recht einladend aus, die Lobby macht auch einen einigermaßen guten Eindruck. Von den zwei Fahrstühlen ging nur einer, jedoch wurde der andere repariert. Die Fahrstuhlfahrt glich jedoch jedes Mal einem Abenteuer. Die Hotelflure wirkten gepflegt. So hatte jede Etage einen anderen Teppich. Zimmer: Das Zimmer war im achten Stock. Es war durchaus geräumig und das Bad war neu. Der Fußboden war etwas komisch gefedert. Größtes Manko war der Blick aus dem Fenster, der den bezaubernden Blick auf den Entlüftungsschacht freigab. Tageslicht war leider Fehlanzeige, weshalb man auch mittags das Licht anschalten musste. Da wir aber eh tagsüber unterwegs waren fällt dies eh nicht ins Gewicht. Service: Die Rezeption war 24 h besetzt. Man gab sich immer Mühe, war nett und zu Späßen aufgelegt. Unser Rückflug ging um 24 Uhr. Wir durften ohne Probleme unsere Koffer bis 19 Uhr in einem extra Raum, der verschlossen wurde, unterbringen. Auch mit Fragen zu Kinos oder anderen Aktivitäten wurde geholfen. Außerdem gab es einen Concierge-Service der Tickets und Ausflüge buchte Fazit: Für den günstigen Preis 100% empfehlenswert. Man darf eben kein 4 Sterne Hotel erwarten. Die Lage ist top!

name: Park Central
title: “Be Careful, Park Centeral had no AC on an 80o Day in June!”
text: We have stayed at the Park Central before. It's a decent hotel that is is usually good value for the price point. However this last stay we had to move on our last night, before an important performance because we were notified the night before that the AC was going to be worked on and the off from 9AM till 9PM on an 80o day. Better to do maintenance on this during the cooler months. This was not acceptable and we paid for a night we could not use, as getting ready for our special day while sweating was not an option.

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Muy recomendable”
text: Hotel muy bueno, con todos los servicios, muy buena ubicación, la limpieza esta acorde a la categoria del hotel, la atencion del personal siempre fue muy amable, y las habitaciones muy comodas tanto la cama como el baño.

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Sehr Zentral”
text:
Wer waren Ende Oktober für 8 Tage in diesem Hotel. Das Hotel ist sehr Zentral gelegen, mann erreicht alle Sehenswürdigkeiten sehr schnell. Wir hatten zwei verschiedene Hotelzimmer. Das erste war sehr sehr Klein das zweite war schon etwas grösser. Man muss Glück haben das man das Grössere bekommt. Sauberkeit war sehr gut. Etwas Teuer ist wenn man die Koffer im Hotel Lagern möchte wenn man erst am Abend einen Flug hat. Ganze 6 Dollar!! Habe das bis jetzt noch in keinem 4 Sternen Hotel erlebt das mann für diese Dienstleistung bezahlen muss.
Aber alles in allem würde ich wieder in dieses Hotel.

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Muy buen hotel!”
text: Muy buen hotel!! Si volviese a NY repetiría sin duda. Estuve con mi pareja de luna de miel, y la verdad es que la habitación estuvo perfecta (Queen room), no tenemos ninguna queja. Si que es verdad que habrá habitaciones mas grandes en otros hoteles de otras ciudades, pero sean realistas estamos en NY así que la encontré muy bien, con espacio para dejar las maletas, un armario con caja fuerte y tv LCD. La ubicación excelente, a 2 min del mismísimo Times Square donde hay de todo, tiendas, teatros, restaurantes, estaciones de metro, bus, etc... La lastima es que ahora mismo esta el hall en obras (en breve ya terminadas) pero hay una zona de descanso que hay wifi gratis. Antes de ir también dudaba del hotel por culpa de los comentarios pero no hice caso y acerté.

name: the Lexington
title: “Beware of blonde night manager”
text: I booked a room at the Radisson after my suburban home lost power in a storm. The hotel was lightly booked, and the weekend manager permitted me and my wife to stay at the hotel for $99 on a Sunday night, $179 on Monday. When I learned that power might not be restored until Wednesday or Thursday, I went down to the Front Desk to inquire about extending my stay, should the power outage continue. The man attending the Front Desk informed me that the hotel had "plenty of availability" and he said he didn't think it would be a problem. Then he asked the night manager, an unattractive, large woman at the desk, and she said the rate for the room woujld be $279. That effectively threw us out in the cold. We booked a less expensive room at the Cosmopolitan downtown. A lovely place. That night manager ruined what could have been a pleasant stay. She should go into a different line of work.

name: Jolly Hotel Madison Towers
title: “Troppo sporco”
text:
Io e il mio fidanzato abbiamo soggiornato presso questo hotel ad aprile 2012. Spendendo 100 € a testa per cinque giorni di solo permottamebto(la colazione sarebbe costata intorno ai 10€ a testa al giorno).
La posizione è fantastica:eravamo in una traversa della 5th avenue e dalla nostra stanza si poteva vedere l'Empire State Building. Niente da dire nemmeno sulla struttura dell'albergo e sul personale sempre cordiale. Tra l'altro un signore alla reception ha origini italiane quindi sa parlare bene la nostra lingua ed è sempre disponibile a consigliare i luoghi da visitare a Manhattan. L'hotel organizza un tour ad Harlem di visita del quartiere più la messa gospel. Io consiglio di farvi dare l'indirizzo della Chiesa ed andarci poi per conto vostro perchè,se non sbaglio,il costo del tour si aggira attorno ai 50$. Calcolate che con la metropolitana ci arrivate spendendo 2,50$. 
Ma arriviamo alla nota dolente dell'albergo:la pulizia!!!!! Il bagno era sempre pulito,ma la camera regnava bella polvere da non so quanto tempo! Ci è bastato alzare la sveglia dal comodino per vederne disegnata la sua sagoma. Il copriletto? Pieno di vichi di sigaretta(la nostra camera era per non fumatori). Insomma,non ci ha lasciati entusiasti per questo motivo. Questo alberga fa parte della catena Nh e sinceramente ci aspettavamo almeno di trovare le stanze pulite.
Poi tutto questo nervosismo passa.siamo nella Big Apple e tutto il resto si dimentica...

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Great Area”
text: The Hotel looks better in pictures. It took me 45 min to check in. The rooms in the Hotel need an upgrade everything was old and smells, The bed was big but wasn't good enough. The hotel is in good area but needs changes ASAP.

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “Much better than last time”
text: We stayed here a year ago in an old room and had the worst experience. They have improved alot. The rooms are VERY modern now. It was much better and more enjoyable this time. Much cleaner and nice tvs finally! Was a bit loud

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Great location, solid value for the money”
text:
It isn't the lap of luxury but for around a hundred bucks a night it is a good value. The room was clean and comfortable and since we were just looking for a place to sleep after roaming around the city all day, that served our needs. The location, right across from Penn Station, is ideal. Walk anywhere or just go across the street and just about every subway line is available.
My only complaint is that check in involved waiting in line for about 45 minutes and there appeared to be several spots at the desk that could have been staffed. Get a few more people on duty, especially on a Friday afternoon preceding a holiday weekend.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Don't listen to moaning people”
text:
Stayed for four nights at this hotel rooms are a little on the small side if you want to travel to new York to stay in a hotel room . But the location of this place is amazing you can walk to almost everythink and if not put your hand up and a cab's there . So don't let moaning people put you off rooms are clean towels and bed changed everyday . The bed is massive and very comfy and trust me 
after all the things you do in the day you need it . We had a great time and would recommend this hotel to freind's and family and would definitly go back .

name: W New York
title: “Style no Substance”
text:
Staff at check-in were apathetic and not well trained (taking 15 minutes to type in an already-reserved room to the system is not good, esp. for NY). 
Room was very small, even for NYC. Interior quality was dated and in need of a makeover -- furniture shopworn and walls needed painting/papering. A/C system was filthy and began squeaking loudly at 3:30am, waking me up. Bathroom large but had no ventilation execept for window which was difficult to open.
Upon checkout, was told that late departure would cost $25, then charged $75 for a three-hour period!!!! Charge was refunded, but I was not told that charge was PER HOUR! What is this, a flop-house?

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “EXCELLENT LOCATION VERY HELPFUL STAFF WOULD STAY AGAIN!!!”
text: We stayed at the Roosevelt in November over Thanks Giving Weekend. We found the location excellent within walking distance of Grand Central, Empire State, Times Square, Rockerfella, and Fith avenue on the next block. The staff were very friendly and helpful during our stay. The rooms are small but the beds are very comfortable and we found it hard getting out of them in the mornings!!!! I would definately stay at this hotel again....Hopefully this year again!!!!

name: Best Western PLUS President Hotel at Times Square
title: “AWESOME SAFE LOCATION BY TIMES SQUARE!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel with my teenage daughter in July for 11 nights & it was a great base. It's a small boutique hotel on 48th street between Broadway & 8th Ave. Only 1 block from the Times Square area, GREAT location! Convenient to everything! Shopping, subways, buses, Broadway Theatres, Central Park, & Rockefeller Center. Very safe area, I had NO CONCERNS at all for our safety at night returning to the hotel.
My room was well appointed, clean & comfortable, as were the public areas. My room had white walls which I loved because during the day it was very bright. I hate dark hotel rooms! Sometimes there was an issue with the hot water for the shower. There's only 15 floors so if you're on one of the lower floors you can take the stairs up to your room instead of waiting for an elevator, you could also go down the stairs zip zip. Come on people stop being so lazy! I'm amazed when the elevator stops at the 2nd floor on the way down & healthy people get in! 
The front desk staff is VERY friendly & helpful, especially Patricia & Suny. Bellmen were very friendly too, Quintin & Al will treat you & your luggage right! 
I highly recommend this hotel if you want to be in the heart of things, want nice clean accommadations & a friendly staff!

name: Astor on the Park
title: “At least the 'critters' were quiet.”
text:
The New York Marathon filled many hotels so I booked the "Recently Renovated" Astor on the Park based on a 3 star listing ny Tourico and JustNewYorkHotels.
The place was a real dump. 
The room reeked of stale cigarette smoke and "other" odors. There was a leak in the ceiling and roaches running down the walls. 
We called JustNewYork hotels and they were rude and refused to switch us to another hotel. The hotel manager offered to change rooms but one was worse than the one we were in; the other, had hot water in the sink, not the shower. Shower enclosures allow water to get on the floor causing leaks and attracting bugs. The TV received only Spanish stations. The location is not convenient, it is near Harlem. JustNewYorkHotels and Tourico misrepresented Astor as a 3 star hotel, try negative star. What a horror. A step above a hostel. Better to sleep under a bridge.

name: Astor on the Park
title: “Average”
text:
I arrived at Astor on the Park a couple of days after opening. The reception area was fine (as in the pictures) but when I got to my room, there was no duvet/cover on the bed, the carpet was full of paint marks and the wardrobe was placed right in front of the window! Strange I thought!- not that there was much of a view anyways. When I originally saw this hotel advertised. it was claimed as 'Home away from Home' - hmmm anything but! I asked to change rooms and the room I got was slightly better. Clean and comfortable, rooms were made up every day with fresh towels etc. If you are in NY you don't spend much time in your hotel room then this is was perfect, but if you are wanting a few more luxuaries away from home then I would not suggest it. There was no fridge, tea or coffee making facilities and certainly no room service. There is a little shop down the block but not all that much to choose from. To be honest I would have spent an extra $50US a night to be more central with a few more luxuaries for the price. 
I heard one couple at reception saying that their phone was not even connected and they were having problems with their shower - not working. 
To be honest many a teething problem, as with most new properties, and I would possibly give it a few more months before staying here to get themselves sorted out. 
The people were friendly enough and would bend over backwards for you.

name: Park Central
title: “Nice Surpise”
text: It was not the first time I stayed in Park Central. It's one the hotels I prefer to stay when in NY. Being a travel agent I surely understand the needs of both hoteliers and clients. But one of the things I hate to hear when people ask something from the reception is the standard phrase: "Our hotel's policy is ...." Specially, if the receptionist has not even tried to help. On my last trip to the city, I needed a late checkout since my flight was delayed for after midnight. I was nicely surprised, when, Drita Oroshi (Front Desk) arranged for a free late checkout of 7hrs!!! I did not had to plead, mention my profession or find excuses. She just checked if it was possible and she arranged it. There is no better advertisement than satisfied clients. I'll definately be back.

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “Great Value!”
text:
I've stayed in many budget hotels, and this was one of the better ones. I recently spent three nights at this hotel and can, without a doubt, say that I WILL return. And honestly, how much time do you really plan to stay in a hotel in NYC, anyway? You're in the city that never sleeps -- get out there and explore!
The hotel is conveniently situated just a couple of blocks from the Port Authority Bus Station (drop point for the NYC Airporter shuttle - $12.50 from LGA, $15.00 from JFK), the A/C/E Subway stop ($2.50 subway, $5.00 AirTrain transfer to JFK), a block from Times Square, and in the heart of the theater district. Taking advantage of the close proximity to the TKTS booth at Times Square, I managed to take in three Broadway and off-Broadway musicals during my three night stay - all shows were within a couple of blocks of the hotel. (If you're looking for a great comedy/musical, I'd recommend NEWSical the Musical, Avenue Q and/or How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying).
There were also food options, galore, surrounding the Milford - Shake Shack was right across the street; Starbucks and McDonalds within a couple hundred yards. Lots of local eateries on 9th Avenue, as well. Food Emporium was just a few blocks away. Looking for last minute, forgotten toiletries? There's a Duane Reade (24 hours) just across from the Port Authority Bus Station.
On to the hotel, itself: I stayed in a recently renovated Queen room - #2603. The room was average-sized for NYC, but fresh and clean. The design of the room was sleek and well laid-out. The room was quiet, too -- either I had no neighbors (unlikely - the hotel seemed very busy), or the walls were well insulated (let's go with that explanation). As a light sleeper, I slept comfortably through the night. The room was also equipped with black-out shades -- an absolute must for anyone sensitive to light.
The bathroom was small, but for a single person, it was more than enough space. They definitely got it right when it came to the fixtures. It looked very modern and new -- lots of glass and chrome/stainless steel. The shower had great pressure (no tub), but be careful as you could accidentally flood your bathroom (the shower curtain was barely long enough to reach the lip of the shower). 
Despite other reviewers mentioning the ongoing construction, I heard none of it. I'm not sure which part of the building is undergoing the renovation at the moment, but I had no issues with sounds or noise (I was there Saturday-Tuesday). The only times that I could hear any noise outside was if a neighbor slammed their door in the hallway, or if an emergency vehicle was blaring its horn on the street (and even then, it wasn't bothersome).
Be aware that (at least for my room), there was a balcony that looked as if it was shared with a neighbor. The windows to the rooms were fully openable, and didn't seem to lock -- I didn't go out onto the balcony, so I don't know if the windows could be opened from the outside, but just be aware of this possible security issue. 
Others mentioned issues with a lack of outlets. I didn't have this issue - my room had more power outlets than I knew what to do with them -- all conveniently situated around the bed and desk areas.
Would I stay here again? Absolutely. The hotel is situated in a great location, the room and amenities were well-appointed and for the price, it is very difficult to beat ($99/night). I was in town for a trade-show, so its location along the shuttle routes was very convenient. My only complaint is the fee for internet usage, but I was barely in my room (except to sleep), so the lack of free wifi didn't bother me much.

name: W New York
title: “W="Wonderful"”
text: What's all these negative reviews about? After reading some of these reviews on TA I was expecting an Econo-Lodge with a bid "W" out front. Not the case. We stayed at the W over Memorial Day Weekend and we were met with an ultra-hip, clean, and magnificent hotel. Are the rooms small? Sure, but keep in mind you're not at a Holiday Inn-Select in Binghampton--you're in Manhattan. Things are tight but the rooms are clean and well-appointed, with nice bath amenities and a cool W robe. The front desk staff and the concierge were both friendly and courteous. The lobby bar is more of a lounge and a great place to have a drink before heading out. The staff does a great job of always keeping the place sparkling clean. The real wheat grass throughout the hotel is a pretty cool touch. The location of the W is perfect. There's a subway stop two blocks away, 3 different coffee places(Dunkin' Donuts, Starbucks and Au Bon Pain) and you're walking distance to Times Square and Central Park. When returning from a night out be sure to have your key card out--there's always a beefy security guard there to make sure you're not trying to sneak in. Overall, it was a wonderful stay at the W. Would I stay again? You bet!

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Excelente ubicación.”
text: Muy buen precio para la ubicación del hotel. El lobby esta muy lindo y el personal es muy amable, el hotel esta muy limpio y el desayuno bufete es delicioso aunque un poco caro, es mejor desayunar afuera! La habitación básica es muy pequeña, pero considerando que uno solo va a dormir y a bañarse esta bastante bien, pero para mi próxima visita si tomare una habitación con cama queen para descansar mejor. El metro esta a unas cuantas cuadras y de todas las líneas, a media cuadra esta times square y caminando llegas al rockefeller center... Sin duda volveré!!!

name: Hotel Carter
title: “bedbugs in hotel carter!”
text:
Don't go to this hotel: there are bedbugs! It's so cheap that one does not expext any luxury, but I do expect a simple, clean and bug-free room. It was not clean, there were clean sheets on the bed and that was it. The carpet was filthy and apparently had not been vaccuumed for weeks, maybe months.
I suffered severe allergy from the bedbug-bites, so now, 6 days after I left the hotel, I am reminded of this terrible experience every minute of the day. My arms, legs, neck and face are red, swollen and ithcy.

name: Park Central
title: “Great Place to stay when in NYC”
text: jessica was terrific at the fronk desk and greated me with a smile. She got me in at 3 even though check-in wasn't until 4. However, room i got had NO view and seemed cramped. One call took care of it and Shepresa got me a room on the 20th floor. This is probably my 4th stay here and have never been disappointed.

name: W New York
title: “Better Than I Expected”
text:
I stayed at the W on Lexington Avenue for two nights (Fri and Sat) and, based on the reviews I had read, was pleasantly surprised. I don't doubt others have had the bad experiences they've written about, and I'm not saying this would be my first choice of hotels in NY by any means, but I had a better experience than many have, so maybe all these tough reviews have had some effect!
The rooms were certainly the smallest I've ever seen in a hotel, period, bar none. If I were truly claustrophobic, I might've been really miserable. It took some getting used to, but it had a certain 'coziness' to it by the time I left. I guess it's 'to each his/her own' on that one. I've also stayed at the W in Chicago (not by the lake, but the other one) and these rooms were really not all that much smaller than those in Chicago as I recall.
I did not find the rudeness or lack of cleanliness so many have cited. I got smiles at the front desk at check-in and upon leaving, there were no mistakes made with my reservation, and my room was perfectly clean. Very small, but clean. 
The daily charge for Internet access is ridiculous, but maybe just a dollar or two higher than the other 4 and 5 star hotels charge. The hallways are dimly lit to achieve a 'chic' look, but not to the point where I had any problem with it.
The AC unit was loud, but in a good 'white noise' way; it was not the kind of 'loud' where it cycles on and off all the time and wakes you up, so I heard almost nothing from the hallways and nothing whatsoever from the street. I was on the 12th floor, and did not face Lexington Ave., so I guess that helped as well. 
Housekeeping was 'invisible' --in a good way -- the room got cleaned while I was downstairs in my conference, but I certainly didn't have the problem of vacuum cleaners and loud conversation among the staff at 8:00 a.m., or anyone knocking on my door, etc. 
So, do they overcharge here? You bet! (My room was $359/night). And, most people would no doubt prefer a bit more space to walk around in and a larger bathroom. Oh, and that shower curtain thing -- that IS annoying and really odd; it does come down to about 2" off the floor so you do get a lot of water on the floor outside the shower.
No question they should spend a few million to really get this place up to par considering the rates they charge.
But my room was clean, the temp was comfortable, the hotel was quiet, the elevators -- while small -- were not especially slow or anything, the front desk people were nice, and I had no occasion to use the concierge, so I can't comment on that.
Overall, it was way better than I expected, given the reviews I had read here, but if I were going to NY on my own dime -- even if I were going alone -- I'm sure there are other hotels I'd look at first, just to have a bit more room and to get more for my money.
On the other hand, if I'm offered a chance to work in NY again and I'm told the meeting will be at the W, I won't be scheming to get out of it just to avoid having to stay there.

name: Comfort Inn Convention Center
title: “Good budget hotel”
text: We just stayed one night here and although it isnt the fancies hotel, it has everying you could need. The area is quiet and a little bit out of the way but not so far that it was inconvenient. The rooms are a but dated and dingy but clean and supplied with everything you could need. I found the wifi connection not very good. The breakfast area is tiny with just a few tables but the breakfast was satisfactory. Toast, waffles, eggs, sausges, yogurt etc were available and although may not have been of the best quality, they did the job. The best thing about this hotel is the staff, they are great, very friendly and helpful. I would stay here again and can recommend it but be aware it is a buget hotel so dont expect the ritz.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Great Location, Good VFM”
text:
OK so there are lots of reviews on here which really slate this hotel. Yes it is old and yes the rooms are small (as are all NYC Hotel rooms). But in terms of value for money I think this was great. We had upgraded when booking, for only a few pounds, to a Penn 5000 room - this basically puts you on a higher floor. The check in was simple and the staff polite and helpful. We had no issues. We were on the 11th floor & yes the hotel could do with a makeover and modernising, but our room was clean as were the towels and the bathroom. The maid came everyday. She cleaned, left fresh towel and changed the bed linen. The TV worked and again we had no issue with this or the room. I think if you do have problems the staff will be willing to help in anyway they can so long as your are reasonable and polite - afterall they are there to help and the few occasions we asked they were really helpful. There isn't a safe in the room, but the hotel does provide free safety deposit boxes - again simple straightforward and not an issue for us. 
The location of this hotel is fantastic. It is right opposite Penn Station with easy access to all the NYC Subway has to offer. You can step around the corner and see the Empire State Building anytime you want to and Macy's is just a block away.
We didnt find (or look) for the coffee lounge that is available to those who upgrade, but there is so much food & drink on offer close by that there seemed little point.
My only "don't bother" is for the Lindy's Diner attached to the hotel - it is overpriced and actually just a short walk away is the Moonstruck Diner on 38th & Madison which is far better value and has good service with a vast menu.
Little Korea is a must - don't be put off by the lines at the restaurants - they are usually fairly short and the food is again excellent quality and tasty.
Another suggestion would be that if you want to avoid the line for the Statue of Liberty is to pre-book before you go. It will stop you waiting for a couple of hours to get through security and on to a ferry.
Another favourite of ours is the Brooklyn Diner on 57th and 7th. It is the same as the one off Times Square but is a little less touristy and has excellent food/shakes.
Don't forget to check out the East Village - St Marks Place has great restaurants and is very vibrant and colourful at night. We enjoyed Virage.
When it comes to gift shop shopping - shop about - those on or close to Times Square charge a few bucks more for most things than those off the beaten track. Especially those at South Street Sea Port at Pier 17.
I would stay here again and I would recommend it - the only bedbug we saw was a giant inflatable one in Times Sq - go figure!

name: W New York
title: “Less black turtle neck, more do your fing job”
text: At that price, you'd like to not be treated like the dirt. I understand the trendy cooler than human W attitude but unless my bed is made, my bathroom clean, the door opened, my bags carried and the towels not frayed, stfu.

name: Jolly Hotel Madison Towers
title: “Una autentica pesadilla”
text:
Ojo con este hotel ,tiene algunas plantas reformadas y otras que son un autentico desastre empezando por la moqueta de los pasillos que no la han debido cambiar desde hace siglos y pasando por el minúsculo tamaño de las habitaciones,las paredes descascarilladas,las camas viejas y nada confortables,baños malolientes y antiguos y que decir del aire acondicionado que suena como una apisonadora,si mantiene las 4 estrellas debe ser pq con total seguridad nadie ha pasado a comprobar el estado de las habitaciones.
Como era imposible seguir en esa habitación pagamos suplemento para cambiarnos a las de la planta reformada pagas como lujo una habitación simplemente correcta .
Por lo que respecta a la recepción destaca por su ineficiencia mal carácter y antipatía de los empleados y de la responsable.
No se lo recomendaría ni a mi peor enemigo.

name: the Lexington
title: “Precio acorde a todo ...”
text: Estuve en el Hotel hace 4 días atrás , realmente excelente y sin problemas , ubicado cerca de los puntos de interés , las habitaciones son un poco pequeñas pero sin dudas que no se necesita mas ... la limpieza es excelente , prolijo en fin nada que decir en contra, no incluye desayuno , pero tiene un Starbucks casi dentro del hotel además de un lugar para cenar también dentro del hotel .Recomendable 100 %.

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “Mould on the Walls - and that is one of the more positive points!”
text:
My sisters and I went to New York to shop for Christmas. The Milford was horrible. The location can't be beat, but the hotel itself is disgusting. The first room given to us had mould all over the walls in the bathroom. When we went downstairs to complain, they didn't even blink, just gave us a different room. Apparently mould is not too uncommon at the Milford.
Both rooms were dirty - other than the bed, which was clean and comfortable. But the floors- ugh! And the bathroom - I am at a loss.
Maybe the renovated rooms are better - but I will never stay in a hotel that engages in the practice of fooling or defrauding their customers. The room(s) we were given were health hazards - and that is being kind. Do yourself a favour and pass on this "deal".

name: Best Western PLUS President Hotel at Times Square
title: “Location/ Renovation/ Service Outstanding!!!”
text: Location, Location in the middle of Times Square.. my partner & I (soon to be engaged) enjoyed the atmospere the second we arrived at the Best Western President Hotel, New York...We stayed in our upscale renovated room the entire day!! Mature staff very hospitable..& polite...I compared this hotel to the Le Merdian 5th Ave ($400 per night)...I was impressed the cost & service.. step out the door your in the Theater Dist. Tour Buses, Time Sq. & great everything... Manager William Bornheimer..thanks a million for sending me my original Driver's Licences that lost in your lobby. Yes Sir I recommend the Hotel to Dr. Trump, Beyonce, and myself just to name a few.. God Bless keep up the great service.

name: Beekman Tower Hotel
title: “Happy Australians Abroad..Fab Location..Art Deco”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights from Oct 7th arriving after midnight.The guy on the desk was friendly and welcoming and efficient in answering our questions. The hotel is in a safe neighborhood and we walked from Grand Central Terminal(about midnight) feeling comfortable with the surrounding streets and area in general. The hotel is close to some pretty funky pubs and diners and grocery stores. We found a fantastic Chinese restaurant 3 min walk from the hotel called Mee Noodle Shop at 2nd Ave and 49 th St..Cheap delicious food, efficient staff and always packed with people. The hotel has huge rooms and it was great to have a kitchenette.These kitchenettes are available in every hotel room (a rarity in NYC I'd say). We didn't like the first room we were placed in as it only had a double bed (not queen as expected) but the manager was able to move us for our last two nights which was perfect for us. The furniture in the room is certainly not modern but art deco as is the hotel in general . The bed and pillows were divine .Probably the most comfy bed I've slept in whilst traveling. The staff on the desk were always courteous and friendly and accommodating esp with our request to move rooms. We were able to jump on the Gray Line Hop on Hop off bus with our 2 day passes at the United Nations Headquarters stop so this was a bonus as well. We did walk into Times Square every day and it was a 20 min walk (much faster than a cab) so the location for us was perfect. This hotel is really quiet at night hence we slept so well. The windows are well insulated. The rooms were cool and the aircon perfect as we needed it a couple of days as the temp was 28 degrees celsius (82 fahrenheit ). This phenomenon known as an "Indian summer". Visited the 911 memorial site on our last day with our pre booked tickets and it really was remarkable how they have monumentalised this whole event and site. Well worth the visit but it did made me feel very sad just being there. Thanks New York City for putting on the superb weather for us. We will be back

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “Very nice stay at the renovated rooms”
text: We stayed two nights at the Milford and had one of the new renovated rooms. The room was beautiful, clean and and spacious (this might vary?) enough for two people. Nice design and with a view over the city and the Hudson River from our bed - pretty cool to stay at 27th floor and enjoy the lights of the city from there in the evening. If youre a light-sleeper - remember earplugs, cause even youre staying at the 27th floor, NYC is still a bit noisy at night ;) Kind and helpfull people in the reception. The hotel is placed only one block away from Times Square and all the theaters and if you come with the bus from Newark, it is only 5 min away by foot. We would definitely recomend this hotel and is looking forward to stay here again, probably after the big renavation of the hotel trough 2012.

name: Best Western PLUS President Hotel at Times Square
title: “Great Hotel-Great Price- Great Location”
text: The hotel in right in times square. You can walk to all the major attractions within minutes. My husband and I stayed at this hotel for our anniversary, and we loved it. I will say that I am a verrrrry picky traveler. If I arrive at a hotel and its not up to par, I demand a refund. I read thousands of posts on hotels before I visted New York, so I was prepared for the small rooms. Although the rooms were small we still got a great bang for our buck. The hotel was clean. And it was nice to come to a warm room because its freezing in New York in December, we just basically left the heat off most of the time and turned on the air when it got too hot in the room. I will say one minor negative thing, some of the hotel staff at the front desk are pleasant, but are NOT very helpful in explaining things. I believe they need to realize that not everyone who vists the New City is from another major city, so a little extra detail in giving directions and when recommending things to do they could do a better job at.

name: Park Savoy
title: “winziges Zimmer aber super Lage! Durchaus empfehlenswert...l”
text: Wir checkten am 19.08.2008 im Hotel ein und waren zu erschöpft vom Flug, um uns an der etwas unfreundlichen Rezeption zu stören. Kurz geschluckt haben wir dennoch, beim Anblick des kleinen fast winzigen Zimmers. Der Schall der Stadt schien sich durch unsere Fenster ebenfalls nicht beeindrucken zu lassen, aber wir hatten unser eigenes Bad mit Dusche und es war sauber und uns an diesem Abend auch total egal. Die Lage ist fantastisch. 2 Minuten zum Central Park, zur rechten Hand die 5th Ave und links über 2 Blocks zum Broadway. Sämtliche Sehenswürdigkeiten wie der Times Square, Rockefeller Center und Empire State Building,um nur 3 zu nennen, sind wunderbar und in kurzer Zeit zu Fuß erreichbar. Auf das Frühstück kann man gut und gerne verzichten, da man an jeder Ecke in Coffee Shops oder Dunkin Donuts genug Gelegenheiten zum Frühstücken hat. Fazit: Wer ein günstiges Hotel in sehr guter Lage sucht und eigentlich nur einen Schlafplatz in NY braucht, der ist hier genau richtig.

name: Comfort Inn Convention Center
title: “Amazing!”
text: Great value for the price--everything was very clean and well-maintained. Free breakfast in the morning with free juice and coffee served all day. The staff is knowledgeable about the area and very friendly. I'll definitely stay here again!

name: Beekman Tower Hotel
title: “Nice room with a great price”
text: We booked a room through hotels.com for a superior suite and were upgraded upon arrival to a balcony room. The balcony was under renovations but we still had a nice view. The room does show signs of wear but other than one bathroom not being cleaned (which was rectified immediately). The front desk staff was very helpful with suggestions and recommendations. It is a quiet area located by the UN. We would definitely stay here again.

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “Nice Surprise!”
text: How pleasantly surprised I was when I checked into the Milford Plaza last weekend. I have stayed many times before but had not been there since the renovation of some of the rooms. Altho the rooms are still very small, they are smartly decorated. The staff could not have been friendlier and the rooms could not have been cleaner. And the location is still one of the best in NYC! Kudos to the Milford!

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Good price, good location, low quality”
text:
This is the hotel in the center of NY and it has very good price for such location.
So, it has a lot of people there. In result - half an hour queues for check-in, rude staff, inconvenient breakfast area.
Double bed is too small for two people.
No coffee machines in the room.
And... they take money for keeping your bag before check out and after check in ($4 per bag). If you need to keep it before and after - you pay 2 times. I see that first time!
Don't go there. Better to choose some other hotel.

name: W New York
title: “Ultra Cool, Ultra Brainless Staff”
text:
I had reserved a non-smoking room with a Queen bed. I got to the hotel late (around 11:30pm) and checked in. Right before I headed up to the room I asked if it was a non-smoking room, and to my surprise, they had slipped me into a smoking room with two beds! What infuriated me was they did not tell me they had done this, and then insisted that there were "no more rooms available" at the hotel, even though at least ten people checked in while I waited.
I finally insisted that the manager show up, who "tried" to help and I was finally too tired and caved in and took the room. It had been "freshened" up with air freshner, that obviously did not help anything.
Net-net - I wouldn't trust these "reservations" that these hotel chains try to confuse you with, especially these "swank" hotels like the W. I think it could have been that I had reserved with a special rate, and they probably just figured that they would give me the cheapest/useless room that they had for that price.
Buyer beware!

name: Park Central
title: “Great Location and Not Bad”
text: This hotel has a fantastic mid-town Manhatten location. Easy access to the subway right at the corner. Great breakfast place and pizza in the next block. Starbucks in the same building. Staff was very friendly and helpful. They upgraded our King room to a two bed double, which worked much better for us, and there was no additional charge. The rate is very reasonable for what you get. The room was clean and spacious and the beds were comfortable. Quirky elevator system, but once you get used to it, it is no problem.

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “Hotel Holiday Inn 57th Street i New York”
text: Är ett bra och prisvärt familjehotell. Ligger väldigt bra till, nära Central Park och ganska nära Times Square. Inom en kort promenad söder ut på 9:de avenyn ligger det väldigt många bra restauranger att äta kvällsmat på. Ett extra plus för poolen på taket. Finns även en bra frukostrestaurang i hotellet.

name: the Lexington
title: “Genial, céntrico...”
text: Fui a NY a finales de septiembre de 2010 y elegimos este hotel por agencia, esta muy centrico a una manzana del metro mas cercano, a 5 minutos andando de estacion central...el servicio fue estupendo, superlimpio, la recepcion del hotel muy amable y considerada con gente que no domina a la perfeccion el inglés..Volveria a elegirlo sin duda.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “amazing location”
text:
my husband and i stayed here16th-22nd december and if you want some where central to stay then its great!! Yes it needs a major refurb but our room was clean and the bed was comfy. The shower was a little to powerfull but it worked!! The location is amazing, its smack bang in the middle of everything and everywhere. We didnt have much dealings with the staff so i couldnt pass comment on how they were. We had an amazing time in NY and that was partly down to where we stayed! The 1 thing i would reccomend iis tking a pair of ear plugs to sleep with it really is the city that never sleeps!!! We would stay there again.
If your looking for somewhere to crash after exploring NY then this palce is great, it clean central what more could you want???!!!

name: Chelsea Inn - 17th Street
title: “Chelsea Inn - perfect location, basic hotel with good rate.”
