text: My 2nd stay at the Chelsea Inn - I think it's great, perfect location and easy to find. The bathroom sharing is fine, I rarely found it occupied and it was always clean. Don't expect luxury as it isn't and nor is it advertised as such. It's a clean, basic hotel in a great location.

name: Days Inn Hotel New York City - Broadway
title: “Nichts besonderes, aber mit gewissem Charme”
text: Das Days ist o.k., wenn man keine besonderen Ansprüche hat. Das Personal ist nicht gerade herzlich, gibt aber effektive Auskünfte. Die 3 WLANS funktionieren am besten in der Lobby, im Bad ist ein Fön vorhanden. Alle Sehenswürdigkeiten sind durch die naheliegende Subway und den Bus leicht zu erreichen. Entspannen kan man im Central Park oder am Hudson im Riverside Park (jeweils 5 Minuten zu Fuß).

name: Chelsea Inn - 17th Street
title: “Unclean”
text: Although the staff was nice and the location was excellent, the hotel itself was a disaster. We were greeted in our tiny ground floor room by a cockroach. While this is no big surprise in an older building in lower Manhattan, he had a friend who showed up a day later: a large brown mouse (or small brown rat; either way, unacceptable). When it rained the shower drain, toilet, and sink all backed up filling the bathroom with a foul smelling black sludge. Unsettling at 2:30 am, to say the least. we brought all of these details to the attention of the management and they assured us that it was normal (?!). For $225CAD per night it was a terrible deal. One bright spot: it did have a nice free breakfast option from the cafe it was associated with.

name: Chelsea Inn - 17th Street
title: “great service,they help me a lot”
text: the room is very comfortable,and the front desk help me a lot.It is a very nice place.

name: Hotel Carter
title: “Do not go there”
text:
If you have booked to stay at the Carter Hotel, Times Square, New York cancel it now. You would be best staying in the local zoo with the animals. This hotel is shabby, unclean (dirty sheets ironed), a death threat with the electrics and if you are lucky you can have mice dancing on your suitcase.
The owners and staff are oriental and gain the OSCAR for the rudest people in New York. We arrived at 4pm Monday 5 December 2005 and after asking for an alternative room, which was worse than the first one, booked out at 6.20pm. 
Luckily we had american cousins staying in New York that week so had some contacts but otherwise we would of stayed in the train station!!! Not one person in the hotel that I spoke to in 2 hours was happy. Do not stay there is may be cheaper but not worth it.

name: the Lexington
title: “Das Hotel ist ok, aber kein WIFI!”
text: Das Radison hat schon bessere Tage gesehen. Die Zimmer haben doch zum Teil schon grobe Verschleissspuren. Die Lage ist gut. Ich kann nicht verstehen, wie Hotels heute noch ihre Gäste mit Gebühren für WIFI ausnehemen. Wenn ich das vorher gewusst hätte, hätte ich ein anderes Hotel gewählt. Schade. Der Service ist sehr freundlich. Aber es scheint wirklich alles extra zu kosten. Unser Zimmer war noch nicht fertig, da mussten wir dem BellMen 1 Dollar pro Gepäckstück zahlen, damit es für zwei Stunden untergestellt werden kann. Es gibt keinen Teekocher, oder eine Mini-Bar auf dem Zimmer. Für 4 Sterne dürfte dies Hotel eigentlich nicht ausreichen.

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “Holiday Inn liegt in unmittelbarer Nähe”
text: Holiday Inn liegt in unmittelbarer Nähe der wichtigsten Sehenswürdigkeiten. Das Hotel selber ist sehr alt und marode. Wer nur Uebernachten will, ist das Hotel ok. Der Preis zahlt man nicht fürs Hotel sondern für die top Lage.

name: Park Central
title: “Love this hotel.”
text: I stayed here Year ago great service then, and when they found out I was staying again they gave me a cool view, and the room is a little bigger. Drita was really nice to me when I checked in. I can't Waite to come back.

name: Hotel Carter
title: “Chinese lovely staff”
text:
I made my reservation thru internet and I was charged in my credit card for the 3 nights booked, when I was trying to do my check in an old and rude chinese lady told me (in her bad english) that she did not know nothing about it and that I had to pay again, I did it and a few hours later thanks that they have a very gentle an efficient guy (english and spanish speaker)in the staff we could clarify the situation and he made the refund to my credit card.
The room was cleaned only once during my stay.
The problems with the staff continue and in my last night another chinese guy called me at midnight! saying that I had to go to the front desk to clarify some payment issues, because I was sleeeping I said him that wait until the morning of the next day and in a rude tone he accepted, the issue was clarified again in the morning and I was right, he did not apologized for his mistake and the midnight call.
Talking about the room is small but works for a maximum of three nights, AC is noisy but works and the shower pressure is excellent, better that in a five stars hotel, the beds are good and the lining is very good and clean.
In summary if they change the chinese staff the stay will be acceptable and more comfortable! Location is excellent and also the price!

name: The Grant Hotel
title: “Great value!”
text: I was afraid to stay here because of the mixed reviews, but the throwaway price ($190 with tax for 3 nights) convinced me to give it a try. My fear was misplaced. The Grant (also known as The Devon) is one of the best travel bargains I have ever gotten. The room was clean and reasonably appointed (about the quality of an older "motel"). I hate hotel room odors of any sort, and my room ranked way better than average, with only a very slight 'small room' smell that blew off as soon as I cracked the window. The shared bath was modern (more than the room), fully tiled, and well cleaned at least twice daily (again with no smell). The guests seem to consist of mostly young bargain travellers. Book on the Woogo website for the best price. Also search for a coupon (I found one pretty easily). Though the booking process was not flawless, it was resolved by staff pleasantly and efficiently.

name: 254 East Vacation
title: “Very Safe and Quiet are of NYC”
text: My 13 yo daughter went on a one week shopping vacation to NYC. So safety was my primary concern. The area is the Upper East Side of NYC. Most expensive zip code in the US. The #6 train is 4 blocks away, numerous delis and cafe on the way. The hotel itself is on the corner of 74street and 2nd avenue. The manager is on site and easy to reach when I ran out of coffee. The room was actually a 1 bedroom apt. Small kitchen with oven/stove, microwave oven and single cup coffeemaker. The bathroom has a tub, a rarity in NYC apts. We were in the back of building and on the 4th floor so we did not have any noise pollution at night. The only drawback to some other visitors is that the building is a walk up, no elevator. My daughter and I did fine with 3 flight up but next time when I go back with my 65 yo mom I will request first or second floor. Also the apt has windows that open, its important for me as I can't stand hotels that seal the windows. We walked to Central Park and the MOMA every day. We didn't not see any other hotels in area so we felt very lucky to find this little Gem in such a nice residential area. We will be back. No room service or other amenties such as gym or business Center.

name: The Hotel 91
title: “Good place to stay”
text:
Nice, clean, new looking Hotel! 
The area is not the best but it isn't dangerous! 
Good value for the money! 
Good Chinese massage just by the corner! :-)

name: Park Central
title: “Great location, top notch front desk service”
text: I've stayed at this hotel on a number of busines trips to NY. Great location near Central Park and Times Square. Carolyn at the front desk provides excellent customer service, greeting me my name - how often does that happen these days?

name: The Grant Hotel
title: “Surprise, surprise”
text: "When you spend as little as 75 bucks for a night in Manhattan, you get a bit scared and expect the least. But none of it comes true: The Grant Hotel is a positive surprise. The room was very clean and spacious. TV and A/C - now what else do you need? Okay, here's the disadvantage: You have to share the bathroom (which is very clean as well). Now that shouldn't be a problem as long as you are not on a romantic honeymoon trip or stay longer than two or three nights. Staff was very friendly. And if you want to get away from lovely Upper west Side: The subway is just two blocks away."

name: Chelsea Star Hotel
title: “A very good value hotel, clean and safe”
text: Stayed here while working at a convention at the Javits Center. The hotel is a great budget alternative to the larger hotels and chains, and it does its job well. It's very small and no frills (no elevator, room service, etc), but my room was clean and reasonably sized (for NYC at least), the front desk staff were really nice and helpful, the A/C worked well and helped drown out the street noise, and the private bathroom was great. It's got a young, funky vibe to it that I enjoyed (even at a ripe old 42!) It's a 20-minute walk to Javits, there's plenty of garage parking right nearby (and decent free street parking, my car was just fine in one spot for two days) and you'll be steps from Madison Square Garden, with plenty of good, less-expensive restaurants and sub shops around. Stay and enjoy!

name: Chelsea Inn - 17th Street
title: “liked it very much!”
text: easy to find, easy to park and take our bags in. people at the front desk were very friendly! they helped us find restaurants, shops, basically everything. our room was sooo cute, but a bit hot. it got kind of loud one night with the gay bar down the street, but i fell back asleep, so it wasn't bad. it was in a great neighborhood, too. i would definitely recommend! also, the breakfast was delicious!

name: Belnord Hotel
title: “Do yourself a favor...DO NOT STAY HERE!!!”
text: Arriving at a hotel, even a budget hotel, l expect a few things...pleasant staff and a nice pest-free room. Didn't get that here. Instead, I got rude staff and a GOD AWEFUL small room with cockroaches!!! Horrible experience that I hope no one else will ever have to go through!

name: The Grant Hotel
title: “Hotel Alexander NY”
text: Dit hotel is ons erg goed bevallen. Dichtbij de metro zodat je snel de gehele stad kunt verkennen. In een veilige en rustige buurt waar je geen last hebt van langs rijdende auto's. Vriendelijk personeel en erg netjes overal. Wij hebben van onze reis naar New York mede door dit hotel genoten.

name: Park Central
title: “Comfortable hotel in great location”
text:
This hotel is on Seventh Avenue between Times Square and Central Park which makes it a great location for staying in NY. It is clean and in great condition. The rooms are a good size and furnishing are good. The staff are friendly and helpful. There is a restaurant and in the morning a really good value snack bar provides really good value coffee and muffins etc. Nearby the is a great range of deli type cafes that provide fantastic food at reasonable prices.
Have stayed here before and was not disappointed in recent stay and would stay here again.

name: Holiday Inn Express New York City-Wall Street
title: “Expensive and noisey”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel twice in the past, but this last trip was my last. When I made the reservation (2 months prior to travel), the stated rate was on par with similar hotels in the area and I didn't think about it too much. However, on my first night, they slipped a bill under my door intended for the next room, and it was significantly cheaper. Then, a co-worker, who made the reservation a few days before his stay, told me he got the cheaper rate. On checking out (after a mostly sleepless night, for reasons that I will discuss next), I very politely asked the manager to adjust my bill, pointing out the difference in rate and the proximity to our office, with the potential for increased stays. She refused without comment.
Ok, so the rooms are small and the bathrooms are so small that it can be difficult to move around without bumping into things. And the proximity to Water Street and Wall Street means that it is noisey at night. Very noisey. Traffic noises, garbage trucks, etc.
On a positive side, the breakfast, such as it is, is free.
Due to the small hallways, I would not recommend this for people who use wheelchairs.

name: Comfort Inn Central Park West
title: “nice hotel”
text:
Just completed a several nite stay at this Comfort Inn and definitely can recommend it. Decent price for NYC specially if one uses their AAA membership when booking. Staff was very pleasant and helpful. Yes my room was small but for one person it worked. It was clean as was the bathroom. Steps from Central Park. The B and C line subways are next block over. Short walk to Columbus CIrcle. It was nice having a breakfast provided by the hotel. Nothing special-sausages, eggs, pastries as well as apples and bananas are just part of the breakfast. Due recommend trying to get a room as close to first floor as possible. Only one elevator and that can get busy during peak times of the day and walking up the stairs if worn out from a day of roaming NYC can be less then fun but its not the hotels fault there is only one elevator. 
A quiet neighborhood away from the crazyness that can be a place in mid town. Will stay there again in the future specially if the price is decent compared to other hotels in Manhattan.

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Vom Paramount Hotel sind es nur 150 Meter bis zu Times Square und Broadway”
text:
Das Paramount Hotel Times Square in der 46th Steet East befindet sich im Zentrum des Theatre-Destrict. Sämtliche bekannten (und auch weniger bekannten) Musicals werden in einem der vielen Theatern in unmittelbarer Nähe aufgeführt. Neben dem Times Square können viele Sehenswürdigkeiten wie das Rockefeller-Center, das Empire-State-Building, der Centralpark und auch die 5.th Avenue problemlos zu Fuss erreicht werden.
Das Hotel hat eine interessante Lobby leider ohne Tageslicht und für mein Befinden zu wenig ausgeleuchtet. Ebenso dir Flure auf den Etagen. Das Personal war stets sehr freundlich und immer hilfsbereit. Unser Zimmer und das Bad waren sehr klein dafür sehr sauber. Ebenso der Kleiderschrank (inklusive Safe). Die leeren Koffer mussten zusätzlich im schon kleinen Zimmer verstaut werden. Zur Unterhaltung gabs ein Flat-TV mit dem üblichen Hotel-TV und vielen heimichen Sendern und ein Radiowecker. Im gesamten Zimmer war keine Steckdose zum Anschluss eines Ladegerätes vorhanden. Dazu musste die Steckdose des Hoteleigenen Föhns verwandt werden. Auf allen Zimmern gab es WLAN, allerdings nicht in Charge und sehr teuer. Gebührenfreien Internetzugang gab es nur in der Lobby. Dort standen sogar zwei PC gebührenfrei zur Verfügung.
Das Frühstücks-Buffet war ebenfalls sehr teuer, dafür lies es kaum einen Wunsch offen. Im Vergleich zu einem Breakfast im Diner ist es dort sehr viel günstiger. Aber das Angbot und die Atmosphäre im Paramount kann man nicht mit einem Diner vergleichen

name: Best Western PLUS President Hotel at Times Square
title: “Emplacement excellent et chambre sympa”
text: Le Best Western Plus President Hotel se situe à deux pas de l'animation de Times Square (boutique, théâtre, restaurant...). De nombreux métros se trouvent tout près et vous emmènent partout. Les chambres sont sympas et bien décorées mais leur taille est variable : certaines sont vraiment trop petites. WIFI dans les chambres, écran LCD, ascenseur, personnel serviable.

name: Park Central
title: “Park Central Hotel”
text: Reasonably priced rooms and convenient location. We were very pleased with our Park Central experience!

name: Hudson New York
title: “Great location, but....”
text: Rooms are tiny...even the "upgrade" queen room for which I had to pay an extra $40. Cannot imagine how small the regular room was. Bar was closed for renovation and Library bar was overpriced and service was poor. Took 3 hours and 4 phone calls to get our bags delivered and promised extra towel and bath robe never arrived. We were supposed to stay for 5 nights but checked out after 1. When I was checking out ( which took ages because there was only one person at the desk) other guests were complaining about street noise in their room. There are better places to stay....and it took 2 emails and 3 phone calls to get a copy of my bill sent to me because they couldn't provide one at checkout....

name: Holiday Inn Express New York City-Wall Street
title: “Interesting Stay”
text: The hotel is nice in a lot of ways but lacks some necessary things. There is no service elevator so the staff is forced to tie up at least one of the only two elevators to do their work. We waited 15 minutes on one occasion for the opportunity to get down to the street level. It has only five rooms per floor and 26 floors. The staff is nice but unable to help with things like luggage as I had to (gulp!) double park and unload the luggage myself. They do have an arrangement with an obscure parking garage on Cedar Street to park for $30 per night-a steal in lower Manhattan for sure. When I called about these things the person at the desk was always very polite, helpful, and informative, and I appreciate this. The room was small at best but, for the low price, was all that was needed. The only downside to it was that the AC is set to hurricane strength so you are literally blown away by the force. It took a matter of minutes to drop the temp five degrees. I guess I would say that it is overkill to have this much force. We froze ourselves at bedtimes, turned it off, and let the temp creep up as the night progressed. The bathroom is also very small, but has what you need. I thought I saw on their site that they had room safes, but they did not, nor did they have the bellman that are listed. The breakfast area is very nice and all the typical Holiday Inn express items are there. The attendants are very friendly and helpful and make it a good experience.

name: 254 East Vacation
title: “254E Vacation New York”
text:
Appartement assez cosy, gérant sur place très sympa. Bien pour une famille de 4 personnes au niveau de la taille, bien entretenu même si la cuisine est minuscule et ne peut pas vraiment être utilisée.
Deux reproches : le prix, même si la proximité de Central Park peut le justifier, paraît tout de même un peu élevé ... et surtout la souris (!!!) certes mignonne qui a fait quelques apparitions pendant les 4 jours de notre séjour !

name: The Hotel 91
title: “Great find in center of everything you want to see in Manhattan”
text:
We spent a few months looking for an affordable hotel on Manhattan, since most of the things we wanted to do were there. The hotel room was for 4 people, two double beds. The beds were very very comfortable, although the room was very small. We had to take turns walking between the beds. It was right next to the manhattan bridge, but it didn't disturb our sleep in the least, slept perfectly. Down the street from the F train, and alot of other train stops are walkable. Felt very safe walking around the neighborhood as there is always people out, its a very busy area. Its also next to a fish market, so it will smell when you first get out in front of it, but it passes once you walk past the stalls. The main point is that it was very very CLEAN, no bed bugs! Hard to find that in Manhattan!
They also hold your luggage for 2 dollar each the day you leave, which is more affordable then other places across Manhattan.

name: The Grant Hotel
title: “Durchschnittliches Hotel nahe des Broadway & Central Park's”
text: Im Großen & Ganzen war das Hotel okay, ärgerlich nur war der Umstand, dass in der eigenen Dusche permanent lauwarmes Wasser lief...Nach 3-maliger Reklamation tat sich immer noch nichts, immerhin konnten wir auf das Etagenbad ausweichen & da gab es dann doch noch eine heiße Dusche (immerhin war es Winter!!!) für uns...

name: The Hotel 91
title: “A little spooky with good beds”
text: In the depth of Chinatown and its smells. Rooms are spacious but expect stained carpet and barren walls. Four women travelling together with no secondary mirror in room. Adequate bathroom with comfy beds. Bed linen appeared clean. Noticed no sprinkler system in room. OK if you spend absolutely no time in the room other than sleeping.

name: Holiday Inn Express New York City-Wall Street
title: “Good hotel for the price and location”
text:
I have traveled to NYC more than two dozen times and have stayed in 4 and 5 star hotels every time. This was my first experience with a Holiday Inn property in Manhattan.
I was not disappointed at all. 
Parking: parked around the corner for 30.00 a day with hotel stamping the parking ticket.
Location: Great location if you want to be in Lower Manhattan. Walking distance to Wall Street, South Street Seaport, Ground Zero/Freedom Tower site, Brooklyn Bridge". Short walk to Chinatown and Little Italy. 
The hotel was very clean with a nice, smallish, lobby area. The staff was friendly. 
The room was large enough and comfortable for two people (my 16 yr old daughter and myself). The beds were comfortable and there was really no street noise. The only noise complaint I would have is that when people left their rooms, the doors slammed very loudly. Other than that, no complaints. The bathroom was clean and had ample amenities.
There was a small business center with free internet service, which was nice as I forgot my laptop.
The breakfast buffet was decent. Someone mentioned the watery eggs, which I'm sure were just powdered eggs, but they were kind of blah. The small omelettes were decent. Selection of bacon, breads, danishes, muffins, etc....My only complaint is that it was PACKED every morning. The poor guy trying to clean and restock the food really had his work cut out for him....
All in all, this was a nice hotel in a good, safe location and I would recommend if you want to make Lower Manhattan your hub of activity. I did miss being in Midtown, but it was a short subway ride away.

name: The Grant Hotel
title: “Bien compte tenu des prix ailleurs”
text: Chambre au rez de chaussez avec salle de bains commune partagée avec 4 autres chambres : pas de pb SDB propre, 2 chambres non occupées et une en réfection (octobre 2008).A l'avenir ces chambres disposeront d'une salle de bain privée, mais les prix vont augmentés. Dans le Hall, accès à internet (1 dollar / 10 mn) Hotel bien situé, métro à 2 mn, puis 10mn du centre à recommander

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Great location”
text: This place offers you a great location and spacious rooms but the rooms are quite average with old furniture and furnishing. I had to stay here after having stayed at a B&B because of my last-minute extension of stay. I was very dissappointed by the furnishing of the room. It oozed a foul odour and it took me some time to get used to it. But this doesn't bother you, this is a great place to stay at, given its location and room sizes.

name: Best Western PLUS President Hotel at Times Square
title: “hotel best western times square”
text:
Hotel bien situé avec une tres belle entrée design
Le personnel n est pas tres agréable particulierement les femmes de la reception !
surtout quand ils regardent un match de foot à la télé ... et qu ils trainent des pieds pour venir
Evitez les Chambres au 3e sombres et pres de la ventillation de l hotel tres bruillant !
Plus calmes en hauteur et mieux décorées

name: Hudson New York
title: “overpriced shoe box”
text: A beautiful foyer, friendly staff, but tiny rooms, loud aircons - if they work! I was very disappointed and hated every night? The hotel is well located, but horrible to stay in. We upgraded the shoe box to a studio and had to move again because the room was to hot and the aircon did not work. In the second studio, it was too loud and whem we switched it off an aircon outside hummed us awake in the loud room. I expect more for almost 500 usd a night!

name: Chelsea Star Hotel
title: “Chelsea Star - Great location”
text: Great location, slap bang in the centre of Chelsea means you can walk anyway within Manhatten in about 20 minutes. Staff are very helpful and the apartment we had was ok. Cleaning staff were very efficient each day (but wouldn't make beds if you left personal belongings in it). Our apartment was at the front of the building on the second floor and we needed ear plugs to drown out street noise at weekend. Also heating was unreliable and came on at strange times. We were cold occasionally at night.

name: Chelsea Star Hotel
title: “the best hotel in NY!!!!!!”
text: This is a very nice hotel, in a very good location (near time Square, Empire state building, pennysilvania station, near the 34th street). Our room ( asuperior room) was clean, with a large bathroom, air conditioner, flat tv. We had towels changed every day. The staff is helpful, friendly (there is also a girl who speaks italian!): you can use the pc (with 2 dollars you can surf for 20 min. the Net); there's a nice terrace where you can smoke, have breakfast or lunch or everything you want. This is a very good position, central and near the subway (thre's a big station under madison square garden(Penn station) where you can take metro or trains going to Washington, ecc). This is a good solution for people who want to visit the city and not stay in the hotel all the time.

name: The Grant Hotel
title: “"Ottimo rapporto qualità prezzo"”
text: Difficile trovare meglio a questo prezzo. L'Hotel non è in posizione centralissima ma c'è la stazione della metro a 200 mt. e in 10 minuti siete a Times Square. Avevo prenotato una camera col bagno in comune e avevo timore. Devo dire che la camera non era grandissima comunque pulita e il bagno appena fuori era sempre perfetto grazie ad un servizio di pulizia costante e puntuale. Il personale alla reception era molto cordiale e disponibile. Al piano terra c'è possibilità di connessione ad internet.

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “buen hotel, alejado centro”
text: bonitas y muy comodas habitaciones, pero hay que andar bastante hasta la 5ª avenida por una oscura calle. recepcion algo fria, sin posibilidad de desayunos.

name: Comfort Inn Central Park West
title: “Location, Location....”
text: Location, location, location.The Hotel was very central, very close to the main museums, Central Park and to main subway lines. Subway nº 2 or 3 will get you Downtown (wall street) in less than 20 minutes. If you choose to buy a one week metrocard this will cost you 29 dollars and you are allowed unlimited subway and bus rides (even to the airports). Mind you, the rooms were very, very, very small

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “Invalorable ubicación”
text: Si bien es impersonal (más de 1000 habitaciones) y hay una multitud permanente en su lobby, todo funciona a la perfección y está a 2 cuadras de times sq con absolutamente todo a mano, líneas de subway y buses, espectaculos, negocios, etc. buen precio. La mejor relación precio calidad para NY para turismo sin preten

name: Hudson New York
title: “what the hell...is this a dorm room?”
text:
i had just finished a few days with a business group and had a night off to spend in new york. i had heard great things about the hudson and decided to explore it on my own. i booked a standard room and noted the staff seemed simply annoyed with helping the customers. i simply took my key and went upstairs. the room was a closet. my sisters room at Columbia during undergrad was bigger. REALLY. i know that some people speak about value. i agree but seriously when a room is this small, what value are we really talking about? i had not much to really do so i dealt with it. the bed was nice and soft. i dropped down and looked around the bar. the crowd was hip but a bit young. the average age was probably 25. i looked around and was soon bored and ventured out of the hotel for other pastures.
overall, a nice decour but the rooms are small; the staff is testy and the experience was much less than ideal. i will not stay here again.

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “A 3 mn de Times Square”
text: Hôtel bien placé à 3 mn de Times Square, wi fi gratuit a renouvellé tous les jours. les chambres sont petites mais bien décorées et propres. Ascenseur rapide, clavier à l'exterieur de l'ascenseur il suffit de taper le numéro de l'étage et la lettre correspondant à l'ascenseur s'affiche. Dans la rue, on trouve des boutiques de souvenirs et de nombreux théâtres.

name: Paramount Hotel Times Square New York
title: “Hotell Paramount i New York- nära till allt”
text: Mycket bra läge vid Times Square. HAde bokat ett dubbelrum "standard" alldeles för litet för två personer. Vi kunde inte ens ha våra resväskor liggande. Skulle med facit på hand tagit ett större rum. De var nyrenoverade och superfräscha med kanonläge.

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “Angenehm”
text: Das Personal war äußerst zuvorkommend und wir waren sehr zufrieden mit dem Hotel bzw. Zimmer.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Great location and friendly staff”
text:
We stayed at the Wellington Hotel for five nights in December. Considering this is a three star hotel, we were very pleasantly surprised. 
The rooms themselves are clean and well presented, with comfortable beds and a good shower. The hotel looks tidy and clean and all of the staff, from the doormen to the cleaners, were friendly. 
The hotel is in a perfect position on 7th Avenue- in the middle of Times Square and Central Park, and with a subway stop right outside. 5th Avenue is just two blocks away, and most of the big sights are within walking distance. There are also some fantastic little delis nearby, including the famous Carnegie Deli which is just across the road. There's also a cafe and shop downstairs in the hotel. The staff were extremely helpful on our last day, as they arranged for a car to take us to the airport.
We will definitely be staying here again on our next visit to New York.

name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Upper East Side
title: “No tourist activities here.....but fun neighborhood location.”
text:
This property is located on 92nd Street which is pretty far from any tourist activities. It is in the middle of a great/cute residential neighborhood with plenty of local small businesses and about 4-5 blocks from the subway. We felt very safe and met lots of locals as we walked the streets.
The hotel is nothing fancy and very basic. Front desk staff was average; cleaning folks were very nice. Our room was very small (typical NY style) yet clean and comfortable. View of rooftops was okay because we did not spend much time in the room. Cab fare is pretty high from Newark (EWR) airport ($79 + $17 tolls) so try to split a cab with someone else.
If you want to explore another part of the city, away from Times Square, this would be a good alternative. However, the rate that we paid seemed a bit expensive compared to location and what we have paid in the past. (It may have been related to Hurricane Sandy)

name: Chelsea Star Hotel
title: “Great value for money, fantastic location, fab little hotel”
text:
When I read the other reviews I was a little nervous as I had booked online so I rang to double check and all was fine (and I would recommend if you are flying in late at night to inform them as some hotels don't hold the rooms). We arrived at 1am and found it with no problems at all (yes it is a little door in the middle of a street). 
The staff seemed friendly and the place was really clean, lovely and warm (as it was a cold snowy December) and actually reasonably quiet considering it was virtually in the centre. As a female, I didn't find the area dangerous, its great for transport (Penn Station) and Madison Square Garden, the Empire State Building and Macy's are all just a short stroll away. There are some good Irish bars nearby and a 24 hour convenience store (very handy). I would definitely recommend this place but its not really for a corporate business stay. Its more like a really high quality budget hotel and its good if you are in your 20's, early 30's. Not so good for families I wouldn't have thought, but its ideal for a New York shopping break. We had a room with a private bathroom but I saw the shared bathroom and it looked fine. The only bad point I could think of is the smell of baking bread in the corridor (there is a Subway sandwich place next door) and its nice at first but it gets a bit too much after a while, but then its only noticeable in the corridor.

name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel
title: “Great location”
text: Great location....a few steps from Times Square, Central Park and 5th avenue. The staff is ok. The room is good and the hotel has a restaurant on the lobby. Its an old building, but it doesnt matter at all...

name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Upper East Side
title: “Quiet, clean and good value for money”
text: This hotel is located on a fairly quiet street on Upper east side of Manhattan. The reception staff were very friendly and lounge / reception area big and comfortable. There is free wifi in the reception area and in addition 2 computers (+ 1 printer) at disposal for guests. The rooms are very clean and during our 5 night stay we didn't once hear any of the other guests in rooms next door or cleaning staff even though the hotel was fully booked. The room has A/C even though it was fairly noisy to keep on all the time. The hotel also has a fitness and pool which we did not use so cannot comment on this part. Less than 2 minutes walking from the hotel there is a little corner shop that sells anything from painkillers to stamps and fresh exotic fruits.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Great stay!!!!!”
text: We stayed at the Roosevelt over the weekend and it was great. At first I was hesitate to stay due to the recent dissatisfied reviews that were placed. I'm glad we didn't listen to the reviews because we had a great weekend. This was our second time staying at the Roosevelt and the first was also great. The moment you pull up to the curb you assisted with your bags and the car valet parked. We arrived three hours before check in and expected to just have our bags held and do some shopping until check in, but they had a room already available and checked us in immediately. Armondo at the front desk was terrific and a great help. We had drinks in the lobby and the martini's were excellent. Our room was clean and very roomy for NYC. The mattresses are new pillow top mattresses that are super comfy. We were on the 18th floor and had a view of the chrysler building which was nice. When we checked out on Sunday they held our bags and gifts that we bought in a secure room until we regretablely left for the day. From beginning to end we had a great stay at the Roosevelt and would not hesitate to book again. If your looking for a beautiful, clean hotel with a great location choose the Roosevelt you won't be disappointed.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Bates Motel”
text: This is the worst place I have ever seen! Small discusting rooms with old small beds that must never have been replaced in the last century. The bathroom was small and the outlets were cracked and barely held up on the wall. The walls were dirty not even a paint job could help this room. The a/c unit didnt turn on to circulate air and the windows didn't open. The rooms and hallways were dark and scary. I took my teenage daughter and got the hell out of there!! Never stay here if your looking for a decent bed, bathroom, lighting, security, peace of mind, or a nice trip! The pictures online for this Hotel are nothing like what you will be getting. This place is a rat hole!!!

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Great breakfast with Tomas, the best ever server!”
text: My friends and I always stay at the Roosevelt Hotel in New York City when we go there for a long weekend to see as many plays as we can squeeze into the weekend. Almost five years ago, we met Tomas, who served us breakfast. With such good service, we went back two to three times per year to the same hotel and feel like family. We've watched as Tomas' son finished high school and gets ready to attend college. Through Tomas, we've met many people in the hotel and have shared the information with many friends, who are now regularly visiting the Roosevelt and Tomas. One man can make a difference in making a stay in a big city feel so special. We feel like we are treated like royalty at the Roosevelt, all because of Tomas! Stop by there and tell him that the Florida ladies sent you!

name: Broadway Hotel and Hostel
title: “Works for the price”
text:
I stayed in the hostel portion of this place in a two bed per room reservation. The room was dark and somewhat cold with a sink and a locker. There are bathrooms down the hall which for me were always clean and open 95% of the time. 
The staff were all very nice, friendly and helpful. I was cold and kept asking for more blankets, and they gladly gave me as many as I needed. They were not able to control the heat though, so even though the room was chilly, they could not improve it. We had a snowstorm one day, and even then the heaters did not kick into a higher heat, but at least we had power. I heard all of the East coast lost power and thousands were without ANY heat, so I was grateful to have any heat and my six blankets. :-) I also like to be very warm when I sleep, so that's just me.
The kitchen area has a microwave and sink, but no pots, pans, utensils, cups, etc. It's better for making simple things or heating up leftovers. There is a "bar" which serves breakfast and snacks throughout the day which I found helpful. 
The elevator is small and slow, so after you take the trip with your luggage, unless you are way high up or have an injury, it's probably better to take the stairs.
The lounge area downstairs is cozy and great. Lots of seating, it's decorated and designed nicely, there are books for trade or borrowing, internet, three plasma TVs which play news in the morning and movies at night. 
Overall I was content with the hostel. I paid more than I thought it should be, but hostels and hotels were very pricey this fall (2011), so compared to the other prices, it was decent. I would like to see better lighting in the room, and in the halls, but in general it was safe, clean and fine. It's close to the train and many delicious, affordable restaurants and stores.

name: Hotel Azure
title: “HOTEL AZURE-RECOMENDADO”
text: Hotel bien situado y con facilidades para desplazamiento en metro. Por su cercanía a atracciones turísticas y comercio se facilita para desplazamientos a pie. Lo tendré como primera opción para volver. Buena atención en recepción. Un poco pequeña la habitación pero suficiente

name: Hotel Carter
title: “Big trouble in what seems little China”
text: Me and a travelling buddy did NewYork on the cheap big time in November of this year. Much to my personal distress of reading the reviews on this website i was really worried about staying here. If your the type of person (like myself) who is just happy to be in New York this hotel is a bargain. The bed was clean, the shower was hot and the room was warm. If you don't mind the lobby/amusement arcade with flasing neons and mismatch furniture then you will be ok at the Hotel Carter. It was actually quite a laugh taking the p*@# out off the oldest security guard in New York and the location was excellent. Anyway how much time are you going to spend in your hotel room in the greatest city on earth?

name: Holiday Inn Midtown / 57th St
title: “Central beliggenhed Gammelt og slidt men rent”
text:
God og central beliggenhed. Venlig service og rene men slidte rum. Fantastisk udsigt fra vores vaerelse til Manhattan skyline og Ikke mindst til poolen paa taget paa sidebygningen som ogsaa er en del af hotellet
Taet paa laes gaaafstand Central Park Fifth ave Times Sq etc

name: The Time
title: “Expect a budget/value hotel...in need of major renovations”
text:
This is a value/budget-type hotel. If you know that going into it, you'll be fine. However, we expected something different after seeing pictures, etc and we were really disappointed.
My mom booked this hotel for a 4 night stay in NYC. She was really excited about staying in a boutique hotel right near the theaters since we were seeing some shows. The lobby and front desk staff upon arrival were great - I was excited to see the room. And then we arrived to something unexpected. Bare bones room, dirty carpet pulled up from the floor, random items lying around that made it clear it wasn't vacuumed (hair pins, etc), a moldy bathroom with a broken fan (yet very clean toilet), a TV that didn't work, heat that was stuck at a super hot temp, a closet with a broken rod and an ironing board lying on the floor. We asked to switch to a cleaner room, but after the bellman showed it to us, we realized the hotel is just old and in desperate need of repairs. As a minor solve, we actually went down to Old Navy and bought flip flops to use for the shower.
With all of that said, the hotel is super convenient to subways, transportation to the airport and of course the theaters. And the staff was very friendly. If they are able to renovate the hotel, it could be a good future option. But as of now, there are just too many options in NYC to choose from that are nicer.

name: W New York
title: “volveré...”
text: El hotel estupendo, super limpio y el trato agradable, solo un pequeño inconveniente, mi habitación era demadiado pequeña, por lo demas increible, acompañado por una ciudad perfecta.

name: the Lexington
title: “Minidoble con minicama”
text:
Habitaciones - Mi creencia hasta ahora era que una habitacion doble es una habitacion con dos camas y mi experiencia es que cuando mi mujer y yo queriamos habitacion con cama matrimonial habia que pedirlo expresamente. En este hotel no. En el Radisson Lexington la habitacion doble es una minidoble con minicama de 1,40 y si quieres dos camas o una cama "king Size" hay que pagar extra.
Nosotros habiamos contratado 2 habitaciones dobles y no hubo manera de que a mis hijos les dieran una habitacion con 2 camas si no era pagando 30 USD extra / dia. En mi vida me habia pasado
Aparte de eso respecto de las habitaciones:
1) El colchon muy blando
2) Armario tambien "mini", comoda de 2 cajones
3) El baño pequeño, ducha fija en la pared (no de "telefono"), toallas tambien mas bien "mini"
4) Internet en las habitaciones de pago, diga lo que diga la web del hotel. Libre solo en el lobby.
5) Eso si, la tele es de 37'' con cable
El servicio de las habitaciones asi asi, un dia a las 8 de la tarde una de nuestras habitaciones estaba sin hacer.
La planta de fumadores (la 5) es inabitable: nada mas salir del ascensor apesta a tabaco rancio , es muy desagradable. El pasillo de la planta 3 tambien huele mal (En la habitacion no). 
La primera noche nos instalaron en una habitacion con una maquina de aire acondicionado enorme en la patio justo debajo de la ventana: toda la noche la maquina funcionando. Nos cambiaron la habitacion sin problemas pero parece mentira que instalen a nadie en esa habitacion
Aparte de eso el hotel esta muy bien situado y comunicado.
Zonas comunes correctas aunque necesitadas de renovacion.
En conjunto depecionante.
Eso si, la tele
Mi mujer es fumadora pero la planta de fumadores es inabitable: sales del ascensor y apesta a humo rancio.
La primera noche nos instalaron en una habiteacion que tenia y 
 La planta

name: Holiday Inn SoHo New York
title: “Comfortable hotel in a good Chinatown shopping location.”
text:
I stayed here with my dad and sister for three nights in November. I'll be honest and say that I stayed at the hotel because I used Priority Club points and it was the only one with 2 beds at the time I booked it, however I had never stayed in the Soho area, so I wanted to give it a try. 
Check in was a little long due to all of the FEMA personnel checking in, but once it was my turn, Tiffany was very helpful and got us checked in quickly. The hotel has a restaurant and lobby lounge, which 2 drinks were $26.00 (yikes) which we drank while we were checking in. I didn't eat the food, but my dad said he had a sandwich and it was excellent. 
We stayed up on the 9th floor. The elevators were pretty quick and we never had to wait too long.
The rooms were all recently refurbished and we stayed in a jr. suite with a view of part of the city. Not a great view, but pretty nice. The room itself was spacious with two double beds, a desk, and a couple of nightstands. The bathroom was spacious with a tub/shower and a decent size vanity. Bath and Body bath amenities were provided, which was nice, but they're really small, so for three people if you are using them, you definitely need more. (I brought my own) There was no mini fridge in our room and there was a one cup coffee maker. Breakfast was not included in our rate. 
The location was EXCELLENT if you are interested in shopping in Chinatown or walking around Soho, Little Italy or even the Wall Street area....it is somewhat of a long walk down to lower Manhattan, but it's doable. The hotel is right above the subway station and yes, you can hear the trains coming in and out. It was noticeable, but not necessarily bothersome. I loved the fact that we could run down and do some shopping and come right back up to drop it all off and do it again. The subway is also close by. (less than 5 minute walk) The hotel is also less than 2 miles to the South Street Seaport. 
The staff was friendly, the bellman was helpful in getting us return car service to Newark airport. 
I would recommend the hotel to people who are interested in staying in the Soho area but for the regular price of a room here, I'd probably stay closer to Midtown if given the choice.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Fab location”
text:
We choose this hotel because of the fab location, ten minutes walk (if that) to times square and five minutes walk to central park. There is a subway stop right outside. We arrived about 3pm and checked in straight away, very helpful staff and bell boy took our bags up to the room and made sure it was all ok for us. Small corner room which was nice as we had two windows to look out. We were on The fifth floor and did hear traffic noise. Not enough to bother us as we slept well after all the walking around but may bother lighter sleepers. Small bathroom but cleaned daily and towels replaced. Good shower and hot water. Bath big enough for me to take a bath but not my fiancee! Air con unit in the room lovely and cold after the heat of the city, but couldn't be manually turned off and was a little noisy. It did turn on and off automatically. Room clean but tired decor.
Never had more than a minutes wait for the lift but may have been a problem if you were on a higher floor. 
All in all I would stay at the hotel again. A good price, great location and clean with helpful staff!

name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel
title: “Good value, excellent staff....”
text: My wife and I and our 14 year old granddaughter stayed at the Hotel Manhattan through arrangements with a corporate travel agent based on location to theatres and midtown activities. It was an excellent choice. The hotel was well managed, the staff was knowledgeable and personable, the location was wonderful. Even thogh the internet access left a bit to be desired -- no wireless access in the room -- I have no difficulty in recommending this hotel to friends and associates.

name: the Lexington
title: “pied à terre new yorkais”
text: idéalement situé sur Lexington avenue, à quelques blocs du Chrysler Building et de Grand Central. Bel hôtel années 1930 en briques, doté d'un luxueux lobby et d'ascenceurs aux portes plaqués or!! Bon restaurant italien.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Dated but good location”
text: There were so many bad reviews on this hotel that I was reluctant to book it. But knowing that we would spend more time outside than in the hotel and having two teenage boys we needed to keep our expenses down. The hotel is in an excellent location. You step out of the hotel and to your right a 5 min walk is central park and to the left another 5 min walk and you are in time square. My boys were comfortable walking around on their own 15 and 16 years old. There are lots of places to eat on the street including lots of food street carts. The subway station is right beside the hotel. The hotel itself is clean. We had a one bedroom suite. It was surprisingly very big. It had a kitchen with a bar fridge, microwave and fridge. No plates, dishes, cutlery, kettle or coffee maker - although there are so many places to eat in - eating was expensive and it would have been nice to at least have a cup of coffee in the morning in the hotel room. We had clean towels everyday. The queen size bed was comfortable. There was a pull out queen size bed also that was very old and uncomfortable - we also requested a roll away bed that was okay. The bedding in the rooms are your typical motel style. With a blanket and a bedspread which I don't know how often get washed. The staff were very helpful and no problems at all there - when requested an additional blanket it was up in my room within 10 minutes. We were on the 6th floor so there was no view which didn't really matter to us cos we were out the minute we woke up and got back very late each night. It was also quiet no noise at all. The bathroom was small and the water in the shower was a little annoying - very cold water would come out in spurts while the hot water was on. This would be a great hotel for families with teenagers and kids but then again I don't know why anyone would take little kids to NYC its just way to busy for little ones.

name: Hudson New York
title: “So much to love and a few things to dislike”
text:
I almost hate to give an "average" overall rating because there were so many thing I loved about this hotel. The staff is wonderful. So friendly. So responsive. Alex welcomed me upon check in and explained the various bars, restaurants, etc. and the neighborhood. I felt welcome and happy to be there. In addition the library bar, the night club, and especially the Sky Terrace are all wonderful and provide such a nice variety of venues for different people and moods. Hands down my favorite time spent at the hotel was relaxing on the sky terrace. What a unique spot in NYC! Outside on the 15th floor, there are many plants, comfortable oversized couches, chairs, lounge chairs, even a hammock. The staff there was friendly, helpful, and accommodating. When I had problems (see below), Olivia, a manager whom my friend spoke to, and Zander were all responsive and kind. The lobby is gorgeous and the location (near Columbus Circle and Central Park, right on the #1 train) is ideal. 
The downside? The rooms are incredibly small. I realize all NY hotel rooms are relatively small and one has to adjust their expectations, but for the price it was disappointing. The space between the wall and the toilet was uncomfortable and would not be accessible for many. On the second morning, my friend woke up with a couple of bites which she suspected might have been bed bugs. She called and management agreed to upgrade us, which they did to a much larger room (with a sofa and much bigger bathroom and closet area). That room was lovely and I appreciated their responsiveness to the issue. We did not get any more bites while we were there thank goodness. My only other complaint was that the wireless internet was horrible. I could not access my e-mail for most of the weekend. When I called their tech support, she suggested I go sit by the door where the signal was stronger. When that didn't work, I never got a call back.
This is a great, trendy, beautiful New York hotel. You will enjoy the amenities, location, and staff, but not the room. But, since you spend little time in a NY hotel room, I'd say it's worth the stay!

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “Localização privilegiada”
text: O local é saída´fácil para tudo, rodoviaria perto, Times Square perto, restaurantes otimos por perto, lojas perto.....muito confortavel, quartos velhos, mais limpos....pontos a melhorar...os carpetes são muito velhos e o front desk tem poucos atendentes para a demanda do Hotel...Ah, o Concierge é insuportavel de gente, vc perde a vontade de uqerer se informar.

name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel
title: “Once In A Lifetime”
text:
Stayed here 28/04/12 - 03/05/12
My first impression was a great hotel the rooms were cleaned every day and they had also replenished the coffee for the coffee maker, Beds changed and fresh towels. One thing I was slightly disappointed with was the selection of TV channels as at the end of a long day just to relax not much on offer but hey it’s the city that never sleeps!! I also gave the swimming pool a try and having worked at the Hilton hotel livingwell health club for over 2 years I was surprised by the colour of the pool it is in real need of an upgrade and filter clean and as far as the supervision not impressed at all. Also it did lack a bar for residents just to relax and have a chat
The staff at the hotel are the friendliest and I had the pleasure of chatting to Tom the Bell Captain and Jean and Eddie. Now Tom the Bell Captain and Gene one of the bell hops are CREDIT TO THE HOTEL the hotel are very lucky to have them friendly, polite and very very good at their job them alone I would come back in a heartbeat

name: The Time
title: “Awesome Location!”
text: My parents came to NY to visit and luckily I was able to book a last minute reservation for them at The Time Hotel. Mr. Katz was extremely helpful and accommodating, he promised to take great care of my parents and kindly had Gilbert escort us up to their room. The rooms were small but extremely clean and cozy. We had drinks at the hotel bar which was super hip and trendy and dinner at Serafina (food was soso). The location of the hotel is right in the heart of Time Square, my parents felt safe in the area with blaring lights, horns and tall buildings. Overall their experience was exceptional and it all stems from their initial hotel experience. I'd definitely recommend The Time Hotel to friends and family visiting.

name: Empire Hotel
title: “great location and staff”
text: We came into town to see a show and decided to stay the night.The location is the best feature, it's a short walk from Columbus Circle so there are several subway trains you can use, and it's right across the street from Lincoln Center. The rate I got on Priceline was pretty good. Rooms in older buildings are going to be small, there is no getting around it. I agree with others, the shower half-wall is not practical. The mini-bar items are horrendously expensive. $9 for a bottle of water? When NYC tap water is among the best water you can get? We checked in at 5pm on a Saturday, went right out, were back around midnight, and before 8AM Sunday there was a bill slipped under the door for several mini bar items that we hadn't used--even if we had used any, how would they have known during that timeframe? I wouldn't expect any staff to enter the room on a Saturday night unless I asked. The front desk staff took care of it right away but I have to wonder how and why that happened. Being cynical I can only say "Nice Try"...I also agree with an earlier comment about there being no flat sheets on the bed-so it's a comforter or nothing. In NYC rooms tend to get dry and stuffy, but then the A/C is blowing right on you as the rooms are so small. Having a top sheet would be more comfortable. The bar is attractive, and there is a mezzanine above where you can take your drink & people watch, and some of them are entertaining to watch! The rooftop pool area closed at 10pm so we weren't able to check it out.I would stay here again if I couldn't get a different hotel for the same $$ or less, but I would check availability at other properties I have used in the past first.

name: Beekman Tower Hotel
title: “ottimo hotel”
text: Hotel bello in zona tranquillissima, stanze grandi con cucinino privato, ottimo se non si vuole andare sempre al ristorante. Metropolitana a 10 minuti di cammino, Times Square e Grand Central Station raggiungibili a piedi, tantissimi posti dove mangiare nelle vicinanze, vari grocery aperti 24ore, bancomat ovunque. Nota negativa il costo di internet a multipli di 24 ore è assurdo, meglio sarebbe pagare a ore visto che per l'email bastano pochi minuti. A parte questo, da consigliare.

name: Amsterdam Court Hotel
title: “Great Deal, Great Location, Will Stay Again”
text:
Amsterdam Court Hotel is located almost in Times Square. The rooms are small (10x10). The bathroom was a good size. Even though the room was small there was plenty of closet space to unpack and we stored our suit cases above the bed. The bed was super comfy. The a/c unit could have been a little bit colder, I wouldn't want to stay in dead heat of the summer but while we were there it was good enough.
The room was cleaned constantly, we always had fresh towels and everyone was really nice.
My only small complaints would be the a/c could have been colder and 1 of the elevators broke down. However, the elevator was fixed within a few hours and there was an alternate elevator not far from it.
I will stay here again and I definitely recommend staying.

name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text: Friendly staff, clean comfortable rooms and in the center of the action of NYC. There is free internet in the lobby, but not the room. Safe in room is large enough for a laptop. 4 short blocks to Time Square, 1 block from the NYC tourist office, 4 long blocks to Rockefeller Plaza and hundreds of restaurants within walking distance. The double decker bus stop is only a block from the front door.

name: Bedford Hotel
title: “Location Location Location”
text:
One thing I have found booking through Trailfinders is that they will always find you a hotel centrally located, which saves both time and money during your stay. The Bedford is one such hotel. An unprententious entrance and small lobby comprising of a reception desk, small seating area, and two lifts. Described as boutique, our room on the 10th was slightly faded from its' best, but warm, comfortable and adequate if not luxurious. The kitchen area was limited and the electric rings lethargic in operation - so slow we used the coffee machine when we wanted hot water for a drink. Apart from that there were two TVs, copious hot water with choice of bath or shower, a 6' wide bed which creaked but was comfortable, and controllable airconditioning units. 
The hotel has no restaurant as such, but Blooms on the corner of Lexington (30 seconds from the front door) has an excellent choice of full breakfasts for $10-12 including OJ and Coffee. 
Location of this hotel is simply superb. The Airport Express bus to Grand Central sets down within 100 yards of the front door ($15.50 single to JFK, $27 return). Subway are buses are as close, and 42nd Street is 2 minutes away. The Chrysler Building is on teh next block in Lexington, and you can walk to the Empire State in 15 minutes (you can see it from the back of the hotel). Having access to Subway lines 4,5,6 at Grand Central, together with cross line 7, means that you can be anywhere in Manhatten in around half an hour - fantastic!
Staff are really helpful and although they were full and could not gives us a late late checkout on the day we were leaving (with a 10.30pm flight) they were only too happy to let us hang onto our room until 2pm free of charge so we could return and grab a lunchtime shower and change of clothes.
I guess this is something of a phobia, but the only thing that worried me a little about is that the floor area is small, and it spreads up over 17 floors with around 8-10 rooms per floor with a lift and stair shaft down the middle. In an old building such as this, I am always happier if there is more than one way down in the event of a fire, or there is an external fire escape route evident. However all rooms were fitted with sprinkler systems!

name: Hotel Carter
title: “Che squallore, sono fuggito!”
text:
Posizione ottima, proprio in centro a due passi da Time Square. PUNTO. Finiscono qua tutte i possibili apprezzamenti per questa struttura squallida.
Hall desolante e sporca, datata e decadente. Le camere non sono da meno, pulizia inesistente, vecchie e rivoltanti. Le lenzuola macchiate ed i cuscini ormai di una tonalità giallo/marrone sotto le federe hanno fatto si che al mattino dopo decidessi di andare via con 3 giorni di anticipo alla ricerca di una struttura più dignitosa. Tutto questo alla modica cifra di 180$ a notte.
Assolutamente da evitare.

name: Bedford Hotel
title: “Nice Central Location”
text: The Bedford Hotel on East 40th Street and Lexington is located in a nice cental location and is an ideal base for shopping and theatre going expeditions. The hotel is somewhat old fashioned and lacks some of the amenities we have come to expect with more modern Hotel chains however because of its location and inexpensive prices I would recommend this hotel

name: The Time
title: “Nice hotel on a great location”
text: We booked at the last minute just for one night. What a great choice this was. The rooms are nice and well appointed. The front desk staff is very cordial, efficient and accomodating. What a location this place has Broadway, Time Square you are a block away from the center of NYC. We have found our new home base when going to NYC!

name: The Time
title: “My time at The Time”
text: Great hotel, very nice employees! You get the newspaper every morning, and every evening you get a card with the next day's weather. To be honest, there are 2 reasons why I love it the most.. first, it has the most comfortable beds I've ever seen! Second, it's right off Times Square.. so if you're there for the shopping, theaters and museums, or anything else for that matter.. you are withing walking distance of almost everything. They also have a small gym for those that like to keep in shape even when they are away.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “I DONT STAY HERE MORE”
text: The Place is good but the Hotel is terrible....old,

name: Beekman Tower Hotel
title: “bonne surprise”
text: En ouvrant la porte, ce n'était pas une chambre mais un mini studio avec cuisine tout équipée, salon, chambre et salle de bain séparée... Localisation super, à 5mn du premier métro qui dessert de nombreuses lignes et présence de nombreux restaurants très sympas proche de l'hôtel Très pratique, très confortable, nous le recommandons vivement!!!

name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel
title: “An interesting family hotel in Manhattan”
text:
It is very interesting to find a family hotel in the middle of Manhattan. It is my third visit in three years and on my each stay I had noticed that mainly families preferred this hotel more than business people. Half of the people around you are children from all of the world, which shows that it is mostly preferred by the families. 
The location of the hotel is very central for the visitors.
Central of many interesting activities. A couple block to the Central Park, close to many theaters. 
It is a very good family hotel run by the Starwood hotel group.

name: Beekman Tower Hotel
title: “un appartement bien placé au coeur de manathan”
text: situation idéale pour cet hotel à 5/10min à pieds du métro et avec le bus au pied de l'hotel qui mène au métro ou directement à Time Square. Appartement 1 Queen room superior: très grand, déco un peu kitch mais très propre (ménage nickel et draps changés chaque jour). à 2 pas de l'ONU, quartier sympa, avec commerces de proximité et super resto pour le petit déj juste en face; très beau bar resto au dernier étage mais cher Vue superbe sur la ville ou sur la rivière. un super bon plan pour New york (emplacement et surface) avec le charme de l'art déco en plus

name: The Time
title: “brilliant ,,,,”
text:
we stayed at the time july just gone i was travelling with my two kids yrs and 12yrs
everyone was so accomodating ..the aircon wasnt working when we first arrived and another was put in our room within 15min : ))) it just got better from there ..the location is awsome time square is a 3min walk ...you are really in the heart of new york thanks to all the staff that kep us smiling when we returned exhuasted after a day seeing the sites 
carolyn daniel and kiera

name: Comfort Inn Central Park West
title: “Preis-Leistungsvehältnis stimmt”
text: Das Hotel liegt wirklich direkt am Central Park und man kann viele Sehenswürdigkeiten zu Fuß erreichen. Trotzdem ist es schön ruhig. Die Zimmer sind sehr klein, aber in Ordnung. Das Frühstück ist reichhaltig.

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “BIEN SITUE MAIS BRUYANT”
text: Hotêl très bien situé tout près de Time Square mais très bruyant dans les étages inférieurs (j'étais au 5ème) car pas de double vitrage. Chambre et salle de bain très propres. Personnel pas très accueillant. Très long pour avoir un ascenseur car beaucoup de monde. Choisir un étage élevé. Pas de petit déjeuner dans l'hôtel mais beaucoup de possibilités aux alentours.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “I come back”
text:
Before booking I informed with friends and never created a great expectation. The hotel is not very clean but offered what we needed. A good bed to sleep, cabinets and a bathroom that works. 
The internet wirelles is poor.
The service was good and location is excellent. 
If you go back to NY I will be there.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Great location... everything else was decent.”
text:
My friend and I stayed at the Wellington for two nights in May 2012 for a weekend trip to NY to celebrate my birthday. We made our reservation through Bookit.com, which admittedly may have been part of our problem. A few weeks before we left, my friend broke her leg, so we had hoped to switch the bed in our room from a Double to a King, so that we would have a little more space. Unfortunately, the hotel and the site both gave me the run around, so we couldn't make a change. 
With that said, the hotel is in a great location... within a few blocks from broadway, just across the street from Carnegie Hall. Upon arrival, we were greeted by a friendly bellman who gave us tips on places to eat, and advised not to walk down to the location where we'd be attending a concert that night.
The rooms are small, and a bit antiquated. Our shower was broken the first night, but we informed the staff and they did fix the problem promptly. 
It would be hard for me to categorize this hotel as anything but average. It was clean, in a good location, and we got a good price ($262/night before taxes), so I can't complain much, but I wasn't overwhelmed by my experience.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Can't Complain Great Location”
text: Stayed at the Wellington Hotel for a business trip. Though yes things were a little out dated and yes the room my be smaller than the average room I felt that for the money paid was very fair given the general location. I did quite a bit of walking so it was nice to have things so close. Also you save on taxi fare. I guess the only issue I would say I had is the mattress was a little hard but overall I was happy with the stay.

name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel
title: “fantastic location...........”
text:
just got back this morning after staying 4 nights,hotel is in perfect location for everything,
if you like staying in nice clean hotels then the manhattan is not the place to stay?????....
the room really needed some domestos, and a complete gutting lol... wallpaper was filthy and peeling off the carpet was dirty and bathroom rotten and just smelt really musty........
the hotel has no bar which is a shame, you can get a breakfast in the hotel but will cost you $25.00 just for 2 pieces of bacon and 2 eggs and if you want beans,toms,toast they will charge you $5.00 each item extra lol...... what a rip off. if you walk just 2 mins next to hotel theres lots of cafes where you can get full english and as much coffee you want for $10.00.

name: The Hotel 91
title: “nice beds in China Town”
text: Good value for the money; clean and comfortable beds. Free internet, close to the subway, sounds from outside was suprisingly low. Perfect place to sleep at after a day of shopping or seightseeing in NY.

name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel
title: “Great location”
text: Had a great stay, was in the city to see a play. Room was a good size for Manhattan and you can't beat the location on 7th ave, a few blocks from Times Sq. Check in was a little slow but all the employees I encountered were courteous and helpful. The discription for parking says Valet, but its a standard parking garage located half a block away, which was fine. Also only $45.00 for overnight which is pretty good in that area.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Great Location to explore NYC”
text:
Our first time to NYC and our first time to America as well. After a ton of research on the web (and mainly tripadvisor.com!) I choose this hotel because of location and budget. I took my girlfriend (whom is now my fiance - i proposed in Shakespeare's Garden - Central Park) as she had always wanted to experience the Big Apple! 
We stayed for 7 nights in a queen size room on the 7th floor. Our room was okay but not very romantic, but it meant we could spend more on the sights of New York City.
Being from Australia i noticed a few things that i found odd - 
1. No switches on the powerpoints (which i think is a bit dangerous)
2. When you flush the toliet the bowl fills half way up ( which i think is a waste of water considering we're trying to conserve water!)
3. There are heaps more people out once the sun goes down!
4. Initially I found the locals quite rude but please remember that you are a tourist and they see them all day everyday and they actually like it if you treat them the same way!
If your on a budget this is a great place to stay to simply sleep for few hours and then continue exploring this amazing city. 
We're keen to go back ASAP!
Cheers Stephen
P.S Our computer died only a few weeks ago and we lost all our New York photos which is quite shattering but a lesson learnt -keep a duplicate of all digital photos if not 3+ sets.

name: Amsterdam Court Hotel
title: “Would Never Stay There Again”
text: After calling days before our arrival to verify that we would indeed have a room with two twin beds we were told upon arrival that all they had was a room with one king bed but after some delay they said that they would send up a roll-away bed. The roll-away was so saggy in the middle that sleep was next to impossible and the king bed was not much better. The room temperature was extremely cold but we were told that the thermostat was central to the entire hotel and they could not adjust it for one room. That was the first night. It was late so we went to bed. The next morning after complaining again about the temperature they reluctantly said that they could possible bring a portable heater to the room. This should have been suggested on the first night. The 24 hour coffee was non-existent since the machine was broken. We never saw the sunny reading room that was advertised. On our last day we went to the complimentary breakfast to find one bagel left, no milk for the coffee, and no one around to help us. I would never stay here again and would be reluctant to stay at any of their sister properties.

name: Comfort Inn Central Park West
title: “Alles eine Sache des Preises”
text:
Frühstück: Super süß und kalorienreich, in Deutschland könnte ich das nicht jeden Tag essen, oft hat man gegen halb 10 schon das meiste nicht mehr bekommen! Außerdem musste man oft Schlange am Buffet, und noch schlimmer, für einen Sitzplatz stehen! Das nervt!
Personal: Super freundlich und immer hilfsbereit, echt top!
Zimmer: Klein, eng, old school. Nicht zu vergleichen mit dem Eindruck der Lobby oder der offiziellen Fotos des Hotels.
WiFi/W-Lan: Nicht etwa im Zimmer! Das geht nämlich nicht mal richtig im 5. Stock! Und das Hotel hat 14 oder 15 Stockwerke! Da muss man sich schon in die Lobby setzen!
Im Großen und Ganzen hat's der Service gerissen! Ich vermute, wegen Frühstück und Zimmer, dass das eben New Yorker Standart ist, ich konnte es leider bisher nicht mit anderen Hotels vergleichen. Denke für das Geld ist es ok! Hat man mehr, kann man sich ruhig ein paar Sterne mehr gönnen, schätze für seine Sterne durchaus brauchbar, aber nicht an europäischen Standarts zu messen!

name: Belnord Hotel
title: “Top Preis/Leistungsverhältnis”
text:
Dass Belnord Hotel liegt an der Upper West Side in einer ruhigen, trotzdem mit allem wichtigen ausgestatteten Gegend, unweit des Central Parks.
Zimmer sind wirklich winzig, dafür sauber und mit allem wichtigen ausgestattet, auch eigenes Bad/Dusche- in dieser Kategorie in NY nicht selbstverständlich.
Für kleinere, 3-4 tage andauernde Aufenthalte optimal, für länger würde ich größere Zimmer beanspruchen.
Trotzdem ein Hotel, dass man vorbehaltlos weiterempfehlen kann und ich wohl nochmals buchen würde.

name: Amsterdam Court Hotel
title: “no frills-great location”
text: The best thing about the place is it's ideal location near all theaters, restaurant row, etc. The rooms are quite small-(although VERY clean) and the lobby and hallways are dark and dingy. The breakfast was held each morning in a small hallway-like area which was very crowded. The hallways and public areas were un-air-conditioned and the elevator was....quirky-with no visible inspection certificate either. I used the stairs. Hot water was intermittent and the pipes rattled noisily on those rare occasions when you could get the shower temperature just right. Internet service didn't really work most of the time. Try to get a room on the 4th floor or above to avoid a "view" of a brick wall! The staff's attitude ranged from mildly rude to quite friendly; they seem to be refurbishing a restaurant area. Basically, it's a place to leave your things and sleep while you stay in NYC.

name: Bedford Hotel
title: “Great choice!”
text:
When my husband and I travel we look for the very best deals possible. Going to NYC, I thought we'd be out of luck on bargain hotel. After extensive (seriously obsessive) research for hotel locations, amenities and prices I stumbled upon the Bedford Hotel. The decision to book the stay was nerve wracking but I did it anyway after reading some good reviews on TripAdvisor. What a relief it was when we arrived! The public transportation from LaGuardia really was simple. The hotel is 2 blocks from Grand Central so the location was perfect. We arrived on a Sunday afternoon so the normally busy business district was quiet but there was a fabulous street fair a block away. We ate our dinner at several different ethnic food vendors. The rest of our week was very busy and having a cool safe place to return to for rest was such a blessing. 
So, for the actual review...the staff were so attentive and helpful. The desk clerk loaned us his umbrella on a rainy day! The lobby was beautiful and clean. The elevator worked great (yipee!), halls were well lit and nicely furnished. Our room was very roomy. The furnishings were nice and new. The bathroom was clean and the view was incredible! 
My husband returned to NYC a few months later and booked his stay at the Bedford with no hesitation and with the same results.

name: Hotel Carter
title: “Aceptable por su costo y inmejorable ubicación”
text: El hotel es antiguo, tiene habitaciones viejas. Cuenta con 3 ascensores que abastecen bien la gran capacidad de huespedes del hotel (tiene 700 habitaciones). La habitación estaba limpia, y la limpian día por medio. Tenía aire acondicionado y un TV Lcd con pocos canales disponibles. El baño era un poco más moderno y estaba bien. El hotel en lineas generales es aceptable por su bajo costo frente a otros hoteles en NY, y su ubicaciòn es inmejorable ya que está a 1 cuadra del Time Square. Como negativo destaco que el wi fi era pago, y que cobraron x cuidar las maletas hasta que la habitación estaba lista para ingresar. No compren excursiones en el sector de turismo porque es todo bastante más caro. Igualmente en un viaje de "bajo costo" volvería a alojarme allí sin dudas.

name: Bedford Hotel
title: “It was o.k....”
text:
Three of us went to NY and stayed at the Bedford, recommended to us by an internet hotel company. As there were 3 of us, we booked a 'suite', which had a separate bedroom, with kitchenette as well. We thought this would be ideal.
Like all other reviews, I have to also say that the location was excellent, although we did find ourselves 'raising our eyebrows' when we saw it all behind the scaffolding.. First impressions were not great! The lobby looked lovely, but the rooms really looked grotty, but then again, they were clean.
I found the staff to be extremely nice and helpful. When we arrived, we found that the room configuration didn't suit us (double bed in the bedroom, and a double pull out couch in the sitting room - as we were 3 women, we each wanted our own beds), so they immediately changed us to a different suite which had 2 single beds in the bedroom, and the double pull out couch in the sitting room. 
The 'kitchen' is literally a sink behind a folding cuboard door, and has a fridge and coffee machine. It was fine. All we wanted really, was the fridge & coffee machine - we knew we wouldn't be cooking so this suited us.
The bathroom was very small and very dated - the grout between the tiles falling out etc, but it was clean. Towels &sheets changed every day etc. The products weren't great, but being women this wasn't a problem as we brought our own.
The one MAJOR downfall for us, was that the bathroom was off the bedroom, which meant that the person sleeping in the sitting room had to come into our bedroom in the middle of the night, which was really not the ideal situation. 
I was surprised to read in another review that they were able to order taxis to the hotel - They would not do this for us, and told us to go out on the street and hail one ourselves. When it was a different man behind reception, we asked would he do it, and again, he wouldn't. Because of this, and 'rush hour' we missed our dinner reservation, and for the other nights, we had to stand on the street a lot earlier to make sure we got there in time. They did however book an airport shuttle for us, which was very convenient. Also, they did allow us to keep the room until 3 p.m. on our day of departure which was very convenient for us. 
The first night as we were so jetlagged, we asked them to recommend a restaurant that was close. They did book us at the Italian restaurant around the corner, but I wouldn't recommend it. The food was nice, but minuscule portions and we were starving afterwards, devouring all the bread and fighting over the breadsticks! and the price was astronomical for what we had - we were studying the bill for ages just to make sure there were no mistakes! (It cost us $80 per person!!!!)
Back to the hotel - No complaints really, except the bathroom situation, but if it's a central location you are looking for without paying a huge price, and if it's only for sleeping, this is the ideal place.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “need of an update, but clean”
text: we have just got back from new york and we stayed in the pennsylvania.
