I was a bit worried after reading all the reviews , most of them not good. however we did enjoy our stay there,not because the hotel was luxurious but because of the great location .It was a few minutes from macys, the empire state building was just around the corner ,10 mins from times square and all the theatres,everything was within walking distance .The hotel is quite dated and shabby in places but although the room was a bit dark and old fashioned, the beds were clean and our bathroom had been updated with new toilet,basin and shower also newly tiled.It was not somewhere we had planned to spend alot of time in anyway so it served its purpose for us.The view from our window was a bit depressing though ,we were just facing other windows in the hotel and with the building being quite high (17 storeys ,I think.) we couldnt tell what sort of day it was outside as it always looked a bit dull and dark ( even though it was glorious sunshine) .I kept the curtains shut all the time ! The maids came in every day and changed the towels , which were lovely and white and made the beds , the check in was fast and efficient , overall our stay there was good but if you are looking for luxury this is not the place for you.

name: Park Central
title: “Excellent place to stay in NYC”
text: Excellent hotel, excellent location and helpful staff. First off I don't need alot of hotel staff support, really just on check-in. I'm really just interested in the hotel room and location and those were excellent. The room was nice and nicely decorated, though it was a pretty small.

name: Bedford Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text:
I stayed at this hotel with my Husband we stayed from the 26th November for 6 nights. After reading some reviews on trip advisor i felt like cancelling our holiday. Those people who have booked this holiday and have not went yet dont get to worried on the reviews. If your looking to go to New York on Holiday you wont be going there to stay in your hotel all the time. Believe me you will only be in your hotel to sleep. We stayed in a 1 bedroom suite and it was basic. A bit dated but it was clean. The bed was comfortable and huge the suite was big. There are loads of cupboards to keep all your shoppong in. The location of this hotel is excellent you are near everything 5 mins to 5th avenue. and 10 mins to Times square. Two blocks away there is a park and there is an ice rink and little market shops were you can buy all kinds of stuff. It is open till late.
The hotel staff were friendly and very helpfull and the doorman is allways there to help but dont forget to tipp him. When we arrived we were allocated are room which i asked for a high floor and no smoking but i was given a smoking room so i called down to reception and they sent up the doorman with a new room key from a room on a different floor this time it was no smoking there was nothing that was to much trouble for the staff. Here is a little tip for you for transfering from the airport to the hotel dont get a taxi they are anything from $40 to $70 if you go out of the airport main entrance ther is a coach they drop you off at your at different locations through manhatten it is $15 single or $27 return and they pick you up and take you back to the airport so you wont spend alot on your transfer you will have more money to spend when your shopping. The bus terminal is round the corner from this hotel about 2 mins walk. Well i hope everyone has a fantastic time in the big apple like we did. I will deffentley be back to The Bedford Hotel again i would strongly recomend this hotel. The only down side of it all is that you have to come home and come back to reality.

name: Belnord Hotel
title: “Empfehlenswert nach Umbauende”
text: Das Hotel hat eine gute Lage für Leute, die nicht mitten im Trubel sein müssen. Die Upper West Side ist eine sichere Wohngegend und da die Subway nur einen Block entfernt ist, kann man auch nachts mit dieser anreisen. Die Zimmer sind recht klein, aber sauber, wir hatten ein ziemlich neues Bad, nur das Bett ist halt "Full size", d.h. nur ca. 1,40m breit. Zur Zeit wird allerdings umgebaut und der Lärm geht so um 7-7.30 los. Also nichts für Langschläfer, aber wer will das schon in NY City sein?! :)) Preis-Leistung ist auf jeden Fall angemessen:es ist schließlich nur ein 1-Sterne-Hotel.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Not worth the savings”
text: This hotel is not worth the savings. Yes, you can save some money here relative to some of the other hotels in the same neighborhood, but you are risking wasting an enormous amount of time when you check in. We stayed in June of 2008 and arrived at 1pm in the afternoon. There are 1700 rooms and not nearly enough front desk clerks to accommodate that type of volume. After waiting on the queue for about fifteen minutes, we were told that the room wasn't ready and to return after 3pm. Fair enough, but it costs us $8 to store our bags in the lower storage area of the hotel and of course we had to tip the bellman who took us there (you can't access it on your own). We returned to check in around 4:15 pm and found a huge line of about 60 people trying to check in with three clerks at the front desk trying to accommodate. Having dinner reservations, we could not wait on the line for an hour, so we went downstairs to our stored luggage and changed in the bathroom! Later that night we returned at 11:30pm and still had to wait on a half hour line to check in. Our complaints fell on deaf ears and the room was less than mediocre and certainly not worth the wait and inconvenience. I do no t recommend this hotel unless you do not value your time.

name: Bedford Hotel
title: “Surprisingly good”
text:
Having read some of the reviews on Trip Advisor, I had mixed feelings about staying at the Bedford. On arrival though, I found that I needn't have worried. We stayed in a 1 bedroom suite which was large and well furnished. The bathroom was on the small side but, along with the room, was extremely clean - the complimentary toiletries were a bonus!! The beds and sofa bed were very comfortable. The staff were very friendlyand were very knowledgable about things to do in New York. 
The location was excellent - within walking distance of all the main tourist attractions/shops. There were lots of bars/restaurants nearby - Scotty's Diner around the corner is particularly good and inexpensive.

name: Comfort Inn Central Park West
title: “hotel eccezionale e in ottima strategica posizione”
text: L'hotel è bel curato, pulito, ottimamente servito. Il personale molto gentile e disponibile. La colazione è splendida, molto ricca. Si trova a due passi dall 'ingresso della metropolitana BC per Times Square e a due passi dall'ingresso del Central Park, in posizione esattamente opposta al Metropolitan Museum of art

name: Amsterdam Court Hotel
title: “Minimalista al maximo”
text: Tuve que dormir 2 noches en el amsterdam court de NY, y para subir a la habitacion era una escalera muy estrecha, el ascensor era para 3 personas, oscuro, la habitacion era abrir la puerta y ya estas dentro, la cama estaba ajustada casi al hueco, con lo que teniamos que entrar desde los pies hacia atras,personalmente no lo recomendaria y asi se lo hice saber a la agencia de viajes que me lo sirvio, la unicaq ventana estaba en el cuarto de baño vieja que daba a un interior muy mugriento,gracias a dios que solo iba a dormir y solo eran 2 noches,repito es mi impresion personal,estaba tan desagusto que ni se me ocurrio fotografiarlo.NO LO RECOMIEDO,

name: Belnord Hotel
title: “parfait comme dortoir”
text: hotel assez bien situé (une rue de la première station de métro). Idéal pour un séjour shopping / visite : pas très cher, mais le petit prix engendre de petites prestations (chambres petites, hotel en rénovation actuellement donc bruyant). Les salles de bains sont propres et il y a un accès wifi dans les chambres (code à demander).

name: Bedford Hotel
title: “quite good actually”
text:
We booked this hotel at quite short notice after a small problem with the booking at the Southgate (not the hotels fault, just the booking agent). Got a 1 bedroomed suite for around £100 a night and to be honest it wasn't at all bad. Although I was concerned as every site I went to about this place gave a different rating
I found the hotel to be clean (maybe the windows could do with a quick wash, and the bathroom was a bit dated) and pleasant. The staff where great, especially the maid and the doorman (who managed to get us a cab to Newark for $60 all inc, and even offered to go around the corner and collect our takeaway). And it had quite simply the biggest bed I have ever seen.
If you want a large room/suite quite cheap without any bells and whistles then go for the bedford. One thing to consider is the hotels location, it is a good walk to Times Square or the ESB
One tip. the filter coffee in the room is foul, Duane Read sell the papers for the machine and starbucks will do the coffee grounds

name: Belnord Hotel
title: “Bedbugs 3”
text:
I spent a week at the Belnord hotel and I had the worst experience in my life.
First the hotel seems right except some little things(no lift..) but on the last two nights I was biten by the bugs at least 50 times.
My arms, my neck, legs were full of bites.
IT'S NOT A JOKE SO AVOID THIS HOTEL IF YOU WANT TO ENJOY YOUR TRIP.

name: Soho Grand Hotel
title: “great location”
text:
Soho Grand hotel is a hip, trendy hotel in a great location. Excellent people watching, fun bar scene, great location for those of us who like to shop away from 5th ave scene.
Rooms were small, but very clean. Staff friendly and courteous. Will definitely come again!

name: Soho Grand Hotel
title: “by far and away the most enjoyable, peaceful and comfortable stay i've had in NY.”
text: second to none in NY, the soho grand is a home away from home. its always a pleasure to come back and sad to leave. great staff, beds are amazing, views are incredible and its a cool place to hangout.

name: Holiday Inn SoHo New York
title: “Immaculate hotel, friendly service”
text: Our experiece at the Holiday Inn Soho was nothing but positive! Upon checking in we found they did not have a non-smoking room for us of the type we requested so the friendly desk agent gave us an upgraded room at no extra charge. The room was extra clean with comfortable beds. The room service was speedy and the food excellent. We did not eat in the restaurant. The neighborhood is true New York with everything from Starbucks to discounted jewelry and hand bags to subway stops just steps away. We were able to walk to the Wall St./Ground Zero part of Manhattan in about 15 minutes. A pleasant walk in good weather; an inexensive cab ride in bad. Everything else is accesible by subway. We will stay there again if we get the chance.

name: Hudson New York
title: “Style over content”
text:
We arrived just before the hurricane so the hotel was very full. We were given an upgrade but our room was in need of refurbishment, the ceiling was crumbling and the bathroom so small that my knees touched the wall when on the loo!!
We were on the 4th floor and our window didn't fit properly so we had thrumping music from the bar every night until 12.30 pm. The bar on the roof looked lovely but was closed due to the weather. I am sure that when open it would be a stunning place for a drink.
There was a little bit of hanging space for clothes but nowhere to put everything else so we lived out of our suitcases.
We tried to extend our stay as the hurricane was due to hit on the day we were checking out. The hotel couldn't accommodate us and were very unhelpful about where we could go. Luckily we changed hotels as we found an absolute gem at City Club Hotel.
They also messed up our friend's booking so they didn't have a room for when she arrived. Luckily they managed to fit a pull out bed into our room (just!) so she had somewhere to sleep. Not ideal.

name: Excelsior Hotel
title: “Appalling Staff”
text:
I have never experienced a place where the staff were so rude and unhelpful. This was my first trip to the States in a party of 13 girls. From the moment we arrived at the hotel to check-in to the moment we checked out - the reception staff were the worst I have ever experienced in my life!
The hotel itself was charming with clean, tidy rooms and easy access to Central Park but it was pretty obvious that none of the staff had never attended any sort of customer service course and really shouldn't have any contact with the public.
My advice would be to stay away from this hotel unless you are happy to pay again for everything you have already booked and paid for, and you dont mind people shrugging their shoulders when they dont want to deal with you any longer. Oh and dont expect a manager to be in attendance at any time for you to speak to.
On the plus side the concierge guys were brilliant!

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “Great Location and Staff for a great NYC experience”
text: Just don't expect a big lobby...staff treats visitors like Royalty.b Friendly and went out the way to help. Beautiful old building....in the beautiful upper west side....

name: Holiday Inn SoHo New York
title: “buena ubicacion para moverse en metro”
text:
si tu idea es estar mas tiempo fuera del hotel que adentro entonces el hotel esta bien. el hotel es decente, y tenes lo basico y necesario. no esperes lujo. puedo agregar que la cama era muy comoda, dato no menor.
esta ubicado en soho pero mas del lado de little italy. esta a una cuadra del subterraneo que te lleva a todos los lugares de interes.
el taxi del hotel al aeropuerto jfk,sale alrededor de 40 dolares.

name: Soho Grand Hotel
title: “Great location, nice friendly hotel”
text: I stayed at the Soho Grand for 7 nights on business recently. In general I found the hotel to be very good. Location is fab with lots of bars and restaurants nearby. My room was very spacious as I was given a corner spot on the 14th floor which had a lovely view over the city. The bed is extremely comfortable and I slept very well during my stay! Free Wifi is excellent and I was given a login and password at check in. Staff were very friendly and helpful, my only problems being when I asked for a DVD list / DVDs to be sent up I never got them, I also had an issue with ordering room service and no cutlery arriving with it - by the time it did arrive my food was cold but this was removed from my bill with no issues. The lounge bar and breakfast are very good with staff very helpful so if you are at the hotel on business the lounge bar is a good location for meetings. All in all a very good stay and I will return to the hotel. If you are going to stay here be aware that the hotel has a loyalty scheme which I only found out about after my stay as it wasnt highlighted to me at check in - unfortunately the hotel are not willing to give points afterward which is a shame as for 7 nights am guessing this would be quite valuable - so make sure you join on line before!!

name: Empire Hotel
title: “Great Hotel- Beware of Barmen at Roof Top Bar”
text:
I just spent a weekend at this hotel with my wife and some friends for a NYC destination wedding. The rooms were clean, and quite large for NYC standards. The hotel is very nicely decorated, pretty moden and I would certainly recommend a stay here if you can get a good deal online. I think we paid close to $300 a night.
One word of WARNING is the bar man/servers at the roof top bar Its amazing in itself the prices of drinks, but what we found was that these 2 guys working the roof top bar on a Saturday afternoon were adding double gratuity onto our bill. So when they say tax and tip is included and dont itemize your bill make sure you take a good look at the final charge. I can only image how much money these guys make on a weekend from charging double gratuity. When we noticed this on a number of credit card receipts we confronted then and they gave us free drink cards and apologized. BEWARE, its hard enough to stomach $16 well drinks and $9 beers without baying an addiotnal 40% in Gratuity..

name: Park Central
title: “Very Good”
text:
Found the staff100% helpful with our situations of early check in, storage , cleaning and help with the in rooom safe. Super service. Very pleasant. Room was clean, beds comfortable, clean, nice linen, and very nice room. 
Very busy hotel but quiet and very well organized staff. Lots of staff to ask questions of. Elavator was great with the touch screen. 
I missed in room coffee but lots of shops nearby, can think of 3 offhand that sold coffee and econnomical meals and snacks. And the Carnegie Deli almost next door. Great for people new to this city . Very happy with my choice of this hotel.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Surprisingly comfortable”
text:
After reading a number of mixed reviews about New York hotels, the Roosevelt was a pleasant surprise and I'm quite a fussy person, the room wasn't massive but for NYC it was adequate, the bed was the most comfortable I've ever slept in, the service from everyone in the hotel was impeccable !
The room was kept extremely clean and tidy, the location of the hotel was practically perfect, there was a great diner for breakfast just down the road which had great food at reasonable prices, you're close to 5th Ave and getting around the city is easy peasy.
Just getting back to the service thing, I had bought quite alot of stuff and wanted to borrow some tape from the hotel to tape up my box of stuff, within minutes a chap was at my room with his tape, taping up my box for me. The hotel gave me an extra 3 hours to check out of my room because I had a late flight, FOC !
They stored my luggage for me until it was time to leave for the airport.
I really can't think of anything negative about this hotel, ah ! 1 thing I think the food is expensive but hey try the many places in the city, buffalo wings in an Irish bar is a good start ! Oh and the bath could have been abit deeper ... now I am being picky for the sake of it eh ... but the shower was great !
I would definitely recommend this hotel and it's location in NYC.

name: Off Soho Suites
title: “A Great place to Stay”
text: Great location and service. Everyone that I came in contact with was very kind and helpful. When I come back to the city I will make a reservation with Off Soho!

name: Excelsior Hotel
title: “Good hotel, great location”
text:
I booked the Excelsior Hotel for a 5 night Christmas shopping trip to NY for me and my mum. I was a bit worried after I had booked the hotel
due to reading a fair amount of negative comments, particularly regarding the staff. However, I was pleasantly surprised when I got there. The hotel is smart looking, the staff were fine, not overly friendly but nor were they rude and they dealt with any queries we had efficiently. The room was as expected, nothing special but the beds were comfortable, the size was fine and there was nothing to complain about. The location was fantastic, right near the 81st subway
so it was perfect for getting around and seeing the city. We never had
breakfast in the hotel as it seemed expensive - $20 not including coffee but there are plenty of delis and coffee shops nearby where you
can get breakfast for less than $5 which is probably a better way to do things anyway. We were barely in the hotel, more just coming and going as there is so much to see and do. I would stay at this hotel again, mainly due to the location but it was a comfortable and pleasant stay there too.

name: Hudson New York
title: “Trendy hotel in a great location”
text:
We arrived in NYC on the hottest day of the year. Outside of the hotel young men dressed in all black were helping with bags and hailing cabs - you'd think the hotel would have let them wear all white when it was 102 outside, but oh well. The escalator up to the lobby was being repaired, so we had to enter at ground level, but there were employees inside with cold water and cold wet towels to cool us off. 
The room was smallish, with a 3/4 bed, but it wasn't too small, and the bed was comfortable, and the room was very cold when we walked in. The room was clean, with a small but nice bathroom and shower. Our view wasn't great, but the hotel has a rooftop bar with an excellent view. The room came with a desk, a flat screen TV, iron and ironing board, and a hair dryer in a bag hanging behind the bathroom door (my wife panicked a bit until we found it)
At night the lobby seemed more like a rave party, with loud music and strange green lights, but upstairs we were not able to hear any of the music below, so it wasn't an issue.
We paid around $125 a night, before taxes and fees, using Priceline. As I said, the hotel is trendy, perhaps overly so for our tastes, but in a great location, with clean, affordable rooms. We would stay there again.

name: New York Marriott East Side
title: “Great location”
text:
We recently stayed at the Marriott East Side for our second trip to New York. Being a 3.5-4 star hotel we were unsure what we would find, but were pleasantly surprised. The rooms were lovely and clean. The bed huge (king size) and comfortable. We had a room at the back of the hotel so we had no trouble with road noise. 
The hotel is situated across from the intercontinental hotel and Waldorff Astoria near the Chrysler building so it is a mere 10 minute walk to times square or 5th avenue for a bit of shopping. 
We had drinks in the hotel bar one evening and found them to be expensive so would not recommend this. 
Definetely would recommend this hotel to anyone staying in NY!!

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Great place to stay in NYC!!!”
text: Surprisingly, based on reading some reviews, I had a great stay. The hotel has been renovating room by room, so I understand I may have gotten lucky with mine. Ask for room 412. Large room, 2 double beds, bathroom was probably 6 by 4, which is fine. I've stayed at some dumps in NYC, and this was not one of them. The bedding and linens were almost brand new. It defintely felt good to go back to the room and crash. I liked the fact that the bar was always crowded from 5pm - midnight, every night. The bar and lobby are really nice. Lots of marble. Checkin and checkout took about 2 mins each. Great location too on 45th and Madison. overall, it was a great stay!

name: Empire Hotel
title: “Very dissapointed with the service and mistakes the hotel made”
text: I was very dissapointed from check-in to check-out. Also, I received my credit card statement today and realized they charged me twice for the mistake they made. I booked with a wedding block for the day of the wedding (with the bloc) and when i checked in they said i was a "no show" from 2 days before. They made me wait 10 minutes before I finally was able to check in. Now the manager said I have to wait until monday and call back for the reservations dep.t can then "look into it". Meantime I am charges another 330 dollars. The new reservations they made for me at time of check-in was priced higher and I had to dispute the different price upon check-out, further disrupting my day. I never dealt with such incompatencies and would never go back to the Empire Hotel.

name: Roger Smith Hotel
title: “Estupendo hotel”
text:
Es un hotel que tiene detalles de hotel de cinco estrellas. Lo único que le falla es el baño que necesita reforma, pero está muy limpio y con detalles estupendos. Estuvimos en una suite de dos habitaciones en una de ellas estaba el salón con un sofá cama y dos sillones muy cómodos, una mesa de comedor y una television muy grande equipada con DVD (puedes pedir gratis peliculas en recepción) Y un dormitorio con cama King size, y el baño. Tamibén había una pequeña cocina puesta por nevera y microondas (Platos, cubiertos, etc)
El personal de recepción encantador y además por lo menos tres personas hablan español, lo que facilita mucho las cosas. Me gustó mucho.

name: Hotel Carter
title: “Muy centrico, compensa lo viejo que es con el precio que pagas (para mi).”
text:
Es un hotel muy viejo. Están arreglando el hall, creo que las habitaciones también. Nuestra estancia fue de 6 días, nos limpiaron dos, y un día nos cambiaron las sábanas y las toallas.
Si no se es muy escrupuloso con la limpieza y el aspecto estético del hotel, compensa por el precio tan bajo comparado con los que hay por los alrededores, ya que esta a 100m. de Times Square. Si además lo normal es utilizar el hotel para dormir y poco más, creo que para eso es suficiente.

name: Amsterdam Court Hotel
title: “Rent og pænt hotel”
text: Central og rigtig god beliggenhed tæt på Times Square. Pæne små værelser i god stand. God og omhyggelig rengøring f.eks. rene håndklæder hver dag. Hyggelig bar og restaurant i forbindelse med hotellet.

name: New York Marriott East Side
title: “rough around the edges”
text:
We stayed here for one night on Saturday January 12, 2008. The location is great within easy walking disytance of lots of attractions. There are a lot of other hotels in the immediate area such as the Waldorf, Intercontinental, Doubletree and the W, so getting a cab was never a problem. It is also a 2 block walk to the subway.
This is an older hortel that has recently been refurbished and they did a pretty good job. The lobby is not too spacious but has a very classy look to it. Our room on the 15th floor was relatively spacious with a king bed with great beddin, a 37 in HDTV and a small but adequate bathroom. 
Now mind youit was January in New York, yet we had to keep the air conditioner runing to maintain a decent temperature. When we got to the room the thermostat was set to 68degrees yet the HVAC unit kept blwing in cold air. We changed the setting to 72 and after a 1/2 hour or so it started blowing cold air again. We turned the unit off and by 2:00AM the romm temp had climbed to 78. By then we were happy to turn the AC unit back on.
In the morning my wife used the hair dryer which was hidden on the top of the closet. It kept turning off and then shot aparks out. A wet head in NYC in January isn't fun. 
The desk staff could not have been more efficient or helpful but it hard to understand why a large hotel in the heart of Manhattan would not open it's restaurant on a Saturday night. Even more difficult to understand why last call for drinks in the only bar in the hotel was at 11:45. There were a numberr of people who came in around midnight to learn that they could not sit in the bar or have a drink.
We did have breakfast in the restaurant. We did the buffet for $21.00. It seemed a little pricy but with $4.00 coffee and 4.00 juices the ala carte menu worked 0out even higher. To be fair the buffet was magnificent.
All in all our experience was OK but there are a few kinks to be worked out.

name: Cosmopolitan Hotel - Tribeca
title: “Convenient, budget hotel with tiny rooms”
text: Extremely good value hotel in downtown Manhattan, very conveniently placed for seeing everything. Be warned the rooms are tiny and there are no coffee or tea making facilities. It does have its own breakfast and dinner places which are very convenient. Staff friendly and helpful.

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “Me encantó el hotel, sin duda alguna repetiré en mi próximo viaje a New York”
text:
He estado alojado en este hotel desde el 18 de enero hasta el 25, en la habitación 2342 (planta 23). Os cuento un poquito sobre el hotel:
La habitación genial, el baño un poco antiguo y pequeñito, pero vamos, que para mi sólo no me hacía falta nada más. La habitación es una doble, pues al viajar sólo siempre es la que suelen dar, vamos, que pagas como si fueras dos personas, pero eso pasa en todos los hoteles, no en este sólo. No sé si es que yo tuve suerte o qué, pero la habitación era muy ámplia, como os comenté, dos armarios, la cama, dos mesitas de noche, varios cajones para guardar cosas debajo del escritorio, la caja fuerte gratis y enorme (ahí guardaba yo mi portatil de 10" con el que os escribía desde allí), y limpísimo todo. Vamos, os digo que si no todos los días te cambiaban las sábanas, reponían las cosas del baño, pasaban la aspiradora a la moqueta, etc. A mí la habitación me la limpiaban por la mañana siempre. Antes de irme a desayunar yo quitaba el cartelito de "No molesten" y ya entraban. Una de las mañanas en que llegué para dejar unas compras que había hecho, me encontré a la limpiadora pasando la aspiradora a la moqueta. De hecho, os puedo decir con total confianza que me ponía para dormir calcetines blancos y andaba toda la noche descalzo de un lado para otro, y nada, ni un ápice de suciedad. El agua del baño super caliente, hirviendo, vamos, me gusta decir esto porque en el 2009 estuve en un hotel de Punta Cana de cuyo nombre no quiero acordarme y estuve una semana duchándome con el agua prácticamente fría, y desde entonces tengo un tráuma con el tema del agua en los hoteles.
A ver si me acuerdo de todo. En recepción hablan todas las chicas en español, y son simpatiquísimas. Antes de irme les hice varias preguntas. Ahora mismo no existe el Milford Club como antes, donde podías desayunar, conectarte a internet con ordenadores y eso, pero lo van a volver a poner. También me comentaron que para este verano van a reformar realmente las habitaciones y las van a poner mejor. Ahora mismo no hay restaurante en el hotel. Lo único que sí os puedo decir es que en la segunda planta hay dispensador de hielo, varias habitaciones tipo "empresario" para hacer conferencias y eso, y una sala donde hay varios ordenadores. Ahí te puedes conectar por 25 centavos el minuto, más que recomendable que coger el wifi a 14 dólares el día... lo digo por el tema de enviar un mensajillo rápido a la familia, que te gastas poco. De todos modos en todos los Starbucks hay wifi, yo todas las mañanas me contectaba allí, me tomaba un cafelito y estaba una horita hablando con mi familia y eso. Lástima que no hice fotos del Lobby, porque iba super estresado todo el día con las caminatas, pero os puedo decir que en la planta 0, es decir, donde entras, hay una escalera normal y otra mecánica, aparte de un apartado de seguridad, donde siempre hay una o dos personas vigilando. También hay asientos para sentarse mientras llega la hora de coger el avión o para lo que quieras, claro, y otro mostrador a la izquierda que es donde te guardan las maletas el día de tu marcha, sin coste alguno, es gratis. En la primera planta está la recepción a la izquierda, en el centro los ascensores y a la derecha otro mostrador del "conserje". En total hay 8 ascensores, que van con letras cada uno. En una parte hay cuatro, de la A a la D, y en la otra de la E a la H. El sistema funciona de manera que si estás en la planta 1 y quieres ir a la 23, desde la planta en la que te encuentres debes marcar 23 en el ascensor desde fuera porque dentro no hay botones. Y arriba igual, desde tu planta marcas desde fuera el 1 y listo, vas para abajo.
En este tema de la seguridad me quiero extender un poquito, porque la seguridad que he visto en este hotel es buenísima, es decir, aparte de los dos que vigilan en la planta 0, cámara de vigilancia incluída, casi todos los días te encuentras dos policías en la puerta del hotel o dentro del mismo. Sensacional. Aparte tienes al botones siempre en la puerta, que te llama a un taxi si te hace falta y habla español. Recalco que la ubicación es buenísima, a dos calles tienes Times Square, a la vuelta de la esquina en la izquierda tienes un subway y en toda la 8ª avenida tienes de todo, desde delis, sitios para desayunar de todo tipo, pizzerías, un starbucks, tiendas de todo tipo, etc. Muy, muy bien ubicado.
Ahhh, por cierto, cuando llegas al hotel y haces el check-in te piden el pasaporte y una tarjeta de crédito, de ahí te descuentan 50 euros o dólares, ahora no tengo el móvil a mano para verlo bien, pero cuando vuelves te lo devuelven. A mí todavía no me lo han devuelto, así que estoy a la espera. Supongo que lo harán para ver si tienes fondos y eso, no estoy seguro porque con las prisas y el stress que llevaba todo el día al final se me pasó.
Como os digo, el hotel está super "apañao", para una semana en New York o incluso dos, está de lujo, en serio, ¡me ha encantado!. Creo que ya os he contado todo, aunque los que vayáis allí espero que exploréis más, porque en teoría hay una sala de fitness que yo no llegué a encontrar, aunque tampoco pregunté porque tenía los pies que me moría del dolor de tanto andar, vamos, como para meterme en un gimnasio, me tienen que llevar al hospital directamente, jejeje. 
Yo iba con mucho miedo, porque en tripadvisor y otras páginas lo ponían como una "cloaca", y para nada es así, ahí tenéis las fotos. Que está antiguo y necesita alguna que otra reformilla, vale, pero de ahí a decir que si hay chinches, pulgas, cucarachas y demás, pues como que no. Al revés, en mi vida he estado en un hotel más limpio que este, os lo prometo. Incluso en Punca Cana, México, Italia, y aquí en España tambíen, os prometo que no he visto hotel más limpio. Ya os digo, que me tiraba por la noche descalzo andando por toda la habitación y los calcetines blancos no acumulaban ni un ápice de suciedad. Más prueba que esa, ninguna.
Entiendo que la opinión de cada uno es muy subjetiva, y que para gustos los colores, pero yo os puedo decir que en cuanto vaya otra vez a New York, repito de nuevo con el Milford. De eso no hay ninguna duda.

name: New York Marriott East Side
title: “Change is Good”
text:
This hotel i believe has 33 floors w/ 600+ rooms.
from 22 up those floors are considered Concierge floors.
which has access to the Lounge.
33rd floor is where the Suite rooms are located.
as well as some rooms such 06 & 28 on the lower floors.
are also considered Suite rooms (acc. to the very informed housekeeper...) ;-D
Pro's
Location-Midtown 49th St. Lexington Ave.
walking distance to Bloomingdales, St. Patrick's Cathedral, Rockefeller Center.
:shops on 59th St. (Claire's, H&M, Express and many more)
:restaurants (Smith & Wollensky steakhouse, Mr. K's, TGI Friday's etc.)
Access to Subway-two blocks uptown to take the no. 6 train (Manhattan bound). MTA bus M101 downtown, stops a block away from the hotel. Also taxi cabs are parked outside the hotel's main entrance.
Rooms: My family & I stayed here last year before the renovation began, and thankfully went back again last month after the re-do.
The changes: Carpet - brown (dull, old, boring) TO
red - (w/ swirl prints, modern and vibrant looking)
Hallway - used to be dark w/ less corner lamps-
NOW, much better lighting fixtures plus more wall frame decors.
The big mirror fronting the guest elevators w/ black chest adds to more sophisticated feel of the hotel.
We had a room on the 27th floor.
King sized bed, w/ a sofa bed.
3 windows, 3 side tables, a ref., flatscreen tv, a/c, coffee maker (3 decaf, 3 regular, 4 condiment packs, 1 set of tea)
BED: 3 shams, 3 feather pillows, blanket, duvet (white sheets)
plus a red bed scarf.
It made the room look much brighter.
The wall paper was beige which is way better than the brown one the hotel had.
The bathroom was almost the same. (marble tiled floors) except for the addition of the bigger mirror and new shower curtain.
B/R Amenities: Bath & Body works products. (small sizes)
4 towels, 4 handtowels, 4 washcloths, 1 bathmat.
hairdryer, 2 laundry bags, iron, iron board (inside the closet).
FITNESS CENTER: its located on the 35th floor. Go to the 32nd flr. to connect to another elevator at the back to get to the FC. They have new exercise machines. Earphones are provided. Most machines are equipped w/ tv screens. 
There's also 2 flatscreen tv sets in the FC. 
A rack of handtowels. Water dispenser. Bathroom.
CONCIERGE LOUNGE: access depending on the room level and membership. Its open from 7am-10am..for breakfast...1pm drinks... 5-9pm for light snacks.... its closed on the weekends though.
SERVICE: our housekeeper was kind & anticipated our needs. We had extra towels in our room & bathroom amenities.
****Needs imrpovement: The front desk staff. Unprofessional and loud in dealing w/ guests. (basing from our obeservation on how they handled the other guests' reservation queries.) 
****FOOD: Best tip, eat out. The Room Service menu didn't impress us. We had a good breakfast at Cafe' Metro 2 blocks uptown by the 6 train station for half the price. 
*****being a Platinum member, i expected that the renovation would also mean providing a fully stocked mini bar. But there was nothing. Also, amenities like a Robe or slippers would have been nice... even a bath gel or mouthwash should be standard in ALL rooms. After paying $400++ / night, those "little extras" would be appreciated.
******TIP: request for a turndown service. they offer sleep oils and chocolates.
******use the door sign for housekeeping cleaning. To avoid being disturbed by the loud knocks at 8am on a Saturday morning. 
*******choose rooms such as 6,7,8, on the high floor. We were told that those rooms are quite spacious plus they have sofa beds... btw, those are rooms w/ king beds.
*******This is a NON-smoking hotel. I was informed that when housekeepers find cigarette's in the rooms (or proof thereof) that the guest/s are smoking in the room, they will call the supervisor, to inspect the further, then bill the guest $250. So think twice if you feel like smoking in your room!
For convenience, we'll defintely come back.
For business travelers? Yes i would reccommend this hotel.
but for families? we were able to see a few rooms that are rather small to accommodate a cot... but if you don't mind the overcrowding, then this hotel might be right for you.
;-)

name: Off Soho Suites
title: “terrible”
text: bathroom so dirty, any kind of money is not worth it. bad experience

name: New York Marriott East Side
title: “Hmmmm...probably not again....”
text:
I stayed here for 3 nights on business. The Marriott Marquis was charging about $400 a night the week I went (I think it was spring break) and this hotel was about $100 less, so my company encouraged me to stay here. Now, I like the Marriott chain, overall. I play the "point game" when I travel on business so while there might be better choices nearby, I chose here for "other" reasons. 
The good: 
1) Nice bedding and clean room.
2) Friendly and professional staff. 
2) Decent wait times for an elevator (which can be a problem in other large hotels in NYC).
3)Quick room-service
The not-so-good: 
1) Immediate location is not that interesting (and yes, I know this is Manhattan, but I was here on business and stayed reasonably close to the hotel after working a long day). It was too far of a walk for me to see any noteworthy "sites" such as Times Square, Central Park, etc.
2) Building seemed dated and in need of an immediate refurb.
3) Price could probably get something nicer if you aren't playing the Marriott Point game.
4) Rooms were small for the price paid.
5) No view even though I was on a higher floor (unless you like staring at an office building across the street).
6) Overall "old" feeling to atmosphere (and I don't mean the people, just the "tiredness" of everything associated with the property).
Will you have a great time if you stay here? Of course. It's NYC and that should overshadow every nuiance I've cited (it just won't be greater because you stayed here).

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “We really enjoyed staying at The Roosevelt”
text: My friend and I stayed at the Roosevelt a few weeks ago. From the moment I made the reservation until the moment we checked out, everyone was very friendly. We were a little apprehensive at first after reading some of the reviews on Trip Advisor, but quickly realized that some people just like to complain. Yes, the rooms are small, but who cares? Our room was spotless and very quiet. When we checked in, the man at the desk told us if we were unhappy about anything, to simply call. We arrived at 11:00 am and they had a room ready for us. We had a great time and would definitely stay there again.

name: Amsterdam Court Hotel
title: “Minste rom noensinne”
text: Hotellet var helt greit, men er dere 2 som reiser og har mer enn èn koffert sliter dere med å få plass på rommet! Døra går nesten ikke helt opp fordi senga står i veien. Det er plassert en air condition på veggen like ved senga som bråker noe vanvittig! Senga var også mindre enn andre queen-senger vi fikk andre steder i USA. Men hotellets plassering er ypperlig...

name: Off Soho Suites
title: “Goed, simpel.”
text:
Een simpel hotel, met als pre dat je behalve een slaapkamer en een badkamer, ook een aparte woonkamer annex keuken hebt. Niet superdelux, maar gewoon goed voor een goede prijs.
De wijk is leuk en gemoedelijk, met veel restaurants in de buurt.

name: Milford Plaza Hotel
title: “Perfecte uitvalsbasis”
text: Op loopafstand van Times square en diverse metro stations, is dit hotel ideaal als uitvalsbasis voor trips door New York. Hoewel de kamers er wat oud uit zien, zijn ze netjes. Mijn kamer had uitzicht op een andere vleugel van het hotel, maar dit zorgde ervoor dat er nauwelijks lawaai te horen was van de straat.

name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel
title: “Filthy, filthy, filthy!”
text: I am a travel agent and booked a room for myself (with a travel agent rate, so they knew this when I checked in) at the Manhattan Times Square for 2 nights to visit family. I asked to be moved after the first night as the room I was in was filthy -- torn and completely stained carpet, blood spatters on one of the duvets, slashed lampshades, broken lamps, I even had to clean the sink out before using it. The phone was caked with black grime. First they refused to move me, but relented and moved me to another room. It was less filthy, but even then I had the "pleasure" of washing out the bathtub full of someone else's grime and hair before I could take a shower. The air conditioning in both rooms was sub-par, never getting truly comfortable despite the thermostat being set at 65. There is no sound insulation to speak off, so whatever activity is going on on either side of you sounds like it's in the room with you. A foul and disgusting hotel.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “A great option in NYC”
text: I stayed at the Wellington because it offered a good rate on a reputable discount web site, and I was hugely pleased in every respect. It is an older hotel and definitely not for travellers looking for the latest upgrades or 5-star amenities. That said, valet parking was easy and convenient, the reception and abundant bell men were most helpful, the room was on the small side but comfortable and well appointed, and the internet was reliable. I enjoyed the location just north of the Times Square neighborhood because it was an easy walk from theatres but was relatively quiet and less populated. I will definitely return again and have already begun to recommend it to others.

name: Empire Hotel
title: “MOLD IN ROOMS!!!!!!!!”
text: The Empire Hotel NY is a very hip and trendy location, but they tried a little too hard with the design of their showers! We stayed on the 5th floor for a weekend and with the first attempt to shower, we noticed that there was no shower door, so the bathroom floor gets water everywhere while people shower! I am in construction/real estate for a living and said there is no way that was supposed to be designed that way, but we were there for a fun trip, so I didn't think much of it. The second night, we came back to our room and while laying in bed noticed that part of the ceiling had been painted with primer to cover a water leak from the bathroom in the room above us! After discuss the issue with the front desk, they said they were AWARE of the water/mold problem and were doing their best to go floor to floor to resolve the issue. I said 'so I've been sleeping in a room with mold for 2 nights and breathing it in with your knowledge of it' and his response was 'we are doing our very best to fix the design flaw and hope that you'll come back soon!' NOT A CHANCE

name: Empire Hotel
title: “EXCELLENT!”
text: This boutique hotel offered the highest level in customer service recently experienced! Within 15 minutes of being in my room, I received a call to inquire as to whether the room met my expectations and standards. The price was really great and the location can't be beat...right across the street from the Lincoln theatres/centers and within walking distance of the best retails stores and restaurants. Although the weather did not permit, the hotel offers Indoor/Outdoor Rooftop Bar & Lounge but I did have the pleasure of dining at Ed’s Chowder House restaurant within the facility. Overall, the room was small as expected from the older hotels, but did not lack atmosphere, cleanliness and comfort. Again, for the price, service and location, it will be my hotel of choice again for future visits.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Just a place to sleep.....in your clothes, on top of the blankets.........”
text: My boyfriend took me to NY for the first time for my birthday on May 26th, he chose the Hotel Pennsylvania for our weekend stay. What can I say besides absolutley horrible!? We waited almost an hour to check in and went upstairs to the 12th floor to out "250 sq ft" room (which is still tiny). The hotel is old, dirty, and smells. Everything is outdated. The doors to the rooms look like bomb shelters. Big heavy metal doors, and you have to step down into the room like you are going in a bomb shelter. We opened the door and the door hit the tv stand, we turned to the left and had to squuze past the bed, we went into the moldy, nasty bathroom and ran right out. We had a great view of a brick wall. The room was a shoebox. You couldnt open the closet door all the way because it hit the mini fridge, which was on the floor next to the tv stand. The air was broken for 1 1/2 out of the 2 days we stayed there. We called the manager & said the room was supposed to be 250 sq ft. He said "not all of the standard rooms are 250, some are 100 sq feet, you are still in a standard room, which is what you paid for." We asked to be moved, they would not do anything about it. We were mad but thought "oh well, we just have to sleep here, we will be out the whole time". Well then my bf went to use his travel money visa, the prepaid money card and there was nothing left on it. He said there should be $200 still. We called & it said the room took out an extra $150 from his card. We called downstairs and they said they charged his card $150 in case we order any movies. WHAT!? That is ridiculous anyway AND this is a cash card, they took all of his spending money. We tried to get it refunded, someone told us to call at 9am and the manager would do it. We called at 9am and the manager told us it would take 5 business days after the holiday to refund the money. The place was just horrible & disgusting, there were stains all over the walls & floors. We also called the manager about the dirty, moldy bathroom and they sent a maid up to spray it with bleach. The maid told us they paint over the mold in the shower, but it usually washes away in 2 weeks, thats why it's there again. Great excuse. We paint over the mold. My advice....................stay far away from this place. For $200-300 a night for a standard room, I would rather sleep on the street then stay here.

name: Amsterdam Court Hotel
title: “Gerne wieder”
text: Die Lage ist super, New York zu Fuß ab Broadway oder mit öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln. Gratis Kaffeespezialitäten und netter Service. Im Januar 2007 wurde renoviert, sollte also nochmal besser werden. Preis/Leistung einwandfrei.

name: Amsterdam Court Hotel
title: “Pessimo hotel, sconsigliatissimo.”
text: Sconsiglio vivamente questo hotel! Dopo una sola notte me ne sono andata, la camera era talmente piccola che non sono riuscita ad aprire la valigia. Non c'era armadio ma una specie di rientranza nel muro coperta da una tendina (sporca). La camera era fredda e rumorosa. La peggiore sistemazione mai provata.

name: Roger Smith Hotel
title: “Volvería”
text:
Fuimos a este hotel porque nos lo recomendó la agencia, la verdad es que nunca se nos hubiera ocurrido coger un hotel de clase turista en Nueva York, pero nos sorprendió gratamente. Cuidan hasta es más mínimo detalle, las habitaciones son muy grandes y la limpieza es estupenda. 
Nosotros tuvimos un problema con la calefacción de la habitación y lo dijimos en recepción (por cierto, hablan español) y a la vuelta ya estaba solucionado.
Otra de las cosas que nos hizo decidirnos es que el desayuno está incluido, cosa que es difícil de encontrar en un hotel de la gran manzana. Tienes de todo, bollería, fruta, lácteos..... y por supuesto, café.
La situación es inmejorable, y además tiene una estación de metro muy cerquita.

name: Hotel Grand Union
title: “Brilliant - Hotel Grand Union NYC”
text:
Having previuosly stayed in New York i was not expecting much as standard in New York for hotels seem to be far less than if you stayed anywhere else in the US. But i was pleasantly suprised.
The hotel was great, great location, staff friendly and room cleaned daily.
The room was basic but clean. We stayed on the 9th floor with no view but then not many rooms in New York has a view. Air conditioning in the room which was great as the temperature was 83 degrees!
Would definitely recomend this hotel and would definitely stay here again on another visit.
Cafe that seemed to adjoin the hotel was great not expensive at all and friendly staff. We used this restaurant / cafe for Breakfast on Saturday and Sunday morning.
Monday morning there was a great place to eat opposite. Absolutuely huge with a great selection. Sushi made to order, bacon & eggs and the price was ridculoulsy cheap.
So all in all great hotel with great surrounding facilities.

name: Empire Hotel
title: “Great hotel especially for younger people”
text:
I stayed at the Empire Hotel with a friend for 4 nights a few days before Christmas and was really impressed. I would say this hotel is more suited for younger people.When you first enter it seems more like a night club rather than a hotel and there is an actual night club at the very top. We didn't spend much time in our hotel but the time that we did we really enjoyed ourselves. Had the nicest cocktails I've ever had, however they are quite pricey but nevertheless worth it :) 
The staff we encountered were helpful and friendly. On our arrival are room got upgraded too.with out us asking. I wouldn't be put off by the night club at the top of the hotel, it did not effect us getting a good nights sleep and we were 6 floors up. Can't comment on the food as we did not eat anything there, but the hotel was very clean and the maid service excellent. I would stay at this hotel again if going back to New York.

name: Bedford Hotel
title: “Calido Hotel”
text:
Estuve en las primeras semanas de enero por una semana.
Excelente ubicacion, a metros de Park Ave y de Grand Central Station.
Calida recepcion, tuve que esperar un poco para el check-in ya que habia llegado temprano, pero la habitacion me fue entregada antes de lo previsto.
Habitacion con 2 camas Queen, heladera, cafetera y bacha. Conexion a internet gratis (muy importante en NY ya que en muchos lados cobran hasta 20 dolares el dia de conexion).
Hermosa vista desde el piso 12 al Empire State.
La habitacion siempre limpia, el baño tambien y la temperatura (ya que era pleno invierno) muy agradable en su interior.
Muy recomendable.

name: Excelsior Hotel
title: “Very Nice”
text: Came in NYC to see the St. Partick's Day Parade. Two younger children, wife and self. Found the Excelsior to be an excellent bargain and very clean. Booked the suite. Kids slept on rollout, with no camplaints and played video games. The bed was VERY comfortable and the down comfortor on the bed very warm. Room came with robes, and again extremely clean. Had dinner and a guiness around the corner at O'Brien's nice little pub. Breakfast a little pricey but was very good. I would recommend the Excelsior. Right across from Central park a nice walk to the MET, which is directly across the park and the Museum of Natural Science is right across the street.

name: Hotel Grand Union
title: “Excellent Location - good sleep”
text: Stayed in Room 504 - faces the street, a little noisy during the night but not too bad, had a view of the Empire State. Rooms were clean and very comfortable, great showers very powerful. Location is 5-10 min walk from Grand Central, 33rd St station is less than a minute away, Times Sq is about 15/20 min walk. Lots of good places to eat breakfast nearby, the Captains cafe was good and theres a cafe/deli opposite the hotel which has alot of choices for breakfast. Staff were helpful, there is internet available to use, free for 10 mins p/d. Also there are 2 unsecured wifi access to select, from this room ;-) - All in all for the price i paid this is a excellent choice if you want good location and a good night sleep after walking about in NYC.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Excellent Location”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel on two occassions and the location is second to none. Both times I had an exceptionally large room (booked a twin room). The rooms were cleaned on a daily basis and fresh towels provided. 
By no means is this a 5 star hotel but I did not find it as bad as other reviewers. I'm sure the rooms are hit and miss.
Macey's is only a minutes walk while Times Sq is less than 10 and the Empire State is just around the corner.
The bar in the hotel isn't bad but not a very lively place and the food in the restaurant is good too. 
I would recommend this hotel for anyone looking to be in the centre of things on a lower budget.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “The Roosevelt Hotel was great.”
text: My two daughters and I stayed for 3 nights at the Roosevelt just before Christmas and really enjoyed our stay. Our room was nice and quiet and clean. The staff was very courteous and helpful. The eggnog served in the lobby was just great. The decorations were beautiful. A very classy hotel. Would not hesitate to stay there again. Had a luxury ride back to the airport, thanks to the doorman. Everyone was just great!

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Fantastic hotel - would definitely stay again.”
text:
Loved the hotel from the minute we walked into the lobby. Dreading going to our room as I heard a lot of the rooms are small in NY. Well I was pleasantly surprised we had a very spacious room with a king size bed that could have fitted my whole family in. The bathroom was clean and well lit - as I have a thing about using bathrooms when I'm on holiday. Great location. 
Staff very polite and helpful. We stayed at the same time as others who gave bad feed back and we honestly couldn't fault the place. We had trouble with our safe but the security man came up within 5 minutes, as my husband had forgot to put something in the safe he went to it again but it failed to open. Again, the security man came up within 5 minutes to tell us we wouldn't be able to use that safe but could use one at the reception desk and offered a complimentary dinner for us both in the Teddy's Restaurant - we said it was no inconvenience and he insisted we accept the meal, which I must admit we went to town and had a three course meal which was truly delicious. I must remember to do something to the safe if I stay again because it was the best meal we had while in NY. 
I don't know if it makes any difference who you book with but it does seem that the people who booked with pricerunner had the bad rooms. We paid more for our room about £140 and I booked through Airmiles. 
Just can't wait to go back, hopefully next year with my sister so I can do more shopping!

name: Hudson New York
title: “The Perfect Valentine Getaway”
text: My boyfriend and I were looking to do something very romantic in Manhattan. We are residents of New York City and thought it would be fun to get away at a nice hotel in the city. We chose the Hudson hotel near the Columbus Circle area. Everything about our stay was perfect, it made our first Valentine's together that more memorable. We checked in on a Saturday afternoon at 3pm. We were helped by Hudson Regional Guest Experience Manager, Ms. Shacazia Brown. She was very pleasant, knowledgeable and all smiles upon our arrival. She made us feel very welcomed and seemed thankful about having our business. We were checked into our room within 5 minutes. She gave us a brief tour of the hotel's Library Bar, Hudson Bar and Restaurant area. She knew in advance that is was a special romantic weekend and presented us with chocolates and a bottle of champagne in our deluxe studio room. The decor was amazing- dark, hardwood floors with white and silver steel furniture. I must have said at least three times during our stay, "I want to LIVE here". Instead of visiting the MOMA, we ended up taking a nap for two hours after feeling how comfortable our queen size bed felt. After we returned from dinner, we had reservations at the Library Bar near a fireplace. It was such a romantic setting for celebrating our love. We relaxed for an hour and went back to our room to freshen up. We had 11pm reservations at the Hudson bar and were seated immediately. The DJ played great tunes all night as we sipped champagne, ate strawberries and danced. The party was filled with people of all different ages and cultures. It was nice to be in a different atmosphere for a change. We ended the night sleeping like babies in our comfortable bed. The next morning we had breakfast at Hudson's beautiful rustic style restaurant. The breakfast selection was divine and my palate was extremely satisfied. Upon check out the next morning, we were greeted and checked out in 60 seconds. As we left the hotel, my boyfriend and I smiled at one another and agreed we must come back for another visit very soon! The Hudson hotel is definitely a wonderful choice no matter what the occasion.

name: Hotel Carter
title: “hotel Carter solo por necesidad”
text: Nos hospedamos durante 2 noches en este hotel por estar cerca de la zona cercana al lugar en donde a tempranas hora mi hijo rendía exámenes...Pero es tétrico en los pisos ,-alfombras paredes en pésimo estado : el cuarto en el interior lucia con baño re acondicionado pero puertas viejas en mal estado , las camas sí contaban con sabanas limpias sólo la 1ra noche , la TV mala imagen -canales locales y el teléfono una pieza de museo

name: The Time
title: “Nightmare on W49th Street”
text: This hotel is run by amateurs. Booked an online package that included parking and taxes. Only trouble the package was a mystery to the staff who was rude and argumentative when we tried to get the terms of the package applied. Of course, the parking garage did not want to honor the "free" parking and the manager of the hotel had to accompany me to the garage to straighten things out. Rooms were small and poorly maintained. Plumbing was substandard, for example, and carpets were worn and frayed. The king bed was soft and lumpy. Overall, a lousy experience and pricey to boot. Stay away!

name: Hotel Grand Union
title: “Great Location, Shoddy Hotel”
text: We stayed at this hotel for 5 nights over New Year 2006/2007. Tiny beds, tiny bathroom, dirty carpet, no temperature control in the room, consistently left too few towels - I could go on and on. The staff were clearly bored and were not interested in helping in any way. We had to pay for our stay on arrival, rather than on departure. We had to beg the manager to split the cost of our room across a couple of credit cards rather than pay on just one as "it messes up our accounting". If you stay here make sure you bring your own iron and ironing board as they are "against hotel policy". I will never stay here again. Dreadful.

name: The Time
title: “nice stay”
text: I just got back from a 5 night stay at The Time. It was fine for what we wanted, it was clean, with good service, and a great location. Barely any closet space and very little room to stretch out made it hard for us and our luggage to fit into the room comfortably. Our room was small but we expected that. The hotel overall was about average. On Friday and Saturday night the lounge downstairs had some kind of party that we thought was going to ruin our night's sleep, but we were pleasantly surprised when we got off the elevator on our floor (the 9th) and couldn't hear a thing. I would stay there again if I was stopping in on a short trip, but if staying for a while I would opt for another more spacious hotel.

name: Hotel Grand Union
title: “steer well clear!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text: recepionist seemed to have problem with females, told us that reception was shut because he was on his lunch, when asked for a morning wake up call, he replied why not just phone one another to save him the bother, when toilets blocked on the fri night, told us that it would be mon morning before it could be fixed, just downright rude/attitude problem.............just like a turkish fawlty towers.........never again!!!!!!!!!!!

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “Repeat customer”
text: This was my second stay at the Belleclaire, and it has only improved. The renovated rooms are beautiful and comfortable; loved the ipod docking station and flat screen TV. I had a room facing out onto the street and was able to get free wifi from somewhere in the neighborhood. The staff are outstanding and always very helpful with directions and advice. The location is excellent; only a short walk to the crosstown bus stop and to the subway and more great restaurants than one has time to sample. Consistently the best value on the Upper West Side.

name: Holiday Inn SoHo New York
title: “L'unico rilievo riguarda la...”
text: L'unico rilievo riguarda la rumorosità che è appena sopportabile nei piani alti dell'albergo (eravamo al tredicesimo piano). Abbiamo richiesto il trasferimento dal quarto piano dove non era possibile dormire. La posizione dell'hotel è strategica per chi ama stare dowtown.

name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel
title: “Ótima localização e cama confortável”
text: Hotel muito próximo a times Square, próximo ao metrô e com cama confortável. Possui serviço gratuito de recebimento de compras pela internet. A apenas a alguns passos do Rockfeller center, da broadway e da 5th avenue. Serviço de internet gratuito apenas no lobby.

name: Hotel Carter
title: “Hotel Carter - Melhor Localização de NY”
text: Não existe hotel mais barato e com melhor localização que este. Você paga um valor equivalente ao nível de serviços que irá receber! Mesmo assim, para quem vai à NY para comprar e ficar fora do hotel, vale a pena... principalmente, para pessoas jovens que não se importam com conforto e não querem gastar muito com hospedagem!

name: Excelsior Hotel
title: “Bewertung gilt nur für Zentrallage NY”
text: in zentrumlage NY ist mehr Ruhe kaum möglich. Daher ist Bewertung an Zentrallage und dem Zweck des Besuchs ausgerichtet. Es handelt sich um ein Business-Hotel und kann nicht als Familien-Hotel verstanden werden.

name: Excelsior Hotel
title: “Mooi, comfortabel hotel op een uitstekende ligging.”
text: Mooi hotel op een uitstekende ligging aan Central Park. Metro om de hoek dus dat is lekker handig. Lekker uitgebreid hotel voor een goede prijs. Comfortabele kamers en netjes. Hotelpersoneel (behalve de ontbijtdame) is echter wel onbeleefd en onprofessioneel. Bij binnenkomst werd er al geschreeuwd en maakte de receptioniste op een wel heel onprofessionele manier duidelijk dat ze een break nodig had en tja vriendelijk waren ze niet, maar of dat nu aan het hotel lag of het feit dat je in een grote stad zit is nog maar de vraag natuurlijk. Goed hotel in het algemeen dus je krijgt waar voor je geld.

name: The Time
title: “Great Location”
text: Stayed there for a week just recently. The hotel has an ideal location for visits to sights in manhattan & subway to further destinations. The staff is very friendly, the rooms are spacious, and the housekeeping cleans the rooms very well. Overall, very very pleasant stay with no negative point at all! Will definitely go back!

name: Hotel Grand Union
title: “Not recommended”
text:
First things first, this place is a 'budget' hotel in the sense of NYC, but it was far from cheap. My partner and I travelled here primarily on the strength of the tripadvisor review which said it was okay. Our trip wasn't plagued with major concerns, but lots of little things kept cropping up.
First off, we arrived at 3pm and the room wasn't ready. Not a major deal, we were able to hold the luggage and go off to explore the city but, after a 10hr+ journey, it wasn't ideal.
When we eventually got into the room, we were shoved way up on the 9th floor (of ten). There's only one lift; it takes an absolute age to get anywhere, and it's only big enough for about 5 people - less if you've got luggage.
The room itself was stale, dusty and smokey. As a non-smoker, this was particularly off-putting. It wasn't a bad size, but there was only a shower and basin - no bath. The shower itself was a constant source of delight, either being too hot or cold but never right. The plumbing seemed to have a mind of it's own too - constantly alternating between sub-zero and skin-scorchingly hot. I didn't touch anything! After 7 days this was a real pain.
Indeed, showering seemed to cause more problems than it was worth. On our last night, we returned having been out all day (as one does in the City that never sleeps) to find no towels in the room. Not one. A swift phonecall later told us that 'housekeeping was closed' and that we wouldn't get towels until 7am. So not only were we unable to shower when we wanted, we had to wait on towels which, predictably, never came the next morning. Eventually housekeeping did deliver them, after another phonecall, but that's not the point!
There was also some roadside noise to contend with, but nothing major. The grumbling of the hotel's plumbing was more of a concern to me, but it never stopped me sleeping. The dust did that.
The location can't be knocked however. Two blocks away from the Empire State, 4 from Madison Square Garden and on the same block as a metro station (33rd Street, on line 6 I think). A 'leisurely' 20 minute walk direct to Times Square, the hotel seemed quite safe and secure as well.
In summmary; great location, not so good room and scary plumbing! Wouldn't choose to go back there, but wouldn't knock back a free stay there either.

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “Wonderful Stay”
text:
Had a wonderful 3 night stay, autumn special package. Room was simple but clean and cosy, felt like I was going back to my own house. Room was more spacious than I had expected, flat screen TV, radio that allows you to directly plug in your ipod. Toilet was clean. Pity it was a little dark in the shower area (bathtub). The mini fridge was pretty noisy too, so I unplugged it. And the radiator wasn't working. Good thing it wasn't too cold. 
Hotel staff were friendly and extremely helpful. Allowed us to use the gym shower room (only 1 room) for free, to freshen up before departing for the airport. Pretty near subway station, near central park, upper west side, away from the maddening crowds further downtown. 
All in all, a pretty cool and popular hotel. Constant stream of guests checking-in and walking out / coming back.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “not as bad as they say”
text:
Booked this hotel as It was the only one we could find for a five day shopping/sightseeing trip at the beginining of December.
After reading all the reviews I was very apprehensive. Some good postings were outweighed by the "very bad" reviews. The closer we got to the trip the bad postings became more and more. My wife is very fussy about cleanliness and for that reason I was dreading the trip, but we both agreed we wasnt going to NY to sit in a hotel room all day, so we wouldn't let it worry us.
On entering the hotel we were impressed by the lobby. Clean and Tidy, very busy. On checking in I asked if the room had been refurbed, to be told it had been a couple of years ago. I then asked for one which had been done more recently, and was given 1026 on the tenth floor. Putting the key in the door I slowly open the door expecting the worst.... but... NO. The room was smallish, but the bed was big. Bathroom very small, and hot water was a bit scarce !! One window, overlooking the back street, so noise was not a problem. As far as location goes you could not ask for more. Penn, MSG, Mac'ys and Empire state within five mins walk, and Times Square only 10 mins.
Overall for a two star hotel you get what you pay for. It must be a mega task to keep a 1700 room hotel spotless. My tip is to ask for a refurbed room when you check in. Dont pay to much attention to the scary postings you may have read, Didn't see a single mouse !! NY is fantastic, enjoy !!

name: Hotel Carter
title: “Hotel pourri mais super bien placé !!!”
text:
hôtel très vieux. le ménage laisse a désirer, il a fallu réclamer en deux fois pour avoir du papier toilette et du savon et les autres jours pour avoir des serviettes propres!
la télé, avec 3 chaines doit dater des années 50, les meubles de la chambre hors service et le matelas avec des ressorts qui vous massent la nuit !
un seul atout à cet hotel c'est son emplacement, à 100 mètres de Times Square! C'EST TOUT !!!!!!!

name: Empire Hotel
title: “Completely overrated. Empire in name only.”
text: We booked 4 rooms (for 8 people) for 7 nights, specifically requesting non-smoking and Superior Rooms and somehow ended up with 3 tiny rooms (obviously Standard Rooms) on the smoking floor on our first night with unsightly views of the buildings directly opposite, and only 1 Superior Room on a non-smoking floor. Like others before me have mentioned, there was no room for suitcases, let alone ourselves in these rooms. The lingering stench of stale cigarette smoke greeted us the moment the lift doors opened. Incredibly disappointing after 24hrs of flying from Australia. After complaining the following morning, the 3 tiny rooms were "upgraded" to the 11th floor. Admittedly these rooms were much larger, however, they were directly underneath the nightclub. We were lucky to get a few hours sleep each night. The thumping and droning sounds from above woke us up constantly and were especially bad on Friday and Saturday nights. When we complained about this to the hotel manager, we were told that he had not previously had any complaints from these particular rooms, which we find very difficult to believe, but has had complaints from other rooms on the 11th Floor. We also found one of the staff members at reception, Helena, to be particularly rude, unsmiling and unhelpful. As it is, I am writing this at 3am on our final morning in the hotel, as we have been rudely awoken by someone tripping the hotel's fire alarm system, not once or twice, but on last count six times! That, combined with the drone from above will ensure that we will not be getting any further sleep tonight. On a positive note, the hotel's location is brilliant and the rooftop pool deck is fantastic for those travelling in summer. Concierge was very helpful but understaffed.

name: Empire Hotel
title: “Not quite what we were expecting”
text: This was a 5 night trip for my Mother's birthday and the hotel did give us a great view, as requested. However, the room was a lot smaller than we expected, more like a small double than triple. We only had 1 mirror in the bathroom, which was tiny and with 3 girls this made getting ready a struggle! Far worse though was the noise in the early hours from music on the 10th floor (we were on the 11th). This is a nightclub run separately to the hotel and music goes on until 4am most nights! We ended up moving rooms to 6th floor, which was much quieter at night. On booking, the hotel had a spa on website but in fact, this had apparently gone months ago so we were disappointed, plus the pool is really just a plunge - the web photos make it look a lot more impressive and a lot of guests said the same thing. That said, the hotel staff were accommodating when we asked to move and in particular, concierge were great in helping us to book theatre and trips. Hotel is well situated, close to Central Park.

name: New York Marriott East Side
title: “Un hotel favoloso, in un posto MERAVIGLIOSO!!!!”
text:
Il nome di per se è già una gran garanzia (mai delusa da un Marriot), ma quando si entra nella hall di questo hote in particolare, già si respira l'aria di tranquillità, di eleganza, e di classe! Arrivati in camera, ci si rende conto della cura con cui ogni dettaglio è stato sistemato per rendere il più confortevole possibile il tuo soggiorno! Insomma, camera stupenda, molto spaziosa, il letto era buono (consiglio il king alle coppie, nel queen si rischia di stare strettini), la pulizia eccellente, peccato per il bagno che era un pò piccolino!
Vogliamo parlare della posizione? Noi abbiamo girato la città praticamente a piedi! Percorrendo solamente tutta la Lextington già ci si rende conto della zona in cui ci si trova, è piena di negozi stupendi, posti dove mangiare ogni 10 passi, e poi tutti i rumori di New York che la rendono così affascinante e unica! Si è a due avenue dalla 5th dove ovviamente c'è lo sfarzo più sfarzoso (scusate il gioco di parole), si può raggiungere Central Park, L'Empire, la Grand Central Terminal, le Nazioni Unite e molti altri luoghi di attrazione, a piedi! E poi vogliamo mettere l'emozione di uscire dall'albergo e trovarsi davanti il Chysler Building? Insomma se volete vivere New York veramente, dovete girarla a piedi, e questo è il posto ideale per farlo. Agli amanti dello shopping dico: ragazzi potete entrare in un negozio della 5th, uscire con mille buste, andare in albergo e lasciare le buste, uscire e ricominciare!!!! In una sola parola FANTASTICO!!!!
Stanza al 14esimo piano ottima, silenziosa e con bella vista su altri palazzi!
Unica nota negativa: un albergo così non può non dare gratuitamente la WIIFI in camera!

name: Hotel Grand Union
title: “Not a comfortable sleep”
text:
If you looking for a good nights sleep may want to consider your comfort....
foam like mattress too soft and 
window air condition is less than 2 feet from bed...not an ideal place for a good night sleep.

name: Excelsior Hotel
title: “Never again”
text: The Excelsior Hotel does not excel in any way. My wife and I wanted a romantic weekend in NY and chose the Excelsior due to the pictures we on its web site. I wish we did not judge this book by its cover. The staff was not only rude and arogant, but when asked a question the answer was usually just plain wrong. While we checked in the clerk received a telephone call and I stood there while she argued with the caller about retrieving her laundry before it was stolen. The continental breakfast would not have passed at a roadside motel let alone an upper west side hotel. The only saving grace was its location, very easy to access the entire city by foot or subway.

name: The Time
title: “Great Location, Great Atmosphere”
text: I chose to stay at the Time b/c of it's location. It's is right across the street from the theater where Chicago is playing. The Gershwin is right down the street and Time Square is right around the corner. It's a few blocks over from great shopping and Rockefeller Center and short walk to Central Park. The room was very clean and nicely appointed. The room had an awesome flat screen tv and very nice updated bathrooms. The staff was extremely accommodating and offered great recommendations for eating and night life. They offered turn down service complete with a chocolate on your pillow! Great value, awesome location, paired with a friendly, knowledgeable staff - what more could you ask for! I will definitely stay here again.

name: Hotel Wales
title: “First Trip to New York”
text:
My partner and I chose the Hotel Wales because the location was close to our friend's apartment. I had read the reviews that seemed good and the price was right (compared to other hotels in the area) and what a pleasant surprise. It was elegant yet cozy and comfortable. For a hotel over 100 years old, the decor was updated, the room and bed very comfortable, albeit small, but the bathroom with the huge walk in shower was over the top. Initially we were disappointed about being placed on the inside core of the hotel with no view but found it to be very quiet and peaceful and we were only there to sleep and get ready for our next adventure in the city. The rooftop lounge was very cool, but wish there were cocktails and snacks all the time rather than just a couple days a week. The location was very convenient to Central Park, the Museum District, and the subway was not far.
We also had breakfast at Sarabelle's. The food and service was great, but a little pricey.

name: The Bentley Hotel
title: “Excellent quality for an excellent value”
text: My fiance and I stayed here for a weekend Xmas/engagement trip. She of course did not know of my plans and the hotel staff, especially Su, Julietta and Roopesh who were absolutely fantastic about coordinating together to get us an excellent room with a view and level of service that was absolutely perfect to go along with our engagement. As an individual who was trying to plan a perfect weekend for our engagement, I couldn't have asked for a better group of people or a better facility to cater to our experience, making it such a memorable one for years to come!I would also like to extend a thank you to Peter Gallo, Conrad, and Gina from the central reservations department for being a great help towards booking the service we experienced! Thank you all from the bottom of our hearts for a great weekend!!

name: Stay.
title: “Very nice stay”
text: The location cant be beat, its just 10 second walk from Times Sq, staff were very friendly and hotel and room were very clean and modern! we couldnt hear anything from the outside considering its so close to Times Square but we were on the 9th floor. restaurant and Aspen club looked amazing but we didn't eat there! We couldn't complain of our room size for me it was ok, we had a small wardrobe and the beds are REALLY COMFY, some other guests complained that their rooms were really small and didn't even have a wardrobe. that wasn't our case. I recommend this hotel to anyone, plus price cant be beaten!

name: Cosmopolitan Hotel - Tribeca
title: “Great for the price”
text: This is a nice hotel in a fantastic location, and for Manhattan inexpensive. If you're traveling alone or as a couple on the cheap, they have loft-style rooms, with the bed on the 2nd level. But, if you are tall (or average height if you're a male), you'll have to watch your head. That level was designed for the 5'7" and under crowd. The furniture is tasteful and modern in an IKEA sort of way. If you don't need amenities beyond a tiny shampoo and mouthwash, it's a great place to stay.

name: Soho Grand Hotel
title: “Hip Hotel, Great Neighborhood”
text: I stayed at the Soho Grand for four days on my first trip to New York. The Queen Deluxe room was much larger than I would have expected for a NY hotel, and was appointed tastefully. Large down pillows and soft sheets made for a comfortable sleep. When I had down time it was relaxing to lounge on the bed and watch the flat screen TV. The hotel is newer (built in 1996), but has a retro quality. The lobby has a very cool atmosphere with eclectic music playing softly throughout the day. At night, a DJ played in the lounge. Location is excellent with plenty of restaurants nearby. Close to several subway stations as well. Unique hotel in a cool neighborhood is a nice break from the lights and noise of mid-town.
