Bonus feature- Soho Grand emailed me prior to my arrival see if I wanted a loaner iPod and Bose docking station, as well as a Goldfish in my room (Yes, Goldfish).

name: Hotel Grand Union
title: “Excellent for the price!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at the Grand Union for 6 nights in June and found no fault in it at all. We were on quite a tight budget so did not want to spend too much on a hotel. After reading the other reviews on Trip Advisor we decided on the Grand Union and were glad that we did.
The hotel room was larger than we expected, extremely clean and quiet. The staff were not over friendly but certainly not rude! There was a fridge in the room which was useful and reception provided me with a hairdryer for free on request. The internet access was good. The hotel also stored our luggage on the final day at no extra cost. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone on a budget.
The only thing I would have to say was not so good was the food at the diner attached to the hotel. We ate breakfast there once and were not very impressed.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Looked at 2 rooms and LEFT!”
text:
Unless you can do Penn 5000 (the only decent rooms), do NOT stay at this hotel. 
We were in NYC on business. I booked "Superior" rooms and were told they were lovely. I checked in and found dirty hallways, rooms without numbers (some were written in by hand in marker), and a tiny, grimy, unsanitary room. The walls looked like they hadn't been painted in 30 years, covered with scuffs and dirt, the areas around light switches dark from use. The grout around the tile in the standup shower was black. The ceiling in the bathroom was heavily peeling with plaster puckering out. Remember, this was "Superior"!! I asked for another room and was assured it would be better. The second room had stained and dirty carpet, a heavily worn toilet seat, broken furniture...I couldn't even bring myself to sit on the bed. I was with a group of 5, including my boss. One of my colleagues had already checked in and her room was also horrible. She found long strands of hair on the towels.
NYC was nearly sold out, but I managed to find other hotels for us and we left. The manager did not charge us for canceling and did offer to move us to the Penn 5000 rooms, but it was too late. So many international travelers stay at the Penn -- it's embarrassing to think that this is their only impression of American hotels. The place is a DUMP.

name: Comfort Inn Times Square South
title: “Adequate”
text: The hotel was in a good location. The room was clean but very small and in the basement! The best I can say about the room, besdies being clean, was that the water in the shower was hot and had good water pressure. The breakfast buffet was adequate.

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “Belleclaire's cool if you book the Diner special”
text:
Hotel Belleclaire is in a fairly quiet (for New York City) neighborhood, the Upper West Side, so it's not a 'partyer' hotel, but that was fine by us. It's still close enough to the touristy areas (Lincoln Center, Times Square, etc.) that it doesn't feel out of the way. The economy room is actually pretty spacious for NYC but the shared bathroom had a funky smell and the door didn't really close all the way! The room also comes with a sink but our room didn't have a light near the sink so at night you couldn't see in the mirror to shave, wash your face, etc. However, the room and bathroom are clean so overall our stay was comfortable. The restaurants in this neighborhood do tend to close on the early side (by 10pm) although there are a couple cheap 24hour options nearby. 
We did a great deal on the "Manhattan Diner" special where you get breakfast free at the diner across the street every morning. That was a big plus. The service was also really friendly and helpful, although I didn't trust the advice from the 'concierge' in the gift store.

name: Stay.
title: “Great location”
text:
We stayed here for 5 nights. After reading about the other reviews, I was a bit nervous about the size of the rooms, so tried to prepare myself. We also booked our room on the 8th floor as we did not want the noise from the bar...and how lucky we did!! The bar was rented out on 2 occassions, while we were there, for a private party and they were loud!
The first impression of our room was good. I imagined it much smaller. We had enough room to store our suitcases on the floor but the "wardrobe" was small. We only hung up essential items. Bed was comfy, bathroom was small...It could do with an update, our sink had a hairline crack, which did not make it look nice. We did not have a problem with the door keys, there is a small arrow on the card, which shows the way you have to use it. 
The aircon in the room was very noisy, which was suprising for NY, where everything is airconditioned. We only turned it on, when we left the room. There are air con units on the side of the building as well, which humm, but this is NY and it is noisy. 
Some of the staff were really friendly, especially the cleaners and door staff, but the rest were pretty unfriendly. I`m not sure if that was the NY mentality though...
The location of the hotel is fab....It is 5 seconds walk from Times Square and we could see the M&M billboard from our room. 
The lobby area looks nice and shiny, the lift is slow, but again, we went prepared and did not mind walking down the stairs a few times instead. 
Would I return?---Yes, with an upgrade
Would I recommend?-- Probably, again, only with an upgrade.

name: Hudson New York
title: “I nearly cried!”
text:
I booked through Trailfinders at fairly short notice ( a month ahead) and for a period during New York Fashion Week so accept that my choice was limited. This was a surprise birthday present for my partner and I wanted it to be as close to perfect as possible. Checking in was fine and the public areas of the hotel are quite stunning if you can cope with the very dim lighting. 
However, I nearly cried when we opened the door to our room. My university hall of residence room back in the 70s was bigger than this and this was supposed to be for two people. There was barely space to get in or out of bed except from the bottom end of the bed. Lighting was "moody" but useless. Hanging space was minimal and there was nowhere to store luggage. The bathroom was the tiniest I have ever seen on dry land with one of the shelves coming away from the wall so, again, nowhere to put toiletries. No robes, no tea or coffee making facilities, although a hairdryer and iron were provided and the shampoo, conditioner and body lotion were good quality (Aveda).
There was a permanent musty smell and the air conditioning was very noisy. Hardly conducive to a romantic holiday! The room might be OK for a single person but not for a couple no matter how close you are! It might be OK for one night, maybe two, but we were staying for five!
A further disappointment was that on two nights the main bar was closed for a private party and the library bar as well on one night. The rain stopped access to the roof terrrace. As the cost of drinks was pretty outrageous, we were really only interested in people watching but it was made clear that this wasn't going to be an option unless we were prepared to stand all night in a dark corner of the foyer.
All in all, very disappointing.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Best Location in NY. Worst service in NY. You decide.”
text:
Pay attention, cause I stayed at this hotel about 6 times during the years, almost every time I've been to New York. And I really know what to expect from Wellington.
The good: location. If you think location is everything, don't think twice and book it. It's 2 blocks away from Cenral Park and about 10 blocks from Times Square, but you do want that. It's a 10 minutes nice walk at maximum, and you skip the frenzyness of being into Times Square, which I'm not sure it's a good option. That's why I had always chosen Wellington... untill NOW.
One of the problems: BEDROOMS. Some COUPLE bedrooms are really nice, and most of them are resonable and acceptable for such a crowded and expensive city like New York/ Manhattan. Problem is if you are with a friend and want a twin bed. The twin bed rooms SUCK HARD. IMAGINE CROWDED - VERY CROWDED ROOMS. If you're out for shopping (most of us are in NY, don't we?), there's no place for you and your luggage in the room. It's an exercise of logistics and there won't be any place left for circulation or even cleaning. You can choose Queen Bed room - allright - there are nicer ones - but isn't this hotel already overpriced???
Bathroom - another problem - mine was so crowded that I couldn't even open the toilet with taking the toilet paper out of the support - if you can believe that! Only when the paper was half used, the toilet would open properly - hehe this was surely someone's joke. There's no space for anything besides you and one personal item at a time at the twin room bathroom - any woman would surely hate that.
Baggage is always a problem here. There are LONG LINES - REALLY LONG - to leave baggage in the store room and take them out, the lobby is always extremely crowded, lot's of people hanging in every place. My gosh, it's a hell inside.
As usual in NY, all works much better with good tips. No tips in hand, and the bel men staff can be VERY RUDE - even agressive.
Not sure where I'm gonna stay in NY next time - BUT I'LL AVOID WELLINGTON FOR SURE - there must be a better selection.

name: Hotel Carter
title: “schifoso”
text: Non vi recate mai e poi mai in questo hotel.........fa schifo!Vecchio, tenuto da cinesi e la moquette puzza.....Certo siete a due passi da Times Square ma credetemi spendete un pò di più e non farete il sangue marcio. Noi abbiamo dormito con i profumatori per le valigie sotto al naso pur di non sentire quel fetido odore nelle nostre narici.

name: Soho Grand Hotel
title: “Classy hotel, nice stay at impressive hotel”
text: Having seen the lobby of the hotel, I wanted to stay at the hotel for so long. I booked a special weekend package and got a very good deal. The service was nice, people are very kind and very helpful. the athmosphere is very stylish and the hotel is calm. It has a soothing effect. My room was very nice although not so extravagant as the lobby. I was hoping for more art deco in the room. The bathroom has a classic design and was nice. The Shower was good which is important to me. And of course, the view. I had a delux grand room, it has a superb view of midtown, empire state, Chrysler, time Square ... And all the water containers of SOHO. I had a great experience and hope you will too.

name: Park Central
title: “Fantastic Location .....Great price ...Thoroughly enjoyed our stay”
text:
We stayed here for 5 nights at the end of August.Got a great deal on the internet
Stayed in a Concierge King room.Keep looking on their website as prices are changing virtually every week(cancelled my first two reservations and rebooked as price kept changing ...almost 50% reduction on original price I was quoted) .Ideal location for most of the sights.All of the staff were great and had no problem with the lifts.
Overall great value and would recommend this hotel !!!!

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Location, but that's about it..”
text: If you go to NYC to tour the city, see the sites, and enjoy the night life, this hotel might be a good fit. If your coming to relax and stay in... Spend more $$$ and pass on this place. The rooms are small and have not been updated in years. The color scheme is dingy and old. Tiles are cracked, fixtures dont work, cables are hanging out of the wall. But it has a great location, and decent price point.

name: Club Quarters Midtown
title: “Great location”
text: They allowed us to check in early (11am) Nice clean room. Small, but its NYC under $200. Water cooler with bottles on each floor is a nice touch. It was perfect for a quick overnight in the big apple! Repeat guest at this hotel and will be back.

name: Chelsea Savoy Hotel
title: “Looking for double beds, great location, and a place to sleep and get ready without the high price? Chelsea Savoy is the one!”
text:
Found out not too many hotels that are reasonably priced in New York offer two double beds. Thankfully we came across Chelsea Savoy! Great prices for 4 people...trust me! It's a great location too...several blocks (like 20) up you can walk to Times Square (lots of stuff on the way up), 1 block from Avenues of the Americas with tons of shopping and eating. Walking distance to madison square park and Shake Shack! The subway are located literally around the corner outside the hotel either at 7th or 8th ave. there's a few bars around the area and walking distance to restaurants. 
To be honest we only used the hotel to get ready in and sleep. With so much to do in NY there was no point staying in the room. Front desk was very nice-always saying hi and bye when we walk in and out. When we first arrived, we were several hours before check in but they allowed us to leave all our bags with them so we can start to explore. 
Not really a view, but I wasn't there for that. Two beds, clean room, cozy for 4 adults. Flat tv ad lots of plug in outlets (ESP for girls!) bathroom was a good size--only problem is out tub was a little clogged ad took some time to drain, but we didn't mind. 
Great housekeeping!!! SO nice! We alway left late in the morning because we came from west coast time. Even if they were done doing their rounds, they would come back to check on us of we needed the room clean. Always gave us extra towels (the best!) and room was tidy everytime we came back. Lots of drawer space and closet. Not a fancy hotel but great for its purpose and great staff! Highly recommend.

name: The Bentley Hotel
title: “Great Hotel and outstanding service from staff”
text: I recently had a 5 day break in NYC with a girlfriend. It was both our first visit to NYC. The hotel was spot on. The staff are incredible, they simply cannot do enough for you and their service cannot be faulted. Bar having to pay for Internet usage and maybe a new Interior decorator to boost a few decorative aspects in the rooms (odd flower features!), we really enjoyed our stay. The room was fantastic size, good view of the river, 2 huge and very comfortable double beds and everything was spotlessly clean. Thank you to all the staff for their brilliant and friendly service.

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “Location! Location! Location!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at the Belleclaire for 2 nights in the end of November 2005. This hotel is perfect if you're on a budget and just want to use the room to sleep after a full day out doing touristy stuff. Rooms are clean, staff is very nice and welcoming. But the best thing is its LOCATION. It's surrounded by very good dinners (there's one just around the corner to the right which has delicious food), it's near the tube and it's in a very quiet area. If you happen to arrive by car on a Tuesday after 12pm and find a parking space just in front of the hotel (as we did) you'll be happy to know that it's free and you only have to move the car by 11am on Thursday.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Reasonable hotel”
text:
This place is ok if you don't mind the usual bulk traveller sleeping place. Staff are good apart from perhaps the grumpiest barman in the state.
Rooms are a good size and the view is ok if you like lots of glass towers and advertising signs.
Main drawback is being close to the commercial hell of Times Square but I hear some like this sort of environment.
Showing a bit of wear and tear but not too bad.

name: Hotel Carter
title: “Hotel Carter - Espelunca perfeita!!!”
text: O Hotel e velho, sujo, assustador...mas a localizacao e perfeita...ao lado de um dos teatros da Broadway, e vc n anda nem um quarteirao e ja esta na Times Square. Se eu voltar a NY, volto para fica la novamente. Como eu ja sabia que o hotel era velho e provavelmente sujo...eu levei roupa de cama e toalha...e depois deixei por la! Como eu sabia que a limpeza das camareiras n iria ajudar muita coisa...assim que fiz o check-in pedi para n limparem o meu quarto...e assim fiquei um pouco mais tranquila tb. Enfim, pelo preco q se paga e pega localizao q se tem ele pra mim foi o melhor hotel q ja fiquei! :)

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “;no sleep for 4 nights!”
text:
stayed in the edisson for 4 nights overall first 2 nights then went on cruise when we arrived first room we were given was grotty 2nd room ok had been decorated but very noisy on return from cruise back to edison hotel for 2 more nights room given ok but again very noisy air con like a jet engine no sound proof from outside at all had no sleep at all on 2nd night reception not interested on checkout . 
location of hotel brilliant public areas beautiful shame about the state of the rooms very disappointed wouldnt go back what a shame needs serious updating ,our thoughts were also the same as several other guests

name: Club Quarters Midtown
title: “A real find in the heart of the action”
text: I was hesitant about a non-chain hotel in NYC--you never know what you might get, especially at such a low rate for a great location, but I was so happy with the decision to stay here. The hotel is just 2 short blocks off of Times Square and the theatre district (the reason for our visit), and was very clean, the most important part to us. Additionally, the hotel is quiet, modern but still has the "old New York" charm, and in a very safe area, We were able to check in early with no hassle and check out late, storing our bags there even afterwards until our train left that night. The staff was very helpful and kind and did I mention the terrific cost? I probaby would pay more for this gem of a hotel. I have absolutely no complaints and will definitely stay here again.

name: The Franklin
title: “Too small for comfort”
text: Had booked six night stay but left after one. Had the largest room , but: no place to put luggage, limited draw and closet space, tiny bathroom, but worst of all there was little space to move around since bed took up probably 80% of room. On the plus side was a great location and splendid staff, but none of this could make up for the limited space.

name: Hilton Manhattan East
title: “Affordable (for NYC) hotel with a "boutique" feel”
text: Very nice hotel. The rooms are definitely small, but very clean and the beds are really comfortable! Good quality mattresses and bedding make for a good night's sleep. One complaint is that the walls must be super thin because if a neighboring room is making a lot of noise in the middle of the night, you will hear every word. We actually had to ask the neighbors to keep the party noise down after they came in loudly at 3am. Other than that though, no complaints. I've stayed there twice and have been extremely satisfied with the customer service both times. Wish they had better water pressure, but all in all I would recommend this hotel, and will likely stay again.

name: Club Quarters Midtown
title: “Excellent location, great if long stays room is not a priority”
text: I stayed at the Club Quarters Midtown for 2 nights. The hotel is one of the typical narrow buildings sandwiched between two other buildings - what else would you expect in downtown NYC? The person at the desk was very courteous and offered us suggestions for dining etc. The rooms are tiny (again Downtown NY this is what you would get mostly). It was a confined space to say the least. The solitary window was small and above the air conditioner and was in a corner. So if you really want to see outside the room you would have to lean over the A/C and crane your neck (not the the view of the west 45th street is something you would want to be seeing for hours anyway). My only main gripe was that the bathroom door had no locks. It was a sliding door - to save space ofcourse but that doesn't mean it shouldn't have a lock. Other than that everything else was great. It was very quiet in the lobby as well as inside the room (though you can hear the garbage truck come after midnight and might bother you if you are light sleeper - but again, you would expect such things in a big city). But the location of the hotel was just fabulous. Near to Times Sqaure, walking distance to Radio City Music hall, close to 5th avenue etc. We happened to be there during brazil day and the avenue of americas was just wild with a huge crowd partying with road side shops etc. Lots of dining options nearby and quite a few deli shops next to the hotel for that morning coffee and breakfast. The hotel does give free coffee and more importantly free bottled water (which was a precious thing if sightseeing NYC on a warm day like we did during the 2011 Labor day). Overall, I would recommend this place for those who want a nice place close to Times Square (and all the activity) and just come to the room at night to get some rest before heading out again.

name: Hotel Carter
title: “SQUALLORE TOTALE!”
text: fondamentalmente sono stato costretto a sceglierlo in quanto ero a ny all'avventura con mia moglie e a ora tarda abbiamo scelto il primo a tiro che dall'esterno sembrava ottimo! alla reception freddi come ghiaccioli, riusciamo a farci capire e ovvio prenotiamo per una notte, si deve prima assaggiare la torta... ci accompagna su' un addetto dell'hotel e fino a qua' sembra tutto bene... apriamo la camera, non voglio esagerare ma mi veniva da vomitare!!! fortuna per loro che io non potevo farne a meno visto che non rimborsavano ed era tardi, uno squallore totale! armadio sporchissimo e rotto, lenzuola sporche, finestra rotta che spifferava, bagno sporchissimo e senza asciugamano nonche' con la vasca piena di calcare! mochette che puzzava, abbiamo dormito vestiti!!! neanche il coraggio di una doccia!!! una vergogna, dovrebbe chiudere a mio parere! costera' anche poco vista la sua posizione, pero'.... mai piu'!

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Pretty Good”
text: This place was pretty good. If you got lucky (on the right side of the hotel) the view of times square was nice. The hallways are a little grim, but I couldnt find anything wrong with the rooms or bathroom. The room was a little on the small side but, for NYC, probably considered big. No complaints-Id stay here again.

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “Location, Location, Location..............”
text:
We stayed here in September last year and opted for a room with a shared bathroom. The first room we were offered was quite big however, it smelt a bit damp and was quite far away from the bathroom. Therefore, the staff moved us to another room at our request and although the room was smaller, it was situated next door to a bathroom and did not have the damp aroma! This room and the shared bathroom were clean and although we did not have a fridge or in-room movies as per what is advertised, this did not matter to us.
The staff ranged from very friendly, to passive but were always on hand if required.
Best of all though, was the location of the hotel in the Upper-West Side which is a beautiful neighborhood with some good bars, restaurants and shops and everywhere else in Manhattan, that was not within walking distance was easily reached via the Subway. 
All in all, the rooms at the Belleclaire are perfectly fine and provide everything you need if you are going to be out and about the whole time and I would definitely stay here again, given the location and the decent room rates.

name: Dylan Hotel
title: “Excellent location, Very Clean”
text: Stayed in this hotel for three nights.Was told not to expect muchfrom NY hotels but this was very nice. Decent sized room with modern fittings and all very clean. Not much noise from outside either which wasquite good. Would definatley stay here again

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Location, Location, Location!”
text: This hotel ranks at about the most expensive (next only to Rome) of my travels, and that was at the Hot Wire Price. I shudder to think what it costs otherwise. Still, I was pleased. I am in need of a knee replacement, so the location right on Times Square meant that we could walk to see our friend perform at BB King's, walk to see "Phantom of the Opera," walk to see another friend perform just off Broadway, walk to take the Circle Line boat tour, and walk to the NBC studio tour . We saved a lot of money that way. The room was fine; At first we were put into a smoking room, and we said we needed a no smoking and were in a hurry, so the staff moved our bags, and when we came back we were in a similar room on the 46th floor with awesome views of the city. This entire floor is no smoking. There was a mini bar, which we never used, and an in room safe which we did use. I personally do not care for the ultra modern, black and brown decor, but that's the antique dealer in me! The room was spacious, with a chair and desk, and the bath was nice with adequate hot water. It would have been nice to have free wi-fi in the room, but I opted not to pay the extra $12.50 a night for that. There is free wi-fi in the lobby, which I used on my last day, while waiting for a cab to the airport. I am surprised at the negative comments about the staff, because I found them all to be extremely polite and helpful, from the bellboy who moved our bags, to the concierge who gave us written instructions on taking the subway to the 9/11 memorial. We already had our theatre tickets, but they had a separate theatre desk. Anytime we asked for anything, as shower caps, razor, etc, they always said they'd bring it right up, and always added "with pleasure." There was a tea/coffee maker in my room, but I had read that they were available upon request, so I asked for it, though was told all these "deluxe rooms," had that. The smoking room we had at first did not have one, but there were several at the desk in the foyer of the floor, so anyone could have it. We also asked for more hangers, etc, and everything we asked for was brought up, promptly. Their housekeeping department operates on a 24 hour basis, so I have no complaints. I did not try the restaurant or room service, but was told, by the concierge, of several good, fairly inexpensive (for NYC, anyway) restaurants in the area which were good. I would probably choose this hotel again, especially if I could get another third party discount. Even though it was expensive, the location made up for it. Yes, you can get cheaper places. You can save a lot by staying just across the river in New Jersey, or by staying on Long Island. I have done this before, but have now decided it isn't worth it for me. I saved a lot by being able to walk to a lot of main attractions. Also, the queen bed was very comfortable, and I did not hear any outside noise in the hotel.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Good value- ideal position.”
text: I had read many mixed reviews on this hotel ranging from excellent to awful so I went with an open mind. I was told that I had a recently renovated room. It was much smaller than rooms in the rest of the USA and the view was of another wall! Decoration was tired but nonetheless it was very clean and the bed comfortable. The bathroom was tiny but had been newly refurbished. At the end of the day the room served its purpose as somewhere clean and comfortable to spend the night. Staff were helpful. The hotel's position was fantastic being less than 5 minutes from Central Park but also within easy walking distance of the Rockefeller Centre and Times Square. The subway station was literally outside the door. I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to friends.

name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel
title: “Godt hotel midt i New York”
text: Meget fint hotel. Vi nød især den fine indendørs pool på 5 etage virkelig flot midt i New York. Værelset var fint servicen var i orden. Vedligeholdelsen af hotellet var dog langt fra danske standarder

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Good location, Very dated”
text:
Just back from another trip to NYC, we are very open minded and have stayed at a variety of locations and class of hotels. The Edison is without question in a great spot, right on Times Square and near the subway. The main issue is that what is advertised is far from what you find when you check in. The rooms were small, with not much space. The bathroom was tiny. You could wash your hand hands in he sink, your feet in the shower whilst having a number 2! 
Our room was nothing better than a decent hostel.

name: Cosmopolitan Hotel - Tribeca
title: “Reasonable....”
text:
This was accepable - no more no less. Breakfast at The Soda Shop wasn't our cup of tea. Strange and very expensive place. I needed a glass of milk to wake up after a night in the air. $2,75 + tax. The it was certainly paid!!
The following days we had breakfast at Starbucks. We met the locals and could have all the milk we wanted without paying extra.
The majority of the folks at the front desk did what they had to do - and you had to jump around telling silly jokes to make them smile. One of them them was outstanding when we had troubles with SuperShuttle on the day we left.

name: Hotel Wales
title: “$375 a night for a closet?????”
text:
I just found this website but would like to comment on a stay in December 2001. We had a special price of $275 a night supposedly a $100 discount off the regular rate. What we got for $275 was a small closet overlooking a small air
shaft. This closet did not have a closet to hang clothes in---only a small space behind a stationery mirror that could only be accessed by a tall left-handed person. The bathroom was almost as large as the room, but looked vintage 1920. The hairdryer did not work. The toiletries were nice, however. The room was clean, and the bed very comfortable, but $275 for this. There was supposed to be a
complimentary continental breakfast, but we were told it had been discontinued. Might it have been available if we were paying full price? I was apprensive about the location 4 blocks below the beginning of Harlem, but the neighborhood was very pleasant. In summary, the Wales is decent and respectable, but very much overpriced.

name: Stay.
title: “Amazing location, horrible room”
text: I brought my cousin from Texas to NYC (she had never been) and wanted to show her a good time. We decided to stay at the Stay Hotel, being super close to everything. The location is what you pay for- it was great to walk out onto Times Square! The price was unreasonable for the tiny, closet-sized room we booked. There was two of us and we couldn't move around at all! The bathroom was untidy and needed a deep cleaning. Our "city view" was of a brick wall with no daylight coming in. The hotel staff was very friendly and always willing to help us. The elevators were super small and couldn't fit two people plus luggage, so we constantly took the stairs. We were on the 2nd level, and the bar/club noise was unbearable. The elevator made an awful noise that kept us up all night. Perfect hotel for someone who wants to party all night-sleep all day! Perfect location though. Would stay again if the rooms were bigger!

name: The Bentley Hotel
title: “no heat???”
text: The hotel looks hip in the photos but it's aging badly. It's 60 degrees in our room and they tell me they can't turn on the heat. They brought a space heater but not exactly the accommodations I bought. View from the 21st floor is great but don't eat there.

name: Hotel Wales
title: “Hotel Wales”
text: Hotel piccolo ma carino.Punto dolente la colazione,ma per location e rapporto qualità/prezzo direi che è ottimo.A pochi metri trovate musei e nelle vicinanze la metropolitana.Praticamente in fronte all'Hotel si ferma l'autobus.

name: Dylan Hotel
title: “Good Boutique Hotel - a few problems”
text:
I stayed here mid January for three nights and was actually quite pleasantly surprised. Because I stay in NYC hotels at least 2-3 times a year, I pretty much know what to expect for the $300-$400 a night price range - small clean room, tiny bathroom, little to no view. I think once one's expectations are thus lowered, one can start looking at other details!
The queen size bed in 1106 was super comfortable - I absolutely adored the feather pillows, however a friend of mine, also staying in the hotel, hates feather pillows and was unable to get an alternative. The room was very clean, as was the bathroom. I particularly enjoyed the nightly turn down service (with chiocolates) and the bathroom amenities, shower gel, shampoo, conditioner etc which are packaged in chemistry type jars - very cool. There is a mini bar in the room (with non mini charges for the items contained within) and a coffee pot with complimentary coffee. Service was impeccable from the front desk, bellman, room service to restaurant and bar, I experienced them all and had no complaints.
I enjoyed the lobby, although not big, it did have plenty of seating room with complimentary copies of NY Post and USA Today.
The location is fabulous, especially if you want to be in midtown. The price was average, just under $300 a night for a standard queen room.
The areas of concern and opportunity - 
The shower temperature would fluctuate from just perfect, to icy cold several times within a 20 minute span. At first, I reacted, as anyone would, by turning the the temp control more towards hot, resulting in scalding water hitting me once the hot water returned, Needless to say, I soon learned to suffer through the few moments of cold without touching the control! There were 7 of us staying in separate rooms - we all had the same problem.
The heat in my room was suffocating - and it wasn't even turned on! There was absolutely no way, that I could tell, to effectively regulate the temperature in my room. I even had someone up to look at the strange thermostat (which didn't seem to work at all) and he agreed that my heat wasn't even on. Thank goodness I was able to open a window - I kept it open, in NYC in January for the entire 3 days I was there, and it still was very warm in my room. That give you an idea of how stifling it was. 
The lighting in the room is very good for those of us who think "green" and want to save energy, however, it truly was substandard. Even with all the lights on, the room had that eerily green flourescent glow, and I found it hard to read, even with my glasses on. This was also true in the bathroom - not easy to apply make-up for some of us middle aged women!.
Bathroom had little to no space to put your own toiletries etc. and had no bath tub - which didn't bother me, but bothered others in my group.
If you are looking for a view, don't expect one here - we all ended up with views of the windows of an office building directly next to the hotel - I kept my drapes closed at all times for obvious reasons. I'm sure there are some rooms with better views, we just didn't get any!
There is some scaffolding around the building - however, I really had no objection to this.
All in all, I enjoyed my stay at this hotel. The issues, to me, were minor and the good far outweighed the bad. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “There are better options for the same money in New York-- go to the Warwick!”
text:
Hi there,
I never ever write reviews for anything just because I am always skeptical about the outlook of people who give scathing reviews and wonder if the glowing reviews are written by hotel staff/ affiliates. However, my experience at the Millenium has been so terrible it deserves a review. I have been in New York for a few days over the past couple of weeks. So, I have stayed in a number of mid-range priced hotels-- the Warwick, the Westin near times square and now the Millenium. The Millenium is by far the worst I have ever seen. 
I checked in at 7pm following my flight, and my room was not yet ready. Apparently, the room wasn't clean yet. So, I ask how long the room will take to be ready. The man at the desk responds that they are extremely short staffed and no one has the guts to tell the managers for fear of losing their jobs but that they are doing the best they can. He then throws drinks coupons at me, and asks me to wait. I proceed to the bar and have one drink and a salad. This takes about an hour. My room still isn't ready. I head back to the bar where I chat with other clientele who like me, have their bags and no room. 
At 9:30pm I am told my room is ready and that I am being upgraded to the Premier Tower. My room is on an extremely low level and backs up to an alley. So, I can hear all the LOUD sounds of the city and all the rooms when I step inside my room. I then notice that the bed is dirty, sheets are thrown all over, and the bathroom smells funky. This was the beginning of my stay. I will never stay there again, and will tell everyone I know to go to the Warwick. It is cheaper, cleaner and quieter. It is a better hotel. This hotel was the absolute pits--- please avoid at all costs and do not book your clients there!

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Never never ever againI cannot”
text: I can't understand how this hotel can still be operating considering it's condition. We were moved at our request to three different rooms one no better than the other--torn wallpaper,dirty, worn and stained carpeting along with rotted woodwork. The room was so depressing we checked out a day earlier forfeiting $200.00. Dont't let the impressive lobby fool you.

name: The Franklin
title: “No vayáis, es un timo¡¡¡”
text: Es un hotel pésimo, mal cuidado, en donde no funciona nada como debiera. El servicio es malísimo, se funden los plomos de la habitación, no funciona la calefacción, el desayuno no puede ser más pobre y, además, te cobran al final 12 dólares por persona y día por un supuesto servicio que no te dan. No sé cómo se puede recomendar el Hotel Franklin al precio que vale. Si no lo hubiera pagado por adelantado me hubiera ido a los 10 minutos de llegar. El personal del hotel, empezando por el director, es maleducado y no solucionan los contínuos problemas que surgen por su mal estado de conservación: se limitan a decir que es un hotel viejo. Las habitaciones son pequeñísimas, el armario para guardar la ropa es impresentable y el cuarto de baño es como de pensión de tercera categoría. Recomendaría a Hoteles.com que lo sacara de sus hoteles, porque la decepción es tan grande que acabarán perdiendo clientes.

name: The Franklin
title: “hotel molto carino e molto ben posizionato”
text: l'hotel è davvero un gioiello, anzi gioiellino visto le ridotte dimensioni. abbiamo viaggiato in 2 e la camera petite queen è fin troppo "petite"!!: molto carina, pulita e curata nei minimi dettagli, ma davvero troppo piccola per 2 persone con bagagli (non c'è armadio!!) e lo spazio vitale è ridotto all'osso. consiglio di spendere qualche dollaro in più per una stanza più grande. per il resto eccezionale, wifi impeccabile, come il servizio dell'hotel.

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “Helt ok med bra service”
text:
Bodde 6 nätter. Rummet var ganska litet, men funkade för oss. Rent och fräscht, dock lite slitet. Nära till flera riktigt bra supermarkets samt frukostställen, bl a Café Lalo. Det finns ingen resturang på hotellet, så man får äta ute eller köpa med sig till rummet. Gratis och riktigt hyggligt kaffe finns i receptionen.
Belleclaire ligger lite avsides, men det är väldigt nära till tunnelbanan (Linje 1) som går via Times Square till South Ferry.
Ett stenkast från Central Park.
Fri wifi på hotellet.

name: Hilton Manhattan East
title: “Very Good Value in East Manhattan”
text:
I think I got a room during the work week for under $200. Are you kidding me? A room in NYC under $200!? And in a decent neighborhood?!?
The hotel has recently undergone renovations. It looks like Hilton bought 2 small hotels that were close together and formed them into one Hilton hotel, so this is not your traditional Hilton property. It's more like a 2 towered boutique hotel. I made the mistake of going up the wrong set of elevators and into the wrong tower. That's how I found out! 
Anyway, backing up a bit, I checked in on a Tuesday night. Check-in staff very friendly and helpful. I was told that I received a Hilton Gold member upgrade. Great! However, I got to the room and thought, "Really? This is an upgraded room?!?" It was very small...even for Manhattan. Probably about 180 square feet. The view was non-existent. I wonder what my original room looked like! But, for the price, I really couldn't complain. And the room was cute,clean, and appointed with normal Hilton stuff, and the bed slept perfectly fine. I had no issues whatsoever. 
I would stay here again, easily, for the price. I was just 2 blocks away from the Shuttle to Time Square and I could walk to Time Square in about 20 minutes. A great great alternative to the uber expensive properties around W. 42nd St.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Hotel Edison in Heart of Times Sq, NYC”
text: Lew,June,Cherie & Dan visited NYC 7-14 thru 7-17-12 & stayed at Hotel Edison right on 47th St ( at 7th Ave) Times Sq. Very convienient to subways, restaurants, ect. Room had 2 queen beds, good tv; but air conditioner needs to be revamped mostly hot air. Bathtub very hard to control water on shower; very strange set of faucets in there. Not much room in bathroom at all. Good value though for the price. Everyone was very friendly; except bellhops. They didn't respond very well when asked a question. Maybe they didn't speak English well. Check in & checkout was very efficient. To store luggage before we left had to pay a small fee .50 each bag; which isn't bad; but when picking up luggage they didn't have a good system. Had to wait in long line; which was stressful as we had to get going walking back to Port Authority for Greyhound bus. Like I said; good value for money spent; but would have liked better air conditioning & at least a vanity outside small bathroom for easier get ready for 4 people.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Ideal Times Square Location”
text: Located at 7th Avenue and West 44th St. in Midtown Manhattan, this hotel is within walking distance of Times Square, the theatre district, restaurants, and many tourist attractions. Subway stations are also located nearby on W 42nd St. Had a one-bedroom suite on the 50th floor which had a full ensuite bathroom and a secondary bathroom. Only negative was the line-ups for the elevators during busy times. Be aware that when using the hotel's wireless internet system, the charge is per day per device.

name: Stay.
title: “Good but a little noisy and dark rooms”
text: A very centrally located hotel with nice employees and good cleaning. On the downside: Dark rooms, irritating elevators (to small and extremely slow) and poor noise isolation towards hallway. The location makes it unavoidable that there is trafic noise, but that is only to expect. Relatively stiffly priced rooms compared to i.e. deals offered at Intercontinental Times Square at 44th and 8th where my friends stayed. So i am not tempted to come back. All in all.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Poorly managed hotel - check-in and room cleaning slow”
text:
We were very disappointed with this hotel. During the day, the lobby looked more like another airport terminal with people waiting to check-in. Nowhere near enough chairs, so people were sitting on the floor.
The check-in time was 3.00pm, but they couldn't be bothered to clean our room until 4.00pm. No apology whatsoever. Queues to check-in were long. When we eventually got into our room, it was small, but fortunately was by then clean!! There were crumbs on the carpet outside our room door. In four days the carpet was never vacuumed!
I have travelled extensively and have never stayed in such a badly-run hotel. I loved New York and hope to go back there one day, but it certainly won't be at this hotel. They gave me the impression that they couldn't care less about their customers.

name: Cosmopolitan Hotel - Tribeca
title: “very very happy”
text: If your main necessity is not a big room and a lot of space, then this is an excellent place to stay. Extremely clean, good service, excellent location, subway just in front, and very affordable. Will absolutely stay there every time I return to NY. I recommend it!

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “EXCELENTE HOTEL”
text: pasé un fin de año excepcional en nueva york y este hotel nos completó la experiencia, buenisima ubicación, a unas calles de times square, en la avenida madison llena de tiendas y atracciones, podiamos llegar caminando a casi cualquier punto (times square, rockefeller center, grand central station, empire state, macys, la quinta avenida) el personal fue muy amable, hasta nos preparaban desayunos especiales, y en general el hotel es muy limpio y bellisimo, sobre todo en esa época por sus arreglos navideños

name: Hilton Manhattan East
title: “Good hotel now with a touch of Hilton modernity.”
text:
I stayed here once before when it was called the 'Tudor' hotel because of the good location. East 42nd street gives easy access to midtown by foot or cab and i can walk or get a taxi easily to any sight, midtown meeting, or the shopping areas. the swanky Helmsley hotel is almost right next door so you know you are in the right location. not stuck uptown or downtown.
The Tudor was a landmark hotel, i.e. an old manhattan one with brass foyer doors, pavement canopy, sturdy bathroom fittings, and features like that which i liked, Hilton have kept these features, which is great, staying here i know im in manhattan from the feel of the place.
what Hilton have done is totally refurbished the foyer and restaurant, they have done a good job, and they have done the same to the rooms. room lighting, colours and feel were perfect for me. The result is that they have breathed new life back into a nice but tired old hotel. Its also means i can now get Hilton points on my loyalty card.
However be warned, its still an old Manhattan building so the rooms are not big. But they are clean. well quipped, and the beds are good. incidentally the number and location of power points is impressive. I had more than six sockets to choose from!! some 5 stars hotels fall flat on that one...
i like the fact that its has quirks like a strange light control unit with lots of buttons, older bathroom fittings, a brass doorbell! This tells me im in manhattan and thats great.
The airconditoning works well, no problems here, i had it on the lowest setting and it was fine, (other have complained on her but A/c is never silent..) and the wall controller was brand new. The bathroom had what looked like a brand new illuminated mirror which was huge and didn't steam up after my shower.. i like that.. and it had a nighlight, excellent. The old Tudor hotel had black marble washbasin areas, Hilton have kept them. And the plug in the sink worked... again many 5 star places i have been to dont get the plug right.
The WIFI worked perfectly too...
i like this hotel.... for businesspeople who are practical, economical, and like to feel like they are in Manhattan its great value, and comfortable, and has lots of sockets and a big flatscreen TV.. Although the desk area in my room was very small. This is the one and only negative point in my view.
If you are on holiday, its also great value and comfortable. But be warned, if you are expecting a view of the manhattan skyline you will have to go somewhere else and pay about two or three times as much for your room. This is no skyscraper, but what it is is a nice old hotel which now has the care and attention of Hilton to look after it. And when you step out the front door, look left and there is the beautiful Chrylser building, what more can you ask for? :-)
Staff were all excellent, breakfast hot and cold all good.
And there are a couple of lively local bars across the street (which wont trouble you with noise) if you fancy a nightcap and find the hotel bar too quiet...
check the hotel website for pics in case the ones on here are pre - refrubishment

name: Stay.
title: “THE BEST FRONT DESK IN TOWN”
text: JAZYLYN, FATEMA AND NORMA they are the best. Jazylyn always smiling, Fatema takes a while to smile but she is great and Norma new in the hotel and a very nice person and very effective. Norma was a great acquisition and we hope she stays forever. Walter is the best concierge around, always a helpful person. Besides he knows everything and speaking in at least three languages. Me and my wife had a good time in the hotel and we thank these fantastics people. Luis and Maria Scarlet Araujo

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text: I stayed in this hotel with two friends in December; we booked a double double room, which consisted of two bedrooms and a little kitchenette. The hotel has seen better days and could do with being re decorated as the decor was a little jaded. Our room was very dark as the windows looked out on to a shaft. The room was always too hot and there was no way to reduce the heat. While they provided a little kitchenette, there were no cups or cutlery of any kind. There was a kettle and a fridge but you couldn't make a cup of tea so it seemed rather pointless. The hotel is very clean and the location is excellent. All in all, it suited us as we wanted somewhere central, clean and very reasonably priced. This hotel is fine if you plan to spend very little time at the hotel, and who wants to sit in their hotel when they are in New York.

name: The Bentley Hotel
title: “Une vue de rêve à l'avant dernier étage !”
text:
J'ai réussi à me payer cet hôtel grâce à une formidable promotion, alors à ce prix là, j'ai été comblé, la chambre était spacieuse (une suite junior) et la vue incroyable ! Mais si j'avais dû payer le prix fort, je dirais que c'est un peu cher pour le service...
Un autre point fort: la literie est incroyable !!! je n'ai jamais dormi aussi bien de toute ma vie ! Alors, après des heures de marche, c'est très apprécié !

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “At Times Square but not the best”
text: We stayed in the part of the hotel strangely called the Premier Hotel. Premier it was not...A reasonable place to stay very close to Times Square with staff that were mostly unhelpful and more often than not were nowhere to be found. Trying to catch a cab in 44th Street was imposssible (although that is common in NY) and you end up paying premium for a town car. The room was acceptable, quiet although not shielded from the bright lights of neaby Times Square awnings. Given that a buffet breakfast was included in this "sale" price, it was quite reasonable. It would certainly not be worth paying the usual rate charged for hotels in this area.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “4th visit already planning 5th”
text: Stayed for 4 nights, 4 of us shared a suite, and well worth the extra money...we had a fantastic time, rooms spacious, clean and any problems fixed in double quick time. Staff at Park Cafe even helped when our wine opener snapped....opening our bottle, so it was feet up and relax after a busy day! As everyone says, great location...you will see lots! Another tip....try and arrive at 4pm and allow for 2hrs to get to hotel, unpack and walk to Rockerfellar Centre and travel up 67 floors in 43 seconds to see the Manhatten by night!! Cost $20 but $2 dollar vouchers in leaflets hotel lobby.

name: Hotel Grand Union
title: “Tolles kleines Hotel direkt am Empire State Building”
text: Kleine schnuckelige Zimmer im Zentrum von New York. Tolle Adresse, wenn man mitten in New York übernachten möchte. Die Zimmer sind zwar klein aber ausreichend. Im Zimmer gibt es ein großes Bett, einen Tisch mit zwei Stühlen und einen Schrank mit einem TV drin. Das Bad ist klein aber man kann sich trotzdem drin bewegen. Und seien wir mal ehrlich, wenn man in New York Urlaub macht, dient das Hotel doch eh nur zum Schlafen. Direkt gegenüber vom Hotel gibt es eine Frühstücksmöglichkeit. Die U-Bahn Station ist direkt vor der Tür. Nettes Servicepersonal und sehr hilfsbereit. Gerne wieder. Für uns in New York ein ideales Hotel und Standort um alles in New York erkunden zu können.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “my stay june 2012”
text: This was my first time in new york, this hotel was right next to time square with easy access to anything i wanted to do. My room was just fine, clean and tidy. during my stay they had begun decorating the rooms and corridors and laying new carpets and all was looking nice. I would recomend this hotel to anyone wishing to see the city. There is a bar attached with a guy that comes to play the piano, kinda jazz music he was EXCELLENT and i spend severall hours watching him. Overall a great location and a good quality hotel.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Good Tourist Hotel”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for a couple of nights in May 2012. The hotel itself has an "art deco" styled lobby area with cafe off the main entrance. The reception staff, porters etc were all courteous and helpful as were the staff in the cafe where we had breakfast. There is also a deli next door with seating upstairs.
Our room was on the 14th floor, but not having been refurbished was very tired indeed although clean enough; also the air conditioning unit did not work which would be more of a problem in the summer months (work is presently ongoing refurbishing rooms).There was very little noise from the traffic when the window was closed but on the second night there was a fair bit of noise from a pneumatic drill on the construction site opposite in the early hours (to be fair this was probably exceptional).
The hotel itself has a great location and is no more than 100 yards from Times Square and within walking distance to Central Park and many other attractions.
Having stayed in a few Manhattan Hotels, this one stands out for its location and is probably competitively priced when compared nightly rates at some Manhattan hotels - after all with so much to do very little time is spent actually in the hotel.

name: Cosmopolitan Hotel - Tribeca
title: “Great value/Learned a lesson...”
text:
I've learned from trying incessantly to get hotel deals in NYC that you will have trouble doing better than the Cosmopolitan. The rooms are spotlessly clean, the beds are comfortable and although the staff can seem impersonal, it may be because they aren't familiar with tourism and honestly don't know the answers to your questions. There is a market just over the street where you can get cold drinks, chips, sandwiches, etc., and masses of restaurants that deliver including a terrific breakfast place whose name escapes me. There's one of the oldest and best French brasseries in the city, L'Odeon, two blocks away, and a plethora of new, hip restaurants recommended in Zagat within a short walking distance. You can walk up to Soho in moments. 
Century 21, the best discount store in the world, is five minutes' walk away. I've learned my lesson, have tried more expensive hotels that were less clean and paid a lot more. I won't do it again, I'll just come back here.
BUT, AND A BIG BUT, MAKE SURE YOU DON'T GET A ROOM NEXT TO THE MAIDS' CLEANING ROOM/ CENTER...THEY START EARLY IN THE MORNING AND THEY SHOUT LOUDLY TO EACH OTHER AND ARE REALLY NOISY IN SOME DRAMATIC CENTRAL EUROPEAN LANGUAGE AND YOU WON'T GET MUCH SLEEP AFTER 9 A.M. IF YOU ARE NEAR THEM!!!!

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “Hotel tres agreable et bien placé à Mnhatan”
text:
Un tres bon hotel , propre , bien decoré et chambres tres pratiques et tres propres. Le personnel est adorable et à disposotion à tout moment. Je recommande cet hotel , il est bien placé 2o min maximum a pied de time square.
Tres bien desservi niveau metro et bus , juste en bas de l'hotel . On est parti en famille et le confort de l'hotel etait tres bien ! On a passé de tres bonnes vacances et on a bien profité de New York !

name: Hotel Stanford
title: “Hotel Stanford - Not awful, not great.”
text:
The Hotel Stanford is very much a small budget place. It’s fairly conveniently located on 34th Street and Broadway and is right next to a subway station, Manhattan Mall and Macy’s. The delights of Times Square are a 10 block walk if you are suitably energetic or one stop on the subway. There are a couple of nearby bars such as Jack Dempsey’s on W 32nd which was pretty good and had excellent food but if it’s a wild night out you be better heading to the Village or up to Hells Kitchen for a better selection of pubs.
The Hotel itself seems to cater for the Korean market as that’s who the clients seemed to be on the whole as well as a good proportion of the staff.
The room was small even by New York standards and could probably do with a bit of basic redecorating. The linens and towels were clean and replaced each day. The in room facilities were basic but the safe was a welcome addition. The bathroom was functional and clean but don’t expect loads of fluffy towels. The air conditioning was not great and even at the lowest setting didn’t really get the room totally cool and comfortable, in fact it was even malfunctioning when we arrived and had to get the Front Desk to arrange for an engineer to get it going.
The biggest minus for the room was the bed. A double in name but designed for a far smaller person. I’m 5ft 9 inches, hardly a giant and even I found the bed very small and narrow, but with another person in the bed it became very cramped and very uncomfortable.
The Hotel was relatively quiet although we were at the end of a corridor and on the 9th floor, with a partial view of the Empire State Building. You’d still be better off trying to sleep using ear plugs as NYC never really gets quiet even at the dead of night.
We didn’t take up the offer of the complimentary breakfast so cannot comment.
In general I would say that the Hotel was basic and functional. Clean with so-so staff and fairly convenient if you want to explore New York as a tourist.
The cost for the room was probably a little over the top for what we got but as with all budget hotels you take your chances. The low rating for this place is based on comparisons to better experiences in the past at other budget Hotels such as the Edison, Milford Plaza and the excellent Belvedere all of which were of a much higher standard than this place for only a few bucks more per night.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Hotel Roosevelt : splendeur passée”
text:
L'hôtel Roosevelt est bien situé. Le lobby a du caractère et le charme des années passées.
Chambres minuscules (on peut y mettre un lit de 140 cm, pas plus) et plutôt sonores (on entend tous les bruits du couloir).

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “Recommend with reservations”
text: Mostly pleasant staff and a large room helped to offset fact that the shared bathroom had only one small towel bar for 3 rooms, almost no hooks in the room, a stained carpet and a noisy air conditioner.Plus for hair dryer, iron, frig, tv. Very nice neighborhood.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “better then i expected”
text: when reading some reviews about the wellington i was a little scary of what i might find but when we got to our room preaty quickly it was lovely a little small but i mean your not going to be staying in there all day for most people but we were only in there when we woke up and we stayed out all day new york was so amazing lol, great maid service sheats changed every day highly recomeded for people with small children or teenagers.

name: Cosmopolitan Hotel - Tribeca
title: “La honte hôtel”
text: Avec mon amie on vient de passer deux nuit dans cette hotel à New-YORK , début août ,et on est déçu sur toute la ligne . D'abord le prix est exhorbitant: 545 dollars les deux nuits ,sans petit déjeuner ,pas de quoi se faire un thé ou un café !! avec un ascenceur qu'on attend à chaque fois plus de dix minutes ,et qui nous obligent à prendre les escaliers au moins deux fois sur trois . La chambre ! Deux grands lits occupant presque toute la pièce ,pas de lumière du jour ,fenêtre donnant sur cour à un mètre cinquante d'un autre immeuble , et impossibilité d'ouvrir la fenêtre unique ,donc pas d'air . De plus un personnel d'acceuil assez antipathique . A éviter +++++

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “You get what you pay for”
text: When we booked this hotel we were told by the travel agent that it wasn't a luxury hotel by any means but it was in a fantastic position, it was a safe area for walking round as a family and it was clean. And that is exactly what we got. The kids room with twin beds was far nicer than ours, with lovely old furniture and an amazing view and our double room was melamine furniture with a view of a wall but we were out exploring the city from 8am to 10pm and just wanted to sleep when we got back so anything more luxurious would have been wasted on us. It was clean and warm and I'd recommend it for a safe budget hotel for a weekend family trip.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Great stay for the money!”
text: This hotel is simple, functional, and nothing beats it for what you do there: sleep. We got a free upgrade just for asking, the hotel staff was wonderful and courteous. They attended to our needs promptly and were pleased to do so. The bathroom was teeny, tiny, but again functioned for the 3 night stay. We did not try the hotel restaurant or lounge so cannot review on that. However, there is nothing that beats this location and the room was clean and comfortable. Despite what some other reviews said, there are four elevators and all of them were very quick considering that there were over 20 floors in this old hotel.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Never ever ever again”
text: We have just got back from around the world extended trip and on our travels by far the worst Hotel we have ever stayed in was the Wellington Hotel. When we arrived the lobby looked ok when we checked but dont let that fool you. We took a lift to our room if that is what you would call it....it was small very small, the bed just about fitted in because of another small bed with straps across it was across the end of it, we tried to move it but it was to heavy to shift. The bathroom was so small you would have to come out of it to change your mind. It was a very cold night but a window was jamed open about 5 ins. for air so a cold wind of about 50 mph came into the room. There was a small cupbord with an ironing board flung into it which looked like it had being in a war. The room was like a fridge but for the life of us we could find no heating unit or control unit so we had to take things out of our case to put over us in the bed. About 4am We could take the cold no more and decided to try and get into another Hotel by ringing around, but we could not get anywhere as they all said they were booked up. About 6 30 am I went down to see the Manager and when I told him about our room he said he would give us the Penthouse Suite, Wow says I yes just bring our bags down and he would sort everything out. On my return to the desk I was handed a new key so off to the lift, which only brings one to the penthouse suite.......On exit from the lift there was3 penthouse suites, and one door had a hole in it, our suite had no hole in the door and it looked ok, the small kitchen had a micowave and coffee maker but not one bit of cutlery , plates, cups in any of the drawers or cupboards. the fridge was just one lump of ice on the top inside. The bedroom did have some holes in the wall which at some time could have been the TV bracket. Outside on the small Balcony You could have started a cigarette factory with the dogends. Do you think you could call this place A HOTEL .........We dont...

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Not bad for the price”
text: Well...let me start off by saying I LOVE NEW YORK CITY! Ok...the hotel? I like it and I would stay there again! There are two sections to the hotel and due to circumstances beyond our control (a pest in our room) we were able to move over to the new section. It has about 24 or 25 floors and we were on floor 24...NICE VIEWS of the city!!!! We booked our hotel and flight on newyorkcityhotels.com and that was the way to go!!! We saved SOOOOO MUCH MONEY! And we got a New York Pass (NOT THE CITY PASS!!) it is much better! The hotel is located perfectly in between Central PArk and Times Square. There are 2 subways right outside the hotel and a WONDERFUL restaurant downstairs. Starbucks across the street!!! The subway is the way to go in NYC (get the metro pass for a week) it will save you money too. Sooo back to the pest in our room. We had a WONDERFUL HUGE ROOM in the older section of the building. The room was great. 2 rooms with a fridge and sink. 1 queen bed in one room with a pull out couch, and 2 twin beds in the bedroom. A HUGE bathroom and a fridge and sink. This room was amazing compared to all the rooms I researched when I was booking my trip...by the way the room didn't stink, wasn't nasty or anything...we enjoyed our first 2 days! Then...the smell came. It was as if something died...so we started looking. Well we came to find out that it was a dead mouse in the bedroom under the bed. It smelled soooo bad that we couldn't stand it. We even named him Marty (sad!) Sooo we went down to the desk and we started searching for a room. There were no other rooms like the one we had...so they tried putting us in smaller rooms (not going to work! I am not sleeping on the couch when I was sleeping on the bed that Marty was under) Ok...sooo they ended up giving us 2 of the rooms on the 24th floor of the NEW building! VERY NICE ROOMS! GREAT VIEWS!! VERY SMALL!!!! COmpared to our old room (Marty's room) our two rooms weren't bigger together than that one!! CRAZY HUH!?! But it was fine for us and we enjoyed the views...we got a limo ride to the airport among other things. I would FOR SURE stay there again...but I will sweep through the room for any critters first! THANKS WELLINGTON!!!

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “March 2003 - Slightly Over Priced...and flippin cold!”
text:
We found the Belleclaire on the net. It was our first trip to NYC and we were unsure of what to expect...we weren't dissapointed but did feel that the pictures on the website were misleading. The website made it seem a lot plusher that it actually was.
We had a 'delux' room with ensuite. The room was sparce but clean. The fridge was handy for drinks etc. We had no view at all - it looked out over the back of the building which was dingy to say the least. The bathroom was small but had a shower over bath. We were woken on the first night by the heating system having an airblock....it was like someone hammering on the wall! I called the night porter who was friendly and apologised but it went on for an hour.
The location was great for us with the manhatten Diner across the road for breakfast each morning and just a wander away from the Metro station.
I think that we were expecting a little much for the money we paid....I guess this place is ideal if you are fully aware that it's cheap city accommodation.
If you don't have high expectations you won't be dissapointed.
I won't say that we would NEVER reccommend it but we would warn people of what to expect.
FYI We paid £350 for 3 nights in March 2003

name: Hotel Grand Union
title: “Hôtel très bien situé juste à...”
text: Hôtel très bien situé juste à côté de l'empire state.An niveau de l'accueil,le personnel est indifférent par rapport à vous.Les chambres sont très petites mais très propre.Au niveau du déjeuner il y a tellement de bons breakfast que n'hésitez pas à vous ballader pour en trouver un. La force de cette hôtel est le rapport qualité-prix et surtout son emplacement extra.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Good for those on a budget”
text:
I was a bit concerned about the hotel after reading reviews before arriving but they were unfounded. The bed bugs were a worry but there were none in site. An room upgrade was offered at check-in from a twin to two doubles. The room given in the 300's was a twin. Coupled with the corner view over looking 33rd Street it was back to reception where I was moved to a quieter room on the 500's. Over the road from Penn Station and MSG the location is a good base with it just a block from Macys and two from the ESB.
I would certainly have no hesitation staying there again new time I'm in town.

name: Hotel Carter
title: “w il Carter, a morte il Carter”
text:
leggendo le vostre recensioni pensavo di andare a stare in un porcile... invece ho trovato una situazione ben diverse, niente topi ne zecche, soggiorno positivo se non per il bagno dove, nella doccia, l'acqua invece che scendere, saliva. quindi al quarto giorno avevamo il bagno allagato, glielo abbiamo fatto notare alla donna delle pulizie e da lì in poi ce l'hanno sempre curato come anche il letto, che sempre fino al quarto giorno era sempre disfatto, al rientro in hotel la sera lo trovavamo sempre come lo lasciavamo al mattino.
però devo dire che per il prezzo e la posizione proposta io ho accettato anche "le scarse condizioni igieniche", quindi se non siete schizzinosi come il sottoscritto PRENOTATECI PURE!

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Icky”
text: Booked a one night stay for a business trip and, in a word, yuck. I love a luxury hotel like the next gal, but if it's a business trip I set that aside for one basic requirement: it must be clean. It was not clean. I was upgraded at check-in to a Premier Club Room. I'm thinking this must be great . . . quieter, free accecss to club lounge with snacks and goodies. Think again. This was one of the most disgusting rooms I've ever stayed in. See the photos; there's nothing else to say. If I were you, I would not stay here. Check out my recent review of the Omni Berkshire which is my new go to place to stay in NYC.

name: Chelsea Savoy Hotel
title: “Basic, clean, close to everything”
text:
This hotel was a great value. I stayed Sept 11- 15, 2010 with friends. We had 2 rooms, one with one double bed, and the other room with two double beds. The room with the 2 beds was considerably larger (understandably) but both were good. The rooms were somewhat noisy from being very close to the street but that's to be expected when you're on the second story. The rooms were always clean and the bathroom quite spacious. 
The hairdryer in our room worked surprisingly well, in hindsight it was a waste of space in my bags to pack my own. Our room didn't have a fridge which was a bit of a downside when having drinks or food in the room, but there is ice that can be used if necessary. 
We only attempted the continental breakfast on our first day, it was bagels and muffins. We couldn't find a toaster and it didn't look that appetizing so we walked down the street to Dunkin donuts. At 6th and 23rd (right down the block) there is a great place we got breakfast called corner cafe, as well as a place called toasties at 7th and 23rd that had good and cheap breakfast. 
While the staff weren't overly friendly that's not what I was looking for in a hotel anyway. It was affordable, close to everything (subway stops right across the road), and clean.

name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel
title: “Décevant”
text:
Nous décidons de profiter de notre voyage a NY pour loger près de Times Square. Sous recommandation d'une agence de voyage française nous choisissons cet hotel, à un prix plutôt compétitif.
Cependant, lorsque nous sommes arrivés sur place nous avons été un peu déçu. En effet, bien que le lobby de l'hotel fasse très neuf, les chambres n'ont pas le standard que l'on pourrait s'attendre dans un hotel comme celui ci. La chambre était froide, la fenetre n'était pas entièrement étanche et en février il fait très froid.
Cependant, le personnel est très agréable et il y a un accès gratuit à internet dans le hall de l'hotel !
Je recommande pourtant cet hotel car il est très bien situé mais il mériterait d'être refait !

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “Pas mal, vu qu'on l'a pas payer trop cher”
text: L'hotel etait en renovation lors de notre sejour donc il y a vait quelques desagremment. Malgres ca le personnel est assez sympathique. Il faut comprendre et parler anglais obligatoirement car le francais leur est totalement inconnu. Sinon la chambre etait assez propre sans dire qu'elle resplendissait mais bon. Notre chambre etait avec un sdb partagée avec 3 autres chambres mais sinon la chambre en elle meme est tout a fait correcte. par contre la sdb est vrt miniscule toilette baignoire et c'est tout pas de mirroir ni de lavabo...

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “relieved after reading reviews”
text: we were worried aftre reading reviews having already booked this hotel. These fears proved groundless, the rooms were spotless all linen was clean and everything worked o.k. the location is great the ideal hotel for a few days sightseeing.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “New York New York is a wonderful town”
text:
This was our first trip and we weren't disappointed. The location is excellent, the hotel is a bit run down in places but it is clean. We asked for a high floor so we heard less noise but the windows aren't sound proof so you hear everything , even 22 floors up, but to be fair its a city that never sleeps so we should have expected it. We bought the all tours bus ticket for $54 and it was great, especially the night tour where you see Manhattan from Brooklyn, be prepared for the ride over the Manhatten bridge if your on the open top bus, scary as hell! 
Food is expensive but the Deli next door to cafe edison is great for breakfast. Ask for doggie bags if you can't finish but want something to eat later as the meals are hugh, its the done thing anyway. Drink is expensive @$14 for 2 beers we found Hurleys up one street to be really nice and homely with good live music. Turn right outside the Edison and you are on Times sq, but if you turn left and keep walking you get to the Pier and they have a NYC yellow water cab and you can hop on and off all day for $24 and you get a great view of the Statue of Liberty on the way back.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Great time at the Roosevelt Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Roosevelt hotel from 1/23/04 - 1/25/04. We had a great time in New York. The Hotel, was clean and nice. The concierge service was awful. They were no help at all. Well unless you spoke with a french or english accent. But if you spoke regular english, your on your own!! The front desk was ok, it just depended on who you got. Some were real nice while others just could not be bothered. The cleaning lady on floor 4, was just the nicest she could be!! She was a big help!

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Nice Hotel -good deals”
text: Stayed here during a vacation in New York. One of the best deals in New york. It seems far away from everything, but really isn't. It is also right across from Grand Central Station. Room was good. Service was good. They were helpful and nice. My complaint would be the smoke factor. The whole lobby seemed to smell of smoke. There is a bar to the left of the lobby.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Greatest location in NYC!!!!!”
text:
I think the location is so good, just 4 or 5 block from time square. 
The price was a bit expensive because of the location.
But, there was no laundry room, the warm water sometimes not work, small deluxe room and too many people in lobby.
Anyway, there was good.

name: Hilton Manhattan East
title: “Tudor United Nations Hotel”
text:
Awful service- avoid this hotel
Service is awful on ALL levels. The manager, Brian promised me a one bedroom suite with a terrace after Virginia in reservations failed to follow-up on several "issues" she created during the booking process. When I arrived, Brian was unfamiliar with the system and could not distinguish between a room with/without a terrace? I switched rooms twice before I was placed in a room with a terrace by Andre (apparently the only person who knows how to locate a room in the system). 
I was promised several things that I did not receive. I purchased two double beds (as detailed in my original booking IN WRITING), but the manager tried to tell me that they do not guarantee that (although it was confirmed in writing?). I paid for a package that included breakfast but was told it would have to be confirmed before I was given vouchers (again, this was IN WRITING and included in the price). 
I recently had knee/foot surgery and when I limped out of the shuttle to the front of the hotel, the attendant did not assist me. He simply watched me get through the door and then asked if I "had it" (after he saw the manager at the desk). 
The concierge works until 8pm and as I approached the desk at a few minutes before 8pm he promplty ignored me. Mind you, he was still at the desk and acknowledged my presence by avoiding eye contact. I asked if he was "off-duty" and he simply replied that he could provide information only if I had a "quick question". 
Mold was found throughout the bathroom/in the tub. The floor, door and tile in the bathroom were filthy. House cleaning did not vacuum the room during my stay. The cushions on the couch were ripped and the insides exposed. 
The hotel staff does not acknowledge guests when they enter/exit the facility. I wish I would have kept my prior reservations at the omni! I would not recommend the Tudor to anyone nor would I book here again. 
I'm a frequent traveler and am familiar with the issues one can have when in a new city, so I took the time to fully research my choice of accommodations before embarking on my trip to New York. How could I have been so wrong? PLEASE do not make the same mistake that I did with this hotel. Avoid contact with managers Brian and Michelle as neither is knowledgeable regarding the reservation system. However, unlike Michelle, Brian is very personable and apologetic (unfortunately, this did not translate into an ability to correct the errors that had been made). Do not deal with reservation agent Virginia as she has no idea how to navigate the reservation system. Do not rely on the concierge for information as they do not want to work and avoid the attendant as he is not going to help with bags. 
Had I not paid for my reservation in advance I would have left the hotel before checking in!

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “Loved it!!!! great hotel, nice people and great service!!!”
text: Very recomended, Great managment, nice people very clean hotel, I will sure to come back!!! great rooms!!

name: Hotel Belleclaire
title: “tres bien rapport qualite prix”
text: hotel tres bien situe tout pres du metro et de central park petit resto pour le petit dej juste en face ,sympa au manatthan diner ouvert 7j sur 7 et 24h sur 24h.la salle de bain tres propre et le grand lit super confortable nous avions une suite avec 2 chambres separees avec une porte grand ecran plasma dans chaque chambres .le personnel tres sympa pour commander le schuttle pour le retour .si je retourne a new york je sejournerais de nouveau a l hotel belleclair

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Okay, but not highly recommended”
text:
I have stayed at the Roosevelt Hotel several times over the past few months, always on business. I must say that the service is lacking most of the time. On two visits I was locked out of my room and had problems obtaining another key that worked. One time, even the security person's master key didn't open my door. Rooms can be small, but the biggest complaint would have to be the showers!!!!!
