The temperature control is SO sensitive that a hair width will change it to scalding or freezing and sometimes when you finally adjust it and can handle the temperature, it will change while you are showering and you don't dare try to adjust it!! Heater/AC units are extremely loud and the in room fridge froze everything. Also, room smells are an issue.
Location is great, but you will have to wait for an elevator and then fight for space to get on or off the elevator. I will not stay at the property again, would prefer to walk a little further and stay at a more comfortable hotel.

name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel
title: “HÔTEL À RÉNOVER”
text:
Voilà un hôtel à deux pas de Times Square dans le coeur du Big Apple et sa vie grouillante ! Notes de contraintes: 1) une insonorisation avec les corridors et de chambre à chambre tout à fait insatisfaisante et dérangeante.2) un WiFi inexistant sauf les 30 premières minutes dans le lobby. 3) une salle à dîner pour le petit déjeuner à prix prohibitif.4) un service de billeterie pour spectacles à prix phohibitifs 5) un hôtel vétuste À RÉNOVER( la rénovation du lobby est débutée)
Notes positives1) une situation exceptionnelle 2) un service de conciergerie acceptable 3) un service de" housekeeping" tout à fait bien 3) un lit confortable 4) un coffre dans la chambre

name: Cosmopolitan Hotel - Tribeca
title: “Great Stay”
text:
I stayed at the Cosmopolitan for 3 nights from the 30th May to 2nd June with 3 friends. We booked the largest room with 2 double beds and a sofa bed and were pleasantly surprised by the amount of space. There was enough room for all our suitcases and shopping bags, also plenty of drawer space, although hanger space was limited. The hotel was clean and service was good. 
After reading the reviews on Trip Advisor I knew to book a room at the back of the hotel, away from the street noise. We were in room 705 which was very quiet, despite the roadworks which were going on at the time.
The location was great, thanks to the subway and it was amazing value.
I would advise anyone planning a trip to upgrade to a larger room and ask to be situated away from Chamber Street.

name: Stay.
title: “Buena experiencia”
text: Un hotel bueno relación calidad precio para lo que puedes encontrar en New York. La única pega es que quizá las habitaciones son bastante pequeñas, pero se duerme de lujo en la cama. Nos gusto mucho pq es pequeño y te tratan muy bien sobre todo el relaciones publicas Walter un chico majisimo nos ayudo mucho con los itinerarios de visitas y otras curiosidades para ver.

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “Anonymous service in midtown hotel with tired decor, not enough lifts, overpriced food and drink and noisy hotel corridors.”
text: Stay if you get a good price compared to other hotels. Pray for a large room because they are good but there are no finishing touches. Baths resemble large shower trays. No bubble bath. Carpets are dark brown in colour. Furnishings are drab. Beds are extremely comfortable with excellent linen. Staff are surly and unwelcoming. You have to pay to store a bag at reception per bag. They could do so much better. The bedroom door has gaps around it and you can hear people talking in the corridor and the lift doors and chimes if you are near them. Very small bath room with oddly low toilet. Top tip? Ask for room well away from lift, close to top floor and not overlooking Lexington avenue. Take bubble bath. Ask for a bath robe. Bring bottled water.

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “Great Location - lovely staff”
text:
Ideal location - only 10 mins walk (if that) to Grand Central train station.
staff were friendly and helpful.
Our room was upgraded on arrival to a lovely king size bedroom which was very clean and with plenty of room. There was no noise from any A/C units or traffic so a good sleep every night.
The added benefit was the use of their computer in the foyer to print off our flight boarding passes for our return trip - free of charge! 
The only downside was the cost of the drinks at the bar - but it is expected for hotel bars in the city and to be honest, it wasn't a drink oriented holiday and would not put us off staying there again.

name: The Westin New York Grand Central
title: “Really should have been a Sheridan”
text: My family checked into this hotel on Thanksgiving. At the time of check in the regular guest line was shorter than the SPG line, so I went into the regular line and the clerk told me there were no rooms available and to wait. After 4 of us were standing in the small lobby with very limited seating for 1/2 hour, I saw there was no line at SPG and told my story tot he SPG clerk - she said she had a room ready fore me. Good thing I didn't rot on the vine waiting for the first clerk to accommodate us. Our room was fully remodeled, and it was nice, but not Westin nice.... it was more Sheridan nice. The gym was nice, however, no fruit in the fruit bowl. The wait for an elevator was acceptable, and a guest showed us how to hold down a combination of buttons to get an express ride down. All in all we thought the hotel was okay, but did not live up to our expectation of a $375, per night Westin.

name: Hudson New York
title: “A waste of money - I ended up with a black eye the room was so small”
text:
We booked this hotel for a weekend break in New York. When I arrived the doorman was very friendly and efficient, I was very impressed. Sadly that was the best experience I had at the hotel. 
I arrived at the check in desk alone, my partner was arriving an hour after me. They asked for a credit card, I didn't have one but said my partner would be along in one hour to check in and that they could have the card details then. I was told I couldn't check in until I had a credit card or a $150 deposit. I was very tiered after a long trip and very angry at being treated like I'd empty the mini bar and do a runner in one hour. We had just paid £1200 for a 4 night stay, I was not impressed.
I finally managed to check in leaving a $100 deposit (all I had on me) and arrived at my room. On the Hudson website it says styled on cabins from an old fashioned yacht, they forgot to mention the room was the size of a cabin on a yacht, tiny. I ended up with a black eye after getting out of bed and smacking my eye on the TV on the wall as it was so close to the bed!
Next the bathroom, absolutely tiny, I'm only 5ft tall and quite small. Sitting on the loo my knees nearly touched the wall in front. The shower head in the shower was absolutely black with scum (looked like it had never been cleaned) and the base of the bath had worn away to reveal the concrete underneath the enamel. There were hairs all up the walls and around the bath too.
As for dusting and cleaning, I don't think the room had been cleaned for at least a couple of weeks there was thick dust everywhere and marks on the sides where other guests had spilt drinks etc.
The Hudson does have a couple of good points. The bar is very trendy although very pricey, 2 glasses of champagne each nearly £100. Breakfast at the hotel is very good, although the canteen is so dark you can hardly see what you're eating. In fact the whole hotel is so dark including the corridors and rooms I recommend you take a torch with you!

name: Comfort Inn Times Square South
title: “We loved it here, would definatley go again”
text: For the price this accomodation was excellent, the staff couldnt do enough to help. The room was clean and modern. I would not recommend for families with young children as the rooms are a little small.

name: Da Vinci Hotel
title: “Great budget stay in NYC”
text: My boyfriend and I just got back from a week of seeing the sights in NYC. Every day, we walked until our dogs howled, and returned to the Da Vinci Hotel for the night. At a time when I couldn't find a place on Hotels.com for less than $390 a night, the Da Vinci's $192 per night, with all taxes and fees included, was a huge deal. Easy to get to from La Guardia (got our 7-day unlimited Metro pass for $29 in the airport, caught the M60 bus to the N train at Astoria Blvd, got off at 57th St and walked the 2 blocks to the hotel - an easy 50 minutes), we found our room small but adequate. Most importantly, the room and the marble bathroom were immaculate (and no bedbugs!). The desk staff were cordial, but they did miss our 3 am wakeup call the last morning (triple redundancy saved us). The continental breakfast was included, and wasn't much, but we got out the door in the morning with at least a cup of tea and a muffin. Two blocks in the other direction was Columbus Circle with its subway access to the A,B,C,D and 1 trains, and Central Park where we rented bikes for a day and rode around the park and to the tip of Manhatten. I'd certainly stay here again.

name: The Mansfield
title: “Nice hotel & good staff.”
text:
Surprisingly good hotel, really clean, nice decor, staff really friendly. 
Stayed here for 10nights, only small complaint is the noisy A/C BUT it was ok really. Main thing is it was easy to control and kept our room cool.
Bar/restaurant is also very good, free coffee is good but there is better alternative at Gregory's coffee 2mins walk.
Location is great for shopping and for getting to Central Park. We booked a suite which was a good size and comfortable for 2 adults & baby!

name: 60 Thompson - A Thompson Hotel
title: “NY break...”
text: I think that the label 'Boutique' is really another word for less than what you would expect for the money you're charged. And it is unfortunate. The rooms are very small, the service is a bit slack, and there was no heat as they are on a single pipe system which is common in NYC but not ok when you pay $500 and freeze throughout the night. The room wasn't ready when I arrived which was ok as I had plans. But when finally checking in I had to ask for my bag 4 times, when asked if I could extend the valet parking with 2 hours I was told I had to come back in the middle of the day to get the car and then have it re parked and I would still be charged for another 24 hours of parking? When asked if they could recommend another garage nearby they couldn't, and as I had not brought laptop and sadly have no smartphone (I know, sad...) I couldn't research myself. They then said that they would 'look into' it and I suppose they still are, I am back at home in a warm house. They same happened when the query about the heating was put to them, I suppose they are still investigating that too. Or is it just that they really couldn't care less and just don't bother at all. We usually stay at the Ritz Carlton at Central Park, a lovely hotel with all amenities and at about the same rate, you actually get a room that can be heated if the temp drops outside. We tried the Thompson as we wanted a change of scenery, next time it will be back to views of Central Park instead and the Ritz. I hate being cold, it doesn't matter that the staff is hip and happening with jeans and shirts hanging out....

name: The Shoreham
title: “Need to (re)train staff”
text:
Pros: bed was comfortable, nice linen, massage chair, good location
Cons: room small, shampoo not replaced, minibar not topped up until asked, fitness area is small, an attitude of inconveniencing the front desk staff when checking out. 
Note to management, do spot checks on shampoo and minibars, train staff on what to top up, train staff on customer service with a smile.
Not a patch on Essex House Hotel.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Such a great location”
text: A week before departing we changed our booking to the Edison and were so pleased we did, the location is super, 3 subway stops very nearby and a great cafe for breakfast, what more could you ask for. Our room was adequate with two double beds for the 3 of us, clean and comfy beds if a little bit noisy from the street, but hey this is New York the city that never sleeps. Staff were friendly and even got us a limo back to the airport for the same price as a taxi. Would definitely stay here again

name: Dream New York
title: “Great location, fairly reasonable for a NYC hotel...”
text:
Location is great! Between 7th and Broadway, very close to Central Park and 5th Avenue shopping... There are so many cafes, pubs and restaurants just steps away from the hotel. In the evenings, it is so much fun to walk couple blocks down on Broadway to see all the lights. Check-in and check-out were so easy that took only a few minutes. Kevin at concierge desk was so helpful arranging airport transfer for us. Public areas were kept in good condition. Especially the rooftop is a trendy NYC place. The hotel is great especially for young travelers who intend to have fun time in NYC. Subway Station -yellow line, 57th street- right on the corner of the hotel, only a few meters away... 
We were traveling as a group of families and we got the smallest room of all! We almost couldn't move around in the room. There was no closet for our clothings, only a small rack and a few hangers on the corner. The bed was the smallest double bed I have ever seen in a hotel room. The bathroom had a shower with curtain and again was too small to move around... 
The rooms looked clean but the carpet felt so dirty when you step on it . Also the room itself was so dusty! Bathroom sink and floor were not clean enough. The minibar worked with motion sensor and I find it very stupid. It charges you whatever you move around inside of it. So, stacking our doughters milk could have cost us a lot of money but luckily the reception staff deduct those costs from our bill. Wi-fi was free in the lobby but charged in rooms. I think it should be free everywhere in the hotel. I booked through Booking.com and they did not mention this.

name: The Alex Hotel
title: “Nice stay- would definitely return”
text:
We had two double rooms for a girls weekend. The location was great for us, nice emoyees and reasonably priced. Rooms were very clean, comfortable and the hotel was very quiet.
Nice bar with outdoor seating.
I'd definitely stay here again.

name: The Westin New York Grand Central
title: “Perfectly located and brand new”
text:
This hotel is perfectly located within walking distance of Grand Central Station and Time Square. The room we had was modern, clean and well decorated. Bathroom was spotless. A bit expensive though. The restaurant and the bar were not open so we had to go out for a drink (Well, it's not too bad... we were in NYC, right?)
The concierge was very helpfull and found us the mos perfect restaurant in Little Italy.
There's a Starbuck on the corner so you can have breakfast there without paying 28$ per person.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Much better than expected after seeing previous reviews.”
text: We arrived at the hotel at 3am after a sticky start at the airport. It was my husband's 50th birthday that day and with all the negative reviews of the past we were anxious. However, we needn't have been. We were upgraded straight away from a standard double and given a corner room with views over central park on the 23rd floor. The room was quiet, very clean as was the bathroom. Although it was a little on the small side, the shower was very good and we were given plenty of clean towels every day. The temp outside was very hot, in the late 80's, but we had very efficient air conditioning so it wasn't a problem. The staff were very friendly and we didn't mind having to use the safety deposit boxes behind the desk as they were very efficient. We would definitely use the hotel again, you couldn't fault the location. A must is the Rockefeller Centre at night, great views of the Empire State and all of New York, also do the Staten Island Ferry, best free trip ever. The best bus tours to go on are the Gray Line - blokes in red waistcoats. The night loop to Brooklyn is brilliant. Have a great stay and enjoy!

name: The Shoreham
title: “Location great, Rooms tiny!”
text: As other reviewers have noted, this hotel is in a great location. From here we were able to walk to musicals and plays on Broadway, go to Central Park, and eat at some great restaurants. The concierge was helpful in making recommendations for us based on the fact that we were a family with 2 young kids. The room was small, but tastefully decorated. The bathroom was ultra small- barely big enough for a tall person to sit on the toilet without kicking the sink. The view from our room was of the back of three other buildings- like being in a tunnel of concrete. The elevator is super small and often slow if you are checking out at a busy time. Definitely a tight fit for 4 people and 2 small suitcases. I am aware that this is New York, so the smallness of the hotel is outweighed by the great location.

name: The Mansfield
title: “Terrible hotel”
text:
Hotel staff was lazy, rude and unprofessional. To your requests and concerns they will shout on you back, not helping at all.
They have tried to charge my credit card two times, for a double amount.
We could not check in and enter the room before 16h. Moreover, they could not give us clean sheets and towels (?!) until 20h that day.
The room and bathroom were far from clean. 
There was a huge hole above the window, where the AC device is (20cm on each size of the AC). So you are sleeping next to the opened window, which is impossible "to close". It was freezing and noisy (ventilators from another building, less than 5m away from the window, working 24h a day). 
Internet was free but poor, not working at all. Not even during the night, not even in lobby. I could not receive/send very simple emails. 
Don't let them blind you with their "complimentary coffee and tea", "free internet", "no charge for pets". This hotel is very bad value for money and you should avoid it.
I use to spend 100 days a year travelling all around the world, usually staying in 4 stars hotels. This is the worst hotel I have ever been it.
Location is good but everything else is disappointing. Shame on hotel management.

name: Comfort Inn Times Square South
title: “Convenient for travel and major attractions”
text:
The hotel isn't in Times Square, but it's not far from it (a couple of blocks). Some rooms overlook the current Times newspaper offices and the main bus terminal (which makes it convenient for buses, a taxi dispatch and several subway lines - stations for various lines are interconnected by underground walkways there). The neighbourhood isn't great looking though there are some well run deli's and coffee shops nearby. I read somewhere (Choice hotels site?) that the hotel has a restaurant - they must have mixed that up as it doesn't, thought there are places to eat nearby.
We've been to New York before and know hotels are pretty expensive there, like many other big cities where real estate is at a premium. We got a good rate (for the date) via Quick Book and stayed a whole week at this property. We paid a bit more per night than on previous trips, but the room was a whole lot better, and there were more facilities including breakfast.
The first room we were allocated wasn't the type we booked, but I got the duty manager to change it as we wanted a king size and just one bed. The 4th floor room was clean, modern and well appointed with a good TV, safe large enough for a laptop plus cameras, passports etc. The rooms are however small and there's isn't a lot of space for luggage - you have to be disciplined with your stuff. The bathroom was fine - clean and everything worked well including the shower (to operate the shower you have to pull down on a small ring on the end of the bath tub faucet/tap spout which can be confusing). I used the free wifi successfully several times with both a laptop and a wifi phone. Connection speed was OK. You have to get the access code from reception. We had no trouble sleeping. The bed was very comfortable, the aircon worked if you wanted it, you could open the window for fresh air (though that made it a little noisy with the sounds of the city). I asked about a refrigerator/microwave but apparently they only had 3 rooms with those facilities, which were all in use. In the end we didn't need them, and chilled a bottle of wine using the ice bucket.
We had a few minor niggles during our stay, but most of these were dealt with by the front desk staff - the maid took the complimentary newspaper away before we had a chance to read it, the phone wouldn't allow me to make a local call and so on. Be aware that there may be a small daily charge if you use the safe.
The breakfast was good, with a selection of cakes and pastries, cereal, juice and waffles. The breakfast room, in the basement, is small but adequate. Some problems come from how guests behave and use it, with some folks choosing to sit long after they have finished eating, seemingly oblivious to other guests waiting. It pays to get in there early if possible, and you can always grab something and take it back to your room. Tea/coffee were available there 24/7 along with complimentary snack bars. There were also vending machines and a ice maker. There was also a coffee machine in the room and the maid left enough for a couple of cups each day. Bottled water was also provided in the room some days.
All the staff at the hotel were great, particularly the guy running the breakfast room. The front entrance and lobby weren't great to look at, particularly as there was construction work going on when we were there, and you sometimes get bags of trash piled up, but it's functional. There's a concierge desk available for booking tours, tickets and transportation, though we didn't use it. There's a small waiting area in the lobby and the staff will hold luggage for you. They kindly let us use the restroom downstairs to change and sort out our luggage before our transatlantic flight home.

name: Dream New York
title: “Great location but over top charges”
text:
We stayed at Dream 2 nights for a business meeting. Rooms are big, specially for NYC. Staff has and attitude. Not sure why, maybe its a NYC thing. Location is great, just a few blocks away from Times Square, but not right on Times Square. Which is great as its not noisy. 
Incidentals can get very costly. We asked for a bottle of water, got charged $5.00 just to take it up to the room and then of course, tip and tax , which made it for a very expensive little bottle of good old H2O. $14 is a lot for water - I think-. Also, we asked for a taxi to go to the airport, and the bellman said, they had a "car" right outside that will be the same rate as for the taxi. It was NOT! Total cost was more than 25% than the taxi....
In general its a good place, but I will not stay there again next time Im in NYC

name: Comfort Inn Times Square South
title: “THE HELL HOLE OF NEW YORK.”
text:
I want to start by saying this is my first ever review but after staying at this hotel i feel its only right to tell people to stay away.
It all started when you first pull up to the hotel it looking like a building site with rubbish bags all over the the place and to say they smell it was like being at a rubbish tip, Also i would like to add that before you get in the hotel you always have to walk pass the hotel staff puffing away on their cigrettes 2 inches from the door.
After this you walk through to the reception area which is more dirty than any i have ever known i really wanted to wash my hands after touching any thing in that room.
To be honest the staff behind the desk were ok cant complain about that they gave me the key and off i went after tripping over 10 bags as the room is so small.
So up the lift i went to the 14th floor hallway was clean so that was a good point.
Into the room well when i say room more like a cupboard i thought it was going to be small but a place for the suitcase would of been nice then to top it all off looked out of the window into the building opposite you could see what was on there computers so you need to leave the blind down all day which does not help when you feel your in a prison cell any way.
The next morning after a good night sleep as the bed is nice at last the hotel has got something right we went down to the breakfast room, we took one look at this and laughed and went out for breakfast i did not fancy eating 1 inch away from the person next to you seriously it was that small and im not lying.
The location of the hotel is very good as its right on times square but the avenue its on is dirty smelly and just a hell hole there is no way that my wife would of gone out on that road at night on her own.
Then to top all this off the last morning we got up and checked out which the person on the desk just took the key and did not say a word which i thought was rude and as the hotel had booked the taxi for us i just politely asked is that my taxi outside and his reply was DONT KNOW JUST GO AND ASK this was so rude so i just walked out.
Right i must finish with this hotel is cheap BUT DONT STAY HERE AND IF YOU HAVE BOOKED I FEEL VERY SORRY FOR YOU.

name: La Quinta Inn Manhattan
title: “Excellent location”
text: We stayed at La Quinta Manhattan on Nov/2011 with a family group. We had confirmed reservations for 3 rooms. They pre-approved 4 rooms (one more than my reservation) in my credit card but, when we arrived, only 2 rooms were available. 2 couples had to share the same room for the first night. They told us that the guest that was supposed to leave decided to stay, so, they couldn`t honnour our confirmed reservation!!! The next day they mooved the couples to theirs own rooms. The rooms were on the back side, no view, but very comfortable and clean. Everything was fine for the rest of our stay, nothing else to complain.

name: The Westin New York Grand Central
title: “Posizione strategica!!!”
text: Ci sono stato per tre notti durante il viaggio di nozze e l'esperienza è stata splendida. Posizione centrale, nel cuore di midtown, vicino alla grand central station e a pochi minuti a piedi dalla Fifth Avenue e da Times Square. Dalla grande finestra della mia camera si vedeva il Chrysler Building. Accoglienza, ordine e pulizia di alto livello, ottimo!

name: Dream New York
title: “What's the fuss?”
text: It is an ok hotel if you can get a good deal on the price. It is promoted as some trendy, high end, design hotel but, although it may have been like that 8 or 10 years ago, I really do not see what the big deal is today. The big plus though is the location. A morning run in Central Park is just 5 minutes away. Apart from that I would say the hotel is between average and good. But again, only if you get a good price and when you don't expect a great hotel. It's a good place if you plan to be out in town most of the time and just use it for a well located place to sleep.

name: The Alex Hotel
title: “boutique luxury apartment near grand central terminal at great price!”
text: My family of four (2 adults and 2 kids) stayed at the Alex hotel during the late summer of 2011. We had planned to meet a friend to watch US open qualifiers. We were thrilled to see that the room was actually an apartment with two separate bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, and a living room/kitchenette. The entry way was large. It looked much like their web photos do. We got a great price on this and couldn’t believe we could have so much space in the city. The smaller bedroom was quite cramped and the living/kitchen area was small too, but it was sufficient. We ended up stuck in our room because of Hurricane Irene and the hotel did everything it could to keep us updated, safe, and comfortable. They even sent up bottled water and fruit and moved us to a lower level. The internet was available for a fee, but worked well. The exercise room was fantastic! They even had fresh lemon water. The hotel’s location was also great, only a few blocks from Grand Central as well as Times Square. The staff couldn’t have been nicer or more accommodating. I should warn you of one thing - that if you come to the Alex, there will be lots of tempting and pricey treats in the kitchen that you should avoid unless you want to pay a lot more at check out!

name: The Alex Hotel
title: “Great city stay”
text: Great Manhattan location. Short walk to Rockefeller Center and all the great nearby shopping. All types of rooms. We've stayed a few times and have been upgraded to a one bedroom with kitchen. Their regular rooms are just fine too. There is a bar and restaurant in the lobby which is convenient, as well as a diner across the street for an alternate breakfast. Whenever we stay in NYC we like to stay at this great boutique hotel.

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “Did the job required”
text:
Just back from a 5 night stay at Doubletree Lex.
Room was very clean, however the bed was pretty rubbish, as was the linen and pillows. On the plus side: bathroom ideal,large TV, fast Internet, quick lift, free to use office facilities, good situation, and reasonable value.

name: The Westin New York Grand Central
title: “non tornerei assolutamente.”
text:
Quando tornerò a New York non tornerò sicuramente qui.
La posizione è ottimale ma credo che ci siano hotel piùà economici e con servizi e personale migliori.
Subito ci si scontra con il personale del ceck inn, poco cordiale e maleducato. Sono le uniche persone maleducate e scordiali che abbiamo incontrato nel nostro lungo viaggio tra California e Florida!
Poi i facchini che molto sfacciatamente ti chiedono mance più alte (soprattutto i giovani) e le stanze non sono per nulla insonorizzate. 
Da evitare quelle sulla strada, anche se al 20esimo piano, si sente il passaggio continuo di auto e sirene dei pompieri (normale a new york ma non normale sentirsele in camera!)
Da evitare assolutamente.

name: Stay.
title: “Considerando l'offerta che...”
text: Considerando l'offerta che prevedeva uno sconto del 20% con un pernottamento di almeno 6 notti, il rapporto qualita' prezzo e' stato eccellente. Posizione ottima per visitare la citta'. L'hotel è servito benissimo dalla metropolitana e c'è un piccolo market nelle vicinanze.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Basic but OK”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Wellington from 16 to 18 November and we had 'managed' our expectations based on previous reviews on this website. This trip was organised through work so we had no choice about accomodation. 
Bad bits
It must be said that the hotel is very tired and in need of decorating. 
Double rooms are small and walls/carpet grimy and stained. 
Our particular room was on the 16th floor and looked out onto the wall of a neighbouring building.
Be prepared to wait 5 to 10 minutes for a lift that's got enough space for you to sqeeze in!
Better bits
Our bathroom was reasonably modern and the shower was excellent - really woke you up in the morning!
Bed sheets were clean and bed was comfy enough
Daily maid service
Most of the staff were helpfull and friendly
Diner attached to the hotel was good for breakfast or lunch
Best bits
The location! 10 minutes walk from Times Square, the main Broadway areas, Central Park, etc., and 20 minutes from Macy's, Bloomingdales and the Empire State building.
Price - cheaper than most of the other big hotels in the area.
Would we recommend it? To be honest it was great as a cheap, basic hotel that we only used when we needed to crash out at the end of a tiring day in this amazing city. If you're on a budget and are prepared to complain if you have any major issues (which we didn't by the way), then I'm sure that you could make this work for you.
This was our first visit and if you haven't visited New York before then here are a few thoughts;
Buy a bus 'hopper' ticket. These buses run all day and depart from stops across the city (one of the downtown loop stops is directly opposite the Wellington). The bonus is that each bus has its own tour guide who points out some really interesting things whilst giving a history of the city!
Taxis are pretty cheap but don't expect the driver to be able to speak English.
Take lots of money! Bargains galore in the shops (loads of offers in Macy's) - the shops there DROP their prices in the run up to Christmas unlike the UK shops who put there prices up!
If you want designer clothes there are organised trips to designer outlets - get on one of these and allow a whole day for the experience.
Electrical goods are cheaper in general - we bought 3 i-pods and saved over £100. Use ATM's rather than take too much cash over with you - the exchange rate is better (we got $1.9 to the £)
Eat at the stardust diner on Broadway the waiting staff sing and dance during your meal and they are EXCELLENT - it's like getting a broadway show thrown in with your meal!
I could of course go on and on - we did a lot and saw a lot but didn't even scratch the surface. Just go and enjoy the atmopsphere in the city that really doesn't sleep. It's noisy (cab horns, sirens, shouting, etc.), brash and wonderful. By the way we went to some 'interesting' places like China town and little Italy but never felt unsafe - just keep your wits about you as with any big city. 
Have fun....and if you need a guide my wife says that she's available......

name: Da Vinci Hotel
title: “Excellent For The Price!!!!”
text: Wow! What a great find! The Da Vinci has it all. It is just two blocks away from the N, R, W, Q (accessible to La Guardia) and 1, 2, 3, A, B, C, D subway lines. The rooms were small with two full sized beds but included a fridge. The bathroom was updated. A short walk to Times Square. Continental breakfast was basic, but good. If you are looking for the Hyatt, this is not it, but it is very clean with a great location and a very reasonable price. I will stay here everytime I visit NYC from now on!!

name: Park Central
title: “Terrible Hotel”
text: This is the worst hotel I have ever stayed in. No air conditioning during a heat wave. Rooms had a fan unit but you could not set the temp and it never blew out cool air. Rooms were dirty and moldy smelling. Mold on ceilings and mirrors. Dirty carpet. One room the bed sheets were not clean. We switched rooms 5 times. One room, the toilet leaked all over the bathroom floor.All hallways smelled of smoke and were very hot. No cold water in vending machines,staff told us to buy water in the gift shop, but the gift shop was out of water too.Saw numerous guest bringing fans up to their rooms.Was told by the staff if we wanted a fan we had to go buy one, just like the other guest. Internet never worked the 5 days we were there. Staff was very rude.Had to ask maid several times for towels,ice bucket liner,glasses, etc...Tried to call every number to get towels, and they never answered the phone.Had to make numerous trips downstairs for things the maid never brought.When I asked why they never answered the phone the manager said they had so many complaints to deal with that they didn't have time to take phone calls.Staff was extremely rude.Slept on cushions on the floor for 4 night because the mattress on the pull out bed in suite was so thin you could feel the metal coils through it, but at least that suite didn't smell of mildew. Tried to change hotels but every thing was book for the 5 days we needed a room. Horrible hotel. Stay at your own risk and call 311 to complain. I think it's a health hazard to not have air conditioning.

name: Hudson New York
title: “Small rooms, Good location”
text:
Stayed here the first week of February on business. The best aspects of this hotel: 1.) Location 2.) Common Areas.
There is a great lobby and a couple of happening hotel bars. The hotel is situated near the Columbus Circle Mall, as well as several restaurants, starbucks, little markets and pharmacies. The staff was also very friendly.
The rooms are small. If you've got a queen size bed, the width of your room will be the width of the bed plus one foot on either side (I had the 150 sq. ft. room). My colleagues complained that when they sat on the toilet, their knees touched the wall (they're about 6 ft tall). As I'm only 5'5", I didn't have this problem. 
If you are looking to relax in your hotel room, this may not be the place for you. The room is small and the t.v is about 9" and shoved into the closet. If all you want is a place to sleep, then this hotel should be just fine.

name: Hudson New York
title: “Happy Hudson”
text:
During the first weekend of February My wife and I decided to take a weekend and enjoy NYC, we had previously stayed at Royalton in NY, their sister property but we wanted to try Hudson as it was just the two of us and not our daughter. 
We arrived at the hotel extemly late after a 5 hour delay and were welcomed with a warm and friendly smile by the Front Desk Agent. As he made small talk we proceeded with the check in process and he explained that we were upgraded to a one bedroom suite. We were very happy with that after hearing that the standard rooms are rather small. When we got to the room were were suprised to see how much they did with the space. The living room was off the foyer and their was a long hallway leading to the bedroom and a very large walk in closet and very large bathroom. (only downside no tub). The design of the room is great with beautiful hardwood floors and wood walls, it gives it a very cabin like feel. They also are redoing their TV's as I was told, so if you are into that thing in Manhattan you will be excited to see a large flat screen in the living room and a 27" in the bedroom. (but it is NYC, so why be stuck in the room.) As it had been an extremly long day we were off to bed and happy to notice that we did not hear any bar noise as previously mentioned. We were on the 8th floor.
The next day we woke up and were very happy to noitce that there are two Starbucks with in a stone's through of the hotel. Also their is a CVS and a grocery store where you can get what you need. I loved the fact that they had vending machine's on the floor and they were hidden behind a door that said "Eat" of "Drink" the prices were not bad either $2 door a soda is pretty cheap. 
We went out and enjoyed the city that day, we took the subway to SOHO and shopped and realized that we did like our hotel not in the middle of everything but rather a place to escape to. The subway is a block away and if that is not close enough for you, you have some issues. 
That evening we had a late night dinner in the Hudson Cafeteria and the food was great comfort food with an elegant twist. The bar was very inviting and the staff always made you feel welcome. My favorite was Library bar where you could sit infront of the Fire and enjoy a cocktail and a book. 
What I love about Morgans Hotel Groups property's is the attention to Detail and the amazing peices of furniture that they have in the rooms and the lobby. I went to the W union Square to see what all the hype is about. It looks like nothing more than a Westin with a couple of contemporary pecies from Pottery Barn. I would never stay at another hotel in NYC. Other than Royalton or Morgans, and I can not wait to see the new Mondrian they will be opening in SOHO. Again this hotel is a great place to stay and the staff is top notch.

name: Comfort Inn Times Square South
title: “Perfekter Ausgangspunkt in New York”
text:
Bei unserer Ankunft im Hotel wurde uns mitgeteilt, dass unsere Reservierung nicht ausfindig gemacht werden kann. Das Problem lag allerdings bei unserem Reiseveranstalter und nicht beim Hotel!
Nach erfolglosen Versuchen jemanden vom Reisebüro zu erreichen (es war 23 Uhr) wurden wir nach ca. 5 Minuten dennoch eingecheckt und bekamen sogar eine Suite und uns wurde nichts berechnet, bis die Sache geklärt worden war, was am nächsten Tag der Fall war. Nach zwei Tagen Suiteaufenthalt bekamen wir dann unser eigentliches Zimmer (ein Standarddoppelzimmer, das wir auch gebucht hatten). Die Zimmer waren beide mit Kingsize Betten ausgestattet, die wirklich groß genug waren. Die Betten waren auch gemütlich.
Beide Zimmer waren wirklich schön und modern eingerichtet. Nach Wunsch werden Bettwäsche und Handtücher täglich gewechselt. Dazu muss man die Handtücher auf dem Boden lassen und für die Bettwäsche muss man ein kleines Schildchen (liegt auf dem Nachttisch) aufs Bett legen, um es dem Housekeeping deutlich zu machen.
Ein höher gelegenes Zimmer ist auf jeden Fall zu empfehlen. Am Besten auf der Seite, die zum Times Square herausschaut. Das Hotel ist relativ schmal gebaut. Es gibt daher 3 bis 4 Zimmer pro Etage. Insgesamt gibt es 19 Etagen.
Das Personal am Empfang war sehr hilfsbereit und freundlich. Besonders Edward, Sophie und Will haben uns sehr weitergeholfen.
Kostenlos stehen täglich zwei Flaschen Wasser, eine Kaffeemaschine (der Kaffee, Zucker, die Plastikbecher etc. werden täglich wieder neu hingestellt), ein Fön und kabelloses Internet zur Verfügung. Auch das tägliche Frühstück ist kostenlos, das wir aber nicht wahrgenommen haben, da man in New York einfach so viele andere Möglichkeiten hat. Im Frühstücksraum gibt es eine Eismaschine. Auch das steht den Gästen zur kostenlosen Verfügung. Für das Eis hat man einen Plastikbehälter im Zimmer.
Was uns aber am meisten beeindruckt hat, war die Lage des Hotels. Unglaublich zentral gelegen! Sehr wichtige Sehenswürdigkeiten/Orte wie Times Square, Empire State Building, Madison Square Garden und Vieles mehr ist in 5-10 Minuten zu Fuß zu erreichen!
Insgesamt haben wir 8 Nächte im Comfort Inn verbracht und waren rundum zufrieden.

name: 60 Thompson - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Great location, good service, average rooms”
text: We stayed at 60 Thompson from a Thursday to a Sunday. We had an early flight & arrived at 10am. Our room happened to be ready which was a bonus. The room itself was average, small and slightly worn looking. There were traces of the last guests - a letter left on the dresser, water in the ice bucket, but the bed appeared to have been changed & overall the room was very clean. If you are planning to use the room for business, there is no desk. Our only major problem was the noise on the Saturday night. Not the hotel's fault - we happened to be next to a very rowdy room who was smashing doors & yelling most of the night. As with most boutique hotels the sound proofing just isn't there & even during the other days & nights we could clearly hear flushing toilets in other rooms, speaking & closing of doors. The hotel is in a great location and the staff is exceptionally friendly. Would we stay again? For that price we will probably look for another hotel close by.

name: La Quinta Inn Manhattan
title: “Worst hotel ever”
text: If you want heap this is what you will get. Two bad instances , one they cancelled my reservation and I was not notified until I arrived. Ended up in a closet of a room. The other time I had a reservation for two nights was delayed because of weather. I was assured the one night was taken care of but it showed up on my credit card. Called la Quinta corporate and was told it was the owners decision and they could not help.

name: Comfort Inn Times Square South
title: “Good Value”
text: We stayed in mid-August and yes the rooms are small and the breakfast area is small but for the price we paid, I'd go back. The location was 5 minutes from Times Square, close to subway etc. Hotel staff were very friendly and accomodating. We arrived 3 hours before check-in and Skylar (hope spelling is correct) was very helpful and got us into our room with no delay. We were able to get out and enjoy the city without dragging our luggage. Even when we checked out, the hotel staff stored our luggage for about 6 hours. Again, we were able to still go out and enjoy the sights while our luggage was stored. What they do for you outside the room counts as well. Overall a great value!

name: La Quinta Inn Manhattan
title: “I'd happily stay here again”
text: Several of us stayed here for three days in January while attending the NRF Conference. Since rooms were not over priced we were a little hesitant but were very happily surprised. Rooms have been recently refurbished and very clean, beds are a 9 on a scale of 1 to 10, LCD and WiFi. Rooms aren't huge but very very comfortable. I'd very happily recommend and stay here again. Service was good, and hotel staff was friendly. Location is also very convenient.

name: Stay.
title: “prezzo servizio ottimi”
text: posizione perfetta, praticamente a Time Square, camer un pò sacrificate ma pulite e con letti perfetti, bar interno alla sra frequentato molto bene e con DJ. Assolutamente perfetto per week end lungo, per vacanza più lunga forse un pò troppo sofferte le camere Giandomenico

name: Hudson New York
title: “Buyer Beware”
text:
We visited NYC over the Christmas Holiday and booked our hotel through Priceline. Because I had read many online reviews, I was prepared for a VERY SMALL room. The room size met expectations. We bid 170 dollars for the room and with taxes & fees, we paid about 200 a night. Priceline rates this place with 3 and a half stars; shame on Priceline...I expected more with this rating.
Upon check-in, we requested a non-smoking room on an upper level. The staff accommodated. We had been warned through reviews that if you are on a lower floor it can be noisy because of 
the bar below. When we called ahead of time with these requests, we were told that we had to call Priceline...saying that usually you call the hotel directly, but in the case of the Hudson, you call Priceline. Priceline was required to tell us that such requests (a non-smoking room & upper level floor might mean additional charges!!) They did not. When we requested an upgrade to a king size bed at check-in, we were told it would cost an extra 60 dollars a night; we declined. We thought our bed would be a double, but thankfully it was a queen; no extra charge! The bed in this very small room was very low to the floor, presenting a challenge getting out of it. The room safe was level with the floor, requiring that you get down flat on the floor to use it. It was a challenge opening luggage, but I managed to put a couple of decoartive barrels together to serve as a luggage stand. There was a rack for the other bag.
Please do not stay here if you expect to sleep at night...the steam pipes creaked and crackled every time the heat came on. I asked if the engineer could check this and was told that the building was SO OLD that it was impossible to stop the noise. The technicians checked it anyway and nothing changed. I solved the problem somewhat, by running the fan continuously so I would not be awakened every time the heat came on. It was very cold in NYC during our stay so the heat came on regularly.
There is absolutely no sign outside indicating that you are approaching the Hudson Hotel (we were walking from the subway stop;) you had better know the exact address with exact numbers or you will pass it by. The escalator takes you up to a dark hotel lobby, rather depressing...the hotel room corridors are very dark and narrow and downright dangerous.
The bathroom was small but it worked; there were a few small shelves for toilettries. Only once did I have to kill a cockroach crawling in the tub.
I was charged for an item from the mini bar which I did not take; I called later when I discovered the charge and the billing office removed it with no argument. It had not appeared on the bill under the door at the morning of chek-out. We had a deposit of 35 dollars per umbrella (we used two) placed on our bill in case we did not return them. We did!
The hotel has a great location, near Columbus Circle, subway stations, (we never took a cab...) Starbucks, cafes for breakfast, a large mall, called The Time Warner, (I think.)The concierges were VERY HELPFUL. Thorough, friendly.
We would not return to the Hudson Hotel. When friends ask us where we stayed, we are embarrassed to say...by chance, they are familiar with the place!

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Bad reviews are 100% true”
text:
A terrible, terrible hotel - even if it is cheap. We stayed during Sept 2003. Dirty, old, battered, peeling, cracked, saggy, dank, smelly, stained, with toilets that frequently overflowed (3 times in 6 days). 
Overall it's just depressing. Don't stay at Hotel Pennsylvania.

name: Hudson New York
title: “Hipster heaven or my version of ...?”
text:
The most expensive and least comfortable hotel I have ever stayed in and I travel a lot. The Hudson is painfully trendy, so if that is what you seek - be their guest. If you want comfort and good sleep, look again. The rooms are miniscule, even by NY standards- about 18 " from bed to wall. No desk, but a hip, tiny table and chair. Very dim florescent lighting - hard to put on make-up well. Anyone over 5'5" will have to sit sideways on the commode or knees will hit the wall. No coffeemaker. My room had a tiny TV whose volume wasn't loud enough to be heard over the very loud AC unit, located behind the headboard. The toilet flushed itself about once a minute. The shower (no tub) drain was very slow, so I had to shower fast or risk an overflow. The bed was not the worst, only the second worst I have every had. The hall lights are very low. I think that is so you can't see how dirty the halls really are.
And the cost for this hipster heaven? $671.28 for one night. And then they have the audacity to charge extra for internet access.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Never again”
text:
I would never stay here again. It was truly the worst place i have stayed. The rooms are dark, dirty and you get teh feeling that the carpets. curtains, if you can call them that, and the blankets have not been cleaned since the hday the place was built. The final straw for me was when i ran teh shower : i was greated with torrents of brown water filling the bath. I stayed one night and left. Never again.
I spend the rest of my stay and my other trips at the Park Central on 7th Avenue. Great place

name: Hotel 373
title: “lo necesario”
text: Hotel pequeñito, pero con una ubicacion excelente, se puede ir paseando a todos los lugares de interes turistico, nosotros cogimos el metro solo dos veces y por que estabamos cansados. No hace falta cogerlo, das un paseo y vas a todos lados. La limpieza de la habitacion muy buena. La unica pega que pondria es la insonorizacion de la habitacion, por lo demas todo muy muy bien, lo recomiendo. Ah que se me olvidaba, quiero decir que el personal estupendo nos ayudaron bastante y en todo momento muy amables.

name: Hotel Stanford
title: “Posizione super. Ottimo rapporto qualità/prezzo”
text: Perfetta scelta. Non mi sento di dire diversamente. A due passi dall'Empire State Building, a 5 mt dalla metropolitana e a 10 minuti da Times Square. Al momento della prenotazione noi avevamo chiesto le camere più nuove perchè non tutte lo sono e ci hanno accontentati. Consiglio la scelta della camera con i letti singoli: sono comodi ed è più facile riposare che nel letto matrimoniale. Colazione abbondante e ulteriore plus per questo albergo.

name: Hilton Manhattan East
title: “Wonderful experience”
text: I recently visited New York City for the first time December 27th thru January 2nd. I was very impressed with the Crowne Plaza at the UN. I arrived and was immediately helped by a very friendly doorman who helped with our bags and immediately found out which room I was in and took our bags to our room. Check in was quick even though the person checking me in was being trained. I was happy with the room because the twin beds were larger than I expected so that was a nice surprise. The maid service was awesome they didn't just make the beds and replace the towels they did as much to restore order to our room which day by day seemed to gather more and more souvenirs. It's a boutique hotel which I thought made it less stuffy from the fancier hotels, and the rates were awesome $139.00 with a rate change to 199.00 on the Tuesday before New Years Eve until January 1st. I did not get to explore much of the hotel because I was busy exploring the Big Apple. Enjoyed my stay at this hotel and will certainly pick this hotel for future trips to New York!

name: Hotel East Houston
title: “Super Stadthotel in bester Lage”
text:
Mal wieder in New York, mal wieder auf Hotelsuche - da fiel uns im Internet das East Houston Hotel in der Lower East Side auf. Nicht zu groß, nicht zu teuer, wunderbar mit Bus und U-Bahn zu erreichen und ganz in der Nähe von Soho und Tribeca gelegen, war es genau das Richtige für uns.
Äußerst freundliche Menschen begrüßten uns, und, obwohl wir bereits am Vormittag eincheckten, erhielten wir unser Zimmer.
Die Zimmer sind - für New Yorker Verhältnisse - mittelgroß mit einem geräumigen Bad. Was immer etwas knapp ist, sind Schränke und Ablageflächen, auch dabei liegt das Hotel im guten Mittelfeld. 
Der Service ist wirklich gut, sei es, ob man Eiswürfel braucht oder Infos oder eben der tägliche Zimmerdienst.
Im Keller gibt es morgendlich ein "continental breakfast" - dies hier war "outstanding". Neben endlos Kaffee, Bagles und Muffins gab es auch frisches Obst, Wurst und Käse, sogar Yoghurt.
Man konnte sich das ganze auch zusammenstellen und ab mit dem Aufzug auf die Dachterasse, die nicht nur den Rauchern Erleichterung schaffte, sondern allen einen schönen Blick über Manhattan bot (selbst eine Toilette wird dort zur Verfügung gestellt!).
Kurzum: Wir kommen wieder!

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Amazing location and would reccommend to anyone mick and paula thompson uk”
text: What a great spot this is.The location is superb,right on times sq.We were on 27 floor and slept like babies,no street noise.The staff were very attentive and helpful,the team on the concierge desk were very informative and willing.Our room was massive with a king size bed and 2 big easy chairs with a great view of times sq.Our room was clean and comfortable.The maids did a great job every day new towels and fresh beds everyday.42 in telly in room also.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Nice NYC getaway”
text: fantastic location- walk all day and night to Central park, theater district and Times Square, zillions of restaurants and attractions. Very adequate room size considering you are in midtown Manhattan. Accomodations are very modern with clean and updated bathrooms, furniture, etc. 2 great food spots inside the lobby- Norma's for incredible brunch and the delicious hamburger joint known city-wide. Hotel guests receive special attention at these busy restaurants.

name: Club Quarters Wall Street
title: “Clean, quite convenient, and the subway station is nearby”
text:
This is hotel is in a great location if you want to be in the Wall Street area. 
The hotel is generally quiet, and there's big drug store just across the street but I don't think it is 24hr though. 
The hotel lobby isn't big and grand, but the front desk service is fairly quick and professional. Nothing chirpy like you get in southern states, but efficiency and politeness is good enough for me. There's a lounge just beyond the front desk. It has a TV and couple of Internet PCs that guests can use for free. 
The rooms have wireless signal so your laptops or phones with WiFi can access the Net too. I wish the rooms have a small electronic safe though. 
There's no bottled water in the room, you have to go down the hall to a water dispenser to get your own. I like the cordless phone provided in the room though, cos it offsets not having a phone in the bathroom. 
There was no room slippers provided and I sort of missed that. 
There was nothing in the little fridge under the TV. If you want snacks and drinks stocked, you have to order them in the morning and they'll be in by evening. Might as well buy your own. 
Housekeeping did a great job daily cleaning up and straightening up my mess. 
All in, nothing fancy, but clean, quite convenient, and the subway station is nearby.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Enjoyable stay”
text:
Hotel staff was friendly and helpful. Even the doormen tried to help us find affordable parking for guests that were visiting us at the hotel. The rooms were very clean and beautifully furnished. Bathroom modern and updated, very pretty. Bed very comfortable Room size very good, especially for a NY hotel. Wonderful location.
Enjoyed stay very much.

name: Hudson New York
title: “Loved the Hudson”
text:
Just returned from a week at the Hudson. Loved this hotel! The location is not to be beat. Across from Time Warner Center. Close to subway and Central Park. The room was a bit smallish. The bed was extremely comfortable. 
I used the business center. Was well stocked and very convenient. 
The staff was more than friendly. Promptly greeted and offered assistance. Every time I saw a staff member, they greeted me. 
The hotel is very trendy and fun. The private park was amazing. 
The only detractor that I found was, as in other reviews, the bathroom is very small. I am very short and I found it confining, however, I was determined to make the best of it and adjusted. The toiletries were superb. One good thing the bathroom had was an ample shelf to put your makeup, curling iron, etc., which not all hotels have, so I feel that this helped. 
I had to switch to another hotel for the rest of my stay and was veeerrry sad to leave the Hudson. I will definitely stay there again.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Perfect hotel for the night”
text: We stayed in Le Parker Meridien when attending a military ball on Saturday night. We were well within walking distance to some great restaurants, the hotel staff was friendly and helpful, and the room comfortable and clean. TV was old - hummed and had fuzzy reception. But who cares, we had better stuff to do.

name: Hilton Manhattan East
title: “Muy recomendable”
text: El hotel se encuentra muy bien situado y comunicado: se encuentra muy cerca de la Estación Central y del edificio Crysler. Puedes ir caminando perfectamente al Empire State y a Times Square. El personal del hotel es muy atento y algunos hablan español perfectamente. Las habitaciones son muy acogedoras. Buena limpieza. Si volviera a NY me volvería a alojar en este hotel.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “So many choices, but Parker Meridien is a great one”
text: I have stayed here several times now and will pick it as often as I can get a good rate, relative to other nice spots nearby. I am always impressed at check-in with their "Welcome Back Mr. ___". This time I messed up and did not put two people on my reservation and did not even know it included breakfast. Our check-in host made sure we got the proper certificates to both get the free breakfasts. That is no small deal as breakfast at Norma's can easily run $30-40 a person, but is worth it. No kidding, this may be one of the top breakfast spots in the world. I have never seen so many diners taking pictures of their breakfast plates. But they are pretty awesome. Back to the hotel - the Jr. Suites are a great choice in Manhattan for this location if you can get them at a good price. Good space, nicely appointed, a bit contemporary but very comfortable with room to move around. Everything is nearby as you can take a hearty but doable walk to Broadway theaters, Art museum, Nat. Hist. museum, and of course Central Park, Columbus circle, shopping and plenty of really good restaurants are so close. Also, the lounge is a comfortable, fun spot to watch folks go by, Norma's is a "must do", and the hamburger joint is quirky spot, with OK food but fun and unique to have right in the lobby.

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “Very Nice Hotel”
text: We went 21st November 2011 - there were 5 'young at heart' ladies and 1 young lady - and were where very impressed - we arrived and unfortunately we were given king size rooms for three in each room but only with 1 bed (bit difficult) so we rang down to reception and they were changed immediatly to 2 rooms with double beds in (apparently got us mixed up with the very nice man that knocked on our door thinking he had the same room....... shame) (55chicos - thats what the ear plugs were for then, we did not need them either - We were on the Police station side also, on the 6th floor) - we did not eat in the hotel but the Cafe next door and one down the next block towards Bloomingdales on the same side of the road this was the better one and value for money - impressed with the cookie for each of us upon arrival at the hotel they were lovely - the hotel shop was very reasonable bought 2 sweatshirts for 40$ - very nice place no bugs, clean towels every day could not fault it - very close to most of the sites - Central park, Bloomingdales, Macys, Times square, Rockafella centre, the Subway is next door for the Up Town and one block up for Down Town - dont forget to go to 9/11 Memorial, is a must, beautiful even tho still building work still going on (Breaks your Heart) other than that all is very safe in the area, never felt threatened at all even at night

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Abgewohnt”
text:
Das Hotel ist leider schon stark abgewohnt und alles ist doch recht alt. Der Preis ist New York typisch recht hoch, dafür ist die Lage ganz gut, nur etwa 5 Min. vom Times Square entfernt.
Das Personal ist recht freundlich. Wer bereit ist für ein kleine sFrühstock zusätzlich etwa 25USD auszugeben kann es tun, ansonsten gibt es die Üblichen Fast food Geschäfte oder auch Cafes um die Ecke.
Zum Flughafen LGA kommt man recht fix. Metrostation zum durchfahren ist nur ein paar Blocks entfernt.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Great stay, great location”
text: Perfect location for all things NYC, whether business or pleasure - this is a great spot!

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “If it weren't for the stafff”
text: I guess it's my Midwest sensibility, but I'm always underwhelmed by accommodations in NYC, and this is no exception. The strength is its location--a relative oasis in Midtown, near the park, subway, theater... everywhere. And the staff is efficient and... just great. I know the construction is just temporary and not their fault, but when I was there in November, there was drilling on a Sunday at 7 am. I regularly slept through fire alarms and I couldn't sleep through this. And "temporary" I don't think means like a few days. I think it means months to a year of foundation work. I ate breakfast elsewhere, but the dining area is obviously insufficient, the spa closed while I was there, the lobby hardly obvious, sheathed in scaffolding. I would stay there again in the future (like a year from now), but I would call first and see about the general state of things. As for the reviewer who mentioned closing certain areas of the hotel... My understanding is that the most tedious of work is next door, not in the hotel, and at least from when I was there the noise is so loud that no part of the hotel is safe. I was on the 29th floor and still hurting. The room? Large for NY but kind of sterile. I did get a peek of a higher floor room, and that was better. Other than the front desk staff, the other high point was the bar on a weeknight.

name: The Marcel at Gramercy
title: “L'hôtel St Marcel at Gramercy...”
text: L'hôtel St Marcel at Gramercy est bien situé dans le quartier EAST SIDE plutôt tranquille et il se trouve assez près des transports publics, bus et métro. L'accueil est très agréable et le personnel discret et efficace. Les chambres ne sont pas très spacieuses et la décoration générale un peu triste. Mais dans l'ensemble pour un séjour touristique d'une semaine c'était très correct. Heureusement le petit déjeuner a 13 dollars n'est pas compris dans le prix de la chambre car il ne présente rien d'exceptionnel. Attention toutefois car les tarifs indiqués sont toujours hors taxes, comme partout à NEW YORK ! Les taxes sont importantes et représentent un peu moins de 20 %. Pour notre séjour de 8 nuitées, les taxes ont coûté presque 400 dollars, ce qui n'est pas négligeable. Un détail parfois énervant, le fait qu'il n'y ait que deux ascenseurs, utilisés également par le personnel de l'hôtel, ce qui fait qu'il faut parfois les attendre assez longtemps. Je ne déconseillerai pas cet hôtel a des amis. Mais si je devais retourner à NEW YORK pour un séjour touristique, je pense que j'aimerai découvrir avant tout un autre quartier que celui de Gramercy mais cela ne remet pas en cause la qualité de l'hôtel et de son tarif correct pour une ville comme NEW YORK.

name: The Mansfield
title: “Great Location, Great Hotel, Great staff!”
text:
My sister & I stayed at this hotel at the end of October.
After reading reviews before our arrival at this site I was very skeptical.
We had a wonderful experience there. The staff was wonderful & the location of this hotel is perfect. The rooms are very clean & small - expect "europe" type of rooms and you will be prepared.
I have nothing bad to say about this hotel & plan on staying there again
in the very near future. NY ROCKS!

name: The Marcel at Gramercy
title: “Excellent”
text:
J'ai séjourné 10 nuits dans cet hôtel idéalement situé à Manhattan. L'accueil est très agréable (mention spéciale à Lindsay et à Juan), l'endroit est parfaitement propre et décoré avec goût, la terrasse sur le toit donne une vue imprenable sur l'Empire State Building. Préférer les chambres donnant sur l'arrière pour plus de calme. Ambiance sympathique, branchée sans être kitsch, et quelques petits plus qui font la différence : deux ordinateurs et une imprimante à dispo, thé et café toute la journée, conseils d'adresses sympa. La station de métro de la ligne 4-5-6 est à deux pas et dessert une bonne partie des lieux à voir. 
Une adresse précieuse pour un rapport qualité-prix intéressant.

name: Hotel Stanford
title: “Buena estancia en hotel céntrico.”
text:
Pasamos ocho días fantásticos en NY a principios del mes de diciembre de 2008. Dos semanas antes de ir aún no teníamos contratado el alojamiento, y la cosa pintaba un poco mal!!! Aunque inicialmente habíamos pensado en alquilar un apartamento, finalmente optamos por un hotel. Y lo cierto es que ha sido una gran eleción.
El hotel Stanford tiene una ubicación genial, a una calle de Macy's, con el Empire State y la Fifth Avenue a la vuelta de la manzana, y Times Square a 10 minutos de un agradable paseo andando. Parada de metro en la puerta, y la Penn Station a 200 m. Además está situado junto a los hoteles Radisson y La Quinta Manhattan. Una zona muy céntrica, pero a la vez bastante tranquila y sobre todo segura.
Sobre la estancia: viajamos un grupo de 4 chicas, con lo que pudimos reservar una suite genial para las 4 con una pequeña salita. Baño con ducha y bañera, TV de plasma y vistas. Y nos salió muy bien de precio. Unos 500$/por persona para 7 noches. La habitación está totalmente reformada, y muy limpia. Especialmente el baño, que siempre brillaba.
La mayoría del personal del hotel es coreano, bastante amable, y los porteros son hispanos, muy serviciales. Además, el hotel estaba invadido de españoles (las fechas eran propicias para ello, pues era el puente de la Constitución).
Si hay que ponerle alguna pega al hotel, es lo que otras críticas mencionan: el desayuno, que es bastante limitado, pero suficiente, aunque después de una semana ya estábamos cansadas (Se puede remediar yendo algún día a desayunar a cualquier lugar de los alrededores). Y sobre lo que se dice de que el ascensor es lento: no es para tanto.... Además, cuando estuvimos nosotras estaban en obras para instalar un nuevo ascensor, con lo que, problema solucionado.
En fin, una estancia muy agradable en una ciudad fantástica, a la espero poder regresar muy pronto.

name: La Quinta Inn Manhattan
title: “Good value and location”
text:
My husband and I stayed at The Manhatttan Laquinta in November 2007 and I would recommend this location. We found the rooms clean and the staff helpful. The continental breakfast and daily newspapers were a nice bonus. The location is very close to Macy's, subway connections, and MSG.
We were pleasantly surprised to be in the heart of little Korea and had great restaurants all along the street many being open 24 hours. We felt safe at this location and I would stay there again. I would like to thank the manager Sunnie for her help in making our stay in New York City great. I look forward to coming back.
Yours truly ST.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Good, solid choice for mid-town”
text: Other than spotty elevator service, our stay at Le Parker Meridian Mid-town was more than satisfactory. Pleasant personnle, clean rooms, flexible maid service, and location is excellent.

name: The Alex Hotel
title: “dibattuto: mediocre sistemazione buona posizione”
text:
premetto è stata la mia prima volta a ny.
Ho letto le altre recensioni, ho visto la posizione, il numero di stelle e ..sigh il prezzo e mi sono detto: non posso prendere una fregatura.E' così è stato: non ho preso una fregatura.. ma probabilmente non ho trovato l'albergo che cercavo. All'arrivo hall piccolissima non sembra neanche di entrare in Hotel: non è un problema; inizialmente mi avvisano che ci sono solo camere queen size mentre avevo prenotato una king: al mio diniego però mi chiedono solo di attendere qualche minuto e mi preparano la stanza prenotata: risolto anche questo.
Camere grandi, come il letto: arredamento vecchio stile anni 70 tutto in legno in parte rovinato. Bagno piccolo con vasca - doccia.Tutto abbastanza nella norma: 5 piano e la vista del Chrysler building mi rasserena un pò.
Considerazione: da un Hotel da oltre 390 dollari a notte( senza colazione e senza free wifi ) un europeo o forse un italiano si aspetta molto ma molto di più.
Però la posizione secondo me è il punto di forza per chi vuole girare manhattan. a tre isolati la Grand Station da dove partono treni e metropolitane ; siamo all'angolo tra la 45th east e la 3 avenue: da qui passeggiare verso sud e o verso ovest a "due passi " da qualsiasi attrazione merita, veramente.
Conclusioni: dibattuto; sarei falso se mi dichiarassi entusiasta. Forse la prossima volta opterei per un appartamento. Oppure consigliatemi un albergo che valga il prezzo pagato.

name: Club Quarters Wall Street
title: “buon hotel”
text: Posizione comoda, trasporti metro vicini, personale gentile ed efficiente. Abbiamo soggiornato in questo hotel per 2 notti approfittando delle offerte fine settimana e ci siamo trovati molto bene. L'hotel è pulito confortevole e accogliente. Il letto molto comodo (molto meno il divano letto in cui ha dormito nostro figlio). Gratuitamente distributori di acqua e pc con internet in ogni piano

name: The Shoreham
title: “el hotel perfecto para visitar manhattan”
text:
Estuve en el Shoreham durante 5 noches. Es un hotel de los denominados boutique, es decir en el que no hay servicio de comida, por el contrario no encontramos con un hotel acogedor, moderno, y limpio. Las habitaciones no son excesivamente grandes, pero a la vez son acogedoras, las camas son grandes y comodas y el baño es espacioso.Hay ordenadores con cnexion a internet gratis en la recepcion y lo mejor: una cafetera express gratis para todos los clientes, lo que, teniendo en cuenta el cafe de nueva york es un puntazo a favor.
Lo que mas destaca de este hotel es su situacion, a 100 metros de la 5ª av. y cerca de lo Times square el rockefeller center, etc... ademas en la zona del hotel hay bastantes restaurantes de diferentes tipos.
Sin duda en mi proxima visita a N.Y. eligire este hotel.

name: The Shoreham
title: “Had a great stay”
text:
Three of us stayed for 7 nights over Thanksgiving week at the deluxe 2 queens room. The room was very big, but the bathroom was small. The room faced another building so we couldn't open the shades, but that wasn't a big deal. The room was hot even though it was very cold outside, so we had to turn the AC on from time to time (I'm glad the AC worked, or we would have been miserably hot). The location is excellent, just half a block from 5th Ave. The staff was friendly and the two computers in the lobby were very convenient to use. We felt that paying $16 for a continental breakfast at the hotel was way expensive for what you got, so we just went to Cafe Europa a block and a half away. There are other choices of places to eat nearby as well.
We would definitely stay there again.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Birthday celebration”
text: I felt some trepidation about staying at this hotel after reading the reviews before travelling, but it was absolutely fine. The rooms were not spacious but we were not paying 5 star prices. Location was brilliant, right next to the subway, two blocks from central park and only a few blocks from Times Square. We found all the staff helpful, room was clean and adequate. Lifts were sometimes very busy at certain times of the day, but we had a very enjoyable three days at this hotel - you do not go to New York to sit in the hotel room.

name: The Marcel at Gramercy
title: “tolle lage, freundliches personal, schöne zimmer”
text:
hotel ist liegt super, unweit der u-bahn-haltestelle an der 23. midtown manhatten wunderbar zu fuß erreichbar.
sehr zuvorkommendes hotelpersonal. etwas dunkler eingangsbereich - dafür aber recht stylish.
die ersten beiden nächte mussten wir leider mit einem extrem kleinen zimmer vorlieb nehmen (im 2. stock dürfte es nur so kleine geben), weil wir erst spät einchecken konnten und das hotel nur noch das zimmer übrig hatte. erst am übernächsten tag war wieder ein größeres zimmer frei, in das wir dann anstandslos umziehen konnten. beide zimmer aber sehr sauber, modern eingerichtet und komfortabel (das kleine halt wirklich zu klein für 2 erwachsene mit koffern).
leider kein free wifi - sollte eigentlich standard sein, finde ich. gegen relativ hohe gebühr hätte man sich zugang kaufen können.
fernseher bzw. empfang hat immer wieder gespuckt - aber es gibt ja auch anderes, das man in NY tun kann :)

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Feo, da miedo”
text: Lo peor, sin internet en la habitación y en el lobby se paga, feo, buena ubicación, buena ducha, sucio, atención desplicenteFeo, da miedo se parece a las películas de miedo, cobran mucho por las llamadas locales, si no fuera por la ubicación, lo demolería. Si se usa sólo para dormir y bañarse está bien, las mucamas atentas, el personal del mesón unos pesados

name: The Milburn Hotel
title: “Staff is incredible”
text: I stayed at the Milburn because both the Lucerne and the Excelsior were booked. (I usually stay at one or the other in NYC.) The staff at the Milburn are friendlier than either of the other two hotels. The only real complaints I had are that the bell staff are no where to be seen, there was no robe in my room, and the bathtub couldn't be plugged, so a bath wasn't possible. The water pressure isn't great and the housekeeping staff were noisy early in the morning (7am - vacuuming shortly after 9 am.) I would stay here again if need be because the price is incredibly affordable for this area of the city.

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “Not What You Would Expect for a Large Hotel”
text:
We stayed here for one week and was not impressed to say the least.
First of all to pay the bellman to store your luggage while you wait for your room to be ready was RIDICULOUS. But having to pay the bellman again to retrieve your luggage was even more RIDICULOUS... Don't the bellman receive an hourly wage? Looked like they were thriving on the luggage storage/retrieval tips. Even saw a bellman in the corner counting how much he made. UTTERLY RIDICULOUS!
In such a large hotel to be renovating the business center when it seemed the occupancy was high was also crazy. How can you move your business center to one of your meeting rooms and only have one desktop available? Not what you would expect for such a large hotel. Not everyone has a laptop!!!!
The rooms were also not in the best conditions either. The bathrooms needed some work. The rooms needed renovating. The fitness center smelled MOLDY!!!!
The best thing about the room was the flat screen tv. Also the fact that a restaurant was beside it and the subway was within walking distance.
Would not recommend this hotel and would not return.

name: Econo Lodge Times Square
title: “Great location - Clean and Convenient”
text: Stayed at this hotel for one night on 10/24. I stay in a lot of Manhattan hotels in this price range and this one is right up there. Great staff at the front desk, clean public areas, nice crisp white linens, and a clean bathroom. Pair that with a great central location, free bottled water and a nice TV selection and I'm a happy traveler.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Great place, great location and very clean”
text:
The Millenium Broadway is in a great location for all tourists visiting New York. The rooms are spacious and clean. We were on the 33rd floor and heard no noise from Times Sq. It's located on a side street just off Times Sq.
We did not eat in the hotel, so cannot comment on the resteraunt. We did eat everyday from the deli across the road, which was amazing and you could get anything you want to eat day & night.
A tip for travellers who do not leave till the evening, we checked out at 12pm and kept our backs in the reception, but due to the 90 degree heat we required a shower , so we got showered in the gym on the 16th floor, so all fresh for travelling back to Scotland.

name: La Quinta Inn Manhattan
title: “BEWARE!! SCAM!! DO NOT BOOK THIS HOTEL!!!”
text: Booked the sister to this hotel, The Red Roof Inn Manhattan via hotel website (Apple Core Hotels), got a confirmation number and thought I was set. Then they called this morning to inform me they had made a mistake and I no longer had a reservation here and would have to stay at their other hotel located across the street, the La Quinta Manhattan. As you can see this La Quinta hotel has terrible reviews! When I arrived in NY I tried to talk to the staff at the Red Roof, explaining I had made the reservation, had a confirmation number, had paid for the room, all to no avail. I was sent packing to La Quinta. But after hauling my bags through the snow storm to this hotel, they said they could not accomodate me after all, since the person whose room I was to take had not checked out. It was outrageous. They shook their heads, too bad, and told me they'd made me a reservation at another hotel, which also had terrible reviews and where I would never have voluntarily stayed, then they told me I could take a cab there AT MY OWN EXPENSE. You cannot trust this hotel chain. And they won't care. Look elsewhere!

name: Econo Lodge Times Square
title: “Weekend getaway”
text:
We had a wonderful stay at the Econo Lodge Time Square. This is our third time staying at
this hotel and we will be going back. The beds are great and location is great. Nice continental breakfast. Natasha and the other ladies at front desk was very kind and helpful.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Decent Budget Hotel”
text:
After having read reviews of this hotel I arrived with some trepidation as to it's standards, however the room was of a decent size, clean, tidy and secure - All you need of somewhere to be used as a base. The hotel was always busy and the staff did seem a little stressed but they were always polite. Fantastic location as Time Square, Central Park and 5th Ave a stroll away. 
As long as you are not looking for luxury then this is a great hotel to use a base I will definitely use it next time I am in NYC

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text: Was worried about staying after reading reviews but should't have. Just returned from a great 5 night stay. Ok the room wasn't the biggest bit it was clean and who goes to NY to sit in a hotel room. Location superb. Central park 5 mins away and Times Sq 10 mins walk away. Would definetly use hotel again.
