name: The Shoreham
title: “Céntrico, limpio, moderno, super recomendable.”
text: Hola, acabamos de llegar de Nyc y no podiamos dejar de hablar del hotel Shoreham en el que hemos estado. Como sabemos lo que se sufre hasta q llegas y ves donde te has metido, queremos deciros q no dudeis con el Shoreham. Es super centrico en la 55 entre la 5 y la 6 av. Está muy limpio, cambian las sabanas y toallas a diaro, te dan un albornoz y aspiran la habitación tambien cada dia. La decoración es muy moderna y minimalista, nada q ver con el tipico hotel con edredón y cortinas de flores. Te dejan el periodico en la puerta de la habitación cada mañana. En la habitación tienes tv plana de 32 pulgadas, equipo de cd y minibar. Cuando llegas te reciben con una copa de cava en recepción. El desayuno no está incluido pero tienes en el hall una maquina de café, chocolate e infusiones gratis para cuando te apetezca. La cafeteria es super cool y tiene un reservado increible. Os cuelgo unas fotos para q veias q lo dicho y lo q vereis en la web del hotel corresponde con la realidad, y eso q nosotros estuvimos en una habitación doble normalita, la 312 para ser exactos, no quiero saber como serán las superiores. Si aún asi teneis dudas y quereis saber algo más, aqui estamos.

name: Sohotel
title: “Perfect for a short stay in SoHo/Lower East Side”
text: I wasn't sure from reading the reviews if this was a good place for an older woman travelling solo. I could not have felt more secure. Room was small but well designed. The bad was comfortable and the linens fresh and clean. Beautiful brick exposed wall, nice hardwoods. Bathroom was small but efficient. There was coffee in the lobby, but no other food available in the hotel, but plenty of options within a stone's throw. Great location. Will stay there again.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “great location and price”
text: This hotel offers reasonable rates and a wonderful location. Easy to walk to subways, time square, etc. Nice hotel with friendly staff. We felt safe there. Rooms were decent enough. This is great value to see the Big Apple.

name: Hudson New York
title: “What a disaster!”
text:
I stayed here on business, and was astounded by the poor quality of the service and facilities. The only thing this place had going for it was the location.
I sent a letter to the hotel detailing my complaints (via email & USPS) and to date have received no reply. Below is a detailed description of my experience. I would just add that my fellow business colleagues staying in the same hotel were equally appalled and we all have no plans to ever return.
1.On the evening of the first night of my stay, I invited a few friends to my room. In person, I asked the concierge to arrange for six glasses to be brought to the room. When the glasses had not arrived 30 minutes later, and a call to room-service had gone unanswered, I went back down to the reception desk. The receptionist said the concierge had left for the evening but that he would take care of the matter himself. Twenty more minutes passed and still no glasses arrived so I again went to the same person at the reception desk to inquire. This person’s reaction was to inform me that he had already called housekeeping to ask for the glasses (rather than, say, apologizing for the delay and working to rectify the matter). When I told him that despite his call no glasses had arrived, so perhaps he should do something further, he promised to call again. When the glasses had not arrived 20 minutes later (yes, this is now over an hour after my first request), I went to the library bar and fetched some glasses myself. The glasses from housekeeping never arrived. 
2.Later the same night, a security guard knocked on the door and informed me of “numerous noise complaints” related to my gathering. In a rather aggressive manner—and prior to giving me a chance to respond—he proceeded to outline the dire consequences should the noise level not go down. First, I pity those who had to launch “numerous complaints” before I was informed of the problem—from their point of view, that can not seem to have been responsive. Second, I had no intention of disturbing anyone and indeed there was no threatened second visit (although, given the apparent dysfunction of the hotel, that may have been for other reasons!).
3.Neither our guests that night, nor I, were particularly impressed with the interior of the room where, for example, the floorboards were literally coming apart at the seams and some were even lifted from the floor. The shelves in the bathroom were coming out of the wall and had to be pushed back in, and in addition the room fan was quite loud. 
4.I had two computers, one personal and one for business, so I called the desk to ask if the charge for Internet service was per room or per computer and were told it was per room. The next day when I needed to use the two computers, I found this information was incorrect. The receptionist said she would put a note in our account such that we would only be charged once for that day. Despite this promise, upon checkout there were two charges which I then had to spend time at the front desk correcting.
5.Upon checkout, I arranged for late departure for my husband who was travelling with me. Despite this, and in contravention to a “do not disturb” sign, someone knocked on the door at around 10 am and kept at it until it was answered. When my husband pointed out that late departure had been arranged, that regular checkout time had not come, and there was a no disturbance request on the door, the woman who knocked responded that guests sometimes forgot to remove the sign upon leaving. It did not seem to dawn on the person that an apology was in order. 
6.On the day I arrived I left a message for a colleague with the concierge. She verified that the guest was in the hotel, and took the written message (in an envelope with his name on the front) from me. My colleague received this message upon checkout 2 days later! This is simply unacceptable.
7.It seemed sadly consistent with my experience at the hotel that the vending machines on my floor were out of order when I arrived and remained so for the duration of my stay.
In sum, the hotel seems to be in a state of disrepair with little communication between the employees and even less commitment to making guests feel comfortable. Both as a business traveler and as a frequent traveler, I know that I will not stay at that hotel again or recommend it to anyone else or to others at my company.

name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Fifth Ave
title: “Modern, clean, free wifi/breakfast, amazing location!”
text:
We have stayed in a lot of Holiday Inn Express properties, mostly because I find the beds/sheets/linens are consistent property to property (comfortable!) and I love the free hot breakfast. I was concerned that in NYC I would run into problems I hear are consistent with many budget friendly hotels (loud street noise, cramped rundown outdated rooms, rude staff, having to pay for everything - breakfast/wifi). 
I was so pleased that none of this true at this property!! The staff were nothing but wonderful and accommodating. Our room, albeit small (you will find this in EVERY hotel room in this city, you want a big spacious room, splurge for a $700/night suite somewhere), was spotless, modern, and the beds were comfortable. We had zero street noise, in fact, I could not even hear anyone in any of the neighboring rooms. Wifi is free and high quality (I noted that in a lot of other hotels you must pay for wifi). 
Breakfast was hot (eggs, bacon, sausage, biscuits, pancakes, cold/hot cereal, fruit and yogurt), and the staff worked tirelessly to make sure everything was stocked. The breakfast area is tight, but they have done an excellent job arranging the seating, and my husband and I never had to wait to sit down. Yes people are conversing amongst themselves.... you want a quiet private breakfast, either take it to your room (via the convenient and readily available trays) or go buy it yourself in a restaurant. Good luck finding a free breakfast of this quality at this room price somewhere else.
There were some complaints made by other reviewers, but really I feel they are unwarranted and the writers had a ridiculous notion of what to expect from a hotel in NYC. For the price, and being 1 block off of the center of Times Square, and within walking distance of Rockefellar Plaza, The Theatre District, ect..... this cannot be beat!

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan Chelsea
title: “Perfect hotel in great location”
text:
Me and my partner stayed at this hotel for 5 nights and could not ask for more. Reception staff were very polite and friendly o arrival and gave us all relevant information including the free wifi code and a drinks token. They also gave us the option of a two double or a king room which was nice. We opted for the king room was was amazing.
Bed very comfortable, bathroom was spotless, tv was around 40" and gave you the usual American tv channels. A free safe was very useful to store expensive items. The room was refreshed every day without fail with fresh towels and didn't have to call reception once with any problems. Our toilet became blocked and we requested help as we were leaving the hotel one morning and they said they would get someone up to sort it which they did well before we got back that day.
Staff always acknowledged us each morning and night as we left and returned to the hotel. The concierge lady was also extremely helpful with suggesting where to go to eat.
This hotel is only 3 stops on the subway from times square which takes around 4 minutes. There's a subway two blocks down which takes 2 minutes to walk to.
I would definitely recommend this hotel to everyone staying in new york for any purpose and would easily stay again when I revisit.

name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Fifth Ave
title: “Excellent Location”
text: As others have said excellent location,compact but clean and functional hotel. Easy stroll down the block to Times Square,Macys,Union Station,Bryant Park . Excellent.

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Bene purchè in offerta”
text: L'hotel è bello e curato, la camera, una quadrupla d'angolo con 2 finestre, era spaziosa e dignitosamente arredata, con letti comodissimi. Ma il bagno era delle dimensioni di un francobollo, con la porta che sbatteva sulla tazza e la doccia nella vasca con la tenda. Pulizia della camera un po' carente: sotto al letto ho trovato la scarpa di una cliente precedente! Comunque è un bell'hotel, personale disponibile (ma i facchini non hanno toccato una valigia per aiutarmi nella prima rampa di scale necessaria per arrivare alla reception, nè mi hanno indicato dove prendere l'ascensore!), posizione strategica, ingresso scenografico. Da considerare solo se in offerta su expedia, viste le tariffe normali!

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “Just ok for short visit”
text:
Staff at front desk is not very courteous. When we arrived for check-in, man sitting behind his desk looks up at us and says: Yes?. Apparently, we were distrubing him. The lack-of-service attitude is consistent with both of the staff members that we encountered (also hispanic woman). According to our reservation , check-in was at 2:00, but the staff told us to come back at 3:00 only.
Also, before checking out, we looked under the beds to ensure that we had not forgotten or dropped anything. To our shock, we found a device to repel critters (not sure for what insect or critter it was exactly).
Good points: free parking, ideal location, reasonable pricing.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Parfait pour une 1er découverte de NYC”
text: Les services de cet immense hôtel sont sommaires mais suffisant pour découvrir NYC avec un petit budget. Pas de prestations supplémentaires ni meme la wifi ce qui est dérangeant quand on souhaite découvrir la ville. L'hôtel est vieux mais pas vétuste, est vraiment idéalement située

name: Herald Square Hotel
title: “Would stay again - enjoyed the character”
text: I stayed here May 15-17 on business. The hotel is older and that gives it a bit of character (for example - only one of the elevators goes to the 9th floor (where my room was) - the other elevator goes to the 8th and you have to take stairs up from there). There is bullet proof glass at the reception desk - I didn't mind it. The desk does after all look out directly on the street. Seemed that most guests were European. The lobby area is not all that - but then, I don't pick my hotels for the lobby. The rooms are small (expected) but comfortable. The decor is fine, and everything in my room was clean and worked properly. You aren't getting all kinds of freebies with this hotel - but internet was free and worked very well. The hotel is in a good central location - easy to get to Penn Station, and other parts of NY. It was my first real trip to NY so in addition to business I wanted to spend a bit of time catching some sites and I was able to easily see a lot. Times Square is only about 10 blocks away, Central Park is about 15 blocks, and United Nations not far either. Bryant Park and the NYC Library are about 4 blocks away and the Empire State Building is 2 blocks away. An easy cab ride to Financial District and you can see all the parts down there (9/11 memorial, wall st., etc. - that cab ride is about $10 with tip).

name: Dream New York
title: “Dommage pour les chambres au 13...”
text: Dommage pour les chambres au 13 etages car audessus bar et musique jusquà 4h du matin les nuits du vendredi et samedi sinon satisfaite

name: Washington Jefferson Hotel
title: “Nice Staff, Clean Rooms”
text: Bathrooms very clean, room ok (rugs old), bed ok comfort, housekeeping staff is super nice, front desk peeps ok. I'm not sure why this hotel has gotten such high marks bc it's just ok. My room was very small, but, wasn't bad. Nothing to write home about but not terrible either. It was inexpensive and clean, and that was enough. The free wireless was SUPER slow.

name: The Marcel at Gramercy
title: “Bonne situation tres bel hotel”
text:
Nous avons passé 6 nuits dans cet hotel tres bien situé. Personnel sympatique, hotel tres propre. Nous avions une chambre coté cour, donc plus calme, pas tres grande, mais tres confortable.
Tres bonne situation, avons tout fait à pied. 5 min de Union square, 15 min de l'Empire State.
Petit dej en terrasse par beau temps tres agréable, et vue sur l'Empire.
Je recommande

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “Worked for us”
text:
Our family of 4 stayed at the Travel Inn for two nights before a cruise. We wanted to be close to the terminal so we chose this hotel. We arrived at 11AM expecting to have to store our bags before check in but to our pleasant surprise, they allowed us to check in early! Thank you!
I was a little worried about what looked like a nightclub across the street and there was also a police station (or fire station?) and thought there'd be a lot of noise. But there wasn't and we slept comfortably. Location was fine and we walked to eateries on 9th. Didn't realize how close we were to Times Square until our last day!

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Great location - Good Value”
text:
Stayed there on a recent weekend. Got a good price on the room, especially by New York standards.
Room was clean, good-sized and relatively modern although the TV could use some updating. Bed was very large and comfortable and bedding was quite nice. Room had a very useful desk in front of the window with an actual Aeron chair which was a nice touch. The bathroom was decent-sized, had plenty of good quality towels and nice shampoo, conditioner, etc. Only small negative was that the tub had been remodeled using a "bath fitter" type insert so the floor was a bit springy (yes I'm being picky).
Location is excellent, adjacent Carnegie Hall, one block from Central Park, a ten minute walk to Times Square and a block from two subway lines. Our room on the 20th floor had a partial view of the park.
Lobby was OK, but nothing special, but the lobby bar is definitely worth a visit. A couple good beers on tap (Leffe for one) and everything came with a cocktail mix of warm nuts and very yummy deep fried olives. I didn't make it to the "Burger Joint", but in the lobby, behind a curtain is literally a burger joint with $8 burgers. Where else are you going to find that in NY?
Very good experience and would visit again.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Feels glamourous”
text:
The hotel is in a great location two blocks south of the centre of Central Park. There is a Starbucks across the street from the front entrance, but you will need to venture farther afield (several blocks) to find breakfast/brunch on a Sunday (the wait at the hotel’s restaurant was over two hours). The Burger Joint in the hotel’s lobby is a good choice for burgers, but make sure you have enough people in your group to send someone off to grab a table as soon as it becomes available.
Check-in for us was fast and straightforward, and we were allowed to check in at around noon on a holiday weekend. The staff was quite pleasant and personable. We found them to be quite accommodating throughout our stay, and when we requested something, it was handled quickly and professionally.
The two sets of elevators meant a stop-over on the way to the 42nd-floor swimming pool. There appeared to be a charge for guests to use the fitness centre.
We had a Deluxe room that would have seemed spacious in the Prairies and felt downright palatial in Manhattan. My partner and I had divergent views of the décor. I liked the Mad Men 1960’s feel of the room (with built-in furniture and a small bar) that seemed glamourous in comparison to the Westins we normally frequent. Though the room was spotless and everything was in excellent repair, my partner found it dated (though admitting the service and location were better than the Westin Times Square). The swivelling television stand was cool and useful for watching in bed or in the sitting area, but it is probably time to get rid of the CRT television in favour of flat-panels. The room was very quiet during our stay, and the bathroom was clean and modern (though I would have preferred a shower door to the curtain). Our view was of buildings, as one would expect in New York (though the park view from the pool level was quite nice).
One thing I particularly liked about this hotel is that everything was branded and felt expensive/high-quality/tailored. From towels to shot-glasses to gel-ink pens, everything was marked Parker Méridien, and the normal hotel stuff (do not disturb sign, keycards, etc) were more whimsical than you would expect based on the marble-and-columns lobby. The hotel has gone out of its way to differentiate itself from major chains (though still Starwood). Interestingly (given the abundance of generic hotels in New York), we have since noticed this hotel’s interior (hallways and rooms) used in both Law and Order and The Good Wife.
Thanks to the excellent service, good location, and generous room size, this is my new favourite hotel in Midtown.

name: Dream New York
title: “Parfait, pour tout sauf peut...”
text: Parfait, pour tout sauf peut être le manque de langue Française, sinon impéccable, proximité idéale, de plus faisant partie du groupe 1) hotel - 2) restaurant et eptit déjeuner - bar pour les fêtards le tout séparé seulement par 1 porte

name: La Quinta Inn Manhattan
title: “A fantastic value place to stay”
text: My family and I stayed at the La Quninta over the Easter break and had a fantasic time. The hotel is close to all the major attractions; benefits from helpful staff, decent-sized rooms, a great bar with a view and a fine continental breakfast. The hotel made our first trip to New York memorable..and hopefully it will not be our last!

name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Fifth Ave
title: “Awesome location!”
text:
We (my husband and I) stayed here Aug. 4 - 7, 2011.
Room was clean, small, but again clean. King bed was comfy. (I am not sure how much space there would be with two doubles.)
We had 2nd floor room (not much of a view) and I am glad we did. Elevator was slow at times so we would use stairs.
Front desk was fine and friendly.
Maid service - exceptional.
Free breakfast was o.k., only went down once but it was a great way to start off the day.
Coffee - always available and free, 24 / 7.
Had pizza from across the street one night to get my NYC pizza fill and it was great. Also sold six packs and bottles of wine.
Two blocks to Times Square and all the subways you need.
We did not have car and can't give info on parking. We took Amtrak into city.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Great Location, Minimal Accomodations”
text: Lobby was very cozy. Rooms were dorm size. Standard double beds are actually twin beds unless you ask for double/double upgrade to full size beds. No vending machines, no iron or refrigerator in room. Can hear noise from streets below or nearby rooms. This is obviously an old renovated building. The locations was excellent. Staff was polite. This is a great place to stay if you require minimum accomodations and perks.

name: The Mansfield
title: “Sehr zentral, kleine sehr nette Zimmer, Kaffee for free”
text: Das Hotel in der 44. Strasse nähr 5th Avenue ist wirklich mittendrin, Broadway, Times Square, Emire State Building, Central Park, Madison Square Garden, Grand Central Station etc. in lockerer Fussweite. Die Zimmer sind klein, aber schön und stilvoll eingerichter, der Service ist prima und eine netter Raum mit 24-Stunden Kaffee ist sehr nett, Frühstück ist in Ordnung (Auf Anfrage vor Ort kostenlos). Der Fitnessraum ist zwar ohne Fenster, aber gut ausgestattet. Alles also prima. Sehr zu empfehlen.

name: La Quinta Inn Manhattan
title: “Great Room Great Price”
text: Stayed here with my sister (who was visiting NYC for the first time) in April and she picked this room for $79 a night. I've stay in many a NYC hotel room, so naturally, I was terrified before I got there but, once there, was shockingly surprised. The hotel has absolutely no character or charm... but the room was clean & spacious (NYC standards), the service friendly, the location great -- all at a really affordable price for NYC. I was floored. The bathroom was marble! (BTW the bathrooms are nothing to write home about but at this price they are.)

name: Econo Lodge Times Square
title: “Location, location, location”
text:
We booked this hotel because of it's location and we're really pleased that it was so close to Times Square, Broadway theaters, and my husband's work conference. 
POSITIVES
**Location! Only a 5 min. walk to Times Square and an easy walk to all the Broadway theaters.
**Cleanliness - Our room was very clean. We did the usual bedbug test, especially since it's New York. We also checked the bedbug registry and they have no reports so far.
**Continental breakfast - Not a huge selection, but they had bagels, coffee, pastries, cereal, etc.
**Shower pressure - I hate when I go to a hotel and the water trickles out of the shower head. Great pressure here.
NEGATIVES
**We could not adjust the heat and it was quite warm in our room and really hot in the hallways.
**Noise - We could hear street conversations, honking, and outside noise all night. There are window air conditioning units in the windows and the sound just goes right through the vents.
**Room size. Our room was TINY. Only one of us could walk to the bed at a time. The other person had to duck in the bathroom. It was hard to find a place for both of our suitcases. My husband left his by the door to the room. We did see inside another room while it was being cleaned and it was larger and the furniture layout was better than ours.
**There was some problem with their key card reader and they could not re-set our key so we had to wait for someone to walk us to our room and let us in. Minor issue and it was fixed later in the day.
**Our tv reception would come and go. It was perfect the first day and fuzzy after that. I checked to make sure the cables were secure and they were.
We were not in our room much since there is so much to do in NY so it was perfect for us. If you are planning on staying in your room a lot, I would not recommend it unless you are alone. It is cramped and hot. For sleeping purposes, it was fine. I was so tired from exploring NY all day that I could tune out the street noise and get a good night's sleep.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan Chelsea
title: “Wonderful stay at 4 Point Sheraton”
text:
Spent 4 days at this gem hotel back in July and totally enjoyed the experience. To begin with, New York hotels are expensive all year around even for a single room especially during the summer months. So when I found out this hotel offers a special rate of $140 a night for a nice double room in the middle of Manhattan with free internet included, I had to jump on the deal even it is 3 months ahead!
Location of the hotel is simply unbeatable - in the heart of Chelsea between 6th & 7th. Hotel premise is on the quiet W. 25th street, totally tucked away from the busy traffic. So many shops and restaurants around and easy walking distance to subway stations with multiple metro lines (E line at 8th/23rd St. takes you directly to JFK). Definitely a good base for NYC trips. It is a not a new hotel but 4 Points did a good job of maintaining the interior/decor updated. My room was definitely roomy (considering this is NYC and you will pay a premium for space) and nicely decorated with two twin-beds, work station, LCD tv and an OK bathroom. Couldn't be happier with the space. . Hotel does come with a nice bar and a restaurant with outdoor seating which I did not use as NYC is filled with great eateries in every neighborhood so it's best to explore the dining options outside. Internet as mentioned, is included in the rate but there are two free computer downstairs in the lobby for guest use if you don't have a laptop.
Many reviews here complained about the front desk staff and service but I did not encounter such problem during my entire stay. In fact, I considered them pretty ok, I guess it all depends on who you ran into. Maid service, on the other hand, could have been a bit better but it did not bother me too much.
In all, this is an above average hotel from the amenities point of view. However for the room space you get - if you find a good rate, I must say this hotel provides some very good value. I have stayed in a number of other NYC hotels with smaller rooms, older facilities, mediocre service and significantly higher price before, all I can say is this 4 Point Sheraton certainly beats all of them. I would definitely return in the future, if I can find a special rate again.

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “Great Value!!”
text: The hotel has a great location and everything you need available. We arrived at ten in the morning and they allowed us to park early. It was a great value, we will definitely return again!

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Roosevelt March April”
text:
New York rockt ! -- Wie Berlin !
zur Info: 6 Nächte 2 Personen in einem kleinen Zimmer (Kingsize Bett) 860 EUR (April 2009)
Der Drucker im 24h Web-Room hat die TCP/IP Adresse 192.168.1.6 und lässt sich per lpd direkt ansprechen.

name: Washington Jefferson Hotel
title: “Great location, great value.”
text:
This was my 12th visit to NYC and the first time staying at the WJ Hotel. Great location, easy walk to Central Park, Times Square, Broadway Theatres and just around the corner from the closest subway. 
Love the free Timeout magazine - nice touch. I specifically look for hotels that supply free wi-fi (I think it's absolutely compulsory) and the WJ does just that.
The staff on reception are fabulous. Really helpful and super friendly.
Now, the room ... OK, so I've stayed in some small hotel rooms and this was by far the smallest room ever! But, when you're in NYC you don't spend time in your hotel room until you're too exhausted to move anyway. But, be warned fellow travellers, if you like a bit of floor space or you're into swinging cats, this is not the place for you. I, however repositioned some of the furniture and made it work.
The bathroom was super small and I ended up leaving the door open to give the room a feeling of a little more space! But considering the price I paid for the room, this wasn't really too much of a hassle. 
The bed was pretty hard and the pillows flat but it was ok.
The room was kept reasonably clean, although a freshen up of the carpet would be most welcome! I also had a problem turning off the heating. On my first night, despite it being freezing outside, my room was like a sauna. The next morning, reception promptly sent up a maintenance man and he turned the heating off for me. It stayed off for the 10 days of my stay and was fine. 
Despite the teeny tiny living quarters and the bed being right next to the door (and I mean right next to the door), this hotel was great value for money. 
I thought it was such good value, I've just booked my return visit.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Great hotel for a great price”
text: My partner and I have stayed in New York 3 times now, 2 of which were at the Edison. On the other occasion I stayed in a 5 star hotel that had nothing on this excellent establishment. The location is fabulous, the rooms are clean and on one occasion we arrived at 9am and they let us check in then for no extra charge. I cannot recommend this hotel highly enough, when we return in a few months we will definately be staying there again.

name: Hudson New York
title: “For a young, hip crowd”
text:
I recently stayed at the Hudson Hotel on business. I was surprised that we had a business meeting there. There are some meeting rooms on the lower level. 
When I first entered the hotel (at 2 pm), there was disco music playing loudly and the feel was much more of a club than a hotel. I thought I must be in the wrong place! The staff were all very courteous and helpful. I had an upper level room, which I would recommend if you are interested in sleeping. Others in my group were on the lower 4 floors and could hear the club music all night. 
The rooms were well-equipped, but tiny. I felt like I was on a cruise ship. Paneled walls on either side of a double bed, which was actually like a futon rather than a standard boxspring/mattress combination. There was a tiny desk, which I could not even sit at with my laptop. 
I actually doubled over with laughter upon first seeing the bathroom- everything was miniaturized! The tub was approx 2/3 of a normal tub size with a clear window that was open to the room. This could be a problem if you are sharing a room with a colleague or friend. There was a pedestal sink, toilet and a shelf or two, squeezed into approx 3 feet of space. I am a small person, so was able to navigate fine. However, I was glad my 6'2" husband wasn't with me- his knees surely would have hit the wall if sitting on the toilet.
All in all, I really enjoyed my stay. Great ambience downstairs, quite a club scene. Easy walking distance to many things I was interested in seeing. 
However, this is more of an "experience" than a hotel. I would not take young children to this place, and honestly if on business would stay elsewhere. The desk was just not practical for working on a laptop, and the bed wasn't comfortable enough to sit and work there very easily. 
If you are with a young, hip group of people, this may be the place for you! But it is really not practical to share these tiny rooms with others in your group if you care about privacy or personal space at all.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan Chelsea
title: “Adequate hotel in a great location”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for 5 nights over 4th of July. We used our Starwoods points, but checked the pricing, and it was very reasonable for NYC. Overall, we would stay here again if we wanted to be in Chelsea. 
The hotel is adequate by NYC standards. The room and bathroom were tiny (as expected), but had everything we needed. We were on the 16th floor, so it was fairly quiet, except for people opening & closing their room doors. The beds were very comfortable. The decor was a little worn - the bedskirts were stained (looked like mud splatters) and the shower floor was also a little yellowed. Free internet & free bottled water (2 per night, but you can always ask for more at the front desk) is great! Maid service was good, no complaints. Front desk was very friendly and efficient, never more than 1 person in line. 
The best part of the hotel is the location. Very convenient to subways, with lots of amenities nearby. We ate 3 different times at Eataly, Mario Batalli's upscale Italian food court/ grocery store - everything was simple but amazing. Also, if you like French macarons and pastries, you must try Maison du Macaron on 23rd -- amazing flavor selection. Starbucks just down the street. For the 4th of July fireworks, we were able to walk to the pier to see them, which was very convenient. If you don't feel like wandering out, the hotel restaurant has a great happy hour ($5 drinks) and decent Mexican food.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “nous etions 15 jours dans l,hotel wellington 1.9.12 au 15.9.12”
text: Je reviens de cet hotel wellington avec ma petite fille, je ne comprends pas que des touristes ne sont jamais contents, voila, j,avais commande une chambre standard, et on m,a donne une petite suite, salon, cuisine salle de bains, et chambre , cela fut absolument genial, je pense, car l,hotel est propre, et les gens qui y travaillent toujours serviables, quant à la tapisserie que certains disent abime, je vous dirais que c,est les touristes qui avec un cutter ont taillade au passage, je l,ai vu , alors, toute cette petite suite etait tres propre, situee dans l,ancien batiment, la femme de menage toujours a renouveler tous les jours les draps, et la situation est tres favorable, en face bus, et a cote le metro ??? donc ?? nous avons vraiment apprecie l,hotel wellington , et c,est la verite, paule de montesquieu

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “la differenza tra vecchio e vintage”
text: Brutto albergo. Purtroppo non c'era altro a NY, durante la fashion week. Ho pagato tre volte quello che ho pagato a Las Vegas la settimana scorsa, in un albergo magnifico. La pirma camera che mi hanno dato era fumatori, ma in un modo pazzesco. Alle mie proteste si sono offerti di passare con lo spray deodorante...alla fine mi hanno dato una penthaouse, almeno sulla carta, ma perderebbe il confronto anche con un tre stelle italiano. Gli ascensori credo siano gli stessi di qualche decennio fa...statene lontano. La posizione però é buona...ma certamente non basta

name: Hudson New York
title: “Young, trendy and not pretentious”
text:
Just returned from a stay with my girlfriend and got to say this is the coolest and most relaxing hotel I have stayed in. 
OK the rooms are not that big, but they are functional and very cool and with New York outside the door who wants to spend much time indoors ?
The staff are very helpful and not in your face at all, however any requests and one small problem i had were dealt with immediately by the young professional staff, with no fuss and with a smile on their faces.
The bar is a great place to people watch, especially in early evening when the working day is finishing.
If you want impersonal, in your face, over the top attention from staff don't stay here, stay in a big chain hotel. If however you want to be treated as an individual by attentive friendly staff who remember your face from one day to the next then this is the place for you. I for one will definately be back.

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “A fantastic hotel, couldn't have been better.”
text:
Visited the hotel for a long weekend in Jan 2011. Room ready on arrival at approx 3pm. 
After reading reviews, I requested a room on a higher floor due to potential noise nuisance from the street and Fire Dept. I was given the option of floor 10 with a nice view or floor 16 with the view of a wall! Decided on the 10th floor room and was assured it wouldn't be too noisy. Throughout the stay, we could hear the Fire Dept sirens however they did not keep us awake at any point. Walls are thin and we could hear our neighbours on occasion however, this did not keep us awake at night either. 
The room itself (1004) has a nice view, as promised, and was not to far to walk from the lift (one of my grumbles in most hotels!). It was very clean and spacious enough for 2 people sharing. 1 king bed and a sofa. Plenty of drawer and desk space. Wardrobe was large enough however not many hangers available. Approx 10 which is not a lot for 2 people. Bathroom was small but again, not a problem. Sink was outside of the bathroom which was handy. 
Public areas are pleasant and clean. Staff always made an effort to greet you and were on hand if there was anything you required. The bar was closed a few times when we returned to the hotel but sure it opens 6pm daily. A beer and a spirit with mixer was approx $20. Slightly expensive but it's to be expected for a hotel on Lexington Ave. Bar food was very impressive and reasonably priced. 
We ate breakfast at the hotel on our last morning and it was very nice. Full menu available. We had the buffet for approx $23 each. For other breakfast alternatives there is Cafe Metro which is next door to hotel (cheap and cheerful) or I would highly recommend Raffles at the Raddison (left out of the hotel and a few blocks along).
The business centre was excellent. 60 mins free browsing. Printing of boarding cards was free. 
Wifi available for a charge in the room however, free in the lobby. Very reliable. 
Location is very good. Approx a 15 min walk to Times Sq. 
All in all, we were very pleased with our stay and could not fault the hotel. As we had stayed in NYC before, we were pleased to be slightly away from the hustle of Times Sq but close enough to the main attractions.

name: Sohotel
title: “Cute and affordable”
text:
Love the decore! We stayed for 9 nights and had a great time checkin out the city.
The location is great, bed was comfortable, rooms were small but we didn't mind As we were only sleeping there anyway, rooms cleaned daily.
Bad: tv reception was poor and no safe or phone in the rooms.
I would happily stay here again though.

name: Hudson New York
title: “Tiny,Expensive, but Ecclectic”
text: Stayed at the Hudson Hotel near Central Park West from for a few days after Christmas. It's entrance goes almost unnoticed since the facade is plain, but the overhead treelimbed foyer, and mysteriously lit hallways and lounge are for those that enjoy an ecclectic ambiance over classic New York City grande hotels. The rooms are clean, but are very tiny, plain, and not worth the steep rate. The bathrooms are barely bigger than the small closet. The hallways are painted a dingy cement color, and the dimly lit hallways added to the gloom. For the price I expected more, and if I just wanted to find a plain clean room with a good location then the Comfort Inn in Times Square would have fit the bill.

name: Econo Lodge Times Square
title: “Awesome!”
text: My daughter and I just got back and will stay here when we go back to NYC! Inexpensive (got it for $159 on the hotel website), near everything, friendly staff, free breakfast, free USA Today at your door in the morning, room service response in 2 minutes, nice hard water pressure in shower, free chips and water in the room.........I could go on. The hotel is about 2 blocks off the bright lights and bustle of Times Square, but it was actually a quiet little residential area without a lot of outside noise. Breakfast was great : coffee, juice, tea, cocoa, oatmeal, croissants, bagels with cream cheese or jellies, danishes, muffins, cereals -- lots to pick from. No, there are not tables to eat at, we just brought the stuff back up to our room. They give you discount coupons for a great restaurant around the corner on Restaurant Row when you check in. The bed was comfortable. Yes, the room is tiny, but my daughter and I walked around in it just fine. What are you doing in your hotel room anyway, cartwheels?? Subway is a couple of blocks up and there are tons of restaurants all around. 24-hr Pharmacy right next door, just in case. The only thing negative that happened to us was no hot water one morning. We went out and about and did a few touristy things, came back 2 hours later and it was all fixed. Plus, there are many reviews that mention a slow elevator - we did not think so at all. Clean, comfy, good area (felt totally safe walking at night), good price. Thanks Econolodge!!

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “Best NY hotel for the money!!”
text: I agree with the last review. This is the absolute best NY hotel for the money. The room was clean although outdated. There were not a lot of little amenities like the higher priced hotels but heck, I'll buy some with the money we saved. The location was fabulous and we easily walked to plays and Central Park. The room was big by NY standards and the kids even used the pool. We've stayed at a lot of much higher priced hotels in Ny but if you want good value and a comfortable place to stay, I'd highly recommend The Travel Inn, NY.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “POSIZIONE IMPAGABILE MA...”
text:
La posizione non ha prezzo, ma mi hanno dato una camera a dir poco vergognosa!! ricordo ancora la vasca da bagno sporca di mercuro cromo indelebile, ed un braccialetto di pelle sotto al mio letto che è rimasto li 7 giorni... e chissà da quanto era li..... camera vecchissima ed impolverata! ma ad altri miei amici è andata meglio, loro avevano una camera dignitosa..
p.s. non sono uno schizzinoso, ho fatto tanti anni nei boy scout a dormire nel sacco a pelo in un fosso... quindi non penso di essere eccessivo... sicuramente il peggior hotel della mia vita, ma ero troppo felice di essere a ny!! della camera non me ne fregava nulla!!!
nella descrizione ho scritto che ci sono stato a maggio 2011 in realtà sono stato a novembre 2010

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan Chelsea
title: “Hit or Miss...mostly miss”
text:
This hotel is hit or miss. I'm a SPG platinum member and I've stayed at this hotel dozens of times and the regular staff recognize me by face. There is no such thing as an "upgraded" room at this hotel cause all the rooms are basically the same. Some have old tube TV's and the newer/upgraded rooms have a flat panel. Other than that there is no difference in rooms. Many times I've checked in with a confirmed king bed reservation and all they have are double beds. As a platinum guest I should ALWAYS get my confirmed reservations regardless of capacity. I always request high floors because the windows aren't that well insulated. If you happen to get a non-street facing room, especially on a low floor, you will be bombarded by noise coming from a bar on 24th street. This bar has an outdoor back patio and the noise carries all the way to the top floor. If you happen to get a room next to an Ice Machine...then goodbye sleep. Another MISS are the pull down shades. While they look modern and trendy they don't block out any light. Good luck trying to sleep in. Once I did have a room with curtains and pull down shades and this was a slight improvement in blocking out the light. When I was there last they were upgrading/fixing the elevators. They did an upgrade to the elevators a few years earlier which resulted in a really bad wood stain on the panels and burlap type of material on the rest of the cab. Unfortunately the stain was very poor and the fabric material is worn and doesn't hold up to the daily wear and tear. Hopefully this has been fixed. 
Four Points provides free high speed internet, but there is no WiFi in the rooms so you have to be connected via ethernet cord. Years and years ago there used to be wifi, but they've disconnected that service. Now you do get free internet via ethernet, but I wouldn't call it High Speed. 
Now I don't want to be totally negative. The staff has always been friendly to me upon check-in since I'm a regular hotel guest. The location is a HIT, with close proximity to public transportation, MSG, and cool neighborhoods. The rooms are faily clean and they've "modernized" the bed linens to a more contemporary/clean look. This is a HUGE improvement over the previous bedding.
I booked another stay for early November and I will do another posting to see if things improved. It had such bad experiences during my last stays (double bed instead of king, low floor which was noisy, voicemail light that blinked constantly even though there was no voicemail, etc) that I've been staying at the W Times Square usually at rates only $50-75 more a night which is well worth it.

name: Dream New York
title: “Hotel design jouissant d'une excellente situation”
text: Cet hotel est très bien situé car il se trouve entre Central Park et Times Square. On a alors la possibilité de faire pas mal de choses à pieds. L'intérieur est magnifique et assez épuré. Le personnel est sympathique mais personne ne parle français. Par contre, les chambres sont petites pour le prix et assez bruyantes (prévoir des boule quies). Malgré tout, elles restent très agréable et possèdent : minibar, sèche cheveux, fer/table à repasser, peignoirs, radio/réveil d'excellente marque, écran plasma et j'en passe (La lumière bleutée au bas de la pièce est apaisante et la literie confortable). Ne vous étonner pas de la présence de videurs/physio à l'entrée, ils sont là pour le bar de l'hotel. On a aussi la possibilité de laisser ses bagages une fois l'heure du chek-out dépassé (très pratique pour se libérer de ses affaires en attendant le départ). N'allant pas souvent à l'hotel, c'est une question que je me posais, donc je préfère le préciser.

name: Dream New York
title: “camera pulita e posizione perfetta per lo shopping!”
text: Ho prenotato questo hotel tramite expedia ad una buona tariffa, la posizione è perfetta se vuoi girare a piedi (5-10 min.) la zona vicino Central Park, 5th Av., Times Square... la camera e il bagno erano pulitissimi, tutto ben accessoriato e con 2 finestre! Il personale è molto cortese: siamo stati davvero soddisfatti!

name: Park Central
title: “Horrible room, unfriendly staff”
text:
Our experience was also awful. The room was one of the oldest, dirtiest, I have ever stayed in. I was so thankful my 2 small children weren't traveling with us - if so, I would have checked out in an instant.
We too had a terrible time getting our room. When we were finally checked in at 5pm, we were checked into a smoky "non smoking" room without working electricity. We were moved but it was quite an ordeal.
With the exception of the bell staff, everyone else was rude and unhelpful. The concierage wouldn't help us get theater tix and wouldn't make a dinner reservation for us. No one ever smiled at us, it takes an eternity to get a live person on the phone at the front desk, the front staff even were yelling at guests. 
I have travelled all over the world for the past 30 yrs and this is one of, if not, the worst run hotels I have ever seen.
The only redeeming factor is location.
In response to the guest who had a nice room, there must be a small section of the hotel that was renovated. You were lucky.
I would never stay there again.

name: Hudson New York
title: “our floor and room reeked of room deodorizer”
text: After enjoying a wonderful courtyard lunch at the Hudson in the early fall, I decided to book an overnight stay for our anniversary. I decided that the smaller than average room size wouldn't matter, which in fact, it didn't. What was offensive, however, was the overwhelming smell of the air freshener that greeted us the minute we walked off the elevator on to our floor, and followed us all the way into our room (smelled like the pungent cherry deodorizer in the ladies room at Penn Station.) When I went to look out our window at the view, I noticed that we were a few floors above a giant vent fan that was loud and spewing a foul odor, hence the need for the equally foul room deodorizer. I would recommend the hotel for a casual lunch, drinking, relaxing and people watching in its many charming areas indoors and out, but I would caution against an overnight stay before first checking out the room location.

name: Hudson New York
title: “Cool Atmosphere, Small rooms- If you are over 5'5 Beware of the Bathroom!”
text: I think the Hudson is a fun hotel to go to if it is your first time in New York. The club downstairs is espcially interesting and the last time I stayed there they were filming sex in the city on the premises. On the flip side, the front desk is very snooty and disorganized, but hey, it's New York! And yes, the rooms are small. It wasn't so much as the small sleeping area I was uncomfortable with, it was the bathroom. If you are taller than 5'5 then be cautioned because it is going to be really hard for you to use the toilet with only about 5 inches to spare. This room kind of made me feel like I was on a cruise ship. So, overall, if this is your first time in NYC, and you want a really groovy young place to stay, the Hudson is for you. If you are more concerned with quiet, comfort and a decent bathroom then this is not your joint!

name: La Quinta Inn Manhattan
title: “Great for Hockey”
text: Had a wonderful six days end of September in NYC, a visit which was enhanced by the La Qunita Inn, being close to the ESB and the home of the Rangers. Although the elevators were sometimes semi-functional, this did not prevent us from enjoying the premises. Would definitely consider a further stay at the hotel when we visit again.

name: Hudson New York
title: “I loved it”
text:
After all of the poor reviews, I had read here, I was reluctant to stay at this hotel. But I Like it a lot: Great Location; Very Fashionable; the Restaurant was great; the Library very confortable. And a Winter Garden amazing!
My room was a superior and the size was good.

name: Park Central
title: “Not bad for New York Standards”
text:
A friend and I stayed at this hotel for 4 nights over a weekend. The lobby was nice and the front desk person was pleasant. We initially reserved a standard room with a king size bed. When we requested a city view, he advised that a standard room with 2 double beds with a city view is available. We were very happy with that because we would each have our own bed. Our room was a nice size. It looked cleaned. The bathroom was not too small and it was clean. However, we noticed that the drain plug for the bathtub was yanked out and left lying in the tub. We were hoping that housekeeping would notice it and do something about it. Nothing was done to it for our whole stay. It wasn't a big deal because the water drained just fine. 
When I had to call a friend who was staying in another hotel in New York, there was no phone book in the room and had to call front desk for the number. They said they did not have the number and would send a phone book up to us. The phonebook never arrived. As we prepared to go out that evening, we went to the front desk and there was a phone book right in front of them. I guess they were either too busy or lazy to look it up for me. 
Elevators are slow but we did not have to wait for an exhorbitant amount of time.
We paid approx $300 per night (taxes included). I would stay in this hotel again.

name: Herald Square Hotel
title: “Excellent location, everything else was so-so”
text: We stayed there for 7 nights - in 2 different rooms. Both rooms were noisy in the morning and you can hear people talking loudly and slamming doors. The second room we had was just next to the rooms where they were renovating which may explain the noise - not sure about the first room. The staff were mostly ok except for this grumpy lady in her 30s who was awfully unhelpful. They provide lockers at $2 per usage if you need to leave your bags at the hotel after check-out. The first room we had was very small but the second was slightly bigger and newer. The selling point for this hotel is its location at 31st & Broadway which is 2min walk from Macy's and 1min walk from the subway which is just 1 stop from Times Square. Me and my wife were there on Thanksgiving and we could catch the parade literally just around the corner. Yes, if you need a cab, get one off the street for one yourself, as the reception charges a ridiculous price. Room comes with free Wi-Fi internet access and LCD tv with HD channels.

name: Washington Jefferson Hotel
title: “Excellent location”
text: This was our first trip to New York, and after reading some of the negative reviews of the WJ hotel, we are very pleasantly surprised. It was spotlessly clean, the staff were polite and helpful and best of all was the location - it was very quiet (for New York) and very easy to walk to most of the tourist sites. It was also good value - around half the price of some hotels on Times Square. Can recommend breakfast at Georgio's Country Diner, just around the corner. It was excellent. We shall definitely use this hotel again the next time we are in NY....

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan Chelsea
title: “Comfortable hotel with super friendly staff, excellent restaurant and bar”
text: Very home-like feeling. Big smiles everywhere and the staff in the hotel and restaurant cannot can do enough for you. Rooms are standard but clean and comfortable.

name: Park Central
title: “Loathed Park Central”
text:
We stayed for 10 nights from the 10th November, 2005, in a room that was a dark as a tomb day and night. That we could cope with, but the toilet that wouldn't flush properly, and flooded the bathroom was a nightmare. It happened on our first night, and we told we were in a "low pressure" room. The sink would not empty either. It happened again on our final night - it took housekeeping till 4 am to clean the bathroom, and we had to fly to Vienna the next day! No sleep was possible, and the staff would not even consider a discount on our last night's stay.
The housekeeping staff never could count the towels, and routinely forgot that every bathroom needs a bathmat. Calls made using a phone card with 1800 numbers were charged at outrageous rates, despite the fact that the public phones in the lobby did not work. The lifts were also a problem - 10 minute waits for a lift down from the 14th floor were routine. We were told by a staff member that the hotel was being run by a group who really didn't care to spend any money on the hotel, and did not give a damn about the guests. 
We can well believe it, and would not stay there again if they paid us!

name: Park Central
title: “Disappointed”
text: Rooms were small, outdated, and bathrooms were dirty. Sheets were terrible, felt and sounded like we were sleeping on paper towels. Staff was okay, not overly accessible, did what they were suppose to do however never went the extra mile. One good thing . . . GREAT location for a reasonable price. Wouldn't stay there again, but would stay in the same area of town.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Great remodel job for right before flat panel TVs came out.”
text:
Park view tower room views are the best of 
NYC hotels, but rooms (especially bathrooms) are tiny even by NYC standards. Take some room design Inspiration from le meridian Philadelphia or others. Bar was great, lobby and other common areas: thumbs up. Good service - bell, door, getting cabs, etc.

name: Hudson New York
title: “Not worth the money”
text: So you pay an average of $200 per night for an art deco hotel which is nice to look at but certainly not worth the money. Yes alot of NY hotel rooms are small, but my god this was a closet with cheap furniture. Not recommended for anyone coming for outside of NY, you can certainly find better hotels for your money with bigger rooms and friendlier service

name: The Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Si vuelvo a New York, vuelvo a este hotel”
text: La atención del personal fue muy buena. Tienen personal que habla español. Como pasamos 8 noches, por cortesía del hotel, nos dieron una habitación mas grande. La ubicación es muy buena, esta muy cerca de la estación central y de Times Square. Las camas son comodísimas!!!!

name: Washington Jefferson Hotel
title: “Avoid at all cost”
text:
I booked to stay at this hotel for a week in November. When I arrived with my traveling companion, having specifically booked a room with separate beds, we were given a pitifully small closet of a room with one bed. When we asked to be put in an alternate room, we were advised that there were no vacant rooms available but as we were staying for a week, they were sure they could move us the following day. Unsurprisingly, this proved to be rubbish and did not happen. Furthermore, i was awoken during the first night by a concierge called London welcoming guests into their 'large twin bed room'. This served to rub salt into our wounds.
The room itself was cramped, very loud and extremely hot. The air conditioning didn't function and was bolted onto a half open and somewhat grubby window. The closet was so small we could not unpack into it and instead had to live out of our suitcases for the week. The staff were unhelpful and unsympathetic to the situation and their customer service was non-existant.
Having contacted Max Izmaylov, the 'Director of Sales' at the WJ Hotel, since my return, I have received no response whatsoever and given the lack of customer service WJ offers, I don't expect I will ever receive a reply. Do yourself a favor and don't stay here.

name: Econo Lodge Times Square
title: “Central and clean but mini”
text:
My partner and I did stay at the Econo Lodge for 2 seperate days in May.
We have been a little concerned because of the General Econo Lodge Brand reputation but the reviews have bees so good and we only needed to stay one night so we booked the Hotel. We did not regret it.
The Hotel is on 6 floors in a residential side street near Times Square.
It has only opened it's doors a few weeks ago so it is still new and clean.
I hope they can keep up the standard over time.
The rooms are small and even if you keep in mind that NYC Hotels are always a little smaller than average we still have to say that this was the smallest hotel room we ever had (so far). Breakfast is served in the lobby. There is no seperate Breakfast room but they have seating around and provide coffee, tea , pastry donuts and fruits.
We asked for a late check-out for 1 PM (Check-out time is 12pm) and the Hotel policy is to charge 25US for it. We decided to safe the money and vacate the room on time.
One of the drawbacks of this Hotel is that it has no luggage storage facility and since the Grand Central left-luggage has also been closed this can create a problem if you have a late flight or train out of the city. For a good rate we would stay at the Hotel again.

name: Washington Jefferson Hotel
title: “Fabulous, clean hotel with great staff!”
text:
The running theme in the reviews for this hotel are about the small rooms, and mine was no exception (only about 24 inches surrounding the twin bed on all 3 sides, and had to step OVER the toilet to enter and exit the shower!). However, I can't say there wasn't enough room for my luggage or toiletries, the small armoire provided plenty of room to hang my clothes, and there were lots of electrical outlets available to charge my cell, camera battery, MP3 player, etc.
The room was SPOTLESS, and the maid did an excellent job daily. The down comforter and pillows were comforting after long, tiring days sightseeing, and the sheets were always sparkling white and crisp.
The staff was super friendly...can't recall one instance where I passed by a staff member when I wasn't greeted with a smile and friendly "hello". They were super-quick with special requests and seemed genuinely happy to help with their knowledge of the city.
The view from the room was a dark, ugly airshaft, but I saw this as a plus because it kept out street noise which, along with the thick walls between rooms, made for a very quiet stay.
My only complaint about the WJ was that one day during my 4 night stay they turned off the water for maintenance with no notice and I was caught half-way through my shower with no water pressure. I see this as a minor inconvenience and isolated incident that would not keep me from staying at the WJ again.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Ideal location, pleasant staff, comfortable & lovely room”
text: Much larger room than I expected, very quiet. Easy to get everywhere I wanted to go: park, theatre, museums. Staff was courteous and helpful. Cute touch with classic cartoons playing in the elevators.

name: Herald Square Hotel
title: “Wonderful and cheap!”
text: Stayed here for 8 nights over New Year's 2008/09 and couldn't have been more impressed. Staff were friendly and helpful, hotel has great amenities (guest laundry was very handy), the room was much bigger than we thought it would be, with a huge bathroom. Location is obviously a drawcard, but the room was a quiet oasis in the heart of the city. Compared with other hotels in NYC in this price range, the Herald Square is exceptional. Highly recommended!

name: Washington Jefferson Hotel
title: “Loved it”
text:
Was supposed to stay here with my bf for one night, but we actually stayed two extra nights, and we would definitively go back.
The room was not very big, but that didn't bother us. It was clean, the staff was nice and made the hotel feel exclusive. 
Great location too! Close to everything, Central Park, Empire State, Fith Ave.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan Chelsea
title: “Would not stay at this hotel again”
text:
While adequate and not a disaster by any means, this isn’t a hotel I would select for a future stay in Manhattan, simply because far nicer hotels can be had for a lower price in superior locations. Even if using priceline, this hotel isn’t a bargain by any means. If I had to sum up the feel of this hotel in one word it would be “claustrophobic.”
Location:
This hotel is on a very dead side street on the border of what is supposedly Chelsea. It’s a few blocks to the subway station, but it is desolate at night and quite uncomfortable to walk some of those blocks. There is nothing happening around the hotel at night and very little in the daytime. On the plus side, this means it’s a quiet hotel which may suit some people. 
Lobby, rooms and beds:
The tiny lobby in this hotel leads to immediate feelings of claustrophobia which are vastly magnified when more than five people stand in the space. The downstairs bar is also cramped. The rooms are very very small, even by NYC standards, and the tiny hallways leading to them are even more claustrophobic. Once a tray is placed outside a room, it is hard to walk around, as the hotel is so small that only a few rooms exist on each floor. Oddly, only parts of the rooms have been renovated in recent years, which means while you may be treated to a newer bed, or carpet, the furniture is bound to be of the dinged-up-cheapo-particle board variety from the 70s. This was really dismaying and gave the rooms a pretty awful aged look. Both the rooms we had were a definite mixture of old and new : Terribly old run-down duvet with many lint balls permanently attached across the surface, but relatively new sheets and mattress; Horrible marked up ancient (and ugly) furniture, but new carpet. Small ancient TVs (but at least they functioned, which is more than I can say about many a NYC hotel room). The windows in both rooms were so filthy, it was difficult to see out of the grime. On the plus side, the windows are some of the best in the city in terms of noise reduction ability. The dark décor in the rooms makes one feel even more imprisoned. 
Bathrooms:
Of our two rooms, both had full renovations in tiling and sink area, but only one had a renovated shower. This was quite a contrast, as the older shower was one of those ancient sliding glass door varieties where the door doesn’t quiet sit right. 
For those who like a bit of space around their sink area and can’t deal with mini-sinks made for tiny hotel rooms, be prepared. While I quite liked the new renovated sink area and adequate toiletries, I could easily see that anyone in need of space wouldn’t be able to handle these tiny bathrooms, especially the miniscule sink.
Temperature control:
Amazingly, they use ancient window units.
Staff: 
The desk folks were always very friendly and helpful. Housekeeping really did a great job cleaning the rooms (not so much clearing the hallways, which were always cluttered). However, the permanent aging and staining that already existed in the rooms made it hard to get past the “rundown” impression upon entering the room, even if it was cleaned well each day.
Internet:
There are free terminals and printers in a business center on the first floor, literally in the coffee bar/café area of the hotel. This is a great plus if you can get on one.

name: Washington Jefferson Hotel
title: “Super little hotel”
text: We spent five nights at the WJ and would stay there again in a heartbeat. Friendly staff, clean room, outstanding location, quiet yet close to everything.

name: Park Central
title: “Great Location”
text: Location was key, close to Central Park, 5th Ave. and Times Square. Rooms were average sized and clean. Staff was friendly, but front desk was very slow.

name: Hudson New York
title: “Claustrophobic Chic”
text: The hotel was very hip and the design of the lobby and bar outstanding (which was to be expected). The service was fine. But this was the smallest hotel room I have ever seen in my life and it was the standard room. As a frequent visitor to New York, I've stayed in some pretty tiny rooms, but this was almost funny. Basically, if you prefer chic to square footage, you might want to give it a try. If you actually prefer the ability to walk around the room (or even around the bed) without stumbling into something I'd look elsewhere.

name: The Alex Hotel
title: “Wir kommen wieder”
text: das hotel liegt in einer guten lage war sehr sauber und das personal ging auf fragen mit fundierten antworten ein. uns wurde fast alles ermöglicht und war das zimmer sehr sauber und isst man im restaurante sehr gut. wir kommen wieder ins alex, weil die lage top ist und wir sogar ein raucherzimmer bekommen haben weil wir eines wollten.

name: Sheraton New York Times Square Hotel
title: “Great location good value”
text: Good hotel very clean. Service was good all staff members were nice. Easy to get a cab out front and in time square it is almost impossible. Bathrooms in room are tiny but beds comfy and clean. Lounge is ample. A good place to stay with a great location

name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Fifth Ave
title: “Höchstens befriedigend..”
text:
Auch wenn man NY viel nachhält, würde ich dort nicht noch einmal übernachten. 
NY-Marathon(6.11.11) ist Hauptsaison und 350 € pro Nacht für Verlängerungstage sind deutlich zuviel. Zimmergröße mal gerade 80 cm zum bewegen um das Queensize Bett herum passen einfach nicht mit dem Preis zusammen. 
Ausstattung, Service und Sauberkeit sowie die Lage sind gut.
Akkustisch schlecht scheinen Zimmer nach vorne zu sein.
Straßenlärm sowie die sich auf der anderen Strassenseite befindlichen Klimaanlagen reduzieren die nächtlichen Schlafstunden auf ein nötiges Minimum.
Und ich bin da kein empfindlicher Mensch. Bei Gewitter schlafe ich immer durch.
Zu einem anderen Preis vielleicht zu empfehlen...

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Great location, clean hotel, small rooms”
text: Very clean hotel with a great staff. Norma's is a very good hotel restaurant and you just can't beat the Burger Joint behind the velvet curtain.

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “Highly recommended”
text: I got a double double rooom for a good price (207 with tax). The room was clean, decent. The staff was helpful. The awesome features are the free parking (one spot per room) and the walkable access to Times Square. It was a decent place and excellent location for the price.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Excellent experience!”
text: We stayed at the Millennium Broadway for 4 nights - Aug 28-31, 2009. We booked through Travelzoo and paid a total of $743, including taxes. Before arrival I was somewhat apprehensive since the price/location equation seemed too good. But everything worked out fine. Good sized room, king-sized bed, flat screen TV, in-room safe, quiet (30th floor), efficient elevators, friendly staff, efficient check-in & check-out. The only quibble would be the bedspread - a bit thin - but then again the AC worked very well. Plus, a great location a few steps from 7th Avenue, between 44th and 45th Streets. Very good value.

name: Washington Jefferson Hotel
title: “Washington Jefferson”
text:
Das Hotel liegt in einer Nebenstraße nur 2 Blocks vom Broadway und Times Square entfernt.
Wir hatten ein Standard-Zimmer gebucht mit Anfrage auf 2 getrennte Betten was wir auch bekommen haben. Da wir ziemlich früh angereist sind war unser Zimmer noch nicht fertig wir konnten aber die Koffer kostenlos unterstellen und uns New York ansehen.
Das Personal war durchgehend sehr freundlich. In der selben Seitenstraße befinden sich kleine, feine Restaurant deren Preise für New York angemessen sind.
Das Preisleistungsverhältnis könnte deutlich besser sein, die Standard-Zimmer sind sehr sehr klein sodass man Schwierigkeiten hat sich im Zimmer zu bewegen. Unser Zimmer lag in den Hinterhof hinaus, der Ausblick ist nicht gerade schön dafür war es sehr ruhig. Einzig die Klimanlage ist sehr sehr laut und lässt sich obwohl selbstregulierbar nicht leiser stellen.
Das Bad war ebenso sehr klein, es gibt keine Ablagefläche, zu zweit im Bad zu stehen ist nicht möglich. Es gibt nur einen kleinen Schrank der aber nicht einmal für eine Person ausreicht.
Natürlich ist man wenn man New York besichtigt sehr wenig auf dem Zimmer aber für den Preis den wir bezahlt haben haben wir uns doch etwas mehr Komfort erwartet.
Das Zimmer wurde aber jeden Tag absolut sauber gereinigt - da gibts nichts zu beanstanden.
Der Flughafenshuttle, der vom Hotel organisiert wird ist auch sehr gut und unsere Koffer konnten wir auch wieder kostenlos im Hotel lassen bis zu unserem Abflug.
Alles in allem ein kleines nettes 3 Sterne-Hotel mitten im Zentrum, mit kleinen Zimmern und etwas überteuertem Preis-Leistungsverhältnis.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Praktisch und angenehm”
text: Etwas skeptisch kamen wir beim Hotel an, das von außen wenig Eindruck macht. Valet-Parking und Einchecken funktionierten zügig, problemlos und sehr feundlich. Unser Wunsch nach zwei Zimmern mit jeweils zwei Betten war perfekt berücksichtigt worden. Die Zimmer im 15. Stock sind nicht groß. Aber anders als in anderen Großstadthotels in den USA konnten wir immerhin die Koffer abstellen und öffnen. Die Badezimmer sind ein wenig verbraucht und könnten ein "Update" gebrauchen. Alles war aber sauber. Das Hotel liegt sehr zentral. Vieles lässt sich zu Fuß erreichen. Auch die U-Bahn ist quasi vor der Tür. Gelegenheiten für Frühstück usw. gibt es in der Nachbarschaft mehr als genug . Der Preis dafür ist, dass die Zimmer nicht gerade ruhig sind. Klimaanlagen und Straßengeräusche produzieren eine gewisse Lärmkulisse. Aber dafür ist man mitten in Manhattan!

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan Chelsea
title: “Best Staff in New York - Hands Down”
text: I travel weekly - all ove the country. The staff at this small, hip Chelsea hotel is absolutely unbeatable! The Front Desk staff is always "on", although they do many things at the same time, they never skip a beat. The service is not cookie-cutter but personable, warm & always friendly. If you ask where to go to eat, they will whip out 50 suggestions on the fly. The rooms are hip with the most comforatable beds in New York. They have a winner here!

name: Hotel Gansevoort
title: “Great Location”
text: My husband and I enjoyed our stay. We had a nice room with great view. We felt a little too old to be staying here (53), but only because we weren't able to stay out partying past 2, when neighborhood was still quite lively. The rooms are modern and bathrooms great! We didn't really notice noise problems we saw others complain about. I did use spa and that was a little strange where was set up in the basement (small curtained room), but the treatment was excellent.

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “Good Hotel”
text:
Me and my boyfriend stayed in this hotel from Dec 31st to Jan 6th, We originally only booked for three nights for over New Year, but because of the great location and price online at Opodo we extended our stay here.
I would say that the whole hotel seemed nice, everything in our room was clean, the carpets werent worn and the bathroom area was in perfect condition. We had no problem what so ever with the lifts being slow at any time of the day. Staff were very helpful from checking in/out to giving information and directions on places we wanted to go. At the end of our stay we had a bill for the minibar for three items, when we had not even opened the fridge nevermind take things off the ultra-sensitive shelf, but the staff removed them off the bill without any fuss. Our room was also facing the fire and police station, but I think we only noticed the sirens maybe three times in our stay, no problem at all.
When we extended our stay we changed rooms, we were allowed to stay in our room past check out time until the next room was ready which was before 3pm, and we were upgraded to and king size room for free which was just that bit bigger then the queen but it made a lot of difference, as the queen was ok, but a bit small with the suitcases in.
I would say the one downside to our stay was being next to nosiy guests in the 1st room which was next to some very noisy teenagers who had no respect at all for the other guests, twice security was called to quieten them down, i personally think they should have been thrown out the 2nd time as they would come in around 4-5am shouting screaming down the corridors and in their room. It would seem the walls were a bit too thin.
As i said, great location, only a walk away from times square, 5th avu etc, or just as easily get the subway as the station was right next door and you can get a day pass for only $7! bargain! We ate at Pax for breakfast which is just around the corner as they had breakfast specials which were cheap enough and good quality, but also try Ess a Bagel and Metro cafe next door for the sandwiches and salads.
Overall, a good hotel in which i would stay again!

name: Holiday Inn New York City - Wall Street
title: “ICK!”
text: Sheets were not changed after 5 nights so I removed and informed front desk, twice. Hotel policy states they are only required to change after 3 nights - and this goes for most hotels. This begs the question-were they changed before I checked in? Furniture was not wiped down (tea rings evident on night stand after a week's stay). Hotel chosen because of convenient Wall Street location; however because of multiple construction projects, it was noisy. Aside from the cleanliness issue, this property is a good value.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Best location”
text:
Can't beat this for location. Just a few steps from Times Sq and Broadway. All
major sights mor-or-less within walking distance.
Hotel is pretty average. We asked for and got a decent room with corner view (on
32nd floor). Bahroom had the smallest bath I've ever seen but the shower facilities are fine.
Not luxurious but more than adequate for a sightseeing trip to the Big Apple.
Overall it is worth the trade-offs to get this location but make sue you upgrade to a deluxe room a the basic rooms are supposed to be minute.

name: Park Central
title: “Pessima struttura ma centrale”
text: Eravamo in tour e questo è stato il nostro ultimo albergo. Rispetto agli altri, molto puliti e confortevoli,il Park Central è stato in assoluto il peggiore: sporco è dire poco, tende macchiate di muffa, polvere in ogni angolo, moquette che aveva visto giorni mogliori...inoltre lampadine fulminate, bagno mal funzionante sempre avvolto dalla condensa ed antiquato, spazi ristretti. In compenso la posizione è strategica e quasi fa dimenticare la pessima e trascurata struttura alberghiera. Nota positiva: il personale parlava italiano e veloce nell'effettuare prenotazioni.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “fantastic hotel”
text: stayed here for our 25th wedding anniversary and the hotel was fantastic brilliant location staff are wonderful and we emailed them prior to trip and when we got there they upgraded us and sent champagne and chocs to our room could not fault this hotel at all the rooms were realy clean and comfortable

name: Sohotel
title: “Hotelzinho Fofo!”
text: O Sohotel é fofo, aconchegante, pertinho de tudo, e é no SOHO! Já basta...

name: Hilton New York
title: “The reviews are accurate”
text:
The NY Hilton rates were the highest rate I've ever paid for a hotel room. Was it worth it? Yes and no. As a child, I lived down the street from the hotel and it was part of my daily scenery. I therefore, attained a special satisfaction, staying there.
The room was spacious and clean, with all the fixings one would expect from Hilton. Checking in and out was quick. The personnel were pleasant enough. The location is perfect, close to Central Park, Times Square and the subway. I liked that we weren't IN Times Square where traffic is so often at a stand still. I liked that there was a curved driveway, where we could exit/enter a cab with out feeling rushed. 
For $400+ a night free WiFi and breakfast would have been nice.
Would I stay here again? Probably not.
Do I regret having stayed here? No, not at all. I read multiple reviews and was aware of the pros and cons and it was exactly as advertised and reviewed.

name: Park Central
title: “Sentralt beliggende”
text: Hotellet anbefales for ukestur til Manhatten.Kort avstand til alle severdigheter på Manhatten.Two blocks til Central Park.Rommet var tilfredstillende for oss to som ikke krever luksus.Kort veg til coffeshop,breakfast/lunch steder. Kjøpte fortreffelig middagsrett i matbutikken på 57th street som vi tok med på rommet en travel turistdag.Undergrunnsstasjon ved sideutgangen av hotellet.Kjøp ukesbilett på automat ,gjelder både på buss og bane.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Terrible”
text:
I CANNOT recommend this hotel and would suggest that you stay elsewhere. 
There were numerous problems- heat not working, phone not working, multiple phone calls to get a simple item, noise. When I complained to management, the response was rather cold with an unwillingness to take responsibility or to provide adequate amends. I even took the time to speak with the general manager, but he refused to be helpful and was not interested in knowing what the issues were and was hostile. Clearly quality and customer service are not important to this hotel’s management.

name: Washington Jefferson Hotel
title: “sehr empfehlenswertes Hotel”
text:
- sehr günstig gelegenes Hotel, Central Park, Times Square sowie Subway in unmittelbarer Umgebung und fußläufig in wenigen Minuten erreichbar
- freundliches Personal
- Zimmer zwar klein, aber zweckmäßig eingerichtet
- kein Frühstück, in der Nähe aber mehrere Cafes zum Essen (für Selbstversorger: nahes Lebensmittelgeschäft 24h offen)
- leider keine Möglichkeit im Zimmer, Wasser für z.B. Tee oder Kaffee zu kochen
