- am Tag der Abreise wurde vom Hotelpersonal ein Shuttle zum Flughafen organisiert, sehr angenehm, sich darum nicht selbst kümmern zu müssen
- insgesamt ein empfehlenswertes Hotel für eine Städtereise nach NY; ich würde es jederzeit wieder buchen

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Great location, beautiful hotel”
text:
This hotel is great. Awesome location, close to times square, Central park and amazing shopping. The rooms are very nice, comfortable. My only suggestion is ask for a high floor, if you are on a low floor you hear a lot of street noise.
Nice gym, and pool on the top floor.

name: Washington Jefferson Hotel
title: “Washington Jefferson Hotel”
text: Små fine værelser med gode senge og gode badeværelser. Fin rengøring. Hjælpsomt personale. Perfekt beliggenhed. To gader fra Broadway. Den næste investering hotellet bør gå i gang med er bredere garderobe forhold og måske noget hurtigere trådløst. Ialt havde vi 6 rigtig gode dage i New York

name: Washington Jefferson Hotel
title: “Washington Jefferson Hotel NYC”
text: Je recommande vivement cet établissement, situé sur la 51th West à 2 rues de Broadway, évitant l'effervescence permanente de la rue. Tout est à proximité. Hôtel agréable, bien tenu, confortable et cosy. Réceptionnistes et grooms très sympathiques. De bons conseils. Y retournerai avec plaisir !

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Rimelig hotell med fantastisk beliggenhet!”
text: Hadde ikke de største forventningene etter å ha bestilt ett 3 stjerners hotell rimelig, midt i smørøyet på manhattan. Men, ble positivt overrasket. Hotellet er koselig, men ikke forvent luksus. Rommene er små men duger til å sove og slappe av på. Det flotte med hotellet er beliggenheten. Noen få kvartaler unna times square, rett ved Central park og shoppingmekkaet 5th avenue. Det at subwayen lå rett ved hotellinngangen var også et stort pluss.

name: Sheraton New York Times Square Hotel
title: “Would never go back”
text:
Stayed here last summer for a long weekend with my husband, and had an awful experience at this property. My first impression upon arrival at the hotel was that it was crowded, too busy, and loud. The sheer volume of people and disorganization of the lobby area was fairly hectic. Long waits for the elevators, long waits for the front desk. As we discovered, the noise is not exclusive to the lobby ares - on our last night at the hotel, the couple in the room beside us came in rather late and proceeded to scream at each other for the next hour or so. I called security three times indicating that the noise was a problem (you could hear every word), and each time they said they would come to address the issue, but after an hour, they still had not. I called down a fourth time and threatened to take further action if security would not address the issue - and only then did they ask the couple to please be quiet. It was extremely unpleasant, and the 1+ hour it took to resolve the issue was not exactly customer service at its finest. 
While that experience created negative feelings about the hotel, the location is great, and the rooms were a decent size (especially by NYC standards), but overall, I would never return to this hotel.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Wonderful hotel in the heart of New York.”
text:
We stayed at the Millennium Broadway for a week on our honeymoon and had a fabulous time!
Right on Times Square, we could not have asked for a better location from which to explore the city. The room was huge - with the biggest bed I have ever seen! And whilst not recently decorated it was very clean and we could actually see Times Square from our window!
The room had very good air conditioning - it was very hot when we were there - and as we stayed for a week (longer than average apparently) we were given a fridge which was ideal for keeping drinks and bottled water cool.
From here we were able to walk to the Empire States building, central park and get the tube to anywhere on and off Manhatten Island. 
We would go back to New York and stay here again - a fabulous place to stay!

name: Park Central
title: “Uma boa opção em NY”
text: Extremamente limpo e confortável. Quarto com ótimo tamanho, o que é raro em NYC. A localização é muito boa também, perto de tudo! Tem metro, Starbucks e outros restaurantes que ficam abertos até tarde perto.Os funcionários são muito atenciosos e acessíveis, com destaque para a Guest relation Elizabeth, tenho certeza que ela irá te ajudar em qualquer coisa que precisar. O Hotel cumpre o que promete, é uma excelente opção de estadia.

name: Park Central
title: “Manifestazione in albergo”
text: Ho soggiornato in quest'albergo per tre giorni; devo dire che la posizione non è niente male perchè si trova a pochi isolati da alcuni dei più bei posti di New York (Central Park e Times Square). Le stanze sono nella media; la pulizia non è il massimo. La cosa che più mi ha colpito è che durante il mio secondo giorno di soggiorno (mentre ero in visita alle Cascate del Niagara) alcuni ospiti dell'albergo avevano protestato allestendo una vera e propria piccola manifestazione per lamentare la sporicizia e soprattutto la presenza di pidocchi in alcune stanze.... La sera l'albergo era un subbuglio, personale di quà e di là... Per quanto sia indispensabile mantenere la lucidità e l'obiettività, devo dire che da quale momento in poi non vedevo l'ora di andar via. Ci sono comunque altri vicini e più rinomati alberghi!

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Hotel Pennsilvania : vieux, sale, personnel incompétent, à éviter”
text:
Idéalement situé, mais a besoin d'être entièrement réhabiliter.
- les cafards sont présents dans les salles de bains et les cages d'ascenseur.
- les barres de douche rouillées menacent de tomber
- les prises électrique pendent des murs.
- les peintures croutent avec l'humidité
- isolation inexistante.
- 1h30 d'attente pour obtenir notre chambre
- le point info présent, mais personnel incompétent.
A ne surtout pas recommander.

name: Tribeca Grand Hotel
title: “Grand by name, grand by nature...”
text:
As a journalist who travels the world on various city-break features, I can whole-heartedly say that New York's Tribeca Grand is one of my favourite hotels in the US. 
A sister venue to the stunning Soho Grand, TG effortlessly embodies the style, vibrancy and allure of the city itself.
Cool and savvy without being oppressive, it possesses some of the best service in Manhattan - and some of the best looking!
Don't bother staying anywhere else.

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “A bargain but you get what you pay for!”
text:
My girlfriends first trip to New York and what a way to start. The room stank our best description was it was a combination of smoke and of urine. Maybe smoke isn't so bad but why give the choice of a smoking or non smoking room? Anyway by the time we had been directed to our 3rd "non-smoking" room (which was also stinking of smoke but less of urine) we decided that we weren't going to get any better here.
We put up with this hotel and still had a great time in New York. The location of the hotel is first class and in a reasonably safe area. It isn't exactly a quiet hotel but it is NYC after all. The staff were fine and friendly as long as you didn't ask anything of them. The room was cheap but adding in the cost of cleaning all clothes afterwards that adopted the stench and the 2 cans of Febreeze we used and we'll be staying somewhere else next time. You have been warned!

name: Sheraton New York Times Square Hotel
title: “Train-station type of hotel, 4star service”
text:
Good room – spacious, clean. Good view from 50th floor.
Healthy breakfast in club lounge – limited but healthy choice - they have eggs, juices, porridge, some fruits (banana, apples), cereal, tea and coffee
Service - suffers... I left an item for overnight laundry, and at 7am it was not in my room as promised the night before. At 7.10, I just wanted to find out what’s happening, and during the next 20 minutes I tried to speak to reception, concierge, operator, laundry...everyone was happy to transfer me to someone else. No one knew where the shirt was, and no one wanted to deal with this ‘search’. It exposed a total chaos in this hotel.
When I told the next day not to charge $18 for this service, the receptionist deleted it at once even without understanding what happened... such things probably occur there on a daily basis.
Overall feel in this hotel is that it’s so large that it’s difficult to provide a truly good service. One certainly does not feel any luxury here.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Great Midtown Location...clean and comfortable”
text:
Travelling with two adults and two teenagers while visiting local art schools. Stayed 3 nights in an upgraded suite and a double on the same high floor. A/C worked well during 90 plus degree weather, and rooms were clean and beds were comfortable. Thankfully No Bugs, although a nearby theater was closed during our visit due to those nasty bed bugs...front page of Daily News had a huge article on NYC bedbug outbreak during our stay so we were thankful we stayed at the Parker. 
Double facing Central Park had a great view. Old school big tube TVs and NO FREE WIRELESS INTERNET access were a big disappointment for everyone...(c'mon management, it's a new millenium...I Pads and HD flat screens should be standard everywhere by now in a hotel of this class)...but otherwise rooms were typical size and layout for NYC. 
ENCLOSED ROOF TOP POOL was open (although stifling in the heat and humidity) and kids didn't want to use it, but we loved having access to the outdoor roof...views are good, there's lots of rubble and some areas are closed off and in disrepair, but still a nice perk for midtown--but they close the rooftop access early so you can't sneak up to take in the nighttime views.
All in all, we enjoyed our stay and weren't bothered at all by the press and Jonas Brothers/Camp Rock folks holding interviews while we were there...but for the herd of black Denali Limos parked out front, you'd never know any teen idols were in the hotel...someone was doing a GREAT JOB there...
I like this hotel, and I hope management continues to repair and improve this property so it will be here when my children come to visit with their families.
Prices are comparable to nearby higher end properties...so it's still worth the price of admission to stay at the Parker.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Wonderful”
text:
Booked a last minute trip over the phone for a saturday night. I mentioned that I was bringing two dogs as I found out they were pet friendly. So the reservation was complete and I went ahead and paid the "pay now and save" option. We checked in and somehow got an upgrade to a Junior Suite from Deluxe room...very nice. Since I already told them about my dogs, I wsn't aware that I had to register my dogs. Our suite was nice and had the right plan/idea. workmanship/craftsmanship was just a little weak.
Went out for dinner, but had to cut it short...got a call from the hotel saying that my dogs were barking like crazy (oops!) Ran back to the hotel to find out that the security guy was at the door and he was pissed...made it sound like we snuck the dogs in. BTW, my dogs were right next to me as we were checking in. 
Anywho, I went to the front desk and "registered" my dogs. $50 per pet is very affordable. What annoyed me was the fact that one of the front desk (female) employees whispered loudly to the gentleman who was helpling me "...I can't believe they did this, it's $50 per pet, and that's a hundred dollars". But I wasn't going to open my mouth and start anything since we were at fault :-) besides I was tired and already had a few drinks and didn't need any hoopla. I just stood there pretended that I didn't hear anything. Then the gentleman very politely gave me the paperwork and nicely asked me to not leave the dogs in the rooms by themselves. Done.
Check out was a breeze. Somehow someone ordered breakfast and put it on our tab...they took care of the error immediately.
I like the 12:00 PM checkout. 
I would definitely stay here again, but I first need to try out the other pet friendly places... Hotel Penn, Marriott Marquis, 70 Park Avenue etc etc.

name: Park Central
title: “Gute Lage”
text:
Die Lage des Hotels ist ausgesprochen gut, gelegen zwischen Central Park einerseits und Times Square auf der anderen Seite.
Zu beiden Punkten kann man zu Fuß sehr schnell - innerhalb von 15 Minuten, gelangen. 
Eine besondere Notiz ist angebracht für die sehr gute Unterstützung in einem Problemfall mit der Fluggeselschaft, durch die Mitarbeiterin in der Rezeption mit dem Namen Ellen. Zuvor kontaktierte andere Mitarbeiter waren der Situation im Vergleich dazu nicht besonders gut gewachsen.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Hôtel Wellington New York”
text:
La qualité principale de cet hôtel reste sa situation, l'hôtel en lui même est viellot, la propreté sommaire, le confort juste suffisant et selon les chambres la vue nulle (du 5ème étage on ne voit pas le ciel et en face la façade de l'immeuble en u).
Wifi payant.

name: Holiday Inn New York City - Wall Street
title: “très bien placé et confortable”
text:
Je n'ai rien à redire sur la chambre: petite mais de bonne tenue.
Attention avec la notion de "petit dejeuner inclus", qu'il m'a fallu réglé! C'est la seule ombre au tableau.
Accueil sympathique, et climatisation efficace. En face de l'hôtel vous trouverez la réserve fédérale, inutile de préciser que ce quartier est bien protégé! 
Pour l'hygiène, le niveau est correct - la salle de bain est propre, et l'hôtel propose de contribuer à l'effort environnemental... ce n'est pas si courant aux USA.

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “Good Deal for Manhattan”
text:
We stayed at the Travel Inn June 8th and 9th. The big plusses about this hotel are the free parking and the pool. We arrived in NYC for the two hottest days of the year so far, so the pool was a godsend – really! The location is great – walk to Time Square and Empire State building, and if using the Grayline Tours, a short walk to Grayline location. 
We reserved two double\doubles – one for my husband and I and one for my sister-in-law and two daughters. We requested non-smoking rooms because my 8 year old daughter has asthma and lingering cigarette smoke can be a trigger. The last thing we wanted to do was end up in an emergency room in NYC.
Both rooms were comfortable, but the bathrooms a bit small. One of the rooms reeked heavily of cigarette smoke (the other room was fine). We went to the front desk to ask for a non-smoking room. They explained to us that they didn’t have “Non-Smoking” rooms, but the maids “spray” something to get the smell out. We all know there is no such spray! On the way to our rooms, we noticed that some rooms had “Non-Smoking Room” signs on them….hmmmm. Anyway, my daughter stayed in the non-stinky room while my husband and I stayed in the stinky room. A little unpleasant, but not intolerable. If you have allergies or asthma and cigarette smoke is a trigger – this may not be the hotel for you. 
Noise-wise, there were some loud guests sitting out on balcony all hours of the night throughout our 2 night stay. I wore earplugs and slept well, but my husband was a little annoyed. I suppose we could have called the front desk - but we figured that it was New York and noise was part of the package.
Aside for the stinky room issue, the location, friendly staff, pool, and parking make the Travel Inn a good value.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Edison Hotel, NYC - Perfect stay”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Edison Hotel on Thanksgiving weekend (from England). After reading the reviews on Trip Advisor we were a little apprehensive before our trip. However, we had a fantastic stay at the Edison. Our room was on the 14th floor and it was quite large with a handy hallway and closet (great for storing shopping bags). The bathroom was quite small (as i imagine most are) but was clean and looked new. Considering the hotel is in Times Square, it wasn't noisy at night. (just the odd siren and horn honking which is usual). Would have liked a better view, but you cant have everything!! The lobby was nice with a nice seating area and the Piano bar was how you would imagine an authentic american bar. We only popped in there once for a quick drink, but had we had more time we would have probably gone again. Sofias italian restaurant adjoins the back of the hotel, again, we didnt have chance to go in, but it looked really nice and busy. We sampled the Edison cafe one morning, not overly keen on the breakfasts. We discovered Dannys (just a couple doors away from front of hotel) which does the most amazing all day cuisine. They have a breakfast run, then it all changes for lunch and then dinner. Lovely full breakfasts, or fresh fruit, bagels, just everything. We were gutted we had only discovered it on the last day and we had walked past it about 50 times!!. As for the location of the hotel WOW!!! Walk to the end of the street and you are in Times Square. Walk out the back entrance and you are in Times Square. Just fab!! So convenient after a day out to drop bags off, and go out again. Also,in the evenings, you could go elsewhere, then come back and go out again to Times Square. One bit of advice though, if you go to the Marriott revolving bar (come out of back of hotel and enter Marriott) do not go for the evening buffet. The food is awful and not worth the money. But it is nice to go for a drink there as the bar revolves 360 degrees 48 floors high so you see all of NYC! Try Bubba Gumps in Times Square. Fun dining experience. This was our second trip to NY, so we didnt really do all the sights again, mainly shopping although we did walk across the Brooklyn Bridge and back again ( a total must as the views of Manhattan on the way back are breathtaking especially at sunset, also try Grimaldis pizza place under the bridge on the Brrooklyn side) and we went to Central Park again which is just gorgeous. The top of 5th Avenue by Central Park and Tiffanys, Plaza Hotel etc is just proper NYC, just like in the films. Went to Woodbury Common this time, got some great bargains. Stayed at the Belvedere Hotel last time which was just as good so would recommend either hotel. Please dont worry about staying at the Edison, it is totally fine and a great price (unless they have some dodgy rooms which we didnt stay in). Christmas time in New York is just magical. Enjoy!!!

name: Herald Square Hotel
title: “tolle Lage, ansonsten unmögliches Hotel”
text:
Einzig die Lage ist posotiv, direkt am Empire State Building, nah an der Mertro und zu Fuss zum Times Square.
Das Hotelzimmer war so klein, dass wir nicht mal wussten wo und wie wir unsere Taschen aufmachen sollten. Das Fenster im Schlafzimmer liess sich nicht öffnen und zeigte auf einen Luftschacht, der nicht wirklich zu Tageslicht oder frischer Luft beitrug. Das Zimmer war extre muffig und unglaublich warm und stickig. Klimaanlage direkt neben Kopf des Schläfers in vielleicht 20cm Abstand, funktionierte auch nur insofern als sie laut war! Das Bett war megaunbequem. Wir konnten dadurch 6 Nächte lang kaum schlafen, obwohl wir abneds platt waren, was die Urlaubsfreude doch sehr trübte. Im übrigen hatten wir ein renoviertes Zimmer gebucht und dieses war keinesfalls renoviert und 220,- Dollar pro Nacht sind dafür absolut zuviel.
Ach so- unsauber wars auch, im Bad z.B.schwarze lange Haare überall,waren auch bei unserer Abreise noch da.
Unser Fazit: nie mehr, es gibt in der Nähe etliche andere Hotels in ähnlicher Preislage.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Amazing location...”
text: We stayed at the Hilton New York last week and were very pleased with the location! It was close to everything and when we didn’t want to walk there was a subway nearby to take us to Brooklyn or Coney Island. The Hilton itself was clean and centrally located. The rooms were spacious, especially for New York standards. It was nice to see that they checked for room cards in the evening, we came back very late several evenings. The only minor issues we had was with housekeeping, they called to see if we were out of the room, we are in NYC and stayed out late and were trying to sleep in when the phone rang. I can say it was surprisingly quite, which was fantastic, I have heard stories that noise can be a problem in NYC, that was not an issue here. Also the air con keep and would not warm up, although that could have been just us as we like it a bit warmer ? The breakfast area was nice; I really liked the flax blueberry pancakes, and the convenience of a Starbucks to start the day. The view was beautiful from our room! The staff was great when we needed an umbrella, directions, or help with activities ? we would defiantly stay here again on any future visit to NYC!!

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “New York New York”
text: Stayed for seven nights with my girlfriend, check in was fast and friendly when we got to our room it was really nice, quite spacious with a desk flat screen tv and chair. Every day our room was cleaned and our bed made up perfectly. The hotel staff were always helpful and polite, the bar was pretty pricey but I found that about most bars in New York. We stayed on the fith floor and it was quite noisy but we still slept ok. When we checked out there were a few items on our mini bar bill I was unsure about so I asked reception about them and they knocked them off without question. Will stay there again but maybe on a higher floor. There is a handy gift shop inside the hotel for any gifts you need papers sweets etc. We didnt eat once from the hotel as there are so much places to eat nearby.

name: Sheraton New York Times Square Hotel
title: “Good option”
text:
I was in NYC just for the weekend on my own (without the family). This hotel is very centrally located and within easy walking distance to Central Park, Rockefeller Center, 5th Ave shopping, MOMA, and Radio City Music Hall. Heading down a few blocks further is Times Square. I picked this hotel solely for the location, knowing that I would not spend much time in the room. That said, the room was clean and nice. No complaints. I'd opt for this hotel again in the future. 
 I would definitely try to find a deal on this one, though, because I don't think that it's worth over $200 a night as posted on the website.

name: Hudson New York
title: “D'une tristesse...”
text:
Grande déception pour cet hôtel. OK c'est Starck, mais du Starck qui a vieilli et pas très bien (c'est souvent le cas du Starck vieillissant...). Malgré une reservation longtemps à l'avance, nous avons attendu plus de 45 mins avant d'avoir les clés de nos chambres. 
La propreté de la chambre laisse un peu à désirer, mais le pire a été le bruit... Même les boules Quies n'y ont rien fait...
Le lendemain changement de chambre : une petite chambre si sombre que même à midi, il faut mettre la lumière - pardon les néons... Après visite d'autres chambres, je peux vous confirmer que beaucoup de chambres sont minuscules et très très sombres. 
En résumé, allez-y y prendre un verre; les bars sont bien plus sympas.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Very good hotel - even if it's in Times Square”
text:
I attended a conference at the hotel. I was very satisfied with my one night stay. 
Pros:
comfortable beds
shower with great water pressure and temperature
very nice view from the 30th floor
Cons:
movies menu didn't work
room was a little stuffy when I first walked in
temperature control was a little difficult
I must say that the conference food was much better than the rubber chicken that you usually get. Nice selection and I was very happy with the lunch.
I'm not a fan of Times Square area, but since this was business and not pleasure, I was very happy to stay at this property.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Hoel très bien situé - chambre vieillote”
text: Nous avons séjourné 3 nuits au mois de mai 2009 dans une king size bedroom dans l'aile de l'hotel. Chambre vieillote, moquette pas fraîche, salle de bain moyenne et tv d'un autre siècle. Le point positif de cet hotel est sa situation. A 2 pas de central park et de time square. Hotel de classe touristique, entre 2* et 3*. Pdj servit au restaurant de l'hotel. station de metro devant l'hotel. les chambres de l'aile de l'hotel auraient bien besoin d'être rénovées. Un peu cher pour le comfort que l'on a mais on paye surtout sa situation centrale. Concierge plein de bons conseils, personnel de récpetion un peu froid

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “DO NOT STAY HERE!!!!!”
text:
this is the worst hotel I have ever stayed in in my life!!!!
we arrived at the hotel at the correct check in time, to find our room was not ready. the hotel lobby is nice, so we were shocked by the standard of room- dark, dingy and dirty. we asked to be moved- staff were rude and unhelpful and said housekeeping would come and tidy up the room. the housekeeping assistant came 5 minutes later- she was the rudest little lady i'd ever come across in my life, and when she left there was still hair in the bath!!!!the carpet was stained, the bathroom was tiny- with no fan, the bedding was itchy. we were moved the following day- the room was slighly better- but still no where near as good as the pictures shown on the net.
Generally all staff were unhelpful.
excursions and attractions booked via the hotel are a rip off.
on the plus side location is excellent and there is a real good deli next door where you can get amazing food up until quite late.

name: Holiday Inn New York City - Wall Street
title: “bella sorpresa!”
text:
io e mia sorella abbiamo alloggiato in questo hotel, all'apparenza dimesso, anche perchè, al momento, nella zona di Wall Street ci sono lavori in corso e l'hotel stesso è in fase di ristrutturazione, con una hall angusta e piccolissima. All'arrivo in camera la sorpresa: la stanza, pur non essendo grande, offriva un'ottima vista dall'alto dei suoi 18 piani e si presentava ariosa, con l'arredo sobrio ed elegante; il letto era veramente confortevole, tessuti e asciugamani di qualità. Il bagno piccolo ma ben arredato e pulito.
Dovessi ritornare a New York prenoterei sempre nello stesso hotel

name: Park Central
title: “Perfecto!”
text:
Realmente es un hotel perfecto: buena ubicación, lindas habitaciones!
Estuvimos 7 días y realmente descansar en esas camas era lo que necesitábamos después de tanto caminar!

name: Holiday Inn New York City - Wall Street
title: “ottimo rapporto qualità prezzo stanze ok servizi sufficienti”
text: Siamo stati con amici all'Hotel Reserve. Posizione comoda sia per Lower Manhattan che per Midtown e le principali attrazioni (è a 200 mt dalla fermata metro rossa, blu e verde Fulton Street e a 100 mt dalla Broadway x un mitico taxi giallo :-) ). LA Lobby è microscopica ma il personale è attento e disponibile. Se pero' uscite dal seminato improvviasano troppo e danno risposte parziali e insoddisfacenti. Insomma come sempre meglio arrangiarsi da soli ! Le stanze sono minimaliste e dotate di un discreto bagno comodo e pulito. In generale c'è tutto e la pulizia è buona. scarsa l'armadiatura e i mt quadri complessivi rapportati a un 3 stelle italiano ma per gli standard di NYC è + che buona. Pressochè inesistenti servizi vari, anche se internet gratuito ovunque è ottimo. Alla fine per 87 EURO a notte per una tripla è un affare.

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “can't find a better deal in the city..”
text:
I have stayed in the city many many times at several different hotels, from 4 star to youth hostiles and this has to be the best deal in the city.
Free parking yes that is correct free parking in N.Y.
Two blocks from the Henry Hudson Parkway, four blocks from Times Square, location is great.
The a/c was very very cold perfect for july 30th 90 degree temps. Just one other thing, DO NOT Go in July because if I cannot get a room You are in trouble.

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “Can't beat it!”
text: We stayed here twice, at the start of our trip, and three weeks later, at the end. On the first stay we were on the third floor, right next to the pool - the room didn't have air con, but did have a real opening window and plenty of space. The second time we were on the sixth floor, in a room with an uncontrolable a/c unit, and right next to the lift machinery! The pool is unheated, spacious and seems little used which is a pity. The staff were freindly and helpful. There are two parts of the hotel, one part seems to require a change of lifts on the third floor. The diner next door offers splendid value breakfasts, and the best pancakes we found anywhere in North America! For a budget evening meal, cross the street to the Kraft Restaurant. The Travel Inn is an excellent budget stay, very conveniently located with all the amenities you need (except an in-room coffee maker).

name: Sheraton New York Times Square Hotel
title: “Great NYC location...very good hotel.”
text:
Got a very good deal on Hotwire ($140). Love the very central location of this hotel...step out the revolving doors, turn left and you can see the bright lights of 42nd Street just down the hill.
Absolutely nothing to complain about here. Even a seething mass of young dancers for some kind of international competition could not detract from the overall excellent experience. 
Everything you'd expect from a Sheraton, this is a very well positioned hotel that allows anyone easy access to the best of NYC. Good sized rooms, great amenities and facilities. Clean, surprisingly quiet and comfortable.
Renovations on the exterior were the only very minor issue to note but had no impact on us.

name: Tribeca Grand Hotel
title: “We Loved the Tribeca Grand!”
text: We booked this hotel through Priceline and I was a bit worried when I read the mixed reviews. Not to worry the hotel was fabo - the room was average size, but clean as a whistle. The bed was comfy and the view from our window of the streets of Soho was so quaint. We weren't bothered by the noise from the bar at all. We had drinks at the bar - be prepared - it is $12 a pop at least. Great location - away from the hubbub of Times Square - easy walking distance to the Bleecker Street pubs, Little Italy restaurants and Canal Street shopping. Want to go back!

name: Hotel Gansevoort
title: “Don't do it...Tired TIRED hotel...Service not good- Roof top pool...NARLY”
text: Well...I am not sure what we thouht it would be like...but whatever it was we thought it WASNT..to start out...they didnt have the correct room and when we ask for the room we had reserved..and payed for ...they said they were BOOKED...but then 10 mins later we they saw our paper work...WOW a room arrived.....oh and this room---STUNK of SMOKE>>burns on the rug....hair on the toilet...ahahha....so we leave...again...NO ONE says anything at the front desk...heads down...NO customer service..the nicest guy there was the one caring our bags all over the place! When we returned we did have another room...It was clean...it was on the 8th floor and it was quiet...We were woken up a few times by the druck teens from upstairs..but on the whole it was quiet...UPSTAIRS...Turkish Baths and MTV Spring break smashed together...naked people in the pool doing god knows what..it was discusting!! Breakfast so expensive....19.95 for a yogart and some fruit...................would never stay there again...only good point it was in a great area

name: Hotel Gansevoort
title: “Party Hotel”
text: Firstly this hotel is in a fab location, we were impressed with all the cool bars and restaurants in the area. The room was on the small side but it had everything that we needed. Breakfast was included with the room and you have two choices which isnt so bad. Unfortuantely what we didnt know was that this hotel is 'PARTY CENTRAL'. They had a Plunge Party from 8am till 8am or that was what was advertised - it was still going on at 4am! Dont get me wrong I love a good party or club but this was just ridiculous. We decided to shop on that morning so we had to keep coming back to the hotel to drop off our bags. Becuase of this hotel being so uber cool there was a massive queue of girls trying to get into our hotel for the party which meant it was difficult for us (RESIDENTS!) to get back in - this went on all day and as the day went on the music and the people got louder. We thought that if you cant beat them join them so we did - BIG MISTAKE! The staff were very rude and the clientale are just there to 'be seen' and absolutely love themselves - not the type of people I like to associate myself with. A shame that this let the hotel down slightly as there was no way we could use the pool or even get a seat in the bar - you would think that if you are paying to stay that you would have priority but obvioulsy not.

name: Park Central
title: “comodissimo”
text: Ottimo hotel, comodo soprattutto per la posizione tra Times Square e Central Park sulla 7th. E' molto grande, il personale l'abbiamo visto praticamente solo all'ingresso, ma non abbiamo avuto bisogno di nulla. Camera spaziosa, pulita, insonorizzata. Ingresso della metropolitana a un passo dalla porta di accesso laterale. Colazione da starbucks o all'americana nei ristoranti della via a prezzi più umani.

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “Pulgas en la habitación”
text:
No se como explicarlo, pero esto no me había pasado nunca. Nos alojamos durante una semana en este hotel un grupo de amigos. 
La ubicación es bastante buena, aunque se vé un poco de gentucilla conforme vas avanzando en la dirección del hotel 42nd Street. Está cerca para acceder a la zona de Times Square en unos 15 minutos andando. Nosotros fuimos en Enero, por lo que hacía bastante frío y a veces cogíamos un Taxi, ya que eran bastante económicos.
Nada más llegar al hotel nos dijeron que no teníamos ninguna reserva, habíamos llamado una semana antes para confirmarlo y no nos pusieron ninguna pega. Tras discutir más de 15 minutos, por fín encuentran nuestra habitación. (Cuando nosotros estuvimos alojados nadie hablaba español).
La habitación es amplia, con grandes ventanales (muy viejos). La habitación era para 4 personas con dos camas de matrimonio. El baño muy muy sucio, con humedades y viejo. La habitación llena de polvo. 
La segunda de las noches, nos despertamos todos con un importante calor y picor en el cuerpo. Observamos que había unos pequeños bichitos por el colchón y la almohada. Dos de nosotros tuvimos que ir al médico porque las pulgas nos habían provocado una reacción alérgica en la piel enorme. Estuvimos todo el viaje con antihestaminicos y con cortisona para paliar la hinchazón de la piel. 
En el hotel se excusaron cambiándonos de habitación y diciendo que quizás hubieran venido en el equipaje del avión... ¿Yo les contesté que a 50ºC bajo cero en el avión hay pulgas? Es cierto que en la otra habitación ya no vimos pulgas.
En fín, un desastre... no os fiéis por el precio del hotel y ni se os ocurra ir allí.

name: Hotel Gansevoort
title: “Great Location....Shame about the hotel!!!”
text:
Let me begin by saying the Ganesvoort is overpirced, dirty and a disgrce to '5 star' hotels....You should be ashamed!!!!
I had travelled with my girlfriend and her family and intended to stay at the Ganesvoort for 4 nights as we had been informed it was 'the hottest place to be in New York'. I agree that the location is fantastic and the nightlife is top class with celebs floating around on every corner. However......on arriving at the hotel we could not believe the 60's looking exterior was only 5 years old reminding us of a budget hotel chain found in dumpsville. 
On entering the hotel yes the lobby is decked out relatively cool, purple lighting, funky music but the ambience is just cheap. Nothing as you would expect for the rates that you are paying. We checked into our rooms and ok they were adequate, a little small but again overpriced!
The club on the roof top is a cool spot at night but as any night clubber will adimit a club during the day is just seedy and dirty. Floor tiles were broken and wallpaper coming fromt the walls. Hardly worth the outrages prices of crystal they were trying to offload! 
From the website pictures the roof top pool looks unbelieveable, just spectacular....only one thing to say.....Seriously disappointed!!!
I can see why people stay here becasue the nightlife around the meatpacking district is simply awesome and we loved our night out expecially dinner at the Spice Market opposite and breakfast at Pastis. But for our 4 night stay we deicded to move hotels to the New York Palace Hotel for traditional class and top class service. This hotel is the true gem of New York. Long live the Dorchester!!!

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Good and bad”
text:
When I first got to this hotel, I was really blown away by the friendly staff. The bellhop was very friendly, as were the people at the front desk.
When I got to my room, it turned out it was already occupied. No problem, they switched my room very quickly and all was well.
But the room was a bit disappointing. It was small, a picture was missing from above the bed (with the hanging material still on the wall), I had to dust the lamps myself, a lightbulb in one of the lamps was burnt out, the TV remote didn't work properly, the bathtub stopper didn't work, and the sheets didn't fit the bed. THAT IS THE WORST! Instead of a proper fitted bottom sheet, they had laid out a top sheet that didn't fit the bed. So the bottom of the sheet didn't cover the mattress pad. Very weird, and I found myself trying to remake the bed the best I could or think about all the other feet that may have touched that same mattress pad. Not a pleasant thought.
But the hotel in all was clean and nice and the location was great and the people friendly (of all the people I encountered during my three night stay, only one was rude), and I liked the hotel despite its faults.
It may have been that I was in New York city, the bright lights of Times Square were steps away, and it was easier to turn a blind eye this time than others. But imagine how great it would be if they would get the details right!

name: Park Central
title: “solides Hotel mit Top Lage”
text: Da die meisten NewYork Besucher sowieso selten den ganzen Tag auf dem Zimmer verbringen, ist dieses Hotel durchaus empfehlenswert! Die Zimmer sind sauber , Toiletten auch , die Lage ist absolut ideal und die Preise moderat. Die U-Bahn liegt direkt am Haus , zum Central Park sinds nur 2 Blocks und Times Square und Rockefeller Centre sind bequem zu Fuß erreichbar.Was braucht man also mehr ? Ich würde es wieder nehmen.

name: Herald Square Hotel
title: “Good Hotel, Nice Stay”
text: Stayed here with my girlfriend in Feb 07 and it was perfect for what we required. The price is very good for Manhattan. It is midtown and is only 2 mins from the Empire State building and 5 mins from Macys. There are loads of subway stops within 5 mins walk. The room was clean and comfortable. The bathroom was basic, clean and the shower was good so no complaints. The staff were friendly and there was absolutely no wait for checking in or out. I would definitely stay here again.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Het hotel Pennsylvania in New York”
text:
Wij hebben voor dit hotel gekozen, wegens eerder verblijf en de ligging.
Bij aankomst kregen wij een hele kleine bedompte kamer, welke rook naar sigaretten, met uitzicht op binnenplaats.
Nadat wij dit hadden aangegeven kregen wij een prima, grotere kamer hiervoor terug met uitzicht op het straatbeeld. Dit werd direct geregeld.
De kamer werd elke dag schoongemaakt en de handdoeken werden dagelijks verschoond.
Wij hebben niet in het hotel gegeten, omdat wij het leuker vinden om buiten de deur te eten.
Het personeel hebben wij als vriendelijk en behulpzaam ervaren.
De ligging van het hotel is geweldig en daarom zeker een aanrader.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “UNA VACANZA QUASI PERFETTA”
text:
Se non fosse per l'ottima posizione del'albergo non lo raccomanderei a nessuno.
Le camere sono sporche, l'arredamento è antico e il personale non molto cortese.
A chi volesse soggiornarci consiglio di farsi assegnare le camere ai piani alti perchè meno logore.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Perfect location for a great hotel.”
text: Perfect location. Close to pretty much everything. Short walk to central park, subway, broadway and shopping. The rooms are great everyone is polite and the service is top notch. We have stayed here both times we visited New York.

name: Tribeca Grand Hotel
title: “Fashionable boutique walking distance to China Town and Little Italy”
text: The firendly modern service and unique design of this boutique hotel impress. It is in a great location, being close tothe financial district for business, but far enough away so you can lose yourself at evenings and weekends. The rooms are not a bad size for New york and are decorated in a modern fashion (athough may be due some redecoration). The bar is fun and is open late... can be busy and noisy, but that is part of the buzz of the place!

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Excellent Location”
text:
I don't usually end up north of 50th or so in New York, but this hotel location was well worth the couple extra blocks. The location is quiet and convenient, with a subway stop just at the corner, plenty of shops for a quick bite, and a starbucks directly across from the front hotel entrance.
We got a really good deal on the rooms, which were functional and minimalist; our main goal wasn't to spend a lot of time in the hotel, anyway, so I wasn't really that picky. A coffee machine in the room would have been nice for coffee/tea.
Our rooms were on the 9th floor, and though we were close to the elevators, it was very quiet.

name: Tribeca Grand Hotel
title: “Not bad for NYC”
text:
Our experience was a bit of a mixed bag but overall we did enjoy our stay. 
Negatives: they had a party in the lobby both nights we were there. We were promised a room higher up but they could not give us one. Only when we kicked up a fuss, we got a room on 8th floor. We still heard the party a little bit.
The hotel is not cheap but that is just NYC , I guess.
Carpets are a bit old and grotty and need updating. 
The area: I would not stay in TriBeCa again, is a bit dodgy around Canal street. I prefer Soho or upwards.
Positives: nice room with lovely bed and linens. Good size as well. 
Free coffee, tea on 7 th floor. 
Concierges and doormen vey helpful and friendly. 
I do advice the hotel of you want to stay in that area. The architecture and design are quite special.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Super høstferie i New York”
text:
Dette hotellet hadde en sentral og flott beliggenhet,
med kort avstand til forskjellige serverdiheter og opplevelser.Gå avstand til foreksempel Centrel Park og Brodeway.
I møtekommen og trivelig betjening,fikk f.eksp. bytte rom uten problemer og spørsmål.
Kan hende litt mye kø ved heisen i rushtiden, og litt gammelt intreniør og tapeter .

name: Hotel Gansevoort
title: “would stay again!”
text: came into town with a friend for some business and some fun! the hotel...great, fun location with fantastic restaurants and shopping (although the area for shopping is expensive). hotel staff is very friendly and helpful. our room had a view of the cobblestone streets and pastis, it felt very old new york in a great modern building. bathroom and room spacious, very clean. so many great bars in ny, but having our very own rooftop bar to wind down the evening was perfect!

name: Sheraton New York Times Square Hotel
title: “Pour son emplacement”
text: Très bien placé entre Times Square et Central Park. Mais chambre quelconque avec salle de bains vieillotte et minuscule. Lobby ressemble à un hall de gare. Intéressant de payer le supplément de 50USD pour une chambre club qui donne accès au lounge ouvert 24h/24h au 40eme où il est possible de prendre petit-déjeuner et boissons.

name: Sheraton New York Times Square Hotel
title: “Hall de gare !”
text:
Hôtel très mal insonorisée, les portes claques jusque tête dans la nuit. La SDB est très petite est plutôt moche. Le hall est un congelo l'été. Le peti déj à 30 D est un scandale.
La wifi payante aussi.

name: Solita Soho Hotel
title: “Travelling on a budget and wanting to stay in Soho?”
text: Booked this hotel for a six night stay in NYC, and couldn't have chosen a better place to stay with our budget. The location was perfect, and the staff was very friendly. We booked a standard room with one queen bed, but upon arrival we were upgraded to a 'two double bed'-room in the top floor without any extra charge. -They thought we should have a bigger room as we were staying for almost a week. The room was plain, but very clean. The beds were really comfortable, and I loved the massage shower. It was more than big enough for us, but then again, we're used to European size rooms. We also had an amazing view from our window. We weren't troubled with any disturbing noise, but that might be due to staying on the 7th floor. I have recommended Solita Soho to friends travelling on a budget looking for a good location in NYC, and they were really happy with the hotel. Would definitely stay there again.

name: Hotel Verite
title: “Great hotel and great location”
text:
My wife and i recently went on our visit trip to New York and after many hours of searching the many options we chose the Verite. We could not have been more pleased.
Firstly location it is midway between 23 street and Union square Metro stations. A couple of blocks behind the Flatiron building where there is also a great little park.
For the hotel itself. On arrival service was great, check in was quick and easy. The room was small modern and quiet. If the room had a downside it was dark due to curtains to prevent the office works across the road looking in. But this is New York who wants to spend time in the hotel all day! The storage space was a little limited but again not much of a concern. Our room looked over 19 street so was generally quiet, there was the occasional noise, again folks this is New York, i cant help but think the people on here complaining about noise are a bit over the top. I have stayed in many many hotels in small towns and big cities and i have stayed in more expensive hotels in smaller towns that are noisier than the Verite.
Coffee in the reception earlier was very handy to wake up and plan the daily attack on the city. There is great restaurants and cafes for breakfast lunch and dinner if needed and plenty of local Delis 
No question we would go here again. If your budget doesn't run to the big names in central locations with 100s of floors, or if you prefer to stay in an independent hotel can well recommend the Verite

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “Fantastic!”
text:
The room was everything we'd hoped for - and then some. Between the stainless steel sink and fixtures in the bathroom, the luxurious down bedding and warm decor in general, it was very appealing and cozy. I slept like a rock in that bed. The staff was impressive, most notable the Concierge named Jason. He was phenomenal!! He got us 5th row seats to see Blue Man Group (on a Saturday night) with less than 24 hrs notice. He was extremely helpful and because of him we ate like kings in some of the best restaurants in the area. We would definitely stay there again. 
The location was very convenient. Close to Times Square, Rockefeller Center and great shopping. If you're into sightseeing, it's conveniently close to the Waldord Astoria which is where you can catch a free shuttle to the docks for one of the sightseeing cruises, sightseeing tour buses also stop here to pick up riders. Anyone who knows how much is costs to take a cab from one side to town to the other will appreciate the free shuttle. 
Great hotel!!

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Good value”
text: Large bland hotel but spacious rooms and friendly staff. Quiet and in an excellent location. Good conference facilities and excellent rates. All in all excellent value and a safe choice without being a memorable experience

name: Hotel Gansevoort
title: “loved it”
text:
Stayed for a 2 night break last weekend for a shopping trip.
Hotel is very cool. Nice rooms and bathrooms. Rooms a little on the small side but thats usual for New york. Great bar on the top floor. Very busy in the evening.....Q's around the corner to get in.
I ate at Pastis twice (which is 10 steps outside the front door). It was lovely.
Vey noisy at night with all the cabs 'honking' at 3 am but thats pretty normal for NYC.

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “Hotel Travel Inn, Manhattan..New York”
text:
Excelente servicio y ubicacion, su cercania a Times Square garantiza una estadia agradable para cualquier turista. Facil acceso al Subway en diferentes rutas, igual a la Terminal de Buses y la gran variedad de restaurantes a su alrededor desde comida rapida a cenas formales.
Volveria a disfrutar de estos servicios.

name: Hotel Gansevoort
title: “Nice hotel but it's a noisy area!”
text: My husband and I (50 somethings) just spent the weekend in NYC visiting our daughter (student at NYU) and our son (student at The New School). We decided to try the Gansevoort on our daughter's recommendation. There was alot to like -- our room was very nice with a wonderful view of the Hudson River and NJ; the service was good; the restaurant (Ono) was great; and it's close to lots of good restaurants in the West Village area. The big drawback was, however, street noise. The hotel is in a big "clubbing" area of NYC -- and despite being 10 floors up, we were awakened both nights at ~ 3:30-4:00am by loud voices, honking, and sirens as the clubs let out. So if you're young and go to clubs yourself it's probably a good choice. We'll head back to the Soho Grand or the W on Union Square next time we go for the weekend.

name: Ramada Eastside
title: “excellent”
text: very attractive in location. it is very convinient for visiiors to travel around of new yourk . located in the central of the city. the hotlel is very flexible for checkout. i will still select this hotel in I will be New York next time.

name: Solita Soho Hotel
title: “What a great time!”
text:
Be it your first time, or a regular visitor, the Solita is a wonderful place to stay for location alone. This little boutique is modern, clean, and staffed by some very friendly knowledgeable people genuinely interested in the seeing that you have a great time on your visit. Transportation between the airport and hotel is relatively easy, the check-in and check-out were a breeze, leaving you relaxed and focused on whatever brings you to New York.
Located in Lower Manhattan, it sits at an apex of several areas of the city putting the Lower Eastside, Greenwich Village, Meatpacking District, Broadway, Canal Street, Little Italy, East Village, West Village, Chinatown, WTC, Financial District,etc. all within walking distance. Several subway lines make stops at Canal Street and within the general vicinity of the hotel, leaving you with basically the entire city at your disposal in a matter of minutes.
Rooms are clean and reasonably priced, cleaning staff unobtrusive but prompt, and again the staff - who were very helpful arranging transportation, providing directions or suggestions for sight seeing, shopping, dining and night life. 
I definitely have the Solita in mind for my coming return visit to New York.

name: Doubletree Hotel Chelsea New York City
title: “Loud!!!”
text: Currently staying on the 24th floor and there is a roof top club/ bar playing loud music with a ton of bass across from our room. Even with the ac on there is so much noise. After traveling all day would love some rest.

name: Park Central
title: “Tranquilli !”
text: Sono appena tornata da un soggiorno in questo hotel e vorrei rassicurare quanti, dopo aver letto le recensioni qualche tempo fa, si sono preoccupati della pulizia (bed bugs) e degli ascensori. Ho pernottato al 10° piano, altri amici al 9° e al 18°, tutto regolare! Gli ascensori sono regolati in maniera elettronica e offrono un rapido servizio, ottima la colazione. La posizione è invidiabile. Buon viaggio. AZ

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Good, but not impressed with details.”
text: I stayed there at the end of August 2012 for business. The locations is fine, though not really central (it's a few blocks from the subway though). The room was spacious, the bed comfortable, and the view rather nice, but some parts of the room could be renovated (old tv, stains in the bathroom walls that looked like blood). I would recommend this hotel for the price or for a business trip -above all if you work for the UN- but would stay in another hotel if I had the means!

name: Larchmont Hotel
title: “Great location, very small room but OK”
text:
I stayed in a single room - the smaller size room. The room was decent. I didn't really like the shared bath but I knew about it when I made the reservation and they were clean. The AC worked well. The two things I didn't like - 1. Two of the 3 nights it was noisy because of people in the room next door, in the hall, or outside. I kept the AC running to drown out the noise even though I then ended up feeling too cold. 2. I like the room dark when I sleep. Unfortunately, because the door was not properly fitted or too old, etc., light from the hallway came in from around the door jamb and along the bottom. I ended up putting a blanket over the door to block the light. Also the windows didn't have curtains or drapes so light from the street lamps peered through the venetian blinds. 
The location was great! Close to subway stops, restaurants, etc. Nice neighborhood. The room was so-so, but it was definitely not bad. Next time I might see if I can stay at a nicer place for a few dollars more. If I can't find something a bit more updated, with a private bath and curtains, I'd consider staying at the Larchmont again.

name: The Hotel at Times Square
title: “Pretty Decent Hotel in NYC”
text: Stayed here on 8/1/12 for around $200. We were able to check-in early. Room was small with window going to closed in stairwell but bed was comfortable and room was clean. A/c in room worked well. We did not stay much in the room so it didn't really matter the size. Great location. I'd stay here again for a cheaper stay in NYC.

name: The Hotel at Times Square
title: “I would return to this hotel”
text:
The Hotel at Times Square is a nice little hotel in the heart of Manhattan. It is close to broadway, times square and transit. The rooms are an okay size. We had 3 in our room and it was okay. The other ladies we went with did have an issue with their room. There was mold in the bathroom and bugs as well. They told front desk that evening, and then were moved to the best room in the hotel. So other then the trauma of the first night they had a good stay as well. The evening front desk gentleman was a little confused about our billing and in the end, I had to suck up the extra cost, as I was tired of explaining.... 
That would be the only down side I had and the reason I put in average. The breakfast was good and the coffee offered 24/7 was also good. The air conditioning was awesome, as we went to New York and the peak of its hot time... 41 in the shade....... sweating from places I didn't know existed...lol Next time I would go in the spring or fall.

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Loved UN Plaza!”
text:
This is quite a late review but I felt compelled to write one. We went in October 2011, This was our first visit to New York, my boyfriend and myself chose this hotel mostly for the views from the rooms, we weren't disappointed! We could see both the Chrysler and Empire State, My boyfriend spent ages every day taking views from the window. I forgot the doorman's name but he was Lovely, nothing was too much trouble, in fact all staff were very helpful and pleasant. 
We were slightly worried about location thinking it may be a bit out of the way of all the action but its only a 10 minute walk to times square etc. There was a great little coffee cart right outside the hotel every morning for all the people going to work, its the one place we found 'proper' english tea, very pleased. 
Beds were huge and very comfortable, only quip about the hotel was the bathrooms, completely covered in mirrors , not sure I like seeing myself of the loo but hey ho..
Swimming pool was amazing we went in the evening, It was cool seeing the New York skyline all lit up whilst having a swim! Didn't try the gym but amazing views there too.
I'd recommend taking some binoculars for your bedroom window as you can see right down to the Freedom Tower etc. We were on the 38th floor, lifts VERY quick! Only had breakfast once in the hotel, was very expensive as you'd expect but very nice. 
I miss UN Plaza so much, everyday me and my boyfriend say how much we want to go back haha, so if you're thinking of booking DO, you won't regret it and the views are to die for!
Katy&Sean x

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Super situation, à 2 pas de Times Square!!!!”
text: Je cherchais avant tout un hotel tout près de Times Square comme je connais déjà le quartier. Il faut savoir que Manhattan est très cher donc si vous chercher un hôtel correct pour dormir celui là est parfait. Les palaces plus luxueux sont hors de prix!!!!

name: ONE UN New York
title: “You pay for the views”
text:
My mum and I stayed here in June 2012. 
PROS:
When you first get to the hotel, it looks amazing. So classy and well presented. 
It's in a great safe part of the city, only a few blocks down from Grand Central Station. 
When we got to our room on the 28th floor, the views across the city took our breath away. We got to see the Chrysler and Empire State Buildings light up each night, and could see all the way downtown. 
Our room had the basic amenities - closet with iron & ironing board, full bathroom with bath.
CONS:
The room was pretty average, with scuff marks all over the walls and the bath desperately needed re-enamel. 
It was disappointing that you have to pay extra for wi-fi in your room. 
I had to ask the concierge 3 times to fix my bedside light, which wasn't great. 
OVERALL: Definitely worth getting a room just for the view, everything else you can put up with.

name: The Helmsley Park Lane
title: “Great location and nice rooms”
text:
The longest part of my planing is always regarding hotels. It's hard to combine everything we want: great location, rooms that are clean, spacious, with plenty of amenities, nice service and of course, with reasonable prices.
I'd like to reinforce the "reasonable": that doesn't mean "cheap"- but value for the price.
I thought my experience with the Helmsley Park Lane was just that. Location is stupidly good - and as someone who works with technology, being 50 mts from the Apple Store is something you have to grab without asking.
The check-in experience was good - not great. I can't complain, though - I arrived too early. But they did allow me to get in earlier than usual. The service is fine - I really don't use it much - and the room I stayed in was worthy of its price. Spacious, wifi working fast, nice bathroom - great shower.
Overall it's something that's worth of what you're paying. And if you're looking for location, it's probably one of the best prices you'll get in the area.

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Still pretty good after all these years”
text:
Memories. In the 90's, we used to play tennis at the rooftop club then go around the corner to reward our exercise with a feast at Palm Too. We often would recommend the hotel to friends and relatives visiting as it was always reasonable and comfortable with a hint of class.
While searching for a room at the last minute, the hotel came up with a decent rate. Just the hotel name made me smile. I decided to try it out. It did not disappoint. The staff was quite helpful and friendly. The rooms are nice, but the carpet in my room had one massive stain. The view was perfect. The location might seem a bit out in left field, but it actually is not too bad. 
Bottom line, I would stay there again.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Desastroso. Me daba hasta miedo.”
text:
Con una amiga contratamos un viaje organizado a New York y nos alojaron en este hotel.
 Creo que es el peor hotel en el que he estado. Viejo, mal cuidado, tenebroso...
 En el baño habian telarañas.
 Solo puedo recomendar este hotel por su situacion centrica en Times Square.
 Hay cientos de hoteles mejores al mismo precio.

name: The Helmsley Park Lane
title: “Great Value for Money”
text: Loved this hotel. The location is great. We had a wonderful view over Central Park. We were originally on the 10th floor, but due to a mix up we then moved to 20th floor. The room was lovely and spacious. No noise. We thought it was really good value for money through Expedia. Continental breakfast was included - dining room for breakfast was beautiful. We found the staff lovely - I have medication that needs refrigeration and as the mini bar fridge is weighted you can't put anything in there - so after speaking with the staff they brought up another fridge and installed it in the bathroom - at no extra cost. Nice work. We would definitely stay here again!!

name: Thompson LES - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Can't find your reservation but we are still going to try to charge you twice.”
text: When I attempted to check-in, the hotel could not locate my reservation. Fortunately they were not at full occupancy. I had my confirmation printed out and gave it to them. Still no luck. They created a new reservation and we were soon in our room. Well, after returning home, I saw there were two charges from the hotel. One was my total I signed for at check out, the other ($460.00) was unknown. When I called to inquire, a front desk rep told me it was a 'no show' charge, and they had a 'strict' no show policy. When I was explaining the confusing at my check-in, she interrupted me and said there was nothing she could do. So the computer obviously located my original reservation and flagged it as a no show. I finally spoke to a manager and he credited the money back. Complete idiots manning the front desk.

name: Doubletree Hotel Chelsea New York City
title: “great location, noisy room”
text:
The value overall is great for this hotel, you can't really beat the price if you want to stay in the city. 
The location is great -- 5 min walk from the subway that will get you everywhere
The room -- very noisy! I'm usually a heavy sleeper but got woken up multiple times by people walking upstairs and closing the doors. At one point I actually thought someone walked into my room.

name: Thompson LES - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Gorgeous property and Amazing Staff!”
text:
I don't really like to post my experience (good or bad) because I don't get the time to do so... i'm always on the run and never in a place with good internet connection (talk about 3rd world countries). But here i was in New York for a good week and was visiting my cousins from Calgary. We decided to meet up in NY since it's been 3 years since I came here... We decided to stay in the lower east side area because it was hip and happening from all the TimeOut reviews and articles that i had researched from back home. 
This is another reason i don't like to write reviews because i'm too detailed and could end up here for an hour. 
Yes, the reason i'm writing is because i do see a lot of reviews on Thompson LES and some are good and some are okay and some just outrageous (i don't know if these are true)... But let me state my side of the story and how it was so satisfying and just left me breathless from the first day to our check-out. We stayed in one of those Studio Kings on the 8th floor which was quite high but the view was not what i was looking for. Anyways, i didn't come here to stay in my room, i was here for my cousins and our good time in NY. During our stay, the staff at the front desk was more than giving, extremely courteous and very attractive i should say... They never said no to anything but came up with some suggestions all the time ... very young staff but i could tell they were in to it... Very cool and not up tight as other standard Hilton's and the Marriotts that we are used to... 
I was disappointed that they didn't have a restaurant but the front desk staff introduced us to Meatball shop and other neighborhood restaurants which were sooo good... Besides, all that the manager on duty during check-out actually invited me back to the hotel on my next trip to NY and said he'll buy me a drink or two in the new restaurant that they were opening. I will definitely be back just because of that gesture and involvement in his guest when i mentioned about the restaurant absence. that was my only complaint (so to speak).

name: Larchmont Hotel
title: “Nice European Feel”
text:
after spending 2 nights in a hostel on the upper west side, the Larchmont was fantastic.
bath clean and room immaculate.
Continental breakfast was a joke, but as another reviewer noted, a lot of great places in the area. For just over a $100 - this is going to be my go to hotel in NYC.

name: Wellington Hotel
title: “Super beliggenhed”
text: Beliggenheden er helt i top. Lige uden for døren på 7´th avenue kan du på din højre side kigge lige op til Central Park og til venstre se lige ned til lysene på Times Square. Umiddelbart udenfor ved 55´th street er der nedgang til subway. Hotelets personal virker flinke og imødekommende og værelserne er pæne og rene. Rengøring hver dag. Selvom man ikke opholder sig meget på værelset på sådan en byferie er det nu rart med sit eget badeværelse samt mulighed for at se lidt godnat fjernsyn! I hotelets kiosk kan man bestille transport til lufthavn når man skal hjem (24 timer før) Efter check ud på hjemrejse dagen (senest kl. 12.00) kan hotellet opbevare din baggage mens du bruger de sidste New York minutes ude i byen. Alt i alt et godt tre stjernet hotel med god service.

name: Thompson LES - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Chic and cool”
text:
This was my first visit to New York. I'd have never thought to stay in the Lower East Side, however, the location made for a unique and memorable NYC experience. I loved it. 
There is also a most remarkable music venue right next door (don't worry - there is NO noise into the hotel!!)
Roof top pool to cool off in the Summer - how cool is that!!
The rooms are great. The service is great. The location is great. What else is there?

name: The Helmsley Park Lane
title: “Nice location. Clean, but needs to be freshened”
text: My family and I just returned from a 4 day stay on the 38th floor (city view). The staff was fantastic; the location outstanding. Directly across the street from Central Park and a short walk to great restaurants, shows, and shopping. This is an older style New York hotel and although it was clean, the furnishings and finishes are slightly worn and dated. All told we had a very nice stay and would reserve again. One word of caution… there were 4 staying in our room but breakfast was only included for 2.

name: The Helmsley Park Lane
title: “Perfect location and great hotel”
text: Superb location on Central Park South. The subway is less than a block away, walking distance to Times Square, Rockefeller Center, and Fifth Ave. shopping. Central Park is just across the street. I read reviews talking about less than helpful staff, but I found every single staff member friendly and helpful. It says a lot about a hotel management that there were many long time staff. The dining room where continental breakfast is served has a wall of windows looking out at Central Park. A great way to start the day. The hot chocolate is heavenly! I also read reviews complaining about the rooms, but our rooms were beautiful. The hotel upgraded us and let us check out late. It was a pleasure to stay there.

name: Hudson New York
title: “Perfekt für den Städtetripp”
text: Großartiges, modernes, für NYC eher kleineres Hotel in perfekter Lage: Zwischen Central Park, Hudson und Theater District gelegen, mit der Subway vor der Tür ist es DER perfekte Ausgangspunkt für den New York Tripp.

name: Doubletree Hotel Chelsea New York City
title: “OK Hotel, Nothing Special, only Two Elevators so Long Waits”
text: Only two elevators for 26 floors, so be prepared for some long waits. The hotel's fine, nothing special, and the "free" wifi is only in the lobby, so you'll be paying for it if you want it in your room. This is a little deceptive. No other benes, really, so the next few nights I moved a block away to a Fairfield Inn that was nicer, free wifi, free breakfast, larger room.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Is there nothing this hotel won't charge you for...”
text: I don't like this hotel, the rooms are small (no different to most NY hotels), the bath is so shallow you could barely accommodate a goldfish, the TV picture is awful ( forget about HD, this is coat-hanger for aerial quality ), the internet is slow and they charge $50 per 3 days...PER DEVICE (in fairness they compd us 2 additional codes, but if they have to charge, which by the way is a joke, it should be per room), they wanted to charge me $2 to store my bag after I'd checked out and they charged me to receive a DHL letter. On the plus side, the gym is well equipped, treadmills, free weights and Ipod connections for cardio machines. If you need to use Grand Central whilst you are there, it is well located.

name: Solita Soho Hotel
title: “Clean, Inexpesive, Well-located”
text: The Solita is a great hotel if you want to avoid midtown tourist crowds and high prices. My wife and I, along with my sister, split a room on the fifth floor with two double beds, facing Grand St. The rooms are small (I would not add a 4th adult), but are clean and well-appointed. The beds are also very comfortable, and the double-headed shower is very soothing. A bit of noise reaches the room from the streets below, but it is nothing out of the ordinary if you are used to living in a city. As far as location, I don't believe I have ever stayed in a better one in the City. I often stay at the Millenium Hilton near the WTC site because of its great rooms and rates, but the trade off is a remote location. The Solita is two blocks from Mulberry St. in Little Italy, and you can walk to the best bars and restaurants on the LES and in Soho within 15 mins. The best pub in NYC, Puck Fair, is a three-minute stumble away at the corner of Layfayette & Houston. Finally, the B-D-F-V-N-R-W-6 trains are all within a five minute walk as well. Highly recommended if you are looking for something affordable below midtown.

name: Thompson LES - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Loved it!”
text:
We chose Thompson LES for its location. Easy to walk to interesting bars, restaurants and boutiques, and a short cab ride to Williamsburg.
We arrived at 7pm and our room wasn't ready, which isn't really what you want to hear after a 7 hour flight. But, we were taken up to the bar and offered a cocktail on the house which actually did make things better, we only waited 10mins and we were in our room, all forgotten about.
I was slightly concerned about out room (after reading a review about the 7th floor) which was opposite the club and right next to the lifts. But as we were out most nights, we never really had any problems with noise as there was a double door to our room, we could slightly hear music and people in and out of the club but never became an issue. We drank at Above Allen anyway one night (great views of the Empire State Building). But I possibly wouldn't have put bedrooms on the same floor as a club. 
However, we were extremely pleased with our room, it was huge! Gorgeous comfortable bed, amazing rainfall shower and great seating area, it was clean and modern. Maids came everyday to change towels etc and leave chocolates on the bed, we also requested an iron and they were straight up with one. Oh and Kiehl's products!
If I could have changed anything I would have like to have seen a kettle and mugs in the room to make a cup of tea and free wifi (there was a laptop which you could check anything on for free at the front desk, but felt a little awkward with people around). And, not to have a room on the 7th floor.
But I must say the staff were very welcoming and helpful all of the time and you were never once ignored, they are the best staff I have come across in a modern hotel, I wish they were like this in all hotels.
I would definitely stay here again on my next trip.

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Best Hotel on New York's East Side”
text: While tough to get a room when the United Nations - just across the street - is in session, the Millennium Plaza is available much of the year. Breathtaking river side views, looking east; dramatic cityscapes in rooms looking west. Check the hotel's own website for really good rates. Noticeable security because of VIPs and diplomats who stay at the hotel. Gracious and friendly staff. While the hotel has a bit of a 60's feel, it is first-class in all ways, except ... WiFi Internet. The Internet is outrageously expensive and slow. But, there's a Starbucks two blocks to the west.

name: The Jane
title: “more bed bugs”
text:
My daughter and I stayed for 3 nights. Loved the hotel, the room was even smaller than expected but still it had character. Shared washroom was clean and nice. Loved the location.
However, I too encountered bed bags - I am covered in bites, at least 30. Never considered it could be bed bugs, spoke to the person at the desk when we checked out and he indicated they have had no cases for years so thought maybe it was something that came in the window. I have now been home for 4 nights and I can't sleep because of the itching!! I did some more research and realized that it has to be bed bugs. Luckily I suspected that so washed everything at home. Seriously hope I didn't bring any back with me because these bites are driving me crazy!!
Unfortunately this has turned the trip of a lifetime into a hellish experience. I definitely won't risk returning ever.

name: Larchmont Hotel
title: “Pretty good really!”
text:
My partner and I booked this hotel earlier this year when it was getting more favourable reviews than it has been for the past few months. I watched in horror as our holiday loomed and review after review provided tales of bed bugs, widespread dirt, and poor service.
Imagine my relief when we finally got to the Larchmont after an 18 hour flight. It's fine! When you're paying US$120 a night for a room, and you're in an absolutely prime location for everything you could wish for - restaurants, numerous subway lines, character-filled streets as well as a central point from which to explore the whole of lower Manhattan - it's pretty churlish to complain about the less satisfactory aspects of the hotel. Yes, it's got worn furnishings, dirty carpet and the stench of stale cigarettes throughout. Yes, the showers fluctuate from scalding hot to icy cold in milliseconds, the air conditioning units sound like freight trains and the breakfast consists of day-old pastries. But in our opinion it was really good value, as long as you're willing to put up with those relatively minor issues. if you're not, it's best you stay elsewhere. 
Showers and toilets were always available, the beds were really comfortable and we fould the staff amenable, though not entirely friendly. We would stay here again, unless we won the lottery and could upgrade to somewhere fancier.

name: The Jane
title: “rooms vary a lot, check in early”
text:
We always read reviews before picking hotels and I knew the Jane had rooms that were noisy and that most larger rooms had views of the Hudson .I therefore asked for a high floor with a view.
When we checked in to our captain's cabin about 5.30 pm it was on the second floor with no view .The bathroom door was also jammed shut and had to be opened by an employee.We were told that if we got down to the lobby early in the morning we might get a better room .Both of us were very tired after a night with very little sleep and the flight from the UK and were not happy to be kept awake by the techno beat reverberating through our pillows until the early hours and also having to call down for someone to open the bathroom door again which took some time with various tools while I stood waiting for a pee.It did have a fantastic bath though.
Our next room on the fifth floor had a great view as it was on the corner of the building with three windows.We were delighted although we were a bit disappointed to find a shower and not a bath.The door did not have a lock that could malfunction so all looked great.That night it turned very cold and our room had mainly outside walls . We fiddled with the AC to find some heat with no luck and just put some clothes on in bed as there was no extra bedding in the room.We should have phoned down but desperately needed sleep.When I asked for blankets the next day I was told that the heating was not on "because of the date" Late October in New York is never cold one assumes.Strangly enough the heating came on full blast the next day when we had piled more bedding on but for the rest of our stay we enjoyed the room in spite of the traffic noise which, again, being on a corner was considerable.
 The rooms are furnished in an attractive Moroccan style and the bed was comfortable.The decor in the cafe and bar is atmospheric and the staff are generally friendly.The Bar lounge is a very popular place to be in this area of Manhattan and we felt that priority is given to this rather than the resident guests.The cocktails we had were disappointing and overpriced and the food in the cafe a bit a patchy as our first meal was stone cold.
If we were young and wanted to dance all night and then stagger to our room at 5am it would be great but for value the tiny single rooms are obviously the best value for budget travellers and we did no feel that we had any sort of bargain with our Captain's cabin although we got 20% off our first night for the noise. 
The neighborhood is great and we preferred the quirkiness of The Jane to usual chain hotel blandness. The management seems a bit haphazard though and there were moments when we thought longingly of the Ibis at Heathrow where you can get a good night's sleep in a nice room for under £50 with a kettle .
I would say that unless you are traveling with someone who needs a single room, as we were, then budget wise it might be better to get a late offer somewhere else.The location would not be as good probably ,decor not so interesting and the trip not so memorable but it would not be quite so much a matter of luck if you got a good room or not. In spite of this I would say it made our trip to New York more interesting and I am glad we chose it.

name: The Helmsley Park Lane
title: “FANTASTIC!!!”
text: My daughter and I just spent five days in NYC celebrating her recent high school graduation. I read many reviews after booking our trip and have to say I began to get a little worried! Some of the reviews of this hotel were not very complimentary. Our trip was perfect. The Helmsley was perfectly located and had the old New York charm. Our view from the 10th floor was breathtaking. Central Park was beautiful. The doormen greeted us and were more than helpful. The check in was painless and they allowed us to go to our room as soon as we arrived (9:30 am). We were thrilled as check in isn't until three. The room was very clean and huge! I would encourage anyone to stay at the Helmsley!
