It is an older hotel and the furnishings do border on being antique. The area is not as congested as Times Square and every thing you need or want to do is in walking distance. We only took a taxi to the airport and the subway to Soho. Enjoy your stay!!! We can't wait to go back!! We LOVE New York!

name: Park Central
title: “hotel tres bien”
text: hotel proche de s grandes avenue tre propre et confortable .dommage que le resto de l hotel sois cher .exemple petit dejeuner buffet froid avec cafe tre bon mais 21 dollar.et cherrcher des restos vers manathan beaucoup moins cher.exemp 7 av.2wap geanr +2 verrre de vin 75dolar..manathan 9 av+2 dessert 56dollar .

name: Park Central
title: “Park Central Hotel New York”
text:
La chambre était propre, grande et très confortable. Dommage qu'elle donnait sur une cour intérieure avec un grand mur gris juste en face. De ce fait la chambre était sombre et il fallait allumer les lampes toute la journée. Heureusement nous ne passons pas nos journées dans la chambre.
Au point de vue service, nous avons téléphoné depuis notre chambre à la réception pour demander que quelqu'un vienne réparer notre coffre qui ne fermait pas. Bien que la réceptionniste ait dit qu'elle nous envoyait quelqu'un, nous n'avons jamais vu personne et notre coffre n'a jamais été réparé.
Autre point négatif : les longues files d'attente à la réception.
Sinon l'hôtel est bien placé et surtout très calme car nous n'entendions aucun bruit depuis notre chambre.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Perfect for our NYC wedding”
text: This is my 5th time staying at grand Hyatt NYC and without doubt the best! Since it was our wedding trip we came from Ireland for our july 26th wedding. The check in was fantastic really friendly and I think the receptionists name was Lsaura she made it very welcoming. We had a corner room and it gave us lots of space for all our wedding stuff. Didn't eat at the hotel but had drinks which was good. Rooms spotless and tastefully decorated. I think this hotel is a real manhattan experience and would recommend to everyone .

name: Thompson LES - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Very clean hotel in chic part of town...”
text: Very clean hotel in chic part of town lots of great restaurants close by & in hotel the sushi is great. Hotel staff were very helpful and the views from the bar on the 7 th floor is one of the best

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “very poor service”
text:
I am a Platinum member of the Hyatt rewards program because I have nothing to complain about Hyatt hotels, but my feelings have changed after a very poor experience with the Grand Hyatt New York.
Sam at the check-in counter made a huge mess of my check-in experience. First, he checked me into 2 imaginary rooms - rooms that did not exist. Second, he gave me key cards that didn't work. The other check-in staff insisted that it was the correct room and to follow their "directions". Only when I said that such a room does not exist did they stop to think and to check. When they finally admitted their mistake, they gave me the correct room, but now the key cards didn't work! Lastly, the hotel failed to note down that I wanted my 2 rooms on the same floor, and the same general area as I was travelling as a family, even though I had specially called the reservations line the day before to inform them about my request.
When I finally made it to my room, I found that the room door handle inside the room was broken. I notified housekeeping who assured me that they will send someone to fix it. 2 days later and it was still not fixed.
I told the check-out staff of my poor check-in experience but they didn't care less. 
I hope the Pritzker family does something to protect their good name.

name: ONE UN New York
title: “WOW VIEW”
text:
This was the hotel we chose for our honeymoon. Very nice, not the best we stayed (check my Loews Santa Monica review if you want to see what i like) - but clean, confortable and with views to die for!
Nice hotel in center, good balance quality - money.
Btw the Honeymoon was perfect and we loved every minute.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Un hotel que en España no dejarian mantener abierto”
text:
Despues de las largas horas de vuelo, aeropuertos, transfers, aduanas, etc... llegamos al hotel con ansias de llegar a nuestra habitación y estirarnos en la cama.. y sobretodo de una ducha. La entrada, por cierto enorme, nos parece enorme y la primera impresión es buena. Vamos al mostrador de recepción para hacer nuestro ingreso y cual es nuestra sorpresa cuando tal y como si estuvieramos en Port Aventura, una cinta va indicando el orden en la cola.... delante nuestro al menos hay 20 o más personas y van llegando y llegando. En el mostrador al menso trabajan 8-10 personas (alucinamos) solo ingresando huespedes!!! Sabiamos que era uno de los 5 hoteles más grandes de NY, peró tanto!!!!!!!!!.
Habiamos reservado cama de matrimonio porqué era más económico y la chica que nos atiende dice: que si nos parece mal ponernos en una de 2 camas (pensamos que al ser más cara estaria mejor... que no perdiamos nada), nos dan las llaves y solas con nuestras maletas a buscar ascensores (al menos hay 10) y a la caza y captura de la habitación 351 (en un hotel de más de 1700 habitaciones).
Por logica, bajamos del ascensor en el piso 3 y cual es nuestra sorpresa al ver el hall de la planta 3..................... cochambroso, oscuro, paredes despintadas, humedades, viejo, manchas de no sabes que en la alfombra... cogemos y intentamos buscar la 351, però es como un laberinto (no sigue un orden normal de numeración) vamos de pasillo en pasillo y viendo esas paredes de mal en peor, poca luz (cada vez menos), las puertas de las habitaciones desconchadas, agujereadas, peladas... peró eso si se abren con tarjeta. Por fin llegamos a la 351 y al abrir la puerta.........brrrrrrrrrrr un frio helado, una habitación inmensa peró igual de "cutre" que los pasillos, paredes con humedad, antiguo todo, sin TV, el armario es una pequeña habitación toda cochambrosa y tenemos 2 puertas cerradas (una en la entrada y otra dentro de esta habitacion-armario) que suponemos que comunica con otras habitaciones. Optamos por no sacar nada de las maletas y ir corriendo a comprar RAID para matar a cualquier ser viviente que pudiera circular por allí. El baño no tiene luz y es más antiguo que "Matusalén" y en la bañera grietas enormes que supongo que la habitación de abajo se duchaba al mismo tiempo que nosotras..... Un esperpento de hotel.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Very roomy and well appointed”
text: We only spent one night at the Parker Meridien and we found our recently remodeled room to be very well concieved: roomy, contemporary but warm styling, very comfortable bedding and a convenient place for every item (a rarity in city hotel rooms). We had a lovely, romantic 19th floor cityscape view toward Central Park. Of course, the hotel is also well located, near to theaters and fifth Avenue, but without the hubub of the theater district. We opened the window for the night and there was hardly even any traffic noise! We didn't have a chance to see it, but were told by another guest that there is a very attractive swimming pool at the top of the hotel. Tried unsuccessfully to get into Norma's for breakfast. Since we were able to book the room with Starwood points, even better!

name: Thompson LES - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Great deal for a hip hotel in NYC”
text: I was looking for a hotel with an outdoor pool because I was there during July. Few hotels in NYC have outdoor pools, and the other ones that I found were outrageously expensive. The Thompson LES was a good price and I love the LES. The hotel staff was friendly and accommodating. The pool gets crowded in late afternoon so get there early.

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Great views, ok rooms and service”
text: Stayed on a recent trip as my preferred hotel was booked out. The views from my room were amazing and the room itself was grand, about average for Manhattan. The fitness centre was good with extended hours which helped. Location is good even if the street is a little dark and creepy.

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “gute Lage, Preis-Leistung OK”
text: Das Travel Inn liegt nur wenige Fuss-Minuten vom Times Squere entfernt und ist somit mit der U-Bahn gut erreichbar. Das Zimmer war für einen Städtetrip ausreichend groß und sehr sauber. Das Personal ist freundlich. Was fehlt ist eine Bar. Das Frühstück nimmt man außer Haus ein, in New York ist das aber kein großes Problem da im Umkreis von 5 Minuten genug Lokale dafür zu finden sind. Alles in Allem würden wir wieder dort buchen.

name: Park Central
title: “Flott hotell med fin beliggenhet”
text: Hotellet ligger kort vei fra times square, central park og det meste av teater. Fin standard på hotellrommene og flott lobby. Starbucks på hjørnet og Subway tvers over gaten gjør det lett å få seg frokost, og det er nok av resturanter å velge i rundt hotellet.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Stay at the Millennium”
text:
I just got back from a great four-day stay at the Millennium. I had a corner room overlooking Times Square. I've read some of the rather negative reviews, so was a bit apprehensive, especially since 4 of my friends were joining me there, based on my research. We all had a great time, although I had the best room. (Party central!) It's a fabulous location and we all experienced wonderful service, from the front desk, concierge, and cleaning staff. Actually, the only negative thing was the fact the ice machine on my floor was broken and I had to go to the next level to fill the bucket. Not a big deal. I would recommend this hotel to anyone! I booked on hotels and got a really good rate. 
One tip: don't waste your time or money going to the View at the Marriot Marquis. The drinks were awful and expensive and the "view" was no better than I had from my room. It's not on the rooftop of the hotel and you spend a lot of time looking into boring offices as it rotates around.

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Disappointing”
text: Beware of being offered upgrade. Standard room with two double beds was upgraded to "Superior" room with 1 x king size. Assumed room would have sofa bed for daughter only to find travel bed which when opened meant not able to walk around the room or use drawers. Room was drab at bed and located close to elevator and ice machine which prooved very noisy due to 2 inch gap under the door. When complained was told no other rooms available despite booking family room. Felt let down.

name: Hotel Gansevoort
title: “Loved the pool side bar”
text: The pool is lovely especially in summer. Great to hang out there.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Stylish, Great Serivce, Fab Location”
text:
Stayed here for two nights on a business trip and had a fantastic time. 
I had a junior suite without the park view on the 38th floor (there are 42 floors). View over central park was AMAZING from the lobby of this floor - definitely try for park view if you can.
Junior suite was large with spacious living area and large bedroom area, divided by rotating TV unit. Bathroom was utlra-modern with wall-length walk-in shower cubicle and ample space.
Room service breakfast was quick and tasty with lots of options (not cheap mind you). The hotel were very quick in responding to all of my requests for assistance, including opening my bathroom door when I managed to jam it shut!
I didn't use the pool or gym but hear that my colleagues were pleased with the facilities.
Location is fantastic - one block from central park, one block from Abercrombie and a subway stop close by should you be using that mode of transport.
Also, during my stay a very high profile policitician was also staying - and if it's good enough for him, it's definitely good enough for me!

name: Doubletree Hotel Chelsea New York City
title: “Priced Right”
text: The price was right for our family. This is a newly built property with nice comfy beds and flat screen TV. It's location is somewhat out of the way from majot tourist attractions however there are two subway stations within an easy walk. Highly reccomended as the hotel is new and clean. Not a lot of ammenities but if you're on the go who needs all that anyways.

name: Thompson LES - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Not a flawless stay @ the Thompson LES but manager handled it well...”
text:
My girlfriend and I booked the thompson hoping to have a romantic weekend in NYC but when we arrived at 5pm and were told that the room was not ready, i thought this is off to a bad start. The manager apologized for the inconvenience and offered us a drink at the bar while we waited. It took about 20 min to get our room so we enjoyed our drink while we waited...
Once we got the room, we were happy with the overall look. Its very trendy, dark, and romantic. Also, quite new which is good.
The next day, we left the hotel around 9am and returned around 5pm. To our surprise, the room had not been cleaned. We called the front desk and the manager who offered us the drink was working so i informed her of the situation. They sent us fresh towels right away and i requested to have the room cleaned once we left the room for our dinner. This was done. 
Besides these two incidents, we liked the hotel overall. It has a nice look to it, nice spa and gym, and the manager did handle the situation appropriately in my opinion. I would give the hotel another chance... Hope this helps.

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “Maravilhoso”
text: Os quartos e o hotel são limpíssimos!O atendimento é ótimo,fomos atendidos na hora quando precisamos.A localização é muito boa,em frente situa-se o departamento de polícia,na mesma quadra tem um mercado muito prático e é muito perto da Broadway,fomos aos show a pé!Recomendo!!

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Ask for a room above 25th floor”
text:
On a recent trip to NYC, my husband had a function to attend at this hotel. We actually turned the trip into a family vacation and chose to stay the majority of the time at a less expensive hotel (see related reviews in NYC of the SoHotel) and only spent one night here. We booked to attend a conference, but they were out of the conference-priced rooms, so we were not able to be placed with the others attending the conference (which turned out to be a blessing because of the spirited activity of the late into the night festivities). I recommend that you ask for a room on a higher floor for this reason unless you don't mind the conferencers roaming the halls all through the night on the floors below the 25th.
This hotel's lobby is beautiful. The hotel bar is nice and serves very good cocktails. There is a open kitchen style restaurant in the lobby beside the bar and also a grab and go market that has beverages and snack foods (see related review).
Check-in was fast, friendly and efficient. After a 3 minute wait with the only two desk clerks busy a little before the actual check-in time, a man from the VIP check-in came out to help me. He was very helpful, fast, and pleasant.
There are 10 elevators that take you up to your room with the furthest 5 from the check-in desk going to the 25th and higher floors, and the 5 closest to check-in going to the lower floors. I believe all elevators go to the banquet level. This was a little confusing in practice, however, and twice we found ourselves on the wrong elevator.
The room itself (a double double) was a big hit with our kids who loved the dramatic purple decor and full wall mural and the electronic lighting switches. Our other hotel was great but not luxurious, and the kids said this was their idea of what a NYC hotel should look like (I personally preferred the hominess at the other hotel). I did love this hotel's bath and its amenities. It had waterfall tub and sink fixtures, a rain shower fixture and a full bath tub. The bath products, white ginger by portico, were also very luxurious. The toilet however was loud enough to make you think that you were about to take off at Laguardia's airport.
The beds were another story. They looked good on platforms, but were very small and uncomfortable. I might not have noticed this except we had just come from a lot less expensive hotel where the beds were queens, not doubles, and were super comfortable.
The location is a good one too if you want to be near Grand Central Station, in mid-town and close to most of the tourist destinations.
I would probably stay here again if I had not already found the place I want to stay if I return to the city.

name: The Helmsley Park Lane
title: “Aging but still the Queen of Park Lane”
text: Had a wonderful stay mid-February for four days. We used to stay here often 10 years ago but had not done so in the last five years. Spacious rooms overlooking the Central Park, excellent service all around and very central location for all our interests reminded us what we have missed lately. Yes, the rooms and technologies may not at par with more modern hotels but at least for us, the above mentioned qualities definitely outweigh these minor concerns!

name: The Hotel at Times Square
title: “perfect”
text: after trawling the internet looking for something that wasn't a large corporate hotel and was reasonably priced we came across this small hotel minutes from Times Square. it was perfect. our room had 2 queen size beds, aircon and a clean and well functioning bathroom. the staff were helpful, there were free computers to use in the reception area and a great breakfast included. the price was very reasonable. my sister and i were travelling with my 12 year old daughter....we all loved the hotel.

name: Larchmont Hotel
title: “Piccolo è bello?”
text:
L'hotel è un delizioso piccolo palazzo nella zona del west village più tranquilla e romantica, non costoso per il luogo in cui è ubicato, davvero centrale e comodo per visitare downtown Manhattan.
La stanza al primo piano era piccola, anche se non scomoda. Il bagno in comune è pulito. Ci hanno tenuto i bagagli tutto il giorno e alla sera ci hanno lasciato utilizzare il bagno della zona comune dopo la nostra giornata in giro, anche se avevamo già effettuato il check out, sono stati tutti molto gentili.

name: Park Central
title: “bello ma...”
text: L'hotel Park Central si trova in posizione ottimale. La camera che ci è stata assegnata aveva due grandi letti ma la richiesta di avere un letto matrimoniale, essendo in viaggio di nozze, è stata acccolta è ci è stata assegnata un'altra camera. La camera non era molto grande e la pulizia approssimativa soprattutto nel bagno, in cui non venivano rimessi i prodotti di cortesia. Il costo dell'albergo molto elevato, senza colazione. I bagagli si possono lasciare ma al costo di 3,75 dollari a bagaglio, anche solo per qualche ora. In camera il rumore era continuo causato da un termoventilatore.Molto bello il televisore 42 pollici. Il personale gentile e disponibile. Magari spostandosi di qualche street si potrebbe trovare qualcosa di meno caro,,,

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Adequate”
text: Just came back this morning from NYC. Like the others I was slightly nervous about the hotel, however, I really have no complaints. Don't expect to be sleeping on silk sheets or anything of the like. However, this hotel's location cannot be beat, seconds from Times Square. You literally walk out the front door, turn to your right and are in the middle of it all. I would recommend this hotel strongly, location is key. In NYC you aren't going to be doing much other than sleeping in your room anyway. Bathroom and room are fairly small but it's good enough, a nice clean, affordable place to stay near Times Square.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Modern, clean, great location”
text: We were upgraded to a Deluxe King room. The size was decent, for NYC standards. The room and bathroom were clean, and up to date. The beds are super comfortable. There was a mini fridge and personal safe in the room. My only complaint is that there was no coffee maker in the room. From reading other reviews, I heard that they offer free coupons for coffee at their coffee shop, but this was not offered to us. In any case, I think people would appreciate a coffee maker in the room, instead of having to go down to the lobby.

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Still just as great the second time!”
text: This was my second time staying at Millenium UN Plaza hotel. The hotel is great and the staff is very friendly and accommodating. It is not too far from the city. If you like walking not a problem at all. My girlfriend only wears heels so we didn't walk to the heart of the city. Beautiful view. Security in fron of the building made me feel safe. Concierge held our luggage after we checked so we could go out on the town until our plane left. AMAZING!

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Poor Security - Poor Service”
text: Booked a room online for a one night stay on Saturday night in November. Requested A 2:30 pm check in time. Arrived at 3 pm and was given a room. Put the key in the door, opened the door, were greeted by another couple ALREADY IN THE ROOM. They screamed, we screamed, apologized, then went back downstairs. The front desk asked if we wanted to check in. After explaining that we already did, they apologized but told us there were no more rooms ready yet, and to check back after 4pm. We went back an hour later (were asked by the same desk person if we were there to check-in) and were given another room with apologies and assurances that this room was ready and unoccupied. Went to the room, opened the door, and it was a mess and currently occupied by a service person. At this point my wife was very concerned for her security at this hotel and we decided to book another room elsewhere. We went to the front desk, explained what happened, and asked for a refund. We were informed that because we booked online, we weren't able to get one. To their credit they did offer a suite at the same price, but we already booked another non-refundable room. After the assistant manager refused to give us our money back we saw the manager who agreed. Weeks went by with no refund. I called back to see what happened to my refund and was told that the "General Manager" overruled the manager and decided we shouldn't get our money back. Very poor service and customer treatment for rooms that are not inexpensive at $600-$700 a night.

name: Travel Inn Hotel New York
title: “Excellent plan pour séjourner à NY”
text: Très bon rapport qualité-prix pour NY, spécialement pour cet hotel très bien tenu et propre, qui est situé (42nd st West)idéalement très près de Times Square. Chambres 2 lits doubles plutôt spacieuses. Très calme et sécurisant, et pour cause car il est situé en face d'un commissariat local de NYPD, qui heureusement n'abuse pas des sirènes... Nous y retournerions sans problème. point négatif: WIFI payant, 6.00 USD l'heure...

name: Park Central
title: “posizione eccellente”
text:
posizione eccellente, camere piani alti spazione (nella media di nyc), pulite. Tv, accesso internet (a pagamento), caffe' complimentary. Colazione in htl sconsiglita xke' molto cara. Nelle vicinaze ci sono moltissimi locali dove fare ottima colazione a costi abbordabili. personale cordiale.
camere al piano 8 disastrose. cercate sempre di farvi assegnare camere dal 24mo piano in su.

name: Ramada Eastside
title: “Good”
text: The room was clean & functional. Worth its price !

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “New York City Sizzler trip”
text:
My Wife and I stayed at the Grand Hyatt New York on June29&30 2012 with some friends.
They had a special running for $199/night which is a great price for New York City.
 The location is great being a few blocks away from Times Square. We found the
check in to be an easy experience as the staff were friendly and we had an early check in.
We were given coupons for free coffee or bottled water which is a nice perk since coffee
is over $3.00 at the snack bar they have. The rooms were very clean and the cleaning staff
were very friendly when I asked for extra towels.
 The only negatives were the charge for the wireless internet connection and the fact
that the room could have been cooler even though it was set at the lowest temp. of 65 degrees.
It was very hot that week end though as the outside temperature was 95 degrees.
 All in all I would stay there again especially if I could get the same room rate.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Muy buen hotel”
text:
El hotel es Antiguo, pero muy bien mantenido. La habitación siempre estuvo limpia y en condiciones. Es cierto que la habitación es "chica", pero tiene el lugar necesario para una estadia corta. La atención fue correcta y el checkin bastante rápido (20 minutos). 
La ubicación es EXCELENTE!, podes ir caminando a todos lados. Muy recomendable.

name: The Jane
title: “Quirky little hotel - great location, great bar, great cafe, but very small rooms!”
text:
My mom and I had a wonderful stay @ The Jane. We really enjoyed the quirky atmosphere of the hotel and had a great time at the bar and Cafe Gitane. We stayed in a bunk bed room with shared bath. The only down side to our stay was not being able to get ready or "hang out" in the room at the same time -- the room was too small. And, also, there was some "weird" stuff going on in the shared coed bathroom at one point -- an older gentleman seemingly making tuna fish? Hmmmm. Odd. The bathrooms were clean overall, but I definitely wish they had provided us with waterproof shower shoes rather than cotton slippers. The robes also could have been a bit bigger/longer since we had to walk thru the halls in them.
But, that being said, we really enjoyed The Jane and I would be inclined to stay there again -- especially if I was traveling solo. The rooms are affordable and the bar was great fun -- awesome, albeit expensive, drinks -- but really cool atmosphere! Cafe Gitane was also spectacular!
Definitely "borrow" some bikes when you visit -- take a ride down the river trail. Great fun!

name: Thompson LES - A Thompson Hotel
title: “great place”
text:
I stayed at LES for 5 nights from Jan06 to Jan11. The hotel is new, I like the rooms a lot, we had a phantastic view towards Washington Bridge with a breathtaking sunrise to be seen from bed.
Everybody working there was really helpful and friendly. 
The bar is open now as well and although they told us that they had not done much marketing yet it seems that the guests are not only from the hotel.
Some very nice restaurants in walking distance.

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Nice view, nothing else”
text:
It has a nice view to the south Manhattan and quite nice rooms. 
Sauna and pool and gym are complimentary... good!
Down side: they carge you 13 USD for the internet connection
No breakfast

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “Great Hotel - Would stay again”
text:
Stayed here 27 -31 Jan and loved it! 
 Fab location, gorgeous room, great bar and friendly staff.
 Delicious cookie on arrival too!

name: Thompson LES - A Thompson Hotel
title: “great weekend!”
text:
This is a great hotel with kind staff members and fabo amenities. I recently stayed here with my friends for the weekend while in town celebrating a 30th birthday. We picked this hotel primarily due to location and it's proximity to our activiites, but I was pleasantly surprised at well we were treated. The staff at the front desk was very accommadating to our needs, very knowlegable about the area, and they were prompt to help us with anything we asked for. 
We were upgraded to a king suite which was modern, clean, and spacious. We had huge windows with a corner balcony, which was much needed because the weather In NYC in August is so nice. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay here. We will definitely be back!

name: Hotel Gansevoort
title: “Awesome Location”
text: Whether you are staying at the hotel with or without your family, the hotel is located in a great part of NYC. Convenient to excellent restaurants and clubs, it's perfect for those wanting that fun night out in the city and all within walking distance. ONO, the restaurant located on the property, had a great ambience and fresh food. The rooftop bar is a great place to hang out and have cocktails if you don't feel like going out. Traveling w/my family worked out well because the hotel is pet-friendly and the neighborhood is too! My 2-year old had a blast because of the roof top pool as well as the easy walk to local playgrounds. We would definitely visit again!

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Not a 4 Star Hotel”
text: Not awful but absolutely not 4 star quality or service. The room was standard (bathrooms could use some updating) and the location was good. We ordered room service for breakfast one morning. It took over an hour, one breakfast was completely forgotten causing an additional 40 minute wait. The woman taking our order barely spoke english which resulted in NOT ONE of our 3 omlettes prepared as they were ordered. They were also clearly made with powdered eggs and tasted horrible. For $170 breakfast, we at least expected it to be edible.

name: Hudson New York
title: “Hip und klein”
text:
Das Hudson Hotel am Columbus Circle ist sicherlich eines der hipsten und stylischsten Hotels in dem ich je gewohnt habe. Der Empfang ist zugleich der Eingang zum Hudson Club und ist an sich schon eine Sehenswürdigkeit New Yorks. Das Hotel ist von Philippe Stark designed - und das ist wirklich in jedem Eck des Hotels zu sehen. 
Leider muss man für das Design, die Lage und den Preis extrem kleine Zimmer in Kauf nehmen. Zu zweit sind die standard Doppelzimmer fast zu klein um sich zu bewegen.

name: Hudson New York
title: “On y retournera pas”
text:
Nous avons fais 4 jours dans cet hôtel, cher pour ce qu'ils proposent.
Certes, très très bien situé, proche de Time Square, et de Central Park, mais alors les chambres franchement. MINUSCULE !!! rare sont les placards, la salle de bains est tellement petite que cela en est ridicule. Comment mettre une douche, un lavabo, et des wc dans 3 m2 !!!! 
La déco super sympa, car Starck et tout l'hotel aussi quoique trop sombre à mon goût. 
On avait réservé cette chambre 5 mois à l'avance, et on nous a mis au 4ème étage. Un bruit pas possible pendant la nuit, nous savons que New York est très bruyant et en perpétuel mouvement mais ....
Autre chose : le bruit de leur climatisation. Impossible de dormir.
Le personnel est peu souriant, peu sympa et pas du tout arrangeante. Ne pas prendre son petit déjeuner là, car bcp trop cher. Il y a des endroits à Breakfast partout. 
Chose sûre, nous n'y retournerons pas.....

name: The Helmsley Park Lane
title: “Love the view! Can't get a better place for the price on Central Park”
text: We have come to this hotel 4 times now. Staff always nice and I love that I can bring my dog. The location can't be beat. We were so close to the Macy's day parade...just walked out the 58th side and got a great view.

name: Murray Hill East Suites
title: “A for location, F for everything else.”
text:
I stayed here to attend a conference nearby. The price and location were great. Everything else was not so great. This must have been an old studio apartment building that has been repurposed as a hotel. Everything smelled of stale cigarettes both in my room and in the common areas. I never unpacked my suitcase during my stay, just to try and keep my clothes from absorbing that smell. It didn't work. 
My room was 100% 1980's decor. That's a long time to go without any remodelling.

name: Murray Hill East Suites
title: “Great location and value”
text: We stayed here on the final phase of our epic trip. A great location being near to grand central so handy for NYC sightseeing. We had a one bedroomed suite with kitchen (enormous!) and very comfy sofa bed.very nice staff they kept our bags until 4. Wifi reliable and lovely shower.kitchen had lots of utensils but we kept getting take away food from fantastic local delis - every food imaginable. Airport buse are a few minutes away I wish we were there now.

name: Hotel Gansevoort
title: “Great visit to the Big Apple”
text: It was a great hotel. From the moment we arrived the staff was helpful and courteous. We were travelling with two young children and they were made to feel quite at home for our weekend stay. Check in was quick and room was very comfortable. Hotel is very close, 2 blocks from the nearest subway which made travelling around the city quite easy. Neighborhood gets a little noisy and lively at night, but it is the city that never sleeps. Overall a wonderful experience, would gladly stay there again. If only they put little chocolates on your pillow when they turned down your bed it would be a complete fantasy getaway.

name: Park Central
title: “situation exceptionnelle”
text:
Hotel confortable, nous étions au 4e étage donc pas de soucis d'ascenseur et de bruit. La chambre était suffisante pour 3, les lits confortables. Nous avons pris le petit déjeuner à l'extérieur car les environs fourmillent d'endroits ou manger. Le personnel est disponible même si la barrière de la langue se fait sentir. Toutefois, James de la conciergerie nous a aidé pour appeler l'aéroport afin de récupérer nos bagages perdus.
Nous choisirons à nouveau cet hôtel pour notre prochain séjour

name: Hotel Gansevoort
title: “Posizione felicissima”
text: Questa sistemazione offre innanzitutto un'ottima posizione, si trova nel Meatpacking District, una delle zone più chic e trendy di New York, piena di locali cool e ristoranti. Le camere seguono le linee della catena, sobrie e moderne ma in questo caso un po' piccoline. Molto bello il roof con la piscina, sarà piacevolissimo d'estate. Consigliato.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Picky Perfectionist rates Edison high”
text: If you want to be in the thick of Times Square action this is for you. Art Deco. Felt safe there. Restaurant a "polish t room". Rooms with two double beds bigger than typical NYC hotel room that is for sure. Lots of elevators--don't have to wait for long. Also a bar. Convenience store two doors down for beverages and snacks helped too. Across the street from a theatre. Bathrooms small but full tub. Air conditioning good. No bravo channel on tv. Stayed on 9th floor to avoid early morning street noise. Tiny bit of mildew in bath tub area but not enough to make me stay somewhere else. Be prepared for the crowds in Times Square! ATM in lobby. A gift shop. Payphones in lobby. Lobby has a thing where you can check your home email for $1.00 for 5 minutes. Have to pay 50cents for a bucket of ice. The restaurant will put an automatic 15% gratuity on your check but if you call them on it they will cheerfully take it off. We searched the internet for hours and are glad we stayed here and would stay there again. We had a guaranteed ns reservation and checked in very late and ended up being put in a smoking room but it wasn't bad. Activating phone for local calls takes $50 so we didn't do it but still could get voice mail messages. Sounded like a rip off to activate it so we didn't.

name: The Jane
title: “Great for someone travelling alone”
text: This is a great hotel for someone who is travelling alone, because the rooms (the majority if not all) are for one. Great location in greenwich just below 14th street, the staff very nice, and for New York, great price. I recommend it to anyone travelling by themselves.

name: Loews Regency Hotel
title: “You pay for what you get”
text: This is by far and away one of my best upscale hotel choices. The cost makes regular visits prohibitive but if you can get a deal or want to splurge for an occasion this is where to stay in NYC. Great location on Park Ave. Not in center of thngs but close enough.

name: Loews Regency Hotel
title: “Beware: Oversold led to an upsell”
text:
We stayed at the Loews Regency NYC from August 10-14, 2012, and used the Summer 4 Suites promotion. We have a 7 year old and a 1 year old and liked the idea of the Loews for Kids program. We booked a king one bedroom suite with an adjoining superior twin room. Upon check-in, the adjoining room wasn't ready. At 9pm, the adjoining room still wasn't available, so they open a second adjoining room. When we walked in the room, the carpet was wet and the entire room reeked of cleaning fluid. We were told that the carpet would need to be shampooed the following day and we'd have to leave. Obviously, this was unacceptable. We were told this room was the only one available and so I requested that the Loews walk us to another hotel. Instead, the Loews upsold us to a VIP suite. The Loews told us basically it was our problem that we weren't happy with a room with wet carpet. Housekeeping acknowledged that this room wasn't fit for occupancy, but the front desk offered us the ONLY other option - to move to a rarely used VIP suite (for an additional $1000) - a permanent resident lives on the floor and we were told doesn't like to be bothered, and this suite is the only other room on the floor. Not exactly VIP treatment to be asked to walk on egg shells.
Throughout all of the above, I was stranded in the airport 500 miles away (JFK had closed) while my wife and kids were in the hotel. It was 9pm when the room with wet carpet was opened and with two tired kids, the options were limited. I didn't get to the hotel until 2am.
The Loews didn't honor our original reservation and beyond that gave us a room that would never been given to a guest walking in off the street. They took the opportunity to upsell us when they should have either upgraded us or walked us to another hotel. It was insulting to be given a room in that condition with wet carpet and reeking of cleaning fluid and then be told it was our problem we weren't happy with it.
It's a shame too because it's a lovely hotel and a great location. But the problems with the adjoining room (and the room with the wet carpet was given to us instead of the room we originally reserved) and that the hotel chose to upsell instead of upgrade makes me not want to go back or recommend this property.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Absolutely Not 4****!!!”
text:
The room furnishings were not what I think are attractive, a little IKEA ' ish looking. The platform bed and mattress were extremely uncomfortable. My husband and I got very little sleep, because we were sleeping on such a horrible mattress The Air Conditioner could not be lowered to my comfort level, I had set it on 65 degrees, but the room temp never got above 74. I asked maintance to come up and look at it, but it didn't help. It was very hot and humid, so when I was in my room I had hoped to get relief. I think I could have done much better at another hotel for the money I spent on a night here
.

name: Ramada Eastside
title: “buonissimo hotel a 2 passi dal centro”
text: Abbiamo alloggiato in questo hotel per 5 notti durante le feste di Pasqua. Ci siamo trovati veramente bene, le stanze come il bagno non sono grandissime, ma sono più che sufficienti tanto servono solo per dormire la notte! Si può scegliere tra fumatori e non fumatori la colazione è compresa cosa che a New York non è facile trovare, ed è abbondante, frutta, cereali, latte, yogurt ecc ecc non manca nulla. Internet è accessibile sia wii- fi che da pc fisso senza costi aggiuntivi. Ottima la posizione, zona tranquilla e a pochi passi dal centro. Anche il personale è sempre disponibile per qualsiasi informazione. Dovessimo tornare a New York torneremo ancora al Ramada Eastside!

name: Loews Regency Hotel
title: “Great location and clean, spacious rooms!”
text:
My husband and I had a very nice stay here in April. The location is great (within walking distance of Central park and Times Square) and the rooms are quite spacious and clean. In fact, our room even had a kitchenette! This is very uncommon in hotel rooms in New York City. The beds were soft and comfortable. The rooms were quiet and we never heard any other guests from our room. Every staff member that we encountered was pleasant 
 An unusual feature of this hotel is that they are pet friendly! We saw many guests with their dogs in the lobby and we confirmed with the front desk that it is a pet friendly hotel. They even have "bring your pet" packages that include things like dog treats and dog beds. They are also kid friendly and have "American Girl" packages that include amenities for your child's dolls.
The only downside I could identify for this hotel is that they charge $14.95 for internet access. I thought that was quite high and decided just to use my iPhone for any Internet usage I needed.

name: The Jane
title: “The Jane Hotel - Prisvärt hotell i kanonläge”
text:
The Jane Hotel är ett mycket prisvärt hotell med ett perfekt läge nära Meat Packing District i New York. Rummen med Bunk Beds är trånga men fungerar bra för att sova i och att förvara sina saker i då man är ute på upptäckarstrået.
Toalett och dusch är renstädade, men för dig som inte gillar att dela sådana utrymmen med andra är inte detta boendet för dig.
Det är något lyhört, men AC-anläggningen dränker effektivt alla andra ljud.
Restaurangen i bottenplan är en pärla, och vi kan starkt rekommendera deras frukokstmeny.
I bottenplan finns även en nattklubb som kan uppfattas som störande för ljudkänsliga.
Omgivningen med de låga byggnaderna och de lummiga gatorna är en liten oas i New Yorks annars häktiska miljöer.
En sak till: New Yorks taxichaufförer hittar inte till 113 Jane Street. Åk till Meat Packing och promenera de sista kvarteren.

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Great time”
text:
i read many reviews and it seems all based on what you are looking for, we had a great time in this hotel, we came to visit NY city and needed a nice clean place centrally located to come back to after a long day of fun time in the city.
pros:
VIEW, what a view you can't go to sleep
bed, large and comfortable
size, the room is quite large not NY style
TV, big flat LCD
cons:
bathroom, could use some touch
subway, about 5 min from there (seems a lot after a whole day outside)
Internet, with charge
we didn't use the hotel facilities at all so I can't tell much, when we arrived (7am) there was no room ready and they offered to refresh at the fitness center, we came back at noon got a room with a view to the east river and changed it to a city view.
true, the rooms aren't the top of the art but just look outside the window and you forget all about it (rooms start from floor 28 so I guess all rooms have great view).
for a 160 (without tax) per night I think this is a very good deal for NYC.
hope it was helpfull :-)

name: W New York - Downtown
title: “Perfect For Downtown”
text:
W Hotels are known for their great service, and this one was no exception. The employees were friendly, rooms were stylish (as usual) and the hotel was very clean. Location-wise, this hotel worked well for us as most of our activities were in the downtown area, but it was pretty far down and for a tourist, it might be more practical to stay closer to Soho or Tribeca near good shops and restaurants. Walking around the construction to get to the subway stops was kind of a hassle.
Speaking of construction, the noise was a non-issue for us and we were right in front looking down on the site. I was worried we might wake up to the sound of jackhammers, but it didn't happen. What we did wake up to was the sound of our neighbors turning on their TV at 3:30 AM. I think they had a baby who wouldn't go to sleep and were trying to drown out the baby with the TV. I was never able to gauge whether they had the TV very loud or if the walls were just really thin, but that part of the stay was unpleasant. 
The other concern was that The W would feel like hipsterville. Not the case. There was a perfect mix of trendy people, tourists and business types, so we felt right at home.

name: W New York - Downtown
title: “Best hotel to stay in New York”
text:
Our family drove to New York City over the Memorial Day weekend. We wanted to stay in the Tribeca/Financial District and after searching for and reading the reviews for hotels in the area, we decided on the W New York (Downtown). In a word - Outstanding! Because of the reconstruction of the buildings in and around ground zero, there is a bit of a challenge to get to the front door, but once there, we were very happy with our choice. We were whisked up to the fifth floor for our check-in and Andrew (at the front desk) was very helpful to us. Check-in (for our two adjoining rooms) was a pleasure and a breeze. He explained the services and facilities and answered all of our questions. The bellhop brought us to our room, explained everything to us (including how to adjust the A/C) and left us with a smile.
The room was clean (some scuffs on the white walls that could use a bit of touch-up though), well sized and the bathroom was larger than we thought it would be. Well stocked snacks and bar (if you wanted to indulge) and a bed that was probably the most comfortable bed we have ever slept in. Our room faced the construction site and we could see the Empire State Building in the distance.
It's the little things that would make us to want to come back. VERY good coffee served in the lobby every morning (which was replaced by iced lemon/lime water during the rest of the day) and floor mats in the elevator that were changed every 8 hours that read "GOOD MORNING", "GOOD AFTERNOON" and "GOOD EVENING". Simple, but impressive.
The location is great. A few blocks away from Wall Street, Battery Park, the river, Century 21, and a few subway lines. We have stayed a few times in the Times Square area and although that was very convenient for the tourist attractions, this location was a lot quieter and easier to get around in. 
We will be back.

name: Courtyard New York Manhattan/Fifth Avenue
title: “Great Staff and Location”
text:
I purchased this hotel through Priceline. The location of this hotel is great, there are so many things in walking distance from this hotel. There are also plenty of subway stations in walking distance to get you to other parts of the city. I took the NYC transit bus into the city instead of a cab, which takes you to Grand Central and from there it's only a 5 minute walk to the hotel. 
The Hotel itself is small and on a relatively quiet street which helps with the nose in the rooms. I called a day in advance to let them know I would be getting in early and they had a room waiting for me when I checked in at 1pm.The staff is great, very helpful, especially Sophia at the front desk. There was one bellman, that was a little crass, other than him the rest of the staff was wonderful.
The lobby is small, nothing fancy but perfectly clean. There are only 7 rooms on each floor. I asked for a quiet room, and was given a room on the back side of the hotel at the end of the hallway, next to the housekeeping room. It was perfect, I didn't need a view, there where no guests room next to me, so I didn't hear people in the next room. I will say the doors to the room are a little thin, as I could still hear people talking in the halls at night. But since there are only seven rooms on the floor there isn't much noise in the hallways. I actually never saw anyone on the floor. 
The room (807) was actually pretty big for NYC standards. The bathroom is your typical Courtyard Marriott bathroom with a hairdryer, soaps, shampoo, conditioner, lotion, shower gel. The room had a small safe and plenty of desk space with a coffee maker and TV. My only complaint for the room was they don't have the Bravo channel. There was free wifi in the room, I didn't try it though. The beds were supper soft. I do wish that Marriott would get longer sheets so that the sheets cover the comforter during the night, or put a duvet cover on the comforters. I really didn't like waking up in the middle of the night to readjust the sheets so I didn't touch the comforter. Other than that this is a great hotel and would recommend.

name: The Jane
title: “The Jane Hotel”
text: Jeg og venninna mi dro på shoppingferie til NY. Vi hadde selfølgelig mye bagasje da vi sjekket inn på Jane etter 12 dager på ett annet hotell. Hotellet i seg selv er helt gjennomsnittlig, men vær OBS på at de minste rommene har køyeseng og en strørrelse på ca. 1,70 x 2,3 meter!!! Vi måtte sove med koffertene i bunnen av sengen og gå ut i gangen når den andre skulle skifte. Morgenen etter ei natt på byen måtte vi grave oss ut. Altså, lite golvplass!! Aircon. virket ikke og vi måtte derfor ha døren åpen på dagtid for å få gjennomtrekk og litt luft inn. Det var 3 dusjer og 4 toaletter som hele etasjen delte. Disse rommene anbefales ikke til noen som reiser med bagasje, eller som ønsker privatliv!! Dette er det værste hotellet jeg noen gang har bodd på og jeg skal definitivt aldri mer dele bad med mindre jeg er på backpackertur! Eneste pluss - hotellet ligger i gåavstand til Soho og flere gode resturanter. Det ligger også nært Meatpacking district og Chelsea. Men obs! Nærmeste metrostasjon ligger noen kvartaler unna!

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Never again”
text:
For approx $400 per night we expected more. The reported fantastic view of Central Park from floor 36 was totally unexpected as it appeared as a small area of distant green trees surrounded and overpowered by high rise buildings with additional views of rooftop buildings either under construction or piled with refuse. 
We travel regularly and this is the only hotel with a bathroom so small that I could wash my feet in the bath and wash my hands in the washbasin whilst sitting on the toilet. However the bed was exceptionally comfortable.
The pre arrival booking service help was great and the staff were friendly however whilst Seppis restaurant outside area was a haven for the smoker and it had tables reserved for those who favour tobacco we regularly had to place our order up to four times to get served and had the same problem in trying to get the bill.
We will not be returning to Le Parker Meridien.

name: Doubletree Hotel Chelsea New York City
title: “Hotell Doubletree NYC-Chelsea- Utrolig bra hotell!”
text:
Vi var to venninner som var i New York for tredje gang. Vi bodde 12 netter på dette hotellet, og er virkelig godt fornøyde. Servicen var veldig bra. Du følte deg alltid hjertlig velkommen og det var alttid et hjelpsomt personale som møtte deg i resepsjonen.
Rommene var til enhver tid fine og rene. Spesielt badet var vi veldig godt fornøyd med, noe vi sjelden pleier å være ellers. Senga var også veldig stor og god, og det var stor tv, varmepumpe og god nok plass på rommet. Eneste minus var at vi ikke hadde minibar.
Hotellet lå sentralt, ikke langt fra Madison Square Garden, og med ca. 5 min. gange til Macys og Manhatten Mall, og ca.10 min. til Times Square.
Samtidig som var det så sentralt, var det lite støy rundt hotellet.
Alt i alt, er vi veldig godt fornøyd med hotellet, og kunne gjerne bodd der igjen!

name: Hotel Newton
title: “Basic but spotlessly clean, friendly & right beside a subway stop”
text: I would recommend this hotel if all you want is somewhere to wash yourself, lay your head at night and maybe watch some tv. The rooms are extremely clean and comfortable.

name: The Jane
title: “A NY fais comme un New Yorkais”
text:
Après mon deuxième séjour au Jane, je ne pouvais me permettre de ne pas laisser de commentaires sur cet hôtel (il fallait que je me fasse une seconde idée :-) ) ..... situé au coeur du Meatpacking District au sud de Chelsea, le Jane est sans aucun doute le seul hôtel du coin qui vous permettra de dormir à moins de 200$ la nuit dans un décors recherché et un style qui lui appartient.....Ici pas de chichi, on ne vient pas pour le luxe et le confort mais pour l'ambiance jeune et branchée de NY qui tous les week ends se rue au bar de l'hôtel, quant à son restaurant, classique et abordable contrairement à ceux du quartier et ambiance française appréciée.
Je recommande vivement cet hôtel en cabine pour 125$ la nuit car il faut le dire, à NY on préfère dépenser son argent dans autre chose que dans un hôtel....
Un habitué du Jane !

name: The Hotel at Times Square
title: “Great location, dated furnishings, worn linens, poor service.”
text: This hotel is in a great location for theater going. Easy walk to Times Square and all theaters, restaurants, and Rockefeller Center. Staff however are not friendly with the exception of the bar tender in the 2nd floor bar (very small bar). She was great. Front desk and breakfast room staff were somewhat put out and bothered by the large number of teens there for spring break. The furnishings in the rooms were dated and worn. The bathroom is very small and the door has glass in it limiting privacy. Shower pressure is good and plenty of hot water. Linens were thin, worn, and rough. Breakfast was moderate in quality and the buffet area was not clean.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Muy buen hotel, excelente ubicacion”
text:
Me toco una habitacion amplia y baño privado amplio, muebles nuevos, muy linda. No tiene internet gratuito y desde el hotel no te permite conectarte a servidores gratuitos, esto fue un inconveniente para mi. Hay personal que habla español pero no en el bar y a veces es dificil hacerse entender lo que uno quiere comer. La ubicacion es perfecta para desplazarse desde alli a todos los lugares de Manhattan.
Volveria sin dudarlo!

name: The Helmsley Park Lane
title: “Great Location but not my type of place”
text:
Must start off by saying that this hotel was chosen by a client and would not have been my first choice. 
Location is great for the city, 1 minute to the subway and across from Central Park. 
Room was fine and comfy though some things were a little dated.
Only ate one breakfast in the hotel which was very expensive and distincly average.
Service was OK but I came away feeling that this hotel used or was trying to be something it isn't - ie a top class hotel. It certainly is not.

name: Doubletree Hotel Chelsea New York City
title: “schöne kleines zimmer”
text:
Zentrale Lage.Das zimmer war klein aber sauber und relativ neu eingerichtet.
Das Personal am beim Einchecken war langsam aber freundlich,musste rückfragen.
Der Conserge war sehr eifrig und zuvorkommend und kompetent.
Es waren 2 lifte vorhanden die sehr langsam waren dadurch längeres warten auf den Lift

name: The Hotel at Times Square
title: “Nice little hotel, fantastic location, pity about Ashok on reception”
text:
I have just returned from a 3 night trip to New York with my parents and a stay at the 'hotel at times square'. Having read the reviews on tripadviser I chose this hotel as the reviews were generally good and the price we found on hotels.com was very good for New York.
First impressions were very good, a nice lobby area and a fairly seemless check in process. I had previously contacted the hotel to request adjacent rooms and this was granted, we were located on the 12th floor.
Both rooms were a good size and contained a nice big comfortable bed, plasma TV, Radio Alarm which you could dock an Ipod into and a clean bathroom, I could have no complaints about the bedrooms.
My parents had a small problem with the bath plug which they reported to reception in the morning, the plug was replaced and fixed by the time they returned later in the day.
The only negative point of the whole visit to the hotel at times square was the checkout process, as mentioned previously we booked via hotels.com at a nightly rate of $123, when we checked out the guy behind reception tried to charge us $135 and told us that this was the correct rate (this is despite showing him a copy of the confirmation from hotels.com). After about 20 mins of discussion and phone calls our bill was amended. Throughtout the whole process the guy (his name was Ashok) showed no commen sense or customer service and was quite frankly not interested in helping us, we appeared to be a problem rather than a guest at the hotel.
I noticed a another guest earlier checking out who appeared to have a similar problem, I would incourage future guests to check the nightly tariff when you check in to avoid any problems when checking out.
To summarise this is a nice little hotel in a fantastic location, nice clean rooms and a bar where you can grab a beer for $3! Only negative thing I can comment on is the dreadful service that Ashok provided during checkout.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Das Hotel Millennium Broadway New York liegt direkt am Times Square,also absolut zentral”
text:
Super zentrale Lage,wenn man aus dem Hotel raustritt und ca.30m läuft, ist man direkt am Times Square, also noch zentraler kann man nicht liegen.
Das Hotel hat die notwendigen Ausstattungen, die man für eine Besichtigungstour braucht: Safe,Minibar und Haarföhn.Wenn man in New York ist, hält man sich tagsüber sowie so nicht im Hotel auf.
Die Klimaanlage kann mann selber regulieren oder sogar ausschalten, was ja nicht immer in Amerika der Fall ist.
Die Subway ist ca. 400m entfernt und der morgentliche Bagel sowie Kaffee erhält man auf der anderen Strassenseite.
Mein Fazit wenn ich New York wieder besuchen werde dann nur dieses Hotel.

name: Hotel Newton
title: “Room was misrepresented.”
text:
I checked what was available and it said it was a double bed.
I checked it out on the hotel web site. The web site said amenities included a refrigerator, microwave and coffee maker.
When I got to the hotel with my print out that said a double bed and went to the room, it was the size of a closet with a single bed, bed side table and a tv on the wall.
It was 11 feet wide with no refrigerator ,etc.
The bed was situated with my head 4 feet from the air conditioner. I got 
4 hours sleep because it was so noisy and the air was blowing only head.
It was clean and I did feel safe for a positive comment.
I would not have stayed there if the available room had been accurately
represented.

name: Sheraton Tribeca New York Hotel
title: “Good experience”
text:
Perfect localization: near Soho, Tribeca, Meatpacking. Nice place to go out at night. Much calmer than Midtown/Times Square. And near all the best shops, such as Zara, Sephora, MAC, Desigual, Uniqlo, Victoria Secret and so many... 
But if you like to be in the middle of chaos and tourist place, so Sheraton Tribeca is not your place.
It doesnt have frigobar, neighter wifi in the rooms. These are the negative points. 
Staff is great , specially Steve Lamour. We had a huge problem with the checkout and he helped with all his patience.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “The best location in NY”
text:
+fantastic location
+very trendy
+comfy bed
+iphone speakers for playing music
+nice food in the hotel restaurant
-it's very big hotel and doen't feel very friendly.

name: Sheraton Tribeca New York Hotel
title: “Smart & comfortable”
text:
Not much to look at from outside the front door, but excellent on the inside. Lobby and rooms are smartly furnished and look trendy and clean. The lobby has a computer station with about 4 computers you can use. NY Times and WSJ available in the lobby daily. The lobby bar also looks pretty good. Staff at the front desk were helpful and efficient.
Skip the expensive and rather blah hotel restaurant and walk 2-3 blocks to Soho for better food. Breakfast was not complimentary so I got some fresh fruit and bagels from the Tribeca Bagel store next door (better sit-down brunch to be had in nearby Soho or the Village). 
Rooms are snug as is typical for NYC, but with nice decor and nice showers. The fan in the bathroom is noisy so we kept it on at a minimum only for showers. Adjustable heating/AC worked well. There is some street noise as you would expect in NYC from cars, but this dies down during the night. There is free Starbucks-branded coffee which you can make with the machine in your room, along with a small selection of Tazo tea. There's also one free bottle of filtered Nestle water (watch out - the small one is free and replaced daily by the maid, but the slightly larger one on the opposite side of the desk is $5). 
Location is very close to Soho and you will be very satisfied with it. However, the block surrounding the hotel is Canal Street which is less nice, so you have to walk a block to get anywhere good. But this only takes a minute. There is a LOT of traffic congestion right around the area so don't be surprised if taxi drivers are reluctant to take you directly there (this will get them stuck in traffic for an hour right around the hotel) -- get around this by telling them you're willing to walk a couple blocks and that they don't have to get into the traffic.
Nice hotel overall. I would come again. We bid on Priceline so didn't know what hotel we'd be getting until afterward, but were happy with the result.

name: The Hotel at Times Square
title: “Location for a Deal”
text:
Not right on Times Square but very close. Between 6th and 5th Avenue (Times Square is where Broadway crosses 7th Avenue). I was in Nw York for three days to see four plays. Three of the theaters were only an easy 15 minute walk from the hotel. The fourth was a 20 block walk up Broadway to Lincoln Center. This is the first time I was ever in New York without using the subway.
The real surprise was the quality of the hotel for the price. I paid $189 a night, which included AARP discount and all the taxes ($27.40). All of the pictures on their web site are accurate. I had a single room which was large with plenty of closet and drawer space and a desk and two chairs. I was on the 9th floor and could even look out half of my window and see the street below and the sky above. Wallpaper and drapes looked new. Bathroom was large and bright and new-looking

name: Loews Regency Hotel
title: “Very good New York Option”
text: I usually struggle to find a hotel in New York that I enjoy. The Regency is very well located on Park Avenue. It is a smallish hotel and therefore it has a much more intimate feel than most hotels in this class. Rooms are surprisingly large although bathrooms are a bit small. My son's room had a small kitchenette which I did not really understand but my wife and I appreciated the combined tea and coffee maker in our room. Room rates are competitive. The staff are pleasant and helpful. My only small niggle is that it seemed to take rather a long time on two occasions for the waiter to take our orders in the otherwise pleasant bar. I will stay here again.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Good Value”
text:
I stayed here during a girls getaway to New York City. We got a good rate through hotels.com.
Overall, I was very impressed with this hotel. It is very centrally located and right next to Grand Central Station -- making subway travel very convenient. Many sights are within walking distance, and almost everything accessible by a $7 or less cab fare.
The lobby is always buzzing with hotel guests and decorated with modern decor. Self-service kiosks made check-in a breeze. 
Our room was a king room located on the 17th floor. The elevators could be a long wait sometimes, but it wasn't too bad. The room was nicely appointed with a low sitting bed, a modern chair (not comfy), and a flat screen TV. We were happy with the size of the room (considering this is NYC). The bathroom was small, and the sink was awkwardly placed with a tiny, tiny bowl. You would get very wet trying to wash your face! But all in all, a great room and a good value.
The staff were very accommodating and helpful. Everything we asked for was promptly delivered. We were even allowed to check-in early and check-out late.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Bathroom design very poor”
text:
Great location. Very busy hotel. I had a modernized room but I think the architect had never stayed in a hotel before.
The bathroom was disappointing. The hand basin was hidden by a very wide ledge above it. The taps were actually under the ledge and the lever to lower the plug was almost impossible to find. Half the basin was hidden by the protruding ledge and the whole counter top was set 3 inches too low. It was a long way to bend down.
My room had motion detector lighting. Very avant garde but if I sat at the desk for 20 minutes working on my computer, the lighting seemed to think the room was empty and closed down. Stand up, walk around and the lighting came on again.
Over my 5 day stay, my electronic room key failed three times. Each time the staff were very apologetic but what a pain. 
And finally, on my last day the steam heating used by the hotel which comes from Grand Central Station was shut down for maintenance from 10pm until 6am so there was no hot water in my room. I was given 12 hours notice of this inconvenience but it was still inconvenient!
I used the Executive Lounge on the 16th floor. Nice location. Adequate continental breakfast. Nice staff. My bill had a duplicate charge on it which was reversed without question - but it should not happen

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Hotel Pennsylvania liegt sehr zentral mitten in Manhattan”
text:
Leider war schon der Check In nicht so wie man es von einem Hotel erwartet - egal welchen Standard das Hotel hat. (45min Wartezeit sind einfach zu viel) Das Zimmer war sehr alt, und dementsprechend auch dreckig. Man hat sich nicht mal getraut das Fenster anzufassen da es wirklich extrem dreckig war- raus schauen konnte man sowieso nicht.
Das Personal hat das Zimmer gut gereinigt, aber das Alter der Zimmer ist eben nicht zu übersehen. Die Lage war optimal. Zimmer war extrem klein für 2 Personen ein 1,20m Bett,....
Ausserdem habe ich meine Uhr im Zimmer vergessen und dem Hotel eine Nachricht geschrieben ob sie diese gefunden haben - sie haben bis heute noch nicht reagiert auf diese mail.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Superlage,da gleich neben Pennstation,dadurch staufreier Transfer von Newark”
text:
Hotel gut zum Übernachten,wer mehr will muß ein teuereres Haus nehmen.
Unser Zimmer mit zwei Doppelbetten für 3 Personen war riesig und sauber
geputzt.Aus der Dusche kam ordentlich kaltes und warmes Wasser.Mehr wollten wir nicht.Wir würden das Hotel jederzeit wieder nehmen.Das einzigartige Ambiente New Yorks in Verbindung mit dem Superwetter,das wir
hatten,der Time Square,der durch seine Illumination die Nacht zum Tag werden läßt,die zahlreichen Gespräche mit den extrem freundlichen und kontaktfreudigen New Yorkern reduzieren die Zeit für den Hotelaufenthalt auf ein Minimum

name: Park Central
title: “Super Lage”
text: Das Hotel hat eine super Lage! Vom Hotel aus sieht man sowohl den Central Park (ca. 5 Gehminuten) und den Times Square (ca. 20 Gehminuten)! Außerdem ist gleiche um die Ecke eine U-Bahnstation die direkt (Express-Zug) zum Times Square fährt. Von dort aus kommt man eigentlich so gut wie überall hin. Zum Hotel: Das Hotel ist eine gutes mittelständiges Hotel. Es ist sauber und man bekommt jeden Tag frische Handtücher (unabhängig ob man sie am Boden liegen hat oder nicht). Leider war unsere Mini-Bar nie gefüllt, auch nicht mit Eis. Fazit: Für eine Städtereise ist das Hotel klasse!

name: Loews Regency Hotel
title: “Okay...could be better - a review from a travel agent & Platinum member”
text:
Just stayed this weekend in a luxury 1 brm suite with my husband, 9 yr old daughter & 20 month old son to celebrate my birthday. It was o-kay. Something was lacking in terms of Loews special service whcih made it just another hotel in NYC (which is known for average hotels). Overall we had a great time because we focused on the pluses rather than the cons.
PLUSES: great location, easy walk to everything, we had a large suite which looked good, food was high quality, gym was efficient, room service/housekeeping/porter were very friendly. Quick response time on housekeeping requests. 
CONS: Check-in staff not warm & inviting but disinterested and insincere - going through the motions. Absolutely NO VIP greeting for Platinum. No prior email contact before arrival (customary with Platinum members), my email request sent earlier to concierge requesting a special amenity be sent to the room with a congratulations note was ignored & I had to make a 2nd request. It arrived (which was appreciated) but without the note for my child so she didn't realize it was something special for her. She was also given an infant's toy instead of age appropriate toy at check-in. Doors in the suite wouldn't close without major slamming (all warped), kichenette was great but had no supplies (no plates, silverwear so it couldn't be used)!!! Bathrooms did not offer any special suite toiletries as other Loews properties do. Turndown not provided on 1st night (even though it was requested), done on 2nd night but other than moving the pillow off the bed and turning the sheet back nothing else was done. Long wait down in the breakfast restaurant both mornings. Summer fun program for kids was not well thought out (all kids should get a prize - a lollipop would have been sufficient!!) so not worth promoting and not worth us coming back in time for (as my child had repeatedly told us all day that we had to back in time for the kids fun activities at 4pm).
SUMMARY: As a fan of Loews Hotels, I love to stay in Loews because of the 'extra' service, attention to detail, fun factor, spoiling of my kids that Loews are renowned for giving but I didn't have that at the Loews Regency. As a platinum member, I got my complimentary suite upgrade which I greatly appreciated but not any VIP service. I did have a perfectly fine hotel with very nice food in the restaurant when I actually could get to a table. It was clean & efficient and if that is all you want then I highly recommend it but then the Hilton & Sheraton also gave me a decent stay for a fraction of the cost. Would I stay again - sure - but I wouldn't expect it to be more than a decent hotel.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Económico e muito bem localizado”
text:
Os quartos do Hotel são anticuados, decoração clássica, espaçosos q.b., mas são bastante confortáveis. 
O Hotel é antigo e isso é bem visivel através da casa de banho, onde parte da canalização é feita por fora das paredes. O que gostei menos foi da casa de banho, mas os quartos são limpos. 
O meu quarto ficava voltado para as traseiras, onde existe um parque de estacionamento vertical (só vi disto em NY), e por vezes à noite ouvia-se os chiar do sistema de ascenção.
O Hotel não inclui pequeno almoço, mas tem um snack bar com aceso pelo loby. Nunca experimentámos este snack porque nas imediações existem bastantes snacks a um preço mais económico. Aconselho ir tomar o pequeno almoço ao "Europa", uma vez que tem mais variedade e opções menos americanizadas.
O ponto forte deste Hotel é mesmo a sua localização, mesmo no coração de Times Square e a um custo económico, apresentando uma boa relação qualidade/preço. Trata-se de um hotel básico e sem luxos a um preço simpático e muito bem localizado.
Aconselho este hotel para quem não pretenda luxos e pretenda visitar NY de forma económica.

name: The Helmsley Park Lane
title: “Tawdry and Dirty.”
text:
My husband and I just returned from a romantic weekend trip to NYC. It was supposed to be both romantic and luxurious but that is not quite how it turned out. We booked a room at the Helmsley Park Lane expecting a decent amount of luxury and pampering. What a disappointment.
The only hotel personnel who seemed to have any clue about how to do their jobs were the desk clerks and even they were not always up to the task having some difficulty using the computers. The doormen and bellhops stood around the lobby or in front of the doors, both revolving and swinging, and only once during our five day stay did they bother to even open the door let alone bother to get out of the way.
The hotel itself has seen far better days with torn and worn carpeting, banged up walls and furniture and stained fixtures and broken tiles in the bath. This tawdriness was compounded by the very poor job the maid service did in cleaning the room. There was a half inch of dust under all of the furniture with legs where the maids had not bothered to vacuum for some time, and even though the maids came into the room every day the room was never clean. Hair dotted not just the bath but the floor and sink after they cleaned. I am not at all sure it was from either my husband or me. The toilet was simply disgusting with a brown ring that looked more like some youth hostel than a fine NYC hotel. We never got clean glasses in the bathroom and there was dust on most of the pictures and television.
The bellhop said there was an iron and ironing board and an umbrella in every room and that was only partially right. There was an iron, no ironing board, and the umbrella had several broken ribs which became apparent on the day when the skies opened and the rain came plummeting down.
The Helmsley touts itself as one of the world's finest hotels and we were certainly expecting a level of service comparable to hotels we have stayed in in Europe, but it just was not there. I will not return and I do not recommend this hotel to anyone unless location is the only criterion.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “A grand hotel near everything”
text:
I am very pleased with the hotel. Is near everything in manhattan, we reach the good places on foot or spending a few bucks in taxi.
The hotel the decor was recently renovated and its great. This is a hotel to come back

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Perfecta ubicación, muy buen precio después de mucho comparar e idóneo para DORMIR Y NO PEDIR MÁS”
text: Con Expedia conseguí un buen vuelo interno con buen precio para visitar New York. En cuanto al hotel es como habían explicado otros viajeros del foro: muy muy CÉNTRICO, cerca del metro, limpio pero antiguo. La habitación correcta (cama para 2 grande y cómoda), baño normalito, ducha con mucha agua y muy caliente.Perfeco para no gastar mucho y poder descansar las horas que pases por la noche. Si quieres que tenga mejor pinta tienes que mirar el NEW YORKER(justo al lado), pero son 100e más y quizás para una ciudad en la que no vas a parar quieto no merece la pena. Lo recomiendo para viajeros jóvenes.

name: Hotel Newton
title: “Fabulous!”
text: We've just come back from an 8 night stay at the Newton. The room (junior suite) was huge and everything was very clean and well looked after. The staff were all friendly and helpful.There was no noise from other guests at all. The only problem was shuttle buses parked outside our window when the subway wasn't working properly for 2 nights, but that's a one off. And the lift isn't that slow, you somtimes just have to wait a couple of minutes. The location next to the subway is ideal and there are plenty of places to eat and drink in the area. I'd especially recommend The Dive Bar on Amsterdam Avenue just round the corner from the hotel. The Metro Diner up Broadway between 100th and 101st streets does a great good value breakfast. All in all, I would certainly recommend the Newton.

name: The Hotel at Times Square
title: “exceptional staff and total amenities”
text: I choose the hotel for it's location only, but was very surprised at how great the staff treated us. The amenities were also fantastic. I encountered a small problem with the parking facility and when I notified Sonny, the manager, my credit card was credited the overage immediately.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Breathless in Manhattan!”
text: My best friend from highschool and I hadn't seen each other for 5 years and we decided to have a reunion at Le Parker Meridien...WOW WHAT A GREAT HOTEL!!!!! The staff at the front desk were awesome- and REID is sooo cute! The 15,000sq ft healthclub and the rooftop sundeck and swimming pool were great also- and only 2 blocks from Central Park! I can't wait to go back!

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “poca pretesa...tanta resa!”
text: partiamo da un presupposto:ny è una delle citta' + care del mondo e trovare un alloggio a prezzi bassi è impresa proibitiva. questo hotel presenta questa caratteristica, unita al fatto di trovarsi in una posizione fantastica, come nessun altro. ma le buone notizie finiscono qui. camere fatiscenti, sporchissime, spartane e diroccate. la doccia, nella nostra camera era "fantozziana"; ed in generale, stanze molto rumorose

name: The Helmsley Park Lane
title: “My birthday trip”
text:
We spent 4 nights at the Helmsley Park Lane Hotel and LOVED it! We arrived on the 9th of January 2008 and were upgraded to a kingsize room on 31st floor. The room was impresive in size and very accomodating with a partial but nice view of the neighbourhood (city view). I read a few bad reviews of the bathrooms and I must say, although they are somewhat dated the showers were really powerfull and the mirrors were fantastic for applying makeup, (which helps if u are a lady!:)). The room was cleaned twice day, lovely clean towels and fluffy robes. Everybody at the hotel from the cleaning lady to Reception staff seemed friendly and willing to help with any queries. The restaurant was good, too. Prices slightly on the expensive side but, then again, we knew that when we chose New York. 
The hotel is close to 5th avenue and just by the Park, so it makes it really easy to go for a brisk walk or just to go for a wonder.
Well connected to the rest of Manhatan via tube stations and busses. We got lost on our way a few times just because we tried to find our way as we would do in London. It's a completely different system! Get a map! Ask for directions, people were very friendly!
There is a lovely cafe just behind the Hotel with an amazing breakfast selection! We ate there every morning. Shopping was amazing, too!
Overall, my choise of hotel was great! We loved it and I would reccomend it to everybody going to the big apple! I will be back!:))

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Not a Good Place to Stay”
text: My husband and I were in the city for a show and had booked a room here. The paint on the bathroom ceiling was peeling in our room and the ceiling was covered with mold. There was no exhaust fan in the bathroom. Also, the room was extremely hot. I put the thermostat down to 50 degrees and it was still hot. It did not cool down the entire time we were there. I would not stay here again and would not recommend it to anyone. We stayed over one night from 3/6 to 3/7, 2004.

name: W New York - Downtown
title: “A very pleasant stay”
text: My husband and I booked this hotel for a three-night stay (July 4 weekend) and it proved to be an enjoyable, comfortable experience—especially for our dog, who was treated with a welcome bed, food bowl and treats (he really loved the latter). Room was a bit small, but the bed was very comfortable and amenities (especially Bliss toiletries, and a small but well-equipped gym) much appreciated. We stayed on the South side of the hotel, which had a great view—we could see a bit of the river from the 21st floor—and was extremely quiet. We found the service to be excellent: fast check-in/check-out, helpful bellhops and an especially accommodating desk clerk who found a packet of theater tickets we left behind while checking in (he brought them directly to our room himself, without any prompting on our part—we hadn't realized we'd forgotten them!). We didn't try the bar or restaurant, nor did we use valet parking (too steep; we got a much better deal at a garage nearby). Subway is close by, and the downtown area has some great parks, biking, shopping (Century 21—I could have stayed there for hours!) and sightseeing. We'd definitely stay there again, and would recommend to anyone who is interested in exploring downtown Manhattan.

name: Sheraton Tribeca New York Hotel
title: “Incredible”
