text: Had no idea how fabulous this location is! Everything is in walking distant, even on a cold winter day! Tons of great restaurants and bars nearby. Was here for a wedding and the hotel staff was extremely accommodating and the price was great for the TriBeCa area. Great for all people!!

name: Sheraton Tribeca New York Hotel
title: “Friendly Staff”
text: We stayed here over the past weekend. The front desk staff is extremely friendly and helpful. We had a standard room with a King bed. It was very small, which we had read about before getting there. This is the usual case in NYC. The bathroom was also small, but suitable, although it had an extremely loud bathroom fan. This hotel is located to some cool shops in Soho, and we had fun shopping there. A couple of things to keep in mind: if you want to go uptown or to Times Square, it is hard getting a cab. We asked a staff member to help us get a cab and he said it would be better if we walked up a block and tried to get one ourselves. We did try and no one would pull over, and when someone finally did pull over he said it was "too far" for him to go and pulled away. We had to walk back to the Sheraton and flag our own cab because the doorman didn't have much interest in helping us. It was an overall pleasant experience. Since there is always something to do in NYC you aren't spending much time in your room, which is a good thing here.

name: W New York - Downtown
title: “Very modern and comfortable”
text:
This property is beautiful - great views of the WTC site and a very stylish lobby. The lobby, while very cool, can feel a little crowded and loud. 
The customer service is not attentive. When I arrived I stood at the desk for a while before anyone came over. I think the staff was watching a youtube video or looking at something on the internet - they were all crowded around one computer and didn't notice that I was standing there for a while. Also, I was overcharged on my hotel folio. I sent an email to the GM's email address as instructed on the folio, but I got no response.

name: Park Central
title: “Gerne wieder”
text: Die Lage des Hotels ist hervorragend. Für einen Städtetrip nach New York optimal. Service ist im Hotel keiner zu erwarten. Der Conciergeservice war gut, ansonsten gab es so etwas wie Service nicht. Die Zimmer sind sauber und gut ausgestattet. Wir haben dort allerdings kaum Zeit verbracht. Allerdings sind die Zimmer sehr hellhörig. Das Preis-Leistungsverhältnis ist für New York sehr gut. Wenn man plant seine Zeit in der Stadt zu verbringen und nicht auf dem Zimmer, dann kann ich das Hotel nur empfehlen.

name: Ramada Eastside
title: “Great value”
text:
I wasn't expecting much for the price, but was pleasantly surprised to find a generously-sized (by NYC standards) queen room and bath. The room was clean, the bed was comfortable, the bathroom was actually attractive and appeared to have been recently renovated. The staff was friendly and helpful, and the continental breakfast was decent. I've had far worse in NYC for more money. The neighborhood is safe, but there's not a whole lot going on in the immediate vicinity; the subway is nearby and taxis are plentiful. 
This is not a destination hotel, but a safe, clean, comfortable place to spend the night. In other parts of the city, you wouldn't blink an eye to pay twice as much for the same room.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Hotelbewertung”
text:
Das Hotel ist weder feucht in den Badräumen, weder zu dunkel in der Lobby.
Der Service ist sehr umfangreich. Das Personaö ausgesucht freundlich und hilfsbereit.
Die Lage des Hotels ist super.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Un sogno....”
text:
Uno splendido hotel in una fantastica posizione ad un costo assolutamente giusto! Ci siamo stati 10 giorni in una camera superior al 49° piano e non ce ne volevamo andare!
Sei ad un passo da tutto ma quando sei in camera ti godi nel silenzio il panorama più bello del mondo. Pulitissimo. Il personale è cortese nella giusta misura... Insomma davvero una scelta eccellente, io ci torno di sicuro.

name: Loews Regency Hotel
title: “Nice, Very Nice”
text:
The friendliest staff I have ever met in a hotel. Welcoming, smiling, check in was a breeze, the room (suite) was excellent. Breakfast at the Regency is a great experience (make a reservation or you won't get in). 
A helpful concierge gave us lots of things to do.
Give yourself a reason to stay there and then enjoy one fine experience.

name: Loews Regency Hotel
title: “Another Great Stay at The Regency”
text:
I had another great stay at the The Regency the night of January 10, 2008. I booked a standard room for a short business trip and was upgraded upon check in to a 15th floor delxue king room as I am a gold member of the Loew's First loyalty program. Thr room was large by New York standards and there was no street noise at all in the room. I also received a complementary bottle of white wine in my room as per my Loews First profile. Much appreciated! The location of the hotel is excellent.
Check in and check out were a breeze and my room was cleaned to perfection. The large flat panel TV was appreciated and the bed was exceedingly comfortable. I did not use the fitness center or dine through room service. Breakfast in the hotel restaurant was excellent and served quickly.
All in all, this hotel consisently reminds me why I keep returning to The Regency.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Nell'ombelico del mondo”
text:
Salve a tutti,
abbiamo soggiornato in questo hotel dal 21 al 25 Novembre 2009 e ci ritorneremo subito.
Albergo centralissimo,sembra proprio di essere nel centro del mondo,mille luci e mille rumori circondano questo hotel ma una volta entrati in camera la città rimane fuori.
Stanze molto ampie e pulite e persone della hall molto cortesi;l'unica "nota dolente" che non c'è l'accesso ad internet gratuito.

name: Loews Regency Hotel
title: “Loews Regency, sorry, not for me”
text:
Good:
Location/Neighborhood
Service/Staff is perfect
Bed & Pillows are #1
Limonade in lobby in the afternoon
Quiet hotel
Housekeeping and turndown services
Bad:
Old hotel, need a big major makeover
Outdated room/Bathroom (2 tiles did fall down during shower) 
Small room/Bathroom with no ventilation
Room service prices and xtra fee(21%fee + 5$ a guest)is a joke
Way too expensive, you have much better hotel for same price or less (Sofitel hotel is still my favorite in NYC)
Loews shoud put money in the hotel and stop thinking that the friendly employees will make up for the running down hotel

name: Sheraton Tribeca New York Hotel
title: “Basic Hotel. Good for Shopping”
text: Stayed as a Plat for the first time last weekend with the wife. It is a 'fine' and basic hotel. I got the usual ''upgrade'' from a basic room to a club floor -- still dont really consider this an upgrade- but nevertheless. This hotel is in a great location for shopping. Next to Broadway and Soho -- some great places within walking distance...There is a club lounge which is very nice and has a great patio, BUT no free alcohol! Which basically renders this lounge useless except for a basic cold breakfast in the morning. What's the point? Might as well go to a nice bar...The rooms here are fine. Basic. Nothing fancy...Staff was friendly...Ultimately, good location for shopping -- and if you want to get away from Times SQ.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Hotel Pennsylvania New York”
text:
Il check in e' andato bene anche se c'era un sacco di fila (ma era sotto il periodo natalizio).
Gli spazi comuni sono grandi e confortevoli, le camere un po meno... sono piccole anche se pulite. Gli asciugamani vengono cambiati tutti i giorni.
Lo consiglio per un viaggio di max 10 giorni...dopo diventa invivibile soprattutto perche' a Ny si fa molto shopping e dopo un po non sai piu dove mettere le cose!

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Good but could be better without much effort.”
text:
This hotel was a fair value for the money, but they could greatly improve the property by paying attention to some minor maintenance and cleaning issues. The mirror on the bathroom door had paint on the edge of it from a careless painter, and it should have been removed and replaced or the paint should have been removed. The base-board tiles in the bathroom appeared to have stains on the tops of many tiles from wallpaper paste residue. The seam between the bathroom floor tiles and the carpeting was rough and uneven. The windows could have been cleaner (the view was fantastic).
I would return because I could overlook the shortcomings, but it does not make sense that the management or the owners (hard to tell which) are not taking better care of the property.

name: Park Central
title: “Ottima posizione e servizi, ma tutti gli extra si pagano cari!”
text:
A parte che New York è sempre e comunque uno spettacolo, non importa in quale hotel si soggiorni, volevo segnalare questa struttura perchè è in posizione davvero felice...proprio nel cuore di Manhattan, tra Central Park e Times Square!
Ben servito da diverse linee della metropolitana, si arriva agevolmente in qualsiasi altro punto della città in pochi minuti...
Le camere sono ampie (noi eravamo alla 1717), pulite e sempre ben riordinate dalle gentili cameriere, attenzione soltanto alle macchinette automatiche delle bevande, che rubano soldi a tutto spiano (ma che poi vengono restituiti alla reception)!
L'unica cosa che ci ha lasciato l'amaro in bocca è stato dover tirar fuori 3$ a valigia per farcele tenere nel deposito bagagli...sebbene dicano che in tutti gli hotel di NYC sia così, scoccia un pochino dopo avere speso 260$ a notte soltanto per dormire!
Comunque l'hotel è consigliato a tutti, sebbene penso che sia possibile soggiornare a Manhattan con un miglior rapporto qualità-prezzo.
Enjoy!

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Solid value at this quiet hotel”
text:
We stayed 5 nights, starting December 22, 2006. Something of a tradition with us -- indeed, our first stay here was New Year's, 1983. 
The old place shows a bit of wear in the corridors. But our corner room (40 feet of windows overlooking the East River and midtown) was nicely renovated, as was the bathroom. 
We make few demands on room service, concierges and so on. So we have few comments on service -- except that it was perfectly affable and professional, whenever we dealt with staff.
The location is a great one, in my opinion: that part of the east side is quiet, neighbourly, unhurried, yet so close to the best shopping (and the subway).
The dodgiest bit was the Christmas clientele: mid-western fleece-wearers; also UK plebs and their nasty teenage offspring. But this may be a seasonal aberration. My spouse will advise: next trip to UN and this hotel is scheduled for Jan. 23, 2007........

name: The Hotel at Times Square
title: “Excelente ubicación. Precio razonable.”
text:
La ubicación del hotel es excelente y se puede caminar a muchas atracciones importantes. Por esa ubicación en NYC y calidad, el precio es razonable y yo lo recomiendo.
Aunque cabe aclarar que no se trata de un hotel boutique, sino de un hotel orientado a gente joven o de espíritu joven. Las habitaciones están en buenas condiciones, son suficientemente cómodas aunque no demasiado espaciosas. La atención es aceptable, aunque tiende al autoservicio, tanto en el lobby como en el desayunador. El desayuno buffet es bueno (considerando que es "gratuito"), pero el espacio puede resultar incomodo para mucha gente junta. El wi-fi resulta insuficiente para todo el edificio.
En síntesis, si uno prioriza la ubicación y no le molesta una atención despersonalizada, considerando que Nueva York es una ciudad muy cara, parece una muy buena opción.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Cómoda estancia en N.Y”
text:
Este hotel reúne todas las condiciones para pasar una cómoda estancia en N.Y.
Está situado en una calle transversal a Times Square a escasamente cinco minutos de la estación de metro más cercana. Rodeado de tiendas, restaurantes y si quieres asistir a cualquier musical, los tienes todos a "tiro de piedra".
El hotel es agradable y las habitaciones están muy limpias y son acogedoras. Lo que menos me gustó fue el baño. Llévate tu propio neceser (gel, pasta de dientes, champú....) porque las amenities son inexistentes.
Las vistas de la ciudad pueden ser espectaculares si consigues una buena habitación.

name: Holiday Inn Express NYC - Madison Square Garden
title: “Convenient Location, Good Rates, Easy Access to NYC”
text:
Location:
This property is on 29th street, between 7th and 8th. It is a short walk from Penn Station and I found 8th Street to be slightly less congested. Keep in mind that events at MSG can make the area very busy, especially if walking with bags.
The hotel is easy walking distance to Herald Square, Times Square, MSG, etc. Its location also makes for easy access to the various Subway lines, PATH trains, and regional trains.
There are abundant places to eat and drink nearby - pubs, bars, Italian, fast food...just about everything!
Check In:
Check in was fairly painless although I had to get a different room because the first one was still being cleaned when I went upstairs.
As a PC Platinum member, they gave me a gift bag with water and chocolate covered raisins upon check in. I thought it was a nice touch! :)
Room:
The room was an okay size...it IS NYC!! :). Plenty of outlets, flat screen TV, comfortable pillows/bed, and was very functional.
There is an okay hair dryer in the bathroom. Toiletries included soap, shampoo,conditioner, and lotion.
My sister has stayed here in the past and they provided ear plugs due to outside noise. They were not offered to me, but I did not find the outside noise bothersome. That said, the walls of the hotel are somewhat thin and it was easy to hear hallway noise.
Amenities:
Complimentary breakfast - it was the normal HIEx breakfast spread - a mix of cold cereals, coffee, juice, sausage and gravy, scrambled eggs, cinnamon rolls, yogurt, hard boiled eggs, etc.
Wifi - complimentary and the front desk provided a code. There are also a couple of PC work stations in the lobby.

name: The Hotel at Times Square
title: “Quel calme!”
text:
J'adore New York mais il faut bien reconnaître que c'est une ville très bruyante.
Là où j'ai été chanceux c'est en choississant cet hôtel sur Trip advisor, les clients m'ont donné leur avis et je me suis retrouvé dans une chambre au 11ème étage (pas de pb d'attente des ascenseurs).
La chambre (1103) donne sur un square à l'écart de la circulation est est très calme (pour NYC).
Accès wi-fi illimité dans la chambre (et ça marche très bien), et le personnel est plutôt sympa.
Pour ce qui est de l'emplacementil n'y a rien à dire, c'est derrière Times Square à l'écart de la foule et du bruit (mais ça je l'ai déjà dit).
Ce sera mon adresse au prochain voyage, c'est sûr!

name: Park Central
title: “Gerne wieder”
text: Dieses Hotel hat eine grandiose Lage in midtown. Central Park und alle bekannten shopping Ziele direkt ums Eck. Das Frühstücksbuffet war sehr lecker, der Frückstücksraum ist ebenerdig auf Straßenniveau mit vollverglaster Straßenseite. Vis avis ist die Carnegie hall. Straßenlärm für diese Stadt sehr gering in diesem hotel.

name: The Helmsley Park Lane
title: “Anche la vista sulla città non è affatto male”
text: Arrivo catastrofico. Ci sistemano in una stanza non provvista di letto per il figlio, in attesa che la nostra doppia si liberi il giorno dopo. La brandina arriva a mezzanotte e mezza dopo ripetuti pellegrinaggi alla reception. Il giorno dopo ci danno la stanza promessa: 37° piano con vista sulla "New York da bere": fantastico! La camera è bellissima e spaziosa, con due letti grandi...Ma i nostri bagagli dove sono? Naturalmente li hanno lasciati nella stanza del giorno prima! Ricominciano i pellegrinaggi in reception, con recupero finale degli effetti personali perduti..Ma ne è valsa la pena. La posizione dell'hotel, di fronte all'ingresso di Central Park e a qualche passo dal metrò, è senz'altro pregevole. Arredamento solido e classico, molta moquette e arredi dorati. NON richiedete la colazione lì, è molto cara. Noi ci siamo arrangiati con lo spaccio 24h/24 lì vicino, del resto con una vista del genere far colazione in camera con un paio di biscotti e succo di frutta è senz'altro cosa da gran signori.

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “New York is a blast”
text:
Stayed in the Metropolitan June 28 through July2. When we arrived at 9:00 p.m. due to delays our room was not ready. They gave us a voucher for beer or wine in the bar but could not use it for a coke -weird. 
Waited about 15 minutes. Room was small and above the fire station but okay. We did have twin beds rather than a single queen. While getting ready for bed, the bed broke. The housekeeping staff was WONDERFUL. We stayed there that night (no problems with the fire station)and the next day they moved us to a suite for the rest of our stay. Very nice!!!! 
the furnishings are dated (reminded me of the early 60's) but I went to see the city, not the hotel. NY is wonderful! We felt safe, walked around late at night, loved Times square, Central Park, saw the Producers, visited Ground Zero. Had tickets for the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island but did not go because there was a 40 minute wait in the sun before we got on the boat. We gave our tickets away. No homeless or panhandlers like we saw in Washington except in battery park). Can't wait to go back and would stay at the Metro. again. It was part of our vacation package from Alaska Airlines and well worth the price.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Un peu au dessous de l'attente”
text: Cet hotel est très bien situé; très belle vue de la chambre Un peu vieillot dans sa décoration. On a voulu nous faire changer de chambre au cours du séjour, parce qu'un groupe voulait tout l'étage ! lobbie très sombre : lugubre.

name: Hilton New York
title: “NYC Hotels Are Expensive-But the Hilton NY Was Worth It”
text:
If you have seen any of my reviews you must know that I like maximum value for minimum price. I didn't get that this time.
My wife and her sister had never been to NY, so when we saw an Airtran sale we jumped on it about a month ago. However, we delayed booking a hotel until last week, but I didn't think the prices were even close to reasonable. I tried on multiple occasions on multiple days to get a hotel around $100 a night in Manhattan proper with Priceline. I even went as high as $150 per night, but nothing worked.
So I did it the old fashion way via kayak, hotels.com and other sites. The Hilton New York came up about $195, but I didn't grab it, hoping for a better deal. Other hotels were running $325 a night (the shower water has flakes of gold in it) and some in the low 200's were not getting good reviews. The next check found the Hilton at $209, so I finally gave in and booked it.
What do you get for $209 a night?
1. A bill that runs into the mid-$500's because of all of the taxes for a two night stay.
2. Location, location and more locations. This hotel located at these coordinates, n 40 45 43.76,w73 58 45.27 is perfectly centrally located, which provides the following:
-Ten minute walk to Time Square at a brisk pace.
-Ten minute walk to Central Park in the other direction.
-The same time and distance to the Apple store made out of glass.
-Radio City Music Hall can be seen a block and a half away from the hotel.
-Grand Central is about 20 minutes away and the Rockefeller Center is about 15 minutes away.
-It was about 30 minutes to the Intrepid Carrier exhibit, but it was quite comfortable.
Exterior:
It is a concrete city hotel, so there is not a lot in the way of greenery on the outside of the hotel. However, the curb staff that greeted you when you arrived were very good, friendly and knowledgeable.
Lobby:
Nice and brightly lit, although I would not say that it was ornate. The check-in staff was always very friendly, however, we got there early so we had to check in our bags and go exploring until about 3pm. As we had a third person, the young lady said she would give us a corner room, because it had a little more space in it. 
Room:
I'm glad she gave us the larger room, because I'd be afraid to see what the smaller room looked like. These rooms are about half the size of some that I have stayed in before, but they were still comfortable and nicely appointed. The lcd tv was mounted on a swivel stand, which made it easy to change the viewing angle. The bathroom was also small (I'd say three people are the max for comfort), but very well maintained and bright. No complaints.
Beds:
These beds had the looks of the super plush ones I've experienced Hyatt Hotels and the Intercontinental, but I didn't sink into them like at those other hotels and it took awhile for me to get to sleep. Plush looking yes, plush feeling, no!
Food:
Let's just say we were not eating anything in the area of the hotel. The concept of paying $15 for a bagel at a restaurant on the corner was totally unacceptable. So using Tripadvisor and Yelp, we found reasonably priced (for New York that is) restaurant within a 15 minute walk like Giorgios Country Grill.
Overall, it is my opinion that this is a very nice hotel. Did I want to pay $200+ for it, well, heck no, because I have been to better hotels for a lot less money. But when you compare it to others in the area, then it stood up well. I won't call anything a value at $200+, but it was good.
Other items:
Wifi is NOT free in your room. However, in the lobby it is free once you enter your room information into your browser. It is pretty fast when there are not too many users, because I streamed a video one night. The next night when a lot of 'surfers' were sitting all over the lobby, the speed dropped to a crawl.

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “Hotel péssimo”
text: Não entendo como o Double tree possa levar o nome Hilton junto. Trata-se de hotel de quinta categoria. Os recepcionistas são péssimos, desatenciosos, mal educados em sua maioria, e os horários de check in e check out são desrespeitados. Nào é limpo e os quartos são pequenos. Sugiro a quem passar em frente que mude de calçada

name: Sheraton Tribeca New York Hotel
title: “My favorite NY hotel”
text:
Staff is friendly and very helpful, provides excellent service consistently. The General Manager has a hands-on style, is accessible and pro-active. 
I've stayed at several hotels in New York - there is no doubt in my mind that the Sheraton Tribeca is my only choice when I return to the area.

name: Millennium Hotel Broadway
title: “Très bel hotel idéalement placé sur Times Square”
text: Nous avons eu une chambre très confortable, au calme, assez grande, et avec une superbe vue sur Times Square et sur Midtown (nous étions au 49ème étage). Nous sommes très satisfaits de cet hotel, malgré le petit désagrément lors de notre arrivée le premier soir car suite à une arrivée tardive, ils n'avaient pas gardé notre chambre (malgré la réservation). Ils nous ont relogé pour cette première nuit à l'hotel en face (classe supérieure), ne nous ont pas fait payer cette première nuit, et nous ont offert le lendemain une corbeille de fruit et une bouteille d'eau gazeuse. Le service client est donc au rendez-vous et nous y retournerons sans problème.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Great location in NYC”
text: Booked through Priceline and got a reasonable deal. Stayed here before and got a great room but unfortunately not this time. Room was clean but small and with no view and room was very dark. Suspect this was because we booked through Priceline. Checkin was slow and the lobby is under renovation. Still a good location in NYC.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Excellent Customer Service”
text: I have been staying at this hotel for 2 years on a weekly basis. The new manager Eric Thieling personally sought me out after I had some housekeeping issues and not only were they resolved but he took a personal interest in my stays. I have traveled to over 51 countries and stayed in the high end hotels Ritz, Oberoi, Four Seasons etc and I can safely say that my treatment at the Hilton is comparable to these hotels. I am always greeting by name and "family-like" status at the executive desk and I know them all by name as well. Ken Jarka sends me amenities upon arrival often and it is very welcome when I have been on the road for some time and having a late arrival. Amy Morena always seeks me out at the Lounge and knows that I love fruit so she helps me to grab some fruit quickly and asks about my children. My EA will personally speak to Eric if there are special requirements. Recently my daughter graduated from Columbia Engineering and I had a block of rooms for out of town guests and the staff was so attentive to every guest, and Eric kindly upgraded me to a suite so I could entertain and it felt like my home away from home. I never stay anywhere else and I have many choices as an executive with a major corporation in mid-town, I chose to come to the Hilton because I know that I will be treated like a long time customer and I feel like I am in my 2nd home.

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Idéalement situé mais aurait besoin d'un rafraichissement”
text: Idéalement situé devant Madison Square Garden et Penn Station. Prix abordable. Grand lit, télévision. Vue sur l'empire state building mais malheureusement les fenêtres sont très sales. Salle de bains petite et vieillotte.

name: Murray Hill East Suites
title: “A nice surprise”
text: We were a party of five: me, my wife, two kids and my mother-in-law. We were looking for two double bedrooms and had an excellent full two-bedroom apartment on 12th floor. By "full" I mean FULL: two large bedrooms with two queen beds each, two renovated bathrooms, one LARGE living room with dining room, a full kitchen and, the cherry on the top, a real solarium. The apartment was clean, the furniture is old style 60's in excellent shape. The location is also very good with many restaurants and transportation around. It does not have the services or the "luxe" of a 4/5 star hotel but I definitely recommend it.

name: Hotel Newton
title: “Great Hotel”
text: Just returned from a woman's trip to NYC. Stayed at the Hotel Newton for 2 nights. It was a great experience. The staff were wonderful. We arrived at 9:00 am on a Saturday and hoped just to store our luggage at the hotel until check-in time. The desk attendant checked to see if a room was available so we could go ahead and check in. He even upgraded our room to a junior suite without me asking. We were able to go to our upgraded room immediately. The room was comfortable and plenty big enough for the 4 of us. The small kitchen was perfect for a Zabar's take out meal and evening desserts. Subway line was 1/2 block away. Neighborhood was nice - close to good restaurants. I will definitely stay here again!

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Loved the UN Millennium!!”
text:
Awesome room, with a fantastic view of the Empire State & Chrysler & Pan Am Buildings. Great 70's retro decor!! Great location and a pool on the 30th floor overlooking the UN. 
Want to go back and stay there again!!

name: Hotel 31
title: “Great budget accommodation”
text:
In the New York October craziness, this was the only place with a decent price tag and good reviews, so I decided that for just a night I could bear to share the bathroom.
The hotel is old but very well kept, so that the wooden doorways and the semi-manual elevator add to his charme instead of being an issue. My room on the 8th floor was spotless clean, and spacious compared to other budget accommodations I visited in NYC (I remember a single room exactly twice the size of the bed). The window incorporates an A/C unit of the kind built in one piece half inside/half outside, and this caused some noise to get through.
The location is excellent: I got out of the 6 station to the sight of the Empire State Building, and in less than 5 minutes I was at the hotel. 
Very kind people at the reception. 
Would definitely stay again.

name: The GEM Hotel Chelsea
title: “Fun boutique hotel in Chelsea”
text: Location is near perfect especially if you prefer the west side. Easy to get up or downtown - lots of areas within a 1/2 hr walk. Very near ACE trains. Also tons of fun affordable restaurants on 8/9th aves. Very kind and pleasant staff. The room we had was small but the price was low for the overall quality of the hotel so no complaints. The rooftop was open and quite nice with a view of the ESB. I think you'll be happy with this place.

name: ONE UN New York
title: “fantastic views”
text:
Stayed here for 4 nights 14th to 18th April on our first visit to New York. Everything from the reception staff downstairs to the pool on the 27th floor lived up to the billing on this site. The room was large and clean, the bed was large,the bathroom large and the view was massive!
We overlooked the East river, Empire State Building and the Chrysler and could see all the way to downtown.
We had breakfast at Johns Diner which was great value for money with endless refills of coffee all for about £3-4.
The location was perfect for us, we had intended to stay near Times Square but after spending 15 minutes there one evening we thanked our lucky stars we were staying somewhere a bit less manic!!
All in all for $179 per night this was one of the best hotels I've stayed in.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Midtown - Times Square
title: “Quality has declined substantially”
text: I recently stayed at the Four Points by Sheraton Midtown, Times Square. I have stayed there several times before and the quality and the condition of the hotel has declined substantially in the last 6 months. Our room was not clean, and our bathroom sink barely drained at all. It took at least 10 minutes for the water to go down after using the sink. There were clumps of black hair on the carpet in our room. We were not able to open the safe in our room after putting in our code. We called the front desk to have it fixed. We then ended up with a safe that opened with any code that was put in (any combinations of numbers). We had problems with the internet going down and called for help. The person who helps with internet access was not available. One of three of the elevators was broken the whole time we were there. The room card system in the elevators takes so long to activate that by that time you miss your floor. In the past we were given vouchers toward breakfast. The hotel no longer does not. The street that the hotel is on is in a seedy neighborhood. In the past we overlooked that because the hotel was clean and a good value for the money. It is no longer that.

name: Hotel 17
title: “Great place - good value”
text:
Me and my girlfriend stayed from 19 - 22 of August. We had read the reviews here and made our decision based on that.
We were not dissappointed. The room was clean and suited our purpose. The bathrooms were equally clean, not to say spotless, and we never found them to be all occupied at once. 
The staff was also more friendly and helpful than what we were expecting ;)
The location is great! Quiet little street, with the excellent Grammercy Cafe for breakfast nearby. Easy walking distance to subway and to interesting surrounding areas.
Where I will stay the next time is a no-brainer.... This place does it for me.

name: The GEM Hotel Chelsea
title: “Fantastic Hotel & Staff!”
text:
The GEM Hotel in New York's Chelsa neighbourhood is a wonderful boutique hotel. It's located in a safe and clean neighbourhood with beautiful homes and businesses, upon entry you are always greeted politely by Jeffery - a wonderful and informative guest services representative. Take the smooth riding elevator upstairs to a spotless, well designed guest room with superior furnishings, hardware, and electronicsI I stayed for three days and it was perfect spot to enjoy all that NY City has to offer. You can book this property via Choice Hotels International.
Fitness centre, business centre - with computers and printer - perfect for printing maps, tickets and discount promotions for site seeing adventures. You will not be dissapointed!

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “Dificuldade no Chek in”
text: Apesar de haver pago antecipadamente a hospedagem em apto não fumante, cama king e andar alto, fui hospedado em apto fumante com cheiro horrivel. Após reclamar, recebi outro apto minusculo, cama pequena. Voltei à recepção, fiz nova reclamação e tive que aguardar no lobby do hotel cerca de 2 horas para receber outro apto conforme minha reserva. Mas, tive que aceitar em andar baixo - 6º andar.

name: Sheraton Tribeca New York Hotel
title: “Buon hotel, ubicazione comoda ma non bellissima”
text:
Buon albergo, buon rapporto qualità prezzo. La zona è centrale, a piedi si arriva facilmente al WTC, a Soho, Tribeca, China Town e a varie linee della metro. La zona certo non è elegante e di notte è variamente popolata, ma ci è sembrata sempre sicura.
Quattro anni fa ho soggiornato allo Sheraton vicino al Moma, zona migliore ma l'hotel non era a questi livelli: aveva camere piccole.
Allo Sheraton Tribeca le camere sono grandi, pulitissime, comode. Il letto è ampio e comodissimo, il cambio della biancheria (di ottima qualità) è quotidiano. Il set cortesia essenziale. La colazione, non compresa nel prezzo, costa circa 16 dollari (tanto) me è ottima. Per i clienti è a dsiposizone nella hall un buon numero di PC con stampante e collegamento a internet gratuito. Internet in camera è a pagamento, peccato.
Se vi occorre il trasferimento in aeroporto sappiate che il costo non è chiaro, insomma bisogna discutere il prezzo con l'addetto alle macchine, questa non ci è sembrata una cosa in stile Sheraton.

name: Sheraton Tribeca New York Hotel
title: “Bom custo benefício”
text: Bom atendimento. Localização próxima a 3 estações do metrô. Os quartos não são grande porém o serviço do hotel é impecável. A rua do hotel não tem um aspecto muito agradável porém basta avançar um quadra em direção ao Soho para estar num local de excelente comércio e bons restaurantes.

name: The Standard High Line
title: “Very pretentious”
text:
Stayed here in June 2012 for three nights. Had made contact with the Hotel before leaving NZ to request a room on floors 8 - 13 after reading other reviews about how noisy it is from the night club upstairs on 18th floor. Also contacted them to make same request on arrival in NYC three days arlier. We were put into a room on 15th floor which altough had AMAZING views of the Hudson River and Lower Manhatten was very noisy at night. The night club goes till around 3am, Thurs- Sat nights. We went up to the other bar on same level and were kept waiting for over 15 mins and so when we did not get served, walked out. Staff are very pretentious and if your not part of the glamour set and under 25 you dont seem to count. The rooms are very clean, very small but very groovy and well appointed although there was no tea or coffee facilities in the room. When I pointed this out the receptionist said all we had to do was ask, but for the huge tarriff I would have thought this was standard issue in all rooms. 
We were delighted with the views, best in NYC but not with service. Word of advice, dress up, try to look as gorgeous as the staff and A List guests and you might get some attention.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Midtown - Times Square
title: “over rated”
text: The rooms were very very small,but to be expected in a city hotel. They say free bottled water, well my husband and I just went, they gave us 1 bottle to share. When your spending hundreds of dollars on a room, they can afford to give each room 2 bottles.The view was of a brick building, however our shades were very thin mesh, so when they were pulled down for the night/morning, they could still see in like we could still see out, it gave no privacy nor did it keep the light from coming in our room early in the morning. The bathroom door is a frosted glass, but you can still see the person in the bathroom, again no privacy. The bathroom was so small, I had to keep the door shut to dry my hair because the sink was right up against the wall so when the door was opened it was in the way.There was no room to put any personal belongings in the bathroom either.The air conditioner was very loud,when it turned on, it would wake us up all night.The location wasn't great .However the staff was very nice, but that alone wouldn't get me back here. I love Sheraton hotels,but I will never stay at this one again.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Midtown - Times Square
title: “If you are arriving in the red eye this is not a good choiceVery”
text:
Very small lobby. Only seating is on a bench. Guests arriving on red eye had to stand around, painful to watch them. One morning when it was raining hard they were told they had to leave and come back at 2. There are no nice coffee houses or breakfast places in the area and tourist attractions don't open until 9 or 10 so I don't know where they all went but anyone coming in an early flight beware.
Our only problem was with the air conditioner, it broke one night and had to be replaced by another used unit. The tech said that he had 8 other air conditioner calls that evening. 
If you have breakfast in their. restaurant the a la carte menu is great, much better quality than the buffet. We found a good dinner for breakfast 3 blocks away on 9th. Ave. Everything else is fast food. Had a lovely pre-theater diner at PIo Pio within walking distance.
Our room was immaculate. All renovated. Great linens.
We did not mind the Parole Office next doors to the hotel not the parolees standing in line but we prefer a prettier and more quiet area such as Soho or Midtown.

name: The GEM Hotel Chelsea
title: “Nice adult hotel in Chelsea”
text: Stayed here for one night after seeing Oprah at Radio City. This was a great location away from the craziness of Times Square. The rooms are small, but very well put together with a kind of upscale feel. They do seem to cater to the gay crowd or business crowd, rather than families. The area is chock full of great restaurants and stores and you a a couple of blocks form the High line park. The bathrooms were very nice with a walkin shower with a rainfall shower head. The sink area did leave little room for toiletries. The service was GREAT!!! Everyone we encountered was very welcoming and warm. On the roof there is an open air deck with lounge chairs & tables to have your morning coffee or justt relax with a stunning view of the Empire State Bldg. I highly recommend the Gem Chelsea if you are looking for a laid back, upscale, quiet hotel in a great neighborhood.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Great hotel in perfect location!”
text: Stayed at the Hilton with my family for a long weekend. Hotel was clean and comfortable. Great location to everything. We all had a great time! Parking was a bit pricey, but hey, it's NY!

name: Room Mate Grace
title: “Excellent experience”
text: We stayed here for a night out in the city. We loved the hotel. The rooms are a little small, but you are staying in NYC right on times square. The hotel is nicely decorated. Each floor has a different wall paper. The pool area was great. The hotel bar has a service window that opens up to the pool. You can order your drinks without leaving the water. The sauna and steam-room were a nice touch as well. They are well kept and a nice relaxing touch. The front office staff was very nice and helpful. The beds were comfortable. Our room was very quite. We didn't hear any of the city noise. The late checkout was a nice touch as well. The room blackout curtains really helped us sleep in too. We did not eat the breakfast buffet so I do not know how it is. There were too many excellent food choices surrounding the hotel to stay in for breakfast. We will definitely stay here again for our next trip into the city.

name: Hotel 17
title: “Great for the price, good safe location”
text: I stayed here with a friend. The staff was accomodating, and safe location. The rooms were not luxury, clean, iron burn on the carpet, water stains on the ceiling, but they were worth the $65 a night for two beds in NYC. The location is really good, close to Union Sq, and 2nd Ave. I would stay here again if on a budget.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Perfetto”
text: Hotel stupendo, in posizione perfetta a due passi da central park, dai negozi della 5th av, dai teatri e dai ristoranti. Metropolitana vicinissima. Stanza spaziosa, letto comodissimo, personale cortese e disponibile. Lontano dal rumore, ma zona sicura. Da non perdere!!!

name: Room Mate Grace
title: “Room Mate Grace”
text:
If there were a 'Good' category, this would be in it!
Excellent location, a few minutes walk from Times Square. 24 hour desk (but practically no Reception area). Didn't need much 'service' but the technician responded quickly to a problem with the wifi. Interior swimming pool, a bit of a luxury, next to the (small but popular) bar. Pool only used by children during our stay.
Elevators to all floors; each floor decorated in a different colout scheme - 'jazzy' but tired. Our bedroom was small; the bed was on a raised 'platform' and the suitcases went under the bed - just as well as there was very little storage space - just a short rail to hang clothes. The fridge and ironing board were not needed. I guess the room gets hot in the summer but there is air-conditioning as well as heating. The 'bathroom' area was divided into a spacious shower, a separate toilet and a small area with sink (no plug) and mirror (and safe).
The room was cleaned daily but, despite deliberately NOT leaving towels to be washed every day, we were supplied with clean ones - unnecessary.
New York prices are not cheap, obviously, so I would recommend this hotel for its location but recommend a 'facelift' before too long.

name: Holiday Inn Express NYC - Madison Square Garden
title: “What a delightful place”
text: The girls decided to take a shopping holiday to New York. I'm so happy we stayed at the Holiday Inn Express MSG. We found the staff to be friendly and helpful. We only paid 129US for a very comfortable room. Would definitely stay here again

name: Hotel Newton
title: “Exceeded My Expectations”
text: Great Deal! The hotel quality exceeded my expectations when I stayed there. This hotel is currently rated 2 stars. My first time at a 2 stars type hotel in NYC. I usually stay at 3 plus types for the past 10 yrs in NYC. It's 2 stars because of the limited service (e.g. No Bellman). BUT the room was definitely a 3 plus stars type room. Clean and comfortable room. Nice room furniture and decoration. Lots of dining places in the area. Pharmacy and Starbucks are across the street. Subway is a block away. Walking distance to Uptown shopping (80's St.). Taxi to Midtown Manhattan is about $8. I'll definitely be back again. I highly recommend this place if the price is about $100 or below (US) per night.

name: Park Central
title: “Trés fonctionnel de part sa situation.idéal pour les cours séjours.”
text: Super bien situé, à proximité de tout, avec un personnel trés présent et réactif. A deux pas de Central Park, de Time Square, des Métros....Un peu chargé en Touristes...mais c'est NY!!! Chambres spacieuses, même si pour certaines, un peu obscures...mais, c'est NY et ses grattes ciels!!! Dommage qu'Internet soit payant, et géré par une sté exterieure... Bref, si c'est pas pour un mois, c'est l'Hôtel idéal!

name: Four Points by Sheraton Midtown - Times Square
title: “Good value in New York, Neighborhood can be an issue”
text:
We stayed for one night in April 2012 and would return. The hotel is clean and the rooms although small have a good set up for working. The staff is friendly and on Wednesdays (at least for the moment) at 5:30 is a Managers party with complementary BBQ and fun beers. We were unable to attend that but it is a nice touch.
There is a small bar in the front, and the bartender there is a real asset! His name is Lev and he is from Russia - intellegent, friendly and engaging. 
The location although close to Times Square can be iffy especially with the Parole Board building 2 doors away.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Average Hotel -- Poor customer service”
text: The Grand Hyatt basically is an average, convention-style hotel centrally located in the center of Manhattan. The best thing about the hotel is that it has a mini-market in the lobby, with very good food options, that is open 24 hours a day, which is very convenient if you want something quick to eat or a late night snack. The worst part about the hotel is customer service. It is abyssmal. It takes FOREVER if you order room service. And if you arrive late in the evening to check in, it often takes FOREVER to get a room--provided that the hotel has not given away your room notwithstanding the fact that you had a confirmed reservation which is what happened to me during my last stay. Because no rooms were available when I arrived at 11:45 p.m., the hotel gave me a parlor room used for wedding parties that had a coach with a pull out bed. (I'm serious.) I later got a so-called apology letter in which the Grand Hyatt's business travel sales manager admitted that "on occasion things like this take place." Next time I'm staying at the Intercontinental or Fitzpatrick, which are far nicer hotels in the same general area.

name: The Helmsley Park Lane
title: “Delante de Central Park”
text:
La zona es excelente!! Al lado del Hotel Plaza. Junto al edificio Appel. Delante de Central Park y junto a la parada de metro de la quinta avenida!!
Para las estrellas que tiene el hotel, la recepción está bien, pero las habitaciones tienen una decoración de hace 20 años y los baños son muy antigüos.
Pero la hubicación es perfecta, así que..........una cosa por la otra. 
No te dicen nada en la reserva y cuando llegas al hotel te dicen que tienes que pagar unos cien euros más si quieres vistas al parque.
A nosotros nos dieron una habitación con las cortinas rotas, y como yo con luz no puedo dormir, bajamos a recepción para que nos la cambiaran. La rotura era más que evidente se veía solo al entrar, y para un hotel de estas características, y de este precio me parece fatal!! Nos la cambiaron.
Voy a Nueva York este invierno otra vez y voy a otro hotel, cerca de la quinta avenida, justo en la manzana de detrás de este, más moderno, más nuevo, a 4 minutos de distancia de este y casi a la mitad de precio.

name: Le Parker Meridien
title: “Un des meilleurs hotels de New York”
text: Raffinement et décor sobre. Grande qualité de service. Petit déjeuner dans le restaurant de l'hotel (au Norma's)délicieux !

name: Room Mate Grace
title: “"rite after the new year"”
text: The location is very close to time square. If there is an negative to the location it would be that there's not a subway station close to the hotel. pool area was fun and exciting. If you stay over the weekend, check out the bar/night club, the music is good and the crowd is very nice. I recommend a table by the pool on the second floor.

name: Park Central
title: “Posizione ottmimale”
text: Dopo essere stato per 8 notti all'hotel Park Central devo tutto sommato dire di essere stato abbastanza bene, il personale è cordiale, la posizione (vero punto forte dell'hotel) è molto buona, infatti, l'hotel è situato sulla 7th Ave all'altezza della 55th se non sbaglio, ad una breve distanza da Time Square e poi la fermata della Subway è esattamente all'uscita dell'hotel. La nostra camera era in condizioni discrete, da segnalare però le fastidiose scosse che prendevo nel mio letto causa elettricità statica e la poca pulizia delle camere (intendo la rimozione della polvere e la pulizia del pavimento).Il soggiorno è piacevole e il rapporto qualità prezzo è molto buono. Favorito anche dal cambio euro dollaro ottimale, ovviamente.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Could be better”
text: The location is excellent - close to everything. Quite expensive. The lobby is very nice but the rooms need some improvements. The shower features are old, the bathroom is small. No complimentary internet. Everything is extra. The beds are comfortable. Very good fitness center. Very helpful staff - no problem here

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Lo Skyline con la "ESSE" maiuscola”
text:
Desidero recensire questo Hotel perchè ha reso il mio secondo soggiorno a New York indimenticabile.
Situato in una posizione strategica ideale,con il Chrisler Building proprio al centro della visuale e poco più a sud l'Empire State Building. A due passi da Grand Central Terminal, con Times Sq. raggiungibile a piedi (mai usata la metro per Times sq.) e vicina alla fermata metro che collega con l'Airtrain per l'aereoporto JFK. Le camere sono luminose,pulite e spaziose: Un comodissimo letto "queen-size" ed una vista su NY da mozzare il fiato. Unica pecca potrebbe essere l'assenza di una vasca idromassaggio (considerato il prezzo a camera per notte) ma è un particolare trascurabile.
Personale è molto cortese e disponibile.
L'hotel è in palazzo molto elegante e in una zona molto tranquilla anche in caso di rientro a tarda notte ( essendo adiacente alla sede delle Nazioni Unite la sicurezza non manca).

name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City
title: “Loin d'etre ce qu'ils pretendent”
text: C'est la deuxiemen fois que je reserve dans cet hotel et la premiere fois n'etait pas vraiment concluante, mais .. le hall de l'hotel est surchargé de monde avec un bar (le soir) qui passe de la musique tres tres forte, on ne s'entend pas parler. L'accueil est a la limite du respect, et ayant une grande habitude des hotels new yorkais, il ne faut surtout pas abdiquer. La chambre etait probablement l'une des pires que j'ai eu dans un hotel de new york, et finalement apres avoir ralé on m'a donné la chambre que j'avais réservée (grand lit !) mais pas vraiment au top. Les baggagistes vous font payer 2 fois la garde de vos baggages (1 fois lorsque vous les descendez et une fois lorsque vous les récupérez , ce qui est inhabituel a NY) et toujours a la limite du poli. Tout se discute et c'est fatiguant, l'hotel est assez bruyant (poste de pompier et de police a coté), vraiment si vous avez une autre solution évitez cet hotel qui est loin d'etre un 3etoiles et demi

name: Holiday Inn Express NYC - Madison Square Garden
title: “Good Choice for those on a budget”
text: I stayed in this hotel over Saint Patricks Day weekend. I got a great rate on Travelzoo. The Hotel is within an easy walk of Penn Central and is a good choice for those coming into the city by train. Their are two subways near the hotel and while it is not in one of the most stellar of neighborhoods, we felt safe walking back to our room at night. The hotel features your standard Holiday Inn express breakfast which was kept stocked. There was helpful staff who could book events for you. Rooms were tiny, but they were clean. The Hotel is in buisness area so their were few restaurants or other types of amentities close by, but plenty within a moderate walk or a subway stop away. Had a good stay in a great city and would stay again given a good deal.

name: Park Central
title: “tipico hotel newyorkese”
text:
Grande hall affollata, baretto poco invitante, portinai professionali, bel centro congressi con toilettes semipubbliche migliori di quelle della stanza...
Stanze pulite, ma almeno la nostra con vista su un cortile e su un muro, piccola, ma con tv a 42 pollici con programmi via cavo.
Bagni piccoli ma rinnovati e molto decenti.
Prenotando via web tramite Expedia il prezzo almeno a gennaio è conveniente.
Molto frequentato da equipaggi di compagnie aeree asiatiche.
Complessivamente, una buona scelta vista la posizione strategica (la metro è proprio sotto l'hotel) a due passi dai musei intorno a Central Park e vicinissima a Times Square.
Vogliono 3,5 dollari per valigia per lasciarle in albergo dopo il check out.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “OK but not great”
text:
For the tariff we paid to stay at the Waldorf, you would have expected a wonderful room, but on arrival at my room, I found it pretty average. I would have expected the bedspread/linen to be wonderful but was very disappointed. The bed was comfortable with lots of comfy pillow, but the whole room has quite an aged feel to it, not worth the price we paid.
It did have a fantastic view of the Chrysler building from our window.
We had breakfast one morning, but at $40 per person, expensive and very average. Why do American have to "cremate" their bacon, it so tough I couldn't eat it. 
Beautiful foyer with a lovely clock which chimes regularly. Also the price of their hot drinks was over the top, at about $10 each.
An experience to stay at the Waldorf, but I don't think I would stay there again.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Midtown - Times Square
title: “great hotel awesome value”
text: Very nice hotel in the times square area of new York. It was a short three block walk to times square and the theater district. Paid extra for a " city view" room but it wasn't worth it. Hotel staff was very friendly and helpful. Will definitely stay there again

name: The Standard High Line
title: “Wow! A hotel to remember”
text: My fiancé and I stayed here for 4 days and loved it. There is an great bar and lounge on the roof, a fun beer garden at street level which was full of folks having a great time and the restaurant was a true delight. The staff was very helpful whenever we needed anything including helping us with some shipping of items. They also gave great tourist attraction and restaurant advice and even a tip to get into a crowded restaurant. I love New York city and have visited numerous times and stayed in a number of different types of quality hotels, but The Standard is now my favorite. However it is on the hip side and definitely not the old fashioned elegant style of some of the other super nice hotels in the city. I didn't even mention the room or the interesting shower and glass wall or the views or the easy access to the high line... looking forward to another visit!

name: Hotel 31
title: “Basic but central”
text: Fine as a base for exploring NY and not wanting to pay too much - although every hotel room in NY is very expensive! Rooms were clean and shared bathrooms no problem - always clean and usually empty. Reception staff very helpful.

name: Hotel Newton
title: “Perfekt beliggenhed, væk fra støj og larm. Meget rent og venligt og hjælpsom personale”
text: Dejligt, dejligt hotel. Værelserne dog små, men skal man kun sove er det helt perfekt. Personalet meget venlige og hjælpsomme.Rengøringen er tip, top. Ligger lige ved 96 street's Subway, som transporterer dig enten til uptown eller downtown. Kan klart anbefale hotellet, hvis man ønsker at være væk fra støj og larm i selve City. Tager 5 min med subway til times suares, så meget tæt på centrum. Gåtur kan også anbefales

name: The Standard High Line
title: “This is a Must, No other hotel like it”
text:
Just returned back from 4 nights at the standard. All i have to say is do Not believe the bad reviews but indeed believe the hype because it is validated. 
Upon picking a hotel, i came across certain reviews that the staff were obnoxious, rude, not helpful and that the noise from the club on the 18th floor could be heard throughout the whole hotel. One word Ridiculous. 
I found the hotel absolutely amazing in every which way. The staff were incredibly friendly and all my requests were met fully without any problems. From the receptionist to the bell boys to the waiters, everyone smiled and was more than willing to help. 
The food at the standard grill which is where we had breakfast everyday was excellent, and this is noticeable from the amount of people who are not residents at the hotel who come to the standard grill for brunch or dinner. 
The room was very clean, the bed very comfortable and the room had a lovely fresh smell. 
And of course the view, floor to ceiling windows, truly breath taking. location is great bang in the heart of the meat packing district and easy access to the high line. The rooms are slightly on the small side but bear in mind your in New York, and the drinks in the bar on the 18th floor despite the amazing view which u have from ur room anyway are very overpriced. 
I don't usually write reviews but felt i had to this time as i spent allot of time in deciding what hotel to stay at, and i came across certain points that people complained about. I would like to say that whoever wrote that these comments clearly have a personal vendetta or have nothing better to do with their time. 
I would recommend this hotel to anyone, who is in New York wanting a fun and stylish experience.

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Ruhiges Hotel mit Blick auf den Hudson in Laufnähe zu Grand Central.”
text:
Das UN Plaza liegt etwas abseits des Trubels am Hudson und dennoch zentral. Die Reception ist sehr unfreundlich, aber wenigstens bekommt man seine Zimmerwünsche erfüllt. Freundlichkeit und Service sind Fremdwörter für die Damen und Herren der Reception und des Concierge-Services.
Große Zimmer, Sauberkeit für NY Standard o.k.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Great Location”
text: Just a few Blocks from Central Park, shopping on 5th Ave, the lights of Times Square and a Broadway musical. We spent a long weekend on one of the executive levels in a king room that was in need of an upgrade. (Rug stained and wallpaper dated) The room was clean the hot water plentiful and the bed was excellent. The exec. lounge was packed during the early evening hours and the morning continental breakfast had a line even though the room holds over 80 guests! This is a hugh property with a ton of guest each day.

name: The Standard High Line
title: “great stay-cation”
text: friendly staff, but not overly so. they keep it cool but know how to smile. excellent location to enjoy the high line, west village and high line. great restaurants nearby. loved our room. will definitely go back.

name: Hilton New York
title: “The hotel in NYC for me.”
text: Okay whenever I am in NYC this is the hotel for me. With nearly 2000 rooms, perfect location and fantastic rooms plus the great service why would I stay anywhere else.

name: Hotel 17
title: “hôtel 17 ,charme ancien,propre et bien situé”
text: Vieil hôtel typiquement New-Yorkais ,plein de charme , confortable pour sa catégorie,propre et très bien situé dans un quartier calme mais animé , pleins de boutiques et de restaurants à prix raisonnable pour New-York

name: Park Central
title: “extra bed”
text: Het is een prima hotel om in te verblijven met de wetenschap dat je de hele dag buiten bent. Wij hadden een extra bed voor onze dochter. Deze werd rechtop in de kamer gezet en kon ik dus zelf plaatsen en opmaken, dit was het enige min puntje, voor de rest een prima hotel wat zeer centraal ligt

name: Room Mate Grace
title: “LOVE IT !!!”
text: i went to the hotel for my 4 year wedding anniversary. It was perfect!! awesome pool, excellent breakfast with many choices , gym and great staff. The hotel walking distance to times square, shopping and tourist attractions. The room itself is great trust me if u could take the bed home you would it truly amazing! Also it was peaceful very quiet. The room is clean and great detail. We love the fact we can adjust the AC in the room .My husband loved there was a ipod dock because he forgot his iphone charger so the ipod dock was a life saver. So if you are thinking to come to NYC RM Grace hotel is the BEST!!!

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Hotel Millennium UN Plaza, ottimo ma con tariffe un po troppo alte”
text: Bellissimo hotel, ottima posizione a 3 o 4 isolati dalla metro, buono il personale, piscina e palestra gratuiti pur se non abbiamo avuto modo di Usufruirne, meglio passar il tempo x altro a NY, camere con vista empire e Chrysler Building dal 32° piano, un po' caro nonostante le promozioni expedia, ma ne vale quasi il prezzo.

name: Murray Hill East Suites
title: “Esta super bien ! buen tamaño del departamento,impecable !”
text:
Viajamos 4 de familia.el depto super comodo,muy limpio,muy bien ubicado!
Tiene todo,cocina,heladera,tostador etc,esta muy bien !

name: Hotel 17
title: “Uitstekende lokatie - tikkie claustrofoob”
text: Buurt zelf, maar ook nabijheid van Union Square metrostation zijn grote plussen. Keurige kamer, incl badkamers op de gang. Wel vrij klein, maar ja 'this is New York'. Alleen is alles erg donker, met daaraan bijdragend behang; en onze kamer had nauwelijks daglicht.

name: Hotel 17
title: “Parfait, idéalement placé et pas cher.”
text:
Hotel situé à 2min d'union square où l'on trouve toutes les lignes de métro, un parc juste à côté pour souffler après une journée de marche. Le personnel de l'hotel est présent et serviable le ménage fait régulièrement et sur demande, les sanitaires très propres et régulièrement nettoyés. Les chambres un peu vieillotes mais pleines de charmes et très bien équipées, lavabo, serviettes, sèche cheveux, TV, armoire, portes manteaux, clim, table de chevet, réveil électrique.
Absolument parfait, nous y retournons et vous le recommandons.

name: Park Central
title: “Lage, Lage, Lage!”
text: Die Lage des Hotels ist ideal. In walking distance, Times Square, Central Park, 5th Avenue, Museum of Modern Art, Rockefeller Center, Carnegie Hall gegenüberliegend und einige der besten Restaurants in New York. Sehr gutes Preis/Leistungsverhältnis. Die Getränkeautomaten funktionierten nicht auf allen Etagen. Gutes Frühstücksbuffet im Haus. Sehr saubere geräumige Zimmer in gutem Zustand.

name: Hotel 31
title: “Basic but value for money”
text:
Having never stayed in a hostel before this I was very apprehensive and scared that this would be a hell hole so to be safe we booked a room with our own bathroom.
However I did not need to worry as this hotel/hostel was basic but very clean and the bathroom was small but functional, the water pressure in the shower was very low but we were on the 12th floor.
The room was a little dated and quite small but it had enough room for our two large suitcases.
Tea and coffee making facilities were provided together with a t.v, alarm clock and an oil heater which we really needed and used.
The room was cleaned and beds made everyday and towels were changed.
I took a look at the shared bathrooms and they were spotless very clean and spacious. Having never stayed in a hostel before I had mistakenly assumed they would be shared as in several sinks and toilets and showers all in one room, but it was just a bathroom with a toilet, sink and shower with a lock on the door.
The location was excellent not too far from the main attractions.
If you are looking for a place to sleep for the night then this is perfect and I would definitely recommend this hotel/hostel.
If however you want to spend more time in your room then this place is not for you, the room in the day was very noisy from all the hooting from the NYC taxis on the main road etc and cold without the heating on.
Overall a good, basic, clean hostel to sleep in excellent value for money and I would definitely recommend it.

name: Hotel 31
title: “Does what it says on the tin”
text: Hotel 31 is acceptable for travellers on a budget who want a short stay in New York with no frills. This review is as unbiased as we can make it, accepting the fact that we had just disembarked from the Queen Mary 2 and, to be frank, just wanted to get back on. This wasn't really the fault of the hotel, so to be objective, it's clean and the beds are reasonably comfortable. The lift is very small and you will need to do lots of trips if you have more than a few suitcases. There is a great pizza place nearby, and it is well located for all New York's attractions. All I would say in detriment is that the soundproofing of the windows leaves a lot to be desired. New York is a very noisy city 24/7, and if you value peace and quiet then it might be better to spend (a lot) more and go somewhere with better noise insulation. As ever in life, you get what you pay for - Hotel 31 is reaonable value, but if you've got more than a few pennies, spoil yourself and go somewhere better.

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Qué vistas!!!”
text:
Las habitaciones están viejitas y tienen detalles un poco desfasados, pero su situación es francamente buena.
Poder tener una piscina y gimnasio en la planta 27 con vistas al East River y a Brooklyn, abierta hasta tarde, para poderte relajar despues de todo un dia caminando por NY es un capricho, pero las vistas desde algunas de las habitaciones son sencillamente fabulosas.

name: The Standard High Line
title: “my wonderful stay at the standard”
text: I just stayed at the standard high line in new york and had a wonderful time ,went there and could not have been treated nicer . very pleasant people at front desk really wanting to make you feel welcome .always a friendly hello when coming in and out more than happy to answer any questions . zack and tanya were great but not to forget Mr . Paul Kashman who was a pleasure to deal with , can't say enough about this guy. I WILL ALWAYS STAY AT THE STANDARD HOTEL FOR NOW ON BECAUSE OF HIM !!!

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Absolutly perfect!!!!”
text: We stayed at the millennium in late august in 2005. We requested a corner room and received it. We also checked in at 11:00 in the morning and got a room immediatly when check in is 3:00 pm. We had beautiful panoramic views of the east river form one window and the empire state building from the other. We were greeted by a bellman who went out of his way to help us out. He brought us a map and all 5 of our bags. We had mentioned that we wanted a microwave, but they said they didn't have one they could give us. the next day they brought one up with dishes and a complimentary coffee maker. Everybody we dealt with went above and beyond. everybody was polite and the room was immaculate and beuatifully decorated. people were always available in the lobby to help with directions. I would definatly stay here again in a heart beat!!!!!

name: The Standard High Line
title: “Mixed bag at the Standard”
text: I stayed here for 5 nights for a work/pleasure trip late November. First, don't get me wrong - this hotel is very popular and sort of exudes this hip urban vibe that is difficult to not want to be a part of. The location is excellent and for that alone, maybe worth the plus 500.00 a night room rate. For what this hotel puts itself out there as, however, it falls a little short. The rooms : while incredibly clean and well serviced every day, and fabulous views was like a dorm room. No room for luggage or clothing or toiletries. For a short trip workable, but this space crunch wore on me as time went on. The shower has a major design flaw - just a short piece of glass separating it from the rest of the bathroom - leaving water all over the bathroom floor every day which necessitated towels on the floor just to get ready. We were on the 14th floor with views of the Hudson - that was fab - and no noise from the club or the street below on that floor. We ate in the Standard Grill for breakfast - frankly awful service. They brought the wrong orders and when we pointed it out - the very surly waiter without a single word picked them back up and walked away. Really?? Your not that special. Save yourself the aggravation here. There are plenty of places nearby to eat with good service. The front desk staff was friendly but unhelpful. The concierge couldn't be bothered to even pick up the phone to see if we could get a restaurant reservation- telling us to just walk down the street and go on in and ask if we could get a table. Another really?? moment. Another concierge sent us to the gallery district in Chelsea. We specifically asked if the galleries had reopened since Sandy and he told us yes - ummm no. We went there - not a single first floor gallery open and only a handful of second floor galleries. I guess I should've googled. Who knew the concierge would lack the knowledge of such basics within the neighborhood of the hotel. Perhaps I'm picky - but when you go to a hotel such as this - these are basics that should be delivered stellarly. That just didn't happen here. The bell staff were the best and most helpful. Friendly guys who remembered you every day and were always offering to help. Nightclub? Impossible. Closed for private parties for several nights - which also means by the way that the hotel elevators are reduced from 4 to 2- as if the hotel guests are the afterthought. The decor is hip and modern, and there are always people around everywhere - lots of great shopping and restaurants. I might stay here again, but was disappointed with the service issues, micro room and shower flaw. It was cool- sure, but not very inviting and comfortable.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Nice, traditional hotel in a great location!”
text:
I have just gotten back from NYC, watching the US Open. During my stay the lobby entrance which connects it to the main lobby/reception was being restored. Not a problem, and after all, is was worth seeing it brand new!
I had an upgrade to a jr. suite and it was amazing. Lots of space for luggage, desk, drawers everywhere, eletronic safe, tv in both room and living room. Bathroom was OK, but I found it a little too small for a 5* standard.
Everyone at the front desk was always thoughtful and helpful towards all my needs. So was the bell service. Housekeeping did its job well everyday.
Good thing about the hotel is its location. It sits on an entire block between Park Avenue and Lexington Avenue, and 49th and 50th. (49th is the only street with no access to the hotel).
You can just walk to 5th Avenue or even to Times Square.
I wont't give this hotel a 5* rating because everything is way too expensive (USD 16 for a bottle of water, for example).
if you are looking for a traditional hotel with good service, great location and lots of glamour, this hotel will easily fit your needs. It has so much history that you can even have a tour of the hotel with breakfast included (cost of USD 50 per person, of course).

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “Welcome to New York”
text:
Welcome to NY, dat was het enige wat de receptioniste zei bij het inchecken. bij de vraag langswaar ik moest voor de kamer kreeg ik als antwoord 'elevators that way'
voor de rest moest je het dan maar zelf uitzoeken. Aan het kamernummer (1136) konden we afleiden dat we op het 11é moesten zijn. Een donker niet al te grote kamer, het lawaai van de airco was het eerste dat ons opviel als we de kamer binnenkwamen. Het was wel koel in de kamer, we zouden de airco dan maar afzetten om te slapen. We hadden gekozen voor PENN Club 5000; hierin is ontbijt(of wat er moet voor doorgaan) inbegrepen. gezien de Karige info die we gekregen hadden gingen we eens informeren bij de 'Bell Captain' waar en hoe laat te ontbijten. van deze kregen we een formeel 'there is no breakfast served', na wat aandringen deed hij toch de moeite om te informeren en bevestigde ons dat we inderdaad betaalden voor ontbijt in de Penn Club 5000 op het 12é. Terug in de kamer merkte we dat de airco niet alleen veel lawaai maakte, maar ook lekte. de vloerbekleding was doornat tot een meter voor de airco. gelukkig stopte het lekken bij afzetten van de airco. Terug naar de 'Bell Captain' dus... de volgende ochtend bleek dat onze toegangssleutel geen toegang verschafte tot 'Penn club 5000'. gelukkig liet een andere 'club-genieter' ons binnen. Na het ontbijt dus terug naar de 'Bell Captian' die de toegang voor ons verdere verblijf in orde bracht.

name: Hotel Newton
title: “qualite/prix”
text:
Chambres très propres, le personnel est très présent. Pensez malgré tout aux boules quiès car le système de climatisation à l'arrière du bâtiment est bruyant. Déco un peu vieillotte mais vraiment pas important. Frigo, micro ondes et cafétière avec dosettes à volonté.
Charles, à l'accueil, d'origine Haïtienne parle français et à été très prévenant avec nous alors que nous cherchions à repartir en Europe. Par ailleurs, il nous a fait une réduction sur la nuit supplémentaire que nous avons du passer sur place alors que bien d'autres hôtels en ont profité pour augmenter leurs prix.
autres atouts: en moins de 10 mn avec la ligne 2 vous êtes sur time square, vous êtes dans un quartier résidentiel et vous prenez votre petit déj' avec les habitants qui partent au boulot.

name: The Kimberly Hotel
title: “Large rooms in the heart of midtown”
text:
Although I'm not a fan of midtown, and I much prefer to stay downtown, I was traveling with my teenage son, so we needed two beds, plenty of room, and some privacy from each other.
Downtown hotels are extremely expensive, and geared toward couples (not the mom & son variety!). So I was forced to look midtown and chose the Kimberly for their wide variety of rooms, at a decent price.
I booked directly with the hotel in December for February 17-19, repeated all my requirements, including the date, and when I called back to confirm, they said you were a no show for January 17-19. I was outraged, as pretty much the first thing a reservations clerk should get right is The Date. 
Prices had gone up considerably since I had originally booked, but they honored the original price for a one-bedroom suite. They screwed up, but they made up for it. Can't fault them there.
Valet parking was swift and seamless, just the way I like it. As midtown is particularly busy, this was particularly important. We arrived early (10:00 a.m.) and our suite was already available for us. Another plus.
I opened the door, and the first thing I noticed was the Absence of Cigarette Smoke. Another plus. So many hotels say the room is no smoking, but they consider it no smoking if You don't smoke in there. Our suite was fresh smelling, clean, and Huge. Large kitchen, fully stocked with all the cookware you could ever need, large livingroom with pull-out queen sofa bed (my son said it was a bit uncomfortable, but being a teenager, didn't mind roughing it), and the master bedroom was huge and nicely appointed. Linens were high quality, the matress was comfortable, loads of pillows, and the comforter was a Very high quality down. Quite nice.
Bathroom was very small, but after staying in many NYC hotels, I've become used to that. Shower pressure okay, nothing great, but no real complaints.
Unfortunately, although my suite was no smoking, the Floor was not no smoking, and the hallways reeked of cigarettes. Not because anybody smoked in the hallways --- they didn't. But because the people in the suites across from mine were smokers, the fumes crept out into the hallway. Waiting for the elevator, outside Mr. & Mrs. Tobacco's suite, was brutal.
Hey Kimberly Hotel --- take a hint from your neighbors at The Benjamin: Make your entire hotel no smoking.
Beyond that, a glorious stay. As all our activity was downtown, we either walked or took the bus, and the bus stops frequently on Lexington Ave. (downtown bound) and Third Ave. (uptown bound), with many stops along the way.
People behind the lobby desk are a bit aloof, but they get the job done. The bellhops and attendants who open the door and help you out are Fantastic. Extremely well-mannered and cheery, without being intrusive.
If the Kimberly were downtown, I'd definitely stay there again. If you're looking for a midtown hotel with large, clean rooms, competitively priced, and comfortable accommodations, I'd recommend it.

name: Gansevoort Park Avenue NYC
title: “Een absoluut leuk hotel maar gehorige kamers, in elk opzicht”
text: In new York zijn recent een aantal nieuwe hotels bijgekomen. Een ervan is het gansevoort hotel, park avenue south. Een goede ligging, dichtbij de metro. Het hotel is redelijk tot goed. Een typisch design hotel waar er al vele van bestaan in ny. Geen top hotel. Voordelen zijn de gratis wifi, het zwembad en de ambiance, deze is hip te noemen. Het personeel is vriendelijk maar worden geselecteerd, zo lijkt het, ook om hun uiterlijk. Dit gaat wel eens ten koste van de service. Het grootste minpunt is de gehorigheid van de kamers. Dunne muren, je kunt alle gesprekken volgen, heel hinderlijk en kost je nachtrust.

name: The Hotel at Times Square
title: “Sono stata in questo hotel dal...”
text: Sono stata in questo hotel dal 31.12.2009 al 06.01.2010, confermo quanto detto dagli altri utenti: albergo in ottima posizione,vicinissimo a Times Square e alla 5th Avenue, pulito, più che buono il rapporto qualità/prezzo.Note negative: il personale della reception non è molto cortese, mentre tutti gli altri dipendenti dell' hotel lo sono e la presenza di un unico ascensore per le stanze dal 3° al 11° piano. La colazione inclusa nel prezzo, non è niente di specialee, ma va bene.

name: Ameritania Hotel
title: “Great location, friendly staff”
text: My stay at Hotel Ameritania was excellent. The rooms were clean and the bed was very comfortable. I priced several hotels in the area and found that Ameritania had the best value. The location was great. Times Square and other key locations were very close. The staff were great and professional. They made me feel welcomed as soon as I walked through the door. Excellent overall experience.

name: Comfort Inn Lower East Side
title: “Fantastic Little Gem”
text:
We stayed here when we went to see a friend perform at a pub nearby and it was wonderful. The staff are all very friendly and helpful. The hotel is very clean (my biggest problem with hotels in general) and looks new. The hotel has a free continental breakfast which is very nice and free WiFi as well. 
The rooms are tastefully decorated but tiny. I don't know if they are smaller than the average NYC hotel room (first time in a hotel in NYC), but the hospitality and cleanliness make up for it in droves. The bed is comfortable. We will definitely stay there again.

name: Ameritania Hotel
title: “Nice updates, good price, but still feels old”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Ameritania on a recent weekend trip to NY. We got a great price for it, so we didn't have our hopes up as far as quality goes. It's safe to say that the hotel surpassed our modest expectations. The lobby is modern, the service was very friendly and helpful, and our room was comfortable and well appointed. 
There were a couple of things that made me wish there was an option for 3.5 stars, however. We stayed on the 2nd floor, so we opted to take the stairs to our room. Although this was convenient, it was clear that the stairs had not been touched in the recent renovations. It honestly looked like a scene out the "The Shining" with peeling paint, leaky pipes, and too much grime for comfort. Similarly, when I went looking for a place to get ice, I found some very creepy and dirty spaces (with the doors open) that were being used for housekeeping, etc. It was eery to say the least. 
I very much enjoyed my stay and was pleasantly surprised by my room and the service, but make no mistake- this is not a 5 star hotel.

name: Hotel 17
title: “hotel 17 - nja”
text:
nonchalant och ibland direkt otrevligt bemötande i receptionen.
slamrande varmvattenrör gick upp rakt genom rummet bredvid sängen.
varning för hotellets taxttjänst - verkar vara receptionskillens kompis som kör svarttaxi. tullavgift skulle ingått i depositionen men gjorde det såklart inte...
sammantaget ett tveksamt hotel att bo på, egentligen bara läget nära union square samt möjligen priset som motiverar.

name: Room Mate Grace
title: “Cool hotel in great location, 2 minor faults”
text:
