We really enjoyed our stay at this hotel, it's perfectly placed for exploring Central Park, Empire State, Rockerfeller, Times Square and 5th Avenue, all within walking distance. Out room was cosy yet funky, although my two minor faults are:
1) The lighting in the bathroom was not bright enough - Could barely see to apply my make-up and I came back with very bushy eyebrows!
2) There was no towel rail or hook to hang the towels on, so they didn't dry properly between uses. We wouldn't have had them washed as often if there was somewhere to dry them.

name: The Standard High Line
title: “Great Look, Great View, Great Food, small room!”
text: I enjoyed my stay. i loved the view from the King Deluxe suite on the 7th floor overlooking the highline. That was my favorite. The bathtub was amaaazing. I wish the room was a little bigger. Felt a little tight.

name: Affinia Gardens
title: “Just right”
text: An all round good hotel. Excellent staff, always willing to help, not in the least pretentious, nothing too much trouble. We paid $229 plus tax for a room on the fifth floor, overlooking the small garden. Whilst not being luxury the rooms are comfortable, spacious, in a good area and the kitchen is a real plus. 5 minutes walk to shopping, restaurants and subway. A longer walk will get you to Central Park. I would not hesitate to return.

name: The Kimberly Hotel
title: “Fantastic place to stay!”
text: We have just come back from a 3 night break in New York with our 3 year old son having had a fantastic time. We booked at the Kimberly Hotel last minute when an appartment company let us down... and we were so glad that we ended up here! The location is great, staff couldn't have been more helpful (suggesting child-friendly restaurants etc). Suites were very roomy and well furnished - beds were amazingly comfy!(although we overlooked the air-conditioning units at the back of the adjacent hotel). The breakfast at the adjoining restaurant was a bargain $10 buffet and they didn't charge for our son! We will definitely be staying here again. (More comfortable and better value than the Waldorf Astoria where we stayed last time!)

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Excellent stay at Waldorf”
text: We rented three rooms at the Waldorf Astoria. Everything from the staff, to room service, to the restaurant was excellent. My granddaughter's complaint when we got home was that her bed mattress was not as comfortable as the Waldorf's. Everything was spotless. You would never know that this hotel is over 100 years old.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Great choice in Midtown”
text: Stayed here over New Year so the hotel was very busy although because it is large and spacious it never felt crowded. We had a corner room on the 29th floor so it was nice and quiet - in terms of street noise that is! Walls are paper thin so you do hear your fellow guests some times and doors banging shut can be a nuisance. Room was large and spacious, very clean and the bed was extremely comfortable. No fridge, mini-bar or coffee maker though. Bathroom is small but adequate. Location is great and because there are so many eating choices close by, we didn't actually use any of the restaurants in the hotel.

name: Hotel Newton
title: “Für den Preis OK”
text: Ich war 12 Tage im Newton und hatte ein Gemeinschaftsbad. Di Lage ist Top und liegt direkt Ecke Broadway 96th Street. Das Zimmer war ok, ist aber ein wenig lieblos eingerichtet und hatte nur eingeschränkte Ablagemöglichkeiten. Das Zimmer ist nicht vollkommen ruhig aber erträglich. Die Ausgangslage ist hervorragen und alle Punkte in Manhatten und Umgebung sind sehr gut zu erreichen. Das Bad ist neu renoviert gewesen und von der Hygiene sehr gut. Das originale amerikanische Frühstück bei Key West Dinner ist empfehlenswert und allein von der Atmosphäre ein Erlebnis .

name: Hotel Pennsylvania New York
title: “TRès décevant”
text:
Le hall d'accueil est un vrai hall de gare.
Pour un prix de 300 dollars, nous avons eu une chambre respirant la poussière et plus que petite, avec un mini-bar vide.
Nous avons donc demandé une autre chambre plus correcte et avons eu une chambre toujours aussi petite, mais toujours aussi minable vu le prix. Lors de ma réservation sur internet, la chambre prévue (avec photo) était superbe, 23 m2. Je ne le recommaderai à personne. Par contre, l'hôtel est super bien situé.

name: Hotel 31
title: “Excellent Location”
text:
Travelled to NY on a weekend break only problem was that we were on a budget.
On the plus side the hotel is in an excellent central location. Expected the rooms to be small and they were but having shopped around knew that hotels that cost a lot more were just a small so not a problem. The decor and old fashioned lift were scarily gothic but I quite like it. Receptionist was very friendly.
On the negative side our loo flooded raw sewage into the room and it took a while to sort out and my friend had kill a cockroach whilst I screamed like a girl. There was also a problem with the booking for friends who had booked nine months before (and confirmed several times) an ensuite room, but found there were none available upon arrival. They were given a room with a shared bathroom that was clean enough if you got in early, and were charged less (and the room had a great view of the Empire State Building) so they weren't too unhappy.
Cost us £150 each for 3 nights. Would recommend the hotel if you are going to New York to shop, wine and dine and need a place to lay your head on a budget. Friends stayed at the Grand Union Hotel around the corner which cost the same but was cleaner and more spacious.

name: Hotel 17
title: “certainement un des meilleurs qualité/prix de Manhattan”
text: quartier et rue calmes 5 mn du métro à Union Square (très nombreuses lignes) à 2 pas d'un café/cafeteria(petit déjeuner) literie et salles de bain impeccables murs et cloisons épais (on n'entend rien des autres chambres

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Walled-off Astoria”
text: Just stayed at this hotel, the third time in my life and probably my last. Arriving at the hotel I discovered that the hotel's main entrance on Park Avenue has been walled off, a fact not disclosed anywhere on the the hotel's website. But that physical appearance,due to ongoing construction faithfully symbolizes what is going on inside this property. The guest feels unwelcomed and shunned. The Front Desk staff is robotic even when feigning joy as they "congratulate" you on the important occasion that brings you to the Big Apple. The Concierges show complete apathy, disdain and ineptitude when making recommendations. The Lobby bar staff shoos you away if you dare step into their domain within 30 minutes of closing (1 am on a Saturday!). When criticized about this, the bar host cited "a NY law that requires the bar to stop serving customers 30 minutes before the bar closes." The housekeepers sound like a stampede as they start their day apparently gossiping aloud at an ungodly early hour in the hallway's supply room. No need for an wake-up call here. The physical plant is sorely outdated and unkept, albeit clean. The buttons on the antique room phones and remote controls have even lost their spring. The rooms smell musty and the a/c is sorely inadequate in the peak summer heat. Overall, stay away feom this hotel until further notice unless you want to feel walled off in the Astoria.

name: The Standard High Line
title: “Had a great experiance from strat to finish!”
text: Lots of fun on this staycation! We are manhatanites and want to do it again...

name: The Standard High Line
title: “Hip NYC Hotel That's Also Welcoming”
text: If you want to experience downtown, this is the hotel to do it at. I used to stay on at the Soho Grand, and have stayed at the Thompson Lower East Side , Morgans, and Gild Hall in the past year, but The Standard is far and away my favorite. The location is perfect, the view lovely, the staff friendly (not distant as in some hip hotels). The resto & bar scene is superb. And I am a born & bred New Yorker.

name: Hotel 31
title: “I'd stay there again...”
text:
My husband and I stayed at Hotel 31 for 3 nights in mid-October. The room was small, but for as much time as we spent in the room it was fine. We had a shared-bath room, but were conveniently located to 2 baths, and never had to wait except for each other, just as we would in any hotel room. The bathroom was clean, the rooms were clean enough, and it was surprisingly quiet in the hotel considering all rooms were full.
The location was very convenient for us, just a few buildings from Park Ave. and the neighborhood was fine even very late at night, though I didn't travel alone. 
I'm glad we stayed so cheaply - I'd rather spend the money on all the other fun things in NYC.

name: The Kimberly Hotel
title: “Très bon rapport qualité-prix”
text: Hotel très bien placé dans la 50ème rue. Suites spacieuses avec chambre séparée, cuisine et salon avec sofa pas très confortable mais correct. Personnel très attentif et serviable. Hotel refait mais dans un style ancien.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Hotel Edison”
text: Excelente localização, átrio excelente, corredores velhos, quartos a necessitarem de recuperação, tudo com ar demasiado gasto, janelas a isolarem mal som e frio. Mas a localização é espectacular, Times Squre a 50 metros!

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Hôtel super bien situé à Time Square... mais très bruyant, dommage”
text:
Nous étions au 18ème étage côté rue et il n'y a pas de double vitrage, les bruits se font entendre dès 3 heure du matin, les boules Quies sont indispensables.
Quand vont-ils changer leur vitrage ????
J'étais déjà venu dans cet hôtel en 2007 et avait dormi côté cour, beaucoup plus calme.
Le petit déjeuner est copieux, et vous avez le choix entre les oeufs bacon, pancake ou toasts et croissant.
Le personnel est rapide pour le service et fidèle. Certains travaillaient déjà ici en 2007.
Les chambres sont en 2 parties , une avec le couchage assez exigüe et l'autre avec un grand salon , canapé et une TV. Pratique quand on ne dort pas et que l'on ne veut pas réveiller son conjoint.
Le grand point fort de cet hôtel est sa situation géographique, tout près des salles de spectacle, de central park, des métros, du rockfeller center des magasins pour le shopping.
Une adresse à recommander avec une chambre qui ne donne pas sur la rue.
New York se vit dehors après tout !!!!!!

name: Club Quarters, opposite Rockefeller Center
title: “Nice Hotel”
text: The Club Quarters at the Rockefeller Center is a quite new hotel of the chain. Rooms are as in every Club Quarters equipped with free Wifi and directl dial phone which makes it perfect business trips as well as the central location. I booked a room with a kitchenette as bothing else was available. Everything was perfect and clean.

name: ONE UN New York
title: “Fantastisk utsikt”
text: Rent och fräscht hotell med utmärkt läge, stora rum (för att vara NY) och möjligtvis stans bästa utsikt. Bra service och bekvämligheter såsom gym, tennisbana och pool (simma med utsikt över Hudson River och Empire state!) Kommer absolut återvända till detta hotell.

name: Hotel 17
title: “Ottimo rapporto qualità/prezzo/posizione”
text:
Ho pernottato 4 notti in questo albergo scelto leggendo le recensioni tra cui anche quelle di questo sito.
Cercavamo un sistemazione in centro ma ad un costo congruo.
L'Hotel 17 si è dimostrato eccellente.
La posizione è centralissima, ben servita dalla metro (un paio di isolati) e con dei buoni ristoranati. La zona è molto graziosa e sicura.
Il personale è cordiale e disponibile, anche nel consigliare come esplorare la città (senza per forza volerti vendere un tour organizzato).
Le stanze sono abbastanza ampie (più piccole comunque della media di quelle americane) ed arredate in modo funzionale (appendini al posto dell'armadio).
La struttura non è recentissima ma è ben tenuta e soprattutto pulitissima. Anche i bagni in comune (che prima della partenza mi preoccupavano un po') si sono dimostrati sempre pulitissimi (li puliscono più volte al giorno); in 4 giorni quello vicino alla mia camera non l'ho mai trovato occupato.
In camera (almeno nella mia) è presente il lavandino (e questo contribuisce a decongestionare i bagni comuni).
Io ero all'ultimo piano, con vista sull'empire state building (una porzioncina); sistemazione silenziosa tranne che per il condizionatore (un po rumoroso di notte).
Vivamente consigliato a tutti coloro che vogliono restare in centro ad un prezzo corretto.
Quando andrò nuovamente a New York sicuramente tornerò qui.

name: Candlewood Suites New York City Times Square
Hilton New York
title: “Will never stay here again”
text:
We stayed here on our visit to the USA from Melbourne Australia.
We arrived at 1am which we had notified them of this prior as we had a late flight.
Check-In was smooth and easy.
We arrived in our room to find a terrible smell, it was smoke like so we rang to tell them of this their answer was to come up and spray it with a peach smell spray which made it worse it stunk they would not change us rooms so we had to put up with it which I found really hard. If we had not pre paid for the hotel I would have found somehwere else.
I took my shoes off to find that the carpet was sticky not just in one spot the entire carpet was like this so I had to wear my shoes from the bathroom to the bed because of the dirty feeling. 
I layed down on the pillow to find it smelt of vomit so we left the pillow with a note the next morning. And the beds are really uncomfortable because the bed rolled in to the middle. Which had us amost on top of each other.
We had to keep the window open because of the smell which had its downside the noise.
It was really old and rundown with rust and paint peeling in the bath room. The functionallity of the bathroom was terrible fancy putting a bench above a toilet. Lets just say my kids managed to knock a few things in there while they were going to the toilet. There was also very little space to put our things in the bathroom.
On our first night when we arrived at 1am we forgot to put the do not disturb sign on but you would think they would have let housekeeping know that we only arrived a few hours ago at 9am they were at our door.
The other thing that I found a problem we booked for 2 adults 2 children but in our room they only had 3 towels. Now I dont think its that hard to provide enough towels when we have said how many people were staying. We were then made feel like a hassle asking for another towel.
They also charge per bag to hold your bag. If we had thought about it we could have held our room for 4 more hours as we checked out at 9am so they could have access to the room but when we went to put our bags in we were charged 3.50 per bag.
To add to the terrible stay I had just bought a new suitcase a samsonite hardcase and when we went to get in the taxi even through my husband went to do it himself the bellman threw it in the cab putting a huge deep 5cm gash in the case. Our other cases never got this and we had flown 5 domestic legs and one international. Really poor and terrible service.
We will never stay here again and likewise will not recommend it to anyone.

name: Hotel Newton
title: “Ein günstiges Hotel mit großartigen Service”
text: Wir waren 2 Wochen in Manhattan und waren sehr froh dieses Hotel gebucht zu haben. Wir haben ein besseres Zimmer bekommen als wir bei Expedia gebucht hatten. Das Hotel hat eine sehr gute Lage auch wenn man in der 94. Straße wohnt. Nicht nur die Metro sondern auch die Linienbusse oder Sightseeinh Busse halten vor der Tür. Zu Fuß lernt man Manhattan wesentlich besser kennen. Zu den Sehenswürdigkeiten hat man es nicht sehr weit. Der Zimmerservice ist hervorragend. Man bekommt jeden Tag neue frische Handücher, Betten werden gemacht und vieles mehr. Wir würden wieder das Hotel buchen, wenn wir einen weiteren New York Urlaub planen.

name: Candlewood Suites New York City Times Square
title: “Zentral, vollständig, gut”
text:
Das Candlewood Suites liegt direkt hinter dem Staybridge Suites.
Erste Eindruck gut, sauber, schneller Check-In, man durfte am Glücksrad drehen für kleine Sachpreise, eine nette Geste.
Die Zimmer wirken neu, geräumig mit kleiner Küche und bequeme Bett. Kaffeekocher, Fernseher, Safe, schickes Bad und kleiner Schreibtisch.
Das Internet ist inkl. und ist gut zum Arbeiten geeignet.
Fazit: Gute Alternative für Aufenthalte in NewYork Manhattan.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “EDISON HOTEL NYC”
text:
On voit Times Square par la fenêtre, et on est à 10 minutes à pied de tous les théâtres, ça compense bien le fait que la clim soit bruyante !!!
Par contre le café est un peu triste, peu attractif: lui préférer le "DELI" sur la 47th St, tout de suite à droite en sortant, ou le Starbucks juste en face..

name: Candlewood Suites New York City Times Square
title: “Topp plassering uten romservice”
text: TIl den prisen var plasseringen av hotellet helt topp. 5 minutter fra Time Square. Eneste minuset var at de bare ordner romet én gang i uka. For vår del som var der i åtte dager betydde det at de kom med tilbud om å skifte på sengene kvelden før vi skulle reise. Men på den andre siden, hvem bytter på sengene hjemme flere ganger i uka?

name: The Kimberly Hotel
title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
My husband and 18 year old son and I stayed at the Kimberly 1-4 September 2004 and we had a great time. What a great asset the doormen Gregory and Jose are - always smiling and helping out - I would go back just to see them at work again!
The one bedroom suite was clean and roomy(the king size bed had the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in) and the hotel is in an excellent location - within walking distance of most places but also near the subway.
The 3 hour boat trip was very good - what a fantasic way to see New York in the evening. 
We would recommend this hotel to anyone and hope to go back one day.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York - Chelsea
title: “Great experience.”
text:
I have only positive things to say about the Hilton Garden Inn Chelsea. I chose it for it's location, and for the fact that the rooms have mini fridges and microwaves, since I was travelling with my 2 children. We had a city-view room on a high floor and never had to wait long for an elevator. The room was very clean - very good housekeeping staff. There was plenty of space to move around. We had 2 queen beds. There was a closet with at least 10 hangers, a dresser with 4 large and deep drawers that fit all of our things. I could stow a suitcase in the closet, and another one on top of it. Plenty of room to pass in between the beds and the desk. The bathroom was also pretty big. Housekeeping supplied replacement bath products daily - the towels were soft - the bedding was comfortable - and every day we were supplied with a coffee filter pack and sugar and cream. The thermostat worked well, and we survived the 105 degree heat index with the wonderful airconditioning. There is a little shop in the lobby where you can find just about anything from aspirin to microwave meals. There is a restaurant, but the food is delivered from a nearby restaurant... Mustang Sally. 
Regarding the area, the hotel is located between 6th and 7th Ave. There is a Mc Donald's across the street and a Starbucks on both avenues, a bank and 2 big drug stores on 6th Ave. I was surprised by the fact that the grocery stores on 6th Ave did not display any prices, but we were really happy to find a Whole Foods on 7th Ave, around 24th street. The hotel is only 6 blocks away from Macy's Hearld Square and Penn Station, and it's not a long walk to Times Square. There is a 1 train on the corner of 7th Ave., and the N & R trains 2 blocks down on Broadway.
The room was just like the photos that are posted on their website.
I would definitely stay here again on my next trip to NY: helpful staff, clean hotel, good location.

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Super location, aber eher laut”
text: Das Edison ist zwar super gelegen am Times Square, jedoch ist es in den meisten Zimmern ziemlich lärmig. Wir dachten wir hätten einen super-deal gefunden denn die Übernachtung war sehr günstig; das Zimmer war jedoch sehr klein und die Gänge und Zimmer sind generell sehr hell/ringhörig, sprich wir wussten immer wann unsere Zimmernachbarn zu Hause waren. Trotzdem, die location machte vieles wieder wett.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Midtown - Times Square
title: “Great location clean comfortable room”
text: I stayed in this hotel for 10 nights with my partner arriving half way through our stay. IT was in a fantastic location. The bed was excellent and there was plenty of room. The only negative was the restaurant we had room service one night, which was terrible for the price, but what do you expect I guess.

name: Hotel Newton
title: “gutes Hotel für Stadturlaub”
text: Für einen Stadturlaub in New York ideal.Subwaystation fast vor der Haustür.Mit den Expresszügen nur zwei Stationen bis zum Timmes -Quare.Freundlichkeit und Service im Hotel sehr gut.Gleich neben dem Hotel gibt es mehrere Möglichkeiten zum Frühstück.Nebenan ein Drogeriemarkt, der 24h geöffnet hat.Kann das Hotel zu 100% weiter empfehlen.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Great service!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at the Grand Hyatt for a week in July, and we had a lovely stay! The location of the hotel is just right, within walking distance of places like madison/lexington/park avenue and also within close proximity to central park and times square. And as Central Station is only next door the subway is also very close by. 
We were greeted by a very sweet and helpful member of staff at the front desk when we checked in, and she was very accommodating when I asked for a quiet room without connecting doors. And when I came to realize that my booking only included breakfast for one of us, she checked with her manager and then gave me six additional breakfast vouchers. I found her helpfulness and service to make a great first impression and like other people have written on this page, when the service is so great it doesn't really matter if the rooms are a little bit dated. We will return for sure!

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites New York Manhattan / Fifth Avenue
title: “Small but perfect for the weekend”
text: This is a new, clean, modern hotel. The location is excellent, close to Macy's and Times Square, and just a short walk from Penn Station and the Garden. The staff was excellent and the Bellman was great at giving us recommendations and direction. The breakfast is one of the better hotel ones that I have had. The rooms are small, but its a big city so this is what I expected. Would not want to spend a weekend there but if you are coming for a night or two and can get this place for a good rate then book it. Oh and best part of all they have a luggage room that they will hold your luggage for you if you are flying in.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Midtown - Times Square
title: “Relaxing stay except for the taxi cab experience”
text: I stayed with my husband and daughther (12 yrs old). The hotel bed is indeed one of the nicest and comfortable bed we ever slept in. The room is very clean yet small to get a round with 2 beds in the room. Great location and very close to Authority Port so got to experience the subway to get to Central Park. The hosekeeping and front desk staff are very friendly. The only thing I didn't like about our stay is the taxi cab service. When we tried to reserved the shuttle with the Conceirge rep a day before our departure (8/21). He advised us to take taxi for $45 to JFK Airport instead of the Shuttle ($22/person). On the day of our departure, the hotel lobby attlendant called the taxi cab. It wasn't one of those typical yellow taxi cab and we were charged $65 to JFK Airport, which is more than what we were told or expected. To my surprised, I called the hotel to confirmed and this time the hotel front desk rep confirmed that it is $65 to JFK and La Guardia Airport is $45. I thought we were over charged because I checked those yellow cab as walking by times square it says on there the cost between Manhattan and JFK is $45 flat rate. It was very disappointing and next time we know better not to have the hotel call taxi cab on us.

name: The Standard High Line
title: “Amazing hotel-will definitely be back! Holiday of a life-time!”
text:
We arrived in style with a chauffeur and were immediately treated like stars. We received a friendly, trendy welcome and were given a free upgrade to a stunning corner room with a huge double bed, an open bath next to the floor to ceiling windows, a see-through shower and a large seating area. With floor to ceiling windows on all three sides we had exceptional views of the Hudson river, the Empire State Building and the Statue of Liberty-amazing, esp at night!! We enjoyed breakfast in The Grill, and drinks in the Living Room bar and in the Biergarten. Although, we were disappointed that we were unable to go the rooftop bar. We also had room service a couple of times which we thoroughly enjoyed. With such an amazing room, we did not want to leave the views but had a fantastic time seeing all the sights in central New York and also enjoyed the less crowded meatpacking district during the day in its cafe's and Chelsea market. In the evening the area around the hotel comes alive with people flocking to the hotels bars and those around it.
This holiday was an experience that we will never forget because of the fantastic city and because of the fantastic staff and overall aurora of the hotel!
Thank you so much for a dream stay and we will definitely be back!

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Good hotel”
text:
Pro: location, large room, clean
Cons: internet access $10/day, a bit noisy, a bit too expensive 
We booked through a promo $240/night pre-paid non-refundable. I knew the hotel, I paid previously $400/night and swear I would not return. But for $240 was acceptable (I had to do the booking in a rush). Room was fine this time. I hate when they request a lot of money for internet access, seems like a luxury. HELLO!!! it should be like electricity nowadays! Imagine paying a fee per day for electricity...

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Das Hotel für den Kurztrip zum Big Apple!!! Sauber, freundlich preiswert und asolut zentral”
text: Für einen Sight-Seeing Trip einfach optimal. Kein schmuddeliges Hostel aber auch kein übertriebener und teurer Luxus. Sauber beguem freundlich und vor Allem absolut zentral. Ein Hüpfer und man ist mitten im Big Apple.

name: The Standard High Line
title: “Biggest room, worst service”
text:
We booked several rooms at the Standard including the Empire Suite, the largest suite, which cost over $1800/night++. Our total bill was well over $5000 for two nights for our rooms, F&B, etc., so our expectations were high. They were not met. My review will be about the Empire Suite.
Check-in
Despite having emailed ahead of time, my name was not added to the reservation made by my friend. I was told I would need to wait for 40 minutes for a meeting of hotel managers to end before checking into my suite, despite showing them the email confirming. 
When I checked in, finally, I was told that the room had mechanical issues. We waited until after 4:30, and eventually were checked-in. There were light fixtures in the room.
Room service
We called several times the first night for turn-down service. They never came. When they cleaned the room the next morning, they changed the sheets etc., but never tied up. In any 5-star hotel I had stayed at, and any time I book a suite, the staff will tidy amenities, etc. At the Plaza, they will dry-clean/iron your clothes. Nothing.
Club
We reserved tables at Le Bain, the Standard's club. Despite having a reservation on my phone, again, when I arrived to check in, I was told I had no reservation. When I showed an email from the club's manager to the bouncer, the bouncer informed me that he was not sure who the manager was. After a few minutes, the situation cleared up and we were shown a table. The club was great, and our hostess was fantastic.
General service
Several times we called for Blackberry/iPad/iPod chargers and were told simply "we do not have any." A good hotel will either offer to buy them for you, or tell you where to get them. Nothing of the sort.
The room
The room was stylish with a fantstic view, but lacked expected amenities and several items were broken. The television in the dining room was broken, and would not turn on. The lighting panels in the bedroom and in the dining room were spotty at best. There was no automatic curtain system, so you literally had to step over couches, the hot tub, etc. to close the blinds in the room. The "guest" shower (the smaller of the two) had watermarks all over the glass and floor, indicating that it had not been thoroughly cleaned.
In general, we were there for a good time, so we did not really care; however, for having the most expensive room in the place for several nights; for having spent thousands of dollars in the restaurant and bar, we expected much more. I will not stay at the Standard again. 
Now, about the positive:
People: The staff, while sometimes unhelpful, are pleasant and stylish
Design: The hotel, while minimalist, is stylish and hip
The clubs: Can't be beat in NYC, though the Boom Boom Room was not open
The food: The F&B venues on-site are amazing, and the service 5-star
The location: Washington and 14. Can't beat it.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York - Chelsea
title: “A short walk to walk to all the attractions”
text: Certainly not the best position in NYC, but great value for money. It is a lovely, yet simple hotel, has just what you need at the end of a long day as a tourist. We stayed here 2 nights with our 3 year old twins. The staff were really friendly. There was a nice little snack shop to get cereal, frozen meals, chips etc. Would definitely recommend as a slightly cheap alternative in NYC.

name: Hotel Newton
title: “Sauber und in guter, schöner Lage”
text: Nette, schöne und relativ ruhige Gegend mit vielen kleinen Läden, Supermärkten, Restaurantes aller Art ums Hotel. Zimmer sind sehr sauber, auch das Bad! Ein Doppelbett zu zweit vielleicht etwas klein, aber für Pärchen z.B. sicherlich ok (-: 2 Minuten bis zur Ubahnstation (West 96. Strasse) in 5-10 minuten zu Fuß im Central Park.

title: “Sauber und in guter, schöner Lage”
text: Nette, schöne und relativ ruhige Gegend mit vielen kleinen Läden, Supermärkten, Restaurantes aller Art ums Hotel. Zimmer sind sehr sauber, auch das Bad! Ein Doppelbett zu zweit vielleicht etwas klein, aber für Pärchen z.B. sicherlich ok (-: 2 Minuten bis zur Ubahnstation (West 96. Strasse) in 5-10 minuten zu Fuß im Central Park.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Looks like a Howard Johnson”
text:
No problem at all with Howard Johnson, but I do not pay $300 (discount thanks to having booked the room for a convention) at a Howard Johnson, for a tiny room (having booked a Grand Club category and a bathroom that resembled that of an airoplane with a bathtub. It claimed to be on the 18th floor but it was actually on the 9th or 10th.
In the morning the lobby seemed to be a train station where everybody had breakfast on the couches. Lines for checking in or out took about 10 minutes. And I can go on...

name: Holiday Inn Express NYC - Madison Square Garden
title: “Snappy answers to stupid questions”
text:
Like the previous poster, I had lots of fun with the thermostat and the shower, but after asking two stupid questions that they say have been asked by a lot of people, everything was fine. There is still work going on in the basement and unless fully booked, I can't understand why they'd put anyone down there.
The room itself was fairly compact but fine, with a hallway leading into the proper room. Storage is at a relative minimum, with drawers under the TV cabinet and only a skinny armoire to hang clothes up in--and the armoire was already occupied by an iron, ironing board and an extra blanket. That said, the bed was very comfortable (with four pillows), the bathroom was of decent size and once I got the heat and shower working, all was right with the world.
There's also an extended continental breakfast with both hot and cold food and coffee and juice available all day.
The location is great, with the 1 subway line a block and half away and Herald Square a five minute walk. 
Got it for $75 a night through Priceline and if I could get that kind of deal again, I'd go back--especially now that I know how to deal with the heat (pull down the thermostat cover and adjust it manually) and the shower (pull down the ring at the end of the faucet).

name: The Standard High Line
title: “Awesome Anniversary”
text: My wife and I had a fantastic time at the Standard and will be back again for more fun. The staff at the Standard was very attentive and helpful from the time we arrived until our departure. We had lots of NYC plans including a U2 concert and the hotel made a great base camp. A post concert dinner at the Standard Grill was an excellent way to cap off our evening. Come to think of it, we ate breakfast, lunch and dinner there and have to say it was good food for a good value. Don't forget to go to the beer garden before you head out on the town!

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Great NYC Hotel!”
text: Check-in was great, and we were upgraded to the club level. The room was spacious by NYC standards and was clean. The linens were really nice and the bed comfortable. The bar was nice, though pricey, and was open late. Our only complaint was that someone in the room next to us left room service items in the hallway, and they were not cleaned up for several hours.

name: The Standard High Line
title: “Great style, location, views”
text:
When planning our annual trip to New York, I wanted to get away from the midtown hotels and stay more towards Greenwich Village. We have walked around the Village numerous times,, but have always gotten lost, what with its narrow streets intersecting this way and that, without the perfect grid system of midtown streets. We also have been following the High Line project--the redevelopment of an old elevated railroad platform into a lovingly and cleverly designed landscaped walkway-- as well as the construction of the Standard Hotel straddling it. So when we discovered the Standard would be open during our planned visit, we eagerly booked there. We were able to get a good web-only rate similar to the soft opening rate the hotel initially offered.
The Neighbourhood. 
 The hotel is located in the Meatpacking district just north of the West Village. It straddles the High Line and is quite an impressive sight, 18 stories tall. We first visited this area when the boutique Jeffrey opened on 14th St. a number of years ago . Back then the area truly did consist of mostly meatpacking facilities. A few of these still remain, but most have become designer shops, clubs, lounges and restaurants. The nightlife here is very active--weekdays and weekends we witnessed crowds at 2 am and later--people who require very little sleep and/or don't go to work until the afternoon, if at all. Over the course of our 6 day stay, we saw exactly 3 children in the area, all during daylight hours and none within the hotel itself. The hotel offers queen or king rooms only; 2 people maximum per room.
The nearest subway stop is about a 5 minute walk away.
The Hotel Public Rooms.
There is a large outdoor seating area in front of the lobby, which is smallish but stylish, a bit retro looking. The elevators all have 2 unique video screens playing a mesmerizing continuously scrolling presentation, with music. There are several lounge spaces on the ground floor, both indoors and out, with the largest being outdoors under (and protected by) the High Line--very popular. The restaurant The Standard Grill is adjacent, also with indoor and outdoor seating. Not yet opened is the top (18th) floor lounge/club, which apparently will have pool, and is certain to be a hot spot once it opens in about a month. It will surely be a velvet rope type of place, and I would expect there may be difficulty (or at least a wait) for guests just trying to return to their rooms. Even now, over the weekend there was security at the elevators, asking for room keys and checking guest names from a list. There is a large gym on the 17th floor with fabulous views in 3 directions, including the Hudson River. There is no business center (but Wifi is free) or spa.
The Guestrooms.
Our web rate was for a Standard Queen, but we were upgraded to a south-facing Superior Queen, a slightly smaller room but with a better view. Apparently all the Standard rooms face north, where one gets a glimpse of the river. High Line and Empire State Building, but mostly one sees a large building being built one block north. From the south-facing rooms, there are virtually no buildings taller that the hotel, so one can clearly see Downtown, the southern tip of the High Line, much better views of the Hudson River, New Jersey and the Statue of Liberty. 
We were informed at check-in as well as via a letter delivered to the room that the floor-to-ceiling windows were non-reflective, so without your drapes drawn, people below can see EVERYTHING, and this apparently has been an issue, based on things we'd read online. Indeed, whenever we looked down at the High Line, there were always people staring up at the hotel.
The room was not large, but I've seen smaller in New York, and things were designed to maximize space--a built-in seating area, 2 sides of the bed placed flush against the wall (the person with the stronger bladder should sleep against the wall). The colour scheme is black, white and beige. The flat screen HD TV froze a lot.
The bathroom was tiled in black with a laboratory-like sink and counter fixture. The bath products were cleverly packaged. Very early TA reviews of the hotel mentioned the flooding situation involving the shower, and we bore witness to this in our room. The shower is not enclosed, with only a small glass partition between it and the sink. Only the water temperature can be controlled, not the volume (this is true of practically every hotel shower we've used for the past few years), so the water naturally flows out onto the floor, which is not sloped enough towards the drain. We learned quickly to form a dam using a towel (very large and fluffy by the way) to contain the water. Indeed, after showering, the driest place in the bathroom was in the bathtub, which was huge and open to the bedroom with shutters. The toilet was in a separate water closet.
The Staff and Service.
The staff was all quite young and stylish, courteous and helpful for the most part. Male staffers seem to outnumber the females. Our one exception was with an unfriendly room service attendant, but this was after midnight and he was doing double duty--taking an order on a mobile phone while delivering our order.
This was a fun hotel in a fun location. It's not a 5 star place, nor does it strive to be, but it delivered on most fronts. Again, it's not a place for families with small children or friends who are not intimate with each other. or for business. Coming from Los Angeles, we think this Standard has more to offer than either of the LA Standards.

name: Hotel 31
title: “Ubicación excelente”
text: Estuvimos 4 noches a finales de agosto durante el huracan Irene. Cuando vi el tamaño diminuto de la habitación con su ventana que daba a una pared y sabiendo que no ibamos a salir por la calle durante 24 horas por el Irene, pensé que no lo iba a aguantar. Habitación tan pequeña que cuesta abrir una maleta entera y ademas sin armario. Era con baño compartido. La habitación lleva un lavabo pequeño que viene muy bien. El aparato de aire es muy antiguo y ruidoso. Sin embargo, aceptaron cambiarnos la habitación no por una más grande pero por una más alta con vista al Empire State Building. Los baños están muy limpios. Lo mejor del hotel es sin duda su ubicación a 2 manzanas del ESB. Lo recomendaría por su situación no por su comodidad.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott New York Manhattan / Times Square
title: “Bed bugs, rude front desk”
text:
I do about 85 to 100 nights in Marriott properties each year and I am platinum. When you do work at the Javits Center this hotel is a common choice.
I arrived an the front desk clerk said my room was cancelled. She said (lied) that my card was now expired, and that Marriott cancels reservations with expired cards. The card was not expired. Without being mean I insisted she recheck, and she insisted I leave. I asked her very nicely to book me at the Marquis. She dissapeared for 15 minutes and came back with a room. No apology. I won't post her name. Later I saw her stealing the happy hour food in the lounge just an FYI so shes not their star employee. She pretended to be a manager, she was not.
All was well for one day, except for some overpriced (for a fairfield level propery) drinks.
The next night I went to bed. Around 12:30am I was drifing off and a bed bug walked across my view. I jumped out of bed, killed it, and put it in the toilet and flushed. The next one I found was full of my blood. I started saving the bodies for proof. After 4 successful bed bug murders I decided to call the front desk and ask for a new room. The guy at the desk was not excited to help me. He let me know there was no similar room. I told him any room would do and he should check it for me in advance. Well, he could not do that because he cant leave the desk. He sent the security guy, and he checked out another room for me and it was bug free.
Here I am reviewing it cause I cant sleep. I have a couple small welts already and am deciding whether to just abandon my luggage and clothes.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan SoHo Village
title: “The PERFECT Hotel”
text: Great location, within walking distance to Little Italy, China Town and SOHO. Particularly close to the Subway as well, making it very easy to get anywhere in New York. The service was exceptional. I reserved a twin bed room, and they gave us two double bed rooms instead with no extra charge. The front desk staffs were friendly and more than helpful to help us with the direction. However, like many hotels in the USA, they will charge you for the bottled water.

name: Hotel 31
title: “Hotel 31 à Manhattan”
text:
Les chambres sont petites mais pour le prix et la situation ya pas photo, ca vaut le coup !
Salle de bain tres propre, personnel aimable, a 5 min à pieds de l'empire state ...
Manque que le petit déj et la salle de bain perso :-)

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott New York Manhattan / Times Square
title: “Nice hotel, good location”
text:
Had a good time in the Fairfield Inn & Suites last october. Stayed there for 5 nights and I got a fresh bottle of water everyday, clean towles when I used them and left them on the floor & the staff was very kind. There's a bar on the top floor of the hotel and you have a beautiful view at night over the city!
The location of the hotel is perfect with Time Square and metrostations just around the corner!
Absolutely advisable for a nice, comfortable stay!
The staff is always there to help and greet you, a special ''concierge'' helps you with all your questions and even makes reservations at restaurants as you prefere.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York - Chelsea
title: “Best in the area at that price point”
text:
I have spent the past five weeks staying at different hotels in the Penn Station/Madison Square Garden area. I'm travelling for business and wanted to stay in Manhattan but within a short walk to Penn Station so I could catch the LIRR out to Long Island. The Hilton Garden Inn Chelsea on 28th ranks first out of the five hotels.
1) Hilton Garden Inn (121 W 28th St)
2) Wyndham Garden (341 W 36th)
3) Hilton Garden Inn (63 W 35th St)
4) Hampton Inn (116 W 31st St)
5) New Yorker (481 8th)
This location had more space than the others. It had a fridge, microwave and an HDTV (as did the other HGI location). One option that really stood out was the Time Warner HD Cable. There were literally hundreds of channels and dozens of HBO and Showtime channels.
While there may be higher end hotels in NY, you'll really have to search to find one in this price range. I'll be keeping this hotel on the top of my list for my next visit.

name: Pod 51
title: “Stranded by sandy saved by pod”
text:
Was recently stranded due to sandy and this was all I could find for me and my mum..
Was great location close to everything we needed with some great resturants nearby..
Staff were very friendly and full of knowledge and help

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Improved Service and Amenities”
text: I got an excellent rate ($160/night) bidding on Priceline for a 2 night midweek stay. Except for the old TV, the room, though small, was in excellent condition, the bed comfortable, quiet abnd clean. I was on the 20th floor and elevator service was always prompt. The room service menu was way overpriced, even for New York (e.g. club sandwich: $19.99). However, one can avoid the mediocre hotel restaurants by walking indoors to the connecting Grand Central Station, where there is a superb Charlie Trotter's restaurant, or contine up the north side escalators to the Met Life Building (formerly Pan Am Building), where there arethree good restaurant options. Also,within Grand Central Station itself is the Oyster Bar and Restaurant for superb fresh seafood. All these options can be accessed without having to walk outside should the weather be bad. Back to the hotel, I found the staff to be uniformly curtious and helpful.

name: Room Mate Grace
title: “Can't wait to go back!”
text: This hotel was a tue gem! What a find!! I had one of the smallest rooms listed on the website but it was plenty big for one and would have been just fine for 2 people. The underbed storage area made it the room feel bigger than it was. The bathroom was well-appointed and I appreciated having a shower rather than a tub--it felt much roomier, I always feel very claustrophobic in hotel tubs. The neutrogena shampoo/conditioner/shower gel were definitely welcome. Everyone, and I mean EVERYONE at the QT was extremely friendly, from the front-desk (very accommodating when my room wasn't ready for check-in--I was early--in taking my bags, helping me find my way around the City, etc) to the cleaning lady who had a smile on her face all the time. The complimentary breakfast was more than adequate and consisted of coffee/fresh juice, bagels, croissants, fruit, yogurt, muffins, and hard-boiled eggs. The pool was a nice addition too at the end of a long day before heading back out to the theatre at night. And there were no creepy men, as someone previously mentioned. It does get a little busy at night in the bar area but it was never a problem and there was always security present. As a female traveling alone, the location was ideal in the heart of the theatre district, I never felt unsafe walking to the hotel. Overall, this was the best hotel experience and I can't wait to go back to the QT!!!!

name: Hilton New York
title: “Wheelchair Accessible, but why do they call it delux suite?”
text:
I think most of the hotels are ADA compliant but Hilton is one of the few hotels in NYC with wheel-in shower, which is a must for my friend with ALS. Since we don't have many hotels/rooms to choose from in the first place, I can't compare our experience with other hotels. 
We booked a wheelchair accessible delux suite room. It was roomy enough for a wheelchair to move around but it was definitely not a suite. I have no complaint about the room itself but I just don't understand why they call it "delux suite". It was a clean, regular room with two beds. I've stayed at a suite hotel in Times Square area before, and it was a suite with a real living room with sleeper sofa, and a seperate, private bedroom. So when I heard "delux suite", I expected the same. We were expecting multiple visitors, planning to use the "living room" section for meetings. 
I also wish they offered a several types of shower chairs/benches to choose from. Every wheelchaired person has different needs and the one in the shower didn't fit my friend's. (It was a bench, while she needed a chair with arm rests to suppot herself in the shower.)
My rating is not for the Hotel itself, but for the so called "delux suite".

name: Hilton New York
title: “Convenient Location”
text: The Hilton is on Avenue of the Americas within walking distance of Central Park and Times Square. Check in was fast and efficient. We utilized room service and the Marketplace restaurant. Prices were on par with NYC. Tony in the restaurant was very attentive and friendly. Viviene was very efficient at check out. The bellmen were very organized at lining up the guests who were waiting for taxis. A*** in the gift shop was the only hotel employee that we encountered that was not friendly and guest oriented. He never spoke. There was no greeting. He didn't even say the total of my purchase. I had to look to see the amount. The change was handed back, not counted back, silently. No thank you, good bye, or anything. Pay attention to the elevators. They are grouped by floor number, they do not stop on every floor.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott New York Manhattan / Times Square
title: “complete dump!!”
text:
by default- with a mix up of ours , we were stuck at 1 30 am w no room for one night- 
we had to stay at this dump- and were charged 400 dollars- even though, we are a marriot member, we knew the room was jacked up in price, the room and bathroom were disgusting- loud air conditioner, thin towels , rediculous bathroom- please be aware- do not stay here- we felt completely taken advantage of- with a rediculous rate.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York - Chelsea
title: “Excellent business hotel”
text:
I can do little more than endorse the other positive reviews of this hotel, but just a few things to add based on a recent six-night stay, following a three night stay in January. The front desk staff are first rate, though I should say that I am a Hilton Honors member. It's worth asking for a room at the back of the hotel as there is construction work at the front at present. There is some noise from the refuse carts in the early morning, as well as from trucks deliverying to the numerous flower shops on 28th St. 
A key benefit is that most of the NY subway routes are no more than a 5-6 minute walk from the hotel and the 4.5 and 6 lines are abour a 10-12 minute walk. If you fly into Newark then the train from the plane gets you to Penn Station in 30 minutes for $15 and from there it is about a 8-10 minute walk to the hotel. If safety is a concern there is a police station on 30th Street and the road is used as a patrol car garage. Local restaurants take a little bit of finding but the front desk staff are very helpful in this respect and prices are lower than they would be north of 42nd Street. 
Calling it the Garden Inn Chelsea is pushing the boundaries of Chelsea a little. It is at the very NE edge of what is usually regarded as the Chelsea neighbourhood.
I've been visiting New York on a regular basis since 1974 and just wish this hotel had been built before 2007. From now on this is my preferred business hotel. It ticks all the boxes as far as room standards and customer service are concerned. What you don't get are a bar with large comfy seats and much in the way of restaurant services in the evening. And when you arrive at the hotel for the first time (of many!) don't be put off by the rather cramped lobby area.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “great holiday”
text:
Having stayed in The Casablanca last year and loving it I decided to come back again.I noticed that the price had significantly increased so I looked around.
I got a really good deal for the Hyatt and it was £800 cheaper than the casablanca ! (saving for 2 for 1 weeks stay).
I have read some of the reviews on here and was worried. When we arrived , the lady on reception was lovely, really friendly and she gave us vouchers for free coffee for every day of our stay.
I had booked a room with 2 double beds and the room was very spacious, bright and modern.The beds are really comfortable.
I was pleased to find an ipod dock and a huge TV.
The bathroom was average size with a fairly small bath but that wasn't an issue.
I never encountered any problems with noise at all and we were facing the road.You did hear the odd door close but not at inconvenient times.
I cannot comment on the food as we never tried any.There are numerous places to eat and drink nearby and all very reasonable ( and huge portions !)
Overall I was very impressed with the hotel.It is huge and impersonal but so what, you don't really spend that much time in there anyway. The lobby is impressive and very busy.
I would definately return and recommend it.I thought it was a bargain compared to the smaller hotels and a great location too.

name: Hotel 31
title: “Bon rapport qualité/prix !!! a conseillé !!”
text:
Bon hotel très bien situé, au coeur de Manhattan (10 min a pied de l'empire State Building et 5 min du metro 6). 
Chambre petite mais fonctionnel, très propre et confortable. Salle de bain petite (pas de chauffage).
Personnel sympathique mais sans plus.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Very nice hotel”
text: Had a great time here. What a huge hotel! Service was top notch, and I enjoyed the staff. Location was prime, right in Rockafeller Center. My room was on the 50th floor, and faced south, could see the lights of Times Square.

name: Hotel 31
title: “Mitten drin!”
text: Sehr schönes gemütliches Hotel mitten in New York. Alles ist zu Fuss zu erreichen ( 5 Minuten Empire State Building, 10 Minuten Penn Station, wenig weiter zum Times Square) und doch in ruhige Lage. Der Service ist sehr freudlich und die Zimmer sehr sauber. Die Gemeinschaftsbäder sind super sauber und auch immer frei. Uneingeschränkt empfehlenswert

name: Room Mate Grace
title: “Hotel QT is Great!”
text:
My wife and I booked our Hotel QT stay online from Sydney, months before, sight unseen. All we had to go was the reviews on Tripadvisor and the Hotel QT website. 
We were VERY impressed. 
1 - it's VERY cool. All the rooms are different, but very trendy and yes, the beds are the most comfortable hotel bed ever. The shower/bathroom/toilet all in the same room didn't bother us, but it might if you're not intimate with the person you're sharing with. We stayed in 2 rooms over 6 nights as we had to change after the first night - we were on the 8th floor right over the street and the noise from the Garbage trucks drove me mad (my wife says she didnt' hear them but they drilled into my head). The great news was that when I went downstairs to tell reception at 3am, they were really nice about it and moved us to a (larger) room at the back of the building the very next morning. This new room, on the 10th floor, was so quiet we overslept everyday!!! 
The room was cleaned everyday, regardless of what time we left the hotel, and the staff were always friendly.
BTW - we booked the Class B room, so I don't know what the cheaper ones are like.
2 - it's 15 seconds to Times Square.
There are also some great bars next door, and a deli 3 doors up. You have to buy your own mini bar supplies which you can do from reception. This is great if you feel like a beer at 3am, but it's very expensive. Go 3 doors up and grab a 6 pack for the same price as 2 beers at reception. 
3 - Breakfast is great and you can eat enough to keep you going. Cereal, Bagels, Fruit, Juice, Coffee, Croissants, Yoghurt etc. You can eat it there, or the guy serving was kind enough to give us a tray to take it back to our room. There's heaps of seating too, just don't get there too late or there's no good pastries left! Remember to tip the nice man!!
4 - The pool and bar look great, but with so much to do and see in Manhattan, we never got the chance to use it. Although on one night we were there I thought we had walked into a nightclub when we came back to the Hotel. 
All in all, we would reccomend this Hotel to anyone young, young at heart, or anyone that wants a grrovy stay in NYC.
Basically, next time we're in NYC, we'll be staying back at the Hotel QT.

name: The Lombardy
title: “Stay Away!”
text: The room was spacious for New York. Our money was stolen from our room when the room was getting serviced $7500!! later the money automatically showed up when the police were called to investigate. Management wasnt even willing to compensate 1 cent to our make up for the our honeymoon being ruined, not even a formal apology..would not recommend!!!! Stay away!

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “Comfy, clean, convenient”
text: This was a pretty cool hotel over all. I switched to this one midway through my week-long trip to NYC as the price and location were better than what I had in the upper east side. I checked in early, about 8 am, and they had a room available for me. It was directly across from the elevators, I mean the elevator door opened, and there was the room. But as it turned out, this wasn't much of a problem. I did hear people occasionally but it truly didn't bother me much. The room was average in size, looked like some of the furniture was a little old (peeling leather on a chair, that sort of thing) but clean and comfortable. My second night there, I didn't get any new toiletries in the room, though I had used the shampoo and conditioner, and had to call down for some. But that was really the only misstep by the hotel. The staff was friendly and efficient but not exceptional. I wouldn't go out of my way to stay here but I wouldn't avoid the hotel either.

name: The Lombardy
title: “Excellent Hotel, Nice Respite”
text: I am in the middle of my stay at the Lombardy, and have found it to be a gem in the middle of faceless Midtown. The staff is very knowledgeable and attentive, but laid back and not in your face. The room is quite clean and inviting. The rooms all have different decor since they're all decorated by different owners, so I got to choose my style among the available rooms. Worked out very well for me - very convenient, street fair right around the corner. I highly recommend it.

name: Room Mate Grace
title: “What a QT”
text:
Just returned from a fantastic 6 night break in New York - partly thanks to the Hotel QT. What a cool place. 
Having stayed in many boutique hotels I found most of them to be a disappointment. However, the QT was better than I expected. I had read a couple of negative reviews before I left so wasn't sure what I was going to get. 
I requested a room high up in the hotel and that's what I got. We were on the 12th floor in room 1205. Nicely layed out room. Bigger than I thought. Huge shower head which made you want to stay in there for hours. Big comfy bed, flatscreen TV, cool magazines and a nice little cushioned seating area by the window. 
Ok it could have done with a few little extra's such as somewhere to hang your towels, a proper wardrobe door rather than a curtain and some drawers but they aren't essentials. You can get by easily enough without them.
The only thing I found slightly odd was the shower and the toilet being in the same little area. They were quite far apart but if you are in the shower and your partner needs the loo it could be a bit tricky. We did however have a sliding divider to close off the shower / toilet room but it might have been better to have the toilet separate. But then to be honest we actually never needed the shower and toilet at the same time so it was fine. 
Our shower / toilet area also had 2 massive windows which were frosted halfway up. My boyfriend was concerned that people from the neigbouring office blocks would see you showering etc. but I am pretty sure they would have to be at a very strange angle in their office to see you. Plus once the shower is going the glass would steam up anyway and when you were sat down on the loo there's no way anyone could see. And in the whole time I was there I never actually saw any people moving around in the offices anyway. So if I couldn't see them ! 
Personally I found it really cool to have a shower and be looking out the window with the sun shining through and the sounds of the streets of Manhattan outside. 
Some friends of ours were in the room opposite us 1206 and their room wasn't as well designed as ours / seemed slightly smaller (even though it was also an E sized room). So I think maybe some people strike more lucky with their room than others. They also seemed to have much more of a ledge around the bed than us as our bed ran width wise along the window and theirs was lengthwise with the headboard backing against the window. So it made it quite difficult to navigate getting out of bed. 
Lots of young media / fashion types stay here so the bar / pool / sauna area are all very cool in their design. 
The staff were all wonderful and helped you with anything you needed - restaurant recommendations / directions etc. None of the snobbery or attitude I've experienced with more expensive hotels. In fact on the day we arrived they were having some cake in the bar area for employee of the month and offered us all a slice which was a nice touch.
Breakfast could be better given there's so much fantastic food in New York but it's fine for what you pay. And if you don't like breakfast at the hotel then there's always a couple of nice deli's just to the left of the hotel - Cranberries and Dunhills.
You couldn't fault the hotel for location either. Literally a minutes walk from Times Square in one direction and a couple of minutes walk in the other direction to lots of the big stores on 5th Avenue. 
At the end of the day if you are worried about the size of your room when you are in a city like New York then all I can say is get a life!
Ah - one final thing I would point out is that when checking out they take the money and then give you the itemised bill. So make sure you ask for a print out before you pay or at least make sure you double check because the room rate we had been quoted / booked wasn't what they charged us. They charged us 50 dollars per night more. Thankfully my boyfriend remembered I had mentioned it was 230 dollars per night not 280 and I had a print out of the reservation confirmation with me. You should remember to do this too. I spoke to them they refunded the difference immediately including the percentage of tax. Thing is when checking in they asked me to sign a slip agreeing the rate of 280. At the time I said it was wrong so I had it amended. However, this was obviously not put onto the computer system.

name: The Standard High Line
title: “Hallucinant...”
text:
Côté +:
Tout a été dit sur l'incroyable architecture et le design en général, la localisation est géniale, le quartier top, le bar a une super ambiance et une vue slendide à la tombée de la nuit... Ca vaut donc vraiment le détour mais pour ce qui est de l'hôtel en lui même...
Côté -:
Acceuil effroyable, tout le monde fait la gueule à la réception, pas un "bienvenue", pas un sourire. Le réceptionniste qui avait une vraie tête à claques n'a même pas bougé pour nous indiquer la direction des ascenseurs ou le niveau de la chambre, pas une explication sur les prestations de l'hôtel (roof top, gym etc..)
Nous avons attendu 30 minutes pour que quelqu'un daigne nous monter nos baggages(après les avoir appelé pour leur demander s'ils avaient oublié...)
La chambre, en dehors de la vue n'a rien d'extraordinaire, on se croirait dans une cabine de bateau...
On avait presque l'impression d'être dans un taudis.... Les linges étaient déchirés, élimés, quelqu'un avait renversé du café le long du mur de l'entrée, cela avait coulé sur la moquette, rien avaît été nettoyé... Le savon de la salle de bain, non emballé avait déjà été utilisé (je suis pour le recyclage, mais dans une chambre a 625$ la nuit cela me semble quand même anormal....)
Un filet de lumière éclaire la douche, une chatte n'y retrouverait pas ses petits, avec une douche a l'italienne mal faite ou l'eau déborde directement sur la moquette..... Pas d'endroit ou suspendre vos linges mouillés.... Et le clou est quand même l'absence totale d'insonorisation....
Chaque fois que quelqu'un se ballade dans le couloir et ferme la porte de sa chambre/(cabine!) les murs tremblent et cela raisonne dans la chambre... Sans parler des gens qui parlent en rentrant au milieu de la nuit, le couloir amplifiant les bruits cela nous a reveillé les deux nuits que nous avons passé la.....
J'allais oublié... L'accès au roof top (normalement privilêge des "happy" few qui résident à l'hôtel) était fermé parceque le temps était couvert.... Quant au Bar non accessible pour cause de soirée privée....!
Pour résumer nous sommes allés de désillusion en désillusion.... Cet endroit est vraiment à éviter, à moins de vouloir tenter une nouvelle sorte d'expérience sociologique "ou comment vous faire prendre pour des pigeons" c'est un scandal et une arnaque sans nom... Aller boire un verre pour admirer la vue au bar (s'il n'est pas pas privatisé bien entendu...et que vous supportez de voir les tables libres qui sont réservées mais qui resteront vides pendant la durée de votre drink)...

name: The Lombardy
title: “Superbe hôtel...”
text:
Nous avons passé 15 jours dans cet hôtel, l'emplacement est idéal à proximité de Central Park et de la 5ème Avenue.Personnels accueillant, grande chambre équipée (salon, coin cuisine, dressing, coin PC avec ordinateur et Wi-Fi gratuit, lit king size et salle de bain moderne). Très propre, la femme de ménage passe tous les jours et laisse de petits chocolats sur l'oreiller...
Malgré tout, un petit point négatif concernant le petit déjeuner: en effet, l'hotel étant en travaux nous avons eu droit à un bon de 5$ par personne pour prendre notre petit déjeuner dans un restaurant à 2 rues de l'hôtel et ce n'était vraiment pas terrible. Nous y sommes aller 2 fois et le reste de notre séjour nous l'avons pris ailleurs ce qui a occasionné des frais supplémentaires.
A part çà, New York est une ville magnifique! Nous y retournerons...

name: Hilton New York
title: “An excellent break”
text:
We were originally booked to travel before Christmas and stay in a different hotel on Times Square. Unfortunately we were caught up in the snow fiasco at Heathrow and had our flight cancelled. We managed to rebook our flights with BA to fly out on New Years Eve and also booked this hotel as a package.
The location of this hotel is superb and in hindsight Heathrow actually did us a favour by closing the runways! (Although we are still out of pocket - thanks BAA!) 
The check-in was really smooth and fast - considering we checked in on New Years Eve and the hotel was very busy and we quickly found our way to our room on the 28th floor and were able to join in the new year celebrations within about 30 minutes of arriving.
The room was spacious and extremely clean.
The bar service was excellent with a comfortable and relaxed atmosphere. All the staff are very polite.
As mentioned previously the hotel is in a fabulous location - a short walk to both Central Park and 5th Avenue for the amazing shopping.
We would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to others and will definitely use it again when we return to New York.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan SoHo Village
title: “Will definitely stay here again!”
text:
This hotel is in a great, safe location.....almost in the heart of Soho and the Village. I have stayed in many hotels and this is one of the cleanest I have ever seen! From the lobby to the hotel room, everything was immaculate. Very friendly staff and quick check in/out. 
My daughter and I were in NYC for a couple of college visits and a little getaway. This hotel served the purpose perfectly. When I go back to NYC, I will absolutely stay here again. Great restaurants in the area, as well.

name: The Standard High Line
title: “Tolle Aussicht und Lage aber teuer”
text: Atemberaubender Ausblick aus den Zimmer mit Hudson River View - sowohl tagsüber wie beim Sonnenuntergang oder nächtens auch auf Lower Manhattan. Ausgezeichnete Lage mitten in Meat Packing District über der High Line. Zimmer nett, freundlich mit viel Spiegelflächen ausgestattet - was aber die Tatsache, dass sie winzigklein sind nicht verbirgt. Kaum Platz für Koffer bzw. KIamotten, aber gut mit allem möglichen und notwendigen ausgerüstete Minibar. Tolle Bild/musikinstallationen in Aufzügen. Unten mehrere Möglichkeiten zum Trinken und Essen, oben mehrere Bars - auch im Freien und mit Jacuzzis mit tollem Blick. Allerdings nach 21:00 sind diese Bars für Hotelgäste nicht zugänglich - was bei den hohen Zimmerpreisen nicht akzeptabel ist.

name: Kitano New York
title: “Small, dark rooms + a front desk manager who doesn't care”
text:
I'm writing this review from a cave.. that it's the inside of our room at the Kiatno Hotel. This hotel calls itself 4-star, but its rooms don't deserve it! My room is a small cavern with almost no natural light. To boot, the walls are paper thin (where is that screaming coming from?). 
Front desk manager was not empathetic or helpful with any alternatives to our cave. She claimed they were sold out with no other options, before later trying to upsell us to other room categories.
I've stayed in a lot of hotels (I am hilton gold, fairmont platinum, priority club platinum, etc.) and my stay at the Kitano has not been impressive so far.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York - Chelsea
title: “Great Hotel”
text:
Stayed here March 12 to March 16 2008. Can't say enough about this hotel. We got an excellent rate booked through the hotel website. Hotel is walking distance from Penn Station, 5 min to Empire State building, 5 Minutes to Macy's, and about a 15 min walk to Times Square. It is right in the flower district so when you look out your window you look down on a street of colourful flower shops. The Subway is close by, and for a couple of girl's from a small city who though the subway would be confusing and complicated, it truly is the best way to get around the city! 
The hotel rooms are small but how much time are you really going to be spending in the room? The bed and linens were really comfortable. The only thing I was dissappointed in was the housekeeping. They changed our towels daily but they never cleaned the bathroom the entire time we were there. We are pretty tidy people anyway so it wasn't like we made a mess but the floor was never swept, and the mirror was never cleaned. They have an environmmental inititive where they only change the sheets if requested which is really great but I still expect the bed to be made and not just the Duvet to be thrown back over the rumpled sheets. If I had been paying the rate listed rigfht now on the website I would have said something, but like I said, we were barely in our room. 
Check in was quick and the staff was really nice and helpful. If you get back to your room and are hungry but your feet are too tired to go out again ask the front desk a good place to order pizza. They recommended a great place to us that is a block away from the hotel and has great thin crust wood-oven baked pizza. To Die for! Too bad I can't remember the name!
I would recommend this hotel to everyone and if I ever make it back I would stay there again!

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Grand Rip Off”
text: I'm a Hyatt Platinum member but I won't be staying here again despite the relatively cheap rates for NYC and here's why. The room was small and worn more like the Pennsylvania Hotel than a Hyatt. But two incidents really turned me off - we ate at the hotel restaurant on a Saturday night at 7:30PM, the small adjoining bar to the pricey restuarant had been occupied by some thugs who were extremely intoxicated and were literally screaming at the top of their lungs. The waiter said this had been going on since mid afternoon and that the manager would do "something." Nonetheless they seated my family two tables away from the ruckus so I asked these guys and ladies to keep it down, they then offered to "tear off my face." management finally did restrain them but apparently at least two of them returned to the bar and was served again was waiting to thrash me when I finished dinner, the hotel detective intervened but said it was my fault for talking to them. My position is Hyatt violates the New York Dram laws by serving obviously intoxicated persons. The next morning was treated to Hyatt'scontintental buffet, two rolls, coffee, and juice for $22 and that was the cheapest option. Grand rip off and dangerous - stay away and pay extra to stay elsewhere.

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “Another return to the Eastgate- keeps getting better!”
text:
This was our first trip back here with my granddaughter who is almost two, we asked the hotel for a crib but when we went into the room it wasn't there. 30 seconds later we received a call from the front desk to advise us the crib was on its way up to the room. When it arrived it looked quite like an old-fashioned hospital bed- white painted tubular steel but it was in perfect condition, smelled lovely and fresh with a bright mattress. Only downside was that with a very restless toddler the metal crib/plastic covered mattress was a bit noisy but we ended up putting her blanket around it and it was fine.
The one-bedroom suite was great, as usual, the furniture has been replaced with very heavy wooden angular stuff. We had a small issue with the coffee table, the top is a honey coloured wood but the huge square legs are dark brown and extend beyond the honey wood. We were for-ever bumping into it, may have been a jet-lag thing too;). We had one bathroom with bath/shower/toilet and another separate toilet, the toiletries provided were acceptable. 
There is a full cooker, microwave, dishwasher, coffee machine and all the glass wear, crockery and flat wear you will need. Concierge organised transport back to Newark (about $20 less that the inbound limo company). Safe deposit boxes in a room behind reception, the reception staff were lovely, very helpful with suggestions for local eateries. There is a really good diner to the right out of the hotel, turn right on 2nd and about a block south - Townhouse Diner (across the road).
Only downside is a bit of noise from the aircon units but by adjusting the temperature before going to bed it was fine. Would recommend this hotel to anyone and would love to go back!

name: Radisson Martinique on Broadway
title: “All good”
text: I can't speak highly enough of this hotel and its staff. I stayed there in December and the staff there were very nice indeed, and they were super-super-helpful during the EXTREMELY difficult moments (not hotel-related) that I experienced in the first two days in NYC. My room was great and the breakfast was too. I'd recommend it to anyone and I'll definitely be going back there again. Big thankyou to all of you there!

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York - Chelsea
title: “Great Place!”
text: Brand new hotel right in the heart of Manhattan. Convenient location. Super clean and fresh, rooms nicely sized for Manhattan. Hotel staff was friendly and welcoming. I highly recommend this hotel, you won't be disappointed.

name: Flatiron Hotel
title: “Cool Hotel, Friendly People”
text:
We stayed at the Flatiron for 4 days while my son visited colleges in NYC. It made a great home base. Central location, close to subways. Many people write about the small rooms, but I'm assuming they've not stayed in New York very often. We had a room with two double beds and it was plenty large enough for my wife, my son and me. 
Definitely try to get a higher floor, as there is music in the lobby nightclub every night. Our room was on the 9th floor and we had not trouble with noise (other than they typical New York street sounds).
Hotel staff was uniformly friendly and helpful. 
Highly recommended.

name: Radisson Martinique on Broadway
title: “A Gem”
text: Charming, sophisticated, clean, comfortable, great customer service, subway out the front door, close to retaurants, shopping, entertainment. Everything you want in a New York hotel. Average cost/night b/w $160-$200.

name: Radisson Martinique on Broadway
title: “It's the best place in NYC”
text:
Wonderful, wonderful----what else can I say about the Radisson Martinique! The front desk staff and bell staff are the BEST in the business. They treat you like you are the most special guest in the hotel----always smiling, friendly, and helpful. In addition, they greet you by your name and go out of their way to make your stay relaxing. The location is convenient to Time's Square, shopping, the subway, and great restaurants. The restaurant and bar in the hotel is also excellent and well-staffed.
I certainly will be returning and if you are looking for great accommodations, then the Martinique is the best choice.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan SoHo Village
title: “Great location!”
text:
It was nice to stay at this quite hotel from Thursday 6st Sept to Friday 9 Sep (last 3 nights in NY), after 5 nights accommodation of crazy Times Square. As Starwood member, we try to stay in Starwood hotels.
We checked-in at 5pm. We booked a traditional room and requested in our original booking top floor with views. We got room 2003! The view from this room was fantastic, windows everywhere, overlooking the Hudson River and the city (photo). We had a very welcoming room and very quiet, right on the corner in Level 20. They offer free bottle of water and coffee/tea facilities for your convenience. At night, they deliver to you room some snacks (popcorn) if you wish to relax in your room watching a movie. The bed is super comfortable. The only drawback is the internet (free of charge) which is really slow.
As we wanted to explore the Soho suburb and restaurants and cafes, we didn’t dine in at the Hotel. They have “happy hours from 4m to 7pm and lunch specials.
The nearest subway station is only two blocks from the hotel. The WTC is only two stations away and 10 min ride to Times Square. There is a Starbucks located just a block from the hotel (right on the corner)
Also a big thank you to all the front desk staff that were very friendly helpful. We would like to thank especially Alexander Ruiz (Front Office Supervisor) for making our stay an unforgettable one. Keep up the good service Alex!

name: Kitano New York
title: “Recent Stay”
text: We really enjoyed our three night stay at the Kitano. The staff was consistently friendly and helpful. It was quiet and we slept well. Will definitely return.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott New York Manhattan / Times Square
title: “Luxurious”
text:
Maybe I'm biased, but staying here in Sep 2010, after travelling for a year in 3rd world countries, this hotel was the bomb diggidy.
Climate controlled rooms, tv, phone, window with a view, bed, linens, mattress, carpeted floor, washroom with hot water, bath tub, toilet paper, 110V electricity, mirror, wall paper, and no bugs! (I'm told most of these are in most hotels.)
The staff are courteous, and the hotel is on a slightly smelly street (maybe it was garbage day), but the overall location is close enough to all the main NYC attractions without having tons of ppl walk by all day and night.
There is a small gym with some weights and treadmill which I never used, among some other if you're dying to impress the ladies.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott New York Manhattan / Times Square
title: “LOVED THIS PLACE!”
text:
