The breakfast is awesome! Way more than any other hotel I have been to. Breakfast is well worth waking up for. (If you can't find a seat for breakfast just bring the food up to your room) 
The lounge is calming with a wonderful fire. The front desk people were alright (not rude) just lacking in friendliness but every other staff member were very kind and charismatic. 
The elevator wasn't slow at all for me and I thought the TV in the elevator was cute.
The rooms were a nice size. I had stayed at the double tree in the middle of time square the weekend before and honestly, everything about this hotel was better. Beds were better, bathrooms nicer, lounge WAY better.
I wish I could tel you about the sky bar but I fell asleep on the comfy bed and didn't make it lol. BUT I saw a line outside and inside the hotel of trendy people waiting to get into the sky bar. If you are staying there don't worry about the line.
This location is a couple blocks to the side of time square but its located around useful restaurants and practical stores. 
I will totally stay here again!

name: Edison Hotel Times Square
title: “Non consiglio di alloggiare..”
text: La soddisfazione generale prende due punti solo per la posizione; si sconsiglia di alloggiare in questo Hotel. La pulizia è un optional, le camere vecchie. Avrebbe bisogn della completa ristrutturazione o meglio una demolizione e ricostruzione.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott New York Manhattan / Times Square
title: “Nice Place to Stay if you have an early am flight from JFK”
text: Nice Hotel. Good Place to stay prior to a flight. Front desk staff very courteous. Rooms are standard FI rooms. Our room had a flat screen TV. They have breakfast out and ready by 430am (self service) which is a nice touch for early departures. I would stay here again.

name: Equity Point New York @ Times Square
title: “Very misleading to be honest”
text: Informed on booking there would be 2 separate beds in the one room. On arrival found this not to be the case...had to share an old worn out double. Shower took 10 minutes to become warm. Room although very small wasn't an issue if you intended to be out and about when not sleeping. Breakfast on par with expectations. Benefits include price, fantastic location and nice bar. Free maps of the city and subway was a nice touch. Honestly, the whole bed situation left a sour taste in my mouth. Had I been travelling alone I would probably rate this place highly

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Lovely room”
text: The hotel is beautiful, if the rooms were a bit worn. We stayed for one night. The location was excellent and the beds very comfortable.

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “Easy access to town”
text: Our party spent a five night stay in the Carlton and were pleased in most respects with this well located hotel. The tasteful decor in the reception area is repeated in the room (3rd floor) which was pleasantly quiet for a busy hotel. I would describe the room as compact /bijou with all you require for a short stay ,in that the en suite was well furnished, but lacking shelf space ,while there was also a safe and huge T V screen (by British standards) A small closet for hanging clothes was adequate for "in and out " travellers. The room was impeccably clean and bathroom items replenished daily. When we required help with tourist issues the service provided was first class. I would recommend this hotel to the discerning tourist as one that will not disappoint.

name: Radisson Martinique on Broadway
title: “"My Stay"”
text: Excellent location and excellent hotel staff. They are concern about giving you their best all the time. The facade of the Hotel is amazing and the hotel itself is very good. However, the real deal of this hotel is constituted by their staff. I totally recommend it.

name: Radisson Martinique on Broadway
title: “Great 1st time trip to NY”
text: This hotel is a great location because it's walking distance to lots of locations and Penn Station. It's very charming with a lot of history, it's over 100 years old. My only complaint is because of it's age, the walls are thin so you hear your neighbors. Otherwise I highly recommend this hotel.

name: Pod 51
title: “Great location, tiny room, but very clean”
text: My partner and I just got back from spending two days over Memorial Weekend at the Pod Hotel in NY. Great location, about a ten minute walk from Grand Central. We stayed in a double room which had a private bathroom. The room is tiny. Very tiny. BUT, very clean. It had a big window that opened wide and had a nice view of the buildings around the hotel. We stayed on the 12th floor. The bathroom is small. There is not a lot of privacy for the bathroom--shower curtain and sliding door to block off the bathroom from the bedroom. Again, very small. But, if you're planning on being out and about in the city for most of the time and only using the room to sleep in, it's fine. I think two of the best qualities going for it are that it's in a great location in Manhattan and it's afforadble. The double room for two nights, including tax came to $383.

name: Pod 51
title: “cockroach!”
text: on our second night I found a HUGE cockroach in my daughter's boot. we were fairly freaked out, screamed, called the front desk where they offered us another room (but who's to say the next room would be safer?), screamed as it crawled out again, then killed it ourselves. yuck! the splat was one-and-half inches wide. since we had a bunkbed room, we both hid in the top bunk and had a fitful sleep. thrilled to leave.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott New York Manhattan / Times Square
title: “would stay again”
text: I stayed with my family for 4 nights in August. The hotel was clean and the staff were helpful and attentive. The air con was a bit noisy and the breakfast area was small but neither were major problems. It's located nr times square but not too noisy and is very handy for the port authority bus terminal and subway. The room was compact but there was plenty of wardrobe and drawer space and the in room safe was great to have. A decent selection of food and drinks for breakfast as well as starbucks coffee in the rooms. I would stay again.

name: Kitano New York
title: “Great hotel”
text: We really liked the hotel very much. Good location to explore NY. Lovely room, clean and very quiet which was important for me. The staff always friendly. The beds were nice and soft which often is disappointing in hotels.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott New York Manhattan / Times Square
title: “Highly recommended from another Fairfield Inn Asst Gen Mgr! Great place”
text: I absolutely love this property! Im a New yorker that currently lives in NC and I always choose this property whenever I go back home to visit and dont feel like staying with family. Im also an assistant gen manager at the Fairfield Inn & Suites brier creek in Raleigh and I must say the times square property is a delight! Its just a couple blocks away from the heart of the city times sq and adjacent to port authority, empire state building, penn station,madison square garden, as well as bryant park. Very safe area!The rooms are small but as are most of NYC rooms however the cleanliness is spectacular! i love the view from the high floor rooms. The rooms are a little close that you can hear everything going on in the hallway as well as your neighbors rooms. The staff is pleasant, however i flew into the city early and was told i would be able to get an early check-in 12pm but was told very abruptly that i had to wait until check-in time. I use Marriotts everywhere I travel i've loved them since I was a kid. I do highly recommend this property should you ever visit the NYC area. Although a fairfield inn it compares to courtyard and higher Marriott brands. Although there is always room for improvement i encourage you to Keep up the good work Fairfield Inn Team! Great job Management!

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “very disappointing”
text:
We planned to stay at the Waldorf Astoria for 12 nights but it became obvious from our arrival that this hotel did not live up to its reputation, which left us searching for a new hotel for the remainder of our holiday. We left after three days and moved to St Regis, which was such a blessing! The staff at the Waldorf, including the doorman, the front desk and concierge provided consistently poor service . It seemed no one could be bothered being friendly let alone helpful. In addition to the poor service , another major disappointment was the bathroom in our suite. We stayed in a suite (rather than a standard room) to ensure we had sufficient space over our 12 day stay not realising that the bathroom was very impractical (our mistake for not paying more attention to every detail when selecting the hotel). For example the bathroom door couldn’t open fully because the toilet obstructed it. The basin was a pedestal style, which meant there was nowhere to put cosmetics or toiletries (most women would find this impossible to manage!!). The shower was over the bath tub and my partner tripped on the first day and was lucky to have survived with no broken bones. 
Also there were several light globes not working in the suite, which meant we were waiting for maintenance men to arrive and replace them. This was annoying and difficult to understand at a hotel of this level. 
On the positive side, the bed was comfortable and the rooms were clean. The bar down stairs was lovely and great for people watching because most tourist visit the hotel for nostalgic reasons. The foyer was also buzzing with people coming and going, 
I wouldn’t recommend this hotel.

name: Kitano New York
title: “Wonderful peaceful hotel”
text: This hotel is in a great location 2 blocks from Grand Central station. The service was very good and I was impressed with how quiet it was. The room was spacious and very clean.

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “Nice apartments and close to most things”
text: We stayed there for 9 days and it was a great home base. The apartment was clean and tidy but a little out of date. That was fine for us. We had a two bedrooom apartment which had one bedroom with a queen bed and one bedromm with two double beds. Two bathrooms, a small kitchen and nice sized lounge/dining area to relax. Perfect for a family of four

name: Flatiron Hotel
title: “Great!”
text: I stayed with my family for couple days, the hotel was very clean and nice. Everyone there was nice, especially George who made sure that we had everything we needed and gave us some great tips bout navigating the city for my parents who visited ny for the fist time.

name: Pod 51
title: “Second Stay at The Pod”
text: This hotel makes a great base for visiting clients in New York City. This time, the staff really impressed me as the concierges (Bryan and particularly Kaira) went out of their way to help me with some very specific needs. My full-size room was just what I needed (small but functional) and its always nice to hang out in the lobby. Besides, you can't beat the price! Look forward to going back.

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “Great location but expensive wi-fi!”
text:
We enjoyed this hotel with a recent week long stay, with a comfortable room, full kitchen and sufficient space in the room, even with 5 of us. Staff at the front desk were ok, though certainly not overly-friendly (but is this a NYC thing?) and the maintenance service was prompt- we had a faulty room switch that was repaired ASAP. 
 However, with the necessity these days of having Internet access for maps, location services, booking events online etc whilst overseas, we were dismayed to learn that access to wi-fi was a whopping $50 PER DEVICE for the week! Naturally we declined, however elsewhere in the US we've found hi-speed free wi-fi to be available in all of the hotels we've stayed in. I would recommend to the Eastgate that they consider revising their wi-fi costs and they may find their front desk less busy, as guests use the net to find out how to get to Macy's or a Yankees game instead!

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan SoHo Village
title: “Covenient”
text: If your travels to NYC take you to lower Manhattan/Soho/Greenwich Village, this is a fantastic option. I've stayed there twice in the past half-year with my wife and son (who is in a wheelchair), and the customer service is simply impeccable. I travel a lot on business, and the service in my t wo recent trips here has been the highlight of my travelling year. Bonus -- incredible location. We drove up both times from Maryland for visits to NYU, which my son is considering for college, came in through the Holland Tunnel and were at the hotel in a couple of minutes without the midtown traffic. Good, safe parking nearby ($25-30/day with the hotel discount, but, hey, it's Manhattan -- and we didn't have to take a single cab). Lots of fantastic/relatively inexpensive/funky-in-a-good-way/non-touristy restaurants within a couple of blocks. Walked to south street market for great, cheap Bway seats ("A Little Night Music) at TKTS booth with no wait in line. Can't be beat.

name: Room Mate Grace
title: “Sin duda, repetiré cuando vuelva a Nueva York.”
text:
Hace unos años estuve en Nueva York, en el Hotel Pennsylvania, y este año nos decidimos a volver, ya que es una ciudad que nos encantó.
Tras conocer varios hoteles de la cadena Room Mate en España, teníamos prácticamente claro que, cuando fuésemos, iríamos a Grace.
Entre tanto, unos vecinos y unos amigos se alojaron allí, y nos dijeron que les encantó, lo que acabó por decidirnos.
Fuimos un grupo de 8 amigos y nos gustó mucho su ubicación. Eso de que estuviera a solo unos metros de Time Square, le hizo ganar muchos puntos.
Nada más llegar, un amable recepcionista nos saludó en español (por lo visto se nos nota de donde somos) y, tras darnos las habitaciones, subimos a dejar las maletas, ducharnos y prepararnos para recorrer la ciudad.
Tanto nuestra habitación, como las de nuestros amigos, eran amplísimas y nos encantaron (para ser totalmente sincero, la de una de las parejas era algo menos amplia, y como les dio envidia de las otras, se la cambiaron a una mayor). Todas tenían diseños diferentes, y estaban en las plantas altas. 
Las vistas desde nuestra habitación no es que fuese algo fuera de lo común, pero a mí me gustaba acostarme con la ventana abierta, para ver el ritmo sin parar 24h de la ciudad, con las oficinas, gimnasios, cafeterías, etc de los rascacielos de enfrente, a los que llegaba el resplandor de las luces de Time Square.
La cama comodísima, siempre limpia y bien hecha, al igual que el resto del hotel, donde casi siempre era fácil encontrarse con alguien limpiando las moquetas, las paredes, etc.
El aseo, también muy amplio, se dividía en dos zonas, una de más de 2 metros de largo en la que estaban los lavabos y el espejo, y otra donde estaba la ducha (a la ducha le pondría un poco más de luz).
La piscina, no gigante, pero lo suficientemente grande como para bañarnos y relajarnos todas las tardes-noche tras patear la ciudad. Junto a ella, también hay una zona de relax, además de una sauna, un baño turco y un gimnasio (que no utilizamos).
El desayuno muy completo y sano, no le faltaba de nada.
Ah, se me olvidaba decir que en la recepción del hotel tienen como un kiosko, donde comprar prensa, refrescos, aperitivos, chocolatinas,... con precios muy buenos (incluso compramos M&M's a menor precio que en un supermercado cercano).
Y bueno, no se qué más decir, simplemente que iba con un poco (muy poco) de miedo, ya que quien insistió que el hotel fuese ese al resto de amigos fui yo, pero todos coincidimos en que repetiríamos sin dudarlo.

name: Equity Point New York @ Times Square
title: “Great location and value!!”
text: My husband and I visit NYC at least once a year and always looking for a new hotel to try. I found Hotel 41 on the internet and the location was excellent along with the price. Previous reviews stated that the rooms were small. That is true, but they weren't as bad as I had prepared myself for. We could move around the bed and there was a nook for clothes and luggage. There was also a desk, chair, and frig which was a pleasant surprise. We have a king bed at home so the double bed took some getting use to. After the first night, we were just fine. Everything was especially clean and well kept. The only problem with the room was the shower. The showers don't have doors. There is just a panel of glass that covers about half of the shower opening and the other half is just open and when you take a shower, there is water on the floor. A towel is provided for clean up, but it was quite messy. Previous reviews also stated that the breakfast wasn't so great. It was just fine. There was coffee, hot chocolate, tea, orange juice, breakfast rolls, raisen toast and bagels with cream cheese and jelly. That is more than enough to get started in the morning and you didn't have to pay NYC prices for a breakfast. One of the best things about the hotel was the staff. As I previously stated, we have stayed in many hotels in NYC and this is the first where the staff remembered us and actually talked to us about where we lived and what we planned to do and see in NYC. They were most helpful with directions and any questions we had. I forgot to mention that the subway is just across the street. Being one block from Times Square you might think it would be noisey, especially at night, but it was very quiet and you didn't hear noise from other rooms as well. I would highly recommend this hotel for the price, location, cleanliness, and helpful staff.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan SoHo Village
title: “Great location”
text:
We really enjoyed our stay at the Four Points, Soho. This was our second visit to NYC so having done a lot of the main sights first time we spent a lot of time exploring Greenwich and Soho which was fun.
The service at the hotel was excellent and our room was very clean. The room was not that big but fine for a few nights. Subway was close by and we walked to Little Italy for dinner one night. Went to see "Wicked" on Broadway which was sensational.
The hotel bar was very expensive but then so was NYC in general.
All in all a great stay.

name: Flatiron Hotel
title: “Perfect spot for whirlwind city stay”
text: We got a great deal on the room- 140 incl. tax on bookit.com- and all of the little extras were wonderful! The aquarium was beautiful and the rooms, though very cozy, had fun touches with a remote for the curtains, iPod dock w surround sound, a tv in the bathroom and a great shower. The location is perfect especially if you don't like being trapped in midtown- you're a short walk away from everything. I could see a longer stay being uncomfortable with the room size and the tv was spotty- a lot of channels didn't come in. I don't know if its worth the $300/night they ask but if you find a deal, it's a great getaway!

name: Pod 51
title: “Clean, Spare, Folks from Everywhere”
text: Just got back from New York where I spent 4 nights at The Pod Hotel. The hotel has given real thought to it's design - seriously functional yet fun. Everything needed was there, and the WC a few steps down the hall, clean and available. My air conditioner/heater worked perfectly. There was a control for it in my room. The public area in the lobby offers a place to get refreshments, meet with friends and work on your computer. It was a very pleasant place and the coffee is great! There is also an outside area that was charming. The staff is most efficient. The concierge confirmed my return flight and printed out my boarding pass. The location of the hotel was perfect. My feet were able to get me everywhere I wanted to go. The people who stay there are part of the art . The Pod is a small, complete world.

name: Pod 51
title: “Clean hotel & great location”
text:
Located a stone's throw from midtown on 51st between 2nd and 3rd, within walking distance of everywhere, and only a 5 min walk to the E subway to JFK. My room was clean, with modern, well maintained fittings, iPod dock / TV / PowerShower.. space is limited and obviously there was a lot of thought put into storage during the design process, drawers under bed etc.. and for a room where space is so tight, was cool to see the usual extras there like a hair dryer and wall mounted flat screen tv. 
I paid for a double room (for single occupancy), just 'cos I didn't want a shared room or shared bathroom - was v good.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan SoHo Village
title: “Works for Me!”
text: My daughter has an internship in NYC and is camping out in a dorm in the West Village, about 8 blocks from this Soho hotel, which I chose off TripAdvisor because it seemed new and reliable. I am very pleased with this hotel. Staff is very friendly and responsive/quick. Room on 3rd floor faced the street but no street noise; won't win a design award but contemporary, feels comfy, has a wall of windows with suede Roman black out shades. Bed is very comfortable; bathroom would be small for two people but new with black marble walls. Free wifi, bottle of water, and Starbucks coffee(maker). Flat screen TV and nice desk area with good lighting and next to window. Sushi/Mexican restaurant (we tried room service--the veggie quesadilla was great and delivered within 20 minutes) with outside terrace. The hotel is very close to the subway so we scooted uptown easily; taxis also have room to park outside the front door. This particular block has no charm, but the hotel has what we needed and wanted. Nice to come back to after a day in NYC. The worst I can say is that the a/c is noisy. Highly recommended.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Great Location”
text:
We stayed in the Grand Hyatt in April and I would return here everytime. The rooms were a good size especially for NY and the cleanliness and service could not be faulted. Being situated at Grand
Central Station was ideal for getting round the city. Only one complaint, the buffet breakfast was way over priced so do what all the New Yorkers do grab a bagel in the lobby! Fantastic

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Excellent service and beautiful public spaces, but the rooms are in need of an update.”
text:
I spent three nights at the Waldorf-Astoria on business, and the service, facilities and overall cleanliness of the hotel and guest rooms is excellent. The location is great and allows for easy travel (as easy as it can get) within Manhattan.
The rooms, on the other hand, while clean and well-appointed, are clearly dated and in need of an update. The bedroom was small with somewhat threadbare carpet in places. The bathroom, (again, very clean) was also quite small and did not have room for any of the typical traveler's vanity items. There was some peeling paint throughout thr room, ceiling and in the hallways.
Finally, the room offered only a rudimentary temperature control, and in this case the only choice was heat or fan speed. Granted, it was winter while I was there, but there was no way to get the room unstuffy, which led to a fairly frustrating need to have the heat on and the window open at the same time. A call to the front desk informed me that the guests have a chooice of heat or cool only from April to May, and in September and October, when there is otherwise only seasonally-available hot or cold air.
Overall, great location, professional staff in a very historic hotel. Would be much better if the living history didn't extend to the guest room, however.

name: Hotel 31
title: “sauberes Hotel, sehr angenehm, sehr zentral”
text: Waren zum ersten Mal in New York. Hatten wenig Ansprüche an das Hotel, wurden aber eines viel besseren belehrt. Zimmer sehr sauber, mit Dusche und WC, geräumiger als gedacht, mit Safe und zwar älterer aber sehr guter Klimaanlage. Personal sehr nett und hilfsbereit. Von der Lage nicht zu übertreffen-nur ein paar Gehminuten vom Empire entfernt, U-Bahn um die Ecke, Frühstücksmöglichkeiten ebenso. Jederzeit gerne wieder!!!!!

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “I was not impressed”
text: This was our first stay at the Carlton. We spent 2 nights for our anniversary. Check in was easy. The front desk employee was not friendly. The room was small, but clean. We were placed on the side of the building by the a.c. unit mentioned by other reviewers. I called to switch rooms, but was told that they were at capacity and can only move us to the unrenovated part of the hotel. So we decided to stay. The picture quality of the t.v. was horrible. No microwave and fridge is filled with overpriced drinks leaving little room for you own items. The corridors are quite dark and a little scary. I wouldn't feel comfortable walking them alone and I'm from NYC! Overall, we were not impressed. Their customer service needs improvement. Spend a little more money and stay somewhere else. On a positive note, the bed was extremely comfortable and it was quiet (aside from the outside noise).

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Grand Hyatt, not bad”
text: Overall, great location, good sized room, would stay here again.

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “Better than expected”
text:
I took my girlfriend here for a weekend to celebrate our anniversary. When researching hotels, all that I really cared about that it was clean because it was just one night and we wouldn't be in the room all that much. I ended up choosing the Carlton because the good reviews far outweighed the bad, I never got a sense that the hotel was dirty, and it is located about 10 blocks from Times Square.
Upon arrival checkin was a breeze; checkin time wasn't until 3 but I got my room at 11 without a problem. The room was much bigger than expected. The only place it was small was the bathroom as getting around the door was a little difficult. The bed was extremely comfy and we slept great. Probably the best thing about the hotel is the location. Sure, it isn't right in the heart of Manhattan, but there are two subway stations within 2 blocks that get to Times Square or Rockefeller Center in a snap. Also, it's proximity to Penn Station meant that we were able to walk to the hotel in a matter of minutes.
The room cost almost $300 but that was to be expected staying in the city. Overall, our low expectations probably contributed to it, but we had a great stay and would likely return if we stayed in the city again.

name: Kitano New York
title: “Fantastic!”
text: Great hotel! Excellent location on Park Ave close to Broadway and the usual attractions. Grand Central station and it's gourmet shops was an excellent source of snacks and breakfast. Small lobby but reasonably large room which was very clean and attractive. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom was large and nicely kept up. Nice helpful staff; only a doorman without other wait staff but really not an issue since it's easy to get from the lobby to the room. Definitely would stay there. I've recommended this hotel to anyone going to New York. I paid around $250 which was an outstanding bargain; even at the regular price of $400 would be a bargain for New York.

name: Room Mate Grace
title: “Excellent emplacement !”
text:
Nous y avons passé 5 jours du 17 au 22 février 2012 surtout dans le but de visiter. 
L'emplacement (2 minutes à pieds de Times Square) est juste excellent ! La petite piscine passe bien pour soulager les jambes des kilomètres dans les pattes !!! ^^ 
Le personnel est très sympathique, les lits immenses et surélevés, la douche très fonctionnelle.
Le seul hic que je relèverai serait le wifi faible par moment et la réception qu'on dirait un petit shop...

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “4th Stay”
text: Back to the Eastgate yet again. The accommodations are clean, safe and very roomy Even the pull out sofa bed is pretty comfy and that's unusual. Having the kitchen is great. It means you don't have to eat 3 meals a day out if you want to save a few dollars. It's also nice to be able to bring home leftovers from restaurants if you like to do that. It's not the most trendy or fancy Hotel but it certainly meets my needs. If it didn't, I wouldn't return again and again. I'll be back.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Grand location, grand price, not so grand deal”
text:
We stayed there for a long weekend last month. 
Very good location. Literally steps from the Grand Central. However, this is the only thing "Grand" about this hotel besides it's "grand" rate starting at $350/night + ~15% tax. It doesn't even have a pool. Since it's on Park Avenue, I'd understand it belongs to one of the Park Hyatt's brand, but Grand? It's about 10-15 minutes walk and two stops on Subway from Time Square, which is where we went for the Broadway shows. Unlike Time Square, there are not many places still open after 10pm.
It's an older hotel with very well maintained lobby and meeting facilities. The rooms, well, are really showing their age. The paint on the room doors start to peeling off. I intended to take a picture of the door, but forgot to do so when checking out.
The King room we got is big and has modern decoration, while the bathroom is extremely small, comparable to those in 2-star motels such as Sleep Inn. We requested a quiet room which was facing inside. No view, but it is very quiet.
No coffee maker in room. We got vouchers for two 12oz coffee/day at the shop in the lobby. It's really good coffee, so is the napkins.

name: Pod 51
title: “I recomend.”
text: The room is small but worth the price and location.

name: Hotel 31
title: “zentrale Lage, nettes Personal, mit Sicherheit wieder”
text: Das Hotel liegt sehr zetral in Manhattan in einer relativ ruhige Straße. Die Zimmeraustattung ist ausreichend für den N.Y. Urlauber. Sauber und mit freundlichem Personal. Wir persönlich, werden mit Sicherheit in einer anderen Jahreszeit nochmals nach New York fliegen und nochmals dieses Hotel buchen. Für uns aber käme nur ein Doppelzimmer mit einem eigenen Bad in Frage. Insgesammt - zufriedenstellend.

name: Flatiron Hotel
title: “Plus ou moins bien”
text:
La situation est bonne car plusieurs stations de métro sont proches et possibilité de visites à pied.
Le hall de l’hôtel est très petit car il n'y a même pas un siège pour éventuellement attendre quelqu'un et la réception est petit comptoir d'a peine 2 mètres !!
Le personnel n'a pas été particulièrement accueillant ni chaleureux; ils me semblaient tous être
des débutants!
La chambre est très très petite mais avec tout ce qu'il faut , avec même des gadgets superficiels et/ou inutiles ( comme la tv dans le miroir de la salle de douche qui m'a gênée pour me maquiller ), la literie était très propres et très confortable mais Il y avait néanmoins beaucoup de bruit de la rue !!! Certaines nuits il y a eu beaucoup de bruit dans les couloirs à cause de clients qui rentraient en faisant énormément de chahut.
Les après-midis il y avait de la musique en live au restaurant et c'est chouette, mais lorsque l'on rentre dans son hôtel on trouve que le hall est plutôt très bruyant car le petit hall et le restaurant ne sont séparés que par une tenture !!!!!

name: The MAve
title: “Super great staff”
text: Very clean and modern looking. Last minute business trip and the staff was so helpful with planning site seeing and mapping my paths. Small room, but perfect for business travel. Stored my luggage safely all day and let me in drop off more stuff to add. Extremely reasonable rate.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan SoHo Village
title: “cozy hotel in a good location”
text:
I think this hotel is a decent choice in NYC depending on your expectations. I book a special rate program through the spg.com website. 50% off the second night but you had to pay a slightly higher rate the first night. Still a good deal. As a spg member I was hoping I might get an upgrade of some sort, but even my request for an upper floor seemed to go unrecognized. I also thought that the fact that I had prepaid my stay might get me a little better service in that regard. But I ended up with a room on the 10th floor. So I could barely see over the building at the back of the hotel. If you are on a floor lower than 10 and on the back of the building you will have zero view.
But that is all quibbling. The room itself was compact but efficient. Flat screen hi-def TV seems to be a requirement of most hotels these days. There is free wifi that worked fine. And an electronic safe in the little wardrobe. The bathroom is nice with a small sink/vanity. The shower is large and done in nice black granite tiles. The a/c is noisy and if you run the fan on auto it will kick on, cool the room artically for a couple of minutes and then shut off for a while. Running the fan continuously makes the noise less jarring and seems to keep things at a more constant temperature.
I found the bed fine, but the pillows really lacking in support.
I did not eat at the hotel. Prices are very high for food as most hotels do. There are tons of places to eat a short walk from the hotel. 
Two subway stations are nearby. The #1 7th Ave line is less than a block away. The C,E Spring Street station is a few blocks away. So easy access to midtown and beyond. Taxis are not familiar with the hotel. I had to direct my cabbie and he still went right past it.
There is a small grocery/deli on 6th Ave, so a short walk away for picking up a couple of things. 
Film Forum is nearby.
The staff were very friendly.
All things considered I think this is a decent choice in the Manhattan. In the last couple of years I have been to NYC three times and this was certainly the best of those hotels I stayed in.

name: The Roger
title: “Excellent boutique hotel”
text: I stayed at The Roger for 2 nights for a business trip in November and really enjoyed my stay. Very nice boutique hotel. Clean and up-to-date room. Very friendly and helpfull staff. Everything you need to enjoy your stay NYC.

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “I AM HAPPY WITH STAY”
text: I certify that this review is my genuine opinion of this hotel, and that I have no personal or business affiliation with this establishment, and have not been offered any incentive or payment originating from the establishment to write this review.

name: The Roger
title: “Loved our stay at The Roger”
text: We just spent Thanksgiving week at The Roger and absolutely loved it. We were booked into a nice room on our first night but we were advised that the room had some problem that needed work. We were upgraded into a beautiful two room suite. We found the staff at the hotel to be exceptional in meeting our needs and providing directions, etc. The Roger exceeded our expectations in every area. We would definitely stay there again in the future and would recommend the hotel to our friends.

name: Sutton Court Hotel Residences
title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
My two adult daughters & I stayed here for a week. The room was large enough to comfortably accommodate the three of us which is not easily found in NYC. The room was spotless & the kitchen was fully equipped. The fact that housekeeping was not included in the rate was not an issue for us.
A delightful surprise was that we had free long-distance calling. There was also free broadband internet.
The area is quiet but with plenty of restaurants & a nearby groceteria. Two subway lines are 5 to 6 blocks away.

name: Sutton Court Hotel Residences
title: “Très bien, conforme à toutes les photos et descriptif”
text: Un appartement vu sur la ville répondant exactement à toutes les descriptions lues et vues. Un seul petit bémol, il faut payer pour avoir le WI Fi dans la chambre.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Timeless Classic”
text:
My husband and I chose to kick off our honeymoon and spend New Year's Eve and the begining of the New Year at the beautiful Waldorf-Astoria in New York. The first word that comes to mind is classy.
The lobby is gorgeous and decorated with red and gold towering Christmas trees. When we arrived, we were given a free upgrade from our standard queen bedroom to a Waldorf Towers room. We had a gorgeous view of the city and could see the fireworks at midnight, albeit over the tops of some buildings.
We ordered room service, which was delicious, and thoroughly enjoyed the traditional Sunday brunch on New Year's Day. From the caviar blinis to the smoked salmon, from the french toast and chicken sausage to the waldorf salad, and topped off with a wide variety of pastries and desserts, it was a scrumptious New Year's feast washed down with a mimosa and sparkling water.
The service was great, the room was decorated in lovely, rich colors and perfectly clean. It did not feel outdated at all, as some reviews seemed to suggest. 
It was expensive. That's just a fact. We probably won't be heading back except for another special occasion-- it would have to be pretty special too. But if you can spring for it, it's a great stay.

name: Sutton Court Hotel Residences
title: “Rare !”
text:
Forces :
Le staff aux petits soins avec ses clients.
Appartement spacieux, lumineux et calme. La suite que j'ai occupée avec mes enfants au 33ème étage, orientation Sud, avait une vue imprenable sur le Chrysler building, l'Empire State building et l'East River.
La literie de qualité supérieure.
Salle de bains avec baignoire et véritable cuisine entièrement équipée.
Une ligne de bus sur la 57ème rue traverse tout Manhattan d'Est en Ouest.
Sutton Court Hotel Residences est parfait et bien mieux qu'un hôtel de Midtown / Times Square !
Faiblesses : 
La climatisation, très efficace mais assez bruyante. Heureusement, elle est individuelle à chaque appartement, réglable et peut être éteinte .

name: W New York - Union Square
title: “Fun hotel and location”
text: The W Union Square has a really enjoyable location that, when you are staying there, makes you feel like a native New Yorker. You walk out the hotel's front door to a mix of high/low characters, shops and restaurants that feels supremely urban and is interesting, especially on days that the Greenmarket (farmer's market as we call it in California) is being held in Union Square Park. The W New York is also one of the few hotels I have found in New York where it is possible to get a room with two queen size beds, a huge plus when traveling with family. Rooms with a view of the park are especially nice. Finding a doorman to help can be pretty random and the desk staff seems pretty uninterested in the clientele. I don't care though, it's a fun hotel.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott New York Manhattan / Times Square
title: “great value”
text: This is a brand new hotel near Time Square conveniently located. Subway station is 2 minutes away and the Theater District is within walking distance. The street it is on looks worrisome but was safe to walk around even at night. It is a great value for the closeness to Time Square but if you want to stay in more "in" street, then you'd need to pay more. We'd go back again. Free breakfast was quite convenient to start the day.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott New York Manhattan / Times Square
title: “Not a place I'll come back to.”
text:
The hotel is new, the rooms are ok for me, smaller than the rooms at the Residence Inn on 6th Ave. The closet was too much but it does have a big HDTV in the room. Hotel is down a side street, which is a dirty street and next door to the New York State Parole board, and a row of adult video stores. If you are willing to see past that, it is near to Time Square and 9th Ave, where the reasonable restaurants are, and the subway. 
The staff was the worse of all the Marriott properties I have stayed at, pretty indifferent, clinical and not very helpful. There was no self-service/coin operated launderette (the in-room information guide mentioned that there was). Not sure if it's a NY practice, but they provides only dry-cleaning service, no regular laundry service. And what pisses me off was that you had to take your laundry to the Front Desk, they will not pick it up from your room !
Breakfast was nothing to shout about and the breakfast area was often full with no place to sit if you head down slightly later.
Not a place I'll come back to.

name: W New York - Union Square
title: “Great location for exploring lower half of Manhattan.”
text:
Although the W is a larger hotel, it is not a super sized, impersonal convention hotel. We generally prefer to stay at smaller boutique hotel but we chose the W for this visit because of it's location, price and room size (needed space for 3rd person). If you want to escape the over crowded TImes Square/midtown area, this is a good option. Conveniently situated at the corner of bustling Union Square. Lots of activity in the immediate area and just a short walk to Chelsea, Gramercy Park and Greenwich Village. For those who are going to a Broadway show, it is a short subway or taxi ride to that area.
The bed was very comfortable. Lighting in the bathroom was excellent.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Disappointed +++++”
text: The room was very shabby - metal coffee table was rusty - bathroom basin was cracked - shower tiles were cracked - bathroom air vent clogged with dust +++. Very noisy - I could hear doors slamming, TV & voices from other rooms. No tea / coffee making facilities. No room in the fridge for guests to store drinks etc - it is jammed packed with over-priced drinks & snacks. No cold drinks available for purchase in the gift shop - guests either have to purchase from the room fridge or go out to purchase! I paid over $2000.00 for 6 nights / 5 days - this did not include internet broadband or wifi in guest room - this was an additional expense - this surely could be included in the the tarriff!!! as it is in most other hotels! Very loud music played in the foyer area which I thought was very intrusive - especially at 6.30am breakfast! Concierge often not available & when he was - most unhelpful. I was advised by the concierge & desk staff that a taxi would be $75 -80 to JFK - luckily I read a review & discovered that this was for a Black Cab - Yellow Cabs are only $40.00!! The hotel staff tried +++ to direct me to a Black Cab as I departed the hotel - I hailed a Yellow Cab - much to the disgust of the porter! Room service was OK. I would not recommend this hotel.

name: Renaissance New York Hotel 57
title: “Thank you to Ms. Lady Hernandez and Ms. Amada Sosa”
text: When I got to the Hotel my first impression was that it was definitively not to my liking. But this two ladies made my stay very pleasant. They tried to accomodate me in every possible way. I'm a bit of a snob when it comes to Hotels but due that I was traveling with other members of my family I felt that to stay with them in the same hotel was the practical thing to do. My room I felt was very small with a nice view. The barthroom was comfortable. But lacking in toiletries but when I mentioned to Ms. Sosa she made sure that I had all I needed. The same thing happened with the refrigerator..they don't have them or at least not in the two rooms we had..but as soon as I mentioned I got one. The hotel has a beautiful terrace on the 17th Floor with a fantastic view and nice for before and after dinner drinks. I will definitively do this one again. THANK YOU.

name: The Roger
title: “Poor Experience; Bad Hospitality”
text: The Roger is newly renovated, and the facility is thus nice. But our experience was poor. Upon check-in, we were provided with no information -- either at the front desk or in the room -- about the hotel -- e.g., is there wifi, is there a fitness center, etc. The room was fine, but bathroom was tiny, with almost no shelf space. And we had almost no water pressure, and thus could barely shower. We could also hear much noise from the hallway and from the next room. We also asked for extra towels but did not receive them for hours; I later called the desk and they were brought to the room. In the room, there's a constant attempt to sell products and milk more money from guests. If you hurt yourself and need a band-aid, you must pay $5. An average size water in your room would cost $6. A package of gum is $5. But the worst was the shock experienced when, upon check out, we were assessed a mandatory $21 "service fee." When questioned, the desk clerk explained that the fee covers wifi, the fitness center, etc. Apparently, acceptance of this fee is made upon check-in, but this fee was not mentioned to me until check out. This fee utterly turned me off to the hotel (and did the same to others to whom I've mentioned it). I've stayed at dozens of NYC hotels, and I have never been charged a service fee. The hotel, though not all bad, should seriously consider the meaning of the concept of hospitality.

name: Renaissance New York Hotel 57
title: “Great location, nice rooms.”
text: I stayed in Hotel 57 for Christmas with my husband. It was a great stay. Rooms are small, as expected in New York, but very modern and comfortable. The lounge serves nice cocktails which are great after a day of walking around the city. The staff was friendly and had no problem letting us keep our luggage there after check out so we could enjoy the rest of our last day there. It's not smack in the middle of Times Square so it has a calmer vibe which is nice at the end of the day. Still, you're in Midtown so there's always something going on nearby. I have stayed in many hotels in Manhattan, big and small, but I truly enjoyed my stay at Hotel 57 and will definitely be back.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan SoHo Village
title: “Noisy”
text:
PROs: Very polite staff. Very nice location, close to fantastic SoHo. Easy to store luggage after check out ...
CONs: The hotels ventilator outside the hotelroom window (rm 207) was very - the only time we could not hear it was when the even louder room A/C started!!!! Not easy to sleep from the noise - and we're normally not sensitive at all....

name: Seton Hotel
title: “NY experience”
text: Arriving in Ny 3 days after Hurricane Sandy we were fortunate to experience the delight of the Hotel Seton. Fabulous location within walking distance of so many sights but also 2 blocks from central station and the subway. Had room on 6th floor with well proportioned bathroom. Not huge but perfectly good for stay in NY when most of the time is way from the room. Surprised that the noise wasn't too bad considering a front room and by the amount of storage for a small room. Simple but stylish, friendly staff, common lounge room, free coffee/tea and free wireless....bonus. Overall highly recommend this as an affordable and welcoming place to stay. Thanks Seton....

name: Avalon Hotel
title: “Good location”
text: I stayed at this hotel with my daughter in November. It is very well located. The room on the 9th floor was spotlessly clean and serviced daily. Furnishings were a little tired but the bed was comfortable. It was generally very quiet, but our room was opposite the lift,so inevitably, there was some noise with comings and goings. The check-in and out was speedy and all the staff were very friendly and polite. We walked Manhattan - up as far as 72nd Street and down to Little Italy (it was difficult to venture any further downtown because of Sandy). Plenty of local restaurants and diners for breakfast and dinner ... who needs lunch after a NY breakfast! All in all I would recommend this hotel.

name: The Roger
title: “Nice litte friendly hotel”
text:
The Roger is a very cute little hotel on 31 and Madison. The best part ofthehotel was the friendliness and helpfulness of the staff. We just had a harrowing trip, culminating with a cab ride from the airport with no ac in106 degree heat. Before we had even checked in, Limda was taking care of my ill wife. Once we were in the hotel, we immediately relaxed. 
The rooms are quite small, but comfortable. There are nice small delis and coffee shops on the same block which are worth visiting.

name: The Roger
title: “Roger that! Mad Men Glamour in the Heart of Manhattan”
text: The Roger is a sweet little hotel in the heart of Manhattan. My room was quiet (even though it was facing Madison Ave. Comfortable beds and bedding, nice bathroom, desk, chair etc. makes good use of a compact space. They've recently refurbished the property and it's got a Mad Men glamour with little touches of sophistication in every corner. But it's the staff that makes it an especially comfortable place to be. Thank you Muslima and all the girls at the bar and restaurant! I'll be back for sure.

name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York
title: “St Giles is always a good choice”
text: St giles is a convenient place to stay in the City. # blocks from Grand Central and within easy walking distances from many attractions. It is always very clean, the staff is extremely helpful and friendly. It is a great value.

name: City Club Hotel
title: “great place to stay!!”
text: This is a smaller hotel but great location 44th st between 5th & 6th avenue.The staff are very attentive as soon as you ask for anything it is delivered to your room quickly.The room was great the luxe double double had ample room for five of us. A few doors down from city club is a great diner where you can have breakfast or pick up coffee,bagels, muffins and take back to your room. Bonus huge homemade cookies in your room every night.we really enjoyed our stay here.

name: Kitano New York
title: “Tolles Hotel im super Lage !”
text:
Wir haben uns sehr wohlgefühlt. Das Hotel ist nur zu empfehlen.
sehr sauber, ansprechendes Ambiente, freundliches und hilfsbereites Personel. Unser Blick aus dem Fenster fiel jeden Morgen auf den Empire
State Building !!! Lage - direkt im Herzen von Manhattan.Wir kommen gerne wieder!

name: Renaissance New York Hotel 57
title: “Memorable, comfortable stay at a cool hotel.”
text: My husband and I stated at Hotel 57 more than two years ago. At that time the hotel was finishing up some refurbishing. We took along our daughter who was almost 2 at the time. Maybe traveling with a toddler to NYC was not the brightest idea but it was fun. When we arrived, the staff greeted us warmly and they were quite friendly. It was our first trip to NYC together and were pretty unfamiliar with the area. They graciously switched us to a larger room on a nicer floor for no extra charge after my husband petitioned nicely. They gave us several vouchers for free breakfast at their restaurant/lounge...I think we only paid for breakfast once in the five days that we were there. The room was spacious enough with a great view of the street. Every morning my daughter would wake up and sit on the window ledge looking at the cabs passing by. I would recommend this hotel based on the service, cleanliness, location and the price. NOTE: I TRAVELLED IN 2009 ON MEMORIAL DAY WEEKEND NOT IN 2011.

name: Comfort Inn Times Square West
title: “I'm horrible with titles.”
text:
Choose this hotel by searching around online for a nice quality hotel that wasn't horribly expensive. Came acroos this comfort inn and read other reviews about this hotel on TA. and decided to try it. Sooo glad I choose this place. Extremely clean; can't say enough about how clean this place was. Especially after all the hype about bedbugs in NYC. I also found out that this hotel opened only eight months ago which has alot to do with its general appearance. It felt like I was staying in a London hotel. The continental breakfast was OK. The lady that was working the breakfast counter was making sure that there was enough food out all the time so people didn't feel like they ran out of stuff. She worked very hard every morning making delicious waffles one at a time for customers. I gave her a tip on our final morning. In the lobby they provide a personal computer for free internet which was nice to look up info on NYC.
The room was on the smaller side but not to bad, I've seen worse. Great TV, Nice shower and bathroom, Surprised to find a nice size mini-frige. The place is close to restaurants on 9th ave. and if you like Time square thats was two blocks up the street. I personally can do without time square but with a teenager traveling with us it's great. NY is extremely safe. Felt comfortable and safe at 1 am walking near and around the hotel.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Only If You Can Get A Great Rate.”
text:
Many visitors compare the lobby of the New York Hilton to Grand Central Station. That’s an insult to Grand Central, which is looking pretty good these days. This place, on the other hand, is noisy and hectic, with people jostling in all directions, insufficient seating, and long lines at the front desk. There’s another line to speak with one of three concierges, some of whom are pleasant and helpful, others who could do with a little less New York attitude. If this weren’t enough, there are two desks that look like information booths, but are inhabited by salespeople shilling other Hilton properties. They tout their “free offers” every time you walk by, and just barely stop short of using the hook to ensnare you. Not exactly a gracious experience.
The hotel is enormous, and the wait for an elevator can at times be exasperating. Our twelfth floor room was fortunately a renovated one, and certainly comfortable for two people. Sleek, built-in furniture allowed space for a king-sized bed, sofa, flat-screen TV. The small bathroom was also updated, with a nice-sized walk-in shower. Housekeeping did an excellent job – the room always felt clean. 
The hotel’s number one asset is its location – walking distance to lots of sights (Central Park, Lincoln Center, Times Square, Rockefeller Center). Easy subway lines are nearby. We didn’t eat at the hotel’s Marketplace Restaurant. It was expensive and crowded at breakfast. There are lots of other places to eat in the immediate area. The New York Hilton is fine if you can dash through the lobby and book it for a decent price.

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “No Frills ... Great Location”
text:
For first time visitors to NYC, the area could be intimidating. Trash is put on the street to collect, but that is common in the city. The location, however, is perfect for a tourist since it is pretty much smack in the middle of New York City. Don't count on the offered concierge service for much information ... the answer to a couple from the UK about how to get to Penn Station was a "it's over there" and a wave of the hand. Do your research using the lobby computers. 
The rooms are small ... good for two people, but plan on doing a dodge/weave/bump to get by each other with three or four in the room. Do not accept a room on the second floor if possible. The breakfast room is on this floor and I witnessed one man in his pajamas at the front desk complaining about the noise level just a few feet from the door of his room. The A/C units are loud and the windows do not open, so bring earplugs if you are a lite sleeper. 
Staff in this hotel could use a little training in friendliness. They tend to be very curt and a bit dismissive and the man working the breakfast room was downright rude. 
Overall, NYMA is a good tourist hotel. If you need a large room, stay elsewhere. Stay here for the location.

name: W New York - Union Square
title: “The Decline of the W Union Square: Stay Away”
text:
Here's the breakdown:
Pros:
- Location (easy access to the East Village, Union Square and the 4,5,6)
- Toiletries (like every W) are wonderful
- Room service is delicious
Cons:
- Attitude and steadily declining service levels (especially when compared to the Le Meridien, Library and now defunct W Tuscany and W Court)
- Rooms desperately need a refresh (very late capitalism)
- Price high compared to other hotels in similar price tiers
I used to really love this hotel - it was the first W I've stayed at and five years ago was really top of the line. But my past few visits have been less than satisfactory and this one, in particular, took the cake for abysmal service. First, the staff was consistently rude and surprisingly unresponsive. Things were consistently late - for example, requesting a robe at 11:30 and getting it an hour later, or having to call twice for basics like toothpaste. On Saturday night, the front desk was unstaffed and the woman at the concierge casually informed me that I would have to wait for them to come back up. When I asked if she would call because we had been waiting for ten minutes, she told me "they saw it on the security cameras and would come up when they could." Also, despite being in the hotel for five days, the hotel couldn't figure out a way to make my keys work every single time...I ended up just getting a new key every time I finished to avoid the hassle. 
Last night, I asked to place an order for room service and Whatever Whenever told me that they couldn't take my order because room service was "out." I called back and India said she couldn't help me and that they would call me when they were ready. Finally, I called the Platinum Concierge to REROUTE me to room service, which is absolutely ridiculous. The food was great but aggravation a good condiment does not make.
Terrible service plus the outdated furnishings, awful elevator traffic, unresponsive staff and dated gym have pushed me over the edge. I'm never coming back. If you have to stay in a Starwood hotel, go to the Library, Le Meridien or St. Regis. If you have the flexibility, go check out the Ace or the Setai. Just stay away from this disaster.

name: Pod 51
title: “Great Mulitple Stays”
text: I have stayed at the Pod Hotel dozens of times going back to the days when it was the Pickwick Arms Hotel and have always had a positive experience. I live about 40 minutes outside of the city, so after night out, I tend to want to avoid the hassle of trains and driving and just have a place to stay nearby. The Pod has always fit those needs. Granted, the rooms are small, but they have always been immaculate on EVERY visit to the multiple rooms I have stayed in. The service has always been decent although I can understand other reviewers complaints about the front desk not always being the friendliest. The location is great since it is slightly outside of the tourist areas so it isn't so noisy. One word of advice is that if you are not a single occupant, do not book anything less than the Queen room because even the double beds are too small for two people to sleep comfortably. An additional note of caution is that the rooms with private bathrooms have a glass wall between it and the main part of the room so privacy is not there if you are staying with someone else (not sure why anyone would design something like that!!). You would be better off using the shared bathrooms/showers in the hall if you want privacy, but just make sure the door lock is working properly after you go in. I had one experience where I didn't realize the lock didn't work and had the door opened multiple times on me while showering with a nearly see-through shower curtain! I have also found that the prices vary quite a bit and it can be quite expensive. I have always booked my rooms for between $89.00 (Single Pod) to $149.00 (Double Pod) but the prices have taken a drastic upswing more recently. I tend to book if the prices are lower than other reputable hotels in the city as a frame of reference. It has overall been a very pleasant experience as long as you get a good rate versus other reputable hotel chain rates. Compare prices before you book.

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “Carlton on Madison hotel”
text:
Just back from NY and I was staying at the Carlton on Madison, good hotel with pleasant helpful staff, the room {401) street view first floor was very good and more than adequate for our needs.
The hotel is near the junction of broadway and as there is a open park area at every Broadway junction the Madison Park is a welcome respite from the congested buildings, a quiet coffee watching the locals walk thier dogs and eat out the buckets :-) {only one} was very entertaining.
I'd recommend the hotel and the city as I never seen any sign of trouble in the entire city and there was more than enough to keep anybody entertained, what did surprise me was the architecture as I never thought there would be so many historic and interesting buildings, a great trip and I'll definately recommend the hotel and the city.

name: Radisson Martinique on Broadway
title: “Radisson Martinique New York City”
text:
Stayed for 3 nights, in April , 2008. Great Location, subway practically underneath the hotel, Macy Dept. store is 1/2 bllock away, Empire State Bldg is about couple of blocks.. about 15 minutes walk to Time Square/Broadway Theatres... Located in Korea town with lots of Korean Restaurents, Massage places.
Business center with free use of computer for internet. Check in at 4 pm but you can leave the lungages with them if you get there early. Cost about $28-32 taxi fare from LaGuardia.
Negatives..would be old hotel with most room has no view, has windows but looking at other windows and cannot see the city or the streets. Weak concierge sevices, located together with gift shop cashier... did not give us the Club Level room (eventhough we booked and paid for as Club Level, citing they have no records) Club Level Rooms are top two floors 15 & 16 has access to snacks and services... Executive levels are nothing more than higher floor 12 and above and no special room or privileges.
Having stayed at Radisson Lexington New York City 5 months ago, both are old hotels, noisey at Radisson Lexington with lots of construction in the building, and bathroom is smaller than Radisson Martiniques. Location is much better at Martinuque on Broadaway. Radisson Martinique on Broadway used to be Holiday Inn.

name: 6 Columbus - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Great Location - Good Value”
text: Our stay at this hotel was perfect. Friendly staff, great price on the room (Priceline), immaculately clean, chic bath & decor, fantastic location for our evening at Lincoln Center. I'd stay here again in a heartbeat.

name: Renaissance New York Hotel 57
title: “LOVE IT!”
text: Great friendly staff amazing location. Great rooms not too small. I would stay here again for sure.

name: Renaissance New York Hotel 57
title: “Great Stay...with a couple of 'issues'....”
text:
Just returned from a one night stay and overall it was terrific. 
The pros....
Instant free upgrade on check in to a larger room (due to being a 'silver member'). 
The room was very clean and sleek, with a lovely bathroom and nice features like a safe and flat screen TV. Bed VERY comfortable with great comforter and four pillows! 
Wonderful Aveda products supplied the bathroom (soap, shampoo, conditioner and lotion only). 
Internet access was charged but credited back on check out (again due to 'silver' status).
Staff in hotel was flawless at check in, drinks in the bar in the evening (live jazz band), and housekeeping. The housekeeper was lovely and accomodating to requests for extra soap etc. We stored our luggage for several hours at checkout (12 noon! So much better than 11:00!) and the bellhop was terrific also.
Great location!
The Cons:
The platform bed invites banging shins against the corners when walking around the room.. This is NOT because our particular room was too small, just poor design of the bed and the corners being hidden under the comforter.
There were only two bath sized towels in the bathroom. At least one more would have been helpful. Also no hooks in the bathroom for wet towels, etc.
The most important CON was arriving in the restaurant for Easter Sunday breakfast/brunch. We were seated (at a table with incomplete settings) only to wait over ten minutes with no attention. We were then informed that the restaurant was closed for the next 30 minutes so they could change over from breakfast to brunch. We left wondering why the 'Special Easter Brunch' was advertised as starting when we arrived and feeling like the service really lacked in professionalism and simple manners. No apology, no nothing. Just "we're closed for the next half hour; if you want to come back then, that's fine". It was such a downer way to end the stay.
We were able to see what the 'cozy' rooms look like as opposed to the room we were upgraded to, and they are seriously small in comparison.
All in all I would absolutely definitely return to this hotel for the room, the overall service and the bar in the evening but I would not return for a meal in the restaurant.

name: 6 Columbus - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Back again to the same great service”
text: 6 Columbus is as you would expect right by Columbus Circle but not so close that you have to endure non stop traffic. I got in from a long flight and was given room keys at 3pm. As I wanted a bath and was given a room with a shower I talked to the bell hop and then reception. Within fifteen minutes I was in a room with a huge bath. The rest of my stay was a joy. Great, responsive and friendly service at a great location in midtown right by Central Park. The sushi bar in reception is very atmospheric (unusual in hotels these days) if a little pricey. Next time I'll be heading right back to Number 6. Thank you.

name: Equity Point New York @ Times Square
title: “Great value - choose a larger room”
text:
We travelled there at Christmas time and thought the hotel was fantastic value, considering what some other hotels were charging for the holiday period.
Having read some of the other reviews, we stayed in the Queen Penthouse suite which wasn't a huge room but more than adequate for our 3-night stay and, as a smoker, the outside terrace overlooking the street below and part of 7th Avenue was handy. We thought it was great value for money, especially as the price included a continental breakfast in the mornings, capuccinos and other soft drinks all day and complimentary wine and chocolates in the room.
The location is just fantastic to walk around all the tourist hot spots - Times Square, the theatre district, the shops on 5th Ave and Central Park. The bar at the hotel is quite cool for cocktails before going out to eat.
I think on my next trip to NYC I'll probably stay somewhere more expensive for comparison purposes, as the rates won't be as high during non-holiday season, but anticipate I'll wonder whether it was paying the extra as we coudn't really fault Hotel 41 for the price or the level of service we received.

name: Comfort Inn Times Square West
title: “Tolles, kleines Hotel im Herzen von Manhattan”
text:
Wir waren für 4 Nächte im Comfort Inn (im Theatre District) in Manhattan. Das Hotel hat 6 Stockwerke und liegt nicht weit vom Time Square entfernt. Das ist als Ausgangspunkt für Sightseeing- und Shoppingtage in NY sehr optimal. ;-)
Unser Zimmer lag im obersten Stockwerk, hatte einen tollen Blick über Manhattan und war sehr sauber. Zur Zimmeraussattung gehörte ein Fernseher, Kühlschrank und ein Safe.
Das Personal in diesem Hotel ist sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit.
Im Zimmerpreis war ein Continentales Frühstück inbegriffen, was man unten in der Hotellobby einnehmen konnte. Hier gab es ein Buffet mit Toastbrot, Muffins, Marmelade, Eier, Speck, frischen Waffeln, Obst, Cerelalien, Obstsäften, Kaffee, Tee...
(-) Der einzige kleine Kritikpunkt, den wir bei diesem Frühstücksbuffet haben, ist die Müllansammlung. Es werden Pappteller und Plastebesteck verwendet. Jede Butter, Marmelade, Cerealien ist einzeln in Plastik-Abpackungen verpackt. Jeden Morgen werden dort Berge an Mülltüten rausgeschleppt... aber das gehört wohl einfach zu Amerika dazu ;-))
Uns hat der Aufenthalt im Comfort Inn sehr gut gefallen. Wir würden auf jeden Fall dieses Hotel wieder buchen.

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “Awesome facility, staff and location”
text: We are pleased to report that on our recent trip to NYC the New York Manhattan Hotel on 6w, 32nd street proved to be a worthwhile investment. The facility was immaculately clean and well cared for, the staff most curteous and helpful. Everyone was accomodating and a pleasure to speak to at all times. The location is superb, centrally located to absolutely everything. seconds to a subway, bus outside the door, but most importantly walking distance to all the central attractions. For those who have been to NYC numerous times as us, it is closer to all the Chelsea, Gramercy and Murray Hill districts. Amazing Korean foods outside the door and of course, right off 5th ave. What more could you want?! Great rates and flexibility if needed. We highly recommend this hotel.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Fantastic location and views!”
text:
Very nice hotel. We stayed here back in 2005 and on planning our return to NY we couldnt find anywhere with such a fantastic view. You should book a room with a Times Square view otherwise it will just be like staying in any old hotel. Its the view that makes it.
The room is large with bed, tv, wardrobe, bath and shower. The room isnt 5 star by any standard but it is very comfortable.
The staff in the hotel were always very helpful. There is free computer access in the lobby and also a free printer so we were able to book tickets and carry out online check in for the return flight home.
There is also a roof terrace with views over Times Square.
Overall very nice hotel, we would return again.

name: Pod 51
title: “Clean, compact, comparatively cheap and conveniently situated”
text:
Pod Hotel is pretty much what it says on the tin, small! Our room (double with private bathroom) was clean and fairly comfortable. The hotel is ideally situated in Manhattan within walking distance of Times Square and the Rockerfeller Centre et al. Whilst it was fairly pricey, when compared with the other Hotels in the city is wasn't that expensive. On check in we found the batteries in our safe weren't working but this was quickly sorted out after speaking with staff on the front desk without any fuss.
Great location, clean, relatively good value and free wi-fi.

name: Avalon Hotel
title: “Les plus grandes et belles chambres pour un petit prix : le top”
text: Arrivés à l'hôtel, nous avons été accueillis avec un charmant sourire. Réceptionniste parlant l'anglais et l'espagnol. Au 12ème étage, chambre 1203, lorsque nous avons ouvert la porte : OUAH.... Super grande chambre (double), très propre,décoration soignée : mélange de classique et moderne. Internet wifi illimité et gratuit, 2 télés avec console de jeu, un coin frigo bar, un salon avec canapé et bureau. Grande salle de bain avec Douche et baignoire et double vasque. Bien insonorisé, climatisation réglable et journal gratuit tous les matins. Petit déjeuner très copieux et très bon : buffet Européen et américain. hôtel très bien situé :à 200 m de la 5ème avenue et de l'Empire State building. Bref, le top pour une famille avec 2 enfants.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Nice location close to Central Park”
text:
Stayed for two nights for a conference close to hotel. Nicely located a short walk about 4 blocks south of Central Park (obvious from a map but north-south blocks much shorter than east-west). 
The main asset is the location, it is otherwise a large hotel, appears to be well-run. The lobby and rooms match the impression one receives from the exterior of the hotel, that it is a bit dated but functional.
Would recommend if like me you are staying for a conference at a conference rate.
ps - note that the charges for hotel internet seemed high, roughly $16 for "medium" speed and $19 for "high" speed.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Good central location”
text:
Have stayed at this hotel 3 times within the last year. The main reason for this was the location, and to earn more air miles! Not very far at all from 5th Avenue, Central Park or Times Sqare.
We went for a few days shopping. Clean rooms, good size. The Deluxe rooms seem to have been newly renovated unlike the Executive rooms. However, esentially there is not much difference between them.
Can be busy as it is also a conference hotel, we found it worthwhile booking into an Exectutive room to get the continental breakfast inc. Nice breakfast, with nice lounge to sit in. Able to help youself to a buffet of fresh fruit, bagels, cerreal, coffee and juice etc.
Is quite pricey, but you know what you're getting which is why I've stayed there 3 times.

name: Gild Hall - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Great hotel in the Financial District”
text: Hotel is fantastic and great value. Great beds, awesome flat screen tv. Very convienient to the subway.

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “Good value!”
text: This hotel isn't about fancy lobbies or luxurious rooms. However, if you put value in location and will spend most of your time outside of the hotel this sure is a hit for the relatively low cost. The hotel is very centrally situated in the midst of Korea Town, don't get scared, this is a small enclave that is just a few metres away from Empire State Building, Macy's, Time Square and Madison Square Garden. The rooms aren't large, but they do the trick if you unpack smartly. We lived at the highest floor (17th) and the shower beam was the weakest we've ever experienced. So if you book, make sure to stay in the lower/mid part of the building. From what we have heard, this is common in high buildings in New York. The breakfast and internet is included, very good value indeed! The breakfast isn't fancy or anything, but again, it'll start your day pretty well with the limited (but well tasting) options. We couldn't find any eggs, maybe the hotel management should change that.

name: City Club Hotel
title: “After the shock,a pleasant stay!”
text:
When booking this hotel through a booking agent,we expected two beds in our room. The exceptionally small room contained one double bed,no chairs,no table ... very small... Those were the negatives. 
The bed was so very comfortable,the room very clean and the shower was amazing ... especially appreciated after a long day of sightseeing and theater-going in NY! The staff was friendly and,clearly do their best to accommodate their customers. The location is perfect and the hotel is so very quiet!
We would stay there again!

name: Equity Point New York @ Times Square
title: “Great midtown hotel!”
text:
Stayed for 1 night in December 2004, and I'll be back again. Awesome location near Times Square and a 2 block walk to our office. Value for the price ($160) is amazing. Was on the 6th floor though and the view was of a brick wall.
Room is small but comfortable, but not a surprise based on the reviews. Staff were helpful. The desk chair could be better or I could lose weight, because it was really wobbly. Shower took a few minutes to warm up in the morning but no big deal. Bed was very comfortable and I couldn't hear any outside noise.
Free high-speed internet, very good breakfast, 24-hour espresso in the bar and free DVD/CD borrowing were really nice features. Also $10 for a day pass to the fitness center down the street.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “It was great.”
text: I liked to location (each of the most important attraction couls be reached very easy), the service and the room as well. The bed is comfortable which is very rare.

name: Pod 51
title: “An extraordinary budget option”
text:
I spent 3 nights in September at The Pod Hotel in a single with private bath, and I was extremely satisfied with the hotel. 
It is very well located, being near 2 different subway lines and within walking distance of a several sites (including MOMA and St. Patrick’s). For those with mobility limitations or with luggage, the nearby E line station can be accessed by escalator rather than stairs. There are many restaurants in the area representing a wide range of cuisines and price options, as well as various stores and a lovely, small public park with an artificial waterfall and shaded seating. 
My room was (as expected) quite small, but it was laid out so efficiently that it did not feel overly cramped to me. In case it matters to you, the bed was a twin. The modern shower had a “rain” showerhead, which I must admit is not to my liking – I prefer an angled spray, but that’s a matter of personal preference.
I thought the hotel’s staff and amenities surprisingly comprehensive for the price. My room and all public areas were spotless. Hotel staff were efficient and helpful, and both concierges I met were informative. (Brian was outstanding.) The hotel offers free wifi and the lobby has several touch-pad computers mounted on a column for guests’ use. The “snack” counter (open from early morning until about 10 p.m. if I recall correctly) offered some delicious breakfast options and some wines and beers at reasonable prices (I didn’t pay attention to other choices). Seating was available both indoors and outside in a small, pleasant, urban courtyard. The roof deck also offered a pleasant respite. 
An aside: There is a bistro just outside the Pod, one you can even enter directly from the Pod - Le Bateau. In the late afternoon, it can be a pleasant place to stop for a drink if you are prepared to pay premium prices. It is open quite late – which is nice – but the later the hour, the louder the music. By late evening, I found the noise decidedly aversive. When I commented on it, Le Bateau staff told me their clients prefer to have the volume of music that high. If you disagree (as do I), please let them know!

name: City Club Hotel
title: “Great location and environment”
text:
I'm still laughing about the comment below regarding lack of TV in the room. The TV is behind a glass wall - when it's off, it's as if it weren't there. 
Anyhow, I have stayed numerous times in this hotel since it first opened, and if you're a theatre-goer, this is one of the most amazing locations. The Red Flame diner a few doors down is a gem, plus DB Moderne is one of the best restaurants in NYC. I love staying at this hotel.

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “Great location and good value”
text:
A friend and I were going to New York to see a show, visit museums and stay one night--but we did not want to break the bank on a hotel. We reserved a room with two double beds for $244 (that price includes tax). The hotel is located in the heart of Korea Town--complete with festive lights strung across 32nd Street. It is a bustling kind of dirty street, a half block off of Fifth Avenue--there are few streets not bustling and dirty in Manhattan. The reception area is nice, clean, and the staff was welcoming, kind and helpful. I asked for a quiet room and was told that all rooms with two double beds are located at the back of the building--the room was quiet indeed. I did not avail myself of the amenities, but there were many including free WiFi, breakfast, a fitness room (cannot vouch for it) and free calling in the US (I like that).
The room was small but perfect for two friends traveling together. There was a gap and bedside table between the beds, and the other side of each was against a wall. There was a dresser, desk and flat screen TV (never turned it on). There was a clock radio that allowed the docking of a Nano. The bathroom was small but adequate--small vanity but good water pressure in the shower. There were plenty of towels and the toiletries included two each of shampoo, lotion, bath soap and face soap. 
Several small quibbles: the pillows were harder than I would like. I love a feather pillow but know this is a personal preference, my husband loves a hard foam pillow of this sort.
