We could hear conversations in the hallway--so if someone was telling friends or relatives good night you could hear every word--made me sympathize with the two rooms adjacent to the elevator, and lower my voice while waiting there.
There is a Starbucks around the corner. The subway was around three blocks which was perfect for zipping up to the Metropolitan and the Frick.
I personally prefer more luxury and space but have absolutely no complaints considering the excellent price and accommodating staff.

name: Gild Hall - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Relaxed Weekend Get-Away”
text: My fiancee and I recently attended a Friday wedding on Long Island and decided to relax in the city for the weekend. After looking around, we were able to secure a relatively affordable (by Manhattan standards) night at Gild Hall through JetSetter. We were very impressed by the design of the hotel and the comfort of our room. Usually we stay in Midtown, but this turned out to be a great place to stay. We were able to walk across the Brooklyn Bridge for breakfast and with a number of subway lines in the vicinity, you can easily get uptown to where you want to go. I would definitely think about staying here the next time I'm in Manhattan.

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “great hotel”
text: perfect location.good rooms.i stayed in this hotel in all the times i've been to NYC

name: Hilton New York
title: “Standard very busy hotel”
text:
Stayed at the hilton new york for one week. The hotel is a standard hotel and incredibly busy with just a multitude of people milling about in the lobby. Having said that rooms are comfortable and quiet. The decor is in need of updating and you can be left waiting for a long time for a lift.
It is fine to stay here if you get a good rate and want a good base from which to explore New York. Central park is a few blocks away and if you are in a high room, you get some good views of NYC.
The staff are all very helpful apart from the receptionist who checked us in.

name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York
title: “Perfect Experience!”
text: I picked this hotel due to location and price. Was worried because Thanksgiving week is busy in NYC and thought I'd probably be disappointed. Not so! The staff was immediately warm and friendly upon arrival. I was laughing with the hotel receptionist/reservationist within 30 seconds. Our concierge a.k.a. Laughing Cat, was Houdini. He pulled so many rabbits out of his hat to make our stay superb. The room was clean, the cleaning staff was accommodating, the view of the Empire State Building from our room was amazing. The bar downstairs was convenient on a rainy evening. Lots of good restaurants nearby. A 5 minute walk to Grand Central Station. I simply could not ask for anything more. I would definitely stay here again. I was not made to feel like another tourist...I was made to feel like family. Amen.

name: Pod 51
title: “Clean, no frills hotel but be careful with request for taxi”
text:
The good:
Fairly central and close to subway
Clean room, towels changed without request for tips
No frills value for money... For NYC anyway
High speed wi fi
The not so good:
Poor service at reception, pretty rude and abrupt staff - this could however be part of the 'New York' culture?
We stayed in a double ensuite room and it was tiny, my husband and I took turns to open our luggage
Temperature control doesn't work, it was either freezing or extremely hot
We asked for a taxi to the airport at end of stay and was given a limousine! Now you'd think this is good coz it was thet same price (USD 50 flat rate to airport) but limos are much slower than taxis as they cannot weave in traffic and had to take longer routes. We almost missed our flight!!!
Overall I would still recommend this hotel but just don't expect great service.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Great location..middle of everything”
text:
First time in NY, this is where you want to stay!!! Broadway shows everywhere, great restaurants nearby, train stations closeby and supermarket downstairs. Room was tiny, clean, luckily for air-conditioning. We were placed near the lifts, got pretty annoying, you can hear it move up and down...but got over it. Oh yes, beware of the mini-bar. They didnt tell us there were sensor pads, once you take something out of the fridge it automatically goes on to your bill. We called to tell them we will placing the milk in and taking the fiji bottle out. They were fine with this.
I wouldnt go back next time, ill stay at W. Apparently, big rooms and modern.

name: Gild Hall - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Gild Hall from 21st Nov. to 25th Nov. 2008 to celebrate my wife's birthday.
We found the hotel to be stylish, comfortable and would not hesitate in recommending it.
We loved the hotels boutique style and ambiance.
The staff were extremely friendly and helpful. We arrived early prior to our room being ready. However this wasn't a problem and they stored our bags securely to allow us a couple of hours to explore the immediate area.
The Gild Hall is located in the Financial District and is only about a 5-10min walk from Wall Street, Ground Zero, Clinton Castle (the launch for the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island), Battery Park and the Brooklyn Bridge. 
There are plenty of subway stations nearby and Time Square is only about a 10 min ride. We found the location to be perfect, the financial district is more sedate (if New York is ever sedate), than Time Square etc, so this allowed us the best of both worlds.
In my opinion the rooms at the Gild Hall were clean, stylish and the large bed was extremely comfortable. Perfect after a long day of sight seeing. We really could not fault the standards. My only slight criticism would be the noisy air conditioning system however once I worked out how to turn it off this was no longer a problem (we were there in November).
Overall we found the hotels standards and location to be perfect. I would definitely stay here again and would not hesitate in recommending the Gild Hall to other travellers.

name: City Club Hotel
title: “Nice room. Weak service.”
text:
We stayed at the City Club Hotel for a four night vacation over the long weekend. I am an experienced traveller, having been around the world for business and pleasure staying in a variety of accomodations (this was my 3rd stay in NYC). The purpose of our trip was a vacation, and for that the hotel's location was ideal, although 44th and 5/6th proved to be a mighty busy intersection. FYI - The street in front of the hotel is the marshalling area for parades on 5th ave.
The check-in at the hotel was uneventful and efficient, as it should be. We were checked into the 2nd floor, 202, which was facing the street (more on that later). The stairs were inconveniently located and rather creepy, so we used the elevators (no problems there).
The king room was large, clean, and just really nice in general, with a really huge plasma TV on the wall (no mirror-setup that other reviews have complained about). It really is a comfortable room. The king mattress was sub-par compared to similar class hotels that I have stayed at. Specifically, the mattress felt old, and the bedding had a distinct, albeit faint, odour of curry (nice on my dinner-plate, not so nice in my bed). The bathroom was perfect, except for a door that would not close. The scuffing on the floor was evidence that this was not a new problem, and indicative of a poor maintanence budget in the hotel (or simply a lack of caring)? The shower curtain was clear plastic, for those of you who like to view yourself in the wall-sized mirror while you shower. Some positive features - free wireless internet (speed was best I've seen for a hotel), and the housekeeping was excellent.
Overall noise levels at night were indeed quite high. The street noise was beyond tolerable levels on Thursday night, as the windows/walls had very little soundproofing capability. I live in a busy city street myself, and am quite accostomed to sleeping with sirens, car honking, etc., but this was quite bad. Everything from the Friday morning garbage pick-up, to the taxi honking. A visitor from the midwest suburbs would probably remain sleepless. A city dweller would not care so much.
The desk staff were useless (not to be confused with the very helpful doormen). Keep in mind that we have high expectations for a hotel on this level. Plain and simple the skillsets they displayed are not on par with either the room price, the claims put forth by the hotel, or the previous reviews on this website (fakes?). First test: I called the day before our arrival to make a simple request that flowers be in our room for our arrival and cost added to my bill. "Jonathan" assured me this was a piece of cake, and would be taken care of. Strike one - no flowers, no apologies, no nothing. Next, we attempted to procure some advice from the desk on nightlife options. Wow, they looked like we asked them for directions to Mars. They were lame, and unprepared for standard service requests throughout the stay. Strike two and three. Bottom line - this hotel desperately needs a concierge. Or retraining for exisiting staff.
I think it's only pretending to be a full service hotel. They've made their money, and now it's not worth their effort to maintain, because people like me keep showing up and giving them money. At check-out, the staff did not even ask us if we had any comments, so it's clear that they are not interested in pleasing their customers. That said, the room was great and the location was terrific. So if you are willing to pay the money and get zero from the staff, or maybe you are a business traveller, then you might give this a 5 star rating.

name: City Club Hotel
title: “Problem with Booking Online”
text: We booked a stay at the City Club for mid-July 2006. We booked the reservation on the hotel's website and thought we booked a queen-sized room. When we arrived, and despite the email confirmation I received and had with me, the hotel informed us that the only available room was a petite room, which was a full bed in a room that would have been better as a janitor's closet because it was so small. Although the bathroom was lovely, my husband and I barely fit in the room together. The TV was not a flat screen, but rather a 19 inch regular old TV. What a disappointment. We were told that the hotel's computerized booking system erred and resulted in us booking the wrong room. To his credit, the hotel manager tried to find us a room at another nearby hotel, but apparently they were sold out as well. The manager then discounted our rate, gave us a bottle of wine and free breakfast for the two mornings of our stay. The only reason I would stay here again is that the manager kept in email contact with me (I preferred email -- he offered to call instead) regarding our room and was quite helpful. The room, however, was so small and the bed so uncomfortable, that next time, rather than take the chance of this type of error happening again, I'd probably stay at the sort of big hotel I was trying to avoid in the first place.

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “Location, Location, Location”
text:
Spent 3 nights at the Carlton for my wifes 30th Birthday. Apon arrival was greeted and told that our room was ready , great news as we arrived in the morning and had only expected to drop off luggage.
Room was small but clean and view from window was excellent. Clear view of the Empire State Building.
After quick shower we walked (4 blocks!!) to the ESB and then onto Times Square etc.
As we were only staying for a short while we didn't spend too much time at hotel but staff couldn't have been more helpful. The lobby is massive and if you want a quiet 5 mins take a seat and relax.
Idea for travellers on a budget, get coffee etc from Dunkin Donuts on the corner before starting your day sightseeing.
Final joy was when asking for taxi back to airport, they sorted a limo transfer!! All this cheaper that preset taxi fare $45 from airport.
Would book again for next stay, planning to do so later in the year.

name: W New York - Union Square
title: “a perfect place from where to take a bite from the big apple”
text: My partner and I had an opportunity to visit NYC for a weekend of play and leisure and the W Union Square was a perfect place for us. From the moment we stepped up to the Welcome Desk, Temara greeted with a sense of professional playfulness that is signature to the brand. Our room was bright and beautifully appointed. The bar was fun, concierge super helpful, and room service fantastic. I can't wait to return!

name: Renaissance New York Hotel 57
title: “Location, location, location”
text: This hotel is in the heart of New York, it’s a fantastic location. The rooms are small but modern and very clean. There is a great bar here too to start your evening off. Once you step out of the hotel entrance you are straight in to the hustle and bustle of the NY sidewalk. I spent 2 nights here and found the staff friendly. It was a little pricey but nevertheless this is where I will stay on my next trip to NY. I recommend highly… enjoy

name: Equity Point New York @ Times Square
title: “Excelente ubicacion, precio y limpio”
text:
Concuerdo con Stefan, las habitaciones son chicas, pero tienen lo necesario y muy limpio.
En lo personal la ubicacion fue lo que mas nos gusto, cerca de Central de transporte y el metro, nos desplazabamos facilmente, Times Square, tiendas abiertas 24 horas, restaurant y teatros.
El desayuno es americano, sencillo pero rico, cafe, zumo y panecillos.
Fue nuestra primera visita a New York y la experiencia estuvo excelente, volveriamos a hospedarnos en el Hotel 41.

name: 6 Columbus - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Excellent location and good value for money”
text: The location was excellent and we really loved our room. Good quality linen, fairly new bathroom and hardwood floors were the best. It was also nice to see a little bit of sky from our window... The staff was really friendly and they did their best to help us with all of our needs. We would like to stay here again.

name: Radisson Martinique on Broadway
title: “buono”
text:
situato in una location straordinaria, a due passi da times square, è l'albergo ideale per soggiornare qualche giorno nella Grande Mela.
La camera che ho avuto modo di provare era discretamente grande, con due letti queen size.
la struttura in cui è sito l'hotel è molto bella e ospita un bistro che offre una buona qualità, sia a pranzo che a cena.
consigliato.

name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York
title: “Good place to stay few days”
text:
I stayed there three days, and it was very ok. The team is very VERY nice, I insist onthis point because it's the better point of this hotel is the employees. The room was very big, but this could be more clean.
There is wifi only in the lobby, this is ok, but this could be more useful if there was more places to sit.

name: Hilton New York
title: “good location”
text:
The Hilton New York is in walking distance to Central Park, Theater District, Times Square and all the glam shopping you could want. We stayed on the Club level. The rooms were very nice, spacious with very comfortable beds, not your typical tiny NYC hotel rooms. Aveda bath products were provided, mini bar and black out curtains. The walls are however paper thin. They have breakfast and happy hour every day for Club Level patrons. They also have a concierge service who can get you reservations to most places. This service is available to everyone at the hotel.
There is a ticket office who provides brokers tickets to all plays and sells tickets to attractions. Of course you pay more, but that's the way they do things in NYC. They have a nice bar and some resturaunts including starbucks. We didn't use any of these so I cannot comment on them. Of couse, summer is a very hot, touristy time to be in the city, but this is a great location, not too much street noise and very secure at nite. 
We took a taxi here from LaGuardia for around $35. It's only about 30-45 minutes to/from depending on traffic.

name: Equity Point New York @ Times Square
title: “Hotel 41 at Times Square - mitt i smeten”
text: Ett fint litet hotell mitt i smeten. Nära till allt! Fina, rena hotell rum och trevlig personal. Frukost av enklare karraktär men så är det ju ofta utomlands. Inget negativt att säga, kan bara rekommenderas. Vi åker gärna hit igen.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Buzzy Hotel”
text: What a great eplace to stay. Step out the door off the hotel and you are a short walk to anywhere. This place has a great buzz about it, it is busy so don't stay here if your looking to chill out unless you stay in your room. We had a refurbed room which was huge and had a view on Central Park.

name: Equity Point New York @ Times Square
title: “La regadera no servia bien”
text:
La regadera estaba fatal. Caia poca agua y la tuberia hacia un ruidero...
El disque desayuno que estaba incluido era un pan con mermelada y jugo de naranja de caja...
Lo único bueno es la ubicación... Y el servicio diario de la camarera...

name: Pod 51
title: “Great location, even smaller than it appears”
text:
Positives- right on the subway line, easy walk to Times Sq, Central Park and many shops. Too far to walk from Penn Station. Hip, cozy lobby. Very clean bathrooms.
Negatives- staff at front desk are not friendly or helpful in any way. Room are VERY small, the sink is the size of one on a airplane. I am 5'2 and the bed was almost too short for me. No shelves for top bunk? or storage . So if you are traveling with just backpack you are fine.
Phone in room did not work to reach front desk. Light fixture by bunks kept falling apart.

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “Perfect for families!”
text: We stayed at the Eastgate Tower Hotel, New York from August 18 to August 24 for 6 nights. The 2 bedroom suite was very spacious and was perfect for 6 people. The location was fine (15 minute walk into Times Square). The staff are all friendly and helpful. The maid, Joyce, was very frindly and always made the room up perfectly. The only two downsides are that the hotel is quite dated and needs decorating. Also there is no restaurant or bar so the price is a little expensive considering these amenities are not available. Otherwise perfect.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan SoHo Village
title: “A l'écart de l'agitation de Times Square”
text: Très grande compétence et gentillesse du personnel au desk (nous les avons beaucoup sollicités) Chambre confortable et spacieuse. Un seul bémol:le bruit de fond (New Yorkais)des extracteurs de climatisation.

name: Equity Point New York @ Times Square
title: “hotel in ottima posizione”
text:
L'hotel si trova in posizione centralissima.
E' a due passi da Times Square quindi in zona centralissima .
Le camere sono un po' strettine e ridotte all'essenziale , ma noi eravamo sempre in giro ...
La colazione era buona e stranamente compresa nel prezzo.
Alla reception erano sempre molto gentili e pronti a soddisfare ogni esigenza.
In sintesi un hotel da consigliare perche' comodo e pulito.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Hilton New York - Being realistic”
text:
Let me preface this review with telling you New York is like my second home. I live three hours away, but travel here one or twice a month, even more so at times, to enjoy the city - and have for years and years. I think what everyone looking for a review needs to be certain they realize is the NYC is a big place - lots of choices..if you choose a "brand name" large scale hotel (such as this Hilton) in midtown Manhattan this realistically is what you'll get:
(1) Accessible location - Times Square, 5th Ave shopping, Rockefeller Center, multiple subway stations (53rd - C, E and B, Q, N, R) within a block (1, 3, 9) lines a block further. Theatre District and Central Park within a few blocks. Starbucks on every block and shopping on Madison Ave within a few more. Radio City across the street.
(2) Clean, updated rooms of decent size for NYC - decent beds, dressers and good size closet space and a locked mini-bar. Bathrooms are a bit small, but clean, marble counters, good shower heads and pressure, very adequate and updated. Large mirrors in bath and full length mirrors on the closet doors. Towels are fluffy. Rooms range from standard fair to suites - so you have options. Although truth be said (from this Hilton honors member) the only time a suite is worth the money is for a long stay or if using for business purposes and the "executive floors" are never really worth the extra. Midtown location and demand at this convention type hotel make it fairly expensive - but remember it's NYC - it's the demand and the location. 
(3) There are several hotel bars and several restaurants - all convenient - but remember it's NYC....meaning average (if that) food, very expensive for quality and drinks are expensive. Even an import beer is $9.00 - but again....follow the mantra <<smile>> it's NYC! If you are going to spend $$ this city has a place for every palatte....street food...local places... (even hit the Astro one block north for a variety of simple/local food - reasonable, fast for breakfast and lunches). Get out of the hotel to eat - hotel restauants are last choice - especially in this city of endless choices in thre area and much more so beyond.
(4) This Hilton is smack in midtown and hosts convention/meeting spaces - it's close to 2000 rooms - so be realistic, it's lobby will be spit-shined marble polished but as big and wide as an airport terminal; and it will have (at times) just as many people...which means long lines for everything...charging for luggage storage ($3.50 per) and lots and lots of service employees that are not trained to act as ambassadors to the city. Again...it's NYC - I have stayed here numerous times, you do get some helpful people and smiling staff and then you just get those that go about their jobs with no extra or any effort to the public.
I travel alot and have stayed at many different hotels in the city - if you want more personalized service and interaction - there are hundreds of boutique or smaller hotels in this city. This Hilton is not one of them - just be realistic! Use the zip check in stations - there are multiple ones in the lobby; it's a good alternative to those long lines. Lower floors get you less wait time on elevators, make a request - and if not - then again, it's a very large, crowded hotel - waiting goes with the territory.
(5) The good part of such a large, centrally located hotel such as this? Lots and lots of taxis at your disposal under a covered area and even better - within a block or two you can access the majority of subway lines to get anywhere in this city. It's a busy hotel - so it's populated, still, walking to and from the hotel (at most times) it is not a desolate (at night) - so that's plus. 
Overall, if you are looking for a great midtown location to many things (Central Park/shopping/theatre/tourist attractions/transportation) and don't mind being faceless - just want a clean, spacious room to sleep and shower in and go about your time seeing the city - this is not a bad choice. 
In all fairness - I have asked for extra towels and they were delivered in adequate time. I have asked the conceirge for assistance in a difficult reservation and got good service. I have had the door opened for me frequently from the door staff, and had my stored luggage mistagged, but we found it and even gave him a tip (which I'm sure he didn't expect) but then he proceded to carry my bags out front for me (which is not part of his job). 
So set your expectations realistically, know what you really got when you choose, and this Hilton most of the time will not disappoint.

name: City Club Hotel
title: “Hotell nära Times Square”
text:
Jättebra läge om man vill vara i närheten av Times Square, men ändå ha ett lugnt boende. Luftkonditioneringen låter väldigt mycket, men från gatan och omgivningen hörs inte ett knyst.
Trevligt med tidning på morgonen och kakor på kvällen. Enkelrummen är mycket små, så det finns inte plats för något skrivbord, soffa eller fåtölj. Rummet rymmer endast sängen som å andra sidan är väldigt skön.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Cant fault this Hotel at all”
text: Stayed at the Novotel, New York for a 5 night break for my birthday and couldn’t have chosen a better hotel. The location of the hotel is excellent for Times Square/Broadway. On arrival we were early to check in (check in is 3.00p.m. check out is 12 noon). Reception was extremely friendly and called a bellboy to hold our cases. My husband had asked for a high room and we got upgraded to the 28th floor (foc) with great views of Hudson River. The room was clean and the king size bed comfortable. Room has a TV, iron and ironing board, Minibar which is full and will charge your room direct via reception if anything is removed. If you want to use the fridge for your own use then ask at reception for the items to be removed. The bathroom (with bath) and shower was well equipped with shower gel, shampoo, shower cap, soap and a hairdryer. Fresh towels were left daily. Only downside to the bathroom was the mould around the bath. Cant comment on the food as always ate out but did bring a pizza back to the room one night which was perfectly acceptable by the hotel. We did use the bar where the staff was again very friendly. (Drinks very expensive though). We will definitely be going back to New York and will definitely consider the Novotel again.

name: JW Marriott Essex House New York
title: “Poor service”
text: The staff at the reception desk was very unfriendly and unprofessional. We had booked a room with a kingsize bed, but they did not have any when we checked in. In fact they did not have a room at all because the guest in "our" room had extended their stay. That was normal business for them. It took 6 hours and 3 receptionist incompetence before we got a tiny dated room. The only thing this hotel has is a view to central park and a nice reception hall. The housekeeping forgot something every day-towels etc etc. The indoorclimate was very poor. We were there to celebrate my husbands birthday so the dissappointment was huge!! Would never stay here again.

name: Soho House New York
title: “Soho average-house”
text:
We stayed at Soho house earlier this year and i must say that for the price i was extremely disappointed. Especially with the room that we had on the library level - it was extremely small and cramped, definitely not what I was expecting from a Soho House. 
The staff is very helpful and did recommend some great places to eat out, they were also sure to check we were members each time we entered the premises.
Breakfast is average, nothing special on that side. Sleep quality - make sure you bring yourself some ear plugs because you can hear people walking in and out of the elevators all night and helping down the corridor.
I wouldn't stay in this Soho house again, it would be good to obtain membership if we lived in nyc for a few reasons, its really nothing special though.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott New York Manhattan / Times Square
title: “Fairfield Inn, vicino Penn Station.”
text: Personale gentile, pulizia buona, Internet gratis, colazione continentale gratis, vicino Penn Station. Comodissimo alla stazione autobus (giusto dietro l'angolo) per aereoporto JFK. Bus ogni mezz'ora, costa meno dello shuttle. Il quartiere non è il massimo, comunque OK.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “overrated, overpriced”
text:
I've stayed at the hotel as well as attended luncheons and meetings here. 
Room:
- I got a particularly small room and it wasn't the most comfortable. Remarkably, my friend's room, at the same rate, was about 2x as big and more luxurious. Hello
- The hotel has a long, storied history and it's reflected in the decor and service. 
- The food served at the luncheons is probably the best i've ever had at any luncheon. 
- Otherwise, a very staid hotel where the older crowd definitely hangs out. I'm probably one of the youngest people roaming around

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “LOVED IT”
text: We went with our school, it was an amazing hotel and very close to the Empire State Building. The rooms were massive and a maid came in once a day to clean the rooms. The veiws from the rooms were mainly building but what do you want! your in new york after all. I am deffiantly going back with the school next year!!!!!!

name: Hampton Inn 35th St. Empire State Building
title: “As basic as hotels can come... and beware of the noise coming from the hallways”
text:
This hotel is really the bare bones minimum when it comes to in-room amenities. The bed is a decent size but it leaves almost no space for anything else. When I arrived in the room it smelled moldy so I needed to air out the room for over an hour before being tolerable. Also, the biggest problem with the room is that since the rooms are jampacked together, the door does not reduce outside noises. I was awoken at 8AM when the staff or other tenants were roaming the hallways or going in and out of rooms. Also, the doors basically slam shut after being opened so I was constantly hearing the doors opening and closing. 
The wifi and complimentary breakfast is nice but doesn't justify the disturbance. The only benefit to staying in this hotel is its relatively lower price and great location. There are several hotel choices nearby and I would probably stay elsewhere .............

name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York
title: “Very Pleased! Great Staff, Great Suite, Great Location!”
text:
We are a well-traveled couple in our early 30's and were looking to enjoy the city for our 5th anniversary along with a final celebration before our first baby arrives in September. I do a lot of research for our vacations - typically looking for hidden gems or great value deals on premium places. I also own a vacation rental company for the community where our beach house is located so I have a lot of experience with all aspects of guest management. We have high expectations for attention to detail and customer service and could not have been more impressed.
In honor of our anniversary and upcoming baby, we received a complementary room upgrade. The suite was very clean, spacious with walk in closet and decorated with stylish yet comfortable decor (see pictures). We also had a terrace balcony with a nice view of the Chrysler building. The suite was stocked with all the amenities. We felt completely safe and the hotel is perfectly located for walking (or quick cab) to the major attractions... just a few blocks to shopping on 5th Ave, Time Square, The Empire St Buiding, etc. It is also ideally located with regard to ease of access for getting into and out of the city to make travel days less stressful.
The staff, including but not limited to Blanca and Jennifer, are top notch and a great asset! They even added a surprising personal touch by sending a gift package to congratulate us on our upcoming baby. They were very professional, warm and welcoming while handling the reservation and check-in process. Our only regret is that we could not stay longer but can hopefully return again sometime soon!

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Against all odds....”
text: I was in NY for a 4-day stay last week, for my son's 18th birthday and had picked the Millenium as it has great views of the financial district and Ground Zero and had always given great service when I stayed there in the 90's - and I'm really pleased to say it hasn't changed. We arrived on the Friday after Sandy and was relieved to see the hotel lights on and the doors open. The staff coped brilliantly with manual check-in and explained well that there was no hot water, phone etc. but we were just happy to have a bed! Hot water was ready for the morning and New York didn't disappoint -even after a very difficult week. Finding us cabs, booking restaurants and generally staying positive helped to cement my view that the service at the Millenium is efficient, polite and what you would expect from a hotel of this standard. Well done all.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Fabulous location”
text:
Stayed three night at the New York Hilton on 6th Avenue. This was my second visit to the Hotel having visited five years earlier.
The hotel is in a fabulous spot for sightseeing and for getting around New York. It is close to Times Square and Broadway and all the main attractions.
The hotel represents excellent value for money. The rooms are spacious, very clean and of a high standard. The restaurant serves wonderful breakfasts and overall the service was of a very high standard.
I would highly recommend this hotel for familes as well as couples.

name: West 57th Street by Hilton Club
title: “Great Location and Nice Rooms”
text: We were lucky enough to book our studio room using our timeshare points within 40 days! This place is very close to Central Park and tons of restaurants and right next door to Carnegie Hall. The room was very modern and nice looking and the beds very comfortable and clean. There was quite a bit of room for a studio size. We overlooked Steinway Piano's and we had a great view of the streets and could watch all of the taxis in the morning. I would love to stay here again, but I think we got lucky having an opening to be able to use our points. The staff was very friendly, the only bad thing was the elevator was really slow.

name: Broadway Plaza Hotel
title: “Good Value Hotel”
text: Good location. The service staff were helpful and friendly. Room really too small for 2 double sized twin beds, making it difficult to move around. Otherwise clean and comfortable, with large bathroom..

name: Algonquin Hotel Times Square, Autograph Collection
title: “A step down for Marriott”
text: Just completed a weekend stay at the Algonquin. I've stay at over 1800 nights at various Marriott properties (and over 5000 nights at other hotels from the Burj to Days Inns). The Algonquin is just not a property that measures up to its historic reputation. The hotel just completed a major reinovation - I wonder what it was like before hand! Our room's bathroom was less than 30 sq feet (and I am being very generous), the floors creeked, and the view was of nothing except a chap working on a Saturday morning at 9 AM doing some maintenance work (no notice by the hotel). The noise from the hallway was continual (lousy sound proofing). The elevators are small and very slow, a coke and ice tea were $18 in the lounge (OK, it's NY). It's web-site said that valet parking was $45 - it was $55. It took over 30 minutes to get the car on a Sunday morning when there was only one other party waiting for a car. Now on the push side, there was free coffee on the second floor (although no free newspapers) and the staff were pleasant (although not polished). As someone points out, the location is great. That said, having stayed at over 30 hotels in the city, I would highly recommend the Sofitel about 100 feet from the Algonquin. BTW, most of my reviews tend to be positive - ergo, my review herein purpose is two fold: to give a heads up to seasoned travelers and to get someone from Marriott to spend some time with the folks at the hotel and get it to live up to Marriott's and the historic standards this hotel deserves.

name: World Center Hotel
title: “HOUSE KEEPING STEALS!!!!!!”
text: Items were missing from the room when we left and the hotel charged our credit card! We were adamant that it wasn't us and it was probably the staff. They charged our card $60 and WOULD NOT REMOVE IT! Instead, they said the best they could do was charge our card $30. If we didn't take anything, WHY SHOULD WE PAY AT ALL? I could get over the construction and the poor attitude of the staff, but that was the final straw. We ordering takeout and the food sat downstairs for an hour and half! We called the store and they said they delivered it a long time ago and someone either took it or ate it. I HATED IT HERE! NEVER AGAIN!

name: Broadway Plaza Hotel
title: “great place”
text: I just stayed at this hotel with my two teenagers and their two friends, we got a Junior Suite which came with two queens beds and a pullout coach. this has to be the biggest room I've ever stayed at in NYC. I've stayed at several different hotels, where I paid more and always got very very small rooms,. this was the best as far as room size goes. The bed was comfy, shower and bathroom appeared new. TV worked good. I got free internet even though they charged for internet. Plenty of open access around there. Hotel location was great, too. I parked for $25 on the next block - they give you a special rate because of the hotel. There was no restaurant but did offer continental breakfast on the 4th floor. It was ok, got coffee and donuts, but not much to choice from. For the price, location and size of room, this was a GREAT deal. I will be back!

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “The location is excellent! The management and customer service are very disappointing!”
text:
The location is excellent! That’s the only advantage of this hotel. The check-in staff is very cold and there is no greeting. 
I want to give an advice to everyone: don’t buy their breakfast package. I paid $10 for the breakfast for each day. When I checked in, the staff gave me coupons (blue-colored) for free continental breakfast in a nearby restaurant Tick Tock Dinner. When I used the coupon in the morning, I just could not believe my eyes. The breakfast only includes one glass of juice, one cup of coffee, and two very small pieces of toast. It’s hardly enough for my three-year old son. The second morning I talked to the front desk staff. The guy was very rude. So I talked to the manager. She said she needs 30 minutes to find out what went wrong. I just don’t want to waste my time to wait for half an hour for this. I requested a refund. But she refused. Later she offered to give me a different coupon (red-colored) for American breakfast-a much better one. Now I realized that the check-in staff tricked me. She should have given me the red coupons. So the management and customer service are very disappointing! I just want to remind everyone: if you pay for the breakfast, DO ask for the red coupon.

name: Comfort Inn Manhattan
title: “just ok for sleeping”
text:
The room was very small and in front of the window was a scaffolding
The service at the reception was sometimes very unfriendly
The price was good for just having a bed to sleep in the middle of Manhattan

name: West 57th Street by Hilton Club
title: “Great "just the two of us" getaway.”
text:
My husband and I got away for three days, leaving our 3 kids behind. We try to do this once a year. This was a great place to stay. We are Hilton owners and got a call to try this hotel. We knew it meant taking 3 hrs of our day to listen to a presentation, but hey, it was a deal we couldn't pass. 
They were a little persistent, though not too pushy with the presentation. We were VERY tempted, but decided to pass. It's a great deal to own a piece of the Big Apple, but at our age and with kids still in school, it's not the right time, plus not a good family hotel... would need two rooms.
We live in the country and love to visit the city. The location was great. We walked to Central Park, Starbucks, restaurants, MoMA. We also took the subway to go to the SkyLine and Eataly. We enjoyed both very much. 
Although there are many restaurant choices you can walk to or take a taxi ride to, it would be nice to have one on site. That's the only reason I gave it 4 stars vs 5. 
We stayed in the studio... comfortable, spacious for a city room, clean, no complaints. I didn't include pictures because they'd look just like the ones already taken by others.
Staff was very helpful, courteous, professional... having a doorman was nice! felt spoiled!
If we have the opportunity to stay there again, we will definitely do so!

name: W New York - Union Square
title: “As far as I know, the BEST of all...”
text:
I have stayed at Westin Essexhouse Parkview room and Westin Times Square Executive room... W Union Square is much better than these two hotels. The staff is very kind and very professional and very helpful.
The location is just great. The room is incredibly large and clean and modern. The bed and bathroom are much higher than NY standards.
I have no idea why people complain. But there's one thing to be aware of. People who hate dogs shouldn't stay. I'm sure you'll see it more than once at your stay. Except that, I will go back to this hotel for sure.

name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York
title: “Empire State Building”
text: Nous étions au 14e sur cour idéal pour le calme (anecdote : il n'y a pas de 13e !). Une vue imprenable sur l'Empire State Building dont le haut changeait de couleur le soir. Accueil sympathique. Grande chambre très propre avec 2 lits king size. On a coupé la ventilation qui faisait un bruit pas possible. Salle de bain petite manquant de finition. Très bien situé pour rayonner à pied, et près de Grand Central pour accès au métro. Très central. Hôtel complètement non fumeur. Pour le ptit déj, le Café Metro sur Lexington entre la 40th et la 41th à 2 blocs est super accueillant. Pour le soir, on a trouvé un Bistro Market pas cher et plutôt bon sur Park Avenue entre la 41th et la 42th juste à côté de Grand Central. Bon séjour !

name: West 57th Street by Hilton Club
title: “Outstanding location”
text: Nice place, modernistic decor, nice view from high floors, wood floors, outstanding staff that make you feel welcome. The location is convenient to everything in midtown like Rockefeller Center, Fith Ave, Times Square, and subway station.

name: West 57th Street by Hilton Club
title: “Fantastic rooms, fantastic location”
text:
Being claustraphobic when it comes to small hotel rooms, I was pe-warned how tiny New York accommodation was. I made it my mission to find spacious accomodation at an affordable price as we were staying in New York for 2 weeks. I am glad to say I more than found it. We stayed in room 1001 which was a King 1 bedroom suite and it was everything I hoped it would be. Spacious, comfortable, quiet, clean, great bed and fantastic service from all the staff. Thank you for making our stay so enjoyable. If we ever return to New York we are staying at this hotel.
The only thing this hotel didn't have was a bar and restuarant but that really doesn't matter when you've got 100's to chose from at your doorstep.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Lovely experience”
text: We booked this hotel through Travelzoo, getting a great deal on a suite. I requested as high up as possible and was given a room on the top 40th floor with great river and city views. The room had fridge with water and cokes and drinks machine for tea/coffee making, extras availble via the maid service. The room and sitting room were warm, clean, pleasently furnished and comfortable, a real sanctuary for the hustle and bustle of the city. The staff in the hotel, diner and bar were friendly, polite and helpful, throughly enjoyed my stay and would recommend booking.

name: Equity Point New York @ Times Square
title: “Gutes Hotel direkt am Times Square”
text: Lage: direkt am Times Square. Wenn man "mitten drin" zu einem fairen Preis unterkommen möchte dann führt hier kein Weg dran vorbei. Das Hotel ist in einem Top-Zustand und verfügt auch über eine sehr nette Bar. Der Service ist ebenfalls hervorragend und entspricht mindesten der Hotelkategorie. Jedoch: Manche Zimmer sind sehr, sehr klein. Wenn man nur 2-3 Tage eine Übernachtungsmögllichkeit sucht, ist dieses Hotel eine richtig gute Alternative.

name: W New York - Union Square
title: “Delightful!”
text: This was the most enjoyable hotel stay I have experienced in a very long time! The staff was delightful, even playful. They couldn't have been nicer or more accomodating. After checking in, we stumbled into the bar/restaurant connected to the hotel, Olives. There we were surprised with one of the most enjoyable and delicious meals we have ever had! We stayed in one of the "Mega" rooms. It was very spacious and clean. The hotel shower is the best shower in NYC! Bliss Spa products are the bath products offered. Having stayed in a "boutique" hotel before, I wasn't sure I wanted to try one again. The W at Union Square shattered all of those myths for me. The W didn't disappoint.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Great location within financial district”
text: I stayed in Millenium Hilton for 6 nights while I was in NYC for a business trip. There are subway stations ranging from 0 to 2 mins walk from the hotel. Nonetheless you can easily walk to Wall St (10mins), South St (10mins) and Staten Island Ferry Terminal (20mins). There's also a free Downtown Alliance Shuttle Bus that plies Downtown Manhattan. Lastly, the hotel is also steps away from Century 21 shopping centre and the 9/11 Memorial.

name: Pod 39
title: “Well run. Clean. Efficient Budget hotel”
text: This is a great value hotel in NYC. If you want an efficient, no frills place to just sleep and shower, you can't go wrong for the money. It is at a great location, 3 blocks from Grand Central Station, on 39th and Lexington. Staff was professional and easy to deal with. Rooms were spotless. Great casual rooftop bar. Wifi in the rooms were a bonus as well as TVs. Showers had fabulous pressure! Beds very comfortable. Only slight negative was the size of the room--we were two guys sharing a bunk bed room and even for us low maintenance types it was pretty tight--imagine a cruise ship cabin. If you are two higher maintenance girls I would not recommend it--two people really can't get ready at the same time! But overall worth the money for me.

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “Room rate very reasonable, excellent location, staff are friendly, rooms clean”
text: Hotel is very conveniently located. Very reasonable rate/clean . Staff friendly.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “over priced and disappointing!”
text: This hotel is showing its age. It has lost the glamor of yesteryear. Rooms (and bathrooms) need a major renovation. Furniture is old and the drapes outdated. The price of the room is expensive and the room service overpriced. Other than its great location in NYC and historic lobby this hotel is totally over-rated.

name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York
title: “ST. Giles NY liegt zentral und gut - wir waren sehr zufrieden”
text:
Waren im März 2011 im St. Giles in NY und waren sehr zufrieden. Lage ist sehr gut - um die Ecke gibt es Scotty´s Diner - sehr zu empfehlen und auf der Ecke gegenüber einen Laden wo es leckere Sandwiches und Bagel gibt.
Die Zimmer waren geräumig und sauber - der Service sehr nett und hilfsbereit. Konnten sogar von unserem Fenster das Empire State Building sehen.
Fazit - wir kommen bestimmt wieder - sehr empfehlenswert.

name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York
title: “Redelijk hotel maar onpersoonlijk”
text:
Hotel met grote kamers, zeker voor New York. Wij waren er eind maart en verbleven 7 nachten in The Court. Buiten koud, binnen ontzettend warm. Airco deed het wel, maar maakte een hoop lawaai. Ramen konden niet open. Zou overigens ook geen optie zijn, want de kamer lag aan de Lexington Avenue met veel geluid van de weg. Goede bedden en prima douche.
Geen goede betaalbare ontbijtfaciliteiten in hotel, in de buurt kan je wel goed op z'n Amerikaans ontbijten.
Geen wifi, maar ook geen computers voor de hotelgasten. Vonden wij een gemis. Wel internetgebruik mogelijk tegen betaling (duur).
Er is wel een bar in het hotel (de Lex-bar) maar het is er erg lawaaiig/ veel Amerikanen. Een goede gastenruimte/ gezellige lobby ontbreekt. Het is echt een hotel om alleen te slapen.
Hotel ligt in een zakenbuurt waardoor er 's avonds minder valt te beleven in de directe nabijheid van het hotel. Is voor ons een minpunt.
Je loopt wel heel gemakkelijk naar Grand Central om de metro te pakken naar andere buurten. Is ook 's avonds prima te doen. Je zit ook dicht bij het Empire State Building. Lopen naar Times Square is ook te doen, maar voor ons niet belangrijk (3e keer in New York). Het is maar net wat je wil.
St. Giles heeft overigens 2 hotels naast elkaar. Op basis van het lezen van de waarderingen en de prijs hebben wij gekozen voor The Court. De ander lijkt ons achteraf toch beter en leuker. De indruk van de lobby met caf'e/restaurant maakte op ons een meer gastvrije indruk. I.t.t. de The Court ligt dit hotel niet op de straathoek met Lexington, waardoor wij vermoeden dat de kamers ook rustiger zijn.

name: Pod 51
title: “I guess it's good for New York”
text:
I'm not very familiar with New York, so I guess it was a little shocking to walk in and see how small everything was. But everything was laid out nicely and took advantage of the small space. The bathroom is absolutely tiny; almost like an airplane bathroom. You have to squeeze by the toilet to get to the shower. 
On the plus side, the service was quite good. I ended up very sick when I was there, and my sister was able to call the concierge and he went and got me some things from Walgreens I needed. That was really above and beyond. 
One day when I was sick, I was watching TV at what I thought was a low volume, but a woman next door knocked on my door to tell me that she could hear every word through her wall and would I mind turning it down. I felt awful about that. But for me, it was a quiet place. I was on the 9th floor, and didn't hear much at all. You hear the occasional honking outside of taxis and street stuff, but not compared to what I was expecting. 
One other nice thing is that they have free wi-fi in the rooms, although it was hit and miss sometimes.

name: Room Mate Grace
title: “No recomendable”
text: Estuvimos en este hotel de luna de miel. Muy buena ubicacion, pero el hotel no nos gusto nada. Entrada sombria, habitacion pequeña pero no hace falta mas, moqueta literalmente pestosa, sabanas sucias y con boquetes, e incluso un gusano en la primera habitacion que nos dieron, que era la 407, no dejeis que os la den, porque no funciona el aire y tienen una maquina superruidosa. La piscina se supone que era muy cool, se puede tomar alli mismo una copa, pero daba sensacion de lena de borrachos meandose. Su dueño debe de tener enchufazo porque lo he visto en la tele muchas veces y tenia una pinta maravillosa. No se que habitacion enseñaran, la nuestra desde luego no... aconsejable.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Great staff, great views, and some good nights sleep 5-8 July”
text:
We were most impressed with the breathtaking views over the 9/11 memorial sight and Hudson river from our room on the 45th floor. The view from the picture window by the lift (elevator) on the other side of the building were also impressive over to the Brooklyn bridge. The staff were always helpful and good with advice (where to eat, where convenience stores are ect). I was a little concerned about being further away from where the action tends to be (in and around Times Square) but needn't have been concerned. I bought a week's pass for the Subway for $29 and there was a station right be the hotel so it was no big deal.
The bed was really very comfortable (unless it was just that I was so exhausted after fun-filled days in NYC)! The room was well equipped and a decent size.
My only criticism really is the lack of free wifi. In this day and age you expect it to be free in the lobby at the very least (not $15 a day)! If McDonald's can give you free wifi when you're only spending a $1 on a drink, I think the Millenium Hilton can stretch for their guests! It's a little thing but you don't realise when you're away from home how much you rely on it. To have been able to Skype my husband and kids from the comfort of the hotel would've made for a flawless review of the Millenium Hilton... oh except I just remembered that the pool was freezing too!

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Stay away!!”
text: Ok, I have stayed here twice and both times it was dirty, dirty, dirty. Ugh. Yes, the lobby and the restaurants are very GOOD. Even the front desk and management are tops. One of the best concierge floors anywhere with great service and food. Nice fitness center. Great location but the rooms were just old and I dreaded returning to sleep. There are such mixed reviews on here that I wonder if there are some areas of the hotel that are renovated and some that are not? Unfortunately I got the worst both stays.

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “Great Value for money”
text: In the heart of Manhattan, you can not get better value for money! The only quibble: Internet in the room is priced too high!

name: Pod 39
title: “Hotel neuf propre bien situé”
text:
j'ai passé 3 nuits au pod39 en septembre 2012, les chambres sont certaines petites , mais bien agencées pour un séjour entre amis, et toutes options , télé, douche wc et meme une petite vue sur l'empire state building . 
Ayant déja fait dans d'autres séjours a N.Y dans des hotels a la propreté suspecte et aux sanitaires communs, ici c'était vraiment le luxe ^^ 
A ne pas rater la terrasse sur le toit de l'hotel au 17 eme étage avec une vue imprenable sur la chrystale tower , l'empire state et tout Manhattan

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Excellent Service”
text: When we arrived at the New Yorker we were originally in a single bed room, we asked for an upgraded room because I was with my mother and we thought we had two beds. The staff was very helpful and accommodated us to a much larger room. Angel was very helpful. The rooms were clean, large and comfortable. It is large, old hotel right in the heart of midtown with a subway stop right next door it was quick access to the entire city.

name: World Center Hotel
title: “Loved the Suite”
text:
We booked World Center Hotel on Priceline's Name Your Own Price. I bid $150 and then had to pay taxes of $40. We got a standard room but upgraded for $25 to a suite since there were three of us. The suite was wonderful - plenty of closet space, two tv's, a kitchenette, and interesting views. I say that because you are overlooking the construction of the new Freedom Towers. It's definitely a little surreal to stand above the site of the Twin Towers. The drilling started at 7:30 in the morning but that wasn't an issue for us since we wanted to get up and start the day. Obviously this will be even less of a problem as the new towers are built.
We parked in a garage right around the corner for $32/day - a good price for Manhattan. Careful if you're using a navigation system - my friend punched in the address as New York, NY and it took us to Washington Street in Brooklyn instead. 
I thought the staff was very attentive and helpful. If the hallway guest closets do not have what you need they wil happily bring it to your room.
The hotel is very clean and modern. I would stay here again.

name: Algonquin Hotel Times Square, Autograph Collection
title: “Update is due”
text:
Nice old hotel in the heart of Times Square. However, at $300 plus per night, this is not the level of hotel I would expect from Marriotts Autograph collection. I was extremely disspointed. We arrived on Thursday 10 Aug, and checked out today 13 of Aug. The rooms have no hot water by 9 AM, and you are lucky if both of the lifts are working. We spent 30 minutes this morning trying to get on a lift to get our luggage to the lobby. Wine prices in the lobby are ridiculous, about 500% above standard retail for the cheapest wine.
We will probably go to the City Center hotel on our next trip. This was OK, but a dissapointment.

name: Broadway Plaza Hotel
title: “Do not stay in this hotel if you want to sleep”
text: If they put you on the 8th floor you will be sorry. The noice from the elevator is so loud that you cannot sleep .. at all! I was told to complain to the manager and when I asked to speak to him was told he is not here. Read the reviews for this place on hotels.com and you will see this same complaint over and over. This hotel obviously does not care and they just want to catch the tourist who will never return again.

name: Algonquin Hotel Times Square, Autograph Collection
title: “Not a fan”
text:
Stayed here last Saturday night. Asked for early check-in at 1pm and received that. Also asked for high floor but was placed on the 5th (out of 12). The room was small as many others have said. It was also clean and the bathroom was "cute". That's the good news. Now for the "rest of the story".
Our room was on some sort of inside "courtyard" next to the elevator shaft. We could hear the elevator coming and going all the time. The room was dismal due to the lack of natural light as the "courtyard" was just an internal shaft with a wall about 10 feet from our window. From the fire exit map on the inside of the door it looks like they have 2 rooms like this per floor. Sad.
I just want to say I am a Platinum member with Marriott and there was obviously no room upgrade. I think the only worse rooms in the building were the same room on floors 2-4. This is how they show their appreciation to their best customers.
We won't be back and history or not, one can do much better in New York. Did I mention this was paid stay of over $400 dollars?

name: West 57th Street by Hilton Club
title: “Enjoyed my stay at this beautiful luxury timeshare property”
text:
The location of this property is in the heart of midtown Manhattan and it's on the same block as Carnegie Hall. You couldn't find a more convenient location to both Central Park and the Theater District.
I checked in the morning of Friday, July 3, which was opening day. The check-in experience was very quick with so many staff members working that day. The staff were all friendly and tried their best to accommodate any reasonable request. I requested and received a Studio Plus room on a high floor (the 20th - the top floor is the 26th). The elevator was fairly quick up to the 20th floor. Key card access is set up in each of the two elevators but is not working yet.
When I opened the door, I smelled the odor of new leather from the stuffed chair in the corner. The next thing you notice is the handsome blonde all-wood floor and an awesome all Italian marble shower stall with a glass wall letting in lots of light from the floor-to-ceiling windows it faces. You can also slide an opaque door to cover the glass wall if you want privacy, but you might prefer not to do that to get the most natural light!
The boutique toiletries are from Archive and include Green Tea & Willow soap and shampoo, Rosehips & Lavender body lotion, and Grapefruit and Neroli shower gel.
There is a 37-inch LG high-def flat screen TV and a Yamaha surround sound projector plus a separate Pioneer DVD player. Full 800+ channel digital cable TV is provided through the Time Warner Cable system. The array of available channels is nearly unlimited. The only downside is mastering the use of three separate remote control devices. There is also free high-speed internet in the room using wired Ethernet access. Wi-fi access should also be available soon.
The bed is comfortable albeit a bit firm for my personal taste. There are three designer lamps in the room, a 2-cup coffee maker, a mini-bar, and a separate refrigerator that you can fill with your own items.
You will find a beautiful Owners Lounge on the second floor across from the fitness center. I won't comment on the fitness center because I did not use it. The lounge features ample seating both inside and on an adjacent outside terrace. There is no kitchen, so all food is catered by the nearby Redeye Grill. 
Continental breakfast is served from 6:30 AM - 10:00 AM seven days a week. They have fresh fruit, Greek-style strained yogurt with fruit or honey, bagels, croissants, pastries, cereal, cookies, cheese and crackers, bread, orange and grapefruit juice in addition to milk and various bottled water, juices, and drinks, coffee and tea, etc.
Evening cocktail hour runs from 5:00 PM - 7:00 PM seven days a week. In addition to soft drinks, red and white wine, canned and bottled beers, and spirits, there are the usual cheeses and fresh fruit plus several hot tapas served from Redeye Grill, including Kobe beef pigs in a blanket, shrimp dumplings, mini quiches, meatballs in marinara sauce, and spring rolls. The food is delicious and a several cuts above the Hilton Club New York, probably because of the caterer used. The spirits are all top shelf (for example, Ketel One vodka and Tanqueray gin).
I truly have enjoyed my experience here and highly recommend it to others.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Such a great location !!!!”
text: After reading the reviews here I thought this place would be awful. I found it to be a great location and the people were wonderful. The room might be a bit dated but soon the whole place will be renvated and will be amazing. I think it was just fine. Certainly don't avoid it!

name: West 57th Street by Hilton Club
title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text: This is a new hotel and I was skeptical but the Hilton impressed me. Check in was a breeze and the staff was very friendly. The location of the hotel (midtown) is great - you are in the heart of the city. The room itself was great. Very quiet despite being in the middle of the city (I was nine floors up) with nice amenities. The rooms are quite modern and the shower is unique but I really liked it. Comfy beds, big flat screen TV and nice bath products. Staff was extra accomodating holding bags for a while after I checked out. Overall, this is a great hotel in a great location. I will definitely be back!

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “THE BEST HOTEL IN THE BEST CITY IN THE WORLD”
text: I stayed at the Waldorf=Astoria with my husband and son for 6 nights on a 'once in a lifetime' trip to New York to celebrate my 40th birthday. What a dream come true! from the moment we entered the fantastic building we were treated special. We had a room overlooking Park Avenue and as it was my 40th, management sent cheese and wine to our room, which surprised us, as we are just an ordinary family, but they made us feel like the only people there. My tips for this hotel are to treat the hotel as part of your holiday (not just as somewhere to sleep) as the hotel is absolutely fascinating and I tried to spend as much time as possible looking around the hotel (they have glass cabinets with items relating to its history and its famous residents) and people watching in the lobby. If i had to be critical (and i really don't want to be) it would be that as its such a beautiful hotel and is very busy sometimes i found it quite difficult to find a seat in either the Park Ave lobby or the main lobby, but its worth waiting for! On another note, we upgraded before travelling from a deluxe room to a Superior Room, which although i don't know what a deluxe room is like, our room was via a small hallway (how posh)!rather than straight off a corridor and i'm guessing slightly bigger, with a better view. The room was equipped with all the necessary items you would expect including mini bar and ipod dock, and the bathroom/dressing area was immense and decked out in marble. Housekeeping did a great job and it seemed everytime we left the room, someone would come in and sort it out for us, including 'turn down' i.e getting the room ready for sleep with dimming the lights, shutting the curtains and turning down the bed......heaven. In a nutshell, THE BEST HOTEL IN THE BEST CITY IN THE WORLD.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Noisy and crowded area”
text: This is right next to the 9/11 site and construction starts early so can't sleep beyond 7 am on Satuday.The rooms are tacky, mostly Ikea like furniture. The service is ok at best. They don't have mobile phone chargers, so make sure you have all the battery life you need.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “my stay in new york”
text: Loved this hotel!!! The old world charm of the art deco stylings helped to make our family vacation so memorable. The place was spotless which is always a concern of mine. we had a small suite that was perfect when traveling with kids. Two tvs was very helpful. I only wish there had been coffee in the room. That was the only thing I wish had been different. I love having coffee when i first wake.

name: Hampton Inn 35th St. Empire State Building
title: “great location, service, and breakfast, very quiet rooms”
text: We spent a week here. It was very close to the subway, less than one minute walk. The staff was very friendly, the breakfast was the best hotel breakfast we have ever had. One day we were unable to eat until 9:45 due to an early morning trip and there was still plenty of hot food for us. We never heard any noise at night and the beds were very comfortable. We would definitely come back to this hotel.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Second visit, this time a suite!”
text: Took advantage of a special and stayed in a junior suite for the long weekend - just the right size and a beautiful view of the WTC Memorial. The location is perfect - between Battery Park City (a nice walk along the river) and the South Street Seaport (just a 10 minute walk down Fulton), and north to Soho and great shopping. Love staying in this hotel - great staff, and a delicious bar for late nights after a show in Times Square. Reserved an extra room for son and daughter-in-law!

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Big money, tiny, tiny room.”
text: For $400 per night, you expect a little charm, a little something extra. If you stay here, set your expectations far lower. You will get a room the size of a shoebox with a view of another building and a tiny bathroom that feels like a public school locker. This hotel is devoid of charm and is simply a place to sleep for a night, nothing more, nothing less. If you want an experience, stay at the Ace Hotel or something similar where the owners actually invested a little time and thought into design.

name: Algonquin Hotel Times Square, Autograph Collection
title: “Beautiful historic hotel, great service!”
text:
No complaints about this hotel at all. We arrived around noon and as the room was not yet ready, they held our luggage for us while we attended a class we were in town for. Later, when we arrived back at the hotel totally exhausted, the check in was very fast and our luggage was delivered to our room within minutes. 
The room was clean and a very reasonable size for NYC. I also appreciated the nice bath and bodyworks products in the bathroom. I could hear a bit out outside noise during the night, but it wasn't so bad that I needed to use the earplugs which were thoughtfully provided - especially consider how close we were to Times Square.
The lobby is stunning with lots of beautiful antique woodwork and paintings.. It's like stepping into a little piece of history and so much more interesting than your standard hotel these days. This hotel is also a very easy 2 block walk to Times Square and 3 blocks to the subway. Not a bad walk to Penn Station and Rockafeller Center either. 
Check out was equally speedy and professional, and they again held our luggage for us for the rest of the day until we made it back after dinner to head home.

name: Radisson Martinique on Broadway
title: “trés convenable”
text:
l'hôtel est idéalement situé sur broadway et sur la rue de little korea.Herald square est de suite sur la droite quand vous sortez de l'hôtel.Times Square est à 2/3min de marche.Il y a une station de metro juste en bas.
Pour la qualité de service il faut dire que les américains n'y sont pas trés attachés ( attente pour le check-in et 2 jours jours aprés notre arrivée le ménage a été fait) mais cela ne gâchera pas votre séjour.
je conseille cet hôtel pour sa situation et pour ses chambres;Elles sont plus que correctes avec salle de bain propres, sèche cheveux,fer à repasser, clim'.le seul hic l'impossibilité d'ouvrir les fenêtres donc d'aérer.
nous n'avons pas pris de petit-déjeuner à l'hôtel mais dans les alentours à moins de 100m vous avez largement le choix.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “worth the price for the glamor and tradition”
text:
we got what we expected. The so called deluxe rooms are really just standard hotel rooms which are somewhat dated and quite small.
What you pay for though is the glamor and elegance and history of the building itself and in that we weren't disappointed. the staff were brilliant throughout the hotel and the service was second to none.
Like a previous reviewer the lobby was closed when we arrived due to a wedding but that just added to the experience, we were able to enjoy the lobby on the following days

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “perfect place to stay”
text: suite was big and perfect for three people, not central location but not too bad, take aways and shops near by. staff were helpful. overall good stay

name: Algonquin Hotel Times Square, Autograph Collection
title: “Great Location, "ok" hotel...”
text:
I stayed here for one night for a business trip. I enjoy choosing Marriott properties b/c I collect the points. The hotel is old and has an antique feel to it. I prefer newer hotels with cleaner lines, but can appreciate the beauty in this. The rooms are very small, the halls are very small... I'm just not used to this. The bathroom was very "dingy".
The lobby is small, but warm. They have a resident cat who lives in the lobby / bar which was by far my FAVE thing about the hotel. I wouldn't run to stay here again, but wouldn't be upset if I stayed here again either. Decent place to stay if you want this location.

name: Room Mate Grace
title: “Trevligt hotell i centralt lage”
text: Bra hotell med narhet till det mesta mitt i centrala New York. Rummen ar frascha och moderna med gratis wifi som funkar utan problem. Trevlig hotellpersonal som svarade pa alla vara fragor, gav tips pa narliggande restauranger och liknande. Kan absolut tanka mig att aka tillbaks till Room Mate Grace Hotel nasta gang jag aker till USA igen!

name: Hampton Inn 35th St. Empire State Building
title: “Want to go back one day”
text:
We have just returned from spending 5 days in NY we stayed at the Hampton Inn Hotel 59 w 35th street. Hotel was lovely however I do have one gripe which is the breakfast room in the hotel was sooo cold they had the air conditiioning on 24/7 which for me made it very uncomfortable at breakfast even though I had a jacket/cardgian on.
I thought (whilst walking around) I might feel at risk in some way but I did not 
 I want to praise the staff at all the shops we visited ( not top designer shops) they were soo helpful to me. They will take you to the particular item you are looking for which impressed me greatly as I think here in UK they would simply point to an area!!
 I would like to say to those of you debating whether to go on a cruise/dinner....go we went with World Yacht Cruises and it was a very lovely evening, ladies do take a jacket/cardigan as the restaurant is very cold for quite a while into the trip I had a jacket (of sorts) but felt very cold for some time. The meal was excellant my husband had the steak and he raved about it, I had the chocolate dessert and it is to die for believe me!!!!!
when you disembark from the cruise walk to the road turn right walk a short distance down and you will see taxi/cabs waiting, these will be cheaper than taking the offer of limo or other kinds waiting for you

name: Hampton Inn 35th St. Empire State Building
title: “Close to it all and a good value”
text: My daughter and I met my sister for a long weekend in NYC and she had booked this hotel through an Expedia deal. She paid $855 for 6 nights and a flight from Detroit, not a bad deal. The hotel is very close to the subway and Times Square was only a few minutes walk away. The breakfast varied each day so it didn't get to boring. There were cheese "omelettes" and ham, eggs and sausage, french toast sticks and sausage. Other items included the usual - oatmeal (from a pouch), yogurt, fruit, muffins, donuts, etc. The hotel was very clean but small as I hear most NYC hotel rooms are. It was a good home base for a weekend visit.

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “Great Hotel”
text:
Very clean. Great Location. Great Price.
Was there Summer 2008 for business, but I would recommend to families as well. 
Close to Empire State Bldg, Penn Station, Madison Sq. Garden. Staff was great

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “Loved The Carlton”
text:
I stayed here for 3 nights in August with my two teenaged daughters. Kids under 18 stayed free which was a big advantage. Other cheaper hotels became more expensive than The Carlton with the charges for an extra person.
We loved this hotel! The room was huge by NY standards so there was enough space for all the "things" two teenaged girls "must" have with them at all times. The linens and beds were way above average as were the furnishing and decore. It was a pleasure to return to the hotel after a busy day.
The hotel is a few blocks from the subway, around the corner from a cheap coffee shop and close to Cafe28 which has just about anything you want to take out or have delivered.
Front desk was reserved yet helpful when we had questions and our request for extra towels and pillows was promptly filled. Our room was quiet and we just loved it. I would stay there again in a flat NY minute!

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “Great locations, price too high, slow elevators, rude staff”
text: I have stayed here a couple of times now and its a great location. However, the elevators are very slow and the staff could use a few customer service classes. They are a little rude and sometimes when they speak to you, you think you are at the local conveinence store. The rates are way too high also. But you are in manhattan so that is expected but even for Manhattan it's pretty high. There is an awesome deli on 32nd. and broadway called speedy's it has great food and good service. All this hotel has to do to improve is: rates a little lower, friendlier staff and upgrade the elevators. The rooms are very clean and remodeled, free internet, free nationwide long distance see not all negative.

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “Great hotel”
text: I stayed at the Carlton in June 2004 with my boyfriend and would definitely stay again when I return to New York. The rooms were very well decorated and clean, and the renovations did not make our stay any less enjoyable. Despite other reviews I did not find the staff to be anything but helpful and polite. Great place.

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “Great Stay”
text: We had 4 nights in NYC. Never having been there before just took a stab in the dark over the Internet. We were very pleasantly surprised by the hotel considering its low star rating. Staff were very friendly and helpful. Gave us toothbrushes and toothpaste when our luggage was 24 hours behind us. They directed us to a sister hotel across the road for free Internet use when our in room service didn't work. Great location - so close to everything. Breakfast was good but often very crowded. But didn't really go to NYC to waste too much time eating breakfast anyway.

name: Comfort Inn Manhattan
title: “Nice location and good value”
text: We stayed here over the weekend (9/10-9/12) and found this to be a great location and a good value. Free wifi with good and fairly easy access in the rooms. The breakfast was good with a selection of cereal, fruit, bagels, hardboiled eggs, donuts, muffins, etc. Coffee, decaf & hot water for tea are available in the lobby 24/7. Our room was quite small, but fine for 2 people. Our room was in the back and you could see the Empire State Building out the window. It was quiet and comfortable.

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “Convenient for those on a budget, lovely staff”
text:
Stayed for 5 nights recently in a large room. 
It's great to have own cooking facilities, fridge, microwave, gas hob; with pots, crockery and cutlery provided. 
The decor is not the most up-to-date, and some of the cupboards could do with a spring clean, but overall this is a great hotel for those who want to explore Manhattan. Grand Central is very close by so it's easy to hop on a train elsewhere too. For people who don't want to eat out morning noon and night, this hotel is great. 
My mother - on her first trip to the US - was impressed with the staff; they offered to post her letters, held our luggage for a couple of hours at no extra charge before we left for the airport, and generally were genuinely friendly.

name: Broadway Plaza Hotel
title: “just the job for a couple of nights”
text: i needed an overnight hotel stop in between moving apartments in NY - booked this via Orbitz as it was, well cheap. $98 for the night plus it said it offered room service. I arrived to be told the hotel was overbooked but they had found me a room - it was a very large room with 2 double beds and a simply enormous bathroom by any NY standards so I suspect if I'd got a $98 room things may have been different. For me the best thing about the room was it was SO quiet outside, literally the odd car going past but no beeping horns or other NY noises. "Room service" turns out to be a restaurant next door the hotel has hooked up with which during my stay was closed for renovations but I did get other menus brought to my room plus when the food arrived the security man called me first to let me know etc, I thought that was good. If I was staying in NY for more than 3 nights I'd probably pick another location but if you happen to just need a place to crash then I recommend this hotel. PS other reviewers have criticised the neighborhood - yes there are a few geezers hanging around trying to sell you sunglasses or whatever but 1. they go home when the shops shut 2. as a single woman from the UK living in NY I can tell you this is NOT a threatening neighborhood; you just need to look like you know where you are going so they don't mark you as a muppet 3. there are far far worse areas of Manhattan. Try Port Authority if you want dodgy geezers.

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “Rude help/tiny room/free is to expensive”
text: Hotel is under construction. When my wife and I arrived at the hotel(? ), got out of the taxi l,there was no doorman in sight.There are two level of steps to get to the front desk. A so called doorman watched as I carried two heavey pieces of luggage up the steps. I asked where the restrooms were and was informed there were not any in the lobby. and none we could use. From then on it went down hill. The hotel personnel were rude and really didn't care. Worst experience I have ever had in any hotel in the world.

name: Room Mate Grace
title: “dietro l'angolo.......times square!”
text:
tutto ciò che nel sito viene illustrato, poi lo abbiamo davvero trovato. senza sorprese spiacevoli di nessun genere.
La stanza ( 1110 ) era confortevole, pulita e accogliente. il letto super comodo e a NY il letto diventa fondamentale dopo le kilometriche passeggiate!
colazione abbondante e varia e soprattutto compresa nel prezzo.
personale gentile e sempre disponibile.
posizione eccellente: a 20 metri da times square.
credo che sarà il mio punto di riferimento anche per altre occasioni a NY.
consigliato.

name: Broadway Plaza Hotel
title: “Beware of the rodents in rooms”
text: Checked in and was very pleased with the size of the room (large by NYC standards). But on my final night, a rodent (not sure if it was a mouse or rat) ran across my room floor and under the couch. When I called down, the maintenance man wasn't overly surprised.
