One of his jobs, he tells me, is to inspect and fill in holes from the rodents. I did get to change rooms, but there was no attempt to compensate for this incident. Wouldn't stay there again.

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “Vraiment trés décevant....”
text:
L’hôtel est bien placé.L'accueil est professionnel sans être aimable.Un hall immense et faussement prometteur auquel on accède par une série de marches à descendre : pas pratique avec les bagages.Un bar ou règne une pénombre masquant la vétusté du mobilier ,l'age des fauteuils craquelés.Tout se gâte vraiment pour la chambre. Située sur une ruelle et mal isolée on a droit jour et nuit aux bruits permanents de machineries diverses.Mauvaise isolation aussi avec les couloirs et chambres voisines.Mobilier mal entretenu et en mauvais état (photo). Pour couronner le tout la salle de bains est indigne d'un hôtel qui se veut d'une catégorie supérieure par les prix pratiqués.Une petite fenêtre (qui ne s'ouvre pas car placée très en hauteur) et dont on a oublié de peindre les pourtours (photo);une cheville au dessus du lavabo (photo). On n'est vraiment dans des prestations correspondant au standing annoncé par l’hôtel et attendu par les clients.
En résumé je déconseille fortement cet établissement particulièrement en dessous de la catégorie annoncée.

name: JW Marriott Essex House New York
title: “Classic hotel ruined by very poor customer service”
text:
Stayed here for 6 nights, and had issues with staff/service on 4 of those nights. Supposed complimentary breakfasts were charged to our account. Eventually these charges (as this happened more than once), were reluctantly removed by a supposed Manager, whose customer service skills were wanting-he then revoked the complimentary breakfasts from our stay (after we had genuine reason to be given them in the first place). We'd read on Tripadvisor that there may be problems with incorrect billing, and were fortunately aware of this-or else it may have been difficult to argue later on into the stay. 
As my title says, a classic hotel that is ruined by very poor customer service.

name: Hilton New York
title: “OK. Not more”
text: Stayed at the Hilton for two nights for business. I ordered an executive room for about 450 a night. The small room I got on the 39th floor had good views, enabling me a glimpse of central park. The king bed was comfortable, but the entire room had that "old" feeling you get from a hotel that needs some major renovations. The tiny bathroom was clean, but definitely sub-standard for the price. The executive lounge offered a comfortable setting for the reasonable continental breakfast and very quick check in arrangements. All in all - reasonable for business, if you don't mind the very small bathroom and the "old" feel of the room. I would still try other places for the same price.

name: Hampton Inn 35th St. Empire State Building
title: “Sehr günstige und zentrale Lage”
text: Im großen und ganzen kann man das Hotel weiterempfehlen. Das Zimmer war allerdings nicht sehr sauber, besonders der dunkle Teppich. Außerdem funktionierte die Heizung nicht, was aber am nächsten Tag behoben wurde. Die Größe des Zimmers war für New Yorker Verhältnisse gut. Das Frühstück kann man sich getrost sparen, trockenes Brot von Papptellern ist nicht wirklich ein guter Start in den Tag. Die Betten und das Bad waren in Ordnung und sauber. Sehr günstig ist die Lage des Hotels, man gelangt zu Fuß schnell zum Times Square und die U-Bahn ist auch gleich nebenan.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Great location for shopping!”
text: We stayed at the Marriott Marquis last year, while the rooms there looked a little "newer" than the Hilton's, the location of the Hilton is so much better if you want to shop. The beds are nice and the pillows are great as is the water pressure in the shower. It's a pretty nondescript hotel as far as character goes and you don't get the feeling of being in great luxury, but if those things don't concern you this is a great place to stay. Location Location Location

name: Hilton New York
title: “first trip ever!”
text: Stayed at the Hilton NY and towers thanksgiving weekend, Nov 25-28 2004. Upon arrival, we were upgraded to the executive level on the 40th floor which included continental breakfast each morning and snacks each evening from 5-7pm. The room was especially small but we have nothing in NYC to compare it to. It was clean and very updated. We were placed near the service elevator and could hear the sounds at all hours but that didn't bother us. Everyone in the hotel was especially nice and courteous. The manager of the hotel came to our room one evening to get us set up with special internet access when the standard access wasn't working on our floor. The location was the BEST! Out the front of the entrance, about two blocks was Radio City music hall. We walked everywhere and took the subway also. The one complaint we had.. Our car was damaged in the valet parking lot. $500. damage! Scratches and a dent on my rear quarter. We've yet to hear back from them on this matter. But overall.. it was a great trip and I would stay there again only when booking through priceline. It's not worth the rack rate.

name: Broadway Plaza Hotel
title: “DON'T BELIEVE THE BAD REVIEWS!!!”
text: We are a family of 4 (two kids 10,5) and we were perfectly compfortable in one of the doubles at this hotel. There is a subway station across the street from the hotel, very convenient. wonderful hotel great staff great cont bkfst. the area is a middle class working neighborhood, so it's a little lonely at night, but you soon get used to it. please stay here and enjoy!!!

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “Bit dissapointed!”
text:
We were on the top floor - 25E.
It's a large "suite" - queen sized bed - in a large room with ensuite bath/shower & toilet.
There is a kitchenette off the main room, and a sofa bed which makes up into a quite comfortable double bed.
The hotel is showing its age! Carpets and general decor are grubby. When we were there (4th.to 8th. July) the restaurant was closed for renovations. Not a big problem for us as we intended eating out anyway. Located on East 39th Street, the location is quite good. Maybe a 15 minute walk to Time Square.
Accommodation in NY is ridiculously expensive - so we paid 4 star prices for this 2 star accommodation.

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “Style années 30 pour ce superbe hôtel”
text:
Situé à côté du Madison Park, cet hôtel à dans ses alentours des édifices tels que le Flatiron Building, l'Empire State Builiding, le Rockfeller Center... Vous comprendrez donc qu'il est idéalement placé pour une découverte de New-York.
Chambre ultra silencieuse, très spacieuse : minibar, bureau, dressing. Le bémol résiderait dans la taille de la salle de bains. Mais quand on connait le prix du m2 à New-York, on comprend mieux :)
Le restaurant est vraiment excellent ! Lui aussi je le recommande.
Très bon souvenir, j'ai hâte d'y retourner !
Quelques photos de New-York sur mon blog : http://viskatcha.com/blog/

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “My wife and I always stay at the Millenium”
text:
My wife and I have stayed at the Millenium several times over the past five years, most recently in December of 2011. We have never had a problem with noise, in fact I sleep better and longer at the Millenium than I do at my own home.
The rooms have plenty of space and amazing views of the WTC site.
As far as criticisms - We get free breakfast due to my Hilton points, but one criticism that I would have is that the list price of $27 for the breakfast is preposterously high. Also it can be surprisingly difficult to get a cab.
Ultimately if you have the cash, this hotel is worth it.

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “The worst hotel in NYC”
text: The worst hotel experience ever. I used to live in NYC and now live in Boston. This hotel was the pitts....On-line said three and a half stars...but it was a one star at best. Homeless people sleeping on ripped sofa in tiny tiny hall area they calll a lobby. Dirty filthy conditions. One desk clerk and one bellman for the entire hotel, Took forever just to get waited on then the hotel bellman and clerk were grouchy and so unwelcoming. Don't waste your money here....be warned....STAY SOMEWHERE ELSE.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Tiny Rooms”
text: Myself and three friends just came back from a six night stay at this hotel. The location is brill so near everything. We booked last August and asked for a Superior Double Double room with a good view. We checked in and went to our room on the 15th floor, what a disappointment, carpet really shabby, room tiny, view of a noticeboard if we could have stretched our necks to the right we might have seen Broadway and Times Square, room was only set for two people, two towels, two glasses etc. We were so disappointed and got in touch with reception straight away, the female receptionist had an attitude, and could only offer us a larger room without a view, apparently room is only superior if it has a view of Times Square. We were then allocated a room on the 12th floor at the back of the hotel, room was the same as the first one only it was 3 foot longer and we were given a portable 3 foot bed to go in the gap between double bed and wall. Room was approx 15 foot long. Again only set for two people, but Housekeeping immediately brought us towels, glasses etc. I spent the week sleeping in the portable bed!!!! We were waiting for our luggage to be brought from the first room and decided to go out to eat, when we arrived back luggage still not there, plus we had a male traveller who had also been allocated to sleep in our room, we all went down to Reception to sort it!!!! We decided just to put up with the room. Hotel main areas were good would say 5 star but the rooms definitely only 3 star. The double room is really only for two people and not four adults.

name: Algonquin Hotel Times Square, Autograph Collection
title: “Wonderful old hotel, but could use more diligent cleaning crew”
text:
The Algonquin takes you back to what New York used to be before all the mega-hotels came to town. It's a small - around 150 rooms - luxury hotel, rich in history, and we were absolutely charmed. The public rooms are open to the lobby (not closed off) but still clubby in feel - comfortable, intimate - and of course the restaurant features the famous round table where various literary lights gathered decades ago. The food was pricey, but excellent. The included continental breakfast was both generous and tasty. Great service all around.
Our room was small (to be expected) but comfortable and well-appointed. The bathroom, which had no tub, was just a step above a cubby. That wasn't really a problem. What was disappointing was that it was poorly cleaned. We arrived late on our first of two nights and so didn't notice until the next morning. Then because we had only one more night there and weren't spending much time in our room anyhow, we decided not to make an issue of it.
I would still definitely recommend this hotel. I feel sure that with the kind of service they offered, if we'd complained, they would have responded promptly. Do shop around for rates. We got a great deal through Expedia.
Business travelers, be aware that their Business Center consists of one computer and one printer that's poorly maintained. You can connect to the internet from your room though.

name: The Wall Street Inn
title: “Very Comfortable Hotel near Wall Street”
text: The hotel is small, but very pleasant. The staff is polite and efficient. Our room was small but very comfortable and completely furnished; the only thing missing was an in-room coffee maker. (Coffee and tea were available all day downstairs in the breakfast room.) The continental breakfast was very nice, although rather short of low-cal/low-fat/low-carb alternatives; for those willing to compromise their diets, however, the fresh pastries and breads were excellent. We did not have a car, but did not find the location in the Financial district a real disadvantage. We had no problems in getting cabs to our events at a considerable distance uptown. One distraction was the noise (loud talking and amplified music) coming each evening from a nearby restaurant with outdoor seating, but the noise stopped after 10 PM, so we were able to sleep in peace.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Maybe The Most Overrated Hotel in NYC”
text: If you like thin walls where you can hear your neighbors watching TV and laughing at 2 in the morning, sheets with a thread count of 10, a heating system that makes noise all night long, time warp furniture and fixtures, incredibly uncomfortable pillows and small bathrooms then this is the place for you. Otherwise go somewhere else. I booked my room thru HotWire, they said it was 3 1/2 stars, there is no where in the world this is 3 1/2 stars. Way too many other places to stay in NYC mid-town, check them out.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Prepare o bolso, não vá com crianças.”
text:
Viajamos em família, dois adultos, duas crianças. O Grand Hyatt é bem localizado, em uma posição central em relação às principais atrações de Midtown, prático. O quarto em que ficamos era pequeno porém confortável, com duas camas de casal e boas roupas de cama, mas não havia sido bem limpo: encontramos um recibo de cartão de crédito de 30 dias antes embaixo do pequeno sofá. A porta rangia alto ao abrir, imagine com crianças dormindo. Se você está viajando sozinho ou como casal, o hotel tem grande chance de ser adequado. Mas, se você está com crianças, melhor escolher outro.
A maior questão, no entanto, é que o hotel e seu staff olham apena$ para o dinheiro. Tudo é cobrado, até mesmo a recepção de pacotes de compras online (e isto não é avisado, aparece na conta, no checkout). Se você tem mais de um aparelho conectado a internet vai pagar por cada um deles (no momento, US$12.95/dia, mínimo). A guarda de malas é também cobrada. Os bellmen (maleiros) são rudes e pedem alto por um serviço simples, levar malas para lá e para cá. Cuidado, podem cobrar duas vezes pelo mesmo serviço (um deles tentou conosco). Não peça ajuda para obter um taxi grande, você vai pagar comissão.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Small rooms....but very comfertable”
text: Came here after two weeks in florida and it was a bit of a culture shock. Very busy hotel with people coming and going all the time and there was a latin music conference going on when we were there. Rooms were small but the beds were class! bathrooms could do with updating though. One thing i would say is to check out the diner connected to the hotel...best breakfast in new york. Overall a pretty good hotel

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “$14.95 internet charge on $450 hotel room is just greedy”
text:
Obviously a hotel for people on expense accounts (like me). Considering that I've stayed at $50/night hotels which provide internet service for free, being charged $14.95 when the room costs 5 times more taints my opinion from the start. 
Try avoid floors 40-50 facing east (a.k.a. 'back' of the hotel), or you'll spend all night listening to the drone of the air conditioning units on top of the building next door. The WTC construction site is just to west of the hotel, and indeed they work 24h/day, but at least you get to see all the action. 
Best part about the hotel is the location. Various subway lines are all a short walk away. Also the AirTrain/A-train combination from JFK airport is super-easy and gets you steps away from the hotel with zero traffic jams in between.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Grand Hyatt”
text:
Très satsisfait, chambre agréable et confortable. Cependant dommage des travaux dans l'hotel. La réception est très impersonelle et on a de la peine à trouver sa place à cause des travaux.
Le personnel très sympa et serviable.
Hotel bien situé à l'écart de Time Sqare ce qui lui donne un côté plus apaisant.
A y retourner... bcp de plaisir.

name: Algonquin Hotel Times Square, Autograph Collection
title: “Class is Still Alive in New York”
text: This is a hotel from a bygone era which has been updated and brought into the present time without sacrificing the very unique and classy heritage that it represents. Our room was a little small, but clean and functional. After all, we only needed it for sleeping and bathing. The bed was, without exception, the most comfortable and luxurious experience we've had in a hotel. What a joy to fall into it at the end of a long day of sightseeing and shopping. But the wonderful lounge area off of the lobby was where we had the most fun. Even if we weren't guests, we would be back there to enjoy a nightcap any time. The staff is outstanding. Their professionalism and friendlieness should be the envy of even the most "exclusive" hotels of New York. We felt safe, we felt appreciated and we have no problem returning there again in the future. It is a rare gem in the midst of the sprawl of Manhattan - but one that should not be overlooked. Be sure to order a "Mathilda" cocktail if you are in the bar and then stop by and say hello to the old girl herself. One very lucky kitty.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “New York at its best”
text:
We returned to the Affinia Manhattan for another 5 day stay on 14th November 2012 and were not disappointed,this must be one of the best locations in New York,next to Madison Sq. Gardens,a stone throw away from Empire State Building,Penn Station,Macys etc....
From the well appointed rooms to the classy Niles Bar and restaurant it exudes comfort.....the staff are only too willing to assist in any way they can and make every guest feel both welcome and valued.
This was our second visit to the Affinia and it wont be the last,the only thing that was disappointing was that the time passed so quickly.I would recommend this hotel to anyone,a good standard and a pleasure to stay in....

name: The Belvedere
title: “Tired but close to Times Sq”
text:
Stayed four nights in this conveniently located hotel just 5 minutes walk from Times Sq. The rooms were confortable and roomy but badly in need of a face lift. Our bath was chipped and the the decor was overdue for a fresh makeover. However it was clean and convenient except for the lifts (elevators). There were 2 direct to the lobby and at peak times (breakfast and check out) the wait for an empty one was unacceptably long (around 5 minutes). There is another one at the end of the corridor but there was no sign to tell you.
Recommend you have breakfast at Patzeria (just 8 doors down the street) if you are a tourist. Both Joe and his sister were very friendly and printed off ideas for places to visit and how to get there.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Good location for theater district/times square but needs some work.”
text: The location is great if you are in town to explore the theater district or the zoo that is Times Square. The hotel is located on 48th between 8th and 9th. You are very close to many of the major musicals and plenty of dining options between the hotel and Times Square. There are also plenty of bars and dining options on 9th away from Times Square in the Hell's Kitchen area. The door staff were pretty nice. The front desk staff was hit and miss. Sometimes felt as a guest I was a bother-other times they were very nice. DO NOT wait for the central two elevators. They are slow, small and ALWAYS full. Not uncommon to wait for 4-5 cars or 5-10 minutes to actually get a ride up or down to the lobby. So frustrating-especially at peak times. A secret-use the elevator at either end of the hall. The staff use these mostly and we were not told about them, but use them. It will save you valuable time on your vacation. The shower was great! and the bathroom nice and adequate. The a/c is pretty noisy but a must in the summer. The carpet definitely needs to be replaced. The walls/doors are not the thickest. Did not try the cafe and the concierge was ok not great. Overall an average hotel. Not great, but not bad. If you can get a good rate worth a look.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Staying Here is Like A History Lesson”
text:
The hotel itself is beautiful with all the standard amenities. And the views! 
The Brooklyn Bridge side is fascinating in the daytime when the East River is alive with water taxis, ferries, sailboats and tour boats. At night, with the bridges lit up, it's quite lovely and romantic.
The World Trade Center side has equally spectacular views of the Hudson River and it's flotilla of ferries and pleasure cruisers. But, in addition, you are looking down onto the site of the World Trade Center as it rises to reinvent itself while memorializing the events of 9/11. The original footprints of the Twin Towers are clearly outlined by cascading pools of water. The dramatic lines of the museum are starting to take shape. As many as 3,000 
construction workers are committed to having the work completed by the tenth anniversary.
It's haunting and uplifting and just an incredible experience to witness. 
I will never forget my stay at the Millenium Hilton and look forward to going back, someday, to stroll amongst the trees being planted at the World Trade center site in memory of those who were lost.

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “Muy buen hotel, moderno y con inmejorable situación”
text: El hotel está fenomenal, la habitación muy moderna y limpia. Muy amplia, aunque en nuestro caso nos habían hecho un upgrade. Cama muy cómoda y muy buena situación, al lado de 2 lineas de metro y a 2 manzanas del Empire State. La atención del personal fue excelente. Me sorprendió, no tiene nada que envidiar a un cuatro estrellas de las grandes cadenas hoteleras de España.

name: The Wall Street Inn
title: “Decent Hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Wall Street Inn starting the Friday after Thanksgiving. I was pleasantly surprised. 
The rooms are small, but to be expected in NYC, but they were always clean as was the hotel as a whole. The location is just off Wall Street, hence the name, and is close to various subway stations making it easy to get anywhere in the city. (Although, many of the subway stations in that area had limited availability over the weekend while we were there, so be sure to check the NYC tranisit site before heading to the subway station). 
The location was generally quiet, especially on the weekend, which can be a good thing for sleeping, but not the best for finding stuff to do. Most of the bars in the area were "corner" type bars, great for stopping by for a quick drink before heading out to one of New York's more exciting neighborhoods. It is also close to the free Staten Island Ferry.
A nice extra is their continental breakfast. It was basic, but the bagels were very good and they had hard boild eggs, which I loved! And it lasted until 11am - even on weekends.
A big plus is they had free Wi-Fi which was fantastic for checking online for places to eat or the MTA (NYC transit) website.
The staff was helpful, but could come off as a little cold at times. They did however suggest a car service to use which worked out fantastic. It was a flat $30 to LaGuardia (not including tip), regardless of rush hour traffic - in case you didn't know, you pay for waiting in traffic while in a cab in NYC.
The price seemed comparable to other places nearby. They also appear to have weekend rates around $300ish, so check into it when booking the room. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

name: Marmara Manhattan Hotel
title: “Wonderful”
text:
Outstanding hotel., pretty much a one bedroom apartment., complete with kitchen, posh bedroom and fold out sofa-sleeper. Very clean and quiet., although the noise from the outside can get pretty loud., just ask for a room on a higher floor. 
Lots of great restaurants and bars just blocks away. Safe neighborhood.

name: Carlton Hotel, Autograph Collection
title: “Très bon hotel”
text: L'hotel est très beau et les chambres confortables bien que un peu petites. En ce qui concerne l'emplacement de l'hotel, super !! Proche des stations de métro qui permettent d'aller partout dans cette ville.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Loved it”
text: We were very happy with the Hotel and our room. I booked online well in advance of our trip, booking online always makes me a bit nervous, but this hotel was everything I ask for and more. We would stay at the Hilton again. Mater of fact our trip took us all around the east/north and we stayed at Hiltons or Hamptons and was never disappointed.

name: The Belvedere
title: “I wouldn't choose anywhere else”
text: Amazing hotel in the perfect location. Executive rooms are definitely the only way to go. Lift is a little slow but it's great. I have stayed here about 5 times and will always return. Great value for money

name: Park South Hotel
title: “Great location and great value for money”
text:
Stayed here for four nights as a second choice. Wanted to stay in the Giraffe hotel round the corner having previously stayed there (another great hotel) but they were full. Was pleasantly surprised and enjoyed my stay. The staff were friendly and welcoming, good breakfasts and plenty of space. There is a small terrace outside if you want to stop for a coffee or glass of wine. The room was spacious with a good sized bathroom. The bed was a bit harder than I would like but it was ok. 
This hotel is great value for money and would now be my first choice.

name: The Standard, East Village
title: “Gem in Manhattan!”
text: Modern, clean, incredible plush beds, sleek, fabulous hotel! I stayed the weekend with 5 of my girls. We had a wonderful time! The location is perfect, Trilby bar/restaurant downstairs was a wonderful way to start our night & the staff was super helpful and friendly. I am so happy to say that I have found my new favorite NYC place to stay...I will definitely be back!

name: The Standard, East Village
title: “Nice hotel - awesome view!!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Cooper Hotel for a weekend getaway without the kids. As other reviewers have said, the standard rooms are very small. But the view more than made up for it. We had a view of Cooper Union and the Empire State Building that was AMAZING! The room was very, very clean and very well appointed. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The only other negative is the lighting in the bathroom was poor. Putting on make-up in the evening was just about impossible. 
The neighborhood is very nice and close to the 6 train and the R/N train. Walking distance to the East Village, West Village and Noho. If I were to stay downtown again, I would stay there for certain.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Posizione eccellente”
text:
Abbiamo alloggiato in questo Hotel dal 24 aprile al 1° maggio. La posizione è ottimale per tutti gli spostamenti. E' in fase di ristrutturazione ma sinceramente ciò non ha creato alcun problema. Personale gentile e servizio adeguato. Per gli italiani proseguendo sulla 42 direzione times square, a circa 100 metri, c'è un bar che fà un discreto caffè. Si chiama expresso.
Lo consiglio vivamente, anche alle famiglie, in particolare per la posizione. Di fronte c'è la possibilità di prendere il bus per l'aeroporto.

name: Algonquin Hotel Times Square, Autograph Collection
title: “Literary History Galore!”
text: Ok, the rooms are small, but you can't beat the literary history in these walls. What a fun place. Love it, love it, love it. Hang out in the lobby and soak in the vibes of Dorothy Parker and gang. (But wait until you can get a good deal- - try not to pay more than $230 for a room.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “A good choice but”
text:
A good choice :
- room are very clean
- staff friedliness is above average
- a central location for visiting new york
- free wifi in the room
- quiet room (at least for our room on 26th floor)
- free fitness center
but
- room are very small
- breakfast at the hotel is really standard and not fancy
- no swimming pool, sauna or steam bath
- price is quite high

name: Park South Hotel
title: “Nice lower cost NYC hotel”
text: One of life's struggles is to find a lower cost hotel in NYC where the rooms are comfortable. Park South totally met our needs. Yes, the room is small but this is NYC and it isn't about the room. The hotel is centrally located.

name: The Standard, East Village
title: “Modern hotel but rooms much smaller than advertised”
text:
I'll start with the positives of this hotel. It is very well located, close to the restaurants and bars of the East Village and Lower East Side and the shopping of SoHo. The subway is nearby, with stations for the 6 and F/V providing easy access to much of Manhattan. The decor in the public areas and rooms is modern but warm, and the lobby area and patio are nice areas to relax in. Take advantage of great coffee at Think, a few blocks south, and free passes to a very nice New York Health and Racquet Club gym across the street.
My room was clean and well-maintained, without any signs of wear and tear. The wardrobe was small but adequate for one person for 3 days, and the Sony iPod player provided great sound. The TV sat in front of the window, so there was a lot of glare, but it had every possible channel. Amenities like a choice of cotton or silk robes and turndown service with a cookie or fruit were appreciated. The bathroom was dark, but a mirror in the wardrobe helped with getting a good look.
I don't like small hotel rooms, so I specifically booked the 350 sq ft Cooper Five room. Well, it was small. Very small. Just under 250 sq ft in fact (including the bathroom and entry hall; yes, I measured, thanks to the idea of an earlier reviewer). The king bed dominates the room, and it's a good thing I traveled alone, as two people in the room would need to coordinate their movement in the narrow spaces around the bed. I found the bed to be quite soft and giving, more than I prefer.
Not receiving the space I paid for was very frustrating, but the room was unlike the description on the hotel's reservation page in other ways too. "All rooms have a window seating area" - except mine. "Bathrooms are a mixture of steam shower and traditional tub & shower combo" - except mine, which had only the combo. "Best views in the hotel....enjoy the breathtaking views" - sure, if you consider the rooftops of the East Village breathtaking. My view north was obstructed by a building one block away; the tip of the Empire State Building barely stuck out.
I met with a hotel manager upon checkout to express my concerns, particularly as to the misrepresentation of the room's size. I was told that not all rooms have the same features (which is not indicated on the website) and that room sizes are approximate. I can accept a slight variation, but my room was 30% smaller than advertised. It was equivalent to a Cooper 2, which is roughly 20% in cost. I didn't get a 20% reduction in my bill, but I did receive a credit and didn't wish to argue further. It was recommended that I book a studio or suite in the future to get the space I want, so maybe the "500 sq ft" Studio 2 will actually have the 350 sq ft I desired.

name: Chelsea Lodge
title: “Highly recommended for the price”
text: Great location (20th St in Chelsea) comfortable bedding, linens. Smaller than usual, even for NYC, but nonetheless, one of the biggest bargains in accommodations in the city. The place is quiet, (surprising for a townhouse), the people who work there were quirky and nice, and the room was cleaned during our short breakfast run.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Excellent Stay - a few hiccups.”
text:
Full-disclosure; I am still here in the middle of my stay but have a few moments to weigh in so far. 
I have seen a few of the reviews that have complained of either run-down or dirty issues - I simply cannot agree. I have been very pleased with the condition of the hotel in general (see "hiccups" below) meaning, this place is neat, clean, and well appointed. 
Staff service, especially the front desk and bell staff, have been remarkable. The front desk staff has been professional, efficient and very helpful. 
Elevators are fast and plentiful, clean and safe. Hallways are clean and modern and free of that occasional "debris" that you sometimes run into, an errant tissue or napkin that seems to sit there for days. 
And, I have not seen one single "critter", which is important to me being somewhat of a phobic. Not an ant, not a roach, not a bedbug, not a gnat, not a fly. Weird to mention, perhaps, but I have stayed in places where this has been an issue. This place is clean, no question. 
Location is perfect. This is 7th ave across from Madison Sq. Garden. Starbucks, pizza, desserts, subway entrance, all within half a block. No better place to be. 
Noise? It's NYC. First, there is almost ZERO noise from other rooms, or voices in the hall, doors slamming or toilets flushing. None. 
Street noise can be eliminated with a decent pair of ear plugs. Not the foam ones, the wax ones. Use them properly and you will hear NOTHING. 
Now, the hiccups. 
When the bell man dropped off the bags, he asked if there was anything else we needed; I stated that we needed more coffee packets. He happily stated that "I will send them right up". This never happened. (more on this bellman in a second)
Secondly, when we moved in, the AC unit in the room was extremely noisy. To the point where it needed to be dealt with. I called the desk, they sent maintenance up immediately, all good. He looked at it and said the compressor was bad, he needed to locate another one. I assumed it meant he would go find a unit and bring it up and swap it out. He disappeared and we never heard back. No follow up, no nothing. So we're using the fan on the unit which is keeping the room moderately cool but can't actually turn on the AC or the noise actually produces nausea. 
So from a service standpoint, there's a bit of a "follow up" issue. Not major, just frustrating enough. Housekeeping has been spotty (last night they showed up at 8:30 pm looking to service the room - a bit late, dont you think?) but overall, these are the things that happen. 
One of the most unusual things is a particular bell man - not sure the name but this guy is bringing the professionalism level of the hotel down a bit. He is the same guy who promised up the coffee packets - and I think he just pocketed the tip and went away. I dont think he really cared whether we got the coffee. 
When we checked in, this same bell man was acting a bit unusual with the front desk staff - demanding high - fives from a couple of the girls - and the girl who checked us is was visibly uncomfortable with this. This is not really a professional display to exhibit in front of the guests. 
This same guy ended up in an elevator with me, my daughter and another family. At that point he started handing out business cards for a local Irish pub and a Liquor store saying "this is the place to go"...clearly, he's getting some kick backs from these places to promote them but it's highly unprofessional, especially when the business cards for a liquor store are being handed out to kids. 
now, is this the Affinia's fault? Not really, this guy is just a typical rouge new york hustler trying to earn a buck. but as I said, it's taking the polish off the professional sheen of the hotel. 
Would I stay here again? Absolutely. They have treated us pretty well, given us a room upgrade, and I am getting some great sleep. Just a few hiccups and this would be a perfect 5 stars.

name: Algonquin Hotel Times Square, Autograph Collection
title: “Enjoyed the Algonquin”
text: The room was small, but clean and very comfortable. The staff was very nice, especially the bellhop and the doormen. We were disappointed that the coffeemaker that was promised to be in the room wasn't. When we asked the desk, they said they have coffeemakers that we could have, but they don't have coffee or filters to go with them. My advice, don't say it's an amenity when it isn't. They also change the time when the lobby coffee is available, so we missed out both days. I would definitely go back to stay again. Very comfortable and close to the theatres. The diner next door, The Red Flame Diner, was the perfect place for an inexpensive meal at anytime, they open at 6am and stay til midnight.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Glad I stayed here once but probably won't return”
text: My daughter and I spent the weekend at the Waldorf Astoria (NYC) for her 18th bday. A lovely, historic hotel an easy walk (or very short cab ride) away from Times Square, Public Library, Grand Central Station, FAO, Central Park, St. Patrick's Cathedral, Serendipity 3, Dylan's Candy Bar, Rockefeller Center, broadway theatres. A cab is needed to access the Status of Liberty and Ellis Island. A bit of a line at check-in and a delay in room availability but hotel text messaged me when room was available. Our bags were stored while we wait. Room was at a discount rate I found on-line. Comfortable, small (but with two beds), zero view, a bit dated with an old sort of odor/maybe mildew? Felt safe and appreciated the after 10pm need for your room card to access guest floors via elevator. Piano Cole Porter used to compose on is on display in lobby atrim, as well as historic clock and historical overview display cases with memorabiliia in main lobby. Hotel definitely seems to appeal to many international guest. Hotel shop has an adequate selection of items that aren't as pricey as I would have expected. Dining and room service prices, however, are absolutely ridiculous. $30 for a Caeser salad? I'm talking absolutely ridiculous pricing. Glitch at check out with bottled water from the in-room refrig erroneously charged to my account. I believe the price was around $7 a bottle. Hotel removed charges but with a slight bit of hesitation. No safe in the room but there is a blow dryer, ironing board and iron. There is not any late night 'grab a snack' dining in the immediate vicinity of the hotel which was a negative for us returning from shows after 11pm. Staff is aloof but friendly. There is a business center.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Zentral - Gutes Hotel”
text: Wir waren Mitte April 2010 für 2 Nächte hier. Unsere Zimmerwünsche, die wir bei der Buchung bezüglich Ausstattung und Lage angegeben hatten, wurden beim Check Inn berücksichtigt. Insgesamt war unser Zimmer aufgrund der Häuserschluchten ein wenig dunkel... Ansonsten war es absolut o.k. Zentraler kann man kaum noch wohnen. Jederzeit wieder...

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Central location, 1920s grandeur”
text: We spent five nights at this fabulously central hotel. The room was small but comfortable, clean and quiet. Just around the corner from Penn subway station and Madison Square Garden it is really a very good base. It's also walking distance to Times Square. With internet access in the business centre and ice machines on several of the floors, there's not much more needed! We will definitely return.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Great place! Construction noise wasn't bad”
text:
I stayed here on August 21-23rd 2010. My wife had to fly out of JFK and I was not trying to drive back & forth to MA in such a short timeframe.
I read reviews & people complain about the noise from WTC construction, but honestly: find another hotel or at least look at maps so you know that you WILL be right across the street from it all.
I was on the 19th floor and could barely hear anything. Just the noise from the TV or AC made it disappear. Now I bet that the 2nd floor would probably suck, but call the hotel 1st to see what floor you might get. It was extremely clean, nice 42" tv in the wall and super comfy king size bed with lots of down pillows. It was worth my $172 per night on Hotwire.

name: Comfort Inn Manhattan
title: “Value for Money, Great Location, Beware of differences in rooms”
text:
Literally just got back from NY. Stayed 3 nights in the Comfort Inn. The location was brilliant. Couldn't have chosen better. The reception was clean and welcoming, most of the staff were very helpful and chatty. Beware of the Spanish, middle aged female receptionist. She is not friendly and not helpful and we witnessed her arguing with the guests on more than one occasion. All other desk staff were really friendly and helpful. Just steer clear of her and you'll be fine. :)
There is a difference in rooms. If your unlucky enough to be given one of the side rooms with one window and no light ask to change immediatley to a front room or back room. The windows make a big difference to the rooms. We asked to change. First the Spanish lady said no, there was no room, not possible. She was lying as the one of the guys swapped us a few hours later to a room at the front of the hotel. The difference was amazing. The rooms were clean and welcoming. A little old in decor and the aircon noisy but relly and truly for the price the rooms are a good deal. Much better than staying a hostel. The showers in both rooms were fantastic and despite reading reviews prior to our trip we thught the bathroom was clean and adequate and not small.
With the coffee cafe next door and Brendans restaurant on the other side you are not short food or caffine.
Do not try the coffee machine in reception! YUK
Internet was free in reception, but there can be a long que.
Two main lifts which were adequate but slow.
Breakfast was not luxe. It was ok. Bread/toast/bagels/donuts/cereal and muffins. It was good enough although repetative. Plastic cutlery, plates and cups were interesting.
Take margerine with you. Unless you fancy defrosting the butter with your lighter you will have problems! Good idea to take your own jams, peanut butter, marmite etc. to jazz up breakfast.
Macy's and Broadway forty meters away. Empire State building right behind the hotel.
The windows in the second room opened without problem and the aircon worked. We did not find the noise from the street that bad.
Construction is going on in the building next door but we didn't hear anything while we were there.
The hotel is old, but it does have character and considering the price we were more than happy. It's right opposite the Hilton which costs tons more.
Didn't actually see the maids but the room was clean and the beds were fresh. Plenty of towels in the bathroom.
The safe worked well and was big enough for all documents, ipods, camaras etc.
Easy to catch taxi's in front of the hotel or in front of Macy's.
Big cheap Old Navy store down the side of Macy's. Value for money.
Area felt safe.
In general, bargain for price - just beware of the receptionist mentioned above!

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Great location opposite Madison Sq Garden”
text:
Great location opposite Madison Sq Garden.
Rooms were very clean but small - I guess small is the norm for Manhattan
Concierge - excellent
Seemed to be waiting for a lift (elevator) for longer than I should have.
My room was by 7th Avenue and got LOTS of traffic noise from cabs sounding horns from an early hour and emergency vehicle sirems etc

name: Park South Hotel
title: “good find”
text:
good location,small rooms with bath.fridge,safe.clean,good staff.
some noise from outside air con.New York hotels are expensive for what you get.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Decent, not 4 star, good if gotten at a value!”
text:
I will start this with the basics, but please read the whole review! This is the FIRST time I have written negatively about service (I honestly am not picky and will stay at a motel 6, etc.). First, the room. Very clean, warm hallways, cool in the room. Bathroom was a mid-range space, not four star. Basic, some outdated fixtures, good size. Room itself good size for NYC. Bed very comfortable, chair and ottoman clean but starting to show wear. Coffee maker and desk area good. TV console great size, minibar fridge stocked (and of course, expensive). View gorgeous over into New Jersey and over the WTC work site. About the noise - we were on the 24th floor and could hear some rumbles, but it did not upset any sleep. Hotel public spaces not impressive, again, basic. Quick check in, elevators, front desk and front doors all within 40 steps. No grand lobby here.
ON TO SERVICE. I promise that I am not picky, yet when I stay at (and pay for) a 4-star hotel, I expect service that makes me feel somewhat special (anything - a welcome note, door help, anything). First, I walked in carrying two large shopping bags and a purse. Went through the revolving door with a door/bell man outside and one inside, no help offered (eve though it isn't that large of a lobby, there should be some help offered to guests). After checking in, still no help offered for carrying bags after passing a different bellman. This is not 4 star service - I wasn't even asked by reception if I needed help, had a preference for floor or beds, etc. Went in and out of the hotel at least 4 times first day, and never a door held open when I did not use the revolving door. 
HERE IS THE REAL COMPLAINT!
The next morning, and this is the kicker, housekeeping knocked and came in the room THREE TIMES while we were sleeping!!! at 8:30am, I did not hear a knock (sleeping), but heard my door open and housekeeping talking to each other and walk in. They then saw us in bed and closed the door. At 9:45, I heard knocking, then the door open AGAIN! I shouted out that we were in the room, and they left. At 11 or so, they knocked once again, but this time I put the security lock on (I must have forgot) so they couldn't get all the way in. FYI - checkout is not until NOON!!!!! At 11:40 a gentleman knocked on our door (we were packing up) and asked if we were leaving!!!!! Of course we are - after we CHECKOUT! I have worked hotels - a simple report shows what guests have checked out. I was appalled that at a 4 star hotel I would be awoken twice by housekeeping HOURS before checkout, then twice more been bullied out. Absolutely unacceptable.
Overall, would NOT stay here again unless desperate or paid almost nothing. Felt overpriced for the room - even in NYC. To deal with poor service, less than stellar accommodations, etc, but have to pay for 4-stars is not okay. Look around for other deals.

name: Dream Downtown
title: “Great Stay”
text: Stayed at the Dream last month and could not be happier. From check in to check out the friendly staff made sure four nights were great. Happening scene at the hotel, great location and some great on site restaurants made it the perfect hotel while visiting Manhattan.. Will definitely stay again!

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Xmas shopping”
text: Clean, well located in Theatre district, friendly staff, a bit pricy but what isn't in this part of town, all by all good deal

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text: We stayed at the hotel for 6 nights. The room and the bathroom were beautiful and clean . They serve contenential breakfast every morning and the food is pretty good, especially the bagels. We found this hotel a perfect location because it is right by the Empire State Building, and about 10 blocks from Times Square. This two star hotel was great value and we got more than what we expected. We would definitely stay here again. Excellent Hotel!

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “A good decision made ....”
text:
I took my nephew to New York as a treat and after much deliberation decided to spend a little extra than planned and go to the Red Roof. New York hotels are extremely expensive and you normally don't get a lot for your money but the Red Roof is definitely worth it. I booked a room with 2 double beds and was surprised at how big the room was in comparison to other New York hotels I have stayed in.
Hotel room was clean, great bathroom and decent air conditioning.
Would recommend highly to anyone. Bonus features of this hotel;
1) Location - just round the corner from the Empire State
2) Free breakfast
3) Free WiFi internet
Downsides
a) Slow check in process
b) Even slower lift (elevator) !
c) Taxes ... added about 25% onto the advertised room rate
Picture attached was taken from the top of the Empire State Building … as you can see, the Red Roof Hotel doesn’t have a red roof !

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Very Noisy and got no sleep”
text:
We arrived on the 22nd of October and were upgraded to a Delux Room. The room was very large by New York hotel standards. It was very clean and you could tell the staff took pride in what they did. However, the noise from Park Avenue was deafening, there was work men drilling from 4am every morning. None of the family could sleep. The thing we did not do was complain I know we should have but I did not want to sound like a winging pom - I was so exausted as were my family. 
The hotel was shabby chic and the staff really had that oldy worldy attitude. 
We stayed in this hotel 2 years previous and it was a more positive experience. 
PS; please remember not to move any of the contents of the mini bar, as you will incure a charge on your account. It took us a while to rectify this. Some good breakfast cafes in Lexington.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Security from hell!!!!!”
text: I've stayed at this hotel many times before, in fact I'm a hilton honors reward member. We were intown for a friends birthday and while getting dressed to go out we decided to listen to music (on a portable speaker the size of a deck of cards) . Several minutes later, we heard a loud police style knock on the door; security. I asked to see picture id, they refused stating "Open the door or we'll knock it down". We were upset, shaking, not sure if it was security or imposters. The gentleman even refused to step closer so I could read their nametags. Then when I spoke to the manager on duty Charo, she stated how she didn't appreciate us threatening to call the police. The entire incident occured because of a noise complaint, that could have been handled with a simple call to the room (I'm doubtful that a small portable ipod speaker compared to the commotion that security caused). Then mamagements response left an unsavory taste in my mouth, we were basically called liars. As a result I've ditched the hilton brand and chosen the W brand instead (and the W time square has noise proof suites)

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Great hotel but slightly out of the way of the main attractions.”
text: This hotel is literally on the doorstep of the world trade centre. The hotel is fantastic but as we were there for Fleet Week, it was slightly out of the way as most of the navy activities occurred near times square. The open top bus does have a stop nearby on Broadway and is a fantastic way to see the city and learn little bits of information that the guide books don't tell you. The hotel is right next door to Century21 which should be avoided unless you plan on spending the whole holiday in there. I thought TK Maxx was unbearable until I went here. It is a fantastic location for the statue of liberty and ferry trips. The pool is very clean and the staff are friendly.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Night time construction near hotel - jack hammers. Great service.”
text: Location, quality of room, food, service was excellent until we needed assistance moving so we could sleep. There were two different sets of jack hammers working all night some of the time we were there. Various hotel staff members denied it was happening, and insisted the hotel was not under construction. True, the hotel itself is not under construction. Something very near the hotel is under night time construction. This hotel is frequently cited as noisy. The big city sounds would have been acceptable, but not the construction noise at night.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Beliggenheten er topp.”
text: Bra hotel med sentral beliggenhet. Gåavstand til det meste. Frokosten var dyr, det var billigere å bestille frokost på rommet enn nede i resturanten. Koselig frokost/lunsj resturant anbefales rett ved ingangen til hotellet og en Starbucks. Vi kommer gjerne igjen :))

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “Loved the apple and the inn !!!”
text: First time visitors from Winnipeg, Canada to New York. We found the location excellent !!! It was close to the subway, the Empire State Building and a ten minute walk to Times Square. The service was excellent and the hotel was very clean. The continental breakfast was adequate but added to the value of the trip!!! Excellent Korean restaurant right next door, we recommend steamed shrimp dumplings for a late night snack. A native New Yorker friend was quite impressed by the size and quality of the room by New York standards. The room was large enough for a comfortable stay and the bed was like sleeping on a cloud!!! The staff was friendly and helpful, although the elevator is extremely slow. Overall, Highly recommed this hotel, would stay again, great value for your money in New York.

name: Algonquin Hotel Times Square, Autograph Collection
title: “Absternerse gente joven. Localizáción perfecta.”
text: Es un hotel con encanto y a mi ententer dirigido a un público mayor. Es todo bastante antiguo y las habitaciones extremadamente pequeñas, cosa bastante típica en Manhattan. Los baños eran pequeños y antiguos. Las camas eran buenas, pero no hay casi sitio para nada en las habitaciones. Te dan dos botellitas de agua gratis cada noche. Los empleados del hotel son muy amables y están atentos a cualquier cosa que necesites. Por su aspecto de hotel boutique y con historia los recomiendo para gente a partir de 40 años. Por el mismo precio o más barato y con desayuno dos calles más arriba tienes el THE HOTEL AT TIMES SQUARE que es bastante más moderno y las habitaciones más grandes. Unos amigos se quedaron en ese y me gustó bastante más. El Algonquin tiene wifi gratis y una localización excelente. Entre la 5 ave y Times Square.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Top Notch !”
text:
From beginning to end our stay at The Waldorf was fabulous ! Our Superior room was spacious, clean and the bed very comfortable. This is an old hotel and the historical atmosphere is worth a walk through even if you don't want to stay.
If you love Art Deco you will love this place! The doormen were very helpful and friendly in getting us taxi's. As far as location, it can't be beat! I will be back the next time I come to NY.
Reserve The Sunday Brunch, you will not be disappointed! :)

name: Algonquin Hotel Times Square, Autograph Collection
title: “Hotel muy bueno en un sitio inmejorable”
text: El hotel nos encantó, es muy acogedor y la gente muy amable.Si es cierto que las habitaciones no son muy grandes, pero la cama es comodisima y todo el mobiliario es nuevo. La situacion del hotel es inmejorable! A 2 min andando de Time Square y poco más de Gran Central. Lo aconsejaria sin duda alguna.El hall del hotel es muy bonito, algunas noches cantan en directo con piano!!!

name: Hampton Inn 35th St. Empire State Building
title: “Proche de tous les sites et moyens de communication.”
text:
+ le sites plein coeur de Manhattna.
+le confort trés correct
+l'accés WiFi et internet gratuit
- Service peu sympatique :
-qui n'a pas accepté de réhaussé l'étage de notre chambre. De ce fait les nuits furent assez buyantes
-qui parceque nosu étions contranit de rester (nuage de cendre volanique) a augmenté le prix de la chambre de 90%
-Les chambres sont aussi petites qu'a Paris.

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “Enjoyed the Red Roof Inn Manhattan”
text: We stayed for 5 nights at the Red Roof Inn Manhattan and we really enjoyed it! The breakfast was great and we were able to get a table as long as we got there by 7:30 every morning. We were able to walk wherever we wanted pretty much from the location the hotel was in. The area felt safe no matter what time we were walking to or from the hotel. Our checkout process was very quick. We heard very little noise since we were up on the 13th floor. Our kids enjoyed the hotel as well.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Some good things and some not so good.”
text: As a former restaurateur, I know that going above and beyond expectations is what it takes to stand out above the competition, and the service at this hotel just did not stand out for me. Stayed one night. Requested an early check-in if possible. Arrived around 11AM, and clerk said no rooms were cleaned yet or available, which is understandable. So I checked my bag and simply asked desk clerk to call me when room was ready and took a walk. 3PM rolled around and no room and no call from desk clerk. I felt like he just forgot to call me. They also forgot my wake-up call. Maybe it was just me, but I detected a general tone of not caring to go out of their way to please guests like a $500+/night hotel should. On positive side, my room was clean and the bed was very comfortable. I recently stayed at a Ritz-Carlton, and asked to be called when my room was ready, and they did.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “perfect”
text: If you want to be close to everything in NYC then this is the hotel for you. Stayed with my wife, daughter(9) and sister in law. Right on Times Square, only one street away from the Roc, only 3 streets away from 5th Ave, right next to numerous shows Mama Mia, Wicked, Jersey Boys etc etc. We felt right in the heart of it. Hotel was lovely. Good reception, lovely lobby, exellent sun deck with outstanding views of the city, great place to sit at night with a drink after a hectic day, and the room was decent, for all that your in it. only complaint about the room was the shower head wasn't securely on the wall but apart from that exellent stay. Would definately go back!

name: Hilton New York
title: “Uitstekend verblijf”
text:
Uitstekende,vriendelijke service,
zeer confortabele geluidloze kamers (prachtig zicht vanuit het 42ste verdiep),
uitstekend ontbijt(gevarieerd aanbod).
Locatie is "top",dichtbij alle bezienswaardigheden op loopafstand,
metrostation vlakbij,taxi onmiddellijk te regelen voor de deur.
Voor tieners"The Apple store(24 uur open)","Time Square Place"op loopafstand,"Hard Rock café","Central Park","Bryant Park(gratis wifi)"...enz.
Verbleven als koppel met 3 tieners,
toffe buurt om te vertoeven dag en nacht!
Bij ons volgend bezoek is het terug ongetwijfeld de Hilton!!!

name: Dream Downtown
title: “Living my dream..”
text:
I discovered Dream hotel downtown last november. It felt like discovering a new star! Since i stepped in the lobby i started to understand why is it called The Dream..it s the first New York hotel i have stayed in that reminds me of the decadence of Las Vegas, in a better way! 
You don't need to go out to have fun! All you need is right there, one step away!
I had a nice room on the second floor and a nice bar and pool just at my door:) How cool is that?
 The hotel staff was warm and pro, but my guardian angel was Greta who couldn't say no for an answer!
 I spent more than a week at Dream's and i can say i was living my dream!
 No need to take a cab to go shopping when you have 14th str right there! J'adore Meatpacking District, the hottest area in Manhattan now!
 I can't wait to get back there!!!

name: Dream Downtown
title: “Dream downtown is a "dream" of luxury and beautiful decor.”
text: The staff was friendly from the doorman, front des to roomservice. My room was on the 2nd floor, (outdoor pool level) and was very nice. I am sure in the summer months it would be a very "hot" room to have with the parties and your access thru your sliding doors to the pool deck, but would probably be noisy with parties in the evening. Since I was there in December, no problem with that! The lobby was decorated fabulously with a lifesize polar bear, reindeer and lots of silver. Very nicely done! Great location to subway, restaurants, and shopping. Lots of "famous" people stay here, keep your eyes open!

name: Park South Hotel
title: “Highly recommended”
text: Ok so we were upgraded to a Junior Suite - but the room was BIG, very comfortable, huge bed, good bed linen, large sofa, coffee table etc. Service was acceptable. Our only complaint was one bath robe instead of two!! Now that's not bad! Was great to have breakfast thrown in and the subway station a 1 minute walk.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “New Yorker Hotel Feb 2012”
text:
Even though I made a booking online it still took at least 20 minutes (after queuing for 1/2hour) to get checked in.
The location around the hotel although in vicinity of Javit centre (about 15 minutes brisk walk) was a bit rundown, but it is close to a big station so that is expected.
The hotel was really nice but in a foregone era, now it needs refurbishment and upgrades. 
Don't include breakfast in your rate it is horrible, fatty and in a Route 66 restaurant open 24hrs (not sure when the clean) everything was always sticky!
The rooms was really small, even though we took one with a view (you could see the river if you checked carefully) so we upgraded to a bigger one which is more expensive but really just looking into other buildings.
The hotel is impersonal, big and extremely busy. Everything is charged extra, the rooms are old but clean. The bathrooms is really old, still with shower curtains (sorry I hate those)! Showers are inside an extremely small bath and very slippery.
The toiletpaper is located behind the door, and once you sit on the toilet you cant close the door you have to get up since the bathroom is so small. 
Definitely not for families, 
Maybe for a business person, the wireless was also very slow but at least for free!
I will not stay here again, for the price I found it really disappointing.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
Nice people attending the hotel, close to a subway station and walking-distance to the Central Park, Museum of Natural History and to many restaurants and bars at Columbus Street; nice rooms.
Just 2 things about my stay: No free WiFi Internet in the room only in the lobby, and there was noise due to a construction in front of the hotel.

name: Hampton Inn 35th St. Empire State Building
title: “Hôtel super sympa et très pratique!”
text:
A 25 pas de la bouche de métro 34th Herald Sq qui vous emmènera presque partout dans New York et à 4 minutes à pied de l'Empire State Building et de Macy's! Le personnel est super gentil et toujours prêt à donner un petit coup de main (garder les valises, petit déjeuner à emporter pour ceux qui ne veulent pas perdre de temps,...) et ils sont souriants! Les chambres étaient sympas, nous étions 3 dans une chambre de 4 et avions tout le confort nécessaire! les serviettes et produits de bain étaient bien changés tous les jours!
Tout ça pour un prix très bas je trouve...
Bref je recommande fortement et si j'ai la chance de revoir la Grosse Pomme, je retournerais à l'Hampton Inn!

name: Comfort Inn Manhattan
title: “There are probably better value budget hotels in the city”
text:
I was under no false illusions about this 2 star hotel and I would have rated it 3 stars but for some major issues which I consider essential when paying a four figure sum (in Stirling) for a 6 night stay. 
The good things about the hotel...
> Friendly reception staff 
> Free continental breakfast (not European though – food is from the American continent such was waffles and bagels)
> Good location 
The not so good...
> Very small double beds which are quite uncomfortable for two adults 
> No view whatsoever – in fact – I think the window had never been cleaned 
> Extremely noisy air con which meant a very noisy night or a very warm night 
The primary reason for my negative review is that when checking out of the hotel the Bell Boy/Doorman asked me if my family required a car for the airport and all that I needed to pay was a $10 deposit. I accepted the offer and was given back a receipt with a bill for $65 but the standard price for a NYC cab to JFK is only $45, furthermore, I could not cancel the car without losing the $10 deposit that I have just paid. It gets worse... on route to JFK the driver informed me that there was still TAX, tip and toll to pay which resulted in the final bill being nearly twice the amount of a standard cab fare.
The hotel and/or the Bell Boy/Doorman has some sort of deal in place with a private car company so book your own cab and if you do decide to stay in this small hot hotel.

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “Great Find Under $200”
text: Stayed at the Red Roof Inn in Manhattan near Korea Town and the Garment District for two nights August 9 and 10. The hotel is in a good location and a short walk to 6th avenue where one can catch the N,Q,R, W line. The simply furnished rooms and bathrooms are clean, and larger than most hotel rooms in the city, that I have paid $100 more for. The front desk staff was pleasant and accomodating, as was the bell staff. Although the hotel is located amidst the "hub-bub" of the city, there was surprisingly little noise at night. Maybe this was due to staying on the top floor. The Red Roof offers a free continental brekfast (rare in NYC) but unfortunately the other guests took full advantage of this and horded food like it was the last meal that they were going to eat. One woman had a huge plate of jelly donuts that she must have been saving for a snack later since I can't imagine anyone eating 6 donuts at one sitting. The guests filling the breakfast area were rude and pushy, and many did not have the common courtesy to clean up after themselves. Another drawback was that there was a sign posted that stated "All Food Musy Be Eaten on Premises". I have no idea what purpose that suits, and I refused to follow that rule after seeing so many guests that were rude and obnoxious. Overall, it was a good choice for the $172 per night.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Good value and location”
text: Location is great; short walk to 2 subway lines; easy stroll down Broadway to the heart of Times Square, and to other attractions such as Rockefeller Center. Many theaters nearby. Hotel lobby was classy and staff friendly. Room was clean and modern. We had one with "skyscraper views" on 31st floor and it had a great view looking west to Hudson River. Room size was not huge but was perfectly adequate. It seems many rooms in NYC come with 1 King bed, as did ours. Ask for a room with a sofa bed (no extra charge) if you have a child. Our 7-year old liked sleeping on that; not sure how well it would work with more than one kid; may depend on how old they are. They advertise that they are kid friendly and seemed to be. Many Europeans were there when we were. Overall, a very positive experience and an ideal base for our sightseeing.

name: Park South Hotel
title: “Trusted Staff”
text:
I just stayed at The Park South Hotel. While there I used the hotel room safe. Today someone called telling me I had forgetten my jewelry, credit cards, and other money inside the safe!!!! This was not costume jewelry, nor was it an insignificant amount of cash!! They called, told me they had everything that I had left and arrangements were mde to send all next day air!! AMAZING!! While it was not only a nice small hotel, close to New York City's garment district, the rooms were adequate in size and newly furnished.Also a free European breakfast each day that lasted until 10 am each day. 
This hotel is a gem, location great. Between midtown and Gramercy Park.
Thank you Park South for being in the top of all hotels to call a guest and report valuables that were left!
Karen V.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Sleepless in On the Ave - Aug 15, 2012”
text:
Visited New York for business and pleasure and wanted to stay in a hotel close to Central Park. Unfortunately, I didn't read the reviews about the construction noise at on the Ave until I had already made my final plans. When I checked in I asked for a room on a high floor and in the back away from the construction. Construction is going on at the Hotel with scaffolding all around building and their building a new structure across the street. So at 7am I was greeted with a construction worker looking at me and drilling right outside my window. Not a pleasant start to your day. Additionally, the bed was as hard as a brick. I don't think I've ever been to a hotel with a bed that had no give. You could literally bounce a coin off the covers. My hip and back hurt me the next morning. To add insult it injury, the tub did not drain out so when taking my shower I was standing in dirty water up to my shins. Three strikes and you're out. I had to get out of that hotel. Those are all the cons.
Pros - The location is great. The staff was very polite and apologetic. The manager on duty was understanding and helpful. When I advised all the issues and that I wanted to leave she agreed to a late check-out of 1pm, comped my room rate by $50 and did not penalize me for early checkout. I really appreciated that. 
If you want a good night's sleep in a comfortable bed don't book On the Ave. You will wake up to jack hammers in your head.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Muy Bueno”
text: Excelente organización. Tiene todo lo necesario para una excelente estadía.

name: Comfort Inn Manhattan
title: “it's OK”
text: Posizione centralissima, praticamente attaccato alla metro e alle spalle dell'empire state building, a 10 min da time square e dal madison square garden (da noi particolarmente frequentato). La nostra camera non era molto grande, ma gli spazi erano ben organizzati: svariati cassetti, cabina armadio capiente. Per il poco che siamo stati in camera non ci siamo mai lamentati di questo. Molto riscaldata, forse fin troppo (siamo stati in marzo, ma le temperature esterne erano veramente basse). La colazione non era proprio indimenticabile, ma per chi, come noi, era in corsa fin dal mattino, fa risparmiare tempo e denaro (why not?) Il personale è un pò "freddo" per lo standard di NY, informazioni centellinate e talvolta pure il saluto sembrava uno sforzo. Ma non importa molto! Nell'insieme consiglio vivamente… VIVA NYC

name: JW Marriott Essex House New York
title: “not so great stay”
text: We booked a junior suite with a connecting double bed room. Room connected only through an outside hallway door and not directly. With one child sleeping in the other room and my husband leaving early for business, it wasn't safe to leave her there so four of us slept in one room. Double bed room had a complete view of pipes. Location is great for Central Park and we walked daily to Rockefeller Center, 5th Avenue shops. The service is great, but I didn't like their lobby setting in which there's no where to just relax. For breakfast we were supposed to receive breakfast vouchers for everyday for all of us due to our Silver Sirius card holder status. But the vouchers were for continental breakfast and a hot breakfast was $15 more/person. Sometimes the server would charge us for 2 people only since the other 3 where children and other times for 5 people. And every time we brought the vouchers they had to go ask someone because they hadn't seen them before. A real hassle. There's no coffee making facilities in the room and we had a tough time finding glasses to drink water from. It was never hard to get a taxi anywhere because the doormen were very efficient. Always greeted with a smile everywhere you go. Sofa bed in junior suite was not comfortable because of the springs and we ended up putting in on the floor. I guess for almost $1000/night it just wasn't worth all the problems. Their price is reasonable for Manhattan, however, and if you have the money to spend on room service and extras, then stay here.

name: Comfort Inn Manhattan
title: “Hotel med frukost”
text: Ett suveränt hotell mitt på Manhattan. En av de få hotellen i New York där det serveras frukost. Mysiga restauranger runt om i krokarna. Ligger precis bakom Empire Stae Building. Perfekt läge om man vill se New York gåendes. Det tog ca 1 tim att gå till Central Park. Därefter tog vi vägen via China Town och Little Italy. Kan varmt rekomenderas

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Top hotel, centraal gelegen.”
text: Ligging van het Hotel is top, lekker centraal gelegen, vlak bij times square en 5th avenue. Jammer dat er geen minibar/koelkastje op de kamer was. Op de gang kon je wel gratis ijsblokjes ophalen en in je wijnkoeler doen. Zwembad was er ook niet, had wel fijn geweest na een dag flink te voet NY verkennen. Verder was de TV ontvangst niet echt van beste kwaliteit, maar ja ben er niet om de hele dag tV te kijken.

name: 414 Hotel
title: “Great value, location -- would definitely go back!”
text: I booked in at the 414 because I had tickets to a Broadway show in winter, and wanted to be able to walk to the theater in case the weather was bad. However, I didn't want to stay in a Times Sq. mega-hotel, so the 414 was perfect. It's just 2 blocks from all the theaters, but has the charm of a European city small hotel. The decor is contemporary, sheets & towels clean & soft, nice bathroom and comfortable bed. Continental breakfast featured delicious mini-bagels & croissants. We arrived well before check-in at 3:00, but the friendly & helpful staff let us store our luggage without a problem, and offered to call when our room was ready, which turned out to be 12:30. For $168/night, I would go back in a flash, but next time would request a room in their back building, which gives onto a quiet courtyard, and not the surprisingly busy W. 46th St. (looks quietly residential, but lots of horses in the morning!). Also, might not go back in dead of winter, as there was more heat than I needed (it's an all-or-nothing situation with the boiler), but this was in no way a deal-breaker. A great find!

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Efficient business hotel”
text:
Great location for business downtown. The rooms are quite large for NY and the bathroom is modern. The best part was that we had a spare afternoon before the flight and the concierge was able to suggest the perfect tour so that I finally managed to see some of NY. 
Gym is brand new and quite well equiped for a hotel

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Loved the Waldorf”
text:
We just got back from our stay at the Waldorf. We stayed for 3 nights and I had booked a deluxe room. Upon check in I asked for an upgrade and was granted a Superior room! (always ask for an upgrade!) The room was beautiful! The AC was not working well and they switched our room the next day to another Superior room. The staff is wonderful. We ate at the Peacock Alley for breakfast. I do not recommend eating there. Our bill was $150 for breakfast and if I am going to pay that much for breakfast it better be made by a top chef and it better be fantastic. It was not. The next day we went a 1/2 block away to a New York diner and ate a great breakfast for $25. There is a Starbucks in the hotel, but it is more expensive then regular Starbucks. I recommend going around the corner to Starbucks, much cheaper. 
All in all it was great!

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Wowzers! What an incredible place to stay on the weekends!”
text:
3 friends and I stayed here over Halloween weekend in 2008 and had an absolute blast. (NYC is a hoot over Halloween, btw!) Staying in the financial district on the weekends is very cheap, and this hotel is just a block or two from countless subway stops. You're also walking distance to Battery Park if you're playing tourist and plan on visiting the Statue of Liberty. 
The rooms are absolutely gorgeous and staying on the 29th floor had incredible views of the river and the World Trade Center site (the hotel goes well above 50 or 60 floors). The pullout sofa and bed were incredibly comfortable, the housekeeping staff was very attentive, and the flat screen tvs in each room were a great perk. For less than $300 each night, you can't beat this in NYC!

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Soggiorno fantastico”
text:
Ho alloggiato presso l'Hyatt hotel dal primo all'undici Agosto,è stato un soggiorno meraviglioso,il personale è molto disponibile.Hai qualsiasi cosa ti possa servire nell'hotel stesso:ufficio postale,ristoranti,negozi ecc..La posizione è perfetta,puoi arrivare da qualsiasi parte a manhattan in pochi minuti a piedi.Secondo me è il posto migliore dove stare in tutta manhattan e a nyc ovviamente.La stanza è spaziosa e pulita.
Lo raccomando senza dubbio a tutti.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Meh...”
text: The lobby of this hotel was absolutley gorgeous and the prices were high...I must say that I was expecting a lot more. Even though it a "chic" hotel, you should really get what you pay for. Every time I walked into the room after a long day at the Javits center, the room smelt. From cleaners or something else I have no idea, but it smelt like toilet water. I had expected a much more luxurious room for may $500/night. I must confess my dissapointment, and the breakfast was not very good even though it was outrageously over priced.

name: Dream Downtown
title: “The best around”
text: The hotel was hip and the service was beyond extraordinary. After check-in, the staff called me by name every time I came into the lobby or needed a cab, making me feel welcome and as if I was a part of a large, extended family. Lots of restaurant, coffee house and bakeries within walking distance, as was the subway. A beautiful hotel, in a great location, with guest services outranking some of the best luxury hotels worldwide? Why stay anywhere else? I won't. To top it off, the beds were incredible, providing a great nights sleep.

name: Broadway Plaza Hotel
title: “Broadway Plaza Hotel di New York - posizionato in centro e vicino a metro e bus”
text: Ottima posizione, 50 metri dalla metro e 100 metri dal bus sulla quinta avenue. Time square si può raggiungere con 15 min a piedi. Attorno all'hotel dopo le 7 di sera è tutto chiuso, ma ciò rende la zona silenziosa. Per strada anche la sera è comunque tranquillo e sicuro. Le stanze sono ampie, pulite, funzionali. C'è anche una cassaforte, phon e tv. La colazione è in una piccola saletta, the, caffè e spremuta d'arancia erogati da una macchinetta, da mangiare ciambelle e muffins. Per il tempo che si passa in albergo non si può chiedere di più. In portineria c'è chi è più gentile e chi meno, tra i più disponibili un portiere di origine napoletana.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Wonderful hotel”
text: An amazing wonderful hotel in the middle of Manhatten. Great bigg rooms, a great hotell staff. They let us have the room 3 hours longer with no fee. There were several diners close to the hotel, who had great breakfast. Times Square and Central park are both close to the hotel. I will definatly stay here again.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Great short break over Xmas”
text:
Located in a great position in new york within easy reach to times square etc. Great spot.
Service great considering how busy the place was at this time of year, rooms decent and no cause for complaint. Would definitely recommend to anyone looking to stay for a new York break. Could probably do with a bit of a makeover to update some of the look and feel to make it more modern but it certainly does the job.

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “We will be back!”
text:
We stayed here in August 2003. Hotel is in a great location - small town Korea. A street filled with Korean shops and fantastic Korean restaurants a great cultural experience. Rooms feature new furnishings and are VERY clean. Easy walking distance to most major attractions. 
Empire state just around the corner. Continental breakfast of bagels, donuts and cereal were perfect for a weekend away. Next we are in New York this is where we will be staying.

name: Park South Hotel
