title: “Affreux”
text: Notre chambre donnait sur la cour intérieure. Nous étions au premier étage et donc avec une vue directe sur le climatiseur. Le bruit horrible nous donnait l'impression continue d'être dans l'ambiance sonore d'une usine. Seul point positif, la chambre nous a été attribuée dès notre arrivée à 9h, et le personnel était sympathique. Le petit déjeuner était très moyen. Il faut jouer des coudes pour avoir une table sale. La rue en été a le doux parfum des ordures. Un quartier très très sale.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Theatre district”
text:
Great location to walk from. Spent hours out and about. A bit startled by the entrance first night when I arrived late, but the hotel turned out to be fine and the staff were all very helpful.
Everything in NY seemed expensive but I suppose this was good value for what and where it was located. Would use it again. Thanks!

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Loved it!”
text: I stayed here for 4 days in Jan, and it was the best hotel i have ever stayed in. The room was so big, bigger than i taught it would be. The bed was so comfortable and soft. Location is great, staff are really friendly and helpful. I would never stay any where else, and rates are great, i booked through their own website. Defo going back here again, would not look anywhere else, and i have been recommending it to all my friends.

name: Grand Hyatt New York
title: “Spitzenlage!”
text: Dieses Hotel war eigentlich nicht unsere erste Wahl - aber es hat hat uns letztendlich sehr gut gefallen. Da wir Ostern und außerdem Spring Break Holidays hatten, war es sehr voll im Hotel. Das war aber nicht wirklich störend, da Gedränge ja doch auch zu New York gehört. Die Zimmer waren ausreichend groß, obwohl wir mit drei Erwachsenen dort waren. Es wurde jeden Tag ordentlich geputzt, aber auch bei uns blieb Abfall und Sonstiges auf den Fluren Ewigkeiten stehen. Der Concierge war immer sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit, obwohl es dort immer extrem voll war. Die Lage ist das Beste am ganzen Hotel! Direkt - wirklich direkt! - neben der Grand Central Station mit besten Frühstücksmöglichkeiten, z. B. bei "dishes" und "Juniors". Ich würde auf jeden Fall dort wieder übernachten. Alles in allem ein guter deal was Preis/Leistung angeht!

name: Blue Moon Hotel
title: “Perfect Fit”
text:
How difficult is it to find a nice room for a family of 4 when the kids are teenagers and want their own bed? Many parents know what I'm talking about. The Blue Moon was our answer and turned out to be a Perfect Fit for our family.
The Blue Moon Hotel is an old tenement building that has been renovated very well. We booked a "Comfort Room" which was a nice 375 square feet equiped with a queen bed, a sofa bed and a pull out trundle. Both the sofa bed and trundle were very comfortable - not the folding type with springs and thin matresses. In addition to the full private bath, the room had an extra sink - very nice touch when four are sharing one bathroom. We were on the front of the building and slept with windows open. We could hear some street noise but this is to be expected and did not bother us at all.
The Lower East Side location worked well for us. Ours was a sightseeing vacation for shows and museums. We took full advantage of the close by metro stops - an easy walk from the hotel. In addition, we enjoyed the local choice of restaurants instead of the hectic hustle of Times Square. We were one block from Chinatown and also had easy walks to find great Italian and Indian food.
Staff at the Blue Moon are all friendly and accomodating. Bagels and coffee every morning and a glass of wine in the evening are all very nice touches. 
I highly recommend for any type of traveler who wants to be closer to a neighborhood experience instead of the commercial skyscraper hotels further uptown. We will definately return.

name: Club Quarters World Trade Center
title: “Convenient location and very safe!”
text: This hotel is located right at ground 0. I had mixed feelings about the location but I'm glad I went. It's a new property (in 2012), and very comfortable. All the usual Club Quarters amenities, bottled water, free wifi etc. Crowds at the Memorial mean good security also. It was wonderful weather so it was nice to walk around, and it's a short walk to Battery park. Depending on where you need to be, it was really great and the price was excellent.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Our new home in Manhattan!”
text: My husband and I went to New York for the second time on Memorial Day weekend. We stayed at OTA last year and had a lovely experience. This year, we booked to stay at another hotel near Times Square. We were so disappointed with the hotel near Times Square that we called OTA to see if they had room for us. They did and we were welcomed with warm, genuine and professional staff when we arrived . Knowing that we came from Times Square and wanted a quiet room, they booked us away from the renovations that they are undergoing. We were upgraded from a regular room to a superior room because we were returning guests. Our room was clean, quiet and comfortable. The neighborhood is delightful and it was so much fun to explore. We felt very safe as it is a residential neighborhood. OTA is only two short blocks from the subway and a quick subway ride to Times Square and other attractions. A big thanks to the staff at OTA, we will be back next Memorial Day! This will be our new home away from home in Manhattan. We would highly recommend this hotel for anyone travelling to New York City.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Not impressed!”
text: I booked this Hotel as it looked very nice on the website. I e-mailed the Hotel to let them know I needed a twin room away from the lifts, preferbly in the corner. To my disappointment, we got a double bed, next to the lift and in front of the construction work so did not sleep at all. The staff told us they were fully booked so could not give us another room and totally ignored the fact that I had got an email confirmation saying we would get a twin room. I asked them what time the construction work would finish, and they said at 10pm! well, this went on the WHOLE night so they lied to us. I was extremely disappointed with their attitude, the standard of the Hotel and lack of knowledge. I would never recommend this Hotel to anyone.

name: Club Quarters World Trade Center
title: “Nice place to stay, good location”
text: This was my first time staying here and overall thought the experience was nice. I didn't stay in my hotel too long because I was busy doing outdoor things. We had 3 people in our room so we had to get a superior room with kitchenette. The bed was a good sized bed, nice pillows, and the carpet was clean. The sofa bed that we were promised looked smaller than we anticipated. It looked like a normal one person armchair. However, when you took out the seat cushion, it revealed a twin sized bed good enough for the third person in our group. He said it was pretty comfortable to sleep on as well. One thing I didn't like was the sliding door for the bathroom. It didn't lock and didn't close all the way for complete privacy. At night, I didn't hear any commotion or people walking around. It was very quiet and we all had good rest. Best thing was the noon checkout. It gave us enough time to pack our belongings and check out without feeling rushed.

name: 414 Hotel
title: “414 charming & lovely”
text:
We stayed at the 414 September 27 - October 1 2006. It was exactly what we had hoped and expected based on the posotive reviews from this website and a few more.
We did not want to spend a huge amount of money for acco
modations (because everything else is so expensive in NYC) but we did want something clean & comfy. Since there are no elevators we requested the first floor. Our room was small but exceptionally clean. The bathroom was actually quite large.
Each room had a mini fridge which came in handy.
A small, charming courtyard was right outside our room and we ate out there almost every morning and enjoyed a few beers and some wine & cheese after a long day of sightseeing.
There is a small kitchenette in the lobby with a microwave, sink, fridge. We ate breakfast at the 414 every morning. Cereal, fresh croissants, fresh huge muffins, bagels, cream cheese, butter etc.
coffee (wonderful!) juice, milk. I picked up fresh fruit from one of the several markets very close to the 414 to have at breakfast.
Loved the down pillows on the bed. .....rare for any hotel to provide down pillows. Staff was very courteous.
If you are looking for a large chain hotel feeling than the 414 is not for you. The 414 does have a very European feel. 
We loved the location, convenient to everything but a off the main drag a bit and also felt very safe.
I would stay at this hotel again & recommend it.

name: 414 Hotel
title: “Nice little hotel”
text:
My girlfriend and I stayed here for 4 nights at the end of April. It is in a great location, only 5 minutes walk to all the restaurants and about 10 to Times Square. The rooms are not very big but that wasn't a problem as we did not come to New York to stay in our room. The bed was comfortable and there is a widescreen plasma tv on the wall with plenty of cable channels.
 Continental breakfast is included but this is pretty basic. You eat in a very small dining area close to the reception. There is a small kitchen where you can help yourself to cookies, muffins, bagels and croissants etc. There is also a kettle if you want tea or coffee and a selection of fruit juices.
 The receptionists were helpful but it was only Mike who seemed to go out of his way to help you and recommend places to eat and also to give directions.
 There is a computer next to the dining area if you need to use the internet and this is free to use.
 The bedrooms were cleaned daily and this was done to a high standard. We had no complaints about this. The hotel was quiet and we were never disturbed during the night. 
 We both recommend this hotel and if we return to New York we will stay here again.

name: Blue Moon Hotel
title: “Great New York Experience”
text: This is the place to stay if you are looking for an authentic New York experience. The hotel is unlike any place I have ever stayed. The archetecture is authentic and it works to make itself a part of the neighborhood. The staff is unbelievably helpful. Paul, the night manager, was always available with anything we needed. Be sure to look at the art in the lobby. The owner painted it himself.

name: Blue Moon Hotel
title: “Great Hotel in Colourful Area”
text:
We spent 4 days in New York and wanted to stay in an area with character- Blue Moon in Lower Eastside is perfect. 
The hotel is friendly and staff are very helpful (a particular thanks to Paul!) and the rooms are full of character. NIce breakfast with fresh bagels from round the corner. You're only blocks away from Chinese, Vietnamese residential and market/ restaurant areas and Little Italy's only a couple of blocks further away. 5min walk to train to take you to Times Square or wherever....half hour walk to Finance/World Trade areas or Greenwich Village/Soho. You really are in an exciting area but still close to cosmopolitan stuff.
If you're interested in the history of successive waves of immigration, check out the Tenement Museum which is literally next door. Guides will take to round tenement flats just as they would have been in 1880, 1930, etc.
Give up those chain hotels and try as slice of life in real New York.

name: Blue Moon Hotel
title: “Fabulous hotel on lower east side - clean, friendly, fun”
text: This hotel was one of our favorites ever! Away from the hustle and bustle of times square and mid-town, the Blue Moon is fun and low-key. You are greeted with wine and a smile when you walk into the lobby and always feel welcome. It is only a few blocks from Little Italy and Chinatown and the hip/trendy hangouts on Ludlow. The rooms are nice and clean, good sized (we stayed in a comfort room - the Abbott and Costello) and comfortable. We recommend the nearby restaurants Tre (Ludlow St), Il Cortile (Mulberry St in Little Italy) and The Nolita House on Houston (near Mulberry) for Bluegrass Brunch. We look forward to going back!

name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Times Square
title: “Average Stay for an Average Hotel”
text: Room was small and the restroom smelled of mildew. The hotel was in a decent area and a few blocks from time square, about a fifteen minute walk at a moderate pace. There was a great deli near the hotel that had the most amazing black and white cookies.

name: Broadway Plaza Hotel
title: “empfehlenswert”
text: sehr gute zentrale lage, zimmergröße und größe des badezimmers für manhatten hotels sehr gut. frühstück und frühstücksraum kann man vergessen. sauberkeit und room service wirklich ok. die geschäfte rund um das hotel herabgekommen, aber man ist zu fuß gleich beim time sqare und fifth av. minus: preis für sept. hoch

name: Hilton New York Fashion District
title: “Lovely but so small!”
text:
I was upgraded to a room with a king bed: it is a good thing I was alone. The room was very small. There would not have been enough space for two travelers with one suitcase each.
But all in all, clean, comfortable, if a little too cozy.

name: Hilton New York Fashion District
title: “Great service”
text:
We stayed for 3 nights in June 2012 in double beds room. Hotel has been refurbished so bathroom and room conditions were like new. Very good value for money through online booking.
Very good service throughout. Cudos to hotel manager Martha Vargas for her patience and great smile while going the extra mile to help me fix my printing/scanning problems.
We will be back for sure.

name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel
title: “RELACION CALIDAD PRECIO EXCELENTE”
text:
Esta muy bien situado, desde la ventana veiamosel Empire state y el edificio Chrisler.
tiene WIFI gratis el desayuno es bastante aceptable y te puedes tomar un cafe o chocolate a cualquier hora, ya que tienen maquina gratuita..
Ls habitaciones no son excesivamente grandes pero a NY no se va a aestar en la habiatcion.
El servicio de limpieza de las habitaciones es muy eficaz,

name: Broadway Plaza Hotel
title: “Hotel sympathique”
text: Hotel bien situé au centre de Manhattan, proche des métros. Personnels de l'hôtel très sympathique et prévenant. Quartier un peu particulier mais sans risques.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Great Experience at OTA”
text:
My husband and I traveled to NYC for our 'first time' visit on March 17th of this year. Our son and daughter-in-law made us our reservation through trip advisor when we called them on our way into the city that day. When we arrived at OTA, we were greeted by the friendly, competent staff. Joana, our telephone contact at the hotel, actually talked to us the last 30 minutes of our trip, guidling us through the busy St. Patrick's Day crowd right to our destination. Robert, another friendly, helpful young man went above and beyond to help us when we ran into a slight problem in retrieving our car from the parking garage. 
The hotel was clean, the price reasonable, close to Central Park and meto access. All in all, the staff made our one night, New York City stay a pleasant experience. We have reccomended OTA to our son and his wife whenthey too travel to this great city!

name: Broadway Plaza Hotel
title: “Spitzen Ausgangspunkt”
text: Das Hotel war für ein idealer Ausgangspunkt zur Erkundung des Big Apple, den die nächste Subway-Station ist nur eine Straße weiter und die nächste nur zwei Straßen. Der Broadway ist Up- & Downtown zu Fuß entdeckbar. Man hat hier zwar den Eindruck, dass die Gegend in der sich Hotel befindet, sehr multikulturell und nicht gerade positiv entwickelt, aber der Eindruck täuscht!! Denn wenn man erst den Charme der kleinen, einfachen Läden kennengelernt hat, kann man von Ramsch über Elektronik bis hin zu floralen Kunstwerken alles bekommen. Der Trubel und die Größe der bekannten Kaufhäuser und Einkaufsmeilen hat danach eine andere Bedeutung. Die Mitarbeiter am Empfang und die Concierge waren top im Service. Das Frühstück beschränkte sich allerdings auf Süßes, aber gibt einen Kraft für die ersten Schritte am Tag. Der Kaffee ist amerikanisch, aber zu jeder Zeit zu haben und auch "to go". Das Zimmer war zweckmäßig, geräumig und vorallem immer sauber. Je höher die Zimmer auf der Broadwayseite gelegen sind, desto besser kann man das Empire sehen.

name: Club Quarters World Trade Center
title: “Best Club Quarters I've stayed at”
text:
I've been to a lot of Club Quarters as part of my business travel. They are usually cramped rooms with very few amenities in the hotel, earning them the unofficial nickname "Club Closet". This one breaks the mold. The rooms are actually fairly large by NYC standards.
The hotel is pretty new, so that's probably a big part of why it seems so nice. The lobby has a great lounge area, with cappuccino machine, newspapers, magazines, TV, internet stations and ample seating. On the roof they have an open and airy restaurant, which has a bar for the evening and breakfast buffet in the morning. There is also a rooftop patio to lounge in the warmer months, or just get a good view of the surrounding area.
If you are planning to visit the 9/11 memorial, you can get much closer than this. In fact you can see the hotel in the pictures on the memorial website (http://www.911memorial.org/explore-memorial, it's the white building in the back left of the photo). Our room faced the memorial, which is lit up at night. I do strongly suggest visiting it, the tickets are free.
If you are driving in, I suggest using the parking lot they are affiliated with, which is on Albany St a block away. If you "self park" it's $37/day, compared to the $50 or so at other garages. They will also bill the charge directly to your room. You can find the address for the garage on the directions page of the Club Quarters website. When you get there, it looks closed, but if you tell the guard you are staying at Club Quarters he will remove the various security measures and let you in. 
I probably shouldn't let out the secret, but unlike most NYC hotels, the room rate at the Club Quarters actually DROPS on the weekend. They get most of their business during the week from business travelers, and so the weekend is pretty dead. As part of their business model though your company needs to be a member in order to make a reservation here. But if you know someone whose company is a member, they can make a reservation for you.
I'd definitely stay at this hotel again.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Nice Hotel in Busy Times Square Location”
text: The Belvedere Hotel is great for it's modest rates. The rooms are some of the largest I have witnessed in NYC. The lobby is grand and staff helpful. Our room was clean and comfortable. Bath products are also excellent! A couple of things to point out...it bugs me that many nice hotels still insist on trying to charge high prices for internet when budget places offer it complimentary. The area is very very busy. Outside the hotel is a constant line of traffic trying to get into the immediate Times Square area. The cabs have a very annoying habit of blasting the horn as soon as the light turns green even if they are 15 cars back! There is also a NYFD station on 8th and 47th which can obviously be noisy if they get a call out. Both these issues where made worse because we were unable to keep our windows closed as the heating in our room was "all or nothing" according to hotel maintenance. The only way to regulate a moderate temperature was too keep the windows cracked all night and enjoy the sounds of the city! The water temp of the shower also reflected this all or nothing condition going from scalding to freezing with out warning. Despite these couple points we had a pleasant stay and think the Belvedere is one of the better hotels in this location, especially for the price.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Excellent!”
text: Great position.....great staff...we had a penthouse suite - 2 balconies! We will definitely stay here again when returning to NY!

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Don't hesitate to stay at the Waldorf.”
text: It is the great old lady of New York and one should stay there at least once. The Hotel is really great, the lobby is a time warp to a wonderful art deco past, it is warm and pleasant. The rooms are big and at times the view is simply spectacular. I find them very clean (been at the Waldorf 7 or 8 times) ,big, very smart and the Waldorf people are always eager to please their guest.It position is a very big plus as one is within walking distance from all major attractions and best shopping in town. The Bull and Bear and the Inagiku restaurants are good altho' expensive but i feel they worth it.If asked whether you would like to take the upgrade option do not hesitate!!!It is worth it.

name: JW Marriott Essex House New York
On The Ave Hotel
title: “Great Choice!”
text: I spent 3 nights in this nice hotel. At the check in everyone was very helpful, they provided us an upgrade to a corner room with several windows, they later called me to check if everything in the room was ok. The room was just as pictured, the room and bathroom with a modern touch. Yes, there is some noise from the contruction across the street but not big deal for us. The neighborhood is very nice. Loved the "Shake and Shack" burgers two blocks away.

name: Broadway Plaza Hotel
title: “für den Preis in Ordnung”
text: im südlichen Mid-Town gelegen, das Hotel hatte bestimmt schon bessere Tage, aber alles sauber, Hantücher täglich frisch,Frühstück Beagels, Kaffee, Saft. sehr kleiner Frühstücksraum-4Tische- Gegend ist etwas trostlos, viele Billig-Läden, aber man ist schnell am Times-Square und Theaterviertel, kann man laufen, Subway nur ein Block

name: The Belvedere
title: “As good as we remembered!”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Belvedere for eight nights from the 4th-11th September 2010, this was our second visit to New York City and because we'd had such a positive experience on our honeymoon in 2007 we decided to stay there again. The location is perfect, walking distance to Times Square, Theatre District, Central Park and main subway lines but we walked to the Empire State Building and down to Greenwich Village from the hotel so I would say if you wanted to explore the city on foot it is an ideal place to stay. Our room was large, spacious and clean, the kitchen area was good as the weather was so warm during our stay, it was nice too have some cold water (and beer) in the fridge for when returned each day. On our first day we had an issue with the tap in bath dripping, which was resolved the same day. We also had some noisy neighbours our first night, which I'm sure you can imagine is not what we wanted after flying in from London that day, but I called down to the concierge at 4.00am to say we were hearing a lot of noise from the people in the room next door and someone came up immediately to ask them to keep it down. Our neighbours throughout the rest of our stay were more thoughtful! The staff were friendly and helpful, the only downside for us was the price of the breakfasts within the hotel as they were fairly expensive when we stayed in 2007 but the price had increased by a couple of bucks this time around. We had breakfast at the hotel on our first morning, every other day we went to a nearby Applebees or the Brasserie across the street. On the whole though, a fantastic hotel and we'd definitely stay there again.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Fantastic Hotel with city views......”
text:
Booked this hotel for 7 nights (27th Dec to 3rd Jan) after reading the reviews on trip advisor......
Our room was a King Bed room on the 33rd Floor with City views ( inc. WTC site ) Yes it does get a bit noisy daytime, but NYC is noisy all the time. AirCon fan was noisy, but liveable ( others have said the same ) but the 42" Plasma TV worked fine. Room was always spotlessly cleaned and the service was faultless.
It is a bit 'Downtown' for most of NYC's attractions, but the cab rides were on average $15 (inc. tip ), the most we paid was $25 from Times square to the hotel in rush hour. When you've paid about $250 a night.... you can live with that.....
Mostly had 'breakfast' in Starbucks, round the corner.
Had room service breakfast on our last morning and it was OK. ( $40 all in )
Don't use the hotel phone to ring the UK, about £7.50 for 2-3 mins...!!!!
Overall impressed enough to go back again soon........
Times Square NewYearsEve was a one-off experience..........
Easily got a cab back to the hotel at 1am NewYearsDay and it cost.........$12+tip..........only in NYC........ :o)

name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Times Square
title: “A comfortable stay with no frills”
text:
I stayed here for 2 nights to attend a conference nearby. While I did not get to do any sightseeing in NYC, I found the location to be ideal. It is only a few minutes walk to Times Square and many great restaurants in midtown. The hotel is on a safe street, while being very quiet at night. My room didn't have any view to speak of (next building), but I had no street noise from the 7th floor.
The room was small, but that's to be expected from a hotel of this price range in NYC. I had stayed at a few HGI's in Manhattan and the room size is comparable. My room had a King bed and a work desk with plenty of space to move around. The wardrobe had plenty of hangers. The bathroom was adequate.
I didn't have much time to have breakfast, but it was nice to get a cup of coffee, pastry and fruit and get on my way. The staff at the breakfast area was very helpful. The reception staff was courteous and always proactive about my needs--asked me if I needed a late check-out (as a Gold member), a map, a taxi, luggage storage, etc, before I asked. I especially want to thank the young lady who escorted me to an ATM machine next door when the machine in the lobby wasn't working. She could have just told me where to go, but she showed me the way. It took 2 minute of her time but a small gesture like this makes an impression on me!
With all this said, I'm taking one point off because of the elevator. No, not because there are only 2, I never waited more than a couple minutes for one. The building is very narrow and tall, much like many hotels in Manhattan, so all the rooms are fairly close to the elevator. This meant hearing the dings of the elevators all day long... and all night long. Needless to say, this prevented me from falling asleep at night. If you are sensitive to noise, I'd recommend bringing some ear plugs. I always request rooms away from the elevator, but in this type of building, there are no such rooms.

name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Times Square
title: “Don't do it!”
text:
We waited 15 minutes for the elevator when we checked in and 20 minutes on our way out. We missed the free breakfast that ended at 10 while we waited.. The rooms are tiny and the shower curtain smelled disgusting. 
Do not do it to yourself- it is not worth the money.

name: Hilton New York Fashion District
title: “Winter Weekend in NYC”
text:
The Hilton Fashion District is a relatively small hotel for a Hilton brand. It's in a great location, 6 blocks from Penn Station and right in Chelsea. Being that I spend most of my time in Chelsea- south - it was nice to be able to walk most places.
The hotel staff is attentive. The lobby and rooms are modern. The lobby is very small so it's not a pleasant place to wait for your room to by ready (mine was ready at 2pm). 
I selected (and paid slightly more for) a high-floor room. I had a nice view of the Empire State Building but it's not worth more than $10 a night more. 
The rooms are small, but it is NYC, but they are comfy. King bed, large TV, nice desk space, good temperature control. There is a neat "bar" cabinet that holds the Keurig coffee maker (nice touch) and space for goodies (ie. vodka, snacks, etc.) that you may bring with you or run out and purchase. 
One downside that wasn't as bad as I thought was there are NO ice machines. You have to call room service. There is no charge (except tip) but I prefer to get my own ice and get it as often as I'd like. Not a huge deal but eh. 
The bathrooms are a nice size for NYC. With nice showers (with good shower heads) and a nice large vanity. 
The only other thing I did not like was they only had small table-top ironing boards in the room. They definitely could fit a regular (albeit smaller) ironing board hanging on the wall in the closet. It was very hard to iron on the bed and on the bathroom vanity (I tried both).
All-in-all, this is a great hotel if you can get a decent price. I would definitely stay here again.
p.s. the restaurant, Rare, that is in the hotel is VERY good - at least the cobb salad I had (and the dishes my friends had) was excellent! The menu looked super yummy and the room service menu was good too and decently priced (although I didn't partake).

name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Times Square
title: “Great place to stay.”
text: Good price, comfortable room great location. This place is in a great location close to Times Square and has plenty of great places to eat close by. Have heard alot about the slow elavators but they have been very fast during my stay. If I visit NYC again I would definitely stay here again.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Elegant, clean, convenient...”
text:
We chose this hotel as one of several offered with an Amtrak vacation package to New York because it looked more interesting than the offerings from the major chains. Even though the (new to us) travel agent erroneously booked us into a room with two double beds, the desk staff had was gracious and able to accommodate us with a single king room. 
Because of media reports regarding bed bugs and NYC in general we were very concerned about this prior to our vacation. We found no evidence of them and indeed came away with no bites. The room and the bathroom were very clean on check-in and were kept well during our brief stay.
This hotel is convenient to the theater district and close enough to Times Square to be easily walkable but far enough that you aren't in its hub-bub 24/7. Our room was a great size and the bed was very comfortable.
The only downgrade I have is that the two elevators can be slow and because it's an older hotel they are a bit small. Otherwise, an great stay.

name: Park South Hotel
title: “Une bonne adresse”
text: Hôtel très bien situé, chambre petite mais très propre. Peignoir à disposition ainsi que des produits de beauté de qualité. Métro tout proche. Petit déjeuner buffet copieux et varié. Seul ennui le bruit de la soufflerie.. dommage !

name: 414 Hotel
title: “Amazing Little Hotel!”
text:
We couldn't have found a place better than the 414 Inn to stay! Located in a residential neighborhood of Hell's Kitchen, it is within walking distance to nearly everything. We were a few blocks from Times Square, Broadway, Rockefeller Center, Central Park, almost everything! There are plenty of places to eat and shop in the area too!
The staff are most helpful, are available 24 hours a day, give great directions, and have great advice for sightseeing and places to eat. The rooms are fabulous (ours was on the 4th floor), extremely comfortable, and always kept clean. My only note to travelers is that if you cannot go up and down stairs, request a first floor room when making your reservation, as the hotel does not have an elevator. 
Staying at this little bed and breakfast was one of the best decisions of our entire trip and we will, most definitely, return to this hotel if we ever visit NYC again.

name: Hilton New York Fashion District
title: “Amazing Stay at this Boutique-esque Hilton”
text:
Just returned from a truly fabulous stay at this Hilton property! It has a boutique hotel feel to it, which I loved.
Positives:
-Rooms are hip, modern, new and very clean
-The property is not huge, like the awful Hilton near Times Square, so I never had to deal with lines, elevator waits, an over-crowded lobby, etc.
-Beds are so clean, and comfortable – this was the best sleep I’ve had, next to my stay at the Andaz, last year in NYC
-Location is good, if you are looking to not be in the midtown area – great food and stores are in walking distance or a really quick cab ride (I was able to walk to Chelsea)
-Staff was helpful
-Great value! The nightly rate was $40 cheaper per night than the Hilton property in Times Square - and this place is sooo much nicer, newer, quieter and cleaner!
-So quiet - that is a HUGE plus for me!
Negatives:
-Because it isn’t a spralling hotel, there aren’t cabs lined up outside, if you are looking to grab a quick taxi. Im the mornings the bell desk was happy to hail cabs down though.

name: Blue Moon Hotel
title: “Inspired by the Blue Moon Hotel”
text:
Thoughtfully, tastefully and authentically restored to its 19th-century ambience, The Blue Moon Hotel provides a wonderful oasis conveniently located in downtown Manhattan. All the woodwork, accessories, furniture and even the decorative tin ceilings in the elevator have been restored by hand, allowing even the casual visitor to "step back in time" and be an aristocrat for an evening. Within easy walking distance of several restaurants and the subway, the Blue Moon Hotel provides great accommodations at a great price--particularly for New York City!
I was even pleasantly surprised by the continental breakfast items, available gratis round-the-clock, including fresh fruit; assorted muffins, bagels, rolls, croissants & bread. Even in New York, where almost everything is impressive, you're sure to be inspired by this urban gem.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Lovely experience - helpful staff”
text: I was very very pleased with my experience at the affinia manhattan. First, the prices were reasonable (by NYC standards). Vanessa P was the staff person who checked me in, and her professionalism was incredible - the kind of care she showed a (directionally challenged) person like me is the reason for which the word 'hospitality' was invented. Thanks, Affinia, and all your staff. I raise a glass to the day when your external renovations are 100% complete, matching the 100% delightful experience I had staying there. My only wish? A bathtub.

name: 414 Hotel
title: “Not Bad!”
text:
We booked this hotel based on the TA reviews. Price was right at $199 per night plus $30 taxes. The location on 46th made it an easy walking distance to Times Square and not really a bad walk to anywhere else. One day we actually walked from the Metropolitan Museum all the way back to this hotel although we stopped several times. Walking much further than Rockefeller Center would be weather dependent however.
Staff was reserved but friendly. We checked in early and had to leave baggage in the small lobby. It had been moved all the way to our 4th floor rooms when we came back. That was a nice touch since there is no elevator. Rooms were a little small but adequate and clean. We were in the front bldg but on the courtyard side and it was quiet. 
Morning breakfast was good with fresh baked goods. Lobby area is very small but had no problems with seating.
 On our last day there they arranged a car for transfer to LGA. I would stay here again because of the price advantage, location, and cleanliness. Just be prepared to do some stair climbing if on the 3rd or 4th floor.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Great location hotel”
text: We visited New York for the 1st time over New year. The hotel proved to be in a fantastic location for the Empire state building, Times Square and the Rockefeller. When we arrived at the hotel we were downgraded from the 32nd to 22nd floor with a very drafty room. The room was a little old fashioned but we were not in the room much. The tap also came off when running a bath which was quickly resolved. As creatures of habit, we loved the Skylight diner on 9th Avenue which offered excellent breakfasts at great prices before 10am. A further recommendation was the Houndstooth pub on 8th avenue for good food and atmosphere. What we really want to thank the hotel for is the limousine service we received when leaving the hotel to catch our flight. We were saved by the quick thinking of the limo driver from the Ivory coast who got us to the right gate and the right time due to traffic and black ice for the same price as a cab.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “It does exactly what it says on the label”
text:
No doubting its a very good hotel. But...it IS a Hilton and had we not had the view over Ground Zero we could have been in a Hilton Hotel in any number of large cities.
At least you know what you are getting.
Special mention has to go to Joe one of the concierge, and Steve one of the Doormen. Excellent service above and beyond. Joe managed to get us booked into a New Years Eve Dinner Dance at a restaurent within 5 mins walk of the hotel at less that 24hr notice and it was fantastic value at $150 for two inc 4 courses + live music + an open bar 9-12pm. Steve managed to get us an immaculate stretched limo for our trip to see Fiddler on the Roof at just $35 door to door!! Thanks guys.
The extortionate prices of the hotels breakfast ($22pp) can easily be avoided.
There ARE a number of good restaurants and deli/diners for that authentic NYC breakfast or brunch in the Financial District.
The Stage Door Deli / Essex Cafe and Paninis are all within a few hundred metres and offer great value for money and are recommended both for food quality and that edgy NYC atmosphere.
For dinner we would heartily recommend Giovanni's Atrium ( Italian ) and Les Halles ( French ) both exellent and again within easy walking distance. O'Haras Bar/Restaurant next to the Fire Station adjacent to Ground Zero is 'ok' but couldn't be recommended, pretty basic food and service, and not that cheap. 
Worth seeing/doing while you are there?
USS Intrepid,
Circle Line Boat Trip,
Central Park etc. 
At the Empire State Building, avoid the queues and buy the virtual flight tickets off the guys in the yellow jackets who will offer you tickets while you are in the queue for the Empire. Sure its a few extra dollars but it will save you anything up to a 3 to 4hr wait. 
Another alert! We bought a City Pass book for a number of attractions prior to going. It states in the City Pass that it allows you to beat the queues and go straight to the front of the line....it doesn't work, you will be directed to joint the queue at the back just like everyone else.
National History Museum adjacent to Central Park.It's good BUT probably needs at least two days to do it justice. 
Cabs were an total lottery. We had the full spectrum from a genuine new yorker type ( a la De Niro )who was great. The other end of the scale was an atrocious driver of far eastern origin who it seemed had little or no idea of geography or driving skills and even decided to stop for petrol and take a leak while the meter was left running and added about $3 to the bill...bizarre.
For real night time entertainment either head for Chinatown ( Winnies is fun, although not for the faint hearted ). Swing46 a really cool Jazz Bar/Restaurant on 46th Street offers a great value fixed price 3 course meal for $22 before 7.30pm, ideal for pre theatre eats. Just along the street from there is a great piano/singalong bar where you will be entertained by Broadway singers for the price of your beers. The Oyster Bar on the lower level at Grand Central Station should not be missed.
New York really is spectacular. 
 Overall a great 50th Birthday trip. I just need a holday to get over it now!!!!!

name: Hilton New York Fashion District
title: “There are better Hilton-family properties in NYC”
text: This Hilton is relatively new. Rooms are small, even by NYC standards. Staff are not very guest-oriented even to Hilton top-tier HHonor guests. When I mentioned two housekeeping issues at check out I didn't even get an apology. When I wanted to extend my stay by arriving early, even though rooms were available, they wouldn't extend my pricing. Business center is a joke -- two old pcs running Windows XP! It is an acceptable property but there are certainly nicer Hilton and Hilton-family properties in NYC.

name: Hampton Inn 35th St. Empire State Building
title: “Hampton Inn - momentan mein New York Hotel Favorit”
text:
Beim dritten mal New York nun endlich mal ein Hotel in Manhattan (vorher stets Brooklyn). 
Die Lage ist unschlagbar. Gerade zum Zwischenablegen von Shoppingtüten oder kurzer Erholung ist das Hotel nahe Empire State Building und Macys gut zu erreichen und zentral gelegen. Kostenloses WLAN ist mir als "Gern auch im Urlaub"-Internetsurfer gern gesehen und ebenso kostenloses Frühstücksbüffet stärkt vorm Entdecken der Stadt die niemals schläft. 
Sicherlich sind die Zimmer nicht gerade die größten, aber sauber und gut im Service.
Sogar ein Kaffeekocher für den Kaffee zwischendurch ist vorhanden, Eismaschine und Getränkeautomat in diversen Etagen.
Der Fitnessraum bietet eine Möglichkeit auch im Hotel einwenig für die Gesundheit zu tun.
Rundherum ein gutes Hotel mit freundlichem und hilfsbereitem Personal. Gerne buche ich hier wieder.

name: The Belvedere
title: “NO WIFI!!!!”
text: Ok this hotel claims they have WIFI, but it is barely functional. If you NEED WIFI Do NOT STAY HERE!!! They will refund your payment for WIFI, but to me its not enough. In case you think it is just my PC, we had 2 PCs a PDA, another guest I spoke with had the same probs, another guest in the lobby with a MAC was having no joy.. wasted 1 hour with tech support.. another guest wasted just as much time. I even switched rooms an it was the same. 3 days later it was not fixed which make me believe it is typical. Location is great. It's a bit dated, but clean. No flat screen TV in small NYC rooms.. location is superb. I will not stay here again because of the WIFI issue. Colleague on the 3rd floor had WIFI though.. ??! I could not get it to go in the lobby either.

name: Hilton New York Fashion District
title: “enjoyed my stay”
text:
Just returned to the UK after 4 days in NYC, stayed at this hotel firstly because I have never had a bad experience at a Hilton hotel and secondly because of the reviews. This is a modern clean and comfortable hotel to which I would happily return, the rooms are fine and bathroom spotless. Contrary to some of the reviews, I found the staff to be polite and knowledgeable and have absolutely no complaints. We ate at Rare the steak house attached to the restaurant we thought it was excellent a meal for four people including wine and 2 rounds of drinks prior to dinner cost $260 inc tip, as for the drink prices well $12 for a GnT which was so strong I had to ask for more tonic didnt strike me as poor value as far as hotel prices go. This hotel is in a brilliant location, a short walk up 7th to Macy's and then a shorter walk into Times Sq, used to tube to get around no problems at all. Couple of places we thought were outstanding, Merchants River House Battery Park the best burger I have ever had 4 meals all different all excellent 2 rounds of drinks $98 fantastic great views across the Hudson of the statue of lib. Secondly the Museum not my usual cup of tea, However I had a great day. Two irish bars worthy of a mention Lanigans passed the red steps on the right side street ( excellent food) amd O'Donahueys very similar.
Well done Hilton

name: Broadway at Times Square Hotel
title: “Awesome stay, can't beat the location!!”
text: We thoroughly enjoyed our stay. We found the hotel very clean and quiet, especially considering how close it is to Times Square! It's out the door and 1/2 block down. Also within a close walk to subways, Rockefeller center, Bryant Park, etc. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Hot breakfast was a great start to the day. We'll be back!!

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Sisters in the City”
text: This was a great hotel for the price we paid. The location is really close to the theatres of Times Square and the lobby and staff are very friendly and accomodating. The room was pretty large for New York standards, and average in quality.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Old and tired hotel. Motel 6 quality!”
text:
The Belvedere is a well located dilapidated hotel. Cute but small lobby area with prompt front-desk service. When we arrived at 10:30 AM, we were able to check in to our room. The small and narrow elevator cab reminded me of a Twilight Zone episode. The hallways are old and tired. No decor whatsoever. The room has furniture that must be 30 years old. The bathroom floors smell like urine and the windows are sealed tight with black duct tape. The linens are comical. The mattress reminded me of an army cot (actually the army cot may have been a bit more comfortable). I surveyed other hotel guest and asked to see another room as our smelled. All of the rooms in the hotel are the same!
The pillows...well...you can guess that one. As far as cleanliness...keep your socks on while on the carpet and shower in sandals. Not sure if there were bed bugs but I brought all of my clothes home in a bag to be laundered separately in steam water. If you pay more than $110 per night for this hotel it's too much. I don’t know who they are paying to pump up the STAR rating for this old bag hotel but believe me it's Motel 6 quality.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Phenomenal Experience”
text: Came to NYC for the very first time with all of the women in my very southern family. We shopped, toured, ate amazing food, and stayed in this breath-taking establishment. The staff were beyond helpful, offering umbrellas and curbside cab-call. Everything was top of the line. We ate breakfast 2 mornings in the restaurant downstairs. The Starbucks Shop was nice enough to stay open an extra half-hour per our request because it was rainy and cold, we needed warm coffee!! Would most certainly recommend this to any and everyone wanting to visit the beautiful big apple. A+++

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “The Best hotel ever!!!!”
text: My husband and I first trip to New York and we booked this holiday via expedia really good as it was recommend by them. I obviously checked reviews by trip advisor seemed pretty good. I am the most fussy person when it comes to hotels, anyways we checked in very tired because of the flight ( KLM best service ) our room toilet door did not shut at all and a musky smell was in the air. We were sooo tired we waited until the morning and explain everything to the hotel reception. She was so nice service with a smile is important to me and I could not fault her nor any of the staff very helpful and friendly. There is no in room safe which a lot of hotels do not have at New York but it's very easy and the staff are very helpful. Cleaners are very welcoming too. I personally would not rate tick tock dinner as there is an amazing take away foot steps away from the hotel (when u walk out of the hotels it to ur left) and starbucks and mcdonalds are opposite the hotel too. Brilliant location too every things was just 10 mins away from each other time square was 10 mins macys literally down the road. I really enjoyed my stay hope you find this helpful.

name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Midtown East
title: “Perfect location...”
text: Just spent 3 nights at this lovely hotel. It is a great hotel for people with large groups trying to cut down costs. Some people in our group stayed in a room with 2 double beds and a sofa sleeper. The room slept 5. Great for city hotel. The location cannot be beat. You are minutes away from the subway stations. It is an easy 20 minute walk to times square. We even walked to central park. Everything is close by. Many restaurant choices nearby like Dos Caminos, Starbucks, 2 Chipotles, cafes, bakeries, etc... So very easy to find food. Also, there is a Duane Reed right next door if you need an ATM plus they have food like fruit cups, water, snacks, etc. There is a cafe on the 12th floor which I did not try but some in our group and it was typical Marriott breakfast food. They serve breakfast only. Also, on the 12th floor they had free coffee and TEA (this is a big one with me). You also have coffee in your room but no tea. Usually, I bring my own electric teapot but I didn't this trip but I was happy there was tea available. There is also a gym. The rooms were very clean and spacious. The views were okay. The lobby was a bit tight for a meeting spot. But it worked out. The Conceirge was awesome with helping out with rides to the airport, etc. They had cookies in the lobby one afternoon that we came back so a nice touch. Definitely would stay here again if cost is a issue.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Great service, very proffessional”
text:
Stayed here May 26 to 29 with my girlfriend. Had read lots of positive reviews. We weren't disapointed. Room was ready on arrival. Although we had asked for king size and got queen. Went to front desk and had room changed right away. Beautifull views of course. Away from all the action of uptown but only 12 minutes by subway, station is footsteps away. Not even 5 minutes to canal street, Little Italy and Chinatown..... You must visit Little Italy, its worth the trip. Starbucks coffee right around the corner and stage door deli 1 block away, serve amazing breakfest (try the 4 egg western omelet.wow).. The room was spacious, very modern and clean. Bathroom was amazing, lots of space, pressure and hot water.
We checked in Thursday at around 7:00pm, checked out Sunday at 12:00 but were only charged 2 days of parking wich was cool cause at 45$/day, it gets expensive. When we checked out, they stored our bags til we left town wich was appreciated. Guys, if your wife likes shopping, Century 21 is a must, just accross the street but a little tip, be patient..The store is huge, full of brand names and really crowded, easy to lose your wife...Ladies, you can very easily spend 3-4 hours in there, mine almost did.
All in all, a wonderfull weekend in New York, but then again, how can you not a fun in New York..Soooooooo much to do. If you're looking for a broadway show, BROOKLYN, THE MUSICAL may not be well known but trust me, worth every penny...amazing voices.
All of the people we met and talked with, staff, store employees, policemen, were ALL VERY POLITE AND COURTIOUS, I WAS ACTUALLY IMPRESSED.
The city has changed lots over the years, very clean and alot safer than expected...
I highly recommend the millenium. A few minutes away from all the action 
A definite 4 star at a 2-3 star price...

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Too small and not 4 star service”
text: First of all no parking and the lot across the street charges $40 to park every time you leave and come back you pay again. The place looked average as were the rooms. They charged me $19 for having the in room coffee and using the hotel soap, PETTY charge to say the least. Not worth the money at all.

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “Richard”
text: Excellent hotel in terms of guest service and comnfort. AnneMara, Leslie and Sanela provide a perfect approach guest relations. Nothing is too small to deal with and they always manage to make booking extremely easy despite often changes. They always make me and my family extremely welcome. Thankyou

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “Quality in NYC!”
text:
Stayed in the Eastgate for 2 weeks while my apartment was renovated and my experience was wonderful. I booked a full studio suite with living room, and it was clean, up to date and spacious. The Kitchen, which I only used for the freezer, fridge, and microwave, was awesome! it was like living in my apartment, but with maid service. The staff was wonderful and accomodated my requests.
Only downside is the cost of internet service, $10 a day or $40ish dollars a week, for what I paid it should be an included amenity, imo.
There are restaurants, bars, and stores conveniently located to the hotel, all are pretty good. Also, don't bother taking a cab, just walk to Grand Central (and visit the market!).

name: New York Marriott Downtown
title: “Great hotel for business travel”
text:
I stayed at the NY Marriott Downtown for a business meeting. I am a loyal Marriott business traveler so I knew what I should expect in terms of service, decor, amenities. After a lengthy flight delay I checked in very late in the evening, so my room was not on the concierge level, but I still had lounge access due to my Marriott status. The hotel is very clean, service is prompt, and the room size is large compared to other NYC hotels. Proximity to shopping and tourism is a plus.
I did see a lot of families also staying at this hotel and they seemed to be enjoying their stay.

name: Broadway at Times Square Hotel
title: “What a Fantastic little hotel”
text: What a gem of a hotel in Times square. Staff are fantastic, the rooms are very clean and its close to the main husstle&bussle without it getting in your way. Would recommend to anyone.

name: Affinia 50
title: “Maybe for Families”
text: Not really the boutique hotel depicted on its website. However, my room was huge for New York standards and the bed was comfortable but the towels were thin and rough. Had a kitchenette with a stove and fridge but no microwave and really bad metal cabinets. Good location but would sacrafice the large room and stay at the W for the same price next time I'm in the area. Not really geared for business travelers but would be a good option for families with children or those staying for an extended period.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Thumbs Up”
text: This was a very modern, nicely appointed hotel. The room was very spacious with stylish furnishings and comfortable linens. The location is great if you plan to spend time in lower Manhattan with easy access to the World Trade Site and the Statue of Liberty. The hotel was not very close to the trendy restaurants, shops and nightlife in Soho and the Village, which are a long walk or short cab ride away. Joggers will love the access to Battery Park and nice paths along the river. I would definitely stay here again!

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Just Average”
text:
This was my first time back to the Millenium Hilton since September 11 had forced its closure. I had stayed in the hotel 4 or more times previous to 2001 and had always been a huge fan of the place- it was sleek, contemporary and well run. This time however, I wasn't as happy. Don't get me wrong- it's not awful, but the service was lacklustre in several areas and the place just seemed less luxurious- certainly it is not in my opnion a 4 star-more like a 3 star.
Like other reviewers we encountered problems upon arrival with regards to the room booked. We had booked a Deluxe double on 33-55th floor with city view and on previous visits this had meant a corner room with a view uptown. The view we had was directly over Ground Zero. I don't particularly have a problem with that but certainly I would not call it a city view- unless they are referring to a New jersey city view. To be honest I couldnt be bothered to argue further with the clerk but as per other reviews- don't expect to necessarily get what you have booked! 
The check in staff were bordering on the surly and they even stated that breakfast wasnt included in the rate which I immediately corrected them on. We were told the breakfast vouchers would be sent to our room later that day and after 2 further inquiries and telephone calls- they were- hardly 4 star service huh?One further problem with the room is that we were on a non smoking floor. On our return to our room on the Saturday we could smell a strong cigarette smell in our room- which had a connecting door to teh room next door- we could smell teh smoke seeping through- and as non smokers it wasn't pleasant particularly as the hotel has very small windows that dont clear the air and air conditioning doesnt really help with smoke. We called the front desk who seemed totally disinterested and it was only when i got angry that he sent us housekeeping with an air purifier which took up a large chunk of our bedroom floorspace and wasnt that efficient- they seemed unconcerned that other guests were smoking on a non smoking floor which I think is unacceptable. Again they seemed disinterested and I was made to feel as if I was making a fuss!
Housekeeping werent very efficient either- granted they tidied the room but it still looked messy- ie they didnt put away teh ironing board and the extra pillows and blankets were just left folded on the bed so the overall impression was a bit tatty.
Now the good bits- the swimming pool is fab and the staff there are friendly and cheerful. Breakfast is good if you can get it as part of your room rate but overpriced otherwise. Room service is overpriced in my view and dont touch the minibar- $4.50 for a can of coke-! there are loads of delis nearby where we stocked up on beverages and stuffed them in our ice bucket to chill- much better!
The rooms themselves may have been refurbished but the carpets look cheap and the place just seems more like a holiday inn than a premium Hilton property. The plasma screen TVs are Ok but they take the place of large mirrors that used to be wall mounted. Now the only mirrors are in the bathroom and on the bathroom door in a dark spot in the room. 
The bar in the lobby is quite nice but expensive- $12.50 for a cocktail seems a bit cheeky when it is really only a standard lobby bar.
We stayed at Embassy Suites which is across from the Millenium by the Financial Center and this is a much better option if you can get a good rate.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text:
Just spent 3 nights in the Millenium Hilton 23rd-26th April, what a fantastic hotel and great value for money.
After reading all the reviews about the Millenium Hilton on this website I decided to book 3 nights for my girlfriend and I through the Hilton website. We managed to get a city view room on the 41st floor including breakfast for £93 per night. We booked this about a month in advance and if you do your homework like I did that is a very good price for a 4* hotel b&b in NYC.
The room was modern and spacious with great plasma tv, internet, cd player, pay per view movies and floor to ceiling windows with an excellent view of the New York skyline and directly overlooking World Trade Centre site.
The hotel is situated in downtown Manhattan so you do have to get the subway or taxis to most of the sites and attractions, but for me this was'nt a problem at all. The subway station is right outside the hotel ($2 for one trip or $10 for 7 trips) and I never spent more than $8.00 on a taxi from the hotel. 
Still loads to do close to the hotel anyway. The fantastic Century 21 dept store is next door, Wall St around the corner, Ground Zero opposite, Statue of Liberty, Chinatown, and Soho only 5 minutes away.
All in all a great hotel, great value and friendly informative staff made this hotel a great place to stay and I'd definatley stay again.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Excellent Hotel In A Great Location”
text:
To my wife here as a surprise for her 40th Birthday, I was a bit concerned at booking the hotel without hr knowing in case I picked a bad one. Should not have worried the Hotel was great, friendly staff and an excellent location as it is just 10 mins from Times Square and Broadway. The Empire State Building is just outside as is Macy's. The hotel also arranged care pick up from the Hotel when we arrived again taking away any stress. The rooms are not massive but had all you need in them and to be fair when in New York why would you sit in your room. The Tic Toc is great value and will fill you up!!! the Bar is also good value. The Hotel provide safe deposit boxes that are installed behind locked doors at the lobby. 
All in all a great break with a hotel that made us feel welcome and safe. Would recommend this without hesitation and will come back in the future

name: New York Marriott Downtown
title: “Nice, but standard, Marriott in the FiDi”
text:
The Marriott Downtown is everything you would expect of an NYC Marriott. It's large, clean, without character, and the service is OK, but not great. Although booked off Priceline, my room was larger than one would expect for an NYC room. The view was nothing special (nothing compared to some of the stunning views of the 9/11 memorial at the nearby Millenium Hilton). 
The location is really dependent on what you're looking to do. If you're working in the area, the location's fine. If you want to be mobbed by sweaty tourists outside trying to see the nearby 9/11 memorial, it's good for that as well. Otherwise, the Financial District is somewhat limited. That said, there's nearby subway access, and it's not that far to walk to greener pastures in TriBeCa and even the West Village.
Service, as is often the case for Marriotts, was the weak point here. There is no one to open the hotel doors, which makes simply entering the hotel tricky of you have two large suitcases (I know, I'm an idiot). The front desk is overstaffed, but moves glacially. When I ordered food delivery, the delivery man was not permitted to come upstairs, despite there being absolutely no security measures on the elevators, which meant that absolutely anyone could have gone up. Finally, when leaving my bags in the lobby before heading out to brunch, I had to wait over 5 minutes for bell staff to show up. The front desk staff, who were entirely unoccupied, watched as a line formed behind me. Rather than do anything to remedy the situation, they told me someone would be there momentarily (not true), and giggled.
Would I come back? Yes, if the price is right. Would I pay a standard rate? No.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Great location, but showing it's age”
text:
Great location one block from Penn Station and many subway lines. Walking distance to many attractions. Safe area and very busy. Police presence at all times. Very good security at the hotel. You must show your room key card to get onto the elevators to the rooms. Great "Tick Tock Diner" attached to the hotel through the lobby. If you like to have coffee in your room, you must ask for a coffeemaker at check in. The same with a refrigerator. This was our first visit and I had read about the small rooms, but I would describe this as TINY. There is just enough room to walk around the bed. Very limited floor space for bags. Closet is small also, so we couldn't store our luggage in it. 2 nightstand cabinets and 3 dresser drawers are the total of the storage space. One small shelf above the pedestal sink in the bathroom holds very limited toiletries. It was adequate for the 3 days and 4 nights we were there, but for a longer visit, I would have to have a larger room. I know everyone says that you are never in your hotel room anyway, but the reality is that it is very cramped for showering, dressing and just moving around.
We only paid $135 per night through Priceline, so we felt we got our moneys worth. Would definitely stay in that area again, but would try to find a larger room. The room was clean and the bed wa scomfortable, but the room had a very distinct mildew smell at all times and the bathroom was not in good condition.

name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Midtown East
title: “Wil be our first choice for future trips to NYC”
text: We stayed here with our family and another family in June 2011. It was our first trip to NYC. The staff was very helpful especially the person we spoke with to make the reservations. Hotel was clean and very nice inside. We were surprised at the "normal" room size after what we had heard about New York hotels. The mattress was great- considered buying one. Essabagel is just a block or so up the street and Certe Pizza another favorite was just around the corner. Great part of town and within walking distance of St. Patrick's, Bryant Park, and other attractions. We even walked from theater district to the hotel but that was quite a trek. Our friends who come to New York on business usually stay somewhere else but after staying with us said they'll switch to this hotel now. Definitely our first choice for any future trips.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Old Titanic”
text: I stayed at the Waldorf in March for two nights. I had the opportunity to stay in several high end hotels and I can tell you that I was not impressed. I realized it's NYC and prices are higher but really folks, 20.00 for two eggs any style in the Peacock restaurant for breakfast? Twelve dollars for a bowl of oatmeal (not that we ordered that) Check out the menu on their website, your eyes will roll back in your head. Ok down to the nitty gritty, the room, 17th floor average size and just plain ugly old yellow and brown decor, with a huge armoure that takes up too much room and an old 27 inch regular TV. The beds were terribly uncomfortable, the bedding scratchy white hotel sheets with a 200 lb bed spread that looked like it belonged on one of the beds on the Titanic and flat pillows. The only modern device in the room was the alarm clock that allowed for an Ipod. I could not regulate the heat, it was very hot, the bathroom was really small and there was no exhaust fan. It took 2 minutes before the water came out of the faucet in the tub and then it took at least 8 minutes before any hot water came out. The curtains, again very Titanic and white sheers that looked so dingy I wondered if there had been a fire. The desk is way to small to do any work on. Don't ever book a room that is near the elevator because all you will hear all night is the sound of a 747 taking off down the runway. The website doesn't tell you that there is a Starbucks down stairs. And it does not tell you that it costs 50.00 a day to park your car and an additional 10.00 if you have an SUV. I paid 120.00 bucks for two days OUCH! The lobby is very "grand" and dark, again like an old ship. I will say that when I checked in I found the staff to be very friendly, including the bellmen, the doorman and any man or woman that worked there. Here's a cool fact that the man who checked me in told me when I had advised him that my father stayed there in 1950 for his honeymoon, he asked if he still had that bill? Then went on to tell me if he still had the bill and wanted to stay there, that the Waldorf would honor that price he paid in 1950. If you are going to have to stay in a hotel, don't you want to have the same amenities or even better amenties that you do at home? I suppose if you are a history buff, you might love it

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Earplugs are provided!”
text:
My wife and I came to the Waldorf Astoria to attend a meeting of my old alma mater. 
We were given a room by the elevators which was not properly insulated for noise. Cars going up and down all night made it difficult for us to sleep. 
When we reported the incident, we were offered ear plugs!
The following day, when we insisted that we would like to have a good night sleep, one of the managers, Mark, who had offered the plugs in the first place, suggested that we move to another room, but at twice the price! 
When we expressed dissatisfaction with this option, we were promised an alternative room, which would be ready in a matter of minutes. We left a cell phone number where we would be called. Five hours later, we had not been contacted. 
Before attending a show at the Waldorf Towers, we complained to Vivian, a kind person at the reception, who spoke to another manager, reassuring us that there would be a room available but that it would take a couple of hours to be cleaned. 
When we returned two hours later, as requested, we were asked to talk with yet another manager, Elena Oxford. She informed us, as kindly as she could, that there were no rooms available at that time. It was 11:00 PM then. 
We asked to be moved to another hotel. We were offered The San Carlos, a few blocks away. After several new phone interactions with Elena, who was always very professional and polite, we were shown yet another room at the Waldorf Astoria, but that now had constant noise from the street!
By midnight, when we were ready to change hotels, we were offered another room, on a higher floor, and far from the elevators. At long last, we could get some quiet time. 
This was a perfect example of a lesson I received from one of my old tutors at university: when a place has a good reputation, I does not deserve it anymore!

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Quiet and comfortable”
text: The Hotel was comfortable and was quiet. Nothing special about the decor nor the size of the room. But there weren't any 'surprises' to darken my stay. I'd stay here again!

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “An old style hotel with an excellent location”
text:
The hotel is in an excellent location. Many tourist attractions such as the Museum of Modern Art, Central Park, the Grand Central Station and many other are at walking distance. At just one block from the hotel there is a subway stations which connects the hotel with downtown Manatthan.
The rooms are spacious, however the downside is that they are extremely noisy: this is because there is a lot of traffic (day and night) and the windows are not sound proof. So if you have light sleep I suggest you bring earplugs.

name: New York Marriott Downtown
title: “Good stay, not particularly special”
text: The lines of this hotel are weird. As another reviewer commented, the multiple series of steps all around the lobby were weird and angular; hard for rolling luggage and ramps might have been nice or all the steps in one place would have helped. I get that it is a downtown hotel though. We had also a weird shaped corner room facing the street mostly which was also narrow and angular. Amenities were plentiful, room was clean, small refrigerator in the room was appreciated. It was completely adequate and not noteworthy. Location good if near what you are there for. I am not a frequent New York traveler so I probably will not stay here again. I would recommend it as far as a good chain hotel choice, but not to go out of your way to stay in.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Location, location & location”
text:
Briliant located hotel, less then 5 minutes walk to Times Sqyare and the heart of NY.
Unbelievable beds which were a god-send after a full day sight-seeing.
Room typical city sized but well laid out and only lacking tea making facilities (which we asked for and were given a kettle).
Highly recommend and would stay there on next trip.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Fab hotel”
text: We had great views, lovely hotel, friendly staff, nothing to much trouble, great location.

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “Very impressed”
text: My boyfriend and I were coming to NY for the first time and having had a terrible experience in a hotel in Paris before, we were worried about where to stay. We literally searched hotels in NY for over a month reading these reviews to find a nice, clean place. We found it here. It wasn't expensive and the room was lovely and clean. Staff were very friendly and helpful and the hotel was situated in a good location. The fridge and microwave in the room was very handy also! The room was spacious with a lovely view. We have already decided when we return to NY, we will definately stay here again.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “A good base to explore New York”
text:
Went there in June 2004. First time in New York. The location of the hotel is fantastic as it is in middle of Broadway and a few minutes from Time Square. It is conveniently located for a lot of other landmarks such as Central Park, 5th Avenue.
The rooms were spacious and clean. Although the hot and cold water taps were puzzling, I got boiling water from both taps on several occasions.
We got late check out, a good buffet breakfast, and the staff were friendly in the diner. The buffet breakfast can seem pricey unless you have kids as they eat for free. Other reviewers recommend nearby diners for breakfast, but i did not think they were any cheaper, especially if you have children.
Charging a dollar for each luggage is a bit mean, but overall this hotel was good value, and good standard.
Also found this part of New York to be safe, taxi drivers knew where they were going and could speak English, and good bargains were on offer during the June sales.
A good tip, for foreign visitors is to register with customers services in shops such as Macys and Bloomingdales. You will get discounts off your shopping, free gifts etc. Take your passport with you to confirm that you are a visitor.

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan / Times Square South
title: “Un soggiorno breve ma piacevole”
text: Abbiamo soggiornato all' Hampton Inn soltanto una notte ma possiamo dire di essere pienamente soddisfatti. L'hotel è molto centrale a pochi passi da Times Square e sia le camere che la struttura sono dotati ti tutti i comfort, manca il minibar ma non se ne risente poiché ad alcuni piani c'è la macchina del ghiaccio, la colazione è ricca e soddisfacente.

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan / Times Square South
title: “Recomendable el Hamton Inn Times Square South”
text: Nuestra estadía en el hotel fue muy buena, los desayunos son buenos. La amabilidad de los empleados excelente, el hotel muy limpio. Excelente en terminos de localizacion. Lo unico malo era el elevador de 8:40 am a 10:00 am por el rush del desayuno y las areas aledañas por los malos olores. Por lo demas lo recomiendo.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Absolutely fabulous and great location!!”
text: I took my boyfriend for his 21st birthday and pictures of the hotel did no justice! I emailed prior to my arrival explaining it was a surprise visit and they upgraded my room to a large room free of charge and with a great city view!! Was in a great location easy to walk pretty much everywhere and was very close to times square!! It was my first time in new York so wasn't sure where the hotel was etc but was amazing! Very clean and the staff was very helpful! Would definitely stay there on my next visit as it's very good value! You would never think it is a 3 star since it has been refurbished! Only ate once in the tick tock diner and only had a desert! But only because we wanted to experience other places all over! Alot of my friends who have been or are going are using this hotel so is very popular!!

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “zentrale lage am neuen WTC”
text: gute location, fassade wirkt sehr modern, zimmer teilweise modernisierungsbedürftig, mittlerer standard. gute verkehrsanbindungen, blick aus dem zimmer fantastisch, leider war ein fenster 'blind'. concierge service aussergewöhnlich gut (half bei der orientierung, tischreservierung, etc). derzeit reduzierte preise aufgrund der baustelle am ground zero. wir hatten ein zimmer mit blick richtung brooklyn und haben keinerlei lärmbelästigungen wahrgenommen. negativ war eine offensichtliche absprache zwischen dem doorman und dem taxifahrer, die uns eine überteuerte fahrt zum flughafen beschert hat.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Wonderful stay at the Novotel”
text:
I stayed at the Novotel for the weekend in June 04, and I was pleasantly surprised at just about everything. Based on other reviews on this site, I was expecting surly reception staff and smallish rooms. 
Instead the staff at reception was very efficient and fairly pleasant. The lobby was always busy and it often looked like the Paris airport with lots of flight crews from Air France.
The room was bigger than I imagined, with room for the king bed, a sofa, desk, TV. And the bathroom had wood flooring, which is a great alternative to tile. The air conditioning was central (not window unit) and was relatively silent.
I was lucky enough to get a room that looked out onto Times Square, and there is a terrasse/bar which has the same view.
I would definitely stay here again.

name: Millenium Hilton
title: “Toller Ausblick aber es ist laut”
text: Von unserem Eckzimmer im 42. Stock (Zimmer 4201) hatten wir einen herrlichen Ausblick auf den East River auf der einen Seite und auf die WTC Baustelle auf der anderen Seite. Somit konnte man sowohl Sonnenaufgang und Sonnenuntergang vom Zimmer aus fotografieren. Wem die Taxi Anreise zu teuer ist, kann auch mit dem Airtran (nach Jamaica) und dann mit der Metro E anreisen. Das dauert ca 01 Stunde und 20 Minuten, und kostet nur USD 7,25. Die Metrostation befindet sich direkt vor de Haus. Mit viel Gepäck ist es allerdings nicht zu empfehlen. Neben dem Hotel befindet sich das Century 21 Kaufhaus. Das Gute daran ist, dass es hier schöne Sachen zum super Preis gibt, schlecht is allerdings, das das Kaufhaus eine riesige Klimaanlage auf dem Dach hat und die jede Menge Lärm (auch in der Nacht) macht. Die Bauarbeiten am WTC sind Montags bis Samstags ab 06:00 zu hören.

name: Pod 51
title: “Too too small and NOT SMOKE FREE!”
text:
I will pay more money to stay in something that isn't the size of a closet, literally. It's a shock when you open the door and see just how tiny it is. Not that I didn't expect it beforehand but in actuality... I booked the queen bed, btw. Sure, you're not in your room that much but when I am I want to be in something better than this.
The other shock was that the hotel has you sign a paper saying you won't smoke in their non-smoking hotel or you will be fined $250. Guess what? EVERYONE WAS SMOKING IN THEIR ROOMS! I called every day and the staff was very nice and knocked on doors (which guests didn't answer) and sprayed some lemon smoke neutralizer down my hall but still...I have to stuff a towel under my door? It was disgusting. When I talked to the supervisor he said well we can't really do anything about it...well why make us sign something when we check in then??
I will say the hotel staff was very nice; loved the large rain shower head although the shower is the smallest I've ever experienced; the free wi-fi worked great; good bars and restaurants close by; subway close as well. My room faced the large air conditioning units in the back and it was LOUD. I had specifically asked for something quieter... guess not. Would have liked coffee maker in the room or coffee somewhere set up in the hotel. Walked around the corner on 2nd Ave. to Morningstar Cafe and brought it back.
Never again!

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Pleased”
text: This was our first visit to the city, so I don't really have a good comparison other than the significant room shopping that I did prior to booking here. Our room was clean, the bed comfortable, albeit small (I opted for the lowest cost as we planned to be out of our room most of the time). Staff was attentive, yet discreet. As others said, the elevator situation was sometimes frustrating, but often gave us an opportunity to chat it up with other guests. Location was good if you plan to be uptown most of the time.

name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Midtown East
title: “Great Hotel - Great Neighborhood”
text: We came to NYC with our 9- and 14-year-old. We were looking for a mid-town hotel but not one right in the middle of everything. We wanted something a little quieter. This hotel was perfect!! The rooms quite large for Manhattan with two queen beds and a pull-out couch. There was an in-room fridge and a safe as well. The subway station was at the corner of the street for easy public transportation. Also, we were able to enjoy fantastic bagels (Ess-a-Bagel), yummy cupcakes (Crumbs Bakery), and delicious Italian food (La Giaconda) within steps of our hotel!
