This was really helpful in the morning on the way out and when we were coming home with tired feet and hungry stomachs - especially with a teenaged boy in tow!

name: Affinia 50
title: “Great hotel, great location, and WONDERFUL staff”
text: My family and I stayed at the Affinia 50 for 5 days in April 2011. The room was exceptionally spacious, comfortable beds, plenty of closet/drawer space and a small but workable kitchen. The neighborhood had some lovely, small wine bars and restaurants. Most of all the hotel had Rome, the doorman. Rome made us all smile every time we saw him with his big smile, kind words and pleasant outlook. We looked forward to seeing him in the evenings just to hear him say "Welcome home my friends."

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text: I stayed here in Dec 2010 with my Boyfriend. The hotel is in a great location, walking distance from times square, macys, madison square gardens etc. The rooms are very small but i dont think that matters when in NYC as you arent in much. Had a great time in new york, will be returning soon and will stay in this hotel again. The tick tock dinner attached to the hotel is great, lovely food, great service.

name: New York Marriott Downtown
title: “Awesome hotel, next to everything downtown”
text:
I was very surprised how much I liked this hotel. The rooms are huge (for NY), which means normal in most other cities. At first they couldn't find our reservation, but they still gave me a nice room at the same rate. It is walking distance to all the downtown locations, and the metro to get anywhere else. Overall, it is 100 times better anything you can in midtown or the east side, and a cheaper price none-the less. Also, the nearby revitalized battery park area is very kid-friendly, and we spent alot of time there!!
Also, Amy was a wonderful help, thanks!

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “Helt ok”
text: Hotellet tilbyr helt greie rom. Det er ikke overdådig eller egnet for en romantisk weekend, det oser ikke av sjarm og varme, og det er noen år siden rommene er pusset opp sist. Det ligger sentralt på Manhattan, servicen i resepsjonen var veldig bra, normalt godt renhold.

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Times Square New York
title: “A great hotel choice in NYC”
text:
You will have a very hard time finding a better hotel choice in NYC than this hotel. I've stayed here the last two times I've visited the city and will likely stay here next time as well. 
There are a lot of advantages, but location and service have to be near the top of the list. This property is centrally located within easy walking distance to the Times Square area and to Grand Central Station. As far as the service is concerned, the staff does a great job of inquiring about your needs and doing their best to meet them. Both times I've stayed here, I've needed an early check-in and it has been accomplished with little effort. They are also great about holding your bags for you until your room is available. As with all Residence Inns, room rates also include a hot breakfast. The quality of the breakfast here is one of the best I've experienced at a Residence Inn and is far superior to the continental-style breakfasts included with many hotel rooms. 
The one disadvantage to breakfast is the fact that it does tend to get very busy later in the morning, both in the breakfast area and with the elevators. So, I would highly recommend that you eat breakfast in the 8-9 a.m. time frame. Additionally, the higher your floor, the better off you are going to be. Not only do some of the higher rooms have great views of the Empire State Building, when riding down the elevators during really busy times it is a definite advantage being on the upper floors. This allows you to get on the elevators before they fill up during the travel down.
Finally, in my opinion, rates at this hotel are very competitive. While not cheap (what decent hotel in NYC is??), the rooms do provide a great value. The suites are significantly larger than most NYC hotel rooms and include a full-size fridge which comes in quite handy. 
All in all, I would highly recommend this hotel.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Great Hotel”
text: Just returned from a week at the Belvedere Hotel New York City. I had checked Trip Advisor when chosing the hotel and most of the reviews were good so we made our booking. The hotel is in an excellent location just 2 blocks from Times Square and one block to subway stations and a short walk up to Central Park. It was very quiet at night though quite warm in the room and we needed to have the air conditioning on all night. We had a room on the 10th floor which was very clean and comfortable with small kitchen area. Staff were very efficient and quickly attended to any small problems we had. The porters gave excellent local advice as to where to eat etc and were friendly with our children who were very impressed with getting our bags taken out of the taxi and put on a gold trolley and taken up to our room! Its not often I am completely happy with a hotel but this is definitely one I would return to and recommend to others.

name: Hilton New York Fashion District
title: “Great Value, Spotless, High Standard, Modern, Central Hotel”
text:
We have just returned from 4 night stay at Fashion 26 and it was great value, spotlessly clean with comfortable bed, fantastic staff who will do anything for you, yummy breakfasts, no sign of bedbugs!
Previously we have stayed at the Marriott Marquis in Times Square and we were worried about booking anywhere else but our buget would not stretch that far this time. We need not have worried, although the rooms are not as big, the standards are impressive and in future we will stay at Fashion 26 and spend the money saved on going shopping!!
Only one complaint, on 20th floor it was very, very hot, even with windows open, the hotel could turn down the heating and save itself some money.
You can easily walk to Macey's, Times Square, Empire State Building, buy one day Yellow Taxi bus tour ticket from hotel and get one day's travel free, much better than deals on the street

name: Broadway at Times Square Hotel
title: “Cheap and pratical choice”
text: We stayed here for a week. It was a wonderful stay, good continental breakfast, clean rooms, and it stays less then a square from Times Square, you can go to many attractions by foot (Central Park, Macys, Rockfeller Center, St. Patrick Cathedral, 5th Av, Park Ave., Apple, Broadway, HB...), but if you preffer there are subway and bus station nearby. We'll certantly be staying here whenever we visit the city.

name: InterContinental New York Times Square
title: “Central location”
text:
Excellent location if you like to be central, with the hotel being just a few minutes walk to Times Square.
The bedrooms are very comfortable with complimentary Tea/coffee, and very comfortable beds. Hot water a plenty, with a powerful shower. The turn down service, daily weather report and complimentary biscuits each evening is a nice little touch.
Nothing to complain about at all!!

name: The Belvedere
title: “Great location and price!!”
text: I stayed at the Belvedere Hotel Feb. 8 to Feb. 13, 2008 while attending the Westminster Dog Show. This is the 5th time I have stayed there. This time there was a group of 6, we had 3 double-double rooms. For the price, it is hard to beat! We always find the staff very helpful. The furniture does need upgraded as does the TV, but it is clean and comfortable and that is most important. Location is fantastic! Subway a block or so away, Olympic Diner around the corner on 8th Ave. wonderful for breakfast. Ask for Gloria if you go. She as been there for years and remembers us year to year. Nice having a door man always on duty, especially when coming in late at night.

name: Broadway at Times Square Hotel
title: “I have found my favorite NYC hotel but that bathroom door...”
text:
If I ever return to New York City, this is were I will stay! 
The room was bigger than I imagined, everything was new and it had the best TV I've ever had in a hotel room (though we didn't use it much). I think it was about a size 40" or bigger flat-screen TV. For you iPod owners, the room also has an iHome instead of a cheap clock radio, NICE! There are plenty of electrical plugs everywhere and FREE Wi-Fi. If you wake up early enough (we didn't) there's free continental breakfast provided downstairs and free newspaper. The hotel has a small but FREE gym that provides water and towels.
We had a king size bed that I miss to this day, SO comfortable!
Service was, for the most part, excellent except for at check-in the Asian guy that helped us had accidentally overcharged our credit card for close to 10 times the amount he was supposed to and didn't tell us. Halfway through our vacation we discovered a few thousand dollars were charged instead of a few hundred and we were in a panic! We thought we were in New York without any money. After talking with the bank all was settled but it was still 30 minutes of stress that could have been avoided. After a deep sigh of relief, all was forgiven and our vacation continued.
The bathroom door is as see-through as a foggy window! We didn't mind it except whenever I had to, you know, sit down. I would do this with the lights off to have as much privacy as possible. If you're not comfortable with the people you're staying with this bathroom door is gonna be tough times for you. I also wished the hotel provided conditioner, all they had was shampoo.
The room can get pretty warm so expect to run that cooler at night.
Location, Location, Location!!!!
Located between Times Square and Rockefeller Center it is PERFECT! Right in the middle of the city and close to everything. 
Across the street is the St. Andrews Pub, we fell in love with this place and we usually went there before bed every night. Conner is the bartender there, he's a nice guy and gives great service.
My only complaints were:
-the credit card "woops" which I'm sure won't happen again.
-the room gets warm
-the bathroom door being see-through
-the Dasani Water machine in the lobby is tricky
-no conditioner
-Bathroom sink water.. the Cold is freezing the Hot is clear lava

name: The Belvedere
title: “Not so great”
text:
I do not think this hotel deserves the rave reviews that it has received. The rooms are small and mediocre and the service is substandard. First and foremost, the road the hotel was on was closed. This may not seem like a big deal, but in the TImes Square area, it can literally take 45 minutes to go around the block. Therefore, not knowing the road was closed added more than 45 minutes to our trip. In addition, there was no way to drop people or luggage off in front of the hotel. What is most upsetting about this is that the hotel admittedly did nothing to notify its guests when it knew of the road closing at least 24 hours in advance (ie emails or posting notification on its website). We never saw a door man or porter in the hotel. When we upset our frustrations, the management simply stated they we "sorry" we "felt that way".
If you are looking for a relatively inexpensive hotel this is okay, but there are much better places at similar rates in NYC

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Times Square New York
title: “Really Impressed”
text:
I have recently returned from my first visit to New York with my wife and 2 young children. I would first like to point out my respect for the excellent staff we met - from the porter, to housekeeping and reception staff. It was a busy time of year (between Christmas and New Year) and we felt welcomed and valued as customers.
Our room (1808) was very spacious as was the bathroom - this may be because it was a disabled room. We had the sofa bed permanently made up and there was still plenty of space. The kitchen area was handy because we have a baby. The staff came to our room and made up the crib which was brilliant!
We had a magical view of the Empire State Building!
I read many reviews prior to travelling regarding the complimentary breakfast. Perhaps I had lower expectations because of these, but we found the breakfast both plentiful and of a satisfactory quality.
The location of the hotel is terrific. You are literally 3 minutes walk from Macys at Herald Square. A further 2 minutes and you arrive at the Empire State Building. Madison Square Gardens is also very close by. Times Square is only 10 minutes walk away.
Nearby Bryant Park was beautiful with all of the Christmas Decorations and Ice Rink erected. It was such a nice surprise to find in the middle of a busy city.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “A bit of a let down”
text:
We stayed at the Waldorf Astoria for one night and have to say that the experience was a bit dissapointing. 
The first room they gave us was pretty big for NY and pretty, but there was a low, thudding noise coming from the hotels huge airconditioning unit or something which was outside just on the same level as the room. I knew I would not be able to sleep in that noise so we asked for another room. I could not help thinking that this was the room they automatically offer to first-timers who don’t know about the noise problem in that room. The next room was in the Astoria Tower and it smelled like tobacco smoke. As we had been confirmed a non-smoking room we asked for a 3rd room.. The 3rd one did not smell of tobacco and was otherwise ok too. It just took a lot of time and energy to get a proper room. And I have never had to ask for another room before, despite loads of travelling around the world.
As I have seen in another hotel with a prestigeous past the staff can be a bit snooty. And they seem to pop into your room rather often. We had put some bread and cheese in the minibar and were "scolded" by someone whose job seemed to be just popping in to your room to have a look at the minibar, in the evening of your 1-day stay.. Why not at the end of your stay? 
Another snooty example from the breakfast restaurant where we were rushed to the table and hastily asked "have you been here before?" in the meaning that do you know how this works. So they have many options for breakfast which come with their do's and don'ts, so the first thing in the morning (before your morning coffee ;-) ! ) you have to be sharp, focused and fast and absorb the rules. Why don't they just simplify things?! One breakfast type in one buffet table etc. It seems to be that "this is the way we have always done things" and you just need to read through the hotel manual so that you know what to do and where.
I would not recommend this hotel to friends or family. It would be nice to tour it for the history, but staying there is not so nice.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Great stay!!!!!!”
text: Just returned from NYC, and The Belvedere was the perfect place to stay. Enough can't be said about the location. So close to Times Square and Broadway shows. But the neighborhood the hotel is located is very quite. Also, Gray Line tours is right around the corner and subway is about 3 blocks. With that said the hotel staff was very heplful and courteous. We were able to get last minute show tickets with the help of the conciere. Thanks. The staff did everything they could do to make our stay enjoyable. Next, on arrival we were told they did not have the king size bed that was reserved. But, if it would be alright we would be upgraded to a newly renovated room. This room was decorated and furnished very elegantly. Even though the room was somewhat small in a European style. It was very comfortable. And the bed was so comfortable it was a pleasure to crawl into after a day of shopping and sight seeing. Finally, we booked the NYC 1 rate. This included the breakfast buffet. This buffet was top notch food no contenental breakfast here.

name: Broadway at Times Square Hotel
title: “Right on Times Square!”
text:
My wife and I stayed 6 nights at this hotel and we chose it for the price and location. Accommodation in New York is generally expensive, but we thought that this hotel was well priced and it's location is great being right on Times Square and Broadway.
The room we had was a bit small, but adeqaute. The bed was comfortable and there was a new 40" LCD TV in the room. The hotel provides free wireless and networked internet access which was very handy. One thing that bugged us though with the room was the airconditioner was a bit noisy and our room had a view of the wall of the building next door which was about 2 metres away.
Staff were helpful and the breakfast that is served in the moring is really quite good with a selection of cerials, bagels, fruit, yoghurt, toast, juice and coffee.
If visiting NYC again, we would definitley stay there again.

name: Broadway at Times Square Hotel
title: “Convenient to Theatres and Times Square But...”
text: My teenage daughter and I enjoyed our stay in New York but probably would not stay here again. If you want to save money and want to be close to the theatres and crowds at Times Square and only need a place to sleep and eat breakfast then consider this hotel. The room was nicely decorated and reasonably clean with the exception of the windows. Absolutely filthy on the outside. I guess with all the pigeons there must not seem much point? There wasn't much to see but still not very nice. Plumbing upstairs makes noise which was tolerable when we were awake but at 4:46am was a bit much. Since the rooms are quite small you sleep near the door and can hear people talking in the hallways. Light sleepers should run the a/c as it helps mask the other sounds. Staff were generally polite; however, one desk clerk wasn't very friendly and when a street person (several sleep next door at the church) followed me in asking for $ he didn't even ask him to leave! Continental breakfast was pretty good and we never had to wait long for a seat. Don't bother taking the elevator down unless you absolutely have to; usually much faster to walk, even from the ninth floor. Two free computers in the lobby were a bonus.

name: Affinia 50
title: “Didn't live up to expectations”
text: After reading all of the great reviews, I was expecting more. We have stayed at the Kimberly and the Benjamin on the same block. The Affinia 50 doesn't compare to either in service or quality. We waited 30 minutes for bellman to come to get our bags, called front desk, said they would send someone, waited another 10 minutes before carrying them ourselves. It was very hard to catch a taxi. Doorman from the San Carlos hotel (across the street) came to help us. Very nice of him, considering that we weren't staying at the hotel. Don't know where the employees were from Affinia. Hotel rooms could use a makeover. Too much furniture in rooms to be comfortable. Could not adjust thermastat. Will not stay here again.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Best stay in NYC”
text:
We travel to NYC about 2-3 times per year for pleasure. This was our first stay at the
Waldorf (past hotels NY Hilton and Towers, Algonquin, Roosevelt, Ritz on Central
Park, Essex House, etc) and this was by far the best experience. Service was polite, 
helpful, and fast! Rooms were extremely clean with a very comfortable bed. Great
location. We actually could not find any fault with the hotel.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “First Class Hotel and Excellent Value For Money”
text: Having just returned from a four night stay at the New Yorker, have to say fab location, very clean and comfortable with friendly and helpful staff. On arrival we were upgraded to rooms on the 36th floor which had superb views over the Hudson River. The hotel was very quiet and the beds very comfy. On departure the hotel arranged our transfer to the airport at a very reasonable cost. Would highly recommend this hotel and would have no hesitation in returning.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Brilliant location!”
text:
Our first trip to NY and fell in Love with it! Hotel was more than we had hoped for with only a 2 min walk to Times Square.
First morning we were woken by drilling workmen in the bedroom next door but we were moved straight away without any fuss. The staff were all friendly and helpful, the hotel was very clean and smart looking. Be prepared where-ever you stay for the sound of Fire Engines anytime of day/night.
Would recommend to anyone going to NY and would deff go back again (hopefully next year).
Once bitten by the City you'll just want more, Fabulous Place!!!!

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “perfect”
text:
thats the second time I've stayed there, it's awesome, they have a incredible concierge service, including 2 brazilians.. Christian and Julieta, there are no words to describe them!
essa é a segunda vez que fico por lá, é maravilhoso, possuem um serviço de concierge incrível, incluindo 2 brasileiros.. christian e Julieta, sem palavras para descreve-los

name: New York Marriott Downtown
title: “wonderful hospitality”
text: It was fabulous, they looked after us so well. We had ordered a stretch limo to collect us from the airport and the whole holiday did not disappoint. Exceptionally clean and comfortable. All and more. Do not take heed of the problems with the lifts hardly bothered us at all.

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Times Square New York
title: “Fantastic view from the 34th Floor”
text: We were lucky enough to stay here free using Marriott points. Reception staff were very friendly. Upgraded to king size on our arrival, we had a room on the very top floor. The view was fantastic and overlooked the empire state building, The room was a good size and the bed very comfortable. Only odd thing was when I wanted to make a cup of tea, there were saucepans in the cupboard, but no hob! Managed to boil water in the huge microwave so even got my daily cuppa. The free buffet breakfast had a good choice of items. Overall an excellent hotel, and I would definitely stay again when visiting New York.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “New Yorker Hotel does the job”
text:
The hotel is an ideal base for all the sights of New York. We enjoyed our 5 day stay and I would recommend it. 
I would just be repeating what most of the good reviews have already said, so I will spare you the time and say "I hope you have a great time". 
In my opinion, The New Yorker Hotel does the job.

name: InterContinental New York Times Square
title: “Brand new hotel”
text:
Stayed here for a quick visit to New York and enjoyed every moment.
The front desk was very helpful, everything we asked they could arrange. Same for the entire staff.
The location is great, not hype like Soho, but good for first time visitors...

name: Pod 51
title: “Perfect, perfect, perfect”
text: We stayed at the Pod Hotel from July 1-4th. The location is terrific. We walked almost everywhere we needed to go, be it Central Park or Times Square or Herald Square. And if walking isn't your thing, there is a subway station about a block away. We had booked a bunk room but when chatting during check-in we mentioned it was our first trip away from the kid and so he gave us a complimetary upgrade to a double. Yes, the rooms are small but they are comfortable. And the shower is awesome. The neighbourhood is great and we at all times felt totally safe. Recommend eating at the Pax wholesome foods and the Ess-A-Bagel for breakfast.

name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Midtown East
title: “met my high expectations”
text:
Had a very enjoyable stay. Staff was very friendly - front desk, doorman, wait staff at restaurant. Was able to find a reasonable rate via Travelocity. Had breakfast in the Cafe on the 12th floor - breakfast buffet was $17, but very good. Utilized parking through Marriott and that was very convenient. They park the car for you, and give them 30 mins and they will bring your car around. They went as far as to stand in the street to make sure you are able to pull out of the spot. Had a corner room on the 28th floor, which had walls of windows. Room was very nice sized, especially for NYC. There were 2 thermostats and could adjust heat/AC easily.
Will stay here again, as long as I can get a good rate!

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Emplacement idéal pour un très bon hôtel”
text:
J'ai passé 12 nuits au Novotel Times Square à New York en juin et juillet 2012 avec deux amies. 
L'emplacement est idéal, au coeur de Times Square, mais un tout petit peu en retrait de l'agitation démentielle du quartier des théâtres, ce qui est vraiment agréable car certains soirs il peut y avoir une foule impressionnante !
La terasse donne une vue incroyable sur Times Square. N'hésitez pas à y aller même si vous ne consommez pas.
Notre chambre donnait au 9e étage, soit le 1er étage qui accueille des chambres mais nous avions quand même une vue superbe sur Times Square. Les chambres standards sont sobres mais très confortables (le matelas est divin !) et grandes. La salle de bain est très correct également, à la bonne taille. On m'avait dit que les chambres des hôtels New Yorkais étaient petites mais ce n'était pas du tout le cas. Concernant le bruit, on est en ville donc oui il y a un fond sonore (sirène flics, ambulances) mais c'est vraiment faible (surtout que je n'étais pas très haut, seulement au 9e étage). Une fois les fenêtres (double vitrage) fermées, vous pouvez dormir tranquille !
A la réception, il y a 5 MAC à dispo (dont 2 dans une salle un peu cachée mais accessible à tout le monde) ce qui vous permet d'aller sur Internet facilement.
Il existe également un comptoir (dans le lobby) uniquement pour vous renseigner sur des visites... On peut vous fournir des plans, infos, etc. Une des personnes s'occupant de ce comptoir est un français (si vous avez un peu de mal avec l'anglais !)
Il y a une salle de sport très bien équipée également au 8e étage.
Quelques bémols : 
- Un soir nous avons décider de manger sur la terrasse de l'hôtel (ils proposent des salades et petits plats) et franchement je vous le déconseille. C'est pas très bon et surtout très cher pour ce que c'est. Pourtant je ne suis vraiment pas difficile en matière de nourriture. 
- Nous avions entreposer quelques petites choses dans le mini bar sans rien retirer, ni consommer et le dernier jour, on nous a donné une facture de deux pages !! Bien sûr, nous l'avons contesté et la réceptionniste nous as dit qu'à chaque fois que quelque chose bougeait dans le mini bar (même sans que cela sorte du frigo) il est décompté ! Donc attention ! Ne signer pas n'importe quoi. On nous a dit qu'il était possible de demander un petit frigo en plus (mais je ne sais pas si ce service est payant).
Mise à part cela nous avons passé un excellent séjour !
Petite info : Si vous voulez (comme moi) éviter de manger tous les jours au resto, il existe près de l'hôtel "The Food Emporium" (8th Ave / 52nd St) qui vous permet d'acheter à emporter pour quelques euros des salades, fruits, légumes (je vous conseille le melon !), gateau, boisson... Le duane reade (superette) en bas de l'hôtel est bien mais le choix est vraiment très restreint.

name: Hilton New York Fashion District
title: “Nice Choice for Downtown - Wish they would try harder though”
text:
Recently stayed here for 3 night stay and overall was pretty satisfied. 
Got the basic room and it was definitely a cut above the standard NYC hotel room. Has all the bells and whistles of a NY boutique hotel room. (My particular room had a view of an alley, so a point off for the dreary view). Great Flat Screen TV where you could also access hotel info. Bed was really comfortable. Plenty of room to move around. Bathroom was well done in tile and glass. The shower logisitics are odd though. The only way in is through the glass door, and there is no way to "test" the water temp without going all the way in the shower and getting hit full force. Also, no door handle on the inside of the shower door, so the glass door slams shut and it's kind of off putting.
Maid service was very spotty. First day no service at all. I called down to the front desk at 5pm and was told housekeeping works til 6pm so no worries. At 6:30, I got a knock on the door for turndown service (Nice touch by the way) and they were shocked to discover that my room had not been cleaned. I had to leave the room for a half hour while they cleaned.
The next day I got maid service but no wAsh cloths or coffee for the coffee machine. Also no chocolate on the pillow for turn down service!!! Love that chocolate.
Some nice touches...mini cupcakes at check in! Free wifi.
Another area they really lost me though is the rooftop garden. At around 6pm they devote one of the elevators specifically to the rooftop bar. However, I suspect the bar isn't really "happening" as they would like, since there were never any lines for the roped off elevator with the smirking doorman. The lines were at the other 2 elevators where sweaty exasperated hotel GUESTS with luggage waited forever to try and get to their rooms. This is just silly and got on my nerves every night.
Also, the concierge SERIOUSLY underestimated the cost of a cabride to JFK.
Overall I think this is a really nice hotel, but they need to try a little harder to get near a level of someplace like a Kimpton Hotel. The devil is in the details and hopefully they will try a little harder, because there is much to like here.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Fabulous”
text: Simply put, the hotel is fabulous. Historical enthusiasts would love it. Beautiful lobby (ie: entire main floor). The bear and bull is great for dinner and drinks. Very pricey but giant portions. Liquid and solid ounces... The bar staff at Peacock alley were tremendously friendly and the concierges will steer you in the right direction for what you seek. (see Vinmore or Roel.... they know what you want !) The suite was spacious but a little run down, bathroom needing a little more charm. Kudos to the doormen who spend their days hailing cabs for mostly unappreciative guests... tip 'em well!!! I'll be back for sure.

name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Midtown East
title: “Always make this my NYC Home base!”
text: Have stayed at the Courtyard Marriott Midtown East for the last 2 years during convention visit. Though not as close to the Javits Center as other hotels, I would never think of staying anywhere else! Free Wireless Internet a real plus! Needed a Refrigerator the first time for some food gifts gotten when visiting family in CT. Called front desk and immediately accomodated, extra pillows etc... not a problem! I had my husband and 3 kids the first time, and there was no problem with accomodating all 5 of us in the more than spacious room. Excellent value for the money! Very good and reasonably priced (for NY) breakfast buffett, with very attentive wait staff.

name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Midtown East
title: “Good if expensive for what it offered when we visited”
text:
We picked this hotel based upon the high Trip Advisor rating and the fact that it was family-friendly. I always find it difficult to give a hotel a rating because the criterion are relative depending upon where you are, with wide variations in quality and amenities across both countries and continents. Make no mistake however, this is a good hotel. Equally, this is no five star hotel. 
The location, being within a few blocks of Bloomingdales, Saks, Tiffany and the Chrysler building is excellent. The hotel is a fantastic choice for families. The beds are comfortable and the rooms spotlessly clean, bathrooms are functional if not luxurious The views are good (although no sign of the Chrysler Buidling from room 2508 where we were). As described previously, the staff are efficient although by no means exceptionally so.
So what is the problem? Well none really aside from the fact that I was paying $600 (£300) + tax per night for what is a mid-range chain hotel. Perhaps the comparison is unfair, particularly given the fact that we probably visited NYC on the busiest weekend of the year, but I couldn't help expecting more for the money. I have read gushing reviews but where people paid half of this rate or less for rooms here. That would be fair value but we could find nothing on Priceline, Hotwire etc that came close. Perhaps we have been spolied by what you get in Singapore or the Far East for £300 (true 5 star luxury).
We too got the hotel car back to JFK at $55 inclusive of toll but excluding tip and this was a good choice after the world's smelliest cab on arrival! Also, for breakfast, the hotel kindly recommended Maddison's which is two blocks away on 1st Avenue. We ended up having breakfast there three times and it was a fantastic experience with great American breakfasts (bacon, two eggs and hash browns for $7 with unlimited coffee) and a real '50's ambiance.
All in all, I would return to the Courtyard. It's a good hotel and our family enjoyed it but I would not pay $600 plus tax per night for it. If you can get it for a more reasonable rate, do not hesitate to stay there - particularly if you are a family with children.

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “Great location but disappointing rooms.”
text: The lobby is grand but rooms are old and need updating and attention to detail. Carpets are dirty and stained . Bed was hard but sheets were high quality. Bathroom was very small with no shelf space. One phone in the room was dead and one bedside light went on only if the overhead light was on. Old hotel but could have been better if clean and attended to. Would not recommend it and don't understand the previous reviews unless they stayed in a remodeled part that we didn't know about!

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Times Square New York
title: “Strong Recommendation for Marriott's Residence Inn on 6th Ave”
text:
This hotel did not disappoint at all. The staff were very friendly, and the rooms as reviewed by others are very nice.
My queen studio was not large or terribly small but well laid out - very new and very clean. It was suitable for one or two people, but not more. The bed was exceptionally comfortable, and it was great having a full fridge (as well as dishwasher and microwave) and granite counters and eating bar (no separate eating area, though other suites have them). There is a sofa bed, but if opened it would make the room cramped, certainly for more than 2. I am not sure if they have any suites with 2 queen beds, (check out Doubletree in Times Square...there are two-room suites that are larger and you you will pay more, and not get a free breakfast). 
The bed was exceptionally comfortable and even the clock radio included a CD player. 
Location: corner of 39th Street and 6th Avenue (aka Avenue of the Americas)..you are 4 blocks from Macy's to the south (also very close to the Empire State Building) and 3 blocks to 42nd Street (the next Avenue over is Broadway and the heart of Times Square). The hotel is well situated for theatre goers and those who prefer being midway to the top attractions that you can reach by subway or by walking - the blocks in NYC are short. Technically this is the fashion district, and there are stores selling buttons, ribbons and garments around the hotel. Bryant Park is at 42nd Street and 6th and a nice respite from the city. They film Good Morning America concerts there and were also filming an Home and Garden television show for the last few days. 
The hotel is about $50 to $100 per night cheaper than comparable rooms right in Times Square (though some are larger but none that I am aware of include a free breakfast).
The very large breakfast lounge on the 3rd floor is the nicest one I have ever seen (tables and chairs but also couches and lounge chairs that are modern and in a tasteful setting, not what you may be used to). The free breakfast is from 6:30 - 9:30 weekdays and 7:00-10:00 weekends. Food is the same every day...fresh and hot, great coffee and juice. The New York Times and U.S.A. Today are made available as well. There is also a large LCD TV in a certain area. As others have indicated there are free social hour meals from 5-7 on weekdays (not Thursdays)...taco night, soup and salad...etc. Was not at the hotel during those hours to take advantage. I heard people complain about elevator service, but I was up for breakfast quite early so this was never a problem. I have never stayed at a hotel in NYC where elevator service was not slow on occasion.
The lobby is long and narrow, and a bit congested when many are checking in and out. There is free internet access at a PC at the end of the front desk with a printer. It came in incredibly handy when I misplaced my e-ticket and needed to print a new one. Kudos to Marriott for thinking of everything. Again, the staff were helpful in allowing me to email them to print my e-ticket when the pdf file could not be opened on the PC.
It is definitely worth the reasonable price (by NYC standards) and the top 3 of the 7 or so different hotels I have stayed at in NYC. I will definitely be back. 
There is nothing particularly special about the stores and things right beside the hotel...the good location refers to what is just three short blocks away to the South or North.
Tip: pack your own container to bring breakfast back to your room, if you prefer not to eat in the breakfast room. There are coffee cups to go and plastic plates, but they may not keep your food warm.
A couple of suggestions to make it better: luggage rack, NYC tourist mags in room. Not crazy about the hallway decor...but no big deal.
Enjoy this hotel, the staff and NYC.

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “tout pour plaire QUE DEMANDER DE PLUS”
text:
Hôtel situé idéalement dans le centre tout prêt de la grande gare centrale (à peine 15 mns à pied).
Beaucoups de choses à voir et à faire à pied...
Supermarché, bar et restaurants à proximité.
Confort de la chambre top peut-être à part le petit electroménager qui pourrait être changer ( fait "jouet" à cause de son plastique ceci dit, il fonctionne parfaitement) .
JE RECOMMANDE CET HOTEL ET Y RETOURNE DES MON PROCHAIN SEJOUR

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Times Square New York
title: “fabulous marriot”
text: My wife and I just returned from the City, the Residence Inn Time Square was fabuolus right from the minute we arrived until we left, we even had to stay an extra night due to bad weather. The staff was very friendly and helpful, the rooms were very comfortable, great having a fridge and micrwave and sitting area. We had a great view of the Empire state building on the 8th floor. There is a great market 20 steps outside the front door, grab some beer and wine and snacks and you are good to go. Did I mention hot buffet breakfast every morning and from Monday to Thursday happy hour on the third floor lounge(the entire third floor) from 5-7pm we had Lasagna and Ceasar Salad one evening all included in the price. Did I mention that yes I was in New York City getting all these extras included in one price. Thank You Marriot, my wife and I have travelled everywhere who in the world rated this hotel only 3-stars this is the only Hotel in 20 years of marriage that my wife has taken her shoes off in a Hotel room. The front Lobby is small that must be the reason it is only a three star Hotel.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Great Hotel & Location”
text: Booked this hotel after reading reviews on this site. The hotel upgraded our room to a New Yorker which was much appreciated. Our room (2107) had a view of the Hudson River, it was spacious enough and spotlessly clean. The staff were very courteous and helpful, which made our stay all the more enjoyable. The location was perfect and we would definately stay here again. The Tick Tock Diner was also very good for breakfast as was the Skylight Diner on 34th street. Times Square, ESB, Rockefeller Centre, etc are all walkable from this location. We purchased the 7 day subway pass $27 each and was excellent value. (see our trip report).

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Times Square New York
title: “Great Place”
text: We stayed just one night, but loved it. Very clean (it's new), luxurious bedding, very good breakfast. Helpful staff - they recommended and made a reservation for us at a nearby vegetarian restaurant that were very good. The location is perhaps the best thing. It was very easy to get in and out of the place (on a weekend, anyway). Also, it was walking distance to Times Square area, theater, but just enough away that you felt out of the craziness once you wanted to get a little peace and quiet. Highly recommend it.

name: Affinia 50
title: “Great Place, Great Price!”
text: My fiance and I recently went to NYC on a little weekend getaway, and had gotten a GREAT deal on this hotel. It was everything you could ask for, CLEAN, friendly staff, AMAZING location. We would absolutely reccomend this to anyone!

name: Broadway at Times Square Hotel
title: “Location Location Location”
text:
Location for Times Square you cannot beat. Hotel room was large enough and cleaned on a daily basis. Limited breakfast with a "jobsworth" attendant very curt and somewhat rude when people didnt use the bread tongues, and place holders in the correct place. To be honest we got some amusement watching his face when this happened.
The hotel lift is very small so be aware when taking suitcases upto your room.
Dont let these picky remarks put you off as we are going back again for New Year. Location is ideal, rooms clean and large enough. 
3 Star hotel in a 5 Star location.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Great hotel experience”
text:
My mum and I stayed at the Sofitel New York from August 29 to September 1. We were celebrating her birthday, attending plays and going to the US Open. We can not speak more highly of the hotel and all of its staff people. 
We arrived just at 3pm on a Saturday and you could tell the front desk was very busy taking care of people checking out and in - even with about five people working behind the desk. I had to wait in line for about 5 minutes and, once I got to the desk, was apologised to profusely for the delay. 
The staff person noted that we had reserved a superior room with two single beds and said that he would check with housekeeping to find us what we had requested. But then he added that he had an upgraded luxury king room available immediately and asked if we wanted it instead. We agreed. 
We were located on the 15th floor with an inside view (that is to say, a view of a the back of buildings - not incredibly beautiful, but very New York/urban looking!) The room itself was excellent - there was ample closet space and hangers, bathrobes and slippers, a gorgeous bathroom with separated bath and shower and a fresh orchid as well as a super comfy bed. The room also boasted a Bose radio with ipod connector and a lovely, giant flat screen tv. 
Coffee is sadly not available in the room but the hotel does make it available for free each morning in its restaurant.
The room was impeccably clean and housekeeping staff returned nightly for turndown service (complimentary bottles of water were a nice touch) when they would do a second daily tidying session. 
The doormen were very kind - were always quick to help open doors and offer a friendly smile and greeting. We didn't take a cab the entire time we were in the city, but saw that they were exceptionally helpful at hailing these for hotel guests. 
We did not eat in the hotel restaurant but did go there for post-theatre drinks on our first night in town. My mother had a glass of white wine for about $13 and I had a very, very stiff manhattan on the rocks for $11 - an excellent deal, especially when both liberally-poured drinks came with ample complimentary bar snacks (cheese crisps and olives). If, for some reason, I am unable to stay at the Sofitel during another trip to the city, I would definitely consider returning to their bar for drinks given the nice ambiance, proximity to the theatre district and affordable pricing. 
The one thing we did note that could be improved was that at night the hotel lobby's lighting was dimmed so considerably that it was almost *too* dark inside. Also, the cost of wi-fi in the rooms was a bit high. That said, the hotel did have three computers with internet access available free of charge for guests in the front lobby. 
I would definitely recommend the Sofitel to anyone wanting to stay in midtown and look forward to returning in the future.

name: Broadway at Times Square Hotel
title: “Great value, great location, too much heat”
text: Our room was located on the seventh floor facing a building. The gentleman that checked us in told us that he was going to put us on the quiet side of the hotel. Quiet meant facing a brick wall, which really didn't bother my husband and I. The main problem was the temperature of the room. It was uncomfortably warm and there was no way to turn the heat down. We voiced our concerns at the desk and the said that they would look intoit. Obviously there was ot much that anyone could do, since the heating system seems to be automatic. Even though there was a sign that said not to open the window, we did anyway. Unfortunately this did not help the temperature of the room. I'm not sure what the answer to the problem was. The morning breakfast was quite adequate and the location could not be beat. Maybe if it is cold outside itwould not be a problem. I should have tried plugging in the air conditioning unit to see if that would have cooled off the room.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Suited us perfectly”
text:
Our family of 5 visited NYC and stayed at the New Yorker in a doubles suite. The suite consisted of 2 large rooms - one with 2 double beds and a tv, the other with a sofa bed, desk, large dining table with 6 chairs, fridge, and another tv. There was also a huge L-shaped terrace overlooking the corner of 34th & 8th. So we had magnificent views of the Empire State Building, Madison Square Gardens, as well as views in the distance of many prominent buildings. Our room rate included breakfast vouchers for each day to get a coffee/tea, juice, and muffin/bagel/pastry. We paid an extra $40/night to guarantee ourselves a terrace since we like to unwind on the balcony after a busy day of touring.
The room was clean and newly renovated. The hotel felt very safe with the security at the elevators asking to see your room key. The subway was right at the corner as well as nearby hop-on/hop-off bus stops. It was a 10 minute walk to Times Square or the Empire State Building.
We used the valet parking. There was plenty of space out front to unload so that was not a hassle. It was quite easy to drive in through the Lincoln Tunnel then the hotel is right there.
The gift shop had very good prices compared to the shops around town. We did not eat at the Tick Tock Diner other than our breakfast vouchers. The coffee and muffins were large and good.
The free wifi came in handy mapping out our schedule for the day. The room was surprisingly quiet for sleeping.
All in all this hotel suited our needs perfectly.

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “Full-Service in One Stop”
text: Travelled to NYC for the first time with my girlfriend who has been there before. A friend suggested this hotel because of their known reputation on great service. We were impressed that the Guest Relations agent was able to answer all our questions and take care of our requests/reservations all in one visit to her desk. Usually chain hotels send you to 3 different places with 3 different lines. Very professional and knowledgable staff who value their guests' time and business. Great stay and great visit. We will return to the Barclay.

name: Broadway at Times Square Hotel
title: “Great location!”
text:
This hotel is in a great location. It is less than a block from Times Square and nearby everything a tourist would want to do.
We got there early in the morning, and although we were not able to check in, we were able to drop our luggage off and they stored it in a locked room. The room was relatively small, but I was only there to sleep and shower. It was very clean and had an iron, ironing board, and extra pillows in the small closet. There was a window air conditioner in the room, which was relatively quite, and quickly cooled the room down, which was a relief being it was nearly 100 degrees and very humid in New York! The bathroom was a decent size and stocked w/ amenities. It also had a small coffee maker. My only complaint about the bathroom was the lack of water pressure in the shower.
The staff was very freindly and helpful. We had gone to NYC to go to a Yankees game. We knew that we could easily take the subway into the Bronx, but not sure which one to go on. The lady at the front desk was very helpful in advising us what train to get on and told us exactly where the subway station was (about a block away). When we checked out, we had several hours before we had to be at the airport and again they held our luggage for us as we explored more of the city.The bellhop, was a very nice gentleman who offered to get us a car service to the airport for a flat rate. We took him up on this, as it was about the same price as the cab fare getting there was and we did not have to worry about hailing our own cab. 
I didn't have the free breakfast they offered, but it looked like there was plenty of food, bagels, danish, coffee etc. There are numerous restaurants right on the same block as the hotel, there is a very reasonably priced deli nearby, that had a phenomenal breakfast. 
I would definelty stay in this hotel again. It is in a great location. And the price can not be beat. For a 2 night stay, in a room with 2 twin beds for a weekend it only cost $360. I have been to NYC a few times before and have stayed at more expensive places, and I can tell you from experience the more expensive places, although they are bigger and have a more elegant lobby, this place can definetly compete with them. So, if you are going to NYC to have fun and explore the city and just need a clean and comfortable place to sleep and shower, this is the place.

name: Pod 51
title: “Bon rapport qualité-prix”
text:
Hôtel bien situé dans midtown. Très belle réception avec lobby attenant décoré très design (Egg chairs), iPads aux murs et wifi gratuit. Petite alcove-café sympa pour le petit déjeuner et prix corrects. Petite terrasse agréable. 
Chambres individuelles (shared bathroom) propres, assez petites mais très correctes et fonctionnelles. Wifi gratuit dans la chambre. 
Salles de bains et toilettes partagés. Propres. 
Un hôtel à recommander dans cette catégorie de prix.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Fragrant, quiet, sanctuary centrally located in New York”
text: From the moment you step into the fragrantly scented candle lit lobby you will be won over by this lovely hotel. The staff are professional, efficient and helpful. Our room we a reasonable size for NY with a great view over the Chrysler Building. The location is only a block and a bit from Times Square one way, a block from Grand central station and a block from 5th Ave. Excellent location. The best thing was the L'Occitane products in the bathroom, just wonderful. We really enjoyed our stay here.

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Times Square New York
title: “Hotel Residence Inn - fint værelse til 3”
text: Vi var 3 voksne personer i et studie med køkken faciliteter midt på Manhattan - tæt på seværdigheder, butikker og subway. Der var desuden adgang til trådløst internet samt morgenmad inkluderet i prisen. Personalet var venligt og serviceminded. Hotellet kan varmt anbefales

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Great place with easy access to Downtown New York”
text:
We've just come back from a great stay at On The Ave. The hotel is superbly located just 2 blocks from the No 1 subway line on 79th and Broadway, just 5 stops from Times Square. 
We booked on line and asked in advance for a quiet room. Our request was noted and met. The room was spacious and well appointed.
The hotel has no facilities other than free wi-Fi in reception. However the Manhattan diner across the street is slice of pure Americana. There's also a terrific store just across Broadway which has just about everything under the sun in it!

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “No Frills”
text: I stayed here for two nights recently. The lobby is quite spacious and there is adequate seating throughout. I usually judge a hotel initially based upon the condition of the lobby. Anyway, upon entering our room, I was immediately taken aback by the actual size of it. Granted, hotel rooms in NYC are never large; however, I was expecting a little more space. Perhaps the designers could’ve spent a little less time designing the lobby and a little more time focusing on the actual guest rooms. When trying to get some sleep the first night, I was awakened numerous times by other guests staying on our floor. The hotel walls are not sound proof by any means. When I awakened in the morning, I noticed what appeared like an insect bite. I thought I might have gotten bitten by a mosquito but then realized that the season temperature was not warm enough for mosquitoes. I later learned that my bite was probably the result of bed bugs. As you can imagine, I definitely won’t be staying here again.

name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Midtown East
title: “muy buen hotel”
text: Muy buen hotel, en midtown, cerca del metro,desayuno muy completo, nos alojamos dos adultos con tres niños y la habitación era muy cómoda, (dos dobles y sofa cama). Lo recomiendo. ( lo único que le agregaría es un frigobar)

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “For once, better 'in the flesh' than web images !”
text:
Stayed for 7 days in October - really enjoyed my stay & would have no hesitation in returning / recommending to others. I must confess to being a little apprehensive prior to arrival - more often than not, the web-site images portray a better than reality image - not in this case !
The Hotel was extremely well maintained, comfortable & clean. Breakfast (as to be expected) was a little dearer than local cafes - but I soon returned the following day/s - i.e. the small increase in cost is far out-weighed by the quality of food / customer service.
Very convenient location, Grand Central is only a very short walk. Also subway very close.
Most Hotels in NY don't have a pool (The Barclay included) - but the fitness centre is very good, also the best steam room I've ever been in, c/w sauna etc.
Decor is a little dated (in terms of material/colour choice), but nothing to be concerned about - everything is in excellent condition.
Well done The Barclay !

name: Affinia 50
title: “Great experience at the Affinia 50”
text:
We just returned from a trip to NY and stayed at the Affinia 50. We were very pleased with this experience and this hotel is a real gem.
 We reserved a one bedroom suite with a king bed. Initially when we got to our room we saw that we had a queen bed. We called down to the front desk and told them that we had reserved a room with a king bed. They told us they would get us a different room and in about 40 minutes we had a room change. We were given what must have been a deluxe room on the 21st floor. This was the best hotel room we've ever had. It was huge with multiple windows, very clean and nicely appointed. Our teenage son had his own space and we had ours. 
I would highly recommend this hotel especially if you are traveling with kids.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “this place is a DUMP!!!!!”
text: This hotel is a dump!!! I understand it used to be a famous hotel in olden days and came under the false impression that this is a five star hotel. It absolutely is not! The place is run down, you can tell the decor is outdated, wallpaper is peeling off..the rooms feel old and stuffy, I was even reluctant to go under the covers or use the towels. The bathrooms are very ordinary and If I had just seen the bathroom, wouldnt be able to tell if it was the doubletree or hampton inn bathroom! Overall, the hotel is not in a good condition, there are signs of age and bad design everywhere, would not recommend this hotel if you are looking for a clean, modern and sophisticated experience in New York. Would recommend some of the newer hotels in the city. The management of the Waldorf really need to spice up their act, and hire better designers and housekeeping services. The staff is also rude and abrupt, they need to do a major overhaul to this place, to make this a truly competitive hotel, get rid of the old stuffy look. If they really want to go for the classic look, they should take a lesson from the ritz carltons in the city, that are painstaking in detail and incredibly clean and luxurious, while at the same time being modern. This hotel does not even come close !!!

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Times Square New York
title: “Mariott Residence Inn New York”
text: Hôtel très bien situé à côté de Bryant Park et Times Square, excellentes prestations: kitchenette, chambre spacieuse et en excellent état. L'accueil du personnel et l'entretien au quotidien de la chambre sont assez désinvoltes.

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Times Square New York
title: “Muy buena ubicacion”
text:
El hotel cuenta con una buena ubicación y tiene un desayuno incluido de buena calidad.
Las habitaciones están equipadas con nevera, microondas, utensilios de cocina e incluso te ofrecen el servicio de comprarte las cosas de comida que necesites durante tu estancia. Las habitaciones son pequeñas, nosotros éramos 3 adultos un niño pequeño y entre las maletas el espacio se reducía.
Tiene un sofá cama, en donde la calidad del colchón es bastante mala, así que dormir aquí es muy incomodo

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “amazing first trip to new york”
text: just spent five nights in new york the city that never sleeps!! we stayed at the new yorker hotel. the staff were all very friendly and helpful nothing was to much trouble check in and out was very quick the staff at the tick tock diner were lovely. we would recommend using grayline bus trips we brought a three day pass which gave us unlimited travel on the hop on hop off buses the guided tours were excellent . every where we went we had a great time can't wait to go back and explore some more. saw most of the tourist attractions two attractions and a trip to statue of liberty and ellis island where apart of the grayline pass which we brought at the tourist information on time square. the hotel was ideally situated for most attractions with the grid system new york is easy to walk around

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan / Times Square South
title: “Nähe Times Square, Subway Station,”
text:
Sehr gutes und vielseitiges Frühstück, traumhafte Betten, zentrale Lage.
Personal an der Rezeption teilweise sehr unfreundlich. Vor allem die männlichen Angestellten. Hotel selbst kann ich sehr empfehlen, war schon 4x in NYC.

name: Pod 51
title: “Love the urban look and location of The Pod Hotel”
text: I love this modern little hotel. The location was fantastic! I stayed here in June 2007 and would tell anyone I know to check it out. The staff was really friendly and helpful with questions. The room was tiny, but great for a couple on a weekend away. If you have more than 2 people, make sure you get the larger room! Our room was clean and modern so I loved it!

name: Affinia 50
title: “Of all of the things I have an affinity for...... AFFINIA 50 is on the top 5!”
text:
I am a business traveler, so my opinion of hotels tends to be that of the most honest. We live in hotel and we are thier mostregular customers. We have high demands and we know what hotels accomodate our needs. This hotel, is one of them. I frequent NY and I have stayed at this hotel 15 times in the last 12 months. To give you an even better understanding of my loyalty I have stayed at Affinia-owned properties at least 25 times in the last 15 months. It has taken some time, but I now walk through the door, and am greeted by my name. (A nice perk) I can honestly say, that there are other hotels in othre locations that I have stayed at more friently that what I have professed at this hotel, and still, I recieve no recognition. That is how this hotel differs.
I can honestly say, this hotel is more what you expect. If you want a hotel that is provides you with the basics, questionable cleanliness, and no flares, then this hotel is not for you. However, if you want individualized expedient service, spacious immaculate rooms ( moms: you'd feel comfortable bringing your baby here with littlefears of MRSA or E.Coli), hospitable staff, yum-a-licious room service, updated furniture, a comfortable & safe setting, ample outlets, and the coziest bed you have ever slumbered in (to the point where you even contemplate stuffing the whole bed in your luggage and running off with it)..... then this is where you belong. Their level of hospitality surmounts every other hotel you've stayed in and is notthing you would ever expect. The reason why thier motto is hospitality is because they are the best of the best. If ever you wanted to live and be treated like royalty, I would suggest you give this hotel a try. They are receptive to couples, older individuals, families, business travelers, everyone. 
Being a business traveler I find this hotel to be very accommodating to my needs.
1. Outlets- tons of them!
2. Office space-- There is an ergonomic chair and a generous size desk that allows me to work.
3. Living space- Good size. Amble seating. Clean and updated furniture. There is even an outlet nearby where I can work and watch TV at the same time. 
4. Bed- A million times better than the Sealy Posturepedic I have at home. I never had REM sleep like that in my life, it was the best!!
5. Room service- Yum-a licious!! (Especially the lentil soup at Mint)
There are truly no words to articulate the greatness that exists in staying at this hotel. I have stayed at places from the Hampton Inn to the 5 star hotels during my stays in New York City, and still....hands down, I’d choose here over any of those. So if you want to be treated like you deserve, I implore you to share in my affinity for Affinia.

name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Midtown East
title: “Courtyard Mariott East Manhattan - Stort fint rum”
text: Kanonbra rum för familj med tre tonåringar eftersom det finns bäddsoffa. Rent och fräscht. Bra läge med en kvarts promenad till Rockefeller center och Central park. Tunnelbana alldeles utanför och flera bra matställen. Vi hade turen att få ett rum med fantastisk utsikt längs tredje avenyn. Skulle boka samma hotell igen.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Great hotel, great location!”
text: We had originally booked for the Waldorf Astoria but having seen recent reviews changed to the Sofitel. We weren't disappointed. We arrived around midnight in a very cold New York but the welcome was very warm. We were shown to our room which was spacious, had a great bathroom with views onto the Empire State and Chrysler Buildings. We ate breakfast in the Red Flame Grill a few yards from the hotel as recommended by other reviewers and couldn't fault it. The hotel has a great location - just off 5th Avenue and great shopping and within a few minutes walk of Times Square and Grand Central Station. The staff were very friendly and helpful and we were given a 3pm checkout on our last day - just 15 minutes before we were due to be picked up for the airport. The bed was really comfortable and despite it's central location we had virtually no noise - just the very occasional emergency vehicle siren that you get in any big city. We didn't use the hotel restaraunt as there are so many great places to eat nearby we explored New York's cuisine. We would certainly recommend the Sofitel and would stay there again.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “The New Yorker is a centrally-located, comfortable place to stay.”
text:
We liked our stay at The New Yorker hotel. Its location is literally across the street from access to trains, buses and subways. Times Square is right down the street within decent walking distance. My wife and I came to NYC to celebrate our anniversary (noting as such in our reservation). We stayed here two nights and had our 19 month old son with us. 
The staff was very courteous and professional. We reserved the Metro Room/2 doubles, and we were given a nice room with a direct view of the Empire State Building. Also, we were pleased to find the hotel room, lobby, and amenities are just as they are described and pictured. I liked the room and how it was decorated with contemporary furnishings. We had to report an issue with the water not being hot enough, but the front desk took care of it right away. They even sent an engineer to our room to ensure we were satisfied. They get a kudos for quick response! 
The Tick Tock diner was a good experience, also. The food is reasonably priced, tasty, and served fast! Our server was friendly too. 
I found the size of the room satisfactory, despite the number of reviews claiming the rooms are too small. I must admit it is slightly smaller than what you might expect, but not enough to complain about. The room is big enough to do what a traveler needs to do in a hotel room- sleep, shower and veg out. It also has a walk-in closet with iron/ironing board. 
We were a little disappointed that there was no coffee maker in the room, as we have come to expect this amenity in two-star and above hotels (the New Yorker being a 3-1/2 star). Although you have the on-site restaurant, it does not replace the convenience of being able to start your day with coffee before getting dressed.
Overall, this a great hotel to stay in. Its proximity to public transportation is a true selling point. We would definitely stay here in some of our future visits to New York City.

name: InterContinental New York Times Square
title: “Best value in town”
text: We checked in to the Intercontinental at nite time and it was wonderful our rooms were facing north and had the best beds Cava the restraurant down stairs is wonderful and the food is first class

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Great location, rooms, service and food!”
text: Wonderful hotel. Rooms are beautifully finished and extremely comfortable without being fussy or uncomfortably trendy. Service is amazing. Staff in all departments are polite and gracious. Hotel is in the perfect business and leisure location. Will be my hotel of choice in New York from now on!

name: Pod 51
title: “Rooms small and a tad pricey, but great location!”
text:
I've just come back from a stay at the Pod. I emailed them direct to book two rooms. I received a confirmation number for the reservation and re-confirmed my rooms the day before I was arriving. I arrived at the hotel about 11pm and when I tried to book in they had no evidence of my booking, even though I had emails from reception confirming the booking. One receptionist was quite rude and refused to believe I had a booking. Fortunately a very kind person called Lau came to my assistance and luckily managed to find me two rooms.
The Pod is in a great location right in midtown. The rooms are very small but to be honest we were hardly in ours. I think the rooms were a little overpriced but I presume it must be due to the time of year. Also, it was snowing in NY when we were there and in both our rooms the heating was really tempermental and would work one day and not the next.
All that said, I would still recommend the Pod Hotel as it is a quirky place, situated on a quietish street. When checking out the staff were very helpful, arranging transfers to the airport and looking after the luggage. They also have a cool roof terrace which I imagine would be great in the summer but is not the best when its snowing.
I would stay in the Pod again as I've stayed in a few different hotels in NY and this was definately one of the better ones. My only advice is reconfirm your reservation and make sure you take a print out of your email just in case of any mix ups.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Great stay at On the Ave”
text:
We stayed at On the Ave for four nights from 08 Oct to 12 Oct 2010. We took three rooms in all, two being panoramic deluxe rooms and one a twin bedded room. Myself and my partner stayed in one of the panoramic deluxe rooms on the fourteenth floor with a channelled view towards the Hudson River.
I generally never book a standard room at any hotel as I always worry about the lowest price rooms. By booking a panoramic deluxe room I had hoped for a larger room but as the room had a small terrace and was reasonably well equipped we were quite happy. The rooms do not have safes which I missed and meant we had to carry our valuables everywhere with us. Our carpeting was also dirty and / or stained, but these were the only two criticisms we had. Generally the staff were really friendly and helpful and we loved our stay.
It was quite clear that the management cared for their guests and I thank them for making our stay so comfortable. I had read previous reviews about slow lifts but we were on holiday so we didn't really find the lifts a big problem. If I was rushing to a meeting then maybe I would have stressed a bit as the doors do take time to open and close.
The location is great and there are plenty of place to eat in the area.
We will be back, thanks again On the Ave - you are doing a great job.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Novotel Time Square : bien situé mais pas propre”
text:
J'ai séjourné 5 nuits avec ma femme dans cet hôtel, au 18ème étage.
Nous avions une très belle vue sur Time Square. Par contre, niveau propreté, c'est indécent : outre le fait que ça sente la cigarette dans le couloir, que les moquettes soient sales, qu'il y ait un trou dans le mur du couloir, notre chambre n'a pas été faite systématiquement (nous avons donc dû demander des serviettes supplémentaires).
La literie est de qualité très moyenne et les oreillers hors d'age sont insuffisants quand on regarde les hôtels équivalents. Nous avons déjà séjourné dans d'autres hôtels à Time Square qui, pour un prix équivalent, sont largement mieux sur tous ces points

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “Fantastic stay”
text: This hotel was fabulous. The location is great (10 minute walk to Rockefeller Centre, Times Square, Grand Central Station). It IS a bit outdated, but the room sizes are huge for an NYC hotel and offer everything needed for a great stay. This trumps the outdated room (tube TV's rather than flat-screens - older wall paper - but, I don't really care about those things anyway - just an observation). The staff was prompt, helpful and extremely accommodating. The bedding was plush and comfortable, shower had great water pressure and the room has a safe for storing extra cash or any valuables. We forgot toothpaste and asked the front desk for any travel size tubes. When we returned to our room, we had toothpaste, toothbrushes, floss and mouthwash waiting on the bed. Great stay!

name: Hilton New York Fashion District
title: “Fresh & clean!”
text:
Great service, the hotel is brand new.
Only drawback is no breakfast included within the price, and the rooms are not very well sound isolated towards the hallway. When people walk in the hallway, you hear everything - wich can be quite irritating when someone comes home in the middle of the night and disturbes your sleep.
Very strange that they haven't thought of this, since the hotel was brand new in 2010.
Otherwise no complaints.

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “Loved It, Loved It, Loved It!!!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel from February 15-17 and it was fabulous! The staff is extremely friendly and helpful! We stayed in a Junior Suite which included a kitchenette. Inside of the kitchenette there is a stove and oven, a sink including a small bottle of Palmolive dishwashing detergent and dish cloths, a lot of cabinet space which held a small frying pan and a medium sized sauce pan and 4 dinner plates, 4 saucers, 4 coffee cups, 4 drinking glasses and 4 champagne/wine glasses. Inside of the kitchen drawer we found all of the silverware/utensils we needed including 4 forks, 4 teaspoons, 4 knives, 4 tablespoons, a cutting knife, and a can opener which also included a bottle opener. The kitchen held a regular sized garbage can and also had a cutting board. There was also a regular sized refrigerator.
In the other room there was a table for two for us to eat at which could also double as a desk. There was plenty of closet (3 closets) space and drawer space. There was a couch directly opposite our King Sized Bed which pulled out to a Queen Sized sofa bed. The room also had a 19 inch color TV and you are given the option of playing Playstation games through the television (for an hourly rate), ordering pay per view movies, and paying to access the jukebox through the television. 
There are a few interactive features on the television, one of which allows you to view your bill and checkout through the tv.
We ordered room service from the restaurant in the hotel and the food is delicious. They specialize in Italian food and we ordered around 8 PM and had our dinner in 15 minutes. There is a menu for room service and for breakfast from a diner nearby. You can get breakfast almost as quickly as the room service dinner when you order. Breakfast was great too! a good tip: When you order breakfast ask them to send you a menu because they have great food! You might want to ask the front desk for menus to nearby restaurants too. One of the places that has great food is Sarge's.
The room had great decor and, the bathroom was nice and clean and the hotel provides you with their own conditioner shampoo, mouthwash, body wash, and moisturizer. The soap that they provide smells heavenly. Even better than some of the soaps that I've used at the larger more expensive hotels. It smells like there's Eucalyptus oil in it.
My husband and I added a few of the romance specials to our room. The first night we had champagne and chocolate covered strawberries and we had the rose petal turndown. We had asked for this to be in the room upon arrival but there was a slight mixup with the time. I called down to the front desk letting them know what time we would be going out and when we came back rose a trail of rose petals led from the door to the bed, our sheets were turned down, and rose petals were scattered on the bed in the shape of a heart and a long stem red rose with baby's breath and palm was placed in the center of the heart.
The staff is very accomodating and helpful. Check-out is at 12 Noon but they are willing to make arrangements if you would like to check out at a later time. We checked out at 2PM.
Grand Central Station is within walking distance of the hotel and there are a lot of great stores as well as supermarkets in the area. There are a few liquor stores and banks as well.
If you want to stay at a place that will feel like home, try the Eastgate. We will definitely be staying there again. We also would ike to try some of the other Affinia properties.

name: Hilton New York Fashion District
title: “Posizione perfetta a Chelsea/Flatiron”
text: Ho soggiornato 6 notti a settembre 2010 al Fashion 26 (l'albergo era della catena Whyndam, mentre ora è passato sotto la gestione Hilton). Si tratta di un albergo praticamente nuovo. Avevo una stanza sufficientemente ampia (per gli standard di NY) con un ampio bagno e doccia confortevole. Grande tv ldc hd, doc per ipod. Armadio e cassaforte, macchina per caffè espresso in camera con ampia dotazione di cialde, frigobar (un po' sguarnito). Wifi veloce e gratis, quotidiano ogni giorno in camera. Durante il check-in mi hanno accolto con un vassoio di dolci. Personale molto disponibile. Per gli standard di NY e la stagione, il costo era davvero competitivo. La posizione è davvero invidiabile, è nella zona di NY che preferisco: caotica ma a due passi si trova la tranquillità di un parco. Ristorante sulla terrazza con carne alla griglia: panorama suggestivo. Consiglierei senz'altro di soggiornare qui.

name: Eastgate Tower
title: “a disappointment”
text: i was disapionted with the eastgate tower, the suite i stayed in was spacious but VERY outdated, the lobby was very nice, but small, also the fitness center had minimal offerings and needless to say was very small, i would not recommend this hotel unless you are on a tight budget and need to stay there

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Good Experience”
text:
Booked a junior suite at what is certainly one of the better hotels in New York. Bed comfortable and rooms relatively quiet despite being adjacent to the lifts.
Bathroom good with upmarket toiletries. 
Some of the fittings are become tired but generally I liked the hotel.
The bedroom was rather dark and lights were needed most of the time to provide reasonable illumination. The bar and restaurant are also rather gloomy and fairly pricey to match. After breakfast on the first morning we decided to eat at the Red Flame emporium just along from the hotel - many other hotel guests also used the Red Flame. The food in the restaurant was very good and the waiters cheerful, but the food was slow in delivery.
There are three PCs in the reception area for guest use. The hotel is in a good location. The staff were helpful and accommodating when overcoming an error in the original booking.
I would stay at the hotel if I visit New York in the future.

name: InterContinental New York Times Square
title: “Posizione strategica.”
text: L'hotel gode di una posizione veramente strategica. Vicinissimo a Times Square , sulla 44th, a due passi dai più importanti teatri di Broadway. Nelle vicinanze sono numerose le possibilità per consumare pasti per tutte le tasche: dai fastfood ai ristoranti eleganti e rinomati. Avendo soggiornato nel periodo natalizio, mi sarei aspettato una hall più accogliente ed addobbata per le feste, invece era alquanto fredda e spoglia di decorazioni. La camera prenotata era una de luxe: le dimensioni non erano generose, ma confortevole, ordinata e pulita. Disponibile e gratuito il deposito bagagli dopo aver effettuato il check-out. Peccato per la mancanza di una connessione wifi gratuita.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Great Hotel, Great Location, Great Price”
text: Trip Advisor steered me right again. Based upon reviews here, I decided to spend 3 nights at this terrific hotel. What a location! Half a block from 8th Ave, right in the heart of the theater district and a few blocks from Times Square. The bed was very comfortable, the room sizable for the price range. Bathroom was well appointed and clean. I had an end room on the 4th floor, but surprisingly the noise wasn't an issue, either from the street or from the service elevator. I didn't use guest services or visit the lounge/resturaunt, so I can't comment on that. I'll gladly stay at the Belvedere again!

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Wow...what a trip , can I do it all over again please....”
text: The hotel was very clean and the staff were more than helpful, room was wonderful with fantastic views , the tic tock diner next door was a godsend with good food at resonable prices,just what you need after long day of walking. Hotel central to macys, 5th ave for shopping and broadway. Would definatley return to this hotel. My only comment is that the drinks vending machines on our landing were not stocked up and would have been very handy for a thirsty traveller.

name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Midtown East
title: “Rien à redire - quand on trouve un prix de chambre correct”
text:
