Hotel bien situé (52eme / 1ere avenue) au dessus d'une bouche de métro ... excessivement pratique lorsqu'on repart avec les bagages et les tonnes d'affaires achetées à NY! A quelques blocs du MOMA, de la 5eme avenue, de central park et de times square).
Avons eu sur demande une chambre à un étage élevé (28 eme) mais toute les chambres sont au minimum au 15eme étage.
La chambre est grande (beaucoup plus qu'au marriot times square south), la literie moelleuse et confortable, la salle de bain nickel. Seuls reproche : pas TV5, pas de mini bar ni de frigo.
Le petit déjeuner, renégocié au check in car inclus dans le prix, méritait de cette négo : très copieux et de bons produits.
Bref, quand on trouve un bon prix : ne pas hésiter. Pour 4 personnes, les chambres sont de bonnes dimensions (demander la 3019 et certainement toutes les chambres en --19 car est bien plus grande que les autres!).
la vue est vers l'Est, sympa mais sans plus.

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan / Times Square South
title: “Convenient to Javits Center & Times Square”
text:
I stayed two nights at this Hampton Inn in May 2011 while in town for a conference at the Javits Center. It's a tall skinny building, with about 5 rooms per floor. The staff was excellent, check in was quick. I had asked for a high floor, to get away from the street noise, and they gave me the top floor (32). It was indeed quiet, apart from the occasional siren that you'll find in any city. The room was a bit small, but reasonable for NYC standards, and it was clean. When I discovered there were only two elevators which the cleaning staff also needs to use, I was a bit concerned, but though some have noted the slow elevator, the wait was never notably longer than any other high rise hotel. I also had no trouble finding a table at breakfast around 8:30 am either morning. The free breakfast was the same as at any Hampton (self-made waffles, breads and pastries, fruit, cereal, coffee/tea/juice, a few hot items, etc.) I easily walked to Times Square and the Javits Center, so the location was great.
There were only a few minor negatives for me. The hallway where the elevators are is narrow, connecting the small lobby to the dining area, which made it hard to get on and off the elevator when people were waiting (which they generally were). It was several blocks to the nearest sit-down restaurant, and the hotel (like all Hampton Inns) doesn't offer room service and only had snack machines on a few floors. The air conditioner, controlled by thermostat, blew a strong current of cold air clear across the room--though Hampton Inn beds are always comfortable, they only provide a sheet and duvet, which meant a choice from being too hot, or sleeping in a cold draft. Finally, there was no bottled water provided in the room (again, not unusual for a Hampton Inn), but they offered complimentary water at the front desk on request. 
I think this is a great hotel for business travellers or anyone in town for an event at the Javits. However, the rooms would probably prove a bit cramped for a family with kids.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Will keep going back without hesitation.”
text: We are just back from a fabulous 4 nights in the Sofitel. The hotel couldn't have been better. As it was a special occasion they upgraded us to a better room on 27th floor with a great view of the Chrysler building, we never shut the cutrains! All staff were so friendly and helpful I am already wondering when I can make it back there!

name: Pod 51
title: “Excellent value, location etc”
text:
My boyfriend and i stayed in the pod hotel for 5 nights in Aug. 
I can't understand why reviews have been suprised by the size of the rooms - The hint is in the hotel name, The Pod - saying that the hotel was great. Yes is is small but you are in NYC and why would you want to stay in your room other than sleep and shower?? We stayed on 7th floor facing the road. Not too noisy at all.
The location is great, walking distance to everything. Roof garden is such a bonus. they don't mind you taking food up there and we had a few beers too. Its great to watch NYC lights at nigth.
I am looking to go back to NYC next year and will defo be staying here.

name: Affinia 50
title: “Affinia 50, exellent hotel in New York City”
text:
We stayed in the Affinia, on the corner of 3rd Ave and 50th street in August, 2007 for 3 days. We booked a Studio Room , which had a total footprint of 322 sq.ft. It included a bathroom, kitchen and bedroom area. The double bed, room area proper, measured 180 sq.ft. Very generous room lay-out.
The kitchen had a stove, refrigerator, microwave and coffee-maker. There was Internet access in the room, as well as a business center with 2 computers. The lobby was very small, but one can hang comfortably in the club room on the 2nd floor. The complementary wine, cheese and crackers every day at 6:00 PM was a nice touch. However, there is no restaurant or other recreational facilities. The place is perfect for business travelers who need a place to stay for a number of days, prepare of warm simple dishes in the evening. There are plenty of places nearby to eat or snack. One restaurant that we can recommend is the "Peking Duck Restaurant "on 52nd street, btw. 2nd and Third Ave. Also an Malaysian restaurant, "Nyonya" in China Town. All in all, we enjoyed our stay very much. 
RAv9092001

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Great Place, Highly Recommend!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for our visit to the City, and from the start, the staff was wonderful, and always very helpful. The hotel is very clean and modern, so we always felt comfortable there. The room was pretty small, but that might be normal for NYC, I don't know. In any case, it was still very comfortable, and it's not like we spent a lot of time in the room anyway! The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom spacious!
I will definately stay here again. Very nice place, and great location too.

name: Pod 51
title: “Pod Hotel / new york”
text:
Hotel tres propre, tres bien placé (10-20min a pied pour 5th avenue / time square)...
La chambre de deux / lits superposés est assez petite, mais propre.
Les douches/toilettes communes sont aussi tres propres, y'en a 4-5 par étages, largement suffisant (jamais eu besoin d'attendre pour quoi que ce soit).
Enfin bref, quand on a pas le budget pour le Mariott, le pod hotel peut etre une solution au rapport qualité prix tres interessant.

name: Hilton New York
title: “Gut Nächtigen in New York City!”
text: Wir (Familie, 2 Erwachsene, 1 Kind), hatten das Vergnügen, im Hilton New York im Mai/Juni 2007 für 1 Woche übernachten zu dürfen. Die Lage ist 1a, nahe Central Park und 5th Avenue, die wichtigsten Museen sowie das Rockefeller Center sind in unmittelbarer Nähe. Das Hotel scheint neu renoviert zu sein, alles sehr modern, sauber und schön, ausreichend großes Zimmer für 3 Personen, Blick auf die Stadt vom 29. Stock aus. Das Einchecken kurz und schmerzlos, ebenso der Checkout. Freundliches Hotelpersonal, das wir aber so gut wie nie in Anspruch zu nehmen brauchten. Ein Fitnesscenter mit Sauna ist ebenfalls vorhanden, brauchten wir auch nicht. Eigentlich waren wir nur zum Schlafen im Zimmer. Man kann wichtige Sehenswürdigkeiten problemlos vom Hotel aus abklappern. Insgesamt sehr schönes Hotel, auf alle Fälle jederzeit zu empfehlen. Beim nächsten Mal werden wir uns allerdings überlegen, ob wir nicht irgendwo im Netz einen günstigeren Tarif oder ein anderes, etwas preiswerteres Hotelzimmer finden können, da, falls man nur gelegentlich privat in der Stadt ist, das Hilton etwas "overdone" erscheint. Wir waren, wie gesagt, nur zum Schlafen auf dem Zimmer, was dem sehr guten Hotel nätürlich keinerlei Abbruch tut. Insgesamt kann man mit dem Hilton nichts verkehrt machen, im Gegenteil.

name: Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden
title: “Awesome hotel, and staff”
text: Amazing stay, the Manager went out of his way to assist us daily, even picked out a great restaurant for us and stayed to make sure we were set. Also stayed at a Hapton in SoHo, new and amazing too.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Truly great service”
text: I have to start by saying that it was the service in this hotel that made our stay better than average, and not the hotel itself. When we first arrived, we immediately received help with our luggage. When we first got to our room, I was very disappointed. I booked a studio suite (410 square ft) and it did not feel like 410 square feet to say the least. The bathroom was quite large so that may have taken some of the square footage away from the room itself. I did read several reviews before booking this hotel so I did ask for a room on a higher floor so that noise would not be an issue. We were on the 18th floor and we might as well have been on the 1st floor with our windows wide open all night. It was seriously THAT noisy. My husband and son were able to sleep right through it (hubby grew up in NYC), but it was the worst night of sleep I have had in months. We also had a problem regulating the heat and were very uncomfortable. I got up several times during the night to make sure my 4-year old wasn't sweating to death. I called in the morning and spoke with Jance (spelling may be off). She was very kind and offered to switch us to a side of the hotel with less noise. I called back a few minutes later and asked if they had any rooms with larger beds. At the time, we were in a room with 2 double beds. My husband is 6'3" and I am 5 months pregnant...needless to say, we did not fit so well together in a double bed! Jance was very accomodating and moved us to a 1 bedroom suite with a king bed and a queen sized sofa bed. This made the stay much more enjoyable to me. The suite was on a different side of the hotel and on the 23rd floor and it was definitely much quieter and cooler than the first room we were in. It was a very clean, comfortable suite and the 2 bathrooms were nice. On our second day, I tried to order a movie and could not get it to work. They sent someone up to fix it for us and he was very nice and was able to get it working for us. On our third day, we returned back to the room around 4pm and had not received housekeeping services. Again, they were very accomodating and cleaned our room while we were at dinner that night. I did have to call again when we got back from dinner because they did not leave us any washcloths nor did they remove the garbage. On our last night, we tried to order another movie and could not get it to work. I called again and they wanted to send someone up to fix it. It was already after 10pm and my little guy was sleeping so I declined to have someone fix it. They offered to fix it the next day but we were checking out. They of course offered to remove it from our bill but when we received our bill it was not removed and I had to call again. I cannot say enough about the service and the friendliness of the staff. It would have been nice if I didn't have to call them everyday, several times to fix one issue or another.

name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Times Square
title: “It's good value in a decent proximity of Times Square”
text:
It's a quite good hotel on the corner of 9th Ave and 39St, especially if you consider the price and breakfast on the house. It's ok for short stays or Broadway shows overnights. Keep in mind that rooms are tiny and I mean it. Subway is in a walking distance, but if it's raining or snowing, the street stretches and stretches ;-) There are often bus tourists in the hotel, so breakfast room can get crowded at peak. Overall it is fair value, but over a week stay would be overkill.
Tip:Avoid at any cost floors with the ice and vending machines - there are 6 rooms on each floor and the machines are awfully loud.

name: Club Quarters World Trade Center
title: “bon séjour dans un environnement incroyable !”
text: hôtel réservé en procédure cachée sur hotwire ; surprise quand la réservation arrive de savoir où était situé cet hôtel titré 4* dans financial. Déconvenue quand vous regardez sur tripadvisor les avis plutôt mitigés voire très négatifs ! et en fait, excellent séjour sous réserve de prévoir certaines dispositions. Les 4* sont un peu optimistes, disons plutôt du 3* + du style Novotel. L'hôtel est assez petit mais propre, personnel très bon. Nous avions une chambre avec lit + sofa (15$ par nuit en plus pour le sofa). Sdb correcte et propre. Les nuits étaient assez calmes car nous avions demandé à l'opposé du chantier. En effet, l'hôtel est juste à côté du chantier de reconstruction du WTC. Travaux jour et nuit ; le mémorial sera inauguré bientôt, le 11 septembre. Pour avoir idée du chantier, prendre le petit déjeuner en terrasse au 20ème : tout simplement époustouflant ! Vue dominante sur l'immense site et les grattes ciels autour. Expérience inoubliable. Voir le petit mémorial ouvert, la liste des disparus, l'hommage aux pompiers,... émouvant. Aller shopping au Century 21 situé à 2 blocks (pas le samedi : trop de monde). Plusieurs stations de métro proches. Ne pas manquer la balade à pied sur le bord de rivière et dans wall street tout proche.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Una magnifica ubicación”
text: Un hotel en donde al principio te sientes intimidado por la majestuosidad de su entrada y lobby, pero que al pasar el tiempo te hacen sentir en familia por la amabilidad y disposición de sus empleados. Este hotel nos encanto por sus habitaciones espaciosas y por tener una magnifica ubicación para ir a pasear, compras o teatros. Es muy central y en mi opinión queda muy cerca de todos los sitios de interés. Al quedar en Park Avenue quedas retirado del turismo que encuentras en otras avenidas, pero a una distancia conveniente. Realmente te sientes muy cómodo y bien atendido. Vale la pena consultar las promociones y upgrades que tienen para las suites. Los concierges son muy capacitados y pueden dar opiniones considerables para restaurantes, almacenes y teatro. Al venir a New York, este hotel siempre siempre será mi primera opción.

name: Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden
title: “Overall a good stay”
text:
I just returned a few days ago from a weekend stay at the Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden. I chose the hotel based on price, and it's proximity to Penn Station, as one day of my trip was going to be spent on the Jersey Shore, and I wanted to be close to Penn Station for when I needed to catch my train.
We (there was two of us) arrived Sat morning, and the room wasn't ready, but the desk clerk let us store our bags and let us know the free breakfast was still available, so we went and had something to eat. The breakfast room was very nice, a little crowded, but the food selection was good, and also tasted very good. They had bagels, muffins (kinds changed daily, the blueberry were excellent!), a couple hot dishes, like eggs and another that changed daily, we saw sausage and gravy one day and just sausage patties the next to make biscuit sandwiches. There's also some fresh fruit, 3 different types of cereals, juices, coffee and tea (served all day). The seating area does also contain two outside tables. 
The room itself was small, but nice. We had two double beds, which were VERY comfortable, a TV that was mounted on the wall, a desk and chair, and a closet. If you want to watch TV and sit in the chair, you may have to move it and sit between the beds like we did, if you prefer not to sit on the bed. There's also a lap desk to hold your laptop if you don't feel like sitting at the desk. 
The room was clean, overall, though there was some ground in stains in the carpet near the window, and the shower curtain had a blood stain on it. The high speed internet access was very good, it only went out on me once briefly, and it's free, which is a huge plus. The hotel writes an access code on your keycard packet at checkin, so make sure to look for it, or ask the desk clerk to point it out to you. We had to call down and ask them where to find it, as they didn't point it out to us at check in. It also expired the morning of check out, before we even checked out, so we had to call down to the desk and get a new one. There's two bottles of water in the room, be aware that their $5 a bottle if you want to have one! 
The staff overall seemed friendly enough. They replaced our keycards with no problem when asked when one got deactivated and no longer worked. There's a 24 hr fitness center on the lower level, and a "business center" in the lobby, consisting of two computers, which are always busy. Their hooked up to printers if you need to print out a boarding pass etc... 
The hotel is in a great location if your attending an event at MSG, or need to be near Penn Station, both are only a short few minutes walk up the street. Times Square is also a nice, leisurely walk, and there's also a subway station a couple minutes away from the hotel that will take you right to Times Square, or all the way down to Coney Island. Macy's is a few blocks away as well. Across the street is Jack's 99 cents world, which has, literally, everything. The store is 3 levels, and VERY crowded, and closes early, even during the week, so keep that in mind if you want to go over. Down 7th Avenue a few blocks was a nice coffee shop called Andrew's. Great food, great service, great prices, and only a short walk from the hotel. 
I do have a couple complaints about the hotel, besides the few cleanliness issues of the room I mentioned above. The hotel is very small, or I should say, narrow, in the hallways etc... The rooms are small, but small rooms are a NYC standard, so I expect those and don't mind that. The elevators, there's only two of them, they are very small, and EXTREMELY slow. We waited at least 10 mins to come down from our room on the 12th floor a couple times, including when we were heading down to check out. Also, we stored our bags when we arrived as our room wasn't yet ready. I was dismayed to come back some hours later, and see that the lobby was being used for luggage storage! The small lobby had bags stored all over it, including ours, of which one bag contained a VERY expensive laptop. Other hotels will store laptops in separate areas in the luggage rooms, this hotel stored bags all over the lobby, in plain sight and unattended! This was UNACCEPTABLE, especially with a laptop! I know there was a luggage room, as I saw it everytime we came in the front door. I just couldn't believe it when we got our bags, and pulled them out ourselves from a corner of the lobby! The lobby is also very small, made smaller from the luggage being "stored" in it! 
Overall, our stay was good, and I would stay here again if I could get a good rate again and if I needed to be close to MSG or Penn Station. That's the only way I'd choose the hotel again though, if I needed to be close to those places, otherwise, I wouldn't. I booked in April originally with a AAA rate of $179 a night, then was able to find a lower non AAA rate for $159 a night (and it wasn't a pay in advance rate) in June, so I changed my rate with no problems through the hotel's website.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Return visit even better than the first”
text:
Our second visit here in less than a year. The good service started before we arrived as the concierge was very helpful & prompt booking tables at restaurants we had been unable to get into EMailing direct. The concierge reconfirmed these bookings for us when we arrived and we dined at those restaurants without any problems or waits for tables.
On arrival at the hotel we were greeted personally by M. Louis Lenglet, the Guests Relations Manager who showed us to our room. I'm not sure whether this was because we were returning guests or because it was my birthday, but he is a charming man & made us feel very welcome & important! We had requested a high floor & were on the 21st with great views of the Chrysler & beautiful Helmsley Buildings. For my birthday, there was a bottle of champagne & some luxury cookies waiting for us & also a birthday card. Nice touch for a special occasion. We had a King Room (Most Prefered catagory on their website) which is very spacious with plenty of wardrobe space. Very quiet & peaceful on a high floor.
The location is fantastic for shopping, restaurants etc within easy walking distance. 
The staff here will do absolutely all they can to ensure your stay is a good one & anything you ask for is attended to immediately. I cannot really add anything to what has already been said in all the other rave reviews other than to say, it's all true. I have not stayed in any other hotels in New York so can't compare but I do know people who've been disappointed or just found their hotels to be ho-hum. So we will stick with the lovely Sofitel for our next visit to this fantastic city, 'If it's not broken, don't fix it'! 
Tips - as others have said, join the on-line loyaly scheme before you go for perks. The 4pm check out was great for us as we had an evening flight back to UK. You also get a free drink in the bar (ask for your voucher at reception). 
We used Franciso's Limo service to take us back to Newark. He is excellent & the cost is too. The doorman are great at dealing with all your transportation needs, including a stretch limo for a special treat if you fancy it, at a very bargain price. 
Sofitel feels like home in New York.

name: Broadway at Times Square Hotel
title: “Impeccable”
text: Très bon rapport qualité-prix. Emplacement super, très prochede nombreux restaurants et pub sur la 46ème, ainsi que Broadway. Personnel super sympa et chambre assez spacieuse.

name: Hotel on Rivington
title: “Hotel on Rivington - July 2012”
text: This property had aimed to be a hipster, rock and roll cool experience on the Lower East Side when it first opened, and I've stayed there often ever since - more because of the location than a love of the place. It seems to now be aiming more for a European crowd. I happened to score a wonderful room this time with a spectacular view of the city from the 19th floor. If you are lower, prepare for a lot of street noise if you face Rivington. The rooms are sadly in need of an upgrade and are showing their age in fray and messed up floors. This particular room was not bad at all by comparision, and had a huge balcony. Only stay here if you get a good deal. Not worth their fall prices unless they really whip this place back into shape.

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Location, location, location”
text: Welcoming and accomodating. Staff eager to cater to you needs whether it be for where to eat, transportation needs, problem solving and generous late check out times. Free wi-fi in the lobby. A breeze to print boarding passes but the best thing about the hotel apart from comfy beds and pillows, well appointed bathrooms was the fact that you are near so many great attractions within walking distance.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Very good hotel in a great location”
text:
We booked to stay at the Sofitel between Christmas and the New year purely for a short getaway and to make the most of the excellent shopping in Manhattan. Reading the reviews on Trip Advisor was one the main reasons for booking to stay here and we weren't disappointed.
The location is superb, almost everywhere of any significance is within walking distance and you can easily pop back with armfuls of bags to drop them off with no inconvenience.
The rooms are very comfortable and clean and every effort is made to make sure things are to your liking - the staff will do all they can to make sure that you are happy. Every single member of staff we encountered was happy to go above and beyond to accomadate any requests we had. The staff here were the among the best I have encountered in recent years of travelling.
I would never normally return to a hotel as I would want to experience new places etc etc but when we go back to NYC next year we will definately book here again. Dont miss out on the diner just up the street for breakfast to make a great start to any day!

name: The Belvedere
title: “Great hotel! Great location!”
text:
We spent four nights at The Belvedere Hotel, 5/24 - 5/28/2005. We had two rooms, one with a king bed, one with two doubles. Both rooms were
decorated nicely, both had a microwave, coffee-maker, and a frig.
The bathrooms were smallish, but very modern and had recently been renovated, with new tile and fixtures. The towels were plush and new.
Each room had a large TV and a desk & chair with high-speed internet access. There is a business center with internet access, too.
We did not eat in the cafe, as we loved the Pigalle cafe just a block up W 48th Street, open 24/7. We booked our rooms via Quikbook and paid $155 each per night. For this price, this is nicest hotel we've used in NYC,
and the location can't be beat. For individuals booking this hotel, please note that lots of tour companies use this hotel for their groups. The complaints about the "slow" elevators were exaggerated. One of our rooms was on the 17th floor and we never waited longer than a few minutes for one to arrive, and this hotel was booked solid during our entire stay. The staff is great and friendly, eager to help in any way they can.
Don't be afraid to use this hotel for a wonderful stay in a great city!!

name: Pod 51
title: “Tudo o que você precisa e apenas isso!”
text:
Hotel estiloso, staff nota 10 mas prepare-se para aprender o sentido de organização. Se você é organizado vai adorar agora se tem mania de largar tudo espalhado pelo quarto, vai descobrir-se num quarto pequeno demais para isso! Leve apena o necessário! e curta o espaço mais bem utilizado do mundo.
localização otima pelo preço tudo super novinho e limpo!

name: Affinia 50
title: “Great location; doesn't feel like a big, impersonal hotel”
text:
We (three people; three generations) stayed at the Affinia 50 for four nights in early October—my first time at this hotel.
I’ve stayed in plenty of different places in New York City-—from the floor of a friend’s apartment in Brooklyn Heights to the Peninsula. My location of choice is generally Midtown east, which I find to be easy walking distance to many things, but just far enough away from the crowds around Broadway and Times Square.
About four months in advance, I booked a studio suite for an average price of $330 per night. I continued to watch prices after I booked, but never found anything that I considered to be a better deal for this holiday weekend.
The Affinia 50 is at the corner of 50th and 3rd Avenue. There are three other hotels in the same block, along with a couple of restaurants and clubs. The Waldorf Astoria is a block away. It is about four blocks to 5th Avenue (Saks and St. Patrick’s), six blocks to Grand Central, and a couple of blocks to the nearest subway station at 53rd and 3rd.
The ground floor lobby is actually quite small, with modern décor and a small waterfall. The doormen, in particular, are very friendly and helpful. We were always greeted with a smile—coming and going.
The room itself was not really any bigger than many other standard hotel rooms, but it did have a tiny but full kitchen (full fridge, four-burner stove/oven, sink, microwave, and some basic dishes and utensils). Our room had two very comfortable queen-sized beds with plenty of pillows (you can choose pillow style if you wish) and nice linens and duvets. The bathroom is small—-only room for one person in there at a time, so having the extra sink in the kitchen ended up being handy. Aveda bath products were a nice touch. Other appreciated small touches included the reading lights with dimmers mounted on the headboards, comfortable working desk, iron/ironing board, and well-designed storage areas in the room and bathroom.
Wired high-speed Internet is available at $9.95 per day. The hotel has a small fitness center (did not use or look), business center, concierge, and lounge area with TVs on the second floor. There’s a breakfast buffet for $14.95, but we did not partake. We made good use of the many take-out places within a block or two, including PAX and Devon & Blakely.
My main complaint was noise. From our room, on the 10th floor, we could hear noise from the street as well as the hallway (people talking and closing doors—-or slamming and yelling, in the case of one group). At a few points, we could hear the TV playing in the adjacent room. For the most part, things quieted down over night, so this did not affect our sleep much.
Also, we ended up with a number of charges for movies and TV Internet-browser use on our bill, although we used neither. The charges were removed with no argument, so all was well…
Overall, I liked the smaller, more intimate feel of this hotel and friendly service, and I would consider staying there again.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “otima localização”
text: O hotel é muito bem localizado, perto de tudo,o, que é interessante. O serviço é muito bom, todos atenciosos e educados. O único senão é o café da manhã, não incluído no preço e muito caro. O apartamento é bem confortável, o banheiro limpo. O lobby do hotel é lindo.

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Nice”
text: Nice hotel, good location. Very friendly staff, storing luggage, etc. Great restaurants nearby.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Stunning”
text:
This hotel was superb. On arrival reception staff were very friendly and upgraded us to a king size room as it was our birthdays. The room was lovey, clean, and the bed amazingly comfortable. Bathroom large and clean- separate bath and shower. They brought us water and a box of chocolates every evening for free as well!We also had a free bottle of sparkling wine waiting for us in our room:)
The concierge booked our reservations for our evening meals at whatever restaurant we wanted and also phoned to confirm our shuttle bus arrangements to the airport. We didnt have to pay for the use of our room phone to do this. The staff at this hotel couldnt have done more- so helpful and friendly.
There is free internet access downstairs in the lobby which is great. May have to wait 5-10 mins if computers are full but this was an added bonus to our trip. We got engaged so could share our photos and write emails to friends and family without it costing.
Location is brilliant, 5 mins Times Square and subway. easy access to Macys. Grand Central and accessing subway to travel. Minutes away from Bryant Park which is great to grab a coffee and sit in the sun watching the ice skating.
I recommend tavern on the green restaurant for an excellent (pricey) meal. Stunning location in central park. Use the subway as much as posible, it leaves you with more time to do things and it is so easy. The red flame diner is good for a cheap american breakfast though if you go after 9 on a weekend expect to wait 10 mins for a seat. It is always busy in there.
I would recommend this hotel time and time again and if I return to NY will stay there again myself without a doubt. Enjoy!

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Great location”
text:
The New Yorker offered us a clean, quiet stay in the centre of Manhatten. Compared with other New York hotels it was reasonably priced - though staying anywhere else in the world for the same price I would expect a lot more luxury. 
The rooms are small but functional with clean bathrooms. The staff were not overly friendly but helped when asked to. The tick tock diner downstairs was excellent (especially the Oreo milkshakes which are a taste of heaven) . The main thing is the location - two blocks from the Empire State it allowed us to explore Manhatten without worrying about returning late at night. I would stay here again.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Viaggio a New york”
text: Posizione ottima, pulizia buona,stanza confortevole, apertura della camera difficoltosa x due giorni e nessun aiuto nel ritrovare le ns valigie.... Anzi pur avendola in deposito da quasi un giorno , è stata consegnata a sera dopo ripetuti solleciti...

name: Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden
title: “Handy and functional”
text:
We stayed at Hampton Inn Herald Square for a week in May. We booked the room through the web site of Tui Hotels Germany and got a pretty good deal.
The room was quite small but on the other hand it's bigger than your average room in London or Paris. Otherwise it was functional, clean and comfortable enough. The hotel has some nice touches like the free buffet breakfast, and free coffee, ice tea, biscuits and so on. The personnel were friendly and helpful.
The location was very good for our stay. It is within walking distance from major attractions and the transportation (underground, buses, trains) are easily reachable. If your flight is for Newark you could consider using the train to/from Penn Station which is 3 minutes by foot from the hotel. The train is more convenient than the bus connection.
There is a construction work going on on the other side of the street so you might want to have a room off the street.
The hotel was very popular during the weekend. You might have to wait for the lift for a few minutes during the busiest hours.

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “Expensive for what it was”
text:
We moved here from the Doubletree Metropolitan (which is only one block away) just for a change but we should have stayed at the Doubletree.
This hotel has a great lobby but the rooms are old and the bathrooms are old. One thing that annoyed us was that it was twice the price of the Doubletree BUT they didn't even offer you free computer access (like they had at the Doubletree) which was annoying. It was quieter than the Doubletree though and they did offer a free coffee machine in the room and a minibar which the Doubletree didn't.
All in all, it was expensive for what it was and I would recommend the Doubletree anyday.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Hyggelig opphold på Waldorf”
text: Rommet var fint med alle nødvendige fasiliteter, men ikke forvent et helt nyoppusset rom. Du betaler noe ekstra for navnet, men hotellet har sjarm, bra beliggenhet og god service. Frokosten var også veldig bra.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Fantastic Value!”
text:
We booked the Belvedere based on the reviews on this site, and we weren't dissapointed.
We arrived 2 hours before check in, but there was a room available. The room was clean and spacious - a small kitchenette, lovely bathroom with complimentry products, 2 double beds (although they were a little small) great TV with in-house movies.
The location was perfect, along a nice quiet street but within 10 minutes walk to Times Square. The Port Authority bus station is about a 10 minute walk and the subway 5 minutes.
the staff were incredibly friendly and helpful and i wouldn't hesitate to recommened the hotel!!!
My only qualm was that a coffee machine was supplied so you coudn't make tea - but that's not really a big issue!

name: Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden
title: “Excelente ubicación y Servicio impecable!”
text: Estuve en el hotel 8 noches e/nov y diciembre. Pasé allí el huracán Sandy! el hotel es un hotel impecablemente limpio, muy bien ubicado, de allí fuimos caminando a todos lados en cualquier horario. Tiene desayuno, lo que es raro e impagable en NY. Es un hotel nuevo, lo que de por sí en NY es un buen punto. sin humedad, sin muebles viejos, todo nuevo. El único defecto diría son los armarios pequeños. Lo que más destaco es la gente. Todos, desde recepción, servicio de limpieza, mantenimiento, todos fueron serviciales y cálidos, especialmente durante el huracán. Nos prestaron sus celulares pra hacer llamados a las aerolíneas, nos ofrecían sus laptops.. qué decir. Un 10 para ellos. volvería sin lugar a dudas.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Room choice very important.”
text:
This hotel is very well located in NYC, and with Penn Station across the road, you can be on the subway and on your way anywhere in town in just a few minutes. It's also a 15-20 (or so)minute walk to Times Square, great for Broadway shows and checking out the tourist spots.
The hotel is in the process of being renovated, but the old world granduer has been retained in the lobby, which makes it feel very warm and welcoming, and a little bit special. There's plenty of room to hang out here with a group, chat with the concierges and plan out your day's events. Big enough so it never feels overly crowded, just enough to give it a buzz in the mornings. 
The biggest problem I had in the hotel was the noise management. I understand NY is a very noisy city. There's cars beeping and sirens and all sorts of things 24/7. The problem here is that the air conditioner in the room is the box-in-the-window type. And the air conditioner passes all the outside noise straight through itself into the room. So you may as well sleep with the window open. If you're a light sleeper, bring your earplugs.
It wasn't only noise from outside though. My bathroom must have shared a common air vent with my neighbours, so when I was in the bathroom, I could hear everything going on in THEIR bathroom. Conversations, showers, toilets flushing, EVERYTHING. Use your imagination. It was weird. I felt like I was involuntarily invading their privacy.
The facade of the hotel was also being renovated during my stay, so lots of banging heard from outside the window, but this was only during business hours when I was usually out of the hotel, so it didn't really bother me.
I travelled with a group and of the three rooms we reserved, mine was the tiniest. Very small. There was just enough room between the foot of the bed and the wall to sneak past, craning my neck to avoid hitting the wall-mounted TV. The bathroom was also tiny. The door smacked into the toilet when opened. With the door closed, there's just enough room to stand in front of the sink. They've still managed to squeeze a shower/bath combo in there though, which takes up most of the room. Also a quite unusual 'up-lighting' design is used on the bathroom mirrors which is kinda off-putting. Nice products though!
The room still had a desk, chair, ottoman and a wardrobe, which probably explains the lack of floor space. So all the amenities to be comfortable, just jammed in a very small space.
I also saw the rooms my friends were staying in, and it looks like I got the dud, since we had all paid the same rate. Theirs were much larger, one even had a separate study nook. Larger bathrooms, with plenty of room to move around. So my advice would be to ask at reception where they're sticking you, and make sure it's not in one of their Tiny Rooms.
Overall, I did enjoy my stay here, despite the noise and the Tiny Room. The location was great, and the staff were very nice and helpful. A special thankyou to Norva at the concierge desk whose suggestions for sightseeing, restaurants and directions made our stay even more enjoyable.
Just be careful which room you're in!

name: Pod 51
title: “Pod Hotel di NY - comodo e funzionale”
text: La camera (matrimoniale) in cui ho soggiornato era davvero molto piccola, ma assolutamente funzionale e pulita! L'hotel ha un ottima posizione, a pochi passi dal cuore di Manhattan (Rockfeller Center, St Patrick, Fift Avenue). Consiglio assolutamente!

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Excellent option in NY”
text: Before I have gone to NY I had read a lot of hotel's reviews and I was a little worried because a lot of hotels are expensive, well localized, but since they are old the comments were not so good. Sofitel NY is a very good option to Stay in Manhattan. I totally recomend.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Had a Great Stay”
text: We picked this hotel after doing tons of research on trip advisor about hotels in new york...My fiance's aunt has a spa (sphatika.com) in the upper west side so I knew I wanted to be in that area somewhere. I really enjoyed my stay at this hotel.. The rooms looked very modern we had a flat screen and I knew not to touch anything in or on top of the refrigerator as there are sensors and you will be charged after it has been moved for 8 seconds from reading on tripadvisor... The best part about the stay was concierge. He went out of his way to throughly explain sighseeing and dining option in nyc. We booked a bus tour that could be used over the course of two days and for an additonal $10 we got a bout tour as well. This was agreat value it was about $40 a piece and the bus tour is hop on hop off so you can ride it to a cool part of town jump out and catch another and again being able to use it over the course of two days was very helpful so we didnt have to spend the whole day being tourists.. I loved this place it was a good value as well and I was expecting a teeny tiny room and I was suprised to find a almoost regular sized room and the bathroom and the especially the shower is awesome! WE also ate at the restaurant and the asparagus and one other appetizer was off the chain but the seafood salad

name: Affinia 50
title: “Awesome service”
text: Visited NY the weekend before Christmas. I have never had better service than at the Affinia 50. I will never stay anyplace else when I am in town. "Thank you" to Sid, your sevice was excellent.

name: Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden
title: “Excellent rapport qualité prix, situation idéale”
text: 1 semaine à NYC en Octobre 2010, cet etablissement nous a donné entière satisfaction. Couchage impécable, chambre propre (un peu petite), petit déjeuner de qualité servi tôt. La position centrale de l'hotel est idéale (à 300 de Madisson Sq Garden). Accès depuis JFK en 1 heure de transport en commun.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
title: “Illusionen”
text:
Dem Waldorf Astoria Hotel geht der Ruf ja schon vorraus.
Die Vorfahrt, die Eingangshalle all das erfüllt sehr den Traum von Luxus.
Der check in war äußerst höflich und professinell.
Zum Zimmer musste man allein, was mich bei einem Hotel mit diesem Ruf, schon sehr wundert.
Das Zimmer selbst war in Ordnung und im Detail ausgestattet, jedoch nicht wirklich überschwenglich Luxeriös.
Vor zwei Jahren war ich in einem wesentlich schönerem Zimmer.
Das Bad hat amerikanischen, gehobenen Standard ist jedoch nicht mit asiatischen oder europäischen Massstäben zu vergleichen.
Insgesammt war der Aufenthalt sehr angenehm jedoch liegen die Erwartungen des Gastes in diesem Hotel ja sehr hoch.

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Posh, chic, yet exceedingly comfortable.”
text: My wife and I recently stayed at the Affinia Shelburne for the first time, and could not have had a better stay. This hotel has a wonderful total package: first-rate amenities, smart decor, unbeatable location, and a staff that insists on making your stay unparalleled. We will be making a return visit the next time we are in Manhattan.

name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Times Square
title: “Great place to stay near Times Square”
text: Forget high prices in NYC. Stay at this hotel and you will have a great stay, breakfast and you will be centrally located. Staff is very helpful too.

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Excellent as usual, and would expect nothing less!”
text: Once again, Affinia Shelburne, you have provided us with a wonderful respite in greatest city in the world. This was our second stay, but our first in a year and a half. While the spit and polish from the expansive renovation has sort of worn, your attention to service and the absolute comfort of the guest has not. Would still enjoy complimentary internet though, and, boy, are your halls HOT! I was very pleased to see that cleanliness was still a priority here, and that the lobby still has that delightful scent to it. Whatever air fresheners you use in the lobby, please don't ever change it! It will forever be my signal that I have arrived in THE CITY!!!

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Great hotel and great location”
text: Spent a few nights at the Affinia Shelburne during a recent visit to NYC. We had a nice one bedroom suite with a nice living area and good size bedroom. View out the window was of the Empire State Building. Everything was top notch and the room was very quiet. Neighborhood had a wide variety of great restaurants and was a short walk to the Theatre District or subway. We have had great luck with all of the Affinia hotels we have stayed in.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Great location, big rooms for NYC”
text:
We spent 5 days here after moving from the Intercontinental on 43rd.
The intercon was great but the rooms here exceeded the size by more than 50%. As with other posts I suggest you ensure a room on the higher floors as the street noise on the lower floors is very intrusive. 
I love the noise of New York but you do need a break. We actually had to move rooms which they accommodated without much fuss, and upgraded also.
Penn station is accross the road and given it has four of the main subway lines feeding through it gives great access to this great place. Buy a $29 unlimited 7 day pass and you wont be disappointed.
The bar downstairs is modern an serves great bar food as well as restaurant meals.
I will return.

name: Affinia 50
title: “Affinia 50”
text: I have stayed here 2x's Once when it was the Plaza 50, and once since it became the Affinia 50. Both times I LOVED IT!!! This past April I took my husband, and he loved the location. So close to the subway, great little diner a couple of doors down. Super friendly staff!!! I would love to stay again, but they have raised their rates so much.

name: Hotel Mela
title: “dreadful experience”
text:
I am thoroughly disappointed and let down. Having had to book into the hotel last week following the devastation caused by hurricane sandy, I booked a week a)knowing that hotels were getting booked up sat and b) because there was no word on when power would be restored, other than the initial view that it could take up to a week. I booked through Agoda - well there was my first mistake. The cancellation policy stated that any shortening of my booking after check in would result in charges - which I assumed, worst case, one night stay. Upon learning after 3 nights that both power and water were restored at my home, I called Agoda to find out what cancellation fee would be imposed for early check out. Astoundingly i was told the hotel insisted on the full seven nights stay DESPITE the fact the hotel was fully booked and people were still desperate for hotels, since then I have had to contend with Agoda staff clearly disinterested, and a hotel that couldn't even be bothered to respond to my emails. At a time when people in distress should be helped, this hotel took advantage and they should feel embarrassed. That is not business. 
As for the hotel? When I went back at 2.45pm to check whether my room was ready, the guy
At the front desk told me apologetically that it wasn't quite ready as it was one of the larger rooms. What a joke. When I returned, and was handed my room key it was abundantly clear that the front desk was trying a new style of sarcasm. The room was the smallest on the floor - as was helpfully mapped out by the fire safety notice. Note of caution for those who DO have the misfortune to stay at this hotel? Avoid room 908 - and I suspect any other 08 room. Tiny, suffocating and the starch fumes overwhelming. I was overjoyed to have finally found a room somewhere, having spent 3 days with no power and water, and it's cost me over $2000. Shame on Hotel Mela.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Good Hotel, Great Location.”
text: Stayed at The Belvedere for 3 nights and overall thought the hotel was really good value. Room was clean and well decorated and was larger than we expected given what we had read about New York hotels. The location is really good (took under 5 mins to walk to Times Sq). Also, on the final day they held our bags until the evening after we checked out without any problems which was really useful. Only real gripe was the unhelpful concierge. Basically, it seems that they have contracts for transport (obviously not the cheapest!) and will not help to arrange alternatives. That said, we did book Shuttle Bus to JFK through them and the driver couldn't have been more helpful.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Best rated for a reason!”
text:
OK, I read all the reviews then chose this hotel. There are plenty of reasons why this is one of the best rated hotels. Great rooms. We had a suite on the 25th floor. Once you put your head down onto the wonderful bed and linens you are done for the night.
Modern amenities. The tub and separate glass shower were wonderful.
A little pricey but worth it.
We will be back.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Watch Credit Card Charges”
text:
I stayed at this very basic and spartan hotel for one night, and was in the room for probably less than eight hours. The room was quite small and the only window faced a brick wall just a few feet away. The location was good, and the price was perhaps a little high for what I got.
My big complaint is that when I got my credit card statement there was a charge for $28; I called the hotel in mid-September and was told it was a mini-bar charge. I disputed this as I was only in the room to sleep and as a frequent traveler NEVER use a mini-bar. They agreed to refund the $28 and as of late November it still has not happened. A colleague I traveled with also got a mini-bar charge that he did not use.
Stay at the Hotel Beacon instead.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Great location, decent room”
text: Stayed 3 nights in mid-May. Insider tip: Rooms ending in 12, 14, 16, 18 are 1/3 bigger than the rest of the rooms. Good: Location can't be beat! Heart of midtown, super convenient to both uptown and downtown. Not as good: Our furniture was very worn, the AC unit was in a piece of plywood in the wall, some peeling wallpaper, loose cable in TV unit - kept having to get up to fix it. But the bedding and window coverings looked newish, so I would rate the room as average. Could hear sirens from fire station on corner, but only occasionally. In all, worth it for the superb location and good value.

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “Good location just outside the hustle and...”
text: Good location just outside the hustle and bustle. The lobby is very nicely decorated. The room was a bit small but the king size bed was incredibly comfortable. Could use a little modernization from their tv's to their bathroom. Overall very pleased with the hotel for our weekend stay.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Good hotel”
text:
Stayed for a week in August with my husband for our wedding anniversary. 
Hotel - Hotel bedrooms have undergone renovation and are very clean and updated. We stayed on the 29th floor, in a corner room, which compared to reviews of other rooms, seems to have more space as we did not find it small at all. (Maybe worth asking for a corner room when you book - also means you get 2 sides of windows/views). View of river was good. Maid cleaned the room and replaced towels daily - room was always very clean. No coffee/tea facilities in room - however 10 mins after we checked in reception called to ask if we would like a coffee machine delivered to the room free of charge - which we got another 10 mins later! They gave us a couple of packets of coffee/milks which lasted a couple of days. We found the staff fairly friendly and helpful. Hotel does not have that many facilities but then you would not use much when staying in New York!
Eating - Tick Tock diner is next door which is ok, there is another cafe/restaurant when you come out of the hotel and turn right, straight across the road (next to Irish place). Of course, there are tons of cafes/Starbucks etc around anyway. The restaurant next to the hotel did very good food and fairly reasonably priced. The Irish place also does nice food. We did not find many other great restaurants around the area - think you would have to know where to go and probably out of this area to get a really good meal. 
Travel - subway is right next door to hotel. Can walk to a lot of things from hotel - including Grand Central Station which is about 25 mins walk away past Bryant Park. Penn station is across the road also. Would recommend using the subway which is $2 a journey rather than being ripped off by yellow cabs! You can also get discounts on buying lots of tickets on the subway. 
Attractions - as mentioned, a lot is nearby. Would recommend Top of the Rock (Rockefeller building) rather than Empire State as queues much shorter and view just as good. Broadway is up the road - can book tickets on ticketmaster or we just went to the theatre and bought them direct and chose our seats. WE used Gray Line bus company and bught a 3 day bus tour ticket where you can hop on/off the various tours they do. The price included a boat cruise which was good. Would recommend going out of the immediate area to see things e.g. Central Park, South Street Seaport etc etc. 
Overall - a good experience at this hotel and would stay again.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “5* reviews here are no exaggeration”
text:
My wife and I chose the Sofitel as the hotel for our first visit to New York on the basis of the reports here on TripAdvisor, and we were not disappointed. The hotel is quite simply superb. We booked a superior with a Queen sized bed on the 23rd floor overlooking the Chrysler Building and the room was incredibly comfortable. Everything you’ve read about the beds here is true. I reckon this was the most comfortable bed I’ve slept in anywhere in the world, and I’m pretty well travelled! The bathroom was elegant, and spacious, although the bath itself was too small, but the shower cubicle was more than fine. Being so high up there was zero noise from the street.
It was our wedding anniversary and we had champagne on ice delivered to our room gratis, not one evening but twice! Evening room service included two small bottles of Evian and a small box of chocolates.
Room service was excellent but expensive, as was the bar and restaurant downstairs.
As everyone on here has mentioned, the Red Flame diner a few feet down on the left is an absolute gem. A real taste of New York, with lightning fast service, huge menu, open 6am til midnight, and cheap as chips.
The Sofitel position is perfect, five minutes from Times Square, Grand Central Station, etc. 
Chat up the concierges and doormen as they are a mine of information.
Also, free internet and printer in the lobby. 
Basically, you can’t go wrong here, I’ll certainly be back.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Location good - shame about staff”
text:
Good bits - excellent location on Broadway near subway stations. We had Panoramic Deluxe room with nice view of Hudson river from balcony. Room was spacious with comfy bed and big TV. Bathroom also spacious with nice decor. Liked the 16th floor roof terrace.
Average bits - hotel was not expecially clean, but certainly not dirty either. Our room looked clean on first look, but closer inspection revealed a fair bit of dust, and a couple of holes in sheets. Attention to detail needed. Price was ok - we got 30% off on our room when I booked - if I had paid full price I would have felt a bit ripped off. Minibar and PPV movies very very overpriced, even by NY standards.
Bad bits - the staff! Not all of them, as the doormen were very friendly and helpful. As mentioned above, cleaners could do a better job but kept room reasonably clean. Main gripe with front desk staff. Refused to let us check in early (we arrived at 12 and check in was at 3). Asked if there was any chance our room could be cleaned early so we could check in and a flat out no. Said they would let us know when room was ready and they didn't. Although fairly efficient, they never smile and never go out of their way to help you out. When leaving, they sneakily overcharged me by $250 - bill said one amount, when I get home and see credit card statement, they have taken more! Appalling really. Also, our door was not securely attached to hinges so hard to shut it properly, and the water in the shower seemed to go from warm to scalding hot whenever it wanted to.
Finally - avoid the Manhattan Diner next door. My girlfriend caught food poisoning from there on our first night.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “The New Yorker Hotel Experience”
text:
After reading many negative reviews of the hotel, my husband and I took the chance and booked for a week stay in this hotel..
I took a lot of pictures of this hotel, our room and of Manhattan.
All the rooms are newly renovated, no more stinky carpets, and dirty paints and curtains as posted in old reviews. All are sparkling new (we were allowed to see other rooms for review). We stayed in the 25th floor. The room was small BUT very nice. The room we had is good for 2 people, very quiet, the AC was not noisy at all unlike one review (due to the renovations). We could not hear any pounding or men at work, or the busy streets down below at all. And I am very sensitive with noise (I wake up easily when I hear footsteps several feet away). 
We had a nice view of the Hudson river, watching the sunset is a treat for me and my camera. The towels and sheets were changed everyday. I had a great time exploring New York City after a good night's sleep in this hotel.
Location-wise, it is very close to Macy's, Duane Reade, McDonalds (open 24 hours), a subway station we did not try, taxis are everywhere (cheap rate we were surprised)...
And a few blocks from the hotel is the Empire State Building.. we love walking! 
The hotel staff and receptionists are very nice and courteous. The security manager even allowed me to take lots of pictures of the hotel. We felt very safe there, and we saw a lot of people checking in on the weeekend. My husband and I were expecting worse, to be honest. But we were very satisfied with our stay there. I loved their bed too. The bathroom is a bit small but hey, it's New York.
As for amenities, we did not try out the gym but my husband did go to the laundry room (we ended up going outside for dry cleaning). My husband did not like the washing machines, only half of the machines worked, he said. 
We used the flat iron and the ironing board, which are tucked away in a small closet. The closet is a bit small if you have lots of clothes and bulky luggages. My husband and I had 2 carry-ons (about 22 x 12 x 13", the standard size for Delta airline luggage), and two personal items-I had my camera bag, tripods and my husband had his backpack.
There is a vending machine near our room, so we had steady supply of ice for free, and the diet pepsi costed a dollar which isn't much for us.
We did not eat in the in-house restaurant because we wanted to explore other food and dining.
All in all, we would recommend this hotel for people wanting to get a lower price and a great stay.. If you are looking for a bigger space and room, be ready to spend more money. You get what you pay for.

name: Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden
title: “Top Hotel - nur weiterzuempfehlen!!!”
text:
Wir waren für 4 Tage in New York und ich das Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden sehr empfehlen. Klasse Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis!
Das Hotel ist super sauber, bietet einen klasse Service (gutes Früstück inklusive; den ganzen Tag über Kaffee und Tee; gratis Innternetzugang im Zimmer, aber auch 2 Computer in der Lobby zur freien Verfügung, an denen man auch gratis drucken kann) mit sehr freundlichem Personal.
Auch die Lage ist super. Nur wenige Meter von der nächsten Subway-Station entfernt (Linie 1,2,3 und A,C,E). Daher auch super zu erreichen von JFK aus (Airtrain und dann Linie A bis Penn Station). Der Times Square ist nur wenige Blocks entfernt, ebenso wie Macys, das Empire State Building,.....
Das Hotel ist modern eingerichtet, alles ist in einem top Zustand und sehr sauber!
Zu den Zimmern kann ich sagen, dass sie zwar nicht allzu gross sind, aber trotzdem super! Wir haben zu viert in einem Zimmer geschlafen und das ging locker. DIe Betten sind auch sehr bequem! Auch das Bad ist sauber und alles funktioniert prima.
Ich kann nur eins sagen: SUPER HOTEL!!! 
Ich würde jederzeit wieder im Hampton Inn absteigen!
Wir haben einige Zeit im Vorraus gebucht und hatten einen AAA (amerikanischer ADAC)-Tarif und haben umgerechnet ca 170 Euro die Nacht fürs Zimmer bezahlt.

name: Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden
title: “ottima ubicazione, vicino alla fashion avenue , broadway, time square”
text: Posizione centrale, ubn pò rumoroso. Stanze piccole per 4 persone, spazi per valigie ed effetti personali insufficienti. Buona pulizia. Due ascensori per 25 piani sono talvolta un blocco fastidioso, abbiamo spesso usato le scale (per 6 piani...), si formano folle di gente in attesa ai piani e soprattutto a painterreno al momento di risalire dalla colazione. Colazione di discreta qualità, buona scelta

name: The Belvedere
title: “Nice hotel, but cold and noise room”
text: We spent two days at the Belvedere and the hotel was very clean and staff polite. Our room on the 4th floor was otherwise good but the street noise was really disturbing during the nights. Also when it was cold outside it was really windy inside as well.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “GREAT!”
text: The location is great, the staff very friendly and very accomodating to my requests. The room was very clean. The front desk staff were very kind and patient, always had a nice tone with me. the restaurant was fantastic.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Pretty Good - excellent service & location”
text:
Stayed at the Sofitel from Feb 1 to Feb 5 2007 and have previously stayed at several other similarly rated hotels in Manhattan.
My overall impression is favourable but, given the stunning reviews this hotel receives on Trip Advisor, I have to admit that I was a little disappointed overall.
Positives:
Location very good - quiet and less than 5 mins walk from Times Square.
Staff are friendly and helpful.
Rooms are sizeable and clean (booked Queen 350 sqft).
Bathrooms are clean, spacious and well appointed.
Slight negatives:
My room a little tired - Decor a bit 80s and old (not particularly well functioning) CRT TVs and hairdryer. Hotel bar and restaurant are lacking in atmosphere.
Overall, if you get a good rate (at or below the average advertised hotel rate on Trip Advisor) then I would recommend the Sofitel.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Négatif”
text: Accueil insipide ; urbanité du personnel à découvrir!!!...; Client Platinium Sofitel je me demande où sont les avantages liés à cette carte ; Le personnel de la réception a besoin d'être formé à la Qualité...

name: The Belvedere
title: “NYC Subway: clean by comparison”
text: We booked our room through Hotels after visiting their website which showed an immaculate, sparkling room. When we were arrived, the air conditioner was not functioning, and was held to the window frame with a piece of plywood. There are NO screens on the windows, which is a safety risk for small children. To put it kindly, the bathroom smelled like a bag lady's underwear. The iron didn't work. The ironing board cover was stained with a foul-smelling substance. We left an item in the room, and made four calls to the hotel with the help of the booking agency before we received any help regarding the return of the item. This hotel is no bargain. Spend a few dollars more, and stay in the same area in a nicer place.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “Super emplacement”
text:
Un hotel très bien placé avec de très belle chambre.
La literie est excellente.
Les chambres avec vue sur Time Square sont très agréable
Le petit déjeuner est délicieux (buffet copieux avec tout ce dont on peut réver)

name: Pod 51
title: “Gut, günstig zentral - The Pod”
text:
Das The Pod ist eines der Hotels in NY, bei denen das Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis stimmt.
Die Lage ist prima, die Zimmer modern und alles ist sauber.
Nachteil ist das sehr kleine Badezimmer und die schlechte Beleuchtung desselben (für Frauen).
Dennoch eine der Adressen in NY um das Geld in den Shops und nicht im Hotel zu lassen.!

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “One of the very best”
text: This hotel is located close to Times Square and the subway, but in a quiet (by NYC standards!) residential area so it offers the best of both worlds. Front desk staff were pleasant and efficient. Concierge was very helpful and housekeeping staff responded immediately to our requests, whether it was fixing a burnt-out lightbulb, providing extra coffee and towels, or bringing a special pillow. Room was very large by NYC standards and beds very comfortable. This hotel also has a pub-style casual dining restaurant which has great food for good value.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Eight Days...of Excellence”
text:
Stayed a week at this hotel last year, and returned for the same week again this year and stayed eight days (Thanksgiving week). 
We had a room facing the Chrysler building on the 20th (22nd?) floor and for NY...was large enough for our needs. Mirrored closet, immaculate bathroom, the bed extremely comfortable. 
Utilized the services of the concierge - no issues there. Had drinks in the bar (Gaby's)...perfect martinis. Used the 4pm late check out without a hitch (some issues last year) and all staff we interacted with were professionals. 
I will definitely stay at this hotel again next year.
The only issue - we were a bit close to the elevator and I could hear the noise in the morning. I'll remember to request a room further away from the elevator next year.

name: Pod 51
title: “günstiges Hotel in bester Lage”
text: Empfehlenswertes Hotel für Gäste, die ihr Geld lieber für Einkäufe als für teure Hotelzimmer verwenden möchten. Die Zimmer sind sehr klein, maßgeschneidert für Einzelpersonen, sehr sauber, komfortables Bett, Waschgelegenheit in Nirosta, Kleiderablage, Radiowecker, Handtücher. Geräumige Dusche am Gang, mit Haarshampoo und Duschgel. Dachterrasse mit nettem Rundblick. Viele kleine Restaurants und Frühstücksmöglichkeit in unmittelbarer Umgebung.

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “Old, dirty, expensive and staff with an attitude”
text:
The Barclays is located conveniently at walking distance from 5th Av and the UN buildings.
However, I would not advise anyone to stay at this hotel. There is a lack of (friendly) staff, the rooms are old, dirty and very expensive.
With only two staff at check in during the entire week (the rest of staff hiding in offices behind check in), it started out bad. Check in almost took an hour, only to be told that the reserved early check in room was not ready. So, two hours later I had to wait again for 45 minutes to get the key. That is unacceptable.
The rooms are small (which I expect in NYC), but they are in urgent need of a thorough cleaning or of a complete renovation. The furniture is dusty and greasy, the bathroom features mould, hair, strange stains. I asked housekeeping to clean my bathroom, but they indicated that would only happen the next day (conveniently after check out). Complaining at the reception was impossible, too busy again. The bed is ok. There is no AC, just a noisy air recycling system. Windows can be opened, but the noise from outside is too much. On the good side, the rooms themselves are quit, I had a room next to the elevators without any noise. There is no wifi in the rooms, but wifi in the reception area is free.
Breakfast is good. During the weekend there is a buffet, during the week there is an omelette station (a very good one actually). Breakfast is expensive though, the buffet is USD 39.00 (ex tax and service). Add USD 9.00 (!) for an espresso. 
As indicated, there is a lack of staff and staff is extremely rude an arrogant. I actually think they are so rude in self-defence, otherwise they would not be able to cope with so many complaints. Since wifi was only available in the reception area, I spent some time there watching one person after the other complaining about possibly everything one could complain about. After all, the old dirty room and the other amenities cost around USD 450 per night and it is no wonder that people are disappointed and demand improvement.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Amazing!”
text:
The best word to describe this hotel is "amazing"! Everything works well: the hotel is beautiful, the staff is very kind, the location is perfect.
We stayed there for a week (Oct.16 to 23) and had a very good time. The room is absolutely quiet, comfortable and clean. The queen size bed (as we have requested, due to price considerations - this is not a cheap hotel) was amazingly good. The sheets were changed every day, and the bed was made again around 7 PM. The bathroom is wonderful: separate shower, everything in marble, towels changed twice a day. Even the soap/shampoo are of excellent quality (Roger & Gallet).
The restaurant is very good, although the prices on the wine list were a bit high. I strongly recommend the breakfast (delicious croissants). Service very kind. 
The staff is remarkable, specially the concierge service. I would like to mention the concierge Daniel, who was very helpful in finding us some delicious restaurants.
I will return to this hotel, and highly recommend it for anyone travelling to NY.

name: Affinia 50
title: “No lo considero Hotel Boutique”
text:
Después de haber estado en el Sheraton , tuvimos que quedarnos en el Hotel Affinia 50 New York ,del 26 al 30 diciembre, porque el vuelo no salia debido a la gran nevada del día 26, y el Sheraton ya estaba completo.El Hotel nos cobro la 1º noche 190 dolares, pero el resto de las 3 noches siguientes nos cobro 120dolares más por noche, es decir un abuso ,310 dolares diarios.(Se aprovecharon de la situación). Nos comentaron que si no salia el vuelo y nos teniamos que quedar el día 30 nos cobrarian 1.500 dolares la noche, por ser esas fechas,
No está en la mejor ubicación de Manhattan. Las habitaciones son muy espaciosas pero la calefacción no es de lo mejor. La TV es antigua. No tienen ni cafeteria para poder tomar un café. Para entrar en internet tuvimos que pagar 30 dolares.
Lo mejor los porteros ..amabilisimos.
Jamás volveré a ese Hotel.

name: Pod 51
title: “"Kanonbra fräscht hotell"”
text: Verkligen att rekommendera. Vi var ett större gäng som bodde och alla var supernöjda. Vi valde rum med delat badrum men det var separata toaletter och duschar och desutmom många på varje plan såman behövde aldrig stå i kö och aldrig "dela" på det sättet att det är helt öppet. De var dessutom helt nykaklade och jättefräscha med dov musik i bakgrunden, mysfaktor! de "billigare" rummen vi valde hade våningssäng, men var breda och väldigt sköna. Det bästa med the pod- NÄRA TILL ALLT. Gångavstånd in till Times square. gick tom fortare än att ta t-banan. t-bana längre ner på gatan 2 min bort. Ja helt perfekt om man vill ha ett enklare, fräscht och centralt hotell

name: Affinia 50
title: “Muy buena atencion. Excelente ubicacion.”
text:
Excelente lugar, muy buena atencion. El personal muy dedicado.
El desayuno muy bueno, las habitaciones son comodas y grandes.
Un lugar para volver.

name: Hotel on Rivington
title: “great hotel”
text: Great small hotel. Prior reviews made me somewhat wary, but I took a chance anyway. Still in the soft opening stage -- but I saw no construction dust or yellow "danger" tape (per previous comments). Staff (tho a bit overworked) were friendly and helpful. Rooms were lovely -- though it may take a few minutes to figure out the lighting and hot water controls. Great complimentary breakfast buffet. I only expected coffee and a roll but there was also cereal, juices, croissants, pastries, and bagels. After spending the day out in the pouring rain, we decided to call room service for dinner. The hotel does not have its own kitchen but orders from a nearby restaurant. Good food and reasonably priced. The hotel is located near a subway line and easy walking distance to nolita and soho. Teany, a great little restaurant, is across the street -- serves vegetarian and vegan food, wine, beer, coffees and a huge variety of teas.

name: Pod 51
title: “Volvere al Pod Hotel”
text: Reservé una habitación individual con baño compartido del 7 al 15 de Junio 2009, tuve la 1417, que nada más entrar me encantó. Sin problemas al utilizar los baños, siempre utilizando la luz que poseia la habitación, no tuve que esperar ninguno de mis 8 dias de estancia para utilizar el baño compartido. Internet muy bien aunque se caia en la habitación, como solución está la recepción. La situación del Hotel es muy buena, metro al lado y en pleno centro. Volveré sin dudas.

name: Pod 51
title: “Non vale il prezzo pagato”
text:
lati positivi:
+ location perfetta
+ pulizia delle camere
+albergo nuovo e trendy
lati negativi
- stanze minuscole (oltre il letto 50cm per lato)
- ascensori continuamente rotti
- lavandino in acciaio non in bagno, ma nella camera da letto
Indefinitiva un bell'albergo nuovo e logisticamente valido ma con camere a dir poco sacrificate:loconsiglierei solose effettivamente più conveniente degli altri hotel in zona, oppure per non più di una/due notti

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Excellent Hotel!”
text: This hotel was an excellent find! The amenities were superb, rooms clean and sleek and the staff was fantastic. The location was also great. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Fabulous!”
text: Just arrived back in Scotland having stayed 5 nights in this glorious hotel. Myself and 15 of my friends were in NYC celebrating some of my friends 50th birthdays. I emailed ahead to Jessie to request adjoining/higher level rooms and when we arrived we received rooms on the 41st floor, free wifi AND champagne and chocolates in each room. 4 of our party were upgraded to a junior suite which became our meeting point! A small tip ($3) each day ensured we had enough glorious Starbucks coffee on hand and a short walk round the corner to the deli provided an adequate breakfast to start the day. The beds were indeed "heavenly" and the double headed shower was a god send after a hard day shopping and sight-seeing. The rooms was spacious with an absolutely fantastic view and immaculate. The bell boy, reception staff and doormen couldn't be more helpful. The hotel is situated just far enough away from the centre of Times Square but as it's near 7th Ave, very convenient for everything. Loads of restaurants, shops and deli's nearby. On our last day (Tuesday) the hotel was celebrating it's 10th Anniversary and before we left, we were treated to a glass of champagne and cake in the foyer and the bell boy took our luggage from our rooms and stored it until we were ready to leave. Can't thank Jessie and the rest of the staff enough for the best time ever. Will definitely stay in this hotel again. Miss it already!!!

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “A fantastic place to stay with great staff”
text:
We arrived for a short stay in New York on our way home after spending 2 weeks in a villa in Florida. After having the luxury of so much space, we weren't particularly looking forward to spending 2 nights with two adults and two 16 year olds falling over each other in a small hotel room. However, we needn't have worried. Upon check-in, we were delighted to find that we'd been upgraded from a 1 bedroom suite to a fantastic 2 bedroom 2 bathroom corner suite with a view of the Empire State Building from all windows. We couldn't believe our luck!
Each of the rooms were spacious with plenty of storage space. The kitchenette was sufficient to store drinks and snacks, and had a cupboard with an iron and ironing board, which came in useful after our previous travels.
We didn't make use of the restaurant or bar on this occasion, as we didn't spend much time at the hotel with such a short stay and a lot to fit in, but it always looked busy when we passed which is surely a good sign.
The staff were all lovely and so helpful - the doormen, the bellboys, the receptionists and the concierge went out of their way to make sure everything was perfect for us. We just wish we could have stayed longer to make the most of everything this hotel has to offer. We would not hesitate to stay here again on our next trip.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Ideal pour visiter New York”
text:
Nous sommes revenus de New York le 22 Mai, mon avis est identique à celui de VoyageFamRen, à part que nous étions au 31e étage et quasiment pas de bruit, je pense que si vous voulez être tranquille il faut demander à être logé assez haut.
Sinon, on trouve tout à proximité: métro, bus ,l'hôtel n'est pas loin de Times Square, nous avons fait beaucoup de trajets à pieds étant donné l'emplacement de l'hôtel.
Accueil très correcte, malgré une heure d'arrivée tardive.
Vous avez une personne dans le hall : appelée "concierge" très sympathique qui vous donnera tous les renseignements nécessaire à vos déplacements.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “GREAT EXPERIENCE”
text:
I brought a group of students to New York for a field trip. We had done this trip last year and stayed at a hotel a block away. Due the the incredibly HORRID experience we had at the other hotel, we decided to spend a little bit more and went to the Affinia. Am I glad we did! 
From the moment we entered the hotel, we were treated royally. There was no wait at the front desk, and the staff there could not have been nicer or more professional. Even though our rooms weren't ready, the Bell staff took our bags and stored them for us at no charge. When we came back and checked in, our bags were right there, and brought out to us with a smile.
The rooms far exceeded my expectations. They were HUGE. 2 beds, a sleep sofa and 2 bathrooms. They were clean and well stocked. The only thing remotely bad that I can say about the hotel is the street noise. It was a wonderful place to stay and I will go back there every year!

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “Met all essential family needs, comfortable and great location.”
text: In NY for brothers wedding. Had two kinda large teenage boys along. Got a suite with pull-out bed, right across from Waldorf-Astoria side entrance. The pull out was a little small, our our boys a little big. The bedroom side was adequate for husband and I. Without large boys it would have been quite roomy... Not quiet, part of being centrally located Midtown. Nice bar downstairs, little pricey. Nice staff, clean, decent bathroom, close to most everything you go to NYC for.

name: Pod 51
title: “Modernes, angenehmes Hotel, jedoch mit kleinen Schwächen”
text: - Sehr schön, ordentlich und sauber - Die Zimmer mit Etagenbetten sind recht klein - 2 Bäder pro Flur (könnte noch ein weiteres Bad sein, jedoch sind diese sehr schön! Shampoo und Duschgel sowie Seife auf dem Zimmer stehen zur Verfügung) - angenehmes Personal - 2 Aufzüge, zu wenig (recht klein, Aufzug hat an manchen Tagen 7 mal gehalten bevor man auf sein Zimmer oder nach draußen kam) - Wenn man sich etwas gewünscht hat, wie z.B. ein weiteres Kopfkissen, eine Bettdecke oder die Reparatur des Telefons musste man dies etliche Male aussprechen. Das empfand ich als ärgerlich!(Daher Hotelservice nur 2 Punkte) - Lage ist nicht schlecht, subway ist 1,5 Blöcke entfernt (Um nach Midtown zu kommen, muss man jedoch an der 42. in eine andere umsteigen.) - Auf der Avenue sind einige Bars und Lokalitäten

name: Hotel Mela
title: “Would Stay Again”
text: Rooms are nice and modern, and yes, very small. We stayed in the queen room and although we did not spend too much time in the room, it was a tight fit with both of our luggage. This is a great location especially if you intend to see a few shows as it is in the heart of the theater district. I could do without being right in Time Square ever again--far too congested, although close to a Subway so it is convenient. Very close walk to Hell's Kitchen for reasonable ethnic foods.
