Under the right circumstances, I would definitely stay here again.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “westin made our trip extra special”
text: Our family stayed at The Westin for my 40th and when they found out they made it a birthday to remember and made me feel very special. The views from our hotel room were spectacular. When Hurricane Sandy hit the city the team couldn't have been more helpful keeping us up to date with what was happening. We were two minutes from Times Square, the location couldn't have been better. It was a holiday to remember and we would recommend the Westin to anyone visiting NYC.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Great hotel, great location”
text: My 20-year-old daughter, her friend, and I stayed at the Belvedere 11/11 through 11/15. We arrived at 11:30 a.m. and were given a room right away. The staff was very friendly, and the concierge was helpful. The location is perfect - very close to Times Square, Rockefeller Center, Central Park, etc. I had read reviews about the elevators being slow and crowded but that was generally not a problem (we were on the 7th floor). The only time we came across this problem was when a large group was checking out, and everyone was trying to get to the lobby at the same time. I would definitely stay there again. On a completely different note, we wanted to go on the Circle Line for the two-hour cruise around lower Manhattan to see the Statue of Liberty without having to stop there. The Circle Line was dirty, smelly and crowded - thankfully, we got off before the boat left. We ended up going on a 3-hour dinner cruise with Spirit Cruises - a lot more expensive but well worth it - dinner, music, dancing, and a wonderful view of the Manhattan skyline, the Brooklyn Bridge and the Statue of Liberty lit up at night - it was our favorite part of the trip.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Great Location!”
text: I loved the deal we got on this hotel so close to Penn Station and close to times square but hardly clogged with tourists. There's a great pub two blocks north. I do wish they posted that the high-speed internet that's offered in the rooms comes with a charge. I figured it was complimentary. Airport shuttle is not offerred complimentary. We took a taxi, which was cheaper than airport shuttle services offered by various companies. Since we were close to the subway and nj transit, we had the underground transportation in the bag....we can go anywhere without using a taxi. the metro tickets were reasonably priced and the subway system is not hard to master as long as you know exactly where you're going. The concierge staff is awesome!!!!!!!!!! I bought empire state building tickets from there so I avoid the lines. They were very helpful to give us pointers on which subway stations to take for certain spots we wanted to check out. I do wish the beds were a little bigger. I shared a bed and they seemed more like full size and I wished they were more like a queen size. Other than that, the room with the kitchennette was awesome. Loved the location. Would book there again.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Tips for Westin visitors”
text:
As a New Yorker, I rarely have the luxury of paying astronomical fees for staying a night in the absolute worst part of Manhattan. But when Sandy struck, I had no other choice to get to work.
Here, I will leave some words to the wise for those of you who do find yourself staying at this hotel.
1) Do NOT make or receive any phone calls from your room. I was slammed w a $20 fee for one FIVE minute INCOMING phone call from the U.S. to my room.
2) The mini-fridge is magnetized - do not pick up ANY item unless you want to be charged...$8 for a small water, for instance.
3) When ordering room service, you will not only be hit with the traditional 18% gratuity and high food prices, you will also be hit with a $6 "delivery fee." Which means one small pot of English breakfast tea = $18.
4) You must pay to get Internet access in the room: another $14 per day to be precise. 
5) If you must eat in this horrible tourist trap of an area, go to Qi (an Asian fusion place across the street...it's actually good and reasonably priced).
Cheaper than other hotels in the area, this place certainly know how to "get you" in the details.

name: Wingate by Wyndham Manhattan Midtown
title: “Nice hotel, great location”
text:
This was the first time that my wife and I visited NYC during Christmas. The hotel was pricey ($1600 for 4 nights but that may be the going rate at this time) but very conveniently located. We were able to walk to Macy's; Time Square; Empire State Building; the Theater District and Penn Station (to catch the subway). Other POIs we were able to walk to but are a bit farther were: Rockefeller Center; St. Patrick's Cathedral and Radio City Music Hall. You would need transportation to Central Park and sites in lower Manhattan (subway was very convenient to see the WTC; Staten Island Ferry, Wall Street.
Wingate is a small hotel. It has 18 floors with only 6 rooms on each. They do offer free continental breakfast which is very good. We had a room on the fourth floor facing the street. We could hear street noise but not enough to disturb our sleep. Our room was nice. We had problems with the security safe and mini refrigerator which was taken care of the day after we checked in.
Housekeeping was adequate. I needed to ask 3 times for additional towels and pillows. And when the room was cleaned, dirty cups were not taken care of or the ice bucket emptied.
Overall I rated the hotel a bit higher than I would if it were not in NYC.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York/Tribeca
title: “Great Stay!”
text: My fiancee and I recently stayed here for one night and we really enjoyed it. As Gold HHonors members we were greeted very warmly by the staff and given two free bottles of water and coupons for a free breakfast at AOA restaurant. We had a room in the back of the hotel and it was very new, spotless, and super quiet. The hotel is perfectly located on top of a subway station and in walking distance to Soho. We will definitely be back!

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Great customer service and awesome hotel!!”
text:
During my recent stay, I came across a small issue with the way my company booked my travel. However, my frustrations were quickly and effectively resolved by the very helpful (and beautiful if I may add) young lady (Sally) at the reception desk. I honestly felt like I was dealing with someone who legitimately cared. I will continue to book my NYC stays at the Westin Times Square for at least as long as she is on the staff because of this pleasant experience! 
The rooms were renovated and very clean as ive come to expect with the fine Westin brand. 
Highly recommended!

name: Hotel on Rivington
title: “Bella posizione, servizio pessimo”
text:
ciao abbiamo soggiornato all'hotel On Rivington durante la nostra luna di miele, la posizione è bella, la metro è a pochi passi ma le camere sono piccole e scure durante il giorno non puoi tenere le tende aperte altrimenti crepi dal caldo, se vai nel periodo estivo, visto che i tre quarti delle pareti dell'hotel sono vetrate.
Il servizio è pessimo, il personale è maleducato e non ti presta praticamente alcuna attenzione, non salutano. Alla reception hanno sempre un atteggiamento altezzoso. 
Peccato per la zona perchè è molto bella e caratteristica, sembra di vivere nella vecchia NY, ma non ci tornerei mai più in quell'hotel.

name: Pod 51
title: “New York city Highlight”
text: Bin total begeistert, Top 1,centrale Lage, 5 Min zur U-Bahn, sehr sauber, Bettwäsche und Handtücher wurden täglich gewechselt, WC und Duschen auf dem Gang modern und sauber, Internet auch im Zimmer , Fenster ließen sich öffnen, Heizung konnte man abstellen: Top Hotel für Top Preis = Reisezeit im Februar 2009

name: Hotel Mela
title: “New Years in Manhattan”
text:
We stayed at this little hotel during our NYE trip to the Big Apple. We were very pleased.
The hotel is very nice, clean, and not too big. It is 1 block off Times Square. I felt I got good value for what I spent.
I did have a problem. But the hotel addressed and and made me very happy. For that, the will get my business on my next trip.
The room I first got had a bed that was too small for me. I'm 6-3, 230 lbs. The bed was only 6 feet long, and as narrow as a twin. I guess that is what is called an "executive" or something. Anyhow, It was too short for me. So they upgraded me to a room with a nice queen that we could fit on. But if you are under 6-1, and travelling alone, the small bed would be more than enough.
The staff were very nice and helpful.
Location was fine for a first timer to NYC. It was a quick walk to 5th Ave, Empire State, Macy's, Times Square, etc. The subway gets you everywhere else quickly and efficiently.
And the hotel has fast free WiFi for guests. Thank god!

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Very nice”
text:
I stayed at this hotel back in June, (it has taken me a while to write the review). I was impressed with the location (quiet and great diner across the street). Not too far from Zabars and Central Park. The room was clean, bathroom was very nice, and the bed was the most comfortable I have slept in. I had no problems with the service, hotel staff was pleasant, but I can see how there might be issues here. 
I paid 268 a night, which I thought was a bit much, but for the location and lack of roaches, I guess it was worth it. We stayed in a Superior room on the 12th floor, great view. Be sure to ask for a room on one of the highest levels, it gets rid of most of the street noise.

name: Wingate by Wyndham Manhattan Midtown
title: “Don't understand this question. If people don' t want to answer a question let be.”
text:
Good hotel. Somewhat pricy. Staff very helpful and professional 
Why do you want 100 characters for this? I am about to quit entirely too much trouble l

name: Wingate by Wyndham Manhattan Midtown
title: “recent trip to NYC”
text: I stayed at the Wingate due to Wyndham reward points covering the cost of my room. I arrived in Manhattan around 8.30 am, and when I checked in, there was actually a room available. In addition, the gentleman at the front desk mentioned that breakfast was still being served, and to help myself. A huge plus was this hotel was one block away from Penn Station, and coming directly from the airport on LIRR, it was a huge plus not having to walk very far with my luggage. At the end of my stay, they were helpful in holding my luggage so I could continue to explore NYC until it was time for me to head back to the airport. The hotel employees could not have been nicer and I have a hard time sleeping in hotel beds - but found that this was not a problem for me on this trip. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone.

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “New York Charm”
text: We stayed at The Barclay for one night. The room was gorgeous, the hotel is very nice in general. Our bathroom was too small, though, more appropriate for a 2-3 star hotel, and worst of all, gunk was up into the sink, making it utterly disgusting. When I complained to the management about it, they apologized and offered us free buffet breakfast. The location of the hotel is spectacular.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “AMAZING HOTEL”
text: This is the perfect hotel when you go to New York City. The staff is extremely friendly and helpful. Upon arrival they take your bags and make you feel at home. That's a pretty nice feeling when your in New York City. Check in was a dream. They certainly try to accommodate you! The room was on the 43rd floor. A view of the cruise ships and Hudson River. Gorgeous! Also, It was very quiet. Sleeping was no problem. The rooms were spotless. We were close to many good restaurants like Smith's across the street. Great food and very well priced. One of the best things we did was buy the pass from City Tours. It's and on and off bus service which was wonderful. All the sites wihere with a guide on board. This is certainly worth the money. The sales people are everywhere in Time Square. We bought the $85.00 package and it was great. I would definitely book the Westin Time Square again.

name: Hotel Mela
title: “Great Location and Enjoyable Stay”
text: Stayed for one evening while in the city and loved this hotel. Clean, updated room. Yes, small, but not unlike most rooms in NYC. The location was great. A quick walk to the theater -- and if you don't already have tickets to a show -- the TKTS booth is just a couple blocks away for discounted tickets. Mini coffeemaker in the room -- nice touch.

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “AWESOME STAY AT A GREAT HOTEL!”
text:
I stayed at the Affinia Shelburne Hoyel in New York City last week for 2 nights. This is the first time I stayed there. WHAT A GEM! It has been recently renovated from top to botom. Great new rooms, bathrooms, beds, carpets, furniture, etc. Beautiful new chic lobby with large comfortable sofas and chairs....I hung out there for over an hour reading my newspaper and using the computers. The Concierge in the lobby was so helpful. I have been a member of Tripadvisor for many years and this is only the second time I felt so excited about a hotel and motivated enough to spread the word and write a review. 
Below is a list of reasons I can't wait to go back for another stay at the Affinia Selburne:
1) Great location in Midtown. Not far from Broadway Theatre. Not far from shopping Uptown (Madison and Fifht Avenue) and Downtown (Soho and the Village). Close to Penn Station and Grand Central Train Stations. 
2) Many great restaurants close by...just ask the Concierge for help. 
3)Extremely helpful and kind Staff....doormen, front desk, concierge, etc. I needed two additional feather pillow and they were delivered to my room in minutes!
4) Awesome newly renovated clean room, beds, hallways and lobby. I slept like a baby.
5)Great prices for a hotel of this calibre in the heart of New York city.
6)Happening new restaurant off the Lobby named "Rare". People I met there came from all over the city to have dinner at this casual restaurant. Some told me it is the best burger in town! There are many other things on the menu including steak, etc. They also offer room service. If you want fancier restaurants, you don't have to go far. There are Italian, Seafood, French restaurants close by. Close to Subway and many other restaurants are only a few minutes taxi ride away. Just ask the doorman to get you a cab.
 I have stayed at many NYC Hotels over the past 25 years and I have never been so excited about a Hotel like the Affinia Shelburne. Newly renovated rooms, not too big, fair prices, clean, great location and awesome service. Luxury at a fair price that won't break the bank. Can't wait to go back.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Sofitel: Belle of New York”
text: My husband and I just spent a wonderful weekend in New York. The trip was totally enhanced by our experience at the Sofitel. The hotel was immaculate, the staff were friendly and helpful (Erica on the front desk was warm and welcoming. We were greeted coming and going. They accommodated an early check-in and late departure without fuss. The rooms were spotless and the bed was everything other reviewers claimed...soft, comfy with beautiful white linens. Fabulous location close to everything. Minutes from Times Square, Fifth Avenue etc. Quiet street with little traffic noise to disturb (we were on the 12th floor). The room size was very good and the bathroom was outstanding. If I have to provide any negative it was the concierge who had the sterotypical level of aloofness (gave us incorrect directions for using the subway...the station he directed us to was closed for construction)but it ended up being part of the adventure of using the NY subway system. You won't regret a stay at this hotel.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Next To A Busy Firehouse”
text: Decent hotel with clean rooms but dated decor. Price was reasonable, but there is a very busy NYFD firehouse immediately next door on 31st Street. The midnight shift drivers of the trucks are not shy about laying on the horn and blasting the sirens when wheeling out of the barn. Get ready for an interrupted night's sleep.

name: Novotel New York Times Square
title: “hotel ottimo...ma la cauzione NO”
text: hotel comodo, anzi comodissimo, centrale, vicino stazione metro e a due passi da central park, moma, times square e i suoi teatri e ristoranti praticamente sempre aperti ed ottimi (consiglio vivamente la steak house attaccata all'ingresso dell'hotel, solo la vetrina è una garanzia non aggiungo altro,provare per credere ovviamente se non siete vegetariani).unica pecca è il pagamento di una cauzione di 500 dollari che viene scalata dalla carta di credito all'arrivo in hotelassolutamente troppo alta e a mio avviso non necessaria.era la prima volta che mi accadeva in tanti anni che viaggio.

name: Wingate by Wyndham Manhattan Midtown
title: “Great location and value!”
text: If you want to stay in a clean, conveniently-located, affordable NYC hotel then Wingate by Wyndham is the place: clean and nicely maintained room (shower has wonderful shower massage head); complimentary wi-fi; complimentary buffet breakfast; friendly, helpful staff; conveniently located near Penn Station, Times Square, and many other attractions just a few blocks away in either direction. Really enjoyed our stay!

name: Wingate by Wyndham Manhattan Midtown
title: “Great hotel”
text: Great hotel with all you can eat breakfast included in the price, free computers in a comfy seating area which is great if you have a late flight like we did. rooms very clean and staff great, perfect location and quiet at nights will defo stay here again if I return.

name: Wingate by Wyndham Manhattan Midtown
title: “FABULOUS!”
text:
I would HIGHLY recommend staying at this hotel. Our experience was superb. The entire hotel staff, from the cleaning team to the front desk crew, was prompt, friendly and helpful. We had some water on our floor from where the AC had leaked and they quickly moved us to another room, even bringing us the new key so we didn't have to come back down to get it.
The room we stayed in (a King) was large and spacious compared to most other NYC hotels. We also appreciated the fact that Wingate stayed true to their free breakfast, free wifi, and other free hotel ammenities even though this was their NYC location. At most other hotels in the NYC area you have to pay for these services even if other less popular locations offer them for free. Thank you Wingate!
Another total bonus to staying here was the ease of access if you are driving in. It was a straight shot from the Lincoln tunnel to the parking garage we used. And then another straight shot back out to the Lincoln tunnel when our trip ended. Super easy, I didn't have to make any blocks, it was perfect!
Great experience! Great breakfast! Great staff! Two thumbs up!!

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “OK for New York - Nothing over the Top”
text:
Nothing fancy about the hotel & for the money given that it is NY, it is OK.
+ side: huge bed, adequate bathroom, good location (can walk to grand central)
- side: slow lift, expensive internet, no views

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “I loved this hotel”
text: I was a bit nervous after reading some of these reviews, but I have to say that I loved the hotel. My husband and I stayed in a superior room on one of the business nights for NYC which was New Year's Eve. The staff was wonderful and ready for us. There was a piano player in the lobby playing holiday songs. Every time we walked in or out of the hotel, someone opened the dooor for us. The hotel was sold out but we waited only moments to check out. The staff was wonderful. The lobby is beautiful. The balcony is amazing. The room was great and the bed was very comfortable. We were so happy, we were sad to leave. I would highly recommend this hotel. We will be going back for sure.

name: Pod 51
title: “Minimal ma comodo”
text:
Consigliato da alcuni amici, che poi ho trovato in loco, ho scelto questo piccolo hotel di cui avevo già sentito parlare.
Trattandosi della mia prima volta a New York, mi ero informato su quali fossero le caratteristiche più importanti da cercare in un albergo: pulizia, camere nuove/rinnovate, posizione comoda.
Sotto questi tre aspetti, "The Pod" è una soluzione soddisfacente: sebbene non si sia visto assegnare un diluvio di stelle (mi pare siano solo 2), presenta un ottimo rapporto qualità/prezzo.
Recentemente rinnovato, l'hotel si trova lungo la centralissima 51st street, una posizione invidiabile: una via tranquilla e comoda sia per i mezzi (la metropolitana linea 6 è a un isolato di distanza), sia per buone passeggiate.
Unico vero neo è la dimensione delle stanze, veramente minima: consiglio a chi viaggia con molte valigie (o soggiorna a lungo) di cercare un'altra soluzione.
Volendo essere pignoli, i corridoi sono un po' bui e gli ascensori lenti; tuttavia, i servizi di reception e la concierge sono davvero rapidi ed efficienti, e la rete wi-fi gratuita in camera è un autentico lusso.

name: Hotel Indigo New York City, Chelsea
title: “Worth the money - a rare find in New York”
text: We were here for only one night. The room was huge by New York standards; bed was very comfortable. Free wifi. Shower was big - the tiled floor and glass panel style. No standing in a bathtub - hooray! High quality soaps, etc, that actually smelled good and worked. Everything very well designed and thought out, from hair dryer to iron to mini bar to good info book and NY magazines. The room was decorated in a modern hip style, no ugliness; a miracle, really. Elevator operation in conjunction with room keycard - very secure. Very convenient location. Staff very pleasant and non-annoying. We have travelled the world, so we know what is good and bad; we run a b&b so we know what people expect; and this hotel will be our first choice in New York, every single time. Congratulations, Hotel Indigo.

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “not the international intercontinental standard!”
text:
The Barclay does not even relate to the intercontinental standards. Staff at the ground floor are friendly and doing their best! Rooms are basic. TV channels frequently shaking! Bathroom tiny and not kept clean. Room service number is always busy (stayed four days). They are obviously under staffed or can not cater for the size of the hotel!! So tried for 20 minutes to get an answer from room service (private dinning as they call it) and not answer (tried thru operator...same thing). Keep in mind you may need 30 minutes to get a taxi to the airport.
In summary, not worth the price!

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “Absolutely loved the Barclay”
text: Just returned from a 3 night stay at the Barclay. Having read some of the recent posts, we had some reservations but not any more. The hotel itself is wonderfully situated within walking distance of almost everything. The check in was smooth and friendly, the rooms were huge and spotlessly clean. prbably the biggest bed we have ever slept in. We were on the thrid floor and had a great view of lexington and the chrysler building. Street noise was ok and not too troublesome. Restaurant and bar were mega expensive with a pint of beer costing $10 so didn't use either but there are plenty of other places around to eat. (Try PJ Moran on w48th between 5th and Park and Langans on E46th between 6th and 7th). I would go back to the barclay in a trice given the chance.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Excellent stay”
text: Just back from three night stay at the Westin with three teenagers. We stayed on 41st floor and unlike other reviewer we had absolutely no problem with odour in the room which was cleaned to a high standard each day. The room was large enough for us all and the view from the window was fantastic, we even managed to get some great photos of the Empire State building from there. Luis and the rest of the staff we spoke to were extremely helpful with giving directions and suggestions etc and although these may seem minor details they are so important when you are in a strange place and time there is limited. We all agree that when we return to New York we would not consider staying anywhere else other than Westin.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Great place for short stay in NYC”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel for one night in late June 2003. 
It is the best hotel experience we've had in our three trips to NYC. 
The room was small, but very clean and the updated contemporary European furniture and bathroom fixtures gave it a nice feel. The lobby was grand and the hotel workers were very polite and helpful. This is a great place to stay if you will be in town only for a night or two. 
It's in a quiet (for NYC) upscale neighborhood and only two blocks from the American Museum of Natural History and the 77th street entrance Central Park and Strawberry Fields. I wouldn't recommend this hotel on the Upper East Side if you want to spend much time sightseeing across the city because you will spend a good deal of time on the subway or incur some pricey cab fares.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Pleasant and Good Value”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at On The Ave for 10 nights in March. It was our first time in NY and I spent a considerable amount of time researching a hotel that would be enjoyable to stay in and fit our tight budget.Taking the advice of several reviews here and others on the internet we selected On The Ave. We were very happy with our choice. The room was good, not luxurious, but clean and comfortable and, I believe, quite large for NY. The bathroom was lovely, clean and modern with a large shower.We did not have much contact with the staff but what we did was efficent and helpful.The views from the roof are fabulous and worth checking out, and the suites look excellent if you can afford a bit more.The location was perfect for our tourist style trip, with the Subway just 2 minutes away and Central Park less than 5 minutes walk. A plesant residental area with families, coffee shops and excellent supermarkets.The quality of a hotel can really change your experience of your holiday in my opinion and I would recommend On The Ave as good value and much nicer than a larger chain unless you can afford something glitzier!

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “excellent hotel brilliant for first visit to new york”
text: the hotel was really comfortable with excellent bathroom, small kitchen, huge wonderfully comfortable beds. It was within walking distance of many sights, easy bus route. Good guide books in the room. The only down was the taxi we had booked didn't turn up to take us to airport very early in the morning but one was passing so we were only held up a few minutes. would definitely stay here again.

name: The Belvedere
title: “Hôtel Le Belvedere: Agréable et bien situé”
text:
Propreté irréprochable - Chambre agréable avec lit king size
Choix entre petits déjeuners buffets: continental ou américain
Personnel ne parlant pas français mais attentif
Proximité de Times Square, de sites touristiques, des théatres
Métros proches - Nombreux restaurants, saladeries, sandwicheries ...

name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Times Square South
title: “Agosto in America coast to coast”
text: Ho passato con mio figlio 4 giorni al marriott in agosto, albergone con ascensori trasparenti e sala fitness a vetri vista Times square, albergo nella media, camera spaziosa con divano e scrivania letto king size, tv al plasma XL, sveglia ricarica iPhone. Ma è la posizione a rendere super questo hotel, ogni volta che esci dall'albergo sia di giorno che di notte rimani a bocca aperta, a piedi con una passeggiata vai a top of the rock, rockfeller centre, central park, MOMA, Columbus Sq. In albergo starbucks e a pochi passi un ottimo ristorante hard rock, con burgher veg, botteghino per biglietti scontati spettacoli brodway, il sabato una folla di gente. Consigliato.

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “We Loved It!”
text: Went to New York to see a play and stayed at the Barclay(intercontinental). The room was the largest we've had in New York City. The room was very clean and the bed was just magnificent. We had the brunch on Saturday and Sunday and it was fantastic. I will definitely stay here again. I highly recommend the Intercontinental Barclay.

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Perfect experience here”
text:
We booked a promotional deal through Travelzoo, which was very affordable. We had a one-bedroom suite for three nights in February. 
The suite was very spacious, especially by NYC standards. The bedroom and living room format worked very well for us, as we were five people. There was plenty of closet space, two TVs and two fridges, which meant that we never felt as if we were on top of one another. 
The rooms and bathrooms were spotless and very attractively decorated. The linens were lovely and the beds very comfortable.
Our room had a view of an air shaft, but we didn't care at all, as we were not there in the daytime very much.
The staff were genuinely friendly and helpful -- not a trace of attitude. 
If we can get a deal here again, we will definitely return. A total delight!

name: The Belvedere
title: “hotel Belvedere à New York: à 2 pas du centre.”
text: hotel conforme à nos attentes : propreté, literie confortable, proche de toutes commodités. Nous étions à 4 dans une chambre avec une kitchenette très pratique au 14 ème étage avec vue sur manhattan.Je le recommande vivement.

name: BEST WESTERN Bowery Hanbee Hotel
title: “Very, very good hotel”
text: very nice people at the reception, kind, friendly and helpful, giving the right information about restaurants, places to go to etc. The rooms were very nice and clean as also the bathroom. Our stay was marvellous. A place to go back to. Breakfast was not too special as all was self service and given on plastic plates, cups and knifes. It would be nice if in the future, normal plates and knifes were used.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
My fiance and I stayed at the Sofitel for 5 nights from 21st February 2005 to the 26th February 2005. We chose this hotel based on Tripadvisor reviews and we were not disappointed. 
Our trip was to celebrate my 30th birthday and my partner had spoken to the manager and asked for an upgrade. Not only did we get an upgrade with views of the Empire State Building but a bottle of champagne and chocolates were left with a card wishing me a happy birthday. The manager introduced himself on our arrival and he and the rest of the staff were always helpful and very professional.
This was the first time we had asked for an upgrade and actually received one. We travel a lot and have stayed at many hotels. I am quite fussy and I can honestly say I did not have one complaint. The bar, restaurant and mini-bar were expensive, but that is to be expected at a top class hotel. The position of the hotel is great, within walking distance of all amenties. Duane Reade is a good chain of stores that provide everything you need at cheap prices and one store is situated right around the corner. There are also some Deli's very close by so you can get a decent breakfast at a good price. 
We stayed with family in Long Island for the rest of our trip and they too have only heard good things about the hotel.
We would definitely stay here again and recommend the hotel to family and friends. In addition, we would check out their other hotels first when booking accomodation in other countries.

name: Hotel Indigo New York City, Chelsea
title: “One night stay we would have liked to have extended”
text: We were staying in NYC one night, post-cruise. I found the Hotel Indigo through price line. What a find. Excellent, all around. We spent a very wet night in NYC, but our room was dry, warm and good sized, by NYC standards, with a large bathroom with large shower and wonderful bed and linens. The street is basically the flower / plant district, so walking on the sidewalk in the pouring rain was a bit difficult, but it would be an interesting street to check out next time. Some great restaurants nearby, and we would have loved to check out the roof-top bar, but for the rain. Very easy walk to Penn Station, or take the subway to the 28th street station. We will definitely be staying here again!

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Really great”
text:
I read the reviews and was afraid! The thing to remember is that there is a delay in the reviews posted (in order to verify) and so when I went to write this I found two recent new reviews which would have allayed my fears. 
Our first visit to New York was off to a great start when we saw our lovely room on the sixth floor. Beautiful new decor, very comfortable bed, good bathroom and the kitchen facilities useful. The location was spot on to visit many mid town attractions.
Service was excellent and so dicrete that we never saw a cleaner but the results were there. Nice toiletries (aveda), flat screen tv, cd player/alarm clock, iron/ironing board and safe in room.
The door staff and reception were approachable and willing to help with local info. I hope to return soon. 
P.S. The lobby was almost finished as we left so if they are working from the top down the renovation and rebranding of the hotel must be drawing to a close.

name: Hotel Mela
title: “Perfect Location, Spotless well decorated rooms, great service”
text: This is a small hotel and a huge value. A friend and I stayed for 1 night. The room was tiny (but what do you expect in NY) large enough for two twin beds, an end table, desk and chair, and armoire, and high speed internet (wireless and cable). Most important, it was spotlessly clean, very tastefully decorated, with comfortable beds and linens. The location is fantastic - between Times Square and Fifth Avenue, with wonderful shops and restaurants. Service was excellent. Our mini-fridge was locked when we arrived and an alarm went off when we tried to open it. The front desk quickly responded to repair the problem. John Paul, the concierge, was friendly and helpful. The adjacent Saju Bistro, which specializes in French Provencal cuisine, is a FIND (it is open for breakfast, lunch and dinner). The food and service were both superb and the pricing very reasonable - under $100 with tip for two of us, including appetizer, entrees. and wine, served attentively and efficiently to enable us to make our 8 pm curtain in plenty of time. Highly recommended.

name: Pod 51
title: “Hotel Fantastico”
text:
Abbiamo soggiornato al Pod hotel nel mese di Giugno 2007, per 7 notti.
L'hotel è situato in posizione centrale ,vicinissimo alla fermata della metro, a due passi dalla 5° avenue e da Times Square.
L'interno è nuovissimo e pulitissimo.
Anche optando per i bagni in comune non abbiamo avuto problemi,le toilettes sono molto pulite.
Le camere sono un pò piccole, ma se andate a New York non starete molto tempo in camera!!!!!.Quest'ultime vengono pulite tutti i giorni e la biancheria viene cambiata sempre.
Il personale è molto cordiale e gentile, c'è anche una signora gentilissima alla reception che è di origine italiana e parla la nostra lingua molto bene.
Pe rmangiare , l'hotel è circondato da ristoranti di tutte le nazionalità,noi abbiamo provato un ristorante messicano(LOS CAMINOS) molto buono, e uno italiano(IL PESCATORE) eccezzionale!!!
Per fare colazione avete l'imbarazzo della scelta.
In generale l'hotel è molto informale, dispone anche di un bellissimo cortile interno e di un terrazzo dove i fumatori incalliti come me potranno fumarsi una sigaretta godendosi la vista sui grattaceli di New York o, prendere un pò di sole.
Consigliamo vivamente il Pod Hotel soprattutto per il prezzo veramente competitivo!!!

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Staff leaves much to be desired......”
text:
Booked on Expedia but they neglected to tell us that the room would be one of the 
un-renovated ones. 
I think the hotel should resort to filling reservations for those particular rooms under construction. Listen to your customer reviews, they’re not happy. The only nice thing about those rooms is their spaciousness. 
As for the staff, get a new one! The front desk girls are plain rude, God forbid you ask them a question or bother them, and housekeeping move like snails. Due to them, you can bet I will never stay at your hotel again Alvin. The only pleasant workers were the concierge’s; I made sure I tipped them well.

name: Hotel Indigo New York City, Chelsea
title: “Pretty Close to Perfect”
text:
I only say "pretty close" because I'm aware that absolute perfection in anything is impossible. My experience staying at the Hotel Indigo was really as perfect as it could be, though, and this is coming from--well--a hotel snob. I can usually pick out several things to be unhappy about in a room--usually involving cleanliness--but this hotel was extraordinarily clean: bed, bathroom, shower, everything. (The sheets are pure white, too, so you can't hide any dirt or stains.) The bed was also incredibly soft and comfortable, as others have said, providing a great night's sleep. The staff was VERY friendly and helpful, and I'd recommend the salmon if you decide to eat there. :)
As for location, Times Square is just a short walk away. Lots of little shops and restaurants along the streets around it, and I felt safe walking around. As a female in the city by herself, that was really important to me.
I'd almost like to mention some tiny flaw so this review doesn't sound too good to be true. Really, though, I can't think of one, so I'll just say that I HIGHLY recommend this hotel. Five stars, easily.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Excellent”
text: Cette hotel est vraiment formidable avec son grand hall est son emplacement en pleins milieu de Manhattan les chambres sont assez petites mais de tout confort vous avez le métro a cote vous êtes sur Time square en 5 minutes et vous avez un excellent restaurant a l américaine ( qui est devenu notre cantine ) le tic toc diner

name: Hotel Mela
title: “Pleasantly surprised by an upscale boutique hotel in great location”
text:
Our outstanding experience started with a reassuring phone conversation with a hotel staff member before we even arrived who helped to ease our concerns about the weather and went on to ensure our overall stay was excellent despite forecasts of a snow storm. We found all of the staff to be absolutely terrific and friendly. The rooms are clean ,comfortable, quiet and well decorated and although not huge, are adequate in size. The bed and bed linens are of superior quality and very comfortable.
There are nice extras such as a work out room, free Internet Wi-Fi , bathrobes, higher quality toiletries and a Hotel Desires program that provides some extra snacks and beverages during your stay. 
Location is about as good as it gets in New York City, near the theatre district and museums, restaurants, etc
This hotels is now our first choice any time we plan a trip to New York. It is a real hidden gem.

name: Hotel Mela
title: “Pleasant and very comfortable, and a fantastic price for quality and location!”
text: This hotel is among the nicest we've ever stayed, starting with the lovely people - friendly and helpful. Our twin room was (contrary to popular belief) actually very spacious for new york, and we had great sleeps with little to no road noise. Beds were very comfortable and bathroom was nice too. The best thing about our room was that however much we looked carefully, we found no, I repeat not a single bed bug! The location of this hotel was wonderful, right across from the belasco theatre and right beside the lovely saju bistro which we ate at every night. This hotel is so worth the reasonable prices, so stop reading other reviewers' complaints about small rooms and unfriendly staff (neither of which are true) and book accomadation at this wonderful boutique hotel in the perfect location! You wont regret it!

name: The Belvedere
title: “Hotel Belvedere di New York”
text: Ottimo Hotel, in posizione centralissima, a due passi da Times Square e dai teatri di Broadway. La stanza era molto spaziosa il letto enorme anche se il riscaldamento altissimo faceva boccheggiare durante le ore notturne. Albergo molto pulito sia per quanto riguarda la stanza che le zone comuni. La colazione costa parecchio in hotel ma nelle vicinanze ci sono almeno 4 Starbucks e un sacco di altri locali dove fare un'ottima colazione a prezzi più contenuti. Nel complesso un ottima scelta.

name: Chambers Hotel
title: “Super staff”
text: This is a terrific hotel - the staff are superb and an asbolute credit to themselves and their hotel. I am always nervous staying at boutique hotels in NYC but Chambers is by far the best we've stayed at. Top location, really cool and comfortable rooms; we would definitely stay at The Chambers again.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Amazing Hotel Amazing Service”
text:
My wife and I just wanted to write this (we never do this sort of thing)
The Westin NYC made our trip the most memorable and special ever!!
Our stay was very special and without doubt a life highlight with our trip to the Apple.
The view from our room on the 42nd floor was simply breath taking, amazing and was beyond our dreams, we were blown away. It was a honeymoon / birthday trip and the management really pulled out all the stops to make it special. Little things go along way and we were made to feel like royalty.
I cant recommend this hotel highly enough, customer care on another level, nothing is too much hassle and they understand hospitality and care
Again Thanks for such great service, The Westin made the whole trip FANTASTIC.
We will be back soon.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Super gelegenes Hotel, jedoch mit Mägeln”
text:
Das Hotel liegt direkt am Broadway zwischen den U-Bahn-Stationen 72 & 79 und ist somit sehr leicht zu erreichen. Einzige Mängel waren die Fenster des Hotels. Durch die typische amerikanische Bauweise zum Hochschieben sind die Fenster extrem undicht. Der Straßenlärm wird kaum gedämmt und ebenso geht sehr viel Wärme über sie verloren. Dieses führt dann leider dazu, dass in der Nacht alle halbe Stunde die Heizung - im Winter - anspringt, die aus Heizlüftern in der Wand besteht.
Abhilfe schafft da nur ausgiebiges Auslaufen in der wundervollen Stadt, sodass man Abends müde ins Bett fällt und dieses "überschläft" :-)

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Hotel nice - location excellent!”
text:
We chose this hotel because it was in the center of it all. We were able to walk across the road & attend the NHL & NBA games, but also visit the concert (at the Madison Square Garden).
Shopping - You just cant avoid it, Macy's is just a few steps away.
The Empire State Building, Garment district, the Broadway - it is all there.
The hotel itself was big, clean & really nice. People, of course were actually very nice too :)

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “We'll be back”
text: We travel to N.Y. 2-3 times a year and like to try different hotels. The Salisbury is definitely the hotel we'll be staying at next time. The rooms are large and clean, but a bit run down. They changed the carpeting on all the floors while we were there, which was nice-- however the design was not very inspiring. Choose a room at the back and you'll get a good nights sleep. The location can't be beat!

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “fabulous hotel”
text: We have just returned from new york, we stayed at the intercontinental barclay. the location is brilliant in easy reach of times square. The meals were expensive, we decided to eat in a deli around the corner from the hotel, it was really cheap but not nasty. we found the hotel to be all we expected, beautiful room and a very luxurious huge bed. Spotlessly clean bathroom. the staff were helpful but not friendly. we would stay here again we enjoyed every minute of our city break.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Un buon hotel”
text:
Con la mia ragazza ho pernottato al New Yorker hotel dal 28/2 al 10/3/2011 e devo dire che ho avuto molto tempo per vederlo per bene dato che sono stato ammalato 5 giorni e non potevo uscire.Aspetti positivi: è un hotel pulito; gli ascensori sono veloci (cosa da non sottovalutare dato che eravamo al 33esimo piano); accanto ha un simpatico bar/ristorante che si chiama tik-tok che è risultato essere comodissimo anche per la colazione; è in un ottima posizione dato che è praticamente davanti al madison square garden e alla stazione della metropolitana di penn station. Aspetti negativi: non economico come hotel; dalle finestre entravano un sacco di spifferi che raffreddavano velocemente la stanza e quindi dovevamo tenere acceso il riscaldamento (con relativo rumore fastidioso).
L'importante per noi, in questa prima vacanza a New York, era quello di non capitare in un hotel sporco, o in zone non sicure e per questo devo dire che siamo restati soddisfatti. Sarebbe comunque meglio prenotarlo con qualche offerta..
New York comunque mi ha dato l'impressone di essere una città sicura e, quindi, anche se uno decidesse di prenotare un hotel in una zona un po' più periferica non penso che rimarrebbe deluso su quest'aspetto.
Enjoy New York!

name: The Belvedere
title: “Super Lage, komfortabel – auch mit Kindern”
text: Im Juli 2010 waren wir (2 Erw, 2 Kinder von 7 und 9 J.) zu Gast im Belvedere Hotel in NYC. Gebucht hatten wir ein Deluxe-Zimmer mit 2 Queensize-Betten, haben aber nach einem relativ günstigen Upgrading ein Executive-Zimmer bekommen. Das Zimmer war frisch renoviert, komfortabel ausgestattet (mit Mikrowelle, Kühlschrank, Kaffeemaschine, kleiner Sitzecke für 2), sehr sauber und gepflegt, das Bad in braunem Marmor klein, aber top. Das Personal war sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit, die Lage super. In 5 Min. war man zu Fuß am Broadway, Bus und Subway waren ebenfalls nah. Insgesamt ein super Hotel, das wir jederzeit wieder buchen würden.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Nichts besonderes!”
text:
Wir waren eine Woche in einer Penthouse Suite! Die Suite hat einen kleinen Balkon, was für Raucher ideal ist, da man nicht extra das Hotel verlassen muss um eine Zigarette zu rauchen! Das Zimmer war OK und sauber. Eine Renovierung der Hotelzimmer ist aber nötig, da das Zimmer an manchen Ecken schon sehr mitgenommen ist!
Die Lage des Hotels ist hervorragend die Dachterrasse im 16.Stock ein Traum, aber ansonsten einfach zu teuer!

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “EXCELENTE HOTEL”
text: Estuvimos en el New Yorker en el mes de mayo de 2011 y la verdad es que quedamos encantadas. Si bien por fuera no nos parecía un lindo hotel por dentro todo lo contrario. La ubicacion es buenisima y la habitación nos resultó comoda. El personal de limpiezxa y encargada muy amable. La verdad es que lo recomendaría mil veces.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “I wouldn't stay anywhere else!”
text: The hotel's location is unbeatable. The hotel is clean and comfortable. Staff is courteous and helpful. As others have mentioned, there is some construction on 57th Street at present, but we did not hear any of it. Our suite was on the 17th floor and on the back of the hotel. I already have reservations there for two trips in 2013!

name: Hotel Indigo New York City, Chelsea
title: “The place to stay”
text:
I would recommend this hotel to all my friends. Great location. Perfect value for price.
Personnel at the hotel were great recommending great restaurants and bars. Especially a girl at the reception. Unfortunately, I can't remember her name.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Absolutely lovely!”
text: Absolutely everything that we were hoping it would be: lovely, quiet, clean, great location, very friendly staff. Honestly, we don't want to stay anywhere else in NYC! Thanks, Sofitel!

name: Ace Hotel NYC
title: “Superb Staff”
text: Very cool hotel in mid-town Manhattan. Very current and fashionable. The rooms are like most New York hotels, not the biggest but the style and ambience of them is very unique. It really is a must visit hotel. Downstairs is always buzzing from 8 in the morning to 3am. The bar is great and the restaurant excellent. It is the sort of place you would go to even if you were not staying there.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York/Tribeca
title: “Great "free upgrade"”
text: La prenotazione ci è stata modificata all'arrivo a New York, ma l'essere spostati qui è stata veramente una gran fortuna. Ottima posizione con la metropolitana che ha una fermata esattamente sotto l'hotel, chinatown a due passi e downtown facilmente raggiungibile a piedi. Comoda ad ogni servizio. L'hotel è bello, pulito, lo staff cordiale. La connessione a internet veloce e semplice da impostare. Veramente ottimo

name: Chambers Hotel
title: “The Chambers was excellent”
text:
I must admit that I arrived at the Chambers with some trepidation after reading some of the reviews regarding the service here. These fears were completely allayed though the moment my girlfriend and I arrived by taxi from JFK and were greeted by a warm and welcoming bellhop and an attentive and informative reception who checked us in.
Throughout our three night stay the service was excellent and all staff members were helpful to a fault.
The King Studio room was amazing with a wonderful shower and soaking tub. The location as well speaks for itself with all the sights and attractions of Fifth Avenue and Central Park on your doorstep.
The only slight hiccup occurred when there was some crossed wires relating to whether breakfast was included in the tariff. This was resolved though in a professional and polite manner.
There's no business centre so you can't check emails, send faxes etc unless you have your own laptop. However the hotel lend out laptops and there is a high speed connection in the room. Reception also checked us in online for our onward flight so we didn't really miss having internet access.
All in all a wonderful stay at the Chambers. Yes it’s expensive but – and rarely for New York - you got what you paid for.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York/Tribeca
title: “prima en betaalbaar hotel op toplokatie”
text: Ga je naar links dan sta je middenin Chinatown, rechtdoor, Soho en rechtsaf ground Zero en iets verderop battery park. Recht tegenover het hotel zit een heerlijk italiaans restaurant, Pepolino. Wil je even lekker maar iets goedkoper eten dan is er keuze in overvloed op loopafstand. Wij vonden Franklin Cafe 222 W Broadway een aanrader. Bring your own wine!

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York/Tribeca
title: “Trevligt hotel med mycket bra läge!”
text:
Vi bodde på Hilton Garden Inn Tribeca i 6 nätter i augusti 2010 tillsammans med våra två tonårsbarn. Rummen var trevliga, vi bodde i ett rum med två dubbelsängar (ca 140 cm breda). I rummet fanns kylskåp, kaffebryggare och microvågsugn, platt TV med en massa kanaler (så klart). Städpersonalen var super och rummet var alltid snyggt och städat när vi kom tillbaka efter långa dagar på stan. Luftkonditioneringen var effektiv men bullrade kanske lite väl mycket, men inte så mycket att det var svårt att sova.
I hotellets källare fanns ett Business Center med 2 datorer och skrivare, gratis och mycket uppskattat av våra Facebook-beroende tonåringar. Hotellet hade också ett Fitness Center med löpband, motionscyklar, skivstänger mm, även det gratis. Personalen i receptionen var hjälpsam och trevlig.
Det bästa med hotellet var dock läget, alldeles intill en tunnelbanestation och med gångavstånd till Canal Street, nedre delen av Broadway samt Ground Zero m fl sevärdheter. Vi köpte 7-dagars obegränsade tunnelbanekort (rekomenderas verkligen) och det kändes fantastiskt skönt att kunna ta tunnelbanan ända fram till hotellet på eftermddagarna/kvällarna.
Vi bor gärna på detta hotell nästa gång vi åker till New York.

name: Ace Hotel NYC
title: “Great, unique, and fun hotel!”
text:
The Ace hotel was a great experience for me and my son (13). I like to give reviews based on the type of hotel it is and tell people more facts than opinion because everyone has certain tastes. This hotel is NOT a fancy, glitzy or glamorous hotel. It's probably not the best business typr hotel either but that's not why I was here. I’ve stayed at the Waldorf and Ritz Carlton and the Ace hotel is not at all like those two hotels but it does not try to be either. I’m not going to complain about not having fancy creams or lotions because it’s not that kind of hotel. Here is what to expect. The Ace hotel tries to mimic the days of old from the early 1900’s while mixing in some vintage touches through the 1970’s. It’s a boutique hotel which focuses on being trendy and whimsical. It pulls it off nicely. If you are tired of the same old regular rooms and same old regular lobbies and want something different then try the Ace. You’re only a 10 min slow walk from Penn Station where you can get on virtually any subway. You’re also right in midtown so expect a lot of traffic, noise and people. It’s NY! The lobby was dim and roomy with a bar at one end and the coffee shop at the other. The restaurants are along either side. Some people complain about the lobby being too dark, that is a fact but I was not bothered by it. You can read a book in it but if you want to do fine needlepoint in the lobby than bring a light. I had a great experience with the service. Checking in was a breeze. We arrived at 10 AM and they didn’t have a room ready but that was expected in NY on a Saturday. They were glad to hold out bags and called me at 2:30 saying it was ready. Our Medium room faced Broadway on the 5th floor. It was tight but spacious by Ny standards and fine for two people. Glad we got the medium but this was bigger than the room I had at the Ritz. We had a turntable which we requested, small fridge, king bed, desk, 32” LCD TV, Polaroid camera and separate bathroom through two doors. We had the basics any 3+ star hotel would have plus the use of the camera (film was $25 for 8 pictures). The turntable had about a dozen records to play and my son is 13 and loved it! About the camera, it’s free to use anywhere you want to take it. It’s like $120 though if you lose it so be careful. We took ours to the Top of the Rock and got a lot of stares and funny faces about the instamatic! Great conversation piece. Yes, the film is a little pricey but hey it’s NY and where else can you get to use a Polaroid camera. The pictures are monochrome (like brown and white) so your pictures look vintage. 
The view was nice and street noise was not bad at all. We had no problems sleeping. Bed was super comfortable and pillows were really plush. We both had a Great night’s sleep. I did notice in the morning that I could hear people talking through the other rooms. So I can understand what others were saying about the hotel not being very soundproof on same floor. However, since it was Saturday night they had a DJ playing in the lobby and he was jammin’! It was very loud but as soon as we got on the elevator and started going up I couldn’t hear a thing. Shower worked fine, plenty of hot water and they supply the body wash, shampoo and conditioner. The faucet looked a little worn and could use a facelift but the bathroom was clean and bright. Hairdryer, bath robes, iron, safe and coffee maker in the room too. The frig was stocked along with an assortment of goodies. The prices were hotel high but actually less than movie theater prices. Here’s a tip, the beer in your mini bar will cost you $6 a bottle but a beer at the lobby bar will cost you $10 (without tip)! Do the math that’s all I got to say. If you need frig space than you may want to inquire about another frig or a room that does not have a stocked frig. They had cookies, wine, beer, Vodka, liquors, candy bars, chips and other stuff. Check out was easy and fast. They will hold your bags until you get back if you check out and still want to spend the day in the city. I took the train in so don’t know about the parking situation. I also did not go to any of the restaurant’s either. We did go to the coffee shop in the lobby. Coffee was great and was moderately priced, probably same as starbucks. If you have your coffee there or in the lobby you can get mugs instead of paper cups. Thought that was nice. They only had a few things to eat so don’t expect to eat breakfast there. They also only take cash at the coffee shop so beware. 
So overall we had a great one night/two day stay at the Ace. I would recommend it highly for families with tweens/teens and/or young adults. Probably not the best place if you’re in your 60’s but who am I to judge if you like trendy hotels with record players. As with most hotels in NY I suggest a nice tip to the concierge when you check in and ask if he/she will be working during your stay. So if you need anything they are very willing to oblige. Please email me if you have any specific questions about the hotel.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Staying in N.Y. Stay at the Affinia Manhattan you will not be dissappointed.”
text: painless checkin-helpful staff-nothing too much trouble-great rooms-comfy beds-added bonus of a kitchen-excellent location for exploring N.Y. concierge booked us a table at Niles restaraunt next door we were highly delighted check out our review of Niles on TripAdvisor

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Every stay, just perfect”
text: Everything about this hotel exceeds expectation. The staff is the key to such a great hotel, they are the best of the best NY has to offer.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Great Location-Times Square on your door step!”
text:
It's situated on 7th Avenue (aka Fashion Avenue) between 31st & 30th street west opps Madinson Square , which is an idea spot to do your sightseeing and shopping. We did alot of walking every where, because most of the places we wanted to see are within walking distance ie Emprire State Building, Macey's & Times Square.
The rooms are good size which includes a mini kitchen ( which was handie), and the beds are big comfortable, staff were friendly & helpful.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Check in and room”
text: I just checked in at the Westin Times Square. My front desk agent, Jamiyl Samuels was extremely efficient and pleasant. He made sure I was satisfied with the type of room and also made a call to the W Hotel where we are staying later this week to request an upgrade. The room at the Westin Times Square is very nice and quite roomy for NYC. So far, so good.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Brilliant Location - just perfect”
text: We traveled back in October 2011 and stayed 5 days. The location is great. Room size good with the added benefit of the pantry. Access to Times Sq, Carnegie Hall, Central Park is brilliant. The hotel's staff are friendly and attentive. Angelo's pizzeria (a few doors down) is a must! The breakfast room is ideal in the hotel and reasonably priced, however the deli's surrounding the hotel are also great. We will be back and we will book this hotel as our first choice. The Grayline hop on hop off is a perfect way to get around. As well as the usual attractions - Empire State, America Museum of Natural History, Statue of Liberty, Top of the Rock we also visited - Chelsea Market, The High Line, World Trade and Grand Central - all must see's. Century 21 is ideal for shopping. Also China Town and Pearl River Mart, Bloomingdales on Broadway (as well as the original store) and Dylans Candy Bar.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Beautiful Rooms, Excellent Location”
text: This hotel is right in the middle of everything but the rooms are quiet and relaxing. Great views of Times Square and super comfortable beds.

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “Wonderful Hotel/Great Location”
text: We reserved a room through Priceline so we were unsure what to expect. However, the Intercontinental Barclay exceeded our expectations. It was in a perfect location: a short walk from Times Square, Union Station, Central Park, and the subway. The hotel itself is beautiful, with attractive and nicely sized rooms (for New York), and a 24-hour free fitness facility. I highly recommend it.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Great "Times Square" Location Hotel”
text:
We spent a few days in NYC and stayed at the Westin Times Square. We were there in Sept. 2011 for the Andrea Bocelli concert happening in Central Park. We did walk to the concert but found it farther than expected so we took a taxi back. Our weather was cool and sunny most days. Unfortunately, it rained for the outdoor concert.
The hotel is in a great location. We were right on the same block with the theaters performing Spiderman and Mary Poppins. We got great prices on same day tickets to Spiderman by going early in the morning of performance (very convenient from the Westin). We were able to walk a few blocks to pick up our sightseeing tour of all of the city.
The hotel is modern and sleek. Our room was in tan and black colors, typically sized for a city location hotel. Check in and check out were easy. The concierge/information desk was very helpful. We asked for recommendations for restaurants and directions and they were always helpful and knowledgeable with a smile. 
There seemed to be a good mix of business and leisure travelers at the the hotel. There is a movie theater and a Starbucks attached to the hotel. You do not need to even step outside to get to them. Although we did not have any meals/drinks at the hotel, they had a nice lounge/bar off of the main lobby, which is actually on the second level. You enter the hotel on street level, but take an escalator to the main check in and sitting area of the lobby. 
We were a group of four adults and we would certainly stay here again if returning to NYC for some leisure time and fun.

name: Night Hotel
title: “Friendly Staff, Clean n Great Location”
text: As soon as we walked in we can experienced an Excellent customer service already eventho we checked in at 2am. The room size is small but well equipped n clean, they also give us welcome chocolate bars n weather forecast for the whole week. This location is excellent for tourist that never been to NYC, Time square just around the corner, surrounded by Pubs n restaurants and shops. We really pleased stay at Night Hotel , we also wanna thank Mr.Simo who helped us organise a transport to the airport : )

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “A good stay”
text:
I stayed at the Shelburne for the ING NYC Marathon week and definiteky was a good choice. I had to stay a week, and I wanted an hotel with a kitchen in the rooms, so this was my choice. The room is definitely big, with a nice living room and a big room with two queen size beds. The bed was definitely confortable and I slept very well on it. The bathroom wasn't so big but comfortable, the shower worked very well and never ran out of warm water. The furniture was not so new but absolutely decent for the prize, the moquette on the floor was ok, I had a TV in each room (but I didn't watch it, so I can't tell if there was Pay TV or anything else). I also had an ironing board and an iron, very useful for I love to personally iron my shirt on some details before putting them on and the laundries at the hotels don't do it as well as I like usually, so I appreciated the find. The kitchen was not very big but not bad, with both electric and microwave ovens, a large fridge and comfortanele cooking fires. You also get dishes, cutlery and some pans and pots. Bring a good kitchen knife if you need it, the one they provide was not a sharp one.
They use to clean the room once a day. They always changed all the towels and i noticed they changed the sheets at least twice in a week, maybe more. The maid at my floor was very kind and whenever she accidentally found me inside the room (I often forgot the "do not disturb" sign) she always asked me at what hour she wouldn't disturb us.
The location is very convenient if you intend to use the subway: you're very close to Grand Central and all the lines are easily accessible from there. If you plan to use a taxi instead you'll better take a good planning of your week before deciding Murray Hill is the best place to stay. Anyway it's pretty close to Times Square, The Madison Square Garden, the Public Library and the Empire State Building.

name: Wingate by Wyndham Manhattan Midtown
title: “Great Value for Business Travellers in Midtown”
text:
I booked myself and my colleague into the Wingate after comparison shopping on Trip Advisor. We were both very happy that I'd done my research!
The Wingate prides itself on being set up for business travellers and this was definitely the case. Free high speed internet in the rooms, comfortable desks/chairs/beds and a heck of a lot more space than I'm used to having in New York City where you can pay $400/night for a tiny box. We paid $315 including tax and there was literally nothing more I could have asked for from this hotel or my room. In fact I've already booked another stay next month when I return to our New York office.
It was a little unfortunate that two high school dance teams were staying at the hotel (teenage girls - you figure it out) but it was a weekend so I guess we can't really complain. Reception was terrific though - put both me and my colleague onto floors where the girls weren't. Again, what more could one ask? Except mute buttons on 100 teenage girls, but I don't think the staff could have helped much on that front.
The breakfast, which is included in the room price, isn't fabulous but it's acceptable and should suit most tastes. The eggs were runny and tasteless, but we were there towards the end of the morning so it might just have been bad luck. But really it's unfair of me to complain - it was free and did the job.
My only suggestion to the property is to ditch the loud pulsating music in the lobby. While it can't be heard from the rooms (so it's not a problem per se) it's quite annoying when you're waiting to meet someone or for your car to arrive. It doesn't seem to fit the brand of the hotel, so I found it a little cognitively dissonant. But that's a minor comment that should be taken in the context of what was a really comfortable and enjoyable stay. I'll be back!

name: Hotel Indigo New York City, Chelsea
title: “Fine Hotel--Sparkling New”
text:
A warm welcome from each staff member, made staying at the small new hotel very pleasant. It is located a few blocks from Penn Station and this facilitates transportation to and from JFK and EWR and within the city.
The rooms are attractively decorated and functional. The restaurant is excellent by hotel standards.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Excellent location and good sized accommodations”
text: Had a four night stay here and all in all it was very enjoyable. Quite spacious rooms with two queen beds, kitchenette with fridge which is a plus (but with four people we had only cups, bowls etc for three!, also there was a stove but absolutely no pots, pans, microwave reheating dishes etc.) We also had a sofa bed which gave our teenaged daughter her own bed. They have a pillow menu (which excited aforementioned teenager) plus offered walking tours of New York on ipod for free - a good bonus for those that want to DIY. Across from Madison Square Gardens, a short stroll to the subway & Penn Station & very close walk to largest department store in the world (Macys), also close walk to Empire State Bldg and not too far from Times Square. Also a plus is the hotel is in a police precinct and next door to a fire station and while sirens make up the New York sound scene they arent too obtrusive thru the night - it just makes for a safer area to be in. Would thoroughly recommend if you can get a good deal

name: BEST WESTERN Bowery Hanbee Hotel
title: “très bon rapport qualité/prix”
text:
nous avons séjourné une semaine dans cet hotel et nous sommes ravis ! 
Hotel proche d'une station de métro et à 30 min à pied du mémorial 9/11 .
Quartier Chinatown est très dépaysant ( on a vraiment l'impression d'être en Chine !! .... et les odeurs d'échoppes de poissons avec lol)
Personnels sympas et polis.
Chambre et salle de bain propre et surtout pas de punaises de lit car nous avions eu quelques appréhensions avant notre départ et nous étions soulagés quand on a inspecté notre chambre en voyant que tout était super clean . 
Buffet petit déjeuné simple mais bien fourni . 
Juste le wifi qui avait quelques soucis pendant 2 jours mais les ordinateurs de l'hotel étaient disponibles à tout moment .
J'y retournerai avec plaisir .

name: Wingate by Wyndham Manhattan Midtown
title: “Comfortable, friendly, but beware of overbookings!”
text: We had a very comfortable stay here. The room was spacious (by NYC standards), clean and very quiet. The staff (front desk and housekeeping) was beyond friendly (smiles, eye contact and seemingly genuine interest in being helpful). It was nice to have the complimentary breakfast, but the food was nothing to write home about. But, hey, it was free and when you're in New York, free anything is great! We were on the backside of the hotel and it was very quiet. This place appears to have really good soundproofing between the rooms and floors as we never heard a peep from anyone, even though the hotel was full. We did, however, have virtually no cell phone signal in our room and had to head down to the lounge on the second floor to make any phone calls. No big deal, especially because local phone calls were free. One recommendation, though. Try to arrive earlier in the day as the hotel was oversold on the night we arrived. Perhaps this was a fluke, but it'd be a pain to travel all day and find yourself without a hotel room.. We got the last room. I felt bad for the 3 parties that were just arriving as we were getting into the elevator. Also, there aren't a lot of restaurants near the hotel serving dinner after 10:00 pm. We had quite a long walk trying to find a place open for business the night we arrived. However, the location is great as far as convenience to the subway, etc. Nice hotel!

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Ruhepunkt in der Großstadthektik”
text:
Wir sind mit unseren Enkelkindern weiblich 15 und 17 Jahre alt auf USA Reise gewesen. Unser erster Stop waren 5 Nächte in New York und hier im Sofitel. Die Zimmer waren sehr geräumig und sauber und ruhig. Täglich wurde auch Wasser kostenlos für die Nacht bereitgestellt. Da das Hotel ziemlich neu ist lief auch die Klimaanlage komfortabel leise. Die Nähe zum Times-Square und anderen Atrltionen war sehr angenehm bei den teilweise unangenehmen Sommertemperaturen. Wir haben den City-Pass leider nicht voll nutzen können, da die Jugend an vielen Atraktionen nicht interessiert war. Für uns war das kein Abbruch, da wir schon mehrmals in New York waren.
Das Hotel ist zu empfehlen, wenn man das Geld ausgeben will.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “New Yorker : un camp de base idéal à Manhattan”
text:
Pour notre première expérience à New York, l'hôtel New Yorker a été parfait.
Pour un prix tout à fait raisonable, nous avions une petite suite confortable et bien entretenu au 22ème étage avec une vue fort sympathique.
Et au niveau de la localisation : le top. A côté du Madison Square Garden pour les amoureux du Basket et à moins de 10 minutes à pied de Time Square et de l'Empire State Building. A côte dumétro pour tout le reste et idéal par rapport aux aéroports de Newark (par le NJ transit à Penn Station) et JFK (MTA ligne 2 et 3).

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “If you're not in your room a lot, it's just fine”
text:
I've read the other reviews here. I must agree, the hotel needs a make-over but it was just fine for a girl-friends getaway as we planned to shop, take in theatre, and be in the room pretty much only to sleep and cook breakfast. Having the kitchen was a plus for us as we slept in late, and were still able to grab our eggs and toast in the room at our leisure.
Our room had two bathrooms which was great for us too. I'd go somewhere else with my husband though....because the hotel is tired.

name: Hotel Indigo New York City, Chelsea
title: “non cercherei altro hotel”
text: è la seconda volta che alloggio in questo hotel e trovo che sia proprio al caso mio. zona centralissima ma lo stesso tempo per nulla rumorosa . camere deliziose e letti comodissimi. ci sono fermate della metro a meno di 1 minuto a piedi e mille locali dove poter cenare o o dare colazione. il personale dell'hotel è di una gentilezza quasi disarmante. se dovessi tornare ancora non ne proverei un altro questo lo trovo sotto tutti punti perfetto e lo consiglio vivamente.

name: Hotel Mela
title: “Small Wonder”
text: Although the rooms are small, the hotel is nice and is in a great location. We were even able to find parking on the street right in front of the hotel!

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Great hotel!”
text:
We were here the week of 12/25 - 12/30/04. Very crowded in the city due to the holiday. This was an excellent hotel to stay at. We had the one bedroom suite which worked out terrific with the kids - they had their spot, we had ours. The kitchenette/dishware was very convenient as we ate in a bit due to the weather (17 degrees!). The rooms are not large (remember this is New York!!) and not new, however they were very clean and well kept.
The location was IDEAL!! Close to Grand Central (about 5 blocks) and it was residential so very quiet, there is a D'Agostino's market right around the corner if you need anything.
The staff was VERY accomodating and pleasant, the bellman were great! The restaurant on site is "OK" however very economical for breakfast as they serve a buffet breakfast. Plan an average of about $50/meal for 3 people when you are in the city.
Needless to stay...this will be our Hotel anytime we come to the city. You will not be disappointed :)

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Some good, some bad and some ugly...”
text:
First the Good:
Prime location on 57th by 7th Ave in Central Park South (right across from Carnegie Hall). Large rooms (really large if you get the suite with two beds and adjoining living room) and the price is very good for Mid-town New York.
Now the bad:
Really no amenities at this property have to go to lobby to go up secondary flight of stairs to get ice. Two old very SLOW elevators. No restaurant, gym or other things you might expect in a hotel. TOO hot. While we were there in Feb. it was over 80 degrees and we had to run window a.c. the entire time we were there as even with heat shut off in room the hotel was just too hot. Internet is $10 for 30 minutes and they even charge this if all you want to do is print out your boarding pass in the lobby using their p.c. Breakfast (continental) is $9 on the 3rd floor daily. Plenty of local deli’s with better selection and as cheap with better food a few doors away.
The Ugly:
The hotel used to be residences (not sure how but so I am told). This meant larger spaces but it has not been updated in 30 years. Peeling paint, low light and just a general feel of old and worn. Carpet looks dirty and old.
Having said this this if you get a really good deal and are willing to deal with the 2 star nature of the hotel then perhaps it is for you. It’s a balancing act but one you should know what you are getting into before you book.

name: On The Ave Hotel
title: “Excellent séjour”
text: Hôtel d'excellente qualité, très bien situé, quartier agréable, supermarchés à proximité, métro à deux rues, très bon service, calme. Même si vous passerez certainement votre temps à visiter NYC, il est appréciable de trouver une chambre confortable au retour d'une journée de marche. J'y ai passé un excellent séjour.

name: Hotel Mela
title: “Great location to explore Manhattan”
text:
The Hotel Mela is in a great spot on 44th St between Broadway and 6th Avenue making it a perfect central location to explore midtown, with great links to the Upper East Side, Upper West Side and Lower Manhattan.
Despite being so close to Times Square, and being in a room fronting onto the road, we found the room relatively quiet. Whilst the street noise could be heard with the window closed, it certainly wasn't enough to disturb our sleep, and if anything for us it enhanced the experience! We didn't go to NYC for a quite holiday, and enjoyed the reminder of what was going on just outside our room.
For our 4 night stay we opted for a Deluxe room and were pleasantly surprised by the amount of space in this city centre location. The room was well furnished, clean, and comfortable and the bathroom was pleasant and bright.
The staff were very friendly and were keen to offer help wherever appropriate.
We didn't make use of the fitness centre - we did too much walking to fancy doing that - but we did make use of the free option to check in and print our boarding passes for the return flight.
This was a great holiday and hotel. We would definitely recommend it and are already thinking about booking again for our next trip to New York (although we just got home today!)

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Gutes Preis-Leistungsverhältnis für Hotel in Top-Lage”
text: Freundlicher Empfang, sofortige Erledigung des Check-ins, keine Wartezeiten, Hotelhalle sehr ansprechend, Personal hilfsbereit, Zimmer - unseres war sehr klein, aber sauber. Preis-Leistungsverhältnis ok. Essen im Tick-Rock-Diner war nicht so toll, aber die hauseigene "Cooper´s Tavern" ist zu empfehlen, Cesar´s Salad sehr gut. Lage des Hotels ist optimal, sehr nahe beim Empire State, Times Square, Macy´s, und aller U-Bahnen und Busstationen. Immer wieder gerne ins New Yorker!

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Good Location”
text:
I rated this hotel with 4 stars because it's an average of the 3 I would give it if we had paid full price and the 5 I would give it for the $82 we paid on Hotwire. As many of the reviews have stated, it is in a great location. Many, many attractions are within walking distance. There is also a good Italian restaurant and nice deli next door. We did not try the $9 breakfast because there are so many other places to eat within a few blocks and wanted to try these, but many of the other guests were eating at the hotel. 
The downside to this hotel is that it is very old and needs some TLC. The heat in the rooms is hot water heat controlled with a handle on the heater. Our handle was broken. We finally figured it out on the last night, but until then, it was so hot we finally had to turn on the air conditioner. One night, during a snowstorm, we slept with the window completely open, but it was still hot. We reported the problem twice, but no one looked at it. The shower certainly woke you up in the morning for, within seconds, it could go from just right to burning to ice cold.
On the up side, the rooms are very spacious with a microwave, refrig, sink and coffeemaker. There are 2 good sized closets and lots of room in the sleeping area. The rooms were spotless and VERY quiet. We were right next to the elevator and the hotel was full, but we never heard it. We are also extremely light sleepers who never travel without earplugs, but we didn't have to use them.
The bottom line is if you can get this hotel for a discounted price, jump at it. I think I would have been disappointed if we had paid top dollar.

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Good Hotel - Good Deal”
text:
After all the horror reviews I read on this website about the cheaper hotels, I decided to spend some peace of mind money and spend a little more.
