I got a deal for the Shelburne Suite Hotel through Expedia for $125 a night. I was glad that I picked this hotel, as it was a very nice hotel, the suites were spacious and the staff very friendly. I checked in very late, and was accidentally given a smoker room, however I would have never noticed it, if I did not see the ash trays the next morning. So I actually decided to stay in the room, as there was absolutely no smell. The kitchen and the bathroom both were spotless and the room service was good as well. If you stay with two people in this room, it is a very good deal. It is located in Murray Hill, a very nice neighborhood not too far from the Chrysler Building. I definitely did not have to worry in this hotel about my valuables or anything. 
Definitely a good deal.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Hôtel Sofitel à New York”
text:
Hôtel de luxe avec un excellent placement géographique , juste à côté de la 5 eme rue , du MOMA , Saint Patrick , Central Park et bien d"autres lieux incontournables ..
Il bénéficie d'un restaurant bar fort agréable .
Service et confort incontestable et un personnel attentionné qui dans la mesure du possible s"exprimera dans votre langue .
Avons été complètement satisfait par cet hôtel .

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Prime Location and a nice hotel”
text:
If you are looking to be in the Times Square / Theater District area of Manhattan, this hotel is a great choice as it is located at 43rd Street & 8th Avenue. Used SPG points so great deal.
The hotel, as most Westins, is very nice. The second floor lobby is big with a bar and restaurant near the 8th avenue side and comfortable seating near the reception area. The service was wonderful throughout the hotel. 
The rooms are a decent size for a big city. The beds were comfortable and the room was clean. A few hiccups: the water in the shower was hard to regulate, the safe kept getting stuck and the TV remote was hard to work. But all fairly minor. 
We did not eat in the hotel. Brought the kids to the Hard Rock Cafe (one block away ), we ate at Shun Lee West (upscale, very good Chinese by Lincoln Center) and we all ate at Tramonti (overpriced Italian but on Restaurant Row). Had coffee at Tom's Restaurant (used for Seinfeld show) up around 112th Street & Broadway (fun). 
Drinks at the Westin bar were expensive (but what you would expect) so we passed. For a few dollars more ($9 for a beer, $19 for a martini) we had drinks at the Mandarin Oriental Lobby Lounge in Columbus Circle. It is on the 35th floor & great views of Central Park and NYC. I can actually say, it was worth the price. Less expensive drinks were had at Smith's just a few blocks away.
Added benefit - the Tampa Rays were staying here and ran into Evan Longoria & Johnny Damon. Overall, an excellent option for midtown Manhattan with the family.

name: Ace Hotel NYC
title: “Hipster central - could be good or bad for you!”
text:
I stayed at the Ace for a week while in town on business. I'm in the design industry and in town frequently, so it seemed an appropriate change of pace from some of the more corporate hotels I have stayed in. They have a well-thought out aesthetic -- kind of a grunge version of a W Hotel with black/white/grey palette and somewhat trite rock 'n roll details (like guitars and ATA cases in the rooms). The lobby bar (with DJs and bands most nights) and the Breslin restaurant are hugely popular and keep the public spaces filled with 20-35 year olds out for a night on the town. The lobby bar cocktails are excellent. If this is what you're looking for in your NYC hotel, it's perfect -- go for it.
Personally, I prefer to go out for my entertainment and come back to my hotel to sleep. It was fine for a couple of days, but the music coming up the elevator shaft, the crush in the lobby, and people wandering around the upstairs hallways smoking and shouting got a bit old by the end of my stay. It's like a very expensive, high-design youth hostel. Super comfortable beds, though. 
The John Dory Oyster Bar and the No. 7 Sub Shop (both on the hotel's ground floor) were much better than the Breslin which seems vastly overrated based on style points alone.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Get a back room...but nice spot to stay”
text: I could not have asked for a nicer spot to stay. The price for a suite was excellent for Midtown, the service polite, and the room clean. If you want a fancy bathroom, forget it, but it was clean and in good order. The rest of the room was simply decorated and BIG. We appreciated the mini-fridge. Take note that the ice machine is down on the 1st floor, and staying high up is good to mute the traffic noise. I would, however, ask for a room not facing the street, if you sleep after 7am or plan an afternoon nap. We did not, so the pounding from the construction site across the street was no problem at all. Would certainly stay again.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “We Loved the Affinia Manhattan”
text:
Can not disagree more with the last person to write a review.
If you want 5 * Book the Plaza and pay a couple of grand a night. If you want the best you can get for the money you have, you cannot go wrong with the affinia Manhattan.
The hotel was lovely. We stayed in a one bedroom suite and it was huge. A little well lived in but spotlessly clean and fit all our requirements. You are so busy with things to do in NY all you want is a comfy bed and the affinia Manhattan certainly had that. 
My husband requested a top floor room with a view of the empire state building. The staff bent over backwards to accommodate our requests and where extremely helpful and friendly. They gave us fantastic advice on places to visits, gave us maps and directions on how to get there. We had a number of excursions we pre booked here in the UK and the staff phoned them all on arrival to re confirm our booking.
The location was very good. We walked everywhere. Took about 20 min to get to time square but it was a lovely walk and we did it daily.
I have recommended the affinia to my in laws and they are staying there later this year. With any luck I will stay there again next year

name: 70 park avenue hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Looking forward to staying here for our wedding weekend!”
text: I'm a big fan of kimpton so when we were planning our destination wedding in NYC this summer we booked 70 Park Ave hotel for our entire wedding party the weekend of july 28th Went on to Facebook to find the secret word for July in hopes of possibly getting an upgrade so we have some more room to hang out with our guests throughout the weekend and within minutes of my posting I had a reply from kimpton saying they would see what they could do. So impressive and the very reason we always stay at kimpton hotels. Whether we get the upgrade or not I appreciate their effort and prompt response!

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites New York Manhattan/Chelsea
title: “Personallized service makes the difference”
text: Our family stayed at the Fairfield based on Rewards membership and its close location to Penn station. We found it also convieniently close to subway line and many family-friendly restaurants. Although the rooms are smallish (welcome to NYC) the main difference was the staff. Without asking the staff went out of their way to help us and accomodate our "tweens" who were just beginning to behave as adults. A view of Empire State building from the room and terrace was really nice. Hotel was very clean and well stocked. Breakfast / lounge area is bright and cheerful. Coffee / tea / hot chocolate was always available as were other munchies from time to time. Staff was will to provide advice for dinners, shopping and sights. Would stay again.

name: 70 park avenue hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Awesome”
text: We loved 70 Park Ave. Our King Premier room was spacious & most of all super clean. The staff were all very friendly. The wine sampling at 5 PM is such a nice touch as well as the complimentary lemon/orange water that is always available in the lobby. The area is perfect & we would highly recommend this hote.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Amazing Stay- Great Getaway!!! 10+++++”
text:
Upon my retuning stay at the Westin Times square I wasn’t shocked to find the same AMAZING quality and service. The room was absolutely amazing and the service was impeccable. The hotel staff was exceptionally kind and helpful. I couldn’t have asked for a better experience. This hotel is very accessible to all restaurants, shops and theaters. I would defiantly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for 10 star quality and service. My next stay in NYC will defiantly be spent at this hotel. Thanks everyone for a wonderful experience.
Dean

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Gutes und relativ ruhiges Hotel in zentraler Lage”
text: Das Hotel Affinia Shelburne liegt zentral in Manhatten, wenige Minuten zu Fuß vom Empire State Building und der Grand Central Station entfernt. Auch zur Fifth Avenue und zum Times Square sind es nur etwa 20 Gehminuten. Das Personal war - bis auf eine Ausnahme - freundlich und hilfsbereit, das Hotel ist sauber, das Zimmer war ausreichend geräumig, gut ausgestattet und ebenfalls sauber. Für die recht zentrale Lage war das Zimmer überraschend leise. Von der Dachterrasse hat man einen schönen Blick.

name: BEST WESTERN Bowery Hanbee Hotel
title: “Pas très cher pour New York”
text: Chambre pas immense (quand on est 4) et sans trop de rangements mais impeccable. Dommage qu'il n'y ait pas de frigo. Quartier assez bruyant (Chinatown) mais fenêtres fermées ça va. Pas très cher pour NYC (par hotels.com). Bien desservi par le métro. Petit déjeuner continental correct dans une salle un peu trop petite pour l'affluence. 5 $ facturés par bagage pour faire garder ses valises pendant la journée après le check-out.

name: The Belvedere
title: “davvero bello”
text:
la posizione era davvero perfetta, in 5 minuti a piedi arrivavamo al rockfeller center, in 10 a central park (dal columbus circle) e in 15 all'empire state building, la metro era a due isolati e la linea che prendevamo era comodissima.
la nostra camera e quella dei nostri amici (cn un letto matrimoniale) era molto spaziosa (quasi 30mq.. più unica che rara), sempre pulita e, in più, avendo la fortuna di essere al 15° piano, anche una vista fantastica, che ha superato di molto le nostre aspettative!!
la concierge è sempre stata gentilissima, ci hanno prenotato di tutto, dallo spettacolo a broadway al ristorante..
un po' caro soltanto il servizio internet, la colazione non l'abbiamo mai provata perché a pochi metri abbiamo trovato un self service molto carino (e con un ottimo cappuccino italiano!) e starbucks uno dietro l'altro..
ci tornerei domani!! bellissimo!!

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “loved affinia”
text: It is a fantastic location and a superb clean room. Very large. Staff are very friendly too.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Good location, bad rooms”
text: The location was excellent, one block from Time Square and we did not hear any noise at night. We were not impressed with the room. The rooms walls were dirty, the sheets were stained, the bed ruffel was VERY dirty and disgusting. The outlet in the bathroom did not work so we had to blow dry our hair in the bedroom. Also the half the blinds were missing so it was a bit bright in the mornings. I also ordered a birthday cake for my boyfriend, it was $70, and not worth the cost. $70 for a cake to feed 4 is outrageous. They didn't even write happy birthday on it like I requested. I have had a lot better cakes for a lot less money. Bottom line is great location with amazing views but needs to be updated.

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
title: “5 Sterne Hotel etwas billiger in New York”
text:
Den zweiten Teil unserer New York Reise verbrachten wir in diesem IC Hotel.
Der Preis ist ca 50% geringer als im Intercontinental Times Square, allerdings ist das Hotel auch nicht ganz so schön.
Man merkt an allen Ecken und Kanten, das es schon etwas in die Jahre gekommen ist.
Das Badezimmer ist klein und alt und würe mehr in ein 2-3 Sterne Hotel passen.
Das Zimmer was wir bekommen haben (Upgrade auf Executivezimmer als Platinumambassador) war sehr schön und für New Yorker Verhältnisse sehr groß.
Leider war auch hier keine Nespressomaschine im Zimmer vorhanden.
Auch in diesem Hotel ist das Frühstück stark überteuert.
Lage ist gut...5 Minuten vom Grand Central entfernt...

name: Hotel Plaza Athenee New York
title: “Classic Upper East Side Hotel”
text: Is this the hippest hotel in NYC? No, but it is a lovely little place in a great location on the Upper East Side. The lobby is not large, but very pretty with marble floors and painted murals. There is a dark and cozy Moorish style bar on the main floor which made an excellent "Vesper Lind" martini and served cheese straws, almonds & truffle popcorn in pretty silver bowls. I could hang out in there for quite awhile. We did not eat at the restaurant. Guest rooms were large for New York with a very quiet and comfortable with fluffy white bedding, king-sized bed, flat screen TV, blackout shades, mini-bar, desk, etc. One wall is devoted to 3 reach-in closets which also holds the mini-bar and safe. While the style of the room might be a bit of a throwback (golds and burgundy), everything was clean and luxurious. No complaints. Housekeeping was great and we never had to ask for a thing. Penhaligon's toiletries were a nice touch. The marble bathroom was large with separate rain shower and soaking tub. The staff was also very friendly. The best thing about this hotel was the location--a block from the action of Madison Avenue without the maddening crowds. We really enjoyed our stay.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Great hotel, loved it, can't wait to come back”
text: My wife and I just celebrated our 10 yr. anniversary in New York City. We could not have picked a better place to stay. Super convienent to Times Square and the Theater District. Subway station accross the street means quick access to everything away from Times Square. Our room was suprisingly big for New York. It was very clean. The staff was very helpful directing us to different attractions. We had a great time and having a great place to stay just added to the experience.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Good Hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Affinia Manatttan from 29th August - 2nd September, 2008. 
Although the hotel was obvsiously built many years ago, the rooms are light and airy. We had a large suite on the 11th floor. The room was spotlessly clean, and our only criticism was that the shower in the bathroom was very small, and considering the size of the suite it certainly could have been bigger without losing much space. The only other drawback was that the room was noisy due to the fire station along the road and lorries collecting the garbage in the middle of the night, plus the general hustle and bustle of New York, so we were not able to get a peaceful night's sleep. 
All of the staff were very friendly, and both the reception ladies and gentelmen were charming and attentive, and also responded to any requests efficiently. The Concierege staff were also exceedingly helpful, and the doormen and chambermaids were cheerful and obliging.
All in all we were delighted with our stay at the hotel. It was our third time in New York, and each time we have stayed at a different hotel, not by choice necessarily but because of the offers available. On the second occasion we stayed at The Astoria, and both my husband and I feel that the Affinia Manhattan was superior in each department.
Thank you guys.
Juliette and Gerald Bougourd.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Great Hotel”
text: We only had one night at this hotel on our way back to UK, but it was excellent, I got a very good price for a Sunday night ($176 inc tax) very clean and spacious, excellent location, only negative comment would be that the bathroom in our studio suite was miniscule, we are both fairly small, but hit the wall when showering! But that did not detract from lovely room and kitchenette, wish we could have stayed longer.

name: Hotel Plaza Athenee New York
title: “Absolutely delightful!”
text:
I stayed here for the first time back in March and cannot wait to go back! My room was lovely and the staff treated me like a queen. On my last night I was having a drink at the bar and heading out to meet friends somewhere on the opposite end of town I had never been--the bartender went above and beyond to make sure I'd get there using quickest route possible on the subway (and this was AFTER I had paid the bill and tipped her so she just as easily could have said "go talk to the concierge").
My room was very cozy, had all the amenities and was even a decent size for NYC. The gym spacious and very clean-- it's the best I've ever seen at a hotel of that size. My room service breakfast was a little pricey ($50 for just myself) but other than that this place is worth every penny.

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Wir wären gerne noch geblieben!”
text:
Ich kann das Hotel mit gutem Gewissen weiterempfehlen. Wir hatten ein sehr geräumiges, schönes Zimmer und der Service ging sehr freundlich auf alle Wünsche ein.
Das Highlight war die Roof- Top Bar mit Blick auf Manhattan bei Nacht!

name: The Plaza Hotel
title: “Excellent Lobby ~ Fantastic Location”
text:
Popped in for a look during a morning walk.
Spent about 10-15 minutes admiring the lobby etc.
Security and other staff on duty. 
Preparations under way for breakfast.
Most impressed with the decor.
Remember to say "G'day" to the staff.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “5 night stay in NYC!”
text:
Me and my family stayed in the Crowne Plaza back in October for 5 nights. We found the hotel location perfect for tourist attractions as it was right on Times Square and right beside Broadway! The rooms were clean but were quite small. We paid extra to be on the concierge floor and I would recommend doing this. We had a good view onto some of New York's skyline and had access to breakfast in the lounge with a continental breakfast selection. The wifi in the room was also free but we were disappointed that it didn't work down in the bar.
Overall a great hotel for a short stay trip in the big apple!!

name: 70 park avenue hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Would definitely go back”
text:
We stayed at 70 Park in December. Just down the street from Grand Central Station. I liked being a little away from the hustle bustle but close enough for those who like to walk. The room was small but very comfortable. It had a very nice ambiance. I would have been happy with a few less mirrors but I understand it's meant to make the room feel larger.
I also enjoyed the evening wine hour.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Fantastic”
text:
What can i say about this hotel? Loved every minute of the stay.
To fill you in, i looked at reviews on this website to determine where to stay and booked through ebookers. Just over £600 flight and hotel each, which i thought was very reasonable.
As a result of taking advise from this site, when i booked i emailed the hotel and corresponded with Johanna Lopez. She was fantastic. I gave her details of my visit and requested to be high up in the hotel, re the noise, which is no where near as bad as wht the reviews say. It's a city centre hotel for god's sake. Loudest things you hear are the fire engines using the sirens that sound like the creatures vehicle in "jeepers creepers". Anyway not only did we stay on the 23rd floor of 28, but she upgraded us to a one bed apartment. The place was huge and had two bathrooms, bedroom, which the best bed in the world ever. so comfortable, living room and kitchen. There was a walk in ardrobe and two further large storage areas. I couldn't recommend this place enough. Central to everything and all staff helpful. Tip- Go to Woodbury Common, Oakley jeans £5, well they were in the sale. In all i spent £700 at the place and had to buy further case to bring back. But Delta allow you to take two bags, so it didn't cost me anymore. Clothes bought for the year.
Any questions email me.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “CROWNE PLAZA TIMES SQUARE NEW YORK”
text:
This was my first trip to New York and the location of this hotel helped greatly with the overall experience of this fabulous city. You step out of the main entrance and directly into times square.
There were four in our party so we had requested adjoining rooms and both of the rooms were very large with huge comfortable beds, Large bathroom with full bath, shower and washing facilities.
The staff were all polite and helpful in every way.
I would highly recommend staying here if comfort & a great central location are high on your list.

name: Ace Hotel NYC
title: “A m a z i n g!”
text:
You'll find the hotel at 23th Street/Broadway. The whole Hotel is so stylish! You've to see it, even if you don't want to check in. The walls are black, with few exceptions, and the rooms are soooooo cool! Black Walls, except that one behind the bed. On this wall, there are sites out of a old encyclopedia. In my room (904, very cosy!) I had the letters C to D. The minibar is a minicontainer, very good filled. You also have a hooded bath robe and a ironing board that reads: "You sure would look better pressed". The beds are very comfortable, I'd like to have the mattresses at home :). You also got a TV, a radio with alarm, a blower. In the bathroom (superclean!) you got the usual towels and also a little "beauty"-set. It contains cotton, a little nail care set a towel to brighten your shoes (O.o?). So much about the room. The staff is very friendly and helpfull in all cases. The Food is also good, but we've to wait a bit long...But thats a drop in the bucket!
It was a m a z i n g, and I'm sad to say, I stayed there only for one night. If I ever go back to New York I'll reside there! My room cots almost 200 Dollars a night, but I had a free bed. If you go with your best friend, it's not so expensive.
All in all: They can be highly recommended!

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Diffident staff and poor value for money”
text: Stayed here for 6 sad nights whilst in NY on business. Booked concierge room category assuming the rate would offer value for money! Bad Move. the breakfast was pathetically small and offered no normal options such as capuccino etc- I had thought the " canapes" would include, like comparable rooms at other Crowne Plaza's, druinks - wrong again. waited 30 minutes for porter on day of departure and then was expected to tip him ( even though he delayed us !) as well as the doorman and the extra guy who pushed the luggage trolley. Clearly the occupancy rate due to location has made this a tired and unfriendly place. Location is OK but forget the rest and look at otehr , more friendly options!

name: Ace Hotel NYC
title: “Awesome Hotel!!”
text: Everything was great about the hotel except room temperature...it was too hot! The staff was wonderful. We got an upgrade when we arrived. True the rooms are dark but we didn't mind. Loved the decor and design. It was a great value for $199 a night. I've stayed in dozens of NY hotels but Ace is now my favorite hotel in New York.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Explore NYC from the Perfect Position”
text:
While this hotel is a little expensive it is the perfect place from which to launch your exploration of Manhattan and NYC.
It is centrally located with Times Square right outside your door. There is easy access to taxis, buses and the subway. Central Park, 5th Avenue and other tourist spots are all within easy walking distance.
The staff are very friendly and helpful. Susana was wonderful helping me sort out some travel problems and gave us excellent service and advice about the hotel and its facilities.
I recommend this hotel to anyone intending to holiday on Manhattan Island.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “The perfect NYC base”
text:
Great room, great people.
Breakfast was truly aweful but everything else more than made up for it and at $6 it was hardly a surprise...
Our room was huge with a fridge, microwave and complimentary coffee machine. With 2 great TVs and very good furnishings the housekeeping was excellent.
Our previous visit to NY included a hotel with more stars and costing twice as much, our next one will be at the Salisbury again.

name: Hotel Mela
title: “A Nice Find”
text:
My partner and I recently traveled to NY. During a casual conversation with a friend who visits NY often he mentioned Hotel Mela. So I immediately came to TripAdvisor to get some reviews. i booked several hotels and in the end decided to stay at Hotel Mela.
We arrived late Friday afternoon and were greeted by a courteous staff. We were a little concerned about the location since we did NOT want to be in Times Square. The hotel web site was accurate in saying they were a block or two away from Times Squre.
Knowing that several folks had suggested I get a high floor room we asked for a higher floor after initially being given the 10th floor. We ended up with a room on the 16th floor. Wanted to make certain we avoided any street noise.
The room was very nicely appointed. We booked the Executive Junior Suite. I wished I had looked at the Executive King since someone from the hotel mentioned he preferred the Executive King. Both had the same rate.
It was hot in NY that weekend and our AC worked beautifully. Nice flat panel TV was also in the room. Pretty decent closet space.
My one small gripe was the small bathroom. While it was very clean it was just small. We could never be in the bathroom at the same time and had to alternate using the sink and mirror. On the plus side the shower did have a window that allowed bright sunlight to come in. Of course folks on the outside could not see in.
The conceirge was amazing. We often asked them to assist us with the address of a restaurnat for which we could not remember the name of the restaurant. Only the general street location. They also gave us great tips on where we should go to watch the PRIDE parade. Housekeeping was very good. We never saw them but the room was always cleaned. Turn Down service was cute.
I would definitley stay here again. If you book on Mela's web site you might want to recheck rates periodically. I did this often and saw their rates flucuate....but not always UP as your visit date got closer. By checking in regularly I was able to LOWER our rates. 
The restaurant next door had just opened. They bill themselves as a Vietnamese French restaurant. Food was amazing. 
Be sure to include this hotel on your list.

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Recomondable para familias, amigos y parejas”
text:
Buena opción para todo tipo de viajes. Muy bien ubicado, nuevo, moderno, limpio y lindo.
La atención no es lo mejor que tiene.

name: Hotel Mela
title: “Yes, small rooms...but great location, helpful staff, nice furnishings”
text:
Ninety percent of NYC hotel rooms are tiny. That's just the way it is. So don't be shocked by the Mela's postage-stamp sized accomodations. They are nicely appointed, fairly clean, and convenient to Times Square and many other NYC landmarks. The staff was very courteous and helpful. 
My only quibble is that the Mela touts itself as a 4 star hotel. 
Sorry, it is 3 star at best.
The Mela lacks many amenities that you would expect in a 4 star "boutique" hotel -- no restaurant, no spacious lobby or lounge, and a tiny workout room. The Mela is a "boutique" hotel in the sense that it provides small, well appointed rooms. There really is no lobby -- there is a checkin desk, and a central cushioned "sofa" wrapped around a support pillar, but there is no room to sit in the lobby, read a newspaper, or meet and chat with friends/other travelers.
Still, if you can get a room at a good rate (I booked for $189/night for late March), this is a great deal. If you get above $300/night, however...I suggest shopping around a bit.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “OK but thats it!”
text:
Just so we are clear I am very selective when I travel which happens on several occasions per month for business...when travelling with family I always seem to be a little less accepting of a semi clean room and kinda ok service!
Rooms was about a 6 1/2 out of 10...was cleaned but could really use a MAJOR CLEANUP...dirty under the beds and dresser, behind the TV etc...Staff was OK but not overly pleasant...if I did decide to stay there again it would be based solely on location and not for a clean or amazing hotel experience..little dissapointed with this property!

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “A GREAT HOTEL TO STAY IN NYC”
text: The hotel is easily accessible by subway and is in the heart of the city. accomodations could not have been better. The room was exceptionally clean. The bed was more than comfortable. The staff treats you like family.;

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “Spacious and clean”
text: Good location, near the famous shops and central park. They have large rooms, good for families. I think all of their rooms have double beds. You have to pay for Internet. We had zero view. The room and the bathroom was clean. The bathroom has a bathtub.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Great Value for NYC!!”
text: The Salisbury is in a great location within the city!! Its clean, the staff is friendly and helpful. The hotel is an older building with basic features, but the room was much larger than I expected. If I got back to NYC I will certainly considering staying at the Salisbury again.

name: 70 park avenue hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Overpriced! Not worth it. Website has false information.”
text:
I arrived into New York City very late one night and hadn't eaten dinner. The website for this hotel very clearly stated "24 hour room service" but when I couldn't reach room service, the front desk told me that they stop room service at 10 pm. What???!! 10 pm on a Saturday in New York City? Are you kidding me? 
They offered to send someone up with delivery menus, and 20 minutes later someone showed up with pizza menus. By the time I ate, it was near midnight.
They make a big deal over how they have coffee and tea in the morning. It starts at 8 am - I needed to be at my meeting by 7 am. Of course there is no coffee maker in the room so I had to go without coffee in the morning.
This hotel is totally not worth it. I will never stay here again.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Great stay, great rooms”
text:
We booked the hotel through our travel agent, but the price was great compared to other hotels in Times Square.
A great hotel, its clean and comfortable. The chambermaids had the room spotless each day. A big thanks to Eric who was exceptionally helpful when we checked in and showed us the bits and bobs in the room. I would also like to give my thanks to Sandra ESP who was very nice when we checked out.
I was very impressed with the free internet use to check out and print our boarding pass.
I did however find the price of wifi extoronate $9.99 for four hours when you can walk round the corner to starbucks and get it for free. I appreciate that this hotel also caters for business, but considering we had come from the UK, maybe an hours free use just so you can email/skype home that you got there okay would have been a nice touch.

name: Hampton Inn New York Seaport / Financial District
title: “Wow, what a find!”
text:
I had a great experience staying at the Hampton Inn at the Seaport last weekend. I've never stayed there before and was looking for something inexpensive. What a find! Clean beautiful room, located close to the subway (a few blocks away on Fulton) and what service. The bellman was so friendly and Berkis and Carmen, two women who worked at the front desk, could not have been nicer. They remembered my name and addressed me each time I came and went. Believe it or not, the service was similar to that I have received at the Four Seasons Philadelphia and the JW Marriott Cancun. Amazing and all for $199.00. Who knew! 
Keep up the good work! We look forward to staying again in the near future.

name: Hotel Mela
title: “ottima posizione in Times Square”
text: Io amo New York, per cui sono felice solo per il fatto di andarci. Stavolta è stata la tappa conclusiva del nostro viaggio di nozze. L'hotel è in ottima posizione, sulla 44ma strada, vicinissimo a Times Square, da cui passano varie linee della metro. Ma è anche molto comodo se si vuole girare a piedi facendo lunghe camminate. Le camere sono piccole, ma pulite. Il personale è molto gentile e c'è il wifi gratuito sia in camera che nella hall. Lo consiglio.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Lovely hotel in great location”
text: Stayed here for 5 nights with family between 4 rooms. All rooms were spacious, clean and modern. 2 of the rooms including my own were wheelchair-friendly. My room was huge with a window that spanned the length of the room. Maid service was daily. Excellent disabled bathroom with walk-in shower but it could have done with extra grab rails by the toilet. Comfy king size beds with ample pillows and bedding. Very good air-conditioning system which could be turned up high or low or turned off completely. Large television, cordless telephone, mini bar, safe and hairdryer were provided. Starbucks coffee sachets are provided which are made using a coffee machine but you don't get a kettle. The views from the rooms were nothing special but the windows opened if needed and noise from the streets was minimal. Very large lobby with plenty of seating areas and the lifts never took very long to arrive. Excellent location on Times Square but not in the middle of the noise and bright lights. Within walking distance of most places, bars and restaurants etc. I would definitely recommend this hotel to others!

name: 70 park avenue hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Can't beat the service here!”
text: We spent 4 nights at this boutique hotel. They were very friendly, helpful and even hosted a happy hour with free wine nightly from 5:00-6:00. The location is great for shopping, dining and other activities. Very comfortable beds, great TV too.

name: Affinia Shelburne
title: “Gutes Hotel/Suiten. Gute Lage, viele Sehenswürdigkeiten zu Fuss erreichbar.”
text: Das Hotel als solches ist gut in Ausstattung und Komfort. Leider ist der Service nicht herausragend (An der Rezeption hatte man als Gast immer irgendwie das Gefühl, gerade zu stören...). Leider war das Hotel auch Überbucht und wir bekamen in der ersten Nacht nicht wie gebucht eine Deluxe Suite mit Kochgelegenheit, sondern NUR ein normales Doppelzimmer. Ab der zweiten Nacht hatten wir dann ein Zimmer "Studio Deluxe" mit Kochgelegenheit, welche in Form einer MIKROWELLE !!!! verfügbar war. Der Kühlschrank war eine überdimensionale Minibar inkl. einer solchen Bestückung zum Kaufangebot. Geschirr oder Schränke für solches fehlten komplett. Geschirr für 2 Pers. gab es nur auf Nachfrage. FURCHTBAR!!!GROSSE Ausnahme im Service-Sinne sind die Conciergen. Dort wurde einem immer geholfen, freundlich und auch zielführend (Okay, den WAL MART in Sacaucus haben wir selber besser und auf billigerem Transportwege[Direkte Buslinie] gefunden ;-) ).

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Excellent NYC value!”
text: Great location for NYC theater goers - & just three blocks from the city's top shopping. Fabulous skyscape views on the high floors - friendly reception - appealing lobby- attractive rooms ... And a very reasonable price for the city

name: The Plaza Hotel
title: “All that you imagine”
text: The renovation at The Plaza is all that you would expect it to be. It exudes NYC!! From the bellman at the front door to your personal butler with your suite ...everything is perfect. The only criticism would be the neon light on the second floor bar which I think is a little tacky considering it overlooks the elegant lobby bar area. The location of course is fantastic!

name: Night Hotel
title: “Excellent Location, comfortable hotel”
text:
Booked this trip a while ago to celebrate a special birthday, read the reviews and was worried that the hotel wouldn't live up to my expectations. 
I have been to New York on several occassions. This hotel is in an excellent location right in the heart of things, all the major attractions are within a few blocks walk. The room was small but no worse than any other hotel I have stayed in in New York. I like to book boutique hotels, something a bit different. 
In response to some of the other reviews regarding the darkness of the hotel. It is dark. Our room was small but it had all the usuals you would expect, hairdryer, iron and ironing board, clock radio, flat screen tv, had plenty of storage space so once we had unpacked and stowed our cases the room was fine. We had a window but little natural light as facing a wall. This is a small hotel in the middle of a block, so I would imagine if you want a proper window you can have a room at the front but then you trade light for street noise.
This is a trendy boutique hotel that is in line with other like minded hotels in the area, a few of which we visited and they were all candle lit.
Only one small complaint, we were woken at 3am every morning, by some kind of hotel activity, we guessed it was the newspaper drop. On the whole we were really pleased with this hotel and would stay again. If you want large rooms and loads of light then book the usual run of the mill hotel, if you want something different, then stay at Night.

name: Night Hotel
title: “Excellent Stay For a Vampire...”
text: Stayed for long weekend recently and was very enthusiastic as hotel looks tastefully trendy and somewhat gothic on web site. Very high standard of decor and super clean hotel with the most comfortable bed, room very small but hey its NYC so only to be expected, great TV, even a good sound system, reasonable price, so why not a perfect stay. Simply this, the hotel is entirely in a state of perpetual darkness in an effort to create a mood.. However, should i happen to be in the hotel in the morning i need light, in the afternoon i need light, at night it gets dark which tells me go out and enjoy nyc. All very confusing to someone as simple as me which left me feeling a little like i had Seasonal Affective Disorder..

name: Sofitel New York
title: “Schönes Hotel mit komfortabler Ausstattung, super zentral zw. Times Square u Grand Central Station”
text:
Das war unser erster Trip nach NYC und das Hotel stellt sich als gute Wahl heraus. Es ist sehr zentral in Midtown gelegen, nahe Times Square. Zur nächsten Metro Station war es auch nur ein Block Fußweg. Das Zimmer war schön eingerichtet, sehr bequeme Betten, schönes Bad und alles sauber. Unser Zimmer lag im 22. Stock mit Blick auf das Rockefeller Center, war also auch von der Aussicht nett.
Den Service haben wir eher weniger getestet, da wir weder im Hotel gegessen haben, noch haben wir den Zimmerservice in Anspruch genommen. Die Zimmermädchen haben aber einen guten Job gemacht, alles sauber und am Abend wurden die Betten auch nochmal aufgeschlagen.
Insgesamt waren wir mit dem Hotel sehr zufrieden und würden es beim nächsten Besuch bestimmt wieder buchen.

name: The Plaza Hotel
title: “Is this "THE PLAZA"??”
text: The lobbies and ground floor areas are amazing, just like you would hope. We had reservations for 2 rooms and they kept assigning us to used/dirty rooms. Finally, after speaking with the MOD we were assigned to rooms where housekeeping had cleaned. Ownership at this hotel has changed over the years, and sadly is reflected in the rooms and service

name: The Plaza Hotel
title: “Opulence”
text:
The Plaza is a gorgeous hotel with impeccable service. My daughter and I stayed in a Rose suite, which is a good size room and has 24 hour butler service. My only criticism would be, we noticed a surveillance camera on the ceiling of the room. It would probably go undetected by most guests (doesn't look like a camera) but I have them in my home and I know what they look like. The chandelier in the room blocks a camera view of the bed, but the living area (sitting space, wet bar) is viewable. I definitely questioned the need and legality of this. 
I must say, though, we wanted for nothing, were well taken care of, and had a fabulous time.

name: Hotel Mela
title: “hotel mela, the best choice!”
text:
per la seconda volta sono tornata in questo hotel a dir poco fantastico.
al primo posto c'è la sua posizione strategica - a 200 mt da times square - cosa impagabile, a seguire le camere non grandissime ma ben curate, nuove, calde, pulite e ben insonorizzate!
il personale dell'albergo sempre gentile e disponibile per ogni esigenza.
conoscendo bene questa magnifica città a mio parere non esiste miglior scelta sulla sistemazione alberghiera!

name: The Plaza Hotel
title: “Then and Now: Simply Great”
text: My partner was looking forward to experiencing the Plaza after the renovation but he was also a bit anxious as it had always been his favourite hotel, and he would have hated to see the charm of the old Plaza destroyed by the renovation works. It turned out there was cause for concern as the Plaza now offers all you could wish for: the former elegance coupled with lots of discrete modern touches that won’t affect the old style. We thoroughly enjoyed staying at this hotel, which has become one of my favourite places too. I’ve never had breakfast in a more stunning atmosphere, the food hall (one of the modern touches that have come with the renovation) is fantastic, and as for the lobby, well, what can you say? It’s simply overwhelming. We also enjoyed having a cocktail at the Rose Club (located on the mezzanine and offering great views of the lobby). Totally different atmosphere there, but well worth visiting. As for the rooms, what I really appreciated was having more than enough space for clothes. In fact, I’ve never had as many wardrobes in a hotel as in the Plaza. Last but not least, we very much appreciated the professional, extremely helpful and courteous staff. Thanks to them we had the steak of a lifetime ?, and only just a stone’s throw away from the hotel. All in all, we have sworn never to go to New York again without staying at the Plaza for at least a couple of days.

name: Cassa Hotel & Residences
title: “Aug. 25th - 31st”
text: Stayed 6 nights at this hotel. New hotel, very friendly and helpful staff, everything within walking distance. The only thing that could be better was the size of the room. They are small, but well laid out.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Great Location, Clean and Friendly”
text: A little pricey, but it was expected since it was in NYC just a few blocks from Times Square. Easy walk to Central Park. Check in was a breeze. Hotel was clean, room looked just like pictures. Restaurant food was amazing!! The server was a little bland, but friendly. The restaurant Manager, Georgio, was super nice, he stopped at every table to talk to the guests, in different languages. He even sent a bottle of wine to our room, my husband and I were celebrating our 1 year annivarsary.

name: Night Hotel
title: “Sexy, hip hotel. Waaaaay coooool.”
text: This hotel is ultra chic, without being overly pretentious. The pictures on their website are pretty accurate, no camera tricks or weird angles to fool you. The black & white theme of the hotel was a wonderful contrast against the bright lights and chaos of Times Square. My husband and I were there on our honeymoon. We found the Kama Sutra book in the nightstand very apropos. The fact that it was placed where a bible would have normally been found was very amusing to us! Although our standard size room was quite small, it was fine with us since we were on our honeymoon and didn't mind having to be cramped up together. For those of you who need their space, you might consider a larger room! My only complaint is that the shower divider wasn't quite wide enough, and water splashed all over the bathroom floor. Oh well, just throw a bunch of towels on the floor...they'll bring you new ones every day.

name: Sofitel New York
title: “à la hauteur de sa réputation”
text: TB accueil et service. Nous avons passé 3 nuits dans ce très bel hôtel. Nous avons changé de chambre une 1ere fois car nous en avions une sans vue au 4eme et pour équipée pour mobilité réduite. ( pas de baignoire....) Sans problème nous avons pu changer de suite...pret de parapliue par le concierge. propreté irréprochable, literie et oreillers très confortable. Rien à dire. Petit déj continental en chambre super. très bon séjour à refaire!!!

name: Hotel Mela
title: “Ottimo per essere a due passi da Times Square”
text: Hotel molto carino in posizione centralissima praticamente comodo per qualsiasi cosa. Personale molto cortese e disponibile. Un po' piccole le camere in quanto una volta dentro si fa fatica a trovare posto per le valige e a muoversi agilmente (la mattina per uscire spostavamo le valige da davanti la porta e le posizionavamo di fianco al letto). Pulizia sufficiente per lo standard americano ad esclusione della solita moquette poco pulita. Comunque nel complesso consiglierei questo hotel per la spesa affrontata (poco più di 100€/notte per camera) che è veramente irrisoria se si pensa che esci e sei praticamente a Times Square.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Excellent location & Anniversary recognition”
text: Well, I cannot fault the location, we've booked for Lion King tonight & are literally falling into Broadway. We're just having a champagne breakfast thanks to the lovely Vanessa on reception who asked about our trip (it's our 20th anniversary). We were also upgraded due to being a platinum priority club member, all in all excellent so far. I'd stop here again on a return trip no problem.

name: 70 park avenue hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “I've been back already - lovely but affordable boutique hotel in great location”
text:
We stayed here on our first trip to New York three years ago and loved it - so when we found out a friend was getting married in New York we know we'd go back, and took friends with us.
The location is perfect - just a couple of blocks walk to Grand Central Station, and the main shopping streets - it's so central we walked pretty much everywhere the whole trip.
The staff are very helpful and there's a great funky but relaxed vibe to the hotel - and it smells amazing from the moment you walk in the door!
The rooms aren't huge but they are well done with all the facilities - and this is New York so for the price they were ideal.
Little touches are fab too - a tray of goodies (which you do pay for but much better than the average mini-bar snacks, and lots of New York books to help you make the most of your time. They'll even print out your boarding pass for you if you complete a short form, and there's a complimentary wine reception for new arrivals every evening.
Apart from the usual attractions - a couple of others we really enjoyed - The Campbell Apartment just inside Grand Central Station isn't cheap but has a great vibe and worth a visit for drinks. The food at Michael Jordan's restaurant - also in the station - was surprisingly good, and don't miss out on Junior's cheesecake. But one of my absolute favourites was Cafe Wha? out in Greenwich Village - a fantastic night out if you liike live music, but do book ahead if you're in a group and check out the website first to see if it's your thing - best night we had in New York by far.

name: Hotel Mela
title: “continuate a cercare”
text:
a metà giugno abbiamo pernottato per tre notti in questo hotel a pochi metri dalla centrlissima time square, la posizione è fantastica ma le stanze sono piccole(e di questo avevamo letto su tripadvisor).la prima notte arrivati in stanza scopriamo che la nostra finestra è posizionata proprio di fronte al condizionatore esterno dell'albergo(notte in bianco).ci cambiano stanza e nella nuova al primo utilizzo si intasa il wc,protestiamo e in tarda serata al nostro ritorno in albergo il problema non era risolto(LIEVEMENTE alterati andiamo alla reception e risolvono).E per finire pulizia scadente.PREZZO 200 EURO/notte
CONTINUATE A CERCARE troverete CERTAMENTE di meglio.

name: 70 park avenue hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “solid hotel”
text:
This Kimpton hotel is a nice quality hotel that offered everything I needed during my stay in NYC. The rooms were a good size, stay was pleasant with the music throughout the hotel and the ipod dock, the wine reception in the eventing, and friendly doorman. The location is in Murray Hill and conveniently located near Grand Central. There are plenty of taxis to catch, and I was completely satisfied with the price my company paid and what I got out of it.
My company is in the trial process of signing a contract with several hotels for our employees, and Kimpton was one on the list. Nothing against this hotel, but I prefer to stay somewhere more hip and young in the future like a W or even a boutique hotel. I guess I'll have to do some convincing!

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Welcome to NYC”
text: Wir waren äusserst zufrieden mit unserer Wahl. Das alte Artdeco Hotel ist in einem super Zustand. Das Zimmer war geräumig, selbst für amerikanische Verhältnisse. Es wurde immer gründlich sauber gemacht und aufgeräumt (auch ohne übermäßigem Trinkgeld).Die Lage des Hotels ist unschlagbar. 2 Blocks von Macys (echt einen Besuch wert!), 5 Minuten vom Madison Square Garden und nur wenige Gehminuten zum Empire State Building. Wirklich sehr empfehlenswert!

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan-SoHo
title: “Friendly staff and great location!”
text: I stayed four nights last week during a week long trip to NYC. This hotel is great! The staff was very friendly and helpful during my entire stay. The hotel is clean and the rooms are a nice size for Manhattan standards. The location was impeccable, with easy access (2 blocks away) to two main arteries of the Subway (including the 1 train). No issues!

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan-SoHo
title: “Not sure......”
text: As a buisness traveler, you learn to accept problems and go forward. However, I encountered too many at this hotel too go anywhere but out. I am a frequent traveler to New york and try to stay in different areas of the city each time. I understand small tight quarters is a part of New York but really-for 299.00 ea. night? Too small for comfort, too noisy(air conditioner rattled)low water pressure, luke warm H20 and the TV disconnected from satelite every 20min. I did address the issue(s) with the front desk and the were very nice and addressed the issue with the temp of H2O but after a long day at work the last thing I wanted was an engineer in my room to work on things that at 299.00 a night should be in perfect order. I was scheduled to stay 3night and left after 2. Again-the hotel staff were very kind and offered assistance to fix the issues but I had enough.

name: The Benjamin
title: “Comfy bed and great location, but rooms were plain...”
text: The Benjamin is in a great location especially convenient for the 50th and Park area... and the service was pretty friendly though they had made a mistake on my reservation when checking in and even after calling in advance and emailing to say I would be arriving at 7 AM, and would be paying for the day before as the check in was early -- they still deleted my reservation from the system. Fortunately they were able to recover it through AMEX travel and rebook my room. The bed is extremely comfy with the softest sheets ever. Sleeping was always a pleasure! Nice amenities. The room was small and standard but the price was not bad for New York. Bathrooms white marble, old, and plain but everything worked fine -- nothing special though. The decor is old fashioned (ivory coloured wall paper), plain, old uninteresting lighting, and well, rather boring to put it mildly. The kitchenette looks old and worn, and the rooms could definitely be in need for a refurbishment. A lot of U.N. people and businesspeople stay here. The clientele is very upscale and a very friendly, nice vibe. Internet worked well though I had to pay each day -- should be free.

name: The Plaza Hotel
title: “nel cuore della città”
text:
ho soggiornato in maggio '12 per motivi di lavoro in questo bellissimo hotel, nel cuore di NY, si raggiungono a piedi molte tappe d' "obbligo" da visitare.
pulizia e cortesia al livello del suo Nome, stanze un po' "usurate" , ma molto confortevoli.
breakfast che soddisfa ogni esigenza.
ogni richiesta ti viene esaudita a qualsisasi ora.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “not bad rooms small”
text: i foulnd the hotel to be overall decent. It was a clean room, which is the most important thing to me. I feel that the room itself was on the small side, and the bathroom was VERY tiny. The bed was also comfortable. The staff was excellent. I probally will try another hotel next time because i felt very squeezed into the room. If your only concern is cleanliness then for the right price i would stay here.

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Not quite up to par”
text:
We are Platinum Marriott Reward members. We were greeted well. We received a nice room with a nice view. We went over Labor Day weekend. The elevators were kind of a pain, but we chalked that up to the holiday weekend and larger crowd. The location of course is outstanding. The property and amenities are more than adequate by all means. The problems were 1) the maids were so sporadic. Sometimes they tried to come at 8 or 8:30 and other times we'd be gone all day and come back @ 3pm and our room would still be dirty. 2) 3 times the maid or evening turn down person barely knocked and walked right in our room with the master key. Unacceptable! Once right after we checked in, someone walked in w/ a master key and walked out and we have no idea who that person even was. 3) The air conditioning had issues in the room. It was either too cold or too hot. 4) The TV had issues too. We called and they said they'd send someone up right away. We left for the day and upon our return the TV was still not fixed. We had to call again and they did fix it finally. I travel a lot for work and I'm a pretty easy to satisfy guest because we are barely in the rooms, but I'm thinking if I'm a PlatinumRewards member and we had this experience... What kind of service does the occasional traveler receive???
We love Marriott and we love NYC, but next time for $400/night, we'll be trying another property.

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan-SoHo
title: “Wonderful Weekend”
text: My husband and I are frequent visitors to Manhattan. We often stay in small boutique hotels or places recommended by friends throughout the city. We opted to book a room for a long weekend at the Hampton Inn, Soho. It was a great find! It even included breakfast. It is clean, friendly, and located conveniently to transportation, restaurants, and shopping. We could not have been happier with the value for our money. We will definitely return to this hotel in the future. It is a true bargain in fabulous Soho.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “Super situation”
text: L'hôtel est idéalement situé, à deux pas du Madison Square Garden et à 10mn à pied de Time Square. Toutes les lignes de métro et de bus sont à côté de l'hôtel. Rien à redire niveau hôtel, tick tock diner super pour le petit déjeuner!

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “Nice hotel, great location”
text: If you are coming to New York and focused on attractions and shows and shopping, this is a fine place to stay. You cannot beat the location for covenience and access for all of Manhattan. This is the second time we have stayed there. The bathrooms are small, but have been redone. It is an older medium sized hotel. The staff were very nice and accommodating. I think the room price for quality and location was worth the money.

name: Cassa Hotel & Residences
title: “Surprisingly big rooms”
text: We stayed at Cassa in June of 2011 on our honeymoon. Firstly the hotel is very well located for NYC first timers, roughly in the middle of Manhattan Island at 70 West 45th Street, between Fifth and Sixth (just west of Times Square). Secondly it is new (works were still being completed to the adjoining residences during our stay, they had no impact upon us though I note) and the rooms are accordingly clean and modern. The other thing about the rooms is, for NYC hotels (we saw several friends rooms), they are big. We had plenty of room for cases and luggage, something some of our friends envied very much! The hotel also has a gym in the basement which is functional, if not a little small. One thing we did not try during our stay was the restaurant, partly because it seemed a little pricy, partly because there were many options around the hotel (Starbucks across the street, street vendors outside and a short walk to the offerings of Times Square and Broadway). NYC also provides so many amazing food and entertainment options we were hardly in the hotel, we loved that city. In summary I would have no problem recommending the hotel to anyone, it is modern and clean with large (for NYC standards) rooms and friendly, efficient staff.

name: Cassa Hotel & Residences
title: “Booked on Hotwire”
text:
Saw a 4 Star Hotel in Midtown for $138 a night on a Sunday night on Hotwire, and was booked into the Cassa. I immediately read the trip advisor reviews, so I was prepared to deal with the full size bed problem that others have detailed.
I checked in, and was told that since I booked on Hotwire, I would be given a room with a full size bed. I asked for an upgrade, and the clerk told me $50 for a queen bed or $75 for a king bed. I then asked for a complimentary upgrade, and was told that that would be very difficult since their hotel has been sold out for months. Terrible reasoning, given that she already has indicated they have rooms with queens or kings available. She typed away for a while and continued to discuss the fact that hotwire bookings automatically get put in the smallest rooms. Then out of nowhere, she realized that the room that the computer had already booked me into was a room with a queen. So I said "great" and was ready to take the keys. She then had to radio up to staff to inspect the room. After waiting for 7-8 minutes, I was given my keys and we were on our way. Very long check-in process.
The room was good. Large Flat Screen TV, good A/C, Queen Bed, Walk-in shower. Got ready and headed out for the night. After returning to the hotel around 2am, we got ready for bed. At 3:30AM, I woke up to the sound of someone sliding a key into my door and trying to open the door. By the time I got up and looked through the peephole, the person was gone. Strange. 
At 8am, we were woken up by VERY loud drilling above us. I called down to the front desk and they said there was no construction going on in the hotel. I told her there clearly was as I could barely hear her on the phone with the loud drilling. After 10 minutes the drilling stopped. Drilling noises were not a nice alarm clock, particularly after a night of drinking.
The front desk arranged for a car service to JFK on the way out, which was helpful.
Overall, Cassa is lucky to receive an Average rating. Worth $138 for sure. But nowhere near being worth the $350+ their website was showing.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Not up to the required standards”
text:
Stayed in this hotel with my wife as there was a conference during May that my friend was attending. The only exceptional thing about this hotel is the location. Yes only the location was superb! In Broadway, near Times square and near the subway. My recommendation for your transfers from and to the airport, if you are not driving will be the yellow cab. For 2 persons the cost is $60 USD inclusive of tips one way. We felt that the yellow cab was most comfortable and easiest way to travel to and from the airport. 2 of us used the super shuttle from the airport and regretted our decision though it was probably $30 USD cheaper than the cab. Ok, back to reviewing the hotel.
Service was seriously poor, most staff don't smile nor greet you, maybe 1 or 2 staff did, I only remember a chamber maid did and a few security guys did, maybe i am invisible to the rest of them. I am not expecting staff to greet me all the time, but for a 4 stars hotel in such a developed country, I expect better, maybe at least a smile. Front desk staff and the ones operating the phone service are the worst lot, they have the can't be bothered with you attitude. I went to the concierge to ask for some assistance all they gave was vague answers leaving you with not much alternatives, they are always eager to direct you away. I realized that doing some research on my own was better than asking them.
Also to take note that trying to boil some hot drinking water or to get it from the hotel is a challenge, they have a coffee maker in the room and they expect you to boil the hot water using that, no boilers. Quantity from the coffee maker? A cup. If u need larger quantity of hot water, be prepared to boil several times. Alternative, pay for it by ordering pot of tea from the room service because only when you pay then you will get of a pot of hot drinking water.
Rooms were old, you can easily see that it is due to lack of maintenance, I think the shower curtain bar in the bathroom is gonna detach soon. The bar is slanted towards the middle like too much weight on it overtime, screws and rivets are also exposing. I sometimes am afraid that with a light tug, the whole thing is gonna fall on me. The bathroom has a very musky smell as well, shower curtains has two layers, waterproofing sheet and a cloth piece, whenever u accidentally wet the cloth piece it is difficult to dry. I think that causes the smell. Walls are thin as I hear party goers returning at night and noises from the room that you get ice from. Every time someone tries to get ice I would definitely know because the door hinges will tell u by making annoying noises, due to lack of oiling. Occasionally u will get to hear the ice making machine creating ice. Overall to be fair the room is clean, clean sheets, bath towels and it really has got a lovely view of the city. Beds and pillows are comfy too but the noises unbearable.
Conclusion; I won't recommend people staying in this hotel unless u really have got no other choices, this one is a definite last on my list if you are looking at Times square area simply because the amount that u are gonna pay will be a premium 4 stars price and it has got nothing close to 4 stars except it's location, around the same price you did probably be able to choose the hotel that starts with M nearby in Times square.

name: 70 park avenue hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Very nice for the price”
text:
I stayed here in January with my sister, on our annual "sisters" visit to the City for eating at great restaurants and seeing shows. We got a great price -- $200-- and both agreed as we left that we would come back again. Because it was a boutique hotel, there was never a line; there was always a hello; we never had a problem getting a cab (which I needed, as I was using a cane for walking that week); and we met and enjoyed other visitors. The room was just fine (nicely outfitted, etc), and although the bath was small, it was fine,too.
I stayed in the location before, and really liked it -- in a lovely neighborhood, but close enough to walk to theater (I just couldn't this year because of my injury.)

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “We have stayed here 3 times now and are going back for a fourth next year”
text: We have stayed in several other 5 star hotels in New York and just chanced upon this one 3 years ago and we liked it so much we have stayed every year for the past three years and will most definately be going back. The staff are genuinely helpful and friendly, everyone we have dealt with has gone out of their way to assist us. It is really well located, close enough to Times Square to be in the centre of things but still maintaining a calm atmosphere inside. I have now recommended the hotel to 2 different friends who have both also had a reallly enjoyable stay here.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Nice respite from the noise and bustle”
text: I stayed at the Westin last week while up there on business. Check in line for Starwood members was longer than the line for "regular folks" (15 min wait) and I almost switched places, but someone kept beating me to it. Staff was very gracious. Room on 26th floor was very nice and spacious although I was surprised to hear how loud the noise was from doors shutting in the hallway, folks walking around, etc. Was charged $6 as a "handling fee" for having the Business Center send out a package via Federal Express. Room service was excellent (nice service, yummy), but equally expensive. I find it somewhat odd that one can only get a bathrobe upon request and the newspaper is not left at your door, but instead is left in a stack by the elevators. The combo of the two could result in some weird moments if folks caught you grabbing your paper first thing! :) I did hear other business folks talking to each other about how they prefer this hotel over others as well...one benefit to standing in the check-in line for so long. Overall, I agree and I'd stay here again because the bed is deliciously comfortable and the folks were so nice, but there are some rough edges that could be corrected.

name: Hotel Mela
title: “Note 1”
text: Bei unserer Ankunft am Vormittag gegen 10 Uhr war das gebuchte Zimmer nicht frei. Wir erhielten ein Zimmer der höheren Kategorie und konnten dieses sofort beziehen. Das Zimmer war sehr geschmackvoll und neuwertig eingerichtet. Alles bestens, ebenso im Bad, welches für New Yorker Verhältnisse recht groß war. Das Personal war freundlich, nur hat man uns den Shuttle zum Flughafen nicht gebucht und dies mit einer Haftungsgefahr begründet. Die Gäste waren überwiegend im Alter zwischen 30 und 50. Der Fitnessraum ist sehr schön, jedoch dient er eher dem Ausdauertraining. Die Internetnutzung ist mit 8 Dollar/15 Min. sehr teuer. Die Lage des Hotels ist genial. Das gegenüberliegende Restaurant ist sehr gut und preislich i.O., nebendran ist ein Subway.

name: The Blakely New York
title: “Lovely Hotel :)”
text:
Brilliant hotel, very nice rooms. Beds are very comfy and bathrooms really nice.
Everyone always says New York hotel rooms are small but this was very spacious and plenty of room for two of us. 
Decent hairdryer, iron etc provided. Breakfast was simple but nice enough. 
Staff very helpfull, nice when you arrive as porter comes straight out to help with your bags. 
Good location, 5 mins from Saks 5th Avenue, Tiffany's Juicy etc. Also 5mins from Time Square, walked everywhere once in new York.
No complaints and would def recommend. Plenty of restaraunts right on doorstep.

name: Hotel Mela
title: “Genial”
text:
La verdad es que fuimos de viaje de novios a N.Y y despues de mirar muchos hoteles encontramos Hotel MELA y os aseguro que acertamos con la elección, el hotel esta muy centrico, vamos a 25 metros de times square, y muy cerca de la 5 avenida, el personal muy atento y educado, y todos hablan español. Las habitaciones estan muy bien y despues de todo un dia de andar agradeces este tipo de hoteles, la verdad es que solo tengo buemas palabras y gratos recuerdos sobre este hotel, lo recomiendo a todo el mundo. 
la unica pega que le vi, es que no tiene restaurante, pero a ambos lados del hotel hay restaureantes, pero en N.Y. por la comida no hay problema.

name: The Benjamin
title: “Accommodating staff and great room”
text:
The front desk clerk was very accommodating when I asked to check in early -11am- since I told her i wasn't feeling well. In fact, she went to the restaurant to get me club soda.
The room was great - wonderful bed.

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “Excellent”
text: My son (20s) and I just returned from 4 day "mother and son" trip to NY, and had a simply great stay at the Warwick. We live in Northwest Arkansas now but I worked in NY for years and know midtown well, so I knew I wanted a midtown west location, an authentic NY atmosphere, and a decent sized room, room service, an onsite bar/restaurant...the Warwick seemed to have it all, so when I was able to get a $144 (plus taxes) winter rate for February, we booked. It turns out that the majority of the Tripadvisor reviews were right. We were greeted with a smile, registered in 5 minutes. As for the rooms, my son's was on the 20th floor, had 2 beds, a lovely granite bath that was fairly large (just like the nicest one in the photos), clean as a whistle, nicely outfitted, bed crisp and white. Perfect. I think this was one of the renovated rooms. My room on the 24th floor was also very clean and fresh, big sunny windows, lots of space (these rooms are twice the size of most NY rooms), had a king bed and a sitting area. Yes, as some reviews say, there were a few scuffs on the older furnishings, and a few carpet stains, and the sofa in that room should be recovered or replaced...but I loved this room anyway. It had some elegant touches, high ceilings, felt safe and cozy, great bed....the only real complaint is that my room had the tiniest bath I think I have ever encountered. It was hard to get in and out of the shower with the door closed. I am a fairly petite person, and I was the only one using the bath, so it was manageable - however if my husband had been with me, I would have had to ask for a different room. Now, having said that, don't for minue let that keep you from booking this hotel. The tiny bath was nicely appointed, and the rest of the room made up for it. As for the staff, everyone was professional, nice, efficient - without exception. When I accidentally left my glasses at Randolf's they kept it and made sure it was returned to me. Lovely. The two times I ordered room service it arrived in 15 minutes, nicely presented and delicious. Randolf's bar is very nice - I had a very good crab cake with my martini. Murals breakfast bar was too expensive, so we only ate there one day. I have stayed in about 10 hotels in midtown west area. The Warwick may have just become my NY hotel "home." My sincere thanks to the Warwick staff for making our trip so pleasant, and for helping make it a week of great family memories in a magnificent city.

name: The Benjamin
title: “Nice Boutique Hotel in Manhattan for 3”
text:
It's hard to find a nice hotel in Mid Town/East Manhattan that sleeps 3. We had our teenage son travelling with us, and really appreciated that this lovely, older hotel just a block from the Waldorf Astoria could accommodate us. The suite had a separate living room with Queen pull out and small kitchen with refrigerator, sink and microwave. It was pricey, but we felt we were paying for the extra sf (the website says 550) and it seemed in-line with other hotels that we've stayed at in the area. (So all in all we paid a little over $1/sf per night for the suite). As noted in other posts - it is true that the bathroom is very small, and the toilet lid (plastic) does not stay up. But for me, the rooms and furnishings including bed were extra clean and the bed so comfortable that I barely noticed the bathroom. If we weren't all family, the bathroom situation would have been awkward.
Service was excellent save a distracted doorman when we arrived and one concierge that was nice but not serious about telling us how to get from point A to point B. The bellman and front desk stepped in. However, all the other doormen, the bellman, all the front desk personnel and the other concierge were extremely helpful and all get 5 stars from us. The restaurant - The National - was excellent both for lunch and breakfast with an interesting menu, ample portions and we liked the atmosphere. Most of the waitstaff were on top of things. Our breakfast waiter was having a bad morning and spent too much time complaining to the other waiters and not enough time watching us. If not for the couple of things mentioned above, we would have given the hotel 5 star. 
The spa/workout area was nice, lots of windows/light. The elevators were slow, but again it was what we expected for a boutique hotel. All in all we will return. We'd like to stay again - next time in a suite with a terrace.

name: The Lucerne Hotel
title: “New York Heaven!”
text:
After an overnight international flight I arrived at 7.30am ready to leave my bags and try not to fall asleep somewhere in the park until check in - but was beautifully surprised when the wonderful staff checked me in straight away and sent me upstairs for much needed rest!
This hotel is an absolute gem!!! I only stayed for two nights before meeting friends out in Sag Harbor, but would have loved to have stayed longer.
Beautifully appointed, in a wonderful neighbourhood and within walking distance of everything New York has to offer. I am a walker, so found it equally easy to walk all the way from the hotel into Rockerfeller Plaza as to catch a cab - to experience New York and all it has to offer. Access to park is only a block away from the hotel and that is always a treat anyway, in the fall even more so.
I have New York friends who are always staying in the city overnight who have never heard of this little wonder and am telling everyone what a find it is.
Yes the room is small, but if you are spending more time in your hotel room in New York City (other than just sleeping there) there is something wrong with you!!!
Thanks again for a wonderful stay - I will definitely be returning.

name: Duane Street Hotel
title: “beautifully designed rooms - interesting street views”
text: if you appreciate well appointed and designed small hotels, you should try the Duane. great location in TriBeCa, walkable to plenty of cool bars and restaurants. the rooms are small but beautiful. comfy beds. i had an interesting view from the 2nd floor, as the room had floor to ceiling windows that looked right out onto the street, where a bunch of black town cars were idling. kinda weird, but the curtains were thick and the sound proofing amazing, so it was quiet. if you can get the Duane on special rate, it's worth a visit.

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “great night”
text: We spent one night in the Warwick to attend a wedding nearby. I was really impressed with the size of the rooms. There was several feet of space around the bed, a desk, plenty of closet space and a reasonably sized bathroom. The decor was lovely and the staff was professional and efficient. I'd go back for sure.

name: Royalton New York
title: “FABULOUS”
text: When arriving at the Royalton I was promptly greeted at my car. Within minutes, I was escorted to the front desk. This is no ordinary front desk. It is very private. The whole hotel is intimate in the look, the feel, the attention given to guests. I stayed on business and all I could think of was how romantic the atmosphere is and wished my husband was there with me.

name: Smyth Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Trendy, Friendly and Fun in TriBeCa (now stop charging for WiFi)”
text: I had occasion to spend a couple of nights at the Smyth Hotel recently, as a friend was having a drinks party in the hotel's basement Toro Lounge in celebration of his wedding. The Smyth Hotel is part of the Thompson group of hotels, and has a characteristic on-trend feeling in its decor and atmosphere, fitting comfortably into its TriBeCa location (the hotel makes liberal use of black and artfully inadequate lighting). In addition to the Toro, it has a good restaurant on its ground floor, Plein Sud, which is well worth a try. The rooms are a decent size for the city, the furnishings are trendy and adequate and the bathrooms are actually quite sophisticated and have some good quality toiletries. Staff are friendly enough in that trendy NY hotel sort of way, a trace more warmth would not go amiss, but I'm not quibbling. I will take issue with the policy of charging for WiFi, however, which is just crass and unattractive. "But it's New York" doesn't cut it. Otherwise, a perfectly nice stay in the middle of one of my favourite neighbourhoods.

name: The Blakely New York
title: “Wedding in NY”
text: We travelled to New York to get married, we stayed at The Blakely, what a great hotel. There was a group of us of all different ages staying at the hotel in different rooms. We stayed in a suite which was great as we've got a 19 month old baby. As you walked into the room you walked into the lounge and to the right was a kitchenette and the bathroom and to the left was the bedroom with 2 double beds, plenty of space. It was lovely having the lounge as when we put our baby to bed you didn't disturb her because we could go into the lounge. The breakfast that the hotel provided was a great start to the day, a $2 per person tip they charge for this. The hotel staff were all really helpful and ever so nice. The loaction of the hotel is really good to explore the wonderful city. Our stay couldn't have been any better and would definately stay there again.

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “No feathers please”
text:
We loved the location of this hotel. All mid town attractions are within walking distance. 
Had a fabulous king room with a small bathroom and a huge balcony/view which we wish could or would have used. In the spring, we will definitely request the same room with the hope that we will take advantage of the outside area the room provided. Staff was friendly and helpful. The long line for check in a small lobby area moved quickly. Every staff person wanted to assist in any way they could. A wonderfully warm welcome to NYC. 
Prior to arriving we had a few requests - no feather pillows and no down comforters. Unfortunately, we did not realize that our requests were not met until we returned from the theater at 11PM. Knowing housekeeping was not about to change our bedding at that time we decided to make the best of it. Unfortunately, in the morning we were coughing, sneezing etc until allergy pills kicked in to remedy the effects of down bedding. We were reminded to check every thing upon entering our room for the first time; and not to assume that all requests would be met. This was a disappointment to us since we did call the hotel in advance to personally remind them of this important request. We are hopeful if we return for visit they will get it right the next time.

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan-SoHo
title: “A great deal & location”
text: I will return to this hotel when in NYC. 2 blocks to the subway, great walking neighborhoods all around it. The breakfast is very good, everything was good, no complaints at all.

name: Royalton New York
title: “Excellent overall”
text: This hotel is of a very high standard. The rooms, bathrooms etc are very nicely presented and the staff are excellent. It is in a great location for all the attractions in NY. Would highly recommend it.

name: Moderne Hotel
title: “I love it!”
text: It was such a great experience. The staff was helpful and super friendly. Can't beat the location. Which really enhanced our trip to NYC. The room decor was very tasteful. What a cool place to stay. And we will return soon.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “Simply great!”
text: We sincerely want to thank W Times Square hotel and its team because we had a wonderful stay. The employees were really caring and always smiling, the room had a beautiful view on Times Square and was really comfortable (especially the bed).
