I loved the decoration, the music and the perfume when you enter the hotel. Perfect place to stay at the heart of NYC. Thanks so much.

name: Moderne Hotel
title: “Superb small Hotel”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for a week. We loved it. The decor is fantastic, the beds soooo comfortable and the staff are just brilliant.
The hotel is just off Broadway at 55th Street, so is an easy walk to Theatres etc. It is surrounded by great places to eat and just a short walk to the Metro and busses.
We bought 7 day unlimited Metro passes at just under 30Dollars and they are so wothy it. We travelled extensively on the Subway and Buses including a trip down to Coney Island.
Final comment must be to compliment Victoria on the front desk who is outstanding. If you are going to New York, please try this hotel out - you will not be disappointed!

name: Moderne Hotel
title: “Awesome! Great Rooms and Top Notch Staff”
text: I can't say enough about Moderne! The hotel is very trendy and comfortable with clean rooms and nice amenities (love their bathroom soaps and body wash!). The staff is top notch and EXTREMELY welcoming and accommodating. Centrally located to Times Square, Central Park and Hells Kitchen, it just was a great experience. Only wish there was a lounge however the patron area boasts of complimentary wine, coffee and fresh fruit!

name: Royalton New York
title: “Comfortable hotel with great staff”
text: I stayed in Royalton for only one night with my fiancee and it was a really pleasant experience. The hotel is very well located, in a central part of Manhattan. The staff was extremely friendly and effective and the room was spacious, clean and comfortable. Not a cheap hotel - but worth its price.

name: The Benjamin
title: “Really liked it, friendly staff”
text: We found the hotel to be quiet and clean and the staff friendly and helpful. The doorman, Mohammed made our stay more enjoyable. The lobby was totally unusable as they were remodeling, so there was no place to sit and relax. However, it was a very small area, so we probably wouldn't have used it anyway. The room was very clean, but the bathroom was pretty small. It was made up for by having a separate area for a nice closet and kitchenette with a small fridge with ice maker. That was a pleasant surprise. The room didn't have a view of any kind, but we were out so much it didn't matter. We were fairly close to Rockefeller Center, St. Pat's Cathedral, and the Waldorf Astoria.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Great stay at reasonable price for New York”
text: We stayed at the Salisbury Hotel at the end of July. There were 4 adults and 2 kids in our party. The suite was very spacious especially for being in New York. Nice location, as just 2 blocks from Central park and only about 10-15 minutes down to Times Square/ Broadway shows. Room was very clean. Other family members stayed at the Waldorf Astoria and when we went to see there room, we were very grateful for the Salisbury. We paid 1/2 the rate they did and had more than twice the space. They were paying for a fancy lobby and wide halls, but not comfort for themselves. 1 block away was the Associated Supermarket, which was reasonable for soda supplies and chips. Also, saved some food costs by doing PB&J. Breakfast for $4 was acceptable at the hotel. Elevators are a little slow especially at peak times, but really a minor inconvenience. Highly recommend the Salisbury.

name: The Pierre, A Taj Hotel, New York
title: “This Hotel is like a Palace they treat you so well”
text: They are waiting on you hand and foot. If you tell them its your birthday they bring you complimentary birthdays. The concierge is great. Stayed twice because the first time was so great. across the street from the plaza and near the apple store. the best location. personally i believe it is nicer than the plaza and cheaper although it is expensive if you are looking for a luxury hotel its great.

name: The Pierre, A Taj Hotel, New York
title: “The closest thing this side of the Atlantic to Buckingham Palace”
text:
I don't have a noble title, but we received Posh treatment from the staff at the Pierre. Maybe they received their training from the Queen's buttler. It was truly awesome. I can get used to this in a wink. I consider myself as a seasoned traveller, but this was better than your average stay at a Four Season.
I had walked past The Pierre while staying at the Ritz Carlton in Central Park and I kept a pending visit in my "to do" things. This time I decided to book a room. It had to be one with a good view of Central Park as it still gives me a joy to look at it from above. I went for a signature room, not yet a suite, but as good as one. (as a curiosity, our room in the 22nd floor is the only room in the floor. The rest of it is a private apartment!)
The rooms are not cheap, but you get back every penny and then some more.
What you get is the feeling of being an old time owner of one of those multimillion dollar apartments facing the park. The hotel does not have the grandiosity of The Plaza entrance and it's crystal dome, but you get the feeling of being one more neighbor of the upscale high rise condos. By the way, half of the hotel space are actually private apartments, so in a way you are part of them.
Everyone from the doorman, to the front desk staff, to the elevator operators (they used to have leverages and had to open and shut those heavy doors, now they assist you so you don't get a sore finger while pushing your floor button), give you their best smile and talk back in a selected vocabulary. (Maybe I should send my kids to work here so they learn to talk properly...)
Our room had floor to ceiling windows, a foyer, big bathroom (for NYC standard that is), and a bed to make you forget all your business problems. 
Maurice at the Concierge and Sanela Mrkulic, Director of Guest Relations are the best kept secrets of NYC.
The location is perfect to walk or to take short cab rides to the museums, restaurants and other nearby attractions, the rooms are spotless, the service is trained to please the Royalty.
The only thing that needs improvement is the service at the restaurant. I had to ask for service, to have them take away the dishes and so on. it seems like they were a concession and not part of the hotel. Hopefully they will fix this. We only had breakfast here as we used Zagat reviews to select our dinner restaurants and their score left them out.
So regardless of this small inconvinience, The Pierre is my new reference for the NYC hotels. What it lacks in grandiosity it over compensates in intimacy and service. I have not been at the Peninsula or the Mandarin but I see no reason as they can't compete with the address and the Postal perfect views of this hotel, not to mention the dedication to detail from the excellent staff.
If you are planning something special, don't even think about it, this is the place to stay and you will only regret that you have to fly back home some day.

name: The Benjamin
title: “Mohammed the door guy is awesome!”
text: We had dinner at the National and it started raining and Mohammed was so sweet and offered us an umbrella .

name: Royalton New York
title: “WOW!!!!”
text: A friend suggested we stay here and wow was I blown away how incredible this place is. I love NY especially the neighborhood the Royalton is in. I've stayed many times athe Bryant park and it's a great place but doesn't hold a candle to the Royalton. It's a great place to be able to conduct business while shopping is close by and so is times square, central park and a lot of great entertainment spots. I can't say enough about what a great time, the staff is awesome. Just gives you a warm and homie feeling. Can't wait to come back. Only a few weeks!!

name: Smyth Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Exceeded our expectations.”
text:
My husband and I checked into The Smyth in TriBeCa after a long haul flight from Sydney. We were not yet out of our taxi when Kevin greeted us to help us with our bags. The lobby is very stylish with a contemporary feel. Daniel checked us in and put smiles on our faces when he gave us a complimentary upgrade to a suite.
The suite was lovely, especially the bathroom which had a huge tub and a rainfall shower. We stayed in 6 hotels during our USA trip and this is the only hotel which provided a shower cap! They had Kiehls amenities, and Dean & Deluca snacks in the minibar. The bed was one of the most comfortable I've ever slept in, and they had a good range of cable channels to choose from. Additionally, the room was surprisingly quiet for NYC.
The location of this hotel was perfect for all our downtown sightseeing needs. Walk out the front entrance about 10 steps and you're at the Chambers subway stop, and sights like Battery Park, Staten Island Ferry, World Trade Centre Memorial, and the Century 21 Department Store are all within a walkable distance. There is a Whole Foods 2 blocks away, and a Pain Quotidien 2 doors down from the hotel where we breakfasted every day.
We had a wonderful stay here and would return to, and recommend this hotel to anyone wanting a stylish and quiet oasis from which to enjoy this phenomenal city.

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “Home away from home”
text:
I travel to NYC a few times each year and have made the Warwick my base when visiting NYC from Australia. 
You can't beat the Warwick for it's location, history and style.

name: Hyatt 48 Lex
title: “Great NY hotel”
text: This is a great hotel. People are correct that the lobby is tiny and unimpressive however how much time do you really spend in a hotel lobby? I'd rather have a bigger room than a huge lobby. My room was a great size and very clean and comfortable. I could control the temperature of the room and make it as cold as I want when I slept. Granted most hotels have thermostats you can control in the rooms but in my experience they only work about 50% of the time. The staff is very friendly and helpful. My one complaint is I set out the door hanger for breakfast delivery before I went to bed, and when I got up in the morning and went to get my paper it was still there. No one picked it up that night so no breakfast for me. I mentioned it to the staff when I checked out and they were very apologetic. Also the temperature in the cardio room seems inconsistent. I went down one evening to work out and it was freezing in the room and I went down another day and the room was like a sauna. The location of the hotel was perfect for me, away from the Times Square madness but within walking distance of a lot. Overall this is a great hotel and I would definitely stay here again. I travel to NY quite a bit for work and this could easily become my preferred hotel.

name: Smyth Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Great service makes a great stay”
text: I just had a three night stay. We moved to the hotel after a dispiriting night at the Tribeca Grand, making reservations to change at 11pm, and choosing Smyth in part because of the cheerful patience of the reservations desk as we dithered, considering the hour. We arrived at about 10 in the morning, were greeted by smiling bellmen and a courteous desk clerk who got us into one of our rooms after a short wait for housekeeping to check its status, despite the early hour. Coffee brought to us in the lounge as we waited! The concierge was terrific and gave us some great ideas for walks and reservations for meals which helped make the weekend a stellar one. I liked the hotel furnishings, and rooms and all the typical things on a “nice hotel” checklist (including quiet), but a huge part of what made it a great stay was the exceptional politeness, professionalism, and efficiency of the staff – right down to getting rooms cleaned in the short windows when we remembered to take door tags off. Kudos to all of them, and to the management that is required to keep an operation running like that.

name: Royalton New York
title: “NEW YORK TRIP”
text:
Great hotel. Best bed I have ever slept on. Pricey but would recommend to anyone. In room internet but could not connect to www. Would definitely go back.
LNMD93

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “An excellent choice”
text:
We stayed here (2 rooms booked for 2 couples) from 21/5 to 26/5 and had an excellent holiday. 
Positives
•Excellent location, walking distance from all the key attractions a couple of streets down from Macys (3 mins), Empire State (less than 10 mins) and Time Square (10 mins). Only about 25 mins walk from Central Park and Grand Central Terminal. Hotel is opposite Penn Station which has links to most major subway destinations. 
•Brilliant service in the hotel. Staff very friendly and helpful and the standard of cleanliness was good. When we arrived the computer system said one of our rooms was not ready, which turned out to be an error, it was fine. The desk clerk went to check the room himself to ensure it was ok – excellent service. Concierge is also very helpful and will issue you safety deposit boxes for free which are located in a locked room in the reception area. There are quite a few staff around reception and the front doors which makes it feel a safe place. 
•There are a number of sites with cheap deals to this hotel. We booked with Hotel Opia and experienced no problems at all. The other reviews concerning Hotel Opia refer (I think) to the Guest Rooms which are cheaper, we were in a Studio Suite. 
•Very large rooms with comfy beds and good facilities. More room than you need for a couple in both our studio suites. One room had two double beds and the other suite just one. Bathrooms are small but good showers and big enough for what you need. Decoration was pleasant and TV was large. 
•Hotel Restaurant has really good food for dinner and is not noticeably more expensive than other restaurants of a similar standard. When we went it was not very busy but there was no reason for this. 
•Good cheap places to buy breakfast nearby. Bagel Mavern (across the road on 7th avenue) is good value for a large breakfast. Do expect ‘New York style’ service in here though – ie not as friendly as the hotel! 
•The renovations occurring to the hotel had no impact on our stay, except for the fact you have to enter the hotel from 31st Street which is no hassle at all. 
Negatives 
•The hotel was very noisy at night. This is not internal noise that the hotel have any control over but the street noises (mainly taxis, fire engines and trucks). Having spoken to people who stayed in more expensive hotels this problem seems to apply to most NY hotels. Our rooms were on the 10th and 17 floors facing 31st street and the noise was the same in each. Be prepared for noise, and bring earplugs and you will be ok. I am a light sleeper but did manage to get used to it. 
Other tips
•On the tourist attraction part of this website a lot of people recommend getting up very early to beat the queues at the key attractions. If you are not an early riser then don’t worry too much, I think this advice depends on the time of year you go. People in our party went to the Empire State and Statute Liberty late afternoon and the queues seemed to have died down by then, and there were was no waiting– just avoid the peak periods (approx 10.30am till 3.30pm)
Overall the Southgate is a good choice for anyone looking for an excellent location and a good value hotel.

name: The Blakely New York
title: “Comfort, service, and location - terrific small hotel in NyC !”
text:
The Blakely is is comfortable is every way: the rooms are nicely furnished, the lnens are good quality, closets are roomy, the bathrooms are well-equipped, the tea/coffee self-service is convenient-- and it is nice having book shelves in the room, with hard-bound books !
The Blakely really distinguishes itself in *service* ! I requested a room with a quiet location, and the request was honored with courtesy. When I arrived, the front desk, serviced by Marleni, confirmed a dinner reservation, and Marleni also took care of requests for small problems with the bathroom tub/drain, quickly, efficiently, and courteously.
The hotel is located on a quiet (for NYC) side street, West 55th, about a block from Sixth Avenue, and near Seventh Avenue/Broadway--Times Square -- but the feeling is "miles away" from the density of those areas.
The Blakely is great !

name: The Lucerne Hotel
title: “Nice room, good location”
text:
I stayed here the night before a big meeting and the staff was very accommodating, even when I arrived around midnight to check in. The lobby is small but functional, and there is a concierge which is helpful. My room was a 'queen superior' which had 2 beds, a desk, TV, a closet with ironing board, safe, hangers, and a nice bathroom with a full tub, lots of free shampoos and soaps, and plenty of towels. Good water pressure in the shower. The free wifi internet wasn't working for me, but I didn't follow up with the front desk so it was probably just a glitch.
They allow pets, which worried me, but other than hearing some dogs jingling down the hallway I didn't hear any other barking or room noise from my neighbors. The hotel is in a great location, just down the street from the #1 subway line, and the doormen were very helpful with directions. Plus they held my bag for most of the day since my flight was not until the evening.
Overall, a very pleasant stay - I just wish I could have been there longer because the room was so comfortable!

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Be Warned!”
text: We arrived at the Southgate Tower after enduring a terrible journey from Las Vegas so were looking forward to a nice room with some space to crash out. We were allocated our room on the eighth floor. Something should have warned us what to expect when we alighted from the elevator to be met by the lingering stench of cooking, but nothing could prepare us for the horror of what was to be our room for the next 3 days. the room was absolutly minute and positioned at the side of a service elevator (hence the smells) The carpet was stained and filthy, the furniture and decor old and very worn. The bed was queen sized and the cushions that were on the bed looked very greasy, although the sheets and pillow cases looked clean, I didn't dare to look at the mattress!! There was only enough room for one bedside table. The bathroom was the tiniest one I have ever seen. The windows would not open I beleive they were stuck down with years of filth!! We hared down to reception to complain and requested another room but were informed that the booking had been made via Access USA and I needed to get in touch with them and sort it out they would have nothing to do with it. I did research this hotel, virtual tour ect, but unfortunatly didn't come across any negative reviews. We have now returned home (with quite a few bites between us I might add) and are in the process of complaing to the travel agent we booked with. Let this be a warning make sure your travel agent deals direct with the hotel and not access usa!!

name: Hyatt 48 Lex
title: “A great experience!”
text: This is a relatively new hotel. It is not far from the Grand Hyatt (located near Grand Central Station). We had been staying at the Grand Hyatt but decided to add an extra two nights to our stay in New York City. The Grand Hyatt was sold out, so we moved to Hyatt 48 Lex. We arrived at around 9:30 am in the morning, with a lot of luggage. Our greeting was very friendly and they provided us with a clear run down of what services the hotel offered. They happily stored our bags and placed them in our room when it was ready. The room was fantastic. It had a small kitchenette, with microwave and dishwasher. Had we been staying longer, we would have made better use of these facilities. The room was modern, fresh and clean. It was also quite spacious. There was a lounge area for guests on the second floor, with complimentary refreshments available - a great addition (although we didn't get the opportunity to use it). The location is really good, although pick-up and drop-off access is a little limited - there is a space outside for taxis to pull up but they won't wait there (so ordering a taxi for a certain time is not really an option). Flagging a taxi requires you to go to the corner of Lexington Avenue, as taxis tend not to go past the entry to the hotel. Having said this, the staff were more than happy to help us flag down a taxi, even when it seemed that every taxi was off duty or in-use. The cost of this hotel was a little more than we would have liked to have paid during this trip (we were away for 4 weeks so had to be a little more careful); however, it certainly wasn't extravagant. Given how impressed we were with the facilities and the staff, we would happily pay the same again. We have stayed at the Grand Hyatt a couple of times and were far more impressed with Hyatt 48 Lex. It is a more intimate hotel and has a lot of added extras that make it a great place to stay. We will definitely stay there again when next in New York City!

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Definetely value for the money”
text:
Stayed Jan 1 to Jan 4. Booked through Quikbook at $160/night for a 2 double bedded room. Arrived very early (10am) no room available and I did not expect one to be. Called around 1:30pm room available (had asked for quiet room) but when we got to the hotel about 20 mins later turns out they had given us a room by the elevators (the clerk indicated this might be noisey). So we waited for a different room which was available about 15 mins later
I should note there was just 2 of us, me (more than middle aged), and my 13 year old daughter. We have travelled a far bit, and this was our 3rd trip to NYC in 1 1/2 years. previous stays were at the renaissance Times Square and the Michelangelo hotels. This time I wanted cheap, great location for shopping and clean.
Bell hop very pleassant and helpful. Lobby is very small and quite plain by NYC standards. I was told by bell hop that concierge had left for 3 month holdiay, so no concierge available.
Room was a normal size hotel room (which means big by NYC standards), and bathroom was smaller than expected and plain. Overall impressions were that hotel is dated, particularly common areas, hallways. Clearly used to be apartment units at one point (noticed doorbell buttons at each door to rooms, not working though).
I like a firm bed and it was. Pillows smallish, and definetely problems with soundproofing in areas (ie I could hear some of the bathroom noice to the room next door, could clearly hear noise from hallways, and the plumbing would make a large mooselike moaning sound at times (even in middle of night)
Elevators very very slow in morning breakfast peak hours.
The above are the negatives. However overall i would go back. The room and hotel were very clean. The maid service pleasant and accomodating. The location great (1 1/2 blks to 5th, right by subway, about 2 blks to park etc). The Italian restaurant was superb and so handy (reasonably priced, great fast service, very good food, including pizza, pasta and a great organic greens with beets salad). Starbucks across the street. did the breakfast which I was not a fan of but 13 year old daughter loved. It was worth the $4 charge each. We were not in the room more than a ccouple of hours each day ( 1 hr in morning maybe 1-2 hrs at night, except to sleep and to drop off purchases). I am very particular re cleamliness and cannot fault the hotel at all on this.
If you want an upsacle NYC experience this is not it. We have stayed at the renasissance Times Square and the Michelangelo, bof of which had nicer common areas and rooms in terms of decor, but I don;t need that and for $160 / night I am very happy.
Parking was a great deal (special for the Salisbury ) at $28/night, just 1 1/2 blks away.
The one thing that could have been a problem for me is the heat-. halls very very hot, and room too was too warm. But the windows open, and then it got very very cold our last 2 days in NYC, which cooled the room down too. I tried the A/C but it would not cool the room down enough!! Not sure what that would mean come the summer!!!!!!! so beware of that
Overall great value for the money

name: Hyatt 48 Lex
title: “Loved it”
text: I stayed at the Hyatt 48 Lex with my family (wife + 3 kids) on Dec 23, 2011 and we all loved it. The hotel is beautiful (as is expected from Hyatt), the location is great, and the staff was very friendly and helpful. The rooms are very spacious for any city but huge for NYC standards. Access to the beautiful & relaxing lounge was a plus and my kids especially loved the complimentary hot chocolate all day. I travel around the world on business and stay at very nice hotels. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone. We are definitely going back in 2012.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “Excellent hotel overlooking Times Square New York”
text: Stayed here 4 nights to celebrate my birthday. Absolutely fantastic hotel located right in the action of Times Square. Booked a "Cool Corner" room which gave us direct views overlooking Times Square from one floor-to-ceiling window and a side view from another similar window. Amazing views especially at night. The rooms are stocked with absolutely anything and everything you can think of - packed fridge full of a variety of soft and alcoholic drinks and also a picnic style basket of savoury and sweet foods. Of course you pay for these luxurys but it's good to have them on hand in case you get peckish! They do however provide you with free bottles of water each day and the day of my birthday Room Service arrived with a complimentary Cup Cake which was beautiful! The bed was huge and fantastically comfortable, the bathroom well stocked with toiletries. If I had to say anything negative about the room it would probably be the obscured glass panel that divides the bathroom from the bedroom - it doesn't really give you much privacy once you put the light on - but perhaps that's me being a bit prudish! It certainly didn't spoil my enjoyment of this hotel on my first trip to New York and I would certainly recommend it to everyone! They were even kind enough to organise our return transport to the airport as we were flying on to another location. Thank you W Hotel you made my birthday!!

name: The Lucerne Hotel
title: “Our new home in NYC”
text: We stayed here for a few nights right after Thanksgiving & loved it. Not only was it spacious, beautiful, very clean, newly redone bathroom and to top it off it was also reasonable in price. It has a wonderful restaurant & bar. It is a beautiful building too. We like to stay in unique places that have their own individual charm & this place has it.

name: Hyatt 48 Lex
title: “New Hyatt in New York”
text:
We stayed at the Hyatt 48 Lex the weekend before Christmas and found to to be excellent. Even before we checked in, I got a foreshadowing of the great service in store for us when I called the concierge concerning tickets to Phantom of the Opera. The were most helpful and were able to obtain the tickets which I collected on my arrival. 
The check-in area is tiny, but they were very efficient and we were in our room within minutes. The rooms were average in size but had excellent amenities including a small sink and refridgerator. The bathroom was very modern in design, with a large shower. The noise level was low overall, but I could hear the elevator at night.
The only drawback might be the two small elevators. The wait for them could be long at times. Also, there are only two rooms in the hotel with double beds. All the rest have kings, so plan accordingly. The beds themselves were comfortable.
We had a drink at the bar in the restaurant and enjoyed the friendly staff. We also had breakfast and found the service sluggish, but the food good.
The location was fine, with most everything within walking distance or a short cab or subway ride.

name: Moderne Hotel
title: “Terrible hotel with poor management”
text:
I stayed in the Moderne in September 2008 and WOULD NOT RECOMMEND THIS HOTEL TO ANYONE. I booked and paid for a double bedroom at the Moderne online, and telephoned the hotel 2 days prior to my stay to ensure that they had received my booking. On arrival at the Moderne we were informed that THERE WERE NO ROOMS AVAILABLE. The receptionist stated that our booking had been transferred to the “Ameritania Hotel”. I was told that there was no manager to discuss the matter with and that nothing further could be done. I followed my instructions and checked into the “Ameritania Hotel”. Our room smelt of stale smoke, it was so small that we could not wheel our luggage in, and it was filthy.
The next day I went back to the Moderne to complain and was told that the manager was not available to speak to me and the receptionist suggested that I call the hotel manager as he was unlikely to call me.
I have felt compelled to write this review as I would not want anyone else to be cheated by the Moderne. There are plenty of alternatives in New York and I would not consider either the Moderne or the Ameritania Hotel to anyone even as a last resort.
Nadia from London

name: Gramercy Park Hotel
title: “As good as it gets”
text: We absolutely loved this hotel and would stay again. We stayed for a weekend in October which is high season in NYC. We shared with them that it was our anniversary and they very thoughtfully had a bottle of champagne waiting when we arrived. The public and private areas are beautiful -stylish with great art, furniture and furnishings. The designers kept what was good from the original building and augmented it with unique touches everywhere. We loved our room which was a Luxury Loft. The restaurant had great food, a good vibe and excellent service. Whoever is running this place is a real pro because the entire staff was on their game -helpful but not fawning. They could not have been more pleasant or responsive. The hotel communicated well via email both before and after our stay. The neighborhood is fantastic, with so many great restaurants nearby. The location allowed us to get anywhere in Manhattan easily. Staying here was a real pleasure. Highly recommend this.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “New York New York!!!”
text: New York is the most amazing city!! The salisbury was a great choice for us. We were travelling with our two teenage boys and so we were thrilled with the size of the rooms. The decor is dated but i think it adds to the ambience of the whole place. Our room was spotlessly clean, beds very comfortable with cable TV and good quality towels and tolietries. All staff were extremely nice and helpful. The breakfast was included in the great rate we got through expedia.com.au which was great as it saved us having to search out a place to eat before we started our very busy days exploring this fabulous city!! Location is brilliant, only a short ten min walk to time square and broadway shows (Lion King was superb!) We used the hop on hop off bus which was great, especially if you have limited time. Central Park only 5 mins away with the horse/carriage rides directly out front. All in all a wonderful stay in a wonderful city, Thankyou Salisbury!!

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “Classy place, well positioned.”
text:
We loved our week at the Warwick. The position is very close to the South end of Central Park and just around the corner from MoMA gallery and the Rockerfeller Centre. The staff were super friendly and efficient. The room was quite small but OK for the three of us and probably good by NYC standards. It was an easy walk to Times Square, where we enjoyed a lovely meal at Angelo's Italian Restaurant, an NHL hockey match at Madison Square Garden, and Wicked the Musical on Broadway.
We walked to all of these places and it was as cold as 0F...part of the NYC experience! The Warwick has a great little bar in the front corner, I think called "Randolphs". Didn't eat at the restaurant though so can't comment on the food or service there. There are many bakeries/cafes in the area that serve typical NY breakfast of coffee, bagels, pastries and fruit.

name: The Benjamin
title: “Great stay in a great room made possible by Brian Jones”
text: A warm greeting at the door by Mohammed, excellent service at the desk by Brian, and a beautiful suite helped give my wife and I a wonderful New York stay. We have been Benjamin regulars and will continue to be on our New York visits. Keep up the good work and continue to make your appreciated upgrades.

name: Moderne Hotel
title: “Do Not Consider”
text:
Although I read many reviews on Trip Advisor, I usually do not write reviews of hotels. However in this case, I feel compelled to warn you of what you are actually getting. My main warning is: You will be fooled by pictures you find of the hotel on the internet and the hotel website.
Our first room was absolutely disgusting. The non-smoking room was unbearable. It smelled of cigarrette smoke and lysol spray. The AC/Heating unit was in bad shape with paint peeling off. The AC unit did not work...and I needed it. The hotel kept the rooms too hot, and you really can't control the temp with your room unit. I stayed in late December and I had to sleep with the window open, and all I could think about is how many cockroaches I must be letting in and out. We stayed one night in the room and we had to move rooms due to the smoke.
Our second room was just as bad despite the room didn't smell like smoke. The Heat/AC unit did not work, and neither did a separate AC window unit. I'm not sure if it would have mattered because the black-out curtain in front of the window also wraps around the Heat/AC unit and window, so you are isolating your room from the temperature control. The units are very good noise makers. The walls in The Moderne are paper thin. You can hear people walking through the halls and the doors slam shut.
Bathroom: In our first room, the toilet was up against the wall, and they had the tioliet paper dispenser on the wall too. I am not kidding when I say that you had to sit on the tiolet at an angle due to the configuration. In our second room, the tiolet was moved closer to the shower, so this was not a problem. I did not like the shower because of the glass wall design. It puts water all over the bathroom floor.
If available, you can request a mini-frig to be brought to the room. This was quite hilarious. The mini-frig could not have been manufactured after the 1970's. It was old, disgusting, and should be embarassing to the hotel.
The beds: My complaint about the beds is that they are designed to be really low to the ground. Just a matress, no box spring. I wouldn't say that the beds were uncomfortable.
The Lobby: The lobby is not quaint. It is small. You cannot sit in it. You could not arrange for people to meet you in it. You can walk up to a 1 person desk to check-in, and then you can walk out of the lobby. That's it.
Outside: The images of The Moderne from the outside that you might find on the internet are out-dated. The sign looked in bad condition (sut) and wasn't lit. You could barely see the entrance. Your likely expression when you walk up to it for the first time will be "What the hell?!"
Location: Honestly, the location is really not that great. It is on the edge of where you want to be, but not close. It is a good 13 or so blocks to time square, yet it's too close to mess with the subway. You can definitely tell you are leaving the safety of numbers when you are walking to The Moderne at night.
The Good: I liked McGee's irish bar across the street.
Bottom Line: If you are a guy planning a trip for your special someone, don't go cheap and stay at The Moderne. Upgrade to some other hotel, unless you want to hear about it for forever and you like making excuses.

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan-SoHo
title: “bonne prestation”
text: voilà un hotel bien situé pour faire des visites à New York. A deux pas des lignes de métro. Une bonne prestation. Deux bémols: une climatisation dans la chambre un peu bruyante et un petit déjeuner, bien que copieux, qui se fait dans des assiettes jetables... Le personnel est agréable. Un petit truc : les chambres sur la rue donnent sur Watts Street, accès au Holland Tunnel, avec un trafic assez important. Demandez une chambre sur l'arrière de l'hôtel.

name: Smyth Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Still great, area even hipper...”
text:
I have stayed here a total of 30 nights since its opening, and love the LES and the area, the King Suite on the back and up high is perfect, and area dining and night scene is so much better than the Meatpacking and Soho area, though its close by. great music venues nearby too...
You cant go wrong with the hip, trendy, modern, off the radar feel of this property.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “W Hotel Times Square is absolutely amazing!”
text: This was my fifth trip to NYC and this time to celebrate a 50th birthday. The W Times Square was by far the best experience we've ever had. The staff, atmosphere, room, views, etc. completely exceeded our expectations. Beginning with the staff at check-in ... courteous, accommodating and friendly ... we were then given a corner room with unbelievable views of the Hudson River and Times Square. Our room was lovely and very clean with all the amenities we expected and more. The location is perfect with a Starbucks right out the front door and shopping, Times Square, theaters, restaurants and everything else you can imagine within steps of the front door. If all that wasn't enough, on our last night, the hotel sent up a complimentary bottle of champagne. I can't imagine staying anywhere else in NYC.

name: Cassa Hotel & Residences
title: “One of the Best Boutique Hotels”
text: I've stayed in boutiques hotels in Europe and USA, and I can say that Cassa Hotel is one of the best!!! During last November we made a weekend trip to celebrate my wife's birthday to NYC. After a little research, I found this hotel and decided to stayed there. Since the moment that we arrived, the staff greeted us with a great smile. We got a very nice and confy room, very trendy furniture and very spacious. Location is great and close to a lot of attractions. The bathroom is very nice and clean. I will definitely stay here on every trip to NYC.

name: The Benjamin
title: “Very Clean, luxurious hotel, great location, excellent staff, exceeded expectations!”
text: This hotel is wonderful! I highly recommend it! The rooms are very clean, beds comfortable, large bathroom, rooms are quiet. We all had a great night's sleep, we heard no noise from the city! this hotel is conveniently located, easy to access the city on foot. The staff is friendly, efficient and accommodating, the concierge was so helpful! I highly recommend this hotel, whether you are looking for a luxurious weekend, or a convenient location to explore the city with your children. We can't wait to return!

name: The Lucerne Hotel
title: “Super hotel in a great area!”
text: We loved this hotel! There was a heat wave in NYC during our visit. Coming back to our lovely, clean, quiet room at The Lucerne Hotel each evening was a treat. The A/C worked well. The staff was friendly, helpful and efficient. Honestly it is close to everything you need (subway station, Central Park, loads of terrific places to eat). Try the cute little Peruvian restaurant down Amsterdam Ave. Their La Brasa Chicken and Peruvian goulash were outstanding.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Beautiful hotel, wonderful location, kind personnel, the place to be in NYC!”
text: I am a Starwood customer and was treated very well from the time I made the reservation through Starwood until Checkout.. The service was prompt and friendly. Anyone I asked for information and was not sure of an answer found one. The location was superior and convenient for everything that we did. I had a corner deluxe room which was great. It was clean and loved all the windows. It made our trip and experience to remember.

name: Gramercy Park Hotel
title: “Bohemian Perfection!”
text: this reminded me of my Home in Laguna Beach, CA minus my 4 dogs. Every detail was perfect and the staff was perfectly friendly without the stuffiness that you get from other hotels and resturants.

name: Royalton New York
title: “Great Location, Very Nice Staff”
text: We stayed at the Royalton for a week in August. The location is great. We were able to walk to a lot of attractions, the Public Library, Bryant Park, Times Square and many others. The staff was very nice and helpful. Enrique, front desk, set us up in a very nice room on the top floor of the hotel. The rooms are very large. This was one of the largest hotel rooms I've stayed in and I've stayed in quite a few. We had a queen bed and a long seat/built-in couch that my 16 year old, 6'/185 lb. son had no problem sleeping on. The bathroom was not the biggest but it was nice and functional. The ipad was a nice touch. My son got the most use out of it. I also must mention Jenny, front desk, and John, bellhop, was really friendly and made you fell welcome. The only reason I can't give them a 5 is because they don't have ice machines for the guests. Everyday we had to get ice from the bar downstairs. Thanks so much Royalton. We had a great time!

name: The Benjamin
title: “Continue to love it ...”
text: I wasn't going to write - because it all continues to be wonderful. It would be negligent of me not to recommend such a lovely place. The staff and rooms are equally lovely. The service has always been gracious and proactive. I'll go back again and again.

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan-SoHo
title: “hotel hampton inn manhattan soho new york”
text: da prendere in considerazione vista anche la ricca colazione compresa nel prezzo e la vicinanza alla fermata della metro. unico neo è la posizione troppo a ridosso dell'holland tunnel per cui dal pomeriggio fino a tarda sera c'è la fila continua di macchine in coda con conseguente alto livello di smog.

name: The Pierre, A Taj Hotel, New York
title: “Hôtel The Pierre : une expérience innoubliable”
text: Hôtel exceptionnel. Demander une chambre en étage élevé avec vue sur Central Park. Vue magique depuis la fenêtre de la chambre. Service réactif et très courtois. Recemment refait, décoration impeccable et chambre très confortable.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Not like it used to be”
text: We have always stayed in the exec concierge rooms as the lounge serving all day tea, coffee and snacks plus late afternoon appetizers and a continental breakfast was very convenient. However, they have moved the lounge to the 5th floor a ways away from the elevator, whereas the exec rooms are still on the top floors. So, no longer convenient and a huge disappointment. The lounge, however is close to the biz conference rooms. The rooms now have no personality and seem too cool and impersonal, and clearly oriented to male biz travellers, but happy for the free wi-fi. Would have been nice to have a fridge and this was not a problem when the exec lounge was close by. Now who's going 35 floors away to get a cuppa, or an apple? Will look for a new go-to next time we're in NYC.

name: The New Yorker Hotel
title: “zu empfehlen”
text: Die Lage des Hotels war wirklich super. Von hier aus kann man uptown oder downtown alles zu Fuß erreichen (allerdings nur mit bequemen Schuhwerk!). Die Subwaystation liegt direkt am Hotel und man kann mit der Linie E uptown bis zur airtrainstation zum JFK fahren. Die Zimmer waren sauber aber klein. Für einen Dollar täglich fürs Zimmermädchen wurden sie auch immer wieder hergerichtet.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “Disappointed”
text:
I have just returned from a stay the renowned W hotel, and as we usually stay at W hotels or SPG hotels I was completely shocked at the hygiene levels in our room. We checked into the corner room on one of the top levels and as I went into the bathroom I noticed that the toilet was dirty as were the tab tops. The tables looked as they had not been wiped down at all and still had black smudges and water marks (from an eyeliner or mascara). The bed sheets were also stained! Having called the 'reception' to explain the situation I was told that the manager would pay a visit to the room, however after a 30minute wait, a cleaner was sent to our room who said she did not have the right cleaning equipement to wipe down the tables and that the black marks would not come out. I then demonstrated using a tissue. After a couple of calls to reception a manager was finally sent up and having seen the state of our room she apologised. At this point we had been waisting time in our room (1.5hours) having to explain simple hygiene to a world renowned hotel group. Our trip was to celebrate our anniversary and this experience took out valuable time we had planned together!
As an SPG platinum member we were really upset at the state of room especially as we were unable to check into our room until 2pm as it was being 'cleaned'.
On a more positive note the hotel is in a great location and the bar/living room area was nice. The higher level rooms have a great view, but after this experience I would be reluctant to stay here again.

name: 70 park avenue hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Gutes Hotel zu vernünftigem Preis”
text:
Gute Lage zwischen Lower-Manhatten und Midtown, nahe 42nd/Central Station.
Zimmer teilweise etwas klein (-), erhielten Zimmer im 2. Stock (-), Personal sehr bemüht für guten Rundumservice (+), sehr gutes Embiente im Hotel (+).

name: The James New York
title: “Shopping break in NYC”
text:
We've just stayed at The James for almost a week and loved it. The hotel is very clean, modern, well decorated and the rooms well appointed. Staff are all very helpful and friendly. The location is great too, with plenty of shops, bars and restaurants nearby. A subway stop is available closeby. We were given a local map with all the shops, bars and restaurants on. It was a lifesaver on a few occasions! Navigation not being one of my strong points. The room itself was nice and as mentionned by previous reviewers the bathroom and its vanity screen was quite a novelty! The bed and pillows were very comfortable. Plenty of fresh water available and a turndown service. My favourite perk of the hotel was the little treats available in the lobby. At breakfast there was coffee and scones, fresh fruit and water in the afternoon and wine, cheese and crackers in the evening. What a great idea! 
We used the rooftop bar on several occasions and loved it too. Stunning setting, good cocktail list and attentive staff. Our only criticism was re the David Burke Kitchen, but I wouldn't let this cloud my rating of the hotel. For breakfast, Le Pain Quotidien on Grand St offered a nice selection of pastries, breads, eggs and oatmeal. For something more, Balthazar on Spring St also enjoyable.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Excellent location”
text: Stayed here with family or four nights over weekend. Extremely busy in New York bu this is probably normal. Excellent room, clean and quiet with view of Hudson river. Staff very helpful. Would stay her again.

name: Hotel Metro
title: “A wonderful retreat in the middle of Manhattan”
text: From the minute we walked into the lobby I knew I had selected the right hotel. It was clean, and welcoming. the front desk staff were efficient, helpful and pleasant. Our room was very well appointed with huge comfortable beds. We were on the 12th floor so street noise was not an issue and we slept well. Breakfast the next morning was good and plentiful - a nice selection of bagels, cereal, juice and coffee. I would definitely return again and hope to soon!

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Execellent location”
text: This hotel can't be faulted for value for money - rooms are spacious, the location excellent. Just one or two negative comments - although we had e-mailed back in November asking for a quiet room, we were facing the street and on the 6th floor so by 5 a.m it was pretty noisy. We made a couple of phone calls from the room and the final bill didn't list the correct numbers and overcharged by at least one call (we were also told listening to voicemail counted as a call)- so it's worth keeping a check on this or avoid using the hotel phone altogether. we had a one room suite and the sofa/pull-out bed was definitely not comfortable for my 17 year old daughter - the iron bars could be felt even if you added a couple of blankets to the mattress. The advantage of the 6th floor was you didn't have to wait for the lifts - they could be a long time (probably seemed longer as you couldn't tell which floor they were at unless you were waiting in reception) - the lifts do hold ten people but not all hotel guests seemed to want to acknowledge this fact! The staff were friendly and helpful, the breakfast queues easily avoided by taking food out. All in all we wouldn't hesitate to stay here again.

name: The Peninsula New York
title: “It's outstanding”
text:
Great New York hotel experience! Service is way beyond good.
Friendly staff goes out of their way to make you feel welcome and it home.
Yes it's pricy but if you want the best this is a place to be. Concierge was especially helpful in making dining plans.

name: The Benjamin
title: “Exactly what we were looking for...”
text:
We stayed at The Benjamin in one of their basic guest rooms from Feb 4-8 2010. We booked it through Hotwire the day before we left and got a great deal ($160/night with taxes). Overall, it was exactly what we were looking for... it was clean, close to the subway roughly two blocks from the 53rd St. station), had a friendly staff, and fit our budget. 
The staff (specifically Ken, the new guy @ the front desk) was very helpful. They sent us a complimentary bottle of wine for our anniversary and gave us a late check out (2pm) at no cost! 
For us, the hotel was mostly a hub/place to sleep than anything else, and it was perfect for just that. We didn't use the spa or room service or any of those types of amenities. Their pillow menu was nice though and we certainly took advantage of it. I think that if you were going for major luxury, however, you could find somewhere better to stay.
The hotel bar (The Emery Bar) was nice and had good martinis, but it was always pretty empty and closed early (11pm). The conciege recommended a deli around the corner (The Metro Cafe) which was mediocre, at best. The front desk recommended a diner around the corner (Morningstar) one night when we wanted a late night burger (and didn't want to pay the $20 for a room service burger). It was a very generic diner, but a good place for a late night snack and well priced. 
Overall, I would return if I found a similar rate but I would definitly not pay more than $200 for a room.

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Great place in Times Square”
text:
This hotel was perfect for our family trip to NYC. The room was spacious and the view was great. The girls stayed in one room and the guys in the other. Both rooms had different views of the city and the concierge lounge had great food. 
We took a taxi or the subway to the different plays and shopping places. No problems getting around.

name: Four Seasons Hotel New York
title: “Fantastic hotel”
text:
Me and my wife stayed here for 7 days we checked in and our room was over looking a building site so the next morning i requested that we be shifted however i had to pay extra as the room had a separate living area and great views of central park.The bathroom was large and the separate living area was great as when my wife went to sleep i could stay up without disturbing her.
The Conceirge was very helpful and gave us some good tips for Restaurants and shows in new york we had breakfast voucher amount however suggest not to have it as it does not cover the cost of breakfast even at 45 dollars per person.
My only gripe is that internet is not free considering what you have to pay for a room a night.
All in all a very good hotel and the staff a very friendly and helpful staff.

name: Hotel Metro
title: “very good hotel in great location”
text:
Stayed at Hotel Metro for 4 nights as a group of 4 in 2 rooms. We flew back to the UK Sunday evening 28th Oct (last Virgin flight out i think). Whilst the horror of SANDY is now part of New York history, we were lucky it did not affect our holiday.
The Hotel Metro is an ideal base for your New York experience with clean well appointed rooms, great showers and toiletries, room safe, breakfast is a bonus (hard to find in New York hotels) and although they use paper plates and plastic cutlery, there is a choice of fresh muffins, pastries, cereal, bagels, toast, OJ, etc with coffee or tea to send you out to explore this great city. The hotel staff were hard working and very polite, the concierge and both doormen (especially matthew) were very helpful and guided us to great bars, restaurants, trips etc.
I look forward to staying at this hotel in the future and thank the staff for a great time.
New York was all we expected and more and will bounce back from the recent hurricane carnage.

name: Ritz-Carlton Battery Park
title: “Best hotel in the Battery Park area by far”
text: Just spent three nights at this hotel this week (8/13/2012). Staff and service level was outstanding. Room was well appointed and the bathroom room was especially spacious. The extensive marble in the bathroom was very nice and included detailed wainscoting. The Bose wave radio was a nice touch and made me feel at home. Turn down service was also a nice touch and the maids were very courteous. This is an excellent location if you have business in the Financial District. Battery Park along the Hudson is right outside the door and a one mile walk on the Hudson while continuously viewing the Statue of Liberty was a special daily treat. The lobby is not especially grand nor is the nondescript facade. Those minor quirks were not problematic for me and I appreciated that the elevators require key cards both day and night. My room was sufficiently large but the closet was a little snug and required me to place my suitcase at the end of the bed vs. stowed away. I was on the 12th floor and was pleasantly surprised by how little street noise I could detect. This is my second stay at this property and I have nothing but positive things to say about it.

name: Four Seasons Hotel New York
title: “Very Good, Not Amazing”
text:
My husband and I spent a night at the Four Seasons for a quick trip to the city. Via American Express Platinum we were able to check in early and received a $100 spa credit and breakfast. The check-in process was smooth and very nice. We were upgraded and had a corner room with nice views. I was only surprised that while the layout and furniture were nice, the all-beige decor seemed a little tired - and there was nothing on the walls - no paintings or anything. It was as though it had been taken down or something?! The carpet and chair upholstery wasn't stained, but seemed worn. The bathroom was lovely and large, and who doesn't love Bulgari toiletries. The room was quiet and we slept well. Room service breakfast was very nice and fresh. No complaints. 
It was my spa experience that was my only issue. Since we had the credit I decided to have my nails done. I had gel polish removed and re-applied. To soak my nails in acetone for ten minutes they charged $30!! and of course the manicure was way overpriced as expected for a hotel spa. Unfortunately the nail technician did not do a very good job on the new polish and it was all stuck to the skin under my nails, and it was just an awkward hour and a half spent with her. I have no problem overall with what they charge, but in general expect excellent service and a pleasant experience and did not feel the Four Seasons lived up to it in this case. 
I would certainly stay here again when in NYC but will probably try some of the other Fine Hotels in NYC first.

name: 70 park avenue hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Hotel 70 Park avenue bien situé”
text:
Hotel confortable, propore accueil sympatique, mais salle de bain trop petite, il aurait fallu mettre une douche plutot qu'un bain.
Bien situé, non loin de l'empire state, de Time square. Les petits déjeuner chers, et pas de chocolat chaud

name: Mandarin Oriental, New York
title: “Outstanding Hotel”
text: We spent the weekend in New York and stayed at the Mandarin Oriental. The hotel staff were extremely efficient and made our stay most enjoyable. The hotel located on the upper floors of the Time Warner Center has great views. Our room had a beautiful view of the Hudson River. The lobby and restaurants have a great view of Central Park and Midtown. The room is a good size and the bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was large and luxurious. Check in and check out were a breeze. The two nights we were there we asked the bellman to get us a taxi. Instead he put us in the house car which was offfered gratis. It was much nicer driving in a clean luxury car. Everything about the hotel was first rate.

name: The Peninsula New York
title: “Fantastic location and attentive service”
text: Have just returned from a 4 night trip with the family. We all quite happily shared a junior suite with the kids on the sofa bed. The rooms were spacious and spotlessly clean, and the views of 5th avenue from the swimming pool on the top floor were fantastic. Although a bit pricey, the location is perfect for sightseeing/shopping, and the staff were amazingly attentive - nothing was too much trouble. We tended to eat out for lunch and dinner, having only breakfast at the hotel which again is a bit pricey but couldnt fault it for variety or quality. Would definately stay again or try another hotel in the chain.

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan-SoHo
title: “Hotel Hamptonn Hinn e Soho nuova frontiera di NyC”
text: Hotel situato a Soho un quartiere particolare di Manhattan fuori dal solito giro turistico. Ricco di negozi, gallerie di artisti e di locali da newyorkesi. Ma se desiderata catapultarvi nella Città la metropolitana è a due minuti dall'albergo e vi porta ovunque. Buona soluzione! L'albergo offreservizi essenziali, prezzi buoni, personale molto cortese, colazione inclusa e macchina del caffè in camera.

name: The Strand Hotel
title: “The Strand Hotel - Excellent!”
text: This hotel was nice! I never expect much when using those unpublished/biding sites but found this gem of a property with one. I found the hotel staff to be completely pleasant from welcome to that last hailing of a cab. I found the rooms to be well appointed with comfortable beds and linens. Morning breakfast is "European". Convenient to all theaters on foot or in a cab/car.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Girls Weekend”
text: Booked Crowne Plaza Times Square through Magellan Vacations (great company to book through) and was given a great rate. We booked a double suite corner room which was nice. I really enjoyed the corner room, gives you great panoramic views of NYC. I honestly have no complaints about the room. The only complaint I have is the fact that the hotel knew we were celebrating a bachelorette weekend and they did NOTHING to make it special or memorable for us. Other than that, the location is GREAT - right in the heart of the theatre district. Go check out Dallas BBQs on 42nd street (right next to BB Kings) - they have some great simple food and AWESOME drinks (try the Tsunami)

name: The Benjamin
title: “THE BOMB DOT COM”
text: The Benjamin is one of the finest hotels I have been in the US. The service is top notch and the location is the best . It is in the heart of the city and very close to all attractions. The employees are well knowledgeable and repsectful. Everyone greets you with a smile and friendly personality! This is a must stay hotel and its worth every penny you pay!!!!

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “excellent location, budget family hotel”
text:
For NYC, you can't beat the location and the price. It's across the street from Carnegie Hall, and next door to the Steinway Piano showroom. It's a couple of blocks from south Central Park, FAO Schwartz toy store, and Bergdorfs (okay, so I window shop). We enjoyed the Brooklyn Diner one block west and we walked south to Times Square in 10 minutes. It's a longer walk through Central Park up to the Metropolitan Museum. (Alas, the old Russian Tea Room across the street has closed down, but the gold bear sign remains intact. ) One day we walked from the United Nations past the American Girl Doll store and St. Patrick's Cathedral, through Rockefeller Center and back up to the hotel. 
The room was small for 2 adults and 2 teens: 2 double beds with itchy cotton/poly sheets. Only rooms with 2 queens were the pricier suites. (We previously stayed in a suite and loved it.) The small room had a bathroom door that did not close. Prepare to wait for the slow elevator, or else run down the stairs. The hotel charged $3 only once for the breakfast buffet: mostly doughnuts, cereal, & croissant. If you're looking for healthier fare, buy it and bring it to your room as all rooms have kitchenettes. NYC can be enjoyed w/o spending a fortune.

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Location yes --- but not worth the price”
text: I cannot argue --- this hotel has one of the best locations in the world : Times Square is literally out the Front Door. But this hotel is simply too big to enjoy. In fact, it is monstrously large. Do not expect any kind of individual or personal treatment, unless you go out of your way to ask. I am a long standing Marriott customer --- but I will never stay at this particular one again. Other Marriotts nearby won't have the same location, but they will certainly cost a lot less and be a better overall value.

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Wonderful stay”
text: Myself, my wife and my 13+ yrs. old daughter went to USA summer vacaction trip. New york was first destination. We stayed in this hotel which is situated on the heart of the city. Manhattan's times square. Very busy hotel. We were on the 11th. Floor. The room was very neat and clean. The washroom was loaded with modern toilettes. There was complementary two bottles of 1/2 lit mineral water. Beds was soft and comfortable. Check in time was very less. They provided the room key within 10mint with a sticker which to be paste on the suitcase mentioning room number. As soon as press the no of floor near the lift, immediately I will know which lift will go to particular floor.

name: The Peninsula New York
title: “As expected - simply perfect”
text:
We stayed here on a recent visit in September when the entire city was busy. I would like to thank the entire staff to make our trip a special one. Kristin from Guest Services was a star - always smiling, regardless how busy. 
The location is perfect for the business & leisure traveller and we had great tips for restaurants from the concierge (Fabian?). Thank you for making our stay in NYC so memorable.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Comfortable and Convenient”
text: I was very fortunate to land a very nice rate at the Crowne Plaza for three nights over President's Day weekend. The room I was in was terrific - well appointed, very large for NYC, great TV, a chaise lounge and an ample-sized bath with nice amenities. I had no issues with noise at all. Hotel staff was very pleasant and non-intrusive. Only small peeve is that the elevators are fairly slow, even though the two elevators banks are split and the elevators themselves are designed to be express It still takes time, especially during peak hours. Do note that there is a charge for wireless Internet. All in all, however, a really superb stay.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Thanks Trip Advisor!!”
text: Thanks to Trip Advisor. It was just what we expected. Location was amazing. One block to Central Park and Subway Stops at each corner. Good sized room and clean. We stayed during the week and had very few problems getting the elevator. The staff was attentive and congenial. The beds were comfortable and had good pillows. It was great to have a fridge and a microwave. Yes it was old and our view was of the alley and the apertments next door, but it was quiet and we had no problems sleeping here. We had a hallway in our room, which actually acted as a changing area for our teen girl. It had the kitchenette in it and a mirror, so we stayed out of her way and she out of ours. We will definately stay at the Salisbury when we go back...The Green Cafe next door was good too as was the $3 breakfast at the hotel.

name: The Strand Hotel
title: “Excellent location and staff.”
text:
A rather new hotel in NY that is very clean and well staffed. Service is fantastic. Only drawback is that the free continental breakfasts have turned into an over priced breakfast that is average at best. Spent $60 for two people for a very small breakfast. Better to eat elsewhere. 
Overall though, a good place to stay while in NY business district.

name: The Strand Hotel
title: “Empire state of mind”
text: My husband and I just spent a long weekend in NYC and this was our first stay at The Strand...we loved the hotel! We have visited NYC many times and this hotel offers a great location, with beautifully furnished rooms and wonderful amenities. The check-in staff was extremely friendly and helpful. Our housekeeper kept our room immaculate with nightly turn-down service and gourmet chocolates.The downstairs bar/restaurant offers an inviting atmosphere and the rooftop bar is AMAZING. There's no better way to unwind after a day of sightseeing and taking in a show than from the rooftop, which looks directly at the Empire State Building. Very romantic! This location is ideal, as you are within walking distance to Broadway, Times Square, etc, plus the subway is very close. If you want to visit an oasis in the city, walk to the High Line from the hotel...gorgeous flowers and plantings, chaise lounges, and more beautiful views of all the city has to offer. We will come back to The Strand !!

name: The Peninsula New York
title: “Once in a Life Time experience”
text: I have recently stayed at the Peninsula 1 night for business and all I can say is it is worth every penny. Great Hotel, Great service and Great location. The room that I have stayed was small but enough for 1 nights business stay,

name: The Lucerne Hotel
title: “Beautiful Surroundings and Wonderful Service - what more could you ask for?”
text:
My family stayed at the beautiful Lucerne for 5 nights. We had great service, a clean and spacious (for NYC) room, very comfortable beds, quiet nights, good room temperature and courteous bellmen. The bellmen were wonderful when asked for recommendations for restaurants, buying some snacks and how and when to use the subway. Each time - the recommendations were great - thanks Manuel! 
Central Park and The Museum of Natural History are within a short walking distance. A convenient subway entrance is right down the street. There is a great restaurant called "Good Enough to Eat" a short walk away that we visited twice!

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan-SoHo
title: “Très bonne surprise”
text: Hôtel rénové depuis 7 mois. Très confortable. Chambre un peu petite mais chaleureuse et bien équipée (wifi, TV LCD, coffre où j'ai pu ranger mon ordi portable). Très bonne literie. Grande salle de bain moderne où on s'y sent bien. Petit déjeuner compris et très copieux, service de café et thé 24 s/24 gratuitement.

name: The James New York
title: “Can't wait to go back”
text:
Our stay at the James was magnificent. If you like smaller hotels with a lower profile but yet very chic, this should be it. The staff are very friendly and I loved that they do their job almost invisibly; you never see chaos going on, or people running around. We had a deluxe king with a fantastic view on the skyline and the river. The bed was very comfortable. We loved the mini-bar selection and its adequate prices. 
I loved the lobby, as it really was an oasis of peace in a busy city. They serve free cookies, fruit and wine, which is a very nice touch. 
The location is probably the best thing, as you are in Soho, but in a quieter area, but nevertheless close to all the action. There are a couple of places to have brunch very close. 
It's a pity it wasn't summer, because their rooftop pool looked very inviting! 
Can't wait to go back.

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Great location..very small room”
text: The Metro is ideally suited for touring New York. The roof top terrace is very pleasant. The breakfast buffet is good. The gym is small but not busy so that is not a problem. We have traveled extensively in Europe and been to New York several times. Our room at the Metro was the smallest we have ever experienced. The bathroom was approximately 2.5 feet by 5 feet. The bedroom was approximately 7 by 11. The bathroom door could not fully open because it hit the foot of the bed. While you don't spend a lot of time in your room you want to be comfortable when you are there. And at the prices of these room you should expect an adequate space. After bringing our complaint to the management we were informed that the hotel has a number of smaller rooms that it books out during busy times. Presumably we were unfortunate enough to get one of these rooms.

name: Ritz-Carlton Battery Park
title: “Recently emergency stay during power outage”
text: We were stuck as were many without power for several days. The Ritz downtown gave us a lovely room at a reasonable rate - not increasing their rates like many other local hotels. They were very flexible with us as far as checking in - checking out as we didn't know going in how many days we would need the room for. Staff was very friendly, helpful, and sympathetic to our stress and needs. Good free coffee in the lobby! Thanks Ritz Carlton!

name: Four Seasons Hotel New York
title: “The best hotel in NY, discrete heaven yet full of celebrities”
text:
We again went to the NY4S which we simply love to go everytime. The rooms, the service and everything about this hotel is just perfect. It lacks a swimming pool if you need one, we do not in NY. But its Ty lounge is fabulous, the staff is just great and its restaurant Joel Robuchon offers an exquisite world class food experience in the utmost relaxed service atmosphere so to us it is simply perfect.
Our daughters loved the fact that the hotel had Jennifer Aniston and Justin Bieber in the hotel. Last year the Boston Celtics where hanging out in the lobby, never felt so small! Guests there are all discrete and all enjoy the peaceful atmosphere commanded by its magnificent entrance hall. So that is probably why all celebrities feel good staying there, enjoying themselves and not being disturbed. One of these celebrities is actually my wife which also enjoys the peaceful and distinguished atmosphere.
The 4SNY is always a wonderful experience so we keep returning to it everytime.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “hotel affinia manhattan allie le confort et place”
text:
hall d'accueil tres grans et agréable avec tous les services de conciergerie.
la chambre : j'avais une chambre avec un très grand lit, conforme aux photos, très grans, salle de doucheavec mobilier type contemporan, la pièce a vivre lit très confortable avec choix de l oreiller, grand écran plat fixé que vous pouvez tourné côté lit et côté salon qui comprend un canapé et un fauteuil, beaucoup de choix de chaine (plus de 50)enfin coin bureau separé par un rideau qui comprend un réfrigérateur.2 placards, un avec rangements et l autre avec table à repasser,je recommande vivement cet hôtel,etant cloué à l 'intérieur étant à manhattan pdt la l ouragan irina, j avais l'impression d 'etre chez moi et était heureuse de pouvoir profité d'une si belle chambre.
Emplacement idéal sur 7e avenue, à 10 minutes de times square,5e avenue, et juste à côté de penn station qui dessrt quasiment tout manhattan et nyc en général.quartier sûr pour se promener même le soir
bref, si vous hésitez entre 2 hôtels, choisissez celui ci, vous ne ser pas déçu!!!!j'en suis sur!!
l seul bémo pas de petit dej inclus, qu'on oublie vite quand on voit lq chambre et qu'on y prend ses quartiers et des starbucks et coffee shop à tous les coins de rue (sinon plateau de courtoisie dans la chambre avec thé et café)

name: The Strand Hotel
title: “Good location”
text: Our room had a beautiful view of the Empire State Building and the roof top bar was beautiful. The location of the hotel is a great home base for sightseeing - kind of in the middle of everything. Great area for walking and exploring the city. The rooms were clean and efficient. The desk staff was helpful, although did recommend to us 2 different restraunts to try that had gone out of business. Breakfast at the hotel was not a very good value, but there is a starbucks and an au bon pain a block away. Overall a decent experience.

name: The Lucerne Hotel
title: “We've found our home away from home in NYC”
text:
We visit our son attending Columbia U. in NYC from time to time, and the Lucerne has become our hotel of choice. Great service, quiet, comfortable rooms, vibrant-convenient neighbourhood. We parked 3 blocks away for $29.00 a day.
We took the subway to Brooklyn, South Street Seaport and the west village, plus cabbed elsewhere for under 15 bucks, all from within steps of the hotel.
2 tips; bring a corkscrew/bottle opener and something to pour water into the coffee maker in your room. It doesn't have a carafe, and the mugs aren't easy to handle.
We'll definitely be back!

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “A Perfect 25th Anniversary Thanks to the Warwick!”
text:
My husband and I decided to celebrate our 25th Wedding Anniversary in NYC. After much research, we decided to stay at the Warwick Hotel. We obtained great phone service and email service response when arranging and a very good rate directly with the Warwick. Upon arrival late in the evening, they were very warm and welcoming, even though it was after midnight. Then they surprised us by upgrading us to an Executive Room. The room was beautiful; so wonderfully large, quiet and impressive. A nice note and plate of delicious cookies enhanced the welcome.
This started our vacation on a very positive note and continued all the way until we left. The location is perfect. Noise did not even bother us. We had the air conditioning on because of the hot weather, and being from San Francisco, we slept so well and it was very quiet for us City folks! It was quieter than our home!
Everyone greeted us, Randolph's Bar was warm and cozy and great drinks. NYC and the Warwick gave us a trip to always remember!
Note to the Warwick: May want to change the music in Randolph's to some of the famous jazz from NYC for an even more inviting atmosphere.
We cannot wait to return and we will ALWAYS stay at the Warwick! Thank you so very much!

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “Fine hotel for NYC”
text:
Stayed here for a few nights due a conference being held at the hotel. Overall, the hotel was nice but a bit worn as others have commented. Check in was fine and workers appeared to be nice but did not have much interaction with them either.
Fitness room was very small - just a few machines. Of course, it is an older hotel in NYC so that is to be expected. 
It is in a good location and within walking distance to many sights. I think this hotel would be fine for most tourist purposes but would not pay an extreme amount for it.

name: Four Seasons Hotel New York
title: “Outstanding Hotel, great location”
text: Four Seasons is outstanding world-class hotel, luxury amenities, excellent service, personalized approach to any client's needs. Exceeded our expectations. Purchased stay from SOPRIZ.com - great booking and accomodation experience.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Nice, but noisy”
text:
Great location, just across Madison Square Garden and walking distance to almost everything. Friendly staff, but Wi-Fi costs 15$ per day.
Bring your earplugs, cars are honkin all night in the city that never sleeps, and there is also a Firestation nearby.
But great location, Penn Station is just across the street, no need for taxi or subway when coming or leaving by train!!

name: Royalton New York
title: “Wonderful Hotel - terrible staff”
text: I stayed at the Royalton hotel for 5 nights.the hotel itself is wonderful - I had a King delux room which was lovely - very spacious, clean and crisp the only downside being I chose a city view over an option to have a bath which I regretted as the view isnt particularly great. The only downside with the room was there are no tea and coffee making machines which is normal for upmarket hotels - it just annoys me because I dont want to have to pay through the roof for a cup of tea. The reason I have only given this hotel a 3 star is due to the staff - they weren't rude as such just acting like they couldnt care less, there were problems with the internet throughout the stay, which on the first 2 occasions the staff refused to acknowledge on the 3rd day we finally did get some help but you also have to pay per 15 minutes which is not great when you need to access quite a lot of emails. The main problem with this hotel was the doorstaff - I found them very friendly on arrival and leaving when tips were expected but during my stay they were unbelievably rude slouching on the railings talking to each other and ignoring the guests - not bothering to even break the conversation when you arrived back never mind opening the door for you! its a real shame because I would give the hotel a 4 possibly 5 star but the staff really lets it down.

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “I LOVED the Warwich NYC”
text:
We came to NYC on Dec 11/12 2006 and stayed at the Warwick. I have to say that I was impressed. The room was very nice, bed very comfortable. The staff were all so very nice. I loved the doorman...I thought he was the man!!! 
The only complaint was that in December the temp outside was like 50 degrees and even with the heat off in the hotel room it was very hot. But we just cracked the window and all was fine. 
The Warwick is located close to everything we wanted to see. It is walking distance to Rockefeller Square, Radio City, St. Patrics Catherdral and also to Time Square. We had a fabulouse time in NYC and staying at the Warwick NYC contributed to it. We will definetly stay there again!!

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Very good hotel”
text: its a five star hotel in the heart of Manhattan.Everything is walking distance from there.its strange that the reception is on the 8 floor ,but its no problem.the breakfast is ok but there are many deli's around.the revolving restaurant on 44 floor is nice for a panoramic but no gourmet dinner.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Fantastic Christmas time vacation”
text: This hotel experience was first rate starting with the wonderful front desk service. Bellman, concierge and housekeeping were all helpful and made our four night experience one to remember. Walk to any theatre, subway two blocks, security more than adequate. We felt completely safe and would return if we ever have the opportunity. Location was perfect for anything we wanted to do in NYC

name: The Strand Hotel
title: “Great hotel, excellent value for money, would definitely recommend it!”
text: We booked the Strand for a special celebratory 60th birthday visit to New York and were very impressed. It's ideally situated - very close to Empire State Building etc. Rooms were small but very clean, comfortable and well furnished - the most comfortable hotel bed I think I've ever slept in!
