Breakfast being included was a bonus and it was very good. Some Trip Advisor reviews complained about polystyrene cups but this was a very minor issue - lids were supplied for take-out too if required! The rooftop bar on the 21st floor was very expensive but well worth a visit at least once for the spectacular views of the Empire State Building lit up at night. All in all, a fantastic trip and we would recommend the Strand Hotel to anyone visiting New York.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Would Never Recommend This Hotel!”
text: Our stay was a prepaid gift, but the desk people required a credit card from us on arrival, "for incidentals." Of course, our credit card was billed for the entire amount -- a discounted rate that, in our fairly sophisticated opinion, was too high anyway. We and our benefactor had to make many calls and provide several copies of the prepaid booking, to try and straighten the situation out, and after a week, we think we may be making progress. Unlike some reviewers, we found only some of the staff to be rude. Most of the people we have dealt with have just been clueless. No one seems empowered to make a customer-oriented decision. After an average room, average service, and a very substandard billing experience, we would advise other travelers to go elsewhere.

name: The Benjamin
title: “The Most Delightful Hotel in New York”
text:
I have been staying at this hotel over a period of 8 years and quite honestly this hotel cannot be faulted for anything:
- Rooms are delightful and comfortable
- Location 50th and Lexington cannot be bettered
- The staff is always delightful and happy to assist in anyway possible.
This hotel is a great place to find peace and quiet in a city that does not sleep.

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Hotel in New York”
text: We really enjoyed our stay here...they upgraded our room and sent us wine and cheese! Great Service!

name: Royalton New York
title: “Royalton New York - Brilliant!”
text:
We stayed at the Royalton for a few nights at the begining of Feb
We were both impressed with the hotel, the location is excellent, literally a short walk from Times Square! Great place to explore the city from.
The room we stayed in was on the 14th floor, it was clean, roomy and comfy. Even had a balcony although it was a tad cold to go out there. Bed was comfortable but the pillows could have been a bit firmer. 
Mini bar is expensive (paid around $8 for a bottle of water!) but then all mini bars.
Bathroom was nice and clean and has the best shower! 
The lobby area has a lovely bar, and the restaurant is very good, steak was lovely! 
The staff were always friendly and helpful, even at 5am when we were checking out there was someone to help us with our bags and help us get a taxi.
Would definately stay here again

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Great Hotel - Great Location - Great Room”
text:
My wife and i stayed in the Westin for 3 nights at the end of May.
Arrived into Newark and took the bus into the Port Authority bus terminal, this was cheap and easy to do and very very close to the Westin, so was a breeze. We arrived early and the room was not ready, but we expected this and the staff immediately offered to take our bags until 3pm when the room would be ready, we came back about 3:30 and the room was available.
What a room! Booked a corner room, we were placed on the 39th floor and had amazing views of the Empire State building along one side and up and down the Hudson on the other. Room was clean and fresh and all the fittings were in perfect working order. nice flat screen TV for when we were relaxing. 
The only tiny problem we had was our fridge locking itself on our last day, but a quick phonecall to reception had a man at our door in under 5 minutes who fixed this promptly. 
Check in/out was quick and easy, the business centre offers free use of the internet for checking in for flights, which was very very useful.
When asking for advice from the hotel staff they were all friendly and helpful often finding us a map and often pointing out discounts that are available.
We never used the hotel restaurant, as we ate out all the time and looking at the prices i am glad we did.
The location is fantastic, very close to the action of Times Square and quite central for all the shopping and sight seeing.
In conclusion i would highly recommend a corner room at the Westin, we have already promised ourselves we will stay there when we go back next year (hopefully).

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Decent price for upscale good accommodations”
text: Rates can vary considerable so check for different dates. Check-in can be a little chaotic.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Great Hotel, Great Price, Friendly Staff...”
text:
...Perfect Location, WONDERFUL MEMORIES MADE!
After days and days of searching (and reading reviews) for the "perfect place" for us to stay in NYC we truly found it! The Salisbury is pretty much the perfect location to most anything one would want to see in the city.
We,my bestfriend and I celebrate our friendship each year with a trip to the city to "unravel" and catch-up. We already made plans to stay at the Salisbury next year.....hopefully in the same suite!!!! Ask for a 57th street view.....Hola Perros!!!
The 1 bedroom suite was HUGE!!!! I mean huge!! Yes,the bedding is a tad outdated and the bathroom was a little small but everything was exceptionally clean and if anything did need attention,it was taken care of. The hallways....hmmmm. I read peoples reviews of the old,odd smelling hallways? HELLO? If you base your hotel experience on the presentation of hallways,you've got a problem! 
The continental breakfast was perfect. Worth $3? Definitely!
The staff was friendly and accommodating (and funny). I'm sure we will never be forgotten!! Getting a cab is a breeze,luggage transfer went smooth but I must say the parking garage thingie was a little rough. It's only two blocks away but trying to park and get to the hotel at 4 PM. may cause a major check-in delay (traffic wise). Call ahead for directions to the parking garage then take a cab to the hotel to check-in.
Over all,we had a wonderful time at the Salisbury. Many wonderful memories were made ,it's a great place for the price and location and we look forward to staying there again next year!

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Loved it !”
text: This hotel is located in the heart of Times Square and everything is a stone throw away be it theatres, cinemas, and night life. Amazing location and fantastic spacious rooms. Highly recommend it.

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Tolle Lage und große Zimmer!”
text:
Für NYC verhältnismäßig große Zimmer, tolle Lage gegenüber MSG und Penn Station (der Flughafen-Shuttle ist daher sehr zu empfehlen). Der Verkehrslärm ist zu ertragen, NYC ist nun mal keine leise Stadt.
Zimmer, Ausstattung und Sauberkeit ist soweit in Ordnung.
Service war ok, Empfangsdamen zum Teil unfreundlich.
Statt W-Lan-Raten im Hotel zu zahlen, kann man besser in den umliegenden Cafés surfen.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Loved the Westin - Would recommend”
text:
I booked the Westin Hotel Times Square for 3 nights in the beginning of April 2008. I did not want to arrive in New York City to discover that the hotel was grotty so I booked a hotel that was slightly above the average price and I was not dissapointed.
The hotel was very smart and its location could not have been better - it was one block away from the centre of Times Square, with a subway station a 2 min walk away. 
The rooms were large, considering this is a New York hotel, and were very inviting. We had the most comftorable bed ever (which is a feature of the WestIn) and the shower had two heads for maximum use. We had the use of a flat screen TV and cable, alarm system etc. We stayed on the 22nd floor and the views were magnificent. We could even see New Jersey across the river! 
We did not sample any of the food seved within the Hotel as I considered it over priced, but all the restaurants you could possibly need were within easy walking distance - even a Ben and Jerrys parlour opposite the entrance. 
I would definately recommend this hotel to any fellow traveller - you will not be dissapointed!

name: Mandarin Oriental, New York
title: “Fantastic!!”
text: Absolutly fantastic hotel in perfect location,we stayed in a Deluxe Hudson River view on the 47 floor with view overlooking the west of Manhattan and Hudson River.We stayed for 4 nights and enjoyed every minute of our stay.The rooms are huge and the bathrooms amazing,huge marble shower with rainforest shower head certainly wakes you up in the morning.We used the gym and pool which were great and The Lobby Lounge is a great place for drinks and food with the most amazing view of Central Park.All the staff were very friendly and we can't wait to stay there again.

name: The Lucerne Hotel
title: “Fantastic”
text:
Had a corner room on the 7th floor - it was relatively quiet from street noise, and VERY quiet from hotel noise. Was there with two other women and my 7-month old daughter. Our room had 2 full-size beds. We all had plenty of room to spread out. 
The room was super clean and I felt comfortable having my baby crawling on the floor. I was even able to move the one bed to the window wall so that I could have her sleep with me without fear of her falling out of the bed - and the underneath of the bed was clean, too. There were two extra pillows in the closet to create a barrier for her at the bottom and top of the bed, too. The pillows were very comfortable, as was the bed. 
The bathroom was pretty tiny, not alot of counter space. But there was a desk right outside of the bathroom that we women were able to store our personal HABA supplies. And the shower was great - wonderful water pressure and plenty of hot water, even with late showers at 9am.
The hotel provided us with a complementary copy of Time Out. Very nice. The restaurant next door was fabulous for brunch. 
The location was fantastic. Upper west side is unpretentious. Two parks within 2-blocks for running and playing. Lots of shopping, museums, and great restaurants. 
We will definitely stay here again. Whether for business or pleasure.

name: Royalton New York
title: “For elegance in midtown you can't beat the Royalton”
text: The Royalton used to be my favorite NYC hotel. Recently I have become bored of midtown and tired of paying exorbitant rates so my center of gravity has shifted south to Soho; however for those wishing to stay in the heart of the city the luxury and romance of the Royalton is hard to beat. The location is perfect, especially for a show on Broadway or a nice meal at Victor's Cuban restaurant. The bar is just exquisite and the rooms are beautifully designed. Some even come with sunken tubs making this a great couples getaway. The Royalton can be very, very pricey so its important to book well in advance. If you are looking for a good deal then keep looking. If special is what you are after then you will definitely find it here.

name: The Strand Hotel
title: “Full of surprises, a great hotel in the heart of Manhattan”
text: We walked to the hotel from Grand Central and were greeted by the most friendly staff at the door and front desk. We were able to check in a one pm, and our 18th floor room was great! It was immaculate and comfortable. Great bedding, nice shower with stone tile floor. Nice big window with city view. No noise at all. Everyone we met up with, from housekeeping staff in the elevator, bar staff, front desk was exceptionally friendly. Really noticably different than a typical NYC hotel. We loved the rooftop bar with the glass ceiling that was opened in a section so that you felt outdoors on the roof. Really cool decor, fun drinks, nice people. Amazing view of the Empire State Building. Worth visiting for a drink before heading out for the evening. There is some flexibility on the 2 drink minimum policy...The included breakfast was a nice surprise. Really good coffee...a nice assortment of food including baked goods, fresh fruit, cereal, etc. The location is great for walking...very central to many sites and easy walk to metro. We loved this place and will definitely go back.

name: The James New York
title: “Soho's finest!!!”
text: Simply put, there is no better stay in Soho than the James hotel!!! Perfectly located, Great food, Incredible views from every room I've tried (almost all)! Clean, New, Beautifully furnished rooms with great showers and bathrooms!! Warm and friendly staff waiting to help at any chance they get and did I mention PERFECTLY LOCATED!!!

name: Ritz-Carlton Battery Park
title: “Excellent Harbor Views”
text:
The rooms are spacious for a manhattan hotel and the bellhops were always helpful with bags or in tracking down taxis. The view of the Statue of Liberty and Battery Park from the "Harborview" rooms are excellent.
Do the "bed and breakfast" plan if you can. For $40/day extra, we received the breakfast buffet for two and free valet parking (ballpark $120/day value)? It's an excellent value. 
Our only disappointment was with the Spa. The treatments were decent, but it is not a full-service spa that you would expect of the Ritz. It's basically two treatment rooms next to the fitness center. No place to relax before or after a treatment (no sauna/steam room/pool/etc.). And it's not like the treatments were less expensive than if it were a full-service spa.

name: Four Seasons Hotel New York
title: “Ausgezeichnetes Hotel”
text:
Ich kann dieses Hotel wärmstens empfehlen. Alle Mitarbeiter sind freundlich und hilfsbereit, ohne aufdringlich zu wirken.
Der Zimmerservice ist schnell und die Qualität sehr ansprechend. 
Wir hatten ein Deluxe Zimmer für 4 Nächte gebucht und es war jeden Penny wert. Die Bäder sind geräumig und luxuriös eingerichtet. Das Zimmer, für New Yorker Verhältnisse, sehr groß und gepflegt. 
Die Lage ist sensationell und Gebäude und Lobby sehr geschmackvoll und sauber.
Unbedingt über dem 10. Stockwerk buchen, um dem Strassenlärm aus dem Weg zu gehen !
Für mich das beste Hotel in New York in dieser Preislage.
Ich komme wieder !

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Great location”
text:
We were on the 39th floor, in a corner room - great views of the river and surrounding buildings.
We couldn't have asked for a better location - it's 2 minutes on foot to the Port Authority, 4 minutes to Times Square and the Theatre District, 30 seconds to the nearest metro station and it's surrounded by loads of places to eat.
Do bring your laptop if you're planning on using a computer at all - the business center charges $0.50 per minute. I believe each room has free internet; ours did.
Room service is speedy and the staff is kind and efficient.
Our only complaints:
1. Unventilated bathroom: It didn't have a fan and the window was a showcase window so no air circulated and it smelled a bit fishy each time we came into the room. Suggestion: replace all bathroom windows with the click-open windows that are in the rooms.
2. Old bed: It was obvious that legions of guests had sat up in bed while eating or watching TV, so the section of the bed where one's shoulders and back rest was sunken and lumpy. It was rather difficult to get a good night's sleep on such an old bed - it's clear it stopped being a Heavenly bed years ago. Suggestion: lie on the beds regularly and replace them immediately if they don't meet Heavenly standards.

name: The Lucerne Hotel
title: “Perfect location, good service, great room”
text:
We started a three week holiday in the USA with a 2 night stay at the Lucerne Hotel in New York and I have to say I don't think we could have made a better choice. It started our holiday off perfectly.
I'm not sure what type of room other reviewers who weren't happy had, but ours was great. Plenty of space (three of us), comfortable beds, A/C working fine, clean and fresh and a decent sized bathroom.
The staff were very courteous and helpful. We arrived quite late and were hungry. They gave us a choice of nearby places to eat and good directions.
The only downside is the adjacent Restaurant. It is franchised and not associated with the hotel. We tried it once for breakfast but weren't impressed. Expensive, service was average and the food was OK but not worth the price. We ate out for the time we were there. I would thoroughly recommend Isabella'sRestaurant which is only a couple of blocks away (77th & Columbus).

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “Good outweighs the bad”
text: A friend and I stayed at The Warwick for 6 nights recently . Would stay there again even tho street noise was really bad, Room next to us played their TV really loud at 4:00 A.M. and the water was cut off to repair a leak while I was soaped up in the shower! That shows good things must have out-weighed the bad !!

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan-SoHo
title: “Hampton Inn Soho, prima hotel”
text: Prima hotel, dichtbij metro, drankjes in ontbijtruimte zijn gratis en heerlijk na een lange dag in de stad. Een uitstekend ontbijt; wel moeilijk om met plastic messen te snijden. Vriendelijk personeel! Kortom, we zouden het zo weer doen!

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “EXCELENTE UBICACIÓN”
text: El hotel esta en una excelente zona a 5 min caminando de CENTRAL PARK y a 10 min caminando de TIMES SQUARE, el camión turistico "Hop on hop off" pasa a solo 2 cuadras y tiene fácil acceso al metro si quieres ir a un lugar más lejano, como por ejemplo el estadio de los Yankees que esta a 25 min en metro, y a 30 min en metro para llegar a el muelle para abordar el barco a la isla de la estatua de la libertad, muy cerca de Broadway. Las habitaciones son amplias y las camas muy comodas, el hotel esta en un edificio bastante viejo, pero no por eso es malo, el elevado es antiguo y funcional, el desayuno es buffet, nada del otro mundo, tiene un bar que esta bien para tomar un par de tragos antes de salir en la noche. Como en todo Nueva York es un poco complicado tomar taxi por la zona en la que esta, es un hotel funcional si es tu primera visita a NY, recomendable para viajeros.

name: The Lucerne Hotel
title: “Nice Hotel in Quiet, Upper West Side”
text:
We stayed here 9-2-04 thru 9-6-04. I chose to stay here based on first, a great price I got from Hotel.com and then secondly, from the reviews I read here. 
This is a nice hotel, and a very beautiful exterior. It is in a very upscale, residential part of the Upper West Side of Manhattan. It is one block east of Broadway on 79th St. It is within walking distance to the Museum of Natural History, which my kids loved. The subway is one block away. We used the subway everywhere we went. (You can get a metro card for $7 day for unlimited rides.) The kids loved it. Depending on where you're going it can get confusing if you aren't farmiliar with the NY subway. But, much quicker and cheaper than a taxi. 
I expected a little bit nicer rooms based on the photos. The rooms reminded me of a Holiday Inn. Nothing special. We had two double beds, a desk and an armoire with the TV inside. Not much space to unpack your clothes for a family of 4. The bathroom was sufficient. It did have granite countertops, and tiled floor and walls. But, again I was not impressed. It was clean and the maid service was good. The only thing negative I can say was on our day to checkout the maid knocked and knocked and then tried to come in our room at 8:00am. Fortunately, we had the top latch locked. A little annoying.
They give you a door hanger to pick the USA today or the NY Times. Nice touch. Also, there was an umbrella in the closet, but we didn't need it. We had great weather. 
We were greeted by a very friendly bellman who assisted us to our room and gave some excellent restaurant suggestions for dinner. Speaking of restaurants, we never ate at a bad one. There are dozens with walking distance of the hotel. Not to mention the great Zaggots rated Ice cream shop across the street. I had the Key Lime, with graham cracker chunks... it was amazing, but it was also $5 for one scoop. 
The concierge was the most impressive part of the hotel. He was always available in the lobby or by phone. He made numerous restaurant recommendations, subway suggestions, etc. For example; The US Open was sold out for the day we wanted to attend but he quickly found out information about a screening being held at Rockefeller center on a 40 foot screen with stadium seating and tennis courts with free kid activities. It was even better than going to the ArthurAshe Staduim and fighting the crowds and long subway rides out to Queens. He was a crutial part of our trip and very knowledgable.
We loved New York! However, when we go back we plan to stay in Time Square, just to be closer to everything. (We spent a lot of time riding the subway to and from Time Square). The hotel was nice enough that I can't say anything bad. But, I would much rather be closer to the points of interest. But, that's just my personal opinion. 
If you want a nice hotel in a quiet part of town with lots of nice restaurants with patio seating, you'll enjoy The Lucerne. If you're looking for more bright lights, people watching and being in the middle of the madness, you will be bored here.

name: Royalton New York
title: “Mamma Mia!!!”
text:
Spent a fantastic four nights in the Royalton on a surprise trip for my wife's birthday.
Used the services of the hotel concierge prior to arrival to make some special arrangements such as a birthday cake to our room etc., they couldn't have been more helpful.
A couple of pointers: -
1. The lighting is dim, but all lights have almost invisible dimmer switches on the side giving more than enough light when fully on!
2. The breakfast vouchers (if purchased) don't make it clear what they cover, but it turns out you can have just about anything from the menu, just ask!!!
The location is excellent, but don't choose this hotel if you are going to complain about the bar prices, it's New York, spend the money and have some fun.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Bra beliggenhet,gammelt hotell”
text: Hotellet har svært bra beliggenhet. Store familierom med sengeplass til 6. Rommet er rent og ryddig, men er gammelt. Ikke gratis trådløst nett. Hotellet tar 9 $ pr person for en ok frokost.dette burde vært gratis.

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “Une Merveille...”
text:
Excellent!!! je conseille vraiment cet Hôtel !!! 
Emplacement idéal.. Times square, Central Park.. tout a proximité.. 
j'ai adoré l la déco, nous avions réellement l'impression d’être dans un film américain... 
seul petit bémol: l'accueil pas terrible.. .
les chambres sont spacieuses et confortables... 
Ma prochaine escapade New-yorkaise nous retournerons au Warwick...

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Zero Service, Tiny rooms”
text:
I'll keep this brief, even though I would like to write paragraphs about how bad this hotel is.
- No Service (selected the so called "service express" button and no one answered even after a combined 60 rings). This continued throughout stay.
- took 1 hour for bags to be delivered to room
- small rooms
- no upgrade for platinum members 
- poor views
- dirty rooms with peeling wallpaper, markings on walls, cheap furniture, aging matresses.
- Concierge (all) are useless
My suggestion, stay at the Hilton across the street. That's where the rest of my family stayed and they had much larger, cleaner, rooms with MUCH better views. Service was complete opposite of my experience (very friendly and helpful).

name: Cassa Hotel & Residences
title: “Muito bom custo benefício”
text:
Hotel muito bacana, situado próximo a Times Square, mas sem a bagunça da Times... próximo ao metrô, Fifth Avenue. 
O hotel é limpo, organizado e com decoração moderna e contemporânea. Vale a pena, para quem busca algo próximo a Times Square, mas não gosta da bagunça da praça..

name: Affinia Manhattan
title: “Excellent Choice!”
text: We just returned from a lovely weekend in NYC. One of the most pleasant discoveries was the Southgate Tower Suite Hotel. After reading horror stories about other NYC hotels, we chose the Southgate because the ratings and reviews were all very favorable, and the rates were affordable. We were not disappointed!! Starting with the courteous doorman; the friendly, lovely young lady at the front desk; a very clean, spacious suite with a nice view; a relaxing, delicious dinner at the Niles Restaurant; and, a quick, efficient checkout with arrangements made for a towncar to take us to the airport......it was a wonderful experience!!! We definitely look forward to staying there again.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “They have the Westin basics down, but need help with service.”
text:
Thanksgiving week brought me to Westin New York Times Square. This was my first visit after years of staying at the Doubletree Times Square for work. Neither hotel is anything to write home about, but for the price and checking that $500 a night for “average” hotels was not uncommon during Thanksgiving, they’re not horrible.
Overall I sum up my Westin stay as good. This location has the basic Westin stuff down. Heavenly bed and heavenly bath are fine. Where they lack is in service. Now to their credit, being the Thanksgiving holiday, I’m not sure if they were on limited or secondary staff. Regardless it should not take the operator 12-15 rings to answer the telephone. Four co-workers reported the same delays in answering. For seemingly simple requests, comparing stories, not all of our calls were placed at what would be peak check-in and check-out times.
I was extremely displeased with the speed of their so-called “high speed” internet service. The connection was expensive, and so slow that they ended up crediting me as it’s less than dial-up speed was un-usable. Unfortunately due to being booked, they could not move me to another room.
The bedding and bath products were quite nice, as Westin has become known for. Yet, I found my room not to be stocked with items such as a laundry bag, robe and extra toilet paper. My co-workers alerted me to this, but the hotel does not supply shower gel. Though they did have bath bars.
In-room television was above and beyond with a 42” LCD HDTV, and unlike most hotels that just put in an LCD screen with “stretch-o-vision” SD programming, the hotel offers 15 digital channels. Including all of the local NYC network affiliates (excluding WNBC), ESPN and ESPN 2, Universal, and I believe Discovery or National Geographic HD. The hotel services/ppv preview channel was in HD, yet the film previews were SD stretched.
Upon parking your car with the hotel Valet, they warn you to give an estimated 30 minutes for them to have your car ready for you. Both times I called for my car they had it waiting for me in 12 and 15 minutes respectively. As of 11/07 cost for valet parking was $48 + $3.49 sales tax.
The hotel had great access to 42nd Street Times Square subway station, the main hotel entrance is on 43rd Street at 8th Avenue, yet they also have a 42nd Street entrance by going to the second level on the attached movie theater and Starbucks.
Toilet noises weren’t bother some, or noticeable until I read fellow TripAdvisors’ comments about the noise. Not until then did I begin to notice, and in my 12th floor room it was not a bother.
At check-in two staff members recommended the Brooklyn Diner on 43rd Street in Times Square for breakfast, and then the West Way Diner as an alternative on 9th Avenue north of 43rd St. After waiting 15 minutes for a seat in the Brooklyn Diner, and due to a limited menu, I left. I found the West Way to have a very large menu, with quick service and decent prices for NYC. A great recommendation from Westin staff.
Upon arriving at home, and checking my credit card statement, I noticed they double charged me for parking on the last day. Had to call accounting during their normal office hours, but they did correct the problem.

name: Smyth Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Merveilleux”
text:
Nous avons passé un incroyable séjour, l'emplacement étant idéal pour visiter la ville, les chambres très confortables et biens agencés, le service impécable.
Nous avons aussi apprécier les serveurs du restaurant ainsi que la qualité des menus proposés.
Salle de sport pratique et très propre.
Remerciement tout particulier au directeur qui en plus d'être sympatique et compétent, parle couramment français.
Je recommande fortement cet hôtel et son personnel.

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Great rooms for families with children.”
text:
We reserved a "family suite" which includes a bedroom with a queen bed and another room with two double beds - very comfortable for myself, my husband, and our two teenage children. At most hotels in New York, I would have had to reserve two rooms for our crew. Needless to say, this saved us a lot of money. The room was clean, the beds were comfortable, the bedroom was much quieter at night than I had expected. Street noise on the 7th floor wasn't bad for the room with double beds. The AC was a bit noisy, but we all slept well.
A continental breakfast with lots of choices was included in the room rate. Also Wifi.The hotel restaurant had very good food. The rooftop bar had a fantastic view of the Empire State Building a block away. It was too hot for us the week we were in NYC, but looked nice.
The service we received was pleasant and efficient. The concierge was very helpful. Food at the hotel restaurant was very good. Location was easy for Broadway plays, shopping, restaurants. Lots of options within walking distance, and easy access to quite a few subway lines.
We'd definitely stay at the Metro again.

name: Ritz-Carlton Battery Park
title: “Would stay here again”
text:
My husband and I traveled here with our ten year old son.
Yes, you sacrifice costly taxi fares because of its remote location from the usual tourist sites, but, in return, you get great views!
Loved the hotel for its: views of the Statue of Liberty and Battery Park, concierge, room size, atmosphere, service and bars
The concierge recommended restaurants that perfectly fit our desires; we wanted food of various cuisines, and the restaurant needed to be child-friendly. No, they weren't cheap, but we felt no buyer's remorse, for the the food was always delicious, and our child was always welcomed warmly.
The bar at the top of the hotel served the best snacks and margaritas! So that they can enjoy the great view, children may enter at 4:00 pm.

name: The Benjamin
title: “Great Stay”
text:
We had a great stay at the Benjamin. We went for the one bedroom suite. 
Good size room(s)...package included spa discount and breakfast or parking, booked direct on hotel website. Big fan of the pillow menu...we chose three different ones...very relaxing quite room that was a good spot after dinner and a show...there is no lobby but I was okay with that we generally don't sit around the lobby of a hotel...staff was very friendly and helpful. I would highly recommend the weekend package, all in all a great time.

name: The Benjamin
title: “The Benjamin Hotel”
text:
O Hotel é muito bem localizado, quartos generosos, uma mini cozinha muito pratica, funcionários no limite da cordialidade americana, a não ser um ou outro mais simpático.
Deixa a desejar o tamanho da toalha que é muito pequena para um Hotel desse padrão e aqualidade do chuveiro, baixo, sem pressão e de dificl acesso.Rou pa de cama muito boa e bom espaço para guradar malas e compras.

name: Cassa Hotel & Residences
title: “NON SI PUO' CHIEDERE DI PIU'!!”
text:
Fantastico hotel consigliato da un amico..
Struttura nuovissima e confortevole, noi alloggiavamo al 25esimo piano ed il letto era comodissimo ed il bagno con una doccia ampissima.. non manca nulla e non si puo' chiedere di piu' per un soggiorno a new york.
posizione strategica a 5 minuti da time square e starbucks per la colazione difronte all'hotel..
unica nota dolente e' che non ce' wi fi gratuito in camera ma lo si deve pagare.
ed il condizionatore un po' rumoroso, ma noi lo spengevamo dal generale ed il silenzio era servito.. lo consiglio a tutti

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Absolutely enormous impersonal factory hotel”
text:
Impersonal factory hotel: one number checks in, another checks out. Rooms were good-sized but cookie cutter, every room exactly the same. Waiting for elevators felt like being in Grand Central Station: hordes of people milling around. Elevators were pre-programmed to take you to your floor but little or no explanatory signs so lots of confusion. Being in the lobbies (8th and 1st floor) was absolutely frenzied, literally hundreds, perhaps thousands, of people coming and going, with waits for everything. The rooms were set up in a circle, so that noise and smells from bars and restaurants was ever-present. There was never any sense of respite or any peace whatsoever. 
Linens were second-rate, towels were fifth-rate. 
Good gym, but no pool or locker room facilities.
Housekeepers extremely nice. Everyone else (waitresses, check-in staff, theater desk people) looked exhausted and frazzled. 
Location can't be beat if you want to be on Broadway. 
We will not go back. Even with a bargain rate, this is no place we want to return to. Ever.

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Nothing personal”
text: It's very impressive: the 48th floor lounge, the view from the amazing fitness center, and the location – you leave the hotel for your Broadway show 5 minutes before it starts... Our room (regular rate) was surprisingly large with beautiful view of the square. Personally, I'd stay in other parts of town, but if you like being around Times Square and to feel like you are one among thousands of hotel guests – this is a good hotel. Bare in mind you'll be staying at a landmark - where lots of outside visitors come to hang out

name: Cassa Hotel & Residences
title: “Consigliato”
text: Hotel in ottima posizione, time square a 100 mt, metro a 3 minuti a piedi, starbucks per colazione di fronte, posizione strategica per muoversi per turismo. Essendo stato più volte in hotel a new york ritengo che la posizione sia molto importante e l hotel cassa e' veramente strategico. Ingresso in hall piccola ma sempre presente con almeno 3 persone disponibili, informali e cortesi, camera non troppo grande ma quella con un piccolo upgrade che si può concordare si ottiene un letto più comodo. Unico difetto assenza di armadio comodo pertanto bisogna un Po arrangiarsi se il soggiorno e' lungo, ma nel nostro caso per 5 giorni va bene. Attenzione. In camera si paga tutto, dunque non fatevi prendere dal desiderio di portarvi a casa anche solo il kit da barba perche' all arrivo lasciate un deposito consistente di circa 300 dollari che viene poi non incassato se nn prendete extra. Internet funziona molto bene peccato che sia a pagamento per un importo giornaliero di 15 dollari, ma anche questo e' accettabile. Pulizia ottima, camera silenziosa, ascensore sempre disponibile. Consiglio vivamente questo hotel.

name: The Benjamin
title: “Muy bien,”
text: La verdad es que las cosas no empezaron bien en el check in tuvimos un problema,hice la reserva por internet especificando que necesitaba una cama supletoria para el nene,no lo tenían previsto,tampoco es de recibo que quieran cobrarte un suplemento cuando te han confirmado la reserva con la roller bed de marras,eran 10$ x noche,proteste y pedí hablar con el director y la verdad que con mi mal ingles y el poco español que hablaba el figura,llegamos a un acuerdo rápido, pagaba los 10$ extra x noche por la camita pero a cambio reconociendo el error que habían cometido al confirmarme la reserva, me dieron un upgrade,la habitación era más grande con un saloncito y más pijadas, incluida una carta de almohadas sin ningún coste adicional,la primera vez en mi vida que me dan a elegir entre almohadas con plumas de ganso, de copos de latex, recubiertos a su vez por plumón,una almohada de avestruz,almohadas cervicales de yo que se que pollo,vamos que las utilice todas,bandeja de fruta y chocolates de bienvenida,champagne la ultima noche,el avión de vuelta salía tarde y tampoco me cobraron el late check out,nos trataron realmente bien.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Luxury loved it”
text:
Fabulous place, rooms, location & views. Just off Times square. Stayed there for one night on a business trip. The modern, spacious and airy entrance set the tone for the hotel. The staff were courteous and my business companion was lucky enough to be upgraded to a suite free of charge. There was a mistake in the booking but this was resolved immediately. The room I stayed in was on the 16th floor couldn’t fault it for a minute, everything was spotless and seemed new. The type of room that feels you were the first person to ever stay in it. Fantastic views over the Hudson river so much so I slept with the curtains open so I could wake up to the view.
Unfortunately cannot comment on food or breakfast as had to leave early. 
Would love to come back here for a few days.

name: Ritz-Carlton Battery Park
title: “Loved it!”
text: My mom, sister and I stayed at this facility the first weekend in November. Suprisingly, it was the best deal we could find on a room that was big enough for us to share (weekend rate of $475 a night). Upon check-in, I was told that we had been upgraded to a room with a view of the Statue of Liberty - I didn't even have to ask. The view was amazing, especially at night when the Statue and bridge are lit up. The room was decent sized, and we had two double beds that were very comfortable. The bathroom, as mentioned in other reviews, was very large by NYC standards -separate tub, shower and toilet room - all in marble. Very nice! We used the concierge several times, and they really went above and beyond and their recommendations for restaurants were right on. The excercise facility is on the top floor and is a good size with numerous machines and free weights (and towels and bottled water are provided). We found the staff to be very friendly, though I wouldn't say I was completely amazed by the level of customer service - my sister and mom made comments that for such a high-caliber hotel, they had to open their own doors and were ignored by the staff a few times. My only other negative was, as a tourist, this location is a bit remote (for the areas we were interested in going to). You do have the Staute of Liberty, Ellis Island and Ground Zero within walking distance. We did, however, miss a dinner reservation before a show because we underestimated how long it was going to take to drive to LIttle Italy for dinner and then down to Broadway for our show. It seems like this location would almost be more suitable for business travelers. All in all, though, you can take a subway anywhere in New York, and I would stay at this faciltiy again. I was also very happy with the brisk fall weather and the beautiful trees with their changing leaves - a carriage ride through Central Park was a highlight of our trip - beautiful! Definitely a nice time of year to visit!

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Hotel Salisbury New York”
text: L'hôtel est trés bien situé (proche de Central Park et de Times Square), les chambres sont spacieuses mais pas trés modernes. Comme il y a des travaux juste à côté de l'hôtel (rénovation d'un immeuble), c'est assez bruyant sauf si vous demandez une chambre avec vue sur la cour. (je vous le conseille vivement).Le petit- déjeuner servi à l'hôtel est d'un trés bon rapport qualité-prix. Globalement bon hôtel, pratique pour une famille.

name: The Benjamin
title: “hotellet ligger central”
text: vi fik et værelse med en meget store aircondition uden foran vores vindue og var det samme storrelse som vinduet og det larmede meget.så fik vi en anden efter 2 dage og det var det samme men nu fra nabohotellet,og nar du har kun 7 dage og skal flutte 2 gange er lidt for meget ,så det var meget skuffende

name: Hotel Metro
title: “A True Gem!”
text: During our stay in NYC, the weather was mostly cold and sometimes rainy, but the Hotel Metro provided a very warm and inviting haven for us. My 5-year-old felt right at home with the staff, and said her favorite thing to do was relax in the lobby with a cup of (decaf) coffee! We had a family room and a king room, and they were fabulous. This is such a charming hotel, and the rooftop terrace was the best of all. We will definitely return.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Excellent location - but struth, no fridge!”
text:
Stayed there with my wife while on holiday from Australia.
Location excellent, beds excellent and bar very good.
Arrived at 3am and staff then were excellent and went out of their way to assist.
Not so good when leaving when a comment by the guy who appeared to be in charge of setting up for a conference in the business area on the 4th (?) floor - where we were directed by reception to be able to weigh our bags prior to going to JFK almost meant that this would be a negative review.
Memo to him..if you dont like a guest's attitude , say so in a manner that he cant hear you'next t'mem , or else you'll be in trouble!
And remember that people may be in a hurry to get to the airport!
But apart form this one guy who possibly was just having a bad day, the staff were excellent.
Only whinge I have was that coming from AustraliaIi dont think I have ever been to a hotel that did NOT have a fridge in the room but this one didn''t..
So if you wake up at 3am and want a cold glass of water or lemonade you can't just open the fridge door and take a quick gulp.
My first visit to New York, and if I return, despite there being no fridge, I'll stay there again.;

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Günstig, perfekt gelegen und geräumig!”
text:
Das Hotel ist zwar nicht mehr das Neueste, jedoch hat ein wirklich super Preis-Leistungsverhältnis und liegt zudem direkt an zwei U-Bahn-Stationen. Der CentralPark ist direkt um die Ecke und man kann ebenso locker zu Fuß zum Times-Square laufen. Die Zimmer sind sehr geräumig und die Betten USA-mäßig extrem bequem. WC und Bad sind groß, normal eingerichtet und sogar Flat-TVs sind vorhanden. Frühstücken braucht man nicht unbedingt im Hotel, da es in direkter Umgebung genügend Möglichkeiten zum Essen gibt. Immer gerne 
wieder!!

name: The Benjamin
title: “un charme très désuet”
text: hôtel à l'ambiance très années cinquante. Le service est approximatif (une suite réservée des semaines auparavant n'était pas disponible le soir de mon arrivée !) mais plein de bonne volonté. Localisation parfaite pour un week-end musées.

name: The Benjamin
title: “Veramente fantastico!!!”
text: Questo albergo è veramente straordinario,il personale è eccellente, io e mio marito abbiamo chiesto 2 volte il cambio stanza per motivi di rumore e ce l'hanno cambiato ogni volta. Una settimana prima della partenza, l'albergo t'invia il menu per i pillow, puoi scegliere 12 tipi diversi di cuscini (gratis), il letto grandissimo un King Size, e poi la locazione è stupenda è vicinissimo alla 5th av.! Lo consiglio a chi vuole spendere un pochino di più ma avere tante comodità! Alessandra

name: The Muse Hotel New York
title: “4th " end of summer"annual trip to NYC- The Muse”
text:
This is becoming an annual getaway for my 21 year old daughter before Uni starts. We have previously stayed at 4 other properties in NYC. The Royalton,The Belevedere,The Omni Berkshire.
I would compare The Muse to (quality) to The Royalton .
Last fall my husband and I visited a Kimpton property in Arizona Firfely and was so impressed with the service there that I inquired if they had any properties in NYC anticipating my August getaway !
So naturally I booked us into The Muse.
Location - If you want to be steps from Times Square it is !!!
Rooms- Wow nicest I have stayed in( NYC) Rm 1901 wonderful and has a tiny balcony that you can look over a part of the city . Very spacious for a city room. Bathroom (Royalton has that beat) ...but really lets not nit pic .It was fine just a bit dated. Ladies very adequate blow dryer nothing like getting one of those that take 2 hours to dry your hair.
Wine tasting -what a great idea koodoos to you Mr.Kimpton ! get there early to get a seat as seating is ltd.They served white(not very good)(but included),red -Merlot not bad , another red escapes me , and for summer they have added White & Red(really pink) Sangria.Met a few guests there to chat to.
We did not eat at Nicos but did meet a friend at the bar before venturing out for the night.
Since this was our 4th summer visiting we are very comfortable in the city. We purchase Metro passes 29 .00 for a weekly ,and that is our transport during our stay. We have always felt very safe and the subways are a perfect way to get around a very congested city.
The Staff - What can I say amazing well trained ,well versed ...they take care of you from the moment you arrive untill you leave.
I was celebrating a birthday while I was there and in my room upon arrival I found some cupcakes and champagne again the small touches imprint the customer !!!
Elevators never a probelm .
So wonderful time in NYC again !
thank-you Kimpton hotel - The Muse 
We will be back !

name: Warwick New York Hotel
title: “Très bien placé !”
text:
Nous avons séjourné une semaine au Warwick du 12 au 19 mars 2010.
Les + de l'Hôtel : sa situation proche du MOMA, de CENTRAL PARK, de TIMES SQUARE, du ROCKFELLER CENTER, de l'EMPIRE STATE BUILDING...et beaucoup d'autres lieux à découvrir à pied.
Autre +: la "petite structure", c'est un hôtel qui a du charme (style années 50).
La Chambre est également très agréable : grande, propre, raffinée.
Les moins : l'accueil assez froid et la clientèle pas très fun.

name: Hotel ZaZa Houston
title: “Houston Weekend Boys Trip!”
text:
The hotel was wonderful, staff helpful, the pool was great for relaxing and having a few cocktails.
One bad point, there is a strange smell in the lobby of the hotel.
Valet was quick and attentive, hotel bar is excellent and food is wonderful!

name: Ritz-Carlton Battery Park
title: “Just Fabulous!!!”
text: We stayed here to attend a wedding. When we arrived, the receptionist informed us that the type of room we reserved was overbooked. She upgraded our room to a suite!!! However, the suite was not ready. Instead of having us wait in the lobby, she personally escorted us to the hotel bar with a great view of the Statue of Liberty. When the room was ready, the receptionist came to get us, and told us the drinks we ordered were on the house. Needless to say we found the service in this hotel first rate. Moreover, the suite was exceptional.

name: The Michelangelo Hotel
title: “Oustanding hotel”
text: All aspects of this hotel are outstanding. Beautiful rooms, extremely helpful and polite staff, great location.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “Business trip became a pleasure”
text: This hotel is one of the best hotels I've ever been too. It's right on Times Square where the lights and the people come alive. NYC is one of my favorite places in the world so there was an enormous amount of pressure for this hotel to be amazing. Truth of the matter is, this hotel went above and beyond my expectations. It was beautiful, modern, amazing, had great service, ambiance was great, rooms were high class as well as high tech, and the location once again was amazing! Truly one of the best hotels!

name: The Michelangelo Hotel
title: “Good stay, prime NYC location”
text: Where do I start? I'm not a fan of grand, over the top style hotels with huge chandeliers, marble and somewhat dated look and feel, however that is just my personal preference and on reflection this hotel's decor is very pretty indeed. The room was absolutely fine. Again a little dated for my liking, but everything worked, furniture and bathrooms in a very good condition and bedding very comfortable indeed. The main thing here is the location, which is absolutely spot on. Within easy walking distance of all main tourist attractions in the area, plenty of good restaurants to chose from and generally very convenient. I said it before and I'll say it again: NYC hotels can be supremely expensive. The Michelangelo proved to be a good compromise between quality, good location and cost. Would definitely stay again.

name: The Muse Hotel New York
title: “Great short stay at this top-notch hotel”
text: Did some homework online to find a great place to stay in NYC in the heart of everything. We did well choosing The Muse. It was such a good location and the service and amenities exceeded our expectations. We had great personal help from Sarah as our concierge. Tours set and dinner arranged for us on short notice. Wine and strawberries welcomed us for the end of our 40th anniversary trip. We had morning coffee on the chaises on the balcony. Good trip and great finish to it at The Muse.

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan Chelsea
title: “Hampton Inn at it's best”
text: I travel a lot for both work and pleasure and am a Hilton Diamond member, so I'm inclined to look for Hilton properties while on the road. I also have to adhere to a budget. This hotel is a gem in it's own right. While the rooms are the normal "tiny" for NYC, the staff are always friendly and the location is great for subway access and restaurants and bars in Chelsea area. Even close to a PATH station. Much better option than mid-town. I stay here frequently when biz calls me to NYC.

name: Hotel ZaZa Houston
title: “Amazing Hotel. Great Location. Incredible Vibe.”
text:
We stayed at Hotel Zaza the first two nights after our wedding and it was an incredible experience!
The room was amazing with gorgeous views of Houston, a very comfortable bed, huge bathroom complete with a full sized bath tub and spacious shower. The overall style of the Zaza is elegant and eclectic, making for a fun and trendy atmosphere. 
While the staff took wonderful care of us, and took care of our every need once we were checked in, they did give us a bit of trouble initially booking our room. We wanted to stay just one night, but they were very hard to work with, insisting that we must stay two nights as they had some type of event going on that weekend. That never made complete sense to us as to why we couldn't just book one night, and even after meeting with the management, we could not get them to work with us. 
With our initial issues booking a room aside, our stay at Hotel Zaza was surreal, and we look forward to our next getaway.

name: Hotel Beacon
title: “petit appartement fonctionnel et agréable”
text:
A 8 mn à pied du métro, 10 mn de métro pour se rendre à Times Square, (ou bien pour 10 $ de taxi), ce petit appartement est super agréable : au 23ème étage avec vue dégagée sur l’Hudson et les toits new yorkais. Encore sur Broadway, entre Central Park et l’Hudson, il est bien insonorisée avec peu de dérangement par les sirènes de police 
La chambre de taille moyenne avec 2 lits d’1.20 m est très confortable et l’autre pièce : salon/salle à manger/kitchenette est séparée de la chambre par une porte. 
Cette 2me pièce est parfaite pour déjeuner ou diner d’une préparation rapide dans la kitchenette. 
Le canapé se transforme en lit d’une qualité correcte (selon notre adolescente de 15 ans et 1.70 cm) mais qui « grince » un peu. Le personnel de l’étage, les concierges ainsi que le « chasseur » du RC sont très serviables et réactifs.
Pas de petit déjeuner à l’hôtel mais un starbuck café à coté ; une restaurant avec de bons hamburgers juste en dessous. Juste en face de l’hôtel, un mini market pas très beau mais super bien achalandé avec des produits bien frais, différents pains et des plats préparés; je vous recommande le jus d’orange à la marque du magasin ; ce magasin semble tout le temps ouvert ! 
Dans la 2me quinzaine d’août 2011, le prix était de 230 € TTC (euros) par nuit pour ce petit appartement fonctionnel et agréable.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Clean, reliable, well located”
text: Not exactly in Time Square, which is a plus for me, closer to "Hell's Kitchen". Talked to a guy who had stayed there every other week for a year and was back on business. Staff are noticeably friendly.

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Very central, small rooms but adequate”
text: Very central to everything in New York, room was small with a small double bed but adequate. The rooms were very clean with room service daily. Breakfast buffet style, tea, coffee, bagels, toast etc., was very nice. Restaurant / bar opposite and adjacent to hotel both nice. Overall great hotel.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Not The Best But Very Adequate”
text: If you want the best Starwood Property in NYC, stay at the St. Regis or possible the W Times Square. I found the Westin to be just fine: larger than average rooms for NYC, nice bathrooms, good club lounge, very good fitness room, great location, friendly staff even in the hectic day leading up to New Year's Eve.

name: Ritz-Carlton Battery Park
title: “Sehr gutes Business Hotel”
text: Das Ritz Carlton ist ein sehr gutes Business Hotel an der Südspitze Manhattans in unmittelbarer Nähe zum Financial District. Zimmer bieten zum grössten Teil einen grossartigen Ausblick auf die Freiheitsstatue. Insgesamt ruhige Lage, erwartungsgemässe Zimmerausstattung. Exczellenter Meeting Venue! Service für ein Hotel dieser Preisklasse angemessen. Werde wiederkommen!

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “lovely hotel but rather small rooms”
text: Perfectly situated in bustling times square, this fun, safe hotel is well priced and full of helpful staff. The concierge is really helpful in arranging anything from theatre tickets to hair salon appointments. The door men were always looking out for my safety and easily arranged taxis.0 Even in the rain, they were there to make sure i didnt get too wet getting in to or out of taxis. Major subway lines are nearby, along with terrific restaurants. The bar scene is lively and the gift shop is unlike others at most hotels. not full of junky tourist items but really good things in case you are looking for a new item to wear out that night. My hotel room which overlooked the lights of times square was rahter small but not unlike other NYC hotels. good products int he bathrooms.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Excelente localização com café da manhã”
text:
Estivemos em NY por uma semana e o hotel se revelou uma ótima opção. Sua localização é excelente, próximo ao ponto mais nobre da 5a Avenida e bem ao lado do Central Park. Possui um bom café da manhã e o quarto é de bom tamanho com um closet muito bom para bagagem e compras!
O hotel é antigo, mas está bem conservado.
Retornaremos ao Salisbury com certeza!

name: The Muse Hotel New York
title: “Almost Perfect”
text:
There can be few better deals in Mid Town. The Muse won't be the cheapest hotel you'll find in NYC. It also won't be the biggest, nor will it have the most facilities. However, it's about ten seconds walk from Times Square making the location ideal - it's also a short walk from many major attractions. Beautifully appointed throughout, the rooms are spacious, well furnished and elegant without being overbearing. The bed was probably the most comfortable night's sleep I've ever had. 
Each day there was a free wine tasting in reception - a great start to the evening and perfect after a long day of sight seeing. 
The team at reception were helpful, attentive and knowledgeble - making the stay a genuine pleasure.
I will 100% stay here again when I go back to New York.

name: The Muse Hotel New York
title: “Fabulous boutique hotel”
text: Absolutely brilliant hotel, clean and tidy and very contemporary. Beautifully decorated rooms. Friendly staff and sooooooo close to times square but far enough from the hustle and bustle!!! Complimentary wine between 5 & 6 pm is a must too!!!! Couldn't recommend higher!!

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Great hotel, great location, excellent staff”
text:
Hotel location was great-- Subways and buses on all corners. The hotel is also connected to a parking garage. Plenty of restaurants, theaters, grocery, liquor and drug stores all within a couple of blocks. Times Square, Central Park, Top of the Rock and many other must see attractions all within walking distance. 
Room was very clean and, from what I understand, big for New York City standards. Windows opened slightly, which was great to experience the New York City sounds. However, when closed, we could not hear anything which was surprising being across the street from a fire department! (which also gave us a sense of security) The king adjustable firmness bed was excellent. The entire hotel was very clean. All staff, from housekeeping to management, were very friendly and helpful; always smiling and greeting you whether at the front door, in the elevator or in the hallways. This hotel definitely makes customer service a top priority.
The hotel always had a person dedicated to helping us with arranging or deciding on what to see, were to eat, etc.--also helped us to learn both the subway and bus systems. Being from a small town in Louisiana, this was appreciated more than anyone could imagine.
Upon checkout, we had a minor issue with the room rate which was corrected within a few minutes--and with a smile!
I would also like to state that I have never received personal emails from any hotel management staff either before and after my stay as I did from this hotel. It was very encouraging to receive an email before my stay asking if they could answer any questions or help with anything before we arrived. I did respond to the email with a few questions which were answered in a timely manner. I was not expecting this. I also received an email after the stay questioning whether or not everything was satisfactory.
Keeping in mind this is not a luxury hotel with outrageous amenities, I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone searching for a nice, clean hotel in a great location with very good customer service. We were not coming to Manhattan to stay in the hotel, however, must say that with this hotel it would not have been a problem! Also must say " The complimentary STRONG Starbucks coffee in the lobby every morning was a pleasant surprise for us Louisiana Women! This is something I have only experienced at the very expensive high end hotels.

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Perfect for NYC Weekend”
text: If you like the hustle and bustle of NYC and are in town for the typical tourist attractions (especially Broadway) you can't beat the location. This is a huge hotel, but they have resolved one of the annoying features of years gone by (slow elevator service). The hotel is right in the middle of Times Square and is very close to Rockefeller Center, several subway stops with access to other parts of the city, Fifth Avenue, and even Central Park. Depending on your room, you can sit right on your own sofa and watch the circus in Times Square from the comfort of your own room. The rooms are relatively large by NYC standards, and are nicely furnished.

name: Indigo Houston at the Galleria
title: “Got taken to houston for my bday last year”
text: i had so much fun the hotel was ready on time and already had drinks for us

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Second visit as good as the first”
text: I reviewed the HGI @ 8th and 48th after staying for a week in June. Was there again Sept. 14-16, and the stay was again very enjoyable. This trip, also ate in the hotel restaurant and was pleased with food and service. Ventured up the block and across the street to Donna Bell's bake shop on 49th. The baked goods here taste homemade, not mass-produced. My daughter was with me on this visit, and she agrees this is the best location in the city. The "Pride of Midtown" fire station down one block stays busy and their comings and goings are interesting to observe from the rooms with views of 8th ave.

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Great location, good value"”
text: Stayed here for three nights in feb 2009 - We found the location to be fantastic - very central. The room was also a good size, with plenty of space to move around. Even though there was a fairly busy street below us, we were not affected by noise. Breakfast was OK, if uninspiring. Food in the bar was reasonable, but there are any number of restaurants within 5 minutes walk of the hotel so there is no need to limit yourself. they did claim a "library" on the website, which turned out to be a bookshelf in the lounge which had CNN running continuously - not really ideal for reading. It was a bit cold for the roof top bar to open, but the view of the Empire State Building was impressive. We would certainly consider staying there again.

name: The Michelangelo Hotel
title: “Great Value Theatre District”
text:
We booked this for November 17-20 2011 at a rate on the average $200 less than other theatre district hotels and during a time most hotels were near booked.
The location is AAA. There is Duke's a few doors down.........an Eatzi's type convenience store open 24 hours that has everything from breakfast to dinner and well as drinks, snacks, latte's and smoothies.
The Bed was a Beautyrest top of the line and fluffy down pillows. While the room was not "large" it was larger than many NY hotels and probably average for most other hotels outside of NY City.
Elevators were fast. You could leave your room, go to Duke's for cookies or ice cream and be back in your room in no more than 10 minutes.
Our room was 520 and my only complaint was the eterge that housed the television. When you pull it out and turn it, you are looking at it from a slight angle from the bed as it is not in front of the bed. Nonetheless, we were able to watch a couple of movies.
We did not eat here. For the $300-$400 range, I would recommend this hotel highly.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Good place worth being off Time Square”
text: Convenient to theatre district, Hell's Kitchen and a good block away from Times Square (I tried to stay away from the more touristy places). Walked to the Javit's Center each day and really liked the lobby staff. The only thing I would improve would be asking the cleaning staff not to change the radio station each day! Will be back.

name: Courtyard New York Manhattan/Soho
title: “location location and location”
text: Small room, bad view, no breakfast, no minibar. Clean, good bed and sheets. Great location. Terrific breakfast just in steps nearby and great dinner in french vine bar Buvette at Groove st. Walking distance to Stomp show. <$10 taxi distance to Central Park. Limousine service to JFK $70 with tips.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “most awesome hotel in New York”
text:
This hotel more than lived up to its reputation! I travelled there with my daughter and a my close friend to celebrate my daughter's graduation (into grade 9)
This hotel was recommended to me by a friend - he indicated that it was a really 'cool' hotel and that my daughter would love it - very young and chic - and he was spot on...
Beautiful rooms - funky decor - very tasteful nothing was overlooked - attention was given to every little detail - even the carpets in the elevator were changed according to time of day...Good Morning...Good Afternoon...and Good Evening. The lobby was spectacular...I loved the 'smell' of this hotel - they actually used to sell the W' scent however it is no longer available...
The rooms were immaculately clean...spa products and the coolest bathroom and waterfall sink...really a treat! The most comfortable beds and pillows I have ever slept on all down and the linens were very soft...
The service was fantastic - friendly staff and very responsive to your needs
I was there during the hurricane ( more of a tropical storm) when all of NYC was shut down - noone could get in or out of the city and people were being held ransom to the rates that hotels were charging as they knew there was no where to go...
The W actually lowered their rates as I had to stay on for a couple more days then expected as my flight was cancelled - that is amazing!!!
I will definitely stay at the W again and highly recommend this anyone that wants something out of the ordinary in a hotel.
S

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Great Hotel, Nice Staff, Right in Times Square!”
text:
We loved this hotel, and will stay there every time we go to NYC. We searched & searched, and found this was our best value for a very clean & spacious room.
We have stayed in NYC before, and tried to pick hotels that cost less. They were tiny, filthy, broken fixtures, and generally gross. If you don't mind spending a little more, you will enjoy your trip a lot more staying in a hotel like the Marquis.
The staff greeted us every time we walked by, unlike most residents of this city. We loved it!

name: Courtyard New York Manhattan/Soho
title: “Cost effective shoice in Soho”
text: This hotel is a standard courtyard offering. Standard clean rooms and friendly service. The location is great, within a walking distance to Soho attractions and stores. Good restaurants nearby that concierge can help you with. A reasonable cab ride from Pennsylvania Station.

name: Hotel ZaZa Houston
title: “Fabulous Hotel!”
text:
Considering that I grew up in Houston, I never knew what a fabulous "vacation" I could have in my hometown, thanks to Hotel ZaZa. Since I live/work overseas, I wanted to book a nice hotel for my visit to Houston, and I was very lucky to have come across this hotel before it even opened. From the initial booking, the service was impeccable! Originally, I booked for a petit King, but due to change of plans I needed a bigger room. When I contacted the hotel through email, not only did they graciously oblige, they also gave it to me for the same rate as the petit King. 
From the moment we arrived, the staff was more than accommodating. They went above and beyond most 5 star hotels in getting us what we needed. The hotel was extremely stylish, the rooms beautiful, and the amenities were also a perfect touch. We loved the unique small pillows, the Bulgari bathroom sets, the 42" screen plasma TV! 
We spent the last day at the pool after we had already checked out, and the atmosphere and surroundings are like you are in some vacation hot spot. The pool is a bit small, but the surrounding more than makes up for it. The pool area also has private outdoor bungalows that are beautifully decorated.
My experience at Hotel ZaZa was one of my best stays in a hotel. 
The only thing I think they could work on is the service at their bar/lounge. The service was extremely slow. We must have waited about 30 minutes for someone to even come to our table. Other than that, I thought their overall staff and service were magnificent!

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Good hotel in busy location”
text:
Sometimes reviewers complain about the hectic of this location, but we like that. We already visit this hotel for 11 years. Of you do not like noise and crowds you should not go to The Times Square area but we like it and so this modern hotel with good and clean rooms is perfect for us. We also like that the top floor rooms recently got very good large showers.
We are priorityclub member IIHG.

name: Courtyard New York Manhattan/Soho
title: “Great Location”
text:
I booked this hotel based on rate an availability and was completely surprised to love the location. It was great being away from the hustle and bustle of Times Square and the convenience of the uncrowded subway station 1/2 a block away was fantastic. 
It was an easy walk to the Highline, Soho and Chelsea.
The staff at this hotel were extremely friendly and helpful. 
To avoid the expense of the hotel breakfast, make a left out of the hotel and head down Varick just under 2 blocks to Getting Hungry. Great selection and very reasonably priced but it is only open Monday-Friday.

name: Courtyard New York Manhattan/Soho
title: “An oasis in NYC”
text: We stayed there from 7/5-7/8/12. We were upgraded to a high floor room with a view (18th floor out of 20). The hotel is small (7 rooms/floor)... so very quiet. You need a room key to access your floor, a feature I liked. The only complaint is that the safe in our room did not close. Also the Starbucks was not open Saturday afternoon, so I had to go next door to Dunkin' Donuts for coffee (do NOT go there- very unfriendly staff). The hotel staff was very helpful with directions, restaurant reservations etc. The rooms were clean, the bathroom updated with large shower,and lots of pillows on the beds. The gym access was free, and very busy! After staying there first, and then going to another hotel in Times Square, we were ready to come back to the Marriott Soho.... We walked to the Ferry for the Ellis Island tour (about a 20-25 minute pleasant walk). The Soho shopping district is only a few blocks away from the hotel. I would definitely stay there again.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Excellent”
text: This hotel has it all. Location: close to theaters, restaurants, subway, businesses, and more. The staff is friendly and eager to serve. The rooms are clean and nicely appointed. Hilton Honors members are treated very well.

name: Hotel Metro
title: “great hotel, great location”
text: This was my second stay at this hotel and had an even better experience than 4 years ago. Staff was very helpful, had a good corner king room (910) that was actually pretty quiet as on the 9th floor. Excellent mid town location. I paid an average of 190 a night - closer to 161 a night but paid 300 for Jan 1st so raised the average price considerably. The attached bar and restaurant was very comfortable for a solo female.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “Girls' weekend!”
text: This was a perfect trip with the girls! Location was fantastic and the service top-notch. We had a "cool corner" room and loved the Bliss products! We can't wait to have another reunion soon.

name: Courtyard New York Manhattan/Soho
title: “Great location, friendly staff”
text: My two sisters and I stayed here for three nights. The rooms were clean and quiet. The front desk staff were very friendly and helpful in providing directions to various locations for us. The hotel is close to the entrance to the Holland Tunnel and so if you need to get to Newark Liberty Airport as we did, it was very convenient. We will definitely stay here again.

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “Clean hotel....great location”
text:
The hotel was clean, in a great location and the staff was friendly. I checked in a Friday evening and was upgraded with a beautiful view of the st. Patrick's cathedral (despite the scaffolding).
The room was spacious, comfortable and clean. The bellman, especially Cesar were warm and accommodating . The concierge were efficient and friendly. I stayed in midtown to be close to friends, but it is a great location for shopping, museums and broadway (see Edwin Drood in preview!) and a short cab or train ride to pretty much anything else in the city. There is a Starbucks across the street and a great bistro next door for grab and go. I didn't eat at the restaurant but may try if I stay again. All In all I would definitely consider this hotel in the future due to its cleanliness, staff professionalism and hotel location. I look forward to seeing the hotel when renovations are complete.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Nice hotel with great location!”
text: We stayed 3 nights at the Hilton Garden Inn, near Times Square. We had a corner room on the12th floor on 8th Avenue. We did not have a nice view, and the fire dept.was up the next block. (often heard sirens) The room was nice, but we've stayed at nicer furnished Hiltons. The staff was friendly. The concierge gentleman was very helpful. The French restaurant connected to the hotel (Pigalles) was good, but very pricey! We enjoyed being close to the subway station, NYC tour bus stops, and Times Square. I felt that $275 a night was comparable to othe hotels in Times Square. (but I was told by a friend that we pad too much for our room) Our next trip to NYC, we might try another hotel.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “If you need to stay by Times Square this is a safe bet”
text: Stayed at this hotel before an amazingly early morning wake-up call (3:30am!) and it was very comfortable. In the interest of full disclosure, I don't like staying in Times Square, but this hotel's proximity to my meeting made it the perfect choice. As a business traveler, I didn't spend much time here, but was happy to have a working business center to print up materials for my meeting. I also appreciated the security in the lobby at all hours. Rooms were comfortable and exactly what you'd expect from a Hilton.

name: The Michelangelo Hotel
title: “Great Hotel - Very Surprised and Overwhelmed”
text:
I wasn't expecting that much - thought this place was a tourist trap.
However, rooms were huge (for NYC) and the bathroom was great - water pressure was a bit blah though.
Got a great rate online- given the location and the room size, definitely recommend.

name: Courtyard New York Manhattan/Soho
title: “Nice hotel, but don't bring a car”
text:
This hotel is not really in Soho, but more on the southern fringe. It's at least a 3 block walk before you're in soho, but still not a bad location.
This hotel is relatively new and since we're Marriott members we gave it a try. We arrived via rental car and asked about parking. We were told at the front desk that valet parking was the easiest (duh) but there was a garage around the corner. No specifics of how far the garage was or how much it cost were offered. 
We made the mistake of using the valet. We were aware that there was no "in & out" parking, so we made it a point to take the car out only once per day. When we got our amex bill, we had been charged $240 for valet parking. Our stay was only for 3 nights, but we were charged $60 the night we arrived and $60 for the two following nights, then another $60 for the morning we left. These additional charges were not on our check out statement.
Lesson learned...next time we'll use the garage. Too bad the front desk doesn't warn patrons of this.
The rooms are small, but well appointed. The view south from our room was very nice. The Starbucks in the lobby offers a small but delicious selection of breakfasts. The Front Desk was polite,but I had to ask 3 times about a Hilton promotion offering Fandango movie tickets and a Courtyard voucher (seems they had run out.)
I'd recommend this hotel, but definitely warn others of the garage fees.

name: Hampton Inn Manhattan Chelsea
title: “gerne wieder”
text: mit einem kostenlosen, reichhaltigen frühstücksbuffet fängt der tag schon mal gut an , die lage des hotels ist ideal für sightseeing und shopping da verschiedene u-bahnlinien ganz in der nähe sind , freundliches personal , kostenloser internetzugang in der lobby

name: Conrad New York
title: “Modern and stylish”
text:
This new property had an opening sale earlier in the year, so I grabbed a "Double Deluxe" Suite for two nights. The interior of the hotel and the rooms are completely redone and very stylish. Rooms are reasonably large (especially for NYC!). Bathroom door is milk glass, but can't be locked. Everything works, and service is very good. 
I/we have stayed in Midtown a lot, so the location was a nice change of pace. We walked to the WTC, Battery Park etc., and there are several subway stations close. 
As HH Gold I got two continental breakfasts for free. On first morning the kids came along, and ate their most expensive Corn Flakes ever. Mind you, the breakfast tasted really good...
The letter containing the breakfast vouchers etc. also indicated that I had been upgraded to a better room. As this was clearly not the case, and the hotel seemed not to be full, I asked about this at the front desk. I was told our bedding was the best for us. Hmm, according to the website the "Superior" Suites are exactly the same, except they are in higher floors and have nicer views. The reply and inconsistency between the letter and reality was the only negative aspect of our stay.

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Great except for the beds and a weird noise....”
text:
I was hesitant to stay here because I thought it might be like a hostel.... But in fact it's very cool and trendy, clean and fun. Checking in at a kiosk is easy and makes sense, and the amenities are pretty good - breakfast was nice and the restaurant looked good though I didn't go.
The rooms are definitely small but very well designed - and let's face it most NYC rooms are small anyway! It's also really great value - the day I was here it was nearly 3 times cheaper than the nearest holiday inn express.
That said: the bed was pretty uncomfortable - the mattress is thin because it converts into a sofa. One night was ok but I wouldn't have wanted to stay longer. Also there was an intermittent high squealing noise coming from my bathroom vent during the night which was very irritating - I was already in bed so didn't want to change rooms but it wasn't very pleasant to wake up to (this was room 2312).
I'd definitely come back again for a short trip, but make sure there's no squealing before settling in!

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “Wonderful place”
text: I've stayed in this hotel a number of times, and it never disappoints. The rooms are not very spacious - but they are more than reasonable for a NYC hotel, and all are lovely, modern and very clean. Only one bad experience: a couple in the next room went out to party and then came back to fight, keeping us up for the better part of the night. But the front desk staff was very prompt in coming up to address the problem, which we very much appreciated. Rooms on the ends are the nicest; avoid rooms near the elevator shaft.

name: Fitzpatrick Grand Central Hotel
title: “LOVE LOVE LOVE!!!”
text: an amazing hotel with wonderful staff!!! so helpful - room was great also - really spacious and cool.. great location!! will def be back.. greg on front desk was amazing - he really did give us loads of good info, helped us each day and could not have done enough!! brilliant stay..

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Superb location”
text:
The hotel is located at Times Square - one of the major attractions. Once you get out of the room you are at Times Square which is well connected. You can spend your time till late night even after dinner at Times Square and don't have to bother to get back. The staff was quite efficient and helpful.
Quality of the breakfast can be improved

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “New York trip of lifetime”
text: we joined our parents at this hotel to help them celebrate significant birthdays for them both with a trip to NY.The hotel were aware of this and made their stay extra special.The hotel is excellent in terms of room standards,service levels,location and value for money..We have stayed in NY several times before in larger and smaller hotels but this is by far the best on so many levels.We will stay there again without a doubt.

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Fancy name but average stay”
text: Was expecting more space and quality fit out for the price. Stayed in a double queen room with lounge room and kitchenette over looking Chrysker Building. Beds were excellent and bath robes best I have ever had. Bathroom was spacious but not that generous in amenities. Housekeeping staff not consistent with restocking as we were there for over a week and more then 2 people in the room had to keep asking for more supplies.
