Location was in residential area and away from alot of noise. Not great for quick access to CBD.

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Does the Job not much more”
text:
Located on 10th Avenue in Midtown the Hotel was an okay distance from Times Square but not really convenient for other attractions such as Central Park, Top of th Rock or Bloomingdales. If you do not mind walking for a good 15- 30 minutes then the location is fine.
Clean rooms but very compact - do not visit New York if you like your own personal space! It was a little uncomfortable for us in the bedroom during Hurricane Sandy as we were locked up for 48 hours and did not have a lot of space to move about (had to sit on the bed all day), however I think this was really a one off experience and hopefully not everyone will be trapped inside! Staff okay, they are not really bothered about Customer Service or 'going the extra mile', this is a Hotel for convenience not luxury.
Hotel offers free WiFi and 4 computers for guests to use in the Reception area - very handy when looking up attractions, shows, restaurants, ticket prices etc. There is also a concierge there, however most of the time we found that it was closed (presume it is perhaps a 9-5 thing?).
Yotel provided food during Sandy, however we were very disappointed to be charged $18 each for lunch and $25 each for dinner, whilst we would have been happy to make a small contribution for the cost of the food we did feel that they were 'cashing in' on the situation. Was also disappointing that they offered no help or information on 'what to do' in a Hurricane or in the event of evacuation especially as most of their guests would never have been in a Hurricane before

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Great stay!”
text: I stayed at this hotel for a conference in January. Loved the bed, very comfy. The location is great, a lot of sights are walking distance, and the subways are very close. There's a Starbucks downstairs if you want a quick cheap breakfast too. The rates for in room internet access were quite high, but there was free wifi in the lobby, although that was advertised nowhere. The only drawback was being forced to watch CNN in the elevators.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “Outstanding service”
text: This hotel is so comfortable and is perfectly located in the middle of everything - Broadway, shopping, Central Park are all within walking distance. Then when you return to this peaceful oasis of a room you can get rejuvenated. The bar is also a very hopping place if you are interested in night life.

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Great Hotel”
text: First family holiday in New York and had a great stay at this hotel. We found all the staff we spoke to polite and friendly. The rooms were not the largest but we went to New York to see the sights not the inside of the hotel all day. The breakfast was a bonus and a good start to our day. The hotel was in a good location, near to the subway, Times Square, the ESB and Macys. We enjoyed dinner at the restaurant attached to the hotel and the place across from the hotel. Would stay in this hotel again.

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “Excellent”
text: Thank you, perfect choice for my sister and I to have our first mini holiday in New York; clean, modern apartments, really appreciated the mini kitchen - strange though to have coffee machine and no kettle - but saucepan OK for heating water for tea (the English have to have their tea!). Sorry that we couldn't have the two-bedded room we had requested, but the bed was so huge we didn't mind sharing. Good choice at breakfast thank you - really set us up for a day of heavy sight-seeing. Staff all very helpful - thank you Jamie and your colleagues on front desk. Had read about slow elevators - but this wasn't a problem we encountered. Excellent location, excellent accommodation - I hope we'll be back.

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Great Location”
text: My second visit to an Affinia hotel and again it was to be highly recommended. Big and spacious room, comfy beds and great views! It is in a great location too. You can walk to many major sights. Loads of local places to eat-our favourite was right next door-Big Dog cafe. Good choice of food and great staff. All in all a fantastic stay!

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Great location in Times Square. Took cab...”
text: Great location in Times Square. Took cab from Laguardia for $30. Right in Times Square. Easy walk to almost everywhere. Rooms are clean and new. Ask for room with square view. Get room away from elevator as they are noisy. There are slot of chain restaurants nearby. Be warned prices are higher for everything in New York. Try restaurant row on 46 th for non chain restaurants.

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Sacraficed comfort for glam”
text: Our 4 night stay turned into a one night stay after we realized this was not a hotel for us. It's very space-aged looking and modern upon arrival. There's a big robotic arm that takes your luggage which I guess is cool but alerted me that maybe priorities were out of line here. We opened the door to our 'cabin' and were shocked. It was tiny. And I mean tiny for NYC. The small bed folded up in the wall (our motorized bed was broken so it wouldn't go back) with a very small bathroom attached with no door just a glass slide. There was a 'desk' where I'd hoped to get work done but it had to hold our luggage since there was no other room. And the bed. If you can even call it that. The reason we left after one night. Neither my husband or I could walk the next day. We're both tall - maybe the bed is better for one small person, but it was awful for us. Especially for the price we had paid. I woke up the next morning so unhappy. The staff was kind and allowed me to cancel my reservation for the next 3 nights and we went down the street to a less expensive but much more comfortable hotel and were quite happy. If you're into hip and space-aged maybe this is for you. If you want room to walk, a door to close on the bathroom, and a bed to actually rest comfortably in I wouldn't recommend it.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “My favorite NY hotel thus far!”
text:
Not sure what all the other bad review were about, but here's my experience.
1. Excellent location to the theatres, also the little 24hrs cafe/baker right next door on 8th ave is wonderful and convenient.
2. Beautiful modern decor throughout the hotel.
3. Helpful staff, gave me tips on getting to the airport on time and even loaned us an umbrella. 
4. Spacious, nicely decorated rooms, had a king sized bed that was the most comfortable hotel bed i've ever slept in.
Personally, I like new, modern, clean looking hotels and this one is my favorite hotel in NY thus far. Got the room at about 50% off the official web page price on priceline.

name: The Muse Hotel New York
title: “Nice Hotel close to Times Square”
text:
Stayed here a few times now and although not the largest hotel it is quite comfortable and fairly spacious compared to many New York hotels.
It is a boutique hotel and the staff are friendly and attentive.
Only 1 block from Time Square so fairly quiet but close to all main attractions and shops.
Rooms clean and well maintained and bathrooms spacious.

name: Fitzpatrick Grand Central Hotel
title: “Home away from home”
text: My husband and I have been going to New York together annually for the past 6 years. On our second trip to New York, we discovered the Fitzpatrick Grand Central and have stayed there ever since. The location is absolutely perfect right across the street from Grand Central. The hotel has a great feel to it and the pub downstairs is a great place to wind down at the end of a long day of sight seeing.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Great base for NYC”
text: Just returned from a 3 night break which I organized as a surprise for my husband's 4oth. Westin was a fantastic base right across the road from the port aurthority bus terminal so we didn't have to walk too far with our bags through the crowded streets. Hotel very impressive, although I did call a couple of weeks prior to our trip to request a corner foom after reading a review on this site. The receptionist assured me she had taken a note of this, when we came to check-in they just said they were sold out of corner rooms and had no knowledge of my call! That was after being kept on hold from England for 5 minutes!!! Anyway, that did not mar our experience,the staff were courteous and delivered bathrobes and extras to our room almost immediately. Shower and bath fantastic.Didn't eat at the hotel - very expensive, steaks were $40!!! Ate out locally more reasonably. All in all a great time, just that 3 days isn't long enough, especially with a 7 hour flight on either side!!!! Enjoy

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Great value”
text: This hotel was a good value for what we paid. Nice location, close to subway and train station. Small room but had a fully equipped kitchen (full size fridge) and bedroom & bath were renovated nicely.

name: The Muse Hotel New York
title: “Cozy Hotel, Great Service, Friendly Concierge”
text: The Muse is a fabulous hotel! The front desk was especially helpful on which restaurants to go to and were always friendly especially Marc C. The beds were wonderful and for being so close to Times Square the room was pretty quiet. The hotel felt so cozy and the decor is really pretty.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Hôtel bien situé, bon rapport qualité-prix”
text: Hôtel bien situé, très proche de Central Park et proche du Rockfeller center. Chambre propre et bien insonorisée. Petit-déjeuner copieux, bon rapport qualité-prix (6$). Le personnel ne parle pas le français. Possibilité de transfert à l'aéroport dans une Lincoln noir (accords avec l'Hôtel) pour 60$ (au même prix qu'un taxi jaune).

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “Great location and comfort”
text:
This hotel is in a superb location. The beds are ultra comfortable and the hot shower pressure was what made my stay great after a long day of sight seeing. The breakfast is expensive please go to Europa cafe which is 2 minutes away. A concierge called David was extremely helpful and the epitome of professionalism.
My only critique is that the safe in our room had been tampered with twice I believe however it was not opened and security came to sort out the problem quickly.they said it was just a electric problem but I think otherwise.
Nevertheless a great stay

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “WOW!!!! Love this hotel....”
text:
Stayed here is for Thanks Giving in November 2009 with my mum as a treat for my 30th birthday and it was pefect. 
Firstly, location - Time Sqaure is either for you or it isn't. Simple. As 2 woman travelling on their own there were areas of New York that despite it's City that Never Sleeps rep were a bits too quite and intimidating past eleven at night. Located on the corner of Time Square facing the tkts ticket booth and well in the hustle and bustle mix of souvineer shops, bars and restaurants you are never threatened of too far from the action. If a trendy or quite location is for you, give this a miss. If this is your first visit to NY, this was our second, this hotel is ideal. The red Greyline open top tours are a must and all routes seem to radiate from this loctaion. With the good underground and it being Mid-Town you are central for all the loctaions you may want to explore. 
The hotel itself if located from the 7th floors upwards, accessed via a lift on the street level. Its a shiny, trendy place, very sleek and modern with dim lighting and a exclusive looking lounge bar. 
We stayed in a wonderful room which was large by any hotels standards let alone New York, with a crisp Kingsize bed, chais lounge, large plasma TV and a view over Broadway. The bathroom although lacking a bath housed a HUGE walk in shower/steam cupboard. Plenty of storage with a large wardrobe, bedside tables and a large draw for your clothes. Neither I or my mother travel light and there was plenty of room! These rooms although comfortable are not homely - they are ultra stylish, all brushed chrome, mood lighting and tinted mirrors.....not ideal for putting your make up on but very New York non the less. Room ammenaties were basic but extras like a coffee maker and suppliers were delivered to your room promptly on making a simple phonecall and was topped up everyday. 
All the hotel staff despite the trendy apperance were genuinely helpful and on hand whenever required. 
I will be visiting New York again at some point and would need a pretty good reason not to stay here.

name: Fitzpatrick Grand Central Hotel
title: “Good, but not perfect”
text: Fitzpatrick was in a good quiet location, easy access to most sites and activities. The only problem was the room, squeaky bed, no hairdryer, no clock radio and no furniture to put anything on but a nightstand. The entire floor smelled of paint, which may indicate renovations, but I would think if they are going to let rooms for the night, it would be passable. I tried to mention this to desk staff, but contrary to many of the reviews on this site I did not find them friendly, busy, but not friendly.

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “Unbelievable beauty”
text: Absolutely loved this experience....not just a hotel...from the moment we stepped out of the car upon arrival, we were made to feel special. Our room was in the towers, club level. Got a GREAT deal on Expedia. Needed a good sized room because we took our ten year old granddaughter. The roll away bed was in a corner of the room, always made up everyday. The bellmen, the maids, the servers in the club buffet area were so kind and efficient. This hotel is a destination in itself. Perfect location, walked a lock r two to subway stations, walked to plays, shopping etc. I can't wait to go back.

name: The Michelangelo Hotel
title: “An Italian gem”
text: Perfectly situated between Times Square and Central Park this is the place to stay. We had a nice big room ann paid a fair price. Every morning you are offered a free coffee and a croissant to start the day.

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “Ideal”
text: We stayed in room 3208 on the top floor with a great view of the Empire State Building.Great location near to Times Square and all the great restaurants on 9th Avenue. The room was ideal with large fridge and facilities for cooking if needed. Lovely comfortable 'pillow top' mattress. Re the gripes from other visitors: we were on the top floor and never had to wait more than a couple of minutes for the lift. We easily got a table every morning at breakfast. They open the bar for breakfast now to increase the seating capacity. Very good all round- no complaints!

name: The Muse Hotel New York
title: “Excellent customer service, amenities and location”
text: This is the best hotel in the Theater district at a very reasonable price. All the hotel staff were very nice and helpful. The rooms were clean, roomy for New York City, modern, comfortable beds and QUIET. The hotel is in a perfect location. Less than 2 minute walk to Times Square, 5-10 minute walk to Rockfeller Center, 15 minutes to Central Park, Grand Central and Empire State Building. I've stayed in numerous hotels in NYC, but this tops all of them in the same price range. I will definitely stay here on future trips to the city.

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “Fantastic Weekend at the Palace!”
text: I stayed here recently for a girls' weekend. The location is great...there are plenty of places in walking distance. The hotel itself is very nice...love the old, historic character that it has. The rooms were a nice size and were very clean. We were upgraded to a room on the 34th floor that overlooked St Patrick's Cathedral which was awesome. The only downside is the extras - such as having to order a bucket of ice at $4 per bucket. We had breakfast here one morning and eggs, potatoes, toast and drink was over $30. Kind of outrageous, but I guess it is to be expected in Manhattan. Overall, great trip and highly recommend this hotel!

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Excellent - Quiet and great location”
text:
What a find. We picked the Metro on a wim out of the massive range of available accommodation in MidTown New York
The streets a little dingy but the hotel is a quiet and calm little oasis away from the noisy streets and bustle of the big city. The lounge is comfortable and the general decor theme is consistently smart throughout the whole hotel. The continetal breakfast is good value and the restaurant serves good value and well prepared meals each night.
Bedrooms are comfortable and well maintained - though ours was a little cramped and next to a bulding site
A major selling point is the location - round the corner from Times Square, Macys, the Empire State Building and Fifth avenue

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Un très bon choix d'hôtel en famille”
text:
Nous avons séjourné dans cet hôtel pour Noël 2009, pour 4 nuits. Nous avons acheté le séjour sur internet (site de l'hôtel), et avons sélectionné une "one bedroom suite" pour 220 $ par nuit HT.
L'hôtel est idéalement situé, sur la 57ème rue, entre les 6ème et 7ème avenue, juste au sud de Central Park.
La 57ème rue est une des rares rues à trafic dans les deux sens (comme la 34ème par ex) donc elle est assez passante, les chambres situées en étage peu élevé donnant sur la rue doivent être assez bruyantes (nous étions quant à nous au 15ème étage sur 17, suite 1515, donnant sur l'arrière, extrêmement calme, murs bien isolés).
Les chambres sont très grandes (pour NYC), propres, bien équipées, la one bed room suite est très pratique pour une famille de 4 ou 5. Il ya deux lits queen dans la chambre, et un canapé convertible dans le séjour, ainsi qu'une table et quantité de chaises/fauteuils. Il y a aussi un micro-ondes et un petit frigo.
Le personnel est sympa.
Ce n'est pas le top luxe (le rez-de chaussée est petit, la moquette dans les parties communes est un peu défraichie), mais c'est très bien tout de même, et c'est un excellent rapport qualité-prix. 
Le petit déjeuner coûte 6 $ par personne, et est très correct pour ce prix (salle de déjeuner au 3ème étage, mais pas mal d'attente le matin lors de notre passage)
Deux lignes de métro sont à deux pas, l'une sur le 6ème, l'autre sur la 7ème, station 57th dans les deux cas.
A recommander

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “Fantastic - would recommend highly”
text:
This is the second time we've stayed at the W. We chose it because of it's location in the iconic Times Square.
From the moment we checked-in we were made to feel welcome and relaxed. The staff are approachable, friendly and always ready to help.The suite we stayed in was clean, modern and roomy. 
We went out for breakfast, (there's a very nice deli a few doors away). We had room service 2 evenings, the food was very good (if a little overpriced...but hey, that's all the extra taxes and charges)
We thoroughly enjoyed our stay!

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “En plein cœur de times square les places sont cher”
text:
Nous avons passés un agréable séjour à NY(8j) en plein times square! L hôtel est tout simplement parfait :
Emplacement parfait : à 100m du métro et de TS à 30m d un très bon resto italien la bella vita et pour les plus téméraires et les plus gourmands un body sushi bar à quelques pas de l'hôtel:-)
Chambre : parfaite et propre, lit King size moelleux à souhait,ménage effectué tout les matin et des placards pratiques pour stocker toutes vos folies faites durant de longues journées de shopping! Inutile de déjeuner à l'hôtel aller plutôt sur TS pour profiter de l'ambiance et avec de la chance être filmé au pied du siège de la abc pour l'émission good morning america comme ce fut le cas pour nous.
Finalement rien à dire sur l'hôtel mise à part le prix qui reste malgré tout assez cher. Compter 2000euros pr 7nuits. Et oui ça fait mal! Mais NY n attend pas et n'as pas de prix!!a refaire...refaire refaire refaire!!!:-)

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “Quiet in the city”
text: My husband and I stayed for three nights at the Hotel Chandler at the beginning of January 2012. Those three nights were just about the most quiet I have ever spent in New York City (and I used to live there). The room was small but extremely comfortable and clean. All staff were gracious and helpful. Although the lobby wasn't quiet because it's under renovation, we were in no way bothered by it in our room. And the hotel management kindly provided compensatory services, such as gratuitous breakfast and wine and cheese receptions. Once the renovation is complete, I'd like to return and enjoy it!

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “Great Location, but the rest of the rooms need to be renovated”
text:
I've stayed at the hotel before, but this time something was just off. I was upgraded to a higher floor as an SPG Platinum, but no suite as usual. The hotel itself is pretty nice, but the room this time reminded of the W-New York on Lex before it was renovated. The modern rooms need to be kept up or they just come across as cheesy. Last time I must have been in a newly renovated room, because everything was great. This time I felt like I was in an older room and also felt a little ripped off.
I've just come to expect nice bathrooms at every W Hotel I stay at and a bath tub with a shower curtain is a big disappointment. There were some nicks in the paint and a few other things that aren't OK for over $300/night.
On the positive side, the staff is always really helpful and the location is perfect for showing around friends that want to see the more touristy side of New York. There's a subway stop right across the street, and plenty of restaurants and broadway shows within a few minutes. 
Had I not stayed in a newer room the time before, I would have been a little happier about the room, but after staying in so many Ws, the room was a let down and to maintain the prices, they really need to make sure all the rooms are renovated.

name: The Muse Hotel New York
title: “Beautiful hotel...”
text:
My Husband and I just returned from an overnight escape from our adorable kids. The hotels itself is lovely, very clean with beautiful design. Our room was on the small side (buy hey, its NYC) but the decor was stunning. Our bathroom was immaculate, not so much as a hint of mold, or dust. The bed had great linens and pillows. The bed was okay... not the best ever but I slept like a rock. The bar/restaurant was great with the best of the hotel staff. Ross was great and had all kinds of great info for us. The front desk staff was okay. Check in was quick but not very warm or welcoming. We were not asked if we needed any info or recommendations. We came home from dinner and slipped our dessert into the fridge. I told the woman at the front desk so we wouldn't be charged $49 for the 7 beers we moved. We were told. "That is fine but your food will only be kept at room temperature" after a brief second her words sunk in (I had been drinking) and I realized how ridiculous her words were. I said "Beg your pardon?" she said the same thing again. So I asked her how the refrigerator kept the beer cold but would only keep my dessert "room temperature".... Hello... She didn't have much of a response and I didn't have the time to reason with someone with the IQ of 10. The next morning the Valet lost our car and didn't know what to do so they handed my husband a phone and asked him to work it out with the parking garage...? Valet was $48 for the night. For that kind of money I want my car back quickly, not an hour later after multiple requests and phone calls. 
Back to the good stuff! Most of the experience was perfect. Our room was on the 11th floor and overlooked 46th and it was pretty quiet, we slept through the night no problem. The location was ideal, you can walk to pretty much every show and Times Square. 5th avenue and all the wonderful shopping is within walking distance during the warmer months. If you need to take a cab it is $15-20 for most places. 
All said, I will be back and I would easily recommend this hotel to a friend.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Excellent location, Wonderful hotel”
text: The hotel staff was wonderful. We arrived at noon and the room was not ready. No big deal; however, while we were preparing our dress attire for the cold weather outside the nice gentleman from the hotel staff advised us the room was now available (which I thought was very nice). The room was large. We have stayed in Times Square before at other hotels and they are tiny. We had a 10th floor room. No issues with noise. Bed comfortable. I can't say enough good things about this hotel. Everyone was just very friendly. We will definitely stay again next visit to NYC.

name: Fitzpatrick Grand Central Hotel
title: “Great Location.”
text:
This hotel is in a perfect location. Within walking distance of all the sights and its mid-town too so you cant go too wrong. 
Its just between 3rd Ave and Lexington Ave on 42nd Street. 
When we arrived, it was 100degrees F. New York was in the middle of a heat wave. Needless to say we were delighted to arrive in the bedroom with the air conditioning on full blast. However, I was unhappy that there was no complimentary bottled water supplied in the room - and even the fridge in the room was empty. So we had to buy bottled water to have in our bedroom throughout our stay. Its not a big deal, but its just something that you come to expect from Hotels in this day and age. 
Aside from that - the concierge were extremely helpful and would always greet you as you were coming and going. They were available to ask about tours etc. The staff in the bar, on the other hand, were not so friendly. They frequently stood chatting to each other at the corner of the bar while we would wait at the bar to be served. Also they were blatantly speaking about other customers and how much they were drinking, which isnt very professional. 
The waiting staff in the restaurant (for breakfast) were friendly.. But we did think that the breakfast was way too expensive. ...and they added 18% to the bill for gratuity - - for breakfast?? 
Our check-in/out experience was fine. There are two lifts available in the hotel, but only one was working when we were there so we often had to wait quite a while for it. One evening, we were waiting for so long that we just decided to take the stairs to the 5th floor.
Also, the bedrooms were not cleaned until the late evening. Most evenings, we arrived back to our room at about 5/6pm to get changed for dinner, and our bed wasnt made. Then we would get a knock at the door from the cleaner to know if she could come in..... 
Anyway, the room was fine, clean and nice toileteries in the bathroom. 
I would recommend this hotel purely for the comfort of the room, the friendly concierge and the good location. Nothing more.

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Great Property, Great Location”
text:
Ideally located in Times Square to feel the buzz yet provides, if one wants, a quiet retreat into large spacious well appointed and surprisingly quiet rooms. Efficient check-in process; fun bank of elevators and large conference/meeting rooms.
Internet access is a tad pricey; restaurants are large and food quality above average, though better choices could be found within walking distance.
The USP has to be location - everything is within walking distance

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “Horrible night”
text: My husband and I spent last night at the Hotel Chandler besides that the place is under major construction they put us on the 12th fl and the elevator only went up to the 11th for some reason. We entered our tiny room which had a full size bed that my husband and I could not sleep in together. They told me they were sold out and couldnt change my room. I dont think you should let someone book a room for 2 and give them a full size bed.

name: Fitzpatrick Grand Central Hotel
title: “Perfect start.”
text:
Stayed in the Fitzpatricks Grand Central for the first two nights of our honeymoon. Staff at reception were very friendly, and the concierge even friendlier. As also first time visitors to New York, staff took time to go over various options open to us to see the city, places to eat, etc. 
Room was very comfortable and immaculate. Overall great feel to the hotel and would return there again. 
Only down side, which was very slight, was that the bar food was only very average for the price paid. But there are great eating out options in the area anyway.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Clean rooms, great location!”
text: Good choice! Had some trepidation about noise level based on prior reviews, but stayed recently at the Hilton Garden Inn and it was just fine. Room was on the 5th floor and heard nothing at all from the subway, hallways or from anywhere.We had a spacious, clean room at a reasonable price and the hotel is centrally located to many sights via walking or even using the Metro which is also very closeby. Was a bit disappointed with checking in as apparently it was a new person (found this out later) who was not very friendly or helpful, but in general, most of the staff were wonderful! Will definitely recommend this hotel to anyone I know visiting the city and hope to return there myself next time.

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Our own private terrace with hot tub”
text: Wow! Staying here was the highlight of our trip. So much fun. The 4th floor fun house is packed with so much lounging, dining, playing around and people watching. The patio terrace was beautiful at night. The food was yummy. Our room was amazin. Nothing like coming back to a private outdoor hot tub to soak in after a busy day out in the city. Will definitely return!

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Unique Hotel”
text: I can't say enough about this place. Yes, the rooms are small, but most people don't go to New York for the hotel room. My room was spotless and had a great view of the Hudson River. The service was some of the best I've experienced. I would definitely stay here again,

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Continues to be Great”
text: For several years I've spent from 6 to 12 weeks a year in New York on business. I've made a pretty serious tour of many of the hotels in the Mid-Town East and Murray Hill area and find the Affinia Dumont to be the best of the lot. Huge, comfortable rooms; a very friendly, smart and helpful staff; and spectacular views from the upper rooms. It really has become my home away from home. Plus, the coolest doormen in New York. I stayed there three times last year, and I'm showing up again in a week and a half.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Ottima posizione ed ottima dimensione delle camere”
text: Ottima scelta per quanto riguarda la posizione dell'hotel rispetto ai vari punti di interesse di N.Y. (5 strada - Central Park etc.). L'Hotel è sicuramente datato ma offre camere molto spaziose e comode. I letti sono molto grandi e comodi ed i ragazzi hanno a disposizione un divano letto abbastanza comodo in una stanza separata, dotata di televisore a schermo piatto.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Disappointed...”
text:
Not really sure how I could have been staying in the same property as all these rave reviews - but they were the reason I chose this hotel! Unfortunately, it did not live up to expectations for me. Yes, it is a great locationn and the rooms are a great size for central New York. Our king bed was very comfortable and the sheets were pristine and high quality. However, the room was not very clean. We found long black hairs on the couch and the carpet looked as though it had never seen the nozzle of a vacuum cleaner!! The dirt around the edges and in the corners was horrible and the carpet itself was shabby. The bathroom was far too small for a room this size and the fittings were cheap and nasty, with plastic panels around the walls above the bath instead of tiles and yellowing sealant that needed replacing. The cupboard was in an awkward place and poorly lit. Our room did not have an armchair and ottoman, as promised on the website, and it was very noisy - yes, I expected some street noise, but there appeared to be some sort of generator outside our room which provided a constant, loud, low pitched hum. 
It was my mistake not to complain as I realise I didn't give the hotel a chance to respond but as it was a trip I had planned for my husband's birthday, I didn't want to be negative about it. Complaining and changing rooms is a time-consuming business and we only had 3 days in New York - I didn't want to waste any time at all.
The free coffee in the lobby was nice but the breakfast was not the quality I would expect from a Hilton hotel. The cold choice was poor and the hot food was cold. We cancelled breakfast after the first morning of our stay so we could eat elsewhere and found better quality at a much lower price. 
If this had been a budget hotel, I might have felt quite pleased with it, but at $300 per night it represented very poor value. The Hilton we transferred to at the airport before an early morning flight home was beautiful - a completely different experience.

name: The Michelangelo Hotel
title: “Excellent location, fabulous large rooms and excellent staff”
text:
I travel a few times a year to NY and usually stay in the same hotel but as the rate was rather high I hunted for a different Hotel. The Michelangelo did not disappoint although some of the reviews were not too good - Rooms were very spacious with an added dressing room and the bed was very comfortable. Having the complimentary breakfast was lovely especially as I was by myself and did not have to venture out - it is just enough to set you up for the day with croissants and scones and a variety of coffee to suit everyones taste. The location is excellent - 2 blocks to the upper end of 5th Avenue and a very short walk to Times Square, Radio City and Top of the Rock. I found it very serene to return to after a hard days sightseeing and one was never disturbed by noise at night.
If there is a downside it is very small - no separate shower but apart from that this is my hotel for NY in future.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Great stay at the Crowne Plaza”
text:
My wife and I stayed here from December 7th to 12th as part of our honeymoon. First off, location, location, location! Our room was on the 17th floor overlooking Times Square. Originally we were put in a corner room on the 34th which had superb views. However, it was a little too high up for me so we asked to be moved to a lower floor. The front desk staff were extremely helpful and had no problem with the move.
The room itself was fantastic. Views onto Times Square, quiet, plenty of room for shopping with plenty of room to spare, Flatscreen TV(which stopped working on the second day but was fixed within 15 mins. Again, fair play to the staff.)
The room was very clean and the maid called every day with the room left spotless.
Check in and out was quick and easy. The food in the restaurant was delicious and the service was, again, fantastic.
The only minor problem was the price. It was a bit over the top, but I think thats just Manhattan. I'd definitely stay here again.
PS The fact that Hershey's is stuck to the GF of the hotel is also a big plus in my book :-)

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Great Little hotel...great location”
text: I stayed at the hotel metro last week, and my stay was excellent! I chose this hotel after reading reviews on it from this sitte. The front desk employees were very nice and helpfull ,they let us check in early too. We were plesantly surprised at how nice the rooms were.( see pictures). We were on the 8th floor, not sure if they were in the process of renovating some of the bottom floors but it seemed that from floors 7 and up were really nicely decorated w/marble nice lighting etc. The other floors seemed to be decent just not decorated as nicely (we only seen this from the elevator stopping on the way up/down. the room was very clean had a nice flat screen tv and was a decent price(booked through Orbitz). The bathroom was clean and properly stocked with all the fixings. The continental breakfast was great too(saved us purchasing a extra meal for two) w/really tasty food it was in a really nice room with tvs on the walls. All in all the hotel was fabulous and would reccommend it to anybody travelling to the Big Apple.

name: The Muse Hotel New York
title: “Poor, Poor Customer service!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text: My mother & sister in law, 2 nieces,my daughter, and myself stayed at this hotel for 1 night. One last summer fun time before school! We arrived early so our room wasn't ready, which was fine since we had a full day planned. We did our daily activities and returned at 5:00 to check in take a shower and get ready for our Broadway show. We had two rooms, so my daughter, my niece, and myself took one room when we entered is was very very hot 82 degrees. We turned down the thermostat thinking it would cool down, we got ready and left. We returned at 11:30p.m. with very tired little ones, when we walked into our room it was still very very hot, so we called front desk, they sent someone up immediately. The man comes in looks at it for maybe 30 seconds and says its broke, I will get you a fan. By this time both girls were about asleep on the bed sweating really bad. I told him that wouldnt work my daughter has asthma and needs air condition not a fan. He left and I called the front desk and explained the incident and he said I will send up a fan, it is August in NYC and a fan was not going to work,he then told me to open the window. I told him we needed another room asap because the kids were very tired, he claimed they were booked and he told me he would call me back in a few minutes. I never received a call, the girls went and slept on the floor of my mother in laws room and I stayed in my very expensive, very hot, hotel room with no working remote control and didn't sleep at all because it was so hot!! We travel alot and I have never ever seen such poor customer service in the U.S. No I'm sorry, no nothing!!!! If you like sleeping in a 82 degree room then this hotel is for you!!!

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Great hotel”
text: This hotel is a peaceful oasis in the heart of the bustling city. During my stay with a series of meetings, this hotel was very nice for my relaxation. I would like to thank the whole team of reception and concierge for help during my stay.

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Love this hotel”
text: This is a great hotel in a great neighborhood. Terrific value with kitchenettes in the rooms. Very week-appointed and convenient. This was my second stay and I will return.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “Simply Amazing, best choice we could have made!”
text: My daughter and I took a long awaited, very special trip to New York and were recommended The W at Times Square. Well, it was everything, and more, that we expected. She, 16, and myself wanted to stay at a trendy New York Hotel, in Times Square where we would be central. It was simply amazing! The service was impeccable, friendly and outgoing staff, and the music to die for! I wish I had bought all their CD's! The beds were extremely comfortable, the view of Times Square was delightful! The only complaint we had was the lack of lighting in the room, however, they were keen on supplying an additional lamp which made the difference. The restaurant had the best breakfast as well! What a great experience! Highly, highly recommend this hotel! Enjoy!

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Veramente al centro di tutto!!!”
text: Hotel a due passi da Times square. A due passi da tutto. Belle camere Atrium Club con accesso alla Atrium Club Lounge con colazione inclusa e aperitivo la sera. Le camere Atrium non si trovano ai piani più alti ma devo dire che il rumore della strada non dava alcun fastidio nonostante fossimo a due passi da Times Square.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Great hotel in Times Square”
text: We went here on business and the hotel was really nice. The accommodations are clean and modern. If your looking for a place in walking distance of times square and many restaurants this is a nice choice. Parking is right next door and is about $35 a day with validation. The staff was friendly. Wi-Fi was decent and dependable.

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Pricey space themed hotel”
text: High price with complimentary breakfast limited to muffins and coffee, very small room, and not overly helpful staff. It may be convenient to Times Square but there are more nicer, much more afforable places accessible via the Subway.

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “Best Hotel in Times Square!”
text: This hotel is fantastic. The rooms are very clean and a nice size for New York City. Free evening snacks and drinks are a plus. The location is excelleant, right across the street from the Port Authority and just a few blocks from Times Square. The entire hotel staff is very friendly and helpful. ANDY, MARCIN, and JAMIE are VERY helpful and will go out of their way for you. LOVE LOVE LOVE them!!! This was my second stay at this hotel, was there in May 2011. I will be returning in May 2012 and I will stay here again.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “voor een citytrip zit dit hotel op een geweldige locatie!”
text: het hotel is op sommige vlakken wat verouderd, maar we zagen dat ze bezig zijn te moderniseren. het ligt op een uitstekende locatie overal dicht bij. centralpark is bijna de achtertuin van het hotel, time square is 5 minuten lopen echt een aanrader dus, als net als ons in een paar dagen een hoop wilt zien en doen.in de buurt van het hotel kan je lekker ontbijten en s'avonds nog een drankje nemen. wij hebben het geweldig gehad !!

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “W Times Square "The Best"”
text: My husband and I had a reservation for another nearby hotel, we checked in and when we saw the room we checked right out! We had read mixed reviews about the "W" but decided we wanted to stay in Times Square. When we walked in the hotel we were greated by the most wonderful staff. We explained to the manager that we were not happy with the other hotel and would like to see a room at the "W". She gave us a tour and showed us a beautiful room. We were able to get a great rate through the internet last minute. We stayed four nights and had the best time! The staff at the "W" is incredible, their motto is Whatever- Whenever and they mean it! The rooms are newly renovated and tastefully decorated. They are smaller, but this is New York in Times Square!! I would highly recommend this hotel to any of my friends and hope to stay there again soon!!

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Cool”
text: Very nice service and we can from there to go any corner fro the city... that ist not a super hotel but the people and attention cool

name: Fitzpatrick Grand Central Hotel
title: “Great Place to Celebrate a Birthday”
text: I just returned from the great state of New York, and I have to say my stay at the Fitzpatrick Grand Central was awesome. My boyfriend was celebrating his birthday, so after walking to just about every place we went, it was nice to return to our nice, comfortable room at the Fitzpatrick. We arrived at the hotel at 6am in the morning after a long flight from California, and they allowed us to check into our room even though check-in was not until 3pm that day! We were very grateful for that. The pillow top mattress was very comfortable and having the robes and refridgerator in the room was a nice touch. Overall I found the hotel staff to be very friendly. One thing I reccommend is to get one of inside rooms to keep the noise out. Our room was so quiet, we slept in every day. I originally had booked us at the Radisson, but changed my mind because of the horrible reviews posted on this site. Just two days before my trip I was able to book at the Fitzpatrick, and I'm so glad I did. I would highly recommend staying there to anyone looking for a nice, comfortable hotel located in the heart of wonderful Manhatten!

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Perfect Location!!!!”
text: This is a great hotel- perfect location. Tons of shopping and FREE BREAKFAST!!! Front desk extremely helpful. Enjoyed my stay and will definitely will come back (:

name: Hotel Metro
title: “new yorks biggest secret!”
text: what can i say? we have stayed at this hotel 3 times now and for the price i can thoroughly recomend it! it is a nice clean art deco style hotel in a nice location with subway access 50 yards down the street,macys the next block(you can see macys from the hotel entrance)and the empire state building is round the corner.there is a cool roof terrace which offers excellent close up views of the empire state building.there is also a roof gym.you can also see the chrysler building from the front right hand side of the terrace and looking behind but dont expect fabulous views.the rooms are of a generous size the family rooms are excellent value which consists of two double beds in the main room and one double bed in the bedroom with big tvs and cable in both rooms.there is also a fridge various lamps drawers table and chairs and FREE WIFI INTERNET! which came in handy with my laptop.the rooms are cleaned everyday and all bed sheets are changed and floors vacumed etc.breakfast consists of bagels muffins toast etc which is FREE also FREE tea coffee hot chocolate,pure orange is available all day for FREE.there is a nice lounge area which they called the "EXECUTIVE LOUNGE" which we had to laugh at as the only minor points we saw was a large rat run around in the "EXECUTIVE LOUNGE" hahaaahaha.also a few flys around the free breakfast that is left out for you too help yourself.apart from that the lounge area was nice and relaxing with library plasma tvs and comfy seating,the lounge was in the process of being updated the last time i was there so it could now be different?hotel staff were ok sometimes friendly but quiet,and some were ignorant and looked like it was an effort to smile.the a/c and heaters in some of the rooms were a bit old and noisey but it was not a problem.i would recomend that you request a high floor with a front view,which would give you views of the empire state building from your room,if you look up also reduces the noise from the garbage men working throughout the night and early morning taxi horns waking you from a good nights sleep.all in all though it is a very good hotel for the location and price and i would stay there again.it feels a nice and safe hotel with no low life hanging around or gangster muppets trying to rob you outside. lol

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Fantastic Location!”
text:
I stayed at the metro with my boyfriend from 1-4 october before going to florida and we had an amazing time.
the hotel is located in a top spot,close to 5th avenue,macys,times square and empire state building which you had a great view from the hotels roof top terrace.
the complimentary tea,coffee,muffins,bagels etc was a great touch as its probably the only hotel in new york to offer this!
the rooms are great with everything you need, ok its not the ritz but you dont need a 5 star hotel in this city as you are never in it!!its comfortable, the rooms are clean,the staff are helpful and you just cannot beat the location.
we did a few excursions like the liberty helicopter ride, the circle line cruise around manhattan which is a must as its a fantastic day out and you see lots of land marks and its cheap!
we also eat the the view restaurant which is a revolving restaurant in times square, the food is ok but the setting is gorgeous, also eat at the tavern on the greenwhich is like a fairy tale land,absolutely incredable and the food was good,we booked these before we went. even though we had only 3 nights here,we made the most and saw everything!!
if you are lucky enough to be going or thinking about going,try the metro,it does get booked up quickly though,one of the cheaper hotels too, you will have a fab time and im so jealous!!!

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Navidad en Nueva York”
text: Estuvimos en este hotel estas navidades, del 24 al 28 de diciembre. El emplazamiento es muy céntrico. Puedes desplazarte fácilmente por todo Manhattan desde el hotel, tanto en metro como en taxi ya que no está lejor de ningún sitio. Nuestra habitación, con dos camas dobles, perfecta para nosotros dos y nuestra hija de 19 años. El pub correcto aunque es difícil tomar un aperitivo ya que sólo está abierto por la tarde. También bien el restaurante. Unas hamburguesas más que correctas. La gente amable. Todo bien. Gracias.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “One of the best hotels in Midtown”
text:
I was booked in this hotel by Starwood Corporate after my original stay at the Sheraton Manhattan at Times Square went all wrong (see my post there for full details.)
Having stayed at many W hotels in the past, this one ranks up with one of the best. The suite I was in was absolutely beautiful. It had a very large bedroom, 2 full bathrooms, living room, two large screen tvs, multiple sound systems... the works. 
The best part of this room is that it is the only room with a full balcony. It has an amazing view, and is perfect for anyone looking to entertain up to two dozen people comfortably. You are separated from all the other rooms, so you can be sure your partying will not disturb any of your neighbors. Also the balcony comes in handy for those who smoke, as all the rooms are non-smoking.
The club in the basement of the hotel is okay, tho never drew a very big crowd. There is a great bar in the main lobby area of the W (3rd floor), and a great place to unwind. The restaurant has some great food (sushi blend), but expect to pay the usual NYC fares. The room service is on par with the restaurant, and can satisfy almost any need at anytime. This goes along with the W's motto: Whatever, Whenever. 
I would recommend this hotel to anyone who is looking to stay in Times Square.

name: The Michelangelo Hotel
title: “Great location, and some updates”
text:
I read all the reviews on this hotel before deciding to book and thought I could reply to some of the previous comments. The best thing about the hotel has been said over and over again...the location is just perfect. The other big plus, as stated by others are the nice size of the rooms. 
I found a rate on Expedia and then called the hotel and they matched that rate, which was $355 for a DeLux room. We had room 534 which looked over 51st Street, and across to an office building. All the good things about the hotel, I think are true. Here is our take on some of the negatives. Our towels were always new and fluffy (not thin as some said). The hallway rugs were being replaced while we were there (there were some complaints on that).....our bedding looked newer, not shabby. There are paper cups now at the breakfast bar and you can take the coffee back to your rooms (at least my husband did). We always had two chocolates by our bed (not just one as someone complained). We asked for a coffee maker which they gladly supplied, but it is true that they do not provide coffee, so we ended up not using it. Our bed, a King, was very comfortable which is so important after a long day of sightseeing! We spent the last five days of a three week vacation there and this bed was the best bed of our trip. 
The only negative, for my husband, concerned the air-conditioning which has been talked about on this site. Yes, it does cycle on and off frequently and this woke my husband up. If you are a light sleeper, this may bother you. I, on the other hand, was not bothered at all by this. I am usually warm and I loved the fact that the air conditioner kept the room quite cool!
We plan to return to NYC in a couple of years and we plan to stay again at the Michelangelo!

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Great experience”
text: A friend recommended this hotel, and it was a great experience. Hotel is in excellent location, very clean and modern, but best of all was the service and hotel staff especially one of the employees Anamaria, she made sure our weekend in New York was unforgettable made us feel very welcome and gave us very useful information, will recommend this hotel to everyone traveling to NY.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
title: “Bel hôtel bien placé, sauf pour ceux qui recherchent la tranquilité”
text:
Tout juste de retour de 3 jours à New York, j'ai séjourné avec une amie au Westin Time Square. L'hôtel est placé au coeur du New York animé et du quartier de Time Square, vous êtes à coté de tout. Ce qui inclut l'agitation de ce quartier très animé... En sortant de l'hôtel, la foule est présente, ce qui peut paraître un peu opressant.
Les chambres sont très belles, spacieuses et bien décorées dans les tons blancs, marron foncé et bleu. N'hésitez pas à demander lors de la réservation une chambre dans les étages supérieurs, la vue vaut le coup d'oeil! La salle de bains est originale: porte coulissante et double pommeau de douche!
Les chambres, tout comme les parties communes, sont très propres, le personnel est aimable.
Je vous recommande cet hôtel pour sa proximité immédiate du centre de New York, mais si vous recherchez quelque chose de plus calme, essayez plutôt les hôtels proches de Central Park South.

name: The Westin New York at Times Square
YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Poor showing for Yotel”
text:
I stayed at Yotel on 7/18 and the experience was lackluster. I was in "cabin" 2337 and although I checked in during the dinner hour, I quickly left for dinner and did not return until after midnight. **The city was near one hundred degrees this week.** When returning to the cabin the room was in the high 80s. I figured it was part of the "green" approach to the place so I did not think much of it, turned the AC down to 70 and quickly went to sleep. By 3:00am I awoke in a pool of sweat, went to the AC controls and found that the room had not cooled below 78 degrees. In addition, when I went to the bathroom to get a cool towel, the lights in the bathroom did not work. I then went for the light in the cabin entryway...no luck there either. The only lights that worked were near the bed and they provided no light into the bathroom.
The next morning I went to the fourth floor lobby to checkout and mentioned my problems to the desk staff. One of them asked me in an attitude if I had called the desk staff about the AC problem. I let her know that at 3:00am I didn't consider that an option. The other employee curtly asked me my cabin number and neither of them offered so much as an apology for the experience.
Staying at Yotel saved my company $50-75 but it was not worth it. Next time I'll be a slightly less, good corporate citizen and stay at a Hilton or Marriott.

name: Fitzpatrick Grand Central Hotel
title: “Fitzpatrick Grand Central Hotel!”
text: Hotel com excelente localização(100 metros da estação central) e atendimento nota 10! Muito confortável e quartos grandes para o padrão de New York e ainda por cima tem um Pub Irlandês dentro do hotel. Recomendo a todos!

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “No Surprises”
text: Rooms are getting slightly tired, but the layout, amentities and location are great. Close to the subway and TimesSquare. This is not the Hilton, but you don't pay Hilton rates. We stayed in a room not facing 8th avenue and the noise was still at times annoying.

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Amazing & central”
text: Really nice hotel... breakfast is basic (bagels and muffins) but they're yummie! Nice rooms, gym on roof.. lovely roof terrace with amazing views of Empire State (must see). No regrets... special thanks to George... very friendly receptionist.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Perfect location, great view, spacious rooms”
text: The Crowne Plaza is directly located at the Times Square in Manhattan and not as many other hotels that claim to be at the Times Squares, but are in reality a block away. The hotel has a kind of stylish interior. The reception is a bit inconveniently located at the first floor, reachable through a stairway. The rooms are spacious and especially the corner rooms, AFAIK no upgrade necessary, are even nicer. Bathroom (in the niche of the main room) and toilet/shower are separated. Price for a one night stay from Sunday to Monday was 320 USD.

name: Fitzpatrick Grand Central Hotel
title: “Muy buena calidad”
text: Acabamos de volver de un viaje a USA y en New York nos hemos alojado en el Fitzpatrick Grand Central. Fantástica ubicación y muy buen hotel. Habitación y baño grandes sobre todo si lo comparas al resto de hoteles que miramos y eran muchos. En cuanto a la limpieza ninguna queja. Repetiría sin dudarlo. Una buena elección sin duda.

name: The Michelangelo Hotel
title: “Our new NY favorite”
text: I booked this hotel online after reviewing many sites. I was looking for a great location at an affordable price for a mother/daughter weekend. We were not disappointed! Because we arrived a little early on Saturday, our room was not yet ready. When the staff learned I was meeting my daughter, they offered a upgraded room with 2 king beds that was availbable immediately. And although the bathroom did not have a tub, as it was handicap accessible, we jumped for it. The hotel is beautiful and the room was quite large. James, the concierge, was great and helped secure dinner reservations for the exact time we needed, speaking both Italian and Spanish. The theatre and restaurant were all within easy walking distance. The complimentary coffee and pastry bar the next morning was nice . My only slight complaint was that the fan in the room kept turning off and on and because we like white noise, we had to set the fan on a lower temp to keep it running, so it got a little cool. We were also on the 3rd level above the street, so a fan was also needed to drown out the noise. They do offer quieter rooms, however. I will definitely be returning the Michelango...a great find!

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Great Location”
text: Went to NYC for a family get together with relatives from outside the tristate area. Although we live in CT, we prefer not to have to drive home late at night. One room we had overlooks Time Square and the other the pier where the cruise ships depart from. This hotel is a fabulous, safe location in Time Square. Although it is not cheap, it has just about everything you could want for. Valet parking is offered so from the very start of the trip, we relaxed. The hotel has shopping, Starbucks, beautiful lounges which look out to Time Square, restaurants, etc. We were able to walk to Rockefeller Center & st. Patrick's Cathedral, Carmine's Restaurant, and a comedy show. We have stayed here in the past and enjoyed our visit as much this time.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “Good and bad”
text:
The Spectacular room, which we had booked ( above 32nd floor), wasn't ready at 3:45, so we took a room on the 21st floor. The room was nice, and we got a thirty dollar discount for taking it.
The big problem is that the walls are paper thin. Our neighbors got in while we were taking a nap. We heard, very clearly, that they were planning to attend a show at the Majestic Theater. After that, we heard them making love. None of this was loud. It was all in regular voices - just things I would prefer kept private. I'm sure they would have , too.
I wouldn't stay here again.

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Yotel was the greatest experience!”
text:
Me and my husband stayed for our Honeymoon at Yotel for 7 days. The first thing that comes to my mind when I think about our stay at Yotel is the crew, I have never in my life met a nicer and more professional crew. Even though you think that nobody is going to greet you because everything is computerized, you are met by people that greets you and helps you. Yotel is fresh, futuristic, modern and special. The rooms are fresh and clean, always clean when you are back from a day spent in NYC. eve if you have a smaller room you dont feel it is so small because the windows are big and the class doors to the bathroom and toilet makes everything much bigger. The complementary breakfast was not my cup of tea, since you only get coffee and muffins. the al la carte breakfast is expensive, you can get much more for less money just across the street. The food however, the lunches and the dinners are awesome and fully price worthy. The tapas inspired food is awesome, I loved the food, it is fresh and delusions.
We will definitely come back to Yotel, and Yotel made our holiday worth wild.

name: The Maritime Hotel
title: “Great Hotel, Fantastic Service”
text: My family recently stayed at The Maritime and I can't say enough about the hotel and services all around. The lobby has a great vibe, the bar is great and the restaurant food is really good. The rooms are very comfortable and quiet. To top it off, the staff could not be nicer or more accomodating. The location is terrific - stay here!

name: Renaissance New York Hotel Times Square
title: “Center of it all”
text: This was a great place to stay. It was the center of Times Square and the theater district. The service was good and the views were incredible. Despite being in the center of it all, the rooms are quiet. Be sure to check out the view from the 2nd floor lounge overlooking Times Square.You cannot beat it for location and comfort.

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Good location, great service and big rooms!”
text:
We stayed at the Affinia Dumont last September for 2 weeks with our toddler son and so we booked the junior suite ( rm 2601) so we would have lots of room. Our view was over to the east river and I was slightly disappointed on arrival to not get the amazing views of the chrysler/empire state etc some of the other travellers had but i was told none of the suites faced that way. But it was a nice view anyways.
Although the rooms are tired with slightly 90's decor& kitchen and and big tv's (no flat screen here), it was brilliant for our stay. It was great to have a kitchen to be able to cook and have breakfast especially with a small child and the living and bedroom was massive. We had a few issues with the childrens channels on the tv and it did take a number of hours to get this fixed, which our son didn't understand ;) but the service was always prompt and attentive. The cleaners were attentive and lovely to chat too. The concierge was briliant and he was so helpful and friendly and always welcoming. On a Thursday I think they had drinks and nibbles in the foyer. We didn't realise until we went searching that they have a coin laundry in the basement, so we could do washing/drying of clothes for just a few dollars. Very helpful for those who have a long stay in NYC. The Barking Dog restaurant did pretty much most food you can think of: salads, burgers, fries, sandwiches and great breakfasts! A great outdoor area off the street which is nice for the summer evenings and SUPER cold beer!! The Barking Dog also supplies room service to the hotel which was helpful for those nights in with children and not wanting to cook after a long day of sightseeing. We arranged a babysitter through the Hotel I think her name was Lori from memory and she was absolutely brilliant! She came with her own bag of toys and a small gift for our son each time she took care of him. Definitely recommended! The location for the hotel was great, quite often we walked back from Central Park to the hotel which was a long walk but a nice one taking in all the skyscrapers including my favourite the Chrysler as well as Grand Central Terminal. It also had a couple of supermarkets around the corner, a large Duane Reade and some cool bars/ restaurants in walking distance. There is a subway station one block up and a cab over to Chelsea was about $10 or so depending on the time of day. One thing I would agree with the other customers is that they should offer free WIFI in the rooms- this would be a negative for those staying on business.
However, all in all, our stay at the Dumont made our holiday extremely relaxing, enjoyable and memorable - thank you! 
I know that if Affinia Dumont was to update their rooms and include WIFI, this hotel would be 5 *!

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “Good choice, would stay again”
text: My husband, son, and I stayed in a suite with 2 double beds 8/20 - 8/23 The room was spacious by NYC standards. The kitchen facilities in the room were handy to keep some late night drinks and snacks in. The location of the hotel worked out really well for us. I had read previous reviews about the hotel being located next to adult stores and a parole office, but it was no big deal. The block is very short and there are plenty of tourists walking at all hours. The staff was friendly and helpful. We arrived 2 hours before check-in time, and were able to get into a room right away. The elevators were slow at certain times in the morning, but that is to be expected. It it's a big worry then ask to be put on a lower level and take the stairs instead of waiting. The beds and pillows were very comfortable. We had no trouble getting the free wi-fi connection in our room. Tthe room had a full size ironing board/iron, a hair dryer, a safe, and of course a coffee maker. The hotel breakfast was good with lots of fresh fruit, cereal, breads, yogurts, and two hot items - usually eggs and ham or sausage. Other hotels I looked at when deciding where to stay offered no breakfast and charged for internet. For transportation to and from Laguardia I would highly recommend Dial7 car service. They pick you up (either at the airport or the hotel) in a nice black Lincoln Town Car. The cars are all leather and spotless, An added bonus is that the drivers don't smell (I've taken some awful cab rides) You can book online or give them a call. I paid less than $45 including tip. Rates may vary depending on when you go, but it was a great way to start and end our trip.

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “The icing on the cake”
text:
We stayed at the New York Palace Towers for the last 4 days of our trip to the US and it was the icing on the cake of a wonderful holiday to America. The stay at the towers was a birthday surprise for my wife and I asked for a room with a view of the Chrysler building and for some flowers to be in our room when I made the online booking. The concierge subsequently contacted me by phone and email to finalise my request for the floral arrangement and confirm my room request. When we arrived we were on the 53rd floor and the spectacular view was matched by the floral arrangement I had requested (compliments to your florists!). Upon returning to our room later that evening a bottle of sparkling wine was on ice with a card to my wife from the hotel.
The room itself was a Premier King, spotlessly clean and the furnishings and fittings were of a very high standard. We found the Towers Club an oasis, we didn’t eat at lunchtime as we were out but breakfast and evening drinks and food were very good and you could drop in anytime to get a drink or coffee. The additional cost of the towers club is well worth it.
We found the staff courteous and friendly and the service we received was excellent. One of the things I noticed was how the staff behaved to each other, they clearly enjoy working at the NY Palace and that comes across in how the guests are treated.
Perfect.
We will definitely stay at the Palace Towers again.

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “Happy except for the lifts”
text: We enjoyed our stay here - we were glad of the 'free" breakfast and especially glad of the free laundry (including free powder. It might be my lack of NY geographical knowledge but I thought since the hotel name including Times Square it was actually in the main Times Square area but its a short walk away. The actual location is a touch seedy but there are so many people around, it always felt safe so that wasn't an issue. Hotel staff were friendly and knowledgable but the lifts really are terrible. We actually walked down a couple of times from the 26th floor! But it would help if people who say had rooms on the 5th floor didn't insist on catching the lifts up and down when they had perfectly good legs and no luggage with them! And people who allow their kids to cath the lifts on their own and the kids just queue jump! (And I say this as a person travelling with kids! ) But overall, would recommend this as a well priced family hotel.

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Hotel tres bruyant, a eviter !”
text: Je viens de passer deux nuits dans cet hotel et le bruit d'une soufflerie installee dans la cour interieure est vraiment insupportable. La reception m'a propose de choisir entre 4 chambres differentes (215, 201, 317 et 501) mais elles etaient toutes aussi bruyantes les unes que les autres. Par ailleurs les chambres sont petites, les salles de bain minuscules.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “Can't Complain”
text:
My Fiance and I stayed at the W Hotel in Time Square from September 22-24, 2006. 
I have to say that I rather enjoyed my stay. The hotel is very well located in the heart of Time Square. We walked back from Central Park and it took us about a half an hour.
The bar at the hotel is very modern and nice. The staff was rather pleasant as well. The rooms were typical W rooms. Very new & modern, although these are a little older than I am used to for a W. 
Overall I would say that it is a very nice hotel if you are looking to spend some time in the center of Manhatten. Beware though as like much of New York, it is expensive.

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Ottima posizione,letto comodissimo”
text:
Sono stato la sett scorsa in viaggio d nozze ed ho soggiornato qui,e' un hotel molto pulito,ben gestito e tt ben educati,la mia camera era spaziosa tranne il bagno(cmq ben pulito sempre!),i letti e i cuscini sono SUPER morbidi e comodissimi ideali per dormire dopo una giornata d camminate.
La colazione e' abbondante,e il ristorante adiacente discreto.
L hotel e' a 50 metri dalla metro che collega parecchie linee quindi una figata!e a 200 da time square,occhio solo ad uscire dopo le 22 perché nn e' proprio iper tranquilla come zona,ma come tt New York d altronde.in un viaggio futuro tornerei sicuramente,ottima esperienza.

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Déception”
text:
Chambre minuscule pour 2 personnes.Le chauffage est très bruyant et peu efficace.En étant sur une petite cour glauque on entend le bruit de la rue car absence de double vitrage.La salle de bain est aussi minuscule avec une grande fenêtre qui laisse entrer le froid et bien entendu pas de chauffage dans la salle de bain.Le petit déjeuner digne de la cantine:tasses et assiettes en carton, des couteaux qui ne coupent pas.Il faut avant de s'asseoir faire le ménage des tables si l'on ne veut pas manger dans les miettes et les traces des précédents clients.
Hotel 2 étoiles pas plus.Le seul avantage la situation

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “great location, great value”
text: We stayed here for a wedding. Bride and groom had negotiated an incredible rate and we loved the location. We were handy to many major attractions ... Rockefeller Center, St. Patrick's, Fifth Avenue shopping, theatre district, etc. Room was small but very nicely appointed and very updated. Lobby is beautiful. Like much of NYC, you get caught with lots of tipping opportunities ... bring your bags in from the taxi, take them to your room, deliver gift basket from concierge. Was not happy that we couldn't check out and then go to room to finalize packing. Check-out personnel said that the minute we checked out, it would remove the key from the system so we had to come back down to check out after we left the room. What's up with that? Surely the computers are smarter than that. Breakfast buffet was very high priced and underwhelming ... suggest you wander outside the hotel for your morning meal. All around nice experience, however.

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “Good choice”
text: My wife and I stayed at Hotel Chandler early April, and we were very pleased having chosen this hotel to stay at. The people working at this hotel were nice and helpful. The location was nice, in central Manhattan, very near to the Empire State Building. Hotel Chandler is not the most luxurious hotel in New York, but offers nice clean rooms with more than just the comfort you need. We had chosen this hotel because of the great reviews on this site, and because the room rates are fairly affordable compared to the rates of many other NY hotels. We made a great choice. If we revisit NY, we will definitely check out the rates and availability of this hotel. And if the prices are still right, we will return here for sure.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Great value for such a central location”
text: Last minute booking as the hotel we were staying in could not extend or stay. This hotel was central to everything and the staff were very accommodating. We were offered a room at the front or a quiter room at the back, we opted for the quiter room. The room and bathroom were a little small but spotless. I would definately keep this hotel on my future list.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “Yuck!”
text: What a disappointment! The rooms were small and in bad condition. There was a big stain on the wall. Mirror was broken. The chic was all cheap. There was almost no service. The lobby/lounge on the seventh floor was just plain obnoxious. I feel so ripped off.

name: Renaissance New York Hotel Times Square
title: “If you've just got to be in Times Square, this is a great find”
text: We stayed here over a weekend and I couldn't have been more pleasantly surprised. Times Square is never my first, second or third choice in NYC -- way too crazed and frenetic -- but we had to be at this property for work reasons. That said, this is a lovely hotel. The design is pleasantly modern -- once you get up to the lobby level, the space is well-organized, inviting and calming -- pleasant gathering spaces, a small gem of a lobby bar, and the lounge -- which overlooks the main Times Square are -- is a must experience for drinks and appetizers. The view is absolutely amazing. Rooms aren't spacious, but you can't expect spacious in NYC. The design was perfect, modern and extremely convenient. The bedside lighting is really inspired, and the bathroom was large, spotless and with every amenity. Bedding so comfortable and clean! All in all, just a super experience.

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “A great find!”
text:
We booked a "superior" room for three evenings and were quite comfortable. The front desk staff helped us with luggage and took our car to valet parking, which was available to us within 10 minutes of asking. 
There was plenty of closet space & drawers should you need to unpack any belongings. As mentioned in previous reviews, the shower is large and the Aveda products were restocked daily. I liked the little blue tiles and 20s style design of the bathroom. The bed, pillows and comforter were all very clean and comfortable. 
Location was extremely convenient and it was a nice resting spot between adventures. Our only disturbance was the fact that we were on the second floor and able to hear the noise of the hotel bar, on the first floor. I suggest a higher floor. The bar seemed nice, with a street front door, but we didn't have time to stop in for a our complimentary glass of wine. Took a peek in the gym which was small but fully equipped, with a sauna. Check out went smoothly with no hidden charges. Overall I recomend this place and will be back again.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “The Girlz loved the CP in the NYC: Part 2”
text: I was one of the “Girlz” on the labor day weekend trip (See Nashville, TN reviewer). I can’t say enough good things about the Crowne Plaza. The hotel is centrally located to Time Square, the subway, and the Broadway theaters. It is very clean, modern, and the service was great! The upgrade we received upon check-in put the icing on the cake. I would not hesitate to stay here again.

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “Great Value”
text:
This hotel is a great value because of all the inclusions -- daily breakfast, evening drinks/appetizers several nights per week, wireless internet, laundry, etc. The location was very convenient for walking to the Times Square area, or for catching the subway. There's a Duane Reade store in the Port Authority building nearby (open 24 hours). Our room was on the top floor and we didn't experience any of the elevator waits others have reported, thankfully. The room itself was nice, the kitchenette was appreciated, and while the staff wasn't excessively friendly, they were polite and helpful. We did find the room air conditioner a bit tricky -- the choices were "freezing cold" or "too hot" -- you really couldn't find a comfortable temperature in the middle which the unit would maintain.
Overall, we would definitely stay here again, and recommend it to friends and family.

name: The Michelangelo Hotel
title: “A GREAT HOTEL & GREAT LOCATION”
text:
We stayed one nite on Nov. 13, 2004 for our anniversary. I had requested an early check in, when I called to confirm the reservation they said no problem. We arrived at 1pm and was told our room would not be ready until 3pm. I then said I was told over the phone that an early check in would be no problem. A room became available within minutes. The room was very nice & clean. I was surprised at the size of it & the bathroom also. We had dinner at the resturant in the hotel
I believe it is called limoncellos. The food was average & the prices reasonable.
I had an apple martini that was $10.00. The location of this hotel is perfect! We walked to the wax museum in the afternoon (about 9 blocks) & then to 45th st for the "ave Q" show at 8pm. (very good show!) We chose not to do the complimentary breakfast because of the reviews on this site. We asked the bellman to recommend a good place to eat. He sent us up just one block to the Stardust diner. This is a 1950's theme diner where the waiter & waitresses get up & sing oldie songs (very fun) All in all this hotel met all of our expectations & we will definitely be back again. New York City is the best!!!

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “A great first NYC experience”
text:
We stayed here over a long weekend in early April '08. Check in was fast and stress-free (there was a line when we arrived but it moved quickly) and the staff was very welcoming. Our room was ready right away (well before the official check in time), and was clean and spacious, very little to argue with there. 
There's several food options there if you feel like staying in at any point on your trip -- we ate at the restaurant on the top floor (which was decent but expensive), as well as one of the restaurants on a lower floor for breakfast and the lounge for drinks (again, both were good and the revolving lounge is fun, but both, like many places in NYC, are a little pricey.)
