The location is a huge selling point for this place and for first-timers in NYC like we were it was a good place to be based (you have Times Square obviously right outside your door, and we were able to easily walk to a lot of sights like the Museum of Modern Art -- but keep in mind that we are both healthy young adults with no children so your mileage may vary.) Getting to the subway from the hotel was also easy. 
The only thing I can't really comment on is the price of the room, since we were able to stay mostly on Marriott rewards program points and therefore got a really good deal. 
All in all, I would book this place with confidence and recommend it to others.

name: Renaissance New York Hotel Times Square
title: “Nice!”
text: I stayed here for 10 days in June . If Times Square is where you want to be then this is the best place to stay. We stayed on the 25th floor and our room was quiet. The room was nice, very clean. The staff was excellent. We ate breakfast in the restaurant facing the m&m store every morning. Very expensive buffet breakfast but it tasted good and staff were very friendly. Had appetizers right next to the window overlooking Times Square which was fabulous. Concierge was very helpful, maids were friendly....can't think of anything negative. I did think the air conditioning in the lobby was really cold, too cold....but I thought that about other places in NY too. Oh and don't forget to tip the maid, she will appreciate it because a lot of people don't .

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “We had the best experience in NYC at Staybridge Suites”
text: My husband and I celebrated our first wedding anniversary in New York City, and were wanting the full Times Square experience. The hotel was within walking distance of all of the TImes Square stores, theatres, and restaurants. The subway to other points in the city was also very close. We had a Kingbed suite, with a very spacious bathroom and full kitchenette (including microwave, range and dishwasher), which was stocked with cookware, dishes, and flatware. We used the laundryroom on our last night in town, which allowed us to travel home with clean clothes. Although the hotel is only a few blocks from the center of Times Square (and right next to the bus station) we were never bothered by traffic noise. We also felt very safe, even walking late at night. The hotel also offered a free (hot and fresh) continental breakfast each day, and during the weekdays we also enjoyed the free cocktail hour, which included wine and fingerfoods. The bed was so comfortable (no bed bugs!), the thermostat was easy to operate, and we enjoyed all of the great tv channels at night. The most impressive thing about the Staybrige Suites was the staff-they were all very courteous and extremely helpful in providing directions and subway line information to out-of-town visitors. They even provided a private car for our trip to the airport, which was cheaper, faster, and more reliable than a taxi. We would recommend this hotel to anyone staying in NYC, and we will definitely book there again for our next vacation to the Big Apple.

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “Great central place to stay!”
text: My sister and I just spent a week in New york and would highly reccommend the hotel Chandler as a central place to stay. Its 2 blocks from the Empire State building and right off 5th Ave. Very very central! Its not cheap but definatly not as expensive as some of the others. We had a small room with 2 double beds but it was fully functional. The shower in the bathroom is amazing and the complimentary Aveda products were a nice touch. The staff were always courtious and helpful. The bellboys are always there to grab a cab for you, should you need it. The staff hand out maps on arrival too, which is great if you have never been to the city before. The only negative thing I could say is the lack of tea/coffee making facilities in the room. The hotel offers complimentary tea/coffee in the lobby but most people would'nt want to go to the lobby in their PJ's of a morning to grab a cup! We stayed on a room only basis but there are plenty of deli's nearby, most open 24hrs. I would advise people to avoid eating out in the area as it is overpriced and obviously geared towards tourists. Take a taxi to Greenwich Village in the evening for more variety and better value for money. However, there is a nice Thai place across the street from the hotel which has lovely food and inexpensive. All in all, the Hotel Chandler is a great place to stay and check out the city as most tourist spots are within walking distance.Take a city bus tour, a must for all the relevent info on the first few days of your trip. There are agents on every corner in which to buy tickets.

name: Renaissance New York Hotel Times Square
title: “Nothing Special”
text: This hotel was nice but nothing special. Great location if you want to be in Times Square. Carpet in the room was worn and dirty. 2nd floor lobby was very dark. Key access in elevator was not operational, anyone could use the elevator (poor security). No place to pull off of the street to unload your car, just the curb.

name: Renaissance New York Hotel Times Square
title: “Location good if you want time square.”
text: The hotel's location is great for being in time square or seeing shows. The rooms are starting to show some wear. The carpets did not look real clean. The furniture has some nicks in it. The service was mostly okay. The free breakfast was to be served until 10 am. We got there at the same time as another couple about 10 minutes before 10 and they were all ready taking the food out of the room. The waiter just said to get our food fast because they were closing. Not very customer friendly. We are gold members and I didn't really see any advantage. The concierge was friendly and helpful. I don't think we would stay here again. We were scheduled to stay 3 nights at the beginning of our vacation and then were planning to move to a different hotel in Soho. But we moved after 2 nights.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Bring earplugs you'll need them”
text:
I booked this hotel for my family ( wife plus two grown up children) to celebrate our ruby wedding anniversary. Most reviews rated it as excellent but I have reservations about this based on my stay
Although the rooms very airy & very comportable the rooms on the 6th floor at the back of the building face a brick wall 5 metres away... not a pretty sight & not the views as shown in the hotel literature. The room at the front of the hotel is very noisy with the local fire engines interupting our sleep three or four times a night & the noise from the subway reminded us of the scene in the 'Blues Brothers'
Caution for parents with young children.... the windows open wide & due to the narrow window ledge a child ( or adult for that matter) could very easily fall.
The rooms were very clean with exceptional work done by the ladies carrying out the cleaning in the room.The reception staff were great but this is the first american hotel that I have visited that didn't supply a porter to help with the baggage at check in.
The remainder of the staff were just "O/K" ....some friendly... some ignored you.
The hotel is ideally located for Times Square & Central Park... & if you want an inexpensive breakfast then the Olympic bar is just across the road.
The barman in the 'Pigallie' was very friendly ... swapping anecdotes whilst enjoying a late night drink ... prehaps one or two of the front of house staff could learn from his friendly approach
Overall the hotel is o/k but spoilt by a little to much noise 
PS
At the time of booking the Hotel were made aware of our celebration but did not acknowledge the fact whatsoever.

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “great location”
text: If you are going to Times Square area this is the best place to stay. Right in the middle of it all. We were able to walk all the way to Central Park. Not that far. Rooms were big. Had 2 adults and 2 kids ages 17 and 12 plenty of room. Prices are high in resturant food ok. Eat at Juniors across the street. Good food and they give you alot. Great Cheesecake. Saw Mary Poppins show it was wonderful. Would see it again. No problems with the elevators. Very fast. Stayed from June 30th to July 4th. People everywhere. Would stay here again. No noise from the street. Were on the 42nd floor. Staff was very helpful and very nice.

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Amazing Hotel, Amazing Location”
text: We booked this hotel having read great reviews on Tripadvisor and we were not disappointed. Infact the hotel exceeding our expectations by far. On arrival the hotel was oversold on our room type- studio, so we were upgraded to a two bedroom suite which was amazing. Fully fitted kitchen, spacious bathroom and very comfortable beds!! The staff were extremely friendly and could not have been more helpful. The hotel was only few blocks away from the Empire State Building, and a block away from the subway station which is on 33rd Street and Park Avenue. The Murray Hill Diner on 33rd street is an excellent place for breakfast and the deli next to the hotel is great for groceries. Duane Read is a chain of chemists where ypu can get all toiletries etc and drinks. There is practcally one on every block. Go to Ferreras on grand st between Mott and Mulberry St for great coffee and pastries- the oldest italian cafe in NY. Whole foods Market on Union square is worth a look for the variety of foods they sell. Century 21 Department store next to ground Zero has amazing bargains on designer clothes, shoes and bags. Enjoy NY!!

name: The Maritime Hotel
title: “Maritime is my #1 choice”
text:
I travel A LOT for my job, and am familiar with a variety of 5 star hotels from all over the World. When it is time for a personal trip to NYC... I ALWAYS stay at the Maritime. ALWAYS! It is fun, sexy, interesting, cool, and very hip. The location is fantastic, and you can walk just a few blocks to some of the best restaurants in the city.
If you want to have the feeling of living in a cool apartment in Manhattan... stay in one of their suites with the open air decks and outdoor shower. Hardwood floors, comfy sofa & chairs... the living room wall is lined with old National Geographics, and the wet bar is flawless. 
The beds - no matter what kind of room you choose - are all super comfortable.. with sexy white sheets and cozy duvet. Great views of the Hudson River... and you'll usually get a beautiful sunset from the higher floors.
The staff has always been very kind and gracious. Maritime has a nice vibe at the hotel - as opposed to so many other NY hotels that make you feel out of place and awkward.
I love the restaurant - Bottega - downstairs. Always great food, and has a really nice energy. You can get everything from Bottega through room service as well.
Whenever I get to NY... I always stay at the Maritime.
It really is the coolest place to stay in Manhattan.
I HIGHLY recommend it!
Chicago, IL

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Beste budget hotel voor gezinnen in NY”
text: Wij er geweest in Juli-08 met een kind van 2 jaar oud. En hebben de goedkoopste kamer genomen. We hebben ons verblijf als positief ervaren om de volgende redenen: - De kamers zijn groot (schoon maar wel ouder) - Ruime badkamer met bad - Het ligt op 2 min lopen van Central Park - Ligt Centraal + Goede bus/metro verbindingen met de rest van Manhattan - Indien nodig gratis een ledikant op de kamer - Ontbijt mogelijkeden ingesteld op gezinnen - Personeel is vriendelijk Er zijn ook veel gezinnen met oudere kinderen. Vooral de grote kamer is dan een +punt. Het hotel is minder geschikt voor koppeltjes, of voor een zakenreis

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Big and Beautiful”
text: The Marriott Marquis is an exciting Times Square hotel as big as the Big Apple and just as exciting. The room was very spacious, easily accommodating a rollaway bed along with 2 double beds. We were on the 23rd floor which blocked out almost all street noise. Rooms are very clean, well appointed, with a large plasma TV. The beds, pillows, and sheets were extremely comfortable. The elevators are outstanding and fun to ride. The 8th floor area also buzzes with fun with good restaurants and great views of Broadway.

name: The Muse Hotel New York
title: “Nice, Quiet, well kept secret!”
text: I have stayed at The Muse twice now and really enjoy it. The location near Times Square is very convenient. The staff is very nice and accomodating and I always seem to see someone famous there. I have heard the restaurant, The District, is great but have not had a chance to try it. The feather beds are the best part!

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Perfect”
text: Het Salisbury hotel ligt op loopsafstand van Boradway, Central Park, the 5th Avenue en vlak bij de belangrijkste metrolijnen, het is niet duur, de kamers zijn ruim, de bedden zijn fantastisch en het is er s nachts lekker stil. De staf is vriendelijk, het ontbijt is uitgebreid en voordelig en wie niet van plastic bestek houdt kan in een dan de tentjes in de directe omgeving heerlijk ontbijten. De kamers zijn ook nog eens voorzien van koelkast en waterkoker. Kleine minpuntjes: wat verouderd pand en iets langer wachten op de lift tijdens de "ontbijtspits" maar who cares als je alle andere voordelen van dit hotel beziet kan ik alleen maar concluderen dat de perfecte uitvalsbasis is voor een heerlijke vakantie in New York!

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Jederzeit wieder”
text: Das Zimmer/Suit war gepflegt und wurden täglich gereinigt. Der Service sehr zuvorkommend und hilfsbereit. Die Lage des Hotels war für die täglichen Ausflüge ideal. Das angebotene Frühstück ist günstig aber nicht unbedingt kulinarisch. Ansonsten jederzeit wieder.

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “My favorite in NYC”
text: We have an office right across the street and always stay at the Omni. This place is great and the restaurant and bar are very nice. The staff is very friendly and helpful as well. I think the room rate was reasonable for Madison Ave in NYC as well. Highly recommended!

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Exceeded Expectations”
text:
Just spent 3 nights at this hotel and was very impressed. We were on the 25th Floor and had the "Stay for Breakfast" rate. Thought this was well worth the money, as it entitled us to a great buffet breakfast, including juice, coffee, pancakes, and waffles in addition to the buffet items. The room was amazingly quiet, especially considering that the hotel is in the middle of Times Square. I am normally a very poor sleeper-but had 3 wonderful nights' sleep at this hotel. Not only was it very quiet, but the beds were extremely comfortable, and the room temperature was good too. The heating system was also very quiet, unlike those in many hotels. Took this trip as a tourist, and the hotel was very convenient to shopping, restaurants, and of course Broadway theaters. Staff was generally good. The hotel is large and modern in design; very striking. Obviously not the place if you are looking for a boutique hotel or personal service- but efficient, well-
located, and very comfortable.

name: The Muse Hotel New York
title: “Très bel hotel à 2 pas de Times Square”
text:
Cet hotel est hyper bien situé si vous séjournez pour la 1ère fois à NY car il est situé dans unne rue perpendiculaire au fameux TIMES SQUARE donc en 2 min à peine vous êtes sur les marches du TKTS (pr acheter vos billets de spectacle). L'hotel est assez chic, il a un beau bar, le matin vous pouvez profiter gratuitement de thé et café, et le soir d'un verre de vin en dégustation (je pense de 17 à 18h). Malheureusement nous n'avons profité de rien si ce n'est sa superbe situation. Les chambres sont spacieuses, très modernes, literie ultra confortable mais nous restons à 2 pas de Times Square et donc prévoir des boules quies pour ceux qui ont difficile de s'endormir (nous étions au 12ème étage et j'ai un TB sommeil mais j'ai qd même dû mettre des boules pour la 1ère fois de ma vie !!!!). En tt cas TB adresse.
Maintenant si c'était à refaire je ne mettrais plus ce prix là pour l'hotel car nous en avons vraiment peu profité et comme nous étions déjà venus à NY être si près de Times Square ne s'imposait plus. Lorsque nous y retournerons (ce qui est évidemment prévu ) ce sera plutôt du côté de Greenwich ou Soho. Mais cela n'enlève rien à la qualité de l'hotel.

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “great time had”
text:
This was our first visit to New York and we were a little apprehensive as to where to stay, I read some reviews and found very few bad ones so decided on the Marquis. After looking on the web very few hotels offered rooms for 3 adults(we were bringing our 21 year old daughter) We were very impressed with check in and had no trouble with the elevaitors. All the staff were friendly and helpful and the room was spotlessly clean. We were on the 42nd floor and had no trouble with noise and had a great view of the river. The breakfast buffett was a little expensive but lasted us all day. We used room service which was there within 20 minutes and my husband said his sirloin burger was the best burger he had ever tasted!
We would recommend this hotel to anyone.

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “Excellent stay, would definitely return.”
text: My daughter and myself recently stayed at the New York Palace for 5 nights; we had an excellent trip. The hotel is beautiful and as so many people have already stressed the location could not be better; walking distance from Central Park, Times Square, Rockefeller Centre, 5th Avenue shops, lots of eateries and close to several subway stations. We stayed in a lovely room on the 29th floor facing the cathedral and our view was outstanding. Rooms were kept extremely clean and all staff members were pleasant and helpful. The sensor snack tray was a dissapointment as very tempting for children to pick things up which you are then charged for, but that is my only complaint. Check-in and out were quick and efficient and the hotel stored our luggage until we needed to leave for the airport and provided us with a little room in which to sort through our bags whilst we were waiting for a taxi, which was helpful. We would definitely return.

name: The Michelangelo Hotel
title: “Très bon hôtel et très bien situé”
text: Cet hôtel, remarquablement bien situé, à tout juste quelques pas de Time Square est un véritable havre de paix dans la ville qui ne dort jamais. Les chambres sont très confortable, décorée dans un style italien (un peu "rococo" peut être ?!...) et relativement spacieuse pour le coeur de New York. Le personnel d'accueil est charmant et le concierge serviable et efficace (en plus, son français est remarquable...). Le prix, si il reste élevé, est tout a fait correct pour un établissement de cette gamme. Pour être vraiment à la hauteur, l'hôtel devrait tout de même revoir le prix de la connexion WiFi : près de 12$ par jour, c'est vraiment très élevé !

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “Not bad for NY”
text: Hotels in NY are notoriously bad value for money an in this context the Omni is not a bad deal. I paid USD 295, for a clean, quiet, modern and efficient room in a great location. No coffee maker in the room, but I did manage to get coffee and orange juice sent up at 5.30am. Everything works and the staff are about as helpful as you can expect in NY. There is a lively noisy bar and a decent restaurant in the hotel.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “O W sempre será uma boa escolha.”
text: Nossa estadia foi de 5 dias e adoramos o hotel , o bar eh o máximo , o atendimento perfeito , restaurante bacana e a localização perfeita para assistir os musicais.Os quarto sao menores que o W de Miami, mas muito bem decorados, o hotel nao tem piscina , mas estando na Time Square vc abre mão disso....

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “LOCATION COULDN'T BE GREATER”
text:
Stayed here for two nights with my Sister & 2 nephews. We had a room with 2 double beds & a view of Times Square. My nephews were happy that Toys R Us was right across the Street. You couldn't ask for a better location in Times Square. The room was nice, the beds comfortable. Close to the subway & to any transportation for that matter. The elevator System was best....you just punch in your floor & it directs you to which elevator to take..we never had to wait. 
Starbucks in the Hotel is great plus. The breakfast buffet is a little bit too pricey for those who don't like a big breakfast & I didn't feel it was worth the money. There are many restaurants to chose from..but please skip Bubba Gumps Shrimp Co...the food is below average & wasn't impressed with the service. Our salad (which we paid $5 extra for with a meal) came after our meal & only after we asked for it. 
Half price broadway ticket booth is temporary located there right on the property, but lines start quite early.

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “Can't Wait to Go Back!”
text:
I LOVED this hotel. 
We arrived 3 hours early... But they let us go into our room anyway,
The room was BIG.. Our view was perfect.
The staff here was fantastic.. Evan, our loyalty ambassador, contacted me a few days prior to our arrival and answered all my questions, thoroughly. Whenever I called the front desk, they greeted me by using "Mr." and my last name. The bellman got us a nice SUV to take us to the airport...
The location was better than I'd hoped for.. We were right near Rockefeller Center and just blocks from Times Square. I always felt safe coming from and going to the hotel.
Be sure to enroll in the select guest program... Free breakfast drinks and Wifi.
You won't regret staying here... Or at any Omni... This was my 3rd.

name: Hotel Metro
title: “Attention très très bruyant !!”
text: Hotel parfaitement situé mais attention excessivement bruyant. Les chambres coté cour sont situés pile au dessus d'une rangée de ventiations. C est simple j ai l impression de pas voir quitté l avion: j ai toujours le bruit des moteurs ds la tete !! Ca gache vraiment tout le reste qui pourait etre bien. Si vous etes fumeurs, vous aurrez la priorité sur ces chambres de seconde catégorie. Et oui le fumeur est un sous client à l Hotel Metro, meme si il paye le meme prix ...

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “Top Lage am Times Square mit Macken”
text:
Die Lage ist echt gut für NYC, direkt am Times Square. Empfang war freundlich uns hilfsbereit. 
Unsere Suite war zwar gross und geräumig aber jedoch sehr abgewohnt und nicht wirklich sauber. Fenster war so schmutzig, dass man fast nicht durchsehen konnte. Bad sehr klein aber zweckmässig. Bett wie meist bei W bequem. Frühstück war sehr dürftig im angeschlossenem Blue Fin Restaurant, Service war hier auch eher unmotiviert. Die Lobbybar ist ganz nett für einen Drink. Hab mir vom Hotel echt mehr erwartet. Für mich kein W Standard...

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “Great experience!”
text: Second time we stayed there. Wonderful experience. Great exercise room. Quiet convenient location. Be sure to join there members club for extra perks!

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “Fab Manhattan boutique hotel”
text: Just got back from a 3 night stay. Small room (bigger than Paris rooms though). Loved the bathroom -nice products,. large walk-in shower. Very clean and comfortable for a base. Front desk staff very helpful-happy to store luggage for a late flight home. Breakfast buffet seemed expensive so went elsewhere. Tea and coffee available in lounge but would've been nicer in rooms. Otherwise, excellent hotel, good location. No hesitation in recommending.

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “Great NY Value.”
text:
NYC is known for its expensive, small rooms. This hotel was no exception on the room-size, but we got it at half the cost of other hotels in Manhattan.
It is truly a boutique-style hotel with comfortable (although tiny) rooms with excellent bathrooms! The bed was really comfortable. This hotel had the best showers of any hotel I have ever stayed. Our rooms looked over a roof, but what do you expect in NY, a beach-front?
The rooms were extremely quiet at night, and I only heard someone leaving their room once. I never heard anyone out in the halls talking or making noise, which is typical at hotels. I've read other reviews were people complained about the garbage trucks and noise in the street, but what do you expect? You are staying in the USA's largest city, not Bodunk, North Dakota.
Great location, within walking distance of several subway stops and the Empire State Building and Grand Central Station. If you prefer to take a taxi, we saw the doormen running up to 31st and 5th to catch taxis to bring them back down to the front of the hotel (not many taxis came down 31st).
The breakfast buffet (they actually prepared the eggs and bacon to order) is expensive to standards in other cities ($18), but is comparable to other places we ate breakfast at in NY.
Negatives:
*The carpet needed to be cleaned. My mom's bedroom slippers turned black from walking on the carpet in the room.
*The hotel needs to install at least one ice maker somewhere in the hotel.
*The hotel staff had stored linen carts in the enclosed stairwell landings, which, in an already small stairwell, seemed really unsafe.
*Plugging in a computer was a little pain because you had to reach under the desk to plug it in. They need one of those lamps with plugs in the lamp like many other hotels have.
*The staff in the restaurant were not that attentive.

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “Great place, Good location and great extras”
text: Stayed here for 3 days during a trip to NY. We stayed by using the Priority awards points from IHG. The hotel was in a good location, 10 mins walk to Macys, and 10 mins to Times Square in the other direction. Clean hotel,nice little suite with double bed and kitchen area, friendly staff. The best thing was the extras...free wifi, buffet breakfast that you could take away & Free laundry.

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Not Terrible, But Not Great”
text: We stayed at Yotel for 5 nights starting April 5. It was our first trip to New York, so I don't know how the Yotel compares to other New York hotels, but I was not overly impressed. There were good things and bad things though, of course. We were travelling as a family and the bunk beds were a great option for us. It was also very clean and quiet (on the 16th floor) and we really liked the galley on each floor with the coffee machine. Free lattes are a great perk! But they aren't kidding when they say the rooms are small. There was only one chair in there for four people and it was very difficult to spend any extended amount of time in our room. The bathroom situation was also interesting. It was a beautiful big bathroom with a waterfall shower head, and there was a door on it, but there was no closing or locking mechanism on the door, and it didn't go all the way to the ceiling, which made for some privacy issues. Our biggest problems were with the beds and the concierge. The mattresses were thin and as hard as rocks. I've stayed at hostels with better quality beds. Apparently there were mattress toppers available but that information wasn't given to us until the day we checked out. It would have been nice to know that at check in, rather than check out. Because of the beds alone, we wouldn't stay here again. And the concierge, Ari, was horrible. He told us there was no point in trying to get Broadway tickets and the TKTS booth because there wouldn't be any available, and that we should buy tickets from him instead. This was a blatant lie made to try to sell us overpriced tickets from the hotel. We also tried to make dinner reservations at a particular restaurant and were told that the restaurant we wanted didn't take reservations, but that we could get reservations at a restaurant HE suggested. Another blatant lie. We declined and tried to walk in to our restaurant of choice and were told we couldn't get in WITHOUT a reservation. We also asked him where we should go for brunch. He made a suggestion and we asked him to make us reservations. He then looked at us like we were crazy and said "Oh there's no way you'll actually be able to get in there". Why make the suggestion then?! Overall, he was utterly unhelpful bordering on outright rude. The rest of the staff were very nice and helpful, though. The location wasn't terrible, but I thought it was out of the way; at least a 15 minute walk from Times Square and kind of out of the way. It wasn't the worst hotel I've ever stayed in, but I would not recommend it unless you can get it for cheap.

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Nearly in NJ!”
text: Loved the staff. Rooms large by NY standards. Clean and comfortable. The street and construction noise was so bad, we asked to move to a higher floor. Where the heat vent rattled loudly. Wifi was nearly useless. It is soooo far west I spent much pf my trip walking across town. And back. Price was great and I generally love Kimpton but the are 0 for 2 in noisy Manhattan.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Solo una parola....FANTASTICO!!!”
text:
Nel cuore di Manhattan...sulla Broadway...posizione favolosa a 1 minuto a piedi da Times Square.Appena uscirete dall'hotel sarete avvolti dalle luci Newyorkesi...fantastico!!!
L'hotel è vicinissimo alle metropolitane [ N,Q,R], [1] e [C,E];di fronte all'hotel M&M's World e sotto è presente Starbucks per la colazione.
Gli arredamenti sono moderni e molto carini.
Noi eravamo al 33° piano.La camera silenziosa, pulita e due letti meravigliosi.
Il bagno nella norma,nulla di speciale.
Il personale è cortese e alla reception sono disponibili per qualsiasi informazione.
Se avete bisogno di fare il web check-in per il vostro volo è possibile farlo gratuitamente in una sala apposita.
Vicino all'hotel sono presenti vari ristoranti e sulla 48th St la Masseria molto consigliato (a 1 minuto dall'hotel).
Superconsigliato!

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Cosa chiedere di piu'?”
text: Veramente bello ,personale cortese ,camere perfette,insomma tutto ok!!!

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “Spotless, family friendly and great location!”
text: We stayed here with our two kids over a weekend. The kids received travel packs when we checked in, and milk and cookies at turn down! Staff was super helpful and friendly. The hotel is a quick walk to Rockefeller center and not too far to Central Park. Overall a great stay, we will stay here again.

name: The Muse Hotel New York
title: “Perfekt für eine Städtereise nach NY”
text:
Das Hotel ist wohl etwas älter aber in einem sehr guten Zusatand.
Zimmer sind groß und sauber. Mit TV, Klimaanlage, Minibar, Safe.
Teilweise ist es etwas laut, Wir hatten ein Zimmer zur Straße hin,man hört schon die Geräusche der Stadt. Falls jemand einen leichten Schlaf hat sollte er nach einem Zimmer nicht zur Straße fragen.
Perfekt für eine Städtereise nach New York, nur ein paar Schritte vom Times Square entfernt.

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “Nice New York hotel in a good location”
text:
We wife and I stayed at Hotel Chandler, 3 days in the beginning of June 2005.
After reading reviews of the Hotel on TripAdvisor, we were a bit anxious upon arrival. 
We had booked our room at the Chandler Hotel through a Norwegian Travel Agency. They could not offer a De Luxe room, only Superior rooms. 
One month upon arrival, I contacted the hotel directly, and asked if I could pay for an upgrade to a De Luxe room. The manager asked my to take up the question upon arrival. We did so, but they told us then that all the De Luxe rooms allready were occupied. 
Fortunately we were offered a lager superior room, without any extras to pay. 
We got a corner room at the 9th. floor. It was very nice, fresh and clean, and the size of the room was guite all right.
We were very satisfied with our stay at the Chandler Hotel. We also find the Hotel's location great.
We did not see any cockroaches!
E.J.O.
Norway

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: We have just come back from a week in New York and were very pleased with the Hotel. Everyone was very friendly and helpful, nothing was too much trouble, (tourist information, transport etc.) and our rooms were enormous. Before going we asked for rooms on high floors with views which they arranged for us at no extra cost. Great location as so many things are within walking distance and there are plenty of places to eat close by including the Barking Dog which was great for breakfast. Very useful having the shop downstairs. I would recommend this hotel to anyone ,

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A fresh hotel with a fantastic rooftop bar”
text:
We chose to stay at the Ink48 for the last two nights of our week-long trip to New York. The hotel is situated close to the Hudson River, about a 20-minute-walk from the Times Square. Our room was more than big enough, clean and tidy, and had a comfortable bed and a magnificent city view. The staff was very friendly.
The breakfast in the hotel's restaurant was very good, but a bit expensive. If you go for it, make sure to try the homemade granola! If you prefer something simpler, there is a diner on the 11th Avenue.
Located on the roof is the hotel's most spectacular feature: The Press Lounge. This is Ink48's rooftop bar, probably one of the most spectacular ones on Manhattan. The skyline view is nothing less than fantastic, and the atmosphere is great. Definitely worth a visit!

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Loved it”
text:
Stayed here in August - lived this hotel. Rooms were big, great beds and a wonderful shower. Staff were great and one receptionist left the desk to call the lift for me when I was struggling to call the lift as my hand were full of the free tea and coffee they put out every morning. Loved the breakfast, which was pretty reasonable in price. 
The view from the rooftop bar was amazing but drinks are pricey. 
Location was great especially for the fantastic restaurants on 9th. 
Overall loved it and would definitely stay here again.

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Fab Hotel - Great Value!”
text:
Just returned from a 4 night stay at this hotel. Great rooms; nice size kitchen and bathroom along with plenty of space in the lounge. Staff were great, especially Donald who met us on our arrival with a big New York smile and helped us to our room. All the staff were very helpful and really made our stay great. Maids were very good, kept our rooms lovely and were not intrusive. Stay here, you'll love it only regret was that I didn't get time to go in the Spa!
Things I thought were extremely good:
1. Free use of internet to check-in and print off your boarding passes
2. Barking Dog restaurant next door, really good food and great for popping into at the end of a long day sightseeing
3. Size of rooms & comfort of beds
4. Size of bathroom - lots of mirrors / hair dryer / shower gel / shampoo etc
5. Good location close to Empire State and Macys along with local subway station
Well done to this hotel for being an absolute asset!

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Great hotel, be careful where you eat”
text: Excellent hotel, very large rooms. Quiet comfortable neighborhood close to subway. Eight block walk from Grand Central. If you like Asian food East is two blocks away and has fabulous food and service, reasonably priced. There are also some amazing delis close by,ask the hotel staff which ones are the best bet. Stay away from the restaurant at the hotel, and the Mexican around the corner is mediocre at best

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “great location in Midtown Manhatten”
text:
Had a most enjoyable 4 night break in NYC with our teenage kids - would highly recommend the NY Palace hotel. It a fab location , 2 mins to Rockefeller Plaza, 10/15 mins to 42nd Street , 20 mins to Empire State, and ten mins to all the main shops. Hotel has a shopping map for the un-initiated. We had really good size well equipped adjoining rooms on the 37th floor and had also booked to have access to the executive lounge - which I definitely recommend as they do light snacks throughout the day and unlimited free soft drinks and beer / wine (u may have to ask one of the staff) - NY isnt the cheapest place !! Breakfast is particularly good and buffet style. Night noise (road works are done at night) was still quite audible even on the 37th floor.
we didnt use the spa or the main restaurant which I believe is very good but enjoyed some casual fayre in the lovely outdoor garden / main entrance. free internet access in the lounge but 15 usd in your room per day
all in - a great place - will definitely be a great base for a first short trip

name: Renaissance New York Hotel Times Square
title: “Great hotel, great location and wonderful staff!”
text:
I stayed here for 14 nights with my husband and our two young sons (5 year old and a 22 month old) as part of our 5-week trip to the US. 
I chose this hotel because it looked very nice and we got a great long-term rate through Marriott direct @ $279 per night. This hotel is in a fantastic location, right in Times Square.
We arrived quite late at night and were greeted by a very friendly lady Gina at the front desk and Sayeed the door man. We had booked a standard room with a King Bed (plus rollaway and crib) and Gina thought that this room may be a little small for us seeing that we were staying 14 nights. Sure enough the room was a little small (would be fine without extra bed and crib) so Gina was nice enough to show my husband a few other room types that were available. So the following day we upgraded to the junior corner suite for an extra $90 per night. She also offered us breakfast (which was not included in our rate for $40 per day for the four of us, which was great. They also sent us another fridge so that we could store the kids food in. Rooms were lovely and clean.
Sayeed has kids himself so he made some great suggestions of places to visit and eat with the kids. He honestly was one of the nicest people we have met. Whenever he would see us, he would always greet us and our kids. Both our boys loved to greet him.
Breakfast was really nice. All the waiters at breakfast were very friendly and great. They would even play with our kids, which was nice. We ordered room service quite a few times and the food was lovely. Loved their chicken burgers!
Housekeeping is fantastic; whenever we would call for something they were always very quick to respond.
All the staff were lovely and very friendly. Everything was great about this hotel, I honestly cannot think of anything to fault them.

name: The Michelangelo Hotel
title: “zentral, freundlich, sauber”
text: Ich habe eine Woche mit meiner Tochter dort verbracht. Wir waren sehr zufrieden. Die Zimmer sind groß die Betten superbequem. Die Lage ist sehr zentral und doch relativ ruhig.Der morgentliche Kaffee und die Croissants sind eine nette Geste des Hotels und werden von allen Gästen geschätzt. Ich würde dieses Hotel dem Walldorf Astoria, in dem ich auch schon gewohnt habe, wieder vorziehen, da die Zimmer renoviert sind und im Vergleich das Preis/Leistungsverhältnis einfach stimmt.

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “Perfect hotel for NYC visit!”
text:
Choosing a hotel in NYC can sometime be a difficult choice. This was a great choice! The rooms were comfortable, spacious, very clean, no bedbugs, fully stocked kitchenette. The complementary breakfast and Happy Hours really helped keep costs down and were a real convenience. There was a lot of choice for both and the staff were always refilling and cleaning up the area.
The bed was one of the most comfortable I have had in a hotel. The room was modern, quiet, lots of storage and a great bathroom.
I cannot say enough great things about this hotel, including the price. I will definitely stay here again when I visit NYC.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Au coeur de times square!”
text:
Cet hôtel est idéalement bien placé si vous voulez être au coeur de Brodway. Les chambres sont propres et bien agencées;elles ne sont pas très grandes mais à New York on ne reste pas beaucoup dans sa chambre.
Les lits ne sont pas très larges mais la literie est bonne ce qui compense largement.
La salle de bain est corecte avec deux vasques et une baignoire, en revanche les wc sont à l'intérieur de celle-ci.

name: Salisbury Hotel
title: “Excelente hotel”
text:
Viajabamos 8 de familia, 4 adultos y 4 niños, las habitacione eran grandes con dos camas dobles,etaban limpias al igual que el baño. El desayuno estaba incluido y era tipo continental , con café ,zumos y bolleria, nada del otro mundo , pero suficiente para comenzar el dia si no eres alérgico a los dulces y dejas la dieta para otro dia.La situacion del hotel es excelente, a un paso de Central Park,Columbus Circle y de la 5ª avenida, con bocas de metro en la misma calle y a escasos metros.
Para concluir es un Hotel que como casi todos los del centro de Manhattan tiene muchos años , pero tiene un buen servicio de mantenimiento y por el precio y situación es una opcion a considerar.

name: The Muse Hotel New York
title: “das hotel muse war genial!!!”
text:
das hotel ist einfach klasse.
wir waren ja schon oft in amerika in grossen hotels
aber keines kann mit diesen mithalten in allen belangen
wer nach nyk fährt und nimmt das muse ist bestens versorgt.
wir auf jedenfalls immer wieder.

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Tiny room, mediocre service, meciocre location.”
text: The room was about the size of a walk-in closet, and was not exceptional in any way. The staff were not terribly helpful. The location was a bit removed from the activities that we were involved in. I was presenting for a conference, and my wife came with me. Neither of us were terribly impressed.

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “The location can't be beat”
text: The Omni Berkshire was such a pleasant surprise. The accommodations were comfortable and the staff was incredible. You can't go wrong if you book here. If I had to create a downside, I would say that none of the rooms really have a great view. But who cares, you are in NY to explore the city not to stay in your room all day. If you stay here, visit Isadora's across the street for breakfast and Crumbs (yummy cupcakes) is right around the corner. And I have to mention that Saks is a block and a half away along with tons of other high to mid range shopping.

name: Renaissance New York Hotel Times Square
title: “Jill at front desk”
text:
Stayed at the renaissance July 2 - 4, 2011. I always stay in marriot hotels. Wow ! I had a great time, right from check in to check out. Beautiful hotel, my room was wonderful and the walk in shower was mind blowing . To crown it all, Jill at the reception was exceptional, she was very professional and gave an excellent customer service. Looking forward to my next stay....oh beautiful lobby with free wi-fi
George from Nigeria

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Really, really good hotel - highly recommended”
text: Excellent position within the City - walking distance of Times Square, Fifth Avenue shopping etc and also close to the open-top bus routes as well. Not so close that there was a lot of noise though. Had the best nights sleep I've had for a long time at this hotel. Very large rooms for NYC, complete with sitting area and kitchen and although the consumables provided by the hotel (e.g water, sweets etc) were expensive they were top quality. Hotel staff were excellent and service was top notch from start to finish. Didn't try the Spa but it also has an excellent reputation and discounts are available to hotel residents. The restaurant next door (The Barking Dog) was great too - friendly staff, wide-ranging menu and nice outdoor seating area. Cannot find anything bad to say about this place - excellent value for money, would recommend it to anyone.

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Can't ask for anything more.”
text: Very pleased with our stay at the Affinia. Our room was ready early morning which was great considering we had just caught the red eye from San Francisco. The staff were all very helpful and friendly. All very knowledgeable about the area, what to see, where to go, how to get there etc. Very handy having a little kitchen in your room and a laundry in the basement. 7 kinds of pillows available from housekeeping. There was a 24hr deli just 2 doors down which had all of the essentials. Great location. Within a couple of blocks of a subway station. Easy walking distance to Empire State building. A nice stroll to all the good shops, Times Square, etc. Would definitely stay there again and recommend it to all leisure travellers.

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Excellent service at an excellent hotel”
text:
I set up a NYC trip for my girlfriend's 21st birthday and asked Ink48 if there were any special touches that could be made; John, the front office manager, took care of everything and then some. Jay, the concierge, was also very helpful. These two individuals truly made our stay the best I've had anywhere yet. Any emails I sent were replied to almost instantly, and the one thing I had a question/worry about was handled within 5 minutes on a busy Saturday night!
The city view studio king room we had was huge: spacious bathroom with double sinks, rainfall shower, and a soaking tub leading right into the bed area, overlooking the city skyline.
One slight minus might be the AC unit, it was a bit rattly. The comfy bed helped make up for it, but there were a few times where it'd kick on and startle me.
As others have said, it's really just a quick walk away from the Times Square area, straight down the road actually. If you're quick walkers like us, it'll take barely 10 minutes. From there you can catch the Times Square subway station to go anywhere.
We had breakfast at two nearby diners, the Galaxy diner and the Westway diner, just a 5 minute walk away near 9th Ave. Cheap and delicious way to start the day. We also had dinner in the same area; there are many, many places to eat in the area if you walk just one avenue down!
Valet parking was expensive (for me) at $55/night with no in/out privileges, but on a hot, busy NYC summer day it was worth it. I tried driving around to find a parking lot, but most were full, one was closed down, and yeah, NYC traffic is the last thing I wanted to deal with before checking in.
We walked to the theater district for a show on Friday night and there were no issues with the neighborhood or area, it was well-lit and felt fine.
The rooftop bar provides even more great views, and the drinks were strong (and slightly expensive). There's a loose dress code, so leave your flip-flops and Ed Hardy shirts in the hotel room.
I'm sure I've bored you by now, but overall, all of our needs were taken care of and we had a wonderful time!

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great position, Great views”
text: We stayed in Ink48 with a small group of travellers for a 50th birthday. The hotel is very welcoming and efficient. It's situated on 48th St & 11th Avenue in Manhattan. Very close to Hells Kitchen where there are some fantastic restaurants & bars, and only about 4 blocks from Times Square. If you get into the higher floors you can see some of the Times Square billboards. Make sure you are back from sightseeing about 5pm as there is a wine tasting every day, a nice way to finish the day while you ponder where to go for dinner. Overall a lovely place to stay.

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “Great but new marketing guy indicates a change in philosophy”
text: We had a lovely stay - great location, WONDERFUL CONCIERGES... the most knowledgeable and helpful in all of Manhattan I believe (we've stayed at so many fine hotels and they were amazing). Our room was great (we asked for an upgraded one to celebrate a birthday. Annoyance - when we checked in the bellman asked us if we'd like complimentary coffee/tea pot in our room and we said yes. That morning we enjoyed both and when we came back the pot was there but the cups were removed. We called and asked housekeeping for cups for the next dayand no answer, called other lines, no help. Next day same thing andcould never get it to work. Beverage people blamed it on HOUSEKEEPING (WHY DON'T THEY WASH THE CUPS?), Housekeeping said it wasn't their job and never notified beverage department. I sent an email about this simple issue and no response. Finally I sent it to a manager and got a call - HOW NICE! However, he told me that they had no business providing complimentary equipment, that there is no system in place to handle it, they want their guests to use food and beverage and he worked for the FOUR SEASONS for 15 years and that's how they did it. Never offered me anything other than "not complimentary", I was turned off - There are other 4-5 star hotels in NY!

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Good location, very noisy”
text:
I really liked the location of this hotel, at 11th and 48th, just off the Hudson river. It's a smaller, chic hotel, with a great restaurant, great bar and lounge, and great bartenders! Our room was a bit on the small side, though elegantly furnished. There was no bathtub. The staff is friendly and efficient, and there was a nightly wine hour for guests. The rooftop bar is possibly one of the best I've ever been to, with an incredible view of the city (facing toward Times Square and Hell's Kitchen) and the Hudson river.
There were two major drawbacks that reduced the rating from 5 to 4 stars. One was the window coverings. There are no drapes, only a modern style white shade, so at 5am when the sun comes up, the room is very bright. Had I known, I would have brought eyeshades. 
The second problem is the noise. We were on the 7th floor in a corner King facing 11th ave and it sounded like we were on a runway at LAX the entire time. There was construction noise, traffic noise and loud horns from the massive cruiseliner that docks just next door. We asked to be moved to a higher floor facing the river and that made a huge improvement. So make sure to ask them for a quiet room, but overall I would definitely recommend this hotel.

name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria
title: “Short holiday with Family”
text:
The Towers is more like an apartment extension of the main Waldorf hotel with its own side entrance. 
We booked through Brenda at New York City Luxury Hotels and received great service and an excellent room rate.
Initially we were a little disappointed with the tiny lobby and were asked to wait for our room in the breakfast/tea lounge which is very cramped. (Breakfast is very average and often over crowded).
However our room was soon ready and we were really delighted to be upgraded to a huge two bedroom suite on the top floor that really defined our holiday.
We did have a problem with the plumbing in the master bathroom and this was efficiently sorted and apology given.
The reception and concierge staff were exceptional during our stay and made all arrangements very easy. Housekeeping staff were also very helpful.
There is easy direct access to/fro the main hotel and the location is great.
All in all an excellent stay.

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Perfect Location, Great People, Unbelievably Large Rooms”
text:
I just walked into the door of my room and immediately opened my computer to write a review of this hotel because it is that good! The lady at the front desk was great, and I really enjoyed talking to her. When I walked in my room I couldn't believe how big it was and it has a kitchen! I have never stayed in a hotel room with a kitchen and not had to pay extra for it. The location is wonderful - you can be most places you would want to go in the city with a 12 minute walk and if not the subway is close by. 
Definitely recommend this hotel.

name: W New York - Times Square
title: “whatever, whenever”
text: Das ist das "Motto" des Hotels. Und genauso ist es. Alle Mitarbeiter sind super freundlich und hilfsbereit. Den Concierge kann man fragen was man will, er/sie hat für alles eine Lösung oder Tipp. Sie empfehlen Restaurants, reservieren Tische, buchen die Sitzplätze im Flugzeug etc. Die Zimmer sind für New York geräumig und man hat allen Komfort den man sich wünscht. Der Living Room in der 7. Etage ist eine super angenehme Lounge/Bar in der man immer gerne verweilt und im Restaurant Blue Fin im EG gibt es leckeres Frühstück (allerdings nicht ganz billig). Zentraler als in diesem Hotel kann man in NY nicht wohnen. Dafür zahlt man den Preis, dass immer was los ist, rund um die Uhr. Also für Menschen die die Ruhe suchen ist das Hotel nichts. Aber für die ist NY wahrscheinlich auch nichts.

name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria
title: “What a great stay!”
text: Although the safe and closet light didn't work and never got fixed while we were there, the management sent us a bottle of wine as an apology. We appreciated the gesture. Location is excellent, service very friendly and also excellent. Room was spacious (we got a corner room) with magnificent views. I would definitely recommend it and would stay there again. Breakfast was very nice. Had cold cuts and boiled eggs in addition to various pastries, yogurt and cereals. The Towers are quite different from Astoria. Much more relaxed and cozy. With a secluded feel in the middle of a busy city. My only reason for less than 5 stars is that the bathrooms could use some upgrading.

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “As expected............superb”
text:
Just returned from a three night stay at the New York Palace and had an absolutely great time. The location is great and the staff are extremely pleasant and very professional. This hotel is top of the range and was offered an upgrade from deluxe room to a room with a view of St Patrick Cathedral at $35 per night or a corner room at $50 per night which we declined as we had gone to see New York and not spend time in our room. However the only minor criticism was that I was slightly dissappointed in the small bathroom and standard Molton Brown toiletries. I also noted that most people breakfasted outside the hotel and Starbucks across the road did a roaring trade from people popping over.
The whole experience was fascinating and sitting in the busy lobby people watching was very interesting.

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “Hotel Chandler Manhattan”
text:
Ottimo suggerimento.
Ottimo rapporto qualità prezzo ed una speciale menzione per il personale della Recpetion, molto disponibile paziente e professionale.
La posizione dell'albergo è ottima nel pieno centro di Manhattan.

name: Morgans Hotel
title: “Great location, very nice staff”
text: Me and my wife stayed at Morgans for 9 nights. It was our first trip to New York. I have to say that I don't think we could have chosen a better hotel for our needs. The location was brilliant. All the great stores were within walking distance, so is Madison Square Garden, Empire State Building (right around the block) and Central Park. Special thanks must go to the hotel staff - everyone was very nice and helpful. When we go back, we will definitely stay at the same place.

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Great value for money”
text: We are a couple in our 50ies, this is unlike anything else we had experienced before. Funky, modern, spotless, functional, friendly staff, soundproof rooms. Roms were, as expected, more the size of cabins on a cruise boat then a regular hotel, but than again travelling to NY we needed just a crash space. No breakfast, but good coffee and muffins gave us a great start for the day. The toilet having a glass door did not cause any problem, as a separating curtain was there to insure privacy. Walking distance to nearest metro/ sub station is10 mins( Times Square).

name: TRYP Times Square South
title: “Family Emergency made easier”
text:
We were only at TRYP for 45 minutes, but the service they extended to us made a family emergency less painful. 
We checked in on November 29th. After settling into our room we received some bad news about a loved one and had to head home. When I went to the front desk and explained the situation, the person behind the counter couldn't have been nicer. I told him I would understand if we would still have to pay for the room. He went out of his way to see if there was any kind of break they could give us, and ultimately they didn't charge us for the room. I'll be calling to thank them directly, but I thought this kind of serviced deserved to be highlighted here also.
Thank you!

name: The Bowery Hotel
title: “Perfect Hotel in Perfect Location”
text: We have just returned from three nights at this hotel and I spent the last day begging my husband to extend our trip - that's how much I loved it. The Bowery Hotel is a wonderful little hotel in the best location - lots of great restaurants and shops on the doorstep and 2 subway stations within 5 minutes walk. The room was so comfortable - they provide everything you need. We had a queen room on the 11th floor and it was a good size and had a great view - perfect for a couple on a short break and really great value for money. The hotel has an old school charm but being new it has all the modern technology you could need (including free wifi and a stupid number of electrical sockets in the room). The staff are very friendly and courteous and seem genuinely happy in their work. It really did feel like home for the time we were there and I don't see myself staying anywhere else in nyc on future visits.

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “Hotel Chandler, unmittelbar am Empire, gute Ausgangslage für Downtown and Uptown Ausflüge”
text:
freundlicher Empfang im Hotel, zeitweise deutschsprachiges Empfangspersonal. Tee und Kaffee ganztägig, internet in der lobby
die 31ste Strasse liegt in Midtown, man ist schnell zum Broadway oder zum Central Park. U-bahn oder Busverbindungen nutzen oder laufen
Empire direkt an der Straßenecke
waren jetzt 2 Jahre hintereinander dort, immer zu empfehlen!
Das einzige was im Hotel nicht ist, eine super Aussicht,

name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria
title: “All what I expected...and more!”
text: What a nice feeling is to meet the expectations I had from an institution like Waldorf Astoria in NYC! I had an incredible stay. The suite I had was breath taking, the staff at the Front Desk, Lounge and of course the Concierge ( best I ever experience) made the best possible welcome I could ever got to NYC. Highly recommended!

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “Hidden Gem”
text: My husband, sister, brother & I stayed here last weekend. We had a FABULOUS stay!! The hotel is beautiful! The front desk was great with putting our rooms “on priority” so we could check-in a little early. I had reserved a King & a Double room. Both rooms were excellent. Super clean! The beds were great. My husband actually commented, he wished he could bring it home. You receive substantially more than you ever would in another NYC Times Square hotel. Breakfast was complimentary. I was expecting your basic coffee & roll… more like eggs, bacon, fresh fruit and more. It was excellent! Free internet and even free laundry! It’s just off the beaten trail of Times Square, super easy to get too. Jamie, our bellman, was extremely friendly and helpful! The staff was incredibly nice. I would highly recommend this hotel… we’ll definitely be back!!

name: Morgans Hotel
title: “Great Location..Excellant Staff...Clean and Spacious Rooms”
text:
If you are walking on Madison Ave you may not realize the hotel exists as there is no large sign or flags to tell you so. In the vicinity of the hotel there is a deli, laundromat, convenience store among other things. 
Check-In
The check-in was smooth and fast. The lobby is relatively small but it feels warm. The front desk was very friendly. The bell man was ready to assist with my carry on bag.
Room
I had a suite which had a large living room and the furniture is very comfortable and makes you feel you are in your own home. The down comforter which they have was great. The mattress is a bit soft for me since at home I sleep on a Tempur-Pedic but it was still a good night sleep. 
Beware: I am travel alot and generally use the laundry bags in the closets to put clothes I need washed. Morgans will charge you 25$ if you take their laundry bag so watch out. 
View-
We had a beautiful view looking Madison ave and to the left you could see the Empire state building. 
Bathroom-
Was a bit small but the shower was great. More importantly everything was clean. 
Electronics-
Everything worked from the TVs, the IPod dock, Telephones, etc. 
Suggestion: Ask for a room above the 13th Floor.

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Perfect Hotel in a perfect location!”
text:
My partner and I stayed at the Dumont for 3 nights in October and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The staff were extremely helpful and sorted out a couple of problems we had with the room swiftly. The room was excellent in terms of size as most of the centrally located hotels have boxes for rooms. If you want space to spread out all those purchases then this is the place for you!
The Metro is only a block away, as is the Murray Hill Diner which was fantastic for breakfast. Being on 34th St means that all of the main attractions are in easy walking distance. We did use the Metro a few times but that was only because we wanted to venture further afield. 
We would highly recommend the Dumont for location, sizeable rooms and friendly helpful staff. We will definately be staying here again when we visit NYC.

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “JUST THE BEST!”
text: What an honor to stay in such a beautiful hotel! First class all the way . We're just back from an 8 day stay @ The New York Palace.. Can't wait to go back. First Class all the way with wonderful staff including Chi An (Angie) @ the check-in desk and Joyce L @ the Concierge desk. Both were so pleasant and helpful.

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “impeccable”
text: Hôtel à taille humaine, très bien situé, au pied de l'Empire State Building, Macy's...Le personnel était accueillant, charmant et toujours prêt à rendre service. Notre chambre était petite, mais au calme, propre et très confortable. Café, thé, accès internet à volonté et à toute heure.

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Sleepless in newyork”
text: I recently stayed in Yotel hotel in newyork with my family and had such a bad experience at yotel and it kinda ruined our whole trip,, very bad service and totally unfriendly staff,, very small rooms ,, no coffee or soap in the room and bedroom and bathroom are devidid by a curtain only

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Nice, Clean Cozy Hotel”
text: Booked via Travelocity eight months in advance and got a great deal for five nights. Checked in after late flight and staff was very accomodating. Loved our little cozy room on the 3rd floor corner with large windows on both side. I did not want to stay up high and location was perfect; had a view of back of old buildings, but I did not mind since it reflected old NY. Room was clean, beds nice, Jr Suite with desk and comfortable chairs. We did ask for an ottoman for feet and they delivered one immediately. Small kitchen perfect for snacks and cooking breakfast. Murray Hill deli & pharmacy down street to stock up. I would pack essential items if come back to save on money, pharmacy nearby is expensive as anything convienient usually is; but deli nearby is fabulous for quick food. Fresh fruit on every corner and restaurants everywhere. Small cozy restaurant connected to hotel (Barking Dog), perfect for dinner the first night since arrived tired. Great patio to eat ouside. Grilled shrimp salad is great along with the scallops. We had a small pizza one night there and it was very good. Cozy spot to drop in for drinks, also to grab coffee in morning. Hit the Spa the first morning to chill from a stressful flight. Get Amy to do the neck and head massage. She is great! Spa is very relaxing. One negative about hotel: don't reserve a car from the front desk. We specifically ask for a Town Car to take us somewhere special one day, and they had their driver meet us in an SUV; needless to say it was a luxury model, but very rough. We got the door-man to get us a Town Car to go to airport. Stick with the door-guys, they are on top of it all. The staff otherwise were very nice. Love the location-- a great place to stay and we will return.

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Loved this Hotel and New York”
text: We stayed at the Marriott Marquis New York Times Square for New Year's 2006 for 4 nights. All the staff were super friendly and our room and beds were immaculate. Even during New Year's the elevators were accessible and not much wait. This hotel wants to make your stay in New York a pleasant one and they certainly did ours. Thank you very much for showing us how nice New Yorkers can be.

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “great hotel very friendly and helpful staff”
text: This is a great hotel . only a few months open, staff are extremely helpful and very friendly. Little mix up on arrival but sorted out in no time. Gorgeous rooms very comfortable beds, lovely bathrooms. Only a couple of blocks from times square. Great breakfast only gripe is restuarant room a little small for size of hotel. would definatelt go back there and would recommend this hotel to anyone. Saying hello to Sonny and Jaimie two great bellboys.

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “A high 3... a 3.8”
text:
First the pros: (a) brand new, (b) free guest laundry, (c) good sized rooms that come equipped with a full sized refrigerator, stove, microwave, plates, glasses, and utensils, (d) free WiFi, (e) LCD TV with over 200 channels (many in HD), (f) friendly staff, and (g) free breakfast. 
Cons: (a) quality of food on offer for breakfast was so so... I still can't get over the horrid scrambled eggs - I found the eggs such a turn-off that I ate breakfast in area diners for the remainder of my stay, (b) food choices in the breakfast buffet were likewise fairly limited, (c) breakfast room was small, so small that it gets very crowded during breakfast, (d) the hallways are narrow, (e) only three washers and dryers in the guest laundry, it was not an issue for me but I can imagine that as the hotel fills up with longer staying guests, it may become very hard to come by an unused washer or dryer, (f) housekeeping, cleaning standards seemed to vary from day to day, and (g) location, right beside port authority on a not very nice side street. Not to say that the area isn't safe because it is but aesthetics wise it could be better.
A word about the rooms, I booked a high room with a NYC view and got one on the 13th floor facing the hotel on 39th. Bit disappointed there. At least there was sufficient separation between the two buildings to allow sunlight in. My room was located right beside two elevators but I didn't hear any elevator noise. Amazed (and thankful) for that! Design wise the rooms were functional but not very stylish or cutting edge. A bit more pizazz would have been nice.
Overall, Staybridge Times Square offers very good value for the USD250-300 per night price range I paid. Shorter staying guests would probably have less use for the in-room kitchen or the guest laundry but it's nice to know the're there just in case one needs it.

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Excellent stay, and a concierge that rocks!”
text:
Just imagine this: After a long exhausting day, you enter the chic, modern Dumont in a quiet place only a few minutes from the Empire State buidling, you take the elevator to your private, cosy 2 beedroom suite in the 31st floor, stand next to the window and unwind while looking the red sun touches the Chrysler buildling. This hotel is fantastic and so much different. We loved every piece of it, and the panorama was so relaxing as it gave you a feeling of freedom and “space” in a city that makes you feel small. The staff is great, but the absolutely best is the witty, british-accent speaking concierge that works from Monday to Wednesday, he simply rocks! 
Tip: *TKTS... “Rock of Ages” and “In the heights”

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Great location”
text: I traveled to New York with my 2 teenage daughters for a vacation and shopping. I thought the hotel was wonderful. The room was large, the bed was comfortable and the view breathtaking. The elevators were not an issue and the only times we waited were at peak traffic times, mainly before and after theatre. We only waited more than a couple of minutes on 2 occasions. I found everyone friendly and accomodating. The area was safe and we walked a several block radius after dark. There was not a shortage of cabs and the subway was close by. One morning we walked all the way to Bloomingdales! I would highly recommend this hotel for quality and location. This was my first trip to New York and I hope not my last. We loved it.

name: TRYP Times Square South
title: “Excellent hotel with very helpful staff”
text:
Excellent new hotel, my wife and I had a room on the 5th floor for 3 nights on October 10-12. it was very clean and surprisingly quiet considering it was overlooking 35th street which isn't a main thoroughfare. Not very far from '34th street and Penn Station' subway station. The Time Square South part of the hotel's name is a little misleading as it is within walking distance (quite a long walk!) of Time Square. I think any closer to Time Square and Broadway would be very noisy as there were thousands (literally) of people in these areas at 11 pm and all the shops were open!
Staff were very helpful with a mix up over vouchers we were expecting for sightseeing bus trips and airport pick ups (not the hotels fault) and it was all quickly sorted out. Thanks to Kiana, Christina and Engel for sorting it all out!

name: The Bowery Hotel
title: “Bowery Hotel is a gem”
text: We celebrated our 10-year anniversary with a two-night stay at the Bowery Hotel. Even though we were in the least-expensive room class (standard queen), the room was spacious, luxuriously appointed with a huge bathroom that had an incredible soaking tub, and we had two walls of floor-to-ceiling windows. Pluses: the clientele was a bit older (40+) -- lots of Europeans, too. I was happy to be in a hotel with this mix, as I was concerned that my husband and I might feel a bit long in the tooth at such a hot boutique hotel. The staff was incredibly accommodating and courteous. Gemma, the hotel's restaurant, served a great breakfast at a reasonable price. The neighborhood is vibrant and hip -- still a little seedy, but we like that mix. The little cajun restaurant on Great Jones, across from the hotel, was cozy and delicious (and reasonable!). The minuses (not enough for me to give the hotel less than five stars, though): the neighborhood is noisy. Perhaps it was the windows (that I wouldn't want to do without!), but Bowery is a very busy thoroughfare, and the honking taxis seemed to be bustling into the wee (read 3 a.m.) hours of the night. Some people might want a fancier neighborhood, but we love the vibrancy of this area. Yes, the room was pricey ($495/night), but we could have spent the same money elsewhere in Manhattan and gotten a lot less. I'd highly recommend this hotel ... but selfishly I want to keep it a secret! ;o)

name: Renaissance New York Hotel Times Square
title: “Great Hotel!”
text:
This hotel is fantastic! I was sorry we only had this room for just one night. The room was probably the biggest room I've ever had in a Manhattan hotel. The location is perfect if you want to be in the middle of the NYC action, as the hotel is right at the north tip of Times Square. If you're a theatre fan, the TKTS booth is literally right across the street. You're within walking distance of Central Park and several subway options. 
If you're looking for great restaurants, go 1 block west and 2 blocks down to Restaurant Row on 46 St between 8 and 9 Avenues. Our favourite there is Le Rivage. The best pizza you will find is Patzeria on 46 Street just west of Broadway. It's a tiny hole in the wall, and is more of a takeout place, but it has a loyal following among the theatre crowd.
If there was anything to criticize, it's the fact that you can still hear some street noise from our 14th floor room. But considering that you're in Times Square, it's not surprising.

name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria
title: “Beautiful Rooms, Top Notch Service”
text: I stayed at The Towers while attending the NYC premier of "Just Go With It." The location was convenient for appointments, restaurants, and shopping. My suite was super clean and beautifully appointed. The daily housekeeping service was thorough. The continental breakfast on the 26th floor was more than expected -- a great variety that includes salmon, 3 different types of granola cereal and fresh berries. The concierge and doormen were helpful and friendly. I had everything I wanted in a luxury hotel -- and more.

name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria
title: “My wedding at the waldorf”
text:
I got married in a suite at the Towers and had the reception in Peacock Alley. The suite was the most expensive one with a HUGE living room, dressing room, HUGE bedroom, bathroom, two study areas, massive hallway...it was an incredibly beautiful room. The furnishings are so classic, the views amazing. My wedding co-ordinator Carmen was wonderful too. We had a small wedding party of 23 so it wasnt the large grand wedding that usually takes place at this hotel but the smallish size of Peacock Alley private dining room was perfect. The food was delicious and the staff at the wedding meal were fantastic.
Having stayed at the regular Waldorf twice before but not the towers, I can say the difference was worth paying for. The service at reception and concierge was so much better, no queue at all, phone answered right away etc, whereas in the regular hotel you can wait ages at the reception desk or on the phone to guest services. 
I had a wonderful wedding there - I got a night free and stayed 3 nights which made it a bit more affordable. I wouldnt hesitate to recommend getting married at the Waldorf, a timeless, classic, beautiful venue for any wedding, large or small.
The free breakfast in the Towers lounge was also great - and if you can, get a window table there as the view is incredible!

name: The Bowery Hotel
title: “great place”
text:
Stayed at the Bowery 2 nights in June. I thought it was a great stay overall. The hotel was interesting and comfortable, while still feeling cool . My room had been "upgraded" to a king on the 7th floor. Although it was a pretty small room, it was very well decorated and the bed was large and comfortable. The best thing about the room, however, was the fact that 2 walls were floor to ceiling windows, giving me a fabulous view of downtown by night and a refreshing view of the grassy courtyard(?) by day. Who knew there was a strech of open land in the middle of New York? These windows made the room feel much larger than it really was and really added a magnificent touch to my stay in the city. As a woman travelling alone I felt comfortable walking in the neighborhood by myself. I loved the hotel's convenience to the East Village, SOHO, Chinatown, etc. I usually stay in Midtown, but loved being in this area. 
The staff were very nice and helpful, although some guests were having trouble checking in when I arrived.
I would definitely stay at the Bowery again.

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Top-Hotel in perfekter Lage”
text:
Das Crowne Plaza liegt direkt am nördlichen Ende des Times Square. Zu Fuß ist man in ca. 2 Minuten mitten in der LED-Werbetafel-Welt des Times Square. Viele ander Sehenswürdigkeiten, z.B. das Rockefeller Center sind in ca. 10 Minuten zu Fuß zu erreichen und auch die 5th Avenue ist weinige Minuten später erreicht. Zum Central Park kann man auch gut zu Fuß gelangen.
Wer Musicals besuchen möchte, der ist im Crowne Plaza direkt am Ort des Geschehens. Sämtliche Broadway Musicals sind in unmittelbarar Nähe. Passend zum Theaterbesuch bietet das Hotelrestaurant, die Barsserie 1605, ein so genanntes Pre-Theatre-Dinner an. Das preisgünstige und kulinarisch sehr zu empfehlende und Drei-Gänge Menü bietet die optimale Einstimmung auf einen schönen Abend. Nach dem Musicalbesuch kann man den Abend gemütlich an der Hotelbar ausklingen lassen, die mit leckeren Cocktails und einer riesigen Auswahl verschiedener Martinivariationen lockt.
Besonders zu empfehlen sind auch die Panoramazimmer. Hier hat man den Ausblick auf Manhattan durch eine 90 Grad Fensterfront. Wir hatten ein Zimmer mit Blick auf den Hudson River, alternativ steht noch die Aussicht zum Times Square zur Verfügung. Trotz der sehr zentralen Lage, hat man im Hotelzimmer kaum noch den Straßenlärm wahrgenommen.
Wir würden dieses Hotel jederzeit wieder buchen.

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “NYC birthday fun”
text: Second stay at a Kimpton & I'll continue to try the boutique chain. The good: excellent rate, birthday upgrades, 4* restaurant, 5*rooftop bar. The bad: hard to reach concierge who forgot to make dinner reservation.

name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria
title: “Grande Dame still the Great One”
text: It's great to see the hotel is still at the top of the game. Cleanliness, service, professionalism and overall quality are all present and accounted for. All the staff seem happy in their jobs and really try to satisfy your needs. Conceirge service is exceptional, snagging tables at the best restaurants and great tickets to Billy Elliot and MOMA. There is a little wear showing here and there, but nothing major. A little pricey, but everything in NYC is expensive. Too bad Mayor Bloomberg can't keep the street trash cans empty, sidewalks repaired and taxi regulations enforced.

name: Renaissance New York Hotel Times Square
title: “Wonderful Hotel!”
text:
This was the hotel I stayed at for my first ever trip to NYC in 1995. I had always remembered it being very nice, but since it is on the expensive side, I never returned there for another stay until this past March. I was able to get a great deal for 3 nights through Marriott Rewards, so I didn't hesitate to book it. The hotel was wonderful in 1995, it has just recently finished renovating, and is now even more spectacular! 
The location is perfect! It is right in the middle, literally, of Times Square. Your within walking distance to Broadway, 5th Avenue, Rockefeller Center (I highly recommended doing Top Of The Rock!) etc... and then there's a subway station right there by the hotel that will get you anywhere else very quickly. 
The rooms are amazing! I had a king room and it was spacious! The bed was heavenly, there was a nice flat screen TV, big work desk with high speed internet ($17/day), comfy chaise lounge where you can sit and look out at the street below. There's a beautiful, marble walk in shower, complete with a bath seat! It was all just so comfortable! They e-mail you before you arrive if you book via the Marriott website, the "virtual concierge" and offer you some extras (of course for a fee) for your stay if your interested. I chose to have a selection of sodas brought up, they gave me 2 Pepsi's and 2 Sierra Mist's, and it was brought up, on ice, within 10 mins of my arrival into the room. 
The hotel employees I encountered were all very friendly and accomodating. I checked in early and my room wasn't ready, so I stored my bags and went out to get some breakfast.
