I came back, and my room was ready, so it was nice to be able to get in early. There are two sets of elevators you take to get to your room. The first goes from the street to the lobby, street level is where the bellhops are, then lobby to your room. I didn't find the elevators inconvenient, as they were always very quick. 
I can't comment on the restaurant, bar, room service etc... because I didn't use any of them. There's lots of wonderful restaurants in the area though. Ray's Pizza just down the street has fantastic pizza! I don't know if there's a full business center, but if you don't have a laptop, and need to use the internet, there's a computer in the lobby with free internet--which is a rarity at hotels! 
The Renassaince is a wonderful hotel, and I will definitely stay there again!

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Great experience for 1st time visit”
text: My daughter and I stayed at the Marriott Marquis from March 22-26. We had a great experience. Everyone was very helpful. We did not find that the elevators were a problem. We loved "The View Lounge" All of the waiters and waitresses were very attentive and courtious. We are from small town Iowa, and found everyone to be very helpful. The location was great. We would definatly stay here anytime we plan a return visit to New York. We knew nothing coming into New York, and everyone made sure that our experience was great.

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “nella media”
text: Situato in una strada non troppo carina, l'hotel è moderno e pulito. Purtroppo pur avendo segnalato che eravamo in viaggio di nozze ci hanno detto che non lo sapevano e ci hanno dato una stanza ad un piano basso (lo sapevano perfettamente!!!). Comunque la stanza era bella e pulita, L'hotel maca, secondo me, di una buona gestione... alla reception (un pò piccola per la verità) c'è sempre il caos di ospiti in attesa di un sospirato ascensore, e i desk sono gestiti solo da giovani non troppo professionali e organizzati! per il resto, è vero che gli ascensori sono un miraggio e la colazione abbondante.

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “Never again, thanks.”
text: This hotel is not what it used to be, that's for sure. We reserved two double rooms for Easter weekend, with a request for early check-in. Not only did we NOT get early check-in, but our rooms were not available until one hour AFTER the regular check-in time. And we didn't get our two double rooms - they only had one double and one king. This wouldn't have been so bad if not for the careless attitude of the front desk staff, who basically shrug their shoulders and say "sorry, but we're really busy"....When we finally got to our rooms, they were stuffy, small, and in sore need of updating. I understand the hotel is due for renovation, but that doesn't excuse the lack of pillows (two pillows in a room with two full beds?), or the worn out sheets with holes in them. TV's are ancient, and incidentals are overpriced. $50/night for parking?? $6 for a small bottle of water??? For the prices charged, you expect at least to have bedding that doesn't make you cringe. I notice the management has a stock response to complaints, indicating that renovations are due soon, but they do not address the very poor attitude of most of the staff. My husband and I got the impression that the front desk staff don't like being there any more than we did, and it shows.

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “Another Fabulous Stay at the New York Palace”
text:
This was my second stay at the New York Palace and I was not dissapointed. This time, we booked a room in the Towers section of the hotel and it was well worth the extra money. Our room was on the 45th floor and had a view over St. Patrick's Cathedral and the Rockerfeller Center. You could also see the Hudson river in the distance. Our room was very large and was decorated in a sleek Art Deco style. The sheets were very nice and so were the pillows. The room also had a large plasma television, a desk, an armoire and two large armchairs. The bathroom was beautiful, large, and functional. The Aqua di Parma toilettries were a lovely touch.
Overall, the room was very spacious and luxurious. 
The service was also impeccable. It was my son's birthday and the staff certainly acknowleged it. It was over the top. He loved it. They sent him balloons, two cakes, and a plate of chocolate-dipped stawberries.
The housekeeping and turn-down service were also amazing. All of the staff members were helpful and courteous. The staff made us feel like royalty.
The New York Palace is a phenomenal hotel and I hope to return.

name: Hotel Chandler
title: “Goed en centraal gelegen hotel”
text: positief oordeel over het hotel na een verblijf van 6 nachten; kamer met een goede prijs/kwaliteit verhouding; men was zeer behulpzaam en coulant in het omzetten van een rokers kamer naar een niet rokers kamer; om de hoek 5 AV Empire State building; ontbijt buiten het hotel, gelegenheden genoeg; 12 E 31st oogt op zich niet zo aantrekkelijk, maar dat is de buitenkant, kijk er doorheen, er is nl niets mis

name: Morgans Hotel
title: “Great Hotel”
text:
We stayed at Morgans for our 5 day honeymoon stint in New York and loved it!
The hotel is chic and elegant without being pretentious.
The staff at the front desk and bellboys are really courteous and helpful. Our concierge (Nicole) was an angel, she sorted out restaurant reservations with us and gave us some good tips about where to shop, etc.
The room was amazing! we were upgraded to a suite (1204) and it was bigger than our apartment in London.
The location could not be better and it is very clean and quiet.
There is a trendy restaurant/bar (Asia de Cuba) where food is goos, albeit a bit hit and miss, but overall it is worth a visit even if just for a cocktail.
If I had to criticise something I would suggest a larger selection of cereal for breakfast, but that's just me being fussy.
Loved it!

name: Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan
title: “Posizione invidiabile!”
text:
Sono stata al Crowne Plaza 4 giorni a maggio.
L'hotel è su Times Square in pieno centro, noi ci siamo stati solo per dormire e come "base" di partenza per visitare NY è davvero ottima!
La stanza era al 16esimo piano con una vista mozzafiato: avevavmo 2 letti qeen size molto comodi, un bel bagno pulito,frigobar, lcd ed angolo gurdaroba con asse da stiro e ferro.
Alla sera bastava scendere nella hall per essere al "centro del mondo": vi sono tantissimi negozi e locali dove mangiare, fare shopping e divertirsi, inoltre l'hotel è vicinissimo ai più famosi teatri di Broadway!
Mi sono trovata molto bene e consiglio vivamente questa truttura.

name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria
title: “Absolutely Perfect”
text: First off, I want to say that the Towers were absolutley perfect. The location was ideal, close enough to walk everywhere but still out of the hassle of times square. The suite was gigantic, having a bedroom, kitchen with full bar, 2 workstations with fax and phones all over the place. Wonderful bed and full marble bathroom. I have stayed in many different locations in NYC and would be hard pressed to consider anything but the Towers for my next stay. Only complaint if I must have one would be the parking on site for 2 days was 90 dollars. A little pricey but doesnt seem to matter to the clientel who stay here. Private elevators with key card access are a nice touch that gets you checked in very quickly and out of the hassle of the huge lobby.

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “Omni Berkshire - The good and the not-so-good”
text:
Stayed over Christmas weekend with family. Wouldnt necessarily call it a 4-star hotel. Lobby was lovely, service was nice. Location couldn't be beat. Workout room was quite nice. And the bathrooms were spacious. 
Not so good - walls were like paper (you could hear TVs in the next room), elevators didn't always work (we got stuck the first night we were there), and since we were on the 3rd floor, we could hear traffic and street noise all night. 
Lots of choices in NYC. Wouldnt pick this one again.

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “Pretty Good NY Hotel”
text:
My husband and I just got back from a weekend in New York at the Omni Berkshire Place. We booked our room through Priceline and got a great deal ($225/night). The hotel was centrally located in Midtown--close to Columbus Circle and Central Park. The hotel itself is pretty nice--our room was small (but it is NYC so I was not concerend with the size), nicely decorated and clean. I should mention that if we had paid the actual going rate for this hotel--somewhere in the mid $300's I probablly would have been disappointed, especially with the particular room we were given on the 3rd floor that looked into the hotel's landry room. But since we got a deal and the only time we spent in the room was sleeping, it was just fine. 
Overall I thought the hotel staff was very nice. There is a concerige desk that set up dinner reservations, theater shows, etc. 
As I said before the location was great for sightseeing--my husband and I actually walked all the way to the Met, but we are in our late 20's/early 30's and all of our friends were in SoHo and the West Village so we spent a lot of time in cabs. So if you want more action and ambiance in NYC this is probably not the hotel for you.

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Fabulous property, incredible staff!”
text:
As a frequent Kimpton guest and Inner Circle member, I was excited to visit Ink48. I was not disappointed! 
The staff was accommodating and friendly; Jeffrey and Victor in particular. They knew we were celebrating my mom's birthday and they went out of their way to make her feel special. Jeffrey has loads of knowledge about NYC; ask him anything!
The room was very nice - 12th floor, modern decor, a phenomenal shower, and a view of the West River and the city skyline. 
The morning coffee, tea and hot chocolate were also excellent. Kudos to the fair trade/organic products!
Anothe bonus: Ink48 is just a few short blocks from Pier 83, where you can pick up the Circle Line boat tour. It's also just a few blocks from Times Square or Central Park. It's away from the hubbub and foot traffic that dominates midtown, but close enough to be near everything Manhattan has to offer. 
I can't wait to go back with my friends and check out the rooftop bar. I hear it's unrivaled!

name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria
title: “Très plaisant”
text: Nous venons juste de retourner de nos vacances à new york. Nous célébrions nos 10 ans de mariage. A la réception de l’hôtel, ils savaient que nous arrivions car nous avons répondus à un de leur courriel qu’ils nous ont envoyé avant notre départ de Montréal. Un des réceptionnistes nous a accompagné dans notre suite ou une bouteille de ‘Sparkling Wine’, (C’est delicieux mais c’est pas du champagne) et des fraises couvertes de chocolat nous attendais. Le concierge est fantastique. Nous recommandons le restaurant bull & bear. Notre chambre étais très spacieuse avec beaucoup d’armoire de rangement, une salle de bain en marbre. Nous recommandons cet hôtel pour quiconque visite new york.

name: Morgans Hotel
title: “i like to stay at Morgans”
text:
Stayed 2 nites in February - great french resturant - Madison bistro accross the street
Room - nice clean and comfortable - i enjoy going down for breakfast at Asia De Cuba
nice staff . good location
Lynne V - from Chicago

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Excellent Stay - location, service, view, room”
text:
We just returned from a 3 night stay at this hotel in NYC and it couldn't have been better. We arrived around 1:30 p.m. and were able to check in and got a fantastic studio room on the 25th floor with a beautiful view of the city including the Chrysler building. The staff were very nice and each time we left or arrived they greeted us. It was a refuge to come back to after a long day of sight seeing. Here are some details/highlights:
-aveda products (rosemary mint)
-very comfortable bed with lots of pillows 
-huge closet with ample amount of hangers
-fully stocked kitchen -- pots, pans, plates, glasses, cups, silverware, fridge, microwave, stove, sink, cabinets
-excellent water pressure in the shower
-full size desk with ergonomic chair
-umbrella in the closet (came in handy one day)
-super fast elevators
-next door restaurant (The Barking Dog) was a good meal for dinner one night
We will be staying here each time we come back to NYC and are 100% happy with our stay.

name: Renaissance New York Hotel Times Square
title: “Renovations were going on while we were there June 8-11”
text:
This was my second stay at the Renaissance and there is indeed work going on. However, the work goes on between 8:00 am and 5:00 pm so it really wasn't a bother because we were out of the room most of the time. The staff were courteous and helpful and even allowed us to check into our room around 11:00 am. I was a little disappointed that we couldn't eat breakfast in the usual restaurant where we could look out over Times Square as we ate, but they are in the process of remodeliing that as well. Temporarily, the dining room is where the lounge was previously located on the opposite side of the building.
Even with construction going on, we had a wonderful stay at the Renaissance and would definitely go back. You can't beat it for location and the beds are wonderful! I also love the large bathrooms and the marble vanity tops with enough space for the three of us to put all of our stuff.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York West 35th
title: “Sets the benchmark for all others!”
text:
Can't possibly say enough wonderful things about this hotel! From the initial welcoming e-mail from the manager, to the extremely pleasant and well-trained staff, this will be our primary stay for each NYC trip! The location is excellent! Close enough to everything, yet far enough removed from the chaos of Times Square. There's a subway stop steps from the lobby, and you're a stones throw away from the Empire State Building and Macy's. 
The rooms are clean, comfortable and very well-appointed. The breakfast is excellent! Great way to jump start any day in the city!
The staff is what truly makes this hotel one of the best I've stayed in. Our last trip was a surprise for my daughter's birthday...they actually sent up a treat & signed card from the staff! These are the little details that make you want to return!
Overall...I now compare all other hotels to this Hilton Garden Inn...Please keep up the great work! We'll be back soon!

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Location location location”
text: The only reason why I would say this place gets more score is because of location. if you want to be in the heart of TSQ this place is very good. With Hilton status I had internet and breakfast free. Breakfast buffet could be rated hight. The rooms are also spaciouse. Typical doubletree 2 two room suites. Cant comment on service much but I would say neutral , like all the double trees are.

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Home away from home”
text:
We have been privileged to stay at Ink48 several times since it opened and I appreciate the people who work there more each time! From the smiling doormen to the accommodating and professional front desk personnel, to the fine lades who clean your room, they are fantastic. We celebrated my husband's 60th birthday there and that was the beginning of a new family tradition. The hotel staff sent a lovely cake and wine to our room with a hand written note! When was the last time that happened to you?
The rooms are spacious and clean with lovely bathrooms and a glorious shower. The beds are so sleepable and my husband loved the pillows so much he actually went online and bought them!
The hotel is located in Hell's kitchen with room views of the Hudson River or the city. We find it very convenient to walk to the theater district Times Square or to the many excellent restaurants in the neighborhood.
We also believe n supporting the Kimpton Hotels because of ther commitment to making a positive social and environmental difference in the community. This commitment to care appears to permeate every aspect of Kimpton Hotels and especially Ink48. And they take dogs:-)
The people that work here are ultimately what makes this a special place to stay n NYC!!

name: Morgans Hotel
title: “Excellent Stay - Great Location - look out for Deals”
text:
This was the 2nd time my friend and I had visited the states together and each time I go away I make it a rule which is not to go to a chain hotel, restaurant or bar (that's one of the reasons you go away to get away from the old and enjoy the new). Morgans Hotel was different and had a boutique, querkiness to it which is what I love. However I did find out that it was a chain but not one that I had heard of :-) 
Usually the hotel is really expensive however we were extremely lucky and found a fantastic deal. The early early bird deal "Book more than 60 days in advance of your trip and get your room half price) We managed to get a double double room for the two of us at $500 each for 5 night in Central Midtown. Which included Breakfast.
The Rooms were spacious, I loved the shower, Room Service came everyday to clean and tidy. There wasn't any tea/coffee making facilities but if i remember on the 4th floor there is a lounge where you could have a shower if you didn't have a room that night and you were checking out. But in there was free tea/coffee facilities all day/night long. 
The hotel is situated between 37th & 38th street on Madison Avenue, 10mins walk if that to Grand Central Station, 15-20mins to Macy's on 34th Broadway. 
We also got the Shuttle from JFK to Grand Central Station. It was $30 return, instead of $45-50 dollars in a Yellow Taxi. The Drop off at Grand Central station is literally round the corner from Madison Ave. We recommend.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Excellent hotel, excellent location!”
text: This hotel is in Times Square just one block from Broadway. Excellent location! Gray Line tour bus stop (I highly recommend this) is half a block away, stores, restaurants, snacks, souvenirs, are on the same block and everything is within close walking distance. I highly recommend staying here...you're in the heart of the action and the hotel itself is wonderful. The staff is superb both in service and friendliness. Two thumbs up!

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Excellent hotel, Fantastic value and great location”
text: Stayed for 5 nights with my wife and couldn't recommend it enough, check in was easy, we were in the room 5 minutes after walking in, room was spotlessly clean and plenty big enough for the two of us but clothes hanging space is a bit limited,that was the only fault we could find with the room, this is New York so you don't spend too much time in the room.Times square is about a ten minute walk up 42 nd st. And the main bus terminal is 5 minutes away.all in all a great hotel and we would stay there again and have no hesitation recommending it to anybody

name: Hilton Times Square
title: “Customer service”
text: After a long trip from the U.K we were very grateful for the excellent customer service we received as we arrived at reception. A special thankyou to Richard who went out of his way to help us and advise us on local places to eat. We had a wonderful stay at your hotel and the staff were all very helpful. Thanks again.

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “First Trip To NY From Houston, Texas”
text: I can not stress how impressed we were with the Omni, the staff and the location! The service was impeccable! If you are going to NY for the first time STAY AT THE OMNI!!!!

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “Great location, helpful staff and nice amenities!”
text:
We arrived in Manhattan a week after Superstorm Sandy, and before the nor'easter. The staff was very helpful, especially the front desk staff. The hotel was very busy - many displaced by the storm were staying there temporarily, as well as Red Cross volunteers, and NYC marathoners, waiting to leave after the canceled marathon. I was very impressed by the hotel staff, who treated everyone graciously. Though the hotel is not brand new, the rooms and breakfast facility were clean and very comfortable. 
Location: great! We walked everywhere - theaters, shopping, etc. because public transportation was not yet back to normal. Disclosure: we walked 6 - 8 miles daily, so if you're tired after a couple of blocks, take a cab. The theaters we went to were both within 2 blocks of the hotel. We walked to the Time Warner complex, Rockefeller Center, Macys Herald Square, Manhattan Mall, the Garment district, August Wilson Theater (Jersey Boys), and Eugene O'Neill Theater (Book of Mormon). We went to both theaters during the nor'easter, and we were fine, though at times, the walk was treacherous since we didn't have boots.
Finally: always, always confirm your hotel reservations, even though your venue says it's not necessary. Since we arrived during the heigh of storm backlash, I'm glad I confirmed because I was reassured that we had a place to stay!
I'll definitely stay here again on my next trip.

name: Morgans Hotel
title: “Deserves an A - very nice, friendly staff, good location”
text:
Very nice boutique hotel, in my view. The staff was extraordinary, very friendly - and saved our st-/day upon arrival: our flight had been delayed, our baggage lost and we had just spent 2.5 hours in one of these shared cabs into town from Newark -- we got an upgrade to a one-bedroom suite. Since we were in town for 5 days, that was truly a significant benefit, much more space and such a nice gesture. Thanks, Morgans!
Also apart from this unexpected treat, my wife and I found the hotel very good. Convenient (midtown) location, between 37 and 38 St, thus just one block from 5th Ave, 2 blocks from the underground. Nice surroundings and decor, the breakfast (continental buffet) offers just what you need to kick off the day (a bit more fruit might be nice but it's fine as it is. NY Times with breakfast is great!! If there are any downsides at all, housekeeping tended to be a bit sloppy (left used bathrobe on bed, forgot a stack of towels in the seating area) and the bathroon is tiny tiny tiny. No way that 2 people can be in there at the same time. All in all nothing that makes me sleep bad and certainly a place I would return to anytime.

name: TRYP Times Square South
title: “A Clean,friendly,fantastically positioned, family friendly hotel.”
text:
Have returned after a week stay over the Easter weekend. Family room was huge, clean and perfect for our visit. Shower was great! Breakfasts and lunch were really good each time we ate. Sangria was perfect at the end of a busy sightseeing day. Wifi really useful to plan days activities. All staff friendly and helpful. Thank you!
Would highly recommend this hotel!

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York West 35th
title: “Great location, staff lacking”
text: This hotel was very conveniently located and close to the subway and Empire State building. Its a pity the staff were slack in helping out with directions to tourist places, seemed to have more interesting things to do like standing around.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Awesome if you can afford it!”
text: My partner and I are backpackers, but we wanted a bit of a treat. We got this hotel through Hotwire for half price than usual. We figured, why not have a Times Square experience?! It was a lovely room, so much space. Luckily, our room faced the back, so we didn't have a lot of flashing lights in our room. (They have blackout curtains if you get a street-facing room). There is free wifi in the lobby, but it was sort of spotty. One of the floors in the hotel is a business centre, so they have some computers and printers you can use for free - those were great, and it seemed like not many people knew about them, so they were available whenever we needed them. If you must stay in Times Square, I would recommend this hotel. It was comfortable and quiet and it had a lot of nice amenities. However, Manhattan isn't so big, so you could easily stay elsewhere (save a lot of money) and walk to Times Square. If you are fancy and have spending money, then definitely go for it, we had no complaints!

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Great location”
text: My coworkers and I stayed 2 weeks at the hotel and the staff met our every need,from the restaurant to the rooms the doorman our stay was great .The security staff was also helpful especially Frampton Wilson who gave warm greetings and tips and advice on getting around

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “Way Nicer Than Expected!”
text:
Did an overnight here last month with my nine-year-old daughter. As a former NYC resident for 16 years, I was completely predisposed to stay at the Four Seasons until I checked on the prices--YIKES! Knowing that the location of the Palace would be terriffic for our theater plans and shopping, I booked a standard room at the rate of $295--same price that I would get on one of the travel sites, and less than half of what they were getting at the Four Seasons. Valet parking and check in were friendly and efficient. Room was a bit on the small side, but offered lovely views over St. Patrick's from the 24th floor. Bed was fluffy and comfortable, and everything was very clean--trust me, I'm very picky on that account. Amazing concierge was able to score us a last-minute reservation at Bobby Flay's "Bar American". Booked on a Saturday night at 5:30 for a 6:30 reservation. Impressive. Room service prices were what you'd expect for a major metropolitan hotel--we opted out of the $40 continental breakfast in favor of a quick bite at the Dean and Deluca in Rock Center.
Overall this was a very pleasant experience and I would not hesitate to return to the NY Palace in the future.

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “GREAT STAY”
text: This hotel room is very big for New York. Me and my spouse had a King size bed on the 11th floor (the very top). It was very quiet. The room was enjoyable for our stay so we were not bumping into each other and packed in like sardines. We had an extra chair for sitting and a good size desk and chair also. There was a large space/shelf type thing to sit your luggage on and another luggage rack and a good size closet. Refrigerators are available upon request. We requested one as soon as we got there and it was delivered that day which was great. (They only have a limited amount per the guest book, so call soon). The drugstrore Rite Aid is like a block away so you can get some drinks and stock up. I thought it was great how they have so many plugs and outlets in the room. They are attached to the lamps so you can plug cell phones, laptops etc into. Internet service worked good and I used computers downstairs to print boarding passes out. We requested extra pillows which were delivered also. The lobby can get a little congested but we never had much of a problem with elevator and we were on top floor. I would suggest to eat no later then 8:30am for a relaxing breakfast. We rented bikes at Central Park, just remember bike riding is not allowed on trails so you are actually renting bikes to ride around the park with cars so I would suggest walking instead, its beautiful. Go in the entrance from Columbus Circle. Do not make the mistake we did and walk too far to go to Times Square. Take a right out of hotel door and the very first left on 51st street (comes up quick) then its just a few blocks down. The luggage man was very helpful and even flagged us a taxi when headed back to the airport. The service here was really good. My only con is that in New York the prices for food are so high. We stuck with burgers and fries and that ended up being 30-40 bucks if you wanted to eat somewhere nice. Its just crazy, but thats New York. I highly recommend "The View" lounge, not the restaurant. Its very romantic. They have little tables for two by the window all the way around. The lounge you can wear jeans and you can do the buffet of heavy appetizers or you can go and just get one drink (cokes count). Just get there like 6 or 7 before their eight dollar cover charge. Its one of our favorite things to do. We also went to "Carolines Comedy" show and laughed till we were almost in tears. This hotel is really nice and roomy and most important of all CLEAN! This is a great time to go also because not as many kids! My only con is the air could be a little quieter, kind of odd system.

name: TRYP Times Square South
title: “Best hotel experience ever!”
text:
My mom and I stayed at the TRYP hotel Monday through Friday. Check-in was at 3PM, but the staff let us check in early (around 11AM). There was no hassle to check in early, the staff members were really great about it~ :) I would totally stay here again. 
We were pleasantly surprised when we opened the door to our hotel room. The room was spacious and extremely clean. The bathroom was beautiful and the queen-sized bed was perfect for two people. Having a TV in the room was great because my mom and I watched our favorite shows after coming home from a long day of travel.
The hotel is located really close to the subway, so you won't have to walk that far to start your day. The hotel is also located extremely close to Madison Square Garden, so if you're planning on watching a Knicks game - this is the perfect location! The hotel is also located really close to Hell's Kitchen, Times Square and so much more! 
As for the cons, there are two - not that it would deter me from staying at this hotel again. Our hotel didn't have a refrigerator, so any leftover food we brought home just sat on the table until the next day. This isn't a huge con, but having a refrigerator would have been really nice and convenient. Another thing that I didn't really like was the view. We were facing the building next to the hotel, so it wasn't very pretty. However, we were on the 5th floor and we kept the curtains closed most of the time. I guess if our hotel had been higher up, our view would have been better. 
All in all, a great hotel. Loved it.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Great hotel, great location”
text: Sometimes the measure of a great hotel is how they deal with problems when things go sideways. In our case we arrived at the hotel after a long flight from Vancouver to find they did not have a room for us. They were very apologetic and made arrangements for us to stay at a nearby hotel for the night. Although we were quite disappointed we understood that these things happen sometimes. The night manager did her best to make up for the inconvenience. The next day, when we returned to the Doubletree the manager personally took care of us, making arrangements for our room to be upgraded to a much larger two bedroom suite with great views over Times Square. We had this super suite for the next 7 nights of our stay. They also provided free Internet access. Then hurricane Sandy struck. Even though they were very understaffed the hotel managed to keep their restaurant open and provide for the needs of their guests. Fortunately this part of Manhattan did not lose power and after a couple of days things began to return to normal. We had to stay an extra night at the Doubletree and again they let us keep our upgraded suite at a very reasonable rate. As far as we are concerned the hotel did more than enough to make up for the initial problem we had with our room. We have no problem recommending this hotel as a place to stay - great staff and a great location.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York West 35th
title: “Great location; terrific service”
text:
We spent an overnight in NYC in January and stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn on 35th St. The location is tops -- just steps from the subway and a stone's throw from Macy's, Herald's Square and the Empire State Building. We took a nice walk to 9th Ave and ate dinner at a lovely Trattoria, Mario's.
The hotel was spotless, the beds comfortable, the front desk accomodating and the overall experience very good. We'll be sure to book there again. FYI we like to get a little air when we are sleeping and the windows open, a plus for us.

name: New York Marriott Marquis
title: “Situation idéale pour découvrir NY”
text:
En plein Time Square et à deux pas des théâtres, cet hôtel permet une immersion immédiate dans l'atmosphère de la ville qui ne dort jamais.
Le restaurant panoramique offre une vue incroyable le soir.
La situation est idéale pour partir à la découvert des différents sites touristiques.
Les chambres sont confortables et assez spacieuses.

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “Had no complaints”
text:
Just returned from a three night stay (June 4 - 7), and unlike some of the other reviewers, had no complaints. Because I booked at the last moment felt as though I'd paid too much for the room (although many other lesser properties - including the the Doubletree Times Square actually - were more expensive for the same time period - there must just have been heavy demand!).
I found the staff helpful, the room clean and well appointed (and a big plus were the extra large bath towels!). Had no problem getting quick help to get cabs from the doormen, even in the rain, and everyone was gracious, welcoming and helpful. The workout center was clean and had a reasonable number of cardio machines and free weights (while well used, never crowded when I was there in the morning). They also provide fruit, towels and magazines - more than adequate although not a large space.
A few less than positive features - no coffee maker in the room, but as others have said, if you sign up for their frequent guest program (which you can do as you check in) they'll bring up 2 beverages of choice in the morning (coffee, juice, etc.) as well as an extra paper (USA today is always delivered). I found that service to be very prompt each morning. The room service menu is a bit expensive as are the items in the mini bar - but that's the case in most nicer hotels. There are so many choices for dining near-by that are open late, there's not much reason to stay in (for lunch - Europa Cafe is quick and good; for dinner try Fresh Basil's on Lex/56th - just basic, good italian!).
I'm in the city regularly on business, and will stay at the Omni in the future - great location, friendly staff, and the rooms/amenities were more than adequate.

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Great Location! Pack light the room is TINY!”
text: The Hotel is modern good location to do it all! I'm a New Yorker but now live in Florida. The room was described as being small, but it was even smaller then I expected. Staying in Manhattan you don't expect to get much for your money. I spent about $700 for two nights and my girlfriend and I were very cramped. I like a hard bed but this was like cell block hard. Nice staff, the bar is even pricer then what you would expect in NYC. I would have given it a higher mark if it was even just a little bigger. You don't spend much time in a room but you could hardly get ready to go out.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Nice suite, but sofa bed not very comfy”
text: There were 4 of us staying at the Doubletree Guest Suites in Times Square and we booked a one bedroom suite with a sofa bed in the lounge. The Suite itself was very well equipped and the bedroom was very comfortable. There was a large screen HD TV in both the bedroom and the lounge. There was a coffee maker and microwave and the coffee and cups were replaced each day along with milk. We spent most of our time sightseeing so we only really slept in the apartment. The only negative point I would say would be that the sofa bed in the lounge was not very comfortable and was difficult to sleep on. Perhaps it would be more comfortable for one person, but there was a dip in the middle which meant you kept rolling into the middle and the mattress is very thin and you can feel the springs.

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “What "Hamptonality" Is”
text:
The staff at the hotel is very attentive, once approached. The rooms were clean and comfortable, albeit not without their flaws. Complimentary internet access and a hearty breakfast are an added feature that few other hotels in the city have. Overall, the experience of staying at this hotel was a positive one. 
One employee in particular, Samuel F., was so kind as to stand outside on a busy street for nearly an hour in order to hail a wheelchair-accessible taxi for my mother. He promised me that he would find us one - they are rare, and in high demand; and he certainly delivered on his word. He saved both my mother and me from having panic-attacks. Samuel is a true asset to the Hampton Inn Times Square North.

name: The Jewel Facing Rockefeller Center
title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text: This hotel was wonderful. Helpful staff. Big clean rooms. Helped us check in and out. My daughter and I stayed form May 25th to May 29 th 2012. This was her first trip to New York and our wonderful hotel made everything great. Wonderful location at Rockerfella. Close to Times Square. Would stay here again on next trip.

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Outstanding and we will be back”
text:
We stayed at Ink 48 on Sat. 8/13. We were celebrating our 30th Anniversey & coul not have picked a better place. Great location, great views of the city and the convenience. Oh and the views from the bar on the 16th floor are amazing! Out door seating is just great!
We came over on the ferry from Weehawkin, walked up a few blocks to 11th ave and checked in. I scheduled my wife for 90 minute spa treatment and she loved every minute!
Times Square is just a short walk away!
The hotel upgraded our room to the 12th floor and also delivered a Complimentary chilled bottle of Campayne and a tray of brownies! Outstanding!
We will certainly use this Hotel again & again!

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “Good Place - Service Good - IF you know how to use it”
text:
Just got back from the Omni Berkshire Place. Had a nice room. Great bedding. Decent Location. Nice Turndown service.
This was all good but...
There is a complimentary car service to the financial district that is provided. BUT if you don't ask the concierge before 8 PM apparently it is not available to you. However, this is not told to you at check in. Also, when you ask the night bellmen about this service, they appear to have no knowledge of it. Therefore, this service is useless if you don't ask for it up front.
Also, the complimentary morning juice service etc. must be filled out and on the door befor a certain time. Look for this when you check in. Otherwise, you will get none.
Overall this was a good hotel. I can assume that they do not tell you all of this in order to let you enjoy your stay without their incessant instruction. However, without knowledge of services, one cannot take advantage of them.
There may be other service of which I am still not aware after two nights at this hotel.
I would stay here again, but would just like to be better informed of the amenities available to guests, and how to take advantage of them.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York West 35th
title: “Great NY stay”
text: Never having stayed overnight in NYC before, this Hilton Garden Inn was a great selection for us! The front desk staff were very friendly and helpful. We requested a city view room and were very impressed as we had room views of both the Empire State Bld and Macy's. Location is excellent and is a short walk from Rockefeller Ctr, Times Sq, etc. My wife thoroughly enjoyed being located so close to Macy's! The bed was very comfortable and the room was quiet. Being newbies to NYC during the holidays, there were several sights we wanted to explore during our 3 day stay and the Hotel's concierge was very helpful and friendly helping us with our itinerary to get the most out of our trip. We enjoyed our stay so much that we'll definitely return to NYC and to this hotel!

name: TRYP Times Square South
title: “Volveré sin dudarlo”
text:
Acabo de regresar de mi viaje a New York y escogimos este hotel por sus críticas y no nos eqivocamos. Fuimos un grupo de 4 amigas y tuvimos una desagradable bienvenida porque no reservamos habitación con camas twin sino dos dobles con lo cual nos dieron dos habiaciones con una cama grande y si queríamos una twin teniamos que pagar 50$ más por habitación y día, con lo cual como la cama era grandecita decidimos dormir juntas, una de las parejas decidió cambiarse de habitación porque la asignada era bastante pequña y al día siguiente nos dieron una muy buena en la planta 9, exactamente la 913, las compañeras tenían la 1204 que estaba bastante bien situada también.(Cuento esto para que lo dejen bien claro antes de ir sino te gusta dormir con nadie en la cama)
Muy limpio todo, las toallas se cambian a diario, el primer día te dejan una botellita de agu de cortesía, puedes hacerte café ya que tienen una cafetera de càpsulas, con varios tipos de café y de tés y sus vasos con tapa por si quieres salirte a la calle con él.
Buena reposición de gel, acondicionador y champú...Hay secador con muy buena potencia.
El desayuno sin ser de mucha variedad, podías comer bastante. Tenían yogures, cereales, queso fundido, mantequilla, mermelada, jugos, unas pequeñas tarrinas con chacina y queso, bollería, panes, huevos revueltos, bacon, salchicas, avena, café infusuines y furtas picadas, melón, piña etc...
Muy bien comunicado a 10 minutos caminado de times square, una estación de metro en la misma calle en la esquina (pen sattion).
Fue una estancia cómoda y tranquila, gracias a Angel el recepcionista que nos atendió, de habla hispana un encanto y nos ayudo mucho. También a Anthony el conserje un chico jóven puertoriqueño que fue especialmente agradable y amable, en general todos fueron muy buenos. Así que ninguna queja del servicio...
Volveré sin dudarlo.

name: Omni Berkshire Place
title: “Will stay here again”
text:
My wife and I came to New York for a four-night combination of work and vacation in early October 2004. We've previously stayed at the W hotel on Lex a few blocks away, but we much preferred the Omni this time. The staff were all very friendly, the rooms were spacious and very comfortable, and the cost was reasonable (by Manhattan standards).
The only minuses were a small amount of inter-room noise through the wall from the adjoining room and the lack of a view (we had a window overlooking a drab utility space).
The best part about the Omni, though, was it's location. Fifty-second street is pretty quiet on this block (very little street noise), yet the hotel is within walking distance of lots of great places: Central Park, 5th ave shopping, subway access, classy restaurants, Times Square, and Rockefeller Center. We will probably try to stay here from now on whenever we come back to New York.

name: TRYP Times Square South
title: “magnifica relación calidad precio y buena situación”
text: Hotel totalmente nuevo, lo único que se echa de menos es un armario algo más amplio, se queda escaso, pero tampoco es algo esencial. Personal muy agradable y servicial, casi todos hablan español. Boca de metro muy cercana. Cafetera con cápsulas que reponen todos los días gratis. Buenas camas, wifi gratis con buena recepción, cobran las llamadas locales (en nyc suele ser gratuito). Muy limpio. El año pasado estuve en el Distrikt, la única diferencia es lo que comento del armario, por lo demás este no tiene nada que envidiarle y es más económico, ya depende que os guste más unas calles más arriba o más abajo.

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “Great Hotel....Superb Location”
text:
We stayed at the New York Palace for four nights in April 2007 Had a comfortable room on the 33rd foor with a spectacular view over St Patricks Cathedral, Rockefella Centre and beyond.This was my second trip to New York.The first time we stayed at the Sofitel which is also superb but the Palace just has the edge for me in terms of style and location.
 So much is within walking distance. Central Park, Times Square,42nd street, Broadway, Grand Central Station,the fabulous shops on 5th Avenue,I could go on !!
 Took the subway one day down to Battery Park and got a water taxi which took us to the Statue of Liberty and under the magnificent Manhatten and Brooklyn Bridges.
 One of the highlights of the trip would have to be going up the Empire State and seeing the look on my kids faces when we got to the top, unforgetable!!!!! Its worth mentioning you can buy an express ticket for about double the price but it saves hours of queuing.
 After a busy day the Palace is an absolute haven to return to and cosset yourself in a sumptious robe and slippers.Your ice bucket is filled and chocolates provided by the turn down service (buy your own drinks and water,mini bar prices are extortionate)
 For dinner I recommend booking a table at Balthazar,a stylish and "happening" restaurant in Soho where you can soak up the New York atmosphere and eat delicious food. If you still have any energy left after that, have a drink in the supremely stylish Gilt bar back at the Hotel. Absolutely Fabulous!!!!!!!

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “A good choice in the middle of Manhattan”
text:
Location is great and is close to everything - including many subway stations leading to everywhere in the city. We stayed on the 29th floor and there was no noise at all, despite being directly above the Times Square with its 24 hour non-stop traffic. The suite is well equipped, with a sofa bed, a microwave, a mini fridge and a mini bar, in-room safe, and dual sink vanity. Beds are very comfortable. The service is mostly okay. The doormen are pleasant, but seem to have some dubious connection with some cabbies waiting in front door. Concierge is also pretty helpful, although knowledge level could be enhanced.
The TKTS booth across the street is a great convenience for people wanting to hunt for last minute Broadway show tickets. Be sure to be there early to get a greater variety of choices and better seating - it opens 3pm and 10am on Wednesdays for matinee shows.
Overall it's a good choice for NYC.

name: TRYP Times Square South
title: “PEOR DE LO QUE CREIAMOS”
text:
Es un hotel muy nuevo, con decoración muy moderna, pero no es el hotel que esperabamos, está algo apartado, de lo que se puede considerar la "buena zona", aunque cerca del Empire, y el metro, la calle es algo "fea", nuestra habitación, 2 adultos y un niño de 13 años, correcta, amplia, el baño muy cómodo. Las vistas, horrorosas mejor tener las cortinas cerradas.
Tenía solo un armario de menos de un metro, totalmente insuficiente aunque sea para una corta estancia, no había un solo cajón ni en el armario ni en la habitación, 
El aire acondicionado era de consola y hacía un ruido insoportable.
El trato del personal inmejorable, siempre ayudando e intentando agradar. Tiene un bara de tapas en el lobby muy agradable.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Superb value”
text: Great value. Clean, modern, great service, terrific staff. Half a block to subway. Could not have been better.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York West 35th
title: “Excellent location, lovely staff”
text: I recently stayed here on points over the Thanksgiving holiday, and wow am I glad I chose this property! I didn't realize when choosing this hotel that it was practically on the Macy's Parade route, and when checking in staff bent the rules a bit and gave us a view without charging the (apparently extra) fee to do so. We comfortably watched the parade from the 18th floor with my family, which was fantastic. The property itself seems very new - our room was lovely (if small, but this is NYC) and the food was fabulous. My only complaint is about the elevators - you need to use a room key to go to ANY floor (not just executive levels), so there is always a scramble when you first get in to make the elevator work. They are also quite slow - we often found ourselves regularly waiting 5-7 minutes for one to come to our floor. If they can get that issue figured out, I'll be back in a heartbeat.

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “Great Hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel for three nights whilst on honeymoon in New York. 
We had a lovely room on the 16th floor overlooking St Patricks Cathedral.
Maid service was excellent, concierge was fantastic and the reception staff were great.
Bellboys were ok, however we found them more interested in chatting amongst themselves rather than helping customers.
We had lunch at the restaurant on the last day which was not very good at all. It took about half an hour for a waiter to come and take our drinks order and then another fifteen minutes to get our food order taken. We were a bit diasppointed as it wasn't what we expected in the restaurant of a first class hotel!
Overall, i would definitely stay in the New York Palace again, I just wouldn't eat in the restaurant!

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Awesome Hotel, incredible service. A must stay experience.”
text: Everything about my stay in the Hudson river suite was top notch. Beautiful views, great amenities, Unbelievable service. I had a second night reserved at the Gansvort hotel the night after and INK 48 blew them away. The Gansvort was half the experience at twice the price. GREAT JOB INK 48. The only place I will stay when I'm in NY from now on.

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “50th Birthday Anniversary for wife”
text:
We usually stay at Kimpton Hotels when we travel because of the exceptional accommodations and service and Ink48 was no exception. From the moment we arrived we were greeted by friendly staff, offered wine to take with us to our rooms and that level of service continued for our entire four day stay. Any service issues were taken care of immediately by the staff and especially Jeffrey, the concierge.
As to the room, we had the Hudson River Suite, and the view of the river and NYC skyline was spectacular, especially at night. We also ate dinner at their restaurant, Print, and again fast, friendly service and the food was to die for!
This is not an inexpensive hotel, but for the comfort and convenience it adds to the vacation experience, it is a great value!

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York West 35th
title: “Stay Here!!!”
text: Just returned from a few days in NYC where I was celebrating a special birthday. We stayed 2 nights at the Hilton Garden Inn on 35th Street. We arrived around noon & were able to leave our bags with the conceirge until our room was ready. Note: Hilton Garden is ideally located very close to Macy's & Herald Square. Check-in was a breeze. The registration personnel were friendly and answered all our questions. They even made a point to wish me a happy birthday, as I had commented during our initial reservation. We stayed in Room 3009 (30th Floor) & the room was roomy by NYC standards. The room was extemely clean with a very efficient layout. The king-size bed was comfortable. Loved the Neutrogena products in the bathroom, too! Our view was lovely especially at night. When we returned from the show the first night, a delicious surprise was waiting in our room. A small chocolate mousse cake with a sweet note from Tiago thanking us for choosing the Hilton Garden Inn & wishing me a happy birthday. It made me so happy & it was so kind. It made me feel special. My husband & I were welcomed each morning with big smiles & warm hellos by the hotel staff from housekeeping; the front desk; the restaurant staff, etc. I would highly recommend the Hilton Garden on 35th Street for anyone planning a visit to New York. I definitely will stay there again.

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “very nice experience”
text: Took husband and kids 11 and 15 years old. Stayed in room 2706. Very nice and very clean--this is coming from Mrs. Germ Phobe--no hairs in the tub, or sink, no mold on the shower curtain, the bathroom counter was spotless, as was the kitchen. The pillows were yummy, the mattress was just regular not bad but not great. Internet access is $9.95 for 24 hours- should be included. Only wish they could have turned the hotel building so we could have had the awesome view of the Chrysler Building.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “All about the location”
text:
Being my first time to New York I really did not know what to expect. What a pleasant surprise when I turned up and found that I had selected a hotel in the centre of it all. The rooms seemed small for what you pay but then this is my first time here. It is really about what it around the hotel than the facilities themselves. The hotel restaurant was adequate for breakfast. The lifts got a little slow at times but that is all I could complain about. The warmed choc chip cookies on arrival were a popint of difference. While we were there interviews were occuring in some guest rooms which did make you feel as though secutiry was a little lax compared to normal.
The separate bedroom with two doble beds plus a pull out sofa were adequate for our family of five. A miscrowave and kitchen bench in the suite were enough to give us some flexibility.

name: Hilton Times Square
title: “Perfect hotel!”
text:
I came with my wife suzen for a weekend in NY and we had the best time!
The location the hotel the room and speacily the bad all of them were absulotly perfect!

name: The London NYC
title: “Great location, large rooms, great restaurant in lobby”
text: We had a wondeful stay at the London with friends. The room was huge, the food at the downstairs restaurant was incredible. The staff was friendly and corteous. I will definitely be returning. The staff upgraded us to a larger room with a better view when we checked in. They were helpful with directions and recommendations of restuarants.

name: The Jewel Facing Rockefeller Center
title: “Nicely decorated and renovated; it is a Club Quarters in disguise”
text: The Jewel is a good value if you can get a 'deal' on rates. It is superbly located right near Rockefeller Center. I have been a victim of a 'bait and switch' at this property before, but I think I've figured out the situation. The hotel is furnished identically to the way Club Quarters decorates its rooms. And, the 'sister' hotel of the Jewel, just a few doors down, is a Club Quarters. The two properties share reservations. I believe this means that they are likely owned by the same people, but the Club Quarters has its 'club' arrangement for members while the Jewel does not have that feature. The Living Room on the second floor of the Jewel is very comfortable with coffee available and a place to relax if you need to wait for your room. I give the Jewel a thumbs up overall.

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “Fabulous location”
text: I just spent 5 days at the Palace, and can't say enough. The location is superior, easy walking to most places, subway stations near by, and nothing except airports more than $10 cab ride away. The staff was also exceptionally friendly, I've never had so many people wish me a good morning! I swear that the maids popped out of the rooms to say hello if they hear you passing by. Best of all, there is a Starbucks just out the 51st Street entrance. Would definitely stay here again (if I could afford it!)

name: Lowell Hotel
title: “I wish Margaret from reservations ran this hotel.”
text:
I know my title may sound strange but I really believe if she did, it would truly be a notch above so many other hotels because of her attention to detail and customer service skills. I don't want to give this hotel a negative review, I wanted to like it as much as Margaret in reservations. It is certainly not a bad hotel, but it has the potential to be a wonderful hotel. In defense of the hotel, since I only stayed for one night, maybe I caught it on an "off" day. I was coming to town for a Dr's appt and because I was so sick I needed my mother and her husband to drive me. I had changed my reservation 3 times because my migraine was so bad and Margaret was very accommodating. The day of my arrival I called to add a room to my reservation. The rooms were around $750 and I was eligible for an upgrade because I am an Andrew Harper member. Margaret made the smart suggestion that I upgrade my room for a couple hundred of dollars and then use the upgrade, and add on my parents room making it a two bedroom suite. I thanked her for even thinking that up and was so excited about my stay. The Andrew Harper rewards also entitled us to a bottle of wine, vip fruit basket, free afternoon tea and a continental breakfast. When we arrived, around 3:30, they said the room wasn't ready and I thought, oh perfect we can go for tea, but we were told to wait in the waiting area, which we did. After about 45 minutes we were taken to our room. The living room was great, it was comfortable, newly re-finished, it had a terrace with a really interesting city view, if you hung over the balcony enough, you could even see central park. I took the nicer bedroom, it had the same city view, a gorgeous bathroom with great amenities. The carpet however was wet from being cleaned and had that weird chemical smell, if I didn't have a migraine, it would have been more livable for me. The other bedroom was also nice, city view, but not as good as mine and it had a much smaller bathroom. But again, we were only there for one night. We had room service for dinner and we were told that it would take approximately 45 minutes, it ended up closer to an hr and 45 minutes. I hate confrontation, so does my mother, but my stepfather yelled at room service which embarrassed me greatly, they took care of the bill which I thought was more than generous (maybe it was part, I really stayed out of the whole thing, I hid in my bedroom). The food was amazing, we had this awesome tomato soup, although it would have been better if it came with the gorgonzola crustini it was advertised with. I had the fresh pea ravioli which was delicious. The VIP fruit basket was 3 apples. No tea. There was no breakfast the following morning. We were also charged a price higher than quoted. Oh, and the lady who did the turn down was lovely I guess to some up.
Pros:
Margaret, Margaret, Margaret....
CIty view suite with terrace
room service
Cons:
Things are just not delivered as promised (I believe this is a customer service issue)
We were charged a price higher than we were quoted
Honestly, I wouldn't stay here again because I don't know what it would be like, this is my only experience with this hotel. It was overall just more disappointing than anything, it would have been better to expect nothing and be surprised along the way.

name: Morgans Hotel
title: “Design et class”
text:
Petit séjour au Morgans pour le réveillon du jour de l'an.
Forcément à ces dates c'est plus cher, mais l'hôtel garde un bon rapport qualité/prix pour NYC
Les chambres sont très belles, déco d'André Putman avec petit canapé devant la bow window et vue directe sur l'empire state building ... j'adore. La taille des chambres est plus petite que la taille habituelle dans des hôtels américains, mais cela reste tout à fait correcte et acceptable.
Il y a un salon/salle à manger très sympa au 4ème étage avec thé, café magazine a disposition. Seul bémol, la salle de bain, qui aurait méritée un bon nettoyage de printemps et un petit rafraichissement (carreaux fêlés, équipements abimés ...) dommage (la note propreté ne concerne d'ailleurs que la salle de bain).
Personnel sympathique et professionnel et ne soyez pas effrayés l'accueil ressemble plus à un hall d'entrée d'immeuble qu'a une entrée d'hôtel
L'hotel est situé tout près* de l'empire state building et se trouve à 10 min env. de Times square, grand central ect ... dans un coin plutôt calme, appréciable si vous souhaitez un endroit chic et discret à éviter si vous souhaitez sentir la fièvre (et la foule de time square). il y a 2 stations de métro pas très loin.
Le resto de l'hotel qui est assez "branché" est très cher, donc si vous voulez vraiment y aller il vaut mieux commander un cocktail (ça vous coutera déjà cher, mais bon Asia de cuba à New York ça a un prix ...!)

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
title: “Staybridge Suites Times Square - Nota 10”
text: Excelente atendimento. Chegamos no Hotel pela manhã e o quarto já estava pronto e ainda nos foi oferecido uma promocão da rede de hotéis permitindo o late check-out que foi fundamental para o tipo de viagem que fizemos desta vez. No ano passado ficamos em outra rede de hotéis bem conhecida mas o Staybridge superou nossas expectativas. O café da manhã é muito e tudo é muito limpo e organizado. Com certeza na próxima viagem irei escolher essa rede de hotéis e recomendo a todos.

name: Trump International Hotel and Tower
title: “Excellent stay”
text:
Booked a one bedroom park suite, worth every penny. From the moment we arrived I found myself wanting to ask the staff who they thought me and my wife were as we were treated like VIP's at every turn.
The suite is finished to very high standards as are all of the public areas. The gym/pool was being renovated, but in all honesty we wouldn't have used it and the hotel let us know at the time of booking, and emailed to ensure we understood.
Before we left the UK the concierge team were emailing asking for our tastes, requests, what would we like in the fridge when we arrive, nothing was too much trouble and all present and correct upon arrival.
I would say the whilst this hotel has everything any other 5 star hotel has, the rooms, there size, the kitchen and the view, make you feel like you have NYC apartment, without shelling out the $2m price tag....the views were amazing.
Having whole foods across the road made for an experience, for the 4 days we felt like locals, popping out to the shop for groceries, mixing with real new Yorkers.
We ate in Jean George's, and whilst the food was good, by wife wasnt feeling great and left quite a lot, to the point that Jean George actually appeared and had a word with our waiter, who asked if everything was ok. Not often you see pride like that.
Booked a couples massage on our last day, fantastic!
It is expensive, but you get what you pay for, there is no lobby bar, but your in NYC....there are tons of bars..with the kitchen breakfast from the deli round the corner is a few dollars for pastries and I went out most mornings for fresh pancKakes. Coffee machine in the room is similar to Nespresso, and just as good.
Top tip, the hotel has a fleet of town cars, this is not advertised, be really good to the doormen and they will offer you a car (Merc) for short trips. Saves a fortune on cabs a d it does look pretty good when you pull up in a chauffeur driven car, let's just say we had no trouble getting into shops who's doors are locked and a burly security guard vets you!
Would stay again, made us feel like it was our home in NYC, staff were great and nothing is too much trouble.

name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City
The London NYC
title: “Perfect Location in the Big Apple”
text:
Just finished a four night stay at the London for a weekend retreat with my wife. I do wish I could give 4.5 stars but I will round up to 5 since the overall experience was great. The hotel is ideally situated in the middle of everything - the park is a few blocks north, Times Square a few blocks south and shopping, restaurants and bars are all within walking distance. We had a room at the very edge of the building that was apparently a little different layout then most of the rooms but we loved it, still huge and we had an amazing view of the city from the living area and an incredible view of the park to the north. I thought the hotel was very quiet, but we were on the 35th floor, I can see how the lower floors would be much noisier.
The good - 
-Exceptional room. Huge and nicely appointed, comfortable bed, great layout, great view, everything in excellent condition and convenient. Flat Panel TV's in both rooms, lots of power outlets, iphone dock alarm clock.
- Location that cannot be beat.
- Great views from the room.
- Overall great vibe of the hotel and area.
The negatives.
- If you are a stickler for over the top Ritz Carlton style customer service, this place is not that. The employees were accommodating and willing but not exceptional. Most seemed like it was their job and and not that happy to be there. Housekeeping and bell staff was great. Restaurant staff was just mediocre. No one says hello or welcomes you back, everyone just kind of does their job.
- They did get my bill wrong but fixed it quickly and politely. We stayed with Amex FHR and were not offered a room upgrade, which seems to be the norm here. Having said that though, the room was still great.
- As others have mentioned, the breakfast is just ok. We had it included with our rate. I would never pay $70 for two to eat their continental breakfast when there are dozens of other great restaurants within a few blocks. We also were entitled to free afternoon tea with our rate, but didn't partake in that.
- They did have a house car but this seems to be a hidden secret that only the bell staff know about and it was not available the one time we tried to use it.
We really enjoyed the place and wouldn't hesitate to go back. The room and location are exceptional. Flute champagne bar is a block away and the Ava rooftop bar on top of the Dream hotel were both great and very close. Faces and Names right next door is great as well, but more of a loud and rowdy crowd than the other two.

name: The London NYC
title: “Great hotel.”
text: I've stayed here on business before and brought my partner back for a holiday. The rooms are considerably bigger than I have experienced in many past stays in the city at other 5 star hotels. The bed and linen are super soft and gave a great night's sleep - I'm one of those people who never believes a hotel bed can be comfier than my own bed back home, but this hotel is the exception. (I'm also strangely addicted to their toiletries). They have a good gym and a great bar. The food is what I would call 5 star NY hotel standard, rather than exceptional - but you're in New York, you have loads of choice. The staff were always friendly and polite, and in this I would say the customer service was exceptional.

name: Lowell Hotel
title: “European Luxury in the USA”
text: Having stayed at the The Lowell 8 times in the last 3 years, it is my favorite Hotel in all of New York, and possibly the USA. If you want to get the feel of being a New Yorker living near Central Park & within steps of the best shopping in the city, you won't want to miss coming "home" to The Lowell. I was there for Christmas in 2003 with my pekingese, and we had the best Christmas I've ever had. Room service is superb, the concierge will arrange whatever requests you may have, and the desk staff treated me & my dog like we were 1st class. The rooms are very quiet and furnishings are very comfortable. Enjoy your trip to New York & please consider this your fine luxurious peaceful home away from home.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Decent hotel for the money in Times Square”
text:
nice big rooms and even bigger bathrooms
nice timesquare views from the higher level floors

name: Morgans Hotel
title: “Très satisfaisant”
text: Comme expliqué dans les avis précédents, hôtel très bien situé, personnel accueillant, chambre très confortable, spacieuse pour Manhattan, bonne literie. Petit bémol, salle de bain un peu petite, pas de baignoire (ce qui est appréciable après de longues journées de marche) mais la douche est moderne et spacieuse. Nous avions le wi fi gratuit dans la chambre, en effet c est un peu bruyant (bruit de la rue) mais pas trop gênant. Petit déjeuner délicieux, dans une salle tamisée intimiste.nous avons en revanche commandé des noodles en chambre de la carte du resto un soir et c était cher et pas bon du tout.. Mais bon c est un detail. Bref, nous avons été ravis et recommandons vivement cet hôtel.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York West 35th
title: “Good location, not a full-service hotel”
text:
this property has its good points. it's very central, especially if you want to do some shoping around Herald Square or take the PATH train to Hoboken. it's also very close to Penn Station.
it's not a full-servie hotel by any means and the accomodations are not really upscale. Clean, yes. Upscale, no. It's quite basic. 
There is no valet parking here and it's in a very congested area. there is a garage across the street, but if it's full (like it was when I went there) you're sort of screwed. Find your own parking!
The room was basic. clean. Small. ok, but not fantastic by any strecth of the imagination.
Unless I couldnt find a better room anywhere else, I probably would not stay here again.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York West 35th
title: “Excellent”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed here during fashion week and the US Open. It was a great stay. Extremely economical,clean, and hospitable. Great location,right near great shopping and the subway so you can get wherever you need to.

name: The Jewel Facing Rockefeller Center
title: “Awesome location!”
text: We were able to check in early, received a discount at the little terrace restaurant next door and we just steps away from Central Park, Times Square, Rockefeller Center. I'd stay again!

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Hospitality House
title: “Awesome stay in NYC!”
text:
We took a group of 4 women and 2 young girls to NYC for 5 days. This hotel was perfect! It was clean, spacious, and comfortable! We had plenty of room to relax after a full day of touring, and the beds made for a great nights sleep! The staff - Dave & Tom (and one staff member whose name I don't know, he is from the Dominican Republic) - they were all GREAT!!! So fun to talk with, and they were very helpful with directions and recommendations...just overall very accommodating! The location is perfect, not in the hustle and bustle of Times Square, but within walking distance to Rockefeller Center and subway stops. We had no problems getting around. We are already planning our next trip and will DEFINITELY stay at this hotel again! 
Thanks, guys, for a wonderful stay in NYC!!!

name: The Jewel Facing Rockefeller Center
title: “Not dissapointed”
text: Check in was a bit of a frenzy, it has a very small reception area with no front desk, only two computers for self check-in. Our room wasnt ready until 4pm so we had to wait a while. The room was a decent size but unfortunately was a double room (there were 3 of us).a quick call downstairs and a camp bed was quickly provided. The room was clean apart from the shower, which was covered in long hairs. This obviously hadn't been cleaned after the previous guests had vacated. I didnt make a fuss about this, just washed them away myself. We were on the 4th floor and had no view whatsoever (the side of an office building), but this didnt really matter as we only used the otel for sleeping in. The room had all the conveniences that you would expect, apart from a safe, but I think this could be done at reception. Despite the slight negatives, we enjoyed our stay and would certainly consider staying here again if the price was right. The location was ideal for all the Broadway attractions, Fifth Avenue and Central Park.

name: Ink48 - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “beautiful experience”
text: I live in Long Island, and I stayed at ink48 for an anniversary mini-getaway weekend with my boyfriend, and it was everything that I was looking for! We stayed in a cityview studio king room, which was marvelous. the view of new york city was STUNNING (and let me tell you, being a native New Yorker, it is hard to find a place with a view like that). The room was impeccably clean and attention to detail was outstanding (you can tell a lot of thought went into the design of the rooms). The hotel had a very chic, young, hip vibe and the staff was extremely accommodating and friendly. The only downfall is that it is kind of far from the action, but not terribly far at all - definitely doable. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a stay in Manhattan.

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “SUPER MODERNO !”
text:
Io e mio marito ci siamo stati a fine agosto, ci siamo trovati benissimo. L'hotel è super moderno, mai visto uno simile, molto utile la possibilità di collegarsi ad internet nella hall del quarto piano, e molto utile la stanza con la macchinetta del caffè e altre bevande calde gratuita !!! E' vero la stanza è molto piccola ma nuova, pulita e completamente insonorizzata dunque ottima per un breve soggiorno in questa città stupenda !!!
La colazione è abbondante con vari tipi di muffin, è molto bello farla in terrazzo...
Come posizione è a 10 minuti da time square, dunque molto comodo ...Concludendo giudizio molto positivo, lo consiglio e ringrazio per le atre recensioni che ci hanno aiutato a scegliere questo hotel.

name: Affinia Dumont
title: “Loved the Affinia Dumont”
text: My three girlfriends and I (including an appellate court judge) just returned from a four-night ("ladies weekend") stay at the Affinia Dumont -- and can't stop talking about the hotel. First off, I booked the hotel for the group based on the past reviews and I am glad I disregarded the few bad reviews. The hotel was perfect for the four of us -- plenty of room (big by NYC standards); the kitchennette came in very handy (especially with the Murray Market next door); the location was great (away from noisy Times Square) and within walking/cab distance to just about anywhere; and the staff were extremely friendly and accommodating. We will definitely be staying here again on our next trip and have even told my husband that next time we are in NYC we too will be staying here. In one word the experience was truly "WONDERFUL"!

name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
title: “Cómodo pero...”
text: Está bien situado, a dos calles de una estación de metro y a 15 minutos andando de Times Square. La llegada puede ser confusa, porque en la entrada apenas hay personal y el check-in tienes que hacerlo en unos ordenadores. Una vez que entras te enteras (porque nadie te lo ha dicho) que la recepción está en la 4ª planta y allí si hay personal para ayudarte. Las habitaciones son muy pequeñas, con camas que se pliegan y se convierten en una especie de sofá (sólo con darle a un botón). El baño está separado de la habitación por una cortina blanca, nada más y tiene una puerta de cristal transparente. La ducha tiene poca presión. No hay armarios, hay dos percheros y dos cajones. Debajo de la cama caben las maletas grandes, aunque el espacio sigue siendo poco para guardar la ropa de dos personas. Hay una habitación en cada planta con cafetera, microondas, etc. El precio de la habitación incluye un desayuno de café/té y muffins. Hay wifi gratis en todo el hotel y 4 ordenadores en la recepción a disposición de los clientes. Creo que el precio es excesivo para un servicio bastante limitado (cama, ducha y café+muffin), aunque por lo que he visto no hay hoteles mucho más baratos en Manhattan...

name: Hilton Garden Inn Times Square
title: “Great Service, Great Location”
text:
Hotel is located literally one block away from Times Square. 
The rooms were a decent size. With a very comfortable bed. 
The people that worked there are by far the best. There is a concierge that is open for about 12 hours during the day (very helpful).There is also a 24 hr convenience store. 
There is a nice Japanese restaurant called Akoi right across the street from the hotel. I recommend it to anyone who likes sushi. 
Honestly, if you booked this hotel then you have nothing to worry about. If you are considering it I suggest you book it.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York West 35th
title: “Excellent hotel for the value”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights. The location is perfect near the subway, close to Times Square and Macys right across the street. The property does lack a restaurant, but there are plenty of places nearby. My friend was worried about bed bugs in NYC, but this was not an issue with the Garden Gate. Very clean rooms. I would definitely stay here again.

name: Hilton Times Square
title: “The best of four Hiltons we tried in NYC”
text:
This week we stayed at the Waldorf, Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square, the Millenium Hilton and this one. This one was the best.
Waldorf was poor, over priced and impersonal. Doubletree had a great location but tiny rooms. Millenium was friendly but noisy because of the building at Ground Zero. Hilton Times Square ticks all the boxes. Great location, warm welcome ( even though the current refurb works means you go in via a side entrance) good size rooms. This is the one we will go back to.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “An Oasis in Time Square Chaos”
text:
Stayed 2 nights (award) and found the hotel just as good as my last stay several years ago. The place was fully booked as there was a jewelry and fashion accesories convention occupying 9 floors. As a result, did not receive any upgrade for Gold status.
PROS:
-spacious 2-room suites with 2 TV's, microwave, small empty fridge, touch-sensored honor bar, and small safe.
-free wireless HSIA for gold and diamond members (no wired access available)
-complimentary full hot breakfast buffet for gold and diamonds (normally $28) at restaurant
-quiet despite outside chaos; comfortable beds.
-central location: multiple subway lines within 2 blocks, close to all theaters, endless dining options
CONS:
-bathtub spout is overpressured like a firehose, as was the showerhead--major need for a flow restrictor. Would be very effective for interrogating terrorists, probably better than waterboarding.
-fitness center: dated Precor equipment that seems to shake and rattle. The room is very warm despite high ceilings. There is no bathroom on the same floor--have to go up 1 floor to the restaurant level.
-business center: temporarily located on lobby level in a tiny room the size of a closet. The least they should do is PUT UP A TERMINAL FOR PRINTING BOARDING PASSES at the front desk (plenty of room)

name: Trump International Hotel and Tower
title: “Beware even at 1,200 dollars a night plus tax there are Bed Bugs in this hotellll!”
text: The General Manager Suzie Mills refused to admit that the Hotel had any culpability in the appalling bed bug bites that my son suffered during our stay. He slept on sleep out couch in the living room and we noticed bites on his body, his ear and his head. These appeared after a couple of nights there and no more appeared once we left .. We did not suffer from these since we slept in a bed in the bedroom. While the service and staff were pleasant - the hotel's handling of this situation when the bed bug bites were reported was one of denial and obfuscation. This left an extremely bad impression and we would not recommend this hotel.

name: The New York Palace Hotel
title: “Towers of New York Palace”
text: Vi booket oss inn på en juniorsuite på the Towers og ble ved ankomst oppgradert til en fantastisk hjørne suite i 46 etg med vakker utsikt over byen. Den private cluben for gjestene på Towers var helt super; nydelig frokost og veldig praktisk med muligheten til å slappe av der med god mat og forfriskninger gjennom hele dagen når det var behov for det. Hotellet ligger veldig flott til mellom 50 og 51 gate på Madison, rett ved Saks fifht og kort vei til Rockefeller center og MoMA, for å nevne noe.
