American Airlines put us up in this hotel after messing up our flight. Stayed one night, with late arrival and early checkout, so spent very little time at the property.
Pros:
Shuttle provided to/from airport.
Friendly and helpful front-desk staff.
Cons:
WiFi did not work; waited on hold for offsite tech support but I gave up before my call was taken.
Air conditioning and refrigerator were loud.
Airport shuttle takes about 10 minutes; not terrible, but for more convenience check out the Hilton located at the airport.

name: City Suites Hotel
title: “A good hotel in a great location”
text:
We stayed at the City Suites on Saturday, April 30th for one night. We booked a standard queen room (not a suite) since we were not planning on spending much time in the room. The room was a bit larger than most boutique hotels in a city. The bathroom had a bit more room as well. We had no problem with noise as mentioned in other posts. The room was very quite.
The best asset of this hotel is the location. We came in for a concert and wanted to bar hop on Halsted after the show. This hotel is perfect as Halsted is only a block away. There are also plenty of shops and good restaurants nearby. There is a train station right next door which makes getting around the city easy.
Overall the hotel is a good value.

name: BEST WESTERN Plus Hawthorne Terrace Hotel
title: “Very Cute Hotel! Loved It”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel on August 29th through August 31, 2005. We were visiting Chicago as a little getaway for my birthday! We had tickets to a Cubs game and this hotel was perfect because it is only like 5 Blocks from Wrigleyfield. The hotel is in a great location if you want to experience Chicago without all of the hustle & bustle of being downtown. There were several little bars and restuarants all within walking distance and Lake Michigan was only about 2 blocks away! We actually spent alot of our time just walking around the neighborhoods and enjoying all of the views of the old homes & historic buildings. The hotel itself was so cute! It was very small and had a more of a bed and breakfast feel about it. I would reccomend this hotel to visitors young and old! It was a great choice!

name: Mark Twain Hotel
title: “Stay Away”
text: Just so everyone knows, this is a transient/SRO hotel. What this means is that you'll be rooming with generally unsavory. It's a safe neighborhood, but not this hotel -- its not intended for tourists. STAY AWAY.

name: Wyndham Blake Chicago
title: “Decent hotel- missing some amenities”
text: I recently stayed at this hotel for my own wedding. Almost all of my out of town guests stayed here as well. I found the hotel to be quite nice in terms of the actual room- it was spacious, had quality bedding and towels, and good bathroom products. I found the staff to be nice but a little pushy. The location was fantastic and many people really enjoyed being close to all the attractions. However, several of my guests exclaimed "this might be the WORST hotel I've EVER stayed in" because there were no refrigerators or microwaves in the rooms. For the amount of money we were paying it was terrible that those sorts of amenities were not included. Moreover, when I called to ask about the refrigerators the front desk told me I could "rent one for $30 a day." Seriously? You've got to be kidding me. To top it off most people ended up leaving their cars in other lots because the hotel charges over $40 a night for parking- that just seems a little bit exorbitant. I would not stay here again for full price.

name: Hyatt Chicago Magnificent Mile
title: “Nothing special”
text: Good location, nice entrance and old rooms. Shabby, wallpapers are opening, TV old and small. needs urgent re-modelling to match the price. I honestly can't find a justification for the price (300 US$). Many better option around the same area.

name: Amber Inn
title: “Cannot get any better for the price”
text:
This hotel I would recommend to anyone. The staff are friendy; the ambience is nice; the rooms are spacious, clean, and well taken care off. You are only 12 - 15 minutes from downtown which is pretty close. 
Highly recommended.

name: Springhill Suites Chicago Downtown / River North
title: “Great value for Chicago downtown”
text: Consider the rate together with it's location, it is value for money. It's clean and modern. And it has a nice and comfortable lobby area, in which I had couple sync-up meetings with business associates. Breakfast area is big and clean as well, it started my days pretty well.

name: Springhill Suites Chicago Downtown / River North
title: “The free breakfast was unexpected and great!”
text: We stayed at this hotel during the Chicago Marathon. My fiance and I both ran the marathon and the location was great. We were close to the river, close to a lot of great restaurants and close to Niketown, close to the L and the subway. One thing I wish this hotel had in our room was a bath tub, especially after the race. Our room only had a shower. The hotel provided breakfasts every morning which helped us save time and money. The staff was very friendly and the hotel was clean and nice. Check out was a breeze.

name: Wyndham Blake Chicago
title: “Just what I needed as a business traveler”
text: Spacious, clean and comfortable room. Internet access is essential for me , so when i ran into a glitch (twice!), I got immediate assistance in fixing my "operator error" problem.

name: Travelodge Chicago Downtown
title: “If you need a place to stay, it serves its purpose”
text: I was in town for a conference and every place in town was booked or extremely over priced. I got a reservation here for $149 a night. I had a 1 bedroom suite. It was basic but clean. Staff was friendly. If your looking for a place to stay, the location is great and it is will accomplish a clean place to sleep and shower.

name: Congress Plaza Hotel
title: “Security??”
text: My son and his fiance stayed there this weekend. Their room was broken into in the middle of the night, while they slept. They awoke to find her purse, his wallet and his cell phone missing. Whoever came into the room would have had to have a room key to enter. The hotel management really didn't seem to concerned about it other than having them file a report with hotel security and the police department. You would think they would be concerned as to how someone would have a key to enter another's room?

name: Swissotel Chicago
title: “Great choice, location and possibly upgrade?”
text: Stayed here last summer for a girls night out. Got upgrade to a gorgeous suite and had the best time. Room was very comfortable, room service was delicious and quick and overall we had a great time staying here.

name: Midway Inn
title: “WORST HOTEL EVER!”
text:
We were driving in from 3 hours away to fly out of Chicago. Since we were going to be getting in late and flying out early, we decided to book an "economy" hotel. Worst decision ever made! 
First of all, we booked the hotel through a website. We were told that they had a park and ride and it was only going to cost us $20 for the duration we were gone. We arrived into our room to find both of the beds missing a leg and leaning to the side. We asked to move to a different room, which they were accommodating. The new room didn't have fitted sheets on the bed, the pillows smelled musty with stains on them (we covered the pillows with extra t-shirts we packed and just layed on top of the sheets without any covers...I wasn't about to use the bedspread with holes in it), the shower curtain was covered in mildew, i was scared to look at the rest of the place,and I woke up early the next morning to find 3 extra guests in our bed (looked like small roaches). The only reason we didn't go to a different hotel was because it was late and the kids were cranky. Plus, we figured we could handle a few hours. 
When we ended up leaving our car there (surprised to find it was still there when we came back on our return 10 days later) we found out it was $30 more than they originally told us. What could we do then since we were already there?
Once we got back from our vacation, as soon as we landed, my husband called the shuttle to let them know we needed a ride. After about 30 minutes my husband called them to find out where they were in case we were in the wrong place. They told him the driver tried to call us but we didn't answer. This wasn't true because my husband had his cell in his hand the whole time and there wasn't a missed call notice. My husband confirmed the phone number with the guy dispatching the driver and was told the driver will be calling us soon. We never received a phone call. This went on for another 2 hours! We were finally told to just get a cab!! We already paid them for their service!!! By this time, it was 3:30am and we had been sitting on the curb for 3 hour with 2 very cranky kids (a 2 year old and a 10 month old). We were literally the last people out of the airport. We ended up having to pay an extra $15 to cram into a cab. 
When we got back to the hotel of course my husband had something to say to the manager. We were told the manager wasn't available and to call back the next day. Of course we didn't want to stay at that rat hole again and since it was so late (ER...early) we decided to just drive home 3 hours. When we called the next day, the manager said there was nothing he could do to accommodate us.
 We paid an extra $30 dollars for the park and ride than we were originally told, waited for over 2.5 hours for the shuttle to pick us up to be told to just get a cab, then paid an extra $15 just to get back to the hotel, then told they wouldnt reimburse us for the cab fair!! Mind you, my husband was very courteous (unlike i would have been) while dealing with these people. By this time, we could have stayed in a MUCH cleaner place for a cheaper price.

name: BEST WESTERN Grant Park Hotel
title: “We always stay here when visiting our son at Columbia College”
text: Although this hotel is quite basic, we always stay here when visiting our son at college in Chicago. The location can't be beat--and the price for the value is the best we've found. Internet is free, parking is only $24 and we can walk or bus anywhere we need to go. The Museum Campus is literally across the street. Yolks is right next door! We have stayed at the Hilton just down the street for more money, then were charged $12 a night for internet, $50 a night for parking and received blase' service. The rooms are basic but clean, and the one time our room was less than satisfactory we were moved at once.

name: Clarion Hotel Midway Airport
title: “Not impressed for a Sheraton property. OLD property in need of updating”
text: For the price and the Sheraton name, i was not impressed. It's an older converted property that needs more updating. Convienient to the airport. Shuttle was slow. Beds were OK, good pillows. OK work area with good chair, but NO plugs nearby. Moderate road noise. bathroom was updated and was decent, had flat screen TV. Noisey AC unit. Overall an OK property, but the Sheraton name calls for higher standards than this and the nightly rate was no bargin.

name: BEST WESTERN Grant Park Hotel
title: “Don't worry about other reviews”
text:
Unless you are planning to spend a great deal of time in your room the Grant Park Hotel was fine. I was part of a group tour so , of course, the price was right. The room had everything we needed including a great view from rm. 904. The pillows others griped about must have been replaced and there wer THREE on each bed (we had 2). We had no noise problem and since I had read other reviews complaing about the thin walls I took some earplugs but never got them out of the package. We pulled up in a motorcoach of 4r people and our rooms were quickly assigned and the luggage was delivered very quickly. 
We had in included breakfast at Mei's Kitchen, the attached restaurant which was buffet style and OK. As to other meals the service can be slow. But a late night pizza just before they closed was promptly served.
The location is very good EXCEPT for the miimal amount of places close by to dine. Head north for some better choices.

name: Clarion Hotel Midway Airport
title: “There are worse places to stay”
text:
Spent 2 nights here during a training session for work. The training event was totally disrupted by other events going on in the hotel at the same time. Please understand that we were holding a education presentation while a very loud worship service/concert was going on in the next room. The front desk staff made it clear to us that it was not their fault. We found a resolution, but without much assistance from staff.
The room I stayed in was not well kept. The window would not latch & allowed a cool Chicago breeze to blow in all night. I didn't discover that until I had unpacked my stuff & it was just too much trouble to leave. Dirty carpet. I checked the mattress, it seemed newish, which was a big relief. When I tried to have breakfast delivered, nobody ever answered the phone - I made 2 attempts. 
If you are needing a place to stay when flying out of Midway, this would work. I think there are better choices that are actually closer to the airport, as well. Unless Sheraton is planning a big renovation, I will find someplace to stay when I need to be in the vicinity of Midway. And if you are looking for training facilities, this is NOT the place.

name: Holiday Inn Chicago O'Hare
title: “Way overpriced and smelled of smoke so badly”
text: Way overpriced ($200 a night), it was an extremely busy weekend with lollapalooza and we expected to pay that much. But I asked for a non smoking room since it bothers my husbands asthma and what do we end up getting, a smoking room. And it smelled horibally of smoke, we went down to the front desk to ask for a non smoking room and of course they didn't have one. Our room also didn't have a blow dryer which it was supposed to have and when we called to get one they said we should have one and they didn't have any. The bathroom was very nice and the bed was really nice but I would never recommend this hotel

name: Chicago's Essex Inn
title: “"Very Handy To Willis Tower"”
text: Visited Chicago last year with my Father it was a joining Hotel for Route 66 tour which tour was just OK nothing spectacular if ever did Route 66 again would just drive you get to stop wherever you want you do not get that choice on a bus tour! I live in Australia so travelled a real long way but Chicago is a beautiful city am planning on visiting again next year with my children.Essex inn is in a good location,have to agree with some other reviews that the cafe downstairs is very expensive and also the menu choices are pretty sparse as well! But would stay again though! There is a starbucks up the road which is handy for your morning caffiene fix!

name: BEST WESTERN Grant Park Hotel
title: “Great on a Budget”
text:
My family and I recently returned from a week in Chicago. 
The Grant Park Best Western was an excellent location and the parking fees were quite reasonable for downtown Chicago. 
Although the hotel was no frills, we were very happy with our stay. We aren't picky travellers and just use the room to sleep.
You can't beat the price and location of this hotel!

name: Inn at Lincoln Park
title: “room ok bathtub cloged”
text: the room was nice,big and clean but the shower had a drian issue the water backed up in the tub not good i recomend they get that fixed

name: Swissotel Chicago
title: “One night”
text: Husband and I stayed one night. Yes there was construction but it did not bother us. We heard nothing in our room. We had great view of lake. Bed was comfortable. We loved the location. We walked to dinner and back from shed aquarium along the lake shore( very nice day). Staff was nice. I would stay again.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile
title: “No problems at all”
text:
We stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn for 5 nights. No line at check in and we valeted our car, checked in and was in our room within 10 minutes of pulling up to the covered entrance. We had our room serviced every day, we had fresh towels for 3 people every day, we had coffee and sugar packets every day. 
The room wasn't small to us, however, we just spent a week on the Carnival Destiny with the same 3 people, including an 18 year old 6'5" boy. Now that was small!
The beds are unbelievably comfortably, weird looking but comfy.
We didn't buy anything from the little room at the front desk cuz it was pricey but did go to the Jewel/Osco grocery store that was around the corner. We thought the restaurant was a little pricey so we went elsewhere to eat.
The valet parking was always ready for us and our car was always delivered promptly. They even gave us quicker directions to the Field Museum then we were going to use.
It is so convenient to everything you don't need a car to get around. There are even movie theaters just down the street. Easy access from I90 both coming into the city and leaving the city.
Didn't have any trouble checking out and my bill exactly matched the quote I received when I made on-line reservations.

name: Chicago's Essex Inn
title: “Great Conference alternative for Hilton Chicago”
text:
I stayed at the Essex Inn as a less expensive alternative to staying at the Hilton Chicago for a professional organization conference. Overall I was very happy with this decision. The room seemed recently remodeled. My king room had updated an updated bathroom with modern decor and furniture. My room included a mini-fridge and large flat panel TV. The bed was comfortable enough.
You should keep in mind this is an older building in downtown Chicago, so there are some downsides. The biggest drawbacks were really small shower with no tub, old AC/Heating system that does not allow for much control (though it was comfortable, I like to sleep in a cold room), and a slow elevator system. These were all manageable tradeoffs for the cost compared to staying at the Hilton (over $100 more per night). Walking next door to the Hilton was a breeze for my conference.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown Lakefront
title: “Great Location”
text: We stayed at the Embassy Suites Lakefront with our grandson in June, 2011. The room was very clean, the "cooked to order" breakfast was great, the guys at the valet station were very helpful but best of all was the location. You can walk to Navy Pier in four blocks and then take a water taxi to the museum campus or get on the "hop on/hop off" bus that goes all over downtown. You are also only about 2 blocks to Fox & Obel Market/Cafe/Bistro. It is similar to a Whole Foods but with a really nice Bistro. We ate dinner at their Bistro one night and it was very good.

name: Springhill Suites Chicago Downtown / River North
title: “Where do I put my stuff?”
text: We had a "larger corner suite" for six days but while trying for a clean look, the hotel forgot some guests like to unpack. There were no dressers, no towel bars in the bathoom, and a tiny closet which also held a built-in four drawer shelf and the ironing board, iron and hair dryer. There was only one night stand for our king bed and one lamp overhead in the middle - not good for bedtime readers! The sink area was only large enough for the sink, with no counter space. There were two open shelves under the sink for the towels; I kept trying to store toiletries there but the cleaning staff would pull them out, put them on the floor, and replace the towels! Our 11 year old was assigned the pull-out couch and we had to put his clothes under the tv shelf; again, no drawers in the living area. There were no in-room movies and tv channels were limited, but we did play a lot of cards at night instead. The water coming out of the sinks smelled horrible. The breakfast area was chaotic and limited; after the first day, we grabbed a yogurt and banana and left. On the plus side, the location was awesome (if you could overlook feeling like a poor cousin to the better-appointed attached Residence Inn) and the staff was always cheerful and helpful. We will stay in the River North area again but not at this hotel.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown Lakefront
title: “great location”
text: We chose this hotel because of the location and it included breakfast. We were on a parking package also. Hotel is located only 3 blocks from Navy pier and one black from Michigan Avenue. You are in the heart of the city here. The staff was very friendly and helpfu. We would stay here again

name: Swissotel Chicago
title: “Very friendly”
text: We were only there one night but it was in a great location and our room had a great view. The people at the front desk were very nice and helpful. The only complaint was that there was gum stuck in the carpet by the couch but I assume the can fix that.

name: Ramada Inn Lake Shore - Chicago
title: “A litte known gem”
text: My husband I have stayed at the hotel once but went back a second time for a meal. The Hotel is a little old but kept very clean. the service was very good and very polite. The restaurant had a Friday night seafood buffett that was the best we had ever seen. We stayed there and attended a White Sox game in the evening, talk about and easy way to get to the game and back to the hotel, cap service was prompt. All in all we had a great stay.

name: Red Roof Inn
title: “Never Thought, It is not that hard to clean!!!!”
text:
We arrived at the hotel after 10:00P.M.on 8/10/2010.. It was my Birthday and our first time away in some time, from 5 Kids and our loving mother who has Dementia. I don't ask for much from a Hotel, 
1. The shower had a red bodly subatance on the walls and tub, not sure what it was!!! I took pictures if you would like me to send to you.
2. There was a chair bu a desk there was a dry dody fluid or something on the chair also. Also have pic. 
3.There was a hole in the wall where a outlet was before and there was no cover on it, u were able to see wires and insulation. Pic Also. 
4. D" was getting into bed and steped on a Heinken Beer Bottle Cap up side down. Also have pic.
There were other things but I feel these are the most imporant!!! 
Thank you,

name: Travelodge Chicago Downtown
title: “You cannot beat this prime location!!!”
text: I've read some of the reviews and I must say that I'm astonished by some of the bad reviews. I did not deal with any rude staff members or bed bugs. In fact it was quite the opposite. The staff was more than helpful. They held our luggage, called a taxi for us and even let us get our room earlier than the allotted check in time. The room and fairly simple. It was more than adequate enough for two people. My only regret is not having a fridge. The room did come with an ice bucket and that is how we kept our beer cold. A lot of the reviews also seem to focus on the grandeur of the rooms. For the location this hotel is a super deal in Chicago. If you stay 2 nights you get 20% knocked off and 3 nights you get 30% knocked off. The red line subway is only a block away which makes all the touristy area's very user friendly. Shed's Aquarium, The John Hancock Building and several of other places are within in walking distance. If your a light sleeper you might want to bring some ear phones because at times you can hear the trains rolling by but overall this is a good place to stay. I mean how long are you really going to spend in your hotel anyway? Especially if the trip is for leisure purposes.

name: Union League Club
title: “Reputation made me uncomfortable”
text:
I stayed at this hotel during a business conference. The participants were made aware of the attire guidelines so I was a little nervous about that. The conference attendees are in the education field and typically dress business casual to casual. After a long trip from the west to the east coast, I wanted to be as comfy as possible. Dressed in my nice casual attire, I arrived at the hotel and checked in. The staff was extremely helpful and I was happy that no one was staring at me (call me paranoid). The bellman escorted me to my room and explain everything in the room. The room was small, but nice. The bathroom was really small and and there wasn't a lot of room to move around. The shower was a nice size, no tub, This was surprising seeing as though this isn't a cheap hotel. Another suprise was that I heard no, I mean NO housekeeping carts in the hallway the following morning! Usually you hear the rumbling around of the cars and the maids yelling down the hall, but not here. It was quiet as a mouse. I don't know if this is typical but I sure enjoyed it :) I also enjoyed the free wifi.
My conference was 2.5 days and I didn't have a lot of extra time but I did take a couple hours to walk outside. It's in the business district so there are lots of people walking around and many stores to visit. There's a Macy's and Sears about a 7-10 min walk from the hotel and the L station is right around the corner which takes you directly to the airport for about 2.50. DO NOT take a cab to the airport in late afternoon because traffic is gridlocked. All in all it was a nice stay, however I like the freedom of dressing casually at a hotel, and the ULC just doesn't allow this. I also prefer a little more space in the room to move around. But if you don't mind this, and are okay with a very small bathroom, the Union League is a quality place to stay with terrific service. I'd say it was the best service I've had which makes it a worthy recommendations

name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel
title: “Mixed reviews”
text: We had a great stay and we did not stay in our room but for sleeping and resting. I would say on average we were out of the room from 9-9 every day for 4 days. The price was a little on the high side but you have to remember, just like in real estate... location location location. We were 5 blocks from the Red line and 3/4 of a block from the Magnificent Mile. Great places to eat near by and great breakfast joints just blocks away. A few other negatives were the size of the bathroom... no place to put your toiletries... it was way too small and there was no counter. Internet is not included which is a major bummer and when you purchase it... even the best one was faulty. I would take your $150-200 and try another place but when you compare to the places closest to this hotel, you are already looking at $350-600 for standard rooms so for this part of town... this is a good deal. Staff was excellent.

name: Travelodge Chicago Downtown
title: “You get what you pay for.”
text: We stayed at the Travelodge for two nights. The rooms were dark, worn and tired. Cramped space. Can't see out of the windows if you are short unless you stand on the bed. Worn carpet, blankets on bed looked like they had not been cleaned in a while. Cleaning staff did not come to our room, so beds were not made, sink and bathtub were not cleaned and toilet paper was not replaced (and we had three of us and were afraid we would run out). Location is OK - we were able to walk and/or take the Water Taxi to destinations, but there are other hotels closer to the action. As I only paid $71 a night for a special promotion, I can't complain about the price, but I guess you get what you pay for. We moved to another hotel for our third night there - located at Wacker and Wabash - and the room was large, clean and wonderful. That night cost us $200 and was well worth it. My advice is to look for deals, but also read the reviews and be prepared. A very low price might look attractive but you may be very unhappy once you get there. And for a bonus: When I got home and checked my bank statement, I found an additional charge for 1¢. Are you kidding me? Someone bothered to charge something for a penny? Next trip to Chicago will not find me staying there.

name: BEST WESTERN Grant Park Hotel
title: “it was a good hotel for the money”
text: We went to chicago for a couple of days and stayed in this hotel.. For the money 145.00 a night it was not bad.. We were walking distants for the musumes. There is a free trolly that picks you up not to far from the hotel either.. We tried the taste of chicago that was ok, but alot of people.. over all the room was ok for the money. the bed was kind of hard, but I would stay there again in the furture..

name: BEST WESTERN Grant Park Hotel
title: “This hotel is OK if you're not paying very much”
text:
The room is itself was OK and the location is all right, especially for the Field Museum, Soldier Field, and the Aquarium.
As has been mentioned, do not plan on taking advantage of the so-called breakfast. If you want a piece of toast and a glass of juice, fine.
The front desk, while pleasant, created a major hassle for me. I had borrowed a wireless network card to take advantage of the free internet, at which time my credit card was charged a deposit fee, unbeknownst to me. On check out, the front desk did not inquire whether I was returning the card, but proceeded to finalize my bill and ask for my signature. At that point I handed over the network card. They did not think to adjust the bill. I was unaware of their failure to refund the deposit until several weeks later, at which point I called and left a message for the front desk manager. No response. I sent a letter. No response. Several weeks later I called again, and talked to accounting. They promised to credit my account.

name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel
title: “Good hotel and great location”
text: I was with my friend to chicago, partly for work, partly for enjoyment. We stayed at this hotel which is located at the Magnificent Mile in Chicago. It was very cheap, located nicely and close to all attractions. In addition, the rooms were completely OK, maintainance was good, and we got free Wi-fi, which I did not get at other hotels in Chicago.

name: Chicago's Essex Inn
title: “Great location, lovely rooms, can be noisy!”
text:
We spent four nights in the Chicago Essex Inn and it was a lovely hotel in a great location, opposite Grant Park with good restaurants nearby. The staff were very helpful and have printed maps of interest and transport links. 
Our room was on the 12th floor and and was a bright spacious corner room, very tastefully decorated. This hotel boasts a swimming pool and a rooftop garden which is a great ammenity. There is a restaurant on the ground floor named Tribute that does good breakfasts at affordable prices. The only drawback we found was that the Loop train runs next to it at an elevated level so it was noisy at night. We could probably have moved rooms and the staff, I am sure, would have facilitated this but we had unpacked and got comfortable and so decided not to and soon enough got used to the sounds of trains in the night.
I would recommend this hotel but ensure you ask for a room away from the train tracks.

name: The Tremont Chicago Hotel at Magnificent Mile
title: “Great BOUTIQUE hotel”
text:
I've just stayed at the Tremont and had a great experience. I must say that it is a BOUTIQUE style hotel. It has classic styling with a European feel, so if you're expecting a place with a giant room, don't stay here. If you want a classy looking room with great staff, this is great. I stayed on the 7th floor and had a great view of the Hancock building from my room. 
The Positives: The staff was great. The girl at check-in was fantastic and gave me advice on where to go (and not) while also helping me to find a place that wasn't $50+/night to park. This is a fantastic location.
The Negatives: They had some weird blinds on the windows to prevent bugs from coming in. I think they're probably better to just permanently lock the windows and get rid of them. Also, there was no coffee maker in my room. There is a Starbucks across the street, but being a girl who's there on business, I'd rather have the coffee while I get ready and really don't have time to stop and get a coffee.

name: Ohio House Motel
title: “Weird little place with awesome staff”
text:
You'd be surprised to find a place like that downtown Chicago. It has no website and is not featured on Travelocity and the likes (as far as I know). I found it in the Lonely Planet Chicago in the budget section after failing miserably at booking any other place for the Chicago Marathon. Everything was booked 4 months in advanced, except for $400 and up luxury suites. This place still cost $89, which would buy you a decent room on a day other than the day before the Marathon (but I think prices a much lower the rest of the time).
Anyway, when it says "Motel", it IS a motel. Straight out of the '50s. It is not just retro-themed, it is truly retro, so if you like that sort of thing, go for it. I still am not completely sure what that gadget that reminded of an old record player/radio (it wasn't a record player) in the corner was, but artifacts like that ceased to exist at least 5 years ago. 
The place was really worn out, but with a remodeled bathroom. The sheets and blankets must have been on those beds for generations. It was clean, although still looked kind of sketchy, the kind of place that would be featured in the noir film. 
Customer service was excellent! The gentleman who helped us check in, was one of the most pleasant people I've ever met and that is the reason why I didn't hate the motel. You can't hate a place where such wonderful people work. We also needed some help the next day and the day shift woman was also great.
I would recommend this motel for people on a tight budget who don't care for frills.

name: The Westin Michigan Avenue Chicago
title: “Excellent Location!”
text: I had a weekend layover in Chicago (coming from the south) on my way home to Honolulu. I wanted a hotel that was close to everything, and the Westin on Michigan Avenue was the perfect spot! My late afternoon flight was delayed for 3 hours, so it was wonderful to walk into the Westin and be greeted with friendly smiles from the front dek staff and have a quick and smooth check in.. My room was on the 17th floor (facing the John Hancock Tower) and I have no complaints with my room. It was roomy and the bathroom was large with two double sinks. The location is convenient - right on Michigan Avenue and a couple of blocks to Rush Street where many restaurants and bars are located. Kira (at Concierge) was fantastic at recommending restaurants nearby, and even provided me with VIP two passes to a nearyby jazz club (saved us $40!). I also loved the fragrance that was infused throughout the hotel -- it smelled like I was in a spa. I found out that it was White Tea fragrance (same as the bath products). I loved it so much that I went down to the gift shop and purchased a bottle of White Tea lotion. I enjoyed my stay -- the entire staff was friendly and accommodating. If you are looking for a hotel that is near shopping and restaurants, the Westin on Michigan Avenue is the perfect hotel.

name: Allerton Hotel
title: “Great location but......”
text:
Everything - rooms, hallways, elevators, etc.- was small and cramped. One elevator was out of order for our entire stay, which made the waits unbearable. I attended a conference, and there was a group of students in the room next to us that were so loud it made hearing our presenters difficult, even with microphones.
That said, the location is great and the staff members we encountered (housekeeping and valet) were helpful and friendly.
I would stay here again if I got a bargain rate.

name: The Sutton Place Hotel
title: “Bumped into the right hotel for a good sleep”
text: Missed the flight out of chicago to Europe and was lost midnight, but I found this hotel through my travel agency.. - I never heard of it, althought I knew a few hotels in Chicago, but what a pleasant experience... - this is a quiet and very nice hotel for getting a sound sleep so one can look into the day with new eyes.. - as said by others, bathroom and bed was good and no noise at all from the street.. - staff was relly above average with regard to help... - it is right in the place of the happening area, so my night was shortened up by a snack and a few pints in the "dubliners", was a cool place..

name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel
title: “Great Location”
text: Hotel was clean, with clean bedding, a great location with some good views from the roof top.

name: The Whitehall Hotel
title: “Great location and pleasant service!!!!”
text:
Lots of charm to this older hotel. Everyone was extremely pleasant and helpful.
Location is perfect for all the great shopping and sites in this awesome town

name: Hotel Felix
title: “Soft beds, weaker water pressure, elevator noise”
text: As other reviews have already claimed, the hotel is clean, beautiful and well located. That being said, I'll add a few things that may be important to some people. The beds are REALLY soft. If you have a bad back like I do, this may be important to know. There are 4 different pillows to choose from, which may help you. The shower looks like it will be amazing, but the water pressure isn't impressive. This may matter to you if you have longer hair. You will not be taking a quick shower. Also, try not to stay next to the elevator. Through the thin walls you can hear the 'bing' every time it arrives on your floor. Otherwise, the staff is great and it's clean, so if you don't need a big room and the things above don't matter to you, then I definitely recommend this hotel.

name: Red Roof Inn
title: “Location, Location, Location”
text:
The best thing about this hotel is it's location. You cannot move for shops restaurants, bars etc.The price of the hotel was reasonable and in comparison to the other hotels in the immediate area was probably quite cheap.
The hotel is in an old building. The foyer has been modernised and is quite comfortable with very good friendly staff. The lifts to the rooms are small and are often quite busy. The rooms themselves are small and whilst the bartroom was clean it was evident that the hoover did not reach the corners of the room with a thin layer of dust running around the edge.
If you are fussy kind of person then you will find plenty to fault this hotel. If you are using it as a base for exploring this great city, are not spending too long inside the rooms and are sensible with your money then this hotel makes a great deal of sense.

name: The Tremont Chicago Hotel at Magnificent Mile
title: “Great Hotel. Great Location.”
text: If you are going to Chicago, make sure to check out this hotel. It is located a block from the Magnificent Mile - right across the street from the Water Tower Mall. The hotel is definitely old but that is what gives it its character. The hotel staff was friendly, the room was clean, the bed was comfortable, the shower was hot. We had a great view out the front of the the hotel on the 11th floor. We were able to go out and see the sites and then come back in the afternoon for a rest before heading out in the evening once again. This hotel is close to everything and a great bargain for a downtown hotel.

name: The Sutton Place Hotel
title: “The Sutton Place Hotel: Did Not Meet Our Expectations”
text:
My husband and I, who are both in our early thirties, stayed at the Sutton Place Hotel In Chicago from December 30, 2004 to January 3, 2005. I will start by saying that we have very high standards when we travel. Unfortunately, the Sutton Place Hotel did not meet our expectations. 
The reason that we selected the Sutton Place Hotel was because “The Connoisseur’s Guide to the World’s Best Resorts and Great Hotels: The 2004 Collection” rated it as one of the world’s best hotels in Chicago. According to the guide, the Peninsula Chicago and InterContinental Chicago were the other two choices in Chicago. We tried to book a room in these hotels as well, but they were completely sold out for New Years. 
The Sutton Place Hotel was built in 1988, but renovated in 2003. All I can say is that it did not look refurbished at all. The carpet and walls in the hallways and rooms had rips and stains. The rooms were the main disappointment. The furniture was old and tired looking, as well as just plain tacky. What was with the black leather headboard on the beds? The computer desk and dresser were faded and scratched, while the bed was less-than-average. Supposedly, the rooms had “state-of-the-art” sound systems, but if these were state-of-the-art sound systems, I would hate to see what a “regular” sound system looked like. I had a chance to see the other rooms and suites in the hotel and they were just as bad. 
The room service was beyond belief – something out of the Twilight Zone. One evening, I ordered room service and was told that it would arrive in 35 minutes. After an hour, I phoned back asking about the order. The waiter who answered the phone informed me that the cook had not shown up and consequently he (the waiter) had to cook and deliver the food. As I was completely mortified that a waiter was cooking the food, I immediately cancelled the order. This was completely unprofessional and unacceptable.
On the positive side, the hotel – lobby, elevators, hallways, and rooms – was always clean and fresh smelling. The maids were fantastic, as they were constantly cleaning these areas. 
The hotel had modern and updated bathrooms with a deep soaking tub and separate glass-enclosed shower.
The service at the door was impeccable and inviting upon our arrival, while the valet parking service was friendly, fast, and efficient. 
The location of the hotel was prime. It was within walking distance to the Gold Coast, Magnificent Mile with all the excellent shops such as Louis Vuitton, Gucci, Saks Fifth Avenue, and Neiman Marcus, as well as the outstanding restaurants, jazz and blues clubs, and martini bars.
Overall, the Sutton Place Hotel was not what we expected for a “world best hotel.” Whoever reviewed this hotel for the Connoisseur’s Guide is sadly mistaken. If you are looking for a true 5-star hotel like the Ritz Carlton or the Four Seasons, I would not recommend the Sutton Place Hotel. But if you are looking for a three-star hotel in a prime location, I would recommend the hotel. If you have any questions about the Sutton Place Hotel, please feel free to email me at tatianashaw@shaw.ca.

name: Allerton Hotel
title: “Another great time in the Windy City”
text: We travel to Chicago a couple of times a year and when shopping on Magnificent Mile this property always attracted me to stay. If you are the type of person who loves to go shopping on the most famous street in Chicago and dine at fine restaurants within walking distance then this is the area to stay. We requested high floor king bed and when we were given our room behind the elevator I have to admit I was concerned we weren't going to get a good night's sleep. Much to my amazement that this older hotel we didn't hear anything! We slept soundly with no interruptions. We didn't use any of the facilities or restaurants as we were invited out on a couple of occasions so can't comment on them. Overall a good stay and excellent location.

name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel
title: “They Would NOT Work With Me!”
text:
This looks like a great hotel and it probably is. My issue is not with the hotel but instead with the staff. My wife and I booked a room with this hotel in October 2011. We had a friend coming in to town and thought we would spend a day in Chicago as we try to do several times a year. We are from Peoria, IL but enjoy spending a couple weeks a year in the Windy City. On this particular trip, we decided to give this hotel a shot. Look at the pictures, how can you not want to stay here at least once?! We were really excited about the trip but early in day, we experienced some setbacks. Our friends flight was delayed by over three hours. Coming from Peoria, the flight delay would have put us quite a bit behind on all we wanted to do. We contacted the hotel at about 9am and asked to either cancel the room or reserve it for the following day instead. We explained the situation and we were simply told "sorry, there is nothing we can do for you". They hung up and that was the end of it. I called and left several messages for the manager but he/she never returned my call. 
Now we are planning another trip to Chicago to get away for 3 or 4 days but I think we will go back to the Comfort Suites on N. Michigan Ave. They have always worked well with us when we need something. Their staff is great and they trust that if something comes up, we will be back! 
I don’t want to this is a bad hotel because I see a lot of people love it; hopefully we just had a bad experience...or lack thereof.

name: The Whitehall Hotel
title: “Great Location, Fab Hotel”
text:
We stayed here at the end of September for two nights on our first trip to Chicago. We had a king room on the 17th floor and booked it last minute on the Orbitz web site. It was great value for money for a central city location.
The check in staff were very attentative, the valet parking and bell boys were very efficient. Our room was not ready but they took my cell phone and called when it was, however we were having too much fun sightseeing to go back for several hours.
There is a lot of history with this hotel and the leaflet dipiciting it is well worth the read.
This hotel is in a fab location, can't fault anything about it. Our floor was quiet, room spacious and very clean, shower good and the bed delightfully large and very comfy!! The only thing that seemed out of place was the old style television, having been very used to the new flat screens but now I am just nip-picking!!
We loved Chicago and the Whitehall Hotel was the icing on the cake!

name: Howard Johnson Inn Downtown Chicago
title: “gotta love the moldy bathroom”
text: If you love musty smell of mold spores in the morning this is the place to stay. If you have never experinced a water bed bath tub you have to check out room 214. The funny part is even the renovation sign was falling apart.. Was a great joke during the trip though.. Aparently a renovation is a new vanity and a shower insert with tons of caulk. Hey if you cannot make it to your bathroom feel free to urinate in the stairway everbody else has, the smell makes it obvious. I will say the only thing this place has going for it is the location and the front desk lady who was very helpful. The website photos are pretty funny to look at after our stay..

name: Allerton Hotel
title: “This Place is a Dump”
text:
I stayed at this property with friends for a girls' weekend on March 23-25, 2012. Interestingly (similar to another review), we had reserved a room with 2 double beds but when we arrived, we were told they only had a king room available and we were charged $35 for a roll-away. Both the king bed and roll-away mattresses were beyond dated and uncomfortable. Bedding and blankets were horribly old, worn, and scratchy. The surfaces in the room were covered with thick dust...I left a message in the dust for the housekeeping staff! A request for extra pillows and blankets required 3 phone calls to the front desk and they arrived 90 minutes later (after midnight when I was already in bed). 
In reading previous reviews, I saw the phone # and contact information for the Director of Operations, Nick Katinos,so I emailed him. He never responded which made me laugh a little since the responses here make it sound like he really cares. I can't say I was surprised.
The positive reviews really stun me...perhaps they have 2 vastly different categories of rooms?
There are lots of other options in Chicago so I'd never waste money at this place again.

name: Wyndham Blake Chicago
title: “this place was lovely Not!!!”
text: the hotel was okay looking from the outside. but inside, that is a whole different story. they messed up our rooms which we reserved a month in advance.we wanted a room with two double beds. but they said all they had was a one bed room with two cots.that just wasn't going to cut it so we talked to the manager and got what we wanted. we never saw any body there any way so there shouldn't have been a problem. all of the staff people were very rude to us. and on top of all that one of the two elevators broke.the hallways smelled musky and damp. we were on floor 4. and the ice machine was on floor 12. that was just great. the only thing that was even a little bit ok was the excerise room they had. it was all nice except the water jug didn't have any water in it. i will never stay there again as long as i live.

name: The Whitehall Hotel
title: “Great location, cheap price, somewhat outdated hotel.”
text:
The Whitehall Hotel sits only a half of a block away from Michigan Ave. A perfect location if you're into the shopping and eating that surround this area. For the price we paid you could not have asked for a better location. 
The rooms, and hotel in general, were old style. Not that it is cramped, but the rooms just seem to be set up differently than more modern hotel rooms. Not that I prefer one way or another. 
The room we stayed in was very clean with a king size bed, 2 cushioned chairs, a desk with a computer desk style chair, and a TV. 
Overall I recommend The Whitehall simply because the price is too good to beat in that area of Chicago. Would stay there again.

name: Travelodge Chicago Downtown
title: “Di poche pretese”
text:
L hotel si trova in una posizione ideale,è centrale e vicino alla fermata della metro.
La pulizia lascia molto a desiderare,a volte le camere non vengono neanche rifatte!considerato il prezzo si può trovare di meglio.letto minuscolo e camera altrettanto piccola.gli ascensori sono molto vintage.non lo consiglierei a nessuno.

name: The Westin Michigan Avenue Chicago
title: “No Luxury Starwood Choices in Downtown Chicago!”
text:
As a platinum Starwood Members, we just completed our third stay at the Westin Michigan Avenue Hotel. As a Starwood Member, you have several hotel choices when staying in downtown Chicago: Westin River North, Sheraton Chicago, W City Center, W Lakeshore, Four Points, and Termont Chicago. We have stayed in all of these SPG properties except the Termont (which is a newly acquired Starwood property). Overall, the Westin Michigan Avenue is a solid average hotel. It is your second best choice when staying at a Starwood property. Your best choice is the Westin River North. Here's some back-up information on our decision. 
Location - This hotel has the best location of any Starwood property in downtown. It is just steps from some of the best shopping in Chicago. Some of the higher rooms even have a lake view. 
Update Grades - As SPG Platinum Members, we have been upgraded during all of our stays. We were accommodated with wine, fresh fruit, and other amenities. This hotel treats their Starwood members very well.
Clean and Well Maintained - Even though this property is older, it is clean and fresh. Rooms are updated and maid service is excellent.
Rooms - We were given a suite with an adjoining bedroom during our recent stay. Large flat screen TV's and signature Westin bed were great. Starbuck's coffee and quick one cup coffee makers were handy. Refurbished gym was nice as it provided more options for tread mills, elliptical, and bikes plus free weights Hotel windows were older, leaked air and need replacement. Shower plumbing was noisy and water pressure was poor. We noticed their signature double headed shower heads no longer exist.
Customer Service - Concierge was either not available or just not there. General phone service took several minutes to pick up. Bellmen seemed non attentive and not engaging with the guests. Please note it was Thanksgiving week which may have contributed to the less than noteworthy service.
In summary, Chicago has some of the best hotels in the world. Unfortunately, if you're a loyal Starwood member, you have no luxury choices. No St Regis or Luxury Collection hotels exist. It time for Starwood to provide their members these options. We would like to suggest the conversion of the Westin Michigan Avenue as the first luxury SPG Hotel in the Downtown Chicago area. This hotel has the location and building to be a wonderful luxury hotel, however, in it's current state, it is just another average hotel

name: Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile
title: “Bad Experience”
text:
This hotel seemed like a good deal, and it's location is great for sure. The room was nice enough...
However, the problems began as we checked in for our one night stay. Rude staff were the norm. For instance, we had a couple of little questions and needed directions, pretty standard stuff, but the staff ignored us and when we did get their attention, seemed very put-out. And we're Hilton Honors members!
There were also lots of little inconveniences: 
- very little sound proofing, so we heard EVERYTHING that took place in the hallway all night long.
- no WiFi, just plugged-in internet (so you have to keep your laptop on the desk in the corner when in the room)
- the printing services that were advertised did not work (and again, no one was available to help us use them)
- we ran out of toothpaste, and found there were no complimentary toiletries if you forgot something, purchase for $5 plus only.
And, at the attached restaurant, absolutely the WORST breakfast buffet I have ever had in a hotel. We had to leave early, so it was one of the only places open at that hour. Big mistake. Even at 6:30am, the food was cold, stale and generally bad. The omelettes, made to order, were the only good option available. And this for something like $15. I'm sure it's good for other meals, but avoid the breakfast!
I'm confident you can find something better in Chicago for this price.

name: Howard Johnson Inn Downtown Chicago
title: “It's allright”
text: True. It was kinda old, but all the amenities worked except for the Wi-Fi which was absent the first 2 days of my 5 day stay. The dinner is really nice, too. The hotel provides really good value for the price.

name: Holiday Inn Chicago Downtown
title: “close to subway”
text: The front desk clerk (Bianca) was very friendly and funny. She had some tips for us out of towners. We were assessed an upcharge for an extra bed instead of one king. I thought that was alot of money compared to what we payed for the room. The room itself was good. Clean, not huge, comfy.

name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel
title: “Great location - clean & friendly”
text: This hotel we found on line after reading reviews here and elsewhere. For the price - the location simply cannot be beat. It is in the heart of it all and close to everything. The place was clean, very clean. Others mentioned the A/C noise, but we did not notice. It is not central A/C but a wall unit but had no climate issues. The room sadly I was a little disapointed in - clean as a whistle, and like major City rooms, bathrooms were small but expected. The reason for the let down was the rooms did not have the same boutique feel that we expected after seeing the lobby and main floor areas. It felt like what I would expect at a Comfort Inn. They appeared to be recently remodeled too just not consistent and a bit of a let down. THE STAFF HERE WAS AMAZING! Pointed us in a direction everyday and even took the time to point out maps and places to visit! Would return, but may seek out a hotel with a more boutique feel throughout.

name: Hotel Felix
title: “Spa-Like Vibe, VERY small rooms”
text:
Hotel Felix is a small eco-friendly boutique hotel with a relaxing, spa-like vibe to it. If you stay there and you like vodka, you're in luck!! The Felix is across the street from EFFEN Vodka. The views from the rooms are the breathtaking, but the rooms are exceptionally small, as are the bathrooms. 
Also, we could never get the air quite right, it was either hot or cold, not comfortable. A major thumbs up for the hotel besides their service is the fact that they offer FREE, I said FREE internet service and the bath products they offer are heavenly!!
The restaurant within the hotel is Elate Restaurant. In my opinion, they are pretty expensive. My friend and I had two burgers with fries and about 3 glasses of wine each and the bill was $125.00. We also had breakfast there one morning and it was good as were the burgers we had the night before.
I would suggest the Hotel Felix for a short stay in the city.

name: The Tremont Chicago Hotel at Magnificent Mile
title: “A bit worn but great location”
text: This is an old hotel that shows its age in wear and tear but we found it clean and acceptable. The location close to Michigan Ave Magnificent Mile is great, right across from Hancock Tower. Our main complaint is the old elevator of which there is only ONE. It won't budge if there are more than 6 people in it. We noticed a service elevator and started using it with no problem. Also, there is no coffee maker in the room. So, if you are looking for a reasonably priced hotel with great location but not much in the way of decor, this is for you. DON'T waste money on the continental breakfast at Ditka' s next door----it's awful!!!!!!!!

name: Hotel Felix
title: “What a Gem”
text:
Ended up at Hotel Felix on a last minute booking. Rooms are small yes but are in great shape, love the bedding and the shower.
No complaints about anything. The bellmen outside were always friendly, when exiting a taxi they always asked us to check and make sure we had all of our belongings. The hotel bar is nice and cozy, only 2 beers on tap but it allowed us to try new things. The resturant next door has some decent night life and the food was great!

name: Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile
title: “Very Good Stay”
text: I attended a convention the week of Nov. 6th. Before I made my reservation, I tried to obtain a room at one of the more exclusive hotels, but they were sold out due to several conventions scheduled that week. The Hilton Garden Inn was a very pleasant surprise. My room offered a good view of the cityline, good size and comfortable linens. I am very picky about my sleeping quarters, and this was very suitable and very clean. The bathroom was adequate. The service and staff was great! This was my first trip to Chicago and I wanted to experience the luxury's that Chicago offers. The hotel is in a great location and the Weber Grill located in the hotel had good steaks. Also, on the corner, I dined at PF Changs, which is always very good. Make sure you visit the Hancock Observatory and dine on the upper level for lunch, make sure you visit the restroom for the view. Also, you can't miss the Navy Pier. My favorite, of course, was the shopping on the Magnificent Mile! What an experience. Needless to say, I came with luggage weighing 24lbs and left with 46lbs and two carry on shopping bags.

name: Swissotel Chicago
title: “Rooms nice, service not so much”
text: I went back to this hotel for the second time for a conference that is there every year. The rooms are still nice, and well kept. The view from the higher floors is fabulous. The conference rooms were comfortable and well appointed. However, the service has slipped. The business center did not notify me about a package I was waiting for, and when I inquired about it they denied having it. Only after I checked the tracking number and it showed delivery did they even look. When I asked the front desk for help they were snippy and unhelpful. The chairs in the lobby are stained and dirty, and really need to be replaced. It gives the lobby a very shabby feel. On Friday, I asked for a 12:30 checkout (regular checkout time is noon). They flatly refused, because of " hotel capacity". I can't believe that half an hour would make a difference to them but it would have make it a lot more convenient for me. I hope the conference goes somewhere else next year.

name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel
title: “Hidden gem!!!!!”
text: We stayed at the inn of chicago for 2 nites the hotel was great. Location was perfect 1 block from Michigan ave 10 minute walk to pier. Rooms are small but clean & comfortable. Only knock LOUD a/c unit. Would definitely stay here again. Big Catt

name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel
title: “great location”
text: we got a great deal on galahotel.com if we were paying full price we would not be happy, the best thing about this hotel is the location, the rooms are shabby, the a/c is noisy and not very efficient I know that there was a heat wave when we were there but is that not the idea of a/c.. The staff were adequate, on two occasaions the terreced bar on the 22nd floor was closed for a private party. If you can get a good deal then this hotel would be fine but dont pay full price.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown Lakefront
title: “Wonderful place”
text: I loved this hotel. Rooms are huge and so is the bathroom. This cleaning service was awesome. The complimentary breakfast was much better than I expected and there was plenty of food at all times. I did also liked very much teh manager's reception. You could have free drinks for two hours and also snacks! The staff was always willing to help, they sure made my stay very comfortable!

name: Chicago's Essex Inn
title: “Very disappointed”
text:
I am very disappointed about this hotel. My boyfriend and I stayed here on December 29th, 2007 and it was discusting. The rooms were not as clean as what we would have liked. We were not told about any of the amenities. The desk clerks were very unhelpful and rude. The sounds from out side were like we were sleeping right on the street. I
stress not to stay here.

name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel
title: “OK Place offering value hotel downtown”
text:
Check in was amusing. I was given a room and walked in on a woman sleeping in her bed. She promptly got up and shut the door in my face and locked it. (Rightfully so!) Considering I had no help with my heavy bag and had to go back downstairs and get another room (struggling with my 50 lb bag w/o assistance) after a very long flight from Tokyo, I found this off-putting. 
The hotel is right downtown and location is fantastic! It's a 30 minute taxi from O'Hare (w/o traffic). Front desk staff were nice and offered useful info for getting around the area. Rooms are a nice size and have great TVs. Hotel is conveniently near trains. This place is great for visiting Chicago. You really can't beat the price!
I would've given a higher rating had I received help with my bags and didn't have the whole check-in fiasco.

name: Hotel Felix
title: “Soooo sooo small”
text: Got this hotel off of hotwire. It was the tinest room I've ever stayed in, no exaggeration. Also limited tv stations. Staff was friendly, everything was clean. However unless you are literally only going to be in your room for 5 minutes, I wouldn't stay here. It just wasn't comfortable and offered nothing special to make up for it.

name: Congress Plaza Hotel
title: “You are only paying for location.......nothing else.”
text:
I traveled with three other girlfriends for a fun weekend in Chicago. The location of this hotel can't be beat, you are on Michigan Avenue and directly across the street from Grant Park, Millenium Park, and Buckingham Fountain. 
Now, to get to any of the fun, young parts of town we either had to walk more than a mile (which was fine) or take a cab. So, I would not recommend this to anyone who can't walk a ways or afford to take a cab.
The lobby is lovely and I checked in in mere minutes. Then I headed to my room......yikes.
First of all my room was miles away from the lobby. I had to take an elevator and then travel through 3 different long hallways. The hallways are shabby and smell. The doors to get through these hallways are beaten up and scary looking.
The room was adequate to accomodate the four of us but it was a dump. It needs a major update. There were two flat screen tvs but one of them didn't work. Someone did come and fix it luckily. The bathroom door only had a door knob on one side, I have no idea what happened to the other half. We didn't have hot water unless you ran the water for about 10 minutes and the first time I ran the shower rust came out.
I wouldn't ever stay here again unless it was dirt cheap. We payed $209 a night for a two bedroom room.
What a dump!

name: Swissotel Chicago
title: “Good hotel, reasonable price, not spectacular”
text: Second stay at the Swissotel. This time I roomed with a colleague so couldn't upgrade to a corner room because it only has a King bed (well worth the upgrade if a king bed works for you). The hotel lobby is a little small and not much going on (the Hyatt next door has "The Big Bar" which is really lively). The Swissotel does have The Palms restaurant located right off of the Lobby which is a fantastic restaurant although it is expensive. Location of Swissotel is not bad but a bit of a walk into the center of town, especially when it's cold. I slightly prefer the Hyatt next door as I prefer a "lively" hotel but would have no problem staying at the Swissotel again in the future.

name: The Whitehall Hotel
title: “Great location, great staff”
text: Arrived at about 11.00 to be told check in time 3.00pm but to return we did within the hour and we had a room. Staff really great, hotel very clean, room very nice, and right near all the shopping. The business centre was very expensive to send emails.

name: Swissotel Chicago
title: “Feather Bed...Nice!”
text: We'd never slept on a feather bed before. Okay, it was a feather mattress cover, but still, it was really nice. We both got a great night's sleep and awoke refreshed for a new day in downtown Chicago. The room was clean and free of bedbugs (we checked.) The shower was great, but we didn't use the separate bathtub. The staff was exceptionally nice, helpful and accomodating.

name: Swissotel Chicago
title: “Chicago Weekend Getaway”
text: Wonderful hotel with a great view! Each summer we stay downtown for a Chicago weekend getaway. This year we stayed at the Swissotel for the first time. The hotel was very nice, with an excellent view of the Navy Pier fireworks on Saturday night. The only caution is the price of meals purchased at the hotel. But since there are so many other great eating options in Chicago, it's no problem. Enjoy!

name: Chicago's Essex Inn
title: “You get what you pay for! Close to Grant Park”
text:
This hotel is old, out-dated and dirty. Our room was clean, however the wall paper was peeling off of the ceiling! There was no light bulbs in the lamps, the carpets had lots of stains! The decor was outdated! The location of the hotel is great! It is close by the free Trolleys, and the staff was helpful! The food in the restaurant was over-priced and nasty! I will never eat there again! My husband, my daughter, and I enjoyed the fact of getting our room earlier than we expected, but maybe if we waited, we could've got a better room! I doubt it! 
If you want to stay close by the festivals this hotel (South Michigan) would be the place, and if you do not care about the atmosphere, then Essex Inn is the place for you! It is also central location for the Loop, and around lots of Mcdonalds, starbucks, garrett's popcorn, and subway restaurants.

name: Allerton Hotel
title: “Could have been so much better”
text: The location was perfect! Staff were pleasant but not really friendly. Room was clean and generally comfortable but wierdly laid out, with the TV to the right of the bed rather than at the foot of the bed. We were in rm 414, which was cave-like. Our window looked out at another building, just a few feet away, so we never knew what the weather was like until we exited the hotel. They charge $9/day for wireless in the rooms. It was free if you take your computer to the lobby. I don't like this policy of nickel and diming people after they pay a high price. In our room, there was absolutely no place to hang clothing, not even a hanger on a rod, not even a hook on the back of a door. The toilet was too close to the shower door, so that if you want toi sit, there's no place for the knees unless you slide open the shower door. The TV remote didn't work-- probably needed new batteries. We stayed 2 nights, but didn't find out there was free coffee in the upstairs lobby until the second morning. They didn't mention it when we checked in.

name: Hotel Felix
title: “Great if your a midget”
text: First it took us thirty minutes to check in and we were the only ones there. When we got to our rooms they were the size of other hotels closets with no amenities. Stay somewhere else!

name: The Westin Michigan Avenue Chicago
title: “We had wonderful accomodations: peaceful, serene, close to great shopping and nightlife.”
text: I would highly recommend staying at the Westin on Michigan Avenue. It was so very enjoyable. We were so close to many great eating establishments and around the corner to great shopping. The staff was very accomodating. Each request was met with prompt and friendly service. The room was spacious and the bed was like sleeping on a cloud. We loved the selection of soaps, shampoo, conditioner and body wash. These items made each shower a great experience.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown Lakefront
title: “Great Location; OK Place”
text: Rooms are very average. I had a suite with two doubles and a sofabed in the other room. Everything was just adequate. All the living rooms face the inside building, and are impossibly bright to sleep in. The bedroom drapes didn't close very well, so they were bright, too. The service was very good. People who worked there were super nice. Valet parking was ridiculously expensive - $39 a night with unlilmited in's and out's. The buffet breakfast that comes with the room is decent and has a lot of choices, including an omelet bar. Great for families. The biggest reason to stay at this hotel, however, and it can't be minimized, is the location. Not on Michigan avenue, so it isn't super noisy, but just a short walk away. There is a cinema in the building which makes late night movie going easy and accessible, even in the winter. One of my favorite places in Chicago, Fox and Obel, is a block away. This gem is a Dean and Deluca quality upscale grocery store, which you can't find outside NYC. It has a great informal cafeteria serving Chicago's famous Intelligentsia Coffee. I love this place to death. You're also within walking distance of Coco Pazzo, one of the best Italian restaurants in town. Fronterra Grill, Rick Bayless' famous upscale Mexican Restaurant, is a short cab drive away. I got a good deal via my credit card - about $215/night, and had four people in the room. Again, not luxurious by any means, but serves its purpose. One other irritating feature is the fact that you have to take two separate elevators, not adjacent to each other, to get to the ground level.

name: The Westin Michigan Avenue Chicago
title: “Stay @ Westin Michigan Avenue”
text: I stayed in this hotel for 2 days for a business trip. The location is absolutely great. Didn't have a good start with the room but upon a complain to the front desk, the hotel's room director (Nurpur) went above and beyond to cater for my needs. She was very proactive in reaching out via emails and phones to make sure that they can get an unhappy customer to be a happy one. Overall, I would love to go back to the place if they change their carpets. Some how the one in my room wasn't very clean but I definitely liked their service; may be primarily because of this director who emphathized to my needs.

name: Residence Inn Chicago Downtown
title: “Outstanding location”
text: Perfect location for walking to the river front attractions. Modern Marriott, upscale, comfortable, helpful staff.

name: The Westin Michigan Avenue Chicago
title: “Nice Hotel but not quiet”
text: The Westin Michigan Avenue hotel is a clean hotel with good service and a great location in Chicago. The only negative is that you can hear other guests walking and talking in their rooms. I think part of the problem is the hallway in the room is tile and you can hear other guests who are wearing high heels and perhaps the wall are very thin.

name: Allerton Hotel
title: “My kind of town!”
text: We stayed three nights at the Allerton this past week and were really happy with our choice of hotels. We were celebrating our anniversary and it was our first trip to Chicago so it would have been disapointing, to say the least ,if the hotel had not been up to par. We stayed in a suite which I booked two months in advance so I got a really good rate through the hotel website (early booking and 3 night stay equalled a nice discount). Housekeeping was great and not the least bit intrusive. We were just going to trade out towels and skip the cleaning on the first day because we were in the room until after noon (very late first night) but the sweet lady insisted that we should have our bathroom cleaned and straightened and our bed freshly made. The most stealth housekeeping I have ever encountered by the way.We did hear plenty of sirens outside (hotel is by the hospital) but you are downtown in a big city duh. it was not a problem and we slept fine. Doorman very helpful and always had a smile. There was a small mistake on our bill but it was quckly rectified with no problem. Oh and when we checked in early it was absolutely hassel free, and they stored our bags for us when we left as our flight out was not until 6;30 pm. Made it easy to spend some more time on the town before we left for home.

name: Congress Plaza Hotel
title: “Congres Hotel Chicago; een aanrader”
text: Het congres Hotel in Chicago ligt aan Michigan Avenue; het shopgedeelte van de stad. Ook ligt het aan de rand van het Millenium Park, dus voor veel wat wils. Service is goed en vriendelijk. Het bed (voor mij) was te zacht en hobbelig, maar dat was het enige nadeel. Gezellige koffie bar 1 blok verder op Michigan.

name: The London NYC
title: “Wonderful ambiance, a truly unforgetable experience”
text:
My sister and dined at in the formal dining room at the London. The food was amazing, quite expensive but no regrets.
A special "thank you" to our waiter for touring us through the kitchen and meeting with the chefs. This was something totally unexpected and very much appreciated.
Signed, the two blonde Canadian sisters

name: The Tremont Chicago Hotel at Magnificent Mile
title: “Maravilloso e inolvidable Tremont Hotel”
text:
Elegimos este hotel para nuestra visita a Chicago en nuestra luna de miel. Y todo fue genial. La ubicación es perfecta. El hotel está muy bien, pero si hay algo realmente valioso en este hotel es Daniel, un recepcionista amable, servicial que hace que tu estancia sea inolvidable. Al decirle que estábamos de luna de miel nos dio una gran habitación con vistas a Hancock Tower y tres desayunos gratis en el restaurante del hotel. Siempre estuvo ahí para nosotros ayudándonos para que nuestra estancia fuera completa al 100%. Si van a Tremont, no duden en preguntar por él, no les defraudará. 
El hotel es totalmente recomendable por su ubicación, limpieza, comodidad de sus camas y por el trato que recibes. Un 10 sobre 10.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Great location and service in theatre district”
text: Rooms are great. Service outstanding (particularly the bfast and wine & cheese). Great value!

name: The London NYC
title: “Are you striving for Mediocrity?”
text:
Absolutely beautiful Hotel! Ordered Breakfast in the room and it was wonderful! Breakfast cost $120, but hey, that's the way it is in a top notch hotel in NYC, right. So then we come back to the suite after shopping and the room is cleaned very nicely, except, our breakfast dishes, coffe cups, etc. are still right there on the table where we left them. I called the front desk and they suggested i put all the dishes, etc. in the hallway. i said Ok at first and then called back and asked if maybe they could send someone to get them. She thought that was a good idea and did just that.
That evening the concierge suggested a restaurant on a barge in the East River. I called a car service that a friend had recommended to take us to dinner. The car service said that they had a contract with the hotel so i must go through the hotel. So i did. It cost $108 for the 15 minute ride to the Restaurant. That's fine, except when we got to this restaurant, there was literally trash blowing against the front door and the place was deserted. I called our car back 5 minutes after he left us and was told by the driver that i would have to call the hotel and pay them again if i wanted him to come get us and take us somewhere else. I got a cab instead who took us to a great place in Little Italy.
I related these problems to the Concierge on duty when we returned. He said that he "was sorry we had a bad experience" and that he would "take care of it". When checking out the young lady asked how was our stay and i said not too good. I then explained it to her and she said that she "was sorry that i had a bad experience". 
If we had paid $99 a night, it wouldn't be a big deal, but at their prices they should do a better job of the small things. They certainly should have some procedures in place for a guest that is less than happy.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Chicago Downtown
title: “loved the pool”
text: This hotel made my stay in Chicago just wonderful. The pool indoors with the adjacent deck with lounge chairs outside overlooking the city was the best part. The room was comfortable and very clean. My only complaint was that the front desk attendent was not friendly.

name: Hilton Times Square
title: “Can't wait to return”
text: Hilton Times Square staff are wonderful, we just returned from a 7 day stay, very helpful, friendly and at all times professional. The rooms could use some work but they are large and clean, the location is the best. Hardly had to wait for the elevator’s, and the service in the restaurant was way above what we received anywhere else. The price of 5.00 for a cup of coffee was terrible, but the service made up for it. Service just about everywhere else was terrible, as we where in a party of six the restaurants put on a surcharge of 15%-20%, had the service been okay we would have not had a problem. The people of New York are charming, had heard they where unfriendly and rude, totally the opposite. What did amaze us is the police are everywhere, we felt very safe walking at night and down Canal Street. Can’t wait to go again and would stay at the Hilton Times Square again. Next trip we will buy all of our theater and sporting tickets in advance as it is hard to impossible to get the best seats for the popular shows when you are there. The concierge was a real asset, they made our dinner reservations, had maps and gave a lot of great advise about what we should do, and what not to miss and mostly they where right on.

name: The Westin Michigan Avenue Chicago
title: “Great location, Westin quality”
text: Stayed here in September for a conference and to attend a Bears game. Very nice corner room with minimal problems. The only downgrade is the food service is not as good as one might expect from a Westin. However, the beautiful view, bed and other furnishings more than make up for that. Great location across the street from the Hancock Tower.

name: The Whitehall Hotel
title: “Gracious, outstanding service”
