text: The Whitehall Hotel has excellent service. OUTSTANDING CONCIERGE. The physical facility shows a bit of wear, but overall, staying at the Whitehall was an excellent experience.

name: Hotel Felix
title: “Horrible service”
text:
I made a reservation at the Hotel Felix through Priceline and I'm not even going to stay at the hotel because the service, prior to my arrival, has been so terrible. Like others, I need a room with two beds. When I called the first time with my request for a room with two beds I was told that my request would be put in the system. I called again to arrange an early check-in, which costs $40 but I thought would be worth the money considering how early my flight arrives in Chicago. I was told that they couldn't guarentee an early check-in but, if I was able to get an early check-in, there was no way for them to know when I would be able to check-in. Thus, I could end up paying $40 for a 7am check-in or a 2pm check-in (regular check-in is at 3pm.) I decided to go without the early check-in but didn't want to get off the phone before I had confirmed that my room has two beds. When I asked they they told me there were no rooms with two beds available. I hung up the phone and got online to see if the hotel's website showed availability for a room with two beds. It did. I then called the hotel again, under the guise of booking a new reservation, to see if there were any rooms available with two beds. A room with two beds was available and they said they'd be happy to make a reservation for me. I then asked if I could just make sure my current reservation could be changed to a room with two beds, since there was availability, and they told me that was not possible. I volunteered to pay an extra fee per night for a room with two beds and I was also told that was not possible.
It seemed pretty clear to me that if I was paying full price for the room they would have been happy to accomodate me but, since I booked my room through Priceline there was nothing they could do. I've used Priceline to book rooms all over the country and have never been treated like this. If they don't want people purchasing rooms through Priceline then they shouldn't sell rooms through Priceline. I'm so frustrated I've booked a room in a different hotel. I'm a fan of getting a deal but I'd rather be treated with respect. Of course, now I don't want to use Priceline to book a room in Chicago again because I might end up with Hotel Felix. I'd rather pay full price anywhere else than step one foot in their lobby.

name: Allerton Hotel
title: “Outstanding!!!! 5 Stars!”
text: We attended the ASTD Conference this week and stayed at the Allerton. Our experience was outstanding from the moment we checked. The hotel is centrally located to everything. The front staff is great with warm greetings. The rooms are adorable! They are not the biggest but who stays in the room all day! Even the bar was wonderful! Next trip to Chicago- the Allerton will be the hotel I stay in. Thanks for a great trip!

name: The Whitehall Hotel
title: “Great Spot In Chicago”
text: With a first time visit to Chicago, I was very impressed. After reading the previous reviews I admit I was a little nervous. We felt the hotel was very nice. The staff was friendly and most helpful. The rooms were clean and well maintained. The air conditioner was a bit noisy however it was not something that would stop us from staying at the hotel on our next visit. Thank you for a delightful weekend.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “The best Hilton Hotel in Mid Town”
text: For business travelers looking for the comforts of home in mid-town, this hotel is the best. Its always very clean, roomy and the hotel staff is friendly. The restaurant is excellent for the breakfast buffet which awaits after a warm and friendly greeting from the most gracious hostess Hannah McCauley.

name: Swissotel Chicago
title: “Very Enjoyable”
text:
My husband & I stayed here for Valentines day. He was sweet enough to book the Romance in the City package. Beware if you book this. To start, he booked the package well in advance, and a couple of days before Valentines they raised the price. We checked in and got to our room, my husband noticed the champagne and chocolate covered strawberries were not in the room. So he called to the front desk and said we did not get the package because did not pay their new rate. My husband was smart enough to have a print out of what he paid for, stating it was the Romance in the City package. So the front desk apologized and said they would honor it. We did get the champagne and strawberries. We called at night to find out how to get the breakfast offer. The person at the front desk said for room service to fill out the menu or go to the Palm restaurant and they would bill it to our room. Well I called back to the frontdesk because we did not have a menu and no one answered, I called 3 times, and I know it was not busy because it was almost 3 in the morning. So my husband called back around 7:30 and they said we needed a voucher and mentioned nothing of room service, we did get the voucher and enjoyed a very good breakfast buffet in their 2nd restaurant, not the Palm like we were told
When we were checking out we asked why we got charged for the pool when it states the package comes with it and it says in their books in the room that its free. The frontdesk agent said the policy changed as of January 2009. And the did not even offer to refund us. 
It was a beautiful room on the 25th floor and overall it was a very enjoyable and romantic weekend, the pool and fitness center was great and the views are amazing!! But if you book a package, beware!! They will rip you off!!!!!

name: Swissotel Chicago
title: “Great room, great location, great views!”
text: Spent the night for Valentine's day....loved the hotel, great room on 34th floor with an outstanding city/lake view. Lots of places to eat within walking distance. Small complaint--my husband didn't think the concierge was very friendly....although he did provide him with the information that he requested. We walked out the door at 6:30 p.m. and enjoyed the great firework display that Chicago is doing on Saturdays in February. Would love to go back when it is warmer.

name: Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile
title: “crowded but the rooms are spectacular.”
text: I have stayed here many times on business over the years and I must say the cleanliness of the rooms and quality is what makes me love this place the most. It is in a very crowded, busy and touristy location which can be a little maddening but I must say it was a very enjoyable experience. On of the concierges Jon was very helpful with suggesting things to do in the area. There a lot of great restaurants in the area and the convenience to everything around the city is really what makes it a quality place to stay.

name: Hotel Felix
title: “good value if you want location”
text: We found this hotel via hotwire - aka we took a gamble - and it was great. The room we had was very small (as in tiny), but very clean and nice. Nothing to fancy but you felt very comfortable there. Our greatest need on our 3 night stay was location. And this was located pretty close to the Mile which is what we wanted. I would not have paid their normal prices online as that would have been too much, but if you find a cheap deal then go for it.

name: Allerton Hotel
title: “Nice location...not so nice service”
text:
It's hard to beat the location of this hotel. It's right on MI ave. We got a great rate for the season and a cheap upgrade to a suite.
However, the service was pretty crappy. I don't think anyone smiled at us once while we were there.

name: Hotel Felix
title: “Great Location, friendly staff, small rooms, strong aircon.”
text:
As others on this site have already mentioned, the rooms in this hotel are quite small. Storage space is very much at a premium with the wardrobe just a curtained-off rail on the wall. I think that a bit more imagination could have helped solve this.
However, the bathroom was fine in our room, bed very comfy and we didn't mind trading some size give the very central location. 
Staff were very helpful and all their restuarant recommendations were great. We walked everywhere and found the hotel easy to get to.
The only other downside is the aircon, which is very strong and loud which meant that we sometimes had to turn it off. The fan speed said low, but it felt like there was an engine running in the room.
Other than that a good stay.

name: Crowne Plaza Chicago - The Metro
title: “Crown Plaza Metro”
text:
We had a wonderful time! With only one exception, all the staff was very friendly. Bellhop was especially helpful. And if you eat at Dine, their restaurant, look for Mandy the server. Very friendly. Rooms were very nice and spacious and clean. Housekeeping was very friendly (and funny) - had great conversations with them in the morning. 
Try the crusted french toast for breakfast - delicious! Wouldn't recommend the breakfast buffet however - pretty pricey for food that was pretty standard and not always hot. 
Hotel is very nicely located - cab trips to several sites(river tour, Adler, Shedd) were all between $4 and $12. Halsted Street bus 8 (which runs the length of Halsted) was used for a trip to Wrigley at the cost of $2.25 (get your CTA pass at the Dominick's supermarket right next door). Nearest Metra station is 4 blocks east on Madison and Union Station is also within walking distance. Willis Tower is in walking distance also.
DIdn't use pool or exercise room - too much to do.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Hannah McCauley, Hostess at Ginger's Restaraunt is Awesome!”
text: Stayed at the Doubletree Time Square for the last month on business. Hannah McCauley greeted me every morning for breakfast, always remembered my name and took great care of me. As for the hotel, its great because its an all suite property with separate bedroom and living with a small fridge, microwave and mini bar. Although typically hectic and busy just outside on Time Square, the hotel is very quite. Its also very convenient to midtown and all subway lines.

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “Great Location and a Well Run Operation”
text:
This place was great. It is very well located - a 5 minute walk from Broadway, 5 minutes from where the Grayline Hop on Hop off tours start and only 2 minutes from a subway station that opens up the rest of Manhattan. The staff are very pleasant and helpful and there are plenty of them around so it is easy to get assistance when needed. The amenities are also good eg breakfast is included in the room charge and has a good range including hot dishes, there is a free internet kiosk and the Concierges know their stuff. The rooms were comfortable and clean, and everything worked.
The place is set up and run to make your stay pleasant – I don’t think it could have been any better.

name: Hotel Felix
title: “Do Not Stay Here! This Is No 4 Star Hotel!!!”
text:
YOU'VE NEVER SEEN SUCH SMALL ROOMS. When I say this is a TINY room, take it SERIOUSLY. I had to sit on the bed for my boyfriend to walk into the bathroom. And I concur with a previous reviewer, they treat Hotwire customers like garbage. The entire staff is trained to parrot the line, "We are a boutique hotel" - well I have traveled all over the world and stayed in hundreds of boutique hotels here and abroad and I'm telling you that the rooms are UNBEARABLY small - not to mention WITHOUT ANY DISCERNIBLE AMENITIES. A tiny ledge is mounted to the wall called a "desk" with a small chair. The "closet" was a 2 foot cut out in the wall with a curtain hanging in front of it. The bathroom consisted of a a tiny sink (NO COUNTER SPACE), a toilet, and a small standup shower. Believe me folks, an RV has more room than this. 
Also, they knew we were Hotwire customers and treated us as such. Our room looked out into an alley. They wouldn't even let us pay more money and upgrade. There must be some mistake because this IS NO 4 STAR HOTEL. It's barely a 2.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Hidden gem just steps from Times Square”
text: My wife, daughter and I just spent a long weekend at the Casablanca. I had read the reviews on TripAdvisor, so my expectations were pretty high. We were not disappointed! The hotel had a European feel, but our suite was very comfortable. Also, I was amazed that we heard no street noise even though we were just steps from Times Square. The complimentary breakfast was great with fresh fruits and yogurt for the more health-conscious and some outstanding pastries for me! We also enjoyed the wine and cheese in the evening. All in all, I would highly recommend this hotel and will likely return for my next trip where I want to have easy access to Times Square and the subway.

name: The London NYC
title: “Good new hotel with slight issues”
text:
I stayed for a week at the London NYC and liked the location, the rooms were brand new and very large and nice for NYC. I stayed in both the lower floor and higher floor rooms. Although the high floor room/suite had a good view of the city, bridges and a bit of the park I prefered the lower floor room. It was more cozy and had a better feel. I wish I had stayed there the whole time. The rooms were clean and nice and very easy to live in. The beds were good and the linens were fine. The bathrooms were good also. The safe needed new batteries which took two phone calls,
the electrical outlets in both bathrooms did not work. The room service was AMAZING. The chef is fantastic, Gordon Ramsey, and everything we had was devine. I did have one major problem though. I stayed on the 54th floor and got on the elevator to leave for the evening with my son. We pressed the lobby button and started to descend. The lift then stopped suddenly, shot up and then began to fall. We free fell and heard bending, moaning and groaning metal hitting together and we thought we were going to die. My son looked at me and said "I love you Mom." I threw myself forward and hit the emergency stop button and the alarm. Security came over the loud speaker and said"I have you", were bringing you down. Not a good start to our evening. I was traumatized and broke down each time I had to get back on the elevators in the building. I was glad to leave. The management credited one night stay for our trouble.
My Father called the hotel to find out what happened and the concierge told him that I was upset because I was running late and the elevator stopped to often. He LIED. I was told it had been serviced and put into use that same day we fell. The management closed the elevator for inspection/repair. Let them work out the bugs before staying here. It will be a great value at that point.

name: Allerton Hotel
title: “Convenient Location but Tiny Rooms”
text:
I stayed at the Allerton largely because I was attending workshop being held in the hotel and they gave me a great rate, $199 per night vs. $300, and it is conveniently located to the Chicago main drag, Michigan Avenue. While the decor in the main lobby and restaurant area is snazzy and the staff generally nice and helpful, there are a couple of things that are hard to dismiss. 
First, the elevators are painfully slow. Additionally, the rooms are so tiny and the bed not very comfortable. I had little room for my toiletries in the bathroom, no where to put anything. Thank goodness it was only me in the room, there would be no room for my husband. It's also annoying that they don't provide a coffee maker in room like so many other hotels do today. Luckily, there's a great convenient eaterie just around the corner on Erie at St. Clair called the Corner Bakery Cafe. 
The redeeming feature is the shower, mine was great, and, again, the location is great.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Big room for NYC. Good value in a great location.”
text:
I stayed for business but there were lots of families, probably taking advantage of the extra space and queen-size, modern sofa sleeper (modular, without the old-style springs). My room was quiet even though it was directly across from the elevator because the separate bedroom door helps block any noise in the hallway. My room faced Times Square, and the room blocked the outside noise fairly well - keeping the fan on constantly helped generate extra white noise. 
The front desk recommended a great Greek diner (Evergreen) a few steps away that served good, basic food for breakfast and lunch at cheap prices (for NYC).

name: Hilton Chicago
title: “Very nice”
text: I recently stayed at this hotel to attend a conference and found it to be very pleasent. The lobby area is very historic, and is wonderfully decorated. Some of the areas of the hotel are very old and many of the rooms are small, but you can see that the hotel is in the process of remodeling. The internet service is expensive, but was probably the fastest service I have ever seen in a hotel of this size. The restaurant in the lobby has great food (try the lobster roll!) but is a bit pricey as well. My only complaint was the cloud of smoke created by all of the smokers gathered near the front entrance that I had to navigate through.

name: The London NYC
title: “hemels,”
text: Ik was te gast in het London NYC en het werd één van m'n beste hotel-ervaringen. Heel centraal gelegen, bezuiden Central Park. Ik had het geluk te vertoeven op een van de best gelegen suites, met gezicht op het park. Maar zelfs als dat niet iedereen is gegeven is het verblijf in de "London" een méér dan prettige ervaring met alle gewenste comfort en dienstverlening,... een absolute aanrader!!!

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “You can't get more in the middle of Times Square!”
text:
This was our second stay at this location and it was even better this time. The hotel is on Times Square (we could see the New Year's Ball from our room) next to TKTS. Even with all the Times Square noise, we didn't hear a thing. The heat/AC worked great. The beds were comfortable, but not enough pillows for our liking.
The front desk staff was very efficient, pleasant and helpful. The dining room was a little slow going, but I think that was because of the large groups trying to sit together that caused some commotion. The breakfast was very good with quite a variety.
Central to the subway, walking to all the theaters, and in the heart of Manhattan. Loved it.

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “Hotel staff so friendly”
text:
I stayed at this hotel with my mother for a week this January. We have been to NYC several times before, usually at this time of year and have stayed in different hotels each time, This was by far the best hotel we have stayed in for the price.
The location of the hotel is excellent - a block away from theatres, Broadway and the subway. Really easy to get about on the subway (we purchased unlimited rides for a week metro tickets for $25) and the hotel is situated close to two different subway lines.
The hotel is in midtown and within comfortable walking distance of many of the tourist sites - Rockefeller Center, St Patrick's, Saks (and other 5th Ave shops), Times Square, theatre district. It is only up the road from the main office of the sightseeing tours - really convenient for boat or bus tours of Manhattan.
The hotel itself is well presented and clean with really friendly and accomodating staff - both on reception or in the breakfast room. We requested a fridge and were not charged for it. The rooms are spacious (unlike the Hampton Inn on 31st St) and the beds are very comfortable. Wireless internet access adds to the convenience.The two computers by the breakfast room are also useful for looking up details about attractions, sightseeing or for collecting e-mails. You can print maps and info for free- handy!
Several people have complained about the busy breakfast - easy answer - go early! We breakfasted at about 7-7:15 each morning and the room was really quiet. Good range of breakfast goods on offer seeing it is free! Hot items, hot and cold cereals, buns, bagels, muffins, pastries, fresh fruit salad and pieces of fruit, yoghurts, choice of juices and hot beverages made a pleasant start to the day and if you are in a rush there are bagged breakfasts available at reception for you to grab and run.
Complimentary coffee, tea, hot chocolate, cookies and apples 24 hours.
The staff bent over backwards to accomodate our every need and always seemed cheerful and welcoming. The concierge is helpful for advice about sightseeing and can arrange tours and tickets for you.
Would recommend "The Jersey Boys" show- just round the corner from hotel.
We discovered a little Chinese restaurant - basic but friendly staff and delicious food- across the street called Lucky Sunday Garden. Had disappointing meal at Cosmic Diner on corner -food realy cold, staff unhelpful). 
Having done all the usual sights before we wanted to do something different this time and took the train to Philadelphia (from Penn Station. (1 hour and 18mins on train)Worth a visit.

name: Hilton Times Square
title: “Big Mistake”
text: Because of many higher rates from the review, we switched our reservation from Westin to this hotel. The bed was horrible. The bathroom was not perfectly clean. The doormen never greet whenever we were in/out. The breakfast was very expensive but the quality was not even standard. (The hostess and server were horrible.) Everything we found in this hotel was nothing more than average, except the concierge. This hotel was not worth for $259/night. I always use Hilton, Westin, or Hyatt, but this one was the worst I ever stayed. Watching the view of newly Westin Tower from our room, I felt we made the biggest mistake choosing the hotel from this site.

name: Hilton Chicago O'Hare Airport
title: “A great hotel at a fair price!”
text: We needed to stay overnight, waiting to see our daughter and family off to Finland. We chose to stay at the airport Hilton so we would be ready for check-in the next day. The rooms were clean and the service exceptional. The only problem was the cost of eating there. the hotel retsurant was high-priced, but we were treated to a great menu and food at the sports bar, and the price was a bit less than the restaurant. If you go, we suggest you eat at the sports bar.

name: Crowne Plaza Chicago Magnificent Mile
title: “Great location, beautiful ambience!”
text: Nice, contemporary decor, pleasant staff. Great convenient location. FYI- walls are thin and plumbing is loud. Pool on 40th floor was not heated when we went.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Awesome!!!”
text: My teenage daughter and I stayed at this wonderful hotel from Mother's Day to May 12th, 2010. It is an excellent place to stay. You are situated right in the middle of time square, you are greeted by friendly staff who are very welcoming, the cookies are excellent and a great pick-me-up after a flight. Our room was a corner suite so we had a magnificant view of the city from the 20th floor. The food from room-service was well presented and excellent quality. The treats that were available in the lobby for the guests as they go out and enjoy the city, shopping and sightseeing comes in handy when you are out and about. We had a great time at this hotel and I would stay here again. My only minor complaint is that the toilet roll holder should be whipped down as it looked like there was crusted dirt on the inside.

name: Hotel Cass, a Holiday Inn Express
title: “Small Room”
text: Chose this hotel because of the central location, and in that respect it didn't disappoint. However, the room was excessively small! We don't usually mind small rooms, but when there is absolutely no storage space for the bags of 2 trans-Atlantic travellers, that I find unacceptable; there was literally no space to store bags without climbing over them. Other than that, cleanliness was good although the decor was showing signs of wear and tear in places. Breakfast was fine and wi-fi excellent. Contrary to other posts, the rooms in this hotel are not bigger than those in Europe; of note, we stayed in another 7 hotels during our road-trip, and every room was at least twice the size, and I'm not exaggerating! In sum, helpful staff, great location, clean but tiny room and a little expensive! Recommend it? Maybe, but travel light!

name: Crowne Plaza Chicago - The Metro
title: “We loved it!”
text: Everyone was so nice and helpful. Beautiful rooms, very clean and such a nice place to be.

name: Hilton Times Square
title: “Situation idéale”
text:
7 jours dans cet hotel, situé à deux pas du cityHall, deux blocs de Time Square et de Broadway. Grace au supplément demandé pour des étages supérieurs : vue imprenable sur Time Square !!!
Service de réservation pour spectacles à Broadway : permet d'obtenir des places idéalement situées. Bar très agréable. De manière générale, service impeccable.

name: Allerton Hotel
title: “unbelievably incompetent service which gets angry if you complain”
text:
I stayed there for three nights in September (Friday to Monday). The customer service experience was scary: a bunch of personnel conspiring against me to cover up a mistake and escalating the matter instead of simply apologizing. You have to remember even at a relatively upscale hotel like this, you are dealing against a group of individuals who know each other and will keep working together after you leave. They can collectively act against you by covering up and even lying for each other. Especially, you have to watch out for the team at this hotel.
They made a mistake in my reservation so they told me that I have to come to registration and check out after the second day and check back in with an accompanying key change at 7 am on Sunday (because I had back-to-back meetings all day). Don't underestimate this as the Crown Inn Customer Service, hotel manager, front desk manager, receptionist, and the security did. All these people, in mixed order, told me that this should not be a problem for me and I have to shut up and not complain. 
First, it took a long time to explain to the morning receptionist my problem as the previous receptionist had explained to me the day before. Then, she apologized to the people behind me in the checkout line but not to me and insisted that this is not a problem. So I remarked that she should first apologize to me and complained about waiting for fifteen minutes already due to an uncalled for check-out check-in at 7 am on Sunday while I am trying to catch a meeting. When she gave up because she could not overcome the complexities of their reservation system, she called for her manager. The front desk manager arrived to solve the problem. He said that this is not a problem. When I told him he should apologize for their mistake, he accused me of throwing a pen at him -which I had put on the desk after signing my new papers – and he called for security. The security came and told me to shut up or he would call the police. Of course, I was late to my meeting. Afterwards, when we come back to our room at about midnight, it was not properly made. 
When I contacted the Crown Inn Corporate after the stay, they apologized briefly (better than the fellows at the hotel who did not apologize until I asked) but implied that they were OK to be rude because I raised my voice at their incompetence. They also said that the room was not properly made because of an oversight and not retaliation and asked whether I contacted the room service at that time.
On the positive, Allerton is right on Michigan Avenue and in the middle of the Magnificent Mile. The rooms are small but nice very clean fairly good sound isolation for the age of the building. The elevators waits can be very long, though. However, the area is bustling with lots of nice hotels. I think it is too risky to deal with a hotel that threatens to call the police because you complained about their mistake.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “It Fits the Bill for Staying at the Center of the Universe, Times Square”
text: Recently stayed here with my wife and 4 kids. The Double tree can't get much better location then where it is in Times Square. You exit the doof and you are IMMEDIATELY in the thick of the Times Square traffic. If this is what you are after, you have found the right place. If you are not seeking some of the busiest sidewalks and shopping that you have ever seen, look elsewhere. As far as the hotel: It was nice but it was lacking somewhat, mostly due to its layout. It is a smallish building that goes up 40 some floors. There is a check-in floor that has a small bar and thats is about it. There are several small meeting rooms, a small workout bar, and a restaurant that was mostly empty on the next few floors. So nothing really to hang out at out of your room if you feel the need to get out. Which brings us to the rooms. The room is a smalling size with a seperate bedroom that share a bathroom. We had six in here and. although the room size accomodates this, it was very tight. But hey, this is New York, Right? The room was quiet with no street noise making it up to the 29th floor which we stayed. 2 flat screen TV's where there with great pictures. A small refrigerator and microwave also provided. Not a lot of drawer space. Overall adequate, but I wouldn't want to stay more then 2-3 days with a large family. No issues with having a family there, but there was little to see where they were overly family friendly. Parking is 35 to 45 depending if you need them to take the car to you. Since we parked it and took transportation, we didn't need it for the stay there. Just tell them that you will pick up your car and bring it around. It saved me $30 and took 5 minutes.

name: Crowne Plaza Chicago Magnificent Mile
title: “Good Value at an Expensive location”
text:
Check-in/out
Staff at front desk were efficient. 
Room/Facility/Lobby
For the price, they've done a decent job with the upkeep of this older property. Nothing that would WOW a traveler, but just a very comfortable stay. 
There's no in-room safe, which I believe they should really invest in adding to the rooms. Most travelers nowadays carry iPads, iPods, etc and we need a safe place to store our goodies. 
WIFI
Free WIFI service throughout the hotel and in the rooms. I love that they're not nickel and diming this service like other major hotels. 
Room: 1901
Best to avoid all the "XX01" rooms as they're all located next to the staff service entrance. Every morning at 8 am sharp, the service door next to my door would start to slam as the staff go about their day. A rude awakening for sure. 
Pool
A small roof top pool is available with a beautiful view of Lake Michigan.
Restaurants
I had breakfast at both the Sky Lounge and the British Pub down stairs. You go to the Sky Lounge for the breathtaking view of the lake (the buffet breakfast food was quite bad). May be better to go for a cup of tea or cocktail at night. The British Pub restaurant downstairs has great service and good quality food. 
TAXI/Train to AIRPORT
USD$8 for taxi to Clark/Lake Blue Line CTA station + $2.50 for CTA train to O'hare Airport.
USD$40 for taxi to O'hare Airport. 
Final Thought
Can't beat the value for Michigan avenue adjacent. Clean comfortable and affordable stay.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “User friendly hotel”
text:
It was amazing experience of NY by staying at Casablanca.
This is the absolutely user friendly hotel since major sightseeing location is truely no distance from here so no need to worry about walking around outside late and enjoying the real NY night. Also the sleep quality is well.
For that reason, I recommend this hotel for non-english speaker as well.(Easy to go out and back) 
Of course persons of the hotel are all friendly and kind to every guests.
They prepared the room wonderful and romantic for our honeymoon in advance.
Mainly guests are like to be matured family or couples so suits to the person who is looking for non "noisy-full of tourist, spoiling mood" hotels.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Surprisingly good...and in Manhattan no less!”
text: Wasn't expecting much, so it was a pleasant surprise. First our limo pulled into a space which blocked traffic. People honking. The hotel doorman protected us, screaming that it was a hotel unloading zone. Welcome to NYC. Pulled into the hotel, a huge line at the counter because of a convention. Doesn't sound good does it? Well being a top tier Hilton member has its perks...I'm ungraded and they give me a free dinner for my wife and I on the house...and in NYC that is worth what....about $100 or more? Long story short, room wasn't available yet, but we had things to do anyway. People were so un-NYC (they were actually friendly!), rooms were large and clean, and it was located steps from so many Broadway shows you could go bankrupt if you like shows like we do. Been to NYC many times, and you either pay up the wazoo for civilized service and a great room in a nice area.....or you go to the Doubletree Guest Suites. Yes, it isn't impressive to say to a business colleague that THAT is where you are staying....unless you are talking to a SMART business colleague....then they'll know what you're talking about.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Top Notch Hotel”
text:
If you are looking for a hotel that oozes charm and comfort then this is the hotel for you. The staff are the best we have ever encountered, they are helpful, informative, friendly and extremely professional ( I must say a particular thank you to Elizabeth for her help during our recent stay). We loved the cheese and wine in the evening before we went out on the town and also having coffee available 24/7 was a bonus.Outside the hotel Times Square is manic but there is such an oasis of calm inside the hotel it was a pleasure to return after a hectic day sightseeing. 
If we are fortunate enough to return to New York The Casablanca will be our #1 choice and we have already recommended the hotel to friends if they are ever in the big apple.

name: W Chicago Lakeshore
title: “W Hotel service is excellent”
text: I stayed at the W Hotel over the Thanksgiving weekend. The service was excellent. The staff was very knowledgeable about Chicago. The rooms were exquisite. The staff did everything to make my family's stay exceptional.

name: Hilton Times Square
title: “Da evitare. Non ai livelli di un Hilton.”
text:
Sono stato in quest'hotel all'inizio di settembre e non ci ritornerei.
La mattina il personale di servizio faceva un rumore tremendo urlando tra di loro da una stanza all'altra e sbattendo gli aspirapolvere nei muri. E visto che la porta d'ingresso era rialzata di 3 cm da terra (vedi foto) il tutto si sentiva abbondantemente dalla camera. Stiamo parlando di un Hilton a NYC !!!!
Inoltre la camera mancava di manutenzione, c'erano segni di usura ovunque (vedi foto).
Internet estremamente costoso.
Uniche noto positive: location ottima, stanze ampie. Ma non ci ritornerò più!

name: Allerton Hotel
title: “Good for Business Travel”
text: My wife stayed with me here while I was on business. There was much to like-- the location is excellent, the concierge was extremely helpful and the room was quiet. I asked for a room that was quiet and had a good view -- I got one of the two. My room was quiet, but looked out on a fire escape. When my wife and I were looking for a quick, casual, but nice dinner (a difficult combination) the concierge sent us to just the right place and got us to the head of the long line. For the business traveller the services were OK. Free high-speed internet (faster than my cable modem) was a plus. Only negatives were the broken sink faucet and toilet that never quite flushed right. If you're going to be busy in Chicago anyway, this is a decent combination of good price and location.

name: Crowne Plaza Chicago - The Metro
title: “Appreciated most by a tourist”
text:
I visited Chicago for the first time this July 4th weekend. It was SOOOO hard trying to decide which hotel location was the best. I was most interested in location rather than price or hotel chain. The Crowne Plaza Metro is wonderfully located for a tourist who wants an all-around experience without leaving the downtown area. It is located on the main "Greektown" street which primarily is several blocks of Greek restaurants (sit-down dining and fast food) and residences. On one side of the hotel is a Walgreens and the other side is Dominick's grocery store (subsidiary of Safeway). Sears Tower is about four short blocks away from the hotel in which you cross the Interstate and Chicago River.
The hotel parking was $35/night but I parked across the street (west) and paid $20/night. At first, I thought "Why did I rent a car when I could just take public transportation?" but then there were a few times I'm glad I had the car to zip around the outskirts. Truly, though, there is no need for a car. The train is very inexpensive from O'Hare to downtown and the bus (Route 20) stops at the entrance of Dominick's and goes all the way to Millennium Park (the huge park next to the lake).
One or two blocks south of the hotel Route 124 (or 126?) can also take you to generally the same block over by the park. I made the mistake of driving my car to the Sears Tower and parking in their parking facility. I was slapped with a $31 charge just to park for about 2 hours. Parking everywhere downtown (except for sparsely-available meters) was VERY expensive. It was the only negative about my whole trip.
This hotel is clean and new and modern looking even though it's a renovated old structure. It's right next to the Interstate but well insulated so you can't hear noise. Also, there really isn't a perfectly-located room because you're going to see the John Hancock building on one side of the hotel and Sears Tower on the other no matter which room you choose. Every room has a balcony.
It's best to go to the Sears Tower Observatory in the late afternoon because of where the sun shines on the buildings, and go in the morning to the John Hancock Observatory because of the same reason. Both observatories give you a different view and perspective. I was glad I took the "Skyline Cruise" from Navy Pier because the distant, all-incompassing view of the skyline was really neat. For the river cruise, I simply paid the water taxi price and used that trip to bring my from the Navy Pier back to Union Station where I got off and walked two blocks to the hotel. The river cruise was $30 which was basically narrated, but the one-way water taxi was only $6 for the same route and distance.
Lastly, if I return I now know the Hotel Monaco, Hotel 71, or Holiday Inn or Westin right on the Chicago River would be the four I would choose based on price at the time. All four of those hotels seemed like THE BEST location for a second trip. But, the Crowne Plaza was the best for a first trip because I felt right outside of the skyscrapers but only steps away.

name: Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile
title: “NYE in Chicago”
text:
I had the pleasure of spending my 2011-2012 NYE in downtown Chicago and stayed at the Marriott hotel. I was very impressed with my room view and the quietness. I was on the 44th floor and pretty much next to the elevator, but had a partial lake view - really pretty. I love that there's floor to ceiling windows! The decorations seem a bit outdated compared to other Marriotts. I was definelty expecting to hear neighbors, especially being NYE, but it was so quiet when we got back to the room...didn't hear any noises from other rooms or the elevator!
The staff was friendly and proficient as it they were very busy that weekend.
The only sticker shock was parking $48/night...but that's just Chicago. 
Very convenient to shopping and not too far from Lake Shore drive.

name: Hilton Chicago O'Hare Airport
title: “Credit when it is due.”
text:
Have stayed at this hotel 4 or 5 times this month and it has been great 4 out of 5 times and on the one occasion I had an issue they took care of it. 
The check in staff is excellent. I love the media rooms and Andiamo has the best continental breakfast. 
Right next to the airport so convenient for early flights. 
Keep it up.

name: River Hotel
title: “Perfect location”
text:
Across the street/river from Trump Tower, close to Millenium Park, Magnificent Mile, Willis Tower, John Hancock Observatory and downtown shopping. We also walked to Shedd Aquarium and Navy Pier. The United Centre (hockey/basketball) was 6 miles so it was a short cab ride.
We had a suite since there was three of us and we needed the sofa bed.Great kitchenette with microwave and fridge.
Clean and comfortable, the staff was friendly and helpful. We'll definitely stay here next time we travel to Chicago.

name: Majestic Hotel
title: “Excellent Hotel, Great Location, Wonderful Staff”
text: I have stayed at the Majestic hotel many times and also rented their executive suite for business meetings. The hotel staff are extremely accommodating and very friendly. The rooms are very nice and the breakfast bar in the morning is wonderful! In addition, the location is perfect! would highly recommend the Majestic Hotel when staying in Chicago.

name: Hilton Times Square
title: “buon albergo, grandiosa posizione”
text: le stanze sono ampie (cosa rara a manhattan) e la posizione è veramente straordinaria. da rivedere la pulizia...

name: Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile
title: “Still our favorite place to stay on Michigan Avenue!”
text: We stay at the Marriott every year over Thanksgiving weekend, and keep coming back. It is perfectly located between Watertower and the Loop -- which makes it great for walking to the parade and Daley Plaza for the Christmas Village, as well shopping up and down Michigan Avenue. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The elevators are fast. The breakfast buffet is good with many cook-to-order specials. The lobby has LOTS of seating, and is a great place to hang out with the family when staying in a hotel for a long weekend. The only downside for us is the double rooms have 2 double beds -- not queens.

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “Great place to stay while in Times Square!”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights in August and LOVED every moment! The hotel is in a great location; close to the theatres, restaurants, double decker tour companies and Central Park. It is a beautiful hotel once you walk through the doors! Everything is clean and everyone is extremely friendly and helpful. We arrived early (9a.m.) and our room was not ready. So we were told to give our luggage to the bellhop and enjoy some breakfast in their breakfast area. As other reviewers have noted, it was crowded but everyone is tolerant of everyone else. The attendants were constantly replenishing whatever needed restocking and they were always very friendly. 
We got in our room and it was wonderful! We asked at the desk if we could have a room facing 8th Avenue. We were lucky that they had one available! It was another great suggestion from one of the reviews. The room was fabulous~ spacious, clean and what a view! I would stay here again without question! My husband ,my son and I thoroughly enjoyed ourselves! When I needed to check-in via internet for our return flight, the desk clerk let me use their office computer to check-in and print our boarding passes! What a wonderful accomodation and a wonderful staff! We couldn't have been happier with our stay!

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “CHECK-IN AT THIS HOTEL WAS A NIGHTMARE!”
text: We arrived for check-in on Sunday, December 06, 2009, at 2:10 P.M. The hotel had a mix-up on our reservations; pets allowed on one floor, smoking allowed on another floor. Also, I had paid extra for a Times Square view and the rooms they offered us didn't have this view. I asked for a manager. The female manager was very rude and finally told us the room had to be cleaned, although it was vacant. Check-in is at 3:00 P.M. We had to sit in the lobby all this time, me holding my dog for over an hour, with no where to sit most of the time because of the large crowd. The bell hop kept asking us what room number we had so he could take our bags up and I told him what was happening. I asked who the manager was. I talked to Y. Packin, Director of Guest Services, and he gave me the same story as the female. We had driven for fourteen hours and wanted a key to our room. It was after 3:00 by this time. Mr. Packin called and went to check on our room. Finally, around 3:30 we were given a key to our room. The ad states pets allowed, but when we arrived, the manager told us pets were only kept on 12th floor.

name: River Hotel
title: “Great location, immaculate & sleek rooms (but small) - AC lame at best”
text:
Would stay here again without a second thought if it weren't for the anemic air conditioning that kept room just bearable. Not what you want in the summer.
Restaurant in hotel is good for breakfast but best avoided for lunch and dinner for its lackluster menu with inconsistent quality. Pizza had flavorless frozen crust flavor and texture - and its an Italian restaurant in Chicago!
Loved the location - loved the modern room aesthetics - again the AC is the bummer.

name: River Hotel
title: “Absolute Nightmare! Avoid at all costs. AC broke but no one fixed it.”
text:
We had a few family members in Chicago for the weekend, so we booked a room at the River Hotel because of the location. It's close to Wacker Drive and the room was contemporary albeit on the small side.
Went out to meet a few people for dinner and we came back finding out that the AC was not working. We alerted the staff at the lobby and realized that the maintenance guy had left for the day. How can the hotel not have a maintenance person 24 hours a day? Needless to say, we were shocked to hear about it. We did not pay more than $150 and get a room that is as warm as an oven. 
When the staff learnt about our story, they unempathetically asked us to open the windows instead!!! Mind you, that does not make any sense considering the weather outside was about 90 F. They then offered to move us to another location away from the river but we refused because we chose the location for a reason and it is an unnecessary inconvenience to us at our expense. It was not our fault to begin with. After that they offered us a crappy fan which finally worked when we gave it a few knocks. It was a warm and miserable night for our family who came all the way to Chicago expecting something wonderful from this hotel.
The next morning, we mentioned about it at the front desk again and all they could do was apologized. Not a single time did they compensate us in a form of a lower rate for putting us through this. After all, we did not sign up for a room which has AC problems. After much complains, the staff finally offer us a free upgrade if we come back the next time. That is not acceptable. What is the use of a free upgrade if the AC is not going to work?? Well, we won't be coming back anyways. He can keep his offer. You shouldn't come here either.

name: Hilton Chicago
title: “Hilton Chicago is a great place to stay”
text:
This hotel is really close to the museums, Buddy Guy's Legends and the field where the White Sox play. It is an easy walk to many of the architecturally interesting buildings.
The Hilton is well maintained and feels very safe. Be sure to check out the ballroom during your stay: it really does look like Versailles, allowing you to imagine what Versailles looked like in its day.

name: Crowne Plaza Chicago Magnificent Mile
title: “Amazing - Wanting to buy a zebra chair ever since checking out”
text: Can't say enough about this place. The decor, the rooms, the staff - they were all incredible. No complaints, concerns, or regrets. Loved the hotel, and loved the zebra chair in the room!

name: River Hotel
title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: This hotel is located on Wacker at Michigan. Lots of restaurants, shopping, sightseeing and Millenium Park close by. The hotel seemed more like a business club -- small lobby, small spartan rooms, built for short stays. But with the rates as low as they are, it's a busy hotel. The entire hotel staff was very nice and helpful. Housekeeping needs improvement. The bathroom floor had not been swept when I checked in and the bedspread had a small stain on it. On the second day, when I returned at 4:00, the room had still not been cleaned so it appeared that cleaning is completed quickly but not meticulously. If you can look past minor issues and alert the hotel staff when there are problems, then it will be worth it to book here. It's not perfect but you can't beat the price and location.

name: Crowne Plaza Chicago Magnificent Mile
title: “overall good service”
text:
we stayed in this hotel for 2 nights oct 1st to 3rd, as we had booked through priceline we were expecting to get a small room near a noisy lift, however, I had rang ahead to ask for a non-smoking room and had mentioned that we were on a special trip--on arrival we were offered an upgrade to a corner suite with a partial view of the lake!!! GREAT. the bed was really comfortable, and we enjoyed our stay . This hotel is minutes away from michigan avenue--for the shops, also an easy walk(less than 10minutes) to the Wendella boat tours 
We ate in the elephant and castle which is attached to the hotel--basic food , price o.k. service good. was very busy the evening we were there.Had breakfast in the corner bakery which is just around the corner--lovely, We would definitely stay here again.

name: W Chicago Lakeshore
title: “nice hotel”
text: all W hotels are the very nice and i love their beds, bliss products and towels, the only thing is, with this location, the staff were not very helpful and wasn't very knowledgable of their job. I thought the W hotel downtown chicago was much nicer and the people who worked there are much more experienced. The location is great, it is by the water so when you look out you see a very nice view..

name: Wheeler Mansion
title: “Our Chicago Trip”
text:
This has been one of our most amazing trips and experiences ever. The Wheeler mansion is divine. The attention to detail in the hotel is beautiful. The outdoor garden area is lovely to relax and take in the atmosphere. The host was most welcoming and helpful during our stay, to recommend events or places to see, it really felt like a personalised service and experience. We decided to extend our stay and our room was made available at a fantastic rate. I will recommend this hotel to friends and family it’s truly an experience that Nat and I will remember for ever.
Keep up the good work kind regards
Nik&Nat from
Australia

name: Hilton Chicago O'Hare Airport
title: “Hilton ORD- Another Great Hilton Airport Hotel”
text:
I like the LAX Hilton...I LOVE the Narita Hilton....I am happy to report that the Chicago airport Hilton ranks right up there with these other two airport hotels.
 It is very well-run property with all the services including bars, restaurants, health club, etc. 
Yes, there are other cheaper alternatives in the area... but if you are coming off a long or late arriving flight, walking straight to the check in counter is a big relief! We were IN OUR ROOM within 20 minutes of getting our suitcases at baggage claim.
Also, you can offset the hotel expense if you are renting a car by staying at the Hilton the night of arrival and picking up the rental car the next morning, saving one-day's car rental fees and insurances. The rental car shuttles are adjacent to the hotel.. it's cinchy!
The staff is all-pro, the rooms are clean, and there is 24hr room service.
BTW: Internet is "free" now at all Hilton brands if you are Hilton Hhonors Gold or Diamond. They also give breakfast coupons to Gold & Diamond... otherwise breakfast is pretty steep and might cost you $30.

name: Courtyard Chicago Midway Airport
title: “Newly renovated but...”
text: Courteous customer service and shuttle driver. Newly renovated but, I think housekeeping could pay a little more attention to the cleaning of the tub. I was impressed with the renovations, good color schemes, fixtures and furniture. I stayed on the second floor and the hallway was a little smokey. Every time I've stayed here I smell smoke and it's supposed to be a no smoking hotel I thought. Anyway, my room itself was fine as far as there not being a smoke smell. My only complaint is the tub and the surround was new but not cleaned well which put a damper on my excitement of the newness. Oh yeah....the shuttle took longer than the 20 mins (about 30 actually) I was initially told to pick me up. That would NOT have gone over well had it been typical Chicago windy and/or cold weather.

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “Much Hampton Inn Love”
text:
After receiving tickets to see Wicked as an anniversary gift, I began doing research for a decent place to stay that was in a prime location. I wanted to be close to Gerswin Theater, and Hampton Inn is as close as you can get! The theater is across from the hotel and pretty much near everything! 
We were allowed to check in early, which was a pleasant surprise. Our room was on the 10 floor and gave a view of the back, but it wasn't awful. It was pretty cool to look out and see apartments and office buildings alike, especially at dusk.
The hotel was helpful at every turn. It was nice to go out and come back and have a message checking on on us and making sure we were satisfied with everything. All the staff was willing to answer any questions and suggest restaurants, etc if you asked. The only turn off was when we left our bags for day, the bellhop was quick to point out that he would not be around when we came back and that he would gladly take his tip at that moment. My husband and I are good tippers and would only not tip for rude service, I thought his statement was uncalled for, as we were going to tip then and when we came back to get our bags. But that was really the only thing I can think of that was "bad".
Again, the location of this hotel is superb, mere minutes from Times Square on the south and Central Park on the north. A train station is one block south and there are plenty of great bars and restaurants to venture in!
We have decided to make a yearly trip to NY and will book a room at this hotel each and every time.

name: Hilton Suites Chicago/Magnificent Mile
title: “Watch out for the sofa bed”
text:
When we arrived, the room layout we reserved (a king with sleeper sofa) was not available, so they put us in a double queen. The smell of smoke in the room was so strong that I called the desk and asked for a new room, and was immediately moved to a king with a sofa bed. 
The sofa bed was really the issue - when we opened it up the first night, the sheets were stained, and there were some kind of food crumbs in the sheets. We called housekeeping, and they came up and re-made the bed. The mattress on the sofa bead was so think, it felt like sleeping on canvas stretched over chicken wire. My daughter slept on it a couple of nights and didn't say anything about it until after the second night - I then laid on it and wondered how on earth she was able to sleep. I ended up calling the front desk to see if they could give us a new mattress - they brought up one of those mattress pads with the cushion on the top. it mad a marginal difference, but I ended up laying the couch cushions on the bed and sleeping on those, while my wife and daughter slept on the king together.
Aside from the sofa and check-in experience, all else was ok - nothing great, nothing terrible.

name: Wheeler Mansion
title: “Beautiful Mansion/Extraordinary Service”
text: We stayed at The Wheeler Mansion February 2012. Coming to Chicago for the first time, Stephanie was EXTREMELY helpful. She recommended restaurants and things to do, she even offered to make reservations for us. She was prompt at returning phone calls when we reserved our room. The mansion was amazing, beautifully restored, surprisingly quiet and very clean. Attention to detail was definitively important while restoring this 100+ year old gem, so much that they even applied UV protection film on the windows to keep the beautiful decor from fading (I'm in the window film business, that's how I know). Most definitively recommended!

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “absolute best, awesome friendly staff, very comfortable, very central”
text:
thanks to vinnie, elizabeth and all the staff for the best stay we have ever had away from home. Their dedication is second to none and they should be very proud of the Casablanca tradition.. great spot next to times square, but quite and very comfortable. Lovely complimentry breakfast (with bagels!) and afternoon drinks is fab. great places to eat recommended by Vinnie. (Saju Bistro)
To put it simply this place is fanstastic!

name: Hilton Chicago
title: “Very good hotel near museums and parks”
text: We stayed here in December to attend the Joffrey Ballet at the Auditorium Theater (just 2 blocks away) and visit the Art Institute (about 6 blocks away). This is a great location for the South Loop, and also reasonably close to the Loop north of the river. It's a very large, older hotel, but the rooms are in good shape and well furnished. Our room with two double beds also had two full bathrooms. Room service food was excellent, and the breakfast buffet was way beyond the normal -- well prepared eggs, french toast, etc, delicious pastries and an omelet bar. The room rate was reasonable for Chicago. We had an interior room, and it would be worth asking for a room with a view of the lake. Parking was expensive but convenient.

name: Courtyard Chicago Midway Airport
title: “Good value, average service”
text: Hotel is in a great location to the airport, with average rooms andq average service.

name: Fairmont Chicago Millennium Park
title: “Beautiful accomodations and staff makes every effort to serve you!”
text: We had a wonderful room with a view of the Lake. Staff was friendly and helpful. We used in-room dining and service was fast & friendly, food was delicious. The location is perfect for downtown activities! Less than $10 cab ride to Navy Pier. Cannot wait to stay there again!

name: Chicago South Loop Hotel
title: “I wouldn't pay full price, but not bad for deal I got...”
text:
I bid for a hotel through Priceline and got two rooms here for $85 each plus tax ($103) for a Saturday night stay in July. I called the hotel to see what size beds we would get, and the staff member was a bit difficult to deal with. First, she told me that I would have to arrange that with Priceline, but I told her that the fine print said to call the hotel directly to verify bed size. Then, she looked it up and told me each room had a queen-sized bed. However, she said she couldn't match the price I got on Priceline when I said that my husband and I wanted to spend an extra night, but that Priceline would make me book that extra night for both rooms. Oh well. I found another hotel on sale for that night! By contrast, the staff at the desk when we checked in/out were very nice.
Each of the rooms we got were very large and each had two Queen-sized beds, a window AC unit, a small refrigerator, a coffee maker, hairdryer, and a bathroom with a shower and deep bath tub. The decor was dated. Our room had ugly golden-yellow bedspreads, but my sister got white ones. The closet had double-sliding mirror doors. There was also a small desk with one chair and a small dresser with a flat-screen tv on it. They said they had free WiFi, but we didn't bring a computer. The hotel also had FREE parking in two lots. However, both lots were full when we returned later in the evening, so we had to park on the street. No one bothered our car, but the hotel is in a run-down area and we didn't really feel safe parking there or walking around either. 
Also, there aren't any restaurants nearby. However, the hotel did have a nice bar with a good beer and liquor selection, a restaurant, and a cafe. We had breakfast at the little cafe. For some reason the restaurant didn't have waffles or French toast, which is what my sister wanted, so we ordered at the cafe. They have one cook and a small cooking area, so it took awhile, but the lady at the counter was nice. There isn't much room to sit, so we took our omelets, hashbrowns, toast, etc. back to our room. They had a decent tea selection and my relatives liked the coffee, but I thought my omelet was rather runny. When we walked past the restaurant late in the evening, it looked like there was dancing inside, but it may have been a private event.
This hotel is close to U.S. Cellular, so we may consider staying there again; however, when we come to town for a White Sox game, we usually stay in a hotel near an El stop, so we don't have to drive there. This hotel isn't close to an El stop, so it isn't very convenient for playing tourist, but it does have free parking.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Service-Service-Service”
text:
Have stayed in many large hotels over the years in NYC, but decided to try the Casablanca after reading all the great reviews in Trip Advisor. Peter called my home the day before we left for NYC to ask if I still wanted an upgrade to a mini-suite as I had requested on my reservation. When we checked in, Peter was at the front desk, and introduced himself as the person who had called me. This is where the service started, and it never stopped. I am a retired businessman who spent over 40 years preaching the value of good service to my employees, and had I known about the Casablanca, I would have made this a required field trip for all of them. The most impressive element of their service is the portrayal that this is not a "job", it truly is each associate's passion to make every guest feel special. We looked forward to walking through the lobby because each encounter made us feel as though we were family friends. We especially loved the 2nd floor ambiance. If you are here for a Friday evening, you must enjoy the piano music during the 5-8pm cocktail hour. We struck up many enjoyable conversations with the other guests in the comfort of this beautiful room.
A small hotel is not for everyone, but if you have the opportunity, you must try the Casablanca; a small hotel with a huge heart!
And, here's a tip I have learned over many years of studying customer service: If you want good service give good service. I have found that even the toughest workers find it hard to be mean when you treat them like they are special people.

name: Fairmont Chicago Millennium Park
title: “Fine. Not great, not bad. Just fine.”
text:
Good -
Location, wine bar in the lobby, sushi restaurant, service at the front desk and the helpful concierge. 
Saturday night I decided to have a glass of wine and not only was the wine delicious, but so was the nice gentleman and lady who served me. She made up a gorgeous cheese/meat tray for me which perfectly paired with the glass of red. Wonderful.
Bad -
The whole place needs a serious overhaul. Everything looks worn out. The rooms, which would be decent if updated are nice size. I upgraded to a lake view (31st floor) for an extra $30 p/nt. Nice view. The carpets, bathroom tile, paint, decor, lamps, everything just needs to be gutted. 
Now, not get me wrong. It was clean and nice, i just think if you are staying at a Fairmont, the expectation is a little more than if I booked the Sheraton. It's loud. LIke most hotels you hear every person that walks by and every door that slams.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile
title: “not impressed!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text: Signed up for king bed. Got 2 queens asked for change. They could'nt do. Did'nt offer change other 2 nights. No chair other than office chair at desk! Good location but other than that don't do it!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

name: Hilton Suites Chicago/Magnificent Mile
title: “Not worth it”
text:
Downtown !! Great to walk around, views, etc., but pain to get to and everything is costly, breakfast, parking, etc.,
 Good service seemed spotty (depends on who you get)

name: Crowne Plaza Chicago Magnificent Mile
title: “A wonderful weekend getaway experience!”
text: We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Avenue Hotel Chicago. When we checked in we asked if we could be in a room that was fairly close to our friends that came with us. They immediately accommodated our request & upgraded us both to 2 suites on the 25th floor. Rooms were very elegant & obviously just recently redecorated. The bed was the most comfortable bed we've slept in with great bedding & great pillows!!! We walked a couple of blocks to the Water Tower Place & enjoyed great shopping there as well as in the vicinity. Had breakfast a couple of mornings at the little bakery/cafe just down the street which was very convenient & not too expensive. Only negative thing was the cost to park our vehicle for 3 nights - $48 per night! Ouch!!! Otherwise, a very enjoyable stay & would recommend to anyone travelling to Chicago.

name: Fairmont Chicago Millennium Park
title: “Amazing Hotel”
text:
Staying at the Fairmont from July 26-29th. I have zero complaints. Room's were updated, clean and bright. Amazing view of Lake Michigan from bed :)
Bathrooms were modern and kept clean.
We took the L from Midway to Randolph (4 blocks from the hotel) on the Orange line to save on Taxi money. 
Everything is walking distance from this hotel. Front desk always willing to suggest things to do and different food to try. Went to Gino's Pizza for that deep dish Chicago treat and went to Lucky's Sandwich near Wrigley. This hotel was the best -highly suggested!!

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “Zentral gelegenes, sauberes Tophotel.”
text: Das Hampton Inn liegt in Gehdistanz zum Times Square, dem Broadway, genauso wie zum Central Park und somit zu den wichtigsten Sehenswürdigkeiten in Manhattan. Die U-Bahnstation ist nur einen Block entfern und somit sehr bequem zu erreichen. Die Hotelzimmer sind für New Yorker Verhältnisse geradezu riesig und der Service wie auch das restliche Personal einfach nur top. Das Frühstücksbuffet ist eine Selbstbedienungstheke mit Oat-Meal und Bagles, dazu Brot, Früchte Joghurt, Waffeln und Muffins. In der Vorweihnachtszeit war ganz schön viel los, aber trotzdem gab es immer ein Plätzchen für das leckere Frühstück. Im ganzen Hotel gibt es W-Lan kostenlos und in der Lobby stehen drei PC's zur Verfügung. Der Bellman und die Receptionisten stehen einem mit Rat und Tat gerne zur Verfügung. Durch die absolut zentrale Lage und die doch sehr ruhigen Zimmer ist das Hotel für uns erste Wahl beim nächsten Besuch von New York!

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “Hampton Inn Times Square North - nära till allt”
text:
Trevligt, rent och nära till "allt"
Bode 2 vuxna och 2 barn så lite trångt men vi åkte inte till NY för att vara på rummet. Bra frukost om än lite mycket folk. Trevlig personal som hjälpte oss att boka aktiviteter utan extra kostnad. Åker vi tillbaks är det stor chans att vi tar samma hotell igen - det fungerade och vi fick vad vi betalde för =)

name: Hilton Suites Chicago/Magnificent Mile
title: “Great View and awesome service...minor issues...”
text: Stayed here on June 16,17 and 18. We arrived at about noon and booked on priceline. We found out the hotel did not have any available 1king bedroom suite so they gave us basically the same room... Our room was on the 22 floor! it was amazing! the views of JHO and Michgan Ave were awesome and the pool on the 30th floor was awesome! Only issue at the hotel is we did not have a phone book in our room and there were only a few channels...the location was great and thanks for keeping the homeless off the corner :) there were also no vending machines in the building and the starbucks closed at 9 :( at the end of the stay i found store right across from the hotel...overall great stay with minor issues i hope to stay there again in the future! keep up the good work! :):)

name: Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile
title: “OK”
text:
Arrived Thu 01 April for 3 nights.
Unfortunately this was Easter and every child in Chicago seemed to be staying here,with long queues for breakfast and the non availability of the pool to serious swimmers after 7 in the morning.
The breakfast situation was easy to control, just avoid around 0830-1000, but the pool was another issue.
One of the main reasons I stayed here was they had a pool. I like to swim every morning around 0730- 0830, but even this early the pool was full of playing kids and their parents, making it impossible to have a serious lap swim. 
While accepting fully the right of parents and kids to use the pool during their stay, why should everyone else be excluded?
Who would suffer if the pool was reserved for adult lap swimmers up to 0900 daily and the kids could have it all day after?
Staff were as usual in a Marriott very helpful and did all they could to accommodate us.
Breakfast was a good buffet, but not the best I have had in a Marriott, that belongs to the Marriott in Marina del Rey, CA.
Room was fine, bit small but nice bed and A/C worked.
Unlike a previous reviewer I hated the lobby.They allow free wi fi access here and it attracted loads of people who were not staying at the hotel, The noise level was unbelievable, even for American Teens.
Handy location, beside everything, you could want.
Tip. There is a huge supermarket called Dominicks just down Illinois street (to Navy Pier) it has a huge cold/hot food selection and a massive wine selection at very reasonable prices.
Would stay again but not over holiday periods.

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “UNA GROSSA BUFALA!”
text: Ho soggiornato in quest'albergo a Ferragosto: sicuramente è in un'ottima posizione, all'apparenza pulito, sicuramente la colazione è compresa. Peccato che la pulizia sia assolutamente superficiale (scatole vuote e mele ammuffite sotto il letto, piano del lavabo mai pulito in una settimana, campioncini vuoti abbandonati sulle mensole della vasca), la prima colazione, che peraltro si svolge in una sala assolutamente inadeguata per dimensioni al numero di ospiti, venga offerta con prodotti che definire scadenti è poco e che il personale sia di un'inefficienza e, a volte, di una maleducazione mai trovata prima. Inoltre, se la camera ha delle dimensioni accettabili per una famiglia di quattro persone, la cosa non può dirsi del bagno, decisamente piccolo e scomodo.Quindi, per ciò che mi riguarda, l'unica cosa postiva è la posizione. Comunque sia, mai più nella vita!

name: Club Quarters Chicago - Central Loop
title: “Good value”
text:
Highly recommended for the traveller who doesn't plan on staying in his/her room too long. Was in Chicago on vacation. Stayed at Central Loop for 4 nights.
Location: Ideal for tourism. About 3 blocks from Millenium Park and the Art Institute.
Also, if you're flying in to O'Hare, save a ton of money by hopping on the subway out there and ride it right into downtown. It's about a 40-minute trip and the subway stop is only a block from the hotel.
Accomodations: Very clean but smallish rooms. The staff is quite friendly but this is pretty basic stuff so you won't have the advantage of a concierge service. The hotel is relatively quiet for being so busy.
A huge advantage for the traveller staying for a while is they have a free laundry service and they even supply the soap!
There is a pub adjoining the main lobby which is handy for having a pint while deciding on travel plans with your companions. The food is passable.

name: Club Quarters Chicago - Central Loop
title: “Everything you need and nothing you don't need!”
text:
The Club Quarters Chicago Loop is a gem! The location is perfect if you are looking to explore the city. We arrived from another hotel by foot and left for O'Hare by the blue line CTA which was conveniently located about 2 blocks away. There is a Starbucks right outside the hotel's entrance and the restaurant in the lobby is reasonable and quite good. The staff was very helpful. We checked our bags with the front desk staff prior to check-in and also after check out, which was great. The staff also gave us great directions and food and tourist recommendations. The hotel has lots of thoughtful touches---bottled water dispensers, coffee and tea available, a living room downstairs with large screen tv and internet desks. We especially loved our corner room which was a studio suite, complete with micro/fridge and kitchen sink. The room had a comfortable queen bed, a great stone and tile bathroom with shower, a desk and an extra easy chair for tv watching. Though compact, the room was spotless and very well appointed with nice linens and towels. We don't tend to spend much time in our room when we travel to a city like Chicago, so it was everything that we required. We felt good about being somewhat "green" during our stay. 
I would recommend this hotel to business travelers, vacationing couples and singles. The service, location and overall experience were top notch!

name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile
title: “Nice stay, nice people”
text: The hotel is just a few blocks from Michigan Ave and from the path on the water front. It's a nice middle road hotel. The staff is very friendly and it is clean. We had a noise complaint of teenagers and it was taken very seriously and quickly. We even awoke to a report under our door that it had been addressed and the hotel was sorry. Impressive. The morning buffet was a bit on the expensive side but that was the only draw back. Nice stay.

name: Chicago South Loop Hotel
title: “Friendly service”
text: If it weren't for Steve in the front desk, I would be sleeping in my car. I arrived 12 hours early before my check in. Steve Went the extra mile and got me my room on an early check in! The room was excellent and larger than most hotels. I was highly impressed and grateful! Thank you Chicago South Loop Hotel and Steve for the excellent service!

name: Fairmont Chicago Millennium Park
title: “Great hotel”
text:
The hotel was fantastic. Check-in was quick and easy, we were given a fantastic corner room on the 35th floor. The room was wonderful - nice and big for Chicago, very clean, bathroom was nice with the seperate toiltet, bath, and shower. The beds were extremely comfortable and it was quiet. Every one whom we interacted with - the front desk, concierges, maids, valet, servers in Aria sushi - were so nice and accomodating. We didn't really have any special requests, but they made us feel taken care of with any questions we had and acknowledging us. The location was great - right next to Millenium park, close to Magnificent Mile and the pier, nice with a CVS right across the street. .
Things that could see any improvement were:
I wasn't that impressed with the restaurants onsite- just ok sushi, but good service. Both restaurants seemed dead - and we stayed over the weekend. The lobby is very dark and very quiet. If you're looking for excitement and people - this isn't the lobby for you. We went next door to the Hyatt and that lobby almost seemed like an airport - very lively, large and open. 
Overall though, we really like the hotel. It seemed classy, was very quiet and comfortable, and provided excellent service. It's a perfect quiet place to stay if you're looking to relax.

name: Club Quarters Chicago - Central Loop
title: “Great option in the loop and close to the blue line”
text:
I had to fly to Chicago at the last minute and needed to stay downtown in the loop. I was able to secure a great rate directly with the hotel. I found the check - in process decent but was somewhat put off by the $35 early check-in fee. If the room is already available and ready what difference does it make if you arrive at 2 PM or 10:00 AM?
I arrived at 10 AM and was eager to get some sleep. I was advised that no rooms were available until 3 PM but if I wanted to pay $35 for an early check in they would make one available. However, after 11:00 Am the fee is waived. Luckily they had a room available at 11:00 AM. The room was spacious enough for my purposes and the pillows were comfy. The bed itself was decent and I have slept on better so I give that a 7 out of 10 rating. The bathroom was on the small side but the amenities were decent enough. I did not like the fact that I had to go to a hallway to retrieve an iron and table. 
I would stay here again if the price was right but would not stay here again if I found a comparable rate at another hotel with a stronger brand name and more amenities.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile
title: “Average hotel in an above average city.”
text:
I went to Chicago last minute when a friends' travel companion cancelled 2 days beforehand. She had booked at the Chicago Doubletree Magnificent Mile because her daughter was taking part in a dance conference so I followed suit. The location of the DoubleTree Magnificent Mile hotel is excellent...it took us 5 minutes by taxi to get to Michigan Avenue, where all the shops are (10-15 minute walk) and mostly everywhere we wanted to go was a less than 10 minute taxi from the hotel. The cookies we received upon arrival were excellent! The lobby is very awkward and strange to hang around in. The parking rates of $43 a day are simply ridiculous but you do have in and out privileges which many places do not. Ben the parking manager is outstanding. Watch your phone rates! My companion was NOT told that each call made has a MINIMUM $20-$25 "connection fee" ON TOP of the crazy expensive phone rates so a couple of calls cost her over $150 dollars.
I booked a "lake view" room which was nice but had many issues. First of all I paid $189 for a "lake view" room instead of $159 for a room with no lake view only to discover that the "lake view" is a peek of the lake through the surrounding buildings. I was surprised that there was no fan in the bathroom which is particularly annoying when you try to see yourself in the mirror after a steamy shower. The selection of toiletries was limited. There was also no safe, which always makes me nervous when leaving items in my room. There was an old sushi tray left in the mini bar that smelled awful and an old carafe and drinking glass that were filthy and left in the room. Room service was very good and timely -I had a chicken cobb salad which was delicious and the bread was very fresh and tasty. The trays that I left in the hallway (which I was asked to do) after I was done were not picked up for almost 24 hours. Watch the items on top of and inside the mini bar; once you pick them up, you are charged so make sure you check your bill upon checkout. I asked for a "quiet" room on a high floor (it was on the 23rd floor) but was put on a floor with several families with small (and noisy) children. There is no free in-room wifi but in the hotel public areas and lobby there is. When we asked the front desk for recommendations for breakfast, many things in the area were recommended except for "West Egg" which is right in front of the hotel and turned out to be the best we had. 
All in all, an average hotel that is sufficient for a night or two if you are not picky. Next time I am in Chicago I will definitely look at all my other options first.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Casablanca helped make our 1st trip to NYC PERFECT.”
