text: Casablanca was EVERYTHING we expected and more. The hotel staff were friendly and extremely helpful. The breakfast (including gluten free bread & cereal for us Celiac's!) was fresh and plentiful. The coffee was excellent. The evening wine & cheese was also much more than we expected. It was a great way to relax at the end of our busy day before we hit the town for the night. The rooms were elegant but small (we were in a single gueen room with a tub), hanger space was limited. Bath amentities were very nice except for the toilet paper - single ply! The location was perfect. We walked in different directions every day and night. Just around the corner from NASDAQ, it seemed to be the centre of everywhere we wanted to go. We are definitely going back to NYC soon and will either stay at Casablanca or try one of their sister hotels.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile
title: “I'd give it a solid "B", maybe even a B+”
text:
Good location, clean public and private areas, (mostly) friendly staff, decent rate. Good-sized room. 
Stayed here for a weekend with my adult daughters for a "girls getaway". Enjoyed the proximity to the lake, Mag Mile, Navy Pier area, and eateries.
We usually shop a fair amount when in Chi, but because we hit a fabulous stretch of weather we spent a lot of time at the beach, which was a nice change (and cheaper!). It's only a few blocks to Lake Michigan.
We also enjoyed having a bite to eat and a drink at the rooftop pool - quite a large pool, clean, heated, nice for sunbathing. Good "perk".
This is a "tourist class" hotel but one of the better ones IMO. I've not had good luck with Doubletree in the past, but this one was pretty nice. I was satisfied with the value for the dollar.

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “Ottima scelta per godersi the Big Apple”
text: A 5 min da Times Square, Broadway, Central Park. Colazione di qualità eccellente, possibilità di bevande calde e mele tutto il giorno. Possibilità di colazione al sacco se si è di corsa. Tutto compreso nel prezzo. Letti comodissimi. Ho dormito come un ghiro io che sono molto esigente! Se provate Hampton Inn non andrete più da nessun'altra prte a NY.

name: Hilton Chicago
title: “We are going back!”
text: Remember our stay here fondly. Great Staff friendly and helpful. Location excellent. Overall a great place to stay. Going back in 2011.

name: W Chicago Lakeshore
title: “Below W and SPG standards”
text:
First of all, let me tell you that I'm a business traveler. SPG hotels are usually my first choice, so over the last 5 years I've spent over 400 nights on SPG properties all over the US. So I have some bases for comparison. 
My wife and I spent last night in this hotel. It was our anniversary and we wanted to go somewhere nice. Overall it's a nice place, the staff is very friendly and attentive. My issues were with the room. We stayed in room 3000 and this was by far the smallest room I've stayed in any SPG hotels. I understand that if you take a Holiday Inn and remodel it is not the same as building a new one, but if that is the case do not call it luxury collection. But this could all be bearable. The biggest one for me was the bed. SPG prides itself with providing the best mattresses and linens so one can truly enjoy his or her sleep. And until now I would say that it's absolutely true. Except this one - the mattress was quite horrible. Soft and lumpy with fairly deep valleys in the middle. It was so uncomfortable that I woke up this morning with a back pain. Comparing to this a shower with leaking pipes was not such a big deal. The only other thing that I wanted to add was that my wife truly enjoyed a magnifying mirror with a large black spot right in the middle of it where the amalgam wore off. 
To the SPG - the name does not make a hotel category 4 - the hotel itself does. This one should not be higher than Category 3.
Thanks,
Alex R.

name: Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile
title: “Fair Value For A Hotel Located Downtown”
text:
If Staying in Chicago for business or shopping the Courtyard is a fairly obvious choice in the mid-range segment. The hotel seemed both new and clean and the strategic location off Michigan Avenue allows for easy access to the city's attractions. 
There is a parking embedded in the building itself and the subway entrance is not far. 
The rooms are fairly small, but not New York-claustrophobic. A bigger television set would have been nice. Even nicer would have been the removal of the standard-issue evil propaganda pamphlets in the drawer, which I had to enact myself.
The staff were polite and willing to give honest opinions about nearby eateries. It was refreshing to be told a place is over-priced or not quite good without monetary gain in mind.

name: The Westin Chicago River North
title: “Ryder Cup in Chicago”
text: Hi, Bernard and I set off to Chicago Sept 23 2012 on a much awaited trip taking in the Ryder Cup at Medinah outside Chicago. Trailfinders organised all for us and booked Westin River North Hotel in Chicago. Great place to stay. At the edge of the Business District on one side and the busy restaurant area on the other. Lovely staff, very competant concierges, nothing was too much trouble. Happy to guide you and give directions. Upgraded us on arrival acknowledging the fact we were staying 8 nights. Down side if it is one is the cost of WIFI in the bedrooms but it is free in the lobby which is very comfortable and beside a lovely open bar area. Beds are HEAVENLY as advertised. Would reccommend it without a doubt. Needless to say being European we really had a ball at the Ryder Cup - all 6 days.

name: InterContinental Chicago
title: “Awesome historic hotel”
text: For anyone bored of the modern look of most hotels these days, this one retains the more traditional styling of the older, historic hotel that it is. The room was quite nice and clean and the bathroom was spacious. Check-in was painless and friendly. And of course the greatest asset the Intercontinental has is the location! Perfect for a shopping spree.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Hand written card from Guest Services asking for a 5* TA review!”
text:
Hyatt Regency Chicago is a huge hotel in a prime location, therefore we would never pay rack rate to stay there, and still wouldn't consider it for a moment even after receiving 5* service for our two night Thanksgiving stay. Considering what we paid for our room (via Priceline bid) we are very satisfied with our overall experience, however cannot give 5* for two reasons: 
1) There is ZERO sound proofing in between rooms (we were in #2810) - it is as if your fellow guests are hanging out in your room. Even the slightest noise could be heard - the clink of a key to the South, all the way up to full blown party to the North. Let's just say if we HAD paid regular price we would not have been too thrilled!
2) The bed was definitely plush, but 2 nights = 2 mornings with a very sore back. I think the mattress was just getting to the point of needing replacing, or it is simply not supportive enough in the first place. Of course that is a very subjective thing, and I wouldn't have knocked a star off for just this reason alone.
Apart from these two points, everything was very enjoyable. On check in I said the magic word for free wifi, and free wifi is what we got. I also asked for a room as high up as possible, and was happy to be offered the 30-something floor... but then the receptionist mentioned that the view wasn't great from that particular room - would we like a different option? So we ended up on the 28th floor overlooking the river with a restricted but still very fine view out over Navy Pier to the lake. Apparently this would have been an upgrade even for regular rate, so for $65 per night it was much appreciated! I love the city... from a bird's eye view!
So we decided to take a nap (rather full from Thanksgiving Buffet with family at a Hilton in the suburbs) right after checking in at around 6:30PM. A little while later we heard a knock, which was just discernible as being at our door over the partying that was going on in the room next to us - someone at which had already hammered once on the door 'dividing' our two rooms! I thought it was someone looking for next door, so I stumbled (in my sleeping 'attire') to the door and told the person that they were knocking on the wrong piece of wood. A lady's voice mumbled something, but I heard my name. I asked her to give me a minute, and then opened the door to find Guest Services with two bottles of water, a package of chocolate covered toffee, and a 'we love you, thanks for interacting with us on FB, here's some goodies, please leave feedback' hand written card! Baffling service to receive in such a vast hotel booked via a discount website - but what a way to roll! We were very impressed, and yeah I really wish I could give 5*. But if a hotel can't make at least an attempt at inter-room noise control then I don't see how they can expect 5* reviews. It's as simple as that. If there was the option, this would be a 4.5* review, but oh well.
Big Bar is wonderful. The Bistro was fine. Renovations to the other restaurant areas are ongoing, but there is still also the Irish Pub themed bar available. We enjoyed the food and drinks and received fantastic service all round. Yes, it is expensive, but not shockingly so.
There ya go! Pay your money, check in, and pray for quiet neighbors. Unless of course you plan to party yourselves - in which case PLEASE try and be considerate to those who are basically sharing your room with you.

name: Holiday Inn Chicago - Midway Airport
title: “Helpful staff, pleasant stay!!!”
text: I stayed at the Holiday Inn Midway in April because a friend and I were checking out Chicago as we may be moving there, and it was a totally enjoyable experience! We were picked up at the airport by the hotel's shuttle, which comes literally every 10 minutes, and then were greeted by helpful and cheerful staff who were smiling and willing to assist us throughout the whole stay! The rooms are quiet, clean, and modern, and the whole hotel environment is very pleasant and up to date. It was a delightful stay overall, and we really appreciated the friendliness of the staff and the shuttle drivers! DEFINITELY stay here!

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Great Property & Amazing Staff”
text: This Hyatt is really a great property all around! The location is great, the staff is outstanding, and the rooms are nice as well (stayed in east tower). The place was clearly PACKED during our stay! They are currently going through a lobby renovation, so a temporary front desk has been relocated to the first floor, which worked out fine. We used the touch-screen check-in kiosks, which were much more efficient than standing in line at the desk. There are several restaurants/bars on site, and out group ate breakfast at the atrium restaurant on the main level. Food and service were great, even though the buffet was $23.00--some opted to order off the menu for cheaper options. Overall, a great property with top-notch staff. Can't wait to go back and see the hotel after the renovations are complete!

name: InterContinental Chicago
title: “Mostly lovely, with a few important strike-outs”
text: I stayed here for 2 nights on business and found the room and hotel quite lovely. But both times I asked for advice on travel time, the staff underestimated by 20 minutes--and I was going to a job interview and catching a flight, so 20 minutes was a pretty big deal. And at 8am, the hot water was out, and I shivered through a lukewarm shower. I'd definitely still recommend this place, just shower early and double check travel times. (Their phone prices are astronomical, by the way, from $2 flat for a toll-free call to $18/minute for international. Wowie!)

name: The Blackstone A Renaissance Hotel
title: “Very Nice”
text:
The rooms were very nice and I loved the shower. Although there was very little view to the park (I was facing the hotel across the street) it was a nice stay. Very quiet and clean and the Starbucks on site was awesome.
 Its a short walk to Yolk for a very delicious breakfast awaits you there and a little jaunt to the Field Museum which I highly recommend! 
I feel the Valet parking is high at 55.00 a night, we didn't even have them get my vehicle the two days we were there. The doormen are very nice and courteous. 
The only Wrinkle was when I first checked in, our room had a connecting door which I hate so I called down to the front desk and asked if all rooms with 2 beds were connecting she said "not all of them". She did not offer to move us which I was not happy about. I told her I don't like staying in rooms like that and she didn't even check to see if there was another room.. just stated "they are not all connecting"... thought she should have offered to move us knowing how I felt about connecting rooms.. Other than the valet price and the room being connecting I had a very nice time and its a nice hotel, the rooms are well appointed and nicely decorated.

name: Hotel Indigo Chicago Downtown Gold Coast
title: “Location, Location, Location!!!”
text: This hotel was excellent from the moment we walked in with its seaside decor charm to how well maintained it seemed to be! Please be warned it cost us $61 additional (for 2 days) to park at the hotel! New cost to us travelers! The beds were ummmm....."very firm", but we still slept well!! And this is a pet friendly hotel and while we never smelled any pets, there was the constant and undeniable smell of pet odor remover everywhere! So just be warned! For a one night stay this was perfect though! Only one block away from the Red Line Subway station that took us straight to Wrigley Field (which was our main reason for our trip)! And only a few blocks away from the "Magnificent Mile"! Also Walgreen's is on the same corner and super convenient!

name: InterContinental Chicago
title: “Back again and not dissappointed”
text: I just checked in yesterday for my annual 5 days stay. As an Ambassador, even though I booked thru the convention web site, I was upgraded to a suite and when I asked for the larger suite with French Doors the staff downstairs just asked me to wait for a moment and then changed my room. They were only concerned that there was something wrong with the first room (which there wasn't, I just wanted the larger one). Both the check in with Margaret and the changing of the rooms with Cintia was quick and efficient. Yes, the hotel is not new and the beds are not the softest in the world but I find the staff as accommodating as can be and no negative surprises. Housekeeping is a little slow but it is a big hotel and really not a big issue. In fact they already put in my record my preferences for next year. I will continue to come back, it's nice when you come just once or twice a year to be recognized and received warmly.

name: The Blackstone A Renaissance Hotel
title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text: What a pleasant surprise to a priceline booking. Great hotel, location, staff, etc. We didn't get to try the Mercat restaurant, but the little cafe on the lower level had great drinks and outdoor seating. Definitely recommend and will be returning next time we are in Chicago.

name: W Chicago - City Center
title: “Above and beyond my expectations”
text: I stayed at this hotel for the IMTS trade show in September, and I will say that everything about this hotel exceeded my expectations. The hotel was hip and trendy, and close to everything. I unfortunately was involved in a car accident during my stay, and Maida at the front desk, made sure I was well taken care of. She called Dr. Allan from Chicagoexpress docs to come to my room and care for me, she had a runner go get me a heating pad, and she even wrote me a get well card. Eden, the concierge was also fabulous with her recommendations. I will definitely be staying here again when i visit Chicago!

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Coolest Hotel I've stayed in”
text: I've never stayed in a work of art before. Friendly staff, great bed, quiet enough. Overall a very good stay. I did pay as much for two drinks at the bar as I usually spend on dinner though. Location is good for Millenium Park and Museums. I would stay farther north for shopping. $5-$6 cab ride from Union Station.

name: Fairmont Chicago Millennium Park
title: “Gorgeous hotel, but be prepared to be nickeled and dimed at every turn...”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for a conference for work, and decided to stay a few extra days to see the sights. The reception area is beautiful, but from the beginning it was clear that this is one of those hotels that tries to sneak extra fees into absolutely everything that they can. We rented a car, and parking costs $51. You have only valet as an option. Wireless internet? over $15/day... their business center was like $5 a minute (and don't even ask how much to print something. Want to work out at their fitness center? Sure, for a "nominal fee"... and on and on...
Absolutely ridiculous... I will say that the wait staff, valet, and bellhops were very helpful (just wonderful), although the concierge wasn't the most helpful. In summary, if you are staying for business reasons, then sure, go for it (especially if you don't have a choice, like I didn't). But I would never come back to this hotel for a leisure trip, and I wouldn't recommend this hotel to someone who is staying at their own expense... unless they don't care how much money they drop. To me, this hotel wasn't THAT nice for that sort of money - I've stayed in MUCH nicer, and not had all of those stupid fees to contend with!

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “très bon rapport qualité prix”
text: un hotel situé près de times square et une chambre très confortable. 2 points négatifs : le petit déjeuner (buffet ridicule et file d'attente pour pouvoir y accéder) et le bruit (porte communicante entre les chambres et rue)

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “OMG! What a great gem of a hotel”
text:
This hotel is better than most resorts I have stayed at. It is impeccable clean, and friendly doesn't even begin to describe it. 
Although the rooms are a bit small, the attention to detail in the great bath products and breakfast and snack offerings more than made up for any reservations about the room. The location is abosultely terrific.
I can't say eneough and would without hesitation stay here again.
Tony's resturant is great and DELICIOIUS

name: Hotel Indigo Chicago Downtown Gold Coast
title: “Only good thing is the location...”
text:
I just recently stayed at the Hotel Indigo in Chicago, IL. We stayed there for 2 nights, a Saturday and Sunday. The only good thing I can really say about this hotel is the location. It was only about a 10 minute walk from Michigan Ave. and had every type of restaurant/store nearby that you could want. 
When we first walked in the decor was great and the lobby looked extremely nice. The staff when we checked in was not too friendly or overly nice but everyone is entitled to having a bad day. We then were told that we had a smoking room, which we were unaware of. When we stepped off of the elevator the entire floor wreaked of smoke. I have stayed in other hotels on the smoking floor and have never had this problem. When we walked into the room we noticed the decor was very cute and colorful but the size was extremely small. Not only was the room extremely small but there was a spider on the wall which had been killed and smeared across the ceiling..quite disgusting. The TV looked to be about a 19" from the late 1990's and was somewhat hard to see from the bed because it was so small. The bathroom was fine and was the most modern thing in the room, although the sink did back up when I brushed my teeth but eventually went down after a few minutes. The room was equipped with a keurig, however we were given only decaf coffee. I'm sure we could have called down and asked for regular but did not feel like going through all that and went to starbucks instead. 
The worst part of my stay was the fact that the walls of this hotel are EXTREMELY thin. For approximately 30 mins we could here people in a room down the hall have sexual relations. It was absolutely disgusting and for this reason and all of the others, I will NEVER stay in this hotel again.

name: Hotel Indigo Chicago Downtown Gold Coast
title: “dissapointed.”
text:
I'm currently sitting in my room in this hotel, with my view of the fire escape and my 1992 era television. Upon arrival around midnight last night, I was told there was only a public parking deck next door but if I wanted street parking, I could come down and start feeding a meter at 8am. It would seem I was lucky there was a $39/day deck next door. I then attempted to enter my room with what would appear to be 2 bad keys. After returning to the front desk (I was treated very nicely by the night manager) she came up with me and it turns out the key has to sit in the slot for 10 seconds before you can get in. Wow. 
The room is ok. The laminate hardwood floors would be a decent touch, if they werent uneven and chipped in parts. I can also hear everything my neighbors are doing. When I called to order some coffee and breakfast, the chick in the restaurant said she would call me back and when I picked up the phone when she did, she just said "yeah?" as if I had interrupted her mid-conversation. When I asked how long I could wait for breakfast she complained about how she was the only one there, and there were other people waiting, and it would be 20 minutes for my yogurt, fruit, and coffee. 
I'm not impressed with the service, the room, or anything else I've seen. I've stayed at an Indigo in Asheville and LOVED it so I was excited to try this one in Chicago. My excitement was quickly dispelled with and now I'm wishing I'd shelled out the extra money for the Dana or Wyndham where I normally stay.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Great stay, beautiful hotel”
text:
We had a great stay at the Palmer House. The hotel is beautiful. Per recommendations on TA, we requested a renovated room far from the elevators. Alfred at check-in was so cheerful & nice and accomodated our request. The room we stayed in was just lovely, and quite large. I would recommend requesting the same things as we did, as the walls really were thin and it was nice to have a room tucked in the corner so the only noises we would be able to hear were those of the room next to us. When the maid was cleaning the room next to us, we could hear everything she was doing so I can imagine it would get frustrating to have a lot of people talking & walking by your room if you're a late sleeper.
The executive lounge breakfast was fairly basic but all we needed for a two night stay. Lots of pastries, bagels, oatmeal, granola, etc. The coffee, Ronnoco, is the free stuff they serve at my work and I don't like at at work and I didn't like it at the Hilton, but it's free so I can't complain too much. The evening happy hour had great appetizers, very delicious. The hotel is in a good location, very close to milennium park and shopping. I would recommend parking at the Millenium Park Garage located at 5 S Columbus Street. It is about a 6 minute walk to the hotel and only $26 for 24 hours - the garage has a website if you google it. However, there are no in and out privelages so if that is something you need, you might just have to bite the bullet and pay the $42 for parking. I read in the welcome book in our room that you should allow 45 minutes for valet to get your car, to me that is insane (especially at that price), but just be prepared if you do get valet. We didn't encounter any bell boys trying desperately to get tips. In fact, we never saw anyone opening anyone's doors and no one even offered to take our bags, albeit small, at check-in. I saw that in another review, and I'm not saying that didn't happen to them, we just had a different experience!

name: W Chicago Lakeshore
title: “Terrible Customer Service-Front Desk and Management”
text: I just got back from my "experience" at the W Lakeshore and I am less than pleased. Upon checkin we were not able to receive our key. Our trip was pre-paid for by my father-in-law as a birthday gift and our names were not on the reservation. His name was the only name on the reservation, due to a hotel error. Due to "security reasons" we could not check in until he contacted the hotel to give approval. Understandable to an extent, but again our names were not on the reservation due to a booking mistake. I was ok with this mistake when the lady at the desk bought us drinks while we waited to get a hold of my father-in-law (who is a lawyer who happened to be stuck in court). After enjoying a few drinks at the bar I walked through the lobby to find a bathroom and all of our bags (which had been unloaded out of my car by valet) were sitting in the middle of the lobby completely unattended. It was check-in time and there were at least 100 people in the lobby. Any number of things could have been stolen! I alerted the front desk of this and they asked me what I wanted them to do. The girl at the desk talked to me like I was not a real guest and stomped over to her manager and clearly seemed like I was asking her to do something out of the question. Her manager also acted like I was being out of line for asking for my bags to be stored. 3 hours later we were able to check into the room and waited over an hour to get our bags delivered to the room. At the end of our stay we ended up paying $48 a day for parking even though when we booked the room there was a promotion for free parking during our stay. The front desk asked me to "prove it," in exact words. Shouldn't they have record of their promotions that they advertise. Should the guest really need documentation? Again our trip was a gift we did not have any confirmation information with us, but the reason why we picked the hotel was because of the free parking promotion. On the website that we booked the room with it still lists the promotion which is still valid for a few more weeks!!!!! Overall totally incompetent snobby front desk and management that think that since they work somewhere nice means they can be snobs. News flash, our stay at their hotel cost more than their monthly paycheck! Our waitress was nice and the man who delivered our bags to our room was also nice, but they were the only exceptions! There are MUCH better places in Chicago to stay! I will never spend another penny at a W hotel!

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Home from Home.”
text:
Our visit began 2 days before arrival when we had a courtesy call from the hotel to ensure all the details for our stay were correct. Never had that before!
My daughter, granddaughter and I stayed here for five nights. We were delighted with all of our stay. From arriving to find balloons, cupcakes and champagne in the room (we had a birthday girl) to the last glass of prosecco just before heading for the airport, perfection reigned.
It has all been said before here on T/A, and it is all true. The rooms are exactly as pictured, we had a large room with two beds and there was plenty of space for the three of us. Beds really comfortable with high quality linens, bathroom spacious with all amenities. We were facing the back on the 6th floor and within the room there was no outside noise, not a sound from next door either.
The concept of 24hour refreshments is pure genius. The breakfast was delicious, and the evening cheese and wine so welcome. The area felt like a living room at home and we were very comfortable there.The free internet was very useful and seemed well used. One night we were too exhausted to go out to dinner and so we had the cheese and wine buffet and headed for bed with popcorn and dvds. How many hotels could you do that in?
The staff here are welcoming and accommodating, especially the girls in Ricks, so special thanks to them. But everyone we met was very friendly.
NY is a very tiring city and very noisy so near to Times Square. Step inside the front door and as it closes the noise and madness just stop. Instantly refreshing.
We almost did not get home, due to the volcanic ash, and sat at the end of the runway for 2 hours whilst a decision was made. We left not knowing the enormity of the situation and arrived in Bristol to find it deserted of planes or passengers. Well done Continental!
There can be no other hotel for us now, and we would highly recommend it for all ages.
Thank you all!!

name: Hilton Chicago
title: “Charming, historical hotel in downtown Chicago”
text: The Hilton Chicago is a huge hotel and a very busy one too. The lobby area and rooms are very grand and somewhat colonial. The rooms were not awesomely huge but they were comfortable and conform to Hilton standards. Navigating the guest floors' corridors were like navigating a maze but that adds to the excitement of being in one of Chicago's most historical hotels that have housed countless dignitaries from all over the world. Location wise, you're right across from the picturesque Grant Park and there is a free shuttle to the Mag Mile shopping district albeit they can do better with a larger bus or more frequent runs.

name: Raffaello Hotel
title: “Horrible front-desk service”
text: The room was okay--not great, but passable--but the front-desk staff was unbelievably poor. I could list numerous oversights and examples of incompetence, but I'll only mention the worst. Even though I fully prepaid for the hotel reservation through an online booking service, the hotel's front-desk staff erroneously charged my credit card for the entire stay, as well. It has been nearly a month, and I'm still waiting for the credit to my account that they tell me they've processed. That's only the most egregious of a long list of problems, ranging from refusing to send up additional towels, mischarging for valet parking, you name it. In a city full of nice hotels, there's no good reason to take a gamble with this one.

name: InterContinental Chicago
title: “All around good hotel”
text: Hotel has excellent location. Rooms are a good size for downtown hotel. All the comfort you'd expect from Intercontinental brand. All-in-all a very comfortable stay. Would recommend this hotel. Had a minor issue with my credit card being double billed, but that was resolved with a telephone call.

name: Holiday Inn Chicago - Mart Plaza
title: “a great week end at Chicago”
text:
I went there for Memorial weekend and booked at expedia. The price was very low for an Hotel closed to the loop. Arrive in late morning but was able to check in with no problem. Room was very clean . Swimming pool and excercise rooms are great . The view over chicago river and sears towers was fantastic . Expect a lot of kids everywhere.
Additionally it is very well situated, walking distance from the loop and the magnificent mile ( a good walk however, but no problem streets are friendly and taxis are easy to catch. Certainly an excellent choice for its price at week ends. Only minorl problem, Restaurant is very pricey. Breakfast is ok but it's over 13$ plus taxes. However, have a walk and you'll find plenty of other choices.
I will come back. Chicago is a great city and you must stay there several days if you want enough time to visit the great museums, walk around (it's a town for people who like walking) , have boat tours on the river and listen to jazz music.

name: W Chicago - City Center
title: “Travel for business”
text:
I stayed at the W Chicago - City Center during a business conference. The location is great, with restaurants within walking distance. Hotel room service was really good. A little pricey, but good. Be sure to come prepared to pay for daily valet parking. 
We arrived early and our rooms were ready. I was originally placed at the end of the hall, next to the fire exit, with the fire escape stairs right outside of my window. I was not comfortable with this location. I asked to move to another room, and they were happy to accommodate my request, but it was not ready for early check-in. As soon as the room was ready, the concierge team contacted me to pick up my new room key. The rooms are tiny, but they will comp you with drinks and wifi, for the smaller room. If you move to a little larger room, which is still small, you are not comp these items. 
I forgot part of my workout clothes and I was immediately offered a t-shirt and hat. I was very pleased with the service.

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “Hier komen we zeker terug!”
text: Onlangs een week in New York geweest en bewust in de Hampton Inn verbleven. De ervaring had ons geleerd dat er grote verschillen zitten in wat de hotels in Manhatten bieden: in ieder geval is goedkoop meestal duurkoop. Via diverse 'review sites' kwamen we op dit hotel uit. Ook hadden we al eerder in een andere Hampton gelogeerd. Service was goed, al hing het ook hier af van wie je sprak. Heel schoon allemaal en kamer was ook ruim en voorzien van alle gemakken die je in deze categorie mag verwachten. Prijs-kwaliteit prima. Ligging niet ver van Times Square heel geschikt en metro op de volgende hoek. Enige punt van kritiek betreft de liften: er zijn er voor het hele hotel van 11 verdiepingen maar twee en dat is te weinig.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Old Hotel....Not that great”
text: It's an older hotel and the room was layed out odd. Not sure if I would stay here again....I really liked the Park Hyatt but of course that is twice the amount. The check in process was long but they had a place where you could store your luggage if your room wasn't ready. The regency club sucked like they all do. Very few are good!

name: The Westin Chicago River North
title: “Great Weekend at the Westin”
text:
I chose this hotel based almost solely on the location - directly across the street from the House of Blues where I was going to be attending an event. Taking the train into Chicago, I didn't want to have to walk too far late at night and the Westin was in the ideal location for my purposes. Turns out, the Westin River North is in a great location for just about everything. From Union Station, it's a $6 cab ride (taken because I didn't want to haul my luggage through Midtown). Otherwise, just about everything you need is easily within walking distance. Lots of great food options, entertainment venues/bars, and Michigan Avenue.
The hotel itself is very nice. There's a large, welcoming lobby as soon as you walk in (and you'll probably be greeted by some delightful doormen). The elevators even have an oddly pleasant aroma around them. The room was really nice - clean, spacious enough, and the bathroom was fantastic. While I did not find the bed to be as "heavenly" as advertised, it was easily 10x more comfortable than any other hotel bed I've found. The staff was friendly and helpful. My only real complaint was the fee-per-day in-room internet, which I find ridiculous at this point in time. I just grabbed my laptop and went to hang out in the lobby for a few minutes when needed, and used the free wifi there.
Overall, it was a great stay and I'd definitely consider it again if I was going to that part of Chicago again.

name: W Chicago Lakeshore
title: “Great Surprise Weekend in Chicago”
text:
We are starwood preffered guest members and got a rate of 129 for a saturday night so we jumped on it for a quick getaway. We arrived to a 7th floor lakefront view and a great little room. The hotel looked really nice. The lobby was really cute, as most W's are, and the gym looked amazing. Pool didn't look too bad either but we didn't use it. WE had drinks at the bar and the bartenders were great. We went to see a show so we took a cab. When we got back later that night they had a DJ in the lobby so we had a few martinis. We went back up the room and ordered room service which was just find until there was a long blonde hair actually inside my burger which ruined the meal. The next day we had breakfast in the lobby restaurant which was excellent, and then we went to the spa and each had an 80 minute treatment that was excellent. The spa was very nice and I took advantage of all the locker room amenities. Overall it was very nice, minus the roomservice mishap. The rooms are very modern but clean. The only major flaw was that the room is small to begin with and the put slat wood sliding doors and a window on the bathroom, so there isn't much privacy. 
I laughed that the mini bar had emergency contraception supplies next to a W teddy bear, as well as room service breakfast that was fruit, whipped cream, chocolate syrup, champagne, and hold your calls for an hour for $150.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Calm under fire”
text: I attended a convention here last week - was there for 7 days. 6,000 participants. I have to say, the restaurant served good food even though they were overwhelmed. The elevators were a little slow, but the hotel provided excellent service with elevator monitors who kept order. My room was reasonably clean (all right, I always clean the phone and lights). Maid service was fine. All in all, a pleasant experience, particularly given the size of the hotel.

name: PUBLIC Chicago
title: “Not guest friendly, especially for families”
text: It was bad from the start. We're a young family traveling traveling with a young one, and the entrance doors are not big enough for a stroller, not to mention a wheelchair. After waiting quite a few minutes for one of the two minuscule elevators, then getting on and not being able to find the floor buttons because the elevators were dimly lit with no backlight on the floor buttons (remember to pack your flashlights), we finally got to our room. Upon entering, it was nicely furnished, but we noticed it was quite small. The beds are 12 inches off the floor, and quite uncomfortable. The walls are paper thin, as we learned after the next room turned on Sportscenter at 1 am as we were trying to sleep. We were meeting family in town, and since there was no room or seating accommodations in the suites, we decided to meet downstairs in the lobby. After getting Starbucks and cupcakes, we were informed 10 minutes later that there was no eating or drinking in the lobby (what?!?). Meaning you can't find space in this place to hang out for a bit and enjoy coffee or a drink with friends and family. I don't get that philosophy, especially for a hotel. There are two restaurants in the hotel, but I must say the patrons were given more preferential treatment than the hotel guests, which is consistent with the other reviews I've read. But hey, there is free wireless, nice Mac desktops downstairs, and nicely decorated. But compared to the 15 or so other hotels we've stayed at in Chicago, ranks up there with the worst for us. Poor customer service, and they've ignored the basics before upgrading the amenities in the redesign. We won't be returning, and I would avoid if you have other options.

name: The Blackstone A Renaissance Hotel
title: “Amazing Stay”
text:
I stayed here during a weekend getaway (and a cubs game) with my girlfriend. The hotel is only a couple of block walk from the Harrison stop on the Red Line, and within walking distance of Buckingham fountain. My car ended parked the whole weekend since it was within either walking distance of Millennium Park, Art Museum and Buckingham fountain, for the rest of the trip we used either the L Train or hired a cab. 
The room was roomy, with an awesome bathroom (tv inside the mirror) and a great shower. They were out of Lakeview rooms but our City View room gave us an amazing vantage of Sears( I meant “Willis”) Tower. The “Gallery” Floor is very cool and worth a visit. 
Overall I was very pleased with the room and will definitely be back! 
Ps. Did I mention that the skyline of the city at night can add romance to a candlelight dinner?

name: InterContinental Chicago
title: “Great Location, Tiny Rooms”
text: If location is your main objective when choosing a hotel, The Intercontinenal is terrific. If you are looking for a room you can relax in and unpack, go someplace else. For a reason no one could tell me, the hotel removed all drawers from all rooms in the old tower. We travel often and unpack as soon as we arrive in a hotel. I have never been in one where this was not possible. We asked to be moved to the "new" tower where there were still dressers but our room and bath there were tiny - fine for one person or a night or two stay but not for more.Also some of the furniture and the wall paper were beat. I also dislike the lobby area. It is huge but there is room for only 6 close friends to sit and 3 of those chairs are hidden behind the stairs. They also charge $15 a day for wifi. Maybe I am spoiled but most places we go, it is free. We visit Chicago several times a year and next time, we'll find another place to unpack our bags.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Good stay”
text: Admittedly, we had a 'mystery hotel' booking through expedia.com. We were very happy with the room, with the staff, with the ambience and the location. All top notch. Room had no view (looked into another wing of the hotel) and the WiFi was not complimentary (what century are these folks in??) but otherwise, safe, comfortable and convenient.

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “très bien”
text:
Nous avons séjourné à new york dans cet hôtel pour la période du jour de l'an durant une semaine, et nous l'avons beaucoup apprécié. En effet, le personnel est toujours souriant et acceuillant. Ensuite, le petit déjeuner est très bon. L'hôtel est d'une propreté remarquable. Les chambres ne sont pas petites et le lit est très confortable. Et pour conclure, cet hôtel est très bien situé. 
Je ne comprend pas pourquoi vous l'avez classer en 2 étoiles car il est plutôt du niveau des 3 étoiles pour ne pas dire 3 et demi.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “great hotel”
text: Location is excellent, rooms are a good size. The view is lacking, and the entrance/lobby is not flashy, but I didn't come to NY for the hotel views. It was a pleasant experience, and I would definitely stay there again (If I could afford it).

name: Hilton Chicago
title: “Fantastic stay”
text:
Stayed at the Chicago Hilton for three nights and from the minute we walked through the door I was very impressed. Check-in was quick, easy and I was very glad that we were able to check in despite being earlier than the advertised check-in time. We were given a twin room with two bathrooms which was brilliant. It made getting ready to go out much quicker! The hotel location is great opposite the park, which is a must see. Although located on South Michigan Ave it is easily within walking distance of all the shops and sights of the whole of Michigan Ave. Would also recommend the street one block back from Michigan Ave for good shopping. For breakfast I would recommend grabbing a muffin, croissant or bagel from the bar just past reception rather than going for the more expensive breakfast in the restaurant. For evening entertainment Kitty O'Sheas is a must. Typical Irish bar with good drinks and live music.
Finally the bed at Hilton Chicago is the most comfortable bed ever. I would have taken it home if I could! Definately made for a good nights sleep.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Just great!!”
text:
Stayed at the Doubletree for 3 nights on pretty much the recommendations given here (had previously booked another and cancelled it for the same reason!).
We were not disappointed. The cookies on arrival to the friendly door and security staff made an impressionable arrival. Then we walked into the room!! Wow we were lucky enough to have a corner room looking out onto Broadway. The room was typically furnished in hotel style! but was well probably larger than my husband and mines first apartment! The space was an added bonus especially in NYC.And not forgeting the maids little note to say thank you for the tip!!
My only small problem was a very unhelpul concierge who happened to be there when I needed some help.
I would definately choose this hotel again when I return.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Floor 22, exec level”
text: Room very nice,twin baths, large room. Downside was being 1 floor away from roof so constant roof a/c machines. Hotel designed for 2 exec floors, current Hilton config uses floor 18-23 so awful lot of people cueing for free evening canapes & morning breakfast & not enough seating. Overall lovely hotel, great location, parking in next block just not sure worth extra for exec rooms, plenty of breakfast options nearby

name: Hotel Indigo Chicago Downtown Gold Coast
title: “Absolutely Terrible Customer Service!”
text:
My friends and I booked this hotel through priceline and got a "deal" for a double queen. The check in was 4pm. We got there 30 minutes early, around 3:30. As we were checking in, the staff told us that our room was already given to someone else. Shocked, we asked how that could've happened when we've already got the confirmation. They informed us that there were some miscommunications between the staff but they'll have the maids clean another room for us. We could've just went elsewhere, but we decided to "be nice" and wait. 
Finally after more than an hour of waiting, another room was cleaned for us. On top of that, they charged us an additional $50 for another bed! After all the terrible customer service, the least they could do was waive that extra bed fee, since the deal we got thru priceline was for a double queen. They didn't even care to apologize for their mistake!! And the so called Valet parking is a total rip off and annoying as ever just to get a staff to come park your car. 
 Customer service is absolutely terrible in every sense! Everything about this hotel is just garbage! save your hard earned money! BOOK ELSEWHERE!!!! AND YOU BET I'VE ALREADY TOLD ALL OF MY CO-WORKERS AND FRIENDS NOT TO BOOK AT HOTEL INDIGO IF THEY GO TO CHICAGO!

name: Hilton Chicago
title: “Great Hotel in a Great City”
text: We booked our stay through Priceline.com and got a great deal. We were only staying one night and we had our 2 year old with us. At check-in, we were upgraded to a suite with a lake view of Lake Michigan. It was beautiful. The suite had a king bed with a living room and a bar and mini-fridge which we didn't need, but if we were staying longer, it would have been a godsend. This hotel is in close proximity with Grant Park which has the beautiful Buckingham Fountain. We walked around the park and even saw a movie being filmed....but if you are looking for a hotel with a lot of restaurants around it, this isn't the one. We ended up eating at the Irish Pub inside the hotel (Kitty O'Shea's) which has great food. (We have stayed here before and always end up eating here.) There are a lot of attractions within a mile including the Field Museum, Shedd Aquarium, Soldier Field, and Navy Pier. They may not be walking distance but we could see them from our hotel window. Overall, we had another wonderful stay at the Chicago Hilton. (Our 4th stay) The only downside is the expensive parking within the hotel.....41 dollars a night is kind of ridiculous.

name: Holiday Inn Chicago - Mart Plaza
title: “Très bon séjour”
text: Hotel proche des principaux sites centraux. Chambre correcte et silencieuse avec la chance (?) d'avoir une vue magnifique côté "loop". Possibilité d'accueillir notre fille, arrivée plus tard séparément, en 3ème personne, sans supplément. Personnel serviable et souriant. Toujours dehors, pas d'avis sur les possibilités et services accessibles à l'intérieur. Ambiance intérieure sans intérêt mais cela nous importe peu.

name: PUBLIC Chicago
title: “Wonderful Experience”
text: Just got back from staying at PUBLIC Chicago for a weekend. The hotel is beautifully appointed and in a nice location, in the Gold Coast/Near North side neighborhood. It is quieter than the main tourist/downtown area though still within walking distance. Above all, kudos to the incredible staff that brought the experience from nice to outstanding. From pulling up to valet to accommodating check-in/check-out times, every experience was a pleasure. Hats off to the concierge who took their time to acquaint us with Chicago to make our experience outside the hotel just as enjoyable.

name: Fairmont Chicago Millennium Park
title: “Hotel Pretty Okay, Location can't be beat”
text: Recently enjoyed a three night stay here. The hotel overall is nice with typical signs of aging. Our room was spacious and very accommodating, but probably could use a good deep cleaning as evidenced by the dust on the furnishings. Bed was very comfortable. Slept like a baby. Somehow my photo of the entire room didn't download properly so can't show you the size of room, but it was definitely one of the largest non-suites I've stayed in. The view was off the charts. Bathroom was nice and large with separate water closet, shower, and tub, all tiled in pretty marble. The concierge club was nicely decorated (a lot more updated than rest of hotel) with awesome views, great continental breakfast, and chic snacks in the evening and two computers with easy Internet access but not worth the extra expense, in my opinion. I think it's a romantic property based on location and cozy, traditional furnishings. It's a block or two east of Michigan Avenue in a quiet little area so it was nice to return afer experiencing the hustle and bustle of the city. The best description is "nice." I wasn't blown away but when my husband is in town for business he enjoys it for the location, which is less than a 5 minute walk to the office, and the room service. Try the halibut.

name: InterContinental Chicago
title: “Not the 4 star I was expecting”
text: I cannot fault the folks working at the Intercontinental. They were great overall, and Guest Services was very responsive to things that needed attention, i.e., additional pillows and towels, etc. The gal at the front desk was very accomodating, and she graciously agreed to upgrade us to a jr. suite (with 2 adults and 2 teenagers, the extra space was a real plus). The gal who cleaned the room was terrific about going through the list of requests (i.e., laundry bags, additional cups, etc.) But the hotel, and the jr. suite we stayed in, were somewhat the worse for wear--the wall paper in the hallway was really chewed up; the sleeper sofa the kids slept on was really uncomfortable; a/c temp. control in the first room apparently didn't work; and we never did figure out what the light switch in the bedroom went to, since it did not serve to turn on or turn off lights. On the other hand, the location was great in terms of our 2 teenagers getting to the Navy Pier, shopping on Michigan Avenue, taking a boat ride, etc. Since the purpose of the trip was to celebrate by stepdaughter's 16th BD, I guess it was a resounding success--she had a blast, and I wasn't worried about the kids getting snatched off the street or lost. But I think the place needs some sprucing up overall. I also agree with some of the other reviewers that charging extra for internet is ridiculous.

name: The Westin Chicago River North
title: “Great business hotel in convenient location”
text:
I stayed at this hotel recently while attending a conference and although the price was a little higher than I would expect to pay for this sort of hotel, I found the location, cleanliness and service were excellent on the whole. Although my colleague and I arrived early the receptionist was kind enough to find us both river view rooms, which were very comfortable.
The one let down was having to wait 15 minutes for the valet to bring our car around which, as there is no self-parking facility at the hotel, we would have expected a slightly better service.
All in all though, I would definitely recommend this as a good place to stay in downtown Chicago, within easy reach of Navy Pier, Michigan Avenue and Millennium Park.

name: Hotel Indigo Chicago Downtown Gold Coast
title: “The indigo hotel is the worst I have ever...”
text: The indigo hotel is the worst I have ever been to.I ordered wine glasses some one took them to my room dirty with lipstick n dusty the worst ever..will never go back. U get what u pay for right!

name: W Chicago Lakeshore
title: “You should try it, ONCE and make up your mind”
text:
Really, you should try this hotel once and decide for yourself. This was my third trip with my family and my kids think it is the coolest place on earth; the pool with the word "wet" at the bottom, the fluffy beds and techno beats playing as a backdrop to the whole experience...it is much cooler than well....me. 
I don't like the dark hallways, feel as though they are dark only because the place has something to hide. Frankly, it might. The hotel is not new by any stretch of the imagination; but it is comfortable. 
As I checked in this time, there was a guy in his late 40's checking in with a "girl" in her mid 20's just in front of me. It struck me that if I were to be unmarried or even, having an affair...this would be the hotel where I'd want to make it happen! The place is full of mojo. 
The beds are comfy, the service is fine and the view from the lakeside is lovely. Try it once.

name: InterContinental Chicago
title: “Great customer service!”
text: Dennis, Cintia, and Brittney were very helpful during our two-night family stay at the Intercontinental in Chicago. Thank you!

name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile
title: “Gutes Preisleistungsverhältnis”
text:
Das Hotel liegt mitten in Chicago an der Magnificent Mile. Von hier aus kann man zu den Navy Piers laufen und das Wasser geniessen. Unten im Hotel ist neben dem normalen Frühstück noch ein Einsteins Bagel Bros. untergebracht, sowie ein gutes italienisches Restaurant, wo man abends hervorragend essen kann. 
Das Hotel ist gut, man bekommt sogar einen Cookie, wenn man eincheckt. Lediglich das Parken nimmt mit 41 Dollar ein Negaivum ein. Das ist doch schon sehr teuer.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Felt very safe and secure, I liked having security guards at the entrance .”
text: Having security guards on the first floor entrance and having to show hotel card gave us a secure felling . Beds were very comfortable , pull out sofa was as expected , adquate ,but not too comfortable, probably fine for young children . Breakfast was great .

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Well equipped but small rooms”
text: The Palmer House is an older, classic hotel. Everything appeared to be well kept up. Room was very nicely equipped but rather small at least by more modern standards. New electronics with HD TV, including digital service on most channels. Comfortable bed and bedding. Bathroom was small and the shower a little dark and rather tight,

name: Raffaello Hotel
title: “Fabulous location”
text:
What a fantastic location for the price of this cute boutique hotel. We stayed for six nights and found the location perfect for our many activities: heading for Starbucks for our morning coffee, walking on the shoreline for the fireworks from Navy Pier, strolling on the Magnificent Mile, getting CTA passes at Waterworks for our six days, catching a bus to the Science and Industry Museum, walking to the river, Grant Park, and the Chicago Art Institute (a very long walk), or heading up to the observation deck and the cocktail lounge of the John Hancock building late at night when no one else is there. 
Upon checking in, our friends ended up on the 15th floor; we ended up on the sixth. When I looked out our window I saw dirty towels in a huge basket. I immediately went down and requested a room on the same floor as our friends, and never returned to the 6th floor. We were given a two bed room which was fine with us. Our bags were moved immediately, no drama. This is not a view hotel, however, the roof top gives you a glance at the lake and an "in your face" view of the John Hancock building as it is right across the street. The beds were comfy, our room was always clean and ready for us at the end of the day, the business center is open 24 hours (which we needed for Oak Park reservations and the Chicago Architectural Foundation boat tour), and we found the staff cordial, helpful, and doing their jobs well- although we didn't need them except for a question or two. We did not eat here in the morning as we felt we wanted to walk for our breakfast rather than pay $15 a head for a continental breakfast.
Starbucks became our morning destination. Cabs were hailed easily, the Chicago Transit Authority Red Line is a few blocks away, and the recommendation by the concierge for dinner at the Rosebud was excellent (albeit expensive but we loved it!)
Only downside- a touch of soap residue on the shower corner, bumps in the floor from old wood underneath the rug, and a small glass shelf (too small to hold your sundries) in the bathroom. This was a disabled room, and our friends was too, so I am not sure if all rooms were equipped with grabrails etc... The shower is overhead, so if you are coiffed, it could be a problem for your hair- I washed mine everyday and loved it.
This is not a full service hotel. It is all about location, location, location. If you are active (don't mind walking or using a power chair) and want to see the city, this is the place for you.

name: W Chicago Lakeshore
title: “loved it”
text: got lucky when i chose to "name your price" on priceline. i chose the area of the city and bid 100. my bid was accepted. at first i was a bit hesitant because of some of the reviews that i had read (not necessarily on this site). however, i was pleasantly surprised. we stayed in a cityview room on the 19th floor. though not as amazing as a lake view, it was still great. you can enjoy the lake view at the elevator alcove where they provide a telescope. i would have gladly paid the standard rate for our room. we had a king sized bed, and the room was quite spacioius. although i could hear people in the adjoining rooms, during the early evening, it was silent when i went to sleep. the hotel is very trendy and hip. wireless is free in the living room (also wonderful for people watching). the staff was very helpful and courteous. the rooms were spotless. would definitely stay here again.

name: Fairmont Chicago Millennium Park
title: “Great Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Fairmont for 3 nights and had a 12th floor corner room. The room was large, clean and comfortable. The staff was helpful, especially the concierge. It was within walking distance of many sites. We would stay here again.

name: W Chicago Lakeshore
title: “This Hotel Rocks!”
text: The lobby is like a tastefully done club lounge, complete with DJ's spinning both weekends nights we were there. Adds a touch of party-time to your trip. The rooms are well done, nice toiletries, firm bed, 42" plasma TV. The rainshower head is nice, and if you can score a lake view, it's about the best overall hotel room feel in the city. Be ready to spend some cash - The valet is pricey ($44.00/nt), bottled water is $8.00/ and the location a few blocks off Michigan requires you to take cabs, but you get what you pay for with this hotel. We're definitely staying here next trip - it's worth it.

name: Holiday Inn Chicago - Mart Plaza
title: “Good Service and Great Views in the Heart of Chicago”
text:
Located at Chicago's Merchandise Mart in the heart of the Magnificent Mile, this Holiday Inn is perched atop the Chicago Sun Times building and the underground shopping mall known as the Merchandise Mart. Easily accessible from both Midway (about 8 stops on the CTA) and O'Hare (about an hour by CTA). Trains on the Loop stop at the Merchandise Mart, which is virtually at the hotel's doorstep. Better signs in the Mart would help guests find the hotel after exiting the CTA train.
Rooms are small but comfortably appointed. Free Internet was great. Many rooms feature fabulous views of Chicago's lively canyon of art deco buildings and newer skyscrapers. The hotel's bar is an all-glass venue overlooking the river with the city's dazzling lights spread out before you. The spacious atrium hosts the hotel's "Regions" restaurant that features a nice variety of entrees, sandwiches, and salads.
The hotel's location could hardly be better. An easy walk to Wacker Drive, State Street, Dearborn and Michigan Avenues. The River Walk is just yards from the hotel.
A concierge desk sits in the lobby but is not always staffed. The front desk is very friendly, knowledgeable and helpful but somewhat understaffed. I had to wait in long lines to get information I needed.
The only complaint I have about the room is that the walls are a little thin. I could hear an annoying cellphone conversation in the neighboring room.
All things considered, this is a good Holiday Inn convenient to shopping, restaurants and a CVS drugstore.

name: InterContinental Chicago
title: “Good hotel”
text:
We stayed to the Intercontinental returning from a family holiday to Arizona ( stop over)
We checked in very late at nite and everything was fast and smooth, front desk offered a good deal for a suite upgrade since we travel with 2 kids.
Suite was a great option since had separate living room with sofa-bed and main bedroom with bathroom (very big) therefore we enjoyed some privacy and extra space for all the bags.
Room are clean and very well equipped. Decor is nice and classic unless the hotel could even improve and restyle the bathrooms that looked a bit dated.
Location is perfect on Micthigan Avenue and view from high floor magnificent!
We stayed at other property in Chicago (5 star) but we were not disappointed from the Intercontinental and we would return again.

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “Tolles Hotel in Super-Lage von Manhattan”
text: Wir sind mittags eingetroffen und konnten unser Gepäck aufgeben bis unser Zimmer fertig war (normal Check-in: 15:00 Uhr, unser Zimmer war schon um 13:30 Uhr fertig). Man geht aus dem Hotel raus und ist zu Fuß in ein paar Minuten am Broadway/Times Square, super Lage! Das Zimmer im 10. Stock ist groß, ebenfalls das Bett (King-bed) sowie der Flachbildschirm. Bad ist sauber, verfügt über einen Haartrockner,Seife, Duschgel. Überhaupt tolles Service: Kaffemaschine, kostenloser Internetanschluss (wir hatten den Leptop dabei), Bügelbrett und Bügeleisen im Zimmer. Im Foyer nette Mitarbeiter rund um die Uhr, auch nachts, kostenloser Kaffee, Obst, Kuchen. Frühstück sehr reichhaltig, sehr amerikanisch, sehr gewöhnungsbedürfig (kein Käse, keine Wurst, keine Brötchen, viel Flakes, Kuchen, Toast, Eieromelette, Marmelade, Honig, Obstsalat - kann alles mit auf das Zimmer genommen werden), eben andere Länder - andere Sitten. Das Hotel hat uns sehr gut gefallen, gerne wieder!

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “No guarantees on rooms”
text: Booked thru hotels.com. Thought I'd prepaid for two queens. Got there and sold out. Sorry. U get two doubles. Read the "fine" print is what I was told Hotel too busy and crowded. Elevators are horrible . Will not stay here again

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Ubicación !”
text: Excelente ubicación, servicio y comodidad. Las habitaciones muy amplias. Tuvimos una habitación de dos cuartos y un sofá cama. Súper cómoda. Una vista increíble desde el piso 40 en dónde estaba nuestra habitación. A la par de los teatros. Definitivamente me quedaría en este hotel en mi próxima visita.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “4th stay, and will return”
text: This was our 4th stay at this hotel. We were initially given room 308, a room in the back of the hotel. Unfortunately, right outside the windows are a bank of a/c units which run 24/7. We were switched to 306 after the first night and enjoyed the rest of our stay. The staff is always friendly and helpful. It is a great place and one can relax in Rick's Cafe any time of the day or night when you are not out doing things. Centrally located and very clean. We'll be back!

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Great Location, Tiny Room”
text:
The location of this hotel is perfect for anyone seeing a show on Broadway. It is such a short walk to the theaters, it is amazing. And, the location, though just a few steps from Broadway and the hubbub or Times Square is relatively quiet. There is a parking garage right next door and a diner on the other side if you are into that sort of thing. There is a subway stop very nearby, or a several blocks' walk to Grand Central Station so you can get to anywhere in the city by subway if you do not want to move your car. It is not too bad of a walk to other major sites. We actually took the subway to the Metropolitan Museum of Art but decided to walk back through Central Park and past Rockefeller Center. It was a long walk, but definitely doable.
The one thing is that the room is very small. I understand that is normal for NYC hotels, but for someone who has not stayed in an NYC hotel before, I wanted to mention when people say small, they mean small! We had difficulty setting our luggage out as there was really nowhere to put it. It was also hard to keep the toiletries in the bathroom as there was not much in the way of shelf or counter space. No room for a chair so we had to sit on the bed. I guess I was expecting the small room to be a bit bigger than it was. Trust me, it is small!
The decor was really nice and the free wine and cheese really made the hotel. It was nice to be able to just sit and relax in Rick's Cafe for a nice quiet break. There was also a small outdoor area off the main room that was nice to sit in. We never saw anyone use it other than us the 2 days we were there, so it was like our private dining area duing breakfast.
Overall, this place is a great place to stay.

name: Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile
title: “Everything else is great but the rooms”
text: Don´t get me wrong, it´s a nice hotel with a supreme location. It´s just that I´ve stayed at the Marriott Courtyard with equally good location and paid a $100 less. Even the room at the Courtyard was better, and the only thing it lacked was the five-star lobby that the Marriott has. The fitness room was nice and breakfast too, so overall it´s ok but not great.

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “würden wir wieder Buchen”
text:
Personal sehr fruendlihc. Zimmer ganz gut gesäubert ausser Bad und ein paar haare am bett. Kekse so wie beschschrieben (24std) gab es nur am anreisetag
Frühstück OK (Styropor Messer,Teller..) Jogjhurt,Früchte leckere Bagels
Lage ...serh Gut
Concierge sher nett erkärt alles!
Kaffee,Tee,Kakao 14h verfügbar
InternetTerminals gratis

name: Holiday Inn Chicago - Midway Airport
title: “Clean, practical, close to airport but not near much else.”
text: This was a business trip that was connected to an all day meeting, hosted at the hotel, which meant that I spent all day and night in the hotel. As far as the location, it was close to the airport with a complimentary shuttle which was great. Our group decided to venture out at night into the city for dinner and went the route of taking the free shuttle back to the airport and hopping a train. This was not a bad experience but it would have been much better if our location was closer to the downtown area. In the immediate vicinity, there was only a few chain restaurants and other hotels as well as lots of concrete and other hotels. With regards to spending the entire day in the hotel for a workshop, the service was so so. The coordinator had to keep calling catering to get salt, pepper, condiments, syrup, utensils. This was definitely a turn off. Another turn off was the $10 per day fee to use the gym, random! On the other hand, the food was pretty good as far as hotels go. Snacks were also provided and these included popcorn, soft pretzels, soda, water, iced tea, candy bars. I liked the variety which included healthy options. Overall, it was a practical place to have a small group meeting.

name: W Chicago Lakeshore
title: “No complaints”
text:
My husband and I had our wedding reception at the W Chicago City Center, and decided to celebrate our 1 yr. anniversary at the W Chicago Lakeshore. 
While City Center is more a business hotel, Lakeshore attracts the partyers. It's likely the hotel will be active (elevators zooming, guests in the hallways, doors closing) into the wee hours. 
The basic rooms are small and dark, but comfortable. Service was willing and friendly, accomodating everything we asked for. The lobby lounge is lively until closing, with great people watching. And the Bliss spa on the hotel's 8th floor is worth a trip -- friendly and unpretentious with *heavenly* services. 
Overall we'd visit again without question. But a quieter option may be City Center. It's slightly farther away from the action, but nothing a quick cab ride can't fix.

name: Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile
title: “had a great stay here”
text:
Loved this hotel! We got a fantastic rate thanks to DVD chicago hotel guy from tripadvisor ($109 a night). 
 Just got back from a 4 night stay. What can I say? Location, location, location! It's in a really good location, has a fantastic lobby, lots of elevators, no waiting. 
The concierges were extremely helpful and knowledgeable and there were usually 2 or 3 on staff at any time. We (myself and two other women) had absolutely no complaints about this hotel, particularly at the price we got. A little, liveable-with complaint-beds were too soft.
VERY GOOD DEAL FOR THE PRICE WE PAID!!!!!

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “hôtel sympa à New York”
text:
Bon hôtel à New York, bien situé. Le hall de l'hôtel est bien, la chambre était assez grande et propre. Le personnel était poli et nous avons pu réserver la navette aéroport depuis l'hôtel. Point négatif: la chambre n'était pas prête à notre arrivé, heureusement le service consigne est gratuit.
le petit déjeuner était inclus dans le prix de la chambre , mais pas exceptionnel (salle trop petite, pas beaucoup de choix)

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Great for Teens!”
text:
checked in on cinco de mayo for a 2 night stay. the valet and bell service was excellent, although we only used it upon check-in, as the garage is just a few doors east of the hotel entrance. security was very tight coming and going from the building.
we booked direct with the hotel in the hopes we'd get a good view, and we were rewarded. we'd asked for a smoking king and got a corner room with commanding views of times square and the hudson river. the room, wetbar, and bathroom were all very clean, well appointed, and overall a great base for seeing manhattan with teens.
2 adults in the king bedroom, and 2 16year old girls on the sofa bed left the room somewhat cluttered with bags, but not annoyingly so. the fridge and microwave came in handy for keeping and reheating the gargantuan NYC leftovers.
housekeeping did a fine job handling requests for extra towels and such. checkout was simple and quick on a monday morning.
i've stayed at both the marriott marquis, and the crowne plaza across the street, and the cleanliness and room size at the doubletree are the best of the three. 
while the hotel is very pricey, and doesn't represent a great value, it was worth every penny for us. the ability to let my somewhat sheltered 16 year old daughter and her cousin have the freedom to walk around times square without supervision, combined with the view, amenities and layout of the room, made it the right choice for us.
if you can afford it, and you have teens who've never been to manhattan, this is a great hotel.

name: The Hampton Inn Times Square North
title: “Hotel Hampton Inn New York”
text:
Eccellente posizione, a due passi da Time Square, Rockfeller Palace, Central Park.
WiFi gratuita in tutto l'Hotel, postazione Internet gratuita, ottima colazione; un po' affollata la sala, ma era in periodo di Pasqua e l'hotel era al completo.
Se dovessi capitare ancora A Ny andrei lì.
Il personale, , ma del resto tutti i newyorkesi, cortese, non si sforza per niente di parlare un inglese comprensibile. Solo e sempre il loro fastidiosio slang; comunque ce la siamo cavata egregiamente.

name: Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile
title: “Good location, but not great for the $$”
text:
Pros: Amazingly comfortable bed & pillows, nice bathroom, great location, helpful staff. 
Cons: Internet costs $15 a day more, slow elevators...had to take stairs 4 times from 14th floor due to how slow they were, very crowded, conventions always going on

name: Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile
title: “Just Loved it”
text:
We stayed for a long weekend 10/11 -10/14. Everything about the stay was perfect. The room was great, the view was great, the location was perfect. The front desk was knowledgeable and helpful as was the concierge. Great restaurant recommendations, helpful with directions. This hotel's location is ideal for seeing multiple parts of the city. 
As other reviewers stated the bathroom was on the smaller side, but it wasn't a problem for us. We didn't spend our trip in there and it was clean and everything was in good order. 
I honestly have not one complaint about this hotel.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Excellent choice!”
text: I found this hotel after reading about it on National Geographic. I was going to stay somewhere cheaper but decided to splurge for our anniversary. The hotel is very well positioned (steps from Time Square) for walking or taking the subway. The breakfast is great - fresh fruit salad, yoghourt, bagels, croissants, danish pastries, hard-boiled eggs, fresh fruit, fresh juices, coffee, tea, espresso, cappuccino, cafe latte, etc. The fresh fruit and hot drinks are available all day. The wine and cheese in the evening is also very good. There is a computer and printer available, and high-speed internet in the bedrooms. The staff are really friendly and helpful. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

name: W Chicago Lakeshore
title: “W Gets a B”
text:
I stayed at the W Lakeshore on June 25. I booked through Hotwire and paid 170 including taxes for the room-a deal for the area and time period (Taste of Chicago). This hotel is ideal for couples or young adults looking to have some fun. Upon checking in, I was greeted with great service, sometimes lacking when you book online. We had fast service for using their parking (it was $39 for 24 hours and allowed you to come and go). The hotel recommended using their service as it was the safest (I'd have to agree as the lot is located above the lobby). I took the time to be friendly to the car parking manager, Dan which proved beneficial as he allowed us to leave our car there extra hours if we needed, without charge, a service I saw others getting denied on. The bellman were fast and friendly and took the time to show us everything in the room. I agree that the hotel is beginning to show some wear-the curtains, hallways, and pool area was looking pretty run-down. 
The room itself was great, if you are a very private person, you will not care for the open-air feeling of the bathroom, a little embarassing if anyone but your loved one is sharing or in your room. The beds are great and our view was of the city versus the water but still nice. A great view of the lake can be seen from the 7th floor patio area. We checked out the bar on Sat night. I think anyone with a family would have been thrown off by the fact that the lobby basically turns into a bar at night-people and drinks everywhere. Getting to your room was no problem, but you have to take a special elevator to the 33rd floor to the bar. The view is great, a round of drinks was $18.
The Navy Pier is very close, we walked there a couple times and the beach is also nearby. Go to the Navy Pier if you are looking for informal, inexpensive dining. If you head right out of the hotel, you'll also find an Irish bar (I don't recommend as the staff seem to give minimal and rude service to anyone looking like they are from out of town) there's Chipotle and Pot Belly too for a quick lunch. For a longer walk you can check out the shops on Michigan Ave. All in all, it was a good experience not as luxurious as I imagined but the location is great, just don't waste your money on full price especially if you are planning to spend most of your time outside your room.

name: Hilton Chicago
title: “All I can say is amazing with Class...”
text: After reading some of these reviews I was scared to check into the Hilton Chicago. I don't know why people make up stories this hotel is amazing and so classy. From the time we checked in till we departed the staff was always there for us and always treated us with so much respect. Our room was ready when we arrived at 8am which was a bonus because we didn't have to hang around and our room was so impressive for the money, we had 2 bathrooms, you never get that no where unless you have a suite. When I come back to Chicago no doubt it will be back to this hotel I won't even think twice. Trust me when you walk through those front doors and through that lobby your jaw will drop at how beautiful it is, its classic with trimmings that are out of this world. Very impressed with this hotel and would give it more than a 5 star.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Amazing service”
text:
I took my wife to New York to celebrate our 35th anniversary. I wanted to be near Times Square and chose the Casablanca for our stay. I let them know ahead of time that it was our anniversary.
We got to New York early, arriving at the hotel before noon. I didn't expect the room to be ready, but they had one for us. As early as check-in you realize that this place is all about service. Everyone who works at the hotel makes a point to greet you and offer assistance. We were happy with the room - clean, tastefully decorated, great bed and a large bathroom.
We went out to get lunch and by the time we got back, there was a bottle of champagne in the room with balloons and an anniversary card made especially for us. We were blown away by their thoughtfullness.
We were completely happy with our stay at the Casablanca and would gladly stay there again. It's quaint, quiet and the staff is incredible.
Thanks to all at the Casablanca for helping to make our anniversary so memorable.

name: Chicago South Loop Hotel
title: “no complaints”
text: We stayed here for a wedding we attended that was near by. We had no compaints and it was a nice stay and Andrew and Jackie were awesome at checkout!

name: Fairmont Chicago Millennium Park
title: “As good as it gets”
text: Fairmont Chicago is beautiful, clean and in a great location. It is very close to Millenium Park and to Michigan Avenue. Navy Pier is also walking distance. The hotel itself has been recently updated, although it still has a charm that beckons to the past. We had a room that gave us views of the lake and the weekly fireworks. The staff was very professional and unobtrusive. I love this hotel and Chicago and will go back any chance that I get.

name: The Westin Chicago River North
title: “Rivernorth”
text: Nice hotel, good location. Great workout facility, Sam makes you feel very welcomed and keeps it very clean. Not huge, one of the best hotel gyms I've been to. Lots of people in hotel, on the river. That's all for now.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Hope To Go Back Next Year”
