text: Booked on the basis of TripAdvisor ranking and did not disappoint. Fantastic location next to Time Square. Excellent, Helpful Staff. Clean Bathroom. Comfy Bed. Excellent Continental Breakfast. Not to mention one of the cheapest places to stay in New York.

name: The Blackstone A Renaissance Hotel
title: “Great area of town, nice historic hotel”
text: We pulled up and they were on us like flys at a picnic, one was helping with the luggage, the other was parking the truck. We stayed two nights, paid $125 on priceline, which I thought was a good price. Asked several times during our stay for local information and the staff was very friendly and knew exactly where we needed to go based on our description of what we were looking for. This is within walking distance of several great Chicago landmarks. Upon check in, I asked for a city view, which they graciously granted! This is a great property. Room was recently updated, not the biggest room, but plenty of room for my wife and I. We didn't eat in the hotel, but the restaurant was packed most of the time we were there. Very classy place.

name: Hotel Sax Chicago
title: “A wonderful stay!!”
text: The hotel is elegant and beautiful and the service super friendly and professional. Everyone made us feel at home and very welcome. We will definitely be returning. The location is close to the Magnificent Mile and other attractions. The food is unbelievably good and the amenities are wonderful, including a bowling alley. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay!!

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Exceptional service”
text:
Despite being literally just steps from Times Square, the location is not the most outstanding attribute for this hotel ... rather, the service is. The front desk staff multitasks, one minute bellboy, the next waiter and then concierge. That actually works well for service though! As they remember the details about what guests like.
And, for those trying to save money, the 24-hour coffee/tea/cookie service available is a big plus, especially since it includes 10 or 12 kinds of tea and flavored coffee. I expected a regular ol' continental breakfast in the morning, but was pleased to find really fresh fruit and low-cal yogurt. And the afternoon wine & cheese service was unexpected ... my husband thinks we saved $30 each per day just in the snacks & drinks you don't always realize you need to grab!

name: InterContinental Chicago
title: “The most difficult review I have done”
text:
I have stayed in hotels and resorts all over the world, and never have I come across a review as difficult to write. I will start with the good, and then the bad. If i could give half stars I would give this place 3.5
The good
1) Location - directly on Michigan Ave
2) The rooms - nice, clean, bed was comfortable
3) Dining/Bars - lots of options, even though we are elsewhere
4) The doormen will get you a cab in less than 30 seconds
The Bad
1) They will nickle and dime you for every last penny, and i felt cheated
a) the mini bar has no price guide. I drank a diet coke from it and was charged $7.12 after tax. I understand you pay a premium for the mini bar, but this is above any beyond what should be legal
b) the gym they charge you $12.00 a day to use it, or $15.00 for your entire stay. I have never seen any other hotel in my life charge for use of a gym
c) parking is $57.00 a night. This is a high rent district, but this is still about $10.00 higher than average
d) our shower was 100% stopped up when we got there. They had to snake the drain during the first night
e) coffee had not been replaced from previous guest
Full disclosure - I paid $89.00 a night through priceline for this hotel this previous weekend. Would i come back for that price? Absolutely. Would I pay the $179 weekend advertised rate? No chance. There are other properties that make you feel more valued and you wont feel like they are trying to take every last dollar in your waller

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown
title: “Business travellers”
text:
Not a good option for single business travellers although would eb great if you had kids.
No good option for room service, which when you are travelling on business, you are more apt to using.I have been with Embassy in past and had great experiences although as a business traveller, it wasn't great.
Room smelt like a smoking room too and was dark with no light coming in the room. Which when you are working, it was quite dark.

name: The Blackstone A Renaissance Hotel
title: “Cost me extra to stay here”
text:
I stayed here as the media guest of a large company, and though I'm happy to report that the rooms are very nicely updated, they are also quite small and you're going to pay extra ($15) for DSL internet access. The beds are great and the door staff are very friendly. 
The only problem is that the desk staff are kids and barely know what they're doing. I had given them my credit card for incidentals and reminded them when I checked out, "Now, you're going to charge the room to THAT card (my sponsor's) and not THIS card, right?" Confused, 21 year old called over the 25 year old manager, who pointed out the card the room was supposed to be charged to, and I was assured there would be no problem. Sure 'nuff, I get home and find they've charged $600 to the wrong card and my checking account is now overdrawn. $100 in overdraft fees and hours of attempts to fix it, I'm still waiting for my money to be refunded a week later, and they've already charged the other card. Does that sound like a 5-Star hotel? Not to me.I won't be back.

name: Hotel Sax Chicago
title: “Love it!”
text: I stayed at Hotel Sax for a wedding and had amazing stay staff was friendly. Bed was comfortable bathroom was nice. Great location and great view. I would highly recommend it for out-of -towers. My next time I go to Chicago I will stay at Hotel Sax again.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Casacrappa”
text: My husband and I spent the day "touring" prospective hotels for an upcoming trip to the Big Apple and wanted to make sure we would be happy with our choice. I'm glad we did! We wanted to make sure we would be close to the Theater but away from all the hustle and bustle. This hotel fit that criteria, however, the hotel is in serious need of updating! The staff was friendly and accommodating, but the hotel, from the entrance to the tiny elevator and the dated hallways and rooms were anything but upscale from what we were expecting. We looked at several hotels in the area and all met or exceeded our expectations. I would not recommend this hotel. There are many other better choices in the city.

name: The Westin Chicago River North
title: “Best Starwood property we have ever stayed at!”
text: This hotel was fantastic! The people were consistently wonderful over the 10 days I was there. The business center was also a big plus and they were very accommodating with helping me to prepare for conference activities (which were at another hotel). The best experience was the gym, which was one of the best hotel gyms I have encountered, and Sam who manages the gym is an amazing personal trainer! He helped me kick up my work outs to a new level and this was all included as staying at the hotel. I can't recommend this place highly enough.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown
title: “Meh... it's alright...”
text:
This was probably our fifth or sixth time in this particular Embassy Suites. 
We keep coming back because of its location-- Just a few blocks of the tollway. Two more blocks to Michigan Ave. CTA Red Line station just a block away, so we could hop on and be delivered right to Wrigley Field. And my FAVORITE restaurants all within a minute's walk (Portillo's, Rain Forrest, and THE original Pizzeria Uno!)
But every time we're at this hotel, I tell my wife that if it weren't for her corporation's discount there's NO WAY we'd pay that kind of money to stay here. The breakfast lines were *unnecessarily* long... I don't see any good reason to force the made-to-order omelette line in to the same line as the buffet items (none of the other Embassy's we've stayed in does this).
Happily, we had the Hilton Rewards so that our Internet was free-- four people each with a laptop and a smart phone would have been a few more hundred dollars.
Our room was 7th floor overlooking State Street... and I did not remember staying awake all night from emergency vehicle sirens. But I think in the past we've always had rooms on the back side or off Ohio.
Elevators were a huge delay all weekend. Besides the smart children pushing every floor button, it sure seemed as though 4 elevators was NOT adequate for the volume of people in this facility.
And I was surprised by the volume of people just outside the front doors dragging on their cigarettes. There's not a lot of room when you enter this hotel. Their revolving door clutch is set very low, so the door mechanically slows down anyone who wants to escape the cigarette smoke. There is a serious gauntlet of hacking, shaking smokers who obviously aren't polite enough to keep their second hand habit to themselves. Yuck.
But,like I said, we'll probably be back just because it's so convenient AND my wife travels for her employment enough that we get discounts and perks. But maybe I'll check the rates and facilities for the Howard Johnson's up the street next time.

name: The Drake
title: “Historic Hotel in Downtown Chicago”
text: I stayed at The Drake for 5 days for work this October. The room was quite nice - I had a room facing the lake. The staff was helpful and the hotel seemed to be very well taken care of both in the main lobby and meeting rooms as well as the hotel rooms. The location is pretty awesome - close to a lot of shopping, restaurants and the lake. The restaurant was decent but not sure if I would eat there if I wasn't staying there. The one issue with the hotel is that it isn't really ADA compliant due to it being a historic building - I had a friend in a wheelchair who stayed at the hotel who did have some issues, that being said the staff was INCREDIBLY accommodating and did help him get through the different meeting rooms. Definitely a beautiful, old world hotel.

name: Club Quarters Chicago - Central Loop
title: “Great location”
text: As noted in other reviews, the rooms are small, but clean and quiet. The staff wasn't particularly friendly, but not unfriendly either. The pub restaurant on premises was excellent. The location was ideal, located close to train and bus routes.

name: The Westin Chicago River North
title: “Fine Service Hotel”
text: I was in Chicago for 4 days for a trade show. I was very happy that I staying at the Weston Hotel because it was not only convenient, but the quality of services offered at the Weston was top notch. I was especially impressed with the Health Club which was the best hotel gym I have stayed at. There was even a helpful fitness instructor named Sam who was so friendly and polite to all the guests who were working out. The continental breakfast in the Executive Room was also first rate and the views from this hotel, especially from the South Side are spectacular.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square NYC”
text: HOTEL MOLTO BELLO SOPRATTUTTO PER LA POSIZIONE, AL CENTRO DI NEW YORK, PERSONALE GENTILE E DISPONIBILE, VICINO ALLE FERMATE DELLA METRO E ALLE MAGGIORI ATTRAZIONI TURISTICHE. SE DOVESSI TORNARE A NEW YORK SOGGIORNEREI DI NUOVI LI'.

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “ottima posizione, ottimi prezzi per lo standard di New York”
text: Per la mia quarta visita a New York, ho soggiornato al Doubletree, posizionato proprio in una delle piazze più famose del mondo, l'hotel non mi ha deluso. Il mio appartamento al penultimo piano godeva di una vista molto bella, comfortevole, spazioso, accessoriato bene, potevo prepararmi da mangiare in maniera autonoma se lo desideravo, oppure bastava uscire nei dintorni per avere l'imarazzo della scelta

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown
title: “Convenient Location But Expensive”
text:
Stayed in this hotel for 2 nights for a business trip. Pros and Cons:
Pros- Great location, plenty for restaurants nearby, few blocks away from Millennium Park, near the train station, good breakfast, big rooms, free internet, gym and indoor pool available
Cons- Expensive (I paid more than $200), Hotel decor is quite old (I expected newer furnishings with the price I paid)

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS River North Chicago Downtown Hotel
title: “good stay”
text:
We just spent three nights here while visiting colleges and family. This looks like an older hotel 
but the room was clean and updated. 
Pros: Large room- this was one of the largest rooms we have ever stayed in with our family. The two of us and two teenage boys, plenty of room to move around, lots of floor space, two beds, arm chair, desk with desk chair...beds were very comfortable.
Separate sink and vanity- My favorite part, there was a full bath with sink, plus an extra sink and vanity outside bathroom. So many hotel rooms that we have stayed in don't even have a mirror with an outlet anywhere in the room for me to dry my hair while someone else is in the shower. It really made each morning go smoothly to have two sinks to use.
Free parking- sometimes they double park to fit cars in, but we had no trouble getting our car when we needed to get out; attendant was very friendly and helpful.
Good location- centrally located, McDonalds across street, grocery store one block away, lots of restaurants nearby.
They sold Shedd Aquarium tickets in lobby, saved us waiting in long line when we got there.
Cons: no free breakfast- coffee and granola bars put out each morning
no microwave or refrig. in room
a little noisy, could hear other rooms and noise from street.
small elevators/lobby elevator didn't go to part of the 3rd floor/had to use elevator outside
Overall I would recommend this hotel if you are fine with a basic, clean hotel.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown
title: “Great Hotel!”
text: Great Hotel experience. Great restaurant. Small exercise pool that families think is a recreational pool with jumping/diving and screaming kids. Room was pretty good and wifi excellent. Breakfast was very good too.

name: Marriott Chicago Midway
title: “Worthwhile stay unless....”
text:
This is a worthwhile stay unless you're really picky.
I can only think of a few negatives with this hotel. First, is that there is no free wi-fi. You can, however, access the wi-fi for free in the lobby though. Second, there's no free breakfast. Most of us, however, need to eat less anyway. Finally, I noticed a strange smell permeating through the hotel. It wasn't great, but it wasn't overwhelming either. My spouse, however, did not even notice a smell, so unless you're sensitive to smells, you probably wouldn't notice it either.
As for the positives: the first is that the hotel, which is very close to MDW, offers a great park and fly deal for its guests. We got a rate of around $150/night and it included parking for the 9 days we were gone. I doubt we could find a hotel room & parking anywhere in the area for less. If I'm wrong, please email me and tell me so. In this case, however, I don't think I am. They have a shuttle to the airport that starts at 4am (its essentially 24 hours), that is complimentary. We used it to take the train into the city for dinner AND to the airport for our flight. 
Second, the room and hotel were pleasant enough and clean. Our room included a very comfortable king size bed and a big bathroom with a great shower. We found the hotel staff friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable. We didn't use the pool or exercise facility available, but both looked sufficient. We did use the business center, which has computers available for use, including printers to print out your boarding pass. 
Third, there is a Starbucks attached to the hotel. There is also a restaurant and bar. 
Overall, I would highly recommend the hotel. It's the perfect place to stay when you need a place the night before a flight. It, along with many other hotels, is very close to the airport. While, the hotel isn't in a great area of town (when is an airport in a great area of town), I wouldn't imagine there are many problems with theft. Seemed pretty well lit and safe.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS River North Chicago Downtown Hotel
title: “Great weekend in Chicago”
text: Stayed for two nights the weekend of the Chicago Marathon. The rooms were clean and very comfortable! The location was great close to the subway station and a short walk to Michigan Ave. The staff was very friendly and helpful. We had a very positive experience and would definately stay again!

name: Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square
title: “Hôtel au style désuet (décoration année 70) mais super bien placé !”
text:
Les plus :
- Hôtel en plein cœur de Broadway (magique). Quartier très animé quel que soit l’heure du jour ou de la nuit. Et très bien insonorisé (ceci dit notre chambre au onzième étage donnait de l’autre côté de Broadway) 
- Station de métro, de taxi et de bus panoramique au pied de l’hôtel
- l’un des seuls hôtels à NYC qui propose 1 chambre pour 6 (canapé lit pour 2 dans le salon, deux lits doubles dans la chambre. Le tout séparé par une porte. Grande salle de bain commune)
- Le café et le thé mis à disposition dans les chambres (ne pas hésiter à faire remarquer à la femme de ménage que vous êtes 4-5 ou 6 car sinon vous allez vous retrouver dés le deuxième jour avec 2 dosettes de café seulement)
- la propreté 
- Attention à vos commentaires sur l’hôtel en arrivant ! Presque tous les garçons d’étage parlent français car souvent d’origine africaine. 
Les moins
- La décoration année 70.
- Le lit clic clac dans le salon – Pas très confortable selon mes enfants ! Petit conseil : faites le ouvrir par le garçon d’étage à votre arrivée et demandez à la femme de ménage de ne pas le fermer le matin ! Sous peine d’y perdre vos nerfs !
- Le prix du petit déjeuner. De toute façon sans aucun intérêt. Mieux vaut sortir et prendre un vrai petit déjeuner typiquement américain dans l’un des très nombreux restaurants prévus à cet effet. 
- les vendeurs de forfait de bus panoramique qui vous accostent en permanence dés votre sortie de l’hôtel. Si vous décidez de circuler selon cette formule, sachez que c’est très amusant le premier jour mais très lassant les jours suivants. Alors un conseil prenez la formule découverte one day ! Ou le taxi (super abordable)
- Les petites coupures en poche en permanence. Car chaque demande de renseignement se monnaye ! Ceci dit c’est culturel aux USA !

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS River North Chicago Downtown Hotel
title: “Friendly Hotel, Good Quality For The Price”
text: Just got back from a 4-day stay at this hotel. I was very impressed by how helpful and friendly the staff was. True, it's not a swanky, luxury hotel like you can find on Michigan Avenue, but it has everything that you need or want and very good quality for the money. My friend and I stayed in a suite, and my friend wanted to sleep on the pull-out couch. Well, the mattress was too lumpy, so we called the front desk, and right away they provided a roll-away, which worked perfectly. You also can't beat the location. I also found the staff to have a great sense of humor and provided service with a smile. I would definitely recommend it.

name: The Westin Chicago River North
title: “Nice downtown hotel in good location”
text: I liked this hotel alot. It was decorated very simply and elegantly. We were on the 3rd floor and did not have any special view, except for an office building across the street. There is alot of construction going on around the hotel and downtown in general. We had an issue with our shower but we didn't bother complaining about it. It was leaking and squirting out the sides. The shower head was also coming away from the wall. The caulking around the bathtub had some mold on it. It was difficult to see at first because the caulk was infact a black color (matched the black marble tiles). The only thing I did not like about this place was that it was extremely dark. The lobby area had very dim lighting and so did the rooms. But that is the style of the hotel. Our beds were very comfortable. I used the gym twice (there's a $10 fee). There was a good selection of equipment and it was clean. We had some drinks at the bar and some sushi one night. I wouldn't recommend eating/drinking at the hotel as they charge around 15% tax on any food/drink at the hotel, which would be the same in any hotel in Chicago. We didn't eat breakfast at the hotel either. There's an Einstein Bagel outside the hotel where we ate breakfast. There are lots of restaurants within a few minutes walk of the hotel. Room Service and Mini Bar was very expensive so we didn't use it. The front desk staff were friendly and even took off a charge for WI FI that my teenage son signed up for using his PSP without asking me. I appreciated that. The concierge staff were helpful with directions and helping us with dinner arrangements. Overall, we had a very pleasant stay at the Westin and would stay here again. If construction bothers you, check with the hotel beforehand because there was alot of construction going on right outside the hotel when we were there in July.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Fantastic weekend!!!!”
text: We had a weekend at this location for St Patrick's.....fantastic location and experience overall, service was great, rooms are clean......had the PERFECT view!!! As a Hyatt member I have never been disappointed, thank you!!!

name: Millennium Knickerbocker Hotel Chicago
title: “Good hotel...”
text: It is quite a nice hotel with a great location. Just one block away from the Hancock tower and the water place. Provides great access to shopping on the magnificent mile. The rooms are clean and good. Staff is helpful. The beds were a bit squeaky tough, maybe because of the frame. The mattresses are very soft, so if you like firm or semi soft; this might not be for you. No free internet in the room, free internet in the lobby.

name: The Drake
title: “Fun weekend in Chicago - The Drake was icing on the cake!”
text: My husband and I went to Chicago for a weekend in April and we had a great visit. The hotel was beautiful and grand, as was our suite. Reasonably priced, great mattress, sheets and towels. It was really terrific. From the front desk to the concierge, the staff was helpful and polite. Great location, with Lake Michigan a stone throw from the front door. Fun shopping and fabulous restaurants right around the corner.

name: Club Quarters Chicago - Central Loop
title: “Das Club Quarters, Central Loop liegt, wie der Name sagt, zentral in Chicago”
text: Die Zimmer sind sauber und modern eingerichtet allerdings nicht sehr groß. Da man sich allerdings die Stadt und nicht das Zimmer angucken sollte, ist das nicht schlimm. Das Hotel liegt in direkter Nähe zum Sears-Tower und zu 2 U-Bahn Haltestellen. Bis zum Millenium Park sind es 15 Minuten Fußweg. Wegen der zentralen Lage und der sauberen Zimmer nur zu empfehlen.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Another great stay.”
text: The Palmer House has exceptional service despite the large number of rooms and guests. The hotel lobby is a destination in itself. I stay at the Palmer twice a year (in Oct and Apr) for business and am never disappointed.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS River North Chicago Downtown Hotel
title: “Great Location!”
text: Just stayed for one night, free parking, 2 free breakfasts with foursquare, great location! I have never stayed downtown and I was extremely happy with my choice. Rooms are nice and modern and the pool is nice and cool. Beds are a little small, and the elevators are slow and hot. Called ahead to the restaurant with my pizza order and just strolled down there when we were ready, the service was great! Micheal is as helpful as everyone says :)

name: The Drake
title: “Old world charm, updated”
text: This was our first time staying at this well known Chicago landmark. Sometimes a visit to Chicago is shaped by the location of your hotel - the Drake is the perfect place to stay when you want to be on the north side of downtown. Walking distance to so many attractions, shopping and the Oak St. beach. In fact, with all the establishments on site, you could spend a lot of time in the hotel if you were so inclined. Public areas exude old-time Chicago charm, and the rooms are elegant as well as updated. During our stay the weather was very nice so we were gone all day. Walked to Lincoln Park Zoo and back, although there is a bus. We did not pay extra for the lake views, and we enjoyed our 4th floor view looking down at N. Michigan Ave. All in all, a wonderful time, and we will choose this hotel again for sure.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Great Hotel & Great Location”
text:
I booked this hotel because of the fab reviews and wasn't disappointed! I spent a long weekend here back in October 07 to celebrate my partners 40th Birthday and he was very impressed with the hotel as well. The staff were lovely and helpful and the cheese and wine on offer each afternoon/early evening was a very impressive extra touch! 
The location is fantastic and our room which was at the back of the hotel was perfect. Our friends did have a room on the front which they said was a bit noisy but I guess you have to expect that in NYC! 
All in all this is a great hotel and I would definately stay here again and I haven't done that with any of the other hotels I have stayed in in NYC!

name: Renaissance Chicago Hotel
title: “It was great!”
text: We stayed at the hotel 4 nights. The first 3 were on business. As a company we had over 500 people staying at the hotel . We had breakfast, lunch and dinner served. It was outstanding! The staff, service, rooms and food were top notch! The room was very clean and up to date. The staff was very helpful and always friendly. The location of the hotel is perfect. We road the "L" from Midway to the hotel and walked the rest of the time. Everything was within walking distance. We road the "L" out a little further and had no problems. We loved Chicago and the Renaissance Hotel! I can't wait to have a reason to go back!

name: W Chicago - City Center
title: “Extreme WOW at the W Chicago City Center”
text:
Back at the W again for 3 nights. I stay at Ws around the world as well as some other hotel chains but always always look forward to be being back at the W city center in Chicago. I got in Wednesday night and the service all the way from the door man to check -in and then the room itself are all emaculate. Slept like a baby..worked out at 7 and unlike many hotels the gym is big enough where it doesn't seem crowded even though there er equite a few people..
Alright..now to my favorite part..my girl Eden is on point all the time. I had called her yesterday before I got in from DC..she caled me back and asked me how many nights I was going to be in and what I wa slooking to do. That's all..I walk in this evening to my hotel and my next 2 nights are all planned out..dinner reservations..hottest club vip list..all the newest hotspots..and here the cherry..she even arranged for the complimentary Acura that all Ws provide to take my party to all the spots. I am a snob.I practiclaly live out of hotels, therefore expect the best. You can't do any better than this! Find out for yourself if you don't believe me. Please call on Eden..she ROCKS!!

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Can you tell why I would return to this hotel?”
text:
The Palmer Hilton is an institution in Chicago. I stayed there because it was the hotel selected by my company to attend a medical meeting. If I had been up to me to select (and pay) the hotel, I would have selected something less old-fashioned and a bit more contemporary. I felt like It was a place my dad would have fitted perfectly. 
On the plus side, the room I had was comfortable, WiFi and internet was very good (it seems to be rare among large hotel chains) and service was good. On the minus side, the decor is a mix of genre (old and new), not necesserarily a good one (just crossing the main hall is in itself a unique visual experience). The ambiance is a bit old-fashionned. Finally food is a really very pricey: a banana was $4 before service and taxes. If you want a banana, it would cost only $1,10 at the Starbucks located at street level. If you go there, you better bring your lunch or be ready to eat outside.
Finally, even though the immediate surrounding is not interesting, the location is excellent. it is just between to major metro lines and at walking distance of a lot of Chicago attractions.

name: Millennium Knickerbocker Hotel Chicago
title: “Very Contemporary room in historic hotel”
text:
This is a beautiful hotel with lots of orginal details. But once you enter your room you are in a very contemporary updated room. The bathroom is straight out of a design magazine. 
I live in Chicago so I knew the area well enough to park in the neighborhood and walk back because hotel parking is very expensive. This is a great location for tourists. Very close to the John Hancock Center, the beach, Museum of Contemporary Art, Water Tower Place and lots of Michigan Ave shopping.

name: Renaissance Chicago Hotel
title: “Wonderfull view and location!”
text: Nice hotel with great views of the chicago river! Within walking distance to the famous chicago theater, oriental theater, millenium park, house of blues,macy's, and great shopping! We took the blue line train directly from the airport for $2.50 a person,and got downtown in 25 mins! The stop off was only two blocks from the hotel. Room service is over priced as was the breakfast buffet in the restaurant, but there are so many restaurants to eat at close by, you won't have to worry. Felf very safe walking around a world class city!

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown
title: “Perfect for a family in a very convenient location”
text:
Despite a very tedious check in wait on arrival, the service and staff since then have been fantastic. The rooms are great for a family being clean and spacious. The children have thoroughly enjoyed the complimentary breakfasts, trying everything from the freshly cooked omlettes to the make your own waffles. My husband and I have also appreciated the complimentary drink and nibbles in the early evening. The hotel is very centrally located for shopping and transport links. I would recommend a high room away from the lifts to minimise on noise from the atrium.
The pool is adequate if a little chilly and there is no changing room so you are required to traipse back to your room in your costume and towel.
During our stay there was free Internet access which I understand is a summer special offer but this is extremely helpful. 
Overall great value for money and highly recommended. The staff are all delightful and happy to help.

name: Days Inn Chicago
title: “Only real problem”
text: Difficulty getting in and out of hotel with suitcases because of concrete pouring. Staff very nice and helpful.

name: InterContinental Chicago
title: “First Trip to Chicago”
text: Nice hotel. Rooms were on the small size but were nicely decorated. Staff was extremely nice and very helpful. Within walking distance of many attractions including Navy Pier, Millennium Park, Art Institute, and even Willis Tower. It is located on the Magnificent Mile and therefore is close to good food and good shopping. Would love to do a return trip.

name: Millennium Knickerbocker Hotel Chicago
title: “Great Location,service and comfortable rooms”
text:
Found hotel on internet.Looked up reviews and decided to book it.Excellent choice.
Great location,easy to get around.Comfortable room,especially bed.
Staff very helpful.Conciege makes great suggestions re whats happening in the city.We took his advice and had a great time ,both at a restaurant and show.
Will definately be back too Chicago and will stay again at same Millenium Knickerbocker Hotel.

name: Hard Rock Hotel Chicago
title: “Amazing staff/Amazing Establishment!”
text: Right when we checked in, we were warmly greeted by the wonderful staff and politely directed to our room. The room was unbelievably clean and beautiful with amazing views of the city. Each floor was a new experience and I will be coming back again soon. Thank you for making my night on the town, a memorable one!

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown
title: “Great staff and hotel”
text:
It really specializes in the American Girl Store promotion. It was wonderful taking 3 granddaughters there. Breakfast was excellent, staff was friendly, and who had time in Chicago to come back for happy hour. Never tested that. 
Convenient location, close to transportation, stores, and especially the American Girl Store.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Good overall but annoying extra charges and few amenities in standard room”
text:
The Palmer House is a very nice hotel, perfectly located for the Loop and Art Institute of Chicago (or walks along the lake and Grant Park). The people on the staff are extremely helpful and pleasant.
It's an older hotel, and the standard rooms are nothing special (although certainly pleasant enough). You can control your own thermostat, the beds are comfortable, and you get the things you expect in the bathroom. The TV in my room was large but "old style." I was surprised that there was no refrigerator or coffee maker, but you can ask and get a coffee maker for free. (Well, they said they usually charge but wouldn't.)
The "extra charges thing" is a bit annoying. Internet works fine, but they charge for it. (They were having some problem collecting charges, so they gave me 3 free days--probably because they weren't able to figure out who was logging on). The gym cost extra. I guess these things are typical of more expensive hotels, but I don't know if customers should just accept this since cheap motels usually provide free internet and a coffee maker and often even some recreation space.
The walls were a bit thin, and I could hear when the next room turned on the water (but I didn't hear noise...maybe they were just quiet or else the walls did insulate sound).
Overall, I enjoyed staying there. The Loop may not be the preferred place to stay for many people (restaurant scene in the Loop was disappointing...best places are elsewhere), but if you do want that area, it's perfectly located.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS River North Chicago Downtown Hotel
title: “chicago christmas vacation”
text: This was the first time in Chicago for me. The hotel is a great price! The location is perfect! Easily accessible to and from airport using the CTA transportation.Walking distance to most venues. The service is friendly, rooms are clean, The restaurant in the hotel is affordable and good. I would recommend this to anyone that wants to go to Chicago with a budget.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Very nice property”
text: Very nice, clean rooms. Friendly, courteous, helpful front desk staff. A bit of a hike to Navy Pier to the conference I was attending. Would stay here again.

name: Days Inn Chicago
title: “good”
text: The handicap bathroom was great over all, but the shower was terrible for me. Had I needed to use the shower again I would have asked for a shower bench to put in the tub/shower, I hope there would have been one available. The breakfast room set up is horrible for someone in a wheelchair. I was disapointed that not one employee in the breakfast room offered to assist me to get my breakfast, very frustrating! I understand that parking is a real problem in the city, but the hotel could some how comp the guests for parking a little bit, how about a reimbursement on the bill for 1/2 the parking?

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “The perfect base for a fun weekend”
text:
This hotel is well-located and has lots of things to recommend it. It is the largest Hyatt Regency in the world but manages to personally interact with guests in a welcoming way that would be more expected from a much smaller establishment. There are a few negatives: the wooden corners of our bed were pointed and protruding, so my shins got dinged up every time I forgot to give them a wider berth; there were no toiletries in the room upon check-in, but that was quickly remedied by a phone call; there was no tub; the concierges don't seem to be able to magically get reservations at high-end restaurants the way concierges in other major cities often can; and you can't store items in the minifridge. That last issue is relevant because you will be bringing back leftovers from the incredible Giovanni's stuffed pizza place about 3 blocks away. (Do not miss this Chicago-style pizza!)
Other positives: the view from the west tower toward the water is wonderful day & night, especially if you are lucky enough to wake up to a snowy morning. There were individual reading lights on the headboard. The shower was hot and had perfect pressure. The word of the week on Facebook will get you free internet, a reduced parking fee, and possibly also another surprise...be sure to visit this hotel on social media! There is a well-stocked grocery store just behind the hotel. I had drinks at the Irish pub and Big Bar on the premises; both were fine. The Art Institute is just a 15 minute walk away on Michigan Ave, as is the seasonal public ice skating rink. And the hotel is easy to reach on the blue line from ORD...just take it to the Clark/Lake station for $2.25 and walk approximately seven blocks east and one block north.
One more thing...if you love the blues, I recommend both Buddy Guy's Legends and Kingston Mines. The latter has two stages with music until about 4 a.m., which made me aware of yet another hotel positive: it was quiet enough to sleep in late on Sunday morning. ;~D

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown
title: “Pleasant Trip, nice hotel, good location, decent price.”
text: Me, my wife, my 2 children (2 and 4) and my mother stayed here for 2 nights. Kids liked the pool. Not huge but enough room even when other people were there. Breakfast was great, as well as the free drinks from 5:30 to 7:30. I made sure I was down there for that. Restaurant in the hotel was nice. Price for dinner for all of us was not much more than the price we paid for lunch at Shedd Aquarium. We took the subway just down the street 1 block to Shedd. Grocery store right across the street from hotel. Would stay again. Did not pay for the wi-fi because 4G service was great on Sprint.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown
title: “Last time I will stay at this hotel”
text: Pool was closed and I was not told at check in. I had heard that you could go down the street and use another hotels. The weather was cold enough that was not possible. Organization as a whole was not good. Breakfast in the morning was total chaos. Happy hour was not happy we left after one drink. My stay was just not comfortable. One more thing- I am sick of the hotel over charging for WiFi. Give it to us!

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Good downtown location, good service”
text: Pleasantly old-fashioned decor. Friendly and competent service. Room was large and quiet.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile
title: “Great Service and Clean Rooms”
text: Hotel was nice, clean and in a great location. Close to lots of restaurants. And only one block off the mile. The only complaint I would have would be the beds were to hard for me but that is my personal preference. I would stay again. All the staff were very accommodating and friendly. Booked it through there site and got free parking at the same rate as the online booking places. They had free internet that is a big help, a little slow but it did the job. It also had a mini fridge, microwave and coffee pot.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown
title: “Beyond our expectations!”
text: We checked in on Xmas eve, staying 2 nights. What a great stay! Check in was a breeze, the front desk staff was excellent, very friendly. The breakfast was great since it was included in the price - the made to order omelets were great, as was the chef cooking them (quite friendly)- wished they had waffles, the pancakes and french toast were a bit undesirable. The pool was a bit green and the spa foamy, both definately needed to be shocked... the pool was open til MIDNIGHT and opened at 5am (for those who didn't mind the imbalance of chemicals). Our room was OUTSTANDING - newly renovated. I didn't like the pillows, however, and had a hard time sleeping (too soft for me). Overall, all 4 of us raved about the hotel and the staff just put it over the top for us!

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Good stay, great location”
text:
I stayed in the city for a few days in November while my husband attended a conference. The location is fantastic, right at the base of where the fun shopping begins. Our room was very clean and on an upper floor facing the river and city which was beautiful. The room felt spacious and had all the necessary amenities--large TV, mini-bar, comfy bed, iPhone charger, safe, coffee maker, large desk area, and several drawers for clothing. The bathroom was on the smaller side but was clean and also had a makeup mirror. 
The hotel itself is huge, with a giant atrium, restaurants, bars, and a little gift shop. 
One reason that I could not give this hotel 5 stars is that it caters to the business traveler--the convention types. it gives you just exactly what it thinks you might need and nothing extra. it's those smaller touches that keeps this hotel in the 4 star class. if you can handle that then I think it's a fine hotel. 
The staff was always friendly and helpful. In fact, a coworker left his iPod in his room and was notified later that housekeeping had found it. We had yet to check out of the hotel so we were able to retrieve it for him.

name: Hard Rock Hotel Chicago
title: “This hotel was just average”
text: Very loud ! Great location. Upgraded to a corner king . Nice views of the city.

name: Hotel Allegro Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Close to Attractions but noisy!”
text: Having stayed at another Kimpton property in Chicago (the Palomar), I have to say the Allegro is not quite as nice. Although the location is fantastic, only a few blocks from many attractions as well as Grant Park, and the lobby decor is great, we found the room to be a bit on the small side. The main problem I had was the noise. We could very clearly hear conversations of those in the next room as well as ...ahm... other sounds at night. Also, the mini bar fridge hummed loudly and about every fifteen minutes would go into overdrive with the humming then quiet down a bit. We were in town for Lollapalooza so we weren't in the room much so it didn't matter that much, but if you are in for business and need a good nights rest, I'd probably choose the Palomar over the Allegro. All of that aside, the room was good value for money, very clean and the staff all very friendly and helpful.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Great location. Beautiful Lobby. OK Room & Service.”
text:
We were very excited for our stay at the Palmer House in downtown Chicago as we had heard wonderful things about it. Our stay started off very rocky. We called ahead to make arrangements for the room because we were going to arrive very late (after 11:00 pm) with three small children (7, 5 & 1). We spoke with a woman at the front desk and asked that we have a pack n play or crib ready in the room. I was told "no problem". I also asked if they had down pillows or comforters. I was told that yes they did. I asked if one of the beds have the down removed. She replied "Would you like us to make the entire room down-free? That would be no problem." I told her that would be wonderful.
Upon our arrival at about 11:10 I asked the man working the front desk if they had prepared the room for us with a crib and removal of the down comforters and pillows. He said that they had not, but did see that the request was noted on our reservation. He said they'd have someone up right away. 
We went to our room and did our best to settle in given that we could not put our baby in a crib. We removed the down pillows and comforterfrom one bed and put them in a pile while we waited for housekeeping to arrive. After 20 minutes I attempted to call the front desk from the phone located between the beds. The front desk answered and I asked for a status update on the cribs and pillows. I received no answer and the front desk hung up. About 10 seconds later, I received a call from the front desk asking if I had received the materials I requested. I stated that I had not, but then the man at the front desk hung up. It became apparent to me that they could not hear me and that the phone receiver must be broken. They called back right away and I answered the phone on the desk (thankfully they had two phones). The man at the front desk seemed shocked that they had not yet delivered the crib and pillows and said that they would be up right away. I also informed him that the phone between the beds was apparently not working. (The defective phone was not replaced during our stay).
15 minutes later we received a knock on the door. They had brought the crib, but no pillows. We informed housekeeping that we had also asked for a down-free room. They left and came back about five minutes later with the pillows. So, we got off to a rocky start to say the least. (Note: a previous review stated that the Palmer House charged extra for a crib. That was not the case for our stay as the crib was free).
The room itself was ok. Not very big, but that's to be expected in downtown Chicago. It seemed a bit dated with a tube TV. The heating/cooling was not the best. We had to turn the thermostat down to the coldest setting possible just so we didn't burn up. We also cracked the window to cool it down a bit. (It was 29 degrees outside). The lobby was BEAUTIFUL! There were many people just lounging around having drinks and taking in the beauty of the place. 
The location was GREAT! It was just across from Milennium Park. There was a Starbucks, Corner Bakery, McDonalds and Dunkin Donuts all right there for breakfast. We were also very close to the El, which was great for hitching a ride to the north end of the Magnificent Mile, but it was quite loud. The Concierge was helpful providing directions and a map of downtown. 
Unfortunately, the Palmer House charged an arm and a leg for internet and offered wired only in the room. Too bad iPad/iPhone users. I utilized the 3G on my cell phone instead. Not sure why these older hotels don't get with the times. Strange that your cheaper hotels include internet for free. I guess if you're willing to pay for an expensive hotel, you don't mind the extra for internet (and parking for that matter, which was not cheap).
On day two we checked out the swimming pool. It was a decent size and had both a shallow and deep end. Unfortunately, someone had detached the safety rope dividing these two sections making it too easy to meander to the sloped part of the pool on the way to the deep end. Not the safest thing for kids. The water was warm enough. They seemed to have a bit of a drainage problem on the pool deck as there was a LOT of standing water that was very cold. They had plenty of towels for guests to use and a number of chairs and tables.
We didn't try the restaurant and opted instead for delivery from Giordano's Pizza. 
Overall, we had a nice stay, but it was not nearly as good as previous stays in downtown chicago. I do not think we'll be back.

name: Millennium Knickerbocker Hotel Chicago
title: “Our Third Five Night Stay, Another Wonderful Experience!!”
text:
Our first two visits were in 2009, dealing with the death of our closest friend, and the staff came to treat us like supportive friends. Also what a great location and fascinating place to stay!!
Our late April, 2010 visit, this time entirely for pleasure, was another AAAAA+ wonderful experience. From the Doormen, Desk Clerks, Managers (Reservations/Food Service) to the Bar Tenders, Waiters and Concierge's service (please none of you ever leave), the friendly staff is there to help make your stay the best. We also loved the new menu in the dining room and how it is also available in the bar area. Who also could forget the fine piano entertainment? Hope he stays too!!
We also love the history of the hotel...the people who have owned it and stayed there...the Lobby, Bar and Ball Room must be seen, (wow) including the first lighted Ball Room floor in Chicago. Looks great for receptions. Finally, the rooms are comfortable, cared for and well decorated.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Awesome Staff and Fun location”
text:
My younger sister and I recently stayed at the Casablanca while visiting N.Y. for her 18th birthday/Graduation gift. Everything about the hotel is great! The "guys" were so friendly and helpful while at the same time being very professional. THey went out of their way to make our stay comfortable and fun. The room was nice and the breakfast was great to have available (ok, so we only got up in time to eat it once!) Having the wireless internet connection was over the top, since I sent pictures home daily of our experiences. The hotel is in a great place to see and do everything and it was fun to be near all the excitment of Times Square (litterly right at the door). So many shopping opportunities!
I highly reccomend staying here and even for all my Dad's worrying, we felt very safe. 
Just a note to all: take the subway.......what looks like close on the map.is not so close expecailly if you get lost like we did walking. The subway is right there and takes you right to the major places.
We had a wonderful time and made many memories!

name: Renaissance Chicago Hotel
title: “Excellent Hotel, Great Value”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel about five or six times. It keeps getting better. I recently stayed the weekend before Jan 1. The hotel was crowded, but everything was perfect and service was as gracious as ever.
I was upgraded to one of the larger club rooms. It was wonderful. The room was huge with a large bay window with a fantastic view of the river and the new Trump Tower under construction. The bathroom had a separate large soaking tub and shower. The bed was luxurious and very comfortable. 
Service was excellent. The hotel offers a complimentary shoe shine service which is especially great in the winter. I called to have my shoes polished over night and they were returned gleaming in 10 or 15 minutes.
The location is excellent. You're about a block or two from all of the wonderful shopping on Michigan Ave and just around the corner from the flagship Macy's on State Street. 
The health club, pool, and spa are very nice. They've were renovated last year. The equipment is excellent and they actually have a good selection of free weights in addition to the usual machines.
I ordered room service for breakfast and everything was delicious and served very promptly. 
The high-speed internet service was fast and dependable. It was a little pricey, but no different that other hotels I've stayed at.
Chicago does have other and even more upscale choices such as The Peninsula, Four Seasons, Ritz-Carlton with the Mandarin Oriental and Shangri-la on the way. A night at one of these hotels will easily be 2-3 times the rate at the Renaissance. They are beautiful and luxurious 5-star hotels, but it's hard to justify the extra cost when you can get affordable luxury at the Renaissance.
I can't think of anything negative about this hotel. Highly recommended.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Great Hotel - Very Convenient”
text: Just got back from a weekend in Chicago where we stayed at The Palmer House. Our room was small, but since we weren't in it that much it wasn't that big a deal. The hotel is lovely, with all the historical details in the lobby beautifully maintained. Everyone we encountered was so friendly, and the festive air really put us in the Christmas spirit.

name: Hotel Allegro Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Modern & Fresh”
text:
This is one of my favorite hotel experiences by far. It smells great when you walk in, and it's right next to the theatre, if you're interested in going. There's one hour each day (either at 5 or 6 pm) where they host a happy hour - sangria, beer, and wine - for those who are 21+. The rooms are gorgeous and outfitted in a modern style. At first glance they seem a little small, but you have everything you need and all the space you need. Besides, it's downtown Chicago! Get out and do something! (I highly suggest Second City!)
It's an older edifice that's been completely gutted & remodeled. It has class and charm!

name: The Drake
title: “Great Location”
text: We really enjoyed our stay here and would love to come back. It has a great location about a half a block away from Michigan Ave. All the staff, from the front door to the front desk, were great.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Nice but nothing spectacular”
text: Stayed 4 nights for a combined business meeting/couples getaway. This is a busy hotel that hosts a lot of conferences and it definitely has the "conference hotel" feel, despite being newly refurbished and more upscale than many conference hotels. Our room was a standard king, rather small with almost no storage. But the bathroom was very nice and we liked the decor. I would say the best quality of the hotel is its location. Overall we had a pleasant stay and no major complaints but I'm not this place warrants a AAA Four Diamond Award.

name: Renaissance Chicago Hotel
title: “excellent”
text:
When we bid on Priceline for $150 per night for a weekend getaway we were delighted to get this hotel. It is right on the Chicago River cnr of State Street - within moderate walking distance to almost everywhere. We walked to Sears Tower, the Shed Aquarium, and all the way up to Millennium Pier.
The complimentary in-room Starbucks coffee was a treat, as was the good quality (Lather Inc) toiletries in the beautiful bathroom. Pity that breakfast was $18 each (so went a few blocks south and enjoyed "Corner Bakery" instead). The lounge bar is very reasonably priced for a relaxed/casual dinner.
Would definitely recommend AND return.

name: InterContinental Chicago
title: “Great location, great view, small room”
text:
I booked this hotel on hotwire for a great rate of $113/night. When we got there, she upgraded us to the historic tower. The room was on the 32nd floor and had a great view. It was, however, very small. I had to climb over the armchair to get in and out of my side of the bed. The bathroom was gigantic, though, which was nice.
I am allergic to feather pillows, so I called down for foam pillows at 11:15 pm. It took about 45 minutes to get them, which I thought was excessive.
Other than that, I liked this hotel. It's in a great location for exploring Chicago, the conceirge was very helpful and friendly, you could check in for your flight in the lobby, and the pool is really nice.
I think this hotel is worth the good hotwire rates everyone seems to be getting. I think I would have been disappointed if I had paid more for it, though.

name: W Chicago - City Center
title: “Good Location - and that's all”
text: Stayed at the W as a meeting site, got an inexpensive room rate and an experience that matched. Would never want to stay again if could avoid, at any price. W City Center was a poor venue for a meeting site. Staff was courteous, but seeing staff trying so hard to make everything look so cool was painfully adolescent. Lobby, halls, room all dark and noisy. Room was as small as a good sized master bath. Food service was terrible - looked flashy but cold and tasted plastic. I would not again choose to attend any meeting or seminar held at this hotel as was too unpleasent of an "experience".

name: The Drake
title: “Wonderful Time at The Drake Hotel!”
text:
My wife and I spent the week in Chicago to celebrate our 15 year wedding anniversary. We decided to stay at the Drake Hotel based on reviews and reputation. We were not disappointed. We were upgraded, and were given a celebratory chocolate cake (which was delicious). 
Our room had a great view of the lake, and had plenty of space to stretch out and relax, plus two large flat screen TVs. We ordered room service once for breakfast, and very much enjoyed the Eggs Benedict and French toast. The concierge was helpful on several occasions and save us an hour waiting at Geno's East with priority seating.
We look forward to the next time we can stay at the Drake.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Beautiful hotel but service was a bit sporadic”
text: Just returned from a mother daughter weekend in Chicago...two adults and two children. We arrived a bit early on Friday to check in so we left our bags and were to receive a text when the room was ready - we realized around 6:00 we never received a text. When arrived back at the hotel and got to our Executive Floor room - housekeeping was currently in our room so we were never sure if the room was ready early or not...she did however turndown one of the 2 double beds. If this was a turndown service we never received it again. We decided to head upstairs for the appetizers from 5-7 but got there a few minutes before 7 and it was all cleaned up - we were able to grab a few apples and sodas. We stayed in Friday and had local pizza delivered and watched a movie available from the service on tv. Breakfast was included on the floor above and it had so much to choose from but with a conference there it was very tight in the small food area and not much seating available. We spent the morning out and came back for a few hours and left again - that day we did receive new towels but the trash was never taken nor were the glasses cleaned or replaced with new ones. Sunday breakfast was a mad house with no where to sit - people eating at the credenzas in front of the elevators, kids running around, etc. Overall we had an excellent stay and the room was very comfortable and beds very comfy but just found the housekeeping service to be a bit off...the bellmen and valet were all excellent. We could hear guests in the room beside ours at various times of the day and they were not being "loud" - there were a few places in the room that needed cosmetic help such as wallpaper peeling and this was the case in the hallways too. Overall a beautiful hotel.

name: W Chicago - City Center
title: “Not bad, not great”
text: Stayed for two nights in late March. 1st night was in a Wonderful room--very small with my wife and I sharing a full sized bed. Bathroom is more of a lavatory. We asked and were upgraded the following night to a MUCH nicer room (Spectacular?). Good size, comfortable bed and couch, adequate space for 2 people to unpack their bags. Decor is nice. Workout facility also good. A nice but not spectacular stay. We have had better luck with the Westin brand in general.

name: Renaissance Chicago Hotel
title: “If you stay don't park here, you will be charged for that plus internet service.”
text:
I rented a room there for 2 nights , thinking that well usually all people park at a hotel , if they have driven or rented a Car. As a paying customer you would not think they would charge you to park your vehicle. WRONG ! Be expected to pay for that BIG.
Also think internet access is free, think again there is a charge for that as well.
Next time I will look for a reasonable hotel, with out all the rediculous prices tacked on.
Don't beleive me, call them first upon staying there.

name: Renaissance Chicago O'Hare Suites Hotel
title: “Great Airport Hotel”
text:
This is a terrific airport hotel. All of the amenities of a typical airport hotel, but in a very spacious, clean and inviting setting. Breakfast was great, there is a Starbucks on site and the rooms are very spacious, well appointed and extremely clean. Within 100 yards of a Blue Line stop and an easy cab/train ride into the city. 
4 Star value as well.

name: Millennium Knickerbocker Hotel Chicago
title: “Our stay at the Knickerbocker made our first trip to Chicago a memorable experience!”
text:
Prior to our visit in Chicago, I did not know anything about the city. I frequently use TripAdvisor.com to research and plan my trips, and this is how I found out about the Millenium Knickerbocker. We stayed for 4 nights, which reduced the price per night due to an online hotel promotion. We are normally budget hotel frequenters (i.e. Hampton Inn). I cannot say enough good things about this hotel.
1. Accomodations: we booked a superior king (which is a corner room). When asked to upgrade to a room with a view, they gave us a street view of East Walton Street (where the hotel front faces). Although disappointed at first, we loved the room. There's enough space for two people and we experienced no outdoor noise from the street. It is a small one-way street so there's not a lot of thru-traffic. The bed is very comfy, the modern decor is funky and the bathroom is cool with the big shower stall and rainfall shower-head. It felt like I was in a spa bathroom.
2. Service: everybody was extremely helpful. I read a Frommer's Chicago city guide book cover to cover before arriving, but we also relied heavily on the concierge staff for many suggestions. Les and his staff were fabulous! They are so knowledgeable about the city - all the restaurants suggested were excellent and their sight-seeing tips were so helpful. Tjhey secured us reservations for places that weren't in my little guide book and we loved them! If you don't know Chicago, use their hotel concierge service for suggestions.
3. Location: the hotel is located on the northern end of Michigan Avenue, but it seemed so close to everything. On a nice day, you can walk the Miracle Mile down to Grant Park or the Chicago River in 20 minutes. You are near so many restaurants and shopping, all within walking distance. The Hancock Observatory is 1 block away (all the locals said to go there instead of the Sears Tower). We did not rent a car (the price is high for parking at the hotel or basically any hotel) and just cabbed or walked everywhere - so worth it.
4. Drawbacks: their restaurant menu (and room service) are a bit pricey for me. The food was good but I would prefer going someplace nearby for breakfast instead of dining in.
You will always read good and bad reviews based on personal experience, but ours was nothing but excellent. I recommend staying here and will stay here again on our next visit to Chicago.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “a must for any trip to New York”
text:
Trip advisor member from Merseyside, England
My Husband and I and our two freinds stayed for 3 days at this Boutique hotel which has it all, the rooms a little small but spotlessly clean and comfortable,and the enormous shower is great, the location is perfect. The hotel staff are superb, I broke a tooth on my visit, I asked if they new of a dentist, not only did they advise me of one, but spoke to the dentist personally, (even though he was off duty), and made me an appointment the next day before his surgery started, this was a godsend to me at that time, so a big thanks for that.
There is daily cheese and wine in the evening, a lovely touch, and also FREE internet use, which was just great. The adjoining restaurant, Tony's, was also very good, the meals are of a massive portion, and enjoyed every mouthful. 
So all in all an extremely fabulous time in New York, made by the fabulous time we spent at the Casablanca hotel, can't wait 'till we visit again, 'cos we would certainly stay there again.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Great Little Hotel”
text: This couple highly recommend this smaller, less crowded, quiet hotel within 1/2 block of TimeSquare. Service is excellent;Continental AM and PM snacks are a plus.Rooms are not a Marriott size but very comfortable.Would return..

name: Hotel Sax Chicago
title: “Geat Stay Friendly staff”
text: We recently traveled to Chicago for the first time for a weekend getaway. We decided on the House of Blues Hotel because of location and reviews. We also wanted to go to the Gospel Brunch next door on Sunday. The hotel was booked full the night before, but they were still able to let us check in early. The staff was very friendly. The room was very nice and the bed was comfortable. The only downer to the room was the mini bar, which like all mini bars is way overpriced. When you pay that much for a room, they should just give youa bottle of water! The bathroom was fine, but the tub / shower was more of a shower. You would have to work hard to fit into the tub. It was 1/2 to 3/4 size. Everything else was good. The bell station was helpful and kept our bags while we looked around some more on Sunday. We had a great stay.

name: W Chicago - City Center
title: “Overall, a very disappointing stay!”
text:
Many of the aspects of our stay were so bad as to be a little funny. We could only laugh about it afterwards, though.
We booked our room through priceline. When we arrived we were greeted promptly, and sent straight toour room. This has to be the designated priceline room. Directly across from the elevator, it took our breath away. Actually this was because the room was so, so small that a full breath removed the oxygen from the entire room. A path about 3 feet wide around the "queen" bed was all the space that there was. To this add: a heat register that made so much noise as to make sleeping difficult, a wall mirror which had apparently come off of its mounting, and just leaned against the wall, an inoperable phone (probably to prevent complaints). I really can't imagine where we would have put our luggage.
Needless to say, we went down to the desk to make other arrangements. We were offered a couple of extra cost upgrades. We opted for the "mega-king" which was smoking, but we were desperate. That room was actually quite nice, but unbelievably hot. We slept with the heat off, and the window open, and we were still warm. There was no hair dryer in the room. A phone call to housekeeping and 20 minutes produced a hair dryer which didn't work. We gave up before the second replacement arrived.
A few positives: The "style" department brought us a very nice deodorizer to help neutralize smoke odors - worked great. The second room was quite spacious, and yes the toiletries were nice.
However, it is impossible to offset all of the other problems. It is very difficult to accept this hotel as a four star establishment. They have a serious quality control/maintenance issue at this facility. Until this is resolved, we (and everyone else) should stay away

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS River North Chicago Downtown Hotel
title: “The location can't be beat”
text: Time and time again I return to this hotel when traveling on business. The location is awesome with many wonderful restaurants and bars within walking distance. The rooms are kept clean and the maids do a good job of freshening them up daily. I also looked at their website and found a coupon to be upgraded to a suite for free which was a nice plus as the room was more spacious and included a refrigerator and a small couch, chair, and table area. Bathroom was nice and clean, bed was comfortable, can't complain about much. It is a little annoying to navigate as the hotel is in two building and only connects on the 4th floor. Also shower pressure and temperature wasn't great and I found it difficult to get the thermostat on a good temperature and was constantly adjusting. Staff is nice and helpful and parking is free which is a good cost savings if you have a car. The hotel isn’t perfect and the hallways are semi-dated but the rooms are refreshed, comfortable, and clean. I’ll be back.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile
title: “Four Points is OK but there is better out there”
text: We stayed at the Four Points because we were making a trip with our 6 year old to the American Girl store and this hotel is recommended on the AG website. We booked the AG package and were given everything promised. Our daughter loved the "extras" that came with this package and she was treated like an adult. She also loved the swimming pool and the breakfast at the hotel was one of the best that I've ever seen. Other than that, the room which was promised to be a king had a smaller bed and the room itself was extremly small and really nothing special. The lobby is very small also. It is 7 blocks from Water Tower Place (about a $6 cab ride). This isn't one of the grandest hotels in Chicago, but it met our needs for the night.

name: Renaissance Chicago O'Hare Suites Hotel
title: “Very Nice "Airport Hotel"”
text:
We needed a hotel near the Airport. The Renaissance was Great.
Their shuttles had longer hours of opperation than other hotels. (that we needed)
The room was nice , and the staff was friendly.

name: Hard Rock Hotel Chicago
title: “disappointed...”
text: overall, the hotel is pretty nice. however, it is WAY overpriced. the food in the restaurant was average at best and unbelievably expensive. my husband and i ate breakfast one morning and just for the 2 of us, it was $40. we both had eggs, bacon and potatoes. RIDICULOUS. they had the worst coffee i have ever tasted in my life, hands down. the room was nice and clean, but BEWARE THE REFRIGERATOR!!! they have sensors in them, so if you so much as MOVE a drink, your card on file will automatically get charged. we read the sign (after picking up and inspecting the wine and liquor selections!) that stated you would be charged automatically, even if you don't drink the stuff. just for taking it out of the fridge!!! keep in mind, the vodka was $35 and the size of a can of Coke, so we were charged for it. thankfully, we had a "discussion" with the people downstairs and they took it off of our bill, since we could prove we didn't drink it. it was just frustrating. the hotel was just average, but NOT WORTH THE MONEY!

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “A very good experience!”
text: This hotel is one of the oldest in the city, having been rebuilt after the fire of 1871. It was a great experience not only in being able to stay downtown in Chicago but to be surrounded in history where I stayed. I highly recommend this establishment!

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “An oasis steps away from Times Square!”
text:
This was our second visit to the Casablanca and whenever we need a hotel room in New York this is where it will be. Not for us the sterile and impersonal chain hotels, here you are treated as an individual...a guest. From the moment we arrived we felt at home. Of course the wine and cheese and champagne reception six nights a week isnt the only reason why I want to return! There is the friendly staff who go out of their way to give you directions, recommend restaurants, and help make the trip what you want it to be. The breakfast of bagels, various cereals, cream cheese, fruits, eggs, different teas and coffees etc etc is plentiful and staff go out of their way to try and find your favourites_the cinnamon and raisin bagel for me! The lady serving even remembered my daughter and I from last year!
The rooms are small as you would expect in New York and so are some of the bathrooms. I have learnt a bathroom in the double bedded room is smaller than the King bedded. But nevertheless it is adequate. Lighting too could be a bit brighter but then my daughter needed it for studying.The rest of the hotel has such character and we love the lounge especially with its all day help yourself service of coffee, tea, iced water, fruits, cookies etc. Fantastic when you have come in thirsty with aching feet from a hard days shopping! And of course the free internet which was well used.
And all this literally steps away from Times Square. My message to the owners:Dont change a thing about the character and staff of this hotel! You have a real gem here.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown
title: “Good Stay, Good Location”
text:
This hotel is located on State St.
It is nearby to a number of fine restaurants and attractions.
All of the major attractions are either within a taxi ride or walk.
The hotel is nice, the main lobby is not as extensive as you would expect for a regular Embassy Suites but the restaurant area and pool & fitness center are very nice.
Our room was on the 11th floor and we had a view of the downtown area. 
Pros:
Location
Views
Accessibility
Pool & Fitness Center
Cons:
Restuarant (No high chairs visible)
Basic Room Features
This hotel is a very good hotel if you want to be close to the attractions and the such.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Loved It!!!!”
text: Everyone there was friendly and extremely helpful. Hotel and room looked exactly as pictured on the website.The only bad thing is that the only parking is valet and it is $50 with no in/out privileges. I would suggest parking at the Millenium Park garage that is only 5 blocks away and half the price. Also upon check-in they charge your credit card $75 for incidentals but refund in about a week if there weren't any. This hotel is within walking distance to Navy Pier and right on the river. Went to a Cubs game and took the L-train (the full Chicago experience); for 2 people round trip was only $9. The experience riding the L was different and a little scary but fun at the same time and cheaper than cab fare.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Excellent location bed too small!”
text:
We stayed here for four nights, part of a three week trip in the states. We were booked into a double beded European plan room. Did not really understand what this was as our travel agent booked it for us and we did not notice until we arrived there. We were given the European room like it said on the label, hotel had no other rooms to offer us as they were fully booked lots of conferences on.The room was very small which was not a problem but the bed was too small for a comfortable night's sleep, very poor for a Hilton chain.
Advice to fellow travellers, make sure you book a room with a big enough bed! watch out for the so called European plan ! as you can not always change rooms if the hotel is full.

name: Omni Chicago Hotel
title: “Fine stay, but room for improvement”
text:
The Omni Chicago has a wealth of offerings to recommend it: unbeatable downtown location, a relaxing and sophisticated atmosphere, comfortable accommodations, and a staff that understands hospitality. If I were considering only my room and the foregoing, it would rate 4.5 stars. However, there were a few unexpected annoyances whose combined effect had me doubting I'd return. To wit: 
. a somewhat awkward check-in on the third floor instead of street level. I can't imagine most of us like having to schlep luggage down a hallway and up an elevator *before checking in*
. far too few elevators for a tower of this height, thus constant waits/packed cars at most times of day (both sets: street>3, and 3>penthouse)
. a vintage bathroom wall phone, positioned such that you couldn't avoid knocking it off the hook -- then had the tedious job of hanging it back up, always right out of the shower
. a family/pet-friendly atmosphere that was occasionally overwhelming: dogs loose in the hallways, noisy children everywhere, double-wide strollers blocking every conceivable doorway. I know, none of this is the hotel's fault -- but if you're courting that demographic, you need to have a plan in place to control it. 
. poor hallway acoustics that magnified the endless sounds of slamming doors and screaming children
In sum, I reiterate that the Omni is a fine property in a great location with top-notch staff. But I'd prefer to leave the Ugly American chaos of Michigan Avenue outside my hotel. That's difficult to do here.

name: Days Inn Chicago
title: “Days Inn at Diversity and Clark – an OK stay! Why? NOT anything special!”
text:
I’ve stayed at this property off and on since 1993. I’ve seen this property grow from an almost raunchy hotel to an American standard hotel. My last stay at this hotel was in March 2001.
PLUSES… 
1.) rooms are significantly cleaner than back in the 90's and 2001
2.) lobby is much nicer
3.) mattress is very good, entirely better than back in the days
CONCENRS…
i.) Polish speaking nationals. yes, they now have 99% Polish speaking personnel in the hotel which either do NOT speak ANY English or too little to make heads or tails of anything they attempt to say or even comprehend. This is NOT positive! The United States is an open door, however, we MUST insist that people who are employed in this country at some point MUST speak some English; even if they are predominantly in housekeeping. How do these people have their working papers for the country anyway? They probably don't ... sharing SS#!
ii.) toilet brush REQUIRED in the bathroom
iii.) no iron or ironing board in the room
iii.) no refrigerator in the room
Also, I didn't appreciate leaving U$100.00 smoke security. In addition, they quabble about 800 phone calls. 
It is a good hotel for one night. It is what I would refer to as a quickie hotel. 
U$85.00/night including the tax is too much! The best price is U$69.00 including tax.

name: Days Inn Chicago
title: “It is an excellent value.”
text: We were very pleased with the staff and our room. Public transportation was a short walk away. We felt safe in the neighborhood, and there was many dining options with in walking distance. The staff was very friendly and helpful to us as we were first time visitors to the city. We would definitly recommend and stay again.

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Casablanca is Perfect”
text: Great hotel, do I need to say more. We stayed 4 nights, 5 adults, 2 rooms. One adult is so obsessive that she turns the bed down and unfolds all the towels searching for hair etc. Even she was satisfied that this hotel is clean. The 2nd floor lounge is a joy. The gym they sent us to was excellent (only a short walk away). The location is great. But best of all, the staff is as nice as can be. I almost didn't write a review so I could keep this gem available just for us--I totally recommend it!

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown
title: “loved the made to order breakfast”
text: we stayed at this hotel from july 1st thru the 4th of 2002. fairly close to everything we wanted to see. loved the free made to order breakfast , was a definite plus for this hotel. The room was a bit on the drab side and was'nt as clean as we would have liked it to be.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS River North Chicago Downtown Hotel
title: “Excellent emplacement dans le centre de Chicago pour qui dispose d'une voiture”
text: Parking gratuit à l'hôtel avec un confort très supérieur à un motel pour un tarif raisonnable si on réserve un peu à l'avance ; l'emplacement dans Chicago est central avec des chambres suffisamment spacieuses et sans être trop bruyant. Le service rendu par l'hotel est sans reproche et complet (quotidien USA To Day déposé chaque matin au pas de la porte, station internet en libre accès, VOD, etc..). déco de la chambre et des salles de bain agréable ; c'est une très bonne adresse.

name: InterContinental Chicago
title: “Had a good stay”
text:
Stayed for one night during my stay at Chicago. Booked it at Hotwire and gotten a good offer considering the location of the hotel.
