I am surprised that the hotel is ranked 40+, considering that the room was pretty good and the bed was comfortable. It is along the magnificent mile and is accessible to different places. The hotel had a rich history, do check out the indoor swimming pool, reminds me of the old pool in the 60s.
Do consider this hotel if you plan to visit Chicago.

name: Days Inn Chicago
title: “Great Value, Great Location for a Different Chicago Experience”
text: We arrived at the Days Inn Lincoln Park late in the evening after an exhausting day of travel that started 14 hours earlier. The directions on their website were excellent so we had no problems finding it despite being tucked into a residential / retail neighborhood and they even made sure that we approached from the right direction so we could take advantage of the valet service. The front desk staff may have been the best I have ever experienced. Not only did they help us find Chicago deep dish delivery, they got us menus and coupons and even offered to order it for us. When there was a problem with our room key, they sent someone up with us to make sure that our new keys worked. The hotel is an older building that has been refurbished. The room itself was comparable to other rooms in this class of hotel. The bathroom was small and dated, but clean. As I mentioned, it’s in a mostly residential /retail neighborhood, and on a busy corner. If you are light sleeper, you might have a problem with the noise, but it didn’t bother us. Be sure to request an upper level floor if one is available. The next morning, we enjoyed their complementary continental breakfast including belgian waffles and coffee. We were spending the day in the city before driving back to Ohio, but we didn’t want to get our truck out of valet parking and leave all of our luggage in there after finding new parking. The front desk stored our bags for the entire day for us and didn’t charge us anything extra to leave our truck there until that evening. The hotel is walking distance to Wrigley Field, brown and purple line CTA trains, and Lincoln Park. The neighborhood itself is also great and has good shopping. If you are looking for five stars, this place isn’t it, but it is an excellent value in a great Chicago neighborhood. We will definitely stay here again.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile
title: “Four Points Chicago - fick behålla rummet längre”
text:
Ett mycket trevligt och välbeläget hotell. Vår flight hem gick på eftermiddagen och när vi frågade om vi kunde få behålla rummet några timmar extra för att slippa krångla med väskor och sånt så var det inga problem. Vi fick bara frågan "Hur länge?" - och sen ja då är det klart.
Jätteskönt när man har en lång resa framför sej

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Great place to stay”
text: I recently stayed at the Casablanca Hotel October 29-Nov 1 with three family memebers in a suite. I have nothing but good things to say about this hotel. Our room was a decent size for NYC and very clean. The evening wine and cheese was great as was the breakfast (both free!). The staff was very friendly and helpful. The hotel is steps away from Times Square in the heart of the theater district. The subway is also just steps away. Being in midtown was is great b/c you are right in the middle of Manhattan with easy access to uptown and downtown. I would definately stay here again! Feel free to e-mail me is you have any questions about this hotel and/or its surounding area. Enjoy!

name: Casablanca Hotel Times Square
title: “Treated us like family”
text: We just returned from a business/family vacation to NYC and have nothing but positive comments about this hotel. Joe and the staff treated us like family from the moment we walked through the door. We were traveling with our two children and were given excellent advice on fun and interesting restaurants and tourist spots. The relaxed atmosphere at the Casablanca and the attentiveness of everyone who works there was such a highlight of our vacation. We truly felt like the comfort of home everytime we walked through the doors.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown
title: “Poor Service Nasty Staff!”
text:
I was recommended to stay at the La Quinta from a friend whom had stayed there. I arranged three rooms for over a week each through the Manager Gary Pratt. Who turned out to be a nasty little jumped upstart. I was informed all our rooms would be upgraded. None of which were done. Two of the three rooms were very noisy with the vent making a loud droning sound continually. I complained and was eventually moved to a larger room. This room was even noislier. Both my colleagues mentioned this upon their visit to my room. The last night, I had to put on Noise cancelling headphones in order to get a couple of hours sleep. When I informed the front desk that I wanted to receive some compensation, "Mr Pratt" as he now called himself aggressively approached me informing me I got a good deal and I should be happy. He is a nasty little man that should not be in the hospitality industry! He reminded me of Basil Fawlty of Fawlty Towers 
Whilst the staff were OK, none of them seem happy to be working there. 
Breakfast was so lame and the staff unfriendly, we only went there twice, the second time to confirm it was so bad. 
Do not stay at this hotel!

name: Hotel Lincoln
title: “Perfect Chic Retro Stay”
text:
Fantastic hotel with a boutique high end retro chic feel & finish! Very friendly and helpful, recommending things for us to do prior to our stay via their Facebook page then making us feel very special when we arrived by very kindly giving us a bottle of champagne in our room as it was our honeymoon. We stayed in a suite and the rooms were a great size, very clean with a fantastic huge comfy bed! 
Location is great for Lincoln park and walk able into the city, although you can also walk down to the subway station in approx 10 mins to access the whole city. Very easy access by bus to Wrigley Field if you are seeing a Cubs game (would highly recommend) 
We only ate breakfast in the restaurant which was delicious although slightly more pricey than you can get else where although you do get very good quality food.
All in all a fantastic hotel, that offers something different to the standard chain. Would definitely stay there again next time I'm in Chicago.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Holy Metropolis Hotel!”
text:
Stayed at the Hyatt for a conference, the hotel was sprawling for sure. It accommodated our conference of 1200 plus one other one (that I know of) - there were some minor inconveniences involved (like elevator waits at check-in, check-out time) but overall the staff was friendly and efficient and our stay was wonderful and the kids loved traveling through what they called the "underground city" in the sub-level floors. Loved the little "convenience" store on the first floor that had a toaster and microwave that you could buy inexpensive foods and cook them yourself.
We got a room in the newly renovated East Tower on the 32nd floor (avoid the high floors if you expereience vertigo!!) - the floor to ceiling windows made me very nervous at first, but I eventually got used to it. Beds were comfy, valet service was especially helpful - and you cannot beat the LOCATION!!! Expect crowds (this is Chicago you know) - check out the BIG bar, and make sure to take a walk along the river....

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Loved the Regency”
text: We stay in the downtown section of Chicago a few times each year at different places and locations. The Hyatt Regency has one of the best locations for shopping, theater, museums or just cruising the streets. It had some mixed reviews but the more recent ones were very positive. All the rooms have been recently renovated or updated. We were able to check in early and actually see two shows on the same day." Nogalar" at the Goodman and " Ethan Fromm" at the Looking Glass theater both walking distances. We are going back in August for more plays.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown
title: “Great value, location, and room”
text: I thoroughly enjoyed my experience and plan to stay at LQ Chicago Downtown next time we visit Chicago. As a returns member, I have stayed at LQs across Texas (my home state) and the US, and this location definitely sets the bar high! I found the staff extremely welcoming and accommodating- from the young man who checked us in, Melissa at the front desk to Ariana and the rest of the breakfast staff, and Tom, the gentleman who checked our bags. These individuals were extremely hospitable and friendly. The room was lovely and clean with stylish decor and a nice view. The breakfast was hot, filling, fresh, and FREE! These beds are so comfy! Even though this immediate area is mostly business, the CTA is very user friendly and the hotel is close to millennium park, good restaurants, and an awesome dive bar- stocks & blondes. Enjoy your stay!

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Beautiful hotel”
text: We stayed at the Palmer House to go shopping and see the aquarium in Chicago. It is located directly between the two although the walk is a little long for both. The hotel lobby is beautiful and all the staff seem nice. We got the package with the aquarium tickets so the room was not anything special but it was clean and we didn't hear any other guests while in our room. The only problem was that the elevators from the rooms down to the lobby take a very long time. At first I thought they were broken and just took the stairs down 16 floors.

name: Ivy Boutique Hotel
title: “Cute new hotel in a great location..but be prepared to wait”
text:
I stayed at the Ivy while I was in town to attend the Prince Welcome to Chicago tour and it was a lovely experience.
We arrived late Sunday evening and immediately were offered an upgrade to a King Suite (vs. the standard room we booked on Hotels.com) for a mere $50. Totally worth it because the suite was amazing! A separate sitting room with remote control blinds and beautiful furniture. Also a well stocked mini-bar, but of course everything was an arm and a leg. Large bathroom with a soaking tub and rainforest shower stall (SN- I saw a couple of comments about the temperature of the shower, it's actually just a somewhat tricky faucet, but the water gets really hot). Bedroom was beautiful with a King size platform bed. We didn't partake in the gym (which is actually down the street, but they give you as many passes as you like), but did visit the rooftop bar. We didn't get food, so I can't comment on the wait that many people have complained about, but our drinks came very quickly and were really good ($13, but that's normal for Downtown Chicago). The rooftop itself is GORGEOUS with plenty of heat lamps for chillier Fall days and lots of ambiance.
Check in and check out were smooth and the staff was very accommodating to any requests (example, they didn't have an iron in the room, but brought one up quickly when requested) that we had. 
The only downfall of this stay was everything to do with transportation. While the hotel does have Valet (despite what other reviews say) they actually appear to use another hotel's service, which makes the wait very long even if you call in advance. It was difficult to get a taxi also (granted it was late, but most Downtown hotels have taxis on call), though the Bellman was willing to help.
All in all, I recommend this place (especially if you can get a good rate), it's in a great location and the pros far outweigh the cons.
Pros- Great service, beautiful rooms, fantastic rooftop bar and great turndown service with treats
Cons- Valet Parking and Taxi Issues

name: Hotel 71, Wyndham Affiliate
title: “One of the best hotels I've stayed in!”
text:
Our room at Hotel 71 was perfect! We had a corner room with windows on two walls of the room overlooking the river - absolutely beautiful. The room had more than enough space to comfortably accommodate three adults. Beds were queen size and very comfortable (I'm quite picky and get back and hip pain if I sleep in a bed that's too firm. I had absolutely no pain after sleeping on these beds for three nights.) Housekeeping always had our room clean by the time we got back at around 5pm, and never bothered us when we had our 'do not disturb' sign up. They always brought us more coffee and towels when we requested extra. The bathrooms were also spacious and had enough counter space for our flat irons, make-up, etc. My sister is very picky about bathrooms and she was very happy with this one. We were on the 25th floor and didn't hear any traffic during the night; just the occasional siren.
The location was perfectly set in the middle of downtown Chicago. We walked to Magnificent Mile, Navy Pier (about a mile away), Millennium Park, Art Institute, and many restaurants in the area.
We didn't try the hotel restaurant or room service so I can't comment on those. But there is a delicious Italian restaurant a few doors down with great thin crust pizza and fantastic tiramisu.
I've stayed at a few other hotels in downtown Chicago, but I absolutely plan to stay at Hotel 71 next time I'm there!

name: Hotel Allegro Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Wonderful hotel, perfect location”
text:
Great hotel conveniently located near public transportation lines. Within walking distance of Millennium Park and The Art Institute of Chicago, and just a few blocks from popular retail clothing stores. The House of Blues is also located nearby.
Hotel room was beautifully decorated, but both the room and bathroom were small - very nice, but small. Easy to overlook though since the hotel is one of the less expensive ones in the area. We enjoyed our stay and will stay here again on our next visit to Chicago.

name: Hard Rock Hotel Chicago
title: “Fair”
text: The upside - the rock and roll memorabilia is very cool, the bar and lobby has a great ambiance, the drinks were very well made, the bar waitstaff was prompt and efficient and the rooms (at least the one I had) are very large and comfortable with nice amenities (although it was weird having John-Paul-George-Ringo watching me in the bathroom!). The downside was the rooms are dark as the lighting is poor. The hotel restaurant was a real downside. Service was slow and the food was consistently delivered cool or cold, not hot. Relative to the experience, the hotel was on the expensive side.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Loved it.”
text:
Our 5 day stay at the Palmer House was great. The staff was super friendly (especially the bell desk!), and the hotel itself is beautiful.
Pros
- Awesome location - so easy to get around
- Great staff
- Beautiful rooms (assuming you get one of the re-done ones - we upgraded to a bigger room and it was worth the extra $20 per night)
- Amazing gym
- Starbucks in the lobby - good place to meet and get caffeine fix
Cons
- No WiFi and it's not free (the hotel is one of the oldest in Chicago and built with super thick walls, making WiFi difficult)
- The regular rooms are very small, but typical for the age of the hotel (if you are by yourself without a lot of luggage, it's fine)

name: MileNorth, A Chicago Hotel
title: “Great hotel,excellent location”
text:
We spent six nights in this great hotel and found it excellent in every respect. Great staff and great breakfast. We did not get any dinners in hotel as there were a number of great restaurants close by.The location is fantastic close to shops on Michigan Avenue and within easy reach of the many parks in the area.All staff were very helpful and friendly and could not do enough for us.
We will come to this hotel again the next time we are in Chigago.

name: Ivy Boutique Hotel
title: “need to work out some kinks ...”
text:
They only recently opened and there were some technical problems (TV, air con, internet). Worse, the room smelled like sewage a couple times! And there were some other, smaller issues. 
But, the staff was nice (if not super competent), the room was large and mostly nice, the bed was really comfy, and the shower incredible. 
It's in the real touristy section of town, surrounded by other hotels and near the Rainforest Cafe.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Nice hotel, limited dining options, remote location, requires cab ride to get around”
text: The hotel was very nice, clean, and the staff was friendly. The location was less than desirable. If you want to get downtown for anything you need to take a $10 cab ride. The restaurants in the area (outside of the hotel which are very good but there is only 1 plus a cafe) are not within quick walking distance which again requires a cab ride. While this may not be a deal breaker for most, I prefer being able to walk a few blocks have shops and restaurants close by and feel the city energy . Hyatt Regency is great if you're attending a conference at McCormick but would not recommend for a tourist or someone who wants to get out and about.

name: Omni Chicago Hotel
title: “I want to go back!”
text: The Omni Chicago on Michigan ave is a fantaastic hotel! The rooms are a little on the small side but I guess thats the price you pay for being right on Miracle Mile. The Omni was a little on the pricy side but again, you get what you pay for. Great walking distance to everything on miracle mile, navy pier, John Hancock tower and easy L Access to Wrigley Field. I would definatly go back.

name: MileNorth, A Chicago Hotel
title: “Great room, great location, great stay!”
text:
Stayed a few nights on a business trip in June.
Great little property. I had a nice view of the city, looking north, I think. Each day I walked to the BCG offices on LaSalle, about a mile away. Nice walk, great food and shops all around.
Bed is very comfy. Minimal hall and street noise. Very clean.
The a/c fan was perfect for me. I usually sleep with a noise machine, now a great iPad app. 
I generally prefer a constant hum of a smooth a/c fan and I could set this one on high and it was perfect.
Elevators were a little slow but it wasn't a big deal. I think it may have added maybe a minute to my commute.
I would stay here again in a heartbeat.

name: Millennium Knickerbocker Hotel Chicago
title: “Quaint and homey with a must-have location”
text: Just got back from a short trip to Chicago. For my first time in the Windy City, I wanted a hotel on the Magnificent Mile, and not too expensive (I got a deal on Lodging.com for $109/night for this 4 star hotel). The Millennium Knickerbocker was perfect under these criteria. The hotel is on the North end of Michigan Avenue, directly across Walton Place from The Drake, and only a block to the running/cycling/bike path on Lake Michigan. So, a fantastic location. Yes, the rooms were small and, yes, the bathrooms were even smaller, but they were completely functional. For those going to Chicago to see the city and not hole up in their room the entire time, this hotel was great. The rooms are not glamourous and some of the decor even seems a bit thrown together, but everything is clean and sanitary. Bring your own shampoo/conditioner/soap though...the stuff they provide isn't so great. The service was first-rate however, especially that of the concierge. Whenever we inquired about the location of a certain restaurant or a boat tour, instead of merely pointing us in the right direction, he gave us priority passes with which we could avoid lines. Though the next time I visit the Windy City, I'll probably try another hotel, the Millennium Knickerbocker was terrific for a first-time trip.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Warm reception and service!”
text:
I treated my mom to a weekend and Chicago and enjoyed a wonderful time. The staff at the Hyatt was exceptional. I appreciated the warm greeting and help throughout the weekend. Check-in and check-out were made so easy. The bell captain and bellmen were so friendly and helpful. The concierge desk was very helpful providing information about attractions. We had booked a river cruise recommended by the concierge. We had some difficulty finding the dock in time. We went on another nearby cruise, immensely enjoying ourselves. We were able to easily attain a refund on our deposit for the cruise booked through the hotel.
The room was spacious and clean. The beds were comfortable. The hotel was in easy walking distance of Michigan Avenue and other attractions. Inexpensive cab ride to most destinations. I would definitely stay at this hotel again. Good representation of the warmth and hospitality of this wonderful city!

name: Hotel Allegro Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “boutique hotel, reasonable rates with outstanding atmosphere and friendly staff”
text: My sister, nieces, and I stayed at the Hotel Allegro since we were seeing 'Wicked' which was playing at the Cadillac Theatre next store and/or may be attached to the hotel. The hotel was more than we imagined. So chic and modern, overwhelming atmosphere in the lobby with wine/cheese hour, plenty of options for dining, extremely helpful staff - even packed us up the extra-ordinary continental breakfast to go. Would definitely recommend to anyone in the Chicago theatre or business district.

name: The Silversmith Hotel & Suites
title: “Silversmith in Chicago”
text: This is the second time I have stayed at the Silversmith. The accomodations are great - rooms well appointed and clean. You need to be OK with noise from the L, but otherwise this hotel offers first class accommodations at very reasonable rates. Very close to many of the key attractions in the Loop. Lots of food options nearby and easy access to public transportation.

name: Millennium Knickerbocker Hotel Chicago
title: “Posizione eccezionale. Nulla di più”
text: Siamo a 30 metri dalla Michigan North! Con i mitici bus CTA 151 e 147 si può andare ovunque; se invece hai bisogno o vuoi farti un giro sulla famosa metro sopraelevata, e non vuoi prendere coincidenze, la fermata Chicago/red è a 10 minuti. L'Hotel rispetta pienamente il suo standard, ma sicuramente non si fa ricordare. Aspetti negativi sono a)la connessione Internet che ad ogni modo è sempre a pagamento(anche nella lobby!); b) la colazione non inclusa (ma questo è quasi uno standard in USA); c) alle mail non rispondono. Il costo della camera è vantaggioso solo se si usufruisce di una promozione(nel nostro caso con Expedia).

name: The Drake
title: “They ruined Mothers Day!”
text: I just returned from the Mothers Day brunch of May 11, held in the Gold Coast room of The Drake Hotel and just had to express how angry and disappointed I was. When my party and I first arrived we were seated promptly enough but it went down hill from there. After 15 minutes of waiting and with no server even approaching our table, we finally flagged down a waiter who sent someone over. This server, Reggie, told us that he was the back waiter and that Patrick would be our front waiter all while leaning on our table and giving us attitude. Im not really sure why he felt the need to explain this to us, as all we wanted at this time was for SOMEONE to take our drink orders. He took our orders and after a time came back with our drinks. He placed them on the table without saying a word even after we all thanked him individually after placing the drinks beside each person. Not one youre welcome. This put an immediate bad note on the occasion. We were also put off by the fact no one explained to us what we were to do. Do we order first? Do we just head up to the brunch table? We just sat there dumbfounded at the lack of attention. After waiting yet another unusually long period of time, a member of my party got up and approached the Director of Banquet Services who turned out to be completely unfriendly and unhelpful. The only saving grace to this whole fiasco was the waiter named Patrick. He was really great. He saw what was going on and was very attentive to us after seeing what we had been going through. We finished our meal and decided on having dessert. We ordered some coffee that was served cold and had to wait, again, for some hot coffee. After we finished our meal we asked for the bill. After being quoted a price of $37.50 per person over the phone from one of the restaurant hostesses at the time I made the reservation, the bill reflected a price of $177.00 or $59 per person. Where did the extra $21.50 per person come from? The only thing we had to drink was water, coffee and the complimentarge of $26 was added bringing the grand total to $220! When I made the reservation, the hostess also told me that each Mother would get a rose. Ours never received hers. You have no idea how angry I am. I have been to many a brunch that cost half the price and been treated twice as well. I am surprised and shocked that a hotel with a high reputation would allow such antics! You can be very sure that I will never step foot in this hotel again and will tell all of my friends and co-workers what a sham the Drake Hotel truly is.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Great stay!”
text:
We booked the Palmer House through priceline, and I was a little nervous because of some of the reviews on here, but we had a great stay! We paid $99 a night (including taxes and fees) for a Thurs to Sun stay.
We came into town on the Amtrak, and had no problem checking in at 1:00pm. Our room was one that had been renovated with a king size bed. The bathroom was a little small but both of us could stand in it at the same time so it didn't bother us. THe bed was very comfy, Air conditioning worked great! The only thing that I will mention was that there are a lot of rooms on each floor so it can be a bit of a walk to the elevator and the ice machine. From what I could tell there is only one ice machine on each floor. I saw that another review mentioned free WI-FI, but its not free, you have to pay for it. 
I loved the overall 'historical' ambience of the Palmer house. Concierge was nothing but helpful, and friendly, even printing out a map for me. I would highly recommend asking concierge for the guide book called 'Concierge preferred, Chicago Icons' just for the maps on the inside alone. Also has good info on where to eat, and shop and what not. 
We used a 3 day transport pass for our four days in Chicago, which was great! Right outside the hotel there are stops for the red-line subway as well as the blue-line. Easy walking distance to many clothing stores, restaurants, and Millennium park. There is a CVS right across the street from the Wabash st. entrance.
We found the Palmer house to be an great hotel in an excellent location! We will definitely stay again!

name: MileNorth, A Chicago Hotel
title: “Fantastic mid-range hotel”
text: This was a great stay. From the moment we arrived and were upgraded to a studio suite I was impressed - by the service, location, and facilities. Probably the best-value hotel we have ever stayed at, given how nice and central it is to many downtown sights. Highly recommended. The one minor drawback was the long wait for the elevators. This large building is served by just two cars.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown
title: “OK place”
text: Stayed here because no other hotels were available in the loop or theater district. For $318 including tax I consider this WAY overpriced. No Bar, no work out room and small pool and hot tub. Of course, this is downtown Chicago so the price must refect that fact. Room was boxy, AC noisy and very spartan amenities. Try another chain like Hampton, Summerfield Suites, etc.

name: The Drake
title: “Top Hotel - Idealer Ausgangspunkt”
text: Das Hotel spiegelt tatsächlich den Glanz vergangenere Tage wieder. In der Lobby wird einem ganz schnell klar, wie es in Chicago zu Zeiten von Grace Kelly & Co. zuging. Das Hotel ist zwar schon etwas in die Jahre gekommen, aber die Zimmer bieten immernoch einen hohen Standard. Der Service und die Mitarbeiter sind alle sehr bemüht und kümmern sich um jedwede Angelegenheit umgehend. Der Fitnessraum ist relativ groß und verfügt über eine Viezahl von Geräten, so dass keine Wünsche für einen umfangreiches Training übrigbleiben. Das Hotel verfügt über gleich drei stadtbekannte Restaurants, die alle zu empfehlen sind. Ebenso liegt das Hotel direkt an einem kleinen Strand, der jedoch nicht direkt einlädt, um dort länger zu verweilen, weil ein 10spuriger Speedway direkt daran vorbeiführt. Allerdings ist die Joggingsstrecke, die fast direkt am Hotel vorbeiführt, sehr zu empfehlen. Außerdem beginnt die Michigan Road direkt vor der Tür, somit sind alle Shopping Highlights (Bloomingdales bspw. direkt gegenüber) schnell erreichbar. Alles in allem ein tolles Hotel

name: The Silversmith Hotel & Suites
title: “Great Location at a great price”
text: We stayed 4 nights at the Silversmith and thoroughly enjoyed it. The staff provided excellent service at all levels. I followed the advice by other reviewers and asked for a room away from the noise of the trains. We were given a suite on the seventh floor away from the trains. They could be barely be heard. The room was spacious and clean. The location is centrally located and ideal for our sightseeing plans. For the price, we were impressed. We would definitly stay here again.

name: Omni Chicago Hotel
title: “Great staff, dark rooms”
text: Went to Chicago with my mom and 10 yr old son for 2 days. Arrived at 10:30 am chicago time. We were told we could have a room now on oneside or wait for the otherside, none of them faced Michigan ave. Took the one that was ready. In minutes we were in our room with luggage following us up. The room was clean and well done. The room was VERY dark, there was a building very close blocking ANY view and ANY sunlight. I called the desk and was told ALL rooms are blocked from sun there because of surrounding buildings. Staff was friendly and helpful. Our tv did not work properly so Joe from maintainance came up a few times, he even stayed passed quitting time,missing his train home to change the set when he could not fix it. The breakfast buffet was expensive but good. Overall the staff made the hotel, just disappointed on the lighting and lack of view.

name: InterContinental Chicago
title: “Toll”
text: Sehr gutes und gepflegtes Hotel mit ausgezeichnetem Service. Schade, dass der WIFI nicht kostenlos war. Ausgezeichnete Lage des Hotels im Stadtzentrum aber doch ruhig. Das Schwimmbad ist in ausergewöhnlichen Zustand und Duschsachen mit Tuechern gratis zur Verfügung. Das Frühstück war ausgezeichnet mit grossem Angebot.

name: MileNorth, A Chicago Hotel
title: “Affinia Surpassed Expectations...”
text:
Steve, Andre and Peter were some of the most helpful and kindest hotel staff I have encountered. This hotel has a great location, right next to some of the best dining experiences in the city. Cabs, convention center buses... are easily accessed. The staff mentioned will gladly give you some great local references for things to do and where to eat. They will even give you an express pass to the front of the line at World Famous Gino's East....right next door!
Very clean, very helpful....this was a GREAT first time Chicago visit. Hint: If need a ride to and from airport, take a taxi if you have more than one person...shuttles charge per person - but if you are solo take the Go Shuttle by baggage claim.

name: Hotel Allegro Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Cozy size room, but comfortable”
text:
The room really is small, and felt almost claustrophobic in the bathroom, there is a work desk which is nice, and the TV is great size, even though they didn't have HBO or a channel guide anywhere to be found.
But we shared the same sentiments as many on here, the hotel is obviously a older building but it has been nicely renovated and has a nice sheek modern feel. The lobby is on the second floor of the building which was a new one for us, but the lobby was great. We were there over a weekend where weddings seemed to be going on all the time, but they were relatively under control and non-intrusive and not too loud. Upon check-in the front desk let me know about the weddings and put me on a higher floor so it wouldn't bother us during our stay, which was much appreciated.
Free Wine and social hour from 5-6 every day was a really nice touch. And the staff was great, all we could ask for.
For the rate we payed for a great location in Chicago it was perfect.
We were fortunate enough to not have a car, as I really see no where in the whole city of Chicago where you could park for

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Absolutely fantastic!”
text: From the valet, to the staff, amenities and room, you couldn't ask for a better hotel to stay in. I will definitely be staying here again!

name: MileNorth, A Chicago Hotel
title: “Good stuff”
text: Stayed here for our "babymoon," yeah I didn't know this was a thing either...great location being right downtown about a block or two from Michigan Avenue and right next door to Gino's. Really, like the modern feel and layout of the room. Had dinner at the hotel restaurant and it was fantastic. I had swordfish for the first time and it was amazing. Had no idea fish could taste like that. Wife had the pork chops and they did not disappoint. Hats off to the Top Chef Master.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York West 35th
title: “Great central location”
text: We have been going to NYC for the last 5-6 years and we enjoy staying at some place different everytime. We have stayed at the Omni Berkshire, Crowne Plaza, Best Western President, and the Marriott Residence Inn. This year we stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn on 35th Street (between 5th and 6th Ave) March 13-15, 2009. We originally booked the Marriott Residence Inn until we located this hotel on TravelZoo for $139.00 a night. Stayed on the 15th floor, room 1509 with our room facing uptown. The rooms are rather large for NY standards. Each room has a microwave, coffee maker, and mini refrig. The bathroom was very large and the shower was awesome. Also each room offers both wired/wireless internet at no charge, 32 inch HDTV, and a niced sized work desk. The hotel have 3 elevators and the wait was always mininum. Hotel also offers a concierge, small bar, restaurant, and a pantry with snack foods and beverages, also provided free coffee each morning. Parking garage is across the street from the hotel, along with one just up the block....original parking price is around $42.00 for 24 hrs, though if you get your ticket stamped at the Hilton the price is around $35.00. The hotel has a subway station (Herald Square) right around the corner. Empire State Building is located one street away, Macy's is across the street, and Times Square's is a short 7 blocks walk away. The hotel offers a breakfast buffet, though a bit pricey. There is a great restaurant (Andrew's Coffee Shop) located just up the street at 35th St and Broadway that offers breakfest, lunch, and dinner at very reasonable prices. This was an excellent choice for this years stay.

name: MileNorth, A Chicago Hotel
title: “Fantastic!”
text:
We arrived on Saturday night and were greeted by Victor who took our car and luggage and then Rocio at the Front Desk. She was outstanding. She arranged for a room move the next day since all that was left was a room on the 8th floor and I just felt like been higher up.
Judging from experience at any other hotel, the following day the staff would not have had a clue about our request to move, but they did here, and they had already blocked a couple of rooms at a higher floor for me to choose from. This was a very pleasant interaction. Due to my background in the Hospitality industry, I inspected both rooms and I was very pleased to find them extremely clean, very well appointed and with great amenities. The bed is so comfortable that it made it difficult for me to want to get up in the morning. My only complaint would be that the A/C could not be set to a low fan setting. or perhaps I did not know how to use the digital thermostat. The sofa was comfortable and the recliner was the "icing on the cake".
The staff is very friendly and made us feel recognized and special. Well done! The gentleman with the beard who works at the Front Desk is an outstanding individual. Not only does he work very long hours, but he keeps the place running smoothly. He was very quick at paying attention to details, always alert and observant. He is an asset to the hotel.
Last but not least, I have to commend their Concierge. I have come across a few good ones and right now he is at the top of my list. He is knowledgeable, attentive, distinctive and friendly. Superb!
I will return to this hotel the next time I visit Chicago due to the great service, the convenient location (walking distance from anything!) and comfortable rooms. I will recommend it to all my friends.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Daughters Wedding”
text: My daughter got married at tthe River East Arts Cernter so the Sheraton was very close. The rooms were spacious, clean and great views of the city. The staff was very helpful, administration outstanding, and the River patio was great for boat and people watching.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown
title: “Muy recomendable”
text: El hotel es moderno y esta muy bien mantenido. Esta a pocas cuadras de la zona comercial de Chicago. Llegue a las 9am del sabado y me dieron la habitacion. El personal de recepcion sumamente amable y dispuesto a ayudar con cualquier consulta. El desayuno estuvo completo. Muy buen aubicacion para ir al United Center ya que el bus (20) pasa a una cuadra del hotel, frente a la Opera House. Volveria al hotel sin dudarlo.

name: MileNorth, A Chicago Hotel
title: “all factors positive except no free wi-fi”
text:
I got out the taxi, terrific welcome by bellhop and reception, large new room, large new bathroom, great location. I can't believe a hotel of this quality doesn't offer free wi-fi. Coming from the UK I refuse to get ripped off for roaming charges and rely on free wi-fi to get the myriad of emails any business person gets every day. Out of the hotel and straight down North St Clair St for 150 yards, great breakfast place – the corner bakery has free wi-fi all day.
Problem – room 507 and that side of the hotel has a truck delivery yard at ground level and you hear all the trucks loudly beeping in the night air, all night, as they reverse into a loading bay. It sounds to me like an alarm clock. I changed the following day to the North St Clair St side 1403 and all was terrific again.
 I would probably use this place again

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Nice room. Good location.”
text: I spent one night at this hotel on a recent business trip. The second stay at this hotel, the location is great and the vibe is very lively. The staff was very kind and upgraded my room even though I only spent one night. View of the lake and river was great. Also, my room was huge and the bed was super comfy. Surprisingly nice for a conference hotel.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Sheraton Rises Above the Rest!”
text: I travel to Chicago multiple times each year for both business and pleasure. I have stayed at numerous hotels in and around Chicago. I can tell you that the Sheraton Towers is simply the best place to stay. The staff is incredible, friendly and inviting. The manager personally welcomed me the last time I visited! The location is amazing! Just blocks away from Navy Pier and Michigan Avenue. My kids love the pool. I love going for a run by the lakeshore. The Sheraton rises above the rest!

name: Crowne Plaza Houston Galleria Area
title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: Sopped over here for a few nights and it was an excellent experience. Sam the Manager was amazing and treated us like royalty, (something other hotel I have stayed in could take heed of!) When the shuttle was not available this guy took time out to run us into town in his own car. That's service! Will definatly recommend to others and also hope to return on a personal trip next time. Thanks to George the barman, Maria and Cindy on reception who was so helpful with check in, printing etc. Rooms were perfect and had everything needed for both buisness and personal stop over. Thanks again

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Best hotel staff I've ever encountered!”
text: Word to the wise, check with the hotel prior to check in about their debit card hold policy. But this hotel bends over backwards to accommodate its guests. Charles, the front desk manager smoothly and professionally got me checked into the most amazing corner room (for the government rate no less) and last night I unceremoniously dumped my dessert (creme brulee) all over the lobby. Maintenance guy David not only cheerfully cleaned up my mess, he ran and got me a replacement dessert. The next day he remembered me (fondly even!) I can't wait to come back for pleasure with family!

name: Embassy Suites Houston Downtown
title: “Above and Beyond”
text: I stayed at the Embassy Suites on a business trip. I am an employee of Hilton and know what to expect from the brand and was completly blown away by the service. The team here at Embassy lives by the phrase "above and beyond." We checked in very late but the front desk clerk made the process quick and painless. Our room and the hotel was of extravangant design. The next morning we woke up early to enjoy breakfast before starting our soon-to-be stressful day. Great cook to order omlets made by Abe and Gregory. Both having given exemplary service. Later in the evening we enjoyed the manager's reception with bartender Jason. I truly believe one of your key star players. The only accident I encountered was with Tina in breakfast. I believe there was a miscommunication. I had asked front desk for some in room coffee. Soon after, front desk did a follow up call, (much appreciated), although, I had not recieved the coffee, cream, and sugar. A couple minutes later, Tina arrived with the creamer and sugar only. I explained I had ordered coffee too and she said something about charging me. I was confused since what I wanted was in room coffee, not room service. I assume this was way too much to ask for. She went downstairs and brought the correct order back and when I said thank you, her reply was "Ya." Tina was the only person I felt could be improved upon. Other than that, Alex and Richard in valet were absolutly fabulous. Richard even asked when checking out if he could assist me with directions. Wonderful staff and wonderful stay.

name: Hilton Garden Inn New York West 35th
title: “Super Lage, toller Ausblick”
text:
Wir hatten ein Zimmer mit Stadtblick - der Ausblick war spitze.
Die Lage des Hotels ist sehr gut. U-Bahn direkt vorm Hoteleingang. Empire State Building, Madison Square Garden, Penn Station sind ums Eck.
Wlan ist kostenlos und gut. Gepäck konnte am Abreisetag sicher gelagert werden.
Das Hotel kann man nur empfehlen.

name: Sanctuary Hotel New York
title: “Very tiny room in excellent location”
text: The room is very small even by NY standards. If you are the claustrophobic type, you may want to stay elsewhere. The windows are frosted so you can't see outside, which makes the room feel even smaller. The shower has no door, just a curtain to separate it from the bedroom. The water pressure was decent though the shower knob pulled off when we tried to adjust the water temp. Breakfast was average. Unless the rate is pretty reasonable, will not stay here again

name: JW Marriott Chicago
title: “Best place to stay in Chicage”
text: My wife and I stayed here for her b-day weekend and they made the stay exceptional. It's right down town near everything and the hotel staff made sure that every little detail was taken care of. We were treated like royalty.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Great Chicago stay”
text: I attended a professional conference at the Sheraton Chicago and had the best time. Ideally located, exceptional service and nice atmosphere. I'll definitely stay there again.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Great Hotel, Amazing lobby and grand rooms”
text:
A quick two night business trip in Chicago. This was my first stay at the Palmer House and one of the nicest Hilton properties I've stayed in. Quick check-in with no one in the Hhonors line. Was recognized as a Hhonors Diamond before check-in and upgraded to a room on the executive floor with two double beds and two bathrooms. The room was very nice and I liked the period decor the second bathroom was great for travelling with colleagues. There was a small walk-in closet of both sides of the room.
The executive lounge was located one floor above mine, a quick walk, or there was reserved elevators that only served the executive floor and needed key card access. It was one of the largest executive lounges I'd seen, staff was polite and attentive to our needs. I know the lounge is advertised as 'continental breakfast' but this was still one of the few lounges I've seen that didn't have some sort of scrambled eggs or bacon for breakfast. On the 22nd floor we could just barely hear the elevated train go by, I'd be worried about a room a little lower down as the train runs down the street at the height of the 3rd/4th floors. But on our floor the noise wasn't an issue at all.
The hotel was centrally located with several restaurants in the area. The front desk was quick to point out local places to eat.
I didn't have time to experience the on site restaurants, or fitness area. The lobby area bar was always quite busy and we ran into a few people that came there for drinks but weren't staying at the hotel.
I'd have no objections to staying at The Palmer House again and would even consider going out of my way to do so while in Chicago.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Love this hotel!”
text: Great location, great customer service, good rooms, great beds, good gym! I would like to spend less money, but hey, you get what you pay for. I have stayed here many times last year. If its good enough for the president of the United States (he has been staying here many times at the same time as myself) then its good enough for me!

name: The Silversmith Hotel & Suites
title: “Great Location, Great Price, Decent Hotel.”
text:
I stayed in this hotel with a group of friends while in Chicago for a wedding. Overall it was a pretty good experience given the price of the rooms. I think we received a really good deal on the rooms because it was December in Chicago- not exactly the height of tourist season. 
The Room:
My friends and I stayed in 2 conjoining rooms right across from the elevator on one of the upper floors. There was no view out of our windows other than the building next door. I'm not sure if any of the rooms have a view at this hotel or not. 
The furnishings and overall vibe of the room was that it was quite old, but nice enough. The rooms were decently spacious and comfortable, but nothing special. The bathrooms especially felt very old. 
The Service/ Hotel Overall:
There is a very nice lobby on the 2nd floor with computers, a piano, and lots of seating. This was convenient because we arrived early and our rooms weren't ready yet. The concierge and the other staff were all very friendly and helpful. The one thing that was "off" about the hotel was that the street-level interest consistently smelled very bad. 
The location:
This was the BEST thing about the hotel other than the price. The hotel is about 2 blocks from Millennium Park with great museums and entertainment. Most attractions are walkable from the hotel. However, for the things that are not within walking distance, the hotel is located HALF a block from the El- Chicago's transit system. This was extremely convenient, especially because you can ride the El directly to both of Chicago's main airports! We saved a lot by not taking a cab!
So, If you want a hotel that is not expensive and is in a very convenient location- stay at the Silversmith. If you are looking for luxury, look somewhere else.

name: JW Marriott Chicago
title: “Nice and Spacious”
text: Nice hotel - rooms were quiet and spacious. Comfortable beds with an elegant decor. The bathroom was huge by hotel standards. The lobby bar was great to grab quick bite, free wi-fi and of course, people watching. Service is what you would expect from a JW resort. I wish this hotel was located on Michigan Avenue, although I would stay here again.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Huge, inattentive and poor customer service”
text:
This place is so large you're just a number, they don't really care about their "guests" and they make promises they don't keep. For almost $200 per night (conference, supposed discount rate), you expect a lot more.
It's supposed to be an upscale hotel, but it had no comforter on the bed, just a thin blanket between sheets with a spare blanket in the closet. I had to keep the room cool for my roommate and I asked for a comforter just before I went to bed (because I hadn't noticed there was none). They said it would take 20 min. to bring up, so I had to do without, since I needed to get to sleep. They were supposed to send one the next day, but in 3 days, it never came.
I also had to specifically request a telephone book, because there wasn't any in the room. I requested extra drinking glasses, but got paper coffee cups. The drain plug would never stay down, which I needed for taking out and putting on my contact lenses, but I only thought of it when I was ready for bed or getting ready for an early meeting, so never had a chance to ask for them to fix that. I assumed that would also take at least 20 min. or so for someone to come and I never had that kind of time when I was thinking of it. 
Every time you tried to reach the operator or front desk (which never went to the front desk anyway despite the labeling on the phone) you get a recorded message with loud music and advertisements running for Hyatt while you wait a long time for the phone to begin ringing for someone to answer. So if you're calling at night for a wake-up call, you are blasted with music and running ads just before going to sleep. I also couldn't check out with the video check out because the button for checking out was disabled on the screen. Then, when I wanted to make a speedy exit for my flight, I had to wait for a long time listening to their music and ads before I could get someone at the front desk (had to go through an operator this time too) to check out.
Stay away!

name: theWit, a Doubletree Hotel
title: “Nice theater district location, hip hotel, friendly helpful staff.”
text: Stayed for RSNA 2012. Bus to McCormick was 1 short block away at Reinassance. Didn't get to the rooftop bar, maybe next time. State/Lake restaurant on ground floor used once, was good upscale pub atmosphere. Would stay here again.

name: Hard Rock Hotel Chicago
title: “Zentral und rockig”
text: Das Hotel macht seinem Namen alle Ehre. Musik in der Lobby, der Bar und im Restaurant sind ebenso wir Bilder von Rocklegenden und Gitarren als Dekoration allgegenwärtig. Entsprechend cool ist das Design der komfortablen Zimmer. Aufgrund der sehr zentralen Innenstadtlage ist es auch nachts relativ laut. Im Restaurant haben wir vorzüglich asiatisch gegessen. Bei frühzeitiger Buchung kann man einen attraktiven Zimmerpreis erhalten.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Loved this hotel”
text: I loved the people, the location, and the view. I just wished I had a little more time to spend in Chicago as I was literally minutes from Millennial Park and never made it 3 days. Kudos to the GMAC Conference organizers and the hotel staff!

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Great service for the price. I loved the complimentary happy hour, cookie buffet, and huge breakfast buffet.”
text: Great for the price and location. I love all of the complimentary activities. The room was huge and the beds were comfy. Service was quick and super nice. However, the elevator situation is a little strange and it takes forever to use them.

name: Hotel Allegro Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Wonderful Hotel in Theater District”
text:
My husband and I stayed for the weekend to see a play (the theater was right next door) and to see a ball game. We could not have been more pleased with the service and staff. Yes, the rooms are not as large as some hotels but this is an older hotel refurbished and is clean and neat and attractive. The bath is stocked with "extras" and the bedding is lush.
The staff was wonderful from check-in to checking out. The concierge, Mark, was great. He was very knowledgeable and obtained us tickets to the ball game at the very last minute (good ones). We did not have to wonder about any tourist things to do, everything was explained in detail and help given when needed. It was a great trip, made better by the service. You can always pay more for a larger, newer hotel but you will find no better service anywhere.

name: theWit, a Doubletree Hotel
title: “Cons Overshadow Pros”
text:
I've traveled for 5 years as a consultant and have stayed in a wide range of hotels across many states and countries. I value comfort over style any day. Overall, this one isn't bad, but for the price, it's hard not to feel ripped off. For $300, I expected more than friendly service, a good location and generic trendy room. I wanted a good night's sleep and that was sadly lacking. The entire stay, I couldn't help thinking about those Holiday Inn commercials about being smart and not overspending and how they were talking about hotels like this.
Pros:
- Rooms are nice...nothing bad, but nothing special. They try really hard to be trendy but the "unique" pieces don't really evoke any emotions for me either way.
- I like the music in the lobby and the nature sounds in the hallway.
- Staff is very friendly and accommodating
- Location is great for downtown Chicago
- Rooftop bar was your typical cool business people hang-out on a Thursday night
Cons:
- SO much noise. People sound like they're in your room and I wasn't even near the elevator. Tried to take a nap after a long flight...nope, housekeeping was extremely loud. Every door open and close sounds like your door. Woke up at 7am to a woman having a phone conversation for almost 2 hours. I don't know where she was, but it sounded like it was in my room. Not only could I hear every word she said, I could hear the person on her phone. Can definitely hear the train as well...including the train announcer saying "Doors closing."
- Bed was not great. It's a little on the firm side. Pillows were ok. It made me miss my bed at home. The sheets felt rough. and the sheets on one bed had these dark streaky stains on them...ew! Needless to say, it was hard to sleep soundly.
- "Cool" bathroom sink was very wide and shallow. It looked nice I didn't enjoy the splash backs it caused.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Westchase Mini-Suites
title: “Excellence...”
text: I want to give a great big Excellence to these special people Ressie, Denise Austin, Abraham and especially Paulette who puts her heart into the breakfast Bar in the am. Also am very please with the Front assistants who dilgentlly provide help in every area!!! Since my last visit in 2011, WHAT EXCELLENCE CHANGES for the better customers like my husband and I to enjoy our stay here in the beautiful Best Western Plus in Houston, Texas!!!! Thank You again staff for excellent service!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Beautiful, iconic Chicago hotel in the heart of the city!”
text:
Frank Sinatra, Judy Garland, George Burns, Frankie Vallee, and Nat King Cole have all performed at the famous Empire Room at the Palmer House Hilton. It’s a hotel that holds a place in Chicago’s history with the original hotel being built in 1871 and being destroyed in the Great Chicago Fire just a few days after it was finished. It was immediately rebuilt, and then rebuilt again in 1925. That is the structure that still stands today. The lobby is grand – these were the days when folks flocked to the lobby to socialize and people watch (remember no TV). It is still a great place to sit, people watch, and enjoy a drink. 
We visited in December so everything was beautifully decorated for Christmas. Our room was on the 20th – Hilton Club Floor. One room was a double and was very large – plenty of room to spread out with a large walk in closet and decent size bathroom. The King room was a bit smaller, but completely adequate. In both rooms, it looked as if the bathroom had recently been freshened up with new paint, wall paper, vanity and sink. The tub was a little tired but clean and I like the vintage look of an older hotel. The hallways are decorated with pictures of all the celebrities that appeared in the Empire Room. It was fun to see all the people that performed there from the 30’s to the 70’s. 
We were able to walk into the Empire Room as there were no events scheduled. It would be a great place to rent for a wedding or large party. 
The fitness center is very nice – lots of cardio machines, weight machines, plus free weights, exercise balls, and mats. It cost $10 per day, less if you have status with Hilton. The pool and hot tub? Well, we were there on a December weekend so there were lots of families staying in the city for a holiday trip…. therefore the pool and hot tub were crowded with kids. Maybe other times wouldn’t be so bad. 
The hotel staff was very good, friendly and efficient. 
Parking costs were outrageous! Park in one of the nearby parking garages and walk or take a cab to the hotel. It would be cheaper than the $55 per night at the hotel. 
Overall a beautiful, iconic Chicago Hotel in the heart of the city. Great atmosphere, great location.

name: Hotel 71, Wyndham Affiliate
title: “Great Value, Great Location"”
text:
Great Chicago Location. View of the river was beautiful.
The rooms were huge, especially compared to other Chicago hotels. The rooms were clean and the staff was friendly.
Only negative is the wait for the 1 elevator..sometimes up to 10 minutes. As long as you plan ahead, it isn't too big of a problem.
Will stay here again!

name: The Willows
title: “Jim bennett”
text: Great small hotel that has quick access to transportation and great location on north side. The included breakfast was adequate and staff was extremely helpful. The rooms were quite nice and very clean. We will definitely stay here on our next trip. Can't say enough about the friendly and helpful staff.

name: theWit, a Doubletree Hotel
title: “Chic and convenient for a big city getaway”
text:
My husband and escaped to the city one night and stayed here. It was a fabulous experience and we look forward to returning. Here's the rundown...
First, this is a Hilton hotel (actually, a Doubletree). My husband travels frequently for work and is a Hilton Honors members, so he was able to get an upgrade to a corner suite. We were on the 24th floor, NW corner. We had a lovely view of the river. I suggest you try avoid a room facing directly S/SW, as it's likely your only view will be of buildings and the L train tracks which run right outside the hotel. Even if you're not a HH member, it's worth asking for an upgrade. You might be surprised!
Our suite was clean and tastefully decorated with contemporary decor (see photos). There was a small kitchenette, table and TV/lounge area. Adjacent was a spacious bedroom with king bed and enormous windows facing north and west. The bathroom also was spacious and featured a shower and separate tub. "Roof" is the open-air bar/restaurant on the 27th floor (more on that below). We our room was directly below it, but you'd never know it. Speaks to the stellar soundproofing. 
Definitely make a visit to Roof. Admittedly, the drinks and food are not cheap ($15 for a glass of wine), but the atmosphere is fun. Roof takes up the entire west side of the hotel. The south end of it is enclosed while the north end is open air, i.e., no ceiling. Down the center of the north end is a large concrete table/counter with seats around. Directly down the middle of the counter is a fire tough that is lit during chilly evenings. You can visit their website to get a visual. I've been to Roof twice now and my biggest complaint is the service. Your best bet is to head directly to the bar to order your drink, otherwise expect a lengthy wait first to get have someone take your order, then to receive your drinks. It's a popular spot and after 9pm, the music gets turned up. And if you're looking for an intimate spot to meet someone for cocktails and conversation, this is NOT the place -- regardless of the hour. 
We didn't eat at Roof, but we did eat breakfast in the hotel restaurant. Service was prompt and food tasty.
Other things to note...
The lobby is tiny, and bustling with activity as it's on the corner of State/Lake, and steps from the L train. No need to have a car. 
The hallways have a sound system which pipes in birds chirping in the morning and crickets in the evening. It's very subtle, but nice.
All in all, it's a fun hotel, well decorated and clean, and located close to many attractions. Be sure to walk one block north and take the stairs down to enjoy a lovely walk along the river.

name: The Willows
title: “Very Friendly Hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Willows for Chicago Pride, and the staff was amazing and so very helpful. They went above and beyond to make our stay great! From helping us with our bags, to telling us the best places to visit. I would highly recommend the Willows Hotel to all my friends and also I hear talking about staying in Chicago. 
It was a fabulous Girls Weekends! Can't wait to do it again next year!!!
Erika Hanyzewski

name: Crowne Plaza Houston River Oaks
title: “Overall location and facility above average for business travel.”
text: I did appreciate the checkin service it was very quick and professional. The concierge - Mandy was unbelievable, she was very informative and reminded me of the talent normally found at a Ritz Carlton. She remembered all names of everyone in all parties and offered assistance and service information above and beyond. The overall hotel is average yet affordable but the showers are to way to small and the bath faucets are difficult to operate.

name: Hard Rock Hotel Chicago
title: “Un excellent choix”
text: Cet hotel est très bien situé pour faciliter la visite des principaux centres d'intérêt. La décoration intérieure, en rapport avec le nom de l'hôtel, est réussie. Qualité du service et confort très satisfaisants. L'ambiance générale de l'établissement est détendue.

name: Hotel 71, Wyndham Affiliate
title: “FANTASTIC HOTEL, FANTASTIC CITY”
text: After a long and exasperating internet search I finally booked my vacation at the Hotel 71 and it was wonderful!!! I trust in TripAdvisor and did alot of searching. This hotel got semi-mixed reviews. I always weed out the bad and am glad I did. From the time of check in to check out it was great. The room is not the biggest that I have stayed in but it was very comfortable for it being a very old building. The bathroom is very spacious and the TV in the bathroom is a nice touch. The bed was very comfortable. The best thing is the free WiFi it helped me keep in touch. The front desk personnel was always friendly and helpful making sure to say hello whenever we came into the lobby. I would definitely stay at this hotel again. It is very close to everything. In Chicago, you don't have a car, the public transportation is always available and goes whereever you want to go. Do yourself a big favor and book your next stay at Hotel 71. The only thing to remember is if you are taking the "L" from the airport to the hotel is to make sure you go the right direction when you come out of the train station, we got confused and were walking the wrong way and got confused so we had to take a cab to put us back on the right course. The directions on the hotel website said 3 blocks but if you are new to the city, you don't know which way north is.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Sad stay!”
text:
I wish I could like this stay but I find it hard to convince myself to do so...everything from check in to room condition, air-conditioning to concierge to check out was disappointing....
I am here only because my conference is here...
PS: be careful to check your bill when you check out. The mini bar systems is cranky.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Westchase Mini-Suites
title: “From Iowa to Houston”
text: We stayed here for about a week, and the Suites were wonderful. There was plenty of parking, and the the rooms were comfortable and fresh. The kids hit the pool immediately and the wife and I were able to sit and visit with Houston family members. The service was very good...Kudos goes to everyone, but especially Paulette at the breakfast bar-I'm usually not one for breakfast, but Paulette and the breakfast bar started the day off perfectly! She treated everyone like family, and made our stay there very relaxing. Thanks Best Western!

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Just OK”
text: Great location but the rooms and bathrooms are quite unimpressive. The restaurant is quite overpriced but I suppose every hotel's is however this one comes with a rather surly bartender .

name: Hotel 71, Wyndham Affiliate
title: “WOW!”
text:
now i read all the good, bad & ugly about this hotel here on tripadvisor and decided to "take a chance" . i really cant believe anyone would write something bad about this place. ok, so they don't have a pool get a grip, go somewhere else if you really want a pool. 
when i checked in there was a problem with the reservation, because of 1800 hotel NOT because of the hotel, and they were very nice about the whole thing and right off the bat the lady at the front desk said not to worry they had rooms available. John Castronovo the business sales manager came out explained the whole situation and took my booking upgraded my room and the room rate was even LESS then what i had booked at. John apologized for the mistake made by 1800 hotels and was very helpful through out my stay. Being the dummy i am i read here that there were no "black out" curtains in the room, so as soon as i got in the room i looked, nope couldn't find them either, and i had a view room on the river so that meant when it was time for bed the room was still bright as day from the lights outside. the next morning i spoke to John and he was shocked at the story i told him. john said he would send a crew up right away to check because of course there are "black out" shades in the room. so i went back up to the room to check again for myself, and OF COURSE they were there. housekeeping had just pushed them back farther then i had looked.
i had room 1014 a premium view room with two queens. was a fantastic room, the bathroom with two separate vanities a huge tub, walking in shower with built in seat. the wifi in the room was great, very fast. i was able to buy movie tickets on line and make dinner reservation too. there are 4 elevators, NOT two as someone here has stated. more correctly TWO BANKS of elevators. i never waited more then a few seconds for one. the gym on floor 37 (or 36) is very nice all new equipment and has a great view too.
not sure why some people have complained about the property but in my opinion, its a very nice place to stay and i'll be back for sure.

name: James Chicago
title: “Cannot ask for more!”
text:
Pros:
- Great location. Mins away from a lot of great shopping.
- Comfortable beds, quite at night.
- Very friendly and knowledgeable staff!!
- Modern look and feel. iPod dock in the room, Large flat screen tv.
- I had to go back to my room because I forgot my sunglasses while the cleaning lady was cleaning the room. She asked me to swipe my room key to make sure I was staying there. Felt good knowing they don't let any random stranger walk into rooms.
Cons:
- Slow elevators.
- Rooms were slightly small.

name: Omni Chicago Hotel
title: “Excellent hotel, great deal, terrific location!”
text:
We got a terrific price on a suite at the Omni Chicago after friends told us about a deal by using a promotion code from the Travel Zoo website. Booking with only 24 hours notice we got a beautiful suite on a Friday night (12/19/08) for only $129. Upon check in we were also given a $25 voucher to use towards food or drinks in the hotel's 676 Restaurant. Our room was on the 18th floor with a south facing view over the city and was comfortable, roomy, modern and very clean. The hotel's valet parking cost us $25 for the evening which is comparable to local parking garages but much more convenient. 
A definite highlight at the Omni is the 676 Restaurant on the 4th floor which has excellent views over Michigan Avenue. We enjoyed drinks at the 676 in the evening and a delicious brunch there the next morning. The brunch was only $19 per person and included a choice of organic meats and cheeses, made to order omelets and a wonderful selection of fruits and fresh breads. All in all we were very happy with the Omni's service, value, and amenities. I would absolutely stay at this hotel again and recommend it highly. 
As a native Chicagoan who enjoys frequent weekends at the City's hotels, I happily look forward to spending time at the Omni again.

name: ACME Hotel Company Chicago
title: “a very pleasant surprise”
text: A great hotel right in the middle of downtown, super service, a thermos of coffee by your room when you wake up, good breakfast. Very cool looking with a young modern look. Price is excellent and the hotel quality is far above it's price: hence the great surprise

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown
title: “Comfy but dated”
text: We picked this hotel due to the location near magnificent mile, and it was a convenient location. Many restaurants and shopping areas. It was expensive for the condition of the room. The bathroom was clean but needs updated. There were three of us and the mirror/vanity area was extremely small, only one person could use it at a time. One person tried to use the mirrored closet doors but they came off the track. The pull out sofa for the third person was uncomfortable and we had to pay 10.00 extra. Why? Overall the staff was very pleasant and helpful. I would stay there again due to location.

name: Hotel 71, Wyndham Affiliate
title: “No problems...great time”
text:
We were upgraded upon arrival from our king/river room to a king on the 36th floor with a conference room attached! It was a little odd to have another room with a HUGE table in it, but the views were great. We had three windows facing in different directions...the river, towards the lake, and one toward the art museum and water beyond. 
 The bed was comfortable, plenty of pillows. The bathroom was nice, the bath products smelled like sherbert! Our daughter didn't have any problems with the internet.
 Great time.

name: JW Marriott Chicago
title: “Lovely hotel for a weekend break”
text: My mom & I took a shopping trip to Chicago for a weekend break. The room was FABULOUS! Very clean, lots of space, the staff were so friendly and helpful, and breakfast room service was excellent. I really miss that huge tub in the bathroom!

name: The Silversmith Hotel & Suites
title: “Never again”
text:
It seemed like such a promising start: they had a room ready for me when I got there very early. Sure it was a queen, and I'd paid for a king, but I could put up with that.
Sadly, it was all down hill from there...
After heading out for the day I returned to the room for the evening and tried to set up a wake up call, but for some reason the phone in the room was set to 'rotary' and while I could hear it churning, it wasn't connecting with anyone. I gave up and set alarm on my watch and went to bed. But I couldn't sleep because of the stratchy things in the bed: turn out they were toe nail clippings. Yep, the bed had only been made after the last user, the sheets hadn't been cleaned. Disgusting.
In the morning I went for a shower, but the setting on the shower head was stuck between two settings and wouldn't move. All I was getting was a dribble by the one cluster of massaging jets: the other two clusters were too full of gunk to send water out. DISGUSTING!
I told the Front Desk this (again, phone not working... had to go down in person), and when I returned for my second (and thankfully last) night the shower was working properly and the phone working. And the sheets appeared to be clean. Unfortunately the rest of the bedding wasn't so good.
I had noticed it was cold the previous night, but there was a major cold snap on in Chicago so I just put it down to that. That day, however, had been mild and so there shouldn't be a problem. That is when I really looked at the bedding (other than the toenail-ridden sheets) and discovered there was only one blanket on the bed. A summer-weight blanket. And the bed spread was also a summer weight blanket. Also, no extra blanket in the closet, as you'd expect in most hotels. I spent the first half of the night waking up every hour, getting up and turning the heat up in the room and then tucking myself back in and hoping it would get better. Finally, around 2 am I got up, maxed out the heating, folded the blankets over a few times and got fully dressed before returning to bed. I managed to sleep the rest of the night until my early wakeup call.
When I tried to check out using the on-screen process it said that it could not be done. Great! Another stop when I am trying to rush out... I go to the front desk and am told that I couldn't check out that way because I had prepaid the hotel through a third party, and I had to pay for the incidentals. I said, yes, but I gave you a credit card for the incidentals at check in. It is the credit card that you just finished saying "should I just leave it on your ...... card?" I am treated to a lecture on how if I had gone through the hotel to book my room this wouldn't have happened. Way to punish your customers!
To add insult to injury, I am coming off the elevators on the first floor and the bell man walks by, heading away from the front door. I am almost at the front door (a good 30 feet away) and I hear "Hey you! Do you want a cab?" yelled at me. No, I don't want a cab, what I want is something to help me forget the horrible stay I had at this disgusting hotel.
P.S. It is a day later and I now have a major head cold. Wonder why...

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown
title: “Great Location”
text: I made reservations on the internet but had a few questions. When I called the hotel directly the staff was very friendly and helpful. Check in was a breeze and the staff from the bell hop to the check in couldn't of been more helpful. The only negative was the pull out couch. It was old and very uncomfortable. Everything else was great.

name: Hotel 71, Wyndham Affiliate
title: “Exactly what we were looking for”
text:
We ended up at Hotel 71 after a Hotels .com search for downtown Chicago hotels close to the magnificent mile.
The price was right and were were surprised with an unexpected upgrade to an Executive Deluxe. The newly renovated room was lovely, the view spectacular, and the ease of walking around to where we wanted to go was exactly what we were hoping for and more. Michael and Kareem were wonderfully welcoming and the only thing I would change is to forego the valet parking and just park the car for the weekend. We never drove anywhere!
Walked the mile and then over a few blocks to Fado's Irish Pub.. authentically fun atmosphere, cold beer and excellent appetizers while we watched the football games.
That night we walked- literally- one block over the bridge to eat dinner at Smith and Wollensky . We had a river view window table, excellent service and the best Steak Oscar I have ever tasted.
We'll definitely be back to Hotel 71

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Westchase Mini-Suites
title: “Todo perfecto”
text:
Salvo la tapa del control del aire acondicionado que estaba a punto de romperse, todo en la habitación era perfecto y de la mejor calidad. Las camas, toallas, y los productos para cabello y cuerpo fueron excepcionales. El desayuno excelente, con pancakes con la forma del estado de Texas.
Una muy agradable estadía.

name: Dana Hotel & Spa
title: “honeymoon perfection”
text: what a great location and beautiful setting....obviously once in a lifetime but I would absolutely recommend this place to everyone traveling to Chicago. The rooftop balcony was cozy with little fire pits and a great view. Our service was excellent as well, the valets, concierge and other staff all very helpful in finding great places and making the best of our trip.

name: The Silversmith Hotel & Suites
title: “Too noisy”
text: We booked two rooms for one night through Travelocity for $206 per room, including taxes. When we checked in, the hotel had reserved one room for 2 nights. Luckily, I had my comfirming email with me. They honored the reservation without question or complaint. (Thank you, Shannon.) We ended up with one suite and one regular room. Both rooms had views of brick walls and HVAC units--no view. The suite had a bedroom that was a separate room. The hotel is located immediately adjacent to the el train tracks and the noise from passing trains was very intrusive, even though we had rooms in the back. At midnight trains were still going by almost constantly (one to two per minute). It reminded me of that scene in Blues Brothers where they are at Elwood's place and the el rumbles past. Jake says, "how often do the trains come by?" Elwood says, "so often you won't notice it." I'm a good sleeper but I could not get to sleep until I got up and found some ear plugs that I had thrown in my bag for a different trip. The ceilings are 12 ft high, the WIFI is free, and the location is wonderful (just off Millenium Park, a block west from the Art Institute). The valet parking was $46 per day. The Self Park at 55 East Monroe (about 1.5 blocks away) is the nearest, I believe. I paid $63 for 28 hours at the Self Park so I wished I had used the valet service. The staff was friendly & helpful. Despite the pluses, I would never go here again because of the noise problem.

name: ACME Hotel Company Chicago
title: “Excellent Stay!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at ACME in mid-August, and we still talk about it when someone brings up Chicago! 
Hip decor, friendly staff, comfy bed, perfect location, awesome views, convenient parking, great price, and yummy continental breakfast. I loved the little extras: the robes, morning coffee delivered to our door, and IPhone docking station for music. 
In fact, we loved our room and our stay at ACME so much, that we decided to stay in and relax during our evening in town.

name: Hotel 71, Wyndham Affiliate
title: “Excellent location and spacious rooms”
text: I stayed for 6 nights at Hotel 71 for a conference. I would strongly recommend staying in a "river view" room. They have the best view of Chicago for a very convenient price! It is in the heart of the city and close to many places. But if you are looking for luxury and entertainment in the hotel (SPA, swimming pool, etc.), this might not be the ideal hotel. Yet if you want to discover Chicago and are looking for a comfortable place to stay, that is THE hotel you should go. I think my room was about 40-50 m2 and I had a King size bed! Breakfast is not included, but just on the corner there is a very nice place for both breakfast and lunch. If I go to Chicago again, I would definitely stay there!

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown
title: “Downtown location with service, value, and style!”
text:
