Absolutely delighted with this property, and the almost residential feel of its location. The staff at this Fairfield Inn offers the same personable & professional service attitude I'd expect from a larger Marriott property.
Magnificent Mile shopping less than 2 blocks away; 5 miles from Wrigley Field; many major museums, amusements, sites, and venues - and hundreds of restaurants - within 5 minutes by cab. (Ask the care staff for a list.) You can also pop across the tree-lined, two-lane street for high-end fast food, or repair next door for a marvelous prix fixe new-French dinner at Les Nomades.
Clean, safe/secure, with basic business services (and printer for your boarding pass), and a more-than-continental breakfast service is included with your room. Basic rooms are not large, but the beds are high-end comfy, so who cares? :) (Also no in-room safe, but surely the front desk has a solution.)
Don't think, just book... and enjoy!

name: James Chicago
title: “Amazing stay!”
text:
The staff at the James were lovely and helpful. From the moment my taxi pulled up to the door to the minute I pulled away, they were courteous, polite and pleasant. Check in was easy. The room was lovely. I loved the tap water bottle and the little desk nook. It was quiet at night - couldn't hear any other guests, and I feel like this is one of the only hotels I've ever stayed in where I didn't feel too cold or hot at night without having to adjust the temp controls. The bed was luxurious and soft and the in room robes were cozy. 
Staying at The James was everything a hotel stay should be: comfy, quiet, pampered and worth the fair price.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “A great place in Downtown Houston”
text: Probably my sixth stay at Magnolia Houston this year -- always great!!

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Dirty”
text:
I stayed at the Sheraton Hotel and Towers for a second time this March because the conference I was attending was at the hotel. The location is good (walking distance to most everything). However, the room was filthy. I had to move the bedside table to plug in a charger and it was disgusting to see the amount of dust and discarded items behind there. I even left the table pulled out in hopes that housekeeping would clean behind there but they never did the entire time (4 days) that I was there.
I also looked under the beds and it was very dirty under there.
The windows were so dirty I couldn't even enjoy the view.
Finally, wifi was a joke. I could barely load email nevermind watch any video.

name: Hotel 71, Wyndham Affiliate
title: “Hotel 71 far exceeded my expectations”
text:
My reservation with Hotel 71 was obtained through priceline and we had 40+ people traveling with our group. Our group was a combination of both adults and small children and the hotel was great in accomodating both. The hotel rooms are beautifully decorated and extremely spacious. The views of the Chicago River are amazing from the hotel. Getting in/out of the hotel was very simple as the hotel offers valet parking with in/out privelages that is included in your nightly parking fee. 
From the time we checked in until the time we checked out every member of the hotel staff went above and beyond to ensure our stay was enjoyable. This ranged from trying to get all of our parties on the same floor or at least close by so that the kids could easily play in each other's rooms to the front desk employees "chatting" with the kids about their American Girl dolls and their excitement to visit the new store. 
The bellman and valet parking attendants ensured our cars were ready and waiting for us the second we walked out the door and jumped to help unload our items and get them to our room quickly when we returned from our excursions for the day. 
The maintenance staff helped us with a vending machine problem and because we were not able to get the machine to work he had breakfast delivered to our room for all of our troubles so that my daughter was able to get some food before she competed that day. Not only did he resolve the problem but he actually checked back with us later in the day to ensure that we received the breakfast and that everything was okay. 
As a guest, these gestures may be small but they meant a lot to us as it shows that the employees of Hotel 71 truly care for their guests and are willing to go the extra mile to ensure that their stay away from home is as comfortable and enjoyable as possible.

name: The Silversmith Hotel & Suites
title: “Mold and Mildew Problem!”
text:
I really wanted to like this property and, I wanted to wait for a response from the hotel before I wrote my review but, 3 weeks later and no response.
The Silversmith is a beautiful property in a very convenient location with a gret bar and deli on the property. The room and bath were large and nicely updated but we just couldn't get past the horrible smell in the room. This was not the 'room closed too long and a little musty' smell. This was a 'knock you to the floor when you open the door' smell! Overpowering mold and mildew stink!
We told the front desk as soon as we checked in but they had no other rooms available. We asked that it be cleaned or sprayed and they said yes but, when we returned from dinner it appeared to be exactly as we left it. We went across the street to CVS and purchased 2 cans of Lysol spray and attacked the bath, carpet, drapes, bedding, etc. then left for the evening. We returned to a slightly better smelling room but, really, got very little sleep all night.
Mold can raise very serious health problems for many people with any kind of respritory issues and should be taked very seriously! I understand that issues occur when you are running a business but what really bothered me is the way we were just waved off with no compensation or appologies. The staff was polite but ineffective in offering any type of resolution to this problem - even after I completed the 2 surveys they sent me - no response from the hotel what so ever!
When booking a 4 star hotel such as the Silversmith, you should be guarenteed a clean and comfortable room. The Silversmith did not meet my expectations for the basics and my valid complaint was not handled well at all.

name: Courtyard Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile
title: “Nice, great price for location!”
text: Chicago definitely beats NYC on downtown hotel prices! Busy Christmas week, but this hotel delivered in all categories. Stayed here for points, but location was awesome, bar, "Viand" great, friendly desk & valet. Only negative, I had to actually call inside once for the valet to come get my car as I sat in it, streetside. Be warned, however, parking prices are some of the highest in the country...$42/nt valet...self park, no in & out, $30/nt.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “wonderful stay”
text: The hotel is impeccable. checked in with Lanette and she genuinely cares for our needs. Our room wasn't ready when we arrived but she offered to take our luggage and also (later we found out) she gave us an upgraded room. Breakfast at the restaurant downstairs is a MUST! Best breakfast ever; fresh juice station, bakery station, chefs stands for different tastes.. etc. Exceptional services through out the hotel! The concierge was really helpful (sorry that we don't remember her name but her mother in law lives in Boston),and you even see the general manager adjusting the picture frames in the lobby. What a wonderful experience! Thank you. Michelle and Darren

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown
title: “Mike Campbell-Front Desk is Wonderful!”
text: When we were checking in, Mike Campbell asked what brought us to Chicago. When I told him that we were in town for a funeral, he offered his condolences. As soon as my son and I had gotten into the room and put our suitcases down, there was a knock on the door with a porter giving us a box of goodies and a lovely note offering sympathy and signed "The Homewood Suites Team". That one act of goodwill and thoughtfulness impressed me greatly. Hilton, whatever latitude you've given your employees to do things like this for guests is terrific. Mike, I'll never forget your kindness during such a sad time.

name: Courtyard Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile
title: “Very good hotel but room for improvement”
text:
This is actually a very good hotel. The rooms are nice, the restaurant is good and staff is very friendly. It shows that the hotel is recently renovated although the room doors to the hall way are not very good isolated. Everything that happens on the corridor will be witnessed in the rooms. In a previous review there were some complaints about the internet but that seems to be resolved completely. In room we had perfect wifi connections with 2 laptops an iPad and an iPhone. Congrats on that!
Although you can call for room service to clean you room at a certain time it is always a surprise whether they had cleaned the room or not. Very annoying when you return to the hotel after a day trip and the room is still not cleaned! This should be an easy fix and should be fixed right away.

name: James Chicago
title: “Average stay -- food was dreadful”
text:
Well located for shopping and central to most of Chicago, I chose this hotel recently over the conference hotel during a speaking gig in Chicago -- I thought well for one night I'll choose style over convenience 
Not a good choice!
The hotel is lovely -- light and airy, the check in was smooth, I got my Flip upgrade and it went downhill from there 
The "suite" was oddly set up with silly furniture in the living area - not conducive to lounging at all -- the couch was horrible to even sit on and noisy as all get out -- air conditioning that rattled, a low vibrational hum that clicked on and off all night and the worst room service food ever -- delivery was friendly and prompt the food was tasteless and cold 
After no sleep and learning that the car service doesn't start until 4 (please put that in your information package) i had the wonderful experience of a surly, couldn't care less waitress at breakfast and more bad food -- really David Burke?????? 
Check out was smooth but at no time did the front desk even ask me how my stay was -- trust me I would have told them 
Lovely to look at but uneven to stay at

name: The Silversmith Hotel & Suites
title: “I am down-grading my rating, but still a nice place”
text:
This was my third stay here, and I'm a little disappointed about this last trip. First, prices have gone up significantly; it's still a fine "value," but our "suite" was on par price-wise with a nice room at the Renassaince/Westin-types. 
When we landed at the airport, I called to ask the El Stop to detrain. I was calling on my cell. The woman who answered said, Yadda, yadda, "I'm with a guest now, please hold." So I held. 5 minutes later, I hung up. I tried again, same thing. And I held. I called again later, as we were now getting closer to downtown and I was a little nervous. Same answer, so I shouted out "I just have the quickest question," and she started arguing with me! You can tell I'm peeved about this. It's b/c service here used to be so wonderful, and there were always plenty of staff in the past. I had chalked it up to a single problem until I was at the desk later that day and the staff person did the same thing. I told her it was okay with me to attend to the caller, which she did (I have no idea if it was the same person).
This was our first stay in a "suite" here. True, two rooms, which was our goal. However, and I guess this is in keeping with Prairie style, the wall between the two rooms is 3 feet shorter than the ceiling. This defeated the purpose of having a separate work space for me apart from my husband. Too loud.
Gym is 3 aerobic machines. Not a big deal in nice weather, as you are a block from the walking areas, but that's 6 months of the year that are touch-and-go.
Business Center is $5 to use (each time), and only one computer prints. If you stay on 10th floor with the breakfast room, the servers are TOTALLY stressed out on weekends (but they're sweet). Bagels weren't even bagels, stale bread in square bagel form. But the zucchini bread was awesome. Coffee very good.
Location is still prime, prime, prime. And not nearly as expensive as the Palmer House.
I had felt the pleasure of staying here was in part the service, and I found that lacking this time. Hopefully, it was just a passing phase.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Typical conference hotel”
text:
Stayed here during a conference and thus very good rate. Nice lobby, friendly service despite absolute zoo of people checking in and out. Location is good - near to magnificant mile but nice by the river and view out over the lake.
Mixed bag overall as with many of these big city conference hotels - hotel is older and shows its age in various places, especially in the bathroom which was clean but needs some maintenance (regrouting and a long crack big enough to put your finger in between the counter top and sink basin) or better remodeling. Bedroom very nice with all white cotton bed linen, great view towards Lake Michigan, antiquated heating/ac that adjusted eventually. Room service breakfast - just over $14 including all charges for a bowl of oatmeal that took 45 minutes to deliver. Pluses - large bowl. Minuses - poor flavor, miniscule bowl of poor quality dried fruit, supposed to come with cream which is actually a glass of milk. hhm. (Starbucks does far better with oatmeal. lol.) Typical of such hotels, decent choice if you get a good rate.

name: Dana Hotel & Spa
title: “Amazing!”
text: I chose this hotel because of it's location for my wedding and my company does a lot of business with them (I did a little name dropping when booking my block of rooms!). From the first phone call for reservations to the moment we pulled up with our luggage, the amazing service didn't stop until they put us and our luggage in our car 2 days later. My new husband doesn't like boutique hotels and even he was impressed with the level of service we received (and he loved the big down comforter on our bed!). They couldn't do enough for us and our guests. I want to find an excuse to stay there again since I live in the burbs!

name: The Silversmith Hotel & Suites
title: “Holiday Inn Plus”
text: The bottom line is that this is a Holiday Inn. A little nicer furnishings but basically a Holiday Inn. The biggest issue I have with the hotel is the location. It's right on Wabash and the "L" runs 20 feet away every 3-5 minutes. We had a room in the back which I requested and the "whooshing" sound went on forever. The noise is an annoyance, but not a prohibitive issue. Staff tries hard. All but one young man who works on Sundays and has an attitude. Management probably knows who he is. I won't give his name, but he's slight of build. Couple we were travelling with had a problem with a distinctly moldy smell in the room. They were finally moved, but it took a lot more arguing than it should have. And this was dealing with the manager, not my arrogant friend. Room rates seem to be all over the board on this place. Weekend rates can be reasonable or outrageous. We stayed for three nights. We had three rates and the highest rate was twice the lowest. And you don't get a lot of warm fuzzies walking on Wabash after dark. The hotel insists there's no problems, but they sure have plenty of security in the ground floor entry. In terms of hotel preference, the Silversmith ranks in about the middle of the pack of Chicago hotels.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Great Location, Beautiful Hotel, Decent Rooms”
text:
My Fiancé and I took the train to downtown Chicago for our anniversary. We choose this Hotel because of its great location. We booked the hotel through Priceline so we were very happy with the cost. I was very impressed by the lobby of the hotel. Everything is Marble with gold trim. There is a beautiful bar and cocktail lounge in the lobby. Our room was smaller but had a huge marble bathroom. There was a walk in shower that was lovely.
We loved the location because we could walk to Michigan Ave and go shopping. We could also walk to a bunch of different restaurant. The view was not so great because it looked straight at another building and we got a close up of their brick walls.
The hotel had a few shops and a coffee place located directly inside of it. 
We loved that the hotel so much historical value inside of it. I am not sure if I would rate it a 5 star hotel but it was very nice and we would defiantly stay here again. It is walk distance from the train station, but I would recommend a cab ride in winter.

name: The Willows
title: “Our second stay at the Willows”
text:
Excellent inn-like hotel in pleasant area of North Chicago, with easy access to centre of city. There are plenty of restaurants, coffee shops, shops,,cinema, bars etc in the immediate vicinity. The hotel is situated less than 10 minutes walk to Lakeshore Drive and the amazing attractions and facilities of the people friendly lakefront. 
Continental breakfast and newspapers are available (self-service) in the lobby. We usually loaded the tray and brought it back to our room. Coffee, tea and snacks are provided 24 hours a day. As we were helping out with our newborn grandson who lived with his parents a couple of blocks away, that 24 hour service was a bonus!The rooms are a little dated but clean, comfortable and warm. Maid service was very good.
The reception staff, day and night, was excellent. Advice and assistance were given readily and always with a smile. Maybe because it is a comparatively small place compared to the modern high rise city hotels, the staff seemed to know each guest and all were greeted with a cheery 'good morning' or 'good evening'. I must single out the young lady on duty during the day, whose name has slipped my mind. Besides being generally helpful, she surpassed herself on my last day when I was checking out. I had ordered a cab and waited outside for the usuall rapid arrival. She noticed I was still there a few minutes later and sent out another staff member to flag one down on the street. 15 minutes later i saw her racing towards me. She herself had run up to the high street and spent ages trying to hail a cab in a very busy morning rush hour period. No success! However, she suggested she arrange a private limosine service to the airport which would cost $10 extra. 5 minutes later I was on my way- many thanks!

name: Carlton Inn Midway
title: “Nice lovely hotel!”
text:
The stay at this hotel was so pleasant. I booked a room after reaching chicago midway airport and the staff kindly let me do it. They were very cooperative.
The hotel room has all amenities in it and was very clean.
I am glad I stayed at Carlton Inn Midway hotel.
I would recommend it to anyone who can/wants to spend $100/night for a neat stay!

name: Comfort Suites
title: “Stay here, don't bother looking further”
text: This hotel is awesome. The location cannot be beat with cvs walgreens etc just outside the diir. The staff are ammazingggg. Warm, kind, helpful- you feel like family and that's part of what makes this place a gem. The free breakfast is an added bonus with lots to pick from hot & cold. The units are huge and views are stunning. The finishes might be a little old and not fancy but I don't care and believe me you won't either. Great stay. Will be back and tell others. Love this place and Eileen the manager is super!

name: James Chicago
title: “Always great!! still my Choice No1 in Chicago.”
text: The James has the perfect combination of location and service. Great staff, clean and it has the “James” signature that always has been offering. Rooms are fantastic, great bedding, turnover service is a nice touch, and toiletries from “Intelligent Nutrients” are awesome... daily showers were a perfect wake up!!! Breakfast was delicious with great service. Front desk service and concierge amazing great...There was a negative minor thing, related to the paint maintenance in some common areas of the building.... really minor thing... but they need to be addressed in order , for the management to keep up the standard of this hotel within the competitive market in the “Windy City”. Always will be my first option to stay in Chicago. Thank you to The James’ team.

name: Courtyard Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile
title: “What more could you want?”
text:
I have had many trips down to this hotel and I wouldn't stay anwhere else! 
It is a beautiul, clean property like all courtyard mariotts; the staff are amazing. From the second we arrived to the second we depart on all stays, the staff have been outstandingly friendly 
It is the perfect hotel in the perfect location; it is a 5 minute walk from the hancock building, a short walk to navy pier and the tribune tower. It couldn't be in a more perfect place.
The front office manager Martin is (like me) from Manchester,UK and he went above and beyond for all his guests and staff.
The hotel restaurant is beautiul, but I also recommend the little italian retaurant aross the road.
On site is a great restaurant, starbucks, shop, fitness centre, car park and swimming pool. 
I love Chicago, its one of my favorite cities in the world,and wouldnt choose anywhere else to stay but the CY Marriott Mag Mile.

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Great hotel”
text:
Just had3 night stay at Amalfi and highly recommend it. Walking distance to shops,restaurants,and many attractions.
Very central location. Large clean rooms.
Great cockails every evening and continental breakfast daily included in rates. Special thanks to concierge Suah Siki who was so helpful and friendly - he helped make our stay even better.

name: Courtyard Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile
title: “Can't Beat It!”
text:
I really can't say enough good things about this hotel. Arrived Saturday, March 13 at noon and were allowed to check in early with no issue, the only delay was the front desk person spent a few extra minutes trying to match a room to my request online (high floor, corner). The various doormen I encountered were always helpful with directions, getting a cab, or just holding the door open. Didn't use the pool or gym, but both looked nice. Room was very clean and quite, beds comfy. Location was outstanding, 1/2 a block to Michigan Avenue, a Dunkin Donuts across the street, and a Trader's Joe's right across Michigan Ave. There are about 5 Starbuck's, Subway's, and Walgreens withing walking distance, as well as the bus stop to the museums. All the tourist eateries are within easy walking distance (Gino's East, Rainforest Cafe, Ed Devevics). Don't miss Carson's for Ribs, maybe the best Ribs and Pork Chops I've ever had.
Also a short cab ride from Second City.
Really, everything was perfect.

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Great Hotel”
text: Fantastic Location, couldn't be better. Rooms are nice, everything you need. Breakfast is laid on some tables near the lift in the morning on each floor - so people wander down in their pyjamas, grab some fruit, coffee, croissants etc and head back to rooms. 2 out of 3 mornings I was there - breakfast was scarce - few crossiants, a couple of tired bananas - that sort of thing - it could have been much better. That said, the hotel is great - if breakfast is important to you - it might not be the ideal place - but apart from that it's all good.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Nice treat”
text: We live a little ways out of Houston and came in for a play at the Alley Theatre and stayed the night at the Magnolia. Very good service, room was nice, great shower/tub, bed and pillows were great. And this is the quietest hotel I have ever stayed at.

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Great small hotel in downtown Chicago”
text: We loved our stay at the Amalfi. It is very well located which makes it easy to get to Michigan Ave and to the Chicago Art Institute. We only had to take a cab one night to the restaurant. Rooms are nicely appointed, clean and with all the regular necessities, iron, bathrobes, hair dryer etc. The hotel has simple clean contemporary look which is very nice. We enjoyed all the staff they were very helpful. They feature a continental breakfast on each floor which is very smart. They also have a complimentary manager's happy hour every evening from 5:30 to 7 pm which is perfect. My only suggestion is to put a TV listing in each room so guests don't have to scroll through all the listings to find the one you are looking for. (I am not from Chicago so I don't know the channel #s.)

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Palmer House Hilton....very historical”
text: This hotel is full of reminders of the "star filled" past, with pictures and dates from all the stars that performed in it's Empire Room in years past. The lobby is breath taking, full of elegance of times gone by. The rooms however were a bit "strange". They were nice, don't get me wrong but there were some odd variances in the size of the rooms. My room had two beds and was...well...pretty normal to say the least. I mean it was perfectly adaquate and the beds were very comfortable but it lacked....something. I mean you could see the age of the place, in the door jams and edges of the doors where they had been scrubbing and painted over. And the "entertainment / TV stand/ Dresser just didn't seem to fit the decor at all. I realize I may just be a bit picky, but no flat screen either, just a big old 32" TV and the walk in closet didn't have a switch on the wall, but a pull string to turn on the light. I guess it's the little things sometimes. When I went to a colleagues room he, his room appeared to be a room that almost wasn't, it was noticably smaller than mine. Then we went up to another colleagues room and his room appeared to be a suite, it was about double my room. All for the same price. I was on the company's dime so I didn't say anything but if I were paying I would have had to discuss this with the front desk. They charged a $10 fee to use the gym which I thought was kind of strange also. The rest of the hotel is amazing, the lobby/cocktail area is incredible as was the food. The location is great also a train station right out side for convienent dash to the airport when we were leaving, and tons of attractions within walking distance. I'd also recomend "Millers PUB" right around the corner, the food was good, and the atmoshphere is amazing as well. All in all I'd recomemend this place to anyone traveling to the area. Just realize that it's NOT A NEW BUILDING, and what it lacks in more modern decor it makes up for with charm and romance of a time gone by.

name: James Chicago
title: “Bad Info on Twitter & Smoky Hallways”
text:
I picked Chicago for two reasons: the proximity to CLE (5 hour drive for us) and the awesome rate I got on Jetsetter. As I was perusing for hotels, I saw the special for The James. Their website looked cool and they responded to my questions about their gym on the Twitter, so I booked it.
We checked in and immediately noticed the super hip vibe. Being not so hip, I demanded that the Chef take ridiculous pictures of me posing with art chairs. Because we had absolutely NO SCHEDULE for the weekend, we headed up to our room to relax after the long drive.
Honestly we found ourselves a bit disappointed with The James. When we arrived on the 7th floor we noticed immediately the overpowering cigarette smoke waffling through the hallway. As we opened the door to our room, we were greeted by two double beds. Nothing says anniversary like two double beds! I called the front desk to let them know I reserved a kind room and would like to move. The front desk informed me that unfortunately they were sold out of kings. Obviously it being our anniversary celebration I was a wee bit ticked about the bed situation. I also picked The James because of an interaction I had with the hotel on Twitter. The husband and I have been working out religiously every single day and I didn't want our trip to slow down our momentum. Before I booked with the Jetsetter I took to social media to ask if anyone had stayed at The James and if so how was the gym? Did it have a sauna, steam, or spa? Within a few hours The James official Twitter responded that yes it had all of the amenities I was looking for and they looked forward to my stay. I immediately booked the hotel.
Fast forward to the first morning of our trip. The Chef and I awoke and headed to the gym. We were completely disheartened as we paraded through the lobby down a flight of stairs in our gym clothes. How tacky. Once we walked in we were greeted and asked where the locker rooms were. The girl at the desk informed us that there were no locker rooms and if we needed a restroom there was one in the lobby. Not cool. I asked about the steam and sauna and was immediately shot down. Apparently I had been misinformed by The James CHI Twitter the girl explained. Feeling a little steamed that I had specifically based the booking on the rooms and the gym I hit the treadmill with a furious vengeance.
The James had it’s issues and I would probably never stay their again however it does have some major pluses. The location is the jam. You are literally in the heart of the city surrounded by shopping, restaurants, theatres, the river walk, and anything else you heart possibly desires. The staff is also fantastic. The front desk worked really hard to get us in a king room and lucky for us they managed to on day #2 of our trip. They also moved us to the top floor so we wouldn’t be surrounded by smoke. The staff really improved on what could have been a really really bad stay.

name: The Willows
title: “A real gem”
text: Just finished staying at the Willows Hotel in Chicago. Although our room was small, it was very comfortable, and the staff went out of their way to help in any way they could. Very friendly, and they were very helpful in arranging transportation and advice on local restaurants and directions. Great location in Lincoln Park, easy walking to some great restaurants and to a couple El stops when we wanted to go down to the Loop. Highly recommended if you're looking for a small quality hotel on the North Side.

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Great Hotel”
text: Great hotel that is close to many attractions. Rooms were clean and nicely decorated. Staff were helpful with information on local restaurants/tours and assisted with bookings/reservations. Breakfast on every floor was wonderful with lots of variety. I would definately recommend this hotel.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “21 anniversary”
text: By far one of our fav hotels in Houston! They treat you like family. They greet us by name even at crub side. We stay here evey year. Rose petal and the works for Wedding and anniversary packages just ask! Close by 4 star dining

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Wonderful!”
text: We were in Chicago for a family wedding. All of our family stayed here. The staff was very friendly and helpful. It was so nice to walk in and the staff greeted us by name. Yes, parking was expensive. It was slightly higher then some of the public parking but you could take the car out and return at anytime. Great location. We walked and Used the hop on hop off trolley tours, which was suggested by the staff. Great place to stay.

name: Comfort Suites
title: “Excellent Stay at the Comfort Suites”
text: I had a short stay at the Comfort Suites for a podiatry conference that was held at the Hyatt Hotel down the street. To my surprise the staff at the Comfort Suites was amazing. One of the days, the guest services manager even provided me with her umbrella for my morning walk, as it was raining in Chicago, that morning. Everyone was so gracious and courteous- welcoming me every instant, with a lovely smile. I was comfotably escorted to a room with a fantastic view of the river and beautiful avenues of dowtown, Chicago. This stay was affordable, convenient, and in the heart of all the city's attractions. Thank you to the wonderful staff. See you next time. Comfort Suites has now become my preferred business hotel.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Relaxing in Chicago”
text: The lobby was so relaxing, I actually fell asleep there listening to the piano and watching ppl. The french resaraunt is awesome, especially at breakfast. Room service was great and it was an all around relaxing few days.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown
title: “Awesome style! Good location!”
text: This hotel is so neat. It reminds me of the jetsons or something. Very contemporary. Within walking distance to hard rock cafe and shopping. Staff didn't really pay attention to us at all, but we didn't need anything so that was ok. We only stayed one night and were shopping all day, but the time we spent there it was everything we needed. Big tv, big bathroom, awesome style, comfy beds. We took a lot of pictures in the lobby and nobody paid attention. Have no idea about breakfast or any other amenities though as we didn't utilize anything but the room.

name: The Willows
title: “Perfect Hotel”
text:
We just returned from 5 nights at The Willows. The hotel is wonderful and the staff is very knowledgeable and helpful. This was our first trip to Chicago and after reading several reviews online, decided we didn't need to pay the high prices of hotels downtown, and booked this hotel directly from the property.
We stayed in a king room on the 2nd floor. The hotel has only 4 floors for easy access to the lobby. The continental breakfast was perfect. There's nothing fancy about it, just your typical bagels, muffins, danishes, cereal, yogurt, fruit, etc. There's also hot coffee and water for tea available all day as well as lemonade and cookies and fruit at 4pm. The snacks and drinks available throughout the day was a life-saver as my husband and I both came down with bronchitis and spent more of our vacation inside the hotel than we had planned! Needless to say, the beds are comfortable and splurging for the king size room is great, especially if you plan to spend any time in your room. The king rooms come with two comfy chairs for reading or TV watching.
I can't say enough about the neighborhood. We took plenty of cash with us thinking that meals out would be expensive in the big city, but came home with over half our cash supply. The neighborhood seems to cater to young professionals and has lots of great food options for fairly cheap! The best find was Molly's Cupcakes on N. Clark...the service was impeccable and you've never tasted cupcakes so good or so creative! Of course we also tried the popcorn, hotdogs, and pizza. Stay away from Geno's East. I heard they've changed the recipe and it's not the same as what some might remember. We loved Chicago's pizza on N. Sheffield (they have other locations too). That's the pizza you should go for. 
I wouldn't say this is the best hotel we've ever stayed in, but for a city hotel that is tourist and local friendly, you can't beat the deal. It is close to the "El" and runs along a VERY safe Brown/Purple line. We're already planning our return trip when the weather gets warmer!

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Overpriced, airport like hotel”
text:
I am stunned that this hotel is rated as four stars on Trip Advisor. Simply because a hotel charges an arm and a leg for a room does not make it four stars. I stayed here for two nights, not because of my decision but those who were traveling with me. To start, we spent 45 minutes in the lobby waiting to check in. The lobby is a very expansive atrium that reminds me of an airport ticketing hall. Guests were corralled through roped lines to check in at one of 3 open stations out of about 20 that were at the desk. The room is loud and packed with people - not a good way to start a "relaxing" trip.
We stayed in the West tower. I cannot complain about the room, but also don't have anything great to say about it. It was about the size one would expect in a Chicago hotel, but I have seen better quality of furniture and materials in a HI Express. For the price you can do much better in the city.
I had no issues during my stay until leaving. We called ahead to have our car (which was parked valet) brought around to the front. We were told it would be about 20 minutes. This was fine, as I understand they have a lot of people in the hotel and a lot of cars to move. However, after going downstairs 20 minutes later and not finding our car we were a bit miffed. We asked the valet if it was coming and he said yes, they were just behind. After waiting another 20 minutes we asked again and he had no record of the car being requested. They managed to get the car about 15 minutes later - more than an hour after being initially called.
I think the valet service speaks to a lack of staffing at an enormous hotel (biggest in Chicago). If you are looking for a hotel where you feel like herded cattle - this is it. If you want a relaxing trip I would suggest looking elsewhere. Probably somewhere smaller.

name: Residence Inn Chicago Downtown / River North
title: “Great location and value at the Residence Inn Marriott”
text:
We have just returned from a weekend trip to Chicago where we stayed at the Residence Inn Marriott. This hotel was newly updated with everything you needed for a great cost. 
We saw a show at the House of Blue which was a walk-able distance from our hotel. There were ample amount of restaurants, bars, shops, etc from the hotel as well. This hotel is in the heart of the city and very close to the river. The famous Harry Carey's restaurant/bar is directly across the street, which we went to twice! There is an Einstein Brother's Bagel's next door as well, which was convenient for snacks/coffee. 
All the rooms were suite style with a modern kitchen, sofa and chair, flat screen TV, bed and bath. The kitchen was not fully equipped, but had everything that was needed for a week: glasses, plates, bowls, wine glasses, pitchers, can opener, tupperware, etc. 
The continental breakfast was open early and was great!! They had multiple varieties of warm drinks (which were good while being in Chicago in Nov!) such as coffee, tea, hot chocolate, etc. There was a waffle machine (popular for the kids!), muffins, bagels, cereal, eggs, bacon, etc. This was one of the top free continental breakfasts we've had. 
The staff was friendly and helpful. They helped us with directions, getting taxi's, restaurant/bar suggestions, etc. One of the best things they did for us is be honest on what was a walk-able distance for us from the hotel versus needing a taxi. 
For the value, this was a great hotel. We plan on coming back to Chicago and staying here a second time. I would recommend this to anyone with kids and dogs (they have a pet program)!!

name: Dana Hotel & Spa
title: “OK Hotel”
text: I stayed at the Dana September 2-6, 2011. The hotel is in a great location; within walking distance of the Red Line, Michigan Avenue, the Art Institute, Millenium Park, and the Navy Pier. My check in was OK, although the redhead at the desk wasn't very friendly or welcoming and she appeared incredulous when I gave my name(?)...I then offered ID although she did NOT request it. The negatives I encountered were: long brunette hair found twice in the bath towels (that's why I bring my own wash cloth); the room smelled stale (I bring air freshener); the room was too dark even with every lamp turned on. Positives were: the most comfortable hotel bed I've ever experienced!; friendly and attentive bell hop/doormen - Caesar was great!, friendly and patient concierge; I loved the wide plank flooring in the room and the ceiling to floor windows. I would be comfortable recommending the Dana to a friend. I plan to revisit Chicago Spring 2012, but will try another hotel just for the sake of being in another area of the city.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Palmer house -- impressive architecture and historic charm”
text: I had read mixed reviews of the Palmer House on this as well as other sites. Our experience there was delightful from the moment of check-in to our visit to the concierge desk. The location was convenient for our purpose (visiting various Chicago universities). My teenage son and I were given a spacious room with two beds and renovated bath despite our low cost Priceline booking. Obviously, this is not a "new and shiny" contemporary hotel, but an historic structure. I happen to like "quirky" so the retrofitted corridors with celebrity photos and odd nooks & crannies were interesting to me! The lobby is gorgeous; our room clean and quiet; the staff friendly and accommodating. I felt as if I was in a first rate, city hotel and I was. I would not hesitate to stay here again.

name: Courtyard Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile
title: “Great Property”
text:
Great location, just a block east of Michigan Avenue in heart of Mag Mile. Very clean and comfortable room, larger than I expected. Staff was very polite, courteous, and helpful. 
Small pool, but again very clean. Kids loved it, but don't expect Olympic lengths.
Heed the warnings regarding oversized vehicles in the parking garage. It is tight!
Would definitely go back without hesitation.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Wonderful Hotel!”
text: It is a wonderful hotel! It is beautiful, clean and so comfortable. I highly recommend it!

name: theWit, a Doubletree Hotel
title: “Enjoyable Stay - But Watch Out for Charges”
text:
I was prepared to give theWit a totally positive review, as I recently enjoyed a nice 2 night stay there for business. I have stayed at many other places in Chicago, and I will add theWit as a hotel to consider when coming to the city. The hotel is modern and clean, and the rooms are a nice size with comfortable beds, modern bathrooms, and a fairly updated look. The restaurant - State and Lake - was great, both at breakfast and lunch. As a Hilton Diamond member, I received breakfast vouchers (for a set $$ amount) that could be used at State and Lake toward any items on the breakfast menu - which was much nicer than the typical continental breakfast offering at other hotels. The hotel location is nice as well - right by the L and within walking distance to the State Street shopping and restaurants. 
The only real disappointment, for me, came after I checked out and had been home for a few days. As a Diamond member, I received 2 small bottles of Fiji water in my room (along with oranges and a granola bar - very nice!). There was also a $6 bottle of Fiji water in my room (in addition to mini-bar offerings - which, it is important to note - the mini-bar is sensored, so if you move something, you are charged for it). I never touched the $6 bottle of water, but did drink one of my complimentary bottles of water during my stay. At check-out, my hotel folio showed no charges outside of room and tax... but when I checked my credit card statement, I was charged - TWICE - for the $6 bottle of water. I called the hotel and they have credited my card... but since this was a business trip, it will now create additional expense reporting hassles and delays me in completing my paperwork. Compared to the good things about my stay, this is not a major issue - but I felt it necessary to warn other travelers to beware of extra charges following the stay (a co-worker of mine experienced a similar issue). I don't usually have these types of issues within the Hilton hotel family, so this is a bit of a disappointment after an enjoyable hotel experience.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Loved the hotel, needed a better room”
text: The historic Palmer House has undergone a beautiful renovation, but it's hard to change the size of the rooms. Our king was so small, we could barely move around. The bathroom was good for one person only, and that's if you kept the door open. Finally, the walls seemed paper thin. I would go back, but only if I made very sure what room I was getting and where it was located. The staff was great!

name: Dana Hotel & Spa
title: “All is good in the Dana hood!”
text:
Hip room, bar, spa and hotel in general. Not thrilled with the check in folks..but hey, I'm not there to make friends. Concierge super helpful as I needed to buy 2 bottles of Veuve and he sent me to a place closeby that I would NEVER have found alone just strolling along (that place alone is worth a viist if you are a wine buff!).
I had a corner room with floor to ceiling windows..loved it!
I'm not a shower person though..I like my baths so this was the only downside for me...though I will say the shower was big enough to have a party in!
I'd stay here again with friends, but not on business or with family..just a bit too hip for them.

name: The Willows
title: “the willows hotel”
text:
Hotel tres chaleureux par son accueil et son organisation. Café ou thé disponible a toute heure. Excellent confort de la chambre.
Choix des chaines de TV gratuites un peu limité mais WIFI gratuit..
Quartier sympatique et centre ville tres facile d'acces par bus ou metro.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Lovely place in downtown Houston”
text:
Great place to stay especially when you can catch one of their specials, such as the free valet parking.
Room rate includes a cocktail hour, bedtime milk and cookies and a breakfast buffet.
My only issue is that on the several nights we have stayed there has been a private event on the lounge level and the cocktail hour and milk and cookies has been in the lobby and you don't get access to the billiards table.
Also has a nice pool on the roof of the building.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Chicago - Downtown
title: “My customers were happy and so was I”
text:
I used the Hampton for a multi-day business seminar, and the staff could not have been easier to work with or more accommodating. It was an exceptional value for the location and my customers had nothing but positive comments. The fire station on the next block is noisy, but everyone I asked said they slept through the activity. If you have a large group in the meeting room, rent the microphone, as the acoustics can be challenging.
Overall, I'm very pleased with the experience and would return for both business and leisure.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Great place for business travelers”
text:
A group of us planned a business trip up in the windy city during January. I have used the Hyatt before [years ago] and remembered I enjoyed my stay so I booked 20 of us in it again.
Check in was friendly and easy. My room was on the 12th floor and the others were higher up. The elevators, although plenty of them, where very slow and seemed to stay on the penthouse/executive levels for extended periods of time. 
There is a great work out room but can get very crowded and overbearing especially if you are trying to use free weights at all. I finally gave up on working out on day 4 because it was just too much [not the hotels fault] so if you do enjoy working out, best to bring some bands or other items to use in your room.
The rooms were spacious, updated and clean. I had no issues with housekeeping although I felt there may have been some snooping in my stuff while I was out [nothing stolen but just not how I left it]. The TV is large and swivles so you can view it from the table and work area, the bathroom was a good size. The lighting in the bathroom really is poor but they do offer a magnifying mirror that has a light so that is a bonus. I heard from co-workers that their water pressure absolutely stunk, but mine was excellent. 
There is 'The big bar' downstairs or as we like to call it, the wall of liquor! Always packed and very friendly wait staff. Great area to eat or have a night cap. The breakfast buffett was amazing but was $22 dollars a person. So we ate their once and then either got something from the vendor across from the giftshop or ate at the Billy Goat Tavern which is across the bridge. 
We did rent out the Astor Suite one night for a customer meeting. The suite was awesome and again the staff that helped us make the meeting a sucess was great.
There was always taxis available if needed and plenty to do! The location of this hotel is great and although the photos I have added are not amazing they do give you a feel for the place. 
Overall, I would definately stay at the Hyatt again!

name: Comfort Suites
title: “Amazing Hidden Gem!”
text: Despite being right on Michigan Avenue at the river, you could walk right past this place and never notice it. My friends and family and I stayed there for my 30th birthday and it could not have been more amazing! The rooms were huge - each equipped with a full kitchen, stove, dishwasher, etc., and even a washer and dryer! The staff were more than accommodating and the complimentary breakfast was an added bonus. We were able to walk to our downtown destinations and save ourselves some cab fare. If you're planning a trip to Chicago I HIGHLY recommend staying at the Comfort Suites on Michigan Avenue!!!

name: MileNorth, A Chicago Hotel
title: “Absolutely beautiful hotel”
text: We live in Michigan and have made many trips to Chicago with our son (he was 7 at the time of this trip) and the Affinia was the best hotel we've ever stayed in. We stayed in a queen suite with a fold out couch. The room was beautiful, and the whole hotel was immaculate. I can't comment on service, since we didn't order any, but the location was great. It was within walking distance of the pier and many other Chicago attractions. There was also an awesome pizza place right next door. It's more of a business-type hotel, so I wouldn't recommend it to people who want to have entertainment at the hotel for their kids.

name: Crowne Plaza Houston River Oaks
title: “first stay at crown plaza”
text: Have to say this place is an absolute joy to stay in. After 35 days at work overseas, no one wants to spend his first two nights in a motel. But after staying I wished I could move here. The staff is excellent. My hat is off to Mandy and Sheila. There were several other employees that helped also. Hoping my stay at other crowne plaza is close to this. Thanks to the staff and employees. Will not look any further when in Houston next time.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Very nice hotel. But don't book just for the happy hour and milk and cookies.”
text: Very nice hotel. I made my choice for this hotel based on the evening happy hour and milk and cookies before bedtime. If I had to do again I would not have based my decision on those two things. My husband and I left the happy hour which turned out to be a small nook in the lobby serving drinks in paper cups. When we returned from dinner it was time for the cookies and milk which all we saw was 1 tray of cookies and no milk in sight. Pretty sad. But the rooms were nice and the location was perfect.

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “First time in Chicago”
text: My husband and I travelled from Ireland to the US on April 28th and spent five nights at the Amalfi. We are so glad we chose it. The location is perfect. We had a room on the 4th floor which was wonderfully quiet. The bed was extremely comfortable and so we slept very well....a necessity when sightseeing every day. Absolutely loved the fact that breakfast was available on each floor by the lift. Also loved the happy hour where drinks and finger food were served. This hotel is really good value. We loved Chicago.

name: Comfort Suites
title: “Great -- especially for young families”
text:
We've stayed here twice -- two adults, and 3/6 year old kids. The kitchenettes are very handy, with a real fridge, microwave, and stove. The King suites have a separate bedroom and an easy-to-use sofa sleeper. The included breakfast is a great time-saver. Rooms on the NW or NE corners have good views of the river. It's within walking distance to many things, and within a block there are buses that'll get you (without transferring) to Shedd/Field Museum and Museum of Science and Industry. There's a Walgreens and a few reasonable fast food joints on the same block. The lack of a drop-off area didn't seem to keep anyone from stopping along Michigan Ave to load/unload. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The value was great for what you get.
The only notable problem was elevator congestion.

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Great Staff/Great Location”
text: I just stayed at the Amalfi with my sister and niece (6 years old) while we played tourist in Chicago. The staff was amazing and hotel was the perfect experience. Clean, modern and I loved the breakfast service on every floor (lots of folks in their jammies grabbing a pastry or coffee. The nightly cocktail hour is such a great idea. How nice to be able to unwind after a long day hitting the sites. Nordstrom's is conveniently located around the corner along with tons of great restaurants and sites within walking distance. We had several special requests and the staff were responsive and fast to meet our needs. Would definitely stay there again!

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown
title: “Fantastic Fairfield”
text: Every single staff member that we came in contact was exceedingly helpful and polite. In most hotels the staff are typically polite because their job depends on it, but this hotel's staff seemed to enjoy their work and it was obvious in their treatment of their guests and easy, friendly manner. The accomodations were clean, the price was reasonable and the hotel is barely 2 blocks from the heart of Michigan Ave and within walking distance of the Navy Pier.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown
title: “Great Hotel!”
text:
After reading the reviews on the site, I stayed for three night at this hotel in late January for my first visit to Chicago. We pulled up to the front of the building where we were greeted by hotel staff who helped us unload and valet parked our car in a nearby garage. Being a hotel in the midst of downtown, the ground floor is not much more than elevators that take you up to the main lobby on the 6th Floor. The room we stayed in was on the 12th floor and had a nice view of downtown. 
The room itself was a nice suite. Although not brand new, the room was clean and the bed and pillows were extremely comfortable to sleep on. It may have been the best sleep I've ever got at a hotel. The kitchen area of the room was one of the highlights with enough kitchenware for the average traveler to prepare their own meals if they desired. The cleaning staff did an excellent job straightening up after us each day. The hotel offered free breakfast and the offering was great. The breakfast eggs were fantastic. If you're adding in meal costs, this was a huge plus with getting delicious, hot breakfasts cooked for us each day. They do offer a diner M-F each night but with being in a great restaurant city like Chicago, we splurged for eating out (By the way, I highly recommend the Big Bowl Thai restaurant nearby. Everything is fresh and was the best restaurant we ate at. Ginos East and Al's Beef were ok. Heaven on Seven was good too.)
The staff was very friendly and helpful at all times. We made a few special requests which they were prompt in service. Location in downtown Chicago couldn't be better. You're two short blocks from Michigan Ave (Magnificant Mile) with tons of restaurants nearby within walking distance. Leave your car in the lot and take the bus where you want to go. Bus routes can take you easily to the museums, united center, willis (Sears) tower, the loop, just about any place downtown. It's the cheapest way to travel downtown and other passengers are average people.
Without question I would stay at this hotel again. In fact, this is the only hotel I'll consider until someone can show me a better place to stay in Chicago.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown
title: “great location - views limited”
text: Great location to walk to all the sites. Unfortunately, the view is limited even on a higher floor due to being amongst all the other tall buildings. Suite was nice and roomy with comfie bed. Shower pressure could have been better. Major downside was there are only 2 elevators for 19 floors of suites so you did have to wait quite a long time.

name: theWit, a Doubletree Hotel
title: “OVERRATED”
text:
We stayed this last weekend & were so very disappointed. We were quoted a different rate at the desk (had this reservation since June) & it was $100 more/ night. I told her the rate I booked the room for, back in June & she said if I could "prove it", they would give me the original price.
The elevator, hallways + our room were hotter than hades, despite having the AC on 65 or below. The king size bed is no such thing (had to be a queen size) & was uncomfortable. Internet is $10/ day for the lowest bandwidth. There were always four valet "boys" on duty yet they only said hello & didn't do anything else. We had one great concierge & 2 snotty ones. Every one at the front desk was rude except for one lovely guy that gave us terrific recommendations. One of the managers told me to "think positive, it will be ok" when I complained that my key didn't work in the elevator, leaving me floating from one floor to another. For being a rather new hotel, it was nothing short of trendy, cheap stuff that already looks years old.
There are wayyyyy too many other cool places to stay for wayyyyy less money. It put a damper on our weekend getaway.

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Wonderful Experience!”
text: My husband and I frequent the Amalfi. It's our favorite hotel in the city. Not only is the cocktail hour and continental breakfast phenomenal, but the hotel employees really care and strive to make your experience great. My husband and I stayed last Saturday night for my birthday. Melissa, who works at the hotel, made reservations for us at Roy's for dinner. She set us up with a great table and the restaurant even put an insert in the menu for my birthday. Thank you so much, Melissa! We truly had a great experience at the Amalfi and you really helped to make my birthday memorable.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Chicago - Downtown
title: “Definitely going back!”
text:
Finally! A great place to stay in Downtown Chicago that is affordable, clean, in a great location and with a superior staff! I couldn't believe the state rate was such a bargain, and even though the valet parking wasn't cheap, the service provided made it a good value.
The front desk staff on check-in was exceptional. Very polite, professional and friendly. We asked for directions and recommendations several times for restaurants, the lakefront, museums, and a local bar - all of their assistance was spot on. 
The guys at the valet stand were so helpful. We decided to go around the corner to get a bite to eat and asked them to keep the car close by so that we could use it afterward. They made the arrangements and did it all without skipping a beat. Though I would allow 15-20 minutes lead time when you call for the car from the garage.
As a Hilton Honors gold member, they upgraded me to a spacious suite with a king size bed in the bedroom, a full living room, and a kitchenette with a mini-fridge and microwave. The decor looked new and everything in the room worked great and was spotless. I loved the cabinetry they used (looked custom) and the granite countertops throughout.
The breakfast service was one of the best I've had at a Hampton. Lots of choices, including different selections for fresh fruit, and good hot entrees. Plus it's located on the second floor with great views of the street below. They had breakfast attendants who were responsive and helpful.
The doors to the rooms are not sound-proof however. But since I had a suite, the noise didn't make it through to the bedroom.
All in all, one of the best Hamptons I have visited.

name: James Chicago
title: “Perfect spot and perfect staff.”
text:
I spent the forth of July in Chicago and couldn't have stayed in a better place. Perfect location, very good staff. 
They were doing some remodeling of some rooms without any inconvenience for the guests.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Great experience! Thanks Brian!!”
text:
I'm extremely happy with my experience at Sheraton Towers Chicago. I arrived very early in the morning but Brian was kind enough to go ahead and let me check into my room. The shuttle bus I rode from the airport stopped at several downtown hotels but none looked as nice as the Sheraton. The inside of the hotel is just as spectacular including the INCREDIBLE view from my room. Every part of my experience, from the greeters at the front door to checkout, exceeded my expectations. The hotel is adjacent to a very beautiful river that runs through downtown. The icing on this experience is that the room rate was very reasonable. There were many hotels in the area with higher prices but I can't imagine having a better experience. 
Oh, one more thing.... the beds are incredibly comfortable.

name: theWit, a Doubletree Hotel
title: “Ok Experience”
text:
Positives - 
-Great Location 
-Great Room. Very modern. Awesome view! 
-Spa option is great! 
-Good live music.
Negatives -
-Room was not ready when I arrived. Hotel gave me a 30$ cedit at the roof top bar where 2 drinks cost 34$. Although I gave them my cell # they never called me. After 2 hours I inquired again where they found me a room. Total inconveince after a long day of traveling. 
-You have to wait forever for an elevator. 20 min some cases. One night it took me 25 min get a bucket of ice! 
Overall feedback - Disappointing for the money. At the price I paid and the competition of 5 star hotels in Chicago I expected more. The last thing I want to be doing after a long day of traveling is wait for my 5 star room. Vacation is short.....Time is important.

name: James Chicago
title: “Friendly & central - highly recommended”
text:
I'm just back from staying 3 nights at The James with my wife, who'd been on a programme at the Kellogg School of Management the previous week.
The staff are very welcoming and friendly, and keen to deliver great service and advice. The free wifi is invaluable, and the compliementary bike hire was great. What makes The James ideal for a short city break however is its location; within easy walking distance of so many of Chicago's great attractions, shops, restaurants and bars.
A few minor gripes which had I paid full rack rate would have irked me more - scarcity of storage space in the room, lack of subtle bedside and wardrobe lighting, and comfortable chair/desk to use laptop easily. That said, I wouldn't hesitate to go back, and will consider the sister hotel in New York when I next visit Manhattan.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown
title: “Outstanding value on the Magnificent Mile”
text:
Downtown Chicago is expensive. Expedia saved the day and found a great rate at a Marriott property on the Magnificent Mile. Close to shops, restaurants, and transportation.
Clean, excellent beds and bedding. Thick walls so you don't hear the next door's TV. :-) 
Enjoyed having a PC and printer in the lobby. Was able to print the airline boarding passes there.

name: Omni Chicago Hotel
title: “Sono stato benissimo”
text:
Sono stato davvero bene in questo hotel, ho trovato tutto quello che cerco in un hotel solitamente. Gentilissimo e simpatico il personale, bello il bar ed ottimi i cocktail. 
Anche la colazione è stata all'altezza lla situazione, con una bellissima vista su Michigan Avenue. Molto spaziosa e comoda la camera con anche la living room all'ingresso. Ve lo consiglio. Un po' caro il valet parking ma a Chicago funziona così.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Chicago - Downtown
title: “Sorry, won't be back”
text: We stayed over a long weekend to see sights and visit family. We stayed in a corner suite that faced the fire station. It was a very noisy not only because of the sirens, but also because our furnace fan was loud and ineffective at heating our corner suite.(I would have hated to stay in that room when it gets below freezing outside.) The maintenance man came and turned the furnace on after our first night without heat. Old unused baseboard furnace vents outlined the outside walls of our rooms and were falling off with some of the metal parts just laying on the floor. The windows were thin and opened without screening to the outside street below. There was much confusion over our booked room through out our stay. Thankfully, Ronnie was very helpful and straightened our charges out. The cleaning staff did a great job of cleaning our room over our three day stay. The complimentary breakfast was good. The hot tub was a warm tub our first night, but on the second night, it finally did get hot. The sauna did not work. The pool was clean and had plenty of towels for guests. The afternoon front desk was the same workers all three days we were there. At times we found them to be unprofessional and rude. There are several choices of hotels in Chicago, therefore next stay to visit our family, we will look for something else.

name: theWit, a Doubletree Hotel
title: “Great room, great location”
text: Loved the room, bathroom was especially great and spacious. Reception staff very welcoming & concierge helpful. Housekeeping not that great at getting the room serviced at a decent time & no way communicating with them - couldn't even establish what language they spoke & couldn't get them to tell someone to sevie the room. Didn't eat at the hotel, but roof bar not as exciting as everyone makes out and very overpriced.

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Amazing Amalfi !!”
text: Was in town for four nights. A very nice hotel with courteous and friendly staff. I really liked the casualness of the breakfast buffets on each floor. Would highly recommend to anybody who wants a conveniant downtown hotel.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “You ruined my wedding day.”
text:
It was my wedding day and we had made reservations for a room at the Magnolia for our wedding night. We stopped by the hotel after our wedding ceremony and my HUSBAND (yeyuh!) checked us in. He also requested to be upgraded to a suite and paid an extra $200.
We went to our reception and during this time, my wedding planner took our belongings to our hotel room for us - some snacks, a bottle of champagne, and our overnight bags. In the bag, she left a wedding gift from one of my bridesmaids containing a card and $350 in cash. My planner dropped these items off with the front desk, telling them to make sure these items get put in our room before we got there later that night.
We arrived at the hotel at 2AM, but our things were not in our room. Since it was already late and we were exhausted, we just went to sleep. I have to add, since we did not have our overnight bags, this meant we slept with our CONTACTS IN, unbrushed teeth, had no change of clothing, and I had to sleep with all my makeup on. Now girls, you understand when I say this feels AWFUL. Sleeping with a full face of airbrush makeup on? It's my wedding night and I have break outs and clogged pores waiting for me in the morning? NOT OK.
In the morning, we called my planner and she assured us that she had dropped our things off. After talking to the valet, the bellboys, and the front desk, we finally discovered at noon that the hotel had taken our things TO THE WRONG ROOM. They took it to someone else's room! We look through our things, and the gift from my bridesmaid was missing. THEN to top it off, we find out that our "upgraded suite?" NOPE. We weren't even upgraded! We were in a regular room!
When my husband talked to the hotel to try and remedy the situation, they said that they could do nothing but file an incident report for the stolen items (which may or may not get recovered) and refund us for our upgrade. UH, YEAH - isn't the refund obvious? We didn't even GET the upgrade in the first place. Can you do anything else for us? Nope!
On a normal day? OK, fine. Things happen, I'll just not stay at Magnolia again. On my wedding night? SO not cool.
Terrible customer service, mediocre hotel. The 1 star is because our REGULAR room was clean.

name: Dana Hotel & Spa
title: “Best buy in Chicago”
text:
I travel to Chicago 3-5 times a year for business and have staed at the Dana the last three times. I really like it. The location is fantastic, particularly for the price. I've stayed at the Westin, the Sofitel, Double Tree, Monaco, Amalfi, Affinia, etc. and think the Dana is the best buy. No tubs in the rooms and two tiny drawers are my only complaints. In addition, the welcome staff is sometimes inexperienced and the concierge IMHO knows less about Chicago than I do (he sent us to The Frog Bar for seafood and it was mediocre.)
The restaurant at the hotel is really great, and the sushi bar is extraordinary. With breakfast included, this is by far the best buy in Chicago.

name: Hotel Burnham - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Burnham made Chicago "My Kind of Town"”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Burnham Kimpton Hotel the weekend of November 16th. I was there on business but arrived early to take in what Chicago had to offer. As we had arrived early we had lunch at the Atwood Cafe in the hotel and met the most amazing waiter Nick. Now mind you, all of the staff at this hotel were phenomenal but for me Nick went above and beyond. Not only did he wait on us through lunch, he also made certain when our room was ready and had a surprise of "Garrett's Popcorn" (a must) and a very nice note placed there ahead of our arrival. Darryl was also a wonderful employee to meet; in fact everyone we encountered was terrific. Would HIGHLY recommend this quaint and personable venue for anyone looking to experience not only the windy city, but the warmth of Chicago. We are looking forward to another visit soon and will definitely repeat our stay at the Burnham Kimpton Hotel.

name: Crowne Plaza Houston River Oaks
title: “Another Great Stay”
text: I have stayed at this hotel now several times and it is always a great stay. Reasonable rates, super friendly staff and also the staff seem to be truly caring. I have been undergoing treatment at MD Anderson Cancer Center and they also have a shuttle to the center. The rooms are renovated and clean. The beds are super comfortable and the hotel also has a very nice view from the upper floor rooms. This hotel is always my first choice when going to Houston.

Address: '160 E Pearson St at Water Tower Place'
name: The Ritz-Carlton Chicago (A Four Seasons Hotel)
title: “Love this hotel”
text: Just returned from a stay with my granddaughter. This is my new favorite hotel. We felt so welcome there that I will visit Chicago again just for the opportunity of staying at this wonderful hotel with the nicest, most helpful staff. Love, love this hotel.

name: Hotel Burnham - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “An excellent representation of the Kimpton brand”
text:
If you've stayed at a Kimpton hotel before, you know what to expect: a boutique-style hotel with character; cheerful and good service; excellent cuisine; good location. The Hotel Burnham in Chicago does not disappoint: from start to finish, my husband and I had a marvelous stay here!
We were in Chicago for five days to visit family, and we picked this hotel because 1)location and 2) its affiliation with the Kimpton brand. The young staff are excellent; always up-beat, always helpful and informative, and quickly responsive to any reguests. It is obvious that they are "house proud" and have high morale, which is always a boon to guests.
The lobby is small, but with a cozy sitting area off to the side with a fireplace that I'm sure gets lots of use in the fall and winter months. A free glass of wine may be enjoyed here in the late afternoon..a nice Kimpton touch. The very fine Atwood Cafe is adjacent to the lobby, which is open all day, with a delightful "al fresco" section for the summer months. The Cafe is famous locally for its delicious Sunday brunches, so reserve ahead if you wish to partake. The price for a quick lunch there was jaw-dropping for us ($73.00 for two bowls of soup, a selection of artisan cheeses and bread, and two glasses of wine) but perhaps, being from Las Vegas, we are just not used to Chicago prices. I will say however, that, although simple, the quality of that lunch was superb: the soup was delicious and the cheeses were exceptional.
Our room was too small, as sometimes happens with Kimpton, as theirs are always older buildings that have been redone, but the decor was lovely and the accommodations were spotless.
Special kudos to the room service staff. My husband and I always treat ourselves when possible to room service for breakfast when we travel, and the service provided here was exceptional: it was pleasant, accurate and fast.
The location was perfect for us, although some might wish to be closer to the upscale shopping that is offered in the Miracle Mile area.
If you wish to dine off-site for dinner, The Trattoria No. 10 is exceptional! It is less than two blocks away, and offers top-fo-the-line northern Italian cuisine in a charming basement "bistro" atmosphere. The service was outstanding. (more under a separate review)

name: Comfort Suites
title: “Incredible value, best location, spacious rooms, amazing staff!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel 18 months ago, and liked it so much that when I knew was visiting Chicago again this was the only choice - and I'm so glad I came back!
I was very late getting to Chicago - my train was delayed by 8 hours - and when I contacted the front desk to tell them that I was on my way and not to cancel my reservation, I was reassured by the very friendly staff. When I eventually arrived at half past midnight, the welcome I received was lovely. The room was amazing, with great views of the Tribune building, and I couldn't get over how big the room was. The bed was very comfortable, I had everything I needed to cook, and the washer/dryer was the icing on the cake. Breakfast was also fine, although I'm glad I didn't wait till the last minute to go down to get it, as the food was running out!
This hotel would be perfect, apart from a couple of little things:
 - there's only two lifts, and there's 25 floors. This meant having to wait quite a while sometimes to get on the lift, and this wasn't helped by the cleaning staff wheeling their carts on at the same time as people were checking out. My suggestion is that the staff either bring the carts up early, or wait until after the checkout/going out rush to bring them up. 
 - the server at breakfast was quite abrupt - which surprised me as the rest of the staff were so pleasant. 
 - Free WiFi was great, as was the computer and printer in the lobby. However, the WiFi didn't work in my room on the 21st floor.
These are all minor things though, and overall this is one of the best hotels I've ever stayed in. Next time I'm in Chicago I'll definitely be booking this hotel!

name: theWit, a Doubletree Hotel
title: “Yes this hotel IS ALL THAT !”
text:
You can believe the hype when it comes to this hotel. Modern, clean, friendly staff, good food and the little details that made this place all that. 
My husband and I stayed for my 40th birthday. We were greeted at curb side by the valet. It was pouring out and they walked me to the door under their umbrella, very nice touch. We received our warm cookies at check in.Waiting in our room were chocolate covered strawberries, champagne and a "happy birthday " note. Very sweet !! We ordered room service that night. Very tastey food and very reasonable price. The next day we had lunch at State+Lake. We enjoyed it so much that we had dinner there too. Would recommend stopping in to grab a bite there any time of the day. They do make the best pancakes. * Note if you are planning on going to the ROOF (lounge+bar) stop at the front desk. On Friday and Saturday night you must get a wrist band and be escorted up on the elevator. You feel VIP treatment. Also worth it. We had no issues with check out the next day or any issues with valet. We will stay here again and I will recommend this hotel to all our friends.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Decent Hotel and fantastic location”
text:
We stayed at the Sheraton for 2 nights earlier this month. The rooms are decently sized and clean, albeit the accomodations are a bit outdated. The safe to keep valuables is operated by a physical key, so you must be careful not to lose it. The entryway light was a bit annoying because it kept blinking before it finally burned out the next day. If I had to give one complaint, it would be that housekeeping did not service our room after we left for the day late morning, even though the service staff was still on our floor when we were leaving. It wasn't a big deal since our stay was so short, but still. 
The location of the hotel was fantastic though - convenient to Navy Pier and extremely walkable to all that downtown Chicago has to offer. I would stay here again for the value compared to other hotels.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “excellent service - great location. fine hotel”
text: would return anytime without question. quiet well-appointed room. excellent buffet breakfast included. central location.

name: Hotel Burnham - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “It is the standard for Excellence!”
text:
The Burnham is an exceptional hotel experience. From the moment you see it, you know the place is unique, warm and welcoming. The location can't be beat, the rooms are spacious and well appointed; you could easily stay inside your entire trip. The Atwood Cafe gets better each time you go there. The complimentary wine hour is a very nice way to get to know other guests.
The real key to the Burnham however, is the outstanding team of people working there. On this trip, I got to spend time with Emil, Darnell, Kelsey, Terrell and Vane. Each of them are extremely professional, gracious, and clearly proud to be part of Team Burnham!

name: MileNorth, A Chicago Hotel
title: “A great central hotel”
text:
I found this hotel excellent. The bar and restaurant are being done up at the moment which is the only downside. However its location is excellent, staff are pleasant and helpful, rooms are large and have fridge, iron, dressing gowns and wide screen tv and more. 
A very enjoyable experience

name: Hampton Majestic Chicago Theatre District
title: “Slightly missed it's mark”
text: I stayed here for business in July 2012. While everyone on site was very friendly I felt the room was a little musty and didn't feel as modern and clean as they were touting it to be. For example, the curtain was stained with something icky like chocolate when I went to open them- I know it's hard to prevent those types of issues. It felt like a remodel that slightly missed the mark. It was fine for a couple days for work, but I've stayed at other Chicago hotels that I preferred (see other reviews). The breakfast was standard- waffle stand, some fruit and yogurt, etc. I would liked to have seen some bottled water or sodas and fresh OJ instead of the machine.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Good hotel in great location!”
text: I recently stayed at the Hyatt Regency for four nights from May 24 thru May 28 ( Memorial Day weekend ) for a convention. I must admit that after reading several reviews, I had concerns. Those concerns were quickly put to rest. The hotel is huge, it has two towers ( east and west ). The main registration is in the east Tower, most people don't know there is an auxillary check in in the lobby of the west tower which is only staffed limited hours. The main activity is in the east tower which is where the majority of the restaurants, concierge, gift shop, lobby bar are located.
