There is an overpass which connects the two towers that has chairs and tables for you to look at the hustle and bustle of Chicago or you may decide to walk across the little street to the other side. The hotel is located downtown on the Loop which is accesible by the Orange Line ( Lake and Street). I flew into Midway, hopped on the train at the airport for 1.75 and enjoyed the 30 minute ride to the hotel. It is about a four or five block trek to the hotel but I enjoyed the exercise. I checked in at the west tower with no problem . i had my choice of rooms in either tower

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Good location, excellent service”
text: I stayed at the Hyatt for a two nights on a business trip. My room was oddly shaped to give a stunning view of the river and NBC Building. Both the room and the bathroom were spotless and the room had an air purifier which ran silently. The hotel was well staffed with individuals who were knowledgeable about both the hotel and the surrounding area. I would not hesitate to stay here again and plan to return with my wife for a weekend.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Good location, rude front desk people, overall pretty average”
text:
I booked two rooms for a business trip (one for me, one for an opposite sex colleague). My confirmation said "two rooms" but upon check in the woman at the front desk said her info said we only had one room and was insistent that we take one room - despite the fact this was a business trip and we are opposite sex colleagues. The Sheraton front desk staffer made us dig out (with a slow wi-fi connection) the original confirmation - which was a pain and insulting considering we were telling the truth. She was anchored to the idea that we could only have one room and as we got visibly frustrated her colleague, who was standing beside her, took charge of the situation and eventually checked into two rooms... phew. 
Other than that unfortunate entrance the breakfast was excellent, location very good, but overall a pretty average business hotel. We went for drinks at the Trump and were blown away - it felt like a different world. Next time I'm staying at the Drake...

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “LOCATION LOCATION AND LOCATION !!!!”
text:
This hotel is very well located . You are walking distance to the most attractions.
For this trip, I was looking for a hotel in a good location and this hotel has it....
I trully recommend this hotel if you have the same interesting.
Rooms and service were fine and no complaints at all. 
Beautiful lobby and bar.
You can have fast meals at Fox and Obel and breakfast at Starbucks.
We had the main meals at Cheesecake factory restaurant.

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “Excellent location!”
text: This hotel is located very close to many great restaurants, shopping, and a short walk to the waterfront trails. Also very simple to find using transit from the Midway airport. The rooms are big, clean and the bed was very comfortable. Staff was extremely friendly and attentive. We mentioned it was our anniversary when we checked in and they left us chocolate covered strawberries and a nice note the following day! Small touch that meant a lot. Would definitely come back here.

Address: '160 E Pearson St at Water Tower Place'
name: The Ritz-Carlton Chicago (A Four Seasons Hotel)
title: “Great hotel, Great location.”
text: I stayed at theRotzCarlton in Chicago for a business meeting. It was a great experience and I plan on staying again for my next meeting.

name: Park Hyatt Chicago
title: “Top Shelf Hotel”
text:
The entire experience of this hotel is five star. Great staff, helpful concierge, wonderful rooms with great amenities. I brought my son on his first big trip to Chicago and everyone from the door man to the front desk treated him like royalty. This is a big deal to a seven year old.
We stayed in a double room with a great view of Michigan Avenue. The rooms are very well decorated and very comfortable. Great bathroom with a huge tub and plenty of space in the vanity area.
I will be back!

Address: '160 E Pearson St at Water Tower Place'
name: The Ritz-Carlton Chicago (A Four Seasons Hotel)
title: “What every 5 star hotel should be!”
text:
It is rare that I give such a glowing review but this Ritz really does have it all done perfectly. 
The rooms are spacious and very comfortable. The decor is luxurious without being over the top. The views of the City are great. 
From checkin to housekeeping to the restaurants and doorman, the staff is wonderful. They are inviting and friendly. You get the feeling that if you needed something they would do just about anything the help you. But since they thought of everything you don't really need to ask for anything. 
The location is obviously terrific. The hotel is in a very busy area of the city but once inside it is like an oasis of calm. 
I had both room service and dinning at the restaurant on the 12th floor lobby. Both were terrific - food and service alike. 
I wish that every hotel experience was like this one at the Ritz. It was absolutely wonderful.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Great hotel, fab spot, super service”
text:
We were a bit nervous about staying here having read so many negative reviews. We could not be more happy that we did stay here. The hotel, which is in an amazing location, right off millenium park, close to metro stops, shopping and restaurants, is a top class joint. 
The lobby is spectacular and what you don't get from the photos is a sense of how relaxing this place is. The buzz of the lobby, with the flow of people and the background music (slightly soft jazz/chill out) give this place a fantastic atmosphere. Just sitting in the lobby bar, watching it all go by is a treat. It's almost like the place to be seen. 
The service was excellent at every turn; check-in, bar and restaurant, and cleaning staff. Everyone was extremely polite and friendly. A smile goes a long way. The concierge was outstanding. Aside from giving us great restaurant and logistics advice, they booked almost all of our restaurants in the evenings. Extremely thorough service.
The bathrooms are a little small; big deal! How long does anyone need to spend in the bathroom when in a hotel anyway? The pool in the leisure centre was tiny, which is my only real criticism, and we probably would have made better use of that area had it been bigger. It seemed crowded as a result any time we walked by.
In short, the hotel is fantastic. Do not hesitate to stay here. I had called in advance to arrange flowers for my wife who was celebrating her birthday during our stay. Everything went like clock-work. I would definitely not be afraid to stay here again and hope to in the near future. Go, enjoy, and don't believe everything negative you read on TA.

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Perfect for a short stay”
text:
What a wonderful hotel.
The staff make you feel welcome.
Continental breakfast is served on each floor every day. Breakfast in bed - a perfect way to start the day!
Packets of tea, coffee, and even hot chocolate are provided in the room, but no milk! Fortunately, you can get milk at the breakfast buffet.
Pity there was no microwave in the room.

Address: '160 E Pearson St at Water Tower Place'
name: The Ritz-Carlton Chicago (A Four Seasons Hotel)
title: “Classic elegance”
text:
Classically elegant city hotel. Views are lovely, and the art deco decor in the rooms is a nice change from stodgy hotel rooms. The beds are very comfortable and everything (cleanliness, sheet quality, service) is up to Four Seasons' standards. 
The location is also spectacular - perched within one block of the best boutiques and department stores on Magnificent Mile.

name: Hotel Burnham - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Location, Comfortable Stay”
text: Found a great place to stay on the south side of the river, just two blocks from Michigan Avenue and Millennium Park! Less than a block from the Red Line as well. I look forward to staying here again soon!

name: Comfort Suites
title: “Big Rooms, Low Prices”
text:
The Comfort Suites on Michigan Ave could not be in a more perfect location, situated smack in the middle of all Chicago attractions, a few blocks north of Millennium Park, a few blocks south of Miracle Mile, a few blocks west of the lake, and an easy train ride from either Chicago airport. It is located right alongside mostly much more expensive hotels, like the Hard Rock and the Hyatt Regency.
The lobby is very small and nondescript...we nearly missed the hotel several times just walking by. But the rooms are very large (especially for an affordable hotel in a ritzy downtown location) and nice. We had a suite with a king bed in its own private room (with a washer-dryer in the closet), a fold-out couch in the living room, and a well-appointed full kitchen (with all the bowls, plates, utensils, and cookware we needed). Everything seemed new and clean and well-maintained. Our high-floor corner room had views in 2 directions.
Two minor drawbacks of the hotel, which may not even be drawbacks for some: The mattresses are VERY soft. If you have a bad back, you probably won't appreciate the marshmallowy pillowtop bed mattresses or the thin fold-out couch mattresses. And the internet is wired ethernet only, which pretty much tethers you to the desk, rather than allowing you to enjoy connectivity across the whole enormous suite (Wanna check email in bed? Sorry, not possible, unless you pack your own really long ethernet cord)
For downtown Chicago, the value cannot be beat--you'd be hard-pressed to find more space for less money in a similarly awesome location--and I would definitely recommend this hotel to Chicago tourists.

name: Hampton Majestic Chicago Theatre District
title: “love it here”
text:
Arrived here late evening, after a very long day and drive. The helpful valet took my luggage, my car, and within 5 minutes I was in my clean and comfortable room. The bathroom is updated, the adjustable shower head actually worked to massage my sore shoulders and the bed was comfortable. Breakfast included oatmeal and fresh fruit, and good coffee. It is not cheap, but I'm glad to be here.
Secure (pw protected) high speed internet connected immediately, so I'll be ready for my meetings.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Comfortable and warm experience”
text:
Upon my arrival at midnight from a long tedious day of travel, I was greeted by registration staff who honored my request by giving me a fantastic corner room with a city/lake view. From that initial experience I felt welcomed, respected and valued as a customer.
I then had the pleasure of becoming acquainted with a housekeeping person who was responsible for maintaining my room for two days over the weekend by providing the best housekeeping services (along with those service providers who followed her). However, she stood out because she paid attention to some of the room details that most travelers take for granted. There were remnants of grout on my and some of the other 20th floor bathroom floors - apparently not cleaned up by workers as a result of recent tub/shower work. This person took the time to clean and remove the residue from the floors - an act that made me regard her highly and appreciate her attention to care.
Quality service and personable staff interactions really matter to me. In addition to the outstanding service of these two exceptional women, LB's Cafe's friendly staff, and other pleasant and professional hotel personnel who I encountered during conference dining and receptions, I can honestly report that I had a great time, in spite of the weather, and will continue to support and recommend Sheraton Hotels.

name: theWit, a Doubletree Hotel
title: “Very Cool”
text:
Great decor, very modern/urban. The beds were great, lots of fluffy pillows. Touchscreen phones where you could just touch the screen to get your car brought up. Chirping birds and waterfall sounds in the hallways during the day and then at night it changes to crickets and soothing night sounds - I could've slept in the hallway, it was very relaxing. Check out the spectacular city views from the very chic ROOF lounge. There are mini-fire pits on the tables. I didn't get to eat at Cibomatto - italian restaurant in the hotel - but I heard from others who have dined there that it is amazing. 
The staff was very friendly. We were always greeted by the bellmen when we were coming or going. The housekeepers in the hallway would always look up and say hi or good morning. 
Awesome Stay!

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Great loc in River North area”
text: We've stayed here before and really like the location. Very convenient for shopping and dining options. Value is rated high, since I got the king room booked at $99/night. My wife enjoys the continental breakfast since it's set up on EACH FLOOR of the hotel. No need to go down to the lobby.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Plumbing Issues and Rude Staff = WORST HOTEL IN HOUSTON!”
text: My wife and I decided to celebrate an anniversary at a good hotel in Houston. Based upon the reviews at sites like Tripadvisor we decided on Magnolia. What a complete mistake! Where to start. First night we were given a room with a fantastic urban view of an adjacent abandoned building complete with broken windows and graffiti artwork. After a nighttime visit to the bathroom (2AM) the toilet began to overflow and filled the marble floor with water. So we called the front desk and were greeted by an agent who snickered and gave us a "We will get right on that" answer. We waited 45 minutes before calling the front desk again. After another 15-20 we were greeted by the manager (in a suit) who took care of the plumbing and mopped the floor. Problem solved by 3:30AM. Next morning we were looking forward to the breakfast so we began to get ready. My wife was brushing her teeth and turned the faucet on to wash her brush. Instead of clean, clear water the brush was sprayed with SEWAGE!! Another call to the front desk and 15 min later a maintenance guy knocked on the door. We welcomed him in and began to explain what had happened. Instead of listening...he began to argue with us. So we decided to go down to speak with someone who wouldn't treat us like idiots. The manager was courteous and offered to move us to another room. But after experiencing plumbing issues in our room there was no way we were eating food at this establishment. So we decided to make our exit to another hotel. We packed up and came back downstairs to check out. The agent who checked us out treated us very rude and topped off our visit at the WORST HOTEL IN HOUSTON. I make this claim not based upon plumbing issues but how the staff reacted to the situation. This business has obviously focused more on aesthetics than hired qualified staff. The only positive part of our trip to the Magnolia was the valet service. These guys are very accommodating and helpful.

name: MileNorth, A Chicago Hotel
title: “A little Gem!!!”
text: We stayed for 3 nights in March 2005 and absolutely loved this hotel. It is just off Michigan so right in the heart of Chicago. There were 3 of us and we had a superb room on 23rd floor. One kingsize bed and a pull out sofa. We would especially like to thank the really helpful doorman (you will know who you are we discussed golf!) He was so smiley and really helpful. Don't believe the negatives - it is a small, warm and friendly hotel and the Bar/Pizza place next door is also excellent.

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “Excellent stay, great service.”
text: Sofitel Water Tower is an amazing hotel in the heart of Chicago. The location was outstanding with access to great shopping and the Chicago waterfront. The rooms were well appointed and always spotless. The bathroom was spacious and sparkling. The bed was incredibly comfortable and the sleep restful. The restaurant in the lobby had a large selection and food quality was tops. All staff were exceedingly helpful and courteous. A great stay and I would not hesitate to visit again!

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Disappointing”
text: I was very dissappointed with our stay. I had stayed with you several years ago on business, and was very pleased. I live about 75 miles away, and often spend weekends in Houston with my girlfriend as a way to get away from the "grind" of our busy lifestyle. When we arrived, we had to circle the hotel several times trying to valet park. The valet area was triple parked waiting for service. We ended up self parking and walking with our luggage around the block. When I checked in, the front desk did not ask if we wanted to upgrade our room as your website indicated they would. When I asked, I was told they could not accomodate any upgrades. When I arrived at my room, I was shocked that it was small with few amenities. No flat screen TV, no refrigerator, no microwave, few accessible power outlets and poor lighting. My girlfriend attempted to use the internet, but found no instructions. I called the front desk, they quickly answered and said "front desk, PLEASE hold". I waited on hold for 10 minutes and gave up. The lounge area was adequate, but the the Dining area offered primarily "bar" foods. Not what I expected from what is advertised as an elegant inner city hotel. Spa services were available, but from someone not affiliated with the hotel, and at a very expensive rate. In addition, you had to leave the hotel for spa services, or have someone not affiliated with the hotel come to your room. Upon leaving, I tried to call for a bellman to bring a cart for our luggage but was again greeted with "thanks for calling PLEASE hold", before I could ask for anything. I again waited on hold for about 5 minutes before I gave up. I brought what I could carry myself to my car around the block, and had my girlfriend wait in the room with the rest. When I arrived at my vehicle in the self park area, I found advertisements/fliers stuck to my windshield for a strip club. Apparently, the self parking area is not secure, or the attendant allows solicitors to attach advertising materials to the vehicles. I pulled up front to the valet area and told them I was only trying to load my vehicle. I was told I could not leave my vehicle there while I retreived my remaining things from the room. I called my girlfriend and had her carry the rest down as I circled the block waiting to see her exit the hotel. Our overall experience was not what we had hoped for in an overnight getaway. My girlfriend commented that although accomodations and amenities were not as nice as some of the other hotels we have recently stayed at in the Houston area, it was really the service that made our stay unpleasant. I will not likely stay with you again or reccommend you to others until room updates and service improvements are made.

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “Great place to stay”
text: Echo the previous reviews.. location is great for Michigan Ave, Hancock Centre, Gold Coast etc. Public transport close and very inexpensive if you get the 3 day pass. Didnt eat in the hotel, but had drinks in the bar a couple of times .....nice cocktail list. As with most Sofitel's the service is great. Would recommend this hotel for a stay in the windy city

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Love it!”
text: Super place to stay. I live in the Houston/Galveston area and always stay at the Magnolia when staying downtown for sporting events, theatre, opera or just a girls night out.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Chicago - Downtown
title: “Go For It!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel from August 20 to August 31, 2010. I have no complaints other than that one of three elevators was down for the last day or so of our visit, making it a bit of a wait to go up or down. That's it! Pictures of the room are posted for your review. The room and bathroom were kept very clean, to me the most important thing of all! Toiletries (shampoo, conditioner and moisturizer) were replaced daily as needed - never had to ask. Nothing was lacking - we had a fridge which we used a lot, a microwave and coffee maker which we didn't use at all, a chair with ottoman for reading and a great T.V. The bed was so comfortable I slept through the night - most unusual for me. I loved the duvet and pillows. Despite previous postings of noise from the fire station down the block we weren't bothered, maybe because we live downtown and are used to City noises. All the staff were friendly and helpful and we encountered no "attitudes". The breakfast was adequate and we were able to get seats the times we did go down. You can get coffee anytime. There is a business centre with free internet so you can Google or print off your boarding pass. We didn't use the pool so I can't comment on that. The cost of the room was $149.00 per night plus tax.
One of the things I liked best about this hotel was the location. It is about a 4-5 minute walk from the Grand stop on the red line. We were even able to use the transit system to take the El from the Airport to the hotel by taking the blue line to Jackson, and then transferring to the red line to go north to Grand. It worked with no complications other than that I have to get a lighter suitcase for myself...a younger, stronger person would have no problems. We bought a weekly pass for the El and used it to go everywhere - Andersonville, Chinatown, Oak Park, Bucktown, etc. etc. The hotel is also an easy walk to the Magnificent Mile and the Loop. As for restaurants and cafes, there are many in the immediate area. Some I would recommend are Lou Malnati's, Portillo's and Ed Debevic's. The place we enjoyed eating at the most was Ann Sather's (Swedish) in Andersonville. In the end result, there's no shortage of things to do in Chicago and I 
would go again anytime, booking at this Hampton Inn.

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “Great location”
text:
Good rooms with wonderful spacious bathrooms. Centrally located. Very helpful staff.
It is a busy commercial hotel but we stayed on a weekend and found it was pleasantly quiet.
Good rates. I would definitely recommend.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Chicago - Downtown
title: “A Great Chicago Hotel”
text: The Hampton Inn & Suites in Downtown Chicago is a great value! Rooms just recently renovated, all areas well maintained. Staff is excellent! Awesome restaurants very close by.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Classy Hotel, Great Views”
text: I accompanied my wife here on a business trip of hers, we loved the hotel. The rooms were nice & clean, great matresses. Our view of the Chicago River from the 19th floor was awesome. The lobby is impressive & there are lots of great places within walking distance - Magnificent Mile shopping, the Art Institute of Chicago, Millenium Park, Navy Pier, etc. The only thing preventing a 5-star rating is that the bathrooms were unspectacular - - kind of old & outdated, but no big deal. As always, the room service was outrageous - $35 for a huge french toast breakfast just for myself (which was delicious). Everything was very clean, concierge was great, central location, defintely recommended.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Excellent location especially with Chicago Go card 3-day pass.”
text:
2nd time in chicago ever, and the first time, we actually stayed on the magnificient mile's Westin Hotel, which was fantastic. This time around, stayed off (1 street off Michigan Ave) at the Sheraton Towers, and sort of think it's a little better location. 
Do get the chicago Go card at smartdestinations.com and the 3 day pass was what was best for me. There is a Greyline tour bus that has a stop right across the hotel, so used that service to shuttle us around the city! Great tour as well !
Westin was on the mile, but I felt this was better located (bottom of the mile). Tons of bars to walk to, and the Red line train wasn't too far either (about 1/2 mile I think). Great view of the Navy Pier as well !

name: theWit, a Doubletree Hotel
title: “Well, I was forewarned”
text: When I got in the cab at O'hare and told the driver that I was staying at The Wit he laughed. He warned me that the bar/restaurant on the roof of The Wit was the place to be in Chicago. He also told me that you had to be 30 or younger. He was right. The lobby is small and cramped. After 4pm it is a hopeless mess to get through to your room. The rope line runs outside but the lobby is too small to handle the crowd. The elevators from 4pm on are packed and the amount of perfume and cologne in the elevators is astonishing. You need oxygen to make it to your room. The rest of the hotel is quirky and a little fun. One thing you will find out very quickly is that square sinks look nice but are totally impractical and impossible to use. The rooms are a tech person's dream. The wireless is wonderfully fast and easy to use. The rooms are suprisingly quiet and nicely decorated. I will let you find out for yourself about the sounds in the hallways...pretty cool touch. The staff is young and superficial...but so is everyone else in the hotel. The restaurant is likely the darkest place you will ever eat. You can't read the paper or for that matter see two feet in front of you. Food was good. I want to tell you to avoid the place if you are over 30, but it just has too many cute things to really trash it. So, you too are forewarned ,but enjoy it if you can.

name: Hotel Monaco Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Hotel Monaco Chicago is the best!!!”
text: I travel to Chicago every year for a meeting and we always stay at Monaco. I think there would be a protest if we were made to stay anywhere else. The staff go out of thier way to make you feel welcome and comfortable. The rooms are wonderful and I love the large bay windows to sit in. This is where I nap or read between meetings. Furthermore, Monaco is perfectly located near everything!!! When I finally visit Chicago with my family for a vacation, I will stay at Monaco ONLY!!!

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Great for Seeing Jersey Boys”
text:
My husband gave me tickets to Jersey Boys as a Christmas present so we decided to stay overnight at a hotel in the Loop. I booked the hotel through Hotwire and got the Palmer House for $106 (not as cheap as some of the other reviewers but still a very decent rate for a downtown Chicago hotel). 
We had no problems with check-in. We requested a renovated room upon check-in and the front desk clerk was happy to fulfill our request. Our room was a long walk from the elevator, which meant it was a little more isolated so we had less noise from neighbors. We heard doors closing but the walls were thick enough to prevent hearing any activity through the wall. The room was a little dark since it faced another building. The king bed was comfortable enough and the overall room condition was fine. There wasn't a lot of counter space in the bathroom (almost a pedestal sink) but there were small open shelves under the sink. The closet was a walk-in, very unusual for a hotel, which we didn't use since we're there just overnight. 
The best part of staying at the Palmer House was the short walk back after the show. While everyone else was trying to find a cab, we walked less than a block to the hotel. 
We didin't eat or have drinks at the hotel but they have opened a new restaurant and bar in the lobby. We went around the corner to the Beef and Brandy for a decent, reasonably-priced (for downtown Chicago) breakfast. Also within a block are two drugstores (CVS, Walgreen's) that have inexpensive bottled water, snacks and even souvenirs. The bottle of Fiji water in the room was pricey ($6?).
Overall, I would recommend the hotel for short-term stays. I don't know if I would be as comfortable in that room if we were staying for a week. I don't recall any other seating besides the bed and the desk chair.

name: Park Hyatt Chicago
title: “My new favorite hotel in Chicago!”
text: I usually stay at the Sofitel Water Tower, but at the suggestion of a Chicagoan friend, stayed here. It was fabulous! Definitely will return. Same for my cousin, who lives large & usually stays at the Peninsula. We were both completely bowled over by the level of service. Spotlessly clean, beds & bedding that were divine, phenomenal view & location, quiet, a comfy reading chair, free wireless, a great bath tub for soaking, choice of morning newspaper, superb staff & quick room service. The hotel restaurant, Nomi, is sophisticated & pricey but outstanding. Honest, I don't usually use so many superlatives & I am not a plant. I simply could find no fault here. It was worth every penny.

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “Decent place, dated decor but otherwise good hotel”
text:
Overall a good hotel and decent choice to stay, particularly if you have a good discount. However, if you are paying full price, you might want to reevaluate your other options first.
Pros:
- Location: steps away from the Mile and right in the area with a good mix of nice restaurants and boutique shops. Taxi stand is right next to the building, making catching a cab at an inconvenience hour very early morning a breeze.
- Soaker tub and separate shower in a 4 star, i guess that's a plus?
Cons:
- A bit dated decor in the room and in the hotel hallways.
- The soaker tub is a bit small in comparison.

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great place to stay in the heart of downtown Chicago”
text: I'll keep this short and sweet... the Palomar is a great hotel in a great location. My wife and I stayed here while visiting Chicago for a friend's wedding. The room is great with a big 'ole jacuzzi tub, comfy king-sized bed and big floor-to-ceiling windows which allowed us to take in the cityscape. I definitely recommend staying here is you are visiting downtown Chi-Town

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Fantastic in every way”
text: I recently stayed at the Palomar for a week. From check-in to check-out, the staff attention to detail is flawless, friendly and formidable! It would appear that the staff really enjoys working for this hotel, and their can-do attitude means that as a guest you are treated well and your business is appreciated. Many other companies and hotel chains would do well to understand that when management appreciates its employees and empowers them to make decisions and solve problems, they will deliver top-notch service. It's that simple. If that is what the Kimpton Hotel corporate culture is all about, all I can say is Bravo!

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “only way to experience houston”
text: great service, clean rooms, lovely hotel. i really enjoyed the evening cookie reception. hotel is in great location and offer transportation within good portion of the city. would definitely stay again and recommend anyone staying in the dowtown area to visit this property. Only downside is having to pay for parking.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “This is a wonderfull hotel the staff works had to accomadate you.”
text: Excellant hotel, I would definitely consider stay again.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Chicago
title: “Most Relaxing and Fun Days Ever”
text: The friendly caring staff, the beautiful suite, the amenities made this the most relaxing and enjoyable visit we have ever had to Chicago--and we have been to Chicago many times!! Our comfort was assured, and with thermostats in both the bedroom and living room we could adjust the temperature easily. They provided everything we needed including an umbrella which came in handy on the first day of our visit.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Great Hotel - Will Stay Again”
text: Our in-house travel agent referred us to the Magnolia and we are so pleased he did. Not only was the staff accommodating, friendly and professional, but the hotel was clean and was properly staffed for the number of attendees. Our room was clean and ready upon our arrival. The events manager is exceptional and very helpful. We will definitely use the Magnolia again.

name: Hotel Burnham - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Excellent stay at a historic landmark!”
text:
Stayed in the Burnham for 3 nights in September 2009. We won this hotel on Priceline and were very lucky with the Burnham. This hotel is just great: incredible staff, central location, amazing building. The Kimpton Group obviously did a great job in restoring this historic landmark! The rooms were smaller than average, but they were nicely decorated and added to the boutique atmosphere. We had a room on the top floor, overlooking the Chicago Theater, which was quite a view.
We had dinner at the Atwood Café, which was lovely. 
Chicago's major attractions were within walking distance (The El, Chicago River, magnificent mile,...). For other attractions, public transport is not even a block away (red and blue line, and of course, the El). The blue line is the direct line to O'Hare, so we did not have to order a cab to get from and to the airport.
This hotel was a great experience. Would love to stay here again.

name: Conrad Chicago
title: “everything good”
text:
We were only there for one night, but were impressed by every service we came across. We arrived with a tight schedule and allowed the concierge to make a reservation through a brief phone call on the drive in to Chicago for a sushi restaurant within waling distance (Sunda) that was first class. The restaurant comped us a free drink as a result of the relationship with the hotel, making the experience even better. A quick walk back to the concierge provided directions to the train that sent us on our way to the red line station (2 blocks away) and a train to Wrigley field and a concert. Our late-night return to the hotel for a drink and evental collapse into an extremely comfortable bed completed the evening. The accomodations were spacious, clean, and comfortable. I generally sleep poorly in a hotel, but the room was at the end of a hall on the 14th floor and extremely quiet. Sleep was not a problem. 
In summary: convenient location, helpful and courteous staff, cleam, comfortable room, comfy robes, free wi-fi, convenient parking, nice sound system in the room, and I wouldn't hesitate to stay there again.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Chicago
title: “Beautiful Location, Convenient to Shopping & Lake”
text:
I recently stayed here for one night only, but was able to get a great feel for the property. To begin, you can't beat the location. Whether you are there to shop, enjoy the lake or have a nice retreat following a day of meetings, you will not be disappointed. 
The rooms are on the smaller side, BUT - how can you beat looking out your full window to the lake. To be honest, when I was in the room I was realizing that unless I have my family with me or I'm there for more than a week, the size was perfect. The bathroom was also a great size and there was plenty of closet space. I heard no outside noise. 
The team that works there was very courteous, knowledgable of the area and took great care of everyone.
I went to the spa for a simple male manicure and they were able to accommodate a last minute appointment and the manicurist did a great job. The spa is very warm and welcoming. 
Overall, I would book a stay here if your travels require you to be in Chicago. It was an incredible value, and while I like the Ritz, I think the location and views of this one can't be beat!

name: The Peninsula Chicago
title: “Pampering and Service - “Par Excellence“”
text: We stayed at the Peninsula Chicago for our anniversary last week. We had stayed there once before and now I remember why we loved it so much. The service was out of this world. From the moment we checked in, the staff took care of our every need. We arrived very early and our room was not ready. They upgraded us at no cost to a suite so we could get into our room, so I could get to a meeting I had on time (yes…a little biz before pleasure). The concierge ordered a complimentary wine be sent to our table at dinner, even though we ate at a different hotel. She made the reservations and did a perfect job. She even arranged for complimentary transportation via the hotel Mini Copper. On top of all that, she had monogrammed pillow cases delivered to our room that evening. We also did a couples massage and were extremely impressed. While the massage was very good, for the cost of a massage, the spa facilities are unimpressive. The rooms have more amenities and luxury features than you could possibly list. The turndown service, room service, doorman, concierge, front desk, and EVERYTHING was great. The trip was worth every dime. Keep up the good worth.

name: The Talbott Hotel
title: “Wonderful hotel! I would not hesitate to return”
text:
We stayed at the Talbott hotel for three nights in July. I had read about this hotel on trip advisor, and took the great reviews with a grain of salt. Although I am partial to boutique hotels, I wondered how the hotel could be so highly rated. Believe me, this hotel deserves all it's accolades. The hotel is perfectly located in the heart of Chicago, one block off the Golden mile. The real selling point about this hotel, however, is a service of the staff. Every time you enter the hotel you're welcome by many staff people. After the first day the staff greets you by name. Additionally, our room was not ready for the 3 o'clock checking. We waited about 20 minutes and then were told that the hotel it upgraded us to a suite for our inconvenience. We certainly did not have to do this. It was greatly appreciated and the room we were given was absolutely exquisite
The attention to detail and the location of the hotel, together with the service it provides make this a real gem. Do yourself a favor and stay here.

name: Conrad Chicago
title: “Great Location!”
text:
Another great experience at the Conrad Chicago while visiting my son in August. I stayed in a
"Pure Allergy" room which provides air purifiers, and special mattress and pillow covers to reduce allergens (dust mites, mold spores etc.). I enjoyed complimentary in-room high-speed internet access, 42-inch plasma television, Bose surround sound system, nice large bathroom and nice sized closet (extra deep). The bed was very comfortable as was the bedding. I appreciated the pillow menu. I didn't request other pillows as it seemed that there were 4 different types of pillows already placed on the bed. I did not mind going down for coffee in the morning. The coffee is stationed right off the elevators on the lobby level. The coffee was amazing...much better than what would be provided by a Mr. Coffee in the room! They provided 2 additional toiletry choices for guests to try. I chose the vegan selection packaged in a travel case. Nice touch! Service was excellent. They promptly brought me a brand new hair dryer when I discovered the one in my bathroom did not work. They also took care of my son's bicycle while he stayed at the Conrad one night. They locked it up inside the hotel on the Rush Street level (probably where luggage is held for early/late arrivals/departures). The parking directly across from the hotel was a $10 savings per night over valet parking; perfectly convenient and Rush Street is covered by the mall crossway so bad weather is not an issue when crossing Rush from the parking garage into the concierge level of the hotel. Conveniently located one block from the Mag Mile and centrally located between the Water Tower and the Loop (north/south). We also enjoyed the Chicago Symphony at a free concert in Grant Park which was easy walking distance (10 mins). You can choose great seats or opt for a picnic on the lawn and byob!

name: Radisson Blu Aqua Hotel
title: “Good Value for High End Hotel, Slow Elevators”
text:
Pros:
-Rooms are all different with a modern design. Adds a lot of character. Rooms aren't huge but have everything you need. 
-One of the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in.
-Gym/pool/outdoor area is fantastic. Not to be overlooked.
-Architecture is fantastic
-Helpful staff
-Great location (5-7 minute walk from Magnificent Mile) and just down the street from Millennium park
Cons:
-Elevators are ridiculously slow.We had friends staying 2 floors above us and at one point it took about 25 minutes just to go back to my room to get something then come back up. It actually dampens your stay as it gets VERY annoying. Note: there is a back elevator that they failed to tell us about that is used less and would have made the stay MUCH better. 
-Lobby smells like perfume... it's not overly strong, but if you are sensitive to the smell, it may be troublesome.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Chicago
title: “Outstanding hotel! Old-school grandeur, yet kid-friendly”
text: We stayed in a one bedroom suite on one of the upper floors. Views were sensational. The room itself was white, crisp, clean and airy--heaven. Breakfast downstairs was delicious. One of the things I love most about this hotel is the service. Concierge was incredibly knowledgeable and friendly. Despite a having a very grand and formal atmosphere, the staff were incredibly warm and welcoming of my children. They were treated like VIPs and they loved it! They had kid-sized robes in the room, and at night someone arrived with milk, cookies, two teddies, and a board game. That's one way of guaranteeing my return business--treating my kids like they're appreciated guests too. One of my favorite hotels in the world.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “If your in Houston, this is the place to stay!”
text: My husband and I love to get away to Houston and the Magnolia is conveniently located near great resturants and plenty to do within walking distance.

name: The Talbott Hotel
title: “Cannot be faulted!”
text:
What a fantastic hotel! We cannot speak more highly of this hotel, which we chose on the basis of location and Trip Advisor reviews.
The hotel is situated within a few minutes walk of the shopping strips and the John Hancock Tower. There is a fantastic grocery store across the road where you can buy fruit, salads, sandwiches and drinks. The hotel has a small bar and restaurant in which the prices are very reasonable. There are many restaurants within 5 minutes walking distance.
From the moment we arrived after a long overnight flight from Japan, the staff were extremely polite, friendly and helpful, from the doormen through to the reception. 
The decor is tasteful and classy, with the look of a well maintained antique style. There were interesting finishes throughout such as old style inhouse phones and light fittings. The detail and care put into the furnishing of the hotel made it a far more interesting place to stay than a stock standard hotel which is no different from any other you have stayed in. 
We stayed for 10 days.
Our room was big, had plenty of drawers and hanging space, an inhouse safe, a big bathroom with double sinks, hairdryers, bathrobes, a turn down service with chocolates, access to a fantastic gym a 5 minute walk away which I used 3 times and Apple TV in the room, giving free internet access. Free WiFi also available with a fast connection.
We were on the 6th floor and I am a light sleeper, but I had a sound sleep every night. The bed was king size and so comfortable I wanted to take it home!!
The staff were amazing. Everyone we came into contact with was friendly and inviting. One evening our television wasn't working. It was 10:30pm and we had just returned for the evening. A maintenance technician was at the room and had it fixed within 5 minutes. Likewise with the hairdryer. I blew a globe in one of the lights in the hallway of the room. I knew it was not working, but didn't report it and when we returned that evening, it had been fixed. 
One morning I was waiting at reception to ask for a gym pass. The lady at reception was on the phone speaking to a guest. The doorman noticed this and seeing me in my gym gear, retrieved the gym pass register from behind the desk, took me aside and gave me a gym pass. 
One evening I was in the lift returning to my room and the lady doing the turndown service was in the lift with her basket of chocolates. She offered everyone in the lift a chocolate!
We were very sad to leave and would recommend this hotel to anyone. We cannot speak more highly of our experience there. Next time we return to Chicago, we will definitely stay there again.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Very comfortable, friendly hotel in a good location”
text:
This hotel has roomy, well appointed rooms. Comfortable beds with fair linens (the bedspread and bolster needed replacing).
Staff is friendly and helpful. 
Good downtown location is 3 blocks from Metrorail and the underground tunnel shops and restaurants.
When you consider the complimentary full american breakfast, the free drink at happy hour, milk and cookie buffet and free high speed internet in the evening, the price is not bad. 
Parking is expensive - valet parking is $25, but there are several lots and garages nearby.

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “We love this place!!!!”
text: Great location, very nice and helpful staff, and nice rooms. Bobby and Bleu were very helpful. We will be back for sure!!!

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Potrebbe essere meglio”
text: Hotel centrale a pochi metri dalla Michigan Av. Bella ed efficiente la hall, un po' piccoloa l'area della colazione. Camere un po datate ma pulite, effettivamnete un po fredde e con un clima rumoroso che di notte deve essere spento. Il bagno era con la vasca con doccia, e con la tenda. manca un adeguato corredo da bagno e le ciabattine da camera.

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Second time, just OK”
text: I stayed here last year and posted a glorious review. We return to Chicago almost every year in summer so I reserved the hotel again. This time, it was just ok. No bad experience here, but the staff seemed to have too much fun among themselves, which will eventually take away from customer care. I wonder if the Kimpton reputation of being the best place to work for is backfiring upon themselves. I was extremely disappointed at the wine reception because they were serving very cheap wine ("Rex", to be exact, which can be purchased at grocery stores for less than $10 per bottle). I thought that they could try a little harder to find interesting wines for a little more money. I will probably try another hotel next time.

name: Hotel Burnham - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Amazing weekend getaway”
text: My husband and I just returned from Hotel Burnham to celebrate our one year wedding anniversary. I knew there was construction going on around the hotel, but I chose to stay here anyhow (I found an average rate of $155 a night on the hotel's website). Our stay was absolutely amazing. As soon as we said our last name at check-in, they wished us a happy anniversary. When we returned to our room the first evening, there was a bottle of champagne waiting for us. Our third day there, we had asked for some assistance finding places. They knew we would be doing a lot of walking, and when we returned, there was a bottle of water waiting in our room for us. The service we received at the Atwood was incredible as well. The server remembered us on our second day and seated us at the same table we had the day before, saying he would seat us at our "usual." The wine reception in the evening was a very nice touch as well. Never have I stayed at a hotel that paid such attention to pleasing their guests. My husband and I never had a problem sleeping, but we were on the 14th floor. If you stay here, you need to know there is construction going on. If you do not request a room on a top floor, you will probably hear the noise. I know if we return to Chicago, we are going to stay at the Hotel Burnham again.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Chicago
title: “The whole experience at the hotel is absolutely perfect.”
text: First and foremost, the staff is over-the-top accomodating. Everything was thought of ahead of arrival. I had my 2 young sons (3 and 5) with me and shortly after arrival, complimentary cookies and chocolate milk were brought to the room. Additionally, and equally impressive, was the cleanliness, decor and layout of the room. The furniture is perfectly maintained and beautifully appointed. The overall stay was just spectacular and my boys are asking when we're going back.

name: The Peninsula Chicago
title: “Outstanding Hotel in the Heart of the Gold Coast”
text: Room as well laid out and very spacious (for Chicago Standards)! Service was excellent throughout our stay (we were doing some shopping downtown for the holidays). We spent one evening at the bar downstairs and I must say that it was cozy, warm and the bartenders/drinks were outstanding. Not the cheapest place to stay in Chicago but at least you are able to obtain a great experience in return. Cannot go wrong with this property.

name: Hampton Majestic Chicago Theatre District
title: “Fabulous Hotel...Wonderful Staff...”
text:
.stayed here with our two teenagers and we all absolutely loved this hotel. From the moment we arrived until the moment we left, the staff were always very helpful and accessible.
Front door valet parking for one flat free for your stay. We never had to wait more than 10 minutes for them to retrieve our car.
The rooms were very large and spacious with wonderful high ceilings. You never felt cramped in this room. Beds were very comfortable, towels were thick and plentiful.
Free wi-fi in our room which worked very fast. The continental breakfast included was great - hot items such as eggs and ham were available along with a good selection of cereals, fresh fruits, pastries and breads.
The location is ideal. We were able to walk most places after receiving directions from the friendly lobby staff including the aquarium. It wasn't that far at all. We did take the subway one night and it is conveniently located around the corner from the hotel.
There are a lot of great stores near the hotel for shopping as well there is a theater right next door to take in a Broadway show.
We had a great time in Chicago and couldn't have asked for a better hotel to stay at.

name: Hotel Monaco Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “It's a Kimpton and it's that standard that you'll get.”
text: You'd think that a hotel as fancy as this - I don't usually stay at upscale places such as this, but the Memorial Day trip to Chicago was different for once - would have more sound proofing. But then again the "EL" really is that noisy especially at bends and doors and dry walls can only silence whatever interior noise there may be by so much. That being said, there really was hardly any noise and you're pretty much just in room to sleep at night and not to hang out during the day. Of course said room was immaculate and so was the bathroom. The bed was too soft for my liking but the next person of course might say it's perfect. Getting WiFi to work however is a small pain in the neck. Either you're a Kimpton member or you pay. Pay for WiFi? At a hotel as pricey as this? Come on, man! Of course there's the third option to sign up as a new member but then you'll want to use an e-mail-address of yours solely dedicated to get spam and during sign-up make sure that you unclick about a dozen newsletters and offers. And also, Kimpton, why is there no breakfast? That's ridiculous. Yes, certainly, there's room service and a menu to choose from but places that ask a tenth of Monaco's lodging cost per night offer a complimentary breakfast. So, there goes your 'excellent' rating. On the plus side Monaco's location is fabulous. Within just a few steps you're either standing in The Loop, on the Magificent Mile or in Millennium Park. As impressive as that is, it's too fancy-shmancy for me. But if you're a business traveler coming through Chicago it'll be right up your alley.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Great accomodations. Great value.”
text: great price. friendly and responsive staff. nice to have internet, breakfast, drinks, snacks included in price - no unexpected add-ons. Good location - just a two blocks from metrorail stop.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Weekend getaway-- relaxing, refreshing, and fun”
text: We live close to Houston and love to go in and experience the boutique hotels which are usually more expensive but being close to home don't incur the travel costs. The Magnolia is one of our favorites because it has extras-- 2 free drinks at happy hour, cookies and milk before bed and a free breakfast-- all good. Its rooms are well appointed-- although all the views aren't that good but most are nice. Although be careful with room service-- they charge $2.95 for delivery and add a 21% gratuity!! So don't feel compelled to tip the delivery person. Other benefits-- you can walk to the ballpark, to many restaurants, to the Bayou Place Entertainment Complex, Alley Theatre, Jones Hall, Wortham-- and catch the Metro to the Museum district. So park your car and enjoy-- oh, valet parking costs $25.00. So our $99 internet special ended up costing us $179.00 with tax, valet, and one room service-- still an affordable weekend for a room that usually costs $250.00 per night. Oh-- and it has the only rooftop pool in downtown Houston-- it's small but nice.

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “A very pleasant stay”
text:
I stayed at the Amalfi over Labor Day weekend. Overall, I had a very pleasant experience. The hotel is centrally located downtown, right across the street from Harry Carry's. Be prepared to pay $35 per day to park at the hotel. 
The lobby is very different, but beautiful, with a baby grand piano and bright, vibrant colors. Check in was smooth and efficient. 
The hotel only has 6 floors, so you wont get a view of the skyline (our room had a view of Harry Carry's). The entertainment center takes up a lot of space, which makes the room feel smaller than it actually is, but it was very pleasantly decorated. The bed was very comfortable- the pillows were soft and fluffy and the sheets were definitely high quality cotton (I guess about 350 thread count). The bathroom was fabulous- lots of counter space, fluffy towels, and the shower was excellent (dual shower heads). The DVD/CD player was a little hard to figure out, but the front desk helped me figure it out. 
The gym was well equipped, with 3 treadmills, 2 ellipticals, and free weights.
I was not able to participate in the evening cocktail hour, but the breakfast spread was great. It was served on each floor, which was very convenient, and there were baskets so you could take breakfast back to the room. There was coffee, tea, juices, danishes, rolls, and fruit. 
My only complaint was that the hotel has no kitchen, so if you want room service, you had to order it from Harry Carry's, which was a little pricey.
All in all, I had a very good experience at the Amalfi and would definitely stay there again.

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Incredible eye for detail”
text:
I stayed at the Palomar for 4 nights between April 19th and 23th 2012 and was impressed. The Palomar truly offers the service that you expect from a hotel in this class (but that you rarely get anymore these days). Whilst the rooms, lobby and the hotel overall are comparable to other hotels in its class, it is the eye for detail that sets the Palomar apart (ranging from the lighting in the room, to the daily wine reception in the lobby, to the helpful people at the reception (receptionist Indre was lovely). The Palomar is a breath of fresh air when compared to the chain Marriots or the Hiltons in the same area). Compliments to the staff of the hotel!
From a practical point of view, the hotel is very well located just two blocks away from the Magnificent Mile and next to the Grand Red metro station (with easy access to and from the airport - be it O'Hare or Midway - so no need to face the costly taxi ride and rush hour traffic).
I booked the Hotel through Hotels.com and got a very acceptable rate (GBP 112).

name: Conrad Chicago
title: “Great Location”
text: Stayed for 3 nights. The hotel is in a great location close to all amenities' great shops, restaurants and places of interest. Rooms are well appointed with massive comfortable beds and crisp clean sheets. Walk in shower fab, very clean and luxurious bathroom, really nice atmosphere. As we are Hilton Members we never received an upgrade or any extras, this had something to do with not booking the hotel direct as we had been travelling to Seattle and Alaska, I asked my travel agent to book the Conrad for me. I never expected that. I enjoyed the cocktails on the roof terrace, they make a great mojito. I really enjoyed this hotel given the size and location I would definitely stay here again. There was 1 glitch during the course of our stay we could never get a hold of the hotel concierge, even though the front desk gave me specific times to call back. For a hotel of this reputation I would have expected a little better. Although the front desk tried to make up for it, it wasn't quiet the same service as having access to a concierge.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “I only wish every city I visit had a Magnolia!”
text:
I have stayed at The Magnolia in Dallas so my decision was easy, however the Houston property is even nicer and the location is super convenient to business, entertainment, shopping and restaurants. 
The staff is super attentive and friendly and the rooms are impeccably clean and comfortable. 
Plus the value....the price is excellent considering you recieve a complimentary breakast, cookies and milk and a couple of free drinks at the bar! 
I actually just booked a stay in Dallas for next month.

name: James Chicago
title: “Love The James”
text: We think this hotel is great. My husband and I stayed here two weekends ago and then came back with our two teenagers this past weekend. We think The James is wonderful. First the location is ideal, one block off MIchigan Ave. at Ontario, there are so many great things to do nearby. The hotel is just the right size, big enough to have good amenities, a great bar, restaurant, workout room, but small enough to feel intimate. The staff is wonderfully friendly and accomodating. When they discovered we had returned after staying there two weeks earlier, they were so pleased and really bend over backwards to give us an exceptionally nice room. The rooms are somewhat small, but I think really typical of a downtown metropolitan hotel. The large flat screen TV is very nice. I would recommend this hotel highly and will be sure to stay here again. We found great prices for the James both at Expedia and Orbitz.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Chicago
title: “Rooms are tired.”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Four Seasons Hotel in Chicago for a Friday and Saturday night in August. We had a "superior" room, Which is their basic room. The room size was fine. The carpeting had a large stain between the bed and the dresser. The sink counter had ring marks and blotches that made it appear dirty. Upon touching it, I found that the marks are permanent. Guess, I expected better. We enjoyed our breakfast in the dining area. Overpriced, of course, but excellent. The hotel is in a great location, walking distance to great shopping, restaurants and Holy Name Cathedral. Nice workout room.

name: James Chicago
title: “I LOVE the JAMES”
text:
I LOVED this hotel. The room was so chic and trendy, the bed was comfortable, great slippers and robes. I love the Keihl's bath products in the bathroom. We went during my birthday weekend, and they had a card and plate with pastries waiting in the room. We got a great deal on a junior suite from Travelzoo, but when we tried to take another trip to Chicago, the deal was gone. I really recommend the hotel. I LOVED it. 
The ONLY problem we had was with the David Burke Steakhouse. The service was horrible, they switched our order with the table next to our's and the only compensation was they took off a $7 side dish we ordered (and they were nice enough to NOT charge us for the other side dish we DIDN'T get). DON'T go there. Go to the Lawry's accross the street.
But stay at the James. (BTW- its not a 3-star hotel like the website lists- its at least 4-star)

name: Hotel Monaco Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A Gem in Chicago”
text: My husband and I stay at this boutique hotel each time we spend the night in Chicago. We have never been disappointed. It is one block off of Michigan Avenue so is relatively quiet. It is close to shopping, the Art Institute, Symphony Center and wonderful restaurants. The staff is very friendly. The room is comfortable; some of them have window seats that look out onto Wacker Drive. It is a real gem!

name: Hotel Burnham - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Nice location, nice style”
text:
Nice hotel in a good location, esspecially if you're looking to go to the theatre or go shopping. My wife and I stayed here for a couple days with our two young children. The rooms are small, but they were fine for our needs. Front desk staff was a little distracted when we checked in.
GREAT coffeshop on the block. Good reseteraunt in the hotel. 
Following the trip, the hotel's assistant manage sent a personal note responding to the areas of improvement I mentioned in the online survey form I filled out. It was nice to get a response that wasn't a form letter.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Left wanting more...”
text: We stayed at the Palmer House for 5 nights from Nov 10th 2005. The staff were good and the location was ideal. The hotel lobby is not representative of the rest of the accomodation on offer. The rooms are in need of a refurbishment. The bathrooms in desperate need! The wallpaper was peeling off - Don't know why they had wallpaper in the bathroom. The room was comfortable but we had very noisy neighbours - the walls were not very sound proof!

name: Hotel Monaco Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great location in Downtown Chicago!”
text: Boutique hotel with some very nice touches, like complimentary glass of wine in the lobby each evening! Couple minutes walk to the Magnificent Mile; few minutes in opposite direction to the Art Institute of Chicago. Front desk staff and door staff very friendly, great bed linens, and room very clean. We had the Mediterranean Suite.....fantastic window seats (more like window beds, they were very spacious) Great place to take a break, lie in the window and look out on towards the river. Close to Mortons, The Steakhouse, if you want to splurge; coffee and bagel shops nearby as well. Great area to walk around and explore during the day and evening.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Great view of the River”
text:
I stayed here for a conference at the McCormick Center. The hotel was quite nice. Clean, comfortable room. Very good view of the river.
There was a mix up with my room reservation causing some stress, but the concierge supplied me with complimentary internet access in the business center to contact my colleague to get it straightened out and I caught a movie at the theater across the way while they stored my bags. Good service!

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Comfortable”
text:
Nephews wedding~ Group rate. Suites spacious. Clean and comfortable. Rooftop pool and gym clean and maintained.
Staff courteous and helpfull. I left my dress belt at home, consierge aided me with yahooo directions to nearest mens store. Nice panoramic view of Houston. Central to downtown
facilities. Valet or park yourself, garage parking.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Not that great”
text: I stayed here for a business conference. The rooms are outdated and not all that clean. Everything costs extra. Internet is $12/day. Shula's food is mediocre and way overpriced. This hotel is convenient for conferences if held there, but 1 block away is an embassy suites and it is much nicer. So if you don't mind walking a block, I would suggest the embassy.

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “great design, excellent comfort and perfect location”
text:
Sofitel Water Tower is the best representation of what Accor is doing about Sofitel for a few months already. There is a real trend to upgrade the Sofitel brand to something more luxurious.
This hotel, superbly located at walking distance from Michigan Avenue, the Chicago shopping area, is an excellent deal and one of the good choice you can do in this city offering a large selection of five stars hotels. The building itself is very interesting and the interior design is as good as the architecture, modern, trendy and very interesting.
Right away you arrive in the large airy lobby, you feel like in a cocoon and it's perfectly relaxing and Sofitel is always looking at The French touch you can find everywhere even in the staff.
I've been welcomed by a french young girl who was efficient and quick, exactly what a traveller needs after a long journey but nobody offered help to escort me in the room with all the bags and it's a bit unfortunate.
Anyway, i've found my room by myself and i haven't been disappointed at all. Even if it was a standard room, the size was really great and the large window overlooking the city makes the room so clear and liveable. No word to say about the perfect bed where you wanna jump right away you come in the room especially if you feel tired due to the jet-lag. Sofitel "My Bed" is a wonderful concept of sleep quality with different matress and a lot of pillows. You'll feel like on a soft cloud. The cleanliness was perfect everytwhere and the bathroom with a seperate shower and bathtub with Frette bathrobes and towels and L'Occitane amenities just wonderful for an ultimate destress experience.
Same satisfaction for the excellent breakfast and the Benedict Eggs on Maryland crab cakes are to die for... Fresh fruit juices and perfect croissants add an agreable touch to a wake up at Sofitel Water Tower.
I've noted also a good equipment with a state of the art Fitness center and a few Mac for free access to internet at the first floor.
To resume, this is truly a very good hotel and at a very attractive rate for a quite expensive city. Maybe working a bit on the service attitude would be good but it's already very OK and i just say that cause i use to go often in Asia where the service is excellent.
I really recommend this hotel for business and leisure.

name: Hotel Burnham - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “My first boutique hotel expereince was a great one.”
text:
I booked the Burnham when traveling to Chi-town for a conference. It was highly ranked by Travel and Leisure Mag. and a good value plus it included high speed internet. Immediately upon arrival, I could tell the difference from the typical corporate hotels just from the demeanor of the front desk staff and bellman. they made you feel more like a guest in their home than a customer. Everyone seemed genuinely glad to work their and very familar with the other Kimpton hotels.
We had a great suite. Not huge but well decorated and equipped. The Aveda (sp) bath products (facial cleanser and shower gel not typical at Hiltons) plus Starbucks in the morning and wine in the afternoon were great touches. My wife loved the location across the street from the HUGE Marshall Fields (she visited it like it was an amusement park); the second largest dept. store in US. 
I had two burgers at the Atwood Cafe (midwest beef is irresistable to this southern boy) and they were great. Saw some of the other dishes and they looked very good, but more "froo-froo" than I was in the mood for. 
I thoroughly enjoyed my stay and will only stay there when visiting Chicago...unless I come across a great deal at the Peninsula.

name: Hotel Monaco Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Perfect”
text: This Hotel was beautiful. The staff were amazing. We were upgraded to a double queen river view suite. The view was spectacular from the "Meditation Nook"(Window Seat). We will definitely go again.

Address: '160 E Pearson St at Water Tower Place'
name: The Ritz-Carlton Chicago (A Four Seasons Hotel)
title: “Amazing service, Fantastic Hotel”
text:
I have had to stay at this hotel a couple of times for work. Each time I have been happy with the great service and comfort of the hotel. If you can get a lake view even better. The staff is always willing to go above and beyond. They have arranged delivery and shipping of packages for me without any trouble. 
The last time I stayed I got snowed in and had a high fever and it was the nicest place in the world to get sick. When I called for tea, they brought me my own hot water electric tea kettle to use for my stay so I could make tea whenever I needed it. The bed is luxurious. The bathroom is well laid out. The toiletries were L'Occitane. Wonderfully thick robe and slippers were provided.
I have eaten in the hotel restaurant which has been fine, but not spectacular. Our real favorite is the hot cocoa in the lobby/bar/cafe. It is delightful on cold winter nights. 
If you need to buy some items at the Water Tower Mall the elevators to the hotel give you direct access. Again helpful during the winter when you don't want to take a stroll outside. 
There is a small business center with computer terminals and printers. 
The only negative is taxi drivers seem to not understand there are two different Four Seasons properties and even if you tell them the Water Tower they drive to the wrong one!
A wonderful luxury hotel and I would return again and again, as long as someone else is paying for it!

name: The Peninsula Chicago
title: “Superb in every category”
text:
I stayed for four nights in an Executive Suite at The Peninsula while visiting friends from my college days. This was my second stay at The Peninsula and it won't be my last. In addition to the stunning service and facilities, I was able to get a very decent rate under one of their summer specials.
My room was extremely spacious (see photos)--separate living room, entrance hallway, connecting hallway, etc. One of my favorite things about the Peninsula is the amount of room devoted to dressing--plenty of closet space, drawers, and mirrors. The sound-proofing was superb--windows open you could hear sirens and all the other sounds of the city, but once they were closed there was no sound from outside.
One of the most attractive things about this room was the bathtub with a window overlooking Michigan Avenue--I took baths just to be able to look through the window! 
The technology is, if anything, over the top--I counted six telephones or equivalents (like the voice-operated one in the bathtub) in the suite, two televisions, a stereo system, and the Peninsula-standard electronic control systems (see photo)--on one morning when I slept in light and housekeeping knocked on the door (a long way from the bedroom) I just had to roll over and hit the "Privacy" button on the phone--a light turned on outside the room and that was it.
No complaints at all about this trip, but I do have two suggestions, both from The Berkeley in London--
1) The deck chairs on the sun roof outside often appeared occupied even though no-one was there--it would be worthwhile to clean these more frequently or to put up a sign asking people to clear away their belongings when they were done so that more people could enjoy the sun deck.
2) Shoes left overnight for polishing should be returned with temporary shoe trees.

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Great!”
text:
Wonderful! The other customer reviews were accurate. Everyone in our family from parents to college age to teens loved this place! 
The smaller hotel lended itself to great customer service. The staff responded to each of our requests/questions.
Exceeded our expectations!

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Incredible!”
text: This hotel cannot be beat for location, price, & atmosphere. The location is ideal, at the corner of State & Kinzie. There are fantastic restaurants & bars all around, including House of Blues & Harry Caray's. We stayed in a "Corner King" room. The room was amazing. Two of the four walls are floor to ceiling windows. Even just being on the 5th floor, we had great views of the surrounding area. The decor and amenities are unmatched. The decor is very clean & simple but luxurious. The hotel is easy to miss from street level, but shouldn't be. The staff were extremely friendly and accommodating. Its a perfect home base if your plans revolve around River North, State Street shopping, or Clark Street nightlife. Even if you'll be on the Mag Mile, this is a short cab ride away. We've officially named this our downtown hotel of choice!

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Was an ok stay”
text:
The stay was ok but my only complaint was that the bed was filthy when we checked in. I noticed a couple hairs on the pillow cases and was a little concerned and upon pulling back the sheets to inspect further I found more hair than should ever come off a person from just sleeping in a bed. I am not sure if they didn't change the sheets or if something happened with the laundry load but it was gross. 
I called the front desk and told them about it and that I would be heading out for the afternoon and could they please change them. They said they would. 
I came back at about nine that night and no one had been to my room yet. I called back down and this time sent a manager up to inspect and she agreed that the condition was unacceptable. I told her I didn't want anything but some clean sheets.....although I did get a 25 dollar credit at the bar to use while I waited which was a nice gesture. 
My only other complaint was that in the end the bed was not all that comfortable. You sink so far down and have no support.

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “Good (not the greatest, but good)”
text:
Great location about 3 blocks to water tower. Great shopping around hotel (Lululemon, Urban Outfitters, American Apparel etc.) Right next to "Viagra Triangle" dining.
$47 valet park per night, but average for Chicago.
Easy checkin. First room had damp smell. Asked to be relocated immediately. Next room much better. 
Noted puddle of water from under sink. However was not enormous, and didnt want to complain a second time, so accepted room. 
Bed very comfortable. Great HDTV. Robes, slippers, sewing kit, soap, loofa, shampoo, conditioner, shower gel, nail filer thing, qtips etc included in marble bath. Toilet speakerphone.
Shower water temperature either an extremely long delay or mind of its own. Would start out cold, then lukewarm, then cooler again, then extremely hot even after turning temp down it would stay hot, then get cold. 
Free coffee and newspapers in the restaurant in the morning. 
The French theme was fine. I found everyone to be very friendly and aside from saying Bonjour to you, they would answer in English with zero atttude.
Overall, would recommend if looking for a hotel in this area, if you get at a good price.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Good hotel, but not 100%”
text:
Comfortable medium sized hotel with well-furnished rooms, free breakfast (kinda), free Internet and good workout facilities.
Staff are on the whole quite helpful and friendly.
The hotel could get five out of five if it wanted to. However, it just doesn't give you that 100% feeling, for the following reasons:
1) Sloppy cleaning - Every day at least one thing wasn't cleaned. Upon closer observation it would appear that the rooms are never checked after cleaning.
2) Elevators - Take hours to arrive. 
3) Breakfast - The free continental breakfast is a nice touch. However it really doesn't include that many things, and even doesn’t have toast. Interestingly the paid for breakfast requires the same effort to collect, and also the same effort by the staff, who simply give you the bill. That doesn't stop them asking for a tip. Something important ran out every day too. For example coffee, or bread, or forks. (Forget about telling the staff if you have a dirty fork.) 
4) Pool – small and freezing cold. I can still feel it now, two weeks later.
Apart from these points it’s a good place to stay and I would go again. A 3.5 really but lets give it a 4.

name: Hotel Burnham - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Room with a View”
text: I spent a long weekend at The Burnham in December. After reading reviews here about massive constant construction across the street, I called in advance and they offered to place me on a higher floor, and to give me a sleep-kit if I should need it, but I didn't. All the exterior work seemed finished to me, and it was never a problem at all. I got a great rate (thanks to a Zipcar discount) on a room that was obviously worth much more. The queen room wasn't huge, but I've seen a lot smaller, and the view from the 12th floor was magnificent and made it seem much more spacious. It was very comfortably appointed, with a chaise in the bay window, where you can read, relax, or watch the snow fall if you're lucky enough. The hotel is also perfectly located for sightseeing and getting around to other neighborhoods in town. Complimentary wine hour is well appreciated and popular, so the small lobby can get cramped. Best to bring yours up to your room and enjoy it with the view. A 9AM shut-off for the complimentary coffee seems a bit early to me, but there's a Lavazza shop next door. Otherwise the staff was gracious and accommodating all around. A very positive experience for me.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “The Houston Magnolia is a flower in our great city!”
text: We had a delightful stay at the Magnolia and would hope to return soon. It is so fun to stay in downtown Houston and enjoy the restaurants, clubs and theatres. Additionally when you are in a hotel that takes care of your every need you have put the icing on the cake for a great weekend get away.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Chicago
title: “Now THIS is a Four Seasons Five Star Property!”
text:
Great location - close to shopping (on top of Bloomingdale's) but also easy to get around for business. I stayed in a corner room on the 45th floor which had amazing views. The beds and pillows were super soft and comfortable. Service at front desk and concierge was attentive. Fitness room is small but there's a nice pool as well. Free wireless internet in the room was easy to access.
There was a noise issue with the air conditioning in the bedroom - the electrician came right away but it wasn't very warm outside so I was fine with just having the air from the living room and turning off the air in the bedroom.
Easy check-in and check-out. A happy trip.

name: The Talbott Hotel
title: “Superior Staff”
text: Just got back from a first time trip to Chicago with 3 of my friends. Chose the Talbott because of it's location and because we prefer smaller hotels. We were not disappointed! I don't think I've ever encountered such a friendly and helpful staff. The rooms were spotless, comfortable, large, and well appointed. The bellmen were not only efficient but gave us many tips about getting around the city. The concierge was superior giving us fantastic ideas of what to see and do , arranging for tickets and even giving us discount coupons for our shopping. We even met the general manager who made sure all of needs were being met. The location of the hotel is wonderful - 2 blocks from the "magnificent mile" and an easy cab ride to all of the museums and parks. I gave it 5 stars but it deserves 10.

name: The Talbott Hotel
title: “Nice contemporary traditional small hotel”
text: We enjoyed a wonderful stay at the Talbot in Chicago. Based on previous reviews we requested an upgraded room for $20 extra per night and were very happy.
