The room was very large, very clean and well appointed. We requested an early check in and were pleasantly accomodated. Free wifi was apprciated. Large flat screen plasma television worked great. The ate at the restaurant (Bice) and were very pleased with both the service and the food. We will definately return to the Talbot and will recommend to our friends and family.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Thoroughly Enjoyable.”
text:
We were heading to the Chicago area to visit relatives in the suburbs and decided to stay in the city for the first night. The Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers offered a great deal for booking 21 days in advance.
It is in such a great location on the river with lake views and near the magnificent mile and navy pier. We walked the entire city and had a fantastic nights sleep on a very comfy bed!

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “marshmallow beds”
text:
On the plus side, it's a great location with great views of the river, and the lake. Steps from Michigan Ave and all the action.
On the down side, I was first put into a wheelchair accessible room, which had a low ceiling and an open bathroom (no tub, just side shower area of floor). While the bed in this room was "normal" (i.e. generally firm), the shower was only really useable as a handheld shower, as the water shot across the shower area horizontally with the head placed in the wall mount. After getting moved to another room (I couldn't deal with that for 3 more nights), I did get a great view of the river and lake and Navy Pier, but now I had what others have described as the bed from hell. So soft it's like sleeping in a marshmallow. Not something I've ever experienced in any other hotel ever. While it might sound appealing, it was so soft it was difficult to change positions and move around, and my companion actually had to sleep on the floor as it was too soft and bad for his back. When I complained about the bed at checkout they did remark that "they are working on that" which may mean they plan on replacing them, as many of my travel companions also complained about these beds. Solely for the horrible beds I would not recommend staying here (unless you want a really soft bed with no back support).

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “We couldn't ask for anything more”
text: We just returned from our daughter's graduation in Chicago and I was in charge of arranging the long weekend for 20 of our extended family who chose to attend. Back in November I searched for hotels based on price and location and I thought we had reserved rooms with the Sofitel. When in May I called to confirm the reservation I was in dismay when I never returned the completed authorization by the deadline and the rooms were released. But Michael Wallace tried his best to assure me that they could accommodate us the best they could based on the circumstances that it was a holiday weekend as well and actually completely sold out. We were able to get enough rooms and they were very patient during our hectic checkin trying to get us all near each other as well. The rooms were beautiful and the beds most comfortable and who can forget the croissants. The location could not be beat and We had perfect weather and perfect weekend. Thanks to all.

name: Hampton Majestic Chicago Theatre District
title: “This is THE hotel of choice for the business traveler in downtown Chicago”
text: After having stayed in a number of downtown hotels and finding them all lacking in one aspect or another, the Hampton Inn Majestic is my new home away from home. The room was tastefully decorated, spacious, comfortable and clean; the complimentary breakfast buffet and in-room Internet were welcome amenities; and the staff was courteous, professional and helpful. The hotel is very secure and within easy walking distance to excellent shopping on State Street and some very fine eateries, including my personal favorite, the Berghoff. The hotel is the perfect destination for the business traveler, but I'm coming back with the family for a weekend in the city.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Chicago
title: “Always look forward to it”
text: Travel to Chicago frequently and usually stay at the Four Seasons. Good location, very comfortable rooms, excellent fitness center, top rate service...everything you'd expect from the Four Seasons.

name: The Talbott Hotel
title: “Very satisfied”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at this hotel for 6 nights. I loved the decor of the hotel. The location is perfect for tourists and a person like me who have lived in the city before and know how to get around the city by public transportation. You can easily access to the red line and #22 and 36 bus to Lincoln park/ wrigleyville area for night out. The concierge service, especially Gene was so helpful. I just did not like one staff at the front desk, a blonde girl, she was not much helpful when I asked her small help. Other than that, I really liked our stay and I highly recommend this hotel to my friends!

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “A Must Stay”
text:
We enjoyed every minute at this hotel. We came in on Valentine's Day, but decided to stay an additional night to fully enjoy all that the hotel had to offer. We relaxed in the rooftop spa overlooking the Downtown skyline, which was the most beautiful vision I've ever seen. 
The staff was efficient and very friendly. I was given a tour of the hotel before staying there highlighting all the history behind the hotel and art exhibits. The atmosphere was very serene. I recommend the Sambuca Package because it pays for two entrees at the Sambuca Jazz Cafe, which was an experience within itself. We were catered to our entire visit.

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “Outstanding facility, very comfortable everything, service could be warmer.”
text:
I stayed one night on business. Had a room on the 16th floor (right across from elevators, but no noise issue at all during the night -- but kind of wondered what the big deal is about being Silver Level in the hotel's program if that gets me right across from the elevators with a so-so view). Great work space, plenty of strong lighting, easy electrical access, and easy to use (t-mobile) wireless. Terrific TV (flat, huge, swivels). Well-stocked mini-bar. Well-designed closet, generous sized bathroom with nice design and level of quality furnishings. Shower pressure excellent. Speaker phone by the loo ... a little odd. Bedding extremely comfortable -- extremely. 
Room service dinner. Hamburger cooked medium -- if you don't like bright pink, go for medium well. Fine size portion and above average quality. Breakfast was very fine. Fast service. Ordered the basics (oatmeal and toast -- the best oatmeal and toast ever; that might sound underwhelming, but order it and see for yourself).
Had a box delivered, room service delivered, restaurant breakfast, counter check in, and doorman hailed a taxi. The doorman was very helpful with luggage and making sure I knew where I was going. Everyone else was efficient and pretty business-like, in contrast to the Sofitel in Manhattan, where everyone was friendly and welcoming. That was a little disappointing. Still, I'd stay there again, business or pleasure.

name: Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers
title: “Wonderful Sheraton Club Staff”
text: Evening staff were a delight. Gave great ideas for dinner and evening entertainment. I usual stay at the Marriott, however, after this trip I will definitely recommend the Sheraton Towers to other colleagues.

name: James Chicago
title: “CUIDADO CON EL DESAYUNO”
text: Muy confortable y con una excelente ubicación. No lo contrateis con desayuno, es un timo. No hay buffet y te meten en el restaturante con la carta (plato + cafe+ zumo de naranja+impuesto+ propina = 40-50 dolares) y luego te dicen que el desayuno incluido solo cubre 12 dolares y medio.

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Hotel!”
text: Stayed here with my adult daughter over the weekend. We had driven separately from different cities. I arrived first and told the parking attendant that my daughter would be coming and I would spring for her parking. When she arrived he he called her by name--she was surprised and impressed! Staff was so friendly and helpful. I arrived before check-in but was given a better room that was ready right away. Loved the decor altho the elevator floor is weird--optical illusion. The location is great. We had to go to the Merchandise Mart for a show and it was easy;also the train is across the street. Nordstrom is a block away.We did not eat at the restaurant so I can't comment on that. I would definitely stay here again.

name: MileNorth, A Chicago Hotel
title: “Topp hotell med perfekt beliggenhet!”
text: Anbefaler på det varmeste! Stilig og moderne hotell rett ved ALT; shoppinggaten 'Magnificent Mile', strandpromenaden, Hancock Tower, restauranter, parker etc. Prøv deep pan pizza på populære Gino's East vegg i vegg - hotellet ordner deg forbi køen, hotellets egen seafoodrestaurant eller få gode tips fra consiergen. Hotellrommene har høy standard og er romslige. Vi bodde to voksne og to barn på dobbeltrom m to queen beds. Har også fine suiter og juniorsuiter. Skulle forvente mye høyere pris for denne type hotell. Sjekk ut baren på takterrassen i 29. etg.! Lekker. Beregn inn kostnad til parkering, som ikke er billig i sentrum - men enkelt m hotellets valet parking. Ikke noe å lure på - dette er stedet å bo i Chicago!

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Chicago - Downtown
title: “The absolute best hotel”
text:
The Hampton Inn and Suites in downtown Chicago is truly an outstanding hotel for many reasons. First the room is very clean the bed is comfortable. Second the staff is very helpful and very professional. Third the location is very good.
What separates this hotel are the little things. The hotel has a spa, pool, sauna, and fitness center. In the pool area, there are ample towels so you don't have to go to the front desk to get them. In addition there are many water bottles in the fitness room saving time and money after a workout.
In addition there is an excellent breakfast including breads, hot and cold cereal, fruit, hot choices which change daily, teas, and juices. Today the hot choices were sausages and French toast which I didn't like. I mentioned this to the staff and they offered to make me eggs and waffles which were great. They just find every way to go out of their way for you at this hotel.
There is also a computer room with 4 terminals in case you want to connect to the internet. There is a printer as well.
I would stay here again and again and recommend this for everyone.

name: Hampton Majestic Chicago Theatre District
title: “Good hotel, great location”
text:
We stayed for 3 nights in the Hampton Inn Majestic in August 2010. The hotel is located very close to the Monroe station on the blue subway line. We took the subway to and from O'Hare airport which was about 40 minutes away. It was easy and at cost of $2.25 per adult one way, it was a far cheaper alternative to a taxi. The entrance to the hotel is small as the lobby is situated a few floors above the theatre. We stayed on the 11th floor in a room that contained 2 queen beds. We found it quite spacious, the beds were very comfortable. The bathroom was good with plenty of space around the sink for toiletries. 
The breakfast was okay, it is included in everyones room rate. There were a few hot items and breads, cereals etc. The area does get quite busy though.
The hotel is in a very good location just a few minutes walk from Millennium Park.
We loved our trip to Chicago it was even better than expected. The museums such as The Field & Art Institute are very good. Chicago is an excellent destinations for families as there are many interactive attractions for the kids. We will certainly be back as there is still more to see. To save on the attractions we bought the citypass. Also have a look on the explore Chicago website as they have visitor discounts for various attractions & shops.
Thank you to the staff member that helped with taking our bags to the subway station.

name: Hampton Majestic Chicago Theatre District
title: “A Hampton Inn in the Center of Chicago!”
text:
Hampton Inn fans will find the usual amenities in this hotel – well-appointed rooms, styrofoam breakfasts, helpful staff, and reasonable prices. The great advantage of the location is that it is just around the corner from the Monroe stop on the CTA line from Ohare, so taxis are not necessary to get there. Get a multiple-day bus pass and use the 151 bus around the corner for the 10-minute ride to North Michigan Avenue. 
When we came out of the subway and tried to find the hotel, nobody in the neighborhood seemed to know where it was, so we’ll tell you: it has a small entrance right next to the big theater marquee on Monroe. (It’s in a converted office building, with the lobby on the fourth floor.)

name: Conrad Chicago
title: “Faultless!!!”
text: Not really much to add to the title really, everything you could want from a hotel from a warm welcome to a great room, nice bar food, everything very clean, complimentary tea and coffee in a morning, just all wonderful. We would without doubt be back to this hotel if we returned to Chicago.

name: Radisson Blu Aqua Hotel
title: “Validissimo”
text: Splendido hotel della catena Radisson. La posizione è strategica: a ridosso del Millenium Park, del Magnificent Mile, del Navy Pier e del lungo lago. Interni fusion e di grande atmosfera. Camere ampie, pulite e dotate di ogni confort. Splendida la pascina all'aperto tra i grattacieli (valida anche la piscina al coperto e il centro fitness). Ottime possibilità di running (tra Millenium Park e lungo lago suggerisco decisamente quest'ultimo in direzione sud: strepitosi panorami della città). Super consigliato.

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great stay.”
text: Weekend visit to Chicago for my wife's birthday was well spent at the Palomar. Second time there and was once again treated exceptionally well. Everyone at the front desk is eager to help. They made dinner reservations and sent a bottle of wine to our room for a birthday treat. Squeaky clean room. We love the Kimpton atmosphere. $48 a day to park hurts, but that is probably standard for Chicago. next time we will fly in and use the subway which has a stop right by the hotel.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “A wonderful night in the city of chicago suburbians”
text:
otter Palmer built the hotel 137 years ago as a gift to his wife, Bertha Honore. Since then, it has been burned down (Chicago Fire) and undergone multiple owners and renovations. Currently, it is undergoing another face lift and we just got back from a quick one night trip there. We got the hotel through priceline so we paid under $100 for the night. 
The hotel is huge (over 1600 rooms). Our check in was easy and all staff we came in contact with was very nice. We stayed in a standard room (8th floor). 
The exterior is definitely a mess as others mentioned but the lobby still looks great and the bar creates a nice feel to it. The hallways on the room floors have been redone completely. Square Frames hold soft focused b/w pictures of famous performers that once performed in the Empire Room back in the day. Extremely classy. Our room was large. The colors were bold (bright greens, reds, black and white, deep cherry woods). Nothing bad to say about the decor inside the room. The bed was very comfortable and the sheets were great. There was a desk with an internet connection (believe it was an extra) and another lounge chair with an ottoman. 
The bathroom was small. There was a bowl sink which was a nice touch and i think they kept the former floor and wall tile. We did have hot water (noticed that was mentioned) however the fixtures for the shower were old and the water pressure was sub-optimal. The tolietries were Crabtree and Evelyn and were ample and pleasant smelling. There were plenty of towels.
The TV was a small tube tv that was very far away from the bed (one of the minuses of a large room) and they also had Figi Water to intice you but it was $6.50 per bottle. (Hint: stop at the CVS across the street for snacks)
We ordered room service for breakfast and it was nice. Overpriced but very good food. We did not eat at the Lockwood so not sure how that was even though it was advertised a lot. 
The hotel is in a great area of visitors who want to do shopping downtown, see shows and be close to Millenium Park. State Street shopping is a must along with a visit to the bean. 
Finally, I noticed they are adding a lot of amenities to compete with new build hotels (flat panel tv with announcements, kiosks to check in to your flight with printer, trendy bar that is being built and complete renovation of the fitness center). 
I will admit, i am a sucker for places with rich history so the hotel already won me over with that. I have stayed here over 10 years ago and remember my experience being pleasant but this past one was definitely above average. I wouldn't say this is a family focused hotel however the rooms are big enough for a few kiddies on rollaways without you tripping on them. There was nothing that was negative about the stay HOWEVER, the amenities that are being renovated take away from a full Upscale experience. As we only stayed a night (and live in the Chicago Burbs), these werent a must but someone visiting this city for a longer stay, i can see how not having them can impact your trip.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “A fantastic hotel and city”
text: We took our 4 children to Chicago for spring break. I was a little worried after reading some reviews of the Hyatt. Boy were we suprised!!! The rooms were beautiful with a wonderful view of the city. The staff was helpful, friendly, and overall delightful. The rooms were beautiful, clean, and quiet. Our trip could not have been better. The hotel was in the perfect location and when we needed our car, our wait was only 10 or 15 min.. The city and the hotel were wonderful and we will go back to both!!

name: MileNorth, A Chicago Hotel
title: “Excellent compromis”
text: Un excellent compromis, emplacement très pratique, central, confort quasi parfait, à la seule exception d'un lit un peu bizarre car rehaussé de quelques vingt centimètres. Du coup, un peu bancal, un peu mou. Etonnant dans cette gamme de prix de d'hôtel, où les lits sont généralement parfaits. Sinon, le reste, très bien. Studio-room très grande, bon design, accueil parfait.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Nice business hotel”
text:
The hotel is a very nice business hotel.
The rooms have a good size and are well kept.
These not a real restaurant - but a "club" room where breakfast is served, and you can get "bar grub"´(burgers and such).
Nice fitness room, and a nice roof terrace with pool and spa. 
For Houston - a downtown location is not as great as a foriger may think. Downtown is quite dead when the working day ends. But at least its very quite.

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Impeccable service”
text:
Stayed here six nights with my son. Got a deal at 119us per night for a double queen room on travel ticker, a great resource for Chicago hotels. I wanted something with a breakfast as teenagers are always hungry.
We got there early and were able to check in right away. I requested a fan for the room, I like the noise to help me sleep, and it was already set up before I could tip the guy! The front desk is also the concierge and they were very knowledgable on the sights I wanted to see. You check in sitting down and the staff seem to remember you, due to the small room numbers I imagine.
During my visit they were experimenting with drink 'coupons'....going to the happy hour which were given to me upon check inthey had discontinued it a day or so later, I still have them as a souvenier. I think they were trying to restrict some guests for ordering too much of their top shelf liquor. I enjoyed their italian beer and their house drink, a lemonish martini. Worth the dollar a drink tip, not required. My son would order a coke but he didn't like the evening offerings. That could be changed around a bit, more finger food as the offerings could be messy when socializing. Perhaps gourmet pizza bits. I only was at the hotel for two nights during the manager welcome so not sure if they switch around the menu. I did notice some 'hoarding' at the continental breakfast, excellent. good quality baked goods, juices and coffee/tea. Also very nicely presented. I did see many people unaware that they could go to another floor if they were out of something, perhaps a note placed on each floor explaning this to alleviate frustration.
Also I was able to use the free computer and printer in the business center with two macs and 3 windows and no wait there either. 
What I liked best was the close proximity to Andys jazz club around the corner.
I read in other reviews about the location. It's not bad, a little scraggly but being improved and the proximity to Trump tower it should even become a better area.
My room was on the sixth, top floor a nice view, directly across from the lounge. Very nice and quiet after 8. 
If I return, I would stay somewhere else but I would highly recommend it to anyone visiting Chicago.
Also our flight was to be later in the evening and the bell hop watched our luggage.
When we returned, they didn't even ask for our tickets and had them ready. Great service, a few bucks tip goes a long way at this property.

name: Amalfi Hotel Chicago
title: “Great Location”
text: This hotel was super nice, and since it was a couple of blocks from Michigan Avenue, it was a lot cheaper than staying right on. It was still a great location - literally two blocks from Michigan Avenue. They had a reception each night that was fun. Try the Amalfitini! Also, Harey Carey's across the street is great.

name: Hotel Burnham - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Almost flawless”
text:
Beautiful hotel (rooms, lobby, and exterior), friendly/competent but not obtrusive staff, and great location. Yes, the rooms are on the small side, but not uncomfortably so. It was actually great to have the bed so close to the huge window with the terrific view. Bed super comfortable. Everything ultra-clean. 
Now.. you're waiting to hear about the flaw. The 'pets welcome' policy includes barking dogs. We didn't complain about it because my husband and I could not hear the two dogs on our floor that barked constantly from our room. You could hear them quite well from my son's room two doors down, but he said it didn't bother him. So, this may not be fair to mention because I have no idea if the hotel would have done something about it if we had. Otherwise, the hotel was very quiet (and I am pretty noise-sensitive). 
Everything else was perfect.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “The Worst Big City Hotel”
text: I have stayed here before. It was OKAY, but I expected after the trumpeted 150 Milion renovation it would be better this time. Just the worst. My greatgrandparents used to stay here--maybe it was something then but it is nothing now. The Lobby is beautiful and the ceiling is not to be missed--but then run from this place. Phones don't work--for example, if you press the message button you get the director of food and beverage. The room service button didn't work either-you have to call the operator for everything and hope that they pick up. The rooms are TINY. I didn't need a remote control for the TV--I could use my toes! And the bathroom--well let's just say I have suits larger that that. I had a lovely view of a fireescape and could never tell if it was day or night. Yet it is packed with conventioneers. Maybe those are the folks that give it good reviews--I don't know-but I have been here twice in 6 months for about a week each time and it is awful.

name: Hyatt Regency Chicago
title: “Great Value”
text:
I spent one Saturday evening at the Hyatt with my fiance for a night downtown. Check in was very busy, we felt like we were in Las Vegas, but the woman who helped us was friendly and efficient. We had room 1572 a city view king non-smoking and we were very impressed with it. It had a little bit of fun with color and was definitely roomy enough. The bed was very comfortable and the view was fantastic. We woke up to a view of the river, John Hancock building, the Tribune building, and the rest of beautiful Chicago. One problem was that the shower literally needed to run for 15 minutes before it warmed up. We called the front desk after 5 minutes and they said to just continue to let it run and call back in a few minutes and if it still isn't working they will send someone up. It did eventually get hot, but it threw us off by 15 minutes. 
Big Bar in the hotel was a really fun place. You can't beat the view and the 48oz. martinis, margaritas, beers, and drinks are very fun. They are pretty reasonable at under 20 for all of the Big drinks. Most of the clientele looked like they were guests of the hotel stopping in to get a drink before dinner or clubs. It would be a great place to go for the start of bachelorette party or girls night out with the big fun drinks and Big appetizers. There were a lot of groups like that there. The location is fantastic, the valet is expensive but very courteous and quick with your car, and the 16.95 breakfast buffet was above average. The service in the hotel was good but not fantastic. All of the waiters, bellhops, and front desk people just were a little off in service. It seems as if the Hyatt is trying to improve this because with literally every time you interact with an employee you get handed a survey. I booked my room with Hotwire and got a great deal, I think this hotel is worth every penny. I would definitely stay here again.

name: Magnolia Hotel Houston
title: “Best hotel stay ever!”
text: Everything was exceptional. Keep up the good work.

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Very very nice hotel”
text:
We're just ensconced on our first night here, but the impression is so strong I thought I'd write the review now. Hopefully all will continue to go well.
Front desk is attentive and courteous, same with bellman. We had a suite (17-year-old daughter in tow), and it was very generously-sized, with a front room that has a fold-out bed, TV, sitting area. Very well designed, the bath in the center has doors on both sides for privacy.
Excellent location, a block from the river on State Street. I don't know why I'd stay anywhere else.

name: Hotel Monaco Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “I would stay here everytime”
text: We're big fans of Kimpton hotels, and have had many great experiences there, but this one was just over the top. It was a combined business/leisure trip, and we were upgraded to a two-room "Mediterranean" suite that was huge, functional, and just stunningly beautiful. Big window seats were great to relax and enjoy views of the river. The staff was incredibly helpful and pleasant, the location was both close to work, shopping, dining and tourist-y stuff. The Kimpton loyalty program (Kimpton In Touch) has nice perks, too. I get to Chicago a couple of times a year, and there is no doubt this will be my first choice hotel from now on.

name: Hotel Monaco Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Spectacular Stay at the Awesome Hotel Monaco”
text: We could not have asked for more during our recent stay at the Hotel Monaco in Chicago. We received awesome service from a friendly staff. Every request from a fan for the room to starch for ironing my husband's shirt was fulfilled. We were very happy with the location, the free wine hour, and the room decor- absolutely loved the window seats overlooking the river! Will definitely stay there again and would highly recommend it.

name: Sheraton Los Angeles Downtown Hotel
title: “Good downtown hotel”
text:
We really enjoyed staying at this downtown Los Angeles hotel. It is conveniently located to L.A. LIVE and the financial district.
The Front Desk clerk (Jessica) was very pleasant and helpful. Our room was spacious and clean and the Sheraton Sweet Sleeper bed and pillows were very comfortable. The bathroom was also very clean. However, I found a single long brown hair (obviously from a woman) in the bathtub. How did the housekeeper miss this???
I found the price that we paid for the Sheraton "traditional" room to be an excellent value, especially when compared with other hotels in the downtown area.
The only concern I have with this Sheraton is their lack of security. The hotel is easily accessible from either the front entrance or the Macy's Plaza mall, but the hotel elevators do not require your room keycard to use. So, anyone (including thieves and other sinister-minded perpetrators) can just walk into the hotel elevators and stop off on any floor that they want (although there are a few floors where a room keycard is required). It is a disturbing thought and I hope the Sheraton will address this issue soon.
Other than that, we would definitely stay here again.

name: Sea Rock Inn
title: “the perfect place to stay”
text: The motel is close to lax so when we arrived we could go straight to bed without the hassle of driving through half of the city. The people at the reception are very friendly and the room was clean. You even get a hair blower which is rare in this category. Probably a good idea to ask for a room downstairs. The upper ones are pretty heated up in september. Would go there again.

name: Sea Rock Inn
title: “Excellent location, excellent service, super clean, highly recommend.”
text: The Sea Rock Inn is the best. I'm really happy to have stayed for 3 weeks. Great value for the price. Terry was excellent, very pleasant and very helpful. I highly recommend this place to everyone, you won't be dessapointed.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Eagle Rock Inn
title: “Great location for visiting Hollywood and Rose Bowl”
text:
As they say in real estate, the three selling points are location, location, location. Best Western Eagle Rock certainly has it for those visiting Hollywood and Pasadena. The motel is right on Colorado Boulevard and a short 10 to 15 minute drive to the Tournament of Roses Parade and college football at the Rose Bowl. 
Head west on Colorado and you're an easy hop, skip and jump to Hollywood without getting on the freeway; or crawl on the nearby Ventura Freeway (Highway 134) to the studios at Burbank. Both Hollywood and Burbank are about 20 minutes away.
We've been to Los Angeles twice within the last two years and stayed here both times. We will stay here again. It's not fancy. Just a nice, functional, comfortable motel with a super-nice staff. They go out of their way to help you with directions around town and are quick to respond to issues related to the motel. 
Colorado Boulevard is a busy street and you can hear the Glendale Freeway traffic at times. But it's not overwhelming. We ran the fan on low at night and could hear nothing but the fan.
The only real downside to the property is the breakfast room. It's way too small. The owners should consider taking out a room or making some accommodation to provide more space. While the breakfast was ample, we don't go for the free breakfast or spacious seating. We go to Best Western Eagle Rock for a comfortable, conveniently-located, moderately-priced motel to get a good night's sleep that will make our trips to Los Angeles enjoyable. And that's exactly what we've found it to be over the last two years.

name: Holiday Inn Express Century City
title: “Value for money”
text: This hotel had an excellent location, free internet and breakfast included in the price. My room was spacious, clean and quiet and equipped with a huge TV. The hotel staff was very helpful and minor problem with internet connection was promptly fixed. I stayed in Los Angeles to attend a conference. My impression was that I had a much better hotel for almost half the price than my collegues who stayed at the conference hotel.

name: Hotel Monaco Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A very good choice!”
text: This hotel is rated 10 out of 163 for a reason. Spencer and I were in town only a short time to catch a concert at the Chicago Theater. Unfortunately, we didn't have time to enjoy everything the Hotel Monaco has to offer (wine hour, hot chocolate, time to relax in the window overlooking the river...), but that didn't stop us from being very impressed and wanting to come back. The service was excellent from the time we called en route for an earlier check-in to the time we left valet parking wishing us a safe trip home. The location is perfect with shopping, restaurants, the Chicago Theater, and Millennium Park just a few steps away. The room was clean, comfortable and quiet and the staff met every request without hesitation. We cannot wait to come back and spend more time in this great city and hotel!

name: Holiday Inn Express Century City
title: “Just what the doctor ordered”
text: My son and I flew into LA from Chicago for a 24 stay. He had an interview at UCLA for his residency and I came with to visit family. The last thing my son wanted to do was share a room with his mom. Rather than reserving 2 rooms, I made a reservation for a room with 2 separate beds. Instead, the hotel gave us a room that had a spiral staircase with one bed upstairs and the other downstairs. It was a suite. I even got a welcome goody bag. I was blown away. The staff was so accommodating, from the valet, to Sohaib, to Troy at the front desk answering all my questions, giving directions and relocating my lost boarding passes. Every member of their staff was kind, considerate and helpful. The location: great. Breakfast and coffee: great. Staff: great. Room: outstanding. Thank you again for the superior accommodations. You really make your guests feel important.

name: The Hotel Wilshire, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Nice little boutique hotel”
text: We stayed here while visiting my son in Hollywood. The location is great, very near LACMA and the Tar Pits. Although we drove right past the small, poorly marked entrance. The room was well appointed and the bathroom was very nice and modern. The large shower was excellent. I like a firm bed but this one was just a little too hard. We made the mistake of eating dinner at the rooftop restaurant one night. The food was just average and the service was absolutely terrible.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Mikado Hotel
title: “Worst place I ever stayed would not recommend.”
text: This place had very poor service I imediately felt unwelcome as I entered. Very unfriendly atmosphere. Room were ages, very poor quality and floor creaked. Parking space was too narrow especially for large vehicles. Overall worst place I ever stayed at would not recommend staying there to anyone.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Mikado Hotel
title: “Yuk”
text: The hotel looks great on the picture but for the price you pay you would expect a better room. The parking spaces which are in the bank, are cramped I was afraid i would get my car door hit. The room feels tiny and we got the feeling of the crawlies; it feels more like a filthy motel than the nice hotel they make it to be. (bring your own portable DVD player.) I left a day early cause I couldn't take it anymore. I was willing to pay for both days as I knew they would. They and charged me $100 deposit upfront which remained in my bank for 7 days! They serve a free breakfast in their restaurant next door which is okay if you like cold, half cooked eggs, mushy potatoes, (not hash browns) and warm orange and apple juice. The neighborhood is NOT what you would think, but If you need a couple of good liquor stores nearby you're in luck.

name: Howard Johnson Los Angeles
title: “Nice rooms, but Poor Hotel, poor service Staff”
text:
Well they remodel some rooms and everything is brand new, The Front Desk staff very poor service I request one extra blanket and said to me thy don't have extra.
The decor in Front Desk is ugly, in the Web page show Pool, this hotel they don't have pool and fitness center.
The Breakfast is ok

name: Comfort Inn - Los Angeles / West Sunset Blvd.
title: “Sunset Blvd, free parking, broadband and that's it”
text: Quite small rooms with free broadband, free wifi in main lobby, free parking in the yard, free breakfast with doughnuts, etc. though Starbucks just around corner, 7/11 across the street. There is also a very small pool but does not look too attractive. The place is ok if you just need a bed and no extra.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Mikado Hotel
title: “Peaceful, Asian-inspired Hotel”
text:
I decided to choose BW Mikado because of a previous stay that was quite pleasant. Again, the hotel proved it was worth staying at again. Check in was prompt. The gentleman at the front counter anticipated my arrival and the keys/room were ready. The lobby was classy - it has a grand piano! Upon arriving at the room, I noticed how clean and modern it looked. As always, the room was comfortable.
Internet connection was fast, enjoyed the private balcony, and the view from the room. There's a Japanese garden in the middle of the hotel. The red bridge stood out. The hotel also offered free continental breakfast located at the restaurant next door. 
I will definitely come back to this hotel.

name: Super 8 Hollywood
title: “GREAT PLACE”
text: This is one of the best locations in hollywood. Close to all atractions also close to subways and bus station for transportation. Great breakfast and clean rooms.

name: Comfort Inn - Los Angeles / West Sunset Blvd.
title: “Average At Best”
text:
Location is reasonably convenient, but rather rough. Parking is included, and secured at night.
At check-in, reservation through Hotels.com was not in the computer system, but the rate was honored. Service was adequate in the day, surly at night.
Rooms were average. Mattress was very hard. Walls were EXTREMELY thin, could hear normal conversation (and worse) easily word for word. Bathroom was clean, with engineered stone walls in the shower/bath (better than I expected).
Breakfast (included) was typical continental. Waffles were a plus.
Overall, not quite "average" but maybe earns the rating given the price. Definitely not worthy of anything higher. Would have been worth shelling out a few extra bucks for a different place.

name: Valley Inn & Conference Center
title: “Time for new mattresses!”
text:
We checked in at 11pm. The neighborhood was a little rough. The bed was awful, it was as if someone had thrown a foam mattress on top of the old mattress. If you got too close to the edge, you'd roll off the bed! 
We forgot our shampoo and there was no small bottle of shampoo like in all the other BW's in which we've stayed. We washed our hair with a very small bar of soap, and barely had enough left for bathing. The heavy curtains covered the air conditioning unit, so we had to prop a chair under the curtains to hold them up so we could get cool air into the room. When we checked out the next morning, the two men at the desk barely spoke English, so it was difficult to communicate with them. We finally gave up and just left. For the price, it was fine, but I would never stay there for more than one night. We almost never stay in a AAA two diamond, and this is the perfect example of why.

name: Hollywood Inn Express South
title: “Cocroaches......... Rude staff....really horrible experience”
text: So Ive been travelling all over the world and i'm pretty laid back....i also dont normally write reviews as i dont mind a bit of dirt or if something is not perfect but we checked in to this motel and i always ask for a room upstars as there are less insects...anyway i was sat on the bed when a huge cocroach ran out from under the bed....i was a bit grossed out but decided to try catch it..... until i pulled the cover back off the bed and found loads of little lice looking things crawling all over the sheets....I have stayed in some awful places in vietnam and never seen anything this bad, so i went down and said at the desk that i was willing to stay there if they could move me to another room which they refused to do and they also refused to give me a refund so we had to leave and pay for another room in another motel! DO not go here

name: Hollywood Inn Express North
title: “Life's Nightmare”
text: I was there with my parents and sister, so we were 4 people and had a reservation of one room with 2 double beds . WE reached the hotel at 1:00pm but the manager didnt allow us to enter before 2:00pm as that was the check in time. We had lunch nearby and returned. The manager was highly rude and did not agree that a room was booked for 4 people. To avoid any further arguments I asked how much would I need to pay for 2 extra people and he asked for 50$ per person. I had researched many hotels before that and none had such an expensive guest rate. I asked him to give me the receipt and he bluntly refused. Upon asking the reason he just said that I wudnt give you any receipt of this and you might as well leave as he didnt want us to stay there. He was insane. I called up hotels.com and they spoke to him. He told them that he offered us only 10$/guest and that he is refusing as I tried to hit him!!! On hearing this I immediately left that place!

name: Hollywood Inn Express North
title: “Didn't stay, even though had prepaid”
text:
We arrived about ten in the evening on July 19th. The neighborhood is to put it mildly "scary". We were asked to give a $10. deposit for the tv remote; therefore, everytime we went out we took the remote with us to avoid "losing" it. We asked for Kleenex and were given an extra roll of toilet paper. There are no towel bars, lamps, or clock radios; in fact, nothing that the "clientele" can "mistakenly" take with them when they flee in the middle of the night. 
It was difficult to find another hotel in L.A. in the middle of the tourist season; but even though we had a nonrefundable prepay; we called and called until we found somewhere else and checked out. It was well worth paying twice to escape.
On the positive side, the place is very clean and what is in the rooms is not shabby or worn; so if you can live with the other conditions, then it's probably a good deal.

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “GREAT PLACE TO STAY”
text: Trino in the bar is the best server I have had in a long time

name: Nite Inn at Universal City
title: “Lawsuit waiting to happen”
text:
Booked this hotel because of the location and they had a jetted tub.
Parking was terrible had to get up very early to move the car so other quests could get out.
The main problem with this place was the beds. Two beds in the room and both had springs sticking out of the side of the mattress I almost cut my leg open on it.
They charged a big price for this room which would have been OK if the room was nice.
Too bad someone with more insight doesn't redo the rooms.
It is old and the so called breakfast was a joke.
find another place is my advice.

name: St. George Motor Inn
title: “Most awful experience of my life”
text: Stayed here because it was late at night and other motels were booked, it was awful dirty and stained bed sheets, very thin walls you could hear everything that people were doing most disturbing, sketchy, and uncomfortable experience of my life, and I have done some traveling across the united states and around the world

name: Hollywood Inn Express South
title: “Worest places I have ever stayed”
text:
This hotel is even worse than any low developing countries. Dirty room and rude service.
What is poorest hotel in LA? come to get the answer.

name: Nite Inn at Universal City
title: “Save your relationship do not stay here !!!!!”
text:
I have never ever written a review in my life but felt compelled to put something down to save you all from this hell hole.
Trust me this place is the worst on the planet and I have stayed in some grotty hotels. Once checked in we noticed that all the curtains were closed and the room was in darkness. We turned on the light and I can only describe it as a candle flickering in the corner..... We pulled back the curtains to reveal what we had got ourselves into, Instead of replacing the carpet in the room they appear to have cut around the bed... "Hey it saved them having to take the bed out the room". On closer inspection we noticed that the bed sheets were not clean. The bathroom was like something you would find at a festival...... 
If you close your eyes and imagine a crack house with pimps waiting outside your door you will have a good picture of the nite Inn.
Being a fellow bargain hunter I came to realise that this is a no go, go stay at the Hilton over the road and enjoy your holiday, It may be $100 more but just do it!!! Oh and try get your money back from the reception is another experience.... GOOD LUCK

name: Ramada Los Angeles Convention Center
title: “Creepy Crawlies”
text: I stayed in two rooms during my trip. The first was infested by ants. The second infested by ants and I saw a large cockroach. When I realized the whole building was infested I decided to check out. Neither room had been cleaned in days as I noticed a lot of dirt under beds. TV also didn't work properly. Whoever is running this place does not care about anything but taking your money. The manager was supposed to call me to apologize but she still hasn't. DON'T STAY HERE!!!!

name: Ramada Wilshire Center
title: “Ramada? Are you serious?”
text: If this is what Ramada has become, then I will have to cross the hotel chain of my 'hotel' list. This is a neighborhood motel at best. The motel had a nasty carpet, missing hardware on the furniture, bathroom tiles broken/ missing, etc... Everything you would expect from a $35/night motel out of the travelers magazines you find in IHOP and such. And if that was the price, I am good to go. If you are seeing a show at the Wiltern, it's tops. One block to the right, the show. 1/2 block to the left, great Korean BBQ before the show. Makes a great eve. But the motel itself needs some solid work to call itself a Ramada or hotel. If they ever decide to upgrade and figure it all out, it's a grand stop for the Wiltern experience. If they don't, I will begin the search for an alternative in the hood.

name: Sunrise Hotel San Pedro
title: “It was fine”
text:
In traveling to destinations in California I've noticed that the air conditioning units are not running for the guests checking into the hotels. Obviously, the high cost of electricity in mind but we guests ARE paying for the room and it would be nice to have it comfortable when we get there instead of waiting several hours for the room to cool off.
This hotel is next to the piers. Great location for getting to dive boats (we were scuba diving for the weekend). There are also shops, restaurants and a few other attractions near by. Close to cruise ships, it's a great one or two night stay. Rooms are big, beds comfortable and the price was right on the internet for what we were looking for. Clean room, the towels smelled fresh and laundered instead of that heavy bleach smell you get at some properties.
Recommended for shorter stays, desk clerk was helpful and staff were attentive and prompt when I requested an extra blanket and pillows.

name: The Historic Mayfair Hotel
title: “Needs new staff”
text:
I was in Los Angeles and the prices were so high that I had to book one room for 5 people at the Historic Mayfair Hotel on West 7th street. The neighborhood was ok. The hotel lobby is very good looking, the floors were clean and it smelled good. We were a late check in, I did call from the airport to make sure the room was kept and that a cot was put in it. 
When we got there, I had to almost argue for the cot, I had called and when I reserved I asked for it. 
The room was big and clean. It needs a little renovation in the bathroom which was tiny and couldn't fit 2 people at a time. 
The next day, I needed to go to Hollywood, Grauman's chinese theater, we were 5 adults. When I asked at the front desk, they told me in a rude matter to go to the bellman's desk. I went and he called a taxi. The taxi arrived 5 minutes later. After half the ride was done, I noticed that the taxi didn't have the normal 'taxi permits' in the car... it was illegal! I asked him for which company he was for and he sai that he was for none and that he was the bellman's cousin!!!! He was rude and made very impolite comments on us being a group of women. 1 man on 5 people. 
We ended up paying 40$ for a trip that cost us 25-28$ in later taxis. 
The next day, we asked for a taxi again and I said that I didn't want the same as yesterday, that I want a REAL taxi. The bellman was very angry and didn't call the company for aout 30 minutes. I ended up calling them myself. 
One night, we came back from a show and wanted a pizza. The night audit was very rude and just screamed at me that he didn't have any.... I asked the security guard who was very nice and gave me 3-4 numbers and even the websites.
Talking about the internet, the service was so slow that I had the time to go take a shower before my Ipad downloaded a hotmail page!!! No printer was available in the 'business center'.
We took the breakfast, 9$ a person. It was horrible, most of the food was cold and what needed to be cold was hot... let's say it was the first and last time we went. 
So in general the hotel is clean, but the service is HORRIBLE!!!! If you go there, prepare yourself before and don't ask for anything!!!!

name: Bevonshire Lodge Motel
title: “The Price was Right”
text: Went to LA to see the Price Is Right. We didn't expect much from the room because it was inexpensive compared to others in the area. It smelled like cleaner which is a good thing but I think family members must clean the rooms. The sheets were clean but the blanket on the bed left little to the imagination. Large rooms and the proximity to The Grove shopping and Farmers Market was great...about 10 minutes in a relatively safe neighbourhood. (I wouldn't walk it alone though). I would stay there again as I said the price was right and we had brought blankets with us to camp out on the street for the last night. At the gate 2pm Sunday for the 1:15pm taping Monday. Worth every minute of the wait to see Bob Barker and be in the audience. If you are going, bring an alarm clock and hair dryer if you need those items, although was happy to see a large bar fridge and microwave in the room. We didn't use the pool but as you can see by the photos you couldn't really hang out around it so don't book this hotel if you want to lounge at the pool, looked clean and inviting, if the weather was hot enough.

name: Royal Pagoda Motel
title: “NOt well maintained and staff that don't care.”
text: To start, its too far from the nearest metro station, the phone didn't even work. my friend said his bed had bedbugs, and the people next door kept us up all night being rude and talking loudly on a cell phone out on the balcony and nothing was done about it. This place sucks.

name: Super 8 Hollywood
title: “Absolut ausreichend!”
text: Die erste Nacht in Los Angeles haben wir in diesem Hotel verbracht! Zu Fuß ist es etwas weit zum Hollywoodblvd. Da man aber eh ohne Auto in den USA verloren wäre, ist es absolut kein Problem von dort alles zu erreichen! Das Zimmer war sauber und groß. Das Frühstück ein typisches Motelfrühstück. Alles in Allem aber absolut sauber und ok! Würden dort wieder übernachten!

name: Ramada Los Angeles Convention Center
title: “je le conseille”
text: hotel bien situé, personnel aimable, chambres propores et spacieues. très bon rapport qualité/prix

name: Royal Pagoda Motel
title: “Large clean room at a cheap price!”
text: We searched online for a decent place to stay close to dodger stadium. This place is about a mile away. The room was spacious and VERY clean. Loved the wood floors. It was very quiet at night. Only complaint is parking is very limited. Well worth the price,, great bargain!

name: Ritz Milner Hotel
title: “agreeable simplicity”
text: the hotel is tidy, clean, on a great location. Rooms may be a bit small, but for a working trip, very good. Above all, the staff was allways friendly and willing to help. for the price it is above expectations!

name: Kawada Hotel
title: “OK - dont stress if youve already booked it.”
text: hmmmmmm, a bit of a strange one, staying in downtown is not really helpful - staying near hollywood boulevard would have been better. Had to pay $15 per day extra for Parking - so would have preffered to use that money for a better location, and you have to use the valet. Staff a bit distant, but would help if we asked. Not a very good location, but good for catching the metro - which we did most days. Nothing special like a pool or fitness room. Could use a communal computer for checking emails (1 for whole hotel). To be honest, wouldnt recommend. But it was clean and safe, and that was our requirements.

name: The Wilshire Hotel Los Angeles
title: “I liked their hospitality”
text: We reahed late in the evening but the welcome we received at the check in counter was really amazing! A special mention for Ms. Johanna who was very helpful and efficient. We were in our rooms in flat 10 minutes from the time we reached. The rooms are spacious and I would say by all standards a good value for money!! They certainly need to do something about their Internet which is hardly available in the room and every time you need to use it one has to go down to the lobby. overall experience was good and would certainly stay their again during our next vsit.

name: Quality Inn Hollywood
title: “Welcome to the Hotel California...?!”
text: ...Or maybe the hotel should be named Adequate Inn. We were visiting family in the area plus seeing a few of the sights and chose cheap and cheerful. Well, not so cheerful and certainly not cheap. The day we checked in, the gentleman at the desk asked for my I.D. and promptly coughed over my driver's license! The only redeeming feature was the bed, which was comfortable. The fire alarm was set off one night thanks to some drunken guest, but the a/c unit in the room was loud enough anyway, it kept waking us up. Bathroom has definitely seen better days and towels were well laundered and thin... everything felt dark, damp and claustrophobic. We chose to eat breakfast out of the hotel. My husband says it felt old and dirty but they probably don't care. A tip - search for somewhere further west or rent something at Manhattan Beach!

name: The Historic Mayfair Hotel
title: “What positive is there at the Mayfair on 7th st?”
text:
Just plain disgusting. Disgusting service, rooms, and the area just should of been a clue. The general manager Sadler* I believe his name was? walks with his nose up in the air, even eyeballed my wife and I as if we were some criminals, I only make six figures, tip very well and have respect for everyone. Even my "Hello" to him didn't seem to ease the situation. but enough of just that one disrespectful staff member. Spent well over $500-700 just for a week but recieved my 150 deposit back so more around the 500 field due to false promises provided by the front desk. I was promised pro-rate if I decided to stay longer than the day or two originally planned but my company meetings ended up lasting longer. Two days of 80 dollars each day were not combined in the extended stay which was promised by a young female at Front Desk, so i had to spend 160 dollars for two days than pay their 150 dollar deposit and another 350 dollars for the weekly stay. People listen to these reviews, the staff cannot function a hotel promptly, I found a Jewish Manager and Baggage man to be the only helpful staff members but their schedules seem to have them only their for a very few hours of the days. You would think this was a classic hotel with great history, it's more of a hotel were you Addicts and Prostitutes find business. Pay the extra 10 or 20 dollars, you will have all the amentites which should be provided and you won't sleep with the fear of bed bugs. This is the first hotel I've had to put a thumbs down too, God Bless. 
Quick Notes:
Internet is 'hi speed'? More like 56k speeds.
Witmer Gang is near and fortunately avoided being robbed.

name: The Hotel Wilshire, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Don't miss the roof!”
text: When I first pulled in I was met by a very friendly valet. The rooms are clean and comfortable with a contemporary feel. The mattress cover was noisy. The housekeeper was very nice. I went up to the rooftop in the morning and was surprised at the beautiful view. It was a gorgeous day in LA and I could have spent the afternoon up there. Would have loved to have seen it at night. Oh well, next time!

name: The Historic Mayfair Hotel
title: “What a dump. . .”
text:
My wife and I stayed one night at the Mayfair. . . and will never do so again.
The only positive thing I can say is that it's close to the Good Samaritan Hospital, where my sister just had a triple bypass - the reason we were there.
Where do I start?
The staff was not, in the slightest, cordial or friendly - they seemed to not care even a little - very apathetic.
Way overpriced for what you get - the rooms would have been an embarrassment to Motel 6. The headboards on the beds were attached, crookedly, to the wall. The TV wouldn't work until I re-arranged the plugs. The coffeemaker was broken - the little brew-stopper thing so you can pour a cup while it's still brewing - I had to fix that so I could make coffee. The dresser looked like something Goodwill refused to accept, the table in the room looked like it came out of somebody's break room, and the commode was one of those pre-motion detector truck stop toilets with no tank, just a valve. I didn't take a shower there, after my wife took one, and couldn't get the water temp adjusted - apparently, the cold water is almost hot enough to shower with, leaving the hot tap turned off.
They also charged us a $150 deposit for "incidentals," but wouldn't explain what they meant. 
If we hadn't been so wiped out from being on the road all day, we would have went somewhere else.
Stay Away.

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “A very quiet airport hotel!”
text:
I was able to bag a $76 rate on Priceline for this hotel. We got in to LAX at 11 PM and needed to start bright and early towards Arizona. This is a fairly old hotel with stains on the floor and outdated rooms, but it was surprisingly quiet. In the morning when we looked outside our window, we could see planes getting ready to takeoff. WE HEARD NOTHING ALL NIGHT! It was great. Cudos, also for the great shower.
The only negative part of our stay was the $22 valet parking fee. There is not a place on the entire property to park your car yourself. It is all valet.
However, even at $98 it was still a pretty good deal in my opinion and we were not disappointed.

name: The Wilshire Hotel Los Angeles
title: “Far better than the price suggests”
text:
Maybe I`m just a bit of a peasant or something but this hotel was fantastic for 3 stars.
Location is good if you have a car, and PERFECT if you are attempting LA via public transport. Apart from the run to / from LAX we saw everything (Santa Monica, Beverley Hills, Burbank, Hollywood, Long Beach, Downtown etc) via the Metro system for just $6 a day. And there is a stop right opposite the hotel on Wilshire Blvd. 
The rooms are perfectly adequate for visiting the city. If you want to spend your whole time in the room, pick the Beverley Hills Hotel, or better yet another city. Far too much to see in LA to hang around in the room! Having said that, bed was large, appointed well, and if you ask for a back facing room its quiet and has a great view of the Hollywood sign.
The car service they provide to LAX is also excellent. Same flat rate as a cab ($55) but its a brand new Lincoln limo.
Stay here when in LA (and your not a movie star)

name: Hollywood Historic Hotel
title: “Lovely staff and big room but very run down”
text: We stayed here for one night during our honeymoon before catching a flight and couldn't wait to leave. The staff were lovely and really helpful, and we were delighted when they upgraded us to a suite. Unfortunately, the room wasn't great. Although it was clean and very large, it (and the whole hotel) is in dire need of a re-fit and total upgrade. The decor is from the 70s/80s and the room stank of something - not necessarily nasty but almost as if it had been washed down with bleach too often! Points for service and trying, but we wouldn't stay here again.

name: Radisson Hotel Chatsworth
title: “Hotel sympa, ville beaucoup moins.”
text: Bon hôtel, proche comme on peu l'être à Los Angeles de Universal Studio, Hollywood, Venice. Les chambres au RdC autour de la piscine son super. Pas de restauration réellement proche de l'hotel hors mis bien sûr le resto de l'hotel qui est en revanche cher.

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Thanks for the memories”
text: I spent one night at the chic Palomar recently with my beloved for a romantic rendezvous.. Overall, it was a very good experience. The room was fab, tastefully decorated and spotlessly clean upon arrival. The check in was a breeze too and the front desk staff friendly and cheerful after our long day of travel. The bed was oh so comfy and we were eager to give it a try...We had a great time at the bar and restaurant, Sable, that was packed and staffed by expert bartenders. The only downer was housekeeping who knocked on our door as 8:00 am the next morning clearly ignoring the "dreaming" tag posted on the door knob. Not sure why she would be knocking on the day of check out so early anyhow. The managers wine reception was fun. The Palomar's locations is top notch and the local neighborhood safe into the evening. We look forward to our next visit, but this time for more than a quick getaway.

name: Radisson Midtown at USC
title: “Pet Friendly”
text:
Only reason staying here is convenience to USC campus.
So called "Executive suite"
My room was pet-ready because here was dog food leftover on the floor of my closet and resting in the closet door tracks. The iron board had dry-rotted foam beneath the cover that kept falling to the floor whenever it was opened. The hair dryer bracket was ripped off the wall.
The staff was inattentive with the front desk being unmanned for about 10 minutes in the morning (when people typically check out).

name: The Hotel Wilshire, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Excellent”
text:
I loved staying at The Hotel Wilshire! I can't say enough about how chic and impressive the decor is. The rooms are spacious, extremely clean (it's brand new) and the beds are so comfortable!
The rooftop bar was amazing and had a great view of the city. The rooftop drink menu is out of this world! I would highly recommend the Bourbon Smash!!!
The service was impeccable - the staff was friendly and accommodating. 
I will def plan on staying here again! I love everything about this place!

name: The Historic Mayfair Hotel
title: “It's not too bad at all”
text: I needed to stay a night after concert in Los Angeles so I chose this hotel after looking into so many different hotels and their reviews. It was pretty good and I was satisfied. The staffs were very polite and nice. The room was smaller than how it looks on their site but it wasn't dirty or smelly at all. What I wish was they have a better shower. It was hard to control the temperature of the water and water pressure was low. The bathtub was well... not a tub I would take a bath in. If it's for a single night, I would stay at this hotel again.

name: The Historic Mayfair Hotel
title: “Pretty Poor”
text:
I reserved at the Mayfair because it was the closest hotel with availability to the E3 Conference.
Staff was friendly and helpful, but overall the hotel is pretty shabby. Rooms are dingy. Television in the bedroom did not work. One bedside lamp had a burned out bulb, the other a broken switch – so I spent a few minutes assembling a working lamp from the two.
Internet connectivity was very slow and unreliable, bad for business travelers.
The Mayfair is servicable as a crash-pad, but not for anything else.

name: Ritz Milner Hotel
title: “Good hotel, good location”
text: The Ritz Milner is very close to several attractions in the downtown area-Orpheum, Staples Center. The staff was friendly but not overly so. Our room was very tiny- the bed was about two feet from the door and the window seemed to be facing an alley which was slightly noisy but not bad with the window shut. Our keys never worked and had to go back down stairs each time to get a new one. Not a big problem though. Parking was easy and we walked to several restaurants close by. Would stay again if i didnt plan to be in the room very much.

name: Super 8 Canoga Park
title: “Great Room, Nice People, Sucky Wireless”
text:
We stayed here Friday, June 15, 2012, Room 119. Compared to the experience we had at the BW Cypress on Katella, we were apprehensive as we drove in, kind of run-down looking on Topanga Blvd. However, the gentleman who checked us in was great. We arrived at the room and opened the door and WOW, clean, bright white sheets, bright white towels, great beds! 
We did have an issue with the wireless internet. We had three computers and only one would connect and that was only at dial up speed. 
The grounds are nicely landscaped and the pool was clean though we did not use it.
There is a Sushi place immediately next door and actually shares the same parking lot. I have to say we were up till after nine and people were lined up out the door waiting to get in. AND, they took some of the hotel parking so it was tuff finding a place when we came back from our outback experience.
All in all, we would stay here again because the value is there, we just did not like we could not get internet as we depend on it when we travel.
We did not take breakfast however I will tell you it is two cereals, plain corn flakes and frosted, plain little bagels with cream cheese, some pastery and two juices.

name: Americas Best Value Inn & Suites Granada Hills
title: “We were treated very and we'll be back”
text: We were very satisfied with the service. The establishment was very accommodating to our needs. We were pleasantly suprised by the size of the rooms-they were not small claustrophobice sze rooms like so many hotels we have stayed in for the same prize. Excellent location, just 1 block from I-5 . We have stayed at differemt America's Best Value in California and we've never been disappointed. We always look for these first before we decide on lodging whenever we travel. We always get a great deal for the money. Of course look for their promotionals to get the best price and book early if possible to get the ideal rooms.

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Fantastic stay at the Palomar Chicago!”
text: We spent three nights at the Hotel Palomar Chicago and absolutely loved it! The staff was amazing and the extras that Kimpton Hotels do for their guests are wonderful. They have a wine reception each night in the lobby and because we are Inner Circle members with Kimpton we were upgraded to a spa suite. I would recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to Chicago.

name: The Dixie Hollywood
title: “Friendly staff but dont expect too much...”
text:
All I have to say about this hotel is the staff are very friendly and the pool area is not bad. Its not a bad location being on Sunset Blvd, but not what I expected. Rooms are average to say the least. Very musty and not exactly clean. The staff are great and made me feel good about the stay but unfortunately its not a great place to stay. 
Stay in Beverly Hills or Santa Monica if you are going to LA....

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Hotel in a Great Location”
text: This was our first stay at Hotel Palomar...a choice based on Tripadvisor reviews and ratings. The prior reviews are spot on. This is a fun, conveniently located hotel that has much to offer. The front desk staff was great on check in. They explained things very well and were very welcoming. The room was clean, modern and inviting with a GREAT bed. We opted a higher floor room. Ours was on the 16th floor below, we later learned, the fitness center. We experienced quite a bit of noise from above so, in the future, would opt for a different floor. We visited the bar for a drink after shopping in the afternoon. We had a difficult time finding someone willing to wait on us. Once we got the attention of the server, however, he was quite attentive. When we visited later, the bar was full and energetic. A fun night spot. The nightly hosted wine reception was crowded, but service was fast and the wine tasty. Breakfast in the restaurant was great. We suggest joining the hotel loyalty program as it carries perk including a mini bar credit, newpaper and wifi. We have long been wedded to staying at the Sofitel when enjoying a weekend in Chicago. In the future, we will be hard pressed to pass on Hotel Palomar. The hotel is centrally located to shopping and dining. All in all a very enjoyable stay that we will surely repeat soon.

name: Quality Inn Hollywood
title: “Good Value Hotel”
text: Since I wanted to stay in Hollywood, I couldn't have picked a better hotel. Reasonable price, good breakfast, nice shower, thick towels, nice sheets and pillows and comfy bed. The room was not big but it did have 2 double beds, 2 chairs, a table plus an armoire for the TV and drawers. The hotel was very secure. The refrigerator was bigger than usual. The only negative thing is that it is not very soundproof so just bring your ear plugs.

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “WAY TO GO RADISSON LAX!!! Accomodated over 450 people for a yoga training and did it WELL!”
text:
I attended a yoga training held at this hotel for 2 months (April 2011-June 2011). We lived on-site for the entire time. By the time I left, I knew the names of all the staff and every nook and corner of that hotel. I can't say enough good things about the staff! They were wonderful and very very accomodating. The food provided at a food bar in the lobby was surprisingly good. I am not one for buffet style food, but it was actually very good and fresh. They used a lot of organic products and provided a huge array of fresh, alternative drinks like smoothies, wheatgrass, fresh squeezed juices, coconut water, and many more. Room service was great and was provided 24/7. Good for us as we were up at all hours of the night. I think may hotels would have a hard time accomdating this many people....especially this crowd, but they were super organized, prepared and ready to made changes as needed. WE also used all of their conference rooms for "lectures" and "clinics" and the mainballroom became a huge yoga practice room. Excellent facilities!
THe rooms themselves were standard fly-through hotel rooms. Decent enough, nothing really stood out. The only drawback I could find in the rooms was the ventilation in the rooms....I doubt anyone staying there a night or two would even noticed, but when you are there for 2 months and have wet laundry drying in your room (we had to wash our yoga clothes out by hand most of the time in the sink for time's sake and by choice-the hotel provided washers and dryers). Our thermastat didn't seem to work. We had maintenance check on it several times, but apparently the problem was never resolved..it just got very very stuffy and humid in the rooms. I heard that they were going to remedy that as many rooms had the same issues. 
Again, if you are thinking of staying here for a few days, even a week, this is your place. Other than the ventilation, which is not the staff's fault, it's awesome! 
Other pros:
-Car rental facility on site (separate from the Radisson and provide very very low rates)-II rented a car almost every weekend for around $36 TOTAL for one day with taxes and insurance.
-24 hour shuttle to the airport
-Separte shuttle to Manhattan Beach, which inlcudes stops at the Mall (with all your basic department stores, Whole Foods and a ton of restaurants)
-There is a Trader Joes, a regular grocery store, like Safeway, two CVSs with 24 hour pharamacy, a medical clinic for walk in injuries/sick, Bed Bath and Beyond, 2 Starbucks, Panera Bread etc.
-The local bus can get you anywhere from the stop near the hotel..I took it to Santa Monica..was a straight stop no changing of bus.
-Krispy Kreme doughnut kiosk located inside the Crowne Plaza (about a 10 minute walk down the street
-an awesome sushi kiosk located in the Crowne Plaza-some of the freshest sushi i've had and i've had a lot--it's a lone guy that prepares the sushi to order -he is only there from 5/6-10pm M-F or something along those lines.
-The pool at the Radisson is heated
-They have a bar/lounge in the lobby that servies food until 1am or something like that. I had the best burger ever there...
Again, the stafff....EVERY SINGLE PERSON, whas wonderful! They take customer service to another level. I've stayed at 5 star hotels that have not come close to this type of service. 
As a side, my husband, coincidentally stays at this hotel when traveling for business as required by his company. He is only in a night at a time.....this is one of his favorite hotels for the location and convenience. 
The only reason I am not giving it 5 stars is because of the ventilation for long term stayers.....hopefully they will remedy that soon. My husband says he has never encountered this problem there at all...so maybe it was just our floor?

name: Ritz Milner Hotel
title: “speechless”
text:
I was looking for a cheap hotel for one person (mois) Summer 2004 this hotel well catered for student budgets, I usually like big chain hotels but this was a trip I was making for personal reasons.
I agree the website has NO information on it, I had no idea if I had breakfast or if I was in a trwin/double/queen room, I relied on my agent for that. The pictures made it look great.
On arriving I got a real downtown apartment block feel, the liftshafts were old and dingy and I held my breath ascending in case it would stop. I must have been making faces when I went in as I was shocked.
The hallways are nice ENOUGH but my room was shocking (I just reminded myself of the price) Carpet was dirty, TV was on an old stand whick looked like it would fall off, lack of storage, drawer unit was stained (cheap pine) the bed had a broken spring to there was a big dip in the mattress. my warderobe was a door into a little musty room with no lighting so I dont know if I left anything behind and 2 auld wire hangers.
The batrooom had an old curtain, loose floor tiles and a smell emitting from the drains, bad toileteries trown there and stained towels I was lucky to get a bathtowel and had to make do with handtowels after a shower.
There was no minibar as stated, no hairdryer as stated and no iron. Airconditioners were loud and werent really effective for hot august weather. Coffee maker had dirty glass and a foam cup.
Now on to breakfast, I was told I had breakfast and was given a card at reception each morning and proceeded to the diner dirty, run down I was scared to eat there dust was an inch thick in the walls and grease lined everything, I was served breakfast by a dirty homeless person one morning and that took the cake!!!! I think he got an hour work to get breakfast each morning. I began to feel I was staying at a fleabag hotel.
Then I was told next morning that I wasnt entitled to breakfast anymore because my tour group stopped that deal (I wasnt with a tour grooup, I booked privately) But It was a blessing after previous experiences.
I wanted to change rooms but was told it was booked out.
Walls paper thin.
I dont think I will ever stay there again.
Looking across the road at the beautiful Hyatt regency hotel I stayed at the previous year was sickening.

name: Hotel Monaco Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Hotel Monaco Has Flair”
text: I am a frequent travler to Chicago. I was part of a larger group conference and probably had the smallest room the hotel offered. With that said, it was very comfortable. The furnishings were very nice but the bathroom was small and spartan with lmiited toiletries. I have stayed at Hotel Monacos in DC, Denver and Portland, and Chicago suffers by comparison. The building is quite old and there was only so much improvements that could be made. With that said, it is still a nice hotel and worth considering for the location and price.

name: Motel 6 Los Angeles - Hollywood
title: “R & R”
text: very good location in the heart of hollywood very clean rooms

name: Hollywood Downtowner Inn
title: “Great Location”
text:
You will love this place if you are in Hollywood to see the city. Its isnt a luxury hotel , i mean you can see that by the great price.So if you arnt a pampered poodle you will have a very nice stay. 
 The staff was so nice. We had to check out a day early because of a death in the family and they didnt give us any problems. I would recomend it to all my friends and fellow travelers.

name: Comfort Inn Near Universal Studios Hollywood
title: “Ok if you only need a place to sleep”
text: Hotel was very outdated. Pipes were leaking in the garage. The staff was less than interested that we were there. Security doors were propped open and that made us a little nervous. Neighboor is a little scarey. Bathroom faucet was hanging off of it's bracket and I asked for one extra towel and they did not have one available. Breakfast was day old food and extremely crowded and confusing. Everything was stale including the cereal. If you are looking just for a place to sleep this place is tolerable. If we were staying any longer than 16 hours I would have moved to another location. Next time we will stay elsewhere.

name: Motel 6 Los Angeles - Hollywood
title: “Pretty good value in Hollywood”
text:
We chose this motel for its combination of location and reasonable price. It's close to Hollywood Boulevard and the area with Kodak Theatre etc is not far away on foot. We didn't have a car with us, but there is parking underneath the motel for $10 per day. Our room had two beds, which was great, and we had a comfortable sleep. The toiletries provided are a bit light on - average soap and no shampoo - but if you're staying in lots of hotels like we were you probably have enough from elsewhere. 
There is a laundry off the foyer, which proved very useful. The only disappointing thing was the internet signal. It was fine in the foyer, but abysmal in our room. The room was only about three from the elevators at the street side of the floor, but we still couldn't connect without standing outside the elevators or sitting in the lobby. There is a computer room/business centre on the ground floor though, for those who don't have their own computers.
Finally, people who walked in off the street and asked for a room were charged a lot more than we were online, so beware of this if you haven't already made a booking. It's worth staying here if you can get a decent deal online and don't mind sitting in the foyer to access the internet.

name: The Historic Mayfair Hotel
title: “Très bon hotel pour les groupes”
text: Bel hôtel, un peu désuet. Pas dans le meilleur quartier, mais proche du centre d'affaire de L.A. Petit déjeuner complet. Un grand hall et son magnifique piano blanc libre d'accès. Des agents toujours à l'écoute.

name: Hotel Monaco Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Fun hotel in a great location”
text:
