We had a great stay at the Hotel Monaco. Rich, the concierge on duty when we checked in, was welcoming and very helpful, and we found the rest of the staff to be friendly and helpful as well. The room was clean and well appointed, and we loved the window seat. We were less than 10 minutes from Grant Park and the State Street Macy's (check out the ceilings there...fantastic!), and we were close to the train as well. 
We didn't try the food at the affiliated restaurant (South Water Kitchen) because there were other restaurants nearby we wanted to try. 
Overall, it was a great experience, and the next time we're in Chicago, we'll be sure to stay here.

name: The Historic Mayfair Hotel
title: “Das Mayfair war wirklich historisch”
text: Die gezeigten Fotos der Zimmer sind nicht sehr aktuell. Telefon fehlte auf dem Zimmer (nur das Kabel dafür war vorhanden), Handtücher waren auch nicht vollständig. Wenn man nach einem langen Flug ankommt, möchte man sich nicht noch um alles kümmern müssen. Rezeption war freundlich und bemüht. Das Frühstück (nicht inkl.) im hoteleigenene Restaurant war aber dann ein guter Start. Die angegebenen Gebühren für die Parkgarage hat man uns auch nicht berechnet, obwohl es im Katalog angegeben war. Für eine Nacht reicht das Hotel aus.

name: Motel 6 Los Angeles - Hollywood
title: “average hotel”
text: get what you pay for rooms have large beds staff are generally nice there is parking underground but tge breakfast is not really breakfast at all just coffee all in all fin efor what yo pat

name: Hotel Monaco Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “We'll Stay Again, But Will Be More Specific Next Time”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel Monace on June 19-20, 2009. The visit was to celebrate our 20th anniversary, although we didn't make any type of announcement to the hotel staff. Wine reception and turndown service were great touches - loved the window seat, though not the best view, and the concierge staff was most helpful.
While the stay was relaxing in all respects, there were a couple of little disappointments. First, we had requested a quiet room on a higher floor and away from the elevator. We were given a 4th floor room that was right across from the elevator -- ding, ding, ding. The first greeting we received once inside our room was barking from the dog(s) next door -- but that soon quieted down. We later found out that this pet-friendly hotel puts the patrons with pets on the 4th floor if possible. I'm not sure how a middle-aged couple without a pet ended up on the that floor; we probably should have asked for a different room, but we didn't. 
Later on Friday night (after midnight), I was awakened by two couples, obviously staying on opposite ends of the 4th floor calling down the hallway their plans for the next day - and, of course, their goodbyes for the evening! That was rude to the highest degree.
The room itself was excellent, we just would have been happier with a better location within the hotel. Without reservation, we will stay here again, but next time will make sure to follow through with making sure our room request is exactly what we want.

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Wonderful hotel, great location”
text:
The rooms are spectacular - spacious, beautifully decorated. Funky cat-themed robes and fuzzy socks. I spent two nights here on business and would only stay here the next time I'm in Chicago. There were three of us on this trip and we couldn't believe we got such a great hotel for such a great price.
We ate lunch in the restaurant which was also very good, although there are many, many other choices within walking distance. It was hard to get a table as a walk-in on that particular day, but they were happy to seat us at a high table in the bar area which was fine with us.
Overall a great stay and highly recommended.

name: Saharan Motor Hotel
title: “Great Stay - nothing was too much trouble”
text: I picked this blindly off the internet, and couldn't have been happier. The manager helped with booking cars to get all locations (drivers he booked were friendly and extremely helpful). I highly recommend this hotel to anyone wanting good value for money, location is convenient for the Hollywood walk of fame and Runyon Canyon. Thanks for a great stay

name: Azul Inn
title: “Great Location”
text:
OK ! I first booked a Kimpton hotel few blocks away from this hotel and then changed it !Anyway, I am not comparing this one to a Kimpton hotel, but overall it was a good stay.
The room is clean and updated. The free parking is a HUGE plus, cause we had two cars. The location is great. Can't be better for me. 
I just grabbed a cup of tea from the breakfast bar, but it was usual breakfast. It is interesting that somebody said he skipped it because it wasn't organic !! I am not sure even Ritz-Carlton offers organic food for free ! 
The lobby is not as clean as the room and has a strange smell. Also the front-desk had problem with communication. 
If you want to be in the area and don't want to spend a lot of money book this motel. It is not disappointing at all !

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Nice Hotel Great Location”
text: We stayed at this Kimpton property for 4 nights in late June. Our room was well appointed and the hotel's location was excellent, being close to a red line station. The roof level pool was relaxing after a hard day's sight seeing. We had breakfast in the restaurant once and could not complain. Being a Kimpton In-touch member, the free wireless internet was very useful. Overall, The Palomor lives up to the Kimpton brand.

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “Excellent value for money”
text: We went to LA for an event and since we started to look for an accommodation a bit late, there weren't any decent hotels left in downtown. That is why we chose this. When we arrived we understood that it was a really good choice: the rent-a-car offices were in the same area and we could reach any by a shuttle bus, there were plenty of parking lots in the surroundings, it took us only 20 minutes to go to the downtown even with heavy traffic of LA, the food in the restaurant was very good, the staff helpful and professional, the room spacious, comfortable and clean. So, if you don't mind to go by car, this hotel is an excellent choice.

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Thanks a million for making us feel so special!”
text:
A big thanks to Mike and the rest of the Hotel Palomar staff. We stayed three nights over the long holiday weekend and at check in they asked us why we had come to Chicago. In passing we told them about it being my Husband's birthday and our Anniversay. We headed out for the afternoon to do some shopping and upon our return we could not have been more surprized to find Champange and Strawberries with Sauce waiting for us along with a card wishing us best on both of our special events!
The hotel was clean, hip and all around a fun place to be in the heart of the city. Plus if you have not eaten at Sable yet - go just for that!

name: Saharan Motor Hotel
title: “OK hotel but great location!”
text:
Saharan is right between Hollywood & West Hollywood. Literally around the corner from hollywood boulevard. Right near Ralphs supermarket. 
Rooms are a bit shabby - powerpoints did not work. 
Perfect for anyone on a budget and want to stay close to Hollywood!!

name: Hollywood Downtowner Inn
title: “Naja - Frühstück und die Lage des Hotels ist ok...”
text:
...ist aber nur etwas für die Durchreise. Die Sauberkeit lässt zu wünschen übrig. Neben verschimmelten Essensresten im (ausgeschalteten) Kühlschrank und einer eindeutig benutzten Damenbinde in einer Schublade, haben wir im Bad den Dreck und die Seifenreste von mindestends 10 vorherigen Gästen gefunden. Der Sektkühler auf der Microwelle war voll mit Müll (u.A. Essensreste) Aber wie in einer Bewertung schon erwähnt, habe ich die Hoffnung, dass es nicht in jedem Zimmer so aussieht. Wir hatten ein sehr kleines Zimmer mit einem Bett.
Das Hotel ist in LA sehr gut gelegen. Metro ist zu fuß in 3 minuten erreicht, jedoch ist es aufgrund einer Baustelle und der Hauptstraße sehr laut und spätestens um 6:00 Uhr vorbei mit der Nachtruhe. Alles in allem ist das Hotel jedoch für die LA Erkundung super gelegen und auch das Frühstück ist super. In keinem anderen Hotel habe ich solch eine Auswahl gesehen. Von Cornflakes über Rührei, Bacon, Pancake und Früchten ist alles dabei.

name: The LA Hotel Downtown
title: “spacious rooms!”
text:
We stayed for 3 nights at the Marriott Los Angeles Downtown. We were here for a business/leisure trip. So location was perfect for us. 
The room was great. Very spacious. Very clean.
We had a kingsize bed for us and a rollaway bed for our son. 
Even with the rollaway bed we had plenty of space in the room.
The kingsize bed was extremely comfortable. I seem to sleep the best in Marriott beds for some reason. 
The staff is very friendly & helpful and pointed out some tours for us.
The restaurant is good. Fast service and good food. Breakfast buffet is good, but a bit pricey (around $20 for the buffet), but I guess these are LA prices.
I highly would recommend this hotel.

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Really great Hotel”
text:
This was my first stay at a Kimpton branded hotel and I have to admit that I am totally and fully impressed. 
Pros:
The Palomar is trendy, but not trendy to the point where any comfort is sacrificed. 
The service is fantastic and the staff is friendly. They gave us early check in and the hotel manager personally emailed me the day before my arrival asking if I needed anything special. I thought that was pretty cool.
Every night they have free wine tasting with thin crust pizza. A great touch. 
The workout facility was top notch.
The room was very clean and the carpet plush. The bed was comfortable. The bathroom was very nice with granite upscale touches you'd expect in a luxury hotel along with Kohler faucets.
Free internet for Kimpton members (free membership)
$10 worth of mini-bar credit.
Turn down service in the evening.
Subway station is around the corner (very convenient)
Cons
Not a lot of cons, but perhaps the rooms aren't enormous in size. I guess I shouldn't expect that from a downtown Chicago hotel.
No microwave or mini-fridge. Again, not many luxury hotels have these, as they expect you will be not be bringing home leftovers.

name: Millennium Biltmore Hotel Los Angeles
title: “Lovely Biltmore”
text:
We stayed four nights at this hotel. The room was fine, the bed comfortable and the bathroom clean and tidy. The aircon worked fine, the coffee maker worked fine, the tv worked fine. The staff were accommodating, friendly and helpful. Above all, the beautiful lobby and reception rooms/halls were stunning. It was all very 1930's and absolutely charming.
The windows are not double glazed, but they are old and have shutters. All in keeping with the vintage feel of the hotel. A little traffic noise, but we did not experience anything too bad and I AM a light sleeper! 
The food and service were all good. The location of the Biltmore is also a plus as it is within easy walking distance of the theatre district and many downtown locations. Convenient to Blue Bus and Metro stops.
Our experience was most enjoyable and we were sad to leave the Biltmore and Los Angeles. We would stay at the historic Biltmore again.

name: Conrad Chicago
title: “Stylish Luxury in Chicago!”
text: From the moment I pulled into the valet, I felt our two-day stay at the Conrad was going to be nothing short of excellent - and it was!!! From the luxurious yet comfy lobby to the caring staff at the front desk, you are well taken care and it truly shows. The elevators were quiet and smooth, our room was spacious with a comfortable bed with an assortment of pillows, and the bathroom was absolutely beautiful. I travel 9 months out of the year and have seen a variety of hotel amenities - Conrad's amenities are some of the best! The outside terrace is fun for cocktails and appetizers. Service in every area is tops - and the location is the best. We walked to a great Italian restaurant 2 blocks away - and you can't beat taking the elevator to the mall!! Convenience all the way! We will be back :)

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Beautiful hotel, clean and modern decor, friendly staff.”
text: The Palomar is an excellent choice if you are looking for a place to stay within walking distance to the shopping of north .Michigan Ave and vicinity. It is also located near house of blues and theaters. Beautiful hotel with new rooms and trendy decor. Great hotel!

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “Run Down and Past it's Prime.”
text:
We were very disappointed with this hotel. The Good: Very close to airport, free shuttle from LAX every 15 minutes, nice coffee shop, pool looked nice. Took a 10 minute trolley in front of hotel to the pier for $5/person. Concierge desk was extremely helpful. The Bad: Rooms were old, we were on the 11th floor, and the hallway had moldy smell. Carpet was stained in our room and completely run down in hallway. Bathroom was suspect- ragged towels, run down shower curtain, washcloths were damp!, found hairs on the floor around shower.gross. We were "up graded" to a room with a Sleep Number bed and both of us woke up sore because they were so uncomfortable. We attempted to order room service but there was no menu. We had to call room service twice before a menu was brought up to our room. When menu arrived it was empty so I gave up and just called to get a menu over the phone. We assumed the business room computers would be free (we needed to print boarding passes), but found out you have to pay about $8.00 for 15 minutes and one dollar per print. Ridiculous. 
We will not be returning.

name: Hollywood Downtowner Inn
title: “Great for the price”
text: Exactly what I thought it would be. A funky west hollywood motel experience. down the street from some great hollywood landmarks and just minutes away from Universal studios. Rooms were clean and staff was friendly. Some great Thai restaraunts within walking distance as well as some great characters along the street. Area not for everyone, Eclectic is a word I would describe it.

name: Hotel Monaco Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great stay at Hotel Monaco”
text:
We booked one night at Hotel Monaco Chicago - and a large snowstorm threatened our travel, so we decided to stay another night. What a time! The staff was friendly, helpful and genuine. The room was funky and cozy. Great decor! We loved the window seats where we watched people and traffic hustling by. Free Wifi was a plus. Location was exceptional for the variety of touristy things that we wanted to visit.
We really liked the goldfish we requested. Maybe a little silly, but it was fun to have a pet to "come home" to.
We loved the wine hour and the Starbuck's coffee in the morning. The snowstorm made for a chilly touring day, and it was nice to come back to a warm, cozy room.
We will stay here again and highly recommend you give Hotel Monaco a try!

name: Motel 6 Los Angeles - Hollywood
title: “Can't beat the location”
text:
First of all, you have to understand that this location cannot be beat. It's on Whitley, which is less than a half-block from Hollywood Boulevard. This is a famous street -- the Hollywood Walk of Fame is here, in addition to Kodak Theater and Mann's Chinese Theater. There is a lot of foot traffic on Hollywood Boulevard, locals as well as tourists, so it's great for people-watching. You can walk to restaurants and bars as well as stores like American Apparel, American Eagle Outfitters, two vintage clothing stores and souvenir shops. Mel's Drive In is literally right around the corner.
I actually just got back from my stay. I went with my sister and her son. Getting past the location, which was excellent, the motel itself wasn't exactly wonderful. It looks good from the outside -- it's in a pretty nice area of Hollywood -- but it's a Motel 6. There are stains on the carpet in the hall and the elevator takes forever to arrive. But, the room was clean and adequate for our needs.
For $10 a day you can park underground, and the attendant (wearing a white button-down shirt and vest) will bring you a wheeled luggage carrier.
Best of all, they allow pets, which was my No. 1 priority. AND it's inexpensive. With the one night of lodging, pet fee ($10) and parking fee, it was $90. And you should know that's a steal in this area.
If you're looking for a place to rest your head for a night or a weekend, I recommend Motel 6 Hollywood. If you're coming to LA and plan to spend a lot of time in the room on some kind of extended getaway, I'd look elsewhere. 
Honestly, this is a good place to stay in the heart of Hollywood.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel San Pedro
title: “Friendly staff, great deal for San Pedro cruise passengers”
text: Chose this hotel in order to take advantage of their package that allows you to park your car for free if you stay the night before your cruise departs from the San Pedro cruise terminal. (And it includes free shuttle to and from the cruise terminal.) First impressions: staff at bell desk and front desk are very nice. Pleasant, friendly, competent, professional. Also, the marina location is very picturesque and should make you feel like you're on vacation even if you're not. Other impressions: some things are a little rough around the edges. Carpet in the hallways looks like it's due for replacement; holes in the dust ruffle on the bed; bottom of the bath tub appeared to be permanently stained a queasy shade of grey; wallpaper under the window has seen better days; and most irritating complaint is the self-closing doors on the guest rooms slam shut very loudly -- maybe when your own door slams shut you don't really care, but when the doors on seven other rooms slam shut after you've gone to bed, you DO care. But the stuff that matters most was fine, including a clean room; good bed, sheets and pillows; ample hot water and all-around an efficiently run hotel. Had dinner and breakfast at the restaurant. The food was better at breakfast than it was at dinner, but service was better at dinner than it was at breakfast. In both cases, the servers were friendly, including the bar tender. (And the bar area is a comfortable place for solo travelers -- including those of us women who don't always feel at ease going to the bar alone). Bottom line: it's a DoubleTree! And the cookies are great!!

name: Holiday Inn Express - Los Angeles Downtown West
title: “The only place I got bug bite”
text:
in general this place is ok as the price is quite reasonable based on the location. however this is the first time I travelled to LA and I immediately got bug bite in this motel. the bed sheet wasn't very clean and the closet feels smelly as well. unforturenately we left all clothes we bought in outlet in the closet and we found bugs when we tried on them back home. we spent whole weekend and try all we can to kill the bugs. 
we wrote the Intercontinental group to raise this issue but the hotel insist their rooms are very clean after a "bug inspection" by outside company. 
anyway, just a friendly remind to those who are going to stay in this place, be careful!

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “Convenient Place to Stay”
text: We stayed here for one night prior to a cruise. The shuttle service was convenient. We enjoyed taking the trolley ($3 round trip) to see some of the local sights. Too bad we didn't have more time, or we would have liked to get off at more of the stops. The room was clean and served it's purpose for the night (although it could use a little TLC). The staff was friendly and helpful, especially one of the housekeeping staff. We were about to board the cruise ship when I realized that I had forgotten my jacket in the room. I called the hotel once we got on the ship and the wonderful employee gave me his e-mail to contact him. We e-mailed back and forth a couple of times during the week, and arranged for my jacket to be put on the airport shuttle so I didn't have to return back to the hotel. It was truely superb customer service!

name: The LA Hotel Downtown
title: “nice place”
text: we stayed there for 3 nights while on a Cosmos tour. The room was big, clean and the pillows to die for. The lobby had iced water available all day - very welcome as the heat was about 110 d in the city. Only complaint -NO teabags and for Aussies that was a no no. However a call to housekeeping provided enough to keep us going until we could find a market. We ate from the bar menu - plenty enough for two of us.

name: Ramada Limited Canoga Park/Warner Center
title: “family reunion”
text: We all met up here for a family reunion because the rates are affordable for a very large group of people!! the rooms are very roomy and clean. The rooms have large beds and a beautiful pool. The continential breakfast is wonderful and it helped alot. Thank you Ramada for a wonderful stay!!

name: Holiday Inn Los Angeles International Airport
title: “close to airport for stopover.”
text:
used this hotel for stopover from Vancouver to Melbourne. Close to airport a free short shuttle ride away. Hotel was very nice and staff at front desk extremely polite and helpful. Room was clean with 2 large QS beds good size too, a bathroom with all requirements but bath needed a bit of repair to enamel worn off due to water damage. Great pillow choice also, 2 soft/2 firm
each. Has basic amenities ie toothbrush etc if you forget yours complimentary too. Great pool outside also.
Ate in their restaurant and had a great selection. Mcdonalds was right next door and petrol station was next to that if you require any other basic items. Otherwise nothing else around area. Just a suggestion....Tours will collect you from hotel if pre booked. We did La city sights day trip to fill in time 8.30 to 4.00 return. Ready to catch shuttle back to airport.

name: Ramada Limited Canoga Park/Warner Center
title: “FORGET ABOUT THIS PLACE”
text: From the moment you check in there is certainly a sense of insecurity throughout this property. The so called " manager" (who apparently is there day and night) treats everybody like if he is doing them a favor. Not only theyy would argue with you but they are even fisty. Too many issues to describe during a two day stay so no use.Cancel your reservation if you have one, you will save a pityful experience .Hopefully Ramada officials take note of what guests are saying here.

name: Sheraton Los Angeles Downtown Hotel
title: “Excellent hotel”
text: I visited here in 2009, the hotel had just been done up and when we walked in we got a shock as the pictures on the internet did not match the hotel we were in. it was very modern and everything looked brand new. The bed at this hotel was massive and very comfy. the hotel was very well situated as it is right at universal, walking distance. we used the down town area at night as it had alot of nice restaurants round about and nice shops etc. I would recommend this hotel and i would defiantly go back if i was going to LA again.

name: Travelodge Hollywood-Vermont/Sunset
title: “Basic and decent botel outside the centre of LA”
text:
Summary: A decent, relatively cheap, and basic place to stay in LA.
Location: In the Hollywood area, about 10 minutes (drive) from the Kodak Theatre, 15 minutes from the Griffiths Observatory and Universal Studios. We had a car so found it easy to get around, there are buses nearby, but cannkt comment on good / easy they are to use. The hotel is next to two hospitals so you can get ambulance noise, but it's not too bad. There are a couple of fast-food joints nearby which are walkable.
Room: A decent size, with enough space for us and two suitcases. There is also a small fridge and a coffee maker. The bathroom is also a decent size. Note, there was no lift so we had to take our suitcases up the stairs... please bear this in mind when booking this motel.
Cleanliness: Room and bathroom was nice and clean. The corridor / walkways are outdoor are a bit worn but fine, and still clean.
Breakfast: There is a basic breakfast of fruits and cereal available at reception. Hot drinks available too.
Internet: Free wireless is available... the connection is reliable and speedy. We used it for Skyping and uploading pictures and it worked fine.

name: Sheraton Los Angeles Downtown Hotel
title: “Not the best in Downtown”
text: Stayed on a work realated traing, so did not pay myself. This hotel is great if you are their for work realated issues, but not for vacation or leasure. It is not in good area of downtown. The rooms are fine, good veiws of city etc.

name: The LA Hotel Downtown
title: “Marriott just OK...needs updates.”
text:
Overall, Staff very friendly except we wanted to go to West Hollywood and the Bellman called a friend "Pablos Limousine" - he took us there at a reasonable rate and we cabbed back to hotel later. However, we called and made an appointment with them again on Sunday round trip and one minute before we were to be picked up, he texted me to say he would not be able to pick us up. No explanation, no notice...just a I'm sorry!! BAD BUSINESS!! Luckily, another bellman at the hotel called a service and they were very reliable and punctual for full round trip. I reccomend "Andres Limousine" for you sedan needs.
Back to the Hhotel, the TV's are from the 80's and need to be updated to flat screen, bar needs to be open longer (especially when there is 12,000 conventioners in town), furnishings are old but decent, need a fridge in rooms or honor bar, room service needs to be 24hrs, and elevators need replacing (only 2 worked during visit). 
Staff all were friendly but will stay at the JW Marriott on next visit as it is in the Staples Center with lots of things top do around it.

name: Sportsmen's Lodge Hotel
title: “Good simple lodging”
text:
I stayed here after reviewing the competition and checking out the reviews on this very site.
I noticed the manager responded to those who did not have an optimum experience, which was, to me, a good sign.
I arrived at the hotel, everything is pretty clean, solid, and as advertised. definitely no dive.
I was a little dismayed on hearing about the 10 dollar parking fee (this place is full of parking spots), and I had neglected to notice that breakfast wasn't included.. as it usually is in South America as a matter of course in most any hotel. 
I had parking fees waived as it was low season, so everything was pretty good.
except when I wanted to use the advertised (on in room tv) fitness room. No longer open, they offer a discount at a nearby fitness place. I walked by and it didn't seem worth more than the 5 dollars it cost, so I skipped it and ran up the nearby hills.
aside from that, good room, everything else worked, 
worthwhile place.

name: Travelodge Hollywood-Vermont/Sunset
title: “Dont bother”
text: Stayed here one night because we left booking till the last minute ( on the travellers must never do list) it was a weekend so busy everywhere . Room was a tight fit for the 3 of us. I was the lucky one that got locked in the bathroom 30 minutes later !!! it was as poor effort .. no apology from the hotel what so ever I know you get what you pay for but its right next door to hospital so all nihgt were sirens and helicopters landing at the hospital > it was clean though ??

name: Motel 6 Los Angeles - Hollywood
title: “A 150 M HOLLYWOOD BVD”
text:
TRES BIEN SITUE TRES PRES HOLLYWOOD BVD
A 2 MIN A PIED DU KODAK THEATRE
A 25 MIN EN VOITURE DE L AEROPORT.
BON MOTEL DE CHAINE.
PAR CONTRE PARKING 10 DOLLARS / NUIT
POUR LA SITUATION / PRIX :PARFAIT
2 PC AVEC INTERNET ET CAFE A L ACCUEIL.

name: BEST WESTERN Hollywood Plaza Inn
title: “Location is great, rooms are comfortable, service has room for improvement”
text:
We stayed there for 3 nights at the beginning of october, did not book in advance and were lucky to get a free room at 2pm in the afternoon. You should not arrive later, you might not find a room available. I recommend to book a room in advance if you stay more than 1 night. 
positive aspects
- directly on Highland Ave, only 5-10 min walk to Hollywood Blvd, very convenient if you like to go to Madame Tussauds, Walk of Fame, Hard Rock Cafe, Hollywood Museum, Chinese Theatre and many souvenir shops
- free parking, many parking spots
- close to metro station Hollywood/Highland, close to Universal Studios and Hollywood bowl
- rooms are clean, big, beds are comfortable 
- because of noise in the room service personell offered to switch rooms for free (we were offered a room with jacuzzi)
- because of the trouble we were offered a private shuttle to the airport for a special price; when the car came it was a black strech limousine - awesome!!
negative aspects
- DO NOT stay in room 343, the water heater is above it and is extremely loud at night
- shuttle to airport is $15 per Person
- breakfast is not included in hotel room

name: Sportsmen's Lodge Hotel
title: “Good value for the price”
text:
We stayed at the Sportsmen's Lodge to be closer to friends who live in the Valley. It definitely saved us money, but it's not the best location if you're not planning to go to Universal Studios or that sort of thing. However, there's not really one great place to stay in LA since you have to drive virtually everywhere. 
The rooms were clean, the bed was comfortable, and the staff was friendly despite being overrun by 3 British school groups who were stranded in the US due to the volcanic eruption. My only complaint is that we booked the business suite specifically to have free wireless internet access, but even after multiple phone conversations with their technical support, it never worked. Overall, I think it's a good value for the price and perfect for families since it's not exactly romantic or hip.

name: Travelodge Hollywood-Vermont/Sunset
title: “Simple hotel, great staff!!”
text:
This hotel is perfect if you visiting the city for a couple of days. The Travelodge is an ok hotel so don't expect 3 star quality. We arrived at 10 in the morning and normally hotels make a big deal out of early check ins, not this hotel. The front desk man is really friendly and we had to wait for 30 minutes to get our room. He offered us to have breakfast first and gaves us some information about city tours and theme parks. 30 minutes later we got our room. 
The room were we stayed had 2 separate bedrooms and a bathroom. We had a microwave and a refrigerator. Everything is simple, good enough to stay for a few nights. The breakfast is simple as well. There is some toast, fruit, cereal, pastries and coffee and juice. There is free wifi internet so perfect to keep family and friends posted on your adventures.
The location is great. Near the hotel is the subway entrance and you can take several bus lines. Perfect location!!
Overall it is a simple hotel and the staff is really friendly.

name: Hollywood City Inn
title: “Great hotel ! Great Staff !”
text: My husband and I stayed 7 nights at this hotel . We found it at TripAdvisor and was a wonderful experience: The service : very good .. all team : always helpful , the hotel location is fantastic ! Was a pleasure for us to stay in a so confortable place with so nice people.

name: Travelodge Hollywood-Vermont/Sunset
title: “Convenient Location”
text: This motel can be considered as one of the better motels. It is very conveniently located, close to LA's main attractions, and close to the metro and freeway. We really enjoyed our stay here. The staff was friendly, the rates were good, and it was pretty clean and safe.

name: Motel 6 Los Angeles - Hollywood
title: “Buona posizione!”
text:
Il Motel 6 di Hollywood è un classico motel americano, stanze ampie, semplici e pulite.
La posizione è molto buona, si trova in una strada che incrocia la Hollywood Blvd, quindi nel cuore di Hollywood!
E' ottimo per turisti che cercano una soluzione economica ma comoda e pulita.

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “Committed To Customer Satisfaction”
text: My husband & I stayed there prior to going on a cruise ship leaving from San Pedro. I chose this hotel because it offered free shuttle service to & from the airport. Great feature. Having never been to Los Angeles, I asked the hotel Concierge, by the name of Tim, to direct me in the easiest & most economical way to get to the port. Tim was exceptionally friendly & helpful & informed me that there was no shuttle or bus service, that a taxi would cost me $150 & that I was better to take the "Limo/Car' service offered through the hotel for $120, but would give me a deal at $99. As that appeared to be the way to go, I booked the car service to not only take us to the port, but to pick us up when we returned from our cruise as we were staying another night at the Radisson before returning to Canada. Throughout the cruise as we talked with other passengers, we learned that there is indeed a shuttle service from hotels to San Pedro & that the taxis advertise $53 from LAX airport to the port. I was extremely upset over this & felt I had been taken advantage of by the concierge. Due to a delay in the ship clearing customs, we did take a taxi back to the Radisson & it only cost us $57!! To cut a long story short, both Tim & the car service apologised for the misleading information I was given & did not charge me for our initial ride to the port for our cruise. We did hire the car service & a driver for a 3 hour sightseeing tour of LA. This was very expensive at $65 an hour & of course had there been more people to share the vehicle the expense would have been less. But we really enjoyed having a personal tour guide. The rooms in the hotel were large & beds very comfortable. So all in all, I would certainly recommend the hotel & the car service. I have learned through the experience to now check out prices & availability of transportation for a new city, using the internet.

name: Sportsmen's Lodge Hotel
title: “Don't Stay Here If You Plan On Using The Shuttle To Universal Studios”
text:
The bed was quite comfortable considering I'm used to sleeping on a Tempurpedic mattress. The remote wasn't bolted to the nightstand which was also nice. The sliding glass door leading to the balcony had sheer curtains as well as black-out curtains. The first light source when entering the room was very near the door (not in the middle of the room like some hotels I've stayed at). The room came with an iron, ironing board, hair dryer, coffee pot, coffee and tea bags, ice bucket and liner, 6 shirt hangers and 6 pant hangers, suitcase holder, an extra blanket, a desk, two chairs, a vanity outside the bathroom (no chair), and a mini-fridge. 
The switch for the lamps on the nighstands were on the lamps themselves (I've stayed in hotels where I had to get out of bed to turn off the nightstand lamp), There was a recycling container for paper, cans, and bottles (nice touch!). There is a card for breakfast service that you hang on the doorknob. There is a "do-not-disturb" sign you can hang on the doorknob (Yes - I have actually stayed somewhere that did not have "do-not-disturb signs!). There is a back entrance that you can access with your room key (which is near the elevator and much closer to the parking lot). 
The wi-fi service is an additional $10 for 24 hours. The bathroom did not have a fan or a window. There was a vent over the shower but it did not have a motor. There were only two large bath towels (I'm used to four). There was only one bar of soap (instead of one for the sink and one for the shower). My biggest complaint, however, is regarding the shuttle service to Universal Studios. The current driver is consistently late leaving the hotel for the park and leaves the park early when bringing guests back to the hotel. The driver is required to write down a return time from the park (there are only 3 to choose from) for each guest he brings to the park. I chose 5 PM. I arrived at the pickup spot at 4:50. I waited until 5:15 to call the hotel because the driver never showed and I was told that he had already completed his 5 PM pickup. Then I was put on hold while they "tracked him down" but he couldn't be found. The hotel took my number and said they would call me back as soon as they found the driver. I decided to just take a cab. I was already back at the hotel by the time the front desk called me back. The shuttle service was the main requirement when I was researching hotels, so for this to be the subject of my biggest complaint is very disappointing. Like the title of my review states, don't stay here if you plan on using the shuttle to Universal Studios. 
Note: My reservation confirmation stated that parking was $10 per night. I was not charged parking for my stay, but I do not know if it was because it was comped due to the shuttle service incident, so if I were you I would call the hotel directly.
I would only recommend this hotel to a friend if I could also warn them of the shuttle service, wi-fi fee, and lack of a bathroom window/vent.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel San Pedro
title: “Glad I didn't pay full price”
text: I'm typing this from the hotel as I think it's worthy of a below average review. Checked in last night to a smelly, small, obviously smoked in room, overlooking the dumpster area. It's a room that should be converted to something other than a place where people are expected to stay. Running the HVAC system only made it smell worse. I requested another room and was told the hotel was "pretty full".... so I waited. Finally they found me another room, which was more acceptable but average. The pool is in an awkward area next to the road, the HVAC system is much more complicated than it has to be (the instructions on the wall say "You will find instructions to the Heating/Cooling Unit inside the Guest Directory on your desk. Please call the Front Desk should you require further assistance." Why so difficult??) The room wasn't as clean as I expected, with fingerprints & smears on the mirrors, hairs on the bed, etc. On a plus side, they've made some nice improvements with the last renovation. It was refreshing to finally see a hotel honor the "hang your towels up if you don't need them washed to save water" theory... unfortunately there was no place to hang them up. Why no towel hooks? Maybe I'm getting picky in my old age...

name: Super 8 Los Angeles Airport/LAX
title: “Tipico motel americano”
text:
Motel su 2 piani e vicino all'aeroporto, pulito con colazione internazionale a buffet.
Stanze spaziose e pulite arredate in tipico stile americano.
Nonostante la posizione vicino all'aeroporto, le stanze sono silenziose di notte.
E' in una posizione comoda x raggiungere tutte le attrazioni di LA visto che se siete in vacanza ad L.A. significa che avete sicuramente noleggiato un auto; nei dintorni ci sono supermarket, distributori di benzina, fast food e quantaltro.

name: Hotel Monaco Chicago - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Must ask for larger room”
text:
Their website gives the impression that they have two, and only two, types of rooms: regular and suite. The rooms actually come in a wide variety of shapes and sizes. When checking in, we didn’t make any specific request, so we got a narrow room with a bed that was too big for it, and no view to boot. Lesson learned -- specifically ask for a big room, and a river view, or at least a view out on to Wabash Avenue.
Also, definitely take them up on their offer of a free pass at the gym down the street, the exercise “room” is more like a closet. And the curb in front of the hotel gets crowded, so dropping off luggage can be an adventure. The bellhops do their best, but someone directing traffic would be better.

name: Motel 6 Los Angeles - Hollywood
title: “Zentrale Lage ist von Vorteil”
text: Für eine Nacht durchaus in Ordnung, zentrale Lage lässt einiges zu Fuss erreichen. Wird gerade renoviert. Zimmer ok, Sauberkeit ok, allerdings nichts für den gehobenen Anspruch. Für eine oder zwei Nächte durchaus auch für den erhöhten Preis, das ist nur die Lage, zu buchen!

name: Super 8 Los Angeles Airport/LAX
title: “Exactly what I expected and a little more”
text:
Free shuttle from LAX was great and once I worked out were the pickup was the Driver arrived.
Friendly staff checked me in and even though the planes overhead were loud and annoying to begin with I slept like a baby till morning. Big TV, clean bathroom and comfy bed.
In the morning I used the free taxi phone to call a taxi which came within minutes!

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “Convenient Location”
text: We stayed here just as a layover. Got there late at night, hotel was very busy. Valet parking guy was rude cause we weren't paying for valet, we were just dropping off our luggage so we could return car to rental company but he had a problem with that. Reception desk was nice. Rooms need to be updated. One of the walls was almost falling apart. Yet the room was clean and offered a comfortable night stay. I would not recommend for staying more than a night. Their aiport shuttle service is very good.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Los Angeles Downtown
title: “Great stay downtown”
text:
Came to downtown LA for the FYF Fest. Wanted to be walking distance to the festival and this was it. 
The room was newly decorated and spacious.
The staff was helpful and friendly at both check in and check out.
There was some noise outside, but this is a metropolitan city with real city noises outside, deal.
Would happily return if in the area again.

name: Sportsmen's Lodge Hotel
title: “This is a quintessential southern california classic!”
text: Very comfortable, great service, we have stayed hear numerous times!

name: Sportsmen's Lodge Hotel
title: “Accommodating!”
text:
Although my reserved room was not acceptable (too musty and run down) the staff was extremely accommodating and relocated me to another room overlooking the pool and gardens. I did have to pay an additional $10/night in order to get this upgrade, however, since the base cost was very affordable this was fine with me. 
The Patio Cafe was good and the location was excellent.

name: Villa Brasil Motel
title: “Little but worthwhile”
text:
I found this place on the internet by trying to find an inexpensive hotel in LA, Culver City area. This place was great.We stayed 6 nights.Not much around it, but that's fine. I'm an early riser so every morning I'd get up and read outside where there are tables and chairs outside every room under a canopy of blooming flowers. So peaceful. The people were helpful whenever asked and had no problems with us coming late. The bed was comfortable, there was a coffee maker, microwave and little fridge. Very convenient. I also loved the shower. It had amazing water pressure and felt wonderful. 
Would definitely stay again.

name: Hollywood Hotel
title: “Bad Service, not worth the money”
text: My family stayed there while I was in the hospital for a few days. The service staff were terrible! The rooms were overpriced, and mediocre. The neighborhood is edgy, and it's name does not do it justice. Not recommended

name: BEST WESTERN Hollywood Plaza Inn
title: “should have learned in Redondo Beach”
text: We should have learned from the last Best Western but I guess you get what you pay for. This room had mold growing around the ceilings I doubt it was even safe to sleep in Thank goodness it was only for 1 night. I can definitly say we will NEVER stay there again

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Los Angeles Downtown
title: “OK room, so-so service.”
text:
At check-in they tried to assign me a regular room even though my reservation was for a "deluxe". 
The breakfast buffet was $18+, so I ordered off of the menu, big mistake. Rubbery over-easy eggs, never saw waiter again...no water, no refill of my drink, no one checked to see if everything was ok, they were simply too busy cleaning up to wait on customers.
I even left a note about the lack of service on my guest check, yet never heard from anyone. I ate all other meals off-property due to their lack of concern.
Keycard had to be replaced/reprogrammed more than once. I eventually ended up carrying 2 keycards with me to save me from any more trips to the front desk.
Location is convenient, downtown is becoming quite popular again.
I never saw the free shuttle van, and when I asked how to get to the train station, I was told that I could walk, no mention of a shuttle at all. Nice walk, although hot. None of the street people bothered me.
I had to call security at 3 in the morning due to a several suites full of drunken sorority girls running amuck.

name: BEST WESTERN Burbank Airport Inn
title: “Clean Newer Hotel... However you might wanna read my comments”
text: This hotel is relatively new and the room I was in was clean and updated. However, the morning breakfast (which was supposed to start at 0600-9000 hrs - rarely began at 0600) was never open at 6:00 a.m. when I needed to leave the hotel. It would open at 6:12-6:15 daily-I stuck around one morning to see how long it would take the maid to open it up; I complained about this nothing was done to correct the issue. If you need high speed Internet, this isn't the place for you; my speed-test on several occasions was less than 1 mbps, often came in for downloads at .78 mbps (slightly faster than dial-up). Also, the hotel is not really close to anything; it is in a mostly commercial/industrial area away from major shopping/dining areas. Oh, and if you happen to get this place on Priceline.com get ready for a room facing a very noisy and busy major thoroughfare (these are the ONLY rooms available for Priceline guests). I attempted to change rooms the first night but was told that I would have to contact Priceline.com and pay an additional fee to get a quieter room. Just as few objective observations about my stay.

name: Comfort Inn Near Hollywood Walk of Fame
title: “Absolutely acceptable standard, I'd stay again if I want to be right in Hollywood”
text:
Stayed 7 nights in Room 106 on first trip to USA and LA, delighted to find that staying here put is within 1-2 walking blocks of all the action at Hollywood and Santa Monica Blvds, and right on Sunset. Its only 3-4 blocks to Melrose and maybe 10 blocks West Hollywood and Sunset Strip. whatever the actual distance was we walked to and fro comfortably. But you can't beat being only 2 blocks away from the haert of hollywood Blvd. Right next door to the left of the motel is Starbucks, then El Pollo Loco, Wendys, Burger King. Supermarket is a couple of blocks down Sunset with many smaller shops on the way there, most stocking alcohol. Next door to the right is In/Out burger, across the road is IHOP. So all the fast foodies abound. 
Our studio room was cosy: great king sized bed, comfy smallish but OK pillows, great shower (which easily fits more than 2 people :) in. Wifis (there are 3) were initially confusing but once sorted worked fine. Didn't use TV. Air con was noisy but necessary to keep it cool. Pool available but didn't use it. Street noise acceptable considering the business of Sunset Blvd. 
The male Indian manager Anisur was very obliging and talkative and friendly, the Mexican maintenance man looked after us very well too. It was so easy to come and go from by foot. The breaky is fine - have lots and save eating during the day. Great espresso is avaible at bespoke cafes in both directions. There's a fantastic Brasillian restaurant nearby, maybe one block past Sunset and La Brea corner. Great little laundrette across that same intersection - ask for Oscar and he'll look after you very well. If you start Hollywood Blvd from the La Brea end you start the Walk of Fame with Elvis and the Beatles so its handy. There is no need to spend more on rooms that this place charges, unless you want something special or higher-end. We knew we were taking a calculated risk with it being so cheap but it was perfectly functional, clean, with every-day people and great prices so we were and still are happy.

name: O Hotel
title: “No more than a night or two”
text: An average experience with the O Hotel. The King room was small, with a tiny bathroom that got pretty wet with every shower. Room on the 3rd floor looked directly into a tree but a city view room would probably just look across the road from where the hotel was sited on. Only the comfortable bed redeemed what would have been a gloomy stay. Reviews were right when they say lighting is an issue. Corridors were dim, and so were the rooms.

name: Cadillac Hotel
title: “An Old Classic, But Not for Everyone”
text:
This is one of the oldest hotels in LA, and was where many movie stars looking for a beach vacation back in the 1920s stayed. Obviously Venice has changed a lot since then. The scene on the beach outside the hotel can get pretty wild, but that is part of the Venice ambience of today.To me the biggest problem is that the stores underneath the hotel have open fronts and blare loud music all day, so if you're in a room at that end of the hotel you are not going to get much peace. And these are the rooms that have the best ocean and sunset view, so if not for the beach crowds and especially the music, these would be the best rooms in the house.
The issue of noise also applies to several small hotel properties along the promenade. So if you really want to stay along this part of Venice Beach I'd say to stil go for The Cadillac, because no other place has this kind of history.And maybe if you're out all day the noise won't be an issue.
My other caveat is that the hotel has gone through a room updating since the last time I stayed there. It used to be good value to be right on the beach, but I'm not sure if that's still true. If the rates have shut up it might be worth considering one of the more upscale beach front hotels slightly to the north, in the Ocean Park area of Santa Monica.

name: Travelodge Hotel at LAX
title: “"does what it says on the can"”
text: Stayed 1 night after late night flight. shuttle perfect. check in efficient. room clean but extremely dated and dowdy - however wouldn't be a deal breaker in choosing again. Quiet even so close to LAX. Breakfast was one of the very best we had on our trip. Would be hard to fault if only given a serious upgrade.

name: Beverly Laurel Motor Hotel
title: “Clean, Good Location, but no extras”
text: We chose the Beverly Laurel for its location and that worked out very well for the three of us. We were able to walk from our hotel to the museum and to other neighborhoods that we wanted to vist. The hotel was clean and the beds were comfortable, but there were no extras in the room to make us feel more welcomed or taken care of . No coffee pot for tea or coffee in the room, no little hand lotion or conditioner. No complimentary breakfast and no coffee or computer in the lobby. The price was good and I would stay there again if I wanted to be in that location, but I would have realistic expectations.

name: Hollywood City Inn
title: “le quartier n'est pas génial”
text:
l'hôtel est correct, le lit un peu mou, le petit déjeuner n'est pas terrible.
il est juste bien situé pour aller voir hollywood boulevard et le cinéma chinese theater. quand même à 20 minutes à pied.
à part ça il n'y a rien d'autre à voir dans le coin qui est mal fréquenté le soir.
attention aux parkings dans la ville, il vaut mieux choisir un parcmètre plutôt que les parkings payants assez chers.

name: Travelodge Hotel at LAX
title: “Overnight Stay”
text: Booked one night stay after arriving from UK via Zurich. Pick-up and shuttle return was good. Hotel very near LAX and the freeway, but we had no trouble with noise. Check-in and out quick and competent. Had booked direct with the motel. Small shop on site with usual supplies.Room large and clean, A/c not too noisy for sleeping. Swimming pool available, but did not use. Good Dennys restaurant on site. Continental breakfast was above average, clean and with a good selection of cereals, yoghurt, bagels, toast, muffins and fruit. Excellent airport hotel for the price.

name: Rodeway Inn Convention Center
title: “Close to the Staples Center:)”
text: I need to share my experience as downtown LA can be a stress in itself trying to go to a Lakers game:) I went on Spring Break with my 15 year old son to a Lakers game. The Good Lord blessed us as we walked into Motel after Motel finding that we could not afford the big fancy Motels downtown. We wandered into the Rodeway Inn to be greeted by a sweet young lady at the desk named Nancy. She made us feel at home and gave us a fantastic price for a room so close to the Staples Center. This Motel was clean and felt like home. It is not a large Motel but small and comfortable. They have a nice outdoor pool, parking for free, breakfast, and internet access to my computer. We were so tired we woke up late to eat the next morning and to our pleasure Azab Uddin the manager told us to come in anyways and he would let us eat a late breakfast. You will not find a nicer group of people. Thankyou again Nancy and Azab for being so kind to us Montana folks who were lost in the shuffle. God Bless.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Los Angeles Downtown
title: “Unexpected Quality in downtown LA”
text:
The good: The hotel itself is a very nice hotel, fabulous lobby and wonderful staff at the front desk and valet. The bartenders and happy hour were also nice and reasonable. I was impressed with the size of the room (2 Queen) and the beds were super comfortable! The hotel is also located in an area easily accessed by the freeway. And, surprisingly the fitness center was not half bad. After spending numerous trips depressed over the sad state of hotel fitness rooms this one was decent. Plenty of room, decent machines and a TV etc. 
The bad: The room was a little "beat up" - paint chipping, chips off of the furniture etc. It also got a little noisy with the helicopters from LAPD (landing pad is a few blocks away) but I am also a light sleeper. I thought the shower had a super low head and low water pressure. Back to the fitness room: they need new cardio equipment and new free weights - granted they worked they just need an updating. 
The Ugly: The service at the restaurant for breakfast. ugh! Seriously, there were at least two waiters on both my visits and a minimal amount of people in the resturant however, the service was horrible. We would sit around waiting and waiting and waiting just to place our order. Then wait around forever to be noticed to get the check. As a former waitress myself I dont get it - maybe the waiters were pulling double duty and cooking some eggs in the back as well.

name: Comfort Inn Near Hollywood Walk of Fame
title: “Excellent value for the location and dollar.”
text:
After reading some of the other reviews of this property I suggest that if you want a 4-5 star hotel, stay at a 4-5 star hotel. When I booked this hotel I was looking for a good value close to the "Walk of Fame" and other Hollywood locations at an affordable price and that is exactly what I got. Yes, it is an older "motel", yes the neighborhood is a little sketchy but we felt safe. 
The front desk staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome, did a great job of explaining breakfast times and items, and quickly sent up extra towels when requested. It is obvious the management is doing everything it can to make the faciliity clean, fresh, and updating things they can update. Our room had been painted within the last 1-2 years, and had carpet that was clean and updated in the last 1-2 years. 
The price was exceptional for the area, and we walked from the hotel, to Hollywood Blvd, and back without any issues at all.
All-in-all, if you are looking for value in close proximity to the Kodak Theater, the Jimmy Kimmel Show, Mel's Diner, the Chinese Theatre, and other Hollywood tourist staples, this is an excellent value.

name: Hollywood Hotel
title: “Miles from anywhere, rude staff and noisy”
text:
I'll start with the good points. There aren't many. 
+Our room was lovely. 314. It had two large beds, a flat screen TV, HUGE shower as well as a fridge and mircowave.
+ It was clean.
OK, now for the bad. 
- First of all when we arrived, we were told that there was a $100 security deposit. After double/triple checking our reservation details, NOWHERE did it say that this was the case. I've also been advised that a security deposit shouldn't amount to more than one night's stay... which this was. However, front desk wouldn't budge. We found the manner of the people there incredibly patronising and often overbearing. So we handed over the last of our money (cue frantic call to the parents in the UK in the middle of the night) and headed to our room. 
- We weren't offered any help with our bags. For a hotel which purports to be high class this is a bit of a let down,
- The area is VERY dodgy. We had a beautiful view of a run down store and drunks patrolling the street chucking cans of beer around. I wouldn't walk around there at night. The noise from the road was horrendous, be it police sirens or fights breaking out. I also feel that the hotel misrepresented exactly where they were- we phoned beforehand and were told that they were close to Hollywood Blvd. Well. They are. Pity that it's at the very end and about $40/$50 in a cab to get to the decent part. (I say "decent" loosely. Let's go with touristy instead)
- There was construction work going on throughout our stay at the hotel with some rooms being refurbished. We were not notified of this upon check-in and it was disturbing, to say the least. 
- Front desk. Oh my word. Where to begin? It should be enough to say that every time we went there some poor soul was complaining or upset. We had our own fair share of problems and were met with impatience and condescension at every turn. 
We called from our room as the outside line wasn't working. My sister asked politely how to remedy this. She was hung up on. I called back and explained that she had been hung up on and merely wanted to know how to access the outside line. There was NO apology and an abrupt direction to press such-and-such, which we had already tried.Before I could point this out the lady slammed the phone down and refused to pick up again. We simply had to use our mobiles instead.
Another instance was when I asked at reception what the best way to Venice Beach was. The man behind the desk slapped some documents onto the desk, told me to "go right and get the bus" and then proceeded to yell at someone over his shoulder. I asked for some clarification (as there were a few buses and stops) but he didn't seem to hear me and went off into the back. 
- There is a pool and sauna, yes. What they don't explain is that you need to reserve a space in the sauna, go to reception and pick up a seperate key. You're also not allowed to use the facilities on the day of check out. I went for an early morning dip and was barred entry. I asked why this was so, but apparently my money was only good enough the night before. Nice. 
Overall I would certainly NOT recommend this hotel. Our room was lovely, but after seeing another guest's I could see we were merely lucky on that front. It's not worth the hassle and rudeness. I had a much better experience at less expensive establishments.
TIP: If you're nearing the end of your funds then there's a cracking supermarket up the road, Jons, where you can pick up some cheap eats. All of the noticeboards are in Spanish but the staff there were only too happy to help.

name: Comfort Inn Near Hollywood Walk of Fame
title: “Good location but with problems.”
text:
This hotel is on Sunset Bvld but it's actually very close to the Walk of Fame. The metro is 7-10 minute walk which is where the Walk of Fame is also. The room I was in was spacious with a fridge but no microwave. There is a communal microwave in the lounge/lobby. Also the method to access the TV is very strange/different. 
There are homeless people around but it didn't bother me as they just mind their own business and you will also see them on the metro. The breakfast area is tiny and has the usual assortment of items. 
Lots of restaurants and shops around so finding a place to eat shouldn't be a problem. It can be noisy so if you're a light sleeper it might be a problem. No free computer to use but there is an pricey Internet cafe around the corner.

name: Cadillac Hotel
title: “Worth paying more elsewhere”
text:
I had stayed at the Cadillac several years before, and heard that they had renovated since our last stay. I couldn't really see the improvement on the queen room we stayed in. There were stains on the carpets, the window didn't work properly, and the bathroom wasn't very nice. 
Also, I have to echo the comments I have read by others on TA - the area just isn't that nice. In summer/peak season I'm sure it isn't as bad, but in November it was deserted on weekdays except for loud homeless people who heckled you occasionally when you walked past. It didn't bother us too much since we're used to cities, but at night the area was quite seedy and felt quite unsafe, and we wished we had paid more and stayed somewhere else! Also, it was noisy at night (from other guests in the hotel, and the street outside).
The staff were very friendly and helpful.

name: Cadillac Hotel
title: “It's a nice hotel. It's Venice Beach!”
text:
It is right on the beach! They have free Starbucks coffee. The rooms are really nice with ceiling fans and the bathrooms are clean and new.
It was a very pleasant stay.

name: Beverly Laurel Motor Hotel
title: “Absolutely "NOT" worth the price...”
text:
I chose this hotel because of all the positive reviews I read on internet and on "Lonely Planet". But I was sooo disappointed :
1. First there was indeed a smell. You know the same smell when you walk into a store selling vintage clothes. It's difficult to live in it. The smell was on the beds, on the towels, everywhere.
2. OK, the rate was $90 a night, but quality only worth $40. The wooden drawers were dirty and old. There were cracks here and there filled with dust and dirt. Towel racks were old with dots of paint, looked like they were covered with dirt. I had to use the towels on it and it gross me out.
3. Dirty dirty dirty. I'm serious, there was blood stain on pillow case, and the pillow itself was yellowish!
We stayed for a night and we quickly moved out. We ended up at the "Days Inn" at Glendale which cost me only $75 per night, and believe me, Days Inn was way way better!!! I don't know, if you are always "on the road", always prepared to sleep at train stations, OK with not taking shower in days, then I think Laurel Hotel is good for you. But if you are a "normal" person who likes cleanliness, then don't ever think of going in there because it is not in hotel standard (not even motel standard compared to DAys Inn).

name: Conrad Chicago
title: “Warmth in Wintry Chicago”
text: New, pleasant and clean - great location with direct access to Michigan Ave and shopping.

name: Palomar Chicago, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Top Notch !”
text:
I am a fan of the Kimpton Properties. They are a top notch company. Their staff is experienced, cordial and helpful. Their hotels are meticulously clean and the bedding, unfortunately, makes you want to sleep in on vacation! The hotel is steps to the metro and 1 block to the bus.
I would recommend this hotel highly.

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “Recommend the Raddisson LAX”
text: This is a very good hotel, despite the fact that it is only 3 star. Also dont be fooled by the dull brown facade. Its really beautiful inside. We had a room on the top floor. The decor was impeccable, with a king sized bed and huge television. We had a fantastic view of the runway, great for plane spotting and totally soundproof. The only downside was the restaurant was a little pricey so we did not eat there, and the pool was very noisy from the planes flying overhead, but exciting! The standard of Radissions in general is never disappointing. They also provide a courtesy bus to the airport (you can walk there!) and to the beach. Well located.

name: Hollywood Hotel
title: “Underwhelmed”
text: Not very clean. Good value for LA I suppose but would spend more money next time. Well-located for studio tour - not far from Burbank. Really noisy room - stayed two nights and first night nobody slept! No heat in room - had to cart out an oil-heater from the closet and plug it in (hard to find a plug) and leave it on all night. Very awkward. Poorly-designed/appointed room with mini fridge with microwave on top of it just plugged in and left almost in middle of a blank wall. Horrible to look at - mould in bathroom, dirty carpet. Photo of hotel misleading - not front door but entrance from parking lot!

name: Sheraton Los Angeles Downtown Hotel
title: “Avoid the jr Suites!”
text:
The hotel is average but avoid the Jr Suites! A quiet sitting room adjoins the bedroom and the bedroom wraps the elevator shaft! In general he rooms are "standard" but a bit drab/dated. The dark interior lobby(s)...there are multi levels...are connected by escalators. The meeting rooms are in the sub subterranean levels which translates to no cell/internet service in the lowest level meeting room. When the escalators aren't working..oh well!
The hotel located as part of the Macy's shopping center has lots of food courts and the hotel has an upscale dinner restaurant and a nice breakfast area.
Bottom line is that it is an OK place to stay if downtown LA is where you want to be.

name: Beverly Laurel Motor Hotel
title: “Affordable room with excellent service!”
text: My stay at the Beverly Laurel Motor Hotel was a pleasurable experience and I would definitely consider it for any future LA lodging needs. Upon arriving to the hotel my wife and I found that the underground parking lot was a bit too small. (I drive a mid-sized Oldsmobile and I had a hell of time getting around the lot.) But I guess that's to be expected for LA parking. Parking was free though and it was a just a minor inconvenience. When we checked in, the front desk agent on duty was extremely polite and very helpful. When we entered our room, it was clean, spacious, and the decor was fun. The room included a microwave and fridge and I hear for a few extra bucks you can get a kitchenette. We tried to take a nap on a Saturday afternoon but it was a bit too noisy. The hotel was quiet at night though and we got a good night's sleep. There seemed to be a slight moldy odor in the room, but it wasn't that noticeable. They may want to consider an ozone machine (a popular device used by innkeepers that wipe out any and all kinds of odors) Everything about this place though was swank, totally 1950's. Staying here was what I always thought LA motor motels would be like, from the contemporary decor in the room to the soda machine that looked like it was from 1953. Plus, Swingers cafe attached to the building is a great place for all American diner food. Actually, even better than your average diner. With an extensive menu that included anything from bacon and eggs to hummus and pita, to ostrich burgers. I mean come on, ostrich burgers! At check-out the front desk staff again was very polite and very friendly. A very pleasant surprise considering that city's reputation for rude struggling actors working as waiters and bartenders. Room rate was $84.00 for Saturday and Sunday night.

name: Holiday Inn Los Angeles International Airport
title: “Great Stop Over”
text: We stayed at the Holiday Inn Apr 14, for an early morning flight the next day. I found the place to be quite nice. The rooms were large and everything was fresh and clean. The resturant was great and they even have snacks at happy hour. I would stay here again if I were flying out of LAX, but you wouldn't pick this location for anything else, of coarse.We needed the shuttle bus for 3:30 am and he was right there ready to take us.

name: Millennium Biltmore Hotel Los Angeles
title: “You're better off at a motel 6”
text:
I stayed here for two nights for a work convention. The nice thing about this hotel was the common area. The decor is very nice and to be honest that's what probably attracts visitors to this area. Their bar is also very nice (but very expensive $18 a drink) and customer service was the best at the bar. There was a nice older gentleman assisting us at the bar and he was great! The rest of the staff could take a tip in customer service and work on acknowledging and greeting their customers with a smile. The worst part about this hotel is that people EXPECT a tip, as if what they are doing was going out of their way when actually it's their job. I tip anyway, but their faces seem to beg for a tip.
The actual hallways to the rooms were like a scene from "The Shining." Everything was old and looked like it needed some updating. The room itself consisted of one bed, which was very uncomfortable, and one antique armoire which held the T.V. and one nightstand, which was a pain for us given only one person had access to the light. The old fashioned shutters, while gave a nice effect to the room, required dusting and it looked like they had been painted over their dust. There was no mini-fridge in the room so keeping your own refrigerated snacks was not an option. Additionally, the room was very cold and the heat took forever to kick in, while some other colleagues reported theirs not working as well as trouble with flickering lights. The windows themselves have not been replaced so that would explain the noise levels coming from outside and difficulty keeping the room warm. There were no extra blankets provided in the rooms on hand as other hotels would provide. Now, their site says that all rooms are equipped with 1) flat screen t.v.s (false, our room had a boxed older t.v.) 2) mp3 docking station (false, just a telephone) and 3) wi-fi for a fee (No connectivity to the internet in our room, plus the rate would be $10 PER appliance). Additionally, we had to manually turn off the lamps individually, no wall switch to control them which is kind of a pain. The walls were so thin you could hear the elevator bell ringing and people talking as they walked up and down the hallways. 
The bathroom was the worst hotel bathroom I have seen in a long time. I think hospital bathrooms are nicer. It really looked like they tried to make the interior nice by decorating with a "nice" mirror but really, they didn't try hard enough. The paint was awful, the water pressure while I didn't mind it was like you were standing under Niagara Falls, the sink slightly draped over the the bathtub, and one of the mirrors in the bathroom was just plain tacky. They really should have put a mirror in the bedroom because it was difficult for two people to share the mirror in the bathroom. The toilet was old and really needed replacing, no counter space what-so-ever, the bathroom fan looked like it needed replacing, and you could see the outline on the ceiling of an access door. 
The board rooms where the conferences were held varied from appearance. Of course the Crystal room was nice, spacious with it's balcony seating above. Other rooms however, were UN-AIRCONDITIONED which was awful as the AC was not working. It felt like we were in a sauna since there were so many people in there and we were not allowed to keep the doors open secondary to safety regulations. I was wondering what the hotel staff would have done if someone passed out due to a heat stroke. 
Their on line site is sketchy. There are no details on where to park. I wonder if that is because valet is $40 a night. And the rooms pictured on their site look NOTHING like the room I stayed in. At the rate of $189 (which was the convention fee price) plus $26 in occupancy fees, I definitely felt better off sleeping at motel 6. If in the area, try the Kyoto Grand. That hotel is A LOT nicer and worth your buck. There are other historical hotels that are able to maintain their historical theme without sacrificing comfort in a MODERN way
Overall, my experience with the hotel was poor. They get one star for the decor of their common areas and nothing more. I will not be visiting the Biltmore Hotel in L.A. ever again.

name: O Hotel
title: “NOT a scary downtown place”
text: I needed an overnight place to stay near Staple Center as I was going to a concert there. While it IS in walking distance, I wouldn't recommend it at night. As a single female I was very concerned about finding a hotel that I'd feel safe in. I felt VERY safe. The staff at the O was SO friendly. They all cheered, "Have fun at the concert" when I left. Since I just needed a place to sleep, as long as the rooms were clean, I was happy and they were. Clean, funky, and QUIET. I had a view of a wall, but who cares...I was there and then left. IHOP is right across the street and Subway is next door. There may not be any amenities but there is always something going on around the hotel. This is not a resort so don't stay if you're expecting more than a nice, safe, clean spot to rest your head and then go out and party somewhere else.

name: Conrad Chicago
title: “Faultless Fantastic”
text:
I echo what has been said before and what will probably be said again after this review.
The staff were amazing even down to the handyman/plumber with his bucket and plunger we met in the lift. He wished us a good day and I felt it was genuine.
The hotels rated ahead of this one must go good because this was outstanding in every sense of the word and great value for money.
All I can say is come see for yourself, you won't be disappointed.

name: Hollywood City Inn
title: “Buen servicio también en español..”
text: Hotel que en apenas a 100 metros de parada del metro que te deja en la puerta del teatro kodak. Personal de habla hispana que te ayuda con el tema del idioma. En apenas 5 minutos subes al observatorio Grifi y en 15 a las letras de Hollywood. Muchos huéspedes en el hotel que le hacen estar trotado, pero dispones de parking gratuito, desayuno de cortesía y buen servicio de limpieza.

name: Conrad Chicago
title: “I cannot say enough GOOD things”
text:
This is the first Conrad I have stayed at and now am unsure if I can stay at less in the future. This hotel was immaculately clean, stylishly decorated, and attentively staffed. If you're looking for a hotel in the Mag Mile area of Chicago, I highly recommend you try the Conrad Chicago.
It always annoys me when properties change their attitude when they realize I'm a Diamond HHonors member as they should treat all guests with respect. This property had a great attitude even prior to check in when they realized my HHonors status. I cannot say enough good things about the staff at this property. 
The rooms were very spacious. I was upgraded to a corner king room. The room was a good size with VERY comfortable bedding. In addition to having the standard two drinking glasses set out by the ice bucket, they provided two tall glasses, two wine glasses, and a wine bottle opener. 
The bathroom was extremely large. It had a granite tub and a separate shower. The bathroom was stocked with quality bath products and a robe for use while at the property. A toilet was located in a separate water closet. 
A pleasant surprise was the free internet for all guests (not just Gold and Diamond HHonors members). It's been a while since I've seen a full service or luxury brand offer free internet as a benefit to guests. It seems that the more you pay for a hotel, the more their internet usually costs.
This hotel was great. I suggest you give it a try next time you're in Chicago. I'm going to try the Conrad Miami next month.

name: Hollywood City Inn
title: “UN SITIO GENIAL”
text:
Nos encanto el hotel por varias cosas: su ubicacion, cerca de la parada del metro y de paradas de autobusea, la zona, bastante tranquila, aunque tampoco salimos mucho por la noche, las habitaciones correctas y limpias, bastante grandes. El dueño, Paco, es un sol, super amable y simpatico y te da toda la informacion que quieras. El desayuno nos encantó: los mejores donuts que he probado nunca¡¡¡ Muy agradable desayunar junto a su piscina. 
Lo recomendaria para familias y grupos de amigos.

name: Comfort Inn Near Hollywood Walk of Fame
title: “Perfectly acceptable, nothing special”
text: A good value hotel (especially given free parking) in a central location. We enjoyed the treat of waffles and cakes for breakfast on the first day but something a bit lighter would have been nice after that! Also very little space for breakfast so often had to stand or perch on the edge of someone else's table. Other than that, no complaints.

name: Holiday Inn Los Angeles International Airport
title: “Functional”
text:
The title sums it up. 2 or 3 out of 5.
It's handy to the airport and other things if you have transport and, like the rest of LA, not handy to anywhere if you don't. The area itself is pretty dubious. The rooms are clean and tidy and everything worked, although they are showing a fair amount of wear. Road noise is surprisingly high and, at times, invasive.
The staff were variable - some were good, some were bad, most were fine so long as you were very exact about what you wanted.
I'd stay there again if there was nothing better on offer for the price (and arrange better transport next time!) and needed to be in the same area, but otherwise I'd try the Quality Inn next door first - it is quieter, newer and lower priced. That or one of the other half dozen hotels littering that stretch of road.

name: Beverly Laurel Motor Hotel
title: “Hotel in ottima posizione, se capita ci ritornerò molto volentieri”
text:
Una via di mezzo tra un hotel e un motel.
Personale cordiale, piscina piccolina ma comoda. 
In generale sicuramente un ottimo rapporto qualità prezzo.
Buonissima posizione, vicino a tutto (ristoranti, centro commerciale) e anche alla fermata dell'autobus! Zona molto tranquilla e ben frequentata.
Camere pulite e grandi.
Contro: parcheggio e wireless a pagamento. 
Nella struttura non ci sono ristoranti, anche se ce n'è uno attaccato alla struttura che però sconsiglio.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Los Angeles Downtown
title: “Kyoto trapped in Downtown”
text:
Downtown LA, mmm, yet if you have to Stay in Downtown Kyoto tries hard and is OK. Downtown is and can be a sad refelection of what LA really has to offer. Chose Kyoto Hotel for a 1 night stop pver and dint want to stay near airport. Having been to LA several times yet never Downtown. Caught Flyaway bus from LAX to union station and hotel shuttle promptly picked us up from Union Station. Front Desk staff were helpful and freindly, Maria suggested options for dinner and gave us directions for various venues near by. 
Room and furniture was in good condition and clean, yet styled in outdated browns colors, very 70ish.
We walked ( during the day ) from Kyoto to Staples cntre and back via theatres. ( Drop in to Disney Theatre and join a tour).
Area around hotel is sad ( so much of Downtown is) Homeless are around and after dark Hotel shutlle was happy to drop/ pick up within short distances.
If you need to stay Down town for a reasonable price for a reasonable room then Kyoto is OK. If not dont stay Downtown..sorry LA , Downtown is just sad. LA I will be back Downtown not .

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “Terrific value, airport hotel”
text:
The area around LAX would not be my first choice for a location when visiting Los Angeles as a tourist but this was close to where I needed to be.
