This was my second stay here and both times I bid Priceline, for a 3* at LAX, the most recent $55 per night plus taxes. The Radisson is the closest hotel to LAX although there are many other options in the area that are almost as convenient. They run a free shuttle to/from the airport.
The check in process was quick and pleasant, the only service glitch was the alarm clock that went off at 4 am.
The room was spacious and clean, the beds reasonably comfortable and the rooms appeared to be updated since our 2005 visit with warmer colors and updated bathrooms with granite and marble. I requested two double beds ahead of time and they accomodated my request. There was a TV with a very limited number of stations including HBO, iron and ironing board. No in-room safe or refrigerator. I believe there was also wireless internet.
The bathroom shower was fine although it took a bit of work to get the hot water on, toiletries included shampoo, conditioner, lotion and soap. There was a hair dryer and coffee maker in the bathroom.
There was an outdoor pool and a small health club that was located outside the building that had treadmills, a stationary bike, ski machine and some weight equipment. There are a couple of bars, a casual restaurant and a nicer restaurant.
Parking, as with most of the LAX hotels, is an extra $13 per day with in and out privileges.

name: Vagabond Inn San Pedro
title: “Pros and Cons”
text:
We ended up here because we were looking at the last minute, and most other hotels were booked up. I don't think it was a mistake that the Doubletree and the Holiday Inn were full before the Vagabond!
Check-in went fine. We had a back room on the 3rd floor. We started to get worried when someone rode the elevator with us and cautioned us that the hotel wasn't safe, especially in the back.
The people in the room next to us were, shall we say, party animals. Not only did they scream, yell and play music through the night, but their friends drove by and honked their horns loudly several times in the wee hours. 
This is not the hotel's fault, but I noticed that at the front desk there is much video footage flashing on, showing goings-on around the hotel. I didn't want to call the front desk because I had a kid trying to sleep in my room, but it is a small hotel and I'm sure they heard the late-night revelry as well as we did. So I am perturbed that they did nothing -- absolutely nothing -- about it. And the room doors slam LOUDLY unless you purposely close them quietly -- which, I assure you, our neighbors did not.
The neighborhood itself felt unsafe, and nothing could convince us to stay at this hotel again. It was clean, I'll say that for it, and only $75. But the next night we moved to the Double Tree. Need I say more?

name: Sportsmen's Lodge Hotel
title: “Gutes und bezahlbares Hotel in L.A.”
text:
Im übersichtlichen und verhältnismäßig ruhigen Studio City direkt am Ventura Boulevard gelegen, ist die Sportsmen Lodge der ideale Ausgangspunkt für Ausflüge und Unternehmungen in Los Angeles. Supermarkt, Cafés und Restaurants sind ganz in der nähe. 
Das Hotel selber ist ebenfalls übersichtlich, gemütlich und hat einen mondänen Hollywoodstil. Vom Ventura Boulevard bekommt man in den Zimmern nichts mit. Die Zimmer selber sind recht groß, die Einrichtung ist absolut in Ordnung und es gibt keine auffälligen Abnutzungserscheinungen im Zimmer. Auch das Bad war sauber, was uns besonders wichtig ist. Glücklich kann sich der schätzen, der ein Zimmer mit Balkon zum Pool hat. Von den Balkonen auf der Rückseite schaut man leider nur auf den Parkplatz. Das man den Parkplatz anders als noch vor einem Jahr bezahlen muss ist allerdings ärgerlich, denn es stehen mehr als genug Plätze zur Verfügung. Zudem muss man an den PCs im Hotel für die Internetnutzung bezahlen. Wer ein internetfähiges Gerät dabei hat kann allerdings das kostenlose W-LAN nutzn.
Wir waren jetzt das zweite Jahr in Folge für 6 Nächte in der Sportsmen Lodge und würden sicher auch ein weiteres Mal dort bleiben.
Als Tipp: Für das Hotel gibt es immer wieder gute Angebote, bei denen man z.B. 4 für 3 Nächte bekommt.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “Convenience at a good price”
text:
I have stayed here about 6 trips now. LMU is just up the street and it is very close to the airport. Very reasonable cost relative to the Sheraton and the Westin just down the street. The hotel is very clean and easy to get around. Restaurant is easy for breakfast and the kids have liked dinner there in the past. The fridge in the room is a plus.
The elevators are a bit bouncy which can startle you the first time you take them. On the most recent visit there was a banquet in the facility and the parking was a challenge but other than that, a normal easy visit.

name: Airtel Plaza Hotel and Conference Center
title: “Disappointed”
text: We purchased this hotel though a "name your price" offer and maybe that was our mistake as we were not able to ask for ammenities like a free breakfast and parking. When we arrived at 4;00 pm we were told that a room with a king-size bed was not available and were given a small room with a queen-size bed. It had a couch, a desk, the bed and not much else. The hotel is fairly large with a 3-story building and a 5-story building. I believe that we were not given a room to our asking because we received a nice discounted price. The hotel is next to a small airport but we were not bothered by the planes taking off and landing. Upon arrival were were told that there was no free breakfast offered and that they charged $10.00 for parking. Later in the evening I realized that I had forgotten my razor and when to the Front Desk to see if I could get a disposable. They do not offer any "forgotten" toiletries like razors, toothbrushes, toothpaste, etc, that we have received at much lower rated hotels for free. I bought a disposable in the gift shp for $2.00. We will not stay here again.

name: San Pedro Inn and Suites Hotel
title: “great, but noisy”
text: beautifully remodeled rooms, comfortable beds, air conditioning not working when we first checked in, but fixed immediately, breakfast an added plus, THe only downfall was the traffic noises that increased about 5:30 am. Bring earplugs. Close to the pier.

name: Hilton Checkers Hotel - Los Angeles
title: “Pleasantly Surprised”
text:
I stayed here for one night with two other friends. We had planned a night on the town, starting with dinner followed by bar hopping and ending with our night at Exchange LA. 
When we arrived, the hotel seemed to be dwafed in comparison to the surrounding hotels. The hotel exterior felt somewhat dated, leading us to think that our room may be direct excerpt from Grandma's house; however, upon entering the lobby, all prejudice was proved to be wrong. We were pleasantly surprised, the entire interior of the hotel felt nicely refreshed; starting from the lobby, stemming to the elevators, hallways and rooms.
Check in was swift and excellent. Special thanks to Jessica for going above and beyond our expectations as guests. When making the reservation, I did make extra requests for a nice room that was both quiet and with a view; the staff accomadated these requests! The room was a great size and nicely appointed - the in-room coffee maker was an added plus. The hotel is also located within walking distance to a number of bars for those of you looking for some drinks. There were also a number of restaurants in the area. We ate at Bottega Louie which is a ~10 minute walk and definitely recommend it if you have the chance.
Overall, our stay was fantastic. while being brief, I definitely look forward to returning sometime in the future. I would recommend this hotel to everyone looking to stay in the Downtown Los Angeles area.
PROS:
- Exceptional PM Staff (Specifically, Jessica, at the Front Desk. She made us feel welcome and was both friendly and codial. Thank you!)
- Has a both elegant and contemporary feel.
- Hotel is nicely upkept: very, very clean.
- Cool room keys. No need to insert it, simply tap it against the door lock.
CONS:
- Parking $~45.00/night Valet ONLY**
- WiFi Charge $9.99/day
- Bottled Fiji Water & Potato Chips Package in your room is $35.00! Careful!
**To remedy the expensive valet, you may want to opt for parking provided by the nearby lots. We parked at Pershing Square Parking garage - overnight parking was $16.00.

name: Courtyard Los Angeles Century City / Beverly Hills
title: “Great stay near UCLA”
text: We have stayed several times at this hotel with excellent service. Even when the lobby was a mess, they made every effort to keep guests happy. The new lobby is great, rooms comfortable, quiet despite being on Olympic, and the bell/valet staff is very friendly and accommodating. Close to Westfield mall and a great Gelson's grocery store.We stay here every time we visit our son at UCLA.

name: Hilton Checkers Hotel - Los Angeles
title: “Checkers used to be luxury- now its average at best. The service makes the difference.”
text: The employees seem like they are bothered to interact with customers. Departure from the Wyndahm days. Rooms are clean, hot water tanks need to be replaced. Seems like in maintenance mode only. Such a gorgeous location with history; and it is just being run by employees who are not proud.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Carlyle Inn
title: “Fine for short stop”
text:
We stayed here travelling up coast - only had one night in LA and this was fine for what we were wanting. Being our first time in LA had heard scare stories about staying in hotels in terribel areas so we chose this due to the fact that it was in Beverly Hills.
Location is excellent, Ivy restaurant is just along the road from here. Staff were also very helpful. They sorted out all trips we wanted to make on arrival and kept out bags and let us use car park until up till 6pm, well after checkout.
Hotel was quite basic but clean and fine for a bed for the night which is what we were after. Free breakfast rolls in the morning which was good.
Would stay here again if ever back in LA

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Carlyle Inn
title: “Great staff”
text:
We arrived in LA on the hottest day they've had since records began (113F before the thermometer broke), but the air conditioning worked a treat. 
Had requested a room close to our friends, but told when booking in it was not possible and to come back the next morning. Was told next morning we would be moving rooms, but we had booked a sightseeing tour and the hotel staff moved all our luggage even the items we had forgotten to pack!!
A PC linked to a printer was located in the lobby which we used to print our boarding tickets for our flight home to the UK. At LA airport we were able to check-in quickly. Free coffee and cookies were always available.
The rooms were modern and clean with plenty of thick white fluffy towels. Parking was available at a daily rate of $11. No swimming pool but there is a hot tub and thick matresses on the sun loungers.
We used the blue and orange line buses to go to the Farmers Market and the Berverley Shopping Center. We caught the Orange 220 bus from the Beverly Centre and it stopped outside the Hotel. Heavy traffic on Robertson Blvd which we overlooked but was not intrusive and did not keep us awake.
Good selectio of hot and cold breakfast - pity about the plastic cuttlery. 
The only downside - not many restaurants within walking distance, but there is a very good Thai restaurant on the corner of Robertson Blvd and Olympic - around 300 yards.

name: Comfort Inn Near Old Town Pasadena - Eagle Rock
title: “Good Hotel, Great Location!”
text: Very nice hotel, located right in Pasadena. This was a conveinent stopping point for me. The rooms were clean, breakfast was great and staff was friendly. I would definitely stay here again!

name: Conrad Chicago
title: “Nice!”
text: Comfy beds, well appointed rooms, par for the course for the Conrad. Breakfast was delicious! Valet or self park in the lot right accross the street and walk to everything!

name: Comfort Inn Near Old Town Pasadena - Eagle Rock
title: “Still a 2 Star Hotel”
text: No matter what people say, it is still a 2 star hotel and it feels like that. Noise is a major factor, from the road, rooms overhead, staircase and rolling suitcases on the upstairs walkway all sound like a herd of elephants going by. The rooms are dingy with outdated furniture and linens. The towels are paper thin as are the sheets and there were holes in the sheets. The breakfast area was too crowded and not enough tables for people to sit at The place made me wrinkle my nose every time we walked in the room.

name: Airtel Plaza Hotel and Conference Center
title: “Surprisingly good hotel and value will make us come back”
text: This a really good hotel. Their staff was welcoming and cheery from the every moment we were there even til when we checked out. We had requested a double room as we were with our kids and it was a nice surprise to have a room with two queen sized beds (most of where we stayed was double beds, makes it tight). We were there to visit family over Thanksgiving and also do some sightseeing. It was the perfect location as we visited family nearby and then we also went to Universal and Hollywood. We had food leftover for Thanksgiving and though our room did not have a fridge and microwave, when we asked if they had any, the staff was quick to send one up. This was a nice upgrade from a Best Western type hotel where we typically stay at and definitely safer as we were able to park our car in a secured parking lot near our room. We will definitely come back to this unique boutique hotel when we visit our family. Thank you for the free internet - made the kids happy.

name: Crowne Plaza Los Angeles International Airport Hotel
title: “Friendly staff”
text:
Stopped here overnight before setting off on a marathon drive around the western USA. The check in staff were very helpful and friendly, dealing with three very tired Brits with good humour and efficiency. the bed was very comfortable, the air conditioning kept it at a very equable temperature. We had a meal in the restaurant, our waiter was friendly and the food well prepared and fairly rapid in appearing on the table. I would recommend this hotel, parking is a little expensive , but it always is in the city.
The only thing I would complain about is the charge for Wifi. I know that a lot of hotels do charge , but I think that it comes across as penny pinching by the hotel and the rates they charge for the service seem excessive in most cases.

name: The Standard Downtown LA
title: “Stay here every time in LA”
text: love the vibe...staff is awesome...restaurant is great for breakfast and dinner. rooftop is sick!

name: Airtel Plaza Hotel and Conference Center
title: “Solid satisfying stay, would stay again, no”
text: I was attending a conference at another hotel (marriott) but I found that the Airtel had better rates as well as more raves than complaints (are Priceline always unhappy, so I sorta ignored them) so I booked it independently. It proved to be a great choice from the time of arrival to departure. The front desk agent noticed that it happened to be my bday that day, so he upgraded me to a suite, which totally caught me by surprise. The front desk agents were extremely cordial and helpful and even took me to the local CVS since I needed a battery for my camera. Had a great supper at their restaurant. They had complimentary coffee at lobby which I needed to catch my early 7am flight to LAX. Really good hotel, I was satisfied.

name: Hollywood Hotel
title: “Ideal”
text:
I arrived here with doubts about how I would be received having read other reviews on this hotel.
Many of them could not be more wrong.
This is not a luxury hotel BUT it is clean and comfortable and the staff (despite other posts) were friendly and helpful. I booked this hotel for a long weekend in LA. It's near the metro which takes you anywhere you want at a ridiculously low price and it is excellent value for money.

name: Sheraton Los Angeles Downtown Hotel
title: “Pulito, belle stanze, peccato per la posizione...”
text:
Anche noi, in coppia, l'abbiamo trovato un po' scomodo per la posizione...la sera è isolato rispetto al resto del mondo! Ma può essere anche un bene, visto il caos di L.A ;)
Per fortuna avevamo la macchina (il parcheggio in effetti è caro!).
Internet carissimo, se confrontato ad altri alberghi americani...ma quello che ci interessava l'abbiamo trovato: pulizia (sopratutto per bagno!), stanze nuove e confortevoli, personale gentile.

name: Crowne Plaza Los Angeles International Airport Hotel
title: “Mixed thoughts but would stay again”
text: I thought I would try this hotel as I love hotels with views over the runway. This hotel didn't dissapoint in that regard - got a room high up looking over the southern runways so was very happy the hotel helped out with the request. The room itself and the facilities were good for the price. Didn't try the breakfast or the facilities downstairs so can't rate those. The parking was confusing. The TV was new but the signal kept cutting out on particular stations for some reason - I hope the renovations were not causing it. We also requested a late checkout to return to our room to see that they locked us out, so we had to go all the way back to sort it out. I plan to stay again but hope those little issues don't repeat themselves and they were just a one off.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “Great choice of hotel at LAX”
text:
After researching the LAX hotels we decided on the Sheraton based on past reviews, closeness to airport, and the rate included a breakfast.
The room was spacious, clean, quiet and the beds were really comfortable. The staff were friendly and attentive.
Breakfast was amazing, and set us up for the day!!
Only small downside was we had a 25 minute wait for the shuttle at the airport to get to the hotel. We would choose this hotel again to stay at.

name: Comfort Inn Near Old Town Pasadena - Eagle Rock
title: “Enjoyed our stay”
text: The staff was friendly and very helpful. The room was clean and pleasant. The location was excellent, close to where we were going, restaurants were near enough. And the scenery of the nearby foothills was beautiful.

name: Hollywood Hotel
title: “Comfortable Hotel, Nice service, Closed Subway, Good Price”
text: 3 nights in this hotel. Sincerely, I am happy. Everything was good. Ask a room on the patio: very quiet. I recommend also because the Subway red line is very closed: direct to Hollywood in 10 minutes, and also Universal in 15 minutes. it is great. the welcome is good, swimming pool pleasant, they like foreigners, and they propose airport shuttle service.

name: Millennium Biltmore Hotel Los Angeles
title: “COULD NOT HAVE BEEN HAPPIER!”
text:
My husabdn and I stayed at this hotel in August 2009. I have found some reveiws on this hotel to be unbeliable as we could not fault this hotel, it's location or staff. It is grand, beautiful and spacious. The resturant downstairs is fantastic, I had the best meal of my life in it and can not wait to go back. 
We were so impressed with our stay that I have booked this hotel again for this October.

name: Millennium Biltmore Hotel Los Angeles
title: “Nice Hotel But Watch for Hidden Costs”
text: This is a very nice historic hotel in downtown Los Angeles. My complaint is the hidden charges that are not mentioned prior to booking and make this a very expensive hotel. Parking is $40 a night and Internet connection is $10 per day, per computer (so if you are staying with someone who also uses a computer everyone pays $10.) Parking garages in downtown LA charge appx $75 per week, which, if I had known the cost of parking at the hotel I would have made other arrangements for my car. Travel in the LA area still requires a vehicle. While there is WIFI, the guest is charged regardless. Even the Business Center Facility downstairs charges by the minute.There are no "free" wifi zones within the hotel. However, if you walk outside, across the street to the park, or down the block to Starbucks the WIFI is free. Internet connection is now such a part of business that it is akin to being charged to use your cell phone within the hotel. These extra charges amount to between $50-$60 a day. So, just be aware of the fees if you plan to stay in this lovely hotel.

name: Travelodge Hotel at LAX
title: “Worked out fine for the day”
text: We stayed at the Travelodge LAX for the day (day rate of $49.95 plus tax) during a long layover on our way to Fiji and a long layover on our way home from Fiji. We had looked at other day rate options near LAX (Hilton and Westin), but they would only let us stay until 6:00 p.m. Travelodge lets you stay until 8:00 p.m. And the Travelodge was much cheaper. The rooms were very clean, but both rooms we stayed in (225 and 226) had a funny odor to them. We just opened the sliding doors to the patio and were not bothered by it. We would definitely use Travelodge at LAX for a long layover again. The free shuttle worked out really great as well. The pool area was pretty nice as well.

name: Comfort Inn Near Old Town Pasadena - Eagle Rock
title: “Thank God, its Comfort Inn”
text:
After a long day travelling my wife and I needed rest, we passed by many hotels we did not even think of stopping since we knew there had to be a Comfort Inn nearby, and there it was, we both knew that we will be extra comfortable here.
With no reservation the front desk personnel were great, it took 3 min. to check in, the clerk was so gracious and helpful. We ended up with a room exactly what we asked for. we had a great night sleep, the place is quiet, charming , comfortable. we had great time.
Comfort Inn is our number 1 choice, always.

name: Hollywood Hotel
title: “More than adequate!”
text:
I too am a reviewer who is puzzled at the bad reviews that this place has received. The hotel was more than just 'adequate' for us and unless they have done major renovations and fix ups just before we arrived, I would say the others are just super picky?
The location is great for catching a Red Line subway, which, when you're in LA you probably would want to do to visit Hollywood Walk of Fame etc. Don't bother walking if you have to go more than a few blocks as the walks are very boring and shady characters are always seemingly lurking. It's not like Manhattan where you walk 20 blocks and don't even realise because there are things to see on the way.
Anyway, the whole hotel and room was very clean and well appointed with TV, fridge and microwave included. Everything was fully operational in our room. There is a guest laundry on the premises. We did not need to use the parking. Despite what the other reviewers have written, we found the staff to be very helpful and friendly. The room space was comfortable. Breakfast was excellent, the service was excellent and they even make you waffles to order. The breakfast room was also nicely decorated for Easter at the time. Out of all the places I have been this one had the best breakfast ever. I would not hesitate to stay here again.

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “Typisches Flughafenhotel”
text:
Wir hatten das Radisson am Los Angeles Flughafen als Start für unsere Rundreise gewählt. 
Bei dem Hotel handelt es sich um ein typisches Mittelkassehotel direkt am Flughafen. Die Lobby macht einen guten Eindruck. Das Zimmer war normal, wobei es schon recht stark abgewohnt war. Wir hatten leider keine Sleep-Number Betten, was schade war. Das Zimmer war sauber.
Wir hatten eine Rate mit kompletten Frühstück, welches typisch amerikanisch ist.
Die Parkkosten sind nicht zu verachten und lagen bei ca. 25 Dollar.

name: Millennium Biltmore Hotel Los Angeles
title: “A gem”
text:
We arrived (by train, so out of our control) at 9 am, in jeans and floppy hats, with hiking poles sticking out of our rucksacks. The front desk people were friendly, courteous, and let us check into our room immediately. 
The hotel's public areas are, of course, stunning, but I had read some negative comments about the rooms. So we were pleasantly surprised by our spacious, well appointed room. On the third floor, in a standard room, we had a view of Pershing Square. Our total bill for the night including tax and 4 long distance calls was $208. My only complaint was that they charged me $1 each for toll free calls, but I think this is fairly common in some luxury hotels.
Anyone who thinks these rooms are small hasn't traveled much outside of the US. I'm looking for an excuse to go back to LA so I can stay there again!

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Royal Palace Inn & Suites
title: “short stay”
text:
stayed here june 2012(for 4 nights)
rooms comfy and clean
checking in quick and easy
valet service excellent and free
easy access to hollywood, santa monica,lax

name: Hollywood Hotel
title: “Great Location, Poor Hotel”
text:
The Ramada Hollywood Hotel is well situated just one block from the Metro Red Line subway and two separate Metro Rapid bus lines. I found the location convenient for business and pleasure and used public transit for the duration of my stay. This hotel is ideal for business travelers and tourists who do not want to rent a car.
Locational advantages notwithstanding, I do not recommend this hotel to anyone. During my stay, the hotel itself was sorely lacking on many fronts:
-The elevators are very, very slow, and the stairs are roped off as emergency exits only.
-My room (one queen) was smaller than average.
-The television set did not work well, and the cable went in and out every night.
-The floor in my room was stained, and the comforter was severely worn.
-The bathtub was elevated far above floor level, resulting in unsafe entry/exit and a lack of headroom. I am able-bodied and nearly fell getting out of the tub EVERY night. And at 6'1" my head was uncomfortably close to the ceiling.
-My room was remade despite hanging up the "Do Not Disturb" sign. I inquired at the front desk and was informed that I should stop by every morning and request that my room not be remade. For the record, I did that the next three days and they did not enter my room.
-Each room facing the courtyard has a patio, but the patios have no chairs. And because the courtyard is so small, there is no privacy.
-Access to the swimming pool is through the parking lot, and it closes early (8 PM). Also, there is no hot tub.
-Breakfast is served in the basement, which requires a painfully slow elevator trip. I was in a hurry every morning and was disappointed at the lack of "portable" pastries and fruit that could be consumed on my way to the subway station.
The Ramada is located near L.A. City College "somewhere" between Hollywood, Little Armenia, and Silverlake but not actually in any of the three. The neighborhood is walkable but a bit worn in, and I suggest that women be careful walking around by themselves at night. There are several nearby restaurants of varying quality, but the best are a healthy trek away. I walked to them, but most people would be better off driving. There is a Rite Aid at the corner of Santa Monica, but the nearest grocery store is located north at Hollywood (not too far from the restaurants at Prospect).
At $105/night (20% discount for staying >3 nights), the Ramada is not a bargain. Parking is $15/night, which didn't matter for me, but is a bit steep for this part of L.A.! I feel ripped off. Well, I feel like my company got ripped off! Really, the only redeeming feature of the Ramada itself was my ability to print out my Southwest boarding pass before heading to the airport. If the subway station weren't a block away, this hotel would probably devolve into some cheap motel of last resort.
Overall, I suggest you look elsewhere. This place won't kill you or give you bed bugs--I survived here for four nights--but this is not the way to see L.A. I'll be staying elsewhere next time.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “Location and great nachos too”
text:
In LA for business at the Sheraton LAX. You couldn't ask for a better location -- three minutes from the airport. You do get a bit of noise from the air traffic but not so noticeable that it is problematic. The rooms are spacious the regular amenities. 
What I care about:
Internet: 3 star -- 12.95 / day but at least there is free Internet in the lobby
Breakfast: 3 stars -- OK and you can order a la carte
Pillows: 4 stars -- lots and comfortable too
Towels: 3.5 stars -- not fluffy but comfortable and a good size
Water pressure: 5 stars -- have it your way ... excellent
Restaurant could use more staff.

name: Hollywood Hotel
title: “Less than So-So”
text:
I thought the best aspect of this hotel was the location, less than a block away from the Metro Station. Also the continental breakfast was acceptable. While the lobby and the lower levels were attractive, there were several problems with my stay. The elevator service was terrible. The elevator closest to my room rarely worked. The doors to the stairs were marked emergency exits, and indicated that alarms would go off, so I was stuck using the elevators. 
My room was a bit dingy. Gum was stuck to the carpeting and the furniture looked very worn and stained. The bathroom was not clean. Hair and soap were stuck to the walls. The bathtub was clogged and the TV and remote did not work properly. The TV was a plasma screen and looked nice, including a keyboard that was supposedly available for Internet access. So I signed up for the service and found that the TV and keyboard did not work properly. I was charged for the internet anyway. I had a technician come up and unclogged the bathtub but he could not fix the internet and TV problems. 
I had to make sure I put "Do Not Disturb" on my door because housekeeping sometimes came early in the morning. I found my door did not lock when I closed it sometimes. 
The internet terminal in the lobby seemed to only accept credit cards and charged minimum $5.00 for each log on. The first day I was there there was water dripping above the terminal. Then It did not work for several days of my stay and didn't come up again for the last day of my stay. 
The ATM charged a $5.00 service fee and did not work sometimes. The vending machines did not often work as well. Rite Aid had an ATM that only charged $2.00. 
The hotel charged $15.00 a day for parking, which is not bad considering what you pay elsewhere. However the attendants always asked for something different on the way out. Some asked for the entrance ticket while others asked me to pull off the rear view ticket the hotel issued. I did not use my car as much because of the availability of the Metro. 
The neighborhood was immigrant lower middle class. There were some homeless people wandering around. I found people were generally approachable in the neighborhood and I also liked the dollar store a few steps away from the hotel. 
I'm not sure I would choose this hotel again. Not a three star hotel, two at the most.

name: Miyako Hotel Los Angeles
title: “Great Location”
text:
This hotel is within walking distance to so many great bars and restaurants. We stayed here for a party that was just down the block. So convenient!
The only thing that is not convenient is the parking situation. It was a bit confusing figuring out where to go for self parking. Then, once you park, there is no easy way to get to the lobby. 
Nice rooms, though and all the staff were nice.

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “Accogliente”
text: Non sarà l'hotel più nuovo e fashonista tra quelli che affollano i dintorni dell'aeroporto ma è di sicuro accogliente e comodo per trascorrere una notte prima di partire per un volo troppo mattiniero. La camera che avevamo era forse un po' piccola per gli standard americani ma c'era tutto il necessario; il bagno era molto pulito e l'insonorizzazione ottima: eravamo affacciati su uno svincolo stradale e non si sentiva nulla (e io sono molto sensibile ai rumori). Ottimo rapporto qualità/prezzo con circa 40 dollari meno della media degli alberghi di quel livello.

name: Hollywood Hotel
title: “Watch out for Cruella!”
text: We just stayed there on our honeymoon and it was the worst hotel we have stayed in, in America! The woman with the sour face on the front desk is rude and unhelpful to say the least, we called her Cruella! On the last day I asked if we could keep our room for another half day as we were not flying home till the evening to which she replied they didnt provide?! Whoever her manager is, she is losing him money and guests... awful breakfast, smelly rooms and very old fasioned.. oh and there are renovations happening at the moment, builders in first thing in the morning but actually they were the friendliest!!

name: Park Plaza Lodge Hotel
title: “I liked it very much!”
text: This hotel is a hidden gem. My experience was the opposite of the previous poster. My room was very clean. The bathroom was immaculate. The housekeeping staff even straightened my stuff on top of the dresser every day. One day I lost my room key and the front desk staff knew my room number and made me a new one instantly. Great location right next to the Grove and Farmer's Market.

name: Courtyard Los Angeles Century City / Beverly Hills
title: “Comodo y amable”
text: Muy comodo para hospedarse de negocios. Solo lamento que no tengan el desayuno incluido en el precio. Aunque no queda cerca de ninguna atraccion, para mi funciona muy bien por la cercania del evento al que asisto.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “An airport hotel”
text: Not much else need be said. Noisy. But you have to take that with the terriority. Nothing negative or positive I recall

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Royal Palace Inn & Suites
title: “Good Deal”
text: The room was clean, though a little cramped with two huge beds, but I didn't care. The beds were really comfortable. We spent very little time in our rooms. The pool and jacuzzi were great, but the pool-side furniture was a little dirty. Continental breakfast was fine. Fresh baked cookies in the afternoon for the kids! All the staff members were good-natured, helpful, and friendly. They were very nice with the children. I would go here again because it is a reasonably-priced find in Los Angeles, and there were lots of great restaurants nearby. You might have some difficulty finding parking for an SUV, we did, but it was not big deal. Also, don't expect gardens or stuff like that, it's mostly concrete. Close your windows at night and turn on the air conditioning to get a quiet sleep .(Heavy traffic on street outside) We stayed for three days in the middle of the week. I don't know what it is like on weekends.

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “Excelente ubicacion”
text: Estuvimos 1 sola noche y esta muy bien ubicado a 5 minutos del aeropuerto. Si quieren salir a cenar pregunten por el troli. Los lleva a Manhattan beach. Excelentes restaurantes y los regresa cada hora al hotel.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Carriage Inn
title: “Pleasant stay in LA!”
text: Stayed here whilst on a Travelsphere tour of the west coast of the USA. It is just outside LA but still not very far from the main Hollywood attractions. . There are two parts to the hotel - the motel section (which is set out like a traditional US motel) and a tower block section, where we stayed. The room was clean and comfortable and reminded me of a room in a UK premier budget hotel chain (but is more expensive than the latter as we overheard someone in the lobby enquire re: room prices!). The view was of a busy main road. The corridors of the hotel were quite shabby looking, and looked like they needed a good re-paint. We used the free shuttle bus to get to the nearby mall which had some interesting places to eat - and there is also a Denny's restaurant near the hotel which is very convenient. The front desk staff were helpful and there is an internet terminal and ATM in the lobby, The stay was pleasant but unremarkable. A good base to explore LA.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Royal Palace Inn & Suites
title: “Dirty dirty DIRTY!!!”
text:
I am a flight attendant so I have a lot of experience in the hotel department and this is the worst I have seen yet. Yes the beds were comfortable although the do sink in the middle so if you aren't sleeping alone you will be sleeping at a funny angle. 
As soon as we walked into the building there was a terrible smell. To me it smelled like a mixture of smoke and mold.
VERY tiny bathrooms. No bath tub, just a small stand up corner shower.
My biggest turn off to this place was when we were leaving the room I was gathering up my final things and a maid pushes past me and walks over to the bed and pulls off the blanket. Im not talking about the one on top that everyone knows never gets washed, Im talking about the thinner one under that. I watched her take that blanket across the room and disappear into a different room. I was hoping maybe this was a laundry room but I had to check and when I did, I SAW HER PUTTING THAT BLANKET ON A FRESHLY MADE BED!!!!! Disgusting. Who knows who had that blanket before me OR before that person. How long do these people go without washing things. Do they do this with the sheets as well?? 
I DO NOT suggest staying at this hotel. It is chceap for a reason.

name: Conrad Chicago
title: “Wonderful Hotel -- Would Definitely Stay There Again”
text: The Conrad was wonderful. I used my Hilton points to stay for one night before I had to check out the following day and go across the street to the Chicago Marriott where my conference was being held. I much preferred the Conrad over the Marriott. The king-bed room I had was huge and had great amenities. It had those great snuggly robes and slippers for guest's use. I especially enjoyed using the immaculately clean soaking tub (which was right next to the glassed in shower) after an afternoon of bike riding along Lake Michigan. The room was very clean upon arrival. It had a large desk, comfortable lounge chair and ottoman, a very large flat screen t.v., bose sound system, a DVD player and an alarm clock/docking station next to the bed for your Ipod. I was on a lower floor (6th) and occasionally you could hear the El train rumble by, but I only noticed it occasionally when I was awake (did not bother my sleep at all). It is in a great location. I didn't try any of the restaurants in the hotel so I can't comment on those. The fitness center was adequate. It had less cardio eqiupment than I thought it would for a hotel that size (I think 8-9 pieces?) and their weight equipment could use some updating. All in all a great stay and I would definitely book into this hotel again.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Royal Palace Inn & Suites
title: “Nice Hotel Great value”
text:
The hotel meets all my requirements; good location within a maximum 20 minutes drive to all LA attractions, safe neighbourhood, reasonable price, free breakfast (good one), free parking (tight but wonderful benefit in LA), guest laundry (helped me a lot), big comfortable room w/siiting area, fridge and microwave (You can save at eating).
For me a hotel is a place with free options just to have a sleep and save to pay for attractions. The staff were awesoome, very kind, very helpful and knowledgeable; especially Fred, thank you for everything. I would defintely recommend the hotel for families and I will stay there every time I am in LA.
You must try The Lobster restaurant in Santa Monica, (expensive) but amazing!!! Just five to seven minutes drive from the hotel.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Royal Palace Inn & Suites
title: “Good value for the price!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed here on our vacation, and we both thought it was a great motel for the price. It's a Best Western, so you can't expect the same amenities as The Four Seasons. :) Our room was huge (as was our bathroom!). Housekeeping came faithfully every day and did a good job. The parking lot in back is on the small side, but we rented a Subaru Outback for our trip and had no trouble manuvering our car in and out. (One word of caution: if you get back to the motel too late at night, it's very likely the lot will already be filled up. But you can park on the street -- we were able to get a spot right out front) The front desk staff was very helpful and always had a spot-on answer for any questions we had, whether it was on how to avoid L.A. traffic, to where you could find a good bottle of wine. All in all, I'd definitely recommend anyone traveling to L.A. to give this place a try.

name: Millennium Biltmore Hotel Los Angeles
title: “Better Then Expected”
text:
I recently stayed at the Millenium Biltmore evening of July 25th as I needed a place in the Los Angeles area without having to drive back out to Riverside for the evening. I was slightly concerned about the hotel in reading reviews here but after staying it was not as bad as I had feared. I arrived around 7pm on the evening of the 25th and was quickly helped with the bellman and the car was whisked away within seconds of it being unloaded. There was no wait at check-in which was polite and professional and the bellman literally followed us to the room with my friend and I with the only exception him taking the service elevator while we took the public one even though we both met up on the 8th floor at the same time. 
He quickly showed us to our room and unloaded all of our bags as my friend had quite the shopping trip on Rodeo Dr. earlier in the day and asked if we needed anything additional and even offered to fill our ice bucket which I thought was a nice touch. 
As we planned to go out later in the evening I called ahead for the valet to get the car ready and by the time we walked down after the call which was approx 10 minutes the car was ready and waiting for us.
As stated in previous posts with it being an older holtel the rooms vary in size but the room I was located in was quite large and maybe even a bit too large with the furniture that was in the room. I do believe the room could use a bit of an upgrade in terms of bedding but the rest of the furniture seemed plentiful and there were plenty of both electrical outlets in the room for all of the stylist products of my friend to use. While the view of the room wasn't much you could see parts of Olive St which is better then most buildings which are smaller in size in crowded downtowns. 
Check-out was fast and efficent and once again I called down to have the valet get the car ready ahead of time and this time it was only about 5 minutes after I left the room and the car was ready and waiting once again.
Overall the staff were professional and helpful with my only hesitation staying there again the aging beds and linens which could definately use an upgrade to bring them up to the 4* standard.

name: Conrad Chicago
title: “Faux Art Deco?”
text:
Despite being a longtime Hilton visitor, this was the first time I have stayed in a Conrad. Because of a number of meetings and a private dining requirement, I was booked into a suite on the 17th floor. The room was very spacious with all the facilities necessary and the service from friendly check-in to waiters and concierge could not be faulted. It was and expensive stay but the value for money was there...a big tick in my box.
Try as I might, I couldn't work out how old the hotel was. There was a definite art deco feel to everything with the main colour being sort of beige. The lifts (elevators) were straight out of Gotham City and appeared to be designed to give out as little possible interior light as indeed were most of the public areas. I'm still not sure whether the hotel was designed as a "1930's Experience" or if indeed it was from the 1930's...
In any event, most impressed and would certainly visit again if on business...if not with the assistance of night vision goggles.

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “Per riposare in attesa del mattino dopo”
text: Situato veramente all'uscita dell'aereoporto internazionale. Lunga attesa per la navetta che poi fà un lungo giro e ci deposita come ultima tappa sul ritorno verso l'aeroporto. Camera insonorizzata :non si sente il traffico aereo. Moquette malandata,antica, bagno pulito ma datato.Ristorante interno ancora funzionante alle11 PM con cibo normale e prezzi un po' all'insù,ma adeguati,vista l'ora e la distanza da altre fonti di conforto.Stanza spaziosa, biancheria pulita ,ci mancavano i bicchieri per posare lo spazzolino in bagno: fatto notare alla reception al check out e, senza battere ciglio, mi applicano uno sconto di 25 US$ sul prezzo camera.Concierge utile e preciso nelle risposte.Distanza dall'affitto macchine 6 minuti con taxi e 7 US$ spesa,compresa mancia autista.

name: Hollywood Hotel
title: “worse worse and worse again”
text:
We had a Room with View right to the main Street. We double checked if there are really Windows in the Room becaus it was loud as they weren't. We could not sleep at all. The curtain was ripped as well the carpet, the Hook ups in the Bathroom were rusty and old. The Hotel was fully booked and the complimentary Breakfast was terrible. If you had a chance to get something. Because the Staff was overhauled. Glad that we stayed only this one night. Never ever again. I contacted the Ramada Company and I got just a Aplologies Letter from the Manager. Thats it!
If you want to stay cheap you can do this better in any other Motel.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Royal Palace Inn & Suites
title: “Ok für Kurzaufenthalt”
text: Das Hotel liegt verkehrstechnisch gut. Wir haben Santa Monica/Venice Beach, Hollywood/Universal Studios und das Getty Museum besucht und logierten zwei Nächte im Hotel. Das Hotel ist ok für einen kurzen Aufenthalt. Für einen längeren Aufenthalt oder wenn man viel Zeit im Hotel verbringen will, empfiehlt sich ein Hotel mit umfassenderer Infrastruktur auszuwählen. Unser Zimmer mit Sofabereich (Suite) war rückseitig gelegen und ruhig. Allerdings war es etwas muffig. Man hat auch den Eindruck, dass der Zeitpunkt für eine Renovation langsam fällig wäre. Der Name Royal Palace ist irreführend und weckt falsche Erwartungen. Das kostenlose Valet-Parking funktioniert einwandfrei. Das Frühstück war etwas über dem Durchschnitt vergleichbarer Hotels.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “These are the people who really strives to provide superior service every time”
text:
I was surprised and delighted during my last stay at this wonderful hotel, when I was about to check-in, the very friendly and happy staff at the front desk told me that my upgrade to junior suite has been already arranged. To be honest, it was my very first time as a SPG memeber experiencing this, without even asking for it, they did it in a very nice way that made me feel so at home.
Late check-out, and all the rest of the perks were automatically given, hassle free all the way .
I would like not only to recommend this "value for the money" hotel, but more because of their staff, from concierge to the manager, everybody goes the extra mile to satisfy your needs.
Congratulations and continue to be the best choice around LAX !

name: Travelodge Hotel at LAX
title: “Very nice hotel for the price”
text: Please do not let the outside of the hotel or the surrounding area fool you. This is a very nice, clean hotel. I have stayed here twice in the past two weeks and I was totally satisfied on both occasions. When I first checked in I was a bit concerned because it was dark and raining so the hotel looked a bit run down. Once I got in to my room, I was very impressed. The hotel is a bit dated by the bed was confortable, the room was clean and the bathroom was spotless. There was no bath tub but the walk in shower was the size of a bath tub. The best part about the hotel is that the wifi was free, free parking, and there is a Dennys connected to the hotel. The staff was nice and accommodating.

name: Radisson Hotel at Los Angeles Airport
title: “posizione strategica e ottimo prezzo e servizio”
text: per la terza volta pernottiamo in questo hotel e anche questa volta rimaniamo molto soddisfatti. per los angeles, anche se può sembrare strano, riteniamo la zona dell'aeroporto strategicamente ottima per il pernottamento, infatti gli spostamenti verso le principali attrazioni sono facilitati dalla vicinanza delle strade migliori per arrivarci, considerando il tremendo traffico che in quasi tutta la giornata è possibile trovare. la qualità dell'albergo e del servizio è in linea con gli alberghi posti nelle vicinanze deglia eroporti maggiori. servizio efficiente, troverete sempre una camera a vostra disposizione a prescindere dall'orario in cui arrivate; posizione ottima, 20/25 minuti da venice o santa monica e 40/45 minuti dagli studios; stanze confortevoli e pulite. ottimo rapporto qualità/prezzo.

name: Travelodge Hotel at LAX
title: “You get what you pay for. . .okay for a LAX layover”
text: I only paid $60 for one night so I wasn't expecting much. I got in at 1:00AM so I had to call three times until I got someone on the phone for the airport shuttle. That was a bit frustrating but I just rolled with it because I was tired. The desk staff person was friendly and pointed out the breakfast and internet usage. I had a hard time finding my room because it was all the way in the back. I helped another woman try to find her room. It's a bit confusing. The room was just okay. The bathroom was very clean but it only had a shower. The bed was okay. There was an air-conditioner left running in the room which made the air stale. The really liked that there was a Denny's right next door though.

name: Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Disappointing stay, won't stay again”
text: Stayed here for 3 nights in early September. Rooms are average, quite small & look worn. Horrible, creepy artwork over bed of a man looking down on bed. Bathroom floor had many scuff marks from the door that wouldn't close easily. Shower/bath combined was dangerous as no slip mat in there. One evening our toilet overflowed so we laid towels and the bath mat over tiles to stop it flowing onto carpet in room. We reported it & went for swim in their pool. Came back and half the floor had been mopped up, other half still had water. Wet bath mat still where we left it in doorway near toilet, soaking wet. Reported it again on way out to dinner. When we returned the remaining water had been mopped up & bath mat back placed back near the shower. We presumed it had been replaced until the morning when we went to use the shower. The bath mat was completely soaked with the water it absorbed from the toilet the night before. Disgusting. I personally went to find housekeeping on the floor to get a replacement. Not good enough service for the high price they charge for the rooms. Also, no free wifi available anywhere in the hotel. Again, not good enough. For what we paid the service was far below the standard one would expect. We certainly won't stay here again and do not recommend this hotel. (we are from Melbourne, Australia)

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “Adequate for a stopover”
text:
Had a short overnight transit at this hotel. First impressions were good but the rooms are quite tired looking but adequate. One does not stay at airport hotels and expect wonders - even if it was a Westin.
However, my greatest peeve is the service at the hotel. Check-in and Check-out was rather slow and this can be annoying after a long flight (for the former) and when you are rushing to catch the shuttle bus (for the latter).
One thing I would note that needs a large improvement is the attitude and service level of the front door staff. I was carrying three big pieces of luggage and they did not even try to assist me as I was making my way across the expansive lobby to the front doors (ditto upon arrival). They made a show to help me load into the shuttle bus but it was the driver that exerted himself to help while two of the front door staff were having a protracted conversation while pushing the bags to the driver to upload. Thereafter, they looked expectantly for a tip from myself even though I do not think they are worthy of it.
So in the end, adequate but some training is required of the front door staff for this to be an 'inspiring experience...'

name: Miyako Hotel Los Angeles
title: “If you're in that area, it's THE place”
text: If you need or want to stay downtown and near Little Tokyo, you can't beat it. I had business meetings very nearby, so it was the logical choice for me (since I didn't want to bother with a car), but I was ultimately impressed by the room and staff. I booked through an online room broker and when I called the day before my arrival to confirm the reservation, the hotel staff had no information--yet. (The broker ended up not faxing my reservation until the day of arrival.) In any case, during the phone calls before the reservation came through--when I was a nervous wreck--the front desk staff was unfailingly polite and also advised me on how to resolve the issue. The common areas of the hotel are very clean, and my room was spotless. There were small nicks in the furniture, and this is clearly not a new hotel, but the room was spacious and well-appointed. The snack bar in the lobby had quite a selection of drinks, sandwiches and snacks and is open long hours, and there are some fun sushi shops right around the corner. It's kind of a scruffy neighborhood, but I did not feel unsafe. The rates are also extremely reasonable.

name: Miyako Hotel Los Angeles
title: “Bad faith. Won't stay again.”
text: Booked room through PLine. Asked for non-smoking. Gave me smoking, smelly room overlooking busy street. Blamed this on late booking. I believe this was not because the non-smoking rooms were booked, as the hotel seems uncrowded and not busy, but because of the priceline booking. Poor location of self park in public lot distant from rooms, elevator. Room in bad shape. Cigarette burns in table. Stained chairs. Bathroom in bad shape, cracked tile, cracked sink. Someday, someone will file a class action against priceline/these hotels which typcially do not provide the three or four star class advertised by priceline. Further, priceline does not notify purchasers that parking is not free.

name: Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Gorgeous hotel, great location for Hollywood tourist attractions”
text:
I stayed here for two nights on business late July and was thoroughly impressed with this hotel. It's stylish and full of typical Hollywood glamour. Rooms are a decent size, pool and bar areas are well looked after and the staff are super friendly. There's a great gym and spa too (although I didn't use the spa as the prices were ridiculous!)
I personally prefer West Hollywood, or Beverley Hills to stay in, but if it's your first time in LA and want to visit the Chinese Theatre, Walk of Fame etc then you really couldn't be any closer.
The only gripe I have is that the pool was closed on my last day due to a private event, meaning I had no real place to relax while waiting for my flight that evening. I suspect that due to the great pool scene and hotel location this could be a regular occurence.
I also called room service for food when I first arrived and was told someone would call me back. I waited half an hour, no call ever came and I had to go to a local fast food joint instead.

name: Miyako Hotel Los Angeles
title: “Good Enough For Short Stay”
text:
Stayed here one night with three family members after getting a pretty good deal with Priceline. Check-in was easy and all our dealings with the staff was courteous and quick. Space felt a bit small with four adults and our baggage. The room and bathroom felt slightly worn, but it wasn't much of an issue to us, though it may be to others. I agree with other reviewers when they say that it's not AS nice as it shows in the hotel's website.
As for location, it is in downtown LA which isn't a particularly convenient spot if you're doing the touristy things, which we were, and LA traffic doesn't help the distance. The front desk explained both the valet and self-serve parking options. We used the hotel's valet, which was easy and quick, even though it cost more than the self-serve parking around the block. 
All in all, we were satisfied with our stay, especially considering what we spent and the time we were there. Though i'm not sure I would choose a downtown hotel to base my stay in LA as a tourist.

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “Great for a conference or layover”
text: I spent 4 nights here for a conference, so I had a chance to try out all the hotel's amenities. The airport shuttle is very convenient, running about every 20 minutes and making only 1 other stop on the way to LAX. Checking in and out were quick and painless. The room was large and comfortable. The restaurant, grill, and lobby bar are all good, with interesting menus and great service. If you want more than a treadmill you'll probably be disappointed in the exercise room. The pool is a little small. There are computers available in the business center that allow you to print boarding passes and check in for your flights. The concierge and staff are very helpfull. I'll definitely stay again.

name: Travelodge Hotel at LAX
title: “it's an awful hotel”
text: The room we got was dark and dingy due to a blown out ceiling light and the carpet felt and looked dirty. The ceiling was peeling and patched several times. The bedding had holes in it and the beds were hard. One of the shower taps was loose and you could see the holes the taps came out of the wall. I thought we were in the "hood". There's signs on the hotel entrance door about the amount of the cash kept in the lobby and a bullet hole in our room's window. I would never stay here again. The pictures are deceiving.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “Value for your money”
text: The rooms are clean, but everything from the hallway carpet to the furniture was stained, dingy, and old. The food is great and the service is ok. Stay here if you find a good bargain.

name: BEST WESTERN Woodland Hills Inn
title: “TRIP FOR A FRIEND”
text: Great Location, right off the 101, across the street from jerry's deli, great nite clerk. thank-you. would stay again.

name: Hollywood Hills Hotel
title: “Great Views Great Pool”
text: We stayed for 4 nights up on the Hill, room 301. We had a fantastic time here, the rooms were comfortable and clean, and the staff were amazing, really super helpful and polite and happy. The pool on the hill is great, we spent a few days lazing by the pool and were pretty much the only people using it. The views from the top of the hill, from the apartment and the pool are nothing short of spectacular. The rooms may be a tiny bit tired, and could do with a paint, but we didn't care about that at all. The location is perfect, a 5 minute walk from reception to Hollywood Boulevard. This place has two hotels, the Hollywood Hills Hotel, up the hill, and down the bottom of the hill The Magic Castle Hotel. If you want spectacular views and an awesome pool then head up the top. We can't recommend this place highly enough, we'll be back.

name: Dunes Inn - Sunset
title: “Good value for money and close to Hollywood”
text:
If you're looking for a comfortable motel that isn't to expensive but is still close to the hustle and bustle of Hollywood than this is a very good choice. 
There is a small reception area with very friendly and helpfull staff.
The rooms are clean, not very big. A decent size bed with a good hard matras, the pillows are on the small size and there are no extra ones in the room available. There is a fridge available but no coffee making facilities. Breakfast is not included in the price, there is a restaurant on the property but it was closed when we stayed here and it didn't look like it would reopen any time soon. A down side is that the lighting in the room is very bright white "hospital like" lights.
Airconditioning is available and you can also open the windows. A parking lot is available on site, and is free.
There is a 7-eleven next door and the motel is in a decent area, only about 5 minutes from Hollywood Boulevard.
A very good choice when looking for a cheaper solution in LA and still close to all the action!

name: Hollywood Hills Hotel
title: “Fabulous Staff, Awesome Location”
text: The location of this hotel is great. We loved the peaceful setting and the funkiness of the building. The bedding and bathroom were clean but the walls were grimy and in need of painting. The staff at the Magic Castle where you check in were fabulous. It really made our stay to be so well taken care of. We would definitely stay here again and hope that some walls get cleaned/painted in the meantime.

name: Figueroa Hotel
title: “Absolutely Delightful”
text:
My sister and I stayed 4 nights at the Figueroa Hotel because we were attending a conference at the Convention Center which required long, full days. The location is absolutely unbeatable, so close to everything, safe and convenient.
My sister books countless hotel reservations for her work and thus took care of these arrangements, before our arrival she had expressed how wonderful, patient and caring the staff was from her very first inquiry. 
I have been in hotel management for longer than I care to admit and have been fortunate to experience accommodations all over the world, including Morocco. I must admit prior to arriving I was a bit skeptical about the theme and how well it could be done in the center of LA... how very wrong I was. From the moment we stepped inside the walls I was blown away by the details and caring that went into the property. It delivered a feel so genuine and welcoming I craved our return after the long days. 
Every single staff member was exquisite. Professional, courteous, caring and attentive. The rooms were revamped in the spirit of the Hotel in such a brilliantly inexpensive manner to allow for the rates to be so reasonable right in the middle of everything. Our room was bright with a large closet and very clean. My sister and I both enjoyed some of the best nights of sleep we can remember.
The pool was beautiful, the bar was awesome and the restaurant (which drew locals as well as guests) was charming.
This is a delightful property that has worked hard to deliver a unique experience for an incredible value, I would absolutely recommend it and hope to be able to return some day!

name: Royal Palace Westwood
title: “One notch above a dump, beware!”
text:
Stayed at this hotel mid April, for one night. It is very antiquated, particularly in the common parts and though I read it had been given a makeover, this must have been very cursory.
We are a couple with an 11 year old so we chose a junior suite at $175 night consisting of a sitting room with Z bed, table and chairs and a bedroom with saggy queen sized bed. There was also a bathroom with small tub. Everything appeared to be quite clean, (not sure of carpet though) but the bed was very, very saggy. Needless to say due to the the floor and poor bed quality we hardly slept at all. Must also say that internet connection wasn't brilliant.
The continental breakfast, which others have described, is very poor, stale bread and Danish, small selection of cereals, couple of juices, tea and coffee which is laid out in a very depressing interior room just off the depressingly narrow hallway/entrance to the hotel.
In short, I'm sure you could do worse in LA, don't know the city well enough but would assume you could also do a heck of a lot better!

name: Crowne Plaza Beverly Hills
title: “Great value, great service, great location”
text: I stayed here on a Saturday night, and everything exceeded expectations. The staff was particularly courteous and attentive. Beds were very comfortable. And the location is less than a mile from Rodeo Drive -- a moderate walk or a short cab. The only thing that could have been better was the view -- but I really didn't spend that much time in the room itself -- so much to see and do outside. My sister and her family stayed at the Beverly Wilshire (for 3 times the price), and I thought the service here at the Crowne Plaza was friendlier. They went out of their way to make sure I had an enjoyable stay.

name: Figueroa Hotel
title: “Figueroa Hotel, the best place to stay in Downtown LA!”
text: Great vibe, great atmosphere, the most uniquely decorated hotel, fun to stay in. I love the Figueroa Hotel! It’s so accommodating in so many ways, comfortable, very clean, good food, great prices. To me, it is the best hotel in Downtown LA, at the very least. I wasn’t expecting this Moroccan hotel to be so home-y, but I would definitely choose to stay here when I need to be in Downtown. The rooms are like going on a little adventure. The staff is wonderful, warm, and very welcoming. I would also go there to eat, too, great food, and very reasonable, not to forget a fabulous atmosphere in the lobby. In so many ways, I was treated very nicely here. Stay here when you are going to an event, too. I think this hotel is a treat to the senses. Thank you Figueroa, for you being you! Well done.

name: BEST WESTERN Woodland Hills Inn
title: “Tres bien”
text:
Motel vraiment agréable :
personnel accueillant et chambre très confortable. Le seul point négatif serait le bruit de la climatisation.
Le motel est bien situé, proche des commerces et restaurants.
Motel où nous retournerions avec plaisir.
Je recommande.

name: Hilton Los Angeles Airport
title: “Excellent Stay before a long flight”
text:
Staying over at this hotel mainly due to an early flight out of LAX. This hotel is very busy due to through traffic and all. However, the service is great. The shuttles going to the airport are practically every 5-10 minutes. There is a Hertz desk at the hotel, so I was able to drop off my car there without having to deal with it at 5 AM.
The rooms are very comfortable and even though its at the airport, there is slight noise from the planes taking off. However, it is super quiet at night, when it matters most.

name: Travelodge Hotel at LAX
title: “Très correct pour le prix.”
text:
Navette gratuite pour l'aeroport, 5 minutes à pied de l'agence de location , Alamo et Hertz. Parking gratuit et petit déjeuner correcte, piscine. Chambre vieillotte mais très spacieuse. Café et thé dans la chambre.
J'y retournerais sans problême.

name: Coral Sands Motel
title: “Endroit correct mais sans plus”
text:
Pour le prix tout près de Hollywood, à Los Angeles, c'est correct. En fait, l'accueil est assez moyen. En arrivant, le stationnement donne sur l'arrière des chambres (plutôt laid), et la réception est assez froide. Les réceptionnistes sont protégés par une vitrine et ils nous font part de directives sérieuses au sujet des visiteurs nocturnes. D'accord... mais nous ne sommes pas ce genre de personnes qui reçoivent des gens la nuit... Au moins, c'est rassurant de savoir que le motel est bien sécurisé et qu'il y a quelqu'un à la réception 24 h sur 24.
La chambre est correct et très propre, c'est ce qui importe. Le WIFI fonctionne très bien. La douche est grande, et la pression de l'eau est extra! La salle de bain est toutefois petite. La chambre d'à côté était en rénovation. Peut-être les chambres seront-elles rénovées bientôt? Les chambres sont dotées d'un petit frigo et d'une cafetière. Le petit-déjeuner n'est pas offert, mais il y a un Jamba Juice à côté et une pharmacie au coin de la rue. La pièce commune est une très bonne idée. Elle offre des laveuses-sécheuses et du détergeant, un ordinateur pour consultations rapides et une bibliothèque avec livres dans divers langues et dépliants touristiques. 
Le quartier un peu moyen. Pour aller à Hollywood (Walk of Fame), il vous faudra environ une demi heure à pied en passant par l'est d'Hollywood, où il y a beaucoup de sans-abris (qui peuvent parfois même être agressifs). Ne soyez pas seul. Je ne recommande pas Hollywood le soir de toute façon. Ce n'est pas un endroit rassurant, plutôt étrange même.
Rapport qualité-prix, c'est correct. Vous pouvez peut-être trouver mieux. J'avais failli réserver au Downtowner Inn sur Hollywood Boulevard. En fait, je l'ai vu une fois sur place, et je ne le recommanderais pas, car il est en plein dans l'est de Hollywood, dans le quartier des sans-abris. Je préférerais le Coral Sands.

name: Coral Sands Motel
title: “Wahnsinns Unterkunft!”
text: Sau geiles Hotel! In direkter Nähe zum Kodak Theater (2 Metro Stationen). Sehr sauber! Super Lage! Sehr freundliches und zuvorkommendes Personal! Sauberer Pool und Wirlpool!

name: Figueroa Hotel
title: “Oasis Downtown”
text:
Have Stayed here a number of times over the last 15+ years, and I’ve never written a review. I stayed here last in Jan 2011. The Fig never ceases to amaze me. This stylish, under-the-radar riad-of-a-hotel was at the forefront of the boutique hotel scene in the 1990s and it’s still is one of my top 10s anywhere. I come here a few times a year for business and pleasure – Convention Center, Nokia, LA Live are all across the street.

This wasn’t always a great spot – actually just the opposite – but I’ve stayed at the Westin, Hilton, you name it, and this place is now at the epicenter of downtown…shopping, dining and entertainment. Great rates, fun, fashionable and economical accommodations. Cheapest parking downtown that I have found. The Ritz-Carlton charges around $40, parking here is less than half that. Travel a lot and the hotel’s colorful, upbeat pan-Asian/N. African style is a breath of fresh air from the “standardized,” catalogue-fueled digs that are the norm these days. The familial, professional staff is a rarity. And the proprietor is a witty, bright-eyed guy whose inimitable style was one of the initial sparks that helped ignite the whole boutique hotel trend. He always seems to be here, and always seems to have the time to say hello, sometimes share a story. Great stories! The bar and pool areas are highlights, a touch of CB-Demille glamour in the 21st century, and the hot tub is always hot! The unheated pool can be a shock, but the proprietor appears to be holding onto his Swedish heritage – Still, this is LA, not Uppsala. It certainly ain’t the Ritz, but it’s not meant to be. This place is a beacon of old-school hospitality, and one of a small handful of its kind left in the states. It’s ironic that it was a trendsetter when it reopened with its new look, and it is still setting trends today – character driven, reasonably priced accommodations with friendly service in a convenient downtown setting. 3-stars is the new 5-stars! Baring Devid Geffin buying the building, can't imagine staying anywhere else.

name: The Standard Downtown LA
title: “"Standard" says it all -- this hotel is NOTHING special”
text:
I stayed here on business because it was very close to the meeting I had the next morning.
I'd imagine if you are in your 20's and hip and trendy is a top priority this place is great fun. But if you are not and value service and amenities -- dont stay here. I am 8 and 1/2 months pregnant, when I checked in with the hotel's velt no one offered to help with my bags -- a first. So I schlepped my bags in (no doorman to get the door either) and checked in. Check in was fine. My room was large -- but neednt be given the minimalist layout. I had a soap, shampoo and conditoner. No lotion, no cups by the wash basin and no bathrup. The room, although a non-smoking room, smelled mildly of smoke, but not bad. The walls were somewhat thin and I could easily hear other doors opening and closing and the bing of the elevator.
I ordered room service breakfast the next day. The guy who delivered it acted as if I inconviennced him by placing my order and was not friendly at all. the breakfast was pretty good though. Upon checkout the computer was down and they said they would fax my bill within two hours. It never came.
I was simply not impressed. It was clean, but very utilitarian. If you prefer the Four Seasons, Ritz, or even a nice Omni type hotel....dont stay here.

name: Crowne Plaza Los Angeles International Airport Hotel
title: “Location near LAX is this place's big virtue”
text:
I am sure that other hotels in LA can offer a better LA experience. However, if you need a decently priced hotel near the airport ( technically in the airport boundary) this works.
Got a good deal on room rates via Hotwire, so this ends up being a good deal, what with the free airport shuttle and a couple of food options in- house. There is not much in the immediate vicinity, so either you taxi to some other part of town or you make do with the hotel's restaurant selections. They do offer live music some nights which can be nice.
One quibble...I really dislike hotels like this that charge for Internet access (throughout the hotel, even in the lobby). Bad joss.

name: Figueroa Hotel
title: “Unique hotel. With a few improvements could be a masterpiece!”
text:
The charm of this hotel lies in it's ambiance. The moment we walked in the door, we felt like we had been transported to Morocco, and we expected to see Rick and Ilsa at the bar with Sam tickling the ivories. The room was enormous, but the mattress could have used changing; there was a spot in the middle that seemed like the springs had been worn down and we kept rolling into it in the middle of the night. My back was not happy with that part of the trip. The outdoor patio complete with a bar, a pool and a spa were a pleasant surprise, and we even got to see the owner, Uno, feeding the pet iguana in the cactus! 
The location was perfect. Right across the street from the new LA Live, the Staples Center and the LA Convention Center. If you get a chance to, check out the Grammy Museum. It houses some interesting memorabilia and fun interactive displays. Since it's on the outskirts of downtown, walking to the Historic Core is a bit of a hike, but well worth it once you get there. Be sure to check out Grand Central Market for some incredibly cheap produce and good Chinese food.
Also, DO NOT MISS The Original Pantry on the corner of 9th and Figueroa. They have no locks on the doors because the diner has never closed since 1924. That in itself was enough to make us go in. This year is their 85th birthday, having never turned the lights off and never locked the door. The home fries that they serve with breakfast are cooked in a cast iron skillet that has been in use AT LEAST since the 1960s. Needless to say, it's a seasoned pan! 
Overall, the hotel is a very nice place to stay as a base for your explorations of downtown LA, however if you're looking for the Ritz-Carlton, stay elsewhere. It's very minimal in its amenities. There is no coffee maker or alarm clock in the room, the television is small with only a few stations and the water pressure in the shower could have used adjusting, I almost got blasted out of the room when I turned it on the first morning. But for the price, it was just right and the location cannot be beat!

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Not as nice as other westins that I have stayed in.”
text: I was in LA for a four day conference at the end of September. The hotel is of an older design where there is a lot of exposed concrete. Combine that with a night club at lobby level and the place seems more like a gathering hall than a tranquil lobby. The standard room is on the smaller size and unfortunately for me my room had probably just had the carpets cleaned so they smelt quite like mildew. Lucky for me though the windows actually open so i could air out the room. Parking is not cheap at 38 per night. I personally found this expensive considering my car rental was 65 for four days. I found the cost of parking to be disproportionately high. Street parking is very hard to find but if you do its free from 6 pm to 8 am. I was going to the convention center so you can move your car to a lot on the corner of flower and Olympic one block from the center for 5 dollars for a day if you get the early bird. I just drove leaving at 8 to the lot. Overall I enjoy the westins but I probably would not stay here again if I were attending a convention here.

name: Crowne Plaza Los Angeles International Airport Hotel
title: “A good quality hotel, rooms in need of refurbishment”
text:
I stayed here in October 2010. The main reason for me choosing the hotel was due to it's airport location and complimentary shuttle bus as I was on a late arriving flight.
The public areas of the hotel are clean and welcoming, if a little dated. The front desk staff were extremely efficient and helpful on check in and a credit to the hotel.
I had upgraded to a club level room located on the highest floor of the hotel. Whilst the room had all the basic facilities it was most definitely in need of refurbishment. The carpet had several stains and the walls were marked in several places. There was a letter in the room explaining the hotel rooms were undergoing refurbishment, this is much needed as the rooms are very dated and not what you would expect from this brand.
Room service was quick and efficient, all the staff are encountered throughout my stay were friendly and courteous.
If all of the rooms are being refurbished I would definitely stay at this hotel again, although I'm not sure the additional supplement for a club room is worth the money.

name: Crowne Plaza Los Angeles Harbor Hotel
title: “Nice quiet and friendly hotel”
text:
I stayed at this hotel using Priority Club points. We given a large corner suite room at club level. Other than the bathroom is small, the bed room is fine.
Check in without problem with friendly front desk personnel. There is free parking at hotel. The club lounge was open and breakfast was provided for Priority Club Platinum members but the food selection is limited.
Very close to pier and LA Maritime Museum. The surrounding is very quiet and not much activities.

name: Holiday Inn Express Los Angeles-LAX Airport
title: “They where there when we needed them”
text: On the 21/06/2011,we where just returning from Las Vegas after spending time with relatives,after checking in at the staff counter,and having some dinner and about to receive our seats,there was a gut feeling that we where not going that night,so I rang my supervisor in sydney australia and he asked have they cancelled the flight yet because nothing is flying out of sydney.I checked the departure boards and our flight was not there,then checked with the staff counter only to be told that 2 Sydney flights cancelled due to volcanic ash cloud over southern australia,then had to find accomodation and holiday inn came to mind,and found holiday inn express to be very accommodating at such short notice and reasonably priced.

name: Figueroa Hotel
title: “Where is the manager?”
text: This isn't your average motel. It is more a mixture of Moorish-Mexican-Psychedelic style in a building that dates back 75 years. It has a great location if you need to be near the Staples or the Convention Center and you do not walk the neighborhood after dark. Also great if you are a history buff that enjoys living like people did in the early part of the century. No microwave, weak lighting, no coffee maker and no clock in the room. A mattress hard as a river bed. One night a band played for a birthday party outside our window at 80 dbs (about the sound level of a commercial jet) until 11PM, although a written notice announced that they would end at 9:30.
