When a game was played at the nearby stadium, the lot ($8 night) had no parking places for guests. The manager was never in.

name: Holiday Inn Express Los Angeles-LAX Airport
title: “Good Value & near LAX”
text:
Our flight was delayed and we stayed here for one night prior to our return to OZ. There is a courtesy pick up & drop off to LAX - about 15 minutes away. Good prompt regular service with polite & helpful drivers.
The hotel was pleasant and the room was comfortable and clean - with a huge bed! 
We had a complimentary breakfast as part of our deal , and it was excellent . Full American hot breakast served by courteous friendly staff.
Internet access is available - but a touch pricey.
We extended our check out time to coincide with an evening departure time from LAX . This only cost a few extra dollars , but was so worth it , as it meant we could shower immediately before a 16 hour flight , and not have to sit around all day waiting .
There's a McDonalds close by , but unsure of how safe the area around the hotel is - we were there on a Sunday and it seemed quiet - a bit isolated actually , so we made the most of the big flat screen TV in our room - it was the end of our trip after all - and we were more than ready for some rest. Therefore we spent all our time there in the hotel or the room , and it was extremely pleasant.

name: Conrad Chicago
title: “Etwas enttäuschend...”
text:
Zum Ende unserer USA-Reise stiegen wir noch zwei Tage im Conrad in Chicago ab. Wir haben ein kleines Zimmer bekommen mit Ausblick auf das dicht daneben liegende Bürogebäude. Wenn man denen dort keine Show bieten wollte, musste man bei Aufenthalt im Zimmer die Vorhänge geschlossen halten. Das Bad war recht groß mit separater Toilette. Das Hotel liegt recht zentrumsnah und man kann in kurzer Zeit zum Hancock-Center und zum MacMile laufen. 
Unsere Mini-Bar war leer, ich habe hier aber auch nicht nachgefragt, warum das so ist. Immerhin wurde in der Lobby morgens Kaffee to go angeboten. 
Als wir am ersten Tag um 15 Uhr in unser Zimmer zurückkamen, war der Zimmerservice leider noch nicht dagewesen. 
Immerhin gab es für einmal 24 Stunden W-Lan frei.
Ich werde dieses Hotel nicht mehr buchen.

name: Crowne Plaza Los Angeles International Airport Hotel
title: “Hotel Quality is declining”
text: Carpet has stains, bathroom tub did not even drain the water--it was just gross. Beds are comfortable, but the appearance of the room and hotel corridors are terrible. It is convenient to LAX and they have a shuttle, but so don't other hotels. This hotel is in need of updating.

name: The Standard Downtown LA
title: “Perfect choice”
text: Pour qui souhaite passer un moment downtown, le standard hotel est parfait a Los Angeles. Un restaurant qui sert une cuisine de dinner americain typique mais bonne, chambres design très confortable, nous avons ete upgradés et surtout une piscine sur le toit avec un bar qui attire une sympathique cohorte de branchouilles le soir venu, la vue est panoramique sur toute la ville. Une escale parfaite pour visiter les musées d'art contemporain à proximité. Déco branchée, barbier coiffeur à l'entrée, personnel aimable et jeune qui ne se prend pas la tête.

name: Crowne Plaza Los Angeles International Airport Hotel
title: “poor service, room issues, but not awfull”
text:
OK, on the whole this is an OK hotel, but a few things happend during my stay that bugged me, and if you read my other reviews it is clear that I am NOT someone that complains much. 
I was happy to get a great rate on Priceline for this hotel, but when I checked in I went up to our room, opened the door and there was a towel on the floor and the TV was on?? I thought I was barging in on someone so I had to yell "hello, hello" but the room was vacant. Looked like the cleaner failed to turn off the TV and left a dirty towel on the floor. Went to the "Dinning Room" for dinner, but the waiter walked us down the dinning room and through a door and sat us in the bar under a TV playing sports with no Explanation?? Other people were seated in there too and they also seem confused. I wanted to treat my wife to a nice dinner but ended up having pizza in the Pub! Yes I know I could of ordered off the main menu but why pay for a fancy meal if you have to eat it under a TV with some game I don't care about. Other than that it was prretty typical. I just get the impression that because most people probably only stay there one night before or after a flight, they don't worry about making you feel too comfortable. If you are booked into this hotel, don't worry, its fine, but I really did not feel it lived up to the Crowne Plaza name.

name: Hollywood Hills Hotel
title: “sehr entäuscht, aber typisch für America”
text: Rezeption war sehr unfreundlich konnte mir sehr wenig Auskunft geben. Das Zimmer war nicht sauber (Haare von Vorgänger, Staub, Lurch) Das Cafe das sehr gelobt wird ist nicht zu empfehlen außer man hat einen guten Magen. Auf Hygene wird hier nicht sehr geachtet. Das einzige gute war die Lage des Hotel, man war in 5 Minuten am Hollywood Blv und bei der Metro

name: Millennium Biltmore Hotel Los Angeles
title: “Ottimo ristorante”
text: Ho soggiornato in questo hotel 4 notti molto bello nell'hall bar e ristoranti un Po' meno nella stanza abbastanza andata con gli anni. Cmq nel complesso un hotel soddisfacente consigliatissimo il ristorante all'interno ottima cucina a prezzi davvero convenienti, per il parcheggio abbiamo usato un pubblico di fronte all'hotel 4 giorno 40 dollari. Infine la zona dove e' ubicato non e' un granché ma per chi ha un auto e ben collegato con le free way

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Great stay!”
text:
On checking in we asked for a room on a higher floor, we got it (26th floor). We requested in our booking a king sized bed, we got it. The bed was huge, lying in the middle you couldn't touch the sides. The bed was very good plenty of pillows - it was part of our honeymoon trip. We loved the view and in our jet-lagged state enjoyed watching the sun rise every morning from the bed. The curtains were left open for most of our 4 day stay.
It's the second time I have stayed here - the first time was for a large conference in 2010 - this time I got to see a little more of the hotel. Everything is contained within the building including several fast food outlets on the floors above the lobby.
At one stage we tried to get to the rooftop for a better view but ended up in the steak restaurant. Perhaps we got lost.
I can't remember the cost of wifi in the room but it was for free in the lobby. In fact if you go down to level 5 in the elevators and then walk down one level you get a very quiet booth seating area which still receives the free wifi signal from the lobby. It's a good airy bright quiet place to check your emails. There's also a small indoor circular track one floor below that level for running. The guest elevatots go from lobby level to level 5 - for the shops do it the old fashioned way and take the stairs.
Transport around this hotel is good - we went as far as taking a bus from Beverly Hills and it stops a block away from the hotel. Cool. I think the metro was 3 blocks away - but close to a Ralph's.
We had a door to an adjoining room which was kept locked. I guess the people in that room were on their honeymoon too.
There was one little attention to detail that I appreciated. I often leave my reading glasses next to the bed when I fall asleep. Housekeeping folded my glasses and put them back into my case for safe keping when refreshing the room. Thanks for that!

name: Sheraton Universal Hotel
title:
“Don't stay here.... No rooms are cleaned
And they had a power outage when we were on 12 th floor!”
text:
Awful
Need I say more? Checked in and walked into a filthy room with dirty towels on floor . 3 hours later .. They came
Up with fresh bedding and still never cleaned room
After 3 days, we ate the hotel
Stay ( we prepaid)and went to
Mariott Newport beach which was amazing .
Cost me a fortune to change hotels but had to. Sheraton is a business Quick stay not for a mom with a teenager.
Live and learn from our mistakeS

name: Custom Hotel
title: “Nice airport hotel”
text: The title says it all, this is a nice airport hotel. It's only a short drive from LAX and there's a free shuttle you can request by calling the hotel. The location isn't great if you're planning on sight seeing, as the hotel is of course situated near the airport and is a good 30-40 min drive from Beverly Hills. That said, there are buses which can get you to other tourist areas and city tours are available which will pick you up. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The rooms were modern and very clean. Nearby you have parking, a few shops including a large supermarket and a few restaurants, pretty much all you would ever need if just passing through.

name: Millennium Biltmore Hotel Los Angeles
title: “bellissimo hotel, se si sta nell'hotel.”
text: sono andato tra natale e capodanno a los angeles in questo albergo. si trova a downtown, che è un quartiere essenzialmente di uffici, per cui la sera ci si ritrova in un quartiere deserto, con negozi chiusi e pochissimi ristoranti, e dei pochi, la maggior parte sono fast food di scarsa qualità. l'hotel è bellissimo, un edificio degli anni 20, molto elegante, cosi come gli interni sono veramente ricercati e raffinati, di ottimo gusto, molto gradevoli e piacevoli. la stanza era molto luminosa, un ottimo bagno,il letto era enorme, televisione perfetta,molto pulita; i servizi sono funzionali e il personale molto gentile e disponibile. c'è anche un parcheggio,però spendendo la metà si può usare uno comunare di fronte all'hotel, al coperto e sorvegliato 24h/24. l'hotel è perfetto per chi ha una macchina e si muove, per chi viaggia in affari, (il wi-fi però si paga), ed è veramente un hotel elegante e di gusto, raffinato;peccato solo che si trova in una zona molto poco frequentata dal tardo pomeriggio in poi.comunque lo consiglio perchè noi ci siamo trovati benissimo.

name: Custom Hotel
title: “Kudos to Breanna”
text:
Breanna was superb. I was disappointed that Custom House did not provide the little perks that other Joie de Vivre hotels have such as wine flights or bath butlers. She was so concerned that she showed up at my room after check-in with a glass of wine. This gesture brightened my initial perception. Hats off to Custom House for employee empowerment.
Having Ralph 's next door and refrigerators in the rooms is a great convenience. Deck 33 is a fun place for drinks and appetizers were very good. All staff were cordial and made us feel at home. 
I would return to Custom House if my activities were in this area.

name: Holiday Inn Express Los Angeles-LAX Airport
title: “Great airport hotel”
text: For what it is, this hotel is great. This is by far the best Holiday Inn Express we have stayed in. It appears to have been another hotel before being adquired by HI as the property, inside and out, looks nothing like the typical HI. Staff was extremely pleasant and helpful. Room was large and comfortable. There was a business center with free internet and printing. The breakfast (included) was a full hot breakfast with eggs, ham, bacon, potatoes, muffins, bagels as well as fruit, yogurt and cereal. It is also very convenient to and from the airport . I would stay here again.

name: Figueroa Hotel
title: “Downtown Los Angeles”
text:
Auf unserem Kalifornien Roadtrip hatten wir auch Gelegenheit im Figueroa Hotel zu übernachten. Downtown LA bietet zwar nicht so viele Touristenattraktionen, wie Hollywood, aber für einen Zwischenstop im Herzen dieser riesen Metropole eignet sich dieses Hotel sehr gut. Es ist ganz im Südamerikanischen Stil gehalten und wunderbar eingerichtet. Auch ein Pool, sowie beheizter Whirlool gehören zum Hotel und laden in dieser sonst sehr lauten Stadt zum verweilen ein.
Für Besucher mit Ziel Hollywood würde ich jedoch ein Motel oder Hotel in Hollywood empfehlen.

name: Holiday Inn Express Los Angeles-LAX Airport
title: “Nothing special but serves purpose”
text: My friends and I stayed here after spending two nights at the Holiday Inn Express Walk of Fame. We moved here to be closer to the airport. Overall, there were no problems. The staff was friendly and helpful. The room was somewhat different than the previous location - the beds were regular size instead of queen and there was no refrigerator. Internet access was available but it was spotty. This hotel was older and it looked it. The carpet was hideous (although clean). The lobby could really benefit from redecorating. But, other than those trivial things, it was what we needed and it felt safe. The shuttle service was outstanding and available when we needed it at 4 am.

name: Coral Sands Motel
title: “Hotel Coral Sand Los Angeles”
text:
L'hôtel est sympa avec sa piscine, il y a un grand parking, les chambres sont grandes. Dommage que la salle de bain soit petite et qu'il n'y ait pas de petit déjeuner.
Un peu loin quand même de de la partie intéressante de Hollywood boulevard

name: Travelodge Hotel at LAX
title: “Albergo modesto ma vicinissimo all'aeroporto”
text:
Como ed economico, questo alberghetto situato nell'area dell'aeroporto di Los angeles. Per chi ha un volo la mattina presto, come noi, lo consiglio, anche se lascia a desiderare sia per la vetusta' della struttura che per le stanze, maleodoranti e non proprio pulitissime.Nel prezzo, deboo dire anche'esso modesto, rientrava anche la prima colazione, che non abbiamo potuto provare in quanto abbiamo lasciato l'hotel prima delle 6 a.m. per trovarci in tempo al check in.
Altra cosa da tenere in mente, questo albergo non ha ascensore, pertanto se prendete la stanza al piano rialzato, dovrete trasportarle su per le scale,percio' provate a prenotare una stanza piano terra. Il personale a dire il vero è stato molto gentile sia al check in che alla partenza. Offrono anche un servizio navetta sia da/verso l'aeroporto che da/verso l'autonoleggio ed anche questa è una comodita' non da poco. Penso che per una notte possa anche starci.

name: Inn at Venice Beach
title: “This hotel is awesome! Awesome customer service, awesome location, awesome awesome awesome!”
text: Martin is the man, so nice and accomidating, rooms were so cute, so close to the beach! I am coming back here to stay when in Venice! I am from Las Vegas so I know hotels! The rooms were clean and the continental breakfast was great! Loved the little court yard for eating and the people there are awesome! If you come to Venice beach you should definatley get a room here!

name: Custom Hotel
title: “Good spot near LAX”
text: Enjoyed my spacious room with views over the airport. Breakfast buffet was tasty. Daniel Hirsch was very accomodating and pleasant to deal with. Would recommend for a more interesting stay close to the airport.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites LAX
title: “Perfect place to stay near airport if you have early/late flight”
text: This was my second stay at La Quinta LAX. I take one trip to LA from the east coast each year and always take a late flight that gets me in after 10pm PT, so I always spend my first night in LA at an airport hotel before moving on to my final destination in California. This hotel is close to the airport, very clean and comfortable and provides a free continental breakfast so that you can grab something on your way out in the morning. I usually take the free shuttle from the airport to the hotel and then I get my rental car in the morning. Depending on what car rental company I'm using, I either take the shuttle back to the airport in the morning and then get the appropriate car rental shuttle, or if I'm renting from Fox. It's within walking distance of the hotel, so that is really convenient as well. There is 24 hour McDonalds right next to the hote for late night snacks. The area the hotel is in is not all that great, but neither are ANY of the airport hotels I've stayed in near LAX. I would highly recommend this hotel for a 1-nighter. It's under $100, it's conveniently located and it's clean. Waiting for the shuttle at the airport can sometimes take 15 minutes or so which is a drag when it's late and you've been flying all day, but other than that, I have no complaints.

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Great..slightly expensive!”
text:
I've camped at this hotel for over 5 months now and found this a great place to stay at along with some other downtown hotels I've reviewed earlier. Expensive, if you dont have a priceline price or a govt rate. Else, this place is super comfortable.
Well appointed rooms, the beds and linens - nice, great newly done bathrooms etc. Onsite restaurants that are open until 10pm, food that you may not find anywhere else nearby if you decided to eat a late dinner. 
Some of the previous reviewers have mentioned bedbugs here. I,ve never been putup in a room with one though so I would doubt those claims.
The downside..noisy elevators if your room happens to be close to one. In a nutshell, I'd always stay here if in the area..

name: Hilton Los Angeles Airport
title: “An airport hotel that meeds your needs”
text:
I stayed at this hotel because I had a 6:30 am flight the following day. We arrived during what appeared to be a Filipino event. First, protestors convened in front of the hotel while other Filipino merry-goers flooded the hotel lobby. Fortunately, as a Gold HHonors member, there is a dedicated check-in making the process swift and efficient. We received a room on the tenth floor which also happened to be their updated floor. 
Soft carpets cover the entire room while granite countertops can be found in the bathroom. This is my first time here so I can't compare it with un-renovated floors. Nonetheless, the room contained basic amenities: coffee maker, fridge, cable TV. 
The hotel is home to a plethora of dining options. We opted for the restaurant because it seemed the most quiet from the cacophony of the events going on. The menu featured modern entrees such as seared salmon with cherry tomatoes and asparagus. For $25, one can also opt for the buffet, but I didn't have a chance to see what it offered. 
The room afforded a really amazing view of one of LAX's runways. Although the jet noise presented some noise problems, it didn't really bother us too much. Furthermore, after 10 pm, there weren't nearly as many flights. 
At $109/night, it's a very reasonable price. Proximity to LAX cannot be beat. The hotel is located on Century Blvd and is a few minutes drive to the terminals. 
I don't know when I would stay at the Hilton Airport again, but if I ever had an early flight, it would be my first choice.

name: Super 8 Los Angeles / Culver City Area
title: “Sehr schönes Motel”
text:
Wir verbrachten im September 2012 zwei Nächte im Super 8.
Ich muss ehrlich sagen, dass ich vorher etwas skeptisch war, da ich schon in ein paar Super 8 ware und die Qualität sehr schwankte.
Bei unserer Sucher fuhren wir direkt erstmal an der Einfahrt vorbei. Es ist etwas unscheinbar und wenn man sich auf den Verkehr konzentriert, nicht sofort erkennbar.
Es waren sehr viele Parkplätze vorhanden und wir konnten bequem wählen.
In der Rezeption war ein sehr freundlicher Mann, der unsere Reservierung zügig bearbeitet und auch das Storno unserer 3. Nacht sofort und ohne murren eintrug.
Wir waren im oberen Stockwerk untergebracht und als ich die Zimmertür öffnete, war ich doch sehr überrascht. Das Zimmer war rießig, extrem sauber und sehr nett eingerichtet. Wie gesagt, ich hatte mich auf schlimmeres eingerichtet.
Wir verbrachten zwei sehr ruhige Nächte in einem sehr bequemen Bett. Das Frühstück war jetzt nichts besonderes, aber immerhin mit Waffeln, Zimtschnecken, Obst, Kaffee, verschiedenen Säften und einer Auswahl von Müslis ganz Ok. Vor allem die Waffeln mit Sirup schmeckten gut.
Die Lage fanden wir eigenlich ganz gut, da man schnell in Venice, Hollywood und Bell Air war und dazu die Fahrt nach Downtown und Disney Land soch in grenzen hielt.
Für Los Angeles eigentlich typisch, braucht man aber natürlich ein AUto, da zu Fuß von dort nichts zu erreichen ist.

name: Super 8 Los Angeles / Culver City Area
title: “era quello che ci aspettavamo, pure meglio!”
text: camere grandi.. Cmq nello standard Usa, personale ok carino e cortese, park ok molti posti, prenotato con booking.com senza sorprese, spazio colazione molto carino, semplicissimo, ma piccolo angolo in dehore soleggiato con anche pochi tavolini fuori. Siamo stati 4 gg all'arrivo, e abbiamo prenotato con booking.com sempre.. un altro g alla fine del tour usa x il ritorno a casa dal lax. Baricentrico per un po' tutto. E' cmq in uno stradone con pochi negozi.. Ma stica..

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “I enjoyed it... but colleagues had issues”
text:
I did not have any problems, but two of my colleagues did.
The hotel is extremely nice, clean, well appointed and the food was very good. There also seemed to be quite a few employees around the lobby directing guests.
(Note: I've only stayed at 3 LAX hotels) The hotel lobby is far less crowded than the LAX Hilton and it is much nicer than either the Hilton or the Four Points by Sheraton around the corner.
Parking is $25 per day and they have some sort of airport parking (3 day minimum) for $16 a day. The airport version of the parking is a few bucks more than other airport parking which looks like $13-$15 from the signs around. The advantage is that the airport shuttle runs VERY often. When I was sitting in the lobby for 10 minutes working on my computer the shuttle came twice!
I only had lunch and dinner here. Lunch was amazing but breakfast was just ok. A colleague of mine had dinner here and she said that dinner was awesome.
Two of my colleagues had problems with their rooms. One could not find his reservation, which could have been his own fault because his name was mis-spelled. On the other hand, my other colleague got a call from the front desk at midnight demanding that he check out of his room immediately. This was ridiculous, because he only checked in a few hours earlier....!!! Needless to say he was extremely upset.
If I was given the choice and the price was similar, I would MUCH rather stay here as opposed to the Hilton or Four Points, which are the only other hotels at LAX which I've stayed at.
Basically, better shuttle service from LAX, not nearly as crowded, excellent food.

name: Crowne Plaza Los Angeles International Airport Hotel
title: “I'll never stay at this hotel again!”
text:
After a tiring flight from Winnipeg to Los Angeles, I needed to rest for 7 hours before my long haul flight to Malaysia. I went to Travelers Aid at LAX and leafed through their folder for a hotel which had a hot tub because my back was killing me and I really needed to relax before my 16 hour flight to Malaysia. Travelers Aid was very helpful and called several hotels that advertised hot tubs. When Crowne Plaza was contacted, they informed Travelers Aid that their hot tub was working so I checked in with them. The room was okay so I took a nap, had dinner, and then changed to check out the hot tub. That's when I received my rude shock. The so-called working hot tub was cordoned off with yellow warning tape, like a scene from CSI, and when I crawled beneath the tape and dunked my toes into the water, it was freezing cold! I thought perhaps it wasn't turned on so I turned it on. The bubbles came up but the water remained cold while I sat beside the freezing "hot" tub for 15 minutes, shivering my butt off! I went upstairs, completely distressed, and complained to the front office, who, instead of apologizing for it, blamed Travelers Aid, who had done absolutely nothing wrong. Later, when I checked out, they wouldn't look me in the eye and were quite rude when I tried to get my valuables out of the safe deposit box. They wouldn't help me when I told them I didn't know how to work the funky box and finally, after shoving around, I managed to get it open.
Please do not stay at this dump!

name: Hollywood Hotel
title: “Niente di eccezionale”
text: Prezzo molto buono, in posizione decentrata... e cmq a LA ci si muove solo in macchina. Fermata della metro vicina... ma no fatevi ingannare dal nome, per arrivare agli Studios ci vuole un po di tempo, anche se in modo comodo, sfruttando la metro.

name: Custom Hotel
title: “Wish we stayed longer.”
text:
The place opened a few weeks before we got there. Some very cool, trendy, modern decor and concept. We liked the place, the neighborhood, and proximity to other locations.
The pool area is very cool.
We can't wait to go back and stay a bit longer.

name: Super 8 Los Angeles / Culver City Area
title: “bonne surprise”
text:
petit motel qui ne paye pas de mine, par contre dès que vous entrez dans la chambre, c'est super. Très grandes chambres avec coin repas micro onde, cafetière et réfrigérateur. 
Petit dej possible au lobby. Bien situé pour profiter de santa monica à des tarifs abordables. Centre commercial de westefield à portée de voiture.

name: Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Great old time Hollywood hotel.”
text: My wife and I stay here about 5 times a.year. we have tried other hotels in the area but for us when we want a Hollywood experience the Roosevelt is the place. The large main lobby is very relaxing and the evening pool parties are open to tenants, you never now who you will see here! Located mid point on Hollywood blvd most clubs / theaters are either a short walk or cab ride away .. the great service throughout keeps us coming back over.and over again. We also enjoy the malts and onion rings at 25 degrees. ;-)

name: Crowne Plaza Los Angeles International Airport Hotel
title: “Good Stay”
text: We stayed four nights here. The staff was friendly and helpful, and the breakfast buffet delicious. The average-sized rooms were cleaned daily. If you're renting a car, parking is $11 a day. Near the airport, but noise is no problem.

name: Days Inn Hollywood/Universal Studios
title: “Nicht unser Favorit”
text:
Das gebuchte Zimmer für 3 Personen war viel zu klein.
Vorhandene Stühle mussten entfernt werden, damit überhaupt Platz für Koffer war. Frühstück auch für amerikanische Verhältnisse mehr als dürftig. Dazu sehr wenig Platz im Frühstücksraum, teilweise Wartezeit auf freien Tisch.
Die Umgebung des Hotels ist leider auch nicht besonders gut. Für einen nächsten Aufenthalt in LA würden wir auf keinen Fall wieder Hollywood wählen.

name: Inn at Venice Beach
title: “Schönes Strandhotel”
text: familiäres Hotel mit sehr gutem Service, Frühstück inclusive aber ist natürlich nichts Besonderes. Touren, Stadtrundfahrten für Los Angeles im Haus buchbar. Sehr freundlich. Alles in allem sehr empfehlenswert.

name: Days Inn Hollywood/Universal Studios
title: “Bien situado, buen servicio, calidad media”
text:
El hotel está muy bien situado, a menos de 5 minutos del paseo de la Fama, a la altura del Madame Tussouds, Teatro Kodak, Teatro Chino, El Capitán, y rodeado de tiendas de souvenirs y servicios como los autobuses turísticos, taxis, metro o un rent a car.
La calidad de nuestra habitación era un poco básica, destacando como carencias la calidad del colchón y humedades en la pared del cuarto de baño. Había un mueble cajonera que alojaba la televisión, colocado delante del armario empotrado, lo que dificultaba el acceso a éste.
El hotel carece de ascensor, y, aunque nuestra habitación estaba en planta baja, había que subir unas escaleras y no había rampa para minusválidos (o no la vimos), lo cual, si vas cargado de maletas, es un inconveniente.
El desayuno es gratuito, aunque el espacio reservado para ello es bastante pequeño, con lo que hay horas en las que no quedan mesas libres; en temporada alta debe ser un problema.
Hay empleados que hablan castellano, como la chica de los desayunos, aunque alguna recepcionista no lo habla. Destacar la atención de un chico latino, cuyo nombre no supimos, que se portó de maravilla, ayudándonos en todo lo posible. Solo sabemos que era estudiante de teología, desde aquí un saludo.

name: Sheraton Universal Hotel
title: “Plusses and Minuses”
text: This was my 2nd or 3rd visit to this property and my first since the renovation. Even as a repeat visitor, it's hard to find the entrance to this hotel. Staff check in was fast and friendly. I was upgraded to an "Executive" room which was basically a large junior suite. The room had nice/new Sheraton furnishings, but the new-ish flatscreen tv was way too small for the room/the way it was positioned (too far from the bed or sofa to see). The main problem with the hotel in the guest room as well as in the Terrace Room where I attended a cocktail reception was the lack of functioning A/C. I think the management is aware of this issue (as evidenced by the fan placed in the room at check in). The room wasn't terrible, but the ballroom was unbearable. People were sweating in their gowns and suits and constantly stepping out to breathe. Room service was fast and delicious. The lobby bar was a great place to catch up with an old friend. Good beers on tap, great cocktails, good service. Valet was fast. The only other problem (potentially a deal breaker if you're here on vacation) is that the elevators were woefully below the hotel's capacity. I'd wait 5-10 minutes on average. (To be fair, there were 2 events in the hotel and it was a busy Saturday night) but a trip to/from your room shouldn't take 20 minutes.

name: Days Inn Hollywood/Universal Studios
title: “Sentralt til det meste som en familie ønsker å se”
text: Meget sentralt, bra basseng, litt små rom til familie på 5,vi bodde her både i begynnelsen og slutten på ferien, hyggelig stab, ok frokost inkl i prisen, god parkering i kjelleren. Noe slitt. Sentralt ift Universal, The Getty Center, Six Flaggs Magic Mountain (berg & dalbaner), Kodak Theatre, Hollywoood Walk of Fame, etc, etc.

name: Inn at Venice Beach
title: “Great location”
text:
I picked this hotel as a place to recover after a flight from Australia to LA. We also stayed again for 2 nights at the end of our trip. It was close to the airport and only a quick 15minute drive. The staff were very nice and allowed us to check in early at 11am. 
We got the same room both stays and the room was cold and smelt like cigarette smoke which I thought was unusual for a non-smoking room. 
The free breakfast and free wireless internet were great. 
They don't have any room service or restaurants here but head away from the beach for one block and you'll find an amazing italian restaurant with the yummiest garlic bread.
It's only 2 blocks away from the beach and was a really good spot to stay so we could skate along the beach.

name: Custom Hotel
title: “Great trip, cool people”
text: Had a great time at the Custom Hotel. Spent a week here! The staff was crazy good. As soon as we got there the girl at the front desk (Chelsea I think) took her time asking us about our trip to LA, had we been there before, etc etc. Gave us some suggestions about where to go, what to do, what to eat at the hotel bar (Coconut shrimp, AMAZING!) Bar33 was fantastic. The bartenders Odey and Sean were awesome! Great service, very talkative and fun. They even stayed open late one night because people were having such a good time there. Pool area was nice and chill and right off of the bar. Cleaning staff was always smiling and polite. Would love to come back. Location was cool as well, just about 15 minutes from everything. Also, I wanted to take the bed home. The Coffee Bean on corner of the street=awesome!

name: Embassy Suites LAX North
title: “Really nice hotel for the value.”
text: Really nice hotel for the value. The complimentary breakfast and managers reception was a nice treat. The suites were really nice and having the two rooms made the experience much better for a 3 night stay.

name: Hollywood Celebrity Hotel
title: “great value”
text: very close to major tourist sights. excellent service by friendly and helpfull staff. rooms large and comfy as well as clean. would definately recommend to friends and family. have no hesitation in staying here again.

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “Consistently good value and very convenient if need to be in and out of LAX”
text: Stayed here twice this week, had stayed here several times before. It continues to be very well run, and extremely good value. Seems that it is priced much lower than several other major hotels which are just slightly closer to the LAX terminals. It is well with the extra few minutes on the shuttle or in your rental car, since it is comfortable and very good value. I will continue to stat here whenever I am in LA and need to stay near the airport.

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Beverly Hills
title: “Amazing Service”
text:
Wow this place is so great, the service here is one of a kind!
Thanks everyone!

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites LAX
title: “Prima hotel voor an one night stay”
text: Dit hotel is goed bereikbaar vanaf LAX met een shuttle. Vriendelijk en behulpzaam personeel. Ruime kamers met voldoende facilliteiten en schoon. Goede prijs/kwaliteit verhouding. Minpuntje: 3 liften is wat krap als iedereen 's morgens naar boven/beneden wil.

name: Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “The Perfect Stay”
text:
Arrived super early (8.15am) and by 10.30am a room was ready for me. Great size with a view overlooking the rear entrance (perfect for me as I wanted somewhere quiet). Location was fantastic - across from Grauman's Chinese Theatre and only one subway stop to Universal Studios.
Public Kitchen had great food and the bar staff were very helpful and friendly.
Had a great stay, the only glitch was the cafe 25 Degrees. 25 degrees was pretty ordinary. Who serves eggs without toast? An extra $4 for toast is outrageous. And only one of the wait staff was friendly, the rest were downright unhelpful.
I'd recommend the Roosevelt to anyone.

name: Renaissance Los Angeles Airport Hotel
title: “It is a nice category 4 marriott hotel”
text: Considering it is an airport hotel, it is nice and comfortable. We used our marriott certificate stay there. It is worth it. It is near the airport and shuttle is convienent. And we also get upgrade to a junior suite. Next time I need to stay in LAX, I will definitely choose this hotel.

name: Hyatt Regency Century Plaza
title: “Good location - Great Service!”
text: There was so much that was great about this hotel. The rooms are very nice, clean and well appointed. The staff are all professional and courteous. We did a large event there and everyone from the sales manager to the bartender to the servers went above any beyond my expectations. There was never a "no" to be heard. Since we were working through the day, the kindly brought us the room service menu in the ballroom and took our orders there - this has never been my experience at a large hotel like this. Would highly recommend for business or pleasure. The spa is also terrific! Overnight parking is too much!

name: Venice Beach Suites & Hotel
title: “Excellent Location!”
text:
We spent 1 night in Venice Beach after a drive down the PCH! Venice Beach Suites & Hotel was a perfect spot to stay. We would definitely stay here again. The hotel staff is super friendly & the room was perfect. Wish we had known how wonderful it was & would have planned to stay longer. Our only regret was the uncooperative weather - it was foggy & cold.
Hope to plan a trip here again.

name: Holiday Inn Express West Los Angeles
title: “So central, yet so inexpensive”
text:
I have to admit that I was a little concerned about staying in this location, as it's on the intersection of Santa Monica Boulevard and the entrance and exit ramps of the 405 Freeway! But I needn't have worried. Once inside the hotel, you cannot hear the outside noise.
Our room was basic as all HIE's are, but it was very clean and tidy, and the bed and pillows were very comfortable. The breakfast offered is basic, but complimentary none the less, and free WIFI is available to all guests. The hotel provides on-site underground parking for only $10 per night.
The location actually makes moving around very easy. There is a bus service leaving opposite the hotel which will take you to Santa Monica Pier for only $1, the freeway is on your doorstep if you are driving, and entry and exit to the hotel is surprising easy.
For a low budget, clean, comfortable and convenient hotel, this is the one!

name: Venice Beach Suites & Hotel
title: “Perfect place to stay in Venice & LA!”
text: The hotel is literally on the boardwalk! Overlooking the famous Venice Beach. You could not be any closer without getting wet!! It is located right in the heart of Venice Beach. Street performers and stallholders perform outside your window. This however is not obtrusive as it only takes place during "office hours". We were just yards from the famous "Muscle beach" and Bodybuilding "Pen"! We could see all the action from our window. "Speedway" runs the length of the beach giving vehicular access to the rear of the hotel. There was no long stay parking on site but parking on the streets nearby was convenient and free, with very helpful advice and a map provided by the hotel staff. The hotel is old and not what you may be used to if you stay regularly at large upmarket places. However we had just been on a 5 star cruise and stayed for 4 days at a very upmarket Vegas Suite and in comparison the Venice Beach Hotel was perfectly satisfactory! It was clean and offered everything that we needed. The rooms were spacious and offered "efficiencies" (fully equiped kitchen). They were in fact mini suites or "condos". The bedroom was spacious with a comfortable bed, good lighting and effective window blinds as well as plenty of closet (wardrobe) storage space and furniture. There was a ceiling fan and tv with dvd player and free local call telephone. Also complimentary (100% free wi-fi Internet access). The kitchen had microwave, fridge, cooker, etc and a dining table. The bathroom was spacious. Staff were very helpful and courteous, helping to plan days out and offering us maps etc. Venice is a wonderful place to spend a vacation but it is also ideally located for all of LA! Just minutes from LAX airport and easy to find if you are driving. Very close to Santa Monica and handy for Hollywood and downtown. It is safe and relatively inexpensive. Venice itself offers the legendary beach, with nice sands and surf. The amazing entertainmant of the boardwalk performers and vendors as well as all the history and canals. I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again next time we visit LA! Highly recommended!!

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Beverly Hills
title: “Very pleasant Thanksgiving stay”
text:
Just got back from a 4-night stay here and it was very comfortable. We had an inner-courtyard room, which was preferable since I am not a good sleeper away from home and always hear every noise. This trip, I was able to sleep without ear plugs every night--no problem. 
I chose this hotel on the basis of room type (wanted a kitchen), location (on the edge of Beverly Hills and on Pico--which is a reasonable east-west route through LA) and price. My intent was to cook Thanksgiving dinner. My mistake was not recognizing that the rooms have no ovens! So I modified our plans and it still worked out well.
It's nice to be able to roll downstairs in the am and eat breakfast. They had a fairly standard breakfast buffet with cereal, fruit, yogurt, make-your-own-waffles, pastries, bagels. They also had scrambled eggs and some type of meat (sausage, ham). One day they had someone doing omelets, but not the other 3 days. We also went to one afternoon reception, where they had burgers and beer/wine.
I used the small exercise room one day to run, which worked out well. They have 2 treadmills and a couple of bikes, along with some free weights and a weight machine.
Parking was self-park or valet. We chose self-park and it was fine and cost $22/nt.
Finally, one thing I really noticed--the staff was very friendly. They always said hello with a smile, I don't usually pay attention to this, but it was distinctly noticeable.
I would stay here again. It met our specific needs nicely.

name: Holiday Inn Express West Los Angeles
title: “Nothing Special, Decient”
text: Rooms are Ok...all entries are from outside....free parking....neighborhood not the greatest, but I wasn't in fear for my life....

name: Crowne Plaza Beverly Hills
title: “Totally Disappointed!”
text: I've booked a room because of its name : Crowne Plaza, but what I found was a terrible Hotel. The room was dirty and smelly. I asked in the front desk for another room but they did not have one at that moment. On my 3rd day, the bathtub starts to flood. I asked again for another room and what I got was another dirty and smelly room, stained towels, smelly pillows, used band-aid in the floor...On the check out I have filled the guest survey but never had an answer for my complains...so...I would not stay here if someone paid me to!

name: Hollywood Celebrity Hotel
title: “Perfect for tourists”
text:
My partner and I travelled from Australia and had been advised of the great value of this hotel, and we weren't let down at all. We chose this location because we wanted to see Hollywood, and we truly could not have picked a better hotel. 
It is close to the main attractions, tours, shopping, restaurants so the location couldn't be better. 
The staff were extremely friendly and helpful, not just on arrival, but any time we approached them, even if we were just passing through reception.
Lovely room, free wi-fi, cable and breakfast. 
Highly recommend this hotel!

name: Hilton Los Angeles Airport
title: “Better than average airport hotel but still an airport hotel”
text:
At times, when I transferred in LAX, I stayed at this hotel. 
Our company has a very competitive price at this hotel. so value wise, positive for me.
Room itself is clean but you can tell it is tired and at areas you can sense a make over of old / cheaper materials. You can smell smoking occasionally in some rooms / floors that are supposed to non smoking rooms. I do not like that but can understand it will be difficult to catch offenders in this kind of high turnaround hotels.
A lounge at 18th(?) floor is available for premier HHonor members. Not a whole lot of selections in its continental buffet, weak compared to several other Hilton properties I have stayed.
I would give it 3.5 star. Better than average airport hotel but still an airport hotel.

name: Renaissance Los Angeles Airport Hotel
title: “Very nice airport hotel.”
text: I've stayed at this hotel a half dozen times over last few years and have always found it to be a quality hotel. Rooms are clean and updated and include a safe in the closet. Very close to LAX airport makes it convenient for early morning departures. Quality windows keep traffic and aircraft noise to acceptable levels. Nice gym and pool area. Lobby area has this funky new age music playing that is to loud and annoying. The bath towels on this last trip seemed thin and worn.

name: Crowne Plaza Beverly Hills
title: “It could offer more”
text: I stayed at the Crown Plaza Beverly Hills for 4 nights and the only thing I can say is that it was just ok. When booking the room, I asked for an early check-in, if possible (at 12:30 PM, instead of the regular 3:00 PM). Arriving there, my room wasn’t ready and they didn’t make too much effort to find me another one, so ok, I went out to have lunch and, returning after 3:00 PM the room was available and fine. Next day, I went down to have breakfast and they told me that I had booked a room with continental breakfast. So, if I wanted to have the hot dishes (full breakfast) I would have to pay extra USD 5. Ok again, USD 5 is not much, but I think it was ridiculous that they booked a room with continental breakfast, if they had full breakfast available. Ok, I could have paid the extra 5 bucks, but why didn’t they include it in the room rate? I found it very constraining that waiter had to check what I had for breakfast in order to issue the bill. For this kind of details, I guess it was just ok.

name: Crowne Plaza Beverly Hills
title: “A comfortable stay”
text:
I was here for two nights in June: my second stay at the Crowne Plaza. I found it to be very comfortable both stays, and since I often have business nearby will undoubtably stay again.
Check in went well, and the desk staff was very helpful. My rooms both times were as requested, and were large, with nice views, lots of light, very comfortable beds, a lounger and an ottoman, and well-apppointed bathrooms, wireless that worked well, quiet.....no complaints, though I agree with those that say that the breakfast is so-so here. However, it is walking distance from several other restaurants. The location is quite convienent for west side activities.
A good value for what you get and for Beverly Hills; recommended.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “Service/ service/ service”
text:
From the moment we checked in the forien exchange student with no personality, to the filthy room that we had to move out of, to the beuitfull resteraunt with no service and at best average food. It was disapointing because when we stayed here in october it perfect. My daughter is going to school in La in fall and your hotell made perfect since i guess we have to look else where.
GARY TURENNE ROOM 338

name: W Hollywood
title: “Good!”
text:
I looking at the rest of the reviews, a common topic was 'party hotel' wherein the lobby turned into a party; the concierge turned into bouncers. Another common theme- an apparent aloofness among the staff, especially with valet. Yet another common theme was plenty of noise- especially from unruly guests. 
I didn't find any of these common themes to be accurate- that isn't to say the people who posted those comments are wrong, it is to say that it is apparent that the W Hollywood is trying to change their market. I hope so- the party scene doesn't fit the Starwood culture (but if it drives occupancy and rate, well.....<shrug>). 
I was at the W for a lodging industry conference- the hotel performed very well- in all respects. One thing I do recommend- GM or Rooms Director- start replying to these Tripadvisor comments. It looks as if in the past some good reviews were commented upon, but we know incosistency is not the way to go. If group business is what you're after, planners (especially independents) use Tripadvisor a lot to look for commonalities in these hotel reviews.

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Beverly Hills
title: “Convenent location, good value.”
text: We stayed for a week and have stayed here previously. It is very functional, however limited in relation to a resort feel, i don't think its trying to potray a resort feel, just thought is was worth mentioning. The free breakfast helps keep costs down, as this is L.A. and a simple breakfast somewhere can run $10+/person. The valet parking is very conveinent and the attendants are very prompt. Rooms are very large with small kitchenttes, making longer stays more bearable.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “This place sure knows how to make you smile”
text: I was traveling with my husband and two small children. We had gotten in an accident and was shaken up by it all day. When we finally got to our hotel, we were treated with wonderful costumer service the moment we walked in the door. The front service desk was kind, quick and easy, we also had help right away with our bags and everything we had in our car since it was towed. Our mood changed from being sad and worried to being relaxed and happy as if we were on a vacation. The best part was speaking to the hotel manager named Justin because he took the time to give us a call and to let us know that we will be taken care of and he stood by his words. Our day turn from traumatic to an anmazing fun family night! Thanks to Four Point by Sheraton and Justin! We will be staying there again.

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “Great stay after long flight”
text: The Westin LAX is a terrific hotel. It was very close to the airport and the shuttle service was easy to use. Check in was fast and efficient and we checked in at 11:00 am as we had just arrived after a long flight from Australia and were very tired. The king room we had requested was not available but they were able to give us two doubles which we grabbed in a flas. We arrived in the room and immediately hit the beds and were in dreamland for 3 hours. The beds are "heavenly".We later sat in the lobby and relaxed. great place to people watch. Pool area is nice and the gym is great for workouts. It was surprisingly very quiet during the night considering the proximity to the airport. We had breakfast in the restaurant the next morning and the quality of the food was very good with prompt and personal service. We will definitely be back.

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Great downtown hotel!”
text: Wow! Starting to really love priceline. Scored big on this very nice downtown hotel with all the amenities you'd hope to find, for $87.nt, when everywhere else was asking for at least twice that. My room was on the small side, but nicely done and the bed was awesome. The hotel itself is an atrium style downtown highrise, complete with glass elevators and indoor fountains. Check in was pleasant and efficient. I needed a one night stay somewhere nice, specifically in a downtown LA location, and feel that I got what I asked for and more.

name: Hollywood Celebrity Hotel
title: “If you have to stay in Hollywood then this is a convienient, cheap & friendly place.”
text:
This was our second stay in Hollywood, thankfully only a quick overnight stop this time! My Hubby, Mum & Dad found the Celebrity Hollywood Hotel to be in an extremley convienient location, minutes walk to Mann's Chinese Theatre and all the tourist spots but in a quiet side road behind the Hollywood/Highland Centre with limited noise and friendly/helpful staff.
The art deco interior is a nice touch, the rooms however are in need of modernisation. Although they are massive (to say the least) the bathrooms are shabby with poor shower facilities, old tired towels and the beds are not the most comfortable. 
Have said all this you have to remember this is Hollywood and you don't get much for your $ dollar so the fact that a reasonable continental breakfast was included, there was free internet access at a stand alone PC in the lobby and they made an effort with availability of gym/leisure equipment you can't really fault the place!
Also there is a lovely patio with chairs/tables out front of the hotel which we found to be a great suntrap in the morning.
The staff at the Celebrity Hollywood Hotel really make the place what it is, they are very friendly and always willing to assist. They even stored our luggage for us all day even after we had checked out as we had a late evening flight..

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Beverly Hills
title: “Great Place!!!”
text:
I am a Gold Elite member with Marriott, and travel quite a bit. The service received at the Residence Inn Beverly Hills was superb! Everyone from the reception area, to the breakfast and valet were polite, cordial and extremely helpful!
The room I was in was very clean, quiet and plenty of room. Almost too much room for one person! The hershey's chocolate at check in- being Gold- was a nice little touch.
I will be back soon!

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “Comfortable and affordable”
text: Westin LAX was a very comfortable stay with all amenties nearby and proximity to the airport and southern beaches alike. It has a comfortable pool and spa with a good fitness center. The business center and lounge even though small is perfect for ones need. It is a very comfortable business-leisure hotel in LA.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “Not good for Business Travellers”
text: The room was small and the internet connection was very very slow. If you are a business traveller DO NOT STAY AT THIS HOTEL. There is free wireless internet, but the connection was so slow that it wasnt worth it. The room was very small with no room to spread out.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Hollywood Hills Hotel
title: “Good Value”
text:
We were planning thow to see the Cirque show so we decided to stay in Hollywood. We are from San Diego so we know Hollywood is a little rough but we wanted to walk to the Kodak Theatres and see the sites on the way. So we read TA reviews and booked this hotel.
I don't think the parking is free anymore but we found a parking spot right next to the hotel. We were planning to pay for parking but this spot was literally next door. So I think we saved 12.00. The lobby has many pictures hanging of famous actors and was going for the old Hollywood Vibe.
The hotel is in rectangle shape with the pool in the middle. Our room was on the bottom floor and when we entered the room we were surprised with all of the art they had up. It was similiar to the lobby but they had even cooler pictures, some were even new like Harry Potter and old like the Beatles.
We were able to walk all the way to the Kodak Theatres from our hotel and see everything on the way and get some good food. Maybe a mile or two. It was a little seedy until we actually got to Hollywood Boulevard, which is funny to say because the Boulevard is a litte seedy. What I really mean is unlike the Boulevard where there is traffic and stores, where we walked, it did not have alot of pedestrians walking around. If my husband was not there, I probably wouldn't have walked by myself (even though I know I would have because I would convince myself not be a wimp).
I didn't get to eat at the restaurant because we were going to try out this awesome breakfast place down the road.
If you want to cheap hotel close to Hollywood Boulevard this is it. 
I am more of a people watcher person so I would probably stay more on the boulevard if I had too this again but that would also cost about about $100 more.

name: Hilton Los Angeles Airport
title: “Nip Tuck?”
text:
Have you ever run into someone who you knew in their youth, but had not seen for some years? That's how I felt about my recent stay at the the Hilton LAX. I still recognised the vibrant hotel I once knew, but could see its age, the years having taken their toll. 
I must say that the spirit was still there. The staff were fantastic; friendly, helpful and considerate. But the signs of age were hard to miss. The rooms felt tired. Old fixtures, large boxy CRT televisions, no mini bar and an "oldish" phone. Some of the floors (the pool level) had a lingering cigarette smoke odour. 
As with many hotels, like the Hilton, it seems the more you pay for a room, the more you'll be asked to pay for extras. Internet? $13.00 a day (even if you get 7 days as a package). A warm soft drink from the machine in the hall? $3.00. Park your car? $20.00 a day. Print a colour page from the computer? About $5.00.
Of course, all these things don't make the hotel bad. I'd stay again. It's location is great. Service is top notch and the rooms are comfortable. The weight room is modern and large. And the outdoor pool and spas are heated. The water pressure in the bathroom showers was surprising refreshing! If there is a water shortage anywhere in the Western USA, I'd look to the Hilton as a possible cause. 
The hotel is relatively well soundproofed, although you will know when planes are taking off if your room is located on the East-facing side. 
So, like an old friend, you can forgive some of the lines around the eyes. But it may be time for the Hilton LAX to "have some work done". They are in L.A. after all.

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “Fantastic Staff”
text: I needed a hotel near LAX and chose The Westin since it was close and the rate was good. I liked the Westin more than others near the airport right away because it's located on a slightly quieter strip of Century Blvd. The valet parking/bellmen were incredibly friendly, welcoming and kind. Robert brought my bags to my room and told me about all the various hotel amenties. He was genuine, warm, and friendly and made me feel so welcome. He printed out my boarding pass for me and also some local information I needed. I had a bit of a mix-up with my car rental company in dropping it off at the hotel, and Noe and Raul, especially Noe, went out of their way to help me out. They called the rental company, had my bill faxed over so I could see a copy, and provided me with information about LA. I didn't interact much with the front desk staff. They were fine but not the level of warmth of the front door staff. My room was pleasant enough, but nothing special. The best things about this Westin were the front door staff and it's location near LAX but not quite so busy and hard to get to as the other hotels (also on the free LAX shuttle, which is nice). The signage getting into the hotel needs improvement - I totall missed it and had to go around the block. A friend meeting me there at the same problem. Also cabs were blocking the cab wating area and wouldn't move so cars could not get by, but that was a cab and not a hotel issue.

name: Hilton Los Angeles Airport
title: “Needs updating”
text:
I stay at this hotel several times a year when I need to be near LAX for an early morning flight out. There are many hotels near LAX. This Hilton is really no better or worse than many of the other full-service hotels in the area. 
Room service and the restaurant are good. The work out facility, while well equipped, is in the basement---meaning there is no view. Not that the view from the upper floors is great (well, if you like to look at planes taking off and landing, then it is good). 
The front desk staff is extremely efficient, quite kind and very accommodating. And, most importantly, they are quick. The check in process is the star of this property.
My only real complaint about this Hilton is that the rooms are looking really tired (Ok, for many this is a big issue). They still have tube TVs sitting on tired furniture, the bath fixtures look like they were installed in the Carter Administration and the carpets are well past their prime.

name: Luxe City Center Hotel
title: “Near perfect!”
text: We stayed at this hotel for the first time as part of a group, so we didn't choose it, but we will for sure be back! For the service, the location and the rooms, it was great. They are still remodeling the restaurant/bar, so we were not able to try that, but there were so many other options just out the door, it wasn't a glaring problem. Our room did have a distinct smokey smell, especially for a non smoking room, that was a bugger. The only other issue we had was that we asked for an accessible room and were changed from the originally booked one, into an accessible one at check in, but it wasn't accessible. We managed as i knew they were sold out, but next time, we will make sure. And like i said, there will absolutely be a next time!

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Hollywood Hills Hotel
title: “One of the best kept secrets in Hollywood area”
text: remodeled with all new furnishings, marble spa shower and bathroom, marble kitchenette wet bar, great mattress for sleeping, collectible quality autographed artwork on the walls, spotlessly clean guestrooms, cute pool in the courtyard, and an amazing top notch diner restaurant off the lobby (the food is really THAT good, service fast and friendly). Walking distance to the Hollywood & Vine Metro subway stop, and just 2 blocks off the #101 Freeway, secure parking is worth the valet fee. It's maybe 1 mile east of the 'heart' of Hollywood, but certainly close to everything and a bargain for it's location and upgraded condition. Look forward to staying here again.

name: Hilton Los Angeles Airport
title: “Very good for the price”
text: It is always a matter of price/quality. For less than 130 dollars we got much more and better service here than in the hilton resort in moorea,polynesia where we payed 6 times the price for rude and lackadaisical service. For an airport hotel i think this is great. The VIP lounge has very short hours and the morning breakfast far from adequate, but all the rest worked just fine for us.

name: Hilton Los Angeles Airport
title: “Always comfortable, good service and reasonable price”
text: Booked online, great room, quick check in, shuttle to and from airport. Comfortable, well appointed.

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Business + Pleasure”
text: I grew up in Newport Beach, but I had to stay in Los Angeles for about 5 weeks in January for a business opportunity. They gave me really good rates and treated me very well.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Hollywood Hills Hotel
title: “Great place to stay, but .....”
text: Normally I would recommond this hotel to anyone. We've stayed here several times over the past 4 years and loved it. The hotel is clean, you're close to everything and the rates are reasonable if you're there off season. Unfortunately they made a few changes on our last stay. They've added a charge of $15 a night to park your car. They've also added a valet service for the attached restaurant, so the valet fills up the parking ramp with restaurant customers and there's no place for the hotel guests to park. The valet then shuttles your car to a "secure" parking area a couple blocks away, and everytime you want to go someplace you have to wait for the valet to have time to get your car and bring it back .. all for a mere $15 a night. We really liked the hotel, too bad they had to screw it up .... I think it's time to find somewhere else to stay.

name: Embassy Suites LAX North
title: “Great customer service”
text:
This hotel is very clean and the front desk is very welcoming. There is a free hotel shuttle to and from the airport and it seemed like it was every 15 to 20 minutes. 
The rooms are nice and large. The only really negative thing to say is the complementary cocktail hour is not the best for Embassy Suites standards. The h'orderves they had were popcorn, Asian mix, and nachos which the cheese ran out 30 minutes after they started it. I think they did come and refill it. The breakfast in the morning was very good.

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “beautiful and fancy hotel I cannot forget.”
text:
I stayed with a friend coming from Japan. That was when my friend was about to leave for japan after seeing around San diego and LA using his one week vacation. He did not hesitate to pay a lot of accomodation fee for this hotel because the hotel looked great and also that was the last day for him to use his dollars in the US. 
The bed room was spacious enough and everything clean. Ive got impressed by a huge picture hanging on the wall at the lobby. 
I had a great time staying this hotel and I like to stay there one more time in the future.

name: W Hollywood
title: “Unparalleled Service and a Stellar Location”
text:
First, I am a fan of W Hotels and try to stay at one whenever I can. While some are better than others, you are assured a good stay. With that being said, I was blown away at the level of professionalism at the W Hollywood starting with the valets to the front desk to the room staff. Always greeting me with a smile and asking if they could assist in any way. 
With only one night at the hotel, I was pleased at it’s location so close to cool shops and great neighborhoods to walk through. Even decided to have dinner on the property at Drai’s and loved the food. Recommended highly.
Will be my place to stay in LA.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “First Impressions Last a Lifetime”
text:
I was gavely dissapointed as I walked into the Sheraton gateway in LA Airport , the service from the reception staff was terrible, and very dissapointing. However when I went to their sister hotel The Four Points, I was met like I was a old friend returning for a visit. The concierge and bell person were so welcoming, as I had arrived 3 hrs before check in, and wanted to store my bags. They took me to the reception desk and said there will be room available for me. I watched as Patricia Rior seved the guest in the line before me, and she is just what any hospitality company needs. She is absolutly great at her job and so welcoming and calming. I have stayed in hotels arround the world and this is the kind of service and attitude that every guest deserves. She explained eveything and I can go about my day full of knowlage (provided by her) about the hotel and about LA as I am a first time visitor. Also there is free wireless in the hotel, including the rooms. Not in the Sheraton gateway 2 blocks away. In the internet dependent world we live in you would expect a great name like the Sheaton to offer free wireless in the rooms, but no, only in the lobby? 
For a hotel like the Four Points to outshine its sister hotel The gateway in so many ways, depends not on the decor or the room rates or the great gardens and pool or the fancy leather chairs, it depends on the people you have working with your guests every day, as they are the face and the voice of the property. The Leather chair in the Gateway cant talk. I am facinated by the stark contrast between the two. Well done to Patricia and the Four Points management. PS: thanks for the comp bottle of water, in the Gateway you have to pay over $4 for the water in the room. Small things make people happy, and then they come back..... 
Cheers

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Service was horrible”
text: Stayed for 2 nights over New Years. Asked for wine glasses to be sent to the room and never received. Went to bar to ask and was told to call room service. Went back to call room service and we were told there would be a charge to deliver two empty glasses. Finally gave up and drank the wine the next day. I have stayed here a dozen times over the years and the property has slipped to a 3 star at best. Not up to Westin standards. Loved the beds however.

name: Embassy Suites LAX North
title: “Older hotel with great staff”
text: I spent a week here waiting for my niece to be born. The hotel is showing it's age a little, but everything was tidy and the staff were very nice, especially at the breakfast and cocktail receptions. We must have looked pathetic spending Christmas Eve in the hotel lobby, but everyone kept a smile on their faces and wished us a happy holiday. The omelets were a delicious departure from some other breakfast buffets I've been through. I would have appreciated free internet since they are an extended-stay property and my USB modem did not get a signal in our room.

name: Venice On The Beach Hotel
title: “What a wonderful hotel”
text: If you want to avoid the hustle and bustle of city life, marvel at the wonderful beach, watch the sights and explore Santa Monica and beyond, then this is the place. Mine host Greg, is just superb at making life easy, especially for the travelling tourist and nothing was too much trouble. This boutique hotel is easily one of the better ones we have stayed in and would highly recommend to any traveller.

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Four star concrete treehouse”
text:
On arriving, I have to say I was astonished to find out this was a four star rated hotel. With the exception of the centre bar area, it is without doubt the most unattractive hotel interior I've ever seen. The design looks like inside of a mother ship - you'll know what I mean when you see it. The staff were aloof and a little bothered by the interuption, something quite unusual for us as everywhere else we've been in Califonia has offered a truly exceptional level of service. The rooms have a pretty decent view through huge windows of a somewhat uninspiring LA downtown, there is no mini-bar but there is a bar fridge. The cups were disposable - amazed they get away with that in a four star. The rooms are in serious need of an update, the stripey wallpaper and old carpet was truly tragic and a new coat of paint would clean the room up considerably. Room service took a long time but was worth the wait, (the chocolate brownie with ice-cream was voted best in the entire universe by our two sons). There were no bath robes as promised - not a big deal but if you're not going to provide something, then don't brag that you will. The beds and linens were exceptional, we all had a fabulous sleep.
The shopping in the area is dismal, I tried to occupy myself with it while the boys visited the Dodgers Stadium (tour was great apparently). The Macy's at 7th+Fig let the team down but the walk there will take you past some very interesting buildings.

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “stained sheet,tiny room, broken elevator”
text: I don't even know how to start and where to start..Our sheets had blood and makeup stains all over them. This happened right when we got in to the room at midnight. It took them one hour and 45 minutes to send a lady upstairs to change the sheets for us. and I passed out on the most uncomfortable chair in the room. she came up to the room with an old gentleman who was walking with a cane and couldn't help her changing the sheets so we had to help the lady ourselves!(sill I don't know the reason for having the cane man in our room at 1:45 at night??? They never changed the sheets after that(we stayed there three nits)It's the smallest room you can ever find.It's just a bed,a desk, a tiny bathroom, window and the door! You have to pay 60 dollar more per night for an upgrade to a bigger room. want to know how much bigger?1-2 square feet bigger!(funny huh?), internet service 12.99 per night per computer. parking? 42 dollars a night! crappy restaurants. You can hear everybody in the hall way when you are in the room. The downstairs club is so loud. if you are at the lower floors, you better not plan on getting back to your room before 3:00 a.m or u can hear Rihanna singing all night long! Elevators broke 4 times(each and everyone). The service was really poor.Gosh, Please don't waist ur money. If you can't afford spending 20-30 Dollars more per night,u r safe to stay where u r at. Don't even think about even giviing it a try! oh,business center hrs are 7 am to 7 p.m,and 9 am to 12 pm(3 hrs) on sat,closed on sund(why do they even have it?) the pool is open till 10 p.m but the doors close at 9 p.m. what the hell?

name: Los Angeles Airport Marriott
title: “We will be back”
text:
Clean rooms, nice staff, perfect service.
A good place to stay when travelling with good shuttle service and perfect and very motivated drivers.
If needed we will be back.

name: Embassy Suites LAX North
title: “Parking was a significant problem”
text: I wish I had seen the review regarding parking being a potential issue for some travelers. If I had been informed by the hotel website when I booked that they had limited parking in their single floor parking garage and used another garage on the same block for "overflow" parking, I would not have booked here. As it turned out I lost time looking for a space in the hotel garage before being directed to the overflow garage. Unfortunately the overflow garage was fenced in. This made it difficult to find an exit for my young children (4 and 6 year-old) and me to walk through with our luggage. We then had to walk through a poorly lit alley behind the hotel to reach the front lobby. I would not have agreed to this for my family if I had known ahead of time. I did not feel safe. It would not have been as much of an issue for me as a single person. Although I received "complimentary" parking, a member of management was not on site to provide me with any further compensation. Overall, we lost an hour of time searching the original garage, finding the overflow garage, finding our way out of the overflow garage, and getting to the lobby to finally check-in! Unacceptable.

name: InterContinental Los Angeles Century City
title: “A solid four star hotel in a four-star location”
text: I stayed at this hotel for one day and found it to be a solid four-star hotel in all respects. They upgraded me to a corner suite which had a balcony with a spectacular view. Everything lived up to the four-star level except possibly the pool which was not a scene and had a small pool area. But it was very acceptable. My room was fine, quiet and nicely furnished. They do charge for Internet in addition to parking. They have a town car that will take you to places within one and a half miles but I was not able to use it. It cannot be reserved but utilized on a first-come first-served basis. I would say this hotel is comparable to the Century City Hyatt which is about a half a mile down the same street. The one reason the Hyatt would be preferable is that it is immediately adjacent to the Century City shopping mall and walk able from the hotel. The Intercontinental is too far from the mall to walk. Bottom line is the hotel is fine and I would highly recommend and stay there again myself in an instant.

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Bed Bugs in the Westin Bonaventure Downtown LA”
text:
I am a regular Mon-Thurs business traveler to LA. I've been staying in the Westin Bonaventure Hotel in downtown LA since December 2007. It's a great business hotel and it has many conveniences. Unfortunately, I stayed two weeks ago in room 2958. (Yeah I have a good memory for numbers) It's one of the smaller suites on the top floor of the hotel (aside from the restaurant and rotating bar levels which are 30 and 31). 
Room 2958 had bed bugs. I didn't see the bugs but I noticed the bites immediately. Like I said, I am a very regular traveler and have heard about these things. They were definitely bed bug bites, the right pattern, the right appearance, the right insanely itchy sensation I have read about. I'd never actually gotten the bites before but I'm sure these were bed bug bites...also I noticed it the next morning after staying in the hotel and I did not have them the night before. There's nowhere else they could have come from.
The manager at the front desk who is very friendly and helpful, he always helps me out since I basically live in the hotel, is named Patrick. When I told Patrick that my room had bed bugs and that I was sure they were bed bugs he explained to me that it's very difficult to prove anything but that he would have someone inspect the room. They didn't find anything..which isn't surprising since the bugs are really small and really hard to see and usually live in places that we can't see unless we rip out floorboard and mattress fluff. He said they would fumigate the room anyway. I asked him to call me and let me know when they had fumigated the room, and to keep me posted if they did find the bugs, etc, just for my own peace of mind. (I mean I really do live in this hotel) He still hasn't called me back and it's been about two weeks. 
Obviously that sucks and I'm a little pissed at Patrick. But I am more upset because right now I am in the Westin Bonaventure hotel in downtown LA writing this review at 11:21pm in a room on the 22nd floor and I can't sleep because my skin is crawling thinking that it may have bed bugs. I'm not sure why I came back to the hotel because I've gotten so used to living here I guess I didn't think I wanted to leave. I mean, Dec thru May were fine, no bed bugs to worry about. 
Needless to say, I've decided to switch hotels for next week - or maybe even starting tomorrow night. I can't sleep here anymore. If you've never had bed bug bites, trust me, you don't want them and you should not stay in this hotel for at least a little while and you should especially not stay in suite 2958.
I feel bad for besmirching the hotel's name, but it's the truth and I thought I should warn other travelers.
Best,
A

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “Need some improvements”
text:
This hotel is near the airport which is a plus and the restaurant is good.
The problems were:
The Hotel didn't answer emails pre the visit, which were important.
The swimming pool was being rebuilt and no one told us when we booked.
The room wasn't made up and we had to ring housekeeping three times.
They charged our credit card for services we haven't used after we had left the hotel and we had our final bill!
Nothing to do with the hotel but if you are staying in this area:
If you want to see LA quickly then do either book a city tour or take a local bus to the beach both worth doing.

name: Farmer's Daughter Hotel
title: “So Not Worth The Price”
text: Although this hotel is nicely situated near The Grove, LACMA and Beverly Blvd., it is basically a Motel Six. Sparce furnishings reminded me of a garage sale in Nebraska. Nice staff and the adjoining restaurant was tasty, but the pool was small and crammed into a corner of the property - not inviting at all. Walls were fairly thin and I could hear the neighbor showering. The channel guide did not match the actual television stations, which I found very annoying. They claimed to offer room service, but the section with the room service menu was missing from the hotel's guide book. For $189/night I expected a lot more.

name: Hyatt Regency Century Plaza
title: “Good Value, nice quiet Location”
text:
Our first hotel in the U.S on what is to be a long trip. We found the hotel to be fantastic. We loved the location, as it was a tidy area, with lots of interesting things to watch from the balcony. We saw a movie being filmed across the road one morning. The valet service was good (but $35)and all the staff were impeccable.
The location across the road from a shopping mall and supermarket was also handy for travelers with children who needed essentials.
Overall, a great experience, and a perfect location near Santa Monica blvd if you have a rental car.

name: Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Worst hotel in LA!”
text: A group of us traveling for business were scheduled to stay at the Roosevelt for over a week. To put it bluntly, the hotel was completely unacceptable to the entire group. Filthy and disgusting rooms. We could not cancel our first night's stay and had to scramble to find another hotel. The overall consensus of the Roosevelt was extremely negative. Not one redeeming factor. A Holiday Inn is better then the horrid Roosevelt. Everyone was relieved to leave the Roosevelt the next morning. Do not believe the PR hype. This place is a disaster. The best place to stay in LA is L'Ermitage in Beverly Hills.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “This place is disgusting!!!”
text: Avoid this hotel at all costs. I recently stayed at this hotel for one night on a layover to Hawaii. The furniture was dated, the front desk person was extremely rude. The halls reeked of a musty odor. I must say this was not what I expected of my first experience in a starwood hotel.

name: Hollywood Celebrity Hotel
title: “Good Price/Good Location”
text:
I stayed at the Celebrity from Nov 17-20. We booked the room directly from the hotel and got it for $79/night. The room was clean, very spacious and included a kitchen area. Our room was on the first floor (there are only 2 floors). The room was a bit noisy as you can hear everything in the room above you, including people walking around, so request a room on the 2nd floor.
