The hotel offers a good continental breakfast with a variety of juices, muffins, croissants & bagels. They offer free use of a computer with internet access in the lobby which is really a nice touch. The parking lot is free, but very small.
The hotel is within a 5 minute walk to hollywood blvd, and all the attractions.
Overall, like most hotels there are a few kinks, but our stay was a pleasant one.

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Loved it”
text: Got there Friday afternoon, left Sunday afternoon, and we have no complaints whatsoever. Before booking the trip we read a few reviews that complained about the parking, then again if you really must stay in downtown you dont want to park anywhere thats not covered and secure, the Bonaventure parking was 35, others without valet parking where five dollars less and you either had to walk across the street or a couple of blocks. That was the major complaint we came across. Once youre inside the hotel the staff is very helpful, polite and friendly. We stayed in the green tower, the elevators were pretty cool with an awesome view of LA. The room was great, at the front desk they told us our agent had booked a double bed room, but they were able to accomodate us with a single queen size room. I could write a lot more great things about this place, all i can say is that if youre going to stay in downtown this hotel is the way to go. The main reason we were there was to see our Dallas Stars play against the kings just a few blocks west of the hotel, i cant think of any other place i'd rather stay if we go back. GREAT PRICE>

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “Great Place”
text:
This is a very fine hotel. The room was large and very clean even had
a little refrigerator with free bottled water. The prices at the resturant were reasonable. I had lunch there and it was very good. Not a beer drinker but their bar features a wide variety of beers. The only thing is I went down at about 10 p.m. and ordered a Tom Colins but the bar tender did not know what it was. This is a first class hotel at reasonable prices considering the area it is very near LAX.

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “No up to most Westins”
text: if you are looking for the usual Westin quality, you are in for a big disappointment. This hotel does not deserve it's star rating, the hotel inspector needs to visit. They say they have a pool, but it is off in a detour area that they send you up some back stairs through garbage to find and then when you get there it is dirty and partly closed off. So there is no pool

name: Hollywood Celebrity Hotel
title: “Friendly Staff, but Room was Problematic”
text:
We made a booking over the phone and was offered the suite for alittle more money. Room seemed decent on first impression, but the problems started to surface when we were about to settle in for the night. We were lounging around when after a while we noticed the soles of my niece's feet were black. Then we noticed ours were too. The carpet was filthy and we had to resort to putting the bed covers on the floor and walking around in our shoes. The bathtub was clogged and we were pressured to take our showers in a hurry so that the water doesn't overflow. A previous reviewer was right about the air conditioning as well, it was rather noisy. In the end, we had to request for a room change, a smaller room with no more problems and no discounts.
The staff were friendly though and did try to fix things. And the location can't be beat.

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Loved it”
text: I love this hotel and have stayed here on a few different occasions. I mainly stay here for business but I would not hesitate to stay for pleasure. The rooms are very nice and clean. The toiletries are great. They give you magazines to read about what is happening in LA and enough TV channels to suit me. The last time I was there they were recruiting extras for a film, unfortunately I was too busy and heading off to work. I would not recommend leaving the hotel late at night alone if you can help it, it is downtown LA and there are a lot of homeless people. Be careful with the restaurants inside, some are good, others not so much. The staff here are very pleasant and are very willing to change your room for a better view if you just ask. Parking is valet parking only, just tip what you think they deserve. I have never had a problem with them, they were always nice.

name: Embassy Suites LAX North
title: “nicht beeindruckt”
text: für ein Hotel der Hilton Group Family waren zuvile Kleinigkeiten nicht zufriedenstellend. Durchgebrannte Lampen, leere Fernbedienung, dreckiger Duschvorhang, nur ein Set Handtücher. Der Service war leider auch nicht der beste, musste morgens schon meinen Anschlussflug bekommen und konnte nichtmal Frühstück auf dem Zimmer bestellen. Alles in allem nicht was man im Hilton Group Standard erwarten würde. Das Zimmer war zwar sauber und ordentlich aber etwas klein.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “Good Value”
text:
This is a great airport hotel. They operate free shuttle that runs every hour.
My room was similar to something at a Hampton Inn, but with much nicer bedding. I think they go overboard with too many throw pillows. Those end up on the chair. I needed a good night's sleep and that's what I got.
The management has thought of just about everything. Coffee maker, iron, pen and paper. There is free wifi, but it only runs 128k and I think that's shared. It's enough for checking email. You can pay for faster access. 
Downstairs is a restaurant, bar and a large lobby with a big plasma TV. 
I highly recommend staying here for a layover, or day room. However, be advised that aside from the airport, nothing is within walking distance. If you want to see Hollywood you should rent a car or take a tour.

name: Venice On The Beach Hotel
title: “Simple hotel, great value, location, parking”
text: We enjoyed our stay at Venice on the Beach. Very few hotels in this part of LA offer such a nice combination of value and location. While not a luxury hotel, Venice on the Beach has free parking, great views and a congenial host. The rooms are clean and simple although very fussy people might be bothered by the fact that a previous guest's suitcase wheels had left some marks on one wall. The hotel is just south of the active part of Venice Beach, so we enjoyed both the peace and quiet of a residential area with a short walk to the more lively section. Our only problem was that we were so tired when we arrived that we forgot to read the note from Greg and did not clue into the fact that guests need to put a "Clean this room, please" sign on their doors when they want maid service. We wondered why the trash hadn't been emptied until we checked out and I read the note.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Hollywood Hills Hotel
title: “un pezzo di storia di Hollywood”
text: Buon hotel che rievoca la storia di Hollywood con le fotografie e gli autografi che tappezzano tutte le pareti. Le stanze sono molto ampie, dotate di tutti i comfort, compresi frigorifero, forno a microonde e l'immancabile macchinetta per il caffè. La posizione è strategica, non lontano al Walk of fame e a distanza contenuta da Beverly hills e Santa Monica. A due passi dall'hotel si trova anche la celebre scritta Hollywood. Staff cordiale, molto capiente il pacrehggio incluso nel prezzo. Per la colazione o per qualsiasi altro pasto c'è un'ottima caffetteria proprio sotto l'albergo

name: Hotel Angeleno
title: “Outstanding Hotel and Service”
text: Beautiful hotel and outstanding service. I was traveling on business and was not familiar with the surrounding area. Chris provided me with a list of local things to do and made some great restaurant recommendations. I highly recommend this location whether you are traveling for business or vacation.

name: Renaissance Los Angeles Airport Hotel
title: “Beautiful Hotel, Great Service”
text:
We stayed at the Renaissance Montura on Saturday, March 25, 2006. There was four of us and with the senior rate we paid $98.00/night...$111.86 with all the taxes. Excellent price for a beautiful hotel, close to the airport with no noise, seemed like a safe part of town.
-Check in was very quick and the staff was very nice.
-Free shuttle bus to and from LAX runs 24 hours.
-Clean, beautiful rooms (furniture was a bit large for these smaller rooms)
-We had a light breakfast in the hotel restaurant and it was delicious, service was excellent and when the food came to the table, it was on beautiful dishes and garnished with fresh fruit etc., looked like a picture out of a magazine. My toast was made with thick homemade bread and my daughter's french toast was garnished with fresh strawberries and she said that it was the best french toast that she has ever had.
-Burger King is across the street.
-Budget car rental across the street, I rented from Alamo which is about 1 mile away. To save on taxi fees, I took the shuttle back to the airport and walked downstairs and caught the alamo shuttle. 
I highly recommend this hotel. I was in California for about a week and stayed at other hotels if you would like to look at those reviews. 
Area/Hotels:
North Hollywood - Holiday Inn, Beverly Garland
Anaheim (Near Disneyland) - Holiday Inn Express
Huntington Beach - Best Western Huntington Beach Inn
Long Beach - The Coast Long Beach Hotel

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “For $69 it was OK, but I've had better nearby for less.”
text: Large room. Lots of jet noise and pool party noise until midnight from the airline crews that where staying there and drinking up a storm. Bed good, but not heavenly. Other furniture worn and outdated. Since it was cheap and I was coming in from Australia, I was ok with the stay. And it only cost 75 cents to go up to the Santa Monica Promenade on the Big Blue, but other hoetels are closer and nicer. Local calls $1.50 each. I had a great stay at the Hilton for the same $69 rate, and a $59 rate at the almost as good, but better placed Raddison, so I'd pass on the Westin unless I couldn't get a great rate somewhere else.

name: W Hollywood
title: “NOT GOOD”
text:
I don't even have the energy to provide a detailed account of our experience, but I can tell you that I have stayed at Starwood properties all over the United States and this was the worst experience I have had and I only stayed one night. The GM may turn the negative reviews around as I have heard good things about him through the grapevine. There were a couple of exceptional staff (CJ and Marc), but for the most part it was pretentious, insulting, discriminating, and overrated.
Don't:
Expect to get into the nightclub if you are not "someone" or know "someone" (Yes, Drai's is owned by another entity - Victor Drai). This will eventually wear off as all new L.A. Clubs do. 
Count on using the pool if they have a private event up there. 
Expect to be able to have a cocktail and/or sit out on the patio off the Living Room in the lobby (as there was a private party there, too). 
Expect courtesy 
Expect air conditioning or temperature control. 
"WISH" for anything reasonable because wishes really DO NOT COME TRUE HERE.
Do:
Save your money and stay somewhere you will be treated with class
Stop in for a poorly made cocktail just to see the Living Room
Wait and "WISH" the GM, Jim McPartlin, listens to all the negative feedback and does something to change it

name: Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text: This hotel was comfortable and neat without all the frills. I was a little nervous about booking because it was the only hotel left with rooms on a busy LA weekend. But, I was pleased to find helpful staff, a clean and stylish room, and a great view of Hollywood. The location is perfect if you are looking to walk to dinner or a movie, or just check out the walk of stars.

name: Venice On The Beach Hotel
title: “Great location, charming and very clean!”
text:
I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at Venice On The Beach Hotel. It was right on the beach and the manager Greg, could not have been more helpful or kind. He gladly accommodated my late arrival and made me feel very welcome. My room was very clean, comfortable, and charming and also included a huge flat panel tv that was quite a surprise. This isn't a big fancy chain motel where everything is cookie cutter perfect - rather it is a quirky, personable, memorable place that makes you feel at home. I will certainly be back. 
Good restaurants and fun shops nearby too.

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Great Hotel. Great Price”
text:
We stayed at the Westin Bonaventure for 4 nights from August 14-18, 2006. The hotel exceeded our expectations. The staff were friendly and helpful, especially the concierge who answered all our questions and explained the transit system for us.
We loved the fitness centre. It was always open and each piece of cardio equipment had its own t.v. that you could plug your headphones into.
The hotel itself is huge and several levels of the hotel have small restaurants and cafes that are not owned or operated by the hotel, but are great for grabbing a small or quick breakfast.
The hotel has a breakfast buffet that is good but at $18.95 a person we didn't want to eat there each day.
The room was small and a strange shape as mentioned by previous reviews but the king sized bed was very comfortable and I loved the pillows.
We ate dinner at the Bonaventure Brewing Company in the hotel and it was very tasty.
The hotel is about 2 blocks from the metro and made taking transit very easy to use.
Would stay here again.

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Great Priceline Stay”
text:
I had my doubts about this hotel due to all of the negative reviews, but I have about decided that the majority of people who post to tripadvisor.com are either perpetual pessimists or people who are used to exemplary accomodations wherever they go. I have stayed at a number of hotels that have been poorly reviewed on this site and never had a bad experience at any of the ones I've ended up staying at. 
As for the Westin Bonaventure, for $60-$70 per night, this place is awesome. Yes, the parking is high, but with a priceline rate, you're still staying in downtown LA for under $100/night. That's pretty good. 
One warning--be careful if you check in late. The Westin garage is full every night and if you are not a hotel guest who has managed to get in earlier in the day, they will send you across the street to park, which is $50/night. Try to get there early or pick your rental car up when you can park it early in the day. Once you get your car registered with them, you can get in even if the sign says the garage is full.
Yes, the rooms are a bit on the small side, but for a couple, this poses no issues--at least not for us. The rooms are well appointed, and the bath was bigger than the larger Westin room we stayed in out at the airport before we left. We had a room on the 30th floor with fabulous views, great air conditioning and a heavenly bed! Housekeeping was great, and everyone we dealt with was courteous.
The location is totally convenient--a good section of downtown with super-easy freeway access. Room service was surprisingly good, the brew pub had decent food, though service was a bit slow, and there are a ton of food options to choose from in the area, so you aren't stuck with hotel priced meals. It's a walkable area, at least during the day and early evening. 
The pool is fine, with big fluffy Westin towels, but keep in mind it is a "rooftop" pool and a bit on the small side. Also, wear your flip-flops--the concrete gets hot and is pretty sooty from being 5 stories above downtown and near a freeway. Not a luxurious pool by any means, but kind of cool to lay out and look up at the surrounding skyscrapers.
We had quick and easy check-in and out, and while our experience with the concierge wasn't the warmest, he was efficient and courteous. This hotel is enormous and busy--I'm sure they do their best.
Bottom line, the hotel is convenient, more than comfortable, and if you get a decent rate, you should have no cause for complaint. in addition, this hotel has been in a ton of movies, so you'll probably recognize it. It's a very LA experience!

name: Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Don't eat in the restaurant!”
text: The breakfast was terrible--bread doughy, eggs just so-so, bacon, yuck, and the potatoes were unedible....$40.00 of bad!

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Impeccable Service”
text:
Seems like all the reviews are the same so I'll try to write about different aspects. First, the service is great. I'm in the medical field so I don't get perks like business people. So, try to get a good deal on priceline. Shoot for $65-ish for weekdays. 
Little touches like the Hotel Operator greeting you by your name on the phone was very nice. The hotel has a lot of choices on food. Most open until 8pm-ish but I can tell that they make most of their business during lunchtime with all the LA downtown business workers strolling in. I ate most of my lunches in the hotel and only 1 dinner on the top floor Japanese restaurant. The japanese restaurant was overpriced and didn't have much of a selection...but the service was excellent. 
Gym: Those little 'pods' off of the track displayed on Expedia/Orbitz, etc aren't the only machines. There's a separate room with more machines and free weights. The running machines had TVs. Towels and disposable headphones are supplied. Free weights are good but only went up to 50lbs. No bench press.
Internet: High speed is offered for $12.95/day. Easy to use. 
Parking: $25/day. The parking staff is probably the nicest on the property. The first night, I tried to look for a cheaper alternative, but most places within a 2 block radius had similar prices. There is a place called Pershing Square Parking that charged $14 overnight...but no in/out and it was 4-5 blocks away. I decided to pay for the convenience and parked at the hotel parking.
Safety: I have to say, I lived in NYC for 4 years and I'm from Chicago....LA downtown is DEAD. It is perfectly safe during the day but the streets clear out at night. I felt safe on the big streets but I noticed a lot of homeless people on the sidestreets. It's ok if you're a guy but just be careful if you're a girl walking alone. 
Pool: Layed out twice. The pool is privately gated, but anyone can use it if they stick their hand through the gate and open it from the inside. Perfectly safe though...I'm sure 100% of the people at the pool were hotel guests. The poolside chairs/beds were very comfortable. Not your ordinary cheap poolside chairs. 
Other: One day the bathroom light bulbs went out. Got too lazy to tell them and decided to just use the alternate light source in the shower as the bathroom light....When I got home that night, room service had fixed the problem w/o me reporting it. Everybody greets you warmly. Just a really good experience. Yes, the beds are nice but aren't you sick of reading about this on this site? 
Location: about 45 minutes to Santa Monica Beach. 15 minutes to Glendale Mall. 3 minutes to Little Tokyo. 10-15 minutes to LAX. 
Have fun!

name: Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “ok”
text: I stayed here for work.The staff is not very efficient or friendly. I went with a friend (were both younger 21 and 23). The staff did not pay attention to use-the were giving tons of attention to the older guests-like we didnt matter.The hotel is way old, but clean.Bathroom was way small.We did get upgraded to a junior suite-they oversold the regular rooms. If that was a junior suite-I would hate to see the regular rooms, they must be the size of a shoe box. They were 3 walkin closets-how much space do you actually need-not 3 closets worth. Great location-I do give it that.Hotel is just ok

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “Westin Ripoff”
text:
I just made my reservation over the phone for a stay for myself and my wife at the Westin LA Airport. I would have done this online but I wanted to make sure my one night stay with Starwood points could be made along with one paid night. 
After I made the reservation, I checked my reservation confirmation email. The night with points was correct, but the reservation for the paid night was only for only one guest and the agent had also misspelled my name, so my SPG number wasn't entered. 
I sent Westin an email to get these errors corrected. They corrected my name and SPG number, but were unwilling to change the reservation to apply for two guests, because their change policies do not allow them to change a reservation with a non-changeable rate, even though they made the error. In the same email they referred to me as a "valued customer". They made it clear that I am not. 
Think twice about staying at a Starwood property. Obviously, even valued customers don't matter to them. I will be switching back to Hyatt / Hilton after this.
Jay

name: Sheraton Gateway Los Angeles
title: “Good LAX hotel”
text:
We've stayed here a couple of times as vacationers on the weekends. I thought the weekend rates were reasonable for this level of hotel.
Our rooms have been clean, and the entire hotel has been above par.
Parking was $13/day for in and out use of the lot behind the hotel.
Although the jet noise was occasionally heard, they have done the right job with soundproofing and double glazing, and it was seldom intrusive.
The Paparazzi Restaurant was willing and able to modify an entree to meet my wife's dietary needs. And the Starbucks in the lobby satisfied the morning fresh coffee cravings.

name: Hyatt Regency Century Plaza
title: “Very comfortable hotel”
text: Spent one night here in Decmeber at a great rate on Priceline. Very well furnished room, comfortable bed and very welcoming staff. Was treated as if I were paying full price too! Very clean room with all the ameneties one would expect from a hotel of this class. Lovely balcony with a good view. It is now operating under the Hyatt umbrella and is no longer a Westin.

name: InterContinental Los Angeles Century City
title: “my third visit... always wonderful!”
text: we just spent another great week at the intercontinental los angeles in century city, and are glad we decided to repeat with this property. i'll go back as often as i can. room service is terrific on food and timely delivery, the entire staff is helpful, pleasant (unlike some places in nearby beverly hills) and accommodating, all services are exactly as they should be, and because this is a fairly large hotel, you can often get exceptional deals and packages through online travel sites, as we did. under $150 per night including a luxe car? yes! we had a standard room that showed a little bit of wear, but having stayed in deluxe rooms there before (they're beautiful), this was small penance. great location for shopping, dining and more. go and enjoy it!

name: Hotel Angeleno
title: “Excellent !”
text:
Stayed here on arrival in LA and again for one night before returning to UK
Excellent hotel!! A little out of town but courtesy transport to LA and the standard of service was one of the best we encountered while in America this year.
Staff were absolutely brilliant and nothing too much trouble. Reception staff were unbelievably helpful.
Transport was arranged back to the airport and the staff organised a limo as it was cjeaper than the shuttle bus! this was wonderful and the perfect end to our holiday
Highly recommended and would stay again with no hesitation.
thank you for a brilliant stay on both occasions.

name: Hyatt Regency Century Plaza
title: “fine hotel (beware of construction)”
text:
We spent three nights at this lovely hotel, and had a great stay. However, there is significant construction happening across the street, so if you do not get a room facing the ocean, your view and quiet will be destroyed. 
We had booked two king beds rooms, but, when i said we did not want construction views, we had to get two rooms with two double beds. Supposedly, the king rooms all face the construction--and when I did see into one, it looked nightmarish. ROMANTIC STAYS BEWARE if a large bed is crucial to your enjoyment.
However, our spacious balconies had an excellent view of the hills, west LA, santa monica, and off to the pacific horizon. FANTASTIC for ocean breezes!
The check-in process was smooth and friendly, and the valet service is excellent---efficient and fast. The rooms were clean, with comfy beds and nice bathrooms (including double-headed showers and decent (but not super-spacious) bathtubs.) The internet service in-room is very fast, and gives you a genuine 24 hours for 10 dollars. There is wireless in the lobby as well.
Room service was fast and efficient, and Breeze, the on-site restaurant, is delicious. Many of the items are organic, with free-range and hormone-free meat and veggies grown in their dedicated garden, cooked fresh. It's very pleasant to dine outside on the patio, too. 
All and all, I would definitely come back, but only if I was assured I would not face the construction--not until it's done.

name: Hyatt Regency Century Plaza
title: “Pamper With Paper”
text:
We stayed there the weekend of March 21/22. They now have automated check-in at a kiosk, which I found quite impersonal and unwelcoming.
Our room was fine, yet they use paper cups in the baths and no other glasses are available in the room. On our second day, the maid threw away our papercups and did not replace them. Maybe she was mad because we had to call at 5pm since our room had not yet been cleaned.
The towels are not the kind you would expect with this level of a hotel. No thick, plush stuff here, just serviceable K-Mart towels.
We wanted to use the pool on Saturday, but all seats were filled. There was no shade anyway, so it wouldn't have mattered.
Saturday night we had to wait a good 20 minutes for the valet line as they seemed quite understaffed. Valet parking is now $31 a night and self-parking is so inconvenient as not to be a choice.
It's still a nice hotel, the rooms well-furnished except for the cups and towels. We did see a bill left by someone who had just checked out...they paid more than $25 a night than we did, so all is not bad!

name: Waldorf Astoria Chicago
title: “top top top hotel in chicago”
text: now this is what you call a hotel. impeccable service, great location, amazing food and luxury at its finest. the rooms are massive and the amenities are delightful. my wife and i felt like we were back to our honeymoon as this hotel provides you a mini-getaway within a very busy city whilst being bang in the centre of it. highly highly recommended if your wallet can handle it

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown
title: “Perfect base for weekend in Chicago”
text:
I travelled to Illinois from the UK on business, and booked Friday and Saturday night at the Homewood Suites so that I could have a weekend in the city. The location was perfect, walking distance to Michigan Ave for all the shopping and touristy stuff, and literally 100 yards to the L (red line) for getting out to the surrounding areas.
The room was great: not exactly 'wow' decor but clean and really well stocked. I was expecting a 'suite' to be a larger than average hotel room with seperate sitting area. It was actually a 3-room mini-apartment, with an open lounge/kitchen, bedroom, and bathroom. Two flatscreen TVs and a huge bed. Breakfast buffet eggs and bacon were great for the hangover(!), and the kitchen meant that I could cook up some lunch rather than eat out if needed.

name: Hotel Angeleno
title: “The hotel is lovely, but out of town and difficult to travel from if you don't have a car!!”
text:
The Angeleno was a very nice hotel, though it is right by the freeway. If you don't have a car, don't choose this hotel unless you have a lot of money saved for taxis. We were told that a taxi would cost $50 to Beverly Hills - the nearest tourist attraction other than the Getty Centre. We didn't have that kind of money so ended up getting around on the City Sightseeing tour. We found out about the free shuttle from the internet, and weren't told about it by the hotel staff.
We were lucky we were on the side facing away from the freeway, though there was still a fair bit of road noise. There was nowhere within walking distance of going for food, so we went to the hotel restaurant, which to be fair was very nice. 
We felt that location seriously let this hotel down, as otherwise it isn't too bad.

name: Howard Johnson Inn & Suites - Reseda
title: “Still a great place to stay at very affordable rates”
text: I recently visited with family in the LA area and stayed here again. The entire staff is friendly, helpful, courteous and professional. The cleaning staff keeps the rooms in good shape, and they are most helpful when things in the breakfast area, or in your room, get low. The rooms have small refrigerators and flat screen tv's. Wireless internet service and continental breakfast are included. They have a pool. You can park behind a locked gate. I highly recommend them for their service, cleanliness, very reasonable rates, and the entire staff. At the front desk I dealt with a young man named Ulysus, and with Mina, the manager, who I remembered from my last stay. We had quite a nice chat.

name: Hotel Angeleno
title: “6 days in LA”
text: Excellently located hotel for all usual LA attractions. Helpful,friendly staff who were only too pleased to help. Clean rooms,adequate size. Lovely pool area especially at night when the fire is lit!free shuttle is great for going into Westwood village, as is their car that you can book to take you to LAX. Free wine in evenings. Rooms a little noisy(it's right on the freeway) but to be honest we were too tired to notice it after a days sightseeing.

name: Hotel Angeleno
title: “When in LA”
text:
This was a great value for money hotel in Los Angeles. The cylindrical shaped hotel had good rooms, great atmosphere, good restaurant and was close to Beverly Hills and most of the other sites... Rooms were clean, and of a good size... The staff were very helpful and ever ready to help... it was like almost 30 minutes drive from LAX Airport, which is not too bad.. Bathroom was nice and well serviced.
Would definitely go back again

name: Hollywood Celebrity Hotel
title: “Bien démarrer un sejour à LA”
text:
Hotel extrement bien situé à Hollywood, juste a coté du Kodack theatre de Hollywood Bld.
Les chambres sont grandes et confortables. Petit déjeuner et parking compris ! Internet 1mega dans chaque chambre.
Bref c'est un rapport qualité prix imbattable ! Tres bien pour une étape de deux trois jours à LA.
Nous y avons séjourné à notre arrivée en californie.

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “Best bed ever!”
text:
Me, my husband and 12 year old son stayed one night at the Westin at LAX. We arrived early in the evening after a looong flight from Europe and had a very early flight the next morning so needed a place to crash. It took a little bit long before the shuttle picked us up (45 min, and not the max 20 min. as promised).
Check inn went smoothly and the room was quite large , 2 double beds. THESE BEDS...... they wrote about "Heavenly" beds! Well, i know what they mean now! It was amazing, firm but soft and the blanket was a dream. Try the heavenly Westin beds!

name: Hilton Los Angeles Airport
title: “Buona posizione per l'aereoporto”
text:
L'hotel si trova in una buona posizione per andare all'aereoporto di Los Angeles ma per il centro città è molto scomodo. Fuori c'è un bus che in 90 minuti porta a Santa Monica ma per Los Angeles è meglio il taxi che con circa 60/70 Usd porta in città. L'albergo ha un bus gratuito che fa servizio da e per l'aereoporto.
Le camere sono spaziose. Noi abbiamo soggiornato per due volte a inizio e fine viaggio chiedendo una camera a due letti ma in entrambi i casi non siamo stati accontentati. La seconda volte le lenzuola e il cuscino erano sporchi di nero. Nonostante la vicinanza all'aereoporto il rumore degli aerei si sente poco. Consiglio di far colazione allo Starbucks che c'è in hotel-
Per un Hilton mi sarei aspettata qualcosa di più.

name: Waldorf Astoria Chicago
title: “One of the finest hotels in the U.S.”
text:
No other hotel I have visited in the past 5 years has spent as much on high end decor, spacious room/suites, linens and quality staff. I doubt they are making any money, but the guests are the big winners. The service is world class and continues to improve with each visit. I have been hugely impressed with all staff ranging from front desk attendants to concierges to chamber maids. 
The health club and men's locker room are both luxurious and well equipped. Definitely not to be missed.
My only criticism is the price to quality and service in the restaurants, particularly at breakfast time. The experience is not up to par with the rest of the hotel but I have no doubt this will be corrected in short oreder.
Finally, if you want a world class meal, walk down Rush St. to "Zinc." Terrific.

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “The Sofitel was great”
text:
My wife and I just returned from a four day trip to Chicago and the Sofitel was wonderful. We had a suite in the 23rd floor and it was everything that I had imagined. We have stayed at the Waldorf-Astoria in New York and other upscale hotels. This was by far the best. It was super modern. We had flat screen televisions in each room. The King bed was the most comfortable hotel bed that we have ever slept in. When the Bose alarm clock went off, I didn't want to get up. They sent us two Voss waters and some truffles the first night. Everything was well done.
The hotel is two blocks from the Magnificent Mile and everything that we wanted to see was a short walk or cab ride from the Sofitel. We will definitely be back.

name: Trump International Hotel & Tower Chicago
title: “One week at Trump Chicago”
text: Excellent room, views great. Service was spectacular, from the concierge and other staff. Car and driver service awesome. Highly recommend. We went for a run on a very hot morning, and the concierge without prompting, offered us water as we walked by. The staff all seem there to please.

name: Hotel Angeleno
title: “Bring earplugs and enjoy the savings”
text: The management of this hotel wisely has priced the property well below the neighboring hotels because of one major factor: noise. The hotel is attractive and has been well kept up for being more than 40 years old; however, it sits only a few yards from the busiest freeway in California. There is street noise at all times of the day. And, for the next two months, there is additional noise because of freeway construction across the street. The hotel is not in a convenient location for anything other than visiting UCLA, seeing the Getty or visiting friends near by. You must have a car and there are no shops to walk to. I have stayed at the hotel twice before because it is a bargain; but, this last week, will be my last. I couldn't sleep because of the excessive noise. I come to LA a few times a year and will try another place that is not on top of a freeway. On the plus side, the rooms are clean and the staff is very friendly. The hotel breakfast is expensive but tastes good.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown
title: “All the comforts of home!”
text: I just visited the Homewood Suites in downtown Chicago with my family. I can't say enough good things about our stay! Our room was beautilful and we had an amazing view. The staff was so kind and helpful. The location could not be beat, we were close to everything and right across from Nordstrom! With two free meals during the week the hotel was an excellent value. The breakfast is served daily and offers many options. I have family in the area and I will stay at this hotel again and again!

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Mitten im Loop”
text:
Das Palmer House Hilton befindet sich direkt im Loop und ist über die blaue CTA-Linie direkt vom Flughafen zu erreichen. Das alte Gebäude mit seiner riesigen eingangshalle hat viel Scharm. Die Mitarbeiter sind freundlich und hilfbereit. In der State St., die Strasse ist direkt am Hotel befinden sich die ersten Shopping-Läden, so das man nicht weit hat die ganzen Tüten wieder ins Hotel zu bringen.
Die Zimmer sind geräumig und super sauber. Wir waren auf dem Executive Level, mit eigenen Expressaufzug in den 23. Stock, inkl Frühstück und abendlichen Snacks. Softdrinks und Kaffe, Tee waren von morgens bis abends umsonst.

name: W Los Angeles - Westwood
title: “Consistently Excellent”
text: I travel a lot -- for business and for pleasure (with my family). I have stayed at the W Westwood several times over the past 2-3 years (during business and family trips). While some hotels can "fall off" in key areas of quality, my experience with this place has been consistently excellent. The location is a bit off the beaten path; but this makes it a nice retreat, with everything you might need on the property (luxurious yet cool atmosphere, pool, nice bar). Most importantly, a commitment to good service has been apparent in my interaction with the staff during each visit (from the Welcome desk, to the Concierge, Housekeeping, and pool bar). Also, they have a "W Insider" (who apparently tracks repeat customers to help ensure a good experience). This person made sure the Welcome desk was aware of my check in requests -- and they went out of their way to accommodate, even though I was a bit crazy during check in (on the phone, multi-tasking). Bottom line, this is one of those "can't miss" places.

name: The Palmer House Hilton
title: “Una bella sorpresa!”
text: Il Palmer ci è stato consigliato dal Tour Operator per la sua posizione centrale ed è vero, è a metà strada tra il lago ed il centro, proprio all'interno del Loop ed abbiamo usato la macchina solo per spostarci la sera... La hall è spettacolare e la camera era accogliente, grande e pulita. Attenzione al parcheggio: chiedono 51$ al giorno!

name: W Los Angeles - Westwood
title: “Chic, centrally located West Hollywood hotel”
text:
If your vacation plans take you all over Los Angeles, the W in Westwood is a good option in terms of value and location. It's within easy driving distance of Rodeo Drive, Robertson Avenue, Melrose, and The Getty Museum, as well as within walking distance of Westwood Village and UCLA. The Village has everything you'd want or need while away from home: a large theatre, a 24 hour CVS, a Trader Joe's, Starbucks, banks, coffee shops, salons, bars, restaurants, etc. It's very safe to walk around day or night.
This hotel is as chic as one would expect from the W Hotel chain, but not so perfect or sterile. The foyer is expansive and offers most everything you'd want in a business or vacation hotel: a very helpful concierge, efficient front desk check-in, Nine Thirty lounge/bar, stylish sofas so you can sit while you use the free lobby WiFi, sitting area with table top games, flavoured water, and a small computer centre (free to print boarding passes; otherwise $8.95/15 minutes or something exorbitant), and public washrooms.
PROS:
- Location - 15-30 minutes by car from most tourist spots, including walking distance to Westwood Village
- Quiet - neighbourhood feels very residential and quiet
- Value - chic, high-end hotel that would cost double in a high demand area
- Decor - chic and inviting, with fun details like elevator floor mats that say "Good morning" or "Good evening" according to the time of day; nice touches like bath mats that say "STEP,"
- Amenities - small outdoor pool with hot food service near the pool, 2 computers to print your boarding pass (you have to pay to use them otherwise; in-room WiFi available for $14.95/day or $38/3 days), gym, on-site spa
- Room - small bar fridge, Bliss bath products (nice!), in-room safe, spacious corner king suite was sub-penthouse level and had a view
- Car Service - we didn't use it, but the W offers short drop off only car service with an Acura
- Coffee/Tea - The Nine Thirty lounge/bar offers complementary coffee and tea in the morning, as well as pastries/yoghurt for purchase
- Late Night Room Access - after 10pm, the elevators require you to swipe your room card to get to your floor, a nice security touch
CONS:
- Parking is $35/day, valet only
- No in-room coffee maker, although you can request one
- No free in-room WiFi, although there is free WiFi in the lobby (and comfy sofas to sit in while you surf the 'net)
- Not in the heart of the action of Sunset Blvd or Melrose, but not far by car
- The Backyard Restaurant (by the pool) has a good but small menu and friendly service. Oddly enough, both times we went there, one of us would not receive our drink and the server spilled water on us.
RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Parking - there is self-parking at the end of the block at 1015 Hilgard (corner of Weyburn) for $7 until 10pm or $14 for 24 hrs with in/out privileges
- Westwood Village - Trader Joe's (exit the hotel, turn left, turn right at Weyburn and it's 1-2 blocks on your left), Denny's for pancake breakfasts, Starbucks (exit the hotel, turn left and follow Hilgard until it curves, keep going and it's 2-3 blocks away)
- Car Rental - we researched and had an excellent experience with Midway Car Rental, who offers unlimited mileage and super efficient/friendly customer service (book on-line for best deals; to get to their office, wait at the Hotel/Car Rental pickup area under the red sign & wait for the QuikPark shuttle, which drops you off right at their office)
- Restaurants: STK (high-end steakhouse; TMZ-type paparazzi hang out next door), lunch at The Lounge in the Hotel Wilshire (rooftop pool/restaurant with a view of the Hollywood sign), The Coffee Bean Company (a chain coffee shop; the cold blended pure chocolate frap-type drink is marvelous, as is their cappuccino)
- Drive - drive up to Malibu and enjoy the 27 miles of beach; stop by the side of the road and climb down the cliffs to get to the rare public beaches; drive up further to Paradise Cove and have an amazing seafood dinner at the Paradise Cove Beach Cafe (it's busy but worth it)

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Great views!”
text: Stayed here for part of my honeymoon, and had a great stay. the views from the towers are great, and there are plenty of stores right in the hotel, even room service was fast at 1:30 in the morning. The service was superb and the location is great too, right next to the highway.

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “Great hotel”
text:
I just got back from a week at the LAX Westin and have no complaints. Check in was fine, my room was ready when I arrived at noon. Valet parking was smooth and easy. The lobby is spacious enough that if you need to you can find a quiet spot and rooms are large, clean, and comfortable (with the Westin heavenly bed package). Location along the LAX strip isn't great for tourists, but fine if you have business down there or have a rental car. 
Despite what some reviewers have written, I never once heard a single plane during my stay. I could see them out my window, so close that I could practically reach out and touch them, but I never heard them. 
The hotel was full most of the week with conferences and business seminars, but with all of the meeting rooms away from the lobby on the 2nd floor, you would never have known it. Also, despite the full house, the elevators ran quickly and I never found myself waiting. 
All in all, about as a good a stay as you could expect at an airport hotel.

name: The Westin Los Angeles Airport
title: “Grand Entry..small pool”
text: The rooms are clean and average in size. The noise is appearant but not over the top. You can hear the planes till about 11pm and then strat up again about 7/8am. The pool is ok, not as beautiful as one might expect give the luxurious entry to the hotel. I highly reccoment the room service, nice omlettes and someone who payed attention at culinary school.

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Hotel professionale.”
text:
La seconda volta che soggiorniamo in questo albergo. Centrale e comodo da raggiungere, di grandi proporzioni con vetrate e ascensori affascinanti. Enorme, quasi dispersivo, completo di tutti i servizi (i più importanti sono tutti esclusi dal prezzo della camera). Stanza grande, comoda e pulita. Con arredi e bagno (lavandino malfunzionante e acqua calda al minimo) che cominciano ad essere un pò datati. Colazione ottima e cena buona. Parcheggio comodo ma un pò lenti nella riconsegna dell'auto. Perfetto per affari.
Tutto il personale si è rivelato cortese e molto professionale.

name: The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites
title: “Super Lage direkt Down Town L.A.”
text: Super Lage direkt Down Town L.A. Das Hotel ist eine Augenweide und man hat alles was man benötigt direkt in der Nähe. Das Parken ist mit 45 Dollar pro Nacht schon ein High Light. Einmal pro Woche findet in der Straße vor der Bücherei ein Farmer Market statt. Dort kommen die Banker mittags zum Essen hin und dort gibt es viele leckere Sachen zum Probieren. Von dort aus kommt man überall gut hin. Wenn man ein Zimmer auf der ersten Hälfte der Hoteletagen hat, kann es sehr laut sein, da die Fenster nur einfach verglast.

name: SLS Hotel at Beverly Hills
title: “Not really a luxury collection”
text:
Upon check in, I had no help with my lugguage and there was no door man. The bathtub is weird and same with their shower set-up. I didn't like it at all. 
They rooms are dark and dingy with mirrors everywhere, which i don't mind but what's the point if you can't see anything. Its great if you're having hanky panky - but otherwise cheesy.
The conceriage is usless. Rude and not helpfull = no tip. If they don't like their job then do something else.
Awesome pool ... great service and great food! Good gym and location. I'm a Starwood Plat member....otherwise for the price...GO to Mr C hotel. Their towncar service is reliable and the guys who work there are great.

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “Excellent”
text:
We had a junior suite on the 25th floor, it was excellent. The suite was huge, had a lovely king bed and was beautifully decorated throughout. In fact, the entire hotel was beautifully decorated and thoughtfully designed. 
The hotel staff were all first class, reception were prompt and very polite and the concierge was the most knowledgeable I have ever encountered.
We didn't eat in the restaurant although it was always busy. There are many great places to eat within a very short distance of the hotel.
The hotel is very well situated just a block or so from some great shopping on Michigan Avenue and you can also catch the trolley tour bus outside the Hancock Centre.
Would certainly recommend this hotel to others looking for good quality four-star accommodation. We'll definitely stay there the next time we visit Chicago.

name: Hilton Los Angeles Airport
title: “Vriendelijk personeel”
text: Ruime kamer, een beetje ouderwets. Er is een zelfparking aan de linkerzijde van het hotel of de duurdere valetparking. Het ontbijt is zeer goed met een goede bediening. Niet ver afgelegen van Avis, Hertz enz...

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “I never wanna stay anywhere else in Chicago”
text:
The outside of the hotel is pleasing to the eye and very classy. The front desk staff is so attentive and wonderful. We got to the hotel at 8:30am on a Thursday after a red eye and requested to check in early. They didn't have rooms available yet, as check out wasn't until 12pm and check in wasn't usually until 3pm, but they said they could give us a room by 1pm. They also didn't bat an eye when I advised them that my boyfriend was allergic to down feathers and said they would "defeather" the room. We left to go sightseeing after leaving our bags with the bellman (very patient while we organized ourselves!) but the woman at the front desk asked for a phone number to contact us once our room was ready. She gave us a call at 11am and left a message to let us know our room was ready and our keys were at the front desk.
There were robes for each of us in the room which was nice. The room was simple and modern, but very pleasing to the eye. We were on the 10th floor with a view of the buildings (Hancock tower was viewable) and a small courtyard/park next to the hotel. The bed and pillows were wonderfully comfortable and the bathroom was gorgeous, complete with marble tiles, shower and counter. Full size hair dryer was supplied (not the connected to the wall mini kind!!), separate tub. And there are speakers in the bathroom so you can hear the TV in the bedroom! Magnified mirror in the bathroom (helpful for shaving to my boyfriend!) along with a live bamboo plant in the bathroom. 
The lounge is nice, very modern with a good vibe, but currently allows smokers which was a disappointment. STRONG martinis, but very attentive service to go along with it. Great atmosphere. Didn't eat at the Cafe des Architectes but hear it's very good. 
There is a small adorable boutique shop that is just adorable and has wonderful items available including soaps, lotions, jewelry, intimates and novelty books. 
I voiced my only displeasure (smoking in lounge) in their survey after my stay and promptly received a personalized e-mail from the hotel manager. I love this personal service, wouldn't hesitate to stay here again. This is an awesome location close to Hancock tower, the shops/mall and just everything we were looking for!!

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “High Five”
text: The staff at this Hotel is excellent. Every employee from Reservationist to check out was efficient and professional.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “Gutes Hotel, hatten aber mit Widrigkeiten zu kämpfen”
text: Das Hotel ist vom Preis-Leistungsverhältnis an sich empfehlenswert. Allerdings hatten wir Probleme beim Aufenthalt. Dies hat den anfänglich guten Eindruck sehr relativiert. Als Ersatz ist uns das Abendessen im Hotel und die Parkgebühr erlassen worden: 1. Nachts gegen 12 Uhr kam es zu einem Rückfluss aus dem Kanlisationssystem, so dass die Badewanne mit stinckendem Abwasser gefüllt war, das nicht mehr ablief. Die Toilette war nicht mehr zu benutzen. Leider konnte das nicht behoben werden. Uns wurde nachts und am nächsten Morgen empfohlen, die Toiletten an der Rezeption zu benutzen. Nachdem wir klar machen konnten, dass man sich auch am morgen waschen möchte, ist uns ein Hotelzimmer am anderen Hotelende zum Duschen zugewiesen worden. 2. Darüberhinaus sind Ameisen über unsere Koffer hergefallen.

name: Howard Johnson Inn & Suites - Reseda
title: “Surprisingly pleasant stay”
text: This was a very nice hotel considering the location. Having grown up in the SFV, I knew Reseda wasn't the best location but was pleasantly surprised at how nice the hotel was. Very clean rooms and roomy. Nice staff and lovely continental breakfast. The flat screen TV was a hit with my husband. The only thing that could be improved is to title your wireless internet connection. There were quite a few to choose from and it was hard to figure out which one was from the hotel.

name: Hilton Los Angeles Airport
title: “Alta qualità, basso prezzo.”
text:
Hotel ideale per sosta breve tra un volo e l'altro oppure per noleggiare auto e visitare Usa. 
Navetta gratuita dall'aeroporto.
Hotel bello, nuovo, pulito. Camere molto grandi, bagno bello con ottimi prodottipulizia (non di marca Hilton).
Piscina esterna riscaldata (apre alle 6 am) e 4 Jacuzzi, palestra sempre aperta. 
Internet a 13 usd in camera, gratis nella hall. 
Parcheggio a pagamento, sosta breve (10- 20 min) gratis. 
Colazione anche con caffè e prodotti Starbucks, ma solonel bar della hall.

name: Farmer's Daughter Hotel
title: “What FUN!!! We loved the whole deal. Great location, great staff, way FUN!”
text:
It was wonderful.... we'll spread the news wide and far. Tart was a fabulous Christmas breakfast. We had our family in a suite for Christmas Eve and Christmas. Dined and movied, shopped at the Grove. Hiked Runyon Canyon after fabulous breakfast on Christmas. Adam the front desk guy was such a delight. The valet, the waiters... perfect. We will definately be back. 
We too have a "farm stay " on our farm in Oregon. We have it decorated very 
"agri-chic", and fun. So much appreciated. all your details.

name: W Los Angeles - Westwood
title: “Nice rooms, hotel was a bit too trendy though”
text:
Stayed here for two nights and it was pretty nice! We checked in really late on our first night there (like at 1AM). The lobby was a bit overwhelming at that hour. Music was blaring and the whole place felt like a dance club not a hotel lobby. It was a bit too much after traveling on a plane all day. I just wanted to get to my room, not deal with the party scene, scantily clad people, and all that noise.
We were rewarded when we finally did get to our room. There was a bottle of champagne and a chocolate dessert set out for my birthday! It was a nice surprise treat for 1AM. 
The rooms themselves are quiet and spacious. There is a lot of hallway noise and banging around in the morning though from the cleaning staff. They were especially loud when they were right above our room. Our room was a junior suite and it had a separate living room with a couch and tv. I'm not sure if every room is like that but it was nice.
I liked the toiletries in the bathroom. They were Bliss spa products and smelled lemony.
This hotel does have some crazy charges though - wifi, valet parking, room service, etc. We asked for beach towels one day and they put a $50 charge on your card until you return them. We returned them and I asked to make sure they would remove the charge and the guy said he would right away. Well guess what, the charge was still there upon check-out! I asked them to remove it again and they finally did. Just make sure you double check your bill at check-out. 
We had a 50% off coupon for room service and our breakfast bill for 1 croissant, 2 muffins, and 2 glasses of tap water was still $14.
The elevators are super annoying here. You have to insert your card in just the right way to get to your floor. If another group already entered the elevator and did their card then you are screwed. The elevator is already zooming past your floor before you get to insert your card and press your floor button. You will end up going way up to a high floor and then you'll have to ride the elevator back down again to your floor. I heard numerous people complaining about this. The hotel should just get rid of the need to swipe the cards first.
I would stay at this hotel again if the price was right. The rooms are pretty luxurious and the hotel is in a nice location. It is easy to get to other areas in LA from this neighborhood as long as you have a car!

name: W Los Angeles - Westwood
title: “overpriced, dated, lobby feels like a pick up joint”
text: This is definitely not a place for middle class families. I got a good deal on a suite, apparently due to low booking. However, the daily cost jumped seriously when mandatory parking was added on. No self parking whatsoever -- all valet. And the staff are kind of sickly sweet edging for a tip every time you turn around. After a while I gave up and stopped tipping altogether. Breakfast was ungodly expensive. For a family of four light eaters (oatmeal, waffles, etc.) we couldn't get out of there for less than $90. They charge for internet and make it clear that the cost is "per device." The lobby feels like a pick up joint out of Boogy Nights. Our room was nice and spacious. However, once out of the room, we were very uncomfortable with blue lights, needy staff and Paris Hilton wanna bees everywhere. The W is convenient for families visiting UCLA. But if you book a room for ~ $300 per night, be prepared to spend nearly $500 with one meal. Next time we'll stay on Wilshire and drive to campus. One last note, if you do stay there, look at your bill carefully when checking out. A $100 room service charge was incorrectly added to our bill. Took three phone calls and two days to straighten it out. (Despite all the "luxury," their accounting staff aren't available on weekends.) To their credit, though, they did remove the charge and apologized.

name: Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel - A Thompson Hotel
title: “Super, super, super”
text:
Dieses Hotel liegt einfach göttlich. Sofort wenn man rauskommt steht man auf dem Hollywood Boulevard. Alle Annehmlichkeiten hat man in der Umgebung. Die Metrostation, Drugstore, Shopping Mall mit Foodstores, Kinos, die Seightseeingbusse.
 In diesem Hotel ist die Rezeption nicht wie sonst am Haupteingang sondern hinten raus. Da viele Stars in diesem Hotel absteigen, fällt es dann nicht sofort auf, wenn ein Prominenter eincheckt.
An der Rezeption wird man zuvorkommeng behandelt und sehr sehr freundlich.
In sein Zimmer kommt man nur, wenn man sich im Fahrstuhl mit seiner Zimmerkarte einckeckt und den 
Stockwerk drückt. Die Zimmer sind sehr modern eingerichtet. Wir hatten das Glück, genau auf dem Hollywood Boulevard, Madame Tusseaud und das Hollywoodzeichen zu sehen. Die Betten waren nicht mit der üblichen Decke versehen sondern wie wir es kennen mit einem Steppbett. Wir hatten zwei Betten und die waren beide riesengroß und einfach superbequem. Eine Minibar war im Zimmer.
Haben wir aber nicht benutzt. Der Aufenthaltsraum ist ziemlich dunkel rustikal gehalten, aber da es ein altes Hotel ist (Marlyn Monroes Geist soll noch darin spuken) passt es dazu.
Der einzige Wermutstropfen war, dass wir eine Durchgangstür hatten zum anderen Zimmer und somit etwas hellhöriger war. Dieses würde ich beim nächsten Mal sofort sagen, ein Zimmer ohne Durchgangstür.
Das Swimmingpool war in einem schönen Garten angelegt. Einfach traumhaft. Die Liegen sind mit dicken Auflagen vesehen. Man liegt so bequem. Allerdings kann man das Swimmingpool am Wochenende kaum benutzen (war bei uns so), da am Samstag der Pool für eine Geburtstagsparty gesperrt war und am Sonntag immer die Tropicana Party stattfindet. 
Internet kann man in der Lobby umsonst benutzen.

name: Hilton Los Angeles Airport
title: “Bon Hotel pour 1 nuit à Los Angeles”
text: Hotel confortable, très proche de l'aéroport. Y avons séjourner une nuit avant notre voyage dans l'ouest américain. Excellent buffet au petit déjeuner.

name: W Los Angeles - Westwood
title: “Perfect Stay in LA”
text: Even though this W hotel is not the newest in the SPG portfolio it is very well maintained on a beautiful street in West LA. It is walking distance to many restaurants, whole foods, trader joes and coffee shops. I was in the property for 9 days on business and honestly did not want to leave. The staff were prompt and courteous, the room was large with plenty of room to stretch out and the hotel is not over crowded with partying LA people. It actually felt very relaxing. I will definitely stay again. As a side note, I used some SPG points to stay one night at the SLS while I was in LA and I feel the staff at the W are far superior when it comes to treating guests with excellent service.

name: Farmer's Daughter Hotel
title: “Overpriced and depressing”
text: Funky denin bed covers and cushions and good quality toiletries doesn't make up for this so called hotel being a depressing place to stay. Firstly, it is not a hotel but a motel and while the rooms were clean, there were no frills. The "wardrobe" had a cheap looking curtain across it and the room was quite frankly stark. It was also dark and depressing with (again funky) but inadequate lighting. The air conditioning unit was powerful but noisy and traffic on the man road is invasive. I was in a second floor unit away from the road but I could still hear it all night. There was only a coffee making machine (not kettle for Brits who prefer tea, and small plastic straws to stir with). The accommodation is also grossly overpriced for a basic motel. It's one big advantage is its proximity to the Farmers Market shopping centre. Definitely NOT recommended.

name: W Los Angeles - Westwood
title: “Good Alternative to Hyatt Century City”
text:
We travel to LA about 6 weekends a year and usually stay at the Hyatt Century City. We had been wanting to check out the W sowWe stayed here Saturday night to take in a baseball game, We had a corner suite. Here are some pros and cons:
Pros: Room was large, room service is all night; mini bar nicely stocked, comfy bed, quiet room.
Cons: There was only 1 person checking people in so there was quite a wait-it wasn't terribly long, maybe 15 minutes but still longer than we have experienced elsewhere. The shower/tub combination was quite small-not large enough for two people. The lighting in the bathroom was very poor-no way you have enough light to shave and do makeup. No black out drapes -just plantation type shutters. They look nice but do not keep it dark in the morning.
Overall, it was okay...we will probably look elsewhere the next time we are in town. But if you don;t mind the above cons, this is a nice hotel all around.

name: Trump International Hotel & Tower Chicago
title: “Wow!”
text: This hotel is amazing...the service is unparalleled and the views from the rooms are amazing. Being from Chicago, I thought I had seen everything. But the views from our suite were amazing.

name: Hilton Los Angeles Airport
title: “Hilton Los Angeles Airport And Towers à peine 10 min de LAX”
text:
L'hôtel est idéalement situé à 10 minutes de l'aéroport international de Los Angeles. Il est doté d'un shuttle qui vous dépose exactement devant le comptoir de votre Cie aérienne.
La chambre est assez bien insonorisée malgré la proximité immédiate de l'aéroport.
Les lits sont confortables. Les chambres sont d'une propreté irréprochable.
Le petit déjeuner est parfait, varié, abondant, digne de cette chaine.
Nous avons testé le restaurant "le café" pour le dîner et avons été déçus : la caesar salade à 20$ avec 4 petites feuilles de romaine, 4 croutons et 2 petits morceaux de fromage !!! Je rappelle qu'aux USA, il faut ajouter les taxes et les TIP !!
Je recommande vivement cet hôtel si on doit prendre l'avion mais pas si on veut visiter Los Angeles; il est excentré bien sûr.

name: Farmer's Daughter Hotel
title: “Cool and funky”
text:
Great little hotel close to most sights. Still alot of walking involved and found it best to take a taxi. Great staff. Super clean. Great beds but pillows lumpy. 
Excellent restuarant on site.

name: W Los Angeles - Westwood
title: “A hidden jewel in the L.A. area.”
text: A wonderful hotel with glorious rooms (it doesn't get better than suite 803) in one of the best locations in the metro L.A. area. The staff is caring and attentive -- and you'll be spoiled by the best valet staff you'll ever come across."

name: Sheraton Gateway Los Angeles
title: “Any other SPG property beats this one”
text: I have stayed in Sheraton Gateway a couple of times before, and the only reason I stayed there this time is because I forgot that I swore I would never stay there again. I so strongly dislike this hotel. The staff is difficult and no matter what you ask, the answer is always no. They charge extra for EVERYTHING and if you decide not to go with the valet parking (which takes forever to get your car) you are stuck at a public lot across the street in the back of the hotel. It is reasonably priced, but it is further away than you think and it has some antiquated system of checking cars in and out so you end up in a long line. You can't win. Wait forever and pay $28 for valet, or wait forever and hike to your car for $14. I called the day ahead to see if there were refrigerators in the room and there weren't...which is fine, but then I was told that I could request a fridge when I got there and as long as there was one available there was no charge for it. Nope. $20/day charge. Which also is fine - as long as you let me know when I call about it. The rooms are great (small bathrooms), but they are not any better than The Four Points Sheraton or the Westin that are both down the street and do not have all the issues that this hotel has. I would definitely suggest staying at one of those hotels over this one. Oh, I almost forgot. I am an spg member and I pay a freaking lot of money to own 2 weeks with starwood that I never use. At most hotels, I have access to the club lounge with my membership. Not this one. I will not be staying here again...and if good service floats your boat, you should stay somewhere else!

name: SLS Hotel at Beverly Hills
title: “Treated like Hollywood Royalty! The Only Place to in LA”
text:
This was our second stay in less than three months at the SLS Beverly Hills. I point this out because my wife and I are people that love different hotel experiences and rarely stay at the same hotel. We've stayed at the Beverly Hills Hotel, L'Hermitage, Four Seasons but after that first stay at the SLS, we couldn't wait to go back. So much so that I had won a weekend stay at another luxury hotel and I choose to PAY to stay at the SLS again. 
From the moment you arrive,you feel like a movie star. The hotel staff is one of the best I encountered. Whether it was the valet or the housekeeping staff, everyone treats you like you are their primary concern. It is truly a level of service that you read about in travel magazines but rarely get to experience.
The restaurants and room service are all run by Jose Andres, an innovative chef who's The Bazaar at the hotel is one of the hottest tables in LA. All of our meals at the hotels were unbelievable and again the staff were some of the most accommodating and courteous we've encountered. Be sure to have breakfast at Tres and have the French toast(like s bread pudding). At night, have a drink at the bar next to The Bazaar and order the Jose Andres Gin and Tonic or a Margarita with salt air foam. Keep your eyes peeled for celebrities as they flock here.
After you check in, you'll enter an elevator with "other guests" muraled on the walls upon exiting your floor, you'll see a pool table with the words "Satan Loves Sinners" stitched on the side. There's an electronic painting of a victorian era man than slowly changes into a monkey. Your room is as funky as the rest of the hotel. Amazing beds, modern decor, and a tv hidden within a mirror. 
The roof top bar looks like something out of a movie set with a beautiful and attentive staff to match. The gym and spa leave nothing to be desired. You literally forget you are in one of the most congested parts of Los Angeles within the walls of the SLS. They also offer a chauffeured car for short trips.
You can't help but feel like one of the Hollywood elite when you stay here. And you should because all the SLS staff treats you like one! Take my word and stay here on your next trip to Los Angeles. My hat is off to the General Manager of the hotel who not only directs this fine staff but heard about a special event we were celebrating and made our stay extra special. Keep up the amazing work! We'll be seeing you again next year!

name: Farmer's Daughter Hotel
title: “Great Location, but sub-par”
text:
The hotel is heavy on kitsch but light on clean. There was no soap in the room (which still had leftover open toiletries from the last guest), and when we asked for some, housekeeping told me they didn't have any. The soap finally appeared about three hours later. But housekeeping didn't appear at all the next day, so the towels, bed, and trash were never removed or replaced. A call to the front desk got us an apology, but no clean towels.
There were other annoyances to the room as well: no drawers to put your clothes, so we were forced to live out of our suitcase (ok for me, but not my wife), and the only way to turn on the bedside lights was to go to a switch at the front door.
The hotel's location is great for anyone not wanting to drive all the time. It's across from the Farmer's Market and the Grove shopping district, so you can easily eat and see a movie without getting into your car.

name: Hotel Angeleno
title: “Great Location - Fantastic, Friendly Staff”
text:
The Hotel Angeleno may just be the best value for a hotel of its caliber in the LA area. I traveled to LA with 10 other family members for a law school graduation and the hotel was able to accomodate all of our needs [no easy feat when dealing with such a large group]. From Lesly who greeted us on check in (after having helped me arrange a city tour for the group while I was still on the east coast), to Nick our guest relations contact, fount of information, and all around nice guy, to Jower who very ably helped to handle some last minute issues and assisted us through a very smooth check out, all the staff we encountered were always willing to share information and help us out in any way possible.
The rooms were clean and comfortable. The air conditioning worked very well (this is important given the constant highway noise). The pool was nice and the gym adequate.
One caveat though (and do not let this discourage you from staying here). The hotel is located at the intersection of Sunset Boulevard and I-405. There are NO eateries or shops located within reasonable walking distance. The hotel restaurant and cafe are very expensive. Take advantage of the free shuttle service that the hotel offers. Within their three mile radius are plenty of reasonably priced places to eat and shop for groceries (which you can store in your in-room refrigerator) that will allow you to stay within your vacation budget. Also consider having food delivered to the hotel. One night we had pizza, salad, and drinks, delivered from California Pizza Kitchen and the entire family had a pizza party.

name: Hilton Los Angeles Airport
title: “Great hotel overall, but not great value”
text: This particular Hilton is your standard Hilton hotel, with all the amenities that a business traveler could want, nice comfortable beds, reasonable broadband internet access ($9.95), reasonably good if not average breakfast bar, and well-appointed bathrooms. I did feel that the $225 price tag (incl taxes) was a bit steep, so it receives low marks from me from a value basis. I might instead stay at the nearby Embassy Suites (always a good stay). I stay at this Hilton for single overnights when arriving from Asia and before I travel back to the East coast.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Los Angeles International Airport
title: “Schlechtes Dienstleistungsverhältnis”
text:
Wir hatten etwas Pech mit dem Zimmer, war direkt neben Klimaanlage und Eisautomat, dadurch war es immer sehr laut. Auch die Zimmer sind schlecht isoliert, dadurch hört man jedes Wort, wenn jemand vor dem Zimmer durchläuft.
Frühstücksbuffet kostet extra, Parking 19 Dollar pro Tag.
Alles in allem ein sehr teures Hotel mit eigentlich wenig Gegenleistung.

name: Farmer's Daughter Hotel
title: “Farmers Daughter is a Treasure.”
text: Great place!!!!! We had an excellent stay at Farmers Daughter Hotel. The staff is wonderful and the service is unbeatable. You've got to try their quaint little restaurant called Tart, not only were there local people eating there but we were able to do some star gazing at the same time, it was great!! The rooms are like none other we've experienced in our travels. They have that awesome country theme that made us feel at home, from the comfortable beds to the flat screen tv's to the down home hospitality you definately get your money's worth. Don't miss this one when travelling to Los angeles!

name: Hilton Woodland Hills
title: “Priceline = Rude Front Desk Reception”
text:
We needed a place a stay following a wedding and since we were making an early AM departure --- we weren't too picky. We heard of a winning priceline bid for this hotel for the same date we were staying and booked the room through priceline at a great rate. 
Having used priceline before, I am aware that you don't necessarily get your choice of smoking/non-smoking or king/double/single. But, I always believe it is absolutely foolish for a hotel to offer rooms on priceline then treat winning bidders rudely --- which is exactly what this hotel went out of their way to do. 
First, the hotel must have been vacant. We booked last minute for $55. Everywhere else in LA was considerably more. Our friends booked rooms the traditional way the night before. When we called in advance to ask if we could possibly check in early, Rita (the front desk receptionist) looked up our reservation and said --- come to the hotel and we'll see. By the time we got to the hotel at 1:30pm, some of our friends (who did not book on priceline) had already checked in. Rita told us we had been preassigned to a room and that it would not be ready for an hour or two. While she is telling us this --- other people are checking in with the other front desk receptionist. I told Rita that we have to get ready for a wedding and any room will do --- we are not picky. She said that there are absolutely no rooms available. At this time our friends returned from their rooms and told us the maids have just cleaned the rooms near them. Rita told us that all rooms are preassigned and we were assigned a specific room. I asked her to switch and she said it was impossible. Rita was genuinely going out of her way to be rude to us and sincerely did not want allow us to check-in or wanted to ensure we got a bad room. After expressing shock that they would not allow us a room, but allowed four groups of our friends to check in (and knowing that the hotel is not sold-out) and after Rita continuously telling us there is no way --- I asked to speak to a manager. Rita then spent 5 minutes browsing her computer and 10 minutes in the back room before she returned and said there was a room available. 
The room we received was not a special room --- on floor 9 (out of 15) right next to the ice machine. It was two double beds --- although we told her we preferred a king --- we were fine and didn't complain. I was shocked that she was holding this room back and didn't offer to us when we asked --- it wasn't an upgraded room. As Rita gave us the keys --- it was as if she had been defeated. She was quick and rude about it. 
If the Hilton Woodland Hills doesn't want Priceline guests --- they shouldn't put their rooms on Priceline. I didn't care where I stayed. The only thing that Rita's treatment did was to ensure that when I have to pick a particular hotel and book traditionally, I will not return to this hotel. 
BTW, the thermostat in the room is programmed to restrict the temperature from going below 75 degrees (despite the fact that it was over 100 outside) during the day.

name: Los Angeles Airport Marriott
title: “Bien pour une arrivee”
text: Chambres propres et confortable exellent petit déjeuner . Par contre l'hôtel semble vendre plus de place en self parking que de places disponibles

name: Sofitel Chicago Water Tower
title: “Fairly new hotel, great service!”
text:
Sofitel was a fairly new property in a very good location. One large city block away from the large stores, Bloomingdales, Saks, etc on Michigan Avenue. The Hotel is also walking distance to resturaunts. 
The only thing wrong with Sofitel are the weard wash cloths, they look like puppets, and NO COFFEE MAKER IN THE ROOMS. Although you can order from room service, breakfast is awesome.
The staff at the hotel were excellent.
The room was a bit small compared to other 4 or 5 star hotels.
The hotel does allow pets, which I am not one for this feature because of cleanliness issues, fleas, mites and pets sniffing your $300 Boss jeans. 
Sofitel, get rid of the pets. We personally find this disgusting.
Do keep in mind Chicago seems to have a problem with cabs. I personally experience this on a couple of trips. No A/C, bad body oder, you name it, they have it. We are not a fan of public transportation but the trains are fine.
If you want a larger room and do not mind a corporate style hotel, try the Renaisance River North, awesome views but a few blocks from Michigan.

name: Hotel Angeleno
title: “DO NOT stay here. Waste of money.”
text: My wife and I stayed here 26th June to 1st July. On arrival we were asked for my credit card "to confirm booking" I asked why as I paid cash in advance, the guy on desk said "incidentals" I was to pay 50 dollars EACH day and would get it back on last day. So it comes out our spending money, no use getting it back on last day!! Staff seem uninterested and at times rude. Cafe by the pool closed most of the time. Food overpriced and not great. Rooms very basic. For price we paid expect alot more. All this after being told we had no booking (wich we did) Honestly go elsewhere.

name: Waldorf Astoria Chicago
title: “One of the nicest hotels I've ever stayed at”
text: Very friendly staff, no pretensions but everything was new and lovely. The kids were so content with the fireplace in the living room, the terrace and TV in the bathroom mirror, that they didn't really want to leave the hotel, though it was in a fun neighborhood, close to restaurants, the lake, and walk to Millennium Park. The health club made me sad to go back to mine.

name: Wilshire Crest Hotel
title: “A great place to stay in LA”
text:
I recently stayed 4 nights at the Wilshire Crest. Location worked well, it's on the Hop On, Hop off bus route, trips to downtown and Santa Monica weren't too bad, overall as good a location you can get in Los Angeles.
Bed was very good. Bathroom was ok, the shower controls were very difficult, and you either got very hot, very mild or cold, and not a lot in between. .
Loved the complimentary continental breakfast and wi-fi, some of the other LA hotels should take a page out of the Wilshire's playbook!

name: Hotel Erwin, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Great service, great views, great location!”
text: I stayed at Hotel Erwin in late November for a romantic night with my boyfriend, and it exceeded our expectations on all levels! When we arrived, we looked for free parking for a little while with no luck. Then we pulled into the Hotel entrance and the nice Valet named Paul pointed us to an open space RIGHT in front of the Hotel! We grabbed it and checked in, where we were greeted by Aaron. He was incredibly helpful, made us reservations for a great table at The Lobster in Santa Monica, and ordered a cab for us before we even thought to ask! To top it all off, we arrived at our room to be surprised by a nice bottle of champagne waiting for us! We had delicious drinks at the rooftop lounge, cuddled under a blanket next to the warm fire as we overlooked the Los Angeles skyline and the ocean to our right. At checkout the front desk was very helpful once again. It was a wonderful night, the room was clean and modern with a beautiful balcony view, and we had a GREAT time. I 100% recommend this hotel!

name: SLS Hotel at Beverly Hills
title: “This is hotel is ghetto chic.”
text: So I am here during memorial day weekend. The hotel is not in the heart of Beverly hills it's about a 10 minute cab ride from that area. Not thrilled about that. The pool area service sucks and the pool itself it not that great. Not as pictured. The original adjoining room arrangements were not met. They couldn't even put us on the same floor after all. The restaurants in hotel are just average. The room itself is ok girls no good lighting for makeup smokey mirrors cover the room very dark feeling. Linens are just basic not as plush as I had hoped. I would not stay here again.

name: Hotel Erwin, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “party hotel.”
text:
