Service is friendly. room is clean and big enough.
it was a bit noisy since it next by Venice beach, music from bar stop about midnight.
Air freshener in hotel made me headache all the time, it's lucky they don't use it too much in room.
rooftop bar share the same elevator with guestroom, you can expect to ride it with full crowed drunker sometime.
Location is right front Venice Beach, but the area is a bit scratched.
Parking is like $38 per night. Use street parking instead.

name: Trump International Hotel & Tower Chicago
title: “Setting a high standard for service and quality”
text: Well...I may not like to watch him on TV, but Trump does know a thing or two about providing outstanding service. From the minute you walk into the hotel, they remember your name, the service is discreet and outstanding, there is pretty much nothing you can ask for that you won't get. (To their credit, the Concierge was even able to obtain Oprah tickets when every other avenue we tried had fallen through!!!). I was down with a group of women for a couple of days of shopping and culture. Never have I had a group so unanimous in its praise for the service of the hotel. Mind you, it doesn't come cheap; although they were very willing to provide group rates for the rooms (and the group rate was excellent), any service or meal you have within the hotel is super high end. But...you get what you pay for. It is as luxurious a stay as anything you could ever ask for. In fact...we all liked it so much, we're going back for a second shot at it! If you're looking for some pampering, this is definitely the place to go (and to also get some of the best high views of the city!).

name: JW Marriott Hotel Los Angeles at L.A. LIVE
title: “Unacceptable customer service”
text:
I had high expectations for the Marriott, after readying many reviews. The rooms I had booked, (2 doubles interconnecting) were clean modern and of good standard, the pool area was small but nice atmosphere with friendly staff very busy on the weekend. During our stay it was my son’s 11th birthday, after informing the reception staff at the front desk they made a lovely gesture of a wakeup call with all his favourite treats, a really lovely surprise for him. We had some trouble with very noisy neighbours on the Friday and Saturday nights from 11pm until 2am to 3am, I noted that the weekend hotel clientele were young and out to party, the hotel bar during the weekend was very popular and busy. 
My own experience is tainted by the exceptionally bad rude staff member and customer service, on check out. We had issues with incorrect charges on the checkout invoice. I discussed these with the receptionist but charges had not been refunded as I was promised over 2 weeks later.
I booked 2 rooms for 2 adults & 3 children with breakfast included. I was overcharged by $400 for the 2 rooms. At check in or at the restaurant it was not explained that there was a limit to our breakfast spends (our rate included breakfast). However we had a breakfast buffet each day for 2 adults & 3 children there were charges then added for different amounts daily, even though breakfast was included. How can there be different charges although we had the same breakfast daily? I contacted the Marriott help desk on the 7th of September 2012; I am still waiting for a response from them 6 weeks later!! Not enough good Marriott. 
Luckily I booked our stay with Booking.Com they have been fantastic, with their intervention I got most of my money back. 
I would not stay at this hotel as it is not in a great location in LA, unless you are visiting the Staples Centre for one night only.

name: Howard Johnson Inn & Suites - Reseda
title: “sauber, komfortabel, preiswert!”
text: Wir haben ein preiswertes Hotel für eine Nacht in L.A. gesucht, von dem aus wir dann unsere USA-Rundreise starten konnten. Dafür ist dieses Hotel perfekt. Freundliche Mitarbeiter, saubere Zimmer, Bagels zum Frühstück, kostenloses Internet - und die angeblich beste Burgerkette direkt gegenüber. Zur Umgebung kann ich sonst nichts sagen. Dieses Hotel würde ich wieder wählen.

name: Loews Hollywood Hotel
title: “Average Hotel”
text:
Great location for Hollywood walk of fame, but thats about it, everything else is taxi rides away and minimum spend at least $20 to get anywhere else.
The hotel is average, like a 3 star hotel, old and rooms really need refurbishment, 
This hotel was a Renaissance, and now its a generic lower quality brand, from the look of the place, its may have been a case of the Renaissance brand terminating its agreement, for lack of standard, ie the owner probably refused to refurbish it so they dumped it, 
They advertised Club rooms, with evening drinks and breakfast, but on arrival, we were advised, that this type of room does not exist, and we were like WTF, but they compensated us with vouchers in the bar and breakfast in the restaurant.
The conceirge people are absolutely useless and carry a huge attitude, like they really are not interested in helping you.
I would not recommend this hotel,

name: Trump International Hotel & Tower Chicago
title: “Fabulous customer service”
text: Wow - even though you haven't made it easy to tell you how much I enjoyed my stay here (I would add a link for reviews that are easily accessible or an email contact - can you tell I work in the web/internet world??) I am extremely picky, vocal and I LOVED my stay at your hotel. I was there for the Chicago Mid Winter Meeting, one of the largest dental conferences in the world held at McCormick place. My stay at your hotel made me realize that it can actually be a treat to travel for work. It's been a very long time that I have enjoyed such "over the top" customer service. From the moment I pulled up to your lovely hotel from my delayed flight, my long traffic induced cab ride, and my exceedingly grumpy demeanor, I immediately realized I had entered a whole new world. I have stayed at many St. Regis', Four Seasons, Ritz Carltons along with some very nice boutique hotels. It's been a long time since a hotel has exceeded all of my expectations. From beginning to finish you all have excelled at all that you do, from the most charming and efficient doormen, to the front desk, to my great room, to the staff at the restaurant and lounge. I unfortunately didn't have time to enjoy your spa, but the rest was so good that my experience compelled me to tell all of my friends and send you my appreciation. I know there are other public ways I can "rave" about you, but then again, I don't know if I want to share you.

name: Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn
title: “No major complaints - Nice overall”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights during our honeymoon and found this to be a nice hotel. Its in a good location, plently of places to eat and drink that are within walking distance of the hotel. Metro station is a 15-20 minute walk away. Hollywood walk of fame is 1 stop away.
Rooms are fine, although we did have to change on our second night as they patio door didnt seem to seal fully when closed so freeway traffic was terrible, second room slightly less noisey. Balcony just barely fits a table and 2 chairs, so sitting out there was a challenge. Free wifi throughout the hotel. Layout of the hotel is a little confusing in my opinion, I could never find my way back to reception without going around in circles first. 
Parking is $15 per night. Hotel has a nice pool area, gift shop with helpful staff regarding tours etc. Restaurant was nice, however staff seemed a little run off their feet even though it was not full.
Overall we were happy with our stay.

name: The Los Angeles Athletic Club
title: “The Los Angeles Athletic Club in downtown LA- Review of my birthday party and overnight stay”
text: I recently had my birthday party at The Los Angeles Athletic Club in downtown LA. I reserved the bar called Dukes which is located on the 2nd floor of the club. Dukes was the perfect size and it was pretty cool too! I would describe it as an upscale sports bar with a Cheers feel! It was perfect for my group of friends. About 150 of my friends showed up to the party and most of us reserved hotel rooms and made a whole night of it. The hotel staff did a great job of preparing Dukes for my party and they were very accommodating during our stay. The club as a whole had a real authentic and luxurious feel to it. We were all very impressed with the newly renovated hotel rooms and the party was a hit! The following morning my friends and I enjoyed the complimentary breakfast and used the clubs workout and spa facilities. If I didn’t live so far from the club I would definitely want to join and become a member. I would recommend The Los Angeles Athletic Club to anyone who is looking to throw a party, join a gym, or stay in a hotel. This place is awesome!!

name: Waldorf Astoria Chicago
title: “Amazing”
text: We were totally wowed by this hotel. The hotel staff was incredibly attentive and wonderfully with the children. We went for my son's birthday and the staff left a gift and a hand-written note wishing him a happy birthday. It really made the trip special for him. I had a massage while there and I have to say the spa was great. I really enjoyed the relaxation room and the soft robes provided. I also liked the no tipping policy at the hotel. It made things so much less complicated.

name: Hotel Erwin, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Awesome hotel with a fun vibe and great food and rooftop lounge.”
text: Hotel just got renovated recently. The bed was really comfortable and the sofa bed in the suites also just got new mattresses. Tthe minibar is fully stocked with great items. Had breakfast downstairs both mornings we stayed and everyone loved their food. Staff was very nice and helpful. Location right next to beach and not far from Santa Monica. Lots of good restaurants and bars nearby but the High rooftop lounge at the hotel was awesome. Definitely make a reservation.

name: The Los Angeles Athletic Club
title: “wow.”
text: Checking in at the lobby desk made me fear the worst, but once I reached my room on the 11th floor, it was like hitting the jackpot! The rooms are very masculine but luxurious. I had one of the suites with its own living room. The city views made me feel like I was back in Chicago. The hotel offers a free breakfast in the restaurant every morning and it had lots to offer. It was also great getting to spend some time in the revitalized downtown area...so much to see! Make sure you have dinner down the street at Bottega Louie, you won't regret it!

name: Hotel Angeleno
title: “joie de vivre? mah!”
text: hotel scomodo, fuori dalla città, vicino ad una delle tante autostrade, personale scorbutico, camere poco confortevoli, rumoroso, assolutamente scomodo con i mezzi pubblici, lontano dall'aeroporto, reception poco cortesi, non trovano le prenotazioni effttuate e gia pagate, non danno informazioni ai turisti, caffetteria e ristorante all'ultimo piano dell'hotel con prezzi esorbitanti e porzioni ridottissime

name: Trump International Hotel & Tower Chicago
title: “chicago is an awesome place to visit”
text: We didn't run out of things to see and do while in Chicago. Go in October if you love haunted houses...went to one while there and nothing compares to how awesome it was, back home. I am planning a second trip back soon. We stayed in a suite, only because someone paid for it, but it was sweet, amazing view, and we ordered every kind of pillow they had available on their "pillow menu". Tv inside the bathroom mirror was awesome.

name: Trump International Hotel & Tower Chicago
title: “Beautiful hotel, outstanding service and unsurpassed amenities.”
text: We travelled here with a large group for Memorial Day weekend. The outstanding service started as soon as we arrived. Mr. Colm O'Callaghan and the rest of his staff consistently went above and beyond - making reservations, recommendations and accommodating us in all of our needs. The views from all of our rooms were spectacular and the beds were so comfortable we didn't want to get up in the morning. The Terrace bar is a definite must - more spectacular views and the perfect place to enjoy the sunset. The location of the hotel is highly convenient to many downtown attractions. I can't say enough about our wonderful experience here.

name: Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn
title: “Nice hotel, good location - too close to the freeway”
text: My third Holiday Inn that was 'ok' and not spectacular. This hotel would get a higher rating but for the price. A very average room - totaly standard - for over $200 - seems too much. The interiors were tired and nothing seemed exceptional. My room overlooked the parking lot and was very close to the freeway and the noise was audible all night. On the plus side, a centre court area with a pool was very relaxing and warm. Breakfast in the restuarant was very good and great service. I'm not sure what's up with Holiday Inn's right now but they don't seem to be really 'showing up' at all as anything other than very 'average.'

name: Waldorf Astoria Chicago
title: “A wonderful stay, but minor disappointments”
text:
Mrs. D and I booked Elysian for our annual trip to Chicago when we celebrate the anniversary of our engagement, do some shopping and dining and catch a show or two. We booked an Executive Suite via the hotel website and were upgraded to a Gold Coast Suite upon arrival - how nice! The front desk staff acknowledged the anniversary correctly, but later that night a complimentary dessert was delivered to our room, along with a note from the general manager, wishing us a "Happy Birthday." The first of the minor oversights.
Our suite was very nice with a northerly view up Rush Street. The bed was very comfortable and the bath large and inviting. Closet space was generous and the in-room wet bar a nice amenity. Though it was cold outside, I enjoyed stepping out onto the balcony for a breath of fresh air in the mornings. Turndown service came on our first night - but then not again. The second of the minor oversights. 
We dined at Balsan on the first night of our stay and it was really very good. Make sure you order the tarte flambe - rich, crispy and delicious! 
We returned from the Chicago Boat Show on our second night of the stay and wanted to share a bottle of bubbly in the room before going to dinner at Girl and the Goat (thanks Peter, Chef Concierge!) but Housekeeping had failed to re-stock our room with glassware. There was not a glass to be found, so we had to call for delivery. The third of the minor oversights and one that would be repeated the following day, too. On the final night of our stay, it took about :30 minutes to get our glasses and ice delivered to the room. 
We were not able to use the car service described in previous posts. One time the car had just departed and the other time we were told McCormick Place was too far for them to oblige us. 
I enjoyed use of the magnificent workout room and locker/spa facilities and enjoyed a Spa shave with Oscar (a nice indulgence) that left me feeling pampered.
We ordered breakfast in-room one morning and the entrees were delivered barely warm to cold. We used the in-room microwave to warm them and they were edible but not very good. The coffee was hot and strong, which I enjoyed. And for $18 per entree, I would have thought toast would be included. Nope - it's offered as a side for $4. 
Apart from the minor oversights of the Housekeeping staff and the in-room dining experience, this was a wonderful mini-vacation for us and we are sure to return.

name: Orlando Hotel
title: “Ok but we expected more”
text: This was our last stop for 2 nights before heading back to the UK & we had been recommended this hotel before their recent renovation, it was a bit disapponting. The room was clean enough but the bathroom was tired & very cramped. The public area was nice with a free internet pc but the restaurant breakfast was very disappointing, we didn't bother for the 2nd morning we walked down to the Farmers Market instead. The location is pretty good being midway between the Grove & the Beverley Centre,a taxi to Hollywood Blvd was about $35. The open top tour bus stops nearby. Overall we were a bit disillusioned by our 1st visit to LA by the exhorbitent level of tipping expected.

name: W Los Angeles - Westwood
title: “gerne wieder!”
text: Das Hotel besticht in erster Linie durch sein frisches, stylisches Design. (Sogar die Aufzüge wurden nicht ausgelassen) Es ist jedoch alles andere als klassisch: Die Einrichtung der Zimmer erinnert ein wenig an die hippen 70er Jahre, allerdings sehr modern umgesetzt. Die Bar und das Restaurant sind klasse, der Service und das Essen einwandfrei. Meine "Extrawünsche" was das Essen anbelangt (bin Vegetarier) wurden gerne erfüllt. Die Lage des Hotels ist ruhig, mit dem Auto kann man aber Sehenswürdigkeiten und Einkaufsmöglichkeiten gut erreichen. Ein großer Supermarkt ist nur zwei Minuten zu Fuß entfernt. Von den Zimmern in den oberen Stockwerken hat man einen tollen Blick auf Bel Air und Beverly Hills. Alles in allem war unser Aufenthalt tadellos!

name: Waldorf Astoria Chicago
title: “A Night Of Elegance”
text: Our stay at the Elysian was extremely relaxing and enjoyable. Upon entering the Elysian, you pass through an elegant courtyard which eminates a Parisian feel. After which you are greeted by gracious and friendly hotel employees who hold the door, start the revolving door for you and check you into your room. The ambiance in the lobby is exquisite, with a beautiful lounging area and fireplace. The room itself is totally amazing with all the immenities of home, such as: microwave, stove, fireplace,stocked refrigerator/freezer, giant size bathtub, extremely comfortable bed and pillows and the overly impressive television which appears in your bathroom mirror for viewing while bathing. Since we only stayed for one night on a Sunday, we only experienced dining in the Balsan which was truly delightful. The staff is extremely friendly and gregarious, and the food is out of this world. Most of all we enjoyed our visit to the spa. My husband was pleased with his pedicure, and he said, "I have traveled all over the world, and I have never had a pedicure quite like this one." I had a massage from Tarra, and it was truly the best massage I have ever experienced. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone planning a stay in Chicago.

name: Trump International Hotel & Tower Chicago
title: “Donald got it right!”
text: My husband, our 2 teenage boys and myself stayed for 3 nights in July at the Trump Hotel. I looked at almost every hotel available in Chicago before deciding on The Trump. I wanted a memorable time with our family as this was our last trip together before our son leaves for college. I selected the Trump because of it's location, completely non-smoking policy and why not....it looks great on their website! What a fabulous choice... We loved it! We got upgraded to a 1 bedroom suite which allowed us to completely spread out. Amazingly beautiful room.... large bedroom with the most comfortable king bed, living room with tall windows allowing for great views, 2 bathrooms, complete kitchen with big refrigerator.....unbelievable. We took in everything the hotel has to offer. We ate at Sixteen every morning for breakfast. Perhaps it is a little pricy but not that bad. The food was good, service was excellent and the views from this16th floor restaurant were spectacular. We went to the fitness center a couple of times. Top-notch! It was a pleasure to work out with such nice amenities everywhere....individual tv screens on new cardio equipment, bottles of Trump water available, clean and bright room, lots of weight machines, and the views! We also went to the new outside Terrace Restaurant/Bar on the 16th floor. It was a beautiful night and we were lucky enough to get a table. The views of the Chicago River, Wrigley clock and Chicago buildings lit up at night were beautiful. Very memorable! During our stay, we walked everywhere....up and down Michigan Avenue, along the river, to the lakefront.....the hotel location is ideal. We took the Wendell boat ride which we would highly recommend and we went looking for the best pizza (thin crust). By the way, our vote goes to Ginos over Guiordanos! Overall, we loved staying at The Trump Hotel and we had a fantastic time in Chicago.

name: Sheraton Gateway Los Angeles
title: “Great Guest Service by Diane Cheeks”
text:
I would like to first start off by stating that this is my 2nd stay here at the Sheraton Gateway Los Angeles and the 2nd experience has been EXCEPTIONALLY great!! From the time we checked in, to the level of Guest Service over the phone by Diane Cheeks has been wonderful. All things are extremely important due to the nature of our stay. We are here on a medical trip for our 7yr old son. Diane has made certain that erroneously charges were removed and we had ample enough towels. She always called back to ensure we were okay.
We are grateful and blessed to have been serviced by Diane Cheeks. 
As a result, my husband and I will definitely consider the Sheraton Gateway L.A. for all future stays when we are in the LAX area. 
Warmest,
Freunda "TeAnn" Gray
Room #1020

name: Courtyard Los Angeles LAX/Century Boulevard
title: “convenient airport hotel - these guys are pros (and pretty cool, too)”
text: Spent a whopping 5 hours at this hotel but they were the most convenient, hassle-free 5 hours we could have hoped for leading up to our flight back home. Had a very late check in (no problem) with good AAA rate, had plenty of PCs and printer stations to print out our boarding passes (super convenient), shuttle driver was pumped and ready at 6am to get people to the terminal asap, and coffee was brewed and ready. Rooms are what you expect - cookie cutter but clean and modern. Wouldn't necessarily plan an extended stay here since they cater to the traveler on-the-go but kudos to the Courtyard for helping end our trip on good note.

name: The Los Angeles Athletic Club
title: “Great Place to Stay in LA”
text: I stay at the LAAC once a month and I love it. I especially appreciate the workout facilities. The buffet breakfast is wonderful and the staff treat you well. The robes and fruit baskets in your room are a welcome addition. I highly recommend staying here to my coworkers and friends.

name: SLS Hotel at Beverly Hills
title: “Lovely Addition for USC parents”
text:
As the choices of 5 star hotels near USC are not extensive (can't wait for the Ritz to open near LA Live!), we thought we'd try the SLS which is 7 miles away to be close to our Trojan water polo playing son. It has a lovely entrance and a nice receiving staff that directs you away from the restaurant (which seems like the hotel entrance) to the actual entrance on the right. The desk help was pretentious but upgraded us to a suite as we are Starwood gold members. The room has a contemporary vibe although overdone with too many mirrors. We also didn't like the shared shampoo/soap/lotion bottles. With viruses an issue, who wants to touch bottles strangers have in the shower? There has to be another way to be earth-friendly (how about pump bottles that can have santitized pumps replaced between guests?)
Anyway, the restaurant looked fabulous with cozy, private eating areas. However, we chose to eat at nearby Matsuhisa which was a little crowded (sat us at the sushi bar due to "previous table reservations" which never materialized) and although delicious with good service, way too expensive ($270 for 3 people?).
The hotel beds were fine and we like when hotels stretch design to be fresh and exciting. The rooms just aren't as inviting as they could be as the furnishings are a little stark and uncomfortable (and I love modern--it just needs to be more user-friendly).
Finally, we are so tired of the $10 waters in the rooms of so many hotels! If a hotel wants to be environmentally conscious, just have filtered water available for free. It's insulting. Just because one has money doesn't make one stupid. Parking was $32 which is the norm in LA.

name: Farmer's Daughter Hotel
title: “Great Motel for the $$$”
text:
Okay, so after reading lots of posts about this hotel, I was not really sure what to expect with the service and being that it was an older renovated motel how clean it would be. We stayed at the hotel for 4 days and what I was glad to find out when I arrived was that our service was fantastic! The staff was so helpful in answering any question that we had whether it was advice on getting to the walk of fame to the best route to see the lakers game. They were great!
The hotel itself even though older, was fresh looking and very clean. Our room was very nicely done and clean. Great location to boot, I would absolutely stay here next time I am in LA!!!

name: Trump International Hotel & Tower Chicago
title: “A luxurious place to sleep and indulge”
text: My Mom and I stayed here for Mother's Day. The King City View Room was HUGE and extremely comfortable and inviting, very warm. The beds were excellent. The bathtub was amazing with well designed hardware. The color palette was beautiful. I would highly reccomend the pool and fitness center. Some of the room service and spa menu items are outrageously expensive, even comical sometimes, but there was a great variety on the menu, which is great for people with special diets, or just someone feeling like a peanut butter banana panini is a more interesting choice for breakfast then your ususal coffee, muffin, eggs bacon...

name: Trump International Hotel & Tower Chicago
title: “Letting things slip...”
text:
I have been a lurker on this site for a couple years and after my recent stay at Trump I decided that I needed to write a review about my experience.
I have stayed at Trump three times now. The first two times were phenomenal! My family and I have always stayed in the “46 type” room between the 19-23 floors. We love the view of the Wrigley Building and the magnificent Chicago lake front and river. The rooms were always flawless, the service was great and there was not much more that we could ask for. 
Upon arrival our favorite doorman, MK, greeted us by name, said he was so glad that we were back and helped us to check in as usual. It was a great start to what should have been a fabulous stay. Then things started going downhill, first of all, we had to wait a good 5 minutes before anyone came to the front desk. Where was all the staff? One of the male concierge’s came over and started chatting with us; he was charismatic and let us know that if there was anything he could do for us, to please let him know. Well, there is something he could have done, he could have either checked us in or got someone to check us in. Instead of doing either of those things he went back to his desk and started chatting with one of his coworkers. 
When someone finally did check us in they were very nice. She acknowledged that we were return guests and said she was glad that we had come back to stay at Trump. Then she gave us our keys. I need to stop here for a second. The last two times I have stayed at this hotel not only was I not handed my keys, I had someone take my family up to the room, show us where things were and of course open the door for us. As I took the key, I didn’t think too much of it, but after everything that happened during our stay I can now see how our stay was destined for disaster from the get go. 
When we got to our room, everything was beautiful as usual, our youngest daughter called down to attaché to see if she could get an XBOX, and they obliged, two hours later it wasn’t in our room and when we called down to inquire we found out that they had left for the night. In previous stays we had always called the attaché desk as late as 11:00pm with someone there to grant our wishes and now at 9:00pm no one was there? It wasn’t even a holiday. 
Before heading out for some shopping my husband and I decided we wanted to stop by the concierge desk to see our favorite concierge Alexzandra. To our dismay we found out that she was recently transferred to another property. When we did ask the concierge questions the girl either didn’t know the answer or was robotic. I don’t ask that much of a concierge, but when I want to go to a fine dining option that isn’t as mainstream as Charlie Trotters I expect the concierge to deliver, and she did not. 
As a family we heavily rely on a concierge. We like to be able to throw out an idea and have the concierge make it happen, and on this trip things just weren’t the same. We decided to go to restaurants we had already been to since the two concierges we spoke to could not come up with anything that we hadn’t already been to. My oldest daughter is a fashion forward 16 year old who loves exploring Chicago’s indie neighborhoods. Normally the concierge would come up with a detailed plan of attack for her stay, but no one seemed interested in providing a level of service that actually required some thought. Needless to say we were disappointed and she was bored.
I think the most disappointing service issue we had was that there was an overall lack of attention given to my family. The only person who called my family by name was MK, all of the other staff members didn’t even make an effort to address us by name. No one was particularly rude, but at the five star level I want extraordinary and that is what I used to get at the Trump, and it is a shame that that is no longer the case.
During our first two trips to the Trump, service seemed to be of the utmost importance to this hotel, they had staff everywhere. They had great staff. Now, it seems like they are cutting back on their most valuable asset and forgetting why their customers stay there. I don’t stay at a hotel to be left alone; I stay at a hotel to be pampered! I want somebody to open the door for me, I want the concierge to know my name and I want to be escorted to my room. When I am paying thousands of dollars a night, I expect the best, and Trump did not deliver.
Mr. Trump, you have a lot invested in this property, I advise you to go and stay there. I think you should see what your hard earned money has bought you. This hotel is slipping, I have quite honestly received better service at Holiday Inn’s then I did on my last stay at your hotel. We used to LOVE your hotel, my daughters begged me to bring them back here, but after the service (lack of) we received on our most recent visit we will be going back to the Peninsula, as they have continually met our needs without a bat of the eye.
I don’t want a refund for my stay, I want my time back and that is far more valuable than any monetary sum this hotel could refund me.

name: Farmer's Daughter Hotel
title: “'Come On Down'- show prep great!”
text: Stayed 2 nites mid Jan 2005. CBS security guard recommended when we asked about hotels. We came to LA to go on Price is Right and this is certainly the place to stay if going on that show. Right across the street from where you line up at 4am. One of the hotel desk clerks gives a nightly detailed presentation on how to get picked from the audience and other helpful tips. Our room was clean and fun. Decor is Farmer funky. Even the staff dress like farmers- courtyard is nice place to hang out as is the lobby. Nice looking pool that was closed because it was Jan. Great shopping and dining center right across the street "Farmer's Market". Also near Hollywood and Rodeo Drive, etc. definitely need a car. $10 mandatory valet parking is only negative but we'd stay again as it was a clean place and staff was escellent- Even if we didin't get picked on Price is Right!

name: Waldorf Astoria Chicago
title: “Ultimate in Luxury.”
text: I stayed one night here for a Chicago Cubs/Milwaukee Brewers game. It was also my Fiance's birthday. This establishment was extraordinary! I have stayed in world class hotels in NY and LA and this is above them all. The design touches and the level of service is awesome. Also the lunch I had at one of the hotels restuarants was one of the best tasting meals in recent memory. Everything is top notch- plush bedding, Bowers and Wilkins sound system on and on. I was also offered a free upgrade to a larger room upon check in (which I gladly accepted). Finally ,a nice personal touch was when we stopped back into the room after shopping-the GM Kevin left a personal note wishing us a great time at the Cubs game. Highly recommend this establishment and look foward to using the spa facilities next time!

name: Hotel Erwin, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “The Hotel Erwin was an amazing treat, I will most definitely be returning soon!”
text: Hotel Erwin has it all! A stellar location, literally steps to the boardwalk, amazing rooms that are unique and homey all at the same time. The service was excellent, the staff anticipated every possible need and were really friendly and likable. There are not enough words to describe the rooftop bar, you have to see it to really appreciate it!

name: Hotel Palomar Los Angeles - Westwood - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Love this hotel”
text: I've stayed at the Palomar several times for both business and pleasure, alone and with my family. The staff is unfailingly welcoming and friendly and the vibe in the lobby inviting. The rooms are spacious and well appointed. If you have a dog you can bring it, but if you don't you won't feel in anyway intruded upon by others' pets. When my daughter has joined me she has enjoyed the pool. I'm a big Kimpton fan--they always do it right. The hotel is on a rather deserted strip, but you can walk to Westwood in about 15 minutes. Or, heck, it's L.A. what are you doing walking anyway? DRIVE!

name: Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn
title: “Great hotel - excellent location”
text:
we stayed with 2 children at the Beverly garland. the room was spacious, clean and comfortable, they have a very nice pool and jacuzzi, laundry room (which was very very convenient-wash and dry-3$ a piece).
wifi in the room, and a free shuttle bus to the metro and universal studios.
There is a small playground and a tennis court and a fitness room on the property.
There is also restaurant right outside the hotal named "tula" --food just ok and service very slow.
we loved how close the hotel was to universal and the city walk.
i would defiantly stay here again.

name: Hotel Palomar Los Angeles - Westwood - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “extremely nice”
text: I was in LA on business and was put up here by my company. The hotel is very nice. The staff were very nice. I had left my telephone charging cable at the previous hotel on this business trip, and the hotel let me charge my phone each night at the lobby so I'd have a phone for business each day.

name: Hyatt Regency Century Plaza
title: “Ba?ka bir yer dü?ünemeyiz”
text: Her gidi?imizde burada kal?yoruz Kalmaya da devam edece?iz. Lokasyon ve hizmet mükemmel

name: Farmer's Daughter Hotel
title: “terrible”
text: I read the reviews and went to their misleading web site and thought this would be a great place to stay. It reminded me of the bates motel with kitsch!!! We made reservations for the week but only stayed one night cause we already payed for it. The next morning at check out they charged us an extra 80 bucks for canceling! we were also charged twice on my credit card and i'm still waiting for my refund. now for the nice-the motel is right across from the grove and you get free parking.there are many other better hotels for the same price very nearby, pass on this one

name: Hyatt Regency Century Plaza
title: “Hochwertige und einen angenehmen Aufentha”
text:
Das erste, was Sie bemerken, wenn Sie das Hotel betreten wird, ist seine Größe. Es ist in einer fantastischen Lage mit Malls und Einkaufszentren gelegen ganz in der Nähe. Achten Sie darauf, ein Zimmer mit Downtown LA als die Skyline kann atemberaubend sein, an klaren Tagen zu erhalten. Der Service hier ist Durchschnitt beim Vergleich gegen den Rest der LA Hotels, aber tat es keinen Abbruch meines Aufenthaltes.
Leider aber gibt es einen schönen Pool habe ich nicht die Chance bekommen, es zu genießen. Es scheint, als würde es eine angenehme Erfahrung sein.

name: Hyatt Regency Century Plaza
title: “wunderschöner Pool, große Zimmer mit Balkon, gerne wieder”
text:
Nachdem wir freundlich empfangen wurden, waren wir sehr überrascht von unserem Zimmer: es war sehr groß, sauber und hatte sogar einen Balkon. Lediglich ein paar Zigarettenkippen lagen auf unserem Balkon, die das Housekeeping aber sofort entfernt hat.
Eine besondere Erwähnung sollte der Pool erwähnen, der wunderschön ist. Überraschenderweise ist er auch nie überfüllt.
Das Shopping-Viertel im Rodeo Drive ist weiter entfernt, aber eine Mall und ein Kino in der Nähe bieten auch viel Ablenkung.
Einzig der Concierge Service wirkt leicht distanziert.
Der Starbucks in der Lobby schließt relativ schnell, also sollte man mit seinem Frühstück nicht zu lange warten.
Internet im Zimmer ist zu teuer, in der Lobby dafür gratis. Parken war für L.A.-Verhältnisse sehr günstig (um die 20 Dollar für das Valet Parking!)

name: Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn
title: “Beverly Garland Hotel Review - Perfect for Families Visiting SoCal!”
text:
We discovered this gem of a hotel quite by accident through Priceline.com and boy, what a find! The room we had (kids' suite + king bed room plus breakfast) was well worth it. The restaurant was nice, and that way we got breakfast out of the way early & didn't have to go anywhere else. It's listed at $240 a night, but we got a deal through Priceline. The only surprise was the extra $14 we had to pay for parking. But hey, it's L.A., so I guess that's appropriate for the area.
The Beverly Garland hotel is the perfect solution for families visiting Universal City Studios and other Southern California attractions. Hollywood & Vine, Grauman's Chinese Theatre, Madame Tussaud's Hollywood Wax Museum, and so much more are just a brief drive away. Or take the complimentary shuttle, which will take you pretty much anywhere, even to the Metro subway (I felt safe riding it with our kids, by the way).
Kids' Suites are what make the Beverly Garland hotel perfect for families. We stayed in the Deluxe Kids' Suite room (it's huge!), which has a partitioned-off area that gives kids the sense that they have their own room. Its kid-friendly decorations, separate TV, CD player, video games, and bunk beds made our kids feel right at home. The freeway is nearby, but it didn't bother our sleeping at all. 
In the "adult" part of the room (by itself it's twice as big as a regular motel room at least), there's a king-sized bed, dining table and chairs, another TV, wireless Internet, coffee maker, refrigerator, microwave, comfy sofa, and more. So both us adults and our kids had an area to ourselves to take a break from being together 24/7! Nice.
The kids enjoyed the pool and the nice play area. Kids stay free, btw, and they eat free at the restaurant on the premises. In the summer the Beverly Garland hotel has "dive-in" movies and a poolside bar. 
All in all, I highly recommend this hotel! We will be back for sure!

name: JW Marriott Hotel Los Angeles at L.A. LIVE
title: “Beautiful hotel”
text: Hotel room was luxurious, service was excellent. I would happily stay here again and recommend it totally.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Hollywood Walk of Fame
title: “Fantastic Location & very good service”
text:
Stayed here for two nights for a quick weekend away to LA. 
Hotel is a bit difficult to cross the road to the entrance when driving at night as super busy with traffic, however, easy enough.
Valet parking was useful as parking is a premium around town. Literally 5 min walk to all things Hollywood & close to shops, places to eat & tour offices etc. Noise from road was a little noisy but wedidnt have a huge problem with it.
Room was spacious, basic layout & clean. Bed very comfy.
Serivce was excellent. Staff were very accommodating & even gave me some toothpaste which was lovely! Also helped organized star tour aswell which picks up from hotel. Other tours can also be organized there too. Staff were not over bearing but particularly friendly, especially front desk staff. The lady who looks after the breakfast room was also good & very appropriate & professional when guests were asking extremely stupid requests at breakfast!
Breakfast included too which a lot of other places chagre extra. Basic hot food & continential options, very adequate.
Overall enjoyed our stay. Would recommend as value for money compared to similar hotels nearby. Apparently it is rated 2.star which is ludicrous, definatley a lot more than that!
Would stay again & have recommended friends to stay there soon aswell

name: Sheraton Gateway Los Angeles
title: “Good Hotel For The Price”
text: We only stayed for 1 night due to an early LAX flight but it was a good value. The service was great and professional. The room was clean. They had a Starbucks on sight which is always a plus. Great location if you are flying out early.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Hollywood Walk of Fame
title: “Second time and still good.”
text: We stayed at this hotel last year and when we returned this year to the area we did not hesitate to stay again. Many of the same friendly staff are still working there. Great location ...Starbucks and Subway right across the street as well as a good pizza place. Just a 5 minute walk to the Hollywood Walk of Fame, Hollywood Tours and a short drive to numerous other attractions. Pool is a little small for the number of guests. Wi-Fi was working must better than last year. We will use this hotel again when we return to the area.

name: Hilton Los Angeles / Universal City
title: “Great Location but that's it”
text:
We stayed here for a few days before heading home and really only picked it as it was close to Universal Studios. The hotel was built in 1983 and I don't think anything has been upgraded since. It looks very old and tired. They still have old CRT TVs in huge ugly cabinets. The first room we had the bed was broken so that you kept sliding to the side as you tried to sleep. Then what ever was broken, would squeak and clang whenever you made the slightest movement. We complained the next day and they moved us to another room.
The rooms weren't very clean, lots of hair in the bathrooms, dusty and very grubby windows and curtains. The first room we had still had a dirty towel hanging on the back of the bathroom door when we checked in.
The freeway noise was only a humm in the background but you could here lots of noise from the surrounding rooms. The house keepers seemed to work in pairs and were extremely noisy almost yelling at each other in spanish. We tried to have an afternoon nap before flying home late at night, but they put an end to that.
The bar/lounge area in the foyer was closed more than it was open and the restaurant only seemed to do buffets, we were there over thanksgiving so maybe it was something to do with that. They also had private functions on when we were staying and these people would use all the seating in the reception area which meant we had to stand around waiting for shuttles, taxis etc. I thought this was very poor treatment for paying guests.
It's about a 5 minute walk to Universal studios and City Walk. City Walk is the place to go for dinner.
I'd only recommend this hotel if you are planning to go to Universal Studios.

name: Sofitel Los Angeles
title: “Loved it!”
text:
We came here after a week in Tahiti and it was perfect!
We could relax, see the sights and eat :)
The food from room service was amazing. 
The third floor pool was beautiful, and we were 
the only people there! My husband loved their gym,
and I didnt mind it either because we got to met a movie star:)
Everything was beautiful and the staff was very helpful with everything
we wanted or needed. We will go there again for sure!

name: Rodeway Inn & Suites Pacific Coast Highway
title: “A surprising clean, friendly, convenient, comfortable Place”
text: After read the good reviews about this place at Trip Adviser, we booked 1 night. Front desk is very friendly, rooms clean, shower good, flat-screen TV. I particularly loved that the sheets are crispy fresh. Great location. Within one mile, there is a big mall, i.e. Trader Joe, Whole Foods, Peets coffee/tea, Kohls etc. McDonald is right across the hotel. Along PCH, many fast food restaurants, buffets, and seafood restaurant. 24 hours CVS is nearby. We ended staying 2 nights here as our base hotel to hike PV, visit the Glass Chapel, tour Sony Studio, and Santa Monica area. Great price for a clean, comfortable stay. Definitely will be back in we are in this area..

name: Rodeway Inn & Suites Pacific Coast Highway
title: “Very good value for money!”
text:
We arrived at the Rodeway Inn in the late afternoon and were greeted by Mr. Patel who assisted us with the check in procedure and gave us some general info about the motel and the surroundings. Our room, situated on the second level was bigger than I anticipated, equipped with two queen beds, a table with two chairs, a very large tv with cable, airco, a fridge and a microwave. The bathroom looked quite new and was spacious too. Ventilation and water pressure were very good.
Beds were very comfortable and airco silent enough.
There is no breakfast served (only coffee available in the main office), but there are plenty of fast food restaurant in the immediate surroundings. Finding an actual restaurant was a bit more of a challenge, but, albeit few, there are still some choices close by (on foot). The location gave the idea of being in the suburb or a big city, but I got the impression that this is a common impression in many parts of Los Angeles.
We were pleased with our stay at the Rodeway Inn, we found it to be a clean motel that offers many comforts for an affordable rate and that is ran very efficiently by Mr. Patel. I would surely recommend it to other travelers.

name: The Ritz-Carlton, Los Angeles
title: “Perfect”
text:
If you want a great hotel in downtown LA then this is it. A great place to stay, rooms are fab, beds great, service good. We stayed in club and it was one of the best we have been to. A massive room well fitted out with leather chairs etc, great food and drink.
Would recommend

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Hollywood Walk of Fame
title: “very good”
text:
the hotel was clean and staff very helpful and friendly , location is great walking distance to shops rest; and attractions would definately stay again
thank you
A Barry

name: Hotel Erwin, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Wonderful hotel and fantastic service!”
text: We booked this hotel for 2 nights over the internet for an $89 special. When we arrived, we were greeted by the bellman/valet who took our luggage and us to our room. For $50 I upgraded to the partial ocean view apartment. It was wonderful - a living room with sofa, chair, fireplace, 42" plasma flat screen TV, kitchen fully stocked, dining room table and chairs, beautiful bedroom with plush Beautyrest mattress, TV, etc. Both rooms had a balcony. The only negative is there is valet parking only at $16.50 per day. You can park on the street if you can find a place. The views overlook the Santa Monica bay and the Venice boardwalk. There were restaurants within walking distance but at night it was a bit spooky with homeless and pot smoking folks! It was so cold we checked out after 1 night. The hotel has been remodelled and they are going to add a restaurant on the roof top floor. There was complimentary high speed internet in the room. A great place!

name: Hotel Erwin, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Love, love, love Marina Pacific Hotel!!!”
text:
I LOVE the Marina Pacific Hotel. I visit the Marina Pacific every 3 to 4 months to recharge. It is my home away from home. All my friends and family know this is "my" hotel. The rooms are great. The construction took awhile but was worth the wait. I'm anxious for the restaurant and room service hopefully. Everyone from the front desk to the housekeeping staff always go out of their way to make sure my stay is as wonderful as possible. 
It's close to the airport so a shuttle from the airport is easy and convenient. Hanging out at the Venice Beach boardwalk is fun and free entertainment just watching all the people. It's fun to sit on the balcony and watch the crowds from the comfort of your room if you feel like it. Lots of good resturants within walking distance and some even deliver. 
If I ever ran away from home, this is where my family would find me. :o)

name: Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn
title: “I can't say ENOUGH about how amazing the staff is!!!!”
text:
When I was looking for a place to stay in L.A, I just wanted a clean place to sleep. After a bit of research, I decided on the BGHI even though it was a little more expensive than the other middle of the road hotels. I AM SO GLAD THAT I DID!!
I accidentally left my entire jewelry bag (with approx. $3500 worth of jewelry) in the room and they found it and sent it to me. I've become a little cynical over the years and sometimes forget that there are still honest and good people in this world!!!!!
In addition to this, they staff was kind and the room was spotless.
I WILL stay here again!!!!

name: Hollywood Orchid Suites
title: “Fantastic service!”
text:
The location of this hotel is prime for seeing the main hollywood area. When we were staying here, we even got glimpses of Katy Perry when she was performing there! However, because of this, we couldn't see the chinaman theater which was a bit of a disappointment.. 
The staff was superb here. probably the best of our entire trip. the receptionists were friendly and helpful, providing us with lots of information and allowing us to see the rooms before we booked them. House keeping here was also amazing, especially this one lady (whose name escapes me, but she was hispanic and has the thursdays off), who was so helpful especially at breakfast, toasting bagels for us and just providing us with breakfast service even though its suppose to be a self serve thing. 
The rooms were nice and suited our needs well. We stayed in a 2 king bed room which had a well equipped kitchen and dining area. It felt like a small apartment! It was clean and the internet good!
Downstairs, in the basement, there is a laundry room with cheap laundry facilities! Only 1.25 per load washed! same with drying! Stamps can also be brought downstairs. 
The parking was secure and fantastic. There were lots of parking lots, each customised with a famous movie stars name printed next to the number. In order to get to the parking lot, you needed a key that came with the room card in order to open the gate making the parking area incredibly safe. 
Right infront of the hotel is a larger more expensive hotel which has a NYPD small office located within the large hotel making it safe too. because of the closeness of the NYPD, and because the Orchid is at the back of the big hotel, there is actually a CCTV camera monitoring this street, increasing security. 
Additionally, the large hotel infront had a Hertz rent a car base which allowed us to easily return the car we had rented. 
A fantastic location with fantastic services and pretty good rooms! Rather cheap too!

name: Rodeway Inn & Suites Pacific Coast Highway
title: “nice enough”
text: This was a nice enough place to stay for two nights while touring the lovely Rancho Palos Verdes area. Felt safe, and the proprietor was friendly and attentive to the customers' needs. Continental breakfast was small, but had what we required.

name: Sofitel Los Angeles
title: “Perfection”
text:
The Sofitel Los Angeles was our favourite hotel on this year's trip to the U.S. 
From the moment you arrive you are greeted by helpful doorman/bellhops that take your luggage and whisk you to the front desk. From there you actually get conversation (!) and an attentive staff member that personally walks you to the hotel's elevators.
We had a low room that was overlooking the Beverley Centre. There are no issues with noise or light as there are double curtains and proofing on the windows.
The room was spacious and had a nicely appointed bathroom. Our only grime, although minor, was that the beds sat out a bit from the wall (due to plugs for the telephone, etc). We usually sit up in bed while watching TV so the plugs made this a bit hard to do.
The hotel is also not within walking distance of the Grove. We caught a cab (easily done through bellhop at hotel and concierge at the Grove). 
We had breakfast in the restaurant. Very swanky! But we weren't made to feel left out. The staff in the restaurant were, again, extremely good. Making *conversation* and bringing more food than what we ordered. Bonus!
At check-out, we needed to query a charge on our bill and the staff member was quick and efficient. While we were sorting this out, a bellhop from outside came and got our bags and the other front desk attendant assisted in getting a taxi. Such great service!!
We will be back.

name: Jerry's Motel
title: “Great price, great central location.”
text: We were looking some something cheap, clean and well rated. Well, we found it. This place is great. Very cetrally located which was awesome and the rooms were very clean. There is a safe in the room which was great. All in all, I will definitely stay here again! Don't be scared by the location, it's LA not Beverly Hills!

name: Sofitel Los Angeles
title: “Honeymoon Heartbreak”
text:
I am CURRENTLY writing this review from the bed of my room. This is the first thing I have reviewed and considering I am doing it on the first night of my honeymoon should provide some contextual insight into the levity of the situation. 
The good: the valet, bell man, and front desk clerk are incredibly attentive, eager to help, and friendly.
The bad: The rooms are incredibly cramped. The arrangement of the rooms and design are odd and seem incredibly inefficient. After we got our 4 pieces of luggage ( 1 suitcase, 1 garment bag, 2 carry on size cases) we pretty much have to barrel roll over the bed to get around each other.
Rolling around on the bed on one's honeymoon sounds like a good thing, but not in this case. The mattress is incredibly firm. Too firm for me. The springs make loud creaking noises with each movement. In the hour we spent laying down after driving in, my back and neck are incredibly sore.
I called guest services and they sent a young man up with a double bed size mattress pad for our king size bed. He turned to me and asked "Will this be okay?" to which I said "not really.". He returned with a king sized down mattress pad and I helped him put it on the bed. We tried it out, but there was no real improvement. We just made reservations at the OMNI. I am willing to sacrifice the $670 that I paid at the Sofitel and another 400 at the OMNI to get my wife a better bed.

name: Sofitel Los Angeles
title: “Comfy Comfy Bed”
text:
I have never slept so well when travelling. Loved the toiletries supplied at this hotel too.
It was great to be situated right across from the Beverly Centre.
My only qualm would be that the valet/doormen were very pushy. There just appeared to be way too much staff on, and they didn't want to take 'no' for an answer. Frustrating for travellers that aren't use to this practice.

name: Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn
title: “Excellent Customer Service Driven Facility”
text: The Beverly Garland and its staff are amazing! This was my 2nd year here and they remembered me, by name, from last year! (and not just the front desk, but most of the staff) The Staff here is top-notch quality and all about making sure I was taken care of and had an excellent stay.

name: Hotel Palomar Los Angeles - Westwood - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Another great Kimpton experience!”
text:
I am loyal to the Palomar in San Diego, and when I mentioned on my last stay there that I had to travel to LA, I was of course told I should stay at the Palomar in LA. I have to say from start to finish it was another perfect experience! 
I want to add that they had a happy hour wine tasting going on and I was so excited to see that they also had hot cider with a nip of cognac! I was coming down with the sniffles and the front desk girl alerted me to the "Medicine" the hot cider and cognac were perfect for my ailing body. 
Thanks again Kimpton for your great service yet once again! I really need to sign up for your rewards program as I am becoming a "regular"

name: Hilton Los Angeles / Universal City
title: “Really Impressed”
text:
I spend lots of nights per years in hotels traveling for business. That being said, it is tough to impress me or to even break out of the norm. The Hilton Universal City did both. 
I arrived early but my room was ready. The food in the Sierra Cafe (had the chicken & sausage alfredo) was terrific and the service from the front desk, to the dining room staff, to the gentleman who just dropped off a basket of fruit in my room, has been outstanding. Very attentive and overly helpful.
After spending 100+ nights in hotels this past year (2009) this one really distinguished itself and has totally earned my loyalty.

name: Hotel Bel-Air
title: “Hotel Bel Air........where to be glamourous with the Hollywood A Listers!”
text:
The Hotel Bel Air in Beverly Hills was a hotel experience to be remembered.
We loved it in every way.
The staff of Concierge Mark, Recepionist Diego, and the whole team made us feel welcome from the moment we arrived.
Our suite was private, exclusive and soooooooooo comfortable.
The property is the place to be seen in Hollywood and over lunch the curiousity of spotting your fellow guest exceeds the wonderful dining experience.
The valet parking immediately creates a sense of service and exclusivity from the moment you arrive as does the welcome tea, five star home baking , and welcoming staff.
The resteraunt is equally excellent and wortth exploring.
Hotel Bel Air is my kinda hotel .
The drivers by the way are great and worth asking about Beverly Hills.
I want to go back as soon as I can!
p.s........for comtemporary art lovers and those who like the alternative.............check out the wiseman collection down the road!
Remember though that its exclusive and a wonderful chance to see how Fred Wiseman and his estranged wife lived .
Enjoy your stay and tell them I cant wait for our return

name: The Mark
title: “Great Place, First Class Service”
text:
We had a very pleasant stay at the Mark Hotel. Wonderful and competent reception staff (particularly many thanks to Julita Kropiwnicki) made us feel as at home, once we could enjoy all hotel awesome facilities and perfect location next to Central Park. An attention to details that you can only see in top notch hotels (cleanliness, politeness and timing response of staff, decor, facilities). No issue with the early check after long haul flight was a relief! The next few days of our stay there remained in the same style of friendly service and understated elegance.
The Mark is for meaningful memories and a place to call home when you are in NYC. We will be definitely back there.
The family living in Dubai.

name: Jerry's Motel
title: “This is a great place - a hidden gem”
text: I needed a place to stay one night during a huge international solar power conference at the LA Convention Center. Every hotel in and near downtown LA was booked solid by the time I was making my reservation and I didn't want to have to stay too far away and get stuck in the horrible LA traffic on my way to and from the convention center. It was a real challenge finding a place to stay - every hotel in my company's travel booking service was booked except three total fleabags, all with terrible reviews on the Web. Orbitz had nothing close by, there was just nothing available close by. Then I came across some positive reviews for Jerry's Motel, I contacted the motel and they had a room, so I reserved it. True to other reviews, Jerry's Motel is a nice, family-owned, clean, well-maintained and very affordable motel run by Jerry, who is a very gracious and accommodating host. I ended up checking in much later than I intially told him I would, and though i tried calling him to let him know I'd be late, my Blackberry wasn't working and it took me a while to get in touch with him. Jerry said no problem, he was holding a room for me (he doesn't take credit-card reservations, it's the honor system). Free parking, clean sheets and bathroom, nice flat-screen TV, off a busy street but very quiet nonetheless, A/C. When I'm traveling, especially for work, I don't need anything fancy, I just want a nice, quiet room where I can rest and work, and feel well rested when I emerge in the morning. Jerry's fits the bill.

name: Jerry's Motel
title: “$100 less per night than the Westin”
text: For a motel you get a really great deal. I was in town for a business convention and didn't feel like paying $170/night at the Westin so I found this place online. It was only a 10-15 minute walk (about 1/2 mile) from my convention and there's a corner store right next door. Jerry was very friendly with check in and everything. They clean up your bed while your gone and replace towels, which I didn't expect. Each room has a big tv and is pretty cozy. I will definitely come back when I have business in LA again.

name: Sheraton Gateway Los Angeles
title: “Personal touch”
text: My wife and I have been coming to the Gateway Sheraton in Los Angeles for more than 10 years. Over the past few years, a number of employees have stood out by providing exceptional service. This includes two Concierge employees who work in the lounge on the 15th floor, Juan and Veronica. They are friendly and professional, always. Two bartenders in the restaurant's bar (Mario and Horatio) went out of their way to make us comfortable during this most recent stay. Both also provided exceptional service and were obviously very experienced and pro's at what they do. One addtional comment relates to Mark, the Food Services manager. Without knowing who he was, he answered several un-related food questions about the hotel and was more than helpful in guiding us to answer our questions. Hat's off to the staff at the Gateway!! Keep up the good work!!! BH

name: Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn
title: “Fantastic Hotel!”
text:
My husband and I chose this hotel after lots of internet research, since this was our first trip to L.A. This was just a great place to stay for several reasons:
First off... LOCATION LOCATION LOCATION!! The location was ideal, because we planned on visiting Universal Studios, and we were also attending a taping of a sitcom at Warner Brothers Studios in Burbank... the hotel was a very short drive from both of these. In addition, it took us less than 10 minutes to get to Hollywood from there too, and the freeway access was quick and convienent! LAX was about 45 minutes in good traffic, same with Santa Monica pier.
The staff were amazing! When we checked in, I mentioned that the reason for the trip was to celebrate my hubby's recent 40th birthday, and we received an immediate room upgrade. We also weren't charged for parking for our entire 4 day stay, but to be honest, I'm not sure if his birthday was the reason for that... during the massive storms in L.A that started half way through our trip, the power went out in the hotel one day (not for very long), so perhaps we received free parking because of that inconvience... but regardless, it was a $14 per day savings, so we weren't asking questions!
The pool was open and very well heated, and the surroundings were lovely.. well treed. The rooms were spotless. The only "negative" I noticed others pointed out was that the rooms don't have in room safe's but we had no issue with this, we simply locked our belongings in our suitcase. 
Would I stay again... without hesitation!!

name: Hotel Bel-Air
title: “Oasis of Calm, Wonderful Service”
text: We loved our 5 night stay at the HBA. The staff was efficient and very friendly, securing last minute reservations without batting an eyelash and learning our names immediately. Housekeeping was invisible and fast, tidying up our room sometimes seemingly within 5 minutes of our leaving. We loved the location and the quiet it provided, and our room, while on the smaller side I believe, was prettily decorated and was not at all cramped after 5 days and provided ample closet space. We enjoyed a very good dinner and several breakfasts in the hotel dining room, and drinks in the very cozy bar. I would definitely rebook on my next trip to LA. Having stopped into other hotels on this trip for various reasons, I found them to be impersonal and corporate in comparison, as well as priced even higher.

name: Jerry's Motel
title: “Excelente relacao qualidade-preco”
text: Grande retorno sobre o valor pago. O atendimento foi muito gentil e a localizacao eh otima. Tudo o que precisei, inclusive check out late fui atendida. A recomendacao do trip advisor foi minha referencia e eu aprovo-a plenamente.

name: Hotel Bel-Air
title: “Bel-Air southworld culture”
text:
I believe the Hotel Bel-Air is better than The Beverly Hills Hotel and its bungalows. It is similar to nouveau
Californian with in 2004 very Norma Desmond tones.
When I think of it I think of southworld culture and water as still as glass with a big perspective like Devil's Lake State Park of Baraboo, Wisconsin's south shore.

name: The Mark
title: “Stay down the street”
text:
Room was clean and bathroom very nice but service is spotty. Housekeeping and bar people rude 
& not up to par on dealing with hotel guests. No where to sit once the bar gets busy (6:00)
It took asking to see the manager of restaurant & bar to be able to have a 20 minute drink in the restaurant with guests. Overall The Mark needs to work on better customer service.

name: Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn
title: “Great California Experience”
text:
A friend and I traveled to Hollywood and stayed in this hotel. It was a quaint, comfortable shady getaway in the midst of a city. We enjoyed the fireplace and lifesize ottomans while! lounging in the pool area. Most of all the customer service was excellent. The people in the front desk area and housekeepers went out of their way to make it a great stay.
Thank you

name: The Redbury
title: “Great for extended stays”
text: I stayed for an entire week at The Redbury while on business and the extra living space and kitchen area was definitely a bonus for the extended stay. Here are the details: the kitchen has a sink, microwave, Kuerig coffee maker and a small mini fridge, the sitting area has a comfy couch and several chairs with a flat screen on a swivel, the bedroom has ample storage, a ceiling fan and the bed was nice and soft, the bathroom sink area was a little cramped but the shower was amazing. My only gripe about the hotel was the noise from the courtyard on certain nights, but that can be drowned out by turning on the bathroom fan or running the a/c fan. The staff was super friendly and helpful. I'd stay here again.

name: Hotel Bel-Air
title: “Schlechte Zimmer, Kein Service Und Viel Ärger”
text:
Mit 2 Sternen wäre dieses Hotel schon überbewertet, so unser Urteil nach einem abgebrochenen Aufenthalt im so hochgepriesenen „Bel Air“. Weder Ausstattung, noch Komfort und Service lassen für uns eine andere Bewertung als ein „mangelhaft“ zu. Das uns angebotene Zimmer entsprach in etwa den Anforderungen an ein Zimmer in einem guten Motel, nicht jedoch einem Raum in einem 5-Sterne-Haus. Das Zimmer mit einer geschätzten Größe von 25 Quadratmetern machte einen zwar sauberen, jedoch in die Jahre gekommenen Eindruck. Ein kleines zugewachsenes Fenster ließ nur wenig Tageslicht in den stickigen Raum, geschweige denn Luft. Das Mobiliar und die Dekoration wirkten größtenteils abgewohnt. Anspruchsvolle Gäste sollten nicht zuviel erwarten. Dies gilt auch für das Bad. Einfach ausgestattet mit einem einfachen Waschbecken, einer Badewanne mit defekten Armaturen entsprach es ebenfalls nur einer Einfach-Herberge. Einen exklusiven Bodenbelag oder schöne Wandfliesen sucht der Reisende hier vergebens. Völlig unakzeptabel die Hellhörigkeit unseres Raumes. Die Dusche des Nachbarzimmers war nicht zu überhören, genauso wie das Servicepersonal vor dem Zimmer. Morgens ab 7.00 rollten die ersten Reinigungs- und Wäschetrolleys über das raue Pflaster vor unserem Raum. Schlafen – Fehlanzeige!
Auch die öffentlichen Bereiche entsprachen nicht unseren Erwartungen. Die Hotelvorfahrt ist wenig spektakulär. Von einem Parkplatz führt ein schmaler Pfad in einen kleinen unscheinbaren Empfangsbungalow, den man kaum als Hotelhalle bezeichnen kann. Ansonsten erstreckt sich das Hotel über mehrere Gebäude in einer schlecht gepflegten Gartenanlage mit entsprechend langen Wegen. Einzig ansprechend: die Hotelbar, die eine Art Club-Atmosphäre aufkommen lässt. 
Zum Service im Hotel „Bel Air“ können wir nicht viel schreiben – denn er war eigentlich so unaufdringlich, dass man ihn gar nicht bemerkt hat. So haben wir beispielsweise 7 mal um einen Bellman für unser Gepäck bitten müssen, bis dann mal jemand kam. Besonders unerfreulich: das wenige Servicepersonal war auch noch ausgesprochen unfreundlich. Unsere Beschwerden über die Unterbringung wurden einfach mit einem überheblichen breiten Grinsen und Schulterzucken abgetan. So eine Behandlung erwartet der Gast selbst in der einfachsten Absteige nicht. Das Personal im „Bel Air“ können wir somit einfach nur als unverschämt und frech bezeichnen.
Wir haben nach der ersten von vier gebuchten Nächten die Konsequenz aus schlechter Unterbringung, mangelndem Service und nicht adäquatem Zimmerpreis gezogen und sind vorzeitig abgereist. Mit dem Ritz Carlton haben wir dann doch noch ein besseres Hotel in Los Angeles gefunden. Das „Bel Air“ können wir somit niemandem empfehlen. Wer allerdings gerne in Motels wohnt und den Preis einen Luxushotels bezahlen will, der sollte sich dort einmieten. 450,- USD/ Nacht und jede Menge Ärger – das ist Luxus der besonderen Art. Für uns allerdings nicht, uns sieht dieses übrigens auch schlecht gelegene Hotel nie wieder

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
title: “Excellent hotel Stay”
text:
Stayed here for a business conference trip and glad I did. I was greeted with kindness from upon my arrival by the bellmen opening the cab door to the doormen greeting me farewell on my departure. All staff were full of smiles and seemed to be truly glad to work there. Even the housekeeping staff smiled when they greeted me with "hello". 
The hotel itself was beautiful and clean. I didn't notice a speck of fault with the cleanliness. Rugs/flooring looked new and the hotel looked new as well.
Room was a decent size. The bed was comfortable with plenty of pillows. Bathroom had marble-finish with a walk-in shower and a tub. Turn down service was plus. 
LA was warm in the day then cooled rapidly at night and the rooms air system worked well going from "cool" to "warm" in an instant. Or, if you enjoy the cool air, the room had a pull-out window if you want to enjoy it. 
Hotel is located in a quiet area of downtown on the opposite side of the "action" of LA Live and the Convention Center were my conference was held. But the distance and hills made it too long of a walk and $10 for one-way taxi fare was too much for such a short trip. Luckily, a Metro subway station (that's right 'subway' in LA!) was right around the corner. Tip: the walk to the station is down a steep hill (OK for the morning), but when you return to the Omni, take the cool "Angel Flight" incline train to avoid the steep walk up. 
I asked for a high room with a view and was provided one facing Grand Ave with the Walt Disney Concert Hall in the distance. I was able to witness a few TV commercials being made as Grand Ave. seems to be popular road for filming car commercials.
All-in-all, it was a terrific hotel for my stay. I would rate it as a luxury hotel, without the luxury price. It was great for my business stay and I would bring my wife there if we wanted an LA "get-away" couples trip. She'd love it. 
One last tip: Join Omni's Select Guest program before you arrive and get free water upon arrival, daily turndown service and clothes pressings - this was a big savings & convenience on my business trip.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Hollywood Walk of Fame
title: “Second Time as good as the first!”
text: This was the second time I had stayed at this hotel. We went the first time in Feb 2010 and liked it so much that we knew for sure that is where we wanted to stay when we went back. It's only a short walk to Hollywood Blvd. and Hollywood and Highland Center. The complementary breakfast was awesome and saved us a lot of money. The staff (front desk and valet) were both really friendly and helpful. Both times I've been it was just me and another female friend but we always felt perfectly safe in our location. I'll always stay at this hotel when I visit Hollywood.

name: The Mark
title: “Great hotel with fantastic staff (dont be put off by online service)”
text: Second stay at the hotel and it was as good as ever. Spotlessly clean, fantastic staff, lovely rooms. We were let down slightly by the online staff who we spoke to prior to arriving, very unhelpful and at times rude. However, this was just one person and all other staff couldn't be friendlier. Unfortunately a little noisy at night but thats New York for you, the windows are not double glazed and there are so many electronics in the room, its like being in a space shuttle and ended up spending 5mins every night trying to cover all the lights up!

name: Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn
title: “Good Value Hotel & Close to Universal Studios”
text: My husband and I stayed here for 3 nights in Nov 08 and we found this hotel fairly average. It was clean and quiet with all the relevant amenities one would expect for a 3 star hotel. The hotel had a minibus to take their guests to Universal Studios every hour (which was v convenient and it only took only 5mins) and the Concierge was v helpful with giving directions and organising tours to downtown LA, the Chinese Theatre, Beverly Hills etc. Foodwise, the onsite restaurant is OK but a little bit pricey. For decent food head to CityWalk at the side of Universal Studios (although it's still pricey!). This hotel is not close to anything else except for Universal Studios & Warner Bros Studios. If you want to be downtown and nearer to the other attractions - don't stay here.

name: Sofitel Los Angeles
title: “Sofitel Los Angeles”
text: What a wonderful property! This was my second stay and everything was absolutely perfect!

name: Sofitel Los Angeles
title: “Always a great experience”
text:
99% of the time I am in L.A. for business I stay here at the Sofitel. Perfect location, I am always happy with my room with the french doors. I love looking at the mountains. The staff is very helpful and friendly.
The beds are like sleeping on a cloud. 
Usually I have very happy with the food at Simon but this time my dinner and dessert was not up to par.

name: The Redbury
title: “Beautiful Rooms.... HORRIBLE Management!”
text:
I originally wasn't going to write a review about my customer service experience...just ways the hotel could improve...but because I still haven't received a response to my email to management I'll have to post it all here. 
I stayed at the Redbury for an entire week at the end of April so I feel like I got a good feel of how this hotel works. I vacillate between anger at my horrible customer service experience and actual ways the hotel can improve so this review will try to be as levelheaded and fair as I can make it.
I hope that the good and bad will be taken as ways they can improve their service in the future!
Let's start off with the good!
The Good:
-Beautifully decorated and huge! A real rock star meets old Hollywood vibe.The smallest is 750 square feet! The bed was soft and comfortable! 
-There is a DVR in each room so I was able to tape my normal shows and watch them in my vacation downtime!
-Location Location Location! It is a one minute walk to the Hollywood and Vine metro station and only a block away from Trader Joe's!
-Delicious smelling lotion and shower gel!
The Bad:
The Cleaning Crew.
The maid service times were very sporadic! One day it was finished by 10:00 am other days it hadn't been started by 4:00 pm.
I'm quite sure my sheets were not changed every day and the last three days I was missing a top sheet! Other than that the one time I was in the room while she was cleaning-she was efficient and courteous. 
Individual Coffee Machines. 
-I understand these are popular nowadays...but really! A six ounce cup of coffee had been almost drained by the time I went to enjoy it on the balcony. 
I know I used at least 3 coffee pods every morning. A coffee maker would be a lot easier and much more economical! 
Speaking of coffee...
I requested splenda and coffee pods everyday from the cleaning staff (underneath the note I left a generous daily tip) and everyday it was ignored (even though they sure didn't forget the tip) LOL 
I had to go get the coffee pods myself from Cleo and the front desk every few days.
Just a suggestion... only having Bold and Decaf is not the way to go! There are entirely too many flavors to only offer sleepy time tea, decaf and bold coffee!
The Bathroom
-The rain shower is nice and all if you don't mind the lack of water pressure but the water never got steamy hot...more like luke warm. (I was in 312)
-The sink is one of those really sleek flat ones that looks like it needs to be a prop in a sexy commercial. It's completely flat with small beveled edges.Would have been perfect for doing a line of coke in a music video. Not actually conducive for washing your face or brushing your teeth!
My room not ready or properly checked!
-The day I checked in they hadn't itemized the room properly and as I was unpacking two men (they were quite apologetic) came into the room to check out the minibar and such.
-I had to return a DVD that someone had left in the DVD player. There was a vinyl record missing from one of the covers and an open bottle of your water sitting one of the end tables by the couch.
Technical Issues!
-The lighting system is ridiculous! Every night around 3 am the pot lights over the bed would come on and wake me up. I finally figured out how to fix it...after almost a week of staying there. Not to mention you need a diagram to keep track of all the light switches and what they turn on and off. At least 4 different sets in the kitchen and living room alone!
The DVR and remote is way too complicated to work-and I'm a bit of a techie. It's one of those universal remotes and it's just confusing! (see picture) 
No Car Service as stated on the Website!
-The car service...(one of the reasons why I booked The Redbury) was not available. That was a bit annoying but I was told that they would give me a voucher for a cab. Not exactly what I was hoping for decked out to the nines to go to a red carpet event but I didn't have much of a choice. Well I gave them the time and date I would need the cab and I get to the front desk and when I arrived they had no record of it. Sigh:(
Luckily the cab company was "right around the corner" and it literally took a few minutes to get to Graumans theater but I ended up paying for the cab myself.
The floor to ceiling Windows must come with a disclaimer!
-Just a note for the single traveler and non exhibitionist couples...The white sheer shades that filter light so beautifully during the day...are completely transparent at night.
