I realized (around day five) (when the hotel filled up a bit more) that I could see entirely inside the rooms across the courtyard from me. Like everything! Yes, I'm talking to you certain couple.
If there was a light on at all-I could see straight into the room. Please let people know that they might want to draw the black out drapes at night in the rooms facing the courtyard.
I wish I would have realized this before traipsing around my room in my underwear or reenacting the entire end scene from West Side Story. (don't ask)
A Billing Snafu Times Two (or Three)
-The staff tried to charge me twice for internet access even though the terms of my booking offered "FREE INTERNET"
-It took three weeks and a call to their billing department for them to release the 1050 (150 a day for a week ) hold on my card. They were apologetic about it but the excuse was that "sorry that week hadn't been batched out properly"
-My last billing issue was the straw that broke the proverbial camels back!
The Management! UGH!
I was locked out of my room on a very early Saturday morning after being at a film fest for almost 16 hours. 
Long story short. (lol too late?) The manager was rude and treated me like a criminal. I told him that I had been billed that previous Wednesday for the entire amount of my stay (almost 1800 dollars total) and that I had checked my credit card balance that morning like I always do. He said their computer system didn't have any record of it and asked to see proof. (Really? Wow! What happened to the customer is always right?) I had to call my credit card company at 1:00am for them to say... Yes, I had been billed the full amount even though the hotel's computer was showing otherwise. The manager wasn't even apologetic! One faulty computer system and a very tired and embarrassed me later.... I finally got back into my room. The next day I considered leaving-but I figured the refund would be more hassle than it was worth. I even saw that same manager coming out of the Cleo restaurant the next day and he just looked right through me. The management was terrible, and if that situation had been handled with a bit more finesse I wouldn't have left with such a bad taste in my mouth!
I expect MORE customer service at a smaller boutique hotel... not less! That manager really cast a pall on what would have been a lovely vacation and first time to Hollywood.
On the bright side...all the front desk attendants were nice as they could be. I just wish things would have been handled differently! 
Well, that was my honest Redbury experience. I still have yet to receive a return email from management which makes me think that due to the amount of glowing reviews they just don't care about the few people who really had some major customer service issues! I hope this is not the norm and I my email was lost or something. Hope you can make an informed decision from this. Customer service is paramount to me so as a consumer you have to decide if style is worth more than substance! The bottom line? Beautiful Hotel but Horrible Management!

name: The Nolitan Hotel
title: “Modern gem in a great area”
text:
This was my second stay at the Nolitan - first discovered it about 4 months after it opened. The things I love about this place: great location, simple modern decor, comfy beds, not too loud, all the nice little touches from the comp continental breakfast to wine and cheese at night to proximity door keys that I can keep in my wallet and just wave to open the door.
It's been a great home base for my walks through Soho and Little Italy - as well as up to Union Square. I'd stay here every time I come to New York, except the prices have crept up from ~$350 to $465+ - so I have to now save this for special occasions...
Also, make sure you hit the roof deck at night - fabulous views of the city...

name: Rodeway Inn & Suites Pacific Coast Highway
title: “Excellent rapport qualité_-prix”
text:
Ce motel est situé à environ 40 minutes de l'aéroport international.
Le réceptionniste, toujours disponible est aux petits soins pour vous. La chambre est propre et relativement bien équipée. Parking gratuit.
Un bon souvenir pour un prix très modeste

name: Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn
title: “Good Location. Nice Facilities”
text: We visited California to see my son, who is attending school near Hollywood. The location was great. Very conveneint access to most areas. The room itself was nice and clean. Tula's was average food, I thought the buffet breakfast was a bit high for what you got. We only ate there once. The maids are a little late in the day cleaning, they rarely got there until 3 or 4. The elevators were a little slow and parking is $11.00 a day. The grounds are lovely and they have a free airport shuttle. I would stay again.

name: Rodeway Inn & Suites Pacific Coast Highway
title: “Excellent rapport qualité/prix, confortable et propre”
text: Probablement le meilleur hôtel sur PCH. Ayant séjourné dans d'autres hôtels sur L.A, le rapport qualité/prix de cet hôtel est excellent. Ma chambre était propre et spacieuse. Le service était impeccable, le manager était disponible et serviable. Je reviendrai ici lors de mon prochain séjour à L.A. Je vous le recommande vivement.

name: Hotel Palomar Los Angeles - Westwood - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A hip little gem with stellar service!”
text:
I was in town for a business trip working with UCLA and discovered the Palomar through them. UCLA has a corporate account with the Palomar, so rates were very affordable especially for a Los Angeles hotel. I don't know if it is the Kimpton policy, or specific to his hotel, but the customer service is the best I've experienced. Every employee always said hello or asked if there was anything with which they could help me. And, I felt as though they meant it. 
If you order room service breakfast, there is an option to also get your boarding pass delivered with it, which is great!
The in-room furnishings and fixtures are modern and really nice. It seems to me they have thought of everything. I'm going back 3 more times in the next 3 months and can't wait to stay there again.
They are also very pet friendly, and if I were traveling with my dog, I'd love to be at this hotel.

name: The Nolitan Hotel
title: “Great staff, all the extras, convenient location”
text:
The Greeting:
I was across the street from the hotel, which is where the cab dropped me off. The doorman must have spotted me, because he left the hotel, crossed the street, helped me with my bag and welcomed me into the hotel. Check-in was a fast, smiling breeze
The Extras:
Free continental breakfast every morning
Free wifi
Free NYT or WSJ at my door every morning
Free umbrellas (there was a rainstorm all week)
Plush robe, slippers, amenities
The Staff:
Warm, kind, eager to help
The Room:
Modern yet warm. Ample space for me. 
Super comfy bed and pillows
Great bathrooms
The Location:
A few blocks into town upon exiting the williamburg bridge
Steps from Little Italy/Mulberry St and SoHo - great walking neighborhood.

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “Fun for Fashion week”
text: The first time I stayed at this hotel it was fashion week back in February. despite the crowds and paparazzi surrounding the place check in was quite smooth. The room which was a suite overlooking Bryant Park was fabulous. The sweet living and dining area and the very large bedroom were quite nice. But the real zinger here was the very large bathroom. A fabulous tub for soaking and a very large walk in shower with incredible,incredible water pressure was a real treat. The bath products, the robes, bed linens were all quite nice and very,very, clean and white. The management sent up a lovely bottle of champagne and chocolates to welcome us ,probably since we had one of the most exspensive rooms the hotel offers.Since that visit I have stayed multiple times at this hotel and highly recommend it to my friends and clients . If not just for the water pressure alone everything else is always fantastic!

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
title: “Very luxurierst Hotel in downtown of LA”
text: I was there alone for 5 days. The Location is very Bad. But the Hotel is very Good and clean. I wont suggest people to Rest in downtown LA. It's a scarry area. Be careful.

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “Nice Chic Apartment style hotel”
text:
What I notice right off the bat was the service which is excellent. Before I even reach in my purse to pay the cab..my door was open and a firm hand was reaching out for me with my luggage. 
The hotel is very chic,sexy and modern which may not suit everyone taste. The rooms are very clean , simple, modern kind of Ikea-ish ( in a good way).
The cellar bar has a great happy hour with a professional crowd. The onsite restaurant is Koi which has great sushi in a fashionable atmosphere.
The hotel is in great location for restaurants , shopping( Alice & Oliva is right down the street). There is a coffee shop right next door. The Bryant park Grill is across the street.
Great hotel for business or a sexy weekend in the city.

name: Sheraton Gateway Los Angeles
title: “Fun Memories”
text: My husband & I stayed here for 1 night before departing via LAX for an around-the-world honeymoon trip. We'd actually 1st met at the hotel 10 months earlier during a Peace Corps orientation before heading overseas for volunteer service. So we stayed more for the memory of it being where we first met, but it would be hard not to really enjoy the nice, clean furnishings and very comfortable accomodations.

name: Elan Hotel Los Angeles
title: “The perfect reviews say it all - this is a very good place to stay”
text: This hotel and its staff set standards; room was perfect, comfortable; I slept well and that's all I ask for. Breakfast was good - parking was arranged and I was even directed to a local dive when I asked. There is a good sushi cafe just up the road for a quick snack. A taxi was arranged in accordance which a special request I placed. As I said - everything was perfect.

name: The Mark
title: “Wundervoller Aufenthalt - sehr angenehme Lage, zentral aber ruhig”
text:
Ich bin eigentlich ein Fan vom Mandarin Oriental in New York, habe aber nach diversen Empfehlungen das The Mark ausprobiert. Fazit: das Hotel hat mir extrem gut gefallen. Besonders toll war die Lage. Ruhig, aber dennoch optimal gelegen, vor allem bei guten Wetter, wenn man die umgebung zu Fuss erkunden kann. Das ganze Hotel hatte eine tolle Atmosphäre und Einrichtung. Das Zimmer hat mir sehr gut gefallen, auch das Essen war sehr zu empfehlen.
Man könnte eventuell kleine Abstriche beim Service an der Tür, der Rezeption und beim Concierge machen. Das Reinigungspersonal war hingegen wieder super!
Alles in allem auf jeden Fall ein sehr gute Alternative. Oft gibt es im The Mark auch für New York recht günstige Angebote.

name: The Nolitan Hotel
title: “Good choice of a boutique hotel in Soho”
text:
good localization in Soho! Staff was really caring and helpfull in a lot of ways. Room was perfect and the bed, incredibly comfortable. COmplimentary continental breakfast is ok and if you want some different choices, there are plenty nearby the hotel! 
I would stay at Nolitan again!!!!

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “unbelievably helpful”
text:
We (2 of us) stayed at the Distrikt Hotel just before Hurricane Sandy. The rooms were just right for the price -clean, modern. Staff were extremely friendly and the lobby drink of warm apple cider spot on. The locational was good allowing us to walk to most theatres, the Highline and Times Square.
We were booked (and had prepaid) for 6 days but we had to leave early due to the hurricane. The staff could not have been more helpful and accommodating.
We'll be back

name: Inn New York City
title: “Fantastic times ten to the sixth power...”
text: Returned for the second time to this home away from home for another wonderful stay at the Inn of New York City. This time we stayed in the library suite. The rooms were spacious and cozy and afforded us the pleasure of having a family member spend the night with us. The kitchen, as always, came fully stocked with a full breakfast, and scrumptious and elegant snacks and treats. The location of course is splendid with easy access to all parts of the city and more. We can't wait to come back and extend our gratitude to Ruth,Elyn and their staff for their kindness.

name: The French Quarters Guest Apartments
title: “Can't beat it!”
text: We've stayed there twice, and you can't be the staff, the rooms, and the location! Colin and his staff are wonderful, the rooms as clean and the location can't be beat. Great restaurants, theaters, shopping, and a 10 minute walk to most midtown attractions. Can't wait to go back again and visit our friends at the French Quarters next year!

name: Inn New York City
title: “an isle of serenity in a sea of humanity!”
text: Inn New York City has become a home away from home for us on when we are visiting Manhattan for a weekend or longer. Each unit has a unique personality, but all provide the sense that one has been transported to a bygone era. The decor, with tasteful antiques abounding, is serene and genteel, at the same time that modern amenities such as wireless Internet and flat screen televisions are also at hand. The service -- right down to the detail of recalling and providing a bouquet of my favorite flowers on each visit -- is predictably excellent. There is no more romantic or relaxing accommodation in New York!

name: Greenwich Hotel
title: “Sophisticated and Relaxed Boutique Hotel”
text: We enjoyed the location of this hotel, with a very city feeling, yet fresh, sophisticated and upscale. The personel and service at the front desk during check in was very helpful in making dinner reservations and getting tickets for a Broadway show at the last minute on our last night on the East Coast. We liked our room with a bath, large and spacious, and especially the afternoon light in the bedroom. All the extra amenities were a surprise. The bar area was relaxed and comfortable, and a little dark for us. The Italian Restaurant had a stylish design and the food was delicious. The dining area with its bar seemed very popular. We asked for a table away from the bar, which was quieter and we enjoyed looking out the window at the city view. The staff at the entrance were very welcoming and helpful. Enjoyed the boutique size and more intimate feel of the hotel.

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
title: “Pampered by the Omni”
text: Our family stayed here during Anime Expo 2011, as this was one of the top-rated hotels giving a convention discount. We were fortunate to be upgraded to a Club Level room on the 16th floor with access to the lounge on the 17th. The breakfasts and cocktail hour that are included with the Club Level rooms were so bountiful that we were able to skip some meals. We enjoyed the view of the Disney Concert Hall and California Plaza from the top floor, especially in the evening. If you're tired of restaurant food, the Grand Central Market is within walking distance, providing a wide variety of fresh produce, as well as stalls touting a variety of ethnic meals at a decent price. Quite by accident, I stumbled upon the Farmacia y Botanica Million Dollar AKA the Million Dollar Pharmacy @ 301 S. Broadway. Since visiting pharmacies and grocery stores are my favorite shopping spots while on vacation, I had to stop in at this most unusual pharmacy. If you are looking for candles, oils and sprays to bring back lost loves, lost money or good luck, you are in the right place! Back to the Omni--what I most appreciated was the friendly and helpful staff. Despite the crazy cosplay costumes, we were treated as honored guests from the bell staff at the front doors to Jose in the lounge on the top floor.

name: Sofitel Los Angeles
title: “Great location, value & decor”
text: This was my 3rd visit to this Sofitel and once again was a great experience. Friendly & helpful staff, fabulous suite and great location for shopping & restaurants make it perfect for work & leisure.

name: Hotel Palomar Los Angeles - Westwood - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Does customer service exist anymore?”
text: I am a big fan of the Kimpton chain so when I decided to visit Los Angeles I stayed at th Palomar in Westwood. BIG MISTAKE! First of all when we arrived they charged our credit card way more than we were supposed to be charged and they waited the next day to refund the card without the slightest sympathy, then we had a situation with our room and instead of trying to help us all they had to say was "there's nothing we can do," so I decided to speak to a manager (I think his name was Hami) and of course all he had to say was "there's nothing we can do" so I spoke to another manager (Victor) and his response was...yup you guessed it "there's nothing I can do." All in all the next time I decide to stay in L.A I will not step foot at the Palomar Westwood. If every hotel in L.A. is booked I will sleep outside on the floor before I stay there.

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Simply perfect!”
text:
This was my third time in NYC and first time in the Distrikt hotel. I stayed here for 6 nights and I have to say that there was absolutely nothing negative I could say about this place. It is exactly what you want from a boutique hotel in the middle of the city! 
Firstly the location is superb and everything is within easy walking distance (Times Square, Bryant Park, Rockefeller Centre, Fifth Ave, Empire State Building, as well as Bars, Restaurants, Subway Stations, and taxis).
Then I have to mention the staff at the hotel, they could not be more helpful and friendly - this is particularly unusual for New York City!!! They were always on hand to recommend places to go, places to eat, things to try and things to avoid! 
They made an effort to ask about our day, our plans for the evening, and day and simply greet us every time we walked through!
The rooms are a nice size, clean and comfortable. We requested a high floor (room 2603 - 26th floor) and had an awesome view of the Empire State Building! I was also surprised by how quiet the room was given some of the more negative comments on here. The only negative was the lack of bath in the room but then again this isn't something I was expecting, just something I missed after days of endless walking! :-} 
The little extras like the morning coffee bar and evening warm apple Cider, the weather cards and chocolates on our bed in the evenings as they turned down the sheets, the umbrellas they provide when it rains, the dressing robes and complimentary toiletries in the room, and the effort the staff made to ensure we were content made everything more special. 
I would not hesitate to come back and/or recommend this place to friends and family. It truly was a fantastic trip, made even more perfect by this choice of hotel!!!
Do not be put off by any of the negative reviews on here, focus on the positive reviews as they are all pretty much on point!! This place is truly brilliant and we have had such a wicked time in New York!!
If any of the staff read this, I thank you for this and wish you a Happy Holiday!! :-)

name: Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn
title: “Splendita atmosfera”
text:
Hotel molto bello, con una favolosa atmosfera, nel fine settimana si possono vedere i film in piscina, ci sono molti spazi interni ed esterni per sedersi, bere un drink, connettersi a internet. C'è un negozio molto carino all'interno, una piscina molto carina e un bar in piscina simpatico. Noi viaggiavamo con due bambini piccoli e la kids suite è ideale. La colazione eccellente. Abbiamo usufruito del ristorante anche la sera, la cucina è discreta ma il servizio lascia un pò a desiderare, tranne un paio di camerieri molto gentili. La posizione è comoda per raggiungere qualsiasi parte della città e comunque si trova in una zona molto servita.
Ci torneremo, lo consigliamo assolutamente

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Fantastic Hotel.”
text: My fiance and I spent the weekend at the Distrikt Hotel. Our room was small but extremely comfortable, modern and clean. The location is fantastic as well. The rooms are not entirely soundproof (you can hear some noise from the room next door) but we put the fan on and it was loud enough to block everything out. Overall, we had a great stay and we will definitely be returning.

name: Hollywood Orchid Suites
title: “Awesome location, great value for L.A.”
text:
We spent three nights here at the beginning of a two week Cali trip. You cannot beat this location for the money. We had a two room suite with two king beds, one in each room. Kind of weird, but it worked for us. There is an apartment type kitchen if you want to go to Ralph's for groceries, but you're on vacation, why cook? We did reheat leftovers and put together sandwiches a couple of times, and bought some fruit to supplement the meager breakfast offered in the lobby. The room itself wasn't beautiful or stylish, and the beds were spongy, but it was clean and safe and had lots of room to move around. Parking is free in the underground garage, but it's a tight squeeze. The best thing about this property is how close it is to Hollywood Blvd., you go out the front door and cross to a breezeway that leads to the center of the Hollywood and Highland Complex. Lots of restaurants and shopping here, and a quick walk to the Walk of Fame and Mann's Chinese Theatre. We went with the camera early in the morning when no one was around and we could explore the imprints in the cement. At dusk it is a scene to behold. It's apparently cleaner than it used to be, and I never felt uncomfortable, but it is still a little seedy in spots. 
For a great breakfast go to Dukes next to the Whisky a Go Go on Sunset. Really good food and lots of it for not a lot of $$. The Farmer's Market on Fairfax is really fun, good eats there too.

name: Crosby Street Hotel
title: “Location, style and service. What more do you need..?”
text:
I was looking somewhere special for my girlfriend and I to take my Mum and stepdad on his 60th birthday and we certainly found it. 
In the cool heart of soho is this gem of a hotel. Ok the free upgrade for my stepfarther from a deluxe junior suite to the $3750 a night Crosby Suite helped but we enjoyed our standard room almost as much. 
The hotel is beautiful. Looks like it has been around for years but actually only built a couple of years ago. This means it is purpose made to please. There are little touches everywhere (loved the free cuff links) and light streams in from all sides. 
The staff are great but not fussy and the whole place has a relaxed luxurious feel.
I have been a fan of the firmdale hotels for a while and this is another great addition.

name: Elan Hotel Los Angeles
title: “I'd stay at the Elan if ever in LA again”
text: Terrific, friendly and helpful staff. Rooms had everything we needed. Great location, yet quiet rooms. 3 x computers in the lobby with fast internet access + 1 printer. Happy hour is put on by the hotel each evening serving Aussie wines + cheese at no extra charge. A yummy breakfast is included in the rate.

name: Hotel Palomar Los Angeles - Westwood - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Nice Hotel, Way Overpriced Parking”
text:
This is a very comfortable hotel in an excellent location. We stayed here for four nights and had very few complaints. The staff treated us well. The decor was beautiful. The beds were very comfortable with terrific sheets. The TV was excellent. The rooms were well maintained and very clean. Happy Hour was fun (though not the best wines in the world). They have fresh coffee and tea in the morning available in the lobby. Try for an upper floor facing the south. if you're facing Wilshire Blvd., you will hear the traffic noise no matter how high up your room. 
The exercise room is tricked out with lots of brand new whiz-bang machines. The pool is very small as is the entire pool area. There is an outdoor fireplace in the pool area which is a nice touch.
BTW, Boulevard 16, the restaurant in the hotel is excellent. Very nicely prepared food, but not too precious.
*Major Complaint: This has already been voiced by other reviewers--the cost of parking. It is the only option available and is ridiculously expensive.

name: Hotel Palomar Los Angeles - Westwood - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Hip Property with Excellent Attention to Detail”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at the Hotel Palomar in Westwood for two nights over Memorial Day weekend. Upon arrival, we were greeted at the valet by a friendly bellhop who took our luggage inside. Check-in was quick and the clerk was friendly and offered helpful information, tips and suggestions. In fact, all employees we encountered at the hotel were very friendly. 
Our room was on the 12th floor with good views overlooking the city. The room was an average size. The bed was comfortable and the room was spotless. I liked the contemporary décor. The bathroom was a good size and they had nice bath products. There were also several magazines to read in the room as well as the complimentary NY Times available. My only complaint about the room is that at times the walls seemed a little thin. 
We headed downstairs for the complimentary wine hour. It was the beginning of the Kimpton summer promotion that has summer cocktails and Wii games. We had some wine and sangria and played Wii bowling while munching on cheese and olives. Though we didn’t try the appetizers while we were at the restaurant because we had dinner plans, they looked very good and their happy hour prices were quite reasonable for a property of this caliber. Free tea and coffee was also available in the lobby each morning. 
As far as the surrounding area goes, we didn’t spend much time there, but it was very nice and there was stuff to do nearby. The pool at the hotel also looked inviting and there was a small fitness and business center on the 6th floor. 
Overall, I really enjoyed our stay at this property and would stay again. It was easy to find, the staff was excellent, and the property was comfortable and clean. Thank you Hotel Palomar for a wonderful stay!

name: Hilton Los Angeles / Universal City
title: “Horrible, horrible, utterly abysmal (thought I was going to write horrible)”
text: Stayed during 2nd week of October. Waited for 45 minutes to check in. Was overcharged, has been more than 2 weeks and hotel still have more than $400 hold on my debit card. Went to the restaurant about 45 minutes before closing and was told by maitre'd that it would be better for me to go to the lounge because they weren't going to put any fresh food out. I went to the lounge, and the chicken nachos I ordered had no cheese. I ordered a slice of key lime pie, they brought it out and it was still frozen. On the night before my flight, my neighbors were having an out of this world party. One that was still going on at 3 am. I called the front desk. They said they would handle it. The party continued, and I called again and was told that a manager would call back. The party finally broke up around 7 am of its own volition. The manager still hasn't called back. The person at the front desk apologized and said that the manager forgot and even though she had slept onsite, they really didn't feel that she should be bothered. Like I said in the title -- HORRIBLE, HORRIBLE, UTTERLY ABYSMAL

name: Hotel Palomar Los Angeles - Westwood - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “a great place to stay in LA”
text: We stayed at the Palomar for 7 nights during our trip to LA. We'd been to LA before so had a reasonable idea of what to expect about the hotel's location and local amenities. We walked everyday into Westwood village. It was a pleasant five to ten minute walk, and our kids did it easily and without complaint. Westwood has everything you need. and we had good access with our car to all of LA. The hotel is stylish but without being overbearing. We felt comfortable there. Staff were friendly and helpful. Our room on the top floor overlooked Wilshire Blvd. There is some traffic noise but nothing unbearable. After all, it's LA. In room facilities were good. With kids in tow, we kept the mini bar locked. Restaurant prices were reasonable. The happy hour with free wine between 5 and 6pm was a nice touch. The only downside is the valet parking charge. But as we got a really good nightly rate for our rooms, by the time we added valet we were still in front of other comparable properties in the area. The pool area is great. Some reviewers have commented that it is only big enough for 'five or six people'. Don't know how big those people were, but the pool was ample for our kids and others to have a great time.

name: Sofitel Los Angeles
title: “Excellent Stay - Fantastic Room”
text:
This is a great hotel although I am a little biased as the rest of my trip around the US I was staying in 3 star hotels. However the hotel lived up to my expectations of a 4.5 star hotel.
The room was nice and spacious, it was a nice novelty seeing the hollywood sign from my bedroom! The tv was nice and large and the bed was so so comfortable. I liked how each evening they would re-stock the complimentary evian water and re-make your bed if used since the cleaners came to the room during the day. The bathroom was also spacious. The shower had great water pressure and I LOVED the L'Occitane bath products!!! This is what won me over! Great choice Sofitel!
I went to the restaurant twice during my 4 night stay and I thought it was fantastic. The food was amazing. I thought it was reasonably priced considering it was attached to a hotel. The cocktails ordered were also excellent.
I thought long and hard about the location of this hotel when booking as I did not have a car. Although it's not in the most picturesque street like some other hotels, it was very conveniently located. I was there to shop and I walked to Robertson Blvd, Rodeo Drive, The Grove and Farmers Market and Melrose. It was a really safe area for a single female to walk around.
The outdoor pool, whilst small and had intermittent bar service, was very nice.
The only downside was that there was no free wifi. I think when you are paying these kind of prices, wifi should be included. For $9.95 I was happy to walk to the Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf for free wifi.
I would definitely stay in this hotel again.

name: Elan Hotel Los Angeles
title: “Great Hotel, great location, reasonable price”
text: Great hotel, nice and very well located. The rooms are a little bit small, but everything is new, clean and modern. The hotel offers free internet access at the lobby and a very good breakfast. The only complaint is about the room service, which was a little slow when we ordered food. The lobby attendants were all nice and very helpful. I highly recommend this hotel.

name: Crosby Street Hotel
title: “Great Service, Spacious Upgrade, but Still Expensive!”
text:
A fab, fab hotel. Service is very good, intimate, you know you are at a special place just from the fact that the hotel is set back from all of the other buildings on Crosby Street. Room on the 11th, twice the size of a normal hotel room, apparently an upgrade so not sure what the standard room looks like. Very comfortable bed, plenty of space to spread out, great bathroom, likewise spacious. There's a great little smoker's balcony, at least on the 11th floor off of the elevator lobby. Also, ask to be taken to the roof so you can see the small garden and chickens they have up there.
Would recommend on visit to New York but not sure I couldn't find something cheaper with more value.

name: The French Quarters Guest Apartments
title: “Great Hotel, good area”
text:
I booked a room in the French Quarters February 13, 2012 for the next day, Valentines Day. The person who took my reservation was very friendly while taking my information. He checked to see how I was getting into the city, and told me about a parking garage they have a deal with that was only a block away, $30 for 24hrs. 
When we checked in, they were able to upgrade us to a room with a King, originally they only had Double-double rooms. It ended up being the same low price of $200, which is low in comparison to the other hotels in the area.
The room was great (103). Extremely comfortable bed. Kitchen area was nice (keurig coffee machine, sink, minifridge with water, electric stovetop). Large flatscreen TV with DVD player. Desk with a hook-up to the internet (including instructions). Closet had, iron, ironing-board, and a little stool for luggage. Dresser with 3 drawers. Decor was very nice, with a brick wall behind the bed. Bathroom has a large stall shower with a glass door/wall. Room was spotless.
My girlfriend had issues sleeping in the early morning, because the traffic outside (garbage trucks, delivery trucks, etc.) but that is any NYC hotel, especially on a lower floor. Newspaper delivery right outside your door (New York Post). Continental breakfast.
The bar attached to the hotel was very cool. Burbon Street. We had a few drinks there before heading out. There are a number of bars/restaurants within 5 minutes of the hotel.
Overall great stay.

name: Sofitel Los Angeles
title: “Fantastic bed, great looking restaurant/club”
text:
We had a fantastic 2 night stay here. The bed is one of Sofitel's special beds that really was like sleeping on a cloud - I've never fallen asleep so quickly in my life!
The bathroom amenities were high quality (L'Occitane) and I hear that you can request a view of the Hollywood sign (which we should've done).
While I only got a walking tour of the restaurant and club, they looked very stylish, and a great place to spend an evening. The club had a really nice outdoor area, with booths, and devices with flames/fire to keep you warm.

name: The French Quarters Guest Apartments
title: “An Oasis of Calm and Comfort Right in the Center of it All”
text:
Conveniently located 2 blocks from Times Square and within a very short walking distance of Broadway shows, this hotel is in the center of it all. And yet, it's a quiet oasis of comfort. 
Step through the front door, and you feel like you are in your own private brownstone. This hotel has less than 20 rooms and is staffed around the clock. The front desk folks know the guests and are happy to help. When we stepped out the front door into some unexpected rain, John at the front desk, even offered us his own umbrella! 
The beds are comfortable and the linens and towels are plush. Every room has its own safe. 
Perhaps the best part of the hotel is that it is consistently crystal clean. Everywhere. 
I've never seen a better managed hotel. If I win the lottery, I'm hiring the manager away to manage my own home. In that case Colin, you can name your price.

name: Greenwich Hotel
title: “Great Hotel”
text: We have spend 5 days in New York and the first time at the Greewich Hotel, The hotel is fantastic, the spa as well, great restaurant and fantastic brunch on Sunday

name: Magic Castle Hotel
title: “Best Part of Hollywood”
text: We loved Magic Castle Hotel and their staff. We arrived a little after 9a to see about dropping off our bags, and they were super. They gave us our garage card (parking is under the hotel) and offered us to the breakfast. They were able to hold our bags and said they'd call when our room was ready. They had maps and reccomendations and spent the time with us to make sure we were comfortable. When we were able to check in at around 1p, our bags were already in our room and we were offered a glass of a sparkling citrus drink. Take advantage of their extensive snack and dvd list as well. The room was a good size and very quiet. The staff really went out of their way to make our stay amazing and it really was.

name: Inn New York City
title: “Why stay anywhere else?”
text: My wife and I visited for our 10th Anniversary. We have visited NYC several times and stayed in mid-range hotels in Mid-town but they don't compare to this inn. We totally felt like city residents with our own private entrance, a full kitchen stocked with gourmet goodies, and space to move around that you just can't get in a hotel room. The Inn itself has a great location on the upper west side, very close to 72nd/Broadway subway stop and a quick walk to Central Park. Relatively quiet, safe neighborhood. We stayed in the Vermont Suite for the first half of our visit and then moved to the Spa Suite as a treat. Both were very spacious, furnished with lovely, interesting antiques and well appointed with every item one could possibly need. Vermont was very quiet and private. Spa suite was more luxurious and spacious but not as quiet. Service was very discreet and, although there were other guests, we never saw or heard them. With the free goodies and lack of add-ons, the cost is very comparable with midrange hotels like the Sheraton we stayed at on our last visit and we got so much more for the money. Can't imagine we would stay anywhere else on our next visit!

name: Inn New York City
title: “The Definition of Luxury...”
text:
Throughout the world, hotels rooms are criticized for being too small...or furnished with tacky and worn furniture. New York has no shortage of complaints such as these. But this review is of a different place...one that needs no help from me...but is so special, I needed to write something about it.
If you are a traveler of discerning taste, one who appreciates fresh flowers, a leather couch, oriental carpets, possibly a Piano, and the quiet feeling of being in your perfectly appointed private pied-a-terre, Inn New York City is your home away from home. 
The Inn is a renovated brownstone comprised of 4 spectacular suites. The Upper West Side establishment is entirely discrete. No signs point out the property. Upon arrival, we were greeted warmly by the owner, Ruth Mensch, who happily poured us a glass of sherry while processing our payment. 
Our suite, The Vermont, was unbelievable...Antique appointments and a kitchen Julia Child would have happily cooked in...A spiral staircase heads to the lower level bedroom, a quiet and dark hideaway in a bustling city. The high quality linens are changed daily...even the bedspread and the way the bed was set changed every day. All was as should be...great water pressure, high end bath products, fluffy towels and very nice robes.
The suite's bookshelves are stocked with plenty of diverse reading material, from light to weighty...tour guides to classic tomes. Current magazines are also included, as well as brochures for just about every tourist attraction in the city. Delivery menus for many of the area restaurants are also there.
You get a basic supply of edibles included in your costs...a bowl of fresh fruit, bottled water, OJ, coffee, Boylan sodas, pastries, milk, cream cheese...replenished daily. 
Validated parking is $13 a night at a garage 2 blocks away. 
Inn New York City isn't a Hotel or an Inn in any normal sense of the words. It far surpasses the ideas normally considered when using those terms.

name: Sheraton Gateway Los Angeles
title: “Buena opcion si desea estar cerca del aeropuerto”
text:
Escogimos este hotel porque teniamos un vuelo muy temprano al dia siguiente. Habiamos pasado el dia entero en Los Angeles y llegamos al hotel como a las 6 de la tarde. Es necesario explicar que este hotel no esta cerca de la ciudad de Los Angeles. De hecho, yo diria que esta casi dentro del aeropuerto. Es un hotel muy agradable, con comodas habitaciones y con opciones de restaurantes dentro del hotel. A nuestra llegada, preguntamos cuanto costaria un taxi a Los Angeles, pero era muy costoso. El concierge nos explico como llegar a Santa Monica y seguimos su recomendacion. Fue una excelente idea. Tomamos un autobus de la ciudad que nos llevo a Santa Monica por 1 dolar y tomo como 25 minutos para llegar. Una vez en Santa Monica fuimos a la playa y luego a una calle peatonal y centro comercial que nos agrado mucho.
Al dia siguiente, el mismo hotel nos ofrecio un shuttle gratis para llevarnos a nuestras terminales del aeropuerto. En unos pocos minutos estabamos chequeandonos para nuestros vuelos.

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
title: “Enjoyed our stay!”
text: We spent 3 nights pre-cruise at the Omni. We really enjoyed our stay, the rooms were spacious and comfortable, the entrance and public rooms were beautiful, and the staff were friendly and accomodating. We didn't use the hotel's shuttle bus, but the area between the hotel and the subway could be a bit scary at night. We weren't sure about staying in Downtown LA, but public transport is brilliant and everywhere was really easy to get to. We didn't eat or drink at the hotel as we found both to be very expensive but there was a nice pizza/pasta place across the road which also sold great cocktails,

name: Sofitel Los Angeles
title: “Really nice modern hotel”
text:
We stayed here two nights at the end of our trip in california. LA isnt really my kind of place, as its not the kind of place you go for a wander, you need to drive everywhere which is why I gave it 4/5 stars for location, but Im not sure where else i would have liked to stay in LA as Beverley Hills seems like the nicest area to stay, but it takes a while to get to the beach.
The hotel itself was really nice and modern, the pool is outdoor and heated but small, but the terrace around the pool was really nice with big comfy loungers and quite cool round loungers and flat screens (very LA!).
The only thing that annoyed me is both the constant seeking of tips and the parking, as Valet parking seemed to be $29/day. We stayed in one other hotel in LA the night before and looked around a few, and the expensive parking and seeking of tips seems pretty consistent everywhere. Anyway, to save a few quid we parked across the road in the beverley centre (big shopping centre), and at nights we parked in the road behind the hotel for free until 7am. The beverley centre was good for shopping and had some good value restaurants on the ground floor.
I would recommend this hotel as a nice place to stay in LA and we got good value through expedia.

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
title: “Great stay at the Omni!”
text: We just spent three nights at the Omni. It is a great hotel, with spacious rooms and attentive service. The rooms are just a notch below luxury, but they are spotless. The location is very convenient to just about anything you want to do in L.A. The hotel is in the financial district, so there is not much within walking distance. But, L.A. is not a "walking" city. All in all, we were very pleased with our stay and would book the hotel again.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Hollywood Walk of Fame
title: “Many small problems”
text: Stayed at Holiday inn express 2 nights in july. It may be close too "walk of fame" and Universal and the hotel has got many good rewiews from other who have stayed her, but we where not satisfied. Awerall no problems but many small problems that not should been on a hotel like this make the rewievs not satisfied. For exampel had we problems with our door, we had booked for 5 persons but didnt get any bethclose for the sofasleeper. The ramp too the parking on floor 2 is wrongdimensioned for many cars so you "bump in" with the front of your car. We got home late from Universal one day and there's was no parking left for us, the hotel had rent out all places to people visiting Hollywood bowl. Also the smell on our floor (probebly something from the pool) is almoust disguisting. And the internet did not reach our room. No, overall not as good as expected.

text:

name: Greenwich Hotel
title: “The Greenwich Hotel : un lieu chic et discrèt!”
text:
Nous avons trouvé cet hôtel très chouette, à la hauteur de ce que nous attendions. Il faut bien regarder le numéro dans la rue car les chauffeurs de taxi ne le connaissent pas (il n'y a pas de panneau extérieur indiquant que c'est un hôtel).
Le service et la qualité des chambres sont très biens: bonne déco, très propre...etc...distribution d'eau et de bonbons tous les jours!!
Un seul bémol toute fois, nous avons trouvé que les éclairages étaient un peu trop sombres dans le lobby, l'ascensur, les couloirs et la chambre en général. L'ambiance tamisée est voulue, mais c'est dommage!

name: Trump SoHo New York
title: “Brilliant staff, lovely hotel and wonderful area of Manhattan”
text: We've stayed in New York many times and like to experience different areas that have different things to offer for each trip and this time we chose Soho as our stay last time was in Tribeca and we love the downtown vibe. The room was lovely a high floor with great views of the city with fantastic comfortable bed and spacious bathroom etc etc. But the most impressive thing about the Trump Soho hotel has to be the staff they must be the best in New York! and we do have some experience. In every area of the hotel the staff are just great, helpful, friendly not in your face but there for anything you need nothing else to say really except we can't wait to return!

name: The French Quarters Guest Apartments
title: “An Oasis in the heart of Manhattan”
text:
Lovely boutique hotel. Colin and his staff add an excellent personal touch. He made sure our time in NY was as pleasurable as possible. The rooms had a real unique charm. The bar and restaurant next door (Bourbon Street) offered excellent quality food in a vibrant atmosphere.
A real gem!

name: Hollywood Orchid Suites
title: “New Year at the Orchid”
text:
Our party of four adults spent New Year's at the Hollywood Orchid. Having stayed at a few other hotels in West Hollywood , NoHo and downtown I would place the Orchid in the same category. It's not a palace but if that's what you want then fork over $300 a night and stay at the Renaissance or Roosevelt. See what $150 a night buys you in other notorious tourist traps like London, Toronto, New York, etc.
The Orchid has nice large rooms with two completely separate sleeping areas. We stayed in room 106 beside the pool and found the place quite adequate for our needs. Access to the Hollywood/Highland mall is only steps away, half the room price could account just for the convenient location alone. The parking is quite good, the staff friendly and helpful. We felt that it was good value for the money and would have no problem staying there on our next visit to LA.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Hollywood Walk of Fame
title: “Quiet rooms, perched above the action, and reasonably priced.”
text:
I did a king executive suite (quote unquote)... call it what it is, a large standard room with couch. Quiet, clean, tasteful earth tones and LCD with plenty of cable channels.
Parking is fine, and reasonable. I usually stay at the Renaissance next door and talk about inflated costs, time-consuming elevators and walking...way more expensive than this quaint hideaway just a 5-minute walk from the heart of tourist Hollywood.
I don't do tourist, just stop here when in area for business. So I can say that knowing when/how to drive around here is the biggest concern you shd have. ;) I'd rather be driving in Mexico City...
Excellent golf options close by.
Bathrooms are spacious and nicer than some Hyatts. Room felt clean and climate control was flexible with added value in always-on fan white noise.
As always, HIE has some great locations.

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “5 star service for 4 star price”
text:
This hotel is truly fantastic - every care is taken to make your stay perfect. The rooms are a really good size, spotlessly clean and have very modern furnishings. You cannot hear any noise from outside and there are loads of little details like an iPod dock, molten brown toiletries and free wifi. Plus fluffy slippers and a super comfy robe. The bed is sooo comfortable that you don't way to leave it each morning. 
The location is perfect - 5 minutes from times square, empire state and the rockerfeller and a short cab ride from all other parts of the city. The hotel has a great modern and trendy vibe so feels very boutique but isn't at all pretentious. It's got a great bar too!
The best thing of all about this hotel has to be the staff. Every single one bends over backwards to meet your every need whether it is helping you with luggage or shopping, answering queries at reception or getting you a cab. My friend mentioned she had a bad flight when she arrived and they sent up a drink on the house!!! The best person at the hotel is Sarah the concierge. She made so many great recommendations for places to eat, drink and visit and got us reservations and guestlist at some of the best places in manhattan - she's really good at judging what you'll like and getting you in there. An absolute star!!!
All in all this is a fantastic hotel and in my opinion it's 5 star at 4 star prices. I don't think I'll stay anywhere else in New York from now on!!!

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
title: “Beautiful hotel”
text:
We stayed for 4 nights in LA and we were very pleased with the Omni hotel. Its a beautiful hotel in the financial district of LA. We at first thought oh no we might be miles away from anywhere as we didn't want to hire a car but we were 5 minute walk away from the metro that took us to downtown LA and to universal studios for a fabulous $1.25 each! Could not complain for that! 
Our great hotel offered a free car ride within a 3 mile radius so we used it a couple of times once for the bus station as we wanted to go to Santa Monica (bus journey 1hr 30m so bit of a killer but worth it when you get there) and to a restaurant that was reccomended by the hotel. Tip the driver as its only curteous to do so and I can't believe the amount of people we saw on our whole trip that just refused to tip! 
Amy at guest services was fantastic and deserves credit in our great few days in LA. She gave us fantastic help and advice on what bus trips to do and where to eat, we SO reccomend Maria's Kitchen - gorgeous Italian and very reasonably priced. We took the hotel car there and they picked us back up - excellent service on both accounts!
Our room was big (2 double beds which helped with the jet lag!) clean, decorated nicely and a huge shower seperate to the bath itself. We even used the pool one evening and that was lovely just to go and chill out after a long day out.
Use the Hoppa Buses from downtown LA to do your sightseeing - well worth it!
Universal Studios is a must on anyones to do list and if you can head to Santa Monica beach as you won't be disappointed. 
This place was a great start to our trip...onto San Francisco where I will review the Hotel Carlton next!

name: Hilton Los Angeles / Universal City
title: “Erschreckende Veränderung”
text: Bin seit Jahren in Hilton Hotels unterwegs, weltweit und bi seit langem Diamond Member- was bedeutet, ich bekomme diverse Gratisleistungen, wie z.B. Frühstück... so dachte ich. Das Hotel ist nach wie vor gut aber... auf einmal gab es für die Hilton Honors members eine separate Frühstücksecke- mit altem Brot, Kaffee und Marmelade- und das wars! Ich war doch etwas erstaunt, wie man Kunden behandelt, die im Jahr über 60 Nächte dort verbringen! Die Höhe kam jedoch noch- als ich nach einem cappucino fragte, bekam ich einen- für 4, 50 Dollar. Im hinausgehen kam ich dann am Starbucks ( im Hotel) vorbei- wo ein deutlich besserer Cappucino dann 3 Dollar kostete! Mein Fazit: Hilton Hotels sind durchaus gute Häuser- aber mit diesen kleinen Unfreundlichkeiten haben sie mich, zumindest in den USA vertrieben, nach nunmehr 5 Jahren Treue.

name: The Nolitan Hotel
title: “Great Find!”
text: What I loved about the hotel is it's location (near the subway and loved the neighborhood). Also, the staff are very helpful and accommodating. The hotel itself is quite modern and new so I have no major complaints. The room is somewhat on the small side but it was fine with me. =)

name: Latham Hotel
title: “could be better..but not bad either”
text:
the good:
rooms are comfortable but bland
rooms were clean
some nice staff....some don't even acknowledge you are a guest or exist
great location
free wifi
in room coffee and iron board / iron...blow dryer too.
the not so good:
their courtesy car....called to use it..not available for most of the day....no driver
no drinking glasses of any kind in your room...weird...another reviewer pointed this out
door man while nice could not remember my name and I was there well over a week. if I know your name you should no mine. hotel 101
water pressure.....not so good. 
it was raining...door man could clearly see I had no umbrella...how about offering me one?? 
tip...do not get a room in the hallway by the elevator unless you want to know who comes and goes, what they are saying at 6AM and the ring every time the elevator stops on your floor. 
so with the good and the not good the Latham is just average...with a little effort the Latham could be a really good hotel.

name: Hollywood Orchid Suites
title: “Muy bien situado, apartamento muy espacioso”
text:
Lo mejor de este hotel es, sin duda, la ubicación. Justo detrás del Teatro Chino, a unos metros del mismo Hollywood Boulevard pero en una calle muy tranquila. Justo al lado de la puerta del hotel hay un pasillo que tiene entrada directa al "Hollywood and Highland", un centro comercial que da directamente al Hollywood Bvd., por lo que solamente hay que atravesarlo para llegar a él. 
Estuvimos 4 noches en agosto. Como éramos cinco, reservamos una "Deluxe 2 Bed Suite" con una cama supletoria. El apartamento era muy espacioso, al entrar estaba el comedor con una cama de matrimono, una tv enorme, una mesa con sillas, la cocina completa separada por una barra americana. Luego seguías por el pasillo y llegabas a una habitación también bastante grande con otra cama de matrimonio, armario y otra tv. El baño estaba correcto (váter y bañera) y fuera estaba el lavabo y el espejo. Cambiaban las toallas, hacían las camas y vaciaban las papeleras todos los días.
Las habitaciones están en varios pisos bordeando un patio con una piscina que se puede usar hasta las 9 de la noche. El desayuno estaba bastante bien y variaban alguna cosa de un día para otro. Como había pocas mesas en el lugar donde lo servían, siempre puedes cogerlo y llevártelo a la habitación.
El personal del hotel muy simpático y atento en todo momento.

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
title: “Nice Downtown Hotel”
text:
My daughter and I stayed at the Omni at California Plaza. It was close to activities downtown and travel from there to Hollywood and other tourist destinations in the morning was easy since traffic was coming toward downtown. The room was nice and the beds comfortable. The staff was friendly and helpful with one exception; our in-room safe was locked when we arrived and no one ever came to reset it for our use during our three night stay despite two requests. 
 Parking was by valet only and, at $30.00 a day, was too much. The subway was only a couple of blocks away (Persing Square) and that was convinient when we went to Universal Studios. We had a10:00 a.m. flight out and was aftraid traffic would be bad going to the airport. We encountered a slight backup as soon as we got on the freeway but it was clear sailing after that. A welcome surprise. I would stay here again if the price was right.

name: The Nolitan Hotel
title: “New York visit”
text: The service at the Nolitan was excellent, both in advance of the trip and during. The requests for items to be left in the room were all completed as requested. The hotel in Nolita is in an excellent neighborhood for exploring and the roof provides a great view of the city. The concierge Casandra was excellent including shipping a box of goodies back to Seattle for us. Worth a repeat.

name: The Nolitan Hotel
title: “Unique Downtown Experience”
text:
I have stayed at the Nolitan on two occasions. On the second stay I ended up in a top floor corner room with incredible views of downtown and the Brooklyn Bridge. Quite an experience. Furnishings and finishes are top rate and the little restaurant downstairs, while not worth going across town for, offers a tasty selection of culinary delights. Pretty good martinis, too!
Overall, I would recommend this hotel. The only caveat is trying to get a cab. For some reason it can be quite a challenge to get a ride...we had to hire a car to get to the airport after the bellman spent 15 fruitless minutes trying to hail a cab.
If you are in the design biz, or appreciate good design, I would recommend giving it a try...

name: Hollywood Orchid Suites
title: “Très bon hôtel idéalement situé près de Hollywood Boulevard”
text:
Environnement : Parfait pour visiter Hollywood Boulevard qui est à 2 min à pied, à 10 minutes en voiture de Universal Studios
Accueil : Très bien, un petit mot sympa au check-out pour notre retour en France
Confort : Junior Room 2 Double Beds + Kitchenette (mais pas de micro-onde, dommage)
Propreté : RAS
Breakfast : Oui et choix varié
Parking : Oui gratuit et fermé
Wifi : Oui gratuit et très bien

name: The Pearl Hotel
title: “A Wonderful Room in a Lovely Hotel”
text:
The Pearl Hotel came well-recommended on Tripadvisor and I was not disappointed. It would be difficult to find a hotel more central to everything Manhattan has to offer and yet my room (on the top floor) was unbelievably quiet. I was thrilled to find my standard king-size room was luxurious, comfortable, clean and new. I had requested a bathtub and was given one. The bathroom was large and fabulous.
I paid $400 a night (booking online about three weeks earlier) and although expensive, the Pearl is worth every cent. My friend and I enjoyed the wine and cheese hour, on every day between 4 and 5pm, as a moment's peace during a busy visit. Breakfast is included and is simple but sufficient. You can walk from the Pearl to anywhere in midtown and to Central Park. The Pearl is also directly opposite the Eugene O'Neill Theatre where we saw The Book of Mormon. The hotel staff are helpful, polite and friendly and it was a treat to stay at The Pearl in the middle of the world's most glamorous city.

name: The French Quarters Guest Apartments
title: “Magique”
text:
Nous avons passé une semaine dans cet hôtel en Septembre 2010. J'ai juste un mot à dire: fabuleux!
C'était parfait du début à la fin, accueil et service chaleureux, emplacement idéal. La chambre très propre et la literie très confortable constitue un vrai bonheur après les longues heures de promenade en ville.

name: The Nolitan Hotel
title: “Promising Start”
text:
I was a little nervous about booking a new hotel for fear all the kinks would not be worked out. However our stay was near perfect. 
First--the service was excellent. They were all very attentive and helpful. Our room was not ready upon arrival (3pm arrival) so we left our luggage and walked around for a bit. When we returned, the room was still not ready but the gentleman immediately upgraded us to a higher floor since the original room was not available. Doormen were all helpful We did run into one issue with the access to the offsite gym. At the time they seemed to be still in the negotiation stages with Equinox. We were able to use it the first morning but the second morning was at 24hr fitness. Both gyms were fine so it was not a big deal and I was very impressed how the staff did take care of it and came to a solution. 
Second--the rooms were great but not for everyone. They are small but for NYC standards they are certainly not the smallest. Toilet is separate from the rest of the bathroom which I actually prefer. Shower and sink are open--no door so you need to be pretty comfortable with the person with whom you are sharing the room. The rooms are stark but sharp--bare but chic. Probably falls in the industrial chic category. The balcony was nice as well but would like to see the addition of small chairs. 
Third--the rooftop was great. No tables and chairs but still a great view and a nice place to enjoy a drink. 
The extras--we took advantage of the free bikes. We had to wait a few hours since hadn't thought to reserve ahead of time, but it was well worth it and a lot of fun. The mini bar was the best and most reasonable I have encountered. Hendricks gin for $6, Boylan tonic water $2, St Germain (!!) $6, Piper Heidsieck for a fair price. Honestly, to be able to make a good gin and tonic for $8 in NYC is a steal. I would also suggest to read the hotel book in the room because it is actually helpful and gives good information about the area. 
So overall, great stay. The hotel gives you every opportunity to have a fabulous stay. We got the room at a very good price off a Jetsetter ($207/night) however if they continue to provide this level of service I would pay their current price. I love this area of Manhattan and hope to return soon.

name: The Pearl Hotel
title: “Great Theater district hotel”
text: I live in NYC but stayed here for a week. Great location for this Theater district hotel in a quiet street except for the two theaters on the street when showing. I normally hate going to the Times Square area because of the tourists but it wasn't bad. It was a nice stroll in the morning to catch the train. Rooms were a decent size and clean. Porters and bell boys were friendlier than desk staff. A mini-fridge, microwave, and safe were included. For women used to powerful hairdryers, bring your own.The ones provided were weak.

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
title: “Nice room but...”
text: My two adult sons and myself stayed for just one night at the Omni. The check in, after doing the on line checkin, was great! Everything including my breakfast slips and room key were in an envelope with my name on it ready to go. The room was perfect and very comfortable. The staff was very helpful as we wanted to walk to Staples Center for a concert and they told us the safest and quickest way to go. The breakfast the next morning was my only complaint. We had a total of nine people, six of whom had stayed at other hotels in the area, that all arrived to eat together. The buffet was awesome! The food ordered off the menu was above average but the SERVICE was HORRIBLE! I had to leave the table, after requesting a coffee refill four times, to find someone who would bring us more coffee. (it was our FIRST refill, not fourth or fifth) Another one from our party also had to leave the table to obtain MINIMAL service. I own a restaurant, and tend to be sympathetic to overworked food servers, HOWEVER, this was not the case here. No more than six other tables in use in the entire restaurant, and our server stood talking to other staff for over twenty minutes while we waited. The room and the hotel is fabulous. Don't expect much from their breakfast service

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text:
Location is outstanding
Restaurant is amazing
Reason why this review has been put as average is because when booked on Bookings.com we booked rooms that had two double beds in each because we were travelling as friends. We then were informed we would have to pay extra for this. Did this. Then both rooms had a double and a single instead of two doubles. No explanation of why or how this happened!

name: The French Quarters Guest Apartments
title: “Quelle belle découverte....”
text: lors du volcan islandais qui nous a permis de découvrir cet hotel

name: Loews Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Nice Hotel, Nothing Special”
text: The Loews hotel is a nice hotel but suffers from something that is becoming more and more common...nice upscale lobbies and common areas with mediocre rooms. While the room is a nice size, the decor is bland, boring, and just plain ok. The hallways are very dark and uninviting. The lobby is nice however and SoleFood (the hotel restaurant) is modern and nice.

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
title: “Very good hotel, location ok”
text:
We arrived at the hotel at around 10pm after a long day of flying from London. The hotel does not have an airport shuttle so we paid for a taxi (around $45).
Being tired, we were pleased with the swift check-in. The first impressions of the hotel were good, a nice modern lobby with sealed off garden area, a very nice and spacious room with great view of the rest of LA from the 15th floor. The swimming pool was small but never had more than 5 people so a brilliant place to relax. The gym was very modern. The lady at the concierge, Amy, was extremely helpful and friendly, even at the busy times ensuring that she was acknowledging everyone waiting. The bellman was also great...we were walking out of the hotel to go buy a plug adapter, but he insisted on getting one for us, he didn't even take any money. So as well as the hotel being great, we were mightily impressed with staff.
Even though the hotel is in downtown, we were slightly disappointed with the location being there as a tourist. The plaza next to the hotel was not lively, with only a Starbucks. However, the metro station is only a 5 minute walk and very cheap, around $1 if I remember correctly. It will take you direct to the Walk of Fame, Universal Studios, etc. The Universal Studios area was great, as the restaurant and bar area is extremely lively at all times, reminding me of Piccadily Circus in London.
Overall, the Omni is a great hotel. Comfortable and good facilties although as a tourist, I would have preferred to stay in a hotel in the Universal Studios area, as it is still cheaper than W.Hollywood/Hollywood, closer to the main sites and has is lively all the time. Whether the hotels there are good or not I'm not sure!!

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Great hotel if you prefer living in the busiest part of NY”
text: This is a small (for US) hotel just 1 minute from Time Square, a busy, noisy, worn part of Manhattan I think. No cozy restaurant or bar close by. Only all these pizza and sandwich places. But the hotel is very nice, without a hotel bar or restaurant but a breakfast room. You can choose the 'breakfast buffet' for 10$ and then have different cereals, bred and fruit to choose from. A bit poor.. And then you can pick different eggs and sausages meal in the menu, all quite expensive. The hotel and rooms are very fresh modern and clean and the beds are just like coming to heaven! You never want to get up! Staff extremely friendly, but that's US right?

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Excellent Hotel, good price”
text: We spent 3 nights here and felt it was great value for money, friendly staff always helpful and keen to please or assist. The rooms lack decent views but remember this is central NYC. The bed was devine with feather mattress topper and feather pillows. Breakfast was delicious with plenty of . Big bonus it has free wifi so you can check out the area for nice restaurants. A few minutes from Times Square, we would recommend this hotel to anyone.

name: Westin Philadelphia
title: “Gerri and richard are great concierges!”
text: We came to Philadelphia because my husband had surgery at wills eye hospital. This westin is very nice maybe a bit dark in Lobby but the services were outstanding. the concierges helped us with so may things, quit was very stressful and they managed and helped to relieve some stress and allow us to focus on the immediate problem.

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Distrikt hotel - excellant!”
text:
Firstly, appologies for the lateness of this review, my Wife and I stayed there November 2011 for my 40th birthday.
I booked the hotel from one of the web based hotel booking sites, totally off the cuff with not a lot of research gone into the booking, imagine my surprise when we later looked on TA and found that it was ranked so highly of all the New York hotels.
What can I say that hasn't already been said, the place is a really nice hotel with friendly staff that are always willing to be as helpful as possible. As I said, we stayed there for my 40th birthday and we were also there for thanksgiving, both of these days we had a sweet left for us in our room, a small birthday cake with a candle for my 40th and a couple of small pumpkin pies for thanksgiving. Both of these were nice gestures that made our stay more pleasurable.
The hotel has a small bar and restaurant, we only used the bar once but found it very nice. The barman was friendly and attentive but not intrusive, just like a barman should be, and even poured us small samples of cocktails that were left over from peoples orders (hope that doesn't get him into trouble).
Although there was no concierge the hotel did have a guy in reception to help with anything, and I mean ANYTHING, even handing out umbrellas when it was raining. He hailed cabs whenever one was needed and seemed to be an encyclopedia of local knowledge, it was as if nothing was too much to ask of him.
The only ting I regret about this hotel is that we never tried any of the hot apple cider they had by the door, by all accounts its a little bit on the nice side, just means we have a reason to head back again:)
I have to give this hotel a top mark as there is nothing to fault of the place, the whole of the hotel is spotlessly clean, beds are comfortable and changed regularly, and the whole stay there was top notch. They even gave us a higher room with a view of the Empire State Building, which we asked for after reading about it on here.
My Wife and I are intending to go back to New York and although we would both normally book into a different hotel to get a different experience, this is one hotel that we WILL be going back to.

name: Hyatt at the Bellevue
title: “Pricey -- and in need of renovation”
text:
I'm a loyal Hyatt Diamond member, and I had high expectations as set by prior Hyatt experiences elsewhere. I was disappointed by this hotel. While it is "fine," the room was in desparate need of renovation for the price point we paid (stained carpet; stained couch; ceiling above sink in bathroom with drywall exposed). 
On the positive side, it is a great location, and XIX is a very nice place for breakfast. 
They claimed that renovations are starting this month -- but since the General Manager has stated for three months on TripAdvisor that renovations are "starting now" I'm a bit skeptical.
Net-net, a fine place for $100-150 per night . If you are paying over $250 (as I was), you are better off at the Four Seasons or the Ritz.

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
title: “Fantastic property & great value”
text: Fantastic property - perfectly located for our concert at Disney Hall. Great rooms, amenities, service. Fabulous value. Highest recommendation.

name: The Pearl Hotel
title: “A real Pearl ...”
text:
This is definitely my new favorite hotel in NYC. 
We arrived early morning and were upgraded to a Deluxe King. The room was gorgeous, spacious and totally soundproof considering we were facing the buzz of 49th street theatre goers.. Loved the ample continental breakfast served in a very tastefully decorated space with lounge type sofas overlooking the lobby. No tacky breakfast tables here. The attention to detail is foremost and I will definitely return.. Thanks for a great weekend experience!

name: Latham Hotel
title: “Consider this as a good value option”
text: The lobby was small and there were less staff than I expected. They had a very nice bellman/valet, and the front desk staff were friendly and helpful. The small number of staff could make for a slow check-in at peak times. The room was larger than I expected for the money in this part of town. Decor was better than I expected based on the other Tripadvisor ratings. The business center was sufficient for my needs (computer, printer, copier). The location was good for me (near restaurants, and PATCO station). My family walked all the way from Penns Landing and didn't complain about the distance (about 1.5 miles).

name: Latham Hotel
title: “Great value for one night--great location”
text: My husband and I decided to stay here because we needed something inexpensive for only one night. The Latham is located right near Rittenhouse Square (less than 2 blocks away) close to fantastic restaurants (especially this very cute italian place called Branzini on 17th St.--2 blocks away, get a table in the courtyard.) and close to shopping. This was a short trip to visit friends and we didn't spend any time in the hotel room. It was clean, easy to check-in/out, sufficient for what we needed for a night. And at $115 you can't beat it!! It's not a bad place at all, just not the Ritz. The parking option is valet only ($31). Worth it because we arrived on a Sat. evening and couldn't be bothered trying to find a spot. But the garage around the corner (we found out later) is only $12. Oh well! Oh, make sure you request a high floor, non-smoking! We were on floor 13. I think it's always nicer to be higher up (no noise).

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Excellent Selection-”
text: It was my husband birthday and was looking to stay at the triumph International hotel, however it was sold out and I was extremely excited that we had chosen this property. From the time we approached the entrance Jonathan, concierge greeted us readily available to take our bags and get us check-in. Front desk staff was extremely helpful, with the area. The room was very clean and larger than your normal hotel space in NY. The beds are wonderful..The second night it was rainy, therefore we enjoyed the bar at the hotel. Anthony is AWESOME! He worked a double/triple shift and was there for breakfast has well, we did not sit in his section & had Robert has our waiter. Robert was good but... Anthony had come over to talk with us. He pulled up a chair and start providing us direction and answering any questions we had. Then the following morning he was our room service as well... Anthony continues what you are doing & thank you for great hospitality. On the second night of our stay we had turn down service with a cake and a birthday card for my husband. Very nice touch. THANKS for listening at the front desk/reservation. Upon are return to New York we will stay with the Distrik Hotel again. If I have missed any of the staff names please forgive me, the ENTIRE staffs were great. To the General Manager I take my hat off to you, continue the training that you have, I would like to know what your secret is.. ?

name: Courtyard Philadelphia Downtown
title: “Great Center City location!”
text:
We stayed here for one night back in the fall. Philly is a great town and this location makes it so easy to avail oneself of some of the electricity of Center City.
Check in was prompt and courteous, even allowing us an early check in. The room was a basic King room but was large enough. It was a higher floor so we had a great view of the Delaware River.
There is a nice indoor pool, restaurant/bar and valet parking if one chooses that option. The location right by Penn Square can make it tricky to navigate if you are using your vehicle frequently.
It is within walking distance of the Reading Terminal which has unending eateries. The Courtyard is right by many department stores and right off Broad Street where there is the Kimmel Center and Broadway type Theaters.
Next time we are in Philly I would put this property on top of our list!

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
title: “Friendly and comfortable”
text:
Stayed at the Omni one night for business travel. I found the hotel comfortable, quiet and more than satisfactory for my needs.
Following the advice of other Trip Advisor users, I joined the Omni's Select Guest program (free) so I earned frequent flyer miles and got express check in, several newspapers and a complimentary morning beverage. The staff were friendly and efficient.
The room was large and comfortable. Every convenience one might expect, as well as free wireless internet. The king sized bed was piled with mountains of covers and was so inviting I fell asleep the minute my head hit the pillow (having arrived from the east coast!). As a result, I didn't even turn on the television, but a card on the bedside table listed an array of local and cable stations available. I didn't hear a noise all night.
I could see an outdoor lap pool from my window, so that is available, although, obviously, you could have an audience.
Although there is not much of a street scape in downtown LA, I did take a walk the next morning and there are a few coffee shops around. The Disney Concert Hall is nearby and that is worth at least walking around if you have the time.
In sum, it is a very friendly and comfortable hotel -- a wonderful place to spend a night away from home.

name: Andaz Wall Street
title: “Great Hotel”
text: We just returned from our annual Christmas visit to NYC over the weekend of December 9-11. The Andaz is the best hotel we've stayed in and we've been going every year for the last 15 years. The rooms were large by New York standards, modern, clean and very comfortable. The staff working the "front desk" could not have been more friendly and helpful. The financial district location is a little out of the way for tourist purposes but the subway is convenient and you could get anywhere you wanted quickly. The hotel breakfast was a little pricey but what hotel breakfast in a 5-star New York hotel isn't. If you don't want to pay $50+ for breakfast just go around the corner, there are lots of choices within a block or so. All in all a great hotel.

name: Hyatt at the Bellevue
title: “Stately building with frayed edges”
text:
On a business trip to Philadelphia, I spent two nights at the Hyatt Regency Bellevue. This is an adequate hotel; nothing to write home about but also a decent option.
Pros: The location is very central; there is a full gym (not a hotel gym) attached to the hotel and included in the rates; the restaurant/bar at the top of the hotel (XIX) was elegant and served good food.
Cons: The room was small; furnishings tired; some of the fixtures were in need of replacement; style was very Victorian and could use some refurbishment

name: Andaz Wall Street
title: “Fantastic Stay at the Andaz”
text: A group of nine ladies 25-45's stayed at the Andaz Wall Street for a long weekend, I cannot fault it , it is without a doubt one of the best hotels I have stayed in. Adam (front of house) came out to greet us as we arrived, from there the service we got was second to none. I got an upgrade to a suite which was wonderful, all the staff were helpful, friendly and so polite. The rooms were spotless and had a wonderful relaxed atmosphere. The food was amazing in the restaurant. You get what you pay for!! New York was brilliant. Adam was on hand to advise us on places to visit, how to get there etc.. etc. I would definitely return here. So easy to get uptown we shared cabs 4 persons in each it cost $5 per head incl. tip. New Yorkers do expect 20% gratuity on everything, but I have to say the service we got everywhere we went was worth every penny. It was lovely to get away from the busy city at the end of the day and into the relaxed atmosphere around Wall Street. We stumbled across a fantastic little diner in Chamber Street called The Kitchenette, we had the most amazing lunch with the friendliest staff, their pomegranate belini's were divine. I could go on... Visit The Rock at night, the views are amazing. We all had a Pedicab around Central Park 3 seater carriage cost $22.00 pp, we did haggle for a giggle but the drivers were so lovely and informative we gave them $25 in the end. Ground Zero is a must, very moving and surreal also. The monuments are an absolute credit to the people there. We all loved New York and the Andaz made it all perfect for us. Highly recommend it :)

name: Andaz Wall Street
title: “Not as great as 1st stay, but still better than most NYC hotels”
text:
