My fiance and I stayed at the Andaz Wall Street over Thanksgiving weekend. This was our 2nd stay at the hotel. The front desk service was exceptional and the room was as immaculate as my 1st stay. Our room wasn't ready for early check-in but we were notified via email 2 hours later that our room was ready. Later that day we took advantage of the complimentary wine in the lobby in the evening before heading to dinner; we were glad to see many other hotel guests taking advantage of this, as it created a really nice, fun atmosphere. We also grabbed a nightcap in the hotel bar (Bar Seventy-Five), which is a very unique, modern space atypical of any other hotel bar.
Despite the many outstanding aspects of my latest experience staying at this hotel, the areas of concern arose during this time were:
1. Still wish they provided iron/ironing board in ALL rooms. Had to request both again and waited 30 minutes before receiving one.
2. Pillows are way too soft. Didn't sleep well both nights of our stay.
3. Walls are very thin. The young family staying in the adjacent room seriously disrupted us early one morning. We endured 2 hours' of hearing the parents arguing and screaming at their toddler to stop yelling, and for their older child to behave. The children seemed out of control and the parents' seemed at their wits' end. It got so bad that I called the front desk and they had a manager contact them, at which point we heard the parents argue over not being able to control their children and the children further continuing their misbehavior. THANK GOD they were checking out later that morning!
(FWIW, this is not the type of hotel that is conducive to travel w/ a young family w/ multiple children. It's quiet, mostly business travelers during the week and savvy, sophisticated urban travelers during weekends/holidays.) 
Given my familiarity with NYC and my complete distaste for many of the overpriced, overrated Midtown hotels w/ tiny rooms & bathrooms, I'm more than happy to stay at the Andaz Wall Street any time I'm in NYC. Hopefully the next time around we'll have quiet guests around us!

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “great location, great staff, great hotel”
text: My sisters and I stayed for 4 nights in a grand view room. The view was okay, not as good as we expected because it did over look a giant parking structure, but other than that it was pretty good. The staff were very friendly and helpful. We had actually booked the room for April but we had a change in plans and needed to push our trip back, they were very accommodating and gave us no hassles about switching dates, which was a huge relief. The hotel is also in a great location! We were able to walk almost everywhere we needed to go, Broadway, 5th Ave shopping, Bryant Park, Central Park, Terminal 5, and there are subway entrances all around. We will definitely stay here the next time come back to New York.

name: Westin Philadelphia
title: “Central location, stylish older hotel”
text:
This Westin has older bones but remains stylish. Rooms well furnished, marble bathrooms were clean and acceptable. Central location easy to find. Valet parking was fast and efficient. 
Bar and lobby area of hotel are enclosed with no outside exposure, a bit of a miss from this older design. 
Fridge in room was not stocked but was on. Went to Di Bruni Bros a half block from hotel, an excellent local grocer to stock a few drinks. 
Breakfast service does not list cereals, an odd omission. See photos for king room pics and breakfast order card.

name: Magic Castle Hotel
title: “The Best Hotel in the World”
text: At first sight this may look like a typical US hotel or motel with rooms overlooking a smallish pool in a courtyard. However, before you even get to that point you are greeted by enthusiastic, friendly staff who welcome very new guest with a champagne flute of sparkling lemon drink while you are registering. If that is not enough, there is a cucumber water dispenser and bowls of fruit in the lobby for your enjoyment. Then, as you register they give you a list of DVDs you can borrow free of charge together with what they call the 'minibar', sweets and snacks and cans of soft drink which you can ask for at any time, again completely free of charge. While sitting relaxing by the pool one afternoon a receptionist came round with a box, asking if we would like a 'popsicle' - fruit iced lollies distributed to guests around the pool. The breakfast in the lobby can be eaten in the pool area in the morning, or else taken back to the fully equipped room, with a microwave, cooker, fridge and coffee maker. We had a separate bedroom and sofabed in the living room so our daughter had her own space. A full sized dining table was useful for takeaways. Every time we needed technical help a handyman appeared straight away, even to show us how to tune the TV to run the DVD player. This is the second time we have stayed here, and since our last visit the rooms have been refurbished. We had a problem with ants in the bathroom, and they were eradicated within fifteen minutes. The location is excellent, cross the road, take the first turning on the left and go into the Kodak Theatre via the rear entrance (where the Oscars take place), then go through the shopping centre to the Walk of Fame, Graumans Chinese theatre and a Metro station. The Magic Castle , next door, is a club for magicians where high profile international magicians come to stay and perform for each other. They hold formal dinners during the week for over 21s only, but on Sundays there is a champagne brunch which allows children, and has a (slightly) more relaxed dress code. Before and after lunch you can attend the various rooms to see magic shows, or explore the quirky building. If you are visiting Hollywood this is the best hotel to stay in, particularly for families.

name: Loews Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Pros and Cons”
text: The Loews hotel is in a good location. The people who work there are incredibly helpful and friendly. Our room was clean and a nice size. Was it worth $250 a night (including tax)? I don't think so. Also, the doors slamming drove me crazy! They need to find a way for the doors to shut quietly. We were in our room around 4PM while house keeping was still cleaning, and the doors were constantly slamming. Fortunately, at night, it was pretty quiet.

name: Loews Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Just OK”
text: My husband and I stayed at Loews this past weekend. We arrived at 3:45 and they did not have any king rooms available yet. They gave us 2 free drink passes so we went to the bar to relax. The band was terrible and way too loud. We could barely hear each other. The people at the front desk were very courteous. An hour later our room was ready. Turns out they were hosting 6 weddings so things were undoubtedly busier than usual. The room was just OK. Since it was Loews, I think I expected more. It was very small, the TV didn't work very well and the bed was hard. There are better hotels to be had in the downtown area, especially for the price.

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “Unobtrusive luxurious service!”
text:
Having compared many hotel reviews, my husband and I finally decided upon The Bryant Park Hotel for our recent trip to NYC. We much prefer boutique hotels and this one certainly did not disappoint. The location is superb, the Bryant Park itself is a wonderful oasis in the middle of the hustle and bustle of such a busy city - a great place to chill out. 
From check in (very swift and friendly greeting by Robert - thank you) to check-out (late check out arranged with Nicole's assistance - thank you), nothing seemed to be too much trouble. I had contacted the hotel in advance of our arrival with a request for additional pillows - required due to having had surgery earlier in the year. Not only was my request honoured, but our room was upgraded and I also received a get well card from the staff. It was my birthday whilst I was there too and I was also treated to cupcakes and a balloon in celebration - I was certainly looked after very well indeed. Darren Sumner, Director of Front Desk and Guest Services, telephoned me upon arrival to check if we required anything else - a very nice touch which was greatly appreciated.
The hotel itself is 'very cool' and spotlessly clean. Unfortunately, we didn't get a chance to visit the Cellar Bar which now offers an open bar for residents every week night. It's obviously a popular spot though as there were queues of partygoers outside on a number of evenings (although we certainly didn't hear any music when we retired to bed).
Our room was very spacious, the bed was extremely comfortable, the bathroom had a large bath and a wonderful rainfall shower with fresh towels etc provided not only during the daily room cleaning but at the evening turn-down service too. I have no hesitation in recommending The Bryant Park Hotel - I certainly hope that I will have the opportunity to visit again in the not too distant future.
Many thanks again Darren to yourself and your very efficient team!

name: Andaz Wall Street
title: “Ultra modern rooms, great service, nice amenities”
text:
We enjoyed a fun weekend at Andaz. The decor is ultra modern, too cool for school hip, everything black, white or beige, glass & mirrors, electronic blinds & lighting system. Not our personal style but totally fun for a weekend stay.
The room is spacious with high ceiling. The bathroom area is almost as large as the rest of the room. Bed and comforter very comfortable, air ventilation system quiet and effective. Furniture, fixtures, bed linen, towels, personal care items all of high quality.
Mini bar items, except for booze, are complimentary and generous with sodas, juice, bottled water (still & bubbles),  terra chips, Dagoba chocolate bar. They replenish the items every day which we found impressive.
The best thing about Andaz is the complimentary, throughout the day cafe service in the lobby. From morning to evening, you can get coffee, cappuccino, latte, tea, cookies, candied walnuts, fruits, all served by friendly staff.  Wine & beer in the evening. We truly appreciated this amenity.
Wifi  is complimentary and easy to connect. Frankly, we are morally opposed to paying outrageous hotel charges for Wifi.
On our first day, we asked for extra towels and pillows and they were delivered promptly.
Location is worth mentioning. Downtown in the heart of Wall Street. We didn't care about not being close to the main tourist sites in midtown, but if that's important to you, Andaz may not work for you. Keep in mind subway stations are nearby and public transport is generally good in NYC.

name: Westin Philadelphia
title: “ABOVE AND BEYOND! 5 stars”
text: we had a fabulous 2 night experience at this hotel; excellent customer service, very clean, beautiful decor, perfection! the people are what really stand out at this hotel. they are so kind and helpful. the most impressive part of our experience came after we checked out. the next day, i realized i had left a brand new, tags-on designer dress in our closet. i called the hotel and CLARICE from housekeeping had promptly turned it in. the honesty and integrity of the people at the westin brand, particularly in philadelphia, is why we are loyal spg guests! so i'd like to personally thank leonard and ryan from the front desk, and kelly and clarice from housekeeping for taking care of a customer's needs even after check out. a little bit of honesty in today's society goes a long way and i am extremely grateful for that! thanks a million and we will be back :)

name: The Pearl Hotel
title: “Hôtel intéressant”
text:
Nous avons passé un séjour inoubliable à New-York en étant hébergés au Pearl Hôtel, dans une suite queen size.
Les points forts: 
La situation idéale à deux pas de Time Square et très calme; on peut faire plein de visites à pied, de Central park à l'ESB, en passant par la 5 éme av; les musées y compris l'intrépid et c'est un bonheur de pouvoir sortir le soir au spectacle, au restaurant, faire les boutiques à côté de chez soi, après des longues journées de marche;
La literie hyper confortable; je ne me souviens pas avoir si bien dormi que lors de ce séjour et le bonus c'est que les enfants peuvent avoir un vrai lit aussi confortable.
La salle de bain spacieuse et luxueuse, une belle baignoire et une grande douche moderne avec toute commodité de toilette.
Les points corrects sans plus.:
Le petit déjeûner plutôt basique, où on ne risque pas de s'attarder pour le confort ou la gourmandise, mais qui reste bien pratique et nourrissant avant de démarrer sa journée.
Le ménage et le personnel en général, juste ce qu'il faut, sans chercher à être aimable.
Les points qui nous ont déplu:
L'accueil, expéditif et impersonnel; comprend, comprend pas, c'est la même chose. Ils pourraient au moins donner une petite fiche en français pour les explications. On n'a plus oser s'adresser directement à eux. Notre sauveur a été Mourad, un portier très sympatique parlant français, à qui on pouvait demander tous les renseignements. Et ce qui nous a paru symbolique des relations humaines de l'hôtel, au petit déjeûner, une responsable passait parfois, mal aimable comme tout, pas un sourire, ni un bonjour à la clientèle, ce style "surveillante" nous a un peu choqué.
Malgré cette froideur et la frustation de ne pas avoir d'"amazing view", nous retournerons sans doute dans cet hôtel pour le confort des chambres, surtout avec enfants, son calme et sa situation.

name: Hampton Inn Philadelphia Convention Center
title: “Great Hotel, not so great area-BE ADVISED!”
text:
I have agree with some of the other reviewers-this hotel is located in quite a scary area. In terms of proximity to Philadelphia's downtown area and attractions, the location is great. However, we did not feel safe around here (outside of the hotel) even during the DAY, and at night we were even more uncomfortable. In fact, the combination of homeless people/gangbanger-thugs/and random man urinating on a wall near the hotel deterred me from venturing out to a nearby convenience store at around 9:30pm on a Saturday night. I actually turned around and went back to the hotel. 
The hotel is very clean, our room was spacious and clean, the fitness center and pool area are nice, and the breakfasts were wonderful. My only complaint about the room was that the shower faucet and head were loose, but this did not have any effect on the quality of the shower. The bathtub filled up a little during the shower, but I can live with that. Our view (7th floor) was that of a parking lot and run-down buildings. 
While my wife and I would recommend this hotel because of it's exceptional staff, cleanliness, and amenities, we do not plan to ever stay here again if we are in Philadelphia because of the not-so-safe location. Then again, we don't really plan to ever visit Philadelphia again because of it's "not-so-safe" areas that seem to take up most of the city.
Overall Summary: YES to Hampton Inn, NO to Philadelphia

name: Latham Hotel
title: “Visitare Philadelphia”
text:
Sicuramente una volta era un gran bell'albergo......ora è un albergo molto confortevole...e in un ottima posizione...la camera molto pulita e molto comoda...
il personale stupendo e premuroso......sopratutto con noi italiani......
puoi visitare Philadelphia a piedi senza bisogno di muoverti con i mezzi....
peccato averci passato solo 3 notti...speriamo di tornare..............

name: Andaz Wall Street
title: “Wall Street Banker”
text:
This was the first stop we had for our 25th Wedding Anniversary trip of a life time and we could not have started in a better place - first off we were met by one of the hosts, we talked to most of them by the time we left and they were all without exception very helpful - first off they wished us a happy 25th anniversary and upgraded our room - the room was a very high standard even if I made an effort I could not fault the room - as I am not a drinker having the free mini bar ( every thing was free but the booze ) was great to be able to twist open a nice cold water at the end of a day or juice in the morning brilliant.
The fact that its a short cab or tube ride away from the hustle and bustle of the City is a very good thing - if you asked me if I would ever stay there again its 100% yes.
Why a Wall Street Banker because you can always bank on getting the best service a great bed and the finest shower in New York City at the Andaz Wall Street.
room 1012

name: Magic Castle Hotel
title: “FANTASTIC service!”
text: The Magic Castle Hotel exceeded my expectations even before our arrival. After calling earlier in the day before check-in and explaining some rough travel circumstances, we were given a complimentary room upgrade. Once at the hotel, we were greeted with sparkling lemonade. The service only got better from there over our 4-day stay - from the delivery of free snacks and DVDs to our room, the prompt housekeeping staff, to the helpfulness of the staff in giving us public transit and walking directions and recommendations of things to do on our stay, I couldn't rate this hotel more highly. The pool, open 24 hrs, was heated, and feels cozy in the center of the hotel. The rooms, though not ultra-modern, were incredibly spacious and apartment-style, and the beds were incredibly comfortable. I would stay at the Magic Castle over and over again.

name: Hotel Palomar Philadelphia - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great location and friendliest staff”
text:
My wife and I really enjoyed our 1-night stay at the Hotel Palomar. The hotel has a unique, quirky character and is perfectly located for exploring Rittenhouse Square and Center City. Restaurants, shopping, and historic attractions are an easy stroll from the front door.
Our room was comfortable, impeccably clean, and—staying on an upper floor—blissfully quiet at night. The bed was on the firm side, but we had no trouble sleeping. This is a pet-friendly hotel, so if you have any allergies be sure to ask for a pet-free floor.
The hotel staff were extremely friendly and helpful. In fact, they might very well be the friendliest I've ever encountered traveling. Who would guess you would find that in Philadelphia instead of a tropical, remote, or more exotic location? I still can't believe it.
I'd definitely recommend the Hotel Palomar.
Suggested nearby eats: Dandelion Pub, Parc, Marathon Grill for Breakfast
Nearby attractions: Rittenhouse Square, City hall, Fairmont Park ("Love" sculpture)
Nearby shopping: Walnut St.

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
title: “centralissimo”
text:
Struttura carina, rimasti delusi per l'assistenza e la sistemazione ricevuta. In viaggio di nozze ci è stata riservata una camera con due letti singoli ad una piazza e mezza (120cm).
Nelle vicinanze non c'è nulla. Indicato per convegni.
Parcheggio molto caro: da evitare se siete in macchina.

name: Hyatt at the Bellevue
title: “Great Location”
text: Great location, the hotels public areas were beautiful. rooms were newly refurbished & very comfortable. Access to the sporting club was a great bonus, everytrhing you can possibly imagine under one roof. would definately stay here again.

name: The Pearl Hotel
title: “The Pearl Hotel - a pochi minuti da Times Square”
text:
Questo hotel è comodissimo perchè si trova praticamente all'inizio di time square. Inoltre la fermata della metropolitana è dietro l'angolo.
La camera era spaziosa e uguale alle foto presenti sul sito, la pulizia impeccabile e la gentilezza del personale altrettanto.
Consilgio vivamente questo hotel non solo per la posizione davvero centrale ma per il rapporto qualità/prezzo in quanto inclusa nella tariffa è compresa una piccola colazione a buffet dove c'era una vasta scelta di brioche e ciambelle accompagnate da the, caffè, succo di mela, succo d'arancia e un dispenser di cereali. L'unica piccola osservazione che posso fare è che la colazione era poco fornita di roba salata (non vi erano le uova, il bacon, i salumi e così via), in poche parole era puramente una colazione all'italiana.

name: Penn's View Hotel
title: “Charming Hotel in Great Location”
text:
Description: The hotel is a boutique type and some rooms have jaccuzi tubs and fireplaces. The linens and mattresses are great and there are different styles of rooms to fit different budgets and needs. Downstairs is a fine Italian restaurant, but the real attraction is the wine bar on the first floor. It has an incredible number of wines by the glass, and serves an awesome cheese platter. Try any one of their many wine-flights. 
Location: The Penn's View Hotel is located at the very end of Market Street near the river. It's in Old City, and the location is great for all the shops and restaurants of Old City. In nice weather, you can get to pretty much anywhere walking from the hotel, but the subway line runs down Market as well. It's about 13 blocks from the Reading Terminal Market, and about half that distance walk from the historic Philly attractions like the Liberty Bell. 
Staff/Service: We've stayed there many times and have always found the staff to be gracious and accommodating... helping with recommendations, reservations, special needs for special occasions. 
For the money, it is a wonderful alternative to one of the larger hotels.

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “No other place to stay in NY”
text:
Have just come back from NY after staying at the Bryant Park Hotel for 5 nights. I've stayed in many hotels from my various trips to NY however I have to say that Bryant Park is now the only place I will stay! The location is great - very close to Times Square but on Bryant Park on a quiet street ... you wouldn't believe you are so close to the heart of the action! So location 5/5
The staff are all very friendly and really efficient. From check in, room service, door men, concierge to check out - all very helpful. 5/5 
Room was very spacious for NY standards, with a lovely balcony and lots of natural light. Bathroom spacious, modern and most importantly spotlessly clean. The room was a delight! 5/5 
The hotel itself is very sexy (the lifts in particular) and the Cellar Bar with the current open bar from 5-6pm was a really nice touch and served by some lovely ladies!
Koi Restaurant - wow! Food here was unbelievable. You have to try the Crispy Rice with Spicy Tuna, so delicious we had to order two servings!
All in all, an amazing stay and I can't wait to return. It's the ONLY place to stay in NYC!

name: Latham Hotel
title: “Latham Motel”
text: So I read the reviews before I booked a room at The Latham and was fully aware that this was not going to be the Ritz Carlton. However, I was not expecting such a sorry, pathetic excuse of a hotel. After two nights there, you couldn't pay me to go back. The first room I was in, the sink was clogged, there was hair all over the bathroom (horror of horrors), the carpet was coming off the floor, and the sheets were about 50 thread count (a generous estimate). The second room was slightly better although this time the shower was clogged and the room smelled like a dining hall. The walls are paper thin, the lobby reeks of smoke and when I asked where the business center was, the front desk lady gave me a puzzled look and asked me what exactly I was looking for (never mind the fact that the hotel did indeed have a business center which was called "Business Center"--you would think the staff would be apprised of that). All in all, in my humble opinion, my experience was horrible, to put it mildly.

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
Courtyard Philadelphia Downtown
title: “Not Impressed”
text:
I booked this hotel based on comments on Trip Advisor. I was there for a conference so I wanted to stay near the convention center, but my husband and daughter came as well so it was about half leisure. 
Once you got past the beautiful (but small) lobby, and into the actually hallways and rooms, you could have been anywhere -- there was nothing distinctive or elegant about it. The hallway on my floor smelled weird (we were there for 4 nights) but the room smelled fine. Everything looked worn. I guess I expect when I stay in a (fairly) pricey hotel in a big city, I expect something extra...
The location was pretty good for us -- the Reading Terminal Market was the best part. But I visited some colleagues in their room at the Hilton Garden Inn and their room seemed newer and the location was much closer.
I also got coffee at the Starbucks at the Marriott next door and, although it was very typical Marriott in it's style, it had a huge lobby, with a central bar and...a Starbucks.
Having said all that -- everyone who worked there that I encountered was super friendly, and they came to fix my closet door immediately. 
Another thing I liked, which may seem weird, is that the TV turned on to the channel it was on when you shut off the set. This seems so small but every other hotel you go to starts at that stupid Hotel channel and you have to go back to the channel you like...
Anyhow -- I'll definitely stay somewhere else next time...

name: Westin Philadelphia
title: “Our "go-to" Philadelphia Hotel”
text: My husband and I really like this hotel. In fact every time we travel to Philadelphia this is our first choice in accomodations. The staff are all very friendly and accomodating from the valet staff to the front desk. The rooms are spotless, and well-kept. Great location too.

name: Penn's View Hotel
title: “My Kind of Hotel”
text: After flying non-stop from Hawaii to Atlanta and then catching a connecting flight to Philly, we were greeted with a friendly handshake, refreshing ice tea, and a cozy comfortable room with a view of Penn's Landing and Market St. The room was so quiet, we had to open the windows to hear all the wonderful street noise of this historic city. Just loved it, since we live on the beach and are tired of hearing the roar of the ocean all the time. The roll-a-way bed we requested was already waiting inside the room when we entered and was very comfortable for a 10 year old child. All of the staff were very friendly including the housekeepers. And the complimentary breakfast was quite elaborate with many choices. The parking was very conveniently located adjacent the hotel with a 24 hr. attendant, so I didn't have to worry about break-ins or smashed windows. At $21 per day parking, you have in and out service, which is very reasonable compared to other hotels. All in all, our Philadelphia visit was enhanced by staying at this friendly and conveniently located hotel.

name: Penn's View Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text: I stayed here for two nights because of a business trip. It was a GREAT location and great room. I had a queen size bed, which was perfect for one person, and could be ok for two. When you're staying this close to everything in the city, why would you spend a lot of time in the hotel. It was a little noisy due to parents not being able to control their children, but I really enjoyed the stay. Breakfast was good too.

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “Great location, small rooms, takes itself too seriously”
text:
Stayed here in May 2010 for a wedding
great location - across the street from the park, the grill, ny library, close to times square
a great location for kids, given the park and carousel across the street and the fun bakery cafe on the block, but this hotel is definitely not set up for families. this is a hipster place with red elevators. i always felt like we had to prove our right to enter the hotel or go into an elevator. no one was rude to us, but it didnt have a welcoming vibe. they must get a ton of rifraf who arent guests trying to get into the hotel.
fun to have a bar on-sight (downstairs), but nyc has this absurd law that our son couldnt be with us in there, even if not seated at the bar, so we couldnt be with our friends who we never see.
small hotel rooms, but oddly spacious bathrooms (the bathroom was nicer than the room itself)
a poor exercise room set up.

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “Trendy hotel perfectly located”
text:
This hotel is a landmark building and the inside is very stylish and fashionable. Rooms were very nice as well. Location is perfect for NYC and price was reasonable (including valet parking). The staff and concierge were very helpful and friendly. 
Would likely come back if they correct the Wi-Fi which was our only complain. It is around $10 per device and per night, which is outdated in this time of Smartphone's and Ipad's (As a Canadian, roaming data charges are too high). Since we had 2 IPhones and 1 IPad and only wanted to check a few things, it was problematic. I had found several hotels with free Wi-Fii but decided to try this one despite the Wi-Fi charges.Unfortunately, we couldn't even catch Wi-Fi during our stay on the 15th floor with our Mac devices. It seems to be a common issue. The whole Wi-Fi issue was surprising considering they claim to be fashionable. We had to go in the park to get it which was unacceptable and disappointing. I hope that they correct that situation.

name: Hyatt at the Bellevue
title: “Great location for Center City”
text: Nice place. Booked it sight unseen and thought it to be a bit pricey. We had coupons for the second part of our stay, so we weren't too concerned, but a King Suite runs around $325 a night. We stayed on the 14th floor in an inside room (no view). The room didn't have a coffee maker or fridge (other than the over-priced mini bar) and my wife complained about the length of the cord on the hair dryer (but she had fortunately brought her own in anticipation). Room had an iron, 3 phones, and a bidet. The hotel's best feature seems to be its location, walking distance to most of the center city. Plenty of great restaurants and nightclubs in the area, walking distance even in December cold. The hotel itself was very spacious, check in on the 19th floor was a little weird, valet parking was pricey $30.00/day +tip). We didn't eat at their restaurant but the menus were very expensive ($12.00 for muffins and coffee). Not crowded, saw few guests, staff very helpful, even over the phone. Great exercise facility (5 floors with indoor running track) and Starbucks on the first floor (along with several other stores). Any other questions, we'll be happy to e-mail!

name: Hyatt at the Bellevue
title: “Great Stay, Great Location”
text: Stayed here to attend a performance at the Kimmel Center. Located about a block and half from the hotel. Parking garage next to the building. You pay for the 24 hour price but the hotel validation gives you in-and-out privileges. Service is good, and there are great restaurant, eatery, shopping and night life options in the building and many more all around the area. Very close to the Art district and less then 5 min drive / 15 min walk to the historic district. The only issue was with the elevators. There were two small elevators and you usually have to wait a while to get on or get one that isn't full.

name: Andaz Wall Street
title: “Excellent hotel!”
text:
Very good hotel! Spacious rooms, very good and friendly service delivered in a very casual way.
The rooms are very cool with big bathrooms with windows into the bedroom (in our room at least) which is great if you are a couple. Complimentary minibar and free glasses of wine in the lobby before going out for dinner!
Would definitively stay here again if I would stay at lower Manhattan.

name: Penn's View Hotel
title: “Very nice once you get past the parking”
text:
My boyfriend and I recently spent a weekend in Philadelphia and chose to stay at Penn's View. Neither of us had been there before, so we were happy to locate the hotel and pulled in front to unload our bags, as the hotel's website advised to do.
Well. The hotel itself doesn't have a parking lot, but recommends parking in the paid lot next door ($42 for the weekend). We didn't even get a chance to get our bags out of the car when the attendant for the parking lot rudely yelled at us and told us that only people eating at the restaurant and wishing to have valet parking could pull in front of the hotel. God forbid we had known the city better and wanted to go park elsewhere! There were 3 or 4 gentlemen working in the parking lot and it was so utterly disorganized; each one told us something different ("Park here! Give us your key" "Why did you park there? I don't need your key") and I was afraid it was a bad omen for the hotel stay when I literally wanted to cry before we even got into the place!
So: expect trouble if you arrive during restaurant hours and/or want to park somewhere else.
Once we got the parking situation settled and got into the hotel, however, it was fantastic. The staff was very nice (the gentleman in the morning was particularly nice; I think his name was Antonio?), check-in was no problem, and our room was very nice (and different!). The continental breakfast was very good - fruit, muffins, scones, cereal, hard boiled eggs, waffles, bagels and the location of the hotel was perfect for visiting the historical sties; we were able to walk to the visitor's center and other sites. They have free wi-fi, but we were unable to get it to work with the iPad.
Aside from the parking, the only other bad thing to happen is this: the bathrooms have very thin walls. If your neighbors decide to do very loud, indecent things in there at 8 am while you're trying to get ready for your day...you'll hear everything. The fan for the room is pretty loud, so we were able to mostly drown out their moaning with that.

name: The Pearl Hotel
title: “Neues Lieblingshotel in New York”
text:
Sehr geräumiges Zimmer, tolle Betten, großes Bad mit sep. Wanne und riesiger Dusche ( TV im Bad natürlich auch vorhanden, nur ein beleuchteter Kosmetikspiegel wurde vermisst ). Kleine Küchenzeile mit Kühlschrank, Microwelle und Kaffeeautomat. Noch nie so ein ruhiges Zimmer bekommen 
(4 Aufenthalt).Frühstück mehr als OK, eben NY, täglicher Weinemfang von 16:00 - 17:00 Uhr. Sämtliches Personal sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit. Die Hotelbeschreibungen in den gängigen Portalen sind zutreffend. Wir kommen 100% wieder :-)))

name: Omni Los Angeles at California Plaza
title: “Bello ma occhio al parcheggio”
text:
L'albergo e' sicuramente ben tenuto ed in ottima posizione. Le uniche pecche sono che il minibar non puo' essere usato per roba propria e parcheggiare e' quasi impossibile a meno di non pagare 40 dollari al giorno nel parcheggio dell'albergo,decisamente un furto.
Il servizio e' comunque cordiale e le camere sono spaziose.

name: Sofitel Los Angeles
title: “Schönes Designhotel direkt in Beverly Hills”
text: Tolles Designhotel direkt gegenüber der Beverly Hills Plaza-Mall, sehr stylisch. Ich hatte ein großes Zimmer mit Blick auf die Hollywood Hills, allerdings entsprach der Standard des Zimmers in Bezug auf die Einrichtung nicht dem der europäischen Sofitel-Hotels. Auch das Bad war sehr "amerikanisch". Super Fitnessraum, sehr aufmerksamer Concierge-Service.

name: Sofitel Los Angeles
title: “Sofitel Beverlyhills”
text:
Bra hotell men tänk på att parkering inte ingår (och kostar en slant per natt). Mycket trevlig och service inriktad personal. Hotellet har en bra atmosfär, en välkomnande lobby och ett väldigt härligt pool-område på taket, en oas i storstaden.
Dessutom så ligger Beverly-center precis på andra sidan gatan med mycket bra shopping, om man har bil så går det lätt att spendera en vecka här för att besöka alla närliggande servärdheter.

name: Hampton Inn Philadelphia Convention Center
title: “Better than I thought”
text:
I read some of the reviews, and some people were disappointed. We weren't. I was just dad and the kids, and we ended up with a king suite. OK, it's not the Waldorf, but it was up to Hampton standards. Room was clean and everything worked ok. Pool is tiny. My daughter and I were swimming and it was great, but a group of seven girls came down and there wasn't room to breath! The pool is about the size of twenty bathtubs, so don't expect much.
Breakfast: Staffed by two nice ladies on Sunday morning, who made sure everything was replenished. Instead of sausage, bacon or eggs, they had this crumbed bacon and cheese thing on a bagel. It tasted ok, but it's still a mystery what it actually was.
Parking: We were able to park overnight on Vine street just a few blocks away. It was free at the meter after 8 pm. Yes, it's always scary leaving the car on the street overnight in a strange city, but it was still there in the morning, and best of all it was free.

name: The French Quarters Guest Apartments
title: “Great hotel in great location”
text: We stayed in this hotel during Thanksgiving. Highly priced, but a great hotel with value for all the money. The hotel is small and cosy, rooms are nice and the bed was big and with all the linen, pillows and perfect matresses! Staff was very helpful and nice. We have been to the city several times before but always stayed on fifth or Madison. The French Quarters was located perfectly between 8th and 9th avenue in the middle of Restaurant Row, with a lot of different restaurants to choose from. It only took us 5 minutes to walk to Times Square, and 15 minutes to walk to Macy's. Still it was in a quiter neighbourhood, with smaller buildings and friendly people around. The Bourbon Street bar which is on the ground floor of the hotel was a really nice play for an afternoon drink, lunch or party at nighttime. Beautifully decorated, with really polite and friendly staff, and great food! This is an all time favourite, we willl def. stay here again next year and the years to come!

name: Magic Castle Hotel
title: “The Other Reviews Were Right”
text: The actual hotel is a bit older, but the rooms were nice - clean, very comfortable bed. Location was excellent! A block away from the Walk of Fame. Good restaurants nearby. Pool was 8' deep! I've stayed many places and these were some of the nicest, most helpful staff I've ever encountered. Continental breakfast by the pool - great scones. Free round-the-clock snacks being available was just fun.

name: Trump SoHo New York
title: “great hotel”
text: Nice hotel, good location close to the Soho attractions and easy to get to meatpack. The bar is nice and was really happening during our stay there.

name: Trump SoHo New York
title: “Excellent hotel experience”
text: In the past we have always stayed in midtown. This is the first time that we didn't. One of the reasons we chose trump soho was because of the great promotion they were having. It was the leap day special and you couldn't beat the price. The rooms (we had two) were spacious unlike the rooms we had in midtown. We have stayed at the waldorf and the palace we, also, were very pleased with the soho experience. Would, definitely, go back and highly recommend it to all!!

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “good value for money, good location but breakfast not amazing”
text: I believe this hotel offered us what we were expecting: a good bed, a nice modern bedroom with all key facilities in 2011, a great location to visit NY, a nice stay. The breakfast was simple, probably too simple but there is so many places in NY where you can have a great breakfast that you forget about it and move on ! Yes the surranding is not amazing explaining the price I suppose...

name: Westin Philadelphia
title: “Great - Except Parking”
text:
We had a fantastic stay at the Westin Phila. The staff was very respectful and were always there if we needed them. The bed was fantastic and very comfortable, I didn't want to leave it in the morning. The room was complete with a fantastic desk and minibar to enjoy. 
During the night there was a lot of slamming doors, which would normally not be the fault of the hotel. In this case however, the doors would slam no matter what unless you gently brought it to close, which seemed to be a waste of time for most people.
Parking was the biggest issue for me. It was attached to the hotel, but for $180 a night, I expect free - or at least inexpensive parking. It was $35 to park yourself, and you had to pay each time. Because of this, I took the valet parking for $45, which allows you to leave and enter the hotel as much as you please during your stay. When we arrived at the hotel around 2:00PM, we waited ten minutes until I actually had to call the reception desk for someone to park our car.
Other than those two issues, it was a great stay with very polite staff and excellent accommodations.

name: Loews Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Philadelphia is a culturally/historically rich city.”
text: This hotel was quite centrally located, near major historical tourist sights and not too far from the railroad, however,as a Loews property, it was disappointing. The building itself seemed like a converted office building that made little sense in terms of the layout as a hotel.Felt awkward.

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Society Hill Hotel
title: “Great Location on Business”
text:
This my first time at a Sheraton while on business, previous employer preferred Hilton. Wow what a difference. I understand this location is recently renovated and you can tell with a few lingering original fixtures (bathtub and heater). Bedding and linens are very plush, plus new furniture (love the arm chair with pull out ottoman I need that at home!) Definitely spring for the club level if the rates are close (In my case they were identical) it includes continental breakfast and evening drinks and appetizers. I'm in a perfect location 2 doors down from the club and around the corner from the 24-hr gym. 
My only gripe is that the renovated gym did not include floor mats under their treadmills so after the hotel started filling up with a conference mid week I was woken up by *thunk thunk thunk* of runners on the treadmills. The vibrations are loud and travel across the hall. Sounds like an off balance washer on the floor below but definitely confirmed the runners (and thankfully not *ahem* enthusiastic neighbors!!). So any popular gym hours (4am-7am, 5pm-9pm) if your room is near the gym you'll get serious noise when someone is running hard. On the plus side you won't need the wakeup call at 5am! Oh did I mention they have a real person doing the wake-up calls still?? None of those goofy automated things that are complicated to set and a real person calls you in the morning (as far as I can tell).
Service is outstanding, the valet guys are great (I'm still blue collar and rarely business travel so valet always makes me feel awkward), concierge was wonderful and didn't bat an eye when I bashfully asked if the neighborhood is ok for a young lady to walk alone after dark (it's winter so it's dark super early) and the staff in the club lounge are friendly and reminded me to relax after a loooong day at work and reminded me to feel free to grab my wine to-go so I could lounge in pj's in my room! 
As a young business traveler and somewhat homebody this has been a welcoming place to unwind after long tough days on the opposite coast.

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Perfect NYC location”
text:
We had a wonderful experience at the Distrikt. The rooms are just beautiful and the location is perfect for walking everywhere.
The staff is very helpful and the lobby computers are available if you need them. I will definitely return on my next trip. Very reasonable for a city hotel.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Philadelphia Center City
title: “Great location”
text:
Overall evrything was great. Ease of checking in, clean spacious room and very comfortable bed and pillows.
I do not like paying $100 more per nt because it is a special event wkd, eg the marathon, even when booked months ahead.
And for the addntl price, no breakfast included. Buffet at $13PP- not reasonable when used to European hotels w breakfast buffets included in most hotels of this rating.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Philadelphia Center City
title: “A wonderful stay--”
text: staff extra accommodating, every effort made for guest comfort and service! It could not have been better except for the pool--lodation and cloudy water, and no hot tub. Overall, an outstanding experience--bell staff exceptional!!

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Very clean”
text: Very clean and easy to use. Beds are very comfortable. I don't like that the linens slide around the bed. This hotel was a lovely experience. The staff is really really nice and approachable. Love that different ethnic groups were behind the front desk. Free wii fii, coffee or hot apple cider were nice touches. Keurig machine in room made me bringing my favourites from home a easy and comfortable.

name: Magic Castle Hotel
title: “Pampered and great breakfast”
text: I was so grateful for the suggestion at Trip Advisor that this was a number one choice for LA. They treated us as if we were in a first class hotel. The room was huge and pleasant with kitchen. The breakfast by the pool was really a delight. Wi-Fi easy! Location is central near Hollywood Blvd. for the Chinese theater, Kodak theater. They drove us to the restaurant at the top of the hill and picked us up after dinner!

name: Le Meridien Philadelphia
title: “Bellissimo albergo, ottima posizione.”
text: Abbiamo soggiornato a Philly per 2 notti in questo splendido albergo ultramoderno e curatissimo prenotato tramite booking.com e, quindi, ad un prezzo scontatissimo. Le camere sono grandi ed accessoriate di ogni confort, compreso televisore in HD. Unica pecca: la connessione ad internet è a pagamento! C'è una bella fitness room ed un bellissimo lounge bar all'ingresso. Il parcheggio della macchina è caro (30 dollari al giorno oltre tasse), quando proprio dietro l'angolo se ne trovano altri a buon mercato.

name: Courtyard Philadelphia Downtown
title: “Overpriced?”
text:
Stayed at Courtyard during a convention, mainly because it appeared to be family friendly. Unfortunately, the pool was closed for resurfacing when we arrived so we had to trek to the pool across the street at the larger Marriott (which was quite nice). We were pleased with the service (asked for a fridge, and there was no charge) and friendliness of staff. Room was fairly large but not a lot of table space to put things on, and bathroom sink was tiny with no place to put toiletries. So accommodations were just ok but at least they were very clean. Location downtown was terrific, just a block from Reading Terminal Market and the trolley that goes all around town. 
For the price, I would have expected a little more in the rooms but I guess it is downtown. We didn't have a car but thank goodness - overnight parking downtown cost around $36/night no matter where you parked.

name: Hotel Palomar Philadelphia - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Dog-friendly convenience”
text: We went to visit family in Philadelphia for Christmas, and decided to spend some time touristing downtown with our extra large dog. The Hotel Palomar was the perfect dog-friendly hotel. The location is convenient to everything. The staff was exceptionally nice and efficient. The room (king bed, sofa, wired desk) was beautiful and spotlessly clean. The bathroom was huge, with a jetted tub (which we requested in advance). They supplied dog dishes and a dog bed. The only negative -- not the hotel's fault -- was that our dog was afraid of the elevator. Otherwise, it would have been the perfect experience. Shout out to Charles, the best doorman in Philadelphia.

name: Radisson Plaza-Warwick Hotel Philadelphia
title: “Great location”
text: We have stayed here for several Philadelphia overnights...it's a great location, walk out the door and one lock to Rittenhouse Square! Staff is always nice & efficient, rooms tidy, amenities such as a coffe shop right inside and good bar. This last trip, we even brought our dog....he loved getting a chance to trot around the city!

name: Doubletree by Hilton Philadelphia Center City
title: “Doubletree Hilton Philly”
text: This hotel is really good, Ive had the chance of staying here two years ago and all the staff has been always nice and very helpful. The food quality is also good and the rooms are always clean. Housekeeping staff is extremely nice as well.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Philadelphia Center City
title: “Great Location, Friendly Staff and Ammenities”
text:
Doubletree by Hilton is a great hotel in a central location of Philadelphia. I traveled to Philly for business and was pleasantly surprised by the decor and the friendliness of the staff. The room was tastefully decorated and clean, and came with a fantastic view of Broad Street. The first night of my trip I ate at the restaurant in the hotel (The Balcony). Although there were limited options for a vegetarian, the Tomato soup and salad I had were tasty. 
Parking ($25/day for self-parking) was convenient as the hotel has a relationship with the garage right next door; however, there were issues with getting in/out because of the outdated system the garage uses. I was told, however, that they are in the process of updating this to work more efficiently.

name: Andaz Wall Street
title: “Sets new standards in service”
text:
We loved staying here. Our room was spacious and beautiful- the snacks and drinks were very convenient- but the highlight was the service.
We called in to the Saturday Farmers's Market in the square next door. I bought some chutney and a few other delicious bits and pieces for a friend we were visiting later that day. Later after doing some other errands we popped back into our room and had a call from reception asking if we had left something behind. They then brought the jar of chutney up to our room! We'd been chatting to a member of hotel staff who had helped set up the market and somehow or other they had worked out who we were. I was surprised and delighted.
The staff in the lobby were always exceptionally helpful and even learned our names. I had lunch with a colleague in the restaurant, and he two was surprised at the very high standard of service. When he initially arrived at the hotel my husband and I were having some coffee in the lobby. Straight away a member of staff came over to offer him some too.
On another note, this was my husband's first trip to NY and it worked out to be a brilliant location. Subway lines were so close. We didn't regret staying downtown at all.
Can all hotels be like this please?

name: Courtyard Philadelphia Downtown
title: “A very nice Marriott Courtyard”
text:
My wife and I stayed at this Courtyard during the Independence weekend. All I can say is "Oh Wow". The location is wonderful. The train station is only two blocks away. We took the train directly from the airport (Train ticket is cash only). The Reading Terminal Market is a block away which you can enjoy a lot of good food and fresh produce (especially during weekend).
The hotel room is fairly new. The bed was very comfortable. I am surprised how noise-isolated the room is. Our room was right next to the ice machine but I could not hear any noise in our room.
The hotel's fitness center is spacious, clean and well equipped. Each cardio machine has its own TV screen. We enjoyed our workout very much. The whirlpool was a bit dirty and cold. We went in and out within 5 minutes.
We enjoyed our stay very much. The only complain is I wished we had a room with a better view (rather than looking across the Residence Inn).

name: Doubletree by Hilton Philadelphia Center City
title: “Great Customer Service!!!”
text: Just want to give a shout out to Tyree Miller, the super friendly late night front desk person at this Philadelphia Doubletree. Tyree really went above and beyond to ensure we were given the highest level of customer service! The hotel itself is incredible...great views of downtown and an excellent restaurant with a delicious breakfast buffet in the morning. But the friendly staff just really cant be beat. I hope my job sends me to Philadelphia more often so I can stay at this hotel again.

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Society Hill Hotel
title: “Incredible service and great location in Philadelphia”
text: I felt compelled to write this review since I read a few reviews before we booked this hotel and my friend was a bit apprehensive. Apparently, someone had stayed here in the past and had experienced bedbugs. As a former investor in a 640 hotel in LA, I tried to educate my friend that bedbugs can appear in the most expensive hotels as well as the dirtiest hotels. The problem is the traveler; especially foreign travelers with less than perfect hygiene practices. We rented two rooms for the week and both rooms were in excellent condition. The hotel was recently renovated and it showed beautifully. We both were so impressed with the staff. You see, we had made our reservations on Priceline and had to combine multiple reservations for the 7 day stay. The front desk was extremely patient in working out adjoining rooms and accommodating our requests. The bell staff was more than helpful and the maids were gracious and also very accommodating. Ignore the one isolated case of bedbugs since I highly recommend this hotel.

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Society Hill Hotel
title: “Great Location for Philly's Waterfront Area”
text:
Stayed here during the last week of May - first day of June for a conference. Hotel was only four stories high but sprawling enough to accomodate over 270 of us very comfortably plus many others not part of the conference. Nice functional lobby with very friendly and accomodating front desk staff and concierge. 
The fourth floor room I had included twin queens, desk and what looked like a 46" LCD flat screen TV (which I never turned on). Spacious bathroom with the usual accoutrements. Plenty of large, fluffy white towels! All very clean and relatively updated. The view out the window overlooked the HVAC equipment over the lower roof with the spars of the converted 4-masted tallship (Moshulu)/restaurant a couple blocks away at Penn's Landing on the Delaware River. I don't think any room has an unobstructed river view due to trees and the relatively low stature of the hotel. 
None-the-less, this is a great location due to the nearby historical sites (Liberty Hall, Penn's Landing, etc.), great restaurants and the short 15-20 minute walk needed to get to city hall and many other venues. I've stayed in the downtown core section of Philly on previous trips but I definitely liked this location far better due to the reasons listed and the general lack of heavy traffic. The nearby restaurants were both diverse enough and we were always able to get in and out within the lunch hour.
Conference facilities were fine as well. I would recommend them to anyone looking for a conference/convention venue in a historical city - especially is you wanted evening entertainment and good food!

name: Penn Tower Hotel
title: “Overpriced and Disappointing”
text: My mother and I stayed for 3 nights when my father was having surgery. Room desperately needed to be refurbished. No cable TV, had to run water in shower 20 minutes to get hot water, rough, frayed towels, torn wallpaper and missing fixtures, not even an alarm clock provided. Must walk 3/4 mile to get to hospital. Would not recommend.

name: Holiday Inn Express Philadelphia Midtown
title: “It was OK....”
text:
I stayed here because it was the last "conference hotel" that still had rooms, and now I think that wasn't a coincidence. It's just slightly of a too-far walk from the convention center (altho in fairness I don't think it bills itself as being nearby), and I didn't find out until the last day that there was a back door that cuts a block off that walk. It would have been nice had the staff mentioned that, since I booked under a conference rate. 
It's possible that the other annoyance was a complete fluke. One day there was a notice about a FIRE DRILL in the hotel during the day - fortunately, I missed it due to being busy. But the very next day there was a notice that the window cleaners would be there, and to close our blinds early. I get that occasionally stuff like that is necessary at a hotel, but it seemed like to do this on back to back days is too much for those of us there for both days.

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Society Hill Hotel
title: “Renovated Rooms Are Great - Surrounded by History”
text:
I was in town for a large conference (June 2012) and was pleasantly surprised by the Sheraton Society Hill. I enjoyed having so much history right outside the front door and it’s very easy to walk anywhere downtown from the hotel (though it will take 15 mins or so) Cabs were plentiful if you needed to get someplace and didn’t want to walk. 
I was given a King room (newly remodeled) on the 3rd (Club) floor. Since everything in the room was remodeled there isn’t much to say about it except it was comfortable, clean, new and very enjoyable.
The club room was very large and with your room key you could stop in at any time and grab a free water or soda. The gym looked completely new as well and there is also a pool at the hotel.
If you want to be in a smaller hotel that has a lot of history all around it, don’t stay downtown among all the financial buildings and stay here instead. 
The only downside was that on ½ the floor, the emergency intercom was experiencing random static all weekend and the same speakers are in your room. I had several colleagues who were also attending the conference who were kept awake most nights by the static. When they complained to the front desk they offered to send up an engineer but conceded that there was probably nothing that the engineer could do. Since it was a sold out conference, there were no rooms to move them to.
I have posted pictures of the gym, club room and my room.

name: Society Hill Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text: The location of this hotel was fantastic - right in the heart of the historic section of Philadelphia and close to heaps of great bars/restaurants - this can mean it gets a bit noisy on the weekends but I had no trouble at all sleeping with a pair of earplugs. Staff were very friendly and welcoming, as a budget option with character in a great location I would recommend this hotel.

name: Society Hill Hotel
title: “Do not book this hotel!”
text:
This hotel is by far the worst hotel in wich i ever slept. It´s noisy. It´s old and there is nothing that is not broken and the beds are small. I bookt this for three days and it was hell. The internet was broken, the wire´s where hangen frome the sealing and it kept goning on. There was only one nice person in the staff. There is no 24 desk so you have to do it all in the afternoon. I arrived a bit before check in time and asked about parking. Thet didn´t know and gave me wrong instructions. This is not what you want when you are downtown in a unknown city with a lot of one way routes.
It;s close to everytthing that's the only good thning i can think of. Close to this hotel is The Bestwestern Hotel Philladelphia on Chesnutstreet. They are good and help you. they helped us with internet.
So Conclusion: Do not book!

name: Andaz Wall Street
title: “A sleek, modern, comfortable hotel that treats you like a celebrity”
text: The minute you enter this hotel you are immediately greeted at the door with friendly staff who personally sit you down to go over your check in. The lobby of the hotel was immaculate, modern, yet comfortable. The lobby had a table with complimentary refreshments so that guests could rehydrate or energize themselves throughout the day. The rooms were immaculate and clean, particularly the modern bathrooms that included rain shower heads. The rooms come with a complimentary mini bar (excluding alcohol) that is refilled each day with various drinks and snacks. The hotel restaurant "Wall and Water" had great American and European fare of a five star Michelen restaurant. Overall, the staff was friendly, helpful, and the hotel and its services far exceeded my expectations.

name: Hotel Palomar Philadelphia - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “The best!”
text:
Wish I could give them 6 stars. 
We've stayed here twice for weekend getaways, traveling with our dogs on both visits. The staff truly couldn't be nicer--and not just the front desk staff, I mean *everyone* we've encountered. We saw lots of familiar faces on our 2nd visit, and some of the hotel staff remembered us too (or at least our dogs, who are pretty darn cute). 
For those who don't know, the Kimpton hotels are probably the most dog-friendly anywhere, and the Palomar Philly is especially welcoming. They even have a brunch in the warm weather months with a special doggy menu. (And yeah, that's ridiculous but it's a lot of fun and our pups loved every minute!)
The rooms are lovely and very well kept; we had a spa king room on our last visit and the enormous bath was a nice luxury. 
We love this place and hope to return again and again--the wonderful staff really make it feel like home (except fancier and with room service)!

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “A Gem in Midtown”
text: We frequent Manhattan about six times a year, staying over when we make plans for dinner and a show. This was our fist visit to TBPH but it won't be our last. In fact, if it's available we would dream of staying anywhere else. The room was beautiful and immaculately clean. The staff was pleasant, helpful and made us feel very welcome the moment we arrived. We highly recommend this wonderful hotel and with beautiful Bryant Park right across the street, you can't ask for more!!!! Bravo the staff at TBPH.

name: Courtyard Philadelphia Downtown
title: “Nice place. Decent Location.”
text: Clean, good service. Nothing extraordinary but its a nice hotel. The location is close to the shopping district and there are plenty of restaurants, bars and pub within walking distance.

name: Andaz Wall Street
title: “amazing”
text: this hotel is really amazing, the place is very nice and chic. The room was very clean and modern. The thing that i was most amazed about this hotel is the service they have. First you can have sodas and snacks from the minibar as much as you want. They give you capuccinos with little pastries in the morning, and wine with tasty snacks at night. Mike was really helpfull, and also was Vasil made the best coffee. Im so glad that we decide to go to this hotel and im really looking forward to come back.

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Outstanding!”
text: This hotel lives up to the reviews. We arrived after a diversion to Boston due the snow storm, tired and dispirited, but from the moment we stepped through the hotel doors we were given a warm friendly welcome. The lobby and breakfast room are fun and contemporary, the rooms extremely spacious, with an amazingly comfortable mattress, not found in many five star hotels. Considering it is in a busy neighborhood the noise is slight and sleep quality good. Traveling with teenagers the proximity to Times Square , subway and other sights is very convenient. We definitely will be back. We loved this hotel.

name: BEST WESTERN Center City Hotel
title: “OK for the money”
text:
If you want a great hotel experience, this is not your place. However, if
you can get past the dark hallways and oddly painted elevators and the 
semi-rude staff, the room itself is pretty comfortable. The later check-out 
time of noon is also convenient. With a discount, it is worth what you
pay, but no more. I would go back to this hotel because of its location,
but not for the atmosphere.

name: Microtel Inn & Suites by Wyndham Philadelphia Airport
title: “not worth the money”
text:
The room and hallway carpets were old and dirty. 
The breakfast area was messy. 
WiFi not working at all. 
bathrooms with hair and dust bunny's everywhere you turn. 
elevator not working.
overall the hotel was bad

name: Rodeway Inn Center City
title: “Great staff, great location.”
text: It's hard to beat the location of the Rodeway Inn City Center - walking distance to most major tourist sites, convention center (if in town for a trade show), etc. Public transit is also just a hop-skip-jump away. Hotel staff was very friendly and accommodating. Room was clean, and as a single traveller, I felt safe. My room had a large flat screen TV, single serve coffee maker and I very much appreciated the 2 free bottles of water that were replenished daily. Cons I encountered: TV remote was finicky (staff resolved), no in-room climate control (staff made adjustment upon request), unable to pickup strong enough signal to take advantage of the free wireless services, cracked tile in bathroom and corner stall shower only (didn't really make a difference to me). Definitely not a 5-star hotel, but I would stay again without question!

name: BEST WESTERN Center City Hotel
title: “Needs updating”
text: Hotel was nice enough. Walkable to downtown if you are fit. Hitel needs remodleing. Staff were very nice and free parking is great perk that close to downtown. I paid $150 would have fealt better if Ihad paid $100

name: Loews Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Not Very Accommodating”
text: This hotel has a great location for business travelers. It is on Market Street a couple of blocks from City Hall. I had a relatively large corner room with nice views. The amenities were standard for a hotel of this nature. The beds were comfortable and desk space adequate. Wireless internet is available for the usual $10 a day. My only complaint is that the front desk was border-line rude when I asked for a late check out to prepare for a 2:00 meeting downtown. This may not matter to tourists or those in town for a convention, but my advice to business travelers is to consider another hotel that is more accommodating. There are plenty in the immediate vicinity.

name: Loews Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Would Definitely Come Back!”
text: We've stayed here a couple of times so far, and I must say I was pleasantly surprised. We parked one block away in the parking structure across from the Reading Terminal Market. I don't remember how much it was, but it wasn't cheap. Check-in was a breeze, even though there were quite a few people in line. The young man we had was professional, courteous and knowledgeable. He honored my request for a quiet, corner room as there was a wedding party there that weekend. It seems like they do allow pets since the woman in front of me had a golden retriever with her. They have a lot of elevators and it wasn't ever too long of a wait for one. The hotel is in an old bank building, so I thought that was sort of neat. Our room was huge! Large windows on two walls, giving us a near panoramic view of the city below. Unfortunately, we got stuck with two double beds as they were out of king-sized beds, but at least they were comfortable with nice fluffy pillows. TV was okay, not a new flat screen but it had plenty of channels to choose from. Small closet and safe. The bathroom was also pretty spacious, and I like how the toilet felt enclosed since it was in the far corner behind the wall. Tub was fine, clean, and water pressure good. Don't remember the toiletries but I'm sure it was okay. Location of this hotel was fab, tons of restaurants, shopping and a 10-15 minute walk to the Liberty Bell which we saw on this trip. Pretty amazing once you get to it, and it's a freebie. We ate at this wonderful Vietnamese restaurant in Chinatown which was also a quick 5-10 minute walk away. I think it was called Vietnam Restaurant, there are two similar restaurants (Vietnam Palace was the other one, I think) and they are right across from each other and I chose this one since the decor looked a little nicer and I've heard good things about it on yelp. There was a great gym at this hotel, surprisingly. Tons of cardio and weight machines, so I was very pleased. There's a spa located next to the gym which seemed nice, but I didn't have any services so I cannot comment. We had drinks in the lounge/bar downstairs and that was fine. I don't recommend their desserts however, they were pretty boring and far too sweet. All in all, I would definitely come back, especially when they offer the Travelzoo discounted rate.

name: Hotel Palomar Philadelphia - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Amazing Hotel!”
text: I have to say that more often than not I am a bit disappointed in my hotels that I book with out seeing. The Palomar, however, did not disappoint at all! Everything about our visit was great. The style is so creative with practically a surprise around every corner. Staff was completely helpful and the breakfast at the restaurant was delicious! The rooms are generously sized... our double was perfect for myself, hubby and the kiddo's. I was a little nervous about the cleanliness because they do allow pets there, however, they were spot on... you'd forget all about that policy until a cute little pooch would walk on by you. Loved that! La piece d'resistance was the free happy hour in the lobby... such a nice vibe! and then there was the great location. Clearly, we loved the Palomar! I would strongly recommend.

name: Andaz Wall Street
title: “Modernes Stadthotel”
text: Das Andaz Wall Street ist im südlichen Teil Manhattens gelegen. Im Vergleich zu vielen anderen Hotel in New York ist das Andaz sehr modern und minimalistisch. Die Zimmer sind großzügig und schlicht eingerichtet. Die Lage im Financial District ist eventuell nicht optimal für Touristen, da viele Sehenswürdigkeiten nördlicher liegen. Dennoch muss man sagen, dass das Hotel gerade für Geschäftsreisende super geeignet ist.

name: BEST WESTERN Center City Hotel
title: “Dump”
text: This hotel was selected by a reservation group that handled our conference. It is a real dump. NO HEAT. We tried turning the heater on and it sounded as if the entire building was on the verge of collapse. When we called customer service we were told they were "working on it". It's going on 8:00 and we are still wearing layers of sweaters and scarves. The bathroom door was warped and would not close. You can see through the sheets. I was afraid to ride the elevator, as it looked like something out of a horror flick. The lock on the room doors are the size of lunch boxes. I've never seen anything like it. The staff were nice but turned rude when we asked if they would be able to fix the heat or if we could possibly receive a discount. This is the worst place that I have ever experienced. Save your money...it is a real dump and needs major renovations. One side of the hotel looks as if it is being bulldozed. The windows are knocked out and it looks vacant. I will leave a note for the manager, as this is unacceptable for $110 a night. I would have paid more just to be able to take my scarf off. The pictures on their website were probably taken 20+ years ago. Save yourself the agony.

name: Magic Castle Hotel
title: “Absolutely Loved Our Stay”
text:
We needed a quick get-away for a weekend... and spent out time here 4th of July weekend. 
We originally made our reservations from Orbitz.com, but when our room was not was what we expected, the manager quickly upgraded our room to a suite with no extra charge or fuss.
We were greeted with sparkling lemonade and were continually accomodated with cold popscicles through-out the hot day along the pool.
They even had people come and give us the forecast for the following day.
Everyone at the Magic Castle Hotel was more than accomodating and gave us the most relaxing weekend I have had in a very long time!
Thanks again!

name: Magic Castle Hotel
title: “misinformed”
text: We telephoned from the East Coast, but were not informed (a) that the Magic Castle Club has a dress code or (b) no children are allowed. So, our stay was very disappointing for our two teenageers. For one of them, the Magic Castle was to be the birthday surprise. The hotel should inform potential guests.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Philadelphia Center City
title: “Very nice”
text: It is locted and a very good area. There are alot of food places, shopping and sightseeing within walking distance of the hotel. The room I had was right beisde the elevator and it was not noisy at all. I thought it would be but it wasn't. Very nice hotel. The rooms were a good size. You have to pay for internet. I was kind of suprised by that.

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “Cool Hotel”
text: This is a cool, small boutique hotel. The rooms are larger than in most Manhattan hotels. Our room had wood floors and it looked out at Bryant Park across the street (a small side street at that). At night, if you don't feel like walking any more, but you're not ready to be cooped up, the park is a very relaxing place to hang out and watch people (and drink cheap store-bought beer, although it's against park rules). The Koi Restaurant in the hotel is still a trendy place to be for locals, and it is an absolute madhouse from happy hour through 10 or 11 at night during the week. And the food is fantastic. If you want to be a tourist (which we were) the hotel is 5 minutes from Broadway and a short walk to the Empire St. Building. The "entertainment director" (the concierge) will book anything for you and make great suggestions for what's overhyped and what's not. The staff is cool, too. The pop singer Usher was staying at the hotel while we were there. The morning he was going to put on a free concert at the Park, which was our first morning there, having arrived the night before, there were crowds lined up down the sidewalk on both sides outside the hotel. We walked in and out of the hotel at least 5 times past the crowd, all of whom wanted to try to sneak into the lobby to see Usher, and the staff didn't give us a second look, because they memorized our faces when we walked out the first time. Great place to stay.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Philadelphia Center City
title: “Too many critical misses; too few hits.”
text:
Misses:
1. Desk staff was unhelpful during initial phone inquiry.
2. Possibly the most uncomfortable bed in the history of uncomfortable beds.
3. Noisy room (6th floor) -- could hear e-v-e-r-y little intrusion like water in pipes, door locks, footsteps, conversations, street noise, etc.
4. Poor satellite TV selection -- no HGTV, NatGEO, Nik, or Animal Planet.
5. Poor HVAC room control -- either freezing or muggy hot. 
6. No free WiFi in room; megabucks per day.
7. No notification by front desk when all elevators stopped working.
Hits:
1. Location, location, location -- easy to walk anywhere in Center City.
2. Yummy cookie at check-in.
3. Helpful concierge staff.

name: Trump SoHo New York
title: “Lovely but”
text:
I found this place lovely and the staff very helpful, but for the life of me I do not get the dog thing. I certainly don't have a problem with dogs I have one I am very fond of, but its a dog and it stays at home when we holiday. So I would probably look else where when choosing to stay in New York on my next visit.
But in saying this I couldn't fault the lovelyness of this place, the view was amazing and the bed the best ever.

name: Rodeway Inn Center City
title: “Nel cuore di Philadelphia”
text:
Piccolo alberghetto nel cuore della città, a due passi dalle maggiori attrazioni turistiche e al centro della zona dei locali.
Zona tranquilla, poche auto in giro, un sacco di gente per le strade: il posto ideale per soggiornare qualche giorno.
Stanze senza molte pretese, così come la colazione, ma per pochi dollari dormirete comodamente e in un posto di tutto rispetto.

name: Trump SoHo New York
title: “Amazing View from our room”
text:
We stayed a week in this hotel. We were sorry to leave. The staff were sooo friendly. Unbelievable to think they were New Yorkers :-)
We stayen on 34th Floor and the views were magical of Manhattan from our room. We didn't enjoy breakfast at the hotel restaurant, we found the service there was lacking, but being in Soho, there was no problem finding a breakfast or eating spot nearby.

name: Trump SoHo New York
title: “Girls Weekend”
text: Trump Soho is a classy, trendy, decadent hotel. I absolutely love it here ! My friend and I were so impressed with the room, especially the bathroom with sunken tub and dual vanity. Soho is a great area with amazing restaurants and nightlife. I highly recommend Trump Soho especially since it is directly across from the Holland Tunnel and parking as well.

name: Ritz-Carlton Philadelphia
title: “Amazing Service”
text: We recently stayed for 3 nights for our daughter's graduation. The overall service was amazing - from the personalized check in, to the excellent bell boy service from Jimmy - who was cheerful and helpful always and most surprisingly a hotel painter/ handyman who we met in the lift - who asked us how our stay was going. When we said that it was going well - he actually said " what can we do to make it better !" It really was the best start to our day....

name: Loews Philadelphia Hotel
title: “the Loews was fine.”
text:
This was a nice hotel. The room was nice and clean. It was a standard hotel room but was fine. Nice bed, nice desk and a lovely divan to read on. The bathroom was nice and roomy. 
the gym is great--all sorts of equipment but it closes at 10PM. Wish they kept it open later. The restaurant Sole is very good and the bar scene was really hoping. They have maintained some very nice features of the old PSFS bank which was the original blgd. Veyr nice and helpful staff. Very good location to walk around downtown Philly. It is right in the middle of town. Go up to the 33rd floor and check out the view of city hall and the rest of the city. Surprised that they don't have a small lounge up there serving cocktails.

name: Radisson Plaza-Warwick Hotel Philadelphia
title: “Everything above and beyond expectations!”
text:
I had the most fabulous stay earlier this week at the Radisson Plaza-Warwick. I have been working my butt of all summer at a summerstock theatre in CT and I desperately needed a break from living in my teensy billeted bedroom. Walking into the hotel after the heat and travel was like an oasis in a desert. This hotel has a truly lovely lobby, with comfortable seating and complimentary fruit infused water, which was so welcome on the sweltering day. I arrived in the early evening, and it wasn't too busy, but I found the front desk staff were friendlier than I'm used to (even at higher star levels) and chatted with me in a really genuine manner - nothing rehearsed or phony. That may be a silly thing to care about, but I was travelling without my boyfriend for the first time in years and it made me feel better about travelling alone. 
What happened next was truly to me the height of great customer service. I had booked my room as a last minute Name-Your-Price on Priceline, and had accidentally booked for the wrong day. It was my mistake and it could have been a total disaster! However the guest services rep switched the reservation with no issue at all, and eased my embarrassment with such a grace; it was so appreciated. Other hotels I have stayed at having bid on from Priceline have sometimes made me feel a little bit second class to their usual clientele, mainly by making a point of "well, you DID book on Priceline" so I should not have high expectations. This was not the case at all at The Plaza-Warwick. I felt from the moment of arrival straight to checkout that I was a valued guest. It was a really nice feeling.
I was shown my room by a very pleasant bellhop, which was kind because I only had a small bag. Nice touch. The room itself felt very luxurious for a 3.5 star. It was roomier than others I have stayed in, and the layout was excellent. The Sleep Number bed was fun. I wasn't so big on it for sitting in bed, but it really was excellent to sleep on.
