The furnishings were mostly new - the tv unit was a little worn - but overall it was in great, updated condition with expected and unexpected amenities: widescreen tv (with the bonus of free HBO and some HDtv channels), coffee maker, hair dryer, free plug-in internet, etc.
Speaking of internet, I was without my laptop, so I went to use the business centre, which had two computers for guest use, a printer, fax, etc. When I went down shortly after arriving to check my email, one of the stations was in use, and the other seemed out of order. I checked with the front desk agent, and he very kindly allowed me to use the computer in the Club Lounge. That was a really great touch. Like I said, the little things make it! I didn't particularly fit in in the Club Lounge, being under 30 and female, but it seemed like it had everything a business traveller would be interested in: some hors d'oeuvres, wine, big screen tv, dessert, newspaper, computer, couches, etc etc. 
The room service menu sounded really tasty, but the kitchen was closed by 10:30 pm, and I was out at the IMAX until past midnight, but the front desk had several recommendations for late-night food in the area. I decided to sleep on it, and had breakfast delivered instead. It was on the usual hotel-pricey side for what it was (eggs cooked as ordered, sausage, potatoes, english muffin) but it was presently nicely and brought up quickly and in the friendly manner I was now used to at the hotel. I would say that both the sausage and the potatoes could be a little more flavourful, but they were not offensive in the least. 
Having slept so well in the Sleep Number bed, I was actually up with several hours to relax before checkout, eating my breakfast and watching the free HBO. I was sad to check out (and head to the youth hostel I had actually intended to spend both nights at) but found that also to be a speedy and painless process. I don't usual leave a hotel having had such an across the board good impression. This hotel truly outstripped it's rating. It felt 4 star in every which way. Thanks for the lovely stay!

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “Fun Experience”
text: My stay here was great. I don't remember what type of room I stayed in but it was big but also sparse. It was definitely comfortable and I really liked the bathrooms. I find bathrooms to be very important to me when I book hotels and theirs was awesome. There's turndown where they move the gigantic pillows from the bed, turn on the sound machine, close the drapes and give you a pair of slippers. I loved how they provided an umbrella in your closet in case you didn't come prepared for unexpected rain. I thought the LCD LG TV was a bit small for the room and fell they should invest in larger ones. I definitely liked my stay. The front desk was nice and the bar at the hotel was great. I stayed on the middle floors so I couldn't hear the bar at all. What you should keep in mind is that there was a 150 extra hold on my card for the room which gets taken off. If you pay with debit, you'll see it in your statement if your on top of such things, but you won't see it if you pay by credit card. I had a good stay.

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Great hotel near everything you need!”
text:
We loved this hotel. Rooms were a good size - for new york! Although breakfast is expensive there are loads of places to eat on 9th avenue (do a right out of the hotel and first left) that serve a great breakfast! The hotel is on the same block as a subway entrance which is good when you need to rest your legs! It is only 2 blocks from times square and broadway, which means you dont have to go far until you are in the middle of the action.
The staff where helpful and friendly and could not be faulted.
Overall, this was a great hotel that I would happily visit again!

name: Microtel Inn & Suites by Wyndham Philadelphia Airport
title: “You Get What you Pay For”
text: You get what you pay for here. Room rate is cheap and hotel provides the minimum. Our room was clean but did not have any amenities. The breakfast selections consist of oatmeal packets, cereal, and bagels. Coffee and hot water are also available. Shuttle to the airport is fast and convenient. There is also a computer in the lobby if you don't have a lap top. If you just need a place to lay your head the night before a flight, this place qualifies.

name: Loews Philadelphia Hotel
title: “classy”
text:
Classy, expensive, centrally located to EVERYTHING with one of the most helpful staff I have ever encountered. Restaurant/bar is very good-but eat outside of the hotel!! 
rooms are clean-not real spacious but adequate and comfortable. Great place for a special weekend or trip

name: Four Points by Sheraton Philadelphia Northeast
title: “Perfectly nice but only the people stand out”
text:
The thing that stood out about this hotel was the staff. Everyone we talked to was extremely friendly and willing to help. We were greeted with a smile and it felt authentic. When we needed help it was provided generously.
Other than that... it was just OK. I'm not sure what this hotel is convenient to (highways, attractions, etc) but whatever it was, it wasn't what we needed. As others mentioned, the road it is on (Roosevelt Blvd) is very complicated to navigate and definitely added a few minutes to most of our trips. If you are coming here frequently and know what you're getting into, then these things probably aren't a problem. If you're not from the area and this is your first trip, you should be sure you want to get yourself into this, as opposed to something right off the interstate. 
The room itself was nice, but not exceptional. Everything was very clean. The TV was small but the pillows were amazingly comfortable. We had 2 beds but only one desk to work at, but we had a nice little mini-fridge and microwave. The price we paid was relatively high for what we got, but Philly is a big city so it wasn't outrageous.

name: Fairfield Inn Philadelphia Airport
title: “More basic than most”
text: The room was quiet but more basic than other Fairfield Inns that I have stayed at. Very good service. Same breakfast as others. Convenient to hotel and highway. I would probably stay here again if I arrived late or had an early morning flight.

name: Hilton Philadelphia City Avenue
title: “Falls Below Expectations”
text:
The rooms were fine.
The $90/night wireless fee is completely unreasonable in this day and age.
I specifically went to the front desk to leave one door key for my husband, who was supposed to arrive very late. The lady at the desk told me that they would just make him a new key. When he arrived, there was no note for the room, and the front desk had to call and wake me up.
The service in general seemed not very friendly and not very competent.

name: Loews Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Great stay”
text:
My husband, my son and I visited Philadelphia to see the historical sites and the King Tut exhibit. We got a great rate at the Loew's of about $161 per night, using a AAA discount. We parked in their garage which was a little steep at $30+ per night and then checked in. The desk clerk was extremely friendly and pleasant. He presented my son with a kids' welcome kit in a drawstring gym bag which was a nice touch. Our room was on the concierge floor which entitled us to continental breakfast and complimentary use of the fitness center. The room was not huge but it was well-appointed and comfortable and it did have a great view of the city and the river. The only odd thing was that the maid came to see if we wanted turndown and never came back. (We mentioned this in our exit survey and received an apologetic email from the manager.) Continental breakfast was good. There were bagels, scones and plenty of fresh fruit. The Loew's is also a pet-friendly hotel, so one sees cats and dogs in the hallways with their owners. 
We enjoyed Philadelphia and are already planning a trip back. We will definitely be staying at the Loew's again.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Philadelphia City Center
title: “Very Nice”
text: We stayed at this hotel with our family. It is close to convention center. Hotel is very nice. Rooms are very clean. We enjoyed our stay.

name: Hilton Philadelphia City Avenue
title: “Beautiful Hotel, great location”
text: In town for a quick business trip. Room was clean and bed was very comfortable. Our room had a very nice view. Went to the Polo Lounge, service was good and the lounge was a great place to meet friends for drinks. Found it easier to use the valet service than try and find parking. Valet attendants were very friendly and efficient. The location was perfect, just a short ride to the major universities, downtown and on City Line.

name: Sheraton Philadelphia University City Hotel
title: “Convenient to UPenn Hospital”
text:
We stayed at this Sheraton when our son needed surgery at UPenn. This Sheraton is located about a 10 minutes walk to the hospital or 3-4 minutes taxi ride. Taxi's were available 24hrs. It is not convenient to go to Philadelphia center. 
 The area is safe & clean, and we felt comfortable walking day or night. There are a few eatery's near-by. But we had difficulty finding a breakfast place near-by--and the hotel offered little.
The hotel and rooms are clean and basic. The rooms had a computer with wi-fi, but the wi-fi did not always work. The only food available seemed to be a Chinese restaurant that is by the lobby. This restaurant was always crowded so the food must be good. We enjoyed the small bar there which was not crowded. You can also sit on the front 'porch' to eat or have a drink. Overall, this was an 'ok' place to stay for a short time.

name: Ritz-Carlton Philadelphia
title: “Solid hotel in good location”
text:
Stayed at the Riz with my husband and 4 month old son. We paid 230 for a weekend night and that seemed to be a fair price. The rooms were clean and nice and the building was historic and pretty. It was great to b so close everything as well. My only complaint was noise. We stayed at the end of a hallway and perhaps there was a wedding at the hotel. There were several very loud guests between 11 pm-1 am and we could hear everything even with the tv on. The hotel overall is a great choice although I would never describe it as luxury. 
We used the pool at the hotel down the street they have an agreement with bc the ritz does not have one. The gym and spa were nice but the pool was a smallish lap pool not great for kids

name: Andaz Wall Street
title: “Klasse Hotel in NY”
text: Wir waren vom Andaz Wall Street absolut begeistert und haben uns sehr wohl gefühlt. Das Hotel ist neu und modern eingerichtet. Die Zimmer sind für New Yorker Verhältnisse riesig. Vom bequemen Bett bis zur Regendusche im Bad: alles top! Nichtalkoholische Getränke (Voss-Wasser, Bio-Eistee etc) und verschiedene Snacks aus der Minibar waren ebenso kostenlos wie heiße Getränke und abend ein Glas Wein in der Lobby. Das Personal ist unaufdringlich hilfsbereit und sehr freundlich. Problematisch war lediglich unsere Anreise mit dem Shuttle-Service von JFK. Unser Fahrer brauchte mehrere Anläufe, um das Hotel zu finden.

name: Trump SoHo New York
title: “Loved this place!”
text: This place was great from start to finish. The valet out front was super helpful with our car and suggesting alternative parking. The front desk service was really nice - they offered upgrades at good rates, although we just stuck with our original room. Check-in followed by complimentary champagne and strawberries. The room was so much better than I was expecting. I've stayed in a lot of NYC hotels and this room did not compare. It was so nice!!! Great room amenities, very clean and modern, really nice bathroom with a big separate tub with a view. The best part of the room was the bed. It was so comfy...I could not get out of it! Overall it was a great experience - everyone was very nice here. Great location for Soho shopping. I will be back!

name: Hotel Palomar Philadelphia - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Our favorite hotel”
text: Can't say enough great things about staying here when in philly - the staff, the rooms, the ambiance are just so above and beyond. So unique and welcoming.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Philadelphia Northeast
title: “Nice hotel”
text: This hotel met all of my expectations on a weekend stay. The front desk staff checked me in quickly and courteously. The room was very clean and in good repair. I like that the hotel offers free wireless Internet access. I would be glad to stay there again.

name: Renaissance Philadelphia Airport
title: “Good”
text: I have stayed here a few times in the last couple of years. I like the location of this hotel and is the main reason I stay here. Service and staff at this hotel is great, nothing to complain about. My only complaint would be that the hotel does look a little old and compared to the other Renaissance I have stayed at in the past, the cleanliness is not up to my expectations (the bed skirt cover looked a little discolored and there were markings and stains on some of the walls. But for a day or 2 while in Philly, I would recommend this Hotel. The Staff, Service and Location also the price makes this a great stay in Philly. I will be staying here again next time in Philly. Message to management, a little renovation would make this a great hotel.

name: Andaz Wall Street
title: “mooi hotel, verkeerde locatie, service hapert”
text:
mooi hotel, modern.
locatie is niet fijn, weinig te beleven buiten kantoortijden, onhandige metrolijnen in de buurt, vrijwel altijd overstappen.
service hapert, lang gewacht om kamer in te kunnen (uren), minibar werd niet gevuld. bovendien woerd er gezegd bij inchecken dat we geupgrade waren, terwijl we gewoon voor die kamer betaald hebben. neppe beleefdheid...
klinkt best negatief, maar wel leuke tijd gehad, gewoon negeren die dingen.

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Excellent hotel for an excellent trip”
text:
Travelled to Distrikt Hotel over the Easter Weekend for Silver Wedding, 18th and 21st birthday triple family celebration, chose hotel after research on Tripadvisor as wanted room for me and my husband and 2 grown up children and we were not disappointed. Street might not look great at first sight but mainly due to being opposite Port Authority but no problems and really well positioned for Times Square and Subway to take you anywhere in Manhattan . Rooms were very clean, modern and contemporary and all we could want considering didn't spend a lot of time in there, computers in lobby very handy and bar on an evening very welcoming-Didn't pay for breakfast but ate in Dean and Deluca in the New York Times Building at end of street every day which was lovely, reasonably priced and all you could want - coffee, muffins, pancakes, bagels and eggs etc..would thoroughly recommend it.
The walk over Brooklyn Bridge on Easter Sunday in the sunshine was a huge highlight, and the views were brilliant, this was followed by lunch in Petes on the Brooklyn Heights pier, the views from Rockefeller Center on an evening were truly fantastic and well worth the wait !! Serendipity (off Central Park) was a wonderfully magical experience, chilli dogs followed by Frozen hot chololate was the dream and to be recommended ! only downside was pre booking transport from JFK with NYAS which was disappointing, it took an age for a mini bus to come at JFK(to be told by guy at aiport we'd been overcharged) and then coming back waited for bus at Port Authority for a while and then when it came had to then change at Grand Central Station, next time may get Airtrain to Subway station for travel into Manhattan.

name: Renaissance Philadelphia Airport
title: “Better than Expected”
text: Stayed here one night, as we missed our flight connection home. Arrived very late and very tired to a nice, comfortable, clean hotel. Check-in was quick and easy. Staff was pleasant and empathized with our situation. We had no luggage with us, and therefore had to take advantage of any and all toiletries offered. The room was huge...I could have done cartwheels across the whole room! The bed was very comfortable...I slept like a baby. Bathroom was big, maybe a little old, but good sized. All the toiletries provided were of decent quality. There was a room service menu for breakfast that had quite a few options. There appeared to be other dining options available, but we literally stayed in this hotel for 7 hours. 24 hour shuttle service to and from the airport was very convenient. We really had no complaints. If we ever need a hotel in Philadelphia again, I would not hesitate to stay here!

name: Fairfield Inn Philadelphia Airport
title: “fantastic!!!”
text: Wow!!! I was a little worried because it was near the airport and didn't want to hear planes etc. - heard not a peep! - The room was clean - the beds so comfy - the sheets soft . The breakfast room was really well stocked - and coffee and tea available 24 hours. What really made this hotel stand out though was the staff. They were friendly, helpful and just generally very kind. The lady that worked the breakfast room was so sweet and cheerful - she really made our stay a little special (I think her name was Christal). We'll be staying here again.

name: Renaissance Philadelphia Airport
title: “Good Stay”
text:
I stayed in this hotel 1 night for a personnel trip.
The location is bad. Very hard to get to, but then most hotels in the area are a challenge.
The staff was very helpful. There was a huge line but they took care of us very quickly (less than two minute wait). I was on a special rate but forgot my card, but they gave it to me anyway. 
The room was very good, typical for Marriott hotels. Clean room, comfortable bed.
Check out was very quick.
Only thing that was strange was there was 100 kids running abound the hotel. Not sure why, did not affect my stay, just odd.

name: Loews Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Indeed one of the loewest class hotel!”
text:
We booked directly with this hotel December 15. 2004 for a corner unit up on the 28th floor. When we got there, they gave us a smaller room beside it which to an unattentive customer appears like it is in a corner. Worse, the toilet was not flushing. It was broken!
So finally, after requesting for a change and 2 hours wait, they gave us a room adjacent to it- it was the room we originally paid for which was not occupied to begin with. These two rooms, intended for family use, has a common privacy door that can be closed if a family decides to keep their individual doors open. 
We left for dinner and night cap and returned around 12 midnight only to find out that the common door was locked. Our keys did not work! We called the concierge who told us to wait for security to open the door for us. After 20 mins, they came up and were unable to open the same door. They reasoned that another guest who is occupying the other room locked the door from within. The security was unapologetic and uncouth after we complained this should not be happening. 
We spoke to the female night supervisor over the cell phone who never bothered to investigate and checked the situation for herself. Finally, after an hour, maintenance came and found a key to open it. Frustrated with the whole situation, we decided to leave and take a walk around the immediate vicinity. As soon as we got back, we discovered the common door was locked again!! 
We complained the next day to a female day supervisor who apologized and promised to give us a free night whenever we decide to. She took our address and promised to send the voucher. The free night voucher never came.
The experience was the worse we had. We had no choice to leave and find another hotel because it happened in the middle of the night.

name: Hilton Philadelphia City Avenue
title: “Hotel Average - Pricey Food Good”
text:
I stayed at this Hilton during a business trip. It was disappointing for a Hilton brand. The housekeeping standard is more like a motel rather than a hotel. The carpet was not vacuumed well. I had to call guest services early in the morning to bring toilet tissue since only a partial roll was left in the room on my first day of check-in. 
The room had 2 queen beds and a 32-inch Flat Screen HDTV. The bed was very comfortable. The temperature control in the room worked well. 
The staff were friendly. The valet service was very good.
In the lobby they had a daily fruit infused water and a fresh fruit basket for guests.
The food was good. The full service cold/hot breakfast buffet was included with the price of the room. We had dinner twice at the hotel in Delmonico's Steakhouse. It is pricey as one might expect with the Delmonico name. The soup, salads, steak and fish were all good.
If I were in the area again, I would probably stay at another hotel due to not having the room maintained to a level that matches the above average price.

name: Holiday Inn Philadelphia Stadium
title: “Great Location”
text: I had an early morning flight form Philly and booked this hotel for the price. I was nicely surprised by the quality of the hotel and staff. Checking in and out was easy and the staff very friendly even at 5am. The room was spacious, clean and comfortable. The location was very convenient to the airport.

name: Loews Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Cool hotel though stingy”
text: Room was cool! Booked through Orbitz & was greatly pleased with amount paid for room. Was misled though seeing that pool & gym were at an extra charge. (Orbitz & hotel blame each other for this misconception.) Had to argue my way though after 10 mins, didn't have to pay extra charge. Hotel's right across from Hard Rock Cafe & within walking distance to everything. Would stay again if I found a good price.

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Preferred hotel in New York”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel 5 times. I love staying here. It is located in a very accessible location. The hotel linens are younger than i am. It is a great choice for me for business. The restaurant prices are wonderful. They make it so much easier to just eat in the hotel and then head off to work. Linda is exceptional in the restaurant.
This is the one place i choose to stay on a consistent basis.

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Hotel very good. location excellent.”
text: Booked this hotel after reading reviews on tripadvisor. Stayed for a week and enjoyed our stay. The room was very clean and quite large by New York standards. The first morning I discovered the shower door was not closing properly and then the shower control broke when i was having shower. Both problems were fixed later that day. The location was excellent though the street is a little run-down. My only small complaint would be the bar/restaurant. We did not use this for breakfast as there are loads of places nearby but the bar itself lacked atmosphere and seemed to be rarely used by guests.

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “Un must....”
text:
Le Bryant Park Hôtel est un endroit sublime....luxe et discrétion pour un hôtel en passe de devenir un des hôtels branchés de New York. 
La déco est raffinée et design, le personnel est aux petits soins, le service est irréprochable.....bref...un oasis à deux pas de Time Square et de l'Empire State Building. 
Le restaurant de l'hôtel, le KOI est un restaurant gastronomique japonais...un véritable enchantement....
En un mot....le top absolu

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “Excellent !”
text:
Très bonne surprise, car réservé dans le cadre d'un package, le Bryant Park est tout d'abord extrêment bien situé, à 10 minutes de Times Squares, 3 minutes de l'Empire State. Les chambres sont spacieuses avec une grande salle de bain (douche et baignoire pour notre catégorie).
L'hôtel abrite le Koi restaurant, tendance asiatique et sushi bar délicieux ! Ainsi que le cellar bar ou la jeunesse New Yorkaise se presse les soirs de weekend.
Dernier point, le personnel est tout à fait adorable, des portiers à la réception en passant par la room service, ils sont tous charmants et efficaces (petit ciln d'oeil à Ryan)

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Stylish hotel”
text: Stylish and clean hotel very nicely located. Only two things were bad, the free WiFi did not work on Android devices and there were no minibar in the room.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Philadelphia Airport
title: “Typical Cookie Cutter Courtyard. Didn't Disappoint.”
text:
This was a Courtyard that did its best to be like every other Courtyard. Not that that's necessarily a bad thing.
I stayed here during extended business in Philly. I booked this for a very reasonable rate after blind bidding on Priceline. Because of this, I was especially happy with my stay.
If you are using the airport shuttle, you should note that you ought to call ahead to the hotel when you land, as its shuttles may not be running a regular schedule. I waited a little bit, thinking they ran a regular schedule, before having an attendant at the ground transportation booth call ahead for me.
The hotel is located relatively close by. The facility is nearly identical to Courtyards that I stayed at, including Columbus, OH and Savannah, GA. Check in was smooth. The room had contemporary furnishings, and a comfortible bed. My room also contained a fridge.
Overall, nice stay.

name: Sheraton Suites Philadelphia Airport
title: “Great Stay”
text:
We were visiting Philadelphia with our two children (3 and 1 and a half) and chose to stay here even though it was a half hour drive from our main attraction (Sesame Place). It was well worth the drive. Even though there were "All Suite Hotels" closer, there is nothing like the Sheraton Suites.
 As all the recent reviews stated, the hotel looks great with their recent renovation. The lobby and bar are beautiful and modern looking. Very inviting. I loved the open atrium. Rooms are very nice and comfortable. Great Sheraton bed.
Even the pullout sofa bed was very comfortable. 
As for the complaints about customer service, most of the people I encountered were very nice. There was one lady in the morning who seemed a little "cold", but it didn't affect me in any way. I also asked her for some pillows for the sofa bed as we did not get any, and they were never delivered. However I never followed up and I am sure they would have gotten it for me had I asked again. There were a bunch of pillows on the regular bed so we just used the extra ones for our kids.
There was a really nice lady by the starbucks. I asked her for a drink that they had never made there. She told me she didn't have the right materials for the drink and she would try to make it without it. She gave it to me for free and it was great.
Overall it was a great stay and I will definitely stay here again.

name: Travelodge Philadelphia Convention Center
title: “Nice Visit”
text: Hotel was in easy walking distance of the attractions and subway/train station. One negative is that a homeless mission was next door but it was not as bad as I would have thought. Rooms were nice and clean but I wish it had a microwave and fridge.

name: Holiday Inn Philadelphia Stadium
title: “A good night's slepp”
text:
Stayed here for two nights in August 2011.
The hotel is very convenient for the stadiums and the arena, although that makes it a little remote for visiting the city (which we did). It is also well located in respect to the airport, and they offer a free shuttle to the airport.
I was working at the Arena, so the location was perfect. I also visited the city using the subway system and was only a 15 minute commute (3 dollar round trip).
The room, whilst dated was renovated and very spacious. The room was also very clean, and to be honest I have no complaints.
There were two queen sized beds with varying pillows (pillows had tags telling if they were soft, hard etc). There was a desk, a tv, a microwave, a coffee machine and a fridge in the room. I was lucky to have a beautiful view of the city skyline, but my colleague was equally lucky having a view of the stadiums. Overall rooms were great. Shower was clean, and like a sandblaster (lots of pressure). I did end up with a slightly cold shower on the second morning. Wifi was free, but not exactly hi-speed....
I ate at the restaurant and bar and found the food to be good and the prices were also good. My main complaint would be with the coffee...nasty stuff. Wish there would have been a Starbucks or something like that either in the hotel or close.
Overall the hotel was good for my needs. I am not sure of the value, as Io never saw the bill.

name: Ritz-Carlton Philadelphia
title: “A Home Away From Home”
text: My wife and I have been guests at the Ritz for about 2 years now. We stay at this "home-away from home" 2 days per month. This hotel is the friendliest place I ever stayed. The service personnel are some of the finest ladies and gentlemen I have ever met. We will return 12/07-and I am sure we will again be treated like royalty.

name: Comfort Inn Downtown/Historic Area
title: “ok for this price in Philly”
text: I stayed one night there with $124, ,which I think it is very pricy. I had a room with the river view and noisy street. Room is not very clean. The tub has some stains and I feel there are som bag in the other bed. Good thing is there are two beds in the room. A/C and street were so loud that I had to put earpluges to sleep. The view from my room is very beautiful and the staffs are very nice. Breakfast was okay.

name: Trump SoHo New York
title: “Amazing Hotel”
text:
The staff was so courteous and friendly that I instantly felt at ease as soon as we checked in. Even the maid ran out on the day we were leaving and wished us a safe trip home. They have a concierge that will look after your every need but the doormen and front desk staff are always ready to recommend a restaurant or to give you directions. I had a deluxe one bedroom suite on the 32nd floor. The view was absolutely stunning, I loved just lying on our bed and staring at the Empire State Building at night. If you want the same view get a one bedroom suite 21st floor or higher that ends with 10 (3210, 3310 etc.) It's worth the extra money just to admire the majesty of that American landmark.
 The hotel is nicely situated to the Spring St. subway station but also a short walk to Canal St. and Prince St. stations.(All separate lines). SOHO is such a beautiful area with all its boutiques and cafe's and restaurants and it was only a fifteen minute stroll from the hotel to Little Italy. If you want to see Times Square, hop on the subway and ten minutes later you're there. We used the subway exclusively in the daytime and saw everything from the Statue of Liberty to Coney Island. This was the best hotel experience my wife and I have ever had not only because of everything the hotel had to offer but also because the staff was so professional, courteous and friendly you truly can't wait to come back.

name: Renaissance Philadelphia Airport
title: “Fine but for a checkout problem”
text: Overall I enjoyed the ambiance. The room was clean, well appointed with upscale fabrics. I did not get to try the restaurant since it was a short stay. I was hoping to get a hotel closer to the city, but despite that it was an enjoyable stay. The problem came as a result of the desk clerk swiping my card for "incidentals" although the room was prepaid. So although I did not charge anything to my room I was billed by the renaissance for an additional night's stay! They tried to make it seem like it was my fault. That experience was the only down side to my stay in Philly.

name: Hotel Palomar Philadelphia - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Ok stay”
text: Because of my experience with the Palomar in Los Angeles recently I decided to try the Palomar in Philadelphia. Kimpton seems to have found a good formula for their hotels: modern, clean rooms and great beds. However, I stayed for three nights in a 'City View King" room, a room on the 17th floor, but it was small and dark and had no real view of the city, not that I cared much about that but still ... don't advertise it like a "City View". Overall it was an ok stay.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Philadelphia Center City
title: “Great location, great hotel”
text:
We were pleasantly surprised by this hotel. The location was perfect with a lovely view, the staff was really nice and helpful, and it was a great value. It has an indoor pool and hot tub, gym and racquetball court. The rooms were spacious and clean, beds and pillows were very comfortable.
We got a deal on hotels.com and it included a free buffet breakfast in their dining room - very good! Really, nothing negative to say about this property.

name: Magic Castle Hotel
title: “Muy buena situación”
text:
El Magic Castle Hotel está magníficamente situado: puedes ir andando al mítico Bulevar de las Estrellas, donde hay que pasear de arriba a abajo para poder ver las estrellas, el Kodak Theatre... LLegar hasta allí es complicado en coche por el tema del aparcamiento. Por eso tener un hotel cerca lo consideramos una ventaja. 
Para visitar el resto de sitios que interesa conocer en Los Ángeles, el coche facilita mucho el desplazamiento, sobre todo si dispones de poco tiempo para ello como era nuestro caso. El Magic Castle dispone de aparcamiento gratuito cubierto, lo cual supuso otra ventaja.
El personal de recepción es muy amable, y eso siempre es de agradecer. 
La habitación era una suite para cuatro personas, tipo apartamento: mesa y sillas, nevera, microondas... aunque nosotros no hicimoe uso de nada de eso ya que sólo estuvimos dos noches. Lo peor fue al llegar, ya que estaba en la última planta (tres pisos) y no tienen ascensor. Como nuestro equipaje era algo numeroso y pesado (estábamos haciendo un recorrido por California), fue un inconveniente tanto al llegar como al marcharnos.
Nuestra habitación no era gran cosa, a pesar de ser espaciosa. El sofá cama era bastante incómodo, y la cama de la habitación principal era Queen size. Resultó algo pequeña, ya que la tuvimos que compartir con nuestra hija. Creo que no es una habitación para cuatro, ya que aunque la cama del sofá no era pequeña, era imposible que durmieran cómodamente en ella dos personas: el colchón era francamente malo y se hundía en el centro. Nuestro hijo mayor la utilizó las dos noches y no resultó muy confortable. Hubiera sido una pequeña tortura que durmieran en ella los dos hermanos juntos.
Disponía de aire acondicionado y ventilador de techo (en la habitación principar), lo que es de agradecer.
El precio incluía el desayuno. No era muy variado (muffins, galletas, cereales, algo de fruta, yogures...), pero suficiente. Lo malo es la escasez de mesas para desayunar. Nosotros tuvimos suerte los dos días, pero efectivamente era cuestión de suerte conseguir una.
Tiene una pequeña piscina, junto a la que están dispuestas las mesas del desayuno, que nosotros no llegamos a utilizar.
En resumen, un hotel sin grandes pretensiones, pero al que se puede ir si lo que se busca es la localización y un servicio adecuado sin excesos.

name: Trump SoHo New York
title: “TRUMP SOHO TRIUMPHS OVER ADVERSITY”
text:
My initial reaction to this hotel was anger and frustration. My room wasn't ready on arrival, and I was forced to change out of an expensive suit in a basement bathroom stall. I work out religeously, and I had no idea their gym had not been completed. The Trump Soho set up a room as a replacement gym with a couple of eliptical machines and that was it! Unacceptable! Also, their late night room service menu was ludicrously limited. However, the Trump Soho had a better "come back" then Richard Nixon!
The manager of the hotel insisted that I be upgraded to a fantastic room on the 35th floor. I was provided passes to a full service gym a few blocks up Varrick Street. I was also comped my room service meal.
Other then my personal issues, the hotel shines in a multitude of ways:
1. The location is superb. You are in between Soho and the West Village, two of the most lovely, authentic areas of New York. Countless boutiques, restaurants, and lounges surround you. Several subways are within walking distance and it is wonderful to avoid the sterility and commercialism of Midtown.
2. All the rooms are some of the largest you will ever have in NYC. The furnishings, towels, etc are all top notch, and a guest is enveloped in luxury. The bathrooms are simply sublime.
3. The hotel is new. Thus, everything works, shines, and is fresh.
4. The staff, although a bit too young, inexperienced, and dependent on looks and hipness, will bend over backwards to meet your needs. They are willing to listen to suggestions from an older, but perhaps more kmowledgable traveler, about restaurants and shops in the area. (Mas Farmhouse is incredible!)
5. The Italian restaurant attached to the hotel is a sibling establishment of an esteemed Italian restaurant in Miami and they may be going through some growing pains, but the food was very good and the chef and manager were willing to make the changes necessary.
6. The bar was beautiful with beautiful people, and the top notch liquors were mixed well by the trendy bartenders.
I ended up having a great hotel experience and I am planning to return to the Trump Soho the first week of August for a week. I may not get as many upgrades, but the hotel will be an absolute gem once the initial kinks are worked out.

name: Holiday Inn Philadelphia Stadium
title: “Great price, crappy location”
text:
We were in town for 1 night to watch the Flyers playoff game and were able to get a very good price using a discount site. The hotel is very convenient if you're in town for just a game. If you want to tack on any sightseeing, the hotel is very far removed from the action and it is diffcult to get a cab (in my experience) to come get you. There were cabs outside at 5:30 am when we headed back to the airport (shuttle only starts operating at 6 am). The restaurant has been closed for some time and I'm suspicious of the reviews that talk about it recently being open. 
The room was clean, beds were comfy and lots of hot water. We were on the 5th floor and on the parking lot side but had no issues with the noise (weather may have helped as it was cold and rainy).
Next time, we will stay closer to downtown and take the subway to the game.

name: Travelodge Philadelphia Convention Center
title: “YOU GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR!!!”
text: This place looks nice when you first walk in, and the staff was nice at first. When we walked up to our room and entered, it was like entering a very small bedroom with two beds..The room was like 75-80 degrees when we walked in and the staff came up and "fixed" it, but said if it doesn't kick on he will bring us a fan! What??? I didn't pay this money to stay in a room that has no windows or air!!! this is rediculous!! Luckily we won't be in the room too much since we are here for buisness, but I highly do NOT recommend anyone stay here!!!! EVER!!!

name: Radisson Plaza-Warwick Hotel Philadelphia
title: “Great deal”
text:
Nice, clean rooms. Bathrooms are a bit small, but clean and well stocked.
Nice lobby, great location. We would definitely stay here again!

name: The Bryant Park Hotel
title: “L'endroit ou aller !”
text:
Hotel idéalement situé (entre la 5ème et la 6ème avenue, à une dizaine de blocs de Central Park), vue imprenable sur le Bryant Park, la bibliothèque, une partie de Time Square, l'Empire State Building, etc.), chambre superbement équipée-spacieuse-confortable-cozy (encore un grand merci à Darren pour son accueil très chaleureux à notre arrivée), service de chambre très discret (dans le bon sens du terme) et efficace, et sans oublier bien évidemment cet endroit magnifique qu'est le Cellar Bar.
Encore tous mes remerciements à toute l'équipe pour ce séjour qui restera à vie gravé dans ma mémoire.
J'en redemande !!!
Pour ceux qui hésiteraient encore, n'hésitez plus et foncez les yeux fermés !

name: Travelodge Philadelphia Convention Center
title: “You Get What You Pay For”
text:
I stayed at the Travelodge over Labor Day weekend. Yes the hotel is on a side street and it's possible you can get a room without a window. But the hotel is located in a good area. Both Reading Market and Chinatown is a block away. You're also not too far away from Phlash Shuttle. 
However do be careful at night as there are homeless people waiting for a free bed at the shelter 2 doors down.

name: aloft Philadelphia Airport
title: “Pleasant place, but avoid first floor”
text: Aloft hotels provide a contemporary, trendy experience. This hotel near the Philadelphia airport is like other Alofts I've seen... with a lobby area that is as much hang bar as check in counter! The rooms are comfortable with furnishing that make most other hotels seem boring. There's enough substance to this hotel that you expect it to be a lot more expensive than it is. My one warning is to decline the room if they offer you a room on the first floor. They made a point to tell me that the door between the lobby and the guest rooms provided a sound-proof barrier. But the door itself makes a racket every time it slams behind someone coming or going.

name: aloft Philadelphia Airport
title: “They DO NOT tell you about hidden when booking on line”
text: My stay @ the Aloft was terrible 1 they don't tell you about the 7 dollar parking or the $50.00 extra room fee when you book on line. We lefts in Aug. and it's almost Oct.and we still haven't got our $50.00 back from them when you call no one I MEAN NO ONE is available. That left a very bad taste in our mouths so PLEASE be careful when booking with them on line. VERY UNHAPPY nice place to stay if you have no other place to go.

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “A Wonderful Experience...”
text: My two girlfriends and I decided to take a trip to NYC for the annual Christmas tree lighting ceremony at the Rockefeller Center. I have been to NYC numerous times and had looked very long for a hotel to book, and I was extremely picky due to the bedbug epidemic. I got an awesome rate for this hotel for two nights and every review was positive. Unfortunately, my day of arrival I had the flu and was very sick and tired. The staff was very welcoming and checked us in more than 3 hours early so that I could get some rest. They had set up hot cider in the lobby (which I loved) and helped us with any questions we had. Our room was incredibly comfortable and very clean. Everytime we left and came back our bed was made and everything was back in place again. Beds were very comfy and found no signs of bedbugs...thank goodness!!! That evening the bell man carried a case of water to our room for us and even offered to keep our water in fridge downstairs so they were cold. Umbrellas were provided for use on the days we had rain and we had a cab for us anytime we wanted. Overall, I had a wonderful stay at The Distrikt and I plan to return very soon. The staff couldn't have been more friendly, and the service was spectacular :)

name: Sonesta Hotel Philadelphia
title: “Needs some more work to be above average”
text:
so,this is a tough one. hotel at check in was fast and efficient - we drove a long way in a snow storm, go there and were able to upgrade our room to what the call their "executive suite" - which meant you had a flat screen tv and some updated room amenities. we got into the room and compared to other places we stay in cities would say the room was "adequate" - TV was flat screen, but analog, no room refrigerator <which is usually helpful because of some dietary needs when I travel for several days> which meant I needed a good size ice bucket to keep certain things cold until morning; the room had no way to open window and was very stuffy <read below> - the towels were not luxurious but functional enough, the bathrooms were the tiniest I have been to in a long time <the door just "cleared" the edge of the toilet in swinging open and closed> - the ceiling was low - when I got into bathtub and stretched I hit the ceiling (I am 5'11") - oh yeah - and the phone next to the bed was not working - - ok now onto day 2
I head out from room on Day 2 around 10 am - -get back around 1:30+/- and room has still not been attended - ok fine - so I sit down at desk to do some work and I hear "drip drip drip" - and get up , go to bathroom area - nothing in sink, then turn on light in shower/bath area and I see the "drip drip drip" is coming straight out of the light fixture above the toilet <good thing I left toilet seat open or I might have been wading in some of it>// so I IMMEDIATELY turn off the light as the "light bowl" was literally filled with water, go out to phone and call the desk to report the "WATER PROBLEM" in the bathroom coming through the "ELECTRICAL FIXTURE" - so I wait, and wait - and about 15 minutes later call and say: "DID I MENTION THE WATER WAS DROPPING THROUGH AN ACTIVE LIGHT FIXTURE?".....yes yes - they paged the engineer she should be on her way..... + 5 min: I open the hall door and askthe housekeeper to page the engineer or someone.....ok now +20 minutes I call again - the desk says the engineer is on her way - a few more minutes , and finally a knock on the door - the engineer comes in, looks and then mumbles something and runs out????!!! OK FINE - so I sit there and wait some more - about 10 minutes later engineer reappears with assistant - they unscrew light bowl and dump it out - dripping seems less and then stops - SO, the room above had a leak from the roof (<big snow storm nite before> and engineer tells me that I have option to move rooms - I GUESS SO - 
ANYWAY - to shorten this up - they do arrange a similar room on same floor and now I have to REPACK all my bags and materials, get the bell man up to help me move , let my husband know that room has changed and to call me before he returns from meeting - 
2 hours later - all set in new room - 2 hours of my life I would not get back
later that night - new room was even "STUFFIER" and warm that night ....if that was possible...
in the wee hours we decided to get up and check the actual wall unit - we opened it up <licky for us?> and took out the filter and the air started flowing better - in the sun, we looked at that filter and were totally grossed out - it was dirty and packed with dust and debris - we stuck our head out in the morning, caught housekeeping on the floor - who put in a nice clean filter - - WTH?! anyone got a maintenance checklist at this hotel????
Plus side : 
everyone was very professional, eager to correct the mistakes and front desk offered us some options as comps - we chose some drinks at their bar (reviewed separately)
Hotel is in great location as far as getting around Center city and all it has to offer
So individual staff made up for lack of overall management of the hotel - 
there is no excuse for the experience we had - just sloppy engineering/maintenance
Until they get their facility maintenance act together - these "exec rooms" are a $100 value "at best".... not what we paid for them

name: Comfort Inn Downtown/Historic Area
title: “Hotel on a highway”
text: Stayed in this hotel recently i had a view of the river,the bridge and the highway below me. The noise was unbelievable all the time you could hear the noise of cars and the bridge a train passed over it every 10 or 15 mins. I got no sleep at all. Checking in i waited 20 minutes before being seen to, the receptionist had to take all calls while checking in people as well. The hotel offers a complimentary shuttle service within a 3 mile radius to and from, i took advantage of this and being in this vehicle with this driver was a nightmare he regulary cursed and sweared and his driving was a nightmare.On our way to our location he said get a taxi back as it was to busy and he said he wasn`t coming back. I tried to arrange a late check out and i went to reception 3 times, the first time the girl said the manager was stuck in a traffic jam this was at 9am, so i went back at 10am and was told he had not arrived yet so i returned again at 11am and the lady said he was not starting until 2pm and this was the same lady i had spoke to at all times. So in other words i just had to check out even though i would have been prepared to pay a nominal fee for a few more hours. The complimentary breakfast was ok if you like rice krispies and bread because that was all that was there, there was no fruit. i checked out and left bags at hotel and then i came back to see the manager on duty (Andrew) and told him all my woes he said thanks for letting me know and have a nice day. Finally another guest on the way out said you get what you pay for but as there was a convention in town there was nothing cheap about this hotel. Advice stay somewhere else.

name: Embassy Suites Philadelphia - Center City
title: “Elevator nightmare”
text: Waited 30 minutes for an elevator in order to check out. Had to end up carrying luggage down 16 flights of stairs! Also, DO NOT go for feee breakfast!!!!!!

name: Club Quarters
title: “Amazing Location”
text:
This hotel has the "European Botique Hotel" charm. Dont expect a 5 star hotel, but expect a very clean, comfortable hotel in an amazing location! 
Walking distance from all of the museums, historical landmarks, shopping and AMAZING food!
The rooms are small and the windows smaller, but comfortably decorated with newer TV's etc. Bathrooms are RV small, but doable. 
The rooms are very clean! Free wifi in every room as well. Also a free happy hour (food) in the bar downstairs.

name: Crowne Plaza Philadelphia West
title: “Excellent experience”
text: We stayed there over Thanksgiving along with a couple of other relatives. Everyone had an excellent experience. The hotel was right off the highway, and the room provided a very comfortable spot for a rest break before heading over to my brother-in-law's for Thanksgiving dinner. We stayed two nights, and the staff was courteous throughout. I ordered room service for one lunch and, when I found the meal too spicy, they readily replaced it without any hassles. The hotel is situated adjacent to a shopping center, which included a Starbuck's. A very good value.

name: Hilton Philadelphia Airport
title: “Weekend Stay”
text:
Checkin on Friday and out on Sunday Drove to Phila for family funeral. 
Service was good. Greeted at the lobby door each time. 8 pm checkin was average. Wait time could have been less for I was tired. The real lemonade and cookies in the lobby were definitely welcomed and good. Requested extra tea and splenda and missing washclothes on second day. Both were provided immediately. Room was clean and smelled good. Requested frig for medical reasons while traveling. It was in the room and at no charge. 
Location was convenient to 95 and family activities in Germantown and West Phila. Was able to find my way with navigator to various locations under 1/2 hour. 
Hotel amenities were excellent. Designer tolieties were very nice. Shower was OK. Hand held shower would have been nice in my standard room. I see it is in the higher priced suite. This is a must in all rooms these days. This is a hotel breaker for future trips for me since I enjoy it in my home. Bed was very comfortable, slept well. I couldn't get the blackout curtains to close. Coffee/tea products were great. One coffee cup had a hair in it which I rinsed out in my room. Coffee maker needs to be flushed every so often so I can get clear hot water the first time. Parking is free and plentiful. I didn't have a chance to experience other amenities such as pool, fitness center, free wifi. The note on the desk was confusing leading me to think hotel wifi might not be free and not to use public fee service provider. No microwave in the stnd room but was able to use one in the cafe area which was nice for a saved on late night snack. Room service breakfast was on time and good. In hind sight, it's the same price as breakfast buffet with more choices so next time will go to restaurant. 
My overall stay was nice. I liked the bed the best and shower head the least.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Philadelphia Center City
title: “Very good location, not much more”
text:
The hotel is adjacent to the conference center and Reading food market.
The staff at the desk were all nice and helpful.
The elevators had a bad smell and old carpet. 
The corridor and the rooms need updating, all around tired.
The indoor pool was ok, quite small and tiny towels are provided.

name: Embassy Suites Philadelphia - Center City
title: “Loved It!”
text: I NEVER write reviews, but our stay was so pleasant I just had to give the hotel a 'shout out.' My husband, two kids and I just stayed here for a quick Spring Break visit (2012) and were very pleased. We love to travel and have learned that just because a hotel is part of a chain doesn't mean you'll get the service you might expect. But Embassy Suites always delivers. From the complimentary breakfast and Manager's reception to choosing TGI Friday for dinner everything was just as we'd expect from a nice hotel. Thank you to the Omelet Check -- he was awesome and so patient with my little one!!! Service was A+ and they went over and beyond in providing us with extra soap, towels, to blankets for our air mattress all with a friendly, service-oriented demeanor. Can't remember the names but everyone was friendly and helpful from our check-in person to housekeeping. Loved it and we can't wait to return. There was so much to see and do that we couldn't squeeze it all into 3 days! Definitely visit the Please Touch Museum, Franklin Institute, and the Battleship (NJ?).

name: Hilton Garden Inn Philadelphia Center City
title: “Good Locatation, Decent Room, LOUD AC!”
text: Good Location. Not the best part of town, not the worst. Loudest air conditioner that I have ever had the displeasure of listening for 4 nights.

name: Club Quarters
title: “Great location, great for business traveler”
text: I am a fan of Club Quarters, I like the smaller hotel with the conveniences they offer, they have complimentary bottled water stations at the elevator on each floor, free wifi, free printing, a nice lobby with coffee and tea. My room was small, but clean - when I'm traveling, I don't spend a lot of time in the room, I would rather be conveniently located to great restaurants and within walking distance to the places I need to be. I will be back.

name: Holiday Inn Hotel Historic District Philadelphia
title: “Stay anywhere else if at all possible”
text:
in order of issues:
-1st day: took over an hour to get a sandwich the first night. 
-2nd day: gift shop food was old tasting, room wasn't cleaned bed unmade, no conditioner only shampoo!
-Entire time: internet service was practically nonexistant 
Will never stay there again

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “GREAT place to stay”
text: We cannot say enough good things about the Distrikt Hotel. We stayed there for our 40th anniversary celebration in New York. The hotel is small...but the rooms are good sized, especially for New York. The staff was incredible...helpful, knowledgable and friendly. The hotel is across the street from the Port Authority Bus Terminal and just half a block from the entrance to the subway (be prepared for a long walk once you get underground). We'll happily stay at the Distrikt in the future!

name: Embassy Suites Philadelphia - Center City
title: “Acceptable but not worth the price....”
text:
I stayed in a king bed suite with 3 other adults to watch the Winter Classic. The room cost $250 per night which seemed rather expensive since this did not include parking ($44/night). The room itself is large, kinda dated, but clean. Although it's a suite, it does not include a full kitchen or kitchenette. It does, however, have a small sink and refrigerator.
 The bathroom exhaust fan did not work and a metal access panel in the shower stall did fall off the ceiling into the tub.
 There is a $12/person buffet at the TGIF on the second floor of the hotel. The buffet had a variety of hot and cold choices....not the greatest but it was convenient. Location was north of some of the main bar areas but there were at least 4 bars within a short walk. To get to the stadiums, you either need to drive, cab it, or take the metro.... It is not walkable. I would stay here again, however, I would only pay $150/night. Anything more would not be worth it.

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Downtown Hotel
title: “Excellent Hotel and Service! Best Hotel I lived in”
text:
I am a frequent traveler and I have lived 80 or so nights in this hotel. The hotel staff is customer excellence personified. Every night is an experience in itself. The staff is so much friendly that you feel like you are in home. Philip Marcano, Candis, Salahah, Edward (EJ), Ryan Todd, Tony, Brianna etc, great and extremely friendly folks. They have been nice every time I have stayed here for 25 weeks. Thank you folks, for your courtesy and I look forward staying you are the hotel for many more nights. 
For Hotel:
Excellent and cosy rooms
Great Beds, really comfortable
Nice Breakfast Buffet, very good selections
Lounge with necessary snacks and drinks for Platinum
Very Good Room Service
Great Location
Best Part - GREAT STAFF!!!!!
It has been a pleasure staying at this hotel
Best,
Jitesh Desai

name: Radisson Plaza-Warwick Hotel Philadelphia
title: “Excellent rapport qualité/prix”
text: Un hôtel très agréable qui répond à tous les besoins en terme de confort : admirablement situé près de Rittenhouse square, et de multiples restaurants, il est néanmoins fort calme ; les chambres sont d'une taille suffisante , bien entretenues, le personnel aimable et courtois. Wifi et business center en libre accès.

name: Hilton Philadelphia Airport
title: “convenient location, suitable airport-style hotel”
text:
First off, it was a bonus that they had an airport hotel. When I got off the plane, I was able to call and be at the hotel within about 20 minutes at no cost - very handy!
The location is great if you want to stay by the airport. We found it easier to use it as a home base for a couple of days, and then easily make it back to the airport. 
Check-in was quick, and the hotel itself if as you would expect for an airport hotel. I had a bite to eat in the restaurant (sports bar), and it was reasonably priced with quick service. We ate the buffet breakfast twice, and it was average. The service was really friendly and fast, so that made up for the so-so food selections. Our room came with breakfast, or we would not have eaten there again.
The rooms were pretty standard - not the softest bed ever, and decent linens. My bathroom had a bit of wear on it, but you could tell it was clean. It is not what you would expect from a Hilton in a big city - but again, it is pretty standard for an airport hotel at a cheaper rate.

name: aloft Philadelphia Airport
title: “It's OK”
text: We arrived at the hotel and it was a pretty nice place. Very contemporary. Looked like everything was purchased at Ikea, so I was worried that things might break. There is no restaurant at the hotel, hmm. The pool was tiny and crowed. The beds were hard. Pillows were very small. Bar area in the morning was dirty. This place was far from everything. Never again.

name: Crowne Plaza Philadelphia West
title: “Reunion and Stay Over”
text: My class just had our 25th. Reunion at the Crown Plaze hotel on City Line ave. and everything was perfect. I wanted to write a small testimonial to indicate how the Hotel and staff were perfect. The food was great, bartenders fast and knowledgable, facilities were flawless and the location made it easy for people to find and access from all around the area. While most people weren't aware of the responsibility of the Hotel and Banquet group that was because they allowed us to focus on each other as they handled everything in the background perfectly. I'd strongly suggest anyone planning such an event to consider the Crown Plaza on City Line.

name: Holiday Inn Hotel Historic District Philadelphia
title: “Safe location, clean rooms, friendly staff!”
text: I had to be in Philly for an extensive period of time & stayed here at Holiday Inn. I always felt safe here. The staff was always accomodating, the rooms always clean, & the hotel is in a great location to walk to many different places. The food in the bar was always fresh and hot, though it did take a little longer to get the meal. Breakfast is either from the menu or the buffett. Try To stay in a higher room, 7-8 th floors-great views if you can face the bridge! Have a great stay! This is where I will stay when I return to Philadelphia!

name: Crowne Plaza Philadelphia West
title: “Stay here only as a last resort”
text:
I stayed here while on business in Philly as a last resort; all other hotels in the city were booked due to the Phillies playing in (and winning) the World Series. First off, I had reserved a non-smoking room, but upon arrival learned that there were only smoking rooms available. No other options were offered to me.
The hotel is approximately a 20 minute cab ride from Center City and UPenn, and about 30 minutes from PHL. There were some restaurants within walking distance (Houlihans, TGIF), but generally all the action is far away so except to drive/cab. One other note about the location, because you are so far from the city center expect to call ahead and wait for a cab.
The hotel is in the process of renovating the rooms, so if you must stay here you should request a renovated room. There is a significant difference in everything from the lighting to mildew growing on the walls of the unrenovated rooms.
I also tried the buffet breakfast, which was nothing special but passable for a hotel. The coffee was good.

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Downtown Hotel
title: “GOOD LOCATION IN DOWNTOWN PHILLY”
text: This was a last minute priceline reservation. Good - the location was excellent for walking around the historic area. The staff - though in other reviews were considered rude, was very accomodating. Deliah, who checked us in, was very friendly and helpful. The rooms were fine -clean, comfortable, quiet. I was rather surprised that there was no frig or microwave - this is the 5th weekend we have had to travel for sporting events and it is the first time there was no refigerator. Other than that, I paid $105 plus tax which was good, parking was $40 for the weekend,bu that is comparable to other ciites.

name: Embassy Suites Philadelphia - Airport
title: “P T.”
text: When I travel to Philadelphia this is my choice of hotels hands down every time. I could not ask for a more friendly and courteous staff. I was there two weeks ago and a member of the staff said to me welcome home. That made me feel really good. It goes to how comfortable I'am at the Embassy and how great the staff is there. Everything from access to everythng ,to a great breakfast and clean rooms Excellent!!!!

name: Philadelphia Airport Marriott
title: “Loved this hotel and staff”
text: This hotel was such a pleasant surprise. Rooms were very clean and well-appointed and quiet. The restaurant and bar were very efficient and the food was quite good. The hotel staff was excellent! I can't say enough about the staff. So polite, very efficient. You can tell they really try to please and succeed at doing so.

name: Embassy Suites Philadelphia - Airport
title: “My stay at Embassy Suites.”
text: This was my third time visiting Embassy. It's always great staying here. Everything we needed was here. The food was great and the staff was very helpful. Easy access to the parkways and easy travel to downtown Philadelphia attractions, plus great access to all sports arenas. The breakfast was fantastic. The lines was short and the cheft was really great.

name: Philadelphia Airport Marriott
title: “Un po' caro, ma senza dubbio una notte da signore senza uscire dall'aera aeroportuale”
text:
Ottimo hotel, pulito, completo, ben organizzato.
Ci si accede a piedi dal terminal B.
Alla reception, il personale é molto cortese ed efficiente, attento alle varie esigenze.
Le camere sono belle, in ottime condizione, spaziose, eleganti e funzionali. 
L'aria condizionata é regolabile, quindi se non amate l'A/C eccessiva, potrete regolarla fino a fare dell vosra camera iun ambiente vivibile e non un frigo. 
Altra pecca: le tende non arrivano a chiudere ed oscurare l'entrata della luce, chi si sveglia con la luce in camera sa di cosa parlo...
Al primo piano c'é ristorante e bar aperto fino all'una di sera.
Si da la carta di credito al momento del check-in ed il pagamente verrà effettuato da loro durante la notte, al risveglio la mattina vi troverete la fattura passata sotto la porta.
Il buffet della colazione non é male, abbastanza vario e con molta roba fresca, c'é anche la possibilità di avere omelettes fatte al momento.
Unica pecca: un po' caro: ho pagato di base US$189,00 + tasse ed internet (a pagamento, 12US$ per 24h di colegamento)

name: Comfort Inn Downtown/Historic Area
title: “Could not sleep”
text: Unless you are a very deep sleeper, do not stay at this hotel... that is, unless you don't intend to sleep anyway. My friend and I stayed at this hotel and we were in a room that faced the bridge (city side). Neither of us could sleep. We ended up getting out of bed finally around 3 or 4 am and requested to switch rooms. The clerk moved us to a room on the opposite side of the hotel that faced the river instead. It was quieter but still pretty noisy. We had to turn the fan on in order to muffle out the sound of the traffic and trains that traveled by all night.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Philadelphia Center City
title: “Return visit”
text:
Was here last year same time to watch the Phillies and sightsee. You can take the subway from the airport right to the hotel for 7 bucks. Good deal. Takes about 20 minutes. Hotel's in a great location. It's steps to Reading Market, Chinatown and a short and pleasant walk to Penn's Landing, Rittenhouse Square, Independence Hall, etc. 
Rooms are nice and clean like Garden Inns tend to be. Free internet in the business centre on the main floor. Restaurant/bar on the 10th floor is decent and has great city views. The pool and gym are well maintained and updated. Free cookies in the afternoon in the lobby and I helped myself to 4. 
There's a 24 hour store called "Wawa" across the street and some shady characters hanging around, but nobody bugs you. It's a big city and you run into this type of thing in every major city.
I'll stay when I return to Philly next year. 
P.S. Great city

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Absolutely Wonderful Midtown Hotel”
text: I decided to give this new hotel a try, and was so glad I did - I really loved everthing about it. The design is beautiful - elegant and clean-lined modern but very inviting. The bed and linens were extremely comfortable and the bathroom beautifully appointed. The entire staff seemed very friendly and helpful. I enjoyed the breakfast buffet in the cafe, and the coffee was delicious. The Midtown location was just perfect for me, since I was arriving by train, going to the theater, and doing a lot of other sightseeing. I felt very comfortable staying there as a woman traveling alone. The rates right now are very reasonable - they will probably go up, but I hope they will stay affordable. My only regret was that I didn't plan to stay longer - I will defintely stay there on my next trip to New York.

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Luxurious”
text:
I stayed there for one night, I shared a room with a friend, and it was luxurious, 2 big beds,and the bathroom is big with a shower cabinet and a bathtub. The room has a cool TV, with a nice window viewing tall building of Philly, good view to wake up to!
I advise you to eat at the french restaurant of the hotel, deliciousness.

name: Residence Inn Philadelphia Center City
title: “Great location, but it is still a Res Inn”
text:
This hotel has a great location and the facade of being a business class center city hotel...but that's the problem, it is still a limited service Residence Inn.
The first morning, the hairdryer wasn't working. After calling down for a hairdryer and then waiting an hour and still no delivery, the front desk never had one delivered and didn't seem to understand that wet hair and the need for a dryer in the morning before going out was an immediate response item.
Later in our stay our room had not been serviced. There are no housekeepers come late afternoon, so while towels could be suppled, the room was left unserviced.
Overall we had a great trip to Philadelphia, but the rate was the same as the full service Marriott next door. So the trade off was breakfast included and kitchen facilities versus full service hotel, for us the lack of service wasn't a good call, but the breakfast and kitchen were put to good use.
Also the location is perfect. We arrived by Amtrak and took the Market St. Frankfort subway to the hotel and back to the 30th St station, otherwise walked everywhere.

name: Sonesta Hotel Philadelphia
title: “Nice stay for 1 night”
text: We arrived in Philly around 2pm and checked into our room with no problems. We were on the 7th floor. Parking at the hotel was easy but expensive - $33/day! That was more than NYC or D.C. Staff was friendly. Hotel was in the middle of downtown and within walking distance to everything except Pat & Geno's to get a cheesesteak. We took a cab. By the way, we thought Pat's was better. Ate and drank at the hotel bar. Very nice. Bartender was very nice. The waitress was not very good. When you empty your beer and still have to wait 15 minutes to get another something is wrong. Felt very safe during daytime. However, I would not stray to far from the hotel at night. Went to NYC, Philly & D.C. this trip. Out of them all I'd say Philly was the most dirty and unsafe place we went. I'd stay at this hotel again. No problems.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Independence Park Hotel
title: “Fabulous historic updated hotel in walking distance of historic sites”
text: The staff was friendly and helpful. They provided us with great recommendations to nearby restsurants and helped with the use if public transportation. We were able to walk to historic sites. Room was updated, nicely historically period decorated, and good sized

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Independence Park Hotel
title: “Fantastic location to Independence Hall”
text: What a great find & wonderful staff! Everyone was so friendly & the location couldn't be beat. Short walk to Independence Hall & Constitution Center; great local restaurants steps from the hotel. Includes breakfast buffet. Overall: big thumbs up!

name: Embassy Suites Philadelphia - Center City
title: “alot of extras but one minus”
text:
Ok, I got this hotel room through priceline, name your own price. for what I paid it was real good, it came with a complimentary breakfast that was served buffet style at the adjoining tgif restaurant. it was good breakfast food and it was free. the room I stayed in was huge, the living room area was humungous, we hardly used it, the bathroom were very clean which is important to me, that night they had an open bar down at the lobby, which of course was way cool, drank about three or four greyhounds. the only two minuses are.
1. elevators are slow, small, and usually packed, we were on the seventh floor and used the stairs a few times because of the aforementioned reasons.
2. to valet park your car in their garage for the night was 40 dollars! they do wash the car, but 40 dollars to park your car over night, seems way too much for a hotel guest. we were not expecting that in our budget, but we also didn't expect the free breakfast or the free drinks in the evening, so it evened out.

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Good for a night”
text: Good location, friendly staff, chic rooms. Great for a date night, a getaway, or a place to stay for out of town guests. Its a good hotel, not cheap but worth it for a place you don't have to worry about the details, they are handled.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Independence Park Hotel
title: “Nice hotel”
text: We came for memorial day weekend, the hotel is very nice, friendly front desk, good location, The room is small but it was clean. We really enjoyed our staying !

name: Embassy Suites Philadelphia - Airport
title: “Terribly Expensive and Terrible Service”
text:
We picked this hotel because of the airport shuttle. We arrived at 9pm and needed food service. There was no room service and the restaurant was closed early because "it is a holiday" Presidents' Day. Really? We were told to order out! No information in the room about ANYTHING. Not even a phone book. We were told to come to the desk for take out menus. Really? 
We left at 5am so we couldn't take advantage of the "Free" breakfast. There was Continental breakfast- coffee and 1 donut! Really? No discount for no food (room service still closed due to Presidents' Day)
Shuttle to airport ok. Shuttle home- non existant. We waited 11/2 hours at the airport. Called 4x and told to hire a cab. No cabs were found even after a call. Finally the shulttle showed and we were told they did pass by 2x but it was too full to pick us up. Really? no one in the 2 other groups saw the shuttle either. Both of the other groups had to wait an hour, too. 
Terrible, terrible 
Cost $250.00- but they did let us park there free for the 4 days we were away. We will pay someone else next time. Never again!
Oh, did I mention the food on the elevator floor? Terrible

name: Club Quarters
title: “Great location, small but comfortable and practical rooms.”
text: I had the smallest room between the 4 of us that went to Philadelphia, but it was clean, it was comfortable, and there weren't many noises from the inside. That being said, our first night in town was a Saturday night, and if you've got a room that is on the side of the hallway that is away from the elevators it is located right over a cab stand. We didn't get much sleep that night, but it was much better on Sunday night. We didn't eat dinner at the restaurant, Davios, however the breakfast was absolutely terrific and more than reasonably priced. Overall I will look for Club Quarters locations when I travel again, and when we go back to Philadelphia next year will make sure to eat breakfast everyday at Davios. Oh, as a side note, you've got to park at the Liberty Mall across the street, as there is no "hotel" parking.

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Downtown Hotel
title: “Pretty good”
text: When we walked on to our floor and saw breakfast plates sitting out in front of a few doors at 4pm I was skeptical. However our room itself was quite clean and the staff was very nice. The walk to the Philly Convention Center was very doable if you are in good health. I was bummed they didn't have continental breakfast but they do have Starbucks coffee in the rooms and a Starbucks in the lobby.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Philadelphia Center City
title: “Nice hotel, weird location.”
text:
An unusual location above a parking garage, right on the edge of China Town. Also one block from a main shopping area, and six blocks from the Liberty Bell.
This hotel was great, especially at this price over a holiday weekend. Clean, friendly and quite a surprise. The restaurant and bar on the 10th floor was not very expensive.
Our room was kept very clean by Sara and the desk personnel were very nice.
We were next door to Reading Terminal Market (just about anything you might need), around the corner from Hard Rock Cafe. We could and did walk many places. Would suggest the double-decker bus ride to see a lot in a little time.

name: The Windsor Suites
title: “Excellent stay at Windsor Suites”
text: We stayed at the Windsor Suites for 3 days in October and really enjoyed our stay. The room was large and everything was working (including the hot water as some people have had problems with according to other posts) even though the room was a bit dated. From the location of the hotel we were able to walk to all the places we wanted to visit. If we come back to Philadelphia we will stay here again.

name: Philadelphia Marriott Downtown
title: “Great location/ noisy inside”
text: Nice hotel, fairly updated rooms but extremely noisy- could hear people talking in the halls and was woken up by housekeeping .The bed was uncomfortable. Lobby was crowded and chaoctic but front desk staff was nice and helpful. Location was great. In walking distance to liberty bell, art museum, etc. I would stay here again if the rate was right.

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Pretty Perfect”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights while on business. The hotel is in the center of everything, walking distance to the office, shops, restuarants, Rittenhause park. Fabulous room, nice living space, big bathroom, neat dressing area which was a nice surprise. Bed was amazing, if you like LOTS of cushion. If you prefer a harder matress/bed this might not be the place for you. I felt like I was sleeping on a cloud. A little wear and tear on the furniture but didnt make much of a difference. 
Hotel staff was very accomodating and friendly. Utilized the concierge who was efficient, friendly and very helpful. 
I have never stayed at a Sofitel before and I will now look for them where ever I travel.
Great job!

name: Club Quarters
title: “Very Nice Hotel!”
text:
I had read reviews first, so I knew the rooms would be small.
I told my travelling companion this, and when we first arrived he replied - the room isn't small!
By US standards it is. But I've stayed in many small European hotels, and I'd say this room was as large or LARGER than most small European hotels.
Everything was very nice and in excellent condition. In fact, everything looked brand new!
I've had back problems at home - but sleeping in my twin bed - I had NO back problems the entire day.
Everything was perfect, including the staff, who were very friendly.
Room was quiet. Location was excellent - right in City Center, and only 2 blocks from the Suburban train station.
But as others wrote - no fridge, and no shelf in shower to hold washcloth, soap, shampoo etc. That they should add - but certainly was only a minor inconvenience.
Would definitely stay there again!

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Downtown Hotel
title: “mixed feelings”
text:
This hotel was not that wonderful. Check in service was great. The guy that checked us in was really nice and speedy. Room was average. The cordless phone did not work. When I used the speaker phone to call for room service, the woman on the other end seemed absolutely miserable and I felt like I was really bothering her. 
The bartender downstairs at the bar was great as well as the concierge. Breakfast buffet was terrrible! Don't waste your money. It would be better to just walk to another little restaurant in town. Or perhaps ordering off the actual menu would have been better. But the buffet food was really nasty. In the fruit section of the buffet, there was actually a plate of pineapple with hair on it for everyone to see. The scrambled eggs was more like egg soup.. the potato's were the pre-packaged frozen diced ones and they were not warm or cooked well. Everything else just seemed like food that has been reheated and reheated a million times. Nothing fresh- even the coffee canister that they put on our table was dirty. Service was rather awful as well. A man seated close to us complained to the manager, she basically used the excuse that it's due to high volume --- We didn't really get upset about anything, not big complainers (though i may sound like it now!) - just took it for what it was worth, ate and left. 
Additionally, we parked our car in the garage. And it costs $20 /night. I wish this was noted on their website when booking. On the website it says Valet and Self Service parking.
