I assumed the self service parking would be free. So that was just an additional cost I was not prepared for. Also.. for a hotel that has about 7 elevators. We took the elevator down to leave and it basically stopped on every floor and we ended up being jam packed in like sardines. Going down from floor 24 to 1 took forevverrrr. Didn't really bother me as much as it did others, but found it a little funny. Overall, there was nothing about this hotel that blew me away. The location was great but I will definitely try a different hotel within the same vicinity before returning. If you really just need a room to sleep in and don't want to use the hotel for much of anything else, then you would probably be satisfied. Hope this is helpful!

name: Holiday Inn Hotel Historic District Philadelphia
title: “Nice hotel”
text: I spent one night at this hotel, although I would have liked more. It’s perfectly situated for the Historic District. Good sized room, nice bar, lounge and pool. My room could have been cleaned a bit better and when I complained they sorted out the problem without a fuss. Staff were very helpful. I would stay here again.

name: Sonesta Hotel Philadelphia
title: “A great hotel,very friendly staff,central and well kept rooms.”
text: The staff were very friendly as were all the people in Philadelphia. Our room was very comfortable and clean, we also had a breakfast included as well as a reception in the evening with cheese and wine. If you do o to Philly visit the "Ducks Tour" and the Old Town, also the King of Prussia shopping mall stopping of at half time to have a bite to eat in the "Cheesecake Company", absolute heaven.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Independence Park Hotel
title: “Lovely Old Hotel”
text:
We usually stop in Philly a couple of times a year and we always choose this hotel.It's a lovely old building with a nice historic decor.The rooms are nice and comfortable and there is an adequate breakfast in the morning.The location is superb,right in the heart of historic downtown and a bonus is that it is close to a SEPTA subway station on the Market-Frankfort line,which can take you via 30th St Station to the airport for the fraction of the price of a taxi.
I'd recommend this hotel to anyone.

name: The Windsor Suites
title: “Clean, quiet, and friendly!”
text: This hotel was wonderful-- for only $99 a night. Rooms were incredibly spacious (nice kitchenette, dishwasher, table, desk, easychair, 2 closets, 2 beds) and very clean. The desk staff was very friendly and helpful. The Irish Pub connected to the lobby is a lively spot on weekend evenings, and provides a convenient place to grab delicious breakfast as well. Centrally located just a block from the famous "LOVE" and city hall, this is where I will be staying in Philly for the forseeable future.

name: Sonesta Hotel Philadelphia
title: “Very Average”
text: Stayed at this hotel this past weekend using the GoPhila Promotion.The hotel needs a renovation ASAP. Check in went smoothly and front desk personnel were fairly nice. Upon entering the room we were shocked at the small size of the double beds. All of us woke up the next morning with some very severe back pain. The beds had no bounce to them and were as hard as cardboard. Just plain awful and I will be following up with the management there as I have stayed at other Crowne Plaza's and never experienced this before. The other major problem was the bathroom. The sink was outside of the bathroom which was annoying and worst, the bathroom itself was so small that anyone who may have been 6 feet or so would not have been able to use it. This needs to be addressed and it is NOT a comfortable shower or bathroom experience due to the lack of space. The carpet was worn and after maid service on the first day, I came back and my blanket has cigarette burns on it. Another turn off. No Showtime or HBO, just STARZ.The parking here is $28 (free with the GoPhila promotion) so keep that in mind, but you will pay at most downtown Philly hotels. Overall, this place seemed like a Howard JOhnson or Holiday Inn and I would not recommend.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Philadelphia Center City
title: “A real lack of communication and secuity”
text:
I stayed at this property in July and had an unsettling set of events happen on the afternoon on my departure. 
Let me say, there was NO criminal activity involved. However, what did occur showed a complete lack of coordination between hotel departments and a laissez-faire attitude toward guest secuity and comfort and this hotel.
At appx. 2:00 PM (I had pre-arranged and paid for a late check out since I had a late flight) my room phone rang. The person identified themselves being from "engineering" and "even though I had a 'DND' on my door" they needed to come in to work on the alarm speaker in my room. I told them it wasn't a good time because I was napping, but that I 'd be checking out a little later. The very aggressive person argued with me, insisting they needed to come into the room. After saying no 3 times, I finally had to hang up.
About 45 mins later, it started with another phone call, which I ignored. 2 mins later, a knock on my door. It got worse. Over the course of the next 10 mins, I had (between knocks and rings) about 10 attempts to get in my room. Having already stated it wasn't a good time, I ignored them all. Finally, I called the front desk and explained what was going on. I asked if there was an emergency or something urgent why they would need to get into my room. The front desk clerk stated "I don't know anything about engineering". 
Impossible to nap, I decided to get into the shower and get ready for my pick-up. After about 10 mins, I heard what sounded like someone trying to get into my room door. After quickly getting out of the shower, I discovered my room door open, with someone trying to flip open the security bar to gain entry. I immediately slammed the door shut.
I called the front desk and asked to speak to a manager immediately, but they were "in a meeting". The assistance of a security guard was not offered. I was anxious at this point to get out of my room, which I did.
On my way out, I went by the front desk and asked to speak to a manager again. After waiting 15 mins, the Assistant GM appeared. He was courteous and listened to my situation, but could not offer any explanation for what happened. 
At this point, I headed to the airport to catch my flight.
I immediately followed up with an message on the hilton.com website which was unanswered and unacknowledged.
Through an internal investigation department where I work, they were able to get some answers. They found out there was a contractor working in the hotel doing "fire equipment testing," which included compoents in guest rooms. That day, my room was the last room on which they were working and the contractor was over-zealous and was going in no matter what..
He had a master key. It looks like some of the basic components of hospitality, and guest safety, security, and respect had not been imparted on these workers.
I guess what concerned me more is that others in the hotel, including the front desk the others members of management didn't even seem to to know they were there working in the hotel that day.
When I still had not heard back from Hilton after a couple of weeks, I sent them another email, asking why I had not heard from them. I finally got a short email back. They explained to me that the matter was closed. The property had explained to them that the 90-second conversation we had the lobby had finalized the matter. No formal aplogy. No formal explanation. It's a real "oh-well" kind of atmosphere. Other chains would have handled this much more professionally and more rapidly.
I don't upset or rattle easily. I think many other guests would have been MUCH for upset than me by all this!!!!
This hotel is the the center of the city with a lot of activity swirling around. Guest secuity and safety should be first and foremost!

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Great hotel”
text: Just stayed here on a friday night,shopped around for best price in city & sofitel offered best deal, walked to merrian theatre, rooms here are excellent!! Location great! Lobby bar fantastic,service & cleanliness couldn,t have been better. They held our bags all day saturday while we toured historic phila, i would definitely recommend this property & great location for theatre or touring phila,best way around town is to walk. Also had great breakfast one block away at little pete,s diner. Zagat rated diner open 24 hrs.

name: Hyatt Regency Philadelphia at Penn's Landing
title: “thin walls but LOVED IT!!!!!”
text: My family and i were in town over the weekend for a wedding and we were so impressed with not only the hotel, but all of the staff from the valet to the hotel management. My husband worked for the Marriott for many years and we had never experienced this kind of attentiveness at a hotel. On the morning of check out at breakfast i mentioned laughingly to the wait staff that i was tired because of a party that had happened the night before somewhere on the same floor that we were staying (it finally finished at 3am). The next thing I knew the restaurant manager came over and apologized for my lack of sleep and offered me and my family a free breakfast. The front desk always had a smile and were ready to answer any questions we had. Then upon leaving the valet asked if we needed directions and if there was anything else we would need as he helped us put everything into the car. Even though the rooms were small and the walls were a little thin the staff was so nice that if we ever found ourselves back in Philly we would visit again. One experience after another they continued to impress. Thanks for helping to make our weekend so nice.

name: Hyatt Regency Philadelphia at Penn's Landing
title: “Stuck with pull out couch!!”
text:
I would not recommend this hotel at all. My flight was delayed, so after a sitting in the airport for an extra couple hours, my reward was that they were out of rooms, so I was offered a living room with a pull out couch. I travel to the area frequently, and thought I would try something different by staying here. Will not be coming back again, nor will I recommend to co-workers.
As others have mentioned, parking is expensive, so consider this when comparing hotels in the area

name: Philadelphia Marriott Downtown
title: “Great Hotel”
text: My wife and I just enjoyed a great stay last Saturday. I must tell you that this hotel could teach a class in customer service. The bell staff and parking attendants are very hard working and polite. This is by far the cleanest hotels that we have ever stayed in. Thank you for a great stay and we will be back the next time we are in Philadelphia.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Independence Park Hotel
title: “One of the Best Best Westerns we have ever visited.”
text: The staff was excellent, service was perfect, room was immaculate, and the location was great!

name: Residence Inn Philadelphia Center City
title: “OK. A few hiccups, but good value in a great location”
text: Stayed here with my family -- they were touring while I was in town on business. The location was perfect for both activities (on Penn Square, near Reading Terminal). Rooms were spacious and very well-priced for the location. The housekeeping was a bit suspect -- there was a layer of dust on top of each television. Also, if you valet park your car, expect an unreasonably long wait for your car. (We waited over an hour on a Friday afternoon.)

name: Hyatt Regency Philadelphia at Penn's Landing
title: “Very nice hotel”
text: We only stayed one night. It was very nice. Nothing exceptional. The employees were all very courteous and efficient. My only complaint is that there is no privacy in the bathroom. There were French doors that did not lock or even close flush against each other. Other than that, the room was comfortable and nicely decorated and very clean.

name: Holiday Inn Hotel Historic District Philadelphia
title: “Great Location and good hotel”
text: Great location in Historic District (you don't need car, subway etc.). Clean room, good service and stuff, worth the price. The only thing my wife and I were disappointed was that we had a reservation for a crib and they didn't have any available for us throughout our stay.

name: Embassy Suites Philadelphia - Center City
title: “Great location with OK rooms”
text:
Overall, we were pleased with this hotel. Location was great, service was pretty good, and the staff were friendly. 
The hotel structure is a bit dated but the rooms have been upgraded. Only the bathroom and the bedroom was quite small and crowded. 
Breakfast was OK but we've had better.
Bottomline: we would stay here again when we travel to Philadelphia.

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Not quite luxury”
text:
I'd really like to give the hotel a better rating because the location is nice, the rooms are well appointed, and the beds are comfortable. There are touches of the purported luxury...friendly employees calling "bonjour" and fluffy robes in the closet. But the lackadaisical maid service prevents me from giving the hotel 5 stars.
I stayed in the hotel for 5 nights and the bedding was never changed. Some nights the water from the ice bucket was not emptied and the toiletries were only replenished once. The bathmat was picked up off the floor and rehung and the tub was never cleaned. Furthermore, the room was never cleaned until late afternoon. It never seemed like the job was thorough.
On the other hand, the turndown service with a bottle of water was nice. The hotel was basically quiet. I'm not sure if I"d stay here again.

name: Omni Hotel at Independence Park
title: “Usual Great Stay . . .”
text: I stay at the Omni when I am in the city playing tourista. I love Philly (I grew up in a burb a LONG time ago), so love returning and enjoying the city. Omni was the usual luxurious place to stay - good conceirge who recommended dining places. Comfortable room - excellent location. Parking is expensive, but only when you are not used to these prices. Visited several historical sites all within walking distance. Even though it rained one day, we got wet when we weren't darting in to a building. Overall 5 stars every time at the Omni -

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Excellent hotel in a convenient location”
text:
I stayed with my wife at the Sofitel for 2 nights and was very pleased with the accommodations. 
Everything in the hotel was very clean and the staff was very helpful and courteous. The hotel has a restaurant/bar in it which is convenient. There are many other restaurants and bars in the area and you aren't really too far from anything. If in Philly doing some site seeing, I recommend the hop on hop off bus as it's inexpensive and lets you travel the entire city.Enjoy!

name: Holiday Inn Hotel Historic District Philadelphia
title: “recommended”
text:
We live only 45 minutes away. We got the hotel through priceline at a rate of 60.00. Add 20 parking and 8 tax, and that is the total. Initially through priceline, I received a king bed smoking room and when I called the hotel to get double beds the only thing that was left was a double bed smoking room. I had them switch me to the front desk and when I asked for an ionizer in the room to remove the smoke odors, the front desk staff just switched me to an non smoking room two beds. Just doesnt get any better for that price.Room is clean and nice in an excellent location very close to Independence Hall . Renovations still going on in lobby, but not a problem. Everything appears to be well cared for.Wireless internet is free
Add to that the 10.00 tickets that I was able to secure for Art Garfunkle at the Kimmel center during the Community Rush hours and I am in bargain heaven.

name: Morris House Hotel
title: “My safe heaven”
text: I stayed at this hotel during the storm for 2days I had originally only planned to stay 1 night but because of the storm I stayed 2 night in one of the nice suites they have. I felt very comfortable there it reminds me of a condo it feels like an apartment but has all the amenities of a hotel. I could get room service. Through the whole thing the lights never went out and the advice if the hotel remained 24 hours. The staff made me feel like I had nothing to worry about the hotel ran like nothing was happening I could still get continental breakfast and afternoon tea and cookies and I loved the hot cider.

name: The Windsor Suites
title: “Are you serious?”
text:
The place seemed just fine. It was a bit of a walk from some of the places we went to in the City, but after the first night walking back to the hotel, we realized the streets were friendlier from a cab. 
What threw me though at this place was that at no time when that dreamy, scruffy looking concierge was checking my party in did he suggest we ASK for housekeeping services. Yes folks, I'm serious, it's not an automatic given at this place. I was speechless when at 3 PM I returned to my room to find the bed and the bathroom in the same state of disrepair that I left it in that morning when I left at 8 AM. Apparently, according to the concierge on duty at the time I called down, I hadn't requested housekeeping. There was no extra charge apparently for it and of course my room wasn't any cheaper for not having it... but since I hadn't requested it at the time of my check-in the day before, I hadn't gotten it. 
To be fair though, the fella did offer to send someone up to take care of it then, but I figured at that point since I was leaving in the morning, I'd save the $5 bucks I would have tipped the cleaning lady and slept in my unmade bed that night.

name: AKA Rittenhouse Square
title: “BEST LOCATION EVER, LOVED the Hotel”
text:
We stayed here for 8 nights right after Christmas. We had taken the red-eye from San Diego and arrived at the hotel at 7:00am. The warm lobby smelled WONDERFUL and we were welcomed as weary travellers. The two bedroom suite was great although I had thought it came with a fireplace. Apparently none of the two bedroom suites have fireplaces. Oh well, no big deal. Our room was fantastic; extra large, comfy, & high end. 
I can't say enough about the location. This hotel is in the IDEAL spot; much better than where the Four Seasons, Marriott, Wyndam, or other high price hotels are. There is a great Italian gourmet market within a short walk, coffee houses, high end resturants and all my favorite shops (Anthropoligie, Athleta, Coach, Lagos, Ann Taylor, H&M, etc etc). 
Everything was fantastic EXCEPT the housekeeping. The place is spotless but they only have housekeeping every 5 days. They come to pick up trash from the room daily (except Sunday) but the kitchen got messy quick and towels became a problem. For $25 a day they will clean your room more, but I think it should be done at no charge every other day.....I'm just sayin.
We will stay here again. It was my husband and I, our two kids and my sister-in-law and there was plenty of room. The sheets were high quality and the water pressure great. High ratings for this hotel.

name: The Independent
title: “Wonderful Stay”
text: We stayed for 2 nights during a recent visit to Philadelphia. The location is excellent and within walking distance of the historic sites. The room was very nice - clean and comfortable. The included breakfast is nothing to write home about, but everything else about the hotel is first class. The staff is very friendly and helpful and made our stay quite pleasant. Our room was on the third floor and some street noise was evident but not bad.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Independence Park Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text: Great location, across the street from the old Customs House. The staff must have read the previous reviews about unfriendliness, as they were very pleasant. We were there during the Wednesday Wine and Cheese Manager's Reception, and found him to be very friendly and personable, making a point to visit with everyone. He was most helpful with touring suggestions. Rooms vary a lot, ours was L-shaped, but spacious enough. Breakfast Room, under a skylight covered roof in the lowest level was very pleasant.

name: Holiday Inn Hotel Historic District Philadelphia
title: “Buon rapporto qualità/prezzo”
text:
Sono stato un paio di settimane fa per tre notti ospite in quest'hotel.
La posizione è ottimale per visitare la Old City e il complesso storico dell'Indipendence Visitor Center (Indipendence Hall e Liberty Bell), però è un pò distante centro attuale della città, in quanto di sera questo quartiere è un pò deserto (come un pò tutta la città d'altronde).
La fermata della metropolitana è comunque molto vicina quindi ci si può spostare facilmente.
La pulizia è nel complesso nella norma, viene fornito il wifi gratuito in stanza e la stanza che mi hanno assegnato era molto spaziosa.
Gli unici due nei
 - la non eccellente cortesia alla reception alla quale hanno risposto un pò infastiditi alle uniche due richieste di informazioni che ho fatto, ma questo l'ho avvertito un pò in tutta la città a dispetto del nome!
- vicino l'hotel è presente una caserma dei vigili del fuoco e un paio di volte mi sono svegliato quando sono partiti a sirene spiegate.

name: Hilton Inn at Penn
title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
This was our first stay at the Inn at Penn. We had a great stay. The hotel offers spacious, well-appointed rooms and top-notch technology for guest services. Rooms and public areas are clean and well-maintained. Everyone from the staff that we encountered was very friendly and professional. We traveled with our two kids - 2 and 5, and the restaurant staff did an excellent job accommodating our needs at breakfast and lunch. 
We will stay there again during our next visit to Philly.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Philadelphia
title: “Nice hotel, location and smooth ripoff”
text: Right on Logan square, with a beautiful view if you can get those rooms. 10-15 minutes walk to shopping and theater district. The usual Four Seasons polish though nothing particularly special at his location. Now, $49 daily parking fee? That's out there. It's so high it should be advertised when you reserve really. A smooth scam if you ask me.

name: Morris House Hotel
title: “A gem in Society Hill”
text: We just spent Valentine's weekend in the Morris Hotel and it was special. The luxury room was perfect for us- flat screen TV, WIFI, windows overlooking the gardens, free chocolates and bottles of spring water, robes in the bathoom, very nice breakfast and, above all, an excellent staff. The sitting rooms with the blazing fireplaces invite warmth and relaxation. A special dinner menu was included that topped off the weekend. Everything is walkable to all the historic sites and center city shopping.

name: The Independent
title: “Nice room but...”
text:
The good...the staff was great, very good restaurant recommendations! The room was nice, loved the hardwood floors, comfy beds, big bathroom, nice shower. Good breakfast delivered to your room, nice wine/cheese reception. Great location for historical sites, as well as for shopping, and Reading Market.
The bad...during the night there were loud banging noises which woke us up. We could not figure out what it was, slamming doors, elevator, toilets flushing? Maybe it was just our room (309)?

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Fint hotell nära Times Square”
text: Hotellet levde verkligen upp till våra förväntningar. Ett rent och fräscht hotell med utmärkt läge nära Times Square. Ett stort plus var även att flygbussen från Newark stannade endast ett par 100m från hotellet. Hotellet har gångavstånd till Central Park, Empire State Building, Rockefeller Center och andra sevärdigheter. Personalen var mycket trevliga och hjälpsamma. Skulle vi åka till New York igen skulle Distrikt Hotel definitivt vara ett alternativ för oss.

name: The Windsor Suites
title: “Grand studio près des musées à Philadelphie”
text: L'hôtel est très bien situé, il est possible de se rendre dans les musées ou en ville à pied. Une petite kitchenette et un coin repas permet de manger dans la chambre pour changer du restaurant. Mais nous avons été obligé de prendre 2 studios pour 4.

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “Klein aber fein”
text:
Ganz in der Nähe vom Time Square und nur ein paar Meter bis zur Subway. 
Das Zimmer war zwar klein, aber super sauber und gepflegtes Bad mit nicht zu kleiner Dusche. Wir hatten täglich frische Handtücher, auch, wenn wir sie nicht auf den Boden gelegt hatten.
Im 30. Stock hatten wir einen super Blick auf den Hudson River (besonders mit aufgehender und untergehender Sonne sehr schön) und konnten auch das Empire State Building sehen.
Alles Personal war sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit. An der Rezeption hat man bereitwillig Tipps gegeben, Tickets bestellt und auch sonst geduldig zugehört, wenn wir mal wieder nicht die richtigen Vokabeln gefunden hatten. ;)
Alles in allem wäre das Hotel jederzeit wieder meine Erste Wahl, da das Preis - Leistungs - Verhältnis mehr als stimmt!

name: Rittenhouse 1715, A Boutique Hotel
title: “A Charming Boutique Hotel”
text:
Located centrally in Philadelphia, this small and utterly charming hotel is a real find. Upon arrival in Philly, I dropped my bag off at the hotel and was assured that I'd find it in my room when I came back from work. And indeed, it was in my room as promised. The lobby is beautifully but not ostentatiously furnished and is welcoming, as is the staff.I felt like I was visiting a friend's house because of all the personal touches. On couple of occasions I had to ask for help and received it promptly. My room was clean, comfortable and attractive.
There is a complimentary breakfast in the morning, in an equally appealing setting. Individual tables were set with cloth napkins and mix and match porcelain china, again a personal touch.
The complimentary breakfast (self-service) is continental style, but one can order additional items such as eggs. 
All in all this was a great experience.

name: Alexander Inn
title: “Boutique Hotel for Two”
text: Philadelphia is a walker's city and this spot 's proximity to all things downtown is pretty good! It has the ambiance of an old hotel but with all the modern conveniences. If you are looking for flashy, homogenized lodging, don't come to this Inn. If you like interesting, comfortable and friendly, try this Inn. If you want to spend the day in your room, you will be cramped. If you are on a budget, you will love this place. Also , feels safe and sound and the windows open!.

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Downtown Hotel
title: “Ok hotel that needs a facelift!”
text: Sheraton is located in a decent location in Center City -- it's a few blocks further north than one would ideally be situated, but still an easy walk to transportation, restaurants, etc. The hotel itself is fine, but really needs some upgrades. Our room had no light switches -- you could only turn on the lamps from the lamp itself, which was a little annoying. The water pressure was weak and lighting in the bathroom was odd thanks to the flourescent lights. The furniture needs to be replaced -- what was in our room was dated and damaged (e.g., dents in the coffee table). I'd stay here again if the price was right (as it was when we were in town during Penn reunion/graduation weekend), but if I had a choice, I'd go with another property -- like the Westin, which is better located and nicer inside.

name: Rittenhouse 1715, A Boutique Hotel
title: “Great comfort at an affordable price”
text: Conveniently located to Rittenhouse Square, this boutique hotel has comforatble rooms, high end linens, is reasonably priced and has a great staff that is friendly and helpful. The cafe for breakfast is a bonus nd a must.

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Downtown Hotel
title: “I'd stay there again.”
text: If you're like me, your more interested in the city your visiting and and less affected by the amenities of your hotel. Hotel's location was excellent, situated close by to some major museums, 10 min walk to whole foods, 10 min walk to the subway, 15 min walk to reading market. Overall safe, yeah you walk through downtown and most big city american downtowns will have bums or the like hanging around. Hell, my 7 yr old and I went just about everywhere by foot, sub and bus. We prefer to take mass transit when available. Hotel was older, been kept up well. Very happy with the concierge, I left my jacket at home and they gave me one from the lost and found that had been there forever. Always greeted with a smile and a hello. Weightroom was dated, cardio is ok, pool is ok. Paid about $70/night through priceline. Got more than I paid for.

name: Distrikt Hotel
title: “FANTASTICO”
text: bellissimo hotel a pochi passi da times square, dintorni dell'albergo tranquilli e sicuri. camere moderne e spaziose. personale accogliente. splendida vista sui grattacieli dalla nostra stanza.

name: Hotel Monaco Philadelphia
title: “Good, but could be a lot better.”
text:
Overall, this is a very nice hotel. Staff was nice, Valet was decent (brought the wrong car out the first time we called for it), and the food was good at Red Owl and room service.
Two complaints though....
1: King size beds...not very comfortable. I thought for the price of the rooms, the beds would be very nice. But was very dissapointed in them. Tossed and turned the first night and the second night woke up with a sore back. That might just be me though...
2: I booked a 'Parkview King' room expecting a "overlook Independence Historic National Park" as advertised. Instead I got a view of the building next door. If you looked out the window and turned your head completely 90 degrees to the left you could see this "overlook Independence Historic National Park," as promised. Very Very dissapointed. Felt a little ripped off, should of booked the King Deluxe room and saved money, the view would of been the same. (We were in Room 1019, by the way)
Everything else was pretty good, great location. Everything is within walking distance. Overall, I'd say its a good hotel, but just came up well short of what I was expecting when I booked it/what I paid for it.

name: Chelsea Pines Inn
title: “Excellent hotel in a good location”
text: The more time I spent here, the more I noticed the attention to detail in this excellent hotel. We had a nice quiet room with a wonderful shower. The breakfast was fine and the staff polite and welcoming.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Philadelphia
title: “Fabulous, chld friendly hotel”
text: Lovely facilities, great rooms. My grandsons were greeted with their choice of toys from a cart; milk and cookies came at bedtime. Wonderful, attentive service. Fine pool and hottub tho the pool could have been a degree or two warmer. Room service was prompt and elegant--we had pizza and incredible shrimp cocktail.

name: The Rittenhouse Hotel
title: “It's just a great hotel”
text: From the minute the front door is opened for you to the valet opening your car door as you leave you are treated to one of the finest hotels anywhere. Great, large rooms, a great restaurant, Lacroix, superb service at every turn and an incredibly friendly staff. The Rittenhouse is rated as one of the top hotels in the world and it is easy to see why.

name: Alexander Inn
title: “A true bargain in Philly!”
text: This locally-owned boutique hotel is perfectly located in Central City. The rooms are small but comfortable, the staff friendly and there when you need them. Breakfast is excellent; it puts many chains to shame. Coffeemakers in the rooms would be nice but not a major factor. Parking is at a lot three blocks,away and at a reduced rate. Highly recommended. I will stay there again.

name: Hotel Elysee
title: “Elysée Lived Up to the Top Ranking”
text:
Nearly everything about the Hotel Elysée surpassed even the high expectations we had from reading past reviews. 
The room was large; the bed, super-comfortable and the staff was genuinely available, helpful and pleasant. The breakfast included fresh high-quality choices, and the happy hour left us feeling that we'd joined a lively club with members we enjoyed meeting.
What makes the Elysee even more appealing is that the restoration has been done in a way that presents the hotel and its rooms and spaces as 100% up-to-date, but nevertheless mimicking what a luxury hotel in New York (or actually, Paris), must have been like in the '20s or '30s. The furnishings, bathroom fixtures and decoration all evoke the de luxe place we might have imagined staying if we ever had enough money or leisure to have taken The Grand Tour 80 years ago.
The prices vary dramatically based on demand, but the hotel's own website is transparent and easy to navigate and compare. We got a summer bargain, which made the weekend in New York all the more fun.

name: Hyatt Regency Philadelphia at Penn's Landing
title: “It was great”
text: we had great service, the room service was fast and good....the front dest staff always ready to help you...the maid service was good... i do not understand why people do not relax and have more fun...if i needed something i called down to the desk...simple as that....you are right in front of a ship and submarine...be sure and go see the submarine..and dont forget to see the Mutter Museaum.....men turn green for some reason but worth the vist...

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Decent place that is overpriced!”
text: In terms of cleanliness and pleasant staff ...The hotel is average. When you consider the price, the extra charges ($45,night for parking, $10 for internet, $2 per morning croissant, $5 for a bottle of water) oh my goodness that is when the location, access to stores, nice staff and all really don't make the hotel a value.

name: Library Hotel
title: “4 nights of bliss at the Library!”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Library for 4 nights from 30th August 2012 to the 3rd September. My wife repeatedly described the hotel as "perfect". The staff couldn't have been nicer or more helpful. The room was lovely, comfortable and quiet. We have been staying in hotels across the world for decades and this has to be up there with the best. Great location too. We will be back.

name: Library Hotel
title: “Summer in the Library”
text: Staying at the Library was truly a magnificent experience. The staff was friendly, helpful and not snooty at all. The hotel itself is in a great location, walking distance from Bryant Park, Time Square, and the legendary Fifth Avenue. We enjoyed a wonderful view of the NY public library and the surrounding area from our many windows. The room was impeccably clean and comfortable. The Junior suite was large and spacious with high ceilngs...The wine and cheese from 5pm-8pm was awesome. They had a great variety of snacks, wine, and champagne in a tranquil setting. The roof top bar was a nice place to relax after a long day of sightseeing. Our flight did not leave until late in the day, so the hotel stored our luggage without any problems. There is always someone on hand to hail you a cab and help with your luggage. Whenever I travel to NYC this is where I will stay. The free book on checkout was a nice touch and will be an great momento. Thank you for an outstanding experience!

name: Chelsea Pines Inn
title: “Fantastic gem of a place”
text: We stayed for a five day weekend at The Chelsea Pines Inn and had a wonderful time. Our expectations were fairly high after reading such positive reviews, but all were met or exceeded. All of the staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful. We felt truly welcomed from the moment we stepped in the door. The location was perfect. We could walk almost everywhere and there was great access to the subway for getting across town or to other boroughs. There were delicious healthy choices for breakfast and it was so relaxing to start the day with a leisurely breakfast in the atrium (the weather wasn't nice enough while we were there for us to sit out in the garden). We stayed in the Rock Hudson room, which was quite spacious, and delightfully decorated. Even though we had a window over 14th Street, with the window closed, the room was very quiet. We were a couple but I would also feel very comfortable staying here if I was travelling to the city alone. We will definitely be back. NYC is such an amazing city to visit - and to stay at this fantastic gem of a place made it all that much more special!

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Superior Sofitel”
text: Using Jetsetter, I got a top floor junior suite (Rm 1421) with an open north view towards Liberty Place complex (and the Westin hotel, which is also nice!) for $120/night, which was an incredible deal. The hotel is located in a prime area within a couple blocks of Rittenhouse Square, and not terribly far from the historic sites and museums. The room was nicely furnished with small, but acceptable, signs of wear. The layout and size were great, with a bathroom that could be accessed from the room entrance (like most hotels) or via the dressing area with two closets on the far side (UNlike most hotels!). The bathroom had a separate stall shower and tub, expanses of marble and L'Occitaine products everywhere--many of which came home with me. The bed was feathers above, below and under your head. There was only the feather duvet on the bed, no blanket or sheets, which made regulating temperature an all or nothing proposition in the warm weather. But it was luxurious nonetheless. I ordered one cheese and fruit plate from room service, which was delicious, well-presented and delivered exactly at the promised time. I did not use the valet parking or need the concierge's assistance, but the Front Desk staff I dealt with briefly were all very friendly, though the "bonjours" delivered with a pronounced Philadelphia accent were amusingly over the top. Overall, I was very favorably impressed with this hotel and could recommend it to anyone, especially if they can score one of the junior suites.

name: The Rittenhouse Hotel
title: “Wonderful hotel and we would definitely be back”
text:
Rittenhouse hotel has lived up to its reputation, excellent service from the time you walk into the door, very comfortable beds, clean rooms and excellent service leaving the hotel.
My only distress is the ritten square but that is not part of the hotel. Keep it up Rittenhouse staff, excellent job !

name: The Independent
title: “Best kept secret in Philadelphia”
text:
The Independent is in a great location. Easy walks to a variety of restaurants and coffee shops. It is only several blocks to the theater district on Broad Street and to city hall and major shopping. Only a few blocks to Market Street with additional shopping as well as links and public transportation to Philadelphia sights like museums and Independence Hall. Close also to Reading Terminal Market. Easy to flag a cab outside the hotel. 
The rooms are well appointed, are very clean. The staff is helpful and courteous and the price per room is quite competitive with the modest chair operations and a bargain compared to the "big names". Safe neighborhood.

name: Hilton Inn at Penn
title: “Very convenient Hotel near to UPenn”
text: If you have business or family at the University of Pennsylvania, this the ideal Hotel as the location is perfect. It was recently renovated, so the rooms are adequate, with new bathrooms and super soft beds. Even if not part of the Hotel, Pod restaurant is in the same building and I liked the food there.

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “'France in Philly' concept is a bit contrived, but great hotel overall”
text:
This was a great hotel for a number of reasons, with the amazing bed topping the list. We slept wonderfully--although some of the credit is probably owed to the light-blocking curtains. The bathroom was also impressive for a non-suite room, and the L'Occitane amenities were really nice. The location was perfect--we walked from the hotel to Independence Hall and to the art museum (though I think we're willing to walk a bit farther than most). The hotel lounge had a cool vibe, and had some creative cocktail options. The room price seemed really reasonable for the quality, although parking is not included and is pretty pricey (I think it was about $40/day). We did park our car at the hotel, though, and thought the valet was usually quick and very convenient, as it snowed while we were there. 
Service at the hotel restaurant during brunch was AWFUL, however. Our waiter did not stop by our table for over an hour after taking our orders, and seemed to ignore our attempts to flag him down. Additionally, all the hotel staff attempt to speak French, and as a Francophone, I found it really obnoxious...if they're still saying "bonjour" when people order cocktails at 11pm, it's clearly all for show. There weren't too many other drawbacks. We ordered room service once, and it seemed to take a really long time for it to arrive (it was just dessert). Also, there isn't much sound proofing from hallway noise (though this saved us from oversleeping more than once).

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Downtown Hotel
title: “Not the cleanest hotel”
text: The bathroom was dirty, the toilet, shower curtain floor and sink. The room looked like it hadn't been vaccumed. I only paid $45 and was only there one night and actually aside from sleeping, only in the room for a couple hours. Can't imagine if I had paid full price or was staying longer.

name: Alexander Inn
title: “Great little hotel”
text: I had never been to Philadelphia and so picked this hotel because it was close to my son's apartment. What a great location and even though the my room was small I really wasn't there enough to make it a downside. Bathroom was clean and perfect for one person. The staff was very helpful and the continental breakfast more than adequate. I will definitely book here when I visit my son again.

name: Library Hotel
title: “Loved the Library Hotel”
text:
From the moment we arrived, the hotel surrounded us with comfort. The employees were unfailingly courteous and helpful. My husband left his glasses in the taxi, and the front desk workers helped with calls to try and track them down. Adrian, who helped with our luggage, was charming and helpful throughout our stay.
Our room was one of the regular doubles (#905) and although it wasn't a large room, we were very impressed with the level of comfort and amenities. The room's layout was very well organized to maximize space, and we didn't feel the least bit cramped. The bed was very comfortable, the bathroom was lovely and there was lots of closet space. 
Breakfast was served in a lovely room with large windows and tranquil decor. The pastries and fresh fruit were very tasty, and the coffee was excellent. The very pleasant ladies staffing the breakfast room were happy to toast bagels or bread, and provided help in any way needed. And I loved having the local newspapers and magazines available to read during breaifast. There is also an afternoon wine and cheese hour, which we didn't manage to fit in. Both breakfast and the afternoon wine/cheese are included in the room rate.
The location of the hotel couldn't be better. Grand Central and Bryant Park, both about 2 blocks away, have excellent subway connections, and many museums and sites are close by. I hope to return to NYC in the next year or two, and will definitely stay at the Library Hotel again. It felt like coming home at the end of each day in the city.

name: Rittenhouse 1715, A Boutique Hotel
title: “Disappointed”
text: My husband has stayed at 1715 for work and raved about it. So we decided to book a romantic weekend getaway there. Unfortunately it must have been an "off" weekend for the hotel, because I wasn't impressed. Pluses - location, size (nice to be one of only 8 rooms). Minuses - some of the staff was very friendly, but others were downright grouchy. None of them were particularly knowledgeable of the city or general area, which was surprising. Couldn't get past the fact that a piece of pear in the fruit salad on the Continental breakfast clearly had a bite out of it - teeth marks and everything! Unacceptable for an expensive boutique hotel. I wouldn't recommend this hotel based on my experience. But as I mentioned, my husband has had favorable visits there.

name: Philadelphia Marriott Downtown
title: “Nicest Staff!”
text:
Overall, this Marriott is pretty generic. The location is walkable to almost anything you might want to see or do in Center City Philadelphia, right across the street from Reading Terminal Market (skip the hotel dining and go to the market for a fresh snack or meal!)
My room was spotless. It's true, this hotel does not have the most up-to-date amenities (old televisions, I noticed wallpaper peeling in one corner), but it's perfectly serviceable. Internet is paid, but there is a Starbucks with free WiFi in the lobby.
Parking is a fortune ($45/night incl taxes) if your company isn't picking up the tab. And make sure to allow a good 20-30 minutes to get your car from valet if you're leaving during a busy time (Sunday around check-out).
The reason I am writing this review, however, despite the Marriott's overall unremarkability is that the staff was INCREDIBLY nice. Everyone I encountered from front desk staff to housekeeping was particularly friendly, nice and accommodating. I needed extra towels and they were there within 10 minutes WITH A SMILE. Really a pleasure. Kudos.

name: The Independent
title: “Pass on the Chain Hotels and Stay Here”
text:
I arrived at the Independent Hotel in downtown Philadelphia in evening. The street entrance is discreet with an elevator taking you to lobby. There is an employee waiting there to quickly take you through your registration with a waiting area (fireplace, flatscreen tv, coffee bar) and then onto the room. I stayed in room 503 which is on the top floor, corner room with hardwood floors, high ceilings (20 feet) and two large queen beds. Extra bedding was in closet and a deck with computer cord. Bathroom was large with double head shower. Small mini fridge with coffee maker. All in All, very very nice and warm and toasty. Keep in mind this was the storm of the century outside. The staff was attentive and gave us great walking tour tips, even mapping it out for us. There is a computer room which was handing for pre boarding on our flight back. I loved this hotel.
The area is walkingn distance to everything. And we walked at least five hours a day seeing the Old City, South Street, Rittenhouse Square, Reading Terminal...Took the subway to Wachovia Center for Nova games (10 min ride) which was only one block to Broad Street. 
If you are planning a trip to Philly and don't want to spend tons of money but still want a cool experience, THIS IS YOUR HOTEL.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites San Antonio-Airport
title: “About as perfect as a business hotel can be”
text:
Close to the San Antonio Airport, restaurants, and shopping galore. Very reasonably priced, very clean, with excellebt customer service. 
Area is also very, very safe and close enough to easily access the Riverwalk in a 15-20 minute drive. SeaWorld would be much farther (about 40 minutes around the Loop 410)
Could not recommend more in a single review.

name: The US Grant
title: “Well worth the cost”
text:
The US Grant is a beautiful hotel. The decor felt luxurious, especially the bathroom. Our stay was very enjoyable. We were there for our anniversary and the staff went out of their way to pamper us. We enjoyed both the Grill and room service. The food was delicious and the lounge performers were very good.
The US Grant is located in a prime location with many available activities.
On our way out, Maxamian, a doorman, offered to give us a tour. I am glad we said yes. The history is amazing and the tour was one of the highlights of our stay.
One of the few times we didn't feel let down or ripped off when paying the bill. We would recommend this hotel.

name: Rancho Bernardo Inn
title: “charm and christmas lights!”
text:
beautifully decorated for christmas---love the fireplaces burning, garlands with lights, the 17 trees.
the whole property was charming and there were lots of little private spaces and gardens to sit on a bench or cuddle :) The landscaping is beautifully manicured.
The rooms were good, maybe a little upgrading would be nice in the bathrooms but the whole property and the spa make up for them!
Spa treatments were great--the massage in the outdoor garden cabana room for no extra charge was a nice surprise.

name: Old Town Inn
title: “wonderful staff”
text: We stayed for 2 nights in early November. The location is very convenient and there's free parking in their lot. We enjoyed the breakfast and though it wasn't swimming weather the pool area looked lovely. We left some items in the room by mistake and when we called the desk Anna had our items and mailed them back to us within days. She was outstanding, as were all the staff we met. We'll definitely return and will be happy to recommend this Inn.

name: Four Points by Sheraton San Antonio Northwest
title: “Great Place”
text: My friend and I stayed her las Saturday. We were looking for a location close to La Cantera Shopping and this hotel was right around the corner. Lobby and outside patio area were very nice as well as the rooms. We ate breakfast there in the morning. We had a bagel and coffee but they did have a nice breakfast buffet. Would definately stay here again!!

name: Rancho Bernardo Inn
title: “A lovely place to stay!”
text: We stayed here only 2 nights/3 days as we had to move on, but we thoroughly enjoyed our visit. The main building is absolutely lovely, every inch of space is beautifully decorated and landscaped. The grounds are exquisite, very nice to stroll through. The Veranda dining area was beautiful and food was great. The adult pool was very nice. The staff is very professional , friendly, and courteous. Our room in the Valencia building was well appointed with nice furnishings and plush bedding & linens. The bathroom was well designed with 2 separate dressing areas. The only things I would caution about: we arrived at night and it was a little difficult to locate our building in the dark, despite directions from the valet staff. Secondly, the Valencia buidling did not have an elevator and our room was located on the second floor. Not a huge problem but made hauling our heavy suitcases up the stairs a little challenging. Be sure to ask for a first floor room if necessary.

name: Omni San Diego Hotel
title: “Great hotel for Downtown San Diego”
text:
My husband and I celebrated our wedding anniversary with a night in San Diego. We had purchased a night at the Omni San Diego at a Fundraiser. From the moment of booking the customer services was great. 
Our room was not quite ready upon arrival, which was 12noon and check in was at 3pm, and we didn't expect it to be. However we were offered the opportunity to store bags and immediate use of the pool and facilities. The front desk person asked for our cell phone number to call when our room was available.
The pool area was lovely. On the 6th floor it offered views of the convention center and bay. However it was an exceptionally hot day for San Diego (101 on the patio), so we chose to have lunch at McCormick's and Schmidts, located in the hotel. Again, excellent service, wonderful bloody Mary's and a great lunch of assorted seafood dishes. I personally loved the crab stack.
Before lunch arrived to our table, the front desk called and had a room ready for us. the room was facing the city and a good size. The only thing I found odd was the bathroom seem so much larger in porportion the sleeping area, but it was very nice and clean. The amenities were very nice and all of the soft goods were in excellent shape.
We had a great time walking around downtown during the day and at night. The hotel is the perfect location for attending a convention, baseball game or concert on the embaradero. If you don't mind walking, you will never need a taxi.
Thank you Omni San Diego Hotel!

name: Hyatt Regency San Antonio
title: “Wedding stay - very nice and great location”
text:
We were in San Antonio for a family wedding and all the out of towners stayed here.
(The wedding was not at the hotel).
The hotel had everything needed and the location on the Riverwalk was great.
There were plenty of activities and the pool and fitness area were well equipped.

name: Springhill Suites by Marriott San Antonio Downtown / Alamo Plaza
title: “Nice new Sprnghill Suites”
text: New hotel with lots of color. Rooms are nice and have some personality. Beds not bad. HD TV in every room. Breakfast area decent with eggs, bacon and waffles. Walking distance to Alamo, convention center. Biggest drawback is $21 for parking per night. Ftness cener connected to the Fairfield. Very adequate. Staff is friendly.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Island Palms Hotel & Marina
title: “Very relaxing.”
text: Spent the first week in October weather was beautiful , hotel staff was very accomadating and friendly. I would highly recommend. If you enjoy the water and like to watch the boat traffic coming and going this is the place for you!

name: Rancho Bernardo Inn
title: “Nice stay for any event”
text:
Stayed for a corporate event, grounds are just beautiful, Rooms are spacious (stayed in the Greens) as are the balconies, maybe a bit dated but still very nice. Air Conditioning is very loud, makes a strange noise when going on and off. Walls are definitely thin, heard things above, below and to each side... Electricity needs updating, I had their hair dryer, the TV and the coffee machine ono and blew the circuit in bathroom and kitchen area of room. Maintenance fixed immediately upon calling. 
Food was just OK, room service was cool, not hot and the "crispy" calamari was no longer crispy. Event buffets were OK, feeding 200 people must degrade service. It wasn't bad, but it also wasn't anything I would remember. I assume the restaurants must be better.
The staff is fantastic - very friendly, helpful and accommodated all needs. 
Signage could be better as it is dark at night and can be confusing but overall a nice place to stay.

name: Bay Club Hotel & Marina
title: “1st trip to San Diego”
text: Very nice location on Shelter Island. Parking is only $5 a day, which is much cheaper than other hotels in San Diego. They have happy hour in the bar every day from 4-7. Half price appetizers and discounts on beer and wine. We took advantage of that almost every day of our trip. The rooms are average, but clean. We used the pool and jacuzzi all but one day of our trip. Nothing fancy but it was very relaxing. Complimentary breakfast every morning was decent as well. Seems they go all out on the weekends, it's more basic on the weekdays, but either way a free hot breakfast. Everyone was very pleasant that worked there. I have no complaints and would recommend this hotel.

name: Hyatt Regency San Antonio
title: “I had a pleasant experience”
text:
I was impressed with the Hyatt Recency San Antonio from the moment I was dropped off at the front doors. Several people immediately offered to help me with my bags. My experience at the front desk was pleasant as the front desk clerk was very polite and helpful. She thoroughly explained the payment procedures which I'd never had done before. She then gave me a brief orientation to the elevators, dining areas, etc. For the most part I found all the hotel staff to be friendly and helpful. Also, all telephone contacts were courteous. While at the airport I remembered that I forgot my receipt which I needed for reimbursement and I called the hotel. They promptly sent me an invoice via email which saved the day.
My room had a great view and I could see the Alamo from my window. I really never was bothered by excessive noise from other guests or hotel activity. I had no problems with the temerature controls and the blackout curtains worked well. The hotel itself is beautiful with many water features. I was there for a conference and the hotel offered us a great discount on our breakfasts. My experience with the hotel restaurant The Q was positive. I had prompt service, friendly staff and the food was good. At lunch the hostess explained the pasta buffet and other specials.
I was very impressed by the Q Bar.The bartenders were very personable and informative. The service was never anything but prompt. The bartender explained all the beers that he had on tap which was a great selection, but he also directed me to a large cooler by the bar which held a large variety of bottled beers. There were a number of limited editions in the case and he was able to describe the ones I pointed out. 
The location of the hotel was great, only less than five minutes from the Alamo and the Riverwalk right at the door. 
Negatives:
Only a couple items:
 The carpet in my room was stained and old. 
The remote would not turn on the tv but it would change channels. So I had to get up and turn the tv on or off. It didn't exhaust me doing that but frustrating.
The toilet seat would not stay up, but would suddenly slam down.
The concierge was aloof, but he was the only staff member I found like that.
Overall my experience at the Hyatt Regency San Antonio was very positive. I definitely would return to this hotel with my family. All the staff should be commended for their service.

name: Country Inn & Suites By Carlson San Antonio Airport, TX
title: “Very pleased!”
text:
Beautiful new hotel. Exceptional decor. I'd stay here again!
Business desk has lots of electrical outlets, with wired and wireless Internet. Beautiful vases, lamps and art-deco bathroom make this a perfect room for a romantic getaway, too. Two (2) flat screen TV's. VERY comfortable bed and pillows. Great service, friendly staff. I don't think I have ever rated a hotel as a 5-dot (excellent) before, but this place deserves it.
Very minor squawks: Rooms are well sound-proofed, but this is an airport hotel, so you will probably be waken in the morning by the noise from the jets taking off. I don't know why hotels don't run their bathroom ventilation systems, but no air moved in or out of our bathroom. (I don't know why many motels leave vent systems off so that the moisture build up in the rooms...) I wish there were a couple of coat hooks near the front door.

name: Hotel Contessa
title: “Great experience”
text: This was a great hotel. It was a trip where my girlfriend and I made it official. We had the best time. The staff was was very attentive, polite and helpful. We will be visiting again, maybe a honeymoon or something. We will recommend to everyone.

name: Bay Club Hotel & Marina
title: “Great Hotel”
text: We stayed here 2 nights in August, and loved it! Nice breakfast (get there early if you want strawberries!) and large clean room. We had a Marina view room and could see (and hear) the concert at the resort next door from our balcony. A really nice unexpected bonus!! Would definitely come back again!

name: Rancho Bernardo Inn
title: “Older but Charming”
text: The Rancho Bernardo Inn is showing it age but makes up for this with its semi-secluded location and helpful staff. The property sits in a residential area which sets it apart for other hotels in the area. The golf is good and the rooms are spacious although a little dated. The K-cup coffee maker is a nice touch for coffee or tea in the morning because it gives the guest(s) a choice of coffees and tea. I wish other hotels would use this system. This property does not have the "Wow factor" of newer hotels/resorts but my overall experience was a good one and I would not hesitate to stay here again.

name: Omni San Diego Hotel
title: “Great hotel”
text: Wonderful location. Friendly staff, good room and great pool. The only complaint I have us that there were two large and long black haira on the bathroom floor in room. I would stay here again. Parking is a little expensive.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Island Palms Hotel & Marina
title: “Great place with great staff”
text: Our family of 3 stayed here in a suite and sweet it was. The queen sized beds were nice & firm, we had lots of seating, a great place for dining in, and a great pool/hot tub area. The food in the restaurant was good and very reasonably priced. The worst thing I can say is that the hair dryer cord was too short!

name: Hotel Contessa
title: “It really is PET FRIENDLY!”
text:
My hubby & I just spent 2 nights at the Hotel Contessa, we have stayed there many times before but decided to bring our pup this time. Wow they really ARE pet friendly! They even have a "Pet Room Service" Menu. We ordered twice for her. Presentation was awesome. She got her own tray with a WOOF placemat. A bowl for her BOTTLED water, (Us humans got tap water in a glass.)and a rose in a vase. First night... Fido's Favorite Chicken, second Barkers Beef Tenderloin. Both were a hit. 
Our human food was as always terrific, room clean, staff friendly. We will be back. Love it!

name: Bay Club Hotel & Marina
title: “A Little Bit of Heaven”
text: I love the Bay Club on Shelter Island...It's off the hotel strip, quieter. They have a wonderful included breakfast buffet daily. You can eat inside or pool side. You have a lovely view of the marina. The rooms are very nice. Only drawback in the summers are the summer concerts at Humphrey's Half Bay which there are cars parked everywhere sometimes taking your spot. I love being on the water, it's very relaxing watching the boats. Rooms are clean and staff very friendly.

name: The US Grant
title: “Amazing Hotel”
text:
The US Grant has served as a romantic getaway for my wife and I for several years. It has never disappointed!! It is one of the most Historic and Romantic places you will find in San Diego in addition to exceptional service, immaculate facilities and beautiful rooms. Not to mention close proximity to anything downtown, 5-10 min walk (or bike cab), 15-20 min to SD attractions. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who likes quality. 
While there are plenty of dinning options downtown, and I've tried plenty, the Grant Grill is in its own special category. Alberto, the Grill manager, knows exactly what the restaurant experience should be and doesn't disappoint. Make sure you strike a conversation when he approaches your table and ask him to recommend one of the Grill's own coctail creations. You can spend your entire stay at the hotel if you so desire...as we did. 
The US Grant is absolutely amazing-without question!

name: Omni San Diego Hotel
title: “Great Anniversary Trip!”
text:
We stayed two nights in July 2012 to celebrate our wedding anniversary. We got a great room rate through Jetsetter. The hotel really went above and beyond to help us celebrate our anniversary. They gave us a very spacious, corner room with great views, but even better was the complimentary champagne, chocolate covered strawberries, and water! We really enjoyed the complimentary beverage service every morning (coffee and OJ). 
The front desk attendant that checked us in recommended a fabulous restaurant for Friday night: Searsucker. Yummy food and drinks and great vibe! The hotel was in a fantastic location in the Gaslamp Quarter. We easily walked to dinner both nights. 
Our only complaint is that the walls/windows were a wee bit thin. While the noise coming from the neighborhood bars was quite loud until the wee hours of Saturday morning, more unexpected was our neighbors waking us up early on Sunday morning...repeatedly.

name: Old Town Inn
title: “All in all very good”
text: We want to emphasize the very good service. The front desk was there for any questions for us. The included breakfast was ok. From what we saw San Diego hotels seems expensive generally, so the price level here is ok too.

name: Rancho Bernardo Inn
title: “Great Place”
text:
We took a trip to RBI for wedding plus made a vacation out of it. It was a great place to stay. Beautiful scenery, relaxing and their food was excellent. Even our kids loved RBI. We all miss already their great breakfast outside in the patio area overlooking the golf course and mountains.
The rooms were very comfortable and clean.

name: Hotel Contessa
title: “Not Bad but needs updating and some cleaning”
text:
Great location near the Riverwalk. Lobby looks great and most of the hotel property; however, the rooms can use improvement. The suites are comfortable and roomy. The carpets are dirty and there is a musty odor in the room. The bathroom toilet needed cleaning and even after housecleaning came to clean it the sides were left dirty. The hotel has a friendly staff and especially the Concierge was outstanding. Both during the day and evening the hotel desk clerks were rude and not welcoming, they could take lessons on respect and a welcoming attitude from the housecleaning staff. The food at a catered event was substandard and bland. You are better off going off hotel property for meals. Nearby ZINCS is outstanding, great food and very reasonable. Across the street DRINK has a decent happy hour. 
All in all, I would stay in the hotel again, however, there are better properties including the WESTIN across the street.

name: Bay Club Hotel & Marina
title: “Remarkable Service!”
text:
We were so impressed with this entire facility! At check-in, I was genuinely greeted and filled in on the hotel. There was a bit of construction occurred in the parking lot but it was still easy for hubby to find a street level parking space. 
THE ROOM - Our room was on the second floor and faced the parking lot which faces the San Diego bay. There was a beautiful sail boat anchored in the bay which was perfectly centered by the window from our room's deck...perfect! The rooms are quite large for San Diego with areas for dining, working, watching TV and sleeping. The building is older but the room was super clean and well maintained. The bed was very comfortable and the room was quiet...what more could we ask for! One disappointment was the odd smell on the deck in the morning - not sure if it was coming from the room heater which we had turned on or just something else...
THE SERVICE - From check-in to check-out, we were floored by how sincerely helpful and concerned everyone was. We stopped in for Happy Hour and the bartender was also waiting on tables on the outside deck...boy has she got energy and a great attitude! I had one of the best martinis ever and the pours were generous.
THE FOOD - We only tried appetizers as had plans for the evening and we will definitely be back. The Coconut Shrimp was not the usual small, over cooked and under sweet disappointment I am used to...instead the shrimp were quite over sized, perfectly cooked and sweet enough to be eaten without a sauce. Hubby tried several times to steal one after I shared a bite with him. The jalapeno orange dressing was a bit bitter and not sweet enough for the shrimp so I just left it alone. Hubby tried the Pork Sliders and was also very pleased. 
We also tried the complementary breakfast which was loaded with pastries, fruit, breakfast meats, scrambled eggs and more. It was a special treat for us as we usually just have a protein shake in the morning.
I think we have found our home away from home when needing a "stay-cation" close to home - we will definitely return!

name: Old Town Inn
title: “Truly a great hidden gem!”
text:
Not a chain hotel, but great individual service, care and detail is part of this smaller hotel's charm. Very good pricing for this hotel. It does deserve a 5 star rating, even if small and without
an onsite restaurant. Well kept rooms and hotel property.
Beautiful landscaping, nice clean pool and areas, clean rooms, nice furniture, good bedding, soft pillows. Very beautiful and charming setting. Area surrounding the hotel is business or light industry. But good location near the I-5 and close to many tourist sites.
We stayed in the newer building, so can not speak to the other units, but they appeared to be
equally as nice. Liked the rooms floorplan, bath and dressing room space. Nicely arranged
mini-refrig. and microwave in wall space.
The rooms, carpet, furniture, wall hangings, bedding, lotions, etc. are all nice.
Breakfast is provided, it is what one generally is served, which does include hot items of waffles and oatmeal, boiled eggs, cereal, toast, orange juice, coffees, teas, pastries, muffins, fruit, etc. The breakfast room is very nice, but one does notice that
the staff goes out of their way to refill items as well as taking pride in keeping it clean and
in tip top shape. We greatly appreciated the staff, reception, etc.
Location is next to Old Town, so one could walk, as a short walk, 2-4 blocks from the hotel, or drive and park. The Trolly station is within walking distance in Old Town area so if one does not
have a car this hotel works if you plan to take the trolley or bus. Many shops and restuarants in Old Town. Within a short drive to other dining options and other areas of the city. The hotel is near the airport, Balboa Park, Gaslamp District, beaches, downtown, La Jolla, etc.
I/we visit San Diego often and this is a good choice, especially for budget travel. Parking is free.
Excellent experience and we will certainly return to the Old Town Inn.

name: Palomar San Diego, A Kimpton Hotel
title: “Not Impressed”
text: We stayed at the Hotel Palomar in San Diego last week. The decor is lovely, edgy, staff was nice and helpful. I would say the room we stayed in was a king sized bed...and that is it! Very very small room, to the point where I could hardly make it around the bed without hitting my ankle or knee on the frame or dresser. Small tv, curtains needed attention, as they were not attached at the top and the ceiling is prob 16 feet...so the light came in early. They needed to be rehung or something, and the staff should have noticed this when tending to the room. I could have called, but we were there only one night, and by the time we figured it out, I was ready for bed. Pricy place for such a tiny accommodation.

name: Bay Club Hotel & Marina
title: “Peaceful stay”
text: The Bay Club hotel is situated on Shelter Island next to a Marina. The view was so nice, and it's proximity to a beach and charming walkway was quite pleasant. The room we stayed at was spacious and smartly appointed. The staff were personable and the food was good. Given it's location, the cost of the stay was very inexpensive. I was surprised at how lovely it was for the price. This facility will become a regular for us, and I would recommend it to anyone who wishes a respite from day to day craziness.

name: Hotel Solamar - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Perfect hotel in a great location”
text: What a really nice hotel. The beds were very comfortable and the staff was great. JP at the pool bar was terrific and Cory who runs the Valet service couldn't have been more helpful. I was really impressed and would stay here again. The hotel is very clean and right in the middle of the gas lamp district with all the action. Perfect.

name: Hotel Solamar - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Chic Hotel in Gas Lamp district”
text: We stayed 3 nights in this hotel staff were great. The room was very nice and comfortable. Located in trendy Gas Lamp district. Great for hip younger crowd who like go clubbing in the evening. Lots of restaurants and bars nearby. Horton Plaza is in walking distance with stores, movies etc. Pro's -morning coffee and evening wine tasting Cons -If you drive or rent a car it costs $40 a day for parking. Sign up for their loyalty program before you go to be able to have Wi Fi free and you get other perks.

name: Hotel Contessa
title: “A nice time in San Antonio”
text: The room (bedroom and sitting area) was very comfortable and clean, and there was a door to separate the two so I could watch TV while my husband slept. The bathroom was large and immaculate. I would have like a small refrigerator for leftovers and there was certainly room in the dressing area. The pool area was very nice, the chaises were very comfortable, too. Towels available, even late in the afternoon. The lobby was extremely comfortable to hang out in, and nicely decorated. Able to get some work done with a coffee or wine in the afternoon looking out at the beautiful river walk. The bed was a king and I slept great, even though the pillows were a little too hard for my taste. The hotel is situated on a nice quiet area of the river walk, but not far from all the activity if that's what you want. The air conditioning worked great, even though it was very hot outside. The staff was friendly and helpful, the little store well stocked with all the necessities we forgot to bring. Room service was speedy, and the BLT was good. My only 2 complaints (and no hotel is ever going to be perfect) is that the valet parking was extremely slow and very expensive ($30 a night, and it took an average of 30 minutes wait for our car, even after calling for it ahead of time -- the gentleman ahead of me waited nearly an hour.) This might keep me from staying there if I had places I had to be on time for (like a wedding, or dinner reservation, and this is why I rated the service as average) Also, the hotel doesn't have HBO, but they do offer free internet service. All in all, I really enjoyed my stay.

name: Bay Club Hotel & Marina
title: “Excellent place to stay in San Diego, CA”
text: Great breakfast included in your price. Hotel is a bit old, but clean and a great location away from noise, sits right on a Marina next to Humphrey's. Staff is REALLY friendly and helpful. I would definitely stay there again.

name: Rancho Bernardo Inn
title: “My favorite place in the world!”
text: Rancho Bernardo Inn is one of the most beautiful and relaxing places anyone could stay! I have stayed there many, many times. The rooms, spa, food and dining are incredible. My most favorite thing is sitting in front of the outdoor fireplaces with a glass of wine. Look for Vicki will at the Veranda. Her laugh us contagious!

name: The US Grant
title: “Luxury hotel in middle of city”
text:
Stayed 2 nights and was impressed by the "Great Gatsby-like" lobby, staff, and rooms. The beds were very comfortable with luxury linens - didn't want to get out of bed. Slightly larger room provided a larger bathroom as well. Had breakfast in the restaurant both mornings and the food was terrific.
The hotel is across from the outdoor shopping mall on one side, and entrance to the Gas Lamp district on the other; which is convenient location. The city streets in that area are typical dirty city with a range of business folks, homeless, and hipsters that come out at night. However inside the property it feels like you're not within the dirty city.
Down side is that there are no views, windows look onto other building or down streets. So the drapes are drawn for both ambiance and privacy in the rooms. And there may be street noise as it most cities - just put the fan on low for white noise when you sleep.

name: Residence Inn San Diego Mission Valley
title: “Fantastic stay, we will be back!!”
text: We stayed for a few nights, wonderful hotel. Rooms are nice and spacious with a kitchen. Breakfast was great, snacks and complimentary beer and wine in the evening was an added bonus as well. Pool was nice, we will definately be back!

name: Ocean Park Inn
title: “Great every year!”
text: Excellent location, great views, very attentive staff, awesome breakfast included. We have stayed here every year for the past 4 years, will definitely continue to come back. Thank you.

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Downtown
title: “Great location, great service”
text: This is not your typical Courtyard - it's a converted bank building in downtown San Diego - we stayed two nights and walked/rode our bikes everywhere. Loads to do and a really vibrant downtown. It was a 'Birthday Weekend' and '...all we did...' was ask if we could have a couple champagne glasses and Alexis not only brought us a pair to our room but at her own expense dashed out to get us a 'champagne stopper' so we could savor our champagne over two sessions. WOW - the finest hotel in San Diego - for that matter in California would have a hard time matching the service provided by Alexis. We'll definitely return.

name: Sommerset Suites Hotel
title: “Excellent, start to finish”
text: It began with the excellent assistance I received from Jennifer and staff in re to setting up accommodations for 30 guests and seeing that it was carried through without missing a beat. We were greeted with wonderfully refreshing fruit infused waters at check-in desk, and reservations were handled professionally. Every effort was made to assist and follow through with plan. Our room was very comfortable, clean and quiet with a view over the pool. We were allowed early check-in and late check-out. Hotel is situated within walking distance to everything you could want, and every type of food. Park and walk.

name: The Pearl Hotel
title: “Another stay at the Pearl "gone great"”
text: My wife & I are in S.D. every year for business, and have stayed at The Pearl Hotel almost every year since it opened. I've read the other reviews, and agree with hip, retro-modern, cool atmosphere. It really is like staying over at a "cool" friends house. Also, the entire staff was great, working as a team, without the "attitude" so common today at nice places. I worked all day writing while sitting at the bar (its' closed during the day), and accomplished my goals. The food is good (my wife is a "foodie") and we always eat there during our stays. Its just nice when your on the road, and get where your going, to not have to go somewhere else to have a drink, eat, or just chill-out. Its just a great place to be.There is a little road noise, due to its proximity to the street, and the bar crowd can create some noise if you turn in early. We usually ask for a room towards the back that is a little more quite. I guess in summation I would say that if you enjoy the mortuary quite, cookie-cutter corporate hotel style, stay at one of those. They're all the same, and easy to find. If you want to stay at a nice, easy-going fun place, stay at The Pearl. I would recommend The Pearl Hotel to everyone except the up-tight traveler.

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “VERY BAD CUSTOMER SERVICE”
text: had a really bad experience at this hotel we paid $600 dollars for one night and customer service was really bad on top of that the lights went out for about 30 minutes and then they claimed we took drinks out of there refrigerator and had them charged to our account people never stay here....... also the manager that spoke to us seemed kind of races and did not really do anything about our stay... also my friend lost her id and bank card at the hotel so now they are charging her to have it mail back to her!! bad bad bad bad bad bad bad never book a room here ever

name: The US Grant
title: “Best Guest Relations in the Industry”
text:
My parents selected the US Grant in San Diego as their vacation hotel while celebrating 40 years of marriage. Demi Ricario in the Guest Loyalty office was extremely helpful with arranging a surprise for them when they checked in. The Hotel uses software to alert their staff to special guest accommodations, and I was able to arrange my parent's favorite beverage to be chilled to my specific instructions and delivered to their room upon check-in. Demi even wrote them a note on behalf of me and my sister and she offered the drinks complimentary in light of the milestone. Demi and the Hotel's help wasn't just platinum quality service, it was a kind and loving gesture to parents I love so much.
