In addition to Demi’s service, she was also logical and thoughtful with assessing my idea. She was a good listener, she looked into the details, and called me back and clearly outlined the results. It’s so rare to deal with anyone over the phone and feel confident they can help you and respond to your needs in a smart and efficient manner. Thank you US Grant and thank you Demi!
If you want to feel cared for in a home-away-from-home, chose this hotel for your stay in San Diego!

name: Palomar San Diego, A Kimpton Hotel
title: “Excellent stay”
text:
Second visit to San Diego for 4 nights and first visit to the Palomar Hotel ,a boutique hotel whit a very good location near city center , shops , harbor , restaurants, shopping mall ,bars , nightclubs .... enz Santa Fe railroad station 4 bloks , public transportation accros the street , exellent , frendly and helpfull staff and outstanding service , clean and gorgeous large room whit king-sized bed , balcony and city view , nice pool . huge badroom , At the impeccably lobby every morning you can get a newspaper , koffie or thee for free , breakfast at the resto at the first floor good service and food . At this property from business to solo traveler you will have a great stay.
Mr Patrick Van Acker , Belgium

name: Hotel Solamar - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Very hip and fun place to stay.”
text: My family enjoyed our stay at this hotel. It was very hip and modern. At one of the wine events held daily, there was a cat joining us in the lobby area. Very pet friendly. Of course, if you don't like animals, you can enjoy the room which is very comfortable and with beautiful decor.

name: Ocean Park Inn
title: “Great location, comfortable (but not luxurious) rooms”
text: We wanted to spend a weekend hanging out in Pacific Beach and the Ocean Park Inn is right at the epicenter. It's located right along the boardwalk and most rooms have views of the pool, boardwalk and ocean. The rooms are nothing special. However, the rooms were clean, staff was very friendly and helpful, and secured underground parking was provided ($10). Nice outdoor pool/whirlpool also.

name: Palomar San Diego, A Kimpton Hotel
title: “Average hotel”
text: We stayed at one Skyline View Suite. The room has an average size but it was quite dusty with greasy fingerprints every where. The furniture quality is pretty poor and the sofa upholstery was full of old spots. The restaurant is OK but not special. People here are friendly but the place needs some deep cleaning almost everywhere...

name: The Pearl Hotel
title: “Fantastic Stay!”
text:
I have been looking forward to staying at the Pearl now for quite some time, and last weekend I finally got in after seemingly months of them being booked solid (summer in San Diego.) After finally staying, it more than lived up to the hype!
I stayed in two rooms during my stay: the gem and the jewel. The first night was the gem, and it was the smallest room I have ever stayed in... however it was also one of the best for it's price (even compared to rooms three times it's size at other hotels!) I was easily able to plug my laptop into the HDMI port of the 42 inch tv mounted near the wall, and then sit on the bed and control some of the movies I have prepared for my evening. The bed itself was also VERY comfortable, and featured a very lightweight summer comforter sandwiched between two clean and very soft (high thread count I imagine) sheets.
The second nights stay was in the Jewel. The jewel was much larger and had a larger bed as well. The bed was the exact same make it seems so it was also very comfortable, and there was again a large HD television (panasonic) in the room for me to plug my computer into easily via an HDMI port. Also in both rooms were two wonderful little beta fish (one per room) which me and my girlfriend found quite amusing (I've never seen fish in a hotel room before!)
All in all, I would steer clear of the gem if you are claustrophobic or dislike small spaces, but if you're anything like me, and love cozy little places that are well furnished and VERY practical, then you will love the "bachelor pad" that is the gem. I have never stayed in the pearl's largest room as they were sold out both nights, but I can bet they are very nice!
All in all, if you're looking for a luxurious get away, the pearl is not for you, but if you have an interest in something different you just might love it. The staff was also extremely friendly and helpful - some of the best i've ever experienced even compared to the nearby resorts. You also should dine in the evening if you are interested in some different and VERY tasty food, or simply get a drink at their bar (which is buzzing with activity on the weekends!) where they will make you whatever you wish exactly how you like it!

name: Hyatt Regency San Antonio
title: “WONDERFUL”
text:
Went to the GSA Conference and stayed at the Hyatt Regency San Antonio. Everything was WONDERFUL. The decor, the room, the service - all was great. Hotel is directly on the Riverwalk. It was convenient to everything!.
Had in-room breakfast and it was truly wonderful. Beware though, they already include the gratuity and delivery in the amount - so no need to tip extra.
Jose Rosales checked me out and offered to print my boarding pass. He provided excellent service.

name: Palomar San Diego, A Kimpton Hotel
title: “Personal touch a plus at Palomar”
text:
Stayed at the Palomar for a business trip. Desk staff very friendly and greeted me by my first name throughout the stay. Rooms are clean with soft comforters and pillows and jungle patterned robes -mine were a zebra and leopard print :). The room appears small but I had plenty of space for my luggage, a desk for my laptop, a chair to relax in. There is a refrigerator and safe in the room. 
The work out room was kept clean and the water cooler was replenished with water regularly. I worked out every morning and had 1-3 people in the room with me with plenty of room for all of us to exercise. The roof top pool is clean and bathtub warm- very relaxing. Enjoyed a brief swim in the AM. I had a view of the pool from my room and it was used by many guests in the early evening.
Happy hour had musicians a couple days of the week. The Sangria was refreshing. There is beer and wine as well. Trent Hadcock, a guitarist, was pretty good. 
Didn't get a chance to try the restaurant as the conference I was at provided quite a bit of food.
The business center had easy access to computers and a printer to print our boarding passes for the airline trip back home.
Mike, the consierge was very helpful with suggestions for sight seeing or local restaurants. Keegan from the Food network stopped by one evening during happy hour and spoke to Mike. After he was through, our group talked to Keegan and learned he had opened upon a new restaurant about 1.5 miles on 5th avenue called DBar. Mike set up transportation the next day for us. It was great.
There is a free shuttle that will take you within a 3 mile radius. It was not always available. We had better success when we scheduled it in advance. The drivers were very friendly and gave us advice about the local area as well.
There were also a couple of bicycles out front but I didn't have an opportunity to use one.
The hotel is close to a CVS and 7/11 and there were many restaurants and small shops in the area. The hotel is close to Pet Co Park- about a mile or so and close to the convention center- also about a mile. 
Overall, enjoyed my stay and so did my companions.

name: Ocean Park Inn
title: “Ocean Fix”
text:
Can't be much closer to the ocean, listening to the waves as you sleep. Price is right, clean rooms with great parking. Only real flaw, new carpeting is needed. When booking request the quiet side or next time we would preferably book the rooms right on the boardwalk, worth the extra money. Great location for a lot less cost. 
Patrick was very friendly when we checked in. Went the extra for making our stay as great as possible.

name: Hyatt Regency San Antonio
title: “Excellent home base for a visit to San Antonio”
text:
Attended a three day business meeting at this hotel, and extended my trip by a day to do some additional site seeing.
First off the location is just about perfect for those wishing to enjoy downtown San Antonio and the Riverwalk. The Alamo was a 2-3 minute walk right out the front doors of the hotel, and the Riverwalk is right out the back doors. 
The staff was very friendly and courteous. All of my interactions from the front desk staff, concierge, wait staff and bartenders to the maids and maintenance staff were very pleasant. It seemed like what ever my question or request, they were happy to talk to me and help. 
I ate breakfast and lunch at the hotel everyday, and dinner one evening. They were all very good, and at no time did it seem like 'regular" buffet type meals. Breakfast offered eggs, meat, potatoes and very good picante sauce. A generous section of fresh fruit and pastries, and lots of very good coffee.
Lunch was free range chicken and a very tasty fish, a southwest style cold salad and some wonderful deserts. Another lunch was cold cuts and cheese tray, along with ships and salsa.
Dinner was a petite filet and it was cooked exactly to my liking. Interestingly the steak at the hotel was FAR superior to the one I had at Landry's later that week.
My room was clean and spacious, and while I had an "interior" view, it did look out over the beautiful atrium lobby and River-walk.
Took advantage of the rooftop pool one evening, and it was a nice experience as well.
There is plenty to see and do within walking distance of the hotel. Shops, museums, historic sites, and more restaurants and bars than I had time to explore. I also took a bit of a hike and walked down to three of the five historic missions on the mission trail. The Alamo was originally Mission Valero and from there Mission Concepcion was a 4 mile walk, some of which was on city streets and other parts on the Riverwalk trail. Sadly not all of it is open, but the parts I was able to get to were very nice. 
The National Park Service main visitor center is at Mission San Jose, and it is the largest and most complete of the four. Mission San Juan required a bus ride and a 4 mile round trip walk, despite what the park rangers tell you, the 42 bus line doesn't take you very close. I did also get to visit the Espada Dam and aquaduct, an ingenious irrigation system used to help farm around the Missions. The last Mission Espada was an even longer walk, and with no bus service I was getting hot and tired so I returned to the hotel to cool off on the Riverwalk.
Most of the chains have places on the Riverwalk such as Rainforest Cafe, The Hard Rock Cafe, Dicks Crab Shack, Coyote Ugly, Howl at the Moon, Landry's and others. I enjoyed meals and drinks at The County Line, La Paloma, Mad Dog's Pub, and several others.
All in all I had a wonderful visit, and plan to return with my family to show them a beautiful southwestern city.

name: Bay Club Hotel & Marina
title: “A Good Value in a Fabulous Location”
text: We stayed at the Bay Club in October for a family trip. The rooms are good size and the value with the included breakfast is quite good. The rooms feel clean, but the carpet and other parts of the hotel are in need of an upgrade and there is a musty smell in the hallways and rooms. The kids really loved the breakfast. The marina view is spectacular and enjoying the view from the pool area is even better. We really loved staying on Shelter Island. With a little remodeling, the Bay Club could be a prime destination.

name: Sommerset Suites Hotel
title: “I have traveled many places, Sommerset was outstanding!!”
text: I needed to be in San Diego, CA for approximately 7 weeks. Staying at the Sommerset Suites was like being home. Everyone was accommodating, the service was excellent, the rooms were extremely comfortable. I have fibromyalgia and a bad back, so sleeping on a comfortable bed is extremely important for me. The bed and bedding were like sleeping at home! The hotel was extremely clean and the staff was always working hard to keep everything clean, including the grounds. The purpose of my trip was to be with my college student, who had major surgery over the Christmas holidays and I needed to travel back to California to be with her. She stayed with me at the hotel until she felt comfortable enough to stay on campus. I also brought my little seven pound poodle with me. Both of them felt like they were at home. The entire staff, from management down to housekeeping were outstanding and made you feel like family. One of the nicest hotel I have ever stayed at that made me feel like family!!!!! The location was great, close to groceries, restaurants, shopping malls, etc. I will definitely stay there whenever we go gack!

name: Residence Inn San Diego Mission Valley
title: “Nice hotel, served it's purpose”
text:
My husband, daughter and I stayed at Residence Inn for a week in mid July 2011. The hotel was clean and seemed to be recently renovated. 
The pros included:
-Separate bedroom in our suite
-Pullout couch in living room, so an additional relative could stay with us
-Kitchen area with fridge and microwave and dishwasher
-Convenient location- near to Sea World, the zoo, airport, etc.
-Complimentary breakfast
The cons included:
-Difficulty parking- parking lot was full EVERY night and spots were tight
-We stayed on the 2nd floor in the rear of the hotel... apparently the hotel is built into the side of a hill, so we were below groundlevel, which prevented much sunlight from getting into our room
- Drains in our room were clogged throughout our stay- both the bathroom sink and the shower drain
- Due to "pet friendly" nature of hotel, family members had allergy issues
Overall, the Residence Inn was not a bad place to stay and it served it's purpose. We were able to get a good night's sleep there, with breakfast in the AM. If we were to stay there again, we would request an upper level room for more sunlight, as well as look into the possibility of a room that doesn't allow pets.

name: Residence Inn San Diego Mission Valley
title: “Nice Residence Inn”
text:
Stayed 3 nights while on business and had a good stay. Hotel was located off the interstate; a few minutes from Sea World and the zoo. They had just renovated the hotel, so it looked modern and fresh. Parking was $13/day.
I requested a top floor corner room and was given one. However my room faced the interstate, so there were some car noise. Hotel was situated far away from the interstate, but it maybe a problem for light sleepers.
Room had just be renovated and had new bedding and furniture. I was given a family suite that had a master bedroom and kid's bedroom with bunk beds. Kitchen had stainless steel appliances and there were 2 LCD TVs.
As with other Residence Inns, they offered free breakfast and evening socials. The breakfast was nice with hot foods such as sausages, eggs, potatoes. The evenings socials were a big hit for me. It was convenient and I didn't have to spend money to go out to eat. They had hot dogs the first night; tacos the second night; and pasta the third night of my stay. Beer was free as well.
Overall this was one of the better Residence Inns. It is perfect for business and leisure trips.

name: The Pearl Hotel
title: “The Pearl is hands down the best place to...”
text:
The Pearl is hands down the best place to stay, eat and drink in SD. The rooms have style, the food is awesome and the staff is cool. Just stay there.
DS
San Francisco

name: Bay Club Hotel & Marina
title: “Relaxing stay at the Bay Club Hotel & Marina”
text:
This was my second stay at the Bay Club Hotel & Marina. I really enjoyed my first stay at this hotel, so when looking for a place to stay for my daughter's 6th birthday, I knew I wanted to stay here again. Upon arrival, the front desk staff was warm and welcoming. I needed assistance with my luggage and a very friendly gentleman took my bags to my room and also offered very helpful suggestions for delicious restaurants in the area. 
Our room had a limited view of the marina, however, it was nothing major (a fence slightly blocked our view). The room was simple and spacious enough for an adult and small child. The only downfall to the room was that I could hear my upstairs neighbors every step very early in the morning and very late at night. Other than that, it was a very quiet and pleasant room. 
We only ate the complimentary breaking once during our 3 day stay and I was somewhat disappointed. During the week, breakfast ends at 10AM and we arrived around 9AM and all of the food containers were on the verge of being empty. The food was warm and it was delicious (I had an egg dish, sausage, bacon, and toast), I just wish there were waffles like there was during my first stay at the hotel. I guess I came on the wrong morning! 
Overall, this was another relaxing stay at the Bay Club Hotel and Marina and I would definitely come to this hotel again sometime in the future.

name: Rancho Bernardo Inn
title: “Fabulous family celebration of 50th wedding anniversary.”
text: We have travelled extensively as a large family group complete with young children and teenage girls. They all declared that this stay was better then their many trips to the Greenbrier. Everyone was so helpful and friendly and the grounds are simply gorgeous. The gals all enjoyed the spa while I (Grammy) joined Granddaddy and the guys in some golf. Both have all wanting to return next year. There is not a lot for the younger children to do as they cannot (understandably) use the spa pools with their moms. One kind dad took them to the zoo. There is tons to do in the San Diego area but you are always anxious to get bak to the Inn. There is a warmth and peacefulness there that draws you in. Add fabulous food, flawless grounds and a pleasant staff and you have a total winner.

name: Hotel Contessa
title: “Hotel Contessa is excellent”
text: We stayed here over a weekend this summer. I was able to get the room free by paying for it with AA miles. It is on a quiet area of the River Walk not far from all of the action. The rooms are very spacious. We really enjoyed the rooftop pool.

name: Bay Club Hotel & Marina
title: “Very noisey making it hard to get any rest”
text: We went and bought a fan to attept to cover all the lobby noise and peoples TV in next room. For the price of the room, expected better noise control then Motel 6.

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Downtown
title: “Great Place, Super Location”
text:
This hotel is a short walk to the popular Gaslamp District.
The rooms are spacious and beds are comfortable.
Shower pressure is great.
The breakfast buffet is wonderful and at a good price.
All hotel staff were very friendly and willing to help.
This is a great place to stay while visiting San Diego.

name: Bay Club Hotel & Marina
title: “Great Get-away”
text: We purchased this hotel through groupon, and our stay exceeded our expectations! We had a lovely room with a view of the harbor, and there was a walkway all along the San Diego Bay . Pool area was small, but tables were set up outside for our breakfast (included) and happy hour. A great hotel for the value we will be returning to, even without the Groupon!

name: Rancho Bernardo Inn
title: “Fabulous tranquility and the best spa!”
text:
Stayed one night with my daughter for a spa treat. Property is exceptionally clean, beautiful grounds and a very secluded feel. Location is tucked away from the busy feel of the city life yet is convenient to everything. We had the best spa treatments we've ever had ( and we have had our fair share) and highly recommend the spa. Fabulous!
The room was spacious and very clean. We received an unsolicited room upgrade which was very welcomed. Sheets are the only issue, a little on the thin and rough side but very adequate. 
This property is delightful and I would suggest it to anyone looking for value in a peaceful, clean and friendly property.

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “Hard Rock Does It Again!”
text:
We visited San Diego on a business trip for a convention held at the convention center. The Hard Rock is directly across the street from the convention center, a five minute walk with time to wait for the traffic lights to change. 
Driving from the airport to the hotel was an interesting challenge, if you are coming down harbor drive (in front of the convention center) you will have to circle the block because 5th Ave is one-way so you can pull in front of the hotel for valet parking. I will note, valet parking was ridiculously expensive! About $40 a day, plus tips, by far the most expensive valet parking I have ever had to pay anywhere. There is public parking which is $24 a day around the corner. 
The lobby was very modern, they were playing music when we first walked in, and behind the desk they have a wall sized LCD screen playing music videos. We got in on Saturday afternoon, the front desk quickly checked us in, and got us up to our room on the 11th floor to our room facing Petco Park. I will warn all of you, your key card is required to go anywhere in the elevator, so be sure to have it with you all the time. 
The hotel was very quiet, with the exception of Saturday night. The beds and pillows were very comfortable. The maids do not automatically come and clean the room. There is a door hanger that is two sided indicating if you are requesting a room cleaning, but the front desk explains all of this in detail upon arrival. The rooms are very clean and well set up. The mini bar and snack bar is filled with all sorts of interesting things; they had everything from red bull, vodka, reeses, to the first aid kits or a toothbrush. 
The bars downstairs were both very nice, but what really impressed me was the restaurant Mary Jane's downstairs. By far the best restaurant in the hotel! We only had a noise issue on Saturday night, due to all of the partying downstairs, I briefly visited downstairs and they had the elevator area roped off and were ID-ing guests coming in from the outside. 
The hotel is within walking of a ton of fabulous restaurants and Westerfield Plaza. The trolley stops right in front of the hotel. Overall, a great experience.

name: Hyatt Regency San Antonio
title: “Great Location”
text: I loved this location and the staff was over the top! This is right on the river walk and directly across the street is the Alamo (l block). Also 21/2 blocks from the convention center and right in the restaurant area of the riverwalk. Christmas is a fabulous time to see this! Weather was great! I got a great price on priceline for this. Don't rent a car unless you have to as the self parking garage is $27 a night!!

name: Palomar San Diego, A Kimpton Hotel
title: “Palomar (formerly Se)- Fun Boutique Hotel”
text: My husband and I stayed here on a trip for my HS reunion and loved it! It was right in the middle of the gaslamp district. We booked a Travelzoo deal and were able to upgrade to a suite for a great price. I read the reviews before we went and most of the negatives were that it was a "party hotel". Since we were going for my reunion (without our kids) that didn't bother me. We wanted something fun and close to where we were going. The suite was fabulous! Decor was great and it overlooked the rooftop pool (which turned into a nightclub). It was loud in the evening and at night but we didn't mind since we went to the club and had a great time. If you are going for a quiet, family stay I would not recommend this hotel but if you want something in the heart of the gaslamp district that is fun, this is your place.

name: Residence Inn San Diego Mission Valley
title: “Good time at the Residence Inn”
text: We read many reviews for San Diego area hotels before selecting the Residence Inn Mission Valley. Cleanliness and comfort for a good value is important to us. Our stay was 3 nights, 2 of those on the weekend. We wanted a comfortable place to lay our heads after busy days around the city. Our room was a very clean king suite with sofa bed. The mattresses on both beds were firm and the feather pillows a bit flat. We had requested extra and they were there upon arrival. There were 2 TVs which was great for the kids. Parking was included in our booking but will cost $10 per day in the lot. The spaces are small, perfect for compact cars. Continental breakfast with a french toast station and scrambled eggs. In our experience, the included breakfasts at most hotels are not great and this one met that expectation. If you like cereal and toast with a piece a fruit, it will work for you. We ate the breakfast one day, the eggs are tasteless but the french toast was pretty good. If you like to start the day with a good, healthy meal you should look for restaurants or utilize the kitchen in your suite. Sitting out by the pool with a cup of coffee or juice is a great way to start the day. We didn't use the pool however the area around it was clean and the pool appeared to be as well. We heard no traffic noise and none from surrounding rooms. We were on the 2nd floor near the stairs. It's very easy to access Old Town (visit the Old Town Mexican Cafe, it's awesome!), Sea World and not far from Coronado Island. This hotel met our needs and I would stay here again on a return trip to San Diego.

name: Old Town Inn
title: “the best customer service at any hotel i have stayed at”
text: my husband and i stayed at the old town inn in october. they were the nicest and most accomodating staff i have ever encountered. they were helpful from drugstore items i forgot, to letting my husband watch the football game after checkout before our cab took us to the airport. it was so convienent to the transportation that when we go back ( and we will!!!) we would definately stay there again and not bother with a car again. everything worked out better than i could have imagined.

name: The US Grant
title: “Charming and Elegant”
text: This downtown, centrally located hotel is charming. The entire staff from the front desk to the bellmen and valet were exceptional. Beds are very comfortable. A great hotel for conferences.

name: Palomar San Diego, A Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Gaslamp Quarter Hotel!!”
text: I love Kimpton's! Visiting San Diego for the 1st time, and my favorite hotel company has two in this city. The Palomar was beautiful, right in the Gaslamp. Restaurants, bars, shops, all in the area. Hotel has a pool - fun! Bar was great, yummy creative drinks!! Can't wait to go back!

name: Palomar San Diego, A Kimpton Hotel
title: “There's a new Kimpton in town.”
text:
The Palomar, San Diego has arrived….almost. I can say without hesitation that every contact I had with hotel staff was superb. Valet, bellstaff, front-desk, wait staff, all great. You should also know that I am a regular guest at the Solamar, the other San Diego Kimpton.
As an inner circle member I always hope, but never expect that I will be upgraded. This time I received a wonderful upgrade to a Flat on the 19th floor. I had 1,000 square feet just for me. I’ve never stayed in a Kimpton with a full-kitchen, dishwasher included (not that I was going to use it). It had a nice living/kitchen area, a large dining room table, a bedroom with a large walk in closet and 1.5 baths. Did I mention the balcony with the beautiful view of Downtown San Diego….
At the risk of sounding ungrateful, there are a few things that need to fine-tuned at the Palomar.
-Housekeeping of my particular room. The carpet in the living room was stained, really stained. It needs to be shampooed and soon. In addition, the previous guest left several items of trash in the drawers of the walk-in closet. From the receipts that were left behind and the boxes, it must have been a really wild time. When as a guest you find these things, it makes you wonder…what else isn’t clean.
-The bathroom. There are absolutely no, we’re talking zero towel racks/hooks. Strange for a hotel chain that prides itself on reduce/reuse. 
-Window coverings/drapes. There are zero blinds/drapes/window coverings in the living room/kitchen/dining area which is fine. Just be mindful that you are in full-public view. The window coverings in the bedroom are poor. If you are bothered by light, you will be very unhappy. I travel with a sleep-mask and earplugs, so I was fine.
Overall, I’ll give it a B and I would definitely stay here again.

name: Rancho Bernardo Inn
title: “Beautiful and Romantic!”
text: My Husband and I had an amazing Anniversary weekend here. The property is so quiet and beautiful. We would just walk around and get lost, it was great! The fireside lounge is awesome, make sure to check it out.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Island Palms Hotel & Marina
title: “Wish we could stay longer”
text: We took a quick trip to San Diego and stayed here for only one night. What a great hotel! We booked online and were upgraded to a room with a beautiful view (a great view of Marina!) upon arrival. The hotel room was clean and updated, bathroom had no tub, but very spacious and modern, sparkling pool and a restaurant with decent food and reasonable price. We ordered room service for breakfast and it came right on time. We're definitely going back!

name: Rancho Bernardo Inn
title: “Best overall hotel/inn experience my family has ever had!!! Service incredible !!!”
text:
The beauty of theentire establishment was very impressive. The service was unbelievably friendly - form the front desk to the coffee girls. Especially the young gentleman "Blake" , the bell hop. What a great first impression.
It was truthfully the first time in over ten years that I slept very comfortably in a 'hotel' bed.
My wife loved that there were many plugs and extra space in the room - and VERY clean.
My kids loved the many pools and fountains throughout the grounds. 
The spa was incredible and beautiful.
I thoroughly enjoyed the golf course and the helpful staff there as well.
Our dinner in the "fine dining' restaurant was top notch!! Being a restauranteur myself - I was extremely impressed with the chefs attention to detail and the knowledge of the food by the waitstaff. 
Knowing how difficult it is (first hand) to have a staff follow through with an IMAGE that owners and management want to portray - I have to totaly commend the upper management of this facility. I want to know there secret !! The staff could not have been more helpful and friendly!!!

name: Sommerset Suites Hotel
title: “Great Location & Value in the Hillcrest District”
text:
Our stay was for only one night 06/24/06, but will stay here again. The Sommerset Suites Hotel next to Mercy Scripps Hospital in the Hillcrest District of San Diego is a very nice basic hotel (like a Courtyard or Extended Stay Suites) with all of the amenties of home, Stove, Refigerator, Dish Washer, etc. The One Bedroom Suites were a little Small, with the above listed & a Reclining Chair. However, the Two Bedroom Suites were very large with a pullout sofa and the listed above. It was very roomy (larger than alot of one bedroom apts) and clean (including the refigerator, stove, microwave, cabinets, etc.), which makes it a great place to stay with kids or family members. The Hotel is south of Hotel Circle, so it's not as busy as the other places off of I-8.
The Hillside District is great for walking around, safe either at day or night, with plenty of good restuarants and night life. Skip the hotel breakfast, try Hash House A Go Go about 1/4 to 1/2 mile down from the Hotel, HUGE BREAKFAST PORTIONS it's worth the wait & you'll have plenty of left overs. The Happy Hour at the Sommerset is nice, Free Soda, Domestic Beer, Wine, Crakers, Cheese, Nachos, etc. good for the small pool or Barbaque next to it. Downtown is a 15 minute drive, Seaworld is only 10 minutes away, while the Zoo is 3 to 5 minutes by automobile.
Should you be visiting someone at the hospital, ask about the Hospital Discount while making reservations with the Hotel, there might be one?

name: Sommerset Suites Hotel
title: “A Disappointment”
text:
Pro: one-bedroom suite cost only $107/night (with the special 4+ nights stay), good location, clean rooms, full kitchen, crib already in the room when checking in, courteous staff at reception desk.
Con: VERY thin walls and floors, could hear upstair neighbor stomping around all night. We asked for a quiet room and was told that we had one, but could still hear the traffic and people in the pool. The shower temperature fluctuates frequently and in drastic range, both my husband and I almost got scalded. The hotel can really use a good renovation. The maid service is terrible: they took away dish towels without replacing them, forgot to empty trash bins under the sink, and never bothered to replace coffee/creamer/sugar etc or the paper towel. Breakfast was unimpressive, containing just coffee, muffins and pastries; plus it was all gone by the time we went down around 8:30-9am, eventhough it's supposed to be available from 6:30-9:30am. Sirens can be heard every night (about a handful of times when we were there), it woke up my two-year old one time (scared him) and I had to soothe him back to sleep. TV remote control was bad, the number buttons didn't work. Sofa bed was terrible, thin and lumpy mattress with the metal wires of the frame sticking right into your back.
Overall impression: this hotel has potential to be really good, but it just failed on so many levels.
Recommend. No, we will not stay there again.

name: Hilton San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “An okay stay”
text: Thankfully, I realized that this hotel didn't have the conjoined rooms (with a door between adjacent rooms) just in time to choose this hotel over another. What I didn't realize is that there is only valey parking (about $40/night for overnight guests) so I passed the hotel the first time around thinking there was a garage on the other side. Once we valeted the car and were checked in, everything was smooth sailing from there. The king size bed seemed a bit shorter (length wise) than most beds, but the large widescreen TV and comfy pillows made up for it. The walls are thin and I could hear people at the vending machines up the hall, but at least the hotel provides ear plugs in the room to mitigate the noise. The only annoying thing was that the bathroom door wouldn't stay open without something propping it open. The room was clean, no water pressure/plumbing issues, and I actually considered ordering room service with the decent menu. Our stay was good for one night, which is all we needed.

name: Pacific Shores Inn
title: “Excellent as always and very acommodating!”
text:
Jim was most gracious in taking care of us. I lived for 10 years just the next block over on Dixie Dr. during the '90s and whenever my housemates and I had family visit us that we could not accommodate, Jim Silver and his staff at Pac Shores were always there to take care of us as if it were our second/extra home! We always remember that and even though all of us have moved away, we always make Pac Shores our first choice whenever any of us from the Old Dixie house are in town. Jim and his staff make it feel as though we never left!
In terms of this most recent stay, Jim & Karla were super nice to accommodate me on such short notice as it was a spur of the moment weekend surf getaway for me and my girlfriend. There were no hassles for checking in, parking, storing our boards in the room (we are longboarders) & even extending our check out by one hour since the water was so warm and we wanted to have a slightly longer surf session on our last day. All the amenities were in perfect working order and even though the hotel was rather full, it did not feel crowded or imposing. The rooms are quiet and comfortable and hearing the waves crash even with the windows closed made for a very restful night after hitting a few of the old local bars well within walking distance! Thanks Jim & Karla!
I recommend staying at Pac Shores to all my friends and even random people looking for a place to stay in PB -just like when we live there. Looking forward to my next stay and many after. In fact I may be planning a surf excursion for my friends from OC & Nor Cal in the near future and also a reunion event for all the denizens of the Dixie House...
Sincerely,
Kenny Weisbart
~General Manager

name: Holiday Inn Express Sea World
title: “Great for Overnight”
text: Holiday Inn always provides good service. The rooms are basically all the same with the usual reliable amenities,service and great showers. This property is very close to Seaworld and was our first choice, so we were delighted when there was a vacancy.After dark was a bit scary as we encountered several homeless persons just crossing the road to go to Dennys.. However that would not stop me from staying here again as its not in a location where you would need to venture out at night

name: Hotel Contessa
title: “The very best place to stay on San Antonio's RiverWalk”
text: I frequently travel on business and stay in higher-end hotels. Although not associated with a 5-star chain, the Hotel Contessa deserves 5-star ratings. It simply is the most elegant, customer-oriented, value-priced hotel I have experienced anywhere. My husband and I have been here 5 nights and the staff continue to amaze me. We have been treated like royalty. The rooms are spotless, the food excellent. This morning, John and Orlando waited on us for breakfast. They quietly served us, kept our coffee cups full, and all with a very caring and professional presentation. Given the opportunity to return to San Antonio, we will stay at the Hotel Contessa and recommend it highly to all of our friends and family. It is the best!!!!

name: Holiday Inn Express Sea World
title: “Great value, friendly staff”
text: The hotel was a little difficult to find even with a GPS. If you don't take the turn immediately you will end up on the freeway and waste an abundance of time. Don't let the exterior of the building fool you.l As you enter the building you are greeted very friendly by the front desk. The reception area is tasteful, modern and the adjacent breakfast area is clean and welcoming. I had a non-smoking room which had modern furnishings, pillow top beds, fair size fridge & microwave. I wasn't impressed with the overall area however it was in close proximity to the Sports Arena and accessible to major freeways. The room was clean and the bathroom really impressed me with a granite countertop; something I wasn't expecting. The TV was the old type but they are slowing being replaced by flatscreens. I did not think the coffee pot was sanitary as it was made all of plastic and you drop the filter in as well. So when I wanted to make tea, my tea tasted terrible as it smelled like coffee or a mix of the two. Those need to be replaced by a new system with a glass carafe. The walls are relatively thin so that was a downfall if there was someone noisy next door. The hotel is fairly quiet and you do not hear the street noise.The free breakfast was great offering cereal, milk, yoghourt, juices, pancakes, toast, bagels, scrambled eggs, bacon, sausages, coffee, muffins, hard boiled eggs. There is a computer in the reception area you may use with free internet and there is an elevator in the building. My major concern would be the back door which is connected to the parking lot does not close properly which is next to the elevator as well. This is not a good security feature as if someone does not check the door behind them, it won't close properly and anyone can enter the elevator and roam the halls. The reception area has survelliance and monitors it however this is not enough. For the safety of the guests, and being the brand name holiday inn, it is imperative the door get replaced. Guests must use their room cards for the door to open however, sometimes the door sticks. I must say the hotel definitely is great value and the staff really try hard to make your stay as pleasant as possible. Keep making the improvements.

name: Hilton San Diego Resort & Spa
title: “no free wi-fi in rooms, sewer smells, no free shuttle”
text: Not business traveler friendly; no free shuttle from hotel ($50 roundtrip for shuttle or cab with tip) and no free wi-fi in rooms (free w-fi only accesssible in lobby and around pool). Rooms have antiquated plug-in internet access for a fee. Sanitary sewer smell from sink in bathroom.

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “Classy”
text: Quality staff & facilities, exceptional operation.

name: Residence Inn San Diego Mission Valley
title: “central but isolated location”
text: Agree with the previous reviews. One week stay here in april 2005. Great family hotel. Central but very isolated location. Iif you can understand this its a perfect place for families. Can't walk anywhere. Clean rooms, great breakfast.

name: Holiday Inn Express San Diego Airport - Old Town
title: “Park and Fly”
text:
We stayed here because of the convenience to the San Diego Airport and their Park and Fly package. The price is quite reasonable, too. Check in was easy and fast. The room was small, but clean, and very warm. Couldn't ever get the temp regulated enough to be comfortable. While the beds looked to be very comfortable, they were not. I found that I did not sleep well, nor did the people with whom I was traveling. Perhaps it was the temperature, but the bed seemed uncomfortable and I awoke with an aching back. 
They not only provide shuttle service to the airport and pickup upon return, but will drive you to Old Town which is close by. We used the shuttle to eat dinner in Old Town and they dropped us right at our restaurant. When we called them to pick us up, they came quickly. Pickup from the airport upon our return was very quick. 
Upon our return from vacation, they offered us complimentary breakfast as it was early morning. They have the best cinnamon rolls anyone could want. It is hard to only eat one. They are moist and flavorful. All-in-all, a good experience when you need a Park and Fly option. I would give this 3.5 stars if this option was available.

name: Hilton San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Great Hotel in a great location”
text: This hotel is reasonably priced and is in a great location a real great hotel will stay again was peaceful even during Comic con !!!! we will definitely stay here again also try the old town trolly a great way to see the town and find out your spot

name: Vagabond Inn - San Diego Airport Marina
title: “Killer location, friendly staff, clean and comfy”
text: I've averaged 45 stays per year at the Point Loma Vagabond Inn for the past 3 years and have come to love this value gem in San Diego. The front staff are extremely hospitable and courteous, the rooms impeccably clean, comfortable and utterly serviceable. Close to airport, great walks and restaurants. The pool is warm and clean. The neighbourhood is a busy location, and the fishing industry starts early, so earplugs are useful if you plan to sleep in.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Rancho Bernardo
title: “Not my favorite Courtyard”
text: I am a Marriott fan, but found this room design to be badly planned and would not stay here again. Very clean, nice facility in a nice location next to the freeway, but layout of room was awkward. Bathroom was to left as you enter room. Then must pass through narrow opening to get into main room. An oversized armchair was placed right next to this opening, requiring the chair to be moved before you could pull your suitcases into the room. We were constantly dodging this chair to enter the bathroom, and there was no space elsewhere in the room to get it out of the way.

name: Ocean Park Inn
title: “Had a wonderful stay”
text:
Stayed from June 19-21. I made the reservations with a little trepidation as Tripadvisor reviewers seemed to either rant about the hotel or rave about it. 
We had a very pleasurable stay. We had a 3rd floor, ocean front room with king bed & pull-out sofa, refrigerator, and microwave. We arrived early on the 21st, and OPI accommodated us by getting us in the room by 12:00. They also allowed us to keep our car parked in the garage until 3:00 on our day of departure so we could enjoy more beach time. 
The room was a basic hotel room but everything was functional, clean, and in good condition. While we were there, they were painting the exterior - can be a pain to deal with maintenance like this when a guest; however, the workers were circumspect, and I'm always pleased to see hotels invest in their properties, instead of just milk profits out of it. 
The balcony off the room was very tiny, but sufficient to sit and enjoy a morning coffee or evening wine. The sound of the ocean from the room is lovely. The continental breakfast is a little basic - definitely room for improvement. However, when we were there, the staff was getting instructions on a waffle machine, so there may be upgrades coming there!
Across the cul-de-sac street from the hotel was a small shop called Pacific Beach Surf Shop. They have a larger shop a block down in same complex as Hooters. Danny at the Grand Ave shop was awesome - very helpful to my son, who signed up for surf lessons. 
We enjoyed meals at Nicks and Green Flash (strong drinks!) 
One comment I'd make is that most of the boardwalk along this area are residences (small condos/hotels). I was expecting more shopping along the boardwalk than there was. I wasn't disappointed - I think it made for a quieter, more kid-friendly experience - however, it was unexpected.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Rancho Bernardo
title: “Excellent service during training class”
text: I went for a week training class and the service was top flight. Our class was so impressed we all pitched in for an extra tip for the staff at the end of the week. The last day I had a large test and they did not have any blueberry muffins at their breakfast buffet. They made a new batch and brought them to the testing room before the test for me. They really went beyond the normal with their service.

name: Hilton San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Great Convention Location, Some Incorrect Info Given by Staff”
text:
This is the PERFECT location if attending the convention center, which is across the street from the hotel. Waiting to cross the railroad/trolley tracks can be an inconvenience so just be patient! Ask for a room NOT facing the tracks and you'll have no trouble getting a good night's rest. Bed was VERY comfortable. I appreciated having a coffee maker in the room - thoughtful amenity!
The continental breakfast, $14.95, was a great value - loved the fresh fruit, delicious muffins and lots of extras for the oatmeal. Salmon and seafood stew, especially the stew, was delicious! During our 5-day stay, we were never disappointed with the food or service in the restaurant; manager Judy Francis was most accommodating and gave wonderful recommendations on wine and entrees. Wait staff was friendly and efficient.
I was, however, aggravated by misinformation given to me by some of the front desk staff. For example, when I called to check on our reservation through the convention, I asked about adding my Hilton Honors # to the reservation. I was told this couldn't be done because this was a third-party reservation. I didn't pursue the matter with the young lady at the front desk as she seemed determined that I would not get my points. I decided to wait until I checked in and would ask about the points then. When I got there, it was OK, but then when checking out, I was told I wouldn't get the points. Dah! I complained to another person at the front desk and was then told I would, indeed, get my Hilton points. During this initial phone call, I also asked about fees and storage for having FedEx boxes sent to the hotel. The same young lady told me that there were no fees. I was pleasantly surprised at this news, but then frustrated when I checked out to be charged $10.00 per box. Such misinformation by front desk staff can easily sour one's guest experience. Friends joining us for dinner were also told they had 2 hours for valet parking; the restaurant manager validated the valet parking ticket for 3 hours so we really didn't have to rush our meal after all! 
I called the hotel a few days after checking out and spoke with George, the general manager. I wanted him to know what I did and did NOT like about my recent stay. I stressed that everyone, especially the front desk staff, needs to be "on the same page" when providing information to guests. He appreciated my positive remarks and seemed concerned that, indeed, some at the front desk failed to provide accurate information.

name: Residence Inn San Diego Mission Valley
title: “hotel san diego mission valley”
text:
surclassement gratuit sur demande
le ménage quotidien des chambres n est pas impeccable
la situation par rapport à sea world et au zoo est excellente
le petit déjeuner est vraiment frugal
le parking est payant : 13 USD/jour
un excellent séjour dans l ensemble.

name: Holiday Inn Express San Diego Airport - Old Town
title: “Fab Hotel, close to Old Town”
text: We had a wonderful stay at HIX Old Town. The room was lovely and clean and surprisingly quiet, given its close proximity to the Highway/Airport. The staff were very friendly and extremely helpful. There is a free shuttle bus to the main attractions (ie Seaworld, Old Town, MSS Midway). There is also plenty of parking for your vehicle.. Old Town is within walking distance (about 5 - 10 minutes) and there are some excellent restaurants in the area.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Golf Resort San Diego
title: “No Internet that works more then 30 seconds”
text: They didn't clean my room at all. They have no wifi but in lobby and the plug in Internet that you have to pay for is horrible. You might as well have no Internet. So if you need to use the Internet don't stay here. My front door to my room was opened when I went to the room. The cleaning lady was right outside my room when I left that morning and didn't clean my room. This double tree is very old with stains on the carpet and drapies. It was water and hair on the floor of the bathroom. I travel a lot and would not recommend this hotel to anyone. The only great thing about the hotel is the location. It is a mall if stores and an overwhelming amount if restaurants . But there are other hotels in the area. I won't be back here.

name: Holiday Inn San Diego - Mission Valley
title: “Decent value at discounted price”
text:
This is an older Holiday Inn that is good in some places, and a little lacking in others. Overall, it is a decent value if you can get it at a discounted price.
Value - through Priceline, I was able to book this hotel for a three night stay 12/1-4/2006 at $45 a night. Including taxes and fees, it came to $158.85. I think this is a good value for a decent hotel in San Diego. At the regular price listed on the Holiday Inn website of $119 a night, I would prefer a newer, nicer property.
Amenities - there is a small restaurant and bar, which I didn't try. They also have a small outdoor pool and spa which looked sparkling clean. However, I felt it was too chilly to use an outdoor pool during my stay. I'd have prefered an indoor pool in December. They also have a small fitness center. In the room, there is a coffee maker, ironing board and iron, hair dryer, two phones, plus an ethernet plug for free high-speed internet access. There were no ethernet cables in the room, but you can borrow a cable from the front desk. There is no wireless internet access in the rooms, although I was told it is available in the lobby for a fee.
Mechanicals - the older Amana HVAC unit was noisy, because the plastic grill buzzed against the housing. I fixed it by partially loosening the cover. Doing that, I noticed that the foam air filter was dirty; it should be cleaned more often. The toilet sometimes required multiple flushes, which reminded me of early low-flow toilet design. There was plenty of hot water and water pressure for the shower. It had a shower-massage head that took me three days to figure out the "normal" setting. The shower surround and faucet looked dated, but everything worked. The sink and faucet just outside the bathroom looked new, and had a granite counter.
Decor / comfort - it looked like the room had been redecorated within the last couple of years, with new furniture, carpet, bed linens, curtains and wall coverings. The bed linens and towels were nice, and each bed had four pillows.
Noise - you could definitely hear hallway noise, such as people talking and doors opening and closing. It wasn't busy during my stay, so this wasn't a big issue for me. The HVAC fan helped mask noise, but it was controlled by a thermostat and thus turned on and off. This hotel is just off a freeway; I could hear a little traffic noise if I focused on it, but it didn't bother me.
Security - the neighborhood seems safe and I didn't notice any problems during my stay. However, a relative works across the street and they have had some car thefts and break-ins in the past. That business has beefed up its security and now looks like Fort Knox. I'm no expert and don't want to go into specifics on a public website, but the security could be improved at this Holiday Inn.
Parking - the main entry driveway is narrow and winding, as another poster mentioned. If you're driving a large motorhome or towing a trailer, I'd recommend you use the second entrance, which takes you around the back of the hotel. There is a handy lower-level covered parking lot in back, with an elevator to access the rooms. Parking is also limited around the entry, but abundant in the back. I found the individual parking spaces to be smaller than what I'm used to, which seems to be typical throughout San Diego.
Staff / service - I had good interaction with the staff. The front desk staff was helpful providing driving directions, and housekeeping kept the room looking great. Every day I had fresh sheets, towels, soap and shampoo, and coffee packets.
Location - it is conveniently located off of I-15 and Aero Drive. There is a Jack-in-the-Box restaurant next door along with a small strip shopping center that contains a Kinkos and a few other restaurants. If you cross to the other side of Aero Drive, you'll find a grocery store, Wal-Mart and other stores. It didn't seem particularly close to the stadium.
View - I had to take a photo of the view out of my second-floor room, which provided a scenic vista of the HVAC units arrayed across an expanse of rooftop of the restaurant and lobby. I especially enjoyed the artfully placed, crushed aluminum beverage can, thoughtfully tossed out a window by a previous guest. I was amused and not bothered, as I wasn't there to look out the window, and it is fairly typical of older Holiday Inns. However, if I was paying full price, I'd ask for a room with a nicer view.
In conclusion - I would stay here again at this price, and recommend it to others with the cautions noted above. If any of the negatives I mentioned are really important to you, I'd recommend staying at a newer property.

name: Hilton San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Conveniently located”
text:
I stayed here last week and the location is great. It is right in the gaslamp south area near the restaurants, clubs, bars, and convention center. 
The room is nice with big bathroom, but the balcony is very small. I had the view to Hard Rock hotel and it was a nice view. 
I think the strength of this hotel is the location, if you want to spend time in the downtown. That was what I did. I went to enjoy the restaurant nearby and the roof-top club at the Hard Rock hotel. Enjoyed the night and just a walk back to hotel. No drinking and driving!
The valet is a bit expensive at $40 (the only option).

name: Hilton San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Super location, great value and responsive service”
text:
We got a really terrific deal (on one of the deal sites) for a five night stay over spring break.
Pros: Excellent service, from the bellhop and front desk to the concierge and housekeeping, everyone was friendly and responsive. We requested a quiet room so our toddler could sleep better (we had heard about the train whistles, etc.) They gave us a room overlooking the Lofts on 5th, which wasn't picturesque, but was quiet! We also brought a white sound machine, just to be safe. 
We had a few other requests and needs (new cable for internet--old one didn't work, room needed to be cleaned--we were out all day to come back to unmade beds, etc.) all were taken care of promptly.
The pool and workout area were very nice and overlooked the convention center on a terrace. At night it was lovely.
The location was perfect for walking to a game at Petco Park (so fun!) and to shop and eat (Cafe Chloe and Broken Yolk were great for breakfast).
Cons: The rooms were clean, but need updating. Sheets, towels, bathroom fixtures and hardware. 
They are updating to WiFi which will be much better.
The trains are a pain, especially when they get stuck. Bells going off like crazy. Not the hotels fault, just a problem for the entire area.
Parking was $40 a night. We found a place that was $10-12 a night, more for game days, at 6th and K St--only a few blocks away. Big savings! The valets were totally cool about it. Don't feel badly about not using valet!

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Hacienda Hotel Old Town
title: “Relax, relax , relax!”
text: We stayed in the Best Western Hacienda Old Town San Diego for a quick two day getaway on a holiday weekend. I love this place! It is super nice, clean and beautiful. It is in the perfect spot within walking distance of many restaurants and shops. Our room was very nice and peaceful being at the end of the hallway. It also over looked old town San Diego and the airport/bay area. I also used the computer and printer in the lobby which was very accessible. They have a restaurant on the property which is nice in case you are tired and do not want to walk anywhere. Great hotel!!!

name: Hyatt Regency San Antonio
title: “Okay, but probably won't stay again.”
text: Hotel was a bit overpriced for the value. The coffee shop had weird hours; the lobby gets congested; the beds are VERY firm; and you really need to request a river or Alamo view because if you don't you'll be looking at rooftops with trash all over them; the pool is very small, also. However, the location is Fantastic - right on the Riverwalk and very close to downtown and the Alamo, and the rooms were clean and well-maintained. Needless to say, we won't be staying here again should we come back.

name: Hotel Contessa
title: “The Best of San Antonio!”
text: I have been to San Antonio many times and have tried all the usual top hotels. The Hotel Contessa outshines them all. There is no need to look anywhere else. The location is perfect if you want to be just a few steps away from the madding crowd on the River Walk. The rooms are beautiful suites with lovely decor and terrific bathrooms (LOVE the Aveda products). The hotel bar (Cork Bar) and restaurant (Las Ramblas) are wonderful. The rooftop pool is perfect. You will not be disappointed here.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Golf Resort San Diego
title: “Needs a renovation!”
text: Amenities such as a hair dryer that are standard in comparable hotels, are missing. The layout of the hotel makes it inconvenient to lug heavy luggage.

name: Holiday Inn Express Mira Mesa
title: “GREAT HOTEL...WOULD DEFINITELY STAY AGAIN!!!”
text:
First and foremost, the hotel is right off the freeway (Highway 15)...it made getting around the city more convenient.
The staff, especially at the front desk, were all friendly. Check in and check out were fast and easy. 
The rooms are spacious, clean, and well furnished. The rooms had a ref, microwave, hair dryer, and coffee maker. The beds were comfortable to sleep in. We slept really well even when the smoke alarm went off in the middle of the night since the battery needed to be changed. The sheets/linen were clean and seemed new. 
The parking lot gets somewhat crowded at night since they shared parking lots with Quality Inn Suites (right next door) and Dennys but it was not difficult to find parking spots. 
The complimentary breakfast was great. Hot foods were served such as biscuit and gravy, bacon, sausage, eggs, and warm cinnamon rolls. It made the stay even better. 
Overall our stay was very pleasant. The hotel was better than the expensive hotel we stayed at in Las Vegas.
I definitely would recommend this hotel to family and friends.

name: Kona Kai Resort
title: “If I had THREE wishes.......”
text:
OK, it's soooooo hot in Arizona in the summer that we ALL zip off to San Diego.
Our last stay at Kona Kai had some issues BUT rumor had that they were going to spend $1 million on renovations. 
Maybe one should ask when????
So we decided what top three things we would address ASAP.
1.) Tear out the carpets - yesterday.
Our first room was soooo disgusting that upon opening the closet door my wife almost gagged from the smell.
The second room had an odor of left over animal pee by the patio door.
What funnnnn changing rooms three times!!
Next choice room, it was not great but at this point after a long drive - just live with it!!
2.) Clear the A/C filters!!
This was a VERY hot summer in San Diego (almost 90 daily).
The a/c was absolutely required and it just would NOT cool down properly.
My wife, the Arizona native, knows air conditioning and decided to figure how to remove the ac filter for cleaning.
I find it best to back away from an upset woman.
She removed it, brought it to the tub and washed off what must have years of crud.
Just disgusting to see this had not been done for soooooo long.
What a surprise, she reinstalled and it was a beautifully cool late afternoon / early evening.
3.) Get the kitchen (food quality) and servers (lack of interest) sorted out.
If you book a room with free breakfast - bring your own instant oatmeal and heat water in your room. Take the breakfast certificates back home as a souvenir.
It is the saddest breakfast buffet and the severs have become sooooo disinterested. 
Perhaps they are receiving GREATLY reduced tips and are just going thru the motions. 
Dunno but someone step in, please.
They have cleaned the mold from the outside of the building since our last stay.
Room decor is still '80's with big 'ol tube TV.
VERY nice pool and grass area adjacent.
You MIGHT want to rethink this as a "Resort". Just sayin.....

name: Kona Kai Resort
title: “Quiet Modest Resort”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights. Booked it through Bookit.com. They do charge $15 a day for parking & you need your hotel room key to open the gate. 
It's good for families. The rooms are clean and they have comfy beds. They have a fridge in the room. The outside structure does need some updating. It looks a little weathered, but it's a great location. Across the street is a great sidewalk that is along the water which is great for walking or running. 
We stopped by their restaurant to check out the menu and everything was over priced for how they were running it. We had much better meals out. We ate one night at the Japanese restaurant - Umi Sushi. Great service and one of the best places to eat sushi. Red Sails is good for Seafood. Old fashioned seafood restaurant. We ate outside on the deck. We both had grilled fish that was very good. There is a Vons & Trader Joes grocery stores down the street in a shopping center where we picked up misc. items for snacks, breakfast (muffins & fruit) & etc. The shopping center also has a pizza place, Panera and we ate one night at Five Guys. 
The housekeeping staff were always fast and friendly if we needed something. The front desk person the night we checked in wasn't very friendly or helpful or not what was going on in the area. I stopped by the desk the next night and their was a different lady there with blonde hair who was very friendly & helpful. 
There is a pool for swimming. The beach is just for tanning or for kids to play. It's located right on the boat channel, so not good for swimming for little ones. We drove over to the Sunset Cliffs & beach two of the nights to watch the sunset. 
Easy place to get on the HWY to travel around San Diego. We took the kids to the San Diego Zoo & San Diego Safari Park.

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel San Diego - Mission Valley
title: “4th year staying here for 4 days of FUN!”
text:
Every year I and several hundred of my friends descend upon this hotel in August for lots of fun and frolic. From the moment I check in at the front desk, I'm greeted warmly and staff even remember me from last year! Never had that before at a hotel. The bell staff are great and lug every one's stuff to their rooms (and each cart is FULL to the MAX). The rooms are clean and my calls to the front desk always answered. My event is LOUD, BUSY and I'm sure A LOT of work for the staff. They meet every demand and with kindness. Their conference rooms are have comfy chairs and come in various sizes to meet all needs. The sushi bar is tasty and it's nice have a full service restaurant and a to go coffee shop on sight. You can also got a microwave/fridge in your room if you ask. 
I don't often stay at Crowne Plaza hotels, but this one goes all out for their guests and I should probably stay more often!

name: La Quinta Inn San Diego Scripps Poway
title: “Good value, but slightly scruffy hotel.”
text:
This La Quinta is perched above Highway 15 with some of the rooms facing directly on to this road. 
As La Quinta's go this one seems a bit rougher around the edges than most. Rooms are clean and comfortable but the public areas are a bit worn.
Pool is good - right temperature and a good size. Free internet which is a big plus and the breakfast is the usual La Quinta fare.
OK overall for the price.

name: Holiday Inn Express Mira Mesa
title: “Sparkling clean, good service, comfortable room”
text: We spent two nights at the Holiday Inn Express. We were delighted with the overall service provided, the friendliness of the staff, and were especially impressed with the cleaniness of the entire facility. The Express is close to shopping and entertainment, but quite a trek to downtown San Diego. We give this hotel a "two thumbs up" and would stay there again.

name: Motel 6 San Diego Downtown
title: “Great location, great staff, great time”
text: Firstly, this is a Motel 6 not a Radisson or Hilton, so some perspective, but we loved it here. The staff have been friendly and helpful, providing tourist information and answering any questions with humour and politeness. Our room was immaculate, cleaned every day and the bed was comfy, couldn't ask for anymore. The location is great, equi-distant from Little Italy and the Gaslamp and an easy walk for all but the laziest guest. Free parking, free coffee and a minute of the interstate. Go Motel 6 !!

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Hacienda Hotel Old Town
title: “MAKE SURE YOUR RATE AT CHECK OUT IS THE SAME AS CHECK IN!!!!!!!!!!”
text: The hotel was very beautiful and yes the restaurant staff was great, but I agree the front desk staff needs a lot of work. I was given a price (as a walk up) of $110.00 for a room with 2 queen beds plus $12.00 for parking ( Why? Where are you going to put your car if not in the hotel garage?) + $5.00 Resort fee + $2.50 for some other stupid fee and at time of check it jumped up to $131.00 + all the other fees. They said the night auditor found a mistake and corrected with never saying a word to me about. YOU SIGN FOR AN AGREED RATE AT TIME OF CHECK IN, YOU SHOULD PAY THE SAME RATE AT CHECK OUT!!!!! The staff and GM are very rude. The GM Laughed that I was complaining over $20.00 a night difference. They can blow their hotel out of their fanny for all I care. I will stay in a fleabag hotel before I will stay there again!!!

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel San Diego - Mission Valley
title: “Comfortable hotel. So-so location.”
text:
Good stay. Comfortable hotel. The only cons would be the charge for parking and the location. I booked this hotel through a discount service where I didn't know the hotel before I bid. I thought I got quite a good rate until I read the reviews and realized I would have to pay $12/day for parking. That turned a good rate into only an ok rate. I did not have to pay for internet since the clerk at check in comped me. I guess they have the discretion to do that. The clerk may have been nice to me because my room wasn't ready at first and I was going to have to wait an hour. I was willing to wait since it was only about noon and way before the scheduled check in time. 
I loved the room. Great view. On the side away from the freeway. Fridge and microwave. 
I'm not a fan of the hotel's location, Mission Valley. It's a rather isolated tract of hotels and a few low rent restaurants. So if you're looking for a romantic or interesting setting, consider the beach or other neighborhoods. On the other hand, you have quick access to all the major freeways in San Diego. So driving is pretty good. If you don't have a car, this place would be bad though. Stay downtown instead.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Hacienda Hotel Old Town
title: “Lovely Courtyards”
text: This is a great hotel complex on a hillside with lovely courtyards and fountains. With multiple buildings stepping up the hillside, it is easy to get lost in the quaint planted courtyards if you don't pay attention. The rooms are basic with a comfy bed and a character befitting the California Mission style of the complex. And the walking distance proximity to Old Town is ideal. The hotel restaurant lacks prompt service. But, luckily there are plenty of higher quality restaurants nearby in Old Town. I was pleased to see recycling bins in the rooms. However, their shower product bottles were not recyclable, indicating a serious lack of basic corporate environmental responsibility. Additionally, I was not able to connect to the high speed internet either in the room or by Wi-Fi in the courtyard. But I didn't feel like calling the front desk to resolve the problem. So, I suppose I shouldn't hold it against them.

name: E-Z 8 Motel Old Town
title: “At least it was clean”
text: I chose this motel because it was cheap. The internet price was only $55 for 3 people in one room with 2 queen sized beds. I also liked the free wifi promised on the website. When we got there we found out that the wifi was only free in the lobby. Since I did not purchase the wifi, I could not check the website to find out that it did, indeed promise wifi in the rooms. I have yet to find contact information to a main office to complain about that. Also, this motel was not quiet. The neighbors were noisy at all hours. The rooms were, indeed, clean. However, the room did not smell fresh. My son complained about an odor, but i did not notice it.

name: Mission Bay Motel
title: “Good Location by the Beach”
text:
Well, having stayed at this location several times over the past 7 1/2 years, I am surprised that neither I nor anyone else has written about it. Well, ok...perhaps that MIGHT be, because there truly isn't much to say? 
The Mission Bay Motel is simply what it sounds like. A Motel. It has quite a few years on it, ( Oh, I'd venture a guess of about 30 years or more) and offers few "extras" or amenities as you might expect in most Hotels or other Motels ( ie; Days Inn, Motel 6, etc). The rates I have paid vary anywhere from $60 up to $160 depending upon the time of year and the room. Romms seem to vary from a single ( which are located on the western side of the property both up and downstairs ( 2 level establishmant) to the room with 3 beds( no, not a 3 bedroom...1 room --- 3 beds) with a kitchenette( actually a stove and a mini-fridge with some supplied utentils). You are not really paying for the simpleness of this location ( though there is a small pool directly behind the office on the Mission Blvd with a fence around it) but more so for the location......one block from THE BEACH!!. There is also a Hooter's Restaurant directly across the street and up the stairs. There is also one of the best bars for sightseeing in Southern California called La Heina's ( located ON the beach boardwalk and slightly to the south) which is touted as the ONLY open deck bar in California located on the Boardwalk. I sure would love to know if this is true, but aftre a couple hours there you forget why you are there. 
Back to the Motel, though, there is no ice machine, there is no soda machine, there are no vending machines. There is a liquor store on the same block just to the south. There is a Burger King JUST to the North across the street. There is a Tony Roma's restaurant across the steet, as well as a couple of fantastic breakfast eateries ( make sure to visit The Eggery for early morning breakfast). 
The Motel does offer both smoking and non-smoking rooms, but of course I can only tell you that I have seen smoking rooms during all but 1 of my stays. One time I did have to stay in a non-smoking room which I hated, but respected by stepping outside to smoke. I can't say how often that practice is followed, so be prepared. 
All the rooms have a color tv with a remote and get basic cable ( about 60 or so channels) and HBO only. They do have a little clock radio with AM/FM but you'd be better served to do as I do and bring a Boom-Box and CD's ...after all...you are at the beach!! You may wish to bring your cooler or a mini-fridge to store soda, beer, ice in. You depending on how long you are staying, you may even want to bring a mutli-outlet as they only have a couple of outlets in the rooms.
Speaking of, one of the BEST things about staying at the wonderfully simple motel, is not the name, the service, the maids, but something MUCH more.The LOCATION!! Think of it this way. you are in Pacific Beach...you can go drinking on Garnet St and walk back to your room ( 4 blocks) and not worry about drinking and driving. You can also get a room as I do on most holiday weekends ( unless I am in Vegas) and go enjoy yourself with beer on the beach and make or take at least ONE good reliable friend who will watch your belongings on the beach while you walk ONE BLOCK back to your room to use your own BATHROOM.
See what a worthwhile investment it is? No drinking and driving, good location, parking is ok except for on weekends . Most get parking in front of their rooms. Some may have to park on the north end of the Motel or on the street. Holiday weekends parking is insane, so if you are there on a Friday, my advice is DO NOT LEAVE. Take a taxi to downtown for about $25 bucks, a bus ( which stops in front of the motel) or walk. If you live in town, just take a cab down, why bring the car? 
If you have kids, be preapred as this is a beach area and sometimes the language and scenery can be a bit R-rated, but not too. Police try and keep a good job on things, but as in any college town, summer destination, where you have women , men ( well..young men) ,
beach and beer well....sometimes you need a little extra help.
 The staff at this motel is wonderful though sometimes a little tired from long hours trying to help guests and keep an eye on things. They always keep fresh coffee in the office and a number of flyers for out of town guests to use for sightseeing around the area.
Simply put, this is in my opinion, a great value for your money. If you need glitz and glamour, there are other hotels/motels around the way, but if, like me, you care for a tv, a locked door and convience, this is your place. In all of my stays, I have never seen any pests of any sort...so that has never been an issue. At least for me. As many times as I have been there, I have never once had any problem other than a problem with a backed up toilet which was repaired quickly.
Lots of foreigners tend to stay here I would imagine because of "Location" and "Zonies because.....It's near water. Not sure what a 'Zonie is? Ask when you check in...
Have Fun

name: Hyatt Regency San Antonio
title: “All round good stay”
text:
Let me get this out of my system first. When you book a room in this hotel no this, there is NO rooms for smokers. They will however let you book a smoking room before arrive and when you check in the break the bad news. If you're a non smoker then dont panic the hotel does offer a lot. 
Hotel rooms are a good size and the photo's on the web site are exactly what you get. Which for a change is quite refreshing. Each room looks across at other rooms so keep your curtains closed and this also leads to a lot of noise during the day. Now lets talk location, it is excellent. You can see the Alamo only around one block from the main entrance and its right in the heart of the riverwalk area, so all you couple outs there this could be for you. The pool does boast a roof top pool, I did go up to view in be didnt use it as it was quite small so you may want to skip this. The rates for this hotel were quite reasonable but parking is around $20 or so a day. Dont bother with valet parking what a waste of money and its right beside the hotel. There is also a rumor that the valate guys have light fingers and like to steal from you cars. So be smart. Other than that you'll enjoy this hotel and I would say that I would tsay here again.

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “Bachlorette's Love the Hardrock”
text:
Hardrock San Diego is designed for young people who want to a blast. I went down with 5 of my friends for a bachlorette party and we had a complete blast. The staff went above and beyond to make you feel like you were a rock star. From the bell hops to the resturants to the room, everything was amazing.
Pros:
Large Rooms
Amazing Staff
On site food and Clubs are a blast
Cons: 
Pool is small and charges for the best locations at the pool on weekends
Staff at the pool not nearly as good as the staff throughout the hotel
Not a good place to bring your kids

name: Howard Johnson Inn - San Diego
title: “Not exactly a five”
text:
The rooms were nice, the service fine. But Friday night partiers outside the room at 2 am, yelling and swearing... not good. Another man and his woman fighting in parking lot 2 days later.
And the continental breakfast was pathetic. Frosted Flakes cereal, milk, rolls in plastic and coffee seems like the absolute minimum to qualify for the name.

name: Howard Johnson Inn - San Diego
title: “do not stay here”
text: bring your gun you will need it , also no sleep people at all hours of the night coming and going,also this place is like camping, not really camping would be cleaner really do not go here

name: Bay Inn and Suites
title: “Hotel NOT nice for the price you pay!”
text: My family & I stayed At Bay Inn & Suites expecting this place to be nice but when we arrived I knew we had made a bad choice.The rooms were small, carpet was in need of cleaning, we were watching TV when all of a sudden it shut off by itself & NO, IT DID NOT HAVE TIMER ON. It did not work period...TV was making sounds like it was trying so hard to turn on, but couldn't do it. I called the front desk & they were suppose to have sent a maintenance person up but person never showed up, I checked out before they arrived. People please do not let the pictures or the name of the place fool you. Stick to motel 6 if you need a room that is cheap, you will over pay at Bay Inn. My family & I were VERY disappointed. We over payed for this type of place.

name: Hotel Occidental
title: “so grim.”
text: I have stayed at places like this before, and thought they were fine--this one is just a little too cheerless for me.
