The tiny cubicle of a room, the airplane flight path directly overhead, the street noise and light that the miniblind just could not deal with, the lack of anywhere to eat right around the hotel, no bathtubs (showers only)--I just couldn't do it. I had reserved 7 nights there, left after one. The staff, esp. Ecaterina on the swing shift, were very pleasant and helpful, and if you are totally prepared and aware of what you're getting, it would be fine. I realized for me, it was not enough.

name: Howard Johnson Inn - San Diego
title: “Great Value”
text: Located in the hotel circle area of San Diego. Great value property. The room was equipped with a refrigerator, microwave, tv, hairdryer, iron, and a safe all for under $80 including tax.

name: Mission Valley Resort
title: “San Diego on the Cheap”
text: Recently, while on a business trip, I booked two nights at the Mission Valley Resort. My company had put me up in a expensive down-town hotel for two nights and I elected to stay on my own dime for a few days just for a little R&R. The company paid hotel was $200/night. I could go on and on about the differences, some slight some not so slight but in the end, Mission Valley Resort was safe, clean and centrally located. It had ample room for me to park my car, a nice swimming pool and a really, really convenient family restaurant and shop connected to it and with the money I saved, I was able to buy and eat like a king in La Jolla and Laguna Beach. I guess you could say, I did San Diego on the cheap.

name: Harborview Inn and Suites
title: “False Advertising”
text:
The information provided by this hotel offers a clear example of false advertising. This hotel provided no bar, breakfast, or hotel shuttle. In fact, when I enquired about the shuttle I was told they did not provide this service. The manager, or it least I believe it was the manager, did say she could arrange transport for $25. I organized a taxi on my own that cost $10.
In addition, the rooms were in desperate need of attention. There was even an uncleaned ashtray in my non-smoking room.
I only stayed for one night, though reserved a room for three nights. Of course, my credit card was billed for the entire time despite my pleas. I have contacted my credit card company emphasizing the false advertisement.

name: Surfer Beach Hotel
title: “AWFUL, Gross and no air conditioning.”
text: Don't waste your money.. We went there for our 25 anniverary, and OMG it was AWFUL. First off they lost our reservations... even when I gave the women our confirmation number she couldn't find them.. She did get us a room with an ocean view, we get to the room and it looked gross. You know its bad, when my husband came out of the bath room and said.. DON'T take a shower WITH OUT your flip flops on.. My gym has better looking showers!!!! There is no air conditioning.. Our room had the "saftey light" on the balcony NO TURNING IT OFF.. so we couldn't leave the sliding glass door open for some AIR we were on the third floor.. (there was an old rusted fan in the room.. does nothing without cool air) but we couldn't sleep with a bright light on.. It was just awful.. so at 1230 am (7 hours after checking in) we checked out and went across the street to Best Western..

name: Beach Haven Inn
title: “Avoid spring break, but otherwise OK”
text: A decent enough place: rooms are clean, location can't be beat, price is right, staff is nice. Don't make the mistake of going there (or anywhere near Pacific Beach, for that matter!) during Spring Break, though, unless you're there to party :-) Don't waste your time at the "continental" breakfast.

name: San Diego - Days Inn Harbor View / Airport / Convention Ctr
title: “proche de tout et confortable!”
text:
cet hôtel est situé à 30 min à pieds de l'aéroport, il donne sur la marina (juste une route à traverser), où il est très agréable de faire son jogging ou de se balader, au bout se situe le seaport village, super mignon et on y mange très bien. Situé à 5 min à pieds du trolley, qui mène à la vielle ville, aux quartiers touristiques (ils sont cependant accessibles à pieds en 30-45 min maximum!), à la frontière mexicaine pour les outlets (45 min de trolley). Le zoo est à 1h30 de marche ou à 30 min de trolley/bus. On peut prendre le ferry sur la marina 15 min à pieds depuis l'hôtel pour aller passer la journée sur l'île du coronado). IL y a plusieurs magasins de location de voiture autour de l'hôtel, accessibles à pieds, bon marché. La plage de la Jolla n'est qu'à 30 min de voiture et vaut le détour. Los Angeles est à 2h de route, et la magnifique plage de Santa Monica est sur la route pour LA. L'accueil à l'hôtel est super, ils renseignent très bien les touristes. Le petit déjeuner est copieux et compris dans le prix expedia, nous n'avons rien payé en surplus. La chambre est faite tous les jours. Une navette est mise à disposition à n'importe quelle heure pour le départ vers l'aéroport au retour, il suffit de la réserver la veille (gratuit).
Bref: très bon séjour dans cet hôtel, même le bruit du trolley ou du train qui passent tout prêt, ou des avions, n'est pas gênant car l'isolation est bonne (il suffit de fermer les fenêtres!! d'autant que les chambres sont climatisées).

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “Disappointed ... and not sure why”
text: I was expecting something special from this hotel and it just didn't deliver. The room was okay - nice tv, ipod docking station, small bar to drink the $40(!!!) vodka or munch the $4(!!!) chocolate bars. My room was on a lower floor overlooking the street, which although not of the harbour, the view was a good street view with large windows. But was the room better than a Sofitel or Westin or equivalent? The answer is no, just smaller if anything with no bath. The hotel tries so hard to be trendy it fails - the downstairs bar is just full of suits straight from the conference centre across the road, the restaurants are overpriced (and except Nobu have no reason to be), the spa is (yet again) very expensive. Location is perfect, valet parking is expensive, internet (if not in your room rate) is very expensive. The resort fee adds to the price ($17 a night for what?). I like nice things and don't mind and can afford to pay, but I like to feel like there is value for money - which this hotel does not provide. The Gaslamp district has an array of restaurants and nightlife and entertainment a lot more entertaining and better value than this hotel provides.

name: Motel 6 San Diego Hotel Circle
title: “Don't even think about it”
text: RUDE RUDE RUDE! My husband and I made reservations at Motel 6, based upon proximity to the airport, for our arrival date. We called to confirm the day before our departure and they said they didn't have a reservation for that day but they had one for the week prior. Now, of course, they made a mistake because we knew what day we were arriving in San Diego (from New york) yet they refused to acknowledge their mistake, screamed at my husband on the phone and then proceeded to charge our credit card out of spite. (The ordeal has since been rectified by Motel 6 customer relations but only after the San Diego establishment fought it). Don't stay here!!!! La Pensione in little Italy is close by, cheap and pleasant, with a great coffee house nearby.

name: Quality Inn Airport SeaWorld Area
title: “Low Quality Inn”
text: My one major complaint throughout my stay was a sewer water-like stench coming from the bathroom. The water was shut off throughout the building for about an hour at one point. I'm sure it was for maintenance issues but why take the chance. The whole place just looks unmaintained. Daily servicing of the room was good. There is a $5 a day parking fee. The parking lot is very small, so finding parking on the hotel lot is not garanteed. Would have dished out a little more $$ for a little for quality.

name: Ramada Plaza
title: “Family vacation”
text: We stayed a week at the Ramada Plaza. We chose this hotel for two reasons. We wanted to be in the hotel circle area, which is close to all attractions with easy freeway acess. We had stayed in the hotel circle area about 6 years ago, at a different hotel. The second was price. We went through a travel agent and the package price was under $90 per night with two queen beds. Ramada has a good reputation, and we were banking on it. Rather than trying a hotel we have never heard of. The hotel staff were very good and freindly. The room was a good size, with a fridge and micro, and a very sm. one cup coffee maker. The bathroom area had two sinks, one in the bath with the tiolet and nice shower with full sized tub. The other in a dressing area, which made it much easier for two people to be getting ready at once in the morning. Very nice comfy beds, comforters and four fluffy pillows to each bed. Just right for watching TV in bed and proping your back up. Free parking was good, most of the time we parked right by the door. The restaurant on property was too exspencive, and had very limited menu items. We did buy dessert one night to take up to our room. Big mistake...two cups of ice cream, and one piece of chocolate cake, $18.00+ tax. There is a little store down the street that has just about all you need, at resonable prices. There are two great restaurants we found on hotel circle. Adam's and Abbie's just to the east of the hotel same side of the street and Hunter steak house, just on the otherside of the freeway both are very close by. Great food, and excellent service at both. They have a nice laundry there. We had to wash clothes half way through our stay. The desk has soap for $1.25, the washers and dryers are new and commercial grade. They only cost a $1.00 each. Very reasionable, and efficeint. I happend to do laundry on Wed. night, and was surprised to find a extra special treat. They have a food and beverage reception every Wed. night. They have wine and beer, sodas, cheeses, friut and vegies, crakers. We were dissapointed with the pool and jaccuzzi(sp?) area. On the web sight you see a lg. pool lots of chase lounge chairs, and nice surroundings. The reality is a very small area, even smaller pool which only goes from 3ft. to 4.5ft. , the jaccuzzi's bubbles were sad, lots of noise and not much power. Only 3-4 chase loung chairs, two umbrella tables one with benches and one only had one chair. Not much vegitation, a few tall trees on one side. Pluses for the pool area were that both were clean, warm, and hot. Plenty of pool towles, and a phone to call for more if they run out. They do have a computer in the lobby area you can use. Don't plan on being able to use it unless you like to wait. The sign says 15 min. limit, and is not inforced. If you have a laptop bring it, they do have internet in the rooms. We just don't have a laptop, and needed directions from time to time. Over all we had a very nice stay. We had a room in the back (ask, if you want one that is quiet, and closest to the pool) if you want a fridge and micro you have to ask for that as well as a no smoking room. I would recomend this hotel for the most part, would really be nice if the pool area was better. If you don't care much about swimming and such, it is a great place to stay.

name: Super 8 Motel San Diego / Sea World
title: “Not the greatest”
text: Stayed at Super 8 for a couple of days; some of the rooms smelled like cat litter and others were very small. Not much room to move around with all the furniture they try to put into some of the rooms. Our room had an unwanted pest (cock roach) in it, one night and also heard another member of our party had the same thing. Hotel was re-done but still has more work to do. Hard to also park in the parking lot with a staircase, on both sides of the building protruding out into the parking lot. Other hotels next store, look way better (like Great Western). Would not suggest this hotel with the type of people that come there. Had a derelict next to us; had door and window always open. Was drunk and bedding was totally stripped and didn't care.

name: Comfort Suites Mission Valley
title: “Broken AC, staff/management did not help”
text: We recently stayed at this hotel. We checked in around 1:30pm. Most hotel rooms are stuffy and hot when first entering them. We started the AC unit and fan and left the room. We returned around 8:45pm and the room was still hot! Our friends were staying in the adjoining room and I walked into their room to see if their AC was working the same. Their room was cold and they didn't even have the fan on. We called the front desk and they said they would send someone up. 30 minutes pass and we receive another call asking what the problem was. I explained again and was told someone would be up...again. 1 hour later, maintenance finally shows up and proceeds to tell us that nothing is wrong with the AC unit. 30 minutes later, the front desk calls back and says there is nothing wrong and nothing they can do for us and that they would put a note in our file. It is now 11pm and we had 2 children with us. We had no choice, but to endure the night. We were NEVER even offered another room. The next morning I asked to speak to the manager. I was told she was not in and would not be in until the next day. The front desk clerk said she could only refund the $8 parking fee. I explained the refund was not sufficient. The clerk said she could call her manager(Elizabeth Ming) on her cell phone. The manager answered the phone call and stated that we would have to contact her the next day when she returned. I asked the clerk to refund the parking fee to start with and I would speak with her manager the next day. The clerk proceeded to tell me that she could no longer refund the $8 parking fee! I called the next day and spent 2 hours being hung up. I was told she was with a customer and would help when she was done. I was on hold for 40 minutes! I hung up and called back and was told she had gone to lunch! I asked the clerk(Davina) to call her on her cell phone and find out when she would be back. The clerk said she called, but got no answer. I asked her to call again and I was put on hold. I hung up and called back and another clerk(Cedrick) said they had customers in front of them that they needed to help. What about me?! I was the customer just yesterday and received no help from anyone there! I asked for the corporate number and Davina said they had no corporate office and Elizabeth Ming was who I needed to speak to. I spent 3 hours trying to get the problem resolved. Lauralee at the corporate office was extremely helpful and had my problem and refund resolved in less than 30 minutes! I WILL NEVER STAY HERE AGAIN!!! And I plan on letting everyone know what horrible staff they have working at this hotel!

name: California Suites Hotel
title: “GREAT HOTEL.”
text:
My room had alot of closet space,also came with a microwave and fridge,,and the kids liked the heated pool an spa..also it was all gated in very safe an secure..Also proved a very nice continental breakfast bar.
Not far from seaworld and the beach

name: California Suites Hotel
title: “Good Value for the Money”
text: The hotel is clean and affordable. The courtyard is as pretty as the pictures on their website. It's in a quiet, safe neighborhood and is within 15 minutes of the zoo, Sea World, and multiple beaches. The ladies in the office are friendly but somewhat inefficient. My only gripes are you can't flush the toilet more than once every half hour because the tank takes so long to fill, the shower head is only about 5 feet above the bottom of the tub, and the room had a musty smell. The internet is $6.95/night and it's not wireless. The breakfast is coffee, juice, bagels, and cereal. Fortunately, we got a room that didn't face the pool. We walked by the pool several times in the evening and there was always a group of people and they were usually loud enough to disturb sleep. I would recommend this hotel if you're on a budget but make sure you request a room away from the pool area.

name: Mission Valley Resort
title: “Best Value I have ever had”
text: I recently went on vacation with my family to San Diego. The Mission Vally Resort far exceeded my expectations. The staff were extremely friendly and the rooms were exceptionally clean, not to mention it was very easy to get everywhere we wanted to go! I would definately reccemmend it to famalies that are on a budget.

name: Ramada Plaza
title: “Refrigerador”
text: A pesar de que pedí refrigerador a mi llegada y al día siguiente, no tuve habitación con refrió, el ultimo día me comentaron que me podía cambiar de habitación para tener refri... Información que me pudieron dar deseque que me registre. También se descompuso el aire acondicionado a ña media noche y el único comentario fue cambies e de habitación a otra lejos viendo que tenía dormidos a los niños, esa no es una solución aceptable

name: California Suites Hotel
title: “Nice Hotel”
text: My husband and I stayed for 2 nights, it is nice hotel, clean, good size for 1 or 2 adults, in a good area near convinance stores and restaurants, will stay here again if in the area, very friendly staff and eager to please.

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel San Diego - Mission Valley
title: “One night stay”
text:
I just came back from my one night stay at the Red Lion Hanalei Hotel. 
It was a nice/clean room on the first floor. Larger then I expected and right next to an atrium with a waterfall and Koi pond. Bathrooms were clean, bed seemed clean, and housekeeping was great! Room service not all that bad considering they were completely booked. Everyone was courteous and next time I go to SD I would def. go back to this hotel. 
I loved it!

name: Mission Valley Resort
title: “The worst ever!!”
text: This hotel was the worst one I have ever stayed in. Many family members stayed here since we were attending a wedding that was held at the "resort". The room smelled like a boys locker room. It was dirty, the wallpaper was peeling, we had ants in the bathroom. The linen was very old and thin. Other family members had similar rooms. Several of us complained and were told if we didn't like it we could just leave. Unfortunately our rooms were already paid for. Do yourself a favor and stay anywhere else!

name: Days Inn & Suites - Sea World/Airport
title: “We found our stay great!!”
text: Upon arrival to the hotel the front desk clerk was not very personable but after a few minutes she seemed to warm up. I did not let that first impression make any sort of impact on me. I thought the hotel was clean, had everything we needed & most importantly the kids had fun in the pool. It is very centrally located for everything we needed. Close shopping and all freeway exits but everything you need is within walking distance. The added bonus of the hot breakfast was more than we could have asked for. I will not dispute that fact that there are some areas of the hotel that do need updating but I am certain that will come. I would not hesitate to stay again.

name: Good Nite Inn Sea World
title: “Okay Hotel”
text: Stayed here twice. Its a hotel where you get what you pay for. The blanket on the bed had hairs on it but the room and bathroom was clean. The front desk employees were all very nice and willing to help. There aren't any hair dryers or any other great amenities but is an ok hotel for staying a couple nights. The tv worked but had lines running through it and made sounds, better than nothing. I will give the housekeeping ladies an A+ because they were working hard and were there to help when needed. Plenty of parking and the hotel is close enough to things. Overall, I wouldn't stay here long but an ok place to stay for a short time.

name: BEST WESTERN Golden Triangle Inn
title: “The power of Trip Advisor”
text:
Good freeway access. Easy to get to La Jolla or Mission Bay. Room good size, clean, somewhat worn. Parking for cars only, no cars with trailers. No view, no pool. Second floor, end units best. Standard Danish and coffee breakfast. Requested non-smoking room, room reeked of smoke. Use Febreeze.
Receptionist was having protracted argument with both customers in line ahead of me. Expedia had not forwarded their reservations. Instead of trying to solve this issue, she was sarcastic and very argumentative with them. When I walked up to her, her greeting consisted of "What's your name?" With no further word, she located my reservation, literally tossed my keys to me and disappeared into the back office. So much for a welcoming greeting.
The room has a cube refrigerator (you defrost),TV, tub and shower, pretty basic Best Western stuff. The bed was made without a fitted bottom sheet. The maid used a top sheet for the bottom sheet (top sheets are smaller than bottom sheets). Naturally, whenever I rolled over the bottom sheet came undone and in short order wrapped around me. Impossible to sleep as everytime I rolled over I had to reset the bottom sheet. I mentioned this to the front desk the next morning and they said they would have the maid put a fitted sheet on. That evening I discovered she again used a top sheet and shorted the sheet so that a good third of the end of the mattress had no bottom sheet. I re-made the bed. Next morning, same promise. I asked to be given the bottom sheet, I would put it on myself. I was handed a mattress pad. I asked the receptionist if her life depended on it, could she tell me what it was. She said she did not know. So much for knowledgeable staff. She suggested that if I wanted a fitted bottom sheet I should go to Walmart and buy one. That's just what I did. On leaving I mentioned that I was really put off by the reception I received and the bed linens. The response I got was basically, "Yeah, that's too bad". Then inspiration struck: I told them I was going to review their hotel on Travel Advisor. Almost INSTANTLY the manager/franchise owner appeared. After listening to my concerns with an obviously well practiced show of well practiced professional sympathy he offered to take 10% off my bill, which covered the cost of buying a fitted bottom sheet. I asked him if he thought it was inappropriate for hotel guests to provide their own linens. He stated that "No Best Western provides fitted bottom sheets". Of course his statement is nonsense. In checking with Best Western's corporate offices they said each Best Western is individually owned and the bedding type is determined by each owner. The customer service rep seemed taken aback that they were using top sheets instead of fitted bottom sheets. The owner's explaination of the rude reception I received was "Well, that's a good reason not to make your reservation through the internet". Huh? I told him I made my reservation directly through his hotel and still received a rude reception. I understand it's not the Four Seasons, but his staff is still presumptively in the hospitality business, they just don't know this.
So, if you want reasonably priced, good location-- bring your own sheets, know how to defrost a refrigerator and be prepared for anything from rude to indifferent service from the staff.

name: Wyndham Garden San Diego near SeaWorld
title: “Great service”
text: Excellent place to stay. I didn't know what to expect, especially since this trip was not planned, but I was pleasantly surprised with guest service. My family and I will stay here again. Thanks.

name: Kona Kai Resort
title: “What a relaxing experience!”
text: My wife and I decided to stay at the Kona Kai Resort over the Labor Day weekend with our 7 year old daughter. We had made plans to watch the Hawaiian Luau show that Kona Kai runs on Fridays in the summer and then stay the balance of the weekend. First off, checking in and parking were a breeze and very efficient. When I entered the lobby to check in, the first thing I noticed was the warm Spanish Villa styled lobby area. The huge fireplace, cushy chairs and couches, and warm tones immediately put me in a good mood. We were greeted by the manager Dennis Vinegas who assured us that our stay would be memorable (and he was right). Our bellman, then helped us to our room and took care of our baggage...he was so fast that he actually beat us to our room (I still don;t know how he did it!). When we got to our room, we noticed that we had a great view of the main courtyard and pool, as well as the marina (and a nice balcony to take it all in)...what a specatacular view. After settling in , we saw the Luau/Hula show which was fantastic...the food was delcious, in particular the Kahlua Pork and the Lomi Lomi Salmon..I have to admit I went back for seconds and thirds! The show was very nice, with children and adult perfomers and even two fire dancers...The next day,(Saturday) we awoke and had breakfast in the main dining room. Again, it was a very comforting place, with it's vaulted turret ceiling and beautiful views of the Shelter Island Marina...and the food was plentiful and freshly prepared..and most importantly, served efficiently and courteously. The wait and bus staff was qucik to cater to our every need. Later, we went to hang out at the pool and jacuzzi and spent the bulk of the day just lounging and relaxing. The hotel has a pool cocktail/food server and we definitely took advantage of their services. The Calamari and the Mojitos are a must-try.by the pool. We had dinner offsite that night (another story which is not so nice...I won't mention the place). But we made it back in time for a nice evening soak in the jacuzzi and for our daughter to play on the playground adjacent to the pool before heading to bed. Thewre were other families in that area with a fire going in the firepit on site which gave the evening a real "clambake" celebratory feel...a very nice night. On Sunday, we again had breakfast in the dining room (we ate breakfast there every morning)...then did some sight-seening down by Seaport Village (a short drive away)...it was warm outside though, and we found ourselves back at the pool again by early afternoon for more swimming, mojitos and calamari! The whole experience of this place was perfect for us...the hotel has so many areas where people can gather and play cards, visit with family etc.(there were many family reunions and a few weddings that weekend...but there was always plenty of space on the hotel grounds to do your own thing)....The decor and service at every level invited you to relax, and enjoy...and that is really what you want out of a mini-vacation...the bottomline on our trip is that we intend to return and make more family memories very soon. Our thanks to Dennis and staff for a great and memorable labor Day weekend!

name: Good Nite Inn Sea World
title: “Would stay again”
text: After reading horrible reviews we were worried to stay here. However, we had a great stay. The staff were helpful and friendly. The room was clean and safe - remember this is an old hotel so it's a bit worn. However it's cheap, and close walk to old town and trolley. It is near a strip club - however we had no issues with people around the area. Would stay again. Thanks to the staff who made our stay enjoyable.

name: Travelodge San Diego Mission Valley
title: “hotel service”
text: The room was clean as best as expected but the carpet was very dirty. There was no iron, ironing board, refrigerator or microwave oven in the room. The ice machine by our room was not working and guests constantly tried using the ice machine with no avail. We were told it had been fixed. No out of order sign was posted. The housekeeper was very friendly and accommodating.

name: Comfort Suites Mission Valley
title: “Rooms are way too small to be considered "suites"”
text:
The front desk receptionist was friendly, once we were able to check in. (Unfortunately, we got there at the same time the hillside was on fire, which delayed our check-in - no fault of the hotel.) Got to the room and was completely disappointed. The musty smell of urine hit us as soon as we walked in. The kids' suite barely fit 2 adults and 2 teenagers. We booked this hotel based on the price and the room photos. The rooms do not look ANYTHING like the website. There was only a small "kid-size" table and chairs - no place to put a laptop or eat a meal. We had to walk on the bed to get around another person. The shower leaked and the carpet was wet. WE WERE UNCOMFORTABLE THE WHOLE TIME! 
There was apparently a girls' volleyball tournament being held in the area, and most of the girls staying at this hotel were unsupervised, since they spent most of their time running back and forth outside our room, then crank-called our room at night. The breakfast buffet was adequate, when you could actually get to the food around the teenagers.
The location of this hotel was good, and it is within walking distance to several restaurants, shopping and the freeway.
All in all, I would not stay at this hotel again. Next time I will spend more to get an actual suite at another hotel.

name: Four Points by Sheraton San Diego
title: “If you get a good deal, this is a decent place.”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights. This was our first Sheraton experience after a very poor one at the Mission Bay location a year ago. 
We are a family of 4, but this hotel only stocks rooms for 2 people. This means that we never had enough towels or washcloths. We had to make repeated calls. On our last night, we didn't have enough washcloths & they never did bring us any after my husband requested a couple of towel sets. He called again, just asking for washcloths, but we never received them. In the morning, I used half a hand-towel to wash my face & decided to shower after we reached home. 
They also don't keep their pool stocked with towels. On our 2nd pool visit, we had no pool towels or room towels. We had to wait for them to deliver our room towels so we would have a pool towel. The pool itself was a large L shape, so it accommodated lots of splashing kids. The water was mostly shallow, but one end of the pool had a small area that was 5 ft in depth. The bottom of the pool was cracked, my 12 y.o. pointed out. There was quite a large spa. I'd never seen one so large. The water was a cloudy greenish color. We didn't use it. I thought the swimming pool was a bit cloudy as well, but we were only in the pool area in the early evening, after a hot day so I'm sure that had something to do with it.
Even though we stayed 4 nights, housekeeping didn't clean our room the first night. They woke us up at 8 am. We left by 11 am & returned that evening to an uncleaned room.
The TV had very poor reception. Many channels were fuzzy & the sound was distorted, including local channels. 
Our bathroom sink was slow / clogged upon check-in. They fixed that very quickly. 
The closet was a small cabinet by the door & the bar was hanging perpendicular so that you could only view the front hanging garment. Everything else had to be hung behind it. A nearby room had a normal closet, from what I could see walking by. I'm unsure why our closet had that design. 
The outside lobby area & hallways were clean & nice in appearance. 
We had a room at the end of our wing and there was an exit door to a parking lot. We were able to park next to our room. 
The hotel was near a freeway & it was a short drive to get where we needed to go.
It was quiet. We didn't really see very many guests.
Our a/c did keep the room cool.
The sink was inside the bathroom which made it difficult for a family of 4 to get ready to go somewhere. I used a wall length mirror outside of the bathroom & a nearby outlet to get myself ready while my family used the bathroom.
There was no room service menu. I sent my 12 y.o. to the front desk to get one, but they didn't have one either. He finally came back with a restaurant menu. We decided not to use it because I was uncertain if they were room-service prices or not and we were unsure of the open times. The prices were pretty steep & there was no children's menu or affordable item for a 2 y.o.'s meal. A club sandwich was around $10. Other things were more expensive. We visit San Diego once to twice a year, so really, food isn't a concern at a hotel because we usually have other plans, but sometimes we do like a late-night snack.
The people who checked us in & out did so quickly & were friendly. The check out woman wanted to know about our stay. I mentioned the HUGE towel problem. She apologized. But again, we stayed for 4 nights, with 4 people, & had to call EVERY day about the problem. I've had this problem with a Sheraton before.
If you get a good deal, this is a nice property, but I would not pay premium prices. We got a great deal so we were okay with our stay, overall.

name: Hotel Contessa
title: “Loved the Hotel Contessa”
text: Me and my husband stayed at the Contessa from Jan 1-5th. This hotel is very nice from the outside and inside. When we first arrived the bellmen opened the door's for us and this lasted through our entire trip. Checkin was smooth...even upgraded us to a larger room with no price change. The room was very spacious, modernized and clean. We had a city view side and it was quiet for us. The bed was very comfortable. Very nice location on the riverwalk. I believe all room's are a 2 room suite. We never tried their restaurant. But plenty of good eat's on the Riverwalk.

name: Diamond Head Inn
title: “Disgusting Dirty Carpet and Furnishings”
text: I use to stay at the Diamond Head Inn every year in the Fall for a week but after my trip this year I will not be staying in the future due to the staining on the furnishings and the carpet. I have always stayed in the one bedroom suite with deck facing the ocean, which is their best room. I had to go out and buy a blanket to cover the couch due to unknown stains and burn marks, put towels down on the chairs to sit and never took my shoes off as the carpet was heavily stained. I have stayed in hundreds of hotels and this was by far the most disgusting room I have ever stayed in, I still get a sick feeling when I think about my stay a few weeks ago, I even ended up checking out early due to the condition of the room. I would of given this hotel three or four stars a few years ago based on location and price but back then the carpet was new and furnishings only had minor staining. Not sure when the Owner last inspected this hotel but he should consider new Management immediately

name: Mission Valley Resort
title: “Rude Reservation Staff”
text: I made reservations for 6 rooms at the Mission Valley Resort. The price was $99.00 a night per room, and I asked if they could work with me to get a better deal. The two ladies that answered each time that I called were rather rude, uncaring, and not cooperative. They made no effort whatsoever to help me. Fortunately, I received a call from the staff at the Holiday Inn Select which is next door to the Mission Valley Resort. They were super friendly, nice, caring, and willing to work with me to secure a group rate. Everyone I spoke to from the front desk clerk to the person in sales was a charm at the Holiday Inn Select. Therefore, I promptly cancelled my reservations at the Mission Valley Resort. In fact, when I called to cancel, the lady who answered the phone at the Mission Valley Resort did not give me a chance otherwise to tell her about their terrible service. The place might be nice, but the staff needs some fine tuning.

name: Comfort Inn At The Harbor
title: “Don't Be Crazy!”
text:
I stay at A LOT of Comfort Inns, but this one was a pure example of why many people shy away from them, and why I would seriously consider not staying at one again. I don't know if it was just the room we got, but it was the most horrible room I have ever had at any hotel in my life. First, it smelled like mildew. I don't know if they have an incredible mold problem or if they use really smelly cleaning materials, but this room STUNK, to the point where I really thought I'd need antibiotics for my lungs after my stay. I would have switched rooms in a second, except I got in really late and had four hours I had to spend in this room from check in to check out, and I figured I could handle it. I never slept - it was terrible. I was spraying body spray all over, trying to mask the smell, but nothing worked. The bed... It was supposed to be a King, but it was a Full or small Queen - couldn't really tell. And it was an old spring mattress, and by old I mean the kind I throw out of my house after 10+ years of sleeping on it. My husband and I kept rolling into each other in the center. And the springs were lumpy all over the place. The pillows, someone else mentioned, are very small. They're square-sized and small, but they're like 6 inches or more thick. I don't know how anyone could be comfortable with that. The room I got was TINY. I mean, enough room for a bed and desk, and that's it. The pictures on the Comfort Inn website are NOTHING like what I experience for a room. The walls had been painted over so many seams and patchings, it looked like it could crumble. The electric sockets were not flush to the wall - they were poking out and looked like sockets from the early 1900s that were never upgraded. Even the power switches were crumbling and old. The bathroom door had its hinges painted over and it was SO loud and creeky, nobody could sleep through someone else in that room going into the restroom. And you had to force it to stay shut. The shower is an old tile shower - Tile on all 6 sides, like the kind of shower you see at campsites. It was kind of gross - I wish I had a pair of flip flops to wear in it, like I wear when I'm camping. The AC unit was pumping very humid, sort of cool air, and never cooled off the tiny room enough. There was a creepy window in the bathroom that led out to the street. I didn't want to leave it open, but the air flow was better with it open. I have pictures to prove ALL of this, so don't believe some of these SUPER positive reviews that you see here. I have been a fan of Choice Hotels for years, for their quality w/ value, but this experience was the most disgusting and disappointing I've ever had.
In regard to service:
In all fairness, the guy who checked me in at night was VERY nice. I'd give him a positive review.
BUT, the next morning when I had to check out and get back on the road quickly, NO ONE was at the front desk. I waited for a while, I called out to them, etc. No one came out to help me, even though the whole front desk area was all opened up and appeared to have someone there. I ended up having to leave my key across the counter on their computer keyboard and hope they'd get the hint that I officially checked out. That's another "first" for me!
I'D NEVER STAY THERE AGAIN! You couldn't pay me to stay there.

name: Kona Kai Resort
title: “VERY NICE PLACE TO STAY WITH A GREAT LOCATION”
text: Stay one night. room was clean and t.v. worked. rooms could be updated. front desk person, trudi, was great. she went out of her way to make sure my cab was on time. she even found me a soft drink and didn't charge.

name: Surfer Beach Hotel
title: “la mia esperienza ha avuto solo un lato positivo..”
text: Non discuto sulla camera a pian terreno con vista sui container dell'immondizia, non discuto nemmeno che invece dei 2 letti matrimoniali mi son trovato un letto e un divano letto..ma il materasso del divano letto era peggio di un letto di chiodi: impossibile dormirci. L'unico motivo per cui consiglio quest'albergo è la sua posizione sull'oceano nel bel mezzo di Pacific Beach!!

name: California Suites Hotel
title: “California Suites Hotel à San Diego”
text: Le séjour s'est très bien passé : l'emplacement est assez central pour rayonner dans San Diego ( à condition d'avoir une voiture), l'hôtel est très propre, chaque chambre est une suite avec une kitchenette, très pratique pour économiser sur les restaurants (non équipée, pas d'ustensile de cuisine). Piscine et Spa très agréable, personnel compétent. Le petit déjeuner buffet est très correct. Un bon rapport qualité-prix, une bonne adresse pour rester même plusieurs jours

name: Hotel Contessa
title: “Can't recommend the Contessa”
text:
On March 13, this year, my wife and I took a two-day vacation to San Antonio, Texas, a city we hadn’t visited for over fifteen years. The riverfront was dramatically changed, mostly for the better, but the new Hotel Contessa where we stayed is not one of the better changes.
I requested a low floor location, but we were given a ninth floor suite so high up that when we looked down we were too far above the river to appreciate the view. We had a closer view of the towering parking lot directly across the river. The window in the bedroom was located about waist high, and we had to stand leaning over to look out or we could sit on the bed about a foot from the window and watch cars park. 
I complained and asked for another suite, and we were given one on the fourth floor – after an hour’s wait. That non-smoking room smelled of cigar smoke so I asked to be relocated. Third time charmed – after another hour-long wait – and we were moved down to the third floor and a picture window with a lovely view, virtually floor to ceiling. Regrettably, it was not a clean window. 
The desk clerk apologized and said we would receive “amenities” for our inconvenience, but room service failed to deliver until the next day when a fruit tray arrived. We were also treated to lunch by an apologetic Manager on Duty who protested he would do everything in his power to make our visit a perfect one. It was not within his power. That afternoon I had a couple of strawberries and my wife had two or three pieces of overripe melon, and about an hour later she began vomiting and continued for over ten trips to the bathroom, effectively canceling her trip with me and friends to a riverfront restaurant that evening.
Hotel personnel were gracious, and the bed was quite comfortable (although the sheets were rough, the pillow case was smooth), but my final complaint to the manager was “Everyone was courteous and apologetic, but I wished for greater efficiency.” 
I never recommend a hotel on the basis of courteous, apologetic service. So I can’t recommend the Contessa.

name: Hotel Contessa
title: “Great place”
text: Decided to spend my birthday on the River Walk and selected this hotel because it was brand new - had a wonderful experience - the rooms are warm and inviting - the pool provided a grand view of downtown - the staff was extremely friendly - strongly recommend the place!!

name: Travelodge San Diego Mission Valley
title: “wonderful bugdet hotel”
text:
if your on a budget and would perfer to spend your money on the sites of san dieago instead of more exspensive hotels then this is the hotel you want! it is located minutes from sea world, SDzoo and old town, and mission beach! The rooms are old, but clean and modest, the price is great! The staff was very friendly and the pool area was wonderful too.. The hotel does warn about ordering foods from flyers that are shoved under your doors...DO NOT ORDER THE PIZZAS OR FOODS FROM THE FLYERS!!! NASTY TASTING FOOD!!!
 Other than that, I would stay again on my nest visit!!!

name: Days Inn & Suites - Sea World/Airport
title: “OMG Run & Run Fast”
text: I guess the owners of the roach infested hotel must have read the posts and decided to do a little damage control. This was the worst hotel I have ever stayed at. Rooms were dirty and staff was NASTY. Period !

name: Porto Vista Hotel
title: “Tired inside, but good location”
text: Good location with Little Italy, and the Gaslamp quarter near by. Rooms were very tight and very tired, but we weren't looking for luxury, this was simply a place for us to stay whilst we explored San Diego. The $18per day is a bit steep for valet parking as there is no self parking, just parking on the street. The Glass door restaurant is very nice, but small. The food is also pretty good. All up, an ok place to stay, but don't expect luxury.

name: Pacific View Inn
title: “Solo la posizione !”
text:
Come da titolo: solo la posizione, a 10 metri dalla bellissima spiaggia ! il resto direi molto scarso, struttura fatiscente e vecchia, stanze piccole, letto piccolo e scomodo, niente comodini, una unica luce nella stanza, senza aria condizionata, un piccolo ventilatore molto sporco. Wc piccolo. Comunque c'era il frigo, e la macchina per il caffe'. Parcheggio da prenotare a 15 dollari al giorno (ma te lo dicono quando arrivi.....) parcheggio pubblico nelle vicinanze ma non facile da trovare, wifi gratis. Abbiamo speso 95 euro a notte con booking, non poco per quello che offriva la struttura.
Non mi sento di consigliare questo posto.

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “Outstanding Service !!!”
text:
My girl friend and I had a great stay at the Hard Rock Hotel in 
San Diego. the staff was outstanding !!!
We travel extensively, and were blown away by the attention to detail, quality of
service and overall atmosphere and vibe.
I will definitely send friends and family to hard Rock Hotel San Diego !!!

name: Ramada Mission Valley / SDSU
title: “Fantastic Staff, Comfortable Rooms”
text:
The staff here were so welcoming. It was the little touches such as the big smiles from everyone when we entered the lobby to check in, to the phone call 15 mins after to our room to ensure everything was ok.
The rooms were big, clean and comfortable. Unfortately I was struck down with food poisoning (not from the hotel!!) and so I was confined to my room. This was frustrating, but made more comfortable because I was in a nice room and could relax.
Very easy access to Gaslamp etc including a tram, and I am assured the breakfast was great! 
This hotel is lovely and great value for money!

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “Perfect Location to party in SoCal...”
text: This was the best place to base ourselves for 3 days in downtown San Diego. The pool place cranking tunes on the roof all day, drinks are reasonable and theplace is just really cool. Within striking distance of all the best bars and clubs and a really good place to party when you are in San Diego. They got our booking wrong and we only had 1 bed as opposed to 2 but they were straight up with a 2nd bed so that was fine. Food round he pool was pretty terrible but that sums up America (massive generalisation I know but the fried Calamari was terrible!)

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “Felt like a VIP”
text: From the time we pulled up to the valet to the time we checked out the staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was in very nice condition, the mini bar was well stocked along with the snack tray. We stayed in a Woodstock suite so we had a nice balcony with a view of the pool and downtown.

name: Sheraton Mission Valley San Diego Hotel
title: “Awesome bed!! Staff was helpful and friendly.”
text: A group of us stayed here during Comic-Con... a crazy time for hotels in San Diego. The staff was professional and super helpful. There was a minor problem with our bedside lamp and someone came up immediately to fix it. I needed info on local churches and the front desk not only gave me the info on the phone but printed out mass schedules and driving directions and then delivered these to our room. The best part of this hotel though are the amazing beds and pillows straight from heaven. I am seriously going to find a place to but some of those pillows for myself!

name: BEST WESTERN Plus Cabrillo Garden Inn
title: “Loved this garden oasis”
text:
We stayed at this gem of a hotel for 3 nights pre-cruise. 
It is a small 2 storey garden oasis surrounded by high-rise towers. The staff were very friendly, the room was quiet and clean and a reasonable size, the bathroom small but perfectly fine.
The breakfast was much better than I expected - cereal and pastries, fruit, juice, and always something hot - bacon, sausage, pancakes, scrambled eggs, hash browns. It could be eaten in the small lobby, outside at a table, or taken to your room.
It was a good price and within easy walking distance of all that San Diego has to offer, which is much!

name: Kona Kai Resort
title: “Lousy, bad price, small rooms, bad advertising”
text: Booked a junior suite with a view of the San Diego Bay several months prior to Memorial Day. Arrived on 5/29 to find partial view of a dumpster and parking lot. Room was small, dark, and musty. On a positive note, the front desk was helpful in finding accommodations at a different property unrelated to Shelter Pointe. The hotel's website is misleading and basically false advertisement. I booked the room with an employee over the phone and was assured I would have a partial view of the bay. The manager claims they are changing the sale's pitch for their rooms, however many other properties are available in San Diego for similar price and better accommodations... Stay away!

name: BEST WESTERN Plus Cabrillo Garden Inn
title: “Loved the Cabrillo Garden”
text:
I just wanted to let you know that this hotel was really GREAT.
Instead of feeling like hotel, it felt more like staying at someone's home. The staff was very friendly and willing to help out if we needed anything. It was the first time I felt like a guest instead of a customer. You should be very proud of the service this hotel offers it is exemplary. I will definitely be staying again.

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “The Hard Rock San Diego Rocked our Socks Off :)”
text: This was my first time staying at the Hard Rock San Diego - I've stayed at many other hotels in San Diego and this was by far my most favorite experience. We were there for a bachelorette party and we had a blast - I would recommend this hotel for any occaision; the staff is extremely accommodating.

name: BEST WESTERN Plus Cabrillo Garden Inn
title: “Good value and really cute!”
text:
The Cabrillo is great little hotel and I would definitely stay there again.
Great Price - I got the room for $119 (AAA special).
Free Breakfast & Wireless Internet - They offered eggs, toast, hash browns, juice, coffee, cereals, and Danishes. Sure, it's not a world-class breakfast but good and most of all FREE.
Cheap Parking – We paid $12 a day; most other hotels charged a lot more for parking.
Location - It's in the city, right by the stadium and the Gas Lamp district.
Also it looked like a nice, clean room and it was. The room was on the small side but enough. The sheets and the bed were great and clean. The bathroom was spotless. The staff was very attentive.

name: Sheraton Mission Valley San Diego Hotel
title: “Excellent location/staff”
text: I stayed for the weekend at this hotel. One of the strong points was the friendly, helpful staff. Giovanna and Trevor at the front desk stood out, and Mel and Robert with the bell captain/shuttle drivers were great! I saw one guest really being unhappy about the charge for the parking, which when I checked in was explained very well about where to park and how much it would cost, Giovanna handled herself expertly, as this customer was just not going to be satisfied with any resolution that could be offered. The room was clean and comfy, especially the beds/linens.

name: BEST WESTERN Seven Seas
title: “OK experience”
text: Our room was very nice and well appointed and clean. The help was pleasant but not overly friendly. It is located in the Hotel Circle area of San Diego. This property, like many similar properties in San Diego Motel Circle are starting to look a little run down. They are almost 50 years old and this property seems to need some remodeling. We are accustomed to a free continental breakfast which has become standard in this level of hotel. Needless to say there was no continental breakfast but there were several restaurants nearby. I also thought some of the other patrons staying at the hotel seemed somewhat questionable types to which I was a little uncomfortable.

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “The Hard Rock lives up to there name!”
text:
Go for the experience and you will love the service.
I had some needs that had to be addressed during my stay at the Hard Rock. All of the staff members were really 'in tune' to help me address my needs and make me feel like a total VIP.
I would recommend this hard rock again and again.
smiles

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel San Diego - Hotel Circle
title: “Nothing Special”
text: Hilton Honors Gold Member. Had to stay at this hotel for 6 days. Rooms were okay nothing special to mention. Parking is a big hassle especially when it rains as you would have no option but to walk in the rain. The parking charges is pretty steep at 30 dollars a night. The staff were not too concerned about guest satisfaction. Nothing great to write about food either. Stay here only if you have to or if on a short transit. Location is pretty accessible to Fashion Valley Mall.

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “Were these my friends or employees???”
text:
I recently stayed at the Hard Rock for a week of fun! The ladies at the concierge desk were great! They made us feel like they really cared that we were having a good time and enjoying ourselves. The valet's outside were excellent! The entire staff made us feel like we have known them for years! 
The bed OMG that bed and those pillows were so comfortable! The shower was amazing! Beautiful view, great location in the Gaslamp area. 
thanks everyone for making my vacation great!

name: Hampton Inn San Diego - Downtown
title: “Trains, but no whistles”
text: In my prior stay here the train whistles were very annoying, but I came back anyway because I liked the hotel. The train whistles are now gone, while you can still hear trains and crossing signals but they are no worse than any other city noises. The hotel is bright, cheerful and the rooms are clean and comfortable. Having a shuttle to and from the airport is a great convenience. The breakfast, while not gourmet, is far better than most hotels. The staff was very friendly and helpful, on the Friday that I was there one of the staff brought in home made chocolate chip cookies. The fitness room is small, but for a couple of days it is fine. There is free wi-fi in the rooms and a couple of computers in the lobby area. The location is a short walk to many places and Little Italy is two blocks away. A great place to stay.

name: Point Loma Inn
title: “Will not go back to this hotel”
text:
We had booked this hotel room with kichennette for 4 days. Family with 2 kids. There was too much new paint smell in the room and no way to open the windows. There was no furniture nor any kichen stuff. After complaining the hotel staff bought a few stuff from Big Lots next day. Had 1 phone in room with outgoing calls thru operator for a heavy sur-charge. Also, was an incident when the staff was rude to my family folks when they asked for more toilet paper. Also, as I found out the price was not cheap either. There were several others at the same price with better amenities. Also, we were told that there was no pool nor a breakfast. Kids were conting on San Diego warm water pool and very dis-appointed. We cut short our visit by 1 day but te hotel charged for it any way. I am still figting wth them to get some money back.
Overall, very bad experience for kids and family. I am now even afraid to use the internet bookng... Never know, what you get.
Will never go back there again.
Chitra, Oregon.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel San Diego - Hotel Circle
title: “a good stay”
text: we are from new zealand, reading the reviews had me very worriied about my choices in staying in hotels for our three week stay in the usa we had four days in doubletree club hotel san diego, well on arriving we found the hotel to be very nice the rooms very big we were staying with our two teenaged sons, the beds big and so comfortble lots of pillows big flat screen tv, cookies on arrival, good size bath room with bath nice views from our room, a couch and table with chair for our laptop. the pool and hot tub we used every day it was so good and there gym was good to we had tea at the resturant one night really good pizza over all our whole family loved staying here and would come back again, some times its good to read trip adviser but some people are really so picky for them they should pay more stay at really flash places and stop moaning over all i would give this an 8 out of 10

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Sorrento Mesa/La Jolla
title: “thumbs down for housekeeping”
text:
Stayed here for a wedding in August. The hotel was nice enough, but the maid service could really use improvment. Coffee maker filled with old coffee, lipstick on the mugs, and a good amount of hair on the floor. On the second day, the maid started cleaning my room while I was in the shower, despite the "do not disturb" sign on the door. And for some reason, she only made one of the two beds in the room for our second night. The handwriting on the "your room has been cleaned by" note in the room was that of a serial killer, so we didn't actually complain directly. 
The pool was nice, and they had a nice little selection of snack-food and supplies for sale in the lobby. It would really take the place up a notch if the restaurant/coffee bar at least sold coffee and easy pastries during the day. After breakfast, it closes at like 11, just in time for the late-risers to miss out. 
And like others have said, it is definitely in an office park.

name: Porto Vista Hotel
title: “Great Location - Friendly Staff - Nice Room”
text: My wife & I just returned from a wonderful long weekend in SoCal, and the two nights at the PV made it that much better. The hotel and restaurant (and Valet Parking) staff were friendly and helpful. I highly recommend this place for a number of reasons: Location - perfect for anything in the Little Italy area, which IMHO is the very best of the various downtown neighborhoods. If you are a single 30-something or younger, the "Gaslamp" and "Old Town" party hearty till-you-stagger districts are a short cab ride away, and besides - a cab is much better to avoid the DUI danger, as well as the $20 minimum parking lots over there. If your a bit beyond that age range (as we are) - Little Italy is walking distance charming, friendly, CLEAN, and has plenty of choices for cocktail conversation, Vino Fino exporation, and solidly good restaurants. The neighborhood is spotlessly maintained by the "Little Italy Association", whose workers and trucks are out and about every day. Don't miss the every Saturday 9am-1:30pm Farmers/Munchies Market on 3 blocks of Grape Street (2 blocks from the PV). Its delightful! Back to the PV - the rooms are actually larger than most cookie cutter establishments, and there is an artistic flair to the rooms that defies a category, but a welcome relief from the boring norm of most hotels. The rooftop lounge offers wonderful views of San Diego and the North harbor areas - a great place to sip a libation and make new friends. The Glass Door is a boutique Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner restaurant with a very interesting menu that ranges from regular fare to the exotic (and they do exotic well). Treat yourself to the fresh-made crab cakes and the Smoked Salmon Omlette. BTW - some of the package deals for the hotel include breakfast, which means the place gets swamped from around 9:45 - 11 am check out time, so be early or after that for best experience. The hotel does cater to private functions, so although there was boisterous sound from those celebrations on the "outside" of our north side guest room, the noise was cancelled as soon as the door closed. Oh - and a great bed too! We will stay there anytime our travels take us to San Diego.

name: BEST WESTERN Seven Seas
title: “Very pleasant”
text: I thought this place was a pleasant surprise. Although I didn't have time to take advantage of any of these nice facilities, the pool looked large, clean and inviting, and there was a hot tub. Nice cafe/restaurant on the premises, and very helpful staff and airport shuttle service (doesn't begin till 6 am though, and ends at 10 pm.) My bed was extremely comfortable with plenty of nice big pillows, and the wifi worked well. Good water pressure, mini fridge in room but no microwave. A very quiet and restful and comfortable place to spend a night or two--I'd definitely come back here.

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Sorrento Mesa/La Jolla
title: “Unkomplziert, sauber, nett, große Zimmer”
text: Der Aufenthalt war angenehm, auch wenn wir nicht viel Zeit im Hotel verbracht haben. Das Personal war sehr freundlich. Die Zimmer sind geräumig und modern eingerichtet. Außerdem äußerst ruhig. In der Nähe sind weitere Hotels und Restaurants. Jederzeit empfehlenswert. Moderne Multimediaaustattung im Zimmer runden das Bild ab.

name: Comfort Suites I-15 Miramar
title: “Didn't stay here but wish I had!”
text: We were visiting family for 4 days over Thanksgiving and this hotel would of cost us $100.00 less than where we stayed. But because of reviews on here about smoking; etc. we decided to stick with the non-smoking hotel we did stay at only an exit away. We decided to go check out the hotel on Thanksgiving Day; the lobby was very clean, bright and inviting. The lady at the front desk was very helpful and allowed us to take a look at one of their King Suite rooms...and when they say suite they mean suite! :) It was what I call and outdoor entrance to the room; you walked into a big space where the sofa bed, TV, desk, wet bar with sink, refridge and microwave were. Then you walked down a short hallway; to the right was the bathroom sink and then another door to the actual bathroom. As you cont. walking into the next room it opens up into another large room with a King bed, another TV and closet space. The rooms could use some updating, but over all looked clean, and the best part was you could move around and not feel enclosed in. I must say we were kicking ourselves after seeing the room because where we stayed was nice, but the kind suite rooms were small and made you feel closed in. The other nice part was the inside outdoor courtyard with Palm Trees and water fountains...very inviting if you just wanted to sit or walk around. The pool & hot tub were nice too. I could see parking would become an issue since the Holiday Inn is literally right next door. Shopping centers, freeway access...everything is very close by. 20 min to Sea World or to the beach at Del Mar. You can't go wrong with this area. When we do return, we will be trying this hotel out next time. We had a nice stay at the other place, but think this is worth a try as well.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel San Diego - Hotel Circle
title: “Great for family stay”
text: Nice size rooms with good layout and amenities. Balconies are on the small size. Had view over the I-8 but noise not an issue. Check-in staff could be a little more warming, but other hotel staff where very friendly. Nice size pool and surrounds. Good location for all the surrounding tourist attractions. Parking at $16 not great but knew this at time of booking.

name: Wyndham Garden San Diego near SeaWorld
title: “Hotel stay”
text: The hotel staff was very friendly. Room location was not good, we were traveling with other family and requested rooms next to each other. She said she gave us rooms next to each other. Well I don't consider one room on one side, and laundry next to it, then the other room past that around the corner past the maids quarters. Not at all happy with that. Lots of younger people running around using foul language. Constant running past the rooms. Probably would not stay again.

name: Americas Best Value Inn Loma Lodge
title: “Decent, but not for all”
text:
We got two King bed rooms for 5 people for $79 each on a Friday night. Rooms were fine, very clean, although a bit dated and musty. Bed was surprisingly pretty comfortable. The pool was empty, and they were doing some construction around it.
Staff was exceptionally nice. Each room has a sliding glass door, so the outside noise level can be loud. Overall, it was a decent place to plop down overnight.

name: Hampton Inn San Diego - Downtown
title: “Well situated, attentive staff, economical - and noisy”
text:
This hotel is well situated - short walk to Little Italy and the Nautical Museum, etc. and longer walk to the Gaslight district, Convention Center, USS Enterprise, etc. There are no spectacular views, as the San Diego County Administration Building is due west, so at best partial Bay views. However, the hotel is excellently located and economical, usually beating better and nearby properties in price, providing free airport shuttle transport, clean and pleasant accommodations with free WiFi, a reasonable basic breakfast, coffee service in room, etc.
One attraction is its closeness to the AMTRAK station and the MTS trolley system - the latter offers a $5.00 daily pass that is a huge bargain. The deficit with that is the railroad and trolley lines run immediately in back (east) of the property - and the occasional trains are required by Federal regulation to sound their compressed air horns at all crossings, even though they are controlled - which means the electronic warning bells also sound. The hotel provides courtesy 3M "1100" foam earplugs in every room (29 db suppression) and if you can secure a room fronting (west) on Pacific Highway you will be spared much of the noise. If the hotel is running at high occupancy and you get assigned a room on Beech or Cedar street close to the rails or on the open court facing the tracks, you are in for some noise and will appreciate the earplugs. 
Summary: Well situated, clean property with a little wear, motivated staff, airport shuttle, and significant occasional train noise. There is supposed to be a project (to be completed by the end of 2012) that will presumably mitigate noise for at least some of the rooms currently affected, and I certainly hope so.

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “Cool Hotel”
text:
Went to San Diego for a business trip but because of last minute changes it ended up being mostly pleasure. The decor of the hotel is fantastic, especially if you are into the whole Rock 'n' Roll motif. Everything is updated. The rooms are cool as hell. My only complaint for the room was that it was kinda of small. At the time of my trip our room was equipped with a flat screen LCD TV but they did not boradcast in HD, so the picture was kinda crappy. Internet worked well. The on-site bars are really nice and if you are a fan of sushi the on site sushi restuarant is fantastic. 
Just remember that EVERYTHING is a la carte in this hotel and is a little over priced.
Staff was very courteous and helpful. Everything in SD is "No Worries"

name: Porto Vista Hotel
title: “Good Location, Clean Rooms, Low Price”
text:
Stayed here for 4 nights in May 2007 based on recommendations and the forum here at Tripadvisor.
I'll reiterate the comments that others have posted here:
Pros: 
1) The rooms were very clean - a pleasant surprise as the outside of the hotel looks a bit messy (as it used to be a motel and is under renovations).
2) Location - the hotel is within walking distance to the tram stop and all the restaurants in Little Italy.
3) Price - what can I say...I love lower prices...
Cons:
The Porto Vista used to be a Motel 8; so it does feel a bit dodgy when you first arrive. However, when the renovations are done, I'd assume it will be much better.
Note - this hotel is away from the main city center and has a residential feel when walking around at night.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel San Diego - Hotel Circle
title: “Excellent for the value”
text:
We did a 2-night stay over the Easter weekend with 2 adults and 2 kids ( 5 yr old and 8 months). The room was spacious enough for the 4 of us. The double sofabed was an added bonus so our older child got her own bed. 
The warm fresh chocolate chips cookies brought big smiles to everyone. We enjoyed the comfortable beds and lots of fluffy pillows. There was enough room to park the stroller inside the room. 
When we arrived in the room, we immediately checked for A/C and hot water before unpacking. The bathroom was locked and so we called the maintenance/housekeeping. Within a couple of minutes, they came to unlock the door, and maintenance guy checked the A/C and changed the filter to optimize airflow. The A/C unit was very quiet and so you could occasionally hear the freeway traffic. There's also a small balcony which was nice to enjoy some fresh air.
We went to the pool mid-morning and fortunately, we brought the room towels as there were no pool towels when we got there. The towels were brought in around 12 noon. The jacuzzi was extremely hot and so we didn't sit in it. There's also a fire pit to enjoy. 
Overall, our we enjoyed our stay and we'd go back again.

name: Wyndham Garden San Diego near SeaWorld
title: “Happy with my Groupon Deal!”
text: Like ‘Poopy’ above, I too bought a Groupon voucher for my wife and two kids, we were visiting the San Diego for Spring Break. We had to buy two extra breakfast coupons for our kids, but at $7.50/each we were pretty happy with the price. I’m not sure why Poopy wasn’t happy with the deal, we looked at other properties in the area and they were all well over $120-$150, didn’t include breakfast and were for the most basic room! The only drawback was that it was SO busy! We spent half the day at the pool which was full of kids and the other day we spent at SeaWorld which is like 5 minutes away.

name: BEST WESTERN Seven Seas
title: “The best hotel experiences ever!”
text:
I think I speak for hundreds of contractors, military and government reps when I thank you for the care, friendship, hospitality and respect we receive from ALL of you. You all are unique from everyone else I have ever delt with in this job. You remember us as individuals with a name and not just a face. Our contractors from QED had a great stay last week and due to the great people of Best Western Seven Seas, we made some new friends. Please pass this on to the following and don't forget the unseen staff that make it all come together at BW7S. Zach. Jason, Ruben, Betts, Pam, Rosemary, all the cooks, waiters, waitresses, room cleaning, security. Please allow a special thanks to Joe, the owner for making this all possible. Good man! Unique! My special word for my friends at BW7S Hotel is "Unique"..
All Respect And Thanks
Steve Ebeling

name: Wyndham Garden San Diego near SeaWorld
title: “Hotel bums”
text: i would like to say that this hotel needs to keep bums and flatbeds away from the hotel. The business center computer didn't work and neither did the printers. The other guests were loud and smoking with th doors open.

name: Porto Vista Hotel
title: “One star rating- totally not true!!! Stay here ASAP!”
text: I had the pleasure of staying here for the past two nights and enjoyed my time so much! Yes- its right by the airport- and you can hear the planes when you are outside.... yes there is construction that starts at 8am and you can hear it sometimes.... but OVERALL- it is a cheap- totally clean- friendly great place to stay in one of the very safest neighborhoods. They shuttled us to the zoo and back and to the amtrak station for free and it was only $79 a night. We had a great time and the sunsets from teh 3rd floor are breathtaking- if you want a 4 star then pay $200+ for a room- if you enjoy a value- stay here- we will be back!

name: Hilton San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Ask for a room on the other side from the train tracks!”
text:
We had three rooms, all facing the train tracks.....after the first sleepless night - one of our group changed to the other side of the hotel (I did not switch as I thought we would hear the trains whichever room we were in) - but apparently it is a lot quieter on the other side. I did mention the noise on check out and apparently it is in the works to become a 'quiet zone' - meaning no more train whistles, but not sure when that is going to happen.
Location is good - right next to the Convention Centre. Service was excellent. Check in was good....the sink in one of our rooms was not working properly - went out for dinner and when we came back, it was fixed.
We did not receive wine on check in. Rooms were very nice - no mini bar which surprised me. Check out was fine.
We got a deal on this hotel, but I certainly would not pay the normal price. People should be informed that the hotel is situation right next to train tracks!

name: Pacific Shores Inn
title: “Enjoyed our stay...”
text:
We really enjoyed our stay at Pacific Shores Inn. We found the location excellent being very close to the beach.There were many shops, restaurants and public transport within a short walking distance.
The noise from the second story rooms could clearly be heard in the downstairs rooms. Fortunately we had quiet people above us most of the time. 
There was a great continental breakfast of coffee, juice and Danish pastries included in the price. 
The rooms were spacious and clean.

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “Nice facility, missing key attributes”
text:
I visited the San Diego hotel for a conference and was there 5 nights. The first night, a Saturday, they immediately said at the front desk I had a credit card problem when they tried to get approval for $2,000 credit in advance. This issue lingered for the entire stay, it was a hassle to say the least and in the end it turned out to be their error, they put in my actual mastercard number into an Amex approval! In fact, on the last day they purposively locked me and my guests out of our room for over an hour because of this issue. We can't let him check out tomorrow because he has a card issue, so lets make sure he can't have room access or leave? It was finally resolved by me calling my credit card company (I had $30,000 credit!) in their presence and finally they noticed their error. 
Most important failing however beyond the card incident was two out of five nights the noise in the room floor I was staying on was unacceptably high and raucous. Partying was taking place and door slamming was constant until 5 in the morning. I slept not a wink. I called the front desk 3 times during the night and they said they were sending security up, but bit it was never resolved. Two nights I lost a full night sleep, this can really kill a trip! When traveling and using a hotel a fundamental service is a bed and quiet surroundings so a guest can sleep. They failed here miserably. When I talked to the manager the next day, he said he had this complaint from other people on my floor and on other floors and it is common. He said, ya these young folks band together and rent a room for the night so they can take the party from our bar to somewhere and then they leave at about 5am when they sober up as little. He or hotel management obviously didn't care to fix it. He was however dressed (as they all are) very cool , and looked like a real rocker...more important I guess. They did keep throwing small credits at me to appease me each time I complained, but these were severe deficiencies. 
Other winner features: A health club who's aerobic machines don't work, you can't control the TV or music or even hear it some times, and the spa is unattended completely.
Other items: For $15/day internet access could have worked better and for $30/day, valet parking was expensive...one time I waited 30 minutes to get my car...they kind of forgot about me,,,another complaint another small credit. I'd rather get have the car retieved quickly. The hallways are a mess, not living up to the rest of the place in style or appearance and they really need to allow for coffee in the room or the lobby. 
The place in a great location and has potential but doesn't seem to get it regarding the small customer satisfaction items which make a HUGE difference when paying so much.

name: Sheraton Mission Valley San Diego Hotel
title: “Not glamorous”
text: We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights. We got a very good rate through AAA. The location is right near the freeway. However, noise was never an issue. It was a nice hotel. We never were in the room for long periods of time. It was clean and we had a nice two nights. We were looking at colleges and this particular location was ideal. It is close to everything. I would definitely stay here again.

name: Holiday Inn San Diego - On The Bay
title: “It was okay”
text:
I travel quite a bit for work and have stayed in the best hotels and the worst hotels available. This place is pretty much in the middle of the pack. Here is my breakdown.
1. The hotel is a little over priced for what you get but it is at an excellent location. The E&C pub is quite good as are the other restaurants in the area but my room was small and I was traveling with my wife and two young children (1 and 4). We have been here for 5 nights now with 2 more to go and I think we will manage it. I know there are larger rooms available as my colleague has one but all hotels in the area are full thanks to several conferences going on at the same time (I'm here for the engineer's conference). So my advice is to ask for one if needed.
2. Despite the adoption of noise ordanances by the city there are trains and planes to be heard but it is not bad. The noise has so far not woke my wife, myself or the kids. I do have a bay view room in tower 2, that probably helps a bit. 
3. The pool is not heated, in any way. If it is then there must be ice covering it when the heat is turned off. I don't know how the hotel can claim to have a heated pool while keeping a straight face. False advertising if you ask me. My wife and kids snuck a swim in the pool at the Manchester Hyatt where my conference was taking place as its pool is nice. 
4. The dryer on the 11th floor took 3 cycles to dry my clothes. I complained to front desk staff but doubt anything will happen. I'm writing this waiting for the 3rd cycle to finish on the dryer.
5. The staff are friendly and very helpful. I needed some milk for the baby when we arrived and the gentlemen at the desk was helpful in finding some. The requested crib and fridge were delivered to our room quickly after we arrived. 
6. The hotel has excellent services for the tourist, including a shuttle service to some of major attractions. We never did bother to rent a car.
7. Finally, the hotel is a little dated but again, it's okay. 
I would have no problem staying here again but if traveling to San Diego again with the family I would probably shop around for another hotel first to see what else is out there.

name: BEST WESTERN Seven Seas
title: “Decent No Frills Hotel”
text:
My wife and I stayed at this hotel for 1 night during a week stay in San Diego. We were unfamiliar with the area and after searching websites, booked through bestwestern.com. We would have stayed longer, but ended up getting a better deal through Priceline that night.
The front desk staff was polite and didn't have a problem when we reduced our stay from 4 nights to 1. 
Overall the room was nice and the bed was comfortable and the furniture and overall look tasteful. One light bulb would not stay on and kept flickering. The bathroom was adequate, but certainly nothing to write home about. It had been renovated not too long ago. The shower spout was on crooked and it looked a little run down, but everything worked allright. 
Wireless internet is available and free. We weren't able to log on for a couple attempts, but were finally successful. The connection speed was fine. Breakfast wasn't included in our reservation.
The hotel is located in a strip of hotels and there isn't much for food within walking distance. It's next to a highway, but the noise really wasn't intrusive and didn't bother us.
