This is a relatively inexpensive, no frills hotel in a safe area. If that's what you're looking for, than I'd definitely recomend it.

name: Ramada Inn and Conference Center Qualcomm Stadium
title: “Very nice and relaxing stay”
text:
The hotel is just 15 minutes away from the San Diego Gas Lamp destrict and Coronado. The style remembers (intentionally) the American Graffity movie. Very nice people. Very good breakfast for just a few $'s.
Rooms are nice and comfortable. Free parking upfront the room.
Quiet rooms upon request - no problem!

name: Ramada Inn and Conference Center Qualcomm Stadium
title: “bon rapport qualité prix”
text: hotel agréable avec de bonnes prestations : piscine, parking,... nous avons été surclassés en chambre supérieure car disponibilité dans l'hôtel, et sans rien demander ! Hotel proche des axes routiers.

name: Pacific Inn Hotel & Suites
title: “Excellent Treatment for a Hotel before our cruise”
text:
We had a very enjoyable stay and the staff gave us good information as to events and places to eat, good breakfast as well.
Due to a special problem with our son havivg been diagnosed with cancer we left suddenly for home and left keys behind, they sent them back to us by mail, and were very good at giving us the best and quickest route home.
Excellent room and treatment
Ed and Betty McIntyre

name: Hilton San Diego Resort & Spa
title: “We had a blast”
text: On a very hot July 3rd we decided on a staycation to a hotel with air conditioning and a pool. Right choice! We were a bit surprised to find great rates available for same night the day before the 4 th so we grabbed it! We upgraded to a bay villa non tower. Again - right choice. We had ground floor patio and watched the fireworks from Seaworld. Very fun. The pool was great and we enjoyed the water. Not enough lounge chairs whe it was busy so second day pool was harder. We went sailing instead. Very reasonable and very fun. Yes - we will be back. The whole staff turned out for the 4 th of July pool party. Everyone from a management to accounting to catering! All hands on deck with huge smiles. Thank you!

name: Hilton San Diego Mission Valley
title: “It is a treat to be able to use the meeting room for fellowship”
text: We are grateful that the arrangement by the hotel manager. The stay is superb, The rooms are clean and quiet with our double bed rooms facing the hill. Convieniently located close to many of our destinations (La Jolla, Torrey pine, Cabrillo and Balboa park), this hotel is really our best choice. The staffs are friendly and helpful. If there is anything I would ask for more, I would like to have more selections in the breakfast buffet. Overall, I would recommend without hesitation for future San Diego visitors. We will probably visit again soon.

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “Fantastic !! Awesome !! Loved the Hard Rock”
text:
I stayed at the Hard Rock San Diego in January 2008 to attend the Buick Invitational Golf Tournament at Torrey Pines. What an awesome hotel !! The location was great, centrally located in the Gaslamp District. The staff was phenomenal exceeding not only my expectations but my business customers as well. This stay was certainly a welcomed visit, unlike the boring status quo visits with most other large hotels. The rooms were very clean and modern with a sensational shower experience. The beds are comfortable and the room environment was "rockin'". As I checked in, the hotel has the room playing Classic Rock as I indicated my choice in music...nice touch !! 
You will have to eat at Mary Jane's for breakfast and NoBu for dinner..it was fantastic !!
You will love your stay at the Hard Rock !!

name: Hilton San Diego Resort & Spa
title: “Our favorite getaway year-round!”
text: We have been coming here for short visits for 10 years, and have never failed to enjoy the incomparable views, rooms and wonderful amenities at the resort. Perfect place to enjoy the best of San Diego- the weather, the numerous bay activities just steps from your room, Sea World, the San Diego Zoo, downtown, etc. The pool area is perfect for families with clean restrooms and delicious food easily accesible from the deck area. We have always found the service to be excellent as well; on our visit last weekend, we were greeted warmly and helped to our room by Jeffrey. He was genuine, professional and most of all, helpful with everything we needed! Thanks for a great visit!

name: Pacific Inn Hotel & Suites
title: “My Room Went To The Highest Bidder...”
text: After I booked my stay with them they called a couple of days before my trip to tell me that my nightly rate had gone up because Barry Bonds was going to be in town. I agreed to the higher rate and told the woman I would be arriving late. I got to the hotel at 7pm and my room...the last room available had been given away. The hotel was small with limited parking, no elevator just a motel. Also the counter person lied to me said they found another hotel I got there and there had been no call and no rooms available. I spent 2 hours calling and driving around trying to find another hotel with no help from this hotel. I would never recommend this hotel to anyone. I ended up at the Best Western on Harbor , it was great and the people were friendly...give them a try.

name: Hilton San Diego Mission Valley
title: “Great location, but still disappoints”
text:
We stayed here last month as it was the closest proximity to Zoo,safari and sea world. We booked a room with 2 beds. We were surprised to see the size of the rooms comapared to other Hiltons. Front desk told us that they being a business hotel they just have rooms with either a bed or 2 beds and no bigger suites. So there was no chance we could have got a larger room, even if you are ready to pay a fee.
Otherwise the desk and restaurant staff were really helpful. The valet guys were always ready with answers to any questions about the area.Its good for a business hotel.

name: Hilton San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Great Place”
text:
I stay for two days, the hotel is not very big, it is located in a great zone, if you like to walk this district is the place to be.
I didn’t like to pay 35 dlls for valet parking but I had to in order to park my car. It is near Petco Baseball Park, about three or four blocks away. The room I got was very quite, I didin't noticed the train outside, if there was any passing by.
If I have the chance, I will be back to this hotel.
The disadvantages are the valet parking and the absence of free wireless internet. Also, the food is not that great, do not order room service, there are a bunch of good restaurants outside

name: Doubletree Hotel San Diego Downtown
title: “Very so-so, staff need some re-training”
text:
My husband and I stayed last weekend for a wedding, and we were underwhelmed with the hotel as a whole. The staff really didn't seem to know what was happening at all, they messed up my friend's reservation, her drycleaning, and her luggage that was (or was not, according to them) delivered from the airport. I asked the 'concierge' if he knew where the shuttle would be to the wedding (something I would think he would at least be aware of, even if it was a private shuttle, since many many hotel guests were taking it) and he had absolutely no idea, and made no effort to find out for us. Another thing that bothered me about this hotel was there is no mini-fridge. It seems most hotels these days offer that, if you want to chill some water, soda, beer, etc. 
The pool area was nice, albeit windy. We decided that they should move the bar that is currently in the restaurant in the lobby to the 5th floor pool, because there is some great furniture up there, and it looks like it could even be a 'scene', with little cabanas, etc. But it was sort of quiet and boring in the pool area, and I think it had some potential.
Overall, an okay stay, but nothing memorable at all.

name: San Diego Marriott Mission Valley
title: “Might be the worst Marriott property to stay if you are a elite member”
text:
I am currently staying for 6 nights due to a dermatology convention in town. I could not get rooms closer to the convention center below $350 at the Marriott Marquis or at the gaslamp so I decided to stay here at $160 a night. The room needs renovation and very small by Marriott standards. There is no concierge at this property and although there is a concierge lounge, the variety and quality of food/snacks that are available is poor. The concierge lounge is closed on weekends and usually at other Marriott properties, the hotel will give you a breakfast voucher if you are a platinum member. Well, not at this property. 
I ordered a simple burger for room service and the food did arrive on time but was cold and not cooked as I ordered. 
I am usually happy with the Marriott properties due to the consistent level of the properties and the amenities, however unless you have no other options in San Diego, stay away from this one.

name: BEST WESTERN Seven Seas
title: “aahhh it was OK”
text:
Stayed 2 days, Checked in Monday the NON SMOKING room we we're given stank, the front desk was almost no help stating they would send up housekeeping to "spray" some air freshener... it stank of smoke and mildew, I asked for a refund and was greeted with an "you'll have to take that up with Hotel, COM attitude. Finally got in touch with the night desk manager Steve and insisted he come smell the room.
The word he gave it" Pretty Narley" and gave us another room I feel sorry for whom ever got that one, as they stated they were completely booked. I also believe from the attitude there is some prejudice against those who book outside of Best Western proper.
The rooms are small but the beds were comfortable and if not for Steve the night manager changing our room at the last minute the stay would have been intolerable. We paid 97.00 per night and felt it was overpriced. Told you Steve you never know who writes reviews....

name: BEST WESTERN Seven Seas
title: “nice property”
text: We spent three nights at this propery over the July 4th holiday. When we first arrived we were placed in an extremely small room with two double beds. After the first night we requested two queens and were given an interior room that was huge. We had a refrigerator and coffe maker plus a view of the garden area. When you book your room ask for an interior room with two queen beds. Everything was very clean and the staff was extremely helpful. The location was convenient to all attractions and the beach. The rate was very good for San Diego during a holiday week. Be sure to check other booking sites like expedia and travelocity because best western will match their rates. Overall this hotel was good and we would stay there again if we were traveling with our kids or on a budget. Also, there is a great restaurant in the hillcrest area called the "hash house a go go". Don't be put off by the name it was amazing. We had breakfast there and the pancakes were as big as platters. The food was delicous and reasonalbly priced. Don't miss this place for some great food and fun.

name: Hilton San Diego Mission Valley
title: “Hilton San Diego Mission Valley”
text: Nice stay, bed was very comfortable. Friendly staff. Good variety of food at breakfast buffet. Avoided the $16/day parking screw over by parking free on street. Just a short walk, so well worth it.

name: Pacific Shores Inn
title: “gute Lage aber .....”
text: Das Motel ist ca. 50m vom Beach entfernt, dort gibt es eine schöne Promenade. Das Motel ist für den Preis ok, aber sehr hellhörig! eine Kaffee Maschine war zwar vorhanden aber weder Kafee noch Filter oder Kaffee Becher.;-)

name: BEST WESTERN Americana Inn
title: “Cheap prices and good service, BUT... smells like raw sewage!”
text:
My friends and I stayed here during the San Diego Comic-Con last weekend. Here's a breakdown of this hotel:
Positives:
 -The prices were very affordable (~ $89/night).
 -The housekeeping service was prompt and very thorough.
 -They had a pool, but we never used it.
 -There was plenty of parking.
 -The air conditioning was FREEZING cold (thank goodness!)
 -Our room also had a microwave, a mini-fridge, a blow dryer, and a coffee maker.
 -Free cable TV!
Negatives:
 -Although we arrived at around 12:30 and the room was already made up, the front desk told us it would be "about an hour" until we could move in. (We moved in anyways.)
 -There was a perpetual smell of raw sewage in the room; especially in the bathroom. Nothing was leaking and we couldn't track it down to a source, but the smell never went away.
 -The two beds weren't firm enough, and the pillows were too thick.
 -There was no free shampoo or conditioner; they want you to use a single, unlabeled, wall-mounted soap pump in the shower (like at an auto body shop!)
 -The cereal dispenser constantly jammed at the continental breakfast. The maid had to use tongs as a work-around.

name: San Diego Marriott Mission Valley
title: “a most disappointing Marriott and certainly not on my repeat visit list”
text: Easy to access and well located to city and most major attractions, but a most disappointing Marriott and certainly not on my repeat visit list. Rooms are small as are the bathrooms, and in need of updating - soon! Concierge lounge is also small and uninviting. The patio area and the pool are nice.

name: Hilton San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Perfect location and wonderful service”
text: I was fortunate enough to win this hotel for a reasonable rate on Hotwire. When I arrived after a 5-hour drive from Phoenix I as so relieved to find this is a beautiful, smaller scale hotel in a fantastic location, right across from the convention center and in the heart of the Gaslamp District. I was greeted on every turn with incredibly friendly and helpful service from the valet to the registration desk. My request for a higher floor room was kindly accomodated with an awesome corner room with views of the water on one side and city lights on other side. What else can I say? Great free apps and drink specials at happy hour, gorgeous clean pool, very quiet rooms, fantastic service...and did I mention the awesome location? I will definitely be returning!

name: San Diego Marriott Del Mar
title: “Nice property.”
text: The property is very clean and the rooms appear new. Although I did not visit the pool area, it looked very nice from my window and appeared to have a good social scene. The hotel is about a twenty minute walk (5 minute drive) from the Del Mar Town Center, which has some good dining and shopping options. The property isn't really far from things to do, but you pretty much have to drive if you want a good selection. Downtown Del Mar and the ocean is about a 12-15 minute drive. I had a few relatively minor service failures, but although annoying at the time they didn't really taint my view of the overall stay. The Hampton Inn next door is a bit better value and seemed clean (no parking fee, free breakfast and slightly lower rate) but the Marriott definitely has a nicer property.

name: Western Inn & Suites
title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: This hotel's convenience to everything in Old Town is it's biggest plus. Price is not bad either. It is a comfortable, no-frills hotel. The king-size bed was comfortable (fitted sheets didn't fit, though), the water pressure in the shower was incredible. After staying in many foreign countries I've come to appreciate this. A privacy wall outside my room made me feel a bit closed in. There is a nice balcony area with tables on the back of the hotel. I found it accidentally. Sanjay at the front desk was very friendly and helpful.

name: Ramada Inn & Suites Gaslamp/Convention Center
title: “No sink in the bathroom!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel with a friend for 3 nights. We were in town for a convention. 
Pros: 
-Gaslamp location, close to the convention center
-Internet access
-Large suites with televisions in each bedroom. 
Cons: 
-Old unrenovated building with old fixtures, slow elevators and dank feeling. 
-Bathroom was visibly dirty when we checked in. However, the hotel staff immediately cleaned up when we complained. 
-Layout was strange: two separate rooms with bathroom in hallway. The bathroom had only a toilet and a shower-- no sink! On top of that, only one of the bedrooms had a sink in it, so the person staying in the second room had to walk in to the other bedroom just to wash hands or brush teeth. So strange!

name: Hampton Inn San Diego - Downtown
title: “Very accommodating staff”
text:
We stayed here for two nights prior to a flight home. The staff recommended two fabulous restaurants and the shuttle bus took us everywhere that we wished to go. Everyone was extremely polite, cheerful and helpful. 
The room was excellent as always and the pool was a BIG plus after a busy day of sightseeing. Although the Amtrak is a little noisy right behind the hotel, the front rooms are fine. This is a problem along the entire stretch of Pacific Highway regardless of which hotel you choose. Must see: San Diego Zoo, Seaport Village. Places to eat: Top of the Market and Crocce's

name: Sheraton Suites San Diego
title: “San Diego Stay”
text: The staff, particularly the Concierge, Craig, was outstanding. The beds were very comfortable, rooms were spacious and quiet. My only disappointment was that I upgraded to the club level, but the club lounge was not available in the evening.

name: Hard Rock Hotel San Diego
title: “Sensacional”
text: Sem dúvida é um dos hotéis mais modernos do mundo. Além de ficar muito bem localizado no início da Gaslamp Quarter, do Petco Park, do Centro de Convenções, etc. O quarto é bastante confortável. O hotel em si oferece diversos tipos de entretenimento, pois tem bares, boates e restaurantes dentro de suas dependências. Recomendo o Hard Rock sem dúvida!

name: Lafayette Hotel
title: “More like a Motel 6”
text: Terrible, don't know how they got 3 stars, the guy who gave it to them must be high on something becoz this is a motel not a hotel and there was construction during our stay which made it worse!

name: Hilton San Diego Mission Valley
title: “Great location, great staff, loved it”
text: I had heard that Mission Valley wasn't that great but I was plesantly surprised with the Hilton Mission Valley. The rooms were pretty standard for a Hilton but the staff was very helpful, the free appitizers for HH guests were huge and the free breakfasts for HH members were excellent. My wife enjoyed the pool and the fitness facility and was able to do a little laundry while there since the washer/dryers are in the fitness room. Also the location turned out to be right in the middle of lots of restraunts and shopping. All around it's a great pick.

name: HYATT house San Diego/Sorrento Mesa
title: “Good Value”
text:
I booked this hotel for my trip to welcome my son home from his recent deployment. Its close proximity to the Miramar base and more importantly - the availability of a kitchen, so that he could enjoy a couple of Mom's home cooked meals. 
The size was perfect and allowed each of us adequate privacy as well. The desk and grounds staff were wonderful and common areas were clean and updated. I will agree with the other reviewers that the housekeeping staff could use some training and supervision. 
They did not replace coffee or toiletries and came to the room at erratic and often inconvenient times. Two separate days they knocked once, then immediately used a pass key to open the door without waiting. It was frightening. All they would do is make beds, empty trash and dropped clean towels and that was the extent of their service. The carpets and furnishings are dated and worn, but overall the hotel was clean and comfortable. 
Finally, the quality of the OASIS was incredible. Whether eating in the dining room or ordering room service. They were first class service and some of the best tasting food ever!

name: Western Inn & Suites
title: “Bedbugs galore!”
text: I am very sorry to have to write this, but it's a moral issue to warn other travelers. We checked in very hopefully & fell asleep immediately. Waking up 3 hours later I noticed 2 small bugs & killed them. Then my wife awoke, I mentioned it to her & she searched & over a 30 minute period found 6 more. These were BEDBUGS! Bloody & with a distinctive smell (I was really not familiar with them, but she was from her youth). THEY ARE EXTREMELY HARD TO ERADICATE, HIDE IN CREVICES OF CLOTHES, LUGGAGE & ARE THE ABSOLUTE NIGHTMARE OF HOTELS & APARTMENTS. MASSIVELY EXPENSIVE TO GET RID OF. THEY ARE MAKING A "COMBACK" IN NEW YORK HOTELS. We decided to check out immediately, praying we didn't take of the creatures with us. (I only found one in my briefcase later). The hotel was very nice about cancelling all our charges, but it scared us to death. These bugs can easily migrate from room to room in a hotel or apartment building -- or back to your home inside your luggage, & sometimes cost as much as $10,000 to kill them in a single apartment. We hope we were lucky enough not to take any with us. We checked our luggage thoroughly several times. BE WARNED! No cheap price is worth bedbugs. We moved up the road slightly to the Comfort Inn of Old Town, got a great rate (of course we checked in at 3am in the morning - which they held for the length of our stay) & were very satisfied with our stay for 4 days.

name: San Diego Marriott Mission Valley
title: “great location within San Diego for a great value”
text:
We stayed at this hotel due to it's proximity to Qualcomm Staduim (we were in town for a football game). The hotel is about a mile from the Stadium, but the hotel recommended we take the trolley (not because of safety, just out of convienence). I'm very glad we took their advice. The trolley is just across the street from the hotel and runs until midnight during the weekend. It stops every 15 minutes. For $2.50/person/trip (or $5 all day) the trolley will take you all over San Diego, which is a great plus! We left our vehicle at the hotel the following day and took the trolley to Old Town. When we returned, our car was safe in the parking lot. 
As for the hotel.... It's in a business area, but it is kept very clean and is nearby to shopping and restaurants (if you'd prefer to not eat the hotel restaurant, we did not eat there). There's a beautiful pool (and hot tub) along an amazingly manuicured area. Although we arrived to the hotel early (noon), they were able to give us a room on the 8th floor with a balcony and king-sized bed, overlooking the pool area. Our room also came with a mini-fridge (however, I'm not sure all rooms are equipped with one). There was a nice breeze that came in through the sliding door at the balcony and we slept with the door open to take advantage of the fresh air. At 5pm, they have cookies and milk in the lobby. The front desk is more than happy to help you with directions and ideas (even providing maps) of things to do in the surrounding area. They were the ones that suggested us leaving our car in the parking lot the following day and taking the trolley into downtown and the surrounding areas. The hotel is also very family-friendly. All in all, it was a great stay with very friendly staff. I wouldn't hesitate to stay at this hotel again!

name: HYATT house San Diego/Sorrento Mesa
title: “Great Value”
text:
Found this hotel on Hotel.Com Great value and nice room. 
Very clean and spacious. Came back to the hotel about 11PM on Saturday night and was completely quiet. Was a little further to Sea World and San Diego Zoo than I thought but not a bad drive. Hotel suite was very clean and comfortable. Would be a nice place to stay for an extended stay had a small kitchen. Had a nice pool area and small workout room. Grounds were kept up nicely. Overall a comfortable hotel at a great value. I would stay there again.

name: BEST WESTERN Seven Seas
title: “Motel im Hotel Circle von San Diego”
text:
Das Motel habe ich für eine Nacht gebucht. Ein Grund war der günstige Preis. In unmittelbarer Nähe befindet sich eine große Mall (Fashion Mall), die man auch zu Fuss ereichen kann. Die Innenstadt oder die Hafenregion von San Diego ist ca. 9 KM weit entfernt. Hier kommt man am besten mit dem eigenen Auto hin. Das Motel entspricht dem üblichen amerikanischen Motel Standard (Mehrere Gebäude mit zwei Stockwerken und Parken vor der Haustür) und ist für Kunden mit geringen Ansprüchen geeignet. Entsprechend ist auch die Kundschaft eher aus der amerikanischen Mittel/Unterschicht. (Warnschilder an der Tür fordern auf, keine Wertsachen im Zimmer zu lasen und immer die Tür abzuschliesen). Im Hotel befindet sich ein kleines Restaurant fürs Frühstück (nicht im Preis inklusive), welches ich nicht genutz habe. 
Das Bad im Zimmer war nicht sehr sauber aber ok. Ebenso das Zimmer und das Bett.

name: Hampton Inn San Diego - Downtown
title: “Loved this Hotel!”
text: The beds were so comfortable! The staff was extremely helpful (getting us shuttles to Sea World and the Zoo)! And the breakfast was AWESOME! I can't tell you how much my boyfriend and I talk about the biscuits that were at the hotel. Plus we had free wireless internet! The location can't be beat either, we could walk downtown, to the harbor, and the ferry to Coranado. Will definitely stay here the next time I'm in town.

name: Hilton San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Great location, just don't park there!”
text:
Just to clarify the $35 mandatory parking fee is only mandatory if you choose to park at the hotel. There are plenty of parking lots nearby, or between 6pm and 8am, you can park outside the hotel for free at one of the meters! Its very safe as the valet is present 24/7/365!!
The hotel is very modern in style, located just over from the the Convention Center and at the bottom of the Gaslamp area. The hotel is split into two parts - the main hotel or The Lofts, accessed by a private elevator. I was staying in The Lofts, amazing rooms, and upgraded to one with a whirlpool bath. Large oversized rooms await for you in The Lofts, very comfortable king bed, large lounge area, 42" plasma, games station, fridge for your goodies, coffee machine, and then separate bath and separate shower room with window into the lounge area.
Staff really great and accomodating, very present and willing to help. Pool area is small, and can be noisy as it overlooks the tram and amtrak railway so you do get the clanging of the railway crossing bell and the sound of the trains horn. This is the only downside I can think of.
Handy for all of the tourist attractions, close to all of the restaurants in Gaslamp and the Horton Plaza Shopping Center. Ralph's supermarket just around the corner with loads of goodies and fantastic food to go.
Great for families and business alike - a really good hilton!

name: BEST WESTERN Yacht Harbor Hotel
title: “Nice clean hotel in a good location.”
text: I have stayed in this hotel in May 2012 for 3 nights, my room was very clean and comfortable, breakfast nice, location excellent. Internet connection was acceptable.They even gave me free lift to the airport on the way back. Overall I was very happy with this hotel considering very reasonable price I paid.

name: Lafayette Hotel
title: “THE worst ever!”
text: I don't know where to begin. Like another reviewer stated, I wanted to like this historical hotel. However, when we drove up I wanted to cry. I can't name just one thing wrong with it, because there are so many!! I've heard it is under construction to update, but it is still horrible (plus, the only signs of work being done are some orange cones in the lobby, a couple of flyers regarding the work, and a plastic runner going up a stairway....on very very old carpet). The hall leading to our room went passed two offices where you couldn't help but look through the windows into rooms with messy desks. Next, when we opened the door to our room I was in shock! Depressing green walls, smelled bad, the bed was as hard as a rock (harder than the beds I've slept on in China, where they like their beds hard). I couldn't even sleep on it and spent two days with a sore back just from laying on it. Looking out the window from our room we were sickened to see an open concrete area with nothing but windows looking out on it. The only other things to see were a ladder and a maid/room service cart. The windows looked like they hadn't been cleaned in 50 years, with cracked glass and a totally messed up lock. There was hair on the bathroom wall, no counter space...only a small poorly place glass shelf directly above the sink (watch out when you wash your face or you'll hit your head!). After the shock of the room settled in we decided to check out the pool area. It looked NOTHING like the website, which boasted a beautiful setting. The first thing to see was the sign on the gate going in stating that people that are not staying there must pay $5. Does that mean anyone can come and use the pool? In short, the pool was as gross as the rest of the place. I wouldn't set foot in the pool and was totally overwhelmed with how depressing and filty everything looked. I've seen low income housing that looked better! After the first night we couldn't take anymore and checked out. At first one desk clerk told my husband that we would have to be out by 11:00. He told her we needed time to find another place and couldn't be out by noon. That appeared ok. However, when we went to check out another clerk indicated that it didn't matter when we were checking out. Hmm? I prefer hotels that are truthful upfront. Overall, even if they are fixing things up, there appears to be no pride in the condition of the entire hotel. They should be ashamed! At least they should take their pictures off the website, since they are nothing like what it really looks like. I will be adding photos so you can see for yourself.

name: BEST WESTERN Seven Seas
title: “abbastanza confortevole”
text: l'albergo molto carino, il personale abbastanza gentile, l'ambiente confortevole. poca confusione, ognuno aveva il suo spazio. piscina forse troppo piccola con scarzo servizio, ma tutto sommato non male. facilmente raggingibile. economico.

name: Marina Inn and Suites
title: “I can't believe this place was so cheap!”
text:
I paid less than $40 dollars for a stay here on a Friday night. Considering the location, it was a great value! 
I arrived and this incredibly sweet lady named Mel was so helpful! She answered all of my questions about San Diego, events happening in the city, and transportation options. (I ended up going to December nights in Balboa park, an annual festival in the city). 
For those of you who normally stay at luxury hotels, note that you won't have any of those amenities here. But for a budget hotel, this place hits the spot. Most rooms have a great view of the ocean and there's a small continental breakfast with muffins, hard-boiled eggs, and juice. It's located right next to Little Italy and the pier so go take a leisurely walk and explore if you're ever staying at this hotel!
The only downside about the hotel would probably be the parking situation. I checked in at about 5pm and took the last available parking spot. You'd have to do street parking otherwise.

name: Kings Inn Hotel
title: “A special weekend”
text: We visited the Kings Inn for our 45th anniversary, last weekend. We had been there before and it was the same great experience. The rooms are all cozy and clean and the staff, especially David, were very friendly and helpful. We love the Waffle Spot as you can have a GREAT breakfast and not want for lunch at all. Dinner at the Amigo spot is very special especially on Friday and Saturday evenings when there is live music. Our server, Mari was exceptional every night we were there!! We really love the hotel and will be there whenever we are in SD.

name: Hilton San Diego Resort & Spa
title: “Great stay”
text:
What a nice surprise. I made this reservation based solely on mapping services trying to get a Hilton close to the airport. What a beautiful location. Though I was on a quick business trip, I wish I could have stayed longer. Trip back to the rental car providers was quick. Had the breakfast buffet at the onsite restaurant. Very good low carb and protein options.
I was also literally within 2-3 miles of my business appointment

name: Extended Stay America - San Diego - Hotel Circle
title: “Terrible customer service”
text: This motel doesn't have a business office so I asked the front desk clerk to help me print my boarding pass but she refused to so I walked over to the Ramada Inn next door and the clerk there printed my boarding pass without hesitstion even though I wasn't a guest there. That is what good customer service looks like Extended Stay management. Next, I called the front desk to schedule a wake up call. It took me 3 attempts calling 10 minutes apart letting the phone ring for about 2 minutes each call before someone picked up the phone. Also, my room had leaking shower that dripped all night and long strands of hair were found in my "clean" sheets.

name: Hilton San Diego Airport/Harbor Island
title: “BEWARE: This Hotel Double Charged Us!”
text:
When we checked in to this hotel they tacked on an extra $100 in addition to the hold they put on my debit card for our entire stay. Said the $100 was for "incidentals" (after the fact) but never disclosed this to us up front. I was reassured when I checked out the hold would be immediately released on that amount, however it was not at all. 3 days after checkout I see that they have deducted nearly $700 from my checking account, which is DOUBLE a 2-night stay PLUS the $100 "hold" for incidentals (we never purchased anything other than parking). When I called to contest the double charge, I was told (once again after the fact, and contrary to what I was told when I checked in) that I would have to wait "up to 5 business days" to receive the credit back to my checking account. Wait... this was supposed to be a HOLD, not a CHARGE. Watch out, what they tell you up front is WAY different than it actually is.
While the room itself was decent, the bathroom was dirty, with nasty black hairs around the base of the toilet and tub. Elevators were dominated by cleaning staff with their carts, so it was not pleasant getting jammed in there like that. Apparently they don't have a service elevator. The food was outrageously expensive and mediocre too. The manager was rude and very uninformed, told me to "call back later" to talk to accounting if I had a problem. All in all a very disappointing experience.

name: Hilton San Diego Mission Valley
title: “Great value if...”
text: Very nice place and a great value for the San Diego area if you use Priceline...got it for under $80 per night on the weekend.

name: Hilton San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Hilton was a gas gas gas!”
text:
nice contemporary look- great artwork all over the hotel. Gym is fresh and new- free weights, new machines, roomy. Right across the street is the convention center and there are a great set of stadium steps people are doing their workouts on. as well as the waterfront parks on the otherside. 
 Bedrooms were decent sized , the usual comfy hilton beds, well equipped, we liked the little touches like milano cookies at the turndown service- 
Internet service was great and free, wired in the room and wireless in the lounge/lobby area. careful if you are a light sleeper- the hotel is built right on the train tracks and the trolley/train blows its horn at exactly 4am so depending on the side of the hotel you are staying.... Also- friday and saturday gets crazy at the hard rock hotel next door- avoid that side as well on the weekend. restaurant/ bar area is small but comfortable- the breakfast buffett was amazing (frsh squeezed orange juice) but overpriced at $19- Very helpful and friendly staff in the restaurant and throughout. We enjoyed people watching from our breakfast table every morningwith all the walkers, joggers and dog walkers right outside on the bike path in front of the hotel. The location was wonderful with access to the trolley which we used to go everywhere including seaworld and the beaches- so easy we cancelled our car rental! The Gaslamp district is right out the door and we had a ball going to restaurants, movies etc every night. The consierge was very professional and you can buy tickets to the zoo, seaworld etc. from him at a slight discount and charged to the room. - All and All our family had a wonderful stay and would come back again... Good restaurants we ate at RA- great sushi bar in a lively settig - young crowd, al aqua 2, florence style italian. Yardhouse- 200 beers on tap- decent food, Gaslamp tavern- decent pub stle lunch, Freds Mexican- decent- family friendly- the food court at Horton Plaza is an amazing selection- with some healthy options- we had the mongolian grill- pick your own meats and veggies and they wok it up with no oil. good lunch Movie theatre in the horton plaza had better selection, but the one on 5th is a cool old classic place and comfy seats... gotta go through the new hard rock and the bar on the fourth floor- california outdoor living at its best- firepits, city view, cabanas..

name: Days Hotel - Hotel Circle by SeaWorld
title: “Unsatisfactory”
text: On arrival,on early morning we were told that the only room would be in different building on the second floor. This is not what we had reqested on reservation. I recently had a knee replacement and had requested that a room on the first floor. The clerk was very much "take or leave it" attitude.

name: Hilton San Diego Resort & Spa
title: “Check-in was a breeze”
text: Thanks to William and T.C. our weekend vacation started off on a high-note. Both William and TC were all smiles as they helped to find us the most scenic room just steps from the beach. They talked with us about resort activities and ammenities. We even took advantage of the steam room in the spa followed by the lavendar scented towels -- how refreshing! This is a great couples or family get-away with fantastic staff!

name: Lafayette Hotel
title: “Not as bad as some reviews I have read”
text:
My daughter and I stayed there for 3 night in early April. I was a bit apprehensive because of the bad reviews I have read. When I called in advance and asked for a renovated room, the hotel operator laughed at me and said "Ma'm, you are asking for what we don't have based on your reservation," as if to say that for the discounted price($98.00/night for King) on Orbitz, I had to settle for whatever they were going to give me. After putting me on hold for a little while, she came back and said that all the rooms in the main building had new carpets and new paint. Since this hotel was the closest to where my aunt was staying (seeing her and helping her with some personal business was the main reason for this trip), I decided to take a chance. Well, it wasn't so bad. Our room on the first floor facing the pool was acceptably clean just smelled old. Bathtub and showerhead did need some upgrading. I oftern heard some sort of maintenance noise through the wall. Free breakfast with waffles was OK, needed more fruits though. Hotel staff could use some people skills and 
smiles, too. I'm used to more friendly service and I live in New York City! Overall, it was OK. The old hotel did possess certain charm and uniqueness that are different from what typical budget hotels offer. Would I stay there again? Maybe if the price was right.

name: Marina Inn and Suites
title: “Clean and Comfortable!”
text:
We drove to San Diego for an annual gathering and needed a place to stay during our busy weekend. We booked ahead and got a great rate through John at the front desk, who was a pleasure to deal with, as was the woman who checked us in. 
The rooms are clean, comfortable and basic. My room had cable tv, a small fridge, microwave, a safety deposit box, and a clear view of the marina. The continental breakfast was individually boxed cereal and muffins, hard boiled eggs, coffee, tea, juice, and milk.
Here are my pros and cons:
PROS
-great location (easy access to major highways and a short walk to the marina, cruiseport, and the fabulous restaurants of Little Italy, including a late night hand-tossed pizzeria!)
-free WIFI (it was slow at times but sufficient for a quick check of email or googling for directions)
CONS
-parking (parking is free but limited. There seem to be just enough spaces for one car per room and we didn't have any problems during our stay but I could see parking being an issue for someone else)
-noise (the inn is on a busy intersection, near train tracks and also near the flight path of the San Diego airport. You will hear passing cars most of the time, an occasional train and a plane or two fly over. It's not so bad...more like background noise. If you are sensitive to noise, bring earplugs for when you sleep. We grew up in the city so we are used to background noise and we slept like babies...without earplugs!)
Bottom line...There is no swimming pool, no spa, nothing fancy. If you want the Ritz, stay elsewhere. If you are going to be out and about and need a clean, comfortable place to stay on a budget, then this it it! We would definitely stay here again.

name: Hilton San Diego Resort & Spa
title: “Perfect to relax - watch out for location”
text:
recently visited this hotel, and it's a gorgeous hotel in a beautiful setting. the pool area is fantastic and it has everything you need on one site.
the only down-side i would say was the location, we hadn't realised it was so far from downtown and being on holiday from England we did not have a car, so it was a taxi journey to Mission beach or downtown.
the dinner service was expensive and although the food was good, it was no better than other restaurants we went to so we felt this was overpriced and ate from the pool bar the other nights. there is also some building work going on, which we were not notified of before our visit and caused some noise disturbance when we were around the pool.
overall, for a relaxing trip and to stay by the pool it's definitely worth going, but if you want to be out and about I would choose somewhere closer as there isn't much going on around the hotel.

name: Hilton San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Great location for PETCO!!”
text: I booked this trip at the last-minute through Hotwire, so I had no idea what I was getting when I decided to try their offer. I am glad we did! We went to San Diego for 2 nights, specifically to see our favorite team, the D-Backs, take on the San Diego Padres. This hotel has a GREAT location for any number of things. It is less than 1/4 mile from the ballpark, across the street from the convention center, and right in the heart of the Gaslamp District. The rooms were nice, clean, and well appointed. There was plenty of room in a 2 double-bed set-up, where we added a portable crib for our 1-year old. The staff, especially valet and bellmen, were especially helpful. Yes, $30/day seems steep for parking, but with the convenience of valet and in/out service, it really couldn't be beat. Considering you're going to pay $10-$20 to park at the ballgame anyway, it was a great deal in our case. The restaurant was average, though we only ate breakfast there. The buffet did not look too good, but the "Gaslamp Benedict" was great. I don't know that I would have been as happy had I paid the $200+ range the rooms usually go for, but at $119/nt. through Hotwire, I was especially pleased.

name: BEST WESTERN Yacht Harbor Hotel
title: “Must be an old apartment”
text:
Let me start this review off by saying I am a travel agent, and so I got a really good rate at this hotel. I like to check out hotels for my clients and I figured this one might be good because they shuttle to and from the airport and the cruise ship terminal in San Diego. After staying here for 2 nights, I don't think I would recommend it. First off... when we drove up to the hotel, there is no front drop off parking. It looks like there is an area for it, but there is a sign that says No parking / Fire lane. So we had to drive around to the side of the building and bring our luggage to the lobby. As you drive up you kinda look at the place and wonder why it looks like an apartment. We were apprehensive right from the start.
Second... when we checked in the guys didn't seem very organized and couldn't handle more than 1 person checking in. Someone butt in front of me and nobody said anything. Then when we got our room, we took our luggage and wandered to our room. As we were walking there I mentioned to my husband about being on the first floor and that it would seem they are putting us in the bad room because we got such a good rate... boy was I right. Our room was just barely bigger than a Manhatten hotel room. We couldn't even fit the luggage cart into the room. They also gave us a room facing the construction. We figured that is where we had to stay because we got a good rate. Once I turned on my laptop and found out the internet wasn't working there, we went back to the desk and told them to get that fixed. At this point a lady was at the desk and she seemed much more effecient. She found us another room, that was way bigger and the internet worked. So we took it.
Third issue... I think truly this is an old apartment because the sound travels everywhere. The patio door to the outside seems to be very thing and you can whisper outside at the street and you can hear it in the room. It was horrible. I don't think the door closed properly, but even so, the sound was horrible. We got woken up one morning at 1am and had to phone down to customer service to inform them that a bunch of guys where in the pool smoking pot and partying. Since the pool is just around the corner from the lobby, I don't understand why they didn't hear it. 
The ladies who were at the front desk where great and always helpful. The cleaning staff was good and the continental breakfast was better than I had expected (considering the hotel). I don't even think for the price (travel agent rate), I would stay there again. It was way to noisy and the fact that they gave us that horrible room in the first place, was a bad first impression. I won't be recommending it to my clients.
If you are forewarned about this place, then it is ok. Everything was clean and it was so nice and close to everything. Maybe if they did some updates to the rooms and made it look a little more like a hotel and not an apartment, it would be ok.

name: Holiday Inn San Diego - On The Bay
title: “Good hotel, but parking is a rip.”
text: I didn't realize that parking was so costly at this location. I made the mistake of assuming that parking was included. Beyond that, the room was really nice. I had a balcony facing the city with good view of all city lights. We enjoyed that. Later in the night though, it got quite noisy when a train or trolley (not sure which) came through the city. It gave off a loud screaching metal on metal sound. There were other industrial creepy sounds as well throughout the evening in downtown San Diego. Definitely would not live in that urban setting. Back to the room, the bed was super comfy, the bathroom nicely decorated and adequately equipped with plenty of towels and what not. I recommend this hotel if you want a taste of downtown SD for a decent price. We booked through Hotwire and saved some money.

name: Marina Inn and Suites
title: “Best Bang for the Buck!”
text: I was on a lengthy search for a hotel nearby the beach, Sea World, downtown and the zoo until I came across Marina Inn at Grape St. and Pacific Coast Highway. It took me 10 minutes to decide after getting my quote. Once I mentioned AAA, I got a huge savings! When I got to the hotel, my room was ready to go with a pleasant view of the harbor. Once I began driving around, I realized how close I was to everything! Zoo was right up the road, litterally. Downtown was about 5 minutes, Sea World was no more than 10 minutes away! Vicky P takes her job very seriously to work the best deals and ensures the trip runs smoothly! I couldn't ask for a better hotel, hence why I'm returning with my fiance this coming May.

name: Hilton San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Steps from the action, but only a fair hotel”
text:
Loved the location of this hotel, steps from the dining and nightlife options of the Gaslamp district. Hotel was on the smaller side (a plus), and had an intimate feel. As others have mentioned, parking fees sting, at $24 a day, plus tips. Bedding was extremely comfortable, but rooms were a little on the small side (we had a queen, not king room). You could hear every breath on the other side of the door to the room, which given the hotel's proximity to bars, meant several middle of the night awakenings by drunk guests.
We stayed at the hotel with our toddler, and though we had called to specifically request a crib, the front desk had no record of our request, and was out of cribs. It took well over an hour for them to track down a crib for us, and in the meantime we had a very crabby baby. We got our reservation for this hotel through Priceline ($102 a night over Labor Day weekend), which was a steal. I would return for the location alone.

name: Inn at the Park
title: “Family Get Away”
text: We felt like we stayed in a fancy hotel with the valet parking. Customer service was great. We had only been in the room for about 10 minutes when they called to make sure we had settled in ok and if we needed anything. It's also close to restarants and shopping. Also about a mile away from the San Diego Zoo. I would stay here again.

name: Marina Inn and Suites
title: “Excelente ubicación y servicio. Lo demás mediocre.”
text:
Muy bien situado frente al mar y muy cerca de la terminal de cruceros.
El hotel es viejo remodelado y arreglado con poco gusto. El baño no tiene bañera, es chico y el mío era un poco oscuro. la ropa de cama no me gustó aunque estaba limpia.
No obstante estos detalles la habitación era cómoda aunque se escuchaba un poco de ruido de la avenida.
El personal atento y servicial.
El desayuno un poco pobre y había que llevarlo a la habitación por falta de espacio.

name: Marina Inn and Suites
title: “Ottimo rapporto qualitá prezzo”
text: Nel complesso ottima sistemazione. Pulito, centrale e provvisto di parcheggio. Colazione classica dei motel californiani: caffè; thé; muffin; cereali ecc, peró in piedi nella piccola hall. La posizione é comoda nei pressi di down town e con la vista del museo marittimo. Pulito e camere accoglienti sempre in relazione al prezzo. Solo un Po rumoroso a causa della vicinanza alla stazione e all'aeroporto.

name: Hyatt Regency Mission Bay
title: “Spring Break with Kids - SeaWorld”
text:
This hotel is fabulous!!! 
Great pool area with hot tub and water slides was great for our kids. Only complaint would be that seating is somewhat limited. Some families that have stayed here before knew to go down to the pool area and reserve seats by the pool. I'm not really sure they should be allowed to do that, but I'm not really one to complain about it either. The hot tub was also a little small and was packed at night, but we squeezed in...
The rooms were nice size and very clean!!! 
The concierge was also very nice and helpful.
Food choices at and surrounding this hotel were very limited, and thus quite pricey...
We went to SeaWorld for at least a portion of each day we were there. On the map it looks like this hotel is right next to SeaWorld, but it is a good 20 minute walk to get there (and I walk fast). For a hotel of this size in this location, they really need to provide some sort of shuttle to SeaWorld!!! I guess they do in the summer, but not while we were there...

name: Days Hotel - Hotel Circle by SeaWorld
title: “Great Budget Hotel”
text:
For the room rate per night, this was a great budget hotel. All my family needs is a clean bed and clean bathroom and I got both of those. If your standards are higher and require fancier things, you should probably look elsewhere.
The customer service worked for me. When I checked in I asked if I can get a crib because I had a baby with me. Within 30 minutes of getting to our room, housekeeping showed up with a crib and two extra pillows. Also, when I asked where the nearest grocery store is located, guest services gave us the map and written directions are on the back, very easy to follow.
The location of the hotel is pretty good since you can easily pick it up off the highway.
I can't comment on the shuttle service because we did not use it.
I can't comment on the pool because it rained during our stay.
I can attest to previous reviews though that the walls/floors are thin because you can hear your neighbors around you.

name: La Quinta Inn San Diego Mission Valley
title: “Great Value!”
text:
We had a room with 2 queen beds. With 3 of us but it was a bit tight at times, but the room was updated and the beds and pillows comfy.
The breakfast was good and the location was awesome and so was the price!

name: Inn at the Park
title: “Super hotel in Sad Diego”
text:
My wife and I spent 4 nights here at the end of a 3 week trip to California. This was the best of the 7 places we stayed during the trip. We selected this hotel because of the location and free parking and were not disappointed. The hotel is right across from Balboa Park with the zoo, Botanical Gardens, outdoor concerts, and many fine museums. The parking was free and despite concerns there was always a place when we needed it.
It looked like the hotel used to be an apartment building. The room was huge. Besides the 2 queen beds there was a kitchen, dining area, dressing area, and bath. The wireless internet worked well as did the TV. There was a built in combination safe in the room and the staff was very friendly. One of the highlights was the dining area used for breakfast which was on the room level. Great selection of items with some hot dishes which were replenished frequently. Also a great view in all 4 directions including Balboa Park which is right across the street.
The only thing missing was a pool. If this hotel had one it would rate 5 stars in my book.

name: Comfort Inn Gaslamp / Convention Center
title: “ottima posizione x vivere la notte di San Diego”
text:
Nel quartiere + movimentato di San Diego!
Nel cuore di gaslamp - quartiere pieno di ristoranti, bar e locali.
Albergo pulito e con tutto l'essenziale.
Ideale x chi vuole passare qlc giorno a San Diego.
Le camere non sono molto grandi ma troverete tutto ciò di cui avete bisogno.
Dal ferro da stiro al microonde!!
Piccolino l'angolo colazione, ma ben organizzato.

name: The Horton Grand Hotel and Suites
title: “Affordable and great location!”
text:
This supposedly "haunted" hotel is a totally different experience. I paid about 1/3 of the price of others attending the same conference. The hotel is about a 5 minute walk to the convention center, it is across from a night club and very close to the best restaurants and bars in the Gaslamp Quarter. The location is excellent!! Do take earplugs for a Saturday night stay because the nightclub is loud and is open until 4am. I didn't have a problem with it because I read reviews prior to my stay and was prepared. 
The hotel gave me a bit of the vibe from "The Shining" movie, especially if you take a wrong turn or go to the wrong wing of the hotel, but it is such an interesting place to stay. It is not filled with the newest and best furnishings, but it embraces its history. The toilet really has a pull chain to flush it, the tv is hidden behind a gilded mirror above the fireplace. I absolutely loved the balcony, though never figured out how to turn on the fireplace (it wasn't really cold, I just wanted to try it). The room was clean and the one time I went back to my room for a nap and put up the "do not disturb" sign, I was later called to see if I would have liked my room cleaned. Do not count on the restaurant being open, but you don't have to with so many fabulous places nearby. There is a World Market store a block and a half away if you would like a bottle of wine, it would be cheaper than buying a glass anyhow. 
I will stay at this hotel again when I go back to San Diego for the value and the interesting experience of having an "out of the box" hotel.

name: La Quinta Inn San Diego Mission Valley
title: “Not a nice stay”
text: Ice machines all broken in my building - they charge you three bucks to do a single load of laundry, my room faced an auto shop so I got to listen to air wrenches all day and into the evening. The hallways were filthy, the room layout is awkward and cramped, my TV had an enormous hum that overpowered the sound on half the channels.

name: Hilton San Diego Airport/Harbor Island
title: “Great View!”
text: Got a Sat night thru PL for $90. The staff was courteous. Got a 5th floor room that was clean and well appointed. The bathroom was small, but clean. Overall the room was your standard room. However, the view...the view overlooking the harbor was excellent. One negative was the $17 parking if you have a car. Would definitly stay here again if for under $100 a night

name: Hyatt Regency La Jolla
title: “Good Choice”
text:
My wife and I stayed here this past weekend while visiting friends in northern San Diego. We got this hotel by bidding on Priceline in the La Jolla area at an $81 bid. With $19 in taxes/fees and then $20 for self-parking we still found this very reasonable for such a nice area.
We were able to check in at around 3pm and were given a room with 2 queen beds on the 14th floor with a nice view. There seemed to be a lot going on at the hotel with a wedding downstairs and a lot of weekend guests which made for a pleasant environment. 
The room showed evidence of a little wear but was nice and clean. There was a newer flat panel TV with a lot of channels including HBO. We liked the view from our room as well. We went across the parking area and had a great happy hour dinner at Flemings where they had some great $6 burgers from 5-7pm along with beer and appetizer specials. 
Overall we enjoyed our stay and would stay here again.

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Mission Valley/Hotel Circle
title: “Hip, clean, nice location”
text: I didn't want to leave this room; great bed, couch, computer setup, TV, bathroom was just ok. Convenient place to be in relation to getting to San Diego Airport. Nearby San Diego Zoo and Balboa Park. Best thing about this hotel was CLEAN, hip, quiet rooms but action downstairs if you need that. Bad thing was no free continental breakfast and food was pricey at Starbucks cafe. Walked a few blocks down the road and ate an awesome spot which had a wider menu than the hotel's cafe. not much around there except a mall across the expressway -- which is confusing north or south valley cirlce??? Went into nearby Old Town for dinner which is typical tourist trap spot, and another longer drive gets you to Gaslamp district for a more happening crowd.

name: Inn at the Park
title: “Great Staff, Spacious Rooms”
text:
With a short ride from the airport, a central location that's close to several great areas of the city and a spectacular staff - this was the perfect place for me to spend my birthday weekend.
The front desk staff were full of good recommendations for events, how to get around and where to eat. I even got a great recommendation for a facial. 
My room was a "studio" but huge, it had its own kitchen, a walk in closet, and a very comfortable bed. I had more room than I probably needed.
I walked to Balboa Park and the Zoo from the hotel, a long but beautiful walk and in a nice neighborhood. 
My next visit to San Diego will likely be booked at this same hotel.

name: Hilton San Diego Airport/Harbor Island
title: “Best Bedding Ever!!”
text: After reading the less than favorable reviews, I was a bit worried about staying at this facility. We had gotten a very good deal on the room so I was fully prepared to "grin and bear it." The entire stay far exceeded our expectations, however. In particular, the new beds and ultra-luxurious bedding provided one of the most comfortable sleeping environments we had ever encountered with soft, down comforters, luxurious, perfect pillows and high thread-count sheets. My traveling buddy was so enthralled that it was hard to get her out of her bed! We called the front desk the next morning to express our satisfaction and were told that the beds and bedding were all new. Good choice!

name: Quality Inn I-15 Miramar
title: “Good ratio price/amenities”
text: We, a family of 6, stayed for 2 weeks waiting to find permanent accomodations nearby. Service was very good and efficient. Swimming pool clean and kids friendly. Breakfast OK, except that if you wanted to have a cup of tea, you had to bring your own hot water from the kettle in your room, depending upon the goodwill of the person in charge the same morning! We also were surprised at room price fluctuations between the beginning and the end of our stay. I'd suggest that the management draws this fact to the customer's attention before hand.

name: La Quinta Inn San Diego Mission Valley
title: “Great place to stay - near everything”
text:
We lived on La Quinta for 5 nights on our vacation to San Diego and loved it. The breakfast was great and the service lady there was very friendly to the kids. We thoroughly enjoyed it.
Its really a place to come back after a hectic day and relax, though it does not offer any views, the swimming pool and spa are nice.
Couple of nights there were some noisy ppl in the pool after 10pm and management quickly shunned them.
Will surely recommend, more so for vacationer as its nearby everything, literaly 10 mins from all hot spots and does not come in the way of rush hour traffic.

name: Inn at the Park
title: “Loved Park Manor Suites”
text: Park Manor is an older property located adjacent to Balboa Park. The staff is welcoming, gracious, and accommodating. The local patrons in the bar/restaurant were also friendly. The complimentary breakfast served at the rooftop fulfilling. We enjoyed the young families who were also guests at the hotel. My husband and I were very pleased to have found Park Manor. When in the area again, we plan to have Lunch at the Top.

name: Days Hotel - Hotel Circle by SeaWorld
title: “Accomodations were fine; service was TERRIBLE”
text:
After waiting in line 20 minutes to check in, we were given a key that didn't open the door.
No biggie unless your room is all the way at the opposite end of the property.
Then, as we checked in, we inquired about the complimentary hotel shuttle that would take us to the cruise ship. We asked about the best time to take it...10AM or 12 Noon.
Clerk said 12 Noon.
Little did we know that we had to SIGN UP for the shuttle. 
I guess asking him about it wouldn't have tipped him enough to figure that we might WANT TO GO ON IT!!!!! Needless to say, when we came down at 11:45 to catch the shuttle, it was full and we had to wait an extra hour and a half for it to load up and take the guests then come back for us. No biggie, unless you're waiting there with a 3 and 4 year old and you now have no where to go.
BTW, don't forget to ASK for a receipt if you pay cash. As the same genius who caused all of these other problems forgot to mention that we paid in cash, so when we checked out, the clerk had no record of it.
Would I stay there again? 
Well, if they offer me a complimentary night for my inconvenience, I think I'd rather pay the money to get the piece of mind knowing that I won't have to go through THAT AGAIN!!!

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Mission Valley/Hotel Circle
title: “Very nice one night pre-cruise stay”
text:
I got this hotel thru priceline as a one night stay before our cruise. We arrived at 1:15pm Thursday March 31 and Veni H. was the one that checked us in. We were allowed to get to our room at that time, which was nice since we just drove from Orange County Airport after flying in from Portland and being up since 4am. I put down a $250 cash deposit which was returned the next morning, minus the $16 parking fee, so you do not need a credit card like a previous poster said. The room we were assigned was number 744, on the 7th floor overlooking the pool. The room had two beds and was nicely furnished. Everything, including the bathroom was very clean and working properly. The kids and I swam in the heated pool and really enjoyed the warm San Diego sun. The lobby was very nice and offered three computers with free internet and big screen televisions. The hotel was close to the Mission Valley Mall where we had lunch and close to the freeway for easy access. The only improvements I would suggest are that the faucet in the bathroom needs to be longer to make washing the hands easier and there needs to be four bath towels and not just three. It makes no sense to have a room for four with only three bath towels. Veni H. checked us out on Friday and she did a very good job and was very friendly and even knew my name. Overall, this was a great way to start our cruise vacation and I look forward to stay at this hotel again. Please feel free to see the pictures I took of our hotel stay and the video I will post on youtube. 
Robert Ghitea

name: Holiday Inn San Diego - On The Bay
title: “Just OK”
text:
My review will sound very similar to previous reviews. I booked through Priceline for a Friday and Saturday night weekend stay and got a $99 rate for a standard two double bed room with a city view. Check-in was ok, but staff was rather curt. Had trouble with priority club membership. Other staff throughout rest of stay was OK to good. Was placed in "North Tower." City facing rooms are probably as good as the $40 extra bayside rooms. At night, the view of the bay is unimpressive and because there are no walls separating each balcony, the city view is expansive and nice. Also, train noise will wake you up on the city side, but so will cruise ship horns on BOTH sides (they place one pair of earplugs in each room in the bathroom). My room was very worn. The handle on the bed stand fell off when I first tried opening it--making opening and shutting the drawer a real challenge. Wallpaper was patched in several places and stained in several places (quite visible). Carpeting was also stained in several places. Blankets had some crusty stains as well. Sheets were clean. Beds were OK---nothing like the high quality beds most chains have put in their hotels. Free wireless internet is one plus--especially given Holiday Inn still proves no free breakfast.
Parking was rather outrageous at 20/night for self-parking. In a nutshell, this Holiday Inn is an example of why many people are abandoning the chain for Hampton Inns and Courtyards. It is old, worn and tired.

name: Inn at the Park
title: “Definately not a cookie cutter type property”
text:
One night stay on a Monday in August 2006. I booked the Midweek Getaway through the "Specials" link on the hotel's website for $149 plus tax which incluses a Studio Suite, wine or champagne upon arrival in your room and $40 towards dinner at the hotel's restaurant downstairs. Champagne tasted cheap and the hotel restaurant is maybe a 2 or 3-star establishment with 4-star prices.
I arrived very early (8am). The hotel staff was happy to hold my luggage and provide me with a parking permit for their lot while I spent the day in Balboa Park and the Zoo. I got lucky and there was one open space in the small lot when I arrived. Still, free parking is a great plus considering downtown hotels charge $20-30 a day to park.
Check-in is the standard 3pm, but I was given a bit of a cold shoulder when I returned at 2:30pm and asked for my room. I was told it was still too early, but they gave me the room anyway.
Not exactly sure why, but I was given a two-bedroom suite on the 6th floor instead of the studio I had booked. This was a pleasant surprise. I had asked for a room overlooking 6th Avenue since there is construction on the south side of the property near the parking lot, but was told all rooms had already been assigned. 
My room overlooked the parking lot and Spruce Street. Construction was not an issue since we checked in as the crew was ending for the day and left early the next morning.
Anyway, the room was a huge, corner unit. Everything was very clean, and although there is no A/C in the hotel rooms, the corner gave great cross-ventilation so sleeping with the windows open with ocean breeze was excellent. The plumbing is a bit whacky; my toilet either did not flush or it flushed 5-10 times on its own. Water pressure in the shower is fine. Not much shelf or counter space for toiletries so we had to use a table that was just outside the bathroom door.
The kitchen was a nice perk, but we only used the fridge. I suppose if we had stayed longer, we would have cooked meals to save money.
My major complaint was that in the hallway near our room there were 5 or 6 drop cloths that remained there just until we were bringing our bags down to check-out. There was no one working in the hallway that I had noticed.
Before you leave, be sure to go up to the 7th floor and have your free continental breakfast. The breakfast is nothing special (bagels, cereal, fruit, juice, coffee) but the view is spectacular.
If I had the option, I would give this place a 3.5, but it just does not make it to a 4. The property has a lot of character and does not appear to need major renovations, but as you walk throughout the building and your room, you can see that whomever was in charge of painting did not pay much attention to detail. The windows do not move easily and the reception on both the TVs in our room was horrible.
The rooms did have a bit of a musty odor, and if you are a neat freak, you may get a bit of a dirty feeling. If you lack patience and do not have your bags with you, take the stairs as an average wait for the elevator was at least 2 - 4 minutes.
This is not a Hilton, nor did I expect one. For what I paid and for what I was given, I would recommend this hotel, especially if the Zoo is on your itinerary. If downtown and the marina is more your cup of tea, I suggest you find a hotel in that area since you are looking at a 15 minute cab ride (or take the 25 downtown the the Orange or Blue Trolley lines).
P.S. Normally I would not address an issue like this since, to me, it is a moot point: Hillcrest is apparently a gay community. Some have complained about this hotel and its relationship with that community. Personally, I have no idea what they are talking about. We walked around extensively: in the Park, on University Avenue and all the way down 6th to the hotel.
Now, perhaps because I have lived in the NY metro area my entire life I have become desensitized to things like this, but even so, there was nothing over the top going on in the hotel or the immediate area. Perhaps that is not the case on the weekends, but I certainly cannot confirm an "concerns" that have been expressed here.

name: Inn at the Park
title: “Quirky”
text:
Stayed 2 nights on June 20 and 21, 2006 - 2 adults / 2 children ages 4 & 6 years.
Call hotel for any directions. Don't depend on any online direction sites.
Quirky hotel. Parking lot is tiny. Staff okay. Hallways dark. Lobby golden chic. Elevator not accessible from lobby, you need to go up about 3 steps and down the hall - not that convenient. 
Junior Suite was lovely. Beds comfortable. Placed in front of the windows without headboards. Kids kept loosing their pillows throughtout the night. Room is large enough that the kids had extra space to play. Lots of closet space. Seperate kitchen area with a gas stove. Knobs on stove should be replaced - all worn. Make sure you pack some paper towels if you plan to cook. They only supply you with one towel and some dish soap. Kitchen cabinets smells musty when opened. Convenient store across the street.
Bathroom plumbing is awful. Toilet needs to be flushed several times. Tub drains very slowly. Blinds do not close completely.
Hotel directly across the street from Balboa Park and has a play ground area for kids right at the corner. Very convenient. Hotel was memorable because it wasn't a chain hotel and had personality. I would stay again especially if I wanted to go to the Zoo.

name: The Horton Grand Hotel and Suites
title: “Beautiful classic hotel”
text: Very grand french style hotel, with a magnificent entrance and hall. Staff were very helpful and the room was fantastic, like being in an old movie. The bed was so high I had to literally jump to get in, and I'm 5'7"! The downside was that there was no car park, so you have to spend on the valet service. The room didn't include breakfast, but there are cafe's and about 4 starbucks round the corner. Great location next to the lively Gas lamp distric, so you could walk to the bars and restaurants every night. There is a great shopping center very close, with trendy high street shops. Don't leave San Diego without going to Coronado Island, it has a fab beach and you can drink cocktails at the Coronado Hotel, where "Some like it hot" was filmed, a truly charming hotel.

name: Sheraton Suites San Diego
title: “Fantastic!”
text: If you are looking for an EXTREMELY comfortable, high-class hotel, this is it. The bed is a fantasy - I kept waking up before my alarm, fully rested and ready to go, because I actually slept the whole night very deeply. Better than at home, even! The rooms are very well appointed and clean, and the staff were all very friendly and helpful. About the only bad thing was the room service prices ($8 for one scoop of ice cream +$3 delivery charge +18% tip) and the parking lot was treacherous to get in and out of. Would definitely stay again!

name: Hyatt Regency La Jolla
title: “Warm and friendly staff but not the quality I expect from Hyatt”
text: The service was terrific and the staff was very professional. The location is great. However, I just didn't feel that I was staying at a Hyatt. The lobby is modern but with an awkward and empty feel to it. The rooms had modern muted colors but the furniture was bare bones basic with a build it yourself feel. The walls were thin, thin, thin and the doors were as light as a feather. I wasn't even sure the door was properly locked because it did not have a tight close. It is obviously an acquired property that they didn't completely renovate just put the veneer on. Comfortable but if you are looking for something of better quality I would look elsewhere.

name: Handlery Hotel San Diego
title: “Not to Bad”
text:
I stayed here for work in May, the service was great at check in and also in the restaurant. The lead in rooms are average and not attached to the main part of the hotel. I would recommend you up grade to a pool view room or a court yard for the location and view. If your in a standard room you have a view of the car park. This hotel is good value for money and also for people on a budget. Pool area in nice with a little pool side cafe.
There are also some great malls down the road and you can find some bargains!

name: Inn at the Park
title: “First Stay - What a pleasure”
text:
I am so glad I did not let the folks who rated this hotel as "Terrible" talk me out of my stay.
Agreed, if you are looking for a room at the W or a JW Marriot Experience...DON'T GO HERE!
If you are looking for a clean room with charm, a large amount of space, comfortable bed, attentive staff, free parking, and a unique experience...this is the place for you.
My room was large, the furnature was a collection of uniqe pieces and was well maintained. The bath robe was a nice touch on a chilly November morning. I had no banging pipes from the steam heat. I can simpathize if someone did have this experience, however, I did not have a problem at all. Don't miss the prime rib in the restaraunt downstairs... what a treat. The staff was very friendly and accomodating.
Will stay here again on my next visit!

name: Inn at the Park
title: “A delight in San Diego”
text: What a find - but not necessarily to everyone's taste. You will not like it if you are a fan of standard business hotels with formulaic furniture and no atmosphere (or high speed internet access or swimming pool). You will love it if you like a hotel which has collectible and individualistic furnishing and decor, big white fluffy towels, good toiletries, bags of space and the best view (and bagels) in San Diego at breakfast time. It is extremely and explictly camp, but also friendly to all. I had an enormous suite to myself - reminded me of scenes from a Coen Brothers film or The Big Sleep.

name: Holiday Inn San Diego-Bayside
title: “Great location and ammenities.”
text: We were assigned room 232 first. That room was small and dark. The window was basically covered by a big tree. It also smelled a little smokey. Called the front desk and was moved to 126. This was a great room that open out into the putting green area. The kids loved running around this area. The room was clean, nicely updated and roomy enough to add a small crib. The only negative was the HVAC system. It was very noisy. Actually, it would be quiet for a while but get noisy every few mins. Luckily, my wife and 2yr old daughter were able to sleep through it. Service was great. Since we couldn't have a microwave oven in the room, the front desk staff heated up milk for my daughter every night. Will definitely stay here again.

name: Radisson Hotel San Diego-Rancho Bernardo
title: “Just a minor notch below a top business Hotel”
text:
I've stayed here a few times in the past year. It has very minor issues that make it less than say, a Marriott, where everything is new & modern. But I paid about 30-40 percent less than a Marriott or Holiday Inn Express. I booked through a discount website.
Rooms are spacious with a sofa & coffee table in the living area, microwave, mini-refrigerator, drinking glasses made of glass.
Some Pros: 
Clean rooms.
Check-in was always smooth.
free internet. Currently it connects without any login issues, and bandwidth was never bad.
Restaurant on site, but not open 24 hours.
Modern one-serving coffee machine.
DVD players in each room, though I never tried any of them.
Some Cons (just minor issues): 
no free breakfast. A discount is offered IF you pay at check in.
TV's in 3 different rooms are old, like the CRT kind, one was flat screen but still CRT.
Cushions on sofas in 3 seperate rooms are rock hard! Maybe that's so no one sleeps on it?
Microwave was small and old (not quite ancient)
Guest laundry machines looked ancient!
Some furniture looked dated, maybe it's supposed to look antique?
I always got a room using Priceline so perhaps they always put me in a lesser room because I paid less. Lesser room means everything in the room was not new or the latest & greatest.
Pool looked fine surrounded by ample chairs & tables with umbrellas but I never used it.

name: Holiday Inn San Diego - On The Bay
title: “Location, location, location!”
text:
I'm a native San Diegan, displaced, who travels back to SD often. This is one of my two favorite hotels in San Diego, because of the great location. And if you get an odd-numbered room in the Tower, the view is SIMPLY SPECTACULAR. Other than that it's just a normal, ho-hum hotel; nice, clean, nothing too fancy but truly nice enough. The room service has odd hours but because there are so many great restauarants in walking distance, it's no big deal. Especially try the restaurant "The Fish Market", about a 3-block stroll south on Harbor Dr. Also, in Little Italy, try both Filippi's (great food cheap) and Indigo Grill (great food with modern twists, not real cheap, but an appetizer is a meal).
