The other great hotel is the Radisson in La Jolla, which has beautiful grounds. It's far away from the main part of San Diego but near UCSD, La Jolla, La Jolla Beaches, etc. Be sure to try the La Valencia hotel's Sunday brunch but most important, get reservations (and directions) to the well-hidden (and a bit hard to find) but amazing Marine Room. Great ambiance and food (if a trifle pricey), it has a small jazz band for dancing but it is RIGHT ON THE OCEAN. The waves literally lap at it. Just go for a sunset drink and appetizer instead of splurging on a full dinner: you will be SO GLAD YOU DID. It's adjacent to the La Jolla Beach and Tennis Club.
Anyway, depending on what you're looking for (spectacular view and good location are top in my book), I disagree that there are nicer hotels to be had for the money, if you get any kind of break at all on the room rate.

name: Hyatt Regency La Jolla
title: “Big thanks to a professional and accommodating staff”
text: We came into town just for one night to see friends. There was a line at check-in, so I used the automated check-in service but was informed there was no room available yet (it was 4 pm, however). I then spoke with someone at the front desk and she upgraded us and got us a better room -- that's service in my book. And the next day we asked if we could do a late checkout and again the staff came through to accommodate our request. For a big hotel chain, those little touches make a big difference.

name: Radisson Hotel San Diego-Rancho Bernardo
title: “Second Class treatment if Priceline or Hotwire”
text: If you book a room at this hotel through bidding at Priceline or through Hot Rates at Hotwire, you do not get the advertised amenities. Even though complimentary cocktails are touted on the Radisson site and on Priceline, the hotel refuses these to Priceline or Hotwire guests. And, the free complimentary breakfast that everyone else gets does not apply to Priceline or Hotwire guests. For instance: The hotel and Priceline refused to give free cocktails despite repeated representations that free cocktails applied to all guests (Priceline details of hotel, Radisson web site, and even the hotel guide in the rooms). It was very frustrating to repeatedly get a runaround, and not even an apology or even a recognition that the advertising was incorrect.

name: Holiday Inn San Diego-Bayside
title: “Unexpectedly good”
text:
Our family stayed here for 3 nights - our last 3 nights in San Diego. We were relocating out of the country for my husband's next assignment. Definitely a welcome comfort after weeks of packing and moving. 
The 5 of us stayed in a Suite. It was great! Very large living room with a Queen sofa bed and bedroom with 2 Queen beds. There was an LG HDTV the living and bedroom. Very spacious, it could fit all our stuff - about 10 luggages! Beds were very comfortable. Housekeeping was a little slow probably because only 1 staff took care of the whole section. Airconditioning was a little loud but the comfortable room more than made up for it. 
Our package included breakfast at their restaurant which was ordered from the menu. Excellent food and fantastic portions! The place also wasn't over crowded. Kids ate free. 
My husband had to complete a report so they gave him a private business lounge to work in for a whole day, complimentary. it was nice - couches, computer, printer, kashi energy bar and fruit was in the room. 
Free parking, free wifi, free 2hr bicycle rental and complimentary airport shuttle to San Diego airport. It is also facing the marina - you can ride/walk to shelter island on a nice day.

name: Hilton San Diego Resort & Spa
title: “FANTASTIC!!”
text: Always a pleasure to stay at this hotel! It's close to our favorite stops to visit, the beach, 10 mintue drive to the gas lamp district, museaums, and the best place on earth Sea World.

name: Holiday Inn San Diego - On The Bay
title: “Great value and location.”
text: Just spent three nights at the Holiday Inn on the Bay. This was my fourth stay at this hotel and I have never been disappointed. Anyone who wants a beautiful, ever-changing view of SanDiego Bay should request a bay view room in the south tower. We sat on the balcony after a day of sight seeing and just watched all the activity on the water and on the street as well as fireworks from Sea World at night. The hotel shuttle takes guests to the most popular spots around town but many attractions are walking distance, including Seaport Village, Horton Plaza, the train station, the Midway, harbor cruises and the Coronado Ferry. Very good value for nice rooms and friendly, helpful staff at a perfect location.

name: Hyatt Regency Mission Bay
title: “Would not go back.”
text: Room was musty smelling, stain on the ceiling, the door to the room would not shut properly, AC not working properly. Internet $6 for 15 minutes and $20/25 to park you car a DAY. REALLY! I am not a complainer but I was disappointed in this Hyatt. The one in Long Beach Ca was lovely. This one not so much. Big whoop they removed $40 from the parking charges and doubled my points they could have done better. Don't go there.

name: Holiday Inn San Diego - On The Bay
title: “Great location!”
text:
Booked this hotel through Priceline ($60), so expected the worst considering other reviews. However, I was pleasantly surprised.
This hotel is directly accross the street from the cruise ship terminal. The harbor excursions are very convenient (1/2 block south), as is the Star of India (1/2 block North). There is a seafood restaurant accross the street (Anthonys) which offers counter service (great if you're traveling with kids) with outside tables) and fine dining. 
Check in was satisfactory. My initial request (via phone) of a higher floor with bay view wasn't taken into consideration. However, the agent was quick to change rooms to a higher floor after a second request (bay view was $40 additional, which I declined). My room was in the South Tower (a short distance from the lobby and pool - if you want to be close tot he pool, request North Tower) on the twelth floor with a view of Downtown. Lots of construction across the street and the train terminal is also a short distance from the hotel. There was some train noise, but hardly worth mentioning.
Overall, out stay at Holiday Inn on the Bay was really nice. The employees were average, not overally friendly or attentive...but okay. The area was great - very quiet for a downtown location and convenient to all the major attractions. The hotel offers scheduled complimentary transportation to the Zoo and Horton Plaza as well as to the airport (1 1/2 miles away). None of the hustle and bustle of the Mission Valley area. I would stay there again.

name: The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
title: “Disappointing - poor customer service; bad location”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for 1 week. We had read the reviews and without knowing a lot about San Diego we mistakenly booked the Sheraton Marina. To be fair, there were some good points but overshadowed by some very obvious bad points. The Bad: 1. Customer service - The hotel is not very concerned about ensuring a pleasurable experience. We asked for a decent room since we would be there 1 week. Despite our request we were given a terrible room on the fourth floor with absolutely no view. When we complained, all we received was a lack-luster apology. This lack of customer service reflects poorly on Sheraton's reputation and I will opt for other hotels in the future. 2. Concierge - On our first day we asked the concierge for information on transportation. His response was dismissive and kept restating that taking a shuttle would get us where we want to be and it was cheaper. His information was incomplete and inaccurate. So we waited for a shuttle for 45 mins and eventually gave up after a bell hop advised a cab would be only slightly more money. We later learned the Sheraton is not renewing their contract with the concierge service. Again, Sheraton only offered a weak apology for the poor concierge service. 3. Location - Don't be confused like we were, this is an AIRPORT HOTEL. It is far from all the main attractions and it took us on average 1 to 2 hours a day getting to and from the hotel. It was also very expensive traveling to attractions and the options offered at the Hotel were not economical. Had we known, we would not have stayed at this hotel and we would have paid more for a hotel closer to downtown since the cost of taxis quickly makes up for the cheaper price. 
The Good: 1. The gym was fantastic and people would use it. 2. The pool was very good and the grounds were nice. 3. The restaurants were fair to good. But remember, there is nothing close so you are stuck at the hotel unless you pay $20 each way to go Little Italy for dinner.
Bottom Line: avoid this hotel if you are a tourist. If this is a layover for you or a convention, this would be a good hotel.

name: Holiday Inn Express San Diego Downtown
title: “Unsatisfied”
text: Upon check, we waited for 15 min before we were even acknowledged. Then we were waved over by Jennifer who immediately asked for a Credit Card and ID. She handed us the room keys, I had to ask where our room was and where we park our car. Once we got to the room there were pizza flyers on the ground, the room smelled like smoke and there was a wad of hair in the bathroom. We were only greeted once our entire stay. Customer Service horrible. The location (although a little sketchy at night) and view are the only compliments I can give.

name: Hyatt Regency Mission Bay
title: “Disgusting!!!!”
text:
Having stayed in a Hyatt in Florida a few years ago which we loved, we thought we would try this one, as it looked nice and was convenient for the San Diego Zoo and Seaworld. We waited 2 1/2 hours for check in as our rooms were not available! Quite honestly I wish we had left then as by the time we did get to our room 'Disgusting' doesn't come close to the standard of it! They tried to mask the awful smell of damp and mold with an over powering smell of room spray. There was mold on the air conditioner unit, the bins, the bath everywhere! There was a communal balcony, which left little privacy. It was noisy at night. The food in the main restaurant was inedible,the toilets in there had a strong smell of urine and someone was hoovering near us whilst we ate.
We checked out a day earlier even though we had already payed for it! Apart from concierge staff were very unhelpful. 
We would NEVER stay here again even if it was for free! Believe all the bad reviews that you have read!!!

name: The Horton Grand Hotel and Suites
title: “Good Location, Beautiful interior”
text:
I stayed at this hotel last month and was pleasantly surprised. Some of the reviews were not very complimentary, but I had no complaints. True, it is in a heavily trafficked area, so there is noise late into the evening, and early in the morning. However, it is in an EXCELLENT location, close to everything in the gaslamp district and walking distance to the trolley. The interior of the hotel is beautifully furnished with antiques and the numerous lounge areas are very nice. 
Staff was coureous and provide us with everything we needed.

name: Holiday Inn San Diego-Bayside
title: “Nice Facility but....”
text:
We spent a weekend in San Diego making arrangements for my son's wedding next April. We chose the Holiday Inn - Bayside because it is the closest ICH Facility to Shelter Island and the wedding hotel. I am a Priority Club member with ICH and prefer to use their hotels when possible. This is a large and spreadout facility. We were given what I assumed to be a premium room on the fourth floor of the tower building although being on the other side of the hallway and having a bay view instead of seeing the parking lot would have been nice. We only ate breadfast in the hotel as our days were busy and found it to be better than most Holiday Inn Restaurants. 
 Overall we had a pleasant experience with the hotel. The housekeeping staff seemed to be very limited in their ability to converse in English, about equal to my command of Spanish but we managed to make ourselves understood. The only concern and aggrevation I had was our neighbors across the hall. There were people in and out of the room continuously all night long each of the three nights we stayed there and they did not seem to care how many times the door slammed. Daytimes a Do Not Disturb sign hung on the door. (Yes I was tempted) Nocturnal activity of this type in a hotel normally leads me to believe that there may be some sort of illegal activities occuring. This is not what I expect of the upper floors of a Holiday Inn in a seemingly upscale neighborhood. Perhaps they have higher class criminals than we have in New York.

name: Town and Country Resort Hotel
title: “Birthday surprise!”
text:
We came to visit our daughter in San Diego to celebrate my birthday and stayed at the town and country. We were happy to find a clean room, beautiful gardens and very friendly service. The operations manager helped us to plan our visit in San Diego and had great restaurant recommendations! We took the old town trolly tour from the hotel which was a great plus. 
We really enjoyed our stay and look forward to the next time we visit San Diego and the town and country!!!

name: Holiday Inn Express San Diego Downtown
title: “A good place a a reasonable price”
text: I notice a bad review on the page. We had a small meeting at the HIE SD and it was a very good experience. The place isn't palatial but it is quite good. The staff were just great. Very interested and helpful. The rooms are adequate, the bathrooms are small. Everything is clean and comfortable. Good bed and free internet. Has a very nice little set of shuttle vans which will take you any where locally and of course pick up and drop off at the airport. They were working on the hall ways to rehab them while we were there. Good price. Walking distance but a hike to some parts of the downtown. Cab ride to Old Town

name: Holiday Inn San Diego-Bayside
title: “Holiday Inn Bayside was very comfortable”
text: We stayed at the Holiday Inn Bayside for one night before a cruise with a group of several friends. The hotel was very comfortable, our room was very nice and very clean, bed very comfortable. The front desk people were very accommodating. The hotel has a very nice pool area and a mini-golf. The bar was very fun (of course most of it was our group!), the bartender was very patient with our large group and said we were fun. The restaurant was good, we had dinner and breakfast there. Several in our group used the shuttle to the cruise port with no issues at all. We would stay here again.

name: Residence Inn San Diego Downtown
title: “Great Staff, Decent Hotel”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights on Dec 26th and 27th. First the positives, and why I say Great:
1) This hotel has great staff and a special thanks to Ian at the front desk. he was wonderful- extremely attentive to detail- went out of his way to try and arrange a big rental car for us- since we were 8 people 
2) It is right next to Little Italy - so great eating options right there
3) It is not very far from Seaport, Gaslamp and the airport- so high on the convenience factor
4) They offer a free shuttle- which is excellent and prompt
Decent:
1) this is by no means a 4 or 5 star hotel- hence amenities and rooms are as per a 3 star range
2) Most residence Inn's I have stayed at are certainly more spacious- so in this ones it fell a tad bit short
3) Rooms are nice/ decent. Not too big- even though they have a separate living and bed room- they are tiny. Just enough for 4 of us (2 adult two small kids)
4) right next to railway track
But overall- for the price and location- it was good

name: The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
title: “Horrible experience”
text:
Ok, Sheraton Marina management - this is the review I told you I would be writing.
I read all the bad reviews before I booked but thought I could work around the problems 
Where to start. Too much to write about in one review but the front desk consistently lied to me and were very rude. Essentially I had booked two Club Level rooms and they could only provide one room total. They gave me no options. They said they would do ME a favor and not charge me for the other room! The room they didn't have! What?
Its clear that tourists (even well paying ones) are low on the list at this hotel. Unless you are staying here for a conference, do yourself a favor and stay elsewhere.
Listen - I travel a lot and stay in a lot of different hotels. I have hundreds of reviews on this site alone. This is the worst stay I have EVER had.
The rooms are small. The bathrooms are tiny. There is fresh paint but the carpets were dirty and the walls were thin. And this was on the CLUB LEVEL.
I spoke with two different managers trying to resolve my issues and both of them were amazingly rude. Clearly something that is taught at this hotel.
Parking? Self parking is in a DIRT lot on the side of the hotel. For $22 a night I expect little things like pavement.
We had a flood in our room that soaked many of our items. They did not care. No apology even after following up direct with management.
Please stay elsewhere.
Dear hotel management: please don't bother responding to this review. You didn't care when I was staying with you, why pretend that you care now?

name: Hyatt Regency Mission Bay
title: “Noisy”
text: I'm currently staying at this hotel and since I've checked in it's been very noisy. I'm staying in one of the side buildings on the lower floor and everywhere the people walked who were staying above me I could hear. Just stomp stomp stomp when I was trying to sleep as well as all this morning. When someone else turns on their water for a shower you can hear it. Also I've heard people that work here all morning outside talking. When I was dropped off at the hotel (my friends live in San Diego) the parking guys immediately became uninterested in helping me since I wasn't using their parking service. I also started hauling my bags and almost into the lobby before they bothered to ask if I needed any help and when they finally did I was too annoyed to say yes. I feel like the money I'm spending here ia not worth it. It's way too noisy and I haven't felt relaxed at all since I've checked in.

name: Hilton San Diego Resort & Spa
title: “Relaxing vacation in San Diego- Nice stand alone resort”
text: Stayed here for one night in July 2008. We booked on Priceline for $102/night. For the money, this was a very nice hotel. One complaint would be the $22/night valet or self parking fee. Since there is absolutely nothing around this resort, there is no options but to park your car here and pay the crazy rate. Internet is $13 a day but I think you can get free wireless around the pool. The pool area is nice. There are a couple jacuzzi's, a kid's pool and a big pool. There are cabana's to rent for 75/day weekdays or 120/day weekends for the whole day. Overall, the pool area was very nice. Looked at the beach, but its not a beach to lay around and relax but to do water activities or biking. Our rooms were on the 6th floor in the tower. We had a view of the bay as well as the 9:50pm fireworks show at Seaworld. Fireworks lasted around 5 minutes and that was a good fringe benefit of the room. The room came with 2 beds, desk, chair, refrigerator for your things and safe. The bathroom was clean and small but functional. Plenty of towels. We stayed in 2 rooms and one them was not available until 4:30pm. Check in time is 4:00. Check out time is 12 noon. Staff is very nice. If the price is right, I would stay here again.

name: Residence Inn San Diego Downtown
title: “Perfect Hotel!”
text: I was pleasantly surprized with this hotel...my suite was comprised of two large rooms, both with flat screen TVs, full kitchen, large bathroom with walk in shower. The living room had a comfortable couch from which to watch tv-it felt like a small but well appointed apartment, right in the heart of San Diego, a couple of blocks from the Gaslamp District, where all the good restaurants, stores, bars/nightlife happens. Unfortunately, I didn't get a chance to play, but would go again and definitely stay there.

name: Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego
title: “The Giant Hotel”
text:
My boyfriend & I planned a California coast trip - and it began in San Diego, while he was on a business trip and staying here. I met him out here and as my cab reached up the driveway to the Hyatt, I was in awe at it's size. The driveway canopy overhead hangs a complex looking lamp the size of a small trailer home, the lobby looks like a mock Beaux-arts museum. This place is massive. 
Some positives: everything about this place is grandiosity - the stunning views, both from our room & the Presidential club upstairs, the top-floor bar, and the fancy pool complex between both buildings. Location is incredible, although can be a bit of a walk into the the heart of the city. The food in the Presidential club was good - especially breakfast time, as their orange juice was great and they had fresh various jams. The maids working here were complete sweethearts.
However - their rooms, which are the most important, were really lacking. Floor was dirty and so was the bathroom, which had an overflowing drain. When I first got there his tub was half full of murky water and he said he wasn't sure why, it just happened like that. Also, when he first checked in it took them 2 hours to get his room ready (3 to 5 o'clock) because they mistakenly thought he was hypo-allergenic. So the room he got had to be special. But this room, I don't think would be safe for even people with extreme allergies. It was very dusty & murky.
I stayed here for free, but I don't think I would spend my hard earned money on it. I would maybe try lurking in here while staying in the city, to at least see the bar at the top floor, which overlooks the entire San Diego bay. My entire time in California, I stayed in four places total, three of which were Mom & Pop run places, and this place was comparatively not my favorite

name: Vagabond Inn San Diego (Hotel Circle)
title: “Great Deal, Great Location”
text:
This hotel is a great deal for the money. The grounds and pools are very well kept, the rooms are clean and comfortable, and the free wi-fi worked great. There is ample free parking and the microwave and fridge were nice to have. The free breakfast isn't huge, but waffles and cereal were fine for us. The location was great -- short drive to SeaWorld, Old Town and Fashion Valley Mall.
I don't know if we just got lucky and had good neighbors, but the nights were very quite and peaceful. Yes, the highway is near, but our room was towards the back of the hotel and noise was never an issue. 
The staff was friendly and helpful, particularly Cristian. Yes, you could pay more somewhere else and get fancier rooms and thicker towels. But if a safe, comfortable, clean room is all you require at the end of a long day of activities, this hotel is perfect.

name: Hilton San Diego Resort & Spa
title: “Disappointed!”
text: Our family recently stayed at the Hilton in order to visit SeaWorld and Legoland. We were disappointed by the small musty smelling room that we were given. At $259/night I had also expected much more from the property. However, the pool area was not clean and ducks were swimming and pooping in the children's pool. I will compliment the furnishings and linens as well as the fitness center. But overall, this hotel seems best suited for corportate conferences and not for a vacation destination.....not worth the money at all!!!

name: Doubletree Hotel San Diego/Del Mar
title: “Will not Return!”
text: We live in San Diego, but had pre-paid for a weekend getaway at the Doubletree in Del Mar. Here is how it went down. Booked two queen so they gave us a king. Had to move our stuff two floors. Outlet in bathroom inoperable. No suitcase rack for luggage. Asked to have brought to the room - answer, come down and get it yourself. Really? Thought we had a deal for the free breakfast each morning. Yuck. Food was awful. Breakfast is easy to make, so we thought. Found out the food was pre-purchased, frozen french toast, ego waffles, etc. They also hired a new chef to help improve the food. Good luck on that budget. So we finally get our food and no utensils. Had to hunt around for an open table that a fork and knife. This happened both days. I know, why did we go back. Perhaps just bad luck day before. Nope. The pool spa had only one working jet. Just a lot of things not working. Suffice to say we won't be going back.

name: Holiday Inn Express San Diego Downtown
title: “Good place for the night before a cruise!”
text: Stayed here the night before a Christmas cruise out of San Diego. Couldn't have asked for much more. They picked us up from the airport and took us to the boat the next morning for free! They have a very nice continental breakfast bar in the morning that actually includes some hot items as well. There was a drug store within walking distance for any last minute items you might need. I would stay here again before a cruise if the price was right.

name: Hyatt Regency Mission Bay
title: “disappointing”
text:
There were 11 of us. 5 adults, 2 teenagers, 1 tween, an 8, 5, & 1 year old. 
First the positive: Housekeeping. They were beyond sweet & helpful to all of us.
 Red Marlin. The food was great. The waiters were nice.
 The waterslides. (when they were open). Kids LOVED them.
 The water taxi to Sea World.
ALL the rest of it is negative: 
Our rooms were so old & ugly. We were in the same building as the the lobby. Stains everywhere. Really old looking. Mini coolers instead of refrigerators. No light in the closet
The service was very poor. There was always a line for the concierge and the front desk. They weren't even very helpful. 
They ran out of towels at the pool. Towels that you had to "pay" for and then get credit back. The pools were freezing. It was overcast and in the 60's all week. They knew that so why not heat at least one of the pools. The first day the waiter didn't tell us there was a kid's menu at the pool so we ended up getting all of them adult meals. 
Everything costs extra. Parking $25 a day. Wifi. (seriously?) Pool towels (ridiculous!)
The absolute worst was when my one year old shut the adjoining door & was locked in one of the rooms by himself with the chain on the front door. We called the front desk to send someone up with a tool to break the chain and they couldn't be more casual about it. After 3 phone calls to them & 25 minutes later, WE finally broke it open.
We couldn't have been more clear that he was only ONE and by himself. They couldn't care less. We were right above the front desk. It wasn't like they were far. When someone finally arrived we asked them if that has ever happened before and they replied that it happens all the time. So why did it take so long to respond or just bring a tool? 
That was the last straw. We handed them the chain, checked out of all our rooms, and moved on.

name: Comfort Inn & Suites Zoo / SeaWorld Area
title: “Excellent Customer Service”
text: This hotel was amazing I thought! We traveled to Sea World with a group of 27 "special" adults and staff. They called us to get an arrival time so they could literally roll out the red carpet treatment for us...red carpet....cookies and punch....our "special" adults were feeling like celebrities. Our entire stay, they took care of our every need....location is the ONLY drawback as there are no convenience stores nearby or anything...but ....they do provide a shuttle service that can be arranged to take you at no charge....The rooms were clean, beds were very comfortable...breakfast was a bit crowded...but well stocked and great variety! Would HIGHLY recommend this hotel to anyone! Thanks again for your excellent customer service....

name: The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
title: “Convenient location near the airport, Gaslamp Quarter & Zoo”
text: We stayed at the Bay Tower, which is more low-key, less frenetic than the Marina Tower. Unless you're there for a conference, I recommend the Bay Tower. The hotel is not far from the Gaslamp Quarter, Seaport Village, and zoo. Our room--a Traditional Room with a King-size bed--was very spacious and had a desk, seat, chair and loveseat as well as a dresser. The BTL (Bay Tower Lounge) and room service menus were identical. Not sure why that surprised me.

name: Days Hotel - Hotel Circle by SeaWorld
title: “pleasantly suprised”
text: Stayed in this hotel overnight for an early morning triathlon at Mission Bay. This hotel is perfect for a stay where the hotel itself is not the destination. Rooms were clean and comfortable. Staff was friendly and accomodating. Pool area was well kept and nice for a hotel at this price level. Location is great for getting to area attractions quickly. Much better offering than its competitors that are in the same price range. Complimentary in room granola bars, popcorn and water were appreciated!

name: Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego
title: “Manchester Grand Hyatt”
text:
Stayed here for four nights as part of a tour.
 Great views over the city, USS Midway, and Coronado Island.Good rooms and particularly good breakfast buffet in spacious breakfast room. I agree that there was rather a lot of corridor noise some nights. The pool was rather busy so I did not manage to use this. Spectacular lobby with amusing bright paintings of upper classes in 17th century England having picnics. One mother overseeing her offspring looked spookily like Margaret Thatcher. 
The salsa at breakfast was so good I got the recipe from the chef: tomatoes, onions, spring onions, hot chilli peppers, coriander leaves, cumin, tabasco sauce. Cut items finely, boil gently in a little water till tomatoes soft, then puree with a stick blender to the consistency you prefer. 
This hotel is very well placed for visiting the seafront restaurants, Kansas City Barbeque (Top Gun fame), Downtown San Diego and the gaslight district. The zoo and Coronado Island can be reached by taxi or ferry respectively.
 On the seafront we dined x 3 at the Pier House Restaurant and were very happy with it. The Harbor Restaurant was used for the introduction meal and it wasn't very good. Perhaps it would have been better if it had not been a mass catering event. 
You can visit the Hyatt's lounge bar on the top floor of one of the towers for beautiful sunset views. 
The Midway was a really excellent tour. Interestingly the conditions that sailors live under are FAR worse than for prisoners on Alcatraz. My husband had a lie down on one of the enlisted mens' bunks on Midway and struggled to get out of it again, there was so little room. Midway actually does sleepover tours for enthusiasts but it certainly wouldn't suit our family. 
This was overall our favourite hotel of our Californian Tour by Milestones/ Trafalgar. Views, location, room standards, and the great breakfast with good service were the deciding factors.

name: Doubletree Hotel San Diego/Del Mar
title: “Pretty Darn Great!”
text: I really liked this hotel. We stayed for 3 nights, for a sports competition and it was fantastic. Because the hotel was accosiated with the competition, we got free breakfast (which had great food) and a discount on the nightly rate. The rooms were very clean and organized, and the tv was very nice. We got plenty of channels and were thouroughly entertained when we weren't at the competition. It was very close to the beach and Torrey Pines state park. The only cons I have, are that its a tad bit far from the San Diego Airport, but it wasn't too bad. Also, the dinner was a bit expensive, and it took about 45 minutes to make a ceasar salad. But overall, this was a GREAT hotel.

name: Doubletree Hotel San Diego/Del Mar
title: “Beautiful hotel, but expensive and beware of 2nd floor rooms”
text:
I stayed at the Doubletree in early Feb 2010. The hotel itself is beautiful, but expensive. The rooms, landscaping, and personnel were all very nice. There is a small resturaunt that serves wonderful food, but the hotel is within walking distance to a mall with a bunch of other restuaunts.
Let me start off by saying that I have never had to change hotel rooms during any hotel stay. My huge gripe was regarding my room. I checked in around 9PM and was placed on the 2nd floor near the elevators. The floor to the room vibrated as if there was some sort of ceiling fan on the floor below. I was extremely loud, frequent, but sporatic. By 10:30 PM I couldn't take it any longer and told them then while I was already unpacked for tonight that 1st thing in the morning I would need to change rooms. 
When I went down the next day to change rooms there was a list of people who called and complained about the noise because the front desk person referred to a list taped to the phone. My new room was still on the 2nd floor. The vibrating noise was not as loud and the floor did not physically move, but I could still hear the noise.
Later that day, I saw they had placed another customer into the room I vacated earlier. I couldn't believe that someone else would have to endure that noise/vibration so I voiced my concern to the new front desk person. She said that they knew about the issue and it was a problem with the elevators and they were considering converting the rooms into conference rooms. I told her that they should fix the problem and NOT place people paying good money into those problematic rooms. She just shrugged her shoulders. 
I could not believe that no one from the corporate Hilton office is aware of this issue! This speaks very poorly for Hilton quality and I strongly feel if they were aware of the situation, it would be resolved. I placed a complaint with Hilton and am awaiting a call from the site manager. 
So while the hotel was nice, until they resolve the 2nd floor elevator/room issue, I would not recommend this hotel unless you can obtain a room on an upper floor.

name: The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
title: “UNHAPPY GUEST”
text:
TO WHOM IT MAY CONCERN: I originally booked this room months ago & called the hotel to specifically reserve a bay view room. I was told absolutely no problem & they supposedly put a note in the system. Upon checking in, the front desk states "We are at capacity & no longer have bay view rooms but we will give you a marina view" Grrrr.. 
When we arrive in the room, we noticed right away that the couch has white spattered disgusting looking stuff all over it as well as long blonde hairs on it. I call the front desk to complain & they send up a maid with sheets to cover the couch/chair. When the maid places the sheets over the couch she explains to me that those are not stains I am looking at, those are “clean spots where the fabric has faded” BS!! (Look at the attached pictures!)
Not wanting to argue with this woman & feeling stressed already with what was supposed to be a romantic night away from home, I noticed when she left the sheets had stains too & holes in them! The walls had handprints on them. The lamp in room has a clear base, it looked like it had never been cleaned! The drinking glasses were smudged not clean. The cords from snack case were sticking out all on floor. TO TOP IT OFF, it was extremely noisy from other guests very late at night/early morning hours & we could even hear the flushing of toilets from other rooms! This room was over $150 & I've stayed at cleaner $40 rooms in Vegas than this! 
PLUS, parking was $22?!! Every time we left the parking lot, we had to wait for the parking attendant to come let us out because our room key would not scan properly on the "automatic gate" & each time we sat there for several minutes waiting for the parking attendant. For this to be considered a 4 star hotel & part of the Sheraton Hotels & Resorts chain, we were extremely unhappy with our stay & actually disgusted. I left feedback to the hotel on Thursday August 9th & I have not heard from anyone from customer service to even apologize for any inconvenience!! Tacky, very tacky! I’ve enclosed pictures I took with my cell phone for your viewing pleasure!

name: Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego
title: “So far à bit disappointed”
text: Currently staying here, and feel à little let down. Kept waiting till after 6 for checkin in, although did get complimentary breakfast for the wait. Disappointed with room as its small for a family of 4 and just the standard view even though the réceptionist said it was à top view room and thats why we waited so long. Good location though.

name: Hyatt Regency La Jolla
title: “They have some issues!”
text:
My husband and I stayed here while he had business in the area. The hotel lobby is a bit massive, dark and rather chilly. 
We had a rental car- they charge alot for parking, but we were able to find street parking close by on a couple of occasions.
The hotel is NOT within walking distance to LaJolla village, so don't stay here if that's what you are looking for. 
We are sensitive to odors and found our room had a moldy musty smell. They sent up a contraption to remedy this, which didn't work. They then sprayed some horrid fragrance to mask the odor, which only compounded the problem. One of the staff later admitted that they had shampoo'd the carpet and it was still wet, which created the mold problem in many rooms. We were given concierge floor privileges to make amends for this, since there were no rooms avaialble of equal value. This helped. The staff tried to be helpful- they just can't handle certain things, I guess. Carpet cleaning has to be a common occurence in large hotel chains- couldn't they consult their "Hyatt how-to manual" for instructions? The pool area is lovely when not too crowded.
I am not that crazy about the area, so would not stay here unless I had to. Disappointed with Hyatt.

name: The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
title: “Sunny San Diego Sheraton”
text: We spent 3 nights at the Sheraton Marina tower and found the staff to be very friendly and helpful. Our room was fresh and clean and colorful. If you make a reservation be sure to ask for an even room number to get the best view. It was our first time (but not the last) to stay at the Sheraton Marina tower so now I will know to ask for an even number room. We stayed in 541 and our view had a partial view of the marina off in a distance. The rooms on the other side of the hall had a great full view of Coronado Island and the bay. There is a neat little shuttle which takes guests to several points of interest (Seaport Village, Gaslamp District, Anthony's Fish Restaurant and tours of submarines, sailing ships, Midway, etc.) all for $1.00 round trip starting at 10:00am and every 15-20 minutes until 8:00pm. Very nice. We will go back and truly enjoyed our stay. Oh...there's a Starbuck's in the lobby of the hotel which sure doesn't hurt. :)

name: Days Hotel - Hotel Circle by SeaWorld
title: “Nice & Clean on Hotel Circle”
text:
Our family of four stayed at the Days Inn Hotel Circle for 2 nights in late July 2005. We read a lot of awesome reviews and it sounded pretty good. Upon check-in I was greeted with really nice and funny staff. We were allowed an early check-in at 1:30, rather than 4:00 because our room was ready. We had a great rate for San Diego (around $100) especially for the busy summer season. We were even able to buy reduced rate 2 Day passes for Sea World right in the lobby. And he even included a free Shamu plush ticket to redeem at the gift shop of Sea World. There is a free airport and Sea World shuttle available, though we rented a car instead.
Our room was back away from the highway, though there are many room closer to the traffic noise. Our room was also in the inside hallway section with an elevator. Most of the rooms seemed to be "motel type" with outside corridors..so ask for the inside rooms for more security and quieter stay. We even had covered parking for free. We found our room very clean with a microwave and mini-fridge. A little snack basket awaited us with popcorn, granola bar and a bottle of water. The bathroom had plenty of towels and housekeeping refreshed them without us asking. Plenty of counter space for toiletries. Shower/tub combo. No table to eat in room. We ordered pizza and ate on our beds. 
I am such a light sleeper, but we never heard any outside noise from guests, pool or cars. A free newspaper was waiting each morning. 
The only issue with the Hotel Circle area is the lack of restaurants, especially in walking distance. There is a cafe attached to the inn, but we did not go there. There is no free continental breakfast here. 
For the price and the number of days in our stay, this was a great place. We have stayed in MANY hotels on the Circle and this was by far one of the better deals and stays.

name: Handlery Hotel San Diego
title: “"Fart Water Hotel"”
text:
Stayed here Nov 20 - Nov 22/10 as we went to the Monday Night Football Game. We found the location to be excellent. Within walking distance to the Trolley Station and Fashion Valley Mall (which is awesome).
The lobby and entrance is very nice. The staff were friendly and knowledgable and were pleasant to deal with. The rooms were furnished and dressed nicely but could use some more help. The doors didn't close properly so you had to the slam them (which is great when your neighbour comes home at 1am and has to reef on their door to close it OR when you are using the bathroom in your own room and your spouse is trying to sleep). Really though, not the end of the world.
The drain in the bathroom did not work at all, nor did the overflow drain, so the sink was always gross and overflowing. The thing that really got me was the lingering smell. My friend used to call the sulphur smell that water sometimes has "fart water". That's the first thing that came to mind for me. It hung around pretty good. I am sure that housekeeping had to have noticed when they cleaned the room every day...surely they ran the water in the sink? In any event, the bathroom didn't really cut it for me but again, not the end of the world.
The linens / bedding were nice and the matress was quite soft. I slept OK considering we have a firm mattress at home. There was a wedding the first night so there was not much sleep to be had for us given our neighbours were super loud and the noise really carries (as with most hotels I'm sure). 
The pool area is by far the biggest and nicest I have seen so far (a few beauties in Palm Springs but this was nice too). The outdoor furniture was not that cheap white plastic junk either, which we appreciated. The restaurant was OK so we only had one breakfast there. As usual, it was overpriced for what it was. We have found that all hotel fare is overpriced.
The long and short of it is: we would stay again if the price was right. We paid $109 for a Premiere King with bottled water, bathrobe, WiFi, and parking included. During the warmer months, we might pay a little more because the pool area was very nice.

name: Days Hotel - Hotel Circle by SeaWorld
title: “Great Location and well kept Days Inn”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Days Inn from 9-6 to 9-12. It was our first time to San Diego. The Days Inn was recently renovated. The furnishings were attractive and the window curtians and bedspreads were tastefully done. It was very clean. The room had a small fridge, coffee maker, hair dryer, and iron and ironing board. All the necessities to make the stay more comfortable. They have a restuarant on the premises, called the Pam Pam. We ate their many times at the end of a busy day of site seeing. It was very convenient. They have a pool and hot tub. We used the Hot tub each night, which helped relaxe and soothe us for a good nights sleep. The Days Inn is located near many of the more popular sites, Sea World, Zoo, Old Town, and beaches. Most were only a 5 to 10 minute drive away. If you don't have a rental car, the Days Inn does have a courtesy van, which will pick you up and take you back to the airport. They also have a shuttle van transport to Sea World and the zoo. There is a bus stop in front of the Days Inn for another way to get around town. The staff were always courteous and willing to help with any questions or problems that might arise. We would stay at the Days Inn again.

name: Bay Club Hotel & Marina
title: “Nice!”
text: Comfy, friendly, nice breakfast, gorgeous view! Free parking, good access to beach (across the road!), and a splendid marina. We really like this hotel, and will recommend it.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Bayside Inn
title: “good hotel on a budget”
text:
I stayed at the Best Western Bayside San Diego on Oct 3 and was delighted with my accomodations there. I had to catch a train at 6:10 am , so I wanted to stay at a hotel convenient to the Amtrak station. This hotel was a short few blocks to the station and I was able to walk there in just a few minutes.
As a bonus this hotel is 1 block from Little Italy , a Chase bank is across the street ,and only a few blocks walk to the waterfront in downtown San Diego . Lots of wonderful deli s and restaurants to eat at, and many tourist attractions to see without a car. The hotel also has a small pool . The front desk is friendly and helpful as well. The rooms are very clean and nice,many with city and bay views and they are better furnished, with fridge and microwaves, than some of the high price $300. plus hotels downtown but for half the price. I highly recommend the Best Western Bayside Hotel.

name: Hotel Solamar - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Just ok”
text:
Stayed for a quick overnight with my husband on April 22nd. 
Pros-Upon entering we were warmly greeted by the valet which was great and they really knocked themselves out to help. 
Room was nice but fairly small, not inspiring lay out. Great shower! Sounds silly but the water pressure was amazing and I could have stayed in all day : )
Cons- the front desk service was pretty cold and we ended up in a room with a pretty unappetizing view (the dirty rooftop and air conditioning). 
Walls are VERY thin!! About 1am we could hear our neighbors (and their barking dog) in the room next door. I love my dog and all, but I take issue with nice hotels allowing dogs. I could see holiday inn or travel motels but when you go somewhere for a relaxing weekend, I don't want to see or hear dogs everywhere.
Restaurant-service great and food plated well but blah. It all lacked flavor.
Just a little thing. Thei bathroom in the lobby's soap dispensers were missing their spouts. So soap was dripping all over the granite. Just touches that I think hotels should be on top of. For both of them to be broken off??? Come on.
Over all, hotel is just ok. A little dark and not very inviting or warm. Will try somewhere else, next time.

name: Doubletree Hotel San Diego/Del Mar
title: “Sauberes Mittelklassehotel”
text: Das Hotel liegt verkehrgünstig direkt am Freeway. Die Fahrtzeiten nach La Jolla bzw. San Diego Downtown betragen ca. 20 bzw. 30 Min (Del Mar ist natürlich keine Urlaubsreise wert). Unser Zimmer war sauber, zweckmäßig eingerichtet und ruhig. Herauszuheben ist die großzügige Poollandschaft des Hotels (Verkehrsgeräusche vom Freeway sind hier logischerweise hörbar). Der angegebene Hotelstandard (3 Sterne) entsprach den Gegebenheiten. Das Preis-/Leistungsverhältnis ist nach unserem Dafürhalten eigentlich okay; wenn man die Tatsache außer Acht läßt, dass wir in anderen Kalifornien-Hotels (auch "Doubletrees") besser bedient waren.

name: Rancho Bernardo Inn
title: “Pleasant facility, but in desperate need of an update”
text:
I cannot comprehend how this facility was rated the number one spa in America by Conde Nast readers. They must have had an extremely small sample set or something. 
I"m not saying I didn't enjoy my stay - I had a very pleasant weekend here. The service was friendly and helpful. They dry cleaned my sweater after a bird pooped on me. Ha!
I enjoyed a manicure and pedicure at the spa, which were... well which were as good as any other mani/pedi I've ever gotten. Nothing special. The workout facility? Nothing special. No yoga classes, no aerobics. The pools? Nothing special. 
The hotel itself is very dated. I felt like I was staying at Kellerman's, except that Johnny Castle wasn't there to teach me the mambo. The bed and tv were nice but the bathrooms are just very old. 
I dunno. I wouldn't tell people NOT to stay here, but I can't say I'd recommend it enthusiastically either. What I do know is that I will take any future Conde Nast ratings issues with a big grain of salt.

name: Hotel Solamar - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Excellent Hotel -- An Extra Note About Value For Conferences”
text:
The other reviews do well to describe the great quality of the hotel. I wanted to add that I was staying at the Solamar for a conference at the convention center. The hotel is about a 4 block walk to the convention center -- very close. Plus the room rates were about 30% below the so-called conference hotels. So if you are considering staying at the Hotel Solamar for a conference at the convention center, I highly recommend that you do so.
Oh, and Lounge6 is a pretty sweet rooftop lounge.

name: Handlery Hotel San Diego
title: “Mixed feelings but overall, a good stay”
text: We stayed at the hotel for 4 nights (5/9 - 5/12) with a party of 5 adults and 2 children. This was my second visit to San Diego and this time the purpose was for the children to go to Sea World rather than adult stuff. We had a vehicle for our stay so I found the hotel to be very well located for Sea World, downtown, shopping and very close to Old Town San Diego. Only a few minutes drive to either because the I8 runs just outside the hotel and links up everything very well. The rooms were fine, plenty of car parking available, staff were great and the kids loved the pool. On our second last night we were too tired to eat out so we ate in the hotel restaurant, Postcards. The food was so good we ate there the next night and wish we had eaten there each night of our stay. The service was great and the food was some of the best I have ever had in the US. So overall, no real problems, but, the hotel does not have free internet so that is something like $10 per day. There was some roof maintenance going on at the time and it seemed to start at about 8:00 - 8:30 but hey, it's gotta be done sometime right? No big deal. The only major concern was that despite our rooms being pre-paid in TOTAL, a charge was levied against my credit card of over $1,000 Australian dollars for the 2 rooms upon check in. I totally expected a swipe of my card for incidentals, calls etc but not a charge of over $1,000! Although the card was not actually charged, the available credit was reduced for the duration of the stay and for a few days after while the deposit was released. It would have been very embarrassing had my card been declined in a store because there was $1,000 that was not available. To make matters worse, this was not explained at check-in. Having said that, I would still stay there again for the location and the outstanding hotel restaurant. Just a little disapointed this happened.

name: Handlery Hotel San Diego
title: “Too pricey for what you pay.”
text: My friend and I stayed at the Handlery for 4 nights. When we first entered the room, we used the bathroom. The soap from the previous guest was still on the ceramic shelf in the bathroom...GROSS! We were told we would have a smoking room...LYE! Non-smoking hotel. The iron leaked all over my capris when I went to iron them on the highest setting without overloading the water chamber. The gate into the parking lot sucked as well as the 1-way parking lot.

name: Town and Country Resort Hotel
title: “Worst hotel stay ever”
text: We booked our room almost one month in advance, I specifically reserved for the tower room, but when we arrived, were told that it's a first come first serve hotel, al tower room were sold out. We were placed in the Garden room instead. First of all, the room had a terrible smell, carpet was stained and dirty, bathroom looked old and outdated. Basically, this room should have been totally renervated before they even let anyone stay in there. There was even cookie crumps on the bed. It made one thinks that did they even clean the room. Front desk Albert was rude. I was extremely glad that it was only one night. It 's worst than a Motel 6!

name: Catamaran Resort Hotel
title: “Seen its Best Days”
text: At one time this was probably a desirable property. It has a nice location on Mission Bay. Unfortunately it now is down at heel and dog-eared. When I arrived I was directed to the "Tower" where my room was on the 9th floor. There were two elevators and one was out of order. No one came by to assure us the elevator was being fixed and we had to wait while the working elevator(both were very small) crawled down to the lobby stopping at every floor. My first morning, there was no hot water; when I called the front desk they said it was probaly because everyone was taking a shower at the same time. They sent someone to look at my bathroom but they never arrived. The next day--still no hot water! The problem is this is an OLD hotel and apparently the owners haven't seen fit to invest in a thorough modernization. The only good thing I can say is that the evening turn-down service was excellent.

name: Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego
title: “Location convenient, parking cashier and room service slowwwww”
text: Great views. Great staff. The cleaning of the rooms does not appear to be a priority (after 3 one day and after 4 on another). Be prepared to answer the same question three times to the female parking cashier, she does not appear to be in a hurry. Relatively close to convention center and situated directly next to seaport village. Workout facilities was spacious with plenty of equipnent. Too cool to use the outdoor pool, but i am not sure that i want to swim in the same pool that two ducks have taken up residence.

name: Handlery Hotel San Diego
title: “Charge extra for everything”
text: Attended a Navy ships reunion at the Handlery! Don't know how it compares against other hotels in the area, but I did not like that they charged for parking, internet, and to attend the Sunday pool party? Food was gourmet, but expensive! Maybe it is just Southern California. At these prices in Oregon, Washington, & Idaho I'm used to free parking, internet, and breakfast. The reunion was a success and the staff was great. The rooms are older. Best food for the value is at Rickys on South Hotel Circle, fantastic breakfast and number one voted hamburger in SanDiego!

name: Old Town Inn
title: “A great place to stay”
text:
We stayed at Old Town Inn with our two children. They appreciated the pool and the wide selection of free DVD's that they could watch in the in-room DVD player.
We appreciated the great breakfasts, and the fabulous service by the staff. Anna and others at the front desk could not have been more helpful. They arranged van cabs for us, got us tickets to the places we wanted to go, and gave us directions to good restaurants.
Our only quibble was that the hide a bed that our kids slept on could have used a better mattress.
When we return to San Diego, we will definitely return to the Old Town Inn.

name: Comfort Inn & Suites Zoo / SeaWorld Area
title: “Great Location, but awful front desk”
text:
Great location and it was a great budget deal. Problem was at check-in the front desk staff was very courteous. Problem was when we called in about information when we arrived at the airport, the male who picked up the phone was extremely rude. Not only did he hang up on us twice, but he said vulgar things to my son and I. 
When I got to the hotel and asked about this, we were given the runaround and the staff told us that their phone lines had been hijacked. I found that to be very suspicious and I still don't think that was entirely true. 
Besides that occurence, everything else was great, the maid was accomodating in the morning, and the rooms were oldish but comfortable enough for a short stay. Who spends time in the room anyway! Location was supreme and I felt safe there with my son.

name: The US Grant
title: “Absolutely lovely..”
text: Stayed there for two nights. The service was excellent, room were clean and modern, the lobby is beautiful...Had breakfast at the hotel restaurant "Alberto" was a very attentive waiter. We really enjoyed our stay....Highly recommend the US Grant....Cheers.

name: Catamaran Resort Hotel
title: “Simply the best!”
text: Our room was ground floor facing Mission Bay - big windows/doors opening out onto a grass area just before the sand and water. Perfect! We didn't book a kitchenette room but asked for a microwave which was provided with no fuss or bother. Two big beds, two basins in the bathroom/shower room. Massive flat screen tv. Loved every minute of our 5 days stay at the Catamaran.

name: Rancho Bernardo Inn
title: “Great spot for family get togethers and events of all kinds”
text: Wow! My sister was married at the Wildlife Park in San Diego and most family and friends luckily stayed at the Rancho Bernardo Inn. We held three meals there and were estatic about both the service and the food. The service at the hotel is tip top bar none. The staff (everyone from the gardners to the conceirge) went to great lenghts to accomodate every need. We visited with a toddler and a seven year, all found plenty to do there. The staff is great especially the conceirge who knows San Diego inside out. We enjoyed a day at the pool complete with food and drinks! What a special place to visit and catch up with family and friends. WE HIGHLY RECOMMMEND THE RANCHO BERNARDO FOR FAMILY REUNIONS, GOLF, MEETINGS ANYTHING! YOU WILL NOT REGRET THE CHOICE. The landscape and views are wonderful. We loved the spa, worth every penny! We will come back each year, that is if we can!

name: W San Diego
title: “Great value”
text:
Super modern but not pretentious. Staff genuinely friendly and professional. Beds are very comfortable and ammenities are modern and plentiful. 
What's with the carpet in the rooms though? It was super soiled. Do some wood flooring for aesthetics and cleanliness!
Wi-fi isn't free - big negative!!

name: The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
title: “Great Hotel”
text: The hotel was wonderful. A beautiful water view. It is close to Symphony Hall and the location of the San Diego Opera. It is about 2 miles from center city where there are lots of things to see. You must go to the San Diego Zoo if you have children. Our children live in San Diego and this hotel is a good place to stay and get around the city with a car.

name: Hotel Solamar - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Amazing Hotel”
text:
What"s not to like about this hotel - perfect location, amazing guest experience! We stayed there in late march 2010 - they gave us a perfect room with a great view. The pool on the 4th floor is great! We experienced the oyster competition which was fun to watch - even our 6 year old got a kick out of it!
Overall love the Kimpton hotels - as they offer the best value for the money - perfect locations for the most part and the personal touch they add is amazing. They beat the high chains like Marriott and Hilton etc. 
I wish they have more hotels across the country and europe.

name: Omni San Diego Hotel
title: “Overall OK”
text:
We stayed in the Omni San Diego for 2 nights in late June. The hotel is relatively new and in an excellent location near the gaslamp district. 
We travelled with 2 young children and were upgraded to a suite which was a very nice surprise. The room was spacious but there were features missing such as towell racks.
The staff were ok, but made you feel obligated to tip for providing the most basic of assistance. 
Overall I think the hotel is only OK

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Great location very nice staff.”
text: This resort is aimed at families and is located walking distance from Sea World. Not many places where you can let the kids do their own thing and feel they are safe. Very good staff and value for money restaurants. All the rooms have good kitchen facilities if you wanted to cook but a trip to the local supermarket will be needed because the shop has limited stock. Really enjoyed this resort, hope you do too.

name: The US Grant
title: “Great Service”
text: We stayed at the US Grant over the 4th of July and had a great time. The location is near all downtown activities. The service exceeded our expectation. One day, we left the do not disturb sign on the door until 5pm!! We removed it and went to dinner. We did not expect to get any service that day but to our surprise, when we returned at 8pm, the room was clean and the beds were turned down with little chocolates on the pillows. Slippers were placed on the side of each bed and the light were on but dimmed!! Fantastic US Grant!! We love you!! Now that's the kind of service that makes your day!! Also the beds were soooo comfortable I sank right down into the soft sheets and slept like a baby. Dreaming..........

name: Bahia Resort Hotel
title: “Lovely resort”
text: The Bahia resort was a great place to stay and although it is a bit older than some, it is very clean and well tended by the staff. The accommodation was very spacious with great views over the bay. The restaurant happily catered to us late arriving and in need of some food and produced two wonderful dishes. The pool are is nice to relax in , and although it was early March and a bit chilly out, the jacuzzi pool was very welcome. Great walking access to Mission Beach, and easy to grab a couple of busses out and about to La Jolla and downtown. Having a car may be easier though depending what you want to go to see. Don't forget to stop by and say hi to the resident rescued seals. All in all a lovely place to stay and would certainly stay again.

name: Old Town Inn
title: “Really good first impression”
text: A very clean and well run little hotel. The location is so convenient. It was our first visit to San Diego and within a very short walk from the hotel we were able to explore all of this lovely city. The hotel staff were all very friendly and helpful. Lovely to have a nice pool area to relax around.

name: Old Town Inn
title: “The only thing outstanding was the price... but that was enough!”
text:
We booked the family suite for our family of four. Mid week was $165 a night... which is truly a bargain for what we got!! The room was huge, the equivalent of two regular rooms connected by french doors. The main room had plenty of space with a couch, two chairs, coffee table, small dining table, t.v. armoire, and a tiny but well-stocked kitchen that included a small fridge and microwave. The other room held two queen beds, a small chair, a t.v armoire, and a storage armoire - yet we STILL had room for our twins' pack-n-plays!
The room was very clean, but the soft surfaces felt slightly damp. No mildew smell, though. The included breakfast was only OK - pretty much exactly what you would expect from a low-to-mid-range hotel. Check in and check out were without problems, but that was the only interaction we had with the staff. 
We'll probably stay here the next time we go to San Diego to visit family, because the prices can't be beat for what you get. Overall, though, I'd say the glowing reviews here on Trip Advisor are a bit over the top. Maybe people were just so excited by the excellent rates?

name: Omni San Diego Hotel
title: “Excellent hotel with great locality for couples or families-yes its that versatile.”
text: The Omni was awesome!! It is in a great location in the Gaslamp Quarter (next to Petco Park and across from the Convention Center) and is right near the Trolley system in case you want to save money and take the trolley. There are several excellent restaurants within walking distance to the hotel. In addition, they have a Kids club--they gave our kids a fun little backpack with toys and activities inside. Not to mention that every night they got chocolate chip cookies and milk delivered to our room! They loved it and were excited every night when they were about to be delivered. The only downside was that our shower head in the bathroom was malfunctioning the first night, but after a quick call to the front desk, they promised to fix within the next 2 hours or give us another room. They were excellent to deal with and immediatlty got our showerhead fixed. This is an excellent choice whether going with your family or as a couple or with friends. You will not be dissapointed.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Bayside Inn
title: “Pessimo hotel, stanze terribili, arredamento terribile... niente di positivo”
text:
Abbiamo soggiornato in questo hotel purtroppo per due notti durante una tappa del nostro viaggio di nozze.. la camera che ci hanno riservato era al secondo piano, e dava proprio sulla piscinetta dell'albergo presa costantemente d'assaldo da ragazzini urlanti... Era praticamente impossibile riposarsi. La camera era decisamente brutta, nememno troppo pulita.
Da dimenticare.

name: Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego
title: “Spectacular View of the Coronado Bridge and Bay & Great Location”
text:
We stayed at the Manchester Grand Hyatt in San Diego November 11th - 17th. The hotel is slightly dated and while we were there the air conditioning went out for a day but we discovered that you can open the window to your room for fresh air. The staff is very friendly and accommodating and the hotel is in a great location. 
You are in walking distance of the Seaport Village & Shops, San Diego Repertory Theater, Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego, The Midway Aircraft Carrier Museum, Navy Pier, Westfield Horton Plaza, San Diego Convention Center, Maritime Museum of San Diego, Petco Park, and the Gaslamp District. Your really don't need to rent a car if you're going to be staying here unless you're traveling out further than the trolley will take you.
We made use of the Grand Club for Breakfast, Snacks, Cocktails, and desserts and we were very pleased. We did not dine at the hotel, we found restaurants behind the hotel in the Seaport Village that offered a great variety and pleasant atmosphere. While in San Diego you must hit the Tin Fish Gaslamp for lunch and cocktails next to the Omni Hotel which is a great hotel to stay at also. For entertainment the Shout House in the Gaslamp District is a must.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Family Vacation”
text: I was a little worried about booking our reservation here after reading some of the mixed reviews. I like staying at 4 star or higher hotels and so I had the those expectations for this resort. We stayed from June 21 - June 27. We had a Lanai Garden Room, #276, with 2 queen beds. The hotel property is beautiful and has a nice tropical island feel to it. The room did have that "old" smell to it, but we didn't let that bother us much. I was pleased with the look of the room, but it did have some areas for improvement. The furniture and bedding were nice and comfortable and clean. However, the bathtub/shower squeaked everytime you moved in it and looked like it wasn't installed properly. The wood floors are beautiful but could use some occasional mopping/sweeping. We were very close to one of the pools and the kids really enjoyed hanging out there. The hot tub, 2 fire pits, and landscaping made for very enjoyable evenings at the pool. The beach was just a short walk away and very pretty. Next time I think I'll book a bayside room to just walk out of the room to the beach area. Our overall experience was good and we would stay here again. And yes, the resort and parking fees are outrageous, but that seems to be the norm for many of the hotels in this area.

name: Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego
title: “Great location if you don't mind noise”
text:
The lobby of this hotel is truly grand. Stayed here three nights during Thanksgiving week, so the hotel was not busy. Lobby bar was closed for the duration of my stay, but the 40th floor bar was up and running -- an elegant watering hole, and the view can't be beat. The hotel has its own taxi line, so there's no wait to get to distant points (such as Balboa Park). Trolly station is right across the street. The hotel is walking distance to the Gaslamp Quarter nightlife/restaurants, the Embarcadero and Convention Center. Best of all is the harborfront walkway just outside the hotel's door, along the Seaport Village restaurant/shopping row. 
But those train whistles! Bring earplugs, or expect to be awakened at 5:30 a.m. when a freight train from Mexico blasts its way through town directly opposite the hotel. As well, the walls between rooms are thin, and you can hear your neighbors talking if your TV is not on. I had a room with a stunning harbor view on the 24th floor of the Seaport tower (the newer of the two), and management told me that room refurbishments will begin in 2012. A nice touch is the collection of historical photos of San Diego gracing the rooms and public spaces. I'd stay here again (I'm not a light sleeper), and the price is better than other hotels along the harbor.

name: Omni San Diego Hotel
title: “One of the best Hotel”
text: Great service, nicely furnished room and great location makes Omni hotel on of the best hotels in San Diego.

name: Bahia Resort Hotel
title: “What a wonderful resort! Adorable rescued seal pups live on property, too!”
text: Stayed for 6 days over Thanksgiving in a bay view mini suite on the 1st floor. Exceptionally large and clean room with full kitchen and beautiful view. Our daughter enjoyed walking right out the huge glass door onto the grass that led to the quiet beach each evening for a stroll. What a lovely tropical property. Props to the Bahia for excepting responsibility for the care of those seal pups, it's nice when a company steps in to help animals. Would never stay anywhere else, and the location was so close to everything!

name: Hotel Solamar - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Cannot be bettered”
text: My husband and I stayed at Hotel Solemar 30 August for 5 nights. This was our first visit to San Diego and cannot wait to return to this hotel. The hotel is faultless. It is spotlessly clean, the staff in all areas are exceptional, the rooms were beautiful, the beds are very comfortable and we had plenty of storage space for hanging clothes etc. The restaurant staff are very knowledgeable and welcoming and the staff at reception cannot do enough to help. My husband had left his prescription spectacles in a shop at Las Vegas Airport and the receptionists assisted us in locating them and helped us to track the delivery by FedEx - nothing is too much trouble for these guys. Although we did not eat in JSix in the evening, if the breakfasts are anything to go by I am sure it would have been delightful. The breakfasts are fantastic and we had a good deal with comp breakfast and anything else off the menu for $5. What a deal! As before, the wine reception is a great idea - I would have preferred 6 until 7 but I shouldn't complain. We spent several happy hours in the pool area of an evening and it is a great place to hang out. I can 100% recommend this hotel and have advised my travel provider to recommend this hotel to her future clients. Solemar is ideally situated for all that is going on in San Diego with its fantastic restaurants, bars etc all to hand. All being well we hope to return to Hotel Solemar in a year's time and this time we will make our stay much longer.

name: Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego
title: “Hyatt wins with great service”
text:
A sweeping property with prime location in San Diego, including beautiful views of the bay, an enormous gym and plenty of eating options throughout the property. 
Their service was exceptional from reservation to departure, making me feel like a valued customer at every brand touch point. 
And, the beds in this hotel are extremely comfortable rivaling Westin's heavenly beds.

name: Town and Country Resort Hotel
title: “Great night away”
text: We enjoyed a great night at Town & Country in December after a company event. Our room was clean, large and met our expectations thoroughly. The grounds are always very well kept and beautiful, and the location is extremely is to get to with plenty of parking.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Mixed Feelings”
text:
We are devotees of Tripadvisor, and read/looked at all the reviews and members' pictures before arriving at this hotel. The reviews and pictures were spot on! I highly recommend looking at the member's pictures instead of the glossy marketing ones on the hotels' websites. Because of this we were mentally prepared for the sorry state of the bathrooms and dirty gounds. In defense of the hotel for the grounds, there's not much they can do as the hotel is located in what seems like a bird sanctuary....
The furniture, sink and bathtub had some peelings. Upon first entering the room, there was a moldy, wood smell. The TV had an antiquated set up, maybe time for hotel to upgrade their system. Pool/spa areas were clean, but aside from the main pool...the other smaller pool areas were on par with those in apartment building complexes built in the 50's and 60's. 
The one bright spot to this place is the staff. They were responsive and friendly...though the housekeeping staff seems overwhelmed as they did not clean until later in the day. We went back to the room after 2pm and the room was still not cleaned. Our request for an extra blanket was ignored, and no additional skin lotion was provided when the one small tube was out after the 1st night. 
Lastly, be prepared to tack on another $50 per night to your hotel rate as they charge $32 for parking and $17 resort fee + taxes applied to these extra charges.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Island Palms Hotel & Marina
title: “Too noisy!!”
text: This hotel needs to add some sound deadening between rooms and floors. I could even hear the guest next door dropping their change on the night stand. And the sound of the low water toilets flushing during the night would wake the dead. Also, the movie channels said "temporarily unavailable' all weekend. Housekeeping was on the ball when we called and requested a second blanket and the bed was pretty comfortable with fairly soft sheets. I must say that the view from our marina side room was beautiful tho. I was disappointed when I went to take a tub soak and found all we had was a shower.

name: Bay Club Hotel & Marina
title: “Rude reservationist, loud rooms, minimal breakfast buffet. Just average.”
text:
We were really excited about this place. Right on the water at Shelter Island, it seemed like a fun place to stay in San Diego. It ended up being below average for us.
RESERVATIONS:
We booked the room directly, and days before called because the rate had dropped on their website. The Reservations Manager was rude, told me that he was going to "Fire the Web Guy, I Guarantee That" (although the lower rate is STILL on the website weeks later, so he's a jerk and a liar), and that if I wanted the lower rate, I'd have to book the new rate online, and then call to cancel the first reservation, because he wasn't going to do it for me over the phone. He said "Do what you have to do". What a jerk.
ROOM:
We had two rooms, and I'll tell you this. STAY ON THE SECOND FLOOR. It's much nicer and much newer refurbishment. The first floor was so loud that we LITERALLY didn't sleep the first night. We could hear EVERY STEP ABOVE US. The room also was old and dirty. 
The second floor was much quiter, much cleaner, and seemed newer. The HVAC unit was all digital and very cool, compared with the 80's version downstairs.
BREAKFAST:
They bill it as a full breakfast buffet, but it's a continental breakfast plus tubs of potatoes and eggs. And the waiters expect tips.
All in all, we won't be coming back. It was overpriced and not as nice as we expected.

name: Town and Country Resort Hotel
title: “Beautiful Grounds-Great Location-Good Restaurant”
text: Located in Mission Valley area on hotel circle. Hotel circle is the frontage roads on both sides of Interstate 8 which runs from the coast on the west out eastward to the mountains and deserts. All the hotels here are a few miles inland from the ocean so there are no scenic views of classic San Diego beaches. To make up for the lack of view the Town and Country has made their property an oasis of gorgeous landscaping. The location is very good for proximity to all attractions in San Diego. 3 minutes to Old Town, 10 minutes to Sea World, 10 minutes to Balboa Park and the Zoo. Just behind and adjacent to the Town and Country is the Fashion Valley shopping mall--literally walking distance. There is a trolley station right there, too. You can hop the little red trolley and go to Old Town, Down Town to the Gas Lamp Quarter, and transfer to the line that runs all the way to Tijuana, Mexico if you want to... and back for just a couple of dollars. One of the best things about this hotel is it's restaurant called Trellises Garden Grille. The food is fantastic and the ambiance is wonderful. On weekends there is a little live music trio and all the locals come in to dance. (It's an older crowd.) All in all a great place to stay in San Diego.

name: The Sofia Hotel
title: “We loved this place!”
text: What a great location and a comfy room for a great deal. We booked 2 rooms and got nice ones for $82 with advance reservations. We walked all over and took the train when it was a longer trip and the hotel was so convenient. The tv, bed and shower was especially nice. I can't imagine a better bargain in town. Room was tight but it was a renovated hotel with new baths squeezed in and it was fine with us.

name: The US Grant
title: “The staff at The US Grant made my day perfect.”
text:
I was in San Diego for a day only but was able to have lunch at the US Grant. The food was very good but the staff was wonderful. Just the right amount of attention and very generous with information where we had business interests that coincided.
I would go back to spend a night or two just enjoying San Diego and the US Grant.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Maitland Mom”
text: We took our kids here for a family vacation. It is conveniently located and nicely landscaped. Loved being on the Bay and having access to jet skis, boats, kayaks and paddle boards. The food was good and the pools were nice. The only problem we had was our room was not ready at check in. We finally got into our room after 6:00 p.m. My son also left his sweatshirt on the bed and it was not turned in.

name: Old Town Inn
title: “Basic but very nice hotel”
text:
My mom and I stayed in this hotel for two nights and were very pleased with the experience. We arrived quite late on the first night and although the guy at the desk had a little bit of trouble giving us directions from the 5, there was no problem checking us in. Our room, which was in the one-story section of the hotel, was clean and comfortable, but a tad stuffy without the A/C (a card in the room stated that it helped save energy to leave it off, and we could turn it on if we wanted to). I didn't notice the chemical smells that other guests have complained about. The pool was nice but needed cleaning. I noticed them doing so the day we left. WiFi internet worked great the first day, then inexplicably petered out the second day, but I'm spoiled and internet access on the road is just a bonus.
