We never heard any noise from the 5, but the very comforting sound of train whistles reached our room frequently. 
The proximity to Old Town State Park and the trolley into downtown were major bonuses for us. How nice to be able to park at the hotel and explore by public transportation and on foot! 
Breakfast was continental plus - DIY waffles were a nice touch, and hardboiled eggs stick with you more than the heavy carbs of muffins and bread. 
I would recommend this hotel to friends. It wasn't perfect, but it's a convenient place to sleep with some of the nicer amenities.

name: Catamaran Resort Hotel
title: “Just what I expected”
text: Thanks to other reviewers on this forum, I arrived at Catamaran without high expectations. That is not to say I was expecting the worst, just that I went in prepared for what it was - a convenient , family friendly resort in a great location. Yes, it is an older hotel but our room was clean and comfortable. We had a studio which was very spacious with a kitchenette. We saved money on breakfast by eating in the room. We had a lovely maid who did a great job keeping our room tidy. The grounds are very pretty and we felt secure at all times. As others stated, one side of the resort is Mission Bay with an outstanding view. Unfortunately, we were not on that side, but if I ever go back, I am requesting that side. It was a quick walk to the beach and restaurants. The area is very easy to get around by car or bike. Definitely go to Pirates Cove and ride the Giant Dipper, one of the oldest wooden roller coasters in California. I was not crazy about the food at Catamaran except for what was served from the bar menu. I don't like to slam anyone, but the barbecue night could definitely use some inspiration. The buffet choices were very limited and the hot food was not hot. It was not worth the $25 per adult and $17 per child. But the patio and the view of the bay made it worthwhile. The entertainment was a little hokey, but the kids enjoyed it. S'more night was a lot of fun. There were many, many nice people staying at the resort and my daughter made lots of friends. So, to summarize, it is not a five star resort, but at the price we paid ($150 per night!) it was more than worth it.

name: Old Town Inn
title: “Everthing was great”
text:
The hotel was excellent for the price.
Great breakfast no crowds and plenty to eat (loved the waffles,wanted to take the waffle maker home)
Excellent location just minutes walk from the transit centre giving access to all of San Diego
Cant recommend the transit system enough
As seniors we had a 1 hour trolley ride to the Mexican border for $1
would recommend the sdcommute.com web site for planning journeys
In addition to this you only need to turn left on Rosencrans (approhx 1/2 mile to be among all the fast food resteraunts and stores.
Norm and Aileen England

name: Town and Country Resort Hotel
title: “Great place to stay”
text: I recently visited the San Diego area with a friend and we stayed at the Town and County Hotel. We arrived well before the 3pm check-in time but it was no issue at all and they checked us right in. The rooms were clean, spacious and odor free ( no stale smoke smell). The grounds are enormous with multiple pools and restaurants on the property. We ate dinner at Kelly's Steakhouse one of the night of our stay and it was great. The portions are huge, I had the T-Bone which was cooked perfect. From check-in to check-out the staff was friendly and helpful. The Town and County is a great place to stay and I will definetly be staying there again the next time I'm in San Diego.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Not near 4 star”
text: The 'beach' they talk about is NOT a beach- it's a dirty sand front of a man-made bay. Do not get in the water. The house keeping never refilled our built-in shampoo dispensers until the fifth day when I jumped out of the shower & called the front desk to ask them to give shampoo. It's quite a task to refill those bottles- the maintenance guy came with tools to change the apparatus & load our bottles up, so I guess that's why house keeping never does it. The lobster bisque at Baleen made me very ill. I did report these 2 issues to the front desk upon check out & they credited us $50 for house keeping trouble, and $50 for the lobster bisque episode. The bay-side bungalow left a lot to be desired- not worth the upgrade charges. The $17/night mandatory resort fee got us nothing but holes in our wallets- we never used the fitness facility, or sports courts but you must pay for them. There is no beverage service at the 'adult' pool, so you have to go to the main pool with all the kids to get any food/beverage service. There are only 2 restaurants onsite & nothing in walking distance, so unless you cab or drive somewhere, you better like the resort food- and prices. The room service was the same menu as Barefoot bar & grill, but pricier. The staff was friendly, but overall I expected the experience to be better. The ducks were cool to watch (but we have them in TX), the prices on wine were good in Baleen & the staff was friendly. But that's it. I would not stay here again- too many other great places to stay in San Diego area.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Just OK”
text:
One of the main reasons I booked at this resort was the heated swimming pool and it was great.
We went over to use the pool after a day at the zoo, it was already dark outside but the whole pool sitting area was full of used towels on the chairs and empty drink containers. We found a nice spot to sit and watch our children enjoy the pool. The water was nice and warm although the air temperature was very cool. The pool was clean and well lit but we were surprised that
there were no employees picking up around the pool to make it presentable.
The beach area was OK the children waded in but when they came out they had dirt circles up their legs to the water mark. I was glad they didn't actually swim in the water.
Our room had tiny ants that were all over the place. The room itself was OK - a little run down. The staff we encountered were friendly, the front desk was efficient. We enjoyed our stay in the area and found it easy to navigate from the resort to Sea World, the San Diego Zoo and downtown.

name: The Sofia Hotel
title: “The best boutique!!!”
text: Congratulations for the sofia! Its a spetacula r boutique in the best place of San diego. Only a few minutes fron Gaslamp and Horton Plaza! The taxi from the airport is only 15 dollars! The room is small but bigger than NY hotels! We made the check in ealier, the room is very clean and we didnt have any problem with them. The price is very good, remembering that you are in a very good location.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Good, but could be better!”
text:
Unfortunately, the weather was not kind to us during our four days at Paradise Point. The pools were supposedly heated, but not enough to swim in during this cold spell. The beach was quite dirty with debris, so we could not allow the children to play there. Food in the casual restaurant was decent with a good Children's menu but room service breakfast was spotty with the kitchen staff not being able to get the order accurate and having to return several times to correct forgotten items.
We had a two bedroom bungalow on the beach and a separate single room down the street. Both rooms were quite nice and met our needs, although in the bungalow it was necessary to go through the middle bedroom to get to the living/kitchen of the unit. With sleeping children this did present a problem.
 made the best of it by doing day trips to the San Diego Zoo, LaJolla for a walk on the beach and lunch, the Del Coronado for the beach and lunch, all in between raindrops while wearing our

name: The US Grant
title: “Hit and Miss...”
text:
Had been to a Charity event at the US Grant....so when I was looking for a romantic getaway for my girlfriend and I...I booked a reservation online @ Starwood as I am a longtime member... A beautiful Saturday afternoon and checked into the US Grant, while after waiting 20 minutes for 4 staff to wait on 2 guests and myself...I finally asked if I was at the right place....I had confirmed one of their nicer King suites / luxurious bathroom....after another 15 minutes we were up to our room...where we discovered 2 beds along with a large crib bed standing up along with diaper bucket and high chair....when I called down I was told that that was the suite I had ordered....next morning were off to start our day....and our shower had no hot water, after the engineer came up twice they gave us a room key to another room so that we could take a shower....walking the halls of the US Grant in bathrobes....
Anyway we are back to San Diego this weekend and we know we won't be staying at the US Grant.....

name: W San Diego
title: “A great night for us. Expectation management is key.”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for one night over Memorial Day weekend. I was able to secure a military rate of $131, which was great. When we pulled up the valet whisked my car away and was very friendly. The girl at the front desk was also super friendly and helpful. The decor is obviously meant to be chic, and while some may say they're trying too hard, I think they're trying just hard enough and succeeding. The "living room" (lobby) was nicely laid out during the day, and was a fairly busy semi-club later that night with lighting effects and club music. Here is where one needs to begin managing expectations. Do not bring your 90 year old mother or 6 month old child to a hotel whose thing is being young and hip, and which comes with loud music and late night revelers. Use ear plugs if you're on a lower floor and are sensitive to noise. 
The room was spacious and fun. The clock had an iPod dock and the window had a nice bench one could lay on. The TV was flat and big and the wall had a chalk board my wife and I doodled on. The bathroom was nice enough, but (one almost meaningless gripe was that) the toilet paper holder was in a super annoying spot behind you. 
We hung out at the Beach joint for an hour or so before dinner and it was cool. It was fairly empty so we got a seat on the bench and enjoyed a few drinks before the sun dipped behind the buildings. We did not hit it up late night so this may be an unfair assessment, but I can see it being a drunk-girl-in-high-heels disaster as folks try to navigate through a crowd and around furniture pieces in several inches of sand.
The hotel is not quite in the middle of Gaslamp. My wife and I are from New York and have no problem walking numerous blocks to get somewhere - one Manhattan block between avenues is like four SD blocks so it's not that big a deal, but here again, expect a walk, or call a cab. 
Overall we enjoyed our night. The rate was great, the locations was good enough, the room was fun, and the couple of folks we interacted with were very friendly. Also, I appreciate when managers respond to Trip Advisor posts, which the W seems to. Given an equal rate I might stay closer to the heart of Gaslamp, but the W definitely impressed and I would stay here again otherwise.

name: Bahia Resort Hotel
title: “Pluses and Minuses”
text: I stayed at the Bahia Resort for one night in late October while attending a conference, and had mixed feelings about the stay. On the "plus" side, the location is very good, the grounds are nice, the bed was clean and comfortable, banquet food and service, as well as restaurant service were good, and the rate was excellent. The minuses were a few experiences with rude staff members, a dirty-looking bathroom floor, and the fact that the hotel scheduled a wedding reception to run until midnight - with music and dancing - in a room that had sleeping rooms beneath it. The hotel is a little worn around the edges, but depending on what one is looking for, I would recommend it, with qualifications.

name: Old Town Inn
title: “Good Deal!”
text:
The Old Town Inn is a good deal!
In searching for a hotel in San Diego in the $120-$150 range that recieved good TripAdvisor reviews, I found the Old Town Inn for under $90.00 a night. The reviews were very good and, in my experience, very accurate. 
It is near enough to Old Town to walk, though you do have to walk under the freeway. My daughter and I were not uncomfortable making the walk in the evenings. May I recommend Cafe Guadalajara on Taylor St at the edge of Old Town. 
We rented a car and the Old Town Inn is centrally located to the area points of interest with easy access to the freeway.
It was very clean throughout the property and has been well maintained. We used a deluxe room that was on the 3rd floor at the back of the property. There was some traffic and airport noise, but nothing the "fan only" on the AC couldn't mask.
The breakfast buffet was well-stocked with a waffle machine, bagels, sweet rolls, oatmeal, etc.
All in all, the Old Town Inn is a real bargain. If we ever return to San Diego, I will definitely stay at the Inn again.

name: Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego
title: “Slightly Above Average Hotel - Rooms Need a Facelift”
text:
I stay at this hotel every August for about 5 days for my national sales conference. I've been doing so since 2006, so I've had a real opportunity to see how it changes from year to year. The location is awesome: steps from the downtown/gaslamp district and only a 5-10 minute drive to the airport. The hotel is also bordering the seaport village area which is real nice and peaceful to walk around and chill.
The good parts of the hotel are the 2 pools (if you're over 21 go to the spa pool--its much nicer) the restaurants (Sally's on the water was quite nice) and the lobby bar which is a nice place to meet up with people and have a drink. The views are also very pleasant from the 5th floor and up... right over the water.
The only real downside is that the rooms just feel so 1990. The shower is kinda small and average, actually the whole bathroom feels that way and the sink pressure was really weird. The bed was pretty comfortable but the carpeting covering the room was just old looking and not up to snuff with other newer hotels. I stayed in the Harbor Tower, so maybe that was my error but i visited a buddy of mine in the Seaport tower and frankly, it wasn't all that different. 
Overall a decent place-- I'd stay there if you can get it under $175/night but I wouldn't go much deeper than that.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Island Palms Hotel & Marina
title: “Okay stay at the Island Palms”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Island Palms for 3 nights while in town for our anniversary. We really liked the Shelter Island location as it was convenient to a lot of different attractions, yet was quiet and somewhat removed from the hustle and bustle of the city. The hotel backs up to the Shelter Island Marina, with the bay across the street. 
We stayed in the Casa del Mar building and had a standard room. The room was tiny and the King size bed and TV armoir took up the majority of the floor space. The furnishings in the room were somewhat dated. I was glad we had a balcony because the extra space was needed. The balcony had a nice view of the marina. 
The room was well equipped with a refrigerator, shampoo, lotions etc. The housekeeping was somewhat lax. When we returned at the end of each day, the bed was made, but looked like somebody had laid on it after making it. Also, the floor wasn't vacuumed.

name: Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego
title: “Liked it, would stay again”
text: Location is ideal. 2 minute walk to gaslamp district and easy access to Hwy5. Back door is right by sea port village. Lobby area and bar are impressive. Room was average with comfortable bed. The hotel offers every thing a guest would want but at an expense. Have to pay for internet usage, $28 a day parking. Staff friendly and helpful. Only complaint was a dirt shower curtain and very expensive bar/services in the hotel

name: The US Grant
title: “Great place to stay!”
text: We spent NYE and enjoyed every moment. We decided to have dinner in our suite, ande everyone from Brooks, the bellhop, who heated our appetizers, to Mr. Scaramellino, who made sure we had dinner plates and silver, it was perfect. The lounge show was great, and it was a perfect way to ring in the new year. Won't hesitate to do it again next year. Thanks to a great staff.

name: Town and Country Resort Hotel
title: “I would recommend this hotel for a small to medium size convention.”
text: Overall I grew to appreciate the Town and Country Resort Hotel. When we arrived, we were both exhausted and it was late night. I was irritable and tired and the place did not make a good impression. We had problems finding the entry street to the hotel. Later I talked to others who had the same problem. I think all the hotel needs to do is add some well illuminated signs at the driveways. The complex is large with many buildings, several restaurants, at least 2 pools, and a bridge to the Fashion Valley Mall across the trickle of water called the river. Be sure they give you the map of the resort when you check in. I too was disappointed by the room decor, but became happy with our view of the pool, the cleanliness of the rooms, and the friendly staff. Once you get your bearings, you learn the zoo, beaches, harbor, many attractions are not far. But you really need a car to get around, The trolley is across the bridge by the shopping center and it will get you to the harbor, Old Town and some of the tourist attractions. This is a very good hotel for a conference or small to medium size convention. I wpuld not choose it for a short vacation unless you only wish to "shop till you drop" at the mall. it is a terrific mall with a good selection of shops. Otherwise the hotel property seems too spawling and rooms lackluster. We were there for a convention of about 250 people and found it had all the facilities we needed.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Island Palms Hotel & Marina
title: “Great place to Stay in San diego”
text:
We recently stayed at this hotel for 4 nights and had a wonderful stay. We had a suite in the island palms section with a view of the marina. We so enjoyed sitting on our balcony overlooking the marina and watching the sunsets, boats, baby sea gulls... If we turned in the other direction we had a view of the bay and the city! The suite provided plenty of room for the 4 of us with the added benefit of a full size fridge and kitchen area. I also really appreciated the area the hotel was in. It was quiet and it felt safe in this area. You could walk around shelter island without feeling you were in a dangerous place. The longer I was in San Diego the more I appreciated this aspect. It was a great place to 'come home to" after busy days of sight seeing. It was also very reasonably priced, everything was clean 
and in working condition, and it was quiet. We also got a lot if use out of the pools and hot tub. When we go back to San Diego this will be where we'll be staying.

name: The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
title: “Would not recommend this hotel!!”
text: Location of hotel is very inconvenient for activities. Sheraton should provide a shuttle to downtown area and other places, not just the airport. Unable to walk to anything and felt like they know that and therefore charge outrageous prices for drinks and foods. Room was just okay. Cleaning Service was extremely slow and hallways were not always clean.

name: Town and Country Resort Hotel
title: “We were thrilled with the quality of service.”
text:
When we arrived at the Town and Country Resort and Convention Center, we were greeted with a warmth that is rare. The quality of service was truly exceptional. With 4 restaurant options on site, 2 gift shops, 3 pools, a jacuzzi, excercise facility, spa and salon, there is something for everyone. Additionally, a wonderful mall and access to the trolley system is just a short walk across the foot bridge.
When we met Katherine McCarthy, she further extended a warmth and quality of service that was amazing! Some additional staff that stood out as providing amazing service was Angelique at the Trellis restaurant, Brenda at the Terrace Cafe, and Aaron, one of the bellmen.
I would highly recommend this facility to anyone traveling to San Diego.

name: W San Diego
title: “Modern and Youthful. . .”
text:
I was here for four days on a combination of business and pleasure. The longer I stayed here, the more I liked it. The rooms were very comfortable and the finishes were very cool. There were also nice little touches like the quality of the personal care products, the chalkboard on the wall, and the window seat. The bar was very cool also. 
One of my favorite things was the location. It is a very short walk to Little Italy for some great breakfast (Check out Pappalecco) and/or night life. The walk to the Gaslamp district is a little longer but still only a half mile. 
Lastly, the valet service here is top notch. They are super friendly and always offer you water and directions. Be sure to tip them good! 
My only complaints are the quality of the TV reception, the plastic "glassware" at the rooftop bar, and the lack of a chair in the room. 
 I highly recommend this hotel.

name: Catamaran Resort Hotel
title: “My first time!”
text: We recently stayed here for a wedding and it was awesome! I have never been to this hotel before and let me tell you i wish i would have had more time in the room and hotel. It is like a mini zoo with ducks, coy fish, parrots, and other birds and animals roaming free within the resort. Beautiful views and right on the water... We are definitely coming back when we have more time to explore....

name: Town and Country Resort Hotel
title: “Horrible front desk service, totally un-informed staff, and rude”
text: Ugh, what a horrible surprise to arrive at your hotel that you booked 4 months in advanced only to find that they messed up your reservation and are unwilling and unable to fix it. The front desk staff was so unhelpful in regards to this huge booking snafu, that we had to turn around and stay at the Marriott Courtyard in Hotel Circle at the last minute. You would think that due to the competition in hotel circle the staff at town and country would try a little harder. But they don't. If you plan on just sleeping here, you might be ok. But if you need any kind of special service, this is NOT the right place. Staff is uniformed and untrained of how to handle unique guest situations and will be sure to disappoint you if you need any help from them. I would not recommend this hotel.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Island Palms Hotel & Marina
title: “Not too bad.”
text:
We stayed herre for 3 nights and it was fine. It was not the resort style that it had been advertised as on Travelocity, but it is a fine property. It's very obviously an older hotel that's been renovated and there is nothing special about the rooms.
We were upgraded to a marina room on check-in but had requested a bay view, based on the ads we read saying that you'd have a terrific view of the channel watching the big ships go by. We were glad to have had the chage, because on arriving realized the bay rooms would have just had a view of the parking lot.
The room itself was very basic - bed, armoire, bathroom. Really all you'd need, but pretty small. And not much better than your standard hotel chain. Our only complaint was that we could never get it cool enough. It was warm the week we were there and the a/c just wasn't up to the challenge. To their credit, the service person from the hotel worked really, really hard to try to get it fixed and even offered to install a new one.
The two points that make this hotel above average are the staff and the location. The staff is EXTREMELY friendly, knowledgeable and helpful. Every question we had was answered quickly and correctly, every need we had was met. They really make the stay worthwhile. (However, skip the restaurant completely -- service is slow, food is mediocre, it's just not worth it).
The location is ideal - we were 10-15 minutes from Sea World (which was on our list of things to do), maybe 30 from Coronado, and within a quick drive from everywhere else. Shelter Island is lovely and the marina behind the hotel makes it somewhat more exclusive and quiet than others. On the weekends, some of the larger hotels along there have concerts and you can hear them over the water -- and it makes parking tight -- but it was not too much of a drawback.
We'd consider staying again, but we'd really have to debate whether the mediocre, bland room was outweighed by the rest of the amenities.

name: Hotel Solamar - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Perfect!”
text: Had a wonderful stay! The room was very nice, staff was very friendly and the location was perfect. I will stay here again!

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Beautiful Resort, Great Staff”
text: Our family of 5 stayed at the resort and had a great time. The grounds are amazingly beautiful and staff was the most genuinely friendly we have ever encountered. From feeding the fish and sharks to swimming in one of several pools or playing on the beach, this resort has it all. Can't wait to be back!!! I've heard their catering staff is unbelivable too!! If you want to host an event, this is the place!

name: The US Grant
title: “Luxury meets Quality and Great Customer Service”
text: Upon arriving at the US Grant, I was greeted by the valet staff who were all very pleasant, very willing to help and a pleasure to meet to me. The hotel is a beautiful site that is modern day royalty. The decor of the hotel is breath taking and you constantly want to capture the beauty with your camera. The front desk staff and concierge service are extremely helpful, welcoming bringing customer service to a new level. A special note to Front Desk Staff member, Harry. He went above and beyond to ensure that all our needs were meet and was a pleasure to meet. I have traveled to many hotels over several countries and my 2 day stay at this hotel was one of the best vacations I have had because of the service and beauty of the hotel. Congratulations to them and I look forward to going back there very soon!

name: Old Town Inn
title: “Great place to stay”
text: We stayed at the Old Town Inn for Street Scene this year (2003) and it was fantasic! The couldn' have been nicer or more helpful - as we we're clueless to San Diego. I highly recommend staying here. Clean, comfortable and at a good price.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Party of 11 had a great stay. The perfect place to relax and enjoy San Diego.”
text:
The perfect place for a family gathering at Christmas. Paradise Point is beautifully landscaped, the main pool was heated, clean and surrounded by palm trees.......A really lovely setting from which to explore San Diego. Our rooms were very clean and comfortable and were close to the pool (which was perfect for our three children........if you don't have children stay away from the busy pool and opt for a sea view instead). There are adult only pools too.
The only downside was the restaurant prices. We would have had breakfast at the beachside restaurant more often if it hadn't cost $95 a time (for 5). However, there is a great supermarket nearby. Sea World is over the road and all major San Diego attractions within half an hours drive.
We all loved our stay and would highly recommend it as a base to explore the area.

name: Omni San Diego Hotel
title: “Great hotel”
text:
Stayed here on 7/20-22, 2005 for $94/night. It was built in 2004 and is right across the street from the San Diego Padres' Petco Field. It's adjacent to the city's Gaslamp district and the convention center, and the area is under revitalization. It has a pretty good location downtown, although the Manchester Grand Hyatt has a better location right next to the harbor. The Omni sits directly next to the San Diego Trolley's tracks, so you may want a room not close to the tracks. Ours faced the ballpark, and we could see the outfield while we were there. The Padres were on an East Coast trip, so there was no game. I can imagine that trying to get back to the hotel from a tourist site (the zoo, La Jolla, etc.) would be extremely difficult right after a baseball game. 
The parking is valet only at an outrageous $25/day. The front desk staff and bellman were very helpful. Other than some bad directions from one valet, the valet parking service was good. We were given a two queen, non-smoking room as requested. It had a flat-screen (not flat-panel) TV and DVD player. It also had very nice beds. The bathroom's door is a rolling door that doesn't close tightly on each side. So if you were nosy, you could peek through to parts of the bathroom. I used the business center. Internet access was $5.95 for 15 minute increments. Overall, I would recommend this hotel as a solid 4*. Its going rate was around $200/night for the busy summer tourism season. I feel that $94 + $25 parking is a lot to spend per night. Most hotels in San Diego were going for peak summer season prices, so it was a good price for the quality. Many of the rack rates for Hotel Circle 3*’s were around $100/night.

name: Old Town Inn
title: “Ottimo hotel nell' Old-town”
text: Ottima struttura, bella camera ampia e con due letti matrimoniali. Ottima posizione a due passi a piedi dalla old-town e 15 min in auto dalle spiagge. L'unica "pecca" è che la camera risulta un pò buia a causa delle palme davanti alle finestre quindi bisogna tenere accese le luci anche di giorno...Comunque super consigliato!

name: Hyatt Regency Mission Bay
title: “Pathetic / Overpriced / Run-down”
text: We visited San Diego / Mission Bay during one of the worst times a person could ever go there. A big convention was occurring, that we did not know about prior to our arrival. We called around, & actually used the San Diego Hotel booking service. Supposedly, the gods were smiling on us, & the Hyatt Regency had one room available. Boy, we thought we were really fortunate. We got a room in the Bay II area of the Hyatt. This was a pathetic room, with the air conditioner not even working. There were two water bottles in the frig. The price for each was $ 5.00. We will never stay at the Hyatt Regency ever again. The room was small, over-priced & completely rundown. This was a real let-down for our trip to San Diego.

name: Hyatt Regency Mission Bay
title: “Relaxed at the Hyatt”
text: This was a two night stay of four we spent in San Diego the weekend of 4th of July (See review of the Omni). We arrived on Sunday, hoping for a slightly early check in around 2pm and were happily accomodated, I also asked for an upgrade from the standard price line room and was given the choice of a standard King Marina or Ocean facing for $75.00 or a "Corner Suite" on the 11th Floor for $100 addtl per night. We chose the Corner Suite from the staff's suggestion. The Suite was unimpressive because the only differrence from a standard room was a larger office area for your laptop including a rounded desk and office chair. It also had this center island in the middle of it and a couple of extra windows. I called the front desk and told her that the office space was not needed and that we would just take the Standard King on a higher floor if available. She offered us the Regency Club Level room for $75.00 on the 17th floor. What a great change! The room was slightly nicer and only a spec smaller. Instead of the office it had a Big fluffy circular lounge/couch big enough for both of us to lay down and watch TV very comfortably. It had pretty Blue & White pillows and a blanket to cuddle and watch TV (Flat Screen) Huge shower with adjustable massage head LOTS of water pressue! It almost hurt on the fine setting like little needles. Really nice toiletries which I didn't expect. Only bad thing I can say about the room was NO bathtub! BOO! Balcony with Table & chairs set that over looked the beautiful Marina, and I'm glad we didn't opt for the "Ocean" side because that's also the pool side which is Busy Busy Busy with families until it closes. The Marina side faced multi million dollar Yachts and it's was fun to peak out in the middle of the night and watch the fishing boats prepare for the early morning charters. We also had the added benefit of facing Seaworld who has nightly fireworks at 9:50pm sharp! They are gorgeous from the 17th floor of this hotel on your balcony you have a front row view! We did not use the pool it was soo crowded with families like other posters have noted however what do you expect??? It's a family friendly place and if we had kids we would totally do this. Room service was good and fast, I mean really good! Another surprise. We ate at the Red Marlin one night because we were too tired to venture out again from the days travels, and were not disappointed. The steak was perfectly cooked and the olive oil mashed potatoes were great. The service was very good here. We were so pleased and ate while watching the yachts float gently in their slips at sunset. We paid the extra $5.00 for Valet for a total of $23.00 per night and it was worth it to us, since we wanted the ultimate relaxation on our vacation. No worries, we just called down and the car was sitting there right up front with a smiling gentleman waiting for us. We tipped when we returned each evening and were treated very graciously. I almost forgot! The Regency Club was soo worth the extra money we paid. Every morning there was fresh pastries, breads, bagels, fruit/cheeses, coffee(Starbuck's), 4 fresh juices, bottled waters, assorted cereal's, milk, and more I'm sure I'm forgetting! Gourmet jams & jellies, In the afternoon, cookies and soda's and juices. In the evening cocktail's, wine red/white, fruit & cheese, pasta salads ect. We snacked all day & night and everything was delicious. Free Internet & very nice computers already in the Club room ready to go. Lots of space for multiple people and two balconies facing the Ocean and San Diego Bay. I used their computers and printer to check us in and print boarding passes for our flight the day we checked out since they charge I think it's $10.00 per day to have Wi-Fi in your room. We just used theirs and saved the money. It was one step away from our room and no one was ever in there when I was. Lastly I must say the service at the front desk needs some improvement. I called on several occasions for various reasons, or question what not, and NO ONE EVER answered not once! The 1st time I thought, well they must be really busy, but by the second or third or fourth time, I was just irritated that I could not get the front desk to answer, not to be mistaken for the Hotel opperator (who was NOT friendly at all) she did answer and promptly patched me through. When we just gave up and walked down to the front desk I expected to see a crowd of people and every agent helping one, no. The employees were talking amougst themselves and immediately stood at attention "Good Morning!" when we approached. We needed Zoo tickets and they DO sell them (which is why I was calling) at a discount of $5.00 but plus a $2.00 service charge lol. So you save $6.00 for two. And the added bonus of adding them on to the room charge & we were gone in 2 minutes flat. We loved the Hyatt in general and we would absolutely stay here again for the $175.00 a night we paid via priceline which includes the upgrade.

name: Embassy Suites San Diego Bay - Downtown
title: “Embassy wins again!”
text: Having stayed at 2 other Embassy Suite hotels in the US, we just HAD to try this one even though we were booked and staying with another chain in San Diego. We had a 12th floor room with balcony over looking the city and bay - beautiful. Again loved the manager's reception and full breakfast. We ate at the restaurant and found the food delicious. The walk off the street rate was very reasonable I thought, not over the top at all. The bed was king (large ) and really comfy. Will definately stay here again when we head stateside again.

name: The US Grant
title: “Unquestioned Service”
text:
My wife and I checked into the US Grant on March 7th for a six night stay to visit friends. I chose the hotel based upon the reviews of the property and the proximity to Gas Lamp Square. Similar to a couple of other posters we checked into the hotel (room 804) and were disappointed. The room in and of itself was appointed well and comfortable but was much smaller than we expected. Generally we roll with the flow but as we don't get away too often I thought I should at least mention our disappointment to the front desk.
Much to my delight they made an immediate adjustment upon our request and placed us in a truly remarkable room (802). Again, the room was appointed well and very comfortable but was also quite large. 
In addition to our room, the ambiance of the hotel speaks for itself. From the lobby, to the restaurant and bar, it is absolutely beautiful. The restaurant was very good, the bar enjoyable, and the art gallery off the lobby was a nice touch and a fascinating diversion. While all of these aspects of the hotel contributed to our opinion of the hotel, what really sets them apart is the service. I travel fairly frequently and have had the good fortune to have stayed in many well thought of and highly respected hotels. That being said, the service at the US Grant was far and away the best I have ever encountered. There wasn't one incident where someone didn't excel at their job. We were there for just about a day and I had several members of the staff greet me by name. I still haven't quite figured out how they do that. 
The front desk staff, the concierge, the bellmen, the wait staff, and the bartenders were all incredible. Truly some of the nicest people I have ever met. The US Grant is a good hotel because of the ambiance, it is a phenomenal hotel becasue of the staff. 
Now, be aware, it is not a budget property. The foor and drinks are expensive. There is not a pool although you can use the Westin which is a very short walk. The gym is very small and would be a disppointment to anyone looking for a quality workout. I might suggest the management look at forging a relationship with the 24 Hour Fitness that is a short walk form the hotel. Other than that, we were quite pleased and are looking forward to visiting San Diego and the US Grant again in the near future.

name: Wyndham Harbour Lights
title: “Cute LIttle Welcoming Place”
text: We stayed here through our timeshare. The room is the size of a hotel room; small, but sufficient for just spending the weekend. Staff was friendly and helpful - especially arranging a bus tour the next day to Ensenada where we had a great time even though we checked in late. For dinner, we walked a block and a half to the Yard House where some excellent music (from 70's; Jackson Browne, Rod Stewart, Fleetwood Mac, etc..) played in the background. Try the Chilean Sea Bass - it's to die for! Beware of one way streets - it can be difficult getting to your destination. There's valet parking at $25 a day that you have to use because there's no other place to park - so that was kind of a bummer. But our time there was great, staff was very helpful and friendly, rooms were clean and welcoming - there was even stereo playing music when we entered our room. Very nice.

name: Omni San Diego Hotel
title: “Ideales Hotel für 2-3 Nächte in San Diego”
text:
Komfortables, modernes, neues Hotel im Gas-Lamp-Quartier (Down Town) in San Diego.
Schöne Outdoor-Pool- und Fitness-Anlage.
Direkt Verbindung zum Baseball-Stadion (Spiele der Los Angeles Lakers!).
Nur wenige Minuten (zu Fuss) zu den schönen Hafen-Anlagen.
Problemlose Zufahrt mit dem Auto.

name: The Sofia Hotel
title: “Außen hui, Innen pfui”
text:
Die Klimaanlage im Zimmer war sehr laut und ließ sich leider nicht ausstellen, so dass wir kaum schlafen konnten. Nach unserer zweiten Beschwerde wurde uns dann ein anderes Zimmer gegeben. Dies war nicht nur leiser sondern auch nicht so klein und eng wie das erste.
Parken in der Hotelgarage kostet 30 Dollar. An der Rezeption sagte man uns, dass kostenloses Parken an der Straße auch möglich wäre. Dort gab es dann allerdings einen Strafzettel. Also lieber die Parkgarage wählen, ist dann doch günstiger!!
Die Nacht war 50% günstiger, dafür war das ok. Der Vollpreis wäre aber nicht angemessen gewesen!

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Beautiful Setting”
text: I booked my reservation months ago from an advertised special. I live in San Diego and thought it would be fun to get away--locally. My husband and i had a fantastic time. We were steps from the sand, on the bay. Our room was a great bungalow, with a patio and plenty of privacy. We had friends come down one evening, and had a great time hanging out, and making smores (which was included in our reservation). We ate breakfast at the Barefoot Bar and really enjoyed being right on the water. We also spent a lot of time walking the beautiful grounds. It's like you are in a tropical paradise. The staff was so accomodating, and we will definitely be coming back for more weekend getaways.

name: Balboa Park Inn
title: “Ideal for some, not all, travelers.”
text:
This hotel has a lot of character, but it’s not the sort you’d find in, say, an urban boutique hotel. There’s nothing “put on” about this place; it's not trendy and it doesn't have attitude. I found the furniture and decor (including ample bouquets of artificial flowers) pretty tacky/kitschy, but beauty is in the eye of the beholder, and in any case this did not put me off the hotel, which was very clean, comfortable and homey. Fair warning, though – if you’re a traveler who enjoys the sleek monotony of a corporate chain hotel, if you’re a design guru, or if you consider tastefulness to be next to Godliness, this probably isn’t the hotel for you.
Our suite, “Medley,” contained a cozy living room with a television, a smallish bedroom with a queen bed, a modest no-frills bathroom, a spacious fully-equipped eat-in kitchen overlooking the terrace, and two closets. We were able to enjoy San Diego’s famous climate by keeping the windows open at all times and we slept soundly in quiet comfort. It appears that each suite has a different configuration, so those wanting a large, luxurious bathroom should choose a different suite, but the layout and amenities were fine for the two of us. A hair dryer, iron, ironing board and all such necessities were provided. I was particularly impressed with how well-stocked the kitchen was, with a full range of Kitchenaid pots, pans and utensils, in addition to the dishes, coffee maker, fridge, range, microwave, etc. It felt like we were staying not in a hotel but in someone’s small and old but well-maintained apartment. This feeling is amplified by the fact that the hotel is in a quiet residential neighborhood and not the bustling downtown. The location means you can’t just step out of your hotel room and have your choice of restaurants and shops within blocks, but if you enjoy walking it’s a reasonable and pleasant walk to the Hillcrest area which is full of options for eating and shopping. I enjoyed walking past the charming little bungalows and cottages of all different styles that make up the neighborhood. You couldn’t be closer to the zoo, and it’s an easy walk further into Balboa Park. During our relatively short visit we didn’t make use of public transit, but when you call a cab (which the staff will happily do for you whenever you ask), it arrives quickly. The distances to anywhere you’re likely to want to go are generally pretty small, so getting around should not be a problem.
The free Wi-Fi is certainly appreciated. As for breakfast, it’s a tall glass of juice with either a bowl of cereal or a basket of various edible but frankly unappetizing pastries. I don’t choose hotels based on the quality of the breakfasts provided so this was not much of a negative for me.
Bottom line: this hotel would not be right for everyone – some people would love it (“quirky, unique, homey”) for the very same reasons that others would hate it (“tacky, kitschy, dated”). However you can easily get a sense of what the hotel is like by checking out the photos on the hotel’s website, so there shouldn’t be any surprises. If you like what you see online, you will undoubtedly enjoy your stay here.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel San Diego - Mission Valley
title: “If you are fussy - stay here!”
text: I read reviews for hotels in the Mission Valley area as I had stayed at two other chain hotels in that area but was disappointed by both of them. You will not be disappointed by this hotel. I was greeted quickly by friendly and efficient staff and got my room earlier than normal check-in time. My room – a king-sized bedroom – was very spacious and very clean. The bathroom was immaculate and stocked with necessities. What I didn’t bring was available with a quick call – razor, toothpaste, etc. The room offers a large closet, safe, full sized mirror, good lighting, desk area, coffee maker (tea selections were not great) and comfortable chair. The hotel is located right across from the trolley stop making it very convenient to get around San Diego. The bar was comfortable – Gibson is a great bartender. The pool area is clean and has lots of room for enjoying the great sunshine SD t has. There is a fitness center that I didn’t have time for but I will use the next time. Breakfast is available and prices aren’t too bad. Down sides – parking is expensive and no free wi-fi in the room.

name: Humphreys Half Moon Inn & Suites
title: “Excellent place to stay when in San Diego”
text: Just spent a 5 day vacation in San Diego at Humphrey's. Stayed in a suite with a marina view and the room was great. Very clean and serice was very good. We were close to the stage area but there wasn't a concert that weekend so it was very quite. On the marina side you do not get pool noise.The hotel is located close to downtown and most freeways so it is very easy getting around town.

name: Bahia Resort Hotel
title: “Decent Hotel”
text:
My Mother and I took a "girls" trip here in September 2008. We like to try and get away once every year or two. Bahia was definitely a decent hotel, it wasn't quite as nice as we'd expected. We had some weird issues with the Maid staff as well. For instance we never had enough towels for 2 people. Upon arrival there were NO Bath towels, only hand towels and wash clothes.
We also ordered a package that included Corona's with Chips and Guacamole. First we told the front desk to have it delivered on the 2nd day of our stay, but it was delivered on the 1st night, AFTER we'd already had dinner. So we decided to save it in the fridge for the next day. Well when we went out for breakfast,our room was cleaned, and they removed the un-opened chips that we'd saved IN the kitchen. We had to call the front desk and finally speak to a manager before we got more chips to have with our day old guacamole.
The Kitchenette did NOT have a microwave which we though was odd. There is a full Stove w/ oven, but it's not easy to re-heat leftovers as we planned.
We did also order passes to SeaWorld and the San Diego Zoo, and we received that upon check-in and it worked out great. The location is a good location if you plan to visit seaworld. Our patio area was also nice as it opened to a grassy area with palm trees.
Overall this is a decent hotel, and they tried to fix our issues, but depending on your expectations it's not the "nicest" place. It also feels overpriced for what you get.

name: The US Grant
title: “OK, if this were a Holiday Inn. Highly disappointing”
text:
Hi,
I stayed in room 421 on 8/22.
I expect more from a Luxury Collection hotel, especially one with a history like the US Grant:
1. There was no clock or clock radio in the room. There was no way for me to tell the time or listen to music..
2. The bathroom sconces had at least 6 months worth of dust on them.
3. The vent, which is placed oddly inside the shower, at eye level, showed more than an inch of dust.
4. The bathroom scale did not work.
Minor problems:
5. Two of us checked in, but there was only one bath robe.
6. Two of us check in, but there was only one bottle of water.
7. The television image was stuck, stretched across the screen, so everyone looked like hobbits. If the US Grant does not want to offer HDTV, then please do not pretend that it is HDTV. I prefer to watch TV in normal proportions.
8. The TV image was snowy on most channels. 
9. There was no DVD player even though I asked and was assured there would be one.
10. Some people in my hallway got a newspaper. I was one who did not. No one asked me if I wanted one.
11. I told the check out personnel all of this, but I am not confident they will relay the message.

name: Hyatt Regency Mission Bay
title: “Beware of construction and inconveniences”
text: I stayed at the Hyatt Regency Islandia for two nights to attend a business meeting. As has been noted by other reviewers, this property is undergoing a major renovation and it is a construction site with all the usual inconveniences -- passageways are blocked off, noise from the work going on, limited amenities. If you don't mnd any of these distractions, you will be OK here. While I am not at all fussy or persnickety about accommodations, I think this hotel would be better off closing entirely until the renovation is complete. I have stayed here before and enjoyed it very much. With the renovation going on, a guest has to contend with a "restaurant" set up in one of the ballrooms, with a limited menu. The lobby is in a temporary location and the buildings with the guest rooms are in various stages of construction. There is no pool at the hotel (unspeakable in San Diego!) and guests have to go to a nearby hotel if they want a swim. My room was in the Tower, and was one of the newly renovated rooms. It was very nicely appointed, with Art Deco style furniture, a flat screen TV, and a balcony (Which I couldn't use during the day because of the noise and dust of the construction), but had no coffeemaker. You should also know that this hotel is out on the Bay, and is a $25 or so cab ride to downtown San Diego, making it one of the more inconvenient places to stay right now if you get cabin fever. Once the renovation is complete, the hotel is supposed to be a luxury resort with $300 per night rooms. I will probably not stay here ever again, in that case. I should also note that the hotel staff performed their duties with great courtesy and professionalism despite all the racket and confusion going on.

name: Embassy Suites San Diego Bay - Downtown
title: “Good Location”
text:
Good room at a good price. Throw in the free breakfast in the morning and free cocktails in the evening and its hard to beat. Walkable, although a couple of blocks to the gas lamp district. 
Enjoyable stay

name: Humphreys Half Moon Inn & Suites
title: “Quiet Get-Away”
text: We visited for our 25 anniversary and boy did they make us feel special! Very quiet property (we visited the last week of April) and beautiful island. Housekeeping did great, the grounds were cleaned every morning and the front desk staff is fantastic. Our shuttle driver (forgot his name - sorry) recommended some great restaurants and gave us great advice on how to travel without a rental car. The music each night was outstanding and happy hour was a $$ saver! I would recommend for couples and families.

name: Embassy Suites San Diego Bay - Downtown
title: “Never Ever Again”
text:
Problems: 
1. No self park, $29 per day plus tips in and out. Shame on me for not checking. 
2. Internet 12.95 per device per day. Shame on them. 
3. Noise like a monster truck rally coming from the bathroom. Staff assures me that noise was from snaking plumbing next door or renovation 3 floors above, but they are done. After unpacking noise comes back - its the ac. 
3. Back from dinner, two letters under door, Internet is out for night, and pool is out if order.
4. Night two, movie function broken. 20 minutes on hold, sorry, system crashing. 
5. Pillow dirty- yuk!
 This property is tired and worn out. Staff is visibly unhappy and aloof. We have had a great time in San Diego, but this hotel is dismal. I will cross off all embassy suites for any future travel.

name: Gaslamp Plaza Suites
title: “Great Hotel, Great Price”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Gaslamp Plaza Suites for 2 days as part of a Fathers Day trip for our parents that we booked. My husband and I travel to San Diego a couple times a year, and were pleasently surprised with not only the hotel itself, but the price, and how convenient the location was. We opted for the smallest room which was about $100, our parents got the larger rooms ranging up to $ 150. There is a lovely continental breakfast in the morning up on the roof top, and at night the view from the roof top was a awesome. The staff was great and helpful. We were able to walk to everything (shopping & restaurants are very close). We all ate at Sammy's Wood Fired Pizza, which the food was very good, great variety and prices were reasonable, and the Hard Rock... everything was so close which my husband and I like. The only drawbacks to note are that since the location is central to all the nightlife, there can be some noise issues, depending where your room is and Parking is by Valet, or you can find parking elsewhere. In San Diego this is expected, so be ready to pay either way, but it is not too bad at the hotel. I would definitely stay at this hotel again, and for the price I could not beat it, and we all enjoyed ourselves and would definitely come back.

name: Embassy Suites San Diego Bay - Downtown
title: “Great location, terrific happy hour”
text: This ES is very nicely located, across from the Seaport Village. It has a very nice view of the Bay and the ships passing by. As always, the breakfast was very good with a nice variety of fare. We've stayed in many ES and this one by far had the best Happy Hour. The snacks were healthy and filling--the mixed drinks, beer and wine very good. The staff was very friendly and helpful.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Well located San Diego family hotel but a little dated for price”
text: The hotel was in a very good location. It was easy to get to SeaWorld, restaurants, etc. The registration went smoothly. All the employees are very helpful and take time with you. We received a room upgrade upon check-in. The room was a good size and had a small refrigerator. We were a family of 4 so the refrigerator comes in handy. The bathroom was large but had a musty smell and the bathrooms need updating. Overall not a modern room-just average. Room air conditioner is old and made lots of noise during the night. The wood floors in the room were extremely dirty. Our feet were black from walking on them. Even after housekeeping came, our feet got dirty. The $28 parking fee per car per day is ridiculous. But we knew about the parking beforehand so we paid! The main pool is nice. We were there during a busy weekend and there were still plenty of lounge chairs for everyone. Also waitress service and bar service at pool was very good .

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Lovely resort on the beach”
text: The resort has lovely bunglalows on large resort grounds with direct access to the beach and waters. We stayed 1 night and only wished we stayed longer! The room was spacious and decor modern. Beds were comfortable. We loved the resort grounds, especially the beach and access to the waters. We also enjoyed our dinner there. Would recommend this unique hotel!

name: Bahia Resort Hotel
title: “Great hotel for families”
text:
Our family stayed at the Bahia April 4-9th. We had read many reviews and were a little leary about the property. I would recommend this property to anyone with kids. 
When we arrived at the Bahia we thought the grounds were beautiful. The front desk people were very helpful. The room was not ready yet, becuase it was only 12pm, as our flight arrived early in the day. They gave us a pool key and a place to change into our suits and told us to enjoy the pool until the room was ready. The pool, whirlpool and workout areas were nice. Nothing special, but very nice to have. Our son enjoyed the pool & we never had any problems finding a place to sit in the sun. The person that we spoke with while making reservations was very helpful also! I think he actually upgraded our room, because we had requested the lowest price room, which is a garden view (basically two beds and a bathroom) - we were upgraded to a newer Garden View Studio with a kitchenette and living room! It was nice to have our own fridge and stock up on some food/drinks for the week. This room should have cost us about $200 more for the week that we were there! 
Our room was great. It was facing the front desk area, on the third floor - room 642. It was high enough that we could see the bay & it overlooked the Harbor Seals! We would sit on our deck and watch them swim. This was a treat for our 6 year old son. The room was very clean and did not smell at all. Housekeeping did an excellent job keeping our rooms clean & towels well stocked! The only complaint that we did have was that the patio doors are single pane glass, so they did not keep out the sound very good. We never had any problem sleeping though, as we were pretty much on central time zone & went to bed early & up early every day.
The breakfast buffet at the hotel was good. We didn't think it was that expensive, considering the menu items were limited & about the same price as the buffet. We ate the buffet almost every morning. We had the Easter Brunch on Sunday & this was excellent. Alot of food & very well done! The egg hunt for the kids was great, as well as the ride on the boat to the Catamaran (sister hotel). We had dinner only one night at the hotel & their evening menu was also very good. Be aware that this is a family hotel so there will be alot of kids in the dining area.
I liked the location of the hotel because it is so close to alot of areas. We did not rent a car because my husband did not feel comfortable driving in San Diego. We didn't have any trouble finding taxis and it was probably less expensive for us to take taxis than renting a car for the week. We taxied to Sea World - $6 each way....
the Zoo - approx. $20 each way....Pacific Beach area (Mission Blvd/Grand Ave/Pacific Beach Drive) was about $5 each way. We found ourselves going to this area alot in the evening as there were many great restaurants on or by the beach! We never felt restricted by not having a car. We found a little market near Pacific Beach to buy our groceries too.
This is definitely a great hotel for families. We are not too picky, but do like to have a nice hotel room. Our family loved this hotel. I would recommend this hotel to anyone. It is also a great place if you have teenagers, as it is only two blocks to Belmont Park! I noticed alot of teenagers in groups heading over there in the evenings. I felt that this was a very safe area of town for our family too.
If you have any questions regarding the Bahi & would like an honest opion - please email me at crdlahaise@yahoo.com.

name: The US Grant
title: “Should Have Stayer Here First”
text:
Checked in here because I was unhappy with first hotel.
Very friendly staff and upgraded to a beautiful room. The shower was huge with jets everywhere. Very stylish decor throughout the hotel. Very pleasant restaurant. I can't imagine staying anywhere else in San Diego.

name: The Westgate Hotel
title: “We loved the old world charm....”
text:
This is a review of the the Westgate hotel after my very disappointing pre-stay tripadvisor review in May.
If you go in already knowing about the daily facility charge ($15per day) and valet ($32 per day), you will not be disappointed. We were very happy with our stay this past weekend.
My friend and I had an early check in to the Westgate early this past Friday for a fun relaxing weekend in San Diego. ( I live in SD but was enjoying a Girls weekend sans kids)We wanted to get settle into the hotel before heading up to La Jolla for dinner and sightseeing and there was no problems with checking in at 11:45am. It was quick and easy with little wait. (just the way I like it!) The lobby was decorated in an old world European charm which we enjoyed. Although for others, it might not be their cup of tea.
Our room was on the the 10th floor facing the harbor....really wished the NBC building was not in the way of the beautiful view. The room was very well appointed, spacious (probably b/c the double beds were full size instead of queen), with flat screen TV (which we didn't turn on with the exception when the maid turn it on for music during turndown--nice ambiance touch upon our return to our room.), water pressure was excellent---almost felt like getting a good massage which my girlfriend agreed), clean (most important to us), and simply decorated.
We never once saw another guest on our floor which was nice and quiet. The noise level can be high from passerby in the gas lamp district. It didn't bother us as it just sound like white noise. However, it you have a lower level room, I can see that it might be disturbing.
The facility charge included water bottles, wifi, and usage of the fitness center( which we used on one morning only--nice & standard). For a weekend pleasure trip where you have no need for the business center & wi-fi, the additional fee may add up. However, for the business traveler, it's convenient and an acceptable fee.
In terms of location, it's very conveniently located. You can hop across the street and shop til you drop at Horton PLaza where there are plenty of eateries, movie theatre, CVS etc... You are only foot steps to the Gas Lamp Quarters, too.
Valet service was very efficient---I usually telephone the reception desk for our car---and each time we arrived at the garage, our car was there waiting for us. It's definitely worth the $32. (although management should consider lowering the fee to $25)
 We had a brief tour of the Sunday Brunch and didn't have time to partake. However, we would love to come back to experience Sunday brunch in the future. It looked absolutely devine with everything plated so exquisitely. The chocolate fountain would be a sight of heaven for my 5 yo chocoholic daughter if she was there. 
Overall, we had a wonderful stay at the Westgate. It's not the Four Seasons Lanai' (where we were greeted daily by all staff by our surname) by any means but satisfactory for Downtown San Diego.

name: The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
title: “Great Hotel!”
text: The staff at the front desk was very helpful and friendly! There is a Starbucks in the hotel, which is a huge plus! And the restaurant was great as well... plus you can't beat the view! I don't think there is a bad view from any room!! It was close to the Gas Lamp area, but definitely not walking distance, that is the only bummer... but a really quick drive, plus it is super close to the airport!

name: The Beach Cottages
title: “Wanted to love it but didn't”
text: Had a studio apartment on a trip with my family. There is no air conditioning, so we had to leave the windows wide open otherwise suffocate, but nearly died of the heat overnight anyway. Between the heat and the noisy bar-goers we hardly got a wink of sleep. It was intolerable. Also, the place really does need some repairs. They're fairly minor such as a leaky, cracked faucet for one example, but it makes it seem cheap and rather crummy. The next day we moved to the Best Western a few blocks down. There we got a modern room with A/C plus a partial ocean view (no view except at the dirty alley from the studio room here) plus a pool & hot tub for an evening swim. I really wanted to love The Beach Cottages, but I honestly wouldn't recommend this place.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel San Diego - Mission Valley
title: “Tired, older Doubletree centrally located in Mission Valley”
text:
Have stayed here annually several times for a professional conference. This time I stayed on the Club Floor in a one-bedroom suite. The hotel gets a little more "tired" each time. The suite was large with nice furniture and the bathroom was clean and large and the bed very comfortable. However, the bed it smelled strongly of mildew which I corrected with some purchased Febreze. I was disappointed that the room had no refrigerator, corrected when the hotel delivered one for a $30.00 fee. 
The Club had decent but not exceptional breakfast food and the selection of appetizers and alcoholic beverages was below the norm for similar hotels. More disappointing was that the club is closed Friday evening and Saturday and Sunday. They do provide vouchers for one appetizer in the downstairs bar each of those nights and a continental breakfast each morning, which I admit is a reasonable alternative. But if you like to grab some items, eat casually without waiter service (which I do) and take food back to your room, this is not possible.
The valet parking was also quite below acceptable standards. They do have a valet parking stand at the entrance. However, the valet doubles as the bellman and never once in 9 chances came out, even when he could see a car arrive from his bell stand. Each time we had to bring in our keys and several times there was no one to take them. 
We didn't eat at the restaurants, but the bar service was slow but decent. The quality of the food average at best. It did have a very nice pool area and exercise room.
All in all the place needs a makeover, better service and better club service.

name: Humphreys Half Moon Inn & Suites
title: “We hope to return and bring the rest of the family next time!”
text: My husband and I just spent 6 nights at Humphreys and had a wonderful time. We really enjoyed the view from our first floor marina~view junior suite and enjoyed a morning walk every day on the bay walk just across the street. We were there during one concert night and there was a lot of activity but we were able to come and go as we wanted while being able to hear the band as it was playing ~ just a minor inconvience at best. The grounds are beautiful and the room could use a little updating but overall a wonderful lovely stay. The young ladies behind the desk were also very helpful and courteous during the entire time. We will hopefully return one day and bring the kids and their families to enjoy Humphreys and San Diego as well.

name: The US Grant
title: “PERFECT STAY”
text: My husband and I just returned from a 3 night stay at the U.S. Grant and have decided it is the nicest hotel we have stayed in a long time. The newly redecorated lobby is beautiful, and our room was just as lovely. The room service was great, and the staff was gracious and accomodating. I had stayed at another downtown hotel the two nights before my husband arrived and I liked the U.S. Grant MUCH better. Two thumbs up!

name: Embassy Suites San Diego Bay - Downtown
title: “Great location, beautiful hotel, but must pay for parking”
text: Great hotel, beautiful rooms, delicious breakfast--location is great, can walk, take public transportation including the trolly, bus or ferry just about anywhere you want to go. This is a plus, because the hotel charges $20/day for parking. We chose not to rent a car, since the fee for parking just wasn't worth it for us. If you do want to rent a car for a day trip you can easily take the trolly to Little Italy where there are many rental cars available. You can do many sight-seeing trips around San Diego on foot, or public transportation. This was a fun vacation--and beautiful.

name: Ocean Beach Hotel
title: “Location”
text: My teenagers loved that we were right on the beach. It was easy for them to walk over to the hotel and grab a soda or sandwich from the in-room fridge. That was the sole reason we chose this hotel. The courtyard with the view of the beach is charming. The room was clean, and any sand we tracked in was removed daily. If you want fancy, this is not the place. Our room was somewhat cramped, and the bathroom needs updating. Did we care? Not a bit. We were only in the room to shower (plenty of hot water) and sleep.

name: The Westgate Hotel
title: “Are You Kidding Me???? This Place was HORRIBLE!!!!!!”
text:
I'm shocked this hotel is getting good reviews. SHOCKED!!!!!! 
First off, the place is as old as George Washington, and the rooms look like something out of the Shinning! Pink shades, and wallpaper? A round box TV from the 80's? 
But forget that... what about the bed. Sleeping on the bed was a step up from sleeping on the sidewalk. And when I called and complained they said every room has that kind of bed and admitted they have gotten complaints about them. Then they had housekeeping give me two Blankets to put over the bed to make it feel more comfortable. ARE YOU KIDDING ME? FOUR STARS??????? NO WAY!!!!!! I stay at 4 and 5 star hotels and this my friend is no better than a motel 6. 
Have some class and stay across the street at The Grant! That's a real four star!

name: Bahia Resort Hotel
title: “An old resort that has aged a bit, but affordable place to stay.”
text:
Decent hotel, that appears to be resort from decades past (perhaps the 70s), and hasn't had much updating. It does have a nice location on Mission Bay and is offset from the hustle and bustle of the area, so it was a quite stay.
We had a separate cabin style room - received a complimentary updgrade - which was a nice change of pace from standard hotels, and we didn't have to listen to our neighbors. So, if you can afford it, these are nice accomodations.
Aside from that, nothing special. The beds are a bit hard, and the sheets scratchy (why can't hotels pay more attention to the bed and sheets?).

name: Town and Country Resort Hotel
title: “International visitors love the Town and Country”
text: We arrange housing for over 400 international emerging leaders from over 120 countries for the past 30 years and often place them at the Town and Country during their stay in San Diego. They love it! Nice big grounds with lovely vegetaion with a staff that makes them feel at home. -Cath DeStefano, Executive Director, Citizen Diplomacy Council of San Diego

name: Hyatt Regency Mission Bay
title: “Nur ein guter Name”
text: Das Hyatt Regency Mission Bay ist ein typisches Marken Hotel, Die Standart Zimmer sind im 1 Obergeschoss mit Ausblick zum Hotelgarten oder zur Strasse. Das Personal beim Check in ist freundlich ,schnell und kompetent. Die Pavillions im Garten sind leider nur gegen Gebühr zu benutzen. Das Frühstück ist zwar gut aber sehr teuer. Super ist jedoch das Hoteleigene Bootstaxi zu Sea World mit eigenem Eingang. Abfahrt stündlich.

name: Courtyard San Diego Central
title: “Standards have dropped?”
text: I always stay here on business when in the San Diego area. Recently my experience was very below standard. I arrived to wait for about 10 minutes while the receptionist was on the phone. No eye contact, no acknowledgment of my arrival. He eventually knocked on the room next door and someone else came to assist me. Far too long a wait! It's also really disconcerting to see the desk staff if football shirts. I honestly thought that a member of the public was on the phone when I first arrived. I don't get it? It doesn't set a professional tone. My room was not fresh, when I pulled back the curtain there was a sock on the floor. YUCK. The carpet area around the sink had bits of paper on it. I wondered if the carpet had even been vacuumed? All in all not a great stay.

name: Courtyard San Diego Central
title: “Great experience for what it promised”
text:
My team and I booked several rooms here for a business event, and I got the king suite. It was the perfect size for a small meeting, and one thing I love about Courtyards is they get business. They know you have stuff to plug in, so there were several outlets for all our laptops and phones. Only beef is the staff told us the landline in that room had a speakerphone, and it didn't. 
I think someone else commented on this, but while the room was great, the design was ridiculous as there's a door in between BR and LR that is always in your way, and always swinging open. It should ideally open into the LR to be out of way, as you're continually going by this corner to the bathroom and into the BR/LR. 
Love the open lobby with plenty of seating for gatherings and places to charge your laptops. 
Decent fitness center, and I loved how it had windows that overlooked the pool. I can't stand gyms that have no windows. Only complaint is that the A/C wasn't quite working well in the gym.
Downstairs breakfast is handy to have in the a.m., and there's free coffee at the bar if you ask for it. 
Staff was always cheerful and happy to help. One of the cleaning staff wasn't too bright though, as I asked her in the downstairs hallway if there was free coffee in the lobby. After a pause, she said, "well, no. but if you ask for the complimentary coffee... that's free." Ohhhhh boy. Perhaps a bit of training needed there. But at least everyone was pleasant!

name: Ocean Beach Hotel
title: “Stay and Play on the beach at Ocean Beach Hotel”
text:
Great hotel on the beach! We stayed there our last night in the San Diego area. Ocean Beach is a neighborhood beach and the OB Hotel fits right in. Room was comfortable, looked out at the courtyard, but also had a great view of the pier and ocean. Will stay there for a few more days on our next trip. The owner gave us restaurant recommendations and both places we tried were terrific. Thank you Rich, Louis and Sam!
Laurie and Ivan, CO

name: Bahia Resort Hotel
title: “Just returned from our 4th visit”
text:
My family and I (children ages 6 and 8 and my husband) just returned from our fourth visit to the Bahia. We have mixed feelings about this property.
The truth be told, what keeps us coming back, first and foremost, is the location. We love that it is so close to Sea World and virtually anything else you might want to visit in San Diego.
Second is the availability of cooking facilities (we always book a Bayside suite which all have kitchens). 
The pool is very nice. The drinks at the bar are good and they serve a simple lunch there everyday. Science classes are offered for the kids poolside. My kids love them and they are great for giving the grown-ups a break. 
The downside of this resort is the dated and somewhat dark and dingy feel to the rooms. The cinderblock walls and small bathrooms are a real turn-off. 
My other criticism is the noise from the parking area. The bedrooms of the Bayside Suites all face the parking lot so be prepared for car noise.
Next year we will probably stay somewhere else and just sacrifice the convenience of the kitchen.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Beautiful Resort!!!”
text: What a beautiful hotel, the staff is fantastic, and the location is terrific!

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel San Diego - Mission Valley
title: “A good choice”
text:
I stayed at the Doubletree Mission Valley for the second time during a business trip, and I can confirm the impression of most part of the other reviewers:
- The hotel is conveniently located close to a trolley stop: my wife accompanied me and could not use the car, but she had the opportunity to move by, visiting Old Town and Downtown, in a fast and cheap way, without any need to take a taxi. She could also manage to reach the new "Las Americas" outlet shop center at San Ysidro and enjoy a crazy shopping full-day! Downtown hotels may be more comfortable from this point of view, but they are usually more expensive when compared to the hotel overall quality, while in other San Diego areas you definitely need a car to go anywhere.
- OK, the surroundings may be not the loveliest place in San Diego, but the same applies to all other hotels in Mission Valley and Hotel Circle, just overlooking the Interstate 8. The noise coming from the nearby freeway is perceptible only if you have a room facing the freeway itself (which we do), but this was not a real issue for us as we live in town.
- The overall hotel experience was quite good: large and clean rooms, rich breakfast, friendly staff, amenities (gym, heated pool, business center) available.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel San Diego - Mission Valley
title: “Really Good Hotel”
text:
We stayed here at this hotel during the ComicCon - the largest comic book (and more) convention in the world. Therefore, I'm sure we paid alot more than the hotel normally charges. 
But I was pleased with our room, which was just fine. We did pay to be on the executive floor, whereas our friends didn't. The rooms were practically identical, with the only exception being that we had a plant in our room. And our bathroom was much smaller, which didn't make sense to me.
The upstairs breakfast / hospitality area was included with our executive-level (and more expensive) room. This was the first time we paid a higher price for the executive floor, so we made a point to check out the breakfast. It was OK, but the space was warm and cramped. It reminded me of most hotels in Europe, as far as being very cramped in space and somewhat intimate with all of your fellow guests. The main hostess was militant and overbearing. And to our horror (ha ha), forced some other guests to hug her when they said that they were leaving that day. We then took our leave rather quickly and went down for breakfast in the main restaurant. I would not pay for executive level rooms again.
But the hotel itself was fine and the location was great, and was right across the street from the Trolley Stop, which is a GREAT convenience. We did get stuck with the parking fee, but this is normal for this area.
I would definitely stay here again, provided that it wasn't quite so expensive, and it wasn't during the Comic Con!!!

name: Courtyard San Diego Central
title: “WOW!!!! Marriott won me over with this one!!”
text:
I wasn't a big fan of Marriott hotels. In the past when I stayed there the rooms were old, the buildings were old and outdated, and the service was poor. Well one stay at this hotel and all of that has changed. I even signed up for Marriott Rewards because when I am in the San Diego Area I will be at this hotel.
Not even sure where to begin.....how about with the Management. You can tell a good leader when he works the front desk and also drives the hotel van. I wouldn't have known he was the manager. The only way I found out is someone asked.
The rooms are awesome. They are comfortable and clean. The bed was very comfortable and the linens nice and crisp.
But my favorite part of this hotel is the food. I ordered a Turkey Burger for room service and it was one of the best Turkey burgers that I have ever had. It was well seasoned and just delightful.
But the number 1 food experience is the breakfast buffet. The bacon is to die for. I ended up finding out that the Manager special orders the bacon and it's unique to that property. It is delicious..nice and thick and cooked very well.
I highly, highly recommend this hotel. I had a great stay!

name: Town and Country Resort Hotel
title: “Excellent hotel”
text: Have stayed many times and always excellent service, friendly staff and convenient food service choices.

name: Embassy Suites San Diego Bay - Downtown
title: “Great location, above average hotel, overall best value, comfy”
text:
I never write reviews, but my stay at the Embassy has prompted it. Plus wanted to add to what I had read at this site prior to traveling to San Diego.
