Agree...this is probably one of the best hotels I've stayed in while not paying $$$$ for it. I would rate above average to excellent. We really enjoyed our stay.
We requested a bayview room...we were given a corner room on the 7th floor with great views of the Seaport Village and Harbor. For the most part...I thought our room was very quiet and private. 
Our room was clean, spacious, had a bar sink, microwave and small fridge in the galley area. It had a working desk or table in the livingroom for your laptop or if you wanted take-out one night. What I liked about our room was the big huge sink area in the bath AND one outside the bathroom. This way, my husband had one area, I had on area for our "stuff." 
Yes, there is some very minor evidence that the Embassy is currently renovating their rooms. But I do not think you would notice this unless you are on the upper floors and you are deciding to take an afternoon nap at between 1-3 p.m. We did this one day..there was only a very faint tapping to be heard. The only other way we knew there was some construction going on at this hotel was reading about this on this website and a small discreet sign in the elevator. 
I have read here and agree...the beds are VERY comfortable and LOTS of really good fluffy pillows. I see complaints were written about the noise of the a/c or heat. I did not notice the noise of the fan more than any other hotel I have been in. 
Comments on the free breakfast buffet and a happy hour (snacks and drinks). The breakfust buffet is a real value-add considering that eating an equivalent breakfast out might run you about $15pp. Also the Embassy breakfast is probably better than you can get at any Hampton Inn or similar type of hotel that includes a continental breakfast. You can have an omelet made to order...which is more than I have seen offered elsewhere. Now...here's the catch. Get there early if you are aggravated by crowds or people who think that the food will all of a sudden dissappear or that the Embassy will shut down the breakfast area without notice and they will be out of luck. I think you know what I mean. You still get A LOT of people who think that because it's "free," means they can behave as though it is a "free-for-all." The Embassy must have about 7-8 people , possibly more, working the lounge/breakfast area , keeping it clean, clearing tables, and keeping it "fresh." We went about 7:30 daily and it was a bit hectic and somewhat aggravating for us. Once seated and away from the hordes, you can somewhat relax but it is always difficult for my husband and I to relax while watching people act like it is their last meal. We went earlier on our last day and it was pleasant. None of the craziness. I cannot say enough about how polite and courteous the staff and breakfast crew is. 
Now about the manager's reception: no biggie. We went downstairs to check it out and decided to pass. Well liquor and nachos and some "freezer" pizza. Save your calories and don't risk any headaches with the well-liquor. Granted it's a nice idea...but not for my husband and I. 
There is a charge for WiFi [$9.95 per day]. If you can get by without your own laptop in your room, you can use the business center, internet is free. Okay..so you think that the WiFi charge is a bit much? Well...the Embassy makes it up with the free breakfast. [Go outside and order an omelet and see how much that will cost you! ] I did not experience the connectivity issues that others had commented about. The WiFi worked flawlessly.
The pool and jacuzzi is average to small size, but the their gym is a treat with treadmills, elipticals and dumbell weights. One of the nicer hotel gyms I have seen for this class hotel. 
This hotel is 15 min walk from Gaslamp, 1/2 block from their trolley, 10 min walk to the harbor excursions and Seaport Village. Starbucks is attached to hotel downstairs. 
Some comments on the hotel's Pacific Fish Company restaurant.
The PFC will mostly seat people in the bar area, which is noisy and cold. For some reason the air conditioning is cranked in there. The sushi is mediocre at best. My husband had sushi there one night and it didn't look so hot...kind of amateurish (we eat A LOT of sushi). That made me reluctant to try any of the fish. They have a smoked beef salad which is to die for. The Martha's Vineyard Salad is also very good. The food is overall very good tavern/bar food. Again, service is excellent and waitstaff professional. There are so many places to eat in San Diego that I would say there is no need to add this restaurant to your list as "must dine here." I will say that the restaurant is convenient if you come back in late from a day of touring or whatever and you are too tired to venture out much further. You can get a decent meal. A comment..this restaurant also serves the hotel room service. The prices for room service are at least $1.00 more per item, there is a $3.00 room service fee and they add 19% gratuity to the bill. There is clearly stated on the room service menu. 
Parking is $28 a day without any in/out fee. Now stop acting like this is a big deal. Guess what ? You are in the city. Parking is expensive ANYWHERE and most of the hotels are charging $25 to $30 a day. [I did all this research before I went.] One note, we are not 100% sure but we think one of the valets possibly scratched our rental. We did notice until the vehicle was at Avis and they pointed it out. That can happen with any valet service, just be aware.
One review commented on crazy/rude busboys and valets who were falling over themselves to get tips. We did NOT see this. Again, the valets were all very pleasant and extremely polite...as were the rest of the staff.
My last few comments. 
The train!! When reading the reviews about the Hampton Inn and Holiday Inn Bayside...I got a bit freaked out because people were commenting the fact that you can hear the train all night long. Guess what? We heard the train as well in our hotel. Talking to some locals, they indicated EVERYONE who lives or stays downtown can hear the the train at night. Someone even commented that it is some age old agenda by Amtrak with the City of San Diego. We didn't hear the train Sunday night, but did hear it through the week. We got used to it. So be prepared! 
I chose this hotel because it was slightly less expensive than the Manchester Grand Hyatt and I wanted a suite style room. I walked over to the the Manchester to check it out. It is A LOT more plush and caters to business people and older traveling couples. You will pay for this though. Also, parking is $30 per day there. But looking at the Manchester Grand Hyatt and relation to the train tracks...I am sure they hear the train at night as well.
Overall, we had a fantastic experience at The Embassy Suites...will be returning here.
ONE MORE THING: Go to the Fish Market Restaurant (near the USS Midway Museum) and eat at The Top of the Market. You might think pricey but it was FAB and worth it.

name: Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego
title: “Good for business travelers and those who like big hotels”
text:
This hotel is big (not Las Vegas big). There are two towers and a huge lobby that connects them. I was in San Diego for a convention and when I checked in there were only double rooms available. I had to wait 2 hours for a king room. I didn't mind waiting because I was the first in my group to get to the hotel, but I could see where this could be a problem for other guests.
Positives:
- Large room and great view of the ocean
 -- plenty of room to work if you are a business traveler
- Great top floor bar with amazing views of the water and surrounding area
- Convenient location to the convention center
- Walking distance to the gaslamp district (10-15 minutes) although wouldn't recommend if you have limited mobility 
Negatives:
- The hotel appears to be understaffed (had to wait for a room, valet took a while, room service took an hour)
- Too far to walk to the gaslamp if you have mobility issues
- Service is lacking if you
- Bathroom is nothing special (ceramic tile)

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites San Diego Old Town
title: “Not bad, good location”
text: Clean hotel, decent rooms, small bathrooms; Very easy access to freeway and walk to Old Town; Parking garage underneath is tight, especially for larger vehicles to drive around; Need more help at the front desk as usually one or two people were trying to do everything from checking in to making reservations on the phone; Still needs touching up here and there from paint on the walls coming off already, walls to be thickened up, and carpets being about ready to be replaced to be at a really good Fairfield level.

name: Bahia Resort Hotel
title: “God kvalitet og perfekt beliggenhed.”
text: Perfek beliggenhed i gå afstand til Mission Beach og lige ned til Mission Bay. Tæt på Sea World i bil, og ikke særligt langt til San Diego Downtowm. Værelserne er pæne og badeværelserne ligeså. Der er ingen overdreven luksus, men alle nødvendige bekvemmeligheder, såsom pool, fitness rum og tennis baner. Morgenmadsrestauranten (ej inkluderet) fungerer fint, med flot udvalg og sød betjening. God kaffe! Alt ialt fuldt tilfredsstillende

name: Bahia Resort Hotel
title: “tolles Familienhotel”
text:
Das Bahia liegt direkt an der Lagune von San Diego und circa 400-500 meter vom Strand entfernt. Wir hatten eine großzügige Wohnung mit Wohnzimmer,Küche, Schlafzimmer und Bad. Die Küche war komplett eingerichtet, so konnte man sich auch mal ein Steak braten. 
Die Zimmer waren etwas älter, sehr zweckmässig eingerichtet und sehr sauber. Es wurde jeden Tag gründlich sauber gemacht. 
Wir haben Fahrräder gemietet und sind stundenlang am Strand oder um die Lagune gefahren. Es gibt sehr gute Einkaufsmöglichkeiten, die prima per Fahrrad zu erreichen sind.
Parken ist kostenlos. Der Poolbereich ist eingezäunt, sauber und gepflegt. Man kann auch kostenlos jeden Tag eine Stunde Tennisspielen. 
Uns hat es gut gefallen und wir kommen wieder

name: Embassy Suites San Diego Bay - Downtown
title: “Great Experience”
text:
Came her with wife, 3 year old and 2 month old infant over Aug. 24-26 weekend. We had a great time. It's PERFECT for families. I've stayed at a few different Embassy Suites and while all are good for families, this was the best in our experience. Both the manager's reception (serving not only beer and wine but mixed drinks) and breakfast were even better than the other Embassy Suites. 
As usual, the rooms are all suites. As our son is older and we now have the infant, we actually had to use the living room pull out sofa bed and it was surprisingly comfortable.
Didn't have a single complaint. Advice to those reserving city view rooms...train tracks are pretty close so request a room on a higher floor and the noise from the trains shouldn't bother you (didn't bother us - 7th floor).

name: Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego
title: “The lobby is grand but the rooms? Not so much...”
text:
We stayed at this property once before, when the new lobby and tower were under construction (2003)--it is as though the rooms in the Seaport Tower have not been renovated since that time as ours appeared worn and tired, particularly the bathroom. 
The location is terrific and once again we had a fabulous view of the bay and surrounding area. Not sure what is so Grand about this Hyatt, however, other than the public areas which are very nice as is the pool. Oh, and the price--they must have the market cornered to charge the fees they do for such an average room--thank goodness for the views!
If ever we find ourselves in San Diego purely for pleasure I would not stay here and only did so because of husband's business meeting.

name: The Dana on Mission Bay
title: “Best hotel experience in San Diego”
text: I had a great experience at the Dana. The view of the bay from my room was beautiful, especially with a comfortable patio to witness it in. The room was comfortable for four people, the beds felt like clouds, and the bathroom felt luxurious yet simple. Guest service was fantastic, I felt at home. Would recommend it to anyone who is looking for a great place it which to relax and experience San Diego.

name: The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
title: “Loved our stay...”
text:
My husband and I were celebrating our one year anniversary in San Diego and based on reviews on various sites, we decided to stay at the Sheraton San Diego and Marina Hotel. When making our reservation, we let them know we were celebrating our one year anniversary and hoped to get a room in the Marina Tower with a nice view of the marina. Our check-in attendant was kind enough to go above and beyond our request and provided us with a townhouse in the Lanai area which is connected to the Marina Tower. We were SO happy with our stay here. We had a beautiful marina view, the staff was excellent, and the restaurants were great. 
We enjoyed our stay so much that we did not hesitate to book another night at this hotel after our flight was canceled. It is conveniently located close to the airport and is a short drive to many tourist attractions. Love, love, loved this hotel! Highly recommend!

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Nice Place”
text: The Hotel was very nice, Staff was especially nice and helpful, especially assistant front desk Manager Loic Pichardo who went above and beyond. The Location and amenities this property provides are awesome. Everything is immaculately maintaind including the pools, rooms, restaraunts, lobby etc. The property was built in 1962 so it has been there a while but it has been refurbished pretty well. It is very close to Sea World and beaches as well as oold town and gas Lamp. If possible try to get a room along the beach/inlet.

name: Andaz San Diego
title: “Noise”
text:
If you are over 50, this is not your hotel. They have a CLUB NITE on Thurs, Fri, and Sat. The vibration from the amplifiers could be felt through the floor and walls. This hotel is located in the heart of the Gaslamp quarter. There are many fine resturants in the area. It is near everything. The hotel is MODERN. Our friends had a shower with glass walls right near the bed.
Our sink was a steel bowl in a glass case. The staff is very friendly and courtious. I would stay again, but never on CLUB NITE.
 Tony (70 + )

name: Town and Country Resort Hotel
title: “I see the problem, now”
text: I was just at the Town and Country and I figured out why the reviews are so all over the place. The grounds are for the most part very nice and well maintained. I was there for a conference of over 600 people and the convention center was also good. The problem comes in with the rooms. They are all over the place. Mine was small and not that well appointed. It did not even have a desk to work at. Others rooms were better. With over 900 rooms there always seems to be something that needs repairs or updating. And they nickel and dime you for everything. They charge for parking, no free internet, you get the idea. Would I stay here on vacation, NO!

name: Ocean Beach Hotel
title: “Was ok”
text: Needs to get coffee machines in the rooms. New carpet would be nice. Great staff. Awesome views and location is fantastic. Great hotel for pets. Dog park close by. However, the homeless and drug peddlers on the boadwalk takes away from this hotel.

name: Westin San Diego
title: “Great Hotel”
text: I was staying at the Westin for a overnight business trip. The location is perfect for gas lamp district or the water front. The staff of the hotel are very friendly and ready to help with any need you may have. The rooms are large and have incredible beds!

name: Hilton San Diego Bayfront
title: “Great base for San Diego visit”
text: Not only are the views lovely but the location is perfect. The restaurants of the Gas Lamp Discount are conveniently across the street and it's easy to walk around the bay to the Maritime Museum. This is a large Hilton and if you are looking for a small boutique hotel, this is not the place for you but it is a very nice hotel. There is a nice pool and a spa (we didn't use the spa). Our room was on a high floor, the bed was very comfortable and I loved the chaise in front of the window! As honors Gold members we received discount coupons for the breakfast buffet and we dined there one morning. The selections were good and the service excellent. The 50% discount made it worth the money but without the discount, I think it makes more sense to go into the Gas Lamp District for breakfast. The Dole ship was unloading and I agree with others, it was fun to watch the process.

name: Ocean Beach Hotel
title: “A great hotel with a great location”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel over the new year's holiday. The weather was less than we expected but we had great views of the crashing waves right from our balcony. You cannot get ocean views for this price anywhere else!!! The staff was remarkable and it was a real treat to meet the couple that runs the hotel. They gave great recommendations on where to eat in the area.

name: Humphreys Half Moon Inn & Suites
title: “Very Impressed...”
text: After reading some on the reviews about Humphreys my friends and I decided to book this hotel, even though there were a couple of a negative reviews. Every hotel will have some kind of negative right? So we decided to take our chances and were amazed by what we got for the price. We booked a trip deal and got a really good deal on this hotel. The hotel is on the bay on Shelter Island, so it was about 10 minutes from the airport. Didnt bother us at all. We didnt have to deal with all of the downtown hustle and bustle all day. The hotel grounds were beautiful and peaceful and the staff was very friendly. We had a bay view and were able to sleep with our windows open at night. One previous review stated the pillows were flat, we didnt have that experience, but it did look like the hotel had been updated recently. The rooms were smaller than normal, but very quaint and comfy. The concert venue that the hotel has is great too. Even though we didnt buy tickets to the concerts, we did listen to the concerts from the hotel pool and hot tub in the evenings. Very entertaining. I could go on about the hotel, but I wont. I would definitely recommend Humphreys for someone who is looking for a nice hotel on the bay for a reasonable price.

name: The Dana on Mission Bay
title: “Family Holiday”
text: One of our favorite places to visit in the States is San Diego. Over the years we have stayed at various locations in San Diego. This year we stayed at the Dana. Are we ever glad we did. Great location, great amenities and great staff. Loved being on the Bay - so relaxing and peaceful - especially after a busy day at Sea World, the zoo, etc. This will be our choice from now on when we come to visit.

name: Hilton San Diego Bayfront
title: “great hotel”
text:
excellent hotel, great bar, restaurant, and location. 
next to the gasland district with plenty of restaurants and bars.
Fox restaurant first level of the hotel, great food, good ambiance and excellent place to watch a game. 
short cab ride to the USSmidway and other fun places to visit. 
across the street from the baseball park, awesome.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Blue Sea Lodge
title: “Blue Sea Lodeg does not disappoint in terms of value and location...”
text: For those of you who might question a stay at a Best Western, question no longer. From the time we arrived when Jason the manger who was very busy accommodating everyone including us, he gave excellent service in light of the fact that he was flying solo!!! He checked our bags and let us use the facilities until our room was ready, (we tried to check in around noon early). We walked the beach and Pacific Beach town for a bit and then were greeted by Cesar, the desk clerk who was busy trying to accommodate calls and check-ins but made time for us and even offered us an upgrade to an ocean front suite which was WELL worth every dollar!!! The staff were smiling and helpful as well as pleasant and we had a peaceful night's rest! Great location and staff and management who make sure that your stay is comfortable and that you know the area as well. Thank you, Cesar, Jason, AND Lupe for making us feel right at home:-)

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Delightful”
text: I booked this hotel through Travelocity and was quite hesitant after reading some of the comments left by others. I have to say that my stay was delightful. There was a group of 4 of us and the room was nice and big and we didn't feel cramped at all (and that is a lot due to the amount of luggage we all brought for our cruise the next day). The decor was very nice and the beds were very comfortable. We had a room that opened to a lake (I think it was called a lagoon room) . We opened our patio doors in the morning to enjoy the fresh air and to our delight we had a family of ducks join us in our room for the morning. They were very friendly and just came and went as they pleased (where else can you have that happen), We ate breakfast at the restaurant overlooking the ocean and both the food and the service were up to our standards. Overall we enjoyed our stay and I hope to return soon with my kids.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Past its sell by date - poor service and standards”
text:
We had hoped for better. The rooms are in blocks of chalets which are packed tightly together with parking spots outside so it's more of a motel than a hotel. Room OK but small compared to other hotels in USA - clean but buildings are old with old (and so noisy aircon, fridge, bathroom ventilation). Noisy plant room outside (possibly the pump for the duck pond water feature). Housekeeping was terrible - they often didn't turn up till after 4.00pm. Got locked out of the room at one stage due to a faulty door lock - I think they are old too - took ages to sort out - couldn’t get to see a manager (all too busy apparently).
The barefoot restaurant only has about 8 dishes on the menu which is the same for lunch and dinner - never changed all week we were there. The coffee bar is only open in the morning. The shop (Island Market) had helpful staff but was pricey. There are no other amenities nearby unless you drive.
It's only saving grace was that it is just about within walking distance of Seaworld for children (about a mile) - there is no hotel shuttle to Seaworld though. If that’s where you want to go to then that’s the only good reason for staying here - there are many much better places to stay in the San Diego area for the money. Don't stay any longer than 1 or 2 days though and think of it as an overpriced motel with swimming pools scattered around the car parks and you are less likely to be disappointed.

name: The Dana on Mission Bay
title: “Will stay here again!”
text:
Stayed here 7 nights with my girlfriend and her son(age 12) and another couple and their 2 kids(2-6) Everyone loved it! Our first night we had a courtyard level room and the courtyard by the tropical pool is beautiful, but it was a tad too small for the 3 of us for a week, plus we could hear the people above us stomping around. Usually I can tolerate occasional noise, but these rooms have older AC units and the combo of the foot stompers and loud AC was enough to change rooms. The next day we went to the front desk and they moved us to the newer section, which is made of concrete and quieter. We paid $40 a night for the upgrade, but the room was larger, with a view of the bay and worth the extra $$! By the way, the front desk crew was very nice and accomodating to us our whole stay.
We ate breakfast at the Blue Pearl a few times and it was pretty descent. Lunch was ok.
We had 3 meals at the Firefly and they were excellent. We were very happy with the quality of the food and service!
The pools are nice(towels provided in the room), with wait service at the pool by the firefly and a cabana-type bar at the tropical pool.
San Diego has so much to offer, but you can easily stay at this hotel and not leave(as long as you're willing to run a tab)
Since there's a marina behind the Dana, you can rent jet skis, paddle boats, pontoon and ski boats, etc.
I'd recomend this hotel for families, friends,and couples old and young. The staff is friendly, food good, rooms are nice, and you can't beat the location to Sea World, the beach ,downtown and the airport.

name: The Dana on Mission Bay
title: “An Amazing and Memorable Perfect Place”
text:
My husband and I were taking a much needed vacation in San Diego. We wanted something fun but relaxing in a beautiful location. The Dana Hotel is all of those things and MORE! 
First off, you just cannot beat the location. It is set on beautiful Mission Bay and our room overlooked the bay full of jet skiers, kayakers and boaters. We rented bikes and took a short trip to the Boardwalk which is full of fun nightlife and cool restaurants. Also, the hotel property is full of luscious trees and flower beds with two pools. The one pool we went to was rather large and had cabana shade you could sit under for no extra charge. It is a great place to take a nap or read a book. The other pool we never made it but it is located next to a beautiful garden and had a sandbox for kids to play in. It also had a snack bar that serves drinks :) There were two days that we didn't even leave the property. We just hung out at the pool and ate at the hotel. 
Second, the rooms are beautiful. The beds are comfortable and the decor is relaxing. Water in the shower stays warm and the shower head gives a strong flow. (with curly hair this is a must :) ) The housekeeping staff keeps the room super clean and restocks all towels and robes quickly.
The last and rather important aspect is the wonderful restaurants and staff at the Dana. We loved breakfast at the Blue Pearl which has really reasonable prices and AMAZING eggs benedict! We also loved the Firefly because not only does it serve the BEST creme brulee ever the staff is so friendly. My husband and I would get drinks there and chit chat with the wonderful ladies behind the bar. 
Basically, when I go back to San Diego, I know I will be staying at the Dana and I know we will have an incredible experience.

name: The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
title: “Nice place for a vacation.”
text: Pretty decent overall. Very attentive staff. The room condition was great...everything was nice and neat. I had a lenai room but it looked directly at a fence surrounding the tennis court. Self parking is $20/night which i thought was steep. Hotel is not within walking distance to anything so it is somewhat like a resort for someone who wants to hang out at the hotel pool and see other San Diego sights by car. The property has a very large feel to it as well.

name: Embassy Suites San Diego - La Jolla
title: “Very conveniently located to UCSD!”
text: We stayed at the Embassy Suites in La Jolla when dropping my son off for his freshman year at UCSD> This hotel is very conveniently located to the school, and is great for families with several children. Especially older kids. Our room had lots of space, and the pull out sofa in the living area was actually very comfortable. The complimentary full cooked breakfast in the morning makes this a good deal for families with teen boys!!! We will definately stay here again.

name: Humphreys Half Moon Inn & Suites
title: “Unique hotel, nice getaway”
text:
Beautiful property - it's visually appealing from the minute you drive up. 
I was frustrated at check-in, because while there seemed to be a few employees there, only one person was checking people in. It seems that they really like to take a lot of time with people when they check in (not your standard hand them your credit card and they hand you your room key kind of transaction. It's nice that they want to spend time with each person, but I waited about 20 minutes before it was my turn. 
I was very satisfied with my room - I thought it was modern and up-to-date, and nicely furnished. I had a view of the swimming pool area. 
The bathroom was nice, and had a nice array of shower/bath products. One thing I noticed was that if I was laying on the bed I could see a large gap between the entry door and the ground - I could see the ground outside. That creeped me out because who knows what could be crawling through there, but I didn't mention it to the hotel. 
A friend of mine was also staying at the property while I was there, and he was in the building that faces the stage in the concert area. His room didn't seem as nice as mine, but I can't really explain why I felt that way (seemed about the same size - different layout). His balcony was used by the sound crew during the concert, but no big deal because we weren't in the room at that time anyway. 
The service at the lounge on property was excellent - we had a specific request and they went out of their way to fulfill it, which we thought was really above and beyond standard hotel lounge service. We were very impressed. 
Overall, I really liked this property. It's beautifully landscaped and unique -doesn't feel like a regular hotel. I thought the service at checkin and checkout was slow, but other than that I can't complain.

name: Humphreys Half Moon Inn & Suites
title: “A beautiful hotel”
text:
This hotel is really lovely. Large clean rooms and very friendly staff.
Not much to do around the area at nights unless you are prepared to drive.
Would recommend the Red Sails restaurant and the Fiddlers. Very nice and not too expensive. Also Mexican and Italian restaurants which were very reasonable. There is also a seafood reasaurant and a Japanese restaurant in the immediate area but we didn't try them.
The hotel restaurant was very expensive (okay for a special occasion but not to eat in every night). Hotel bar okay if you like jazz as they have live music most nights but there is a cover charge of 4dollars.
Pool bar closes at 7 every night.
The pool area is very nice and there is not a fight for beds!!
There are lots of concerts in the summer, we didn't go to one but heard the afternoon practices. Quite loud but not a problem to us. Concerts on the evening were over by 10.30 so no disturbances.
 We also saw a wedding (right outside our room) That was a little embarrasing as we wanted to sit on outside with our evening drinks but felt as though we were intruding. But it was all over in 3/4 hour so not a great problem, just a minor inconvenience.
This hotel is a great base for sightseeing in San Diego but not really suitable for children as there is not much for them to do apart from the pool and a table tennis table.

name: Andaz San Diego
title: “Excellent Service”
text: Great boutique hotel. Room was quite large. Bathroom had lots of counter space. Comfortable bed. Complimentary snacks from the minibar. Rooftop bar is a great space for a cocktail at sunset. If you're a light sleeper this might not be the place for you. They basically have three nightclubs and you can hear the music in your room. Didn't bother us at all but this hotel has a serious club atmosphere so if that's not your thing you may want to look elsewhere. And as a hotel guest you have access to all the clubs. They also take security very seriously. It's a great alternative to the W. But $35 for parking is just plain CRAZY!!! At least the wi-fi was free.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Blue Sea Lodge
title: “Another great time in SD”
text: This is our third visit to Pacific Beach San Diego in the last ten years. Stayed at this hotel each time. This is a great place to stay; not fancy but can't beat the location and the friendly helpful staff. If you like beach and boardwalk this is it. Great local dining and shopping, sun and surf. Seem like the hotel is being well cared for as the room we stayed in was fresh and appeared fairly new. The pool and hot tub are terrific especially after a swim in the ocean. Lots to do, local bike rentals, walking, surf board rentals and did I say sun. Close to San Diego just a short drive to Old Town, airport, Gas Lamp district, Point Loma and La Jolla a great base of operations for lot of fun.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Loved this place”
text: Good location for the business I had to do. Great amenities, friendly and helpful staff.

name: Hampton Inn San Diego Airport / SeaWorld
title: “hotel stay for anniversary”
text: My husband made arrangements for our 35th wedding anniversary dec 7th 2012. The hotel and the staff were excellent. Not toooooo crazy about the actual location but was super impressed by the hotel, its staff and the room. The location is perfect for access to freeways etc... The staff went above and beyond were polite, pleasant and helpful. Eddie Villalpando was above and beyond in helping, even changing our room the second night because of the noise facing the street. Thank you again

name: Westin Gaslamp Quarter, San Diego
title: “Ottima posizione”
text:
Ho dormito in quest'albergo un paio di notti a settembre di quest'anno.
La posizione é ottima, a due passi dal quartiere di Gaslamp (il più movimentato per la serata) e attaccato ad Horton Plaza. A piedi poi si raggiunge facilmente anche la zona del porto.
Le camere sono spaziose e pulite e il servizio é in linea con gli altri alberghi della stessa catena. L'albergo é inoltre facilmente accessibile in auto ed é dotato di servizio di parcheggio (34$ al giorno). Soluzione consigliata per passare qualche giorno a San Diego.

name: Humphreys Half Moon Inn & Suites
title: “wonderful base to discover s.diego”
text: A group of six of us (three couples) stayed at Humphrey's for three nights 6-8 Jan, 2005, as part of a tour of W.california and Vegas. We were all very pleased with the rooms, all of which looked over the car park and over the bay. Checking in staff were more than helpful and rooms were spotless and kept that way by the housekeeping staff. We had stayed in hotels in San Fran and N. York whose standards were a lot lower than this one and we found that the staff here were a lot more friendly. The pool/jacuzzi area looked lovely - not that we got the opportunity to use it - we experienced an awful rain/wind storm on our second day! Went to a live music nite in the bar/restaurant building and had a brilliant nite. Local people who go to these music nights were so friendly and welcoming. We did'nt see S.diego in the best season (weather-wise) but we are determined to revisit in warmer times and would definitely stay at Humphreys again. Don't know what other reviewers were on about when they say it could do with a refit - our rooms must have been done!

name: Westin Gaslamp Quarter, San Diego
title: “Mooi hotel gelegen in het centrum”
text: Mooie hotel gelegen naast groot shopping mall in het centrum van san diego. Een hotel waar er in Nederland maar weinig van te vinden zijn qua inrichting, service (o.a. starbucks), kamerinrichting en sportfaciliteiten. Het hotel ligt op 10 minuten loopafstand van het convention center en de zee zodat business en ontspanning uitstekend te combineren vallen.

name: Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego
title: “Great location, average rooms”
text:
Stayed here for 6 days. The location is great, downtown San Diego, close to many attractions. The price paid for a double bed room with harbor view, facing west, was a bit over $200 per night. The entrance and the public areas are "grand", but as others have mentioned, the rooms are average. I will try to post pics. You pay for the location and the view (if you have one). One thing that we found annoying was that the walls seemed to be very "thin" and we could hear voices and phones from next door. That is not nice! The staff was very nice and very helpful. If we requested something they would be up in a few minutes to bring it (pillows, a new coffee carafe for the one we broke..).
Before you book, check out the "W", not located downtown by the water, but a 10 minute walk away. Especially if you have no kids with you and are young or young at heart. It has nice bars, and a nice "beach" bar with sand!
Overall, we liked the Hyatt, but we were not thrilled with it. For $200 a night we think it was OK, but not for more $ than that.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Paradise for the kids .... Hades for the adults!!!!!!!”
text: First, I will start off by saying that our kids, ages 8,6,4 and 8 mos, had an absolute BLAST. Highlights of the trip were: waverunners, bonfires, great pool service, and a fun dinner at the local Fillipis's Pizza in PB. We rented a bayside bungalow for 3 nights. The rooms were old. Customer service was terrible .... basically, expect none. There was not enough shade at the pool or the Barefoot Bar. It's basically Paradise for the kids and Hades for the adults!!!! Piece of advice, set your expectations low and you will not be disappointed. We paid $279 for the bayside bungalows and I think it's a fair price. However, NEVER pay $579 for the bungalows .... it's just not worth it!!!!!!

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Paradise Point - a great family getaway!”
text: Wonderful hotel. The furniture and rooms are a bit dated but the common areas and the grounds are the best we've seen. Pools are wonderful. Not terribly impressed by the Barefoot Bar & Grill but would try it again. January was awesome here but the warmer months would be incredible.

name: Andaz San Diego
title: “Rooms not particularly female friendly”
text:
Mid week stay, so night club noise not an issue.
The Good:
Some (operative word) staff lovely -- Lyndsay, Jeff and Tyler
No charge for some beverages and snacks.
Clean and well appointed rooms.
Nice location in Gaslight district.
The Not So Good
No full length mirror in room -- very tough for women.
Poor lighting in room. I was on the second floor (interior) and there wasn't any light from outside so this seemed important.. 
Impossible to hang up your robe after use --- unless you are 6 feet tall (minor issue)
Some staff (Jared?spelling) not particularly customer oriented. 
I think if you are male and need to be in the area it's probably a great place to stay. If you are female find a place with a full length mirror and better lighting.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Blue Sea Lodge
title: “Nice hotel on the beach - great value for the money”
text: We finished our family California vacation in San Diego with two rooms at the Best Western Blue Sea Lodge. The rooms were clean and well laid out with a fridge, coffee maker (with an excellent local Santa Barbara blend of coffee) and microwave. The beach is steps away and the pool area with lounge chairs right at the boardwalk was very nice. Pacific Beach was a perfect location for our San Diego trip, close to Sea World and the downtown area. The front desk staff was very helpful. We enjoyed our stay and would return when in San Diego.

name: Hampton Inn San Diego Airport / SeaWorld
title: “Convenient, good breakfast, older”
text:
We came here for our trip to Seaworld. We thought it would be an upgrade from Days Inn which is where we stayed last time. It is a hotel vs. a motel which is nice. However, it is older with some upgrades, e.g. Newly tiled bathrooms. I was disappointed that they did not offer a free shuttle to Seaworld which Days Inn offers. We ended up paying another $15 a day for parking at Seaworld. The room was a good size but had little drawer room or bathroom counter space. I wish there were towel hooks for the hand towels and hooks behind the bathroom door. Our room was right across the ice maker which disturbed our sleep along with the very loud air conditioning. We moved to another room in the back of the hotel which was quieter. There is also more parking in the back of the hotel (by entrance #3). Breakfast was good except they pre-salt their eggs, otherwise the fresh fruit and yogurt was great. My husband liked the Belgium waffles and different sausages each day. The pool was ok but I had to ask the front desk to kick out a loud family after 10 p.m. 
The hotel is located just below a freeway off ramp which is very busy. There's also a couple of nude bars around the block. My 8 y.o. son kept asking us why the building said "nude" which put us in an awkward situation. It was pretty full when we stayed here, but we may go back to Days Inn next time.

name: The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
title: “Awful”
text: I stayed at the West Tower for 6 nights last week and had 5 different rooms due to the renovations. I spent the week sharing the evevators with hotel staff and hoping it would stop on my floor. I was very disappointed with my stay. The West tower also only has 1 restaurant. I would definately not recommend the hotel here in the near future and avoid a room by the elevator at all costs as you will be stuck listening to them day and night.

name: Andaz San Diego
title: “Pretty Good with some Rought Spots”
text:
I completed a 1 night stay here on Friday. Upon check-in, we were given a choice of the $15 wine card or a cheese plate and a bottle of wine for our Diamond amenity. Since we were a party of two, I asked if we could have some extra funds on the wine card, to which the answer was no. In retrospect, I think I should have gotten the cheese plate and bottle of wine, since the wine bar is expensive and $15 is really only good for about 1 glass.
Check-in was fine. Parking is expensive at $35/night. We used a Diamond Suite upgrade and at first was put in a "Large King." I refused this room and told the front desk this was not a suite. We were then moved to an Andaz Loft. This isn't really a suite. But since I was only there for 1 night, we took this room. We were proactively warned about the, noise from the club above which was appreciated. 
Even though the Andaz Loft is definitely not a suite, I liked the room. I liked the decor, layout and the bed was comfortable. I don't know what this hotel was like before the conversion to Andaz, but i think Hyatt did a good job at renovating this property.
I checked out the rooftop bar/pool and the gym. Both were nice, but nothing memorable.
In the evening, we went to the wine bar. There wasn't a soul there, so we had the bartender to ourselves and got some good service. In addition to trying out the wines, we got some appetizers and the pizza and cheese plate we got were very good. One word of note: make sure to only put money on the card that you are prepared to use. Any leftover money on the wine card cannot be refunded, which I was a bit upset about because I saw no reason why they couldn't provide a refund.
In terms of the noise, yes it was loud. On the night we were there, it ended at about 1AM. For one or two nights, it would be ok for me and my sig other, since we are both heavy sleepers, but i definitely would not be able to take that noise every night.
The next morning we had breakfast and got the best service that we ever received throughout our stay from our waitress that morning. She was very courteous and gave us carte blanche to order whatever we wanted. We gave her a nice tip.
Unfortunately, at checkout, the front desk erroneously charged us for minibar charges which we did not take, and also erroneously charged us for breakfast. For some reason, it took a long time for this to be settled, and I left the hotel a bit annoyed with the staff.
In summary, I'd probably come back for another short stay, but I wouldn't be able to take a weekend here because of the noise. And I definitely wouldn't waste a suite upgrade here.

name: Hilton San Diego Bayfront
title: “perfect location for a convention”
text: A very nice hotel with a perfect location for a convention. Located just across the San Diego Convention Center, this hotel is close to almost everything of interest in downtown San Diego.It is conveniently near the gaslamp district where you will find all sorts of bars and restaurants and is also a few minutes walk to the USS midway museum. Very near also is the train stop which you can take to go to as far as the Las Americas outlet mall near the border of Mexico. The rooms are spacious and adequately furnished and the amenities are above average. I also love the bar with a patio facing the bay where you can have drinks at night. The walkway connecting to the bay walk is perfect for our early morning runs. The only negative thing i can say about this hotel is our experience at the breakfast buffet. We stayed for 5 days in the hotel and everyday we had to wait for atleast 15 minutes to get a table. They do give you a pager but you can't really go very far and there were not enough seats while waiting, so every morning you will see a long queu leading to the restaurant. We tried going early, at 630AM, and late, 9Am, but still the line was long. The staff explained that the hotel was full and that there were several conventions going on in the convention center. But they should have anticipated that given their location or atleast open another restaurant for breakfast if the hotel is full. To make things worst, you get the same food everyday. The choices did not vary and you will see the same type of food on the same tray on the same spot everyday. Again, they know that most of their guests are attending conventions which lasts for a few days so they should atleast vary their food selections (atleast the main courses) everyday. What made us go back to breakfast everyday (aside from the fact that it is included in the room charges) are the very courteous and friendly staffs in the restaurant. Overall, my experience in this hotel was excellent and if you get tired of the same food during breakfast, there is always Starbucks infront of the hotel.

name: Red Roof Inn San Antonio - Airport
title: “Great upgrades and Linda was great again”
text: I truly appreciate someone that values customer service and Linda at the front desk did that. I stayed there back in March and just recently. She is the main reason I returned. Thank you and keep up the good work of the lost art of customer service in this day and age.

name: Hampton Inn San Antonio Downtown (River Walk)
title: “Great location”
text: I stayed here for two nights on a business trip and the location was perfect. It is close enough to everything without being in the middle of everything. There are hotels closer to the river walk but you have to deal with the crowds and people asking for money. The hotel has easy access from the highway and it is not far from the airport plus the Alamo is only a few blocks away. The only issue I had was a delay in hot water but it was close to 100 degrees so who really wants to take a steaming hot shower. Other reviews mentioned the same thing but if you let the water run long enough it became very hot. The pool had a lot of leafs and flowers floating in it but the wind was also blowing very hard so I imagine it was hard to keep clean. Self parking was easy and not too expensive. I have traveled to SA dozen of times but never stayed here but I will make it a point to going forward.

name: Hyatt Place San Antonio Northwest
title: “Great place”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for 1wk and loved it.
Great location, as it is not too far from downtown and not too close either. 
It has a quite of places to eat at close by, and also is not far from shopping malls or attractions.
The hotel operates a shuttle service within I think it was 3-5mile radius of the hotel itself.
It is about a 10min walk to Drury Inn and Suites, of which there is a bus stop that if required you can get a bus to the mall and even downtown. 
Close to us, there was a pool hall/bar restaurant.
Very hot during the summer Months San Antonio. About 106-109degrees in the day and max round the 90s at night.
I would certainly reccommend this hotel in terms of value for money and location.

name: Wyndham La Cascada
title: “A positive experience at La Cascada”
text:
The staff has ben exceptional, we were driving in from the airport and felt like we were not going in the correct direction, so we called the resort and the desk clerk talked us to the resort entrance. We had groceries and our luggage, the valet were there to load and unload for us. The room is large, full kitchen and laundry, jacuzzi, all clean and in order. If I had too "search" for simething that needed improving, it would be the couch! One other item that would make the living room "homey" would be re recliners! We would highly recommend this rresort and the staff.
Jack & Sharon

name: Hampton Inn San Antonio Downtown (River Walk)
title: “Unexpected pleasure”
text: I got this hotel through hotwire and I must say I was pleasantly surprised at the quality of the stay. The complementary breakfast was fantastic. Only downside was the parking spots were a little small but at least free!

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Overpriced!”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for our honeymoon.
For the price of the place, we would have expected big rooms, but the room we stayed in was small and stuffy. At least the bed was comfy.
I felt it was way overpriced for what we got, the Holiday Inn would have been a great comparison.

name: Wyndham La Cascada
title: “great location!”
text:
Just returned from a 7 day stay on the 9th floor in a 1 bedroom unit timeshare. Great rooms, just-okay couch bed for guest sleeping, and very noisy 4am wake-ups daily from garbage trucks below.
The "heated" pool was chilly, 2 computers weren't enough to go around and constant "tipping" to valets for parking was annoying. We paid $15 a day for parking, as well. City spaces are pricey so it was justifiable. 
Front desk was efficient. Flat screen tv was a tad fuzzy. Great location, though, to EVERYTHING. Drove to get groceries and to attend an amazing yearly Rodeo. Cooked quite a few meals in our wonderfuly equipped kitchen. Awesome balcony views of downtown. Mostly a perfect week with the exception of the GARBAGE TRUCKS! We would return there again~

name: Red Roof Inn San Antonio - Airport
title: “Not Bad but could have been much nicer with a few simple upgrades”
text:
My wife and I stayed at this hotel for one night. We used Hotwire and got booked here. The hotel appears to be a clean hotel with no obvious issues. Our room was in good shape and ready on time. Hotwire had booked us a smoking room with two beds and the hotel gladly let us change to a non smoking king bed. 
Here are the things that kept me from giving this hotel a better rating. Most delt with the bathroom.
For a king bed there were three almost airline size pillows...
The towels were those cheap, thin towels that don't dry off anything
The toilet paper said soft on the name..I think they were referring to the paper it was wrapped in
The toilet was the loudest thing I've ever heard.....if you have been on a cruise, you know how loud those things are...this beat them. 
The pillow, towel and toilet paper issues could easily be resolved and would have made a nice difference. I'm writing this from our next stay which is in a Hampton Inn in Harlingen, TX. We payed $10 more for this room and it doesn't have any of these issues...it makes all of the difference in the world. 
Overall, not a bad hotel..but could have been much better

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites San Antonio Airport
title: “15 years using La Quinta”
text:
well i want to say that i always loved using la quinta.....but im not sure if you guys are aware of this but you have been slipping the last few years.....carpets were very dirty and stained and i called the front desk twice in two days and i told them the soda machine on the 7th floor is not working and have not done anything about it....also no towels in the pool two days in a row .....
it was very hard writing this because i really like la quinta.....please get back to the level were used to having here ...thanks loyal la quinta customer....

name: Microtel Inn & Suites by Wyndham San Antonio Airport North
title: “Comfortable, Professional, High Quality”
text:
As a heavy business traveler, I rely on hotels for a number or reasons: comfort, professional services, and quality. This Microtel far exceeded all three of these aspects. From the moment I checked in, I received impeccable customer service. The room I recieved was very spacious, and provided a very comfortable setting for which I could both relax and do some work. Finally, I found the location to be very convenient for all of my meetings throughout San Antonio. I will definitely recommend this hotel to other colleagues and friends of mine that travel to San Antonio, on either business or pleasure.
Charles Whittaker
Executive Managing Director
Frank Crystal & Co.

name: The Dana on Mission Bay
title: “Relax and Enjoy at the Dana”
text: This was our first trip. Since we are from Boston, we are not completely familiar with the area. We tried the Dana because we learned about Bartell Hotels through University of San Diego, where our son is a freshman. The website is great, but the Dana "live" was even more impressive than what we expected from the virtual depiction. We most definately will return. Thank you for all the friendly hospitality.

name: Hampton Inn San Diego Airport / SeaWorld
title: “Great deal for your money”
text: I stayed in the standard room and was very pleased. As an added bonus the front desk attendant, Justin was simply awesome & made our visit!

name: The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
title: “$14.00 parking fee for overnight guests???”
text:
Good Afternoon, my name is Candace and my friend and I am writing out of courtesy to such a beautiful hotel. After attending a seminar at the "East Tower" and paying a total of $12.00 "validated" parking fee ($6.00 for morning, left for lunch, paid another $6.00 for evening), we then stayed the evening at the "West Tower" and had to pay an additional $14.00 parking fee after paying approx. $200.00 as a guest for the evening. On my initial visit to check the hotel out (approx. 
time 12:00 p.m.), Petra, very gracious person, allowed me to take a look at room 1181 for $169.00. Unsure if I could get out of a reserved reservation somewhere else, Petra said she would advise the clerk after her to keep a room available for us making sure we understood it may not be room 1181. I understood. As it was, we left our seminar, successfully canceled our other reservation, and quickly went to the West Tower approx. time was 4:15 p.m. At check in, Lorna, I believe, gave us a room on the 4th floor, 481? I asked if 1181 was available, she said no, to get a room on the higher floors is an extra $30.00 or so. Even though Petra was going to give us an 11th floor room? Yes, she said. We went to the room on the fourth floor and it had two holes in the ceiling from apparent maintenance. When I called the front desk from the phone, they asked me if I was sure. We went back down to the front desk. She and another gentlemen questioned my friend and I as to whether we were sure of the problem. The holes would speak for themselves if they had looked for themselves. She then gave us a room on the fifth floor, #581. At this point a room higher would have been a gracious thing to do, but Petra seemed to be the only gracious one at this point and she wasn't there. The Next morning at check out, 7:00 a.m., after explaining the inconvenience, we were given a $15.00 discount. We're not sure what would have been the thing to do, but it just doesn't seem that that was it. You have a beautiful hotel!! We visit San Diego quite often and definitely would love to stay again. 
However, a parking fee for overnight guests and a bit of attitude from some of your staff, well, these are important things to us and may mean the difference of any return visits and/or any recommendations we may have to our friends. Thank you for your time in reading this review, it is very much appreciated. Sincerely, Candace and Tina

name: Hampton Inn San Diego Airport / SeaWorld
title: “Don't let the neighborhood fool you!”
text: This is a great hotel--definately at the upper end of Hampton properties. While it's located in a very low end neighborhood--next to 2 "all nude reviews"--you never will notice once in the hotel with it's center courtyard and pool. Balconies and decks to enjoy the weather.

name: Drury Inn & Suites San Antonio Northwest Medical Center
title: “Great Stay!!”
text: We stayedat the Drury Inn over the 4th of July weekend. From the moment we walked in we were greeeted with smile. When we reached our room we discovered that the A/C was not working. We called to report the problem and within minutes the night supervisior (Jose Garza) took action and placed us into a bigger room with more ammeties. We were surprised at the quick response and friendly services we recieved the whole 3 days we were there. The morning buffett with hot waffles is an added plus and saves you money and time. Also dont forget the evening reception with cocktails and sodas. You are granted 3 drinks a person and they dont mind you getting all 3 at once to take back to the room. The reception also had hot dogs, nachos, chex mix, and chile. One thing is for sure, we will stay here again and again!

name: Hampton Inn San Diego Airport / SeaWorld
title: “Awesome, helpful people!”
text: I was needing a room quick and well before check-in due to a change in work. I called the hotel and asked if they had a shuttle and room ready. They said yes to both and asked if I was a HHonors member so they could book my room while I was on my way. They also allowed me to check-out late. EVERYONE I dealt with at the hotel, including the shuttle drivers, were super helpful. The room was large and clean with an awesome bed and nice TV. Breakfast wasn't all that bad either. I will use this hotel if I am in the area and need one. Great job staff!

name: BEST WESTERN Lamplighter Inn & Suites at SDSU
title: “Gute Wahl”
text:
Diese Hotel war für uns eine sehr gute Wahl. Das Preis-/Leistungsverhältnis war mehr als gut. Die Zimmer waren völlig in Ordnung und das Frühstück war super. Die Lage war mit einem Mietauto ebenfalls sehr gut, auch wenn man natürlich etwas "ab vom Schuss" ist, aber dafür ist es ja auch sehr günstig und man ist Ruck-zuck auf allen großen Straßen. 
Der Scenic-Drive war super und auch sonst hat uns San Diego richtig gut gefallen!

name: The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
The Sheraton San Diego Hotel & Marina
title: “Better than expected”
text:
After reading all of the bad reviews on this hotel, we were prepared for the week long stay 3/20/04 - 3/27/04. We booked it through priceline and expected the worst. Firts of all, the hotel was in excellent location, only 2 minutes down the street from Hertz, Avis and National rental car lot. The hotel was very easy for us to find after picked up our rental car at Hertz at 10 PM after a very long flight. 
You could see the Shareton from the airport and there were 2 buildings with big red S. These are the 2 towers for the hotel. You can check in at either one and chances are you would get to the main building (East Tower). It was confusing on the 2 towers from people's reviews. The East Tower is the main building with large and nice reception hall, beautiful pool, fitness center, nice landscape. This was also the building we arrived from the rental car lot. At check in, we were told that our reservation was for room on the 1-4 floors. We were given the option to upgrade to a upper floor room with free breakfast and parking for $50/night. We declined the offer and was given a room on the 2nd floor in the West Tower. The West Tower was 1/4 mile down the road on Harbor Dr. It was a complete separate building with its own small pool and restaurant. Our room on the 2nd floor was very nice with balcony and marine view. There was only 1 bed in the room and we asked the front desk at the West Tower to switch to a room with 2 beds. We were given a free upgade to a room on the 7th floor with 2 beds, breakfast & parking were not free. We got a room with 2 beds overlooking the harbor. It was nice and big and clean. All rooms were the same size in the West Tower. Even number rooms have the marina view, and odd number rooms have harbor view. Although the pool was small and cold in the West Tower, the view was much better. All rooms have nice view in the West Tower. Couldn't say the same for rooms in the East Tower. The room keycard also worked as the access card to the parking lot at both towers. It was true that it didn't work. We must asked them 3-4 times to give us a new card for access to the parking lot. Finally, we realized that it didn't matter that the car didn't work. When we entered the parking lot, if the card didn't work, just push the green bottom for a ticket. We didn't get charge for getting a ticket and it was easy to use instead of trying to swipe the card and wait for the arm to raise at the lot entrance. It was also true about the noise. If you were a light sleeper, you could hear people showering and door slaming, or children running up the hall. At the West Tower, you could hardly hear the plane noise from the airport, but you could hear the plane noise from the Navy base across the harbor. The location and the view made up for the noise. Harbor Island was nice & quiet and safe. We felt safe to walk along the harbor in front of the hotel at night. We drove to downtown & the gaslamp quarter for dinner. We were glad that we didn't stay at downtown because there were homeless on the street. 
There was a homeless shelter located a few blocks from the gaslamp quarter. There were many one way streets in downtown and you could easily ended up at the bad section in downtown. With a car, withing 5 minutes of driving on Harbor Island/Shalter Island, there were fastfood, grocery stores, popular Mexican restaurant, cafe so we didn't eat at the hotel. The hotel staffs were very helpful and friendly and gave us advice where to eat nearby. We did pay $16/night parking, and the gas was $2.20/gal in San Diego. Having a car was expensive but also very convienent. The trolley did come to the hotel (The West Tower) as one of the stop. So if you didn't have a car, you could take the trolley to the main attractions. The hotel shuttle runs between the airport and the East & West Towers. After all, we loved the hotel for its excellent location next to the airport and on the harbor, view of downtown from our balcony. San Diego is a small city, it was a 5 minutes drive to Downtown, and 10 minutes to Old Town. If you were a water person, this is a great hotel to stay at. If you were not a water person, many reasonable price hotels/motels at Mission Valley hotel circle would be a better choice.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “avoid this hotel”
text:
I came here for a conference.
average decor in the room.
silverware was dirty almost every time. didn't seem like they care about the cleaniness at all. The glasses had black stuff stuck on it. and half of the glasses smell like bad breath. so I am very unsatisfied with how they clean.
toilet was leaking. after flushing the water drips out. yuck.
and worst of all, I could never reach front desk. the phone just rang and rang. so they are always understaffed. 
if it weren't for the conference, i would never come.

name: San Diego Marriott Marquis & Marina
title: “Excellent location”
text: Excellent location! Gaslamp Quarter is right across and Seaport Village is just beside this big hotel. The room that we occupied has a great view of the pool and the marina. Drinking water with strawberries in the lobby is an excellent touch!

name: Bristol Hotel
title: “Great boutique hotel in ok location”
text: I stayed 5 nights at the Bristol while attending a conference in San Diego. I attend this conference every year and have stayed at many downtown hotels. The Bristol is a great little boutique hotel - the staff were very accommodating - and the rooms were clean with free internet etc. On the negative side, it is quite a hike from the convention center although close to Horton Plaza and Gaslamp. The biggest problem is the location across from the main bus/transit station which made me uncomfortable (as a woman) walking back alone in the evenings. If I had been with a larger group or with my spouse, this wouldn't be such an issue. I would definitely stay there again, but would choose other hotels over this if their location was a bit closer to the convention center and in a safer area.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Fiesta Inn
title: “Best place to stay near Six Flags Fiesta Texas”
text: Great location near six flags, ideal for family, located surrounded by a commercial area (groceries, gas stations, shopping & fast food). Great service, clean rooms, nice pool ,and waffles from continental breakfast are delicious!. Located next to the I-10, few miles from 410 & one exit away from 1604 loop. Friendly front desk and always alert of customer needs. HD TV at lobby. Comfortable and clean beads, noise from exterior can't disturb you even with kids on pool if you stay near to it. Hot water & air conditioner always available. Fast wireless internet connection. Free parking lot. and finally the price is lower than similar hotel chains. Check promotions before booking !

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Fiesta Inn
title: “best for the price”
text: everything was good and people there were very friendly. everything was clean and organize. breakfast serving was ok everything was the same but overall it was good. i would definitely come back for another couple nights stay.

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Antonio Airport
title: “Consistent, Clean, Reasonable”
text: Very convenient to the airport and access to the freeway system for all other San Antonio destinations. Very clean, new, efficient use of space. Free wifi. Good value. Plenty of parking on site and no charge for parking. Snackbar with breafast, lunch and dinner items for purchase. Short list.

name: Residence Inn San Antonio Airport
title: “GREAT STAFF!!”
text:
Great staff, very accommodating. This is an older hotel, but it is updated and clean as a whistle. Everyone was very welcoming, from the Desk Staff to the Breakfast Attendants to the Evening Reception Attendant. Vanessa was especially helpful, as was the rest of the Front Desk. A-1 all the way.
There is only one computer in the Business Center, which was busy in the evenings. A couple more would have been nice.

name: Sleep Inn & Suites at Six Flags
title: “Nice place for the price”
text: Overall great stay. The pool was really dirty when we got there but once we brought it to the staff's attention it was good to go the next day! Breakfast not too great but does have waffles.

name: Fairfield Inn San Antonio Airport/North Star Mall
title: “Always a great stay”
text: I have stayed here many times and its always great. The staff is awesome and the rooms are clean and comfortable. Location is perfect. I enjoy breakfast with the Jimmy Dean sandwiches.

name: Holiday Inn San Antonio NW - Seaworld Area
title: “Very Disappointing Stay”
text:
I frequent Holiday Inns when I travel. Usually I am more than pleased with my stay. The Holiday Inn NW - Seaworld Area was an exception to this rule. This was the worst Holiday Inn in which I have ever stayed. The parking was pathetic. We had to park in an unpaved field next to the hotel. This is a "green" hotel which I knew when we made our reservations. I did not anticipate the room being so warm and stuffy upon arrival. I took all night for the room to cool off enough to be comfortable. The next morning when we left the room and removed the key from the switch, the room overheated again so that we had to return from Seaworld to a hot room. The lighting was awful. 
I had knocked my glasses off the night stand during the night and the next day when we checked out I did not realize until I got home that I had not gotten my glasses. I called the hotel, spoke with the operator who took my report of lost glasses and was told that she would immediately pass it along to housekeeping. I called back the next day and spoke directly with housekeeping. They had not had a report of missing glasses so I repeated all my information, giving them the room number and where I thought my glasses might be. The lady I spoke with told me she would pass this along to the supervisor and she would call me back. I waited until afternoon and called back again. Housekeeping knew nothing of the lost glasses but they would have someone call me back. I never got a call back. I then called the Manager of the hotel. He was not available so I left a message for him to call me regarding my missing glasses. He called me back. I told him the entire story and he said he would check on them and call me back. He did call me back and had found my glasses. I gave him my FedEx number and he overnighted them back to me. About this, I was very pleased; eventhough I had to make 4 long distance calls to get a resolution.

name: Comfort Inn & Suites Near Medical Center
title: “THE MANAGER "MARC" STOLE MY MONEY”
text: please i warn u do not go to this hotel....even if its the last hotel on earth.The manager stole money from me. He ran my card and lied to me saying it was declined,when i called my bank they had advised me infact my card was charged from this hotel, after i just paid him cash for the same amount.They steal and lie about it. Cops came out to the hotel and sorted out everything. Oh and lets not forget my room was infested with ants!!!

name: Sierra Royale
title: “Sierra Royale is perfect for families!”
text: Sierra Royale is great for families! We stayed in a 2 Bedroom, 2 Bath/2 Living Area, fully furnished condo and our kids loved it! They had their own room and bathroom, we had a T. V. in the master and one in the living room . We could stay in and cook or go out while we visited San ANtonio. It was 7 minutes from SeaWorld which was convenient. We wish more cities had converted apartment complexes into hotels, it beat cramming a family of 4 into a 300 square foot hotel room. This place was 1200 sq ft to ourselves! They even have a swimming pool, hot tub, & catered breakfasts. The best part was our own washer & dryer so we could wash clothes that got wet after swimmimg. We will be back to Sierra Royale!

name: Days Inn San Antonio/AT&T Center
title: “OK, barely”
text: Room had a musty smell and there was mold in the tub area. "Breakfast" is supposedly ready at 6:30AM, but the door was not unlocked for another 10 minutes while we stood outside. When we did get in the lobby - still had to wait for the coffee to perk and for the remainder of the meager offerings to be put out. Grounds could use some care, too. Probably will not stay here again.

name: Econo Lodge Central San Antonio
title: “Bed Bugs Bites-Over 200 bed bug bites on me”
text: I arrived at the hotel at 8:00 am . I stayed rhere on the 19th of August. On wednesday morning I found over 200 bed bug bites on my body. I took images of the bites. I camped out tues and wednesday20th&21st. This was the only hotel I stayed in that week. This is the first time this has happened to me. I am not looking for a refund or anything like that. It is my duty to report this. I do not want anyone especially children to go through this terrible pain of itching and scrathing to the point of bleeding and scaring.Be careful.

name: Days Inn Downtown/Riverwalk
title: “Horrible,Stinky,Worst hotel ever”
text: This is really the worst hotel i stayed in ever when i entered the room it smelled so bad,bath room was the worst part very dirty, carpet was sticky bed sheets had spots on them and the mattress box had holes in them and were open there was no sheet or bed skirt on them i did'nt sleep almost all night because i was scared that any bug might come out of the holes ,there is a train crossing so you can hear honkings of the train at almost 2 o clock and again at 4 or 5 o clock,i wo'nt recommend this hotel to any one because it was the last day of my vacation and we did'nt plan to book this hotel they also charged a lot of that stinky room ,and our last day was ruined and it is not even close to river walk.Believe me book anther hotel if you want to enjoy and sleep well.

name: Alamo Lodge
title: “Horrible place, wouldn't go back!”
text: I stayed at this place on a family trip to Seaworld and boy was that a mistake! As we checked in the women next to us was calling the police because her room had been robbed of all her luggage etc, a prostitute walked in circles around the motel, and our sheets were... well we will say "used" by the previous guests and had bodily fluids on them, wet! I bought a sleeping bag and didn't even risk getting under the covers. The people underneath us actually solicited drugs to my mother! This place was a nightmare and I don't recommend it to anyone, and I usually leave nice reviews!

name: Fiesta Inn & Suites
title: “Be Afraid, Very Afraid!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text: I booked the room online, thru Expedia. The pictures they show are hi-jacked from some other site. We arrived on Friday night, it was horrible. I should have run away then but we were tired. The door lock was broken, there were roaches, the fridge didn't work, no microwave(clientel probably pawned it or blew it up cooking meth). We asked for the door lock to be fixed and were told they would have maintainence look at it the next day. We left, went to Wal-Mart across the highway, spent $67 on cleaning supplies, a screwdriver, a knife, and trash bags. We stayed the night because we couldn't find another room. WE GOT THE HELL OUTTA THERE IN THE MORNING!!!!!!! There were drug dealers in the parking lot, hookers turning tricks, people fighting all night. We slept on top of the beds, in our clothes! This place needs to be raided by the DEA, Vice Squad, Fire Marshal, INS, FBI. DO NOT GO NEAR THIS PLACE!!!

name: Motel 6 San Antonio - Ft. Sam Houston
title: “very bad part of town partying and fighting all night”
text: called reserved room all was good right? no i stay at alot of motel 6 propertys and this was right there with the worst of the worst ! i checked in about 10pm and was ready to leave at 10;05! i was there about 5 min when a fight broke out and it was not 20min after that that a party started when i called the frount desk they said they would look in to it! well i just gave up at 12;30 and left it is not somewhere you want to stay ! keep your money and go somwhere other then here !

name: Days Inn Airport
title: “bad motel”
text: Had a reservation and paid in advance, upon arival was charged $2.00 cleaning charge. Went to room 208 key did not work, was sent to room 212. air conditioning was not great but did cool off after being on all day. Went to bed late woke up at 3 in the morning found bed bugs in bed. Went to manager he said we could have another room had a flight at 6 so no help there. Bed bugs are unacceptable and then a neetie attitude from management is terrible. Do Not stay here BED BUGS In Rooms.

name: HomeGate Studios & Suites San Antonio Fiesta Park
title: “Dump”
text: This place is a dump. It should be shut down. The room was dirty when I got there. I would never stay here again. The workers that clean the rooms did not clean. Garbage around the property and dog poop.

name: HomeGate Studios & Suites San Antonio Fiesta Park
title: “Never been more disappointed!”
text: To begin with we called the morning before checking in to see if pets were allowed. We were told there was a $50 "pet deposit" that would be refunded when we checked out. When we arrived, after I had already given the front desk my credit card information I was told that it is a nonrefundable pet fee. $50 pet fee...REALLY? The nightly rate was also higher than I was told on the phone. My family was tired and ready to rest or I would have left at that point. The rooms were dirty and I do mean DIRTY! The bathroom smelled of urine, and the kitchen area was not clean. There were only 2 towels and 1 washcloth in the room. The mattress on the bed was terrible. The rooms were not cleaned by housekeeping. The beds were made and that was it. The trash was not emptied, no vacuuming, nothing! The positives about this place were the continental breakfast and the girl who worked the front desk at night was very nice. This is my first time ever to write a review but felt compelled to share my experience so that others can avoid this dump. We are at another motel tonight that is $20 a night cheaper, $10 pet fee and a whole lot nicer.

name: Super 8 San Antonio/Downtown I-10 East
title: “Decent place to stay”
text: I had a confirmed reservation made online, but the manager at first tried to overcharge me. He finally relented and gave me the online price. The room itself was fine, good air conditioning, pleasant swimming pool with nice blue water. The area is a little rough around the edges, but there is good freeway access. The continental breakfast was OK.

name: Travelodge San Antonio Lackland
title: “Great Value... nice and close for USAF Grads”
text: From the reviews, my expectations were low going into this... However, considering the nightly rates, its close proximity to the Lackland AFB gates, and the fact our days were so packed we only came there to sleep made it turn out to be a pleasant and convenient 4 days while there for the USAF grad. We were two families with kids and had a couple rooms. Kids enjoyed the pool/hot tub (while parents cocktailed) and the simple morning breakfast bar (with a wonderful lady on duty). Our USAF grad enjoyed the very close proximity for her and her airman pals to link up and head downtown with us. As a frequent business traveler used to regularly staying at finer, more expensive locations, this place is certainly not in that class. But again, for the value, traveling with kids, and its location for our purpose, it was just fine.

name: Super 8 San Antonio/Downtown I-10 East
title: “Surprisingly wonderful stay”
text:
Ended up at this hotel after all other hotels in the area were booked. A little hesitant to stay because of outside appearances. I walked in and the lobby smelled really strong of chemicals and I about walked out the door I came in. BUT I was desperate, so after reading the no refund signs and hearing about how the room card is required to stay plugged into some card holder on the wall to operate A/C and lights, I asked if the rooms were decent. The hotel employee said with extreme enthusiasm, "oh yes! I can show you if you'd like". Honestly, it was the only hotel in a large radius that wasn't booked thanks to Spring Break so I was really unlikely to turn the last room down with a truck full of kids, my husband, and my dog, so I took the room without seeing it. The hotel was posted with no pet signs, but for an extra $10/night the hotel clerk said our small dog would be allowed. 
Hold my breath....we get to the room, and WOW! The rooms look like they were just remodeled. The carpet was in excellent condition, the furniture was in good shape, the walls freshly painted, the restroom was super clean with updated showers and shower heads, the TV came with cable and showtime, and the A/C ran super cold. No strong chemical smells as I had feared. My only complaint was the blanket that hotels put in between the sheets and the usually already itchy comforter was the old school knotty itchy kind, but the sheets were clean, the pillows were comfortable, and the bed was soft. Was surprised to see the room included a fridge and a microwave, although we didn't need it. 
Breakfast was included between the hours of 7-10 (great hours I must add) and included name brand cereals, muffins, honey buns, toast. texas shaped waffles, juice, coffee, and milk. Staff continously came in to check on breakfast area and ask if anyone needed anything.
