Swimming pool was a bit small but spotless clean and not overly treated with chemicals which is something I think most hotels are guilty of. 
Hotel staff was really friendly, even after I forgot about the new early daylight savings time change and ended up staying over an extra hour without being charge additional fees. 
Would gladly stay again. Great deal for the price.

name: Mid Towne Inn and Suites
title: “Never stay here”
text: I thought since this was a national hotel that had a good description it would have been an OK experience. We got to the hotel late and our room opened to the parking lot which was bad enough. The carpet was old, dirty and had what looked like a huge circular burn hole in it as well as a dead roach on the floor by the nightstand. The bedspread had tears in it and the linens were questional as to their cleanliness. Thank goodness the hotel had good wireless because as I was awakened by the trains that blared their horns throughout the night, I was able to get a good rate at a real reputable hotel. The final insult was when I took a shower in the morning there was no hot water. Ironically, they had upgraded the countertops in the bathroom to granite. It was not worth the money I paid. The staff was helpful but they did not have much to work with.

name: Holiday Inn Lackland
title: “Never Again”
text:
Stay was the worst ever. We were staying there for 6 weeks for work. As soon as we arrived it was bad, they did not have the rooms that we had booked. 
After 2 weeks of staying there, the bartender refused to serve one of the guys on the crew because she said he did not tip enough. I don't think she has the right to determine who she should serve on that basis. 2 weeks after that I had an iPod and a digital camera stolen from my room. 
The only decent staff that was there was the 2 cooks and the night manager. The rest of the staff was horrible, rude and would tell you what you wanted to hear so you would leave. 
2 out of 3 of us had to wait 2 weeks just for a remote for the TV.
I would not recommend this hotel to anyone even though it is so close to Lackland. It is a horrible hotel with thieves as housekeepers.

name: Ramada Limited Downtown
title: “Not terrible but certainly below par”
text:
They must have improved somewhat since others stayed there, because when I arrived on Dec 31, 2008, it was tolerable for the two nights I planned to stay, after I became acclimated to the place.
First off, when I checked in I asked if I could change my two-bed reservation to a one bed room. Sure, no problem. I went to the one-bed room - ugh! It was in a spooky corner on the ground floor under a staircase right next to the janitorial room - dirty laundry was everywhere in the walkway. The room looked neat, but it smelled of strong chemicals, cleaning products maybe. I immediately called the registration desk and asked for the two-bed room I had originally reserved. Sure, no problem.
The two-bed room was also on the ground floor but in the middle, not buried in a corner or under a stairwell. I was able to park right in front of it. I had trouble opening the door, when I did (the handle turns up instead of down as in other hotels/motels) I noticed the door handle seemed loose, something that worried me the first night, until I thought to put a chair in front of it. Other than that, while the room was "well used", it wasn't terrible. It seemed as clean as one would expect, considering, and the bathroom was in good working order - a real plus. The towels were scratchy and thin. Believe me, I was really appreciating Holiday Inn Express where I normally stay. There was still the trash problem stacked under the stairs, as mentioned by a previous poster. The bed was comfortable, though. There was a small table in the room with two chairs which could be used as a desk setting or as a dinette. No problems with the TV or remote.
As someone else said, the guests tend to hang around outside, on the balconies above, or along the walkways in front of the lower rooms. At first I thought they were setting up their places for the New Year's Eve fireworks, but they did the same thing the following night - no fireworks.
Like others have said, the location was convenient to the River Walk and the Alamo, etc., but it was a rundown neighborhood. It was convenient from the Interstate highways, and easy to find, located facing the Interstate bridge on the service road, and since my room was facing the front, the view of the bridge wasn't appealing. I took my car when I went out, even if I was going a few blocks. It was downright spooky around there, especially at night. If I had known ahead of time a Holiday Inn Express was just down the street, I would have made my reservations there. Parking was free. I didn't try the breakfast. Even though they claimed to have wireless internet, I had to tap into someone's account.
On the trip, I stayed in three cities, three different hotel/motel chains, by far this was the worst of the lot. No comparison to the lovely Holiday Inn Express I moved to in Arlington. Ramada Inn used to be a nice respectable chain but this one was shocking! I won't be back.

name: Ramada Limited Downtown
title: “Shocking!!”
text: We had been driving aroung looking for a hotel, it was a last minute decision to stay the night in San Antonio. Everywehere else we looked was booked and althought the sign was old and faded it said the Ramada limited. I have always heard good things about them so I figure it would be ok. My mistake!, we book the room and left, only to come back after a tour around the town and find the room that was given to us already occupied. We tried and tried the key, and were unable to open it and finally the door open and a man came out, I had my 4year old son with me and he scared us, he said we had the wrong room and I immediatelly apoligize, shaken, and embarresed I went to the front desk. The desk clerk was nice but did not seem surprise, he provided us with a different room and apologize lightly by saying it was a mistake the owner had made, since he was the one that book us in. Their reputation is not at all a good one.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Antonio South
title: “Not Friendly & Disorganized”
text: This was a business trip. The frontdesk was disorganized and unfriendly. First, they could not find our (I was traveling with a colleague) reservation, and then when we tried to put it on different corporate accounts, they just flat out said "that cannot be done" because it was prepaid. I didn't believe that, but it was not worth the hassle to get into it. I wrote an email to the owner of the hotel hoping I would get a response. I did not. The room itself was okay, a little mildewy. It was also across the street from an abandoned house, which was a little creepy. There are lots of other hotels in the area (right across the street, next door) that are similar in price range. I would suggest you choose on of those.

name: Homestead Studio Suites - San Antonio - Airport
title: “Original Roach Motel”
text: My husband and I stayed here on July 21 thru July 27 due to no other hotels having rooms. We have stayed at HomeSteads before in other cities and they were great but this property is in bad shape. Upon entering our room (#307) we lost count of the roaches climbing in the drawers and on the wall. Reported this to front desk who said maint. would be buy to spray----NEVER HAPPENED so we bought our own can of roach killer. Housekeeping leaves alot to be desired also..carpet was never swept and bathroom was nasty. The only positive thing was the staff who were curtious and helpful with info. The manager did state that the property would be renovated soon so my advice is stay away until it is completed although after reading some of the other reviews maybe a couple rooms are liveable.

name: Rodeway Inn Downtown
title: “Comodo”
text: Considerando el costo, creo que es justo. Las habitaciones no son espectaculares, pero estan amuebladas con lo básico, tienen un horno de microondas y un pequeño refregerador por si quieres almacenar o calentar alimentos. Una buena estadía en general. Dado que mi objetivo principal era economizar para contar con mas recursos para las compras lo considero una buena opción.

name: Quality Inn Downtown South
title: “Coming' back!!”
text: Great hotel close to downtown...friendly staff, comfortable and clean rooms with an awesome breakfast. Pool was very nice and clean too!! Will be back in the summer with more family!!

name: Microtel Inn & Suites by Wyndham San Antonio North East
title: “Great Economy hotel”
text: This is no five star hotel however it is a great economy hotel. All of the staff that I talked to were very nice and helpful. My room was kind of small but very clean. The size of the room doesnt matter because its loaded with extras. Nice sized flat screen tv A resting area beside the window that could be used as a sleeping area and a desk. Not to mention its less than a mile from Fort Sam and right beside the highway so you can make it anywhere in town quickly. I do not understand where all these bad reviews are coming from I had a great experience.

name: Homestead Studio Suites - San Antonio - Airport
title: “Good Value, but not really a hotel.”
text: This is more for Long Term stays. It didnt really have the hotel anemities that im used to, but for the price it was great. Its not really practical unless you have a rental car because it is so far from everything. Clean, was very happy except the rock hard bed. probrably pay a little more to find a place closer to the tourst places. Stores and restuants too far away.

name: Comfort Suites San Antonio at Rittiman
title: “Really bad”
text: This hotel looked nice from the outside but all that changed inside the room. The room had a strange smell that got worse in the bathroom, seemed like it was cleaned in a rush. The bed was not done and had stains all over it . The whole room just felt very dirty. The front desk did offer to move us to another room but we just left and found something else. Maybe we just had bad luck with that room but we will not be returning!

name: Super 8 - Sea World / Medical Center
title: “Excelente por el precio”
text: Esta a una milla del Centro comercial Ingram, a unos metros hay un ihop, y una gasolinera. Muy bena ubicacion. Habitacion amplia, personal amable, desayuno diario d muffins, wafle, cereal y cafe. Limpio y confortable dentro de lo q cabe. Con refri y microondas en la habitacion. Le pedi dos veces al joven d recepcion q abriera la caja fuerte xq estaba cerrada, y jamas lo hizo. Estuve 6 noches y cambiaron las sabanas y toallas hasta q se los pedi. Fuera d eso, todo bien. Volveria sin duda.

name: Holiday Inn San Antonio Downtown
title: “Hôtel Holiday Inn à San Antonio, Texas”
text:
Même si les environs immédiats n'ont rien d'exceptionnels, l'hôtel est suffisamment proche du centre historique pour y aller à pied (maxi : 1/4 d'heure).
Attention, pour le petit-déjeuner, il ne s'agit pas d'un buffet : il est servi à la carte au restaurant de l'hôtel ou dans la chambre .
Notre chambre était particulièrement spatieuse avec un coin salon et un lit King Size : mais rien ne garantit que toutes les chambres soient de cette taille.

name: Hotel Mimosa Riverwalk
title: “Great location to visit the city”
text:
We figured that the Holiday Inn name would give us a pretty good place in a city we knew nothing about.
The location of the hotel was perfect. We were able to walk to everywhere that we wanted to see - Riverwalk, Tower, El Mercado, La Villita etc. Even walking at night was fine.
The room was great, a suite with a kingsize bed, as requested. Our flight was delayed and so we did not arrive until after midnight, but all was well. The breakfast was fine and saved us time having to find somewhere to eat. The room was serviced well.
The public areas were clean and wel maintained and the desk staff were very helpful when we had any questions. As we had no problems they were not tested in any way - just how we like it.
Would definitely recommend

name: Hotel Mimosa Riverwalk
title: “Great Location, Very nice hotel”
text:
I was concerned about the scary reviews on this site before I booked the hotel. Evidently the management has received the picture. We stayed here for 3 nights at Thanksgiving. 
The location is great; close to Riverwalk, Alamo, etc. but not in the middle of all the chaos on a busy weekend.
The desk staff and night parking attendant had some personality and were better than average. The room was large, nice, clean, well decorated with a good bed. May have been recently redone. Breakfast had cooked eggs and bacon and versions of each day in addition to the usual wonderful cinnamon rolls.
I was concerned about reported parking. $6 a night is a deal in the city and when I looked at the other lots around, they were unlighted and were not somewhere I would leave my car.
Pool area was very pleasant and a nice place to have breakfast. Real teak furniture and landscaping made it a quiet oasis.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites San Antonio North/Stone Oak
title: “Great Place with Excellent Help”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 4 nites in April and it was Great! Michelle at the front desk was very, very helpful as well as the other employees. The breakfast was good and the room was nice and spacious. The property was very clean and well kept. If ever in this area again, this hotel would be my 1st choice. Thanks for making my stay Great!

name: Americas Best Value Inn - San Antonio / Lackland AFB
title: “Not a bad place to stay for the price”
text:
My wife and I stayed here while visiting our son who graduated BMT at Lackland AFB this past week of 6/17 thru 6/22. We found the motel room clean and not bad at all whatsoever. The motel staff was very extremely helpful and quite accommodating to our needs and questions. Our room was cleaned every day and the service was more then adequate. I read the review online of one customer seeing MICE running around the room and I personally find this absurd and quite unbelievable. The building is cinder block construction and I have yet to see any rodents being able to chew holes through CEMENT! There was not even any cockroaches or bugs in our room and I honestly cannot believe anyone would stoop so low and say such negative things. People want a motel room for pennies on the dollar and yet they expect the Sheraton Hilton for a room. 
For the money we paid and the location being close to the AFB, we could not ask for a better deal. If our two daughters ever join the Air Force and they graduate from Lackland we would stay there again in a heartbeat. I highly recommend to ANY parents, who are planning a visit to Lackland to see their Airman graduate BMT to stay at Best Value Inn. For the price and just a inexpensive place to stay, you will not be disappointed because we sure weren't. If you want high class room with all the bells and whistles then spend the big bucks and stay at the Hilton. If you are just plain ol' common folks like us, then this is the place to stay.

name: Candlewood Suites - San Antonio NW Medical Center
title: “I wouldn't recommend this hotel to my worst emeny!”
text: I recently stay at this hotel a couple of weeks ago. And all the other hotels i could of choosed in san antonio; I had to pick this crapy hotel. First, the staff at the front desk was rude when it came to my reservation; they had poor customer service skills. Then the manager or operations manager was very rude too. If she's keeps having an attitude like that she will be unemployed real soon like the rest of the country. Then second the beds were very unconfortable, I slept in better beds at Motel 6! Finally my Air Conditioning unit was not working good, I tried to ask the Front Desk staff if they could have mantenance to come up to my room to fix it, but they acted like they were dumbfounded like they didn't know what was going on. "So I wouldn't recommend this hotel to my worst emeny!" there are better hotels in san antonio besides this one, when you see it along the 10 fwy, just pass it by; I rather stay at Motel 6 than that piece of crap hotel.

name: Candlewood Suites - San Antonio NW Medical Center
title: “Enjoyed our stay”
text: I will start with the complaints. It was hard to find. but that makes it nice because it isn't right on the interstate and that makes it pretty quiet but a bigger sign would have been nice. the sign was hidden behind a big tree. The staff and guests did smoke right outside the main entrance. I would suggest a smoking area away from any entrances. The room was really clean but it took a lot to get an extra blanket. That said, the kitchen had everything you needed to cook or to just warm something up. It had restaurants near by. It had easy access to the interstate which made getting around San Antonio nice. the grounds were nice. The Candlewood pantry is really nice when you forget something like snacks/drinks or just don't want to leave.

name: Holiday Inn San Antonio International Airport
title: “Some Great Things & Some Negative Things...”
text:
This hotel is very clean with nice rooms yet one very strange anomaly. The curtains do not close all of the way (by design). So if getting dressed beware as patrons in the adjacent office buildings have a clear sight line.. The price was very good and the surroundings safe.
However, this is a Holiday Inn wanting to be a 5-Star Marriott. You will pay for everything including a morning coffee in the lobby - which is $3.00 at Starbucks in the lobby. And you can get breakfast for about the same amount as a good dinner somewhere else. If you go into the restaurant / lounge expect to pay around $15 for a simple meal and $5.00 + for a draft beer. And the restaurant staff was not particularly friendly and English as their second language. Needs more friendly service than it has - or had when I was there

name: Sleep Inn Medical Center Northwest
title: “Incredibly helpful”
text: I picked this hotel because it had great reviews. Now I see why. We were staying there with a group of teens that we had taken to Six Flags, on our way to the hotel our bus broke down, we called the hotel and they shuttled us over in two trips, at no additional cost. Mind you this was after midnight! The next day our bus wasn't ready by check out and they allowed us all to keep our rooms til it was fixed. The staff was friendly, helpful and understanding. I would highly recommend this hotel. P.S. awesome breakfast!

name: San Antonio Marriott Northwest
title: “Outdated, old, dirty.”
text:
I am surprised that they can call this hotel a Marriott. Sheets and pillows are the only item that has been updated in the past few years. The maroon chair is badly faded and brown from all the dirt on the chair. Room and hallway smells dirty. No free breakfast for Rewards members on weekends. Front dest staff not capable. Lost my room key. Went to front desk to get another and gave them my information. It didn't match what was on the computer. 
I stay about 100+ nights per year in Marriott/Hilton chains. This particular hotel is worse than a Holiday Inn Express.

name: Holiday Inn San Antonio Downtown
title: “Excellent Staff”
text: I have been staying at the hotel 1 to 3 nights a week for 8 months. While the facility is an older building, it is clean, kept up and comfortable. Unless you are looking for the Taj Mahal, you will be pleased with the rooms, amenities and the value you get when you stay here. All that being said, however, what really puts this hotel over the top for me is the hotel's staff. They are extremely friendly and pleasant. One staff member, Tammie Wall, is outstanding to the point that she is the best ambassador the hotel could possibly have. Whatever they are paying her isn't enough. She remembers guest names and greets them by name whenever she sees them. She dedictates herself to guests, making it her personal mission to ensure that all is as it should be. The rest of the staff are wonderful too but Ms Wall stands above everyone. Overall, I continue to utilize this hotel for my buisness trips to San Antonio becasue Ms Wall and the rest of the staff sincerely care about the hotel's guests and the rooms are comfortable. Consider me a very satisfied guest. Mark Franken

name: San Antonio Marriott Northwest
title: “Very unsatisfied, will NOT be back!”
text: My family booked this hotel through another website as we always do and we normally are thrilled with our stay. However, every time I turned around something was wrong. When we got to the room my 7 year old son immediately ordered a $15.00 movie off of the TV. We tried to turn it off but it was too late. Then I tried to get online to check on some activites and found out that they didnt have free WIFI. I was very upset there was no free breakfast. Housekeeping came extremely late and never cleaned the counters. On the last day of our stay housekeeping never came. I had to put our trash outside of the room. The cheaper hotels we normally stay in offer much, much more and I am always pleasantly surprised. This one left me feeling jipped on a vacation. :(

name: Hilton San Antonio Hill Country Hotel & Spa
title: “Great Staff, Great Service and Great Experience”
text:
We happen to be at the property when the below reviews were at the pool. We witnessed the families and their behavior. The staff at the hotel should be applauded for their actions. The children and parents were out of hand, climbing an eight foot wall and trying to jump into the pool. All the other families around the pool were extremely nervous that a child would get hurt. The childrens parents were not even watching, and appearred to be arguing. Security came and closed the pool ten minutes early and we all breathed a sigh of relief. Some of the above mentioned family were not even staying at the hotel. There was no racism, just concern for the safety of everyone.
We had a great experience, our son was not feeling well and the bellman went to the drugstore for us to pick up his medicine. The chef went out of his way to and cooked a special soup for our son. Our room was large and overlooked the pool. It is a great place for kids and family. We watched movies poolside while cooking smores over an open fire. It was paradise.

name: Super 8 San Antonio
title: “The hotel was very clean and had good service.”
text: We were there for our 34th anniversary, We want to thank Mr. Ken Patel for all that he had done to make our stay with them very pleasent and taking care of any problems we had. Than again Mr. Ken Patel and God Bless you and your staff.

name: Travelodge San Antonio Alamo
title: “OK, but not the Ritz...”
text: Made reservations online...showed up at 8pm...room wasn't ready, the prices were not as quoted online (Orbitz), and they had us booked for one day less. So, off to a bad start, but things turned around quickly. The staff was friendly and helpful. We were given a room overlooking the pool. My kids are 8 and 9, and with the hotel being almost "enclosed" it was comforting to let them run free just a bit in the enclosed area. Nothing too fance, I assure you, but worth the money. Only blocks from the River Walk entrance....you are not going to be ON the River Walk, but you are also not going to spend $250.00 per night. We had a wonderful time in San Antonio....by the way, get to know the trolley system, as it picks you up right at the hotel...it took as several days to figure this out, but once we did, we used it all day long!

name: Crowne Plaza Airport
title: “Crowne Plaza Feng Shui”
text:
From the moment of driving up to the property, we were greeted by a warm friendly bellman by the name of Stanley. Stanley was well scripted with all the services the hotel provided and also made dining suggestions at local venues. The front desk counter tops were immaculate with marble counter tops to leather desk check-in pads to the silver business card/pen holder. The service at check-in and check-out was great. The rooms were very clean and the beds the most comfortable that I have ever slept in. I will definitely recommend the hotel to my friends and family. 
Rebecca 
Mansfield, Texas

name: Holiday Inn Riverwalk
title: “Fab Location but should be CLOSED temporarily”
text:
This hotel should currently be CLOSED for its renovation work. It is greedy and unfair to try and operate a good hotel in an excellent location while such major alterations are undertaken.
We stayed 3 nights during a tour of Texas and New Orleans.
We arrived at 4pm and were allocated a room on the 16th floor. I really could not believe we were expected to stay in a room which felt like it was on a building site. There was deafening drilling and workmen shouting. We were tired and wanted a rest and I was totally determined to change room and went to reception. Mercifully I got in first before the floods of complaints about rooms started – FURIOUS people objecting to the noise (it went on until 7pm that evening, started again at 8.30am Saturday and also at 9am Sunday) and was reallocated a room on the 6th floor which was fine and although the drilling was going on it was only very faint.
Most annoyingly ALL the balconies were sealed off ‘for health and safety’. This was infuriating as I like fresh air and had looked forward to having a private balcony overlooking the Riverwalk and sitting out there in an evening and also some space to dry a bit of washing. Sadly this was not to be and we were restricted to VERY noisy air conditioning which we had to switch off at night.
Also it was infuriating that the disabled access to the pool was also sealed off and getting there meant having to clamber up some rather steep stone stairs. This really isn’t acceptable – if so much needs to be sealed off the hotel should be SHUT while it is done. Taking people’s money for such sub-standard conditions is altogether WRONG.
The direct access to the Riverwalk (highlighted as a plus by this hotel) was also sealed off apart from a dark and rather scary passage through the basement and a walk through builders and scaffolding out onto the Riverwalk.
This hotel did not even offer a complimentary breakfast to compensate for all these massive inconveniences.
We ate in the hotel on the Saturday night as the Riverwalk eateries were all full with long waiting lists (tip: book in advance for the weekend) and whilst we had a lovely meal it was rather expensive.
This hotel’s bedroom was comfortable (apart from as stated above re noise, air conditioning and no balcony access) and we had excellent towels, toiletries and there was a very good hairdryer.
The hotel is only saved by the fact it is in the world’s most tourist friendly city with the fabulous Alamo and Riverwalk, San Fernando Cathedral and general relaxed and warm ambience.
I just think it is OUTRAGEOUS not to advise people of these works and give them a chance to choose somewhere else with none of the inconvenience.
For that reason and because of their naked greed and disregard for guest comfort I would definitely NOT stay in this hotel if I went to San Antonio again. There are DOZENS of other hotels along the Riverwalk to choose from.
We ate 2 nights just around the corner on the Riverwalk at the Texas Land and Cattle Steakhouse, food was fantastic but just to be warned that ‘rare’ means just shot and might well move, ‘medium’ means very very rare and barely seen the grill and ‘well done’ means what we would know as medium but they ‘don’t recommend this’ !! It wasn’t cheap but it was good.
This hotel is VERY lucky that it is in such a great city, that we had fabulous weather and that we enjoyed being in San Antonio or else I would have felt REALLY angry about their remaining open under such circumstances.
Not amused.

Address: '502 West Cesar E. Chavez (formerly Durango) Blvd.'
name: DoubleTree by Hilton San Antonio Downtown
title: “Not Recommended”
text:
I really wanted and needed to like this hotel because it was the site of my business conference and I had been traveling for over 24 hours from overseas to get to San Antonio, so I was dead tired. 
Unfortunately, my assigned room had cleanliness and noise issues to the point where I checked out after just a few hours. Since the Doubletree was sold out for the conference, I wasn't able to switch to a different room. 
I walked across town about a mile (20 minutes) to the Marriott Riverwalk, where I had stayed before on business without a hitch. You can get the exact same government per diem rate of $106/day in a much better location, right on the Riverwalk by the mall, with cleaner, quieter rooms and more robust hotel facilities. 
For starters, at the Doubletree my room door wouldn't open and the door handle, a lever type, was extremely loose in its socket, so I assumed it was broken. I went back to the front desk and asked for a different room (Sorry, sold out), so the maintenance guy came up to show me the trick- jerk UP on the door handle, not down, since that part of the mechanism was worn out. 
As soon as I walked in, the room smelled strongly of mildew emanating from the air conditioner, which had numerous, dirty black pellets collecting in the vent. Behind the coffee machine, next to the TV, dried coffee drops were spattered on the wall up to eye level. The armchair's arm rests were dirty and worn, the footrest stained.
In the bathroom, the chrome drain plug hardware was inexplicably pulled out and left sitting in the center of the tub. The first towel I picked up off the stack was so stained, it appeared to possibly not have been laundered.
Even though none of this was promising, I decided to tough it out because I was so tired, had an early start the next morning, and the bed linens looked OK. At about midnight when my neighbor in the next room came in, he switched on his TV at the loudest possible volume. The TV of the neighboring room was on the opposite site of the wall from my headboard, so I was blasted awake out of a deep sleep and could hear every word and musical note from his TV show through the headboard and mattress, which vibrated with the noise.
I don't consider myself to be a light sleeper or overly fussy customer- I have lived and traveled in third world countries on several occasions and I also get that even in first world country hotels, "sometimes a wheel falls off," as they say. But until now I've always found Hiltons to be consistently high quality, so I did expect more.
On the positive side, the staff were all friendly, polite and attentive. The downstairs restaurant's breakfast and lunch buffets were tasty, filling and reasonably priced. The conference facilities, including conference rooms and a poolside mixer party, worked well for our group. The hotel also put out comprehensive spreads of drinks and snacks for our meetings that were very nice. 
That said, the quality of the room stay experience really should be the core competency of any hotel. Due to the cleanliness and noise issues with my room, unfortunately I can't recommend staying here.

name: Days Inn Alamo/Riverwalk
title: “Dirty”
text:
We arrived to the Days Inn Alamo Riverwalk and checked in quickly, only to find that our rooms were in another building across two busy roads! There was parking available there however but it made it difficult when you wanted breakfast or towels. 
The bathroom was quite dirty, there was a brown crust in the corners of the shower and there was clump of hair on our towels (see picture). The shower head was a massage type, but it was broken and could only spray hard pulsations of water. 
The room was not sufficiently cleaned. There was a baby bottle cap in plain sight on the floor and another person's underwear in a drawer!
The floor was wet due to water leaking in from the air conditioner.
On our second day, we had to go back to the office acoss the busy roads to get our room key re-activated! There was another couple having the same problem and we had to wait for a good 15 minutes to do this.
Really the only good thing I can say about this place is the location. It was about a 7 minute walk to the Alamo and a 10 minute walk to the Riverwalk.

name: Alamo Inn Motel
title: “Absolute WORST”
text: We (two single moms and four kids) booked two rooms before we left for a San Antonio zoo and family fun trip. The pictures looked nice and their were some decent reviews. We got their to find that it was in a questionable part of town and the rooms had bars on the windows. It was a filthy mess! NO WAY were were staying there with our kids. The "owner" refused to cancel the reservation stating that 3:00 was the deadline and it was 4:15. Had I been informed of that over the phone, I never would have reserved! I could not find information on a website that stated a cancellation time. Not only is the hotel an unsafe family dump, they customer service and management is rude. This place exploits anyone looking for a decent deal. In the end, I have a $164 charge for rooms we did not stay in for the safety of our children.

name: La Quinta Inn San Antonio I-35 N at Toepperwein
title: “Decent hotel”
text: Overall the stay was pretty good but the hotel is old and in need of some repair. The room was small and the beds were small but the room was clean. Basic continental breakfast was ok. I would recommend this hotel as a place to sleep but would not recommend the hotel if you are gonna spend some time in the room.

name: Hilton San Antonio Hill Country Hotel & Spa
title: “Hilton Hill Country - feels like home”
text:
Excellent recent stay at the San Antonio Hill Country Hotel. All staff encountered were extremely service-oriented. Nice touches included cold bottled water at the front desk, evening wine in the lobby, and cookies in the room for Diamond members. 
Had the breakfast buffet in the restaurant and a late-night bite to eat in the bar -- good service and food. Room was spacious and quiet. 
Only a couple miss-steps during the visit. Previous guest left a highly-personal couple of items in the night stand. Fortunately, I was traveling on business and not with children -- would have been difficult to explain. Addditionally, wake-up call was late one morning and non-existent the other morning. Fortunately, I had also set the alarm. 
There is a small business center just off the lobby (convenient for printing boarding passes) and a nice little gift shop. Sat outside by one of the firepits one evening and watched some of "Toy Story 3" projected on a large wall by the pool. 
Location is very close to Sea World and just a block away from Rudy's for bbq.

name: Days Inn Alamo/Riverwalk
title: “Liars, thieves, threatened me & 10 year old, filthy!”
text: Arrived pre-paid (by one month) Aug. 2nd and motel manager tried to get me to let her have a SIGNED and blank credit card slip "in case of damages" and when I said that was unusual, she said it was "standard" - like I was born yesterday. Her tone was demeaning, she alternated between lying and backpedaling. I refused to give her a blank signed credit slip and then she wanted $20 cash which I also refused. She then threatened to throw me & my 10 year old out on the street (you cannot stay in San Antonio anywhere without prior reservations) - the room was filthy, had live bugs and dead bugs everywhere and one of the beds was missing half the linens while the other had makeup smears on the sheets. This is the first time I have tried a Days Inn and I will NEVER stay in one again!!

name: Holiday Inn San Antonio International Airport
title: “Great Stay”
text:
This is a good hotel that is about to be completely renovated. The renovation is in process and I did not hear a sound from construction. 
The current rooms are clean and the new updates will make this place an excellent place to stay. The location is great with easy access to 281 that will take you downtown quickly.
The A/C works great here and my only complaint is that they dont have an eliptical machine in the workout room. But I am just being picky.

name: Hill Country Inn & Suites
title: “Very nice, family friendly”
text: Very nice, family friendly My kids loved the room and loved the pool play area. We will comeback.

name: Residence Inn San Antonio Downtown / Market Square
title: “Best family hotel”
text:
My husband and I with two kids (7 year old, 4 month old). We instantly felt welcomed. Everyone was friendly, and the Wed special (free) hamburger dinner by the manager and staff was a great surprise. We enjoyed our 4 day stay.
To top it off, we left our stroller and a few things, and they mailed it back!!! No hassles.
Will stay again and highly recommend to others.

name: MainStay Suites
title: “Wonderful room, wonderful service, Great value”
text: We were on a park, sleep and fly package. It was amazingly cheap for what we got. They even gave us a welcoming package of cookies and candy. Everything was top notch, except they are 8 miles from the airport. BUT, they pay your cab fare both ways.

name: Fairfield Inn San Antonio Downtown/Market Square
title: “SUPER!!!!!”
text: Clean, quiet, very friendly staff! I just can't say enough about the helpfulness of the front desk staff. One young lady (long, black hair, dark-rimmed glasses) in particular was so very nice. Wish I had gotten her name. Would recommend her for a raise!!!!! Was close to Market Square (which I loved). Downtown/Rivercenter/Riverwalk was only a short trolley ride away! Enjoyed our stay in San Antonio very much.

name: Hill Country Inn & Suites
title: “We'll be back”
text: Family of four included children 14 and 8 yr olds. The rooms were very nice. Staff were great. The pool, I believe is a salt water pool, no chrlorine burn at all. We enjoyed every minute of our stay. Yes the highway by the hotel has some construction, but not a problem at all. The suite we stayed in had a full kitchen. The dw didn't work so well, we ended up washing dishes by hand but not a big deal considering the money we saved by preparing most of our meals. The staff is more than willing to provide maps to the local stores so you can fill your pantry. We have stayed on the river before but this place is so much better. We are going back for sure.

name: La Quinta Inn San Antonio Vance Jackson
title: “Great Staff, Great Stay”
text: Stayed here with my two boys ages 5&9 yoa for 4 th of July weekend. Signed on as a Returns member online when making my reservation. Was able to check in 2 hours earlier that the 3pm check in posted and able to check out later at 1:30 instead of 12pm. Front desk staff was extra friendly and answered all my questions without making me feel like I was a bother. Although this is an older hotel the room was large enought for me & the boys. It was clean and very well maintained. The grounds were clean and the pool was clean. The pool area had plenty of loungers and tables with umbrellas. They even offer pool towels. Whenever we ran into a staff member we were greeted. Despite being right off the highway it was fairly quiet. The only time it got noisy was when a rather large family was packing up their cars. The continental breakfast consisted of the usual fare but also included a waffle area where you could make your own waffles. My boys loved this. At check out I was pleasantly suprised when told that they were going to charge me Sunday nights price for Saturday also. This was an exta $10 off than the price quoted online. I will definately stay here again.

name: Hill Country Inn & Suites
title: “More than average”
text:
all ranch style suite rooms. my room was not very clean, saw mold in bedroom, bathroom. Breakfast not good.
But, the pool was nice. Many families stayed there. Staff was very friendly.

name: Holiday Inn Express San Antonio North
title: “Top Lage - historisches Gebäude”
text:
Auf meiner Reise durch Texas hatte ich das Holiday Inn Express gewählt. Die Lage ist wirklich nicht zu schlagen, man kommt fast überall zu Fuß hin. Es liegt aber ruhig in einer Seitenstraße.
Das Gebäude war ganz früher ein Gefängnis, was man auch im Zimmer merkt, denn man schaut durch Gitter, aber das hat mich nicht gestört. Das Zimmer war nicht sehr groß, aber ausreichend für eine Person. Das Frühstück hat mir sehr gut geschmeckt.

name: Crowne Plaza San Antonio Riverwalk
title: “I Highly Recommend This Hotel!”
text: We stayed in this hotel for 4 nights. Everyone was extremely friendly and helpful. I especially liked our waiter every morning at breakfast! He was very attentive and by the second day had our table waiting for us as well as our coffee and other drinks. His name is Rene Ochoa. As soon as I'd finish my last drop of coffee, he'd come by and very politely ask if he could pour me another cup. Their waffles were the best I've had and I think I gained 5 pounds just from the waffles and delicious coffee! They had a great variety of foods for our children to choose from as well. We really enjoyed our stay and will stay there next time we are in San Antonio. Thank you Rene Ochoa for making it a very memorable vacation.

name: Howard Johnson San Antonio/Near Balcones Heights
title: “Worst hotel I've been”
text: When we arrived they gave us a room that smell terrible, the bed was full of hair and the cover had blod on it. The towels were all dirty, but we were very tired to move to another one after 15 hours driving. Next day we asked for our money back and they offered us a new room and the manager offer to check everything by her self. The room was OK, but next day when we got back, we found that our room wasn't done. Again we got very late and decided to stay on it. The breakfast was terrible also. I will never go back again.

name: Wyndham Riverside Suites Hotel San Antonio
title: “Right on Riverwalk. Nice Renovated Rooms.”
text:
Riverside Suites, San Antonio...First trip to SA and 1st stay here. Let me 1st start by saying this is a Fairfield Inn establishment and a time share property. I am a timeshare owner. After wanting to go to SA, this popped up and I jumped on the opportunity without knowing much but that it was on the Riverwalk (very important to me). This is the only hotel I could stay at on the Riverwalk. I like to look up reviews first but could not find much out on the property so I am always a little worried. Then again, most reviews vary and you just have to take a chance. At the time we were told renovations were still going on too which didn't ease my mind.
First impression from the street was nothing great. It is on a street that's not busy but has a lot of deliveries at all hours. There was this nasty smell outside the door that came from the grates in the sidewalk (reminded me of NewOrl during Mardi Gras!!!) Polly Esters is right next door (Niteclub). The lobby should not even be considered that. It's not your typical lobby, you can not fit more than 4 people with luggage there.
Check in was quick & easy. Employees very friendly. So far I was a little dissappointed and worried about the room. We stayed in a 2BR (Actually two 1 BR apts.). Halls are very narrow (this hotel was renovated from something back in the days). The room was BEAUTIFUL. Italian style decor, One of our rooms looked over the riverwalk. Clean rooms, spa tubs, beautiful furniture, THE MOST comfortable pillows....two concerns were the cold, hard concrete floor (since I have a 1 1/2 yr. old). they were polished and designed to go with the style and the sharp corners on the coffee tables.There could be a more closet space since the only storage you have is a little in the armoires in BR and LR.
It took 2 calls to get a crib.
Rooms had: the works, washer/dryer, stove, fridge, microwave......
The hotel has a small deck on the 3rd floor with patio furniture.
The Location was great. Outside it was right near the elevator to get down to the riverwalk (which helped with the stroller) It was located right in the heart of the "Action" on the riverwalk and of course within walking distance to Alamo and other sites. They did warn us of noise because of its location. You could not hear music or anything from the bars, but after they let out, you could hear the noise on the streets on the weekend. Also, one morning at 3am, a sound of jackhammering or something woke us! You'll have to put up with a few nights of interrupted sleep.There are quieter hotels (areas) on the riverwalk.
One thing I didnt care for was getting two phone calls to "review" the hotel. What hotel calls you and asks for a review? I eventually gave in since I had free time that day and figured it was a timeshare pitch. The kid basically lied about it being a 10 question 30 minute "review" but I got my $40 free gifts for listening for an hour and a half or so. What I dont understand is why they waste their time when I already own a timeshare and that's why I'm staying here! RIDICULOUS! Oh, and they could care less on any comments I might have had about Riverside Suites. It seemed like Fairfield is very popular there (probally their only timeshare company) and they try to push it on the streets, and in a mall kiosk.
Overall, we had a good time, a week was too long to stay there, were pleased with our room etc...(by the way, they are making a lobby on the 2nd floor or something. It would have to blow away what they already have!) Best meal was at the restaurant right below the hotel. 
Hope this is somewhat helpful–

name: The Menger Hotel
title: “brunch at the Menger Hotel”
text:
From the moment my wife and I entered the dinning room we were very much impressed by not only the food display, but with the live back ground music of a solo guitarist. As we sat enjoying our breakfast and drinking our coffee, I finally decided to go and introduce myself and complement the "maestro" on his music. He in turn, not only introduced himself to me as Fernando Santafe, but he also dedicated and played a popular melody to my wife, Maria Alma, at table side. Don Fernando and Leonora, our waitress, certainly provided us with a very pleasant and memorable Sunday morning experience at the Menger Hotel. These two individuals displayed the best attributes that the Manger Hotel can take to the bank. Thank you,
guys, Luis Arturo, author "Moyeboy-51" and Maria Alma Jimenez from San Antonio.

name: Holiday Inn Riverwalk
title: “Fantastic Christmas From the Staff!”
text: When we checked in the staff was very welcoming and accommodating. We had beautiful rooms overlooking the river, and everything is so conveniently located. The manager, Kathy is a delight! We decided to let her know how much we were enjoying ourselves because so often people only contact the manager if they have a complaint. It's important to also let them know when things are done well, and in this case, outstanding! When we decided to spend our Christmas in San Antonio we thought it would be fun, but the hotel and staff definitely exceeded our expectations! Thank you!

name: BEST WESTERN Ingram Park Inn
title: “Great Place - Great Price - Great Location”
text:
We (3 adults & 3 kids) stayed in the family suite (1 king & 2 queens) and it was exactly what we needed and wanted and we were happy with our accommodations.
Room Layout: as you walk in the door you are met with a king size bed, then a half wall separating the bed and tv from the kitchen area. The kitchen area had a table w/ 4 chairs, cupboards, microwave, & college fridge. the air conditioner was also in the kitchen area. The bathroom vanity was outside of the bathroom, allowing us to prep and wash while the bathroom was in use. The bathroom had a toilet and shower/tub and a door that led to the 2 queen bedroom. You could also access the 2 queen bedroom from a door by the king size bed.
Before I booked the room through Expedia, I called the hotel directly to see if all the rooms faced the pool, I was told they do, they do NOT. The majority of the family suites are in a separate building behind the main building that encloses the pool area. The front desk manager was nice enough to see if they had another family suite available for us in the main 'U' shaped building. They did for $15 more per night we upgraded, we couldn't see the pool from our room because of all the beautiful trees in the courtyard, but at least the children didn't have to cross the parking lot to go swimming.
Our room was on the second floor right next to the stairs, but we did not hear any noise outside our door nor did we hear any noise through the walls. We parked behind the building and could see our car from the Kitchen area window.
Pool: medium size, and cold and in the afternoon it is mostly shaded. There are only a couple of tables with chairs and only a few loungers. There is no hot tub. The pool has a child area attached to it that is only 2 feet deep, but it is easy for a younger child to access the main pool from that child area, which I witnessed while I was at the pool. A mother (too preoccupied with her cell phone) jumped in fully clothed (cell phone in hand) to rescue her child who crossed over to the main pool.
You need to get pool towels from the front desk and they are small.
Breakfast: sorry we did not try breakfast.
Workout room: a small room off the pool with a treadmill and bike.
Location: GREAT! easily accessed from the highway and close to many restaurants, gas and a walmart nearby. It was only 15 minutes from the Alamo and Riverwalk, and only 5 minutes from all the major highways to other locations. The area was in a busy section of the city, not out in la la land. And as far as the signs I saw another review commenting on that said "Don't leave valuables in your car, Establishment not responsible" This should just be common sense where ever you go, the hotel is just reminding you to use your head when leaving your car.
We had maid service once during our stay and kept the Do Not Disturb on the door the other days. The maid did a great job, nothing was missing as a previous review stated. We kept our valuables with us and put the laptops out of sight as we would do at any hotel.
The room is worn and there is discoloration along the bathroom floorboard, but we didn't pay for The Ritz and we usually don't when we travel. If you want perfection then pay for it, but for $115 a night we were happy and we would stay here again. 
CONS: the only thing I didn't like was the bathroom, it smelled musty like clothes left in the washer over night, there is no window to air out the bathroom, there was a ceiling fan but it really needs a window and fresh air. Oh yeah, and the air conditioner broke during the night, but they had it fixed by the time we got back in the evening.
OVERALL: it was clean when I checked in, the beds were comfortable, it fit all of us comfortably, and we felt safe leaving our car in the parking lot and felt safe in our hotel room. The beds were really soft, every time my husband rolled over I felt like Peppermint Patty when Snoopy jumped on her bed (Race for your Life Charlie Brown).

name: Crowne Plaza San Antonio Riverwalk
title: “would not stay here again”
text: this hotel is not on the river walk, you have to walk a while to get to it. the parking was not near the hotel and was pricey. there were bums always sitting right in front of the hotel as you walked in. the room was old, outdated and tiny. the doors automatically slammed when people left there rooms so all day and night we heard doors slamming. the walls are very thin, the people next to us were fighting at 4am and we could hear every word. the elevators were always full so we had to wait to catch the next one which would take eight mins. all in all the staff were nice to us and the room was clean but the hotel itself is not that great and we will not stay here ever again.

name: Pear Tree Inn San Antonio Airport
title: “basic but clean and excellent service”
text: location is right next to loud highways but did not affect sleeping. good shuttle service to and from airport. basic drinks and hotdogs for manager's reception. what can you expect for the price? easy access to downtown ( ten minutes). you will need a car.

name: Riverwalk Plaza Hotel & Suites
title: “We put you on the cat walk...”
text: This was probably the worst hotel experience I've had with in the last year. The "cat walk" means you are outside close to the pool and can hear EVERYTHING that is going on outside. The parking garage was a royal pain... make sure you ask for directions on how to get in and out. The front desk staff was less than helpful and our room was dirty. The hotel room was $170 per night. I had high expectations and was let down. I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS HOTEL!

name: DoubleTree Hotel San Antonio Airport
title: “Nice hotel, average location, easy road access.”
text: We were impressed with the service at this Doubletree, in spite of some problems with the elevators. Our room was large, well air-conditioned, and made you feel as though you were in some hacienda. We'd recommend this for anyone needing to drive around while in San Antonio - but not if you want to get the flavor of downtown sights.

name: Hill Country Inn & Suites
title: “Definitely will be back again”
text:
This is the second time we are guests in this hotel, which we love. The staff is very giving, specially Rose (during breakfasts and ready for every need); Denisse at the front desk, super kind and always smiling and Rolando, a kind gentlemen who speaks perfect english and spanish to attend the guests in late night hours ... not to mention Mandie, the manager at the front desk, a beautiful woman with a beautiful mood.
The rooms are acceptable, not expensive, charming and cozy. I was surprised that this time we had the room vaccumed every day with clean towels, which didn`t happen last year. This talks great about the hotel.
Very close to the North Star Mall and other restaurants or shopping areas. I loved listening to the birds in the trees early in the morning and we had a great time over there.
Thanks to all!

name: BEST WESTERN Alamo Suites
title: “Excelente ubicación y seguro”
text: El hotel esta muy bien ubicado, practicamente junto a la I-35 (cero ruido) y a 5 min del downtown. Es segguro pues esta bardeado las puestas de acceso requieren llave de huesped. Sólo tiene opción a desayuno muy, muy básica pero suficiente, eso si te puede tocar desayunar parado si hay mucha gente ;)

name: Hilton Garden Inn San Antonio Airport
title: “Clean, Comfortable and Exceptional Staff!”
text:
We just spent two nights at this property and had a wonderful experience. Neah at front desk is AWESOME! She is professional, helpful & friendly -- we really enjoyed talking with her. Check-in was quick & easy.
Our room was super clean & bed was very comfortable -- the jacuzzi tub was a nice surprise and such a treat. Great flat screen tv -- plus the air conditioner worked great on the hot San Antonio days (Our only room issue was with the lock -- each time we came back to our room we had to have the key reset.)
Jimmy and his staff in the breakfast area are so much fun -- we enjoyed waking up each day to their sunny smiles & exceptional service plus breakfast was super fast and really good. 
Parking was free and we had no trouble finding a parking spot. (The pool is indoor and on the small side -- but very clean) Exercise room was nice & clean. Property outside was well maintained & welcoming.
Overall, we really enjoyed our stay and will return on our next trip to San Antonio!

name: Comfort Suites North IH 35
title: “Totally enjoyed my stay”
text: Very comfortable. The hotel staff was very friendly and professional. They had plenty of recommendations for nearby restaurants and shopping. The indoor pool was great. I definitely enjoyed the free hot breakfast buffet. Will come again!

name: Holiday Inn Riverwalk
title: “One major problem with this Hotel”
text:
Let me get this off my chest before I review the hotel - After a long day of travel and airport delays with a 2 year old, and after a few glasses of wine, it would have taken a freight train to wake me from my slumber. Unfortunately, that is exactly what happened - and I was on the top 22nd floor. Our suite (2205) faced the back of the hotel (the opposite of the pool), and at 1:30am, 4am, 5:15 and 6:30am a train blew it's whistle at every intersection, so it went on for at least five minutes each time. Now, I'm not one to complain, I understand the street level noise, the groups drinking and yelling, cars honking. But this was so loud and so long, it will prevent me from staying here again. It was that bad. Every night. It was so bad I called the desk on the 2nd night at 5am to ask for another suite, but none were available. The guy said they obviously have no control over the train, and that sometimes it is 3 or 4 nights in a row, sometimes just one night. We got 4 nights. I am not blaming the hotel, nothing they can do, but I cannot stay here again unless I am on the opposite side of the hotel - our friends had a room facing the pool and had no noise problems. We walked around like zombies the whole vacation from being up all night.
The Hotel: The hotel is in a decent location, on the Riverwalk. My wife had to go to the convention hall, it is a good walk (0.4 miles) - very do-able. But she is pregnant and combined with the Texas heat, she took a cab, $5 bucks each way. The garage is at the hotel, I see no reason to use the valet. The garage is kind of tight parking spaces (minivan), but we never had a problem parking. The staff (front desk) were very friendly and helpful (upon request, within 5 min they had maintenance oiling our hinges on door because it woke or daughter up). The pool and pool area is VERRRRY small - this should be considered if you have kids and plan on swimming every day with them. Also, just a note - we usually go to the pool after sightseeing etc, anywhere from 3pm-6pm - be advised there is no sun on the pool between those hours, but any other time of day or evening, there is sun (if you can find a place to lay (small area)) The towels they provide at the pool are like the size of facecloths. The restaurant was decent for a quick bite before heading out. Don't expect a grand lobby upon entering the hotel. My wife thought the fitness center was lousy, like 3 machines total (one eliptical)
The Rooms: We got a suite. Reasonably priced. They had a good size bedroom and good size living area with chairs, love seat (with pull out bed) and a table and chairs, sink and fridge. The bathroom was in the bedroom, I thought the layout was odd, it should be in the living are, but I'm no interior designer. The big drawback on the room was lack of storage. There was one 3 draw dresser in the bedroom and one in the living room. There was adequate free space in the bedroom for another bureau or dresser. The room was clean, but just sort of felt dated / worn / tired. But it was clean. The bathtub could be updated. The bed was very comfortable and pillows were decent. We tried to have a drink on one of our two balconies, but the city living noise was too much to relax and enjoy the night air. Free wifi, which was good since the tv stations are limited (how about printing out a channel guide?).
Overall, if you take the train out of the equation, the rating goes up to 4. See HobartLane's restaurant reviews in San Antonio on Yelp.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel San Antonio Northwest / I-10
title: “Good family friendly hotel”
text: We stayed here with another family so we could go to the Zoo and swim. We were a little disappointed about some of the amenities. The website boasts an indoor and outdoor pool, however there is only an indoor pool. We also thought there was an outdoor play area but there was not one. Overall it was a nice, inexpensive hotel. Rooms were of good size. Our friends had a major issue with their AC (bad news since both men are AC guys) that didn't get corrected and they didn't move them to another room either. The food was good, and there was a small arcade area for the kids. Get to the breakfast buffet early if you want a table!

name: Holiday Inn Riverwalk
title: “Loved it”
text: We went for our anniversary. I really hate San Antonio, but I had not been to the Riverwalk in like 25 years, so I decided to give it another try. I was impressed by the Riverwalk itself and also impressed with the hotel. The service was great, nice staff, efficient. I thought breakfast was free for some reason, but it isn't, just FYI. I got a really great price through a "discount" website, so I felt the value was excellent for us, but would have been only an ok value if the full price of like $119/night was what we paid. I would stay here again for sure.

name: The St. Anthony Riverwalk, A Wyndham Hotel
title: “Needs Renovation”
text: Bathroom tiles cracked, tub was clogged, took shower in standing backed-up water, gross door handles missing on dresser, paper cups no glass coffee cups like the ones pictured, table was missing wood/chipped, shady location,across the street from a seedy park, wi fi kept dying. Could hear the residents next door getting loud. The staff was friendly and helpful. Restaurant food was just ok.

name: Holiday Inn Express San Antonio Airport
title: “Great Value”
text:
The hotel was clean, comfortable, and the service was exceptional. The breakfast was reasonable, the internet was good, and the health center was acceptable. The closet was small. Even for a quick 4 day business trip, I had a hard time fitting my stuff in there.
The health center had 2 new treadmills, a bike, a step machine, and a large flat screen TV. I was very pleased with the cleanliness of the health center, the only thing that turned me off were the 2 walls that were completely windows. 
They have a gated lot and parking garage which was convenient for the guests. 
The only other thing that bothered me was the noise of the adjacent highway, otherwise it was a great stay!
I recommend signing up for a Priority Club Membership. When I arrived with my membership I received a complimentary bottle of water. There was also a complimentary happy hour for members during the week.

name: Hilton San Antonio Hill Country Hotel & Spa
title: “Great Stay at the Radisson”
text:
My experience at the Radisson was good. I have few complaints, but some of the problems were bothersome. We (as in my choral group) arrived on a Thursday and we checked out on Sunday morning. We spent very little time in the hotel itself, but the time we did spend was an overall good experience. 
 The room was very appealing to the eye and was quite clean. They provide all the basic things like internet access, television, coffee brewer, and toiletries. My room had a king sized bed and a pull out couch. There was also a nice deck for looking around. The hotel itself was beautiful. In the back courtyard were several fire pits for downtime, and 3 separate pools and a hot tub. Everything was very pleasing to the eye and the environment was comfortable. There was also a decent little fitness center for those would want to get a work out in while they are on vacation.
 Most of my disappointments I encountered during my stay were small things, but there was one major thing that really bugged me. It was 70 degrees and since our group was from Minnesota we jumped on the opportunity to take a swim outside during winter. When we got to the pool we all jumped in assuming that the water would be warm, but to our surprise the water was cold. Supposedly the pool and hot tub were to be heated, but at no point during our stay were they on! The lap pool was heated, but barely. A small issue I had with my stay was that the Ethernet cable in my room was broken so I had to physically hold it in my laptop for access. The bed was a tad bit uncomfortable. The sheets were very stiff. I don’t have any other complaints to speak of.
 Besides the few minor issues we had, our overall stay was great. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who is looking for a comfortable place to stay, but don’t expect to be swimming too much.

name: The Menger Hotel
title: “Love this Hotel”
text: I don't know what the other people are talking about. It is a lovely hotel. Rich with history and lovely atmosphere. My family and i are planning another vacation to the Menger this summer. You can't beat the price and location.

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Antonio Downtown/Market Square
title: “Comfort, Location and Value!!!”
text: I stay at Courtyard-Marriotts frequently and this one is my favorite. Location is excellent being two blocks from Market Square (El Mercado) with lots of gift shops and two good Mex. restaurants. Mi Tierra is not the best Mex restaurant in town, but it is very fun and lively and is open 24 hours a day, so if you want some enchiladas at 3am, they've got you covered. A trolley stop is just out the door taking folks around downtown area and to the Riverwalk or alamodome. Cost is $1.00 RT. Rooms are NOT "shabby", as they have all been totally updated in the past two years with new beds, furntiure, carpet. etc. The suites are excellent value if you need two rooms.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Terrible service, food - for a fortune”
text:
$189 a night (conference rate) and the rooms leak and have cobwebs. Friend's room filled with water, carpet was soaked like a sponge - they did not move her to another room, just put fans on the carpet. It smelled terrible.
My room had no desk chair (despite two calls) and room was twice not made up despite calls to housekeeping. And it wasn't my "do not disturb" sign -none of us had those in our rooms! Rooms often not made up until 3pm or later. Rain knocked out the server, so no $10 a day internet. $20 a day to park your car outside. 
Restaurant service spectacularly bad. Dessert the waiter told me was rasberry was actually blueberry; waiter argued with me that there was "raspberry IN it" (it was creme brulee. Hard to hide fruit in there...what with all the blueberries and all). Casual restaurant was even worse. Food bland, ordinary - twice, hot dishes were served cold.
Sent an e-mail to the manager and answered the "satisfaction" survey with my name and contact info, but no response.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel San Antonio Northwest / I-10
title: “Business travel may be a requirement, but Embassy Suites SA Northwest is a favored hotel choice.”
text: No matter whether I am at the front desk, the dining area, the restaurant or interacting with the housekeeping staff, the friendly, supportive and service oriented staff provides a warm, friendly, and comfortable environment throughout the hotel. The San Antonio decor adds to the environment.

name: Hampton Inn San Diego Airport / SeaWorld
title: “A Pricey but Decent Night's Sleep”
text: My wife and I stayed here for one night in the summer. We wanted a hotel close to the airport, as our flight home left at 6:30AM. This hotel is just a few miles from the airport, and it took five or ten minutes to drive there on city streets. Get good directions before you attempt to find this hotel, as it is tucked away in a busy, and somewhat ugly, commercial corner of the city by the intersection of I-5 and I-8. We have no complaints about the room, which was large and clean. I was thankful that our room overlooked a self-storage facility rather than the street or the neighboring nude dancing establishment. Because we checked out so early on a weekend morning, however, we did not see the breakfast offerings and there were no take-away breakfast bags available, though there was coffee. The high-speed Internet in the room was useful. We would have been happier had we paid $40 or $50 less for the room, but San Diego is an expensive city, and the hotel met our needs.

name: Hill Country Inn & Suites
title: “What a Wonderful Surprise”
text:
This is a jewel of a find for San Antonio lodging.
Clean spacious rooms with a "cabin" feel. 
Location is easy to get to and close to airport, malls and easy access to other San Antonio entertainments. 
We were pleasantly surprised with the accommodations. The front desk seemed a little confused but all in all the stay was pleasant, a good value and better than average.

name: Crowne Plaza San Antonio Riverwalk
title: “Get nickled and dimed, but don't get any sort of accommodations.”
text:
Parking was valet $28/day
Coke machine out of everything
Ice machine broken 
Pool key didn't work
No vent in bathroom
Asked for two extra towels I never got
Pool was third level up and vibrated, view was of buildings

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Palo Alto Inn & Suites
title: “A GoodStay but Room for Improvement”
text:
This is the first Best Western we have stayed at that was a new facility. We were very impressed with the accommodations in the the room and the appearance of the building overall. For a family of four the room which we stayed in was very spacious. Hotel staff was very helpful and accommodating. 
Suggestions for Improvement:
1. Signage for the hotel could be better along with some lighting for the access road. 
2. Biggest complaint was the internet. If I remember correctly it was called Speed Link or Links and for a lack of better words it sucked. When a customer is paying close to $100 a night to stay at the hotel they deserved better than what their getting. More than one LAN cable would be nice. 
To the traveler: If your going to stay at the hotel and use a computer in your room a LAN Cable would be a wise investment.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites San Antonio Medical Center
title: “Terrible Breakfast, unclean and uncomfortable”
text:
Not sure where these other reviewers have stayed in the past, but I chose this place in part on the reviews and I was completely misinformed. The breakfast was terrible, the eggs completely inedible. A "hot breakfast" was advertised, but the only items hot were the fore mentioned eggs and pigs in the blanket that were too inedible as they were hard as a rock. Everything else available was a typical hotel breakfast for which we had much better at a much cheaper hotel the day before in New Braunfels.
They did not have our reservation when we arrived due to booking with hotels.com. Well if you can't communicate with those you advertise with then don't advertise with them. This caused our check in to take an additional 20 minutes or so and with already tired and traveled kids this is a big problem. 
The first room A/C did not work and the room was 80 degrees upon arrival. They did send keys to a new room immediately.
The carpet in the halls were appalling. The bathtub was dirty or stained not sure which. All in all, I felt cheated. Never have reviews let me down so badly. I would not take my family back to this hotel nor recommend it to anyone regardless of location. Have you not seen how many hotels are in the same area and some with easier access to the interstate. Very disappointed.

name: Microtel Inn & Suites by Wyndham San Antonio/Near SeaWorld/Lackland AFB
title: “never again”
text: couldn't find the place with gps , so we called to get directions. Not only was the desk clerk rude, but he was wrong all 3 times we talked to him. finally stopped at a convenience store, and got proper directions. After an hour and a half of driving around, we got there, and were given they keys to an already occupied room.Thank God the chain was in use, because all I could hear was a woman screaming to her husband" I'm naked!". Back to the desk clerk now a little embarrassed and irritated where I receive a new key to a room right next to the lobby. At 5:30 A.M. I am awakened by a golf team who has decided to strategize their day right outside my door. awesome. Couldn't go back to sleep, so decided to make coffee, to realize there was no coffeemakers in the rooms. Even hotels with way less ratings have more iminities than this. Thanks again Microtel.I'll make sure more hear my story, because your staff just said " oops, sorry" when I told them our problems.

name: The Dana on Mission Bay
title: “This place is unbelievable!!!!”
text:
This place was beyond words. My husband and I stayed in downtown San Diego for my business trip at a very nice hotel. We stayed over an extra night at The Dana to celebrate our 5th wedding anniversary and get out of the bustle of the city after the business trip was over. First of all, they upgraded our room to the best suite in the place because it was our anniversary. I mentioned it in the comments when I booked on their site. It was the most unbelievable experience. We rented a kayak and spent 4 hours touring around the area and seeing sea lions up close. We booked a couples message that was great but the spa facilities have something to be desired. All in all, we enjoyed ourselves VERY MUCH and would return to this place in a heartbeat. 
Some suggestions:
- The Blue Pearl restaurant had great service and excellent food. There was outside dining that overlooked the marina and allows you to sit out and see fireworks at Sea World while you enjoy your dinner. PROBLEM: It should be located somewhere else than right by the pool. It was a little too close to families enjoying a night swim with their children. 
- When making your reservation, try to book in the newer section. We walked around and found out that some of the cheaper rooms were in an older section of the hotel.

name: Hotel Indigo San Antonio Riverwalk
title: “First Class Botique for a Great Price”
text:
i had to come to San Antonio for a business meeting, we stayed at the Hotel Indigo on the Riverwalk. The hotel courtyard is the first thing you see when you arrive thru the main entrance. it is sooooo traditional and soooo beautiful. This entire hotel is beautiful; front desk reception fast and housekeeping is delightful and friendly. About 2pm we went down the bistro, "Bridges" for a snack, they were closed, but the two girls were exceptionally friendly and they made us coffee which we paid for at the front desk. The rooms are spacious. They are designed for the Business traveler AND the tourist. The Hotel sits on the Riverwalk and and is an easy walk to everything downtown. They have a fitness center that is well equipped. 
This is a great hotel for business or for the tourist. Prices are perfect.

name: Red Roof Inn San Antonio Downtown - Riverwalk
title: “Very good”
text:
Reception staff excellent, Darlene and particularly Roger, doing an excellent, well-informed, enthusiastic job. Pleasantly surprised to find a distinctly design-led approach to décor and furnishings in a large light room, with an excellent work station, and no fewer than eight electric sockets/power outlets – a very welcome change from the tired furnishings and scrabble to find a free outlet usual in this price range.
An easy walk from the Alamo and River Walk, and $7/night parking fee unusual in US (tho common practice in downtown European hotels), but acceptable.
Downsides were small towels, lack of toiletries (shampoo only), and sketchy breakfast, but very willing to accept this in exchange for style, comfort and value. 
Easily the best hotel in its range that I stayed at during a week-long swing through NM and TX. Pleased enough, in fact that I booked the Red Roof at IAH, which was a slightly different story.

name: Microtel Inn & Suites by Wyndham San Antonio/Near SeaWorld/Lackland AFB
title: “Excellent value”
text: We were here for 5 days for our son's AF graduation. Great staff, clean and comfortable. Pool is small but great at the end of a hot day. Highly recommend an upgrade to a suite, more room, micro and small refridgerator. Super Walmart a few miles away to stock up on supplies.

name: Crowne Plaza San Antonio Riverwalk
title: “Outdated, overpriced, unclean”
text:
I'll start with the worst- the maids do a terrible job. They took the dirty towels off my bathroom floor, refolded them and put them back on the rack. Disgusting. I was there for a conference and this happened multiple times to multiple people there, so it's not a one time mistkae but more of a regular practice.
Hotel itself is not that bad- just don't be fooled that it's a 4 or even 3 star place. It's a 2 star hotel and you should pay accordingly. My company paid for my stay, but I wouldn't spend more than $100/night here. Probably should be less than that.
Also while it is technically on the Riverwalk it's a good distance from anything else worth going to on the Riverwalk.

name: El Tropicano Riverwalk Hotel
title: “Not great but not bad for the money”
text:
I wanted a reasonably priced hotel near where my friend lived and El Tropicana Holiday Inn was it. It is on the River Walk but not close to where the "action" is. You'd have to walk it or a short cab ride ( I wouldn't recommend walking at night). My room was just OK. It had a musty smell to it which I deduced was coming from the A/C. The only chair in the room had a tear in it and wasn't near the desk but on the other side of my bed (No one is checking the maid service?) Wall paper too was tearing off part of the wall. There's a great coffee maker in the room but the maid service didn't clean the cups or give me new coffee pads on one of my four days. Oh, and the bathroom TP role was way too close to the toilet seat. If I was a larger person I'd have to sit side-saddled lol.
That said, the place was clean and the restaurant was good on the night it rained heavily and I didn't want to venture out. Would I go back? Not really. I'd find a closer hotel to that "action" I mentioned earlier.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Terribly disappointed”
text: Attended a wedding and was very disappointed. The views were simply great but the food service and the food very below par. At the wedding reception the appetizers room just did not have enough chairs, and the room was very stuffy for the amount of people that were suppose to be in that room. Being served the dinner the waiters were dripping food on people, chairs and with no apologizes. For a hot dish the food was cold. In the morning there was to be a immediate family brunch in the Barefoot Cafe. We tried and tried to make reservations weeks before the wedding with no luck, finally, someone understood that there was going to be 35 people showing up for this breakfast and assisted, but it was a disaster. In a long table of people some people received their food 20-30 minutes before other people. We had crying children who were hungry and had to watch other people eat because their food was not there. The food again was very cold. I would not recommend this hotel for a family like gathering as a wedding this was beyond a disaster.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites San Antonio Medical Center
title: “Good hotel at a good value”
text:
I was in town on business for a week and I needed a good room at a good price. I found that room at the La Quinta Inn & Suites.
The hotel was conveniently located near I-10 just north of the I-410 loop. There were plenty of restaurants up and down Frontage Road on both sides of the interstate, although you will need your car because it's not in a location that lends itself to walking.
The hotel staff was friendly and helpful and check in was easy.
The amenities were nice as well. The hotel had a nice pool which was always being used but rarely crowded. The hotel had a nice breakfast area that offered a hot breakfast.
As for the room, I have no complaints at all. I had an Executive King Room with a sofa sleeper for an average price of $80 per night for the week. The bed was comfortable. The internet service was adequate.
I recommend this hotel.

name: Hampton Inn San Diego Airport / SeaWorld
title: “Großes, aber gutes Hotel”
text:
Das Hamptons Inn liegt zwar nicht in einer tollen Gegend, dafür aber sehr verkehrsgünstig am Highway und ideal für den Besuch von Sea World. 
Recht große komfortable Zimmer, gute Infrastruktur, gutes Frühstück mit hot Items.
Was will man mehr.
