Für die Verhältnisse in San Diego war das Hamptons sogar noch recht preiswert.

name: Hotel Indigo San Antonio Riverwalk
title: “Very good for location”
text: Hotel is on the river walk but a little deceiving. There is access to river walk from hotel but it is a good walk to the shops/ restaurants. It is still a good place to stay in. The service is great, the rooms ( beds) are very comfortable and the walk to restaurants/shops through the river walk is very nice. In my experience I did not mind the walks.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Wonderfull”
text:
We stayed in june of 2004 but only for 2 nights as we had booked prior to our hols. When we arrived it was like another world as we had driven from la and after our 2 nights were up we wished we had booked another 1 here and less in la!!
Nothing was too much trouble for anyone, the food was great, the room was really nice, the loo backed up when we first used it but the guy came out within 5 mins and sorted the job out, had a lovely time here, we are going to go back this year and stay for longer , it was the highlight of our stay in the states ( and we had done vegas and la in the same trip ) . 
I do not understand the bad reviews i have read but all i can say is i can't reccomend this place enough.

name: Red Roof Inn San Antonio Downtown - Riverwalk
title: “Great Experience”
text:
We needed rooms for several shipmates for our annual ship’s reunion so I contacted Red Roof Inn San Antonio, TX, 1011 East Houston Group Sales Manager and arranged by telephone for our group to stay at the Red Roof Inn.
I had been to San Antonio on multiple occasions but was not familiar with the Red Roof Inn. As it turned out it is an excellent location if you plan visiting the River Walk, Alamo and/or other local attractions. Public transportation is within 200 feet of hotel entrance to attractions and tour trolleys in the Alamo area, and immediate access to the Interstate highway. The airport is 10 – 15 minutes depending upon the time of day and traffic. Everything was really excellent from a local logistic perspective and the hotel was great. The hotel facility is clean and well kept, and done so continuously. We had a group of about 24 people and 13 rooms.
The Group Sales Management I contacted gave us, what we consider, a significant reduced room rate for our group. We were also provided with other amenities’ at significant savings including the conference room use with catering and other services available. The group sales staff did not stop when we arrived at the hotel, they checked with me et al in our group nearly every day to be assured we were happy with our choice. Thanks to Sandra and Lisa.
The hotel manager Max conversed daily with members of our group throughout our four to six night stay making sure we were conformable and happy with our service from the hotel. I have to say, and I am a frequent user of hotels, I have never had a hotel genuinely display such a sincere desire to provide for and make sure clients were happy and comfortable. His staff reflected his desire to please clients. Thanks Max.
The hotel staff made sure the rooms were serviced in a way that was unique. I saw cleaning staff in the hallway every day, yet I never once saw the room service staff in my room. It was like magic, leave, come back and the room was serviced. And, to the person every staff member had a genuine smiling positive greeting. At 5am I would see the parking lot being picked up of any litter by Willie keeping the grounds impressively clean. 
The conference room was always cleaned and serviced when we were ready to use the room. The grab and go breakfast room was continuously cleaned, serviced and replenished from beginning to end of breakfast time. And, Angie smilingly reminded folks sitting in the lobby that breakfast would be over soon so that they may get something before closing. The experience renews my faith that most folks really do care and are willing to go the extra mile. Thank you all Mike Marshall, Ohio.

name: Red Roof Inn San Antonio Downtown - Riverwalk
title: “Just good value, at a good location!”
text:
If you are looking for a hotel at walking distance from the Alamo and the riverwalk, this place is a good choice! The rooms are clean, the bathroom is clean! (but is due for a renovation/replacement in the year to come!)
A minor item; we missed a table (for the laptop) in our room...
Nevertheless, The place looks safe, parking is a bargain ($5) and you can park your car in a garage, nicely out of the sun! 
The staff is very friendly!
Recommended!!

name: El Tropicano Riverwalk Hotel
title: “It was fantastic”
text: Has a great stay at the El Tropicano Hotel, in San Antonio. The staff; front dest, dinning room, bar and room were helpful and pleasant. Food was great. Service was great. Had a wonderful time. San Antonio and the El Tropicano Hotel is our vacation spot in Texas. Thank you!

name: Omni San Antonio Hotel
title: “A solid choice for good nights stay!”
text: The hotel was consistent in all areas. Food. Service and accommodations were solid. Nothing to complain about and you leave saying I had a nice stay.pricing was competitive and staff were exceptional in communicating and making sure our needs were addressed. All in all I would recommend them and would stay again when I want a predictable place to stay!

name: Aloft San Antonio Airport
title: “Very Nice....”
text:
This was the first time we had stayed in this hotel, although we have been to San Antonio many many times. Its about 5 minutes by car from the airport but they also have a shuttle.
The hotel is a subsidiary of the W Hotels and based on a loft architecture.
The lobby area is opened planned, with a small check-in desk, light open bar area, pool table, comfy chairs, work area and coffee and snack bar. One of the best things about this place is that the wireless internet was free and actually worked.
Check in was the only let down, we arrived at 230pm and told our room was not ready and with only one person checking in it got to be a little tiresome.
The elevators are little slow although the 'funky' floor inside is great.
Rooms again are 'lofty', clean, airy and comfortable as well as a great size. The bathroom sink is outside the bathroom itself, divided from the bedroom, so you dont have to watch someone brush their teeth, and where you will find a two person shower with shampoo, conditioner and shower dispensers on the wall. All the usual stuff are there like local magazines, coffee, a safe and so on.
There is a good sized TV on the wall. The nice feature is that if you have an ipod or some form of video player, with the right connecting leads you can plug this into a unit on the desk and watch your own movie on the TV. 
All in all a great hotel to stay for vacation or business.

name: El Tropicano Riverwalk Hotel
title: “You get what you pay for.....”
text:
Stayed in SA countless times, usually at the upscale pricier hotels. Decided to take a chance (and save a few bucks) and book through Hotwire. Best prices, but you only get a general location of the hotel and a star rating. This hotel was supposedly 3.5 stars out of 4 and ON the riverwalk, It was neither. It was an old Holiday Inn far from the restaurants and clubs on the river, but it was $60 a night. If you don't mind walking 20-30 minutes to get anywhere and you don't need frills and don't need a lot of space this is a good low budget hotel.
PROS: Very clean rooms. VERY friendly staff. Close to the elevators self parking ($14.99) with in and out priviledges. Big, clean pool for families. Great prices on alcohol at the Tiki bar. Free, in room WIFI.
CONS: Overpriced food and no room service after 10pm and no late dining options within SAFE walking distance ( Dominos and Pizza hut does quickly deliver.) Old, well worn hotel. Nothing closeby and walking after dark was scary due to the homeless in the are

name: Bristol Hotel
title: “Carino ma non eccezionale”
text:
Camera pulita, ben tenuta ma abbastanza piccola. L'albergo è centrale e da su una via di intenso traffico. La nostra camera dava sulla strada e devo dire che il rumore del traffico si sentiva. Mi aspettavo una maggiore insonorizzazione per un albergo che si reputa di un certo livello. Parcheggio (praticamente obbligato) a pagamento a 26 usd al giorno. Costo camera 228 usd a notte. Non economico. Colazione non inclusa.
Consiglio unicamente a chi desidera stare nel centro di San Diego per comodità ai servizi.

name: SpringHill Suites San Antonio SeaWorld/Lackland
title: “Great Stay”
text: I'm very shocked at the bad reviews I have seen for this hotel. My kids and I had a wonderful stay. The room was clean and the bed was fine. I just don't have any complaints. I will be staying at this hotel again when I visit San Antonio.

name: The Dana on Mission Bay
title: “Uncomfortable Bed and Other Problems - Clean, Good Service.”
text:
I stayed at The Dana last weekend for a wedding that I was attending there. I stayed in a "Standard Courtyard View" room with one king bed in the 400 building which is in the older section of the hotel. Service in the lobby was very good and everything was very clean. 
The room was average sized but the furniture was arranged awkwardly - with all the furniture bunched in one part of the room so it was hard to walk around but the other half of the room was almost completely empty. The place provided to hang clothes is right inside the doorway and next to the sink. Everytime I used the sink I was afraid I would get my clothes wet or dirty. 
The most important part of my hotel stay is the bed. A great hotel room would have a bed that you sleep better in than your bed at home. Our bed had a stiff mattress with a too-small fitted sheet that slipped off the mattress in the middle of the night - there's nothing comfortable about that. The only pillows provided were the fluffy cotton or polyester-filled kind. 
Overall, I would not recommend The Dana to a friend.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel San Antonio International Airport
title: “Great hotel! Great staff!”
text: Great hotel. Clean. Good food. Fantastic and friendly staff. Very pleasant. Only down side of hotel is outdated televisions in the rooms. No bad just not of high quality. Other than this minor issue, hotel is a 5 star!!

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Limited At Best”
text: After looking at the net and seeing the reviews from travel guides, I thought this would be a lovely place. While the grounds were lovely, we found the rooms musty and moldy smelly and mean extremely so. We had a bay side view room which was extremely disappointing and nothing of interest to look at. The rooms in general were o.k., but extremely over priced for what you got. The activities there are primary for the ten and younger children and are not appealing to kids over ten. I would not go back to this resort.

name: SpringHill Suites San Antonio SeaWorld/Lackland
title: “Excellent service, clean, modern”
text: I definately recommend this hotel to anyone attending a BMT graduation @ lackland. They have a pool, a pretty good free breakfast, and a computer for guests to use. If i'm ever in San Antonio again I will def. stay here again!

name: Staybridge Suites San Antonio NW near Six Flags Fiesta Texas
title: “MUY MAL SERVICIO”
text: DESAFORTUNADAMENTE EL SERVICIO EN EL HOTEL FUE MUY MALO, ESTUVE 3 DIAS Y NINGUN DIA HICIERON LIMPIEZA EN LA HABITACION, SOLO CAMBIARON TOALLAS. ADEMAS ME DIERON UNA HABITACION CON UNA CAMA QUEEN, CUANDO PEDI KING SIZE, PEDI ME LO CAMBIARAN Y ME DIJERON QUE NO SE PODIA, MUY MAL, A PESAR DE SER SOCIO PRIORITY.

name: Humphreys Half Moon Inn & Suites
title: “Great accomodations/entertainment”
text:
Spent 5 days at hotel/resort. Large, clean well equipped rooms,
excellent pool/hot tub. Good food in lounge/resturant
with an excellent view of the marina and countryside.
Outstanding entertainment venue there also.
Many big name stars featured there. Harry Connick Jr. played one night in the 
lounge. Humphrey's also has big name stars at their outdoor concert stage in
the summer.
Highly Recommend it. Will Return again.

name: BEST WESTERN Posada Ana Inn-Airport
title: “Best Western, San Antonio”
text: Very friendly service. We arrived late after a long five-hour drive, and were greeted very warmly; the front desk manager was very helpful. Check-in was quick and we were in our room within minutes. The fan in the bathroom needed to be fixed, it sounded like a helicopter taking off. The Continental breakfast had a good variety of food. Would stay again.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton San Antonio Northwest
title: “Great For Families”
text: Stayed here have no negative things to say. Staff was friendly and helpful. Room was clean. Hotel had breakfast every morning which we took advantage of. Dinner served M through Thurs. Got a one room suite a which allowed us separation from the kids. Main areas appeared kept. Exercise room had modern equipment. Beds were comfortable. We will always look at staying at any Homewood location for future vacation destinations.

name: Paradise Point Resort & Spa
title: “Abzocke im Paradies”
text:
Die Lage ist super: in einer Bucht vor San Diego. Aber man hat Flugverkehr (der internationale Flughafen ist nur ca. 10 Min mit dem Auto entfernt). Und nahezu alles kostet unverschämt extra: eine große Flasche Wasser im hoteleigenen Shop z. B. 4,50 USD, Minigolf 10 USD pro Person, das Frühstück ist sehr teuer, die Wassersportangebote unanständig kostspielig ... Lichtblick ist das Restaurant Baleen: etwas teurer als das andere Restaurant in der Anlage aber sehr aufmerksamer Service und ausgezeichnetes Essen.
Die Anlage ist toll, 4 Pools, jeweils Schwimmpool und Hot Tube, viele Liegen - und das alles ohne Aufpreis. Die Rate von Expedia war wirklich sehr günstig, vielleicht war das Personal deshalb nicht besonders freundlich? Wir würden das nächste Mal direkt an den Strand gehen, z. B. in das Best Western am Mission Beach. Aber auch San Diego hat uns nicht besonders gefallen, das ist wirklich kein must.

name: The St. Anthony Riverwalk, A Wyndham Hotel
title: “Good Location, Old Fashioned Ambience”
text: I tagged along with my wife on her business conference which was held at this hotel. During check-in we were told our reserved room did not have a king sized bed as we requested so after we asked if another room could be found we were given a free upgrade to a small suite (it helps that my wife is a Wyndham Rewards corporate traveller). Yes, this hotel has seen better days. The carpet was worn and some of the furniture was beat up. The hallways were like something out of "The Shining" or "Barton Fink". However, the bed was very comfortable, the service was excellent, and the location was very good (two blocks from Alamo and River Walk). The first floor common areas were still opulent.

name: Hilton San Diego Bayfront
title: “classico hotel di lusso”
text:
L'albergo è bello, modernissimo e di design moderno, dai colori chiari, ben strutturato.
ha una bella piscina con dei lettini a doppia piazza dotati anche di televisore.
le camere sono spaziose, panoramicissime. con viste sulla baia e coronado
La colazione è a buffet e abbastanza buona per gli standard americani e neanche molto cara (15 dollari a persona).
L'unica pecca è che è situato in una zona un pò limitrofa dal centro città ma praticamente annesso al cento congressi.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton San Antonio Northwest
title: “Nice and comfortable”
text: We were on vacation in San Antonio and we stayed at this hotel. The hotel itself was nice and the rooms were comfortable and not cramped. The beds were very comfortable, but the pillows took some getting use to. We didn't have any issues with our room whatsoever. One bad thing, when we arrived on Monday, the pool was closed due to someone getting sick and it had to be cleaned and they told us the pool should be open the next day...but the pool was closed all week and opened back on on Sunday when we were leaving. This wasn't an issue for us either since we were gone most of the time and went to Schlitterbahn. The breakfast was good, but I've had better at other Homewood Suites. The staff was very nice and helpful. We really enjoyed our stay.

name: The St. Anthony Riverwalk, A Wyndham Hotel
title: “Will return”
text:
I accompanied my husband on a business trip of his. I loved this hotel. There's not one thing to complain about. Hotel was beautiful, walking distance to Riverwalk, mall and Market Square. Convienience store and drug store close by. The most impressive, though, was the personal attention given by the staff, in every area! 
Hoping the conference is there again next year. I will definitely tag along!

name: Pinn Road Inn & Suites
title: “Great service at a great price!!!”
text:
Was there June 28- July 1st for my son's BMT graduation ceremonies. Service was awesome. Got lots a few times and every time they found me without attitude. Our room was 310 family suite it too was great. The Cameron with fresh towels every morning. Would recommend to everyone! All the staff was awesome. We arrived early an they accommodated us with a room. If you are looking for a clean room, awesome service, and an affordable price... The Pinn Road Inn is the way to go. The only bad thing was that it didn't have a pool, but they made up for it in service. All the comforts of a high prices hotel without the high prices. 
Thanks guys. You made our visit to San Antonio great!

name: Omni San Antonio Hotel
title: “Slightly older hotel with good service”
text:
I stayed here for two nights while visiting some friends in San Antonio. I got a great deal ($92/night) by booking 21 days out. Location was great: 15 mins from the airport, near the highway, a grocery store and lots of restaurants and stores. I even walked to dinner one night.
Check in was quick and easy, the staff was quite nice. 
I had a problem with my initial room and though they were quick to move me, the bellman came up with a key but no cart. I had to move myself without any assistance. I guess I could have asked, but I expected better from a hotel of this caliber. 
Internet is NOT free, but if you sign up for Omni's frequent guest program (which is free), it is free immediately.
Pros: 
Some nice upscale touches in the rooms
Big, comfortable room sizes
Great toiletries and shower 
Staff is eager to please
Cons:
Elevators are slow
Rooms aren't that insulated from hallway noise
All in all, I would stay here again - especially now that my expectation is set.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites San Antonio Fiesta TX
title: “Enjoyed my stay”
text: This was a tucked away quiet LaQuinta. It was very clean and the staff was friendly. The location to Fiesta Texas, shopping at La Cantera or the Rim, and UTSA was perfect. Easy access to the hwy. A pleasant surprize was the size of the hot tub. Breakfast was a large selection of hot and cold breakfast items.

name: Hyatt Place San Antonio/Riverwalk
title: “Just a Couple Blocks from the Riverwalk”
text: Staff was very friendly when checking in and made me feel welcome. My room was a great size, very large with lots of space. The bed was very comfortable and for the most part I slept good. The free parking is a perk and convenient. The walk to downtown in the Riverwalk area is literally 2 blocks away and I walked there by myself at 8pm and felt very comfortable because it seemed there was always a lot of people around. A downer is the noise of a train which was quite constant the second night I stayed and the "musty" kind of smell in the elevator and hallway. Complimentary breakfast was good, with fresh fruit and plenty of drinks and bagels/english muffins.

name: Crockett Hotel
title: “Excellent location!”
text: Crockett Hotel was conveniently located right behind the Alamo, and just off the freeway, so it was very easy to find! Aside from that, it was also a piece of history, with its beautiful facade, with modern conveniences, a lovely atrium which provides a nice visual aspect, and none of the old smell or challenges, such as plumbing issues. It was comfortable, clean, and a great experience.

name: San Diego Marriott Marquis & Marina
title: “Extremely nice with great staff, good location”
text: I stayed here for four nights for a conference and loved my stay. If you are a Marriott Elite member, this hotel has one of the best concierge lounges I have seen. Excellent staff, very knowledgeable and nice, and great location within walking distance to the Gaslamp district and a grocery store. Pricey add-ons, however, with internet and parking being an absolute rip-off, but that is standard throughout the Marriott chain. Directly next door to the convention center and the Grand Hyatt where a lot of other conferences locate.

name: Hotel Valencia Riverwalk
title: “Great romantic getaway!”
text: Hotel Valencia really is top-notch! Everything you'd expect and then some from a hotel of their caliber. When we arrived, we were given a free upgrade to a room with a balcony over the courtyard. The room was beautifully appointed, and the balcony was a great little quaint place to enjoy a bottle of wine. The room lighting and setting made for great romance. The bathroom was very nice, although I'd change the lighting just a bit to better aid in doing makeup. The hair dryer could have been better. The bed was very comfortable and had pillows for days. The hotel is right on the riverwalk, at one end. Just a short little walk to all the main hustle and bustle of the riverwalk bars and restaurants. I was very impressed, and we had a great time!

name: The St. Anthony Riverwalk, A Wyndham Hotel
title: “Historic great location”
text: Recently took 18 couples on a buisness appreciation weekend. The location of the hotel was great. one and a half blocks from the river walk and four blocks from the Alamo. Don't expect a new hotel, this hotel is very well kept, and the staff was excellent to work with. The restaurant was very good.

name: The Menger Hotel
title: “I would recomend this hotel to any one.”
text: The Menger is a beautiful,well run hotel,we only had breakfast, but the food and service were very good.. the reception was very helpful, the pool was lovely, there are lots of history lessons inand around The Menger. My friends and I had five wonderful days,

name: The Menger Hotel
title: “watch your bill”
text: I checked in and we had reservations for 4 rooms 2 each connecting, not only didi that not happen, my room wasn't ready, and I made the reservations for all the couples. Then I wasn't told about a free margarita if your rooms not ready until another quest told be about it. So back to the front desk. Even though I don't drink Margaritas it's the point. The restaurant staff was GREAT. Then the check out, check your bill. I normally stay in hotels that I frquent on a regular basis and don't worry about the bill. I was charged for 2 vehicles a day and called them that day to discuss and was told accounting was closed, strange they can still charge to your card should they miss something. Then called the following day to be challenged that I had 2 vehicles, then told it would be 4 days before they could review and correct the issue if they found it. Asked for the manager, person answred as the manager, was the controller????????? Discussed the bill and she said she would investigate. In the mean time thought about it and remembered we did drive in with another couple, but they are still there, so called the hotel and asked for the manager by name, that is how I found out I never made it to the manager. At that time I was told I had a gold whatever. I have a red Titan. Called the other couple we went with who was still checked in and she went to the front desk in an attempt to clear things up. Now I'm concernned because we had many meals at the restaurant and pool and drinks in the bar that I signed for. What else did I buy, that wasn't mine????? Not going back

name: Hampton Inn San Diego Airport / SeaWorld
title: “meh...”
text:
After reading all the gushing reviews of this hotel, I almost feel bad sayig this, but I was unimpressed. There was nothing particularly 'wrong'...it just wasnt anything special. For me this was a business trip, not a family trip, and perhaps that's the difference.
On arrival I found my TV remote dead- not a big deal, but when I tried to call the front desk to ask for a new one I found out my phone(s) didnt work either. To their credit, when I walked up to the front desk and told them about the issues, the maintenance guy almost beat me back to my room! The breakfast was fine, the room wasn't uncomfortable and the location of the hotel was acceptable...The furnishings in my room werent falling apart, but they weren't particularly clean, either. There was not a business center, only two computers in the lobby, and trying to get in there in front of the kids waiting to play video games was a challenge. I had a first floor room at the back of the hotel, next to the room where the staff apparently stored the cleaning gear (lucky me) so there was almost constant noise. The first morning at about 5:00 someone (I assume one of the cleaning staff) opened my door with a key. They immediately closed it again when they realized the room was occupied, but since the lights in the room are on motion sensors I then had to get up and turn them off before I could try to go back to sleep. 
I will say the staff was, without exception, helpful and polite, but the place certainly wasn't a bargain and it just didnt 'feel' as welcoming as a Hampton Inn usually does. I wont be staying there again.

name: Hyatt Place San Antonio/Riverwalk
title: “Solid hotel with very accommodating staff”
text: I stay at the Hyatt Place Riverwalk whenever I come to San Antonio for business. Although it is located on the riverwalk, it's a walk from the main commercial drag, which is a good thing. The staff at the hotel is ALWAYS accommodating and goes out of their way to deliver great service, something you'd expect with the Hyatt name. My only complaint would be the small bathrooms, simply a result of all Hyatt Places formerly being Amerisuites.

name: The St. Anthony Riverwalk, A Wyndham Hotel
title: “Historic hotel which could be more”
text: We had checked into the junior suite the for a night during the week of 3-19-12 and were given a room on the 6th floor. We were initially told that all junior suite rooms on the 6th floor were facing either the park or given the city view however this is not true, you need to ask. Our room was over the roof of part of the building that had a large and very loud AC unit that would go off at least once an hour. On either side the view was blocked by the rest of the hotel. The light switch in the sitting area which was already dark did not work and neither did the AC motor for that room. In the bedroom it was cold despite the temperature being put on heat. When we called down to the front desk they sent some one up quickly who was friendly and fixed the heater in the bedroom. There is free internet in the lobby and business area but you have to pay $9.95 a night to use it in your room. The room itself was nice and the bathroom was clean and big. The only complaint I had about the bathroom was that the shower curtain did not fit all the way around resulting in water spilling out and onto the floor. Their room service menu is limited and if you order there is 20% gratuity added as well as $2.50 delivery charge. To get the food from order to delivery is approximately 30-40 minutes. As far as parking you can either do valet which is $24.50 or self-parking which is $19. When we checked in we were informed by the valet and the front desk to call down for our car when we wanted to leave however when we called the valet the next day we were informed they do not take call downs and we would have to go down with our ticket and request the vehicle. Overall the hotel is historic with a beautiful lobby but it really could be so much more.

name: Bristol Hotel
title: “Wonderful!”
text:
The Bristol is a small boutique hotel downtown San Diego, very conveniently located. Staff are super-friendly,. Rooms and beds are very comfortable, Hotel is quiet, lovely atmosphere and the welcome at the front desk is warm. Valet parking staff are friendly, courteous and prompt. Restaurant is bright and cheerful, food is good, fresh daisies on each table. 
Would highly recommend this hotel.

name: Omni San Antonio Hotel
title: “Loved the Omni!”
text: We really enjoyed our recent 2 night stay at the Omni. I chose this location because of it's close proximity to Sea World and downtown. The staff was very friendly, and the room was nice and comfortable. When we checked in, they gave my 4 year old daughter a backpack that had all kinds of nice goodies inside. The indoor/outdoor pool is really nice and a great place to relax. They have water floats and toys for the kids. They have a nice workout facility there and also a massage/day spa. I would definitely recommend this place to families and would stay here again.

name: Omni San Antonio Hotel
title: “Great Service; Needs a Facelift”
text:
This is the Omni off Hwy 10, not the Riverwalk. Booked a great rate $99 - a SAVE rate. Was in town for son's Air Force tech school graduation. Was a bit of a long ride to Lackland. 
PROS: Wonderful service. Great beds, nice toiletries, free parking, lots of restaurants & shopping nearby, quiet, thick towels.
CONS: Needs a facelift; small rooms, smaller old fashioned bathrooms. Slow elevators. 
For the $99 rate it was a deal.

name: The Menger Hotel
title: “Just a warning”
text: Our stay in the Menger was good. Unfortunately as we were leaving I left a coat behind at the valet parking. On discovering my mistake I called and asked if it had been handed in. Yes, something had been found. I arranged for it to be sent to me. But alas, it was not mine but a cheap and nasty substitute. Someone somewhere in the Menger knows where my coat is but is not saying. Although it was my own fault for letting the coat out of my sight, I am surprised that it was not returned.

name: Hotel Valencia Riverwalk
title: “Great hotel; great location”
text: The Hotel Valencia was beautiful, service was good, location on the Riverwalk was excellent. The only negatives were no pool, and on Saturday night the hotel bar and restaurant (Citrus) were reserved for a wedding so we didn't have access to balcony to sit and enjoy watching the crowds on the Riverwalk.

name: San Diego Marriott Marquis & Marina
title: “Agree with 1travelca -- avoid the city side”
text: The hotel is ok but the trains on the city side can be very noisy-- I was awake from 3-5 am and I am not usually bothered by noise.

name: Grand Hyatt San Antonio
title: “Great facility - small room”
text:
That really sums it up. They have great heated swimming pool and an awesome workout facility. I love the yoga studio! The view is spectacular and fantastic location. Other than that, the room is soooo small (we have the standard room). You have to pay for everything (Internet, parking, breakfast, water, etc) - again, luxury hotel simply has this as standard - which I simply do not understand.
By the way - for being a luxury hotel, their furniture is starting to run down. The bedside table leg is coming off, the seats are stained. I will not call it The Grand if not for their pool and workout room.
Just to let you guys know - if you are a budget traveler, there is Denny's right across the street - very short walk. They are great there. You can get a to-go and eat it in the hotel rooftop. What a great way to exercise before you eat.

name: Omni La Mansion del Rio
title: “ONLY place to stay on the Riverwalk”
text: We have now stayed here for the last 3 annual visits. Each time is better than the last and the first was pretty spectacular. We so love the location, the atmosphere and the attitude of this property! We travel frequently and we won't stay anywhere in San Antonio but here. We even adjusted our travel arrangements on the most recent trip in order that we could find rooms as La Mansion. You will be treated like you are the only guests on the property, pampered in every way.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton San Antonio-Riverwalk/Downtown
title: “Great Location”
text:
Great Location and Great Place. You are in a walking distance from the main places in the River Walk and only about 20 minutes away from Fiesta Texas and a bit longer for Sea World. The rooms are well kept and good size. If you are traveling with kids you can send them to the living room to watch tv or play nintendo while you relax in a seperate room. 
The pool is small but little kids don't mind much. 
The only complaint I would have is the valet parking. $20/day and they do take anywhere from 30-40 minutes to get your car in the morning when people are either checking out or need their vehicles for anything else.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton San Antonio-Riverwalk/Downtown
title: “Great Hotel”
text: Just returned from a visit to San Antonio River Walk. We stayed at the Homewood Suites and we just loved the hotel. It is located right on the Riverwalk and it was very clean. The breakfast and manager's reception was very good. If you ask for the S. A.V.E rate, the charge is only $99.00 per night. What a bargain! The room was very large with a full size kitchen and seating area. They even had a VCR, so you could bring your own movies to watch. Beds had 3 pillows and were very clean. I was impressed at how nice the room was, after reading some of the other reviews. No need to worry. I would highly recommend this hotel for value and cleanliness. Location was great too! We walked everywhere. No need for a car.

name: Grand Hyatt San Antonio
title: “SERVICE WAS AWESOME!!!”
text:
This hotel is on the river (steps go right down to it) and not far from the RiverCenter Mall (which is GREAT). The hotel is beautiful, the rooms are really clean and nice. The bed and pillows are top of the line and make for a really good night sleep. But the best thing about this hotel is the service from its employees. We had one very minor problem while there and Andrew MacPherson at the fron desk fixed it right away. Andrew checked us in promptly and efficiently. Andrew is the type of employee you want to help all your guests. He made us feel very welcome and answered all our questions about the area. Will definitely stay there again. 
J. O'Brien
Lawrenceville, GA

name: Grand Hyatt San Antonio
title: “A good option for san antonio, make sure your room has wireless connectivity”
text:
My first visit to san Antonio & the hotel chosen by the conference organisers (I usually stay in Starwood properties).
Location fine, next to the conference centre and one end of the riverwalk.
This is a fairly new hotel and has a great ambience, valet & check in were easy and quick and the deluxe room nicely appointed with good views. However, I discovered that the wireless connectivity only worked at one end (the door and toilet end) of the room, not at the desk or bed. I complained & it is clear that this is a known issue and that rooms at ends of the corridors are most affected. This is so easy to fix I'm amazed it hasn't been.
We ate breakfast in the restaurant & the buffet and service was good. The bar is okay, but not well laid out & the music is too loud for conversation.
Small, but nice pool and sun lounger area.

name: Hilton Palacio del Rio
title: “Great Stay at this Riverwalk Hotel”
text:
Stayed here last week for a few nights and I might say that this is a nice hotel...
The hotel is located right on the Riverwalk and has great views from either side of the hotel..
Pros: 5th floor Pool and Hotub with great views of the Riverwalk and City...
 Alamo is a mere 2 block walk
 Rivercentre Mall is a mere 1 block away
 Countless Riverwalk Restuarants located all within walking distance
 Children's Museum located about 5-10 minute walk
Cons: Not much to say, however annoying motion light in closest that would go on everytime you walked in the room or at night if having to use bathroom...
I also want to mention, they have a SmartUse Elevator...at every floor you basically touch the touchscreen as to where you want to go and it tells you what door "A,B,C,D" to go to..pretty straight forward...
The fitness centre is not 24 hours and the pool is only open till 10pm and they lock the door right on the dot....
The restaurant used normally for breakfast is closed currently so you can't eat breakfast on the riverwalk, but instead have it at "Stetsons" which is indoors and a little different feel but still suitable for breakfast..
The customer service at the hotel was incredible and everyone went above and beyond to help you out with any questions you had...
Would stay there again...

name: The St. Anthony Riverwalk, A Wyndham Hotel
title: “Definately Historic”
text: The lobby is very nice when you walk in. The rooms aren't terrible but very outdated. The bathrooms are probably the worst I've seen in a hotel. Reminded me of an Elementary school bathroom. The knobs on the faucet were old and rusted and very well could have been used by Davey Crockett. I was also charged a $20 upgrade fee for a room with 2 beds. Seemed rediculous to me since the room they had us down for cost more on their website. Road noise was noticeable from our room on an upper level floor. Not a terrible hotel but I wouldn't stay here again.

name: Drury Inn & Suites Riverwalk
title: “Loved the hotel”
text: When my wife and I stayed, it was on a business trip, but we mixed in some fun on the riverwalk! The hotel was wonderful. They closed one of the pools because of rain so that only one was open and it was overcrowded. The exercise facilities were nice. The evening snack time and breakfast was great also.

name: Hotel Valencia Riverwalk
title: “Very nice!”
text: Decor was very different in a good way! Very beautiful, beds were awesome, room was very clean. We loved the location in relation to the Riverwalk.

name: Westin San Diego
title: “Fantastic experience”
text: Stayed here on business as I was in town for a conference. Loved this hotel! Spacious, clean room & bathroom, nice shower, plenty of counter space in the bathroom. Bed was super-comfortable, liked the work desk with ample, accessible plug ins. The HVAC system in the room is very quiet. The hotel in general was extremely quiet during my three-night stay. Used the complimentary airport shuttle both coming and going and it was perfect. Didn't try any of the restaurants on the property as I wanted to explore the Gaslamp Quarter for dining. All the staff I encountered were courteous, helpful, and very friendly. I highly recommend this hotel.

name: Grand Hyatt San Antonio
title: “Superb Hotel”
text: great room, clean, not crowded, requested ot have a end of the hallway room, got it, pool floor, excellent, couldnt get on the pool it was after 10pm, time it closes, great view form terrace at this same level. pizza downstairs 24hrs was excellent for a cheap quick meal,

name: Westin San Diego
title: “Juan Verduzco”
text: We had the pleasure of dining in the restaurant every morning during our stay. Juan was personable and gracious with us. He gave us great attention and advise as to where to visit and what to do. We truly had a grand experience during our breakfast our in the restaurant and with Juan.

name: San Diego Marriott Marquis & Marina
title: “Great Location”
text:
Fantastic & friendly staff. Super views of the harbour, easy access to areas of interest in/around San Diego. Close to international airport & shopping. 
Rooms were very clean & of good size. Overall good value

name: Hampton Inn San Antonio - Northwoods
title: “Forget the "Luxury" Hotels - This is the place!”
text: This is a very nice, clean and new property with all of the typical Hampton Inn amenities - great breakfast, free parking, free high-speed Internet, etc. BUT, the best part was the friendliness of the staff, especially in accomodating my early arrival. Everyone from the front desk to the maids and maintenance workers were the friendliest folks I have even encountered in my numerous years of traveling. With easy access to the rooms, this hotel outshines other so-called luxury hotels in minimizing the hassles of travel.

name: The Menger Hotel
title: “Hotel The Historic Menger : service et confort décevants”
text:
Bien que l'hôtel bénéficie d'une situation exceptionnelle sur le plan touristique (au milieu où tout se passe!), je ne le recommande pas : Il manque de service, de confort et de personnel professionnel.
Les intérieurs (le hall d'entrée et la salle à manger) sont très jolis, mais les chambres sont extrèmement bruyantes (sans parler des chambres en face du viel ascenceur!).
Si vous cherchez du calme, du confort et un service professionnel, allez ailleurs!
Pour le même prix, vous trouverez beaucoup mieux!!!!

name: Hotel Valencia Riverwalk
title: “Great location, Good Size Rooms”
text: Location is key when we travel and this hotel was located close to all the nearby must-see attractions. You don't need a car if you are staying at this hotel and if you only intend on staying in the City. If you do rent a car which we did because we spent the day up in Austin and near by Helotes TX. The Valet was very accommodating with extremely friendly. The Hotel was very trendy and also cozy. The room was clean, modern with high ceilings and were larger than standard rooms------either that or the way they set the rooms up appeared that way. We were a bit nervous because the reviews we read on trip advisor were 50/50, but we were very happy staying here. The Staff was friendly overall and it did seem very busy and full as there was a San Antonio Fiesta which I don't recommend going during that time. (TOO CROWDED). The Hotel staff was great given its full capacity of guest. They have a wonderful very trendy bar that was great for relaxing after being out on the town. We found the Hotel to be very nice and would highly recommend it to family & friends visiting San Antonio.

name: The St. Anthony Riverwalk, A Wyndham Hotel
title: “Incredible experience!”
text: My 30 students and I had an etiquette class there in one of the banquet rooms. The hotel is so beautiful, we were all amazed at the art, furniture, and the chandeliers. We had our instruction with a banquet lunch. The food was absolutely delicious. The staff was welcoming and very helpful. We would definitely have another class there.

name: Grand Hyatt San Antonio
title: “Nice hotel away from the crowds”
text:
The concierge level staff was warm and friendly and we enjoyed breakfast and an early dinner drink on the 23rd floor daily during our stay. We were in San Antonio for 9 days (5 nights at this hotel) and although the rooms are quite comfortable, they are built for someone on business staying no more than 2 nights. There are only 2 tiny drawers, which were not large enough for any type of clothing. Everyone in our group commented on the lack of space for clothes. 
The hotel is connected to the Riverwalk and is on the quiet end, fortunately. In two minutes you can be at the mall and restaurants without having to go to the street level and find your way along the one way streets.
It is a large hotel, but we didn't feel crowded during our stay.

name: Grand Hyatt San Antonio
title: “Nice hotel, great location”
text:
We stayed at this hotel during the FBLA convention, which was being held in the convention center next door, and the hotel across the street. As someone who was not competing, however, I was also pleased with the proximity of the hotel to the river walk, La Villita, the Rivercenter mall, and the Alamo. A branch of the river walk is adjacent to the hotel, and also reaches into the mall. The Alamo is a 5-10 minute walk, at most. Also, the Alamodome is about 15 minutes away on foot.
The hotel itself is nice, and the staff are friendly and helpful. The rooms were comfortable. The fitness center was incredible - several cardio machines of varying types, and a sizeable weight room area. They also provide headphones to use as you do cardio, since each of the machines has its own TV/radio built in. The view is also nice, the entire workout area is glass-enclosed. 
It is a bit expensive to travel to/from the airport by taxi (~$30), but there is also a shuttle (not hotel specific) that is around $17. As another reviewer mentioned, the elevators were overwhelmed most of the time by the convention attendees, which was a bit frustrating. Other than that, though, the hotel was great!

name: Westin San Diego
title: “Beautiful View - Nice Room”
text:
I enjoyed the view from the 20th floor, which was overlooking the bay. (A photo is attached.) The room was comfortable, clean, like you'd expect from a Westin. The closet is a bit small, and like most hotels these days, pre-stocked with too much crap to allow you store much in them (Blanket, pillow, safe, ironing board, iron, luggage jack, etc.)
I really appreciated the work desk with numerous outlets, but the chair doesn't go high enough to make the whole scenario functional. I'm typing uphill at the moment.
The lobby is very nice with dramatic two story escalators. The service is excellent here. And the food that I've sampled was quite good!

name: San Diego Marriott Marquis & Marina
title: “Comfy Enough but the Train is LOUD”
text:
I stayed here on business in early June, 2007. This is a typical 1980s refurbished Marriott business/resort hotel. Rooms have been upgraded with comfy beds and new furniture, but not new windows. Common areas are nice, LC's restaurant was decent for breakfast. This is a large double-tower hotel with a lovely pool area and pretty harbor view. The drawbacks are as follows: 1) By far and away the noise from the BNSF freight trains that come through at all hours of the day and night is horrible and will blow you out of bed. Even staying on the bay side view of the hotel will not eliminate the sound (here is my comment on the Windows -- Marriott really needs to upgrade them to make them more soundproof as they are visibly old!!). Bring earplugs. I understand that the trains are an enormous local problem in downtown San Diego for residents, who are organizing an appeal to create a rail quiet zone (a great idea!) to solve this problem. 2) Parking at the Marriott is expensive, and the self-park garage was $20 per day to park a major distance away. Plus there are aren't enough spaces. 
The staff was pretty nice, and kept apologizing for the train noise -apparently everyone complains about this. I would not stay here again for this reason, but I would stay at other Marriott hotels as I have had good experiences with many of them.

name: Westin San Diego
title: “Nice hotel nice location”
text: The first floor including the front desk area was a construction zone. The front desk was on fold up tables. I felt overcharged for the $32 cost of parking. Because of the shape of the building the rooms are oddly shaped. The tv was about 15' from the foot of the bed. Room was very clean and they had Starbucks coffee in the room. Short walk to the harbor and gaslamp district.

name: Hyatt Wild Oak Ranch
title: “Fabulous Place ....we will return~”
text: Stayed 3 nights for the first time this past month and have nothing but great things to say about our stay! Check in was easy, we requested a first floor room with high chair and play pen and our requests were all handled. We also requested a late check out that was accomodated as well. Room was clean and noise was never an issue (we were right across from the ice machine and never heard it). Resturant was a little high on some of their premium drinks and our baby had black feet and legs from crawling (which means the carpet was dirty) but those were the only two issues and they will not keep us from making this our #1 getaway annually! Make sure you take plenty of sand/water toys and plan to spend most of your time here because everything you need is right here!

name: Omni La Mansion del Rio
title: “All that we hoped”
text:
I know this review is a little late in coming. We stayed at La Mansion between Christmas and New Year's for our 30th anniversary. I like historic hotels and we wanted to see the lights on the River Walk. Everything was perfect. I had read some of the reviews that stated River Walk rooms had trees that blocked their view so when I made the reservation I requested that it be an unobstructed view and let them know it was our anniversary. We got exactly what we wanted. We also booked a package that included valet parking, breakfast, and a river tour. 
It is right on the River Walk and we were there during a holiday so we expected it to be noisey but it wasn't so noisey that is bothered us. We checked-out the day of the Alamo bowl so during our stay at any moment one of the college bands or Pep squads could break out in a song or cheer right across or under our balcony. All of this actually enhanced our experience and while I know the hotel didn't put this on just for us if you want a exceptionally quiet place this is not for you. We however loved it all!
Because it rained one day of our stay we decided to try out the restaurant/bar for lunch. We enjoyed it and would definitely eat there again. 
Service everywhere was excellent.
Thank you La Mansion del Rio

name: Marriott Plaza San Antonio
title: “Not a great experience”
text: My daughter and I stayed here in March 2004. The lobby area is beautiful and peaceful. We had a room that faced the courtyard on the 2nd floor, and we were woken up at 4:00 AM by the screeching of the exotic birds. I went to the front desk that morning and asked for a different room. The staff thought I was nuts I think, and they did not extend themselves all that much to help. I was told that the noise would reach us no matter what room they placed us in around the courtyard. We ended up with a room that faced the parking lot. On the next 2 mornings our stay, we were woken up by the loud plumbing noises issuing from adjoining rooms. All in all, this was not worth the $199.00/night we paid for our room. If you are a very heavy sleeper then this is the place for you.

name: Hotel Valencia Riverwalk
title: “Best hotel experience to date!”
text: Outstanding service and courteous staff. Great and prompt room service. Delicious food. Will stay there again.

name: Hotel Indigo San Antonio At The Alamo
title: “Great Hotel Treated as Royality”
text: Not enough can be said about this hotel. Rooms were all clean and had no problems. Some rooms might be small but if you understand that this is a historical building where they were very limited on what they can do when building it. I like that every room I went into was different with original wood floors. Parking we did not need but it was not any different than any other hotel you would find in a downtown metro area. The staff is Awesome, Cruz and his staff really did a spectacular job taking care of everyone in our group. Even going above and beyond what we ever expected. The Bistro had great food and drinks and even live entertainment on Saturday night. Even if you are not staying in at the hotel stop in and have a bite to eat. Hope we are able to return to this Hotel again.

name: The St. Anthony Riverwalk, A Wyndham Hotel
title: “GORGEOUS Hotel but....”
text:
We stayed at this gorgeous hotel while attending my son's graduation from Air Force Technical School at Brooks City-Base. My family has stayed here before, and recommended it highly. First night in the hotel, there was a boxing something or other in town, and we were placed amongst the boxers, who I guess didn't realize there were other guests on the floor. The noise was overwhelming, and the yelling, shouting, laughing, and slamming doors went on till well after midnight. We called down to the front desk twice and asked them to please tend to the ridiculous atmosphere going on, but the response by the security staff was ineffective. I went down to the front desk the next morning to comment on the situation, and specifically asked the front desk person if the same "guests" were going to be staying the next night. I was assured they were checking out that afternoon. Hallelujah! However, the next night we got more of the same, as the front desk had booked more hellions into the room next door. Security was called, not by me this time, at 11:30pm, but again, was ineffective. I finally called down around 1am, but there was nothing done. The party lasted well on to about 230am. I spoke to the front desk on the way out the next morning, and asked to speak to the manager, but was told she didn't come in till "around nine or so". I found that so infuriating I could not bring myself to finish my conversation with the employee at the front desk, except to tell him that we WILL NOT return to the St. Anthony.
 I guess with the economy being what it is, they have lowered their standards too far, with the result being the more well-heeled clientele is being driven out. These idiots causing the trouble should never have been at this hotel...they were more worthy of a Days Inn or Motel 6. How they ended up at this gorgeous property is a sin. Until The St. Anthony figures out how to keep these hooligans out of its property, we won't be back.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites San Antonio Downtown
title: “Our San Antonio Trip”
text: We loved our stay at the La Quinta Inn and Suites Downtown. Everyone was very kind and helpful and they are also very pet friendly. The only thing that would have made our stay perfect would have been a larger coffee maker in our suite.

name: Crockett Hotel
title: “Excellent Hotel thru management by Eduardo Alcantar”
text:
It would take too much space to complement the hotel. Friendly staff, nice rooms, very reasonable rates and above all a friendly, personable and knowledgeable manager, Eduardo Alcantar.
Will return.

name: Sheraton Gunter Hotel San Antonio
title: “Don't bother”
text: We were in San Antonio for my birthday. We are platinum members of SPG and are used to good Starwood service. On check in we were up graded to a suite and the room was large but somewhat dated in decor. When we went in the bathroom we found a very unusual amenity EARPLUGS. They were very needed, we were on the corner and the bus noise went on all night. Never in 22 years did we find such a terrible uproar in a hotel room even in airports with jets taking off. It didn't help that there was a terrible thunderstorm which chimed in all night. I looked at the windows and they were single pane which is unbelievable in a downtown location. This makes me think that management does not care. This was truly a suite which was totally terrible. The lounge is a nice touch. The attendants were friendly and there was FREE WINE ( CHAR-CAB-ZIN) AND BEER (CORONA-HEINEKEN- AMERICAN) They had cheese and hot appetizers with 2 desserts. It is probably worth it to upgrade to use the lounge if you keep one eye closed. We were up the next morning and went to lounge for breakfast (continental) and noticed that the floor was filthy. It had not been vacuumed from the night before. We went in the bathroom and it was like a gas station freeway bathroom. The waste basket was overflowing, they had cloth hand towels that were filthy and the sink was brown with stains. It had not been cleaned. I told the attendant and they locked the door. If the lounge is this dirty on the outside I can only wonder what the food prep area we can't see is like. This little care for cleaning was evident through out the hotel. We had two bathrooms and in one the toilet had brown all over the bottom of the bowl and dirt under the rim. There were cob webs in the windows and the halls were littered with pieces and paper and waste. At the front desk at check out there was garbage in front of the check out desk. It was the dirtiest hotel we had seen in a long time. We were told that the toilet were stained but who wants stained toilets whether it is rust or other. We moved to the Westin and it was like night and day. The Gunter is a historic old property but it could be clean. NO EXCUSES FOR FILTH! Also get an inside room because the outside room with single pane glass are very noisy. They could easily fix this problem by inserting double pane panels in the inside casing of the windows. I was told by management that that they could correct the problem because it would cost $5000 per window. So they continue to put people in bus station rooms and expect them to sleep.

name: Hyatt Wild Oak Ranch
title: “An oasis in the middle of a busy tourist area.”
text:
It felt like home. Families come back here every year...and I know why.
Rooms are like private homes. Everything you need except food. And they have a program to deliver that too. But there's an heb grocery & walmart not far, so I recommend them first.
Quiet, a lazy river w/ movie nights & cone anytime cabanas at no charge scattered throughout the river. Indoor/out door pool w/waterslides at both. Your chikd will need to be about 6yrs old to use them.
Walking paths, smores nights, craft times, and free shuttle to hyatt hill country up the road makr this placeone we will return to again.

name: Crockett Hotel
title: “Overall good hotal”
text:
PROS - Great location, nice updated rooms, great breakfast included.
CONS - Front desk a little disorganized and slow.

name: San Diego Marriott Marquis & Marina
title: “Beautiful Bay Views”
text:
From our 23rd floor bay-view room in the North Tower, we observed the sweeping Coronado Bridge, the picturesque Island of Coronado, the marina, and passing ships--a photographer's smorgasbord. We have admired these scenes in calendars and travel magazines in the past. Now, here we were, celebrating our wedding anniversary and enjoying a room location recommended by previous Trip Advisors.
The hotel has several noteworthy qualities; some are highlighted as follows:
1. Striking architecture and lush landscaping. An almond-shaped tower and its neighboring concave-curved tower, both with dark, reflective glass, are unique to San Diego's skyline.
2. Comfortable and clean guest rooms. We appreciated the bed with six pillows; sofa, chair, and coffee table; and a small refrigerator. The spotless bathroom had thick towels and ample sundries.
3. Variety of food service. We enjoyed the full buffet breakfast at LC's in the North Tower and salads and sandwiches for lunch at the Yacht Club Restaurant. Tasty and generous room-service meals for dinner were delivered in 30 minutes.
4. Hotel maintenance. We made one phone call to the hotel operator to report our broken desk lamp. It was repaired in an hour.
5. Reservations and registration. We called the hotel directly to reserve our senior-rate room. Upon arrival we received everything for which we had asked, and the staff made us feel like welcome guests.
Other comments:
1. We arrived when there was a great deal of activity at the city's convention center next door. We were caught in the wrong traffic lane for hotel registration and spent 20 minutes to correct our error.
2. Valet parking cost $25 per day for hotel guests. With all of the activity, we were grateful to use the services of a polite and helpful vehicle attendant.
3. There was loud music from a nearby outdoor amphitheatre on both Sunday and Monday evenings. This could be a positive for some. However, we prefer selecting our own music and listening when we choose to do so. When we closed the balcony door and drapery, the sound was mitigated but could still be heard in the room.
Conclusion
Overall, we appreciated the location, comfort, cleanliness, and service of the hotel. We will not forget the views from our upper floor bay-view room, and we thank previous Trip Advisors for the recommendation.

name: Sheraton Gunter Hotel San Antonio
title: “"Better-Than-Perfect" !!!”
text: I'm unsure if dictionaries describe something as "Better-Than-Perfect". If not, then stay at the Sheraton-Gunter Hotel, San Antonio to live it. All Hotel Associates were supremely attentive and all smiles to all of our needs. We shall return to the Gunter, often.

name: Crockett Hotel
title: “One of the Worst”
text:
We stayed at the Crockett Hotel as part of an Elderhostel group. There was mold on the ceiling and bathroom tiles, the carpet and spread were musty, the towel rack fell off the wall, the sink was cracked, and ... because there were no fitted sheets ... the bed kept coming unmade, the mattress pad bunched up, and it made sleeping very uncomfortable.
I would strongly suggest you consider other accommodations.

name: Omni La Mansion del Rio
title: “GREAT experience!”
text:
My husband and I came to San Antonio for our anniversary, and stayed here on the recommendation of a friend. We LOVED this hotel. I chose the rejuvenation package, which included a spa credit, free valet parking and breakfast. I highly recommend trying to find a package that includes parking, as the valet is quite expensive, but very convenient. I could take or leave the spa...it felt a little snooty, but the girl who did my nails was sweet and very good.
Our room was on the first floor, literally next door to the Riverwalk entrance. It was a tad noisy at times because people were constantly walking by, but the location was SUPER convenient. We ate across the river, and I was able to run to the room to use the restroom, then return to my table :) The room was very cool, and very nice. 
We ordered room service for breakfast, and it was okay. It looked really good, but I would say the actual taste was average. You sure did get a lot of food, though!
The staff was prompt and friendly, and we did very little waiting for any kind of service. Everything was prepared for us upon arrival, and they even sent an e-mail when our room was ready.
I would highly recommend this hotel! It is very nice, convenient, and has great history! It's hard to find a cheap rate, but you definitely get what you pay for! Getting a good package at least gives you more bang for your buck. I was very glad to pay a little more to get almost $250 in extras!! 
For those who care about the pool - it is beautiful, but kind of small and in a cramped space. I didn't really care because we were mostly out and about, but some might want to know.
P.S. If you stay here and like ice cream, Justin's Ice Cream shop across the river is the best ice cream I have ever had in my life! He will let you sample everything!! They have gelato, sherbet, ice cream and yogurt. Mmmmm......we went there twice!

name: Hotel Indigo San Antonio At The Alamo
title: “Great Stay”
text:
I checked in on a Tuesday and was upgraded to a suite. The staff was very friendly and had great advice on local eateries. The rooms were clean and modern.
The location was the best part, it is a stones throw from the Alamo. It also had easy access to the river walk & a public bike station. We recommend making a visit out to the Pearl Brewery area for a more upscale dining experience.
In the evening the downsides are the street level noise & the park in front of the Alamo has a few homeless people. It's not a concern during the day; use common sense and travel as group in the evenings & you'll have no problems. That goes for any bigger city, though.

name: Grand Hyatt San Antonio
title: “Stayed here for NYE, enjoyed it”
text:
I used Hyatt points for this stay, and we stayed 2 nights for NYE.
The hotel was really nice, the bar was comfortable and pretty fun. The room was a good size, and we had a great view over San Antonio.
The hotel is in a good location, with the riverwalk being very close by. It was a good stay, although I still don't appreciate having to pay $25 a day to self park!
Overall, we had a good time, the hotel staff were friendly and made us dinner reservations. I would go back.

name: Drury Inn & Suites Riverwalk
title: “it was the Best Hotel that we have ever stayed in!!!”
text:
WOW!! 
the staff was so amazing!!!! so friendly !!!! 
bed was so comfortable!
so clean!!
I can not say enough good things!!!

name: Hilton Palacio del Rio
title: “Fool me once...I can't get fooled again!”
text: Poor experience from start to finish. We were told after a long day of travel that room service was available until midnight. (It was 11:30.) Upon calling room service a few minutes later, we were informed they only had desserts. When I called the front desk to ask them, the phone service cut me off. Twice. It was downhill from there. Air conditioning wasn't working properly, there was some kind of repair or remodeling going on somewhere close to my room, because I could hearing the drilling and hammering very clearly EARLY the next morning. The best part was probably when the maintenance worker walked into my room while was in bed. I did speak with the manager who gave me my money back, and I moved over to the Westin La Cantera, which is a much, MUCH better hotel for about the same rate. Most likely will not be staying here ever again.

name: Hotel Valencia Riverwalk
title: “Beautiful hotel and exceptional service”
text: My husband and I had a chance to stay at the Hotel Valencia in San Antonio this April. We were there to attend some dear friends of ours wedding and reception. We actually live in San Antonio, but thought it would be a nice night out to stay overnight at the Valencia. We are glad that we did have the opportunity to stay , as well as attend our friends' wedding and reception at the hotel. The wedding and reception were held at the hotel's courtyard area, which was absolutely beautiful. It had an outdoor water fountain/with cascading water, with a fire lit in front of it and candles surrounding it with a very southwestern/spanish style influence to it. The service from the staff was exceptional during the reception. There were delicious appetizers served, an open bar, and a wonderful dinner and dessert catered by the hotel's restaurant. Our room was very clean and had all the modern conveniences and then some. It was a very hip and contemporary room. Matter of fact, the entire hotel from the lobby to the presidental suite that our friends stayed in for the night, was all very swanky and had a classic elegance to it. The hotel's bar called V-bar was a very fun night out after the reception. It was not overcrowded, had sort of a intimate setting with lounge like sitting and decor and a great d.j. to play a variety of music. We are looking forward to another stay at the Hotel Valencia very soon.

name: Sheraton Gunter Hotel San Antonio
title: “Great location, Wonderful service.”
text: I stayed at the Gunter for a few nights in April and I was very pleased with my overall stay. The hotel is historical with the lobby and certain elements in the hotel that display its heritage. The rooms are updated, clean and comfortable. While the bathrooms are on the small side I still found them well appointed and functionable. The staff was extremely accommodating and friendly--always willing to go the extra mile to make your stay more hospitable. The hotel is just a few steps to the local Starbucks and riverwalk and only a few blocks to the sites such as the Alamo, Majestic theatre, city hall and more.

name: Comfort Suites Near Seaworld
title: “Just Like Home!”
text: This was an awesome hotel. My husband and I loved the convenience of sea world, restaurants, and family. I would recommend this motel to all.

name: Four Points by Sheraton San Antonio Downtown
title: “Nice hotel, excellent staff”
text: This is a great location, short walk from the river walk area. Room was very nice with two beds and a separate sofa area. The staff really made this hotel five star. We arrived late Friday night and checked in quickly. Went up to the room and the guests in the room next door were extremely loud. We went back down and asked if it was possible to change rooms - the front desk woman smiled and changed our room without any issue. The staff continued to be friendly and accommodating throughout our stay. I highly recommend this hotel.

name: Four Points by Sheraton San Antonio Downtown
title: “Good hotel for the price”
text: Clean hotel. Needs more parking. Breakfast was a little expensive.

name: Staybridge Suites San Antonio Sea World
title: “They made us feel welcome....”
text: The hotel made us feel welcome and it was very clean. The arrival process was very good and smooth. It was wonderful experience, heated swimming, free hot breakfast...the room was impecable and had everything we nneded for our stay. It was a great experience. The employess were nice and accomodated to our needs.

name: Drury Inn & Suites Riverwalk
title: “Loved Our Experience at Drury Inn & Suites!”
text: We have stayed in San Antonio before at another hotel, but this one was much more reasonably priced with more extras. Had a small problem with our air conditioner when we first checked in and they switched our rooms, no questions asked. Very clean and wonderfully located on the Riverwalk. The free breakfast, calls, snacks, and locality definitely made our vacation much more enjoyable.

name: Hilton Palacio del Rio
title: “Cockroaches all over the balcony!”
text: Our first night we went out on the balcony and cockroaches were running all over the balcony. We complained and was told this was Texas. Carpeting warn, Shower had mold. Disgusting for the prices they charge. This on top of NO free internet and $22 a night parking

name: Grand Hyatt San Antonio
title: “Was nice and Convenient”
text:
The hotel was very nice and right on the River Walk . It was great for shopping. The rooms were very nice and clean. The pool area was small and there were a lot of small children
so we opted not to try to swim. The bar area had people "lounging" I mean actually laying down on some of the furniture( which seemed to have a lot of wear and tear.) I would stay there again...the staff was friendly and the valet parking although expensive was well worth the money.

name: Omni La Mansion del Rio
title: “Excellent Hotel In Superior Location”
text: Stayed here on emergency basis for second and third nights of a three day business trip after a very bad experience at another downtown San Antonio hotel (see my other review). Beautiful hotel, friendly staff, superb location, at a fair price. I will definitely book this hotel first on return trips to San Antonio.

name: Four Points by Sheraton San Antonio Downtown
title: “Fist class service!!!!”
text: I felt right at home. Will definitely be my first choice on my next trip to San Antonio, TX

name: Hyatt Wild Oak Ranch
title: “Another Great Visit to Wild Oak Ranch!”
text: Just back from another stay at the Wild Oak Ranch. Our first stay was for this past July 4th holiday. It is a wonderful place to take a quick resort vacation. However, with young kids, I do wish there were lifeguards at the pools. It would also be nice to have a restroom closer to the Lazy River pool. There are 2 slides, one at the indoor pool and one at the outdoor pool. We noticed that there was no attendant manning the slides and there were 2 boys (one clearly less than the minimum 48 inch height requirement) that were sliding down at the same time. After awhile, Hyatt attendants did come around and made sure that the kids sliding down had the armband that signified they met the height requirement. During non-summer months, it looks like the outdoor movie night is only on one night (either Fri or Sat?) and on non-weekend nights, the only on-site restaurant closes at 7:00p. It does serve the full menu for dinner now and not just appetizers and pizza like it did during our first stay in July. We had a 2-bedroom unit which was a dedicated 2 bedroom unit and not a 1-bedroom lock-off with a studio. The master bedroom/kitchen/living area was very similar to the 1-bedroom unit we had in July but the master bathroom in the 2-bedroom unit was private (no hall access) and was much wider. The bedroom with the king sized bed seemed the same size. The second bedroom had 2 beds (sleeps 4) and a very large closet. Each bedroom had its own TV and the living room has a large plasma TV and DVD player. The living/kitchen/entry areas of the 2-bedroom unit also seemed slightly larger than the 1-bedroom unit. The property seems to be well maintained and I recognized many of the employees from our first stay.

name: San Diego Marriott Marquis & Marina
title: “Beste Lage zum Konferenzzentrum”
text: Das Hotel liegt direkt neben dem Kongresszentrum. Einige der Veranstaltungen unseres Kongresses fanden sogar in Räumen des Marriott statt. Starbucks im Eingangsbereich vorhanden. Ein grosser gewundener Hotelpool is aussen vorhanden, daran angeschlossen eine Sauna (die für deutsche Verhältnisse aber eher als Warmraum denn als Sauna zu bezeichnen ist).

name: Westin San Diego
title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text: We love Westin. They are pet friendly so we can take our two small dogs which helps make our time away more enjoyable. This hotel is in a ideal location. You can park the car and walk to many of the best restaurants, Hoton Plaza, Little Italy (we went for Art Walk) and many other great San Diego attractions. Staff is friendly and accomodating. Highly recommend this hotel.

name: Omni La Mansion del Rio
title: “Very Nice”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the hotel on vacation during the month of June. Out of all the Omni hotels we’ve visited, this one was the best. The room was clean and included a mini-bar and a 32 inch flat panel TV. All rooms have a balcony however most are shared / common space. The hotel sits on the river walk not far from all the famous restaurants and attractions. Across the street is the famous Majestic Theater so catch a play if you’re in town. Also across the river walk is the River Boat Cruise and Hard Rock Café. 
I have only three complaints about this hotel.
1) The elevators are too slow for a hotel of this size.
2) On our departure it took thirty minutes for the bellman to arrive
3) The hotel valet parking is too high ($30 per night + Tips)
My advice if you stay – park across the street in the city garage for only $7 per day.

name: Hilton Palacio del Rio
title: “Dirty room and floating bath tub”
text:
I've stayed here before and they couldn't have been nicer. On this visit however, everyone except the valet was "cranky"/ rude. There are plenty of places to stay and this isn't the best bargain to be had.
The carpet is soiled and we found bits of paper like confetti around the floor. The bathtub, feels like a plastic tub was placed inside the real bathtub and it was bumpy and made my standing in the tub not secure.
The internet was not working properly and I had to hunt around the room looking for the TV remote (it wasn't next to the TV or the bedside table). The hotel was nearly cleared out from the holidays but I feel like I was given the worst room available.

name: Drury Inn & Suites San Antonio North
title: “Great for families”
text:
This is a great place to stay that is convenient to both downtown or it's less than 30 minute drive to schlitterbahn in addition to being near sea world & fiesta Texas. The breakfasts are great & the afternoon "snacks" we have often used as supper which is such a money
saver for families. The rooms are always very clean & service is fantastic.

name: Hilton Palacio del Rio
title: “Amazing customer service!”
text: The location could not have been any better. We booked last minute and got an amazing rate. The front desk staff was very accommodating. They even gave us a river view room with our low rate! The Bellhop staff let us use their microwave to heat up our dinner from the night before. Everyone on their staff was amazingly helpful and friendly. The hotel was beautiful and it made our trip so relaxing!

name: Holiday Inn San Antonio North-Hill Country
title: “Totally fantastic”
text: Our stay was great. The staff is fantastic to mention the ones I came in the most contact with are Julio, Velma and Melissa. Their service and friendly attitude was second to none. Our breakfast hostess was great also. The rooms are top notch, the food is great and the beer is cold. I have stayed in four hotels Shawn was general manager of, and he always puts a great staff together and the facilities are always well maintained and clean. If you want to be relatively close to Fiesta Texas and a growing part of San Antonio, you should not pass up a chance to stay at this fantastic facility.

name: San Antonio Marriott Rivercenter
title: “The location is on the Riverwalk; the focus is on SERVICE!”
text:
What a terrific Marriott property! As mentioned in the most recent posts, I tip my hat to the Management and staff at the Marriott Rivercenter as the hospitality and service is exemplary. It was obvious to me that this hotel pays attention to every small detail. 
On this topic, Lorrie at the front counter was helpful with restaurant recommendations (don't miss Luciano's as you exit to the rear heading to the patio & Riverwalk), directions and mailing some correspondence for me during my stay. While I didn't catch the name of the breakfast chef, when I mentioned that an omelette description from the menu sounded great, he went back to the kitchen to satisfy my request for chorizo. As I frequently do in Convention locales, I checked out of my room on the final AM, left my luggage with the Bell Captain, conducted my business and returned to the hotel to retrieve my bags and catch a cab to the airport. Joram at the front desk learned that I intended to change into comfortable clothes for flying when I asked the location of the lobby restroom. He instead offered me a "temporary keycard" to access the 4th floor locker and pool area which gave me a comfortable place to change and even take a shower after a long day on my feet. Very thoughtful indeed.
While comfortable and usually accomodating, many of the properties in the Marriott, Hilton and Hyatt genre look alike for the most part and sometimes fail to borrow any style or theme from the city in which they are located. While nothing elegant, my room had a definite Spanish / Southwest look going on which I came to enjoy. 
I will certainly seek out this specific hotel when visiting San Antonio in the future!

name: Home2 Suites by Hilton San Antonio-Downtown/Near the River Walk
title: “Clean, modern, great location”
text:
I stayed here in February 2012 on a conference trip and enjoyed my stay. I would definitely stay here again. 
PROS: 
- Clean and modern (the suite, suite bathroom, lobby, and fitness center were all clean 
 and well kept). This hotel opened in October 2011, so everything's new.:)
- Free wireless
- Small heated pool (my friend enjoyed it). Small but very functional fitness center.
- Excellent location- 1 block from Riverwalk, ~10-minute easy walk to the conference center, 
 felt safe walking around at nighttime.
- Staff was helpful. 
CONS:
- Not a big fan of the cloth shower curtain (gives the bathroom a very, very faint damp and 
 musty smell, but now I'm just being picky.)

name: Sheraton Gunter Hotel San Antonio
title: “Will certainly be back!”
text:
Mr. Harrison,
I would like you to know that I had a great stay and will definitly give the 10 rating when the survey comes in! Staff and accomidations were excellent. I especially enjoyed the bar area with all the wood surroundings and the very excellent bartender. He said he had been there several years. I also enjoyed meeting one of your patrons in the bar. He was an older gentleman (a local lawyer I believe) that comes in a lot according to your bartender. Very interesting character.
Also, I almost forgot.
