One of the young ladies at front desk, I cant remember her name, but anyway she was a great help getting me situated in the business center so I could print out some documents that I needed to get out the same day. She along with another gentleman also helped with getting it Fedex'd out. Many thanks to those people! 
Best regards,
Bill Deshotels
PS: I will definitly try to stay there again on my next trip!

name: Sheraton Gunter Hotel San Antonio
title: “Historic beauty in great location”
text: The Sheraton Gunter Hotel was very convenient for a recent San Antonio stay. It sits on the corner of Houston and St. Mary's streets. The VIA San Antonio streetcar (Red line) stops right out front. The rooms are clean with a clean and simple decor. The hotel staff were friendly and helpful. There is valet parking if you need or want it. I'd say skip the breakfast bar at Barron's restaurant downstairs (the scrambled eggs sat a little too long on the steam table). The hotel is rich in history though -- USAA was founded there and Robert Johnson recorded there. The hotel's old telephone switchboard sits by the elevator bank.

name: Britt Scripps Inn
title: “LOVED IT!!”
text: We have just returned from a 5 night stay and thought this place was excellent. We stayed in the Garden Room and although it didn't look as elegant as the other rooms it was very comfortable and as we overlooked the garden was very quiet. We didn't have a car and although it had excellent access to the park it was quite a walk from the Gaslamp area, which wasn't a problem during the day as it was quite a pleasant walk but we wouldn't have felt comfortable at night. So like when we went to the baseball it meant paying for a taxi which could prove to be quite expensive if you planned to spend your evenings in this area. The breakfasts were brilliant and as I do not eat meat or eggs the granola and the scones we delicious. We really only dealt with Martin during our stay and he was brilliant and nothing was too much trouble. We do not see how you could be disappointed with this place its excellent.

name: Britt Scripps Inn
title: “Details, details, details! This inn got it right! Every thing was perfection---highly recommend.”
text: We were greeted at the door by Martin, who couldn't have been more accommodating. We arrived just in time for evening cheese and wine---delicious! Had beaucoup restaurants to choose from for dinner, as the inn is so convenient to whatever food your heart desires. Our room was absolutely grand and so true to the Queen Anne period. Our breakfast was superb, with Sarah as hospitality host with a capital H! A perfect B&B experience!

name: San Diego Marriott Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Excellent location, outstanding service.”
text:
I stayed here for four days for a conference. I usually stay at the Marriott Marquis but I decided to give the Marriott Gaslamp a try. I'm so happy that I did!
I was greeted by two delightful doorman and a front desk clerk who immediately recognized my Marriott Gold Elite status. She upgraded me to a two-room suite. The furnishings in the room were fine and, as usually, the Marriott bed was incredibly comfortable. The bathroom was clean and well appointed. The room was also quiet.
I ate three breakfasts in the hotel restaurant. The buffet was plentiful, which is typical for Marriott properties. But the best thing about breakfast was the service -- the hostess and servers were exceptionally pleasant.
The hotel's location is excellent. Walking to the convention center, downtown, the Gaslamp Quarter, and the harbor are all quite close. In fact, I walked everywhere during my stay.
The Marriott Gaslamp is now my hotel of choice when I travel to San Diego.

name: Omni La Mansion del Rio
title: “Needs an overhaul”
text: Just returned from a one night stay at this hotel. It is in a very nice location on the riverwalk but it is run down and somewhat dirty. I had reserved a king room with view of river but was given two double beds overlooking the small pool. The room was very run down with worn out carpeting, old bed spreads, sagging mattress and very dreary. The window overlooking the pool opened to a walkway so you had to keep the drapes closed or anyone could look into your room. It was dark and dreary. The tv was about 19inches and very old. As others have said there was little sound proofing so you could hear everyone in the hallway. I was here for a meeting but if I returned I would look elsewhere unless the price was right. The hole place needs fresh paint, new carpet, new tv's, and new mattresses. The bathroom was also small with combined tub/shower. The people were nice and the food at the meeting was slightly above average. If staying at this place I would try and get a view of the riverwalk instead of the pool. It would give you much more privacy. Hope this helps.

name: Westin San Diego
title: “A relaxing breakfast”
text:
Kelly nortan & Juan Verduzca Jr. Gave us great service at breakfast at the Westin hotel. We were tired from the niight before and they kept our coffee hot and serviced our table by keeping our dishes clear. We even asked for a newspaper, and they went and found us one. What a great way to start our day. Good food and service with a newspaper to read.
Thank you! Jan & Lee

name: San Diego Marriott Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Great place to stay right across the street from Petco Park”
text: Am a Marriott Rewards member, but the real attraction was to stay in the same hotel with the visiting SF Giants and attend the baseball series. The hotel is a welcome delight with good rooms and a great lobby level restaurant for breakfast.

name: Country Inn & Suites By Carlson, San Diego North
title: “Consistently good experience leads to my consistent return”
text:
I have been staying here for nearly 5 years on my bi-monthly trips to San Diego. I gave up at Woodfin Suites (new name now) and stayed here based on a very positive experience I had at Country Inn and Suites in Calabasas.
Bed and pillows are the best. The office chair is an Aeron, the best chair ever made for working. The shower heads are great, as is the pressure and the curved shower rod.
For a complimentary breakfast, they have the best. Fresh scrambled eggs NOT diluted with milk or water, bacon or sauage, potatoes or bisquits/gravy, hot fresh oatmeal (not from a bag) fresh cut fruit, 4 kinds of fruit juice including guava juice, fresh muffins, those great DIY Belgian waffles and superior coffee. They serve 1/2 and 1/2 for the coffee.
Kevin B.

name: Hotel Indigo San Antonio At The Alamo
title: “GREAT new hotel”
text: This is a new hotel with a view of the Alamo. it's within walking distance of downtown, river walk, the mall, a trolley that can take you further around San Antonio, and more. The service was superb throughout the hotel. Alex greeted us at the front desk with charm, Michael served us drinks at the hotel bar with stories and extensive knowledge of the area, and the cleaning staff was prompt and thorough. The beds are luxurious, rooms have a flat screen TV with many channels, and each room is unique due to the remodeling of an older hotel. It's a unique mix of history and modern style. I would recommend this hotel to anyone: for business or pleasure, families, couples, or solo travelers.

name: Hotel Indigo San Antonio At The Alamo
title: “Do not use the valet parking!”
text: Do not use the valet parking.....they wrecked our truck and they lied about it....!

name: Country Inn & Suites By Carlson, San Diego North
title: “Great Stay”
text:
We stayed for 2 nights. The room was very clean. The breakfast is great and the parking is free.
The hotel is about 20 minutes from the attractions. We enjoyed out stay. We will stay here again when we visit San Diego.

name: Sheraton Gunter Hotel San Antonio
title: “Charming Historic Hotel”
text: Stayed here for a conference in June 2010 - great rooms and service, and I loved the location so close to the Alamo, historic theater, and the Riverwalk. The catering staff was excellent, and we were so impressed we rebooked our group immediately for the following year. We have high standards for events, and the Sheraton Gunter met them in every way.

name: Hotel Indigo San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “First time to San Diego”
text:
This hotel is beautiful. Especially for the cost! In order to save some money we decided not to have a rental car this trip so we needed a hotel near the heart of everything, including public transportation. 
We found Hotel Indigo on Hotels.com and checked the reviews and customer photographs on tripadvisor.com, there were a few others we were looking at in the area, but we are very happy that we chose Hotel Indigo. When you enter the hotel the lobby is very pretty and modern. There's a lovely seating area with a water wall, the restaurant and bar are just behind it. We didn't eat at the restaurant but we did have a couple of drinks before a game that were delicious. I also used the gym a couple of times it had a decent amount of cardio equipment and even some free weights, the meditation deck was a nice addition as well.
The staff was extremely friendly. When we checked in we were offered a room upgrade for signing up for emails, I really recommend doing this, they have only sent 1 email to us since our trip, and really with spam filters what's the harm. We were upgraded to a city view on a higher floor. We hardly ever have house keeping clean our room while we're in it but the maid left a friendly note under our door letting us know she was around if we needed anything. We also checked out the roof top bar. It had an amazing view of the stadium and super friendly bar tenders. 
Our room was fantastic. We're both fans of modern design and the images available on the hotel's website as well as tripadvisor do not let down. There was a wall of windows floor to ceiling and wall to wall, some actually opened to let in the cool breezes. The king sized bed was fairly comfortable with lots of pillows. The bathroom was large and nicely decorated with a walk in shower. 
The area was fantastic, lots and lots an lots to do within walking distance. Great restaurants, a mall, and lots of boutiques. We walked to the Amtrak station, only 1 mile away, one day to take the train up to Anaheim for the day to go to Disneyland and another baseball game. 
People on here complained about dogs, rude service, and other noise. The other complaints made by cheapskates I can't say anything about. Buyer beware, and read the small print, and all that. The other things I can speak to. I was a little nervous about the dog policy, my husband is not a fan of dogs, but honestly I never heard or saw a single one during the week we were there. To be as straight forward as possible, San Diego is a VERY dog friendly town, they let dogs into Petco Park for all the baseball games and everything. We saw dogs everywhere we went, if you are afraid of dogs or they annoy you maybe you should plan a vacation elsewhere. As for the hotel staff, I thought they were amazing. Never pushy, always polite, and even fun to talk with. I work in customer service, it's something I have very little patience with if it's bad, and I wasn't bothered by anyone. As for street noise, it's a city, and it's no where near as noisy as NYC, people walk around they make noise. I really didn't find it that bad, but there was street noise. Maybe if you're used to absolute quiet at night time you should bring along a pair of ear plugs.
Overall we'd stay there again, we're actually planning on possibly going to San Diego again next summer. The city is gorgeous and there's so much to see and do we didn't manage to fit it all in during this one trip. We're already planning on staying at Hotel Indigo again :) 
Happy Travels!

name: Residence Inn San Diego Downtown/Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Great Service!”
text:
Nicki at the front desk started our visit out with a smile and never stopped amazing us with her personality and kindness. We were allowed to check in early and shortly after checking in we received a knock at the door with a personalized letter welcoming us and wishing me a happy birthday with her desire to hear all about our adventures.
The valets were very personable, and nice. Each of the employees that we encountered took the time to say hello. The breakfast crew in the mornings were efficient and welcoming as well.
The breakfast offered something for everyone with hot and cold dishes available.
The pool area was nice, although there is no jacuzzi.
The rooms were very nice, but the sliding doors of the bathrooms were able to be heard from one room to another. The sink area was more suited to a single person.
the kitchen was well equipped and even came with microwave popcorn.
The location was perfect for exploring Gaslamp, the Embarcadero and Seaport Village.
Overall, this was a fabulous experience with a lot of it due to Nicki and her warm and inviting welcome!

name: Hotel Indigo San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Fantastic!”
text:
Usually when we book through Hotwire we get the same hotels. This time, however, we were given the Hotel Indigo. I'll admit, we were a little apprehensive at first because we had not heard a lot about this hotel. Upon doing some research, we found that they are a pet friendly hotel. This meant two things to us...one that we could bring our four-legged family member if we chose to and two...usually pet friendly hotels have that "pet friendly odor" in the rooms. That really worried us. We decided just to go with it and we took our dog, and decided that if it was that bad we would find something else when we got to San Diego. 
To our complete surprise it was wonderful! The staff was so friendly throughout our entire stay. The room was very clean and fresh smelling..not even a trace of pet odor. We found out after we got there that this is San Diego's only LEED certified hotel. This may not mean much to you but it does to my husband who is an architect. This, simply put, means that they built a hotel that cares about the environmental health of its customers. This is a main reason that the hotel is as clean and fresh as it is. Both our room and bathroom were very large and comfortable. Only thing missing in the room was a small refrigerator. It is always nice to have something to keep cold water in. On the 9th floor there is an outside patio bar that overlooks Petco Park and around the corner from that there is a very nice area of grass for pets, they even provide the "potty bags". It is kept very clean and is accessible at all times, you just have to call the front desk to have someone meet you to let you out after dark. You do not have to take your pet out and walk the streets during the evening/night. We did eat at the restaurant one evening and it was very good and our server was super nice. The only complaint is that it closes so early. Location is great, just a couple blocks down from the main Gaslamp District. Nice walk. Parking is valet so no problem there. 
Overall, we had a great trip and would definitely stay there again. Thank you to the staff for an enjoyable vacation. :)

name: Hyatt Regency Hill Country Resort and Spa
title: “Worth a visit!”
text: Spent our anniversary weekend there. Good facility, great service. Check in was quite smooth. Front staff was very courteous. We didn't like the room and asked for another one. Staff was more than willing to offer us another room. They were kind enough to upgrade us to a junior suite, which was quite spacious, with a huge balcony. Room service was efficient, food quality was just ok. Same with the restaurants.. service was awesome but food was not exceptional. In fact, I got really sick after eating the Blue Cheese Burger and threw up during the better half of the Sat night! My husband loved his steak! Spa facility was small and the attendants and the spa front staff were not friendly at all. Golf area was very nice. Two heated pools and a lazy river. Well maintained pool area. Too bad it was freezing so we didn't try the outdoor pools. Free bike rentals but the bike route actually takes you around the whole facility and is lame. Way too many children running around so it was quite noisy. Could be a great vacation for people with children.

name: Westin San Diego
title: “As usual, oh what fun we had in your "heavenly bed" !!!!”
text: Can't say too much except we had so much fun! Staff was great and the hotel is BEAUTIFUL. Within walking distance to EVERYTHING! THANKS.

name: Hotel Indigo San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Pet friendly, but with deep cleaning,no more sneeze”
text:
This is a great hotel right in the heart of the gas lamp district. My room was spacious, modern and comfortable. It was fun to walk by the buzz of the Padres baseball stadium every night. But even with the stadium close by, the hotel is on a quite corner. I slept with a window open and had no problems with noise.
This is a pet friendly hotel and they do not have pet-free rooms rooms available. As I have a bad allergy to dogs-this worried me a lot. But the hotel provided a deep clean before my arrival, and all the floors are a hard surfaces (not even a rug to deal with), so I actually stayed sneeze and asthma free! 
There is no grocery in walking distance. A 7/11 is right around the corner and a CVS a few blocks down, but for those with food allergies this may be a challenge.
Overall I enjoyed my stay here.

name: Grand Hyatt San Antonio
title: “A Great Hotel in Riverwalk Area”
text:
We came to San Antonio to visit Sea World and stayed at the Grand Hyatt. I thought the rate we received ($149, which included breakfast) was a good deal. The hotel is in a good location on the riverwalk and within walking distance to many good restaurants. I suggest parking right across the street from the hotel for $8 instead of the more expensive hotel parking. Even though the hotel is near the highway, we didn’t hear any noise and our room was quiet. The workout facility is spacious, well-equipped with a good view of the city. For a city hotel, it had nice, big rooftop pool. But it was very crowded with teenagers when we were there so it wasn’t as pleasant and relaxing as I hoped. The hotel staff was pleasant, polite and very helpful. The concierge even called us after we checked-in to welcome us and asked us what time we wanted housekeeping service. We had the breakfast buffet. It was a rather large buffet and the quality of which you would expect from a nicer hotel. The service at the restaurant was like the rest of the hotel- very polite and helpful. 
The hotel décor and room furnishings are contemporary. I thought the coffee shop, bar and restaurant were fine. We didn’t spend much time in the hotel common areas or ballroom/conference rooms so I didn’t see for myself what others have complained about. Except for the bathroom, the room was what you would expect from an upscale hotel- it was clean, the beds were comfortable, and the furnishings were well maintained. The bathroom was spacious and adequate but I can see what others have said about workmanship. It did look like poor workmanship in the installation of the bathroom fixtures. But everything in the bathroom worked with no problems, so the sloppy workmanship didn’t bother me. 
Some of the criticism of this hotel seemed excessive and nit-picky. I’m sure if you examine any hotel with a hyper-critical eye, you’ll find all kinds of problems. This hotel was more than fine for our purposes- a clean and safe place to sleep and shower. I would stay here again especially if I receive the same rate.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton San Diego/Del Mar
title: “Great Place for the Business Travelor”
text: Homewood offers very comfortable rooms. The hotel is very quiet and in a nice area. There is easy access to freeways. They offer a variety of foods for breakfast that would please all types of preferences. In the evening they offer a dinner meal that has to be one of the best around. Each night is different with a salad, main course and an array of beverages including complimentary beer and wine.

name: Hotel Indigo San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Swanky, modern, and charming”
text: We had wonderful stay celebrating an anniversary. We enjoyed the delightful rooms and wonderful service. The front desk and bellmen went above and beyond to make us happy. I know it seems silly to eat hotel food when you're near the gas lamp with all it's choices, but the food we tried was stellar. The $12 steak appetizer was cooked perfectly and the stuffed french toast was worth ordering on consecutive mornings. The meditation terrace was fun and packed on Friday night and quiet and relaxing on the weekday.

name: Omni La Mansion del Rio
title: “Filthy, run-down, and overpriced”
text:
I stayed at La Masion on a business trip in January. I was excited when I saw the website and thought that it would be worth the $200 a night rate. We arrived late afternoon, dropped our bags and went to a dinner meeting. I didn't look closely at the room (unfortunately). When I arrived back at the hotel late that evening, I took a closer look at the room. Everything was filthy - dust all along the perimeter of the room, I moved a chair out of the way only to find it covering a huge WET mess! I decided to try and sleep and to deal with it in the morning.
Taking a shower the next morning was another nightmare - half-used products in the shower - it completely turned my stomach. I went to the desk and insisted that I be moved. They complied, and the new room was slightly better.
Asked for a wakeup call - no system, just manual phone calls. They were 10 minutes late the first morning and half an hour late on the second. We barely made our flight and one colleague missed hers.
When I recieved my credit card statement, I had been billed for both rooms for both nights. (of course!) I have to say the woman who resolved my bill was polite and reversed the charges after I explained what happened during my stay.
All in all, I was EXTREMELY disappointed in this hotel. I can understand that things aren't always perfect, but for $200 a night I expect cleanliness. I am sure you can find better for the price on the riverwalk.

name: Country Inn & Suites By Carlson, San Diego North
title: “Excellent value for tourists and business people alike”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for a long birthday weekend. From this location we went to the zoo, the beaches and Sea World, all within 10-15 minute drives. It is located in a business park area rather than the touristy and somewhat overpriced "hotel row." This is a particularly upscale Country Inn, the room was very nice, everything felt very new. I will say we arrived VERY late on the Friday night (more like Saturday morning) and the hotel's lot (it shares parking with another hotel just across the way) was quite full. Had to park around the side, but that's just a busy weekend in beautiful San Diego for you! We pulled the blackout curtains and actually slept past Noon the next day, so no noise to wake you up and you know on Saturday morning there had to be kids running up and down the hall. Didn't hear a thing!! 
The only drawback I could see was that, because it's in a business park area rather than a tourist trap, you had to venture out a couple of miles to find restaurants, even fast food. I would definitely stay here again, though.

name: Hotel Indigo San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Great Hotel, Great Service”
text:
Stayed for a full week at this hotel for a meeting. Every aspect of my stay was great. From check-in at the front desk with Darren to a spotlessly clean room, great service and food for the meeting, and genuinely friendly people everywhere you turn. Location can not be beat. Just a short stroll from the many restaurants and nightlife of the Gas Lamp Quarter, only one block from Petco Park, and a short stroll to the Marina area. The Hotel's 9th floor outside terrace is a great place to start and finish an evening.
This hotel is the only LEED certified Green Hotel in San Diego and I would recommend it for anyone visiting the area. Great for couples, family, business travel, and particularly for a meeting. If you are booked somewhere else, change your reservation and stay here.

name: Hilton Palacio del Rio
title: “Loved it”
text: I stayed at the Hilton Palacio del Rio over the 4th of July weekend. Had a great time. The room and the hotel was beautiful. This staff was very accomodating. The hotel is walking distance to the Alamo and Riverwalk Mall. Being right on the Riverwalk we were able to pick and choose resturants and shopping. We didn't use the valet service for our vehicle so we saved some money there. The parking garage was only two blocks away so it wasn't an inconvience. I can't wait until we go back.

name: Residence Inn San Diego Downtown/Gaslamp Quarter
title: “This is the place to stay if going to Petco Park”
text:
We stayed at the Residence Inn Gaslamp for one night following a Padres game. Very close to the ball park. Got a screaming deal on the room via price line.com. $179 for a queen city view room. Room 1402 (top level) has view of convention center, Coronado, downtown, Point Loma and even the Bay through the buildings. NICE! Has a pullout sofa bed, full size fridge, well equipped kitchenette. Really nice buffet breakfast included...eggs, bacon, sausage, etc...not the typical continental breakfast fare. Pay parking.
Best value for a nice hotel in the gas lamp. There is no room service.
John at the front desk is very helpful!

name: Hotel Valencia Riverwalk
title: “One Smidge Short of Excellent”
text:
I want to preface this review by saying that my husband and I are in our mid senior years. We can afford more now than when our children lived at home. This was one of the best 5 day vacations we have been on in many years even with the small inconvenience of the bathroom size and noise.
After staying several dozen times at the Valencia in San Jose, CA, we finally were able to experience the Valencia in San Antonio. We had read, on several TripAdvisor reviews, that it was noisy. We had always stayed in a Junior Suite and never experienced any noise in CA. Not so on this trip. We were originally given a Junior Suite, but had to be moved to a regular room because of the recently varnished wood in the junior suite. My asthma bothered me the minute I opened the room door and another Junior Suite was not available. I want to add that all through this experience we were given four diamond treatment. The front desk, the porter, the manager...everyone was friendly, helpful and ready to try to meet our every need.
Now about the noise. When I was in the bathroom, which I might add is smaller than their CA counterparts, I could hear the lady in the next bathroom talking. She wasn't yelling, just talking. I heard her as clear as if she were standing in our room talking. It was a very uncomfortable feeling, so I kept the bathroom door shut while we were in our room and the radio or TV on. I can't actually say I heard any voices while we were in our room area. There were some bumps and knocks, but no voices. I was uncomfortable enough to keep the TV on just in case. Other than that, our stay was very relaxing. We were on the 9th floor, on the side of the building between the river and the street. We didn't hear any noise from the ground, but then our view was of the top of the building, the pool area (no one swam throughout our stay) and a parking lot. None of those make much noise. I can guess that if you stay by the air conditioners, you would hear them so if you wake easily, ask for a room away from them. 
After we settled into the room, we drove our car to the Market Street Parking Garage ( 3 blocks away) parked ($12.00 for 24 hours instead of $27.00 at the Valencia) and walked everywhere almost the whole 5 days. The Hotel is on the Riverwalk and within walking distance of everything we wanted to visit. The parking garage was close, well lighted and we felt our car was very safe. Each time we came and went from the Hotel, we were asked if we needed directions, had doors opened for us and our every need met, day or night. Definitely 4 star treatment.
Inside it is much the same as the San Jose Valencia. The tone is peaceful, water flows inside the lobby, colors are relaxing and lights are low. It has a business center that is very efficient, dining venue (we didn't eat there) and a small bar area. The bar (V-Bar) is, thankfully, not the hot spot that is the San Jose V-Bar. All staff personnel were a friendly, attentive group of young adults and happy to be of help whenever we asked (but I'm sure our tipping didn't hurt their opinion of us). We will definately stay there again but in the future, only in a junior suite.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton San Diego/Del Mar
title: “Great place to stay”
text:
We have stayed here four times and it's a very comfortable Homewood Suites. Close easy on and off access to I5, close to the airport too. TV channels are bad; Lodgnet ugly. But I was told that come December, it will change. I sure hope so since this hotel is so well run otherwise.
I do like the bfast except for the scrambled eggs which are bad. Their waffle mix is pretty darn good.

name: Westin San Diego
title: “My waiter was amazing!”
text: My waiter Teresa at the Hotel restaurant was absolutelly amazing. I travel weekly to different destinations across the United States and she was the best I have seen in 5 years of travel. She went out of her way to be sure I understood the different menu options and checked on me regularly. She also noticed that I was in "work mode" and asked if I would like to take coffee with me as I left. This would not be a normal thing to consider at the dinner hour but she noticed! Just perfect attention to her customers needs! Thank you for hiring such great people!

name: Omni La Mansion del Rio
title: “Amazing for Honeymoon night”
text: Living only two hours from San Antonio, I had always dreamed at staying at an amazing hotel for my honeymoon night. Knowing this, my husband called La Mansion almost six months before our wedding to reserve something amazing for us. Upon arriving there, the valet congratulated us. We were then congratulated by the check-in lady and handed keys to our room. We were giving an extremely quite room way back in a corner of the hotel. Upon arrival, a bottle of Champagne and chocolate covered strawberries where in our room with a note welcoming us to the hotel. The phone rang about an hour later making sure that everything was up to standerds. The parking attendents actually went out to our car at midnight to get something that I had forgotton. My husband and I had a wonderful night. We heard nothing all night, the bed was extremely comfortable, and the room service the next morning was well worth the price. This was everything I ever dreamed of. Checking out the next morning was a little hectic but this can be expected on a Sunday. I have recomended this hotel to lovers everywhere. It was truly amazing!!!!

name: Tower23 Hotel
title: “Luxury on Pacific Beach”
text: Pacific Beach is bar far the more relaxed beach that San Diego has to offer and if you can tolerate the bronzed and the beautiful its a great place to stay. Tower 23 is nestled right next to the peer and offers a little flavour of luxury and style more akin to an inner city hotel. The style is very chic throughout and the rooms are very well appointed. Friendly staff make this a definite recommendation for anyone looking to stay in the area in style.

name: San Antonio Marriott Rivercenter
title: “Great Hotel, Definitely Recommend!”
text:
I had a really great stay at this hotel. The rooms were comfortable, clean, and quiet. The room even had a really nice flat screen TV. Despite staying at nearly the top of the hotel, I never had to wait long for an elevator. Front desk staff was helpful and friendly. 
Location could not have been better. It is right next to the Riverwalk and within a 5 minute walk to the Alamo. Overall, I have only had good experiences at Mariott properties, and this was no exception.

name: Sheraton Gunter Hotel San Antonio
title: “Good location, average staff, below average value . . . above average NOISE”
text: We booked on Hotwire and were there on a Friday and Saturday night. Before tax the room was about $200 per night. We did not realize until we checked in it but we actually had an executive room. The room was large and clean. The bathroom was small and below average. The hotel has been nicely restored and the location is very good: 4 blocks to the Alamo, 2 blocks to the Riverwalk, across the street from the Majestic Theatre, about 6 blocks from La Villita, etc. Our room was on the 11th floor and nearly on Houston Street (front of the hotel). Both Friday night and Saturday night the street noise was hard to ignore but we managed to sleep fairly well. We heard a lot of noise from within the hotel itself, including the adjacent room. The staff did their jobs but there was nothing remarkable or special about the service. Overall, the cost is too high for this hotel. I would classify this hotel as a high 3 star and not a 4 star. Parking is a total rip-off but you can park in either of two public parking decks directly behind the hotel for $10 per night. While there was nothing unpleasant about our stay at the Gunter, I really think that we could have done better for the money. The problem may have been that it was Spring Break for Texas schools and there were lots of families roaming about.

name: Tower23 Hotel
title: “Most Amazing Hotel!”
text:
We actually stayed at this hotel in September of 2009 but I'm just getting around to writing the review. I found this hotel by researching online, it was our first time in San Diego together and I wanted to treat my fiance to a nice hotel stay on the beach for his birthday. We got there a little early and our room wasn't ready so they put us in another room that was better, it was a corner room and had AMAZING views of the beach. The room was awesome, the bathroom was unbelievable, water came out of the ceiling into the bathtub!!! We enjoyed one of the best meals we've ever had at JRDN restaurant that is downstairs, I recommend it to anyone that is going to San Diego. We also enjoyed an room service for breakfast the next morning which we enjoyed on our balcony listening to the ocean breeze. While we were there we did the private surfing lessons that the hotel set up for us which were awesome. Honestly I can't say enough good things about this hotel, we're planning to make a stop for our honeymoon when we head out west next year. 
The only thing that's missing is a swimming pool, but you're literally on the beach so how can you complain.

name: Crystal Pier Hotel & Cottages
title: “GREAT!! Can't wait to return”
text: COTTAGE B ..that's where we just left.This place has been on my "bucket list" it's all I thought it would be!the 2 end studios a and b ,I think are the nicest.they are studios that are pretty large.Bed was king size and comfortable.TV ,fridge,microwave etc.I would bring your own bar of soap..they are skimpy....the place is old...but clean There are binoculars in the room...the beach town itself is pretty DIRTY and if it was not for this place...there is NO WAY we would go.The surrounding restaurants are lousy and the streets are supper grimy...We thought we were in Venice Beach....BUT THE CRYTAL PIER ROCKS!!!!

name: Hotel Indigo San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “A great stay”
text: We loved San Diego and Hotel Indigo. Everyone on staff was really polite and friendly, very helpful. the room had a fantastic view on the 10th floor. They are forward thinking in their welcoming of canine family members and even have a doggie pool and grass lawn on the 9th floor for pets to visit. The hotel was spotlessly clean. I will definitely return to Hotel Indigo.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton San Diego/Del Mar
title: “Great Property and Even Greater Staff!”
text: With extensive travel requirements related to my business, I stay at many hotels and resorts (both domestically and internationally). Due to some unique business and personal requirements, members of my family and I have stayed at this property a few times, over the past few weeks. Having stayed at many Homewood and Embassy Suites locations, this is clearly one of the nicer one's in terms of comforts and cleanliness. But where this hotel truly excels, is in the area of hospitality! The staff, from the front desk, to the kitchen/culinary team, to the housekeepers, to the management, all are myopically focused on customer service and ensuring that the guest has an optimal stay. From a member of the culinary team, "running next door" to get cookies for our children after one of the scheduled dinners, to a member of the "overnight team" granting me temporary access to an additional Suite, just to insure that I had adequate cell phone reception for a very important business call, etc. Just examples of why this hotel and it's staff are truly so special. Can't recommend this venue enough for both your business and/or family travel needs!

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton San Diego/Del Mar
title: “Clean and Convenient”
text:
We stayed here for 5 nights on vacation and we were happy with the hotel overall. We had a king suite. Our room was clean and comfortable. The only odd thing was the layout with the bathroom door - if you opened the door from the toilet/shower area it nearly touched the sink outside - open carefully if you think someone might be brushing his teeth or plan to apologize for clobbering him with the door.
The crew at breakfast did a great job of keeping things cleaned and stocked though a little more variety for fresh fruit might have been nice. There were grapefruit and apples everyday. A couple days there were oranges and bananas. There were also make-your-own waffles, scrambled eggs, another hot selection that varied (sausage, potatoes, biscuits/gravy), oatmeal, yogurt, cereal, muffins, bread/bagels. 
The noise level in the hotel was mixed. It was far enough from the highway that we didn't hear road noise, but we faced the courtyard with the pool so heard the revelers in the hot tub until they closed it down at 10 PM. The hallway doors were nice and tight, but the walls still pass quite a bit of sound - babies crying, people on the phone. One morning they started doing some very loud work in the hallway outside our room at 10 AM, one way to make sure we got out and about after a late night I guess. 
The location worked well for us since we visited Legoland north in Carlsbad and spent time south in San Diego. The free internet in our room worked well, but wi-fi for the iPod would have been nice without having to go down to the lobby.

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Airport/Liberty Station
title: “Great hotel; Great Breakfast; Unbeatable Location”
text:
Our stay was fabulous. There were 6 of us traveling (2 adults and 4 kids). We booked a 2 room king suite; we were kinda surprised when we found that this was NOT a 2 bedroom suite - just a two room suite (exactly what the website said it was; we were ignorantly expecting two bedrooms). The room was nicely appointed; had 1 king bed and a sofabed in one room and a sofabed in the other room. For the first night, we were put up in the handicap accessible room - this would have been fine but there was not enough room in the bedroom to pull the sofabed out (it felt on top of the king bed). We ended up taking the mattress off and putting in the other room (which worked out great putting all of the kids in one room). However, the next day the hotel needed the handicap room so they moved us to a regular king suite (sofabeds pulled out there with no problem).
The internet was fast and free.
The parking was also free - and plentiful. In fact, we left our car parked there for the few days we'd be gone from San Diego. The hotel just jotted down the license number in case there was an issue/question.
The airport shuttle was quick and easy (and free).
The breakfast was included in our room rate - and it was fabulous. Admittedly, it got a little old on the 5th morning but I couldn't complain - they had everything I love - smoked salmon, waffles, decent bread selection, fruits, potatoes, bacon, and veggies. They also had an egg bar - but I'm not an egg person so I can't comment on that.
The "heated" outdoor pool was perfect for our kids. It was slightly chilly at first but we just needed to get in and swim around to warm up. The hottub was fabulous!
Hotel staff was very friendly and accommodating, from housekeeping, to the front desk, to the breakfast servers.
Hotel is located close to several eating establishments right there at Liberty station, not to mention the dozens off Rosecrans (about a 10 minute walk way).
Being a family of 6, there were few hotels that offered connecting rooms or rooms big enough to accommodate all of us; the Courtyard turned out to be the perfect hotel for us. We loved it and will be back.

name: Hilton Garden Inn San Diego Del Mar
title: “Perfect family vacation”
text: After a few days in Vegas, we checked in to this hotel. Everything about our stay was FANTASTIC! We were road-tripping with 3 kids and meeting extended family in the area. The staff was so guest-oriented. They took care of all our annoying requests with such grace. The food was wonderful and very-reasonably priced. We ate more than half our meals in the hotel because it was so convenient! The pool is small but was perfect for our little family. Love, love, love this place. We will be back!

name: Residence Inn San Diego Downtown/Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Good service, spacious rooms, adequate breakfast”
text:
My wife and I stayed in Room 1402 from July 2nd through July 4th. We had just come from a hotel in Mission Bay (San Diego) for a work conference. We didn't know what to expect, but we knew not to park there because it costs $32 per night.
We found that the hotel was close to public parking ($17 per night). When we entered the hotel we were immediately assisted by staff. He was very efficient and professional. He also gave us a choice between a king bed and a lower floor and a queen bed and a higher floor. We chose the former. We were very glad because we had extensive views of the bay and ocean from our spacious room.
The room had a very comfortable bed, a superior television, and everything was clean and in order. The bathroom was ample and the toiletries were of a high quality.
Breakfast is on the second floor. Get there early so that you can find a seat; otherwise, you have to take your food back to your room. The food itself was hearty. They had scrambled eggs, potatoes, french toast and a waffle bar. Decent coffee too!
Overall, we intend to make this our hotel for summers in San Diego. We typically spend the cooler months in a place in the Little Italy area of San Diego.

name: San Diego Marriott Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Great service recovery”
text:
As a lifetime Platinum member at Marriott (over 2,000 nights in my travel career) I have seen the good and the mediocre (never bad at a Marriott property).
My wife and I spent five nights at the Marriott Gaslamp Quarter during the summer travel season. The hotel was very busy on both Friday and Saturday nights (our first two nights). On our floor, there was some sort of a party group that screamed and cursed in the hallway on both nights well after midnight. When I called to the front desk, they sent security up but were unable to keep the group quiet.
On Sunday morning, June 19, we went to the front desk to express our concern and asked to be moved to a different floor. Not only did they move us, but they gave us a better room at no additional charge.
While I don't blame the hotel for the rowdy guests (not much they could do in advance), I do appreciate that they went the extra mile to satisfy a frequent quest.
By the way, great hotel in a great location.

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Airport/Liberty Station
title: “Nice hotel stay”
text:
First trip to San Diego area and this was a good place to drive in all directions from. Close to Cabrillo National Park as well as driving to The Gaslamp and Balboa Park/San Diego Zoo. Even near Sea World. Very nice staff and well designed rooms. Wish the bed was a bit softer but that was only complaint. 
Free parking which is hard to find in this area was good bonus.

name: Hotel Indigo San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Hotel kinda sucks but looks cool”
text: I rated the value a 3 because I dont know what my employer paid for the room. The restaurant, bar, and lobby look great. The breakfast was average... The dinner was awesome. The rooms are spacious but kind of ugly. My color scheme was blue and red. I couldnt turn up the heat past a certain degree, there was a coffee machine without any cream or sugar, and the bathroom didnt have a vent. Other than that it was alright. Room service was affordable.

name: San Diego Marriott Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Nice and convenient”
text: This Marriott is located just outside the main entrance to Petco Stadium (San Diego Padres). It is in the "Gaslamp" section, which is an area filled with bars and restaurants. A mall is about a 6-8 block walk from the hotel. Very near the SanDiego Convention Center. Rooms were clean and quiet. Good, quiet air conditioning/heating system. Car necessary for travel to beaches.

name: San Antonio Marriott Rivercenter
title: “A 3 star room at a 5 star price”
text: Stayed here with my wife for 2 nights using a rewards certicate for one free night. I was suprised that the room on the concierge level was nothing more than a smaller version of a typical marriott courtyard room. The valet service was an absolute nightmare with no sense of order and it took anywhere from 7 minutes to 15 minutes to get your car. Not once did they open the door for my wife. The bill for one of the two nights would have equalled a 2 night's stay at The Menger Hotel. The location is a bit poor despite being on the riverwalk. You are at least a block from the action unless you consider the rivercenter mall an attraction. I've stayed at many SA hotels and for better accommodations and a more "San Antonio" feel, I would recommend staying at The Menger. A lot more history, right next to the Alamo, and a shorter walk to the main attractions on the riverwalk.

name: Westin San Diego
title: “Not up to expectations or of a Westin/ Starwood experience”
text:
I made a reservation via spg.com (platinum member) and stayed at this hotel last weekend. Long story short- the service was pretty slow. Although the staff were nice people (as all San Diegeans I think are)... they are pretty forgetful and not too quick on their feet. Evidence:
1) Called after making my reservation online to reserve a crib... was put on hold and nobody ever came back. I called back and reserved a crib via a 2nd call.
2) When I arrived at the hotel there was no crib in the room.. even AFTER calling back a second time to confirm (or really a third call overall after the debacle in my first point). UGG! So we had a crying 1 year old at 10pm waiting for a crib (which took 40 mins to come up after I called down to the front desk twice).
3) I asked for two rooms next to each other... but they were not connected. This is just somewhat annoying, not THAT big a deal, but when you mention on the phone that you have a family and would like two rooms together... it'd be nice to have the front desk put 2 + 2 together.
4) Finally... on Sunday I called down to see if I could get a late checkout... and again got put on hold and the person never returned!?!?! To their credit, they did call back 15 mins later to apologize (after I sat on the phone for 10 mins just waiting for them to give me a "yes" or a "no").

name: Crystal Pier Hotel & Cottages
title: “A View to Remember”
text:
My husband and I spent our honeymoon at Crystal Pier in cottage B...the last cottage on the end of the pier...on top of the ocean and with a view that took our breath away. If you love the ocean, then the Crystal Pier is probably the most romantic place to stay in all of San Diego, including the Hotel Del Coronado. the Pier is privately owned and only opened to the public from 8:00 am until sunset. The rest of the time, only those staying in the cottages have access. Believe me, waking up at 2 am with a full moon and walking to the end of the pier will be something you will never forget. You feel as if you are the only two people in the world. One evening when we took our early morning stroll, a pod of dolphin greeted us. Incredible! Now where else can you stay and have that sort of experience? The Pier is gated with its own security staff, and allows you complete peace of mind. As for ease, drive your car on to the Pier and park in front of your cottage. Don't drive again unless you want to. The cottages are adorable, vrey clean with incredible views and the sound and feel of the ocean beneath your feet. The kitchens are adequately supplied, but if your traveling by car you may wish to bring some of your favorite pots and pans...otherwise, you have all you need. A grocery store is a quick 2-minute walk and dozens of restaurants and bars are just steps away. 
As for the staff and some of the negative comments I've read here, in all the years we have been going, (we've stayed there at least a dozen times) we have always found the staff more than willing to do whatever it takes to make our stay the best possible...and it always is. 
Expensive? Yes...but, worth every penny. Crystal Pier is a unique one of a kind experience and will make any trip to San Diego one you will never forget.

name: Crystal Pier Hotel & Cottages
title: “We love Crystal Pier”
text: Even though we live here in San Diego going to crystal pier for a week or even a night has been a regular trip for us over the years. One of the reasons we love it is the cabins out over the water let you hear the waves under you at night. Also at night they close the gates so it becomes a little gated community---great since some of the elements in Mission Beach aren't desirable. We love it, walking distance to shops, stores and restaurants, you park your car and leave it (on the pier!) and don't get back in it until you want to leave.They remodeled the cabins a few years back and they are darling. There is a neat private feel to each cabin, each with it's own deck patio (with lounges, table and chairs) overlooking the beach and ocean. We have stayed in almost every cabin over the years but prefer the low number cabins (means you are out over the water further).Unique, fun place to stay.

name: Hyatt Regency Hill Country Resort and Spa
title: “Felt a little out of place!”
text:
My wife and I enjoyed the overnite experience, however, we felt a little out of place as we travel a good deal and this place, although elegant, is considerably overpriced , in our opinion!
First of all, valet parking only ($10.00)!, this of course requires valet room
service, another few bucks! Then, it's so large, one must walk, walk, walk to go to the lobby, resturant, pool, general store,etc.
The employee's are courteous, the service good (not excellent), but the "inconvience" of valets for "everthing" is to much for us! (For instance, to get a corkscrew, room service was the ONLY available option, that took 30 minutes and a few bucks.. have at it, we like our auto "in sight and available", be able to pick type of resturants, short walk to pool, etc.
We'll stay with Hampton, Wingate type, thankyou!

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton San Diego/Del Mar
title: “Perfect for traveling with toddler”
text: Nice suite, plenty of space for toddler to run around. Has a full size kitchen which was so great in prepping our toddlers meals. Very clean, and decor is current. Good breakfast and close to old town and sea world. free parking and plenty of it.

name: Hotel Indigo San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Melissa at the front desk and the whole staff in general”
text:
I just wanted to take a few minutes to commend the AMAZING staff at the Hotel Indigo in downtown San Diego, I had the pleasure of interacting with the front desk staff and was especially thrilled to have dealt with Melissa. She was kind, considerate and extremely helpful to this lost New Yorker. She was patient and took the time to explain the city and give me directions to where I needed to go. She even printed out a bus schedule for me - going way above and beyond in my opinion!
I am a flight attendant and stay at over 250 hotels a year, and my experince with the Hotel Indigo by far ranks in the top 5! I'm also in the businees of customer service, so I really appreciate it when I receive excellent service. Melissa and her staff blew me away with their friendliness and helpful nature - and I'm not easily impressed!
Thank you Melissa for your help and excellent service - it was MY pleasure to stay at Hotel Indigo and look forward to returning and seeing your smiling face again!
Warm regards,
Jason Trexler

name: Westin San Diego
title: “the best wedding every”
text: this hotel is very nice the poeple the hotel itself is nice i would come back and bring friends too .

name: Tower23 Hotel
title: “BEST HOTEL IN SAN DIEGO!”
text:
We spent 4 fabulous nights here and my only regret is that it wasn't longer! 
Room - We chose a Surf Pad as part of a birthday celebration package! Choose this room and you will not regret it! The views are arguably some of the worlds best! Being from Australia we are used to gorgeous beaches and Tower23's Surf Pads deliver views of one perfect beach! The gorgeous sunset views come free with the room and try are some of the best! The room was large and cleaned meticulously everyday by courteous and dedicated staff! Even a request for new pillows was met with a smile. The beds are heavenly! You will not want to get out of bed, which isn't a problem as you can lie in bed and look at the beautiful Pacific Ocean!
Location - pretty hard to beat! Tower23 is right on the beach and the boardwalk, as well as being within walking distance to it her great restaurants and activities, and only a 10-15 drive to the center of SD. Parking is also abundant and the hotels valet parking was affordable and super quick.
Service - the BEST! Upon check in we were sent to our room, only to discover it was still being made up. We didn't mind waiting the 10 minutes on the beautiful tower deck in the sun lounges, although the hotel made us even more comfortable with complimentary cocktails to apologize for our room not being ready! Within 10 minutes we were in our room and not 10 minutes later there was a knock at the door with a free bottle of champagne to wish me a happy birthday! Everything flowed smoothly and staff were always smiling! They genuinely make you feel welcome, and nothing is too much trouble. 
Noise - ignore the other reviewers! They are obviously too stuffy to be staying in such a wonderful location! We had a room right next to the tower deck and right above the restaurant and noise was Never a problem. The glass is double glazed and blocks out 95% of the noise. We were even here over a weekend and it wasn't a problem, even when there was a function on the tower deck!
Oh, and you absolutely have to eat at JRDN - see my other review for this - the food is to die for!
Overall, we loved Tower23, and would happily recommend it to our friends and stay here again when we are next in SD!

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Hollywood Walk of Fame
title: “super hotel”
text:
rigtigt godt hotel til prisen som ligger 200m fra hollywood boulevard. . morgenmad er rigtig god. værelser er rigtig pæne og rene. prisen for parkering er meget rimelig for området.
really good hotel to stay situated 200m from Hollywood Boulevard. . breakfast is really good. rooms are really nice and clean. price for parking is very reasonable for the area.

name: Dolphin Motel
title: “Cute, clean, vintage motel.”
text: Fun little motel. Very clean. Small room with great TV with lots of channels. Good value. Fabulous staff.

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Airport/Liberty Station
title: “Extremely Nice Hotel”
text: My wife and I spent one night at the hotel and found our stay to be very nice. The hotel has spacious rooms, which were very quiet considering that there was an airport nearby. Our room had a view and a balcony. All the decor was very modern and the rooms were extremely clean. We enjoyed the buffet breakfast which was about $10. We were neaby Anthony's restaurant and the Fish Market, so we dined there in the evenings. There is a large park nearby so we walked the park near the shore line and enjoyed being out in the fresh air. The front desk service was helpful and answered all our questions regarding our stay. We would definitely consider this hotel for any future stay in San Diego.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton San Diego/Del Mar
title: “Not knowing what to expect but was pleasently surprised”
text:
We traveled with our 3 young boys(1 year old, 6 year old, and 9 year old.) We wanted something that was kid friendly, and close to Legoland, The Zoo, Seaworld and the beaches and even downtown. The location was perfect for us. 
The hotel staff was wonderful :very helpful. I used the laundry units , which was very convienant. We had very comfortable beds...better then home! They even provided a crib at no charge. We had a wonderful breakfest included in price every morning and dinner 4 of the nights too. We are very happy and would recommend this to our family and friends. They were great!

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton San Diego/Del Mar
title: “No Complaints”
text: Stayed here over Thanksgiving. Location was just off the highway. Can be a bit confusing to get to, but had my trusty GPS. Property was clean, breakfast was goot, hot food was hot and cold was cold. Food was kept well stocked and there was a daily variety in either the eggs for meat that was served. Too cool to go swimming, but it looked well kept. Did not take part in the Managers reception in the evening, but others said it was good. Internet was free and fast. Good selection of TV stations. Room had a few maintenace issues that were resolved in less than an hour (Loose door hinge tht would not let the bathroom door close and a light bulb that was out.) Parking was free, lot well lit. Located in the middle of an office park and high rent housing area so felt very safe.

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Airport/Liberty Station
title: “Lovely hotel and brilliant staff.”
text:
This was our final hotel of a three week trip and it was excellent.
When we first arrived, it seem a long way from how we had read the reviews but in San Diego, everywhere is a bit further away than it seems and this is very central for everything.
Front desk were very helpful and we liked the extra towels and choice of pillows. 
Jim, who runs the bar was a real star and worth having a chat to him for suggestions of places to go.
Lived up to its excellent reviews and thanks for a lovely few days.

name: Hilton Inn at Penn
title: “Monopoly Prices”
text: Basically. this hotel is the only game in town if you want to be on Penn's campus. They know it and charge accordingly. The service did not match the high price and next time I will stay in thge heart of the city and take a cab to the university. Very disappointing stay.

name: Westin San Diego
title: “Tremendous”
text:
My husband and I traveled to San Diego on business but decided to stay on a few extra days to enjoy the city and weather. As others have previously mentioned, this hotel is in the perfect location to get around and the trolley and train station is just a few blocks away. It is not a resort, like some might expect every hotel in San Diego to be, but is definetly one of the most comfortable and welcoming hotels in the city. We visited a few other hotels while walking around and were happy we chose to stay at the Westin. 
We found every staff member to be courteous and helpful, especially the concierge who was always willing to direct us to the best restaurants and shops.. 
The hotel apparently just underwent a complete renovation earlier this year, so everything was brand new, which was great.
This hotel was really tremendous. I would highly recommend it to anyone travelling to San Diego on business or for pleasure.

name: San Diego Marriott Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Wonderful place...”
text: This hotel is completely re-done, great location, perfect area the gaslamp district, The Altitute Sky Lounge on the roof top has a viewo f the city and the ball park, even looks out to Coronado. Wouldn't stay anywhere else.

name: The Independent
title: “great hotel - a bargain at this price”
text: lovely hotel in fantastic location - very good value for money for boutique hotel. queen deluxe room small but adequate with masculine but quality decor. clean, great free drinks in lobby - wine and cheese in evening and hot drinks in day. nice staff . highly recommended

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “Another great stay at Hotel Giraffe”
text:
It was our second time staying at Hotel Giraffe. We found the room this time a little small and realized that our previous stay was in the king superior room rather that the queen. The king definitely gives you a little more space. My primary concern is cleanliness of the facility and they have this down! The cost is reasonable (we used to stay at the "W" in Union Square until we stopped justifying the $500.00 + room charges). 
The staff is very friendly, helpful and professional and you can't beat the location. We're back in June for another stay!

name: Hotel Elysee
title: “Lovely Mid-town Spot”
text: Just the perfect spot with a great location for shopping Madison Avenue and museums. Staff couldn't be nicer and the rooms are very nice and very clean. The breakfast was also lovely and a nice surprise. We also found it amazing how quiet the rooms are from road noise and also hearing other guests in the hallways, we thought we were the only guests in the hotel.

name: Pacific Terrace Hotel
title: “Lovely hotel, lovely location”
text: Beautiful hotel overlooking the ocean. Service was immaculate, room was perfect. Couldn't ask for more.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “The Hotel Giraffe DOES NOT STAND behind their services.”
text: Within half an hour of check-in I received a call from the General Manager at Hotel Giraffe informing me that my car had been involved in an accident while in their possession on the way to the parking garage. Their attitude - not our problem - take it up with the parking garage as if they had no liability or responsibility for what happened. Neither the hotel nor the garage has paid for the damages eventhough repair estimates were promply provided. While I recognize the fact that parking is an outsourced service - in this case Rapid Parking, Inc. - the hotel has not done anything to facilate resolution. I am extremely disappointed in the manner this matter has been handled and continues unresolved. If you are looking for arrogance and complete lack of customer care in matters like this, then The Hotel Giraffe should be your choice in hotels. Good luck!

name: Dolphin Motel
title: “Cosy place!”
text: The rooms aren't that spacious but I'm totally fine with that considering that the price of the room beats everything. It's is definitely very clean! And the staffs are warm and friendly! I met this guy who works there (I think he's the owner but I'm not so sure) over breakfast and he was really helpful to offer me insights as to where my family and I should visit over our stay in San Diego. He even provided maps to various attractions in SD! Thank you!

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Airport/Liberty Station
title: “Nice enough - Not one of the best”
text:
Stayed at this hotel on business. Location was convenient to airport and the places I had to get to. Newer building in good condition, but elevator was painfully slow.
Also painfully slow was the internet access, with many drop-outs. 20th century technology, I suspect. Good thing it was free.
Did not get a chance to use restaurant; it was closed the only night of my stay that I was going to use it. Not too far from Little Italy, so it worked out OK.

name: San Diego Marriott Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Perfect Business Hotel”
text: This hotel has everything the business traveler needs and then some. The complex is enormous, with restaurants, shops, gym, etc. -- you'd never really need to leave the hotel except right outside the door is the fabulous gas lamp district with great food, bars & shopping. on the other side of the hotel is the harbor and a running/bike path. i had a harbor view and and a very large room. it seemed to be a very family friendly establishment, as well.

name: Homewood Suites San Diego Airport - Liberty Station
title: “NO Major complaint here.”
text:
We usually stay at the Homewood suites, Double Tree, or Embassy Suites as we travel with two young children and often require a sofa bed in a separate room to get a restful night. 
Pros: Friendly staff, location from the major attractions. 5 washers and 4 dryers in each of the 2 buildings!!
Cons: hydrogenated powdered eggs; room location did not match my request and we were given a choice of a room across from the elevator or moldy first floor. We took the latter and had the fan on constantly but could not leave the window open for security reasons.
Overall although the room was not what I was used to, the staff was friendly enough to compensate for the minor deficiencies.

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Airport/Liberty Station
title: “Great hotel, friendly staff, wonderful experience!”
text: We live in San Diego and decided to stay at this hotel because we were participating in a triathlon that was taking place very close to the hotel. It turned out to be a great decision. In order of importance, it was very quiet and we slept well. The room and the hotel were immaculate, very important to us, as well as beautifully decorated. The staff was the friendliest staff I think I have ever encountered in our many travels. And I mean genuinely friendly people. There were grocery stores and restaurants within walking distance. The location is fabulous and even though we live in the San Diego area we will definitely return for a staycation. Our stay was better than we could have imagined!

name: Pacific Terrace Hotel
title: “Nice Place”
text: We really enjoyed our 3 nights. The hotel was in excellent condition, clean and the ocean views are great. Very attractive rooms and I really liked the wood louvered sliding doors. The bed was really comfortable. The hotel buffet breakfast was convenient and good, It was not included and was 11.50 per person, but we were told we would get half off. I guess this is a guest price? Nice pool and hot tub. This was our first visit to San Diego and we did enjoy Pacific Beach but the main street was not extremely attractive to shop or walk. The beach walk was very nice along the beach. As mentioned by a few others, the parking fees seem a bit much. Why some of these hotels charge high fees for their rooms and then add on parking fees is hard to understand. I can't see many people coming to Pacific Beach without a car. We did have to pay hotel parking in San Francisco,but public transportation seems more realistic there and so a lot of guests might not have a car and I am guessing they don't want to raise overall hotel rates and penalize non drivers? The hotel rates are on the high side considering that the area is not real ritzy, but I guess the ocean location is the reason for the rates. We really liked the pool area. The pool temperature was perfect and the view of the ocean from the pool area is great!

name: Homewood Suites San Diego Airport - Liberty Station
title: “Great for families with small children”
text:
My husband and two children stayed here for 5 nights in early Feb 2011. We chose this hotel based on the previous reviews and because they offered suites.
Having a full size kitchen was great with two little ones, even if we didn't eat in much. The week day dinners (Mon-Thurs) were a nice touch if the kids were too tired to go out to eat. Complimentary hot breakfast was decent - lots of healthy choices but my kids of course wanted the fruit loops they had never eaten before.
There is a walking trail just out the back door of the hotel that leads you to this most amazing brand new playground. You can also run a 6 mile loop on a little island across from the hotel - ask the hotel manager who is a runner for details.
The hotel also had laundry facilities which was handy. We did not use the pool as it was too cold out (62 degrees) but it looked very nice. The fitness centre had one treadmill, one elliptical, and some free weights.
There is a Trader Joe's and Von's grocery store 0.7 miles away. There is also a Starbucks, a sports pub that serves very good pizza, and a few other chain-type restaurants in a strip mall in front of the hotel.
We will definitely stay at this hotel again the next time we are in SD. The service and staff were superb. Overall, this is a very clean, professional hotel in a fantastic location.

name: JW Marriott San Antonio Hill Country Resort & Spa
title: “Golf resort with other facilities but far from town or shopping”
text:
Very high standards are set in this hotel.
Staff are excellent and there seems to be more staff than guests in the public areas.
Restaurants are very good and offer excellent quality, quantity and value.
For an overseas visitor the cost are quite high but you get what you pay for.
A little far out of main shopping and Town area but most people seem to be there for the golf or onsite facilities.
Taxi and shuttle service to and from hotel are excellent.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Sunset Suites - Riverwalk
title: “Loved San Antonio”
text:
We booked the Best Western as we have an elite Rewards card and always use it when we go anywhere. We fell in love with the Sunset Suites and definately plan on coming back here in the future for a longer stay. The rooms were spacious and newly decorated with an old charm feel. The beds were very comfortable. The breakfast was a hot one, and had great variety.
We were only a short walk from Riverwalk and had the best night walking around here and enjoying all that it has to offer. Can't wait to return.

name: Royal Palms Resort and Spa
title: “A charming, comfortable and relaxing hotel with an extremely attentive, friendly and knowledgeable staff.”
text: Not much more to say except you are made to feel like the only guest at their hotel.

name: Hotel Indigo San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Fantastic location, staff awesome, room...”
text: Fantastic location, staff awesome, room outstanding. I would rate as a 5* hotel, by far the best I've stayed in in the states.

name: Hotel Elysee
title: “great stay”
text: We stayed for four nights at the Elysee Hotel and were delighted. Bedroom was excellent and quiet. Breakfast was terrific. I don't like sitting on a low chair/couch at low tables to have breakfast but there is a large table in a room off the lounge if you get there in time!! The staff were lovely and very helpful. The hotel is in a terrific position and we would definately return again.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “Great find in NYC”
text: Loved this Hotel in a great area of New York. The views down Park Ave and 26th St from our 11th floor suite were fantastic. Staff are friendly, approachable and helpful, esp Franklin, who was great with our kids. The breakfasts in the beautiful foyer are handy and perfect for Australian tastes, and the wine and cheese evenings (although we onl;y managed to catch 2 in a week) were brilliant! The rooftop garden is a nice.oasis in the big city. We never used the New York Sport Club passes, but when you are in New York, there are so many better things to do. The neighbourhood is safe to walk around in at all hours, and there are great restaurants locally(including as specialised as several kosher vegetarian Indian places on Lexington!). Would return here in a flash, although am keen to try the sister hotel "The Library", also run by the HK group, that I've heard good things about.

name: Dolphin Motel
title: “Just very nice experiance”
text:
I booked on Line Traveloge hotel but coudn't stay there.
I guess even if they would pay to me for staing I would refuse.
I drived around and coudn't fined anything below $100 a nignt.
While driving I so the sighn Why pay more, Ask to see a room.
So I check the room and was very happy. The room was very clean. Any thing I want I asked for I gould get.
the personl is very friendly and hotel located in very convinient location.

name: Hotel Indigo San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Top 3 hotels we've stayed at”
text:
I would rate the Indigo Hotel in San Diego as one of of the top 3 hotels we have stayed at in our 43 years of marriage. We went to visit our son, who lives there, and take in a Padres- Giants game. The hotel was way beyond what we hoped it would be. The ninth floor bar had a perfect view of Petco Park, it was located in a great district with bars and restaurants within walking distance, the staff was very friendly and helpful and the price was very fair. I distincely remember a gentleman who worked there that I could swear was there 24 hours a day
The only thing we could find wrong was that the small refrigerator in our room was on the floor. Not that big a deal.
We will stay there again when we visit our son and his friends.

name: Dolphin Motel
title: “Delightful place, very friendly and helpful management”
text:
Loved the place. Basic but perfectly adequate, comfortable clean rooms. Great location. Great sea breezes. Best value for your buck in San Diego. It's close to everywhere you want to be. 
This obviously can't be guaranteed for everyone, but at least in my case, management went out of their way to be helpful with travel directions, and planning and in an urgent situation even provided transportation themselves.

name: JW Marriott San Antonio Hill Country Resort & Spa
title: “Soothing Getaway”
text: I was very happy to be able to spend a couple of days at this resort with my husband while he was there on business. The people are so very friendly and helpful. The property is gorgeous! Our room overlooked the golf course.I took a morning stroll and was amazed by all the beauty. Although I didn't have time to be pampered at the Spa, I did get to hang out by the pool. I was very happy and relaxed. My husband did play golf. He loved the course. I basically, lounged around and did a little shopping. I did eat lunch at Cibolo Moon. It was great! The homemade BBQ chips with chipotle dip was awesome. The servings were Texas-sized. The self parking is a bit far, but it's free. They do offer valet. I am looking forward to going back again, hopefully soon.

name: Royal Palms Resort and Spa
title: “Best Thanksgiving!”
text: The Royal Palm is not a typical hotel. As my family said it felt like home not a hotel. It is old time elegant. You feel and are treated very special by the staff. You can tell they were hand picked not just run of the mill. The hotel was so secluded and private, but so close to downtown Scottsdale. The grounds are beautiful and no detail is left out.

name: Royal Palms Resort and Spa
title: “outstanding”
text: Very friendly and helpful staff. Hotel was well maintained and landscaping in excellent condition

name: The Grand Del Mar
title: “Amazing. Plain and simple.”
text: Stayed here numerous times. Never had anything less than 5 star. Everything is amazing - grounds, rooms, room size and bathroom size, bathrooms have great soaking tubs. Amenities. great for business or leisure. Kids pool. Pet friendly. One of my favorites. True 5 star. Splurged one visit and did Addison. Everything you would think and more. If you need to be downtown San Diego it can be a little bit of a hike. If you need an affordable meal option the coffee shop is perfect just near the lobby. Get some coffee and and a bagel.

name: Library Hotel
title: “Great visit, lovely hotel”
text: Excellent location and hotel facilities are great. Staff we also excellent and very helpful!

name: Residence Inn San Antonio Downtown/Alamo Plaza
title: “The Worst place i have ever stayed in”
text:
I arrived and found a lobby full of fat people in shorts and sandals... the front desk had a counter next to it selling beers and lean cuisine ready meals... i started to worry at this stage.
When i got to my Queen size room i was impressed by the size but it had a horrid 80's style kitchen with a fridge and microwave in there- so ugly, the sockets were off the wall, the linen looked less than clean and the view of the motorway was the icing on the cake. 
I left after 10 minutes never to return again,
americans might like this place, they have all given it great reviews, but as a well travelled european this made my skin crawl. Fortunately i was transferred to the Marriott Plaza up the road which has some character and good service.
stay away!!

name: Dolphin Motel
title: “Quirky - Good Value”
text:
San Diego, CA Dolphin Motel 
April 2007
Service: The registration process was particularly quirky at the Dolphin. They would not take our credit card number over the phone even though they take credit cards at the registration desk. This seemed very odd, as it is 2007. (We were prepared for it based on some previous reviews, however.) We were told we could guarantee the room by check or take our chances that the room would be available if we arrived after 6:00 PM. I decided to wait and talk it over with the significant other. She and I agreed – on THREE things: that there was no reason to send a check; that we would probably get there before 6:00 PM and that there would be no harm if the room was resold. We would simply find a room elsewhere.
When I called back we went through this all again. I explained we would take our chances with the room not being available if we arrived after 6:00 pm. Then they asked for a cell phone number. I wasn’t expecting that and as I am a little protective of the cell number I stated I didn’t want to provide it. This started another round of unnecessary discussion. They seemed unsure if they could reserve the room without the cell phone number. The Dolphin representative then handed the phone over to another rep. We went through the scenario yet again and quickly came to the conclusion that it would be fine for me to reserve a room and take a chance that it would be available if we arrived after 6:00 pm. This seemed a very long route to get to the point where we could actually make a reservation. If the rankings weren’t so stellar, I would have quickly looked elsewhere. I’ll admit I was very curious.
Upon arrival, before 6:00 PM, everything was in order.
Rooms/Cleanliness: Our second story room had a slight view of the marina across the street. The rooms are small and very basic. Ours had one bed, a TV and a refrigerator. Other furniture was of simple board construction. Everything was painted white. The bathroom contained a small shower – no tub. All of the above was VERY clean.
Location: We found the Dolphin to be very convenient to Sea World and Cabrillo National Monument/Point Loma. It is located across from a large sport fishing marina. This is an eclectic neighborhood. While it wasn’t for us, I can see how parking could be a problem in this area.
Value: We paid $71 including tax in April 2007. I have to dock it a point for its quirkiness. However, given the location, cleanliness and the fact that this is San Diego I feel it is an above average value.

name: Residence Inn San Antonio Downtown/Alamo Plaza
