title: “Residence Inn Rocks!”
text:
From arrival to departure, we had an excellent stay at this hotel. We arrived a few hours before check-in, so the front desk clerk suggested we take the trolly to Market Square for lunch while we wait on our room. This was a wonderful recommendation, since Market Square was somewhere we would have never known about had it not been suggested to us. We ended up having a delicious lunch as well as some great shopping. 
The location couldn't be better. We were practically across the street from The Alamo. Our rental car stayed in the parking garage the entire time we were there since The Riverwalk, shopping, restaurants and nightlife were all within a few blocks. 
Very friendly service at the frontdesk. When we called for something like extra towels someone was at our door within a few minutes. The complimentary breakfast was the best we had experienced. Scrambled eggs, sausage, breakfast potatos, waffle stations, cereal, toast, fresh fruit......I could go on and on. I highly recommend this hotel for anyone who wants to experience the history and fun of San Antonio, without paying Riverwalk prices.

name: Dolphin Motel
title: “Absolutely outstanding! Could not ask for a greater place in a great location!”
text:
I stayed at the dolphin for 5 days in June 2006 (I am a student on vacation through the west coast) and found the service to be above what you would find almsot anywhere.
The owner, whose name I have forgotten, (Chief, as I called him) is one of the nicest people I have had the pleasure to meet.I arrived in San Diego not knowing what to do or where to go, and he took the time to explain the best places to go, and how to get to them. This kind man alone is reason enough to stay. For example:
On day 2, my visa card was jammed by my bank in the UK (always let your bank know when you go abroad!!!), leaving me without cash temporarily (my parents sent me some through western union) and the owner offered to loan me some money to get some food. Like I said, a wonderful man!
The rooms were lovely. Extremely clean, wonderful beds with great bathrooms attached, soft towels etc.
The Dolphin also had free DSL and cable TV with many channels, a fridge, and some of the rooms had lovely views of the harbor.
I could not fault the Dolphin in anyway, and as far as value for money goes, I invite people to try to find better. It cost about $50 a night and was worth far more than that.
You do not need to stay anywhere else in San Diego.

name: Homewood Suites San Diego Airport - Liberty Station
title: “The BEST”
text:
Our group of three adults and two children stayed here in Jan 09. We found this hotel via trip advisor.
The suites are wonderful. They are modern, clean, and comfortable. I have high expectations and they were all met or exceeded. There is a full size kitchen. Someone had mentioned that dishwasher detergent wasn't provided, but I asked for some at the front desk and was given 6 packets.
One of the best parts of this hotel is the service. All of the staff were helpful and cheerful. A full hot breakfast is served each morning with a rotation of bacon, sausage, biscuits and gravy, etc. On weeknights, they have a welcome home reception. We were skeptical because we had never had a hotel offer a free dinner option so we had planned to go out each night. However, the food is terrific and there is plenty to eat. For example:meat and meatless lasagna with a garden salad, cold bean salad, garlic bread and cook. 
This hotel costs less than most in san diego because it is not in the popular downtown area, gaslamp area, or harbor area. But, it is only about 5 miles from there and about 3 from the airport.

name: JW Marriott San Antonio Hill Country Resort & Spa
title: “Beautiful resort”
text: This is a wonderful resort. Beautifully appointed. The grounds are well manicured and lovely. Staff are excellent and pay attention to detail. The restaurants and bars are quite good. But this all comes with a huge price tag. Unless they have a special, or you have the bucks, this resort is high dollar.

name: The Grand Del Mar
title: “Surpisingly Spectacular”
text:
It's not really located near anything, but when are merely driving up to the entrance, you realize it doesn't matter.
I'm not sure how old the property is, but gives off a vibe that it is an institution that has been giving 5 star service to hotel clients forever. It is charming and yet grandiose all at the same time. Attention to detail is reflected from the staff (concierge, front desk, bellmen, wait staff, pool staff, etc) to the designs on the moulding on the ceiling of the room.
They somehow manage to decorate boldly (gold, patterns, tassles) withOUT seeming gaudy or overdone. It's warm and welcoming.
I tend to rate hotels based more on staff than amenities, so I will say that I received the BEST service at this hotel... at least as good as any hotel I've ever been in... and I have been in the Mandarin Hotel in Hong Kong, the Peninsula Hotel in Kowloon (Hong Kong), Intercontinentals, Four Seasons, etc. Every person we came into contact with were both courteous and respectful. When they happened to ask you if you needed something, and you did NOT need something, they neither push for you to ask them if you need anything nor do they make you feel like you're wasting their time by sitting in their area and not doing anything. (it's a subtle line that they all seemed to do very well)
Our family of three went (me, wife and 18 month old son) and they included a wooden crib in the room. When I had made the reservation, I included our son's name, and the crib had bedding that was geared toward boys. They also included a small bag of bath materials for babies, including soap, wash clothes, and toys ... these were complimentary. a VERY nice touch!
Complimentary bottles of water were included in the room.
They have 4 pools.... 1 adults only (18 and over), 2 large family friendly pools, and 1 smaller pool that is only 1 foot deep -- great for kids / babies. This is GREAT for kids. 
And yet, you never ever feel like this is a pool for families with kids running around. They seem to treat everyone like an adult with admiration and respect -- even our 18 month old! Upon checkout, they gave our son a small beanie baby toy. another great touch!
We stayed in a Prado suite overlooking the golf course... it seems as though originally they were two individual rooms, and they knocked out a doorway. Made one half into a King size bedroom, and the other into the living room. Both bathrooms remained. 
The entire hotel is spectacularly appointed. The shops are overpriced, and there is not much to do there... We went to Sea World the next day and it was only about a 15 minute drive.
I recommend checking in early, using the pool or spa or whatever relaxation facilities you'd like to use... enjoy the grounds, enjoy the hotel. Then the next day you can go off and explore or enjoy the San Diego activities as much as you like.
It's not in the middle of the hustle and bustle of San Diego, and it's not near the beach...but in my opinion, as long as you'll have this to come back to at the end of the activity filled day, you really can't go wrong. You won't mind driving back here at the end of the day.

name: Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk
title: “Great hotel for a wonderful visit to the Riverwalk.”
text: I've stayed here many times and love the location at the end of the Riverwalk. It's easy to get turned around on the Riverwalk but with this location it was easy to find. It's quiet being at the end. Also love the breakfast and snacks that are offered each afternoon. Such a great value for the money. The rooms are clean and spacious and service has always been great. I now stay at the Drury EVERY time I go to the Riverwalk!!!

name: Library Hotel
title: “Library or Giraffe - you can't go wrong”
text: My wife and I love this hotel. Great rooms. Amazing staff. Great location. If you're up for the extra expense the Jr Suites are totally worth it. And by the way - on the second floor they put out a great breakfast (and snacks and drinks later in the day) in a comfortable atmosphere - so when pricing it against other hotels consider the savings on a NYC breakfast!

name: Dolphin Motel
title: “Fick mycket för pengarna !!!”
text: Jag och min fru letade efter något bra boende i San Diego till rimligt pris då vi rest runt i Californien i två veckor. Vi hittade detta lilla fina motelll med bra läge och mycket trevlig och serviceinriktad personal. Vi tänkte först bara stanna en natt, men det blevt fyra dagar. Rummen är ganska små,men helt ok. Rent och fint, viket vi tycker är viktigt.

name: Westin La Cantera Hill Country Resort
title: “Going above and beyond”
text: Each event that I do at the Westin La Cantera, the staff always goes above and beyond to help! At the most recent event Dawn Moore, Executive Meeting Specialist, made sure that our staff and guests were comfortable and had everything they needed. The night before the event her staff brought us dinner while we were setting up. I have celiac disease and she made sure that each meal was gluten free and never made me feel like a burden when I asked questions for my dietary needs. It was so comforting knowing that she and her team truly cared about us and played a key role in the success of our event and my health!

name: Homewood Suites San Diego Airport - Liberty Station
title: “Can't say enough good!”
text: My favorite part--excellent location. Or is my favorite part the newness? Or the suite layout? This is a beautiful, newly developed neighborhood/area that feels really safe, even at night--still, I appreciated the locked access on all entries. I felt totally safe going to my car late at night, or walking across the free, ample, and well-lit parking lot to the several restaurants in the same complex after dark. This hotel is new and beautiful and right next to the airport, with a free and friendly shuttle to and from--what's not to like? I loved the excitement of airplanes roaring overhead when I was outside--yet the rooms inside were well-insulated against airport noise that might bother anyone. You will have access to free internet, and the hotel does have a locked (accessed by room card) business center so you can read your local newspaper on line or research your next destination! The suites are just down the road from the embarcadero and gaslamp quarter, too, and in the opposite direction is old-town, just a few miles (5 minutes?) away. With three children I absolutely LOVED the suite layout--two bedrooms, TWO bathrooms, and a living room with pull-out couch (three TVs for less arguing) AND full kitchen with large refrigerator, all for less than the price of two separate hotel rooms. My husband and I walked around the neighborhood one morning, noting beautiful new homes, schools, and some new in-process development of old base structures that is pretty exciting! Breakfast at the hotel was included, so that was an additional money-saving benefit I appreciated. We had scrambled eggs every morning, coffee, toast, fruit, home fries, biscuits and gravy or sausage, or make-your-own waffles. I HATED leaving this hotel at the end of my stay! I can't wait to come back. By the way, in reference to a previous poster, we had no weird smells coming from the bay while we were there--probably this is a seasonal occurence or weather-related? That happens in my home town occasionally, too. But we only loved everything about our stay. This is likely the best hotel I've ever stayed in for the money.

name: Pacific Terrace Hotel
title: “Excellent Pick”
text: Just came back and couldn't wait to write a rave review of this hotel. The service is outstanding. If they forgot one small thing- they rushed it right up to our room immediately. Its a great location on the beach- we had a junior suite oceanfront- well worth upgrading to the oceanfront as I don't think the side view would have done it for me. Having breakfast, watching the surfers, dolphins, seals and the local traffic on the "boardwalk' below was very enjoyable and relaxing- even with a 4 year old in tow! Hearing the ocean at night is the best. Pacific Beach is also a great little surfer town, can walk to most restaurants and you are close to La Jolla and not terribly far from anywhere else in the San Diego area. I highly recommend and do not recomend stayign downtown. Nothign there but listening to the train all night (been there and willl avoid at all costs)

name: The Grand Del Mar
title: “It Is My Pleasure”
text:
Stayed here a few weeks ago with 27 family members. We take a family trip each year and have visited Maui (Kea Lani and Ritz Carlton), Grand Caymon (Ritz Carlton), and taken a Mediterranean and Alaskan Cruise with post-cruise stays at Four Seasons Vancouver. The level of service we received during our stay from top to bottom was head and shoulders above the rest. Upon arrival you immediately feel welcome and at check-in we helped ourselves to a snack of cookies and fruit juice and the delivery of our luggage was very prompt. A call to Housekeeping for more hangars took about five minutes at the most and they provided me with more than I requested. As we walked the beautiful grounds we were immediately relaxed and took in all of the scenic lawns, gardens and firepit areas. Our room was on the second floor (three floors total) and overlooked one of the firepit areas which I noticed in the evening would be popular with guests quietly sipping a glass of wine or just visiting. 
Each morning my husband and I would play tennis on one of their two courts and either had breakfast at Club M on the weekend or grabbed a quick bite at the Cent Anni Cafe. If looking for a quick and less expensive option, visit Cent Anni as one morning I had a bowl of oatmeal for $5, I believe, and it was served on white china with brown sugar, almonds, and raisins. Others in the family said that the sandwiches served there were delicious. Several of us also enjoyed Amaya for breakfast and dinner as well as the poolside lunch service. We did not try Addison. 
A few examples of their exemplary service include:
1. Opening Gift Shop up at 10 p.m. so that my niece could get aloe vera for her sunburn.
2. Locating a family member's cane which was lost somewhere within the Resort. 
3. Delivering contact solution to another niece who forgot to pack hers in the suitcase.
4. Reserving a few areas for family pics taken by a photographer on our last day.
I could go on and on but each and every Grand Del Mar staff member had an attitude of "How may I help you" and "We can get that done". 
The rooms are gorgeous and we loved the window which opens (or can be shut at night) between the bedroom and bathroom and, of course, my husband loved the tv built into the bathroom mirror. Housekeeping was very efficient and the chocolate covered oreos and gourmet chocolates left on the bed at night were a very nice touch as well as the comp. bottled water. Also, the beds were ultra-comfy. Mid-week they knocked on the door to switch out the padded seat cushions for our balcony chairs. They almost seem to anticipate your needs.
One afternoon they set up tables, chairs, and umbrellas to present a wildlife display for the kids with an armadillo, boa constrictor, horned bull frog among others which amused not only my younger nieces and nephews but a few of the adults as well. The fresh lemonade served to all was a nice touch. The amount of activities available within the resort could keep you busy; however, if visiting the area for the first time you will want to visit the Zoo, Legoland, downtown San Diego, etc. They will provide you with precise directions if you drive anywhere or if it is within fourteen miles they can provide comp. car service. It is best to plan ahead so that you are able to reserve the shuttle or car service as I believe quite a few make use of this attractive amenity. Have to mention the mini hot tub for the kiddies. So cute and popular with my nieces and nephews. 
In closing the Grand Del Mar is the place to stay whether you just want to relax or as a base for sightseeing. We drove south to downtown San Diego and north to Carlsbad and both places took appr. 25-28 minutes as long as we were not driving during rush hour traffic. La Jolla is very close (fifteen minutes) and the village of Del Mar has a lot of nice restaurants and is a twelve minute drive. We went in between the San Diego Fair and Del Mar Thoroughbread Racing Season so traffic was not as congested. Do yourself a favor and make a visit to this haven.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Sunset Suites - Riverwalk
title: “Best Western was good”
text: We stayed at Best Western for 2 nights whilst we went to see the Spurs play. The hotel is very well located close to the riverwalk. The rooms were very comfortable although a little small for 2 adults and a small child. There was no noise problems as mentioned in other posts. The breakfast was suitable and the service and staff were very good. Would stay here again.

name: Westin La Cantera Hill Country Resort
title: “Great Weekend Get Away”
text:
We just got back from a friends get away weekend at the Wedtin La Cantera. We had a great time!
The majority of our time there was spent by the adult pool. It is secluded from the rest of the family pools with great views of the surrounding hills. The waitstaff was extremely attentive. Dani, Cody and Rob took excellent care of us and we never had an empty glass. It was hands down the best pool side service I've ever experienced at a resort. 
Both nights we had dinner down the road at the Shops at La Cantera. The resort provides frequent shuttle service to the shops, and the drivers were prompt and courteous. 
We had breakfast at Brennan's one morning. The buffet was good, and the omelet bar was great. 
We went for massages at the spa to end the trip. The spa was nice, quiet and relaxing, but not as nice as what you find at other resorts. My massages therapist, Chris, totally made up for the lack of a steam room. He was awesome! I had the 75 minute deep tissue massage, it was worth every penny.
I would go to the La Cantera in a heart beat!

name: Royal Palms Resort and Spa
title: “A magical place that is one of a kind”
text:
I don't even know where to begin when reviewing the Royal Palms... first of all, this is a place like no other I have EVER stayed. Because of that, my Husband and I have come here every summer for the past 3 years, for either his birthday or mine. This year, we came for his birthday and it was very important that it be special because we had a family tragedy the previous year on his birthday. With the help of the romance planner at the hotel, this trip was once again very memorable and special.
The Royal Palms service is by far the best I've ever had at any hotel. Once you arrive you feel like you're in a different place. The grounds help make it feel secluded and lush, even in the middle of the HOT summer. The staff at the pool, especially Jose, are amazing and refill your drinks constantly and move umbrellas in the heat to provide shade. They also remember your name and treat you like family, which is so rare nowadays. Of course the food is great and no matter what you ask of them, they will make it happen for you.
Go to the Royal Palms, you won't be disappointed. They treat you like royalty... such a wonderfully magical place.

name: Westin La Cantera Hill Country Resort
title: “Girls Getaway”
text: I flew in from NY and another friend flew in from Dallas to surprise a San Antonio friend on her 50th. What a great time! The spa was excellent, pools were pristine, and dinner at Francesca's was fabulous. We all agreed that the service throughout the hotel was some of the best any of us have ever experienced. I will be returning with my family on my next trip to Texas. Thank you La Cantera for a great stay.

name: Hotel Elysee
title: “Great mini vacation”
text:
Just got back from NYC after a wonderful weekend! Stayed at the Hotel Elysee (6th time) and said once again to my wife, " I will stay nowhere else in NYC". A true diamond in the rough! Greated with a smile from all members of the staff we were very impressed with the assistance of both Chris and Craig at the front desk. From directions to reccomendations these two gentelmen were "spot on". The room was excellent and the location to EVERYTHING in the city made for a perfect weekend. My daughter turned 16 and requested a weekend in the city....She got her request and we, the family, had a great time! Thanks again Hotel Elysee and staff for making yet another trip to NYC a truly great experience. We will be looking for our next time to visit! Keep up the great work!
Chuck Brooks and family.

name: Westin La Cantera Hill Country Resort
title: “The best ever”
text: The best family vacation is at the Westin La Cantera Hill Country Resort there is always something to do with the kids adults get to relax the staff is super friendly always go out there way to make your stay wonderful... The spa is one in a million ms.Tina is a goddess on the spa she will make you stress free..... The restaurants and the food are amazing and staff is amazing also....... Everybody should go check it out for there self you will not regret it........ Mr. And Mrs. Washington

name: TownePlace Suites San Antonio Downtown
title: “Great hotel near the Riverwalk, Rivercenter Mall and the Alamo”
text:
This hotel was a great place to stay for our family visit to the Riverwalk, Rivercenter Mall and the Alamo — all are in walking distance. We just left our car with the valet and avoided the hassles of driving and parking downtown. 
The room was nice, with a full refrigerator, dishwasher, cooktop and other things that would make an extended stay more comfortable. 
The continental breakfast was better than others I've had, with a couple of different hot items in addition to the usual fruit, cereal, pastries and waffles.
Overall, a nice place to stay in downtown San Antonio.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Sunset Suites - Riverwalk
title: “Best Best Western!”
text: My wife and I just returned from our weekend getaway in San Antonio. We usually dont stay at Best Westerns when we travel because we have had some not so pleasant experiences in the past. When we called the Hampton Inn for reservations they were sold out and recommended this hotel which I was a little reluctant to reserve. The person taking our reservation was very helpful and polite and did a great job describing the hotel. When we arrived we were quite surprised at the beautiful furnishings and decor of the lobby. The room was just as nice as it was a large suite with plenty of room. I have to admit that this was one of the cleanest rooms I have ever stayed in. The rooms are decorated with earth tones and very nice furnishings. We took the trolley downtown which was very convenient. We also thoroughly enjoyed the hot breakfast in the morning and the older gentleman who was cooking was a real delight. We will definitely be back on our next trip to San Antonio!

name: Royal Palms Resort and Spa
title: “Gorgeous Oasis in the Desert”
text:
Touted as the most romantic hotel in Phoenix, this resort delivers with gorgeous grounds, brilliant color even during the hottest month, nooks & crannies coaxing exploration, and a cozy pool.
What's not so beautiful is the inconsistent service ranging from excellent to fair at best. The valet guys are friendly, fast, and eager to help. Another reviewer mentioned a sense of a "tip mentality" but we didn't experience that. The $25+ daily resort fee covers all tips & gratuities which was published in several areas throughout our stay.
We began our 25th anniversary getaway with a couples massage at the resort spa. The massage therapists were fantastic, giving an excellent massage, and were both very professional. Desk staff: the mostly female employees were friendly and professional. But there was a gentleman working the front area who gave an unfriendly vibe and both hubby & I felt we were intruding. I saw him interacting with other guests and noticed his lack of friendliness; he never did crack a smile.
Pool: We enjoyed the cozy pool and enjoyed socializing with other guests. Homero did an excellent job refilling ice water and raced around filling food & drink orders. He was very accomodating and a joy. We really missed him the following day as the other staff person was adequate in his role but not outstanding.
Fitness room: Small, several treadmills, and a few weight machines. It's open 24/7 but the fruit wasn't fresh and the water containers weren't replenished. Someone should probably check on the freshness of the items from time to time. I worked out at 7:00 a.m. and found it lacking.
Room: We booked a casita and it was very lovely. Housekeeping did a fine job keeping our room loving great.
T. Cook's: Was really looking forward to an excellent experience and it was good, but certainly not great. The best part of the meal were the desserts, and they were excellent. Be sure to try the chocolate fantasy.
Romance quotient: The resort knew we were celebrating our 25th anniversary and spread lovely rose petals on our table at T. Cook's. They also decorated our dessert plates with "Happy 25th Anniversary." Very nice touches.
At the pool, newlyweds shared how the resort gave them a rose petal turndown, chocolate strawberries, champagne, and a lovely card. We thought that was fantastic.
After dinner, we returned to our casita and found a rose petal turndown, the chocolates, and a card from our friends. I learned later that the resort does note big anniversaries but told me, "your friend beat us to the punch." Oops.... I certainly wasn't expecting the rose petals, etc. but a card from the resort would've been nice. 
The resort is beautiful and it felt like we weren't in Arizona. But the service was too inconsistent ranging from outstanding to fair. I do hope management recognizes the need for training in customer relations.

name: The Grand Del Mar
title: “We loved it and we'll be back”
text:
The hotel was beautiful, very elegant, felt like a grand hotel in Europe, except the room was condsiderably larger. I liked the expresso machine for coffee in the morning (very easy to use and everything was provided for it). The staff was welcoming and very gracious, every need attended to.
We were upgraded because we booked through this site and we received a resort credit and free breakfast the next day.
I would definitely stay there again and book through this site again!
LG/ San Diego

name: Hotel Elysee
title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text:
I read a few of the VERY FEW bad reviews of Elysee and had to laugh. One said it was too noisy on the street. That's like complaining about too many lights in Vegas. Obviously a rookie. If you want quiet, get a cabin in Yellowstone, but then the whiner would probably complain about the moose being too loud. Hotel Elysee was a great place for us to take our annual theater tour of the Big Apple. We hired a private driver (recommended by Elysee) to get us through rush hour from LGA, and he was terrific - unlike some of the psychotic NY cabbies who test your blood pressure meds. From arrival to departure six days later, the Elysee staff was terrific, friendly and very helpful, and the staff on the 2nd floor goodies room was tremendous.
Elysee's location is perfect - several blocks from Central Park and Rockefeller Center. No need to wait for a cab, as nearly every theater and museum is no more than a 10-20 minute walk, and you are five minutes from two major sub stations, which connect you to anywhere. We walked to shows on Times Square, Carnegie Hall and the Met at Lincoln Center.
No hesitation in recommending the Elysee. It's a small renovated boutique in an older building, so don't expect fast elevators, large rooms and room service. The price is high but competitive, and the rooms are nicely appointed and comfortable. It's noisy because it's NYC, so get over it.

name: Hotel Indigo San Diego Gaslamp Quarter
title: “Fantastico”
text:
Uno dei migliori alberghi in cui abbiamo mai soggiornato! Tutto ottimo! Personale molto gentile, struttura bellissima e ottima posizione, a sloi 5 minuti a piedi da tutti i locali della zona. Il panorama dalla nostra stanza era l'unica cosa modesta, ma non avevamo fatto alcuna richiesta in proposito.
Tra i servizi a disposizione dei clienti anche due iMac con stampante per qualsiasi esigenza, noi ci siamo stampati le carte della città e dei mezzi pubblici.

name: JW Marriott San Antonio Hill Country Resort & Spa
title: “Awesome and relaxing!”
text: We met friends from Minnesota for Easter vacation. There was something for everyone to do. Play golf or just watch the Masters.....lazy river, slide or just lay by the pool. The food was awesome and the kids activities were limitless. It was hard to drag ourselves away from the resort to go to the Riverwalk!

name: Westin La Cantera Hill Country Resort
title: “Great for Families”
text:
Very nice family resort hotel in upscale area. 
Pros:
-Resort itself. Nice, spacious, comfortable.
-Facilities: Extensive. Pools, gym, grounds, etc. 
-Activities: Lots of activities for childern
-Views: Very nice of Hill Country
-Location: Next to Six Flags Texas and Shops of La Cantera 
-Shuttle: Free for hotel guests
-Service: Overall good
Cons:
-Overrun with children. Screaming children in entryway and lobby is not a good idea of a relaxing vacation. Memorial Day weekend approx 150-180 kids in hotel. 
-Rooms: Standard room was small. Property could use a little sprucing up as well.
-Gym: Equipment could use some updating
Overall, wasn't a bad stay, but I probably wouldn't be back.

name: Westin La Cantera Hill Country Resort
title: “Great experience!”
text: We stayed at the Westin La Cantera for Mother's Day weekend, and it was fantastic! I loved the pool area, and that it was open 24 hours a day. The room was very clean and comfortable, very nice pillows. This is the best hotel I have stayed in.

name: Comfort Suites Alamo/Riverwalk
title: “Some Positives, Some Negatives...”
text:
The Positives-
1. All the usual good things like every hotel and great staff. This place was in a good location and had a complimentary shuttle service to get you to the Riverwalk. The shuttle driver Manual was very friendly and helpful. 
2. The front desk actually telephoned us 10 minutes after we checked into our room to see if everything was all right. Great service.
3. We loved that they host a wine and cheese reception for guests every Tue/Wed/Thu - that is so generous and lovely. The hostess Georgia puts a lot of effort into it and is very friendly. We have never seen any hotel do this before especially putting out free alcohol. Nice touch.
The Negatives -
1. They have such a large car park it's a shame they charge you $10 per day to use it. We are not a hundred per cent sure but we noticed what we think are some free parking spots on the street right outside the hotel so something for future guests to take note of. Even their own shuttle was parked there. Check it our for yourself as we are not sure if it is really free.
2. One morning we had breakfast after nine and since we had to wait until 10am for the next shuttle service, we waited in our room till about 9:45am leaving our Do Not Disturb sign on the door until we were ready to leave. When we came back that night our room was not made up. After making enquiries we were told that if you leave your DND sign out after 9am then they will not make your room up! If they are going to have such a rule perhaps it would be good to inform guests??? I have never stayed anywhere and encountered this even when we have left our room as late as 11am. I agree that there should be a cut off time but 9am is too early and Housekeeping should always check twice after they have finished other rooms on the floor. Some people are here on vacation and don't want to be out of their rooms by 9am. Luckily they give you lots of towels to start with so no biggie.
3. One morning I saw about 4 rooms which had their room doors left unlocked and were unattended (door leans against the security bar so that it cannot be closed). Now I do not know if these were checked out rooms left open so the housekeeper would know which room to clean next or just rooms for daily cleaning or even perhaps renovations being carried out on them. But this is the second time I have encountered a hotel with this unacceptable practice. The hotel has a sign in the room that tells you that if anything goes missing from the room then that is your approval to allow a charge for the item to be put against your credit card. Even if these were recently checked out rooms it is unfair to leave them unattended in case someone else goes in and takes something after I have vacated like their unattached hair dryer which I then have to pay $45 dollars for. If a room is not being cleaned by the housekeeper then it should not be left unattended for any reason.
4. Another morning I saw a room by the elevator left unattended. No housekeeper was around. The doors at this hotel are not self closing so if you don't pull it close it will actually remain unlocked. I informed the front desk of this just in case the guest had actually left it that way without realising it. 45 minutes later still nothing was done and the door was still left that way. If it was a checked out room then see point number three. Anyone could have easily entered and taken anything. 
Overall this is an excellent hotel except for one major issue to be aware about. Basically, always, always keep your valuables locked up. Or carry them with you when there is no safe in the room. Perhaps this leaving doors opened by hotels is more of a usual practise than we realise?

name: Hyatt Place San Antonio-North/Stone Oak
title: “What a shame....”
text:
This hotel had an overall rating of #2 for San Antonio. We haven't stayed in others, but it's hard to believe that rating. The service was terrific. The room large and clean and modern. The breakfast was one of the better "free" ones. BUT the noise from the nearby highway was loud, and didn't soften much through the night. Plus the hotel is nowhere near anything special about San Antonio.
So the staff did the best they could and the hotel is nice - but I'd rethink based on those two major handicaps.

name: Library Hotel
title: “Very disappointed”
text: I travel a few times a year to NYC and have stayed at many great hotels. I wanted to try something new and decided to try the library hotel based on the many wonderful reviews on trip advisor. I reserved a junior king suite. After a long trip I arrived with my friend only to be told our room was not available as someone decided to extend their stay. We were downgraded to a queen deluxe. $100 would be taken off my rate making the room $419. While breakfast and the wine & cheese hour were a nice touch I would have much rather stayed a the W or a Kimpton and paid for the extras to actually have the room I booked and paid for. I have never been downgraded before usually the opposite. This trip was planned well in advance and a lot of thought went into choosing our hotel. I am sad because I was hoping this was going to be my new favorite hotel to stay in NYC, it was not.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “Delightful, friendly staff- good value, great service and thoroughly relaxing!”
text:
The hotel is in a good central location- right on a North/South subway line and a fair walking distance from Time Square....
The staff are very friendly and helpful. Professional manner, courteous and smiley.
Rooms were very comfortable, clean and with great beds.
Wine and cheese each evening and a really good breakfast are strong selling points- they set you up for the day and there was nothing better after a hard day than a glass of Prosecco!!
Thoroughly recommended

name: JW Marriott San Antonio Hill Country Resort & Spa
title: “Lovely Property”
text:
This is a beautiful resort but it is imperative that you have a car if you plan to do anything in town. The staff is friendly and helpful as you would expect and the amenities are fantastic. 
A warning, the spa is very pricey as is valet parking. There is a daily resort fee charged on top of the room rate. This is not a property to visit if you hope to cut corners. 
I enjoyed my stay, it was very relaxing and I will probably return again next year.

name: Royal Palms Resort and Spa
title: “Beautiful!”
text:
Beautiful, winding, quaint property with flowers everywhere~
Attentive staff and excellent food!
We would definitely come back

name: Comfort Suites Alamo/Riverwalk
title: “Hotel isn't where they say it is”
text: We were staying here three nights to enjoy the Riverwalk, etc. The building is right up against the expressway so the traffic noise is constant 24/7. By their description the hotel was located 0.1 miles from both the Riverwalk and the Alamo. WRONG!!! It was a $6 cab ride each way. I called Choice Hotels customer service and they checked their website with me, and yes, it states 0.1 miles. In reality it's more like 0.8 miles. When I asked at the front desk, they told me they were trying to get it changed, but I shouldn't be concerned b/c it was only a $6 cab ride. With the 100+ temps in San Antonio, my husband and I had hoped to do alot of "in and out" at our hotel while enjoying all that the San Antonio area has to offer. We have been loyal Choice Hotel consumers, but come to find out that we could have had a balcony room overlooking the river at the Westin for about the same price. In this case our loyalty didn't pay off.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “Hotel Giraffe wins by a long neck!”
text:
We initially chose Hotel Giraffe from its rating and reviews in trip advisor and if anything it exceeded our expectations.
As we were getting married during our stay, we didn't want to leave anything to chance. The Hotel staff, particularly Franklyn could not have done more for us. They were warm, welcoming and helpful at ALL times. Whatever information they couldn't provide there and then was researched for us and presented as soon as possible.
The room was spotless and tastefully furnished in a chic boutique style. 
Tea, coffee, fruit juices, fruits and biscuits are available 24 hours in the hotel lobby.
Breakfast was a continental style with fresh fruit, bagels, pastries, cereals, etc again presented by courteous and attentive staff.
We particularly liked the intimate and romantic atmosphere of the Hotel. The inclusive wine, cheese and pianist every evening 6-8pm provided a perfect start to an evening out in NYC.
The Midtown location was perfect for all the major sights. There are plenty of bars, restaurants and clubs within a 100 yards.
Our wedding in Central Park was all one could wish for, but, the whole experience was firmly underpinned by our satisfaction with the hotel.

name: The Grand Del Mar
title: “Perfect place for a meeting”
text:
This place deserves 5 stars. The grounds are absolutely pristine and the service is even better. The room, while a bit bigger than average for a resort, was quiet. The best part was the bathroom - it has to be 20 feet long, with two sinks, a tub, shower, closet, etc. In the room, as well as the grounds, every attention to detail was taken. The place is fairly new and not that crowded, so I hope that this quality keeps up.
 While this hotel is fairly close to the freeway it is not exactly in the middle of San Diego attractions. It is fine for a business meeting. Unless all you want to do is go to play golf and/or the spa and/or just hike it is fine, otherwise there is not much to attract you. While not as luxurious or the same level or service, La Costa (just up the road) would be a better choice for a getaway.
 The only complaint was that the food for such a first class place was barely above average. There was nothing special about it except for the orange juice, which was one of the best ever at any hotel.

name: Hyatt Place San Antonio-North/Stone Oak
title: “Clean and nice place to stay”
text: This hotel seems very new inside. They provide a free breakfast every morning. It was very busy while we were there, as it was spring break. However, we had better service here than at the Westin La Cantera (which is probably twice the price!). The rooms are large, with a bedroom area partially separated from a living room area that had a full couch, a desk, and a kitchenette. It would have been quite comfortable to have a family in this room. They have a 24 hour snack counter in the lobby for late night snacks and drinks (even alcohol, which I consider a plus). I never had a problem with highway noise and I live in the country. Great place to stay!!

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Class and comfort”
text: My husband is a huge Flyers fan ad we try to get to Philly at least once a year to see them play. Last spring we tried another hotel but nothing measures up to the Sofitel. Great location, super swanky hotel bar with great drinks and a really friendly staff. Not to mention the delicious breakfast buffet downstairs at Chez Colette! This year we went with friends and all four of us just loved our trip and can't wait to get back to the Sofitel come playoff time...(hope I didn't jinx us....)

name: Hotel Elysee
title: “Perfect location”
text: We were very pleased with this hotel. Having stayed at quite a few of the top hotels, it was not a five star hotel; but the accommodations were very nice; it was clean; the staff very friendly and helpful; the location was perfect especially for the events we were attending. And the price was very reasonable, especially considering that breakfast was included which made it very convenient not to have to find a restaurant each morning. We would recommend this hotel.

name: Pacific Terrace Hotel
title: “Loved the Location, little overpriced”
text:
We stayed in an ocean view suite ie king bed and sleeper sofa. Sleeper sofa was supposed to be queen but one 7 year old barely fit. The accommodations themselves were above average but not excellent, though they were very clean.
The staff here are definitely their best asset. Friendly, approachable and just very hospitable all round. Also very family friendly.
The breakfast on offer was cheap and unappetizing, considering the price of a $550 a night suite - yogurt, dry muffins, bagels and pretty bad coffee. Had to pay for parking each night - it should be included in the price of the pricey rooms! 
The view from our room was spectacular. To be able to open the doors and have an unobstructed ocean and sunrise/ sunset view was unbelievable. But right outside of the hotel ie in front of all the rooms is a very busy boardwalk, which kept going pretty much all of the time so patio privacy was a little limited. But the beach itself was also very close and accessible so it was a fair trade off.
Local area is pretty run down but seemed safe enough. We found several very good family run type restaurants within 10 minutes walking distance which were reasonable and good.

name: The Grand Del Mar
title: “Very nice time at a corporate event at The Grand”
text:
Setting: Beautiful, but note that this is not in Del Mar (or even that close). Located on the Penasquitos Canyon Preserve, this is five miles inland. For those familiar with Aviara and La Costa, this is a little more rustic as there is much less development surrounding The Grand
Hotel: Very modern, but the other reviewers are correct - the decor is way over the top. Its supposed to be "moorish" but it feel boorish. Almost like someone had a great idea but got carried away.
Facilities: Did not play golf, but the course looks awesome. Pools are very nice and perfectly heated - not too hot, not too cold. Spa is first rate.
Food: Ate lunch by the pool and the food was actually lower priced than I expected for this type of resort. Beer for $6 - I can handle that. Heck, I pay that on an airplane. Did not try the restaurants, but had a drink in each of the bars (lobby and Amaya). Both were above average for a hotel bar.
Service: Overall very good. Housekeeping for us was particularly strong. Had turndown both nights and the second night someone actually folded clothes we had lying around!

name: The Rittenhouse Hotel
title: “Perfect girls get-away with my teenage daughter!”
text:
I do not have enough nice things to say about my recent stay at the Rittenhouse Hotel with my daughter. I made reservations about a month in advance and took advantage of the Rittenhouse Relief package that included a $100 restaurant credit. When reserving I explained that this stay was a special treat in advance of my daughter's departure for college and requested a complimentary room upgrade if one was available.
We arrived early on Sunday morning to check our bags and head to the spa for the day. The spa facilities are disappointing, but the services were top-notch. After the spa, we completed our check in. I never mentioned my previous request for an upgrade if available, but we were assigned a beautiful suite on the nineth floor. The room was beautifully appointed and my daughter was so thrilled with her special treat. She enjoyed a soak in the large bathtub in the marble bathroom before dinner.
We had dinner at Lacroix. After reviewing the menu online (wonderful, but expensive) I had planned for us to have dinner at the bar so that our bill would not exceed our credit. It turns out that Sunday evenings feature an "Appetite Stimulus" menu for $35 per person in Lacroix, and 50% off a bottle of wine!! We had a wonderful meal, with impeccible service seated at a window table overlooking Rittenhouse Square.
We slept late Monday morning and left the car and our bags at the hotel while we wandered the shops on Walnut Street and generally enjoyed the city.
We learned from both the staff at the spa and Lacroix that Sundays are very quiet days at the hotel, and I am sure that fact is what enabled us to enjoy the upgrade - and I will surely remember that when I make reservations to return for some other special treat.
A special note about the staff - every single staff person we encountered at the hotel was professional, friendly and gracious without any hint of pretention. A+++ and many thanks for helping me make this a special time for my daughter.

name: Hyatt Place San Antonio-North/Stone Oak
title: “Great Hotel; new and spacious rooms with a lot of extras”
text:
I was in San Antonio for a wedding during the July 4th weekend. Due to an AA meeting, all the rooms in SA seemed booked. We booked this room through Priceline on the day of arrival. We got a great deal, considering the peak period. This hotel is located right off the 281 and 1604. It almost backs into a 24hr Wal-Mart, Costco, and a number of fast food places. The location was very quiet. I was amazed with the hotel, I would compare this to a four star. The hotel has ample parking with a security guard outside all night. We came home at 2 AM a couple nights and saw him there.
It took me a couple days to realize that the hotel has a free continental breakfast. The usual cereal, bread, yoghurt, fresh fruit. Breakfast is served until 9:30. There is also an order window beside the breakfast so you can order hot items, if you wish. The various seating areas get pretty full in the morning but there are lots of places to sit, including the patio outside.
The hotel has free wireless internet but it was a bit slow. You can use the two computers in the lobby to check email and print boarding cards. 
The rooms are very well appointed and large. The bathroom was a bit small and the sink was outside in the room but the room itself was pretty big with a flat screen tv, desk, 2 beds, and a seating area with a sofa bed. We slept 4 comfortably.
All in all a great hotel if you don't need to be downtown. However, it is close to all major freeways but be careful, 281 backs up in rush hour.

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Great one night stay”
text: My wife and I visited Philly to celebrate our anniversary and take in an Eagles game. I stayed at the Sofitel in D.C on business years ago and wanted to try the one in Philly. Great location, and service was above par. We've stayed at Westins many times and actually purchased their heavenly bed through Nordstrom but we have never experienced a mattress as comfortable as the one at the Sofitel! You are guaranteed a good nights sleep.

name: Hotel Elysee
title: “Fantastic Stay”
text: My husband and I stayed for one night back in August. We were in NYC for a Yankees game and some sight seeing. Firstly the location is great.....within walking distance of a lot of great sites. The subway station is close by and we got to Yankee stadium no problem. The hotel is great for NYC standards, I stayed at many different NYC hotels of greater and equal standards and enjoyed my stay here even more. We took advantage of the free prosecco/wine happy hour. Was perfect before we headed out for dinner. And the breakfast was great.....we still could not believe it was included with our stay. The room was nice, we had no issues, it was clean, comfortable bed, and it was pretty quiet. Our tv did not work at first, but staff quickly came and figured out it was not plugged in...whoops. Great stay and will definitely stay again!

name: Westin La Cantera Hill Country Resort
title: “Amazing Golf Course, Staff is very helpful”
text: My husband and I are both realators so we hardly get a vacation at all. La Cantera was the ideal location to get away from it all. Everybody here made our stay worth while. The resort and the staff are beautiful. We played the resort course one day and had lunch at the clubhouse. Christine, our waitress, was full of laughter. The food here is very appitizing. Another day we lounged around by the adult pool. David was our server and made us feel as if he was our own personal cabana boy. He offered great suggestions for resturants at the hotel and around the area. The Heavenly Bed really is heavenly and the rooms are a decent size as well. This place has a great location as it is conviently located across the street from an outdoormall. Overall me and my husband were very please with our choice and will be returning to La Cantera soon.

name: JW Marriott San Antonio Hill Country Resort & Spa
title: “Best Family Resort in TEXAS”
text: If you want a family resort- this is the best one! They have a miniature waterpark for the kids/ adults. The property is gorgeous! Will go back this year!

name: Westin La Cantera Hill Country Resort
title: “Wonderful place”
text:
Stayed two nights in September 2011. 
It is extremely well kept. The room was clean and fresh. The public areas indise the hotel were also very clean and well maintained. The exteriors were well manicured. My main negative about it is that it doesn't have a well marked jogging path. There is a nature trail, but it did not seem suitable for me to go running. As a result, I accidentally ended up running on the adjacent golf course. There were no golfers on the course, but running on the course is against the rules. 
I was there for a small convention and on the second day, a larger and louder group had their meeting next door. The staff changed us to another meeting room during the lunch break. Minor inconvenience, but I expected that the staff would have realized beforehand that the other group was going to be loud. 
All in all, great place.

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Downtown Hotel
title: “Fraud!!!”
text: I nve actually stayed at the hotel. I did make a reservation which I cancelled due to plans to go to Atlantic city instead. I was later billed by the hotel for the room and was told that someone had in fact stayed at the hotel in my room under my name and charged it to my credit card. Hmmm, who would have my name , credit card # and exp. date except for a hotel employee? I have tried to settle this w/ the hotel but have been ignored and my credit card company is in the process of disputing the charge. WARNING: there are obviously some scam artists working here- be careful!

name: Chelsea Pines Inn
title: “Chelsea Pines Inn, New York”
text:
We liked very much the friendly and welcoming atmosphere of the Hotel. We could at any moment get help, advice and interesting tips about Chelsea and other places of interest in New York, useful information of the subway system, trains and the airport. We found every day a newsletter full of actuel information of concerts, small unknown museums, art galleries, places to dine and so forth. Incredibly useful and interesting.
We could even have our excellent breakfast in the garden and if one wanted something extra it was available in a minute.
We hope to come back to New York and hope to stay here again.

name: Westin La Cantera Hill Country Resort
title: “Great Service”
text: The Resort is beautiful and everyone was very attentive. I stayed on the Club Level for Business. The lounge was convenient and Paulina Castanon made sure that I had everything I wanted. Had a late night dinner in the restaurant and again the service and attention were excellent. I would certainly stay here again.

name: JW Marriott San Antonio Hill Country Resort & Spa
title: “Great resort for a getaway”
text: We stayed here after making a last minute change of plans. At 97% occupancy when we arrived with last minute reservations, the hotel staff was courteous, pleasant and accommodating. It was busy, but not overwhelming and felt festive. The resort is beautiful and relaxing. With teens, we did find they were lacking in activities very quickly, probably my only complaint. 2-3 days was more than enough time at the pools for them. The pools lay out very nicely with the adult pool overlooking the golf course. The lazy river was nice and relaxing. There are plenty of umbrellas for shade if you desire. The two slides were fun, one much more tame then the other. There was never more than a few minute wait for anything. The food was quite good and poolside service adequate. Alcoholic concoctions were expensive and very light on the alcohol. We brought a small cooler and no one gave us a hard time. The workout facilities were adequate and headphones provided if needed. Chilled towels were a nice plus. We were going to stay at La Canterra, but the hot lobby and hallways with a lack of decent wireless Internet made the JW Marriott a much deserving choice.

name: Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk
title: “Very reasonable on the riverwalk”
text: The hotel is located right on the Riverwalk, though it is not on the main strip. We received a very reasonable rate for Memorial day weekend. The hotel is rated at 4 stars on some website but I would give it 3 to 3.5. The room was nice. It had a very modern feel to it with brown and teal decorations. The staff was very friendly! The hot breakfast and evening reception was okay but it was free. We sprung for a terrace room, but we were placed on the second tower on the twelfth floor. You could hardly see the riverwalk, which was a little disappointing. I had stayed in a third floor balcony room before at another facility and it was great. Also to get to the second tower you have to go up to the sixth floor, then take the breezeway and get on another elevator. This was very annoying in the morning when my dog needed to go outside.

name: Comfort Suites Alamo/Riverwalk
title: “Amazing service, clean and large rooms at a very good rate!”
text: Read some good reviews about this comfort suites and i am absolutely amazed. They treat me like a 5 star hotel would. Rooms are great, staff is super friendly. The owner actually came and personally asked how our stay was. Feel very comfortable at this hotel and highly recommend it. Will stay here from now on!

name: Chelsea Pines Inn
title: “What a find!”
text: I would highly recommend the Chelsea PInes Inn. The rooms are exceptional and the staff attentive and very friendly. One reaaly nice touch is getting the daily newsletter each morning...especially interesting was the bread choice of the day! Great location and a superb breakfast choice. The themed rooms were delightful. Would definitely go back again!

name: The Westin Riverwalk
title: “Beautiful Hotel in Great Location”
text:
This is me and my husband's first time staying at a Westin, and we loved it! 
The hotel is in great shape with beautiful design. You can tell that every piece of decor was expensive. Everything from the light fixtures, drapery, furniture, carpet, looked brand spanking new. The lobby has several sitting areas and a couple of large balconies with lots of furniture for guests to go sit on and look at the riverwalk.
Check-in was quick and they actually pay attention. When I booked through their website, I requested the highest floor possible for my category (Deluxe King Balcony), and sure enough, we had the top floor of the hotel! It had a great view of the riverwalk, hotel pool, and Tower of the Americas.
We are cheapskates but decided to splurge and get a nice hotel downtown so that we can just walk to wherever we needed to go. The Westin was a great location for that. We never had to walk more than 8 blocks to get to great restaurants.
Another way we cut costs is parking our car in the garage across the street from the hotel. If you're not disabled, you should definitely park your own car. The garage is literally about 20 steps across from the lobby. It cost us $15 to self-park. I'm not sure how much valet service costs but I know it's not worth it unless you have a TON of luggage! 
As with most hotels, room service and pay-per-view movies are expensive. I'm talking, $8 for a bowl of cereal and $18 for each movie expensive lol. But, it's expected that hotels jack up the price for things of that nature. It's your choice to use it or not. =)
We will definitely be staying at the Westin again when go to San Antonio!

name: Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak Resort
title: “Rooms need some updating”
text:
Positives:
 - Friendly & service oriented lobby staff (front desk, bellman) - very helpful & quickly offered assistance 
 - Rooms include coffee maker, large in-room safe, refrigerator
 - Two rooms - a bedroom & separate living area - the desk/sofa/chair living area was nice sized.
 - Reasonably priced food/drink at hotel restaurant
 - Nice chairs at pool
Negatives:
 - Rooms needs updating -- lots of stains on furniture, floors & walls
 - Rooms in need of maintenance - door stuck/hard to open, dead-bolt wouldn't fit/didn't work, very slow drain in tub (ankle deep water before hot water starts)
While other rooms may be better...my room had 2 double beds & not sized for that - one bed blocked the entry of the room so could not get suitcase through straight-forward (bed blocked about 2/3 of doorway). There is a very small/cramped balcony - however, as it faced a parking lot, not inviting.

name: SpringHill Suites Phoenix Downtown
title: “Very nice”
text: Nive rooms. Good location downtown. Close to sports venues and area seems okay at night. The front desk staff are very helpful and friendly. Would definitely stay here again. Nice breakfast in lobby-- first one I've had where they offered oatmeal. Very good!

name: Arizona Grand Resort & Spa
title: “Nice place to stay for a conference”
text: Had a nice stay in a large, two-room suite that was very clean. Only real gripe was the price of mini-bar water and pop and fact that hotel is a Pepsi place and I'm a Coke person. Would stay again. Very spread out so walking is part of the experience. Having a car was great for dining off site.

name: LaQuinta Inn
title: “Good for the money!”
text: Convenient to the airport. Clean room. Comfortable bed. No complaints. Recommend.

name: Residence Inn Phoenix
title: “June 2012 visit”
text: This is one of the nicer Residence Inns I've stayed. The kitchen was like an apartment and had a freestanding range, dishwasher, microwave and refrigerator. The bathroom had a separate dressing area from the toilet and tub/shower. The staff was very friendly and helpful. This location is on the service road to I-17. The highway is always audible

name: Motel 6 Phoenix West
title: “Sleepless night”
text: My wife and I stayed the night of January 23, 2012 after a 500 mile road trip. As we were falling asleep at 10:30pm, we heard the sound of two diesel truck engines right outside our window. Soon, we heard mechanical noises and work crews shouting to each other. I went outside and found two High Desert Communications boom trucks working on a cell tower 20 feet from the building. I asked the crew foreman how I was supposed to sleep through this, and he said there was nothing I could do because they could work there anytime, but would be finished by Midnight. Instead, the work continued all night with shouting, truck engines and boom noises right outside my room. I complained (loudly - my bad) to the Motel manager and I got credit for a free night's stay - thanks. Shame on High Desert Communications for ruining my stay and that of others. The Motel 6 manager said High Desert never contacts Motel 6 before starting work, even at night. I recommend you not stay here until the cell tower gets removed.

name: Budget Lodge of Phoenix
title: “Reception made difference”
text:
When I saw the place I was not impressed! I entered the lobby and was received by "Sheila" with a friendly smile. I requested a room and got #210. It was clean and appropriate for a short stay and, as I was in an "unofficial" business trip, adequate. It was also surprisingly quiet for a place central and very close to a highway! I requested a cooler a/c, a fridge and microwave in my room. For a very small charge (@ $2 /day) I got what I requested immediately! "Randy", a very friendly and efficient security guard fixed the a/c and installed the items.
In a "nutshell"< I would not recommend the place for a honey moon, but certainly for a short, very economic stay, ideal for backpackers and travelers in a budget. I am a bit of a snob and prefer 5 star hotels(unfortunately they come with comparable prices!) but I am also very adaptable. "Randy" and "Sheila" made the difference! If the owner would spend a bit on TLC the place could attract a better clientele! Do not expect luxury, remember what you pay and have a good time....

name: Library Hotel
title: “Love The Library!”
text: I understand all of the good reviews, the location and customer service are excellent. At check in, no less than 3 people introduced themselves by name. The doorman changed day to day, but the service level was still extremely high. The room was tiny but very well appointed, nice linens, good use of space. I stayed in a giant suite hotel in upstate NY last night and had a harder time getting ready this morning than at the Library. Had breakfast in the Library Reading Room in the morning - absolutely lovely!

name: Comfort Suites Alamo/Riverwalk
title: “Hands down the best hotel in San Antonio”
text: Where do I begin....the staff in this hotel really care about the quality of their work and the effect is has on their customers as well as their peers. Every employee I encountered always greeted me and asked how I was doing. Quite a nice change from other hotels I've visited. All the public areas are spotless, no messes or unexpected suprises. Even the exercise room was clean. Usually when I use the exercise rooms in other hotels, they have the crusted and dried sweat of the previous user all over them. Not the case here at all. Breakfast is plentiful, as well as the managers receptions during some of the weekday nights I was here. Speaking of managers, the manager introduced himself, and you can tell he runs a tight ship and enjoys what he does. All the staff seem to really get along with each other! My room was beautifully decorated and very clean, maid service was consistent each day I was out, and the channel selection on the TV was impressive. The WiFi is also seriously fast; its way better than what I have even at home! The pool facilities and mini golf really add a nice touch; and if you don't want to walk the literally two blocks to downtown, there is a complementary shuttle service that can drop you off and pick you up whenever you want! Parking is also nice and cheap, and also plentiful. Why pay 30 bucks a night 3 blocks down, when you can park at this hotel virutally free. They even have a security guard monitoring the premise at night. I will be back here in a heartbeat the next time I visit San Antonio and am so glad I found this place!

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
My friends and I spent 2 nights at this hotel (I called in the reservation) and I found it to be very nice. I previously stayed the the Sofitel in LA (Beverly Hills) and it had much more of a French/European feel in regards to decor. Whereas this hotel seemed much more standard. Don't get me wrong, I thought the hotel was very nice. 
Our flight arrived early so we got to the hotal at 8:00 am. Too early to check in so the front desk took my cell phone number and they actually CALLED me when the room was ready (around 10am). How nice!
The beds were FABULOUS; the bathroom was very nice and spacious -- had a phone too! The staff was international and pleasant. There were three FREE Internet computers hidded in an alcove in the lobby with printers and everything! Saved me from paying $10/day just to check email. Loved it!
The concierge was great -- but I can't remember her name...she was a redhead. 
We didn't eat at the hotel restaurant but we ate (a few times) at the Marathon Grill two blocks down the street. Great and healthy breakfast, lunch, dinner, snacks, etc. and they are open very late. Their wheat toast is DELICIOUS! I know, it's just bread but it was yummy!
The location of the hotel is great because it's close to downtown and several great boutiques, bars and restaurants. I spent one afternoon just walking the area and all the shops. I like Philly.
Also shopped at the very cute - Kimberly Boutique: wonderful customer service and a great SALE!! Loved it! I bought these super hot navy blue pants that are very flattering!

name: Comfort Suites Alamo/Riverwalk
title: “Warm and Welcoming”
text: The Comfort Suites staff made us feel very welcome! Everyone, especially Georgia, was so warm and friendly. They provided us with an excellent breakfast buffet and happy hour. It was extremely relaxing! The hotel and suite were clean and well taken care of. The pool and hot tub area was just beautiful. I would strongly recommend this hotel!

name: Quality Inn & Suites Downtown
title: “An excellent choice for (just north of) downtown”
text:
This property is spotless. My room was clean, spacious, and orderly; the pool area was inviting; the lobby and breakfast area, while small, were clean. Breakfast includes a generous spread (eggs both scrambled and boiled, sausage, waffles, assorted breads, pastries (all individually wrapped), juices, cereals, coffee/tea. Every staff member offers a friendly "hello" when you walk in or out. 
It is located next to the Arizona Art Museum, which is next to the McDowell/Central light rail station. You're one stop beyond the edge of ASU downtown and two stops beyond VanBuren and the edge of business/commercial downtown. If you choose to walk, you're about 10 minutes north (along 3rd Ave) from the edge of ASU downtown along a (seemingly safe) mix of apartments, condos, and a couple schools. There's a hotel van parked out front offering free shuttles to the airport and local destinations. A large CVS is just west of the hotel and a large Safeway/McDonalds/Subway/Pizza is a block west.
For me and my family, it's a great value option for downtown. The light rail provides easy access to the airport, ASU, and points beyond.

name: Mokara Hotel and Spa
title: “Couldn't be nicer”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights for the first part of our honeymoon. They couldn't have made the visit any better. We took the couples spa package & had a great time. Just far enough off the river to not hear the noise. But steps away. ALL staff members treated us like regular visitors & were always respectful.

name: Mokara Hotel and Spa
title: “one of the nicest hotels we have ever stayed at - period”
text: we just returned from a trip to San Antonio and loved staying at the Watermark. it is, by far, one of the nicest hotels we have stayed in in many years of travelling. From the moment we entered the warm and inviting lobby, we knew this place was special. The front desk staff and concierge were gracious and helpful the entire time. OUr room, while not facing the Riverwalk, was immense, luxuriously appointed and very comfortable. The bathroom had marble floors and counters and was extremely spacious. A jucuzzi bath , large shower and separate toilet room were great features. Although the hotel was fully booked, it felt as if we were the only guests . It was so quiet and peaceful the entire time. The restaurant on the lower level was very nice for breakfast. They did not have a separate bar or lounge and the restaurant did not really have a great set up for cocktails etc. Nonetheless, there were plenty of other hot spots close by to relax at the end of the day . The lamps on the bed side tables had dimmer switches which was a nice touch and helped to create a warm ambience in the room. Turn down service was also very nice . We really loved out stay at the Watermark and would stay again if we ever return to San Antonio.

name: Mokara Hotel and Spa
title: “Wonderful experience!”
text:
My boyfriend, two cats and I stayed here as night three of our cross country road trip. We had originally booked and arrived at their sister hotel across the river. We were moved across the river to The Watermark after the original hotel informed us that they had overbooked due to a conference that was in town. We were assured that we would be very happy at The Watermark instead and indeed they were correct. We had arrived late in the evening and once we finally got to our room we were thrilled to be walking into a luxurious spa like oasis. The room had a big four poster bed, desk with chairs on both sides, big tv hidden away in a armoire. As well the room had large windows and a balcony with a café size table and chairs, which overlooked the gorgeous river. The bathroom was large with separate shower and Jacuzzi tub. I felt for the most part that it was clean except the jets in the Jacuzzi were orange and grimy, which was either because they were old or not cleaned properly. Needless to say I did not use the Jacuzzi. 
Due to the fact that we had checked in late we ordered dinner through room service, which they call in room dining. The entire dining experience was superb, a man arrived to our room set the table, center piece and elegant placemats included. The food was excellent and although pricy we were happy to have made the choice. The concierge was very attentive and helped us plan the following day. The next morning on our walk over to the Alamo they sent us off with bottled water and a map, the little touches made this place really speical. I was disappointed that I never had a chance to visit the spa or the rooftop pool but both my boyfriend and I agree that we’ll be back. We loved San Antonio and The Watermark.

name: Budget Inn
title: “Absolutely Would Not Recommend!!”
text:
This hotel was aweful, it stunk so bad, when we walked back in after dinner it spealt like someone was cooking cat urine in their chinese food!!
We were suppose to be in a non smoking room and our room spelt so bad of smoke it was like they were blowing smoke straight into our room, when we got home our clothes spealt terrible.
The air conditioner didn't blow out cold air let alone hardly any air at all. 
I wouldn't have paid $35 let alone $50 for this place, I've staid at places alot cheaper that were 3 times better

name: Hotel Elysee
title: “Terrific boutique hotel”
text: Located in the heart of mid-town Manhattan yet on a quiet block. Great staff, nice continental breakfast. Room was very nice, even though it was at the back of the building, which may have helped to make it even quieter. Very elegant, yet comfortable. Parking was reasonable for NYC at $30/night. We were met at the curb when we arrived and the car was valet parked for us. When we checked out, our car was waiting at the curb for us without our ever saying a word. Awesome service, and the staff knows their stuff about NYC. They were even able to get us tickets to a sold-out Broadway show! The best trip ever to New York!

name: Lexington Hotel Central Phoenix
title: “Friendliest staff ever!”
text: We loved this hotel. We came as a large group, so things could have been very complicated. But the staff were so friendly and flexible- they made it all easy! The breakfast in the morning was great, and the location was convenient if you had a light rail pass. There's a station just outside the front door! I recommend this to anyone looking for a great hotel at a great price.

name: Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk
title: “Great Location...for everything.”
text:
We went down with a group and we couldn't have asked for a better location. Great views from the roof and in walking distance of everything. From restaurants, bars, malls and the Alamo, everything was so close and you walk right along the riverwalk.
The hotel itself was an antique delight. Full of history, old pictures and items from when it was a bank. 
The rooftop pool and hot tub was a hit with our group! 
The hot selections at breakfast remained the same, had minimal fruit but was free which was a great way to save with a group. 
The kickback food was typical pub fare but again, was free and a great perk, along with the free 3 drinks per guest, per night. 
Hotel staff were very friendly and quick to answer any questions or suggest great restaurants or places to check out. 
I would definitely stay here again.

name: Hotel Elysee
title: “Wonderful experience”
text: What can I say. Our stay was fabulous! The hotel was everything I had hoped it would be...and then some. The desk staff was terrific to a man...and woman. They were helpful and more importantly, very friendly. Breakfast every morning was something my wife and I looked forward to. Just the right newspapers, just the right items of breakfast food and wonderful service. They toasted Molly's bagel and were happy to make her a cup of cappuccino every morning. We will never stay at any other hotel when we come to New York. Unfortunately, we couldn't take much advantage of our terrace as the weather was too cold and/or rainy, but next time hopefully. Thanks for your hospitality! And please tell the desk personnel we loved them. "You guys got it together for sure!"

name: Comfort Suites Alamo/Riverwalk
title: “We'll be back”
text: Had 2 connecting rooms that were exactly what was advertised. Clean, huge bathrooms, plenty of towels and very comfortable beds. The breakfast was hot and delicious and had 2 of the happiest hostesses we've ever seen. Thanks Georgia for the hard work and kind words! The courtesy van was a blessing as parking in town is nonexistent. All of the staff was very friendly but get to the pool early as it is kind of small.

name: Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk
title: “Excellent hotel choice”
text:
This is an excellent hotel for the money. If you are looking for a nice, comfortable hotel to stay in, this is the best choice. This hotel offers everything quality wise that all your other "nicer" hotels do (Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt, etc), but they offer so much more. Not only do you get a nice clean room, with the option of having a terrace, jacuzzi tub, refrigerator/microwave, second room, or all of the above, but WiFi is free, telephone calls are free, free breakfast, and they also offer a free "kickback" which if you're not into eating heavy at night, you could call it a light dinner and also receive 3 free drinks per person, per night (Jose was great!!). All the other hotels charge for WiFi access and phone calls and don't offer any type of hot-food and you barely get a continental breakfast. In my opinion, the Drury is very comparable. You may not have waterfalls in the lobby, but since when did that become a make it or break it in choosing your hotel?? 
There are 2 swimming areas - one is on the roof and one is indoors. The roof can sometimes be windy, so it can feel a little chilly, but that's why they have an indoor pool also. The rooftop pool offers excellent views and is great to relax in when the wind is light. Being on the 23rd floor puts you up where the wind blows a little more than street level!
The ONLY complaint I have about this stay was that the valet did not inform me that my vehicle had to be jumped when they pulled it around. When I noticed that my clock and radio presets had reset, I had to track him down to verify. I would have preferred to know about this as soon as my vehicle was brought around so I would know right away that I have a problem with my vehicle, which now I must investigate. That is the only thing keeping this rating from being a full 5 stars. 
However, everything else was great and if you are torn between staying at the Drury Plaza Riverwalk and some other hotel on the Riverwalk, I would HIGHLY recommend that you give the Drury a chance. You won't be disappointed.

name: Chelsea Pines Inn
title: “Chelsea Pines Inn: nice place to stay in a quiet neighborhood.”
text:
My daughter and I stayed here at the beginning of December. From our arrival to our departure we couldn't have asked for a better spot. Everyone at the front desk contributed to our outstanding stay with tips on restaurants, plays, and places to visit. Their friendliness was more than I expected even after reading all of the reviews on Tripadvisor. Three guys chimed in and helped us choose a restaurant for our after-theater dinner (and it was a great choice!). We loved Charlie Chaplain the mustachioed cat who slept on the second floor landing (near our room). The WIFI was fast and reliable (which is often not the case). 
The Chelsea Pines is about 20 steps to the subway station and the cab from Penn Station cost only $6.00 (non-rush hour arrival and departure). Our room was quiet (we faced the garden) and much bigger than we expected. The bathroom was sparkling clean and we loved our shower outside of the bathroom--made it easier for one to shower and the other to put on makeup and fix the hair. Our room had a fridge and a safe to put our valuables. 
Breakfast was adequate (would have liked some protein but really appreciated the fresh berries and one morning the bagels had just come in and were warm to the touch!) and served in a comfortable spot with a little sun room filled with plants and backing onto the garden (which must be a nice spot to relax in the summer). 
We loved the location and really couldn't find anything to seriously fault. If you want a pleasant place to stay away from the hustle and bustle of the tourist spots this is it. My husband and I travel quite a bit to many places in the world and I can seriously say that this was one of my favorite places to stay. I intend to return with my husband in tow and stay again.

name: Phoenix Place Hotel & Suites
title: “Good deal, nice place”
text:
This seems to be an older hotel but it was well taken care of.
Our suite was very spacious and very clean.
The staff was great and very accommodating.
Free guest parking and free (albeit slow) wifi.
The free breakfast was very generous with eggs, bacon, lots of fresh fruit, toast bagels, pastry, cereal, potatoes.

name: Embassy Suites Phoenix Airport at 24th Street
title: “No Wifi No Wifi No Wifi”
