text: Dated property, but convenient to the airport. Inroom ethernet connect to the internet, but no wifi service in the rooms... major inconvenience for anyone traveling in todays world. Complimentary snacks and food limited, but bar is pretty decent. If convenient location is important, this place is good but for modern amenities look elsewhere

name: Phoenix Metro North Super 8 Motel
title: “everage to poor”
text: I am not a choosy person. i can be satisfied with simple thing s that meet my needs. Hence my stay here was good and safe except for the internet service that was very poor. I cannot connect to any browser. I was expecting to complete a business talk through internet that night but it failed because of the poor connection. Had it not because of this, my stay could have been perfect.

name: Chelsea Pines Inn
title: “Just the place to stay if you love excellent service”
text:
Daily newsletter with recommendations, excellent breakfast, businesss center, WIFI and printer, tea and coffe and cookies 24 hours, very friendly and helpfull staff.
small but charming room, ours facing the back and very quiet..
great excercise if you live on the top floors..

name: Phoenix Metro North Super 8 Motel
title: “Super 8 experience”
text:
location: Traveling south on interstate, we weren't able to exit soon enough,so we had to exit at next exit before we were able to come back to motel. Motel 6 in the same location.
least favorite was rooms need to update with clean floors no carpet.update restroom and digital TV. better breakfast varieties. Price was a little high for the quality of room. 
best experience was slept in comfortable beds.Able to get a good rest.

name: Phoenix Place Hotel & Suites
title: “SO BAD NOT WORTH A PENNY”
text: I have stayed at hundreds of hotels and motels and never have I paid so much for 1. Horrible service and employees 2. BAD management 3. DIRTY LINENS AND TOWELS 4. Over charged my account and never repaid me. 1st off the front desk woman was completely unprofessional. When my spouse and I got ready for bed at 10:30 we notices dirt and black markings all over the flat sheet. Come to find out they had made the King size bed with a flat sheet!! SO OF COURSE by morning it was no longer on the matress. I called the front desk, no appologies and no action for new linens. My Spouse calls, no action. Now 30 min later the Manager tells us when we called a 3rd time, he has No one to come give us the linens. So we had to go down to the desk to get them. Then after disovering the pillows were severly soilded, the Manager then tells us that he has no more clean pillow cases and if he finds some he will have someone bring them. Of course no one came. I had to use my hoodie as a pillow. And the new sheets were still some what dirty with black markings. I woke up early for our flight to shower. Turns out, of course the Towels had yellowy/ brown stains on them. I walk to the front desk bc the maid who was out side my door told me she didnt have any, even though she was cleaning rooms! The front desk tells me they will bring some, 1 hour goes by, I am mad bc I have a flight to catch and finally the maid give us 3 towels, 2 of which were still stained. Keep in mind these are all white linens and towles. The expierence was horrible, I have never been in such a filthy hotel that had such potential. And to top it all off, when I gave them my debit card to have the 50$ fee pending if anything was destroyed, well nothing was and I was charged the 50$ 3 days later. I called for 5 days at least 12 times to get that and a 47$ amount off my credit. The Manager never returned my calls. The 47$ was cleared the 50$ I am still working on and its been almost 2 wks. I paid over a 150$ for the nastiest hotel I have ever been at.

name: Embassy Suites Phoenix Airport at 24th Street
title: “Home away from home”
text:
Over the past several years I had many occasions to stay at this Hotel. From the moment when checking in at the front desk, you know you are welcome. The staff is outstanding. The Hotel is always neat, clean and well kept. Doug, the GM runs a tight ship and it shows. I have stayed in other Embassy Suites Hotels, but this one is by far the Hotel of my choice. If you just need to get away, travel for business, unwind, release some stress, this is where you need to stay. Not to forget the excellent made to order Breakfast in the mornings. Can't get any better than this. I will definitely stay there again. No matter what brings you to Phoenix, business or pleasure, this is your home away from home.
Thank you Doug and Lacey for making me feel welcome. I will be back.

name: Arizona Grand Resort & Spa
title: “Meh”
text:
The Arizona Grand is a nice idea. I think they could have done better. First, there is a $20 per night "resort fee" that they charge when you check in. This is supposed to cover the waterpark and fitness club. We checked in at 6 and the waterpark closed at 7. They still charged us the fee even though we go 30 minutes in the waterpark. (We would not of gone at all, but we wanted to make the most of our $20. Also, the restaurant there wasn't very good. We waited an hour to get in, the food was super expensive, and the food wasn't that great. The rooms were fine, except that we found a pack of smokes on the porch. The elevator in our tower was a little bit scary. Sometimes when you would step in to it, it would fall a little. It was also really shaky. We ended up using the stairs most of the time. I think the property is too big. They could of built the towers a little closer together so you didn't have to walk as far.
The Waterpark:
The main reason our family chose to stay here was because of the waterpark. They have two slides that go straight down, a curly slide, a lazy river, and a hot tub. I think their main reason to have the waterpark is to collect the resort fee and sell overpriced sodas. When my dad tried to jump in to the lasy river from the side, the lifeguard yelled at him, made him get out, and go around. After about 2 days the water slides gett a little old.
If you have younger kids and don't mind shelling out quite a bit of money, this MIGHT be a good place to go. I would highly recommend you avoid this place, and stay at a place where you get a bigger bang for your buck.

name: Embassy Suites Phoenix Airport at 24th Street
title: “Another Excellent Stay”
text: Stayed here 12/6-12/9 and everything was great. The experience was better than some other suites we have stayed in. The Squaw Peak Lounge has a great view and the folks that take care of you are superb. Food is excellent and drinks (free-Managers reception). Rooms were great too and up to date, no hunkie TV's here. Clean and well kept. Front desk staff top notch.

name: Phoenix Metro North Super 8 Motel
title: “Dirty, worn and smells”
text:
After reading the other reviews and staying at numerous Supr 8 Hotels across the country we didn't think twice about booking a room at this hotel. 
WOW!!!!! This place must have really gone downhill since the last review 6 months ago. Our room is TERRIBLE!!! Sure, the table and "dresser" are surface clean, but the room smells really bad and once I took my sandals off it only took about 5 minutes for my feet to turn black from the dirty carpet. When I moved the table my fingers stuck to the underside it was soo dirty. Everything in the room is worn, scuffed and dirty (except for the top). We should get a discount since we had to clean and freshen the room ourselves. 
Continental breakfast? Cereal, carton of milk sitting in a bucket of ice, packaged honey buns, a loaf of bread sitting in front of a toaster and coffee and orange juice. All crammed in a corner of the lobby. Does not even begin to compare to other continental bkfsts we have had at other Super 8's. 
This is also in a not so desirable location. There is a closed restaurant in the parking and a Kmart next door. Lots of people walking through and hanging out in the parking lot. The hotel makes sure to have a big sign to let you know they are not responsible for theft or damage to your vehicles. I guess that makes them feel better about the lack of security.

name: InnPlace Hotel Phoenix North
title: “A huge let down!”
text: This hotel was old, dated and dirty!!! The service was poor and slow. A breakfast plate sat outside a room for 2 1/2 days until I requested that someone clear it away. The shower was clogged and overheard others complain about the same. The bar was pleasant and the food wasn't bad. Dinning the last evening of our stay was the worst. The watress came out once to take our order (a group of 10 softball players and wives) she never came back to refill our drinks - we needed to get them ourselves at the bar. The food came out over an hour later and it was cold and not very good. We all compalined about the poor service that evening. The hotel computer was not working so we did not get our wake up calls (twice) we also were awakened at 10pm - we had an early game time with a request from the front desk to update our credit card info as it was lost! The pictures on the web site do not represent this hotel! Lots of apologies when complaints were brought to the attention of the front desk but this hotel needs alot of tender love and care and a bit more attention to the guests comfort and needs!!!!

name: Embassy Suites Phoenix-Scottsdale
title: “Nice hotel...”
text:
I really liked this hotel and would have given an excellent rating except that I agree with the previous reviewer about the ridiculas cost of the wi-fi access which is free at every other place that I have stayed in on this trip.
I think that the manager should look again at his reply and try to understand what is being said here, rather than what his view is.
The staff were lovely and the prepared while you wait breakfast was excellent.

name: Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak Resort
title: “Give this one a pass”
text: We reserved a suite with 2 queen beds. Check in time is 4pm. We drove in from California and arrived at 5pm and to hang out, hot and tired until 6pm when the suite was finally ready. We unpacked and went to dinner and then to the water park returning at 10. Housekeeping showed up in the morning at 8:30 to clean. I asked them to come back in about an hour when we would be up and out. We returned to the hotel at 2pm and the room wasn't ready. We went back to the water park returning at 5pm, room still not cleaned. I called to remind housekeeping to come and clean. We left again for dinner and when we returned the room was finally cleaned. I went outside to enjoy watching the families enjoy the pool. I went to the 2nd floor terrace overlooking the pool and found it too dirty to sit in. Went down to the pool and sat on a lounge. I kept feeling being bitten for about an hour when the family came down to go to the waterpark. Sunday, our last day, I discovered that we had run out of toilet paper in the night (housekeeping didn't replace the supply when they finally cleaned). I called and requested they send up some tp for us. I called a second time - same request. It took about an hour before it finally arrived. When I got home I finally had a chance look in the mirror at my leg (see picture). I let the hotel know about the bug bites and requested a refund for a truly awful experience at their hotel. They couldn't find any bugs and suggested I check my home. That was just plain insulting. They did offer to give me a discount on a future stay. REALLY?

name: Chelsea Pines Inn
title: “a safe and cozy gem in a great location”
text:
I stayed at the Chelsea Pines Inn in July to meet with a NY colleague and also visit friends while in town. I booked a suite which was perfect, as my colleague and I met in the extra room. My colleague lives in NY and couldn't believe the size of the rooms. She was going to tell her folks about the Inn for an upcoming visit.
In the room there's a coffee maker with GOOD coffee, and a fridge and kitchen area, which is so nice to have. Free wireless - a huge plus. Breakfast is terrific - so many options. A lovely courtyard out back. The staff were terribly helpful and pleasant. Each morning they drop a sheet of goings on in the area and recommendations for activities. It is extremely well run, clean and cozy. Half a block from the subway at 14th and 8th Ave. Steps from good restaurants, and so easy to get to midtown or downtown. I will definitely stay here again and tell my friends!

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “Très bon emplacement et accueil”
text:
La qualité des hôtels Sofitel n'est plus à démontrer mais l'accueil et le service du Sofitel de Philadelphie sont particulièrement remarquables.
Nous avions de la chance d'avoir à l'accueil une personne qui parlait un français parfait. 
La chambre était très agréable et lumineuse. 
L'emplacement de l'hôtel permet de se déplacer dans Philadelphie à pied.

name: Phoenix Place Hotel & Suites
title: “How can you not stay here”
text: The location wasnt that great, a little hard to find. The service was spectacular! The rooms were fine, and the grounds were great. Nice pool-both of them. Nice lobby and decore in the rooms. Our family found this hotel so we wouldnt have to stay with realitives. i'm glad we did. We will come back every year!

name: Sofitel Philadelphia Hotel
title: “le meilleur hôtel de Philadelphie”
text: excellent rapport qualité prix: un palace au prix d'un hôtel 4 étoiles;une management hautement professionnel, des équipes attentives au client et un service irréprochable, tout y est réuni pour un séjour de rêve

name: Phoenix Place Hotel & Suites
title: “Radisson Phoenix City Center is Best Kept Secret in Phoenix”
text: I had a very wonderful pleasure to stay at the Radisson Hotel Phoenix City Center. This hotel is a very great "secret" of hotels in Phoenix. All of the staff that I encountered had the greatest customer service; the restaurant had awesome food and drink. I enjoyed the pools and the room was great. I will definitely recommend this hotel to anyone who travels to Phoenix. You should be proud to be a Radisson.

name: Library Hotel
title: “this is the best place i ever stay i just love it and can't wait to come back”
text:
From the moment your taxi pulls up you are surrounded by sensitive staff who seem especially able to judge the care factor you require and to get it just right!
the environment is the most civilised I know, the rooms extremely comfortable and quiet and the ambiance in the reading room just perfect for recovering from a demanding day at the office, or sight seeing or shopping. Well done

name: Embassy Suites Phoenix Airport at 24th Street
title: “Worked Well for Us”
text:
Having booked this room awhile back without checking Tripadvisor first, I was dismayed when I finally read the reviews last week before our trip. Since it was too late to change anything we went ahead with out plans to stay at this hotel. We found that, yes, it's in an older neighborhood that is a bit run down in places. However, we never feared for our safety once. Security and hotel staff were always present in the parking lots and on the premises. 
The front desk staff were helpful and kind. The morning chefs were fantastic and fun individuals. They took the time to help you with any requests you might have and were very cheerful in doing so. The pool area was clean and neat to see at night with the gas lamps that surrounded it.
The only major drawback to this hotel was it's age. Supposedly its going through a remodel, but I found that the aging property didn't reduce our satisfaction as a family of 6.

name: Hotel San Carlos
title: “Great hotel with lots of character”
text: We didn't know anything about this hotel before we checked in. It simply looked interesting. We were very comfortable and our kids enjoyed the swimming pool very much. The room was nicely decorated. I was impressed with the curtains and linens for an older hotel. I read the other review about the hotel being dirty...in fact, I think they were unhappy with just about everything...being sarcastic and just plain mean. We found the room and bathroom spotless. I have stayed in many historic hotels. We look for them. This one is right up there with the best. If you are looking for ultra modern, stainless steel, sterile cookie-cutter accommodations, don't stay here. If you are looking for something to remember with lots of character, this is it!

name: Arizona Grand Resort & Spa
title: “Waterpark fun for Kids”
text:
We were at the Arizona Grand in early May for a little sun for the moms and fun for the kids. I had purchased a Living Social deal which included a breakfast credit of $30 which was more than enough for me and my daughter. My friend that I was with had her three kids, and it did not quite cover them but was still a great deal. We stayed for 3 nights (thurs-sat, left on sun) and payed $189.00/night.
Overall the rooms (1 bedroom suites) were fine, nothing fancy. We had to ask for the coffee machine which was supposed to be in there and were provided with an antique 2cup machine....which served its purpose until we could get to breakfast, which was wonderful: they had an incredible buffet with tons of choices (the cinnamon rolls, and french toast were our favorites)! I think the buffet ran $8/kids, & $16/adults...so I was well within my breakfast budget. The restaurant on the premises was very nice with comfortable outdoor & indoor seating and we ate there practically every night. There was a good selection, with kids meals and all reasonably priced. 
The Waterpark was great, and there was a water different area for the younger kids. Our kids dropped there stuff on a chair and went straight to the Lazy River, and next to the slides. They would pop back in every once in awhile to get food or to rest, but were pretty much in the water for 6-7 hours every day we were there. They loved, loved, loved it and even on the last day we had to haul them out to get ready to leave. It definitely made it more fun for them that they were all there together, but i didn't see any kids having anything less than a blast! 
The food served at the pool was good, typical pool fare. A little overpriced but not too big a deal. Their ice creams, and shakes are HUGE, and delicious but 1 for 2 kids is more than enough...not too mention the melt factor. 
Overall, a truly fun experience that I would do again. They do gouge you with the add on fees and taxes at the end which is kind of a bummer. On top of the "resort fee" which is $40.00/day, there was a 13% "suite tax" (surprise!), plus tax= an extra $70/day. so be prepared. Without the deal or some kind of special promotion, I think this resort would definitely be overpriced.

name: Arizona Biltmore
title: “Very Nice Resort!...We Will Return Again!”
text: My family and I have stayed here two times in the past month. Both times were very nice. The grounds are beautiful and well maintained. There are several pools, the main one has a slide for the kids. Our rooms were located in the Ocatilla Club. The rooms are large and nicely appointed. There is a private lounge for guests of the Ocatilla Club. They have a continental breakfast, some snacks throughout the day and then appetizers and drinks before dinner. Later in the evening the put out sweets. The management and staff are very helpful and insure that your needs are being met and that you are enjoying yourself. The food at Frank and Albert's was good, The dinner menu was different, but the breakfast menu was very good. If you play golf there is a course in the resort. There is very good shopping in the mall nearby. You could walk it as the distance is about 1.5 miles each way. This is not advised during the "hot" season, but they also have an air conditioned shuttle that will take you back and forth. We look forward to returning soon!!!

name: Arizona Grand Resort & Spa
title: “Off to a good start”
text:
We have plans to go with friends to the Resort this upcoming Memorial Day Weekend.
I thought it would be a good idea to confirm my request for adjoining rooms. I left a detailed message for the Director of Reservations, Nathan. I about fell over when I got a (very unexpected) returned phone call later in the day confirming that he did indeed receive my message and my request have been forwarded to the people to make it happen. Nowadays it is so rare to actually find any decent customer service!! I was so pleased to have such quality follow-up.
If this is any indication of how the Resort truly operates, then I know we will have a fabulous time!
Lets hope the whole staff functions so professionally!

name: Westin La Cantera Hill Country Resort
title: “Excellent golf course”
text: My friends and I took a weekend trip to San Antonio to relax and play golf, The Palmer course was in great shape and a great challenge to test a golfers "skills' the service was great and Mackenzie the course server came by often to offer drinks and snacks and even helped us find a ball on one occasion, great experience.

name: Arizona Grand Resort & Spa
title: “September weekend”
text: I visited the resort last summer. When I arrived at the hotel the room I was assigned had not been cleaned so I was moved to an amazing suite right on the main path to the recreation pool. Movie night floating on rafts while watching the movie with my kiddos was sooo fun. Everyone was exceptionally nice and I am amazed at how affordable the whole trip was. I drove from LA and would do so again just for the low price, friendly staff, and good times.

name: Arizona Grand Resort & Spa
title: “Great Time at Arizona Grand Resort”
text:
We stayed at the Arizona Grand Resort over Spring Break. Great room, very clean property, excellent gym, great food at the on-site restaurants. 
My biggest disappointment was the Water Park was handled. It was extremely crowded in the afternoon and if you didn't stand in line at the beginning of the morning to grab a chair, you were out of luck if you wanted to go in the afternoon. To make matters worse, although the resort boasts they have 7 pools, again finding a chair in the afternoon is very difficult because people just put their towels on the chairs and then leave to go to other things. Since you pay an additional daily "resort fee" I feel like you should at least be able to find a chair at the water park or the pool.

name: Coast Phoenix Sky Harbor Hotel
title: “Good place to stay - and great value for the money”
text:
Want to her a little fairytale about my recent business trip - Well, I came in on a Thursday at night. At the airport, it took some time to figure out that there is no courtesy phone anymore, but the nice lady from the tourist office gave us the number from the receptionist, who sent a shuttle immediately. Got a king room on 6th floor, facing towards the parking garage and swimming pool, and towards downtown in far distance. West side, man - i was so tired after 18 hours on the road - just fell asleep.
Next morning I noticed a concerto bravisimo: The high pitch from the A/C, which are bolted on the park deck where impressively surrounded by the local garbage truck. Well, it would be time to try out the other side of this building, I thought. Let go, get some food and then ask for a swap of rooms.
Breakfast was just marvelous, and include in the price. This is a great value, nice hot stuff to eat and fresh fruit - delicious. After that I stopped at the receptionist, who hadn't had any clean rooms by then. Noontime would be better to swap rooms, so I got upstairs again, and went back down at 11:30, because the maid wanted to get into my room the third time. BTW: The room was very clean. the only thing I would not like is the elder A/C unit, and the windows needed a clean up from outside urgently. 
Swapped the room to the east side 9th floor - Way better in terms of sound and location. The only thing is the highway close by where some pontiacs with Cop callers on them gave me a little sound track. 
After 6 days, I checked out happily. I always judge the places on price/performance. This one is a good/great one, so I recommend. Certainly there are more eloquent places around town, like the Biltmore, but this is just fine. Thanks for reading, and keep on tracking my stories.

name: TownePlace Suites Phoenix Metrocenter Mall
title: “A Real Treat!”
text:
The manager has a great front desk staff. The women we dealt with were attentive, friendly and helpful. In particular, Chelsea went out of her way to talk to us and make sure our stay in Phoenix was an enjoyable one.
The hotel has a great free breakfast and large eating area.
The pool area is adjacent to the parking lot and by no means luxurious.
However, the rooms are Marriott. Clean ,comfortable and quiet.
It is far enough from the I17 to allow you to sleep with the windows open (yes they open) although I would ask for a 2nd or 3rd floor room not facing the pool.

name: Hotel Elysee
title: “One Big Problem”
text:
I loved my recent stay at the Elysee in every way except for one--if you are a sensitive sleeper and need total darkness to sleep, you may find it difficult to get a decent night's shuteye. In the first room we stayed in, there was a pull down shade and sheers , but the standard curtains (made of solid material) did not close. That first night, I was awake most of the night because the room faced the street and there was a lot of light coming in. The next day, after explaining the situation to the manager, she ended up accomodating us by putting us on a darker side of the hotel-- and although it was a bit better,I could still see light coming in at night.(My husband ended up going out and buying me eyeshades so I could enjoy the rest of our stay.)
Other than that, the breakfast was terrific, the rooms nicely appointed and the staff very sweet. The location is so central to everything. Its a shame that we won't be staying there again because of this one problem.

name: Red Roof Phoenix North - Bell Road
title: “Very nice room and great price!”
text: When we arrived we received great service. The staff was very pleasant, room was nice, clean, comfortable and a great price! I will definately stay there again!

name: Chelsea Pines Inn
title: “Don't hesitate to book a room here!”
text: We chose to stay at the Chelsea Pines Inn based on the very positive reviews we found on Trip Advisor. We weren't disappointed and spent a wonderful couple of days there. Jay and his staff have created a very pleasant haven for visitors to New York. Our room was clean and spacious, with nice amenities. Everyone on the staff was extremely helpful; the night staff was especially accommodating of our early morning coffee request. Their restaurant recommendations were first-rate too, and they readily made reservations for us. It is also easy to get to and from the inn as it is a half block from the 14th street subway station, from which you can easily get to almost any place in the city. We plan to stay at the Chelsea Pines again and have already recommended the Chelsea Pines to others.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Phoenix-North
title: “Nice hotel w pool and hot tub and free cook to order breakfast!”
text: It's motel style, drive to your door, so it's not internal, which is fine. However, the housekeeper did leave my door open after cleaning it. But the management was very adamant about rewarding me for that and gave me a discount! Nothing was taken. The courtyard is beautiful with a pool, hottub, and bar. The cook to order breakfast is the best in the industry for free! You feel weird, but good about walking away without paying for a meal like that! And it's right down the street from Pei Wei and Chino Bandido's!

name: Sleep Inn Airport
title: “Terrific Place to Stay”
text:
Affordable, comfortable, nice pool, Internet access, TV's in sitting rooms, nice room accomodations and more. This is a great place to stay!
Well placed hotel. Transportation by hotel shuttle to and from the airport, both close by. Able to use fitness facility - a REALLY nice facility - next door at the Hilton.

name: Westin La Cantera Hill Country Resort
title: “Our family reunion was here....it was great!”
text: I cannot attest to the food poisoning incidents, but I can attest to the fact that our family reunion was held here last June, a total of 19 rooms/suites were booked, and no one got sick, everyone was happy with the accommodations (all 70+ of us from all over the nation), and the service was admirable. The lobby area was beautiful and served as a nice gathering spot for our group. Lots of pools and space for everyone, great for the little ones as well as our 92 year old Grandmother! The concierge went out of their way to help us with activities for our group as well. This property feels intimate and tucked away, yet is right next door to Six Flags, and easy distance from shopping and other restaurants. Nice golf course as well. Overall our experience was superb!

name: Coast Phoenix Sky Harbor Hotel
title: “A six day stay was six days too long! Lesson learned!!”
text: My overall experience was less than desirable, I payed in advance for the king conc rm when I checked in and was in my room housekeeping came in saying she needed to clean rm, the refrigerator was unstable and unplugged (which I soon found out why), the rm was small nothing like what the pic illustrated, the tv kept going out, the desk clock didn't work and 1 of the 4 elevators was broke 3 out of the 6 days I was here! I'm extremely thrilled to check out today!!

name: Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk
title: “This is the place to stay on the Riverwalk!!”
text: Went to the Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk last weekend for our anniversary and loved it! We were upgraded to the new tower and had an amazing view overlooking the Riverwalk and the Main Plaza, which had fountains that were lit up at night. The room had contemporary furnishings and was lovely, and we liked that the living area was separate and had a microwave and small refrigerator. The staff at the Drury Plaza Hotel were incredibly friendly and accommodating. We enjoyed the complimentary happy hour each night and free breakfast each morning, and I'm not talking about pastries and bagels! They actually served scrambled eggs, sausage, pancakes, fruit, muffins, and beverages! It was such a nice experience, especially given that this was a VERY last minute trip for us as our original plans in Southeast Texas had been cancelled due to the power outages resulting from Hurricane Ike. We will definitely be back to the Drury Plaza Hotel again soon!

name: Hotel Elysee
title: “Not a good value”
text:
We chose the hotel because of all of the good reviews on Tripadvisor. It is true that the location is excellent and that the staff is quite nice. And, there is a certain quaintness staying in a 99 room hotel in NY. But, for $425 per night for a basic room, the value is not there. Let me explain.
No disrespect to our European friends who review on this site, but American expectations for a proper hotel room are quite different: The room must be quiet, the bed superb, and the room spacious. 
First, why not a coffee maker in the room? The continental breakfast is free in the library, so it's not as if they are trying to force you to pay for the product. It is so darn inconvenient to have to get dressed, go down to the library and fill up a cup and hoof it back to your room with cup in hand.
Whatever happened to a free morning paper at your door? Is 50 cents too much for the hotel to spend for a NY times? Or am I one of the last dinosaurs that likes to read a paper in the morning?
Because the hotel is old, you will have to listen to the air conditioning unit under the window starting up and shutting down all night long (just like at a Motel 6). (Up to date hotels have units that are vented into the rooms overhead and the compressors are located elsewhere.)
Our room was in the back, overlooking an air shaft. I was not interested in a view, just quiet. However, there was a 24 hour low roar from some rooftop mechanical units below us. If the windows had been proper, double-glaze soundproof windows, this would not have been a problem. But, they were not.
Our room 92 had no full length mirror (my wife likes that kind if thing), no peephole in the door (to see who is buzzing outside), and, no counter space in the bathroom. If I had stayed at a hotel like this in Europe, I would have thought, "how charming". But at $425 per night in one of the most competitive hotel markets in the world, it just doesn't meet New York standards for that price level.

name: Chelsea Pines Inn
title: “Wonderful place to stay”
text:
My friend recommended CPI for our first visit to NY. And I recommend (or will) to everyone else. The inn was perfect, went beyond our expectations. 
1. Service: from the very beginning the front desk was courteous, professional, and very "welcoming". Checked us in, recommended restaurants, places of interest, and how to get around town. Jay (I believe he is one of the owners) even wrote out the directions for us (no other Hotel, and we've stayed in many coming from Vegas have NEVER had anyone provide this level of service). There should be an additional star(s) for rating.
2. Room: Clean, well furnished, absolutely splendid. Each room has a classic movie-star theme; I smiled, my girlfriend just went "sooooo cute." Fresh towels when needed (and none of that cheap thin-rough kind). Bed was comfortable - even had an ipod station where we plugged in to listen to some tunes. Very modern, yet homey. Great lighting system (can dim to your preference). Awesome.
3. Downstairs: Kitchen - clean, comfortable, and fresh bagels/muffins/orange juice in the mornings. There's a backyard for outdoor sitting, to bad it was too cold to enjoy it.
4. Price: very reasonable. affordable. My friends came by to take a look at the place, and stated: "Dude, you can't get a room like this anywhere in NY for the price you paid." *plus - we stayed the weekend.
5. Accessibility: near the subway - just up the street.
6. Location: We saw Manhattan and in all its glory. Chelsea Market right around the corner - very cool place to hang and get some great eats. Fun walk around the city. We went to union square, empire state, times square, and up to central park to check out the MET (learned a NY lingo). Basically, places of interest are very accessible from Chelsea Pines. 
**review was written by a third party - no gimmick - I have no affiliation whatsoever with CPI - this was an independent inquiry.

name: Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak Resort
title: “Resort for all ages”
text: Pleasantly surprised by this resort. Due to the water park being across the parking lot from the main hotel room it was pleasantly quiet in the rooms despite the abundance of children. This makes it an excellent resort for any age. If you are an early bird Rooms 2432-2435 have beautiful AM sun over a mountain view and then afternoon sun in the living room part of the suite. Great room layouts with doors to separate the living room to the bathroom and then the bedroom provides a perfect degree of privacy but also makes the rooms great for entertaining.

name: Coast Phoenix Sky Harbor Hotel
title: “Friendly staff. Good value.”
text: Friendly staff. Good value. Breakfast buffet was great offering hot and cold items along with made to order omelets and waffles. Would definitely stay again.

name: Crowne Plaza Phoenix
title: “Nice rooms, great breakfast.”
text: Stayed here for four nights and loved the place. Exterior looks like it was designed and painted by kids, but the inside is very nice. The room was a fair size, the bed was huge and comfy and i recommend the rooms with an outside balcony, not an inside one; since fresh air is nice and humidity is not. The breakfast area is large and the food is excellent. Best scrambled eggs I`ve ever had! The restaurant is very nice and the waiter was very good. The young bartender was basically ignorant and a chip on his shoulder; but that could be because he`s young and figures he`s God`s gift to women. A friend/colleague and i decided to go out for a beer and didn`t know where to go. The front desk clerk made arrangements to drive us to a place when she got off work (about fifteen minutes from punch out time) and she dropped us off without taking any money from us. When we got there we the place was closed so we called the hotel to tell them. They immediately sent out the Plaza Van to get us. The clerk who came to get us took the long way back (or so it seemed) and we got to see an interesting part of Phoenix. Excellent, excellent, excellent customer service. My family is planning our bi-annual trip to Florida this coming winter and i think i have her convinced that we need to visit Phoenix as a family instead. I wouldn`t dream of staying anywhere else, even at a higher rate.

name: Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak Resort
title: “Wonderful Spring Break”
text: Spent five days at the Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak Resort in Phoenix. It was an oasis in a large metropolitan city. We were never aware that we were in the middle of Phoenix! Getting there was easy and getting around was easy. The rooms were spacious and well-appointed. Lots of room to spread out in. The grounds were very pretty and we enjoyed the courtyards and architecture. The pool areas were sometimes crowded and some guests got up early in the morning to lay claim to poolside chairs with towels but, there was enough movement that we were always able to find chairs at one pool or another. We found we enjoyed visiting the large, main pool after the little ones had gone to sleep. It was only open until 8:00 p.m. which I understand with paying lifeguards and all, but we would have liked to have seen some adult hours in the main pool later in the evening. Drinks and food were available at every pool and the on-site restaurants were handy and served very good food. All in all, a great one-stop shopping resort for the family. Would recommend it.

name: Coast Phoenix Sky Harbor Hotel
title: “Needs Improvement”
text: We chose this because it was close to the airport and we had an early flight out and also because it had a restaurant where we hoped to have dinner, as we had returned our rental car in the afternoon after checking in. It was just OK but we would not choose to stay here again. The restaurant was dreadful. The room was spacious enough, but the air conditioner was so noisy even on a low setting it was hard to sleep. The bathroom floor was not immaculate and I found long dark hairs near the tub. I thought that the Crowne Plaza brand had a good reputation but this was quite disappointing.

name: Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk
title: “Very enjoyable stay”
text: The hotel is in a great location and the staff is very friendly and helpful. Our room was on the 12th floor, the room was very clean and quiet. (We didnt have much of a view) They offer a lot of extras, with free food or drinks all day long on the second floor. The pool is on the roof with two hot tubs, the view at night is very nice. For to price and location, we will stay here again when in San Antonio.

name: Hilton Phoenix Airport
title: “Room walls and doors must be made of paper.”
text: Room walls and doors must be made of paper. Was up all night because of noise outside in hallway and rooms next door. No shampoo. Sadly I didn't notice until AFTER I was undressed. Would expect more from the Hilton. Too many other hotels in the vicinity to stay at this place again.

name: Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk
title: “Superb hotel choice in superb city!”
text: We stayed here over July 4th weekend - our first stay at a Drury hotel - we were extremely inmpressed - the building is gorgeous - fully restored and renovated former Alamo bank building - many original 'artifacts' and features have been retained - extremely attractive throughout. Our room was called a 'jacuzzi room' - the room itself was not large but it was well laid out and everything was very new and upscale - the bathroom was big and brand new with a terrific jacuzzi tub! The room had a small sitting/dressing area with a partial view of the river. There was also free wireless internet and 1 hour of free long distance calls daily. The free hot breakfast buffet was good - not awesome but definitely good - very busy but the staff kept things moving along very well. There is also a free happy hour daily with beer, wine and mixed drinks - busy - but comfortable seating was available and there is a huge plasma TV showing sports etc. Free hot and non-alcoholic cold drinks are available throughout the day - as is fresh popcorn! All of these 'extras' are very nice and appreciated. There is an open-air roof top pool with 2 hot tubs - the views from up there are great! The staff were very nice and professional but unfortunately not very well informed about the city - they wanted to help but just didnt have the answers to our tourist questions! The San Antonio tourist office is opposite The Alamo and it has great staff - definitley go in with any questions you may have! The hotel's location is excellent - direct access to 'The Riverwalk' but in a quiter section. San Antonio is a first class destination - an extraordinarily beautiful and exceptionally interesting city. Our only complaints about this hotel was LONG waits for the elevators (10+ minutes) and the line for valet (to pick up your car) stretched throught the entire lobby (20 - 25 people on line) - we were glad we arrived by taxi!! We will definitely go back to this hotel!

name: Library Hotel
title: “Great Hotel !!!”
text:
The Library Hotel is unique and well worth exploring. It's in an excellent location in midtown Manhattan. The staff are respectful but very warm and helpful. The room was comfortable and nicely appointed. I strongly advise checking out their excellent website to get a feel for the concept of the hotel. We couldn't have been more pleased with all the hotel offers. An excellent place. I'm sure children are welcome, however, this hotel is probably geared more toward adults. It's a smaller "boutique" hotel, which we like. It is very sophisticated and refined. Not cheap, but no nice place in Manhatten is! Highly Recommended!!! 
Randall & Deanie Vincent
Walker, Louisiana

name: Hotel Elysee
title: “Absolutey exquisite hide-away!!”
text:
I will never stay anywhere else when going to New York City!!
Yes, it was our first time in the city that never sleeps and I am thrilled we managed to choose to stay in this fabulous hotel. Every single member of staff was always and at all times attentive, forthcoming and helpful. Their whole attitude is the best selling point for this hotel!
Our room was of a good size, which was important since we stayed there for 10 nights over the holiday season (Xmas 2005 until Jan. 2006). Furniture of high quality and very stylish. Bathroom of adequate size, nicely smelling soaps and toiletries, bathrobes of soft Turkish cotton. Really good.
Our room looked out on the street and yes, weekdays you get some noise. But, since we come from a city it didn't bother us. However, I would recommend asking a room at the back of the building if you are not used to some level of street noise.
The complimentary breakfast had a much larger selection of offerings than I would have expected and it could keep you going through most of the day. Coffee and teas remain available for the whole day and as from 5pm they also offer a selection of cheeses and wine (and champagne while we were there). It is a very nice touch, in a cozy and comfortable room, but we didn't run back to the hotel every day 'to take advantage' of this.
Personally I would try at all times to stay at this little gem, but by comparing prices! It doesn't exactly come cheap, but you get much more than just 'good value' for what you pay.
The only downside in my opinion, is that you need to leave the area for a fair choice of restaurants. There are some places around the hotel but not so inspired in my opinion. Catch a metro and head down to the village of restaurants' row and choices are much better. It's still close enough, but not necessarily 'walkable'.
Anyway, DO NOT MISS STAYING HERE!!!

name: Chelsea Pines Inn
title: “Lovely Hotel in the Heart of The City”
text: This hotel is such good value and much better than the traditional tourist hotels. The location is excellent and you actually feel that you are staying in the real NY. The rooms were spotless and very comfortable and the staff were very friendly and helpful. One minor complaint was a lack of breakfast one morning but this is easily forgiven considering the selection every other day. I highly recommend this to anyone who wants to stay in a small comfortable hotel at a great value price.

name: Arizona Grand Resort & Spa
title: “Not What I Expected”
text:
No complaints about the staff we dealt with or the hotel as a whole, it just wasn't what we expected or wanted, so we ended up changing hotels. The hotel was wonderful about it and didn't impose any penalties for our early departure.
This is not a 4* resort. The lobby area is heavily staffed with the personnel you'd expect, but in our hotel wing, if you needed anyone (including near the pool) expect to make a phone call from your room.
Water park was not open when we were there, which we expected. The 6 pools that were open are very spread out. So really, there were only 2 available conveniently to us, one which is adults only. And they are in courtyards and get limited sun. 
The athletic facility is so far away, that a golf cart could be called from the hotel, but it wasn't walking distance. I thought I'd try a yoga class, but it was just mentally too much effort to organize.
The rooms are fine, with recent updates. The bathrooms are tiny and not luxurious. But what really bothered me was the exterior of the hotel. Cracks in the stucco. Water stains. Signage that still indicates the "future lobby's" location (clearly long built out) or is broken/missing.
Lastly, the neighborhood wasn't for me. The resort grounds are very nice, but the surrounding area is not tourist-focused nor particularly upscale. The $30 resort fee plus $15 wifi cost made a lot of other hotels comparable in price. And the amenities and level of service surpassed what we found here.
We didn't experience anything bad at the Arizona Grand, but it wasn't what we expected or wanted.

name: The Westin Riverwalk
title: “Nice weekend stay”
text:
Weeekend getaway for me and my lovely wife. We were able to get a nice little discount on the rate by checking or coupons on retailmenot.com. Since I am a Starwood club member we were upgraded to the Starwood-top floor. I had paid for the Riverwalk side balcony room for a little extra romance. Tip: above the third or fourth floor the balcony rooms probably aren't worth it. It takes you out of the Riverwalk feeling and the views from up here are not at all special. Stay on the street side or stay on the lower Riverwalk side floors.
Hotel staff is very courteous and helpful. No issues with the room. They are a little larger than standard hotel rooms. Beds as comfortable. Flat screen tv. Mini bar. Clean. Quiet. All in all very relaxing and enjoyable.

name: Hilton Phoenix Airport
title: “Clean but average”
text:
The staff was friendly, courteous, welcoming and professional. My only complaint is that this was a business trip and we could not get Wifi. Come on guys... this is 2011/2012. I am finding this at a few of the Hilton brand hotels .... having to either pay for Wifi or the Wifi is not working.
In this instance, I had to call the front office on 3 occasions to get a connection to my room. They in turn had to contact their computer guy to rectify the issue. This took an entire day.
The hallways were a bit noisy and with any hotel, get a room away from the elevators.

name: Econo Lodge Airport
title: “Absolute bargain basement accomodations.”
text: I don't know if it's fair to disparage a hotel that's $40.00 a night, but even at cheap prices, one has a right to expect some level of decent accomodations. The rooms were fairly large, but depressingly drab. They reeked of smoke, and the curtains were worn. The "security" of the door (an electronic key) was utterly useless as it seemed to be as easy as cake for someone who knows what they're doing to gain access to your room. The "linens" were a joke. Is it too much to ask to get washclothes that don't have holes in them? And the sheets looked like they had been in use since the 80's. There were hairs on my pillowcase, and burnmarks on the bedspread. I actually never got under the covers either night, and slept in my clothes. Two of the TV channels (cable) had no sound at all. The area is depressing, with only a Jack N' The Box and a seafood place available for those brave enough to walk around the corner. I booked a stay there to attend a Cardinals game, so I knew going in it wouldn't be great. I just thought someone might care enough to provide the basics to anyone desperate enough to stay there. I will say that the front office attendant was extremely nice and helpful, and answered all of my questions with a smile. And there was a coffee maker in my room along with a hairdryer. Neither of which I used. Otherwise nearly any other motel in that area would probably be a nicer stay. (Or maybe not. LOL!)

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Phoenix-North
title: “Something for everyone!!!”
text:
We recently stayed at the Embassy Suites in March. Our original hotel tuned out to be horrible, so my husband and I were on a frantic search for somewhere clean and nice. Luckily we were able to book one night at the Embassy Suites. Although we were not able to stay the second night, the front desk gave us another hotel's number and advice to call quickly as rooms were fast filling up.
The grounds are beautiful with an impressive pool and large area for sunbathing/relaxing/playing. We were there when a youth baseball team was there; however, they had room to play and did not bother us at all. Our room was clean and spacious. It had a small kitchenette area with sink, refrigerator, and microwave. I liked that the bedroom was seperate from the living area. The only negative feature is that the rooms are a bit dated, the bed was not very comfortable, and the AC was centerally controlled. The ceiling fan in the bedroom did circulate the air and helped make it comforable. These were minor things for us and did not sway our opinion of the hotel.
We took advantage of the two hour complementary cocktails in the bar. The breakfast buffet was much better than a regular continental breakfast. Between these two features, the price was very reasonable!
We are looking forward to next March and enjoying the Embassy Suites for our full time in Arizona!

name: Arizona Biltmore
title: “Great service at Frank & Alberts”
text: If you want a truly enjoyable dining experience for breakfast, lunch, or dinner make sure to request one of Maria's tables. You will experience top notch service and a great attitude. We stayed at the resort with our kids, friends and their kids and we all loved our two day stay at the resort. If you are looking for a great steak at Frank & Alberts ask Maria for the "Andy" Special.

name: Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk
title: “#1 for Families on the Riverwalk”
text:
The Drury Plaza is beautiful. It used to be a bank and they kept many of the historical aspects of the bank (gilded ceiling in lobby and large art deco inspired accents). They have kept the hallways tiled instead of carpeted so I was worried about the noise. We were in a corner suite (1422) and never heard any other guests.
The suite was nice with two huge queen beds and flat screen TVs in the living area and the bedroom. There was a ceiling fan in the bedroom. We were very comfortable. The bathroom doors do not have locks and the bathrooms do not have vents. There are also no plastic bags in the trash cans. I thought this was strange but we stayed at the other Drury in Northwest San Antonio and it was the same.
Currently there is construction next to the hotel so be sure to ask for a room on the opposite side where the construction is. We weren't near the elevator but I kept hearing an elevator all night long. I think it was either a construction elevator or buses. I was up all night but my husband and kids had no trouble sleeping.
The manager's reception had limited cocktails/beer/wine and popcorn, nachos, carrots & celery and snack mix. All the snacks were super salty. They also have soft drinks available but only Pepsi products. I was glad I brought my 12 pack of diet coke on my trip.
We had booked a 2 queen room but were upgraded to a suite. I think in the future I will book a suite. It is great when you have kids and can actually send them to another room. 
This is probably the best place for families if you want to stay right on the River Walk. It is a long hike on the river to the Alamo, so if you are just going for the Alamo you might want to consider somewhere closer. We walked to Market Square. It is 4 very long blocks away and the neighborhood doesn't appear to be the best. We were asked for money several times and you walk by a probation center. 
We ate at The Original Mexican Café and it was horrible. Do your research on where to eat before you go. I wish I had. The next day when we were off the River we ate at The Alamo café (a chain) and it was great!

name: Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak Resort
title: “Perfect for Us”
text: I traveled to Phoenix for a wedding that was being held at this resort, and so booked a casita. The casita was incredible, upstairs-downstairs, great balconies, and kitchen. There was so much room, and traveling with teenagers, that worked really well. The staff is friendly and room service was fast! The only reason I didn't give it five stars is that the hotel is just beginning to show signs of wear, and we were right by a pool, so it was a little noisy. However, that wouldn't stop me from staying at the resort again.

name: Coast Phoenix Sky Harbor Hotel
title: “Poor Crowne Plaza”
text:
This is the worst Crowne Plaza I have ever visited. Although the hotel was renovated at some point, as evidenced by the lobby and some updates to the room decor, this hotel is not one that I would recommend.
Upon reaching the airport, it took over 20 minutes for the shuttle to show up after I called the hotel. Since I arrived at night, I thought this was a little long considering a key selling point of this hotel is that it is an "airport" hotel.
I had emailed the hotel my requests related to my room, as I am a light sleeper and need quiet to sleep through the night. I am also a member of the hotel chain's loyalty program. No one responded to my email, which was sent through the property's website at least one week prior to my arrival. After discussing my preferences with the front desk person upon arrival at the property, I was given a room on the "quiet" floor. In the first two minutes in the room, I heard train whistles blaring. OK, let's try another room... The next room features the delightful sounds of aircraft engines. I have stayed at other airport properties (including one at LHR) before and have not heard this much noise. I don't think this property is familiar with the concept of sound-proof or double-glazed windows. I suppose that I should just be grateful for the earplugs and the "Sleep Advantage" CD in the room.
The room is too dark. The lamps do not provide enough light. The lighting in the bathroom is also too dark. The light fixture in the bathroom has a broken covering, too.
Now here's the gross part. I always request two beds, even when I travel solo because the beds are not always up to my standards. I figure with two beds if something is wrong with one, I still have another. Well, in my room at the Crowne Plaza, the first bed has someone else's hair on it. I am not talking about one random strand that may have fallen off the housekeeper as she was making the bed. I am talking about several hairs of different lengths and textures. There is no way that someone could have made that bed and not seen all of that hair on the white sheet -- especially since the hair was jet black!!! The other bed did not show any obvious filth, and given the late hour of my check in tonight (and being on my second room in this hotel), I chose to use the second bed and plan to address the housekeeping issue with management in the morning.
There is one bright spot -- the free wireless internet!
What an overall disappointment! There are many hotel options in Phoenix, I recommend you avoid this one!

name: Arizona Biltmore
title: “Far from the best resort”
text: I stayed here for a conference for work - most of the conferences are at this sort of place, a fairly isolated large hotel complex, so I feel like I have a good comparison group. The Biltmore has pretty grounds, though I found the layout confusing. Hard to find my room (in one of the outlying cottages) and the gym. My biggest complaint is the food. I expect overpriced food, but this is overpriced and bad. Even the gelato from the little cafe was sort of gummy and stringy. I did not try Wright's their most expensive restaurant, admittedly; it probably is somewhat better, but out of my price range for a work trip. Also the concierge was not helpful, repeatedly trying to get you to eat at their places, not even recommending taking the shuttle to the nearby mall. Which also was kind of lame and the only thing really that's nearby. My room was fairly nice, well air conditioned, and large. No complaints, but nothing special either for this type of resort.

name: Arizona Grand Resort & Spa
title: “Exceeded Our Expectations”
text: We made our reservation on short notice, as we had unexpectedly come across some reasonable air fares over the kids' school April vacation week. The AGR exceeded our expectations in every regard. The accommodations near the Oasis Water Park were perfect, the resort's grounds were immaculate and breathtaking, and the entire staff clearly was putting their very best foot forward. If you are looking for a place to take the family for some Southwest Warm Weather R&R....you should seriously consider staying here. Be sure to hit the golf course, enjoy the water park and pools, and don't forget to talk with the concierge about off-property activites including mountain biking, horseback riding and more. Our entire family cannot wait to return! Thank you AGR!!

name: Hotel Elysee
title: “Excelente localização. Quartos de ótimo tamanho e bonita decoração. Cama muito confortável. Staff atencioso.”
text: A limpeza deixa um pouco a desejar. Por 2 vezes tive que solicitar a retirada de embrulhos vazios. O minibar não estava funcionando e não faziam a reposição dos produtos consumidos. Os secadores de cabelo são arcaicos. Os banheiros, que são lindos, poderiam ter pisos aquecidos ou secadores de toalhas pois são gelados no inverno.

name: Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak Resort
title: “Not Too Shabby!!”
text:
Stayed here for a weekend getaway on the Stay 3 Nights and get the third night free. This in itself was a great deal, and sold the hotel for us. We brought our dog along because it was dog friendly, and the website promised welcome amenities for the dog when we got there, we never got anything. This wasn't a huge deal, and our dog didn't care so that was ok. The pools were awesome with a relazing lazy river. Unfortunately, there was a nerd convention in town, and there was a bunch of teenage geeks running around in costumes making a lot of noise. This almost ruined the whole weekend. 
But when you look at things that the hotel can control, they didn't really do any wrong. There was no above and beyond service, but it wasnt bad by any means. We liked the spacious rooms and the pools, and was in a nice location
We will probably be staying here again!

name: BEST WESTERN Airport Inn
title: “Great overnight stay & awesome shuttle service”
text:
Stayed over night here before our morning (9am) flight out to DTW to begin our 7 day vacation. As this is not a BW Plus or Premier, we weren't expecting much at all. We stayed in a room on a bottom floor room facing the long term parking at the most eastern portion of the hotel. We were pleased with the cleanliness of the room, the friendliness of the staff and the mounted pumps filled with soap, shampoo/hair conditioner. Upon entry into the room, there were no weird smells.
We took the shuttle to the airport at 615am. The shuttle van looks to be fairly new, the air conditioning worked very well. The van itself was clean, the ride comfortable, roomy and the hotel shuttle employee basically took our luggage and put it in the van. 
The only thing we did not like was the tv and the available channels. The tv was not flat screen, no HD channels and there were only 25 channels. But, this was to be expected. We were only staying one night, so it was not to be a big issue. Merely passing along this information for my fellow hotel reviewers.

name: Marriott Phoenix Airport
title: “Very good service-tired facilities”
text: Really liked the staff. Facilities were quite tired. Several pieces of the workout equipment were not working.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Phoenix Airport
title: “Fine hotel but noise is a problem”
text: I booked this hotel for the night before my overseas flight, which was comprised of 14 hours of flying time and two stopovers. I took the hotel's shuttle, which leaves every half hour in the morning, to the airport the next morning. That is a convenient service. I have no complaints about the room, which was completely satisfactory, or the breakfast was good. However, I barely slept at all, which was extremely distressing. My room was on the north side of the building in the rear that faces the merger of the 10 and 202 freeways, which happens to be on a curve. The noise was loud and non-stop all through the night. I don't know how less noisy the rooms facing south would be, but if sleep is important to you, at least insist on room that doesn't face the freeway. I have booked a different hotel prior to a trip I'm taking in July with hopes of a better night's sleep.

name: Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak Resort
title: “It was so fun.”
text:
We loved our stay , we were at the hotel most of our 4 day stay and we never were bored .
Drinks by the pool , games and snow cones for the kids , no complaints .

name: The Clarendon Hotel - Phoenix's Urban Retreat
title: “Motel, NOT hotel”
text:
This "hotel" is NOT what its website would have you believe, and it does NOT deserve its star rating.
The décor is hideous – the walls were painted a dark blue/red/purple, and the furniture was shabby. Instead of achieving the mod feeling that they were so obviously trying to achieve, it just looked ugly and dated. The crappy carpet squares didn’t fit correctly against the walls, and felt sticky underfoot. The shower was not clean and the water was lukewarm to cool. The toilet basin was not properly attached, and slammed into the wall every time you flushed. The air conditioning didn’t work very well at all (kept our room at about 80 degrees when on High), and blew hot air directly at the head of the bed. Additionally, the AC controls were on the ceiling, so you had to pull up a chair to adjust them (not that it did you any good). The bed linens were nice, and the mattress was fairly comfortable. BUT, rather than paying for a duvet cover for the comforter, they simply wrapped it up in two sheets. The sheets, of course, didn’t stay on the comforter well at all during the night. The end result was that you were sleeping with 3 bunched sheets and one dirty comforter – not at all pleasant.
The Clarendon Hotel is, quite obviously, a gay hotel. Not a gay-friendly hotel, which we would have welcomed. Instead, we were made to feel very uncomfortable as the only heterosexual couple in the hotel. It didn't help that I am 5 months pregnant, and had to endure "God, I HATE breeders!" and like comments in the elevator and lobby. The clientele was obviously on the prowl for a one-night stand.
The neighborhood is sketchy. There are two doors from the parking area that ought to be locked at all times, but were always open and unlocked during our 5 day stay here, leaving the hotel totally unsecure. When we checked out at 4:00 am, there were 5 different men wandering the halls. One of them even followed us out to our car. Were they guests? People off the street? Who knows? It was very, very creepy.
When we got to the front desk to check out, no one was there. We ended up waiting more than 25 minutes for the front desk attendant to arrive, which made us late to the airport. So much for customer service.
Do yourself a favor, stay somewhere else. This hotel ruined my romantic vacation.

name: BEST WESTERN Airport Inn
title: “First and last night of holiday”
text: What a find! After a long day travelling arrived at airport, collected hire car, easily found hotel and straight to bed. On return plenty of room to repack cases for journey home, easy return of car at a very early hour and homeward we go. Free internet and printing for on line check in. Very easy check in at hotel with helpful staff on both occasions. Cannot comment on food at nearbye restaurant as we were not there for long enough to try it. Absolutely ideal for when using the airport.

name: The Clarendon Hotel - Phoenix's Urban Retreat
title: “Worst Hotel”
text:
We booked our stay for one night at the Clarendon because we wanted to be by the airport. It was advertised that the hotel was minutes away from the airport. Well it was not very close at all we were about 10 miles away and in traffic it took us about a hour to go that distance. When reading it was near the airport I would think it was just a couple of miles. 
While checking in we had a guy in front of us asking where a gay bar was. The clerk was happy to assest and tell him about a bar and started giving details about the activities that went on in the bar. His discription was very inappropriate and unprofesional. 
Once we were done with that experience we noticed the pillows were down pillows. My wife is allergic and called the front desk to ask for new pillows and was laughed at. The clerk hung up with out saying if they would replace the pillows. My wife made a second call and than was told they would have to check on alternative pillows and they would call her back. When called back they could only come up with two pillows. One pillow looked like it was laying in the gutter and the other was over stuffed. 
The air conditioner in the room did not work with the thermostat at all. The room was like a oven and smelled horrible from the disinfectant. Thank God for a portable fan in the room. 
In the morning we were afraid to eat breakfast at this place because of the terrible service we were given.

name: The Clarendon Hotel - Phoenix's Urban Retreat
title: “Worst hotel experience ever”
text:
My wife and I arrived on a Thursday for a 4 night stay over Labor Day weekend. Having never stayed here before, we chose The Clarendon for its pool, not to mention a great vacation package sale on Expedia. 
The hotel's website proclaims itself to be a luxury boutique hotel. Didn't take long to realize this couldn't be further from the truth. Why you ask? The location leaves much to be desired. The elevator is a microwave oven that barely does its job. You can't escape the ever present foul stench that permeates the entire hotel. Our third floor room had an inadequate air conditioner loud enough to wake the dead. How about maid service not cleaning your room until around 5:00 pm? The rooftop bar is a bare bones ramshackle mess. The rooftop pool does not even exist. 
After using the shower the first night, it took several minutes to turn the water off. This happened again Friday morning, but we couldn't turn it off. A front desk girl was sent up who with the aid of some tools managed to turn off the water. Maintenance repaired it later in the day. We were willing to be forgiving for all of these issues, though the next day things took a dramatic turn for the worse.
Our first two days consisted of mostly sightseeing and a baseball game. Minimal time was spent at hotel. Saturday afternoon we decided to return for the hotel and finally use their heavily advertised ground floor pool. Much to our surprise, the parking lot was filled to capacity and we were unable to park anywhere near the hotel. Turns out The Clarendon was hosting a party for the gay community with several hundred people most of whom were obnoxiously drunk hanging out all over the pool, lobby, hallways, entrance, etc while extremely loud techno music boomed endlessly. Admission to the pool was $20.00 for this three ring circus. We inquired how long this party was going on and were told it was from noon to midnight from Friday to Monday. Factor in that was sponsored by Coors Light and Red Bull and you best believe it would be running even later.
The front desk never told us about this at check in. When finally told in the midst of this free for all, the front desk staff extended no apologies. We are not easily offended since we live in the San Francisco Bay Area and have even been in The Castro district at Halloween. The rude staff at The Clarendon were highly offensive to us as and the discriminatory treatment we received are nothing short of inexcusable. We were not made welcome here and checked out after two nights. We found another hotel for the remaining two nights. While going through the lobby, we were made fun of by the partygoers and the hotel staff. We overheard a front desk employee say that we were informed of the festivities during check in. This is a complete lie as we never would have stayed here had we known. 
In short, this was our worst hotel experience ever.

name: Philadelphia Marriott Downtown
title: “Central location”
text: I have stayed here twice and am I big fan. First of all, I love that you can take the subway from the airport to the hotel. I believe it was $7. The hotel is huge, near a bunch of cool stuff and there's a Starbucks (a real one) in the lobby. As I mentioned, you can take the subway either direction from just a few blocks away. Love the gym here, TV's with the treadmills and elipticals. Nice move there. I would recommend this place. Don't rent a car, just take the subway. It's fairly clean and safe, from what I gathered.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Phoenix - Biltmore
title: “GREAT place!”
text:
I love the layout of these suites! Especially when there are 2 travelers and one has to get up earlier than the other! It is just like having a little apartment. There is a separate kitchen with a microwave,apartment sized refrigerator and dishwasher. Small dining table and living room are in one area, then there is a hallway leading to the bathroom and the bedroom. In the hall is a mirrored closet containing the ironing board. At the end of the hall is the vanity. On one side of the vanity is the bathroom, and on the other side is the bedroom with door that you can close! My husband could get up early, leave the bedroom and shut the door. All his clothes were in the hall closet, so he could get dressed and not disturb me.
This place was VERY clean. It was somewhat worn though. Could use new carpet and maybe new furniture. It was not bad though. Bed was VERY comfortable!
The staff was all very friendly and helpful. They have a courtesy van that will take you anywhere within a 5 mile radius of the hotel. There is lots of shopping and dining options within that range, so that was handy. The breakfast was also very good. Location was also very easy to find and despite being on a fairly busy street, we did not have any issues with noise.We were in town for a trade show at the Phoenix convention center. We chose to stay here rather than pay the $250 per night or more prices downtown close to convention center. It was a very easy 10 minute drive to the CC from here. Would definitely recommend this hotel to others.

name: Residence Inn Phoenix Airport
title: “nice hotel- great breakfast- wonderful staff”
text:
My wife and I have stayed at this hotel a number of times/ love the fact that we can open the windows for fresh air/ shuttle service wonderfully helpful as well as the rest of the staff/
always cheerful and helpful/ breakfast buffet plentiful and very tasty including hot food
choices that are prepared fresh each day/ beds compfortable/nice kitchen for long stays/
shuttle will take you to rail line nearby/ Really like this hotel especially the wonderfully
cheerful and helpful staff/ to the manager- good hiring/ always have had a good sleep at this
hotel/ hotel very clean
- nice floral displays around the property and the pool looks nice/
 Only weakness no restaurant on site and except for a couple of oriental restaurants
across the street/ none really closeby- book as early as possible to get better rates/
less expensive on weekends

name: Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak Resort
title: “Disappointed Returning Guests...This Place Used to Be Much Better!”
text:
I certainly agree with many of the reviews below about the disapointment to our stay. We were here for 6 nights during Easter Week as well, and it was a mad house!! We have been coming for Spring Break to Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak for about 6 years, and it used to be terrific. That's why we keep coming back. Not this time!
In order to get a lounge chair at the pool, you had to go down and get in line 45 minutes before it opened at 8 am. Then if you wanted to get morning coffee in the coffee shop, you got into another 30 minute line. Just forget about trying to get into the restaurants. Parking was next to impossible sometimes. The entire resort seemed to be understaffed, over-occupied and just in a state of complete chaos. (Although the front desk was always manned pretty well and friendly.)
They advertise that they are "newly remodeled". Well, take it from folks that have been coming here for years...the rooms were not as spacious or clean as they used to be. They weren't horrible...they just used to be a lot better. They certainly are not up to par with what one expects from a Hilton resort. They remind me more of the quality you get at a Red Roof Inn. The bed we had was uneven, so we felt as though we were going to roll off to the right all night. That took some getting used to. The room next to us had a family of 8 people + a dog packed into it. The dog barked so much we ahd to call the front desk and have security sent.
Overall, this was not the relaxing vacation we expected. It is now only an "OK" resort, and a bit like Disney where everything requires you to get in a line. We love visiting the Phoenix area in the Spring from our cold Upstate NY home, but our family discussed it, and we don't think we will be returning to the Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak next year. We'll keep our eyse open for better reviews of other places here on Trip Advisor!

name: Hampton Inn Phoenix Midtown (Downtown Area)
title: “fabulous stay”
text: This was my first trip to AR and I was very pleased with my stay. The hotel was clean, comfortable, located in safe and convenient location, and had the continental breakfast. I am a huge coffee drinker and the free ALL DAY and NIGHT coffee was HUGE for me. lol The staff was very pleasant and helpful with all of my questions regarding restaurants, sights to see, etc. I was very impressed and will stay here again...

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Downtown Hotel
title: “nella media”
text: L'albergo si trova nella zona centrale di Philadelphia. Le principali attrazioni si possono raggiungere in 10-15 minuti a piedi. La zona è tranquilla e a due passi dalle vie più animate e piene di locali di Philadelphia. E' una struttura molto grande. La stanza aveva due letti queen molto comodi, ma non era particolarmente pulita. Erano presenti dei capelli nella vasca, che non mi aspettavo di trovare in uno Sheraton. Il personale alla reception non era particolarmente cortese. Consigliato per la posizione e per il prezzo che non era alto.

name: Hyatt Regency Phoenix
title: “Comfortable stay”
text: Stayed for almost a week to attend a conference at a great rate. Convenient location near public transit, restaurants, shopping, venues. Approx. $20 for taxi from airport, no shuttle service. Car rental on sight. Staff were friendly and helpful. The concierge staff were very helpful as I regularly had questions about sights and recommendations. Room was spacious, clean, comfortable and modern. I appreciated the ihome dock. It was too cold to enjoy the outdoor pool. The revolving restaurant had great food and excellent view. Unfortunately, it was only open for dinner so the view was limited at night.

name: Holiday Inn & Suites Phoenix Airport North
title: “Very quiet, beautiful rooms!”
text: My son was visiting GCU. The hotel location was perfect, just 15 minutes to the college and 10 minutes to the car rental return area at Sky Harbor Airport. The grounds are beautiful, the rooms beautiful as well. Very quiet even though they told me that they were at full capacity. The rooms are very spacious. The staff was super nice. I would have given the hotel a 5 star rating for cleanliness had it not been for all of the left over glasses and dirty plates left out side from the night before in the beautiful firepit lounge area. Sad to see on my departure morning. Still, I would stay here over and over... this property is just beautiful. Keep in mind the breakfast is not free, it is a "just ok" buffet for $10.00 per person, (I think they do have a childs menu that is free?) or you may order off of a breakfast menu. The main waitress in the breakfast area was extremely attentive, and so pleasant... I wish I would have gotten her name :)! I would highly recommend this hotel, truly lovely.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Phoenix - Biltmore
title: “Clean and quiet room.”
text: This was my first time at a Homewood Suites and I was happy. I found it nicer/cleaner than some of the Residence Inns I've stayed at. The bed was comfy, lots of soft pillows, a huge room service menue, and no problems with the internet service. I was upgrade to a 2 room suite based on being a Hilton VIP member, which was a nice surprise.

name: Hyatt Regency Phoenix
title: “Very nice/Upscale, slow service”
text: Evrything about this hotel was nice. Rooms and workout room are ok akthough rooms are bit smaller than expected. The pool is very small, like a kiddie pool, no laps here. No real views from ther rooms. The lobby is very new looking and big, shame they couldn't put more of it into the rooms. The bar is a good sports bar but pricey. Location is great just across from the Convention Center a couple of blocks from the Baseball stadium and 2 blocks from a catholic Church. Check in was well below average. Front desk was very friendly but it took them forever to check in people about 8-10min per person.....

name: Library Hotel
title: “Pukka Place!!”
text:
A wonderful hotel and an excellent location - close to grand central station, times square, 5th avenue, Empire State etc...
On arrival after a long flight we arrived too late for the complimentary wine and cheese (which is a very nice idea!) so were asked if we wanted a glass of wine brought up to our room. We asked for a glass of red and a glass of white, only to be brought a bottle of each with a lovely selection of cheeses! 
Rooms, although slightly small (which didn't really matter as we were not planning on spending lots of time there) were comfortable and clean. Good view onto maddison avenue. 
Staff were friendly and made you feel welcome, breakfast was adequate but not much of a selection (apart from the coffee's)
