Lots of books everywhere (i suppose it is the library hotel!) having spotted other hotels in NY we are very happy to have choosen the library - and would stay again.

name: Arizona Biltmore
title: “a little getaway”
text: we had friends in town and we picked the biltmore for the historical aspect-glad we did!we live i phx but this place makes you forget!there is a hotel ambasador that will give you a 11/2 hour tour of the property-i we totally loved it!(we tipped at the end) we had a poolside room so that was fab!rooms a aliitle older but had everthing you could want

name: The Westin Riverwalk
title: “Outstanding Service”
text: My nephew graduated from Basic Training-Air Force. We could not get to the door of the hotel before there were hotel personnel opening doors, asking questions and guiding us through the process. If every hotel had service like this hotel; there would no reason to purchase a home.... We dined at the hotel restaurant and Chef Eugene Schlaff came over to visit our table. Eugene you are a wonderful CHEF and HOST!!! He spoke with us at length and advised my Nephew to come back to see him at the hotel even if he were not staying overnight. It is my personal mission to go back and stay for a WEEK! The breakfast buffet is divine and the bread pudding is sinfully delicious. Chef Eugene shared the recipe with me; I made it but of course it was not like his but it was delicious. The bed sleeps like a cloud- I actually looked under the covers to find the name of the mattress. WOW Experience. FIVE STAR HOTEL AND SERVICE!!!!

name: Philadelphia Marriott Downtown
title: “Very satisfied”
text:
I obtained this hotel on a $47 bid on Priceline - it is rated 3* in the downtown zone. The hotel is very large and centrally located on Market Street. Check in was speedy and polite. I'm silver elite (from a credit card) so that may have had a benefit - I was given a room with a lovely view on a high floor.
The rooms in the hotel are quite nice; lush full bedding and a decent bathroom. Photos attached. Wired Internet access costs extra (I believe $9.95 from noon to noon, but didn't check closely - I used dial up) Local calls are $1, untimed. I think because I'm elite, they removed the charge and I got points for incidentals and credit for the stay towards elite (but not points)
The hotel has a pool and a very large fitness center with a good selection of cardio machines (at least 15 treadmills) and weight training equipment.
I'm staying here again (got it for $46 this time!) and looking forward to it.

name: Hampton Inn Phoenix-Biltmore
title: “Heck of a deal”
text:
I unexpectedly needed a room for one night in Phoenix so I ended up at Hotel Highland based on Fodor's review that it was a "heck of a deal" and most importantly for my purposes pretty near the airport, with complimentary shuttle. 
Very run of the mill from the outside but everything changed as soon as you get in. Lobby was very nice with fruit set out, free parking, and the room was great for the price. I loved the bedding, carpet and decor. I wasn't even expecting such a nice free breakfast. There were breakfast burritos, multiple choices of granolas to pick from, huge bowls of raspberries, blackberries and strawberries, which unlike some free breakfast with room places, was constantly being replenished. Staff was pleasant and our room was very queit. For $109 a night, it seemed a good value.

name: Hyatt Regency Phoenix
title: “Comfy”
text: I arrived in a foul mood after united's best attempts at making me never fly with them again. I was met by a smile by a staff member who looked exhausted (it was 2am) but she immediately put me in a better mood and seemed genuinely interested in me. Room was nice, breakfast was a little curious as they have an einsteins bagels in the hotel, but good all the same. I can't put my finger on it, but I liked this hotel. I left with good feelings regarding the Phoenix hyatt.

name: Sheraton Philadelphia Downtown Hotel
title: “Stay Elsewhere”
text: Never Again! One of the dirtiest Hotels I've ever stayed in. Empty beer bottles in the elevator and lobby from the night before. Dirty Bathroom....And it sounded like the room next door was being used by a prostitute, she was going all night. Front desk was of little help. We left early so we could go home and get some sleep. I have yet to get a response from Wyndham to my emailed complaint. Do yourself a favor and stay elsewhere!GM

name: Philadelphia Marriott Downtown
title: “Had a Great Experience”
text:
Just spent two nights at this hotel for business. The hotel is centrally located and everything I wanted to see or do was within walking distance. The room and bathroom were very clean. The bed was very comfortable with nice linens. The rooms also have high speed internet access.
I didn't eat at the restaurants, but there seemed to be a pretty decent variety of places in the hotel (steakhouse, sushi, sports bar/pub, diner type restaurant). There is also a Starbucks in the hotel lobby area. There are lots of good and interesting places to eat within an easy walk though, so go explore.
The only downside was parking. The hotel has valet parking for $32/day. There is a garage across the street from the hotel that was a bit cheaper (I think) and an outdoor lot on the side street next to the hotel.
I would definitely stay here again.

name: Hyatt Regency Phoenix
title: “Excellent Service”
text: I would just like to commend on the great service I've received at the terrace cafe. Our server was friendly but I can't remember her name, I do want to comment though on the excellent service that we got from Chad. He was very attentive, greeted our table first, brought our drinks and continuously check on us. He was very personable and had a warm smile. Good food, could have had a better selection in music, overall experience was great.

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton Phoenix
title: “Doubletree Phoenix”
text: Friendly and helpful staff. The complimentary breakfast buffet is really good. Generous amounts of real bacon cooked just right. Beautiful pool. I have to go to Phoenix often and plan to stay there again. Only downside is the constant sound of helicopters at night.

name: Hampton Inn Phoenix Airport North
title: “Great value”
text: My wife and I came to Phoenix for a concert and found this Hampton to have a great deal on a one bedroom suite for under $90. The hotel is well kept and clean and the staff is friendly. We arrived at 2:45pm and were told we would have to wait as our room wasn't ready - roughly 45 minutes later it was ready.The internet is one of the easiest I've found to get logged on to but it is very slow with a download Speedtest of <1MB. In our 3rd floor suite, #305, we heard every footstep from the people upstairs. I would prefer if hotels would install central air instead of those noisy, under-window type A/C units. The bed was awesome but the air conditioner cycling on and off was disturbing. We didn't sleep very well.

name: Holiday Inn Express Phoenix Downtown
title: “Very pleasant stay and wonderful service”
text:
I stayed in this holiday inn for four nights for a business trip. I had a very pleasant stay due to the following:
Proximity to downtown
Walking distance to a variety of restaurants and shopping places
About 3 miles from the main airport
Great service a particular thanks to Elaine at the front desk and the "always smiling and happy" Yadina at the breakfast area. Even the manager makes it a point to ask if everything is ok.
My room was clean, spacious with a small fridge, and large flat TV.
The pool was clean with plenty of towels ; it also has a nice jacuzzi area.
One comment i would like to make to the manager is to add more healthy breakfast choices such as fruits and oatmeal.
Overall it was an excellent experience. I will stay again at this hotel on my next trip.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS InnSuites Phoenix Hotel & Suites
title: “Buena parada para pernoctar”
text:
Excelente ubicación a las afueras de Phoenix, piscina bien cuidada, aparcamiento y Wifi gratuitos. La habitación es grande y confortable, por la noche silenciosa, el desayuno correcto.
Nos obsequiaron con una cena a base de carne a la parrilla.
En recepción no hablan español.

name: Comfort Suites Phoenix / MetroCenter
title: “We loved this hotel!”
text: This hotel was a great place to stay. The staff friendly, helpful and welcoming. The full hot breakfast was delicious and a nice way to start our day. We will choose to stay here again.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS InnSuites Phoenix Hotel & Suites
title: “Preiswert, Suiten sehr klein”
text:
Im nördlichen Teil von Phoenix gelegen, nach Downtown benötigt man ca 15 Minuten mit dem Auto. 2 Etagen, kein Aufzug. Pool vorhanden.
Viele der Zimmer sind als Suiten deklariert, diese sind aber sehr klein und eng. Ausstattung mit Mikrowelle, Kaffeemaschine.
Internet und Parken kostenlos.
American Breakfast ist im Preis mit eingeschlossen, allerdings darf man nicht zuviel erwarten. Es gibt zwar Rührei und Waffeln, jedoch alles mit Papptellern und Plastikbesteck. 
Die Doppelbetten in den "Suiten" snd nur Queensize ! Trotz Lage an einer Hauptstraße vergleichsweise ruhiger Schlaf.

name: Hyatt Place Phoenix - North
title: “Very nice hotel great stay”
text:
I stayed 4nights here in April 2012 and I must say it was a very nice stay the rooms are very spacious and the king size beds are very comfortable you get a very nice flat screen tv in every room.The breakfast buffet is very nice and u get a good variant of hot and cold food and is really good the only let down is the coffee u get with it very weak but there is a Starbucks coffee machine which the staff will make u a great coffee.
The staff are very nice and great u every time u enter the hotel and if u want a nice quiet night ask them for a room on the east side of the hotel away from the highway

name: Aloft Phoenix-Airport
title: “Nice, modern hotel”
text: My wife and I have been wanting to stay at an Aloft and finally got the opportunity in Phoenix before flying out the next day. Hotel is very clean. Room is very modern, somewhat small, but it works well. Our room faced the airport so I got to watch planes land, which was pretty cool. Room was quiet and you didn't even know you were close to the airport. The clerk at the front desk was very helpful in directing us to a great place to eat. This hotel also offers a shuttle to/from the airport which was very convenient. Can't wait to stay at one of their other properties.

name: The Ritz-Carlton Phoenix
title: “Missing the little things”
text:
I stayed at this hotel on a business trip for two nights. Overall, it was OK. However, I would not call it a luxury hotel. They missed on many little things. A couple of examples:
- we had no hot water one morning
- the clock radio had the wrong time on it
- the restaurant messed up our lunch orders and then the waitress tried to pretend it never happened
- I was on a conference call in my room the day of checkout and house keeping tried to come in to clean my room
None of this (except the hot water) is really a huge deal, but none of them should happen in a luxury hotel. so if you are looking for a buttoned up, luxury hotel, you should pass on the Ritz Phoenix.

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton Phoenix
title: “Little Things Make a Difference”
text: This hotel is located near downtown, and is generally ok. Rooms, lobby, grounds are all clean. Newspaper was not available on Sunday, free WSJ weekend was there on Saturday. Elevators to rooms are slow. Early risers will find packaged muffins and coffee in the lobby. Breakfast is free but a tip is expected. Canned fruit, leftover bacon mixed with packaged scrambled eggs, doughy pastries and imitation creamer are the stars of this dreary event. Seating under bright flourescent lights and rude dining room staff do not help the experience. The rooms are spacious, with small refrigerator, hair dryer and toiletries included. My room had ripped vinyl on a chair, the refrigerator setting froze food, and the toilet gurgled. Another guest complained about a broken hair dryer and broken security lock. My traveling companions complained that they were able to hear everything in the room next to them. These little things make a difference, and keep this location from being great.

name: Library Hotel
title: “Loved the Library Hotel”
text: We just returned from a 4 night stay at the Library Hotel. We were in room 400.002 and it was perfect. Yes the rooms are on the small side, but my husband and I had no problem storing our luggage, clothes, etc. The bed was very comfortable, loved the down pillows and comforter cover, the bathroom was clean and well kept. The neutral colors in the room and the contemporary lines made for a beautiful and well laid out room. What truly makes the hotel is the 2nd floor lounge. From the breakfast to the late night snacks, it was a great place to unwind or prepare for the day. The staff were very helpful with dinner recommendations and directions. The hotel location was a 15 minute walk to the Theatre district or 5-7 minutes to Grand Central Terminal. We have stayed in quite a few hotels in NYC and this is by far our most favorite among the boutique type hotels. If you want impersonal, larger rooms and lots of people, then try one of the chain hotels near Time Square. Otherwise, give the Library a try...I doubt you will be disappointed.

name: Holiday Inn Express Chandler - Phoenix
title: “Nice hotel in a good location”
text: I prefer Holiday In Express hotels for the price and amenities. This one is as nice as the others I have stayed in. The hotel was in a perfect location for our stay, the facility was clean, the beds were comfortable, free wifi was nice, and the continental breakfast was good. I enjoyed the pool and hot tub, which were clean and at a great temperature. The staff was friendly and efficient. One thing to consider is that our room was on the freeway side, which we could hear once the air conditioning was turned off, but it did not bother me at all because we were so tired after running around all day. If that is a concern for you, you might want to ask for a room on the other side of the hotel.

name: Arizona Biltmore
title: “Frank Lloyd Wright inspired property with peaceful grounds”
text: Great hotel with super on site restaurants, helpful staff, glorious grounds, a wide assortment of pools, including the main pool with a swim up bar. A wonderful oasis in the desert.

name: The Westin Riverwalk
title: “Fantastic service dealing with food allergies”
text: It's always challenging trying to find gluten free options, but when you also have other food allergies, it gets even more complex. I'm staying at the Westin for a business conference and mentioned my food issues to the Concierge upon check-in and have been amazed by the personal attention to make sure I can be confident that everything I've enjoyed here is not only delicious but safe for me. Thanks to all of you - Eugene Schlaff, sous chef, Orin McCann, director of food & beverage, Andrew Laughlin, Chef de Cuisine at Zocca, Michael Ruiz, sous chef and Arturo - as well as the wait staff. All showed genuine concern and offered help beyond my stay here. Incredible! Never before have I experienced both incredible service, but great food and wonderful choices. I highly recommend the hotel and restaurant.

name: Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs Resort
title: “Wish It Would Have Been Better”
text: There are a few things to know before booking your stay at this hotel. I have had very good experiences in the past with Hilton, but this resort was not very good. There are a lot of extra fee's associated with this hotel. They are as follows: to use the gym, sit in certain chairs in the pool area, to use the internet, to have shuttle service from the airport, 22% gratuity feel on every item purchased in the rest, pool area, and other services. The staff is a hit or miss. Our room did not get cleaned two out of five days. When I called and complained we discovered that the buttons on the phone didn't work. The lights attached to the bed didnt work. We went to check out paddles for ping pong and they only had one paddle. The girl said "sorry guess you won't be playing today.We don't know where they are." The water machine at the golf course was broken. It's the desert for goodness sake. Overall grounds were crapped out. Housekeeping leaves carts all over. The conference room smelled musty and they left there staff meeting notes for guests to see. No surprise they only had a 40% satisfaction guest rate for March. I was expecting a Hilton resort and this certainly did not live up to the Hilton reputation. Also, this hotel in a crappy neighborhood. Think Compton, CA. Stay in Scottsdale. It it worth the little extra money you may spend to be there.

name: Library Hotel
title: “looks great but bad service and lots of noise”
text: The room looked great but: the worst service ever and construction noise 24h every day. We got a special package that offered bubbly wine when we arrived; we never got that. We asked for wake-up calls but didn't receive them. Sheets were dirty (they said they had problems with the washing machines!). Shampoo, condidtioner bottles and toilet paper were not renewed!! we had to ask for them!!! And inquire if the construction noise has stopped before booking if you are still willing to risk it. We couldn't sleep for 4 nights.

name: Hyatt Regency Phoenix
title: “No Frills, Overpriced”
text:
I accompanied my husband to a show at the convention center. His company gave us a choice of hotels so we stayed at the Hyatt for my convenience in reaching day time venues while he was working - the others were too far away from the light rail. They did allow us to check in early the day of our arrival which was a big bonus. 
The room was merely average - desert generic decor, but sort of a dated look. Linens so-so. Limited TV channel selection. Pay plan for wireless internet access- it was $12-14 a day which is an outrage when it is free at the Holiday Inn Express. Not very fast either.
Housekeeping skipped our room the first day because she saw me enter the room but did not see me leave a few minutes later. She apparently paid no attention to the fact that there was no Do Not Disturb hanger. I had to call late in the day to get the room cleaned and then they didn't leave face cloths or provide an extra roll of TP. Took 3 calls to get it all right.
Having said that, the staff was always responsive and polite (I was polite when I called.)
Limited "amenities" included a very weak hair dryer. Shampoo and hand soaps were provided and a very stinky hand lotion. The "fragrances" were awful. No tissues were provided. (really, Hyatt?) Iron and Ironing board in closet along with one extra blanket.
Laundry service was available which we used because we were extending our trip. I have no idea if prices are in line or not -first time i have ever used such a service. $7 to launder a pair of jeans. The items were returned the same day around 530 pm and my jeans never looked so good.
Day 1, I heard very loud construction-type noises all morning in rooms above and beside us. When I left to go to a museum I discovered a young man on the floor by the elevators cutting the carpeting. When I returned some hours later (apparently he was at it all day,) he was gluing the seams. The rest of the day and all night into the next day, our floor reeked of that overwhelmingly horrible chemical smell of glue. No warnings were given to the guests on that score so that is bad. They obviously didn't care who was breathing those fumes. Are we hotel customers supposed to be huffers? 
Noise continued day 2. 
The concierge employees were most helpful and friendly. Gave us good directions to the light rail, the closest drugstore and restaurants and when they found out upon our check out where we headed next, gave us some small publications and a map. Nice touch.
FOOD: The restaurants were OK-not great. Didn't get to try Compass as it was closed for a private party. Their breakfast is held in a separate small space on the 2nd or 3rd floor that quickly crowds. Buffet offered was $14.95 and limited selections. No vegan entrees on the buffet which was shocking at such a hotel. Come on. Vegetarian fare consisted of eggs-scrambled only. Oatmeal was on the buffet and the only fruit offered was cantaloupe and honey dew. Again. Come on. The only thing good was the coffee. Food was not kept hot enough on the buffet which is a food safety issue. It doesn't take a long time to produce a bad outcome with eggs.
There is an Einsteins' Bagel for breakfast and lunch which is better priced. A 2 to 5 minute walk about the neighborhood shows you that there are much better and cheaper places to eat. Lots of places are open for breakfast. For dinner walk a couple blocks north to the Sheraton and eat at District, or walk south and eat at Kincaid's. For entrees, I preferred District and my husband Kincaid's. The portions at Kincaid's prevented dessert. At District get the whoopie pies and "milkshake." We both LOVED those. There are bunches of restaurants all over the area. 
AREA: a couple blocks from the Hyatt and Convention Center was the Arizona Center which is small outdoor shopping "mall" with mostly restaurants and cheesy gift shops. Some store fronts are closed. It is a tourist or convention-goers trap. There is no drug store nearby - you have to take the light rail. I followed concierge directions with no trouble. It is basically an honor system. You pay $1.75 a ride no matter where you are going. $3.50 gets you all day. No one checks to see that you have a ticket which I find very odd. There are no turnstiles or ticket readers per DC Metro. You 'activate" the ticket but no one checks it. The CVS is the closest to the Hyatt-they said about a mile but it sure seemed further than that. It was right by the rail line but the sidewalks and everything around were run down, littered and dirty with graffiti on the sidewalk and nefarious characters hanging about. I have no idea whether it is safe or not but it sure didn't seem to be. Perhaps the hotel personnel should find out?
SUMMARY: My impression is that the Hyatt Regency management feels they have a captive and well-heeled business clientele from the Convention Center who are on expense accounts and therefore, don't care that the Hyatt is pretentious and overpriced and offer few amenities. Overall, a real bare bones, a la carte hotel. You get only the value of the location and everything else is overpriced for its quality - or lack of same. The management and housekeeping should try to emulate the concierge staff. 
We would not stay here again.

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton Phoenix
title: “Overall great stay, great value”
text: We stayed here in January 2012 for the Fiesta Bowl. The location was great -- 1 block north of the lightrail station, which allows for a quick bus ride to the airport and a 15 minute ride to downtown. We got a great rate especially considering the fact that this was during the holidays, and the staff was very friendly. I have had better breakfasts at other properties, but since it is free, it's hard to complain. Note that breakfast closes relatively early since I think the property caters to businessmen, so make sure you don't miss out. Unfortunately, the pool wasn't heated well (or at all) so the ocean-like temperature wasn't particularly enjoyable. Overall, we had a great stay and would consider returning to this hotel if back in the area.

name: The Ritz-Carlton Phoenix
title: “Tremendous Service Recovery”
text: I stayed at the Ritz last fall and had a slight service issue. Due to some internal communicaiton issues it was not resolved while I was in residence. To compensate I was offered a complimentary stay. I was not going to take them up but happened to have a business trip come up in the area. I must say that I have never had such as over the top service recovery. Every moment of our stay was perfect. We were upgraded to the concierge floor. I have stayed in a number of "executive/concierge" floors and this one was over the top with both the personal touch of all staff and the food/beverage/services offered. The hotel location is great, we were able to walk/run on the trails in the Biltmore area and shop and eat at the Biltmore mall right across the street. Its relatively close to the airport. The food in the Ritz was great on my last stay and seemed even better this time. I like the small pool area and the workout facility is just right for the size of the hotel. I had to move onto a 5 star resort in Scottsdale after my weekend stay and I actually felt I was slumming it! Well done Ritz!

name: Hyatt Regency Phoenix
title: “Very Pleasant Stay”
text:
I would rate the service from this hotel as above average. My stay was as part of a group reservation that I was in charge of making and the staff were exceedingly helpful from the word go.
We had a standard room that was very pleasant with good maid service each day, with the room being straightened each morning around 10:30.
Room service was good and the breakfast really nice, if a little on the expensive side.

name: Arizona Biltmore
title: “Great historical resort”
text: If you are looking for a modern, new resort, this is not the place. This resort has a long history of high class, resort level experience. All but one president has stayed here since the opening in the 20s. Our rooms were fair and older but very clean and comfortable. Big TVs and great beds and a patio next to the pool. Great for the kids. The grounds are immaculate. Clean. Service throughout was awesome with exception of the little cafe. These girls were all fairly rude and short with customers. Most people didn't seem to care as they wanted quick and accurate service. Elsewhere, Biltmore service is true RESORT service. The place is beautiful and really enjoyed the history throughout.

name: Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak Resort
title: “Great Place for Families”
text:
I have stayed at this property twice, and in fact we are going back this weekend. The main appeal is that it is family friendly, has child care (a day camp) on site and also the nice water park. 
Most of the rooms have been renovated, except they left the popcorn ceilings. Another nice feature is the separate bedroom in the suites. The outside of the property feels dated circa 1970's, but it is solid, large and quiet. I never had a problem with noise. One tip: get a courtyard view room in the FRONT of the North bldg. it overlooks a pretty pool and fountain and is quieter than the South bldg. the pool also gets mostly adults.
This is not the best hotel for a romantic getaway, but if you have kids and want to have fun, it's great. The food is fine--not gourmet but fine. the only thing I did not like was no Wifi-you have to pay $12 per 24 hours for Internet service, which I find tacky. 
For those without kids or wanting a more upscale feel try the Pointe Hilton South Mtn or for really intimate, The Palms resort in Scottsdale.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “Great experience!”
text: My husband and I eloped in New York and we stayed at the Hotel Giraffe. It was a lovely hotel and we had a great experience. The roof deck is a perfect spot for relaxing, having a few drinks, etc. The coffee bar in the lobby was an added bonus, as were the generous spreads at both the breakfast and the daily cheese/wine reception. And the location was very convenient to restaurants, shopping , music, etc. I would love to stay at the Hotel Giraffe again!

name: Royal Palms Resort and Spa
title: “Like coming home only better...”
text:
We just returned from spending the past week at the Royal Palms and there simply aren't enough good things to be said about our visit.
From the moment we arrived, we were greeted by an amazingly friendly, warm and caring staff who went out of their way to make us feel welcome. Our first contact was with Tony, one of the valet attendants, who opened our doors, introduced himself and thereafter, always knew us by name. (This was a trait of everyone we met on the property...it was as if we were staying with friends who always greeted us this way.) He took care of our luggage while we checked in and then gave us a tour of the property and then showed us to our room.
We splurged on a deluxe casita and it was well worth it. The room was beautiful, but then again, what isn't beautiful at the Royal Palms? The only other place we have seen that was so completely visually appealing was a resort we stayed at in Tahiti. Obviously very different environments but beauty is beauty no matter where it's found. The entire property makes you feel like you are living in a lovely, watercolor painting. The colors of the buildings and flowers and artwork all make for a serene and soothing atmosphere which you find yourself melting into very quickly.
The casita was beautifully decorated and very roomy. We had a private patio in the back with a view of Camelback Mountain. We had our own patio in the front as well (there are curtains you can let down to increase the feeling of privacy) where we sat and enjoyed the lovely evenings. The bathroom is a slice of heaven. The huge, walk-in shower with built-in, tiled seating is a spa treatment in itself. And the selection of soaps and lotions that are provided are wonderfully luxurious.
We can't offer enough praise to everyone, and we mean literally EVERYONE, who works there. Everyone is so happy and I don't mean in a freakish Disney/Stepford way. It's as if everyone there is absolutely thrilled to be doing their jobs and in finding ways to make you feel content and welcome. We never heard a raised voice, saw a scowling face or felt as if we weren't the most important guests there.
The food in the restaurants is wonderful if just a little pricey but then again, you're paying for unsurpassed quality and service. T. Cook's serves marvelous meals and the Cabana Grill has wonderfully casual lunches (and breakfast brunch on Sundays) and poolside drinks. The poolside service is unsurpassed and again, Rick and Jose (I can't say enough good things about the two of you either!!!) make you feel as if you're visiting their home. And by the joy they demonstrate when doing their jobs, it's no wonder you feel that way.
We didn't use the spa but we visited the boutique area and it was beautiful as well and also well stocked with a wide assortment of spa products.
On our last night there, we had the privilege of attending the General Manager's reception in the Presidential Villa (where President Bush had stayed just 2 weeks prior...regardless of your politics, it's pretty cool to know you're standing in the bedroom where a world leader has recently slept!). Our wonderful friend Jose was there and we also had the joy of meeting Greg Miller, the GM, Rick Behr, Delores (I hope I spelled your name correctly!) the Director of Experiences, and Gregory Casale, the head chef. They were all entertaining and charming and we had lovely drinks and hors d'oeuvres which made for a great send-off on our last night. We were truly sad to leave them, in fact when we left to go back to our casita, Jose made a point of stopping us and letting us know what a pleasure it had been to have us stay with them. It felt so much like saying good-bye to a friend that we hugged him before we left.
My husband had seen the resort on Great Hotels on the Travel Channel but could not remember the exact name of the resort. Since we had never been to Phoenix before, that meant we had to search through every other high-end resort property before he recognized the Royal Palms from its pictures. Even after having looked at all those other properties, we just had a feeling about the Royal Palms and we couldn't have been happier to have made the choice we did. There will be no other place for us to stay on any future visits to Phoenix. Why would we? Coming back to the Royal Palms would be like coming home.
And as a testament to the commitment to service and care the Royal Palms offers, look at the negative reviews of any of the other comparable resorts. Do you see any responses from those properties' management? No. And in the scant negative comments I've seen about the Royal Palms (both of which seemed to come from completely unreasonable people in my opinion), they took the time to respond and see if they could make things right. That says it all to me.
This is the finest property in Phoenix, hands down. I don't need to stay anywhere else to know that. Thank you to everyone at the Royal Palms who made our stay with you an absolute joy. We will be back!!

name: Arizona Grand Resort & Spa
title: “Noisy Resort”
text:
I have taken my son who is 8 years old to Arizona as part of a summer break trip through the Western US.
We spend the first 4 nights at a different resort in Scottsdale and I booked the Arizona Grand Resort for 3 nights so we could spend time at the resorts Waterpark.
The waterpark itself is very nice and never seemed crowded.
The real minus point for us was the constant noise which might be due to having been assigned a room on the main floor but also the layout of the resort which meant that many rooms were facing the courtyard which in our case had another smaller pool.
It felt like being in a big apartment complex with constant noise going on into late at night.
This might all be just personal and seeing other reviews this seems to not have been an issue with others. We were probably spoiled by our previous stay at the resort in Scottsdale which was quite the opposite.
It was a one story resort with beautiful grounds, a nice pool and literally no noise.
The other minus point for us was the $ 30.00 resort fee which is not a problem in itself and we were aware of the fee in advance. I was just surprised to be charged an additional $ 14.95 per day for wifi.
We compared this with the other resorts resort fee of $ 15.00 which included wifi a few other amenities and to be fair, no waterpark.
I can see how this resort is wonderful for some, especially for family with kids but it just wasn't for us, even my 8 year old son preferred the other resort.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Phoenix-Metro Center
title: “Ok hotel, not the best location”
text: Just stayed here and the hotel was pretty good. I’m starting to like the Homewood suites for the space and in most cases the newness of them. This one seemed like it was new but not super new. The room I had was large and comfortable, with decent bedding and pillows. I only had breakfast one day and it was sort of sparse waffles, fruit, yoghurt and bread. I’m use to a little better spread. I didn’t use the pool, or really check out the property but what I saw was decent. My only gripe, very little signage to get from the lobby to the rooms. There are at least 3 sets of elevators and it was not clear which way to go from the elevators to the rooms. Other gripe the location of the hotel not a fan of Metro Centre after staying here, was a little ghetto (Ghetto Center) apparently is another name for the area. Granted almost every food chain was close by.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Phoenix Biltmore
title: “You get what you pay for”
text:
The pros -
Great location, just a few minutes' walk to Biltmore Fashion Park
Big rooms, great for families or just being comfortable
Complimentary happy hour and hot breakfast are great
Super friendly and accomodating staff
Big pool that's heated in winter
The cons -
The rooms are sorely in need of renovation: Small bathrooms, aged carpet, popcorn ceilings (!).
Our room smelled of smoke, interesting since indoor smoking has been banned in AZ for several years now.
We would stay there again, either as a couples or family getaway, due to the room value and location, but we recognize that it certainly is not a luxury hotel!

name: The Westin Riverwalk
title: “we were very impressed and will definitely return”
text: My wife and I spent our anniversary at the Westin Riverwalk in San Antonio, TX and were treated with a very nice surprise. The hotel and staff were wonderful. From the time we pulled up to the time we left, every detail was taken care of by friendly and knowledgeable staff. We enjoyed the views from our 7th story window overlooking the scenic riverwalk, and dined in their Italian restaurant, ZOCCA. The food was delicious as well as attractive. Janie Champagne, Director of rooms, personally spent time making us feel special. This hotel is a must for anyone wanting to visit San Antonio, or for locals wanting a nice gettaway by the riverwalk.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Phoenix Biltmore
title: “Great Place to Stay”
text:
My recent stay at this motel was fantastic! As you enter the lobby you see a large area with fish ponds, paths, and vegetation. Just a very good place to relax and have a drink. 
The room is very large (includeds bedroom and a separate work area), two large lcd tv's, couch and plenty of storage. 
Omaha Steak Company is located inside the motel. I ate there twice since I was traveling through three time zones. It was great resturant without the extreme prices associated with motel resturants.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Phoenix Biltmore
title: “The pool was small but we had it to ourselves both days we were there”
text: My husband stays at this hotel regularly when he travels to Phoenix, which is between 1-3 times a month. He drives a little further because he likes the hotel and he doesn't even take advantage of the free breakfast (because he leaves so early in the AM) or the happy hour... so our daughters and I met him out here for 2 days before a 10 day vacation out west. It was a great start to our vacation. I swam with the girls during the day while he worked and there were just a few other families (during the day) at the hotel during the week. We ate once at the hotel's restaurant for lunch and the food was great, but even better is that you just have to walk across the parking lot to the Biltmore mall where there are other food options (Paradise Bakery, Cheesecake Factory and others) and upscale shopping. It was nice because the hubby had the car and we were not "stuck" in the hotel. The FREE breakfast at the Embassy suites is OUTSTANDING- made to order omlettes, fresh pancakes or french toast, fruit, cereal, breads etc. I wouldn't stay here for a week's vacation, but it had everything we needed for a few days.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites - Phoenix
title: “Outstanding Stay!!”
text: I have switched my in Phoenix hotel arrangements to The Fairfield inn and Suites at 2520 N Central Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85004 because the facility is clean, well kept, and staff are wonderful. I am a picky traveler because I don't sleep well away from home, but this hotel goes the extra mile to make people feel welcome.

name: Legacy Golf Resort
title: “Awesome value...spotlessly clean!”
text: We stayed for one night earlier this month based upon reviews here. We were VERY impressed with the cleanliness, and the SIZE of our room! It was a suite with a fully stocked kitchen...AND even a washer and dryer! For less than $100 for the night...it was amazing!! It was nicely decorated...and VERY quiet. We weren't there long enough to enjoy the amenities...but the pool looked nice...impeccably groomed grounds, and meticulously CLEAN!

name: Arizona Grand Resort & Spa
title: “Amazing resort”
text: This is a fantastic resort for families. Oasis water park is a trip of a lifetime for the kids and adults. The pictures don't do it justice. Lazy river and tide pool were great fun for kids and adults. Poolside food and drinks were great. We will definitely be back. Rooms nice and spacious.

name: Philadelphia Marriott Downtown
title: “Labyrinth oder Hotel?”
text: Das Marriott im Zentrum von Philadelphia fällt in erster Linie durch seine Dimensionen auf: Ohne eine ortskundige Person kann man sich ohne Probleme in dem riesigen Gebäude verlaufen. Gänge und Brücken über Straßen in andere Gebäude gehören ebenso zum Repertoire des Hotellabyrinths wie riesige Hallen und verwinkelte Flure. Ansonsten ist das Marriott unspektakulär: es entspricht dem amerikanischen Hotelstandard und kann ihn in ein paar Disziplinen übertreffen: die Zimmer sind geräumig (aber recht dunkel )und die Sauberkeit war zumindest in meinem Zimmer absolut in Ordnung.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “Luscious room, fantastic view, top standard accommodation by any standards.”
text:
Luscious room, fantastic view, top standard accommodation by any standards. I'm not entirely sure what the price is for other rooms, but I paid $499 for a Deluxe room - one night. Admittedly, it was slightly more than I would usually be willing to pay for something I couldn’t take home to look at, (bar a flight of course) but if I were to do it all again, I wouldn’t hesitate to pay the bill twice. (ok, maybe not twice, cos that would be silly)
The lobby area boats a Grand Piano, swanky drinks bar and some classy music to put any traveller at instant rest. If someone were to be blindfolded and taken inside, I would say the victim could quite easily mistake the location for a gentleman’s club before guessing it was a Hotel lobby. But then, I’ve never been to a gentleman’s club so I could be talking utter rubbish here too. Moving on....
Location
Right in the centre of Manhattan, you cant go wrong with this work of art that is a hotel. A few seconds walk to the nearest tube station, (or subway as they like to call it in The US, not sure why cos I don’t remember seeing a sandwich menu anywhere – beside the point) and a wealth of taxis to be hailed right from the hotel door step. 
Room
The room was very spacious, although it was comprised of a bedroom, mini hall, bathroom and living area. Top athletes would find space to practice in this place. I always request the room to be as high as possible for the view. In this case, I wasn’t disappointed. Everything I had dreamt a New York Hotel View should be, is what it was. Lush complimentary bathrobes are available for use within the room – as is an umbrella. (You would have to purchase them if you desired to take them out. Yes, even the umbrella)
Bathroom
Bathroom was again, spacious, clean and very comfortable to be in. I could see how people may have trouble using the toilet in fear of spoiling the ambient purity of the room.
Pros:-
Free internet is available. If you don’t have your own computer, facilities are provided.
Close to many forms of public transport.
Helpful polite staff.
Just being in the hotel has a way of making you feel special! 
Cons:-
Not for you if you wont be spending much time in the room. Better off getting somewhere cheaper.

name: Pacific Terrace Hotel
title: “Fantastic”
text:
This hotel is fantastic. On arrival we where greeted by friendly, efficient staff; including a very helpful concierge desk. The rooms were exceptionally clean and all had full or partial ocean views. Rooms were fully equipped with Ipod docking station (nice touch), large LCD TV, safe, separate sink from the bathroom to make dressing easier and clean comfortable beds. Large bathrooms, with an abundance of clean fluffy towels and toiletries made for a comfortable start to the day. Fresh fruit and water were left in the room each day and there was a fully loaded mini-bar, if needed.
They offer free wine by the pool for one hour each day (mid-afternoon), which is a great opportunity to meet your fellow guests. The small pool is clean, with sun loungers available and the view overlooking the Pacific Ocean is gorgeous.
Would not hesitate to return if in San Diego. Top tip: Take the tram (train) to the border for a day and visit Mexico. The journey is only 40 mins and the trains are very frequent.

name: The Westin Riverwalk
title: “Wonderful location! Phenomenal service! Highly recommend!!”
text:
My husband and I drove in from Austin for a quick 1-night anniversary stay. The location is awesome - SO close to all the Riverwalk excitement but also quiet. You can walk anywhere! The pool is a bit small if you plan on swimming the whole time, but we certainly didn't! There is SO much to do in the area. The rooms and restaurant are beautiful. 
The in and out valet service is prompt and absolutely worth every penny! I sort of bawked at the $30/day fee but all parking down there is pricey and it is really convenient!! We went out at midnight to drive over to Mi Tierra at the market for some pastries and we were back in 10 minutes :). The valets are so professional and kind.
I want to commend everyone at Westin Riverwalk, especially Doreen Patino who is director of group sales. We chatted with her at the concierge desk about dinner options. After learning why we were there, she gave me her card and said to let her know if we needed anything. Later that night, we got back to our hotel to find an anniversary card and bottle of champagne! The hotel was already perfect, and this was the icing on the cake! 
Anyone wanting a beautiful place to stay right on the Riverwalk - this is your place!

name: Hilton Garden Inn Phoenix Airport North
title: “Great location, nice staff”
text:
This newer property is clean and extremely close to the airport. Staff was friendly and courteous. Free shuttle to/from Skyharbor that leaves on the top and bottom of the hour. 
Rooms were very nice. Well appointed, comfortable. There is an onsite restaurant but nothing else nearby which is the only downside.

name: Pacific Terrace Hotel
title: “Rave reviews were true!”
text: My husband and I met old friends at the Pacific Terrace for a week end get-a-way. Trip Advisor has worked well for me in the past, so I used it to research a beach hotel in the San Diego area. Most of the reviews I read about the Pacific Terrace before going there seemed too good to be true. I almost chose Trip Advisor's number two recommendation because I coud not believe so many positive reviews were possible. I am glad I did not choose number two, but stayed with number one! From our first encounter at the front desk until checking out of the hotel, everything was wonderful. All of the staff were extremely courteous and helpful. The decor was exceptional with attention to detail. Rooms were spotless and nice size with lot of extras like the Ipod docking station at the bedside. Beds were so comfy. Icing on the cake (or rather cookies) was the added touch of fresh cookies at the front desk and a complimentary wine hour from 4 to 5 pm. We were right on the ocean and the view was spectacular. We took long walks along the beach and enjoyed the local shops and restaurants. Our only regret is that we could not stay longer. We will definately go back to this first class establishment.

name: Marriott's Canyon Villas
title: “Marriott knows luxury”
text: Our second stay at the Marriott Canyon Villas did not disappoint. The staff is excellent. The accommodations are superb. The "quiet" pool was great. The room was spacious, two bedroom, wonderful beds, quiet, great kitchen. The workout facility is good. The pools, waterfalls, etc. are very nice. Landscaping is awesome. Even the drinks are great. This is the place to come in the desert if you want to get away from it all and bake in the sun.

name: Homewood Suites Phoenix North - Happy Valley
title: “Exceptional service”
text: My friends and I stayed here for a week (3 suites), and we were all extremely pleased with the hotel. We got a great deal on it through Priceline, so that made it even better. It had wonderfully comfortable beds, very clean rooms that were large enough for all 6 of us to sit together in the living room, and a nice pool/hot tub area with a basketball court. Probably what we appreciated most was the weekday evening meals (beer and wine included) in addition to hot breakfasts. The meals saved us a lot of money, and it was nice to not have to leave the hotel and search for a place to eat every night. I won't say the meals were fantastic, but they were good enough. They did tend to run out of the beer while they were still serving food, so you should get there pretty early if you want a beer. I saw some people asking for beer after they ran out, and some was brought to them. The thing that really impressed me was the service. One of the people who worked in the dining area (his name was Angel, I believe), provided customer service you rarely see. He worked hard and fast to keep up with all the people, and he did so with courtesy and a smile. I think we each commented on him at various points because he was so attentive. Everyone was very friendly and helpful. I had one minimal maintenance issue which was handled immediately by a pleasant man who assured me he would come right back if I had any further issues. This hotel was a big part of why I left thinking that Happy Valley was appropriately named. It seemed like a very happy place, and I was glad to have spent my week here. Also, it's in a great area for shopping, and there's a movie theater nearby. But be forewarned - neither my TomTom nor Google Maps on my Blackberry could find this place and I had to call them to get directions.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Phoenix Biltmore
title: “nice chain hotel”
text: Stayed at this hotel while in town for SHPE{ society of hispanic professional engineers}.great location,next to a great mall with several restaurants nearby. Clean and well kept. 2 mildly annoying problems. The air sytem in the hotel is either off or on.At the time we stayed there it was off. Unless you opened the sliding door you had no air circulating in your room. We were on the top floor so we did just that, but for those on the ground floor that wasn't an option as that would be unsafe. I prefer that the rooms have individual control,again a minor thing. The front desk had no knowledge of other places in the immediate area for shopping, spa services etc. I think that this is something that could be easily remedied. Over all it was a pleasant stay.

name: Holiday Inn Hotel & Suites Phoenix Airport
title: “Would stay again”
text:
Only stayed one night on our way on to somewhere else. 
Swift check-in, excellent comfortable room with comfy beds. Good bathroom and plenty of towels. Nice and quiet which was really appreciated after a long flight from the UK. The restaurant was quite small but the service was good. On checking in we were given a voucher for a free drink, but it was only for 1 drink, not 1 drink EACH! The bar was small and pokey with sport on the TV quite loud - didn't bother with that.
The shuttle bus picked us up from the airport okay and took us to the car rental place the following day (they don't normally, but the driver took us as it was quiet).

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Phoenix Chandler
title: “Very noisy”
text: Spent three nights at the La Quinta Inn and Suites in Chandler, AZ. It is very close to the highway and my room was on the side facing the highway so I heard vehicle noise all night long. The other side might be quieter but I didn't not check that out.. I did not have the free breakfast but it looked like the typical complimentary fare. The staff was very nice, rooms were clean but dated. I would not stay again but only because of the noise.

name: The Ritz-Carlton Phoenix
title: “Truly a home away from home!”
text: The Ritz in Phoenix is one of the best hotels I've experienced. The staff is gracious and always willing to help. The hotel itself is beautiful and so well cared for.

name: Country Inn & Suites Deer Valley
title: “Beware of the security of your credit card information”
text:
The owners of this property also own a Hilton Garden Inn in Avondale. We had a reservation at the Hilton that we cancelled in writing as the hotel was months behind in opening and not responsive or able to ensure that we would have a place to stay when we arrived.
Apparently, this property took it upon itself, without our permission or knowledge to use our info from the Hilton Garden Inn to book a reservation at their hotel. When I responded to their confirmation and requested that it be cancelled, I was met with silence.
I can understand a delay in opening, but why this property would choose to violate my privacy as well as their merchant agreement with American Express is beyond me.
Why would they presume that it was reasonable for us to stay over 20 miles away from where we needed to be?
72 hours before a two week business trip, I had to place a fraud alert on my Amex to protect myself.
If there was a plan B for those of us with reservations, some clear communication would have resolved this entire issue. Instead, I received an email from the Country Inn threatening me with a penalty if I do not cancel my reservation 24 hours before I arrive. What if I had already left home and did not see the email in time?
When I called the Country Inn and Suites toll free number, the agent indicated that she would begin an investigation - I can only hope so.

name: Americas Best Value Inn - Downtown Phoenix
title: “good deal”
text:
This hotel was a good price compared to others in the area. It was about a 15 minute walk to the convention center and other downtown attractions. 
Good things: the decor is modern and recently updated, flat screen tv, bathtub, microwave and fridge, and helpful staff. Its really close to a GREAT Italian restaurant called Cibo. 
Bad things: not close to any convenience or grocery stores, continental breakfast consists of gas station type pastries and coffee. It is in a slightly sketchy location but i felt safe 85% of the time. 
Take a walk to the Arizona Center and go to the Corner Bakery if you want an awesome affordable breakfast.
Overall, i would recommend this hotel for an affordable vacation or business trip.

name: The Westin Riverwalk
title: “Great Hotel”
text: I stayed at The Westin for my birthday. When we checked in the front desk associate provided the best customer service that I have had at a hotel and I regularly travel for business. She provided an upgrade to a suite because it was my birthday. The suite was wonderful. Very clean, the bed was comfortable. We went out to dinner for my birthday and when we arrived back there was a bottle of champagne, chocolates and a handwritten birthday card! The whole hotel experience really made my birthday special! Thank you Racheal!!!!!!!

name: Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak Resort
title: “Great family hotel!”
text: Best hotel bed we have ever slept in!! Great pool for the kids. The weather was a little cool but the pool was heated so we were still able to swim in the afternoon. Plenty of room in the suite. Very nice staff. Provided a refrigerator at no charge and brought to the room very quickly. Also printed boarding passes the morning we were leaving. I think they may have been renovating the kitchen so food service was a little limited but concierge was able to provide detailed local restaurant information. Close to the airport. Free shuttle service available to sister resort at Tapatio Cliffs but that pool is a more adult oriented pool so we didn't stay long at that resort. Would definitely stay again!

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “Wonderful vacation!”
text: This hotel met all expectations and did not dissapoint in any way

name: Pacific Terrace Hotel
title: “Good and Bad”
text:
We recently went to San Diego with some friends for spring break. My husband and I are used to staying in La Jolla. Since our friends were staying at Pacific Terrace we decided to do the same. I had read a review before we went that said "don't stay on the left hand side of the hote"l. When offered an upgraded room on the left hand side we took it thinking, well the review was probably exaggerated. No way! We were up all night one night to the sounds of a screaming bum. Right out to the left of the hotel is a public beach restroom, and small parking area for beach goers. The rest room is active all night long. 
After that being said the hotel it self is very nice. It was recently remodeled. We had an awesome tv, bed, bathroom. The pool was great. You can order food from local restaurants at the pool. The free breakfast in the morning was great. I think the hotel experience would have been excellent had we not have stayed on the left side and had gone for a middle room.

name: Arizona Grand Resort & Spa
title: “My 8 year old daughter and myself had the best end of summer trip ever.”
text: We had so much fun that we were sleeping by 9:00 at the latest every evening. Then we were up early each morning waiting for the Oasis to open. My wife was very jealous that she couldn't make the trip. Our photos and how our daughter won't stop talking about it has "mom" very upset that she couldn't get off work. Next time. Thank you AGR.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Phoenix Airport North
title: “Big Rooms, It's a good place”
text:
First thing you will notice is that it's larger than most HGIs. Very clean, large restaraunt with a good menu. Business center has everything and fitness center is very good. Pool is right next to the road and small.
The staff seems 1/2 asleep. They are polite, helpful - just - sleepy and not very professional.
If you are coming here for business, it will be just fine.
If you are travelling with family and won't be in the hotel for an extended period of time, I recommend it.
*You will need to call and schedule the hotel shuttle in advance.
If you are a VPN user, the wi-fi disconnects constantly and it's a bit frustrating.

name: Marriott's Canyon Villas
title: “Great place, considering the Rattlers In Residence”
text: Stayed here twice on pleasure in August (don't get me started) and loved it. Great conjoining pools with a basketball/volleyball set-up, and the essential pool bar to amuse the grown-ups. Upon arrival I joked with the clerk about needing a high floor to avoid the snakes, and she apologetically noted they only had a first floor unit available, then reassured me with "Don't worry, just keep your door closed - we ARE in the desert you know - but usually you'll hear them rattling if they're out there. Still, only scorpions have actually gone into the rooms as far as I know." Note to self: High floor please! We liked this more than the busier JW across the street with its famous "Lazy River" pool -- think lots of jammed in chubby tourists floating down a drain. Not my style, but some love it.

name: Arizona Grand Resort & Spa
title: “Great girls get-away”
text: We had a wonderful 3 day weekend! We checked in on the 28th of May for a Girls Weekend Get-Away. The staff was outstanding and the room was gorgeous. I usually have a hard time sleeping in hotel beds but this one was out of this world. It was so comfortable. The Oasis Waterpark was very relaxing and very easily accesable from our room. Thank you for your excellent service and ourstanding accomidations. We will definitely stay here again!

name: Holiday Inn Hotel & Suites Phoenix Airport
title: “Great stay, new branding works well”
text:
Stayed for a Friday night before setting off on a Roadtrip. I needed a place to crash after 18 hours of travel. The shuttle was prompt and the drivers I had were helpful and friendly. Reception was most helpful and the bar staff receptive and attentive.
The rooms were what to be expected of a new hotel. I was given a two room suite with kitchenette, two large LG HD TV's, good coffee facilities and a good sized bathroom. The bed was more than adequate and the decor quite relaxing. 
The shower had great water pressure which as I found later is unusual in some parts of Arizona. I was given a voucher for a drink and a complimentary breakfast which was well provided and set me up for the day after a swim in the pool and ten minutes in the whirlpool.
No complaints at all.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Phoenix Airport North
title: “2 week guest”
text: I stayed at this hotel for two weeks while attending a class in Phoenix. The room was very comfortable. The breakfast was great and the weekend bartender Janessa was very nice and would go out of her way to make things enjoyable for someone far from home. I enjoy a couple drinks in the evening to break up the grind of being on the road. I avoided the bar during my stay during the week because the weeknight bartender seemed to be only interested in a tip and didn't have the customer service skills like the weekend bartender Janessa. This is a great place to stay just eat out during the week.

name: Legacy Golf Resort
title: “Legacy Customer Service is Sub-Standard”
text:
We recently booked a suite at the Legacy Golf Resort in Phoenix and had one of the worst customer service experiences that we have ever experienced during our travels. Upon check-in, the staff appeared to have little time to check in the guests that had arrived. After waiting in line for approximately half an hour, we were told that our room was not ready and there was no clear indication given when it would be ready. Upon further inquiry, including a request to speak to the management, we were finally given a room number and told that we could check in when house-keeping was finished cleaning the room. The reason given for the delay was that the previous guests had checked out late and the Resort had no control over this. However, as we approached our suite, we noticed that several of the other suites were still in the process of being cleaned, leading us to believe that the Resort was under-staffed. 
 One of the points made by management while we were booking the suite was the fact that we would love the room and it was worth the wait because we would have a wonderful view of the mountains / golf course from our upper balcony. When we were finally able to occupy the room, we stepped onto the balcony and had a wonderful view....of two Large Eucalyptus trees...which totally blocked any other view. 
 We have booked suites at this resort several times in the past and are very reluctant to do so in the future because of the poor customer service.

name: Pacific Terrace Hotel
title: “wonderful experience”
text:
My husband, 19 year old son and I stayed at the Pacific Terrace last Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights. We loved this hotel. Every staff member that we dealt with was extremely friendly. 
We had made a reservation for a junior suite. The room was not ready when we arrived after 1:00 p.m. We asked about other rooms that might be available and they were happy to show us several rooms to choose from. We ended up taking a room on the first floor. It was more a pool view than an ocean view, but we had a nice patio that seemed private even though it opened up to the pool area. It was Room 117 and was close to the breakfast room but away from the pool traffic.
The room was large and clean. The sink and vanity area is outside the bathroom. There is a very large mirror as well as a magnifying mirror and tons of room for makeup, etc. The robes were nice.
The only thing I felt was not quite up to par was the bedding. It was nothing special and there were only 2 pillows on each queen bed. They were happy to get us 2 more pillows when we asked.
We had spent the two previous nights at the Estancia La Jolla. That is a nice hotel in a beautiful area, but we liked the Pacific Terrace better.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Phoenix Airport North
title: “New Facility, Great Stay”
text: Stayed here the night before an early morning flight out of Phoenix. This hotel appears to be new; all amenities are very up-to-date. Beautiful room. Spent Happy Hour in the hotel bar; it had specials on appetizers and the beer was very cold! Only five minutes to the hotel by its shuttle. Not much in the area near the hotel. If you don't have a car, plan to eat in the hotel restaurant - nothing really near by. We will stay at this facility again when in Phoenix and need to be near the airport.

name: Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs Resort
title: “Too expensive with lots of hidden costs”
text: The hotel was nice, clean and spacious rooms. the Point in Thyme restaurant and service was fantastic. However, I would never go back to this hotel. From the minute you got to the hotel there was hands out for tips and lots of extra costs. A staff took bags from car at door to the front desk - about 30 ft and then clearly wanted a tip. Then another staff took bags in elevator and then clearly wanted a tip and were not afraid to stay, wait and stare until they got it. Then when we wanted to get a cab to the local shopping area they flag down a huge tahoe and it cost us $25 even though they told us $23.00 flat rate. Driver kept complaining about having to spend money on his tires and conveniently only had change that would guarantee a large tip. Coming back to the mall we called a local cab company for the cost of $14.00. I am sure the hotel is trying to give class A service but they should offer more affordable services. The cascades falls said it was open for dinner - however closes at 5:00 pm - went for a drink and appetizers at 4:30 but they would not server food, made a drink which you had to walk up to bar and order and take back to table - yet they had the hand out for the tip. they closed the bar at 4:25. The hotel was not easy to get around and was way to spread out. The internet wifi (which should be inlcuded for $150.00/night) was available for $12.00/day - that is ridiculous and not customer service - just another way to get more money out of the customer. I would never stay here again just for the principle of all the hidden costs. Also - if you wanted to use the gym - you could also do that for $10.00 day. So I was left to ask - what does the $150.00 include?

name: The Westin Riverwalk
title: “High Class, so what....”
text:
As many of my posts, you can take 'em or leave 'em each of us has our own take on things. I see no reason this post to be any different and if high class and respect is what you want then "The Westin Riverwalk" is for you. It has to be to get away with charging as much as 400 plus dollars a night.
As they say; "location location location" and the Westin has that. It is located in a perfect spot in downtown San Antonio good luck finding the driveway on your first pass (hint: it's on the right hand side of the one way street, although you're turning left from another one way street). The valet parking is nice, staff very respectful of your vehicle and of you. Those guys treat you like royalty and in fact everyone does to some point. Be warned, parking is $30.00 per day which is crazy. You can use the parking garage across the street, they do.
Front doormen are quick to help you with a smile and an old fashion tip of the hat. Jose is the best, friendly knowledgeable quick to help you even with dumpiest tourist questions. The front desk staff was equally good, one particular employee (Forrest?) was funny and customer service dedicated even though he was called in on his day off and there were computer issues.
Restaurant, well find somewhere else. I cannot say anything nice about this experience, first impression was expensive and fancy but an unsupervised screaming kids and a very active tiny bar made the experience worthless. You have to walk through the bar to get to the restaurant, the bar was designed to be elegant but was more like a sports bar.
In the end, all I can say is do not rely on staff for a common local non tourist trap places to eat, they will always recommend the very expensive riverwalk restaurants. I cannot count how many employees I stopped and ask; "Can you recommend a local, "travel channel" type place place to get a real Texas style steak/potato dinner?" I even jokingly referred to myself was "white trash, trailer" prices. They still could not help me.
I do not recommend this hotel but only because of pricing verses the setting. I figure you cannot have it both ways. A hotel with high class prices in the middle of a common/tourist area does not always work and can be misleading to some less traveled. Try it and experience it for yourself.

name: Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs Resort
title: “Nice getaway weekend”
text:
My wife and I spent two nights here and really enjoyed it. The hotel is not perfect, but for the rate ($170 a night, including $50 resort voucher) I was happy with it. 
Pros: VERY comfortable bed, great pools and hot tubs (8+ to choose from), beautiful landscaping, ample free parking, quiet rooms, nearby hiking trail, tennis courts, exercise center
Cons: room had some flaws - broken drawer on a dresser, banged up trim in the bathroom, but nothing major. Coupons for breakfast were not delivered to my room until the night before check out, but staff had already cheerfully provided replacements. To reach the parking areas, we had to navigate narrow roadways, which could have been a challenge if we had a larger car
This is a huge, sprawling property, but there are shuttles and everything seems to be within a short walk.

name: Arizona Biltmore
title: “Great choice for family vacation”
text: Great choice for family vacation with grown children, but probably great with younger children too. The all inclusive Octilla is well worth it. The food was excellent and the head chef was very attentive to our daughter's food allergies. He called multiple times to check on things and visited our table regularly as well. The facility is gorgeous, and is a classic built in the 30's but entirely updated and perfectly maintained. There are lots of available activities on site as well as in the area. And it is within driving distance of the Grand Canyon, which is obviously amazing.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “Great location, friendly service”
text:
We had a wonderful stay at Hotel Giraffe. We stayed in the King suite and it met all our expectations. The rooms were big (for NYC) and always clean. The staff was friendly and unobtrusive. The nightly receptions were well-stocked and much better than I've encountered at other hotels. The morning breakfast was also well-stocked and low-key. Plenty of papers and spots for everyone.
The location is great, it's about 15 minutes by cab to Broadway and Time's Square. You can walk to the Flatiron Building and Madison Square Park. A one block walk allows you great views of the Chrysler Building and the Empire State Building and if you fancy a longer walk, you could go there as well.
Also walking distance to the Gramercy Tavern if you want a swanky night out and possible celebrity sighting as well as the dependable Les Halles for steak frites.
It's fair money for what you get and you can get good prepaid packages on the web site. I definitely recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “So comfortable and accomodating in a lovely part of NY!”
text: We enjoyed a lovely weekend at the Hotel Giraffe. It's convenient to many nice places to eat, the room was very comfortable, the staff so accomodating and the amenities in the lobby and the terrace were wonderful. We will definitely return.

name: Arizona Biltmore
title: “Fantastic event experience”
text:
My work hosted an event at the Biltmore and the staff and hotel went above and beyond not only to make sure that my company had what it needed to make the event successful but to make sure that the guests who attended the event, had a pleasant, enjoyable and memorable experience. 
This is why we have continued to host our events at the Biltmore for the past 6 years and will continue to into the future!

name: Pacific Terrace Hotel
title: “cock coach”
text: It was the most horrible hotel that i have ever stayed in. Iv'e stayed at nicer motel 6's. Their were cock roaches all over our room, when we asked if we could get a new room they said that it would be fine and not to worry about it. For your own saftey i would advise you not to stay here.

name: Americas Best Value Inn - Downtown Phoenix
title: “Outstanding Hotel Superb Value, Great Location”
text: The owners in my mind deserve entrepreneur of the year awards for Phoenix. They have taken a hotel and turned it into a retreat. Each room has been remolded, granite counter tops, tile showers, pillow top beds, premium hd flat screen tvs, it is on a par with a Hyatt Place. All while being half the price of any hotel in phoenix. I stay in 100 hotel rooms a year and this was top 5. Amazing! Congrats to the owners.

name: Marriott's Canyon Villas
title: “Canyon Villas Is Awesome”
text:
This property was wonderful. We booked here for 3 nights on short notice because the JW Marriott Desert Ridge was booked. Our villa was beautiful and spacious. Just what we needed at the end of an 11 day vacation in Arizona. We used the shuttle to the JW each day and enjoyed two fantastic days at the pools there. Our 9 year old loved it and we all hated to leave. Lunch by the pool each day was top notch. With access to all the services, restaurants at the JW plus a gorgeous full size condo, we were in heaven. Cocktails with live music outside on the patio was perfect before dinner at Roy's. Who cares if it is 112 degrees? 
We stayed at the Fairmont Princess for 4 days at the beginning of our vacation before going to Sedona and Grand Canyon. The Princess was great, but a different experience. We actually liked Canyon Villas/JW Marriott Desert Ridge better. Can't wait to go back!

name: Hampton Inn Phoenix/Anthem
title: “Really wonderful hotel!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel last weekend with my daughter's softball team. I had called ahead and reserved a group rate with Sarah. I told her that our team was heading up for some scrimmage games in Anthem. When we arrived, we were delightfully surprised to find in our rooms a welcome letter with our team logo and best wishes for a fun time at our scrimmages. There was also a goody bag that the girls really enjoyed. Our team name was posted with best wishes near the front desk. Some of our team has traveled with softball for years and never received this type of welcome at a hotel. It was a very thoughtful gesture that made our girls feel special. 
Our rooms were huge and clean, beds were comfortable, and the breakfast was perfect. All the staff was very friendly. The girls really enjoyed the pool, too. There was lots of shopping nearby and a Denny's and Del Taco in the same parking lot- very convenient!
We really enjoyed our stay and will stay at Hampton Inn Anthem if we ever find ourselves that way again.

name: Americas Best Value Inn - Downtown Phoenix
title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: Well, I'm from Tucson and I was at a concert at the US Airways Center. I needed a place to stay, so I looked into hotels in the area. I had a co-worker tell me that Van Buren was a horrible place to stay, very dangerous. I saw the prices and read the reviews, and I could see that the ownership must have changed. I thought, sure I'll give this hotel a try. Sure enough, it was a great place to stay, the rooms were very clean, there was even a piece of paper around the toilet seat that said it had been sanitized for your protection. Don't hesitate staying here, I would definitely stay here again. The staff was very friendly and accommodating, answered all of my questions and knowledgeable about the area.

name: Westin Phoenix Downtown
title: “Wonderful Staycation getaway!”
text:
To celebrate our recent engagement, we decided on a little getaway. As Phoenix locals, we had our pick of wonderful resort properties to choose from. We were not into hanging at the pool in 110 degree heat! We wanted a cool, modern hotel and the Westin did not disappoint. We chose the Westin Downtown based on its proximity to the Diamondbacks ballpark and also because having stayed at a Westin in the past I knew the Heavenly Beds would be amazingly comfortable. From the moment we checked in, it was a wonderful experience! My fiance mentioned at the front desk our recent engagement and it was nice to be congratulated. After a nice walk to the ballpark to enjoy the DBacks game, we returned to our 18th floor room just in time to see the Friday night fireworks over the ballpark through our floor to ceiling windows! And a very thoughtful and wonderful touch was a sticky note on our minifridge pointing to a wonderful cheese and fruit board left for us in the fridge along with a bottle of wine and a note from the staff congratulating us once again on our engagement! It was very sweet and a much appreciated late night snack. 
The room was beautifully decorated with a modern yet warm look. The view was incredible. The bathroom was huge and spa-like, and, of course, the bed was just as I expected at a Westin-amazingly comfortable. We had arranged for a late checkout until 4pm. It was so relaxing and just what we needed. 
We appreciated so much the thoughtfulness of the staff. We will definitely come back to stay when we are in need of another getaway. I highly recommend the Westin to folks from out of town but also to locals.

name: Marriott's Canyon Villas
title: “Good stay - but overpriced”
text: We stayed at the Canyon Villas for three nights during the last week of March. I had a conference at the J.W. Marriott and was unable to get a room at the hotel, but this location was very convenient to the hotel. There were shuttles to and from the hotel every 30 minutes, but it was a relatively easy 10 minute walk, if you didn't want to wait for the shuttle. The property itself was very nice, surrounded by a golf course. We didn't use the pool. The property is just a 2 minute drive from the Desert Ridge shopping center, which is an outdoor mall with tons of shops and restaurants. Our room was nice, but somewhat smaller than expected. Counter space around the bathroom sink could have been much larger. For $350/night, I was expecting more. We did have a small kitchenette, with a microwave, sink, toaster, fridge, and coffeemaker, along with plates, utensils, etc. This was quite useful. Overall, a decent place, but expensive - I wouldn't have paid more than $250, but my company was footing the bill.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “Perfect Wedding Stay”
text: Recently stayed at the hotel 4 days for our daughter's wedding in the city. The accomodations were absolutely incredible! the service was outstanding, suite was perfect and the roof top bars were absolutely amazing. The new couple live in NYC so I know we will back for a visit and I will under NO circumstances stay at any other hotel. Your staff is amazing, the BEST in the city. Thank you so much for making our stay so incredibly wonderful!! Cindy Butrico Palm Harbor, Florida

name: Sheraton Crescent Hotel
title: “Solid, enjoyable business hotel”
text: Nice, big rooms, big open architecture and a fantastic gym. I didn't try the restaurant or explore much of the grounds. They have a large, on site separate building for events but I did not visit it. The rooms were clean and well kept. They are not ultra modern, but the relative age of the hotel means you get a much bigger room than newer facilities.

name: Marriott's Canyon Villas
title: “glad we bought here”
text:
We had our first arizona holiday last year when we enjoyed two stays at the desert ridge hotel (two weeks and then a short break of four days). During this time we viewed the timeshare villas at canyon villas and purchased a two bed two week package.
We used the accommodation this summer for the first time. We totally loved the experience! The villas are roomy and very well equipped. My son and his girl friend had the lock off portion of the villa and my husband and two other children shared the one bed portion. We had ample space to spread out - with three rooms, two balconies, two bathrooms and three televisions. The kitchen was very well appointed and I enjoyed cooking in the open-plan living/dining room. Cooking for ourselves on the barbecues or in the villa gave us the opportunity to try the excellent meat and fish available at Albertsons (in the desert ridge mall).
