The villas are low rise (three floors) so the views over the deserts are not as good as from the higher floors in the hotel next door. We had a top floor villa in the 2800 block. We heard nothing from neighbours - although I was alerted to the possibility in an earlier post. We really heard nothing from anyone - in two weeks!!! I understand that there are blocks that are better suited to people with young children - additional small pools and squirting fountains - perhaps that is why the part of the complex we stayed in was so quiet.
The only problem that we encountered during our stay was when we were checking in - the room was not ready until nearly five o'clock - just our luck to check in on a Saturday - but the day before we checked in and during the time I was waiting for our room many people were able to access our room - perhaps it was because of the time it takes to clean a two bed villa as opposed to a one bed or studio apartment. Anyway, we were given a $20 credit to have a drink in the bar whilst the room was finished off. 
Matt was pleasant - as has previously been stated. The pool areas were rarely crowded and I must admit we used them most days and did not venture to the desert ridge hotel more than once (I had previously stayed there with my son for two weeks waiting for the rest of my family to join us).
My boys prefered the layout of the villas pools and there was always the opportunity for us to get six sunbeds together.
We tried the hot hot hot tubs on a couple of occasions - quite pleasant in the relative cool of evening - but scorchio during the day - who wants a hot bath when the temperature is 105 degrees?
We will definitely be returning to the canyon villas next summer and are pleased that we made the decision to become owners here - although we do recognise that in July and August the published rates for the villas are exceptional value.

name: Pacific Terrace Hotel
title: “Top Hotel”
text:
Ein kleines, aber sehr feines Hotel, direkt am Strand.
Service war perfekt und sehr bemüht dem Reisegast, alle Wünsche von den Lippen abzulesen. (Es steht Limonade und Tee in den Gängen zur freien Verfügung)
Das Hotel ist im Hawaii-Stil eingerichtet, das Bett ist etwas höher, hat aber eine Treppe, falls man es braucht. Der Balkon hat auch in der Seitenzimmern Meerblick und sind etwas billiger.
In diesem zufällig gebuchten Hotel, werde ich auf jedenfall nochmal einige Tage Urlaub verbringen.

name: Marriott's Canyon Villas
title: “Great Property”
text:
We recently returned from a week long vacation at the Canyon Villas at Desert Ridge. 
We have been to some very nice Time Shares before as well as some very upscale hotels. This property offers the best of both worlds.
We stayed in a 2 bedroom Villa which could actually sleep 8. There were 6 of us and we had plenty of room. The bedrooms were very spacious and the kitchen, living room, and dining room area were very modern and very spacious. The property isn't huge right now but they are building more units. The pool was very nice with a waterfall and a pool bar/restaurant. The menu wasn't the largest I have seen, but because we had a full kitchen in our Villa, we were able to have lunch in our Villa if we wanted. The staff was very friendly and Matt, the Food and Beverage Manager (he also bartends on the weekends) is one of the nicest guys you will ever meet. 
We spent most of the time at the pool at the Villas but we did go over to the hotel a couple of times. A shuttle runs every half hour and it takes you across the street to the JWMarriott Desert Ridge. This is a large but beautiful 5 star hotel. They have 3 pools including a lazy river pool. The service at the pool at the hotel is also great. They are always around to get you drinks or food. Another nice touch is that they bring you pitchers of water all the time to keep you hydrated. This is important when it is over 100 degrees. 
Although the property is a little further out than some of the properties off of Scottsdale Rd., it was a 5 -10 minute drive to get to any restaurant or golf course that you would want. We went into Old Scottsdale for dinner and it was about a 10 minute drive. 
The Desert Ridge Shopping Center is also right across the street from the property and they have 10-15 restaurants, a Supermarket, and all kinds of stores. We ate dinner there three times and could have eaten there every night. Within 5 minutes of the property, you can find a great steak restaurant that rivals any one in New York, great Italian food, other restaurants like Roys which is at the hotel. You can also find any type of Chain restaurant like Bahama Breeze or Cheesecake Factory or P.F. Changs.

name: Hotel Palomar Phoenix - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “I'll be back!!!”
text: We came down for only 1 night to catch a baseball game at Chase Field. Couldn't have had a better time. The friendly staff was great from check in to check out. I only ate breakfast at the restaurant, and it was wonderful. The pool area is unbelievable - Roof top with bar and plenty of room to enjoy the sun or shade to hide from it. I am definitely coming back.

name: Radisson Hotel Phoenix Airport
title: “A Great Stay during April 2012”
text:
The Hotel looks great from the outside - we saw the flowering Cactii in the parking area too. The interior of the Hotel was no disappointment and the staff were wonderful. 
The stay was short but we felt relaxed straight away and the reception staff were pleasant and helpful. Breakfast was good and our waitress Kris was cheerful and helped our day get off to a great start.
We enjoyed our stay and would definitely come back again. Based right near the airport, the shuttle service was easy to use and there would be no reason to go anywhere else.
Ohh - and yes - the bed was really comfy too!
Thanks again!

name: Omni Dallas Hotel at Park West
title: “Great, classy stay in Dallas!”
text: I am an Omni fan and have visited many Omni's...this one was beautiful!! I truly enjoyed my stay while in town on a business trip. You can tell the quality as you pull up and walk in to the foyer. It smelled nice and clean (smell is always a sense that is on high-alert!). The lobby was decorated eloquently and the front desk staff was veyr welcoming and helpful! We had dinner in the restaraunt which was delicous! The chef also sent us out something to sample, very nice! The room was very spacious and modern. I had a great night's sleep! Overall, I would reccommend ot anyone staying in that area! I will be sure to visit this one again!

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Dallas (Galleria Area)
title: “Great Value! Will stay again if in area”
text: We stayed here 1 night on July 2nd. This location is very close to the American Girl store. Hotel has beautiful finishes, very modern. Front desk was very nice & polite. Our room had a ceiling fan, which was a great bonus!!! The bed was a little stiff but I still slept like a rock. Can't beat the price. & location is great for Galleria area.

name: Westin Phoenix Downtown
title: “Excellent stay in downtown Phoenix.”
text: Our expectations were low, so we were pleasantly surprised by this chic new (opened spring 2011) Westin in downtown Phoenix. It's more "W" than Westin. Decor is modern, Asian-inspired and minimalist. Rooms are huge. The spaces were great to be in especially the restaurant, which had a GREAT menu and good food and prices, but needs help in perfecting the implementation to achieve consistency. Feedback-- (1) Westin needs a COTTON blanket option. Down is too hot for Phoenix and, I, for one, am allergic to it. I want a washable COTTON blanket option. (2) The mattress was uncomfortably hard for me. The pillow top was quite sparse and I needed more cushioning. Otherwise, great hotel and good location.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “Will definately stay again”
text:
I was in NYC for a party and picked this placed based on location. I was pleasantly surprised at how nice it is! They have a wine and cheese reception in the evenings and breakfast in the morning included. Parking was only $38/24 hrs for my huge SUV. (for a reg. sized car it is $28). I lived in NYC for 5 years and have gone back many times since and this is a fantastic value for the city! That is some dirt cheap parking for there.
The staff was also very helpful and courteous. I have stayed in some of the large chain hotels in midtown in the past, but never again! This is my new favorite hotel in NYC.

name: Adolphus Hotel
title: “Awesome Hotel”
text: In town on business and needed a convenient location near the Baylor Medical complex. I was quite busy and didn't really get to enjoy Dallas or the hotel, a really pity. The hotel is a beautifully maintained, stately hotel with tons of charm. The room was spacious and very nicely appointed. The little interaction I had with the staff was most pleasant and professional. Would have loved to stay longer. I need to return and have a fine meal in the hotel's restaurant -- really regretting I didn't make time. If in Dallas, I will definitely stay here and recommend it to all my friends.

name: Sheraton Phoenix Downtown Hotel
title: “Great Stay”
text:
I had a six night stay in the Sheraton and it was awesome. I stayed in the standard king bedroom. In my opinion, compared to other hotels I the room it self was smaller than most but the bathroom was larger than most which made up for it. The bed it self was comfortable and the desk was great work space; although I didn't use the desk for internet ( $15/perday). There is a cyber cafe in the lobby with free internet access. 
I was there on business but I did have a ton of time outside of meetings to check things out. which leads me to location. I was able to walk to the museum, the Suns stadium, Chase field, and Pizzeria Blanco ( a definite must ) all from the hotel. The concierge was great with giving direction for all us directionally challenged folks. The hotel is also in good proximity to public transit if that's your mode of transportation. Additionally, pedal taxi as well as the traditional taxi are easy to flag down. 
The overall customer service was really excellent. I called the front desk 3 times( for a bottle opener, a new light bulb for the lamp, and once for room service )during my stay and every request was met in record time. 
One thing that I found interesting was the going "green" initiative. You can but a placard outside your door that says that housekeeping does not to change change your sheets.As incentive for more people to do that they give $5 voucher to the hotel restaurant. So I could have racked up $30. However, if you put the placard out then housekeeping doesn't come at all. Perhaps they will change the policy. I understand that by not changing the sheets everyday you save energy, water, soap, and eventually labor cost; but I personally would just like to have the bed made and the trash taken away every day. 
Overall a great stay.

name: Radisson Hotel Phoenix Airport
title: “We loved it and will choose Radisson in the future”
text: Stayed here on our last night of vacation due to an early am flight out of Phoenix. What a surprise!!!!!!! The room was great and more than expected but the best part was the hotel staff. They went above and beyond the call of duty to make sure we had an enjoyable stay (including shuttle service to a nearby restaurant for dinner). If this hotel is any indication of the overall corporate culture at Radisson, they have sold me and I will seek out their hotels on future trips.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “Great small hotel on Park South”
text: What a great place to stay. European style breakfast buffet, wine and cheese at 5pm, and warm and friendly staff. This hotel is located near the Murray Hill district, on the south side and is very convienent to the subway (two short blocks) or easy to grab a cab if you choose. I will definatley stay there again. I have stayed at several of the hotels in the area and like this the best!

name: Sheraton Phoenix Downtown Hotel
title: “So So Sheraton”
text:
We have stayed at a number of Sheratons around the world and this is the first one that fell below my expectations. The hotel is next to one of the convention centers and close to a number of the downtown Phoenix attractions. Upon our arrival we had to park in the below ground parking area that was very tight. Parking was at a rate of $17 per night. The parking was well lit and had a safe feeling about it.
The lobby was very large and filled with a number of eclectic seating areas. There was a bar in the lobby that was reasonable in price. Checking in was odd. There are a number of free standing desk areas where the host checks you in. There is also a large column in the center of the check in area and people lined up on both sides. The hostess came around from behind the counter and greeted us. I introduced myself and handed her my Starwood Card, my ID, and a credit card. We were assigned a room with two double beds. I asked for a King sized bed and was told they were all accounted for. ( I am glad none of them were missing.) The hostess failed to meet our request. For the first time in over 30 years, the hostess questioned the person with me and our relationship to each other. I understand having their name in case they get locked out, but that was not the feeling I got. As we turned and walked away, we found security standing behind us. Very odd. We were in town just to watch spring training so jeans, tee shirts, and ball caps were the dress of the day. I assumed that if I was in my business attire my treatment would have been different. 
Our room was very clean and tastefully decorated. It had a small refrigerator in a little outcove with the safe right above it. One bed was very comfortable and the other one was so so. Overall we had a very pleasant sleep. In the morning we spoke with the cleaning staff and they were very polite. We took in the gym and it was very nice. Clean, open, and overlooked the pool. 
At check out, there were two gentlemen at the counter. They saw us in our baseball attire and we talked about the games as well as the economic impact of spring training on the area. 
Hotels come in all kind of levels. This review is based on the same class of hotel. Please take that into consideration when arranging for your lodging. Shop around before booking at this hotel.

name: The Fairmont Dallas
title: “Outstanding stay at Fairmont Dallas”
text: I stayed for a long weekend in order to attend a wedding- the staff couldn't have been nicer. I had a few accommodations from the hotel for my stay, and everything was taken care of with a smile- felt it in the phone conversations!! All the staff was outstanding, housekeeping, the breakfast staff, front desk and concierge and the party staff as well- Nice property- beautiful rooftop pool, deck and herb garden. Austin in reservations and Donna in the gold level- terrific. Good location- near Dealy Plaza, train and trolley. Even the toiletries were paraben-free!! Can't wait to return for another great stay-

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Dallas Addison Galleria
title: “Business Stays”
text: I've been travelling to the Addison area for business for the last four years and have always stayed at the LaQuinta Addison Galleria location. The hotel is excellent and the area has all you need for food and other services.

name: The Westin Galleria Dallas
title: “Westin Wonderland”
text: My wife and I checked into The Dallas Westin after a long, harrowing plane ride and car ride and immediately felt welcomed, relaxed and at home. Check in was easy and pleasant. Our room was inviting and modern, our bed was soft and comfortable, the bathroom was clean and unique with an opaque glass door, a non fog mirror, dual shower heads and plush towels. The only problem we had was leaving.

name: Dallas Marriott Suites Medical/Market Center
title: “Didn't live up to promises”
text:
This hotel was picked for its airport and area shuttle. Upon arrival we asked if our wedding party could reserve the shuttle for our wedding party and we were told no but it should be available. Hours later when we requested the shuttle we were told another wedding group had reserved the shuttle and it would be unavailable, so we had to pay for cabs. This issue was discussed well in advance of our stay and again early in the day of the wedding. 
I requested a room on the Hwy side of the hotel, didn't get it. Our welcome baskets for our out of town guests were not all delivered until I saw them at the front desk the day of the wedding, Guests were all checked in the day before. The hotel did deliver a "romance package of champagne and strawberries" to some of our guests, at 10:30pm at night! 
This hotel has good intentions but the follow through is terrible.
I called the manager the day following check out thinking she needs to know what needs to be addressed in her hotel..... I was ignored!
The room was nice!

name: Luxe Stoneleigh Hotel & Spa
title: “lux in dallas”
text: stayed over weekend. met by friendly valet/ bell hop. front desk cheerful .room spacious and large. decor of hotel beautiful....free coffee in am nice touch. some construction but all in back.. pool in summer would be nice....

name: Hyatt Regency DFW
title: “A new standard for fly-in meetings”
text:
Ok, who would stay at an airport hotel unless they absolutely had to? However the Hyatt Regency almost allows you to forget you are at an airport. 
I've been to two meetings here in the last 12 months. Excellent staff. Very comfortable (and quiet) rooms. Good meeting spaces. Food on the better end of hotel conference provisions. Restaurant of even better quality. 
Of course there are the common irritations of business hotels of this level. Paying for wi-fi (but at least not at highway robbery prices and kudos for allowing guests to connect multiple devices for one subscription price). An underdeveloped fitness center but better than so many. 
And the quirkiest item of all - an attached parking garage that has absolutely NO parking level that is on the same level as the front door. Stairs required. 
But these are really only minor concerns and do not outweigh the quality of the facility and good staff.

name: The Fairmont Dallas
title: “Gold Level suite, well worth it”
text:
This was my first stay at a Fairmont hotel and I will definitely stay with confidence at other Fairmont hotels.
The location of this hotel is great and the service was incredible. A few stand out stars were Austin at the front desk, Tony Bennett at bell services and Johnathan in the Gold level lounge.
We stayed in a regular room the first night. Very spacious room, only complaint was odd, stale odor in restroom. 
Last two nights we booked a suite and happened to get one of the 4 upgraded suites. Great furnishings, room was clean except carpet needed major cleaning. Also, there was a weird cutout that needed to be patched up but I completely overlooked that because the room and view were just divine. 
Gold level lounge was totally worth extra cost. Nice food and drink spread, super comfortable, great furnishings and service made this an amazing perk.
If you go, checkout the terrace level. City views will take your breath away.

name: InterContinental Dallas
title: “Comfortable, Attentive Staff”
text: Room was comfortable, small, but well layed-out with a nice desk, outlets on the lamps for computers and cell phone charging, and the bathroom was roomy with plenty of counter space (exhaust fan would have been nice, though. Water pressure and temp were fine (12th floor)). Restaurant staff was very attentive and even checked with the chef and provided me choices off the dinner menu at lunchtime when I expressed a desire for a steak. Bar was fine and the staff there were helpful. Layout of the lounge area was odd for me, but there was plenty of seating with comfortable chairs. I'd definitely stay there again.

name: Sheraton Suites Market Center
title: “Pretty Nice Stay”
text:
The Shearton Suites at Market Center has clearly undergone some changes.  The lounge dinner was definitely an upgrade from before and the self-serve refrigerator with chilled beverages was a major plus.  The lounge attendant, Abu is always polite, professional, and pleasant.  Thumbs up to him.   I was remiss in not obtaining the name of the front desk staff who assisted me during my stay but they too were very polite, and professional.  I clearly felt they were committed to ensuring their guests full satisfaction satisfaction.  
I did have an issue with my AC, but the maintenance engineer was quick to arrive, assessed the issue, made a correction and took a minute to explain what the issue was.  Thanks!!
The one thing I think the hotel needs would be a signal booster / repeater on the high floors for the WI-FI network.  My signal was borderline useless during the evening hours.
Other than that, an overall good stay.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Dallas Park Central Northeast
title: “Worse than most HI express”
text: The features & exterior look like most Holiday Inn Expresses, but my room was really run-down. The lamp was broken, the carpet the dirtiest I have ever seen, and the bath in need of renovation. On the plus side, it was only $75 and the location was convenient for me. WiFi was free and good.

name: Dallas Marriott Suites Medical/Market Center
title: “Good Location, Good Service”
text:
We stayed for 2 nights with a family of 5, including 3 children. We were attending an event at the American Airlines Center on the weekend and wanted something close by. This is just off the freeway about a mile or so down the road. They have a shuttle to the AA center, but it stops at 10 pm, so any nighttime event will put you taking a cab back. Cab ride was about $12 I think. It's not really a walkable area, but there were a ton of restaurants about 3-5 miles down the road.
The room is more like a "junior suite" with beds and a sitting area that is not really separate. The bathroom is in a corner and opens on two sides. The layout of the room was weird, and didn't really leave you anywhere to open a suitcase, and there was too much furniture to move around in order to open the sofa bed. The rooms were clean, and everything worked. There was a flat screen TV, but no HD programming, so the picture was terrible. We only had 3 towels both days and had to ask for extras, but they arrived promptly. The beds were ok, but not the most comfortable.
We originally booked one night and extended our stay with no problems - the front desk was very good. Our rate included a buffett breakfast, and it was delicious - made to order omelets and waffles, some fruit, cereal, pastries, eggs, biscuits, the works. 
For a good or weekend rate, I would recommend. For their normal weekday rates you could probably find something better at that same price level, though.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Dallas - Campbell Centre
title: “Great deal for a hotel in downtown area of Dallas!”
text:
The entrance is a little tricky off the oneway expressway but once you are there the parking was easy. You are not in downtown but close to highland park village which we liked. Very close to SMU campus also. It was easy to hop on I75 and get where ever you needed to go. This is a high rise hotel which has been updated nicely. Bed linens towels and pillows were first class. 
Only complaint I had was we were given an occupied room at arrival which made me disappointed in a Hilton hotel. The front desk said they were so sorry! 
The buffet breakfast was nice also.

name: Hotel Indigo Dallas Downtown
title: “a terrific hotel”
text: We stayed for two day in January and really liked this hotel. It's bright colours and friendly style and like an antidote to the rest of down town Dallas which is a bit soulless. I travel a lot on business so when I'm on holiday the last thing I want is anything that feels like a business hotel. That's mainly what I loved about the Hotel Indigo -- the rooms were fun, unstuffy and comfortable. The public areas were great too and we spent a happy evening with our drinks sitting on the sofas and using the public internet. Even the breakfast was good. If I'm ever in down town Dallas again I would definitely stay at the Hotel Indigo.

name: Budget Suites of America-Dallas
title: “Decent Place to call home”
text: I have lived at Budget Suites for almost a year. There are a couple of people that look shady, but we are in Dallas after all. I would thin it safe to assume that in any large city shady looking people are all over. The only thing I would like to change is the carpet, it needs help. Security is good and there are no junk cars that we mentioned in other reviews. It is quite around here at night. You get a lot of bang for your buck.

name: Motel 6 - Dallas - Fair Park
title: “Horrible. Save your money and just sleep in the car.”
text:
I went in to inquire if they had any accessible rooms available and the receptionist, told me that the owner does not allow anyone to use the accessible room. He said he has no authority to make decisions on that room and it would get him in trouble. I asked if I could speak to the manager to explain the situation that I needed an accessible room and he said the room he was booking me in would be fine for a wheelchair. He said the rooms were really big. The width of my girlfriend’s wheelchair is 23 inches so it is a pretty small wheelchair. Unfortunately, my girlfriend could not fit through the bathroom door. 
 Therefore, I went back to the front desk to please ask if we could have the accessible room or a refund. The receptionist said he could not change rooms because we had already been inside of room 114. We were in room 114 for maybe three minutes. After telling the receptionist that we either needed an accessible room or a refund he refused both. He got very angry at us. I kept asking politely to speak to the manager in which he refused. Finally, after comments from the receptionist like “I can’t give this room out because disabled people tear it up and the boss does not want anyone staying in it. The last time an elderly man stayed in it he wet the bed.” Later he said, “ok, I’ll call my boss but he’s not going to like this. I mean she is in a wheelchair so technically she does qualify.” He called his boss(but he did not dial any numbers, he just picked up the phone) and said the boss said we could stay in the room but he would have to charge us $5.75 extra. I asked for the phone to talk to the manager but the receptionists refused to let me. I told him that it’s unfair to charge us extra, try to deny us a room, and not give us a refund because my girlfriend is in a wheelchair. He was very angry with me. Since I could not get a refund, which is what I really wanted because of how horrible he made us feel, because we were so tired we paid the extra $5.75. I decided not to press the issue any farther because the receptionist was getting very angry. I never raised my voice. I decided I would call Motel 6’s corporate number. They told me he would forward the complaint on and then they would contact me by mail in 15 days. While on the phone with corporate, Receptionist and another customer got into an intense argument in which the police were called. After the police situation, the receptionists called my room and threatened me by telling me if I called corporate he would deny everything and told me we were lucky he let us stay in the room. Just not good people. Very shady.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Dallas - Campbell Centre
title: “Decent business hotel.”
text: The room was nice, typical for a hotel of this type. Bath could use some sprucing up. Breakfast buffet - the food was lukewarm at best, one morning not even that. Fresh fruit and some frozen, eggs, rolls, potatoes, biscuits & gravy. They had an omelet stand, but not anyone there some mornings. Staff was friendly. Only big negative is that the property is close to the train tracks and Rt 75, you will hear both all night. I think the Westin Park Central is a slightly better hotel for the same money.

name: Quality Inn Dallas Market Center
title: “Quality Memories...”
text:
Memories of our stay at this Quality Inn in April 2006 include:
1) Hearing the room next door getting broken into while we were watching "Dallas SWAT" on TV. It looked like they punched through the glass window to get in. The whole building was not secure. Swipe card access at the rear of the building was broken. On the plus side, the police response seemed quite prompt.
2) Walking through the industrial estate surrounding the hotel to the bus stop, then riding the local bus past the bail bonds offices, establishments of questionable repute, and jail/courthouse to get to the city. 
3) Listening from our room to other guests trapped in the smelly elevator trying to call for help at around midnight.
In short, stay somewhere else!

name: Radisson Hotel Dallas East
title: “Great rooms, not so great area”
text:
As a disclaimer, I didn't end up staying the night here. The sole reason I booked this room was to take advantage of a points promo the Carlson Club is running.
Check-in was nice and quick. The lady behind the counter was very nice. The rooms themselves were much better than expected. They are large, had a decent bathroom, a mini fride, a microwave and a medium sized HD TV. The bedding was very comfortable.
The reason I give it a 3 instead of a 4 is because of the location. It's in a seedy area of Dallas where there's really not much to do. The hotel makes you use your room key to enter into their halls. I suspect this is to keep out the riff raff. Parking is free and I think I saw free wireless.
You could certainly do worse. In fact, in this particular area, this hotel is cream of the crop.

name: Sleep Inn Addison
title: “Get what you pay for”
text: You get what you pay for at this hotel. I like Sleep Inns because most properties have a walk-in shower instead of a half shower-half bath. I had a good sleep yet this property IS in the path of the Dallas Airport. But I did not hear the airplanes at night. What I DID HEAR was the constant running up and down in the hallways of children because the walls are pretty thin. And there was a BAD stench coming up from the drainpipe in the shower when the shower was turned on. However it did not stink before the water was started. Water pressure was almost non-existent in the shower. The hotel is in need of a renovation but who knows when that will occur. Breakfast included waffles, bagels, toast, juices, oatmeal, fruit, hard boiled eggs, and danish. Be aware that this property is almost on the DFW land and there are no good restaurants or fast food places within walking distance. Wireless internet is an 11 GBit per second network instead of a 54 GB network. Hotel provides a 24 hour shuttle but you must sign up for the morning shuttle from the night before.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Dallas-Market Center
title: “OK but can't wait until construction is over.”
text:
My family and I stay at this ES several times a year because of its proximity to the hospital district (my doctor is there and we live about 200 miles away). This is a very typical ES with nothing spectacular about it but nothing horrible either. Our last stay, however, left a lot to be desired. I understand that being under construction is never easy on anyone but the parking was almost nil and it took quite a while to get a cart to our car for luggage. The staff at the desk seemed really scattered, especially the young man there, and distracted.
Because my husband is a Hilton Honors member, we travel on points quite a bit. We understand that we are not able to choose a specific room when we travel this way but after we were put in a smoking room with an obvious ashtray on the counter, the first suggestion was to "be up right away to remove the ashtray." Silence. "Well, why don't we move you, instead?" Ya think? Again, distracted and scattered. We have stayed here several times but we have never had an experience like this. We look forward to the construction phase being over and hope that everyone will be on their game by then.

name: Springhill Suites Dallas Downtown West End
title: “Check For Large Groups Before Booking”
text:
I recently traveled with my family to the Springhill Suites in the West End area of Dallas.
Unfortunately, so did the Jr. High and High School Students from Guatemala. All 200+ of them. The night was filled with running up and down the halls, laughing & conversations in the halls, slamming of doors, you name it – think slumber party on multiple floors.
After many direct requests with the students and sponsors, I went downstairs and asked the night manager & guard to please get these kids under control. By this time it was 2:00am. The staff mentioned the hotel was chaotic the week before when the fans for the OU vs. Texas football game stayed there, so this was nothing new to them. Because it was such a large group, the students were on all floors of the hotel so there was no way to get away from the noise.
Fortunately, the kids checked out the next morning, and the second night was great. The thing that makes this hotel a great place to stay (central location/good price) can also be it’s biggest negative because large groups may be staying there – which is typical of the industry, but this is the first time I have experienced it in such a direct way.
The staff responded very well, comp’d my room and offered many freebies to make it right. I would stay there again, but only after finding out how many large groups were in the hotel and their demographics. Maybe more seasoned travelers already know to do this and now I do too!

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Dallas-Market Center
title: “Convenient and Nice”
text:
The Embassy Suites resembles many others - the large atrium with fountains, rooms open to atrium. The staff was very friendly, the rooms clean and large, the breakfast good as always, happy hour okay - I've had better munchies at other Embassy Suites. Lots of mirrors, lights.
It's not really near anything in particular, unless you are needing to be close to the hospital district. But it is very convenient for getting on the highway to go in any direction. We were about 5 minutes from the historic West End with the JFK Memorial/6th Floor Museum. It served our purpose to be close to an office, but also en route to some sightseeing.
They are in the process of renovating some of the rooms - appears to be floor by floor. Nice to see the updating.

name: Homestead Studio Suites - Dallas - North - Park Central
title: “Great place to stay”
text:
I've read the other reviews and, frankly, I wonder if they stayed the same place we did. 12121 Coit Rd, Dallas, Tx.?
The staff is wonderful. Always willing to help. The manager takes such pride in her hotel complex and it shows. This Homestead hasn't been "hers" very long. She's working very hard to make it an ever better place to stay. The grounds are clean and well manicured. Most on the beds were replaced while I was there. A lot of the rooms are being redone.
There are some problems but the Homestead has been without a handyman for a few months. Things did slip a little but they have one now and things are getting repaired. If something was wrong, they bent over backwards to fix it. 
Its convient to every part of the North Dallas area. And a great price compared to the other suites in the area.
Maybe, the other reviewers would have been happier staying at a Hilton type hotel. Nah, they would have complained about something there, too.

name: Days Inn Market Center Dallas
title: “Hooker Hotel and Gross”
text:
So I was at a conference in the area when I found this hotel online. The price was great and the location accomidating. However, when I got to this hotel I thought I was staying at a hooker hotel with the hooker waiting for me. The place is worn, unattractive and filled with trash. For some reason, there is a full-time Dallas Police car there and the parking lot is always empty. 
In order to gain access to your room, you have to go outside such as you might find at a motel. The rooms were reasonable but random people knock on your door and security is a serious cconcern. There appeared to only be a few others in the hotel with me. The continental breakfast is abhorant and barely meets the standard definition of continental breakfast. 
DONT STAY HERE. The reviews are true so this is a heads up notice about what you are getting into. There are reasonable hotels next door stay there instead. The hotel charges $$74.00/night but the accomidations are more like $19.99/night. 
If you want to live another day, find another hotel. Security is a serious concern here. The place is just gross.

name: InterContinental Dallas
title: “No Wireless Internet!!!!”
text: Really!?!? How can you be a 3.5- 4 star hotel and not have wireless Internet!?!?!? You can't. The furniture in the room looked to pretty old. The staff and service was friendly and helpful though.

name: Extended Stay America - Dallas - Greenville Ave.
title: “really is a great deal”
text: I stayed here for 30 nights. It was comfortable and quiet. It's not the Ritz Carlton but it's in a great location next to 24hr JackInTheBox and a gas station/convenience store. If you use coupons it will be cheaper than rent. I got 30 nights for just under 900 and I slept well the whole time. Like I said, the hotel is not elegant but for $30ish per night it's freaking awesome.

name: InterContinental Dallas
title: “Nothing special”
text: I was expecting more from an Interncontinental since I have stayed a bunch around the country. The floors and rooms smelled old (almost like mothballs). The rooms were in decent shape, but nothing I would consider above average. I would suspect nicer places are available in the area.

name: Motel 6 Dallas
title: “It's Now Motel 6 and Never Again”
text: Read reviews about this Motel 6 as being brand new (not one that was another hotel before) and was expecting a new one. The clerk at the front desk was helpful when checking in but when we were struggling to open the front doors with our hands full he was standing by the front doors and just watched without offering to help. The beds were new and very comfortable. The sheets and blankets were very clean and white but the bed cover when pulled back there was a huge (size of an apple) burned hole on the inside of it. The room was extremely hot when we arrived at 8pm and it took till midnight to cool it down. The floors felt uneven, the bathroom was so-so. I just wouldn't recommend this hotel/motel to anyone of my friends or family.

name: Sterling Hotel
title: “Worst experience ever!!!!! Go to Motel 6!”
text: OK, the thought is good. A night’s stay, free shuttle transportation to and from the Cowboy game, and free breakfast the next morning. The idea is good, but the reality is HORRIBLE!!!! First off, when we arrived it looked nice for the mere $100.00 that we were paying. Check in was very slow, and our rooms were not nice at all. It was a very basic Motel 6 room, and I would not even dare my worst enemy to get into the shower. GROSS! But, we start with a few drinks down at the Sports Bar (which was the best part of the whole trip)! So we’re watching another game on the big screen, having a few drinks, and my husband orders some food. We are planning to take the 6:00 shuttle over to the game. Well, at 5:00 (just after my husband ordered his food) the shuttle organizer comes to the bar and tells us that we need to get on the shuttle now. I told them that we were waiting on food and that we were planning to take the 6:00 shuttle. She said that we were the only ones scheduled for the 6:00 shuttle so the bus was not going to come pick up just the two of us. Soooo……The bartender goes and rushing my husband’s food into a to-go box, then we’re boarded on a tiny overcrowded shuttle with standing room only! Needless to say, my husband couldn’t eat standing up! So, we’re taking it all in stride. We arrive at the game and we wait outside the game so that my husband can eat his $8.00 hamburger. The game was fun, had a few drinks, and when it was over we headed out to gate 8 for the shuttle to pick us up. This was around 10:30! Marriott shuttles kept coming and going for an hour with no Sterling Shuttle in sight. By this time an angry and tired MOB of people have formed waiting for the Sterling Shuttle. My husband calls the hotel to ask what the issue is, and they tell him there is a shuttle there and to go find it. Obviously there wasn’t a shuttle there so about 45 minutes later he calls the hotel back and the guy screams at him and hangs up! Finally I push our way through the crowd, board a bus that wasn’t ours and begged for that driver to take us to our hotel! HE DID! Wonderful man! And guess what time we arrived…….12:30AM!!!! 2 hours after the game was over! We could see the stadium from our hotel so it’s not like it’s a lonnnnnggg drive! When we arrive at the hotel there is a HUGE mob of angry people trying to go up the elevator to their rooms. There’s only one working and it’s barely working. So, after another 20 minutes we get up to the room! The next morning we’re still optimistic and are geared up for the free breakfast. When we arrive downstairs, we find out that breakfast was only served from 7-9! Ok guys, lets get realistic. A late night at the Cowboy game where you’ve been drinking, how many can get up, get showered, and be ready for breakfast by 9:00??? WHAT A JOKE! So, for our $100.00 that included the room, shuttle and breakfast, we only received the room! I would definitely recommend the Marriott (because they seem to have it together) or stay at a different hotel and call a cab! It will be less hassle!!! We will never go back to the Sterling EVER EVER EVER!!!!!! My husband jokes that we may buy it next year because with service like this, it’s sure to go under QUICK! Save yourself the headache!

name: SpringHill Suites NW Hwy at Stemmons/I-35E
title: “We wouldn't stay anywhere else!!!”
text: My husband and I arrived for Red River Rivalry weekend, shortly after the funeral of his father, a 50 plus rivalry attendee. We also are newlyweds and had not had a real honeymoon. They made sure our visit was not only pleasant but memorable. We arrived back to our room to find a bottle of wine, chocolates, a long stem rose and the most beautiful card with expressions of both sympathy and congrats for a long marriage. The breakfasts were wonderful the hot tub a nice release for our stress and worry, and the staff was helpful on directions and suggestions for our visit. You have earned our business and expressions of graditude!!!

name: Candlewood Suites - Dallas by the Galleria
title: “Great Location, Great Staff”
text: I just returned from a 5 day stay at this Candlewood Suites and know that I will return to this location on my future trips to the Dallas area. The price was great, with an online special I was able to stay here for 5 nights for $280.00. Location was great, just a short walk to the Galleria and quick drive to many locations, as well as the train to downtown Dallas. The staff was always polite and helpful. I was greeted every time I walked by the desk or passed staff members on the property. The gym is a little worn, but I was still able to get in a work-out before starting my day.

name: InterContinental Dallas
title: “Thank you for Magical Customer Service Moment!”
text: I wanted to take a moment from my incredibly busy schedule to thank the management fom The InterContinental Hotel Dallas. My company spent several nights at this hotel during an event recently. And while the rooms, accommodations, bar and general hotel were as expected (absoutely TOP NOTCH), what was most impressive and the reason for my post, was the amazing customer service provided by management. I especially want to mention the Assistant General Manager Aref. A situation arose that the hotel did not have any control over...yet, he took customer service to the next level and created a magical customer service moment. I was so impressed with his diligence and promptness that I am now taking the time to thank him and the hotel...and will go out of my way to refer others to stay at this hotel and stay there myself again if the opportunity arises.

name: Motel 6 Dallas
title: “Nice Hotel a little confusing location”
text:
I was here just about 2 weeks ago for business. We stay at LaQuinta's all the time. I was in room 101. It had a couch, refrigerator, desk, and a separate room where the bed was. It had the usual hair dryer, iron & ironing board. 
I felt like the maid didn't do that great of a job so I only let her clean once. I always bring my own lysol or clorox wet wipes and wipe every thing down so I didn't see the need for her to come back. 
The pillows and the bed were very nice. It also had a ceiling fan in the living room. 
The staff was friendly enough. 
I say confusing location only because you can only take a right out of the hotel unless you go to the hotel next door and drive along a fence, etc... to make a right. The hotel is close to the highway. There was plenty to eat around there. I was alone and felt safe by myself. I would stay here again in a minute.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Dallas LBJ at Josey
title: “Bring Your own Ice Box LOL”
text: The room didnt have a refridgerator nor microwave which I felt it should .Other then that It was a very neat and clean hotel and the room was nice ..I put my sign on the door stating I wanted me time and the cleaning lady came in anyway ........maybe she wanted to see something I dont know but she said sorry and left...When I got home and got my credit card statement I had a charge from the room for $2.50 ..I called because my room was prepaid and the hotel shouldn't have touch my card so the lady asked me about the bottel of water in the room......SO Bring Your own Water.........LOL

name: BEST WESTERN Market Center
title: “Great stay for two people on a budget”
text: My friend and I were on a tight budget, and we found this great hotel that fit our needs. We only stayed one night and it was close to downtown Dallas and everywhere we needed to go. The staff was very friendly and I would recommend this hotel for those on a budget who need somewhere to lay their head for a night or two!

name: Wyndham Dallas Love Field
title: “Friendly staff, cavernously large room”
text:
Overnighted here awaiting morning flight at Love Field...a very comfy bed in a cavernously LARGE room, with a correspondingly grossly over-sized shower. I'm sure NBA players probably love it, but the rooms took a long time to warm up and feel comfy...an important factor on a night with pouring & freezing rain.
Nicely attired restaurant offered a very tasty apple, walnut & cheese salad which I schlepped back to the (now warm) room. Staff very friendly and attentive.

name: Holiday Inn Dallas Market Center
title: “In the Middle”
text: This hotel is between Children's Hospital and Scottish Rite Hospital. It serves us well when our daughter has appointments at either facility. The rooms are really nice--and bedding is very comfortable. Our last stay--May 29th was very enjoyable. If I had one gripe, it would be that the hotel does not offer discounts to those who must use Children's or Scottish on a regular basis. It would really help out.

name: Ritz-Carlton Dallas
title: “Great experience: where to stay in Dallas”
text:
First, let me say that this is a Ritz: I expect everything to be outstanding (especially given the rack rates) , and this hotel did not disappoint me. The incredibly late check-in (2:30 AM) that went as smoothly as had I been there in the late afternoon, the room was exquisite, the service was outstanding (picking up my shoes to be shined at 3 AM and having them back before 9 was great), and I couldn't recommend a hotel any more than this one.
All of that said, I have two very minor complaints: the iron was missing the "cap" that held the water in, so you had to be careful while ironing not to get your shirts wet; and the shower gel in the bathroom doesn't lather well with just a washcloth (they should either give you a real bath sponge or go back to traditional bar soap).
The location is very convenient for anything in Downtown or Uptown.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Dallas Hotel & Conference Center
title: “Texas Instruments - business traveler friendly”
text: Very close to TI and a nice place to stay for a business trip. Clean, safe and quiet, they have an extra friendly staff and nice breakfast buffet.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Dallas/Market Center
title: “Great hotel!”
text: My wife and I had an outstanding stay at this hotel. The entire staff was willing to accommodate our every need while we were there. The breakfast was very yummy and very well priced for an all you can eat buffet. The bed was super comfy (can I buy one?). We will certainly be returning to this hotel in the future and recommend all of our friends to it!!

name: Dallas Addison Marriott Quorum By the Galleria
title: “Nice business hotel”
text: People and service was very good. Beds comfortable and lobby very nice. Only negative is the Hotel charges $12.00 per day for Internet and the connection was not that good. Hotelnwithin a 5 minute walking distance to a number of restaurants.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Dallas Hotel & Conference Center
title: “Average hotel.”
text:
After realizing that this was the cheepest hotel in dallas in the top 50 of trip advisor I decided to book one night here. I happen to agree to several of the reviews here. The staff in the front desk was rude (during check-in only). The pillows are tall, short, and not very good. The bed is huge. I liked it. It is not nlise. It has breakfast included. That is always a 
Plus.... But nothing fancy, just convenient. It has a really good location. Banks and tons of restaurants nearby. 15 to 20 min drive from almpst everywhere in Dallas. My gps took me to the back part lf the hotel ( i need to get new updated maos maybe). My room was non-smoking but really smelled like smoke... Not too bad... But it did (didn't bother me so i didn't complain). The shower was ok and the bathroom in general was ok. I could tell they have done some remodeling in the rooms, but instead of getting new items for broken stuff in the bathroom, the used glu to put them back together.... Not very nice.
Towels were not very good but they did the work. Pool is ok. Overal, i got what i payed for. Not thrilled about the place. I guess is ranked so high only cuz of the price.
If you are trying to save money... Go for it. If it is a romantic trip.... Try something different.
The free parking is a plus in this hotel, and I LOVED the gact that they had free wifi everywhere.

name: La Quinta Inn Dallas Uptown
title: “Average stay”
text: My wife and I chose this motel for its location, which is great. Lots of great restuarants and shops around the area. This is an older property where the door to the room is adjacent to the parking lot. We were a little disappointed when we entered the non-smoking room. It smelled as if it had been a "smoking" room at some point in the not-so-distance past. The carpet also looked a little worn. Other than that, the room was clean and the bed was pretty comfortable. The free Wi-Fi was nice too. A free continental breakfast was offered and it was pretty standard. They did offer fresh fruit which was a nice touch. The staff was great and very attentive.

name: Hyatt Regency DFW
title: “OK for early flights”
text: We stayed here two separate nights recently due to flight schedules. We booked this hotel just because it was the nearest to the airport (actually in the airport). It was OK (we got a good deal) but I don't think it really was nearer than other hotels because the shuttle was quite slow. Our rooms were both large and comfortable, but the construction/finish wasn't up to Hyatt standards. The restaurant choices are limited (very redundant menus) and overpriced, and airport food service options are not available when you are a Hyatt guest because they are all within secure airport zones. Staff service and friendliness was a highlight - no complaints there. Anyway, OK for one night but not a place to spend much time.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Dallas Hotel & Conference Center
title: “All things good”
text: We had a sales meeting and everything went very well.The Location was great, meeting room good, and food and staff did everything that was needed. Would recomend for meeting or for lodging and I would stay there again if I am in Dallas

name: Crowne Plaza Dallas Market Center
title: “great place to stay”
text: The staff is very knowledgeable and expeirenced. Its proximity to downtown and Love field and the shuttle service is exceptional. It is a little outdated but that is more than made up for by the clean and sanitary condition of the whole property. It is a place that you can feel secure. You are getting good return on money spent at this hotel.

name: Holiday Inn Dallas Market Center
title: “Great stay, but not as good as first time”
text: I originally stayed here a little over a year ago and wrote a separate review at that time. Hotel is nice overall and I would stay here again and would recommend it to anyone. I booked a room here on Priceline for $55 a night. I booked my stay on Priceline for the wrong date and showed up at the hotel 1 week early but they fixed that easily since they had a great staff for check in. The pool was not yet open but they could do a better job of keeping it clean. There was paper floating in it and dirt on the bottom - very unsightly. There were a couple of TV channels the hotel wasn't getting due to some cable problem. And as the other reviewers have noted - the fitted sheet does not fit the bed at all. At night it keeps coming off the bed. The mattress is deeper than the sheet is made for so it does not cover it adequately. Everything else was okay. The food was good, ate at the restaurant twice. Try eating at the Market Diner for lunch and breakfast for some great food that is not as expensive as the hotel food. The hotel food was a bit costly. Overall I enjoyed my stay here.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “pricey, but a class act”
text:
Booked a suite - beautiful rooms, good sized, no amenities lacking. I found housekeeping and door staff eager to help, front desk pleasant and professional. Lobby/common areas very nice, with free wine/cheese in the afternoon, and a.m. pastries were, well, free - a nicety, but in NYC would walk to a real cafe. Park Ave S location is great.
I would gladly stay here again.

name: Hotel Lawrence
title: “Great Location”
text: Close to everything Kennedy as well as several good restaurants and other attractions. The only time we took a cab was to and from the airport - - we were able to walk everywhere else we wanted to go. Positives were historic look, clean rooms, friendly staff, cookies and milk served each night and complimentary breakfast. Areas that could be improved were the fitness room (the tread mills do not turn on easily) and the elevator (only one small one for all guests to share).

name: Wyndham Dallas Love Field
title: “Great for a night”
text: We stayed here for one night as we were only in Dallas for a wedding. The hotel is situated right by Love Field so it was great for us. If we had planned to really visit Dallas I would have chosen a hotel closer to the city center. The hotel itself was very nice. Clean, modern decor. The bathroom appears to be recently renovated with granite sinks and glass shower doors which was nice, but the tile in the shower could have used an update as well. The shuttle service was great - we relied on it entirely during our stay in Dallas and they went out of their way to transport us to and from the downtown wedding. Overall I was very happy with this property and would recommend the hotel, especially if you're only in town for a day or two and don't need a downtown location.

name: The Westin Park Central
title: “Best service I have ever had”
text:
I wanted to make sure that someone knows about Diana Lugg, She is the very best person I have ever encountered in a hotel visit, She is the friendliest and most courteous person at your hotel. Truly I cannot say enough about her, She is awesome.
Then there is Andy and Fernando Mendoza, amazing, Two of the politest young men I have ever encountered. They went out of their way to ensure that we all had rides to where we needed to go, Especially me, I felt that they catered to me, Maybe they didn't but they sure made me feel that way. I really appreciated the services that they provided. Not one time even with the hard time that I gave them (Joking around) did they ever step out of line or anything. 
I have the utmost respect for all three of these people And I would pray that would get recognized and rewarded for their dedication and professionalism that they obviously take pride in. Thank you for a wonderful trip

name: Wingate by Wyndham Dallas / Love Field
title: “Just Right!”
text:
Nice hotel for being in the same hotel chain as "The Knights Inn" Friendly staff and room priced right. I had only two issues the traffic noise (hotel is close to a major road) was unreal. I suggest a room on the third floor and toward the back of the hotel. Also the room had the smell of bug spray. 
Room had flat screen tv, microwave and frig. Again Nice Hotel overall!

name: Sheraton Phoenix Downtown Hotel
title: “Great for business visits, friendly, & professional services!”
text: Overall, my week-long stay during work here was great. The staff always had a friendly smile to welcome you and were always quite helpful with answering your questions. Gym was excellent with machines and even free-weights to use. Pool was awesome morning/noon/night. Internet use within the rooms were excellent. Internet access for the conference rooms could have been better by allowing similar access we had from our rooms. But I guess that's business for ya? Perhaps if they revamped their package-deal of FREE Wifi w/rental of the business conference rooms, it would further convince other businesses to visit here? Seemed pricey with the wifi-access for the conference rooms, if you asked me. Was forced to visit my room w/my laptop just to check emails then return to the conference room we rented to finish-up the rest of my work. Even if the Business Center was available, it would have been a nice gesture of the hotel to just INCLUDE a FREE Wifi package to all our users during the week-long rental of one of their conference rooms. That was the only NEGATIVE review I had for this place.

name: Omni Dallas Hotel at Park West
title: “BEST VALENTINES DAY EVER”
text: This hotel is absolutley gorgeous and yet the prices won't break your pocket book/ wallet. We had the sweet rendevouz package and the room was gorgeous! They took care in decorating the room and when I asked for chocholate covered strawberries instead of the trouffle it was no problem at all! Also the music channel with the beautiful backgrounds on the tv was a nice touch.The valet staff were excellent and very friendly, as were the rest of the staff. This will be the only place me and my boyfriend will stay when in Dallas.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Dallas Central Expressway
title: “Great Staff. Terrific Sleep. Good Location”
text: As a frequent Marriott traveler, I can attest that this location is superb. We had a quality night's sleep and enjoyed the amenities, great location near the highway, the front desk staff were top notch.

name: Omni Dallas Hotel at Park West
title: “A VERY GOOD CHOICE”
text:
The Hotel was excellent ,the staff were very helpful and friendly , the level of service was also very good.
The Breakfast Buffet was great with a big choice and variety .
I would recommend the Omni Hotel Park West wholeheartedly .

name: Sheraton Phoenix Downtown Hotel
title: “Had a great experiance and would stay here again.”
text: Was a great experince staying at this hotel. Would definitely stay here again. The staff was extremely friendly & helpful. Was very satisfied with my stay.

name: The Westin Park Central
title: “Best Staff”
text: My business and pleasure travel generally has me in hotel rooms about 150 nights per year both domestically and internationally. I've spent more than 75 nights at the Westin Park Central in Dallas this year and can't find enough good things to say about the accomodations and the staff. Younis, at the check in desk, is as friendly and efficient as anyone I've ever come across. I can tell he takes great pride in making sure my room and experience is the best it can be. I eat dinner at the hotel occasionally and have found the food to be considerably better than most hotel food I've had. I have breakfast everyday I'm there and I've never had service as good as that provided by Singh M., Oscar and Antonio V. Their greeting, smile and efficient service is simply the best. I highly recommend you give the Westin Park Central a try the next time you're in Dallas and say hi to this team from me. Mike B.

name: Embassy Suites Dallas - Near the Galleria
title: “Terrible Hotel”
text: I am surprised to find such poor quality from an Embassy Suite Hotel. I expect better from the Hilton brand. I stayed at this hotel 11/13/12 to 11/17/12. I spent 4 days here for business. The food was terrible for the seminar. Each day the afternoon snacks were hard and dry. The pastries in the AM were also dry. The strawberries were mushy. The coffee was never refreshed & quite bitter. They had very loud work being performed outside our conference room which was very distracting. As for the dining facilities, the flatware had terrible residue & under the lighting was quite disgusting. A simple wipe off prior to set up would have made the presentation better. I spoke to the front desk. Nothing was done about it & the next morning the same condition was found. Some of the cooked to order food at the breakfast buffet was cold. One of the breakfast cooks was rude and also helped himself to the tip jar when the other cook was out of the area. The dinner cooks and dinner waitstaff were great which is why I rated this hotel higher than one. The maid service didn't come on my last day and my request for more towels never arrived. Also, it is not a great place if you have to work in your hotel room as it is quite roudy in the lounge each night. As nothing was done when I mentioned the poor condition of the flatware & I was quite busy with the seminar and work to do at night, I chose to send a written complaint at the end. The manager contacted me and told me because I wasn't planning on returning then he couldn't do anything for me. I I will not pick this location for next yr's seminar. I will go to Chicago or D.C.

name: The Westin Park Central
title: “Comfy Beds!”
text:
My mother recently traveled to this hotel for a conference and was very wary because of the negative reviews but was pleasantly surprised. She does not have an account but wanted to enter a review because she had been so pleased with her stay.
"The place was great! It was clean, simple, and comfortable. The beds were the best part! Close access to lots of chain restaurants."

name: Sheraton Phoenix Downtown Hotel
title: “Check in”
text: Valet and bellman were excellent !! Front desk needs refinement and training.

name: Omni Dallas Hotel at Park West
title: “Simply a wonderful stay”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights for a convention and it was great! We had a very comfortable room with all the 4 star amenities. It was the best nights sleep we have had in a hotel! The bed was incredibly comfortable. The staff were exceedingly polite. They even gave us complimentary milk and cookies on our first night stay! It is away from the drag of downtown Dallas traffic, which we liked! If you need a great place to stay and dont mind driving 10 minutes to downtown without traffic, this place will satisfy your needs.

name: Sheraton Phoenix Downtown Hotel
title: “This is what a hotel should be”
text:
This was a lovely 4 day stay for a conference in May 2011. The hotel is a nice balance of tasteful architecture and decor along with very practical and well functioning staff, conference space, etc. One of the highlights for me was the fitness area and pool The fitness center is well designed, with up to date equipment. The pool is really delightful. It is well over 25 yards long, and a great way to work out in the early morning, before families or sunbathers come for later in the day. The whirlpool is also nice. My only one small request would be to have a big clock in the pool and whirlpool area. I kept having to get out to look at my watch. It would also be nice to see the pool dimensions written somewhere.
The staff at the front desk were very helpful, calm and friendly. I shared a room with a colleague from another city, and they were able to divide the reservation into a "shared"reservation so both of us could get Starwood points for the room. I had lent my flashdrive to someone who lost it. The hotel staff were quite gracious in helping me look for it and took personal interest in the matter. 
I was busy with the conference the whole time, but went across the street for a lovely lunch at a Greek restaurant, and then a delicious dinner at another restaurant in the same complex (I believe the name was 1130). The hotel restaurant and lobby bar was also very nice- excellent service and reasonable fare. The conference food was also very good for the breakfasta and lunches.
There were also some cute souvenir stores across the street to buy gifts for the kids to bring home. 
I would definitely recommend this for another business trip and conference.

name: Omni Dallas Hotel at Park West
title: “Great Hotel”
text:
This was my first time staying with Omni hotels so I wasn't sure what to expect but I was pleasantly surprised. Their turn down service includes a glass of milk and a big chocolate chip cookie.
If you sign up for their reward program you also receive a complementary breakfast package that will either be left behind your door or someone will hand it to you personally.
The bed was very comfortable and the room, in general, was fairly clean. The bathroom was a good size but the water flow wasn't the greatest.
When I needed to have my stay extended I was moved into the presidential suite... mercy! It was huge and included a library, piano, dinining room area, bar, I think about 3 bathrooms and a sunk in tub. The decor was quite outdated but the room itself was very comfortable.
My one complaint: when I made my reservation via telephone the staff kept me on hold for close to 25 minutes as they tried to find someone to handle reservations.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “Great Experience, nice staff, Romantic get away”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the hotel 10/7-10/10/05. It was a quick weekend getaway from our lttle kids.
I really liked this hotel for a few reasons:
1. The staff from the doorman to the front desk were probably some of the nicest, most professional staff I have dealt with
2. The rooms were well decorated, the beds very comfortable. Borderline boutique hotel without the attitude
3. Each floor had only 7 rooms per floor. Since the whole place has only 70 rooms, it gives the impression of a bed and breakfast or small Inn.
4. 4 of the 7 rooms on each floor had a balcony. We stayed in a room ending in 07. Great little balcony, but there is a busy restaurant in the basement and sometimes the people coming out on Saturday night were a little loud, but not unbearable.
5. The lobby is a great place to sit and have a cocktail. Realxing. The rooftop lounge is really cool too. Very private
6. Extremely convenient to transportation and walking distance to the village/Union Square area without being in a tourist area

name: Courtyard by Marriott Dallas Market Center
title: “Room & amenities great; conference facility lacking”
text:
We had a room here and attended a conference here also. The room was very comfortable and nice. However, we suffered in the conference room with inadequate A/C. Several restaurants and shops within the hotel complex - but very confusing to get from one to the other if on opposite sides or different floors.
Food in the main restaurant was excellent, especially breakfast buffet.
Most restaurants outside the hotel were closed, surprisingly, on Saturday.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Dallas Hotel & Conference Center
title: “EXCELENTE HOTEL !”
text: Muy buen hotel, lo tome por recomendaciones de la pagina. Esta muy cerca del mall North park y de Gallerias Dallas y muy cerca tambien del outlet en Allen, Tx. En relación precio-calidad esta excelente. Cuartos limpios y Camas comodas, así como tambien un muy buen desayuno buffet incluido en el precio. Buena señal de Wi-fi, estacionamiento amplio. El personal de recepción muy atentos.

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Dallas Downtown
title: “family stay”
text: I was in town visiting with my familiy for a wedding. I enjoyed the hotel very much and the staff was extremly friendly. It was in a very good location for us to get to everything. Although I didnt like the fact I had to pay for parking but I here Downtown Dallas is all like that. But for the price i paid i will deal with it. Will recommend.

name: Adolphus Hotel
title: “NICE HISTORIC DOWNTOWN HOTEL”
text: This is a great hotel if you do not need a pool. It is located in the heart of downtown Dallas and does have plenty of cheap places to eat within a couple of blocks. The room and hallways are extremely spacious. Must be a 1912 thing! The rooms and hotel are older but I wouldn't trade the history for an update or remodel. The staff was great and the valet service is top notch. Didn't get a chance to eat here but I have had banquets there with my company and the food is fantastic. Overall it was a great stay and hope to stay at The Adolphus again.

name: Sheraton Dallas Hotel by the Galleria
title: “Club floor GREAT!”
text: We stayed at this hotel for a conference, and were on the Club floor. Beautiful, spacious rooms with great views. Recently renovated, and it looks it. I did see the hallway on a lower floor, and it wasn't as regal. Our floor and room were great, as was the suite used for our meetings. (The bartender was very unfriendly, be warned.)

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Dallas Downtown
title: “Great Hospitality”
text: This was my first time staying at a Crowne Plaza Hotel and I was very impressed with the young man at the front desk named Joseph. He was very cordial in his greeting and helpful in answering any questions that I had about my stay at his hotel. The hotel was clean and comfortable. I will gladly stay at a Crowne Plaza hotel in my future travels and I can highly recommend everyone to else to stay there also.

name: Hotel Giraffe
title: “A Very Nice Boutique Hotel”
text: Had a recent stay in NYC and stayed in one of their upscale suites. The rooms were clean and the amenities nice. One of the elevators was not working during my stay, so it took forever to get up and down to the lobby. Also requested a bucket of ice which never arrived from room service. The continental breakfast w/ juices was quite enjoyable. Would recommend with some reservations.

name: Hilton Dallas Lincoln Centre
title: “Better places in the area for the same price or cheaper”
text:
I stayed here the weekend of 2/11-2/13 and the hotel looks really nice when you pull up and go into the lobby. That's when you find out you are going to pay $14/day to park your car. Seriously? I can stay at the intercontinental, Westin, or Omni and not have to pay to park my car. Then you get to your room. Very clean no issues there other then it looks like the last time it was updated was 1980. Nothing like watching TV on an old box TV when the shows that are being shown are in 16:9 widescreen format. That was nice...... Then you pay $13/day for internet access and it didn't work. I could not get online the help desk couldn't even get me online. Noone would give me a refund for this. The staff at the front desk is super nice i think the issue was just out of their hands. 
Getting to the hotel presents its issues also if you don't have a GPS and you aren't from the area good luck to you. I lived in Dallas for 2 years and had a hard time getting to the hotel for the first time. All in all if i had to recommend a hotel to a friend that wanted to stay in this area i would send them somewhere else. In the end this is not a 4 star hotel. If the rooms were updated it would be 4 star easily but its very dated and doesn't meet 4 star expectations.

name: Hilton Anatole
title: “Beautiful hotel”
text: Expanse, art museum, friendly and helpful staff, comfortable rooms, very small bathroom but everything worked. Restaurant was ok. We didn't go to their famous Ser restaurant that is only open for dinner.

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Dallas Downtown
title: “Quick Get Away for A Good Price...”
text:
My husband and I stayed in September 2011. We went for a concert and a quick get away. I found the Crowne Plaza online and thought it was a great deal and in an ideal location for all the things we wanted to do. The room was nice and all the staff was very friendly. There were three things that I didn't like about the hotel. First we were told that there was a shuttle service but it never came to pick my husband and I up. Not a real big deal since we just drove our car or walked. The second thing was that there is a night club that is open to the public and the bouncers kind of bombard you when you get off the elevator. And the third thing was that the waitresses in the hotel were not very attentive to their customers.
All in all we like the hotel. It was very close to restaurants and sight seeing, and the beds were comfortable.

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Dallas Downtown
title: “Nice hotel, bad location.”
text:
The hotel was nice and spacious and modern. The food was nice and the staff were helpful, we even had a chauffeur who took us places we wanted to go. 
My criticism is that in order to get to your room you had to have a key for the lifts, which is great security, however was very annoying considering there was only one key for our room! 
I'm a sucker when it comes to Dallas, but I've seen better areas of the Downtown. I felt a little lost, being British. So for people who aren't familiar with the area I wouldn't recommend it. There is a DART stop a few hundred yards down the road though.

name: Hotel ZaZa Dallas
title: “Great staff; Great service”
text:
I recently stayed at Hotel Zaza while attending a sports event at the new Cowboy stadium (25 mins by taxi).
First and foremost the hotel staff is amazing. Everyone from the front desk (Morgan & Melissa) Concierge (tyler), the valet parking attendants who drove us in the courtesy cars were very friendly and had many great suggestions and finally the housekeeping staff always smiled and greeted everyone.
Everyone is always striving to assist. which was very nice. The hotel gives complementary snacks and beverages throughout the day as well.
The rooms were very modern, clean and the staff paid very close attention to detain (night turn-down, complementary bottles of wine and fruit, and morning after care packages of gatorade, bloody mary mix and advil).
The bathroom amenities were top of the line Bungalow from Frette.
My only one negative comment was that the hotel doesn't provide mouthwash as an amenity.
Other than that a great stay and great service at the restaurant dragonfly. Joshua the restaurant / bar manager throws the best Sunday party and ensures all his guests needs are met, anticipated and exceeded.
I would certainly return. 
Be sure to choose one of the suites or a balcony room overlooking the pool.

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Dallas Downtown
title: “Crowne Plaza - Excellent Lodging and Service”
text: Enjoyed my 1 night stay. They allowed me to early checkin and then provided a Priority Member gift and breakfast coupon. Ingrid, the receptionist, was very cordial and nice. We definitely come back for another stay. Bary

name: The Westin Park Central
title: “The Cafe in the Park is fantastic. The service by Angelo & Ken was first class.”
text: The Cafe in the Park was fantastic. The service by Antonio & Ken was first class. Excellent food and wonderful service.

name: Hilton Anatole
title: “Typical CONVENTION hotel”
text: The hotel was average at best. Only one restaurant open during my three night visit, which made service slow and spotty. My 14th floor room featured a bathroom smaller than I've seen on Amtrak. The huge gap under the guest room doors (on all floors I'm told) allows the noise from the atrium below to travel right up to your room! AND, when a person opens a guest room door and allows it to close on its on the 'SLAM' is quite loud...a problem that was the most annoying of all. BUSINESS TRAVELERS BEWARE: If you ship anyting to the business center, there is a 'convenience' fee for picking it up, and even a greater fee for delivery to your room. (I had three packages and paid $40 to have them released - another associate paid $60 - and that was just to get them from the back room - no delivery.) There are no nearby bars or restaurants within walking distance, making the Anatole Hotel one of my least favorite convention spots.

name: Adolphus Hotel
title: “Adolphus Hotel”
text: While attending a convention in Dallas I was lucky enough to spend four nights at the Adolphus Hotel, which is conveniently located close to Neiman-Marcus and a short walk from the Convention Center. Although an older hotel, it retains its elegance and attentive, personable staff. My room was spacious, room service was speedy, and my food was hot and delicious. On the morning of check-out I had two large bags of books to be mailed and Ryan and Jerry came to my aid and got everything sent out. My only regret is that I did not have time to enjoy their afternoon tea. Would I stay here again? You bet.

name: Le Meridien Dallas by the Galleria
title: “BEST AROUND”
text:
The hotel itself is very nice with a contemporary look. But what really makes this a top notch establishment is the polite prompful front desk staff of JENNA and NONA (Jenna helped me directly while Nona had her back with whatever was needed). They single handly turn what could have been a terrible stay and experence here, into one of enjoyment and pleasure. They conducted these corrections has fast has they possible could and had a smile on their face the entire time even throught the hicups. I Was very upset headed back to the front desk ready to leave the hotel with my complaints, and do to staff left the front desk with all my problems solved and will not stay anywhere ese but here for now on. THXS LADIES VERY PROFESSIONAL WHILE STILL BEING PERSONABLE..
B and M 1104 top floor :)

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Dallas Downtown
title: “Great Place, Super Friendly Staff”
text: The Hotel staff was very friendly, they offered suggestions for getting around and offered maps without having to ask for one. They let us leave the truck in their parking garage even after checkout since we were staying in the area. Awesome "welcome" package for Priority Club Members: Lone Star, the National Beer of Texas, was included. :)

name: W Dallas Victory Hotel
title: “Staying in style!”
text: A group of high school girl friends stayed at the W for a girls trip. We were treated awesome. It is pricy..but worth it for a splurge! The staff is super helpful and you feel very protected while there. We also went to the Ghost bar and had a blast dancing. The pool was fantastic and the "living room" is beautiful!

name: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham Dallas Love Field
