title: “Not a place for single travelers”
text: Based on a 2-1/2 star rating, I was initially impressed with the price, but upon arrival saw why. The hotel is off the beaten path with dark parking lots and outdoor room access. As a single female traveler, I did not feel safe at all going in and out of my room in the evening. Rooms were OK. Clean but old - cigarette burns in the carpeting and older light fixtures and plumbing. Walls were pretty thin and sleep was minimal due to loud guests and people walking past your outside door late at night.

name: Fairfield Inn Dallas North
title: “Unexceptional....and that's a compliment!”
text: This Fairfield Inn is unexceptional in that it simply delivers on Marriott's promise: clean, comfortable rooms; friendly service; guest-driven amenities; and a price that won't strain the budget. Both Marriott & this property really know their business: this hotel is designed for busy, working professionals, as well as for anyone else that looks for both value & quality. The free high-speed Internet access is terrific; the complimentary breakfast is well-stocked and satisfying; the fitness room & indoor pool provide ample opportunities to keep fit while "on the road;" and they even set up a complimentary, old-timey popcorn cart every afternoon to provide a snack at check-in. Nothing fancy here....just quality accommodations at a fair price provided by customer-oriented staff.

name: Hotel ZaZa Dallas
title: “Stylish and attractive hotel. The noise from the pool bar was the only downside.”
text: The room was spacious, clean and stylish. The hotel has a funky vibe that works. Our only major issue was the noise from the pool bar. The music was cranked till 1AM and was very loud in our even numbered room. If you are there for the bar scene then it is likely not an issue. If you want to sleep before 1 am, bring ear plugs or get an odd numbered room on the opposite side of the hotel from the bar.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Excellent location, wonderful hotel”
text:
Our stay at the Magnolia in Dallas was absolutely perfect. From the moment you pull up to the valet service, to the front desk, and up to your room--everything was top notch. Jennifer at the front desk went above and beyond to help us and make our stay a good one. She's definitely a great asset to the hotel. We only used the shuttle service once, but I wish we would have taken advantage of it more. The driver was kind and very informative about the area. 
We stayed in a Queen Suite and while it was a huge room and very nice, the bed did not seem to be a queen. The full kitchen was a plus and we stayed on the 23rd floor so we had a great view. The breakfast, evening reception, and milk & cookies were just added bonuses to this amazing hotel!
We loved being within walking distance of restaurants and the JFK memorial. It is an excellent area to stay in!

name: Aloft Dallas Downtown
title: “A Gem of a place to stay”
text: I admit, I got a heck of a deal on the room rate, but even so, the suite was comfortable with room to spread out, conduct business and relax when each were needed. The modern decor on top of a re-purposed building is tastefully done. The Staff was outstanding and very helpful even when extremely busy (a convention housed LOTS of folks there). The meeting/party room downstairs (we used it for both reasons) worked out perfectly, but be warned you'll need to bring your own overhead, whiteboard, etc. equipment. Do NOT expect a free breakfast in the morning, this is not your budget rate hotel but a fine gem in the heart of Dallas.

name: Rosewood Crescent Hotel
title: “Great service, Great location, Rooms are nothing special”
text:
My husband I stayed at The Rosewood Crescent Hotel for one night. We chose the hotel based on it's location. We love uptown because of the restaurants and bars. Hotel Zaza and THe Ritz wanted over $300 a night so I opted to stay at Crescent Court for $216.
We have visited the hotel multiple times while staying at Hotel Zaza or the Stoneleigh Hotel, both within walking distance, and have been impressed with the elegant lobby and courtyards. We love Nobu and enjoy the bar at Palominos so it was nice to have both right there, just steps from our room.
The room (Superior King- lowest level room) itself was quite ordinary. The decor was uninspired but we did enjoy having a small balcony (only large enough to stand and look around.) Everything was spotless and the housekeeping staff was very friendly and thorough. We didn't feel like we were being pampered in luxury but we certainly didn't have anything to complain about either. The Valet staff was very busy but still managed to take our car and deliver our car in a very timely fashion.
Overall, it was a pleasant stay and we would return if the room rate is better than that at Zaza or the Ritz.

name: Aloft Dallas Downtown
title: “A must see experience if you want something out of the norm”
text: Everyone was very helpful and really nice!!!! I highly recommend staying there they make you feel really welcome!! The beds were really comfortable where you didnt even want to get up. They have good simple breakfast food and food for at night. Snacks and coffee are available through out the day. The art pieces they had on display for sale was awesome !! Very convienient to to the convention center-walking distance.

name: Hotel ZaZa Dallas
title: “Overdone w/ Poor Service”
text: Judging by the disparity in reviews of this hotel, I guess it really depends what you are looking for in a hotel. If you want poor, dismissive serivce, and a "see and be seen" atmosphere, this place is for you. The service was horrible - from leaving our luggage in the lobby (and then we had to go get it ourselves and bring it to our room), to the front desk staff acting like we were bothering them, to be overcharged on the bill (and not resolving it). If you want to take your shirt off and be seen by the pool, by all means, this is your spot. If you want customer service, look elsewhere.

name: Omni Dallas Hotel
title: “Great hotel”
text:
I stayed here for 4 nights on a business trip and was impressed with the room and facilities. 
The room was spacious with 2 queen beds, lots of pillows and a roomy bathroom with TV in the mirror!
The gym had a lot of equipment, open 24 hours a day with free headphones. 
The restaurants served great food, the buffet style lunch eaten outside was perfect and staff attentive. 
Only drawback was the very slow service at the conference lunches, however they were trying to serve 1100 people and its some distance to the malls (taxi ride away rather than walking distance). 
Would recommend.

name: Rosewood Crescent Hotel
title: “Weekend Trip”
text: The service at the hotel was OK at best. The room was clean but the entire hotel is just old. This would all be fine if the "staff" hotel employees didn't use it as their own private place to party. We (4 of us) went down to the pool and the there was no where to sit because the place was over taken by the hotel staff. Mind you this was a HOLIDAY weekend. Finally, the staff was nice enough to retire to their rooms so the actual guests could use the amenities they paid for. The actual pool was dirty and I got a piece of thin metal stuck in my foot. The bottom of the pool is so uneven our feet all feel like they lost a couple of layers of skin. At the lobby bar the waiter wanted to know what we were going to do and wanted us to join him and his friends. Very unprofessional since we didn't ask him and we just wanted a drink. The only thing good about this hotel is the location. We were able to walk to bars that are just down the street. However, to pay this much money and end up hanging out with the hotel staff in an ugly pool - will just go somewhere else next time. Crescent - you lost 4 guest forever.

name: Baymont Inn & Suites Dallas Love Field
title: “Big nice surprice. I really would come again!”
text:
We stay in Baymont Inn for 3 nights. Staff was absolutely fantastic. We arrived 1:00 am and the receiptionist was kind and gave us friendly welcome. 
Room was huge!! :) There were two kingsize beds, tv, fridge, air-conditioner, iron and nice badroom. 
Room was semi-clean. Semi because the floor because of the carpet was little bit dusty.
Bed was my favorite it was nice to sleep. I couldn't hear any noise at all. So if you like to have nice sleep third floor is good floor to stay in.
At the hotel there is gym, indpor pool and breakfast - I only have good things to say about them. 
Location is bit far from the center but if you need nice airport stay this is the one!

name: Rosewood Crescent Hotel
title: “Amazing service”
text: I stayed on business for two evenings and from check-in to check-out came across the some of the most professional and helpful staff I've ever encountered. There were no rooms ready upon check-in and yet the front desk person made several calls, upgraded my room, and made sure I did not have much of a wait. Additionally, she apologized for the wait - a real rarity and very much appreciated. Everything I requested, including a fan (yes crazy, but helps me sleep through the evening), they were able to meet. The valet and room service were always prompt. I took two early morning classes in the gym and both instructors were wonderful - I believe their names were Josh and Nikki. They were very helpful, patient, and great in explaining everything. The gym was large, very clean, and modern. I didn't encounter the thin wall issue (whcih is often tough) but I was upgraded to one of the top floor rooms which was very large. This is a wonderful hotel which I highly recommend.

name: Le Meridien Dallas by the Galleria
title: “Loved our stay!!”
text: We stayed at Le Meridien for my husband's birthday weekend and loved it! The service was wonderful and Barbara, the bartender, was knowledgeable about both the area and Dallas in general. And she makes a mean espresso martini! Definitely recommend Le Meridien!

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Dallas Downtown
title: “Excellent”
text: Es el mejor hotel en el que me he hospedado. Lo recomiendo ampliamente por el trato que le dan a las personas, de respeto y amabilidad. Sus tarifas son muy accesiblres y siempre hay alguien que te ofrece ayuda amable y eficiente.

name: Candlewood Suites - Dallas Market Center
title: “Relaxing place to stay”
text: This Candlewood is nice. The rooms are comfortable and clean. The front desk at check in, David was very friendly and helpful. The check out lady, Senedu was very nice and helpfl ine getting me on shuttle to the airport. I felt very welcomed at this hotel.

name: Rosewood Crescent Hotel
title: “Cotton Bowl Amazing !”
text: Booking was easy by phone and she described the rooms perfectly. Originally were going to have 4 guests in one room but ended up with 3. Checked in early & room not ready so they upgraded up to a 900 square foot suite w/ FOUR balconies. We were going to grab a cocktail and wait with friends but they offered us the instant upgrade !! Huge king size bed w/ 2 closets , makeup vanity and huge master bath. Lady Primrose bath products were a relaxing touch. 2 bathrooms and full bar w/ fruit and cheeze plates. Room service portions are almost too massive but, they arrive fast. There were hand written notes delivered from the manager and daily temp. & info notes each morning. Downstairs I found Nobu was a hip and fun spot. The courtesy Mercedez were a nice touch and readily available. Spa has dated showers but nice hot baths w/ relaxing waterfall. I am in love with Rosewood Crescent and am looking into one of their resorts in Cabo for the summer. So glad we stayed here !

name: Baymont Inn & Suites Dallas Love Field
title: “Very nice”
text: This is real nice hotel. All staff I very nice. This was very nice for a baymont inn I never thought there would be a baymont inn this nice.

name: The Joule, Dallas
title: “excellent boutique hotel”
text:
clean, close to all downtown restaurants, easy walk (10 mins) to convention centre.
The hotel is small but makes you feel special. Many personal touches ie, turn down service, hotel car service etc.
The rooms were nice and dark for sleeping. Ask for the larger suite rooms.
The pool is small but unique as it has a glass wall that you can swim up to and look down at the city street. Excellent pool side food. Burgers are huge and you can share....tasty too!

name: Hilton Anatole
title: “Nice Stay in Texas Sized Hotel”
text:
I found a great deal at the Hilton Anatole using my HHonors points for one night. I was able to select a corner, exec floor room, which provided a comfortable seating area between the entry/bathroom area and the bed. This was definitely not your standard US Hilton fare, with a significant Asian theme including bronze Asian statutes, and lacquer finished closets and decorations in the room. The seating area included a couch, lounge chair and desk with working chair, all facing a flat panel TV that swiveled towards the bedroom area, allowing you to watch TV conveniently in the seating /working area, as well as the bed. The bathroom was very tastefully done, with a glass and tile shower, including bench. There was also a nicely built combo sink and vanity, with seating/make-up area which I'm sure my wife would have loved if she had been with me. 
The hotel is "Texas sized" with two separate wings, each with their own reception areas, and connected by a large concourse. Make sure you know which side you're staying in before parking or getting dropped off by the cab, otherwise it's a hike between the sides. For Hilton Honors Gold or Diamond members, you'll want to stay in the Tower side to take advantage of the nice Executive lounge on the 25th floor.

name: Rosewood Mansion on Turtle Creek
title: “Room cleaning needs to improve and hotel revamped”
text: Stayed for 6 nights and every night of my stay there was evidence of poor room cleaning. Toothpaste marks left on sink, bath tub scum marks, dirty cleaning cloths left on bed. The worst has to be a mattress sheet that was far too small for the mattress so that I woke up in the morning sleeping on the mattress - haven't done that since my student days. Have to say I'm amazed with the reviews as the whole place seems to be in need of a re vamp. Also completely agree with the thin walls, you can hear people in corridor. The concierge were very helpful and welcoming though.

name: Hotel ZaZa Dallas
title: “If you have visions of sitting by the pool, reading a book, and sipping a beverage, do not stay here.”
text: Came in to Dallas for the weekend. Thought we would have a nice relaxing, holiday weekend, reading by the pool, hanging out, sipping on drinks, etc. I guess the Pool is a real money maker for this hotel. It was certainly not put in place for the guest of the hotel. We went down on Friday morning and all of the beach chairs were already reserved or taken. There were probably 200 people at the pool at this point. Playboy bunnies, drunk girls and guys, muscle heads, rappers, people that really thought they were too cool. Again on Saturday we encountered the same. Did not ever get to sit by the pool or even get in it. Did not meet one person at the pool that was actually staying at the pool. We thought later in the evening we could accomplish our goal, but much to our dismay, the pool was closed at 7pm, so they could convert it to become part of the bar. We took a bottle of wine, on the way to dinner we poured ourselves a glass and went down to get the car. The valet attendent said we could not leave the hotel with the wine. (It was in plastic cups.) I told him it was water and to mind his own freaking business. Screw this hotel. Lots of guys in Mid-life crisis here and lots of getto girls looking for those men.

name: W Dallas Victory Hotel
title: “Not up to par”
text:
Upon making the reservation I requested the in-room refrigerator be emptied of hotel stuff. Also that a small fridge ($10 day) be provided. Asked and was assured both would be taken care of before we checked in.
Neither was. I had to call a request rental fridge and first one they delivered was broken. 
The bedspread had an odd yellow stain on it. The advertised 42" TV in fantastic suite was 32". For $400 a night, it ought to come with at least 42". Looked cheap. The office phone was found laying behind the desk on floor, as was coaster for the two glassed they just set down on bare desk.
No where on web site or when making reservations are you informed of $24 overnight parking charge.
the deeo tub was nice, as was rain shower. I thought room was dark, cold and pretty devoid of artwork. chaise in living room area looked good, but not that comfortable.

name: Baymont Inn & Suites Dallas Love Field
title: “Great place and even better staff!! Will Go Back!”
text: We stayed here with our family and absolutely LOVED it! I am very very picky and spent hours researching and picking a hotel for our 5 night stay in Dallas. We were there for the Cowboys opening pre season game, a little drive from this hotel but not bad at all. The remodel is top notch and clean and very professional for hotel only rated at this star level. The breakfast is very nice! Some hot food choices and lots of yummy carb loading breakfast too! All of the staff went above and beyond with superior service, especially Steve! Thank you for a great trip! ***

name: Sheraton Dallas Hotel
title: “Couldn't believe how bad”
text: So many things wrong with the hotel, but in short just poorly managed. Check-in at 3pm is a myth, and my arrival at 5:30pm wasn't even close. They didn't t expect to have a room ready anytime, and finally got a call well after 7, and when I did come back to the hotel, crappy service. They did offer free Internet, which I wasn't asking, and next time they actually should provide a code to access it. When I got to the room, I don't think it was cleaned, and clearly obviously missed some trash and a half drunken water bottle on one of the tables in plain view within the bedroom. The bathroom toilet roll holder was off the wall, and stayed like that for the 3 nights I stayed at the hotel. Upside was a very large suite. Downside, it ruined my perception of Sheraton, which I always thought of as higher end hotels, and unfortunately not the first time a bad experience at Sherton, but this filthy poorly run hotel has me considering never using the brand again. I stay at hotels at least 20 nights a year, and clearly this is one I never go back to or recommend. Best thing Sheraton could do is send the whole staff back for re-training, and /or get better managers to relaunch this hotel.

name: Hilton Anatole
title: “Awful outdated hotel”
text:
The experience at this hotel was just awful, I stayed there years ago when it was a Lowes hotel but now its just awful and I am sure the management is to blame , I have written a letter to Hilton.
From parking to check it's obvious that management has no clue, its a busy day at a start of a convention and one poorly trained guy at the desk who never explained our 3 rooms were on the other side of the hotel in a different tower, never explained that they charge 50.00 per day per room to have your money on hold for incidentals..
The atrium rooms are awful, the elevators are hot and the hallways on upper floors have no A/C , my room I had the A/C cranked down but it barely cooled off and the 1980 era beds that are well worn as well as the crummy pillows sure made it an awful experience.
The few remaining places to eat were so crowded and understaffed that I finally gave up and came up to the mini bar for a bar , which of course is always a rip off, the restaurant when we did eat overcooked all of our steaks, made the salad wrong , the manager did make good by replacing the steaks and comping dessert and wine ..
Check out of course was not good as the computers were down and I left my em,ail but still no receipts for the 3 rooms, I have petitioned my association to never use this place again, its just a shame that this hotel is what it is now as in the past it was a great place

name: Renaissance Dallas Hotel
title: “Nicest Staff and Great Renovations”
text:
The very best thing about this recently renovated hotel is the staff. The property is one of the few owned by Marriott and the staff is friendly, professional, and eager to please. I have stayed at this hotel before, but last time the hotel was being renovated and the check-in desk and restaurant were re-located to the second floor. Everything is back in place now and beautifully re-done. On this trip, I knew I was checking into the hotel late on a weeknight and called the day before my arrival to ask Jeff, the Manager-on-Duty, to have the Club Lounge save me a plate of food from the hors d'oeuvres hour on the evening of my arrival; wow, an incredibly delicious pasta dish with shrimp and bacon was waiting for me in the lounge when I arrived! My room was high on the 29th floor with gorgeous views of downtown Dallas. When we looked out the enormous windows, we could see there was even an RV show going on next door at the Market Place with over 450 vehicles on display indoors and outside. We actually visited the show during the weekend and walked over there in just a minute. 
The hotel beds were the super comfy Marriott ones with great linens.The towels in the bathroom, however, were not the glorious, plush Renaissance towels, but merely the plain Marriott towels. I swam in the large rooftop pool each morning and enjoyed doing laps in a pool that was all to myself. The many chaise lounges around the pool are beautiful with super thick cushions. My only disappointment was that it down-poured on two nights, so I wasn't able to swim on those two hot evenings. However, there is a well-equipped fitness room when the weather does not cooperate or for those who like to exercise indoors. One other great feature at the hotel--complimentary washers and dryers! We were traveling for two weeks and these machines were great. Leave it to Marriott to offer such a nice amenity for its guests. 
On the weekday mornings, we had breakfast in the Club Lounge. My only recommendation there is that they add hard boiled eggs and bananas to the food line-up so that a healthy breakfast is offered as an option; they do have scrambled eggs and bacon. Of course, I will be back to the Renaissance on my next trip to Dallas!

name: Baymont Inn & Suites Dallas Love Field
title: “Pleasant surprise!”
text: I thought this was a new hotel, but turns out it was an awesome renovation. Very friendly, professional staff. Clean, comfortable, contemporarily decorated spacious rooms with free hi speed internet. Nicely tucked away location just a few blocks off interstate near a host of restaurants and entertainment options, and minutes from Dallas Love Field. Excellent value for the buck. Check this hotel out!

name: Hyatt Regency Dallas
title: “Huge Hotel in a Good Location”
text:
This is a typical monster hotel that caters to conventions and business travellers. Overall not a lot to complain about. Here are the pros and cons:
Pros:
-Big hotel with lots a amenties and entertainment
-Nicely appointed rooms with very comfortable beds
-Good location in Dallas' west end near Deally Plaza
Con
-Have to walk under a bridge that is infested with birds and bats to get to the West End district
I read a few reviews that complained about noise. My room (12th floor) looked over the train tracks and I never heard a thing.

name: Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs Resort
title: “Hilton consistently disappoints in Phoenix”
text:
I am a Hilton Honors member and a fan of the chain for the most part. However this is my third stay at a Hilton property in Phoenix and it was as disappointing as the other two. The Tapatio Cliffs resort is an old property, and while we heard that it is being updated we certainly didn't see that. Hilton goofed up our reservations which we had made a month in advance and as a result upgraded us to the Presidential Suite in the old part of the hotel, as opposed to the new part that we specifically requested. The image that a presidential suite conjures up is usually plush -- this was very far from that. The suite, bed, bath - the whole suite - were very dated and not special at all. Light switches falling off, dilapidated paint and poor air conditioning were features.
Parking was at a premium with limited space. The small and sharp rocks that make up the landscape nicely grated my son's leg into cheese. Room service was way overpriced and the server had to make three trips to get it right. On both of the times we ordered - shame on us for trying twice.
The resort pool - while nice and clean - wasn't special enough to make us go back there again. The one bright spot was the person that checked us in; despite the reservation snafu he was professional, personable and very customer oriented.
I remain a Hilton fan, but will avoid the Tapatio (and the Squaw Peak and airport Hilton). Best of luck to any other traveler.

name: Sheraton Dallas Hotel
title: “I'll try not to stay here again”
text:
Only a single elevator was working in the center tower to floors 29 and higher. I never saw anybody trying to fix it.
Breakfast food was probably the worst I've had in a while.
The location has absolutely nothing around it, but is close to a lot of businesses - so don't stay here for fun travel.
The valet and entrance staff were very polite and gracious. The reservation staff were snooty, slow and not particularly friendly. They need to take customer service lessons from the valets.
Rooms are OK. No showergel was supplied, which given TSA requirements means having to buy it when on a long stay. TV was HD, but only had about 5 HD channels.
Fitness room is nice, but pool is surrounded by tall buildings, although it does get sun for most of the day.
Overall, I'd rather walk to business meetings and stay somewhere better.

name: Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs Resort
title: “Nice stay - dated property”
text:
I was there for two nights on business. Nice hotel, but somewhat dated. Property is very sprawling. 
My room was sort of old-style Embassy Suites with a small bedroom, small living room, separated by bathroom and sink area. Funiture and carpets were showing their age.
I had a first floor room and I was unable to get a cellphone signal (AT&T is my carrier). Since I was there on business - not having cellphone service in my room was a major inconvience. To much concrete in the walls I guess. 
Pools are small and dominated by kids.

name: Hyatt Regency Dallas
title: “Very Nice Stay - Great View”
text: I stayed here the night of Nov 3rd. 19th Floor, GREAT VIEW of Downtown. I had read reviews that complained about the trains going by, on the 19th floor it was a non issue. Everyone was friendly, checkin and checkout were very smooth. Great breakfast buffet at the Centennial Cafe on sunday morning(I Suggest the Southwestern Eggs Benedict). Overall an excellent stay and I will be going back.

name: Americas Best Value Inn - Downtown Phoenix
title: “STAY HERE! Trust me.”
text: The rooms were really cute and obviously newly remodeled, very clean and well worth the reasonable cost!!!!! The beds were really comfy and very clean. The desk staff was very friendly and helpful .We stayed for an event at Chase field, and it was within walking distance. I will stay there again, without a doubt.

name: JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort & Spa Phoenix
title: “Fun in the sun, relaxing oasis!”
text: Our visit 5 years ago and I want to go back soon. The kids rode bides my husband golfed and I walked and enjoyed the spa treatments. Very nice surrounfing neighborhoods. Beautiful area if you like the desert.

name: Rosewood Mansion on Turtle Creek
title: “Hobo in the Palace ....”
text: Nice! What can you say but the service was excellent, everyone was super-friendly, and don't miss the cocktail show from the Rosewood Mansion bar seat. Think clubby decor and heritage drinks from the 1930s and ’40s. Food was a bit steep in price but worth every expensive, precious little bite, especially the mini burgers, smoked short rib tacos, and ceviche. Definitely would return as this felt like 'home' even if we were not as dressed up as our Mansion cohorts. Tip: Go to the Mansion bar at happy hour and have the bartender make you one of his custom liquid specials. Totally worth it.

name: Rosewood Mansion on Turtle Creek
title: “Great relaxing girls' weekend”
text:
I'm originally from Dallas, so have experienced The Mansion many times over the years. This last time I was about to leave the country for work for 5 months, and stayed for a girls' weekend with my best friend. 
We were met with welcoming grace and friendliness which is the true Texas spirit sometimes absent from people in Dallas. The valet was friendly as was our bellhop who showed us to our room and showed us all the features.
We were upgraded to a suite with an additional bathroom and living area which is something I always appreciate--if the better room is just sitting there empty, why not give an upgrade?
My friend and i enjoyed all day out by the pool with some of the greatest margaritas I've had in a long time.
We then met other friends for dinner and wine at the bar while enjoying live entertainment but unfortunately was not my favorite Mansion entertainer, Hunter Sullivan. Just going to one of Hunter's shows is worth a stay at the Mansion if you are into the old charm of Sinatra days. He's not a cheesey Sinatra impersonator but a talented charmer himself. 
The dishes are great. If you just want to have cocktails or wine while watching the show there are great snacks such as my favorite truffle fries or an amazing foie gras. I've had dinner here too which has never disappointed. And the wine list is extensive, a book, and the sommelier is great as well, making wonderful choices each time I've described what I'd like--I had an amazing white Chateauneuf du Pape here last year that I can't forget!
Amazing all around, with friendly staff, the Mansion remains one of my favorite places to stay.

name: Budget Lodge Downtown Phoenix
title: “Great Value”
text: The Lodge is located in the old Downtown of Phoenix- Theater's and Restaurants, Nightlife and even the Tramway is in walking distance. The Room was very clean and quiet. A very warm welcome from the owner, who realy cares for his guests. Just stayed two nights- next Time again!

name: Budget Lodge Downtown Phoenix
title: “Excellent Indeed”
text: Great location, minutes away from the Orpheum Theater. Excellent service, good wireless internet, quiet and clean, looks much better than the pictures online.

name: Hotel Palomar Dallas - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Posh rooms for a great price”
text: I recently stayed at the Palomar Dallas at the recommendation of a business colleague. It was beautiful, clean, modern, and comfortable. There were plenty of towels and a nice assortment in the minibar. Kimpton in touch members receive free Internet so sign up before you go! There is a nice little fitness center in the property. I did order room service one morning and it was verygood and not ridiculously expensive. Mockingbird station is across the street and there are several ships and a Starbucks. Hotel staff was extremely courteous. I would certainly stay here again.

name: Americas Best Value Inn - Downtown Phoenix
title: “great for the value”
text: The couple there were very nice. They up graded me to a king size bed. the room was nice and clean with no bugs. Flat screen TV. The breakfast was lacking though. Bananas, apples, juice and a few packaged danishes and coffee. There is a McDonalds two blocks away in plain view of the hotel. I would stay there again if I went back to Pheonix it is about 7-8 blocks from the convention center and their free shuttle is great.........

name: Rosewood Mansion on Turtle Creek
title: “I had the pleasure of staying at the...”
text: I had the pleasure of staying at the Mansion on Turtle creek this august and to my suprise it was during restaurant week. I managed to get a reservation in the very well remodeled new dinning room, luxury and service everywhere the room was alive with excitement. We had the three course menu with an amazing water melon salad and a slightly less amazing squash soup. Main course was a crawfish stuffed chicken thigh accompanied by a warm salad of potatos spinach and tomato and the sauce.. to die for. She had a corn and spinach ravioli on a crawfish red sauce, which tasted 100% better then it sounds. Deserts were equally impressive and of all the restaurant week establishments I've been, this is my top choice. I will certainly be coming back for dinner. As for the chef Bruno Davaillon, love the accent, he couldn't be a nicer gentlemen. We thank the Mansion for making this night unforgettable.

name: Rosewood Mansion on Turtle Creek
title: “TOP CITY HOTEL IN DALLAS”
text:
Stayed 3 nights as a stopover. 
All the positive of the other reviewers is correct.
What was negative to our opinion.
Airco is very noisy and turning it off during the night was not on option. Room was very warm all time. Opening the window at night was not a good idea neither due to the heavy noise of all the surrounding aircos on the roofs of the other buildings 
Breakfast a la carte is very expensive ( 70 to 100 dollar for two persons!) OK i want to pay this amount for a lavish buffet with lot's of choise but this wasn't the case.
Pool is quite small and pool area is also quite noisy of all the surrounding airco's and vans who deliver at the back of the hotel.

name: Rosewood Mansion on Turtle Creek
title: “Perfect!”
text: My husband and I stayed here for the first night of our honeymoon. Everything was perfect --the room, the food, the service, the atmosphere.

name: Hilton Anatole
title: “Nice, upscale business hotel”
text: Stayed three nights for business meeting. Our room was in the tower. Very spacious room with two double beds. Bathroom was large with two sinks and plenty of countertop and storage. Small coffee maker, fridge and safe in room. Large closet. Parking was free with our meeting but it looks like they normally charge $17/night for self-park. Short drive or taxi ride to downtown Dallas with many restaurants to choose from. Our favorites were Trulock's for nice dinner and Sonny Bryan's on Inwood for BBQ lunch. We paid $18 extra a night for access to executive lounge on 25th floor. Nice quiet spot for continental breakfast in morning and snacks in the afternoon.

name: W Dallas Victory Hotel
title: “Skip This Place”
text:
When in Dallas (for business) I always stay at the Grand Hyatt at the Airport (one of my favorite hotels to date - don't laugh - it is a first rate hotel and perfect for business travelers). However, I thought I would try this place since it is fairly new. What a waste of time and money. Wish I would have read the not so great reviews prior to my stay - they were all spot on! 
First, location is totally awkward. Second, the place is run by a completely amateur staff. Young kids have been clearly hired for their alleged "hipness" but the simple things - directions, printing boarding pass, check-in - seemed a bit beyond this crew's capabilities. Conceriege seemed totally perplexed that we were asking for help. As one previous reviewer said, this place is trying way too hard to be hip and cool and in doing so, it is actually just quite humorous to see all these people taking themselves so seriously as they pretend to know how to work in a hotel.
Ghost Bar is OK but no real views to speak of. Room layout, as one previous reviewer indicated, is completely odd. Good luck finding electrical outlets for a hair dryer - none in the "bathroom" area. Hint - look behind the LG flat screen TV. Also, for such a new hotel, I was shocked at how run down it appears to be already. Furniture looks like they picked it up at a Wal-Mart clearance sale. Its all nicked and cheaply made and doesn't at all fit with decor. Rugs in halls and rooms are already worn. 
Take a pass on this place. Check out the Grand Hyatt at the airport instead - you won't be disappointed!

name: Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs Resort
title: “Great Girls Getaway”
text:
I spent a long weekend in March at the Pointe Hilton Tapatio with two former college roommates, and the hotel was perfect for us. After straightening out a mishap at check-in (we opened the door to our room to find it was already occupied), we got an even better room. The double room with the sleeper sofa worked great for us. The room seemed to have been recently redecorated and although there were a few signs of wear, everthing was fresh and clean.
The grounds are pretty, with different buildings set into the cliffs across the property. We found the staff to be friendly and very accommodating. We loved that they have an adult pool, and spent time by it in the evening when we wanted to relax and talk without any screaming and splashing in the background. We would have liked to try the bar & restaurant at the top of the property, but there were special events going on there each night so we didn't have that opportunity. 
We would certainly stay here again if we return to the Phoenix area!

name: Omni Dallas Hotel
title: “Great hotel”
text: This is a hotel that you just cant go wrong with. The rooms and views are wonderful. Staff is great

name: Adolphus Hotel
title: “Unique and lovely historical hotel with all the amenities”
text:
Stayed at the Adolphus for a professional conference. Without exception all staff extremely friendly and helpful. The lobby areas are sort of "old world" elegant. Lovely large rooms, and the best hotel bed I have ever slept in. In-hotel restaurants are great, and the conference food was excellent.
Within walking distance to other good restaurants and light rail. My association is very particular about where our conferences are held, and I can see why they chose the Adolphus.

name: Budget Lodge Downtown Phoenix
title: “Quiet and Peaceful - Excellent value for money”
text: I stayed at the Budget Lodge Phoenix for two nights in October while attending the PE exam at the Phoenix Convention Centre. Nice room, very spacious with microwave, refrigerator, iron board, wi-fi. I got roadside room.To my surpirse its very quiet and peaceful...I didnt hear any traffic noise.Room was clean and definately a good value for the money.

name: Sheraton Crescent Hotel
title: “Barely okay.”
text: The front desk staff is polite and helpful. My club level room looks dated but clean. There is no refrigerator or safe in the room. Maintenance very quickly repairs the broken lamp. The crescent shape of the hotel is perfect for echoing the sounds all night long from the freeway located across the street. Make sure you do not select a room facing the freeway. The hotel restaurant burns my son's hamburger. This is how I discover that the restaurant manager is also my waiter. If you have patience, low expectations, and want to save a little money, this may be the right hotel for you.

name: Drury Inn & Suites Happy Valley
title: “Getaway”
text: We decided to stay here on a whim after going on a private plane flying lesson. The room was beautiful and the staff attentive. Will definitely try it again if we find ourselves in those neck of the woods again.

name: Sheraton Dallas Hotel
title: “"Truly Preferred Guest"”
text: I just spent a couple of days with my business group on our last trip prior to the holidays, and we were at the desk the day prior to checking out. I wanted to make sure that my SPG number was on my reservation and to ensure that I had a late checkout as my flight was later in the afternoon. Lavaughn informed me that I was a Gold member and proceeded to inform the others in my group about the benefits of the SPG program. I was unaware even though I have been an SPG member for quite sometime of all of the brands under the Starwood umbrella. I have not been using my number at my stays at the Aloft, and the Four Points. He not only signed my colleagues up for the SPG program but gave me the number and informed me that those prior stays I would still get credit for all while checking all five of us out at the same time. I enjoyed our stay and it was apparant that he enjoyed what he did. I also had a great experience with Shannell who operated the phones during my stay she was polite always courteous and professional. It was truly a good stay to end our travel year.

name: Sheraton Dallas Hotel
title: “Fast and friendly check-in”
text: I checked in November 30th, 2011. As I waited in line, Matthew Jones, a hotel receptionist, came over and told me he would check me into my room. I was thrilled to get to another line only to read a sign on the counter that said "you are a preferred customer". I kidded Matthew about the sign and it was a great dialogue that went between he and I and my friends. I appreciate how comfortable he made us feel at such a beautiful hotel. I have give Matthew a gold star for professionalism. What an asset he is to the Sheraton.

name: JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort & Spa Phoenix
title: “Great hotel - do not deal with Alexander at reception”
text:
Beautiful hotel, great grounds, excellent pools and service outstanding in all restaurants/pool. We stayed in one of the suites which was a decent sized room with great flow to the room. Our only issue was the noise of the road nearby however, by the second night, it was obsolete! 
At all times we encountered friendly, courteous staff with the exception of Alexander at front reception. He is not working in the right field. He was unfriendly, unhelpful and even lied to us a few times. When we requested a late checkout, he lied to us again (despite being Elite members) and when he walked away, we asked Brian who gladly accomodated our late check out. Truly, not acceptable for this standard of hotel, for elite members or for any clients paying the fees/rate of this hotel. 
Overall, great location, lots to do and definitely recommend for families with young kids.

name: Omni Dallas Hotel
title: “Top notch, all around!”
text: The new Omni Hotel & Convention Center in downtown Dallas, Texas lives up to the hype. Stayed here as part of a group travel plan and the staff were all extremely accommodating. The room (Deluxe King) was fantastic, bed & shower especially. What I also can't say enough about are the in hotel restaurants. You must visit Texas Spice during your stay, and the Owner's Bar is a first class sports bar. Loved every minute and will stay here from now on when I visit Dallas.

name: Sheraton Dallas Hotel
title: “Great place for a conference~!”
text: This was my first stay at the Dallas Sheraton, and I really enjoyed it! The room was very clean and updated and almost everyone there was very helpful! The only change that we had to make was because our first room was on the 19th floor and both my daughter and I have some difficulty with heights! They changed us quickly and without any fuss! Would stay there again.

name: JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort & Spa Phoenix
title: “Really Wanted To Love This Resort”
text: On first glance this resort has everything you would want. Beautiful street appeal, inviting lobby, wonderful pools and "lazy river" and appealing guest rooms. After a few days we began to question the lack of an acceptable "turn down" service, quality of bedding (especially the pillows) and overall cleanliness of our room. Sheets were stained and not changed regularly. Be sure to ask for rooms facing the pools and golf course for the better views.

name: SpringHill Suites Jacksonville Airport
title: “Great location and property”
text:
Definately a nice , clean property. Close to both JaxPort and Airport......but NOT noisy.
I only stayed one night before going on a cruise. Was perfect for this.
However, I think the best part of the stay was the couertsy of the staff. Alissa at Front desk was exceptional, also the young lady on the night shift was. They went out of their way to welcome and make a brief stay plesant. Housekeeping was attentive also. Morning breakfast attendant was attentive also.
Obviously they contract with "GoAirport" for shuttle service to JaxPort and airport, along with their own shuttle.
Fare was $20pp roundtrip to JaxPort and I could leave my vehicle at hotel while gone. Great benefit. Better deal than parking at Port. Shuttle was timely as hotel assured me.
Overall the hotel was clean and well maintained even down to the parking lot. Saw the pool but did not use.
I believe the professionalism of the staff is a reflection of the GM (Melissa Duncan), as I did speak with her regarding a nice property and excellant staff.
Definatelyy would stay here again , even without using Marriott points. Good reflection on the brand.

name: Omni Dallas Hotel
title: “Fabulous Hotel!”
text:
We stayed at the Omni for opening weekend. The decor and openness of the hotel is very dramatic. Beautiful Dallas-themed photographs and unique, but very comfortable, furnishings. We enjoyed the sports bar with more than 70 TV screens! The breakfast buffet in Texas Spice was excellent with lots of choices. We loved the rooftop hot tub at night, surrounded by the lights of downtown Dallas. We also warmed up next to the rooftop firepit. 
Room accommodations were excellent. The Omni is located in the heart of downtown Dallas, but we never needed to leave the hotel.

name: Wingate by Wyndham Jacksonville / Mayo Clinic Area
title: “Being on the 5th floor did require a long wait for the hot...”
text: Being on the 5th floor did require a long wait for the hot water in both the bathroom sink and shower to start flowing; approximately 1 minute of running water until the temperature was warm enough to bathe. That would amount to quite a bit of wasted water over a year if all the rooms had the same issue.

name: Red Roof Inn - Southpoint
title: “Good value for the money.”
text: Friendly staff and easy check-in. Rooms were clean. A nice no frills hotel.

name: SpringHill Suites Jacksonville Airport
title: “Great property”
text: The room is very comfortable and clean. It had everything we needed. We only stayed 1 night as we were passing through, and I used reward points so I can not comment on value. But we would stay there again. The breakfast was good for free, but they could splurge on a new toaster because the one they have took 10 minutes and had still not browned my english muffin.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Beach Boulevard/Mayo Clinic Area
title: “Best Service During Family Crisis”
text: Due to a medical crisis involving a military family member being treated at the Mayo Clinic Hospital, the USO gave our family vouchers for complimentary rooms at this hotel. I can not say enough about Andre and Joshnae, and forgive me if I can't remember the names of the other staff at the desk. This was a very trying time for our family and while we were there, our loved one passed away. We were asked repeatedly if there was anything more that they could do to help us during our stay there at such an emotional time. The hotel was spotless! The renovations mentioned in earlier reviews appear to have been completed as the decor is very up to date. Our room was on the second floor, and although near the elevator, it was very quiet--no noise from other rooms, the hallway, or parking lot. The location was wonderful; very close to the hospital and there is a wide variety of restaurants right on Beach Blvd., with many right across the street. If I ever return to Jacksonville under happier circumstances I will without hesitation stay here again.

name: JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort & Spa Phoenix
title: “Five Diamond Resort”
text: JW Marriott, Desert Ridge, Phoenix is a 5-Diamond Resort in the true sense of the word. We recently stayed for 4 short nights while attending the Youth Soccer Regional Tournaments at the Reach 11 Sports Complex (about 3 miles from the hotel). The weather was great but so was the golf at both of the resorts Wildfire GC Faldo & Palmer courses. Add to this our daughters G98 ODP Team won the championship for the State of Washington only added to a great weekend. Hint about the green fees - book your tee times on GolfNow website, you'll save 50% or more on most of the courses in Phoenix including the Wildfire Courses at this resort.

name: Red Roof Inn - Southpoint
title: “the best service ever”
text: This has been the best hotel I have stayed at ever. The nicest staff you could ever meet!

name: The Joule, Dallas
title: “WOW”
text: This property is amazing and beautiful. The hotel staff is very hospitable and very happy. The rooms are gorgeous. When you walk into the room you have a moment of delightful surprise on how detailed and high end the finish out is in the rooms. The food from Charlie Palmer is delicious. We also went to PM to celebrate my husbands birthday and the service there was excellent and the dj was fabulous. I just wanted to dance all night. Then the next day we visited the pool area which was very unique, the pool over extends the building so when you are in the pool at the end of it you are on top of main st in the middle of downtown Dallas so the view was phenomenal. I have been to a lot of the hotel properties in Dallas and the Hotel Joule is my far the most luxurious, plush and trendy of them all.

name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Jacksonville - Blount Island
title: “Best place to stay before a cruise”
text: Nice stay before our cruise leaving from Jacksonville port. This hotel is good for this purpose mostly. If you are going to visit the beach, you are decently far away from the beach. The best part about this was the hot breakfast in the morning, buffet style that is free. Good to eat free when you have a family of five! No other hotels are near as close to the port.

name: Wingate by Wyndham Jacksonville / Mayo Clinic Area
title: “Family Trip”
text: Everything was great except that our room was not cleaned when we left for the day and did not find out until we returned that night.

name: The Joule, Dallas
title: “Service above and beyond”
text: The staff at the Joule went out of their way to make a getaway very special for a friend recovering from breast cancer surgery. The small personal touches went a long way to make it a memorable stay. Thank you for all your kindnesses.

name: SpringHill Suites Jacksonville Airport
title: “great idea”
text: Stayed at this Springhill property as part of a "stay and park" option for a recent trip to Texas. Extremely clean and comfortable hotel with breakfast; shuttle also provided to/from airport. This hotel is conveniently located to a large shopping area and several restaurants. For $99, I received 14 days of parking and a great hotel stay. This worked well for me as I was going to need to park my car in a lot anyway for 2 weeks, which would've cost a minimum of $60. So by paying an extra $40, I had a leisurely pre-trip stay and shuttle to the airport. I would definitely consider this option in the future...

name: The Joule, Dallas
title: “Super Modern - Great Location + Pm Lounge & Charlie Palmer”
text: This is one of our favorite hotels in Dallas for our Staycation weekends, its literally a hotel you never have to live and can live without a car for a weekend. Which in Dallas going without a car for a weekend is a rarity. You can walk next door to iron cactus for bfast and lunch, then eat dinner at the ultra swanky Charlie Palmer. You can finish the night off by going to the basement to the PM lounge for a night cap or walk a few blocks to half a dozen other clubs.

name: SpringHill Suites Jacksonville Airport
title: “Nice hotel but.....”
text: Great hotel that is close to airport with a free shuttle. Free breakfast, clean and affordable but the walls are so thin. I could hear casual conversations next door through the night. I had an early morning flight and went to bed early. My neighbors were up until early morning hours. Beware if you are a light sleeper.

name: Sheraton Crescent Hotel
title: “The Best Customer Service and Event Venue I Have Experienced”
text:
I did an event at this hotel at the end of Nov and had an usually high amount of feedback from our guests on the food that was served and the hotel itself. I myself was completely satisfied with the service and working with the events and catering staff was great.
Recently I needed a very last minute event venue and called the Sheraton up a few days before our event. They totally took care of us and were completely accommodating. They are a total pleasure to work with and are always very bright and friendly.
The day of the event I was running around and was doing some last minute things. At one point I went to get some coffee and tea from some special guests, went to the cafe off the lobby and saw that it was closed. I turn around and there was already someone standing there asking what help I needed and was onto it in an instant. The Food and Beverage Manager opened up the cafe, made all of the coffee/tea, offered to help take it to the meeting room and was completely service-oriented and I must say I was pretty impressed. Later he saw me rushing through the lobby (I must have looked a bit stressed) and caught up with me just to ask if I needed something.
In dealing with many hotel staff and representatives in the past its a rare thing when you feel like a friend rather than one of the of countless "clients" they deal with day in and day out. 
This hotel is definitely a venue I will work with in the future. Also, the Sheraton is one of my favorite hotel chains to stay in so I also highly recommended them.

name: Wingate by Wyndham Jacksonville / Mayo Clinic Area
title: “You are not recognizing my rewards partnership”
text: Everytime I book this hotel (which has been 4 times this year alone), I do not get credited with my rewards points or recognized as a reward member. This time they gave me my rewards number which does not look like the number I remember receiving when we signed up. This is very frustrating.

name: Comfort Suites Jacksonville I-295
title: “AFJROTC trip”
text:
In my 28 yrs active duty and 8 years teaching AFJROTC I have never had the pleasure of staying in such a well managed, well ran, clean, efficient, friendly, with professional and genuine hospitality in all my travels. If you are ever in the Jax area and need a place to stay for you, your family, or business org -- staying here is must! The breakfast featured the normal cereals, rolls, bagels, etc but their buffet included real scrambled eggs. I had 4 adults and 31 high school kids traveling with me and every one agreed with me it was the best place we/they had stayed. The staff could not have been more organized or helpful. Check in for that many people took less than 5 minutes. They put us all on the same floor which meant chaperoning was a snap. I left my cell phone recharger in the room. The next mailing day it was in the mail along with a students who also forgot his. If I sound over enthusiastic about this Comfort Inn I don't mean to be. I want to sound as the write up suggest -- overwhelmed! The GM , Mr. Bill Flor, showed for breakfast to introduce himself and thank us for using his Comfort Inn. That too is a first!
Enough of my rambling.....STAY HERE! NUFF SAID!

name: Microtel Inn & Suites by Wyndham Jacksonville Airport
title: “Helpful”
text: I have found your attendant, Derrek to be very helpful and prompt. I needed to work on my laptop and I shared with Derreck that I could not use the internet. He promptly reset the system and I was able to complete my work, he was a lifesaver.

name: Comfort Suites Jacksonville I-295
title: “Great overnight stay”
text: This hotel was great. the staff was extra friendly from beginning to end. It started with a phone call for directions. we were just passing through and i picked this hotel to stay 1 night and then continue on the our way to orlando. The bed was comfortable and breakfast was great. I could not have picked a better place to stay the night. The kids really enjoyed the covered pool.

name: Sheraton Crescent Hotel
title: “Great Service - Otherwise, not that impressed!”
text: Spent a week at this Sheraton on business and if you judged the place by the exterior and lobby, you'd think you're about to step into a 5-star resort. The grounds are very well kept and free parking is plus. Lobby is very inviting with an infinity-style waterfall and huge courtyard. You can tell the bar and restaurant areas were upgraded and also great service. Customer service here is as good as I've experienced at any Sheraton. My excitement about this place turns south when I enter my room. While it was a pretty nice size with flat=screen TV and sitting area, it's way outdated. Furniture, wall paper, carpet, and especially the bathrooms simply need a makeover. The bed was very comfortable, however, and AC worked very well (a must in Phoenix). Overall, it felt like I was staying in a 4 star hotel (lobby, bar, restaurant, exterior appearance) with 2 star accommodations (rooms and conference areas). Location is not the best either. If you don't eat at the restaurant in the hotel, your lunch options are few (and require a trip across very busy 4-lane traffic - at your own risk). However, you're only about 20 minutes from Scottsdale which is where you'll find the best of shopping, restaurants, and friendly people. If back in the Phoenix area, I'd probably stay at a property closer to Scottsdale. Not a bad hotel and the staff was excellent, but could be a lot better.

name: Wingate by Wyndham Jacksonville / Mayo Clinic Area
title: “Mayo Clinic Hotel”
text: This hotel is best for visitors to the Mayo Clinic. The hotel is dog friendly for the dogs being trained at Mayo. As a result, the first room we were assigned had an extremely heavy smell of cleaning solution. We were told the hotel was full, but the clerk was very accomodating and changed our room resulting in a pleasant stay.

name: Sheraton Crescent Hotel
title: “It was a comfortable, relaxing stay, would recommend highly.”
text:
My most recent stay in Sept 09 was very pleasant. Accommodations and availabilty to staff was the best. I look forward to returning again in Sept 2010. Thanks for all your help.
 Mike Childers

name: Sheraton Crescent Hotel
title: “great hotel”
text:
Must say, I was a little concerned after seeing recent post from wedding party guest (although a careful read of the website will indicate that the spa is offsite).
When we checked in, the staff was great -even helped print out my airline boarding pass. Our room was fantastic - HUGE TV and comfy bed. The view (from 7th floor) was great and overlooking pool/waterslide.
As mentioned previously, the cabana was not open and I thought the cabana wasn't either but then I saw kids go over and as soon as the gate opened, the water started flowing and they had a great time. So, maybe it's motion sensitive?
Also, on club level the evening snacks and morning "continental" -more like full- breakfast were GREAT!

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Jacksonville - Baymeadows
title: “Nice okay place”
text: I enjoyed my executive Suite stay at this hotel. Clean, conveniently located close to freeway, friendly staff. I didn't like seeing dirty linen on the walkway to my room. I however reported it and it was quickly removed. Breakfast buffet was great with quite a selection of choices. If you are flying in late, the restaurant closes @ 10.30pm/11pm for room service and the entire neighborhood restaurants are also closed by 11PM..so eat before your late arrival. Clean Gym too..

name: Hampton Inn Jacksonville - I-95 South
title: “Easy on off of I95”
text: Great rates for a Hampton Inn. Rooms clean, staff helpful, good breakfast . Have stayed three different times on my trips up and down I95 and find I look forward to being able to stay here because quality is great price is moderate.

name: La Quinta Inn Jacksonville Baymeadows
title: “stayed for 4 nights”
text: This is a decent place to stay for several nights. It is an older property with all outside rooms. Housecleaning could pay alittle more attention to detail. Desk attendants were exceptional. No restaurant, but morning quick start breakfast was adequate with fresh fruit, but no waffle station.

name: Howard Johnson Inn and Suites Jacksonville
title: “Excellent Customer Service”
text: Jacob & Virginia are simply outstanding. Whatever issues arose, they took care of beautifully. This involved small things from the rooms missing pens, to big things like lacking solid wireless Internet. I have been traveling there on business for 3 months.

name: BEST WESTERN Hotel JTB / Southpoint
title: “Perfect”
text: After driving up from the Keys.. We were in dire need for a clean comfortable place to sleep, and we got just that. Comfy bed and a great shower.. Really what more do you need. Contental breakfast was as good as a continental breakfast could be. Coffee was good and hot...def recommend to stay

name: Dolce Hayes Mansion
title: “Fab place for a quiet weekend away”
text:
We arrived here for one night and we fell in love with it straight away we got upgraded to the laurel suite which was fantastic with a huge huge huge tub in it. it had a bit of a musty smell but hey its an old mansion. we got to stay in the main mansion but the regular rooms are in a building next to it. 
The pool was warm and quiet with very few hanging about. only complaint is that the sun loungers are few and far between.
THe gardens are fantastic. the hotel extremely quiet and the staff very friendly we even got a late check out for $0
We will definately be back again this summer

name: BEST WESTERN Hotel JTB / Southpoint
title: “Wonderful stay 3 years in a row!!”
text: We have stayed at this location in January for the last 3 years. Wonderful people, from the check in to the housekeeping staff, to the breakfast and then the check out. We have NEVER been disappointed with anything. We have a dog and they always make ALL of us feel welcome. The grounds are very nice and we always feel safe here. We would recommend this location to friends and family.

name: Hampton Inn Jacksonville - I-95 South
title: “Simply not clean”
text:
At checking in, we were assigned room # 132. We settled and discovered very quickly many food debris between the beds, and obviously unchanged sheets in one bed.
We went back to reception desk and with apologies got room # 116. We went to that room and discovered that very simply it had not been cleaned at all. Towels on the bathroom floor...sheets hanging ...
Return to reception desk and this time we got room # 215, which happened to be OK.
This story tells me of what is probably a lax policy with housekeeping
In my opinion there are much better options nearby, and this is my last time at this hotel.

name: JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort & Spa Phoenix
title: “Great - up until the bill was slipped under the door”
text:
The good:
This is a great hotel. Check-in was fast and efficient, I was upgraded to a junior suite, and the bathroom, bed and pillows were all great. Very nice décor. Excellent housekeeping. Roy’s downstairs has great food, and it was fun seeing the rabbits and ducks wandering around while eating. Pools are nice, and perfect for kids/families. Service was excellent overall. 
The bad:
Nickel and diming. Internet was $12.95/day plus 3 different taxes. But wait, a day isn’t 24 hours. It is until noon. So if you need internet at 11am, you are paying $12.95+ for internet which will expire in an hour. Sleazy! Why can Courtyard by Marriott provide free internet, but the much-more-expensive JW Marriott charge for it? Annoying. Anyway, when I received my bill I was prepared for the internet charges, but there were other surprise charges. Self-parking is $10/day. Plus 3 taxes. They didn’t tell me at check-in about this, and there are no signs in the parking lot indicating that there is a charge. Surprise! And then I also paid $53+ to receive two packages. I had called a month before and been told by the front desk that there was no charge to receive packages. Yet, for the packages which had arrived slightly before my arrival, I paid $53 for them to hold them and then deliver them to me. Despite being told the wrong information by the hotel, they refused to credit back this charge. 
So overall, although I was extremely pleased with the hotel for my entire stay, I was left with a really bad taste once I received the bill. I would therefore likely not stay there again. What a dumb way to lose repeat business!

name: La Quinta Inn Jacksonville Baymeadows
title: “For the price - great value”
text:
Ok. First of all i want to clarify a few things about the negative points people have left on here. Me and my girlfriend are both college students and were looking for somewhere to stay relatively near the beach for as cheap as possible. We paid $35 a night for this hotel, so 3 nights for including tax was $120 between the two of us; great value.
Firstly, i will address some of the things people exaggerated on here. The hotel looks very old, paint faded/peeling on the inside, low ceiling in the bathroom etc. These are bad points if you paid a lot of money for a hotel and want to nitpick, but in reality it changes nothing about staying there.
Secondly, the hotel was VERY clean. No bugs, no stains, and whatever else people had a problem with. My room was perfect, and extremely large too, we were in the king size room and it was one of the biggest hotel rooms i've stayed in. 
Thirdly, and this is the one that really surprised me the most was people complaining it was in a bad area???!!! Did you even stay here?? For everyone who hasn't, the hotel is located just off the interstate in a BUSINESS PARK. As in, the only things around it were 3 other hotels, and a few fast food places. And not to mention these places looked nice and clean AND had a big lake with fountains in the front of it, which also was clean. I expected a bad place, but was absolutely flabbergasted when i saw it. There is no housing, or anything to make the place 'bad'. Ridiculous.
The rest of the hotel itself was pleasant, pool was clean and so was the general lobby area and the staff were friendly, and checking in was a breeze. The breakfast wasn't anything to write home about (get there early or you miss out) but again i want to emphasize i paid $35 DOLLARS A NIGHT!. It had bagels, waffles, cereals, yoghurts etc. No cooked food, but you can toast anything you want. 
Oh and finally the hotel DOES have free wifi, and free parking.
Never had a problem at all with staying here, and you seriously should ignore the ridiculous reviews people have given on here. Yes the hotel is old, but it is CLEAN. And it is certainly NOT in a bad area.
I would stay here again for the price if i ever go back to Jacksonville

name: BEST WESTERN Hotel JTB / Southpoint
title: “A quite, and very clean hotel with at a great value!”
text: We stayed here several days to be close to Mayo clinic (about 15 min.). It was in a good area, and the ocean was maybe 20 min. away. Major shopping areas within about 7miles. I would recommend for any family, or person on a business trip.

name: Howard Johnson Inn and Suites Jacksonville
title: “Absolutely wonderful staff, will definately stay again”
text: Staff was wonderful right from the start, changing rooms for me because of location. Then even more helpful when we encountered a problem with our cruise and the owner personally drove our friend who was unable to travel with us on the cruise back and forth from the port and gave him a room until he was picked up by family . I felt the staff went above and beyond in helping us before and after our cruise. We stayed two nights and slept well both nights. Our vehicle was parked for the duration of our cruise and it was safe and sound upon our return. When we were picked up at the cruise port, we had great conversation with our "friend" (the owner-Rick) who personally picked us up and brought us back to the hotel offering us coffee or anything to make us comfortable. WILL DEFINATELY STAY NEXT CRUISE OUT OF JAX.

name: Howard Johnson Inn and Suites Jacksonville
title: “Excellent customer service”
text: We stayed here the night before our cruise departed Jacksonville becuase they offered shuttle service to the port. We had selected a King suite but when Peter found out we had five in the party he suggested we needed a suite with two doubles and a pull out. He had the room ready in about 15 minutes even though we had changed rooms. Peter and his father shuttled us (11 total) to the port in two vehicles so we would not be cramped. They were just the nicest folks and we enjoyed chatting on the way. They were there to pick us up on the return even though we were near the last to depart the ship so they had to wait a while. We will definetely saty with them again if we are in Jacksonville!

name: Wyndham Jacksonville Riverwalk
title: “Great hotel!”
text:
My boyfriend and I had a great two day getaway at this wonderful hotel last weekend, and I just want everyone to know how much fun we had, how beautiful the hotel is, how great the service is and we can't wait to go back!!!
We especially enjoyed our morning breakfast, with Jay, who makes the best omelettes and Bonnie who made sure we never ran out of coffee!!!

name: Super 8 Jacksonville Central
title: “Fine for the price”
text: Check-in was fast and the clerk even checked my room to be sure there was internet access. (It was - however - poor and I actually connected with the hotel across the street!!). Otherwise the room was clean and the mini-fridge worked well as did the heat (yes, heat!). There is the usual coffee maker, ironing board/iron, & hair dryer available. The breakfast was typical 8 fare - fine with me. Considering the price, I was very happy with the room. DRIVERS BE CAREFUL: - depending on the I-95 SOUTH off ramp you may pass the entrance to the motel. Make a right turn at the next street and go around the block to the entrance/office.

name: JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort & Spa Phoenix
title: “Wide range of experiences - ours was great!”
text: The wide range of experiences detailed here is amazing! After reading through many and relating to a few, I would like to add my 2 cents and strong positive support of the resort. True, the room was no great shakes, but the property was beautiful. True, it is large enough to warrant getting a map, but it wasn't so big that you couldn't get around without one. True, service at restaurants was spotty, but it was great to have so many choices on-site. And if the service was bad, or the food unmemorable, you could always go to the shopping center across the street that has a wide variety of restaurants to choose from. I highly recommend Mimi's Cafe for good food and good prices. A local's favorite, you may have to wait a while to be seated, but it's worth it -- great breakfast. I felt the resort staff was extremely nice and helpful, but restaurant/lounge staff attentiveness was spotty. We went to attend Spring training games (go Mariners!) but were outnumbered by families on Spring Break vacations. Personally, I have no problem with sharing "my resort" with families. On the one hand, it's our bad luck that we're paying premium airfare because it is a very popular travel time for vacationing families, but on the other hand, what a fabulous respite from rainy, dreary March in Seattle. Worth the price of the plane ticket. Our favorite things: for my husband, the fitness center and spa which he visited every morning. First class and never over-crowded. For me, taking long walks in the morning while he was doing his workout. I walked city streets into neighborhoods but the sidewalks were wide and are flat, safe and easily accessible. Did I mention what a fabulous respite this warm March weather was from our cold, wet Seattle March weather? You can't beat it. Other favorite things: drinks on the sofas/club chairs facing the grassy knoll (good sushi btw); Meritage Steak House - not necessarily the best steak I've ever had, but a nice atmosphere; people watching (we also were there during Fight Night and personally saw or heard of many celebrity sightings); warm weather - oh, I already mentioned that. Usually at this point I'd say "you'll really like it" but reading the past reviews, it's clear that people are looking for different things in their vacation stays, so this may not suit the bill for you. I will say, it was perfect and memorable for us. We'll return.

name: Holiday Inn Jacksonville - I-95 & Baymeadows
title: “Would stay there again if it was Free!!”
text: One of the worst hotels I have ever stayed in.....and our family travels often. Room was dirty, old, and stinky. I was afraid to let my toddler touch the floor. Do not stay here with kids. Booked online, they couldn't find my reservation. I could go on for hours, but I believe I have said enough to give a good idea.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Jacksonville - Baymeadows
title: “Good enough for a short business trip”
text:
Pros:
1. Big room - the bedroom was separate from the living room. 
2. Great breakfast with eggs, sausages, hotcake, made to order omelette and they had Manager's cocktails but I never had the chance to try it though.
3. Helpful Front desk 
Cons:
1. They ran out of toothpaste on my 2nd day and was advised just to buy from the gift shop.
2. There is a gap in the curtains beside the door so people walking the corridors can see you from outside. i think this is the case for all the rooms because I could see the inside of the other rooms when I walk to my room from the elevator. 
3. The fire alarm went off at 4AM because according to the manager the water pressure went down. The manager did send out a letter apologizing.
4. I saw a cockroach walking on the floor going into the plants while having breakfast. 
5. The bed may have bed bugs because I had little bites on my arms towards the end of my stay. 
I will probably look for another hotel when I come visit.

name: Wyndham Jacksonville Riverwalk
title: “Great people, great location, needs some updating”
text:
The Wyndham Riverwalk is in an ideal location. It's very close to excellent restaurants, downtown, and the highway. I came on business, and although everyone I met was nice, and the hotel in general is clean, the place is well overdue for an update.
Check in was easy, however the parking situation is less than ideal. They charged you each day, and the parking lot was a bit of a walk from the entrance.
My bed was comfortable, but that's about it for complements on the room. The bathroom was dingy, many lights didn't work, or flickered when they did. The shower head was poor and the bathtub filled up with water even though it was set to drain. The AC unit kept my room cold, but also kept me up all night. Even though it was set to be on constantly, it turned off, turned down, and made loud clunking noises periodically throughout the night. The housekeepers did a good job cleaning, but even after I left them a note and a tip, they failed to refill my water (you don't want to drink the tap water here).
My TV was a old tube tv and came in fuzzy. I went down to the bar to watch the MNF football game because I couldn't take that TV anymore. It has HBO, but it was spotty at best.
The gym was a bit of a let down, the business center is ok and the pool was small, but they're all there and they work. The breakfast is good and the omelettes are great. The omelette man is very friendly as well. Zach at the bar was very friendly and made some great recommendations for some bar munchies which were also very good. Even if I stayed somewhere else, I'd probably come back for the loaded chips at the bar. 
All in all I'd stay here again if it's the cheapest in the area; however, if something else near by gave me a better deal I'd think about a switch. If this place didn't have such an AWESOME staff it would have been much easier to find another place to stay. A new TV, a coat of paint, and a better AC unit and shower, and this place would have gotten a 5 from me.

name: Red Roof Inn - Jacksonville Airport
title: “Redesigned & Rededicated? Hardly....”
text:
Ever since I stayed at the Red Roof Inn in Ogden, UT (now a Motel 6) several years ago with its new Redesigned & Rededicated renovation, I was hooked on the Red Roof chain for when I needed an inexpensive place to stay. Not a whole lot more money than a Motel 6, but usually a lot better in quality. Their new design made it seem like you were staying in a cool boutique hotel in NYC.
Well, that wasn't the case at all at the Jacksonville, FL airport location. They took an old hotel, put on new bedspreads, slapped some paint on, and called it Redesigned & Rededicated .... NOT!
I tried to sleep in this room for a few hours, but just couldn't, it was so gross. I went back to management and got my money back!
I was traveling from Florida to North Carolina up the I-95, and even though it was in the wee hours of the morning, I couldn't sleep anyway and decided just to keep driving on. I ended up spotting another Red Roof, near the Savannah Airport, in Pooler, GA. It was not Redesigned & Rededicated -- but was infinitely better than the one at JAX. I had a good night's rest.
I was supposed to have stayed at the one on Hilton Head, which is supposed to be a true Redesigned & Rededicated location, but I ended up leaving Orlando too late and just couldn't make the extra time.
My faith in Red Roof is still up there, but I suppose you have to be wary about some of the locations.

name: Candlewood Suites East Merril Road
title: “Nice newer hotel....just needs a few special touches”
text: We were not acknowledged as Priority members, nor given an upgrade, but the room was okay for a short 3-night visit. We stayed in a king bed room, which in this newer hotel was lacking in some furnishings such as somewhere to place our luggage, an end table next to the bed (one was there, we prefer one next to each side of the bed), a separate desk to set up our computers, tables, a couch so both of us could sit down comfortably. There was a flat screen TV, complimentary internet and a small kitchenette with a full size refrigerator. There also was a stationary desk/kitchen table. There's a Publix grocery next door as well as other shopping/restaurants close by. There's only one computer in the lobby, and it was busy the few times we needed to use it for printing..

name: Wingate by Wyndham Jacksonville / Mayo Clinic Area
title: “Good Value, working amenities, clean atmosphere”
text:
Check In:
Fast and convenient. I received a follow-up call the first evening I was to be sure everything was good, that was a nice touch.
The Room:
The microwave and fridge worked well, internet connection was reliable and fast. Beds are not so comfortable and sheets are probably more of what you find at a 2-star accomodation. Good water pressure in the shower and my used towells were replaced with fresh ones every day. The decor is slightly dated and uninspired.
Breakfast:
Here is what is available: fruit, yogurt, waffles, pastries, scrambled eggs, bacon, hash browns, cereal, coffee, and milk. I only had eggs, yogurt and OJ, which were all good enough to get me going.
Fitness/Pool:
There is no thermostat in the gym! I got overheated while working out. But the cardio machines work well and there is a weight machine, as well as a water cooler with towells. I really enjoyed the spa; my only gripe is that the pool area closes at 10pm.
This hotel would be great for families and older travellers, as well as anyone going to the Mayo Clinic. Not great if you're coming to JAX for the beach scene.

name: TownePlace Suites by Marriott Jacksonville Butler Boulevard
