title: “Impressed”
text: Good value - lots of room features for price of regular hotel room. Stayed at this hotel in a studio unit for 2 nights over the 4th of July weekend. It was appeared new, fresh and clean. Appreciated how much storage and thoughtful amenities were packed into a unit barely larger than a normal hotel room without feeling crowded. We had a king bed, sofa bed, flat screen TV, large desk, decent sized kitchenette (with almost full size refig/freezer, sink, dishwasher, 2 burner stove, dishware & cookware) and lots of storage everywhere. The combo closet (accessed from bathroom) / pantry (accessed from kitchen) was very creative. The unit even included a master swtich to turn off all lights at once. Bed was very comfortable. Rate included usual hotel style carb breakfast with make your own waffles, but also had whole fruit and yogurts. Hotel is in a guiet area right off I-95 and 7 minutes East of UNF and St. John Town Center (tons of shopping & resturants). Beach is 15-20 minutes straight East on Butler Blvd.

name: Residence Inn Jacksonville Airport
title: “Family Cruzin”
text:
We stayed overnight prior to our family cruz with Carnival. We had family from New York, Virginia and Nebraska meet at the Rez Inn - we all stay in a very nicely appointed 2 bedroom suite. The trip to the cruise port is roughly a 20 minute leasurely drive from the Inn. You could not beat the accomidations for the price. I wish we would of had more time to enjoy everything the Inn had to offer. 
There are plenty of places to eat in the area.

name: Crowne Plaza Jacksonville Airport Hotel
title: “Beautiful Place to Stay”
text: Mom and I stayed for one night before flying out; what a fabulous experience. The staff was awesome, Thanks Corine :) ~~ the room was perfect, lots of space, a great view of the water fountain, very clean, great bathroom. Overall, it was a great stay. As stated no free breakfeast, but the Cinnamon Swirl French Toast is to die for.....

name: Courtyard by Marriott Jacksonville Airport/Northeast
title: “Good Hotel”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for one night on January 25, 2008. The hotel itself was nice and clean. The staff was very nice and cordial. I would stay at this hotel again if I were to visit Jacksonville.
The only negative I have about the hotel is the shuttle from the airport took forever. This shuttle does service several other Marriott hotels right near the Courtyard so if you don't catch it right when you get off the plane you might wait 30 mins or more. We waited in the cold for a long time a decided to catch a taxi to the hotel. The taxi fare was right under $9.00 for the 6 minute ride.

name: Wyndham Jacksonville Riverwalk
title: “Our Stay”
text: The staff was warm and friendly when we arrived; Accommodations had very comfy sheets and pillows and we had a great experience overall

name: La Quinta Inn Jacksonville Airport North
title: “voldoet, maar kan beter...”
text: Goede bedden, warm water, geen thee, geen mineraalwater, alleen oploskoffie en een strijkijzer, geen gordijnen die het zicht vanaf de galerij wegnemen (alleen maar nepstrookjes en vitrage). Redelijk uitgebreid ontbijt buffet op wiebelige kleine tafeltjes. voldoet redelijk.

name: Crowne Plaza Jacksonville Airport Hotel
title: “Very nice hotel...love it here”
text: We were just traveling through and had stayed here before. We're Platinum Priority members and were upgraded on our arrival. The room was nice and comfortable. The staff was friendly and we'll stay here again, I'm sure.

name: Comfort Suites Airport
title: “Overall good experience”
text:
Comfortable and roomy space with hide-a-bed. The shuttle service was great to/from airport as well as to/from the cruise ship terminal. Front desk was kind and helpful. Price was great. Free breakfast seemed to have it all (eggs, waffle, cereal, biscuit/gravy, fruit, etc.) The only thing I didn't like was the smell in my room. 
Pros: price, airport shuttle, cruise terminal shuttle, continental breakfast, hospitality, room service
Con: smell in our room. I went to another room and it smelled just fine.

name: Hyatt Regency Jacksonville Riverfront
title: “Excellent View”
text: Just about everything was excellent at this facility! The only downside was the Regency Club is closed, but they add 2,500 points to your Gold Passport account as consideration for your inconvenience during the remodel. Valet parking had staff available - no wait, and this was with the Jacksonville Hospital folks pouring out the doors. Reception was immediate, friendly and while she (Monica) had no knowledge of an AARP promotion I was using she did not hesitate to call her supervisor for clarification. The 17th floor room had an excellent view of the river, and the Jacksonville Jags owner parks his ride (yacht) directly in front of the hotel. 19th floor complimentary facilities include a rooftop pool with plenty of chaises, chairs, and tables. They also have a "health club" type workout room with spa. While The Club is closed complimentary breakfast at the ground floor restaurant is included for Diamond members. As I am walking out in the morning Monica greets me by name. She works the evening shift, grabs some shut eye, and working the Sunday day shift remembers the names of folks she checked in Saturday night. Nice ending to a great stay!

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Jacksonville
title: “Never again”
text: Those excellent reviews must have been put in by the hotel management or maybe they have renovated a couple of the rooms. This place is old and run down. The pool is tiny...not the one in the picture shown here.. Service was really sub-par. The room furniture is really old and worn. One night was more than enough of that place for us.

name: Ramada Conference Center Mandarin
title: “A fave of mine...”
text: I will be visiting this Ramada for the 4th or 5th time this March. I am going to visit family in the area and go to St. Augustine for touring. I find this Ramada to be a fantastic place to stay, and the free buffet breakfast is amazing. I am diabetec, and can still find enough "safe foods" at this buffet to keep me going until lunch time. GiGi's Friday night all you can eat prime rib and crab legs buffet is a feast! On our first visit, we had problems with the card key, and at 1 a.m., after the Comedy Show, we couldn't get in our poolside room, we got bumped up to a suite, which was a plus for us! I actually hugged the Manager! I have never forgotten that! The rooms are clean and have everything you need, housekeeping is great and the pool is always clean and temperate. Coming from NY, I like to have a pool I can actually take a dip in without freezing! The staff is friendly and welcoming. And it comes at a great price! Looking forward to returning in March! I highly recommend this Ramada location for a stay if in the area.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Jacksonville Butler Blvd
title: “My First stay at a LaQuinta”
text: The hotel staff overall was wonderful. Hotel is beautiful. Housekeeping could be better. Wish they had a complete hot breakfast.

name: Wyndham Jacksonville Riverwalk
title: “It's alright i guess...”
text: Recently stayed here with my wife for one night and we were satisfied, I guess. This hotel is older and decently maintained. The room was clean and comfortable. The bathroom was also clean but the tub did show some signs of age and their was random light switch in the sink area served no purpose as it turned on nothing but was there to be flipped up and down--go figure. My major complaint with this hotel was the bed linen. It had no visible stains but after laying in bed for 10 - 20 minutes my skin started to itch slightly as it felt that the linen wasn't necessarily dirty but it didn't feel clean either. I had trouble getting to sleep for the next hour due to these skin irritations from the not so clean linen. I would not want to stay at this hotel for an extended period of time but for 1 night it serves it's purpose.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Jacksonville Butler Blvd
title: “Good value - good location.”
text:
We had to arrive late to visit my father in the hospital (St. Luke's is very nearby). We arrived about 11 p.m. and our room was ready and just as we requested - 2 queen beds, top floor, near the back elevator and parking. It was just my adult son and I and we had comfortable beds and a clean, safe room. The location is primarily business and there are a number of various restaurants (including a Cracker Barrel) and other hotels (Hampton, Courtyard, Wingate, Red Roof) within walking distance. We chose this since we didn't want to spend much (only $49 for the night) and wanted to be in this location. I wouldn't say it was immaculately clean, but clean, probably just seemed worn more than not clean. It was very quiet and the shower was one of the better hotel showers we've used. If we had to stay in that area again - I'd stay there again. However, we only had 2 double beds. Had my husband been with us, the double bed would not have been large enough. We'd probably have to either have a king bed w/ roll-away or stay in the nearby Wingate or Hampton with 2 queen beds per room. Always verify if the beds are queen or doubles if more than one person will be sleeping in each bed. Just verify with the hotel the actual bed size. The hostess at check-in was very nice and very helpful. 
Our breakfast (included in price of room) was adequate - not as nice as a Hampton, but they offered boiled eggs, cereals, muffins, and 'u-make'em' type belgian waffles. Definitely worth the price we paid, but I wouldn't pay more for what we had. Good value. Good location. Clean, safe accommodations.

name: JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort & Spa Phoenix
title: “Desert Oasis”
text:
Loved it! This was one of the best resorts I've ever stayed at. The rooms are wonderfull, but the views are breathtaking. I especially enjoyed all of the water features scattered around the property.
There is enough to do that you could stay on the property your entire trip. The local area has lots of attractions nearby. Everything from hiking to shopping to gambling.
We had great cocktails and sushi at Roy's, even if they are a little pricey. I would highly reccomend this resort!

name: Four Points by Sheraton Jacksonville Baymeadows
title: “Poor Management”
text: I stayed in this hotel for one night this week (the second time I have stayed there in about a year) and was awoken at 2 AM by banging noises coming from the air conditioner. I was was forced to turn the air conditioner off and attempted to sleep in my room turned sauna. When I brought this to the attention of the "manager" he unapologetically told me that I should have called down to the front desk at 2 AM and they would have switched my room - I'm not sure why he thought that my switching rooms in the middle of the night would have improved the quality of my stay in his hotel or whether pointing out that I could have done so would make me feel any better. I'm also not sure who decided that this daytime manager that I dealt with is in any way fit to manage a hotel - I can assure you, he is not. Although I will be back in the area visiting a client several times in the near future, needless to say, I would never return to this hotel again - there are other choices in the area. In addition, I do travel a lot and stay almost exclusively in Starwood properties - I will also reconsider my loyalty...

name: Country Inn & Suites By Carlson, Jacksonville
title: “we have family in Jacksonville”
text:
from the front desk
 to the house keeping people
to the breakfast people
to the grounds people
to the maintance people
to the managent
they all a great team. 
as long as our family lives here we will stay here....

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Jacksonville Mandarin
title: “Wonderful Experience!”
text:
After seeing some ho-hum reviews of this La Quinta, I was quite hesitant. But, as this was one of only two hotels in the area I needed to stay at, I chose the La Quinta. While not the Ritz in terms of "fanciness", this place was great, and had everything we needed to enjoy our stay at a great rate. Our stay, celebrating our grandmother's 90th birthday, was enhanced by the nice stay we had at this hotel. It started out with the nice touch of a cookie and bottle of water on the desk upon entering the room. (And, boy was that bottle great as it was 99 degrees and HUMID!!- hotter than Miami!!) The beds were very comfortable, linens were clean, and the room was immaculate. A/C worked great- wall unit controlled digitally. Shower was hot and had fantastic pressure. Cute stickers on the toilet paper that said "if you can't give us a "10", please let us know. There is an iron, hair dryer, small desk and chair in addition to another non-wheeled chair. About 20 TV chanels, mostly local, and a few fuzzy ones, but passable. Free local calls and toll-free calls, which can come in handy if you need to call an airline and have to wait half an hour on hold and don't want to waste cell usage. Location of the hotel is off a busy road, but definitely in deep enough from San Jose Boulevard to have complete silence at night, except for those annoying people that insist on slamming hotel room doors, but that can happen anywhere. Free parking right outside the hotel (as can be expected in this area). Fantastic swimming pool right outside the hotel's front door, entry via hotel key- 5 foot 6" deep. Small sign by the sink said if one forgot anything, you can get it complimentary from the front desk, which is great if a toothbrush or paste was forgotten. FREE and FAST (faster than my DSL at home) internet access that was a breeze to get up and running. The FREE continental breakfast was great, and had lots of choices- eating kosher, we were very pleased to have an OU-wrapped bagel (the OU is small, but it's there!) to eat. Lots of choices in a relaxed room with CNN in the corner. Very nice way to start the day. Staff was friendly and helpful. Piece of paper was put under our door indicating we were already checked out the morning of our departure (I joined their free returns program; not sure if that's why we were automatically checked out, but it takes 1 second down the hall to return the key!). 
One previous reviewer complained about the sticker on the door that concealed the previous hotel chain (baymont)- who cares about a sticker??? Yes, the corny stickers were still there, but the ROOM is what counts! Clean, great amenities, nothing to complain about here. All in all, a wonderful place to stay, and well recommended!

name: Jacksonville Marriott
title: “Not Impressed”
text:
My company paid $199 per night for this room... YES.. $199 a night in Jacksonville??!!??!!! This should be an $89 a night room without the problems. 
First let me say that if I paid $89 for this room I would have been satisfied. I will just go through the list now of why this place was not good, and very dissapointing for a Marriott (which my second favorite chain next to Embassy Suites).
1) for $199 a night, I was given what was clearly a priceline room. On the second floor, just over the roof line of a function room and facing a wall (about 30 feet in front of me). Beautiful view...NOT!
2) The handle on the toilet kept popping off when I tried to flush it, and stuck out about 4 inches from the side of the toilet unless you pushed it in.
3) Sink would not drain properly. Kept overflowing.
4) Key cards kept demagnetizing, so I was locked out of my room 3 times!!! yes..3 times.
4) Indoor pool was so dirty that at only 4 feet deep, I could barely see my feet due to the fogginess. Try cleaning it once and a while.
5) Business Center was soo hot, it was felt like a steam room when other people where in there. In fact, it must start stinking, because they have a deoterizing mechinism that sprays every so often as you sit there. How about pumping some airconditioning into that room!
6) Ordered a sandwich at the bar and it came smothered in Brie (nasty!). How about adding that to the descriptions of your sandwiches!
In Conclusions....Stay at the Radision two doors down if you want to be happy. People seem to love that place. I have told my company, I will absolutely not stay at the Marriott Jacksonville again. Either they put me somewhere else, or I don't go.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Jacksonville Butler Blvd
title: “Great Hotel!”
text: Stayed here for one night on our way to a Cruise in Ft. Lauderdale. I wish we could have stayed longer. They have very clean, spacious rooms, with comfortable beds. The whole hotel looks immaculate, the grounds are beautifully kept and the pool area is very nice. There is a Cracker Barrel restaurant right next door. Booked this through La Quinta's website for only $55 a night, it was a very good deal. Would love to go back.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Jacksonville South
title: “Nice”
text: Dog Friendly! Dog area outside was Clean .Friendly staff & Room services, very clean rooms, nice comfortable bed. Would recommend. A+ X five. Loved our stay

name: Hotel Indigo Jacksonville Deerwood Park
title: “Loved it!”
text:
The front desk staff was extremely friendly. The room was beautiful. I love the wood floors instead of carpet. The bed was comfortable with tons of pillows and a fluffy comforter. The Keurig coffemaker made my stay! I had four cups of great coffee, in actual cofee cups instead of paper.
The pool was nice, and we had it all to ourselves. I will definitely stay again!

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Jacksonville-Southside Blvd-Deerwood Pk
title: “Great Hampton Inn experience ....”
text: We were quite pleased when we arrived to find a clean and maintained facility with large comfortable rooms. ...and as usual the extremely comfortable beds! Well worth the rate!

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Jacksonville South
title: “Nice, clean hotel that is convienent to a lot of places in Jacksonville”
text: I stayed recently at this hotel for one night. The hotel was clean and conveinent to restaurants, and places of interest around Jacksonville. The hotel is priced very reasonably, especially for this location. I would recommend this hotel.

name: JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort & Spa Phoenix
title: “Time Share Offer”
text:
We went there on a Time Share offer of $75/night, 4 nights, 5 days. We booked and paid for a one bedroom villa back in May of 2006. Keeping in mind that we would have to endure a 90minute sales presentation in order to get such a deal. Our friends booked in November 2006 with the same offer, or they were lead to believe so. 
When we arrived at the Canyon Villas our friends were told their "hotel room" was at the hotel and not a villa as ours was. 
We were all greatly disappionted and let the manager Adam know so. We had shared a rental car which we kept at the villa and everytime we wanted to go see them at the hotel (JW Marriott Desert Ridge) we had to valet park which was costly. 
I must say that the time share sales presentation of 90 minutes was the least painful one of its type we have been through. 
However, they killed the sale upon our arrival.
The resort was beautiful as it is only 4 years old.they guys golfed the Palmer course and we ladys purchased services at the spa, used the spa pool (no children allowed) which was wonderful.

name: JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort & Spa Phoenix
title: “Subtle changes made reduced the atmosphere.”
text:
Last year we had a family vacation at this hotel and enjoyed it so much we decided to go back again this year. We arrived on 8/21 and stayed for about a week. The hotel is top notch. The grounds are well maintained, and the pools are in great shape. (Our favorite is the Lazy River.)
Unfortunately, we noticed some things that were changed from last year that we did not anticipate. For example, last year at the pools, there was a childrens menu with lunch items that were reasonably priced. This year, the children's menu was gone, and all lunch possibilities were much higher priced. (This is a real problem for a family of 5.) I really don't want to spend $60 - $70 a day for lunch. I didn't see the snow cone machine either !
Another BIG problem for my wife and I was to try to find a good cup of coffee somewhere at the hotel. Unfortunately, the only coffee was Starbucks. (And we really hate Starbucks !) This coffee is too strong, and way over priced. 
Anyway...despite the above issues, we still managed to have an enjoyable time, but it is questionable if we will go back in the future.

name: Staybridge Suites Jacksonville
title: “Very Accomodating”
text: It felt like home. Everyone was friendly. They were reasonably priced and the service was impressive.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Jacksonville Flagler Center
title: “Never been a fan of Courtyard...”
text: I've completely changed my views! We stayed here for one night on our way from Charlotte to Fort Lauderdale. It was easy to find and convenient to Interstate 95. We checked in at 3 pm. We were given Room 217 facing the main road. The room was very large and clean. The bathroom was also very nice. The hotel was always quiet... there were no disturbances at all. Our room had frig, microwave and coffee maker. Free coffee and tea downstairs. The front desk staff was pleasant. We did not eat the breakfast for $8.95. There are lots of restaurants are located nearby (just ask for the list). Great rate using the senior discount. Liked it so much that we stayed again on the return trip home from Fort Lauderdale. We requested the same room and the front desk kindly accomodated us. We will definitely stay here again if we're ever passing through Jacksonville.

name: Hyatt Regency Jacksonville Riverfront
title: “Great Place to Stay for Football Game!”
text:
I stayed here for the Saints/ Jags game the employees were so nice and we all had a great time! We did not eat there or use the pool or anything so i can not comment on that but overall it was a great stay! The fire alarm went off while we were sleeping and we had to walk down 17 flights of stairs to the lobby but we were given a 50 dollar certificate to use on our room! 
Great place to go with a big group! We got a rate of 99 a night with out group! So worth it!
Also very close to the water taxi that will take you to the stadium!
Who Dat!

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Jacksonville South
title: “Quiet Hotel Convenient to Mayo Clinic”
text: Brought my wife down for appointments at Mayo Clinic. Hotel offers Mayo Clinic discount and is a smooth 12 minute drive away down Butler Blvd. Staff is friendly and accomodating. Rooms are quiet and clean. Room a little larger than most in this price range. Free breakfast was very good as free breakfasts go. Bed clean and comfortable. Grounds are well landscaped and clean. The only thing that bothered me slightly was the air conditioning system. It has a large unit under the window and cuts on and off frequently instead of constantly blowing. Bathroom is clean and roomy with a nice shower. Would stay here on return visit.

name: Sheraton Dallas Hotel
title: “Nice hotel”
text: Easy place to find by car , handy for freeway and downtown Dallas.Nice clean rooms and friendly staff.Plenty restaurants and bars nearby !

name: Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs Resort
title: “Too busy and outdated”
text: We only stayed one night [and that was enough]. there's no room when you pull in by car. Your vehicle is offered to be 'valet' parked. they sent us to our room in a long roudabout way which took a long time to get to. However, we discovered how short a distance we actually were from the lobby, yet it took a five minute walk to get to our room based on their directions. The gentleman that valet parks was rather abrupt and unpleasant and not very professional; you expect at night]. The suite was outdated and old and we paid $199 for one night; which we felt was a rip off. We did find their restaurant [they have several] to be decent and pleasant for a casual dinner. It was too much of a fisasco to get to our car since they valet parked it, and yet we found it close to our room after we checked in. We would not go back again. Maybe 20 years ago it was a nice place but we were disappointed.

name: The Comfort Inn San Jose International Airport
title: “best quality for bang of buck”
text: before here I almost went to travel lodge not far from here since I've had good experiences there before but for about $10 bucks more you are getting a hotel type quality here. I'm so glad I took my family here especially after hearing horror stories of the travel lodge not far from here. ohhh and you'll love there complimentary breakfast!

name: The Comfort Inn San Jose International Airport
title: “Used to be better...but the room is still great!”
text: I stayed in this hotel about a year ago and would have given it an Excellent rating at that time. I can't believe how worn it has become over the year. I think there might have been a change in management. The breakfast used to serve hard boiled eggs and had real half and half for the coffee. Now it is bisquits and gravy, waffles...and some fruit that looks like it has been sitting there for a week. Wish they still had the eggs! Online they advertise Guest Laundry but there isn't one on site...there is a laundromat down the street. As you have read in the other reviews, this is not an area where you want to be wandering outside, especially at night. Other than the above, the room is still fabulous and in the end, this is what I care most about. I also wish they had a fitness center, they are supposedly working on this.

name: Extended Stay America - San Jose - Edenvale - North
title: “Horrible Customer Service”
text:
I was driving from San Diego to San Jose and made a reservation for this hotel. I let the woman know that my Mother and I would be arriving late (11:30pm). 
We arrived to find that we did not have a room because my card had been "declined" (though I had used the card the whole way up with no problems) and NO ONE bothered to call us, even though they knew we would be arriving after hours. There was a very nice gentleman who was doing the laundry who let me in, but didn't have the authority to give me a room. He seemed very worried that we might have to sleep in our car, but couldn't do anything about it. I called the night manager and left a message. Luckily we found a hotel close by that was open at that hour.
I called in the morning and was directed to a manager. I left a message on his machine as well and never was called back. I can't speak for the conditions but the service is horrible!

name: Fontaine Inn Downtown / Fairgrounds
title: “Cheap and Comfortable”
text:
We found this hotel off the 101 in San Jose looking for a affordable place to spend the night. The hotel isn't that big two levels with doors outside. We could hear the traffic at times since our room faced the highway. The room was clean and smelled OK. Carpet was fresh and the bathroom was clean. Sheets looked clean. Although I did pull the bedspread back as soon as I walked into the room. Older television set of course at a place like this your not going to find a flat screen. 
There was a mini fridge and microwave. The towels could have been a little bigger and softer. Light in the small bathroom could have been a little brighter. They did offer a small continental breakfast till 9am. Seemed to be fresh paint on the walls. Bed was comfortable, pillows were soft. Maybe a little too soft for me. I need to bend one in half so I would be a little more comfortable. The room was a little warm, I tried to figure out the A/C but with no luck. Actually I was little afraid to turn it on fearing dust might fly out. They did offer free internet which was nice. 
I was expecting much worse. I was pleasantly surprised. It was a great place to just spend the night if your passing through town. I wouldn't spend a whole weekend here. There was a Denny's just next door and it was right off the highway access. We didn't seem to hear our neighbors. Of Course we were so tried since we checked in at 2am. I felt safe leaving the car in the parking lot. We did park right in front of our room. I would stay here again if I need to pass through town again.

name: Homestead Studio Suites
title: “Not a good choice.”
text: The hotel was not clean, the mattress was so thin /soft you could feel the box springs, the internet was VERY slow, and things in the room kept breaking (ironing borad, alarm clock, etc.). There was also no one to check me out before 6am, even though they told me the night before that someone would be there.

name: Super 8 Motel - San Jose Airport/Santa Clara Area
title: “Totally disappointed”
text: I was so disappointed by our stay. From the moment I stepped into the lobby I was thinking it was a mistake to stay there. The staff was incredibly rude, making check in painful and frustrating. They didnt improve throughout the visit. Everything at this hotel that could be a little off certainly was. The pool was freezing, making it impossible for the kids to swim (a huge disappointment as they loved the super 8 pool up in Vancouver), the bathroom out of order, parking a nightmare, and breakfast lacking in every way. I have enjoyed Super 8 hotels previously, but Im not sure if I would do it again after this trip.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Nice weekend”
text: The Magnolia is in a great location downtown, especially if you are planning to spend most of your time in that area. The valets and shuttle operator were all very courteous and helpful as were the front desk. The queen bed left a little to be desired but the suite was spacious with three closets and a large kitchen / living room area. The bar was not great, but there are plenty of places close by to have a drink.

name: Valley Park Hotel
title: “THE STAFF IS ATTENTIVE!”
text: In spite of the age of the facility it is well maintained and clean.The staff is exceptional, courteous and accomodating. While i did not stay for dinner the complimentary breakfast offering was quite good. For the money you cannot find a better place if your stay is longer than an overnight. Art

name: Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs Resort
title: “Better Places to Stay in Phoenix”
text: I stayed here in the summer of 2003 because a friend had a free voucher. Visitors to Phoenix and Scottsdale, please note: there are MANY, much better resorts to stay at than this one. This is an old property, with some maintenance problems. The water features are nice, but just average for Phoenix. This resort is kind of far from most tourist attractions, etc. For the money (about $100 a night from Memorial Day to Labor Day), try the JW Marriott Desert Ridge (which is a beautiful new resort in north Phoenix). All of the Phoenix and Scottsdale resorts have water features and most have golf courses, too, so shop around. It is a buyer's market with resorts in Phoenix during the summer.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Jacksonville South
title: “Klein und fein”
text: Wir haben uns im Juni 2010 für dieses Hotel als Ausgangspunkt für unsere Ausflüge nach St. Augustine, Jacksonville Beaches, Downtown Jacksonville und zum Shoppen entschieden. Es handelte sich dabei um keine überlaufene Bettenburg und war trotz der direkten Lage zur Highwayausfahrt ruhig gelegen. Das kont. Frühstück fiel nicht so 'trocken' aus wie man es aus anderen Hotels kennt, sondern wurde um Rührei bzw. fertige Omletts ergänzt. Der Pool hat einen sauberen und ordentlichen Eindruck hinterlassen. Das Parkplatzangebot war ausreichend und das kostenlose WLAN stand schnell und unterbrechungsfrei im ganzen Hotel zur Verfügung. Gemessen an dem aktuellen Preis war das HI-Express ein Schnäppchen für das wir uns wieder entscheiden würden.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “A great bargain with excellent service and accommodations, as well as several complimentary services.”
text: Bed was extremely comfortable. The hotel is in a fairly quiet location but several good restaurants are within a block or two in several locations; their shuttle service will take you within 3 miles which opens up more options. Staff were extremely helpful, welcoming and courteous. Loved the time and funds saved with their complimentary high speed internet, breakfasts, reception drinks and cookies & milk 'nightcap'.

name: Valley Park Hotel
title: “Great Customer Service”
text: Would recommend this place for the price and the great customer service. Derek at the front desk was extremely helpful and offered plenty of information.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Jacksonville - Bartram Park
title: “A newer Hampton Inn in a nice location”
text: This was our third Hampton Inn during our US vacation. It was by far the nicest Hampton of the four we stayed in. Located a little outside of Jacksonville, it is not near downtown or really anything. It was great for us as it was a stopover on the way to Cocoa Beach and close to I-95. It seemed brand new (I guess 1 year old). Parking lot was being redone, but no big deal. Not many options for eating close by, but it looks like the area is being developed and will have many options soon. Beautiful rooms and decor. Beautiful breakfast bar area with the usual options at a Hampton. Nice business centre and outdoor pool. Nice staff (gave my daughter extra cookies). Wish we could have stayed here longer. Nothing like these new Hampton Inns. Kudos to Bartram Park Hampton Inn.

name: Grand Hyatt DFW
title: “Convenient but overwhelmed”
text:
I had the unfortunate opportunity to stay at the grand hyatt dfw not by choice but by American Airlines cancellation. When the flight was cancelled, we had to stay one more night in Dallas. We chose to stay at the airport grounds due to convenience. The hotel is located in terminal D and is easily accessible by airport tram. 
It turns out we weren't the only people staying due to cancellation. The check in staff reported she was out of king size beds but when we told her we had gold status, she quickly found a room with a king bed. Ironic, isn't it? 
we were hungry and tried out the restaurant and were told there would be an hour wait. It was Easter Sunday and American must have cancelled half of it's flights. The restaurant was poorly understaffed. We sat at the bar and due to our exhaustion, we ordered to go. The bartender was very busy and impatient. I realized why...she was the only person tending to all the customers at the bar, the snack area and the orders that the wait staff was putting in for drinks for the restaurant. Yes, she was the ONLY person. She ran around, flying from one end of the bar to the other, and back again and slamming glasses and wine bottles around. Soon we noticed she was so backed up, the wait staff started pouring their own wine. And not to mention the piles of dirty wine glasses, carafes, plates, sitting on top of the counter. We sat for an hour waiting for our food to go. We were lucky. Apparently people sitting down dining had a 2 hour wait. Maybe it was just a bad day/night. We ran into another couple on the elevator who bought food from the snack bar. They couldn't even get a plastic spoon. That's how bad it was. 
We proceeded to our room. It was right across the elevators. So you can hear everything. The room was very modernized, with a huge window that spanned the entire wall. Everything is electronic, and with a touch of a button, you can control the blinds, the lights , etc. The shower was quite small, the size of one I would expect in city living, such as DC. THere was a tub, opposite of stand up shower, that we didn't use. The bed was firm, too firm. When we woke up at 5 am the next morning, i hit the button "soft light", but it wasn't soft, it turned on all the lights and blinded me, instead. The worse part was hearing people talking and walking throughout the night. The rooms were fine, just request away from elevator. 
We would do it for convenience for traveling, but otherwise I would highly recommend the new omni convention center hotel if staying in Dallas.

name: Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs Resort
title: “Tolles, gemütliches Hotel, gerne wieder”
text: Hotel macht echt Spass, super Lage und auch sonstiger Komfort ist durchaus gegeben. Der Internetzugang im Businesscenter ist etwas zu teuer für heutige Verhältnisse, aber sonst durchaus sehr empfehlenswert. Wir würden wieder dort absteigen.

name: Comfort Suites Airport
title: “Hotel good- neighborhood questionable”
text:
The hotel is exactly as pictured on the webpage- nice size room, small fridge, sink, microwave (no utensils or cookware provided though). It was clean, and included breakfast was good with both hot and cold items. Staff friendly and small issues were taken care of very rapidly. 
The hotel is very convenient to light rail which as a solo traveling female was fine in the morning. However, returning around 8:30 pm, I did have a rather uncomfortable moment where a group of young men yelled some questionable things at me after passing me on the sidewalk as I walked from the stop to the hotel. I didn't feel in acute danger, but the situation was stressful enough I would hesitate to make that trek by myself after dark again. Unlike many others in the neighborhood, the doors to the rooms are in the interior, which helps with security.

name: Silicon Valley Hotel San Jose Airport
title: “Watch your credit card bill closely!!”
text:
I stayed at the Clarion in May for one night on business and at the time I came away with an ambivalent view of the hotel. It seemed clean and was probably a hotel I would stay at again. However, I just received my credit card bill yesterday and I discovered a strange charge of $200 in addition to the $149 I paid for the hotel and taxes. I contacted the hotel and talked to the front desk person who transferred me to accounting. The accounting person informed me that the hotel is smoke free and I was charged $200 for smoking in the room. There is one problem with this---I DON'T SMOKE!
The accounting person transferred me back to the front desk where I made my appeal. I was promptly denied. They told me that housekeeping reported that the room smelled like smoke and that I was the person in the room at the time. I did notice a very faint odor of smoke when I checked in and didn't feel it warranted a complaint (I am also pretty sensitive to smoke so it obviously wasn't that bad). Anyway, it took 5 more calls to finally get to Kathleen, a voice of reason who promptly removed the charge.
I have several issues with this experience. First, I love the fact that hotels are going completely smoke-free. I would seek out a smoke-free hotel because I hate walking into a room that has had a previous smoker. With that said, no hotel should drop a $200 charge on someone with no other formal notification. I got no calls to let me know I was going to be charged and if I had not scanned my credit card bill line-by-line I may not have even realized I was charged. In my mind this is a borderline practice that may not even be legal. Second, when I called (several times) to get the charge removed I felt like the customer relations people felt like I was lying. I even offered to have my doctor send a note stating that I am a non-smoker. It was way too difficult to remedy this situation that was so obviously incorrect. Fortunately Kathleen stepped in and immediately remedied the situation. I wish I could have talked to her first to save me a lot of frustration.
In summary, what would have probably been a rating of 3 out of 5 has become a 1 because of the issues described above.

name: JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort & Spa Phoenix
title: “Wonderful! Clean, amazing room service, pool service. It's like being in Vegas without the casinos!”
text: We stayed there in July. The hotel, besides from being brand new is beautiful inside and out. The rooms are very spacious. The many many pools are great. There is a lazy river, water slide, kid pool & water spray area. The pool side service is the best I've ever had. Great food & fast.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Jacksonville - Bartram Park
title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 2 weeks and had a wonderful time. The hotel staff is very courteous and always ready to help., especially Mike Rind, Director Sales he is simply amazing and always ready to help. Rooms are spacious and nice. It is worth every penny that I paid for the room charge. Excellent. keep it up!!

name: DoubleTree by Hilton San Jose
title: “Strictly business”
text:
The Doubletree is an older hotel near the San José Airport. My guess is that it is 25 or so years old and it does show its wear. 
My first unpleasant experience was arriving at the Registration area. There was no luggage assistance available. After unloading the vehicle that brought me there and dragging the luggage to the curb myself I was approached by a very rude female employee who demanded the keys to the vehicle that had brought me. I stated that the vehicle was only there to drop me off and would leave in a minute. The employee got very gruff and said that it did not matter and grabbed the keys out of my drivers hand. We said our goodbye’s and when my driver went to get her keys back no one was available to give them to her. Mind you that this was about a minute after they were taken. We asked the first Valet we saw for the key and they had to go find someone else to give them to us. This stupid and unnecessary inconvenience made me angry, what a nice Doubletree welcome for my first day of vacation!
This is a very big, cold, strictly business hotel. 
The front desk was cordial and got us our key quickly, we were the only customer at the desk.
The room was about a quarter mile from the entry. Entering the room the air smelled like cleaning fluid. It also smelled of tobacco smoke. The rug was warn. The room had a nice bathroom with adequate counter space.
We looked for a snack bar but didn’t find one. A golf cart would be necessary to do a proper search for any of their services. We didn’t use any of their services as we didn’t find any welcoming us.
The next morning, the airport shuttle was efficient and prompt and we got to the airport in plenty of time.

name: Comfort Suites Airport
title: “Good hotel”
text: I had a good stay here for business. Staff is friendly and helpful. The hotel has a good location and offered a spacious suite, clean and nice. Reasonable price.

name: Holiday Inn San Jose-Airport
title: “What a disappointment”
text: My wife and I traveled to San Jose to have time to visit with our daughter who was there for a day. We thought we would splurge a bit and stay in a nice hotel so that she could relax until she returned to work that evening. Well, I'll just say that I wish we had chosen a small chain motel, because it would have been nicer and we would paid half as much. First of all, we got to room and opened the windows to discover that we had a view of a wall. A light green wall. When I went down to ask if we could have a room with something of a real view I was told that nothing was available. It was clear from the empty spaces in the parking lot that the hotel could not have been 100% booked and it never looked crowded. While sitting around in the room I noticed a black plastic thingy. When I picked it up, I discovered it was packaging for the last guests personal lubricant. Now, it wasn't unsafe or even unsavory, but it was weird and it showed that the room wasn't cleaned well. There was no facial tissue in the room. The swimming pool was so cold we couldn't get in (well, my wife who can tolerate much colder water than I can, lasted about 3 or 4 minutes). The furnishings were ok, but old. I will say that the bed was fine and the shower was terrific, so there were a few good things. This was a very disappointing experience as we had looked forward to our visit. Oh well, the good part was that it was only one night.

name: Grand Hyatt DFW
title: “Amazing Hotel in Dallas”
text:
this is the first time we are in USA to travel.and we are so happy to stay here
I like this hotel very much because of The rooms are very big and have electronic controls for evrything including window shades.they have a good bar where you can choose any kind of drink,my wife loves the shower with bathtub,very clean room and good service.we will recommended to our friends.

name: Holiday Inn Express San Jose Central City
title: “Great Value and Service!”
text: There was 10 of us, eight of which were adults and two teenagers, that stayed in three rooms for two nights. The rooms were great with "not too hard" hotel room beds that you normally seem to find and with extra option pillows that were "soft" or "firm." Each bed had four pillows and extra were already provided in the rooms. The breakfast was great with "hot" options and with eggs everyday and served our differences and needs with many varities for all ten of us for breakfast. The staff was very friendly and helpful especially on Tuesday, December 29th. All ten of us would come a stay again and would recommend it to anyone. Great price and service!!

name: Hyatt Regency Jacksonville Riverfront
title: “Service really lacking”
text:
I stayed here for 3 nites last week as part of a large convention. My guestroom was very nice and comfortable but I did not have an ipod docking station as did most of my colleagues. I used the automatic checkin kiosk which was great and told me I had 
access to the Regency Lounge. When I called the desk the next morning to ask where the lounge was I was told I had to pay $50 extra to get lounge privileges. I declined but went to the lounge anyway and my key did open the door. I assume since I am a Gold Passport Member that was why I did have access.
The service in the lobby restaurant was awful!!! One morning a collegeague had to walk out because he never got his breakfast after waiting almost 1/2 hour. On Thursday we had a reservation for 8 for lunch to have a small meeting and requested to be in the corner so as not to disturb anyone. We arrived and no table had been set, and then they put us smack in the middle of the dining room. The service that day was awful. The waitress was rude, and inefficient and it seemed like she was doing us a favor by serving us. Then when we got the bill I saw why, since there was 7 of us they automatically add on the service charge so it didn't really matter how she treated us - her tip was guaranteed.
The bartenders in the sports bar were ok but didn't go out of their way to be friendly. The best service was at the lobby bar on Friday afternoon around 5:00, our waiter was wonderful!
The food at our banquets was varied. Lunch on Friday was awful but dinner was average. Service at Friday nite banquet slow and erratic. 
Overall, very disappointed and would not return.

name: Arena Hotel
title: “Clean and safe hotel”
text: I reserved the room simply to be close to the HP Pavillion to see a concert. We were very surprised to find the hotel an excellent place to stay. The room was clean with all the basic necessities. Would recommend to anyone wanting to see a concert at the Pavillion.

name: Courtyard by Marriott San Jose Airport
title: “For the business traveller”
text: Had a good stay here - and only reason I would stay here is if you need to be in this location. It is in a corporate/industrial area - so good if you are working in the area or need to be near the airport. Good clean, comfortable rooms - and very good staff. No restaurant though - but a few decent place just a short walk away.

name: Hotel Palomar Dallas - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Major Disapointment”
text:
My girlfriend and I took our eleven year old daughters to Dallas for a "shopping weekend." We normally stay at the Four Seasons in Las Colinas but opted to try this new "Hot List" hotel, according to Conde Nast Traveler. The location was very convenient to all of the major shopping centers. What was very inconvenient was the lack of service. 
We booked a suite. The living area was bare, I enjoy and appreciate modern decor but this needed some art or something of that nature. The bedroom area was decorated nicely. Everytime we sat on the end of the bed, the mattress separated from the headboard and flipped up. We had to request toilet paper twice and they delivered one roll. We had to request extra towels and washcloths daily (they were aware there was four of us staying in the room). The bathroom was poorly executed. One of the cabinet door hinges was gone so it was barely hanging on. Had a nasty shower curtain, who even sees shower curtains in this type of hotel? I would at least expect a glass door. The bathroom was cheaply put together. Lighting was terrible. 
The room service was 50/50. The first night we ordered, everything was just as ordered with all of the usual accompaniments. From then on it all went down hill. Needless to say, by the time we got our last meal we had to call and ask for flatware! The girls wanted ice cream for dessert at 10:10 but they wouldn't serve it because they don't serve ice cream after 10:00. Service? We never had all of our dishes removed after calling for them to do so. One morning my girlfriend and I were having a bottle of champagne and the attendant removed the almost full bottle, mind you, they had hardly removed any of the other dirty bare dishes. We didn't realize the mishap for probably 20 minutes or so. Instead of bringing us a new unopened bottle they "found" it in the kitchen and brought it back to us. Made us a little nervous and grossed out to drink. 
The pool was disappointing since they did not have bar service. We requested someone from room service come and take our order. Since it was a warm day in May, we wanted a margarita and the girls wanted a non-alcoholic daiquiri. Much to our surprise this establishment doesn't offer any frozen concoctions... not even a margarita on the rocks! Our friendly waiter told us he was previously employed at a luxury hotel in Dallas and was quite surprised with the lack of service the Palomar exhibits. Again, service? How hard is it to blend a drink? 
Upon check out, we called and asked for a bellman to meet us in our room at a specified time. We waited and waited. The front desk even called to inform us our limo was waiting and that we needed to depart. We told them a bellman was scheduled to be in our room 20 minutes earlier but hadn't seen sign of him yet. They assured us he was in route to our room. Needless to say, we never saw him and lugged our luggage down ourselves. Not even an apology or "may I help you with your luggage" once the valets and doorman noticed us.
I"m not quite sure the Palomar understands great service. If they ever want to play in the same league as hotels that do, they definitely need to step it up a notch.
Bottom line. If you expect good service and nice amenities, stay at the Four Seasons or Hotel Crescent Court.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Great place for fun”
text: The place to spend the weekend. Service is top notch. Rooms are wonderfully furnished.

name: Arena Hotel
title: “Excellent value and location”
text: I chose this hotel because we wanted to be within walking distance of the HP Pavilion, and we didn't want to spend a lot of money for a hotel room that would basically just be used for sleeping after the event we were attending. And I wanted the free parking. I was also wise to other local hotels hitting you up with parking fees that aren't apparent when you first book your room, so what looks like a great price for a fancy hotel isn't so great once you have to include the what I consider to be excessively high parking fees. I also liked the idea of the included buffet breakfast. I expected that this would be an older hotel, with possibly older fixtures, given the cost, but that it would be clean and perfectly okay based on most reviews I had read. I ended up being very pleased. The room was large, comfortable, and very clean. Everything worked. The carpet was slightly stained. The hallway seemed a bit musty, but the room itself was fresh and clean smelling. The room overlooked the parking lot, and there were some loud people leaving at around 4:00 a.m., but other than that, it was very quiet. The beds were comfortable. There was a coffee maker, microwave, and refrigerator in the room. The heating/cooling system worked fine. The buffet breakfast consisted of scrambled eggs, bacon, sausage, pancakes, various toast choices, fruit, coffee, cereals, and fruit juices that were good quality, not the tinny tasting cheap stuff. Food quality was fine. It was a short, few blocks walk to the Pavilion. The staff was helpful and polite. The lobby is very nice and gleaming, and the buffet breakfast room was large. All in all, I felt I made a great choice for our needs, and the price could not be beaten. I would not hesitate to stay here again if attending an event at the Pavilion. The only criticism I could make is that there aren't any what I consider close restaurants within a short walking distance. We ended up having to walk about five or six blocks to find a nice restaurant for dinner. But if you were planning to eat at the Pavilion or drive, or the weather was nice (not the pouring rain during our visit), then this would not be a problem at all. And you could order pizza take-out, etc. from your room.

name: Grand Hyatt DFW
title: “An Oasis”
text: I, unexcitedly, decided to stay here as a result of an early flight the following day. I was impressed from the moment I pulled up to the curb. The bellman was great, the front desk staff were extremely courteous and professional and the feeling I got was that I was in a boutique hotel not in the airport but in a very cosmopolitan city, etc. The room was awesome- very comfortable with flat screen TV, great bed etc. The Health Club on the top floor was equally great- mint equipment and the outdoor pool was really nice- granted your at the airport but it is so nice that you almost forget. Needless to say I really liked this place. The only negative obviously is that your captive to the hotel and their offerings but for a night or two you'll be very happy. Lastly, the room service was really quick and food was good.

name: Hotel De Anza
title: “Charm, Style and Special touches in this Old World Hotel”
text:
We really enjoyed our stay at this hotel. It deserves all of its 4 star rating if not more. 
From the moment you walk into the marble lobby you get a good feeling about this hotel. 
The star of this hotel is the hedley club lounge. This is a very special space to spend some time in with plush sofas and many seating areas, a beautiful bar framed by 3 tall arches and a spectacular ceiling and chandelier. On the friday night we were there we enjoyed dinner and cocktails in the lounge while listening to a terrific jazz quartet. The bar menu is quite extensive and our waitress was very friendly.
Our deluxe king room on the 7th floor was lit when we walked in. There were chocolates waiting for us by the dresser and we had two windows which looked out at the city. We have stayed in many hotels in downtown San Jose and this was one of the quietest for street noise. The bed was very comfortable [not too firm and not too soft] and the linens were first class. The room was a good size and the bathroom was quite large for a boutique hotel. 
This hotel provides surprising little touches such as free apples on the check in counter, a pantry to raid on the second floor for a late night snack and a little tv in the bathroom. All the bath products were first rate. Even the ice machines in the beautiful hallways are cool in that they are built into the walls . 
My only minor complaints during my stay would be that the furniture in our room was a bit dented up and the gal that checked us in was all business. She was not welcoming or friendly and never smiled . Also the maid was a bit too noisy working in the room next to us early saturday morning .
Overall we found this hotel to be outstanding.
Parking Tip.
If you do not mind walking a couple of blocks the city parking garage on san pedro has free parking all weekend long.

name: San Jose Marriott
title: “Nicer than most Marriott”
text: this Marriott is relatively new & is upgraded from the usual Marriott experience. I attended a business meeting & then stayed for the San Jose Jazz Festival. We had a large, corner room that was very nice. Larger bath with plenty of counter space. Very friendly front desk & restaurant staff. Even the meeting lunch was good! Excellent Sunday brunch buffet. if you're staying in downtown San Jose, certainly consider this; it's less expensive than the Fairmont, but 1/2 block away & good value.

name: Hampton Inn And Suites San Jose
title: “Clean, comfortable, and courteous.....”
text: Stayed overnight and was met with a very courteous front desk staff member. The front lobby welcomed me with coffee, water, and newspapers and a small sitting area. The dining area was clean with a nice breakfast served with oatmeal, waffles, scrambled eggs, tater tots, cold cereal, yogurt, juices, coffee, and tea. The room was very spacious and clean. The bed was very comfortable. Very good place for the money we spent. I would recommend this place to friends to family for future visits.

name: La Quinta Inn San Jose Airport
title: “Loved the new room”
text: After traveling all day, the newly rennovated room was so inviting, extremely comfortable and clean. I was surprised and very pleased at the stylish comfort and modern look of the room. The keurig coffee maker was an excellent addition to an already pleasant stay. I liked everything about my stay and have nothing negative to add.

name: Arena Hotel
title: “Not so sure anymore..”
text:
I would agree with other reviews that the grounds are well kept and the hotel was clean, which is important but there was a stale smell to the room and the bed was uncomfortable. There was really nothing within walking distance although the hotel appears to be in a down-town type neighborhood. The store fronts were boarded up. Overall, the area was depressing as was the inside of the hotel. 
There is a free breakfast, which was fair- nothing to brag about. I will say the people working there were quite nice!

name: Adolphus Hotel
title: “Couldn't Have Been Better”
text:
I was intrigued to book a stay here after seeing the magnificent pics on this website and especially after getting an incredible discount on my stay thru Expedia. I am always attracted to romantic, historical hotels and always try to at least check them out when I'm in a given town. Upon arriving here, the valets treated me like royalty and helped me carry my bags and were only too happy to help, even when I didn't have any cash readily available for a tip. They seemed genuinely happy to make my two night stay as wonderful as possible. When I saw the gorgeous and super elegant lobby and common areas at check-in, I knew I had arrived! The front desk staff was as deferential and helpful as the valets and my check-in was problem free from the get-go. The room was meticulously clean and beautiful, not to mention huge, a whopping 550 sq. feet and it was only the deluxe, not superior room. The bathroom was elegantly up to date and very tastefully decorated in a tuscany, Italian marble theme. The rooms are appointed with antique lamps that look like cloisonne/Asian vases and I couldn't have felt more comfortable. Though the hotel dates from 1912, the electrical outlets work very well, unlike with some historic hotels and though I can't speak for the wi-fi or internet hook-up performance, everything worked!!! I ordered several room service items and they came promptly and the servers were very courteous and bent over backwards to please.
I have to be honest, I had some trepidation in booking this hotel, as I had read many neg. reviews regarding the thin walls and "lack of privacy" due to poor insulation. Well, I am the original light sleeper and was prepared for hearing sounds of amourous couples, loud tvs and terrible street noise on Akard Street. I have to say that I spent two very quiet nights at the hotel, despite an apparent near full capacity. There was a girl's pre-wedding event going on and I thought, oh no, lots of partying into the night and noise. AGAIN, I didn't hear a thing from anyone, it seemed that no one else was even on my floor; though there appeared to be lots of cars in the garage. I have to say that this was a spectacular experience and you have to stay here at least once. Some nuttos who h ave reviewed this place, have said that it is dated and worn. Not only am I a light sleeper, I am also a hotel snob, and believe you me, this place is a tour de force; I have stayed in the world's best hotels and this one is near the top of the list. Elegance, courtesy, and an alluring history make this a wonderful place to stay. I got a tremendous deal on Expedia and would recommend that you check there for excellent package rates (I paid $205 for a three day car rental AND two nights at this hotel), you can't beat that. I was charged $48 for two days of parking my car ($24 per day), but they did NOT charge me extra hundreds of $ on my debit card, as others have said. There is an $80 per day "incidental expenses" charge which I didn't like, but apparently, since I prepaid the room, they did not actually charge me, go figure.
John, the concierge is a wonderful asset to the hotel and I just can't say enough about my experience here. If this place is good enough for Donald Trump and Queen Elizabeth, believe me, you won't feel any less special here! AWESOME EXPERIENCE.
P.S. I did not get a chance to dine at the French Room, as it was closed on the days I was there (closed on Sundays and Mondays). I will be sure to hit it up next trip. If anyone tries it, please let me know. What a knock-out that restaurant is, much like the hotel itself.

name: Hotel De Anza
title: “Hotel De Anza - Pleasant Hotel in San Jose”
text:
We stayed one night at the Hotel De Anza in San Jose. This hotel was the site of a wedding we attended. The hotel is beautifully decorated and extremely comfortable and clean. Our room had two double beds and tons of space to spread out. There is an armoire with a tv and a desk. The bathroom was huge and had high quality Aveda bath products that were appreciated. At night they have a "raid our pantry" feature where you can go and fix sandwiches and get some snacks - all complimentary. The breakfast is one of the best continental breakfasts I have had in a while. The breakfast is in a dining room and offers cereals, pastry, scones, breads, hot oatmeal, granola, fruit, coffee, & juice. After you eat, staff bring a bill where you write your name and hotel number. That way you won't be charged for the meal. You can order hot food as well, at a charge. The complimentary evening snacks and breakfast help with the high price of the rooms.
Parking: Valet parking is $20. Across the street from the hotel is metered parking. We arrived on a Sunday and were able to park here for free. We put money into the meter at 9 AM Monday when they begin charging to park here.
Negatives: The bathroom mirror is a bit high up and felt like we needed to step on our tip toes to see well. The lighted make up mirror on the wall was also high up (our group averaged 5'4" tall). The outside of the hotel has a painting of a woman diving into water so you would expect a pool or hot tub in this hotel. There are no such facilities.
Bottom Line: If you attend a wedding at this hotel, it is great to stay here just for the convenience. If money is not an issue, this hotel is a comfortable place to stay with a high end feel. Looking for a bargain? Shop around San Jose for a lower priced hotel.

name: Radisson San Jose Airport
title: “Radisson SJ”
text:
Located close to the airport and freeway, but quiet. Approx. 10 minutes walking distance to the VTA lightrail station Gish (connections towards downtown San Jose in 15 min. and to the train station).
You can tell from the furnishings that the hotel is not the most recent one, but it is still in a good state. I was very satisfied with my stay and have no reason to complain.

name: San Jose Marriott
title: “Convention Center Hotel?”
text:
The location of this Marriott makes it very convenient for attending conventions, but they are not prepared for handling the volume of customers conventions bring. After waiting in the valet line for 15 minutes, we were finally greeted and told a bellman would be a 30 minute wait. We decided to do the best we could at carrying our luggage and headed for the front desk line. At early check-in, all rooms with double beds had been taken, even though I had booked months in advance.
We were given the keys to our room and walked in to find a Telemundo swimsuit competition playing on the TV, mops, rags and our previous guests hair all over the bathroom floor. My daughter had to get ready for the convention, so we dropped our luggage and organized a bit. I headed out to see if housekeeping was around to finish the job, but no such luck. A "manager" of some sort opened our door and more or less implied we needed to leave. Hmmmm.......didn't your front desk have record that the room was ready and gave us keys?
Next stop was one of the restaurants for a drink. It was a self-service operation with employees unfamiliar with bar service working. It look a bit for anyone to figure out how to make a drink and where the products were stored. This was the theme for the rest of our visits, but the employees working at Tanq seemed a bit more knowledgable. Other patrons were showing frustration as well, due to NO service in the restaurant/bar area. 
The next day we received the gift of no housekeeping. My husband did walk by a room with a couple employees on a bed watching TV, so maybe it was their break or rest period which diverted them.
The rooms are a bit dated and luckily I had secured a good rate with early booking. I've never left a hotel without tipping housekeeping, but this was my first. The in-room coffee machine will come in handy as the line at their lobby Starbucks was impossible. There is also a Peet's on the opposite side of the convention center by the Hilton which seems to process orders much more efficiently. 
It was convenient only. A few months prior we had stayed at the Four Points by Sheraton which is only a block or so away from the convention center. Between the two, I'd pick the Four Points.

name: Hyatt Place San Jose/Downtown
title: “Lots of upgrades, lots of noise”
text: I stayed at the Hyatt Place during a recent business trip. The property has gone through a serious modernization with all of the amenities you would expect. The staff was friendly during check-in and explained all of the property’s features for my choosing. My room was very comfortable with a sitting area, two beds, a refrigerator, a LG flat screen TV, and a work area. I enjoyed plenty of hot water during my morning shower. However, I must warn guests considering this property to get a room away from the street where the Convention Center train stops. The noise from street traffic, trains, planes, and emergency vehicles had me inserting my ear plugs by 9 PM and occasionally hearing selective sounds through my ear plugs. Thankfully, I had to be up and out by 6:30 AM because I can’t imagine how someone could sleep in. Also, I noticed Trip Advisor states parking is free in reviews from 2010, which makes “free parking” show up as a property’s feature. It isn’t free. It is $21 a day.

name: Hyatt Place San Jose/Downtown
title: “Wonderful stay”
text: Hyatt Place San Jose/downtown was amazing. The staff is friendly and always willing to help. Very nice flat screen TV's in the rooms, also has a hide away mini fridge. Firm beds. Amazing breakfast, free internet and the ability to print free copies from the business center

name: Hyatt Place Jacksonville Airport
title: “What a Pleasant Surprise!”
text: This hotel was so much more than I expected from a moderately priced airport hotel. It is stylish and impeccably clean. The room had a comfortable separate living area with a sectional sofa and a large, high quality television. The room had free, high speed internet access. The bed was extremely comfortable. The desk and cafe staff were pleasant and helpful. A pleasant surprise.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Good stay, good location.”
text:
Our family of 4 (kids, 14 & 10) stayed at The Magnolia for three nights while attending the State Fair. The location was good, not too far away and easy access to the freeway with plenty of restaurant options nearby. The staff was very friendly and helpful! The hotel was in good shape and clean. We took advantage of the complimentary breakfast as well as the paid omelet station and both were good. Not the best we had ever had, but no complaints. The kids really enjoyed the complimentary cookies and milk in the evening, of course. Valet parking was $22/night which, compared to other major cities, is a pretty good price. Of course self parking would be nice and I'm sure you could probably self park in a nearby garage but we didn't look in to that since we were unfamiliar with the area. Would possibly look at that if staying there in the future. I believe the valet uses a nearby garage anyway.
Our room was well appointed and clean. The beds were pretty comfortable, a little on the firm side. A/C worked well but was loud, you could definitely tell when it was running but it wasn't a bothersome noise. This is an older building so you can hear the inner workings such as plumbing, etc. Again, nothing bothersome to us. I had read that the higher floors are quieter and had requested a higher floor at check in which I could have got but opted for the larger room on the 6th floor that was also offered. In hindsight, I would have stuck with the higher floor. Road noise on the 6th floor was bothersome, especially when someone playing loud bass was stopped at the intersection at 2am and it rattled the windows enough to jar me out of a dead sleep. Go with a higher floor! 
The large garden tub in the bathroom was nice and I liked having drawers in the vanity especially since there really wasn't a convenient place to hang my toiletry bag. The lighting in the bathroom was sufficient as well, always a concern when putting on makeup. 
Overall, for the price we paid, location, and amenities, I thought this hotel was an excellent value. I would certainly consider staying there again if I return to the area.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Loved the Magnolia Hotel :)”
text: We had a great time there! They have breakfast every weekend morning from 8-10 (delicious!) and they have the most friendly staff members! :)

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Central and comfortable”
text:
We arrived at this hotel early after travelling by Greyhound. We were able to walk to the hotel from the bus station and even though we arrived by midday, the receptionist kindly gave us our room and we were able to explore Downtown Dallas.
Our warm and considerate welcome flowed through to every aspect of our stay. The room was most comfortable, the breakfast more than adequate and the staff polite and attentive. To add to the hotels hospitality was the offer of two free drinks in the early evening.
The position of the Magnolia was an added bonus. We were only a 15 minute walk to Dealey Plaza , the Tourist Information Centre and the historical and entertainment district. The metro was only a couple of blocks away.
We were there for two days, next time we will stay longer.
The elevators are real fun!

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Clean, and Comfortable minus the screams and noises outside at 2 a.m from the bar crowds!”
text: This was a great hotel with all the perks. We stayed on the side closest to the front of hotel on the 9th floor. From about 2 am -3 am I heard loud screams and hollaring from outside after the bars closed down. I know this is out of the hotels control, so many want to get a room no facing the street to miss these noises and enjoy the comfy beds and get some sleep! :)

name: Hilton San Jose
title: “Average for the high end. Contemporary Style.”
text:
I ended up at this property simply because all the hotels in the area were full. The rate wasn't bad considering the location and quality of the property, but that was only because there was no convention in the attached convention center. I have tried to get into this property when there was a convention and couldn't. So this time, I needed a place, others were full, and I gave it a try. 
It is VERY Contemporary which isn't really my style. If you like that, you'll like this place. If your tastes go more toward traditional luxury, then this isn't the place. To me, it felt minimalist, spartan, and cold. 
The breakfast in the status lounge on 18 was excellent. The lobby bar had a well attended live jazz group and the crowd was relatively young to middle aged and attractive. My room had loads of hot water and fast WiFi, so all in all it was fine. 
For the price and status of this place, it was just average. The Marriott is next door and there are many very nice hotels in the area that claim to be of the same quality, charge similar prices, and are outstanding. Compared to that class of property, this place is only average.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Excellent service, good value!”
text:
Great staff - very friendly - and very quiet rooms make for a really nice stay. 
Free wifi - a bonus given this type of hotel usually tries to charge for it. Our company doesn't pay for inroom wifi so I end up having to pay for it myself at the nicer hotels... which kinda burns when you know that less expensive hotels (e.g., Courtyard, Drury Inn) offer it free. 
Very nice rooms. My only nitpicky items were that the pillows were a little dense and there was only one mirror, with no natural light near it. (Not an issue for guys, of course.) Would have loved a second mirror, even better to have a full length mirror, near a window. 
Otherwise, outstanding experience - I'd go again and would also recommend to a friend.

name: Hyatt Place San Jose/Downtown
title: “Best Service Ever!!”
text: After long days of working we truly appreciated the sincere, friendly and attentive service that greeted us back at the hotel. One evening in particular we had to scrap our plans to go to a Giants game because of a last minute deadline. Instead, we camped out in lobby with laptops, phones and papers everywhere. Immediately, Victor (the restaurant bartendar) came in offered to bring us our drinks. The manager Rolando assisted by Jeffrey, not only delivered our drinks but also served us free appetizers to help ease our dissapointment in not getting to the ballgame. This was followed by our drinks being refilled and later our dinner orders taken and delivered. Victor set us up as if we were in the dining room. Never before have we had such attentive service. They certainly know how to make business travel a truly positive and enjoyable experience!

name: Moorpark Hotel
title: “An amazing hotel”
text:
Generally Moorpark was an amazing hotel, everything from the staff to the rooms, the outdoor area was excellent..
Also if you are traveling by car it is in a very convenient location and it offers free parking. 
Moreover, not more than 100m away from the hotel there are some restaurants like apple bees if you don't feel like driving downtown.

name: Hilton San Jose
title: “There on Business - Was Perfect!”
text: I recently spent 3 nights there on business and it was perfect. I'm an HH member and was on the executive floor. Free wifi was great, and the executive lounge had a great view of the city. The staff was super helpful, very nice, and the cleanliness was superb. It has a very modern feel as you walk in, but its quite cozy. It made for a great home away from home.

name: Grand Hyatt DFW
title: “Great stay... one of the best!”
text: What a great experience... everything about this hotel was high class... the courteous staff, the awesome fitness room, the comfy settings, definitely a great place. Just like another reviewer, our room was facing the airport runway and we could barely if at all hear the planes taking off and arriving... it was kinda eerie because you expect all this noise but it's strangely calm... and just like another previous reviewer, I found myself hypnotized by the runway... you would think that it would get boring, but watching them take off and land over and over was amazing. Anyway, the restaurant at the hotel was awesome as well... we stayed about 5 days and had breakfast each day that we were there. The staff at the restaurant were AWESOME and really made you feel welcome and attended to. The food was great as well. I will definitely try to stay here again if I ever go back to Dallas (but only on the awesome deal we got on the room rates) and it's definitely recommended to anyone staying in the area!

name: Moorpark Hotel
title: “Fantastic Place”
text:
We were travelling to Mammoth Lakes and our flight departed from San Jose so we had to stay a night in the city. After reading all the positive reviews over the Moorpark we decided to stay at this hotel and we didn't regret at all!
The hotel is beautiful, very elegant, spacious and comfortable rooms. Large bathroom. Everything is brand new and very well mantained. 
The facilities are very refined and the staff is simply amazing.
Special thanks to Kaz and Angelica from the front desk and Gloria from the restaurant.
We had courtesy breakfast and it was the best.
Also we would need to leave our car at the airport and the long-term parking is far away from the terminal where our flight departed from. Since my mother has difficulties walking I asked the front desk if I could leave the car parked there for two nights and catch a cab to the Airport and they let me park the car there while I was gone. Really nice!!!
Also very good value for the room we got. We paid around 120 bucks for a large room with 2 Queen Beds, free breakfast for 3 people and a 10$ voucher for the minibar.

name: The Westin Riverwalk
title: “best trip ever!”
text: we stayed here and it was terrific...the staff, the hotel quality, and the locations was awesome...wish we were there more time, just a quick weekend getaway...great place to go back too, the hotel is right on the river and has great views...will be back soon!

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Austin Airport Inn & Suites
title: “Very new hotel”
text:
New, clean and comfortable. Beds & bedding were wonderful ! Reasonably priced. Close to SoCo. 
Service was okay although I wouldn't say it was great. We found out that the tv in our room didn't have a power cord. And when we asked for one, we were requested to change rooms instead of being offered a power cord. We refused to change room. Really, can't they just find us a cord instead of making us pack all our stuff and move? Because I refused to move rooms, and insisted on them getting me a power cord, they eventually did find me a cord and brought it to my room. Even if this is not the Ritz, I think getting us a cord should have been their default solution instead of having their guest haul an entire family of 4's luggage to another room.
So the long and short of this is: Rooms-- very nice; Service-- a little dubious but did eventually come through when we insisted.

name: Courtyard Austin North/Parmer Lane
title: “VERY happy”
text: We don't usually stay at Courtyards because they tend to be beyond our budget. We were thrilled with this one. I presume the price is because it's on the north end of Austin.
