You have to drive to the tourist places. If you don't mind driving, this hotel is in a convenient location. The staff was friendly to a person. The lobby area is open and pleasant. We got a one bedroom suite that was huge. Each room had its own thermostat so everyone was comfortable. The Starbucks information was a bit misleading. Starbucks coffee is served in the morning for a set time. The rest of the time, you have to call the front desk to order the coffee, and you will be charged. Not complaining, just was confused to not see a starbucks in the lobby after reading the hotel webpage. We never ate at the hotel so can't comment on that. We would definitely stay here again.

name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Hotel Rex, a little gem in the heart of San Francisco”
text: Checking out today after a lovely 3 night stay at the Hotel Rex, a real gem in the heart of San Francisco. It's really close to Union Square. Check in was quick, friendly and helpful. Hotel is quirky, individual, comfortable and a lovely change from the usual 'sameness' of rooms in the big chain hotels. We asked for a quiet room away from the road beforehand and that's exactly what they gave us. Room 505 was very comfortable. My only gripe - no tea/coffee making facilities in the room. However, the Library Bar serves complimentary tea and coffee in the morning until 10am and there is a nice buffet breakfast available for $15. Oh and the resident lobby dog, Max the pug, is absolutely adorable! Even has his very own facebook page.

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “Meh.”
text: Stayed in the King Suite on the 4th floor...heard the elevators constantly. The rooms needed a refresh...especially the carpets which were stained noticeably. The restaurant was "re-working" it's menu, which meant no in-house dining option for dinner, unless a sandwich will suffice....not even a burger is available. The bathroom was awesome. The hotel location was good for tourist activites. Cornell and Davis at the door were very helpful...thank you! Some other doorguy was "on his lunch break" at 6:30pm and wouldn't help us get a cab to our dinner restaurant. Overall, an OK hotel, a bit noisy from outside noise, mostly great staff, few services.

name: The Ritz-Carlton
title: “The usual friendliness and good experience”
text: This like my other stays at various ritz properties was good. Their staff is always super friendly and helpful and go out of their way to make sure that you don't need anything. When we we checking out and waiting for my brother to pick us up 3 different staff members if we needed help with our bags or transportation. In fact we needed a cab one night to go to dinner and they gave us a ride in their s500 Mercedes with their own driver. Overall great customer service. My biggest complaint is that they don't provide free wifi, which I think is ridiculous when they charge $400+ a night then expect you to pay $15 a day for wifi. Especially when courtyard Marriott and other budget hotels give you free wifi and charge like $120 a night. Rooms here were much smaller than the ritz in new Orleans. Also the tonga room is very close if you are looking for a cool tropical themed bar for a drink.

name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Could not ask for better Service”
text: This waterfront hotel was excellent. Staff was so friendly and couldnt be more helpful in making sure you have what you need. I would like to say that our valet Neil was so friendly and asked daily if he could do anything for us. Also the valet who was there at night (sorry didnt get his name) also asked what we did for the day and if we needed anything also. I would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to visit San Fran. We walked to the pier for dining and activities and was close. Also the Hop on Hop Off tour picks you up right outside the Hotel. I cannot say enough about this place. I usually do not rate our vacations but I felt this one deserved it.

name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Close to excellent”
text:
I stayed during the Oracle World Conference. Staff helpful, and in most cases very helpful. I didn't eat here so can't review the dining quality and I didn't use the Spa. Public rooms and Bedroom clean, well furnished and comfortable. Close to union square. 
Niggles, only two. 
The mini bar was not re-stocked. There is a Walgreen over the road so I bought my own diet coke. The laundry service sent my shirts back poorly ironed. Having said that, I would stay again.

name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Nice hotel, overated though”
text:
We booked one night at the Hotel Vitale, Deluxe Waterfront King, room for 500/night. It did have a nice view, but just one little window and definitely didnt seem to be anything more than just a standard room which was priced at 300/night. If you plan on staying here, I wouldnt spend any additional money on upgraded room. I would have opted for the Mandarin Oriental with views of both bridges for roughly the same cost!
Pros: Good location, proximity to the Ferry Building was nice. Restaurant Americano was pretty good, decent service at the hotel.

name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “An oasis of calm in the city, with views over Bay Bridge”
text:
Thanks to this stay, the Joie de Vivre hotel chain is my new must-stay for USA. Blissful form beginning to end, and could not have been more different from the colour pop W Hotel in downtown where i spent the previous week.
We ended our SF trip here, following time out in Yosemite and the setting, decor and staff approach were the perfect calm and tranquility we needed. Even better, the amazing staff upgraded us to a waterfront room with the most spectacular view of the Ferry Building and the bay bridge.
Located right on the start of Embarcadero, Vitale is perfecly located for walk or street car and a few blocks away from catching a cable car. 
Amazing roof top terraces to relax with a drink and take in the view, and a spa.
Dining is excellent, great good in a very cool hang out.
The absolute quirkiest of mini bars, including canned oxygen! Free wifi, adds the cherry to the cake.

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “Great Vacation Spot”
text:
Located in great place neaqr to Union Square but far enough away from the crowds. Easy walk to Chinatown, Fishermans Wharf and oher attractions. As a Bonus Mason St/Powell Cable car stops almost outside the Hotel.
Nice inside and very clean. Free wifi which should be standard everry Hotel nowadays. Rooms well appointed and bed comfortable.

name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Best location in SF.”
text: I meant to review this hotel a long time ago. The hotel is modern, clean, and has a hip feel. It is not cheap but it's hard to think you can get that type of value anywhere else. It is in an incredible location right next to Ferry Building and farmers' market, which you could probably spend a whole day at. Easy walk to everything and beautiful view of the Bay Bridge. Chinatown and museum and other sightseeing is a short stroll away. I think one of the funniest experiences we've had is when we asked the concierge about a few restaurant locations and we kept getting a response with the location but also that we should "load the map to our ipad," even though at the time the ipad had been available for like two months maybe at most. Not sure about the hotel's amenities because we didn't use any really, but the room service was one of the best I've ever had. The bar was happening at night although it's very close to a lot of other streets with tons of great bars and food. Pretty much no complaints about this place, would definitely stay again when go back.

name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “First time experience”
text: My wife and I stayed here for two nights during our stay in SF. The staff was very welcoming, visible and helpful. Andrew(concierge) was more than willing to help out with any questions and offer recommendations for dining and entertainment. We actually acted upon his recommendations and found them to be satisfying to our needs. Thanks Andrew. The hotel has an artistic motif and is well maintained. The hotel room is furnished with cable tv,full bath,stocked fridge($),and a comfortable sleeping arrangement. I recommend a stay here but give it four stars based on the parking fee and its relative location from a sketchy area called,"Tenderloin".

name: Hotel Abri
title: “Classy comfort near Union Square!”
text: The staff alone was cool and accomodating enough to make me want to stay there every time I return. The location was very central to lots of great shopping and restaurants. The room was clean and comfortable. No complaints!

name: Hotel Triton - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Home in SF”
text: I would not think of staying elsewhere. Great vibe emanating from great people who really make you feel special. Spirit is alive here! The entire staff make you feel as if you are part of one big family/ Even the service staff is very friendly.

name: Hotel Abri
title: “Cop callers”
text: I stated here on October 5, 2012 on my birthday. I'm coming back to my room after being out for most of the day and when I get to the door of my room my key didn't work. I go down and politely asked for a new key. I showed the lady at the front desk my ID and she asked me for a credit card and then went in the back room for 5 or 6 minutes and came back and asked for another card because she didn't think that I was who I really was after staying at this hotel for over 40 other stays there. Ten minutes later two police were at my door because she and her two co workers had called them.

name: Hotel Abri
title: “Tiny rooms but everything else was great”
text: You can't beat the location, right by Union Square. This is a boutique hotel. The service was very good as the front desk staff always was attentive and informative. The room is very small but nicely appointed and modern.

name: Inn at the Opera
title: “Pleasant stay”
text:
The location is good. There are nice restaurants in the vicinity and obviously it is near the Opera House as well.
We enjoyed the complimentary breakfast. 
The rooms were nice.
The lift is a bit small and some passageways a bit narrow - a la Europe.
I would not recommend driving here because valet parking is $25 per day and there is very little on-street parking in the area.
Overall it was a very good experience.

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “pmiranda”
text: Location is very close to Union Square shopping, restaurants, China Town, so you are able to walk to those places. Pleasant helpful staff. Concierges, especially David were helpful with directions, restaurants, touring advice etc. Hotel room very nicely furnished, spacious, room was very neat and CLEAN! Reasonably priced for location. I have stayed here several times a year for business, and this is always my first choice!

name: Inn at the Opera
title: “Needs Improvement”
text: Great location, near superb eateries, clubs & attractions... But as a regular traveller, I highly recommend that they clean the room and hallway carpets. Woke up weezing, and I do not suffer from allergy issues...

name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Don't Turn Left !”
text:
After a 11 hour flight from the UK, we where very tired, and went for a walk around San francisco.
We tried to find Union square, but turn left when leaving the hotel instead of turning right and ended up in a "area" which was not pleasant.
We passed several soup kitchens and many beggers on the street.
The hotel is not far from union square, if you head in the right direction, but that was my fault, not the hotels.
The hotel is fine, staff very friendly, the coffee in the morning, the wine tasting in the afternoon are great touches by the hotel.

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “Friendly Boutique Hotel”
text:
location is very close to Union Square shopping, restaurants, etc
Pleasant helpful staff.
Concierges, especially David were helpful with directions, restaurants, touring advice etc.
Hotel room very nicely furnished, spacious, clean.Reasonably priced for location.
I would definately return

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great Hotel”
text: We recently spent 7 nights. Great location, only 2 blocks from Fisherman's Wharf. The location was very accessible to the trolley, muni and cable streetcars making it easy to get around. The staff were very helpful and the Gen. Mgr. Jan went out of her way to make our stay enjoyable after our trip was delayed due to Hurricane Sandy. King sized bed was extremely comfortable, and the rooms were small (as the norm in SF), but were clean. Lobby was very inviting. The wine hour from 5-6 was a pleasant surprise. a nice way to mix and meet with others staying in the hotel. We would definitely recommend this hotel and visit it again.

name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Quirky and arty but may not be for those with kids”
text:
Overall OK. Small hotel with muted colours, subdued lighting, dark furniture, lots of art throughout. 1920s style. Not mainstream. Good points:
*Well located hotel. Ten minute walk to Union Square and about two minute walk to cable car stop.
*Free glass of wine every day
*Friendly and helpful staff
*Small, friendly and cosy bar area within the library: I saw quite a few single, mature guests who were able to meet, drink and chat in non-intimidating surroundings. It was very welcoming and laid back
*Weekly movie night in the library area - big screen and projector
*Couple of bone-shaker bikes provided
*Free wi-fi
*If you like art and books, you'll probably love this place
Downsides:
*Room and bathroom were very small. Double beds were small too. Our 9 year old slept in one whilst we were cramped in the other.
*Some of the wiring and cabling left quite a bit to be desired - tacked to carpet and what seemed to be a number of overloaded plugs were jutting out underneath the desk
*one slow, small, cramped elevator
*kids seem a little out of place here as the target audience doesn't seem to be families, although our child stayed free
*not much choice for dining - breakfast buffet only and no kids menu
Probably a great place to stay if you're into art and the like or the drawing room culture.

name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “A great historic literary hotel!”
text: very conveniently located near Union Square. Room was clean,comfortable and furnished in appropriate vintage decor. Only thing missing was an in rooom coffee set up. Excellent food at the wedding we attended...and also the buffet breakfast. Great helpful and friendly staff. A great place to stay!!!

name: Inn at the Opera
title: “Absolutely wonderful”
text: Recommend to anyone who wants great service and doesn't want the big name places.

name: Inn at the Opera
title: “Nice boutique hotel close to theaters and great restaurants”
text:
I've stayed at this hotel twice now and I've enjoyed my stay each time. I've stayed in the small hotel type room as well as a full one bedroom with living room and kitchen. We were made to feel welcome the moment we entered and check in was a breeze. The continental breakfast hours go until 10am which is great for late risers. They have afternoon cookies at the front desk and someone available around the clock to assist you.
The location is ideal for shows at the opera, ballet or the nearby Orpheum theater. There are wonderful restaurants within blocks and easy access to the great public transportation -- a BART station is only a few blocks away. The area is quiet after around 10pm though; if you're looking for nightlife, you'll have to travel to other areas as there were only a handful of small bars in the area.

name: The Driskill
title: “Will be back”
text:
I know where I'm staying the next time I'm in Austin. Hotel has a unique exterior that only leads to an exceptional interior. Upon entering the lobby, the dark woodwork shines in the light. The place certainly has character and you can tell the hotel has been around for many years, but everything is in great condition. The staff was welcoming and friendly, regardless of whether it was the front desk or house cleaning. Everyone was smiling and asking if they could help in anyway. 
I stayed in the Senate room, which didn't have much of a view but loved the room. The bed was very comfortable and I want to find out where they buy their sheets. The radio was on a low level and was set to classical music. Not typically my style but it was very calming that I kept it on the whole weekend. Room also had a nice sitting area with a nice couch and chairs. Free wi-fi in the rooms was also a nice touch.
Excellent location on 6th Street, right in the heart of everything. Plenty of bars/restaurants within walking distance. While I didn't eat in the hotel restaurant, I did enjoy the bar, which had plenty of seating to wind down during the evening.
While this property might be slightly more than other hotels, the minimal price difference is worth it considering the quality of the property and service of the staff.

name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel
title: “Seen better days”
text: Hadn't stayed in the hotel in years, and now I remember why. Dated, very small rooms. Painfully slow internet service. Stayed here with Priceline -- a fact that the check-in receptionist insisted on announcing to everyone standing nearby, as if I should be ashamed by that fact. Presented my Marriott Rewards card, which produced a new annoncement that "you won't earn anything with this," given the Priceline rate.

name: Residence Inn Austin Downtown / Convention Center
title: “More good points and bad points”
text: We stayed at this property twice recently at either end of our holiday. We specifically wanted a one bedroom suite as one of us gets up earlier than the other, so we only looked at properties that had this. I don't agree with other posters that the rooms here are large. If you are expecting just a hotel room, then yes, you would find the rooms large. But this property bills itself as a residence. In fact, the one bedroom suite was very cramped for two people and their luggage. Basically the one bedroom suite is the same as the studio with a wall down the middle. The photos on the web site are very accurate - the layout looked cramped and it was. Other than being cramped, our first stay was very good. The main reason we chose this suite property over others was because of the hot breakfast included. It was good but monotonous - exactly the same thing every day. They could vary the hot items a bit. We loved the free wireless in the rooms - I wish all hotels had that! The happy hour during the week is GREAT! If you are a light eater, you could easily make this your supper. There was always a hot item and a green salad. And help yourself to the beer and wine. And the wine was actually pretty good.The staff at the front desk and on the door are very cheery and helpful. We did have trouble getting help from the cleaning staff - called the front desk 3 times to get extra hangers. Eventually talked to the cleaning staff but none spoke enough English to understand our request! Our second stay was a bit of a surprise. This time our suite was on the back side of the hotel. Right at 10 pm some band started up some where that ratttled the windows! We never did figure out where the racket was coming from. The hotel is 2 blocks from the party district (6th Street) - I thought that would be far enough but obviously not! This was on a Friday night so this may only be a problem on weekends. We insisted on being moved. Unfortunately the hotel did not have any one bedrooms left that were not on the back side of the hotel. But they gave us two studios next door to each other which worked out well.

name: Inn at the Opera
title: “Great location - close to the best Opera or ballet”
text:
The reason for our visit to San Francisco was to see the Romeo and Juliet Ballet in a world class venue. This hotel is practically across the street from that location in an excellent and untouristy part of the city. 
We had booked a suite and were very pleased with what we received. Our suite was situated on the top floor in the back. Most importantly we had real privacy and quiet. There was no one above us and there were no common walls with any other rooms. Great! We had 2 complete and roomy bathrooms and 2 flat screen tv's. There was a large entry foyer from which one could enter either the bedroom suite or through french doors connecting to a separate living room with its own complete bath. The king bed was very comfy. I like to stay up late and my wife likes to go to bed early. I respect her quiet time so it is important that I not disturb her. With the great floor plan she wasn't bothered at all. There was a small kitchenette with frig as well. Everything from the carpets to the bathroom fixtures were clean and of good quality. Nothing showed signs of wear. 
The included breakfast was continental in style, typically adequate but not gourmet, served in a beautiful wood paneled dining room. The coffee was excellent. Old world and very classy with an art and musical feel. 
It was our impression that most of the other clients staying here are elder, sophisticated and well traveled. You won't be finding any bumbling and rude tourists at this location. They'd never find it.
 We booked a limo from the airport through the hotel staff and it was great as well; very professional and courteous treatment. I checked and the price was only about $5 more than for a taxi from SFO to the hotel. We'll do exactly the same thing next time. The price from SFO was $45. 
Its only a couple of blocks to Market Street where you can hop on the "F" Trolley. It will take you all the way to the historic clock tower or anywhere inbetween for just $2, or 75 cents if you're a senior or close to it. These trollies are restored and were built in the 40's. A great feel and ride. Mostly locals take it. Just take exact change and pay onboard. 
It was important for us that this hotel is practically across the street from the War Memorial Opera House where one can see the best Ballet and Opera the west coast of the US has to offer. The website for the Ballet is: www.sfballet.org.
All in all a great experience.

name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “A short stay that'll stay with me for a long time”
text:
We stayed in San Francisco for 3 days to see the sights and made a last minute booking with Hotel Rex because of it's low price and surprisingly high ratings. We weren't disappointed and neither will you be if you stay here. The hotel itself is small, not boutique small but it's definitely not high volume. The rooms are very neat, well presented with an interesting literature based theme. The hotel is also quite green focused (as is the way in San Francisco), however I was pleased that the 'green' options were that, optional and I did not feel pressured by any means. Hotel Rex provides you with the usual amenities such as cable & a mini bar and we were encouraged by staff to use the mini bar for what ever we needed and to just remove any mini bar items we needed to.
What set them apart for me was one particular night of my stay. 
I had to make arrangements for my girlfriend and my 7 year anniversary dinner. Both the bellman and the concierge helped me greatly going through a number of options for me as well as providing me a reservation at a fantastic nearby restaurant, Palominos. With a great seat along with a wonderful walk along the pier I owe all the boyfriend points I earned to the staff at Hotel Rex. 
As we arrived home after a fantasic dinner and walk we were greeted with champagne and chocolate covered strawberries! I have never reviewed any other hotels I've stayed at before but I felt obligated to spread the word about this wonderful hotel.
Stay and you won't be disappointed

name: Orchard Garden Hotel
title: “Clean, quiet and friendly”
text: I picked Orchard Garden for our family vacation for the location (and positive reviews on Trip Advisor, of course!) I wanted my kids to experience the 'real' SF, rather than the purely touristy feel of Fisherman's Wharf. It was a good choice. Location is ideal... easy walking distance to Chinatown and Union Square (where we caught the cable car for an afternoon in Fisherman's Wharf). The hotel staff was friendly. Room size was adequate. Our room was very clean, fresh and unusually quiet. We didn't hear any noise from the hallway or our neighbors. We enjoyed breakfast in the hotel restaurant, Roots. The menu is pretty limited, but the food was delicious and, bonus, organic. One oddity -- the only vent in the bathroom was directly into the bedroom. As a result, the steam from the shower lingered and even fogged the bedroom windows. I would stay here again on either business or pleasure.

name: Inn at the Opera
title: “still the best!!!!”
text:
one would think that sometimes over time, hotels would lose their appeal. well, inn at the opera is not that hotel. the moment you arrive you are greeted like an old friend. the front end people (Evita, Alex, etc) are incredibly efficient. the rooms are clean, upgrades are continuing, the housekeeping staff (Betty, Maria) always are available to you and the breakfast dining is adding new items. The Asst. GM Sean and Javier the front end manager, are so accomodating one almost feels like the welcomed long lost cousin. 
the convenience of being steps from the opera house or symphony hall are the main allure. but do not forget it is also only a feet feet more to the asian art museum and some lovely restaurants.

name: The Driskill
title: “Best location in Austin; for those who love classic hotels, this is IT.”
text:
Chose this hotel for its historic roots and location to the night life of Austin. If you prefer clone style chain, hotels, this will be a departure. It has the elegance, style and vibe that is authentic to hotels in the early to mid 1900's.
Front desk staff was super friendly and helpful. Everyone we encountered had that Texas super-friendly (but not cloyingly so) attitude that makes you feel welcome.
Pros: 
Location to 6th street restaurants and nightlife
Absolutely beautiful interior fixtures and decor that fit the property
Top-notch service that fits the feel of the hotel
big windows and nice view
very comfortable beds, linens and bath area
I wanted to live in the bar area, it is so cool.
Valet parking is fast and friendly
Cons:
Just a little pricey
Some of the hallway carpet was a little grungy and looked like a couple of scenes from "The Shining"
Some claims of the place being haunted -we saw no ghosts.
We were there for a special occasion and the front desk staff were excited and pleased to offer an upgraded room. -That's a nice touch.

name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel
title: “Great location and very good service”
text: Enjoyed a one night stay, great location. Front desk was very helpful. Room was pretty small. They have redone the front entrance and lobby bar since the last time I was there, a nice improvement. Overall a nice property, not sure it's a 6 or 7 Marriott level or worth the everyday price but if you get a deal I say take it.

name: The Ritz-Carlton
title: “Outstanding”
text: We stayed in a club level room at this Ritz for a getaway weekend, and we were consistently impressed with the quality of service and the consistency of the staff. The club level offers an outstanding all day food service that really allows you to be flexible with your other plans and reservations. While the external facade of the Ritz makes you wonder if they originally planned on locating in Las Vegas, the internal features and services are first class. Highly recommend.

name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Great experience”
text: As a visitor to San Fransisco I relied on the hotel staff and they did not dissapoint. Always helpful with arrangements. Stayed here because of the location and it was wonderful,near the ferry terminal but loved the yoga and all the other amenities offered.

name: Orchard Garden Hotel
title: “Large beautiful room, excellent location, WONDERFUL staff”
text:
Our first time to San Francisco, so we chose this hotel based on Internet information only. But it turned out to be a hit. It is close to everything. The room was larger than expected, very clean, very nicely designed. It was very quiet. The bed was very comfortable. And there was nice desk space to work. So, the room was beautiful. But the hit of this hotel was its front-desk staff and a tall smiling gentleman who literally walked into the middle of the street, down a block or so, just to hail a cab for us. It was raining, the traffic was light but steady, and right out there was this guy going all out for me and my kids, who he didn't know from Adam. My kids were amazed at how dedicated he was. And when we needed a driver during rush hour to take us to another city, right at cabbie-shift-change time - which makes finding a cabbie impossible - this guy dialed a reliable driver he knew and in minutes we had a private livery (limo) driver taking us to Oakland. Unbelievable.
The female front desk staff was just the same. Very friendly, super helpful, never in your way but always there to help. My kids and I travel often - Chicago, DC, NYC - and I have never previously run into a consistently-wonderful front desk group. They were ALL nice, and all pleasant, but not in a smarmy, overbearing way. Just like...family welcoming you back, genuinely. Since the lobby is narrow, you must walk by them as you go to the elevator, so passing by them was always a nice warm welcome back. A stab in the dark for us in finding a hotel, but it was fantastic. A great hotel.

name: Coventry Motor Inn
title: “Good value in the end”
text: We stayed here in Sep 2011. When we arrived, the fellow on the desk was quite rude as there was apparently an error with our booking and somehow 2 rooms were booked instead of 1. He was quite angry and threatened to charge us for both. After he calmed down, he was reasonably helpful, the room was generous, clean and the beds very comfortable. The free parking is what brought us here and was great. The location is handy to many good value restaurants and the bus is convenient. We really enjoyed staying in the marina district. So after our rocky start I would say be careful when booking on the website, but overall this is a good budget choice for families.

name: The Driskill
title: “And then the power went out.”
text: The Driskill is in a great part of town, close to everything. The people working there were very friendly. The hotel definitely has a Texas feel. The rooms are on the small side. It's an older building. On our last night at the hotel the power went out from 1am until 815am. We were given glow sticks so we could find our way back to the room. The next day everything was in disarray from the power outrage regarding anything with computers. Credit cards needed to be used the old fashion way and there sound system reverted to playing Christmas music even though it was the end of January. What can you do. Technology. On the weekends the hotel is very close to a street where the University students go to get completely plastered. If you have small children they might see some sites they haven't seen before.

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “Chic, comfortable, convenient”
text: My stay at The Orchard was delightful, and I'd likely choose it again for my next SF visit. The room was very pleasant, fresh, and quiet, despite being in the downtown area. Bed was super comfy, and the bathroom spacious. Plush robes await in the closets. Breakfast room also very pleasant, though the service was slow (perhaps because a large group came in from outside the hotel for some celebration). Just a couple blocks from Union Square. For the environmentally conscious, you'll be pleased to find it's a "Green" hotel.

name: The Stratford
title: “Small rooms, but great location and safe area!”
text:
Yes the rooms are small, but they were clean and comfy. 
Breakfast is included, which was cereal, toast, muffins, fruit, juice and tea/coffee. 
The location of the hotel is its best feature. Right outside your door is the cable cars, union square, Westfield. The area is also safe and busy, with plenty of other tourists. Places to eat are right across the road. Would definitely stay here again.
Being on a busy street we thought it would be noisy, but we heard nothing at night. No A/C but there are ceiling fans.

name: Marina Motel
title: “great location”
text:
We had an adorable little room in the courtyard, and loved our stay here! Were here for 3 nights. Within walking distance to great cafes, restaurants, and bars as well as the Palace of Fine Arts - beautiful! There are bus stops within a block or so that can take you about anywhere you'd want to go in the city. We bought bus passes at the Walgreen's just down the street and were good to go - very convenient. 
On a chilly day, turning the corner to enter the courtyard is like walking into summer time! The flowers are beautiful and everything is well maintained. Make sure to try the Cedar Hill Kitchen and Smokehouse just a block away - GREAT bbq!

name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Good locaion but quite cold”
text: We stayed at this hotel in December.The hotel is well located. Many cafés ans restaurants available on Sutter street and around. But, the room was cold. We could not adjust the heat in the room because it was a central heat system. On top of that, the water was warm not hot so we could not warm ourselves with a good hot shower. We could also clearly hear the street noise even though we were located on the 8th floor. It was so bad that we tought that the windows were opened on the first night.

name: Inn at the Opera
title: “Perfect, almost: a few notes”
text:
It is difficult to draw negative comments about this hotel and I do not want to repeat the same applause about this hotel. So, I just make a few notes that may be helpful.
1. I stayed at the Inn for a conference at Moscone Center. I found the commute to and from the conference site somewhat dangerous, especially after sunset, with so many zombie-ish people at every corner, sometimes at every door on the streets. In fact, it was a bit of post-apocalyptic experience. I saw two arrests for the five days I had to commute. If I were there for opera, symphony, or ballet, the location couldn't have been better.
2. The room is small. If I had a child, it would have certainly been difficult to stay in. Also, there was no desk, so working in the room was almost out of the question.

name: Coventry Motor Inn
title: “Limited facilities but great location”
text:
This is our regular hotel in San Francisco. We have tried Union Square, etc but the Marina area is so much more appealing. Why? Walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf; great shops and restaurants on the local streets (Union and Chestnut); the Marina and views of the GG Bridge, and the wonderful Greens restaurant in Fort Mason. Plus local buses easily take you into Downtown (or bring you back if you walked). 
Staying at the Coventry feels like being a local which is why we keep coming back. 
The only issue is traffic noise from Lombard Street - if you are light sleeper ask for a room at the back. We also feel that some updating of the furniture and TVs would not go a miss. But small gripes and we're already planning our next visit.

name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Location, location, location”
text: Nice hotel, nice bar, people that work there are nice, location is near all the fun locations bars, restaurants, trolleys, the only thing and Its not about the hotel but be warned as soon as you leave the hotel people called San francisco artists will ask you for money handouts, help. I live in Texas we call them homeless, drug addicts, scum smelly people. Thank Nancy pelosi your town needs real help, but the food 4 stars

name: The Queen Anne Hotel
title: “Queen Anne Hotel”
text: Victorian parlor is a delightful place to curl up and read with comfortable, cozy seating and two fireplaces. Afternoon sherry and cookies in the parlor is lovely. Breakfast was adequate but nothing special. There is a nice Whole Foods a few blocks away. if you like to walk and don't mind hills, the location is ideal. We have stayed here a couple of times and look forward to returning.

name: The Stratford
title: “Great location”
text: Great location right around the corner from Union Square, in a great shopping area. The historic cable car runs right in front of the hotel, and you can catch hop-on/hop-off bus tours right around the corner at Union Square. Breakfast is provided in the tea room, basic toast, muffins, cereal, etc. Rooms are smaller, but still had enough room to maneuver, and luckily had a ceiling fan which helped as the rooms got a bit warm. The front desk staff were quite friendly.

name: Beresford Arms
title: “Great Location/Ammenities”
text: Spent three days last week at the Beresford Arms hotel. First, it is very conveniently located to Union Square, cable car lines,clubs, restaurants, etc. The hotel rooms are a little dated, but clean. We had a Jr Jacuzzi suite at 134.00 a night and what a deal for that area. Plus parking was only 23 dollars a day with free in-out privileges. That is small in comparison to some of the hotels in the financial district at 50.00 plus a day. Now if you are thinking Jacuzzi suite you might conjour up a big hot tub..well it's actually a tub and shower combo with jacuzzi jets, however, after a long day walking everyhwere, just filling the tub up and sitting in there with the jets running was very nice indeed for one with a sore body and feet. Whats included with the hotel is a continental breakfast (nothing special just some danishes/croissants/Coffee, but not bad). Also, every day from 4-5:30pm they serve wine and cheese which was just what I needed before soaking in the tub. Mind you I am a pretty big guy and I fit in the tub just fine. The people at the hotel were very nice and seemed to accomodate just about everything and would always ask how everything was going. The room was spacious and had a little kitchenette with refridgerator/sink and some plates,spoons,glasses, but no corkscrew/bottle opener, so bring you own if you need to crack a bottle of wine open. The beds were very comfortable, but I have a beef with the pillows which were not comfortable. That is a little pet peave of mine. I need a comfortable bed and pillow and should have brought my own pillow. The room is in need of updating and the furniture seems like something from the early 70s'. But for the price and it was clean you cannot beat the price or location. Many restaurants were close, including a good Thai restaurant and liquor stores on both sides. Overall I would stay there again, however, I tend to never stay at the same place twice and have stayed at the best and some of the worst in SF. This is in the middle of the pack. One selling point for us was there was four of us in one room and they provided 2 queen beds without additional charges for additional people. So check it out and decide for yourself. If you are looking for a Fairmont/Drake then stay there. If you want a middle of the road with some amenities then this will suite you just fine. It has charm and a nice lobby to sit and chat with people. Also, free Wi-fi and computers to use in the lobby.

name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Great Boutique Hotel, Great Location!”
text: The Hotel Rex is literally a block from Union Square so it is close to everything but off the main roads so it is quiet. After touring around San Francisco we decided we couldn't have picked a better location to stay. This is a very clean well run boutique hotel with all the charm you would expect. It has a small and comfy lobby with an adjoining bar (complimentary coffee and tea available in the morning, a glass of wine from 4-6 in the evening (and before and after it's just $6 a glass - a bargain in San Francisco!) and a small restaurant with great food. Our room was at the back of the hotel and was large, quiet and had two comfy double beds, a desk, a large tv, chairs, a stocked mini fridge (with room for us to slip in a bottle of wine), robes and slippers. All of the staff were wonderful and made us feel totally welcome (even though we arrived hours too early on our first day). They told us to go out and enjoy our day and our luggage would be in our room when we returned - and it was. They were happy to book us an airport shuttle and keep our luggage while we enjoyed our last day in San Francisco. They gave us suggestions for places to eat and to visit and gave us maps with our route marked out. This really is a lovely place to stay and I will return!

name: Beresford Arms
title: “Wonderful stay with two young children”
text:
We stayed 8 nights at the Beresford Arms with our two young children, ages 3 years and 7 months. My husband's family has been coming here for years. We came for a week when our oldest was one year old and we chose it again now because we are able to get a one bedroom apartment (the "junior suite") for around $179/night. The decor is 80's outdated, but I find this hotel so comfortable and friendly, I don't mind at all. The one bedroom apartment is spacious; in fact, the bathroom (complete with bidet!) is so spacious that our son slept there in his pack and play! The street noise (particularly the sirens) woke him, so we moved him into the bathroom where there are no windows. It is true that there is street noise, but hey!, this is the big city. Traffic is the surf of the city, as I've heard said.
The apartment also has a full kitchen, invaluable when traveling with small children. 
We enjoyed the coffee, pastries and fruit each morning for breakfast, saving a trip out with the kids. And the afternoon wine and cheese hour was a fabulous time to get out of the room after nap. The attendant would bring my daughter her own juice box.
In fact, all the front desk staff was extremely friendly and kind to my children and always helped me get my big double stroller in and out of the door. There are two great playgrounds within 1 mile walking distance; one up the top of the hill across from the Grace Cathedral and one at Yerba Buena Gardens near the Moscone Conference Center (where my husband was attending a conference and we would meet him for lunch). It is the perfect central location with kids, especially if you're willing to put some miles on the stroller and get some great exercise. We walked to the Ferry Building and tried samples and ate lunch. I walked them down to Fisherman's Wharf and back a couple times (a *great* workout)! Finally, one of the cable cars turns around and loads passengers only a couple blocks away, near Union Square. 
To sum up, I highly recommend this lovely hotel when traveling with children.

name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Very unique and friendly hotel!”
text: We stayed at Hotel Monaco for 3 nights in a junior suite and really liked the hotel. We had four in a room, which was a little tight, but it worked fine. The location was great, close to Union Square shops and walking distance to many places in the city. The rooms were average size, but very comfortable and unique in design and decor. The staff was friendly and very helpful. The concierge was great about making restaurant reservations and suggestions. Very nice wine/cheese/snack receptions in lobby each evening at 5. Had on the street room on third floor which was a bit noisy with street sounds. Overall, a great choice for a hotel, much preferable to larger hotel setting.

name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “You should definitely stay here!”
text: Hotel Rex has become my go-to place to to stay in the city with its great rates and central location - everything is within walking distance, or just a short cab ride away. The rooms are comfortable and the staff is really friendly - we asked for a recommendation for crab outside of the Wharf, and the concierge gave us a great suggestion for a place nearby that was perfect for what we wanted. This is definitely the place to stay if you're looking for a relaxed, easy stay in SF. The ammenities are better than average, the rooms and the bathrooms are clean, and the location is perfect!

name: Hotel Union Square
title: “Total Relaxation”
text:
We were only there for 2 nights on our way to board our Ship to travel home. The staff were wonderful and could not have been more obliging. We were offered a choice of rooms. Each morning there was coffee the foyer, and in the evening a happy Hour from 5 until 6 with complimentary wine.
The room was immaculate and the bed so comfortable we overslept the 1st night. I could recommend this hotel to anyone. If I am ever in San Francisco again this will definitely be my choice of Hotel.

name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
title: “Ah-mazing stay. Great location, great service.”
text:
What a fantastic choice for staying in SF. We took the BART in (Bay Area Rail Transit). Every airport should offer a train service from their airport into downtown, as its so convenient. Just remember to be mindful of being courteous to the other riders as your luggage, if not put aside properly, could be a hindrance. Its such an easy walk from the Embarcadero BART to the Hilton in the Financial / Chinatown area. Its also an easy walk from the hotel to many of the major attractions -- Market building, Fisherman's Wharf etc. 
I have to say the treatment they give the Hilton Honours members is the best I've ever rec'd. I'm gold and was given a gorgeous bay view executive floor room after booking the cheapest double. When I book a hotel I book a room I'd be happy with so I won't be disappointed and they not only gave me an upgrade, but a several level upgrade. Madonna, I'm not sure of her title, but should be commended for such fantastic treatment of an HH member. 
The rooms, which I understand are pretty much similar all across the board, save for suites and different bed size choice, are very nice. Not large, not small, but the most efficient layout of any hotel I've stayed in. Its reminiscent of a suite on a cruise ship. 
The furnishings and fixturing are all very nice and lux. And the room was so clean.
One room comment that comes up often is about the sound level. Yes, one night you could hear what must have been a party at a bars patio, but it was only the one night and by 11pm it was silent. 
If you get a chance I highly recommend getting lounge access. As the breakfast is wonderful, with fruits, egg wrap, cheeses, hard boiled eggs, pastries, yougurt, breads, cereals, juices, teas, and a automatic latte/espresso machine. And in the eve there was more cheese, vegetables, and 3 hot choices as well as asst beverages. The room attendants were always running around and really good. Not as polished as some of the lounges I've been at in ICs etc, but fast, friendly and efficient. The lounge gets busy at breakfast, but not in as busy in the eve. 
Once again, thank you Madonna and all whom made this such a fantastic, memorable stay.

name: The Ritz-Carlton
title: “The Crème de la Crème”
text:
The Ritz! San Francisco's finest. Life can't get any better.
A stately exterior--a beautiful and elegant interior--an ambiance that shouts "exclusive luxury." That's The Ritz. Guests are warmly greeted upon arrival by a well-trained, attentive staff and offered a glass of champagne, my favorite beverage--how thoughtful.
Everything was perfect from beginning to end. Ambiance and service met every expectation. We can't wait to return.

name: Orchard Garden Hotel
title: “Excellent location, dodgy toilet...”
text:
I am all for eco-friendly hotels and recycling etc, but when it directly relates to the room I find it a bit much. Our toilet didn't flush well or consistently, which I assume was due to water saving efforts on the hotel's behalf but which ruined our experience at the hotel.
We had a two double bed room which was relatively small compared to other rooms we stayed in. The location was excellent though and we could walk anywhere we needed to go.
I found the staff fairly unhelpful though an unfriendly which was not what I experienced in other American hotels.
The location of this hotel meant our stay was satisfactory but the toilet and staff meant a stay that could have been excellent was only average.

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “Great location, value and service.”
text: Located in a superb location, we enjoyed our stay in this boutique hotel.

name: Hotel Union Square
title: “Great location and hotel, horrible parking story!”
text: Hotel has a great location right downtown in walking distance to a lot of attractions. Rooms are small as mentioned in the other Trip Advisor reviews, but well furnished and the front desk staff was very nice. We took advantage of the evening wine tasting (which was just a couple bottles put out in the lobby). Everything was looking good, until we went to leave at the end of the trip. We gave the parking attendant our valet ticket, and he pulled around a similar silver Dodge Avenger, but not ours. He went back down to the parking garage, produced 2 more sliver Dodge Avengers, neither of which were ours either. He didn't seem too bothered that they didn't seem to know where our car was. We went to the front desk and they were as confused as much as we were. After several more frantic searches, we finally found it, but the valet was totally going to let us drive off with someone else's car! Beware!

name: Marina Motel
title: “great place”
text: We just stayed at the Marina Motel for 4 nights and had an exellent time. We were in rooms 20 and 21 which share a bathroom so it is great for a family or 2 couples. The rooms are a bit small but nicely decorated. Our rooms were in the back corner of the courtyard so they were very quiet. There is enough parking for everybody, it is a tight squeeze at times but really you just want to park once and use the bus when going into town. There is a busstop on Lombard not even a block away but forget about that one, walk one block down to Chestnut and take the number 30 bus into town. It will just about get you anywhere. We did get the coupon for the 2 for 1 breakfast but decided that Judy's was a bit expensive especially when across the street from the hotel (on Divisadero/Lombard) you can have breakfast for about 4 dollars. They aren't very fast but the food was good. There are plenty of restaurants in the area as well so when you don't want to eat in town you can always get something near the hotel. All in all it was a perfect city hotel. You can get to the sightseeing points quickly and easily and there are enough amenities near the hotel (a 24 hr wallgreens for example) as well.

name: Coventry Motor Inn
title: “Good Stay”
text: Clean with comfortable beds .Well situated for getting around San Fran without the car.Parking is included which is a plus in a busy city. No breakfast which is a bit of a nuisance but there is a very good diner down the street

name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Liked the Rex very much”
text: I have never been to San Francisco before. After some research (this site mostly) I decided to book Hotel Rex. We liked the hotel very much. It was very clean and very friendly. We were in a nice location, and walked around Union Square to take in the sights. I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for something that was not a typical stay = Not a Best Western. This hotel had style and character, and was very comfy and cozy. Food in this neighbourhood was excellent.

name: The Stratford
title: “On a budget? This hotel is for you.”
text:
Right in the heart of downtown near Union Square, on the Powell cable car line and a block from the Bart (easy access to airport). This was a fantastic location for visiting all of the usual sightseeing spots and much cheaper than neighbouring hotels in the immediate area.
We had a quiet inside room. Cozy, but spotless. I imagine the street front rooms may be a bit noisy due to the cable car running by. The staff is very friendly and helpful. There is a continental breakfast included in a cheerful breakfast room...coffee, toast and muffins. We chose to eat a big breakfast at a historical diner "Sears" just up the street.
We would definitely stay here again

name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Pleasant Experience at Hotel Monaco - GREAT location!”
text:
My wife and son accompanied me on a business trip to San Francisco. On a previous visit, we had stayed at the Omni (GREAT hotel) near the Financial District, but on this visit we wanted to be a little closer to Union Square. 
Reading the reviews on Trip Advisor (as I always do) we settled on the Hotel Monaco. It turned out to be a great decision.
 During our cab ride from the airport, I explained to the driver where we had previously stayed and I asked him about the Hotel Monaco. He said that while, in his opinion, it wasn't quite the Omni, it was indeed a very nice place with a good reputation for service. He did, however, caution us that it was near the edge of the "Tenderloin" section of SF and that we should not venture too far in that direction, particularly at night. This, of course, mirrored several comments that I had seen in several Trip Advisor reviews when talking about the Hotel Monaco's location. In point of fact, however, the location (two blocks off of Union Square in the middle of the Theatre District) turned out to be one of the best things about the hotel. Convenient access to the cable cars, near Union Square, and within walking distance to the Westfield Mall.
Knowing that we would be arriving before normal check-in, I had contacted the hotel to make arrangements for an early check-in. Communication was great and I had received 
an email from the Front Desk Manager assuring me that we could be accommodated. Sure enough, when we arrived (nearly three hours before normal check-in) our room was ready and available to us. Is that fantastic customer service, or what? (Thank you Christine.) The room was clean, smartly decorated, and the beds were very comfortable. The nightly hosted wine hour was a very nice touch.
I would recommend obtaining a free Klimpton InTouch Membership before your visit. The membership entitles you to free internet and a number of other worthwhile services. 
All in all, my family and I thoroughly enjoyed this "boutique" hotel experience. Service, location and class....Hotel Monaco has it all.

name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
title: “Great Location & Comfortable Room with a View”
text:
We were delightfully impressed with our stay here. The rooms were clean & updated. We had a bay view that was breathtaking- there was construction going on next door, so if you are planning on working in the room during the day you might notice the workers & noise (but it was not enough to affect our stay, we just closed the blinds). 
All of our contact with staff were genuine & enthusiastic- I was impressed.
The location is great with restaurants & nightlife within blocks. 
The executive lounge breakfast is the best I have seen with fresh fruit, a variety of choices & a beautiful setting.
We got a great rate & will be returning on our next visit to the area.

name: The Ritz-Carlton
title: “Best hotel stay ever! WOW!”
text: What an absolutely perfect hotel! We loved every minute we spent at The Ritz Carlton SF. The staff is truly amazing, we felt instantly welcome as if we had known these people for years. They really want you to feel comfortable and at home. I have never been treated so well by hotel staff any where! Every time we came back it was as if they were waiting for us to say "Welcome back". Perfectly appointed room, we even had a nice view. Everything you would expect from a hotel of this caliber! They set the standard. Super comfortable beds, perfect bathroom, flat screen TV w/ HD programming, even middle of the night shoe polish service. I have stayed at other hotels in SF that think they are comparable - they are not even close. The Ritz has done it again - they are the best - I wish other businesses would treat me so well. We will only stay at this hotel when visiting SF. I love the location too, it is a perfect base camp for seeing the city. We easily walked down to the Warf and to Union Square, we took the cable cars or taxi's back up the hill, even walked back up from Union Square once - not a bad walk. What a beautiful place to enjoy this city from! So many other things I could say about this hotel -- go stay there and you will see! The perfect blend of having what you want and need when you want and need it! This is what customer service is all about! This is not just a hotel for the wealthy, we are far from wealthy, we were treated like kings and felt very comfortable. You will not feel out of place at the Ritz, they will not allow it. All other hotels pale.

name: Orchard Garden Hotel
title: “Repeat visitor and still impressed”
text: The Orchard Garden Hotel has exceeded our expectations--for a second time. We returned because we love the location, the rooms, the green concept and the staff. Pay a little extra for the "view" rooms and be treated with a balcony and spacious quarters. We will look forward to returning to this great boutique hotel again.

name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Great value and wonderful location.”
text: Only thing missing from the room was coffee. Complimentary coffee service is in the lobby.

name: Laurel Inn, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Great location and value”
text: We've had several great stays at the Laurel Inn. We love the mid century modern design and the amenities. The rooms we stayed in had a kitchenette which is helpful for preparing drinks, coffee and snacks in between shopping and dining within walking distance. Fillmore and Sacramento shopping are easy walks from the Inn and are packed with unique shops and restaurants. There is a bar adjacent to the Inn which offers small dishes in addition to beverages. All this at a great value in San Francisco.

name: Laurel Inn, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “CUTE AND COMFORTABLE”
text: We stayed here in September of 2011 while my husband was at a conference. We actually walked all the way over the hill to the Chestnut street, it was a great workout. The room was nicely decorated, but I think the sofa bed could use a new mattress. They charge for parking otherwise they'd get an excellent rating from me. There's a cute bar/appetizer lounge next door which is very convenient for nightcaps. Overall we really liked it and might stay here for the 2012nFillmore Jazz Festival, since it's a short walk over to Fillmore.

name: The Ritz-Carlton
title: “The Staff Makes the Hotel.........”
text:
I recently returned from San Francisco and had the pleasure of staying at the Ritz Carlton! 
The rooms are beautiful......the beds are extremely comfortable. My room was very quiet! Try to stay on the 6th floor if possible....facing Stockton Street as there is not as much traffic. For even quieter rooms...ask for an inside courtyard room.
The hotel is elegant but it is the staff that makes this hotel special! The valets, Aaron and Miquel are very personable! The Bell Staff.....Dino, Robert and Mike are quick to help me with directions and always make me laugh with their humor and wit!
I'm sad to see Shaun O'Bryan being transfered for he is the one manager that seems to engage with everyone with a smile his face! Truly a classy man!
I plan on returning to the hotel for their tree lighting ceremony and enjoying the whole atmosphere all over again!
Whitney Rector

name: The Queen Anne Hotel
title: “must stay here”
text: We stayed for 4 nights and couldn' t fault the place. Great location, friendly helpful satff. I would advise you to take advantage of the free curtesy car with "Henry" and don't miss the ghost hunt.

name: The Ritz-Carlton
title: “Aging gracefully, but with a few wrinkles.”
text:
My family and I stayed at the RC SF for 3 nights, October 20-23, 2007. It had been several years since my last stay, so I was curious to see how the hotel had aged. My review of the property follows.
The RC SF is located on Stockton St. between California and Pine mid way up Nob Hill. It is an impressive looking structure with the entrance and handsome lobby area located on the fourth (street) level of the hotel. There is construction ongoing at the corner of California and Stockton, but it appeared to be unconnected to the hotel and was not (other than being an eyesore) a bother. 
We arrived around 1 p.m. and check in at the front desk was painless. We had 2 rooms reserved, a Club floor executive suite with a nearby club king room. The suite was ready for occupancy, but the king was not. Both rooms were located on the 8th floor which is the actual location of the club lounge, though I think the RC classifies the 7th and 9th as club floors as well. The elevator for the 8th floor is via keyed access and opens directly into the lounge area where we were greeted warmly by the club concierge. 
Those of you who have stayed on the club floor of an RC know the drill. There is a light breakfast, lunch, tea, dinner and after dinner serving served at appropriate times with coffee, tea, soft drinks, beer, wine and cocktails available all day. The rate runs about $150 a night more than a standard room, but I generally find it worth the money. While there was always a good variety of sandwiches, crudités, cheeses and desserts at the RC SF, the menu selection never seemed to change much during our stay. Still, it is a pleasant space and a popular gathering spot. The lounge is "child friendly" which made it a bit active during parts of our stay. Not bothersome really, but active. 
Our suite was in the typical RC “executive” configuration. The door opened into a small foyer with a closet and half bath. The foyer opened up into a living room with a desk, a love seat and 2 arm chairs. The window provided a view of…well, not much. (I have stayed at the RC SF several times on several different floors and have never had a view of much of anything except buildings.) No balcony, but the windows did open about 3 inches to allow a breeze. A glass paneled door with sheer curtains separated the living room from the bedroom, which was nice sized with what I found to be a very comfortable king bed. The dressing area and bath (with separate tub and shower) was behind the bed. 
The suite was clean and fairly well maintained. A few pulls in the carpet and a bit of torn fabric, but nothing too bad. Other than the bed, the furniture was not extremely comfortable and needed updating, I felt. New flat panel TV’s were present in both the living area and bedroom. Wireless internet at $12.95 a day was available, but somewhat slow. The bathroom was a bit cramped and poorly laid out, I thought, but serviceable. Good water pressure during our stay.
The RC SF has a nice spa with the usual services available. It also has a very good fine dining restaurant on par with other RC properties. There is a talented harpist in the lobby bar during the afternoon and an excellent sushi chef there during the evening. There is a house car available for trips within a mile or so of the hotel. 
The biggest substantive complaint I had during our stay was the noise level in the room. I know that others on this site have made the same remark. The windows appear to be orginal equipment (If I recall the property opened in 1996) and do not have a great deal of insulation. There was a great deal of bleed through street noise at all hours of the day and night, which was annoying. 
Now on to being picky. Service at the hotel started off great and then went downhill. I was quite impressed with Valentine, the club concierge, and the front desk and bell staff...Jason and Joel at the front door were especially nice and helpful. However, the staff members at the lobby lounge and outdoor patio off the terrace bar (on the second floor in the courtyard) were weak. Several servers at the lobby bar were standing around chatting with one another, but not doing a good job watching the floor. Still, the service at the lobby lounge was stellar compared to the patio outside the terrace bar. I attempted to enjoy a spectacular afternoon there with a cocktail but could not get anyone to wait on me. When I finally asked for a drink from a passing staff member (who apparently did not work the patio) I was told to “go upstairs to the lobby bar to get a drink” and bring it back. Odd, I thought, as there were people eating (inside and out) at the terrace restaurant. Certainly not the level of service I expect from the RC. 
I was also disappointed in the servicing of the room. We left early one morning and did not return until 4 p.m. only to find that neither room had been cleaned. When I called the front desk to inquire when the rooms would be cleaned, I was told that I should have asked for an “early” service. Huh?
Again, these are picky comments. As I am sure Mr. Roa (whom I respect for responding to the posts on this site) will admit, however, it is the fine details that separate a 4 star from a 5 star property. 
In the interest of full disclosure, I admit to being a fan of the RC chain and have stayed at dozen or so of their properties around the country. (Pentagon City and Cancun being 2 of my favorites.) To be frank, though, I prefer the Huntington Hotel in San Francisco. It is up the street at the top of Nob Hill on California. Smaller, independently owned, with a wonderful view from the rooms that front California (Grace Cathedrial and the park, with the bay visible in the distance from rooms on the higher floors) and well kept (although, in fairness, somewhat dated) rooms. Impeccable service. While there is no club floor, the Big 4 bar and restaurant compensate by being clubby and wonderful. Plus, even though my favorite rooms there front busy California St., they are much quieter due to heavy, insulated windows. I would have stayed there this trip, but booked late and the property was full.
So, how has the RC SF aged since it opened in the mid 90’s? Fairly well, I think, with the exceptions noted above. I give it a solid 4 rating. If they take care of the noise problem and work a bit on service issues, it will be a 5. All in all it was a pleasant stay. 
I hope this has been helpful and informative. Safe travels everyone.

name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “The best boutique hotel we've ever stayed in!”
text: We selected this hotel for our 32nd wedding anniversary/vacation base. Stayed from Aug. 26-Sept. 4. The Joie de Vivre hotel chain made this hotel stay the best of any we've ever experienced in our world travels. Decorators were inspired by the New Yorker Magazine and strove to create a 1930's California literary/art scene. From the decor to the furniture, Steinbeck et al quotations/ charicatures/wall art, paintings, color scheme, Society list pages in the elevators, library-club-like lobby to lemon and thyme scented toiletries and lemon/green/black room decor, all were well thought out. The hotel excited all of our senses. They asked guests to donate to support a literary charity, in keeping with their overall theme. Everything was wonderful--location, services, food, etc. Convenient to everything we wanted. Only the amount of time it took for the valet to retrieve our rental car from the remote lot (we paid a daily fee) was excessive and visitors should allow a little extra slack if they need their vehicles. We used public transportation -bus, trolley, taxi (including one with a resident parrot!) and were very happy. Five stars!******

name: Orchard Garden Hotel
title: “Excellent option in a great location”
text:
In very easy walking distance to Union Square, this is a bit of a hidden gem. It's fairly recently opened and has a bit of a hippy green eco thing going on, but unobtrusively so and there's a nice enough feel to the place. The quality of the food in the restaurant is very good indeed - a must-try, and frankly excellent value. I had a couple of minor niggles which I spoke to the staff about and I must say my niggles were sorted out very quickly and very professionally - if you are unhappy about anything, just say the word and they really will bend over backwards to help resolve them. I can't iterate enough how good they were in this respect. The rooms are fine, clean, spacious. If you are travelling with a baby, make sure you negotiate the cot because it seems on some occasions they may charge a supplement, depending on how you booked. 
Summary: Location excellent, Price very good, Restaurant excellent, Staff excellent ... what more can you ask?

name: Laurel Inn, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Hen Party”
text: Enjoyed a great girlfriend visit to San Francisco thanks to the Laurel Inn. The room was clean and comfortable. I appreciate a breakfast that is more than continental; protein options included luncheon meats, hard boiled eggs and yogurt with granola and dried cranberries. Blue Bottle Coffee was a fav. Nice touch to offer cookies and lemonade in the afternoon before dinner. We had a car and enjoyed staying in this quieter location over downtown/Union Square area. Very pet friendly so I suppose if you have allergies, this is not the place for you. They even had water and pet treats available at the front desk.

name: CLIFT San Francisco
title: “City Centre Chic”
text:
I booked this hotel for a couple of nights break in San Francisco and therefore location was important. I arrived by BART from the airport and the hotel was easy to find and a short walk from the station. It is located a couple of minutes from Union Square with its shops and the end of two of the cable car lines down to Fisherman's Wharf.
Check in was about as slick as it could have been and I was in my room in no time. Being a Philippe Starck designed hotel the communal areas are dark and funky. The hotel is designer throughout with many great features.
My room was a Superior room on an upper floor which meant that I got a view out over the city (not the greatest of views but at least I could see the sun go down). Being an older building the rooms were a good size and not overloaded with furniture. The room was well furnished and clean, the only downsides I would say is that there were no coffee making facilities and the sockets were few and in poor positions for using the desk. Minor points on balance.
The bathroom was small in comparison to the bedroom but well fitted and the amenities were good.
At night the ground floor of the hotel, with the Redwood Bar, turns into a trendy drinking joint, however, your room key allows you to jump the queue which is great if you're looking for some nightlife.
If your not then you have to stay in your room and I found that at 0200 when the bar closes the noise on the street is loud enough to hear on the upper floors.
All in all a great hotel, although at the weekends you do have to watch out for the "pretty people" who seem to walk straight through you with self importance.

name: Hotel Union Square
title: “Location Location”
text:
I stayed here 2 nights during Christmas. I booked my flight and hotel on a travel site. I read reviews on many hotels before choosing this hotel. I wanted a decent hotel, no roach motel this time. I have always stayed in pretty low rated hotels in San Francisco before this trip. I hadn't been to SF for 15 years. 
The hotel is on very busy Powell street. Two of my favorite stores, H&M and Urban Outfitters are next door. I didn't know this before choosing my hotel. I liked that the hotel is smaller and has some charm. It's a really old building that has been renovated. The staff is very nice, even the maid says hello. 
My one complaint would be that the mattress was saggy. This is funny, because all the dumps I used to stay in had the same mattress issue. I still slept great. I would stay here again.

name: Coventry Motor Inn
title: “TRES BON HOTEL”
text: Tres bon hotel, très bien situé sur lombard street, grand parking, personnel très aimable, les 2 seuls défaults sont qu'il n'y a pas de ptis dèjeunés et il faut payer pour avoir un frigo (5$ par jours) nous le recommandons fortement.

name: Cova Hotel
title: “Nigel & Cynth's stay at Cova, San Francisco....”
text: This hotel suited our needs for our last night in the United States. Centrally located with real friendly & helpful staff. My friends & I will stay there again next year when we will return to San Francisco. It was close to bus route 19 which took us straight down to Showplace Square where we wanted to go. Easy walk down Geary St to Union Square where we caught the famous cable car over to Fishermans Wharf for lunch. Close to bus route 47 which gets you to Fishermans Wharf as well.

name: The Ritz-Carlton
title: “A really lovely hotel”
text:
We are fans of Ritz Carlton but had been concerned about the relatively low rating on Trip Advisor of this one. I contacted the hotel and they were so helpful and reassuring, telling me about the refurb which has recently been finished etc.
Well I needn't have worried. We stayed 3 nights in mid July as part of a near 3 week California holiday and the hotel was just perfect. A beautiful building, very good location and elegant throughout. We were greeted by name all the time and had so many notes and phonecalls asking us if everything was ok.
We stayed on the club level which was delightful. The food presentations were so yummy and plentiful, we really had no room for dining out! The club concierges were wonderful and so helpful.
Our room, a suite, was stunning, and the new decorations are sophisticated and refined. We had flat screen tv in the bedroom, living room and bathroom which pleased pur 13 year old son!
Overall, we loved this hotel and although San Francisco was not our favourite US city, we would without question stay at the Ritz if we return.
If you are interested check out our reviews of the Ritz at Laguna Niguel, which was not such a happy experience, the Regent Beverly Wiltshire, which was great and the Monterey Plaza Hotel which was horrid.

name: Beresford Arms
title: “Value for Money”
text:
When reading this please consider that our stay in this hotel was 9 months ago.
I found this hotel on Trip Advisor some time ago and told our son-in-law, travel agent to book it for us. We stayed 3 nights. 
I love SF and staying in this Hotel put us in the heart of the place. Just one block from us is a street full of a wide variety of restuarants/eateries which we visited often.
The location is good
The building has a lovely old world charm. 
The staff are helpful but bland, matter of fact...never smiling.
Considering the price, the room was a good size, clean and well equiped. Each afternoon they put on wine and eats for the guests. We enjoyed this. Who wouldnt?
Would I stay here again? Possibly. But not until I have looked more closely at the alternatives

name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “A different side of San Fran....”
text:
I was hesitant about booking this hotel as it was not in a central location, however after having stayed in many San Fran hotels even the 5 star seemed to be a bit lackluster/old and this place seemed fresh/new.
I loved the room it was fabulous, modern, clean, relaxing. I could not have asked for more. The hallways are also very quiet, dimly lit, pleasing to the eye. The staff are really pleasant from the concierge to the maids, check-in
The hotel is a few blocks down from Union Sq which you may think a disadvantage but for us we discovered a whole new side of San Fran. We spent our mornings well luchtime actually at The Ferry Building which is across the street and has great casual dining and our evenings in the same area. 'Slanted Door' fab vietnemese/fusion food, 'Boulevard' across the street ranked as one of San Frans' best restaurants.
We went to Union Sq one day and I was so glad to get back to the hotel, the water....so relaxing.
I did think by the website that this hotel was a spa resort directly on the water it's not, there isn't a spa just one treatment room. I will advise you that there isn't much of a downstairs lobby area to hang out in either and the only disappointment I had was the bar/restaurant area. I went their one evening after dinner and it was full of drunken kids, I guess they also open their doors to the main street so anyone can walk in. Otherwise super city hotel.

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “location, location...”
text:
Great location to see the city. Close to all major well known shopping. Transportation available. Parking was $$ @ $55.00/day.
The room was OK. Staff was typically helpful, but I didn't have to bother them for anything.
Safe... I'd go back

name: The Ritz-Carlton
title: “Great For Adults/Great For Kids”
text:
Wonderful hotel in great location near Chinatown and Union Square. Cable car stops right on the corner.
Staff could not have been more accomodating- everyone went out of their way. Prime example was when we called and asked for a diaper pail. They didn't have one but send someone out right away to buy one!
The indoor pool is very nice and the kids really enjoyed playing there in the late afternoon after a day of sightseeing.
Location right near Chinatown made taking in Chinese a good dinner option on days when kids were too tired to go to a restaurant. Concierge very accomodating in suggesting restaurants for that purpose.
Didn't eat at the restaurant, but it seems to get excellent reviews from locals. Room service was very good too.
2 minor nits: Room was on the small side for a place like the Ritz, though that is to be expected at a big city hotel. And room service breakfast menu could have been more extensive- food was good, just not a lot of choices.
Overall, we loved this hotel and would gladly return. The building itself is beautiful, it looks like it had been a bank or government building at some point.

name: The Ritz-Carlton
title: “Consistant...as expected”
text:
As you would expect, great service and nice accomodations. We stayed in a cheap room about $300/nt. The food was excellent (try the shredded Corned Beef hash for breakfast" The service was better than the Fairmont but the rooms were smaller. A great location and would stay there again.
Note : Parking is now $55/nt. plus 14% tax = $62.70. Although, it feels good to my car up at a nice place as well......

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “a good place to stay,breakfast a bit expensive”
text: This is a good hotel in San Francisco, we would stay there again.Ask for a quiet room on an upper floor because of noisy garbage pickup at 3am every morning.

name: Orchard Garden Hotel
title: “Beautiful Hotel, Great Price, Amazing Location!”
text:
We have stayed at the Orchard Garden hotel twice now, once for business and once for pleasure. Both experiences were fantastic, we fell in love! The rooms are clean, the beds and sheets are exceedingly comfortable, and the staff are friendly and helpful. The convenience of free wireless and movie rentals are very thoughtful and show the care that the management puts into the facility. The location right outside the gates of China Town make wandering the city easy, and its close proximity to the Powell St. BART station make travel a breeze.
The icing on the cake is the specials that the hotel will run, lowering it's nightly stays to under $150, as well as it's fantastic happy hour specials (buy a drink, get an appetizer for free).
We recommend this hotel to everyone who asks, so enjoy!
