name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Great stay during our honeymoon”
text:
My partner and I booked a suite for a 2 night stay during our honeymoon in Jan 07, and had the most amazing time. We were put in a suite on the 7th (top) floor, and the 270' view really is as amazing as the website indicates. So many staff members congratulated us on our civil union, in a friendly-but-not-intrusive kind of way. We were given a complimentary bottle of champagne, rose petals were scattered on our bed -- all in, we were made to feel special.
Breakfast in the room is served elegantly, and is super high quality. We very rarely take baths, instead preferring the shower, but we couldn't resist this one, with its view of the Bay Bridge.
Absolutely recommended.

name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “A fantastic hotel that you wont want to leave...”
text:
I spent a night here is September 2006. And it was a complete joy. We didn't have a view we had a wall, but we hadn't asked for one. The hotel was clean smart and funky. The room was big with a lovely bathroom continuing Fresh! Toiletries. 
Although I have noted some negative reviews on here about staff, I found them beyond helpful, just generally made us feel great making the service second to none. The bar is lively with what looked like a post work crowd and I liked that, it didn't feel like a traditional hotel bar. The situation on the quay by the lovely stores and restaurants was a real treat and being opposite the wonderful Boulevard gave the hotel what distance wise was pretty much a second dining option. 
If your looking for traditional glamour, in an old school Nob Hill hotel no this isn't for you. But if your looking for a boutique hotel with all the service of a 5star resort and very reasonable rates, you wont be disappointed. I would stay there again and again and look forward to my trip back.
I stayed at the Lambourne for 4 nights prior to my stay at Vitale and was without doubt the worst hotel I have ever stayed in. I see that its no longer on the site? One can only hope the depressed staff got the help they needed and someone decided to put them out of their misery.

name: Comfort Inn by the Bay
title: “My room had a view of a brick wall”
text: The room was basic and smaller than some hotels I stayed in during our tour of the West coast. It did have all the bits such as coffee making and a safe, plus free Wi-fi although I could not get mine to work but others in our group had no problems. My biggest disappointment was pulling back the curtains and having a view of a solid brick wall less than 10 feet from the window. Everywhere were adverts to upgrade your room for a view but this did not seem worth it for two nights. Not too sure why called 'by the bay' for it is a good 20 to 30 minutes from central Fisherman's Wharf and the hill is steep on the way back. Well served by buses to get to central shopping, and Fisherman's Wharf, but these seem to disappear on a busy Friday night unless you know the system, forget Taxi's Friday nights as they are very busy. Complimentary breakfast included and this was a very good hot and cold buffet with good variety. Found Reception staff a little off handed. Believe my brick wall view tended to put me off this hotel.

name: Powell Hotel
title: “Great Union Square Location; clean, comfortable and a great value!”
text: My husband's company put us up at this hotel for his conference in San Francisco. We traveled with my 8 year old daughter and had comfortable queen sized beds, fantastic location at Union Square and at the Powell-Hyde cable car line. Easy to get around and a quiet, comfortable room. Staff ok, front desk not too friendly but overall nice hotel.

name: Carl Hotel
title: “Great value & location”
text: Both times I have stayed overnight in Frisco, I chose Carl Hotel because price and location were my main criteria for where to stay in the greatest city on earth. Carl is a great pick. On my first visit my girlfriend and I paid about $70 for a ground floor room facing the street. On the first night we had trouble sleeping with the light rail running right outside our window, but on the second night we got used to it and had no trouble sleeping. On my second stay I was given a room on the second floor with the window facing Stanyan street and the noise wasn't a big problem. The front desk people were always very courteous, the room was tiny but clean complete with a microwave and an (albeit tiny) television set with cable. A short walk to Golden Gate Park, Haight Street, SFSU, and some of the best restaurants in the city.

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “Great little boutique hotel”
text:
Small lobby area but very welcoming friendly desk staff.
Room was very cozy with a large bathroom. Amenities had a fabulous aroma. 
I only ended up staying here 1 night as found it a little far up the hill carrying all my shopping. They say its only 2 blocks from Union Square...and it is..but the top of Union Square. Most of the shops are right down passed the bottom of Union Square. I shopping was not my aim when visiting, I would stay there again.

name: Hotel Milano
title: “Great location but below average hotel”
text:
The location of the hotel is quite good. However, the bathrooms, carpets, and walls were quite dirty. Clearly this place is in need of a serious overhaul. A light bulb was completely missing in the bathroom. Two outlets on the walls didn't work (figured one was out after I awoke to my phone being dead...). The shade on one lamp was falling apart. The TV is a 20" TUBE television (no HD) Sorry, but literally unwatchable in today's day in age on a TV that small. The gym was a joke - 2 outdated steppers and 2 bikes a foot from lockers. No weights at all. 
My room's view out both windows was ONLY of was my neighbor's window 10 feet away. So, I had to keep my shades closed for 4 days - this got old quickly. Not sure how even a rumored restoration will fix this.
The proverbial broken A/C when I checked in... I called down and maintenance confirmed - Yes, its broken because they knew that already. Then why did they let me check in and unpack my week's worth of clothes?...

name: Mithila
title: “False Advertising - Don't stay at Mithila Hotel”
text: My husband and I were booked to stay at Mithila Hotel for two nights in December 2010. The website smartly uses classy and tasteful photographs to lend credibility to the establishment, but this fades into obscurity when you enter the "hotel'. The rooms are small, there is NO fridge, NO microwave and the pillows are wafer thin. When we checked in, the Manager indicated that breakfast was served behind us, I turned around expecing to see a breakast room, instead I looked into a coffee machine standing on a miniscule counter...there would've been place for a complimentary slice of toast if they tried. This place gave me the creeps and I certainly wouldn't advise anyone to stay there, it's a dump. (Oh and parking is NOT free as the websit claims)

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “Nice Place”
text: Nice place to stay. (Very) Reasonable accommodations for the price (well worth it). Other visitors and travelers at the Hotel & Restaurant were of a business class - dressed well, and with good demeanor (not rowdy).

name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A wonderful hotel”
text:
We spent three nights at the Monaco at the end of our tour of California and it was great. The room was great, smaller than other American hotels but what you might expect in a city, both the bedroom and the bathroom were decorated to a high standard.
The evening wine hour was a great idea, which other hotel chains should consider offering. It's a great way to relax and meet other travellers, and the wii was also a nice touch. The hors d'ourvres that accompanied the wine were also great.
All the staff we encountered were very friendly and helpful. They couldn't do enough for you. UK hotel chains should learn from the success of the Kimpton hotels.
Whilst in San Francisco we had dinner at the Cheesecake Factory on the top floor of Macy's. I can't recommend this enough - great value, and a high standard of food, together with great views of Union Square and friendly staff. You have to try it!

name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “My SF "home away from home"”
text: Having gone five times at this charming boutique hotel ,I can say only that it is one of the most lovely and welcoming hotels in America. . Done up like a literary salon of the '20's, there is an excellent wine bar and restaurant ; each room is comfortable, though small for large groups, with everything kept in tip top condition. The staff couldn't be better. I recommend the REX to anyone going to San Francisco for their first or whatever visit. It is conveniently located near Union Square, with the Square's shopping and theatre opportunities. Give yourself a treat and stay at the Rex!

name: Harcourt Hotel
title: “Just what we were looking for!”
text:
We booked this hotel, knowing nothing of the area in which it was located. We were looking for a place to sleep during our stay in SF -- something less than $100 per night. We found it. We were a bit apprehensive due to it also being a residence hotel with weekly and monthly rates and many rooms without private baths.
We found exactly what we were looking for. We don't need daily maid service -- we can pick up after ourselves, we don't need the little bottles of shampoo and lotion. This is a 100 year old hotel, with the original claw-foot tub, old elevator, front desk, etc. But the on site manager and the front desk staff were outstanding. We felt completely secure, our linens were very clean (although there was a cigarette burn in the blanket -- who cares!), the bathroom was clean, the common areas were clean. I have recommended this hotel to close friends because it is friendly, clean, walking distance to the heart of SF. 
If you are looking for a Hilton or some other large franchise lodging facility, this is not for you. If, however, you are looking for a place to sleep, a place with some real character and history, and a place where the staff is consistent, honest, and VERY helpful, this is the place for you. We would return in a heartbeat!

name: Harcourt Hotel
title: “Very Bad”
text:
This is primarily a residence hotel, and should not be used for usual hotel accomodations.
It is a very old building with no new upgraids, not very clean, very shabby. The only amenity is a "dining room" with a microwave for residents to heat their meals. The location, the appearance, the clientele, all give the impression of a run down flop house in the seadiest part of town. Most of all, our confirmed reservation for a room with a private bath was not upheld. They gave us a room with no bathroom, and they could not rectify that. We were left out on the street with no place to go. Their "offer" was to charge us "only" the rate for a room without bath - for the room without bath they gave us.
A terrible experience I never want to relive.

name: Aida Hotel
title: “$30 guest fee kills any sembalance this is a hotel”
text:
For $55 a night i don't have high expectations for a hotel, especially in san francisco.
Still the Aida hotel was OK for th emoney - room is decent sized, bed was comfortable, reasonable shower, free wifi.
The part that really p&*ssed me off was the $30 guest fee. I have friends in SF and it was impossible for any to come up to my room for a drink before heading out. Considering how conveniently located the hotel was this was a real social killer.
There is no mention of this policy anywhere on the hotel's web site, not the booking site I went through. How can a hotel have such a policy and spring it on guests AFTER you've made your payment.
What was supposed to be a get together of some friends i made in SF last year was rather spoiled by this hotels policy. I'm not sure what consumer laws are like in the USA but a hotel would not get away with this in Australia!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

name: Mithila
title: “Bed Bugs!”
text: This was the worst hotel I have ever stayed in. It was relatively inexpensive for the location, so the friend that booked it thought it would be a good idea. We arrived and the room was probably less than 200 sq ft and had two beds in it. The bedding looked clean to the naked eye, but that was due to the poor lighting in the room. The second night there, we found a bed bug in our bed. We also found one on the curtains. I returned home with 22 bed bug bites. I had to thoroughly wash everything in my room and spray down the room with alcohol to try to make sure I killed any I might have brought home with me. This was very irritating after just spending over $1k on a new bed two weeks before the trip. Fortunately, it seems I've brought none but but I recommend you avoid this hotel at all costs.

name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Bells and Whistles-Lacks Basics”
text: We were so excited to stay at the Hotel Vitale after reading all the reviews. Upon arrival, we were expertly greeted, made aware of the $42.00 a day valet fee, and expedited quickly to our basic yet comfortable room with a nice view of the bridge. We began to unpack and quickly noted that there was no dresser for our 6 days worth of clothing, so we lived out of our suitcases and one hanging closet. We walked around and loved SF and the close proximity of transportation and necessities. Keep in mind that on the weekends, most eateries in the financial district are closed. We were peacefully sleeping when at 5:00AM four large tables crashed out in the hallway. An employee evidently was preparing for a future event on the 7th floor terrace. The next morning, housekeeping knocked quietly and quickly and came on in at 8:00AM to our shock. The next day, when we returned at 4:30PM to prepare for dinner with family, housekeeping was in our room and we had to wait outside. Also, if you don't get downstairs before 7:00AM, you will miss the complimentary coffee and must pay $3.00 a cup. Overall, they went above and beyond the call of duty for what they feel is important, but a dresser, housekeepting at reasonable hours, and complimentary coffee are important to us. Not bottled water, bittersweet chocolates, robes and pricey spa products for sale everytime you go into the bathroom. Wish it would have been better.

name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Great Hotel-Clean and Friendly staff”
text: I took my husband to San Francisco for his 65th birthday. I booked the Hotel Rex by reading the good reviews on Trip Advisor and was not disappointed. The staff was very helpful and friendly. The wine served at the evening reception was very good and the morning coffee was delicious. Our room was spacious and clean and the hotel location served us well. We had a wonderful trip and will definitely stay there again if we return to SF. For all future trips I will certainly check other sister hotels.

name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Great location, good Hotel.”
text:
Stayed at Vitale for 3 nights from July 16-18th. (at a rate of about $270 per night for a Deluxe Waterfront King Room)
PROS:
GREAT location. The views from our waterfront deluxe room were truely incredible. We were very happy to be able to watch over the Ferry building, and see a good portion of the bay and the entire bay bridge. Very cool at night. Also, the room was cool, modern chic, with a very comfortable bed, flat screen tv, and the usual amenities. Americano is a fun bar/happy hour scene. Walking distance (10-15 min) to Pac Bell park. The "rainforest" shower heads are really awesome, but they have a little "cut out" in the shower door to turn on and test the temperature of the water (which is a neat idea) but it gets the toilet soaked when someone is showering! 
CONS:
The overnight valet is 42 dollars (PLUS %14 tax!) PER NIGHT. This was almost a dealbreaker, but since no one had forwarned me (nothing on the website or told to me when I made the reservation) I wasn't going to forfeit a nights rate. The agent at the desk basically gave me "I know that sucks, but there is nothing I can do" response when I reacted a bit strongly to finding out parking alone was going to cost me upwards of $150 for the weekend. On the Sunday night we were there, my fiancee and I were woken up to what sounded like loud banging coming from pipes in the walls. This went on for a few minutes when I called the front desk. When the agent picked up, I could hear it 10 times louder over the phone. She said something to the effect of "I think they are working on something in the kitchen, I'll get them to stop" We were on the 5th FLOOR! They did stop however. Who authorizes construction at 2am??? We guessed that it was either an emergency, or that guest capacity was at a minimum on a Sunday night. Either way, no follow up or apology was offered, even when I inquired about it the next morning (I just got blank stares from the staff.)
Breakfast in Americano was okay, service a bit akward and cold food (on one occasion)
OVERALL:
A really nice hotel, which is definitely going through some growing pains, which should be hammered out (no pun intended) relatively soon. At the price for the room, plus parking, there are a few other hotels I would probably stay at instead until they work out the kinks.

name: Greenwich Inn
title: “Convenient Location”
text: The greenwich inn is a standard motel. Clean, decent rooms with coffee provided. Free parking. The location is very good. We walked down to the front quite easily. Mel's Diner is just round the corner! Overall good value for money but don't expect 5 star luxury.

name: Travelodge San Francisco - Fishermans Wharf
title: “Bed Bugs!”
text:
The location and value are great, but I was bit all over by bed bugs! I noticed small brown spots on the mattress in the morning (I stayed one night) and then over the next several days the bites appeared and turned into nasty welts. The room had an odd odor also.
Check you beds if you stay there.

name: Taylor Hotel
title: “Uphill from Union Square, good budget hotel”
text:
My husband and I booked it on the internet and stayed here for 2 nights Oct 04. Not at all fancy, but at $50 (plus lots of tax) it is a good price for centrally located SF hotel. (The big hotels were experiencing a nasty strike, so smaller hotels are better choice at this time.) Re location, it is about 3-4 blocks uphill from Union Sq at Post and Taylor. If you walk on Post or Sutter St you will be fine. Downhill on Taylor takes you into very scruffy Tenderloin area, so avoid heading toward Market St from there, though eating at Original Joe’s at Taylor/Market is even worth wading through the tenderloin scene. Plan to do a lot of hill walking going back and forth from Union Square. 
Good location for getting around on public transport, using Union Square as your launch point. To purchase a short term bus pass, head down Post St to Powell St at Union Square. Walk down Powell to the info booth at the Muni/Bart station on Market and purchase a 1-3 day Muni pass to ride all over, including on the cable cars. We got a 3 day pass for $15—a real bargain, as 1-way on cable car is $2. We probably rode the cable cars a dozen times as well as the bus and Muni underground! Take cable cars at stops other than at the ends of the line--off hours are best. 
Take the Muni underground to get to various outer neighborhoods, and up and down Market Street—just show your pass to the station agent at the booth to gain entry. 
The hotel itself is seedy, but will provide you with some good travel stories. A nice extended Indian or Pakistani family runs it—little kids around, and smell of curry makes it rather homey. We asked for an interior room, got one on 6th floor, not too noisy from street noise. Small funky old elevator. Room painted sunny yellow. TV not on cable, no room phone, no lamps. But great old bathtub, opening windows, clean linen, free internet and morning coffee in modest lobby. Double bed was cozy but comfortable. A good bet for the budget traveler who plans to take public transportation from downtown location and be mostly out and about.

name: Orchard Garden Hotel
title: “An absolute 'green' gem in the heart of San Francisco.”
text: We held our 40th Peace Corps Reunion at the Orchard Garden, and it could not have been better. Situated in the middle of San Francisco, just 50 feet from the entrance to Chinatown, the Orchard Garden was an ideal location for all of our friends who came in from all over the United States. The Orchard Garden is a beautiful, new, and environmentally sensitive hotel. The entry is fresh and inviting, providing an opportunity to instantly experience the friendly ambience that pervades throughout. The use of light colored woods and tall ceilings add to the qualtiy of the hotel. In the ground floor, "Roots" restaurant, the chicken ceasar sandwich, with carmelized brown sugar on bacon, is an absolute, must try delight. The rooms are nicely sized, bright, and cheery, and have all the internet connections one needs. Depositing your room key in a slot by the door powers up all the lights and helps to conserve energy. I did not expect a 'green' hotel to be so elegant. Throughout the hotel, the staff, from housekeepers to waitresses, to front office, were eager to help in any way to make our stay more enjoyable.

name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Couldn't ask for more”
text: Wonderful three night stay. Hotel was artsy and fun. Staff friendly and helpful. Centrally located near many amenities; food, shopping, galleries, etc. Good rates. Highly recommended.

name: Civic Center Inn
title: “Filth Pit”
text: This hotel has got to be the worst I have ever stayed in. Room 127. The hot water is non existant. The shower nozzle was falling out of the wall. Pubic hair in the bathroom. TV impossible to see. Cigarette burns in both bedspreads. Surrounded in an area full of prostitutes and destitutes. Do youself a favour and stay somewhere else.

name: The Embassy Hotel
title: “Hotel Embassy”
text: Hotel correcto muy de acuerdo en su relación precio calidad buena antención pero no del todo bien ubicado, pienso que sería mejor una opción en Fisherman o en Union Square aunque el precio sería mas elevado

name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Traumhafte Aussicht”
text: Das Hotel liegt an einer zentralen Lage, ist aber trotzdem sehr ruhig. Die Sauberkeit des Hotels ist sehr gut. Das Zimmer wahr sehr hell. Von dem Hotel aus, hat man den berühmten Pier, FISHERMAN'S WAHRF, in wenigen gehminuten erreicht. Die Aussicht auf die Bay Bridge war der Wahnsinn.

name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Excelente inesperada sorpresa”
text:
Hotel situada en el mismo embarcadero. Buen punto de partida para cualquier excursión. Fuimos anadando a casi todos los sitios, porque teníamos tiempo. El transporte público funciona de maravilla y en pocos minutos se alcanza cualquier parad de Bus o la más cercana de BART (Embaracdaero). NOTA: pedirle al concierge tarjetas de descuento para los alquileres de bicicletas. Las habitaciones estan muy bien equipadas, acogedoras. La cama excelente. Buen sueño desde la primera noche. La limpieza muy bien, tanto en la habitación como en el resto del Hotel. La iluminación muy agradable en todas las zonas. Ruido solo en el lobby por la tarde ya que el restaurante esta abierto al lobby. El personal excelente. Muy atentos y muy amables. Nos ayudaron en la organización de todas nuestras excursiones.
Una experiencia inolvidable. Que la piscina estuviera en un edificio del YMCA a escasos metros, nos extraño un poco. Suponemos que ya no les cabía la piscina. El GYM se queda un poco corto aunque hay de todo. El GYM del YMCA es bastante mas amplio. El SPA, pues bien, para relajarse bien. Repetiremos seguro.

name: Travelodge San Francisco - Fishermans Wharf
title: “Ottima posizione”
text: Albergo in ottima posizione, a due passi dai moli di San Francisco e dalla fermata del cable car che porta in centro. Camera pulita. Personale cortese. Parcheggio interno a pagamento.

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “Nice Hotel close to Union Square”
text: This is a nice smaler hotel just up from Union Square and a couple of blocks to Chinatown. Nothing fancy just a very nice room, great staff, and convenient to such a nice end of the town. Definitely will stay there again. Also, the price was right for the accomodations.

name: Knights Inn - Downtown San Francisco
title: “I hate to say this but......worst hotel experience ever.”
text:
Perhaps we were spoiled by the great, cheap, room we had in Vegas but, man, this place (three times the price of the Vegas motel) was Not Good. It takes a lot to make me want to write a bad review but I feel compelled to warn you all off.
Booked online - no option for twin room so booked a double and sent an email requesting a twin. Never heard anything back and when we arrived they had booked us into a double room. No offer to move us or even apologise. The staff member behind the desk actually said "and it's quite a small double bed too". They did give us the option of a rollaway bed we could use.....for $20 a night. 
When we got into the room there wouldn't have been room to put a rollaway bed anyway! The bed that was in there had a chunk of metal sticking out of it that gashed my friend's foot. Rat-trap on the floor also didn't exactly fill us with confidence either. Walls so thin I could hear a guy in the next room cleaning his teeth.
Charged a $125 "security deposit" to my credit card at check-in, which I've never encountered before and don't yet know if I've got back.
They certainly are mercenary in this place. In your room is a long list of what they'll charge you for every item should they become damaged/lost. From $1300 for the curtains down to $2 for each battery in the remote control. 
You can't even dial a toll-free (75cents) or local call (75cents + 77cents per min) for free. In most other places I've stayed everything bar long-distance is gratis. 
On our last day I asked at the desk about booking a cab as we had to leave at 2.30am to get to the airport. Was told, no problem just call from your room half an hour beforehand. Which is what I did. Was told by the chap on the end of the phone that they don't do that before 4am(?!?!) and to "just go out on the street and hail one". 
Which is what we had to do since the cab company (which my local friend had given me a number for) could only accept calls made from the lobby not a room (which I found out during an abovementioned Expensive Phonecall) and the phone in the lobby was apparently "not working" when I went over to ask. 
So me and my - female - friend were out on the streets of downtown SF looking for a cab, which SF is not the best place for, at 2.30am on a Saturday night with all our luggage. We may as well have been wearing a sign saying "Hi we're desperate tourists please mug us". The cabbie that picked us up got a gratefully large tip I can tell you. 
I picked this motel as it wasn't in the "Tenderloin" area (a bit of a no-go zone apparently) and it was close to town and my friend's apartment. I made a mistake. Choose another place.

name: Mithila
title: “Good value hotel”
text:
The room was clean and comfortable and the location was good - close to Polk Street which has lots of places to eat and also near the cable car. I was transferred from the Amsterdam which had double-booked so paid $50 inc tax for a double room, not sure if booking it directly would have cost more. Car parking was $14. There was some traffic noise but that's to be expected for a room with a view of the street - it didn't disturb me or keep me awake.
The internet access was good, although they tell guests a password isn't needed when actually it is. I don't know why they would do that - it just means an extra trip to reception to get the password.
I couldn't get hot water in my shower in the morning (think there was an issue with the tap because there was hot water in the sink) and unfortunately there was nobody at reception at 7am.
Overall, it was clean and comfortable (really comfortable mattress!) and great value for the area.

name: Mithila
title: “une mauvaise adresse”
text: Un hotel bien situé, mais c'est là le seul point positif. Une heure est demie avant de nous ouvrir les portes, une chambre qui puait la cigarette,une odeur épouvantable dans les couloirs, des croies gammées sur le pas de porte, du linge troué, un petit déj qui n'en ai pas un, et un personnel désagréable et insultant. Bref, à éviter...

name: Knights Inn - Downtown San Francisco
title: “HORRIBLE!!”
text: We stayed only one of the the four nights we were suppose to stay. There was garbage left in the unlined bathroom wastebasket, no kleenex, 2 out of 4 lamps worked, TV only got 2 channels and not very well, holes in sheets, sheets very worn appeared to be washed but stained, blanket had seen much better days,1 bar of soap for 2 sinks and the tub, bathroom door was filthy, shower curtain was dirty, the floors were uneven and soft and squeshly, basebords obvioulsy hadn't been cleaned in ages. We left and went down the street and found a Best Western (Carriage Inn) at a "walk in" rate equal to the Ramada with delightful amenities - fireplace, sherry and nice continental breakfast to your door etc. The man at the desk was pleasant, but never solved any of the problems.

name: Ramada Limited - San Francisco
title: “Gut gelegenes aber lautes Stadthotel”
text:
Zuerst einmal, das Hotel ist sehr gut gelegen, hat einen eigenen, kostenlosen Parkplatz und es ist gut mit öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln zu erreichen.
Aber, man muss in Kauf nehmen, dass man durch den Straßenlärm oder laute Nachbarn kaum zum Schlafen kommt. Wir haben dort drei Nächte verbracht und keine Nacht durchgeschlafen, zumeist wegen spät heimkehrender Zimmernachbarn. Für Nichtraucher ist das Hotel auch nicht wirklich zu empfehlen. Es gibt zwar Nichtraucherzimmer, da man aber vor den Zimmern rauchen darf und dies auch genutzt wird, zieht ständig Zigarettenqualm ins Zimmer. Die Zimmer sind zwar sauber, aber schon ziemlich abgewohnt. Nicht wirklich zum wohlfühlen.
Das Frühstück ist im Preis inbegriffen, ist aber wirklich unterstes Niveau. Man macht sich seine Waffel und Toast in der sehr kleinen Lobby und es ist stä ndig überfüllt. Essen tut man dann im Stehen an der Theke. Sitzplätze oder Tische sind keine vorhanden.
Alles in allem ist das Zimmer seinen Preis nicht wert und wirklich überteuert.

name: Star Motel
title: “Free Parking, Clean Rooms, Great Shower Pressure”
text: We have stayed at the Star Motel on at least 6 different trips to San Francisco. It is located in a good neighborhood (felt safe walking around with young daughter at night). The staff is always friendly and helpful. Rooms are always clean & the shower feels like a nice massage after walking around all day.

name: Rodeway Inn Civic Center
title: “Rodeway Inn Civic Center Don't Count on parking”
text:
Rodeway Inn Civic Center 
2 stars 
860 Eddy St, San Francisco, CA, 94109 United States ?866-539-0036? 
Check-in at 4:00 pm told don't leave any valuables in car. nothing else, Returned at 9:00pm after dinner with Kids. Sorry no parking you have to take you changes on the street! Attendant told us to park carefully wheels in because police give ticket for little reason or no reason. Choose this place by phone representative of hotels com because of free parking. Hotels.com level 3 service said you have to check the hotel yourself they are not reasonableness for their representative advice. Buyers beware!!!

name: Rodeway Inn Civic Center
title: “Great bargain in San Francisco and very helpful management.”
text:
Very smooth check in by very nice managers. Good location one half block from Van Ness and from there you can go any where in the city. Direct # 47 bus to Fisherman's Wharf. Clean rooms and free parking if you want to park a car. Free continental breakfast. 
It is not a five star motel but for the money it's a bargain and my stay's have always been
pleasant. And that is important as San Francisco can be very expensive for lodging.

name: Alexis Park San Francisco
title: “Small hotel fallen in the ghetto area in San Francisco”
text:
I booked this hotel via Expedia.com and had a coupon of $25 so that end up still cost us $95 per night to stay in this little hotel in such a ghetto area in Tenderloin, San Francisco.
Two of us were arrived to the hotel in a Saturday morning prior to check-in time but the young guy at the front desk was so nice to keep our lugguages aside until we checked-in at the later hours.
Parking spaces were very limited and they were all first come first serve base. Glad that we did not have a car so that not a problem to us. The hotel room was clean and was spacious. I think the hotel was recently renovated (maybe a year or 2 ago). There was a LCD in the room and I needed to say the Jacuzzi was great even though it's installed as a shower instead of bath tub kind of whirlpool. It's very powerful and functioning very well.
Internet signal was strong and capable to provide Internet connectivity throughout the room. We had no problem to use the Internet during our stay. Area was ghetto, night time we heard some sirens (police or ambulance) passing by and was kind of noisy especially when your room facing the streets. We did not try the breakfast because choices were so slim and was only served from 8-9:30 every morning. I never heard of a hotel who served breakfast for only 1.5 hours.
You don't want to walk around in the area after dust especially if you are alone traveller. Over all for the price, this is not a good choice when it's fallen in the area. NOT RECOMMENDED.

name: The Opal San Francisco
title: “Great value if you're visiting San Francisco on a budget!”
text: This is a great hotel in a safe area of town. Definitely a great way to save money if you're visiting San Fransicso. Mel's Diner (delicious food!) is located right next door. It's a good idea to learn to take the bus to get around as the hotel is located a few blocks from Union Square. Also, you will have to take a taxi or bus, of course, to visit the Golden Gate bridge, Alcatraz, or Fisherman's Wharf. Overall, a clean, safe hotel, and a great value.

name: Union Square Plaza Hotel
title: “Cheap the only reason to stay here”
text: This was not the greatest hotel but was by the cheapest in this nice area of town. The room was small and the bathroom was very tiny. The desk people were very friendly and helpful heck at 3:45AM the front desk guy went out into the middle of the street and flagged a taxi down for us. I would stay there again because I'm single but would not stay there with a family.

name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A Trendy Gem”
text: Stayed at the Hotel Monaco around the Holidays and my family really enjoyed it. The hotel is decorated in a tastefully trendy style. The lobby and other common areas are particularly impressive. The rooms are not large, but they are comfortable. Like the common areas, the room decor is interesting and well done. I give the hotel staff high marks for their courtesy and great attitude. The entire staff went out of their way to be helpful and make our stay a pleasant experience. After reading some of the reviews, I was somewhat concerned about the area around the hotel. After our stay, we actually liked the hotel's close proximity to great shopping in Union Square and felt the area was relatively safe. The area a few blocks away from the hotel is somewhat run down, but we avoided it by parking in the hotel lot and concentrating our excursions on the Union Square side. I would definitely stay at the Hotel Monaco the next time I'm in San Francisco. The afternoon wine tastings and free massages only add to the great experiance.

name: Rodeway Inn Civic Center
title: “fire the manager and I'll go back”
text: Not a bad facility and a clean property for the price. I'd stay in the street before I would ever stay there again and have to deal with the manage. I have made a complaint to choice hotels and never even got a response. The manager makes his own rules and prices he needs to move back to Iraq.

name: Rodeway Inn Civic Center
title: “Not Recomended”
text: We had arrived one hour early for check in, checked in at the front desk. The lady said the room was ready. Getting up to our room, it was clearly not ready. So we let her know and went downtown til the check in time. An hour later our room was still not ready, at the correct time it was supposed to be. We let her know again and then she told us it would be ready in fifteen minutes. Twenty minutes later it hadn't even been touched. We complained again and WE had to ask for a different room. She should have offered a clean ready room in the first place. She was very rude to us and ignorant. I would not recommend this hotel. Also the walk downtown is not very pleasent.

name: Travelodge Central
title: “mine”
text: it was too expensive for a small room, i was only the from 8pm to 11 am paid $92 plus a $12 parking fee which was hella stupid and feel that you shouldnt have to pay to park where you are a guest

name: Travelodge Central
title: “october stay”
text: Upstairs from me there was the worst noise ALL NIGHT! i could not sleep. i advised front desk but nothing was done. ALL night it was as if someone was dragging furniture around the room. It did not stop all night and way into the moring! it was a horrible nights sleep. It made matters worse that the rooms are bare floors so the furniture dragging went noise was very bad. At check out, it seemed as if the police were getting called to go to that room right upstairs from me. I did not stay long enouph to confirm that. i was just sleepless and unhappy that the noise continued and that front desk did nothing to help. Also since i barely slept, at check out the maid knocked on door and YELLED at me when i asked that i just needed 10 min. to gather my stuff. Horrible experience that night.

name: Union Square Plaza Hotel
title: “Cozy urban hotel, very pleasant and in the heart of SF!”
text: Arrived late morning to go to the D-Backs vs Giants game that day and were greeted and assisted in a most friendly and helpful manner by the young lady at the Front Desk. Fortunately were able to check-in early and found the room fairly spacious, clean, and quite comfortable. Really fun to just walk out the door and you are in the thick of all the hustle and bustle of this wonderful city. Left the next day for Monterey, Ca and were kindly assisted by the friendly and helpful Concierge after storing our luggage so we could go to the SF Museum of Modern Art a short walk away.

name: Union Square Plaza Hotel
title: “great location and fit our price range”
text:
so the hotel is located right in the heart of union square which was great. you are walking distance from all of the shopping. for us it was convenient because we explored using the hop on hop off tour and the bus stopped one block away from the hotel.
the hotel itself is pretty much no frills(of course you get what you pay for). it didnt bother us too much because we were never in the hotel, but there definitely needs some updating. 
if your looking for someplace centrally located and you wont be spending much time indoors i recommend this hotel.

name: Orchard Garden Hotel
title: “Great Hotel”
text: we really liked it. It was perfectly clean and extremely wel kept. We had the chance to take advantage of an offer as the price was reduced for the night we spet there, but it certainly is a Hotel I would go back to.

name: Fitzgerald Hotel Union Square
title: “Horrible experience”
text: The reviews were ok and we were just looking for a clean place to stay in SF for the weekend. Got there and our rooms weren't ready. We had to wait 4 hours. Got to the room. It was filthy. An old saggy double bed - not the queen we'd booked. Had been promised microwave and minibar - not there. The staff refused to do anything to help. Stubborn and rude. They said there were no more rooms left tough luck. We got our money back - thank god and went on line and wound up booking a room at the Sir Frances Drake Hotel for $25 more than The Fitzgerald was charging. Avoid The Fitzgerald at all costs. It's a dump.

name: Union Square Plaza Hotel
title: “Great location, great affodable price, in the center of the city!!”
text: Love this hotel, greta location, very affordable prices. If you plan not to stay in the room and explore the city, this is a perfect hotel. location is great. tons of shops and restaurants nearby. definetly stay there again when i will be next time in SF!

name: Hotel Whitcomb
title: “Good for the price”
text:
I stayed here for a few days during a tour of Northern California.
The location is quite good as yopu can walk to Union Square in about 20 minutes
There are a lot of homeless people about so I wouldnnt recommend walking at night!!
The rooms are small but reasonably comfortable and we had a tiny but adequate ensuite shower room.
There is a Starbucks in the lobby which is great to sit and people watch in the morning.
The inhouse resturant is nice although we only had breakfast there
The staff were very friendly and helpful too

name: Halcyon Hotel
title: “great, clean, economical, lovely people”
text: loved staying here with my mum. the room had a microwave, tv, bath, and fridge. the room was kinda small, but perfect for us. the location was interesting, just a short walk to union square and super handy. but if we walked in the other direction we were in the tenderlion ,which is pretty rough. the hotel seems right in the middle of these two areas, and we quickly learnt which blocks to take and which to avoid. my only wish was for an electric kettle rather than a coffee maker, cause I like to drink tea. the women who worked at the desk were really lovely and friendly and made us feel very much at home.

name: Powell Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text: Checked into the Powell quickly, however the reception staff was not very friendly and did not tell us about the complimentary wine/beer that evening. He did not let us know about the complimentary breakfast in the morning either. I found out by mistake when I saw other guests congregating upstairs eating and drinking. The room was very warm even when we opened up all the windows we were able to open. We turned on the overhead fan, but the room remained stuffy all night. Our room opened up to the interior of the hotel, so all we saw were the windows of the other rooms. It was quiet though because the room did not face the street. The bed was comfortable and there was a large closet and sink and wet bar area in the room. There was a dirty towel hanging on the back of the bathroom door. The window in the bathroom had floor length drapes right next to the sink which I thought was odd given that the sink was jammed up against the side of the wall. Consequently, the drapes were dirty and we could not close them completely because a portion of the drape had come lose from the valance. I thought the room was overpriced, but for this location in SF, I should expect to pay more. One of the entrances to the hotel leads to the cable car turnaround on Powell and Market. Across the street is the Westfield Shopping Centre and an Old Navy as well as other name brand stores. Union Square is 2 blocks away where you will find a Macy's and other stores. Not sure if I would stay here again, but the location is unbeatable.

name: Hotel Whitcomb
title: “a lot of homeless around”
text:
I,ve been there 2 years ago, and the location has been worsing since then , there are too many homeless around. 
the hotel has lowered their standarts, it was full and two elevator were not working, I had to go dawn the stairs from 5th floor several times

name: Powell Hotel
title: “Very nice for the price”
text: This is an old hotel and kind of funky because of it. We had two rooms because we were traveling with family and it seems that every room is a little bit different. The rooms were spacious, though, and one of them even had a separate little bedroom. Our view was of the building behind us, but we didn't mind. Overall, for the price, we were very comfortable and the location was perfect. Also, everything was clean.

name: Presidio Inn & Suites
title: “Lieber nicht....”
text:
Unser Zimmer war spartanisch eingerichtet, verfügte dennoch über einen TV, Kühlschrank und eine Mikrowelle. 
Das Badezimmer war zwar klein aber immerhin sauber. 
Die Betten waren ok - in einer solchen Preisklasse kann man wohl nichts besseres erwarten. 
Die Wände hatten allerdings einige Flecken, über deren Ursprung man nur grübeln konnte.
Der Herr an der Rezeption ließ uns am Tag der Abreise mindestens eine halbe Stunde warten - trotz Klingel und Eile!! - da sein Mittagessen wohl vorging. Im Allgemeinen war dieser jedoch zuvorkommend und hilfsbereit. 
WLAN hat gut funktioniert.

name: Halcyon Hotel
title: “Unbelievable Value, Great Location....My Favorite Budget Stay”
text:
San Francisco is my favorite city and I visit there often, either to and from the airport or just for fun. I found this little jewel one day while I was walking around looking at little hotels. The curbside appeal is modest, you need to buzz in, but once you make your way downstairs to the office a warm greeting awaits you. The rooms are cozy, packed with all the conveniences, and spotlessly clean. I have stayed in several rooms and each one is different. They all have a classic San Francisco charm with a claw foot tub, nice bedding, and a complete equipped kitchenette. It is also smoke free!! Having stayed in dozens of little hotels over many years, this is a great stay, you just can not find a better value for your money. I highly recommend the accomodations, cordial innkeeper, and perfect location. They also have an inexpensive parking garage less than a block away.
I highly recommend this hotel to anyone

name: Travelodge Golden Gate San Francisco
title: “liegt zwischen Golden Gate Bridge und Fisherman´s Wharf.”
text:
Ich war 2 Wochen in San Fransisco. Man erschreckt im ersten Moment, wenn man das Hotel von außen sieht. Aber die Zimmer sind sehr schön eingerichtet. Die Zimmer sind sauber und gepflegt. Unser Standard. Der Preis ist für´s Hotel i o.k. um im teuren San Fransisco günstig zu übernachten.
Kreditkarte wird bei Ankunft im Hotel als Sicherheit verlangt. Nicht vergessen!
Hotelmanager sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit. Frühstück gibt es nicht. Aber um das Hotel gibt es alle Restaurants (Italiener, Mexikaner, Mongole u.s.w.). Man verhungert nicht.
Es gibt einen Bus, der einem zur Golden Gate Bridge fährt in 10. min. Sollte man aber Zeit haben und es ist schönes Wetter unbedingt an der Flußpromenade zur Golden Gate Bridge laufen (gut 1 1/2 Std. Fußmarsch).

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Okay”
text: Stayed with wife and kids. We took two rooms. We usually stay at the Fairmont on Nob Hill. Rooms were up to date and adequate size in our section, which is the newer rear building. Location is good if you like the hussle and bustle of Union square at your feet. Check-in took way too long - I don't know why. Also, at check-in I asked if any upgrades were available for my wife and my room, and was told we could be upgraded for additional $20/night. I took it, and was disappointed to find it was identical to the un-upgraded room my kids had except it was eight floors higher (20th floor). If the added elevation had provided a superior view I could understand; however, the view from the newer "tower" is not great as it does not look down on Union square even if it's facing the square because the original building is in the way. All staff were helpful and friendly. I also liked their lobby-lounge where you can comfortably sit with your laptop. Service there was a bit slow too though.

name: Rodeway Inn Downtown
title: “Good for short stay”
text:
This hotel is close to downtown SF with all the pluses and minuses. The neighborhood is dirty, but the rooms are ok. It is not a highend place, but the cost is reasonable for the city.
I would not recommend it for a long vacation, but for one night it is ok

name: Francisco Bay Inn
title: “1st trip to San Francisco!”
text: First off let me say the hotel was clean no issues there and great location to everything, however don't believe the pictures there is no headboard on the bed and we paid for a king deluxe and got a queen, I know it wasn't a king, the sheets and comforter were so old and thin it stated in the review no smoking in rooms but our comforter had burn holes in it. And if you are looking for comfort well the bed is as old as the sheets and comforter the springs were in our back, mattress very uncomfortable. There is no place to put your clothes, you keep your clothes in the suitcase, my husband had to move the nightstand to put our suitcase on it because I didn't want to put suitcase on the floor. The noise of traffic will keep you up part of the night, the walls are very thin you can hear everything outside. The breakfast well there was a little girl that went in as we were looking for coffee she picked up the pastrie smelled it and threw it back on the the tray, yeah where were her parents? The coffee well they had ice cold water and instant coffee the lady said take it back to your room and heat it in the microwave....Well I was turned off from the little girl. Forget breakfast there.

name: Adante Hotel
title: “Great location - but staff need motivating!”
text:
***We stayed in this hotel February/March 2011***
Booked this hotel as part of a Qantas Holidays Package. The location of the Hotel in San Francisco is excellent. Short stroll to Union Square, Macey's and the shopping district.
The rooms were clean with their own bathroom but horrible Decore`. Hand painted murals that were odd. Room view was internal - looking at another brick wall. No food services were available as the only cafe (on the premises) shut down a couple of months before we arrived. Don't stress though - plenty of cafe's/food places nearby.
The staff were very lethargic and 'lazy'. They were very unhelpful during an emergency when San Franciso was on high tsunami alert after the catastrophic Japanese Earthquake. Local media (and even cab drivers) were alerting locals of the Tsunami Alert. We were concerned and asked concierge about hotel plan - shrugged his shoulders and gave a groan. Not very reassuring of the hotels evacuation procedures.

name: Fitzgerald Hotel Union Square
title: “My favorite San Francisco hotel.”
text: The Fitzgerald Hotel reminds me of a small family-owned European hotel. It is cozy, clean, and quiet, and the staff are warm and friendly. The beds are comfortable, the bathrooms are well-maintained and fully equipped, and the complimentary breakfast is high quality. The Fitzgerald Hotel is located two blocks from Union Square, one block from the Theater District, and an easy walk to a wide selection of good restaurants. The price is right, the rooms are practical, and nothing necessary for an enjoyable visit is lacking. I make a point of staying in the Fitzgerald Hotel whenever I have business in San Francisco.

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “Very comfortable”
text:
This hotel has the basics covered very well. Rooms were new, clean, spacious, quiet and very comfortable. There were six different kinds of pillows to ensure the pickiest sleeper (me) had the perfect one. The bathroom vanity had lots of space for my toiletries which I don't always find in a city hotel. I only ate breakfast at the hotel once (food too salty but coffee was amazing) as Sears Diner (best breaki in San Fran) is around the corner as are many great restaurants. The on-site exercise room is small and uninspiring - use the off-site one for a fee. The staff were friendly and sweet and actually kind! Each of my 4 days started with 3 or 4 different staff members wishing me a happy day. The Orchard is a steep uphill block from Union Square - something to keep in mind if you have mobility issues.
I have stayed at the Fairmont, Four Seasons and Westin St Francis (among others) and they are fine if you want a grand/posh experience. If, however, you are in San Francisco for San Francisco and not your hotel, the Orchard is perfect. I will be staying at the Orchard every time now.

name: Great Highway Motor Inn
title: “Got Bedbugs? Great Highway Inn Does!”
text:
GOT BEDBUGS? Great Highway Inn does! 
This was by far the worst hotel room we have ever stayed in. Yes, there really were bedbugs in the bed (along with someone else's hair). I thought at first the "bug" was a baby roach, but took it to a local pest control office and had them identify it. Can you imagine my horror when they said "bedbug"?
After I saw the pictures on the website, I wish I had taken photos in our room. Room 216 looked nothing like the photos on the site.
The furnishing were old and dingy. The room was extremely cold when we arrived. We turned on the baseboard heater and waited for it to get warm. And we waited .....and waited. It took five hours before we could actually take our coats off. 
The furnishing were sparse at best. There was the requisite bed, lamps and dresser (with goo stuck to the bottom of the drawer). As a bonus, there was a small refrigerator. However, there was no ironing board, iron, coffee pot or clock. But there was free parking and the room was large. 
The bathroom was newer and did have a tub/shower. The water pressure was virtually nonexistent. 
Once we finally got warm and went to sleep, our neighbors had a lover's quarrel and were screaming from the balcony at 4 am. I realize this could happen anywhere, but it just made a bad night worse. And then we found the bedbug. What a way to start a new day!
I would discopurage anyone from staying here under any circumstances-unless maybe you brought your own bug bombs, vacuum, bedding, etc.

name: Fitzgerald Hotel Union Square
title: “tiny, staff was rude”
text: I came to stay with my mother and baby, had warned them that we'd be three people with baby luggage, and was put in a postage stamp sized room. My mother literally had to sleep with her suitcase on her bed with her! The hotel staff was rude when we wanted to switch rooms, eventually we had to change hotels, and then were charged a $50 fee for leaving early. I'm currently trying to get a refund for that extra charge. I think this hotel had the potential to be a cute place, but with their refusal to accommodate us I wouldn't recommend it.

name: Hotel Majestic
title: “Ok but not Great”
text:
The room was large with good sized beds and a nice little couch to sit on but the general decor and bathroom was dated!!! 
I felt like I was in a bedroom in the 1960's and it wasn't a classix feel.
It was clean but the shower was pretty pathetic.
The sockets seemed to be coming off the walls which was a little concerning.
The location was alright. We got a bus into town during the day and a taxi about at night. 
The staff were very friendly and helpful but I don't think I would stay here again.

name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “bra!”
text: Fräsht och bra hotell! var där i 3 nätter och är jätte nöjd

name: Powell Hotel
title: “NICE OLD QUAINT HOTEL”
text: Nice hotel. Small room but just right for a couple. Near public transportation. If you are looking for modern and fancy not the place. Would recommend for a one or two night stay.

name: Hotel North Beach
title: “Basic hotel in a good location”
text:
We stayed at this hotel in September 2011. We were on a road trip from San Diego to San Francisco and so this was our final destination before heading back to the UK. We turned up on the spot as we struggled to find anywhere to stay in the city (there was a huge IT convention going on and every hotel we tried was fully booked). 
The room was clean and the bed comfortable, although being in such a busy location meant that traffic noise was heard most of the time and throughout the night. 
There was no ensuite but the shower and bathroom we shared with other guests was clean. The shower was very powerful which was great to wake me up! 
Great location, right in the middle of Chinatown so plenty of great restaurants to choose from! 
If you need somewhere cheap but clean to stay I would suggest this place, however probably only for one or two nights.

name: Powell Hotel
title: “A Fine Hotel with a Great Location”
text:
The Powell Hotel is just steps from the BART and Muni Stations at Union Square, so it's location could not be more convenient. The hotel itself is an older hotel, built in 1908, I think, and it has fairly small rooms, but not too small.
The hotel's staff was friendly and helpful, even providing a roll away free of charge when a friend came to visit from out of town for an evening. The rooms were clean and well kept, and the noise level was great considering your in the heart of one of the densest cities on the West Coast.
I would not hesitate to stay here again.

name: Adante Hotel
title: “Good location but cramped and unclean”
text:
We stayed in the Adante for two nights when we arrived in SF and again for one night the following week before we left. The hotel is ideally situated only a short walk from Union Square and the front desk staff were helpful. We were allowed to check-in early and were even on our first visit given a larger room (501) than we had booked. The following week we had a normal 2-double room (604) and honestly it was the smallest room we have ever stayed in. We could barely fit our luggage in with the stroller and porta-cot! The first thing you notice when you enter this hotel is that it is old and very cramped. It is impossible to get more than two people with luggage into the elevator and the stairs are very narrow. We made the mistake of returning to the hotel one afternoon around 5pm when a busload of people had arrived to check-in. There was a queue for the elevator for 15 minutes, which was a little annoying.
The room we first stayed in, despite being larger than normal (but still small except for the large bathroom), was very unclean. The floor was sticky and we felt dirty if we did not wear shoes. Even worse our 1 year old was crawling around on it - yuk. As for safety with a child: it was lacking. We were on the fifth floor and if we did not close the window our kids could have just fallen straight out to the ground below as there were no flyscreens. The TV did not receive very many channels and on neither occasion we stayed did the promised free wireless internet work. The front desk provided a cable to use the ADSL connection but it did not work either. Unfortunately also the breakfast was served in the lobby due to construction work, making it a cramped experience also and really there was not much food on offer other than a muffin or toast. All up though, the price was decent and in any city in the world you get what you pay for at the budget end of the market - it just surprised us how poor this place was in relation to its description and photos on its website.

name: Hotel North Beach
title: “good rate but rooms are tiny and shared bath”
text:
the positives: most rooms have a fridge and microwave, expanded cable tv (no remotes though), rooms are clean, computer available in lobby, shared bathrooms are private and never seem to be busy.
the negatives: the single rooms are tiny; bed is not firm and slumps in the middle but is comfortable enough; no control of room temp except to open a window. one room i was in had only dim lighting and no mirror but the second room i was in had a mirror and better desk lamp; desk personnel sometimes seem indifferent and won't always try to honor your room request, such as for a quieter room not facing the street.
the primary positives are the rates and locatio, surrounded by good restaurants and public transit, a very active part of the city. and the place is kept clean.
phones are in the rooms but didn't work during my week long stay.

name: Nob Hill Hotel
title: “Don't ever stay at the Nob Hill Hotel!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text:
We came for leisure to SF for 3 nights, upon arrival at midnight the clerk could not find our reservation, finally around 2 am he gave us a room with a non working shower, the hotel was dirty, dilapidated, noisy, on the morning they asked us to vacate since they were full!
Then upon exiting the hotel the clerk said that they had a room for us, upon this very unpleasant experience and the general condition of this low quality boutique hotel I realized that it is worth to spend the extra bucks and stay at a well know chain hotel. We checked it at the Holiday Inn in Fisherman's wharf and we were so happy we did!!!!!!!!!!!!
The Nob Hill Hotel should not be listed at all as an option to stay in this beautiful city.

name: Inn on Broadway
title: “Proper Choice”
text: It was a great time. I stayed for 4 nights and I didn't get any inconvenience. Cleanings, parking and location was perfect. It could be seen a bit old and not fancy from an outside view but It's totally enough to stay comfortably for your light travel. And there are some nice restaurants and groceries near there like 'the matterhorn swiss' or 'walgreen'. Lastly, I think that their service is good. Unfortunately, I left my belongings at the room, they sent it back to me. They are ready to take care their customers, always. Thank you so much, Inn of the Broadway!

name: Americas Best Value Inn & Suites-SOMA
title: “Für den Preis absolut in Ordnung”
text: Wer ein Auto hat, für den ist das Hotel absolut geeignet. Zimmerreinigung ist täglich und die Mitarbeiter an der Rezeption sind sehr freundlich (Rezeption ist nicht 24h besetzt). Direkt unterhalb des Hotels ist eine Bar, die sehr gut besucht ist, könnte also etwas lauter werden, was aber nicht weiter stört. Außerdem ist direkt ein kleiner Kiosk an der Ecke, wo man einiges bekommt. Ein paar Blocks weiter ist man direkt auf einer Hauptstraße, wo es alles gibt was man gebrauchen kann (Post, Banken, Starbucks ;-), Restaurants). Die Zimmersauberkeit war eigentlich in Ordnung, die Tagesdecken hatten ein paar Flecken und hinter den Schränken wird auch nicht geputzt (auf der suche nach einer Steckdose entdeckt). Parkservice ist auch in Ordnung, kostet zwar etwas, aber dafür wird das Auto auf einen gesicherten Parkplatz gefahren und wenn man es benötigt, sagt man ca. 20 Minuten vorher bescheid und es wird geholt. Alles in allem ist das Hotel zu empfehlen.

name: The Opal San Francisco
title: “Bon rapport qualité-prix pour SF”
text:
Le personnel est adorable, plus particulièrement Angela qui, en plus de ses bons conseils, nous a donné deux chambres séparées : 1 King et 1 double Queen au prix de la chambre familiale sans supplément de prix. La situation pas loin du centre ville avec un excellent réseau de transport en commun: Cable Cars à 3 mn à droite en sortant de l'hôtel, pour aller à Union square, Chinatown... Le bus 47 devant la porte va directement au Fisherman's Wharf devant le Pier 39. Les quelques sdf à proximité étaient plutôt sympas! Le parking, bien que cher mais très utile (C'est le prix à SF). Bon petit déjeuner continental. Il ne faut pas rater le resto "Mel's Drive Inn" adjacent avec son air rétro.
Salle de petit déjeuner petite pour la taille de l'hôtel.

name: Adante Hotel
title: “Dolphins on the ceiling”
text:
I was travelling alone so looking for somewhere safe, central and affordable. I booked the hotel on the basis of other Trip Advisor reviews so thought it was time to reciprocate. It is a nice hotel in a very central location. Five minute walk into Union Square, 10 mins to the cable car/metro. Yes, there are a quite a lot of homeless people on the street as you walk back from Union Square, but I never felt threatened by anyone.
The hotel is clean, comfortable and friendly. The reception staff are very keen to help. Cleaners overenthusiastic so do remember to put the 'do not disturb' sign out at night. There is a good internet cafe downstairs which is also a relaxed place for a single traveller to enjoy a coffee or a beer. It is open until 9.30.
Rooms may be small by US standards but pretty standard for a European 2/3 star hotel. Perfect for a single traveller, but my room would have been ok for couples. I kept the curtains closed as I looked out directly into another window,but the room had very good lighting. And it was so quiet.
And there are dolphins, angel fish and Nemo in some of the rooms.........

name: Super 8 San Francisco/Union Square Area
title: “Good enough for the price.”
text:
I just got back from a 5 day stay. I was attending a convention @ the Moscone center (10 min walk away) I would have much rather stayed at the Mariott but comparing prices $349 for the Mariott and $139 for the Super 8 I knew I wasn't going to get the same experience. The neighbourhood is referred to by locals as the "tenderloin district" there are plenty of drug dealers, drug addicts, homeless, hookers, etc. Follow the advice from earlier come in from the Powell side its only the last block that gets bad. The Hilton a block away hires a cop to stand out front 24/7 and keeps everyone off that block but it just pushes the less desirables to this block. One night I decided I wanted pizza so I went up the block about 11pm grabbed a slice and one my way back I saw a homeless woman urinating on a tree and there was human feaces on the sidewalk.
The elevator in the hotel was a bit iffy sometimes it would come other times it wouldn't. The guests were a bit iffy as well lots of pot smoke on the lower floors and guests running around with bloody noses from coke abuse. 
There are no safes in the room. But f you put up the do not disturb sign the staff won't come in. 
The bedding is clean. The bathroom is clean, Place is cheap. Not sure if I'd go back unless I was on a tight budget.

name: Edwardian San Francisco Hotel
title: “Good value”
text: I booked my room online, the rate was very reasonable, but I was not sure what to expect for that rate. It was a pleasant surprise, the location was great, only five minutes by trolley to my interview in the financial district, the room was cozy not large but clean. The staff was helpful. I think it is a very good value, I will stay again.

name: The Gaylord
title: “Gaylord Suites, ein absolutes Schnäppchen, der Geheimtipp in SFO”
text:
Das Hotel liegt sehr zentral, in der Nähe des Union Squares. Busse fahren quasi direkt vor der Haustür Richtung Golden Gate Bridge ab. Direkt unterhalb des Hotels beginnt Tenederloin an, ein Stadtteil der etwas anders ist. Jedoch würde ich ihn tagsüber als absolut harmlos bezeichnen, ist eben wie in jeder Großstadt, es gibt Gebiete in denen mehr Obdachlose leben und das Rotlichtmilieu vertreten ist. Wie gesagt, Gaylord Suites liegt außerhalb von diesem Gebiet, die Gebiete oberhalb (also den Berg hoch) sind wunderschön (Nob Hill - wird auch Snob Hill genannt, wegen den Prachtbauten) und die Straße darunter ist ebenfalls absolut harmlos. Weiter muss man ja nicht bergab gehen, wenn man nicht will. Direkt um die Ecke liegt ein Supermarkt (Walgreens), ein etwas größerer (Saveways) befindet sich auch in der Umgebung. Das Zimmer hat eine kleine Küche mit Mikrowelle und Kühlschrank + Geschirr, einen LCD Bildschirm, HBO, ein komplett neues Bad sowie ein sehr sehr bequemes Bett, kostenloses WLAN, kostenlose Telefongespräche innerhalb der USA. Man sollte darauf achten, dass man Zimmer in den Etagen 10-12 bucht, da nur diese vollständig renoviert wurden. Man kann auch noch ein etwas größeres Zimmer buchen (deluxe), bei dem dann ein seperates Wohnzimmer vorhanden ist. Die Zimmer kann man auch monatlich buchen für 2250 Dollar bzw. 750 Dollar für eine Woche.
Der Blick aus dem 12. Stock ist fantastisch. Oft wurde auch der Lärm bemängelt. Die Scheiben sind wirklich dünn, aber auf den Etagen 10-12 sollten auch lärmempfindliche Menschen gut einschalfen können. Die anderen Zimmer würde ich dann eher nicht empfehlen.
Sauberkeit der Zimmer ist sehr gut, gereinigt wird jedoch nur einmal pro Woche. Liegt wohl daran, dass Gaylord Suites zu CitiSuites.com gehört und vorwiegend für Berufstätige gedacht ist, die sich mehere Monate in SFO aufhalten.

name: Inn on Broadway
title: “Clean, comfortable, convenient and good price !”
text: Stayed two nights here and it is not fancy but clean, beds are comfortable, within walking distance to sights and attractions. The hotel is in a good neighborhood with free parking on site and a great place for breakfast at the hotel! Great deal for the price! It was a little noisy at night but we were there on a weekend and it is located in the city so some noise is expected.

name: Union Square Plaza Hotel
title: “bien placé mais d'une propreté douteuse!”
text: malgré la mauvaise evaluation laissée, un hôtel à conseiller pour son emplacement central à SF. Le hall d'entrée fait illusion car lorsqu'on accède aux chambres, on n'a pas l'impression d'être dans un hôtel. Cette première impression passée, les chambres restent "correctes" même si la propreté est douteuse

name: The Opal San Francisco
title: “on the road again”
text: hotel génial idéalement situé sur l'artère Van Ness. Proche du civic center et tram'

name: Capri Motel
title: “Perfect and Inexpensive Spot in Cow Hollow”
text: Whenever you just feel like spending a day or few browsing Union Street shops and pubs, or spending some quality time savoring Marina district life on Fillmore and Chestnut streets, and want to be a mere short walk from the Marina Green or an easy bus ride to North Beach, Chinatown, Union Square and the Financial District - and you don't want to spend a lot of money to sleep in a clean room in a very safe location - this is definitely the spot.

name: Edwardian San Francisco Hotel
title: “Great stay for the price”
text:
I stayed at the Edwardian while I found a place to live in San Francisco, and I have to say I was pleasantly surprised. I booked online through their website and got a reduced rate, and I wasn't sure what to expect.
The hotel was very clean, and the staff was very courteous. When I arrived, I had help getting all of my bags inside. I had to get them up to my room myself, but I at least had help getting them on the elevator.
The room itself was very comfortable; not a ton of room to spread out in, but enough to relax. I actually got one of the deluxe rooms with a king-size bed and a private bathroom; some of the other rooms don't have bathrooms. But the room was clean, the bathroom looked like it had been remodeled fairly recently, and it was very quiet. (For the record, I stayed in room 47; fourth floor, in the back.)
With my particular room, there are a few things to keep in mind; being on the top floor, it takes a while to get hot water up that far. A couple minutes tops, but I guess it's something people have complained about before.
The only other thing I would have to say is that, while the hotel does have complimentary wireless (very stable, and pretty quick at that), it doesn't broadcast all the way to the top floor. Again, not a huge deal; you just have to head downstairs a little to one of the common areas. (Which themselves are pretty cozy.)
On the whole, I would recommend the Edwardian to anyone looking for a place to stay in San Francisco. It's close to public transit, or even within walking distance (if you don't mind going on a little trek) to all kinds of places. It's a nice place to stay, and it won't break the bank.

name: Adante Hotel
title: “de verguenza,muy malo”
text:
Hicimos el viaje en septiembre del 2012.
El hotel estaba pagado ya por una agencia de viajes,ya nos lo habian cobrado pero nada mas llegar nos dicen que tenemos que pagar 100 dolares de fianza y encima que si pagamos con tarjeta nos cobrarian mas.
 Los de recepcion entendian español pero no nos ayudaban,nos hablaban en ingles,cuando le pedimos explicaciones sobre esto.Muy desagradables.
 Para subir a las habitaciones, tuvimos que hacerlo por parejas (eramos cuatro) porque el ascensor esta muy mal y no podia con mas peso,daba miedo.
Las habitaciones decoradas con mal gusto y el baño muy viejo. todo el hotel esta viejo.Peor que una pension.
 El desayuno es de verguenza, se da en la recepcion,no se cabe y no hay mesas para todos,y las que hay son pesimas, solo ponen cafe,una maquina de zumo,pan y mantequilla, todo ello encima de una mesa improvisada por las mañanas,que luego recogen y sigue siendo la recepcion del hotel.
 Cuando nos ivamos le dijimos que nos llamaran un taxi, nos vino uno que era familia de ellos o del mismo hotel, nos cobro mas del doble que el taxi que nos llevo desde el aeropuerto, discutimos con el y encima el muy cara se cobro propina sin darnos el cambio.un sinverguenza.
 Nos parecio un hotel malisimo, no lo recomendamos.

name: Super 8 San Francisco/Union Square Area
title: “Great value at the Alexander Inn”
text: Great value for budget travelers. Convenient location with great breakfast (with egg and bacon). A bit old, but great service. Ice machine didn't work while i stayed though. A suite with separate door entrance is available (shared bathroom).

name: The Good Hotel
title: “Party hotel, not for quit times, young party animals everywhere.”
text:
Nice clean rooms, small but effective, pleasant staff
Not a great area, as the hop on hop off tour bus says, "Not a safe area, be careful around here, you will be followed if you look like a traveller"
Lots of bums and homeless, the hotel reeks of GRASS!!!
Might spend a little more next time

name: Capri Motel
title: “Nett, sauber, ruhig”
text: Das Zimmer war sauber, die Atmosphäre sehr angenehm, sowohl ins Stadtzentrum als auch zur Golden Gate. Ist es nicht weit. Trotz fehlendem Kühlschrank und einfachstem Frühstück (nur süße Bagels) können wir das Hotel nur weiter empfehlen, Preis Leistung ist voll ok.

name: The Ritz-Carlton
title: “Top”
text: Das Ritz Carlton in San Francisco hat in jeder Hinsicht unsere Erwartungen erfüllt. Tolle Lage auf Nob Hill, direkt an der Cable Car Station. Wunderschönes historisches Gebäude. Äußerst luxuriöse "RC typische"-Zimmer, Bulgari Kosmetikartikel. Sehr zuvorkommender Service. Was braucht man mehr nach einem 10-h Flug?

name: Super 8 San Francisco/Union Square Area
title: “J'y retournerai”
text:
J'ai passé une semaine superbe à San Francisco. Le quartier ou se trouve l’hôtel n'est peut-être pas un quartier luxueux, (pourtant le Hilton se trouve jusqu'à côté) mais quand on choisi un super 8 on ne cherche pas le luxe. La chambre était fonctionnelle, WiFi gratuit, la salle de bain propre, le personnel souriant et aimable. Il était très agréable de pouvoir passer un petit déjeuner au calme (pas copieux, mais assez: bagels, cream-cheese, OJ et café) avant d'affronter la ville qui ne dort jamais.
L'emplacement permet de sortir sans crainte le soir, de prendre le cabel car, le métro (Bart) ou même des bus. Il y a tout à proximité. Si je devrais y retourner j'irai au même hôtel.
Rapport qualité prix excellent!

name: Marina Inn
title: “Nice & Clean”
text: First trip to San Francisco and a friend recommended this Inn. Though the rooms are small, they are very charming and very clean. Nice breakfast and the rates couldn't be beat with such an easy walk to the Wharf. We spent our last night in Nob Hill and wish we would have been here instead. Much better location and the staff was helpful and friendly.

name: Astoria Hotel
title: “Can't beat the room rates!”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for 5 days last summer, and all in all, it was an enjoyable experience.
The hotel is located at the gate to Chinatown and close to the financial district. 
Staff at the reception is very friendly and helpful. At first, we didn't get the room (2 single beds) we had booked, but it got changed straight away when we complained. In the first room a strange monotonous noise could be heard, but the second room was absolutely fine. In the room, we had a telephone and a small TV. It was clean, just like the bathroom, even if you can't really call them modern. 
In the whole hotel there's a slight smell of ... well, I don't really know what, but it's not disturbing. 
Breakfast contains mainly of toasted bread, bagels and big muffins and is good if you're not too picky. The room it is served in is not too accommodating, however, but it's still ok.
What's really unbeatable about this hotel are the room rates. I doubt that you get a hotel cheaper than the Astoria in San Francisco, and considering that, it's more than recommendable if you don't want to spend to much money and still feel comfortable.

name: Astoria Hotel
title: “Great value and location”
text: Hotel is a tourist class basic accomodation on the doorstep of Chinatown. Nothing fancy but bed was comfortable and breakfast was bagels or muffins with good coffee. Smallish rooms but online price was $69 for a Friday nite so well worth it. Would stay again in a heartbeat.

name: Royal Pacific Motor Inn
title: “Affordable and near Chinatown”
text: U get free parking at this inn and it is at the heart of SFO chinatown! The room is pretty decent. Do try to get a room facing the back of the inn to avoid the traffic noise.

name: Francisco Bay Inn
title: “Horrible customer service, give someone with a better attitude your business”
text:
My boyfriend and I decided to do a spur of the moment trip to see a World Series game. Most hotels close to the stadium were booked, and pricey. This hotel came up as very reasonable ($132.00) for two nights. Couldn't really beat the price. So we booked and headed out. Maybe the lady that works at the desk hates her job...or people in general. Not sure. But upon checking in, I gave her my name and told her we'd be staying two nights. She didn't bother looking at the computer for rooms that were ready. Just stared at me and stated "Check in is at 2:00, no rooms are ready". Hmmm...ok, it's 1:00 p.m. Granted we're a little early. But really? Just entertain me and pretend you're looking for one that's ready. Rather than pitch a fit we made the best of it and walked down to fisherman's wharf. This is the one plus for the hotel. It's close to walk to fisherman's wharf. Once there, you can catch a bus or the trolley to just about anywhere. The area of the hotel is more "neighborhood" but it wasn't bad at all. Never felt "unsafe". 
So we get back to the hotel at about 2:15 and the oh-so-friendly front desk lady has our room key ready. Yay!! We haul our stuff up to the second floor....and shocker! The cleaning lady is in our room....bed isn't made, bathroom isn't ready. I mean really??? We left to accommodate the cleaning time of the hotel, just to get back to a room that wasn't ready. Not to mention our room was right next to the elevator. I mean, a little customer service goes a long way. Knowing that we killed time for an hour....to come back to a room that still wasn't ready and we couldn't at least get a room with slightly better location. Oh, and we were right above the car entrance in and out of the hotel parking lot on top of everything else. 
Luckily we weren't spending much time in the hotel. Pretty much just a place to sleep and shower. The room was clean, and it served its purpose. I'm pretty sure the hotel across the street would have served the same purpose with a better attitude though. 
The icing on this cake of a hotel was on the day we were checking out. Hotel check out is 11:00. We were out of our room....bags in our car by 10. So we figured we'd walk down to get some breakfast, come back up to the hotel and hit the road.
