Well we get to the corner, and somehow the front desk lady managed to high tail it across the parking lot to to the corner and tell us that she'd have to charge us 15 dollars an hour after 11 if we left the car. WHAT????!!! Did you forget the fact that we couldn't check in till almost 2:30?? Should I request 30 dollars taken off my bill then? This is what I wanted to say, but no. I have manners. I'm nice to people. We explained we just wanted to get breakfast, we'd be right back and we'd be leaving. So she was KIND enough to give us until 12 before she'd start charging. She also told us that "We had to tell her that we were leaving it". Wow, okay. So now you want to start exercising courtesies? I never received a simple thank you, have a nice day, thank you for staying with us....NOTHING. I just thought courtesies were non-existent to her. Guess they're just one-way. 
Needless to say we would never stay here again. I won't recommend this place either. No one likes to start a vacation, or spend their money to get this time of treatment in return. Do yourself a favor and stay elsewhere.

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway
title: “Conference ripp off”
text: Attended Semicon West and stayed here as it was one of the hotels on the shuttle pick up route. The cost was a total rip off. $1200 for 3 nights without any breakfast although this was just as well as they ran out of coffee the 2 times I asked for it. I am accustomed to hotels ripping off business customers but this is in another league --- super ripp off !! The hotel itself was very average with the roof top pool on the 4th floor looking shabby....spoke to some users in the lift and it seemed to be very cold. I was glad to leave...shame because I enjoyed the time in San Fran.

name: Super 8 San Francisco/Union Square Area
title: “Hôtel correct”
text: Chambre non fumeur suffisamment grande pour 2 personnes. Grande salle de bain mais baignoire moyenne. Chambre propre. Employés très sympas et serviables. Hôtel très bien situé dans le centre de San Francisco. Situation géographique idéale même. Petit déjeuner très décevant: peu de choses sont proposées et la qualité laisse à désirer. Pas de petit déjeuner à l'américaine. C'est vraiment le point noir du séjour!!

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Avoid this hotel”
text: We chose the hotel since the location was excellent and we thought it would be a grand old dame. My family ended up getting 4 rooms and our problems started right when we checked in. Reception couldn't get our names right so letters, calls and visitors were all told that there was no such guest by that name. We called repeatedly to correct this but the errors still persisted. The rooms were filthy. We didn't want to walk on the carpet barefoot since we could feel all the dirt from years of neglect. The staff was very combative for each complaint we made. Our stay in San Francisco would have been perfect, were it not for our hotel of choice. There are other hotels in the Union Square area that I suggest you stay in. Sadly, this hotel has seen better years. It badly needs a renovation and better management. I do not recommend this place at all.

name: Royal Pacific Motor Inn
title: “won't return”
text: As for good points, the staff is pleasant, our room was clean (but had an odd, funky odor) and the free parking is a huge plus if you have a car. The brown and orange color scheme and low-ceilinged room gave a dreary feel. The lobby and outside areas are rather shabby and faded. Was glad we'd booked for only one night.

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “Good value for money”
text:
My wife and 2 children aged 11 and 14 y.o. stayed here for 4 nights. We chose the hotel based on Tripadvisor reviews.
It's in a good location: close to Union Square but slightly removed from the hustle snd bustle of the square.
Staff were very helpful and friendly.
The accomodations are extremely comfortable and above average. This hotel is more of a boutique-style hotel and we regard this as a big advantage. We prefer smaller upmarket hotels to the larger and grander chains.
We would definitely stay at this hotel again. 
We noted that the owners are due to open a second property in SFO soon.

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Poor hotel, great location”
text:
Don't be fooled by the location or the opulent lobby (as I was). Step into one of the rooms at the St. Francis, and you will be very confused at the high price commanded by the small, spare rooms.
I remembered the St. Francis from childhood, and decided to book it, fooled for the reasons mentioned above. The staff at check-in were slow and unmotivated; there seemed to be no additional attention for SPG status holders. 
The room was very small, even compared to NYC. It was clean enough, but had not been renovated in some time, and felt dimly-lit and dingy. The view was of a brick wall on the other side of a narrow alley. Since I was traveling with my girlfriend at the time, I had paid for a higher level of room, and was truly shocked by the incredibly low value for money. 
In a city like SF, there's no reason to pay so much and get so little as at the Westin St. Francis. Instead, try the Meridien in the nearby Financial District. The rooms are spacious, it often is available for a bargain on Priceline, and the views from the high-floor corner rooms are honestly some of the best in the city (Coit Tower, Bay Bridge, Golden Gate, Transamerica Pyramid, etc.). Wherever you stay, avoid the Westin St. Francis.

name: Comfort Inn by the Bay
title: “Cut above”
text: All of the staff here proved to be a cut above. We would gladly stay again. In particular, Sharon made us feel as tho we were guests in her home.

name: Hotel Metropolis
title: “A pleasant surprise and good value”
text:
Needed a last minute place on a very busy weekend. Macworld show caused near capacity hotels downtown. Found this place online and booked with some trepidation. Upon arrival was pleasantly surprised at the very nicely maintained boutique hotel. Clean rooms, helpful staff, and amenities found in more expensive hotels; free wireless, flat screen tv's, a small gym and morning coffee in the lobby (in addition to the standard in room setup) made the stay a success.
The only reason this is not rated 5 is the prevalence of what appear to be homeless people wandering the streets in the area. But, since this is a block from the pricy 55 hotel, I imagine they have the same problem. 
Finally, the price is very moderate for San Francisco downtown.

name: Monarch Hotel
title: “Absolutely fine for the price”
text:
After reading other reviews on this site I was very much in 2 minds as to whether to stay here but was pleasantly surprised when I arrived. I was expecting drug dealers, prostitutes and gangs on the corner but although it is in a slightly shady area, it escapes the worst of the streets of the Tenerloin area which are largely to the south. 
Having said this it is certainly not in a pretty San Fran district and if you're looking for a relaxing stay in a pleasant neighbourhood with staff who bend over backwards for you, do not stay here. However if you're looking for a budget hotel with decent sized, clean rooms in a very convenient location, then this is the place for you. 2 of us stayed for 3 nights and it served us perfectly and although it is opposite an "adult store", it really doesn't appear to be at all dangerous - certainly no where near as bad as some other reviews make out! We came home after late nights on the tiles and had no problems in the area at 12-1am.
In short I would definitely stay here again for the right price, however if you are at all sensitive and require a picture postcard neighbourhood where people tip their hats as you leave your room/the hotel, this ain't for you.

name: Royal Pacific Motor Inn
title: “Just for the location and parking”
text: We picked this hotel for the location and free parking. Employees at the front desk were very unfriendly. The loby is very very tiny and looks awful. Our check-in took about half an hour as one of the rooms we booked was cancelled somehow. They arranged another room for us and luckily the rooms were comfortable and clean. No breakfast facilities etc - just a basic motel.

name: Hotel Metropolis
title: “Good location, very comfortable. Good value”
text: I was afraid about the comments concerning the neighborhood, but they are really exagerated. The location of the hotel is really good, near good department stores and quiet during the night (I was in the 4th floor with a view to Market St. and I stayed there for five nigths). Easy transportation to anywere in the city. Service is very kind. The beds are very comfortable and the room is OK. I would recomend it for business travelers or couples looking for an urban escapade in SF. Free wi-fi works very well.

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway
title: “Love the Staff!”
text: I've stayed here two times this year for fun and I have nothing but good things to say. The first time I stayed they upgraded me to an amazing corner room on the west side with great views. The views were so nice that I might move to SF some day. The second time I stayed on the east side, but I prefer the west side. Both times the staff was very friendly and knowledgeable. The only thing irked me was the line at the front desk, but that happens at big hotels. If you need a bite to eat, go to Grubstake around the corner. They have this amazing home made salsa verde!

name: Comfort Inn by the Bay
title: “Would not stay here again”
text: We booked a room on the internet with 2 "queen beds, and non smoking. Room stank of smoking and beds were little more than King Singles. My 6 foot son had one bed my husband and I had the other. If I wanted to turn over I had to get out and get in the bed again. I asked to be moved and was told the hotel was full and that as I had booked on line and got a cheap rate the room was as good as I could expect. An hour later I saw a woman come in and was able to book a room on the spot. Breakfast was always full and sometimes there was not even anywhere to sit. Our view was of a brickwall and the room was very dark. Reception staff were fairly rude and talked down to us.

name: Comfort Inn by the Bay
title: “Average hotel only”
text:
Booked this hotel on Expedia using Nectar points! Wish I hadn't as we would have checked out.
Very average hotel. Had requested top floor room when booked it in January - had been advised that hotels in San Francisco get booked quickly in summer and we wanted somewhere reasonably priced and not too expensive to park car!
Staff not particularly welcoming or helpful.
Had room on 8th floor - did have a bridge/bay view when not foggy!!
Room very tired. No mention on booking that there were communicating doors between rooms. TV had poor reception at times. Wifi did work but very slow.
Walls also very thin. 
First night we had a family nxt door with a toddler who yelling/crying and parents were shouting!
Second night someone else in room smoking heavily - despite being non-smoking hotel. Dont know what nationality they were and didnt like to complain. Smoke detectors presumably not working? Put pillows at bottom of door!!
Next three nights no problems thank goodness!
Bathroom the smallest I have ever seen in a hotel anywhere in the USA!
Breakfast area far to small for number of guests. Always busy however early or late you went. Tables not cleaned quickly enough. Some guests just left their dirty dishes on tables. Other guests monopolized it - 1 teenager, French I think - was making waffles for all her family using 3 waffle makers at least twice - you should have seen the queue!! I gave up!!
Equipment poor and restocking not good. 24hr coffee not always available either.
Hotel brochure said there was a guest laundry but on enquiry there wasn't one. 
Also not happy about paying extra for hotel safe $1.75.
Car park very small and tight, once parked no guarantee you would get another space if you went out. We had planned to use public transport anyway. On the one occassion we did go out in the car, we returned early afternoon to get a space. However it was secure parking behind a barrier. 
Would not stay here again unless revamped - unfortunately there are no Hampton Inns in the area which would have been our first choice.

name: Powell Hotel
title: “Just Great--Excellent Value and Location”
text:
We just got back from a business trip to San Fran and stayed at the Powell for $80/night. Our usual hotel, the Chancellor, quoted us $160/night so we decided to give the Powell a try. We checked in very early but they were able and willing to accommodate us. Unfortunately, they put us right outside the staircase they are renovating so we heard drills and hammering all morning every morning. But, being on the sixth floor and on the back side of the building, we didn't have any noise problems from the street.
The rooms are great for the price and you really can't beat the location. Our room was pretty clean, though there was a bunch of dust behind the head board.
It seems the hotel is undergoing a large-scale renovation. Can't speak to the unrenovated rooms but everything else seems just fine for the price. I have stayed in much more expensive, much more disgusting places and was actually very impressed with this hotel. I would definitely stay here again. 
Parking is $30/night and you have to call for your car. You can prolly find cheaper parking in one of the public lots and self park to save money.

name: Astoria Hotel
title: “Gutes Preis - Leistungsverhältnis und sehr zentral gelegen!”
text: Wir haben dieses Hotel aufgrund der Bewertungen von Tripadvisor gewählt und wurden nicht enttäuscht! Das Hotel ist sehr günstig für SF (wir haben 69$ pro Nacht gezahlt) und zentral gelegen (in einer nach unserem Empfinden sicheren Gegend), direkt am China Town Gate und in der Nähe des Finacial Districts. Für uns war auch ein Kriterium, dass ein Starbucks direkt gegenüber ist, mein Freund wir ohne seinen Kaffee morgens zum Mörder. Was wir nicht wussten ist, dass es an die 100 Starbucks in SF gibt und sich deshalb eigentlich immer einer in Sichtweite befindet ;-). Sehr zu empfehlen ist das "Working Girls Café" die Bush Street ein Stückchen runter, hier waren wir immer frühstücken. Das Hotelfrühstück für 4,00 Dollar haben wir nicht ausprobiert, Frühstücksraum sah aber in Ordnung aus. Der Union Square ist in 5 min zu Fuß zu erreichen. Zur BART Station Powell Street sind es ca. 10 min. Wenn man ankommt muss man den Berg hoch laufen, wir sind deshalb mit dem Taxi gefahren (ca. 8 Dollar). Zurück war selbst mit Gepäck kein Problem. Hotelshuttel zum Flughafen kostet 15,00 Dollar pro Person. In diesem Hotel arbeiten ausschließlich Asiaten, die alle sehr nett und hilfsbereit waren. Der Aufzug ist wirklich ein wenig gruselig! Er ist ziemlich groß, aber nur für 3 Personen zugelassen. Uns hat er Gott sei Dank nicht im Stich gelassen. In anderen Bewertungen wurde erwähnt, dass es dort komisch riecht. Das ist uns auch auf gefallen, aber in ganz Chinatown riecht es ähnlich. Wir haben uns gedacht, vielleicht das Putzmittel?! Man gewöhnt sich auf älle Fälle recht schnell daran. Wir hatten ein Zimmer im sechsten Stock zur Bush Street. Tagsüber ist die Straße schon sehr befahren, abends und nachts geht es aber. Wir haben wunderbar geschlafen. Noch ein kleiner Ausgehtipp: Die "Cheesecake Factory" im Dachgeschoss des Kaufhauses Macys am Union Square hat uns gut gefallen, tolle Karte (Burger & Co.) zu guten Preisen (Hauptgericht ca. 10 Dollar) mit einem wunderschönen Blick über SF von der Dachterasse aus. Und unbedingt mit dem außenliegenden Fahrstuhl des Westin St. Francis Hotels fahren! Der Blick ist nicht zu toppen (und kostenlos). Fazit: Das Hotel Astoria hat ein sehr gutes Preis - Leistungsverhältnis, ich kann es nur empfehlen und würde auch wieder dort übernachten.

name: Royal Pacific Motor Inn
title: “Ottima posizione”
text:
L'albergo si trova in un'ottima posizione dalla quale si può raggiungere a piedi la china town, la coit tower, il financial district e little italy.
C'è il parcheggio del motel ed anche un garage privato accanto a cui il motel si appoggia in caso non ci sia più posto auto.
La camera era spaziosa e pulita con bagno ed antibagno, anche se l'antibagno non aveva la porta.
Non ha il servizio colazione, ma poco male perchè attraversate la strada e trovate il 'caffè trieste' ,un'istituzione ormai a San Francisco, che fa degli ottimi cappuccini e delle ottime brioches. Comunque se chiedete il motel vi dà delle brioches confezionate.
Le uniche pecche erano la stanza al secondo piano affacciata sulla broadway che non era silenziosa ed il pianerottolo per entrare in stanza è all'aperto, come nelle case di ringhiera, ed è quindi molto freddo.
Tutto sommato se tornassi a san francisco questo motel lo riprenoterei sia per la sua ottima posizione che per i servizi che offre (internet e parcheggio).
Ah dimenticavo c'è anche la lavatrice a gettone nell'hotel e l'asciugatrice a gettone che con pochi dollari potete lavarvi la roba.

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway
title: “Nice stay”
text: The hotel is in a good central location in the city. The room was clean and comfortable. The staff was very friendly and helpful.

name: Americas Best Value Inn Golden Gate
title: “Für ein paar Nächte akzeptabel”
text: Hotel war ganz ok. Frühstück gab es im Cafe nebenan und bestand aus Saft/Kaffee und einem Muffin. Der Service an der Rezeption war nicht sehr kompetent, da wir teilweise falsche Auskünfte erhalten haben. Vorteil ist, dass das Parken inklusive ist, aber es sind sehr wenige Parkplätze zur Verfügung vor allem am Wochenende.

name: Americas Best Value Inn Golden Gate
title: “Etwas abgelegung und laut aber ok”
text: Wie viele Motels liegt es in der Lombard Street und damit an einer lauten Hauptverkehrsader in SF. Es fahren nahe gelegen Busse in die Zentren. Zu Fuß sind Sehenswürdigkeiten nicht wirklich gut erreichbar. Der Zustand des Motels ist dem Preis entsprechend, hohe Ansprüche sollte man nicht haben, aber es ist sauber und hat eine vernünftige Ausstattung incl kostenlosem Wifi-Internet. Ein großer Vorteil ist der kostenlose Parkplatz (sofern noch Platz ist!).

name: BEST WESTERN The Hotel California
title: “Nice place to stay in Union Square area”
text: The Hotel California is in a good location if you are visiting the Union Square Area. We stayed in a suite that had a king bed and two twins in another room. The suite had no sitting area however. Bathroom adequate size. The staff was VERY friendly and helpful. The restaurant had a great breakfast that was included. Trolley cars were a few blocks away. The only thing that was negative was that there was no air conditioning. You could open the windows but it was noisey. The beds were great. I would stay here again.

name: Francisco Bay Inn
title: “Great hotel for those on a budget!”
text:
PROS of Francisco Bay: Cheap (only $62/night average cost for 2 nights); Decent location within walking distance (1 mile) to Fisherman's Wharf and Pier 38 where you can get a bus tour of San Fran, watch Sea Lions, and take ferry to Alcatraz; Staff is helpful and friendly
CONS of Francisco Bay: Small rooms especially with 2 double beds which felt a little cramped, this may be okay by European standards; We saw a few small ants in the room; The breakfast consisted of an assortment of danishes, muffins, and donuts... We would have preferred some more healthy alternatives including cereal, bagels, etc.; Our room was a bit noisy as the hotel is located on a busy street.
The bottom line is that for the money it is a best buy for the budget conscious visitor. The friendly staff suggested taking a tour of the city by Tower Tours. The tour bus picked us up at the hotel and was a pretty good overview of the area. It is costly, at $38/person for a 3.5 hour tour, but it is a good overview and makes a good first day activity.
Make sure to visit Golden Gate Bridge and Park, China Town, Alcatraz, and the Sea Lions at Pier 38.
San Francisco was a real treat for us and we plan to go back again soon. Unless we hit the lottery before our next trip we will be staying at the Francisco Bay Inn.
Thank you, have a safe trip, and God Bless You and Your Family!

name: Hotel Beresford
title: “Can't Beat Price or Location”
text:
San Francisco is a walking city and this hotel was in the perfect location. Yes, the room is small and a little worn but it was clean and comfy. I had a front room which was noisy in the day but quiet in the night except a little noisy on the weekends. The noise didn't last long. And, who stays in a room in the daytime? 
I arrived before check in time and the room clerk checked if there was a room available which there was. Everyone was very nice and helpful in the hotel. Being in a walking city with hills, I needed a high protein breakfast not rolls or pastry which was served next door in the bar. Sears on Powell was the place for breakfast. (Great coffee)
The front desk made a reservation for the shuttle back to the airport and it worked fine.

name: La Luna Inn
title: “Great time in San Francisco!”
text: I traveled to San Francisco with my brother and the hotel was very good. The staff were great and helpful. They arranged for us to go on a tour to Alcatraz when everything was sold out. You get free parking, free internet, free breakfast (although basic toast and coffee) it was great. The hotel was clean and we got clean towels everyday. A little on the noisy side because it's located right on the street but that we are used to back home. The price was the lowest I could find and I thought it was a great find. It was a quick cab ride to Fisherman's Wharf too which was great and the area we were interested in seeing the most.

name: Hotel Metropolis
title: “Funky and cool, if you can hack the neighborhood”
text:
I found the Metropolis by accident - I'd booked a room on a travel Web site at the York Hotel, a sister hotel not faraway, only to arrive there from the airport with all my stuff and find that the hotel had booked me on the wrong day. No rooms. They did offer a room, for the cheap rate I'd booked the original room for, at the Metropolis. And yes, the area is...rough. I went for a run around the area and almost vomited from the stench. Lots of homeless people, who were actually quite friendly. It is a city, you know, so that's gonna happen (not the vomiting. Just the poor people.)
Inside, however, the Metropolis was amazing. I loved the check-in desk, with its curved, carved wood, and the spacious lobby. My room was small but clean, comfortable and stylish. And Farmer Brown, the restaurant in the hotel, is not just a bar. It's an amazing noveau-Southern place (that does have an awesome bar) with the best cheese grits I ever had. The crowd was cool and friendly, and the chef apparently buys all of his produce from black family farms, which are disappearing. It was an unexpectedly funky find in an unexpectedly funky, pretty hotel. The people who talked about the size of the workout room are right - it's tiny. And the parking situation is odd - if you've got a big urban hotel, you need more parking. Duh.
But I'd stay there again. If you like a real, urban experience, try it. If you're not comfortable with that...don't.

name: Comfort Inn by the Bay
title: “hotel and location is ok - front desk staff was horrible”
text:
we stayed at this hote for three nights and we booked a room with bayview. we actually requested a king bed, but on check in we were told that they only have double rooms left and we should be happy that our room is on the 7th floor (don't know what one has to do with the other). check in was our first experience with the "friendly" and "enthusiastic" front desk staff. during our stay we dealt with 5 different people at reception and they were all 5 either rude, unfriendly or absolutely bored, basically all in the wrong job.
the room was ok. quite spacious and we really had a nice view of the bay and the bridge. the breakfast was always a bit of a battle, as this hotel seems to be very popular with groups, so every morning there were groups coming at the same time so the buffet was empty quite quickly and as there were not too many tables, one morning we didn't manage to get a table straight away. breakfast itself is no highlight, but sufficient.
the location was goog. to the cable car you have to walk three blocks (very steep uphill that is), to Fisherman's Wharf it's about 20-25 min. walk, but there is also a bus going there. parking was with US 26,- (I think) not too cheap.
there are no extra services at the hotel. NO business center with internet access, NO fitness center, NO pool, NO restaurant...
all in all I would say it was ok for what we've paid, but if you want friendly staff - don't go there!

name: Comfort Inn by the Bay
title: “Bed Bugs and Filthy Room”
text:
Don't stay here if you care about avoiding a bed bug infestation in your own place of living. The last night we stayed, we discovered a bed bug crawling on us while sitting on the bed. When this issue was brought up to the Front Desk staff, they did nothing, our rooms weren't changed, we weren't given new reservations at a different hotel, nothing. We had to sleep in the bed bug room, feeling itchy and gross, knowing that when we checked out, we would have to quarantine our clothes, luggage and everything outside of our house when we returned home. 
At check-out, I spoke to the Manager on duty who comped one night for our 'grievances.' I asked whether all of the rooms had moldy curtains, dirty ice buckets, and bed bugs, "of course not," he replied.
I called my friends back home and had them put out garbage bags and clean clothes outside of our house for when we got there. We had to change outside. Our luggage is still in the garbage bags on our patio.

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “A fine place to stay”
text:
We stayed at the Orchard in May of 2005.
THE GOOD
The Orchard is still a fairly new hotel, VERY clean and well-kept with tasteful, serene decor, large room & bath, and a mostly helpful (sometimes aloof??) staff. Door persons get honorable mention here for being especially efficient. But you get free use of a laptop in the lobby (good for printing boarding passes or checking e-mail although there is a small per-page fee for printing), free newspaper, large TV with surround sound, and free DVD checkout (which we didn’t use but is a good option for a rainy day). Room also comes equipped with a refrigerator and a good-sized closet. There are only a handful of rooms on each floor and the twice/day maid service is excellent and discreet--we never saw them come and go.
THE NOT-SO-GOOD
I say “not-so-good” here because nothing at the Orchard was really “bad.” First off, I didn’t think the continental breakfast was anything special. We stayed in four different places along the California coast on our trip--all with free continental breakfast--and of the four, I thought the Orchard’s offering here was the most lacking in variety. And the atmosphere in the breakfast room was a little formal and stiff; my partner and I don’t handle "formal" so well first thing in the morning! In fact, I can’t help but wonder if the entire hotel might be perhaps a little TOO quiet (dead??) for those younger folk who may be seeking something a bit more hip on their visit to this bustling city. The hotel also is a rather grueling walk up a steep hill if you're heading from the Bart and mini metro stations; I would not recommend hauling armloads of luggage from those stations to the Orchard. In fact, I might go so far as to recommend something a bit closer to Market Street if you anticipate using the trains much at all while in town. And although the surround sound in the rooms is nice, this also encourages your neighbors to test these systems out--which our neighbor seemed to want to do at 7 a.m. every morning. There was a little too much noise emanating from the hallways at times, mostly from heavy room doors that were almost impossible to shut without slamming them. And finally, I found the bed to be a little too firm to my liking, and what's with not having a sheet between your body and the comforter?
Overall, though, I would recommend the Orchard. Having a large, clean room in and of itself makes the stay worth it. I think it's a good, solid choice that would be perfect for any first-time visitor to San Francisco--just don't expect anything too risque here.

name: Grant Plaza Hotel
title: “Horrible”
text: The hotel room we stayed is was nothing like the website. Our room smelled of mold. When we asked the front desk for a good chinese restaurant in the area he advised us "I dont eat around here". As this is a hotel in chinatown the front desk should have been able to provide us with information on dining. They we not very helpful. I WOULD NOT STAY IN THIS HOTEL AGAIN!!!

name: Grant Plaza Hotel
title: “Super Location!”
text: Small, small rooms but very clean and right in the middle of everything, especially if you purchase a muni pass. California St cable car 1 block away, Union Square is a 5 minute walk, and Bart Powell Station is within walking distance too. Right in China Town so it's a bit noisy but you just get use to the city sounds. Pretty unbelieveable for the price!

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway
title: “Value for money.”
text:
We were a little apprehensive about our stay at this hotel after reading some of the reviews on this site concerning the friendliness and helpfulness of the staff, however we need not have been. We found the staff to be extremely polite and helpful, offering advice on places to visit although we were not that impressed with their recommendations on the local restuarants. 
Due to the location of this hotel you would need to be fit and healthy to tackle the 30 minute walk to Fisherman's Wharf. The paths/roads are very very steep but offer fantastic views for your efforts. A taxi was about $7.
A taxi from San Francisco Airport to the hotel was $51.
Hotel restaurant basic but acceptable for breakfast.

name: Hotel Beresford
title: “Room”
text: Hotel is in a great location easy access to everything. The only thing that I do wish to mention is that we found the room is very hot. There is no airflow through the room so makes it very hot. The staff are friendly and the breakfast was nice.

name: Hotel Whitcomb
title: “Nice place and location in a Great city”
text: Center location in SF with friendly staff. Rooms has a historic feel to it so don't expect modern but still a comforting and nice place to stay. Beds are AWESOME to sleep in really comfortable.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Americania
title: “Average”
text: My experience with the staff was very pleasant. Everyone was friendly. Although I felt very safe within the property the surrounding area was very unsafe. The hotel itself was clean although seemed a little run down. I keep hearing newly remodeled but I have to believe that happen a while ago. We had friends that were with us and their experience was not very good. We were all there to see the Kraft Bowl. They got there on a Sunday and checked in a little before 3. They had to rush to get down to the park. After the game it was late and they went to sleep except for one in there party. He stayed up later. When he pulled out the couch bed there was no mattress. Not to disturb anyone in the room he chose to sleep on the floor. The next day, they went to the front desk and told them there was no mattress. Thought maybe they should of received a little discount. There response was pretty much oh well. should of told us. My response is it should not have happened in the first place. Not cool!!!!!

name: BEST WESTERN The Hotel California
title: “Best hotel of our 2 week holiday”
text: A lovely light and airy room and though not massive it was easily big enough as a double. The wooden floors were lovely and definitely felt cleaner than some of the carpeted ones in other hotels. The decor was lovelyand clean and the bed comfy with lovely cotton sheets. The location is great, just 3 blocks from union square and the outside noise was limited. The plumbing was a bit noisy at times but this wasn't a problem at all for us. The building itself is lovely with character and some great quirky decorations. The desk staff weren't over friendly but were efficient in their role. The free wine and cheese was an unexpected bonus and although the cheese and biscuits were limited, it's free so who cares! The internet was reliable and the rooms were well cleaned each day. There was a later than usual check out time of 12pm which was great asit meant less rushing. There are loads of hotels in and around this area but for the price we paid we were both really impressed with the room and the location.

name: Holiday Inn Civic Center (San Francisco)
title: “Ok for business; not really for vacation”
text:
This hotel has had what appears to be a fairly dramatic makeover recently,and it shows inth elobby and rooms alike. that is until you look a little closer. Althought the rooms are comfortable, including the bed, the sliding doors have not been updated. they are circa 197X aluminum framed, and do not make a tight seal, allowing downtown city noise to penetrate. 
The bartender on duty was cheerful, and poured a solid drink, and the front desk staff was very friendly and efficient. Value for money, but please fix the sliding doors!

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “a great little hotel”
text:
My wife and myself stayed at this great little hotel between
the 9-14 december, our room was on the 9th floor and the room was always spotless the staff were always polite and friendly and were always willing to help
We would recomend this hotel without hesitation as an ideal base
for those people who like to be near everything.

name: Hotel Beresford
title: “Awesome employees, clean rooms, great location.”
text: I do not usually write a review, but these employees deserve a kudo or two. I go to the city, from Sacramento area, usually 3 or 4 times a year. I stay at different locations but mostly on the Square. We arrived in the City at 12:00, the parking in front is limited to about 3 cars, there was someone parked in one of these spots that, was not using the hotel. The employee went out and told the guy to move, that we were hotel quests. He allowed us to check in early. The hotel lobby was clean, the front desk people where exceptionally nice to us, we got a room on the 7th floor. The room is very small, but smelled like clean sheets, carpet appeared clean. This is not a Hilton or Marriott for sure, but if you are not picky about modern furniture, and if you are only sleeping and watching a little tv, this is a great room for the price, and the location is easy to the Square, just a block and 1/2. The bar attached is great for a few drinks, and continental breakfast is supplied in am, not fancy but enough to fill you up for a few hours. I have stayed at about 8-9 hotels on the Square and I will definately come back again to this one.

name: Hotel Metropolis
title: “Tra gli hotel di questo mio ultimo viaggio in Aprile negli U.S.A questo hotel mi sembrava quello più brutto.”
text: Sono stata in questo hotel nell'aprile scorso, mi era sembrato l'hotel meno adatto ma poi alla fine è stato quello che più mi ha soddistatta. Molto buono come prezzo, la sua posizione è attima , si trova a pochi passi da Powell street ( dove si possono prendere i cable car ) e Union Square . L'accoglienza è stata perfetta, ogni mattina nella hall si può prendere il pacchetto e nella sala al piano di sopra dove dove c'è thè e caffè e altro si può fare la colazione . Qui si trova anche il compiuter con il collegamento ad internet gratis. L'esterno non è affatto bello , ma appena dentro troverete tutto molto pulito, confortevole e bello. Le stanze non sono grandi , ma vi assicuro che sono belle e pulite. E' vero che l'hotel ha due ingressi uno su una strada con molti barboni , vi assicuro che essi non danno alcun problema . Se non avete voglia di vedere questa realtà potete uscire dall'altro ingresso che porta sulla Mason Street dove ci sono gli hotel più inn. Io non ho avuto nessun tipo di problema con queste persone , anzi mi è capitato di fare e ricevere anche qualche sorriso. Loro rispettano noi turisti , e penso vogliono essere visti come persone prima che come barboni.

name: Comfort Inn by the Bay
title: “Great Location, Clean, Updated Rooms, Good Value”
text: We stayed at the Comfort Inn by the Bay last week and were pleasantly surprised. We usually stay at higher-end hotels, but this time we just wanted a bed and bath since we'd be spending most of our time seeing the sights. We'll we couldn't believe what $130 a night got us at this prime location (AAA rate). The hotel is only blocks from Fisherman's Wharf and the less crowded, cable car turnaround. We were in easy walking distance to plenty of very nice restaurants and right across from famed Lombard Street. The hotel was recently remodeled and everything was clean, fresh and bright. Plus we had an outstanding view of the Golden Gate Bridge from our room. We would definitely stay here again. And parking was only $25 a night (which is cheap for SF).

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway
title: “Could be better”
text:
We stayed here for 2 nights.We had a what would have been a great view of the city had the windows not been so filthy.
Dirty hotel room windows give such a poor overall impression.
Food prices as usual in city hotels very high for what is only mediocre microwaved food.We ate there as it was late one night but wished we hadn't.
Not a bad location but generally a hotel that has become a bit 'retired on the job'
And please get the windows cleaned!!

name: BEST WESTERN The Hotel California
title: “Had a great stay and trip”
text:
I recently traveled to San Francisco with two of my friends for a weekend trip. We stayed in The Hotel California and thoroughly enjoyed our time there. 
The rooms weren't excessively large, but they were adequate considering that you don't really spend much time in a hotel room anyway. 
Two of the gentlemen at the front desk, Duane and Tony, were both extremely helpful. They were both incredibly friendly and on several occasions helped us find different locations around town that we were interested in, giving us what turned out to be good advice.
The wine and cheese in the afternoons was a nice touch, as was the complimentary shot of tequila.
Overall, our stay at the hotel was very pleasant.

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway
title: “OK Hotel”
text:
I stayed here for bussiness but stayed an extra night for fun. The hotel was clean and the staff was friendly and helpful. However, the location is not great, a bit of a walk to the sites/dinner through shady areas but cabs were always right out front. The hotel was dated and the rooms were small, but it was clean. Our towel rack fell off the wall and they had it fixed within 15mins. The food there was decent also.
Overall this is a decent hotel and the price was not to bad, if I had a choice I would research to see if I could get a hotel in a better location for a comparable price. 
A big plus is that wireless internet was free (just call the front desk for a code)
Also had an outdoor pool, that people were in bright and early, if you plan on sleeping in get a room away from the pool.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Americania
title: “Goed hotel”
text:
We hebben 3 nachten hier vebleven, het personeel is zeer vriendelijk en behulpzaam echter in de avonduren kan het wat luidruchtig zijn ivm jongeren die terug komen vanuit het uitgaansleven. Ook de homeless kwam je op de straat tegen vlakbij het hotel, maar zeiden niet veel maar wel erg om te zien! Mocht je naar Union Square willen lopen dan duurt dit circa 20 tot 30 mins! De hotelgasten die wij tegen kwamen waren voornamelijk jong en gasten met kinderen hebben wij niet gezien. We hebben altijd in de stad gegeten of een broodje om de hoek gehaald (Subway) dus over het eten kan ik geen oordeel over geven. 
De kamer was prima, televisie, telefoon en internet is aanwezig, alleen was het internet op sommige momenten zeer traag.. 
Totslot was ons verblijf prima voor wat we nodig hadden.

name: Hotel Metropolis
title: “Hotel Metropolis”
text:
Super modernes, sauberes und nettes Hotel. Dadurch das es sehr Zentral liegt auch etwas laut in der Nacht. Aber so sind die Städte. Man hat super Verkehrsanbindungen, Cable Car, Busse, U-Bahn.. alles in weniger als 5 geh Minuten zu erreichen. Essensmöglichkeiten gibt es dort auch genug, die in weniger als 2 geh Minuten erreicht sind. Und für die Leute die Shoppen wollen, das riesen Shoppingcenter liegt quasi schräg gegenüber sowie zahlreiche andere Geschäfte.
Es sind einige Obdachlose vor dem Hotel.. was ein wenig abschreckend ist. Man sollte wenn man aus dem Hotel geht nicht die Straße rechts herunter laufen, vorallem nicht Nachts. So steht es auch im Reiseführer. Wenn man sich daran hält sollte einem nichts passieren.
Schade war, dass der einzige Computer, der für Gäste zur Verfügung stand kaputt war und auch in 5 Tagen aufenthalt nicht Repariert wurde. Für Leute mit Laptop oder ähnlichem kein Problem, da es auf den Zimmern überall eine Drahtlose Netzwerkverbindung gab. Aber wenn man kein Gerät dabei hatte, gab es eben auch kein Internet.
Ich würde das Hotel jederzeit wieder buchen, es hat uns sehr gut gefallen, vorallem gab es jeden morgen kostenfreien leckeren Kaffee. ;)

name: Grant Plaza Hotel
title: “Ideally located”
text: Recently, my husband with my adult children stayed at Grant Plaza Hotel situated at the junction of Grant Plaza and Pine. I am glad that my daughter selected this hotel as it is very ideally situated, good reasonable hotel rate, near to shopping area, near to China Town, near to many restaurants, just a half an hour leisure walk to Fisherman Wharf and most of all hotel staff are very helpful and assisted in many ways.

name: La Luna Inn
title: “hotel de bon confort, bon petit déjeuner, acceuil parfait et bonne situation géographique”
text:
Très bon rapport qualité prix.
Chambre spacieuse et très bonne literie;
Petit déjeuner complet.
Bon accueil
Bonne situation géographique dans la ville.
Attention pour les chambres sur rue, elles doivent être bruyantes.

name: BEST WESTERN The Hotel California
title: “Good :Location, great bargain”
text: Nice hotel, good location, good restaurant on site. Rooms are clean and updated. Great value for your money in a good location, just minutes from Union Square

name: Hotel Frank
title: “Avoid this hotel - protestors shout abuse a guests, incomplete renovations and rude staff”
text:
The hotel has a dispute with former workers who protest every Wednesday Thursday Friday in the morning and late afternoon. I had heard about the protests but didn't realise what it meant. It means been woken at 7am on my holiday but the loudspeaker and having abuse shouted at me for staying in the hotel. When we politely complained about the noise (apparently we'd been given a quiet room!) the staff were rude saying it wasnt their problem and unhelpful saying we should complain to Expedia for not having clear enough warnings. Yes, they deliberately try to ruin your stay. I could deal with this if the hotel was otherwise up to scratch but it's not. When we asked if there was another room they said they would find out and then didn't bother to call back (even with chasing!).
As for the building, it doesn't live up to the photos. It is tired looking and has whole floors and the stairs under renovation (carpets removed etc.) but no sign of work taking place. Also has odd bathrooms where the shower head is so low we had to stoop.
The only positive is the location. But there are plenty of good hotels in the area for the same money. I would not stay here again or recommend it.

name: Comfort Inn by the Bay
title: “We were thrilled!”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights in January and were thrilled with the choice. The location of the hotel was excellent, close to public transport to downtown and a 10 min walk to Fishermans wharf and the cable and street cars. We had three people in our group and all were very comfortable. There was no problem with noise or anything else, the heating/cooling was efficient, the staff very helpful, the breakfast was substantial, the only thing that could have improved was having a fridge in the room but as the ice machine was only down the hall this wasn't a problem. Our suggestion to get a great rate is to shop around on the web and check trip advisor often for the reviews. We would certainly stay here again and recommend it to both friends and family!

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway
title: “Perfect base for exploring the City”
text:
We started our 3 week tour of Calfiornia and Las Vegas here and were not disappointed. It is by no way luxurious and the room we had was next to the lift and small so may be insufficient for some light sleepers. Everyone was really friendly in and around the hotel. It was clean and the lifts were quite quick.
But it was fine for what we wanted it for. Good restaurants in walking distance (Ruths Chris Steakhouse - huge side portions and not cheap, Village Pizzeria excellent Calzone for reasonable price) and we only tried breakfast once which wasn't great for what we paid. We went to Mel's Diner down the road instead which was excellent and 24 hours so if you're having trouble sleeping they are open.
It was a stone's throw away from the California Street Cable Car and regular buses pass by.
There is clearly a homeless problem in San Francisco and there were some sleeping on the streets nearby which being from London I'm ok with. Some people might find it a bit uncomfortable..

name: Hotel Whitcomb
title: “Nice Old Hotel, Not a great area”
text:
Got a good rate through Priceline and got into our room at 11:30 am
so was pleased with that.
Room was very clean and wireless worked well
Staff was friendly and helpful with tour options etc.
Lots of homeless persons around but no one bothered us. We walked to the cable car and tour bus departure points without feeling in any danger. Nighttime would be another matter.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Americania
title: “Nichts Besonders, aber OK!”
text:
Zentrales Hotel, ca. 15 Gehminuten von der touristischen Innenstadt (Market/Powell) entfernt.
Große Zimmer und sauber, aber nichts Besonderes.
20 USD parken am Haus, so gut wie kein Service (es nach nocht einmal jemand gefragt, ob man beim Gepäck helfen könnte!).
Burger-Bude und Kneipe im Haus, ansonsten ist um das Hotel rum, kulinarisch alles tot.
Fazit: Sauberes Hotel, nichts Besonderes, kleine Schwächen, Preis-/Leistung OK.

name: Holiday Inn Civic Center (San Francisco)
title: “Sambie10”
text: Arrived at airport got train15 min ride to 8th street hotel right across the road was great. Checkin was quick. Booked a smoking room with balconey. On entering room it was disgusting very old and smelled musty the veiw looking at a wall. Returned to lobby was very busy returned at night told them not happy with the room. Was told u booked a smoking room. Said yes but dont smoke in the room just wanted balcony the man behind the desk was great upgrade us to the 12th floor had balcony with a great veiw very updated room. I think smoking room means you can smoke in the room I dont do. Thanks Holiday Inn. Getting round is easy you can get passport for 1, 2, ect days which lets u on the tram trains and cablecars Homless people around but felt safe would stay again.

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “A very good stay”
text:
My husband & I had a wonderful time on our trip March 7-9 at the Orchard & although there were a couple of 'cons' to go along with the many pros of this hotel, we would definitely come back again.
We booked through the Orchard's website and paid $149.00 per night (AAA rate) for a king deluxe room and this included valet parking for two nights & free breakfast. I requested a high floor as far from the street as possible with a street view, in case of noise. We received a floor on the 9th floor (there are only 10 floors) with street view and it was nice and quiet. Our car was always brought around within 20 minutes of our calling down for it. The room was clean, large and nicely furnished. The two feather pillows provided were awful and far too small for the king bed so after the first night, I called housekeeping for better pillows and 5 minutes later I was brought three larger (much better) pillows and we slept so much better that night. 
The surround sound system was sort of a waste since all the speakers were crowded on a shelf together above the TV.
The bathroom was large by S.F. standards and the quartz(?) countertops & marble tile inlay in the ceramic tile floor was a nice touch. The blowdryer was fairly worthless to me, however, so consider bringing your own if you want to dry your hair in less than an hour's time.
I found the continental breakfast was great although my husband had actually hoped for pasteries which were not on the tables either morning - just mini muffins, bagels and croissants along with the many other things mentioned in other reviews.
The staff was friendly, greeting us and smiling each time we headed in or out of the elevators and the absolutely best feature of this hotel would have to be the LOCATION. Just around the corner from the Powell cable car stop and just two blocks up the hill from Union Square. Very convenient.
Great stay, good price, wonderful weather.....another satisfied customer.

name: BEST WESTERN The Hotel California
title: “Savoy was poor value, with service problems”
text:
I was staying in San Francisco at the same time a few people I had just met were, and they were all paying significantly (30- 50%) less at their hotels than I was at the Savoy. My room at the Savoy was bigger than theirs, but we were all staying in the same (slightly sleazy--many bums, prostitutes and massage parlors) area around Union Square. Note, the "city-view" rooms the Savoy offers for slightly more on the phone just mean you can see the bums, prostitutes and massage parlors from your room. There's much bettter value than the Savoy.
Also, while the people working there were nice enough, the actual service I got had some serious problems. The voicemail in my room didn't work, and they never fixed it or got back to me when I reported it. The towel rack in my room was broken, and twisted away from the wall the first time I put a towel on it. A note left by two of my friends at the front desk was never given to me, and to make it worse, they gave the note to somebody who knew me that came in off the street. Now, in this case, it was a friend, so no harm done. But the idea they gave a note for me to somebody who came in off the street is such a violation of trust. Also, a couple of times they sent visitors upstairs to see if I was in my room, rather than calling up. Given the sleazy neighborhood, I'd want to see a lot better security.
Not a horrible place, but you can do a lot better. Go somewhere else.

name: Holiday Inn Civic Center (San Francisco)
title: “3 stars hotel charge 4 stars hotel breakfast buffet”
text: This hotel in general is a good value compare to nearby hotels, around $150, less than 5 min walk to BART/MUNI station. Everyone knows the neighborhood wasn't great, but close to BART is the biggest selling point, as you know SF's weather can be unpredictable, I mean who want to drag their luggage after a long flight for 5-6 blocks in downpours ? It seems like they had finally finished their renovation, modern rooms and bathrooms, good complimentary wifi. However, the hallways still have old carpets. Before the renovation, they used to give out vouchers for breakfast buffet for priority club members. Now, they are charging $19.95 ! That is just outrageous for a 2.5-3 stars hotel in SF ! I would expect that price maybe for a Hilton or Sheraton, but not Holiday Inn. Even Hilton Garden Inn would only charge $9.95-$12.95 for their breakfast buffet with cook-to-order eggs ! This place doesn't even have that feature, all they have are scramble eggs. As a Holiday Inn, I would expect something like $14.95 for breakfast buffet to be more reasonable.

name: La Luna Inn
title: “Je le conseille sans problème”
text: chambre spacieuse et confortable avec cabinet de toilette en bonne état et fonctionnel. Lit de grande largeur, trés confortable avec linge de lit trés agréable (doux). Linge de toilette de bonne qualité et changé tous les jours. Seule critique: la proximité de la rue lombard, trés passagère à toute les heures de la journée associée au simple vitrage de la chambre donc assez bruyant mais pour ma part ça n'a pas été une difficulté insurmontable. Situation géographique idéale, bien desservi par le bus. Petit dej continental offert tous les matins.

name: Holiday Inn Civic Center (San Francisco)
title: “Location, location, location..."”
text:
Hotel was well located within an easy walk to major San Francisco sites or access to transit. Staff were very courteous and helpful, identifying nearby restaurants that were all very good.
There is a large homeless population in the area that may take some visitors aback, though the area is being regentrified with planned condos and restaurants opening soon.
I had no problem staying here with my family and would recommend it to anyone visiting this City for an affordable option.

name: Comfort Inn by the Bay
title: “Gute Lage für Stadbesichtigung - eher YMCA Standard”
text: Die Lage des Hotels ist gut. Wenn man die richtige Seite des Hotels - auf die Lombardstreet raus - erwischt hat man einen Blick auf die Golden Gate Bridge. Wir hatten Hinterhof , was wegen der fehlenden Straße ein eher ruhiges Zimmer war, Der Frühstücksraum ist eher YMCA als das eines Hotels. Aber für ein bisschen Toast und einen Kaffee war's ok. Schräg gegenüber: BOBO's Restaurant die defintiven besten Steaks der Welt und leckerste Dungeness Crabs !!!

name: La Luna Inn
title: “Excellent hotel”
text: Excellent hotel, trés confortable, literie top ! Petit déj offert sympathique. Personnel main desk trés aimable et serviable, parking gratuit. Bémol, hotel situé sur lombard st, axe ultra passant 24/7, prévoir boules quies pour sommeil paisible, mais ca n'est pas un problème. Bien situé, marche à pied possible, bus rue parallèle

name: Encore Express Hotel
title: “Great place to be but you get what you pay for!”
text:
This hostel is really conveniently located and is unbeatably cheap for San Francisco - if you are just looking for somewhere to lay your head and grab a shower it's fine! If you want somewhere to hang out or spend time, I'd keep looking!
The room I stayed in (4 bed female dorm) had only one plug socket... which was behind one of the beds. This meant charging my phone whilst in the shower (if the shower room with the sink and socket was free) or sitting out in the corridor with it for half an hour!
I was in a top bunk, which would have been fine except for the heavy glass and metal light fixture that was conveniently placed right above the ladder, meaning that I cracked my head on it every time I climbed into bed (trying to be quiet and considerate at 2:30am!!)
However, the place was clean (enough) and quiet (enough), the showers were surprisingly powerful and consistent and the girl that checked me in was not exactly friendly but she was at least efficient. For $25 a night in the middle of San Francisco I have absolutely no complaints!

name: Comfort Inn by the Bay
title: “Accueil deplorable”
text: Hotel bien place. Staff nul et accueil pourri(evangeline cerbère de service Nous parlant comme a des chiens) petit dej Correct mais surpeuplé. Hotel très moyen. Parking pratique 26 USD par jour + taxes. Chambres avec vue mais petites et moyennes. Je ne le conseille pas. N est pas a la hauteur

name: Hotel Mark Twain
title: “Clean, comfortable and good location”
text:
Overall I would recommend this hotel. The location is very convenient for Union Square and is walking distance from the shopping centres if you want to take advantage of them. From Union Square you can easily take a tram to other areas of the city if you wish. The area is definitely 'up and coming' however it felt reasonably safe to me, similar to many urban areas in other cities in which you should follow common sense and take the usual precautions of keeping an eye on your stuff etc. San Francisco seems to have a very high proportion of homeless and drug addicts through out the city in general. 
You should factor in the cost of valet parking into the cost of your hotel at approx $30 a day. Parking in SanFrancisco is difficult and expensive and the hotel parking is actually a convenient and good deal. It is more expensive elsewhere and parking in the street is difficult and complicated by street cleaning. 
The rooms were very clean and comfortable and suitable for purpose. The bathroom was small but very clean with a decent shower. We had a problem with our light but maintenance were quick to sort out the problem. 
The hotel restaurant Fish & Farm was also very good. It had a nice ambience and served some nice plates of food.

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway
title: “Watch out for the windows!”
text:
Just a warning, we were surprised to find that the window opened up on our 22nd floor. Imagine if a kid managed to pry it open!!! That was not safe feature there at all.
No fan in the bathroon and no vent that worked for us. Room was an ok size but nothing special at all. Really old and basic. It was also noisy there. Parking was expensive too.
View was great and so was the breakfast buffet. 
Would not stay again.

name: Hotel Bijou
title: “Decent hotel in a good location”
text: The Hotel Bijou has serviceable, if outdated, rooms. The beds, in particular, are too soft, though not exactly uncomfortable. However, for the price, it is certainly a decent option. The service is good and the location is excellent - very central with great public transportation. Sure, it's noisy, but this is almost always the case for the smaller, older hotels in this part of town. As for safety, this is downtown San Francisco, People! Sure, it's seedy, has street people, etc. - but I wouldn't call it unsafe.

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway
title: “AVG. HOTEL”
text:
We just returned from a one night – New Year’s Eve – stay at the Holiday Inn Golden Gateway on Van Ness in San Francisco. I got it on Hotwire for $70 – no luck on Priceline for less.
This is a solid 2.5* property. The room was clean and quiet, but the ice maker was broken and the bathroom sink didn’t drain well. These are the little issues that one is more likely to experience at a Holiday Inn. Front desk staff was slow. Elevators had key-card entry, which was a nice safety feature. The area around the hotel is sketchy at best, but that is SF for ‘ya.
Self-parking is convenient and a bargain at $29/night compared to the high parking fees at Union Sq. hotels. Ingress and egress is also convenient via Van Ness. I would stay here again, but certainly for no more that $45 on a normal night – it was ok for $70 on New Year’s Eve considering that the hotel appeared to be sold out.

name: Hotel Frank
title: “very bad hotel”
text:
this hotel is poor 
bad service
expensive 
the beds are very bad

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “The worst service I have ever experienced”
text:
On the whole the hotel is satisfactory, save the lifts which can take ten minutes to arrive. However the service falls short of even the most basic of standards. Not once did anyone fulfil any request. Staff were rude, and at one point obnoxious. One memeber of staff even walked off as i was in the middle of asking a question.
The wireless is also poor and intermittent.
For the same money, stay at The Clift.

name: Beck's Motor Lodge
title: “A Castro Tradition!”
text:
Beck's is not a fancy hotel, nor does it try to be. It is a motor lodge in the gayest part of a gay city. Expect anything different and you will be disappointed.
Pros - Free onsite parking, adjacent to public transportation access, relatively inexpensive, great location.
Cons - Few amenities, can be loud, no-frills
All and all, we love Beck's, and we stay there whenever we are visiting San Francisco.

name: Beresford Arms
title: “Excellent hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed here for 4 nights in November and we loved the hotel. The location is really good, it's about 3 blocks from Union Square. The overall look of the hotel is very nice, you just don't see the style of architecture that this hotel has in newer buildings. Everything is very well maintanined and clean. The room was good, it was surprisingly large for a an older hotel, including the bathroom. The staff was very friendly. And the price was great especially considering the location. The only downside for us was the continental breakfast, the selection was very limited. But hey it was free and there are plenty of places to eat breakfast in the area, so we really didn't mind. We would highly recommend this hotel.

name: Holiday Inn Civic Center (San Francisco)
title: “good hotel in a bad location”
text: The hotel is great and the staff was very helpful. But the location is not very good because of many homeless people at the street.

name: Hotel Union Square
title: “Great location, Good decor but rooms either noisy or small!!”
text:
Stayed 3 nights at this hotel at the beginning of August. Travelling with two other couples. They both had rooms that were at the back of the building, decorated lovely but were very small & dark. We had a room on the 1st floor at the front which was a good size and again decorated lovely but we hardly slept due to the noise from the trams, delivery lorries and emergency vehicles. It is a city hotel in a great location but it might benefit from some double glazing!! The staff were helpful and friendly at this little boutique hotel.
If we were to visit San Francisco again we would stay at this hotel.
You wouldn't want to spend more then 3 nights there though due to lack of a decent sleep or not being able to unpack your case and falling over the corner of the bed (which happened to one of our party).

name: Hotel Whitcomb
title: “proche de tout mais quartier un peu glauque”
text:
hôtel de très bonne prestation, confort ++ avec salle de bain pratique mais petite (pas grave!) Hotel à l'allure très luxueuse et aux prestations onéreuses, breakfast assez cher. personnel sympathique et hotel proche du centre ville (union station, powel, cable car, capitol...) mais les environs de l'hotel sont assez mal fréquentés : SDF en nombre, dealer...mais ne sont pas inquiétants ni gênants.
ville agréable, pas mal de choses à voir et possible à pieds mais il faut s'armer de courage
Je recommande!

name: The Pickwick Hotel San Francisco
title: “Friendly staff, hotel in perfect location for travellers”
text: stayed for 4 nights, what a lovely clean, and useful hotel this is.. Louis the concierge was brilliant loved him, loved the hotel and loved San Francisco....Cant understand other peoples reviews complaining about it.. Check in very quick check out same..with friendly staff to boot...

name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
title: “Disappointing for a Hilton ... a 3.5 star experience ... multiple issues”
text:
First-timer at the Hilton-Financial District ... disappointed ...
GRADE: B- (OK-average) ... it should have been better. On to the review:
HOTEL: A large, almost monolithic,concrete (exterior)-looking hotel nestled at the edges of Chinatown, Financial District, adult-entertainment district, and SF version of Little Italy (along Columbus Ave). Very convenient to all of these and with a bit of additional walking, Union Square & Market St. The hotel is a weak representation of Hilton ... probably primarily a business hotel, with a large lobby ... greeted by somewhat disinterested front desk. It was an odd front lobby ... with a large aquarium, giant clocks on the wall, along with a pseudo-combo-bar-concession/souvenir-stand near the front doors, a giant map of SF on opposite side of front desk, and then towards back is the in-house restaurant named Seven-Fifty, which we did not try. The hotel felt a little dated, a little worn & tired, a little run-down..... and we're not that overly picky. The hallway to our room was rather dim, seemed dingy, & grim vs warm, inviting, bright, or colorful. 
ROOM: Be forewarned: We requested a room on South side of hotel, away from construction going on at North side (new building going up). When we went out for dinner at 6:00, we heard some construction noises & activities still going....so ... ask for the South-facing city view side of hotel. We were situated on a mid-level floor on the 20th floor, and had a view of buildings, as expected, and it was fairly quiet. We could clearly see Chinatown, and the hill-y streets that run through the area. There was a large combo-credenza-desk that ran from wall to wall of the room by the window, with the flat TV on it, built-in A/C-heat unit, and plug-in options for tech-goodies you bring. Seemed ok, though a bit long, and overwhelming. Would have been nicer if not as full-length, and had the extra floor space as well as be able to stand by the window. A nice chaise-style lounge chair made for comfortable viewing of TV. The double-beds were comfortable. The bathroom was an issue.... clean enough, but there were visible cracks in ceiling, peeling paint, and oddly, a rusting towel rack. How do you have a towel rack above the tub, that rusts ?!?! Speaking of the tub, it was elevated ... such that when taking a shower, our heads were above the curtain-rod ... very odd. No, not built for handicapped either. And the towels ... blah.... fairly matted down, somewhat dingy, not very white, and one of them had large holes ..... this is a HILTON ?!?! Paris, would you stay here ??? More oddities: no bathroom cups, no shampoo ... and we asked the cleaning staff in hallway working on another room for these basics, were told they had no more. What ?!?! "No more" ?!?! Wow! Moving on ... the room was warm & musty when we first arrived, so we turned the thermostat on ... nothing happened, and then lowered it to 60 degrees, felt nothing. Additionally, two lamps were not working = bedside and free-standing. Only the small desk lamp was working. 'Engineering' was called = fixed the A/C, fixed one lamp and the other needed a part.... and given we were there just one night, we told him to fix it another day. Sure enough, as the sun set, room was dark even with all the working lights on. TV on helped. Not a huge issue. Lastly, we did have a connecting room, and heard people talking ... but not on that side of the room!!! The voices were coming from the non-connecting side ... thin walls??
SUMMARY: If you're visiting for business and want easy access to nearby Transamerica building, Financial District, Embarcadero, or visiting SF for nearby Chinatown, along with the many restaurants/bars on/near Columbus Ave, this is most convenient. If you're looking for a quaint, romantic, or warm/friendly hotel, this isn't it. For general tourists, there are so many other great hotels at comparable prices and more convenience for sightseeing than this hotel. It is clearly in need of a spruce up, from decor, staff-efforts, and room upgrades. Don't get us wrong ... it is not a dump, but it is not a 4-star hotel either. We recommend this hotel if you get a good rate, or convenience to specific area is essential. Otherwise, so many other great options in this wonderful city.
Happy Hotel-ing !!!

name: Hotel Frank
title: “Great hotel, great location!”
text:
Stayed just for the one night at the end of June as we were only in San Francisco to see Alcatraz. Spent not a lot of time in the room which is unfortunate as the hotel was fantastic. Room was very spacious and extremely clean and modern. Bed was comfortable and we didnt hear any street noise until about 8:30am or so. Free WiFi was quick too. 
Staff were great and the concierge was very helpful. Didn't see or hear anything about the protests which was lucky for us, sounds like the people need to get over themselves as the staff that do work at Hotel Frank seemed very happy to us and guests are entitled to stay at which ever hotel they choose. 
Highly recommeded and wish we had more time there!

name: Warwick San Francisco Hotel
title: “Fantastic Hotel Made Better by Great Customer Service”
text: I stayed at The Warwick Hotel in San Francisco for one night in May 2012. It was a wonderful 24 hours! I booked 2 rooms. One of the members of our party was not feeling well and when I informed the front desk clerk, he went above and beyond to make sure we got an upgraded room to make our stay most comfortable. It was truly unexpected but so greatly appreciated. The upgraded room was actually two rooms with two baths! The standard room was wonderful as well. Spacious and very nicely appointed. The ceiling fan was a great addition to th room, because I like to have that on at home. I felt like all details to comfort were taken in to consideration. The furnishings were very refined and dignified. I almost felt like we were staying in a very upscale hotel in Europe. Aside from the perfection of the hotel and staff, the hotel is in a great location with numerous shops, restaurants, and access to public transportation. This hotel would work well for both leisure and business travelers.

name: Holiday Inn Civic Center (San Francisco)
title: “Ne trainer pas trop tard”
text:
L'hôtel est correctement tenu; les chambres sont grandes et propres.
Pour $21 (sant les tips), on peut prendre un petit déjeuner en profitant du buffet à volonté.
Il est également agréable de pouvoir profiter d'une piscine dans San Francisco.
De plus, depuis l'aéroport, on y accède en quelques minutes via le Bart (pour moins de $9); la station est pratiquement au pied de l'hôtel.
Malheureusement, le point le plus négatif est le quartier. 
Il se situe entre la 8th et market street; vous croiserez donc de nombreux SDF de jour comme de nuit mais également des drogués et des dealers le soir venu.
La police tourne très régulièrement mais il est vrai que ce n'est pas rassurant.
Personnellement, je n'ai eu aucun problème et pourtant je rentrais assez tard le soir.
Le plus simple est de prendre un taxi.
Le plus malheureux est de voir toute cette misère dans un pays qui se dit si riche ...
Sans ce petit désagrément, cet hôtel serait plutôt pas trop mal situé : au pied de Civic Center, à 15mn de Union Square ou Moscone Center ... et avec des lignes de bus ou de tramways qui déservent bien la ville.

name: Hotel Bijou
title: “Excellent rapport qualité prix”
text:
Personnel souriant et serviable. 
Chambres très propres et salles de bains petites mais bien équipées. 
Grand placards. 
Situation parfaite avec tram et câble car à deux pas. Restaurants sympas et boutiques en bas de la rue. 
Parfait pour un séjour agréable. Petite salle de cinéma en bas de l'hôtel. Un film différent chaque soir. 
Petit déjeuner très correct.

name: Hotel des Arts
title: “Great hotel”
text: Super fun, clean, affordable and great location. I've stayed here a few times both with shared bathroom as well as my own bath. Will stay here again. Fun, good coffee in the morning, and nice people.

name: Castle Inn
title: “An Experience that is Difficult to Explain”
text:
My wife and I visited SF for the first time and stayed at the Castle Inn ("CI") for three nights. My initial impression at check in was that maybe we had selected accomodations that ran contrary to our tastes and preferences. We do not have any children and stay mostly at four-star hotels/resorts when we travel. In contrast, the CI is an older motel that has outward facing rooms. 
In the spirit of vacation, and based on user reviews, I kept an open mind. The rooms are what I would term "economy," somewhat in the order of a Comfort Inn or a Motel 6. We found the room to be adequately clean. For those light sleepers, please keep in mind that the hotel is in the city. You will here normal traffic sounds and the rooms are not equipped with air conditioners. This is not uncommon in hotels/motels along the coast as the ocean breeze is used to cool the room. We were not bothered by the traffic and slept with the windows open the whole stay. 
While the rate may seem high relative to the accomodations, parking is free, which is a plus in a major metropolitan area. There is a coffee maker, microwave oven and refrigerator in the room. We particularly enjoyed having the refrigerator as it saved us alot of money on beverages.
Two things that made our stay enjoyable here were: (1) the central location; and (2) Marshall, who provided us with alot of information on where and where not to go. We gathered advise from him almost daily, and based on his suggestions, we were even able to take the walking tour of Alcatraz, despite the fact it was listed as fully booked during the length of our stay.
The location of CI is unique in that it is easy to get to all the major sights and attractions. Additionally, there are a range of places to eat within close proximity to the hotel (ranging from pizza to upscale casual dining), as well as a Walgreens within two blocks. Just ask Marshall for a suggestion. 
We found that the only time we were in our our room was to sleep, so we would not have used many of the ammenities found in higher-end hotels for this trip. There is just too much to see and do. Overall, we were happy with our stay at CI.

name: Warwick San Francisco Hotel
title: “Great Location; Great Price”
text:
I'm joining TripAdvisor finally because I've found everyone's reviews on here to be so helpful when I've planned my vacations. I'm hoping you will find this review helpful as well.
I can't say enough good things about the Warwick. This was our first trip to San Francisco and the hotel is in a great location, close enough to the BART, MUNI and Cable Car. There are many yummy restaurants all within a two-block radius. There was a rental car location just a block away. 
Our room was clean and very nicely decorated. From what I researched most hotels in this area of the city have small rooms. The room here was smaller than say your average Hilton or Marriott room, but the bathroom was larger than other hotels I looked at in the area. 
The price was fantastic. I booked through booking.com and saved a bundle! I may not have gotten a continental breakfast or free wifi, but the price more than made up that difference! 
The staff was always helpful and courteous. They made you feel very welcome. 
Again, I can't say enough good things about this hotel! I highly recommend staying here if you are in San Francisco!

name: Warwick San Francisco Hotel
title: “Little updates since 1913”
text:
Hotwire gave this hotel a 3 1/2 star rating--that was my first and last time using Hotwire. The small lobby with battered furniture and scarred paint was a preview of the miniscule room. If the hotel had been updated at all since it's construction in 1913, it may have been to add electricity and an elevator. There's no AC and even if your room faces the alley instead of the street (as ours did), you get a lot of street noise. The room size was miniscule as was the bathroom.
The staff was friendly. However, the night clerk assured me that I should book a shuttle to the airport instead of a cab because it was cheaper and would only take 15 minutes. WRONG. When the shuttle arrived he told me we were the first (not the last as the clerk had told me) of his stops and that it would take at least 45 minutes to get to the airport. We lost our $15 deposit and grabbed a cab. 
I will never stay at a dive like this again.

name: The Stratford
title: “Pratico”
text: Piccolo albergo, ma sufficiente per passare qualche giorno in questa bellissima città. A due passi dalla principale piazza Union Square, con il cable fuori dall'entrata, e le principali linee a pochi passi. La camera non era male, ma io avevo preso quella più carina, purtroppo era con vista sulla strada principale e risultava essere abbastanza rumorosa, non posso immaginare d'estate senza l'area condizionata. La colazione non era per niente male, tutto fresco e abbondante. Camere pulite e i ragazzi alla reception erano disponibili e simpatici. Qualità e rapporto prezzo da prendere in considerazione. Abbiamo pagato 40 dollari per il trasporto in taxi dall'aeroporto.

name: The Stratford
title: “fantastisk beliggenhed i hjertet af SF”
text: Hotellet har en fantastisk beliggenhed ved Union Square i hjertet af SF. Fine værelser, om end noget små. Vær obs på at der ikke er gratis wi-fi på hotellet. Det koster 11 dollar pr. 24 timer, så det kan godt løbe op, hvis du bruger internettet til f.eks. at finde spisesteder og lign. i SF.

name: Hotel Bijou
title: “Kult - zentral gelegen aber mittlerweile grenzwertiges Viertel”
text: Das Bijou ist ein süßes geschmackvolles Hotel was sehr zentral gelegen ist. Leider beginnt am gleichen Straßeneck eine nicht so schöne Gegend. Wir waren 4 mal im Bijou und es hat flair - nettes Personal und liegt strategisch gut. Zimmer sind klein und überwiegend nicht ganz leise. dafür passt das Preis- Leistungsverhältnis und einiges hat sich zum positiven gewendet, nachdem es neue Eigentümer bekommen hat. Wir würden wieder ins Bijou gehen.

name: Hotel Frank
title: “Fabulous in every way”
text: Stayed at this hotel for 3 days (wish it could have been more) on a tour of California and it was the best hotel by far in all our trip. Room is beautiful, bed & pillows the most comfortable ever had at a hotel. Staff were extremely helpful. Ate in restaurant and had the best meal in all our 14 day tour of California. Location is excellant for sight seeing, a real central location, good at night for eating out, safe to walk around. Renovations are all finished and they have done a fine job. One of my favourite hotels ever and would thoroughly recommend.

name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
title: “Clean, friendly and welcoming”
text: I stayed here with a group of friends for 2 nights to start off out road trip. On arrival, the hotel was clean and we didn't have to wait long to check in. Upon arriving at our room, we discovered that there were not enough towels, but one call to reception and towels were out our door! There was a free safe, hairdryer and iron in the room and all that was missing was a fridge! Would stay here again if I were to go back to San Francisco, which was a fantastic city!

name: Beresford Arms
title: “Immer wieder!!!!!”
text: Ein äußerst empfehlenswertes Hotel: Freundlich, sauber, große Zimmer, gute Betten und günstige Lage: Supermarkt, Restaurants in unmittelbarer Nähe, die Cable Car gerade mal drei Blocks entfernt. Zum Frühstück gibt es Muffins, sicher nicht jedermanns Sache aber in den USA nicht unüblich. Fazit: Ein empfhlenswertes Hotel, gerade auch für längdere Aufenthalte in San Francisco.

name: CLIFT San Francisco
title: “Excellent,modern,well located,trendy hotel”
text: Nice environment, great location, had a nice time at the Redwoodroom on Saturday for drinks....velvet room opened up for a Live Concert.....great location....close to shopping big names....close to cablecar,restaurants....rooms are very modern and complete...stayed on the 12th floor studio....I highly recommend it.

name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
title: “Terrible, terrible, terrible, an absolute false rating of a four star.”
