text: My wife and I thought would be nice to enjoy our honeymoon at a four star hotel, but we thought wrong. I have seen three star hotels have a lot better service and quality. You could smell marijuana smoke in the hall way, and inside the elevators. The hallways are full of trash and no one seems to go around checking on each floor for cleanliness until late in the afternoon the next day. Parking is way over priced and there's no valet parking, what kind of four star hotel that doesn't have valet parking. Front desk personnel argue with you, whatever happen to customers are almost always right. Absolutely terrible hotel.

name: Hotel Whitcomb
title: “Ligger centralt”
text:
Ok hotell, god service, trevlig personal mm
Hotellet ligger i centrala San Francisco men på sämre delen av Merket St. med många uteliggare och skumt folk. Hållplatsen till tunnelbanan ligger strax utanför hotellt. Bekvämt att åka runt. Det är lätt att ta sig till Union Squere och The Museum of Modern Art osv.

name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
title: “Nice hotel if you have an upper room”
text: While the location of the Hilton is a little funky (it is really next to Chinatown, and almost a mile away from the heart of the Financial district), I still recommend staying there. While a large hotel with a mass of people going in and out (and a lot of street noise at the lower levels), the upper levels of the hotel have a great view of the city.

name: The Stratford
title: “Un precio justo”
text: Muy buena ubicación, en pleno Union Square. Al comienzo el hotel no tiene la mejor apariencia, el check-in no es antes de las 3 de la tarde y el personal no se caracterisa por su empatía, el mobiliario es un poco descuidado y está justo al lado de una tienda de Lush. Aun asi, el lugar es bueno, la habitación era muy grande, limpia, iluminada, un baño también muy iluminado, grande y confortable. En readlidad volveria a quedarme ahi ya que tienen precios bastante buenos, eso si, lleven su laptop y paguen la cuota de internet diaria porque arrendar uno de los pc's obsoletos que tienen en el lobby es descabelladamente caro.

name: Grant Plaza Hotel
title: “Sehr gute Wahl”
text:
Wir waren jetzt zum 3. Mal in diesem Hotel und ich muss sagen, wir fahren wieder hin.
Zentral gelegen, nahe Chinatown, sauber und dafür sehr preiswert. Wir hatten Internetzugang die ganze Zeit. Das Personal ist sehr hilfsbereit.Wir empfehlen dieses Hotel auf jeden Fall weiter. Für den Preis kann man auch nicht ein 5-Sterne-Hotel erwarten und verglichen zu anderen großen amerikanischen Städten ist dies eine sehr günstige Bleibe. 
Liliane aus Hessen

name: The Orchard Hotel
title: “Tolle Stadt, Tolles Hotel”
text:
Das Orchard Hotel in San Francisco ist ein sehr nettes, nicht allzugroßes Hotel mit gutem Restaurant und sehr freundlichem Personal. Die Lage ist perfekt: der Eingang zu Chinatown und der Union Square liegen in etwa 5min Gehdistanz, die CableCar fährt an der Ecke vorbei. Die Lobby ist elegant, die Zimmer sind groß, gut eingerichtet und heimelig; einziger Minuspunkt ist, dass die Fenster nicht zu öffnen sind. Ansonsten ein perfekter Aufenthalt!
Gleich nebenan, Ecke Powell Street, liegt ein entzückendes kleines café, dessen Frühstück man ausserdem nicht versäumen sollte.

name: Holiday Inn Civic Center (San Francisco)
title: “Good Hotel, Poor Location”
text:
We did not stay here but did a sight inspection for work (I am a travel agent).
Holiday Inn Civic Centre is another economy hotel located in downtown San Francisco in their "Civic Cenre". I would recommend this to clients over the Renoir Hotel as the interior of the hotel was of a high standard; it was just the location which lets it down.
Rooms are of a good size and family friendly with some rooms interconnecting. Child also eat free of charge when dining with an adult.

name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
title: “Great view for great value”
text:
We booked directly through Hilton's website which had a great deal if you were willing to wait until check-in to select a room type. We ended up on the 25th floor with a view of Coit Tower and Alcatraz. The room was well furnished and clean. We could hear a group get-together in the next room on one night, but it didn't put us off- I only mention in case you are extra sensitive to noise. 
The only major downside (if you have a car) is that parking is either valet for over $50 a night, or self park in a connected garage for $30 a night. Parking is expensive in central SF, but it would have been nice if the hotel could have arranged some discount for guests parking in the garage in their basement.

name: The Grant Hotel
title: “GREAT HOTEL FOR PRICE AND LOCATION”
text: We stayed in this otel in Sept 2012. The location is great cable car is at end of block. By a Citypads and you can ride for free to Fisherman 's Wharf. Union square is 4 blocks from hotel. Room was clean and bathroom looked new.Stayed in room 315 was quiet and can see next street. Staff was friendly espically American guy found me an extra pillow. Had a feel like a couple of Victorian Hotels in Europe I have stayed in. Slight smell in hall but not in room.

name: CLIFT San Francisco
title: “Trendy hotel, disappointing room”
text: I booked the Clift at the last minute as I saw a got a great offer on Expedia. When I arrived at the hotel it was past midnight and the bar/club was in full swing. The receptionist couldn’t really hear me over the music and there were people dancing all around the reception area. I didn’t mind this as it was rather amusing for me but I think that some other guests might have not appreciated this. My first impression of the hotel was “great” but when I got to my room I was slightly disappointed as it wasn’t the same quality or standard as the St Martin’s Lane in London and I was expecting similar standards. The bathroom was very small and about 2* quality so I wasn’t impressed with that. But overall I would recommend the hotel for young trendy professional people. The hotel is located in a great area so it was perfect for me to get around.

name: Hotel Union Square
title: “Gut, aber mit Nachteilen.”
text: Das Hotel entspricht den ortstypischen Standards, wobei es nicht möglich war ein Fenster zu öffnen. In ähnlichen Hotel des Stadt war dies möglich und hat das Raumklima deutlich verbessert. Zumal die Klimaanlage mit stark riechendem Desinfiziermittel und ihrer Geräuschkullisse nicht gerade positiv wahrgenommen wird. Trotzallem wird man sich auch hier wohlfühlen können und vor allem die tolle Lage schätzen lernen.

name: The Grant Hotel
title: “Great hotel!!!”
text: We really liked our stay at this hotel, clean , nice rooms, comfortable, great location and good value! it's a very good place to stay... Complementary breakfast good too... Wifi free just in the lobby... the people at the front desk (asian) were not very frindly... but you can't have it all right?!!! but I would stay there again for sure!!! It's very close to most of the attractions and to the cable car stop... that we enjoyed very much!!! Great place!!!

name: Hotel Union Square
title: “Great Position”
text:
L'hotel gode di un'ottima posizione. E' situato in Union Square, cuore commerciale della città, vicino ai "capolinea" dei Cable Cars (tramite i quali si raggiunge la baia e il Fisherman's Wharf) e alle linee principali degli autobus, permettendo di accedere facilmente alle parti più interessanti della città. 
Le camere non sono molto spaziose, ma confortevoli, sempre in riferimento agli standard americani.
Se tornassi, soggiornerei nuovamente qui, anche grazie al buon rapporto qualità/prezzo.

name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
title: “Loved the location and accommodations fine”
text:
We stayed here for a family vacation to see the sights of San Francisco. We had free room nights and were able to reserve them with no problem. We loved the location -right by Chinatown and a few blocks walking to Columbus Street and all the Italian restaurants. It was nice to be in an area that felt like a real neighborhood, rather than the chaos of somewhere like Fisherman's Wharf. We were close enough to easily get to the wharf, Alcatraz and other sights without driving our car. One day we took the city tour that picks up right by the hotel; the concierge provided details on the one that best fit our needs (1 day only rather than the 2 day of some tour companies).
The room was fine with comfortable beds, although the typical small room of a big city. We thought the hotel was quiet, with no sound from nearby rooms, despite having a few tours and business groups staying there. 
The only issue we found was that the room with two queen beds was too small to accommodate a rollaway as well, an problem with our two kids who can't share a bed. Luckily, there was a small lounge bench (sort of like a contemporary version of a "fainting couch) in the room and it was long enough to accommodate my shorter teen. The hotel promptly provided extra mattress pad, sheets and comforter and she slept there fine. If you had two tall teens and were expecting a rollaway, the room would be a problem. 
We liked that there was a coffee stand with a variety of coffee drinks and pastries right in the lobby. We also went to a small restaurant (just out the front door and left across a small alley) next door for good and economical breakfasts, including Chinese noodles if you prefer that to eggs or pancakes.
We saved on parking by using the public parking garage directly across the street rather than the hotel's pricey valet parking.
Next trip back to San Francisco I'd stay here again with no hesitation.

name: The Wharf Inn
title: “Great location-too much noise!”
text: Clean spacious rooms. Free parking. Friendly staff. Great location. If you get a balcony room be ready for LOTS of street noise. From garbage trucks to tour buses to homeless people shaking containers for money. If you are someone who can sleep thru the noise perfect place. If not try a room with no balcony -view of the parking lot.

name: King George Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text:
We chose this hotel for the location and the price. It is close to parking decks (we used one across the street), and that was a major plus. We also found plenty of places to eat nearby. Union Square is close, and there is huge shopping mall (Powell street - at the trolley turnaround) nearby. There is a Bart stop at the mall.
The room was adequate for the price. It was clean and the staff was friendly. It's an older building so there is no air conditioning (you probably wouldn't want it anyway) and the walls are quite thin. You can hear the other guests through the walls. We were on the back side of the building, so street noise wasn't a problem...except for the protestor from 7am to 8am. We also felt a little uncomfortable walking back to the hotel late at night because we were constantly asked for money from people on the streets, but this would have been the case at any of the more expensive hotels close by.
Bottom line - not bad for the price and location. The rooms are big enough for a couple but would be small for a family.

name: Castle Inn
title: “Nettes Motel an guter Lage”
text: 2 Tage vor Memorial Day, und wir hatten noch keine Bleibe in San Francisco... Aufgrund der guten Kritiken haben wir dann online ein Zimmer reserviert (war tatsächlich noch etwas frei). Zwar nicht ganz billig, aber für SF-Verhältnisse wohl ganz in Ordnung. Parking ist kostenlos, das Zimmer war geräumig und sauber. Die erste Nacht war angenehm ruhig, in der zweiten Nacht dachte leider ein Nachbar es sei lustig, die ganze Nacht den Badezimmer-Ventilator laufen zu lassen... War recht nervig und es gab wenig Schlaf, aber dafür kann das Motel ja nicht wirklich was dafür. Internet hat bei uns +/- nur am Nachmittag funktioniert, sobald ein paar Gäste da waren, gings praktisch nicht mehr :-( Frühstück gibts auch, wir waren aber in einem Restaurant.

name: Mystic Hotel by Charlie Palmer
title: “If you want to stay near Union Square, this is a great choice!”
text:
We just finished a one-night stay at the Crescent and we will definitely go back. 
We live locally (within 45 minutes of SF) and just wanted a reasonably priced place to stay so we could go to dinner and do City things without having to drive home. The Crescent was perfect. It is in fantastic position relative to Union Square, in an unassuming building just a few blocks away from all of the action. From the corner near the hotel, I could see the holy grail of shopping - the flagship Banana Republic store on Sutter Street, and Macy's was also just a few blocks down the street. Other conveniences include the parking garage (extra charge), which is located immediately around the corner, as well as a Starbucks. Finally, the other great thing about this hotel's location is that although Union Square can be busy and loud, the Crescent is in a location that allows for relative peace and quiet, despite being just steps away from everything. 
The reception staff was very friendly and helpful, and when we had confusion over our the hotel room that we had booked, they graciously upgraded us to a suite at no charge. Because of this, we had the opportunity to see two types of rooms - a basic room, and a suite. Both were clean and well-designed, with nice modern touches. The basic room, though smaller than the suite, was definitely do-able, and not as small as some rooms we have experienced at boutique hotels in the City.
The suite was fantastic, however, and we felt very fortunate to be upgraded. It was about as large as two rooms, and had a beautiful exposed brick wall, which made for a really nice atmosphere. The finishes were the same as the smaller room - modern and clean. The bed was comfortable and the room included a large flat screen TV, as well as a minibar with high-end mini liquors. (quite a great selection!)
The hotel also has a bar that seemed to be quite the scene. Tucked away from all the chaos of Union Square, with a great vibe, and some awesome looking cocktails. A great buzz without being overly crowded. We were quite surprised to see this in our little hotel.
We would highly recommend the Crescent as an option to travelers who want to stay within the Union Square area. The only thing that we would not recommend is the breakfast option if you have to pay extra for it. If you are booking through a site like Booking.com which adds a charge for the inclusion of breakfast, you might consider skipping this option. The breakfast at the Crescent was not bad, but it was very minimal. 2 types of cereal, hard boiled eggs, bagels/toast, and yogurt, coffee, and juice. Totally reasonable as an offering, just not sure that it is worth the extra cost. We opted for the Starbucks across the street.
Great hotel though...we will definitely go back!

name: Hotel Mark Twain
title: “Heruntergekommenes Hotel”
text:
Wir haben 3 Nächte im Hotel Mark Twain verbracht. Es ist ein sehr dunkles Hotel, das schon in die Jahre gekommen ist. Der Empfang war o.k., wobei uns niemand mit den Koffern geholfen hat. Die Zimmer sind in die Jahre gekommen, das einzige Moderne ist ein Flatscreen-TV. Die Badezimmer sind sehr klein und schmuddelig. Die Zimmer zur Straße sind rund um die Uhr sehr laut, die Zimmer zum Innenhof sind ruhiger. Das Hotel ist am Rande eines der schlechteren Stadtteile von SF, so dass Obdachlose auf der Straße und in den Hauseingängen rund ums Hotel die Regel sind.
Der einzige Lichtblick war der Coffeeshop mit einem genialen Frühstück direkt neben dem Hotel.

name: King George Hotel
title: “Good location, good amenities.”
text: We picked the King George for its central location and as it came up slightly cheaper than other hotels in this area. The room was modern, nicely decorated and reasonably spacious. Staff were friendly and free wifi easy to use. Situated close to 24 hr diners, one of which will deliver to room via reception. Would stay again. I guess there may be different room types looking at some of the other comments - we were on the first floor and it was absolutely fine.

name: Hilton San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “No WiFi in rooms only wired and I have a MacAir. Room service is awful. I will not return.”
text: I booked my family in here using points left from several years ago. This place reminded me of why I only stay at Marriotts when staying at a full service hotel. Parking 40 bucks a day, room service that was the worst in my 20 years of weekly business travel, WiFi in lobby only, not at all what a Hilton used to be. Waste of points.

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Our romantic getaway in SF”
text:
we live in the South Bay and coming up to the St Francis for a night away is a bit of a tradition for us. As usual it was a wonderful experience. We took advantage of a package that provided us with champagne in the evening and breakfast the next morning. It was everything I was looking for, we will be back.
My only gripe is that the parking cost is a little steep for guests staying the night.

name: Hotel des Arts
title: “Noisy and not so cool artwork”
text: We stayed for one night at this hotel hoping for a good night sleep before going camping at teh northern californian coast. So, first of all artwork was not too impressive, especially in our room -- simply patches with different color, what I can imagine doing in 15 minutes or so. Room was small, smelled badly. Some hair in the shower. We decided to open the window (otherwise it is sealed and there is no AC), but the internal window frame just fell inside the room. So, I was not able to close it back well enough. At this point I did not realized how bad this was. But I realized it when at around 4 am in the morning awful noise started (it was not noise actually -- It was like someone was shooting a shortgun in my ear -- they were collecting smth like 10-20 grabage urns). This guy in the truck was too lazy to leave the truck and move the bins, so he was just pushing them around with his truck. Then an hour later came another truck and brought beer casks for nearby pub. Doors were very thin too. So, it was one of the worst night at a hotel ever. Luckily, we had nice sleep at the tent next night. The breakfast is null. So, expecting smth nice (the hotel was recommended by Lonely Planet), we were very dissappointed. Maybe you will be more likely if you find a room facing not to the pub and not to the back street with garabage bin. The only positive side is location: conveniently close to Union sq etc.

name: The Wharf Inn
title: “Just what we needed”
text: This hotel is within walking distance of the wharf & Pier 39. The room we had was clean but smallish (about 12 x 14) but we really just wanted a place to sleep & shower anyway.There was a problem with the door lock BUT it was fixed immediately. There was a shower only ( no tub) but not a big deal for us. Here is the best part: FREE PARKING!! Other hotels charged as much as $40 per night as a registered guest to park at their hotel. The Wharf was just what we needed.

name: Nob Hill Motor Inn
title: “Still great after all these years”
text:
My husband and I spent a week at the Nob Hill and we had a great time. 
First of all, the location can't be beat. It's in Russian Hill and the neighborhood is full of little restaurants and shops. The 19 Polk and the 45 Union bus can take you anywhere you need to go in the city. I recommend the Muni Passport, good for 7 consecutive days of Muni travel, even cable cars!
The rooms are quiet, comfy and CLEAN. Towels are replaced daily, none of this leave it on the floor crap. Judy and Frank are still there, although I think they're getting ready to retire.
The cable is strange. No sports or news channels, but the basic network, Discovery and four (4!) PBS stations. You'll want to DVR your shows while you're away because you'll get plenty of Mandarin and Spanish stations, but no AMC, Bravo or Lifetime. 
The room is large for the area and boasts the comfort of a fridge/freezer, coffee maker and a microwave. Little pastries are in the office at around 7AM, but you might want to check out Crepe House, Bob's Donuts or Mister Donut if you want something more. 
Tai Chi, the little Chinese joint around the block is very good. As is my favorite Chinese place, Woey Loy Goey, at Grant and Jackson in Chinatown. 
I had a conference at Moscone and the 45 Union got me there in about 35 minutes. MUCH better than staying south of Market, at least in Russian Hill, you've got a neighborhood to explore. The big hotels downtown are a bit too much for me!

name: Hotel Bijou
title: “Buona opportunità di soggiorno”
text: il personale è veramente affabile e pronto a suggerimenti per il soggiorno (ristoranti, itinerari, transfer per aeroporto, etc) l'accoglienza è molto familiare, si vede la passione nel lavoro che fanno. le camere sono molto carine ed abbastanza ampie. ho dimenticato una cosa durante il mio soggiorno e sono stati di grande aiuto per recuperarla unico problema al momento è che ci sono degli importanti lavori di manutenzione nell'edificio adiacente e quindi alcune camere sono rumorose

name: The Grant Hotel
title: “Can't beat the location”
text: As some have already said, this hotel is what it is. We arrived on a Friday night in SF with nowhere to stay, and this was the cheapest place we found close to downtown. It's clean enough and the man on the desk when we checked in was lovely. Be warned if parking your car in the valet car park opposite though - you have to wait in line for ages to collect your car! my husband queued for an hour before we could get ours back! (though the parking is good value). The internet is free to use which is good, and all in all we had no complaints. Oh, this makes me sound like a crazy pedant, but I wish they had real milk for coffee at breakfast, not powdered milk which is disgusting!

name: Hotel Frank
title: “Nur zu empfehlen!”
text:
Mein absolutes Lieblingshotel!
Service war sehr gut, freundliches Personal zu jeder Tages- und Nachtzeit, geräumige Zimmer im 50s Stil - unvergleichlich. 
Zimmer waren sehr sauber und die Betten bequem. 
Sehr zentrale Lage des Hotels, nur wenige Minuten von Sehenswürdigkeiten und Shoppingcentern. 
Informationsstand im Hotel, an welchem man Ausflüge nach Alcatraz, Busreisen auf die Peak Twins, Muir Woods (mit den ältesten Bäumen der Welt), Exploratorium und viele andere Sachen vergünstigt buchen kann.
Restaurant im Hotel auch gut. 
Jederzeit wieder!

name: Hilton San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great hotel and great location”
text: Great location. About a 5-10 minute walk from the piers to see Alcatraz and the sea lions. Great location to catch the trolly into downtown as well. Great service, clean, and good continental breakfast buffet.

name: Hotel Bijou
title: “hotel bien situé”
text: Hotel très bien situé. Proche du cable car et des restos. Avons réservé 2 chambres doubles. Une très grande et une toute petite. Très propre, staff accueillant et sympa. Salle un peu petite pour le petit déjeuner et il n'y a pas de jus de fruits!!!

name: Nob Hill Motor Inn
title: “the parking garage is never safe!”
text:
There is a parking garage next to the office. But never safe! They just sleep like us during the night. My car's front window was broken the next morning right after check-in. My GPS and camera that were kept in the box under the dash board and thus not seen from outside were stolen. I felt terrible all the way staying in SF. Anyway don't rest assured after parking your car. Their garage is open to anybody like other streets of SF. 
Without this, my family and I would have more fun....

name: Hotel Bijou
title: “Kleines Juwel”
text: Zentraler geht's nicht. Zwar liegt das etwas üble Viertel Tenderloin um die (eine) Ecke - aber auch das ist nicht wirklich "schlimm". Zur anderen Seite direkt die große Touri-Info, Cable-Car-Haltepunkt, Union Square. Das Hotel selbst ist äußerst liebevoll eingerichtet und ausgestattet, in dem kleinen Kino, in dem an jedem Abend zwei in San Francisco spielende Filme gezeigt werden, gibt es den ganzen Tag über Kaffee und Tee, die Zimmer sind klein, aber hübsch und sauber. Wenn man eines nach hinten hat, ist es auch, abgesehen von dem recht lauten Fahrstuhl, angenehm ruhig (dafür etwas dunkel). Frühstück ist natürlich das, was Amerikaner unter "continental" verstehen - und wenn man schon einige Zeit im Land unterwegs war, hängen einem die süßen Teilchen zum Hals raus. Das Personal haben wir als sehr nett und hilfsbereit erlebt.

name: Hotel Frank
title: “Nella media, ma non conforme alle foto del sito”
text:
siamo stati in questo hotel 3 notti a giugno 2011, le camere sono buie, piccole e il bagno è veramente minuscolo. i camerieri che abbiamo trovato non sono stati affatto gentili. In compenso la zona (a 200 metri da Union Square) è molto comoda sia per i tanti negozi che per prendere i mezzi pubblici, soprattutto il famoso "cable", da non perdere.
La città di San Francisco è fantastica!!!!!!

name: Days Inn San Francisco Downtown/Civic Center Area
title: “GREAT VALUE FOR THE PRICE”
text: The king size bed suite was very spacious and comfortable. Amenities was satisfactory, especially the jacuzzi after a tiring day. Service was very good and breakfast hit the right spot. Would definitely recommend to anyone having business in the area.

name: Warwick San Francisco Hotel
title: “Wonderful experience right in the heart of things”
text: Stayed for 8 days with family for a wedding and extended trip. We could not have been more pleased with the Warwick. Staff is fantastic and the restaurant is a great place to start the day with very reasonable breakfasts perfectly done every time. Stopped into the Fairmont and a few big names around Union Square, and am thankful we avoided all that hectic, over-priced glitz for the warmth and charm of the Warwick. Can't beat the location, either.

name: The Carriage Inn
title: “Quirky”
text:
This hotel had a lot of quirky charm which sealed the deal for me when searching for a place to stay. When I arrived I was surprised it was also next to the Good & Americania hotels.
Our flight arrived late and the night receptionist checked us in with little fuss. We had 'Big Bertha' room 309 with a bay window that over looks The Good hotel. We had a WiFi pass for all 3 hotels as it was part of the same group. One day it was actually faster when connected to the neighboring hotel.
First impressions were very good. The refurbished rooms was to a high standard, large in size and had great charm. Type writer with a explanation of Big Bertha and also a picture of her by the bathroom was a nice tough.The bathroom fittings were a bit old but it was clean which is most important! The room had twin beds but they were large enough to sleep two adults if needed. The only complaint was the large headboards were a little loose and it kept knocking the wall when moving in bed, wasn't sure if the neighboring room could hear it. But within 10mins in the room around midnight when we arrived we had the room below thumping their ceiling to tell us to keep quiet! I admit my friend was a little heavy footed, but he was bare foot at the time... Rest of the night we were conscious of noise and had no further problems.
In the morning when we left for the day we noticed there was a room by the lift with coffee. At time of check in we were not told about complementary light breakfast and we already made plans to eat else where.
The hotel itself is easy to locate and we arrives from SFO airport on the BART, from the Civic Center station it is just 5-10 min walk along the main road. General location is good we walked all over on the next morning to St Mary's Cathedral, Nob Hill, Lombard Street, Fishermans Wharf, China Town then back into the central area of Union Square!
We took a short cab ride to the Castro for drinks and then ended up in SoMa area for BeatBox for a dance. Initially I was a bit concerned to walk back down Folsom Street, there were many smaller side streets but we stuck to the main road and walked 15mins back to the hotel without any trouble. Day or night there were a lot of homeless people but a general smile and walk by they leave you alone.
This was the 3rd hotel for our world trip and we had fun staying here. We did not use the gym or the parking facilities but they are available.

name: Nob Hill Motor Inn
title: “Great choice”
text:
Would recommend this hotel for a short stay in SF. The couple at the front desk were very friendly and helpful. They gave us some great detailed information about the city. The man doodles all over a map regarding areas to visit (and to avoid!). We found this very helpful. Booked a room that in fact had 1 large room for me and my husband with a connecting room within the same appartment for my twin boys aged 17. They loved this hotel!
Include free parking which is a novelty in this city
Some good eateries just round the corner....fabulous Chinese 'Tai Chi' - really authentic and cheap and 'Pokers' great burgers!

name: The Carriage Inn
title: “Huge room!”
text: The room is huge and nicely decorated. The bed was very comfy. The rooms all had a name of a famous person from San Francisco. On the table inside, an old fashioned typewriter had a typed paper all about that person. There was a confusion on if and where we get a complimentary breakfast. Apparently, you only get one if you bought a certain package? Most of the staff were helpful and friendly, except the woman who checked us in was like a robot. The registration room was very small.

name: The Wharf Inn
title: “Clean, Dated Motel in Great Location”
text:
Stayed in the Wharf Inn overnight after flying into San Francisco and carrying onto Yosemite.
Main reason for booking here was the free parking for guests, a rarity in San Francsico!
Room was basic, clean and adequate but in serious need of a makeover. Very dated and 'old smell'. 
However for our needs it was ideal, an overnight stay, free parking, excellent location to wharf and reasonably priced. If looking for a little luxury, I would look elsewhere

name: Nob Hill Motor Inn
title: “No Problems”
text:
We had a room with 2 queen beds, which was enough for my partner and myself, and a friend in the other bed. We had a small fridge (not tiny, sort of waist height) and microwave, and coffee-making facilities. A kettle would have been useful though!
It was quiet enough, although yes, you can hear people in other rooms if they are loud enough.
Sadly one major piece of 'dirt' (for want of a better word...) was on the toilet seat when we arrived, which was quite disgusting, but other than that the place was clean and the room was cleaned daily (apart from one day when I was feeling ill and asked them not to).
Yes the place could do with a refurb but everything worked as it should and overall we had no complaints.
The staff were nice and really helpful - they recommended places to visit, places to eat and places to avoid (eg unsafe areas). Thanks too to the Indian man on the front desk who recommended sunset in Santa Monica (where we went after SF), it really made for a memorable part of our trip.

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Everything that I thought it would be!”
text:
Lobby and main area is amazing. Historically interesting and regal. Lots of business people and meetings, which I did not care for, but overall the experience was quite wonderful. I do not doubt that this had something to do with the room that they just automatically upgraded me to (the luxe king, corner room....always ask for a corner room...they are always bigger....)
My room was amazingly huge, and the closet alone was massive...The bathroom was on the small side...Room service was quicker than any that I recall and delicious. The "Clock Bar" has wonderful drinks and very attractive and friendly bartenders! Love the shops inside the hotel...Love the overall opulence of the place...Incredible location...can't be beat...One of my favorite hotels in the city, and I like several actually....This one is not to be missed when you feel like spoiling yourself...Be sure to get a big room, as I sense that some might be on the small side...(similiar to a Fairmont hotel in that way...)

name: Hilton San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Hotel in great location”
text: We stayed here on June 3-6. It is just two blocks from the warf but only a block from bus, trolley car and just a few blocks from end of cable cars. Hotel was fine but rooms did not have lots of light - window was smaller and overlooked a courtyard so you didnt feel you could see the city sites from the room. Staff was very helpful and were able to give us directions to use the numerous public transportation sources available.

name: Hotel Fusion
title: “Location's great”
text:
The location of this hotel is so central to so many things that we wanted to explore. But do plan ahead for things. 
If you plan on having a car nearby, you have to have them park it and then call ahead to have them valet it to you. That got a little pricey and took a little of the spontaneity out of just hopping in the car to go anywhere. Sometimes to obtain the car it would take nearly 15 minutes to have them delivered to you. Lord knows where they had to park it, but it was secured. Fortunately the staff was always pretty friendly and were willing to help out to the best of their abilities. 
The rooms were clean and tidy but we thought oddly arranged. Our room didn't have the traditional foyer, hallway, bedroom and bath situation- instead it had more of a seating area complete with a plush pillow filled chaise lounge and a large bedroom on the other side of the wall. While quirky it was still comfortable. The bathroom was spacious and super tidy.
If you plan on doing any sort of business there be forewarned. They do list free internet but the wireless signal is spotty at best. That very well could be because of the city density and not the hotel's fault though. The wireless signal was slow and sometimes non-existent in the hotel room but I also noticed when I was out on the street, I couldn't get a AT&T cell phone signal either.
Beyond the parking and wireless issues, the room was comfortable and an ideal place to start your exploration of this fun city. Great food all well within walking distance and amenities galore. It's not ideal for the romantic getaway nor would I recommend it for business travelers who need immediate internet access, but for a quick getaway where one plans on spending more time exploring, dining and enjoying themselves on the town (and SF is great for that!), this place is a top notch bargain.

name: Nob Hill Motor Inn
title: “Dreary Frisco weather, but fun time anyway”
text:
We picked this motel, because the Tripadvisor ratings were very high and the price was reasonable, especially the free parking. When we arrived, I was a bit disappointed as I'm used to staying in nicer hotels, and I was worried the noise would bother me, but once we were settled in, it was a very nice experience. The owners were extremely helpful and nice to offer directions, etc. 
They also let friends visiting park in the lot for free which was great. The room was fine, very clean, with a nice little kitchen area incl a fridge and microwave. My only complaint would be the walls and ceiling are thin, so if you are on the first floor, you can hear people walking around above. Might want to ask for a second floor room. Otherwise, it's a nicer motel in a beautiful and fun city with lots to see and visit in walking distance.

name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
title: “Some helpful hints (I hope...)”
text:
Based on previous reviews, it just so happens my experience allows me to give you some tips. I will write this review accordingly.
Location: You are about 5 blocks away from anything a tourist would want. But, once you walk those 5 blocks you are at the edge of the tourist areas, market st, etc. so you'll have to keep on walking after that. The area directly around the hotel is not pretty but it didn't feel unsafe. Know that the first few minutes walk after you get out of the hotel there is basically nothing. The Montgomery BART/MUNI station is about a 10 minute walk, Montgomery St. is behind the hotel and it's a much nicer atmosphere to walk through. Having been to SF many times, the only reason I stayed at this location was the confluence of 3 conventions that weekend making hotels unavailable and expensive, I got this place Priceline cheap.
The lobby is nice and I also experienced the disorganized check in process others have written about. After getting to my room, I was not happy with it and the guest service line went unanswered for 10 minutes, so I went downstairs and cut a very long line as I had already waited on one to check in.
The odd # rooms all face the bay while the even # ones face the Union Square area of SF. I was first given an -01 room which had beautiful bay windows with an expansive view of the water. It was a cozy handicapped room with a spacious bathroom and a wardrobe but no closet. It is right next to the soda/ice machine and the elevators. Not all -01 rooms are handicapped but I imagine they are all the same size. I can't vouch for noise because I was only in it for 15 minutes in the morning. The only thing wrong with it was the handicapped shower head was too low for my 6'1 height and was not going any higher. I was not in the mood for kabuki showers. Note that the shower head in my next room was not much higher, if you are over 5 feet you'll be bending over/leaning back to wash your hair in this property!
I switched to a -25 room which after entering tucked into a corner of the building. The view was still of the bay but the windows much smaller. It had a closet and a large chest. The desk area in the corner was great, with shelves underneath and a TV that since it was not in an armoire was easily adjustable to be seen from anywhere in the room. The room, like the -01 room was slightly smaller than the other rooms I passed by but I think the fact that -25 is sequestered away from the room next to it makes it ideal if you like quiet. The only negative is that it's right next to the housekeeping closets so at 5pm and 9 am you hear the constant open/close of the doors as they prepare to work.
My bathroom was small but completely adequate. Bed was comfortable, rooms were very clean. I really enjoyed my cozy room but if you stay here be prepared!

name: Buena Vista Motor Inn
title: “Nice Staff”
text: I needed a taxi, stopped to ask a guy at the street, he seemed to be working at Buena Vista Motor Inn, offered me to ask for the taxi, invited me to eat some of the continental breakfast. I sat at the lobby, quiet comfortable, the clerk called for the taxi. I took time to review the pictures of the hotel, seemed nice and clean. Full of patrons eating breakfast and happy. I think It's a good choice. Free internet, free indoor parking. Indoor rooms, not as regular motor hotels where rooms are in the street with all the noise. If you have a chance go look at it. Nice staff. I am staying at the neighbor hotel. The clerk is not as nice. At the time I was at Buena Vista Motor Inn, my hotel had already pickup the breakfast, the clerk was never nice to offer me for a Taxi, they dont have maps at the lobby, Motor Hotel does. Much better place. Choose this one!

name: Days Inn San Francisco Downtown/Civic Center Area
title: “Nice location”
text:
Nice place with a quite neighborhood, lots of small restaurants and groceries including 2 Walgreens which are all within walking distance. My room was just about average but clean. Bus stop is just outside.
For the price, this hotel is really a bargain. Would definitely come back here on my next visit to San Francisco

name: Days Inn San Francisco Downtown/Civic Center Area
title: “decent place”
text:
I stayed here and had a good experience, especially considering the killer rate I got! The rooms were recently refurbished, and the staff was quite proud of this. They called me after I'd been in my room for twenty minutes to ask if everything was satisfactory. Nice. The room was clean and tastefully done, but small and standard for a hotel chain. The rooms all face a parking lot but I wasn't bothered by noise. 
I liked the location, there were many restaurants in Hayes Valley around the corner to choose from. Also walking distance to the Muni trains and BART for getting to and from the airport. I would stay here again, especially if I received the amazingly low price I got during my last visit. Sure beats the Travelodge on Market St. that I stayed at a year ago.

name: Mystic Hotel by Charlie Palmer
title: “Ubicación centrica y personal muy agradable: en especial Angel y su compañero Rodrigo.”
text:
La ubicación del hotel es extraordinario. En el centro de la cuidad. El hotel está muy bien estéticamente y las habitaciones son muy chulas.
Lo recomiendo para pasar unos días en San Francisco y visitar esta ciudad de EEUU.
Un saludo

name: CLIFT San Francisco
title: “Worst hotel experience ever!”
text:
I have stayed at a number of Shraeger properties around the world, this really was the worst. 
The lobby is quintessentially Shraeger - very dark but overall not bad. I am assuming that the dark lobby essentially masks the dirt that is everywhere else. The room I got was supposed to be a suite - really more like a larger room with a miniscule bathroom.
The room was quite simply, dirty. The room was DIRTY - there was a used condom under the bed and there was a used plaster in the toilet. The carpets were dirty and worn. One simply does not expect this sort of dirt in a supposedly good hotel.
The furniture is from IKEA. For a hotel that is supposedly selling itself on design, this looked like a poster-child for how to furnish your room from IKEA in poor taste.
The bathroom was tiny, stained and had cheap fixtures and a rusty rail. The shampoo etc in the bathroom were FUSED shut so you could not use them. Luckily we had some personal toilletries. 
The thing that irked me the most was that there was no water in room. Most good hotels have at least some complimentary water, if not water in the minibar. I have stayed very recently at the Clift and KNOW that you provide complimentary water on arrival - but this time round there was no water. There was no water in the minibar either. Had to call room service and then got CHARGED $15 for a bottle of WATER which costs $1.50 anywhere else. This was DAYLIGHT ROBBERY but as we had got to the hotel late, we were too tired. We told the front desk the next day and got a nonchalant and haughty reply from the front desk - and they claimed that they NEVER provide any complimentary water in the room and did not apologise for the fact that there was no water in the minibar - they did not even offer to take the water off the bill or at least reduce the price to what it would have been to buy it from the minibar. I think the barefaced lies and treatment after this was what irked me the most.
The residents next door came back at 2 in the morning, shouting and singing. When we called downstairs, nothing was done to stop our drunk and disorderly neighbours from being a nuisance. 
Lastly, the front desk staff I spoke to about the water was just RUDE. I know the MOndrian group is about the "cool, snobby" attitude but that does not amount to customer service. The staff are more interested in whether they have enough hair gel and in chatting to each other than serving the customer. 
I have stayed at a number of Shraeger properties and have decided finally that for the price one pays, the design does not compensate for what are essentially low quality, poorly-serviced rooms with cheap bathroom fittings, toilletries and electronics (e.g. I don't know any other chain that still has box TVs - they are all flat screen except at the Clift which seems to have a bunch of TVs from the 80s).
I never give feedback - but this stay was of SUCH low quality that I thought I would let others know. I plan to send this to journalist friends I have at Conde Nast and The Times in the UK. 
If the clientele the Clift is trying to attract are low-class drunks with no taste, then I suppose, in that context at least, they are doing a good job.

name: Mystic Hotel by Charlie Palmer
title: “Buono”
text: Posizione strategica dell'hotel, vicino a tutto. Appena arrivati la camera era un po' fredda, complice il cattivo tempo. Risolto il problema riscaldamento tutto è andato liscio. Camera confortevole e pulizia ottima. Colazione abbondante e varia anche se non ci sono pancakes che in America mi aspetterei ovunque. Ma fa niente.

name: King George Hotel
title: “Stay clear of the King George SF, they don't care about customer satisfation and will blame problems on everyone else.”
text:
Problems:
-Booked non smoking room, was given smoking room: told it was orbitz fault for offering non smoking when they only had smoking available.
-Run down old looking, cigarette burns in curtains, hot water kept coming through when cold water was running- college burned herself brushing teeth. Maintenance came and looked, said they would leave a note, followed up with front desk and still wasn't fixed when we checked out at the end of the 4 days.
-Room did not have accessible power outlets for laptops, phone chargers etc. We had to crawl under the bed to get to the one outlet (we later moved a dresser and found one behind it). 
-They claim to have free internet but it does not work and when it does it is very slow.
-Only one old slow moving elevator. The maids take it over in the morning when you need to head out so expect to wait for half an hour to get down (we were on the 9th floor so stairs weren't an option).
-After first night asked to speak with guest services manager, was given a comment card, filled out and left for him/her. Followed up twice and still never got to speak with the manger- they obviously did not care.
-We are spending our last two days in SF in the Larkspur, just a few blocks up and got a better rate, great service checking in, free fast internet, free breakfast and the rooms are new and modern.

name: King George Hotel
title: “Comfortable and conveniently located.”
text: I quite enjoyed my stay here. I was in town for a convention at the Hilton, which is literally around the corner and twice the price. Although the rooms were a bit on the small side, the beds were comfortable and my roomate and I found the hotel to be really enjoyable. Being right downtown, it was somewhat loud, but that is to be expected. Everything you need is within walking distance. The staff were great and very helpful. I would definitely stay here again!!

name: Hilton San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “It's all about the location....and the hotel was pretty awesome!!!”
text:
We stayed at the Hilton for 3 nights. Let me start off by mentioning we are Diamond VIP members, so I don't know how or if that affected our room assignment. 
We were put on the 3rd floor and our room overlooked the courtyard. It was quiet and we heard no noise. 
The bed was probably my favorite thing. It was very comfortable and I love the european pillows. The room itself was fairly a good size. 
Due to being Diamond members, we had complimentary breakfast every morning. The breakfast was very good. We ended up eating there every morning. It wasn't a hot breakfast, you could pay $10 for that, but it wasn't that much of a deal.
Now the location is the one thing you want. The Marriott is right there along with the Holiday Inn. There is a grocery store and Walgreens two blocks down from the hotel. To get to the Alcatraz cruise, you walk 4 blocks down Bay Street. To get to Fisherman's Wharf, you walk two blocks north towards the water. There's a In & Out Burger among other restaurants. If you want to go shopping in Union Square, just walk a block to Powell and get on the cable car. It ends in the heart of Union Square.
Walking is the way to go when staying in San Francisco. We had City Passes which allowed us to ride the Muni and the Cable Cars. The City pass also included admissions to a few of the must see places in San Francisco. 
Overall, I was extremely happy with this hotel. We mentioned when we booked the room that it was our anniversary and they had chocolate covered strawberries and champagne waiting for us. I could tell they had just placed them in there because the strawberries were still cold and the ice hadn't started to melt. Plus, the maid was really sweet and she would ask us if we needed maid service or if we needed towels whenever we saw her.

name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
title: “Good hotel for the money”
text: We stayed at this hotel over the Thanksgiving holiday weekend. The location was ideal as it it close to everything. The #15 bus stops 1/2 block from the hotel and the MUNI system in San Fran is so easy to use. Got this thru priceline for $85 a night. Although I requested a high floor, i only got to the 12th floor. Be prepared for SMALL rooms and TINY beds. This was my biggest disappointment. I also had NO flat panel TV in my room. But I have heard that if you book thru priceline, you don't get such a good room as if you had gone thru the hotel directly. But I saved over $115 so that was worth it for me. Definitely visit Mama's Restaurant for Breakfast, Pinocchio for Italian in North beach, Mara's for the best cannoli's and Ghirardelli square for awesome chocolate. Staff was very friendly and eager to please. Esp the concierge Eric and the bell staff. Always available to give directions on where you wanted to go. Don't forget the shopping on Market Street. Good deals at Armani Exchange and AE outfitters. Above all, have a great time. San Fran is a great walking city. So wear very comfortable shoes!!!

name: Warwick San Francisco Hotel
title: “Hotel à éviter absolument”
text:
Accueil épouvantable lors de notre arrivée à 3 (2 adultes et un enfant) alors qu'une réservation et un rappel par e-mail la veille de notre arrrivée avait été fait, il nous a été attribué une chambre double et notre enfant de 12 ans a du dormir par terre. Pas de chambre non fumeur malgré notre demande (faite 5 mois à l'avance!!!). Hotel vieillot, moquettes et tentures sales, l'hotel n'a pas du être refait depuis 30 ans. De plus, il n'y a visiblement pas suffisamment de personnel et le personnel existant est très hautain, inefficace et peu aimable. C'est honteux pour un hotel de cette catégorie et de cette chaine. Nous avons du changer d'hotel en cours de séjour. Il existe des établissements bien meilleurs à proximité pour le même prix.
A éviter absolument

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
title: “Great location and family friendly.”
text:
After reading a few reviews I was slightly concerned about what type of accommodation I'd selected for our trip to San Francisco. However, my concerns were un founded and the hotel was clean, comfortable, spacious and very well located. It's typical holiday inn style accommodation, good price and decent facilities. 
Just over the road from the hotel is a great little cafe which serves breakfast and lunch. The waffles are superb and the coffe selection sublime. I can't remember the name of the cafe, but it has a green canopy over the entrance. 
The location is great for Alcatraz, the cable cars and fishermans wharf. 
We stayed with our 2 boys (3 and 6) and they had a ball.

name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
title: “Weird, hit or miss experience”
text:
We really wanted to love this hotel: it is a gorgeous facility, renovated in a hot, happening style and in a great location but there were some real problems:
As we pulled up, we couldn't get into the valet driveway as a number of bellmen were busy playing (i.e. dancing, goofing with each other and talking), blocking the entrance. We eventually found an underground lot to park ourselves. Cost: about $50 a night. 
When we checked in and got to our room, it had not been cleaned. The bed was unmade and it looked like someone had just left -- radio on, trash in the floor, etc. We were promptly sent to another room where, as we took a quick power nap, someone else walked in (they had checked in and been assigned our room and their key let them in as we slept -- yikes!)
When my husband called to complain, the front desk person started acting like they could not hear him as he tried to explain the trouble. Then they hung up on him. Nice, eh?
Finally, we were assured that all was well. After a FABULOUS dinner in the hotel restaurant (our waiter was the best ever. He steered us to the best entrees and made sure we had dessert on the house), we collapsed in our room only to be awakened by a thunderous noise from the pipes in the bathroom at Midnight. The noise continued and after we (and others nearby) complained, we were switched to yet another room where we could still hear the noise but at least it didn't vibrate the floor of our room anymore (the staff thought there was a problem with a regulator in the pipes). By this time, it was close to 1 am and we had a morning departure ahead.
Then when we tried to check out and head to the airport in the morning, the elevators were not working. We had 3 heavy bags (couldn't carry wine on the plane due to new FAA rules so we'd packed some bottles) and were on the 27th floor. After a while, the elevators finally came back and we scrambled to make our flight.
The hotel is lovely. Two of the three rooms we were assigned had a gorgeous Bay view. Restaurant staff were great. But there are certainly some management and maintenance issues. At the end, I wished we could get the Hilton points we'd spent back.

name: The Wharf Inn
title: “Schönes Motel in Super Lage”
text: Wir waren im Mai für 4 Übernachtungen im Wharf Inn. Die Lage direkt an der Fishermans Wharf ist sehr gut. Unser Zimmer war sehr gut ausgestattet, wir hatten sehr viel Platz. (Leider ohne Mikrowelle und Kühlschrank) Service war tadellos. Unser Blick aus dem Fenster: Skyline von San Francisco!!! Parken konnten wir ohne Gebühr, Kaffee war in der Lobby immer frisch aufgebrüht. Wir konnten vieles zu Fuss erreichen. Cablecar Station ist nicht weit entfernt.

name: CLIFT San Francisco
title: “Mixed.”
text:
We just spent three days at the Clift and found the experience mixed.
 The good:
1. Location--can't be beat.
2. Front desk crew--helpful and friendly.
3. Bed and bed linens--comfy.
The OK:
1. Lobby decor
2. Doormen--friendly enough, but rarely open the door for you.
The bad:
1. Lighting--terrible in the lobby and in the rooms. Hard to even read.
2. Storage--essentially none. They use funny plastic cubes as nightstands and have no dresser available.
3. Room size. Pretty small for a good hotel. SMALL bathroom.
3. Charge for internet service.

name: Nob Hill Motor Inn
title: “Wonderful, friendly visit”
text: My husband and I, along with our three children (ages 10,7,3) recently stayed at the Nob Hill Motor Inn on Pacific Avenue. As previous reviews described, the owners were wonderfully friendly and helpful. They even loaned us a stroller after we forgot ours at home. Our room was very spacious and clean. There was little to no traffic noise, although there was noise from other rooms (TV's, etc.) But nothing to complain about. We would highly recommend this establishment in San Francisco and would stay there again on future trips.

name: Radisson Hotel Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great Location with Top-Notch Service”
text: We stayed with Radisson Fishermans Wharf, as a present from a family friend. From the moment we arrived, they took care of us. The rooms were large, spacious and clean. The room we had looked out to the San Francisco skyline. The concierge staff were extremely friendly and helpful. We could not thank them enough for the service they provided. The hotel is also right next to Fishermans Wharf, with plenty of public transportations on your doorsteps.

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “good location, tired old rooms, poor service - you can do a lot better in San Francisco”
text:
Pros: good location near Union Square and walking distance to public transportation, Starbucks in the lobby, large room
Cons: old, worn rooms with random furniture from the 80'; long waits at check-in/out, service from unfriendly to rude
wouldn't recommend to friends
I booked this hotel on a business trip and staid here for the first time, but have staid any many hotels in SF and previously lived there.
The hotel is near Union Square in easy walking distance from public transport (BART to the airport and Muni across town) as well as shopping in the heart of downtown.
The hotel is made up of three towers with lots of rooms and a large lobby with multiple entrances.
The service is worse than at any other 4/5-star hotel I've staid in SF: The lines for check in were very long, even at the HHonors check-in. The front desk was clearly understaffed, stressed out (according to the agent, they were sold out all week) and unfriendly.
My room was very large for SF with a spacious sitting area and large bathroom. Unfortunately, the furniture seemed to be a random collection of 80's area or older furniture that was very worn (ie laminate was separating from desk) and looked nothing like the picture on the web site for the room category I booked! It appears that they are going through a renovation and my room was clearly an old one. This type of bait & switch is unacceptable!
The room was otherwise clean, the TV functional, the a/c working but very loud. The bathroom amenities were standard Hilton (nice!), but glasses were missing. The windows are single pane, resulting in poor sound and temperature insulation.
Service at check-out was worse than at check-in: the line was winding through the lobby and the wait very long, again even at the HHonors line. While checking out, I provided feedback on the room and the lines (politely, starting off that it is not directed to him, but meant as feedback to be passed on to management) - and the agent actually cut me off and got loud! wow, that hasn't happened to me in 20+y of business travel in 50+ countries and hundreds of hotels! 
Even in a sold-out situation with pressure on an understaffed team, unloading your stress on a guest is certainly not acceptable behavior.
I wouldn't recommend this hotel - many hotels at similar rates offer fresh rooms with great designs and friendly, professional service in the same downtown area.

name: Marriott San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Good chain option near Fisherman's Wharf”
text: Stayed here 2 nights on a getaway. The building is ugly outside with no setback from the street, but the location is great, very close to all things Fisherman's Wharf. We even walked to the financial district and Embarcadero. Lobby is tastefully remodeled with comfortable chairs/couches. Staff were friendly and helpful at check-in and check-out. We were booked into a standard room facing the street; noise from the street was not noticeable. Room was clean enough but there was some dirt and dust in the corners. Very comfortable beds. Would return although would probably not want to pay rack rate (we had an excellent Priceline deal).

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “Great hotel, great location”
text:
I have stayed at the Adagio many times over the last few years and it offers a consistently good service at a reasonable price.
There is also a garage next door that offers half price parking compared to the hotel.

name: Buena Vista Motor Inn
title: “Buena Vista is good European 2 * hotel style!”
text: We stayed at the BV some years ago, and honestly forgot about it while getting caught up in the frenzy of trying to find a deal at a 4* SF hotel closer to the Embarcadero. Well, all was either sold out, OR wanting higher bids..when we remembered the BV! Still mostly the same, BUT now they have the continental bkfast!! OJ, coffee, croissants, muffins (sometimes), and other assorted pastries (NOT Paris quality!:) and apples/bananas! Rooms are basic, but perfectly suitable. We got a king bed, a/c, openable windows to the back (preferred, as Lombard St. is noisy and to the front) for the AAA rate of $125 +tax. We had forgotten that it was AAA and 10% disc. would apply, so the front desk guy went back in time:) and gave us the deal for both nights!! VERY helpful staff!! AND, computer access (free!) next to the breakfast area! AND, they'll let you print out your boarding pass thru their printer!! NO extra fees!! NOT luxury, but definitely NOT buggy!! IMPT. to me, having had a prob. in San Diego!!

name: Courtyard San Francisco Downtown
title: “Not terrible - not great.”
text:
Checking in was a battle of 'You need to pay, your travel agent haven't paid us'. Not the best thing when you check in, and it's 11pm UK time, on a Friday of a Bank Holiday. 
They eventually found the email, that indeed did say they had been paid, and let us check-in. 
We had the same issue at breakfast on the first two days too. 
Hotel it's self was mostly ok, the rooms felt dated, and for the price were quite basic. However all the hotels in the conference season seem to be quite expensive. 
Pretty good location for the Moscone Center, just a 5/10 minute walk.

name: SW Hotel
title: “Clean, nice room, but some noise from street”
text: The SW hotel was the last hotel in all of SF that had any rooms available during Google I/O. I stayed in a 4th floor handicapped queen room (although I am not handicapped). Bed was comfy and clean, room was spacious enough, and the hotel is close to public transportation. I'd happily stay there again. The only con was some noise from the street, which carried in even through the closed windows. However, it didn't stop me from sleeping, but if you're a very light sleeper you should probably avoid a room that overlooks the street.

name: Hotel Fusion
title: “Nice Hotel. Great Location for the Money”
text:
This Hotel was a very nice surprise. It was in a very great location for the price. Walking distance to union square where there's lots of shops and bars. Friendly and efficient staff.
The room was quite spacious! We had a standard queen room. Plenty of space to walk around and a huge closet!! The bed was firm and the bedding was comfortable. Nice bathroom and the quality of the complimentary toiletries was excellent--they smelled great.
In the room was a fridge with drinks and a small basket of snack things that you could purchase for $1-$5.
The soundproofing was excellent. We heard absolutely nothing all night long. Fortunately we were staying over on a sunday night, when the nighclub was closed so that was no issue...but we really heard nothing from the busy street.
For $130 it was really worth it

name: The Grant Hotel
title: “Falls wir wieder nach San Francisco reisen, werden wir das Hotel Grant wieder wählen”
text: Das Hotel befindet sich an einer ausgezeichneten Lage mit kurzen Wegen an alle wichtigen Punkte der Stadt. Die Hotelleitung war äusserst zuvorkommend und das Zimmer sauber und die Betten sehr gut. Da wir keine grossen Frühstückesser sind, war für uns auch das Frühstück gut. Der Kaffee war für amerikanische Verhältnisse gut. Nur die Benutzung der Parkgarage ist teuer.

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Beautiful hotel, but some problems with the cleaning service”
text: I recently stayed at the Westin St. Francis for six nights using my Starwood points. The location of this hotel is great--easy walk to Nob Hill, Chinatown and of course Union Square. I was very pleased with the room, spacious and very clean and of course, the infamous Westin Heavenly Beds. The only thing that was troubling during the stay were some items were taken from my room. I noticed one thing immediately and reported it, and was reimbursed for the item, but after the cleaning service was in the room, it magically appeared again. On the way home I remember a gift that I had purchased for my daughter was also missing. I contacted the hotel twice and got absolutely no response about this. Luckily the items were not of significant value, but I wonder if anyone else who stayed at this hotel had a similar experience. I am surprised that a hotel of this caliber would not respond to even apologize about this. I am a Starwood Preferred Guest and have never had an experience such as this in one of their hotels.

name: Hilton San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Good hotel”
text:
Solid 3 star hotel. Good size rooms (we got an executive king room,) it was clean, decent furniture, very comfortable beds and pillows. Although it could definately use new bedspreads and blankets (they were clean, but outdated and worn.) We had a handicapped room (for no reason) so the bathroom was huge. But the water pressure in the shower was pretty low.
Location was awesome, just blocks to Fisherman's Wharf. Staff was very helpful and polite, and went out of their way making recommendations for places to eat. 
I'm an Honors member, and was told by the reservationist (800 number) that if I upgraded to executive level, I would be on a separate floor (less children) and it includes breakfast. When I got there, I found out that's not the case - since they're a small hotel, they don't have an executive level. However, the manager didn't hesitate to give me access to the free breakfast to avoid a situation, which was appreciated. 
The windows are thin and you can hear the traffic somewhat, but it didn't bother us. Didn't hear neighbors, but could hear them walking around on the floor above us - but it wasn't disturbing.
Overall the hotel was very good, a solid 3 star. It was perfect for the location and price we paid. We wouldn't hesitate to stay there again. 
As a side note, the staff recommended Bobo Quivaris for dinner (not sure how to spell it,) - that had to be the best filet mignon we've ever had in our lives!! The food was OUTSTANDING, the atmosphere was wonderful - very eclectic, and overall an incredible place to dine, we highly recommend it. 
We also went to Aliotos restaurant on the Wharf (pier 43, I think.) The service was absolutely awful (among the worst I've ever had,) and the food was just ok - I wouldn't recommend it. However, we have a feeling just our waiter was bad, and not the others, but we wouldn't go there again to find out.

name: The Grant Hotel
title: “Grant Hotel nähe Union Square und Cable Cars”
text:
Die Lage ist ideal, vom Flughafen mit dem BART bis Powell Street und man sieht schon die Cable Cars.
Entweder man läuft die Powell Street selber hoch oder nimmt ein Cable Car bis Bush Street.
Empfangen wurde ich von einer asiatischen älteren Dame, die doch sehr nett war und obwohl ich früh morgens angekommen bin, habe ich sofort mein Zimmer beziehen können. Das Zimmer hat zwar ein gewisses Alter und aus dem Fenster guckt man gegen eine Wand, aber alles ist sehr sauber. Man hat einen begehbaren Schrank (für mich und die 3 Tage die ich dort war schon zu viel) mit Bügeleisen. Im Bad fand ich alles sauber vor, Handtücher wurden täglich gewechselt.Das Bett war superweich und hatte einen guten Schlaf.
Zum Frühstück gibt es nur Süßes wie Muffins, Donuts und Croissants, was für mich aber ausreichend war. Ansonsten gibt es in der Nähe genug Möglichkeiten anderweitig zu frühstücken.
Somit kann ich das Hotel nur weiterempfehlen und würde es nächstes Mal auch wieder buchen.

name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Consierge scamming tourists”
text: Beware of the concierge Mike he tried telling me that Alcatraz was sold out for months and that I would need to pay him $115 per person in CASH to go. When I asked him if this is the price for children and seniors also he said yes no discounts. I smelled a scam, so I said no thanks. I called my assistant in NY and she was able to get the tickets for all 4 of us for $219 total, this also included a cruise to Angel Island. She obtained the tickets direct from Alcatraz Cruises via the web within minutes. I showed the email to the manager, and informed her of the situation. She was surprised and would talk to him. She offered me a $50 credit on my hotel tab. I truly believe that he makes a business of scamming unsuspecting tourists, and that is deplorable. Lets talk about the room, the bathroom was so tiny you could brush your teeth while sitting on the toilet. It was completely pathetic. I have stayed in other hotels in the area which provide much larger better bathrooms. The same hair strand was on the back of the bathroom door for the 5 days that we were there in addition to a blue gel stain on the bathroom wall. Only positive was the bed was very comfortable, clean , and had nice linens. We had beautiful views from our 19th floor window, and it was very quiet.

name: Villa Florence, A JRK Hotel
title: “Charged for things not used.”
text:
I was charged for the mini bar during my stay and after I checked out. Even though I never used it. The hotel manager Eduardo refused to remove both charges. Just the charge after the checkout date.
The hotel was fine, but the additional charges soured the experience. Being an independent hotel instead of a chain there wasn't much escalation possible. I really would have rather have written a more solid review, but the billing issue was real problem for me. Don't expect much customer support after checkout. It took two weeks to get to the point I finally reached.

name: Hotel Fusion
title: “Good Hotel, GREAT Location”
text:
Stay here for 3 Nights in Mid June.
Location is Excellent and is just 5mins walk from both Union Square and also the BART Station which makes it dead handy if your flying into SFO.
Room are small as mentioned but they are big enough for a short stop over and yes walls are thin, but personally didn't find it a problem.
Reception Staff 1st Class and spent ages working out directions for our route to our next destination

name: Marriott San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Pleasant experience, well located”
text: I was pleasantly surprised by this hotel. It was clean, quiet, nicely decorated. The location is hard to beat; near Fisherman's Wharf, North Beach, and Lombard Street (crooked street).

name: Nob Hill Motor Inn
title: “Wonderful place to stay!”
text: We were two women (older) traveling alone. We can not say enough good things about this hotel. It was very clean, safe area, easy access to public transportation, the staff was wonderful. We were there 9-29-04 to 10-4-04.

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “5 star hotel mm i think not !!!”
text: recently returned from staying 3 nights at this so called 5 star hotel. £150 a night the last few days of a month holiday in america. out side first impression what a grand hotel. walk in side impression very disappointing. greated by smart dressed reception staff , checked in very quick ,then handed notice that water supply was off till 3pm its only 11am ,and after a long flight needed a shower. no joy :( bar area closed restaurant closed. due to refurnishment. work men putting up screens to hide whats going on. !!! was told if we wanted breakfast or eveving meals snacks they could do room service. well im not stuipid and everyone knows room service prices are higher in price !! not offered a discount due to the work. so off to the lift with my baggage 1 lift ? the others cut off in the building area . all guest and staff using one lift so over my 3 days waiting time to get up and down took a average of 10 mins. so i get to my room and think mmm nice cup of coffee . guest what !! no kettle or coffee machine , room service $11 for a pot of coffee ur joking no!!!! there a fridge full of little bottle of spirts and mixers yes over the top prices 5 star hotel rates. then some biscuits crisps all to pay for. a snickers bar $3 thats about £2 for a chocolate bar. def 5 star ratings. bathroom small nice decor 1 bath robe for 3 people to share. room nice to big queen sized beds very comfy. flat screen tv . no wardrobe but hanging space with curtain over it not 5 star. the other hotels i stayed in was days inn id rate this hotel the same standard but you do get a complmentray breakfast at days inn here its $16 for a couple of buns and toast and cofee . lucky we found a nice dinner opposite the hotel . good food good service value for money. french toast to die for.and just up the road is a chinese restaurant that serves american cooked food. basic place but clean good food and plenty of it. recomened both dinners. the hotel offers free tea and coffee in the morning ! in paper cups not really 5 stars !!! i cant believe that the travel agent i booked this with in the uk rated this hotel 5 stars but i did find out that the hotel basically had not told any of the companys booking with them about there on going refurnishment. so i will be complaining to them now ive arrived home. mr adagio manger !! if your running a 5 star hotel run one please not a building site. very disapointed !!!!

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
title: “Superb location, super comfortable beds”
text: We arrived at the hotel at about 1030am after an overnight flight. We were able to check in straight away which was amazing. We were transferred by van to the other part of the hotel as it was raining but in hindsight we probably could have just walked but brain capacity wasn't too flash. The room was very clean, not huge but ok but the beds were very comfortable. After a bit of a nap we got up to explore. What a fabulous location. A short walk to fishermans wharf where there was something going on all the time. We were tossing up between staying near union square or here and we were so pleased we stayed here simply because of the location. We didn't use any of the hotel facilities other than the free wifi (which is a godsend) but we found it to be a perfect base. Staff were friendly and helpful, rooms cleaned, and beds great. No bar fridge (for those Aussie travelers), get used to collecting ice in a bucket!

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Old section getting a bit long in the tooth”
text:
I travel to San Francisco at least once every year and have been staying in Starwood hotels since I joined their club about five years ago. I have bounced between the W, St. Regis & St. Francis. 
What I do like about the St. Francis is the old section overlooking Union Square because the ceilings are high and the rooms have that sense of old San Francisco that I remember as a child staying there with my family. However, the best part is that the windows open wide letting in the cool S.F. air and the sounds of the city complete with the clanging cable cars traveling up and down Powell St. A view over Union Square to Tiffanys, Macys & Nieman is so cIt y. It really doesn't get much better than that for a city experience. If you can time it right be sure to book a lower Union Square room to watch the Chinese New Year parade from your window.
What I don't like about the St. Francis is that the new gourmet retaurant that has taken over what was one of the most wonderful hotel bars in the city. Nothing against the restaurant itself as I have yet to dine there. Cocktails are now relegated to the lobby which diminishes what was once a Grand entrance. Now the lobby is kept impossibly dim littered with too warn, never were attractive furnishings.
All in all, I will probably opt sometime again in the future for the Union Square experience; but I do miss the bathrooms at the St. Regis.

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
title: “Great location”
text:
This hotel is in a great location. We were sent to the Beach St. building which is about 2 blocks away from all the restraints and very close to the piers. Also 1 block away was the major bus stops to take us to the piers further away. We did not want to rent a car because we heard about the price of parking and was very happy we didn't rent a car because everything was in walking distance.
The hotel was kind enough to hold our luggage (since we arrived super early for check in), early check in, changed our room to a king size bed (because I accidental ordered 2 double beds), and late check out for no additional fee. 
The room was a good size, compared to other hotels we've been to it is kind of out dated in style, but who cares. The sheets were clean, no bed bugs, plenty of towels and a working A/C, Heater. The bed was also very comfy and we had a flat screen TV with free HBO. As for the noise level being so close to fishermen's wharf. Had no problem sleeping and didn't hear any noise from the outside. Our room was by an exit so we did hear the exit door slam but it didn't really bother me nor my husband.
My one and only complaint would be the 1 rude bell boy, I wish I had his name so I can put him on blast but he was very rude and we were happy we only saw him our first day and never saw him again. The older bell men are very kind and helpful (just the bell boy with long braided hair is very rude and has a very bad attitude). 
Overall:
Hotel is in a great location and is clean and has very helpful and kind staff (minus the 1 rude bell boy).

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “Great hotel, great loation”
text:
We just stayed at this hotel (7/12). The remodeling is almost done and we were not bothered by it. Our room had a great size, nice furniture and comfortable beds. The staff was very nice. The location is very convenient. It's about 5 blocks away from the Powell St Bart Station, and about 8 blocks from Chinatown. The Hyde/Powell Cable Car is about 3 blocks away. The breakfast place across the street is pretty good with a nice, extensive menu and fair prices.
Regarding comments about the homeless in the area. That is a problem in Union Square. You will find also many homeless in the Haight/Ashbury area. There were many but they leave you alone.

name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
title: “Great Location”
text: Visited here with family April 2003. Staying on 24th Floor views over city were brilliant. Located on edge of China Town and within walking distance of Pier 39, and other sites. Very comfortable and clean even though under going a refurbishment at the time of visit.

name: Hotel Fusion
title: “fantastic location-definite stay!!”
text:
Hotel fusion is a trendy hotel that's a bit on the small side but the location makes up for it. I went with my boyfriend but if I ever go back for a girls trip, I would feel safe staying here again. There a numerous restaurants just outside and loads of shopping (FCUK and H&M are all stone throws away). 
The only complaints are that the walls are thin and the room smelled a bit musty. These in my books are minor issues.

name: Nob Hill Motor Inn
title: “Great value”
text: This hotel is great for its value. (Parking is free!) It is in a safe area. The room is clean, service is great. It is close to all public transportion. The owners are extremely friendly and helpful. They told us where to go and where not to go and also recommended a few very nice restaurants. The only problem we have was the noisy footsteps we heard from the people upstairs.

name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Charming but can be noisy”
text: Overall, the hotel was fresh, clean and charming. The staff were exceptionally nice and friendly. I made several special requests (such as asking to order off the restaurant menu for room service) and was promptly and politely accommodated. The decor was charming and the room quite comfortable, with the exception of the bathroom being on the small size, with very limited counter space and no make-up mirror (very nice to have when you're a woman). I found the walls rather thin and could hear way too much of my neighbors, unfortunately. The restaurant downstairs, Scala's Bistro, was quite tasty.
