If you join Kimpton's free InTouch frequent visitor program, you will receive free wi-fi at all of their hotels -- a nice savings if you're traveling on business.

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “Great staff!!!”
text: Really enjoyed our stay here. Staff really friendly and helpful, especially front desk. Superb atmosphere to the hotel. Good room but with only an ok view. Food was great but hotel loses a mark for having poor vegetarian range.

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Can't Go Wrong Here”
text:
We enjoy visiting the city of San Francisco as much as any other and the Westin St. Francis, one of the city's grand dames, is a perfect fit.
For such a huge property with so many guests, the hotel handles its affairs quite smoothly. Check in is easy, special requests are honored quickly, housekeeping is efficient, supervisors are present to assist, and the concierge desk is generally able to attend to the needs of patrons. Even a hotel operator, who could not locate the concierge for us one evening by telephone, offered to assist us and took the time to contact a restaurant for a reservation.
The lobby is done up nicely with marble floors, sitting areas, and a small shopping arcade. The room we were given was on the 10th floor in the old building, and was a model of beauty with wood molding, blue and gold colors, matching carpet, elegant window treatments, and the so-called heavenly beds and linens (which lived up to their names). The room was fairly quiet though some noise filtered in occasionally. The bathroom was relatively basic. 
We relished the location on--not near--Union Square. It is so close to everything, be it public transportation, restaurants, diners, shopping, sightseeing, theaters, bars, clubs, China town, Market Street, BART, the financial district, Union Square itself (which was hosting a free concert) that we felt we were in the center of all the action. 
Rooms rates are variable so it pays to check around and compare.
All in all, we were quite pleased with this property.

name: King George Hotel
title: “Perfect location in San Francisco”
text: Staying at the King George gives you an absolutely brilliant location for a reasonable price. Rooms are small, elevator likewise. There's a bar on the ground floor, and great concierge service. The hotel is one block from Union Square, Macy's, cable car, Westfield shopping centre (with movie theatres) and there are lots of restaurants and bars in the neighborhood. Recommended!

name: Club Quarters San Francisco
title: “Great Location”
text: Ideal for a business traveler. Has the right amenities for a business trip and it is well priced for all other types of trips.

name: Nob Hill Motor Inn
title: “Le meilleur emplacement pour un prix correct”
text:
Les atouts majeurs de cet établissement sont sa situation géographique et les services proposés pour un prix somme tout correct pour San Francisco.
De surcroît, cet hôtel propose des chambres pour cinq personnes.
Situé en contrebas de Nob Hill et proche de nombreux restaurants, il ne faut pas plus de 20 minutes pour se rendre à pied à Fisherman's Wharf ou à Chinatown et une demi-heure de marche pour atteindre Downtown (centre ville) et Square Union (à prendre en compte que les rues de San Francisco sont en pente très forte).
L'hôtel en lui-même reste assez moyen, mais le prix comprend :
- le petit-déjeuner à prendre en chambre mais proposant d'excellentes pâtisseries,
- le parking gratuit mais aux places limitées,
- internet en Wi-fi mais au débit limité,
- un clic-clac pour une personne (dans notre cas).
Le responsable de cet établissement est "bougon" mais vous présentera avec de nombreux détails les quartiers à visiter et les quartiers à éviter.
Les chambres sont suffisamment grandes mais un peu veillote. Les chambres ne sont pas insonorisées et la climatisation réversible assez bruyante.
Le ménage est correct sans plus (une de nos poubelles est restée pleine durant notre séjour de quatre jours, mais c'est certainement un oubli).
Réfrigérateur, micro-ondes, cafetière font partie de l'équipement de la chambre.
La literie tout en étant correcte n'est pas le mieux en la matière.
Il est enfin à préciser qu'il n'y ni piscine ni spa.

name: CLIFT San Francisco
title: “Clift: Great Bar and Ground Floor, But Improve Service Focus!”
text:
This is a funky Boutique Hotel aimed at a younger (or young at heart) audience which appreciates the contemporary vibe. I am a frequent traveller and have stayed in St. Martin's Lane, the sister hotel in London.
I was really excited about my stay at the Clift, and got a deal via travelzoo, booking on the hotel website for $244/night. Regular rooms were as low as $175 including breakfast.
GOOD POINTS
Great location two minutes walk from Union Square, and very helpful Concierge. Lovely reception area decor. Superb Redwoom Room bar. 
In my room sheets were superb quality, air conditioning worked brillianty and housekeeping was efficient (if noisy in the morning). Spacious deluxe room (333) had two beds and plenty of bathroom space, albeit a 1970s low-style flat backed tub.
LESS GOOD POINTS
FIRST Check in experience was poor; new trainee was trying very hard and was professional, but should have had closer more dedicated supervision from his manager, and she was not able to dedicate enough time to supporting him, this meant he was made to look incompetent, which must have been unsettling to him and not ideal for me the customer either (it took nearly ten minutes to check me in on a simple reservation).
He told us our room category was overbooked, and we were being upgraded to a larger room on a high floor. Yippee we thought. Then I noticed we were being checked into a standard room; when I brought this to his attention we were found the paid for Deluxe Room, but on the very low third floor.
SECOND, the mattress support slats under the bed in my room had fallen out meaning the mattress was unsupported and uneven; I understand these things happen and when I raised it with the front desk when I realised the next morning after a poor night's sleep it was dealt with BUT the response was simply "we'll deal with it" rather than demonstrating concern that I may have had an uncomfortable night's sleep. 
I must stress I was NOT looking for any compensation here. But more of an apology/concern should have been demonstrated by the front desk person at a five star hotel. Maybe this is a cultural thing, but "sorry" goes a long way.
This was a minor insignificant issue for me, but other may not have had the energy to check what the problem with the bed was (the mattress was heavy to lift up!) and a verbal apology should accompany any complaint.
THIRD Housekeeping started asking if rooms were free at 0830am by knocking and announcing "housekeeping" loudly - surely a more efficient system could be established to avoid waking your many international guests who are on a different tmie zone, and a clearer encouragement to guests to use the Privacy Please door guards to avoid this unwanted noise?
FOURTH noise from the street. This is an urban location, and frankly those who complain need to get over it. By the time the traffic gets going you should be out there enjoying the sights!
FINALLY, my rate booked on the Morgans site included breakfast but this was not noted in my reservation and I only received this paid for benefit by having the foresight to print out the reservation at the time of booking and was made to present this to the front
desk. 
Your reservation system needs to ensure all special offer benefits are noted in detail in the reservation. Same thing happened when I stayed in St Martins Lane so this is a systemic problem.
I stay about 50 hotel nights a year for business and pleasure, and had a superb stay at St Martin's Lane earlier in the year, but my experience at the Clift was mixed, which was a disappointment, and most of these problems noted above are "soft" people skill or process change issues which should easily be fixed with management attention.
I tried submitting this via the email link I was sent after my stay, but once I had filled out all the data, the site crashed when I submitted it - a great idea but again you need to follow up on the detail.
I expect high standards from such a five star hotel, and my review is therefore somewhat picky, but I hope fair given the prices some people pay for rooms here.
VERDICT: What would have been an awesome stay was made less so by poor management of trainees, a lack of empathy from the front desk, noisy housekeeping and problems with ensuring guest entitlements are captured when making the reservation online.

name: Park Hotel
title: “Excellent location and friendly staff.”
text: My husband and I are checking out today sadly! We have loved San Francisco and this hotel is a little gem! You walk out turn left and there's a Starbucks on the corner, go round that corner and straight in front of you is union square. You cant complain, the hotel is cheap, clean and in the perfect location! I would definitely stay here again.

name: Andrews Hotel
title: “Good value for money in SF”
text:
The Andrews is just two blocks from Union Square (uphill, though), so location is not a problem. Haven't had issues with the size of the room (a bit small sized, but not tiny). Staff was ok but not particularly friendly. Breakfast included is also a plus, even though lacks variety.
Lack of A/C wasn't a problem as well. Room was very clean, no complaints about that. Only problem we had was related to street noise at night.
I'd surely be back if on a budget.

name: Radisson Hotel Fisherman's Wharf
title: “A little pricey”
text: Stayed at the Raddison by the bay in San Fran the first week of Oct/2012. Average stay is 350/day.The room we had did not have a fridge, which was a dissapointment,the washroom was clean and modern.. They offer a continental breakfast daily but it is extra. The best thing about the hotel is that it is close to most of the must see things, oh i almost forgot,parking at the hotel is 42 dollars a day ouch. MFK

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Great location and lovely room”
text:
We checked in around noon and was given a room key immediately. The ride on the elevator and the hallway to our room was a bit worrisome as it was definitively old. However, as soon as we opened the door, our concerns was washed away. Our king bed room was larger than the usual San Francisco hotel's room with a great view right out to the busy Union Square. Aside from the usual bed and tables we also have a lounge reading chair. The Heavenly Bed is my favorite hotel bed, just enough layers to make me snooze right away.
The bathroom was large and comfortable fitting 2 persons easily. The usual Heavenly bath products are well stocked and presented nicely.
The location of this hotel is superb. It is also great if you want to catch a cable car as the stop in front of the St-Francis almost always have spaces (The cable car always left the Union Square station with a few empty seats so they can pick up other passengers along the way). We had a good time in this place considering the price that we paid for.

name: Nob Hill Motor Inn
title: “excellent, pas assez connu”
text: une tres bonne surprise, j'avais une crainte par rapport au motel mais c'etait parfait, bonne situation, le patron nous a offert le petit dejeuner et les transports en commun pour les 3 jours et 2 nuits ou nous avons dormis là, chambre spacieuse et salle de bain complete, propre et tres aimable, felicitation, un grand merci au proprio

name: Andrews Hotel
title: “A real find in the heart of the Theater District”
text:
We recently stayed at the Andrews while moving our daughter out of her dorm at The Academy of Art University for winter break. While our primary reason for choosing it was its proximity to her dorm, we ended up being very, very happy with our choice.
The thing that struck me from the beginning (even before we got to the hotel!) was how very friendly and helpful the staff is! I had to call a couple of times with questions before we drove up to the city, and each time the person I spoke to was cheerful and able to answer all my questions. This trend continued during our stay...from check-in, through many trips past the front desk with our daughter's things, right through check-out, we got the impression that the people who work there like their jobs, like their hotel, and like their customers.
Our room (a "comfy queen" on the third floor) was very pleasant. Everything looked and smelled very clean and in good repair. The bed truly was very comfortable, the writing desk was actually situated near electrical outlets (not something I've come to expect in hotels, more's the pity) so we could plug in our laptops, the closet was generously sized (the better to store a semester's worth of stuff!). It wasn't a huge room, but it wasn't tiny either...there would have easily been room for a roll-away, had we needed one. We really appreciated the window that actually OPENED, as well as the ceiling fan, as it was an unusually stuffy evening for San Francisco for December! It was also surprisingly quiet. I used to live on Post St., so I knew about the fire station, and was actually surprised at how well the street noises were muffled when we closed the window at bedtime.
Our room came equipped with an iron and ironing board, a hair dryer, a radio, and a very nice flat-screen TV that got a good selection of channels. The free wi-fi worked very well (they have a server for each floor).
I also loved the shower, by the way, which put out GREAT water pressure, and was easy to adjust for temperature.
For those who might be unfamiliar with San Francisco, I just have to add that one of the best things about The Andrews is its location. Some of the reviews have expressed reservations about the neighborhood, but I've lived there and my daughter lives there, and I can tell you that it's a very safe part of town, even late at night. It's urban, sure, and if you're used to suburbia it may seem a little gritty, but it's really a great place to be if you really want to experience the city. The Andrews is only two blocks from world-class shopping at Union Square, Maiden Lane, and the Crocker Galleria. It's surrounded by the city's best theaters, and some of its best dining (Everything from hot dog carts to five-star gourmet! Not to mention some outstanding ethnic eateries...particularly Thai and Indonesian). It's an easy walk to Chinatown, to the Powell & Mason and Powell & Hyde cable car lines, to Powell Street MUNI/BART station, to the Museum of Modern Art, the Jewish Museum and Yerba Buena Gardens. You're also perfectly situated to get public transit to just about anywhere you'd like to go in the city (you don't REALLY plan to drive in San Francisco, do you?). As locations go, it just doesn't get much better.
There were only two things that kept me from giving The Andrews an "excellent" rating, and they're pretty minor:
1) The door between our bathroom and our bedroom had a frosted glass panel in it that allowed bathroom light to shine into the bedroom. Normally that wouldn't be a huge problem (just don't turn on the bathroom light if you need to use it when your companion is still asleep), but, as in many downtown buildings, our bathroom also had a window that opened onto an air shaft shared by another bathroom. Unfortunately, the occupant of THAT room chose to leave the bathroom light on all night, and that made our bedroom pretty bright. It wouldn't keep me from staying there again (in fact, I plan to when we have to move our daughter out again at the end of spring semester), but I will definitely bring something to cover that glass panel! Perhaps the hotel might consider installing some kind of shade....
2) The other less-than-perfect thing was breakfast. It's very nice having it served in the hallway outside your room, but not so nice when some greedy person on your floor grabs all the pastries and rolls as soon as the breakfast is set out, so that when you get out there at 7:15 a.m. there's nothing left but fruit. That's not the hotel's fault, but they might want to consider having an employee check the breakfast stations periodically during the morning and replenish things.
Those two things aside, I wholeheartedly recommend this hotel, and would (actually will) happily stay there again.

name: Courtyard San Francisco Downtown
title: “Great downtown location, and great package value”
text:
Our family of three traveled to San Francisco in mid-August for vacation. We wanted a downtown location to provide a different type of experience and the convenience of the cable cars and other tourist areas. 
We booked our hotel through Marriott's site which was the best deal. I specifically was looking for a 1 bedroom suite and the room we stayed in was fabulous. We purchased the escape romantic package as value of the complimentary valet parking each night, breakfast for two both mornings, and complimentary bottle of champagne far exceeded the normal price for the room-alone. We only paid $30 more per night for these amenities.
The room was a corner suite on the 12th floor, and was by far the largest suite we've stayed in. It had a large coach and chaise lounge, huge bar area. The dressing area between the bedroom and large bathroom as quite large as well. 
You have to use the valet to park unless you choose one of the parking lots nearby. Since it was included in our package, we obviously used it. We didn't have to wait more than 10 minutes at any time to get our car. 
The breakfast is buffet style and kids 12 and under eat free. They have quiet a variety and it was easy to get in and out of quickly. 
The bar and grill area is small. Don't be in a rush for drinks or dinner, though -- the service was quite slow. The wait staff seemed more interested in talking to each other and guests, than actually providing service. It does close down fairly early (10pm) I believe, but you can get individual beers at a very reasonable price in their small market area. The food was OK -- not much selection and we only opted for it as we got in late and didn't want to wander out. If given a choice, I wouldn't recommend it as there was not much to offer, especially for kids, and the price was a bit high. 
The lobby area was quite large as it offered nice seating area, the convenience of Starbucks, and a nice outdoor seating area. 
The location is good as it is very convenient to Hwy 101. 
All-in-all, it was a great location, very well-kept hotel, and the value was excellent.

name: King George Hotel
title: “Gutes Hotel in TOP Lage!”
text:
Die Mitarbeiter an der Rezeption haben uns äußerst freundlich empfangen. Diese Freundlichkeit haben wir während des gesamten Aufenthaltes von allen anderen Mitarbeitern auch erfahren dürfen. Und bei Fragen zu Sehenswürdigkeiten, Einkaufen oder Essen wurde uns stets super geholfen!
Die Zimmer sind total gemütlich eingeräumt. Betten, Schränke und das andere Mobiliar sind 'auf alt' gemacht, aber sehr gepflegt. Das Bad ist sehr sauber, und täglich wurden die kleinen Bad-Artikel des Hauses kostenfrei wieder aufgefüllt.
Zur Lage: das Hotel liegt nur ein paar Minuten zu Fuß von der Cable Car 'Powell-Street' entfernt und ist somit super zentral. Auch Einkaufsmöglichkeiten sind ausreichend vorhanden!!!

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Ranked only # 94 on Trip-advisor for a reason.”
text: I stayed at this hotel for a night in late November,2006. Despite my best efforts to upgrade my room (which I was more than willing to pay more for) I was told this was not possible so I was assigned to a "standard room". It was room #1043. I paid $306.88 including room tax plus $51.30 to park my car for the night. Upon opening the door, I could not believe how small the room was. The room could not have been bigger than 10'X12' -probably smaller. The bathroom was less than 4'X7'. The full size bed barely fit. In fact, when you open the door to the room, it misses the bed by only an inch or two. I asked the bellman if there were more if these miniature rooms at the St. Francis and he replied "quite a few, but most business travelers know better and refuse to book them". I've stayed at my share of "grand old hotels" in New York and throughout Europe that also have some tiny rooms but nothing compares to closet-sized "standard rooms" at the St. Francis. As other reviewers note, the furnishings are tired, and the property sorely needs upgrading. This is truly regrettable because the staff are attentive, the hotel is in a great location, and the lobby and common areas are charming. I'm amazed that Westin is still willing to license this property considering its condition. Certainly there must be other properties in San Francisco far more worthy of their brand. Unless you can be assured of a decent sized room, and you don't mind the "torn and tattered" look, I suggest you book elsewhere.

name: Villa Florence, A JRK Hotel
title: “Best location, Helpful Staff & Comfortable Rooms”
text: The location of this hotel is great. The staff was very caring & helpful. The rooms are comfortable & clean. Housekeeping were there for anything we needed & were happy to help. We had a corner room overlooking Powell St. so it was a bit noisy with all the city sounds. Other rooms away from the street do not have noise problems. Kluetos Restaurant & bar was very good. We are looking forward to our return to this hotel.

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
title: “Average Place”
text: We were going on a cruise and stayed here. The Hotel was average. Rooms were clean but on the small side and yes as other people have reported it is quite noisy. Did not care for the tape on the window which apparently had a broken seal. Breakfast fare was on the high side and we found a diner down the street that was very reasonable. Front desk personnel were great in helping out. This Hotel is definitely not the type of place one would want for a romantic getaway. On the plus side it is within walking distance to all the attractions.

name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “CHARGED TWICE FOR ROOM -- WHERE'S MY CREDIT?”
text: I would have given this hotel higher marks, but I pre-purchased a voucher from Otel. com for TWO HOTEL ROOMS and I told the front desk staff. They assured me that yes the rooms were prepaid and they took a credit card for the deposit for any room incidentals. Well, guess what? Our guests woke up to find a bill under their door, yes I was charged twice for this room. Otel says that I need to wait 5 to 20 days. Sir Francis Drake had an original credit pending and now it is now my bank cannot find it. I'm out $122.50 and I'm very mad. And, the price that I paid was $300.60 for two rooms $150.30 per room and I was charged even less directly from Sir Francis Drake @ $122.50. Sorry to rant, but maybe I'll get a response for the Sir Francis Drake or Otel.com. This is very disturbing.

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “excellent value”
text: large rooms for a city hotel and a very convenient location for shopping. lots of beggers on the streets at night but i think thats just san fransisco!

name: CLIFT San Francisco
title: “Vacation in SF”
text: Not great! I would not stay here again. The service was not good. Our room was lacking. We had to request an ironing board & iron. We had stayed at the Mandarian Oriental and their service is exceptional. So we had expected the same here. NO WAY.

name: CLIFT San Francisco
title: “Failed to meet expectations”
text:
The Clift hotel failed to meet my expectations and is was a major dissappointment. It is definitely not a five star hotel. The general unwelcome 
feel one experiences upon entering the lobby is compounded by the arrogant pushy attitudes of the door staff, front desk staff, and especially 
the cranky concierge. They don't have a pool, there's a pungent smell on most of the floors, and you have to pay for using the internet. The 
hotel is dimly lighted so that visitors can't see the worn and stained carpet. The hotel becomes infested with nightclubbers at night with all 
these cheezy types acting like monkeys on the lobby furniture as well as keeping ourselves and the other guests annoyed with their techno music 
blasting from the spanish suite right next door. And then there's the hotel bar, the Redwood Room. I don't mind paying more for a fine modern 
bar experience but again the Clift has failed in this department. The bar is very attractive and stylish, blending the history of the old grande hotel with the modern elements in a silky smooth collage. That's 
where the positives end - great design, poor execution. On approaching the hostess stand guests are looked up and down before being escorted to an appropriate location. Interestingly, the more attractive the look, the more prominent the location will be. We were seated right at the bar. The sharp looking bartenders were standing around chatting and didn't notice our deep need for a drink for quite some time. On approach, I 
asked what their signature cocktail was. The bartender responded by asking what I usually drink (a Chopin Martini), walked away, made the drink, 
presented it, and said, that'll be $14. Then he asked my colleague what she wanted to drink. She opted for a bottle of becks. $8. That was our 
last visit to that bar.

name: Andrews Hotel
title: “Good, budget hotel near Union Square”
text:
We stayed here for 2 nights in late April. The rooms are pretty small and the bathrooms, particularly the showers are tiny but it was all fine for 2 nights - you couldn't really unpack or spread out! Breakfast is laid out on each floor from 7am and they have small pastries, fruit, juice and coffee - enough to keep you going. The area was fine, best to walk left on exiting the hotel towards Union Square and walk along Post St. We took a taxi from SFO to the hotel, it
cost 45 dollars including tip. The staff were pleasant but you had the feeling they'd rather be somewhere else, and who can blame them in such a great city.

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “Great Location”
text:
Stayed here for a few nights before heading to Tahoe. Great location for resteraunts / shopping and trams to see the sights. Clean hotel, comfy bed and friendly staff.
Would happily stay here if Im lucky enough to vist San Fran again.

name: CLIFT San Francisco
title: “Terrific service Great location”
text: We had read not-so-favorable reviews of the staff in terms of friendliness and were concerned prior to arrival. The concerns were unfounded. The service was excellent and the staff incredibly friendly. It's a fun place to stay in a great location - walking distance of China Town and Union Square shopping

name: Andrews Hotel
title: “Good experience”
text: We just got back from a Friday overnight stay. The hotel treated us well, upgrading us from a queen to a mini-suite with a king. A good location at a good price (for San Francisco). It's an older hotel that hasn't been updated in quite a while, but that's part of its charm. Rooms have small TVs with attached DVD players and a decent lending library. Not a huge selection for the continental breakfast (rolls & pastries, coffee, orange juice and a basket of fresh fruit), but the quality was very good. Not so good: Valet parking ($33 a day, plus tax, and a 20-30 minute wait to retrieve car) and a blast of heat from the radiator in the morning. A free glass of wine is offered from 5-6:30 at the restaurant bar (or at the table, if you're having a early dinner). Having a very high-quality restaurant downstairs - Fino (see separate review) - is a plus.

name: CLIFT San Francisco
title: “Charmed by Clift Hotel”
text: I stayed at the Clift March 23-27, 2003, and loved this hotel. I received a great rate through Expedia, and was delighted to find a hotel that had interesting, funky decor, comfy rooms, and friendly staff. The food at the restaurant was excellent, and my somewhat offbeat requests of the concierge were met in a timely and professional manner. Oh, and did I mention the beds! Ultra comfortable, with great linens, fantastic pillows, and a cashmere throw perfect for TV watching. A few negatives were the noises from other rooms, and the small tubs in the bathrooms. The roomservice menu was fairly pricey, but the food delivered was interesting in presentation and delicious! I would recommend this hotel for any one under 50 (or over 50 and open minded), looking for more than the average chain hotel, but not quite up to Four Seasons stuffiness and price. Nice touches are the candles lit throughout the property each evening, and the romantic alcoves, perfect for a quiet conversation and glass of wine.

name: Club Quarters San Francisco
title: “Perfect for simple business Travel”
text: I spent about 20 nights here in January of 2012 and for me it was quite adequate. Some people don't care for the small rooms but when you're one person traveling alone, this is just fine. If I were traveling with my girlfriend I might prefer the hotel across the street, but for the price, Club Quarters can't be beat in this neighborhood. Rooms were clean, staff were friendly and prompt, room was always made up on time, good in-suite dining options from local restaurants. And for those conducting business in the Financial District, this place is pretty prefect. Again, don't expect large room or fancy stuff. But it's a clean, comfy bed with a nice 32" LCD on the wall, and a pretty nice modern bathroom with excellent lighting. Odd that I noticed the lighting in there, but I've stayed at places with crappy lighting before.

name: Park Hotel
title: “Buono per la posizione”
text: Come in ogni grande città i prezzi per dormire sono sempre molto alti. Questo hotel offre la possibilità di dormire praticamente in centro (a due passi da Union Square, China Town ed il Financial District) nonché vicino a molte fermate dei bus sulla market ed al capolinea del Cable Car, ad un prezzo relativamente basso o meglio più basso di quello offerto da altri alberghi. Camere pulite. Gli addetti alla reception sono sempre stati molto disponibili, addirittura ci hanno aiutato a portare su le valigie con l'elevatore (sembra infatti molto più un montacarichi che non un ascensore) ed anche aiutato per avere informazioni. Noi avevamo il lavandino fuori dal bagno che, se siete in di più, è molto comodo. Vicino alla reception ci sono anche molti depliant su SF da spulciare sia per le cartine ma anche per i buoni sconti da utilizzare. 1 informazione di servizio: se volete comprare il 1 DAY PASSPORT per tutti i bus e cable car lo potete acquistare direttamente sopra il Cable Car.

name: Courtyard San Francisco Downtown
title: “loved the Marriott Courtyard on 2nd & Folsom”
text:
This is not only a better than average hotel but the location was great too. We booked through Expedia (air & hotel combo) so it was a great price. It is only 3 blocks from Market and a10 minute walk from Union Square (major shopping area). 
We ate in the bar/restaurant and had a good meal. The Starbucks hours of operation are less than appealing but that didn't diminish our feelings about the hotel. 
VERY comfortable beds (they have just upgraded all of the beds) and ample sized rooms. The workout room is great but you have to get there early.
The whole experience at the hotel was delightful.

name: Villa Florence, A JRK Hotel
title: “Wonderful Hotel!”
text:
My sister and I stayed at Villa Florence for four nights in May, and we loved it. We found a good rate online and requested a quiet room with two beds. The room was beautiful, and the double beds were extremely comfortable! There was no view - the window just looked out at another wall - but it was very quiet! I can imagine that the streetside rooms would be quite noisy because the hotel is on Powell Street - lots of traffic, cable cars, and emergency vehicles going by at all hours.
The room also came with upscale toiletries- even conditioner, which a lot of hotels don't include - as well as a daily newspaper, hairdryer, small fridge/minibar and a coffee maker with free coffee and tea.
The reception staff was very friendly, and we really appreciated having a computer to use in their small business center. It was great to send e-mails home and print out our return boarding passes. Upon check-in, we were each given a coupon for a free coffee with the purchase of a pastry from their little pastry bar, so a couple of the mornings we started our day with croissants and fruit while watching the people go by on the street outside.
We didn't eat at their restaurant - it was very popular and always busy - but we did go in a couple of nights for a glass of wine and to sit at the window seat to people watch.
The location was ideal - just a couple blocks from the BART station, so it was easy to get to the hotel from SFO. It's also right at Union Square and within easy walking distance of good shopping, Chinatown, North Beach, the Ferry Building, Cable Cars, and plenty of buses.
I would definitely recommend this hotel!

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “Be Aware of the Cost Of Parking!!!!!”
text:
We thought this hotel was in a really easy spot to explore the city, the man when we first arrived was very helpful recommending a Thai Restaurant call Ar Roi just up the ally way from the hotel and the food was excellent - when everyone else offers hamburgers and you just wanted something with veggies! 
Our room on the 6th floor was lovely and big, no views in a big city but what do you expect. We had a great 3 days at this hotel and if you don't mind the housekeeping banging on your door at 8am asking when you are leaving for the day so they can clean your room then your in luck! 
The whole experience was spoilt when we left and were charged $45 a day in parking when every hotel around you was charging $20 and the Valet guy bringing your car back tells you it's only $20 a day for general public not for Hotel people, you can't help but feel ripped off!
Would I stay there again yes would I park somewhere else YES!

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
title: “"OK" for what it is”
text:
For the kind of hotel it is, it does a good job. Don't expect miracles.
Good:
Decent rooms that were clean.
A stones throw from the Wharf
McDonalds 2 blocks away. 
Walgreens across the street.
5 minute walk from Pier 39
10 minute walk from Pier 33 (Alcatraz)
Few blocks from Lombard St (crooked street)
5-10 minute drive from the Golden Gate bridge
Free Wi-Fi
Denny's in-lobby in one of the buildings.
3 blocks from Ghiradelli Square
Front Desk lady was nice and helpful.
Parking in main building is underground and somewhat secured.
Bad:
Parking $40 per night
Hotel is two separate buildings across the street from one another. Only one bell hop who was too busy to help.
Lots of street noise heard on the outside rooms.
Lots of homeless in the area.
Some sirens heard in the middle of the night.

name: Courtyard San Francisco Downtown
title: “Great Location, Awesome Beds”
text: Stayed here the weekend of June 9th, 2006. Great location, close to all forms of public transportation, we didn't have to rent a car. Take the BART from the airport. Three blocks from hotel. Starbucks in the lobby. Rooms were very clean and the beds were unbelievably comfortable. Spent most of the time seeing the city so this hotel was perfect for us. Close to great shopping and restaurants. Great rates as well. Would definitely go back.

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “Very nice large and busy hotel”
text:
I was very curious about how our experience would be at this hotel after reading quite a few of the other reviews...would it be crazy mobbed? Lines around the block?
We ended up having a very nice experience at this Hilton, staying for two nights (Sun-Tues). The check in line (on a Sunday) was about 7 people long but only 1 person deep at the HHonors desk. Someone from the main line got snippy and yelled at me for waiting there until I pointed out the HHonors sign on the desk. A larger sign, perhaps above the desk, could avoid such hassles in the future?
Anyway I requested a remodeled room and was given one in Tower 3. It was very nice, just like the pictures on the Hilton website. It wasn't the largest of rooms, but very nice and definitely sound insulated. Good job on the remodel! Hopefully this will extend to other floors/towers soon. My only complaint would be the shower, which had very low pressure. I know this is probably a "green" thing, but if you have to take a shower twice as long, is a low flow shower head really saving water?
As an HHonors Gold member, I was offered complimentary coupons for free continental breakfast, which consisted of a pastry, drink, and choice of fruit from the lobby Starbucks; OR I could pay $10 upgrade for the full buffet in Urban Tavern, also off the lobby. We took the upgrade but the clerk still gave us two continental breakfast coupons anyway, which was nice for early morning coffee/tea before breakfast. The Starbucks line was sometimes long (20 or so people) but the 5-6 staff there moved the line fast.
Breakfast in Urban Tavern was very good....pretty standard buffet but with some Asian flavor (salmon and rice, lichee fruit). It was busy but not overwhelmed since you have to be seated first, and that caps how many people are there at any given time.
Lobby did have a lot of people there using wi-fi but really it was hardly annoying as some others reported...there were a lot of seats to accommodate everyone.
Location wise this hotel is fantastic. You can get to it easily from BART and Muni and get to almost anywhere you want in the City quite easily.
I asked for a late checkout on Tuesday and it was readily granted (2pm). That is also a HHonors Gold perk so not sure if this would work for everyone, or on a busier day. But was great for us as our flight was 5pm.
I would definitely stay here again.

name: Club Quarters San Francisco
title: “Not the Greatest Thing on Eartch”
text: My husband and I live in the East Bay. We had a one night certificate from our stay at Club Quarters in London. The entire hotel had water problems one morning. Since we have the certificate we decided to have dinner and spend the night at Club Quarters in San Francisco. The location is very close to Embarcardero and BART. Well, the room was clean, but we felt that we were spending the night in the closet. The San Francisco's Club Quarters was no comparison to London's. The common room didn't have wine/ soda hours. The floor didn't have a water dispenser with individual. The front desk staff was rude.

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Avoid the temptation”
text: We booked through Westin 800 number and were assured a "nice" room. When we arrived we were shocked at the room. Small, smelly and plain. After arguing with the front desk they put us in a smoking room in the new tower. My brother stayed the same time and had a larger room in the old section. The room was very old and in serious need of renovation. For what they charge you can do much better in San francisco.

name: Hotel Fusion
title: “Fusion”
text: Fusion is een centraal gelegen hotel, op steenworp afstand van Union Square, de cable-cars en BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit. Het hotelpersoneel is kundig en weet ook werkelijk alles wat je maar over de stad hebt te vragen. De kamers zijn niet supergroot, maar als het goed is zit je daar geen hele dag als je in Frisco bent. De netheid van de kamers is uitstekend. Enige minpuntje vond ik het wat te eenvoudige continental ontbijt. Het hotel is zeker een aanrader, zeker voor koppels en alleenstaanden (zoals ik). Bovendien is het stukken goedkoper dan heel wat hotels in de directe omgeving. Doen dus, dat Fusion C-two-hotel!

name: Courtyard San Francisco Downtown
title: “Muy buen Courtyard”
text:
Estuvimos alojados aquí en Agosto de 2012.
El hotel está muy bien situado, a dos calles de Marquet St. y a cuatro de Powell St.
Tiene todas las cosas buenas que tiene los Courtyard, la habitación es limpia y amplia, al igual que el baño.
El lobby es enorme y tiene un Starbucks en su entrada y un buen restaurante.
La piscina, el jacuzzi y el gimnasio son cubiertos y completos.
El WIFI es gratuito y de buena calidad.
Muy recomendable.

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
title: “First class”
text:
From check in to check out everyone was friendly, helpful and courteous. Room was clean and comfortable, well-appointed.
Breakfast buffet wasn't cheap like most hotels but the service was excellent and the buffet choices were good.
Shuttle to and from the airport worked well.

name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Beautiful facility, not a great place to stay”
text:
I stayed here for two nights earlier this month in advance of a business conference at another hotel. I wanted to be near Union Square and take advantage of some discounts on rooms. Big mistake. The staff was great, especially the Beefeater bellhops. Union Square is less than one block away and there are musicians (trumpet player) who play into the wee hours. The cable cars stop directly in front of the hotel (right below my window) with their clanging bells from 5:30 AM until Midnight. And there are countless homeless people who sleep in Union Station and spend their day walking back and forth in front of the various hotels begging. Sunday morning at 6:00 AM, a homeless woman started screaming that she was starving and no one would help her... this went on for nearly an hour before police asked her to move along. 
Architecturally, this is a beautiful property and very well located, but I needed some sleep and that was not on the agenda. Plus, older hotels have typically very small rooms and bathrooms compared to more modern hotels and this was no different. Plus, the windows were so old and filthy on the outside, it was impossible to see out.

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Tired”
text: I guess for the price and location this place isn't too bad, but this is far and away the worst Westin I've ever stayed in. time for a major room and common area overhaul. They do have some sort of hipster lobby bar/restaurant thing going on but in a city full of that sort of thing it doesn't do much to make up for the overall tiredness that the rest of the hotel conveys. Even with some decent Starwood status your "upgrade" upon check-in just gets you a slightly bigger room in desperate need of a renovation. Stay there if you want to be right on Union Square, really want the Starwood points, and are on a budget but otherwise there's better to be had.

name: Andrews Hotel
title: “Great Hotel”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights in June 2008. Having never been to San Francisco before, we wanted a hotel that was a short walk away from the action.
The Andrews Hotel is a perfect hotel for Union Square and all the bars and shopping that come with it. With Union square comes the cable car route that takes you all the way to Fishermans Wharf - the best way to travel.
Check in was easy, very polite staff, and we were very pleased with our room on the 7th floor. It wasn't the biggest, but we expected this and was perfectly in character of the hotel.
As we were celebrating a belated honeymoon, a bottle of sparkling wine/champagne was waiting for us upon arrival. Very nice! There is only 1 lift, but we never had problems waiting for it, a very nice original feature of the hotel.
Breakfasts were nice, left out on each level for guests to go help themselves to tea, coffee, orange juice, fresh fruit and breads.
By staying at the Andrews, every night, each guest is entitled to a free glass of wine at the Italian restuarant called Fino that shares the ground floor. This was a nice touch, and we ate there on our first night. The food and service were both very very good. 
The only problem we encountered was trying to get an international line so we could phone home. We were not successful, despite the help from reception staff, but when the attempts appeared on our final invoice, they were more than happy to wipe it off. 
All in all, we really enjoyed our stay here, and would definately recommend it to other travellers.

name: Marriott San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “A most enjoyable stay”
text:
We stayed for 5 nights at the hotel and as requested were given a courtyard room which was quiet and peaceful. The rooms were comfortable, clean, spacious enough and with excellent bed mattresses. We only savoured breakfast once but due to sightseeing during the day and being retired folks we were generally too tired to venture out for dinner in the evening. The food at dinner was of great quality and the chef and our waiter Juan gave superb service. We were treated to a bottle of wine on the last evening and a plate full of fruit fit for a king. Generally speaking all the staff were extremely helpful and practised the meaning of customer service.
The hotel is in an ideal location for all the sights and the cable car and we were pleased we had had not booked a hotel downtown which is isolated from the main attractions. One evening after dinner we went to Lou's Blues Bar close to the Wharf and for 5 dollars per head listened to some fantastic blues music. They have live blues music every night and is well worth a visit.
The hotel is not a low cost option but is great value and located in the ideal situation of one of the most striking cities in the world. We would not hesitate to return.

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
title: “Quality of Rooms not great, Good Location”
text:
Pros:
- Very close to ferry building -- easy access so you can quickly get great food / visit the farmer's market
Cons:
- The quality of the rooms were so-so and there were blood stains on the carpet in our room when we arrived. We asked to switch, but they couldn't switch us that night. They did call back the next day to ask if we wanted to switch, but it just wasn't worth it. We asked to be compensated somehow and they gave us $50 off which was nice, but overall we didn't feel like customer service was the best. Not sure if it was worth the nightly rate

name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
title: “Ok hotel in a good location”
text:
I'm super loyal to Marriott as a Platinum Premier ... Its in a good location - between Market and Mission Sts on Fourth. 
As for the actual hotel, its a convention/meeting type hotel. Very busy lobby. All the time. Rooms are small but do the trick. 
Even with my status, no upgrade to even the Concierge level. Bonus that the Concierge lounge is open 7 days a week. Friday morning quiet, Saturday morning PACKED. 
Gym is ok. Has all the regular equipment. Some have tv's that work. 
Biggest issue with the hotel was the cab line. The doorman was more interested in getting people to take the sedan service than trying to wave down taxis. I get that taxis are sometimes tough to come by - but we waited 40 minutes (when we got there we were fourth in line....). Watched the doorman count his wad of cash tips four times openly. That's a bit tacky. 
I would come back but we've enjoyed the JW Marriott near Union Square a bit more.

name: CLIFT San Francisco
title: “Finalement moyen”
text:
Quand on arrive, on remarque avant tout le design très recherché et le côté hyper branchouille de l'hotel (propre à cette chaine).
Mais les chambres restent petites avec un minimum d'accessoires.
Aux alentours de 100 euros, c'est acceptable. Au dessus c'est un peu cher.
Dans l'hotel, il y a LE bar branché de SF : à voir en fin de semaine.
Emplacement étrange : à qques pas de Union Square (où se trouvent tous les hotels de ce type et la plupart des transports) mais également à qques pas de downtown (plutôt très craignos). 
Un peu décevant donc.

name: Executive Hotel Vintage Court
title: “Friendly and clean in a great location!”
text: Our experience at this hotel was nice from the moment we walked in the door. The staff was friendly and so helpful with directions. Parking across the street was convenient. It was easy to reach the cable car and 30 Stockton bus to reach Fisherman's Wharf. (You can hop on and pay your money without going to the end of the line.) Close walk to Union Square, Chinatown, Italian food and breakfast. Loved the friendly guy at the desk with the black vest and orange tie. Go Giants!

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
title: “Really nice location, needs some updating but”
text: Liked the location. I live in SoCal so I did a weekend getaway here. Love the city. As some reveiwers noted, it does need some updating. But, all in all, it was a good stay at a good hotel ... I would absolutely describe my stay as positive. I would stay here again. The value was not as good as it could have been ... but I do really like the location. Also, the service was top notch. Really good service.

name: Hyatt at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Comfortable accomodation, good location”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights in Aug. The hotel was clean and the beds comfortable. There was a mix up with our pre payment, they kept charging the deposit off the credit card and eventually they gave a full refund and only charged on check out. For our trouble, which was over a few weeks and having to actually cancel my credit card, they gave us a free upgrade to a suite. Attached to the hotel is knuckles restaurant which is also worth a visit as the service is good and the food fresh and tasty. Location is great as we could walk to the waterfront and to the restaurants and pier to get the ferry to Alcatraz. Overall pretty good value for money.

name: Hyatt at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Lovely hotel - exceptional staff”
text: We just spent five nights here after visiting LA and before going to Vegas. I knew how touristy Fisherman's Wharf was but if you do choose a hotel in this area, I think the Hyatt is a good choice. We had two interconnecting rooms and although the decor was a little dated, they were spacious and clean. Knuckles, the onsite restaurant is very good and the Starbucks coffee is a real bonus. We also ate at Hollywood Grill, which is opposite the hotel, and is well worth a visit (amazing breakfasts). If I was staying in this area of San Francisco again, I would stay here and would recommend it. All the staff we encountered went out of their way to be helpful - very high level of customer service.

name: Hotel Boheme
title: “Fifty Fifty at the Hotel Bohème”
text:
Stayed at the Hotel Boheme for the last two night in the San Francisco, Napa Valley, Carmel vacation. We had three people in our party the first night we had a fine room with two queen beds. We knew we had to change rooms the second night to a queen bed and a futon. Well the futon turned out to be a small dirty cushon on the floor. The room window was next to the exhaust
vent of the restaurant on the first floor it sounded like a jet engine. We got no sleep that night. The hotel is on the second floor with only a very narrow stairway.
The Hotel is in a great location in Little Italy. Just make sure you do not stay in Room 207. or if they request a futon run to a different hotel.

name: Andrews Hotel
title: “Customer Service - the best!”
text:
We just got back from San Fran and the Andrews hotel was just the best. The service was excellent - Oscar the consierge was amazing - he knew so much and his recommendations for restaurants were right on. Dan, the bartender at the hotel's restaurant was friendly, plus the house wine you get as a guest of the hotel was very good - the Pinot grigio was yum and do get the calamari. The rooms were small but cozy and little things make a differerence like a small bud vase of flowers - it was such a pleasant surprise. Breakfast was great - each floor has their own breakfast set up - so easy which consisted of fresh fruit, pastries, coffee and fresh juice.
The hotel is in walking distance to the trollies and buses so a car is not needed, but if you do drive in get tready for a 28.00 a day parking fee - you do get to go in and out though. We rented a car in oakland because we were traveling up to Napa - next time we'll rent in the city.
We would definatly stay here again - what made this place stand out was CUSTOMER SERVICE - we have traveled all over the worls and have never had the attention nor the personal care as we did here at the Andrews.
Enjoy

name: Hotel Boheme
title: “What a fantastic hotel”
text:
We stayed for 6 nights at The Hotel Boheme and thought it was fantastic. As we had done our homework and read other reviews we understood that this was a small boutique hotel with no lift and were expecting the rooms to be small maybe noisy if we were on the front.
However, I am not sure if staying in room 208 has a distinct advantage over the rooms but it was perfect. We didn't think the room was too small at all, especially compared to hotels in the Centre of London. We had plenty of natural light on the back and it was quiet. It didn't bother us in the slightest that we had to carry our bags up some stairs.
The staff were extremely polite and helpful and couldn't do enough for us. The location is absolutely a plus point, it is safe with plently of restaurants and bars. Washington Square is round the corner, the Beat history on your doorstep and a 20 minute stroll takes you right down to fisherman's wharf and the piers.
The only thing that slightly frustrated us was the noise of the showers when guests woke up early, they were very loud in our room but we used our ear plugs we had bought just in case and we were able to sleep really well.
I would definitely recommend this hotel to friends and stay there again without hesitation.

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Hotel Carlton - San Francisco charm”
text:
I was in SF helping a friend. We had planed to stay at a hotel near civic center but the neighborhood was seriously scary so we ditched that plan. We had previously stayed at The Granada right up the street from the but you have to stay for a week so we decided to see what the Carlton's rates were as a week wasn't in the budget. For SF we got a fantastic rate...we decided to stay 3 nights instead of 1. 
The front desk staff was absolutely marvelous, since they only had a king room they brought up a roll-away and also a mini fridge. The room was nicely appointed and clean.You could here some noise from neighbors, typical city room in an old building. Internet worked just fine. The lobby was really nice and cozy. They served complimentary wine in the lobby too! 
 I absolutely love the neighborhood! Central to most all tourist sites but also some very cool restaurants and bars right around the neighborhood. Oh, yes, there are homeless peeps around...It's the city, come on folks!

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “Stayed Again...Restaurant is even better :)”
text: I stay here for the great central location on Geary ... Its in between the start and end of the Love Fest every year... The large room was great...the bed is great...the bathroom is OK :) The service was more on this year...Will definitely keep this as my hotel of choice in San Francisco...

name: Hotel Boheme
title: “fabulous Boheme!”
text:
We had the pleasure of staying at the Boheme for 4 nights, and have only positive things to say. The position of the hotel could not be better and was convenient for all of the tourist attractions. The room at the Boheme was at the front of the hotel, and being on the main road did not bother us, in fact it was nice to watch the street below whilst enjoying a glass of wine!. I could not praise the staff highly enough, who were always happy to assist and very friendly, and yes, the stairs are steep but we knew this from reading other trip advisors report, and therefore we expected this!.
North Beach is a fantastic area, with lots to do, with a good selection of coffee shops and restaurants.
We hope to go back to SF in the near future and will be definitely staying at the Boheme.

name: Hotel Del Sol, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Awesome Stay! Awesome Location! Can't beat it!”
text: When you arrive, the colors of the hotel and California styling make you smile right away! The room wasn't too small, the beds were comfortable, and the front desk manager Chris helped me and my friend around the city and with our questions. Would recommend this to anyone who wants to enjoy the views and sites in San Francisco but doesn't want to stay downtown! Great place to say!

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
title: “Great location, great hotel”
text: me and 5 friends travelled from england to san francisco on the first leg of our west coast tour. we stayed from june 5th - 8th and had no complaints. all 3 rooms were clean and spacious. the location of the hotel is excellent for fishermans wharf and is very easy to get to. definitely recommend this hotel and san francisco as a whole was a great city. location only 2 blocks away from the trams to union square. alcatraz and golden gate bridge were definitely highlights. will be returning next year

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
title: “Best Holiday Inn ever!!!!!!!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights in may 2010. We hotel staff were more than helpfull, they let us choose what floor we wanted to stay on and what type of bed!!
There us is a resturant at the hotel called Dennys...... the food is great... good value and excellent service...
The hotel is in a great location you can walk to practically everything. However just round the corner from the hotel next to the italian resturant there is a hop on hop off bus!! You can do this for the day or get a 2 day pass.. we got a 2 days pass so we could do all 3 loops. It cost $50 each. It was great an open top bus, took you to all the main site, union square, golden gate bridge, china town etc....
There are so many souvenier shops and places to eat you are spoilt for choice.....
Make sure you book the Alcatraz before you go as you won't be able to buy tickets when your there, they get booked up really quick!!
The are so many restuarnts to choose from the best ones are on pier 39. Great sea food. Also check out the sea lions while you are there.
When you are leaving get the hotel to book your taxi for you back to the airport.... it costs $50 but you get to go in a Lincon...... 
If anyone has any questions please don't hesitate to contact me.

name: Hotel Boheme
title: “Charming and friendly”
text: Just returned from a weekend in San Francisco - stayed at Hotel Boheme in North Beach. A small boutique hotel in a great location in Little Italy. Our room looked out onto the main strip lined with wonderful bakeries and restaurants. The room was darling and brightly painted and the bathroom was clean with wonderful tile and antique fixtures. The room had a bistro table with 2 chairs in front of the window and an elegant armoire. The innkeeper was friendly and informative and made everyone feel welcome and at home - serving evening cordials in the reception area. Definately would stay again!

name: Executive Hotel Vintage Court
title: “Location, Location”
text:
This was our 2nd time staying here and we have stayed at several hotels in the city.
Location is perfect as you are close to Union Square and the hotel district but not right in it. The neighbourhood is quiet for the most part. The Powell Cable Car is only half a block away. Chinatown Gate is a few blocks away, including all the Belden Lane restaurants for dinner. All close by without being in the thick of all the noisy tourist area a few blocks away
. Did I mention how great the hotel desk staff are for giving you directions, restaurant reviews, or just making you feel welcome. Sure the rooms are a little dated, doors don't quite fit well but this is a n older hotel with history. Rooms have a room safe and air conditioning. Only one elevator, but the stairs work just as well when heading down to the lobby. The 5 oclock wine reception is complimentary, we met so many nice couples there like the couple from England, Australia, & New York. Can you name another hotel that does this? Did I mention that we Love the location? 
I could complain about some of the little things but overall we would reccommend this hotel as it it has character and a fabulous location.

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “viziarsi”
text: E' veramente un gran bel posto. Molto "americano", quindi servizio al massimo livello, ma un po? freddo. Non potrebbe essere altrimenti viste le dimensioni... Ogni volta che passo a SF cerco di fermamici, sia che mi trovi per lavoro o per diletto. Da provare il ristorante di Michael Mina, Bourbon Steak, nella Hall. Un po' caro ma molto valido. Il Ristorante Oak Room è più abbordabile e molto meno pretenzioso, con un'ottima qualità. Se si può, da andarci.

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “Minimal decor/minimal service”
text:
I stayed at the Adagio for a business trip. The rooms are in a weird brown colour which was a bit depressing. The size of the room was not bad but the bathroom must be from the 60s. The tub is even for a child too small and just simply ridiculous for an adult.
Well, I choose this hotel for the location but would not return. I stayed at the Ritz Carlton last time for pleasure and will for sure return to that hotel again. 
Overall, do not expect anything fancy.

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “Nice hotel pity they are rebuilding while still open!”
text: Nice hotel pity they were rebuilding whilst we were there last week. They have done 4 or 5 floors but there are still a lot to go.

name: Executive Hotel Vintage Court
title: “No Promised Breakfast, Dirty Smelly Rooms & Poor Customer Service”
text:
Having arrived an hour prior to official check-in time we left our luggage with the hotel concierge and went out for a bite to eat.
Unfortunately things started bad when we were checking in… upon returning we discovered our bags had just been dumped in a corner in front of reception and not locked away in a room and having been promised breakfast with our room (booked via Expedia) we were told that breakfast is no longer available and hadn’t been for a good number of months. We were never made aware of this and were told it was because of the Economic Climate. So basically I paid for a room and breakfast and got no breakfast, so the hotel was in fact stealing money from me as I didn’t get what I paid for i.e. I was overcharged for my stay. I will be taking that matter up further with Expedia but judging by other comments here I am not alone and I think the hotel has been conning its guests. Not a good start. The hotel hosts a daily wine reception for guests which makes me wonder what the Economic Climate is that they refer to? Perhaps if they stopped that and instead put the money into breakfast as promised they might get better reviews!
After waiting forever for the lift to take us to our room (very slow) I was expecting things to get better, they didn’t! The bathroom had a nice long hair waiting for us on the sink with a think layer of dust on the décor around the wall. The bed sheets also had hairs on them so I just used the blanket to sleep on until morning when I requested a change of linen. The linen was eventually changed but we weren’t left any face cloths which was just typical of this hotel.
The hotel also doesn’t offer Free Wi-Fi which is a major gripe of mine with any hotel if it doesn’t. The Internet cost $5 for 20mins or less e.g. if printing i.e. boarding passes.
We only booked this hotel because the room rate was good and adding to that the decent reviews on this site and the supposed complimentary breakfast. However, the hotel was a complete let down, dirty (except for lobby because it leads into a restaurant) with a musty smell in the rooms and poor customer service. Even though we had pre-paid there was some confusion whether we had or not until a staff member showed his collegue.
I would definitely recommend paying more for a better standard of hotel in SF.

name: The Mosser
title: “Great Value for location but nothing special”
text:
The best thing about the Mosser is the price for the location. Rooms are small and bathrooms and toilets are shared.
The best way to describe it, is as a posh hostel. I did admire their commitment to being a 'green hotel' with enviromentally friendly shampoo and conditioner and a 100 % cotton robe (which is not thick enough to cover nakedness mind you). 
I was caught in an earthquake tremor during my stay there. If an earthquake wasn't scary enough, the way the room shook was. I thought the building might collapse, a downside to staying in an old building.
The service at the front counter was okay. There is no restaurant on site, but one next door, which I found to be quiet pricey considering the lack of choices on the menu.
I would recommend to a friend who was on a budget.

name: Hotel Del Sol, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “fantastic colourful motel!”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights at the end of July at the start of our trip accross the Western US. We had a great stay. We parked easily in the car park just outside the hotel and the car stayed there for the duration of our stay in San Francisco. The room was large, colourful and comfortable - we were sharing with our two teenagers and the one room was fine. Breakfast was quite impressive, the reception seems tiny but they manage to put on a pretty good spread of toast, yoghurts, bagels, muffins etc It was pretty cold eating outside, even in July and wouldn't have ventured anywhere near the pool. SanFrancisco in July certainly made the UK in summer feel warm!
We walked easily from the hotel only using one of the scenic trams for the experience rather than anything else! 
We would certainly recommend the hotel.

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Sper Central”
text: Ja die Lage ist genial, Union Square, Zimmer sehr groß ! WLAN Überall, Breakfast zu teurer, netter Aussenfahrstuhl, gediegene Atmosphäre.... immer wieder , Preis nicht ohne :Cabel car vor der tür

name: Villa Florence, A JRK Hotel
title: “Good deal”
text:
Villa Florence located right in the heart of Union Square -- great location -- block down from the St. Francis. Older hotel renovated but quite nicely. Rooms are perfectly adequate -- a bit small with Queen size bed. Do, however, ask for a quiet room. A friend had a room on the street side and heard a lot of noise when a nearby club closed and street noise. Staff is very helpful and nice wine at their happy hour.
Would certainy recommend this hotel.

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
title: “Nice hotel some verage staff”
text: This hotel was in a great location. The breakfast staff were very nice as was the guy serving in the bar and so was the lady who checked us in! (I think her name was Pat & she was wonderful) Thank god they made up for a few of the others who were really average. There was one very rude lady at reception on one day who argued loudly with us regading some incorrect advice I had been given about whether they hold on to your room card when you go out. We had been told they did however when we got back she made a big fuss about scanning us a new one and was very rude when I was trying to explain that we had been told earlier by someone this was not required. She kept loudly refering to my friend standing next to me as my husband which was a bit uncomfortable given we are not married and checked in with different surnames. She was an older asian lady and thank goodness we only had to deal with her the one time. In our room we also had a phone which when I tried to call reception would put me through to some other poor person's room (I thought I had just dialed the wrong number so called them a few times). I told them at reception that this was happening and they didn't seem to care. The next day I tried reception again and got the same person's room so I just gave up. When we called room service for a bottle opener they never came. I am definately glad we stayed in the main building as it appeared a bit better than the other building with the burger place underneath. Overall average but I guess you are paying for the location.

name: Hotel Del Sol, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Stayed in Executive Suite”
text: My husband and I have two small children who are 4 and 2. My father-in-law and sister-in-law tagged along. Instead of getting two separate rooms we booked the Executive Suite. It's basically one large room with king bed, sofa pullout and kitchenette. The hotel was kind enough to provide two roll outs without extra charge. In additional, the hotel did not charge an additional vehicle parking fee since we took two cars. Regardless, of the "savings" the room is a bit pricey. The staff was friendly and the kids enjoyed the video games and books that they can check out.

name: Andrews Hotel
title: “Hotel encantador a un paso de las principales atracciones”
text: En septiembre estuvimos alojados en este hotel, el cual reservamos directamente a través de internet teniendo en cuenta las críticas de tripadvisor (ajustadas lo que nos encontramos). Es un hotel muy bien localizado en la calle Post, cerca del eje central que constituye la calle Market, y de tamaño medio-pequeño en un edificio tradicional, como otros hoteles de la misma calle. Sus instalaciones son adecuadas y es limpio. El Hall es pequeño, pero cuenta con café y fruta a dispoción de los huespedes durante todo el día. El acensor es una autentica obra de arte, ya que se remonta a principios del S. XX, (¡¡ y aún funciona ¡¡¡). La espaciosa habitación en la que nos alojamos daba a la parte de atras, por lo que resultó ser muy tranquila (algo más de ruido la noche del sábado con un bar que había enfrente, pero soportable) y muy luminosa. La cama tamaño king-size estupenda y muy cómoda, El cuarto de baño con ducha muy pequeño. De hecho para sentarse en el inodoro había que colocar las piernas debajo del lavabo (debería ser un poco más ancho). Como detalle por las mañanas en la planta había café, bollería y fruta para autoservicio (no tuvimos problemas en disponer de él, como han comentado otros huespedes). Respecto al personal sólamente comentar que aún estando en california (con claras raices hispanas, y muchos residentes que lo hablan) no se esforzó en absoluto en hablar castellano. Nos entendimos en nuestro inglés básico, pero notamos una falta ese interés por comunicarse en nuestra lengua.

name: Chelsea Motor Inn
title: “Nice Price, Nice Place”
text: We had a good experience at the Chelsea Motor Inn. Very close to Chestnut, which had a lot of cool restaurants and shops. Hi-speed internet and free parking are a big plus. We got two CityPass's that we used to travel by bus everywhere we wanted to go. We would definitely stay at the Chelsea again.

name: Hotel Del Sol, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Would stay here again and we recommend!”
text: Great hotel in a convenient SF location! The neighborhood is great and it is just blocks from all the sights. Staff were nice and helpful...really great with my 2 year old. The rooms were clean and cheerful. We loved the smell of the shampoo/conditioner they supplied. There was a lending library of books/DVDs for our kids and a lovely breakfast each morning. My family enjoyed the pool in the courtyard.

name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
title: “Great location”
text: The staff members that I encountered were all friendly and helpful. My room was very clean and spacious. I had requested a room on a higher floor, which I got. I had the best view of downtown San Francisco. There is a Starbucks located within the hotel, and a restaurant adjacent to the hotel. There are also plenty of restaurants and cafe near the hotel. The hotel is within walking distance to catching the trolley, cable car, and the bart.

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Ottima posizione”
text:
hotel molto grande, dispersivo, ma di buona qualità.
Il suo grande valore è la posizione centralissima.
Le stanze sono grandi e confortevoli.
San Francisco è stupenda.
Consiglio di prendere un taxi dall'aereoporto e di contrattare un prezzo fisso.
All'interno dell'hotel troverete ristorante, negozi, ecc.
Ho anche utilizzato la sala computer con pochi dollari ed utilizzando la carta di credito prepagata.
Ottimo servizio.

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “People with asthma, beware!”
text: This hotel only has a ceiling fan. No ventilation and the windows only open slightly. It is stuffy and when I came into the room, the whole room reaked of bleach. When they moved me, the rooms smelled of some type of cleaning agent, and they tried to cover it up in the building by putting aromatherpy that shot out of the elevator vents each time you would step into it. The linin was musty and if you have any type of breathing problems such as asthma, say a prayer and grab your inhaler! I had to leave and find a different hotel.

name: Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf Hotel
title: “Just walk away... The worst customer services we have ever experienced... Given a choice, we pick no star for this one.”
text:
We traveled a lot with SPG hotels, largely because the chain covers some really good properties in Europe and Asian, we have been happy with our experiences elsewhere overall, till with Sheraton at fisherman's wharf- we stayed for one night between April 30- may1 and could not wait running away any faster, we moved back to our usual favorite in town the mark Hopkins staying for test the week where the old School customer services still value the most...
To sum up our 24 hour experience with Sheraton- we checked in at late pm, had a pleasant checkin experiences with Jim, we were assigned to room 2628, was told it's a preferred guest room, and quietly facing court- yard. The room was okay size, but with a tiny bathroom, barely can move around- tho just done renovation, ceiling was still run-down, we can literally hear most of noises and foot steps from neighbours. But our real nightmare started at after 1am midnight- since we have a minor surgery at USCF centre the next day, we went to bed a bit earlier, but after past mid night- we were woke up by the running water and heavy foot steps from upstairs, then leaking water in the bathroom--- minutes later, we heard loud repair work, with chain-sawing and drilling noises from upstairs at almost 1:30am!!!!! We then have to call downstairs customer services asking what's going on, at first, no response/ answer for ehat's about, quickly few minutes later, same lady call back saying repair work need to be done, and the option for us is to ' move to another room' if we like" -- we requested for manager... And explained our frustration as to a Sheraton 5 rated hotel- this would never have happened!!! Of course, the manager never showed up nor called back, only the same lady, called back- after a few rounds phone calls and complains, the 'work' finally stopped- then we got even calls from repairman at mid of night to wanting look at bathroom leakage.... The end, everything finally gone peace at around 3am -- we woke up again the next morning, but door knock - eventually we put out ' do not disturb ' to rest some- of course, we were late for the hospital but manage to be okay- we checked out the hotel right after wards, to our very surprise- we never even receive a note nor any apology from hotel management about a near nightmare experience!!! One thing for sure, this is our last w Sheraton at fisherman's wharf. 
Guest from Hongkong, SPG gold since 2005

name: Executive Hotel Vintage Court
title: “Another great stay at Vintage Court”
text: My family and I have been staying at Vintage Court for years. When I was asked to make arrangements for a group of friends traveling to San Francisco for a museum weekend, I contacted the staff at Vintage Court. As always, everyone was pleased with our experience there. The location (Union Square Area) is excellent. We parked the cars and walked everywhere we wanted to go. The staff is very accomodating and friendly and the wine reception is a special treat. We brought our own cheese, fruit, and crackers. Our friends commented on the very comfortable rooms and reasonable rates. We look forward to the next time we get together in San Francisco and will definitely stay at the Vintage Court Hotel.

name: Executive Hotel Vintage Court
title: “Nothing short of exceptional!”
text:
My experience at Hotel Vintage Court was nothing short of exceptional!
I travel a lot between LA and San Fransisco for work and I know the hotels around the area very well. Hotel Vintage Court is certainly the best value.
The rooms are spacious, well kept, and full of character. The house-staff is very friendly.
I don't know if it is the shower heads or the water pressure, but it's the best shower I've had in a long time! And even the soap has little exfoliating beads on it.
There are nightly wine tastings (pretty sure it's nighly) and there are plenty of local and international visitors to mingle with. From all over the world! Although I was there on business, this hotel would be a wine tasters delight! (Actually perfect. You could stay and enjoy the unique San Fran experience and then take a short beautiful ride into wine country. When I lived in the city this was one of my favorite things to do).
I'm just happy I can stop shopping around for hotels for my biz trips. Hotel Vintage Court is a cut above the rest.
Art

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “Clean, Great Location, but not worth the money”
text: This hotel had friendly staff, clean rooms, and great bedding. The drawback is the AC unit going out a pipe in the window, with the window having to be open for this to happen. The noise on Geary Street is unbearable, with a nightclub lineup on the sidewalk almost all night, and many drunks shouting and singing 'til dawn. Also every smoker forced to be outside for a cigarette, chose to smoke below our windows, and our room was constantly full of smoke. The price for our room was exorbitant with these consideration. I left before my husband, and when he checked out he was charged for honor-bar items that we did not consume. He paid because he supposed it was me who was not there to say it wasn't. I find that sloppy. Also our bathroom wall had some sort of stain near the toilet, that continued to exist the whole stay. I would assume that cleaning staff should also wash walls when one is paying way over $200/night for a noisy room. And no, I did not bring any of this to the attention of the hotel, since it was a business convention that brought us there, and the room was arranged by head office, even though we were paying. We also knew that the hotel was full, and it would not be possible to move us.

name: Hyatt at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great area great value”
text:
The staff was very friendly and helpful. Couldn't do enough for you. Our inroom coffee pot did not work and within 15 min it was replaced. 
Only issue was in the bathroom. They ask you re use your towels but there is only one hook and no towel bar to let them dry! Also the in ceiling shower head was a little enemic. 
Would definately reccommend

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “Great experience”
text:
My bf and I stayed at this hotel at the end of Jan. 
A great experience. 
Conveniently located near union sq. 
Room is spacious and nicely decorated. 
Complimentary internet.
Aveda amenities.
Frette bathrobes.
Nice food at Cortez.

name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Not as advertised”
text:
Just checked in today. Based on the reviews that I read, I assumed the hotel would be average. Yes, it is. Location is the only thing I can say is good, but honesty there are a ton of hotels all around the Drake. I chose this hotel because it was a last minute business booking. I arrived and the doorman was outside looking for the President who was in town giving a speech. I had to ask another guest where the check-in desk was.
