The desk clerks were not what I would consider over-friendly by any means. I have traveled for the past 2 months and met much friendlier staff. Upon exiting the elevator to my floor [4th], it was like walking into an ashtray. It stinks like stale cigarettes. I will say that my room does not smell too bad, I think you get used to it. My view is the roof and the walls of the hotel. The size of my room is good, the bathroom is small and in great need of repair. The toilet runs randomly, the shower drips and the wood trim in the bathroom window is chipped, dirty, and just plain looks BAD. It also allows for bugs to enter through the cracks. I spent the first 15 minutes killing bugs and a big fat fly that was in the room. I can't imagine a chain such as Marriott or the Hyatt having a room in such a state. The website states all rooms have a refrigerator, honor bar and a complimentary movie channel - I have none one of those things. I found an old Walgreens bag where I think my Refrigerator is supposed to be?? The TV channels offered are reminiscent of pre-cable, because that's pretty much what you get, basic channels. While it may seem nit-picky, I noticed that I don't even have a bath mat in the bathroom. Guess I am to use one of my towels. Outlets are a premium. There are none in the bathroom. The alarm clock is set-up on the desk which is not next to the bed; I am assuming this is because there is no outlet next to the bed - DUMB!
I know the Manager reads these comments and hopefully he will take the time to freshen up the place. It does not require a complete rehab to paint trim and do general cleaning. Location will not sustain you forever! I really wanted to like this place...

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
title: “Typical Hyatt but with the greatest location.”
text:
This classic Hyatt is a great location for business or family. It is situated across the street from the Ferry Terminal so even though it is rather large with the classic Hyatt inner atrium design, once you leave your decent-sized room and the hotel, you are in a perfect spot for sightseeing, foodie interests and hopping on the Street Car or Cable Car to either Fisherman's Wharf or Nob Hill and the Powell line. I have stayed here more than a few times and I can attest that the security of the hotel has improved. One time, I was awoken by a transgendered lady knocking on my door. Clearly wrong. 
Great dining is all around you and Chinatown is also up the Cable Car ( get a day pass). 
The Hyatt San Francisco is a great hotel whose charms exceed its physical structure.

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “Charme der verblassten grossen Ära”
text: Das Hotel Westin St. Francis ist wohl eines der berühmtesten alten Hotels der USA. Der alte Charme ist ziemlich verblasst und ein Teil der Zimmer ist entsprechend mufflig. Im hinteren Turm sind die Zimmer teilweise neu renoviert, zumindest im oberen Teil, wo man eine schöne Aussicht über die Skyline von San Francisco geniessen kann. Das Personal ist sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit. Im Hotel ist auch das Restaurant "Michael Mina", das zu den besten Restaurants von San Francisco gehört.

name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Good Hotel”
text: Overall, a fairly good hotel that comes with all the amenities. It's a bit on the small side so I wouldn't encourage an extended stay here. Most likely, this is the kind of place for business class travelers and long weekends. Classy hotel offers all the basic amenities that come in a hotel room such as complimentary toiletries and what have you. This hotel certainly showcases it's history and obviously hasn't lost it's identity or style, while still managing to retain a contemporary image. Gorgeous hotel lobby is awe inspiring to say the least when you walk in, making you feel as if you're walking into the gold plated interior of a mansion. Service is relatively solid from the staff and all my needs were addressed, complete with a complimentary newspaper at my door. Hotel rooms are small and I had stayed in a single, but enjoyed what the place had to offer. Bathroom is definitely meant for one individual and surprisingly, it's a bathroom that's held up over decades of use as the Drake is kind of a local institution. Now speaking as a guy, I have absolutely no credibility in terms of interior design but I did enjoy the room interior: green and white striped walls that add to a fairly reassuring and comforting feel to the room, which comes with both TV, DVD player and overpriced video rentals. As far the area itself, the Drake is right in San Francisco's Union Square, a tourist mecca full of all the big name retail stores you know: Neiman Marcus, Macy's, Borders, Gap and Victoria's Secret. It also has the convenience of being across the street from a Walgreen's for all your basic needs. But as I said, this is the place for a short stay as opposed to a long one. So if you need groceries, you'll need public transportation to get to a supermarket. But overall, this is a relatively solid hotel and I would highly recommend staying here.

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “loved this hotel!”
text:
we arrived at the adagio after a roadtrip from vegas through santa barbara so we were very weary and tierd. very pleasantly suprised as i dont feel the pictures on the site do the hotel justice. we were met by very helpful and friendly valet and staff .free tea & coffee in the lobby and bottled water was a very nice touch.
our first room was on the 7th floor was fine but was a little on the small side so we asked to switch to a more spacious room
we got a much bigger room on the 8th floor again they were very 
helpful with our request.
loved the rooms very stylish, spotless, bright and airy during the day
rooms could get very warm through the middle of the nite so we had 
to have the ceiling fan on all the time .never used the AC unit at the window as we found it too noisy!
I would reccommend to stay on a high floor as geary street can get very noisy in the early hours.
the bathroom was a little on the small side but ok
I loved the location of this hotel only a few blocks from union square.
I found it very overwhelming and sad the amount of homeless in san fran and some can be quite aggresive. and also how expensive it is compared to other places in the u.s.
having said that san francisco is a beautiful place & we had a wonerful time.

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
title: “Great location, very clean but in need of updating”
text:
Fantastic location but dated.
Welcome to the early 80s, where large open atriums made for an imposing (yet somewhat impersonal) grand entrance. I stayed her for almost a week attending a conference.
The hotel is located in a great spot. You're a two minute walk to the main port in Embarcadero with access to ferries across the Bay and trams out to the world-famous piers. At the front of the hotel, you've got access to cable cars and other transportation options. Was easy to walk around given the central location.
Rooms are fairly large and bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was in need of some updating. Fixtures were worn and wallpaper feeling the impact of age. The room was very quiet (one advantage of an open atrium outside is that you don't hear the doors from your neighbours slam shut in the middle of the night) so good sleep. Room was very clean.
Service was great at reception, though room service was inconsistent. My room wasn't cleaned the day after I arrived (I was out of my room at 630 AM, so no issue with not having access to it). Reception offered a goodwill gesture for the inconvenience and offered to have it serviced (I'm a neat person so it wasn't so much about the room being dirty, but when you're paying a few hundred dollars a night, daily service should be expected!). Daily newspaper delivery was also supposed to be included in my rate. I think of the 5 nights at the hotel, I only received the paper delivered twice (other guests received theirs, so not sure why so inconsistent).
Overall, I'd recommend the hotel for the location and cleanliness. Hyatt should spend some money on updating the bathrooms and wall coverings, but overall a good product.

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Great little boutique hotel smack dab in the center of the business district!”
text: Hip little hotel right in the middle of the business district. Rooms were clean and well appointed. The staff was young and friendly. Don't remember if they had room service or a restaurant on site. After all who wants to eat in their room in San Francisco.

name: The Westin St. Francis
title: “luxuriöse alte Dame der SF Hotels, Traumlage”
text:
Da ich nur für eine Nacht in SF war, buchte ich über Priceline das Westin St Francis. Das Hotel hat unsere Erwartungen übertroffen. Top Lage, schöne, große Zimmer, Traumblick auf den Union Square. das Hotel ist eine San Francisco Institution. Edel wie ein Ozeandampfer im Stil der Queen Elizabeth, mit tollen Lokalen, Bars und Geschäften und zentral im Herzen der Traumstadt San Francisco gelegen. Natürlich gibt es neuere, modernere, hippere Hotels. Aber das Westin hat schon seinen besonderen Reiz.
Praktisch war auch, wie einfach man Zugang zu WLAN bekam. In dieser Hinsicht moderner als so manches Boutique Hotel.

name: Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf Hotel
title: “excellent remodel”
text: The exterior still looks dated but the interior is excellent. They seem to have borrowed some ideas from Aloft Hotels here included a strange, modern, beachy interior color palette. The pool is excellent any time of year and the rooms are bright and cheerful.

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “Nice”
text: Modern style update of an older hotel was a comfortable base for a two night stay in SF. Near Union Square, but at the edge of Tenderloin with its homeless, etc. Friendly, helpful staff. Reasonable alternative to expensive four start chains.

name: Hotel Adagio
title: “love that Adagio”
text:
Loved the location Loved the room Loved the decor
We had a meeting in a beautiful room on the top floor - amazing view - everything was top notch!

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
title: “hotel is fine - tacky location”
text: I was last in SF 20 years ago and loved fisherman's wharf. Returning this year it has turned into a tacky tourist hell hole - there really is nothing appealling about the area though if you want to be surrounded by naff shops, tourist tat and burger restaurants then it could be for you. Granted, it is close to ferries (alcatraz etc) , bike hire, tour buses etc so handy in this respect but I didn't feel comfortable there. The Holiday Inn itself is like any other - clean, efficient and so on but choose your room carefully. This hotel is full of british people on virgin holidays which I didn't like - I wanted to get away from Britain. Unknown to me at booking there are two bulidings, a main one and a satellite called the 'beach' building. It is only staffed in the lobby at peak times which is inconvenient, there is a Dennys in the lobby which stinks the place out and the pool is in the main building which means a 5 minute walk on the main street in your cossie. Get a room looking out onto the courtyard - ours was directly above the main street where trams and taxis woke us up at regular intervals all night - they did move us when we complained. In short - the hotel was fine but its a busy, noisy tourist area so beware.

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Acceptable accommodations”
text:
We booked this room mainly because its free parking. Most hotels in San Fran are charging $30-$50 a night. The room was was tidy, bed was clean, washroom facilities were adequate. 
Staff was incredibly friendly and helpful.
They have a wine tasting in the evening which is pleasant. Free wifi in the rooms and guests have access to computers and printers close to the lobby.. The location was great, close to coffee shops, and little cafe's and bars. Is close to one of the trolley stops. Would recommend this hotel. We were not expecting the ritz. But it was pleasant.

name: CLIFT San Francisco
title: “Impeccable ...”
text:
Nous sommes partis avec nos deux filles à l'hôtel Clift pour débuter notre petit périple en Californie et nous n'avons absolument pas été déçu ! 
Nous étions au 14 ème étage (sur 16) avec une vue magnifique sur San Francisco ... dans une grande chambre pour 4. Etant très sensible aux bruits extérieurs, j'étais un peu inquiète mais la chambre était parfaitement insonorisée ... le mobilier est chic et sobre ... propreté impeccable ... seul petit hic : la salle de bain un peu petite pour 4 mais bon, on y reste pas des heures !
L'accueil et le hall d'entrée sont aussi très agréables ... branché mais juste ce qu'il faut !
J'ai lu des choses négatives sur le quartier ... rien à signaler pour nous. Aucun problème au niveau d'une éventuelle mauvaise fréquentation ... très central et près de tout !
En bref, 3 jours merveilleux dans une ville extraordinaire et très attachante que je vous conseille vivement !
Carole

name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Old but great”
text:
Make no mistake - this is an OLD Hotel and in some areas needs some fairly drastic renovation. With that comment in mind I have to say that I could not fault this hotel in any other respect.
I last stayed at the Sir Francis Drake some 40 years ago and since my memory was a little vague, I contacted David Watkins (he was responding to comments on TripAdvisor at the time) for assistance. His response was quick and most helpful. The arrangements he made for me were marvellous and I am sorry he was not there for me to thank him in person. I had a Queen room in the tower block with a view over Union Square. There was some noise from the nightclub 2 floors above but it was tolerable and did not go too late. The bathroom was, as many have commented, small but it was adequate.
The hotel staff are excellent in the full Kimpton manner. I had stayed a few weeks before at the Pacific Pallisades in Vancouver and my expectations were high. They were met and exceeded. I should particularly mention the doorman, Tom, in his (fake) Beefeater costume. He was extremely helpful both to guests and in fact to any passer-by who stopped to seek directions and advice.
I apologise for getting a window stuck in the open position. which necessitated a call to engineering. Their response was prompt and friendly. However it did illustrate the age of the builing.
I would have no problems staying there again.

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
title: “Hyatt AAA rate good value”
text: the Hyatt Regency is in an awesome location. The AAA rate including breakfast cannot be beat. We had a little mix up. We had requested adjoining bay view rooms on a high floor. When we checked in they did not have note of it but the manager took care of it right away and upgraded us to bay view balcony rooms. My only negative is I am more a fan of smaller boutique hotels.

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
title: “Nice location, but overpriced and in need of an update.”
text:
I stayed here on business and was disappointed from the start. I can't say there was one thing that sank the hotel, but rather they suffered from a thousand small cuts. A few examples:
I was kept waiting at the check-in desk for 10 minutes even though there were three employees behind the desk who were not assisting any guests. In the room, the coffee maker cord was so short that it only worked in one location in the room and the electrical outlet in that location was out of service. They didn't have CNBC or any other business news station on their cable system in the room. I was kept waiting for 15 minutes to talk to the concierge because there was only one person at the concierge desk and he was helping others. Once I spoke to the concierge, they gave me bad directions to Chinatown. The bathroom tub had mold and hairs in it. The window of the room faced a busy street and didn't close securely - thus allowing much street noise into the room. And trust me, San Francisco street noise is pretty serious stuff. The thermostat in the room was probably from the mid-1980's and was not digital, so you couldn't set it to a specific temperature, you could just select "warmer" or "cooler". I chose "cooler" and warm air came out. 
For the price of this place, I would expect one of these things to go wrong, but having to deal with all of them and being harassed by the picketing workers outside was a bit too much.

name: Executive Hotel Vintage Court
title: “Not quite as pretty as the website”
text: I realize that when you get something for a low price it is not always a bargain. This was the case with the Vintage Court hotel. I found the staff to be very nice, but the hotel as a whole left a lot to be desired. After check-in, I proceeded to the elevator. That was the first sign that something was wrong. The smell that emitted from the elevator was quite foul. This smell followed me to my room and when I opened the door to my room it was overwhelming. The room was decorated the same as the picture on the internet, but what you could not see in the picture was the shabbiness of the room. The stains on the blanket, the metal plate over the shower faucet was dangling, the bathroom floor and tub were dirty, and the light fixture in the vanity area that took at least 2 minutes to work. I decided that even though I prepaid for three nights that I was relocating to a new hotel. The next day when I checked out early the desk clerk did not ask me why I was leaving early and in fact told me to contact Expedia to try to get part of my money back. It was as if the desk clerk had been through this before. I think your money would be better spent at a Best Western or Red Roof Inn.

name: Executive Hotel Vintage Court
title: “Liked it!”
text: Ok, so there was left over chinese food left in our fridge from the guest's before (I hope), the valet wasn't really helpful with the luggage, and the Front Desk man was not particularly friendly........However, I liked it. The room was cute, quaint and artsy, the location was really good, and we were really comfortable there. I would stay again. They will also match any internet price if you can back it up. I thought it was a deal!

name: Andrews Hotel
title: “Great friendly hotel”
text: The Andrews Hotel rooms were very small, but nicely decorated & furnished, the cleanilness was excellent. The service was really good & the hotel restaurant superb & very popular with the locals. The free continental breakfast put out on each floor was excellent and the free glass of wine in the bar each evening of you stay was well worth getting back for (served between 5.30 - 6.30). The hotel is a long walk from Fishermans Wharf, but very close to Union Square. The roads are a bit of a killer with them being so steep, but is it not advisable to drive in the city as the parking is very limited. The cable car service is pretty good if you don't fancy walking everywhere. I wore my stepper & on the day we walked over the Golden Gate Bridge we did 41,000 steps (approx 36.8km) so if you like walking it is ideal!! I would definately recommend this hotel to anyone, the room had one of the best showers I have ever used & the bed one of the most comfortable I have slept in.

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
title: “Great family vacation”
text: Came here with siblings, respective spouses, and parents for a relative's wedding. 20 min cab ride to airport, walk to fisherman's wharf and downtown. We upgraded to regency club where we all had breakfast and pre-dinner snacks and drinks. Rooms were gorgeous with big tubs and nice beds. Hotel bar is fun.

name: Executive Hotel Vintage Court
title: “Einfaches Stadthotel mit Charme”
text: Die Lage des Hotels ist wirklich super, direkt um die Ecke ist Chinatown. Bis Downtown ist es auch nur ein Fussweg. Die Zimmer sind ok, aber Haus und Einrichtung sind nicht mehr die jüngsten. Das Personal ist sehr zuvorkommend und sehr freundlich. Wir haben uns wohl gefühlt.

name: Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf Hotel
title: “Great location, but overpriced, and then parking extra!”
text:
I took to work colleagues to Fisherman's Wharf between two projects (on in San Ramon and one in Houston). We stayed at the Sheraton.
Its location is very good, just two blocks away from the touristy areas - far enough to avoid most of the noise, whilst retaining the convenience of exploring on foot.
When we arrived, valet was helpful and parked our car - "included" we were told. The front desk was under-manned, and we had a longish wait to check in. As a Sheraton Gold card holder, I expected to be upgraded, but was not. But my room was nice, with the trademark Sheraton comfortable bed and bedding.
We paid over $200 a night to stay, and the hotel had the audacity to charge another $90 for two days parking. Outrageous - public parking on the same block was $10/day.
Do turn left outside the hotel for breakfast. There are three pavement cafes onthe left - we went to the centre one, and had a great experience. Just past those cafes is the streetcar terminus. It is a must to take this all the way to the other end of the line.
All in all, a nice weekend. But the prices left a bitter aftertaste.

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “A place with character”
text: Comfortable stylish room and great bathroom facilities. The wonderful wine session 5.30 to 6.00 certainly allows a friendly get together for all residents to chat over a glass. A nice touch that others would do well to copy. Hotel location is good but do your homework as to how far things are and in which direction or you could end up in a dodgy district?

name: The Mosser
title: “Best location to visit Moscone Center from”
text: This small but very authentic hotel is located just a 5 minute walk away from Moscone Center. Next to the shopping streets of San Francisco and a 5 minute walk from the cable car starting point. Very helpfull staff. Small rooms but clean and comfortable.

name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
title: “Great location, efficient staff but rooms may need some refit.”
text: We stayed just one night during a family trip. Although we only had very limited time in San Francisco, the location of the hotel helped us spend time effectively. It is very close to major museums and only a short walk to Union Square. BART station is just around the corner. The staff members are of high quality, especially those at the door are very efficient. When we checked out and requested a cab, they made their best effort to find one which would accomodate three suitcases (plus four people). The room was wide enough for four (incl. two kids). It may need some rifit, but is within an acceptable range. The only complaint is that the air-condition is not sensitive enough and thus it gets too dry at night.

name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Nice hotel - no complaints....”
text:
I just came back from a short trip to San Francisco with my sweetie, who had been in San José on business. We chose the Sir Francis Drake for several reasons - the location of the hotel, in the heart of Union Square shopping and dining, as well as a special promotion announced in May on Travelzoo.com (Queen Petite rooms at $99. a night!)
Yes our room was quite small (we were well aware from the pictures on the website) but clean and comfortable.
Nice linens and duvet. Our room was also surprisingly quiet given the busyness of the hotel's location. Excellent base for touring the city.
All in all we were very satisfied with our stay - especially considering the fantastic price.

name: Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf Hotel
title: “Great location, friendly helpful staff, comfortable beds!”
text: My husband and I stayed here for a week's honeymoon after our Vegas wedding a few weeks ago. The receptionist ensured we had a nice room and the bed was really comfortable. The hotel is in a fantastic location and we travelled around this wonderful city using public transport links found near the hotel. The concierge was great and really helpful. The hotel was clean and bright and we would definately stay here again. Thank you Sheraton!

name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Quaint hotel, great locaton”
text:
Loved this charming hotel! I'm a native San Franciscan now living in Las Vegas AND a travel agent for the last 10 years. This was the first time I have done the "touristy" thing in my own hometown as I was a tour guide for about 10 of my friends who have never been to the Bay area.
The Sir Francis Drake is a landmark, perfect location to everythng.
Service was great, rooms were nicely decorated- it was definitely a lovely hotel.
Keep in mind that San Francisco is an old city with OLD buildings, most of the hotels downtown will be a little used and abused, however, they all do try to renovate to give clients nicer amenities without losing the old-fashioned feel of how San Francisco is supposed to be. Old Victorians, one way streets, rolling hills and old world charm- I never thought I would appreciate the history and architecture of San Francisco until I did not live here anymore...
The Sir Francis Drake is the pefect embodiment of what Old San Francisco is supposed to be.
I would stay here again and woud definitely recommend to my clients looking for a boutique hotel in San Francisco.

name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Something different in a great part of town”
text:
Great hotel in a great location for a different take on SF. 
Staff were extremely friendly and helpful. Rooms were spacious and unique. 
It's right next to Japantown Peace Plaza which seems to have regular events, and it's beside the jazz district so plenty of places nearby for live music.
And the surprising high point is that it's just a short walk from trendy Fillmore and Union Streets.

name: Prescott Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “TINY hallways, rooms, elevators... get a better deal at the Westin St Francis!”
text:
Front desk service was impeccable... but for $400/night for Club Level, we were astonished by the Lilliputian size of the elevator and narrow hallways leading to our tiny, tiny room! For the same price, we had a HUGE room at the Westin St Francis with a view of Union Square Park. 
Even at $200/nt we would have thought the Prescott was cramped, and we travel to Europe often, (our expectations are not out of line.)

name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Wonderful and relaxing.”
text:
Wonderful ,,relaxing.............Comfortable and clean................................................
The soaking tub was great! ...............................Truly wonderful to relax and read a nice book ............... .................................... Wish I could have spent more time there!.........................

name: Hotel Vertigo
title: “great vibe”
text: I loved this hotel, it had such a great feel about it and the decor was fabulous! It was located close to everything, and the street itself was full of cute little cafes to get a coffee or bfast.

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Room 3624”
text: One of the best views in the city. You can see golden gate bridge and the entire skyline. This is a great hotel with a great location. If you can try and stay in room 3624 and you won't be disappointed

name: Hotel Del Sol, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “EXCELLENT”
text: Très bon hotel à SF. Chambre propre, personnel très agréable, bonne situation , à 1 rue de Lombard St et des bus. Situation très calme et parking gratuit (assez rare à SF) où à cette periode de l'année nous avons toujours trouvé de la place. Je recommande vivement!!!!

name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
title: “Very handy to everything”
text: We had an unscheduled layover for one night in SFO on account of the weather, so had to find a good hotel. The bed was comfortable, the bathroom was fine, the view was great. Did not try any of the facilities, so the main impression is its handy location to Market St, the cable car, Moscone and the Union Square shops.

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
title: “We always feel cheated”
text:
Because my husband has Gold Passport, we often use Hyatt, and the one in Embarcadero just because it's next to the Ferry Building, but if you must choose Hyatt, the other Hyatt in downtown SF is far superior in every way. Hyatt at Embarcadero is NOT for you, if you value any kind of service. 
My husband usually books our room on Hyatt.com. When he arrives at the check in counter, he hates to be served by Chinese staff, because my husband is of Chinese heritage and his general experience at this Hyatt is that he is treated poorly by fellow Chinese -- like in HK. 
For this weekend trip, because my husband has been very busy, I booked our trip. I purchased flight and hotel together through AA. However, had I purchased them separately, the cost was merely few dollars more at the Hyatt AAA member price. When we checked in, the Asian female staff said that this stay does not count because it was discounted and not through Hyatt.com. WHY ARE THE CUSTOMERS NEVER INFORMED ABOUT THEIR OPTIONS BEFORE WE PURCHASE? I would have had to inconvenience my husband during his busy schedule, but he would have booked through Hyatt.com. Or, in the future, I shall choose to try another non-Hyatt hotel if I can get a competitive vacation package. We have absolutely no reason to stay at Hyatt if there is no Gold Passport advantage; in fact, we have not received any offer for a while that would encourage us to keep patronizing Hyatt! 
And the check in staff always try to charge us extra for any water view. This time, she said that for $40 extra (by the way, the price is different every time, and she did not inform us about the tax and assessment that are charged on top of the "upgrade"), she can put us in a room with great bay view in a much higher floor. During our last visit, my husband got into a big argument match about this "upgrade," and we were too exhausted to bother this time, so we agreed to the upgrade. 
When we entered room 1431, the water was only visible behind the Ferry Building if I stood by the left end of the window and looked out at an angle. The overall view from the room were high rises. We opened the window to look out at the water for which we paid extra, but because of the nasty smell of cigarettes from adjacent rooms, we had to close the window. 
The concierge service is absolutely disappointing, and really night and day from the other Hyatt in downtown SF. The most upsetting part of the interaction is that they do not value the guests' time. They really take their time to figure out for themselves what guests are inquiring. 
The rooms and amenities are pretty standard. This time, the room ran out of toilet paper, and when my husband called for a roll, no one ever came; I got up, changed, went out, and looked for someone with a cleaning cart in the hallway, but I could not find one, so I called this time and offered to go pick one up if no one is available. The woman did not know that no one had yet delivered that toilet paper and insisted that she'll send someone to deliver the toilet paper; a guy finally came with a toilet paper and a box of tissues, which we did not need.

name: Hotel Vertigo
title: “Convenient, Good Value”
text:
Stayed here for five nights while visiting family in the surrounding area. This hotel is convenient to the municipal bus line, neighborhood cafes and grocery shops. Rooms are comfortable with internet access plus a computer and printer in the lobby. Staff was helpful and friendly. We had a petit queen room and it was adequate for two.
Would definitely stay here again.

name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Great Hotel for the money”
text: Hotel Kabuki is nice and clean. We stayed in 4th floor corner room and we love it. The location is great if you are a walker like us, we walked to webster street and have our coffee at Peet's and proceed to the marina and lunch at Fisherman's wharp.

name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Nice hotel and comfortable but that's it.”
text:
Before my husband and I flew to San Francisco, we did a little bit of research on hotels, but as we were in the city for the Metallica Fillmore shows, there was a good rate going for this one and the pcitures we seen looked lovely.
When we got there, we were delighted with the hotel, the lobby area looked nice and we were greeted with a beautiful smelling hotel, however, when we checked into our room (King) we were left very very disappointed. The room was very tired, the carpet worn and it needed a refurb. The room was quite small as well and the balcony area was grotty.
Anyhow, the room was at least clean and the bed comfortable and ideal if you want a comfortable stay. 
It's near a few diners and restaurants so plenty of places for breakfast and dinner. If you don't mind a 20 minute walk to Union Square or the other direction to City Hall, it's in walking distance. It takes a bit longer tio walk to Haight-Ashbury (about 35 minutes). I'm accustomed to walking so I found the hotel accessible and convenient though many took taxis into town but be care late in the evening if you're walking between Union Square and the Kabuki - it's a bit scary with the homeless hanging about - but as long as you're vigilant, it's fine!

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
title: “Disappointed”
text: Although this is in a great location, the cleanliness was not up to par. When we first walked into our room, there were sheets in a pile on the floor, and it appeared it was half cleaned. We were given a new room, but there was a large clump of hair in the shower and stains on the walls and floor. This definitely didn't seem like a 4 star hotel. The bed and pillows were also not comfortable.

name: Hyatt at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great Location”
text:
My husband and I truly enjoyed our stay at this Hyatt. Its location is very convenient to Fishermans Wharf. It seems like the other reviewers have it right. The parking is VERY pricey (but we didn't have a car, so it did not apply to us). A few additional notes:
- On their website they recommend Airport Express as the best way to get there... We want to warn you that this is a CRAZY ride. It is comparable to a roller coaster through the city. It was easy to use and inexpensive, but be prepared for an uncomfortable and sometimes scary experience.
- The pool is located on the third floor which we found strange. Just a heads up if that is where your room is located. It closes at 9 PM (probably to accommodate those sleeping on the third floor.) There were lots of people using the pool and hot tub during our stay and they were both not large enough to accommodate everyone.
- The bathroom does not have a locking door. (Hopefully you are quite comfortable with the person you are staying with.) There is no exhaust fan for privacy or drying out the room either. The shower "door" is a glass panel that only covers half of the shower so the spray goes all over the bathroom. Make sure you have plenty of towels down. It looked like the hotel was going for something ultra modern, but failed to think the space through all the way.
- Knuckles is the restaurant attached and has great food. We ate there twice.
- The internet is not free. However, you can use it at no cost to print your boarding pass.

name: Hyatt at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Eat at the Restaurant, Don't Stay at the Hotel.”
text:
I made a reservation with this hotel, on their company website in early July for a weekend stay in early August. I got an email asking me to check in online, which I did...I show up to the hotel at 2:15. My room wasn't ready-- okay fair enough, their advertised policy is 3pm checkin. I sat and waited an hour (they said they'd call my cell-- which never happened). I check the front desk at 3:30-- my room still isn't available. Mind you, there are tons of people getting checked in in the meantime, getting their keys and going up to their rooms. 
The front desk people were polite, but for some reason they seemed not interested in having me as a customer. They offered no helpful information other than to tell me my room wasn't ready with no estimated time for checking in. No worries-- I won't be back.
The room was clean, but rather drab for the price. The bed was very, very comfortable. The shower was nice and roomy, with good water pressure.
This property is clearly coasting on its location, however-- a shame, since I've stayed at the Marriott, Holiday Inn and Hilton (not at Fisherman's Wharf, though) and gotten way better service. Go to one of these (especially the Marriott, which I've never had a bad experience with) before looking at the Hyatt. Save yourself the potential aggravation.
I ordered room service, which was excellent-- all the food I ate was fantastic -- do visit Hyatt's restaurant, Knuckles, if you are on the Wharf...it is a cheerful, friendly place with great food!

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Great location, comfortable and great price.”
text: Our favorite hotel in SF. Great location and comfortable rooms. I did some research and I got the best price on Westin's website. On Expedia, it was about $100 more per night. The valet parking was expensive, but I guess parking in SF can be expensive. We will stay here again when we visit SF next time.

name: Hotel Vertigo
title: “Fun hotel with Hitchcock theme in great location”
text: We enjoyed our 4 night stay and especially appreciated the value and the location. We found we could walk almost everywhere and enjoyed the many restaurants, shops and even theaters nearby. Wish they would let you see Vertigo in the rooms! They run it continuously at the desk, but don't pipe it into the rooms.

name: Hotel Vertigo
title: “Great hotel at great value”
text: We stayed here for two nights while visiting San Francisco for a wedding. Hotel Vertigo was very well-priced, particularly given the area. The hotel was easily accessible to everywhere we needed to go. It took us only minutes to arrive at each destination. I particularly liked the modern decor, free wireless and high-tech touches like in-room iPod player and flat-screen TV.

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
title: “A Good Place for Us”
text: We stayed at this hotel right after 9/11/01 and remember it being fine for our needs. Returned there Oct. of this year for two nights and again it was just fine for what we were looking for. Contrary to what previous posters have said, we found the staff to be very cordial and accommodating. The room was average but it was clean and had everything we needed -- we were there as tourists to the wharf and didn't spend alot of time in the room so anything fancier/more expensive would have been wasted on us. If we were to return, we'd stay there again.

name: Hotel Diva
title: “Never Again”
text: My husband and I had planned a kid free trip to San Francisco. Unfortunately, we had to change to a more expensive hotel after only one night. We booked the Diva months before our trip, but they put us in a horrible room on the second floor directly above the air conditioning units. The room was damp, the bed was small, and they were stains on the wall. As I have extreme mold allergies we asked to move. They informed us that they only had rooms at the front. My husband and I did not sleep the entire night, even after the front desk provided us with earplugs. The street noise was unbearable. We had planned to sleep in, but men were working on the front of the hotel early in the morning and that made sleeping impossible. We were not informed by either Travelocity or the Diva that the hotel would be undergoing reservations. The second room was nicer than the first, but the beds were uncomfortable and too small for the surrounding frame/bedside tables. We ended up calling around and moving to another hotel. We are hoping that our refund goes through. I cannot express enough how disappointing the Diva was, we spent the rest of our visit trying to recoup the sleep that we didn't get for that entire first night. I would not recommend the Diva to anyone - if you must stay there please request rooms at the back of the hotel. My husband and I are forty - our days of loud hotels and sleepless nights are hopefully behind us.

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
title: “Good hotel/roomy/good service”
text: It's a good hotel in an excellent location in San Francisco. It's right across the street from the Ferry Building which houses fun places to eat, shop and enjoy. The Farmers Market on Saturdays are not to be missed. Hotel location is excellent, service is good, and rooms are roomy. It's a solid chain hotel; nothing to complain about.

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
title: “Bene come previsto. Posizione eccellente”
text:
Soggiornato 3 notti tra il 21/08 e il 24/08, due coppie d'amici in un'unica stanza con 2 queen. Noi ci siamo trovati molto bene. Accoglienza simpatica (siamo in California niente formalità!) e check-in molto veloci.Bagno grande e pulito, per la stanza benchè in 4 (con tanti bagagli per stare 3 settimane) non mi sono sentito affatto soffocato, lo spazio era più che sufficiente,d'altronde è ovvio che se si sta in 4 occorre un minimo di adattamento.Wi-Fi gratuito anche se un po' lento.
Eccellente la posizione. Per S.Francisco bisogna evitare la downtown piena di barboni alla sera. Fishermann al contrario è sempre viva.
Il prezzo può risultare alto,ma per una sistemazione dignitosa in questa zona (ma anche nelle altre cambia poco) difficile trovare meglio, S.Francisco in fatto di alberghi è molto cara.
Colazione non prevista. Parcheggio che può risultare caro per chi ha la macchina,ma non ci sono alternative.

name: Hotel Diva
title: “Perfect”
text: We stayed 4 nights at the Diva. The location was perfect being only 2mins walk from Union Square. Checkin was fast & efficient. The room was clean and comfortable, housekeeping did the room every day, the bathroom area was good we had no complaints at all. The windows (looking at other reviews) were a little dirty but if you go there you'll understand why. The staff were all courteous, helpful and friendly even before we went ! Being in our late 50's/early 60's and having never been to SF before we were a little worried about transport from the airport so we e-mailed the company to ask for advice, the reply was exceptional, they told us who and where to book with on-line and got our holiday off to a great start. The concierge (David) booked us a City/Alcatraz tour with a company called Tower, Fantastic, great day out. The homeless people can be a bit of a pain asking you for money on every corner but if you are sensible and not rude they are harmless enough. All in all we had a pleasant stay at the Diva, loved SF, so all that's left to say is "Great stay Diva and Thank You" !!!!!

name: The Mosser
title: “Great Value in the Mix of it All”
text: I am posting this review for my husband. He has a new job and travels up to San Francisco a few times a month, and often has to spend the night. Since he is working for a start up, he is trying to be cost conscious. The Mosser is conveniently located, right by public transit and the rooms have a nice decor. There are options for shared bath, or private bath. He has done both. He said the shared baths were clean and that there was always one available. Super friendly staff. I hoping that I can go with him on a future trip up to SF so I can experience the Mosser too!

name: Columbus Motor Inn
title: “Cheap and Clean”
text:
We stayed here passing through San Francisco in July 2012. We're used to staying in places more like the Fairmont, so the decor didn't really impress us but you can't beat the price. It was clean and cheap, and the staff were friendly. Hallway was a bit noisy.
Free Wifi and Free Parking.
Great Indian food place across the street. Book there with OpenTable to get points!

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Felt right at home - UK reviewer”
text:
My partner and I took a 15 day trip to California/Nevada incorporating LA, San Fran and Vegas. The Hotel Carlton in San Francisco was our second stop.
This was my first visit to the USA and so I had no previous experience to base this trip upon. I enjoyed LA but after 4 nights I felt ready to move on and we took the short internal flight up the coast to San Francisco - we were not disappointed!
As soon as we arrived at the hotel we were greeted by the front desk as if we were old friends - "We were wondering when you were going to show up" was the greeting, but not delivered with any sarcasm or the over-friendly schmultz that I sometimes feel as a Brit when meeting American's who work in the service industry - it was just really nice and we felt at home straightaway.
The decor of the whole hotel is really interesting. The walls are decorated with pictures and art works from across the globe and the lifts (decked out with a massive world map) were covered in post cards on all sides (I may send one myself from Nottingham and see if they stick it in the lift by the next time we visit). 
Our room was simply beautiful. It was not massive. The television was not huge. It was not palatial by any means... but then whose home is? And this is what the Hotel Carlton felt like - a home, which, when you are travelling to new places, is sometimes exactly what you want!
Our bed was really comfortable and was remade everyday with a yellow and orange cover/pillow combo, which might sound a bit garish, but in actual fact made the room appear really stylishly fitted out and very trendy in contrast to the aqua coloured blinds and fittings. We had a safe in the room which you could program with your own code (a must if you don't want to carry your passport, iPod, traveller’s chqs, etc., everywhere with you). The bathroom was more than ample for our needs and was cleaned daily, with our towels being replaced as often as we left them in the bath for collection.
We came to San Francisco to see the sites (ie: Fisherman's Wharf, Alcatraz, The Golden Gate Bridge, etc.) and so my partner and I have been baffled by the many silly people who seem to come on to tripadvisor to say "the television was too small" or "I didn't like the kettle". Seriously guys, if kettles and televisions are what you get excited about then stay at home and save the money you would have spent on travelling to buy a top of the range TV, toaster, kettle, electric back-scratcher, etc.,etc. Having said the previous, the TV and kettle were both adequate. The kettle boiled water and the tv showed TV shows (what more do you want?!?!? - perhaps less adverts, but that’s an issue for US TV networks and not The Hotel Carlton!)
We arrived at San Fran in Union Square and so this, by our first timer perceptions, always felt like the centre of San Fran. It took us between 20 and 30 minutes to do the walk from Union Square to the hotel (depending on luggage, amount of alcohol drank, etc.) and this was slightly further than I imagined we would be. The walk, as in many places in SF, is rather a hilly one, but as we are both physically fit and able we didn't mind this too much and it also meant that we were away from the majority of noise that SF has to offer. The only sounds I was able to hear in the night were the fog horn on the SF bay and the occasional cop car/fire truck (think there must be a depot somewhere nearby) but the noise was not so much as to become an annoyance and you'll get these sounds in any major city in any country.
The daily wine receptions were one of the reasons that we chose this hotel and these did not disappoint. We always tried to get back to our hotel, or make sure we were just leaving, between 5.30pm and 6pm so that we could enjoy these. Neither of us drinks red so I am unable to comment on it but the white and rose was very, very nice indeed (with the rose being the slightly sweeter of the two). It was a lovely way to end the day by sitting in the foyer and having a glass of wine whilst flicking through one of the many interesting books they had, especially if you'd been on your feet a lot that day! Alternatively, it was a nice way to start the evening if you were going out for a meal. We also got chatting to a few other guests at this time and as people were mingling it just went to enhancing the friendly ambience of the place.
Although a lot of the main attractions and restaurants are located a fair walk away from 
The Carlton there is an excellent but busy (probably due to its excellence) little pub next door called the Fly Bar (if memory serves) which has a great happy hour serving drinks and pizzas fairly inexpensively (check out the local ale “Anchor steam”) and this was useful when we wanted a cheap night away from the centre of SF.
Internet access was available but required a payment after the first free 20 minutes but this was easily avoided by using separate debit/credit cards every time we wanted to log on - and as we only stayed 4 days this never became a problem and we only used the internet quickly to check up on essentials (onward reservations for rental cars, flights, etc.)
All in all we really enjoyed our time in SF. The Hotel Carlton is a home away from home and we loved it. We would heartily recommend it to anyone who really wants to experience San Francisco and enjoy the spirit of this amazing city. The only slight downside is its distance from the Union Square area but we found that the short walk was what allowed us to take in the true atmosphere of the city and to really fall in love with it. At times I was seriously considering the implications of upping sticks from the UK and moving here - I felt so comfortable and knowing we had a place like The Carlton to stay at, I know, played a major part in this perception.
Some tips about sightseeing in SF:
*Find a decent map (ask at the front desk - the one they gave us was exactly what we needed)
*Alcatraz - book online, in advance or take your chances with the queues
*Take a good pair of trainers - you will be doing lots of walking (and the tram is always busy and not that cheap)
*Use "citysight-seeing" for any bus tour made of SF. We used them for LA and really enjoyed it but chose a different firm for our tour of SF and regretted it.(I'm sorry to say I can't recall the name at present - I'll post if I can find the tickets or remember the name)) but whilst we waited for our tour bus for 45 minutes in the Fisherman's Wharf area city sight-seeing buses passed our growing crowd and the clientele looked comfortable. When our bus arrived it was late, overcrowded and some of us had to sit down stairs as we crossed the GG Bridge. (Rubbish service!)
*When the Golden Gate Bridge is clear of fog ...GO! We spent the only clear day on Alcatraz and assumed the day after would be clear for the bridge... it was in the morning, but within 15 minutes thick, thick fog covered it even though it was a sunny day - still go on it even if it is foggy... still worth it!
*Ask Carlton staff for restaurant tips - they know the area.
*Visit the Starlight rooms for a great view of SF
*Take a walk to Chinatown - don't stop at the gate...it only just begins there!
*Clothes shopping around Union Square is great - I 'm a typical bloke who hates clothes shopping, but there are some real bargains to be found in SF so take advantage, especially if you are a UK citizen who is sick of being ripped off by the ludicrous prices we pay at home! (e.g. Levi's jeans $55 = £30. £75 in UK)
Enjoy your trip to San Francisco! If you loved it, and the Hotel Carlton, half as much as we did, it won't be your last visit!

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “Great Holiday”
text: We stayed here for a week in July and were not disappointed. We checked in and were given a junior suite on the 15th floor in Tower 2; there was not a problem with traffic noise in the AM/PM. We were so glad we had a suite, with two women, we were not running into one another and there was plenty of room to move around and store our luggage. The breakfast buffet was fantastic. We "fueled" up every morning before we left to explore the neighborhoods in the city. The location was perfect; very close to public transportation, restaurants and shops. The Cheesecake Factory on the top floor of Macy's was a plus, as was Johnny Foley's Irish Pub two blocks away. We felt safe walking around the city in the day/night. The front desk people were prompt and courteous. The concierges were very helpful. They got us reservations immediately and the directions we were given were precise. Housekeeping was such a pleasure. They satisfied our every whim and always had a smile on their faces. If I ever stay in San Francisco again, I would not hesitate to stay at this Hilton.

name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
title: “Top notch”
text: My conference was at the Masconi (sp) Center and the hotel was walking distance. Rooms were nice but they were a bit pricey. Fitness center was the best I've seen in a hotel. Hotel is conveniently located to Union Square, trolley stops, shopping & restaurants. Overall experience was very good.

name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “VERY NICE HOTEL”
text:
I liked the Kabuki. It's reasonably priced and smack in the middle of Japantown so you're near tons of restaurants, lounges and shops. It's a quiet, low-key neighborhood halfway between the wharf and Market St, largely residential, which may not be your thing.
My king room was good-sized, clean with a nice Japanese motif, a spacious bathroom with both a shower and tub and a sliding door patio (filled with pigeon poo and sometimes noisy pigeons). The bed and variety of pillows made for a good sleep. 
2 quibbles: the cleaning staff is noisy so don''t sleep in past 9am or you'll hear them banging around and talking loudly in the hallway. Also, check your bill: they put a $1/night donation to the Japanese Historical Society automatically on your bill. Not cool. You can get it reversed when you check out but it's tacky of them to tack it on-they should ask your permission at check in!
Still, I liked the place.

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
Hotel Diva
title: “Great location and hotel design!”
text: I stay at the Hotel Diva for 6 nights, good overall experience. The room was clean and comfortable. The location is just great! Less than 5 minutes walk from the Union Square, Shopping Center, Cable Car, Cheesecake Factory and most of the good restaurants. One of a good way to discover the city and the Golden Gate Bridge is to rent a bike, there one rental bike less than 5 minutes walk from the hotel. Great Hotel Design!

name: The Mosser
title: “Very convenient to the convention centers, restaurants, stores, etc.”
text: I liked the furniture , bed and small bathroom as I was only in there in the evening. I was able to have a light breakfast and enjoyed the view of the city streets below. The staff were friendly and accommodating.

name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Zimmer sehr Klein, entsprechen nicht dem Äusseren des Hotels.”
text: Im Dach Restaurant werden Exklusive Partys gefeiert, wo auch Hotelgäste Eintritt bezahlen müssen. Man muss auch darauf achten, das man die gebuchte Zimmerkategorie erhält. Zimmer ohne Safe und Kaffeemaschine nur ein Minibad ( abtrocknen in der Wanne )

name: Hotel Vertigo
title: “Below average”
text:
We stayed in the York hotel for 3 nights at the start of our honeymoon.
We where not very impressed with the standard of the cleanliness room. On arrival we discovered a toenail on the floor, lipstick marks on the sheets, and some of the towels appeared to be stained. We complained & some of the above was sorted out.
The breakfast is a total waste of time, plastic plates & cups, sliced bread & toasters for you to toast the bread in, some fruit, coffee & juice.
On a positive the staff where friendly & helpful. And the room was comfortable, if a little unclean at first.

name: Columbus Motor Inn
title: “Perfectly flat walk to Fisherman's Wharf”
text:
I was most surprised that The Columbus Motor Inn was in a very flat part of San Francisco. I pictured it to be a hilly walk to everything, but it was all flat that we walked in our 2 days there. We had my 76 year old father with us, and a lot of walking hurts his back. This hotel was perfectly located for us, and very reasonably priced with the free parking (we had a rental car.) We had a handicap sticker and parked literally beside the check in desk door. It was so convenient in every way.
Upon arrival we walked a couple of blocks and had dinner at Cioppino's where we had reservations. Lots of restaurants within walking distance.
We stayed in the suite with 2 Queen beds in the main area, and a King bed in a separate bedroom. It only had 1 bathroom, but that was not a problem with 12 and 8 year olds plus grandpa that get baths at night. That allowed the other 3 of us to shower in the morning. The room was MUCH nicer than what I pictured. It was VERY clean and the mattresses were pure white (I always check.) No street noise like I thought, very quiet. 
No free breakfast was the only thing I did not like. We paid quite a bit to eat breakfast in the mornings at different restaurants. (Oh, loved Hollywood Cafe for breakfast, lots of fresh fruit! Also ate at Pat's Cafe, which was also delicious. Great fruit in my oatmeal. Not cheap though for a family of 6) A free breakfast would have been appreciated, like most hotels we stayed at during this 2 week trip starting at Seattle and ending at Phoenix (Grand Canyon.) San Francisco was 5 days into this vacation.
We walked to the trolley, maybe 2 blocks, early in the morning (8:45 maybe?)BEFORE breakfast. The trolley was almost empty at that end of the line and were able to get outside seats. We rode the Powell -Mason line clear to the end, then had to get off the trolley to get in line to ride it back. On the way back it was much more crowded and had people standing in front of us inside. We bought the all day pass from the conductor after we were on board, but shouldn't have. We only rode it that one time back and forth. The lines were just too long later in the day to ride again.
We also walked from the Columbus Motor Inn to the Alcatraz ferry. We had to stop a couple of times for dad to rest, but it was OK taking it slowly for grandpa. If your phone has a GPS app, use it to walk. My husband programmed his phone and it was great, walking all around.
I would stay here again, definitely. Another day in San Fran was needed, 2 wasn't enough!

name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Gutes Hotel”
text: Gutes Hotel in sehr zentraler Lage. Cable Car Station direkt vor der Haustür. Ca. 100 m vom Union Square entfernt. Zentraler geht es kaum noch. Zimmer war ziemlich klein aber völlig ausreichend. Man will ja mehr von der Stadt als vom Hotel sehen. Personal freundlich. Hotel sauber und in gutem Zustand.

name: Columbus Motor Inn
title: “Free parking, close to Fisherman's Wharf”
text:
Stayed at the Columbus Motor Inn for one night after going to a SF Giants game at ATT park. Arrived early at 10:00 and our room was available so we checked in, left our car in the covered parking lot and took the bus which stopped in front of the motel to ATT ballpark. 
Staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was huge with 42in flatscreen TV. We were on the street side and anticipated lots of street noise but it was minimal. Even with the bus stop just outside, it was pretty quiet as the buses are electric trolleys. The sink was separated from the toilet and shower/tub. My only big neg was the bath. Toilet was very close to the door, the room needed a shelf to put clothes and walls and tile was in need of refurbishing. It was clean though, as was the rest of the room. No refrigerator or safe in the room.
Fisherman's Wharf is just a short walk away and the rest of SF easily attainable by the restored tolley F line, cable car, bus or the muni. Free parking is great as other hotels in the area charge $40/day for your car.
It is a 30 minute bus ride to ATT ball park passing through Chinatown and Union Square. The end of the line is the CalTrain station and the ball park is 3 blocks from there.

name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “hotel à faire ou à voir”
text:
Si vous voulez vous faire plaisir à san francisco, hotel à faire absolument. Certes prix élevé mais à peine plus cher que la plupart des hotels autour de Union Square et par contre la grande classe. Prendre une chambre dans les étages élevés, la vue est époustouflante. Hall immense, hauteur de plafond et déco très style Art déco 1930 superbe. Chambre pas immense mais très belle déco également..
A faire le bar night club du 21ème étage qui surplombe la ville.
Restaurant très sympa également le scala's et très bon.
Tout est réussi dans cet hotel.

name: Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf Hotel
title: “Perfect location, good quality”
text:
The best thing about this hotel is its location at San Fransisco's Fisherman's Warf. It is a very nice area with lots to see and do, a must see for the San Fransisco tourist. The hotel rooms are specious and well decorated, room service is of high quality and the pool is quite nice considering that this is a crowded part of the city. 
Parking and Internet access are ATROCIOUSLY EXPENSIVE! The hotel has no place where one can sit down to unwind, the bar is very small and practically inside the reception, it is constantly full with people arriving or leaving.

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “You can do better (elsewhere)!”
text:
Overall, I would not recommend this hotel. We had several problems at it just wasn't worth the hassle. Hotel restaurant seemed popular but we did not try it. 
Parking issues; valet service closes from midnight (even on weekends) to 6 AM. So after paying for parking - there was no place to park the car upon returning from the evening at 12:30 am. The front desk staff was no help. We sat in the car and had to wait for a parking spot to open. Fortunately, after 20-30 minutes, someone left and we were able to secure 1 spot. Anyone who came after us was out of luck. To me, this is unacceptable. 
Hotel temperature: the room heat is controlled by the hotel - you have no individual adjustments. I requested and received a space heater. I imagine this is also an issue for summer. 
Pros: initial check in staff (daytime) was great, location was good. 
Cons: very noisy (paper-thin walls and LOTS of street noise), parking problems, front desk staff (evening) unhelpful, room temperature, lack of towels in the bathroom.

name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
title: “Idealer Ausgangspunkt für Sightseeing”
text: Für europäischen Geschmack is das ganze sehr old fashioned aber wie wir sagen: Zum Schlafen reichts. Frühstück is toll, wenn auch nicht wirklich im Zimmerpreis inbegriffen (20$) Gutschein pro Nacht/Zimmer. Erwartet nicht zu viel aber unterm Strich eine preiswerte Übernachtungsmöglichkeit.

name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
title: “Perfect location”
text:
We spent a week Dec 25-Jan 1 at this hotel. It was , as others have written, perfectly situated. You could not be closer to the Contemporary Jewish Museum or SF MoMA. It is a healthy walk to the Ferry market, which I did several times. Many transit options run along nearby Market St. You can walk to the start of a cable car line. You can cross the street to the excellent Westfield Mall- and its unusual food court below street level.
I agree the Starbucks could be open later hours. I agree the nonsensical snack tray on
the desk should be removed. The business center is somewhat overprices at $.40 a minute for ocmptuer use. The breakfast on the second floor seems slightly overpriced. The health club is excellent.

name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
title: “SF Marriott Marquis tries hard.....”
text: The staff at this hotel deserves high marks for making you feel welcome. At every touch point, they respond with a pleasant word. ( Felt great after flight from east coast.) The hotel itself is fine, but not like the NY Marriott Marquis as someone said in an earlier review. Restaurant choices are limited. The View on the top level of one of the towers is very nice. Two drinks, a glass of wine and two appetizers with tip were $120.00. Breakfast was $52 for two with tip. Buffet was fine, not outstanding. The area around the hotel is not Nob HIll. Unfortunately, there are homeless people are aound the area, so you have to be a little wary. It's also not a pretty area - lots of concrete. The saving grace is a lovely park across the street, as well as good access to transportation and restaurants. Indoor pool and gym very nice. Free intenet in lobby only. For $139 a night, this was a deal. Since this is right by the convention center, check on activity before booking.

name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
title: “Nice hotel, but could use updates in "low tower"”
text: I stayed at this hotel back in June and I was very impressed with the staff in the lobby. My first impression was great. My room was a corner room and it was nice and spacious. However, there was a large iron burn in the middle of the room on the carpet and the light socket blew a fuse the 2nd day. Could use newer style carpet and furniture for the quality and price you pay for the hotel. One word of advice: don't move the water bottles in the refrigerator unless you plan to pay for them. There is a sensor in the fridge that tracks if you take them out, so if you were like me and just moved them out to make room for your own drinks they showed up on my bill. The staff did remove them from my bill after the misunderstanding though.. .

name: Hotel Vertigo
title: “Great Hotel! Stay here!”
text:
Loved The Vertigo! 
Rooms were unique. Hotel was very clean. It's not a 5* hotel but staff was so very helpful. Free wi-fi in the room. Very nice location! Walked to chinatown and Union Square. The only complaint: We were offered a breakfast with our rate and the yogurt was warm. They just had a boxed breakfast sitting in the back room where It should be in the fridge. It's better to go 2 doors down to the breakfast place. It's inexpensive and the food was good. 
I would stay here again in a heartbeat. The men that worked the front desk were the best. They could answer anything and were very helpful. Can't wait to go back someday!

name: Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf Hotel
title: “Dissapointing”
text:
Room was nicely renovated in west coast style and we had a comfortable sleep. This sums up the good things about our stay. The desk hadn't been wiped clean, and there was a sticky section of the carpet. Also, the room had a strong musty smell. The street noise was really loud, and was of course much worse with the window open (so airing out the place was difficult). Had to request towels, and this was not taken care of by time we returned to the room after several hours. Had to call again for service. 
As a Sheraton, I expected a certain higher level of quality, but found this property didn't measure up to others in its class.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great location”
text: After friends told us to stay in union square I am so glad I went with the tuscan inn, even though renovations were occurring. I loved the location. Within walking distance of fishermans wharf. The lobby area is beautiful. The wine reception was great in the lobby, we met many interesting people. The room was small but comfortable and nicely decorated. it was convenient to have a restaurant next door but it was pricey for breakfast which was the only meal we ate there. 4.00 for a glass of orange juice is ridiculous and then I find it for free in the lobby afterwards with champagne! The staff was pleasant and helpful other than the concierge who seemed bothered when we asked her questions. Would definitely stay again

name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Neighborhood & cool perks!”
text: This hotel is in a great neighborhood with easy access to BART to get to other great neighborhoods. Plus it's directly across from the Bay & Ferry Building (bonus)! The rooms are small - trust me - I was even shocked when I got into the room after reading reviews that warned me of the size. BUT - we weren't even in the room much AND it was spotless - maid service was fantastic! The staff is a model for hotels everywhere - all smiles; remembering faces & names - they made us feel like we knew them for many years. The nightly happy hour was my favorite because we met people from all over the country & enjoyed our conversations over drinks. Thanks for a great stay - we will recommend this place to our friends/family & should we return to the West Coast, we will be there again! Can't wait for my next Kimpton stay!

name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “A gem”
text: I fly often to San Francisco, mostly on business. My previous strategy was to use Expedia in order to get the best deal on a random reasonably located hotel in reasonable condition. After sampling a number of hotels that way I've changed my strategy and have settled on the Hotel Kabuki as my go-to location in San Francisco and I now book it directly with the Joie de Vivre chain which is more advantageous than going through a travel bundler. Like other reviewers who like this hotel, I enjoy the Japanese style bathroom with it's soaking tub. I also enjoy other Japanese touches such as the meditation garden, room decor, and tie-in to a nearby spa. It seemed to me that the cleaning people did a more thorough job than at most mid-price hotels. I also was well treated by all staff. As a business traveler, I very much appreciate the free high speed internet -- it's a pet peeve of mine when hotels charge (sometimes outrageous) amounts for that.

name: Hotel Diva
title: “Great to stay with the Stars”
text: Location so close to Union Square was magic. The rooms are small, very functional with cutting edge decor, which we enjoyed. The down side was that they tended to be a bit noisey. Staff were helpful and the rooms very clean the beds were also very comfortable. We would stay here again for the location, and as we were tourists and did not want the facilites of a 5 star hotel (i.e. gyms and resturants) we were happy with the cost saving. The ability to be able to walk anywhere was such a bonus, we would be happy to stay here again. The high speed internet really worked in our room.

name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Good place, great service, 1 hiccup”
text: Beautiful property in the middle of Japan town. Hotel staff was always helpful and pleasant. There was one problem with the final bill; one email to the General Manager and I received a prompt and professional reply that satisfactorily addressed the issue.

name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
title: “Ok, but not great”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights for a conference.
Typical business hotel. Charges extra for internet in the room. 
Everything fairly typical, but no personal attention. Nothing makes you feel "special".

name: Hotel Triton - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Tiny yet very clean room in great location”
text:
My room was extremely tiny but I didn't mind as I didn't spend too much time in it:-)
Great Wine Hour in the funky lobby. Extremely helpful and entertaining staff. 
The hotel is located across the Dragon Gate and surrounded by lots of restaurants and bars. I particularly enjoyed Café de la Presse and Gitane.

name: Columbus Motor Inn
title: “Great deal!”
text:
We spent 3 nights here with our teenage son. It's a basic hotel with no frills. The lobby is very small with only the desk to check in. They have wifi, but no computer for guests. Also no pool or breakfast. But the clean rooms are a decent size and the beds are comfy. They also feature a large flat screen tv. There's a coffeemaker, but no fridge or microwave. I believe you can request a fridge for a fee. We had room 311 which had NO view (just a wall) but I requested a 3rd floor room b/c I wanted something quiet and it was QUIET! This area of Columbus Ave. was pretty quiet, so I imagine a room with a view facing the street would have been ok. 
The staff was friendly and helpful. We mostly talked to Oscar. The hotel is in a great location, between Northbeach and the Wharf, and there are many restaurants in the area. The cable car is just a block or 2 away. We walked or used public transport during our time in San Francisco and that worked very well. The #30 bus stops in front of the hotel and it was very handy! We never took the car out, but the parking was free.
If you're planning on being on the go all day and just need a nice place to sleep, this is the place!

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great location”
text: Great location, clean rooms, free Internet, new flat screen tv. Only downfall is the rooms are not that big, but we didn't spend a whole lot of time in it, so not an issue,

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great hotel, will return!”
text:
Two blocks from Fisherman's Wharf, a great location.Every staff member was personable, and just great, but Keith,the manager, stood out.He really made our stay wonderful, making certain that we had everything we needed.You can tell that Keith is a person who likes people.Beautiful lobby,well-decorated with plump sofas and chairs and fireplace.Very inviting.Rooms were modern,and clean, not even a dot of mildew in the spacious bathroom.Comfortable beds,quite rooms,each with coffeemaker and mini bar.Lovely courtyard view from our room.Concierge service to help you plan your sightseeing,and friendly and helpful porters.There is an airport shuttle service or a town car that you can take to the airport.Ask at the desk.
 Our only complaint was the toiletries... two people in a room, and there was only one small bar of soap at the sink in the bathroom,and one shampoo,one conditioner, in the shower.Another bar of soap should have been in the shower,and two bottles of shampoo and conditioner should have been given.I called the hotel prior to arrival,to ask if lotion was included in the amenities and was told it was, however,it was not in the room.We had to ask at the desk for it.The next day, I had to ask for a second bar of soap and the other things we needed.It would have been nice if the hotel was a bit more generous with these small things that make a difference.
 Overall, we enjoyed our stay and would definately book this hotel on our next trip to San Francisco.

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Felt At Home”
text:
Hotel Cartlon, parked my car, greeted me with not only a smile but a hoot of a concierge, gave us a cute, quiet room, and a phone call to check to see if everything was to our liking. It felt like home. We skipped out early to dinner and missed their complimentary wine, but the lobby was warm and inviting and next time we'll slow down a bit. 
All for around a $100 bucks.

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “A great hotel - would stay here again!”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel Carlton in July 2007 for 7 nights. We were getting married at City Hall in SF and our mothers were staying at the hotel too so we got to see a variety of rooms. On check in we told them why we were in SF and they upgraded us to the top ‘Everest’ floor which has a water cooler and fresh apples in the corridor everyday. Our room wasn’t huge, but we had no need for it to be bigger. As the other reviews state, you can hear your neighbours at times but this only really bothered us on one occasion. Street noise was unnoticeable except for the occasional emergency vehicle siren. Being on the upper floors the views were un-obscured and the windows both had screens, between buildings we could just see the bay. The room was light and airy.
Our mothers were on one of the lower floors and their windows looked out at other buildings which wasn’t exactly pretty and made the room darker. But at the end of the day, it’s not as though our purpose in SF was to spend time in the room looking out of the windows! The sink in my mum’s room got blocked and on notifying the front desk they moved her and upgraded her room to the top floor to make up for the inconvenience.
The reception desk staff were always very helpful, as mentioned in other reviews, especially Theo who always gave great service with a big smile. On our wedding day he arranged for a limo to take us to City Hall (paid for by the hotel) and on our return had placed a cake in a heart made of rose petals and a bottle of wine on the bed. It was so thoughtful and wonderful surprise to finish the day.
We ate breakfast at the hotel restaurant, although found some things to be a little over-spiced for so early in the day. We also had dinner here and everyone in our party enjoyed their meals.
The hotel isn’t perfectly placed for all of the sights, but it really isn’t that difficult to get about using the public transport. I would definitely stay here again and would recommend the hotel to others. My dad stayed at a hotel 2 blocks up the road which was roughly the same price and said that by comparison the Carlton was a much better choice.
We later went on to Las Vegas and stayed in the pyramid at the Luxor. Whilst the room there was bigger than at the Carlton, we found the cleanliness, décor, comfort and particularly the staff at the Luxor, didn’t even compare to the Carlton.

name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
title: “Fantastic”
text:
Great location and service. The concierge, Dan, was particularily helpful. Would return in a heartbeat.
Casey - Vancouver BC

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great location and great place”
text:
We booked this place on a super saver rate and I was a little skeptical of what I might get for that price but it turned out great. We took BART from SFO to Powell, and the cable car from there to the hotel. The Powell/Mason cable car stops within a block of the hotel. The lobby was clean and the staff very professional. We got a room on the internal courtyard and while the room was small it worked out just fine, we didn’t spend much time in the room. The room and bathroom was clean, closet was small. They have an afternoon wine social, but we never made it to that as we had other things on our schedule. 
The things that were important to me were pleasant staff, clean accommodations, good wireless, good location, great price. Tuscan Inn met or exceeded my requirements. If I can get that deal again, I’ll be back soon.

name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel
title: “suprising discovery”
text: We stayed at this hotel by bidding on priceline and we were suspicious at first, due to the price ($100/night for a Saturday), but we were most pleasantly surprised. This hotel is a gem, elegant and understated, located in one of the best areas in San Francisco (close to all the grand and pricey hotels) and in the center of everything. We were upgraded to a room with a view which was super clean, spacious and lovely, the only downside was the street noise (we heard the trams until midnight). A great choice and a real steal for this price!

name: Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf Hotel
title: “Very Mad AT STARWOOD!!”
text:
We were comeing back from sacremento and we wanted to be in a good location for two night's. we got there and becouse of there motel style lobby we went in to the non guest parking and when we got to the lobby they made us pay for non guest parking without giving us the chance to move our car.
