The lobby was very loud too, then the starwood peferd guest check in guy said that are reservation was for july 27 not augest 2, and they wouldnt give us the room, we gave him our recipt and gave us a room. I throught the firepits where for everybody but alot of drunk People took them up and were screaming all night .
NOT A GOOD HOTEL

name: Hotel Triton - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A great place to stay in the heart of San Francisco”
text: We loved staying here and would go back in a heart beat. The location is perfect. Not too far from the shops, the great restaurants and only a 20 minute walk away from Fisherman's Wharf. Having our tarot cards read before going out for a meal was a novel experience. Not many hotels in the world that offer that! All the staff were knowledgable, friendly and kind. They all went out of their way to treat you like a friend that they'd welcomed into their home. Their dining recommendations are worth taking note of too. Our favourites were Scoma in Sausolito, Sears Fine Foods for breakfast and John's steak house in San Francisco.

name: Baldwin Hotel
title: “Very clean, very plain SF Hotel”
text: Always enjoy my visits to San Francisco, the symphony, the ballet, and the museums, are all beautiful! Unfortunately, the hotels are over-priced and the Baldwin is no exception. We got a decent package deal on their website, $280 for two nights including parking, but you have to park the car yourself and it's two blocks away! I've stayed in my fair share of hotels, all around the country, and I have never had to park my car in a lot two blocks away, ridiculous! Now, some positives: rooms and hotel are very clean and it is in a good location. I guess by SF standards, it is good size (around 200 square feet). However, my request for an upper floor room that didn't face the street (as recommended by TA reviewers), was not honored. After checking me into a 3rd floor, street facing room, the gentleman at the hotel desk moved me into a room on the 9th floor, right next to the elevator (901). He said there were no other rooms available, though I saw only two other guests in the hotel during our entire stay. Our street facing room received morning sun, which was nice but our view of the street alley dumpsters, not so nice. The Baldwin rooms are very plain and strangely, the remote control for the tv is glued to a cord on the bedside table which cheapens the entire experience (we are not trustworthy guests?). The water pressure for the shower is poor but housekeeping was excellent and was happy to provide extra pillows for us. I think next time I come to San Francisco for the symphony we'll stay in San Rafael or some other nearby city.

name: The Mosser
title: “location, location, location”
text: The location was absolutely brilliant! You're bang in the middle of everything! The hotel itself was nothing spectacular, not as clean as I would have liked but good enough.The breakfast was pretty much coffee and a cupcake so I'd suggest getting breakfast elsewhere, but if you wanna be right in the middle of the action and particularly the shops! It's a good hotel.

name: The Mosser
title: “Excellent Customer Service from the Reservations Department”
text: I had an untimely situation occur regarding my booking arrangement with the Mosser. I was getting very little help from the internet third party 'book for cheap' customer service department. After much pressing, they got in touch with the hotel and I was able to get exactly the help I needed thanks to MARK from the Mosser in the Reservations department. He was very understanding and extremely helpful. I am very grateful to him. I recommend the Mosser for humanistic and personal customer service.

name: Baldwin Hotel
title: “Excellent value for the location”
text: Overall we had a great stay at the Baldwin Hotel. This hotel is certainly not a luxury hotel but for people who are spending most of their stay out and about in San Francisco this hotel met our needs just fine. While we were there the hotel lobby was under renovation which I think will be a positive improvement. The room itself was a sufficient size and although the bathroom was outdated it was clean and the hot water worked well. The hotel staff was very nice and helpful. The hotel's location is good for accessing everything around Union Square and China Town. Also, the hotel uses key access after 9PM which I thought was a good feature. I would definitely use this hotel again when staying in San Francisco.

name: Baldwin Hotel
title: “Quality Hotel”
text:
Stayed in San Francisco for 3 nights. The hotel was in a perfect location for Union Square and China Town.
The room was spotless with a beautiful bathroom and the AC was perfect. The hotel was going through a refurb at the time in reception but caused no issues. The hotel staff were friendly and happy to help.
Would recommend to anyone staying in San Fran.

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “Great location”
text: I stayed here for business while working on an extended project. The location in Union Square is great and within a few blocks of BART. There are plenty of dining options in Union Square and places for shopping. The room is small, expected in San Francisco, but clean. As a diamond member, I received a coupon for breakfast. I usually upgraded to the buffet because it is one of the better buffet breakfasts of any Hilton. They have steamed salmon, pork buns and other unique delights. This is way beyond the typical scrambled eggs and bacon fare. Service in general in the hotel is friendly. The place gets crowded, so book early.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great location for this walkable city but...”
text: Hotel is located 2 blocks back from the wharf. It's a short walk to many restaurants. I was surprised by the lack of continental breakfast as we've always had this amenity at other Best Westerns- that was a huge minus for us but they do offer a wine reception 5-6 pm. Great- unless you are out sightseeing or on a tour.The staff was friendly and helpful. Rooms are adequate and quiet. There are mini bars in the rooms but the hotel has removed the vending machines (haven't removed the SIGNS for them however) I was told to go to the 7-11. I would not recommend this hotel. The value was just not there for us. Sorry Best Western- I hope you haven't lost my loyalty.

name: Columbus Motor Inn
title: “Very nice, big and clean rooms, great price, great location”
text:
I found this hotel through trip-advisor, and the thing that cought my attention was that most reviews said they were surprised from what they got for that relativelly very-low price. I must agree with those reviews.
It is not the most fancy luxury hotel, but my room was HUGE, a very wide and comfy King-size bed, very large and clean bathroom, big ~40'' LCD TV and even a nice view (i could see a bit of Alckatraz, the tower etc.).
Also, this hotel has free parking, which usually costs about $20-35 in other SF hotels.
I would defenetly come back to this hotel.

name: Hotel Abri
title: “Best Bed Ever!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed in San Fran for 5 nights in July and found a great hotel/flight package through Expedia. The hotel was wonderful overall - amazing location and very cute lobby. It was modern but very welcoming at the same time. Happy hour shots at the front desk from 5-7 which was a nice perk. The restaurant connected to the hotel is horrible - do not eat there. Extremely overpriced and horrible. San Fransisco has some of the most amazing food...most of which is a few blocks away from Hotel Abri. 
Great staff, fantastic bed, huge TV but be warned - they are itty rooms. The suites are three times as large but the regular rooms are quite crammed. The bed and the shower make up for it though. No counter space by the sink in the bathroom which I found odd but was able to accommodate. Overall great stay and positive experience.

name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
title: “Ridiculous Valet/Taxi scam”
text:
Stayed at the Marriott SF for 2 nights and the hotel itself is not bad, nicely updated rooms, good beds and nice plasma TV's in each room, Starbucks in the lobby etc.
Marriott management should be aware that they are doing an incredible disservice to their guests by allowing their valets to operate the racket that they have going on with the Taxis. As another reviewer pointed out (toasty24 review dated 10/27/07) the valets are running a common bribery racket when it comes to the Taxis here (they require the taxis to pay for airport and other fares). It took me about 2 minutes in the taxi line to catch onto this, but it wasn't just limited to so called "airport" fares. If you tip the valets you'll get a taxi right away under the guise of a "reservation" if not you'll stand in line, of course at that point they'll offer you a house car which I'm sure they're also getting kickbacks from. The taxi line takes quite a bit of time and you'll see several empty taxis drive through the valet area that refuse to pay the valets off so the valets will tell you those taxis are off duty and aren't taking any fares. The evening I was in line it was raining and I was wise to their scam so when an empty taxi drove by I said to the valet, "What's wrong, they wouldn't pay?" I then heard one of the valet's coworkers tell him that if he went on break he'd make sure we were still standing there when he got back, and we were at the very front of the line. We eventually got a taxi and we confirmed with our driver that he did indeed pay the valet $5 for the fare, he said airport fares go for 10-15. Marriott management should be aware that these employees are doing a horrible disservice to thier guests by only having the "paying" taxis available to their guests.
Oh, and don't rent a car either, valet parking is $50 a night, which is outrageous no matter what city you're in.

name: Hotel Abri
title: “great staff. small but nice rooms. don't expect the internet to work”
text:
We just returned from a lovely seven day stay at the Hotel Abri. When we arrived we asked for an upgraded room but none were available for two days. We hunkered down in a very small interior room; if we’d been visiting for a few days it would have been sufficient but as we were there for a week there wasn’t even room to open our suitcases. There’s no view from these interior rooms but at least it’s quiet and a good sleep was the priority. They hotel moved us to a new room two days later; strangely it was the exact same room in a different part of the building. There seemed to have been some mix-up regarding why we wanted a new room but they quickly resolved that and relocated us again. From 414 to 404 and finally to room 203 where we stayed for the final 5 days of our trip. 203 is a wheelchair accessible room with plenty of space and afforded us room to open our suitcases and keep them open. 
The staff was fantastic and I’d recommend the hotel for that alone. It’s a small hotel so when you came in after a day of adventure or when you left in the morning you were greeted by familiar faces. 
I appreciate that when renovating the hotel they maintained much of the original infrastructure. The moldings around the doors for example are caked with a century of paint which I think adds to the charm and history of the property. 
The only major issue was the internet. On their website they say it’s complimentary and it was one of the reasons we booked with them; internet should be free in a hotel just as TVs are. Unfortunately after three days of phoning tech support, the front desk, and talking with various staff, the problem was not resolved. Neither my iPhone or iPad would connect to WIFI and having come from Canada I didn’t have 3G service. Thankfully there’s free WIFI that works perfectly a few doors down at the Starbucks. If you’re a business traveler who requires internet often and wants to have it in the comfort of your room rather that in the very public business center (also complimentary) I’d recommend against staying here. I realize that the Abri doesn’t have tech staff and that this area of customer service is contracted out but the people who they’ve contracted need training and need to update their infrastructure. They finally told me that the iPad and iPhone aren’t supported. This seems crazy; both of these devices strictly adhere to wireless standards and moreover, work with every other WIFI hotspot I’ve ever tried. Long story short, the complimentary internet didn’t work as advertised. To be fair, had I brought a computer there is a physical Ethernet port in the room as well which we may have had more success with.
There are so many great places to stay in San Francisco that I would likely try somewhere else on a return visit. The inability to resolve our internet issues in the seven days we were there was a real let down. Internet aside, the staff are lovely, the rooms are clean and well appointed (though tiny), and the place simply has a nice vibe. If the price is right I say book away because more than anything you can’t beat the location.

name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Value”
text: Well-located right along the Embarcadero (an especially good choice for joggers!) Good restuaratns nearby and the ferry to Sausalito is right across the street. Great value for the price. Rooms are not huge, but had everything we needed. Helpful staff and very comfortable beds.

name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
title: “Perfect for a Holiday Spirit boost”
text:
This was the first time I used Priceline. I had looked at Hotwire, and 4 stars were priced at $139-$159, then I looked at regular prices for the Travelodge on Lombard (least expensive hotel I would consider in SF) and got a quote of $86, so I Pricelined for $89 a night, and the SF Marriott said OK. Regular rate on Marriott.com for the room I got was $286 for the nights I booked so I was happy with the rate.
The lobby was in the process of being moved and I found the layout of the hotel a little confusing with three elevator banks, long hallways the had multiple paths to rooms, and exits on 4th street rather than Market or Mission which would seem more logical. Also a little bothersome that they were running blowers to dry the carpets each evening on my floor.
I was given a corner room with ten windows overlooking Market and up Grant to the Chinatown Gate. Plenty of light for a very cloudy week. The heating could have been better, but the room was is great condition. As more days passed the maid service became less well done, but it was acceptable. The lobby staff was great.
As far as the location and the tourist sites, well it is a little off the normal tourist path, but I took the F streetcar from 4th down Market to the Ferry building and then up to Fisherman's Wharf and then the Cable Car back to Powell and Market which was only a block away from the hotel. The buses to other sites were right there so as long as you use public transit there were no difficulties staying here. I bought my bus pass at the Tourist Center and Powell and Market; $24 for 7 days - a bargain. The CityPass is also a great deal if you like art at $54.
I used BART from SFO to the hotel for $5.15 each way. The Powell stop exits on the corner of the hotel.
Cheap eats nearby in the basement food court of Bloomingdale's and at a lot of Union Square places. 
The crowds at Union Square and the cool temps were just what I needed to get into a Silver Bells holiday mood. A great stay, at a great price.

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “If it were just one block closer to Union Square...”
text:
I extended a business trip and stayed the weekend here on HHonors points. My "MyWay" HHonors elite option was for a room upgrade and breakfast. The room upgrade gave us a view room facing west (Twin Peaks) in Tower 1 on the 23rd floor. The breakfast option was a coupon good for a pastry, fruit and beverage at the Starbucks in the lobby. At check-in, I was offered the option to exchange the coupons for a partial credit towards a full breakfast in the restaurant. With all of the other wonderful meals to be had in SF, the Starbucks option was just fine.
The room was a standard Hilton. It was average in size (not large but not cramped). It was in good working order but obviously had a little wear on it. There was a large flat-screen TV with 40-something channels and the majority were in hi-def. The wired internet was so slow to be unusable one night but worked fine the next.
The hotel is located about 3 blocks from Union Square and about the same distance to the Powell St. Muni/Bart station. Unfortunately, it directly abuts the Tenderloin district. This gives it a steady supply of annoying panhandlers in the block in front of the hotel. HINT: If you are headed to Market St. or the Powell St. Bart station, you can exit through the parking garage, which will cut out 1 1/2 blocks of having to deal with the street life.

name: Hotel Triton - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Crazy but cool”
text:
Loved it. The hotel has a great location near Union Square and on the border of China Town. The wacky design inside won't be to everyones taste - but I liked it, and certainly provides a talking point with the lobby staff. The reception staff were chatty and helpful, and the concierge were keen to help us find our way around. 
The room was quite small but very well appointed - the animal printed bath robes were what sold the hotel to me! Just a touch different from the very usual and very boring white fluffy robes. Free tea and coffee in the lobby, wine in the evening, occasional tarot readings, and green apples every day!
I would definitely go back - it has everything I needed and at a very reasonable price too!

name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “dog friendly - great location”
text:
Loved this place - minute I walk in with my bulldog, the manager on duty had her french bulldog greet my dog. 
Rooms are a good size for a boutique hotel ... second time staying here. Great location to the ballpark and to the pier ... just have to walk a little or talk public transportation. 
great value for the money, service is always good ... will stay again.

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Great location!”
text:
A Westin, is a Westin, is a Westin... and I happen to think their beds and linens are comfortable so they are my "go to" chain.
Upon check in it was going to be 48 to park (which I knew) and 15 extra for my "oversized" vehicle (Chevy Tahoe) which I wasnt expecting. ugh! A sweet guy mentioned to me quietly that there was a parking garage right nearby where parking for 24 hours was only $25... perfect. THAT's the kind of help I appreciate! :)
The hotel was comfortable, clean and we had an incredible view of the financial district that my kids got a huge kick out of.
Our room service breakfast wasn't cheap but it hit the spot and their pancakes off the childrens menu got rave reviews from my boys! I love their cofeee and we were all happy.
Upon checkout, they offered to hold my bags until we were finished sightseeing for the day and did it with a smile.
Their $100 rate on travelzoo made this a great bargain... we were out of there for $200 with the room, breakfast and parking... cant do too much better than that in SF for four people in a room. (One mom, three kids.)

name: Hotel Diva
title: “Sympathique à côté du centre ville”
text: Cet hôtel est idéalement situé pour visiter SF, à côté du centre ville et du quartier commerçant, les chambres sont spacieuses, le personnel est sympathique. Le décor est sympathique. On peut juste reprocher le bruit ambiant.

name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel
title: “Excellent stay!”
text: We used our Marriott points to stay here during out trip to San Francisco. We were immediately upgraded for free to a studio suite on the top floor without asking. The view was out of this world. You can see the bay bridge and beautiful skyline. We ordered room service for dinner and breakfast and everything was delicious! The hotel is right next to the fairmont hotel where the rooms cost 5x the amount but you still get the same great location and service for better value! There is a cable car stop right outside the hotel. Such a great and convenient location. The Decor was fresh and modern. The beds were super comfortable. Everything was top notch in my book. Aveda products are used here! Highly recommend this hotel. No negatives!

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Second time and still loving it.”
text: This was our second time at the Tuscan Inn on Fisherman's Wharf. It was just as nice as our first. The staff was wonderful and attentive to our needs and the room, although small, was clean and comfortable. The wine hour from 5 to 6 in the lobby is a bonus for the weary tourist. I would stay there again.

name: Baldwin Hotel
title: “VERY NICE WITH GREAT LOCATION”
text: I was traveling with my daughter and were very pleased with our experience at the Baldwin!We could not have asked for a better location it is very easy to get around in this very nice part of the city.The hotel is located just down from the gates to Chinatown and has lots of great shopping all around with Union Square.We would walk around till 11 at night and found the entire area very busy and lots of things to see and do.The hotel staff is very helpful and we had a wonderful time.I would not hesitate to book with this hotel even though it is older it is very clean and a very comfortable base to explore the city from.Our room was on the ninth floor and we could hear the city noises below like a sax player who played in the evening it sounded wonderful.

name: Hotel Triton - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great location, great staff, comfortable rooms”
text: We loved this hotel. It was a great location to shopping, public trasportation, even walking distance to many places. The staff was very friendly and very helpful. Our door guy, Evan, was very knowledgable and helpful about anything you needed to know.We love the wine hour they had every evening. It was a chance to try great regional wines, and chat with others.The room was what we expected from the website, not fancy but very nice and comfortable.

name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel
title: “Great staff”
text: The location is great and the staff was fantastic -- very accommodating.

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Great home base to explore the city”
text:
Location, location, location applies in real estate and in travel, and this hotel has a perfect location to explore San Francisco. It's right around the corner from the downtown shopping district, Union Square and Chinatown, and my wife and I were able to hoof it to Telegraph Hill, Fisherman's Wharf, Japantown, the Painted Ladies and Lombard Street (though be prepared: this city's huge hills are NO JOKE). Being able to walk everywhere is a blessing, considering the outrageous charge of nearly $50/night to park a car here.
The hotel itself is nothing to write home about, really, but the rooms are adequate and of course have the Heavenly Beds that make Westin worth staying at. The first room they gave us was small and had a terrible view, but we were quickly upgraded when we asked for a better view, and we could see the bay and the sunrise from our next room.
I would recommend this hotel mostly for the location, though if you're expecting something really luxurious for the price you pay, you probably won't get what you're looking for.

name: Baldwin Hotel
title: “Great Location, Great Service, Great Deal”
text: Although we only stay there for a night, it provided us a good experience and memory. Great Location, Great Service, Great Deal. The Towel Orgami - Crab remind us to visit Fisherman's Wharf as our first stop at San Francisco. Love It. Will definitely in our list on next visit.

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “My Favourite Hotel in the World”
text:
Staying at the Carlton could not have been any better for me. It is without a doubt the best hotel I've ever stayed in.
From the moment we arrived, we were treated like kings! The staff, particularly Theo, are the best in the business.
The hotel has a very chic, boutique style and the decor throughout is very modern. The black and white framed photos of scenes around the world in the hotel and the rooms lend a touch of class, not to mention something interesting to look at in the bathroom!
Our room was spacious, light and airy and clean and tidy. We had a corner room which had a double bed which was extremely comfortable. The walk in cupboard was more than enough room for our luggage and our shopping.
The street outside was a little noisy during the night, but that is certainly not the fault of the hotel. There is a fire station nearby, so light sleepers beware. We only ate in the restaurant one morning and whilst the food was to die for, the service was a little slow, as the waitress was by herself. 
It was my birthday during our stay, and unprompted, Theo and his staff surprised me with a birthday cake, birthday card signed by all the staff, balloons, party hats and wine in our room! I was so touched that they had taken the trouble to do this unprompted!
The location of the hotel is excellent, only 3 blocks from Market Street, so good for catching the cable car and a short walk to Union Square.
I cannot recommend this hotel highly enough - I wouldn't want to stay anywhere else but the Carlton in San Francisco!

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Good Value!”
text:
This hotel is great value! I can't believe it is rates only a 2 star?
It has an ethnic charm and the rooms are very clean and decently sized.
If you don't mind walking about six blocks to Union Square?
I also wouldn't walk around alone at night. It can be a bit daunting!

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Great views from a great hotel”
text:
We stayed here 2 nights and were upgraded upon arrival to a room with a great view of the city. We got a great deal over the internet, and it exceeded our expectations. The location is ideal for accessing many of the city's tourist destinations. Park across the street for better rates ($28/day but no in/out privileges). While internet access isn't free through the hotel, there are several open and strong networks that you can use.
A great, casual bar called Dave's right across the street!

name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Loved it!”
text: Stayed 11 nights at the Harbor Court beginning of November, 2007. I loved it. Yes, bedrooms are small but as a single traveller my room was plenty big for me. Bed was so comfortable. Stylish decor. LIked the extra touches like the wine reception and complimentary coffee in the mornings. I found the staff very efficient. I will stay here again on my next visit for sure. The area around the hotel is ecellent - full of upscale restaurants. Very close to Muni/Bart and the streecars which I loved.

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “Massive, impersonal hotel, in a relatively convenient location”
text:
I've stayed here 4-5 times this year alone. First, the good. It's relatively convenient if you want to be in central San Fran. To one side you are only 2 blocks from Union Square, though they other side is the tenderloin district, which is sketchy.
Now the bad. First, if you happen to be in the wrong tower, the rooms are older and stale. and the hallways leave you feeling like you are in an endless, narrow labrynth of some soulless 1990's hotel. Try to get into the main tower (the one with the elevator closer to O'Farrell St. They've updated that tower more recently.
The lobby is absolutely massive, noisy and busy. The line for checking in - if you aren't a HHonors member - can be 20 minutes long. It's everything bad you fear from a gigantic hotel.
The staff is competent, even if a bit curt due to the massive volume of people. My last visit I got the real impression (from more than one person at the front desk) that they were overwhelmed and tired.
I'm a HHonors Diamond member, so they give you some drinks and coupon for continental breakfast for free.
I only stay there because I want to be in a Hilton property and I need something close to Market St. But I know what to expect. A huge impersonal hotel, clean rooms, even if they are a bit small and, depending on the tower you are in, older and a bit dated.

name: Baldwin Hotel
title: “Pleasant Experience”
text: The hotel was in a great location! Close to China town and many shops & restaurants. The hotel seemed clean & the staff was courteous. I arrived early to the hotel and check in time wasn't until 4 so I was able to leave my luggage. This is a good hotel for a good price.

name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “A conseiller pour tous ceux qui recherchent un peu de sérénité dans une grande ville”
text: Le kabuki est situé au coeur de Japantown, à l'écart du centre. Il est idéal pour ceux qui privilégient un type d'hôtellerie différent des traditionnels 4**** américains. L'accueil est chaleureux, le service efficace et professionnel, les chambres spacieuses avec une baignoire de type japonais. Il y a un parking (30 USD par jour) et de nombreux restaurants japonais à quelques pas (je conseille le Sanppo qui propose, en plus des sushis habituels, de nombreux mets japonais moins connus). Petit Business Center permettant de lire ses courriels pour un tarif raisonnable. le quartier est sûr et plaisant, mais il y a malheureusement un peu de trafic à certaines heures... mais parfaitement supportable.

name: Baldwin Hotel
title: “Great location!”
text: A good and affordable hotel with a perfect location near the Chinatown gate. Rooms are quite small but clean and nice. Great value for money.

name: Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf Hotel
title: “Great management staff, but the night wine bar staff has an attitude”
text: We stayed for a total of 4 nights, 2 prior to our cruise and 2 after. The check-in took all of 30 seconds and was a pleasure to deal with. The bell/concierge staff was absolutely the best. The rooms were very well kept and nicely appointed. The only real problem is street noise from the street cars and motorcycles. The hotel is fairly in the center of all attractions of the wharf and is easy walking walking distance from everything. The lady that is in 'Espressi' in the evenings has an attitude that is not in keeping with the rest of the staff. I had a billing question on check out. The manager handled it immediately and without question. Needless to say, when we go back to 'Frisco' we will stay at the Sheraton.

name: Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf Hotel
title: “Great location but need to tell that they are renovating...”
text: Should let you know that they are having renovations when making hotel reservations.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Just okay...but not worth it”
text:
Convenient location, quiet room.
Price is way too high for what it is. Not much relation to other Kimptom properties that i have stayed at and no where near the quality. Service was mediocre, forgettable. Room service was pizza and the worst submarine sandwich I have ever tasted. Breakfast in the attached restaurant was decent (crab-cakes benedict was delicious but service was just meh). 
Don't get excited about their wine hour, 2 buck chuck. I thought that was a joke from other reviewers but it wasn't. 
Parking rates are insane.
Next time I'm in San Francisco I will opt for one of the real Kimptom hotels.

name: The Mosser
title: “Excellent location but maybe a bit small”
text:
Overall it was a very good hotel. The location is central to everything - near to all the transports facilities and shops. Literally 5 minutes from Union Square, where all the main shops and dining places are situated. We realised that alot of places in San Francisco closed at around 9 / 10pm so if you wanted to go somewhere the best place to eat is the Cheesecake factory which closes around 11pm weekdays. Its really lively and always packed. Otherwise if you walk towards the Metreon (Big cinema - which has a Imax screen - excellent) theres a lot of dining places to go after 10pm. Its very safe and lively and very close to the hotel.
Anyways, back to the hotel. The rooms are quite small. Yes it does look like the pictures they advertise, but imagine your own box room - well its about the size of that. We had a Double bedroom and the room was that that and you had a small sink and a separate room for the bath and toilet. Its not very impressive because the first thing you notice is how small it is. Despite this it was very presentable and clean. As its quite cheap and the staff are friendly its generally a nice hotel to stay...but be warned they only have one lift so you may have to use the stairs if you dont want to wait. Another warning is to make sure you have a room with a view. We had to change rooms when we first arrived as our view was facing a brick wall.
Ellie

name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel
title: “Really SUPERB... I mean REALLY. Best hotel experience in years plus FINE dining!”
text:
My wife and I have been coming to San Francisco on our Anniversary since our honeymoon 34 years ago. We have stayed at many hotels in the Bay area. We had not been back to the Stanford Court since its renovation last year. 
We were very pleasantly surprised by the many improvments in decor but more importantly the service and staff were friendly, helpful and the service was the best I have ever experienced.
 The Hotels is located in the heart of everything with ChinaTown, Union Square and North Beach just a short walk from the front door.
The room was spotless, I had some degree of trepidation because of the current outbreak of bedbugs but we expexperienced NO problems whatsoever.
The new restaurant AUREA was not only reasonably priced but the food was superb. I talked with an number of other guests and their experiences were similar. 
On my next trip I will without question eat more of my meals in the hotel as the food at AUREA far surpassed all other dining experiences I had while in San Francisco. 
 I do not hasitate to give the Stanford Court my hearty reccomendation.... and kudos to the staff and management.
Attached is a picture of the view from my hotel room at sunrise... Spectacular

name: Hotel Abri
title: “Perfect Location, Very Comfortable, and affordable”
text:
We stayed at the Monticello Inn for Labor Day weekend. We were 2 couples each with our own room. Upon arrival we were promptly attended to and checked in quickly. Vallet took our vehicle and we headed up to our room. The street it is located on is (Ellis) runs into Powell which is the main street the Trolleys run up and down. This hotel is located in Union Square, your really are in the middle of a great shopping center! Each side you walk you've got shops Adidas, Puma, Bloomingdale's, etc etc! A+ for Location!
Once we entered our room, the only negative thing about this whole expreience was the smell of Freshly baked Subway Bread! Ha ha, I believe because of the way the hotel is built the center subway is one level with it's vents on there roof, there roof is also the first floor of the 5 story or so hotel, so it vents into the shaft of sorts and straight into your a/c unit. Big woop! Seeing as we don't like to hibernate in our room when this city is alive, it didn't bother us one bit, except when you woke up in the morning crazy a sandwhich (he he). 
We reserved a one Bedroom Suite. Upon entering it we were surprised to see how roomy it was. You first enter a living room with a miniature refrigerator, big enough to fit a 2-liter and some can drinks. The Tv is a good sized tv, everything is clean and neat. The couch is comfy as well as the Chair. They have these gorgeous Bay windows with seats built all around it so you can absorb the light if you so choose, cause there isn't much of a view! The bedroom is completley seperate from the living room, there is a door that divides it ( not too common with suites) The decor is exactly as it appears on the website, the stripes look overbearing at first but they are not I assure you! The bed was very comfterble, the sheets where clean. It was very pleasant. The bathroom had a Shower tub Combo, clean as well, no rust or grime build up. This room was a perfect gathering space for us and our friends, seeing as they had gotten a standard room I did look at it and it was very spacious as well. Enjoy the Pictures and the hotel, it is in an incredible location!

name: Hotel Triton - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Another nice stay at the Triton”
text: I've stayed at the Triton off and on for over 10 years. Always had a nice, comfortable stay. Location is outstanding, right at the gate to Chinatown, close to Union Square and Bart stops. Rooms are small but comfortable with nice bathrooms. Lobby is funky but staff is very helpful. And Cafe de la Presse next door has a very nice breakfast menu. Enjoyed the complimentary wine/beer and cookies. All at a nice price. This is an excellent value.

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Very comfortable and pleasant experience”
text: Stayed here for just one night but definitely enjoyed my stay. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful. gave me some great recommendations on places to get food in the area. Had breakfast at the hotel restaurant with my colleague before our meeting. Food was delicious, a bit pricey, but good. Woman in the business center was an absolutel lifesaver! When my laptop wouldn't work she helped me put together my presentation and get everything printed out in time. Loved my room. Very spacious and clean. Super comfy bed. Would stay there again.

name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Elegant Friendly Place”
text: The young and friendly staff of the Harbour Court should give lessons to the staff of other hotels. One genuinely feels welcome and wanted and most of all comfortable immediately upon entering. It's just like everyone says. Fantastic location. Beautiful design. Small but well appointed and luxurious rooms. I especially loved the Aveda bath products and the incredibly soft linens. The view is unparalleled. I went for a self-indulgent weekend for my birthday and left feeling indulged and happy. Thanks Harbor Court!

name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Awesome”
text: I have heard reviews stating small rooms. I guess I got lucky. I had a corner room (610) and it was good sized with HUGE AND COMFY bed. Flat Panel TV, EVERYTHIGN in the bathroom (all Aveda toiletries). FREE Wi-Fi as well as computer and printer to use in Lobby. Free Beer and wine tasting, GREAT location, free newspapers, awesome staff. I would DEFINITELY stay here again and reccomend it to friends.

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “Not quite as expected”
text:
I choose Hiltons expecting a good experience. This time not so much. 
The pricing structure of this hotel and lack of amenties stood out. I was attending a conference and told the conference rate was sold out so had a Deluxe Room at $250. My Deluxe room was a handicap room on the 15th floor facing a desolate city view. Other conference attendees paid the regular rate ($199) and had ocean view. There was no breakfast, coffee, and the business center was a Fed Ex office. No Pool. Most of the staff were courteous but obviously could do nothing to address my concerns. The front desk checkin tried to address by offering a handicap room to my question about what is a deluxe room. Staff appeared stressed and tired to me. 
This Hilton is near the Bart but quite a walk from Conference Center.

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
title: “Nice hotel, for one so large”
text:
What a great property - it's in great shape and the atrium is impressive. If you can, get a room with a balcony facing the harbor - I lucked out.
The staff, when encountered was professional and courteous at every turn. The concierges know all the restaurants and provided two fabulous recommendations while we were there.
The only knocks I give it are the following:
1. the gym is way too small for a hotel with that many rooms. Definitely need bigger.
2. the exhibit and conference space is converted from an old garage, so the ceilings are rather low in those areas.
This hotel serves the Hyatt brand well.

name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
title: “WOW!”
text: Super belle hotel! elle est très bien situer pour tout faire à pied; magasiner, aller au quartier chinois, accès direct pour prendre le tramways pour aller au port. Quand nous sommes arriver à l'aéroport nous avons pris le métro qui nous a conduit à un coin de rue de l'hotel ce qui a coûter $7 sinon avec le taxi ça nous aurait coûter une quarantaine de dollars. La chambre était propre et confortable. et les concierges au front desk était super gentil il nous aidé à réserver pour visiter île d'alcatraz et répondait à toutes nos questions. Bien sur, il est un peu dispendieux mais ça vaut vraiment le coup. Pour terminer si vous y aller n'oublier pas d'aller au bar du dernier étage il y a une vue panoramique sur tout San francisco qui est époustouflante!

name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Harbor Court is Great!”
text: This is a great hotel. The staff is very helpful, the lobby is unique, the room was very quiet and comfortable, it is pet friendly, the wine-tasting is a nice touch. It is convenient to cable cars, buses, and the BART. We had a great week here.

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Great location”
text:
We are glad we stayed at the Westin Market Street for our first stay in San Francisco. The location is perfect as a base to tour the city. We were in walking distance to all the fabulous downtown shopping, restaurants and museums. The service was friendly and helpful at the hotel and our room was lovely. 
I would pick a downtown/Union Square hotel over the Fisherman's Warf location again. Transportation by trolley car or taxi is reasonable and easy to catch in San Francisco. There are so many interesting neighbourhoods that are near the Union Square area to explore. San Francisco is a wonderful city! Do remember to layer dress as the wind can be cool off the bay and the daily temperature was in the 60's when we were there in July.
Love to travel
Edmonton, Alberta, Canada

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text: The Hotel Carlton and it's staff are just wonderful. It is my favorite place to stay and think it is the only place to stay in San Francisco.

name: The Mosser
title: “Muy caro por lo que ofrecen”
text:
La situación del hotel es muy buena. Pero aqui se acaban las ventajas. El hotel es antiguo, las habitaciones pequeñas, los colchones son de tipo inchable y si eres alto tendrás problemas. A mi me toco una habitación en la primera planta que daba en la calle y los cristales no eran dobles con lo que oía mucho ruido.
No lo recomiendo teniendo en cuenta el precio. El desayuno no está incluido.

name: Columbus Motor Inn
title: “Habitacion limpia y amplia. Personal poco cortes”
text: Tras un viaje en coche de mas de 8 horas. Al llegar al hotel en recepción no nos han dado ni las buenas tardes, ni siquiera un "hola", lo primero que nos han dicho es "¿tiene reserva?" ... indicar tambien que al ver que nuestro nivel de ingles no es demasiado fluido, no ha hecho el mas minimo gesto para facilitar el entendimiento. La habitacion es amplia, esta limpia, tiene una cama generosa pero un baño pequeño y algo antiguo.

name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
title: “Okay for a short trip”
text: The Hyatt Regency San Francisco is clearly a dated hotel, but renovations to the rooms have kept it up to par with other mid-level Hyatts (although it may be a bit overpriced). The location is great, right on the Embarcadero and across from the Ferry Terminal. There is also a cable car line right outside the door. We did go through 3 rooms before finding one that was nice, due to awkward window placement in the first rooms. The front desk staff was very kind as well as the concierge. Valet parking was $50/day and the valet threatened that other parking lots were far more expensive. I guess that comes with the territory in San Francisco.

name: Hotel Triton - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Enjoyed our stay!”
text: Funky, fun decor! Great staff! Nice perks! We had a discount on our room, otherwise it may have been a little on the expensive side. The only real negative was that the room had a bit of a smell to it (old building) and the bathroom was nice, but showing a little wear.

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Loved it! What a quality find.”
text:
We booked this hotel for the first few nights of our honeymoon. On booking, they kindly upgraded us to a Kingsize room (but on arrival & check-in didn't actually acknowledge the fact that we were on our honeymoon which would have been nice).
The hotel is beautiful & definately our definiton of a 'boutique hotel' - really nicely decorated rooms and communal areas - an Asian influence, but contemporary & unique. The rooms were really well equipped with comfortable beds, silk cushions, iron, hairdyers, a huge flatscreen TV, fantastic shower and all spotless. 
The wine reception at 5.30pm was a lovely touch and the hotel buzzed at this time - it was nice to have a quiet drink or chat to other guests about their day. The staff were really friendly and professional. I also liked their green credentials and policy towards recycling and laundry.
The hotel is in a great location just minutes walk from the shops & restaurants of Union Square and the cable car stops. It was really easy to pick up a taxi outside and cheap to get anywhere within a few minutes.
We had a great stay and wished evey hotel in California was liked this one - would recommend it to anyone!

name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel
title: “Beautiful hotel, wonderful location”
text: I had the pleasure of staying at the Renaissance for one night with my husband. The rooms are just beautiful, and the Nob Hill area is a great location. We were close to cable car stops, Union Square was a few blocks away and we actually walked to the pier from our hotel. I'd highly recommend!

name: Hotel Abri
title: “No entiendo la calificacion que tiene, es simplemente malo.”
text:
El hotel solo tiene una cosa buena , la ubicación, a dos manzanas de Union Square, que es el centro de San Francisco, rodeado de tiendas , restaurantes, bullicio de gente, tranvía ( cable car ), autobus hop-on hop-off, etc.
Tanto cuando llegamos como cuando partimos del hotel, tuvimos que que meter, subir, bajar y sacar al taxi nuestras maletas ( que en nuestro caso eran cuatro y pesadas porque Frisco era la última etapa de una vuelta al mundo ), ante la indiferencia de varias personal del hotel , entre ellas el portero. En el check-in me comunicaron la buena nueva de que me habian hecho un upgrade de la habitación. este consistía en que en vez de dos camas tenia una cama Queen size, pero la habitación denominada de Luxe era igual de pequeña y el cuarto de baño minúsculo y anticuado y muy poco funcional. El olor del hotel es asqueroso tanto en los pasillos como en las habitaciones, y aunque trataba de paliarlo con la ventilación del aparato de aire acondicionado , lo lograba momentáneamente. Ademas hacia mucho calor dentro de las habitaciones ( finales de noviembre ), y los aparatos de aire acondicionado son de ventana, arcaicos, ruidosos y molestos.
El hotel no tiene restaurante aunque hay uno al lado que debe ser de la misma propiedad.
Tienen una cafetera en el Lobby.La gente del hotel es poco agradable y el servicio es nulo.
La clientela es muy variopinta,y las juergas en las habitaciones suelen ser sonadas. A mi me tocó una noche soportar golpes de puertas, carreras por los pasillos , gritos, etc. desde las 11.00 h. de la noche hasta la 1.30 h. de la madrugada.Los forjados deben ser de papel porque se oyen todos los ruidos, pisadas, taconeos de la habitación de encima, de hecho el hotel es un edificio antiguo remodelado para hotel.
En fin todo un desastre de hotel.
Jamas volveré a ese hotel ni se lo recomendaré a nadie.
Supuestamente es un hotel de encanto o de diseño, no es nada de eso.

name: Hotel Triton - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Have a name? Get the room #. Heck, take the key!”
text: We stayed here last March. The people were nice, but everyone who was working was from another hotel and didn't even know where to buy cigarettes. The rate was good. The room was clean, but way way too small. They allow dogs without a hitch, which is cool. The biggest downside, though, is that they not only gave people my room number without my permission-- but they gave them a key! I came back to my room to find my two friends who I was supposed to meet up with, sitting on my bed. Now, sure-- it was fine this time, but like-- what if they weren't my friends?

name: InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco
title: “Keep coming back”
text: Our 5th stay out of 12 in the area in the past 5 years. While I tried other hotels and was always content, Mark Hopkins always pleasantly surprises and is our favorite place to stay when in San Francisco,

name: Columbus Motor Inn
title: “für SFO super Preis-/Leistungsverhältnis”
text: gute Lage; Personal freundlich; Parken frei und schnuckelige kleine Dachterasse mit Blick auf "die" Brücke. Frühstück einfach aber ausreichend. Internetplatz hart umkämpft. Aufpassen, daß man Zimmer zur Lombard Street bekommt sonst starrt man gegen eine Hauswand und es ist dunkel. Haben gleich en anderes Zimmer bekommen. Rundrum genug Restaurants.Jederzeit wieder!

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Westin Market St. Hotel”
text:
Stay- December 7-9, 2007
2 couples (2 rooms) & 1 Toddler
We had a fantastic experience at the Westin Market Street in San Francisco. 
1. Excellent service- we arrived very early (9:30am) from the airport and just wanted to check our bags but they checked to see if a room was available and one was, so they let us check in. Our other family was arriving later in the day and we checked them in as well as requesting a crib. No problems with this and the crib was exactly what they needed. (No moving sides, though, so if your baby cannot sit or stand up on their own, it might be hard to get them out.) They also requested a fridge to keep the baby's milk cold and it arrived in a timely manner as well. 
2. Location:
The hotel is located just off of Market St. on 3rd. It was a block and a half from the Montgomery BART station and directly on the line for the trolly cars and the #30 bus that took us around town. It was a quick 10-15 minute walk to Union Square and had many restaurants in close vicinity. 
3. Comfort
The legendary beds at the Westin were great! Super comfy pollows and beds. Our bathroom was tiny, but clean and the maid staff was super friendly. A "pod" coffee and tea machine was free in the room and when we asked the maids for more of both tea and coffee, they gave us tons! My husband even liked the shampoo!
Our one issue with the hotel was the mini fridge. They had the normal stocked fridge with the weight sensitive billing process. When we arrived there was an item missing from one of our rooms. We called this down immediately, but it did show up on a bill when we were ready for checkout. When we called the front desk, however, they took care of the problem right away with no fuss.
Overall, this was an EXCELLENT experience and I would definitely try to stay at this hotel again. We got an amazing deal on hotwire. 
Highly recommended.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Love this place........”
text:
Not having stayed in SF for years, I was not prepared for how high hotel rates have become there, but aside from $300/night which we would have had to pay anywhere at the wharf (or more) , this place was perfect. The location and staff are awesome, extremely helpful.
Although there are no views from the rooms, it is a block from the water, muni trans., cable cars, wharf, and about 6 blocks (and an easy F Car ride) from Pier 39. 
I went with two grandsons, ages 8 and 10, and although we tried to stick with all things dungeness at seafood restaurants, we took advantage of the In and Out Burger next door a couple of times, as well as Coldstone Creamery. 
The hotel's own Bistro on the 2nd floor offers quick, delicious, fresh breakfast foods at reasonable prices. Unlike the other Marriott on Columbus a block away, this one at least has complimentary coffee in the a.m. Room has a small fridge.
All in all, we were very satisfied with this property.

name: Cow Hollow Motor Inn and Suites
title: “I travel on business to the Presidio...”
text: I travel on business to the Presidio and have stayed at the Cow Hollow on 3-4 occasions over the past five years. The location is great, but the quality of the place is going downhill a bit. It used to have some kind of simple breakfast (muffins, coffee) if I recall correctly, now there's nothing. The corridors have a strange, unpleasant smell, which I'm sure comes from some sort of cleaning/disinfecting chemical, but smells to me faintly of body odor. The rooms are comfortable and quiet enough, but are dated. The staff was notably unfriendly on my last visit. While they performed their duties adequately, it almost seemed like I was putting them out. It was quite a contrast to what I've experienced at mainstream hotels. Wifi is free and works well enough. I think I'll probably try to find a different place to stay next time, but depending on budget I may be back. The CH is, for the price, a pretty good bargain.

name: Cow Hollow Motor Inn and Suites
title: “Beds are UNCOMFORTABLE”
text:
This dec. trip to Cow Hollow had us tossing and turning all night in the most uncomfortable king bed ever! There was a spring poking me in the back all night and my partner who has a bad back to begin with suffered all night. It was like sleeping in a torture chamber. Will not go back until they get beds that are fit for man. There should be a law against keeping beds beyond their usefulness and inflicting them on unsuspecting guests for which we pay a hefty price. PLEASE GET NEW BEDS!!!!!!! Try sleeping in them yourself. Thank you.
Good place for insomniacs.

name: Palace Hotel
title: “Great location and lovely rooms”
text:
We stayed here for 5 nights in early September. Location is great as you get the BART from the airport direct to the hotel. Come up the exit and there is the hotel door. So good after a long flight from Australia. 
Room we had was a standard room and I asked for a high floor away from street noise and they gave us that which was fantastic. While there was not much of a view it was quiet and that was what we wanted. 
The room size was great. Two beds, large desk, great size TV, good sizw fridge and bathroom also good size and great shower pressure.
I would stay here again for sure. The location to the piers and shops was great. Easy walk to the Wakefield shopping centre and other shops around there.
San Fran is one great city.

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Excellent Place to Stay”
text: My husband and I just returned from a four night stay at the Argent. I was very worried about what we'd find after reading previous reviews. However, the hotel greatly exceeded our expectations. The only visible signs of construction were on the outside of the building. We were given a free upgrade to a room on the 26th floor with amazing views. The staff was very helpful, the room was immaculate, and our room had already been transformed into a Westin-worthy room. Everything was excellent!

name: Redwood Inn
title: “Good value”
text:
Went up to San Francisco over Easter weekend. This was the least expensive reputable place we could find, and it was a great experience. We arrived late at night, and were immediately impressed with the cleanliness of the lobby and friendliness of the staff. We asked for a microwave and fridge in the room, but when we arrived, there was a full kitchenette (oven and all!). The room was a bit old and dated, but not shabby, and it was thoroughly cleaned and restocked every day. The parking was free, which, in San Francisco, is a HUGE plus! Additionally, there was free wi-fi, although the connection was not very high-speed.
The hotel is in a good location. It's maybe two blocks from a bus stop. It's only about four blocks from the "Crookedest Street", but there are STEEP hills, so we opted to drive instead. Someone mentioned stepping over homeless people on the way to and from the hotel, but we came back really late at night several times, and really didn't experience any of that. In addition, we didn't have any problem with noise, but our room was far away from the road.
One thing to keep in mind is that there is tax charged on the room, which was not mentioned when we made our reservations. It was 15% above the quoted rate. We most likely would not have changed our minds about staying had we known, but it would have been good information to have.
Overall, we would definitely recommend the Redwood Inn to any of our friends traveling in the San Francisco area.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “perfect location, comfortable room!”
text: Perfect location, great italian resturant (a little spendy), SUPER concierege. Parking is easier then you might realize. There is a parking ramp across the street that is MUCH cheaper then hotel parking. Really fun happy hour each afternoon with wine and treats. great time to talk to other travelers and find out their favorite things to do in the area. Honestly, San Fran was our favorite trip ever. Can't wait to return.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great Location! Spacious Rooms! Safe!”
text:
My parents and i stayed at this hotel for about a week, and it was pretty mush what we expected from a Marriott hotel. The location was fantastic for it is close not only to Fisherman's Wharf, it was also close to a trolley station and cable car station where you have access to much of the city (check your map -- the trolley and the cable car takes you to two different parts of the city). There are also two car rental places pretty much on the premise (next door to the hotel). We rented at the Avis (the pother one is Hertz) and not only was the price reasonable ($34.00 a day), we were able to return it to the parking lot without any cost (parking can be up to $36.00 a day). There are also various tour companies nearby that can take you anywhere you want -- the concierge at the desk is helpful for these things, Although the hotel Bistro only serves breakfast (it's not bad, but it could be better),there are many places to eat within the hotel area. Breakfast was probably the best at the Denny's a block away located in the Holiday Inn. But as far as restaurants, there are plenty more nearby and it's also two blocks away from Ghirardelli where you can get chocolates and ice cream (as well as food).There are many shops nearby, including a Walgreens just a block away for basic needs (you can also buy souvineers there for a much cheaper price -- this advise was given by a front desk staff). 
The room was very clean and spacious, and very comfortable. I would recommend this hotel and would stay here again for a future trip.

name: The Mosser
title: “Für SF günstig”
text: Die Zimmer sind sehr klein aber sauber u. für die Möglichkeiten auf so wenig Raum recht gut. Das mit dem Bad war nie ein Problem. Auch hier wars sehr sauber. Laut wars gar nicht. Ich kann mir aber vorstellen, dass das zu anderen Zeiten auch anders sein mag.

name: The Mosser
title: “hotel très bon rapport qualité/prix”
text: nous avons passé un excellent séjour, cet hotel est idéalement situé. Proche d'Union square donc des boutiques et de tous les transports (métro, bus, cable-car, trolley-bus...). Les réceptionnistes sont très serviables et le lit était très confortable et malgré la taille de la chambre celle-ci éait charmante. Café et muffins offerts le matin à la reception, idéal pour commencer les journées de balade.

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “Great place to stay”
text:
This hotel is lovely the photos on the website do not do it justice at all. I was really impressed with our checkin it only took about 3 minutes and that was with people queing. Once we arrived in our room it was so large which was great, really clean and such a pleasant hotel. The nicest thing to see was it had tea and coffee making facilities with takeaway cups so we could grab one and be on our way.. which is something of the past in majority of hotels.
The location of this hotel is brilliant just 2 blocks from union sqaure.

name: Hotel Tomo, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Wonderful service”
text: I travel extensively for work and spent 5 days at Hotel Tomo. The staff was spectacular! Very helpful, courteous, and just simply nice. My room was very cute, cheerfully designed and comfortable. I wish I had more business in San Fran just to stay at the hotel. By far the nicest staff that I have met. It reminded me of the wonderful service I received in Japan on another business trip last year. Surprised at the last review by a guest who also stayed in the hotel in May. The decor is anime, not sure what she was expecting but overall it's a lovely, modest, hotel with wonderful staff.

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Gute Lage / gutes Preis-Leistungsverhältnis / in die Jahre gekommen”
text:
Das Hotel Carlton bietet eine gute Preis-Leistung, trotzdem ist der erste Eindruck wenn man in's Zimmer kommt gemischt. Die Zimmer wirken auf den ersten Blick etwas ins Alter gekommen, aberalles in Allem ist es gemütlich und sauber. Einfach nicht so "posh" und "hype" wie andere Hotels. Check in ging super reibungslos und der Service inkl. Beratung über Stadtprogramme sehr gut. 
Nebenan ist eine Bar, wo man sich gut verpflegen kann - es ist aber deswegen im Hotel überhaupt nicht lärmig. Auch gibt's ein gutes Kaffee die Strasse hoch und Einkaufsmöglichkeiten für Lebensmittel gleich um die Ecke. Alles in allem empfehlenswert, wenn man nicht ein Vermögen ausgeben will.

name: Palace Hotel
title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: Spent just one night while visiting my daughter in San Francisco. The staff got us right into a room even though we arrived at 10 AM. It's a beautiful property and the service is excellent. We were upgraded to a Junior Suite and given free breakfast (that one was due to my Starwood status). The Pied Piper Bar is fantastic and the location of the hotel suited us perfectly.

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “Don't Plan a Function There - Worst facility in 23 years of function planning”
text:
Had a function for over 300 attendees. The facility and location is a positive. But so many negatives that it was the worst facility in over 2 decades of planning facilities - based on attendee feedback on the facility:
* $10 per drink?
* $50-$60/night parking
* Changing function layout without discussion or notification
* $90 pp for buffet of simple finger foods and running out of food when the same hotel has all you can eat buffet for $38!
* Unilaterally changed layout of food table to suit their needs but caused a traffic jam for our attendees.
* When event planning staff went to meet with hotel to arrange 500 room nights, charged $14/hr for parking.
* Event entertainment was not comped and cost $73 for 2 hrs.
* Attitude of "let's gouge these folks for everything we can squeeze out of them."
* This was not nickel-and-diming, it was $50-$200-ing us to death.
* I would never plan a function or event there.
Would have been even with the Hilton in Chicago due to their price gouging (prices for rooms are higher at "convention rates" than if you just tell them you are a tourist in town because of the Convention bureau), but the Nikko was a repetitive burr which topped the Hilton Chicago. If you are an event planner or planning a wedding, it was so messed up that it would be cause for being fired or create a divorce. The hotel was notifed and feedback provided.
As a tourist, perhaps it would be ok, but for the price gouging for parking, taxes (all SF), drinks ($10 for wine, $4 for water, really? No really!) The location is good and the lobby area is pleasant. Just don't plan or attend a large function. Oh yes, thanks Hotel Nikko for not telling us the "King Room" that was reserved months in advance is actually 4-6 feet smaller than the regular rooms. We put up with it but it was very apparent that we were cramped more than most hotels, especially for $200. I've stayed at other hotels in SF for $150 that were a better value.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Okay...”
text: The fact that I have to pay $45 for overnight parking is outrageous. I know it's pretty customary for the area, but $45? Does it need to be that much, just because everyone else does it? The room smelled like someone had been smoking in it. The morning 'breakfast'you get would be nice if they had more than one machine to make for the 50+ people they had wanting breakfast. This place needed to be more than average for $200 a night.

name: Redwood Inn
title: “Perfect stay in redwood inn san francisco”
text:
We are guests from Spain and we stayed here for 4 days in redwood inn motel. 
we really enjoyed our stay in this motel. the room is clean, very comfortable, the location is very good. 
It is very close to the main attractions in the city. The manager and the staff are really friendly and helpful. 
we recomend this motel to everybody who visit san francisco.

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Wasted Potential”
text:
The Argent is potential wasted. Rates are usually good but everything else is downhill. Having stayed here 4 times I must say the hotel has issues. If it is full forget getting breakfast, it took us over 1 hour in the restaurant. Rooms can be very nice but once I found rotting food under the bed, once I found dirt everywhere and once my room was triangular/tiny and most uncomfortable. 
The Front desk staff are useless and expect issues checking in and there is no hope they will solve problems. On the brighter side common areas are lovely, some rooms are great and the bar is nice.

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “Nice Hotel, Great Location”
text:
This was our first stop on a three week visit to California. The hotel is really nice and clean, but it's location is the best thing going for it. Just minutes to Union Square so it's ideal for a trip to San Francisco for first time visitors like we were. 
Check in was quick and the receptionist was nice. We were offered an upgraded room for an extra $20 per night which we availed of. The room was nice but quite small so we wondered what our original room would have been like if this was bigger like we were told! 
Our travel itinerary was marked with honeymoon couple, which we were!, so we were presented with a small box of chocolates as we left reception. A nice touch!
We did not eat in the hotel at any stage so we cannot comment on that. 
As another reviewer said the hotel is a little bit soul-less....I would agree with that!
If I were to visit San Francisco again I would probably not stay here unless I got a really good deal. 
The concierge was helpful as we were allowed leave our bags on check out for a couple of hours without charge before we left. 
For anybody flying into San Francisco and leaving by car the hotel is located very close to alot of car rental companies like Hertz, Dollar, Avis etc. They are all located literally half a block away so this proved very convenient for us as picking up our rental car.

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Nice Hotel”
text: We stayed here in January 2003. Great location. The lobby and bar decor was luxurious and contemporary. We found the staff to be very helpful and friendly. The furnishings in the room were nice and we had a great view from 14th floor. The only complaint we had was that the hallway noise carried into our room in the morning (between 6am-10am) due to housekeeping, room service, newspaper delivery and other guest. We enjoyed our stay and would recommend this hotel.

name: Radisson Hotel Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Average Hotel - Friendly staff - Hotel a bit old fashioned inside”
text:
Great location.
Very friendly and helpful desk staff. 
Lifts and hotel corridors pretty old fashioned and a bit run down if I'm honest.
Room was clean - but again could have done with a re-vamp. 
Air conditioning took ages to kick in - so some nights were quite unbearable. 
Quite noisy outside - as the cablecars go past quite early. 
Literally a few minutes walk to the piers - plenty of restuarants about. 
Takes about 15minutes by cab to get to the Golden Gate Bridge - about $17 in a cab. Hard to get a cab back though. 
The pier to get to Alcatraz was about a 10 minute walk ... so great for location. 
Lots of street acts - some of which were quite funny. 
Pier 39 had lots going on - was really nice. Pier 39 is pretty much opposite the front of this hotel. 
Plenty going on - Hotel served its purpose. Wasnt anything luxurious though. 
Pretty basic. But great for location.

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Gutes Hotel in Top Lage”
text: Das Hotel liegt in Top Lage mitten in San Francisco. Die Zimmer sind sehr gepflegt und das Personal ist freundlich. Das Fitness Angebot ist in Ordnung. Leider gibt es keinen Pool. Das Essen ist in Ordnung, aber nichts besonderes. Das Preis Leistungs Verhältnis ist nicht mehr als ok. Generell eher als Business Hotel einzuordnen.

name: InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco
title: “Fabulous location”
text:
Great hotel set in a prime location at the top of Nob Hill in San Francisco.
A short walk from the Grace Cathedral and Chinatown and a trolleybus ride to Pier 39.
Taxis as cheap as the buses so easy to get everywhere.
Staff were excellent and the breakfast from the Top of the Mark restaurant was really good with fantastic views including the Golden Gate Bridge.
What more could one wish for to start a holiday?

name: Hotel Tomo, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Too Many Problems”
text:
We love the location of this hotel, but when we stayed there recently we had no hot water one morning and the A/C was not working during our stay.
The lovely lady who manages the front desk apologized profusely and made an adjustment on our bill, but the physical plant of this aging facility needs to be overhauled.

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “Great Location, Good service”
text:
Hotel Nikko is in a great location to explore the delights of San Francisco, with Union Square on the doorstep and the cable car just down the road ( you can buy your one or seven day passport at the kiosk at the turnaround station on Powell and Market st five minutes away.)
The hotel itself is outstanding. The service was impeccable, with any queries dealt with immediately in a courteous and caring way. The buffet breakfast is excellent with a huge choice and the service was also very good. The swimming and health facilities were exceptionally clean and well maintained. WiFi access is available for $31.95 for three days or use the free access in the Starbucks which is attached to the hotel.
The rooms are a good size - my only negative point was the lack of a bedside lamp or switch to turn off the main light which meant I had to go back to the entrance to turn the light off and walk back to bed in the dark - a little odd! Although my colleague did have one in her room so maybe it was just room 1730 ( I did ask if I could have one but nothing materialised). However apart from that it was a very comfortable stay. Top marks for Hotel Nikko and its staff.

name: Cow Hollow Motor Inn and Suites
title: “Older hotel, but very well kept up; super location!”
text: Have stayed at other similar type hotels in the Marina, but Cow Hollow has the best/biggest/easiest free parking area of any and in SF, that is a BIG PLUS! Obviously an older hotel, but everything seems clean and fairly new. Online rate, when the web site works, is very good (I paid $79). Comfy beds, great views out the windows if you take Lombard side--but be wary, the street is busy and noise may be a problem if you are a light sleeper. TV advertised 80+ channels, but only 50 or so came in--but one doesn't go to SF to watch TV. Fairly quiet concerning the other rooms, some bathroom noise in the bathroom, but that seems common to all hotels. One block from great shopping/eating/movies area on Chestnut Street. Also Mel's Diner right across the street on Lombard. This will now be my #1 hotel to stay at in the Marina.

name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Hotel chaleureux et très agréable”
text: Cet hotel est très bien placé dans San Francisco, à 10mns à pied d'Union Square. Chambres de taille moyenne mais joliment décorées et possedant tout le confort habituel ( télé, cafetière, seche cheveux...), salle de bain pas très grande non plus mais très propre et fonctionnelle, grand dressing pour mettre les valises. Service excellent ( portier, réservation taxis ...) personnel très agréable et parlant français à l'accueil. Une sympathique dégustation de vins locaux avait lieu tous les soirs à 17h30 ! Egalement excellent restaurant. Bref un hotel que je recommande chaudement !

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “Good Value and Experience”
text:
We chose the Nikko primarily for its central location to Union Square, and as home base for my family's first trip to San Francisco. I've been to the city many, many times and stayed in many of its beautiful (and sometimes not so beautiful) hotels. My main goal for my family was to be out and about in the city, so time spent in the hotel itself wasn't a priority. That said, I wanted a clean, comfortable and somewhat upscale and vibrant hotel experience for my wife, and kids (13 and 10), something that reflected the city's unique and wonderful energy. Also, I vetted hotels that had an indoor pool, as that is often the key to a relaxing vacation with kids. The Nikko didn't fail to deliver on those expectations, especially at its price point - a great value as it turned out. 
Perfectly central location aside, the rooms were mostly clean and minimalist in the japanese tradition, with nice upscale touches including a small tv screen within the bathroom mirror. We were upgraded to the club level (I requested available upgrades upon check-in), so we had very nice views of the city in a ceiling to floor window. 
The hotel's amenities and staff were excellent. The lobby is very open and airy, and feels bustling with good energy. Upon check-in, the concierge walked over and offered our kids a week-long scavenger hunt to participate in. 
On our first night, my wife and I let the kids watch a movie in the room while we walked downstairs to have a drink. At first we walked into the jazz club bar (adjacent to an actual, apparently well respected jazz venue), and while not really our scene, seemed to have a lively and energetic crowd. Instead, we opted for the restaurant bar upstairs, which offered a 180 degree difference in mood and atmosphere - quieter, more romantic, which was exactly what we hoped for. Our waitress was excellent and we ended up talking about a variety of subjects from wine to favorite hidden spots in SF to love of baseball.
The indoor pool and exercise facility are a bit dated, but still clean and airy and provided exactly the moments of respite that seem pretty necessary when traveling with a family of four. 
The only other very minor complaints I had were with some of the smaller room details - too many flourescent lights, a bathroom just a tad too spartan for my tastes. But I've stayed in hundreds of hotel rooms from twenty years of international travel, so I tend to be ultra picky about such things. Overall, our experience was very good and we'd easily recommend the hotel to families looking for a similar experience.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Simple & basic, overpriced”
text:
Nicely located, clean, simple hotel. Although we arrived after 3pm, rooms were not ready and we were asked to wait. We had 2 rooms, both were clean and ok, but strangely set up (when opening bathroom door you block passage to room's door) and sparstly equiped (not enough hangers, towels, etc.).
Don't think it deserves 4*, 3* more like it,

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great stay”
text:
We stayed for three nights,our room was on the fourth floor and adequately big enough for the three of us, my husband and adult daughter.The staff were friendly and helpful,it was a good base from which to explore San Francisco.
We took an evening Alcatraz tour and a City tour with Shuttle tours which I would recommend if you have limited time in town.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Noisy and small rooms”
text: Hotel is in a good location with Fisherman's Wharf on your doorstep. Ask for a room facing inwards because the others are very noisy. The rooms at very small. From the photos the mini suites look like they can comfortable sleep 4 but they are too small. The sleeper couch couldn't even fold out. After moving the beds around a bit we managed to fold it out. It was disgusting and we couldn't use it. We needed to hire an extra room for the next nights we were there. The manager was very helpful in accommodating us with an extra room at a lower price. Breakfasts were very crowded if you don't get there very early. The Internet in the rooms didn't work, you needed to go to the lobby.

name: Redwood Inn
title: “A decent hotel in a good location”
text: My husband stayed here with two other couples for a long weekend at the beginning of June. We had called in advance to request rooms away from the main road within close proximity of each other. Upon arrival the individual working at the front desk told us that he had no clue what we were talking about when we mentioned these arrangements. This was frustrating but not the end of the world. The rooms were clean and not too noisy even though we had a window facing the street. The hotel was also in a great location on Lombard street. We were able to walk to almost any place we wanted to go. They also had fresh donuts every morning which was a big hit with the guys. A good stay overall.

name: Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf Hotel
title: “Sheraton Fisherrman's Wharf, San francisco”
text: Hôtel très bien situé, à 5mn à pied du Pier 39. Malheureusement excessivement BRUYANT ! Bruit de la rue, des chambres voisines... Grosse structure. Parking hors de prix, 45USD + taxes par jour+ tip valet parking !

name: The Mosser
title: “Super Lage, prima Parkservice”
text: Sehr zentral in Sichtweite der Market-Street gelegen, sowohl zu Fuss als auch mit Bus/Tram/BART kommt man überall hin. Der Parkservice (Valet, ca. 15 Minuten Vorlaufzeit) funktioniert einwandfrei und ist im Vergleich zum Selbstparken bequem und günstig. Schöne Zimmer mit Sitzflächen vor den Fenstern. Ein paar Schwächen im Detail sind das kaum ins Zimmer reichende Wifi, sowie die relativ belebte und damit laute 4th Avenue, das fehlkonstruierte Waschbecken sowie die jeweils erst nach mehreren Anläufen funktionierende Zimmerzugangskarte.

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Mixed Experience”
text:
I stayed at the hotel recently for 5 nights so got a good dose of a highly variable experience. 
THE GOOD
