The Heavenly Bed is heavenly. It's not that these beds are overtly super-comfortable or luxurious; it's just that I effortlessly went to sleep without once thinking about it. Almost like freakin magic. Amazing.
The gym is decent. Not amazing but better than average. The running machines need better maintenance.
The restaurant for b'fast is also decent and above average for the price point.
THE BAD
I had an order from Amazon.com shipped to the hotel which Amazon split into 3 deliveries. The hotel had the audacity to charge me $15 for each small box or $45 to receive $30 in CD's! Absolutely criminal if you ask me. The concierge refused to reduce the charge to one $15 delivery fee which is bad enough. 
In addition, they charged me for $29 in minibar charges when I had exactly $0 worth of items.
Worst, they charged me twice on the same day for Internet access and refused to deduct one of the two charges.
The Heavenly Shower is not bad but an overengineered gimmick. They'd be better off with rainshower heads in my personal opinion.
OVERALL
The hotel is good looking and has a pretty good position in town. The staff are unacceptably rude for a hotel of this cost and class. Put simply, there are plenty of better options not far away. I have no plans on returning but hopefully they will improve with time.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Really nice hotel”
text: Stayed there for only one night in october. Big and nice reception and a great comfy room and the breakfast was good for US standard! Couple of blocks from Fisherman's wharf....the hotel is right on the spot!

name: Palace Hotel
title: “Great Experience”
text:
We stayed here for one night in November and were very pleased with our experience. The room was nicely decorated and very clean. With high ceilings, nice decor and very large windows, the room lived up to our expectations of the Palace Hotel.
We went for a swim in the indoor pool and a dip in the spa. The pool area was rather crowded, but there's nothing you can do about that, so we made the best of it and appreciated being able to swim in a huge indoor pool in the middle of San Francisco. It was a treat.
We live in the Bay Area, but had been wanting to try this hotel and we were not disappointed.

name: Radisson Hotel Fisherman's Wharf
title: “great location”
text:
This hotel is situated in the perfect spot for people who like to spend time around pier 39, just a few minutes walk to shops, restaurants etc. 
Hotel staff were freindly and helpful and the rooms were clean and tidy, not outdated as some people mention. There were 3 of us in 1 room and plently of space for the short times we were in the room. Only downfall was that it looked straight out onto the car park but we didnt get any noise and just kept the net curtains closed and it was fine. 
Would definately stay in this hotel again and much prefer this location to the union sq area where i stayed on a previous visit to San Fran.

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “Great Hotel, Perfect Location- central to everything!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel as a recommendation from my coworker. I read alot of reviews about the boutique hotels in San Fran and personally I didn't want to run into issues with room temp, water not working, or dinginess. Hotel Nikko was beautiful. The rooms were comfortable (had a double) and the bathroom was actually really nice and big. Concierge outside was awesome in getting us taxis. The lounge, Anzu, was pretty cool... decent, kind of quiet when i went but I had a cucumber martini after a long day and it was great! The location was prime as the Powell St trolley is a block away, taxis everywhere, and the shops of Union Square are ALL around you. The cons is Union Square has alot of homeless people; they werent an issue but its sad to see so many.
If you want to read my experience at San Fran and see pics of the places I visited and ate at please read my blog at www.smileclickkeep.blogspot.com. My Day 1 included North Beach, Pier 39, Ghirardelli Square, and more! 
Hope you found this helpful! :)

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “4 Night stay at Tuscany Inn Fisherman's Wharf”
text:
We had not been to San Francisco previously, so selecting a hotel in the right location and at a moderate price was a bit of a guess. On arrival at the airport we discovered that you can pick up a shuttle bus that will take you to any hotel for $15.00/16.00 per head, and you don't need to book in advance.
If you are a tourist the Tuscany Inn was certainly in the right location, as it is very near to Pier 39, and also tramcars and trolley buses are close by if you want to go downtown. 
We were allocated a 'smokers' queen room at the Hotel on arrival, but asked for a non smoking room, which was readily granted. The ground floor room was quite small but comfortable and clean and tidy, and it looked onto a certral courtyard. The ensuite facilities were provided with fresh towels daily.
Reception desk staff were friendly and helpful, and a welcome drink was provided at 6pm each evening. The reception area is small but comfortable enough for sitting around.
We were not too inpressed with the restaurant attached to the hotel. The menu was fairly limited, staff were not super friendly, and it seemed to us to be a bit over priced for what was on offer. Breakfast was not included in the room price, but guests can get a 15% discount we discovered by chance, but you have to ask!
All in all we had a pleasant stay here

name: Serrano Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Kimpton service and individuality”
text: Stayed for 2 nights 9/28-9/30 on a pleasure trip. Convenient location off Union Square, neighborhood a bit dodgy at night but nothing unusual for a big city. Very close to Powell Street BART/MUNI stop. Hotel is nicely renovated and has a lot of character, which I prefer over a cookie-cutter chain hotel. Goldfish in the lobby! I arrived late on the 28th and the night auditor checked me in; he seemed a bit surly but he was quick, efficient, and explained the hotel's amenities and services. Comfortable bed, nice desk, attractive decor. I enjoyed being able to control the temperature. Small bathroom, but nice C.O. Bigelow amenities. Bathroom was fully stocked with cotton balls, q-tips, plenty of towels. Would stay here again.

name: Phoenix Hotel, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Unique, Funky, and Comfortable”
text: Recently stayed at The Phoenix after two weeks of traveling the coast of CA. Was recommended from my cuz and the price seemed very fair for SF. The courtyard really sets the mood for your stay. With different sculpters, meditation huts, and the heated number 9 pool. Which I reccomend swimming in after the sun has set. The room provided just what we needed from a convience and comfort standpoint. The room also had it's Phoenix touch, with colorful and stimulating decore. It was the pefect way to end our trip and I look forward to my next trip to SF and another stay at The Phoenix.

name: Palace Hotel
title: “Just had the brunch!”
text: Went here for New Years Day champagne brunch. There is a whole huge room just for the food. It's delicious, and the champagne keeps coming. Totally worth the $90 for a wonderful, filling, classy experience.

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “good location, wide rooms”
text:
Location is really good, close to Powell Station, where you can easily get on the Cable. You can walk to Pier 39 in less than 40 minutes. The hotel is clean, has got really big rooms (my experience with my wife and four kids sharing two rooms was excellent). No noise at all. Very good Gym, SPA, and swimming pool (SPA is too hot...).
Downstairs you can have your breakfast at Sturbucks...

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Nice place!”
text: We stayed at the Tuscan for the last two nights of our holiday following our return from Las Vegas. Having spent the first week in a hotel closer to Union Square we had decided to be nearer to Fishermans Wharf. It was a good decision and we were not disappointed with the hotel. Very conveniently situated just a couple of blocks from Fisherman's Wharf. The hotel was very welcoming and efficient and the room comfortable and beautifully presented. Unfortunately the room looked out onto another building, but it was at least quiet and we didn't spend much time there. The bed was extremely comfortable. The wine tasting session in the early evening was a nice touch and extremely popular and the complementary tea and coffee in the morning was appreciated too. I wouldn't hesitate to stay at the Tuscan again!

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great location, service and beer.”
text:
Hello, and thank you for reading.
My wife and I stayed at the Tuscan Inn on June 4-7th, 2006 and really enjoyed the hotel. We agree with the others who have written: "This does not feel like a Best Western."
The interior has a luxuorius feel and our room was clean and well decorated. Although the parking charge is steep, it seems to be the market price in San Francisco, (or as the locals like to call it: Frisco. Just kidding, they HATE the nickanme: Frisco.)
Being the lushes that we are, my wife and I took full advantage of the free happy hour, arriving promptly at five, and not leaving until six. The bartenders were always very friendly and never gave us a hard time about our repeated trips for refills.
Probably the best feature of the Tuscan Inn is its location. With a very short 2 block walk, you are in the heart of Fisherman's Wharf. Renting bikes and riding them over the Golden Gate bridge is especially fun. Around the corner from the hotel, the trolley ride is beautiful.
Last words: stay here. You could go downtown and stay in a fancy high rise, but you could do that in any city. Get the Frisco experience and stay at the Tuscan Inn.

name: Westin San Francisco Market Street
title: “Comodo ed efficiente”
text: Il Westin Market Street hotel è molto comodo, molto efficiente, molto downtown. E' perfetto per muoversi partendo dal centro di San Francisco per raggiungere più o meno ogni zona utile. Vicino a Chinatown, non distante, con una buona passeggiata, dal "lungomare" dei moli, a due passi dalla zona dello shopping cittadino. La struttura è ampia e comoda, ottima ma non economicissima la prima colazione (intorno ai 25 dollari), letti ampi e comodi, un mare di cuscini, servizio cortese e disponibile.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great location, a bit expensive for a holiday inn express”
text: For a hotel in the heart of fisherman's wharf, you cannot really beat the value and the short walking distance to the big sites. I found it to be a bit expensive (compared to other big cities), but I guess that is normal for san fran. Service was fine, breakfast was normal holiday inn express breakfast (who doesn't like the cinnamon buns?), and the room was normal holiday clean.

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “Ehhh....Mixed feelings”
text:
To start off with, im a Diamond VIP with Hilton and have stayed in about 300 hotels...
This hotel was " OK" . It really didnt have anything that would "WoW" you ( other than the $50 valet parking price)
The location was fabulous, i was there for business, i took my girlfriend with me and she LOVED the location. It was close to everything she wanted to do and see.
The hotel is HUGE ( and because its so big, customer service goes down the drain). We werent explained how their room numbering system worked. i think the room number they wrote for us was 13887 . So weget in the elevator, but that elevator doesnt have the 13th floor. ( there are different elevator for different floors, some go up to 30, others only from 30-45)... anyways, after literally 30 mins of walking around with our heavy bags, i went back and stayed in line and they told me the "1" at the beginning is the Tower $, and our room was on the 38th floor. And the attutude they gave me was like " Duh! you should know"
anyways, the view from our room was nice, but the room was small. For an expensive hotel, i didnt like the toilettre collection.
The fitness center was Fabulous, good selection of cardio and lifting equipment, they also had a steam room with showers, very very nice. I have only seen a fitness center like this at the Ritz Carlton.
The breakfast was AMAZING, but in other Hilton's, you get access to the entire breakfast menu for free ( a reward for being a Diamond VIP), but in this Hilton you had to dish out an extra $10 to get access to the Hot Buffet section of the breakfast. Money isnt the issue, its just the principal of it. This hotel came off as cheap, looking to milk money every way they can.
I have mixed feeling about this hotel, although the breakfast and the Fitness Center was amazing, i honestly dont think i'll stay here again.
Oh, and the Pool was out of service, and they didnt even give a coupon for an in-room movie or anything.
Customer service here sucked.

name: Phoenix Hotel, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Cool hotel”
text: Oase midt i San Francisco. Cool hotel med central beliggenhed. 10 minutter til fods til Union Square. Venligt og hjælpsomt personale. Udmærkede værelser og fri parkering - et særsyn i San Francisco. God restaurant og hip bar på hotellet. Mange udmærkede spisesteder i nabolaget - især vietnamesiske.

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “Another great time at the Hilton ...”
text:
Decided to make a last minute trip to San Francisco last week. Hopped on to the Hilton Honors website and found a great deal lickety-split. We arrived a couple of hours before check-in but the front desk was happy to accomodate us. Checked us in with a free upgrade to a tower room with a view without even asking. One of the things I enjoy the most about this hotel is they always pay attention to details. They look at our stay history and focus on what is important to us. On this stay, there were several conventions in town so the hotel was buzzing. Despite the increased activity, the hotel staff was very attentive and quick to respond to requests. I can't ask for more from this hotel.
Now for some tips...there's always a premium on parking in SF. I highly recommend the California Parking garage across the hotel. It's on the corner of Taylor and O'Farrell. 24hr parking with in/out priveleges for $36 which includes tax. The garage is also open 24hrs unlike some others in the area.
For dining options, check out First Crush, Hana Zen, Pucinni & Pinetti and the Daily Grill. Foley's Irish Bar down the street from the hotel is also worth a visit for a pint or two. Lastly, it's a bit of a hoof but if you have time, check out The Press Club. It's a wine bar that is pretty swanky and a lot of fun.

name: Serrano Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Beautiful restored lobby and convenient location”
text: If you haven't noticed - I am a big Kimpton fan and San Francisco has many properties to chose from. The Serrano is a rehab of an older building and they do their best to make it Kimpton worthy - including Kimptonized bathrooms. I was able to upgrade to a corner suite for my stay and the extra sitting space was nice. The building is Spanish revival and the lobby is beautifully restored and the entrance doors are impressive. The building is older but again they do all the things right - free wiFi, coffee and wine. The staff were all friendly and helpful. The elevators are a bit tiny more like Europe but overall it was a pleasant stay. I was not overly impressed with the restaurant associated with the property - Jaspers is more like a bar, they are known for what is on tap and not being a big beer drinker it is not a place I would hang out in much but the burger was fantastic and the omelette in the morning was terrific.

name: Phoenix Hotel, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “TRES DECEVANT....”
text: Choix motivé par le parking gratuit et le petit déj inclus. De plus proximité du centre très pratique. Malheureusement, l'hôtel aurait besoin d'un bon rafraichissement. Chambre pas très nette et restaurant n'existe plus. Le petit déj se prend dehors (par tout temps, à 16° le matin, c'est tonique)... Et le pire c'est le quartier à peine sortis de l'hôtel on tombe sur tous les SDF de la ville, et l'ambiance est plutôt glauque que ce soit le soir ou dans la journée. A éviter !!

name: Hotel Tomo, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Hotel standard dans quartier calme”
text: Prestations correctes mais la déco n'est pas aussi originale que promise. Petit Fitness Center sympathique. Personnel serviable au desk. Evidemment, on est à San Francisco donc il ne faut pas comparer le prix avec celui d'un motel. Le quartier de Japantown est très calme, et assez proche de Union Square (15 mn en bus). Attention en journée, il n'y a pas beaucoup de bus. Il est regrettable que le petit déjeuner ne soit pas compris.

name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel
title: “Not as good as expected from a Marriott”
text: My wife and I stayed at the hotel in late November 2007. A great location for the cable cars and easy to get around. The way the pound is against the dollar the rate was very good but the hotel is just worn out. Our bedroom was a suite with a large sitting room. BUT the TV had been removed and a hole just left. The furniture was tired. I was bitterly disappointed

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Comfortable valuey for money”
text:
This hotel is in a great location. Located near the wharf it is a short walk from all the tourist attractions near the bay. Lots of restaurants only a few blocks away and a Walgreens (large convenience store) a few doors down open until midnight came in very handy.
The room was clean and spacious, the only complaint would be that we stayed on the ground floor so could hear a lot of street noise at night, but otherwise a very pleasant stay.

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “Excellent Hotel!”
text: Our stay at the Nikko was fabulous. I felt pampered knowing that before and during my stay I had staff who were ready and willing to cheerfully and promptly help me with anything I needed! The facilities, both our guestroom and conference room, were immaculate, tasteful and modern. Computer/internet facilities were readily available both wi-fi for my own computer in the hotel room or using the wireless keyboard with the tv in the room. Also, the business center was useful. The downtown location of the hotel was perfect being just a few short blocks from Union Station, Market Street, the cable car line, and the BART. And the concierge was very accomodating in assisting with tour arrangements, especially Tower Tours which have hotel pickup and dropoff for their tours! I would definitely stay at the Hotel Nikko again!

name: Hotel Triton - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Pas mal”
text:
Pour un hôtel avec des chambres à ce prix la je m'attendais à mieux. Certe il est bien placé, devant la porte de chinatown dans le quartier français, mais c'est un quartier assez bruyant. Les petits déjeuner sont livrés dans la chambre, dans des sacs en papier, avec une pomme, un muffin, une bouteille d'eau et du jus d'orange. Pas top.
La température de l'eau chaude est limité ce qui fait que pour ceux qui aime prendre une douche bien bien chaude, comme moi, et ben c'est mort, sinon jvous rassure elle n'est pas tiède non plus. Les lits sont pas tops non plus.Le personnel par contre est très aimable, et pour certains français. Je trouve qu'il et beaucoup trop cher pour ce qu'il est.
Pour se loger à San Francisco a mon avis il vaut mieux un motel qui a son parking, ce qui n'est pas rien a SF puisqu'ils sont tous payants et pas forcement a coté de l'hôtel.

name: Hotel Tomo, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “japan”
text:
nel quartiere japan, un po fuori dal centro ma servito da 2 linee bus .
di stile japan stanze grandi e comode,pulito

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “Nice place to stay”
text: We were very happy with the service we received at the Hilton Union Square. We were able to check in early without any hassles. Our bags were promptly delivered to our room for us. A hotel employee even called us to make sure everything was up to our standards. The room was very nice and clean. The bed was super comfy.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “small room, wonderful staff excellent location”
text:
Our family of 4 stayed for 3 days. The room was small with no space for clothes. However, the location is perfect. The staff is lovely. There is a complimentary breakfast each morning. Eggs, pancakes, sausage, fresh fruit, yogurt, muffins and bagels.. juice, coffee. Our son was not feeling well one night and the hotel went out of there way to help us get him to a doctor.
We would return to this hotel.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “EXCELLENT STAFF, EXCELLENT LOCATION, EXCELLENT HOTEL.”
text: When I usually book a hotel, I do one of those online bids and keep my fingers crossed that the hotel given is halfway decent. I didn't bid this time, instead selecting the Holiday Inn Express Fisherman'sWharf and I am glad I did. Even though the place was packed, our room was very quiet and our bed very comfortable. The breakfast was great and the free internet was a plus. We were so close to everything yet far enough to avoid hearing all the outdoor noises. The staff at the front desk and phone staff were very respectful. My advice to prospective tourists and on line bidders is to refrain from the bargain bidding web sites and choose this hotel outright. The comfortable setting, free breakfast, internet and fine staff makes the Holiday Inn Express Fisherman's Wharf a wise and cost efficient selection.

name: Baldwin Hotel
title: “Great value, great location.”
text: I needed a room for new year's eve and this fit the bill: very nice for the price, staff is friendly, and the parking garage around the corner has a deal with them for overnight parking. It's just outside the Chinatown gate, which makes for great access to fun bars and restaurants.

name: Le Meridien San Francisco
title: “Great location but beware of renovation”
text: Great location that's walking distance from downtown, Chinatown, Ferry Bldg and a short mini ride from union square. Rooms are fully updated and spacious. Only concern is hotel is under major renovation so entire lobby at street level is not accessible and lots of construction activity in early morning, so not conducive to light sleepers. Hotel will be great once renovation is done but for now, maybe try the Hyatt instead.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “We found the staff, rooms location best for our...”
text:
We found the staff, rooms location best for our needs...everyone is friendly, helpful and accommodating all our needs and wishes. The location is excellent for downtown shopping, restaurants and Bart. Cable car roundabout is in next block.. Rooms are quiet on 16th floor unusual for a city. 
Would return in a heartbeat. 
Shirl

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Easy access from airport”
text: Getting to this hotel is a piece of cake once you know how. From the airport, take the skytrain to the Bart Station. Then get on the Bart train to the Embarcadero station. Walk down the street to the Embarcadero and get on an "F" street car to Jones and Taylor which is the end of the line. The hotel is just up the street. My wife and I are going to do it again. It may seem like a lot of train changing but it wasn' a hasell. when retuning to airport make sure you get on the SFO Bart train

name: The Fairmont San Francisco
title: “Lovely Old World Hotel”
text:
The lobby is magnificent and the rooms are well-kept however the room I was assigned was on the small side without a view (I overlooked the rooftop and the tower meaning my only view was other hotel rooms).
It's very close to China Town and North Beach however it isn't as convenient as a hotel in Union Square and is at the top of a very steep hill which seems insurmountable at the end of a long day exploring the city. The California Cable car stops outside the hotel and there is also the Powell St line one block away for when the walk is just too much. 
It's a lovely hotel and I enjoyed my stay however I think I will seek something cheaper when I return to SF.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “All we can ask for”
text:
My sisters and I just returned from a short get away and stayed 3 nights at the hotel. For our purposes we found the hotel to be in a perfect location, close to lots of shopping, to BART station (just a few steps outside the hotel), at the end of the line for cable cars, great restaurants within walking distance. We arrived at the hotel in the morning, warmly welcomed by registration staff and we were able to check in our room early. Our assigned room in the 24th floor had a very nice view of SF and was very clean and well maintained. Having been able to make coffee/tea in the mornings was an added bonus. Before we left to shop one morning, we forgot to remove the do not disturb sign consequently missed the cleaning service. We liked that Housekeeping left a message on our voice mail that asked us to call if we wanted to get the room cleaned that day.
At the business center we attempted to use the computer/printer to print our boarding passes but found a few of the devices inoperable. We approached a hotel staff passing by who happened to be part of security but was very quick to call someone to assist us. The gym has very good machines and free weights and we were able to use twice during our visit. Checking out was very convenient and the parking attendant was very helpful in getting us transportation back to the airport. Overall, we had a very pleasant stay/experience at this hotel, from our first to the last encounter with hotel staff.

name: The Fairmont San Francisco
title: “Grand heritage with a twist”
text:
I stayed here for two nights recently Good loacation high on the hill with views over the city and the bay.
Large comfortable rooms with all the amenities you would expect. Close to the trolley car.
The highlight though is the Tonga Room. This is the hotel bar in the basement where the original indoor pool was. It's now a Polynesian themed bar and music venue that really hits the right notes.
Relaxed dining with a feel good atmosphere and a great three piece band. A good place to chill at the bar or on the dance floor.

name: San Francisco Marriott Union Square
title: “Good Location, small rooms”
text: Good location just off Union Square, great views from the upper floors when the fog clears. Not a very impressive entrance - not helped by the scaffolding that's up at the moment. Efficient & reasonably friendly check in. Rooms are small & bathrooms smaller but well equipped, clean and comfortable. Expensive but seems to be standard for San Francisco.

name: JW Marriott San Francisco Union Square
title: “Great views over San Fran”
text: Great hotel close to union square. Vallet parking worked very well. We also had a lounge access and the lounge had great breakfast. Rooms were nice and we had the view towards the Golden Gate bridge. When it was not foggy, we were able to see the bridge. The JW is better than Marriott in general and I was positively surprised.

name: Palace Hotel
title: “Beautiful, elegant hotel with wonderful service! Very noisy, however...”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel several times and it is always so elegant and gracious. The rooms are beautiful, well designed for both the business and vacation traveler. The gym was great for a workout. My only complaint was a serious noise issue with an absolutely huge party going on in the Garden Court. This event made the hotel actually feel as if it was shaking the hotel with it's vibrations. We were told that there were 1500 guests and they were spilling out everywhere. Even in our room on the 6th floor we could feel and hear the noise and people talking and laughing. Late into the evening people were still out in the hallways wandering around making noise. 
The bed was surprisingly not the normal amazing Starwoods quality that I have come to expect and was a bit of a disappointment as was the number of bed pillows. This was minor compared to the noise issue. We could have complained but did not. The sheets were also quite scratchy.
When we complained about the noise and asked for a different room we were told the hotel was sold out. Also, we were reassured that no more huge events in the Garden Court would happen during our stay but that was simply not true. Another event took place on Saturday night that while not as bad as the Thursday night event, was also quite loud and noisy. I do not understand why the ballrooms were not used for such large events. This problem will definitely affect my decision to stay here in the future.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Lovely hotel”
text: Stayed at this hotel for 6 nights. Chose the hotel for it's central location to the shops,Union Square and most of the transport links,ie Bart and Cable cars. Upon arrival we were given a room in the Historic area. The room was extremely small and cramped but had an enormous shower area half of which you could t use.it was very dark and the view looked out over the metalwork of the air conditioning system which was very noisy. We asked to be moved and this was done straight away to a far quieter room in the new section of which we could not find fault. The breakfast grill was to our liking mainly because of Chelsea, our waitress for 3 of the mornings.how anybody could be so happy and charming so early every morning I ll never know. This was our 3 rd time to San Fran and if we are lucky enough to return we would not hesitate to stay at this hotel again and would recommend it to frienda

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “OK but avoid the breakfast”
text: Good location close to all Fisherman's Wharf amenities, reasonable room and the front desk staff are friendly enough. The breakfast though is memorable for it's sheer awfulness - eat out there are plenty of options around

name: Palace Hotel
title: “Grand Dame of a Hotel with lots of history and character”
text: Stayed for a couple of nights on my way to conference. Great location on Market, close to all the action. Nice bedrooms and public areas. Great main dining room with famous glass ceiling. Had breakfast here which I would recommend you avoid - very poor buffet choice although I understand this place is famous for Sunday Brunch. Place was very busy as there was a huge convention on at the time, so lots of name badges and beer people about. Worth a short stay, but no longer than that.

name: Le Meridien San Francisco
title: “You have to pay for wifi”
text: Le Meridien on Battery Street in San Francisco, CA is a very nice hotel. Nice hotel lounge and bar. Great customer service. The room was lovely. Well-decorated and spacious. But the room had not been thoroughly cleaned. There was a decent layer of dust by the fridge, mini bar, and bureau. If it hadn't been for proximity for a special event I would not have chosen Le Meridien on Battery. The one plus to the location is being steps away from the pier and farmer's market. On Sunday's many things were closed and you had to plan ahead before you came in for the night if wanted something else besides room service and the mini bar. The bone I have to pick with Le Meridien is that you have to pay for WiFi service. They charge nearly $13 a day. In a city known for it's tech sector I think it is absolutely outrageous that we would have to pay for WiFi. All of these things put together, I don't strongly recommend Le Meridien.

name: JW Marriott San Francisco Union Square
title: “Nice but not quite a 4 star standard”
text: It really is a 3-star hotel. And needs some work to be called "JW Marriott". Bed is comfortable, carpet needs replaced. Shower is a bit small. Unlike most JW Marriott timeshare, this hotel does not provide laundry facility for guests use. Decoration is just average similar to the Embassy Suite chain. The property is couple of blocks to Union Square. While we sort of okay with our 4 nights staying during Christmas time, but we will not be returning.

name: Palace Hotel
title: “An original -- both pros and cons.”
text:
I'm torn so I'm going to write this review as objectively as possible. The Palace is just grand downstairs. The dining room is amazing, it's all old school glitz and glamour. The rooms upstairs are charming, if you were in a country house in England. It's just a little out of place, since you know there are 270 rooms or whatever there.
The bed was very comfortable, but the walls are paper thin. I could hear someone blowing their nose (I'm not kidding) and also the pipes of the shower the next morning. I probably wouldn't stay there again.
But the Palace is an original and may deserve some of your time if you love the turn of the century style. It's also in a great location!

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Anything but an”
text:
I stayed here a couple of nights while in town and loved the place. Views of Alcatraz and the Golden Gate Bridge right from my window, and it's right on top of Fisherman's Wharf. My preconceptions about what constitutes a Holiday Inn "Express" must be flawed, because this was anything but an economy-class motel for overnight business travelers. It's a classy joint; to the point I was a little stunned when I walked into my room. I'm no world traveler/hotelier, but this was one of the nicest rooms I've ever stayed in while on vacation.
Anyway, needless to say, I'd highly recommend it to anyone heading into San Fran for any length of time. You're close to everything, the staff is incredibly friendly, and my room was top-notch. Forget Zagat's; you've got me to rely on for your hotel reviews.

name: Petite Auberge a Joie de Vivre Hotel
title: “I would stay here again & recommend it to family!”
text: Wonderful experience, personal attention, & genuine decor! The room was originally decorated with beautiful, unique furniture, books, an opening window & a fireplace. The location was amazing! A short walk to China Town or Nob Hill. The wine & hors d'oeuvres reception was out of this world! Best aspect of Petite Auberge was the service. When made aware of our early departure, the staff was willing to work as a team to ensure that we were provided a convenient & substantial to-go breakfast which was delivered to our room shortly following our wake up call, before 6AM. It doesn't get much better than that!

name: Palace Hotel
title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
We were recently at the Palace hotel and really enjoyed the experience. The hotel combines classic 1920s opulence with modern conveniences. The hotel staff in general and the concierge in particular were truly outstanding and helpful. The rooms, while small, were well equipped spacious enough for a 2-3 night stay. The location is also good - a 10 minute walk to the Embarcadero or ATT Park, and a 5 minute walk to outstanding shopping around Union square. 
Plus, the value here is tremendous.

name: Serrano Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Beautiful Lobby”
text:
Nice & close to Union Square & the shops. The lobby was very pretty which made up for the scaffolding outside. Rooms were comfortable (the leopard print dressing gowns were a nice touch) There is complimentary coffee in the lobby - we were not told about this so did not take advantage of it until the last day - also wasn't told about the wine tasting either (but we were probably out & about at that time each day). The bar/restaurant was very friendly but as with everywhere in San Francisco it was expensive! 
I would recommend the boat trip around the bay which takes you under the Golden Gate Bridge & very close to Alcatraz (great for photographs) Fishermans Wharf is nice for shops and restaurants too.
We took the BART from the airport (approx 8 dollars each) get off at Powell Street & the Serrano is only a ten minute walk from the station. It was a great service.
The buses were very efficient - only 2 dollars per trip (the trams were 5 dollars!) make sure if you get a tram you don't bother until it has room as you will not enjoy the experience if you are stood squashed in the middle unable to take in the views - our tram conductor was very rude to some people - pushing them (he made one lady cry)

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text:
I recently spent 2 nights at the Handlery with my family at the beginning of our two week trip to the US. The hotel is perfectly located for Union Square and the tram is just around the corner. I'd been emailing the hotel as we are a family of 5 and they happily provided two interconnecting rooms for us which gave has so much space and comfort if not a little pricey. The beds were amazingly comfortable and the rooms very clean just a little dated in decor.
We had one room on the main front street which I have to say was a little noisy to the street traffic and I had to wedge some paper in the window to stop in banging, the hotel would benefit from some double glazing.
We did hear the protestors across the road at the Frank hotel but being from the UK we were up and about hours before they were, my husband thought it was really interesting. If you don't want to be woken up I suggest you request an internal room.
We didn't get a chance to use the pool but it looked really nice as we walked through one day.
I would and will happily recommend the Handlrey and to go back and visit soon.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “A Great Union Sq. Hotel”
text:
I stayed last Friday night. Professional staff and service was 5 star. Some of my friends stay here a lot and highly recommend it. So, I had to find out for myself. They were right. I wish I had more time to spend there. 
I WILL BE BACK!!!

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “3 night stay SF Holiday Inn Express”
text: If you are looking for a quiet room and within walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf without paying you know those other prices then go no further. I know it was off season, but that was part of the reason for visiting San Francisco. The trip was more about being a tourist and we figured why not stay in the main tourist spot. As other reviews mention and I agree, there is no reason for renting a car to see the tourist spots unless you are planning on doing it in a day on your own pace. Keep in mind the many tour options. Everything was in walking distance and what wasn't was easily accessible by using some type of day pass. We went ahead and bought a City Pass which was very useful. We did all the tours/museums that came with the pass and benefitted it also by using for all the local public transportaion. Anyway, the hotel is right across or next to the other main hotels, but nearly half the price. The bed was very comfortable and as I mentioned very quiet when we were not out being tourists. Plus you can't beat the free breakfast and free internet (computer on site as well).

name: San Francisco Marriott Union Square
title: “The people are the difference”
text:
Having just returned from my stay at this hotel I am compelled to leave a review.
Beyond the impeccable accomodations, atmosphere and location, what truly impressed me about this property were the people. The doormen here are quite special. Ben, Fernando and Perry are some of the kindest and efficient staff I have ever encountered at any hotel and I wish to personally thank them for making my stay at The Marriott Union Square truly a pleasure.

name: Palace Hotel
title: “It may LOOK like a Palace on the surface, but that's as far as it goes.”
text:
I'm a Starwood Platinum Preferred Guest (also Platinum with Marriott Rewards), so I have stayed at my fair share of hotels. When I had the opportunity to use 3 free weekend nights in San Francisco, I decided on the Palace Hotel because I've already experience Westin, W and Sheraton...and the St. Regis wasn't available. So I wanted to give the Luxury Collection a chance.
Upon check-in, there were no upgrades available. I don't mind staying in a standard room, but this room hardly met any "standards" I have for a "luxury" hotel. The room had an unpleasant odor (mildew, mold, perhaps). And regardless of the fact that I turned the temperature down to 70, the thermostat never dropped below 72 and that still felt more like 75. I also had an alley view. And the cellphone reception was awful - so my internet barely worked. I'd seen similar complaints about the room temperature and reception in other reviews...I wish that I would have listened!!!
I contacted the morning manager after hearing from a front desk attendant that the rooms will not get any cooler than 72 degrees. The manager said that she'd send engineering up right away. They did not come during the 90 minutes I waited in my room. And when I returned 3 hours later, I had no indication of whether they'd come or if anything was done. I walked down to the front desk and the evening manager had no information, but looked into it and found out there was nothing they could do about the temperature. I called SPG to see if I could be moved to a different hotel, but there were no options that night. So SPG contacted the Palace Hotel who said that I could try a different room. On my way downstairs to get the new keys I bumped into a couple who had their door open and were trying to adjust the temperature in their room because it was too warm. I kindly informed them that was as good as it gets.
Upon inspection of the new room - a Deluxe Room on a higher floor - I found it had no odor and also felt cooler (closer to a true 72 degrees). So I relocated. The downside, the room had a connecting door to the next room and I could hear the conversations as if they were in the same room. I was able to stuff towels under the significant gap beneath the door, which helped.
The next day I woke up thinking I could tolerate staying my last of three nights. But my positive feelings quickly faded as I attempted to use the fitness facility and found that my key would not open the door. I had to go back down to the front desk, only to find out that my keys were still active and the door should open. She said that she'd have security meet me at the gym. I tried my keys again several times, until another patron opened the door for me. I inquired on whether he had any trouble getting in and he said that the door was a little tricky. In hindsight, I also remember the guy in front of my the day before having trouble opening the door. I waited for security and he reiterated that the door can be tricky. If you know that a door only works SOME of the time, why wouldn't you fix it?
I reached my final straw when I got back to my room later in the day after sightseeing and neither of my room keys would open my own room door. Apparently the front desk attendant who switched my rooms didn't do the due dilligence to ensure that they were programmed for my two remaining nights. I went straight to my room and called SPG to be transferred to another hotel. To top it off, the same front desk attendant informed the SPG agent that I would be charged $100 for an early departure. After the steam finished exploding from my ears I told the SPG agent I would walk back downstairs and speak with the front desk attendent myself. The agent put me on hold to allow the Palace front desk attendent to drop from the line. When she came back she said that they'd decided to waive the $100 fee - as if they were doing me a favor after 3 consecutive days of problems.
If you are interested in experiencing the legacy of the Palace Hotel, might I suggest you simply stop by, walk around the lobby and perhaps even visit the bar/restaurant. But do NOT pay for a room, unless you can appreciate a warm bedroom, possibly the odor of mildew/mold and you don't mind POOR SERVICE!
Oh...if I had to say something nice about the hotel...they have a really nice pool, with windows all above it. And they have individual TV monitors for the cardio equipment, but they only have 3 ellipticals and 3 treadmills, so get there early or you'll be stuck on a bike.

name: Le Meridien San Francisco
title: “Web deal makes it fantastic”
text: Called reservations - they offered a corner suite room on floor 21 for $550 plus tax, plus $52.00 for parking. Outrageous. I pointed out a web special and they quickly changed it to $165.00 with free parking. The room is fantastic - approx 600 sq. Feet, huge TV at the foot of bed that swivels to the large sitting area. It has every amenity you can imagine. Would be 5 stars other than the ridiculous initial pricing. Housekeeping saved the day washing our clothes in their own machines after 6 pm on a Fri night even after the concierge said that wasn't possible. It was an emergency (don't ask) and it's things like this that build brand loyalty. We're definitely coming back. Wonderful.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Perfect location.”
text: As a first time visitor to San Francisco, I believe I had the perfect location from which to explore the city. The Handlery is near restaurants, shops and transport. The premier room was great for my family of 4 and breakfast in the Daily Grill each morning was delicious. My only complaint was on two consecutive nights we we were woken in the early hours of the morning by the people returning to their room next door who spoke and laughed loudly for at least an hour. The walls must be paper thin! Overall, a great stay. Will definitely be back!

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Perfect location”
text: Great location, 5 mins from harbour and 10 mins from Pier 39. Room was in Holiday Express building 2nd floor overlooking main road and trams. Didnt find it noisy at all. Room was clean, comfy, staff pleasant, breakfast fine, although the 1 evening meal there was disappointing. There is a large late night Walgreen supermarket across the street which had food, toiletries, drinks etc etc, plenty of eating places around. Highly recommend Boudins on the Wharf for breakfast, sourdough soup and ambience. Really recommend taking yr own hairdryer to Holiday Inns in the US, the ones supplied are weak and lethal!

name: The Fairmont San Francisco
title: “Grand old hotel”
text: Stayed here for a business meeting. It was fun to see and stay in this classic hotel, but I was disappointed to find that the room faced inwards and had no view, which kind of defies the purpose of staying on top of the hill. And what a hill it is! It is quite a trek up the hill from the Powell St BART station. The rooms are large and comfortable. The Tonga tiki bar in the basement is worth visiting, but it was smaller and less spectacular than I had been led to believe from the Anthony Bourdain show. The cocktails were strong and tasty, though! However, internet is more expensive even than other hotels of this class, at $14/day, and apparently they charge $15 to use the fitness room! Historical grandeur doesn't come cheap, I guess.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Ottima posizione”
text: Ottimo hotel, a due passi dal famoso Pier 39 all'interno del quartiere Fisherman's Wharf. Possibilità di parcheggio convenzionato. Personale cortese e disponibile, distante circa mezz'ora di auto dall'aereoporto di San Francisco. Colazione non inclusa, ma esiste una convenzione con il ristorante IL Pescatore, sia per la colazione che per la cena.

name: Serrano Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Home from home in San Francisco”
text:
It's always good to come back to the Serrano, as the staff are friendly without being intrusive and the rooms are luxurious without being over the top. The ambiance is wonderful, from the greeting at the front door to the evening wine hour in the lobby every evening. The attached restaurant, Ponzu, is also a gem with knowledgeable and friendly wait staff and a a superb chef. The food never disappoints.
The location of the Serrano is perfect for SFO, close to everything that matters, but not right in the bustle.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Super hôtel”
text:
Situé à 2 blocs du Fisherman's Wharf, le Tuscan Inn est parfaitement intégré à son cadre urbain. Ne serait ce le porche d'accès pour les voitures, on pourrait (presque) passer devant sans le remarquer.
Et pourtant, c'est une petite pépite d'hôtel dans le quartier. Nous en avons fréquenté d'autres, mais nous reviendrons au Tuscan Inn !
Calme, nos chambres donnant à chaque fois sur le jardin central, avec une climatisation très discrète, un équipement complet (coffre fort, machine à café, réfrigérateur, etc ...), spacieuses et bien desservies, nous avons pu nous reposer chaque soir en rentrant de nos pérégrinations en ville.
Si vous ne rentrez pas trop tard le soir, l'établissement offre un (ou 2, ou 3) verre de vin de Californie à ses clients de 17 à 18 h.
Le lobby est très chaleureux, avec une cheminée (et de fausses bûches) bien agréable à contempler, un verre en main.
L'accueil est parfait, nos souhaits sont, dans la mesure du possible, exaucés par un personnel très compétent et très sympathique.
San Francisco ne nécessite pas de voiture si vous restez DownTown, et vous pouvez donc vous économiser le Valet Parking à 50 $, ou alors garez votre "char" en face sur le parking public pour 30 $.
L'hôtel est lié à un restaurant attenant, le Pescatore, où on vous servira un petit déjeuner "continental" avec jus de fruit, salade de fruits frais, café/thé et viennoiserie ou toast ou muffin, inclus dans le prix de la chambre. C'est drôle de déguster des fraises et du melon à Noël ou en janvier ! Bien sûr, vous pouvez toujours commander des prestations supplémentaires (œufs, bacon, etc ....).

name: Palace Hotel
title: “Beautiful lobby. It stops there.”
text:
I stayed at the Palace for 2 nights. Was very impressed when upon arrival at 11 AM, I was given a room. The lobby is breathtaking. Upon getting to my room, I noted that my “view” was of other windows. Understandable. When I started to look around the room, I noticed a thin layer of dust on just about everything and rings from glasses on a wood and glass table top. When I went into the bathroom, the floor did not look clean to me. After taking a shower, I took the hairdryer off the wall only to see it had lipstick on it. This was the last straw. I complained to the front desk and was told I could change rooms. I declined as I had already unpacked some things and was on my way out to a meeting. I was told that my room would be re-cleaned and that a member of management would inspect it. I said this was fine. When I returned after 8 pm it looked like nothing had been done to the room save removing my used towel. The dust, water marks, lipstick, and floor grime remained. My used towel was not even replaced. I called down to the front desk and was told nothing could be done but that management would contact me. They never did. 
Additionally, water pipes in the bathroom alternately ran and dripped through the night. No newspaper in the morning. 
I have never had an issue with a Westin property before and was dismayed at the poor service quality at this property. Let me emphasize it was not the age of the property that was an issue for me. 
I would only stay here again if I got a great deal.

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “Not 4 star but okay”
text: Stayed here last week. Room was small, and very clean. No fridge or microwave. Internet extra by 14 dollars a day. Very, very good concierge service. Convenient location.

name: Le Meridien San Francisco
title: “Great experience, great service”
text: Stayed two nights. Got a great deal through Priceline. Wonderful king size bed. Not much of a view, but no matter. The concierge service was great, gave us great tips for places to run for my son, complete with mileage. No question seemed too small or inconvenient for them. We had a phone problem and a broken lock on the mini bar. Service to fix them came in minutes. We didn't use the room service or restaurants.......a little pricey for our wallets. Great fitness room. We parked at a nearby garage that was less expensive than the hotel parking. Great amenities but the bathroom door set up is strange and not completely private. An odd thing in such a nice hotel. Close to much of San Francisco's popular places. We walked to almost everything. The nice thing about being in the financial district on the weekend is that the banks, etc are closed so there is less traffic.

name: Serrano Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Hidden Gem”
text:
My husband and I booked this trip through AA.com and decided to take a chance on the Serrano based on reviews from Tripadvisor. Close to Union Square, restaurants, transportation, cable cars. Glad we did!
Having stayed at the HIlton across the street, I certainly appreciated the little touches that this hotel had to offer. Everything from the doormen saying "welcome back" to the the "thank you notes" , for tips, left by housekeeping. Everyone on staff seemed as if they really did want to make our stay as comfortable as possible. We did not feel as if we guest number "whatever". The nightly wine reception was a great way to wind down after a day of sightseeing and talk to other guests. Loved the grouping of seats and the availabe games to play.
True, if you go right at the corner, the area can become a bit dicey. However, Dottie's True Blue Cafe was definitely worth going right for. Most breakfasts were at Lori's Diner on Mason a block away. Humberto and the rest of the staff, greeted us warmly each morning which was as welcome as their wonderful breakfasts.
Would definitely recommend Alegrias Food from Spain restaurant on Lombard and Webster. The shrimp, paella and lamb were great. Also Hyde's Seafood Restaurant and Raw Bar, at Hyde and Jackson, on the Mason Hyde Cable line was, delicious. Off the beaten path. Not very tour sty. We decided to mapquest the restaurant and found it to be about at 20 minute walk from the hotel. Uphill most of the way to the restaurant. Great for building up an appetite. I had on hills, and it was not very challenging. Downhill back to the hotel, great for walking off the dinner. The escargot, lobster and roasted prawns, YUMMY! 
Tbe only thing that I can say that I did not like about hotel, was the dirty windows on the 16h Floor. We overloked the Hilton and O'Farrell Street. Got a couple of good pix from the window, so it was not a great big thing.
Can't wait to return to San Francisco and the Serrano will definitely be on the short list of places to stay.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Very good location free parking”
text: Very good location and the parking is great. Hotel pool is very refreshing.

name: Serrano Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “great hotel with a unique quality”
text: We very much enjoyed our weekend at the Serrano. The service was excellent and we really appreciated how helpful the staff was with our infant son. They had a crib waiting in our room when we arrived and promptly brought a humidifier upon re. The happy hour was a lot of fun and we had no problem with the location. Quite the contrary, we felt the location was excellent.

name: JW Marriott San Francisco Union Square
title: “Comfortable stay at the JW”
text:
We stayed at this hotel during the week between Christmas and New Years and were very pleased with the experience. We were visiting our son who lives in the city and we have made this trip at this time for three years. Last year we stayed at the Marriott on Union Square which is about a block away from the JW. We liked that hotel but decided to give the JW a try as we were using points and it was the same amount for either.
Because of the East coast snow storm our first flight was canceled and our second flight left Philadelphia 3 hours late. We arrived at the hotel at 9pm. Check in was very quick and we were told that the Concierge Lounge was open for another hour. That was great news as our son and daughter in law were on their way over to greet us. The lounge was empty except for the 4 of us and were able to enjoy drinks and dessert. It was crowded in the mornings, but evenings were very relaxing there.
 Our room was great. On the 18th floor and facing south we enjoyed the large window with a wonderful view even though it rained much of the time. The bed was very comfortable and the internet was fast and convenient. Housekeeping did a nice job each day. 
 We would definitely recommend this hotel and would stay again if using points. If we were paying, I think the Marriott down the street is almost as nice and more cost effective.

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “Highly Recommend”
text:
Had a great time staying here, the staff were super friendly from the minute we arrived. 
Very clean hotel and rooms located extremely close to Union Square and even had a starbuck attached to the building. 
Also close to car hire firms and main shopping area. Concierge also had greeat locval knowledge or resturants and shops.
I would recommend,

name: W San Francisco
title: “Fun fun place -- everything makes you smile.”
text:
We just spent a long weekend there -- the W is definitely beautiful, great location, great staff & rooms; but it's also fun. Everything from the Buddha nightlight, the Chinese (W)
checkerboard, that little statue to hold your change, and the extra tp roll in a bag that says, "Back-up Plan." Lots of hotels are comfortable and tasteful like this, but here you wander around the room smiling at the little amusements. It's entertaining and different.
Loved it.

name: Le Meridien San Francisco
title: “Great deal via Priceline”
text: very nice up scale hotel in the financial district in San Francisco. Close to BART and MUNI short walk to China town and Cable cars. Near Ferry Building. Rooms and service were perfect. Found parking in the Embarcadero Center for $32.00 per day somewhat cheaper than the hotel. I asked at check in about room on upper floor and king bed and the clerk accommodated my wishes. very pleased with this hotel and service and location.

name: Le Meridien San Francisco
title: “Decent value, good beds and location.”
text: As mentioned in other reviews, the Meridien doesn't have a "wow" factor, but it's nice and clean, and the staff were all very friendly and helpful. It's in the financial district, so the area gets kind of dead in the evenings and on weekends (which is when we were there). The lobby bathrooms are on the second floor, which was a minor inconvenience, and the extra charges can add up (nothing is cheap here), but if you can get past that it's a really nice place with a helpful and attentive staff. One other bonus Iis that I could actually open the windows in my hotel room.

name: San Francisco Marriott Union Square
title: “Great hotel”
text:
The check-in went perfect even if we arrived very late. The rooms were clean, and big. The staff at the checkóin desk were helpful.
The location of the hotel for a city trip is perfect, the Union square is 2 minutes away. Around the hotel there are several Strabucks caffees and diners. We felt very safe as the area is very busy but inside the hotel you did not hear the noise anymore.
I would definitely come back again.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Outstanding Location, Nice Motel, Noisy”
text: Outstanding location in the middle of Fisherman's Wharf. Walking distance from most of the nearby attractions. Very loud street noise. Friendly hotel management and staff, nice and well-kept property. Valet parking service was expensive (maybe $36/day), but it was always nice to have a parking space waiting whenever we returned to the hotel. Rates were reasonable, complimentary breakfast buffet was mediocre and crowded. Decent hotel, but too noisy for my wife.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great place to stay!”
text:
We booked a mini-suite overlooking the wharf. The room was large and clean. In the distance, I could see Alcaltraz. One of the windows opened and allowed the sounds of the area to enter the room. I loved that feature. I heard the street cars, sea gulls, and traffic to enter the room. At night, it was very quiet. 
The location for the street cars and buses could not be beat! Near the hotel was Denny's, Walgreens, Barnes and Noble, Safeway and all kinds of tourist shops. I stopped in a 711 store to buy a lottery ticket and won a $100! 
The hotel staff was very knowledgeable about what bus to take and/or how to best get to an area. 
The free breakfast consisted of eggs (scrambled or omelet style), sausage (links or patties), bread (bagels, english muffins, white, wheat), cereal, bananas, milk, yogurt, juices, coffee, and sweet rolls. The breakfast area does get crowded especially around the four toasters. Hey, it is a free breakfast! I didn't mind the wait. 
The only downside is the tv has a few channels. When we settled in for the evening, it was difficult to find anything to watch. That maybe a personal taste and may not be helpful to you. The Demand movies were $13.99 each.
Bring a pen, I guess hotels have recently stopped putting pens in the rooms.
Free internet access in our room. That is a definite plus! It was really free!
In the lobby, near the business area, there is a way to get your boarding pass. I didn't use it because I am not sure how to.
Definite would stay here again!

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “Nice hotel”
text:
Last year I took my Mom, Gramma, Aunt and Mother-in-law to San Francisco for Mother's Day weekend, and stayed at the Hotel Nikko based on Trip Advisor reviews. I have to say this is a great website!! It was exactly as described by others: (1) a nice hotel, (2) was withing walking distance of some nice restaurants, w/good food, (3) near cable car/trolleys, (4) near great shopping!.
Previous reviewers were also correct, though, that it bordered on a not so nice area, so the street was a bit dirty, would be bums/
homeless people around, esp. at night, so really did not like walking in the street in the evenings--although I will admit that there were ALWAYS lots of people walking around, so it still felt somewhat safe.; and during the day it was fine.
The hotel is nice, the rooms are nice--not spectacular--but nice. We did NOT like the fact that you had to PAY a separate fee to use the indoor gym and indoor pool! They really need to change that. But it is a pretty pool area.
The concierge was good, recommended a WONDERFUL RESTAURANT IN CHINATOWN THAT IS NOT FREQUENTED BY VISITORS, BUT IS POPULAR WITH LOCALS. I DONT REMEMBER THE NAME, BUT I AM SURE THE HOTEL WOULD KNOW, THE FOOD WAS SOOOOOOOOOO DELICIOUS!! YOU HAVE TO GO IF YOU LIKE CHINESE FOOD. Note: the servers speak very little English--
seriously--but we had no problems with our orders. I think we were the only non-locals there!
I have used Trip Advisor for help/guidance on other trips and find people's reviews pretty on-the-money!! I had forgotten to post this review, and wanted to make sure that I finally did it, just to make sure that I can help others, too. Thanks for this great website!!

name: San Francisco Marriott Union Square
title: “Good stay at the Hotel 480”
text:
I recently stayed for 3 nights at the Hotel 480 and have no compaints whatsoever. Its a very decent hotel in a great location.
Its close to great shopping and the Bart as well as being convenient for most of the major tourist options. 
All in all a solid hotel!

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “Great Hotel”
text:
Overall it's a beautiful hotel. The only real complaint I have is that it's not equiped with all the electronic amenities as many hotels are these days. Wireless internet is only available in hotel common areas. To connect to the internet in your room, you have to plug in. TVs are dated and are not flat screen/LCD/plasma. 
Aside from that we had a great room with a fabulous view of the city. Housekeeping and other staff members were very friendly. Starbucks opened early on race day for all the runners in the area. Continental breakfast is awesome and includes a grande drink of your choice, pastry, water/soda/juice, and fruit!!! Couldn't ask for much more!!

name: InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco
title: “Great Stay”
text:
This hotel has tons of ambiance, especially at Christmas time. We enjoyed our stay. The view is wonderful. They really pampered us too. The cost was very reasonable. We are Priority Club members so we received a free upgrade. The rooms were much quieter than others made them out to be. 
Top of the Mark, while expensive, has a wonderful view and the food was pretty good as well. We met friends there who had traveled from Mexico, so we spent 2 hours there visiting and enjoying the view. 
Lots to do nearby. Close to cable cars, Chinatown, Union Square, Tour bus rides, etc. Taxis were not very expensive either (you may need to close your eyes from time to time). 
Can't wait to go again.

name: Le Meridien San Francisco
title: “Do not choose this hotel if:”
text:
1) You need a WiFi high speed internet connection
2) You are travelling with a lot of luggages and you need space
to store extra clothes in your room. Even the best rooms are bad designed, with
a few space in small wardrobes and drawers.
Bathroom is very simple and with only one shelt to put your staff on!!
Our room is a luxury suite, we are paying too much for a very small bedroom and a simple living room.
It is not worthed. Only the good sleep quality and the location make this hotel acceptable for the high rate paid.
Gherardo Milanesi - Italy

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “Excellence in all regards!”
text:
The only possible complaint is the sheer size of the property made participating in the conference require more walking than I would have preferred.
Service was outstanding. Quality unsurpassed.

name: Palace Hotel
title: “Historic and generally ok, but lower your expectations”
text:
Had a couple rooms for a couple nights in December. Staff was helpful, no issues there. The hotel is very historic (i.e. old) and not much can be done without changing the format.
The rooms are taller than they are wide - very high ceilings, but quite small rooms. I found the bed very comfortable. 
The walls are paper thin. I am not kidding that you can hear conversations in at normal speaking levels in the next room. A family member was in the room on the other side. I could wake up to her alarm clock going off. Now those are some thin walls. The hotel is seriously in need of soundproofing or masking white noise.
While there are some good rates out there for this hotel, they make it up in every other way. $48 for a simple room service breakfast is very bizzarre. $15/day for internet. $15 for an in-room movie. No in-room coffee service.
Other than that they do about as good as they can for what it is. Probably not for business travelers, it seemed most of the guests were vacation guests.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “Nothing special about this hotel, however it was clean and in convenient location to transportation.”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights with my boyfriend. I would say that it is an average hotel, and I am not sure what differentiates it from other 3 or even 4 star hotels. I have stayed in some 3 stars where the rooms are equally well appointed and clean. I wouldn't rate this hotel as a 4 star. The pillows were terribly uncomfortable, the sheets were rough. The room was a decent size. The shower leaked. The room was clean. The lobby is nice but wifi was not so great there.
We were on the 12th floor and could hear a lot of outside noise - it didn't bother me as I am used to hearing city noise at night - I think some ppl would have trouble sleeping. Plus the walls are thin and the cleaning staff were vacuuming in the hallway before 8:30am. 
Service was fine with the exception of the check in staff who told us that internet costs 14.95 when in fact it was included in our business rate - we did not find out it was included until the next day which was by pure chance. 
The major pro of this hotel is that it is within steps of the Powell Bart station so it makes transportation to and from SFO really easy. The food court at Westfield mall is also a good place for a quick bite when you're on the go.
It is easy to access public transportation from this hotel to most of the city's tourist attractions - however in the summer time the lines for public transportation in general were really long and a bit of a waste of time - i think next time we would just cab everywhere since it's relatively closeby to get to the main attractions and because we only had a few days waiting for the MUNI consumed a lot of time.
Another thing to note - although the hotel was conveniently located, I would not stay in that area again as it was so touristy and also there were a lot of shady people around the hotel.

name: Palace Hotel
title: “I've never heard of a hotel putting $2,000 worth of holds on a credit card!”
text: I booked my room well in advance and paid for it! When I got my room bill there was some what I consider minor incidentals billed to the room. Upon check out I paid the majority of the incidentals in cash and put a little bit on the credit card. When I got home I saw that there was a $2,000 hold from the palace hotel on my credit card. I've NEVER EVER seen this at all in my entire experience with a hotel especially one that considers itself to be a 5 star hotel. The facilities are alright, the room is dated, beds were way too soft and springy, hall ways echoed, and the bathroom wasn't even luxurious. The location was just fine and the service was a best spotty. Internet was $15-20 per day!!!! I've never ever seen internet and I go to England and Japan quite a bit. If it was up to me I wouldn't stay here again.... I think for what I spent I would have much rather stayed at the Le Meridien (I should have booked that in the first place). I'm offended because I am a littler younger than most people on average staying in a place like that. But NEVER judge a book by its cover and just assume that a young adult cannot pay for a room when it has already been paid for in advance and also be able to cover the incidentals. Trust me what I spent was merely just a drop in the ocean and I'm sorry I spent ANY money with the Palace. As an SPG Gold member I am extremely upset over this! NEVER EVER AGAIN and I come to San Fran once a year. I hear the Mandarin Oriental is quite nice. So I'll be staying there next time! To all you considering to stay here do not you will be disappointed in the value for the money.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Good for a last min trip and near lots of food options.”
text: The roosuper very small. But the bathroom is very clean and the in room AC seems to be working great. Fridge in room and large LCD tv as well.

name: Radisson Hotel Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Okay if you like the smaell of Clam Chowder!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 4 days in July. Hmmm...first impressions, NOT GREAT! Check in staff - RUDE! Our room safe needed a different code everyday as everytime we returned to the room, our safe wouldn't open, granted they did send someone to attend to this quite quickly but strange that it was always after we'd left the room un-occupied! The furniture and carpets are old, need up-graded! Location is great if you like smelling clam chowder all day and all night!! Lots of tramps and beggers hang around the hotel, quite un-nerving.
I wouldn't stay at this hotel again - EVER!

name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel
title: “Good and Bad”
text:
The hotel is attractive with a nice entrance. Coffee and hot chocolate are served complimentary with your morning wake-up call. But I was terribly disappointed with the service at the check-in desk.
I waited for about 6 hours to get a room while dozens of other travelers got served. I spoke with 4 clerks and all told me that my room was not ready. Eventually I was told that I should not expect more since I went through Priceline (although I paid over $100 per night for the room). I called the Marriott national number, and they immediately straightened out the problem, apologizing for the treatment I received. Obviously the hotel employees are instructed to treat Priceline customers this way, since every one gave the same type answers.

name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel
title: “Perfect Stanford Court”
text:
We have just returned home to England after having the most wonderful holiday in San Francisco. We stayed at the Stanford Court Renaissance and stayed in the Deluxe Double room - city view.
The hotel is very luxurious and the staff very friendly and helpful. The surrounding were regal. Room was really comfortable with decor to match the style of hotel. Coffee/Chocolate on the mornings was a real treat and the turndown service with water, chocolates etc. an added bonus.
We had room service one evening and the food arrived on a beautifully laid table with silver service and a rose in a vase. Food was excellent also!
We celebrated our Silver Wedding Anniversary in the main restaurant and spent a fortune but it was really special and the staff were wonderful, explaining dishes and wines. The chef wrote Happy Anniversary in Chocolate on our dessert plates. 
Location is perfect. We walked to Union Square shops in 15minutes, To Fishermans Wharf in about 35minutes. Trams stop outside and these we used several times however taxis actually worked out cheaper and some of the times we had free travel from the hotel.
This hotel has a good reputation from local people and is surrounded by The Ritz and The Carlton - Need I say more!!
We had all the luxury but it was with a friendly smile and service. 
Before we went on holiday we were concerned about some of the reviews we had read and wondered if we had booked the best hotel for our money - but we had no cause for concern.
Will certainly return. Perfect!Perfect!Perfect!

name: The Fairmont San Francisco
title: “Classic”
text: Stayed in the hotel for 3 nights in October. The hotel is old, but in a good way. You can feel the history of the place. The room we had looked out over the bay and the North Beach area which was stunning at sunset and sunrise. I would imagine some people would find the rooms a bit dated, but the hotel is over a hundred years old so we felt it just added to the overall vibe of the place. Our room had everything we needed, the bed was extremely comfortable and the shower was superb. The lobby and main hotel bar is stunning and probably hasn't changed since the hotel was built. The bar is a really great place to sit and have a quiet drink at night and there is the Tonga Room bar/restaurant in the basement which is a bit tacky but good fun. This was our first trip to San Fransico but we thought the location was ideal. Its a nice straight walk downhill to Fishermans Wharf and a similar downhill walk to the Union Square area. The walk back up to the hotel is obviously a bit more of a challenge but the Fairmont sits on a street which is serviced by the trolley's and you can easily get a cab so it wasn't a problem. I personally loved this hotel because of the history of the place and its location. If you don't mind rooms which are not ultra modern then I'd highly recommend it to anyone!

name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel
title: “What I expected!”
text: Typical 4 star hotel. I expected the hotel to be a bit closer to Union square. It is actuially on top of nob hill neat to the fairmont. Didn't think it was at all "worn" as some of the reviews say. I did notice a bit of noise. I could hear the doorman blow his whistle for a cab. 10 minute uphill walk from Powell BART station. Overall good stay

name: The Fairmont San Francisco
title: “Elegant, Sophisticated - Spectacular SF Views”
text:
Plenty of hotels to choose from in SF, but the Fairmont really gets it right: serious quality in the bed linens, decor and attention to detail in the rooms. If the budget allows, spring for a Gold Level room - breakfast, snacks, hors d'oeuvres and drinks in a private, concierge level lounge.
My last trip, we had a corner room with City views: quality bed, linens, seating and desk - the bathrooms are a bit dated (sorry Fairmont), but in every other aspect the rooms are splendid.
Not hip and chic (aka pounding music in all the public spaces) and many of us locals miss the Tikki Lounge; but there are so many bars/restaurants within a 5 minute walk or cab ride, you truly are spoilt for choice. Highly recommend the big buffet breakfast - amazing choices and will set you up for the whole day.
This is a fairly big hotel, but the service levels are excellent: my last trip was staying there after a business event, and they even let me check in at 2pm to drop off bags.
Fairmonts are always good, but this one really excels - even though we're local to the area, it is a great place to stay for a weekend 'away' - easy walk to Union Square and the shops (downhill!) - and don't feel bad about splurging on a short cab ride back at the end of the day - everyone does it. Or take the Cable Car.

name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel
title: “Great Location! Great Price! Superb Staff!”
text:
I just got back from a six-night stay at the Stanford Court. I was totally pleased with the hotel. The rate was great...$170/night. I also stayed on the eighth floor and did not detect any odors whatsoever. The room (also interior facing) was more than adequate...with nice touches such as gym equipment brought to your room if you did not want to go to the fitness center. But what impressed me most was the staff. They were consistently and uniformly wonderful. It seemed that no favor was too big to ask of the staff and that they really wanted to make sure that you enjoyed your stay. 
Was the room the biggest room I ever stayed in? No. Is the hotel the most deluxe hotel in San Francisco? No. But it was extremely comfortable and I would not hesitate to stay there again and would strongly recommend it to others. The ONLY problem I encountered was with the shower. It reminded me of the shower in my college dorm...anytime somebody flushed the commode in another room, the pressure would noticeably drop. Other than that, I truly enjoyed my stay there.

name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel
title: “Fantastic Service”
text: My financee and I stayed at the Renaissance Stanford Court (12/01 to 12/05). What a great hotel for a great price. We did priceline and paid $75/night. As soon as we arrived, the person behind the desk voluntarily upgraded us to a deluxe room. The bed was so comfortable and the bedding set was so great we want to buy the same set for home. The whole staff was simply the best. From the turn down service with chilled water at your bedside, to the complimentary town car service, you will be glad you stayed there.

name: Radisson Hotel Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Radisson...wonderful”
text:
Very friendly and helpful staff. Wonderful room. Sleep Number Beds are the best.
Great View. Close to everything. I would highly recommend the Radisson.

name: InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco
title: “Beautiful Hotel with Elegance and History”
text:
The experience was smooth and professional from start to finish.
