The person who booked my room over the phone was eloquent, professional and helpful. when I arrived, the doormen, bellmen, front desk staff, wait staff, and everyone else were all very professional and inviting. The room was clean, neat and well-stocked. Though it was an older building, there was no musty or dusty smell. I had a drink at the legendary Top of the Mark and enjoyed every sip. 
I love older hotels with charm, so this was a perfect stay for me.

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “Fantastic view and central location”
text: We stayed in a bay view room on level 28, and while the room was nice enough, the view was what made it memorable. We thoroughly enjoyed the fantastic view of the bay, Alcatraz, Coit Tower and the TransAmerica building. As the hotel is currently undergoing renovation of its lobby, we got a stay 2 nights, get the third free including breakfast so it was excellent value (with exception of the wifi at $10/ day). The union square location was very central, with a short walk to china town and north beach.

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “Good Hotel in good location”
text:
We started our recent travels in the Grand Hyatt. The hotel is under going renovations of its reception area however all of the room have been restyled. Our room was on the 17th floor and we had a good view of the city and could see the water between the buildings.The room was a good size and clean and there was everything that you required within the room. However ladi
es if you go to use the hairdryer you may have a problem as the lead to the hairdryer is so short I was unable to blow dry my hair, this was not a problem as I had brougth my own. 
We had a meal in the restaurant located on the top floor of the hotel which gave us a spectactular view over the city to the bay. The food was good and service was also good.
The hotel is located by Union Square which is a good location for transport and to get to all area's of the city.

name: San Francisco Marriott Union Square
title: “Excelente ubicacion”
text: Estuvimos a finales de noviembre en este hotel, las habitaciones son amplias mas no asi los baños, la limpieza es buena y la atención excelente. Al lado del hotel queda una estacion del tranvia, a dos bloques queda el barrio chino y a un bloque queda la plaza de union square, realmente muy buen lugar para tener todo al alcance.... no necesitas vehiculo porque todo queda cerca en tranvia, en taxi o caminando.... para desayunar recomiendo un lugar en la esquina con estilo en los años 60... también hay un restaurant japonés hacia atras del hotel que tiene muy buen sushi.... se los recomiendo altamente

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “service not good, noisy hotel”
text:
First impressions were not good. We pulled up to the hotel to unload our bags etc and the doormen stood and watched, clearly a spectator sport. We unloaded our stuff and walked into the hotel, opening the doors ourselves as everyone was clearly too busy to assist us. The first person to ask if we needed help was the security guy once we had got into the enormous lobby.
Room was ok, nothing special and quite small. We had to ring up for the key to the mini bar as they had not given this to us. We were also told by the front desk that wi-fi was free in the reception, when we tried this out it didn't work and when we asked we were then told there was a charge. The guy did then give us a code to give us free access to wi-fi for our 3 day stay.
It was noisy in the evenings with people running up and down the long corridors and shouting.
In fairness we were not too bothered as we had booked via Hotwire and got a good deal, had i paid the full rack rate I would not have been at all happy with this hotel.
It is in a good location and Starbucks in reception is easy for breakfast coffee as the free coffee in the room is awful.

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “High-class hotel with great service in a wonderful location.”
text: The Hilton is in the heart of San Francisco, walking distance from Union Square, downtown, and transportation to all other areas. The rooms are beautifully re-done and the service was excellent.

name: Le Meridien San Francisco
title: “Can't go wrong”
text:
I'll echo what others have said. Nice rooms, very comfy beds, stylish decor and helpful, friendly staff. Floor-to-ceiling windows offered a nice view of the bay and the TransAmerica Pyramid, even from only the 11th floor. Free business center was a nice touch.
Location is a bit off the tourist path, but you're within 5-10 minutes of Chinatown, the Ferry Building, Coit Tower, North Beach (including City Lights) and the California St. cable car. The Powell line and Union Sq. is close by as well. We also walked to Fisherman's wharf in around 20 mins.
Note that on weekends the immediate area shuts down. The Starbucks across the street is open, but not much else is. But it gets quiet, which is nice.

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “Feel like Home”
text: I have booked two rooms on the Nikko Floor (24th floor) with access to the Club level on the 23rd. fl. The rooms are very clean and comfortable. The atmosphere is quiet and peaceful. Though the beds are a bit small, the decor is modern. The club level is very clean and well kept. My child of 11 yrs. old has great fun in using the free internet access before bedtime. The staff is courteous and sincere, especially the ones in Anzu Rest. and the valet parking. The free breakfast buffet (for Nikko Fl. guests) is excellent. However, the food at dinner time is really not worth the money. I have stayed in many other 5 stars hotels before. Hotel Nikko somehow provide a feeling like home.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “Central location near union square”
text:
Upon arrival we were upgraded by Andre to a junior suite. This room was lovely and also granted us access to the club lounge with free breakfast, evening snacks and desserts- very nice. It also has amazing views of the city. The room itself was large and had a sofa area and a treadmill ! 
The hotel is centrally located near union square and Powell station. We paid 8 dollars for a Bart train to the airport and were quoted 60 dollars for a taxi so recommend this is you want to save money as it stops outside the hotel and is direct. 
The rooms could do with some updating in my opinion, they are a bit dated and the safe didn't work in ours. We reported this on day 1 but when we left on day 4 it wasn't fixed. 
All in all I would stay here again and recommend as it's very central, staff are friendly and it's reasonably priced.

name: The Kensington Park Hotel
title: “Great place”
text: I booked my stay the app Hotel Tonight. The room was very clean and spacious, with a comfortable bed, very adequate bathroom, great location and friendly staff. There were nice amenities in e bathroom like makeup remover. I was able to check in early and take a nap before walking to BART to go to the opera. It was great to be by Union Square and enjoy the Christmas decorations. I will stay here again even if I have to pay a higher rate.

name: The Kensington Park Hotel
title: “dissapointing!”
text: The facility is very old, smell humidity in the lobby and the halls,clean rooms and baths, spacious but no A/C in the rooms and noticeable bad plumbing and electric connections, great location, close to Chinatown, Union Square, Embarcadero, Financial District, and bars and restaurants. $39 valet parking service available (20-30 mins waiting time). Great customer service and very important the pictures in the web look better than reality.

name: Hotel San Jose
title: “One of a kind, but don't expect warm fuzzies”
text:
We stayed last night not realizing the intensity of the hod rod festival going on. When we made the reservation, we were told hotel parking would be for classic cars only and we would have to park on the street. Fine. But we had no idea of the number of cars and people. Nick, the parking guy was kind enough to give us 30 minutes in the parking lot to take a shower and get ready. However, the front desk was lackadaisical and seemed to think that it was OUR privilege to stay with them. We got ready in the allotted time and Nick directed traffic enough to get us on our way to the burlesque festival (THAT'S another review!). By the time we came back (around 1AM) there was a space on the street in front if the hotel.
The room was cool(important in Austin), clean and welcoming with several personal touches that made it stand out. Lotion, shampoo and conditioner that were earth and people friendly. There was a free bottle of Rainwater (local Austin water) to try. There was a box with everything you might need: sewing kit, first aid and intimacy kits. Simple touches that meant alot to a traveler. There was also a small fridge. 
Even though there was alot of noise with the event, our room was quiet and comfy until the morning when there was a constant singing noise that woke me. Pipes?
We wanted to eat breakfast there in the quaint courtyard, but it was not open, so we went to our old standby, Magnolia Cafe. There is room service available as well. 
Rooms are tucked into a maze of cement, wood and plants. You feel like you're a kid in a secret place...an Austin jewel if they can warm up a bit. May have been the event wearing on their nerves, but staff need to remember that the customers are why they have jobs....
We will come back for another stay soon. It's pricey, but you're paying for the ambiance, not the amenities.
Furnishings are very simple, but they have everything you need.

name: W San Francisco
title: “Try the St. Regis”
text:
We stayed 3 nights in early January for a mini holiday.
Check in was easy; we had a late arrival and received immediate attention. Valet service was prompt during the entire stay. 
The room itself was lovely; spotlessly clean and with a beautiful view of the bay. (There is ongoing construction that threatens to block this view in the future). Found the usual amenities in a W - Bliss products, two soft robes, blow dryer, mini-fridge, coffee maker and a range of DVDs for rent downstairs. All were in working order. 
I was sick during the stay and found the whatever, whenever service fantastic when I needed Tylenol at 2 A.M. and didn't want to leave the hotel to find a drugstore. 
On that note, I really needed a quiet night's sleep and was disappointed to hear noisy, intoxicated guests in the hall on Fri./Sat. night. In addition, every morning the maids let the doors slam going in and out of the rooms across the hall making it impossible to sleep.
Concierge service was very slow. I asked for directions which one woman said she was printing for me. I waited to the side while she helped other guests and after 5 minutes she asked "What did you need again?"
The music played throughout the hotel offers the trendy, nightlife ambiance the W is known for, yet on a Sunday morning the same music and blue lights in the hallway give the hotel a garish feeling.
Yes, the location next to MOMA is great and you can walk to Union Square, but next time I'll stay at the St. Regis.

name: Metro Hotel
title: “Great cheap option without the cheap hotel feel!”
text:
This place was wonderful! Since the hotel was in thw neighborhood I used to live in...it was sort of like being at home. 
Good things: 
1. It is really clean.
2. The staff are super helpful and friendly.
3. There is a super cute patio out back where my friends and I enjoyed a beer after a long day of exploring our favorite places in San Francisco
4. Our room was quiet...and bigger than we expected after reading some reviews...this is a big city in a small area so rooms are small in SF!
5. We easily found street parking to leave our car for the weekend.
6. The hotel is located in a safe, central location with easy transportation options to other areas of the city.
7. We had free wifi so my husband could do some work at night when we were just chilling out.
Downsides:
1. We smelled pot in the hallway one evening....I am pretty sure those people were gone quickly because we came back through a short while later....smell was gone and did not return.
2. Our bedroom door was a little funky and would not close properly on it's own.
Yep....that's it! Nothing too exciting to complain about. I would definitely stay here again and HIGHLY recommend it to friends and family visiting the city!

name: Cornell Hotel de France
title: “I love this place, yet it needs a little help”
text:
This was my second stay at the hotel since the first 3 years ago. I continue to love this place. Charming, small, family-run hotel close to Union Square with a terrific american breakfast with table service that comes with the room. Our room was on the first floor in the rear of the building, across from the owners quarters. I am wondering if it was previously the owner's quarters as it had a stale odor of dogs. Yes, the owners have two on the premises, but you rarely see them. As a dog owner and lover myself, it is so easy to get used to your pets' smell, and therefore never notice the smell your home acquires. I think the owners have fallen into this trap, as at the end of the trip, I too got used to the smell. However, I am sure this smell will turn other travelers off and sincerely wish that they would take this problem seriously. I doubt this other floors have this problem. And, yes the rear of the building is very quiet.
My other recommendation is that the hotel owner try to iron a dress shirt on the ironing boards that they supply at the hotel. They are the little flat things. I asked the staff if there was a normal sized board available and they told me that they got rid of all of them. They should keep at least on full sized ironing board for those of use who really need it. We could at least return it to housekeeping when we were done.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “Best Hotel in SF for the value seeking guest”
text:
Stayed at this hotel Jan 31st/Feb 1st on business. Reason for selecting this hotel was purely best price for the location without compromising on quality.
This hotel was a pleasant surprise! Lobby was very modern and clean, front desk check-in was easy, pleasant, staff member very helpful. Stayed in room 1872 which is a corner room and it was excellent. Windows on two sides, terrific view of City Hall and the city. The bed was comfortable, room was clean, and included large flat screen tv. Only the bathroom was a bit lacking, (rather old looking, simple, no lighted makeup mirror, could use some hooks on the wall for hanging towels, some mold in the grout in the shower/tub combo (pet peeve), but it was large size so not clausterphobic)
Hotel is within easy walking distance of restuarants, shopping at Union Square and bart, which was good, as we did not rent a car from SFO airport.
Ate breakfast at the restuarant adjacent to the lobby. Standard/higher price for breakfast, but service was quick, friendly, food good).
Will stay here again in the future.

name: InterContinental San Francisco
title: “They work hard to make guest happy”
text: This is my second time visit to the hotel, however, we encountered an unexpected situation we didn't get the room on the club floor as we planed and booked more than 7 months ahead. Make the long story short, the manager Jasmin Glueck learned my situation, although there was nothing can be done on room issue, I could feel that she took my disappointment seriously and valued my opinions, at the end she was able to took some measurements to make me happy and satisfied. I will definitely come back and recommend this hotel to anyone as they know how to treat their guests.

name: Metro Hotel
title: “Great location, budget friendly, simple”
text:
I came into the hotel with the understanding that is a no frills hotel, and I got what I paid for - to be in a great neighborhood out of downtown. The receptionist was nice and recommended spots to park my car. It's within close distance to some great restaurants, and a quick walk to the lower Haight, Castro and Hayes Valley where there's plenty more great bars and restaurants. Pay close attention to street signs because I ended up getting a $55 street sweeping ticket. After a certain hour, 5pm, parking overnight is a pain to find but that's to be expected in that neighborhood. They have a loading zone right in front of the hotel, so take full advantage of it before you look for parking. The walls are very thin so I heard some guy talking I think in the next room, and people stumbling in at 4am on the 1st floor. There were some dirt marks on the carpet, and the heat wasn't very controlled when I first got there so I had to use the ceiling fan. The decor of the room is very outdated 80's motel like with a tube tv. The pillows were thin, and the blankets even thinner but there are spare blankets in the closet. 
It's a great place to go if you just need somewhere to crash. But I can't say I got a good night's sleep. I didn't really relax there, because I was out most of the day. I'm not sure if I'd stay there again.

name: Hotel San Jose
title: “Hip Trendy, Snobby Staff”
text:
After reading the reviews of this hotel on TripAdvisor I felt I knew what to expect of this hotel. Other reviews commented on the fact that this was a very hip, trendy hotel for the see and be seen set. Other comments were in regard to the hotel staff being very full of themselves. I booked a garden suite in this hotel because of the location and style as I was coming to Austin to get ideas for my business (restaurants)
I arrived in Austin around 11am. I went to the hotel to check in. I knew I was way early, but wanted to just let the hotel know that I was arriving and if there was some slim chance my room was ready it would have been nice to drop off my luggage before setting out to explore Austin. 
Before uttering even a friendly hello the front desk person said "IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO CHECK INTO YOUR ROOM BEFORE 3PM". I thought back to the reviews on TripAdvisor and thought "yup, exactly as I expected". After I explained that I did not expect to check in that early that I just wanted to give my info this man changed his tune. He then tried to be overly syrupie to make up for his rudeness. It seemed very fake and I didn't buy into it. The other staff members I encountered were very friendly however. But some of the staff could use some customer service lessons! All the first guy needed to say was "I apologize, your room is not quite ready" and I would have been pleased. He did offer to call me once the room was ready. They called at 1pm....so it WAS possible afterall to check in before 3pm! 
The grounds of this hotel are spectacular. Very nice, very well designed. The rooms are very stark. Hard, bare, concrete floors. Uncomfortable modern, IKEAlike furniture. We asked for an ironing board and were given a college dorm styled, small ironing board. This would have been ok if there was anything to place it on near a plug. We ended up putting it on top of the bed, very inconvenient. The TV is mounted on a wall with a swing arm, nice touch, but it can't be watched from the bed and sitting area at the same time. 
The location could not be better. South Congress is a very cool area of Austin. Loads of fantastic restaurants and shops within walking distance. 
The pool area becomes a nightclub type setting at night with DJ's spinning music and uber trendy types sipping wine and beer. I'm glad I didn't have a room facing this area as it would have been way too loud as this goes on to midnight. 
Overall, the Hotel San Jose is what it is and if you're the type of person that enjoys style over comfort and don't mind paying for it, this place is for you. I love good style, but for $300 a night I'll stay at a 4 star hotel next time.

name: The Huntington Hotel & Nob Hill Spa
title: “Great Stay, Enjoyed thorougly”
text:
I stayed here with my wife in May 2012. We booked through American Express Platinum and were upgraded to a suite on the top floor with northeastern exposure. Our flight from NYC landed late thursday night so we grabbed dinner and drinks at the hotel bar downstairs where it appears they always have a pianist entertaining the patrons. It was an older scene with most people in their late 60's but it was a nice old bar. This same room is where breakfast is served every morning. The breakfast was great for an American city hotel breakfast. The location was great for taking the trolly to the wharf (I believe it was a 3 block walk to the trolly with level terrain). Coming from west side to the hotel is a steep climb but the rest of the area is fairly easy to walk around. The suite we stayed in had ample space with plenty of light and three sets of blinds/shades to keep the room dark in the AM. Something that really stood out about our room is the windows opened. Since it was the top floor the windows didn't completly open, probably opened about 5 inches, but I am always surprised at how often I stay in a high end hotel and the windows don't open. I like fresh air and I also don't like breathing in the same air thats been stuck in that room for years, so having the windows open in this hotel room was a nice treat. 
I would stay here again and I would recommend to a friend.

name: W San Francisco
title: “exactly what you'd expect from a W”
text:
Great location (next door to MOMA, downtown and commercial - not an area with great San Francisco residential character), small rooms with great beds and shower heads, helpful concierge for restaurant reservations and directions. I can understand those who might feel out of place not wearing all black and being over 30-something, but we had a perfectly good experience there - being people who are 30-something and do wear a fair amount of black. 
We did not avail ourselves of any additional and probably overpriced services, such as the minibar, spa, or parking, and therefore were satisfied with the value we received.

name: InterContinental San Francisco
title: “Quite passable”
text:
Background/Location
My husband and I stayed here for two night (9/5 and 9/6; Wed and Thursday). We are from the east coast and were in town for a motorcycle trip. The InterContinential was within walking distance to where the motorcycle had to be picked up from and other activities our group was participating in (AT&T park, The House of Prime) and pretty easy to get onto 280 for travel. I chose this hotel over the group hotel because it was in a nicer area and I will pay a premium if it keeps me from getting accosted by all manners of riff raff. Didn't care about the proximity (or lack there of) to Union Square. A bit difficult to grab a cab in the area - Howard is not a heavily traveled street.
Staff
The staff was nice, although from the looks on their faces when we walked in (high vis motorcycle gear *not leather* and hair fresh from our sophisticated styling helmet), we would have been asked to leave if we hadn't been staying there. Motorcycle was self-park in the valet garage for $25 a day - well worth the cost of having the bike somewhere secure. Better than the eye popping ~$55/day for a car.
Room
Room was clean and spacious. I didn't pay for a view. I did not expect wireless to be an extra $15 a day charge, which seemed rather outrageous, but fortunately we had a great cell signal. Towels were very thin and of a poor quality. Bed was comfortable and we slept well.
Bar and hotel restaurant seemed to be rather crowded, but did not actually stop in for food or beverage. Mel's is just around the corner for a quick and edible breakfast in a 50s style diner.
I would stay again if I had a similar itinerary.

name: Le Meridien San Francisco
title: “Hip SF Hotel”
text: We stayed in a suite that was very nicely decorated with a big plasma tv that was in the center of the room so you could watch it in bed or in your private living area. That was the first nice suprise. It was such a pleasure to stay in a hip luxury hotel. I highly recommend this hotel since it's very central making cab fare moderate for going to different neighborhoods. Our stay was too short so we didn't have a chance to check out the bar in the hotel lobby, next time.

name: The Fairmont San Francisco
title: “Book a Tower Room for the Best Views!”
text: Lovely hotel, but the parking is very expensive. You can forget about a car, or else, you can find parking for a little less across the street. The service and quality of the hotel and guest room were excellent. I enjoyed getting my hair done in the hotel salon, and that was a lovely experience, also. The Tower rooms gave us a view from the Bay Bridge to Coit Tower and the entire Bay. Stunning!!

name: Cornell Hotel de France
title: “Charming”
text: Charming, great location, great breakfast, great price - will stay there again. I started coughing in the lobby and the manager ran out with a bowl of hard candy - that would not have happened at a chain hotel.

name: InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco
title: “Ne vous fiez pas à sa place dans le classement, top hôtel!”
text:
Arrivée:
Check-in rapide. Ayant réservé une chambre Club, on nous donne immédiatement le code d'accès pour bénéficier du WIFI gratuitement et l'on nous dirige vers le lounge afin de profiter de l'afternoon tea.
Chambre:
De style classique, confortable, vue sur le financial district, grande salle de bain, machine à café, tout y est. A l'arrivée on nous propose la clé qui ouvre le minibar. Les boissons étant gratuites au lounge, cette clé était inutile. Literie confortable. 
Lounge:
Agréable lounge situé au rez de chaussé avec vue sur California Street. Buffet petit déjeuner froid avec saumon, viennoiseries, fromages, charcuteries, fruits, le tout délicieux. Durant l'après-midi, l'afternoon tea y est servi avec une séléction de petits sandwiches et en début de soirée des hors-d'oeuvres et open bar de 17 à 19 heures avec Champagne et autre alcool. Le personnel du lounge est exceptionnelle, avec un accueil chaleureux et toujours un bon petit mot à chaque passage.
Situation:
A Nob Hill, au sommet de California Street. Préparez vous à grimper. Stop de Cable-Car juste devant l'hôtel. A 15 minutes à pied des grands commerces, à 10 minutes de Chinatown. Très bonne situation.
+++ Club Lounge
++ Chambre étage élevée pour la vue
- La nourriture du room service, lourde

name: Hotel San Jose
title: “A Nice, But Overpriced, Taste of Austin”
text:
The San Jose has a great location in the very interesting South Congress neighborhood. The hotel is nicely integrated into the street life - the sidewalk is often the fastest path from one part of the hotel to another. Nice outdoor spaces and an active outside eating area. Very friendly staff.
It's a fairly nice retro / hip design, which fits well with the image and neighborhood. It's a little off in some of the details, though. The mirror over the bathroom sink in our room is set so low that it's easier to shave your chest than your face. And the peppermint all-in-one liquid soap / shampoo comes across as more Motel 6 than Euro. Even the rooms at the back get a fair amount of traffic noise.
All relatively minor issues for a mid-priced room, but this one was not: $330 a night for a spacious but spartan one-bedroom. I'm used to paying extra for hip in Manhattan, but in Austin that's too high a cost for too little hip.

name: Hotel Mayflower
title: “great find”
text: This was our second stay at the Mayflower after 2009. The location is just perfect. It´s about a 10 min. walk to Union Square and the famous Cable Car that brings you to Fisherman´s Wharf is 2 blocks away. The hotel is quite old and some tiles might be broken but that´s part of its charm. The room had a nice size and also had a little kitchenette so you can make your own lunch or dinner if you´re on a tight budget. Right next to the hotel you find a little market that has everything even my beloved Kinder chocolate. Breakfast though is complimentary and better than most continental breakfasts I´ve had so far. The people at the front desk were all very friendly and helpful. The hotel offers its own parking garage which I was told is very tiny. Both times our car (Nissan X-Terra one time and Dodge Durango the second time) was too big but the hotel suggested a parking garage about 2 blocks away for 20 $/24 hrs. which is quite a good deal for San Francisco. For a little bit over 100 $/night this hotel is a great find and we´ll stay there next time we´re in this wonderful city.

name: Le Meridien San Francisco
title: “Class Act”
text: This is a very nice hotel. The front desk and concierge were very friendly and helpful. The room was nice with an bay view. I really liked the bed with the down pillows and bathroom. The location was within walking distance to the Ferry building and North Beach. We got the room on Priceline and paid around $180 a night. It was more than we like to pay, but the town was sold out. I would stay here again. I thought this was one of the better hotels in San Francisco.

name: The Fairmont San Francisco
title: “Staying in a vending machine”
text: The Fairmont has made each room into a revenue generator by installing spring loaded pads under the vast, yes vast, array of stuff it sells in each room so that should you pick up the plush toy, bottle of wine or can of soda you are instantly charged for it. This system is described in the best Orwellian language as "For your convenience, refreshments removed will be automatically charged," so don't dare try to use the very full refrigerator to put your sandwich in. Wi-Fi is $14.00 a day and parking $50.00 plus 14% tax. And there is no coffee maker! Stay where they actually care about your comfort.

name: The Kensington Park Hotel
title: “Great hotel, great location”
text:
We stayed at Kensington Park Hotel for the last 4 nights of our honeymoon. The staff was very helpful with our bags, suggestions of what to do, and providing us with champagne glasses, etc. when we asked. We stayed on the 10th floor in a corner suite and the view was great. There was some city noise, but nothing outrageous. The room was comfortable and clean, although the bathroom could use some refurbishment and the selection of cable channels as well as the quailty of the signal has some room for improvement. The complimentary coffee and tea in the mornings was nice, although make sure to stop by Cafe la Taza a couple doors down to get a freshly cooked breakfast. The hotel is within walking distance to the cable car and BART, and of course Union Square.
We would stay here again!

name: InterContinental San Francisco
title: “Very good”
text:
I stayed here for 4 nights and it is a nice modern business hotel. I generally like staying in a business hotels as I don’t necessarily need to mix with children and tourists.
It’s around 10 minutes walk to the main area which is good as I don’t always like to be right on top of things. The rooms are a nice size and modern. The club lounge is also nice after a day’s shopping to relax and have a glass of wine. It also has a big modern gym. All in all I can’t fault this hotel. It was a good standard.

name: InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco
title: “So stell ich mir ein Hotel vor!”
text: Eigentlich kann man zu dem Interconti nur wenig schreiben, da mit dem Wort "erstklassig" schon alles gesagt ist. Der Service ist sehr gut, die Bediensteten sind höflich und zuvorkommend, die Zimmer up-to-date und man fühlt sich direkt sehr wohl. Ergänzt wird das Hotel durch das Sky-Restaurant und eine erstklassige Lage innerhalb von San Francisco. Die direkte Anbindung an die tollen Cable-Cars macht es nahezu perfekt. Das einzige was man negativ anmerken könnte ist vielleicht der Preis fürs Parken, aber der ist in San Francisco generell nicht niedrig und wer in diese Stadt mit einem Auto kommt, ist selber Schuld. Wenn ich das nächste Mal zurück nach SF komme, definitiv wieder dieses Hotel!

name: InterContinental San Francisco
title: “Great Hotel/Location not so great”
text: The hotel is beautiful, the location is not Ideal!!! It is far from everything, best to stay at their other location "Mark hopkins" This hotel is more for business men wanting to stay close to the convention center. The service however was exquisite. The staff is more than helpful and they even brought me a new scale because the one in the room was not working. The fitness center is nice, however the food is not to my liking. Overall a good stay.

name: The Fairmont San Francisco
title: “Great Hotel with Great History, and Excellent Location”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Fairmont in May of 2010 for a part business/part leisure trip. This hotel was close to many of the different neighborhoods and was on a corner where 2 street car (trolley car) lines intersected - very convenient. The hotel was beautiful, I loved walking the hallway and reading about the history of the hotel - both in the "real world" and it's history in the movies. The staff that I interacted with were always helpful and courteous. We did all the major sight seeing while we were there - Fisherman's Wharf, Alcatraz, etc.., and we fell in love with San Francisco and the Fairmont.

name: The Fairmont San Francisco
title: “fantastic fairmont!!”
text: just back from trip to states with 92 friends and acquaintances , first stop for 3 nights was the fairmont. Was a bit unsure , going by the reviews , I don't know where those people stayed I was in one of nicest hotels I have ever stayed in. Beautiful room with fantastic bed and pillows , wonderful bathroom , the lobby was welcoming and comfortable ,the drinks in the bar delicious and the service friendly and profressional.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “Great location”
text: We stayed 5 nights at the hotel over the Christmas holiday and had 2 interconnecting rooms. The location of the hotel was just great, very central. We paid a little more to stay at the club level and had access to the club lounge. The breakfast selection was alright, they have starbucks coffee and a wide selection of tea, it would be perfect if there was some hot food. One of the butlers at the lounge, Mario was really helpful and friendly, he definitely made our stay at the hotel a lot more pleasant. The rooms are comfortable but do not expect 5 star furnishings, the rooms can do with a little refurbishment. Overall it was good value for money.

name: Hotel Mayflower
title: “Very nice place, very well located”
text:
It is not a fancy hotel, but it is a nice, clean, and comfortable place to stay at a good price. The location is wonderful! It is near everything but away from the hectic Union Square. The neighborhood is nice and you won't find scary people around when you go out of the place, just like fancy hotels around Union Sqare but surrrounded by prostitues, homeless and funny looking characters. The cable car station is a block away, pretty convenient.
The rooms are spacy and very clean. I loved the hand painted decoration. The owners are very friendly and helpful. They even have a parking place and they won't charge extra for it, something very rare around San Francisco. I am a picky person and I like to stay at a comfortable room. I recomend this hotel.

name: InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco
title: “Alt und Gemütlich”
text:
Altes Hotel auf dem Nob Hill.
Wir hatten den Aufhenthalt mit Club Etage (die sich im Erdgeschoß befindet) gebucht.
Das Hotel hat seine besten Tage hintersich gehabt. Die Zimmer sind recht klei( so wie man es in Loondon erwartet).
Die Lounge war gemütlich, aber irgendwie mehr nicht. Da bietet IC bessere Hotels an.
Bei einem günstigen Tarif sollte man zuschlagen; bitte immer wie fast überall in SFO kommen noch 40$ Parkgebühr dazu.

name: Radisson Hotel Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Wunderschöne Lage ist der größte Vorteil von Radisson Fisherman's Wharf”
text:
Wir verbrachten zwei Nächte. Die Lage des Hotels ist absolut perfekt!!!!
In dieser viertel Radisson lage ist am besten (besser als Hilton, Marriot, Holiday Inn, Sheraton und andere in der Gegend . Radisson ist das am nächsten zum Hafen (von einigen Zimmern kann man auf die Alcatraz und S.Francisco Bay zu sehen).
Hotels wie all die anderen Hotels in der Umgebung ist recht gering (4 Etagen).
Schönen Eingang, die Lobby und sehr nette Leute an der Rezeption.
Schwachpunkte des Hotels: 1. Es gibt keinen eigenen Restaurant und 2. die laufende Sanierung.
Hotel braucht wirklich eine Renovierung, dass der Januar ist "außerhalb der Saison" dauert gerade renovieren Zimmer im Hotel. Es sieht so, dass einige der Etagen verwehrt wird und die Arbeiter den ganzen Tag Wiederaufbau Zimmer und Flure.
Das Hotel hat auch seine Restaurant oder einer Cafe, die recht ungewöhnlich ist. Mir wurde gesagt, dass das Restaurant brachte keine Profit, denn das Hotel ist in der Nähe von vielen Restaurants und Bars. Es ist wahr, aber wenn man C.Carlson Concierge bist du keine Chance haben, bei einem kostenfreien kontinentalen Frühstück (Benefit für Club Carlson- Concierge Status).
Praktische Informationen: Die Pier 33 (Alcatraz Schiffe Abfahrt) geht zum ca. 10-15 Minuten. Hard Rock Cafe ist 5 Minuten zu Fuß.
Shuttle zum Flughafen (SFO) dauert etwa 45 Minuten. Kosten: $ 17/1 Person.
Das Hotel ist nicht billig und wahrscheinlich das wichtigste Argument der hohen Preise ist das wirklich der perfekte Ort.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “The best value for luxury in SF!”
text: This Hotel is a dream. Responsive staff and excellent rooms!

name: Hilton San Francisco Union Square
title: “Depends on your situation”
text:
This review really only applies to the executive floor rooms, which are $50 more than regular. They are on the top floors, in the tall tower. We were on the side that faces toward the Tenderloin/Richmond, so the view wasn't spectacular from the room. It was a decent size, but decor was very bland, the room didn't feel modern at all. Bathroom was plenty big, and nice except for the very plain shower/tub.
What made the stay awesome was access to the executive lounge. The view there is about as good as it gets in San Francisco. They have an evening reception and a continental breakfast there, although we skipped the breakfast for an expensive brunch at the Cityscape on the top floor. The food was pretty good, and as it's right above the executive lounge and our table was on the side facing downtown/SOMA/Bay Bridge, the view was amazing.
Our stay wasn't trouble-free, as the tub/shower water wouldn't get hot, and they had to send an engineer who spent 30 minutes in our room fixing it. They compensated us with a free pay-per-view movie, which I guess was nice, but I'd rather not have had to deal with it.
If you were in a non-executive room overlooking the Tenderloin, I can see how your stay would not be anything to write home about. But for us, it worked out very well.

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “Super emplacement!”
text: Downtown, près de tout! Déjeuner cher 24$/pers, la chambre était bien et très confortable, un peu petite peu être, très propre, la salle de bain elle était prèsqu'aussi grande que la chambre. Internet payant (comme partout) et piscine aussi 20$! Personnel très courtoit bon service.Très recommandable.

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “Awesome view and great staff”
text: I stayed in this hotel while attending a conference. I was first impressed by the enormous lobby! I later found out that tour buses actually stop by this hotel just for tourists to take their pictures here (made me feel special staying in a tourist attaction!). We arrived pretty late but were treated really well - we were given apples and bottles of cold water right there at reception! plus access to Wifi for free for the duration of our stay. Our room overlooked the Bay Bridge, very accessible to all forms of public transportation and walking distance to many sights and restaurants. It was also very convenient to have the car rental in the same hotel when we decided to drive to Monterey, Vallejo and Concord. The cleaning lady was very helpful and nice. We were just disappointed that there was no pool.

name: The Fairmont San Francisco
title: “disappointing”
text:
King room 377
I love the hotels positioning on top of historic Nob Hill. It is well 
catered for by all 3 Cable car lines.
After entering the hotel past the unhelpful entrance staff and 
ignoring the old smell, you see the beautiful grand decoration of a 
historic impressive building.
Check in staff are pleasant and extremely helpful as are the bell boys 
and the concierge.
The room is disappointing, as its a little on the small side and the 
cupboard smells of 1908. With views of another building the room is 
not full of natural light. The king bed is great, although not my type 
of pillows and the flat screen TV (cira 37inch) has a good variety of 
channels.
Bathroom is quite spacious considering the size of the room. I loved 
the shower with it's very good waterflow. Towels are fine. Miller 
Harris (lemon) toiletries are ok but smell of CIF bathroom cleaning 
products.
Unfortunately due to the positioning of the bed so close to the room 
door you can hear people walking past in the corridor also the light 
from the hallway illuminates the room so if u have a problem sleeping 
with the lights on... You can also hear the conversations in the 
adjoining room (thin Walls) which we contended with a Spanish family 
singing at all hours.

name: Radisson Hotel Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Gute Lage”
text:
Hotel über Internet gebucht, musste leider 2 h auf das Zimmer warten, trotz Wunschangabe einer früheren Übernahme vor 12.00 mittags.
Das Zimmer hatte 1 Queen-size Bett (nach Buchung), Schreibtisch, TV, Kühlschrank, Kaffeemaschine, Bad mit Wanne. Gratis W-Lan im Zimmer
Leider war das Bad bei der Übernahme schmutzig. Das Hotel wirkt allgemein sehr abgewohnt, auch die Zimmermöbel sind sehr schmuddelig und teilweise kaputt. Außenbereich mit Pool und Sitzgelegenheiten mit flackernden Feuer (sehr schon gemacht).
Concierge in der Lobby und Rezepionisten sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit. 
Nachts war es ruhig, trotz der Lage. Diese ist einfach total empfehlenswert 2 min zu Fishermans Wharf, Seelöwen, Blick zur GoldenGate oder Alcatraz. Aber auch Lokale, Supermarkt, und Strassenbahnhaltestelle direkt beim Hotel.

name: Le Meridien San Francisco
title: “muy recomendable”
text: Hotel muy recomendable: bien situado, instalaciones impecables y bien merecido el suplemento por habitación con vistas a la bahía: última planta, la 25, y una habitación enorme.

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “Toplage, zentral und doch ruhig”
text: Das Hotel liegt sehr zentral und doch ruhig. Man kann hier in dem eigenen Restaurant gut essen, aber auch in den anliegenden Strassen finden sich gute Restaurationen und Clubs.So ist der Fusion Club nur eine Ecke und Johns Grill ist nur eine Strasse entfernt. Im Hotel gibt es einen Starbucks, so dass man auf das Frühstück nicht unbedingt angewiesen ist. Zimmer war sauber und ok, allerdings klein da ich das freundlich angebotene Upgrade abgeleht habe. Bett war Queensize. WLAN ist kostenpflichtig aber im Starbucks kostenfrei.

name: Cornell Hotel de France
title: “Very Bad Experience”
text:
My wife and I have stayed here regularly and enjoyed it. However, this stay required that we be up at 3:15 am for an event in SF. Upon rising, we discovered that the shower was not operating. The problem was not 'no hot water'. Rather, it was no water at all. I tried everything I could find and could not produce even the slightest trickle.
I have fairly low expectations for hotels but, on this occasion, even those were unmet. Obviously, we won't be staying here again!

name: The Huntington Hotel & Nob Hill Spa
title: “Charming getaway for a staycation”
text: I am a Bay Area local. I recently stayed at the Huntington Hotel for a romantic couple of days with my squeeze. I had been to the Nob Hill Spa (which is top notch) many times before, but had never stayed at the hotel. The setting is warm and welcoming. The location is perfect for a stroll, shopping, and views of the city. The Big Four Restaurant has an old world charm (dark wood, cozy) with good (not great) food. The staff was friendly, though a bit less polished than you'd expect from a luxury hotel. We stayed in one of the lesser expensive rooms. The price was right, so I didn't feel particularly robbed when the refrigerator and one of the phones did not work. One thing to note for those watching costs, parking your car in the garage is $39/night. Being a local, I'm not sure if most of these hotels charge like amounts. The valet service, though, was swift and easy. They seem to put most of their resources in the spa. If you stay here bring your swimsuit. You'll want to relax by the pool to get the full benefit of this hotel.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “excellent location, but seriously($50/night parking)”
text: The Parc 55 is in an excellent location, literally across the street from the metro with shopping and dining in any direction. We watched Cirque du Soleil - Totem at AT&T Park and walked back to the hotel which was probably a 15-20 minute walk. We booked online at hotwire and when we checked in I asked for an upgraded room - for $40/night we got a 29th floor city view room with access to the Club Lounge on the 31st floor. Free continental breakfast, drinks, amazing views...worth the extra few bucks a night. So with taxes, internet, parking and the upgrade...what we paid on hotwire was cheaper than the costs we were charged at checkout. Worth it...for sure, but be aware that you pay for parking($48/night) and internet($15/night). All in all, we were very impressed with the Parc 55.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Great Hotel and perfect location”
text: Recently stayed for 4 nights at the Handlery Hotel in San Fan. The room was quite large and very comfortable and had all the necessary amenities (tea/coffee making facilities, safe, fridge). The location in Union Square is ideal with easy access to the major shops, as well as the cable car and many restaurants located close by. Concierge were always helpful and pleasant.

name: Radisson Hotel Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Fein mit Blick auf die Golden Gate”
text:
Das Hotel ist sehr gut in Fisherman's Whraft gelegen. Nah an allen wichtigen Sehenswürdigkeiten und mit einem guten Anschluss an die öffentlichen Verkehrsmittel. Morgens wird man zwar schon ab und zu von den Seelöwen geweckt, wenn man ein Zimmer Richtung Meer bekommen sollte, was aber nicht weiter schlimm ist. 
Vor allem das iHop Restaurant nebenan war zum Frühstücken immer eine Empfehlung wert. Insgesamt konnte man beim Parken noch einen Discount raus schlagen, da wir bei Anreise von den Preisen doch etwas überrascht waren. Ansonsten war das Hotel eher funktional für uns, da wir in drei Tagen San Francisco nur Wert auf eine Übernachtungsmöglichkeit legen. Ergo ist es empfehlenswert für alle die einen gute Übernachtungsmöglichkeit in einer hübschen/lebendigen Gegend suchen...

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “Hotel Nikko - super recomendado!”
text: Hotel muy lindo, moderno, cadena japonesa con toda la tecnología.Hab. amplias, las camas enormes y muy cómodas. Muy recomendable. Relación calidad/precio/hubicación/atención inmejorable.

name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
title: “da ritornarci!”
text: Il Nikko a S.Francisco si trova in una buonissima posizione, vicina al centro e, quindi, a tutte le principali vie per i mezzi pubblici. Ma, soprattutto, x noi è stato comodissimo perchè si trova proprio di fronte ad uno dei punti hertz. Le stanze sono di altissimo comfort...il letto è bellissimo! ke dormite! l'ambiente pulito, per noi è stato tutto ok! Ma più di ogni altra cosa è proprio S.Francisco che è meravigliosa, grande città, grande gente!

name: The Kensington Park Hotel
title: “Very unpleasant experience”
text:
I chose this hotel based on the reviews, location, and price. I stayed June 27 thru July 5th.
By the time I left, the place had become a Jerry Springer episode with some guy on my floor banging on the door to his or his ''girlfriend's'' room saying, ''come on baby, open da door.... come on baby open da door and lemme in", over and over and over. Then it would stop and then start again. I called the front desk about it and they said, "We'll send someone to your room." I told them my room wasn't the problem.
 The walls and windows at this hotel are so thin you hear everything in the room next to you and all the street noise below which goes on ALL night. There was constant pounding somewhere in or adjacent to the hotel for what seemed endless early one morning while sleeping. In addition, doors to adjacent rooms were constantly being slammed, and I don't mean once, I mean over and over and over as if the door wasn't shutting properly. This happened at all hours along with parents arguing and children yelling. The bedding was very poor and worn-out. Don't stay here if you have allergies! Free wireless internet was slow and completely down late July 3rd into the evening of July 4th. 
On the plus side, the hotel is in a convenient location and the staff were helpful and pleasant most of the time. The room description said there would be a mini-bar or frig. This was not true so I asked for one only because I have medication that needs refrigeration. The staff was good enough to put a small frig in my room although it was not very cold.
I'm glad others find this hotel satisfactory but I will not stay at this hotel again next time I'm in San Francisco.

name: The Kensington Park Hotel
title: “Average Hotel in great location”
text:
I chose this hotel based on the many positive reviews in TripAdvisor and am conflicted about how to rate this hotel My prejudice is to stay at 4-5 star hotels when possible. These were so expensive in SF that we tried the Kensington Park. So here are the pros and cons.
Pros: Less expensive, very friendly staff, superb location near Union Square, decent rooms, relatively inexpensive valet parking, great coffee and juice bar in morning, cool benches in the elevators
Cons: Lobby, hallways, and rooms a bit run down, street side rooms very noisy – especially at night (beware if you are a light sleeper), VERY small closet, inadequate air conditioning, door locks VERY noisy when closing – so whenever any nearly door closes there is a very loud clanking sound (beware if you are a light sleeper - our neighbor came "home" at 2 AM both nights, going in and out twice), Inattentive valets – they were not there most of the time, average wait of 15-20 minutes for your car to be brought by valet.
So you decide. Not plush but adequate and noisy.

name: Staybridge Suites Austin Arboretum
title: “Recommended”
text:
Convenient to the Jollyville area, close to the Arboretum - the location makes this hotel a better choice than the Staybridge further north on Research Blvd. The staff is accurate in book-keeping and friendly. Some rooms are due for a refresh, but this does not affect the quality of a stay. For walkers and runners, there are plenty of sidewalks. The Iron Cactus is a decent, but not exceptional Tex-Mex restaurant a 5 minute walk from the hotel (happy hour during the week). The rates vary wildly, mine was 119 one week, 122 the next. It often pays to check with a travel agent for contracts at hotels in Austin.
Chambermaid service was excellent, and they were tipped accordingly. Rooms are available from time to time on the lower floors - Staybridge Suites seem to have a one, slow elevator policy.
Staff was excellent, and not just in normal business - computer failure resulted in no expedited checkout, but staff emailed my receipt the same day.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text:
We stayed in the Handlery for our honeymoon last year... it was a nice hotel, with friendly staff and a nice clean room. My only problem would have been the noise outside as we had a street facing room, I complained to the manager and they offered us another room but it was smaller ( we'd been upgraded for our honeymoon) and they didn't have anything else available so we decided to stay put in the bigger room. I had to sleep with earplugs in as the street noise was extremely loud and that would be my only problem with the hotel. 
It was a great location right on Union Square and the travel links were excellent. A good hotel if you want to be at the centre of things.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Austin Mopac North
title: “Nice Hotel”
text: I have to say I was not sure about staying at this hotel, but it was close to the office I was going to. Boy was I suprised. It was a very nice hotel and the rooms were excellent. I would stay here again in a heart beat. The staff was very nice and helpful.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Austin Mopac North
title: “Schönes Hotel in zentraler Lage”
text: Die Lage ist sehr nahe am Zentrum, in direkter Nähe des berühmten Riverwalks... sehr zu empfehlen für einen Aufenthalt! Viel Spaß

name: San Francisco at The Presidio Travelodge
title: “Location is no excuse!”
text: So the location is good but thats as far as i would go. The linen was dirty, the fridge was filthy and falling apart and the room made my skin crawl. Cheap is no excuse for failing to provide basic hygienic conditions. Avoid.

name: Staybridge Suites Austin Arboretum
title: “Much more than I expected”
text: I knew this was a suite hotel, but I expected one big room with a half-divider or something like other hotels. THis was a full-on one bedroom nicely furnished and roomy. I knew it was a extended-stay hotel (although I only stayed one night) but had no idea how homey and accommodating it was. Every detail of what you might need for a long stay was provided, full kitchen, 24 hour sundries kiosk, plus free drinks and appetizers downstairs each night, big fireplace and lounge downstairs, even a book lending library. Front desk staff so welcoming and efficient. Really impressed me (and I do travel a lot). 5 stars!

name: Barton Creek Resort & Spa
title: “Amazing spa!”
text:
The property is beautiful and a lot of fun. The rooms are comfortable and clean. The spa and service was by far the best I have had so far in all my travels. I booked a half day of spa services and walked out with an amazing, blissful glow :)
A must for an amazing get a way!

name: The Fairmont San Francisco
title: “Wonderful Stay-Superb Service-Beautiful Room!”
text: I've stayed at the Fairmont before but this time was special. It goes without saying that the overall facilities of the hotel are elegant, the lobby is a work of renaissance art, the meeting rooms offer anything you could want and the ambiance is quiet and refined. From the time we stepped out of the car, through check in and up to our room the staff was superb. Nothing was left out from the instructions about getting around the hotel to how to hail a cab away from the hotel. Our room, in the tower, offered a sweeping view of San Francisco and was beautiful. Service throughout our stay was excellent on every level, from the restaurants to the doorman. The breakfast buffet offers eggs benedict and anything else you could want. The dinner menu is small but certainly adequate. The chicken club in the lounge is to die for. I was so impressed with this stay that we booked three future stays in the next four months. None of this service comes cheap but it's worth every penny

name: aloft Austin at the Domain
title: “Average at best - WIFI didn't work”
text: i stayed at the aLoft the last week of August and wasn't exaclty impressed. I had trouble connecting the the WIFI network on both my laptop and iPad. After half an hour on line with tech support, I was essentially called stupid by the tech. I've stayed at numerous hotels in the past month and this is the only one that didn't work. I was happy that the front desk did their best to make it up to me. If you've never stayed at an aLoft, it is a normally a nice trendy hotel. I didn't get a chance to go to the bar adjacent, but will on my next trip. Due to the front desk staff, I have decided to stay again on my next trip to Austin and give the aLoft another try.

name: Residence Inn Austin South
title: “Great place to stay-super friendly staff”
text: This hotel is a great place to stay. I cannot say enough about the phenomenal and friendly staff each and every one of them including the cleaning staff. The ops manager Daniel is super nice and helpful. I did have a small issue with my room but the staff expeditiously moved me to another room and the rest of my stay was fantastic. The location of the hotel is perfect for getting downtown and is right off the exit so easy to get back. I would definately stay here again!.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “Fabulous location, excellent service”
text:
We needed two hotel rooms for four adults. We arrived a few hours earlier than check-in, and the front desk made one of the rooms available immediately. We used the concierge desk every day, and their recommendations were superior. The restaurant/lounge was a great place for a quick breakfast in the morning or drink at night.
We would definitely go there again.

name: Country Inn & Suites By Carlson Austin-North
title: “Nice Stay in Austin, Texas”
text: I love these hotels in general and this one is no exception. Great rooms, and very friendly people. The breakfast is better than you get at similar hotels for the same price. Overall, I have no complaints. Located well... just about 5 minutes from downtown and the convention center. I stayed here insted of my downtown convention hotel. Saved some money and got a great room. Also, just another random comment... Country Inn & Suites have one of the better guest frequent stay programs. Lots of earning and redemption opportunities. Stay at the Country Inn, you'll be glad you did.

name: La Quinta Inn Austin Capitol
title: “Great Hotel & Attentive Staff”
text: My son is leaving Dallas to go to Austin College. He made a trip to meet with his FA rep. He stayed at this La Quinta. He had a wonderful experience. The staff is attentive. Management is excellent. Will definitely chose this hotel in the near future when I travel to see my son. Thanks La Quinta for taking care of my kiddo!

name: Best Value Inn Austin South
title: “Clean & Comfortable”
text: We were impressed with the cleanliness of the rooms, the beds were comfortable, had plenty of towels for 3 people. We ended up arriving later than expected, but there was no problem with check in. The amenities, location, and motel personnel were friendly and helpful. The total experience was great. I plan to use this motel as my stop over location from now on.

name: Crestwood Suites Austin
title: “Don't stay here! Horrible”
text: Pay more and go somewhere else! Mold on shower curtain, hair in bed, carpets dirty, halls stink. No business center. You can tell they are not cleaning the rooms thoroughly. Thank goodness only had to be here one night.

name: Budget Inn Capitol
title: “Do not go here”
text: THIS PLACE IS DISGUSTING, YOU CAN GET A MUCH BETTER ROOM IN THE SAME AREA FOR THE SAME PRICE!!! i went here and paid for a room, went to the room and saw how disgusting it was (it smelled aweful, the carpet didn't cover the floor, cracks in the floor, etc.) i went to get a refund and they WOULD NOT GIVE MY MONEY BACK. i left the hotel, did not stay there and still can't get the money back. THIS PLACE IS A HUGE RIP OFF. and there is a manager named RALPH GOODBAUGHER who is a snake who just wants your money and will hang up on you if you have a problem. THIS PLACE IS THE WORST.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “The only place I'll ever stay in SFCO!!”
text: This facility was SO easy to find, has a great location, amazing staff, outstanding food and drinks. The room was more spacious than most places I've stayed in the city, twice as big as the Sr. Francis Drake and much nicer. I'll never stay anywhere else when we visit San Francisco!

name: Crestwood Suites Austin
title: “DO NOT STAY HERE The worst experience.”
text:
This hotel stay has been one of the worst and I travel a lot. The room was filthy, towels, bed disgusting. And bugs on the bed and floor. Room and halls smelled awful.
When I took my complaint to "management" she showed no concern or care about the problems. Absolutely lousy customer service and respect for valued customers.

name: InterContinental San Francisco
title: “Beautiful hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Intercontinental for two nights in September for a business trip. I had many hotels to choose from in the same price range, but I chose the Intercontinental because it looked beautiful, had good reviews, and I had never stayed there. The staff is very friendly and helpful, everyone from the door men to front desk to room service. I was always greeted when entering and leaving the hotel. Check in was a breeze. The rooms are very nice - modern and clean. The beds are very comfortable and the sheets are sooo soft. The bathroom is well-appointed but a little dim. I do like more light when I get ready in the morning, but I just turned on the hall light and it was fine. The bathrooms only have a shower (no tub), but it is big and has good water pressure. I did order room service my first night and the food was really good for room service. The second night we went to a restaurant called Zero Zero which is just a couple blocks from the hotel. This is an excellent restaurant - gourmet pizza & pasta. I would highly recommend it. 
All in all, I had a very pleasant stay and would return to the Intercontinental again and recommend it to my friends.

name: Travelodge Austin
title: “disgusting”
text: this place is straight out of a horror film. there were used condoms on the floor when we walked into the room. probably the room was rented out to prostitutes by the hour for punjabs extra personal income. when we told punjab this he laughed in our faces. the beds were filthy the bathroom filthy the floors and walls filthy. this place was a nightmare. how can you accept money for the condition this hotel is in. i feel sorry for you.

name: Travelodge Austin
title: “GREAT VALUE”
text:
I stayed at Travelodge this past week because I was taking a UT Summer Statistics Course. Frankly, I was a little nervous because the price was so low. HOWEVER, this is a fairly new building, the rooms are large, there is a large 'breakfast room" with plenty of seating. The hotel includes free internet and free breakfast. The free continental breakfast consists of cereal, toast, pastries, and fruit. Plus coffee, tea and juice. The manager and staff were very friendly. Another big plus was that the number 7 and 10 busses stop right in of the door. The number 7 makes several stops on the UT campus. The only thing I didn't see was an elevator, so if your room is on the 2nd floor you will have to take the steps (but I can use the exercize). 
Location: This hotel is located next to the Highland Mall. There are some restaurants close by and fast food in the mall.
I travel a lot and have stayed at many hotels. I would most definitely go back to this hotel when I come into Austin.

name: Super 8 Motel Austin Downtown
title: “If you are looking for the basics, close to downtown...”
text: This motel is definitely nothing fancy, but serves its purpose. It is low priced, and close to the entertainment district/6th St. I had read some reviews that it was loud because it was on the highway, but I didn't find that a problem, maybe a different room would be different. The continental breakfast was just enough for a quick bite in the morning: bagels, donuts, muffins, fruit, cereal, juice and coffee. The hotel is probably a little old, but kept clean and staff was friendly. Only problem we had was sometimes water went cold/hot in the shower, but I know we were there when it was completely booked for ACL.

name: Howard Johnson Austin, TX
title: “recent stay”
text: okay for price. bathroom could have been cleaner. strange odor especially in halls. need to ensure odors are gone. also ensure bathrooms are very clean, no mold.

name: Comfort Suites Austin Airport
title: “Great Hotel”
text: Wonderful hotel. Beautiful inside and out. A real bargain. The room was huge, the free popcorn was yummy, and the location provided easy access to all Austin attractions.

name: Days Inn Austin University / Downtown
title: “Not entirely satisfied with our stay here”
text: We were given a smoking room (234) right next to the main highway. Neither me or my partner smoke and we weren't given an option of smoking or non smoking room, just given a room that absolutely wreaked. The furniture was old, tv old, bedspread stunk of smoke, carpet had stains on it and looked dirty. Upon check in we were not told about the complimentary breakfast or what hours it was served. This was our 28th hotel/motel stay during a 3 month trip around the States. We rate it as pretty much the worst. Looking back we just felt like a burden on the staff here. My advice would be only stay here if you need to, ask for a non smoking room before they just put you where they feel like. For a Days Inn I expected more, we've stayed at fantastic Days Inns all around the country, it's a shame this wasn't one.

name: Quality Inn North Austin
title: “Good value on short notice”
text: My friend and I went to Austin City Limits in September and booked our room at North Austin Plaza a month before the festival. All the hotels near downtown and Zilker Park were booked, so this was kind of the best option based on the remaining hotels in the city. It wasn't so bad, especially after spending all day in the heat and rain, having a spacious room with queen size beds and a decent shower was nice. The hotel is about 15-20 minutes (depending on traffic) from downtown, but it's right off I-35, so it's location was convenient. The room was comfortable enough for the price.

name: Candlewood Suites - Austin Arboretum-Northwest
title: “No Internet after 6 PM till midnight 90 % of days !!!”
text:
Candlewood is a quite decent hotel but have mayor issues with there cable / WLAN Internet. We stayed 6 weeks and nearly all nights, Internet was damn slow (3 KB/s) between noon and midnight. Unuseable !
Front desk was not willing to help - also they blame us for failure... stupid. Do not book if you like internet.
Also, one of the two gas grill were not cleaned for like 3 weeks - although mentioned at the front desk. IT was linving in the end I guess...
huge disappointment!

name: Candlewood Suites - Austin Arboretum-Northwest
title: “Major Health Violation and Sanitary Issues!”
text: On May 17, 2008 I was staying as guest at the Candlewood Suites Arboretum-Northwest Upon entering the bed and laying for a few moments, I began to notice an extremely odd and pungent smell, I thought maybe it was nothing and tried to ignore. After a little while longer, I kept noticing that same awful smell and I started to notice my clothes felt damp. At that time I got out of bed pulled of the sheets and to my horror realized I had been sleeping in a bed that was completely soaked in human urine! Absolutely disgusted, immediately contacted a hotel employee, CJ, who oversees the property after hours. He advised us that he spoke with the manager and he had said there were no other rooms available and we would have to stay in that room and the room would be compensated for on the hotel. However, to imagine sleeping in a bed soaked in human urine is something to make anyone feel ill in the stomach. CJ, then arrived with new bed sheets so that we could sleep comfortably on a hard floor. This is not acceptable by any means to expect that your guests will continue to stay in a room ON THE FLOOR that is has been contaminated in urine, no other solutions were offered, one of which could have been a rollaway bed or make arrangements for us at another hotel. In the morning at check out when we told the front desk clerk of the situation I am absolutely appalled at her treatment. She did not rectify the situation, in fact she told us "no manager is on duty on the weekends and you will still be due for your bill". Furthermore, she commented that her "housekeepers would notice something like that" implying that we were responsible and trying to get a "free room". We were too exhausted to deal with such incompetent staff and paid our bill and left. Again, it is not a matter of the payment for the room but the quality of service that was provided. In the morning we were never contacted by General Manager Clyde Wilder or the Operations Manager Sean Russell to rectify or even apologize for the experience. I have contacted the City of Austin Health Services and the Better Business Bureau to escalate this situation.

name: La Quinta Inn Austin Highland Mall
title: “Clean and convenient”
text: March is busy in Austin and we were happy to get any hotel at all with only one week's notice. However, we were quite pleased with the location, cleanliness, and price after searching many hotel chains nearby and finding them all full. We wanted near I-35 and near UT. We were pleased with the restaurants nearby as well (Pappadeaux). We will be traveling to Austin to see our granddaughter again, and will check out the La Quinta again.

name: The Fairmont San Francisco
title: “Pretty nice...”
text:
Stayed at the Fairmont for 4 nights. I was in one of the corner rooms in the new tower section. I paid $290 a night. Overall, a wonderful experience.
My room had a sweeping view of the bay from Coit Tower on one side to the Bay Bridge on the other. For this sweeping view, ask for rooms in the new tower that end in "9" (Rm. 69, 79, 89, 99, etc. the higher up the better). If you're staying in the old historical part of the hotel, make sure to ask for an exterior room not the ones facing the courtyard. Of course the higher the floor the better otherwise, be prepared to endure the street noise especially the cable cars that run past midnight! The room decor is traditional as expected of a historical hotel. Rooms are well-equipped with internet access, flat screen tv, iron, etc. The lobby, conference rooms, and other public areas around the hotel are beautiful, well-maintained, and full of historical photos and art pieces; worth looking at. The hotel staff for the most part are low-key but polite and responsive when engaged. They are helpful and very professional. 
The hotel restaurant serve good meals but very expensive but why dine in the restaurant when just steps outside the hotel are plenty of wonderful and unique restaurants to explore. There is a coffee shop a floor or two down from the lobby level, if you just want a quick cup of coffee and a pastry. The Tonga Room restaurant in the hotel is an interesting, kitschy place but worth peeking in and having a drink or two. 
Overall, I would recommend this hotel if you want (and can afford) to indulge a bit such as to celebrate a special occasion in San Francisco. It's an expensive hotel but in spite of what I paid for my room, it wasn’t as luxurious of a hotel as I expected. I felt like I paid mostly for the hotel address, to have the bragging right to say, "I stayed at the Fairmont." :-) But to some people, that’s reason enough to stay at an expensive hotel. If you're looking for value for the money and a more intimate, personal hotel experience, this is not the hotel for you. This is a large albeit luxurious hotel. You won’t feel pampered but you’ll be surrounded by the perceived trappings of luxury. But if you do choose this hotel for those reasons, you won't be disappointed.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “Meet all expectations”
text:
My first choice to stay in SF union square was up to now the Hilton O'Farrell . I decided to give a try to Parc55, based on the fairly good reviews here, and the fact that they had much better prices for my dates.
If you book early enough in advance, the have competiive packages, one including car parking: this avoids you 48$+tax / night extra . Nice deal .
I had a very large room, probably twice the size of a normal room, due to location around the emergency exit stair. The "normally sized" room however are of decent size. If you are above 10th floor, you will get a nice view. The rooms are , as stated on the website, recently refurbished. Everything nice and clean.
Personnel is very friendly and courteous: bell men, houskeeping staff, valet parking,..... They always address you by name (if they have it) and welcome you back . Nice change from the indefference at some other hotels. Housekeeping is swift and they look at the details (for example room service trays do no stay in hallways for hours or up to the next day ....as seen elsewhere).
Very good sleep quality : no noise from inside, very ecceptable noise from outside.
Only two negative remarks:
- parking is valet only, so it takes out some flexibility. Besides, the parking area is not that big and can be busy. The valet parking personnel however are veru efficient to clean up the are as quick as possible.
- internet . As expensive as other places (15$/day ar 50$/week). However, they have a real capacity problem. At peak times, the speed is awfully slow to non-existent (from 54 to ....1 or 0 bps). This is resulting in multiple pages loading failure and error messages. You have to give sometimes 5 tries to get your page loading . Clearly exagerated for the price asked.
In cocnlusin, Parc55 Hotel is definitely a very nice hotel to stay in San Francisco's union square. All -almost- promises that you can find on the web site are genuinely delivered.

name: Quality Inn North Austin
title: “Good Value”
text: We have been staying at this hotel for several years. It has steadily been improving in quality and cleanliness. We are bowlers in the TPEA tournament annually held in Austin the last weekend in June. We have a group of at least 20 rooms each year from Fort Worth and Houston residents. No, it's not the Hilton, but it's clean and pretty well maintained. They allow our group to sit by the pool or in the general area until late into the night and visit. This is great since we only get together once a year. The price is great at $ 45 - $ 55 a night. The back area has some rooms rented by the week so you may want to request a room around the pool area.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Great Location, Very Good Hotel”
text:
We chose this hotel because of its location, the price and the good reviews on Trip Advisor. We were not disappointed.
We used the BART to and from the airport - a couple blocks walk from the Powell station to the hotel. Lots of great restaurants, theatre (live), and MUNI stations very close. The location is great.
The price was very reasonable. We were given a room on the "historic" side of the hotel - the older side. Our room had one double bed and it almost filled the room - that was fine with us as we don't need a lot of space. We actually don't spend much time in the room anyway - other than sleeping. The room was very clean, the bathroom was very clean and it had a good shower, good lighting, hot water and lots of water pressure. The bed was comfortable. Our window looked out to an inner courtyard, but mostly we could just see hotel walls and windows around the courtyard - not a good view, but that is not what we were after. The staff were all very helpful and courteous. We 
used the adjacent Daily Grill for our breakfasts and it was very good - food and service. We would definitely book here again and would readily recommend the hotel to others.

name: Hyatt Place Austin North Central
title: “Very nice”
text: I was pleasantly surprised on arrival at this property. It is quite new, modern, very clean and was an excellent value. The bed was very comfortable and the free breakfast choices were very good. I will return when in the area.

name: Courtyard Austin South
title: “Great Place”
text: I bidded this room on Priceline and got a great deal. The room was fabulous. The bed was very comfortable. There were a lot of little niceties. A metal carafe for the coffee pot, the TV on a slide/pivotal support, a real closet, and a desk that has a pullout lower level so there is tons of room for all your junk and easy access to outlets. Near to the airport, a straight shot down Riverside to the downtown/Barton Springs area and access to 71 and all of South Austin. The front desk guys were great ( I love free cookies), but I gave 4-stars on Service because we had a "Do Not Disturb" sign on our door until 10:30 a.m. on Sunday and our room wasn't cleaned that day. I am sure if we had told the front desk they would have sent someone, but we were late getting back and just wanted to get some rest.

name: Quality Inn North Austin
title: “Extra Charge”
text:
Booked a room through Hotwire April 30, 2011 It's not the best area in town, not even close. Even after the "Renovation", it's still a dump. Like putting lipstick on a pig. I am glad I only had to use the room from 12am till 9am.
The biggest problem encountered was the extra charge posted to my Debit card 3 days after I checked out. I called the hotel and they said because I booked through Hotwire, thiere is an additional charge, that it was explained to me when I checked in. It was not and it overdrew my checking account triggering an overdraft fee. Had I known, I would have had this extra money in my account. I left a message for the Hotel Manager on May 3rd. It is now May 7th and no reply. 
If for some reason you are left with no other choice but to book this dump through Hotwire or Hotels.com, be prepared for an extra charge.

name: Quality Inn North Austin
title: “Nice rooms and a great value!”
text:
My wife and I decided to stay here for 3 nights based on mostly good reviews from this site. The location is very convenient right off of hwy 35. The lobby is really nice with a professional looking and acting staff. We got there in mid morning, but we were allowed an early check-in which we appreciated.
The room we had faced the pool which was nice. The room was very roomy with a seperate bathroom area. This is an older hotel with a few rough edges. The huge mirror in the bathroom needs to be replaced - it was in rough shape. The room was very very clean. The only exception was a few cob webs on the curtain rod by the front door, no big deal. It seemed there was always someone walking around and picking up the grounds around the building. Someone is doing a nice job of training the staff, I appeciated the staff inside and outside of the lobby making eye contact and saying good morning each day.
The hotel was very full, but it was still quiet at night. There is no breakfast included but they do have good coffee in the lobby. 
The free wireless internet worked well.
Check out went smoothly. 
We will stay here again the next time we are in Austin.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Austin - University Area
title: “It was nice”
text:
Quoc (that's his name) at the front desk helped me find my way around since I wasn't familiar with Austin. He was very helpful. 
The hotel is across I-35 from the University. Within walking distance. It is about 10 blocks away from the main downtown area. 
The room was clean and very comfortable although I couldn't figure out how to turn down the air conditioning. The buttons didn't seem to work.
I didn't realize it, but there are 3 Doubletrees in Austin. I went to a wrong one at first. So pay attention to the address.

name: Comfort Suites NW Lakeline
title: “Nice Stay”
text: We had a nice stay at the Comfort Suites. The hotel was clean and quiet and very convenient for traveling with an infant (microwave, fridge, separate sink, solid crib).

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “what a nightmare”
