text: After having a fab week in Hawaii and 3 nights in las vegas, i could not wait to see what san francisco had to offer.Arrived at the Handley at around 10.30 in the evening, and the first thing that hit us was the smell of the drainage in the hotel, had our key for the room could not believe the room it didnt look anything like in the book. The window was cracked from top to bottom and they had put tape over it , none of the windows locked properley and ontop of all that it looked like something out of the film Walking with zombies, as the only people who was walking the street was the homeless.M y husband and myself were followed and pesterd by them when we tried to go for something to eat but failed as we didnt feel safe.When going back to our room we got into bed, could not sleep from the smell of urine in the bed, up wegot and complained we were then moved to a room at the back of the hotel,not much better, but we survived the night. Had a meeting next morning with our Virgin holiday rep and she was marvelous arranged for us to be moved down to the fishermans warf in the holiday inn. Cant fault this hotel clean, loveley beds , nice area to go out in the evening.I advice anyone going to sanfrancisco dont go anywhere near the H andley as it just might spoil your hols.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Austin - University Area
title: “Nice and clean”
text: Rooms were quiet and very clean. The staff was very friendly and the cookie I got when I checked in was very good. The lighting in the bathrooms could have been a little brighter for putting on make-up. But overall, a great and clean hotel. Great location to get downtown. We love to stay here when we come for baseball games at Disch-Faulk field.

name: Embassy Suites Austin - Downtown/Town Lake Austin Texas
title: “20 minute walk into town and no bats”
text: Stayed 1 night in May 2012. Hotel met expectations with the usual breakfast crowd crush if you go near the ending time. While it's a straight walk up Congress across the bridge into the center, it is quite a walk to 6th where all the action is - allow 20 minutes. Big disappointment was - NO BATs. For the unenlightened, there used to be a famous "flock" of bats living beneath the bridge on Congress street. This is a major Austin tourist attraction and when we were there we went the TGIF's just on the other side of the bridge from the hotel to see them come out at night. Our waiter confessed that they had gone to Mexico on their usual migration, but had not returned. Something to do with climate change and the availability of insects, their food source. This fact seemed to be hidden from tourists because a large crowd still gathered along the bridge walkways to see them. If you're looking for the bats, suggest you check prior to see if they ever came back to Austin before you go.

name: Hotel Allandale
title: “Spacious, clean, reasonable, free internet and full breakfast buffet - Fantastic Value!”
text: Northcross Suites was a great find for my 6 day workshop. I was really confused when driving into the facility as it resembles apartment style living - not a boxy hotel. Nicely updated (don't expect extravagance) with full kitchen 2 separate TV viewing areas in my suite. There is an exercise room with a TV to help walk-off the time on the treadmill, stair climber or stationery bike and a great daily breakfast, freshly baked cookies and an attentive staff made my stay pleasant. There are 2 floors with no elevators so if you have a lot of luggage, be sure to ask for the first floor. I will stay here on my next visit to Austin - I felt like I was home away from home.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Austin Northwest
title: “Basic hotel, friendly, and good location”
text: We stayed here as it was in close proximity to a competition my son was participating in. The location was great - right off of MoPac and very close to 183. The hotel was very clean and the staff was friendly. Not a lot of extras here, but it is great for just spending the night. I was a little disappointed with the breakfast in the morning when compared to other similar chains. Overall, I would stay here again if I needed a quick place to stay.

name: Super 8 Austin/University/Downtown
title: “It serves its purpose.”
text:
It's not bad, but it could with a bit more TLC.
It's real problem lies in the fact that it is a bit far from downtown and Austin's public transportation is terrible.
You could constantly hear the noise coming from Interstate 35.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Austin - University Area
title: “nothing special and isolated”
text: The place is perfectly clean and the staff is nice but it's the restaurant is dreadful and I can't say much for the Denny's in the parking lot. There isn't really anything nearby either. So, I can't recommend this place unless you really desperately need a place to stay in Austin. I think you'd do better to aim for a less isolated spot. The walls are also thin so you can hear other people. My room wasn't noisy but others told me that they had rooms that looked over the highway and it was noisy. there's a cemetery in the back. As for a room overlooking that.

name: La Quinta Inn Austin South / IH35
title: “For the Price, Better than Expected.(Pets Welcome)”
text: This is an older motel, much like you would see built in the 70's. The rooms are small and furnishings outdated: But what do you expect for $69.00 a night in Austin. I was afraid it would be a coackroach inn but I was pleasantly surprised by the cleanliness of the room and no bugs. The water was hot in the shower and the bed was comfortable enough. There is nothing plush about it, but that isn't what you would expect at that price. If you are just looking for a place to lay your head and aren't going to spend alot of time in the room, this is an excellent choice to save some money. It has apool that looked fine and has a basic continental breakfast. There was free WiFi in the room. It is convenient to St. Edwards Univ. (about 1 mile), and about 5 miles from UT. It is 25 miles to the San Maros outlet malls. Pets are allowed at no charge.

name: La Quinta Inn Austin South / IH35
title: “Excellent stay”
text: We stayed there on June 19 and we were very pleased. This is our fist time in La Quinta and will definitely won't be our last. The room was spacious, very clean and the bathroom made you feel like you were at home. The pool was perfect.

name: Embassy Suites Austin - Downtown/Town Lake Austin Texas
title: “WE WON'T BE BACK!!! NASTY!!!!”
text: We are staying here as I tpye this. We have two rooms for our family and young grandson. This place is dirty!!! We let our grandson walk around on the floor barefoot in our room while our older kids are at the Davis Cup. His feet were black from the dirty carpet!!!!!!!!!!!!! The whole place, inside and outside is tired and in need of an overhaul. We will NEVER stay here again. We did get one night free, but this isn't what we are used to when staying at an Embassy Suite!!!!!!!!!!

name: Staybridge Suites Austin Airport
title: “AWESOME hotel”
text: This place is just amazing! Pet friendly, hot breakfast is free, super friendly and helpful staff, and free laundry service. We stayed in a suite and it was just like home but smaller. Close enough to downtown to get there without any problems and not have to have the headache of parking and traffic.

name: Radisson Hotel & Suites Austin Downtown
title: “Horrible Customer Service”
text:
Honestly, the hotel itself was nice and I have no complaints about my room or the physical hotel itself. The staff was even very nice and friendly when I first arrived... until an issue arose. I know that sometimes accidents happen and you just have to deal with it, and just because this happened to me doesn't mean everyone else will have the same experience, but I was extremely dissatisified with the way my situation was handled.
I used the valet service because you don't really save any money if you choose not to (something like $18 to self-park and $25 to valet). At some point while my car was in valet, it was damaged. From the looks of the massive dent and scrape marks, it's very apparent that someone, while driving my brand new car that hadn't even had it's first oil change yet, took a corner too sharply and hit either the corner of a wall, or some kind of concrete pillar or pole. Upon noticing the damage, I asked the valet who brought the car out what happened. He shrugged his shoulders at me and walked off. Although I was furious, I stayed calm thinking that the easier I was to work with, the better chance I'd have of them working with me and helping me. I reported the incident to the manager on duty who was extremely rude and short with me the whole time. When I tried to ask her questions she would either ignore me or give me some BS answer in a really rude tone. She only took one picture of the damage for the insurance company so I aksed if she would mind taking a few more from different angles. She rolled her eyes at me and told me the one she got was fine. She took my information but did not give me any of their information, other than the G.M. Executive Assistant's name (who would be the one to file and handle the claim). 
I was able to contact the Executive Assistant shortly after the incident, and she told me the claim had been filed and their insurance would contact me to get my statement. I never heard from the insurance company so I tried to call the EA again but she did not answer or return any of my calls. I ended up having to look up the number for the insurance company online, call the general number and track down my claim number and the person handling the claim. When I finally got in touch with the insurance agent, she was also extremely rude and short with me. A month went by and I heard nothing from the hotel or from the insurance company. I tried calling both of them numerous times but neither ever answered or returned my calls. I was finally able to get a hold of the insurance agent and she told me that they were waiting on the hotel's statement of what happened. Again, I tried to call the EA who again, ignored my calls.
Finally, after a little over a month of doing everything myself and running around in circles, I got an email from the EA telling me to contact the insurance agent. I called the agent and she informed me that the claim had been denied because the garage is a public parking structure and no one from the hotel is claiming responsibility for doing any damage to the vehicle. As I said before, looking at the dent, it's very apparent that it happened while the vehicle was moving so it had to have been one of the valet's who damaged my car. 
I just have to say, that as horrible as the whole situation is, I think the way I was treated and the fact that the EA and the insurance agent never had the audacity to return any of my calls or speak to me over the phone is more frustrating than the fact that my brand new car isn't getting fixed. That makes me feel like they know they did wrong and are too scared to face up to it. At least be able to call me yourself and let me know what's going and treat me with some kind of respect.
Like I said, just because my car was damaged, doesn't mean everyone else's will be. This is just a warning (judging from my own experience, and based on some of the other reviews) that IF you do run into some kind of issue, they would rather be rude to you and try to sweep the problem under the rug than deal with it and make sure that the customer is taken care of.

name: The Fairmont San Francisco
title: “Great hotel, great service”
text:
Was there for a long weekend. Stayed in the tower (the hotel has two buildings) Had phenomenal views of the bay, alcatraz and the Golden Gate Bridge. 
Found the staff to be amazing and extremely accomodating. Were there when you needed them, were not when you didnt. Even room service was very good.. how often do you hear that about a hotel? Would definetly recommend for vacationers and romantic weekends. Great location. Much nicer than the Stanford Court and Mark Hopkins, where I have been in the past. 
All of the cable car lines meet right at the corner btw. One quick hint, there is a little local restaurant about a block away called the Nob Hill Cafe. VERY reasonable prices (as it is not for tourists but locals) and very good food! Right next door is a convenience store as well. Just north of Grace Cathedral.

name: La Quinta Inn Austin South / IH35
title: “value for money”
text:
Thought this hotel was a good value for the price. It appears that the interiors have been recently updated as everything was clean, light and bright. No polyester floral bedspread! Bed was very comfy and big and clean. Noise levels undetectable eventhough hotel pretty full on a Friday night. Was on the 2nd floor and had AC on though.
The continental breakfast was the standard fare, all bakery items were packaged and not as good as a nice fresh baked muffin or bagel, but being all individually wrapped was a fair trade-off for someone who doesn't appreciate strangers handling their food. Ihop in the parking lot if free breakfast doesnt suit you.
The only negative was the location, eventhough it was technically "on the highway" it was on the feeder road at the junction of multiple highways. While this was good because it was close to roads, it didnt have direct access and was a bit difficult to actually get to, atleast for someone unfamiliar with the area.
Pros: nice, clean, quiet, free "breakfast" and allows pets, close to area attractions.
Cons: access a bit confusing, no fridge in the room, close to attractions but not walkable, 
Perfect hotel for tourists/visitors. Not an all-inclusive or "resort" property. Although pool area was nice, wouldnt use this place as a destination, but great home base for tourist after a long day of exploring.

name: Radisson Hotel & Suites Austin Downtown
title: “Rooms Are Dated...”
text:
I'm actually still at the hotel as I write this. I arrived yesterday and will be staying for most of the week. The ride from the Airport to the hotel is relatively quick. The hotel is located in the City of Austin and in a really good location. There are many trendy bars, and restaurants to frequent during your stay, and a nice walk along the river is soothing. The hotel has a Starbucks and Fridays restaurant on site, which are very convienient espicially for those who need their coffee "fix."
The check-in process was very easy and the front desk staff polite, and helpful.I stayed at this hotel last year around the same time and was pretty pleased with the room which overlooked the river and pool area. This time my room was on the opposite side of the hotel wiht views of the parking garage and street. 
I was quite suprised at the condition of the room when I entered. The room was "extremely" dated in dire need of a face lift. On the plus side, the bed is very comfortable and the shower powerful. But a little decorative upgrade would go a long way in improving the rating for this hotel. There are other options in the area, but on the pricy side.
If you are a Club Carlson member, wifi is free. If not there will be a charge. The lobby is a comfortable area with leather seats and beautiful fish tanks.

name: Radisson Hotel & Suites Austin Downtown
title: “Walked into my room to discover someone already sleeping in the bed!”
text:
As a mom traveling with a son to a rowing regatta, I was quite surprised to check in only to go to my room and find a man already asleep in the bed! I managed to make it back to the elevator by the time he was coming out of the door (equally surprised I'm sure) and proceeded back to the front desk to ask the clerk how this happened. My son already had his own key card to the stranger's room and was off with friends so I was concerned that round 2 of waking up this stranger would happen when my son went to what he thought was our room later.
The ONLY concern of the front desk was that there was another key card out with my son. No apologies or concerns for our safety. Nothing. I understand that mistakes happen, but someone should have at least apologized. 
Once in our OWN room, the noise from the street was so loud that we got very litte sleep throughout the night.

name: Hampton Inn Austin - North (I-35 & Highway 183)
title: “Great place to stay”
text: The lobby is posh. There is coffee/tea/hot chocolate available 24/7. Didn't wake up in time for breakfast but saw there was fresh fruit, cold/hot cereal, eggs, sausage, waffles, beagles and juice. There was a small pool, no hot tub. The room was very clean, thank goodness. Reading reviews of other hotels can be quite scary! The front desk staff were very friendly. Hotel is not too far from Chilies and Texas Land and Cattle restaurants. Will for sure stay here again.

name: Holiday Inn Austin Midtown
title: “Great hotel.”
text:
Not much to do in the area. I would suggest renting car if staying here. The hotel was really great. I stayed on the 9th floor and the room was very modern. The lobby had a great little bar in it with a number of tv's. 
The staff was really nice. 
Downside The restaraunt was not that great.

name: Ramada Austin Central
title: “They need to duplicate this in all Ramadas”
text: My partner and I stayed at this wonderful place for 9 nights, we had a wonderful time. The staff was top notch and extremely helpful for someone who had never been to Austin before. They helped us find attractions, places to eat and made for a very relaxing stay. Brian, Robert, Sam and Amanda and I know I am forgetting the rest of the staff but you know who you all are, were just such nice people to deal with. I would recommend this place to anyone going to Austin for leisure or business as a place to stay. It's close to downtown but far enough away that you do have to drive to places which is not all bad. I had worked in hotel management for 4 years and wish I had that staff to work with back then. Professional, kind, welcoming and friendly which you don't see much of anymore which is sad. It had the feel of a home B and B than a hotel with the personal service we got. Thank you and we will definitely be coming back often!!!

name: Hilton Garden Inn Austin Downtown/Convention Center
title: “Wonderful!”
text: Such a great hotel! Beautiful views of the sunrise from our room. Perfect location! 6th street is right there. Best valet! I couldn't have asked for a nicer hotel. So outstanding. The employees at the front desk were helpful and kind. I do wish the rooms had regular coffee, decaf does nothing for me.

name: Embassy Suites Austin - Downtown/Town Lake Austin Texas
title: “Good hotel, careless housekeeping”
text:
We just passed the Memorial Day weekend at the Embassy Suites in Townlake. Austin is a fantastic city, and the Embassy Suites was a good jump-off point for everything we wanted to do and see. Check-in was a breeze. Everyone at the hotel is pleasant and helpful. Free breakfast in the morning and free parking were huge perks for us, and we took advantage of the manager's reception one evening. This hotel is truly ideal for families and those who value spacious and comfortable rooms. Because of the way the hotel is designed - with all rooms facing the interior lobby, the noise level gets very loud. While we were staying there, an entire mob of band kids had overtaken the hotel, along with a wedding party. So throughout the night, there were a few stray phone calls and lots of noise, but it was all harmless. We didn't hear anything from our bedroom - so we really appreciated being able to shut the door and enjoy the peace and quiet! The bed is sooo comfortable. 
Location-wise, it's further away from some of the other downtown hotels, but we are good walkers so it didn't pose a problem for us. There is a bus stop right in front of the hotel if you want to head over to SoCo, and we hopped on the Dillos (free shuttle service around downtown Austin) too. It's also close to Town Lake, which is worth checking out, and the Congress Ave. bridge - where we stopped to check out the bats flying off at dusk, a MUST-SEE. We did use our car to visit the LBJ library and to visit the County Line BBQ on Bee Cave Road (amazing view, great food), and Cental Market (which sold me on Austin bigtime) but we walked or used public transportation to hang out in the 6th St. warehouse district and the shops and bars at South Congress. 
The only complaint we had about the hotel was that our room was left open by housekeeping after they had cleaned it! The room had been left open for a good 7 or 8 hours. We had a few valuables in the room that were too big to stow away, like a laptop and video camera. Nothing seemed to be missing but it really put a damper at the end of our evening and our holiday, and definitely made us feel less secure and confident about the hotel. The manager offered apologies, but didn't immediately offer to compensate us on our troubles. Ultimately, they did give us a discount on the room rate for the last night we stayed. And luckily, this happened on the last night instead of the first! 
All in all, we were satisfied with the hotel. If you're looking for luxury, you may want to check out the Hyatt, The Four Seasons, or The Driskell. But if you're like us and plan not to spend a lot of the time in the hotel, and appreciate value, free buffet breakfast, spacious rooms, and convenient location, then this would be a good bet.

name: Sheraton Austin at the Capitol
title: “Disappointed”
text:
While the hotel accommodations were very nice, there was one problem. When traveling I like to use the Bibles placed by the Gideons. When I found none in my room I called the front desk and asked for housekeeping to bring me one. Housekeeping said all the Bibles had been removed from the rooms and they did not know why. They said they would see if they could find one. Several hours later they called back and said they could not find one single Bible in the entire hotel. 
When making my next reservation I will check with the hotel and make sure they provide this service.

name: Radisson Hotel & Suites Austin Downtown
title: “Would stay again”
text: 3 of my girlfriends and I spent a girl's weekend in Austin and stayed at this hotel. The location was perfect, within walking distance of 6th street. We had 4 girls in one room and 2 full/queen beds and we had plenty of room! The housekeeping service was great (and we sure needed it after our first night out). The front desk service could have been a little more attentive. At one point when checking in, I had to wait at least 3 mins. before the Guest Service agent got off a personal call. The Business Center is a bit of a joke, it's simply a computer in the lobby. If you need more services, there are computers on the 2nd floor that charge by the minute. Other than that everything was handled well. We enjoyed having a Starbucks in the lobby, but I was told they didn't have the syrup needed to make the drink I liked both night we were in town. I would stay here again, overall, and look forward to my next adventure in Austin.

name: Holiday Inn Austin Town Lake
title: “I love Austin”
text:
We live only an hour outside of Austin, and visit Austin on a regular basis. Had the chance to spend the weekend and chose Holiday Inn-Austin town lake. nice, friendly desk staff. lovely room.
the soda vending machines on two floors did not work. The desk staff gave us the free sodas as a "quick nite time fix" to the problem. don't be put off by the older parking structure and elevator.
for anyone wanting a morning run or walk the park path along Lady Bird lake is literally steps away.
The hotel is close to the Captal, UT and all of downtown Austin,

name: Sheraton Austin at the Capitol
title: “Wonderful staff performance from Guest Services Super, Michecl Williamson”
text:
Great hotel with great staff performance by Michael Williamson. Clean rooms and wonderful staff as we checked in with our over-sized van which Mr. Williamson took care of as we could not get our van in the parking garage. Mr. Williamson told us we could park in front and he and his staff would watch the van. 
Mr. Williamson made our two night stay, for a wedding, wonderful. My wife and I will be back as now we have found the best hotel in Austin to stay.

name: Casulo Hotel
title: “Exceptional Service”
text:
I am a road warrior. I stay in hotels 300 days a year. I have stayed in all the major chains.
This hotel is a very pleasant change. It has an oriental flavor to the rooms. The staff 
responds immediately to any concerns. The Casulo Hotel is extremely clean. I have watched 
the staff clean my room ; they take pride in doing a good job. The bar serves meals at night,
and the breakfast is above average. The bathrooms are exquisite. This hotel was a pleasant 
break from my usual routine.

name: Renaissance Austin Hotel
title: “Great place”
text:
I had business in Austin and stayed at the Renaissance hotel. My room was very nice and clean. The bed was very comfortable. The hotel is large and open. You can see the main floor below from every room. Plenty of bars and food options in the hotel. The location is great unless you are wanting to see the downtown area. It is close to 360 and 183 so easy travel access by car to anywhere in Austin. The hotel is about 25 minutes from both downtown and the airport.
I would stay here again.

name: Hyatt Regency Austin
title: “Comfortable place to stay”
text: I stayed here with my family of five from august 23rd to 27th. My son attends UT and we have stayed at many hotels in the area. This hotel is convenient to everything. The view we had was of the lake and it faced the skyline. You don't get this view from other city hotels. We had a 2 room executive suite with an adjoining bedroom for $590 a night. Much better value then the single room at the Four Seasons that we recently stayed in. The staff was friendly and accommodating. One night we woke up to loud noises at 2:30 am. When we realized the people were not going to calm down, we called the front desk. Spoke to Josh who sent someone up immediately. I will stay here again.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Great Introduction to San Francisco”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Handlery March 2-3-4. We loved it ! 
The price was competitive, our room was small but very clean and the staff couldn't have been nicer!
From the minute we walked in we were greeted with big smiles and friendliness and when we left we were encouraged to come back soon. Desk staff Erica and Manny were great and John, the concierge was wonderful. he gave us good tips and directions that were flawless.
Saturday night we asked if we could change rooms because we had the neighbors from Hell and the change was made quickly and kindly. No questions asked.
We ate our meals at The Daily Grill and found the menu to be varied and everything we had was delicious. Again, everyone was very friendly and helpful.
We would go back again in a minute.

name: Barton Creek Resort & Spa
title: “Very nice resort”
text:
We loved our stay at Barton creek resort in spite of temporary power and water outages, beyond the control of the hotel.
The location is great, grounds are beautiful and the staff was friendly. Pools was nice and not overcrowded . There was a nice nature trail.
We would definitely return.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “An absolute gem”
text:
Knowing that the hotel was rated highly in advance we were not disappointed. Efficient staff and fantastic location are key reasons to it's success.
Excellent size room and very quiet after dark. We bought breakfast in advance and ate at the connected restaurant in the Hotel which was very good although not that cheap.
For 2 days however we went to Lefty O'Driscoll's 3 doors down the road and had a fantastic breakfast much cheaper and with more atmosphere. (If the local cops go there it must be good !)
Glad we didn't stay in Fisherman's Wharf which was great fun during the day but not so sure about the evening.
Location in Union Square is perfect for the shops and with the bus outside you can get to all the major sites very easily.
No doubt we will be back in the next 12 months

name: Barton Creek Resort & Spa
title: “An Older Classy Resort”
text: I attended a large business conference at the Barton Creek Resort and it was a very good experience. The service from the bellmen to the front desk to the convention team was friendly and excellent. The sleeping room was nice and comfortable and it offered a wonderful view of the hills surrounding the resort and the golf course. Room service was prompt, all the meals during the conference were on time, fresh and tasty. This staff really has their act together. The only thing I had a problem with was the slowness of the elevators in the short tower. They were extremely slow and one was broken down part of the time. Don't let this stop you because this is a first class resort by any standards.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “Hiden fees”
text: When you check in to the hotel the put a $100 a day hold on your credit card. That means if you are staying for six days they put a $600 hold on your credit card. The cable car is les than a block away. Every time I purchased anything from this hotel I was over charged. Such as the internet fee of $12.95, which I used one time, was charged $112.95. They did finally give me my money back. The purchase at the store, the price on the box of $8.99 and was charged $9.99. If you are on a budget this is not the place to stay.

name: Habitat Suites Hotel
title: “Very unfriendly booking policies”
text: My daughter wanted to stay at the Habitat Suites during a trip to Austin. Her arrival time was unpredictable, so we guaranteed the room to my credit card. Later I found she would be quite late, and I wanted to ensure the room would not be resold because the hotel took her as a no show. So, I called and asked to pre-pay the first night with my credit card. They said they could not charge a cc unless they had it in their physical presence. What?? How did this turn out? She was late. They charged my cc (without ever having it.) They close the office at 11PM -- she could not get in. We don't know if they re-sold her room, but we paid for a room she could not use. I have 35 years of experience as a very frequent traveler and have never seen such an unfriendly booking policy. Nice hotel? Who konws?

name: Courtyard Austin Downtown/Convention Center
title: “Hier stimmt das Preis- Leistungsverhältnis”
text: Guter Service - sehr freundliches und hilfsbereites Personal - recht gute Ausstattung - gute Lage, um die wichtigesten Sehenswürdigkeiten in Austin einfach zu erreichen - würde jederzeit wieder hier übernachten

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Very average hotel in superb location”
text:
Stayed 4 nights at the beginning of November after 3 nights in Las Vegas. Arrived at hotel and requested non smoking quiet room, we were given a tiny double room at top of building which stunk of smoke, went back to reception and he then moved us to another double room on 3rd floor which was slightly larger, smoke free but not enough room to turn in the bathroom and really dark and old fashioned. Again we went back to reception and asked about Club Rooms which I had read about on web site, he let us have a look at one and we took it. It was a lot better than the others, the room itself was big with a very comfortable bed and overlooked the swimming pool. The bathroom again left a lot to be desired and was very small but we had a small dressing area outside it so overcame that problem.
The common areas of the hotel away from reception look pretty worn and tatty. The concierge was the most unhelpful person I know he did not seem to know what was going on anywhere or be able to advise on anything we wanted to know. 
The restaurant next door called Daily Grill serves some good food and not too pricey and always busy with good atmosphere. If you want a real American blow out breakfast suggest you go to Mama's by Washington Square. 
Overall the location is excellent you are right by all the transport and shops but the hotel is very average and not what we expected from an American hotel.

name: Radisson Hotel & Suites Austin Downtown
title: “Do NOT stay here - much better options for your money”
text:
We had a horrible experience with this hotel. We stayed for one evening during the weekend, primarily to experience the Austin bats. The only good part of our stay was the TGI Friday's restaurant and their awesome patio with great views of the bats.
We reserved a suite and it was decent in terms of cleanliness and decor - it wasn't bad, but it wasn't great, either and for what we paid, we could've stayed at a much more upscale hotel. We were travelling with an infant. Once we got him down in his travel crib and finally asleep (hard to do in any hotel), we climbed into bed. It was BROKEN. They have Select Comfort beds where you can select your preferred firmness; however, our bed was split down the middle and horribly uncomfortable. At 3am we were awaken by an announcement (repeated about 10 times, a tad excessive in my opinion) telling us that we could return to our rooms, the fire alarm we heard was a false alarm. Only problem? No fire alarm ever went off in our room - not very reassuring. We never asked to switch rooms because it had taken us forever to get our baby to sleep and we did not want to interrupt his sleep by switching rooms.
When checking out, we brought this to the attention of the front desk clerk. She did not express much concern, said she couldn't really do anything for us but did finally comp our car valet charge ($22) for one night.

name: Courtyard Austin Downtown/Convention Center
title: “Very good room, great location”
text: Known quantity of Courtyard hotel --- very good facilities, everything in great shape --- and close to Convention Center, 6th Street and much of downtown. Only minus is in-house Starbuck's shutting too early (6-8PM?), but alternatives are easily found within a couple of blocks.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Disappointed”
text:
Booked this hotel for 5 nights following reviews on Trip Advisor. 
My wife and I arrived late evening and was greeted by a non too pleasant gentleman on reception. Said very little with no real welcome given. Allocated room No. 262 in the Club section. Bit of a walk to get to room but it was nice and spacious, clean and tidy. However, we got very little sleep as room directly on O'Farrell Street at rear of hotel. Busy throughout night and refuse collected, noisily, during the night.
In the morning we requested a room change and aided by a helpful receptionist we were reallocated to a room overlooking the pool - noise level greatly reduced.
We would recommend that you avoid rooms overlooking O'Farrell Street i.e. rooms ending 60, 62, 64, 66 and 68 on each floor. The quiet rooms overlook the Pool.
Incidentally we were not the only people to request a room change - we heard of a few requests during our stay.
We arranged a room with breakfast package but found on arrival that it was restricted in value - this was not pointed out on our confirmation. We found the Daily Grill very inconsistant on quality and service and after 3 days gave up and looked elsewhere. Didn't have far to look - found an excellent "diner" round the corner on Mason Street called Cafe Mason - food excellent and staff friendly and helpful. Max's across Geary Street also good.
Location of hotel is ideal if you want to concentrate on shopping, but if its sightseeing you want, suggest you locate nearer Fishermans Wharf where all the tourist action is. Hotel close to cable car line and turnaround but large lines waiting to get on throughout the day.
If you want to do Alcatraz, suggest you prebook on the internet as this trip is very popular and books up very quickly. We had to line up for tickets at 7.30am for any cancellations as next available tour was a week in advance. Fortunately we were successful and the trip was great. The city tour by sightseeing tours (gray line) was excellent.
Lots of beggars around the Union Square area. Concierge and bell staff helpful.
Overall we were disappointed with the quality and felt it necessary to submit this review which hopefully will assist any future travellers to San Francisco.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Wonderful Stay”
text:
I have been reading the hotel reviews for about 6 months now and felt that I needed to contribute my experiences as it may help others as it has helped me.
We stayed at the Handlery June 8-June 14. Trying to get to know San Francisco as my daughter will be going to college there. We live in Massachusetts so I can't tell you how much research I did before we got there and as you can imagine, very nervous as this is the place my daughter will live for the next 4 years & 3000 miles away! My goal was to find a small hotel with excellent service where I can come when I visit her for the next four years! I had 3 other hotels on my list and after speaking to Christine, the general manager on the phone before I made my reservation, I knew this was the place for us. As we did not spend much time in our room getting to know the city, EVERYONE there made us feel right at home. I even got to meet Mr. Handlery himself and he made us feel very welcome. Dale at the conceirge desk was so gracious to us and answered every question I had no matter how stupid it may have been. 
Our room was very clean and was very quiet. We faced the pool area. I think there was some kind of convention in town and on one night, there was some loudness by the pool at 11 pm. But it only went on for a few minutes before someone from the hotel put a stop to it. We were impressed. 
We will be returning in August for the emotional dorm move-in with my daughter and The Handlery is were we will be returning and returning again.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Austin Downtown/Convention Center
title: “Convenient location and great service”
text:
I stayed there in March 09 - convenient location, friendly staff, and comfortable room. I needed to print something and scan them as email attachments. I got everything done at their business center (open 24 hours) for FREE! What a deal/service!
Do watch out where you walk/park on the street - no, it's not about safety. There's a stretch of half a block (right next to the hotel) where there are lots of birds nesting in the trees. Beware of their droppings as you walk under them. DON'T ever park your cars there. I saw some cars got covered entirely by the bird poos it's hilarious.

name: Renaissance Austin Hotel
title: “Attractive property, but it's cold and frustrating to be captive there.”
text: Check in was a breeze, very friendly staff. Restaurant was lacking, not much to choose from, expensive, and only one in the hotel. You had to walk or drive to get something to eat. Wireless was terrible, most people I saw seemed to have some problems with it. If you go, take a jacket or sweater, all the conference rooms are cold.

name: Hilton Austin Airport
title: “Great property, shout out for great service”
text: We were just staying one night at the Airport Hilton in Austin, TX. We arrived really late and called for the shuttle. The website talks about how it just takes a couple of minutes to get to the airport. We had to call again and it took around 20 minutes - not bad but after hearing about the quick shuttle, and arriving at 1am I had hoped for better. Then the stay really picked up, allowing me to give a top rating. Jeff from Pittsburgh (according to his name tag) picked us up, apologized profusely since he had also been bringing in a very large group's luggage, really treated us well on the short ride and then hustled in to check us in at the front desk while the other desk clerk stood there chatting. Jeff really made our too-late evening work out! The hotel is really top notch - room was great, lobby was really pretty, hotel was really quiet especially considering it's proximity to the airport. The buffet breakfast was quick and good, with great service again. Would definitely recommend staying there or planning a meeting there...problems, ask for Jeff!

name: Hilton Garden Inn Austin Downtown/Convention Center
title: “Good Hilton choice”
text: Good stay. Requested online and called ahead for early check-in and didnt get it. This was the only "blip" in our stay. They held our bags while our room was getting ready which was nice. Check-in was a breeze and room was in good condition. Restroom door was a bit worn but no worries there. Nice downtown view (was on 15th floor). Not centrally located so walking around was a bit much since the heat was killing us!! Overall a good stay and great customer service. Great cookies and coffee available in the front lobby.

name: Sheraton Austin at the Capitol
title: “one of the best”
text: got a great rate. great location (short walk to bars and restaurants on sixth st and on the north side of downtown so also short walk to ut campus), great staff, comfortable rooms that are very modern except for the bathrooms that are a little dated.

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “Perfect location, wonderful service!”
text: We stayed at the Grand Hyatt August 17-21, 2011 as a family traveling with another family.. We couldn't be happier! The location at Union Square was perfect and was within walking distance of Chinatown and the Powell Street cable car. While each family had issues with our rooms, the managers not only gave credit to our accounts but also moved us to better rooms, and we were very happy. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Would definitely stay again!

name: Hyatt Place Austin/Arboretum
title: “Above Average - especially for 3+ nights”
text:
I had a 5 night stay - and think that I chose the best hotel for outside of the city, mainly because of the suite setup. It is roomy with a workable kitchen with PLENTY of convenience right around the corner. Many restaurants, shops, supermarkets, etc a short drive away - interstate is right beside the hotel as well. If you're wanting a lot of the downtown action, stay downtown. A car is a must for staying in this area.
Hotel details - the suites are in small buildings a lot like apartments. Sometimes parking close was a problem. Rooms were comfortable and clean, a/c was new but fitful during 75-93 degree days, the maid service was okay but not 100% - biggest asset is the bed. Incredibly comfortable bed.

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “Busy area, great beds”
text: Just returned from the Grand Hyatt San Francisco, Aug. 13. First impression...not great as the lobby is small and underwhelming. Not much room to sit if waiting to meet ppl. Loved the fact that Hyatt guarantees connecting rooms with their "family plan" and a discount on the 2nd room to boot!! Rooms were small, but nicely done. Beds oh-so-comfortable! Actually that was the best thing about the hotel. Had brunch upstairs 4 out of the 7 days there with my family. Ok...nothing great. Wait staff very friendly along with the concierges and doormen. Starbucks everywhere as the location was great for shopping and coffee! We did not rent a car instead choose to walk, cab it or take some form of public transportation. Overall a very good hotel.

name: Renaissance Austin Hotel
title: “Nice”
text:
Stayed at the Renassiance the weekend of May 27th. The hotel nicely decorated and the location was good. The room was nicelydecorated and the beds were comfortable. I had one problem with the bathroom, but maintenance was there to fix the problem in less than 5 minutes after I called the front desk. Very impressive.
Overall, I would stay there again if in the area.

name: Hyatt Regency Austin
title: “Great location, great room with a view”
text: We stayed at this hotel 2 nights to attend an event in Austin and it was great. The location was perfect and we had a room on the 16th floor with a balcony and view of the lake. Hotel services were attentive and checkin/out was easy and efficient. Great location and nice rooms -- we will stay here again

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “good value”
text: the location of the best ,right in the center of Union Square which is perfect to who likes to shopping. lots of shops around. view of the restaurants also excellent.staffs was friendly ,tried to help

name: Hilton Garden Inn Austin Downtown/Convention Center
title: “Loved the Crown!”
text: Stayed Apr 22-26, 05 to attend a tournament held at the Austin Convention Center. The room was on the 16th floor with a nice view of the city. Staff was friendly and willing to assist. The room was warm and inviting. We had breakfast at the Rooftop on the 18th floor...the continental breakfast and great! I can't find anything to complain about other than I wished they had an airport shuttle bus...that would have been even super! Enjoyed our stay and the hotel atmosphere was just spectacular!

name: InterContinental Stephen F. Austin
title: “Perfect location but a few issues.....”
text:
Pros: A beautiful old hotel with great bedding, great service, great location just a block from 6th street and walking distance to the capital, restaurants, and boutiques.
Cons: $26 for parking. (I realize this is routine for city hotels) $11 for internet .(cheezy at these high rates).. TVs that will soon be donated to the Smithsonian with fuzzy pictures. We were here during a big golf tournament and sat down to enjoy an afternoon of the Golf Channel.....NOT.....they didn't have it on their cable. We were told that the bar would have it as soon as they opened at 3 PM. We wanted to watch it in our room, not the bar and if the bar had the Golf Channel, why didn't the rooms???
Our room cost us $260 a night and frankly I would think that at that price we could expect free internet service and modern TV' s with all the popular channels.

name: Holiday Inn Austin Town Lake
title: “Exceptional Staff”
text: I recently required oral surgery in Austin, Tx. and needed to find a hotel that was close to the airport as well as the medical facility. The Holiday Inn Town Lake was the perfect choice not only for those reasons but, imagine my surprise when the staff there went above and beyond their job descriptions to be accomodating. They made taxi reservations, provided wheelchair assistance (that I didn't know I would need) and the restaurant chef even made special meals which were off the menu to help me out. I highly recommend this property.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Austin
title: “Have stayed here a couple of times...”
text: and it has been an overall good experience. I personally like the overall ambiance of the hotel itself, large, older, yet well maintained. Was given an appreciated upgrade on last stay to one of the Pure rooms. Recommended for business travel, quiet in the back rooms or courtyard facing. Will stay again when back in the Austin area.

name: Sheraton Austin at the Capitol
title: “outrageous cancellation charge”
text: I reserved and cancelled the same day, more than 72 hours before the stay. When they charged the one night stay anyway, I called them and they said they would remove the charge. They did not do so. When I contested the charged, one "MB" with Sheraton wrote to my credit card company that there was a "one night penalty for cancellation at anytime." I cannot find that policy anywhere on their website. They appear to have made it up on the spot. This practice is abusive to loyal customers. I shall never again trust this company, and will never stay at this property again..

name: Austin Marriott South
title: “Recommend”
text: We celebrated our honeymoon at a Marriott in downtown Austin and wanted to return for our 16 year anniversary, but the original property was sold to another hotel brand. Nevertheless, we decided to stay at this South Austin hotel based on positive reviews, good location, roomy suites, and excellent front desk staff. In fact, a phone call from Jeremy at the front desk to confirm our reservations a week in advance made our stay even better. He offered us a spacious king suite with French doors, a very large living and bar area, a roomy, elegant make-up table, and grand mirror and sink space. This is one of the largest suites we've been fortunate to book, and we didn't want to leave.

name: Hilton Austin Airport
title: “Worst Hilton ever”
text:
Are you kidding - why would anyone rate this hotel so high. Terrible restaurant - more like a holiday inn express, worst bartender with no help, one elevator down and they double billed my credit card and now say they don't even show me starying there. 
This place is a diaster in the mioddle of nowhere.

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “Poor representation of Hyatt name and city of San Francisco.”
text: When an out of town guest tells the front desk that they did not sleep well because of certain situations in the room, the response should not be " wear earplugs" the staff not only represents the entire hyatt brand but also the city they are in. Grand hyatt San Francisco did a POOR job of representing the hyatt name and the city of San Francisco. Any guest who tells a hotel staff that they have a problem should be addressed " how can I make your stay more comfortable" or " I'm sorry you had a problem let me see what we can do for you" Not met with a Rude response. I, my co-workers, company, Family and Friends will no longer consider hyatt hotels as a viable choice of stay.

name: Omni Austin at South Park
title: “Pleasantly surprised!”
text: This hotel was great. My wife and kids loved every bit of the stay we had there. It's about the small things such as the milk and cookies they had for my kids in the room at check in, or the cool refreshing towel offered to us by the valet when we came back from a hot/humid day out. The pool was immaculate and the staff was more than helpful when we had questions. It may be a little pricey for some, but I'm almost certain all will have a pleasant stay.

name: Hyatt Regency Austin
title: “Lovely”
text:
I loved my stay at this hotel with some minor issues. The room was very clean, nice flat screen tv, beautiful decorating (mod, crisp hotel look), but there are a couple of things that need to be improved. The bathrooms do not have overhead fans...I just don't get that at all. And our bathroom door didn't shut properly, so it actually never latched. Also, I heard every single noise in the hallway. The elevator was nearby the room and throughout the night I heard people talking, yelling, etc. In addition, I felt that the air conditioning wasn't up to par (especially when it is 90 degrees outside). It was really warm in the room at night and had to adjust the thermostat for the second evening.
I know it sounds as though I had a negative experience, but these were things I wasn't expecting to be an issue. The remodeling of the lobby was really nice, we were in walking distance of the bat bridge (from which they flew immediately after sunset, pretty cool to see), loved the dinner in the hotel restaurant. The staff was friendly and helpful.

name: Wyndham Garden Austin
title: “Why Go Anywhere Else?”
text: You know how it is when you’ve finally found a great, reliable mechanic you won’t ever take your car anyplace else? Well, likewise, from now on whenever I visit Austin, Texas, I’m staying at the Wyndham Garden Hotel. If the ratings on Trip Advisor are accurate, I’ve stayed in seven of the top fifteen Austin luxury hotels over the years and quite honestly not one of those visits can hold a candle to the kind of customer service I received at the Wyndham Garden. Every member of the staff seemed to reflect pride and happiness in the job they were doing and their funky Austin Music Project t-shirt uniform made everyone equally approachable. Most importantly they all seemed genuinely concerned that their visitors were given the most comfortable stay possible. “VIP service for all” seems to be their credo, from Lynn who took our initial reservation to Alma C. who made sure we got extra conditioner. But there are three individuals whose efforts I especially have to recognize because they went well beyond the call of duty to ensure our comfort even after we had officially checked out of the hotel. As we attempted to leave, we found that our car had died. That’s when Sarah from the restaurant kindly offered us some leftover coolant she had in her car; Jessica at the front desk gave us a few ideas of where to take the car for repairs; and Donald “The Man” would gladly jump-start the car in the morning. (He did just that the following day, spending about ½ hour in the sweltering heat to make sure it wouldn’t die on the way to the Sears Auto Center). Since it was a Sunday evening and all the repair places were closed, Jessica was kind enough to recheck us in for the evening letting us hold on to our weekend rate. And if all that weren’t enough, about ½ hour after we settled back into our room, we got a surprise chocolate & wine snack tray from Jessica and Sarah, along with a Shirley Temple for my niece who was with us. With the tray came a personalized card saying they were sorry that we were experiencing car trouble, that the goal of the entire staff was to ensure utmost comfort and that they hoped that the snack tray “help bring a little ease to (our) stressful day.” Well the snacks definitely eased our stress, but it is the overall kindness and attention to comfort and detail that has left the most lasting impression. So whether it’s for work, play, or a mini-vacation to ease stress, the next time I’m in Austin, I’m heading straight for the Wyndham Garden Hotel. Like I said at the start, if you’ve found something great and reliable, why go anywhere else?

name: Hyatt Regency Austin
title: “excellent”
text:
My girlfriend and I stayed here several times,and throughly enjoyed it ! We had a riverview room everytime,and the view of the river and downtown was wonderful (and romantic).
 Service was first class,the food was good,the room exceptionally comfortable. 
 The only negative comment I would offer was that the air conditioning was pretty marginal during one unusally warm night (in the middle of the winter!)
 This is a great place for a romantic getaway,or for business! Its run by a very professional staff.

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “Expected so much more, got so much less”
text:
We stayed at the Grand Hyatt in San Francisco to enjoy a nice "4 Star" hotel. What we got was lucky to be even a 3 Star experience that made a Motel 6 so much more appealing!
First off, the hotel rooms are small and, as many have said, very outdated. This we could understand, San Francisco has limited space and obviously they can't expand outwards. So it was already expected for the size.
BUT... what wasn't expected was the quality of the building and bed. We never thought we'd say this, but can't they afford to buy a new mattress? At an average of $200 a night for a room, you'd figure on sleeping on a comfortable mattress and not something that looks like it's been there since they opened the hotel 40 years ago. The king-size mattress had giant pits (I'd like to say dips, but they were way too deep) on both sides of the bed where people lay each evening. Only by placing one of the extra pillows into each crevice could the bed be made level to sleep on. This was TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE for a hotel of this quality!! Come on, the mattress could have been replaced for the cost of a single night's stay. Not worthy of a so-called "4 Star" hotel.
And the building... sure, it's a high-rise 36 story building and is bound to sway in the wind. But we were kept awake by the constant creeking, snapping and popping sounds that it made as it swayed in the breeze. We were waiting for the final loud pop before it collapsed on us. Other guests in the bar also complained of the same loud noises. Perhaps a building inspector should take a look before something bad happens?
Then there was the refrigerator and mini-bar. If you're going to stay in the room expecting to use the refrigerator, think again. It was packed top to bottom with beer, soda and wines that if moved at all, you're IMMEDIATELY charged for. That's one high tech refrigerator.. but they can't even put in a flat screen tv? We called the front desk and they were very nice and said to go ahead and remove bottles to make the room we needed and they'd remove them off our bill. They did, no problem (at least not yet, we have not seen our credit card statement). The mini-bar lady came by before checkout to review the contents and noticed one bottle missing in the door of the refrigerator. We figured it was the only place they left for someone to put a drink, but apparently it wasn't fully stocked and was missing a bottle of wine. Good thing we found out, it was also removed from our bill. Note to those wanting a drink.. it's $9.00 for a can of beer. The shelves on the dresser/TV unit were also dedicated to fast grab snacks, so don't expect to use it for storing your clothes. They had mouse-trap like devices with candy bars in them. We'd hate to see the prices for those!!
Everyone from the staff was very nice, unlike some comments we read on here. Staff made it feel like a 4-5 Star hotel, but the room was maybe a 2 Star, bar was okay and fitness gym was up to date.
Now for parking... we didn't pay the $50+ parking fee for the hotel parking. Instead, we parked across the street at the Sutter-Stockton garage and paid a fraction the price the hotel wanted to charge. We arrived around 1 p.m. on Saturday and left at noon on Sunday. Paid only $28 parking. We highly recommend the Sutter-Stockton public parking garage. It's just a short walk and is diagonally across from the hotel.

name: Holiday Inn Austin Town Lake
title: “great stay, will return!”
text:
we only stayed one night. but thoroughly enjoyed the stay. the free shuttle from the airport was awesome. we were offered a shuttle to go to 6th street for the evening but ook a cab instead. Cab was only like $6.25 each way. We ate lunch at the hotel resturaunt. service was great. we ordered chips & queso and nachoes just forf snacking. the server was nice enough to tell us that it was almost the same, giving us the chance to savce some money. we checked in VERY early, at about 10:45 with no problem. Room was huge! Bed was very comfy. Clean restroom and room. Enjoyed soem cocktails at the bar. Service again was excellent. very helpful and helped us find some great places to visit on 6th street. The pool on the 6th floor was great, with a beautiful view of the lake. I can't wait to return and will bring my kids next time.
The only bad part was that we could only spend one evening and had to get up so stinkin early to catch a flight!

name: Hyatt Regency Austin
title: “They try hard, but ....”
text:
Upside - they accepted our priceline.com $125/night bid on a $250/night room. They try hard to please, at least verbally if not with their follow through. And the hotel has been nicely updated.
Downside - tiny rooms and you cannot upgrade, all rooms are the same tiny size. No fitted sheets! This is a sign for me that they care more about their housekeeping than their guests. I will maintain that no hotel can be a four star hotel without sheets like I would at least have in my home. 
They say they will bring, for example, the rollaway bed. But it takes 3 phone calls to actually make it happen ...... (a few instances like this happened). The room service menu is extremely limited. If I had paid full price for this room I would have felt ripped off. 
As it is, it was a little better than ok.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Austin Central
title: “Awesome time”
text:
We were in town for a boys baseball tourney and betwwen the hospitality, service, cleanliness, and other amenities our stay was perfect. In addition we came in with a group in which we needed 10 rooms and the hotel was able to accomodate us with putting the whole team on the same floor, which made for a great time for everybody.
We will always stay at this hotel anytime we come to Austin.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Parfait et irréprochable”
text:
Pas d'autres mots que ceux contenus dans le titre. Cet hôtel n'a que des points positifs et je ne peux que le recommander : situation géographique idéale (en plein cœur d'union square et de son animation, à deux pas du macy's, levi's...). À proximité des boutiques et restaurants, station de bus sur le trottoir d'en face (notamment pour aller au golden gate bridge), station du cable à côté.
L'hôtel est magnifique : style ancien et décoration très épurée.
Propreté irréprochable, personnel et concierge super sympas et toujours près à vous rendre service ou à vous donner des bons plans
Seul regret : que le PDJ ne soit pas compris.
Il y a une piscine à l'etge qui avait l'air très agréable mais en décembre la température ne nous a pas permis d'en profiter...
La chambre est plutôt spacieuse avec dressing.

name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
title: “Piacevole Scoperta”
text:
l'hotel è in centro, vicino alla fermata degli storici CABLE CAR e del pullman a due piani HOP-ON HOP-OFF, e soprattutto in Handlery Square... quindi MACY'S, VICTORIA SECRETS, NIKE, TIFFANY...etc etc...
a 10 min a piedi c'è CHINA TOWN
Colazione americana, camere pulite e letto enorme
CONSIGLIATO

name: Marines Memorial Club Hotel
title: “Beautiful historic building in a fantasitc location”
text: What a gem in the heart of downtown San Fransisco! There is nothing to complain about when it comes to this lovely hotel. The service is top notch, the rooms were lovely, clean and comfortable. The complimentary happy hour each day from 4-6pm is an unexpected bonus and the breakfast buffet leaves you wanting for nothing. Valet parking is right down the street with in/out privileges, though we didn't need our vehicle the entire stay as the hotel location is in such a convenient location.

name: Marines Memorial Club Hotel
title: “Helpful staff, pleasant stay”
text:
Me and my husband stayed 3 nights in a king size room on the 5th floor where the memorial plates were hung on the corridor walls. As we went in the hotel's main door I saw that hotel really deserves the name. Lots of badges, pictures, stuff etc were placed over the walls like a exhibition or a museum about marines. The receptionist was hospitable and after 5 minutes time we were done and going up with elevator to our room. We didn't see any welcome basket of fruits or cookies contrary to eileenm28's review. It wasn't a defect anyway. Room, bathroom, towels were clean. Only problem we had was on the last morning of our stay. We woke up with the noise coming from the next room. Really it was disturbing because we could hear the neigbours' laughing and conversation. They must be talking loudly; what we did is just simple. We knocked on the wall 3 times. Then it was silent.
The breakfast was on the 12th floor, it had a nice scene if you can sit on a table near the window your breakfast will be great. We were seated after a few minutes. Breakfast itself was reasonable. The staff frequently asked if we would like to have more orange juice or something else. 
First night of our stay we needed a AAA battery and it was midnight. Thanks for security because he handled a pack of batteries which he bought from market next door at that time. Next morning when he saw me he asked if I'm okey with the batteries :)
I must say that it's location is really good because it's close to union square, BART Powell St. and cable car station. All these points are a 10 minutes walk away I guess. So if I go back to SF, I'll certainly check Marines for stay.

name: Hilton Austin
title: “Those Queen Beds are sure getting smaller - aren't they”
text: I was travelling with a friend and needed 2 beds in the room. Typically I do not stay in Hilton hotels - they are such convention hotels, but my Friend is tall and I like to spread out in bed, so I booked the Hilton over other hotels in Austin because it was the only Hotel that offered '2 Queen beds'. We checked in, and yes there were a lot of conventioners in the lobby, got to the room to see what looked to us like 2 double beds, not queen. My tall friend can tell because double beds are shorter than queen beds - and sure enough, they were short beds and narrow. I called the front desk to ask why there were double beds in our '2 queen bed' room and the lady at the desk, while nice, said 'those Queen beds just seem to be getting smaller every year, don't they'. Then assured me they were queen beds. Well - they were not. The room itself was smallish but nice. We had a lovely view (can't complain about that). The location was very good. But I have to give it 2 stars for false advertising. And a final note about that convention thing - we needed one first class stamp to mail a letter. We waited in line at the front desk who told us we had to go to their shippng center. We went to the shipping center (a small kinko's type thing) and waited behind 3 men in business suits who were prepping for convention and business meetings. After 15 minutes there was one man left who was unhappy with some presentation and kept arguing with the single attendant in the shipping center. We were aghast that we could not get one single stamp without having to wait all that time.

name: Hotel Palomar San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “...the coldest summer I spent was in San Fransisco”
text:
Even tho the weather did not cooperate in mid-August, we had a great time in San Francisco and really enjoyed the hotel Palomar. It’s a really fun city to visit and the hotel is right in the middle of everything, downtown, financial district, shopping and a very short walk (although uphill) to China Town for shopping and great Dim Sum.
It's a small boutique hotel so don't expect all the amenities and sprawling space of the Marriott, that's across the street. Where you DO have to visit the roof top bar, for the most spectacular view of the city. What the Palomar does have is very friendly and helpful staff, great restaurant (although a bit pricey), free happy hour, and pet friendly. They have a chocolate lab perched behind the desk that was very sweet and friendly. Yes it's loud, yes bums are sleeping outside, but hey it's a downtown city and it comes with the territory. We had a courtyard facing room which was very quiet and clean. Highly recommend for low key, comfortable and hassle free stay in San Fran.
Transportation-Take the Bart from the airport and get off 1 block from the hotel, it's only $8 bucks. A very helpful homeless lady helped us figure out the ticket machine at the station in trade for our old tickets. Hilarious. The cable cars are fun to do once, but expensive. And when you get tired of walking, the old time trolleys and buses are a buck or two for all day and will take you anywhere in the city.
Food-Next to the hotel is a bar restaurant where we ate 3 times! They as well as the rainforest cafe a few blocks away were very good and average priced. For Dim Sum my hubby (who's Asian) searched everywhere for the best one. We stumbled across Canton seafood and dim sum Restaurant which was amazing, and it was my first experience with dim sum. 
Alcatraz – If you want to visit the Island pre-book online at least 2 wks ahead, they get packed. We took a 90 bay cruse from fisherman’s wharf (must see) and we got a good look at Alcatraz and the bridges. Good enough for me.
Weather – The warmest time in the Bay area is in the fall so pack a jacket and warm clothes if you visit any other time.

name: Mansion at Judges' Hill
title: “Love this Hotel”
text: I had been here during a weekend this past month . LOVE the place . Its very clean and neat . Very nice hotel, comfortable beds w/ Egyptian linen, large bathrooms with all the comfort needed . The staff is just awesome, very friendly and helpful . Enjoyed very much the breakfast and the time I had spent here . I will be back with no doubt . Highly recommended

name: Hotel Saint Cecilia
title: “Celebrated Valentine's with Cecilia”
text:
Stayed in suite #1
Reasons to love it: Hastens bed, large photo of Keith Richards circa 1969 in white jumpsuit, turntable and Liz's record collection, HUGE bathrub, outdoor bamboo grove shower, delicious crepes for breakfast.
The hotel creates a rockstar experience, wrapped in an original and highly curated design aesthetic, catered by an over-the-top friendly staff. 
Top 5 hotels all time.

name: Marines Memorial Club Hotel
title: “Steak is Great”
text:
The Leatherneck Steakhouse is a wonderful yet intimate place. The steaks were as good as Ruth Chris,the servers were attentive and friendly, and the view of Downtown with a faraway view of the Bay was fabulous. The prices are also reasonable for this type of place. We ate here twice and the steaks melt in your mouth. Had a side for two of large sized asparagus with Hollandaise that were incredible!! A great experience and would not try another steak place here.
The hotel is also great.Free full buffet breakfast which was great and varied each day.Room had nice appointments,fruit and cheese tray each day. They treat you right and I will only stay here on any visit to SF.

name: Hotel Palomar San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Rooms need a major facelift”
text:
I always stay at Kimpton, they are pet friendly like no other hotel. The service here is what you expect at Kimpton, very friendly.
I walk into my room to find a huge black stain on carpet, it looked like tar. I called down to front dest and someone met me at elevator to give me a new room. The new room still had stained carpet, a stained chair, hole in wall next to carpet and in bathroom the bath sink leg was rusting and the tiles to the bath were very black and dirty. For a $400. a night room I expect a perfect room, no exceptions. 
The rooms here need a major facelift, it's very obvious. The headboards are what the Monaco Hotels had but they have all been replaced.

name: White Swan Inn, a Joie de Vivre Hotel
title: “Good place to stay”
text:
Good value hotel and bed was comfortable. Staff at front desk were very helpful and friendly. location to union square is great, only a short 10 min walk.
Be aware that there is no air conditioning in this hotel so if you happen to be there during a hot spell it may not be too comfortable. We opened the windows but off course it then lets the noise in which cant be helped in the middle of a city.
Breakfast is quite nice but nothing too special. Our room had a fridge with comp soft drinks which was nice.
Overall good value for a hotel in the centre of a city.

name: Omni Austin at South Park
title: “Our new Austin home.”
text:
We have stayed at many hotels over the years in Austin but this Omni will be the place we will return to again and again. Great staff, wonderful linens and comfortable beds.
We got a hotel special for families and it was a great price. Many downtown Austin hotels get you with a big parking fee, the Omni Southpark has free parking. Good pool and super clean rooms. I also love the location on 2 major highways. We are planning the next get away in a few more months.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Austin Central
title: “Needs a Makeover”
text: My company has a contract with this hotel and asks us to stay here at a good rate. That said, this place is in bad need of a makeover. It is your typical Embassy Suites with a pretty atrium, a small-ish indoor pool and a small gym. Typical breakfast and cocktails served in the lobby. However, if you take a room anywhere other than the back wall - farthest from the lobby - be assured you will get 3 hours sleep. At the corner of two highways, this place can get loud. And if that doesn' keep you up, the furnishings and amenities will - outdated wall unit housing TV, beds with thin mattresses and pads, dingy bathrooms that can often stand a better cleaning. If you get the room for $75, take it. Much more and you'll want to head to the Arboretum for the Embassy Suites or Amerisuites. Enjoy Austin!

name: InterContinental San Francisco
title: “Gute Lage mit ungewöhnlichem Ausblick”
text: Das Intercontinental an der Howard Street ist neu und bietet einen guten Komfort - immerhin residierte schon Präsident Barack Obama hier. Es ist eher für Geschäftsreisen zu empfehlen (nahe beim Moscone Center), aber die Lage des Hotels ist auch für Ferien prima (nahe an der Market Street bzw. bei MOMA und anderen Museen). Der Spa-Bereich mit grossem Swimmingpool ist toll und der Fitnessraum ist sehr gut ausgerüstet.

name: White Swan Inn, a Joie de Vivre Hotel
title: “Great place in SF”
text: My wife and I stayed 3 nights during our 3 weeks in California and I fully endorse all the previous good comments about the White Swan. Great location, lovely room, helpful staff, good breakfast , would definitely recommend and wouldn't stay anywhere else in SF.

name: Hilton Austin
title: “Never Again”
text:
Our New Years Eve stay at Austin Hilton Downtown was the last stay at this hotel. I made online reservations through HHonors requesting smoking room on Executive floor. upon checkin, was greeted by desk and told my requests were all taken care of. After entering room , it was obvious it was non- smoking room. I immediatrely called front desk and was told " soory sir, we do not have smoking rooms on executive floor anymore. i asked to be moved to different floor ,and was told not possible. i was then told " sorry for your inconvience, sir , would you like to check out . We are booked full""
i asked to speak to management and was told : they are busy,sir,, it is New years eve ,you know?""

name: Crowne Plaza Austin
title: “Recent Stay”
text: My stay was very pleasant. Customer service was outstanding, thanks to Kevin and Maurice for making my stay a pleasant one. I will be going back to Austin at the end of the month of October 2012. I will surely be letting friends and family know about this hotel.

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “Excellent Service, Clean Rooms, but no parking”
text:
First of all, be aware that this hotel does not have parking. In fact, you have two choices: valet ($45/night) or public parking ($35/night). I wish I had known this before booking. 
With that said, the hotel itself was very clean, amenities felt new, and the staff was superb! From the moment we arrived, the staff was super helpful and cordial from the bell man to the restaurant staff. We had dinner at the Grandview Restaurant on the 36th floor, and felt pampered by the service (even though we had a very messy 10-month-old with us). The next morning, they let me stop by their buffet and pick up some pastries to bring up to the my room (for a very reasonable price). The staff even went out of their way to help me with my baby and stroller.
The location was excellent... just a block away from Macy's and in the center of Union Square. I'm glad the hotel was kid-friendly after all. Downside - Wifi was $9.99, and of course lack of parking. Overall, I felt like everything was clean in the room, had a decent view (and we were only on the 5th floor), and didn't have any problems.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “Cancellation policy is 72 hours in advanced. Don't stay there!”
text: If you don't care about cancellation fees of 72 hours in advanced -this hotel is for you!!!! If you do care about it since there is always a chance that something can happen at the very last minute of your trip, DO NOT stay at this hotel! Even if you talk to the manager of the hotel with more than two days and a half in advance, the manager will not wave you the cancellation penalty....YOU'LL HAVE TO PAY THE FEE... You need to call by 4:00pm 72 in advance!!! In addition, although I've never been in San Francisco I've seeing many more hotels in the internet that looks much nicer, with better prices and without that 72 hours cancellation fee. So why staying on this hotel?...My advice is AVOID Parc 55!!

name: Hilton Austin
title: “Lovely hotel, especially on an expense account.”
text:
I recently stayed here with my husband for a conference -- he attended seminars while I lounged at the rooftop pool :) The lobby & our room was beautiful. I loved the spa, the pool (salt water, which is much nicer to swim in than chlorine) was impeccable & a godsend in the Texas August heat.
Location was okay...easy to get to the 6th St entertainment district, slightly less easy to get to sightseeing, and a local told me it was actually in a "bad" neighborhood, although being from DC I'd call it more marginal than bad. Easy to access via the Airport Flyer bus ($.75!).
Didn't try the restuarant as our stay was short & I was more interested in other food options.
If I'd been paying for it out of my own pocket I might've been less thrilled with the cost, but still didn't seem wildly extravagant.
Really enjoyed our visit & would return!

name: Omni Austin Hotel Downtown
title: “Nicely updated”
text:
We have stayed here several times before & are never dissapointed. It was our 37th anniversary when we checked in, I had booked a King - parlor room & asked for an upgrade when we arrived, telling the clerk it was our 37th anniversary - that day. She said she'd upgrade us to a King suite with a view of the atrium, but I REALLY wanted a balcony. It took some insistance on my part, she really didn't seem to want to give us what I wanted, but after talking to her manager in the back, she accomodated us. we were there for three nights (Thurs-Sun)
We were in room 1810, very close to the elevator (but never heard it from the room). It was a FANTASTIC suite. It had recently been updated. The decor was what I call "Texan".The floors were immitation hardwood - no carpet, a large granite wet bar, a table w/4 chairs, a living area w/flatscreen TV, floor to ceiling windows w/ a sliding door out to the balcony, and a half bath (with immitaion cowhide walls). The King bedroom was a bit cramped, but beautiful, also having the same window set up as the living area with access to the balcony & another large flatscreen TV. 
The bathroom was to die for! It was huge with an all glass, oversized shower & granite countertops. Super, super nice. 
The noise from Sixth St is LOUD at night.... until the weeeee morning hours.... but when you close the balcony doors, that noise is almost totally gone. So that was good. They offer earplugs in the room with an explanation that the noise can be disturbing to ones sleep. It didn't bother us. 
The pool is on the rooftop & very HARD to get to. You take the elevator to the 20th floor, walk down the long hall to a door, then walk up an un-airconditioned stairway (triple digit heat makes that HOTTT) to the pool deck. There was an older lady struggleing to get up the stairs once when we went up there. I felt bad for her. There are no restrooms on the pool deck, you have to go back into that HOT stairwell, down the hall to a "single" bathroom. There is a locker room just off the stairwell door, which I finally decided to check out.... finding there were restrooms (both men & womens) in there. The pool is stainless steel, long & narrow. The water made your skin feel sticky. I didn't like that. But the water temp was good & the strong winds (remember you're on the 21st floor) kept you cool! They have a rooftop bar, but their margaritas left a LOT to be desired. We told the bartender & tried to make better ones, but we gave up. The pool has glass walls looking out over the city & the view is awesome! 
They didn't even wish us a happy anniversary. Which kinda bothered me. My husband asked the hotel concierge to help him get me flowers delivered to our room for our anniversary & they couldn't.
