REALLY? The staff seems distant & just there to do a job. Very unlike the Omni La Mansion del Rio in San Antonio which bends over backward & is happy to make your stay a wonderful experience. (We had stayed there two nights prior to coming here). But this is a BUSY hotel (sold out on the Sat night we were there - our friends tried to book a room so we could hang out more together) :-( 
We valet parked our car (which is new). When we got home & washed it the next day, I found a pretty nasty scratch on my lower bumper which was not done by us. We are SUPER careful. I assume they were driving it up (we came & went alot over three days) the ramp from the garage & clipped the wall. I didn't even call about it, as I have no way to prove any of their drivers did it. Just hate that my new car has a bad scratch. :-(

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Most convenient hotel in downtown San Francisco”
text: Having stayed at Hotel Frank ex Maxwell / Raphael for over 20 years, now closed, we found this delightful hotel with the most convenient location. We enjoyed for 9 days, end Sep/early Oct in suite 1502: the cool water + tea/coffee/cookies and nice apple as well. The weather is warm during the day but cool down in the evening. Problem may be in the summer months where there is no air-condition in the room.

name: Marines Memorial Club Hotel
title: “Perfect-O”
text: We are members but this was our first time to stay at the property. Great locay in Union Square..within walking distance to all eats and Cable Car stop. We had Room 610 which was very large and had 2 queens for 3 of us. The room was in good shape and spotless-the bathroom was small..but adequate. Plenty of hot water and towels. The complimentary amenities included in the rate are wonderful.. buffet breakfast, cocktails, gym, self laundry..it is very clean and perfect for 3 days in the City! I would stay here again by all means..no hotel value compares..and the service is great!

name: Doubletree by Hilton Austin
title: “Don't waste your money. Try Mansion at Judges Hill!”
text: It's not a great hotel, but better than Motel 6. I stayed after having stayed at the Mansion at Judges Hill (MLK & RioGrande), I paid about the same price. The difference in the quality of the room and the staff could not have been greater. I will NOT be returning to the Doubletree, they've lost my business (thanks to the jerky night clerk - a guy). But then after experiencing a night at the Mansion, why would I even stay any place else???

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Austin Airport
title: “Texas Waffles Are Awesome!!!”
text:
Check in and check out time were very quick, that is a plus.
There is a starbucks right acrosss the street in walking distance and a couple of eating places. My kids love the Texas Waffles at all the La Quinta's. 
I wish we would have had more time to stay and enjoy the pool but maybe next time.
The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was clean, and well kept. 
The location of this hotel was very convenient for my visit, it was about 5 minutes from my families house and there were plenty of restaurants and stores nearby to shop.

name: White Swan Inn, a Joie de Vivre Hotel
title: “LOVED our stay at the White Swan Inn!”
text:
My husband and I like to travel spontaneously and were looking for a nice place to stay in San Francisco. We really feel we lucked out in booking two nights at the White Swan Inn on short notice. We greeted by friendly staff--especially Andy who helped us with our car, bikes and luggage, and gave us the lay of the area upon our arrival. 
The front desk staff kindly upgraded us to a larger room. We found our room (#32) to be very spacious, clean, and charming with lovely touches including a sink and make up mirror/hair dryer in a large brightly lit closet, wet bar, fridge with complimentary cold drinks, and nice sitting area. The only thing about the room we didn't care for was the squishy bathroom (2nd sink, bathtub, and toilet). It was really tight in there. 
Each morning, they served us lovely fresh breads, fruits, juice, cereals, egg dishes, and potatoes. Coffee was delicious and always available. Staff also provided us with wonderful restaurant recommendations within walking distance of the hotel. We had no disappointments during our stay.
If you are looking for warmth and charm, we highly recommend the White Swan Inn. We will definitely stay there on our next visit.

name: Hilton Austin
title: “A very good overnight stay”
text: Lively downtown hotel. Very well-situated, close to downtown restaurants and bars and bats! (Don't miss the bats coming out from under the Congress Street Bridge about dusk.) Friendly and courteous staff. We enjoyed a spacious room on a high floor with a good view of the city lights. Self-park or valet for the car.

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “Great sisters weekend in San Francisco-couldn't want better”
text:
Stayed at the Grand Hyatt on Union Square with my sister for a fabulous weekend 9/25/08-9/29/08. It is conveniently located close to Union Square shopping, the Mason St cable cars and the streetcars on Market down to the wharf. The hotel was very nice. The accomodations were clean and comfortable. There was individual air/heat control in the room-not one of those awful noisy wall units. The concierges were amazing. They knew the best ways to get around. They recommended a wonderful Hop-on/Hop-off tour of the city with the tickets good for two days at a very reasonable price. They recommended a fabulous little Italian restaurant "Fino" about 2 blocks walk away and made the reservations for us. They had an appropriate solution to any question or challenge we presented them. They went above and beyond the call of duty in all things. The staff in the breakfast area were very accomodating also and made sure our needs were met in a timely manner. Housekeeping was superb-when asked to bring an extra towel, they were there within 10 minutes. I would certainly stay in this wonderful hotel with this fabulous staff again. As a matter of fact, I am trying to talk my husband into a trip there next year. 
The beds are comfortable with down comforters and plenty of pillows for all tastes.
We were hesitant based on some of the previous reviews. Once we realized that some of these reviews were 3 to 4 years old and when we saw the hotel and the quality of the service, we were sure we made the right choice.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “An amazing hotel with friendly staff”
text:
Staff are very helpful and friendly. Really nice and clean accommadation ( never known aroom to be cleaned so quick and still look immaculate)and great location. Nothing seemed an effort with any of the staff.
Child friendly, but at the same time no children were running riot, so dont let this put you off if you dont have children.
Also pet friendly, but again no barking dogs were heard and rooms did not smell either
We were travelling with a 3 year old.At check in our little boy chose a free gift from the treasure chest. The door staff were great and really friendly with him too. 
The hotel lays on for free hot chocolate in the afternoon with lots of different toppings and early evening wine tasting and warm cider. Definately missing these :(
My mum had a special birthday whilst we were there and due to late email replies organising the cake, Terry from conceierge popped out to local Safeway to pick up a birthday cake for her. An email was sent a few days before we arrived, asking if there was anything we needed help with and to email the hotel. I did get replies back via this email really quick. Just seems to be emails via the website that i had problems with
We had problems printing our boarding passes out in the business suite and as soon as we spoke to Front desk they had it all sorted and we checked in on our flight.
I was unfortunately taken ill whilst staying at the hotel and my husband called front desk at 4AM asking for a local doctors number. Within minutes a duty manager was up to our room asking how he could assist us. Following day a card and chocolate were left in our room. These sorts of gestures really make a difference. We had to extend our stay due to medical concern and Taylor at Front desk was really helpful with sorting a room for us.
The only tiny tiny grumble i have, is that it takes a while for emails to be returned. If you email through the website, so may be best to call direct with any questions. But that really is a tiny grumble.

name: The Inn at Union Square
title: “Charming hotel - excellent service”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for one night. Ann at the front desk was fabulous! She found out we were celebrating my boyfriend's 50th birthday and had champagne, chocolates and a rose sent up to the room!
Great location, very comfortable bed. 
The hotel is older but very nice. Continental breakfast was average. Evening wine and cheese was very good!

name: The Inn at Union Square
title: “European vibe in the middle of San Fran”
text: I stayed here recently with my husband on a holiday to San Francisco, largely because of the positive reviews on this site. If you are a bit of an adventurous traveller and like to stay in places with personality, then this is the place for you. It is not a chain hotel and we loved that. In fact it reminded us of the little hotels in Paris where attention is paid to detail (right down to the Aveda toiletries) and the staff take the time to remember your name. Of course it is in a wonderful location and you can basically walk any where in the city from Union Square or catch the great public transport so see all the sights the city is famous for.

name: Omni Austin at South Park
title: “Survey Says.....Great Place to Stay”
text:
Our experience at the Omni Southpark was a very pleasant one. The staff was very friendly. We made last minute arrangements and arrived after 10:00 pm, when we arrived we had already been checked in and the keys were waiting for us. 
The room was very clean (this is coming from a clean freak) and a nice size. The bed was a little soft, but comfy none the less. There were more than enough towels, the room was well kept and if desired the mini bar was stocked with a good variety of things. 
There was turn down service and chocolates. The pool was very nice and there were plenty of chairs and towels available. 
Overall, we would definately stay at a Omni Hotel again, and would recommend it to others. We normally stay at 3 star hotels or less but this 4 star really stepped it up a notch. This was class with affordablility.

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “Great Staff!”
text:
We were there for New Years. We found the staff exceptional!
It is a busy time for a nice hotel in San Francisco. I think the hotel goes beyond the call of duty to try and make the guests as happy as can be.
The rooms are clean and the beds are great! As the hotel emptied out for a couple of days after the holiday, there were no problems with elevators or the regency club. In fact, we found the Regency club lovely and it has a beautiful view of the city.
The hotel is starting room renavations soon.
The Union Square location is fantastic! Close to everything!
We found managment lovely and would come back in a minute!
We had a group of four rooms, each and everyone of them had a beautiful view, all were clean.

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “Underwhelmed. Stay away”
text:
We booked a stay during Christmas week. Although the desk clerk recommended a particular floor for our two rooms, for the view, the view was not what he promised. We later learned that he was in training. The second room was not ready until after 7 pm. Not very helpful to four weary travellers who had been awake since 3 am that day. 
The hotel manager on duty offered to comp us for one night, then, sensing our displeasure, offered to comp us two nights for both rooms - more than acceptable to me; but he didn't come through on the promise. The bill at checkout comped one room for one night. Later, after telephone tag, he comped each room for one night, and denied the offer to comp us for two.
Food was average. Waitstaff at the restaurant (breakfasts only) was terrific. 
Rooms were also average. The TV worked but with fuzzy picture on most channels. Beds were very comfortable.
The sliding glass door on one room was open when we arrived and required housekeeping to close it, as it was broken.
We will NEVER stay there again. You should avoid this hotel.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “Shockingly, A good experience”
text: My husband and I were a little nervous about staying at Parc 55 b/c the rates were so low. (we paid only $120/night) All the reviews on trip advisor seemed fine, and by the pictures it looked to be a nice hotel. They were right! The hotel was recently renovated, and so all the furnishings were up to date and very nice. It seems like it was an old Hilton or Hyatt that was bought and updated. It's not the 'boutiquey' hotel you typical see in San Fran, but it was a very nice and clean place to retire at night. We would highly recommend it!

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “Great hotel”
text: Did a quick stop in SF, stayed here 3 nights. Rooms are nice, clean, comfortably house 3-4 people in a pullout sofabed as we were looking to save some money on rooms. Great common lounge area on the top floor with large outdoor deck, gym and jacuzzi. Location perfect for shoppers at union square. Would recommend this hotel if it fits your budget.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great experience!”
text: We arrived at the hotel and the valet service was excellent. This hotel made you feel like you were a special guest. I loved the decor and they staff was so helpful. I would recommend this hotel to anyone staying at Fisherman's Wharf.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Excellent place to stay!”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel for part of our honeymoon trip and could not have been happier. The minute you arrive the service is friendly, efficient, and helpful. The concierge is excellent in helping you make the most of your time in San Fran. The rooms are large, clean, quiet, and very comfortable. We loved the wine and cheese reception at 5pm each evening and the lobby is a great place to relax with a glass of wine, lots of comfy seating available. The restaurant attached is also a great place for breakfast, lunch, or dinner. We liked that the hotel was part of the old Cannery Row, giving it character and charm. The location is great, a little touristy but the charms of the hotel take you away from that. The bell attendants are also very helpful and provide great tips on places to eat and things to do! Can't say anything negative, it will be our go to place on future trips!

name: Suites at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Not what I expected...”
text: My wife and I, along with my mother in law, had planned to stay at the hotel for 4 nights during our recent visit to San Francisco but shortly after arrival decided to leave the next morning. For several weeks prior to our visit I had followed the reviews here on TA and due to the glowing reviews perhaps my expectations were a bit unrealistic. First of all the place isn't at all impressive from outside looking more like a parking garage than a hotel. But in all fairness most reviews noted this but what wasn't noted was the unimpressive decor on the inside. The concrete balconies surrounding the inner courtyard are plain and cold...it reminded me of an Alcatraz cell block. The room itself is indeed spacious but it feels "sterile". The carpets are a very strange pattern of dark "dashes" which, to us, wasn't easy on the eyes. I had requested a room with a view, but when I opened the blinds I was shocked to find myself staring at a bare wall only a few feet away. There is somewhat of a veiw from the rooftop, but again the furnishings there are cold and uninviting. Perhaps a family with children might appreciate the kitchen rendering the ability to prepare meals in-house, but don't book this hotel expecting any charm or elegance. It has a bare bones apartment like feel...adequate but nothing special. I will say the staff was very gracious and friendly not holding us to the 72 hr. cancellation policy.

name: Wyndham Garden Austin
title: “Lipstick on a Pig”
text: This hotel was apparently rehabbed recently, but they didn't finish the job. Rooms look like college dorms or hospital rooms with granite touches in the bathroom and minibar and portraits on the wall. Overall, a very institutional feel about the place. I thought I could manage with it for a couple of nights until I tried to use their wireless internet connection--took 10 mins to download a simple page, and nobody could fix the problem. The pool downstairs was empty with dirty standing water at the very bottom--what a view! It was raining when I left, and when I took the elevator back down, I noticed a LOT of water trickling down the door of the elevator. Still a lot of work to be done here to make this even a 3-star.

name: Hotel Palomar San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Excellent hotel!”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights at the end of July and thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. Staff were helpful, friendly and courteous. Had already joined Facebook and Intouch loyalty programme and had free wi-fi, cocktails, breakfast etc. Well appointed hotel in the centre of the city although at first sight, Reception doesn't look appealing. Get past this, and you will have a good time.
Only two negatives are the bar/dining area which was dark and gloomy, therefore difficult to read menus etc. Also the room we occupied had the bathroom opening directly on to one side of the bed and too close for comfort. But this could just have been our room.
Overall, a fantastic hotel and we would defnitely use Kimpton hotels again.

name: The Inn at Union Square
title: “Everything's Just Right”
text:
San Francisco is my home town, and I recently went back there for a high school reunion. I decided to stay at the Inn at Union Square because of the high ratings it received on Trip Advisor. I had stayed at the Hyatt around the corner on previous visits, and my stays were always very pleasant. This time around I'd thought I'd see why this obviously smaller, much simpler hotel was getting such high ratings.
The answer, I think, was mentioned by one of the other guests during my stay..."I love this hotel. They think of everything."
I would say that just about sums it up. 
The complimentary breakfast is generous and VERY good. The "parlour" where the breakfast buffet is laid out is very tiny, with room for 4-6 people to eat. So every morning I loaded up one of the trays the hotel provides and took my breakfast back to my room, where I could catch up on CNN while I ate at my leisure. The complimentary wine service in the evening is pleasant, and the cheese and crackers they serve with the wine are REALLY tasty. My room at the back of the hotel was super quiet, and although I am a light sleeper, I slept really well. My taste in decor runs to clean, contemporary lines, however I found the slightly overstuffed and colorful furnishings here to be "just right" for the personality of the hotel. The bathroom is simple, but I took several long showers and never ran out of hot water. The staff was very friendly (including the irrepressible Ann, who is to "bubbly" what the Eiffel Tower is to landmarks.) The location is central to most San Francisco points-of-interest, and if you want to play tourist, there's a Cable Car stop a half a block from the front door.
One thing in closing. A previous reviewer complained that the lobby is very tiny. I will agree there was no room for an indoor waterfall. But unless you are planning to hold your Junior Prom in the lobby of this hotel, you will find it--along with everything else--to be cozy, charming and welcoming.

name: Galleria Park, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Thanks for a wonderful stay”
text: Last week my two sons and I were guests at the Gallerina Park in San Francisco, we attended a talk given by Chet Conley' about his book titled Emotional Equations, great book, very interesting and enjoyavle talk. One of my sons is in a wheel chair, so accommadations can be a problem, not so at the Gallerina, our every need was met. I can't say enough about the friendly service and exelent accommadations, and right in the heart of Union Square in San Francisco! I'm certainly recommending this place to all of my friends. Thank you Park Hotel for a wonderful stay! Barbara B

name: Hotel Palomar San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great service, location and value”
text:
I'm writing from our lovely room at the Palomar. My sister and I wanted a centrally located hotel and we chose well. We come to San Francisco often, and I would definitely stay at the Palomar again. After full days of shopping, sightseeing and dining, it is lovely to return to the quiet oasis of our room on the 6th floor (facing the garden). 
The manager and front desk staff are exceedingly kind and efficient. We were greeted upon arrival with many treats (check out their Facebook password game). The glass of wine each evening, fresh coffee in the lobby in the morning and ice cold, fruit infused water in the afternoon have kept us relaxed and refreshed each day of our 3-day stay.
The room is very spacious by SF standards, and the housekeeping staff ensured it is both spotless and well stocked. I would recommend this hotel to anyone coming to San Francisco, it is the perfect urban retreat.

name: The Inn at Union Square
title: “I'm ready to go back already!”
text: Just got home and already want to return to the friendly staff and this comfortable hotel. The location couldn't be better. Steps from Union Sq and the cable car line. Restaurants and shopping galore! The staff (especially Ann) were so friendly and helped with all our needs and questions. It is a small hotel in an older building so there were some quirks but nothing that would prevent me from returning...already thinking about booking my Christmas trip. I recommend the Inn to everyone.

name: Hotel Palomar San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great location”
text:
We stayed for three nights. The location is great, right by the BART station - literally over the road. Also handy for the sights, a short walk to the trams, very close to the shops - including 2 minutes from the Apple store!
Hotel is nice and clean, though some rooms have inner views in to a service area, though this for us was handy as we weren't disturbed by the noise from the road.
The room was a little on the small side, and I think the bed might only have been a double, but this wasn't a problem as we didn't intend on spending much time in the room anyway.
The staff were very friendly and helpful with queries on local restaurants and places of interest.
Free WiFi access for those that don't mind joining the free newsletter program

name: St. Regis Hotel, San Francisco
title: “Hooked up the dvd player”
text:
I really cant get down on any part of hospitality that goes out of their way to make you feel comfortable. I needed a DVD player for my son who was visiting me in the room and the front desk went a found one for me.
Food is great and so is service.
Highly recommended

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “CHANCELLOR”
text: We just spent 2 nights again at the Chancellor and this time they now have Suites which are basically 2 rooms connected by a door. I cannot say enough good things about this place starting with their General Manager Wes Tyler. You can tell Wes and his staff all take so much pride in this hotel and the little special things they do really made our stay very special. The huge plus of the suites is having 2 bathrooms, 2 flat screen tv's and you get 2 ducks! LOL Each of my grand babies now have their own Chancellor duck. The little extras besides the shampoo, bath salts, lotion and cute little duck, they also have a jar of hard candy, an umbrella to use should it rain, safe, free wifi, cookies and coffee in the lobby all day long. With the suite you get a small fridge, coffee maker with pods and a 2nd flat screen tv. And how can I forget the pillow menu. A few days before they sent me an email about my arrival with ideas and the day after we checked out we got an email thanking us for our stay. There are no other hotels that have ever done that. Location is great...we are right on the cable car line and 3 blocks from Chinatown. I don't think we would stay anywhere in San Francisco but the Chancellor...

name: Hotel Palomar San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “The Perfect Stay”
text: I had the perfect stay on a five-day business trip. Incredibly friendly and accommodating staff, from front desk to bellman. Kudos to Maverick, the hotel dog, for adding his own special flair! I literally cannot suggest one area of improvement. (Location near Moscone Center was perfect for my purposes, but be aware of the huge homeless population you will encounter as soon as you step out the hotel door. Simply unavoidable in this area.)

name: Four Seasons Hotel San Francisco
title: “Four Seasons Our Ultimate in Hotel Experience”
text:
Our business meeting was at the Four Seasons. We traveled to San Francisco prior to our meeting starting so we could spend time in the city. We have never experienced the service, comfort and 'home like' experience in a hotel before. I don't know how they attract the staff they have but who ever is responsible deserves a promotion. The most professional staff we have ever seen. They treated us like their favorite relatives. They couldn't do enough for us and we felt like royalty. If you plan to be staying in San Francisco this is the place to stay. What ever the price, it's worth it.
We felt the food, service and value was exceptional.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “great location”
text:
The loaction is gr8. You are only a block away from Bart station, MUNI stops and cable car turnaround. The visitors center is also there. From the airport, we took the BART and reached the hotel with no hassles. There is plenty of shopping and restaurants close by. There is a cafe next to the hotel where u can get small eateries, milk, juices etc. The hotel was clean and the service prompt. Our stay was pleasant and I would definately consider staying there again.
The only bad experience was at a chinese restaurant right across the hotel (near the burger king). The prices were atrocious..we paid about 50 usd for one fried rice and one chicken dish. There was a 15% gratutity added to the bill for serving two items at a table for 2. Then there is still space left for you to add a tip. So if you miss the gratutity addition, you may end up paying adding tip.The portions were small and did little to fill us. (we went to burger king later and ate again). The moment you are seated, a trolley with different appetizers appear and they hard sell to make you buy it. The way it is presented, you are led to believe that it is complimentary. Thankfully, I asked !! Beware!

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Relaxing, cozy and comfy”
text: We took advantage of a Giants package offered by the Chancellor. We last visited under a Christmas package that included a suite and lots of other perks. The hotel is small, the beds are very comfortable, the staff is so friendly and helpful. We like to stay on the top floors and see Union Square and hear the cable cars clang their bells as they go by. The Chancellor's location couldn't be better or closer to the action. We look forward to the next opportunity to visit them and their beautiful city!

name: Crowne Plaza Austin
title: “Only if you get a bargain for it”
text:
I wouldn't stay here unless this is the part of Austin you need to stay close to. 
At $150, this was no bargain, although there was nothing especially bad about the hotel. All was mediocre, mattress quality, old TV, toilet (so small you cannot open the door without hitting your knee when seated...), AC, etc. Fairly noisy hotel by a freeway. I'd rather stay at one of the hotels downtown if I had a choice (the Radisson seems to have a good location by the river but I have not stayed there yet), but when all it's booked and you want a not-to-far-from-downtown location, and the other option is only a bad motel, by all means go for the Crowne Plaza. The mall on the other side of the freeway has a good Korean restaurant (don't know the name, the sign was only in Korean).

name: Suites at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Great location in San Francisco!”
text: We stayed at the Suites at Fisherman's Wharf 3 nights. It was a very nice experience, the girl at the front desk was very helpful and very pleasant. The hotel is close to everything, we walked to Ghirardelli's, and Pier 39, and other places nearby. We especially enjoyed the view from the roof top of the building.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Location!”
text:
We stayed here 8/17-8/19 & had a great time! The location could not be more perfect-right in the center of Fisherman's Wharf-well about 2 blocks away. Also only a few blocks away from Ghirardelli Square too. Bring flat shoes to walk around! Great quiet room on the 3rd floor & comfy bed too! Be sure to ask for a room away from the streets!
 Best part was the complimentary wine tasting in the lobby at 6pm-granted the wine wasn't great, but complimentary is always good! Cozy lobby with lots of conversation areas to hang out in and even a lit fireplace which was welcomed on those misty mornings.
 The doormen were super friendly & knowledgeable too-one even walked us to a fun irish pub up the street (The Fiddler's Green) with live music & cheap beers-tons on tap- a real locals joint not a touristy bar which was nice.
 Weather was also great-a bit misty in the mornings-definitely need a light jacket/sweater but there are so many touristy shops around the hotel that if need be you could shop for a windbreaker, sweatshirt, jacket & have quite a selection. Plenty of tourist shops and Fabulous restaurants too. There is a fun wine tasting place downstairs in the lobby...wine snob workers though-no pinot grigio or rose here! 
It is a pet friendly hotel also-we saw a few big dogs in the elevator.
Pictures from the hotel's website matched the rooms exactly-right down to the decor. 
We did not eat at the hotel restaurant but heard that the corn chowder was amazing & award winning. There are so many other fabulous restuarants around this hotel that it would've been a shame just to stay & eat at the hotel. 
 A couple in our party ordered room service the evening before with delivery times of 15min increments- but freezing scrambled eggs and potatoes & warm milk arrived in the morning-i'm thinking room service didn't bother to let them know that the food was sitting outside-they just happend to open the door after the alotted time to get the food and found it sitting on the floor-so not too pleased with that aspect....needless to say we ate breakfast, lunch & dinner away from the hotel.
 We went to McCormick & Kuletos next to Ghirardelli Square for one of the evenings-amazing views with almost every table facing the water-no cheap thrill, but book at sunset and you won't be disappointed! Remember it is a fish restuarant-filet mignon was ordered at our table and it wasn't good at all! & a funky cut too.
 We also ate at Bistro Boudin because it had the authentic sourdough bread bowls-not my fav restaurant of the trip though-my bread bowl was just that-a bread bowl-there was about 2 whole spoonfuls of clam chowder-not worth it in my opinion especially since every restaurant around this hotel carries a bread bowl with soup.
The Buena Vista Cafe for Irish Coffee's-we were told it was a must go-nothing fancy-really a cafe with a counter and a few tables but famous for the Irish Coffee's which were good.
Scoma's Fisherman's Wharf-classic fish restaurant for another seafood dinner, fab seafood!! and a heavy pour at the bar too which was an added bonus.
 The streets were really crowded on Saturday-any claustrophobia issues and the wharf area would not be a good place for you-people everywhere milling around and really there's no open spaces-there must be several hundred to thousands of people going through the fisherman's wharf area on the weekends. 
 We did the self guided Alcatraz tour on Saturday morning-booked it about 3 months ahead of time to get the 1st boat out there-was a great 3hr tour-you can stay there all day though if you want to-there are tenders (boats) going back & forth all day long, again though-hundreds of people. 
 about 30 mins to/from the airport so plan accordingly to avoid traffic times!

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “Not As Good As A Grand Hyatt”
text: I am normally always impressed with Hyatt. This hotel, though, was merely average. The AAA Four Diamond really through me a curve. I was expecting a AAA Four Diamond hotel, but this Hyatt clearly is not. The hotel has no recreational facilities. The restaurant options on site are limited. (With it’s great central location in Union Square, off site restaurants are abundant.) The lobby is somewhat small and cramped, and the elevators are extremely slow. Although the facility was lacking, the concierge staff was very helpful and the hotel’s location is perfect. The theatre district, Market Street, and China Town are all within walking distance. Other trendy neighborhoods like Fisherman’s Wharf and the Castro District are easily accessible by streetcar or subway. This Hyatt was a very acceptable Three Diamond Hotel. And I don’t mind a Three Diamond Hotel, unless I’m expecting a Four Diamond.

name: Omni Austin Hotel Downtown
title: “Not what was advertised”
text:
My wife reserved the romance package. We decided to go to austin for a quick 13th anniversary celebration, 2 night stay, while we wait for our cruise sail date in the summer. Price for what we got was too high in my opinion. Lets go down the list:
1. They gave us room 303, inside corner with wonderful view of the dusty airconditioning ducts. This for romance package? Geez. We went back down to the lobby and mentioned this to the reservation girl and we were immediately addressed by a manager. To Omni's credit we were given complimentary cocktails and an appetizer (about $33) in the bar while they switched our rooms. 
2. During the two days that we stayed we did not receive the rose petals or roses as advertised on their website. Manager told us that rose petals stain and that 300 roses were due to arrive. I guess they never did arrive. They did send up a normal bottle of bubbly... i guess that was the replacement value of the roses. If that was to replace the roses at least tell us. Didnt bother bringing it up again. 
3. I asked about the sauna and it turns out that its broken and been plastered in. No sauna in a hotel of this level? Come on. In the Hiltons, Intercontinntals, Ramada's, and Marriots ive stayed they all have working and clean saunas.
4. Went into the mans locker room thinking i would shower berfore going to the rooftop jacuzzi but was disgusted at seeing the one shower with corroding/rusted pole inside of it. Remove it at least. Wife said the hot water in the ladies locker room took too long or didnt work. At this point just got tired of the problems didnt bother mentioning it to the concierge.
5. Oh and guess what wi-fi internet is $10/day even with this package. Luckily the concierge new our problems at this point and opened it up for one day at least....
To Omni's credit when we mentioned our dissapoinments to the check out clerk, he paid the $18 daily parking for us (2 days). Buffet breakfast included for one morning was great. All else was fine with the hotel, but I wonder about the condition of the fitness center. hmmmm...
So for $241 per night is all this hassle really worth it? No, even though the staff did what they could. OMNI CORPORATE: CHANGE YOUR WEBSITE SO THAT EXPECTATIONS AND AMENITIES ARE CLEAR - DONT KEEP YOUR STAFF IN THIS PRECARIOUS SITUATION WITH THEIR CUSTOMERS.
I wouldnt go back until they renovate their suites and hopefully add a Suana renovation into their plans...

name: Suites at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Every 10 years ...”
text: ... we come back here. We've been here for my 40th, 50th, and 60th birthdays. The first time, it was called the Hyde Park suites. We love the location, just steps away from the waterfront and trolley lines ... and the Buena Vista, where you can drink your breakfast! And even when the breeze was blowing off the bay, the roof deck - protected by clear plexiglass - was warm and pleasant. But we missed the "clang-clang" of the trolley bell this time, and realized that the lack of it must have been the result of a new city anti-noise law or something ...

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “Great room! Fantastic location!”
text: Just returned with family..hotel exceeded expectations and reviews. Spacious room with king bed and queen sofa bed. Awesome location close to square and easy access to Bart, muni, cable cars..we had two rooms with toddler in each room. Convenient microwave, fridge and plenty of coffee! No internet charge! Great buy through Expedia! Really happy with decision to stay here with children rather than St.Francis ..

name: White Swan Inn, a Joie de Vivre Hotel
title: “Second time, would return again!!”
text: We stayed for the second time at this hotel...love the rooms with the fireplace, very cozy. Beds and bedding are very comfortable. This is an older hotel, but that's what we like...alot of character...Breakfast is wonderful, and included....many options. Staff is very friendly and helpful...great recommedations for restaurants..Locations is the best...walked to Union Square in less than 10 minutes...we will be back next year for sure...love this hotel...

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great location, beautiful rooms (some with a perfect view)”
text:
Excellent location just close to anything (by walk or cable car starting just across the street). Nice museum, wine bar, ... and great ice cream shop in the same building.
Perfect and clean rooms.
Consierge that knows her city.
Bar closes too early (just in case you are too tired to go out). Pricing of parking is silly.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Location, well decorated, fun hotel”
text:
We stayed here for one night as friends were having there wedding reception here. 
From a wedding perspective this hotel was amazing. The staff were attentive and me being maid of honour couldn't do anything more for the bride and groom to ensure that they were having the best evening possible. The food was lovely and staff attentive. 
Our room for the night was beautifully decorated, and very large. A nice touch were the dressing gowns in the wardrobe (zebra and tiger print with instructions to release your wild side) along with matching slippers. 
Location is good for pier 39. 
Definately would recommend this hotel to family and friends.

name: Hotel Drisco
title: “Perfect for anyone, but especially for us. Family of 4. Loved it.”
text: Beautiful hotel & neighborhood. Great staff, from front desk to bellmen to cleaning. Excellent breakfast. Spotless. But if you are a family of 4, with 2 teens that want their own rooms, the 2 bedroom suite is what makes this place unbeatable. We've tried all sorts of suites, used roll-aways, had to get 2 rooms. This suite was the best. The 2nd bedroom is down a hall that provides complete privacy. The main room has a comfortable pull-out sofa and slide doors that make it seem like a separate room, with a feeling of privacy in the master bedroom. Prices fluctuate a good deal day to day, so if it's a vacation and you have flexibility, check alternative dates. Pretty easy & free street parking is a plus not available in 90% of the city. I can't imagine a better place in SF. And for a family of 4 like mine, I'm sure you will not find anything better.

name: Suites at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “Dissappointment and let down”
text:
I booked a 2 bed suite 3 months in advance and had confirmation emails upto and even on the day of arrival. I arrived with a baby and a disabled relative after a 12 hour flight to be told our room had been double booked and the receptionist would have to phone around and try and get us somewhere to stay. The receptionist was clueless and it wasnt until i spoke to the manager that he explained that a refurbishment had run over and caused disruptions in the suites, He did organise a very nice hotel to house us in but it wasn't a suite and therefore all the kitchen appliances were not available (fridge, microwave etc) which was essential for my baby. A very dissappointing experience as i was expecting so much more from all the good reviews.
good luck if you reserve a room!

name: Four Seasons Hotel San Francisco
title: “Very nice hotel - good location”
text:
This is a very nice hotel, the rooms are spacious and very well equipped as you would expect from the four seasons - nice big bathrooms, comfortable beds, nice window seating area overlooking Market St. Very convenient for the Union Square area directly across the street. 
Very clean and well maintained - big health club free to guests, open to other members but I will take a well equipped healthclub that is open to a limited one that isn't any day.
My small nit-pick is that the lobby and common areas are somewhat soul-less and there is an almost anonymous feel to it.
Overall though you can't go wrong here -

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “A Hidden Gem - so close to the action!”
text:
This was a great find for us on trip advisor and definitely a great place to stay in San Fran. WIth a trip lasting several weeks, we wanted a hotel that was not going to break the budget but in the heart of the city and close to many attractions... Enter The Donatello Hotel.
This hotel, although not super expensive, provided us with everything a hotel normally does and then some. The room was large, and I have stayed in 100+ hotels in my lifetime. There was plenty of room to walk around, lounge and table, tv, dvd player, fridge, microwave, sink, cutlery and crockery as well as a super large king size bed. It was always maintained every day and always felt extremely clean.
The only thing that bothered the two of us was the bathroom. It was a little old and outdated and the shower head was dreadful. It must have been a water-saving one because it had a lot of power but still felt like I didnt even get wet... After a long day sightseeing, a good shower is a must but unfortunately we didnt get one.
Apart from that, the hotel was awesome. Very friendly staff, large room, one block from UNION Square but far enough away to not be noisy, great price and awesome San Fran feel. Will definitely be back there to stay in the future!

name: Suites at Fisherman's Wharf
title: “location, location, location!!”
text:
Had a very pleasant stay at this hotel recently. Stayed in the 2-bdr suite with the balcony view, which was very comfortable for the six of us. Staff was very helpful (Jessie at front desk and also other young lady who's name I forgot (brunette). Location was WONDERFUL -- a block from the Wharf!!
Sound was not a problem at all -- close your windows if that trolley bugs you! And the rooftop deck -- SPLEDID. You can see Alcatraz from there! 
Would definitely recommend this to anyone who'd like a safe and very comfortable stay by the Wharf!!

name: Omni Austin Hotel Downtown
title: “Overpriced Holiday Inn”
text: I stayed at the Omni because I was traveling with my wife and 21 month old son and they had suites available with "fully equipped kitchens". I booked a one bedroom suite. When we went to check in they told me that had a smoking room available. I notified them front desk clerk that I did not want a smoking room especially considering I am traveling with a 21 month old. The agent went to the back office and told me that they only had 2 bedrooms available but they could have the housekeeping staff sanitize the room. I told her again that I would not take a smoking room and she went to the back office again and came back to tell me that they were booking me into their presidential suite. This seemed to be great service or I thought it was at that moment. When we went to the room we were disappointed right at the moment we walked in. The suite was out of the 1970s and the fully equipped kitchen was very large but had nothing to cook with. There was a stove, microwave, and oven but not one pot or pan. The kitchen was from the 70s with old appliances. The paint was peeling on the doors and the blinds covering the floor to ceiling windows were broken. The dining room table had chips all over it and the chairs and couch were stained. You would also think with the money you would be spending on a 2 bedroom suite you would at least have a flat screen TV. I read that they renovated the rooms but they could not have touched the suites. We noticed it was warm and figured the AC might have been set high so we lowered the temp but nothing worked. I called guest services and 20 minutes later a maintenance person showed up. After one hour and 3 mx guys, I was told it probably would not work. The mx person then offered to switch me to the room next door and also got the key for me. The second room we went to was nicer but again the kitchen had no supplies except for plates, utensils, and glasses. Not once did management call to apologize. The Residence Inn has nicer suites than this place. We ordered room service twice and both times they forgot to bring the whole order. Also, the lobby atrium is like a mini office park. I can not understand how this hotel receive four diamonds. Maybe the regular rooms are nicer.

name: St. Regis Hotel, San Francisco
title: “Great hotel, very expensive”
text:
Booked through Starwood which was probably a mistake. They were unclear as to the final price of the stay. They only quoted one night's price and stated that that price was for the entire stay.
Hotel itself is very nice. The rooms are elegant, well laid out and had plenty of light. All the controls were fully automated and were accessible via a remote by the bed. The bathroom was spacious and the shower featured a rainfall shower head and a seating area in the shower along with a separate bath area. 
The concierge was helpful along with the front desk. Everyone was very courteous and service was excellent. Only blemish would be the lady who came by to fluff our bed. She ignored our do not disturb light and walked right in. I suppose that getting a bed fluffed might be important to some people but it was rather a nuisance to have someone just barge in. 
The restaurant below, Ame, is _ok_ but not as good as some reviews would have it. The staff there was also excellent and helpful although our waiter disappeared for long periods of time to talk ot 2 (single?) females eating together. He seemed to enjoy talking to them quite a bit which deterred from the otherwise great service.
The elevators are quick and we only had to share it once with one other couple. They are well timed and calibrated so you barely notice the acceleration and deceleration of the elevator.
The indoor pool, outdoor lounge area, indoor lounge area and the fitness center are top notch although the indoor pool can be a bit tricky to find. That may have been the reason why it was empty when we went which was a boon for us.
Parking is valet only and internet is not free. There is supposedly a business center but we never could find it.
But for all this there is a price to be paid. At the original price of $800 / night for our room, it would be very hard to justify staying there. I'm sure you can get cheaper rates than that as the price may have been inflated due to the All Star game. Still very hard to justify when other great hotels are in the general location at 1/3 the price.

name: St. Regis Hotel, San Francisco
title: “great location not so great hotel”
text: stayed at the st regis for 4 nights in early august. stayed in a suite (astor) which was pretty small even by US hotel standards and really wasn't anything special - i was on the 15th floor and so no view either. hotel bar was actually really great - good atmosphere and the bar staff were great. the spa was fabulous - great treatments and really cool setting. only had room service (breakfast) but it was efficient if not the best food. the concierge (always something i focus on!) desk was pretty useless - couldn't get tickets for a show that wasn't exactly the hotest ticket in town; booked a restaurant for us that was a really dull local italian with nothing special about it - could have been anywhere in the world and the food was average (i asked for somewhere not too fancy but not too casual that had great food and was typically californian......the place they booked was nothing like this AND when we arrived they didn't actually have our reservation!). directions to places were given reluctantly and there was always a queue. they suggested i take a taxi to the hairdressers which was a 3 minute walk away....! overall, ok hotel, nothing special and wouldn't go back

name: Hotel Palomar San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Wonderful Hotel in Central Location”
text: Just stayed four days here and this was one of the nicest hotel stays I've ever had. The room was beautiful and everything very comfortable (including bed and pillows, which is very important to me). I requested a high-floor interior room as I really wanted quiet, and it was very quiet. Being on the interior, the high fllor probably wouldn't matter. It was very convienient to get the free coffee in the morning as that floor is in the middle of the hotel, and of course, the location is very convenient for public transportation anywhere in the city (being right on the cable car line and the trolley line running from the wharf along Embarcadero). The rates were very reasonable for that level hotel, I thought, and the staff were all very friendly and helpful. I have nothing bad to say at all about it. The only minor quibble I could make is I was surprised they didn't include a shower cap in their free bathroom amenities, as many hotels do, but I did bring my own, so it didn't matter to me. I rented a car to leave SF, and it is also very convenient as there is a Hertz rental desk in the Marriott right across the street.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton San Jose
title: “Convienient, comfortable and clean”
text: I must say that this is one hotel i will recommend to stay as moving around is very easy and efficient via public transport. Food, especially the double tree cookies here are awesome. Do try it and you will want more!

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Very friendly, comfortable and in the heart of Fishermans Wharf”
text:
I booked at the Argonaut as a surprise trip for my husbands birthday. The staff were incredibly helpful, and so friendly. the hotel is right on Fishermans Wharf, and within 2 minutes of the cable car, Ghirardelli Square and some excellent restaurants, with the ferry to Alcatraz and other Piers only a short walk away along the promenade.
Breakfast at the hotel restaurant is good, with prices being average - if you get bed & breakfast, the pastries are huge, and together with fruit will give you a good start even if you don't choose to add anything else - I'd recommend the Huevos Rancheros if you do though, really quite excellent!
Our room was a standard, and was plenty big enough for 2 of us, with 2 double beds. Beds are firm, with good, hotel quality bedding.
The hotel has it's own gym, which although not huge, is well equipped and was empty throughout our stay.
The lobby to the hotel is very large, and used as a gathering area for guests - lots of comfy chairs and an open fire - you'll have to be quick to get a seat next to the fire in colder weather! Each afternoon at 4pm there's complimentary hot chocolate, and at 7pm wine tasting - again complimentary, and both really good.
I would happily recommend the Argonaut to anyone wanting a pleasant base to explore San Francisco, and hope to return myself!

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “Simply excellent!”
text: This has to be one of the best hotels to stay in for business or pleasure in San Francisco. The location is good, the rooms are extremely nice and well maintained (comparable to Omni International rooms), the rooms are surprisingly quiet - I expected to be bothered by the nearby cable cars, but it was not a problem - and the shower is powerful. Even when nearly full, the atmosphere is quiet and adult. Oh, yes, the beds are nice and comfortable with both small and large pillows to choose from. The rate was extremely reasonable for the quality. I could only find two things to quibble about. First, my room was humid and warm on a cold day - due to all of the sound deadening insulation and the solid windows - but that was fixed by using the air conditioner. Second, there is no coffee maker in the room, but on check-in I was told about the free morning brew on the second floor. There were muffins and fruit rolls for sale for only $2.00, much less than you would pay at a nearby Starbucks. Finally, with big hotels like this, using the valet parking is often a problem. It tends to take a lot of time and it can be difficult dealing with the parking staff. That was not the case here, the staff were very professional and swift. All in all, this hotel reminded me of what large-city Hyatts and Hiltons were like in the 1960s and 1970s. Congratulations to Marriott for getting it right!

name: St. Regis Hotel, San Francisco
title: “New 5 Star in San Francisco”
text:
My wife and I spend New Year's eve in the 2 months old St. Regis hotel. From the moment we drove up to the hotel to our departure, we enjoyed the friendly staff, good food, and great modern amenities. 
Compare to other 4 to 5 star hotels the check-in process seems to be quicker than other’s. After checking in the receptionist assigned us a butler and escorted us to our grand deluxe room on the 19th floor. The butler show/demo some of the room amenities to us; the touch screen control panel, LCD TVs, CD/DVD player, and printer/scanner/fax machine. The touch screen controls the shades, room lighting, telephone, temperature, radio, and alarm clock. It also supports a MP3 or iPod, if you forgot to bring the audio cable the butler can provide one to you. Other amenities like the mini refrigerator, CD/DVD player, safe, printer/scanner/fax, and closet are stylishly hidden behind the wall/door. In our room there were 2 LCD TVs; one small 15” in the bathroom area, and the second 32” mounted on the wall in the main area. 
After several hours of shopping in Union Square we decided to relax and order room service for dinner. A decent menu that require some improvement in entree and dessert selection but overall our dishes were flavorful and nicely presented.
The hotel location is fairly convenient. It’s right next to the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, a block away from the Sony Metreon and Moscone Center, and a mile away from Union Square. Luckily our room has a view facing the Bay Bridge direction and was able to see some of the fireworks. 
Overall we were impressed with St. Regis’s services, amenities, and interior décor. Comparing with other 4-5 star hotels we have visited in the US and other countries, St. Regis staff members are one of the friendliest (not stuck up friendly if you know what I mean) we have ever experienced.

name: The Inn at Union Square
title: “Great location, value and service”
text: We stayed three nights and thoroughly enjoyed our time there. Blink and you would miss the hotel but the location is ideal just off Union Square with easy access to trams and buses. The room was not the biggest but was tastefully decorated and very clean. The staff on the front desk were also very helpful answering any questions that we had. The complimentary continental breakfast sets you up for the day but the jewel in the crown was the complimentary cheese and wine in the evening, After a long day walking San Fran there was no better reward than sitting down with a glass of wine and selection of cheese!

name: Hotel Drisco
title: “Wow. What a flawless experience!”
text:
This one-night stay I had at the Drisco Hotel was by far the best hotel stay I've had in a long time, and I travel a lot for business.
First, the process of checking in was so simple - I just said my name and they were already waiting for me - I didn't have to fill out any forms; I was in my room within a minute of walking inside the hotel. Then the hotel itself: it is very small compared to your average Hilton, and there is this great feeling of being a guest in somebody's private home. The decor is well thought through: comfortable and with great touches like window boxes on the floor looking out onto the street, where you just want to sit all day. The bathrobe was really comfy and the toiletries were great. Everything looked customized to the hotel, and the hotel seems to care a lot about using local products (foods, etc.). Also as a great leg up on the big chains, the WiFi and breakfast were complimentary - you just don't get that at hotels anymore, and I think it doesn't make any sense to pay $300+ for a room and be charged $20 for Internet as if it is some sort of crazy person's extra need. The breakfast was perfect: selection small enough to be able to choose from and not feel lost, and every single thing I had was the way it is supposed to be: fresh baguette, good butter, a great selection of jams and meats, and freshly squeezed orange juice. Just what the doctor ordered. The staff were very nice and corteous as well. 
And of course, I don't think you can quite beat the location: it's right in the middle of Pacific Heights with all the charm of San Francisco right there. It is also a 7 minute walk to Cow Hollow and Union Street.
I will definitely be coming back here.

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “Great Hotel, really friendly staff!”
text: A great option in San Francisco. The hotel staff is really helpfull. Rooms are spacious and clean. The only problem regarding my stay was with the wifi connection, it only worked near the door of my room or in the lobby.

name: Four Seasons Hotel San Francisco
title: “Fine..but....”
text: It is indeed an excellent hotel. I can have no complaints about the location, the spacious room, the comfortable bed, or the service. (I must say that when I am paying this much for a room I do not expect to be dunned $6 for a city map! ) But, overall, it could be a good hotel anywhere, there is little San Francisco character here. In town for a meeting on the expense account? This is probably the place. But for an experience of San Franciso? I think I'd look to the Fairmont or the Mark Hopkins next time.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Homecoming not Disappointing”
text: Definitely recommend--best location for nearby restaurants--good variety.

name: Galleria Park, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Spotlessly clean, extremely friendly staff and plenty of style”
text: This hotel was perfectly located near Union Square, yet just set back enough to enable a quiet night's sleep every night. The lobby is spectacular, the room was really comfortable and clean, and staff were possibly the nicest I've encountered. You get free in-room wi-fi (or free 20mins if you use hotel computers) and free use of a nice roof terrace. Also, it's close to Market Street, meaning you can easily get the trolley bus ($2) to Fisherman's Wharf, as well as the more scenic (and more expensive) cable cars. Lots of shops nearby, including a 7-11 and Walgreen's.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Why stay anywhere else?”
text:
Just returned from 4 nights in San Francisco at the Chancellor. Hotel is at the best location in the city and is a gem. Rooms are on the small side, but that is to be expected in a downtown hotel. 
I came upon this place while searching for a highly rated hotel in San Francisco that was not $300+ a night.
The staff, from the front desk, to Matt, the concierge and everyone else, was first class and willing to go the extra yard to please the guest.
When booking, I told Wes Tyler, the manager that we were celebrating our anniversary (45th). When we got to our room, there was a bottle of sparking wine, chocolates and a nice picture frame as a gift.....FIRST CLASS ALL THE WAY.
Room amenities are in abundance......bowl of candies, upscale toiletries, in-room safe, umbrellas for the guest to use, free wi-fi.....even a little yellow rubber duck in the bathroom.
The lobby has complimentary coffee and cookies always available, plus a bowl of apples on the front desk.....All this shows that it is a bunch of little things that go to make up a great hotel experience......anybody can rent you a room!
My congratulations to Wes and his staff.....you got it right.

name: Galleria Park, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “We could live here”
text: This hotel is great. It's beautifully decorated. I wish their decorator could do my house. The staff is always gracious. The location is close to so much in San Francisco and very close to Union Square, but because it's a little closer to the Financial District it's a little less touristy. It's a great value for the area. They have a fireplace in the foyer where they serve wine in the evenings, and they have a garden area with a walking track. I gave it a 4 for sleep quality because there was a bit of street noise at night.

name: Hotel Drisco
title: “Classy n quiet”
text:
We stayed here for 1 night and were mighty impressed. Bed was comfy, room a reasonable size, bathroom facilities good. Oh and it was very quiet. The quality of the wine and cheese (at the evening reception) was pretty decent - much better than the other Joie de Vivre hotel in SF. Staff were helpful and friendly.
Probably the thing to be most aware of when staying at this hotel is its location - it isn't that close to many of the touristy parts of SF and it is near the top of one of the many many steep climbs that we came to love...

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “Good Location, Strange decor, Early Housekeeping”
text: Hotel is in a good location just off Union Square so handy to get around. However this did mean that there was a lot of street noise. Room was a fair size, king bed, flat screen tv, safe , plenty of storage space, free wi fi, Sofa. There is a kind of mini kitchen, which included a fridge, sink, microwave, coffee machine and some basic cutlery and plates. This was next to the bed and had a sliding door to seperate one side of it off at anyone time. Decor was blue and orange with green curtains! Bathroom was a fair size, but was in need of a revamp as there were a few cracked and missing tiles. Shower was a bit weak and for 2 days there was no hot water. When we asked why, the reply was a broken boiler but no apology! Would not recommend if you like to have a lie in in the morning as housekeeping started their rounds about 7.30am!

name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco
title: “alles ok”
text: das hotel war ok

name: Galleria Park, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Best hotel in all of San Francisco!!!”
text: The Galleria Park is truly one of the best hotels in San Francisco! The location is perfecct. Once they park our car, we don't have to see it again until we leave. The hotel is conveniently located between the financial district and Union Square so you can walk everywhere! We've even walked to the Ferry Building - a mere 15 minute walk away. You will find the staff welcoming and extremely knowledgeable about the restaurants and other SF sites. We absolutely love this hotel! The rooms are beautifully appointed and the 5:30 p.m. wine hour is very, very nice! We have met some wonderful people while sipping on good CA white wine. You won't be disappointed if you book a room at this hotel!

name: Hotel Palomar San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Excellent, yet again.”
text:
This is the third time in the last year that I have stayed in this property for 4-5 nights. Again, they exceeded my expectations!
The location is excellent - close to union square, transportation, etc.
The decor is beautiful - the room had new carpet, chairs and blankets since I was there in the spring. They looked very nice. My room, a deluxe king, was a nice size for SF. Huge windows overlooked Market Street. The internet worked great (and was free). The table in the room was great to meet with a coworker (and someone not have to sit on a bed).
The only negative is there is not breakfast available except at the marginal, overpriced restaurant on the fifth floor. There are plenty of places within a few blocks though.
The staff are amazing - always friendly, helpful, accomodating, etc. I already have booked my next trip in a few months at the Palomar - what a great property!!!!

name: DoubleTree by Hilton San Jose
title: “Clean, comfortable”
text:
Great service, kind and helpful staff. Hilton quality to the 9's. Here is an example of how clean this place is---I got on the elevator with a maid this morning, and before she got off she noticed that there were drips of water on the hardwoods of the elevator floor and immediately began wiping them up. Turns out my little lunch cooler was leaking...the cookie at check-in was yummy. 
Wish the rooms had free fridges and microwaves.

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “So noisy”
text: I will start at the beginning I had booked a limo through the hotel i thought it would be a nice way to arrive at the hotel maybe not the car was over 20 minutes late it would have been much quicker not to mention cheaper to have got a cab I and my PA call the hotel who said it was 5 minutes away it took another call to figure out that the limo was at the limo stand even after telling the hotel that I was waiting at the international arrivals entrance. I located the driver who made no attempt to help me over the roads with my luggage and then was very sullen all the way into the city. Upon arriving I went to the front desk where a lady clerk had just finished with a guest and then started tapping on the computer she said one minute and then with out looking up said my collegue can help you. I checked in with no problems and had been upgraded ( all this meant was a higher floor ) the room that they gave me was in a quiet location at the rear of the hotel and I must say that there was no noise at all from outside. The same cannot be said for the floor staff who went in and out slamming doors the maids were the worst the noise started at around 7.00am and literally went on all day long, it is just laziness not to close a door quietly especially early in the morning. The majority of the staff are very very pleasant and efficient apart from two front desk clerks the first I have already mentioned the second was when I asked for a slightly later check out and was told I can tell you on the morning that you leave well that's no help when packing is it after a few more words he eventually agreed why not have just said yes no problem the good points are the location and on the whole the service.

name: White Swan Inn, a Joie de Vivre Hotel
title: “Nice place - poor service”
text: Good location, nice rooms and an excellent breakfast. Small bathrooms. If you know your way around SF, it’s not a bad place to stay. If you’re looking for assistance and service from the front desk, stay somewhere else. I did not get the friendly helpful service you’d normally get at a B&B. Maybe they were having a bad week, but I found Nevin to be very arrogant and extremely rude. The day shift wasn’t much help either.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Great City Hotel - Attentive and fiendly staff, nice rooms and surrounded by alot of nice restaurants.”
text:
I've stayed at the Magnolia several times and have never had a bad experience. The staff is always friendly and goes out of their way to make you feel welcome. And the location is great. Close to many different types of restuarants and the free car service will take you to places that are not in walking distance.
The free buffet breakfast, free wine and beer happy hour and 8:00 pm milk and cookies are a welcome treat especially when traveling on business.
In addition to the niceness of the hotel itself and the staff, the service is great. From the free car service to the maintenance service when, on rare occasions, something needs attention, the Magnolia is #1. When it was pouring rain, I was picked up from the office where I was working in Dallas within 5 minutes of calling the hotel. When one of the TVs in my room wouldn't connect to the main menu, maintenance was at my door less than 90 seconds and had it fixed in under 10 minutes.
I would recommend the Magnolia to anyone who needs to stay in the area, whether traveling for business or pleasure.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Awesome hotel, dog friendly, people friendly”
text:
No complaints here. Very spacious room, great view of the water and Golden Gate Bridge. Very luxurious bedding. The staff was ready to help and very knowledgeable. Only had one breakfast at the Mermaid restaurant which was very very good. It's a neat conversion of an old brick building. Only minor issue was that we could hear the neighbors' conversation through the wall fairly clearly...they were a 4 person family so maybe really loud, but still.
I highly recommend this property. And if you are traveling with your best friend, this is the only place in town!

name: Hotel Palomar San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A terrific, stylish shopper's hotel”
text:
A few years ago I visited San Francisco and I walked by an extra nice hotel and noted the Palomar name. Last month I finally got around to staying there.
From SF International Airport to the center of town you can take a cab, a shuttle, a bus or BART. 
I chose the Bay Area Rapid Transit System (BART) as my method of reaching central San Franciso because all I had to drag on wheels was my carry-on bag. The fare was $5.10 or $5.20. It takes half an hour. As you go up the esculator from the Powell Street station you can see the sign for the Palomar. Can't beat that. Half a block walk and you are there. Map it online ahead of time. 
I was early for my reservation but the staff got me directed to my room. It faced away from the street and over a glass atrium. It was also a bit cramped. I could be in any hotel in the country with this view. I went back to the lobby and asked for a better room. For $20.00 a night more I got a slightly larger room that overlooked Market Street, a main San Franciso street. Granted I did hear some street musicians through the window in the evening but stuff like this stops at around 10 PM. I had three quiet nights of sleep.
I can't say enough nice things about the staff. Want an opinion about a restaurant? You can get several. It happens that the historic, reasonably priced John's Grill is only a couple of blocks away. 
As for the room again. It was clean.
No walk-in shower but a nice bath. 
Nice, light cover for the bed so you can see how clean it is.
Kind of weird to have two desk chairs. Great if you are going to have a couple of visitors to your room.
Reading lights for bed reading could be better (as with most hotels).
Mattress was comfortable as were the pillows.
NY Times delivered to the door. At check out I was told I could have gotten a SF paper if I had told them.
I have to admit that the room didn't have any cutting edge design features like I have seen in Park Hyatts or Westins but it had a nice contemporay look and I felt it was a notch higher than the standard HIlton, domestic Radisson or Sheraton.

name: Hotel Palomar San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Fabulous Place to Stay”
text:
This place was the best!! 
The rooms were very large and comfortable. The beds were great! The hospitality was second to none. I have stayed at Ritz and at the JW Marriott both 5 star and exquisite. The Hotel Palomar is in their league in hospitality and may even rival these folks. We had 2 rooms that were joined and there was at least 1000 sq of living area between them.
The ‘Door-man’ had great recommendations for breakfast and dinner every day and with out exception all were of great San Francisco flavor. 
The Hotel is right by the trolley car system and for $1.50 you can travel through out the city. Hotel Palomar is located right in the heart of Union Square so shopping was close. We forgot the charger for our camera and found that there was a full discount camera store within a one minute walk. The hotel front desk located the store and printed us a map when we arrived and we were able to solve the problem for $29 within 30 minutes of arriving.
Over all a great place we give 6 stars out of a 5 star system.

name: The Westin Riverwalk
title: “Had a great time!!!!!”
text: Just returned from a three night stay at the Westin Riverwalk Hotel in San Antonio. Clean and friendly Hotel. Located on Riverwalk, close to all Riverwalk and Downtown attractions. Would stay there again when in San Antonio.

name: The Westin Riverwalk
title: “Grand location, Fantastic structure, but very pricey”
text: My sister came in from California to stay with us for a week. As her treat, she took us to this hotel for a night of fun on the Riverwalk. The upside is, overall, it was a nice experiance, the bed & TV were friggin "A" & everything smelled like a Holister shop- yummy. But the downside, everything was really expensive. We couldn't even open the little refrigerator to store my 2 year old daughters juice because it's keyed. If we used anything in the room: the water bottles, the items in the refrigerator, the bath robe, even the coffee, ... it would have cost a lot more for each add-on. I didn't have this problem at the Sheraton. The location was probably the best part of the whole trip. The Riverwalk is a lot of fun & is really very pretty. We might go again but we will definately try another hotel. However, if $$money is no object, then this would definately be the hotel I would recommend. Plan on having lots of extra cash & being willing to spend it & you can really have a blast.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “Posizione ottima”
text: Abbiamo soggiornato 3 notti nel mese di agosto in una stanza molto spaziosa con 2 letti queen-size e con ampie vetrate. Il prezzo non si può proprio definire economico considerando che non avevamo nè colazione nè wi-fi, ma a San Francisco i prezzi sono elevati, soprattutto per avere buona qualità. Posizione eccellente per visitare la città (accanto al capolinea delle due linee di cable cars e al visitor center) e anche per lo shopping (market street è a pochi metri e comunque nei pressi di union square). Spazi comuni ampi e hall sempre molto curata e profumata. Veloci ed efficenti sia nel check-in che nel check-out. Lo consiglio e ci tornerei!

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “European style in perfect location”
text:
My husband and I have stayed around Union Square at different hotels for our short stays in lovely San Francisco, but this hotel is our favourite. Staff are amazing - long term and know
their city so share wonderful advise of hidden gems. The rooms are small but if you are a tourist in the city, you are out most of the time. Pillow menu is amazing - wish every hotel had one.
Breakfast or a cocktail in the afternoon is covered as you start out or regroup. Ideal location
for transportation or walking to shops.

name: Galleria Park, a Joie de Vivre hotel
title: “Thumbs Up for Comfort!”
text: Stayed here 2 nights recently. Best thing was the comfortable bed! We had an inside (away from street) room which was very quiet at night. Place is well decorated, but here and there in our room was some chipped paint, but is expected for an older building. All amenities we needed were here, so would recommend. Only 2 blocks from BART, easy 30 minute ride to SFO.

name: Hotel Drisco
title: “I will never stay anywhere else when I visit San Francisco.”
text: I've stayed in many San Francisco Hotels but never again! The Hotel Drisco is my new home in the city. The neighborhood is lovely and quiet, the staff is courteous and helpful, the rooms are comfortable and immaculate, the complimentary breakfast delicious. Real fresh orange juice! Although this hotel isn't downtown there are many restaurants and shops within walking distance. And isn't walking part of the San Francisco experience after all!

name: Courtyard by Marriott Austin Airport
title: “Comfortable stay at the airport”
text: Located just behind the Waffle House and a ten minute drive from the airport by the hotel shuttle, this is a comfortable place to spend the night. With two queen beds, my family of four had enough room to sleep. We left so early breakfast wasn't ready, but the coffee was on and there was that Waffle House nearby. The desk clerk was very helpful and asked if I wanted to book the shuttle and a wake up call - both good suggestions. There are two free computers in the lobby and you can print your boarding pass on them. The shuttle driver was also very nice.

name: White Swan Inn, a Joie de Vivre Hotel
title: “Das gemütlichste und schnuckeligste Hotel von San Fran!!!”
text: Wir würden immer wieder dieses Hotel buchen, wenn wir wieder ( auch mit Kindern!!) nach SanFran fliegen würden. Wir haben uns sehr wohl gefühlt.. Die Mitarbeiter aber auch die Gäste waren sehr nett und gesellig! Das Bette war groß und saugemütlich! Der mit Gas betriebene Kamin schaffte per Knopfdruck Gemütlichkeit. Das Frühstück war ausreichend und der Kaffee und O-Saft haben besser als bei Starbucks geschmeckt! Aber wenn man länger als 5Tage dort frühstückt, schmeckt es nicht mehr so gut, wie am ersten Tag (jeden Tag das gleiche :-(

name: Courtyard by Marriott Austin Airport
title: “Superb Customer Service!”
text: I called the hotel asking if something (food, drink, etc) could be left in my boyfriend’s room when he arrived. My boyfriend travels for work and it’s hard on both of us when he is away. Seeing that I wanted to let him know I was “with him” I decided leaving something for him would be an excellent idea, and it was! Not only were the staff pleasant and upbeat but they were a joy to speak with. In speaking with them, we decided to leave him a decadent treat that the chef would prepare today before his arrival. I am so glad my boyfriend decided to stay in the Courtyard hotel in Austin as the customer service was the best I have experienced!!! Thank you again for making his stay more friendly and inviting!

name: AT&T Executive Education and Conference Center
title: “Fantastic hotel from top to bottom”
text: I recently stayed here for an event at UT, since it was the closest hotel (being right on campus). The downside to that proximity is that people interested in attending UT usually end here, making it a bit noisy. However, the service of the hotel staff and the cleanliness of the rooms more than made up for it. The desk clerk even gave me the option of what I wanted in my room, including what kind of shower (stand-up or tub) and the view out of the window. The hotel manager recommended the best local restaurants and the valets offered to give me a tour around UT. Overall, a great experience.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Austin - Arboretum
title: “nice place but staff was not too helpful”
text:
