we stayed there in February and liked it so planned using it when we have 6 trips to austin. however, ran into issues from very first night with the room (running water noise, broken TV, and room was very cold, couldn't get hot air out). too tired and too sleepy as we checked-in almost midnight, so decided to cover us up and sleep.
next day, set thermostat at 77F and left. 8pm returned and the room was like 50F. called the they said they were sending someone to take care of it. one hour and three phone calls some one finally came. he claimed that we left the temperature display at F, that's for cold. switching to C would have it fixed. we just needed to wait half hour. didn't buy it as apparently he knew less than I regarding HVAC... he kept saying half hour as he played the settings F/C, or whatever button he had no idea... called front desk again and all they could say was half hour and the room would be nice and warm... no, it wasn't getting a degree warmer. finally after 2 hours in the freezing room and five phone calls they asked us to go down. once again, front desk said the room would be nice and warm in another half hour!
no, give us another room. so he did... and went back to 6th room. cards didn't work. went back down, back up, cards work now. started moving stuff over and suddenly heard a shout: "what are you doing in my room!!!" so front desk gave a room that was occupied. that guy had to go down with us to sort things out as his card stopped working.
enough rant. don't understand why they were so unwilling to let us switch room. and they need a better maintenance guy...

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Third time was as good as the first two”
text: We like this hotel because it feels like home, we always get good service and have never had anything to complain about. We will be back.

name: The Westin Riverwalk
title: “Excelente hotel en San Antonio”
text: Estuvimos hospedados entre el 26 de enero al 1 de feb. Disfrutamos de un hotel de primera calidad, las instalaciones hermosas, las habitaciones muy confortables, la ubicación perfecta en el Riverwalk... Pero, lo más recomendable es la atención esmerada y profesional de Sandra -consierge-, Jaime en el bar, José en el desayuno... hacen que disfrutes aun más tus vacaciones. Recomiendo con mucho gusto este hotel encantador.

name: Hotel Palomar San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “central location”
text: the palomar was a nice hotel. nothing special, the decorating was a bit generic. the service was excellent, everybody was very friendly and helpful. being so close to union square, it really was right in the middle of tourist central, but it made a good central location from which to explore some of the quieter neighborhoods of SF. if you are coming to shop at the big name stores, you probably couldnt do much better than the palomar for location and value. it is conveniently located close to a bart stop, which i wish i had known on the way there b.c our cab from OAK was $60 whereas the return trip on the bart was about $5 per person.

name: The Westin Riverwalk
title: “Always the best!”
text: I wouldn't stay anywhere else in SA. I just got back from a conference there and as always, it was outstanding! I go at least once a year to enjoy the heavenly bed, heavenly bath and the wonderful service. This westin is by far the best I've ever stayed at. Highly recommend!

name: Conrad Indianapolis
title: “Beautiful, classy hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for a weekend get-away before he deployed and it was perfect for a relaxing weekend together. The front desk staff was courteous and efficient. When we called to get our room cleaned, we heard the message delivered to the housekeeping staff before we'd even left the floor!
 We also enjoyed the bar, restaurant, and spa. The pool was tranquil as well.
 If I ever go back to Indianapolis, I will definitely stay here again.

name: The Inn at Union Square
title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text:
This is one of the best hotels that we have stayed at. The staff is very friendly and everybody works very hard to make sure that you have the best stay possible. The room isn't huge, but it is comfortable and decorated nicely. The hotel is surprisingly quiet for the the middle of the town. The bed was very comfortable. The hotel is right in the center of town. It is close to the cable car lines and is a 15 min. ride to Fisherman's Wharf. The breakfast and wine happy hour are great. 
The only (very minor) criticism about this hotel is that the safe was on the top shelf of the closet. If you are shorter than 6' you might have get up on a chair to use it.
If you like the big fancy hotels, this isn't the place for you. If you like small, comfortable lodgings with great service, you will like the Inn at Union Square.

name: The Inn at Union Square
title: “Great 4 night stay”
text: I will not repeat the information in the previous review. All that was written is true. I traveled by myself for a conference at the Moscone Center. My husband joined me for the last nights stay before going to Sonoma. As a single women traveler, I felt very safe at this hotel. My room on the 4th floor was very quiet. I could not hear anyone above or next to us. I needed to hire a taxi one night. the front desk staff member actually came out to the street to get me one. Unfortunately, that night I lost my room key card, credit card and driver's license. The staff front desk man wrote down the names and phone #s of 7 top taxis without me asking. At least this made me feel as though I had some control in the situation. Sadly, I did not get my cards back. Luckily I traveled with my passport for the flight home. I would go back to this hotel anytime I am in San Fran again

name: The Inn at Union Square
title: “Surprisingly disappointing”
text:
Could have stayed at a large Union Square hotel like the Hilton or Parc 55 for less money, but chose the Inn due to very positive reviews and the appeal of a small "boutique" type hotel. Staff was very nice and helpful, location was great, but we didn't feel it lived up to our expectations, and we're usually not hard to please.
Check in was fine, but found bed kind of soft and had a noticeable dip in the middle; woke up with a bit of a backache. We tried to use the bathroom, but the toilet wouldn't drain. Had to complain at the desk, which was a bit embarrassing, but they moved us to a different room, which was significantly larger, and that was appreciated. Next morning, the toilet in that room wouldn't drain, and had to complain once again. I know what you're all thinking :), but we didn't plug the toilets. The final plumbing problem occurred on our last day, when the sink backed up with black sludge that looked like a quart or so of activated charcoal. We obviously had not put anything down the sink that resembled in any way what came back. We informed them, but we were leaving, so it wasn't our problem anymore.
The breakfast was adequate, but the rooms where it's served were so small that returning to your room with a tray was not merely an option, but was pretty much a necessity.
Brass fixtures in the bathrooms were uniformly corroded, second room had tiles in the tub that had obviously fallen off and were not replaced well; evidence of mildew in the shower.
The carpets in both rooms were filthy, and desperately in need of shampooing. 
We've certainly encountered problems in hotels before, and usually don't let them bother us too much, but the plugged toilets was a new experience, and hard to overlook. The staff really couldn't have been nicer, but that didn't really compensate for the other issues. 
Probably wouldn't have been as disappointed as we were had it not been for the rave reviews about this hotel that we read on Tripadvisor, which set up expectations that this facility could not satisfy.

name: Fairmont Heritage Place, Ghirardelli Square
title: “An excellent place for a special occasional get away”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Fairmont Heritage Place for our 25th Anniversary. We had a beautiful two bedroom apartment. The kitchen was outfitted with the best appliances - Wolf stove, Subzero wine cooler, etc. I wished we could have stayed long enough to cook some of the wonderful produce we found at the Farmer's Market. I think one of the best things about the room was the quality linens from the comfortable bed to the feather pillows, down duvet, cool crisp sheets and fluffy towels.
The continental breakfast was a good mix of fresh fruit, cereals, bagels, bread, hard boiled eggs and pastry. We also enjoyed the complimentary wine and cheese that was served everyday between 4 and 5 p.m. 
We enjoyed our stay and look forward to coming back some day.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton San Jose
title: “Fabulous, Fabulous, Fabulous!”
text: We were here for a student conference and the hotel was nothing but fabulous! To have hundreds of middle school and high school students in one location can be chaotic, but the Doubletree treated the students and staff so professionally that I am very impressed with the service and caring attitude they gave us. I would stay here again for sure! They were FABULOUS!

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Fantastic way to get that true San Francisco experiance!”
text:
From the moment you walk in and are invited to a wine tasting to Steve the Bellman giving excellent advice on how to enjoy you time on Fishermans Wharf it was a superior experiance. 
The rooms are beautiful and we had a view of the Golden Gate Bridge, Ghiridelli Square and the trolley turn around! 
Can't recommend this enough for a romantic get away in the city.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton San Jose
title: “Good hotel, excellent staff, definitely would stay there again.”
text: This hotel has an excellent staff. Friendly, helpful, with outstanding guest services skills, however, housekeeping is another story. During my stay, I found a tray with beer bottles and a plate with moldy limes behind a chair. The tray had a receipt dated five days prior to my stay. Also, I requested, and paid extra for, a room with a balcony so I could sit outside, relax with a drink and enjoy the sunshine. The balcony was so small it could not accomodate a chair, therefore you could only stand on it. This aspect of my stay very disappointing.

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “Go Wildcats”
text: This is a great resort with top notch staff that are friendly and go out of their way to make your stay a pleasant one from the time you enter the resort. Be sure to visit the Jazz Lounge. The bar tenders are wonderful and good music. We ordered dinner from the restaurant in the lounge and although it was a little pricey, our dinner was very good. The club room and staff are great and the facility is very nice. Great location downtown to unique restaurants and union square is only a 5 minute walk and from there you can catch the trolley and hop on hop off busses. I would recommend staying here and the next time I'm in San Fran, I will try to book here first. Tip, ask for a room with even last number. The room view will be the Marriott. The other side of the building is a bar that stays busy late night and can get noisy very early morning.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “Excelente ubicacion”
text:
Llegamos al hotel y realizamos el check in sin problemas a pesar de que no era la hora de ingreso. A pesar de que el personal no hablaba español con mi ingles intermedio pudimos entendernos perfectamente. La habitacion era muy linda y confortable. El hotel se encuentra ubicado a la vuelta de la estacion del tranvia y a pocas cuadras del downtown, con lo cual puedes manejarte caminando sin problemas. Eso si para el lado del downtown puedes salir tranquilo, para el otro lado a muy pocas cuadras hay una zona bastante fea pero no es necesario caminar para alli. Si estas con auto, sobre la calle del hotel a una cuadra del mismo para el lado contrario al downtown hay un garage que cobra u$s25 la estadia contra u$s50 que cobran en casi todos los lugares.
Lo unico malo del hotel: los ascensores... no hubo una sola vez que no me mareara. Pero esto es solo un detalle.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Post-holiday Pampering with Pegasus”
text: The hotel was art deco exquisite! The breakfast was friendly and tasty. The comfortable suite was private with a panaramic view of Dallas. The cookies and milk goodnight buffet gave us a warm cozy friendly feeling! We immensely enjoyed our post-holiday pampering with Pegasus!

name: Hotel Drisco
title: “Fabulous boutique hotel!”
text:
My husband and I stayed here on the last three nights of our two week trip to California, and it lived up to its reputation. The staff were always friendly and helpful - very helpful. They had great recommendations for local restaurants and things to do. If there was a question they couldn't answer, they would find someone who could answer the question. 
Our room, which was on the small side, was nevertheless everything we needed. It was very clean, and there was efficient use of the space. The complimentary breakfast was a great way to start the day, with cereal, fruit, toast, boiled eggs, croissants and the usual juice, coffee, tea. They had a complimentary town car service that would drop you to either Union Square or the Financial District in the morning. We found this very convenient. We got multi day muni passes, which were very economical and very well used. We would definitely recommend getting these, which you can purchase at the front desk of the hotel. 
We actually loved that this hotel was not in the usual, touristy areas. Not only does it get you away from the hustle and bustle of those spots, but it also allows you to see a part of the city that you may not normally see. Also, the town car service in the morning and the MUNI service will effectively get you to and from the hotel when needed. There are lots of great restaurants within the area, all of which seem to be much more local and much less touristy - which we liked. 
The hotel does not have a parking lot, but there is lots of parking on the streets around the hotel. During the week there is a three hour limit on parking, but we just left our keys with the front desk in the morning and they took care of making sure our car was moved when it needed to be so that we didn't get a ticket. How great is that!! 
There is a reason why this is one of the best hotels in San Fran - it is a really fabulous place to stay.

name: AT&T Executive Education and Conference Center
title: “Great location and service, ordinary rooms and average dining.”
text: We made reservations at this hotel because we were attending events at the University of Texas. This was a great choice, because we were able to walk to many of the events as well as the Blanton Museum. For some of the events, we relied on the hotel shuttle, and the drivers were consistently accommodating. We were also very pleased with the parking, because the valets were so efficient and helpful. If we were going to be out for a few minutes, they kept our car in front of the hotel for easy access for us. They were very friendly and polite. When we arrived at the hotel, we were greeted by a hotel representative in a suit who welcome us and by the second day he knew our rooms and all the individuals in our party. He was very knowledgeable and gracious. He told us he was a student at UT but had quite a bit of hotel experience, which was apparent. Housekeeping was great - housekeepers polite and friendly. Disappointments were our room, which was ordinary and the restaurants, which have limited hours of service. There are times during the day that both dining rooms are closed, and this proved to be a problem for us since we were trying to attend programs and return to the hotel for meals. We ate several meals here in both dining rooms and the food was OK but not great. If we were returning to attend a UT event, we would probably stay here again, but we would make the effort to find other places for dining. I would recommend this hotel to a friend if they were attending an event at UT.

name: AT&T Executive Education and Conference Center
title: “Super Nice Staff, lovely Health Club, Great Location”
text: So, I booked this hotel based, in part, on reviews here. I would agree with most everything said. The staff was super nice and helpful with any questions or needs. I was there during the hottest days of the year, so, the place was quiet and underground parking was easy. The rooms are ok. For all the "energy star" stuff they trumpet, I did find it ironic, annoying, that my sleep was interrupted by the humming of the always-on mini fridge in the room. Multiply that by 400 rooms and we're talking some serious wasted electricity! Another weird one: the place is named after AT and T, and features AT and T uverse boxes on the room TVs. I couldn't buy a movie, so I called the front desk. They sheepishly apologized that none of the hotel rooms are able to use the purchase function on the box, even though it offers movies. The bathrooms are very small and cramped, towels can fall in the toilet easily. Rooms ok, similar to a Courtyard. Health club, although a little walk, was really nice and well kept. Never tried the hotel food; too many alternatives in walking distance. I paid about $120 a night and feel I got a very good stay. The conference center itself was really impressive. The Austin people are sure nice.

name: Fairmont Heritage Place, Ghirardelli Square
title: “Great for families with little kids”
text:
Stayed here over Christmas on our first trip to San Francisco. Loved it! We had a 2 bedroom residence that we Booked through sanfranciscoluxuryhotels.com. 
It was huge, super clean and very modern. The kitchen was a big plus and so were the fireplaces. It was just like having your own really cool apartment in San Francisco. 
The location was great too. The wharf area is great for kids and I never found it a problem to get from there to anywhere in the city.

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “Awesome and we can't wait to visit again....”
text:
We stayed at the Donatello in the Union Square area of San Francisco. It was wonderful, the hotel was great, exactly what we needed. The staff was incredibly helpful and always pleasant. The room and bathroom and the rest of the hotel was A+ when it comes to cleanliness and the upstairs "Clubhouse" was great. Each night after a long day out exploring and walking the lovely San Francisco hills we would head up stairs to the clubhouse where we enjoyed the outside patio and then the clubhouse itself. The clubhouse included the outside patio area, a place to relax and enjoy complimentary coffee/tea/hot chocolare and it also has a fitness area. We stayed an entire week so the hot tub was a great relaxing experience. Being from Boston and YAY, we did win that 2011 Stanley Cup!!!!! we didn't want to miss the games and the relaxing clubhouse with a large screen TV came in handy. The staff knew we were routing for Boston so they immediately became Bruins fans as well to help cheer our team along. 
All in all this place is tremendous in all that it has to offer, location, cleanliness, helpful and pleasant staff. All in all, this made for one of our favorite vacations ever and we love to travel. A place we will revisit in the future for sure!!! Thank you all at the Donatello!
The Gay Family

name: Fairmont Heritage Place, Ghirardelli Square
title: “Fantastic service, great location - best hotel in SF!”
text:
Everything about this hotel was great - I do confirm that it's the number 1 hotel in SF! We were traveling together with my husband - exploring the city of SF. 
The rooms are huge - we got a 2 bedroom apartment with spacious kitchen + dining area, 2 bathrooms (1 with a bath, 1 with shower), cool media system with big TV (+another 2 TVs in the bedrooms). 
The rooms were very clean and very well maintained. 
But the best thing about this hotel is service - concierge service is very good; there is a Cadillac Escalade to take guests to the places around the city and pick them up to take back to the hotel - this is a complimentary service available for all guests. Whatever we needed - there was always someone to help us immediately.
Breakfast is also good, although there is not much to choose from, but the quality of food is good (a lot of fresh fruits and berries). 
Location is very good - a lot of great restaurants around Ghirardelli Square, easy to explore the city, close to piers.
I definitely confirm that this is the best hotel in SF. - After our stay we flu to Hawaii and when came back and stayed 2 nights in Omni hotel (rated Best Luxury hotel in SF in TripAdvisor), which we did not like at all compared to Fairmont, although the price was nearly the same or even more expensive.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Austin - Arboretum
title: “Excellent business and leisure hotel”
text: Excellent hotel - probably one of the best Embassy Suites I have stayed at. The swans in the waterfall were a nice touch. The workout room had good cardio, probably could use some more weight room equipment. Location is convenient to several highways too. And I had quite possibly the best sleeps I've ever had in a hotel. Excellent HVAC too.

name: Fairmont Heritage Place, Ghirardelli Square
title: “Luxury condos at Ghiardelli Squarte with great service, spacious, nice decor, expensive.”
text: Rented luxurious and spacious three bedroom condos at this great facility for $1090/night + tax. Parking cost is almost $50/night. Nice for large family get togethers where you need multiple units. Fabulous service. Basic cost includes daily maid service, continental breakfast, daily afternoon wine and cheese, daily paper, local car service in Escalade within 2 miles will take you to Whole Foods for groceries, mountain bikes (just 2 adult and 2 child bikes for all guests to share), robes and slippers. Good continental breakfast with breads, pastry, large assortment of berries and fruit, juice, good coffee, tea, hard boiled eggs, yogurt, and cereals, Rooms facing North Point Street don't have much of a view. Comfortable beds are kings or twins. Walking distance to good shops, restaurants and Fisherman's Wharf. Highly recommended for families. They also have 2 bedroom and 1 bedroom units. No pool, spa, or restaurant.

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “tappa viaggio di nozze”
text: in ottobre2010.consiglio questo hotel,pulito,bello,comodo in posizione strategica,avevamo una vista spettacolare al 26esimo piano.bellissima la hall quando arrivi hai già l' impressione di aver fatto una buona scelta,molto gentile il personale.sconsiglio il rist. italiano all'angolo,li ci hanno trattatodavvero male

name: Parc 55 Wyndham
title: “Ma la wireless è ancora un optional?”
text:
Albergone pomposo e privo di cura e criterio. Personale simpatico e preparato.
Inutilmente lussuoso perchè privo di un servizio base come la connessione al web.
Suggerito a coppia di zii in viaggio per le nozze d'argento.

name: Moorpark Hotel
title: “Best people and value around”
text: My wife and I have stayed at the Moorpark on previous occasions. They have always gone the "extra" mile to make our stay pleasant. This last stay was for 3 nights to attend the funeral services of our Daughter, Elizabeth. When the girls at the front desk heard of the purpose of our visit they went out and purchased a beautiful ceramic angel and when we returned to our room that evening, they had placed it in our room in a gift wrapped box along with a sympathy card signed by the three people on the front desk...........you won't get that kind of service at the Four Seasons or Waldorf Astoria. I highly recomend the Moorpark and any of the other "joie de vivre" hotels.........they have never disappointed us...............Bill Freeman, Monterey, CA

name: The Fairmont San Jose
title: “Amazing place, but a bit expensive”
text: It was all I thought it would be, but the price is a bit much. When you are paying that much for a room there should be no problems and no issues. Had to wait a bit to check in and that is sometimes okay, but when you don't get an extra half hour for a late check out, it leaves a bad taste in you mouth and your pocket book.

name: Travaasa Austin
title: “Great Girls Weekend Getaway!”
text: What a great place! My BFF and I stayed for 3 days and 2 nights (will stay longer next time!). The all inclusive package is the way to go as it includes 3 meals and snacks, you just pay for alcohol. I loved the "no tipping" aspect as it was included in our all inclusive package and don't worry, you're not treated by the staff as "I don't have to be pleasant because their not tipping me anyway" attitude. Everyone treats you as a valued guest and are very personable and accommodating. Activities were fun and broadened my outlook (meditation, aqua yoga, bull riding (for the abs!). Definitely sign up for the Watsu massage - unique experience and very relaxing! The infinity pool is georgeous.I'm glad to see a guy review Travassa, because most of the couples I observed looked like the girl was having a great time and the guy looked like he would rather be doing anything other than lounging at Travassa. I would love to keep this place a secret, but its too good to keep it to myself!

name: Hyatt Place San Jose/Downtown
title: “Way Under-Rated”
text: While all Hotels have their good and bad days, I'm struggling to understand some of the less-than-positive reviews that I have read about this hotel on this site. This Hotel has many strengths that seem to be overlooked by some of the reviewers. The location is ideal, next to the convention center and in the heart of downtown. There is an onsite restaurant and bar and you can walk just about anywhere. The Hotel has a boutique feeling so it is not a typical convention Hotel. Inside, the Hotel is trendy and is not a "traditional" looking Hotel, like some of the other Hotels in the neighborhood. The rooms are spacious. More importantly, the staff was not only extremely responsive to my needs...they anticipated many of my needs. I've stayed at this Hotel in the past and there were some great renovations put in recently...and I understand that there are more to come. For those of you looking at this site to get recommendations for downtown San Jose, I think this Hotel is getting a bum rap.

name: The Inn at Union Square
title: “Never again”
text:
I stayed one night at this hotel on June 28, 2004. That will be the last night for me. This is a "boutique" hotel with a fake library painted in the lobby; an elevator that makes you wonder if it will keep going; tv's that must be at least 20 years old; and a very uncaring staff. The first room they gave me had no tv whatsoever! A call to the front desk elicited the comment of "oh really?". They did immediately transfer me to another room - this one had a tv at least but the reception was poor at best. When I finished my shower and reached for a towel, I realized that I had no towels whatsoever! Three hand towels was it. 
The only bright side of this hotel for me was the shower - it may have had the best water pressure of any hotel I've ever experienced.
When I return to San Francisco, I'll try the Monaco. A friend was staying there at the same time and the difference between the hotels was night and day!

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Noise, noise and more noise”
text:
No sound insulation so you will experience the traffic (and construction) noise throughout the night. 
General Manager Wes Tyler denied that any construction work was being undertaken in the hotel vicinity! Ha! We were there! We heard it! We spent whole evenings unable to sleep because of the noise issues! 
Do not stay at this hotel! 
Charlton

name: The Fairmont San Jose
title: “Very nice, but not exceptional.”
text:
I stayed here with my husband while he was attending a work conference (held at the Fairmont). So he was there for work (and has stayed there before) while it was my first visit, and I was not working, so we had quite different experiences.
He enjoys working with the Fairmont, and has always has very nice things to say about it. His company has a wonderful relationship with them, and enjoy doing business there. My impressions are my own, personal experience.
I had a nice stay as well, but not outstanding. We checked in extremely early (we arrived at 8 a.m.) I understand this is far earlier than normal hotel check-in time, so my husband had called several days beforehand to alert them to our early arrival, and they told him to call back on the morning of our arrival, which we did. When we arrived they did not have a room ready, but said it should be ready in less than an hour, and that they would call my cell phone (he had meetings) when the room was ready. Now they did not know this, and it shouldn't really matter, but I had a raging chest cold, and was shivery, coughing and miserable, and just wanted to lie down somewhere. I waited patiently in the lobby for 45 minutes, took myself out for hot chocolate, and came back and sat by the front desk. I watched a steady stream of people check in and get sent to their rooms. (Perhaps they were all President's Club members, but then so are we). At 10 a.m. I went up and asked again about our room. The very nice gentleman who helped me said it was not ready, and that he couldn't really say when it would be, but that he could offer me a room in the other building. I was thrilled as long as it had a bed and maybe a hot bath. A bellman helped me up to the room with our luggage, which was lovely.
The room was nice. Very spacious and comfortable. The bed was soft and wonderfully warm. The bathroom had a separate tub and shower, with very hot water. It was not the nicest place I've ever stayed, but it was very nice.
I keep coming back to the word "nice." Everything was very adequate, but not stellar. The furnishings and decor was a little dated, and I actually found a "22-karat gold plated" sticker on the tissue box, which seemed a little tacky. (I gave them the benefit of the doubt and assumed they'd left it on by accident, but still. If you have to tell someone something is gold-plated for them to appreciate it, then maybe it shouldn't have been in the first place). The room almost seemed too large for all the furniture, making it feel a little spare.
There was some noise from airplanes landing at the San Jose airport four miles away, and some street noise from the road below, but we had a lovely night's sleep thanks to the luxuriously soft mattress, pillows, and sheets. I wish we could have taken the bed home with us.
We went out for drinks at the bar in the lobby that night, and had difficulty getting the waitress's attention to order. Once we did, she left and came back five minutes later with questions about each order, and then didn't bring our drinks for another 10 or 15 minutes. Getting the bill proved equally challenging, but the drinks were very good.
Overall, I wouldn't advise anyone NOT to stay there, but I can't think of anything exceptional to recommend it either. I had expected something a little more extraordinary, given its reputation, but it is a perfectly fine hotel. I look forward to staying here again next year, if only for the blissfully soft bed.

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “Great place to stay”
text: We spent 3 days at the Omni in San Francisco which was absolute delightful. The room was well appointed. Bed was so comfortable, we ordered a mattress and box springs from Omni after we returned home. Location was within walking distance of many attractions and the staff were very helpful in suggestions for places to go and the best way to get there. There are good restaurants close by and the steak house in the Omni was excellent. Parking was somewhat expensive, but not out of line with area. Great stay in a fascinating city.

name: The Westin Austin at The Domain
title: “It's cool, modern and new”
text:
I stayed here July 19, 2012. The hotel is exceptionally nice, very well appointed and has a lot of activity in the restaurant and bar. The staff was wonderful, rooms were better than the average Westin and the location can't be beat. Shopping and restaurants are across the street. The breakfast buffet was a little disappointing and could be considered "average" for any hotel but below average for a Westin. Overall, I will stay here again next time I'm in Austin. 
The staff is well-trained in service. Everyone is so friendly and helpful. The doorman, maid, desk clerk and waitstaff were all wonderful.

name: Fairmont Heritage Place, Ghirardelli Square
title: “AWESOME HOTEL!!!!! - did not want to leave”
text: So many wonderful things to say about this hotel and the experience we had there. We booked a one bedroom suite and when we checked in were upgraded to a two bedroom apartment. Amazing staff (this includes everyone reception, concierge, housekeeping etc etc), beautiful and clean apartments, fantastic facilities, brilliant location and easily the best hotel we stayed out in the US out of the 8 hotels we booked throughout our holiday. We were traveling with our 8 year old and 1 year old and the fact that the rooms had a front loader, dryer, microwave and two separate bedrooms within the apartment was absolutely priceless to us. Another amazing facility was the concierge car - instead of hailing a taxi the complimentary concierge car and drive would drive you to or from your destination (the rule was it had to be within 5km from the hotel I think). We used this day and night and found it so handy. The only complaint I would have (and because of how wonderful this hotel was it as easily ignored) was that our bedrooms faced the road and the windows were not sound proofed at all as the night traffic noise was really really loud. Although this hotel is on the pricier side of things it was absolutely brilliant value for money.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Some staff members need customer service training”
text: Nice hotel and location. The staff wasn't very friendly.

name: W Austin
title: “Great location - cool hotel”
text: This W is pretty consistent with other Ws - cool scene, decent/nice rooms, trendy. I thought the location was excellent for downtown nightlife and university activities. Being across the street from town lake/a 5+ mile running trail is a big plus as well. Staff was engaging and helpful - rooms/halls are starting to look a little run down but I wouldn't ding the hotel for that yet. Overall I'd stay here again over any of the other options in the area.

name: Hampton Inn Austin - Arboretum Northwest
title: “Consistently Good”
text: Comfy beds, great breakfast; everything we've come to expect from a Hampton Inn.

name: Hotel Valencia - Santana Row
title: “Hotel with a Split Personality - Pick the One Right for You”
text:
This was our second stay at the Valencia. The first stay was mid-week, was upgraded to a Junior Suite on arrival without even asking, room was great, stay was very quiet and enjoyable.
Our second stay was on this past weekend. We checked out a night early due to noise, but would still recommend this hotel with the caveat that you need to pick your nights accordingly. If you are in town to celebrate with friends, or host a private party in the hotel, this is the perfect spot on a weekend. If you are looking for some really great dining and shopping with no need to get in and out of the car and want to actually get some sleep at night, this is a great hotel on a weeknight.
Despite checking out early, I'm still giving the hotel staff top marks. Santana Row, and the hotel, are places to party on the weekend. Not much the staff can do about that. Our first night was sleepless between midnight and 2am as party-goers poured out of the clubs, making one hell of a racket, but sounding like they were all having a great time. On our second night we returned from an excellent dinner at Citrus (the hotel restaurant) to find our room vibrating with base from a private birthday celebration a couple of floors down (we later found out). We just wanted to sleep, so elected to check out. The staff did everything right - they immediately came up to the room, admitted the noise was bad and apologized, offering to move us to another room. We politely declined and packed up. At the front desk they apologized again and then a manager popped up and offered not only to comp us the night, but to put us up in the Presidential Suite. They took us up to the suite (wow...amazing, gorgeous, huge), but when we got there, even they admitted they could still hear the base. They asked if we'd like to try another room, but at this point understood that we just wanted to go. They carried all of our luggage to the street and loaded it into our car for us, apologizing again. Unfortunate situation handled well. Kudos to the staff. Good hotel, nice rooms, pick your night according to the type of stay you are looking for and you'll be good.

name: Lake Austin Spa Resort
title: “Absolutely loved Lake Austin!”
text:
A friend and I recently treated ourselves to a week at Lake Austin Spa. We had a fabulous experience and would highly recommend it to others looking for a destination spa. We greatly enjoyed the fitness classes, had wonderful spa treatments and attended many interesting and informative workshops on everything from organization, aromatherapy and managing stress. We chose lake Austin when we saw the pictures of the common areas on their web site ...they looked like someone's lake house living room that you would want to hang out in. And the experience definitely proved to be just that. We felt we were visiting a friend with a great place on the lake, with a great staff to help us be comfortable, and to give us lots of options for keeping active and enjoying our environment. The fitness classes were great, with enough variety throughout the day/week that you did not get bored and yet it was not overwhelming. We spent time on the lake as well, which was a lot of fun and I would highly recommend (kayaking, boat cruise). I loved the yoga and water classes (Nautical Noodles, Deep Water Workout, etc). 
The rooms are not luxurious (we were in number #30, which I would recommend as well as any of the rooms above #27); decorated in a shabby chic style, they are quite comfortable and ours seemed to be set up perfectly for two women traveling together - large bathroom, two sinks, private area for toilet shower and large closet spaces for two. The bed was very comfy. The rooms are really quiet, you don't hear your neighbors at all. They had a nice TV, DVD player (with a nice choice of DVD's available at the front desk) and a clock radio with an iPod dock. 
The grounds are lovely, beautiful flowers, garden full of herbs and vegies, and great hammocks hung along the lake to curl up in and soak in the relaxing atmosphere and watch the birdlife around the lake. 
The staff was great, very helpful, very friendly, and knowledgeable. They really made you feel comfortable. And amazingly, they were right on top of things (in the spa, restaurant and grounds), but yet you did not feel like they were in the way of enjoying the resort (did a great job of keeping a low profile while providing great service).
The spa treatments were great, a little higher priced than other day spas I have been to, but in general they were worth it. The day spa facilities were wonderful and we felt like we were treated like royalty. 
Last but not least the food at both the Aster Cafe and the main Restaurant was great. Tasty, interesting and yet low cal. We never felt hungry even though we were eating a lot less calories and smaller portions. 
I would definitely go back and will recommend it highly to friends.

name: Moorpark Hotel
title: “I Will Tell Everybody”
text:
Recently on a business trip to San Jose, I chose the Moorpark Hotel for my stay. All I can say is... "This place is great. Great Service, Great Personal, Great Accomodations and of course Great Food. I was treated like a king. Thanks. I will see you again soon, I hope.
Allan

name: Moorpark Hotel
title: “What a Hidden Gem!”
text:
We love to stay at the Moorpark, and this visit was our third time there. Beautiful dark wooded decor, with a contemporary warm flair. Rooms are very spacious and the beds are the best! Service has always been amazing, with the exception of the curt woman who works in the breakfast room, who tends to be very condescending! The pool is amazing with the cute little cabanas, and the lobby fireplace is always burning!
Pros: Location, Decor, Rooms
Cons: Internet access (has never worked for us in any room we've stayed in)

name: The Fairmont San Jose
title: “My favourite hotel in the Valley”
text:
I have stayed at the Fairmont in San Jose many times over the last 15 years and it is my favourite hotel in Silicon Valley. The rooms are spacious and well equipped particularly in the new tower. The staff are great especially the concierge team, who are very helpful. The Grill on the Alley is wonderful for steaks and the staff in the bar are second to none.
The Presidents Club, which is free to join, provides a special check-in desk, free Internet and free hire of golf clubs and bikes.
There are lots of local restaurants all within walking distance as well as the Convention Center and the Tech Museum.
On the downside the health club is a bit small for the hotel's size and some of the equipment is getting old. Prices in the bar and restaurants are quite high.
Overall though a great experience and one I would recommend to anyone.

name: Microtel Inn & Suites by Wyndham Austin Airport
title: “I loved it and I'll be back”
text:
I was at the Austin Airport and needed a place to stay for one night. I called this hotel using the courtesy phone and from the moment they answered to the moment I checked out they were amazing. The hotel is very clean and well kept. They offer a free hot breakfast, a free airport shuttle, and free local & long distance calls within the US. They also have free WIFI and if that wasn't enough...every day they have warm cookies for your to snack on with unlimited coffee and tea in the lobby.
Most importantly though, the guest service was amazing. The team is so friendly, courteous, helpful, and professional. 
I recommend this hotel for anyone who needs to be out by the airport in Austin. You can't beat the value and the service is second to none.
Thanks for showing me some true Texas hospitality.

name: Hampton Inn Austin - Arboretum Northwest
title: “Great Experience and Incredible Deal”
text: First of all, the price is amazing and we felt we got so much more than what we paid for. We would have felt the price was great even if it didn't have free parking, free hot breakfast that was very substantial, free coffee and fruit 24 hours/day. I always worry when I can't get my usual double espresso in the morning, but they offered a "robust" coffee as one of the choices that worked just fine. The room was clean, comfortable, well laid out, pleasantly decorated, and had a convenient place to put our "stuff" both in the bedroom and the bathroom. The staff was very helpful and friendly, and the woman at the front desk actually called us after we settled in to see if we needed anything and to see if we still needed a rollaway. The room was quiet, no mechanical noises or sounds from other guests or the street. I don't think I've ever been so pleased with a hotel before! After our stay at this hotel we moved to a very lavish hotel 4 times the price and we had nothing but complaints, which makes me appreciate this one even more. On a scale of 1-10, I give this Hampton Inn at least a 15.

name: Hotel Palomar San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Ottimo hotel centrale”
text:
L'hotel è in posizione centralissima, a due passi da Union Square esvoltato l'angolo si è subito in Market Street, all'altezza del centro commerciale Westfield e dei migliori negozi. Il servizio è efficiente, l'unica pecca è la colazione: servizio lentissimo (ho aspettato mezz'ora per una colazione continentale).
A pochi passi dalla fermata del metro MUNI e BART dell'emarcadero e alla fermata della linea F Fisherman's Wharf-Castro.
La palestra è davvero piccola, ci sono solo 2 tapis roulant, 1 cyclette e una macchina per fare pesi quindi è difficile trovare subito posto, bisogna aspettare qualche minuto ch esi liberi.

name: The Fairmont San Jose
title: “This place was fabulous”
text: Great rooms, great beds, great amenities, great location, great restaurants nearby.

name: The Fairmont San Jose
title: “THe Best Hotel in San Jose”
text: I had an opportunity to spend several nights at this hotel and without any doubt this is the best place to crash after a long day. Rooms are clean, a reasonably sized swimming pool, a very comfy location in the center of San Jose. Should I say something negative, then they can improve their room service. Waiting for dinner for about an hour was a little too long.. Strongly recommended. If you book it well in advance, you can get a sweat deal around 130 bucks, otherwise you can pay for the same room about twice as much.

name: W Austin
title: “Don't Waste Your Money”
text: As a resident of Austin staying with an out of town guest, I'm appalled!!!! The room was certainly not up standards for the price they were paying. We had a pool view. DO NOT GO IN THE WATER!! It was so murky and FULL of drunk 20 somethings chicken fighting and breaking bottles. (Who doesn't love a pool chicken fight but this was gross.) Upwards of $350. Room service brought up the wrong food (offered little apology besides a woops). Attempted to use the concierge service for a salon appointment. They did not even know where the pre-reserved car was at time that THEY told us to be downstairs. When we asked for the cross streets to give a cab, they had no idea, couldn't even provide us the phone number. The woman rolled her eyes and huffed when I told her I was a resident and if she could just tell me the salon name I could figure it out. I can't even begin to tell you how rudely she scoffed and stalled before telling me. When we returned we told them we would be checking out the following day instead of staying for the planned 2 nights. To their credit, a manager called who said he would remove the room service charges, and would upgrade us to stay the second night. We politely declined the upgrade and told him we'd already made other reservations. Upon checkout the charge for the car transfer and the room service was still on the bill. For what they are charging, they don't even begin to have their act together.

name: Fairmont Heritage Place, Ghirardelli Square
title: “Hotel (quase) de excelência”
text:
A localização do Hotel não podia ser melhor para quem pretende fugir do centro e estar numa área tranquila e com uma vista maravilhosa.
Os apartamentos do Hotel são muito requintados e confortáveis.
A cozinha está equipada ao pormenor. 
A sala é confortável ainda que os sofás que a compõe sejam de qualidade inferior.
A lareira a gás na sala é esteticamente um regalo.
Os quartos são top sendo que o nosso tinha ainda umas vistas excelentes para a baía.
As casas de banho são extraordinárias.
O serviço prestado pelo hotel é de excelência. Requisitamos duas bicicletas para atravessarmos a Golden Gate e no dia a seguir de manhã lá estavam as bicicletas à nossa espera, com duas mochilas e dois capacetes.
Iamos jantar fora e o serviço do hotel ia levar-nos e buscar-nos num jipe do hotel.
Só não concedo classificação máxima por dois pormenores:
1. Pequeno almoço é um pouco limitado
2. Os sofás dos apartamentos e as paredes do mesmo já necessitam de um remodelação e de uma ligeira pintura, respectivamente.
Quanto ao demais, top, top, top.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Maritime Themed Hotel”
text: The hotel is part of a historic building with exposed beams and brickwork. The rooms are a bit over the top dressed in the nautical theme but this adds to the fun. The beds are really comfy and the room was kept spotless. Staff were friendly and always happy to help. We stayed on the 4th floor which was quiet. There was a family of four next door with 2 young children and we could not hear them. The room was large but no view. The only fault I had (and it's a little one) was that the room was not cleaned until 15:30 every day. Until the last day when they knocked me out of bed at 08:30.

name: Conrad Indianapolis
title: “THE Place to Stay in Indianapolis”
text: I just returned from a two night stay at this property and wanted to share my experience. Every aspect of my stay was outstanding - from the check-in process to the valet delivering my car when I was ready to leave. As a woman traveling alone, I especially appreciated the security provided and professional service exhibited by all members of the staff. The room was lovely and the bed was absolutely luxurious. The evening turn -down service was a real treat - complimentary bottled water by the bed, fresh ice in the silver ice bucket, jazz music softly playing from the bedside CD player, and lights on dim in the bathroom with the TV in the bathroom turned on to the next day's happenings at the hotel. My request for a late check-out was accommodated with no problems. When the bellman noticed that I had been waiting for a few moments to check-out, he proceeded to handle the whole process at his station, even offering to print out directions for my trip out of the city. While I did not visit either of the restaurants on-site, the food provided for our meetings (breakfast and lunch for three days) was very tasty and well presented...all the participants anticipated the next day's offerings, as they were so much better than the fare usually provided at meetings of this sort...another real testimony to this hotel's standards. I am looking forward to returning with my family.

name: Hotel Drisco
title: “Extraordinary service at Hotel Drisco!”
text: I had been looking at small, upscale boutique hotels located in a quiet section of San Francisco. I had read some of the previous reviews and decided to try Hotel Drisco. It is worthy of all of the excellent reviews. The staff was more than helpful in every way. As I am a female traveling alone, I am very conscious of safety and security. The area is very safe and I felt secure at all times. The staff greeted me by name and always asked how I was doing. The amenities were also first rate. But the most impressive aspect of the hotel was the personalized service. All requests were met with a smile and without question from making restaurant reservations to small room repairs. One of the faucets in the bathroom was not functioning properly and I informed the front desk. I expected to have a washer replaced, but instead received a completely new faucet set. The breakfast that is provided was quite enough to satisfy my needs and very tasty. The only thing that people should be aware of is the only parking is on the street and is restricted during the day. I had no problem finding a space in the evening though. The Hotel Drisco was a great place and a great alternative to the large, somewhat impersonal hotels and I would stay there again without hesitation.

name: The Westin Austin at The Domain
title: “Very Enjoyable Stay”
text: Spent our wedding anniversary weekend in Austin and stayed at the Westin in the Domain. It was excellent. We had an enthusiastic welcome, all the staff were exceptionally helpful. After checking in we left our room for a while and found a nice bottle of wine and a greetings card on our return. A very nice touch. Rooms were very clean, modern, loved the bed, so comfortable. All in all a very nice place to stay, called them direct to book and got a great rate. This is now our hotel of choice next time we stay in the Austin area. Highly recommend it.

name: The Westin Austin at The Domain
title: “What a staff!!!!”
text:
I travel about 30 weeks a year on business, all over the US. I've never had the level of service that I received in this hotel! It seemed as if there was a staff member around just waiting for me to need something and they were on it! If all hotels were as focused on top notch service, as the Westin Austin is, people would never bother to go home!
Keep up the good work Westin Austin staff!
Brian Keller

name: Hotel Drisco
title: “one of the best stays - ROMANTIC”
text:
I wanted to take this opportunity to thank you and your excellent staff for making our 15th anniversary, one of the best experiences to date.
Everyone we dealt with, from the front desk to the cleaning staff were top notch. I have stayed in many varied hotels in my life, but this one was by far one of the nicest...we both love historic hotels!
Thank you so much for the amazing room (207). Having a room with a view and one that was so nicely appointed made for a very romantic experience. The champagne and chocolates, with the nice card was also appreciated.
The included breakfast is a great touch and matches the high standards of this hotel
So please thank everyone and if we come to SF again, we will be staying with you! Being relatively close to Califorinia street and the #1 bus made getting to down town/cable cars easy.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “What a great hotel and location”
text:
We have arrived home today after a fantastic 3 week trip to California.
We arrived at the Chancellor to stay for 3 nights before flying back to the UK and we were really are glad we chose this hotel. All the staff work so hard and are always at hand if you need anything. A very special thanks to Wes Tyler the General Manager who arranged a nice Wedding Anniversary surprise for us on our arrival. 
This Hotel is so well located for everything you need. Eating, shopping and getting about on all the transport is all on the doorstep here. On check in we arrived early but no problem they took our luggage off us and stored it away which allowed us to go off and look about. The complimentary beverages and cookies in the lobby were also something we looked forward to when we returned after a long day out and about. The room was very nice and had a nice big bath so i could have long soak before getting ready for a night out.

name: W Austin
title: “Unmatched Service and Location”
text:
Thoroughly enjoyed my experience at the W. frequented many W's in my travels and this one did not disappoint. spent afternoon at pool. Drinks in one bar and food in another, all 3 were great spots with exceptional service. 
Most impressive was the staff. From check-in to check-out they made me feel my room was worth the full value I paid. Further, embarrasses to say, I ran out of room leaving behind my brand new in the box IPAD and left message after my flight. Fully expecting it to be "lost" as has happened with other items left behind over the years in other hotels, i was so excited and pleased to immediately hear back they not only had it but had my platinum info on file to return it! I willl be going back several times this year!!

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “Read 143 positive reviews - this makes it 144! So happy we stayed here!”
text: This was a "bucket list" trip to CA - we were sure we wouldn't return so it was important that this trip went well. I read so many reviews before I booked I made myself dizzy. The Donatello had 143 positive reviews so I picked them & I'm so glad I did! The place is ALL about service & they made every day - we stayed 5 days -- a happy event. Highly recommend this Hotel.

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “Great position - a little noisy”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Donatello for 2 nights when visiting San Francisco. This hotel is great value and in an unbeatable position - just a short walk to Union Square and the Powell Street Trolley line. The staff are really helpful and the rooms quite large and comfortable. The only minus is that it's somewhat noisy at night which I guess is to be expected in such a central location. I would have no hesitation in recommending the Donatello to anyone visiting this wonderful city.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Great value, location, service”
text:
Beautiful historic hotel in downtown Dallas. Our experience was good in every aspect - we had 2 rooms and six people in our party. Service was excellent - everyone was friendly, helpful, and showed classic Texas hospitality. Valet parking was no problem - yes - we phoned before we went downstairs - but we never waited more than 5 minutes. The valet staff helped with directions and tips for traffic and parking. Loved the evening reception and cookies and milk buffet. Very nice sitting area to enjoy these and the breakfast buffet. Rooms are spacious - bathrooms are large. I was worried about elevators based on some of the reviews - they were fast and timely. No problems.
This is a great value - highly recommend. If I return to Dallas - I'll stay again.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Nice hotel with special amenities”
text:
When I travel for races (this time a 1/2 marathon) I'm careful to find a room that is quiet and within walking distance to good restaurants. The Magnolia fulfilled each of these requirements. 
It's housed in an art-deco type building downtown. The rooms are modern and comfortable. They're large for what I'm used to. The bed was comfortable and I slept well. There are clubs and bars nearby but I was not disturbed by noise inside or outside the hotel. 
Each night there is a free happy hour and cookies & milk. The area where these were held was comfortable and we sat for awhile to enjoy our snack. 
There are dining options available nearby as well as a Starbucks atttached to the hotel. 
I would stay here again and have already booked the same chain in Denver for another trip.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “magnificient”
text: An Absolute fabulous hotel. The fact that the company took a hystorical bank building and turned it into a hotel was wonderful enough, but they left the integrity of the building from the architecture to the pictures of the Pegasus. The management and staff were wonderful. I had a suite that had a comfy bed, a wonderful kitchen, and nice sitting area. Our view was of a magnificient church and downtown square. The valet parking was a little steep $22.00, but at least I didn't have to worry about finding a place to park on my own. I left some clothes in my car and the valet retreived them without any negativity. I have traveled all over the world, and this was the best hotel experience I've ever received. Would stay here again without any regrets. MAGNIFICIENT!!!!

name: Comfort Suites City Centre
title: “Loved it !!!”
text:
I just had to write about this hotel. I was staying in Indy for business, but my conference was at a "stuffy" hotel. For the same price, I stayed here and I felt it was much better. The decor was hip and cool. It was just south of the downtown area...still walkable. It is in the shadows of Lucas Oil Stadium. The room was huge (could fit up to 6 adults easily). 
 I was extermely pleased upon getting into the room. The bed was so comfortable. I have not seen this in such a long time. Most pillows and beds in hotels are just awful. This was the opposite. When I walked in the room, I felt like I was in a showroom condo. It had a fridge that you could actually adjust the temp and a thermostat for the room temp. 
 Overall, the staff was great, the breakfast was great (with lots of variety), the business center was nice. They had a restaurant that became a bar/hang-out at night. I did not visit the pool or workout room, so I can't comment about those. I would definately stay there again.

name: Comfort Suites Indianapolis Airport
title: “Good value”
text: We stayed here while attending the Big 10 Championship. This Comfort Suites was clean, the staff friendly and helpful, the breakfast satisfactory. The front desk help asnswered our questions and called a taxi for us. (I wish someone would have brought the aiport shuttle van to pick us up at 2 am when I called to ask for suggestions on how to get a taxi back to the hotel. That is a suggestion during a busy event.) This site is a very good value for the price.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Indianapolis Downtown
title: “Excellent Value Downtown Indianapolis”
text:
Booked this hotel online and it is one of the most charming Hilton properties I've ever stayed in. Property is a vintage building right in the middle of the great downtown attractions for walking and dining. Check out Libertine which is just a block or two away for phenomenal cocktails and food. Try the waffle with chicken liver pate with your drinks, you can crawl back to your great room at the Hilton Garden Inn.
Hotel offers Hillton HHonors members very generous hospitality, I was impressed!

name: Residence Inn Indianapolis Northwest
title: “Second Review, Much the Same”
text:
This was my second stay at the Residence Inn Northwest Indianapolis. Much of my previous review is still applicable.
This hotel is good for business travelers who need to be in the area. It is located in an industrial area with few attractions nearby. The nearest grocery store is approximately 2 miles away. I would not recommend it for visitors who want to experience the culture of Indianapolis.
It provides a good value in the form of a free continental breakfast, large rooms, free evening appetizers, and decent amenities. The continental breakfast provided hot items like eggs and sausage, as well as an assortment of cereals, breads, yogurts, fruits, coffee, and juices. My room was located on the third floor, very large, clean, and quiet. I did not eat any of the evening appetizers. The pool was decent-sized. The gym had two treadmills, an elliptical, exercise bike, and crunch bench, but no disinfectant or cleaning supplies, which made me question the room's hygiene. There was a computer for internet access in the lobby, but the connection was very slow. WIFI was available
The service was hit or miss. For the most part, the employees were friendly and accommodating. However, one female in particular seemed more interested in fraternizing with the male maintenance employees than providing service to the customers or hotel. I also saw some of the maintenance employees browsing the internet from the lobby computer.
I would stay here again for the hotel's value and the Marriot rewards program. Don't expect a five-star experience, but at least you'll get your money's worth.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “I Will Stay Here Again and Again!”
text: This being my first trip to Dallas I was unsure of where to stay. When I learned that there was a Magnolia Hotel in Dallas I figured if it were anything like the one in Houston I was going to be in good hands. Let me tell you, it was even better! The staff was very courteous and helpful and the place was amazing. For the size of the hotel it was very busy with two weddings taking place that weekend but that didn't stop or hinder any of our accommodations. The hotel also offers free rides to local attractions which was a definite plus and our driver, Moustapha, was amazing and very helpful with deciding where we should eat or hang out. It was as if we had our own personal city tour guide who knew all about the city and we didn't have to worry about anything. I had an amazing experience at this hotel and I suggest everyone give it at try, you won't be disappointed.

name: W Austin
title: “Super Trendy as Usual, but Great Service”
text:
We live in Austin, but I had some Starwood points and decided to use them on an evening downtown. Plus, I've stayed T a few Ws and was interested in seeing how ours would compare to the ones in New York, Seattle and Chicago.
I arrived late in the afternoon on a Friday. The front desk agent had the perfect mix of professionalism and friendliness and check-in was speedy and efficient. My room was a Cozy Queen on the 9th floor. It was small, the decor was interesting (though I didn't care for the wallpaper) and the view was great. No complaints about the room, but were I traveling with a family I'd probably want something a little bigger.
My husband arrived later in the evening and we went out. We returned to the hotel around midnight to find the place was party central with a crowd ranging in age from 20 to 60. I was tapped out for the evening, but I'll definitely go back for a drink one day.
The next morning we had contact with more of the W "talent" who were all very friendly and helpful -- the valet, the people in bar selling breakfast items, and the morning concierge. No complaints. W Austin tries to be cool in an earnest sort of way, much like the others. It's a different vibe than what you'd get at The Four Seasons, but it was fun and I'd stay there again.

name: Wyndham Indianapolis West
title: “Great Service”
text: Everything was great except I stayed on the first floor and could hear a door being slammed shut throughout the night. It woke me up two or three times because it also shook the bed a little. Based on the rest of my experience, I would stay here again, but would avoid the first floor in hopes for a more quiet night.

name: Extended Stay America - Indianapolis - Castleton
title: “Perfect Place to stay for extended period of time”
text:
This is the perfect place to stay for those who plan on staying over a period of several days. I stayed there for a period of 8 days and nites, I was very pleased with the room and staff. 
The hotel staff was very informative and accomadating as well as helpful. 
The rooms are efficiency's and mine was in great condition, it also had working applicances--refrigerator/freezer, toaster, microwave and stove. It is definitely great if you plan on fixing some of your own food instead of eating out all the time.
They also had wireless internet if you needed the access. The bed was also very comfortable, the mattress was definitely not worn out like I have experienced in other hotels.
This hotel would be perfect for the working person or someone planning on staying an extended period of time.
The hotel is also in a great location with plenty of things to do within minutes. If you like to shop there is a mall within 3 miles of the hotel as well as plenty of fast food places. There is also a Golden Corral Restaurant right across the street from the hotel.
I would definitely stay there again if I was working in the area.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “We love it and we'll be back for sure”
text:
The service is Supreme, the employees are just willing to help you all the time, the people at the front desk excellent, the housekeepers very very polite, the hotel couldn't be better, I recomended this hotel always.
Congratulations
Magdalena Groover

name: Super 8 Austin Airport, South
title: “Absolutely Incredible”
text: This hotel was far above and beyond any expectations I had. And just minutes from downtown. Every need we had was anticipated. Lavish breakfast and dessert bar. Snacks in the room for free. Starbucks coffee/latte/espresso machine. Video/books library. Sauna/exercise room. Extensive guidebook with thoughtful notes. Helpful employees. Pillow menu. TV in the elevator. I'm just getting started...Serious luxury for this economy price!

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Friendly staff. Bathroom wasn't clean on arrival, elevator & hallway floors filthy.”
text: The staff was very nice and helpful. However, upon arrival, there was hair all over the lid and seat of the toilet. They offered another room, which I turned down at first, but after a 30 minute wait for housekeeping, I decided to take the other room. They kindly upgraded me to a suite, which was nice. I was also surprised at how poorly maintained the elevator floors, and some of the hallway floors were. At first glance, this is a pretty hotel, but look a little further, and it's not living up to its potential.

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “FANTASTIC HOTEL AT A GREAT PRICE”
text: Six of us from Seattle, including two teen-age boys and one very picky adult traveler, just spent three nights and four days at the Omni, and our experience was perfect in every way. The rooms were spacious, comfortable, well-maintained and, most importantly, immaculate; the staff was knowledgeable, friendly, and enormously helpful; and we were thrilled with the price (we booked our rooms through Alaska Airlines and received our third night free), having stayed in hotels that cost twice as much and provide far less in the way of comfort, cleanliness, and service. The Omni is centrally located and offers easy access, either on foot or public transportation, to many cultural attractions, interesting neighborhoods, and great cafes and restaurants. Not only would I recommend the Omni to friends and family, but from now on, I will never stay anyplace else in San Francisco. By the way, another highlight of our trip was the San Francisco Movie Tour--a must if you are travelling with teenage movie buffs.

name: Wyndham Indianapolis West
title: “Happy With My Stay”
text: I definitely appreciate the professional service. I expect a clean quiet place to stay and get it here. The Park and Stay is a great feasture.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Great accommodations in prime location”
text: We stayed at the Chancellor for 4 nights. This is a historic hotel, steps around the corner from Union Square, close to dining, cafes, tour bus stops and cable cars. While it might lack some of the pizzaz and modern touches that other area hotels might offer, this hotel is still preferable. The room was smaller, but clean and quite comfortable. The bedding is always crisp and clean. The bathrooms are older, but very clean. We booked a couple of months in advance, quoted a CAA membership and got a great deal: $125/night! The lobby always offers fresh tea/coffe/cookies/apples. All in all, I would totally stay there again and highly recommend it (unless you're really picky!!)

name: Sheraton Indianapolis City Centre Hotel
title: “Great location, OLD hotel”
text: We stayed for a wedding and were sorely disappointed. The hotel's carpets were dirty. The wallks dingy. The rooms themselves were fine, but the common areas were just gross. The elevators were super slow. The pool was packed. The location is excellent for any downtown activities, but the amenties are really lacking. I'd stay somewhere else the next time.

name: W Austin
title: “Best Hotel Experience EVER!”
text: From the moment I arrived with my brothers and friend it was a great experience. The staff greet you at the door and everything is beautiful, clean, and posh. I felt like I was in Miami, Florida because of the way the hotel was setup and decorated. The room was large enough for 4 of us to be moving around in. The room was decorated contemporary and also felt very comfortable and cozy. They were also very clean and smelt amazing walking in. I knew I would be getting a good nights sleep because the beds were so comfortable. While we were getting ready to go out we were able to hook up our iphone to a docking station they had and play our music. Initially the docking station was not working, my brother called down to let them know in within 5 minutes someone was in the room switching out the docking station for a new one. We had a great view of the river and city. The pool was very posh though It was a typical hot summer day so it was packed and on the small side. They provided oversized, soft, white towels to use and staff walked around to see if you needed anything fairly frequently and conveniently. At night we were able to adjust the lighting in the room and around the bed frames which was blue lighting, I thought it was different and cool. The only thing I would change would be that the bathroom was open with a clear glass door so it made it hard to shower with friends and my brothers there. I had to make them wait down at the pool while I showered then they took turns and we had to wait on the bedroom side while someone showered just to protect their privacy. On the first level they also have a great bar/club like area with several rooms to lounge and have cocktails/beers. It was a saturday night and had a dj after 9pm mixing up some good music. Overall this was the best hotel experience and I will definitely be back again

name: Holiday Inn Express Indianapolis South
title: “state fair”
text: This is a good place to stay if your going to the state faire. It is far enough out of town that it is quiet enough so you can get a good nights sleep but is located close to the museums and other attractions You can get to them and the state fair using less busy back streets. The staff is more friendly then just about any hotel I have stayed at. The rooms are clean and they have a nice work out room, hot tub , and pool. Very secure place to stay. you have to use your pass card to get every where. They will take care of anything you need. This is a grate family hotel.

name: Comfort Inn & Suites N at Pyramids
title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: I had an occasion to stay at this place this week and found that this is a wonderful motel. Started off when I made the reservation I was pleasantly surprised at the very reasonable rate for the area. I found everyone very nice and helpful, the room very comfortable and the breakfast very good. I am going to use this place again.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Indianapolis Downtown
title: “Thanks to other reviewers for recommending this place! It's fantastic!”
text: Fabulous little hotel, awesome location, clean and attractive, tons of charm, wonderful service, great bedroom/bathroom and right in the best part of town. Absolutely loved it and would not have known a Hilton Garden Inn could be this great if not for the accolades by other reviewers. Thanks for the great tip!

name: La Quinta Inn Indianapolis East-Post Drive
title: “Great Stay!!”
text: Very clean hotel, recently updated semi-suite rooms. Beds were very comfortable and the continental breakfast was very good. Location is right off I70 just before the I465 interchange, so very handy to get around city in the a.m.

name: Crowne Plaza Indianapolis Downtown (Union Station)
title: “Average at best”
text: We stayed for two nights due to our sons hockey tournament downtown. I was not surprised by the price for the room but I thought it would have a bit more. It's was a basic holiday inn size double bedroom but with no microwave or mini-fridge. When we arrived a hose was laying in the bathroom with a bunch of dirt laying in the bathtub. We had to take our truck and tried to parkin the underground structure. Well the truck wouldn't fit so I had to valet my truck wich wa 27 per day, ok no big deal right? Except that the valet was parking on the street right in front of the hotel. If you're going to pay for valet it should be a covered area after all it's 27 per day. We were given two passes for breakfast which was a bummer but what really pissed me off was that we had to pay a extra 14 dollars for the kids to eat at a very minimal breakfast. Just to let you know any juice is not included in your free breakfast which included under cooked scrambled eggs, french toast, grits, biscuits and gravy, small danishs, cartons of milk you can get at school for lunch, muffins and bagels, that's it. Ohh wait the milk was for the small selection of cereal. The trains weren't that bad at first, but the second night we woke up at 1200 am to what sounded like a train de-railing for about 10 mins. If you stay on the north side of the hotel you should be ok though.

name: Holiday Inn Express Indianapolis South
title: “GREAT VALUE / GOOD STAFF-TRAVEL AGENT PERSPECTIVE”
text:
I stayed at this hotel with a group of about 50. It was very sufficient for the groups needs. Nothing fancy, but clean and cute. The rooms were good size, and the free breakfast came in handy because we were in a rush every morning when we had to leave for a youth convention. The day staff was amazing, especially Heather and company, and the manager. The night staff had one women who was a little grouchy and all the teens were afraid of her! OF course, with 40 kids walking around the lobby until 100 or 200am every night wouldnt put me in the greatest mood either! The front desk day staff Heather and I beleive the guys name was David, were exstremely friendly and helpful. They helped us with everything from directions, to recommendations, to getting me dish soap for my room! 
The lobby area was very cute with tables and chairs to eat breakfast or play cards at night. The pool was nice, too bad no outdoor pool, but there were some lounge chairs outside to sit on. This hotel was only 10 minutes to the convention center, and I liked the fact we shared a parking lot with CVS, which came in handy. There was lots of restraunts around too, chinese, wendys, taco bell,Mcdonalds, Dennys, and few fancy ones.
A good choice if you are on a budget but CLEAN AND CUTE is a must.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Excellent value for the money. Very nicely remodeled, convenient, great amenities.”
text: Great value in the Dallas West End. Rooms are beautiful, friendly staff, nice amenities, great breakfast buffet and evening receptions. I would definitely stay there again. Valet parking is the only option, but priced reasonably at $22/day.

name: Super 8 Austin Airport, South
title: “Tremendous Value !”
text:
Date: 6/10/08
My teen son and I stayed at this hotel overnight per reviews on Trip Advisor.com. We were not disappointed ! This hotel was an unbelievable value. The room (and hotel) was beautifully appointed with elegant amenities, surely found only in hotels priced two to three times the room rate we paid. Had I entered the hotel with my eyes closed no one would’ve ever convinced me I was at a Super 8 hotel, especially for the price. The room had a refrigerator, microwave, and a large screen TV with built in VHS and DVD player. The bathroom even had a weigh scale. The beds were very comfortable. The wireless internet worked flawlessly. The A/C system worked great. The hotel staff and service were superb and even had delicious goodies in the lobby upon our arrival. The desk receptionist gave great dinner recommendations and even provided discount coupons which we took advantage of. Finally, the complimentary breakfast was unbelievable as it included more than an expected continental breakfast with real eggs, meat, and waffles ! (Texas style) .. and it was all delicious ! The only minor inconvenience I found was that the exercise room was somewhat small and cramped and the single treadmill did not work properly. Otherwise this was a great stay – my son wanted to check in for a couple more nights, but alas, it couldn’t be accommodated in our plans. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

name: La Quinta Inn Indianapolis East-Post Drive
title: “basic and fine”
text:
Stayed at this hotel on our way to Cleveland passing through Indy.
The room was clean. Bed was comfy. Quiet hotel.
I didn't necessarily notice the security issues that another review noted, but I can see that happening. It's honestly not the best part of Indy, but not the worst. The area is definitely so-so. 
Someone did scrape the bumper of my car in the parking lot. Could have been the guy wandering the lot with a broom but not sweeping trash. But that's my only downfall of the place. Which is honestly just the downfall of people not being able to drive.

name: Marriott Indianapolis Downtown
title: “Great location, but overall a hairried experience, I won't be back.”
text:
