It's not often that I am really dis-satisfied with a hotel, and part of that is I travel a lot and I understand when things get a little far out or perhaps the hotel is understaffed. However, after 3 stays at this property, I feel that it is really not well run and I doubt I will be back here under any circumstance.
The property itself is beautiful, a grand lobby, great looking decor, a pretty restaurant -starbucks booth in the lobby, comfy beds and linens -what's not to like right? ---Well I'll tell ya.
I stayed at this property for a week in June 2008 -taking a class that was south of the hotel. EVERY night that I came back to the hotel there were tons of people in the lobby waiting to check in, or ???. It was hard to get to the elevators. Once upstairs the halls were often full of people and then the room internet didn't work. I called repeadidly to have it fixed -to no avail. The halls remained loud (as they had been on my previous 2 visits) well into the night. So not a restful nights sleep.
My room key wouldn't open my room door twice which meant I had to go and wait downstairs with all the others waiting for ?? 
The gym had broken equipment -which I was told would be fixed -on my first visit in May, in June it was still broken. 
After a while -everything about this hotel became annoying, waiting for the elevators, not being able to work out on site, dealing with the numb staff, having to use the internet in the lobby -because at the time the lounge didn't have wireless working either, being woken up at night by doors slamming or people laughing/screaming. --Bear in mind I spend more than a third of the year on the road. 
This hotel really pushed my patience. In the end I checked out of this Hotel a day early and moved down the block to the Conrad. Although the Conrad didn't meet my per diem rate it was well worth the extra $95 to have some peace and to finally sleep.

name: Marriott Indianapolis Downtown
title: “Nice view of Downtown”
text: If you have to stay in downtown Indianapolis this hotel was in a great location. Very close proximity to Rt 65. Great view from our King room on the 10th floor. We overlooked Maryland St and the Lucas stadium and a baseball field. Walking distance to Circle center mall and restaurants. The hotel lobby was clean and the valet (although expensive at $28/night) was prompt and courteous. The valet staff went out of their way to get us some bottles of water for our long drive home. The room was clean and the bathroom was larger than I expected. There was a very convenient Starbucks in the lobby. Be careful to avoid game times as traffic could get congested.

name: Marriott Indianapolis Downtown
title: “typical business hotel - nothing great”
text:
We booked into this hotel because the original hotel attached to the conference was booked out. This was the spillover hotel (since the conference was held at the Westin, which is next door). 
We'd stayed in the Marriott before (Sydney and other places) and we were confident of the sort of stay we'd be in for. And we were not disappointed. We had the typical business hotel feel (nice hotel overall, overpriced restaurant, busy busy = noisy)... but what made it not so nice was that it was overfull with conferences and delegates (I'm not sure how many conferences/meetings they had per day!). 
The bell boys were nice and polite and generally the front of house was friendly too. We'd just found out that we were pregnant and they remembered, which was nice. 
However, what annoyed us was one particular concierge man who was condescending and patronising. We wanted to book the limo service from the hotel to the airport (costs 12 USD per person, which would have made it 24 USD for two of us; a taxi would cost between 23-27!). He spent about 5 minutes trying to dissuade us from asking him to book it (it's easier to get it from the front; it's faster to get to the airport). We explained to thim that our trip from airport to the hotel was diabolical (taxi seats felt like the springs had sprung for good, wipers were not working, air con not working, windows were down so got wet from rain!) and he asked where we were from and whether we had taxis where we lived?!! (what's that got to do with anything?!!). 
Another time, we wanted to rent a car and previously asked one of the concierges whether we had to pay to park in the hotel carpark. There were 3 of us together when we asked and the woman had said that it was free for hotel guests. We were real happy so on the day we rented the car, we approached this same condescending person and asked him for the pass to the car park and he said that we had to pay 21USD for the day. It wasn't the fact that we had to pay that got us, it was what he said when we told him that we had been misinformed. He said "oh, maybe you asked whether you could park at the marriott courtyard? Maybe you misunderstood" (the courtyard is just 2 blocks away and anyway, it's not free there - you need to pay 10USD). Instead of apologising and saying that we had somehow been misinformed, he implied that the 3 of us had misunderstood his colleague. How rude. Customer service - I think not. 
Not impressed with this person AT ALL. Am very tempted to write a complaint letter when I can be bothered. Apart from him and the very noisy corridors (even though we were located at the end of one), it's an average hotel. Because we paid 145USD/night without breakfast (which costs 13.50 +++), it's not worth it.

name: Always Inn
title: “Creepy Crawly Ville”
text: Where do I start? When I first walked in to my room there was a dirty trashcan in the bathtub so I had to ask them to finish cleaning. There is always a group of people hanging out smoking around the outside the office like it's a coffee shop or something. The owners are unreachable. The rooms are completely infested with roaches and flees. You can expect the housekeeper to pound on the door like she's trying to knock it off the hinges. If you're ever looking for sex offenders you can find plenty of them residing at 7410 East 21st Street Indianapolis, IN 46219. They only do linens and housekeeping once a week and there's no laundry facility onsite. The nearest laundromat and grocery store is a mile away and if you don't have a car the only way you can get to it is by cab, (expect to pay anywhere from $10 to $15 for that trip) because there's no bus that goes to the laundromat. Their weekly rate is $185 and that doesn't include the phone which they will charge $10 extra per week for and that's local calling only. They go in your room when you're not there and the maintenance people come and check your air conditioner without warning. The wifi only works in about 5 rooms. The rooms look great when compare them to a room at the King's Inn which look like someone may have set them on fire and even though I would never stay at the King's Inn again at least they didn't have any bug problems. There is a hotel right down the road that charges $185.50 per week and has laundry facilities and their price includes local and long distance phone and wifi and it's within sight of a grocery store.

name: Dollar Inn - Castleton
title: “Worth The Price”
text: We just happened to stay at Dollar Inn because we were about to go to our friends house, but we were kind of drowsy so we decided to stop and get some rest. We came in the front desk and the front desk was very nice and accommodating. We went into the room and we were surprised how the room looked for such a cheap price! Everything seemed to be nice! The next morning, we told the front clerk how nice the room was and she said that it was just newly renovated and repainted. It was a very good experience and I would recommend it for travelers.

name: Caribbean Cove Hotel & Conference Center
title: “Never again”
text: First of all we called in advance, after making our reservation online, to confirm that the credit card only needed to have open the amount for incidental. We were told by a young woman that if we were going to pay cash upon checkout then nothing would be charged. But to our surprise when we got there, the guy at the front desk, with the nasty attitude, tried to run the eintire amount for the 2 rooms. Of course, there wasnt that much available. So when i explained to him what we were told, he nonchalantly said, "oh sorry about that". We drove all the way from St. Louis for this type of treatment. So when we finally figured out how we were going to pay, we got our two room keys. In one of the rooms, the toilet did not work and had a chip on the toilet seat. That's an easy way to pass germs. So once we complained about the room, we got 2 more rooms to which the keys didnt work. So we are standing in the hall with all of our luggage, and 5 kids. He activates them again, supposedly, but they still dont work. We go down a total of 3 times and then they finally work. We finally make it to the pool. The slide is closed and the jacuzzi is not operating. Ok so the kids stay in the pool for awhile, then they were ready to go. Day 2, breakfast was ok but needs more variety. The pool that day day was much better but the water was very cloudy which made me nervous. The pools at home are busy but the water is never cloudy. After we left the pool, we needed new towels.....that we never received. I will never visit Carribean Cove again. It needs remodeling and a better management team. The service was poor. I wish we has went with our first mind and drove that extra four hours to Wisconsin Dells.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Hotel, Great location”
text: What can we say, this hotel, has it all. great service, upgraded upon arrival, given great room massive, with free breakfast, Location is ideal, on fisherman's wharf, ten mins walk to pier 39, see the sealions etc, the bakery, oh my god there is so much to do and see. Hire a bike from blazing saddles two doors away from hotel and cycle the path along to golden gate bridge, across the bridge and on to saulsalito. fantastic. do it!. Take the tram from outside hotel have clam chowder across the road, dance in the blues bars. Smell the seafood........... Thats just the wharf. Go to the baseball (if its the right time of year) We did not have a clue what was going on but hey, it was great fun. Union Square, where Tony Bennett left is heart! everything. AND if you get back to hotel by 5pm there is a free, yes free, wine reception and WII where you can interact with other guests, and drink wine by a log fire and to tell you the truth, its great.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “We have found a favourite!”
text:
Based on reviews on tripadvisor we booked the Argonaut for our recent stay in SF. I'm so glad we did! 
HOTEL
the hotel was very clean and nicely themed. The restaurant attached was very convenient for breakfast each day. The staff were some of the friendliest and helpful people I've come across. We came here after a few nights at the Bellagio in Vegas and the staff at the Argonaut ran rings around them (ie far better!)
LOCATION
could not be better. Right on the edge of the thick of things in Fishermans wharf. From our hotel room we looked over the GG Bridge, Cable Car turn-around, green parkland, beach & Ghirardelli Square. What could be better! Only an easy short walk to pier 39. I am a light sleeper and had no problem with noise whatsoever. 
CHILDREN
our 3yr old was travelling with us and he loved being able to choose a toy from the treasure chest each day. The staff were so lovely to him - he even got given a farewell present!
ADDED EXTRAS
* Free hot chocolate hour each day at 2.30pm by the fireplace
* Free wine hour each day at 5pm by the fireplace. 
* We met so many wonderful fellow travellers and swapped some great stories. 
The only con was that the room
was a bit small (but it is San Fran after all). 
We will definitely stay at the Argonaut on our next trip to San Francisco.

name: Americas Best Value Inn-Indy South
title: “Americas Best Value usually has nice hotels, but.....”
text: We are on the road a lot and usually pick ABI because they are generally nice. This one left much to be desired. The room had rotted floorboards in the bathroom and the bathroom/toilet had a "sour" not cleaned well smell. I didn't realize until we left that I was charged a little more than what I had been quoted when I phoned directly to the hotel for the reservation. I must saw that if good wifi internet is important to you, this location does have great internet.

name: Clarion Hotel & Conference Center
title: “Keep personal items safely with you.”
text: Beware of housekeeping. They ignore the do not disturb signs and enter your room. My room had personal items removed so "they could clean" even though we had late check out prearranged and a do not disturb sign on the door. I was so glad I had taken my laptop with me!! Hotel is not well maintained - smelly and dirty.

name: Caribbean Cove Hotel & Conference Center
title: “Great hotel and awesome service”
text: I am going to have to disagree with what most people are saying on here. We stayed here and we loved it! Our room fit us perfectly~ we had a small fridge, a couch that pulled out into a bed and the bathroom was HUGE! They came in and cleaned everyday. The only thing I thought needed to be changed was after the waterpark closed, I think everyone went into the inside pool....I thought for sure someone was going to get hurt there were so many in there. I did not allow my kids to go in. We even went back 2 weeks later and we are planning on staying there again in the next few months for a bowling tournament. And for whoever posted about how they had to close the pools due to poop being in the pool...ummm...that is a good thing. Unfortunately, you do not know when poop is going to leak out of a baby's diaper....so it is a good thing that they closed down the pool to clean it. I do think they need to update their mattresses to more comfortable ones....but other than that....we enjoyed our stay!

name: Sheraton Indianapolis City Centre Hotel
title: “Awesome stay at the Sheraton”
text: Long flight time from the West Coast. Lucy Devi, the night manager, greeted me and is just the best. Great personality, pretty eyes, very efficient and just made me feel relaxed that I was "home". The room was clean, comfortable and luxuriously appointed with a large flat screen and nice work desk. I was on a business trip. The Club lounge complimentary breakfast and evening wine and hors d'oeuvre was excellent. Very nice wait staff. They recommended Nicky Blaines, just down the street from the hotel. Go see Ben, Bartender of the year. He makes a killer Mojito, almost as good as I make. The Hotel is centrally located downtown so I had short trips to the offices I intended to visit. Got a ride back to the airport in a Town Car. Just a really nice and relaxing visit. Be sure to stay at this hotel and say hi to Luci. You'll love her.

name: Wyndham Indianapolis West
title: “Older hotel, but kept up nicely”
text: I was a bit nervous when I found out that my Priceline bid had placed me at this property, because the reviews were mixed. Some recent reviews were not that good. But to my suprise the motel was fine. Clean and comfortable. Yes, it is an older motel, but the rooms are updated and very clean. The bathroom could have used a bit more lighting, but it had new tile surfaces and the shower had plenty of power. We did not use any of the ammenities at the hotel, but you don't have to worry about your stay. Even with a packed hotel, it was quiet and comfortable.

name: Wyndham Indianapolis West
title: “I would not pay more than $50 for a room.”
text: We booked on Hotwire. The carpet was stained, the room smelled smoky, the size of the room and bathroom were quite small, the closet was missing a door, it is very noisy, the pool area wasn't very exciting but the pool itself was large. The food/drinks were expensive but what we had was pretty good. I liked the 24hour Starbucks but $2 for water was kind of ridiculous. They left us bottled water in the room the first night but never replaced it. The bed was too soft to do anything but sleep on and even that wasn't that great. The TV barely gets any channels and none of my favorites. We had trouble getting our door to open and our TV to turn on. No fridge, but all that granite? Geez. The wifi was very slow. I will never understand why "higher rated" hotels don't have a free continental breakfast. Someone kept stealing our "Do Not Disturb" sign and the maid bothered us every single morning except the last when I used our breakfast order card instead. And this may be dumb, but an employee in the coffee shop attempted to be humorous by telling us our card was declined. I just felt it was tacky. Housekeeping did do a good job in our rooms, however.

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “great hotel and location”
text:
Just got back from San Fran. with husband and two children. Omni staff was helpful and very nice. Our room although on the small size (but expected that w/ a hotel) was very
clean and the bathroom was spotless and large enough for our family. The location
suited us just fine..no big hills to deal with when grabbing a quick bite for breakfast and easy enough with the baby in stroller. The complimentary starbucks coffee in the morning was a plus. We were close to everything and it was easy to get everywhere..we toured the whole city (mostly by foot..we live in NYC so are used to walking!) Again, the staff was extremely helpful especially when we rented a car and they helped us lug our car seat and stroller to the car. We were very very happy with our stay at the Omni!

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Didn't wow me”
text:
Pros:
1) Great location in downtown Dallas
2) Comfortable bed; great pillows
Cons:
1) We had 3 people staying in our room. When I asked for an extra room key other than the one that was issued, the front desk clerk told me that they were all out of extra keys.
2) The elevators are incredibly slow.
3) The hotel room was tiny.
4) At the breakfast, there were breakfast potatoes and bacon but NO SCRAMBLED EGGS!!!!!
5) Dine-in room service took AN HOUR to come up.
6) Make sure you call ahead for your valet. Otherwise, you will wait a half hour for your car.
7) There is no pool at this hotel and the jacuzzi was out of order.
8) There was no HBO or premium movie channel.
Bottom-line, this is a great hotel to stay if you plan on just sleeping here. But if the hotel-experience is important to you, then look somewhere else.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Fabulous Hotel”
text: We recently visited San Francisco for the first time. That being said, we wanted to be near Fisherman's Wharf and found the Argonaut online. The service, location, rooms, wine hour, restaurant, bartenders, wine bar, cleanliness, etc. all derserve 5 stars. Any trip to San Francisco in my future will include a stay at the Argonaut.

name: Residence Inn Indianapolis Airport
title: “Best of the Best!!!”
text: We loved our stay at Residence Inn Airport. We stayed their for a month in May while my husband visited the IU hospital for chemo treatment. We didn’t know they had one and two bedrooms until after we were their. They switched us because it suited our needs better during the stay. It was so nice having the kitchen area in the room to fix meals. We had everything we needed. They came in each day and washed the dishes if I hadn’t done them first. My daughter thought it was so sweet that they made the bed and place her bears in special places around the room with one in the middle of the bed. We really liked the little store that they had onsite with ice cream and candy, chips and other goodies you might need. They were quick to fix anything that needed fixed. We loved the beautiful pool and hot tub. The hot tub stayed hot while you where in which was a wonderful change. We asked about restaurants the ones that they liked and we weren’t disappointed. A negative aspect was upon arrival with reservations in hand they tried to send us next door to the Fairfield Inn. That didn’t work so Fairfield sent us back. That was pretty unpleasant even though one of their people took care of the luggage. The other thing was that 4 days left at the end of our stay they had booked someone else in our room and they moved us back over to the Fairfield. This was not totally their fault because we didn’t give them the dates all at once. We did it in steps when we found out from the hospital what we needed to do. It was during the race time. The thing that I didn’t understand was that they moved us around when we had reservations why couldn’t they do the same to someone else? Overall I would go back. I would just make sure they had my dates right and then double check

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “Omni is very nice....”
text:
We spent 10 nights at the Omni in September and had a fantastic time. The hotel is convenietly located in the Financial district within walking distance of Union Square, Fishermans Warf etc. Our room on the 5th floor did not have a great view but was very quiet and well worth sacrificing the view for. The rooms are in excellent condition, and the maid service is first class. The staff are very helpul and courteous at all times, ensuring our stay went without a hitch. The only small complaint we have is that the one and only bar in the hotel (Bobs bar) is very small and gets very crowded from approx 5pm onwards, and getting a seat was almost impossible around those times. However it is no reason not to stay here. When we first arrived after our lengthy journey from Scotland, we were informed that our room (booked and paid for 8 months previousley) had been cancelled by Octopus travel who we had booked the room through. The hotel staff could not have been more helpful in rectifying the situation.
San Francisco is well worth a visit and has plenty to offer for all. We would recommend visiting Alcatraz and taking the coach tour of the city, however book your Alcatraz tickets online as far in advance as possible to ensure you get the dates you require. We also hired bikes from Blazing Saddles and rode over the Golden Gate bridge to Tiburon via Sausilto. This is a fantastic way to see the bridge and surrounding area (weather allowing). Sausilto is a must see when you are there and can be accessed by Ferry if you prefer not to bike it, dining is recommeded at Angelino's while you are there. We also took a wine tour to Napa valley etc and would recommend this trip, with plenty of samples included in the day ensuring the hoilday spirit was flowing. Union square is packed with all the usual big name shops, but visit the hippy district at upper Haight street for some of the funkiest shops available. We visited the zoo but found it to be dated and shabby with many of the animals not available to view. Of course you must take a ride on a tram while you are there, we would advise getting a day pass for 11 bucks, which allows you to hop on and off all day at your leisure. Finally Lombard St aka the most crookidest street in the world is worth a look with camera in hand.
We had 2 days of cloud followed by 8 days of glorious sunshine while we we there.
Book it up, you will enjoy!!!!

name: Days Inn Indianapolis Airport
title: “Close to Airport and Interstate,but with no sound!!”
text: Recently stayed in Indy to visit Zoo and Childrens Meusem and chose this motel because of close proximity to both.Very pleased with everything-from desk staff,housekeeping to the people who worked in the breakfast area/resturant downstairs.Didn't use the park-n-fly feature,so I can't comment on that.The pool was wonderful for a refreshing dip after a long day of sight seeing.We stayed on the top floor and loved both watching the sunrise and sunset from our window.

name: Radisson Hotel Indianapolis Airport
title: “We had a good stay here”
text: In town for the Indy Pace Car Reunion and stayed here. Have to agree with some other reviewers who said it is a bit hard to find...lots of road construction for sure but you can't fault the hotel for that as I'm sure it is frustrating for them too. Our room was clean. Was missing a few picky things...there was no luggage rack (but we called down for 1 and it was brought up right away), no TV channel guide (they have them at the front desk) and no information about the hotel. You know how you go to some hotels and there is a little binder on the desk with restaurant times, lounge times, maybe a room service menu...that would have been helpful to have. Little details that would have been nice but didn't make me hate it there. Staff were all very nice and extremely helpful and flexible. You do get some airport noise...planes fly overhead quite a bit...but it wasn't all that bad. We didn't notice much noise from the adjoining rooms...but had our AC on most of the time we were in the room which may have made a difference. Can't really complain about anything!

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Indianapolis Northwest
title: “Wish I could have rated it higher...”
text: Stayed here for business. When we first arrived...lots of construction going on outside the property. Check in was speedy & the front desk clerk was pleasant. Lobby was nice. I was put in an accessible room on the 2nd floor. So I had lots of space. Property is very clearly aged. Basic amenities in room. Shower was awesome...hot & great water pressure. It would have been nice to have lotion in the bathroom. Bed was ok. I liked that they had a microwave & fridge in the room. Flat screen TV with lots of channels. Nice selections for breakfast. Downfalls...older property, basic in room amenities, Internet moves at a snail's pace (that sucks when you're staying here for business), walls are thin (you can hear folks in adjoining rooms & all way). I love Marriotts...wish I could have rated this property higher.

name: Ramada Airport Indianapolis
title: “Great place to stay for early morning flight out of IND!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel on Wednesday November 5, 2008. We had a 6:38am flight from Indianapolis airport on November 6. We arrived after 9pm on Nov 5 and the desk clerk had our room ready when we arrived. He scheduled our hotel shuttle ride to the airport for the next morning and processed our parking fee for our car. 
This hotel lets you park your car there for $5/day and offers a shuttle ride to the airport with pick-up at the airport after your flight is complete. I received a business card with the phone number to call when we arrived back in Indianapolis. We called them when we got to baggage claim and the van was pulling up as we were walking out of the terminal. The morning shuttle to the airport was waiting on US! We left on schedule at the time we requested. Great job!
The hotel was very bright and clean and the rooms were comfortable and quiet. I wish we could have spent more time there! The hotel honored all of my requests I entered on their website during the booking of the room.
I would definitely stay here again!

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “Terrific Stay”
text: My family of six recently spent two wonderful nights at the Omni San Francisco. The Omni was our last stop on a two week long family vacation. We enjoyed our stay immensely. We loved the location as well as the terrific service we received at the Omni. At first I regretted my decision not to stay in the Fishermen's Wharf area but I came to find the Omni's location to be the perfect spot to explore the whole city. We walked as well as rode the cable cars (there is a stop right in front of the hotel) as well as the F Line street cars to get around. I highly recommend the Omni.

name: Indianapolis Days Inn & Suites Castleton
title: “decent size room, but the bathroom was gross!!”
text: We basically chose this motel for a cheap place to sleep. The room itself was a pleasant surprise, bigger than I anticipated for the price. The room (not the bathroom) was clean, beds were fairly comfortable, and the room was pretty quiet overall. The mini fridge had no temperature control, as the control knob was broken off. My biggest issue was with the cleanliness of the bathroom. IT wasn't awful, but there were hairs in the sink and I didn't get any feeling that the room had been sanitized. The breakfast was decent, although we were in a hurry and just grabbed something to go. Check-in was painfully slow, but the staff was friendly. Overall, I guess you get what you pay for!!

name: Crowne Plaza Indianapolis Downtown (Union Station)
title: “Attended Wedding There, Best Ever Service, Fantastic 5 Stars”
text:
We had a wedding in Indy this past weekend, reception hall was phenomenal, waiting staff was fantastic, our waiter worked our breakfast from 6am, through the entire reception, which ended at midnight, then he was back at our breakfast at 8am! When does that guy and his other workers sleep!? Recognized many other staff too. Rooms were great, service was great, place was spotless, yes, there is valet parking, and i did worry about putting one of those guys behind MY hooptie's wheel........tried to get them to upgrade upon return, but ended up with my same 'ol clunker.... I noticed the last person's comment, grumbling about the parking,.....It's right downtown, and parking is a huge issue in large cities.....even Indianapolis.....of course it's not free.... We had many rooms, and i heard of no complaints from anyone of our 200 + people group............. 
Their service to us will be remembered by all who were there, the reception hall was decorated perfectly, meals were fantastic, dance floor was great, sound system worked great, the bar staff was more then professional, and the martini fountain was superb. 
the only complaint I, or anyone in our group would/could make, was that the lights on the floor in the reception hall were hard to step around, several people at our table stumbled, but no one fell, going around them in the edges of the room. Definitely not anything to really worry about, but they probably do need to figure out a way to fix that issue maybe. Mount them into the floor maybe.... Other then that, it could not have been better in any way, shape, or form........... 
It rates 5 STARS FROM EVERYONE IN OUR GROUP, I'LL SEE TO IT THAT MORE PEOPLE POST COMMENTS!

name: Radisson Hotel Indianapolis Airport
title: “Great Service!!!!”
text: This Radisson was nicely located near the airport and offered shuttle service. I had come into town for a meeting and had alot of work to do. The desk area in the room, the free wireless and the helpfulness of the desk staff may my stay great. I accomplished everything that I needed to and had a nice space in which to work and relax. The next time i have chance to be in Indianapolis, this will be my hotel. Keep up the great job!!

name: University Place Conference Center & Hotel Indianapolis
title: “No major complants”
text: Stayed here one night while at a conference. Romm was comfortable and of decent size, good climate control system, would have liked a better variety on TV channels, Bathroom was small and dated. Check in was easy but I did have a reservation, check out also was quick and easy, conference facilities were nice and comfortable. Wouldn't hesistate to go here again for a conference, also its right across the street from major hospitals, but if in town for other reasons I'm sure other hotels would be closer for ball games concerts etc.

name: The Magnolia Hotel Dallas
title: “Loved the hotel. Truly a glamorous experience.”
text: Stayed in a suite and really enjoyed having the bed area separate. Because this was a business trip, I was able to have colleagues in my room and not feel "exposed." I also loved the art deco charm and the history of the building. The DART line was only two blocks away and the West End with its wonderful restaurants was only a stop away!

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Wonderful!”
text: My friends and I stayed several nights at the The Chancellor and thoroughly enjoyed the ambiance of an old hotel updated with modern conveniences in a PRIME location with helpful, friendly staff. THE BEDS ARE OUT OF THIS WORLD! The small restaurant was excellent, as well. Ask Mao for his special coke and coffee drink!

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “Best Hotel Ever!”
text:
We had a wonderful experience at this hotel. Extremely clean (even the hallways smelled clean). Large rooms, windows opened, extremely comfortable bed (most hotels are lumpy and over used), great selection of snacks and other amenities, mints, sleep balm, cards, anything you desire! Wonderful extra friendly staff, always available to help. Went as a surprise for my husband's 40th birthday and they sent up a complementary cake, champagne and birthday card. Great location, 1 block from China Town, Easy access to cable cars!
We will definately stay there again!!!

name: Comfort Inn & Suites West
title: “Comfort Inn is Comfortable!!!”
text:
I have beens staying here for work for the past month, I check in on Monday's and out on Friday's. So to date, I have been in 4 different rooms ranging from two queens, one king, and even a suite with a kitchenette and whirlpool bath. Every single room I have been in has been immacualate- upon arrival and when I get to the room at night. Housekeeping does a great job! They have a breakfast they serve every morning and it is good, they have fresh fruit, yougurt, homade waffles, scrambled eggs, various muffins and toast. Dry cereal and juices are available as well. The coffee is my morning savior! Every morning that I have been there, they have plenty of people in the breakfast area eating so for those previous reviews who said the food was terrible, it can't be too bad! Plus just for the record, it's not!
As far as guest services go, the staff has been nothing but extraordinarily nice and helpful. Again, not sure what happens with every customer, but at this Comfort Inn the staff is great! Alex, goes ABOVE and BEYOND to make the guests feel welcome and make sure they enjoy their stay. They are always avaiable if you need anything; extra pillows, blanket, or just a wake-up call. I have not gone swimming here, but from my room I can see the pool and exercise area and I see people swimming and working out! So again, I do not know what was happening when ChipAnnDale were there but the Pool looks very inviting to me!
So, overall this experience at Comfort Inn-West at Indianapolis has been a good one. I definately reccomend this hotel if you are in the Indy area and need to be close to the airport. I would stay here again in a minute and would not think twice about it!

Address: '1152 N White River Pkwy West Dr'
name: Candlewood Suites Indianapolis Dwtn Medical Dist
title: “Spacious place to stay, close to downtown Indy”
text: Stayed here for 4 nights while touring with my company. The rooms are the size of apartments with full kitchens and lots of closet space. Laundry facilities are free. There's a gym and small store by the front desk. The hotel is not too close to anything, so it would be more convinient to have a car. The shuttle is a good way to grab groceries at a local supermarket or go downtown. Overall a good hotel.

name: Comfort Inn & Suites West
title: “Great!”
text: I rely heavily on reviews to pick great hotels, so I thought important to add my own. We recently stayed at this hotel for "Park and Fly" purposes. The rooms were clean and comfortable. The shuttle service was OUTSTANDING. The pool was a relaxing way to spend the evening. It is not a fancy hotel by far, but for the price and the convenience of the shuttle service, and parking, it was great. I would recommend staying here if you need to fly.....

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Excellent would stay again”
text:
The hotel is beautiful, the rooms are decorated with a very nice natical theme. The location walking distance to everything.. The staff is wonderful, they are very friendly and go out of their way to do anything they can for you.. One of the hightlights of our stay at the Argonaut, was meeting their conciege GARRETT HIPPLE is was absolutely amazing!!!.
Garrett, planned all our tours with such excitement, he has a smile that lights up a room, and is very knowledgeable with the San Francisco area..Thank you GARRETT for making our so wonderful, keep up the good work, you are definately an asset to the Argonaut hotel... Will miss you!!!!!!!!

name: Comfort Inn & Suites West
title: “Fine experience”
text: I was nervous about the negative reviews but still wanted to give it a try as it met most of my criteria for the trip--inexpensive yet clean, safe, convenient location and a fun pool for my 3 and 6 year old boys. Overall it was a great experience for the price. Our room and all common areas (except pool/playground) were updated and clean. Pool and play areas are in need of remodeling but were still fun. Found the free breakfast convenient and also the microwave in lobby an easy way to "make dinner" we had bought at local grocery as opposed to going out. Staff was helpful.

name: Hyatt Place Indianapolis/Keystone
title: “Hyatt Place”
text: I stayed at the Hyatt Place for a girlfriends getaway a few months ago. It was very clean and the rooms are nice. I liked the feel of the room as there is two sections, one with a couch, sink, T.V. and desk and then the other with the bed. I would definitely stay here again.

name: Comfort Inn & Suites West
title: “Great place to unwind”
text: Dawnie and Kathy (at the desk) epitomized great service. The room (202) was clean, comfortable, and adequately spacious and appointed. The window opened (a big plus for smokers). The pool and overflow whirlpool (not a hot tub) were warm and clean, though the floor of each need resurfacing and fresh paint. The expanded continental breakfast, including scrambled eggs and hot waffle maker (but no meats), was a welcome change from the typical mini-donuts, etc. Though adjacent to I-74/465, road noise was absent (except when window was open). The room was equipped with a jacuzzi ("Jetta") tub for two. My only disappointment was the abscence of available premium or PPV channels on the 25" TV. My wife and I anticipate coming again for weekend escapes. PS: we read the reviews prior to our stay, and proceeded with some trepidation, using Choice Reward points; I'm very glad we did! PPS: Check out Godfathers Pizza.

name: Caribbean Cove Hotel & Conference Center
title: “No Hot Water to Shower after swimming”
text:
We swam most of the afternoon at Carribean Cove. We went to our room to shower,relax and have dinner. There was NO HOT water.
We were moved to three rooms with the promise of hot water. The water was FREEZING in all three rooms. Our family drove home that evening smelling of CHLORINE, hungry, tired and very disappointed.

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “Really pleased with our choice”
text:
Four girlfriends celebrating significant birthdays; booked 2 rooms. Hotel was able to accommodate our request for rooms side by side. Lots of space; windows that actually open! Comfy king-size bed; sofa, coffee table; mini fridge and micro-wave. Super soft housecoats and towels. Complimentary wi-fi allowed us to research our itinerary and restaurants.
Bathroom wasn't perfect; could certainly use an update i.e. toilet didn't flush quite properly and fixtures in shower were loose.
However, we were well pleased with the location: just one block from Union Square. 
Staff was excellent from the front desk to the porters to the bar to the concierge to housekeeping.
We really enjoyed our stay and will probably stay there next time!

name: BEST WESTERN Indianapolis South
title: “Very good stay. Clean and a great value.”
text: Very nice and clean. Location provides very easy and quick access to downtown. The bed in my room was as comfortable as at any hotel I have stayed in. Located within walking distance to several very good restaurants. Staff very nice and helpful.

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “Hotel stay part was great, marred by concierge and steakhouse”
text:
We were there the day after Thanksgiving. It had a nice upscale feel for a reasonable rate of about $160 for a regular room (Thanksgiving weekend). Perfect if you want something nice that is kid friendly. Our family had a room, and the other family we were traveling with had 2 rooms with connecting doors. Both of our families have children ages 5 to 11. We loved the pretty hotel, decked out for the holidays. We loved its proximity to Chinatown (5 mins walk), and around 10 min walk to Union Square. It was a block away from a Walgreens and McDonalds, which is convenient if you have kids. The children loved their Omni backpacks and the complimentary milk and cookies. The staff is nice and attentive, they clean the room 2x/day. Downside is the concierge. They gave wrong information on restaurants twice - once they gave the wrong address to a restaurant they recommended at the Fisherman's Wharf. Another time they assured (and refused to double check) that a restaurant will be open for Thanksgiving dinner. When we got there, the restaurant was closed. They also were not aware of a fun pack that the Omni loans to kids that contains games and activities and such.
For the restaurant in the hotel, Bob's Steakhouse... It was "ok". One thing a steak purist would frown on is that the steak comes to you with a humongous giant single carrot right in the middle of the plate as if it is the main dish. The steak and the potatoes are to its left and right. Also, the carrot was dripping in glaze that contaminated our steak. When we inquired about this, they said that it is a Bob's Steakhouse signature (putting the carrot in the middle), but you can always ask to put it on the side.

name: Staybridge Suites Indianapolis - Fishers
title: “nice place to stay”
text: Recently spent one night here with 3 friends. Had a great time. The room was clean, beds were comfy, and suite was large with seperate bedroom. Had a pretty interior courtyard. Enjoyed the indoor hot tub. Generous complimentary hot buffet breakfast with bacon, waffles, pancakes, fruit, cereal, yogurt, juice and even fountain sodas. Would recommend to anyone, especially families with young children who may want to nap during the day, in that the seperate bedroom makes it nice to be able to put them in there and shut the door.

name: Comfort Inn & Suites West
title: “Had a wonderful time staying here.”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights to meet up with some family for a weekend and it was great. The pool and indoor play area was a really nice thing so we adults didn't have to sit in the hot sun for the time the kids played. Only thing I think they could improve on is getting some more choices of tv channels. Rooms were very clean and the staff was very friendly and helpfull.

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “Omni is heaven”
text: The Omni was great! The room was clean, comfortable and the service at the hotel was second to none. We loved the coffee/juice and paper deliverey to the room each morning. The evening turn down service was perfect at the end of a long day! I very much recommend the Omni and we will definitely stay there again.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Very very good hotel”
text:
This hotel is in a great location and is within walking distance to the underground MUNI/BART station and the cable car stop for Powell/Hyde and Powell/Mason is right in front of the hotel. The hotel staff is very friendly (especially the concierge), the hotel itself is clean, and the rooms are spacious enough with large closets and a manageable bathroom.
Shopping and dining options are plentiful in the Union Square area.
There is a pharmacy/grocery mart half a block away.
The hotel's restaurant Luques serves very good breakfast at reasonable prices. (they also serve lunch and dinner, but we only had breakfast there).
Overall I very highly recommend this hotel to anyone who is staying in San Francisco. We felt very safe, very comfortable, and very satisfied! We will stay here again!

name: Country Inn & Suites Indianapolis Airport South
title: “Moto GP weekend”
text:
I originally intended to stay downtown for MotoGP weekend, but opted for the County Inn Airport South to save money. It was an excellent decision. You don't have to fight the traffic of downtown Indy during a very congested weekend--AND you don't have to pay 20 dollars a day for parking. 
The other posters are correct--the hotel is brand new and 1/2 of the rooms face the highway. Ours happened to face the highway and the noise was not enough to keep any of us up at night. In fact, we slept very well! The front desk staff was attentive and when we arrived at 3am they helped us check in quickly and said they would not have the maid disturb us the next morning.
The drive to the track was short due to the close proximity to the freeway; breakfast was free and had quite a few options for a continental style set-up. The cookies were awesome!
Another cool thing--there was a policeman in the parking lot at all times over the weekend. Not sure if this is standard or if it was due to the large amount of motorcycles in the lot--but it was much appreciated. 
Overall, a nice stay. If I go back next year, I plan on staying again.

name: Country Inn & Suites Indianapolis Airport South
title: “Nice place to stay at a reasonable price.”
text:
My family and I were driving back home from vacation and needed a place to stay for the night. Having had good luck with the Country Inn & Suites chain in the past, I made a reservation from the road. We were very pleased by the clean, new feel of the hotel. Everything was very nice, and it felt more upscale than the price would have indicated. The complimentary breakfast was better than most, and the staff was courteous and helpful. 
There were only two negative factors, and they were both minor: 1) the common areas on the upper floor (elevator and hallway) were very warm - probably a good 10-15 degrees warmer than inside our room. 2) They could use better signage to help the traveler to the hotel. The hotel is set back from the road and behind other buildings, and the only sign we saw was very small and not well located. I had to call the hotel and ask for directions, and as it turns out I had driven right past it.
I would recommend this hotel and this chain to any traveler without hesitation.

name: Super 8 - 183 Airport
title: “Awesome hotel for kids & family”
text:
we followed the advice of other travelers on Trip Advisor and stayed for 2 nights on family vacation. While we had an itinerary packed full of things to do, you could completely just hang out at the hotel for vacation. They have a great pool in summer with a really nice kiddie area. They have a Wii and Playstation for free--open access for guests, a DVD player in the room (also great for entertaining little ones), a massage chair, snacks in the evening & great hot breakfast, complete with state of Texas-shaped waffles, & even some protein (hard boiled eggs & bacon). They have a fitness room & a pillow selection list on check-in with about 20 different types of pillows to choose from for sleeping--GREAT, and such a reasonable price. Very neat & clean. They have a washer/dryer which we made use of after being on vacation in various places for a week & were in need of some clean clothes. The latte-making coffee machine was great. It was well-used by everyone there at breakfast & was a little slow (makes 1 cup at a time) but that is my only very minor complaint about the whole place. Very helpful staff.
We are staying there again in October for a business trip & bringing my family, I know they'll have plenty to do to occupy them while I work.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Beautiful Hotel in an excellent location. Loved it!”
text: The Argonaut is a wonderful hotel. It's situated in a perfect position by the waterfront just a short walk away from Pier 39 the main tourist shopping and entertainment area. It is also just beside the Hyde Street cable car depot so you can hop on a tram and go any where you want. It is also not far from Pier 7 I think it is for the Alcatraz Tours. The hotel is very quiet and relaxed. It feels very intimate and welcoming. It is family and pet friendly. The hotel has a maritime theme and is beautifully decorated. The rooms are adequately sized with honour bar, fridge, safe, good sized bed and bathroom and air con. The only problem we had with them was a with our luggage. One of our connecting flights to the US was delayed which ended up with us going to San Francisco and our luggage following on a later flight. We were worried we would never see our luggage again and asked over and over again if our bags had been delivered to the hotel for over 24 hours. Always being told no. We eventually made enquiries with the airline who told us that hey had delivered our luggage to the hotel only a few hours after we had arrived but the hotel staff had at no time checked their closet for our bags. They did at least not charge us for our calls to the airline and our call home to speak with family. I loved my stay in S.F. and would returnn to this hotel in a heart beat. They also have a computer terminal at the front desk that any one can use to access internet for free and you can print anything off using their printers again for free.

name: Comfort Suites Indianapolis Airport
title: “Clean, new hotel along 465, no hot water”
text:
We were visiting Bloomington on homecoming weekend so we decided to stay along 465 so we could get up the next morning and get there before the football traffic. The hotel was a little hard to find, it's in an industrial park and there are no signs or at least none I could see in the dark. If you bring along the hotel's directions or mapquest then you should be able to get to it.
The hotel looks to be new, everything is clean and very well maintained. We got a handicapped accessible room although we didn't need it, the room was enormous, 15-20 people could have easily slept in that room. I had hoped to get two separate sleeping areas for the three of us but we got two queen beds in the same room and a sleeper sofa. The partition mentioned on the website didn't separate anything from anything and even if the beds had been on either side of the partition it wouldn't have been large enough to give you privacy.
My major complaint is a temporary one, hopefully, we had almost no hot water in the shower, by the time the 3rd person got in there it was ice cold. And the water pressure was so low that it took forever to get the shampoo out of my hair. We mentioned it on the way out and the desk clerk said something to the effect that they knew about it and they were sorry.
Breakfast was complimentary which is always nice for families, there was eggs, sausage, make your own waffles, bagels, muffins, fruit, cereal, yogurt, tea, coffee, juice.
I'm giving the hotel a higher rating than my personal experience would indicate because the hot water problem seems to be temporary and the hotel actually seemed to be quite nice. It was not good for us because of the privacy issue, most families probably don't care if the beds are in the same room. The location is fine as long as you are using it for the airport (park and fly) or a place to stay when Bloomington is overbooked. Not close to Indy itself.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Hotel - Perfect Location”
text:
We absolutely loved staying the the Argonaut Hotel, it's right on fishermans wharf and walking distance to everywhere that side of town. 
The cable car is in the park right next door and all the tourist busses leave from the street the other side. The hotel staff were really friendly and allowed us to print our Alcatraz booking confirmation that we'd forgot to bring. 
The wifi in the rooms was free if you sign up to their newsletter which was very useful for my iPhone and checking the exchange rate!
When we come back to San Fran we will definately be staying here again.

name: Candlewood Suites Indianapolis Northwest
title: “Guests of the Day”
text: We usually travel quite far on our first day out on a trip. Having to work later before we could get going, my husband and I decided to use some Priority Points and get as far as Indianapolis for the night. Arriving just before 10 p.m., we were heartily greeted by the young man at the front desk and handed our keys to a first floor room. As Priority members, he made sure that we picked out our 'perks' before heading to the room. In a lovely room, we were delighted to find a bag on the desk designating us as "Guests of the Day" with water and more treats in the bag. The room was large, the kitchen very nice and a great place to put the snacks we had with us for the trip. Enjoyed coffee the next morning. We will definitely stay here again if we are looking for a place to stay in the Indianapolis area.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Indianapolis East
title: “Accomodating Staff”
text: We had a nice stay at the hotel. The breakfast was good and the room was clean. Overall the hotel was comfortable. I especially appreciated the front desk staff accomodating our late check out request due to delays in our sporting events due to excessive heat in the area. Having a comfortable check out made our trip going home much easier and less stressfull (especially since we had a 6 hour drive).

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “Not bad at all”
text: I spent 8 nights at the Omni when attending a conference in San Francisco. The hotel's location is fantastic, bang in the middle of town without some of the grime associated with Union Square. The public areas and reception are clean and smart. The room was comfortable and quiet (courtyard rooms are quiet but with a view of the neighbouring office block), but very plain - nothing in there to denote it as special in any way. The service, however, was very good indeed - bright and attentive staff at every level from housekeeping to management. Room service food was fantastic, although for the most part I got take-aways from neighbouring Chinatown. I'll certainly use the Omni again.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Great place to stay - location is the best”
text:
We stayed as a family of 4 with 2 teenagers in rooms with an interconnecting door on the 12th floor facing the front. It wasn't too noisy with the windows closed.
Everything has already been said in previous reviews - clean, helpful staff, good breakfast, so not much to add.
We liked the free never ending coffee from the lobby, free WIFI, brilliant location and trying out the pillows.
There was nothing we did not like in fact. We had breakfast on day one there and it was fine - friendly service, good food. We liked it.
I have often seen questions in the forum about whether to stay near Union Square or Fishermans Wharf and having stayed at the Chancellor, Union Square would win hands down. There is so much to do and the Chancellor is just in the best place for it. You can't beat the location.

name: University Place Conference Center & Hotel Indianapolis
title: “Great Hotel”
text:
Great Hotel, beatiful rooms. The front staff was also very friendly and accomodating on a slight issue we had.
Just know that the hotel is not "right downtown" and you'll have no surprises. The shuttle service is convenient, or you can just walk downtown in about 5 - 10 minutes. The hotel is also close to the river walkway and parks.
Highly recommend.

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “very good deal”
text: a large studio; no extra charge for more than 2 people; 4 family members had plenty of room. very reasonable parking fee for san francisco. a good find.

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “Enjoyed it”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for 4 nights at the end of August, as part of our honeymoon. Hotel is situated in downtown San Francisco and right next to one of the cable car lines, within walking distance of Union Square and the bay.
We had a good clean top floor room. The hotel itself is very stylish and the staff were good. The only thing that let it down was the poor bar and restaurant, however there are plenty of other excellent places to eat and drink within walking distance of the hotel (North Beach is great).
I would definitely recommend this hotel. San Francisco is one of the most stunning and atmospheric cities I have been too and you must get there at least once in your life. Staying at the Omni will enhance your experience.

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “By far our favorite place to stay in San Francisco and we have been visiting the city for over 20 years.”
text: We have stayed at the Donatello four times in as many years and will return again as often as possible. The rooms are very European in the sense that they have all the amenities for a week long stay including small kitchen area with place settings for two and wireless internet connection. The bedding and lighting and decoration is superior to that found in most hotels. The staff is available at any time of the day or night. We never waited more than a few minutes for the elevator. We think the location is one of the best in the city because it is accessible to all modes of public transportation if one chooses not to walk which is our favorite way to visit sights and restaurants and cultural venues. I have recommended the Donatello to all our friends who plan to visit San Francisco.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Austin
title: “A nice hotel- but not up to Four Seasons Standards”
text:
We checked into this hotel this afternoon and I have to say that I am greatly underwhelmed. From the outside the hotel looks like a typical 1980's era big chain hotel. Inside, it is nice, fairly modern and clean, but certainly far from impressive. The room is also clean and fresh, but very small, and feels more like a Marriott than a four seasons. The bathroom is quite small, and overall functionality of the room is so/so.
Nothing wrong with the four seasons Austin, however it is far from what you would expect if you had ever stayed at a four seasons before. Definitely over priced and over hyped. I have stayed at over 30 different four seasons and this one is by far the least luxurious.

name: Canterbury Hotel
title: “Canterbury Saved My Life!”
text:
As a traveling musician I have to stay in various hotels across country from New York to Colorado and back, always trying to make myself at home. Before staying at the Canterbury I was having many terrible nights sleep at other hotels we won't mention. My sleep was affecting my tour tremendously. 
Staying in the Canterbury not only was the best sleep on my tour so far... it changed my perspective putting me in a better mindset. I felt like I was Macaulay Culkin in Home Alone 2 and Brendon at the door treated my Nissan Versa like it was a Rolls Royce!
Thanks Canterbury you made me feel like first class citizen!
Sincerely,
Jim Wolf 
New York, NY

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Super Clean!!”
text:
The Chancellor Hotel was surprisingly friendly and efficient, and best was that the room was super clean! Something I really appreciate. The room I was in has been recently updated with nice furnishings and flat screen TV, and, something that made my day is that there were plugs in the bathroom so you could have a bath, unlike many hotels.
In addition, the hotel has a service where you can use or buy 'specialist' pillows (I guess is the right term) that include a pillow for the bath, should you be so inclined, or eye pillows for relaxation. There are a few fees associated with some of these, but it's a great idea!
It has free high speed internet which worked perfectly.
Only thing missing - tea and coffee in the room.

name: Embassy Suites Indianapolis - Downtown
title: “Great time at the Embassy”
text:
We stayed at this resort on a three day field trip. It was a great experience of Indianapolis. The resort was right downtown, which gave us a breath taking view.
 The bright atrium welcomed us to the resort. The staff was very helpful.
 The suite we stayed in was awesome! It had a living room and a bedroom. The bedroom had two queen beds and a dresser. The room also had a nice t.v. and table. The living room had a t.v. with a key board connection. It had a couch that pulled out to a bed. Also it had a mini fridge and a microwave.
 The bathroom was nice and clean with a double sink and shower/tub.
 The breakfast is great and was the cleanest buffet I have ever ate at. It had a great variety of eggs, pancakes, waffles; danish, and cereal. It also had great coffee.
 The location was just great! walking distance to monument circle, the capitol, shops and famous resturants. Also for the shoppers, there is a mall attached to Embassy suites!
 I recemend this resort to anyone. Hope you choose here, because I want you to have the same amount of fun we had.

name: Holiday Inn Indianapolis North/Carmel
title: “See Kyle at the bar”
text: Great service, clean room. Make sure you stop by the bar and see KyLe.The place was easy to find and in a good location. I ate at the bar three nights and the food was top notch. Kyle made the experice great.

name: Sheraton Indianapolis Hotel at Keystone Crossing
title: “Mostly good!”
text: My Wife and I stayed here for a weekend away. It is a very noisy and crowed hotel. It is very nice though. There was a junior tennis tournament going on in Indy and because of it there were kids everywhere. They were laying on the floor in the lobby watching tv and running all over the place. Bad timing. We had one issue getting our room cleaned the first day and had to come back several times while the maids kept saying 20 minutes. We will be traveling alot to Indy over the next 4 years because of a daughter in college and am not sure if we will pick this particular Sheraton again.

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “Great Hotel”
text: The Donatello is in the heart of downtown san francisco, great location, the rooms are large,clean and modern . We enjoyed our stay . The staff are friendly and courteous. Close to everything including Union Square, cable car, great restaurant and bars

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Wonderful staff at the Chancellor”
text:
Stayed here in September, and really enjoyed the hotel. It was centrally located in Union Square, lots to see and do close by. Easy access to Cable cars and buses. The hotel is very clean and comfortable. There is no air conditioning, but it wasn't a problem. The restaurant (Luques) serves lunch and breakfast, and it was good. The hotel supplies free coffee/tea and cookies at the lobby. There are also apples available.
I have already recommended the hotel to friends who will be visiting San Francisco, and I would definitely stay here when I return.

name: La Quinta Inn Indianapolis Airport Lynhurst
title: “Very thin walls”
text:
The staff of this hotel is excellent, very friendly and very helpful. The rooms are clean and well maintained. The breakfast is just average.
BUT I wouldn't recommend this hotel because the walls are paper thin. I am a very sound sleeper....so it surprised me how often I was awakened. Someone drove outside my window and I could hear the gravel moving!! I could hear two guys talking in the hallway...and they were just having a normal conversation. I just thought maybe because they were just outside my door, but when they went into their room ACROSS the hall and CLOSED the door, I could STILL hear them talking!!! Thank goodness, they went straight to bed. In the morning, I didn't have to wake up to my alarm, the jets taking off in the morning were loud enough.
Another thing I didn't like is that there is no computer for guest use. I travel alot and every hotel I have stayed in has a business center....even if that means just one computer in the lobby. So no printing boarding passes in advance or checking your flight. Just one of those courtesy things that most hotels do now.
And then my pet peeve. Housekeeping knocks on your door before check out time. Why can't they check with the front desk to see if someone has checked out. Because of the paper thin walls, I had to listen to them knock on doors and yell "housekeeping" all the way down the hall.

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “Excellent stay at the Omni!”
text:
What a great hotel! I booked this hotel for one night using Priceline. I asked for a four star hotel for 75.00, and it was confirmed within minutes! The hotel website shows their rack rate rooms at 245.00 a night. Beautiful room, with bathrobes in the closet, Huge bathroom and the most heavenly beds! 
I would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting a luxury room at a very low price!!!

name: Hyatt Regency Indianapolis
title: “Great Location, Average Hotel”
text: We were in Indianapolis to attend a Colts game, so we could not have asked for a better location - the Hyatt is just 2 blocks from Lucas Oil Stadium and the Colts Grill is just across the street. I liked the modern room design and decor. I didn't like the HVAC system at all. Although we set the thermostat to 65 degrees (as low as we could), the room stayed at 70 degrees and above (even when the outside temp was in the 30s) and never stopped running. Very loud blowing air. We like to sleep in a cool room. We couldn't open a window to get any cool air either. The thermostat doesn't tell you the room temperature, just what it is set to. We tried turning it off, but the room got very stuffy. The valet service was very good, although a little pricey at $30 per night. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The Hyatt shares a huge building with PNC, so the actual entrance to the hotel is hard to find. This part is under construction so maybe they are making it easier for guests to figure out. We will probably try a different hotel when we visit Indy again.

name: Canterbury Hotel
title: “Second time just as bad a first”
text: After our first visit a few years ago when everytime I used the hair dryer or curling iron we blew a fuse I swore I wouldn't go back. But we heard the new owner was putting some money into it we thought we would give it a try. Worst idea ever. First room we were in was 86 degrees. After having air on 3 hours only went to 78. They came and looked at it. By the time we got back from dinner 4 more hours it was only 77. So 9:30 they moved us to a smaller room that was 76 degrees. 11:00 called them up AGAIN. Looked at it and said ok is that better. If my husband wasn't feeling sick and asleep I would have left then. So the entire night it never got lower that 75 degrees. If I had paid $40 for a roach motel I might have expected no AC But when I spend $200 I would hope AC works. And if they put any money into the hotel I did not see it in either of the 2 room we were in. And the hallways were even hotter.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Loved it!”
text: I stayed here a year ago (meant to write a review sooner) because this family-owned hotel really deserves it. It is in a great location near Union Square - just up the hill from the cable cars that start from Market Street and walking distance to Nob Hill. I was travelling solo and felt very safe here indeed. Nice room and bathroom and a great breakfast room (yummy blueberry pancakes!). The hotel also provides free tea and coffee in the lobby. Reasonable rates and very helpful staff. Would definitely stay here again.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Brilliant”
text: We stayed at the Chancellor on the first 3 nights of our honeymoon (an explore of California and beyond). It was such a great find, brilliantly located right in the heart of the city with the street car stopping right outside. Really friendly staff, in particular the bar staff who were full of top tips about where to head on our travels. Can't fault this hotel for location, cleanliness and friendliness.

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “Loved It!!”
text: This is simply one of the best City hotels we have ever stayed at. The location was superb right in the heart of the financial district and within walking distance of everything. The staff were courteous and friendly and the free internet access was a nice touch and always accessible. It was all the nice touches that made you want to stay night after night including the turndown service,mints and lovely bathroom products. This was our first stop as part of a west coast tour and it started off our vacation. We WILL definitely be staying here again.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Austin
title: “Wonderful!”
text: From the location on Lady Bird Lake to the attentive staff to the super comfortable bed, this is hands down the best hotel in Austin. You'll never want to leave. Extremely accommodating and relaxing.

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “Great start to our Honeymoon”
text:
We stayed at the Omni as the first part of our Honeymoon. We then went to Seattle and then Vancouver.
The overall experience was a pleasure with the Omni. We saw the good reviews on this site and email the hotel for room rates. With a short while we had an email back and we replied to confirm we wanted a room. We asked the guy to call us in the UK for our card details and within another half hour we had a call from a lovely guy called Matt. He took our details and we had some chat. He then emailed me a confirmation of booking and sent me some details on how to get from the airport to the Hotel.
The reception was great. All the staff wished us their congratulations on our marriage and they even gave us a bottle of sparkling wine and their was a hand written card as well. The room was a good size and the bed was comfortable. Their was a gym we didn't use.
Location is great as well in the financial part of the city, just a few minutes walk from downtown. The Trolleys go past the front door as well.
Thanks again to all the staff, we will seek out another Omni if we are in the US or Canada.

name: La Quinta Inn Indianapolis Airport Executive Drive
title: “Bom hotel, mas precisa melhorar o atendimento”
text:
Bom hotel, com boa localização. Fica relativamente perto do centro (para quem está de carro).
Um pouco mais antigo que a média dos La Quinta, mas ainda um bom hotel!
O serviço de quarto deixa a desejar. Uma das vezes o serviço de quarto simplesmente não foi feito, e em outra foi feito parcialmente. Em favor do hotel, esclareço que saí darde do quarto, mas ainda pela manhã, de forma que fiquei insatisfeito com o serviço.

name: Holiday Inn Express Indianapolis Downtown City Centre
title: “Nice stay in a jacuzzi room”
text:
We arrived late by train and were given a jacuzzi room - nice! We didn't expect this, but it made the stay even nicer.
Bedding was comfortable. Location right across from Lucas Oil Stadium and 5 minutes walk from the train station was perfect. A shuttle to the airport is a block away. There was an additional fee to park in their lot, but we didn't have a car, so it was not an issue with us.
Breakfast at holiday inn expresses are really nice, with quite a nice spread of hot and cold dishes. 
I recommend this hotel to others.

name: Baymont Inn & Suites Indianapolis South
title: “Great service, good facilities”
text: I just spent last week at a local woodworking school. The Jameson was close to the school, local shops and loads of restaurants. The service was great and I especially was grateful to see laundry facilities in the hotel.

name: Baymont Inn & Suites Indianapolis South
title: “" Great Coustmer Service "”
text:
I have been saying in a Jameson Inn since Nov. 2, 2010 from Little Rock Ark. South Bend Ind. and the last month and a half at Jameson, Indy South. I own a Construction Company and have stayed in a lot of hotels and if I am in a city that has a Jameson Inn and Suites that is where I'll be. When I read the bad review that was posted on Feb. 8, I had to respond. Everyone that works at Indy South have been very nice to me and all my employee's, they all are professional and helpful, from from desk to maintiance staff. 
 So when reading the review that called out MISTY... I am the contruction worker staying at the hotel!!!! MISTY Shushed you for a reason YOU WERE LOUD... Remember you are a guest at the hotel. You don't own it.. There are other people staying and trying to sleep. . Kuddo's to entire staff for doing a great job.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Indianapolis Downtown
title: “Great value! Clean and nice free breakfast”
text: We always stay here. For the price and the value you can't find better. Great breakfast! Rooms always clean!!!

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “You will not be disappointed when you select the Donatello Hotel in San Francisco.”
text:
I have a time share at the Donatello but I have also used the hotel if rooms come available when there is nothing available with my time share. 
The bar is a hot spot and they have happy hour every night. The bar tenders are gracious and knowledgable. Not a large bar but comfortable. They often have live music. Every person connected with my stay go out of their way to make you feel wanted and at home. The bell staff give you the impression that it is not just a job but a profession! One of my favorites has been employed there for 17 years. The location is excellent--a block from the Geary and Curran Theatres--a block from Union Square which is surrounded by many major shopping venues. It has been awhile since I have dined at the restaurant but I hear the food is great. On Friday nights there is a wine tasting reception with an array of goodies. The rooms are clean and sparkle. The ammenities are exceptional. It also has a fully equiped exercise area and a spa. The only negative is that the parking is not included. It's my home in the City.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Fantastic place to stay in SF”
text:
Stayed Nov 9, 2008 in room 35#. 
Positive:
- Valets are super friendly. They have to handle people coming in on a very busy street with no parking, yet took care of us with out issue when checking in, unloading car, ect. 
- Location. Perfect for tourists to SF. Pier 39, Giardelli Square, and many major starting points for sightseeing in SF are less than 5 min walk. Tons of good eats nearby also. 
- Suprisingly quiet, considering location. 
- Good quality rooms.
- Free Wifi. 
Negative
- $40 p/day to park. I guess thats what it takes to park in downtown SF, but still, Ouch. 
Overall, really a great place, at a great price ($169 p/night). Highly recommend to SF bound tourists.

name: Baymont Inn & Suites Indianapolis South
title: “The Continental Breakfast Was Good”
text:
The rooms were average. We stayed in a room with two queen beds. The room came with a fridge and microwave. We had a late check-in and I booked this room through Priceline.com. An hour before arriving, I called to inform them of a late check-in and to see if we could get a non-smoking room with two beds. He said that usually room preferences weren't guaranteed because it was a priceline purchase but since they had some available, he would accomodate us. I thought that was a bit excessive and blatantly put. Meeting the clerk in person, he was nice and helpful. 
The continental breakfast was good. Lots to choose from-waffles, muffins, oatmeal, cereal.
There are lots of restaurants around the area. It's an easy on-off to Hwy 65.

name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
title: “Centrale, elegante e comodo”
text:
L' Omni è un hotel elegante nel Financial District di San Francisco, che in sé non ha grandissime attrazioni, ma è la base più comoda per raggiungerle tutte.
La hall è inusualmente ampia e alta, con tanto personale pronto ad assistervi. Le camere sono grandi, tenuto conto che qui lo spazio dev' essere assai caro se tutti i palazzi si sono sviluppati in altezza già decenni fa. L' isolamento acustico è ottimo, non si sentono proprio nemmeno gli sferraglianti cable car. Grandi i letti, bagno elegante e di stile tradizionale come la stanza. Wi-Fi gratis se aderite al loro programma di fidelizzazione.
Il risultato è stato un soggiorno molto confortevole, elegante e senza pecche. Provata anche la loro steak house, Bob's Steak & Chop House, dove la carne era ottima e i prezzi molto buoni.
Ci hanno proposto la loro limousine per tornare all' aeroporto, che è costata credo solo 5 dollari più del taxi scalcagnato con cui eravamo arrivati, memorabile per la gentile battuta con cui ci aveva accolti il taxista asiatico: "Italian? Mafia!".

name: Drury Inn Indianapolis
title: “Great hotel”
text: What a great hotel! The staff is extremely friendly and helpful. Seemed they couldn't do enough for us Breakfast had everything we needed. Evening happy hour and late popcorn an added bonus. The rooms are clean and roomy. I will return if in the area again.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Great service and charm!”
text: We were met by Rory upon checking into the Chancellor. He and everyone else were just what we expected - friendly, efficient, and attentive! We parked around the corner and by the time we walked back our room was ready. We were surprised with gifts in our room from the staff celebrating our anniversary - champagne, glasses, chocolates, and a gift wrapped picture frame from the Chancellor! We were also pleased with the size of our room (especially in the city), a small view of Union Square, the very comfortable king sized bed, and cleanliness! They offer 12 different types of pillows (yes, 12!) and almost as many different in-room ways to relax (foot baths, massaging chairs, etc....). The rooms were quiet even though there were lots of people there. The small bar downstairs was perfect for a night cap at the end of a long day. All of our questions were answered with more than just a simple answer. Highlighted maps, personal knowledge and suggestions were given and appreciated. The hotel has old-school charm and the staff more than make up for any amenities that the newer hotels would have. Centrally located with the cable car pick up across the street or a safe, 30-minute walk to the Wharf. We would highly recommend this hotel to everyone!

name: Hyatt Regency Indianapolis
title: “Great stay!”
text: With the reviews on here I was a little nervous about our stay here. But, we found the Hyatt to be a great location, our room was spacious and clean. The bed was VERY comfortable and we loved our view of downtown. The TV was a great size and we thought it had a lot of channels. The shower was hot and had plenty of pressure. We truly couldn't find anything to be negative about(except the cost of parking). We will be back! Thanks Hyatt and Indy for a great birthday! :)

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Nice location but some problems”
text: Nice place for a first stay in San Francisco. Near the Pier 39, the cable cars, the Alcatraz Cruises ... We liked this hotel but when we return to San Franscico, we will choose another one. Very bad Internet Access. Due to the price per night the internet access must be included and this is not the case!!! No WIFI access!!! Our room was not cleaned when we came back at 2pm, intolerable!

name: Hilton Garden Inn Indianapolis South/Greenwood
title: “Beautiful, but...Pillows Were Like Sacks of Cement”
text:
The wife and I did an overnighter here attending a family function off-site. The room was beautiful, relatively new and scratch-free. A relative stayed here at the same time and except for a king vs. twin beds, the rooms were identical. Everything worked. I liked the well-organized hutch containing the coffee brewer. micro and fridge.
