The king-sized bed, albeit a set-your-own-firmness mattress came with a multitude of smaller, square-shaped pillows, each one less comfortable than the last one. I refer to them as "cement sacks."
Neither of us got a good night's sleep account of the pillows.
The next morning a bunch of us ate breakfast together in their grill. There was a choice of the buffet or order from the menu. I checked out the buffet and saw several items were out or low and I advised the cook staff who's body language told me my advice was not appreciated. They did replenish those items quickly to their credit. The food was just OK, not bad but nothing special. I enjoy biscuits and gravy when traveling and was slightly disappointed in the gravy that was pretty bland tasting.
Our waitress to her credit was very obliging and informative.
I would stay there again in the future and call housekeeping for softer pillows if necessary.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Indianapolis South/Greenwood
title: “Very nice accomodations but . . . . . . . . .”
text:
Requested extra pillows (4) three times and received one 7-1/2 hours later.
Couldn't hear TV or sleep due to noisy heater.

name: TownePlace Suites Indianapolis Keystone
title: “Great setting and view”
text: it was a romantic weekend getaway and i was so surprised on my entrence of the Hotels beautiful surroundings and hospitality by the staff so nice and pleasent , It couldn't have been scripted more better then to fine out we were the VIP for the day ! WOW not one bad thing happened perfect is all i can say ! Thank Very Much

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “Our special place”
text: Five years ago we spent our honeymoon at the Donatello and fell in love with it. Since we live in Sacramento, we use it for our get away place to the city. We've found our favorite restaurants within walking distance. The staff is always pleasant. The lounge on the top floor is always a comfortable spot to go. After a nite at the theatre or Giants game we love to go to the 2nd floor lounge for a drink and some pleasant live music.

name: Courtyard Indianapolis Downtown
title: “Nicest,and most helpful staff”
text: Stayed labor day weekend with some friends, had a great time. The staff were helpful in every aspect from giving us directions to broad ripple, honest restaurant reviews, and helping us get a free night during our stay

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “Perfect Place to stay in San Fran”
text:
Very large clean and modern rooms. Great value in superb central location. You're only a short hop from union sq and all the shopping etc. You're also very close to the trolleys that head up to the wharf.
The breakfast is not really worth bothering with but there are some great places near by.
We will return

name: Residence Inn Indianapolis Downtown on the Canal
title: “Comfortable hotel”
text:
I will define the stay at "Homely" since it is a non-formal hotel with basic services in place. The rooms are spacious with full kitchen. 
What makes this hotel my favourite is the location. This is situated along side the river. On a sunny day, people having jog, families with cycle-rickshaws and pedal boats, with ducks floating in the water make it a very soothing and lively scence
Flip side - not all the staff memebers of the hotel are cooperative and sensitive theier patrons but good part is you have a very good ear in the form of its General Manager (Vicki) and she is all there to help whatever best way can be done
Proximity to the downtown shopping area, Lucas stadium, Childern's museum and the Zoo (in fact we walked to the zoo from the hotel, along the canal) makes it better to stay

name: Drury Inn Indianapolis
title: “Nice folks!”
text:
I was staying at the very plush Drury Inn in Dayton and called to make a reservation at the sister property in Indianapolis. The woman on the phone was very friendly and worked at getting me a "better rate." And she did. The staff at this hotel are very obliging and pleasant and do a lot to make a stay at an ordinary place very pleasant. I was there for three days with my two dogs... it's a great hotel for pet owners.
When I first checked in, the room I was assigned to didn't have working heat. The desk clerk said she would see if she could get it to work while I went to get some dinner. I was really tired, so I just went to the Cracker Barrel next door, which was pretty good. Came back from dinner... they'd had no luck with the heat in that room and moved me across the hall to another room that not only had working heat, but was a little nicer too, I thought. 
Both rooms were clean and well-maintained (except for the one heater) but could use a little updating. The bathrooms are really relics from the seventies with brown and mustard tiles. Plenty of hot water and good shower pressure, excellent towels, And really, those are the things that are important.
Drury Inns ofter lots of little extras... an hour of free long distance service, free ethernet access (not wireless, alas) an evening reception and full breakfast. The evening thing was well-attended, but as a result the reception area and lobby was full of cigarette smoke. I'm not a die-hard anti-smoker by any means, but we're all getting so used to places being smoke free (and smelling cleaner and fresher as a result) that this was kind of unfortunate in the smallish lobby. 
The Drury doesn't charge extra for pets, and they were great to honor my request for a ground floor room. There aren't any big areas for airing dogs, but what is there is adequate. The hotel is situated off of a side street, and sandwiched between two restaurants (Bob Evans and the aforementioned Cracker Barrel) so it feels relatively sheltered. I see from a previous review that someone suffered vandalism to their car while they were there. It's possible to park where your car can be seen from the window of one's room and if I were worried about my vehicle, I'd park within sight and certainly under a lamp post. 
This hotel is convenient to the ring road, pyramids, art museum and not too bad for getting to the state fair grounds. Many construction workers and tradesmen seem to be long term guests there. The rates are pretty reasonable, about $70 a night when I was there. A comfortable place to stay at a reasonable price.

name: Embassy Suites Indianapolis North
title: “Big and noisy but adequate lodging”
text:
Stayed at this hotel while in town for a 50th reunion. There were not many of us there with our group but hundreds there for an enormous event in Indy that weekend. First the good things: Large two room suite with sinks in bathroom and bedroom. Room with upholstered furniture, television and large desk and bar. The set up of rooms very nice. Liked open door to tiny outdoor patio - great to let in fresh air. Staff seemed friendly, breakfast was tasty but average and cocktail hour with free cocktails and snacks a nice touch although very crowded and noisy. Hotel had good location with restaurants in close proximity, even walking distance.
Bad points: Hotel is an atrium design so noise level high. Atrium never seemed clean. Fountains that were never working throughout big open area very dirty looking with things floating on bottom. This is where you had to et breakfast so not too pleasant and very noisy and crowded. Room as well as hotel was fairly old and well used. Elevators extremely slow with one not working at all. We were on 8th floor-need I say more. The hotel had just gone non-smoking the month before our visit but I think our room had been a smoking room and the smell was in upholstered furniture in room. Our toilet ran constantly which was annoying.

name: La Quinta Inn Indianapolis East
title: “NO SPEED CHANNEL”
text:
Hotel in Indianapolis with NO SPEED CHANNEL.
Breakfast area is so small.
Hallways smells bad
Room was clean.

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “An excellent hotel close to Union Square”
text:
We ( coming from Switzerland) had been mooving our son from Tennessee to San Francisco,and we had been staying for a month in the Donatello. We had been absolutely satisfied. First of all a very warm reception has been given to us. The room had been spacious and very nice, and it had always been spotlessly clean.
The hotel has also a nice bar an a very good restaurant. We enjoyed our stay so much and we absolutely recommend this hotel.

name: Embassy Suites Indianapolis North
title: “Hotel had a great vacation atmosphere.”
text: The location was good for exploring areas that were both inside and out of the city. I recommend self transportation if you dont like a lot of cab rides. Great thing was you have many choices of eating places within walking distance. Pool and hot tub were very relaxing. The great staff was very freindly.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Austin
title: “An outstanding place to hold a meeting”
text:
I hosted a week-long series of meetings for over 200 attendees. The service was beyond impeccable - I heard numerous compliments for both large and small ways the staff made us comfortable. I worked with dozens of staff people, and they were uniformly helpful and cheerful - not once did I hear "no we can't do that". Additionally, the food from banquet services was far better than other hotels I've used.
As an example, on Wednesday afternoon I asked if we could have Thursday lunch on the lawn instead of the dining room, since the daytime temperature was nice. Not only did they make the switch without a complaint, but no additional charge (unlike other hotels), and they even gave me an opportunity an hour before to change my mind back when the wind kicked up.
One member of my group forgot the charger for his laptop. He went to the concierge desk which lent him a replacement (free!) that fit his model - most hotels wouldn't have had a stock, and even if they did would have charged for it. That made a big impression!
Location is very nice, on the lake, with great hiking and biking trails just outside the door. (And the hotel rents bikes, which are in good condition.) It's just a few blocks walk to the music and dining areas.
Yes, it's not quite as luxurious as other Four Seasons hotels. But having the outstanding service was far more important than a huge hotel room.

name: Hampton Inn Indianapolis Northwest - Park 100
title: “One of the nicest Hampton Inns”
text: This Hampton Inn was so clean and seemed to be pretty new. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The continental breakfast was good as always with Hampton hotels. We were in town to visit the Children's Museum. This hotel was about a 12 minute drive from the museum. It was the perfect choice. I would highly recommend this as a very nice place to stay. If I am ever in town again, I will make sure to stay here!

name: The Donatello Hotel
title: “Perfect Location & Great Service”
text: The staff at the hotel was great, especially the concierge located on the top floor (i can't think of his name right now!) The location is a block away from Powell Street and the cable car lines. There are quite a few restaurants open pretty late just down the street on Post. I felt pretty safe walking around at night in this neighborhood

name: Four Seasons Hotel Austin
title: “Unless you're shelling out bigtime for an upper-end room, stay the Raddison”
text: The Four Seasons Austin has both "city view" and "lake view" rooms. The "lake view" rooms cost quite a bit extra. When I called to book, I specifically requested a King-bed room with a view of Town Lake. Again, upon checking in, I made sure that the gentleman working the check-in desk confirmed I had a lake view room. Imagine my surprise when I checked into my "lake view" room on the second floor, only to find that virtually half the window was taken up by the balcony of the suite next door, and that the view of the lake was almost entire obscured by trees. The room had no balcony, and no way to open the window. Moreover, I found the room to be fairly small. Needless to say, I was not pleased -particularly given the lengths I'd gone to request this "lake view" room and the fact that I was paying extra for it. I went back down to the check-in, and explained the problem. The gentleman at the desk was clearly aware that the room I'd been assigned was not a desirable one, and did not seem particularly happy that I was requesting a proper lake view room. When I explained to him that I wanted a lake view room with a balcony, he claimed that those were in a different room category and were all taken regardless. However, he did place me in a virtually identical room on the seventh floor. I was hoping to change and quickly head to dinner but the reservations desk did not notify the luggage attendant that my room had been changed, so it turned out that my luggage had been delivered to the wrong room. This took another trip to the lobby to sort out. On the plus side, the restaurant is quite good, and I enjoyed an excellent Sunday morning brunch on the patio outside. However, I could have had the same view of the lake and a comparable quality room at the Radisson a few blocks down, and probably paid a lot less for my room. Overall somewhat disappointing.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Great Location”
text: We had a great 3 days at this hotel at the start of our holiday. When we checked in (very efficient) we were told we had the best room - we did!! Top floor with a view of Union Square. The room was excellent, the staff were so friendly and helpful and nothing was any trouble. Coffee and cookies on tap all day. SFO was having a heatwave at the time but we did not find this to be a problem at all - a fan was available if we wanted it. Housekeeping was always good. The hotel could not be faulted and we would stay here again without a doubt. A great hotel in a great city.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Exellent choice for a family”
text:
We just returned from a one-night stay at the Argonaut. This was our second visit in about three years. We got a very good rate of 169.00 a night, and as a Kimpton member, received a free upgrade to a 4th floor, bay view room. On our previous visit, we had a courtyard view room. Other rooms are nonview interior rooms and we have not stayed in those. Staff was very friendly, and our room was really, really clean. We parked in a garage near the hotel for 32.00 (the maximum rate); the hotel valet parking charges 39.00 not including tax. There is no garage connected to the hotel.
We travelled with two older children and the room was large enough to accommodate us comfortably. Good sized bathroom. Very comfortable beds and pillows, and efficient heat/air in each room. We did not have any trouble with noise from adjoining rooms, but I don't think the hotel was full on the night we were there.
My only negative is that although the hotel is located on the quiet end of Fisherman's Wharf, near Ghirardelli Square (which is being renovated), and the cable car turnaround, the rest of Fisherman's Wharf is so trashy. I'd forgotten how unpleasant it is to walk past junky souvenir stores with hoardes of people! But the city is beautiful, riding the cable cars to Chinatown or beyond is always fun, and Golden Gate Park and the Presidio are lovely.

name: Hampton Inn Indianapolis Northwest - Park 100
title: “Best staff in Indy”
text: Stayed several nights and will only stay at this location in the future. It is centrally located for our activites and it's not but a couple years old, clean, excellent breakfast, staff - from floor mopers, cook, front desk on up to management. Just a super nice stay. We've stayed at higher priced and lower priced hotels in Indy and like the three bears, find this hotel just right.....

name: Drury Inn & Suites Indianapolis Northeast
title: “Very much worth it”
text: I've stayed at a lot of hotels in this chain, and this was probably in my top three. Great service and superb rooms, great pool, breakfast, etc. First time we had the 5:30 kickback, and it blew us away with the variety of hot and cold snacks. We booked two rooms the morning of our stay and Jessie put us in two rooms adjacent to each other on the quietest part of the floor. I've always believed in the value of the chain, but this took it to a new level. Even though it's on the far outskirts of town, this will probably be the hotel I stay in anytime I have a stopover in Indianapolis. Definitely worth the trip and the stay. One of the best hotel values you'll find.

name: Comfort Suites Indianapolis
title: “2nd time here, good as the 1st..........”
text:
newer facility, convenient to several area restaurants. far enough off highway to be quiet, but still convenient to I-65.
very friendly staff, spacious clean rooms, frig/microwave, comfortable bed.
breakfast is quite adequate....pastries, fruit, yogurt, cereals, hard boiled and scrambled eggs, and sausage (although i have to admit it was "different looking").
lots of area restaurants nearby.

name: Omni Severin Hotel
title: “Never again!”
text: The room was so small, not enought outlets to do hair. Bathroom was dirty when we arrived(dirt and hair on the floor behind the door and toilet had not been cleaned under the seat), no exhaust fans. Fire alarms went off three times starting at 11:00 at night! We were on the 7th floor and evacuated by way of stairs because that is what the intercom said to do. When we got to the first floor we were told it was a prank and for us to walk back up to our room(That is 14 flights of stairs i had to climb and I am 52!!!)! We told of our disapointment to the consierge and desk clerk who did not show any concern or seem to care, just stated that it is a Historic Hotel. For the price I paid, I was extremely dissatisfied!

name: Drury Inn & Suites Indianapolis Northeast
title: “You won't be disappointed . . .”
text: Stayed here while checking out the City/Children's Musuem. This was my first Drury stay and I wasn't disappointed. Staff was really friendly, facilities were all clean, breakfast was good, good location and loved all the free extras (soda/happy hour/popcorn/parking/internet).

name: Hilton Indianapolis
title: “Hilton Indy”
text: This is a excellent hotel.... Located right downtown in the mix of things. Right by the Circle Mall.....The staff at the hotel made you fell so good you didn't want to go home.... The entire staff go's out their way to make you feel at home..

name: Comfort Suites Indianapolis
title: “Great stay!”
text: We stayed at this hotel as we were traveling to South Carolina. Great location and very new and clean! Right off I-65. We had a very spacious room with separate sitting area. Breakfast was also good. Highly recommend.

name: Embassy Suites Indianapolis North
title: “WE DON'T STAY ANYWHERE ELSE!”
text: We have stayed here on several occasions over the years. I like staying on the top floor with the patio door, and this is my daughters favorite thing also. My husband and I have privacy away from our daughter with the two room suite with two tvs. And the breakfast is wonderful! Great value for the money and I love the location.

name: Super 8 Motel Taylor
title: “Toilets wouldnt flush stuff wouldnt help!!!”
text:
Had 2 roomsnext to each other thank godness. We checked in to the hotel at 4:00 pm . We took stuff to the room then we left to go eat .Party in other didnt get there until 7:00.
We decided to go gambling . My other party went to there room flushed toilet ran over no. 1 not 2 .we called front desk they asked what did we put in it . He said he was alone and couldnt leave the front desk. If we should come down get the stuff and clean it up because he couldnt leave didnt offer to move them.He would get a plunger for the toilet 
when he could leave the front desk. 7:30 they went to eat came back then we went to casino 3:oo am got back water was still at the top of the toilet . Called front no answered checked out in the morning ask the girl at the front desk about it she didnt know any thing about it . got the managers numbers will call on monday.she didnt care couldnt give me a discount because the rate 49.49 with my aarp discount .so reported her . I told her what I was going to do she didnt care.

name: Sleep Inn University Place
title: “Sweet Rest For the Best”
text: Perfectly located for work in the north Charlotte area near hospital, university and all Charlotte attractions including Panther stadium and Nascar HOF... Numerous restaurants - including my quick fave Bojanges (next door) as well as upscale favorites for Steak, Sushi, Sports Bars and convenient to Wallgreens... This is a very well managed hotel. The GM, Sam is an absolute gentleman and from the desk staff to room care everyone is very pleasant and helpful. Very nice breakfast nook, outdoor pool and wonderful contemporary rooms that are comfortable and totally state of the art from the flat screen tvs to the great wifi service... You'll get a very affordable rate with the same type accommodations as others charge twice as much - so get a sweet rest for the cost of the best... don't overlook this wonderful place when looking for a wonderful place to stay! Also very convenient to all the major thoroughfares for easy travel in the area.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Charlotte
title: “WORST EXPERIANCES EVER!”
text: As a Hotelier, I have never experience such bad service before, it's surprising to me that a Night Auditor would treat a guest the way they did, with No “S” on guest service skills whatsoever specially from a “Starwood hotel franchised”, as stranded passenger, I had no choice on my selection of stay, greeted with no welcome attitude, neither explain when ask about my departure time, the way the operated there limited shuttle schedule, no communication in part to the Front Desk. Worst part came on the next day on my departure, no courtesy to acknowledge you from a lady that was working on the front desk, here attitude were like, I was doing her or them a favored to stay there, I would make sure that someone on upper management understands that our product is based on Service and not on Attitude specially on such competitive market.

name: Extended Stay America - Charlotte - Airport
title: “Good room-- Ok service.”
text:
Super clean space. Stayed here for a week. Felt like a small studio apt with kitchen, bathroom and small closet. Some neighbors were loud but overall quite at night. Offered shuttle service to airport and Walmart but I didn't end up using it. 
Had a random guy knock on my door that I didn't know so I called to inform the front desk but I was told they didn't have security on-site to come check it out and didn't follow-up on it. The lady said that they would have the shuttle driver come around but he wouldn't be back for another half hour which didn't feel reassuring. Also, guys would be loitering around or outside the balcony a few doors from my room. That made me feel a little unsafe being a solo female travel. Customer service at the desk was just okay but could sense they didn't even want to be there. Maid service only came once during my stay to replenish soap and clean towels. They were stingy on complimentary products like creamer and soap.
I would pick a different extended stay next time.

name: Sonesta ES Suites Charlotte
title: “Just like home”
text: This hotel is wonderful! They thought of everything--literally! From the moment I arrived they made me feel like a guest. They added so many nice touches, it was better than being at home! They had everything--from Microwave popcorn in the room, to Security at night that left me a nice note on my car, not to leave my GPS out! Wow! Stay here!

name: Charlotte Express Inn
title: “I would come back”
text: Just wanted to post that this is a great hotel to stay. The people where generous and very informational when trying to find my hotel room. If I visit Charlotte again rest assure I would come back to the Real Value Inn.

name: Sonesta ES Suites Charlotte
title: “Good for family budget stay.”
text:
I was here on a business trip and meetings where we needed a private conference room. This is more of a family/extended stay place where you can have a small kitchenette and basic amenities in the room. Staff was very helpful and courteous.. Tues thru Thurs they have a pretty filling buffet and free wine/beer/cokes from 530-730. Also have a more complete free breakfast than other hotels in the area including Fairfield and HI Express. So if on a real budget, you can get breakfast and dinner free..
Hotel is a little worn, but OK. Rooms were quiet.. Great location fairly convenient to Carrowinds, so attracts a lot of families in summer..
Internet was flawless and much easier to connect than the other hotels mentioned..both of which I had normally stayed at until this trip. I'll probably be back.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Charlotte
title: “Good customer service; not best area of town”
text: This hotel has an excellent staff. They remember everybody's name, what you have done that day, etc. Mr. Alex, Mr. Jeff, and Miss Kookie at the front desk really go out of their way to try and do everything they can to ensure a good stay. Miss Cathy and Miss Cindy take care of the bar (note - this hotel does NOT have a restaurant - the food is ordered from elsewhere). The bar has two local beers which are good. Mr. Walt takes care of everything going on on the property. The location is in a somewhat "sketchy" area of town but there are many amenities around it. It is also easy to get uptown (other cities' downtown area) by the light rail which is right across the street. A CVS, Firehouse Subs, and other shops are near the hotel along with some restaurants. The hotel gives you a coupon for 10% off at a BBQ place that is nearby. The hotel itself is nothing very special but the staff (including Mr. Mike the GM) are excellent.

name: Sonesta ES Suites Charlotte
title: “Stay Awhile”
text:
Wow! This place has a lot packed in for the traveler. You could stay for awhile before getting bored. The suites are comfortable and well designed. The breakfast offered variety, including fruits and waffles and other pastries. The gym was sufficient, better than many others, and the laundry is adjacent...and save your coins, because it's complimentary. There's an outdoor court for basketball or volleyball, and there are two grills for guests. The room has a dishwasher and two eyes on a stove. The price was comprable to other hotels in the area that didn't offer as many amenities. Nice!
We only had a couple of issues - one was the shower curtain. It sagged, falling off its snaps at the seam. The fan wouldn't come on, but we didn't report it as the temperatures were moderate. 
What a lot to offer. Plan to stay for awhile and enjoy this hotel stay.

name: City Center Inn
title: “Horrible!! Unsafe!!”
text: Oh, my..where do I start... As soon as we pulled in the parking lot, we were approached by a scary man begging for cigarettes and money. He was looking to see what he could steal from my car as I was trying to get my things out and hide the other stuff from view. That was at 6pm in the rain. When we came back from dinner, we couldn't even get out of the car.. he was back and walked right up to my car window!!! I had to call the front desk to tell them to get security so I could get in my room! If I wasn't staying there with a friend and about 10 guys to protect me, I NEVER would have stayed here! (My friend was working for a band in the city..the crew and band were staying here.) I also saw a man looking in the rooms and banging on the doors to beg for money and such. My friends said they saw him looking to break into the cars in the lot.

name: Studio 6 Charlotte Airport
title: “good airport location/excellent value”
text: I stayed at this property May 20-22. I paid $43.00 per night. The room was a decent size and had a full kitchen. The air conditioner worked, there wasn't a lot of street noise and the bathroom was clean. It was a fine room about 3 miles from the airport. I have no complaints. Good, basic accommodations at rock bottom prices with a kitchen included. The Sheraton (@$150.00 per night) is .37 miles away. You could walk there, hang out in their nice lobby and drink at their bar and save yourself lots of cash by sleeping at Studio 6.

name: Budget Inn Charlotte
title: “bof bof”
text:
sale
personnel peu aimable 
la navette pour l'aéroport a lieu quand bon leur semble
petit dej servi jusqu'à 9h seulement
rien à faire autour de l'hôtel

name: La Casa Inn
title: “Omg the worst hotel I've ever stayed at...”
text: This hotel was unbelievable....They first off did not have any towels! they had one towel in the room and when we went to ask for some the lady at the front desk said they did not have any. We decided to go buy our own. Room service did not even come to ask if we needed any! No room service at all the whole 2 nights we were there! The tv did not work although someone did come replace it the phone in the room also did not work and they knew this but never came to replace that. They had not soap, shampoo, or anything else that a hotel usually has. The room was just plain nasty...it felt dirty me and my friends had to wear shoes all around the room and bathroom. Do not stay here unless you are use to beig in a dirty, nasty, filthy, grundgy, and discusting environment.

name: Red Roof Inn Charlotte UNCC
title: “Nice Stay!”
text: My daughter and I stayed here for her Cheerleader Competition. The lobby was nice and well decorated. We were able check in early and the rooms were nice and spacious for two people. We booked a double bed room and the view overlooked the parking lot. They offered a hot buffet style breakfast each morning with a nice seating area. The hotel was clean and had two elevators. Our room was on a top floor and fairly quiet. The beds were extremely comfortable and they offered plenty of space to put your belongings, clothes, etc. The bathroom was also sizeble for your needs. They did not have, however, an indoor or outdoor pool. You also would need a car to travel to some of the local restaurants, shops, and grocery stores. I would definately stay there again.

name: Super 8 Charlotte Sunset Road
title: “Average- great price”
text: Average motel, around the clock security and room was decent, clean, about your normal motel room, maybe a little cleaner, great place if you just need a bed for a night, stayed during some time spent at charlotte motor speedway, is in great location almost walking distance from motel.

name: Knights Inn Charlotte
title: “Hotel knights Inn - próximo ao aeroporto”
text: O hotel tem um bom atendimento e um café da manhã razoável (torradas, cereais, panquecas café e leite), simples porém agradável. O quarto tem um bom conforto e são limpos. Fica próximo ao aeroporto porém não há comércio próximo (lanchonete, mercado etc). Fica ao lado da rodovia 85 o que facilita o deslocamento pela cidade para que está com carro. De um modo geral a relaçao custo-benefício atende as expectativas para que quem não quer muito luxo.

name: Country Inn & Suites By Carlson, Charlotte - I-85 Airport
title: “Flight Cancelled at Midnight CI&Suites to the Rescue w/ Fast-Friendly Service”
text: The shuttle comes to the hotel every half hour 24 hours. Wow that saved me a cab drive and fare. The gentleman put my bag in the van even though I had no reservation and gave me a discount card for a stranded passenger rate $59. This included a spacious and clean room with HBO, a bathtub, and a hot breakfast. Alonphso made sure to put in my rewards number and Dawn got me to airport in a few minutes with a nice smile and the presence of mind to suggest writing this up in Trip Advisor. What a smart and loyal employee! Thanks Country &Inn Suite staff you were lifesavers. GWB

name: The Leland
title: “Stay somewhere else!! ”
text:
Me and my wife drove to Detroit to see a Tigers game one very hot July day and stayed at the Leland. Booking the hotel on hotels.com, we were not sure what to expect. I was hoping for at lease a Red Roof Inn class of room. Man, was this far from it. It took us moving to 3 different rooms before we found one that had air conditioning that worked. Then, once in our room, the walls, bathroom, TV buttons, couch, mini kitchen was very dirty. The only plus was that the hotel was close to a people mover station that made it easy to go from place to place. If the money was put into this building for restoration, it COULD be a beautiful place.
There is a reason this place was cheap. YOU GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR!! My recommendation is to spend a few extra bucks and stay at the Holiday Inn just across the way.
One really good thing that came from staying at the Leland, is that from the switching rooms, to the "Gothic" clubs in the hotel basement, and the "haunted" atmosphere of the hallways, we have memories that will last a lifetime.
P.S. If you are going to be driving through Luna Pier on your way to Detroit, stop by the Beak Jerky Outlet... YUMMY!

name: Sun Suites of Charlotte
title: “Nicht gut - no recomendation”
text:
Dieses Hotel war das schlechteste in welchem ich je gewohnt habe. Der Teppich dreckig, tote Insekten in den Ecken, die Zudecke des Bettes hatte Brandflecken, das Bad war nur oberflächlig gereinigt.
Aber das Schlimmste war der Gestank im Zimmer. Es roch so stark nach Desinfektionsmittel, dass ich Kopfschmerzen davon bekam. Tja und ein Fenster zum Öffner auch nicht da. War glücklicherweise nur jeweils in der Nacht und nur für 2 Nächte da.
Nie wieder.
Bitte nicht buchen !!!
Don't book this hotel !!!

name: Quality Inn - Charlotte
title: “Great Value at an Older but Well-kept Hotel”
text: I stayed here four days on an impromptu visit to Charlotte. The Hotel is convenient to the airport, the City, the southern suburbs, and highway. The Management was superb and the staff were friendly and efficient. The room was clean and the mattress and bedding were terrific (for a change). The hotel offers smoking and non-smoking rooms, a full breakfast is included in the rate, and I was very satisfied with my experience. This hotel is a great value.

name: North Charlotte Inn
title: “Good place to rest for a night”
text:
I was on a cross country trip for rest and relaxation with various friends and stayed at hotels between stays at friends homes. I was only staying for a night as I rested on long drive days so I did not need anything fancy.
Microtel offered a friendly staff and a safe comfortable room.
That was all I needed.

name: Microtel Inn by Wyndham Charlotte Airport
title: “We always stay at Microtels if they are in our area needed and have always been pleased.”
text: A good experience. Never got an extra pillow that I asked for but other than that a great night spent!!

name: Doubletree Hotel Charlotte Airport
title: “Excellent staff!!”
text: I missed the last connection home from Charlotte & needed a place to stay. At the last minute I saw a room show up at this hotel on the Hilton app. I called the hotel immediately & was told they had 1 room (every other decent hotel within 15 miles was sold out). I booked the room & the agent said he'd send the shuttle. From the moment I got in the shuttle I felt taken care of. The lady at the front desk was super sweet and made sure I was taken care of (my water b/c of status, cookie, hotel shuttle reservation back to the airport). She remembered me the next morning when I was waiting for the shuttle & was just as friendly then. They really turned what could have been a really stressful night into a pleasant stay. Will definitely try to stay here if I need a room at CLT again.

name: TownePlace Suites Charlotte University Research Park
title: “Feared for our safety!”
text: The hotel itself was okay (and I really mean just okay)...not at all what you would expect from a name like Marriott. The room was in need of updating. But we could have lived with that. What we could not live with was the "elements" in the hotel. When we first arrived, my husband told my teenage son and me not to go outside to walk the dog or for any other reason because the appearance and the conversation of the people hanging out in the parking lot made him feel uncomfortable. In fact, he would remove his jewelry whenever he had to go out. No big deal...we were there only for one night and would simply stay inside. But at about 5:00 in the morning we were awakened to the sound of two men in the room next to ours arguing and fighting each other. (The walls in the hotel room were extremely thin!) The arguing was so intense that I literally got down on the floor for fear that bullets might start flying next door. And that was before they actually starting physically fighting! After about 45 minutes of listening to this and fearing for our family's safety, my husband and I just collected our kids and checked out. My husband had barely slept and he had a 4 hour drive ahead of him, but we sim ply could not stay there another minute. Before we left, my husband called the front desk to report the fighting next door, no manager was available and the front desk clerk did not seem inclined to do anything about the problem. When we checked out early my husband told the desk clerk our reason for doing so. The clerk said that the manager would contact us, but no one ever did. I would never ever ever stay at this hotel again.

name: Continental Inn
title: “Won't be back”
text:
Last year, we chose the cheapest hotel we could find (around 40 dollars) and it left something to be desired. This year, I considered higher star hotels in the $120 range, but based on the reviews here, decided that the Continental Inn would be a good compromise. I was disappointed, as all three people in my group both agreed that the cheaper hotel from last year was even better! 
First, the staff was fine - friendly and helpful, but not enough to make this place "worth it". As for the room: When you open the door, it actually hits one of the beds and can't fully open because of the tight space. That bed also is within one foot of the air conditioner, making it difficult to sleep in because the air is SO CLOSE to your face. (I slept on the far side of that bed, but the closer side wasn't acceptable). The room was clean enough, one hair in bathroom, but no biggie. They gave us plenty of towels and pillows The beds were well made. However, at first, I didn't even think they had mattress covers, because I could feel the seams/grooves in the mattress. But after I got in bed, I realized they had the cheapest possible ill-fitting mattress covers, and all three of use complained about them sliding around and bunching up under the sheets. Also, the hotel rooms are outside entrances only, meaning every single car that drives into the lot makes noise and keeps you from sleeping. The walls are so thin that fellow guests rolling their luggage woke me up. I generally sleep quite well, no matter where, but between the bunched up bed, air conditioning, and noise, I couldn't sleep much at all. :( Lastly, another reviewer recommended the breakfast, and the hotel website mentioned the hot breakfast including waffles and eggs. This was one of my deal-makers. However, the breakfast consisted of two cereals, a few packaged baked goods, a waffle maker, some hardboiled eggs and some old bananas. They had terrible apple juice and Sunny D orange juice. They needed to refill the butter and silverware (had to eat my waffle with a spoon rather than a fork). Now, don't get me wrong -- I expect this breakfast at your typical cheaper hotel, but I had higher expectations here. 
All in all, this hotel was not worth the money. I woulld have been satisfied with it had it been the typical $40-50 cheapy hotel -- for which I have lower expectations. However, for that extra 25 bucks, I expected better. I would not stay again, even if the price was right. I don't often do reviews, and I again want to say that I have no complaints about the staff... but the hotel itself was outdated, too small, and needed small upgrades to make it even acceptable. I have reasonable expectations, but this just is not the place for me.

name: Residence Inn Charlotte SouthPark
title: “Average but better than nearby Courtyard by Marriott”
text: After a bad experience at the nearby South Park Courtyard (see my separate review) on the way to Florida, we stopped at the next door Residence Inn coming back from Florida. It was definitely better than the Courtyard - much bigger room (we had an efficiency with a separate living area/kitchenette), cheaper after taking into account the free breakfast, located in an even more quiet area of an office park, and a much better mattress. However, this place had some problems, including a broken elevator, which the staff said had been acting up for awhile (leaving only one elevator for an 8-story hotel), no washcloths in the room (the staff brought them up right away when we complained), really lousy soft pillows, and also what appeared to be stains on a couple of the pillow cases. The breakfast area is big, but there were not a lot of hot offerings, and the rolls/danish were not very good. Also, you can't park all that close to the hotel (the unloading area is not all that big either), and the parking is in an office complex garage next to a remote area (the garage does have security personnel checking it, however). I will probably give this place a try again in the future, but it needs to make some improvements.

name: Doubletree Hotel Charlotte Airport
title: “Great airport hotel!”
text: This hotel is near the airport and has a shuttle. Rooms are consistent with other Doubletrees --nice. I was not welcomed as a Diamond member. However, the breakfast was great and very well done. I will stay here again

name: Doubletree Hotel Charlotte Airport
title: “One of the best!!!!!!”
text: I have stayed at the Doubletree near the airport several times and have always felt it was a top notch property with first class service. The breakfast buffet is always great, fresh, and has so much to offer. the entire staff at this hotel truly understands what great customer service is.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Charlotte SouthPark
title: “Southpark Marriott”
text: Clean rooms, nice beds, good location, friendly staff...safe quiet area.

name: Quality Inn & Suites
title: “Room had bad smell”
text:
That this place used to be a La Quinta explains things a bit.
This is a hotel with exterior room access only, ie no indoor hallways etc. The windows of many of these rooms are covered with plastic, under renovations apparently. This wasn't made known to me when I booked the room at the front desk.
But the main issue was the smell when I opened the door ! It was an over-masked type of smell, like they used too much scented cleaner to cover something up... but the scented cleaner isn't very nice. I almost switched rooms, but didn't want the hassle. I left the door ajar (with the night lock on) and cranked the A/C to max, and that together with my adjustment of the scent seemed to help. 
Nice king bed, quite comfortable. High speed wireless worked well. One-cup-at-a-time coffee maker was good and quick.
This hotel is under the approach path for Charlotte-Douglas Int'l Airport, so if you don't like the roar of jets going overhead, you might not want this hotel ! The door sealed the noise ok and the A/C fan helped too. I am a pilot actually so I quite honestly like the sound of jets cruising low overhead.
Although breakfast is available from 6:00 am onwards, when I went down at 8:00 am the staff were just making coffee then, and the garbage was overflowing.
I don't recommend the pool (see picture).
There are about 10 hotels within a mile of this hotel all along Queen City Dr. and the area. There is a Food Lion about 1/2 mile away.

name: The Blake Hotel
title: “Recently updated? Needs more!”
text:
I stayed here not by choice, but because of a convention I was attending and this is where my company booked us. This is an older hotel that advertises it is recently updated. Yes, many aspects have been, the rooms are nicely furnished, new bedding, but.....they need to continue and do more work to bring it up to todays standards. The AC is ancient, although I had the thermostat set at 60 the entire stay,it never got below 75 in the room. The bathroom, although updated, is not practical. The sink installed is large and rectangular, and takes up most of the counter. The shower is enclosed by a piece of glass that only covers 2/3 of the opening and is stationary, which means the floor gets wet every time. This makes no sense whatsoever. 
The elevators are also old and very slow.

name: Microtel Inn by Wyndham Charlotte Airport
title: “Great value and service”
text: The Microtel exceeded our expectation, which was to get some rest for 1 night between 2 long-haul flights. The room was clean, quiet enough given the proximity to airport and motorway. The best though was the unexpected extra perks: free internet, free breakfast (with fresh waffles) and especially the very friendly staff and great service. Thanks especially to James the front-desk clerk for his helpfulness and service worthy of a 5 star hotel!

Address: '508 E Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd'
name: Hilton Garden Inn Charlotte Uptown
title: “Great Hotel and Staff!!”
text: I stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn Charlotte for a recent business trip this last week and found both the hotel and its staff to be top-notch. From check-in to breakfast time to checkout everyone at the hotel had a smile to greet and were helpful in every detail. My room was clean, well-furnished and housekeeping were super. I do want to commend Kristin at the front desk as always having the right answer and being a step-ahead to help the guest, she made my stay special with her above-board customer service and knowledge of the local area. When I'm in Charlotte again I will stay here!!

name: The Blake Hotel
title: “Needs a cash infusion”
text:
The Blake tries really hard, that is the best that I can say for it.
We stayed on a Saturday night for a convention recently and while we had a good time I was disappointed with the room. The bathroom was dirty, things felt "used", the AC was not very strong, there is no soundproofing and the beds are only average (reserved a KING room and got two smallish queens).
Ate at the on site restaurant and it was decent but pricey.
There was a $10 parking charge overnight, I should have contested it but I didn't have the energy at the time. No one checked the pass and it was not a secure lot so you could skip this if needed.

name: Hampton Inn University Place
title: “Not up to Hampton standards”
text:
This was first Hampton Inn that I did not find up to standards. Prior to checking in I advised the front desk that I was a Hilton Gold which should communicate that I was a regular traveler.
Unlike other Hamptons I have stayed in, the fabric on the furniture was very frayed and there was someone else's hair in the bathtub. 
It is not my practice to complain, but at breakfast the (very friendly) breakfast manager inquired about my stay and once I related the problems she and the front desk clerk visited my room. They were sincerely apologetic and promised me a coupon for a free night's stay. 
I do believe that this might have been a (bad) luck of the draw since the standards of Hamptons are usually pretty good and since I am regular visit to Charlotte I will give them another chance in the future.

name: Charlotte Marriott Executive Park
title: “Wonderful stay, friendly staff”
text: We enjoyed a night's stay at this lovely Marriott in Charlotte. The staff was very friendly, the breakfast buffet was delicious, the room was clean, and the pool was so refreshing! They have a wonderful area outside by the outside pool with a deck and outdoor bar and fire pit. There also is a "beach" volleyball court outside the pool area where it was fun to watch the kids play. We were on the 18th floor with a great view over the area. My only negative response is that the room was quite small and the bathroom also.

name: Hampton Inn University Place
title: “Reliable and comfortable place to stay”
text:
This is the second time I've stayed here and both trips were for concerts. Hotel is minutes away from Verizon Wireless Amphitheater with many restaurants and shopping centers closeby. The busy traffic intersection is the downside to being so close to all the activity, but the hotel is quiet despite all that. We got a great rate by booking online with the "no refund" deal. Being confident we would stay there after a previous visit we enjoyed made that commitment pretty easy. 
Check-in was completely painless. Shemekia was very friendly and approachable, and I appreciated her attention to detail. Our room was great--king bed, N/S with a mini fridge and microwave. The room was clean and very comfortable. Nothing except home can beat a Hampton bed. The bathroom had been renovated with new granite countertops and new cabinetry, but I was disappointed to see the tub area was still original. We had an issue with the shower curtain rod, but I reported it and was pleased to find it had been resolved when we returned from the concert. 
For my next trip to that area, I am positive I will return to this hotel. It is clean, comfortable, conveniently located, and very affordable. Hampton Inns are my favorite hotels, and this one did not disappoint.

Address: '508 E Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd'
name: Hilton Garden Inn Charlotte Uptown
title: “Nice weekend in Charlotte”
text: Spent the weekend of January 28th at the Hilton Garden Inn visiting with family and going to a Bobcats game. The hotel is directly across the street from the Nascar Hall of Fame and 2-3 blocks from the Time Warner Arena. The area is safe and walker friendly. There are places to eat nearby. We had a king room with whirlpool. The bed was SO comfortable. The room was great, quiet and the hotel breakfast, which was included, was excellent. We would certainly go back!

name: The Blake Hotel
title: “Unique”
text: The lobby really had a cool and original look. Very lovely ballroom and halls. Cant wait to see it after the remodel is complete. Look forward to next year.

name: Hampton Inn University Place
title: “Best hotel experience ever!”
text: My colleague and I chose this hotel based on my husband's recommendation, even though it wasn't on the list of hotels suggested by our company. Boy, are we glad we did! Everyone was incredibly nice, especially Faith, who helped serve the continental breakfast each day. There was a group of Fulbright Scholars staying at the hotel and Faith made sure that she made them feel welcome and also introduced many of them to other guests. During our trip, there were manager's receptions catered by area restaurants each evening and again, the hotel staff was extremely friendly and accommodating. It was such a pleasant visit: we felt like we were at home, not at a hotel! I will definitely stay here again if I visit the Charlotte area!

name: Holiday Inn Charlotte-University Place
title: “Impressed”
text: I stayed at the Holiday Inn Univ. Place about a few days ago and noticed a change in customer service (i had stayed a couple months back). I commented to someone at the front desk about how I felt like my stay this time around was much better than the last time (customer service wise) and she mentioned to me that there had a been a change over in the Management and that guests should see a lot of positive change from here on out. I was also told that the hotel will be undergoing some superficial renovations which will definitely help with the atmosphere. I had a great experiance and can't wait to see the upcoming changes!

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Charlotte Airport North
title: “Suits the Purpose Very Well”
text: 10/25/12 was our second one-night stay here, and we'll be back. It's very convenient to Charlotte's airport, which was our most-important criteria when we first chose to stay here, but it's the overall comfort that will keep us coming back. We were very well pleased with the cleanliness of the rooms, lobby, and hallways. The rooms are sizeable and quite comfortable and noise hasn't been an issue at all. The beds are very comfy and the TVs are relatively new LCD HD sets. The staff has been friendly (and they haven't had to solve any problems for us). All in all, I can recommend it.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Charlotte City Center
title: “Great place to stay for a conference”
text: I stayed at this property for a weeklong conference at the convention center in July 2012. It is conveniently located between the convention center and a great outdoor restaurant/bar/shopping area downtown. It was close enough to everything that I did not need to rent a car. It was a flat $25 cab ride from the airport. The room was good size with a nice desk for working. I purchased the "stay and eat breakfast" package. I think it was only about $5 a day. This included a hot breakfast sandwich and a drink each morning in the lobby which was both good and very fast and convenient. I also ordered room service pecan-crusted trout one night that was very good. Lastly, I made use of the hotel gym which had a decent selection of equipment. I could not have stayed at a better place for the price.

name: Westin Charlotte
title: “Yup. Still like the Westins”
text: This is a good location downtown - central to business and restaurants. My room was fine - clean, quiet, and all the necessary things you'd need. I was on business, so quiet and a good bed are the key features I'm looking for. Westin, as usual, delivers.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Charlotte Airport North
title: “Decent and dog friendly”
text: Room was clean. Breakfast was good... fruit, yogurt, hard boiled eggs, waffles, cereal, bread products, juices and coffee. I brought my very large lab/pitt with no problems. No pool... sigh. Parking was fine. Very easy to get around. I WOULD stay here again.

name: Hilton Charlotte Executive Park
title: “Good but nothing extra.”
text: We just stated here. It was a nice hotel. Clean. The bar tender was nice. My only complaint is that the complimentary breakfast was quite slim. It was only bagels & a muffin tray. No fruit or even peanut butter for the bagels. Coffee & juices were available.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Charlotte
title: “Expensive internet!”
text:
Friendly reception staff, good room, good food in the restaurant - so why only an average rating?
$9.95/day/device for internet access, that's why! Yes, it's free in the business centre/lobby area, so in effect it's a charge for privacy & convenience. 
We booked the Embassy Suites as part of a package - had we booked personally we'd have been looking for free wi-fi as part of the deal.

name: Wingate By Wyndham Charlotte Airport I-85/I-485
title: “"Consistent Professional and Service Oriented staff"”
text: I have had the pleasure of getting acquainted with The Wingate by Wyndham years ago due to needing a home for hosting numerous business meetings and classes throughout the year. I have come to know the staff by name and You can't find a more caring and service oriented staff. Willing to help and answer any questions you may have about the area. I give the Wingate very high marks for their location minutes from downtown, the airport , Favorite restaurants in walking distance "Hardees , Showmars etc...and literally located seconds from the interstate. My last class held there was on July 18 and as always -exceeded my expectations. Keep up the Great Service-It is hard to find

name: Wingate By Wyndham Charlotte Airport I-85/I-485
title: “Doesn't compare to the Wingate in Atlanta-Buckhead”
text:
I must be spoiled but this Wingate was a disappointment. I stay at the Wingate in Buckhead-Atlanta at least twice a month. I am a regular and have gotten spoiled by their special attention and service. So, when going to Charlotte-thought that a Wingate would work. Wrong!The comparison to the Atlanta Wingate tells all:
1. Anytime you need a ride within a 3 mi radius-- the Atlanta Wingate says Yes! At this Wingate they said ... 'No, We only will take you to the Airport. The van sat their unused but they wouldn't take me 2 miles away. 
2. The free breakfast at the Buckhead Wingate includes a Latte machine and a person who will make you your own omelette. At the Charlotte Airport Wingate-- a coffee machine, and no service.
3. The room was similar to the Buckhead Wingate but the ottoman was stained and needed cleaning.
4. The Charlotte Wingate doesn't have a bar which is a shame. The Wingate Buckhead has a bar with a place to hang out until 11pm. 
You get the point.

name: Omni Charlotte Hotel
title: “Omni Charlotte Hotel”
text: My nieces and I stayed one night after a long day at Carowinds. The room was clean and well stocked. The coffee cups were travel cups with lids, a convenience since we were leaving before the restaurant opened. The towels and sheets were good quality. The shampoo, etc. was also of good quality and not strongly perfumed. The iron didn't heat very well so we called houskeeping and within 10 minutes we had a new one delivered. The robes were a great touch. We were on the third floor and the outside noise was a little loud after midnight (normal for a Saturday evening)

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Charlotte Airport / Coliseum
title: “Not Bad - Probably Better for Airport Stays”
text:
We had stayed at this particular Homewood Suites a few years ago. We've never needed it for any kind of stay associated with a flight out of CLT, but we have found it convenient enough for our purposes, especially since they have the larger suites that we need at better prices than most other places in the Charlotte area.
I have to say that I was a little disappointed this time. Not necessarily about the service (all was courteous), or the cleanliness and condition of the room (no complaints), but that our room was not ready at 4 pm when we arrived to check in. We were on our way into town for a wedding that evening and had arrived early, so we thought it was a great opportunity to relax a bit beforehand. Unfortunately, I was informed that there was a late checkout for that particular room and they were just going to clean it. We got into the room a little before 5.
Now, I do understand that late checkouts are not uncommon, and that there could be more of them at this particular hotel due to the unpredictability of flight schedules. But I have been told point-blank as a guest at hotels in the past, when I requested a late checkout, that it wasn't available because they needed the room. It was a somewhat minor inconvenience in this case, but, nevertheless, as far as I am concerned, a 3 pm check-in time should mean that the room is ready at 3 pm. I don't think that's unreasonable.
Otherwise, the stay was OK, about what I would expect. The rooms are comfy as you would expect for Homewood Suites. Breakfast was fine and typical of Homewood.
All-in-all, this is a good hotel for those who need an airport hotel. We didn't, and so we may look elsewhere in the future.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Charlotte Airport
title: “Better than expected”
text:
We were just overnight before catching a flight home.
The hotel is easy to find and near major highways although a U turn is required to enter the driveway.
Lots of parking close to the doors.
Very easy to get to airport.
The TripAdvisor recommendation was mixed at best but I knew the Marriott brand was pretty good and we wanted to be near the airport.
We had reserved an upgraded room for only $15 more and for $109 we ended up with a suite! I thought there had been a mistake. It appears all rooms have been redecorated. Very modern style but comfortable. Two reasonably large screen TV's. A very comfortable bed and a large bathroom. Had a small fridge. There was some beer and wine for sale at a reasonable price from the desk area.
Staff were not overly friendly but were business like and looked after all our needs which was fine with us.
Breakfast was full or continental at a reasonable price. Being buffet style you can have all you want. My wife just wanted a muffin and coffee. Me, the whole thing but they only charged me for one breakfast, $8 I think. There was a staff member present to help.
I guess the only problem was finding a place to eat after we checked in the night before. Being near the airport there was a few non licenced "take out" style restaurants in the area. We drove (we still kept the rental) about 2 miles on Wilkson Blvd towards downtown. We drove by a place called the Ranch House. It looked like a private club as there was only a small sign and the windows were covered. We turned around and luckily, a couple was just leaving. They recommeded the shrimp cocktail so we went in. It was a local steakhouse and some seafood. 
Nothing fancy (read expensive) but good food and lots of it. 
TripAdvisor reviews had suggested there was a lot of noise from aircraft. Well, it is very near the airport! They have a shuttle by the way. By 10:00 pm, the number of flights reduced and once asleep, there was no problem. The hotel was very quiet. 
They are building a major addition to the hotel which will about double the size. There was no construction while we were there (weekend) but assuming one was up by 8:00 am I cannot see noise would be a problem.
So, the Marriott Courtyard was considerably better than other airport hotels we had used and it took less than 5 minutes to get to the rental car return! Good value.

name: Westin Charlotte
title: “great stay”
text: good stay with excellent service. directly across from the convention center. parking is very expensive if you have to drive into the area. if doing business downtown car is not needed and weather is pleasant for walking

name: Omni Charlotte Hotel
title: “Wedding Weekend”
text: Must say, living in Charlotte and never having stayed in my own town as a tourist, it was a pleasant surprise to see the Uptown area working continually to make this a great business or pleasure destination.

name: Wingate By Wyndham Charlotte Airport I-85/I-485
title: “Great Stay”
text: Hotel was very clean and fairly new. Rooms have microwave and refrigerator. The information on the site doesn't say so but there is a shopping center in next door. It has a Food Lion (grocery store), Family Dollar and there are a few fast food places also. Wireless internet in the rooms as well as an ethernet cable. Continental breakfast is average. Hotel staff was accomaditing for the most part.

name: Westin Charlotte
title: “Comfortable convient stay at the Westin”
text: The Westin is located in downtown Charlotte directly across from the convention center and one block from the NASCAR Hall of Fame museum. It is a modern contemporary hotel with bright comfortable finishes. We were attending a conference at the convention center so it has a great location for that. Service and staff friendliness were excellent. We had a corner room on a high floor which offered a great view. We had room service one evening and it was quick and very good tasty. We dined one morning in the hotel restaurant and that was good also. I have stayed here twice and would most likely stay at the Westin again.

name: SpringHill Suites Charlotte Ballantyne
title: “Less than I expected”
text: The Springhill looks new but it has some drawbacks. If you get an even numbered room you may have to deal with the road noise. As vehicles drive over the brick crosswalks it sounds like rumble strips waking you from your sleep. The room may be a suite but it has only a small microwave and refrigerator. On the positive side there are a large variety of restaurants nearby.

name: Aloft Charlotte Uptown at the EpiCentre
title: “Hated this hotel”
text:
There were several good things about this hotel:
1. The shower was great. Nice water pressure.
2. Beautiful view of the city
3. Great location downtown. We were within walking distance to the Convention Center, where my daughter played volleyball that weekend, and lots of great restaurants.
4. The room allowed me to hook up my portable dvd player and watch movies on the flat screen TV.
5. There was a beautiful view of the city. We stayed on the 7th floor.
There were several bad things:
1. You have to ride the elevator to the 5th floor in order to reach the hotel lobby.
2. The air condition was so loud it would wake you up at night.
3. If someone turned the light on in the bathroom, it showed in the sleeping area and would wake you up.
4. The walls were paper thin. You could hear people talking in the hall using normal voices. You could also hear the street traffic outside. I had to wear ear plugs.
5. The lobby looked like a party area. At night the lights were dim and candles were lit and there was loud music playing.
6. The bed was hard and you were provided with 2 small pillows for a king size bed.
This hotel is for young people who like to party and/or who don't mind not sleeping. It is not peaceful at all. I would not recommend it to anyone. The entrance to the hotel is on S. College Street with only a small sign in front of it. My 15 year old loved the pool table in the lobby.

name: The Blake Hotel
title: “Fabulous, convenient hotel!”
text: We stayed at the Blake Hotel this past weekend. It was beautiful...the room was nicely appointed and very clean, and the lobby was absolutely gorgeous. The staff were very friendly and helpful. Especially nice is their shuttle service - on Saturday morning they both took us to our destination and picked us up when we called for a ride back. The concierge Anthony was very helpful, providing us with excellent information and directions through the city. I would definitely stay here again!

name: Holiday Inn Express Charlotte-Arrowood
title: “Foreign visitors, be carefull !”
text:
Being European visitors, we regularly come to The USA and due to the ease of access, we almost always stay in Hi-Ex hotels. Altogether in IC hotels group, we highly exceeded 50 hotels all over the World. Like the great majority of foreigners, we purchase electronic equipment and any optic devices on-line in The USA and have them delivered to our hotel. So far, we were always more than welcome in any US hotel and we had wonderful service regardless of the comfort level.
For a similar case, when I wrote a message to the hotel about a delivery, the manager replied that they don't have any storage space with an impolite message and without any courtesy ! I've informed immediately IC Hotels Customer relations and cancelled this hotel. I resrved Holiday Inn Express, Mathews; her is the reply of Ms. Noemi, The manager of the second hotel we have moved to :
 " We will be glad to hold your packages for your arrival. I inform my front desk staff accordingly. "
In Hardeeville Hilton Head Hi-Express (Manager Ms Cindi) and at Charleston Hwy 526 & 17 (Manager Ms Rebecca) we had a warm welcome with all our deliveries waiting for us ! In a manner we, the foreigners, we contribute to the American economy with our purchases.
Anyhow, as I previously mentionned, we didn't stay at this hotel in order not to spoil our holiday in Charlotte and we had wonderful welcome at the Matthews one, Arrowood may be comfortable or not. Front desk staff was polite on the phone. I've just wanted to inform about the mentality of the management level. If you want a totally problem free time, I would recommend to go and stay in Matthews or at South Pineville Holiday Inn Expresses !
Stayed October 2012, traveled with family

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Charlotte
title: “Soup to nuts perfect!!”
text: We had a fantastic stay at this hotel! We were greeted by smiling and professional front desk staff who were more than helpful. The lobby is attractive, relaxing and peaceful, full of live plants, water features and a great seating area. Our room was great, especially since the bedroom has a door that you may close off from the family room/wet bar area (we were travelling with our one year old). We ordered "to go" from the in hotel restaurant both nights: Omaha Steak House (of the well known Omaha mail order steaks). Exellent food, highly recommend the "obnoxious chochalate cake!" A nice offer too, by ordering "to go" and picking it up yourself you manage to avoid the "room service charge." We would stay here in a heartbeat again!

name: The Blake Hotel
title: “Great place to stay.”
text: We stayed here for one night as we were going to the Bon Jovi Concert at Time Warner Cable Arena. The location off the highway made it very easy to find. The check in process was very quick and friendly. Our room was extremely nice with a Large bed and very unique and modern bathroom. Everything about the property reminded me of an upscale, modern and eclectic New York City property. The best part was that we could walk (safely) to the Arena and back late at night with no problems or concerns. Definately a great Hotel.

name: Roberts Riverwalk Hotel & Residence Detroit
title: “Overwhelmed, understaffed, too far from city”
text: The staff were doing their utmost in a very challenging situation however the lack of enough personnel to handle both Tigers World Series guests, Detroit Lions guests, two functions downstairs leaves me with a very unpleasant time. Dirty rooms with a coffee maker and cups but NO coffee, no tea, no condiments. The room is sweltering and we were unable to control the heat coming in even with the heat off and or air on. We opened the windows all night to try to cool it and even with the outside temperature being less than 40 degrees, there was no relief. The stains on the decorative pillow on the bed made me tear off the comforter(not that we needed it with the heat) but it was a worn and dirty room. Nice people work there and they are trying but a general lack of direction was evident. If the safe in the room says it has a key and that if the key is missing they will charge you $35.00 then you assume there would be a key. I called down to a rude person to whom I said, :There is no key in the safe, I'd like it noted that it wasn't here". She rudely snapped and said come downstairs and get one!

name: Marriott Detroit Airport
title: “Labor Day weekend 2012”
text: I had a good time at the hotel. I had stayed before. The last time I had trouble with the WiFi, but it looks like it was my fault. Close to the highway, and for me close to family. I got a double this time and it was rooomy. Will stay again. I would have gave the hotel a 5, if they had a breakfast buffet like the Embassy up the street.

name: Sheraton Charlotte Airport Hotel
title: “Fine Stay”
text: Spent 1 night at this hotel. Good rate on hotels.com Free parking, Easy check-in. Nice, clean room. Neat indoor/outdoor pool off the lobby. Staff was friendly and helpful. They call this an airport hotel but I didn't see or hear any airplanes. Nice stay, would repeat.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Charlotte - Gateway Village
title: “Great Rates and Location”
text: My husband and I planned a trip to see the Charlotte Panthers. We tried our luck with the downtown Doubletree. We could not be happier! Easy check-in. Delicious warm homemade chocolate chip cookie! Yum! Clean modern room with great view. Super location to the stadium! We cannot wait for our neext trip to Charlotte and another stay at the Doubletree!

name: Omni Charlotte Hotel
title: “Short on service and amenities”
text:
As a platinum level Omni Select Guest program, I found the stay in this Omni somewhat short of expectation. What I liked was the view from my 12-floor room window. Where I find dire improvements need to be made to up the scale of the hotel or in keeping with the brand is as follows:
Gym is so small that it might just contract with the commercial gym on the lobby level to better service guests
Business center's printers (2 of them) had error messages on them
Non-smoking room smelled like being smoked and housekeeping came in to spray, resulting in an odd mix of smoke and chemical smell
Front desk service is lax
The evening local delicacy is tray of salted peanuts, from the bar downstairs probably. This falls short of what other omni provides.

name: Holiday Inn Charlotte - Center City
title: “Thanks for your honesty!”
text: My husband and I recently stayed at this hotel. Everything about our visit was great. The reason I am writing this review is to thank Kathy McNair and the housekeeper (I do not know his/her name) that clean my room on February 20. I left my debt card in the room when I checked out. I called Housekeeping that night and spoke to Kathy McNair. Kathy said the housekeeper had turned in the card. Kathy said she would mail it to me on Monday. I received the card. I want to thank both of them very much for their honesty.

name: Omni Charlotte Hotel
title: “Worth every Penny!”
text: We stayed 2 nights in a Superior Double Room. Large room (600 sq feet) with a wall of windows and a great view. We paid $119 a night. We went to attend a basketball game at the Time Warner Arenna. The hotel is in a great location...we parked our car and walked everywhere. The staff we encountered were friendly and helpful. Room service was prompt and valet was an easy process. Did not try the internet. My two very small gripes: 1. The hotel is connected to an office building with a food court. When I iniatally read this on the website, I thought that this would be perfect for a quick bite or Starbucks coffee in the morning. None of the stores were ever open our entire stay. We stayed on the weekend so maybe it is only open during the week for the office workers. 2. Our room was the last room on the hall with the stairway door being the next door. We were awakened multiple times by the door slamming. Also there was what appered to be an ajoining room. Not sure what this room led to as we were the last room. I was awakened at 2:30 by multiple men talking...could see the light under the ajoining door on. This was a little unsettling as it went on for quite a while. Overall, I thought this was a nice (not outdated at all) hotel and felt it was worth the money.

name: MotorCity Casino Hotel
title: “Casino hotel without the noise of a casino”
text:
If you want to be in a hotel with a casino, this is your place. If you don't - you can stay here as well. The set-up between hotel check-in and the casino allows you not to see or hear the casino but at the same time the casino is just down the hall.
The rooms are airy and spacious. My bathroom didn't include a tub so the shower was oversized. I liked that. The view from 1306 wasn't much but it was a short walk to the elevator. The ice machine is near the elevator at the end of the hall.
Internet is free and worked fine. The safe fits a large laptop. There is plenty of drawer space and his and her wardrobe cabinets, including 2 robes. Great extras. The bed was comfortable and housekeeping did their job as expected.
There is a small working desk/chair and 2 stuffed chairs and a small table. 
The front desk staff were efficient and helpful. Security is located near the elevators on the main level, so you get that feeling of safety.
I look forward to my return visit in August!

name: Charlotte Marriott SouthPark
title: “Very Upset Bride!”
text:
It has taken me almost a year to write this review simply because it took me that long to calm down. We booked our wedding reception at this venue hoping that they would deliver everything that was promised to us. Unfortunately, the night of our reception they were understaffed and our food was not what we selected during our tasting. So many small details were overlooked, and for a wedding, this is major. Several of our guests had issues with their rooms and some did not receive their free breakfast vouchers. I could go on and
on...Please do not trust this place for your most special event.
It is not the hotel that it once was!

name: Detroit Marriott at the Renaissance Center
title: “A fine hotel, nothing special”
text:
I stayed at the Marriott for three nights as I was participating in a conference that was also at the hotel. Check in was easy and fast. i had a room on the 44th floor. The room was clean, with a view of the river and Canada beyond. Water pressure in the shower was great. I also appreciated the large (38"?) flat screen television in the room so I could watch the baseball playoffs. The bar off the lobby was nice, but understaffed. I had a pizza from room service one night that was good. A friend and I walked to Greektown one night for dinner from the hotel and agreed that it was a sketchy walk, but no more dangerous than some walks I take in my hometown of DC.
All in all, the hotel met my expectations.

name: Charlotte Marriott SouthPark
title: “Elegant though dating a bit”
text: RECOMMENDED: Located just off the South Park Mall but far enough way to avoid street noise, the Park Hotel is a bit like staying at your Aunt's house. Little decorating touches, elegant styling, plush carpet and general attention to detail make for a very comfortable stay. The property, built in the early 80's, has gone thru 1 major renovation and is currently being painted. Bathrooms are bright though fixtures getting a bit dated. Beds comfortable and room nicely appointed. Check-in stylish and fast. This hotel attracts a different sort of clientele and is worth a visit.

name: Detroit Marriott at the Renaissance Center
title: “Great TEAMS!!”
text: I was in Detroit for the TEAMS '12 Conference & Expo, not knowing really, what to expect. The event was great, the venues awesome and the accommodation stellar. I was so impressed by the happy friendly service the hotel provided. The view was spectacular and the bed?! What can I say!! I would definitely recommend this property to any one. It. Enjoy!!

name: Westin Charlotte
title: “The Westin Has Lost it's Sparkle”
text:
Let me preface this by saying that I was a HUGE fan of this hotel. I loved having the opportunity to stay here for work. Everything about this hotel...service, rooms, bar, said "chic." I recently had to spend a night here for work. My last stay had been three years ago. Wow...a lot can change in three years. Sure, the bar and lobby area still have that uber cool vibe...but that is all that remains of the Westin of the past. Here's a summary of my stay:
-Upon entering my room, I quickly noticed nicks on the desk and night stand. Had chalked that up to years of wear. 
-My remote control had food crusted on it and the numbers had worn off.
-Pressed the "service" button on the phone to schedule a wake up call and no body answered. I'm not talking about not answering on the first ring..NOBODY answered. 
-Stepped into the "heavenly" shower to see pink mildew covering the shower head.
-The bath towel deposited long black hair on me as I dried off (I am a blonde)
-My parking was to be added to my room. It wasn't. So, when checking out...I mentioned it and was told just to pay the parking attendant. I said I didn't have cash and they said to use my credit card. Not the service of the Westin of the past. 
-We had two days of work meetings at the Westin. There was NO heat in the ladies restroom and the toliets were not flushing properly. I felt like I was using a restroom in a football stadium...on a cold winter day. 
-Our conference room was freezing, while my teammates in the next room were actually getting sick from the heat. 
-The table water served with breakfast tasted horrible. 
I was really disappointed. Not sure if there is new management at the helm or if the hotel has just gotten complacent since they have been the only higer end game in town. That is not the case anymore with the Ritz and even lower end (though newer) uptown lodging options.
