If you are just meeting at the bar, you won't likely notice the difference..but I would think again before booking a room....or an event here.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Detroit Downtown
title: “one more reason to love detroit”
text: we came to detroit for some easter r and r picked this marriot we were not disappointed clean room friendly staff easy and quick checkin/out the pool was great with wonderful views we don't need to look elsewhere for our next trip to the motor city!!

name: MotorCity Casino Hotel
title: “Wow, small room, few amenities, and it was on the executive "luxury" floor”
text:
This staff was entirely wonderful, from the moment we entered the building to leaving. All were attentive, predictive, and helpful. But that did not aid the property itself as it left a lot to be desired. My biggest issue was that it was a luxury suite, on an exclusive floor. I found it to be full of children running up and down the hall until 3-4am because their parents were in the casino and not supervising their offspring. It was otherwise loud and noisy, like being inside a base drum. The concierge lounge was always full of those children, with very few items available for consumption, and no alchol, even for purchase. The beds were ok, room was clean, but I won't likely return. 
Went to the restaurant upstairs, and while the service was excellent, the food that we got was very good, they were out of most things, The wine list looks incredible, but they have very few on the list that is actually in stock, and it took 3 bottles of wine (replaced) before they finally got a satisfactory one to the table, 1 was corked, 2nd was vinegar, and the 3rd one just seemed like table wine.

name: Hilton Charlotte Center City
title: “fantastic hotel”
text:
This was one of the best situated hotels in a city that I've ever experienced! Directly in the heart of downtown Charlotte with great walking access to almost any area you could desire.
Rooms were typical of a strong Hilton brand - clean, comfortable, quiet.

name: Hilton Charlotte Center City
title: “Loved It!”
text: One of my fav Hiltons so far. Loved the purple and yellow room decor. We had a larger room with a huge bathroom. Very clean, huge TV. We had room service for dinner and breakfast and it was the best food I've had at a Hilton yet. It was easy to get to, you got to pay for parking but that goes with being in a city. We went for a nice walk around town. Very professional staff. Only complaint is it was pricey but we got what we paid for.

name: Greektown Casino Hotel
title: “GREAT STAY”
text: Staff was friendly , very clean , great location. Cant wait to go back. It was a great get away with my wife. Casino was very very clean nice set up never felt like we were smothered by other people. Staff went out of there way to make us feel welcome. Games were great played all night.

name: Charlotte Marriott City Center
title: “Some Problems but OK overall”
text: Pulled up to the Valet at about 4PM Saturday to check in. Uniformed Valet asks "Are you Checking In and would you like to Valet your car?" I say yes to both questions. He then comes back to me and says the Valet is full and I will have to self park. First time I have ever encountered a Valet Parking being full. The garage he pointed me to was extremely filled and I was very fortunate to find a space (someone was leaving at that moment). There were 4 other cars looking for spots in a very congested parking garage. The gate entering and leaving the parking garage were permanently open but yet they charged me $12 per night to park. I could have said nothing at check in and parked for free. Room was OK, but the hallways and lobby are a little worn out. Restaurant Savannah Red was excellant with great service. The Breakfast Buffet the next morning was good also.

name: Greektown Casino Hotel
title: “Okay.”
text:
Well the rooms and the common spaces are gorgeous, but this hotel is not without its flaws.
Check-in was smooth, and the young woman behind the desk was friendly, the room was spotless and beautiful, and the hotel is convenient to everything downtown Detroit has to offer.
However, there were two major problems. 
1: Since the hotel is attached to a casino, the smell of cigarette smoke is unavoidable. As a non-smoker, I was pretty turned off.
2: I was on the 27th floor...and the windows were not properly sealed. There was a terrible draft (the temperature at night was in the low-30s) and I woke up with inflamed sinuses. I don't know if the windows in the other rooms are like this (I've stayed here before without incident), but this made for a very uncomfortable and chilly stay.
I'd stay here again, I suppose, but for business trips, I think I'd be better off in the suburbs.

name: The Westin Detroit Metropolitan Airport
title: “Great Hotel in addition to desirable location”
text: Normally I try not to expect much from airport hotels, but Westin Detroit Airport rivals hotels which have been destination onto themselves. Within most of the hotel is is hard to distinguish you are at the airport. We stayed there because we needed to be at the airport for a flight. The room was very comfortable and well-appointed. The lobby has one secluded sitting area where you could watch some of the planes pulling in/out of their gates. As a frequent traveler to/from Detroit airport, this is a wonderful lodging option.

name: The Atheneum
title: “ABSOLUTELY FANTASTIC - AGAIN!!!”
text: I love this hotel! Everyone from the front desk staff to housekeeping, to bellmen, to valet staff, to wait staff etc., etc., are cheeful, friendly, kind and professional! The rooms are incredibly large and comfortable and the location in Greektown can't be beat. This is my fifth or sixth stay at the Atheneum and I honestly can't imagine staying anywhere else!

name: MotorCity Casino Hotel
title: “Surprisingly nice Conference Location”
text: Upon arriving, I was a little concerned because in a residential area that doesn't have a lot to offer. Once I was inside, I had no reason to leave for my 3 day conference. The rooms are lovely and plush, with all the amenities you need. I was on the 7th floor and it was quiet. I enjoyed the bar up top which had a band and dance floor, good bartenders, fun surroundings and a great view of the skyline. As a conference center, very handy with the walk from rooms to education areas pretty easy, lots of eating options between sessions and good food served at the conference. The meeting rooms were all close and it was easy to navigate. The service from the bell staff, to front desk, to security to banquet servers to housekeepers was excellent and consistent. You could tell they were trained and motivated to customer service. Nice job. So I splurged for room service and ordered a pizza. My Little Caesars Pepporoni pizza came up piping hot and I swear the best I have ever had. The cheesecake was awesome too. I did not venture into the casino because of the busy conference schedule, but qutie a nice hotel and look forward to attending at least business functions in the future here again.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Detroit Downtown
title: “Great place to stay in Detroit”
text: This is a lovely hotel, great value for money in an excellent location in Downtown Detroit.

name: Detroit Marriott at the Renaissance Center
title: “A very nice stay”
text:
Hotel was quite nice, if occassionally obnoxious to get around. It's located directly in downtown Detroit which was excellent for accessing things (The people mover actually stops in the building) but also made parking quite expensive. Bed was lovely and soft, all of our special requests were met (extra feather pillows, high floor, early check in), and staff were generally very helpful and friendly. The one exception to this was issues with the valet/ parking staff when trying to check in and out.... there is no short term parking for check in. 
The room itself was well outfitted and quite comfortable. Tub could use updating but was adequate and everything was nice and clean. The view was fantastic and the floor to ceiling wall of windows creates a definite feel of luxury. Overall a great experience.

name: Holiday Inn Express Detroit - Downtown
title: “Good location in downtown Detroit”
text:
We stayed at the Holiday Inn Express for the 2010 Frozen Four. We paid a little more than we normally would have for a Holiday Inn, but since it was a special event weekend, this was to be expected and we were happy to be downtown and near the People Mover to get back and forth to the games. The Holiday Inn Express more than met our needs. We arrived early in the afternoon and our check-in went quickly. Our room was fairly spacious and although the hotel is listed as recently updated, did show some signs of age. The bedding and decor had been changed, but the carpet and paint could use a little updating of their own. The bed was surprisingly comfortable and we both slept well, which is unusual for us in a hotel. The breakfast was well-stocked and went quickly despite a packed hotel. The staff did an outstanding job of moving things along on all 3 mornings we were there. The valet parking was reasonably priced and very efficient, especially considering the crowd.
In short, if you're in town for an event and need a convenient place to sleep, the Holiday Inn Express would be a great choice for you.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Hotel Detroit-Dearborn
title: “Good choice”
text: I stayed here for one night for business in October 2011. My check in experience was seamless. The staff were professional, cordial and recognized me as a Hilton Honors member. My room was very spacious with a king bed. I did not hear any noise - either from other nearby guests or outside. The bed was very comfortable with quality linens. The meeting rooms were spacious and met our group's needs. I am staying here on my next business trip to the area. I highly recommend this hotel.

name: Hilton Charlotte Center City
title: “Valetparken freundlich, den Rest vergessen”
text:
Als Hilton Goldmitglied bekam ich nicht wie sonst ein Zimmer auf dem Exec Floor auch nach der Art des Zimmer fragte niemand, der Check in ist eine Frechheit arrogant und unfreundlich, es war mein drittes Hilten in einer Woche und das schlechteste. Die Menschen die dort arbeiteten gaben mir das Gefühl der völligen Gleichgültigkeit.
Die Zimmer sind eher kleiner aber ok, nichts besonderes, das Duschgel hat gefehlt, die Betten sind "Hiltonlike" sehr gut.

name: Arizona Biltmore
title: “Perfect service-Remarkable solitude and relaxation”
text:
I was looking for a quiet getaway. The Biltmore Resort and Spa provided just that within the confines of the "Occtilla". 
The room was quiet and adjoined by a semi-private pool. The room was elegantly furnished and left nothing to the imagination. Comfort, style, and elegance best describes the amenitites. 
Dining within the Biltmore was another treat. The waitstaff was friendly, knowledgable, and very courteous. John and Martin stand out.
Room service was very prompt, and unobtrusive.
The Biltmore sent me home relaxed, and more than wishing that I should have booked a longer stay.

name: MGM Grand Detroit
title: “One of the Best Hotels”
text: The MGM Detroit is perhaps one of the best hotels in the Midwest, and one of the top in the country. The typical guestrooms are spacious, well-appointed, extremely clean, and worth their cost. What really makes this hotel a gem is their top-notch staff who is quick to answer questions, help whenever and wherever possible, and extremely energetic. While at the hotel, individuals were always willing to ask if I needed assistance - evidence that the staff is willing to make the stay as enjoyable as possible. Yes the casino is a catch to staying here, but the hotel makes one want to return again.

name: Inn on Ferry Street
title: “Forgetful Staff”
text: My husband and I stayed here when I had an art opening. Beautiful buildings and easy to find. Our room wasn't much to speak of...more like a nice hotel room than the romantic B&B style as described to us. Small too. My husband had wanted to surprise me with their roses/chocolates/champaign, but the staff never put it in the room. There was a wedding party booked the same weekend and the guests were very loud, which would have been o.k. in a regular hotel, but in a 'house' it's annoying.

name: Holiday Inn Express Detroit - Downtown
title: “Great location if you are downtown”
text:
This hotel is a great location if you are attending events downtown. I attended the fireworks show and it was a quick 10 minute walk from the hotel down to Hart Plaza. 
The front desk staff and bell desk staff were excellent especially parking my car and dealing with all the cases and boxes I had for this trip.
Cookies were in my room when I arrived (unexpected surprise).
Rate for one night (06/27/06) was $141.45 and parking $17.00.
Highly recommended if you are in the downtown Detroit area.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Hotel Detroit-Dearborn
title: “Perfect Stay”
text:
The hotel is close to the highway and about 10 miles away from downtown. It is located in an area with another hotel, Chillis and Red Robin and therefore there is some security around which makes you feel safe. 
The hotel is huge and well equipment and the staff was very friendly. I even found an personal welcome note with my two bottles of water in my room plus chips and the delicious chocolate cookie. Everything was clean and it was quiet, too. If you do not mind the distance to downtown, it's a perfect stay.
Only the breakfast seemed to be overpriced, I checked it and decided not to go for it.

name: Westin Charlotte
title: “Luxury!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Westin for 2 nights in mid- Sept.
It was Heavenly! We stayed at the Holiday Inn the night before, only because the Westin was booked, and the Holiday Inn was mediocre at best. The Westin was glamourous! We loved the huge lobby with the river running through it. The staff was the best! We never opened a door, everyone greeted us, everyone was so full of personality and so friendly! We took advantage of the conceirge services and the lady was the most helpful. They have pre-printed directions which are so helpful and they have town cars waiting at the front door ready to wisk you away ( at a very reasonable rate too!) The best part had to be the room. The bed truely is Heavenly. It was so wonderful that I am buying their heavenly mattress out of their catalog so I can have the same mattress at home! The sheets, pillow, comforters were the softest feeling and as fluffy as clouds. I slept so well! The bathroom ws immaculate, how wonderful! They had dual shower heads and a real hair dryer. We did not get good cell phone reception inside the hotel, but all the other wonderful qualities made up for it! The location was great also! Right off 277 - very easy to find and easy to walk around downtown. We Loved it and can't wait to go back!!!

name: The Westin Detroit Metropolitan Airport
title: “Loved it - will stay again”
text:
Hotel is located at DTW - In McNamar terminal which is very convenient.
Used park and stay for early morning flight. Valet park and pick your car up when you return.
Room was beautiful and overlooked indoor court yard. 
Quiet even being at the airport.
Pool was awesome and empty so son had fun going from pool to jacuzzi.
Food was awesome. Room service was so fast.
All personnel were so accommodating and friendly.
Room was very clean and we loved the heavenly shower and pillow top beds.

name: The Westin Book Cadillac Detroit
title: “downtown detroit hotel”
text: Wedding venue, huge rooms, several great restaurants in hotel, excellent service

name: Drury Inn & Suites Indianapolis Northeast
title: “Great Value”
text: This hotel is great. Everyone is very friendly from the front desk to those serving food and drinks. This hotel does not have a bar but a 2 hour kickback is offered at the end of the day that includes hot snacks as well as beer & wine. They also have a fountain pop machine available most of the day and they serve a hot breakfast, not just some continental. The rooms are clean and spacious and the beds are comfortable. Can't say that about all hotels. Only recommendation I have is request a room on the east side of the building, someties I69 can be load on the west side. If you are staying in Northeast Indianapolis I would recommend staying here every time!

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Lovely!”
text:
Stayed here for 2 nights enroute back to the UK - cheaper for us to come back from Vegas through SFO than Vegas direct.
Lovely hotel with great staff. Room was fantastic - if you are travelling and packing space is at a premium then your room has L'Occitane products replenished daily of shampoo, conditioner, shower gel, body lotion and soap. There is also a supply of tissues, cotton wool and cotton buds and a hairdryer. We didn't take a key for the mini bar so don't know what that was like.
Our 2 nights made full use of the wine tasting which as another reviewer says makes a great group gathering and we got chatting to some lovely people including the Blue Angels as it was Fleet week!
Our only problem was eating in the Restaurant on our first night. Our waitress could not explain the menu to us - I wanted to know how the mussels were prepared and she didn't know! I ordered them and both starters came but half way through our starter, she came with our main meal! She was sent away but brought them as soon as our starter dishes were cleared! No rest in between! I asked for Salmon with veg and mash with the sauce on the side but it came with fries, veg and the sauce everywhere! She took it back and back it came again but they just scraped the sauce off and shoved on some fries and now the veg was cold! The waitress was told to take it away - by this point, I didn't want anything else to eat so didn't re-order. I was happily chatting to my husband whilst he ate his main meal only for the waitress to appear with the bill! No chance of dessert then!
I went through to Reception to ask them to get the manager for me. I explained all to him and he was very sympathetic and told me he'd take care of the bill. Next night when we came through for a drink he told us that the round was on him! Good customer service but it shouldn't have happened in the first place. Despite this, we ate breakfast there both days without any problems.
I really would recommend this Hotel to everyone.

name: Greektown Casino Hotel
title: “Dont forget anything including a key card.”
text: Don't go there if your last name is different than your husbands. While you can appreciate the discreation if you are entertaining/purchasing an escort. (Which is what they cater to apparently) My wife and I were on the last leg of our trip and booked there with 4 other couples convienent to Ford Field and atteneded the game. My wife went with her friends afterward forgot her rm key and was met with indifference, treated as if she were entreprenuer of the street walkers guild and denied access to our rm even though our addresses matched however our names did not. They wouldn't even let her get our vehicle that she possesed keys to. She then had to stay in one of our friends rooms. Their response was to dictate a policy that is not posted and to remind us that perhaps my wife could have been an unwanted guest to our room in case I was cheating on her. Yes we did pay 160.00 for the abillity to have our moral compass swayed if need be but not together. Policies need to be posted if resrictions apply. Stay at the Anthenium .Way better price, bigger rooms without the hassle and still nicely located to sporting events.

name: Drury Inn & Suites Indianapolis Northeast
title: “Great place to stay!”
text:
My husband and I spent a Saturday night at this Drury Inn. We have never stayed at a Drury Inn before - and we were very impressed! Check-in was quick and easy. Our room was very clean (and I am a "neat freak"!). The bathroom was spotless and had a terrific shower. We were out and about during the day on Saturday, visiting family. So, we didn't have the opportunity to enjoy the free evening food or drinks. But, we did go to the free breakfast. There were lots of choices - scrambled eggs, sausage, french toast, hot oatmeal, cold cereal, muffins, etc. Also, there were several stations for making your own waffles.
We will definitely return to this hotel!

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great location, but bring your earplugs....”
text:
We stayed at the Argonaut for a weekend in August 2007. We selected the Argonaut for its location right on the water in Fisherman's Wharf.
The hotel is in a great location -- it is on the edge of the Fisherman's Wharf area and it is close to cable car, streetcar and bus stops. Our room was large and very clean. The nautical decorations are tasteful.
The biggest problem that we had with this hotel was the thin walls. We heard our neighbor's television and laughter late into the night. Another issue that we had was with the bellhops. On Friday afternoon when we arrived, we wanted to take a cab. There were three parties waiting for a cab in front of the hotel, and the bellhop was having difficulty in finding cabs for us. Instead of calling a cab company to get some cabs or making some suggestions for public transportation, he told us to walk a few blocks south and we should have better luck finding a cab. It took us a sweaty half-hour to find a cab -- it was not a great way to start our trip! We relied solely on public transportation after that experience, however, and were fine.
Our room had a Golden Gate view. I would not recommend paying extra for the view. The weather was foggy in the morning, and the window is not conveniently located for enjoying the view while relaxing in the room. I don't think that you would miss anything by not having the view.
In short, the location and appearance of the hotel were excellent, but the thin walls and the lack of assistance with transportation will keep us from staying here in the future.

name: JW Marriott Indianapolis
title: “What you'd expect from a JW...”
text: I travel to Indy for business 2x a month and always stay at the JW. From the time I pull the rental car for valet to when I go to the front desk for my room, I am greeted by name or (at worst) "Glad to see you back, sir". This property and staff have it all - great rooms, great view, excellent location, awesome staff... I could go on and on; but this is what and why I am a loyal Marriott Rewards customer - for this type of experience! The HIgh Velocity sports bar is rivaled only by the in house 4 star restaurant (and breakfast is excellent, btw...). Nothing to complain about - oh, the bathrooms in room - excellent showers and amenities!

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Overpriced with tiny rooms”
text:
This hotel isn't worth the price. Rooms are very small, traffic is horrible, and service is poor. Beware the hotel room doors that open out into the hallway - we almost got smacked! We booked online, and paid extra ($449) to get a room that was supposed to have a Golden Gate Bridge view. We were very disappointed in the room, which was so narrow that only a small passage existed between the end of the bed & the wall. As for the "view", you could see a smidgen of the bridge, if you looked past the noisy street, through the trees, and if you leaned to the left and hunkered down a little. I looked at the
fire evacuation map on the back of the main door and saw that our room was one of the smallest on the floor. I went back to the front desk and asked the manager on duty if we could have a larger room or one with a view. He condescendingly explained that hotel rooms in big
cities like San Francisco tend to be smaller than rooms in places like Las Vegas. He ended up giving us a somewhat larger (but not spacious) room with a nice Alcatraz view. 
The hotel is centrally located at Fisherman's Wharf, but that means getting to and from the hotel is a nightmare of traffic snarls with the accompanying noise and pollution.
Valet parking was terrible, too. When I left our car with the valet,
I asked how long it would take to get it back. He said to call 5-10 minutes ahead. When we requested our car around 5 pm, it was a 20 minute wait.
We ordered room service breakfast, which arrived on time, but lacked presentation. The croissant was naked on a plate (no cover, no plastic wrap, just out in the open), and we got no jam, no butter, no glass of water, nothing.
The shower head is mounted terribly high on the wall. I'm 5'5", and could barely reach it. The shower curtain was mounted on a straight rod, and kept billowing in while I showered.

name: Inn on Ferry Street
title: “We LOVE the Inn on Ferry Street !!!”
text: We just did the 'Dining in Detroit' package for $305 for a King Suite and a 4 course meal and bottle of wine plus desert for two at the fabulous Whitney Restaurant. Our tab for dinner at the Whitney came to $195 - so our room only cost about $110 for the night. The Inn also gives free van service anywhere within a 5 mile radius so we took advantage of that to do some DUI free bar hopping downtown Detroit! As others have described, the Inn at Ferry Street is absolutely beautiful, the rooms are very nicely appointed and very clean, the service is great, the ambiance is better - what else can I say? Fantastic! When we returned from the bar, we grabbed two glasses of wine from the honor bar and sat outside in the courtyard gazebo and enjoyed a beautiful Michigan Spring night with the hustle and bustle sounds of the city as a backdrop. A must stay place for out of towners to really get the feel of Detroit, especially if they enjoy architectural gems.

name: Residence Inn Charlotte South at I-77/Tyvola Road
title: “Very nice stay”
text: We stayed at the Residence Inn Charlotte South at I-77/Tyvola Road for two days in October 2012. I recently had surgery on my foot, so we requested a handicap/accessible room. The room they gave us was very nice, clean, and (most importantly) easy for me to negotiate in my wheelchair. The bed was very comfortable, and the bathroom was large. The doorways were wide enough for my wheelchair to easily pass through. The staff were very nice and helpful, and the breakfast included eggs, bacon, sausage, etc., not just pastries as some hotel breakfasts do. The location was convenient, and there were several restaurants close by. The museums in downtown Charlotte were easily accessible from this hotel. I would recommend it.

name: Omni Severin Hotel
title: “Not Quite a 4-Diamond, but Okay and Good Location”
text:
I stayed there as part of a four-day conference. The actual conference was in the convention center. If you're booking a conference and plan on having your staff stay at the Severin, please note that it's about a 10 to 15 minute walk from the conference enter. Depending on the time of year, that could be a pretty uncomfortable journey.
The hotel is located across from Union Station, right downtown, near the RCA Dome and the new Lucas Oil Stadium. 
The lobby is very nice, with a reasonable restaurant that serves a good variety of food at the regular high hotel prices. There is a bar located just off the lobby as well. There is also a coffee shop just off the lobby that was a nice selection of items. There is no self parking for this hotel so be prepared to pay $25/night to valet park, or park a block or two away at a public garage.
The Indy downtown is great - clean - safe with lots of restaurants, bars, and a large mall. There are a number of major hotels downtown, including Marriott, Hilton and Hyatt.
The room was average sized with a comfortable bed, an average bathroom, a desk area, and a couch chair. It includes a ironing board and coffee maker. It does not include a safe.
The bathroom was average - not updated, but clean. Little shelf space and a toilet that required two or three flushes to "do its job" despite seemingly sending hundreds of gallons of water swooshing down the pipes. The shower was older, without the new curved rods that give you more head room. There was some mold in the tile.
The carpet was a bit worn, had some wrinkles in it, and the chair cushion was a bit torn and faded. The alarm clock was an older model that used colored buttons to indicate buzzer or radio rather than the newer LCD radios. But it worked fine.
The hotel is fairly quiet without a lot of street noise and you don't really hear people walking around much. Oddly, there was a recurring whining sound from the elevator mechanism. I say that it was odd because I was located a good 10 or 12 rooms away from the elevator. But I guess the elevator is mounted in a way that it resonates sound across many rooms. Also, the A/C unit performed well, but was very loud, and would turn on with a loud "clunk!".
There is wireless Internet for $9.95/day - but if you join the Omni Frequent Points program, it's free - and it's a good, fast connection.
The staff is helpful and friendly - no issues there. House cleaning did a good job, but they didn't usually get to the rooms until later in the day.
As noted in a previous review, there are two elevators and if you try to head up or down during a busy time, prepare to wait a while for one. The 13th floor is labeled PH for Penthouse, but according to one person staying on that floor, it's no different than other floors.
In general, an adequate hotel that's clean, but a bit long in the tooth. It's a solid 3 diamond hotel.

name: The Westin Book Cadillac Detroit
title: “great hotel”
text: stayed here this weekend for U of M and Lions game, hotel is fantastic. Watching all of the valets literally sprint from the hotel to the parking garage to retrieve cars as quick as possible is refreshing. staff and hotel are great

name: Residence Inn Charlotte South at I-77/Tyvola Road
title: “Would Highly recommend”
text: Me and my family stayed there last year when we visisted Carowinds and this is one of the best kept hotels that I have stayed in........... The rooms were well cleaned, comfy beds, descent kitchen to cook in and most of all the rooms we very cool which me and my niece loved. because walking around Carowinds park all day and coming back to the room made us feel much better. A big hi5 to your attendants that help keep your establishment well kept.

name: Residence Inn Charlotte South at I-77/Tyvola Road
title: “Relaxing Family atmosphere”
text:
I stay at this hotel at least 6 times a year, Every time I stay I'm greeted with warmest smile and hugs. The rooms are always clean and quiet. The kitchen staff make the most delicious food from their small kitchen. Breakfast is always satisfying and if you're in town for the evening social hours...try their BBQ sandwiches.
Any request I've made is met with a smile and prompt response and the staff is knowledgeable of the local area. They have made great suggestions for dining and entertainment options.
This R.I. truly feels like a home away from home.

name: Omni Severin Hotel
title: “over priced, over rated, over rude”
text: We stayed for two days. Found that the bed linens were not changed from the previous guests, but the bed was made. Floors were need of vacuuming. The breakfast buffet was over priced, and the staff was very rude. For the price not what I expected.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Hotel Detroit-Dearborn
title: “A1 service”
text:
I cannot say enough about the service that I get at this unassuming hotel. Detroit/Dearborn Doubletree is a midsize hotel about 10 mins away from Detroit. It is across from the Ford Dearborn campus. The grounds are well kept, very secure with the security guard circling the grounds every few minutes or so. The interior of the hotel is not flashy, clean and well kept.
I am at this hotel on a weekly basis and I would say that I am very qualified and in a great position to rate the service that I receive at this hotel. I have also witnessed the same excellence in the service shown to all guests.
The staff at this hotel will go beyond the call of duty. I was very sick a couple of weeks ago, and the restaurant staff had prepared chicken noodle soup for me. There was also another time when a staff member went out of his way to run an errand.
Every check-in is greeted with a smile, and of course a warm cookie!. On Mondays, during check in time, the manager is usually there to greet the weary travelers. The same service excellence is noted even though the hotel maybe sold out during the spring season when the Detroit Lions players are there or when the hotel is swarmed by peewee hockey players.
The hotel also has the best taxi service available to their clients, which is at a very reasonable rate. Sam and his sidekick, Ali have always been extremely reliable and are always there at the beck and call of the hotel.
There are other hotels in the immediate area, but the service that I get at this hotel is unbeatable. I would not trade this for a spiffier room. This is home away from home for me.

name: The Westin Detroit Metropolitan Airport
title: “It's the place to stay when flying from/to Detroit”
text: Convenient, some rates include 10 days parking, valet service, wonderful beds, decor, terriffic staff. Only one complaint - it is very dry in the room. Solved that by filling bathtub with water in the evening.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Charlotte Airport South
title: “Great Place”
text: Best La Quinta we have stayed at. Very safe neighborhood, big rooms and nice staff. Definitely will stay again when traveling to Florida. Great to find a pet friendly hotel with such great rooms. The only downside was the heating system was noisy.

name: Homewood Suites Charlotte/Ayrsley
title: “Wonderful stay”
text: We came to the Homewood suites for a whirlwind weekend wedding and were delighted by the hotel and the service we received. The rooms were beautiful, clean and well equipped, AND they had fully stocked kitchens which was awesome. The even better part was the complimentary cocktail hour with Chef Matt, and complimentary dinner and breakfast provided by the hotel. Overall it was a wonderful stay for a reasonable price. STAY HERE! You will not be disappointed!

name: Arizona Biltmore
title: “Enjoyed the Biltmore”
text: My husband and I just spent a week at the Biltmore, staying in room 3313 in the Valley Wing, a nice large, well kept room,overlooking a smaller pool, for a $265 convention rate.( The third floor rooms have no balconies.) We were prepared for the extra charges and all billing was correct. The hotel is an architectural delight - the grounds lovely - most of the staff are more than pleasant. I took the gratis architectural tour of the hotel and grounds and it was extremely well done, done by Nathan, the lead concierge and 13 year employee . ( I tipped him $10, but he did not have his hand out...) The front desk clerk felt a bit defensive when we registered, but calmed down when I was reasonable about room questions. Apparently many of the rooms are so different in size, ammendities, that it is probably a real set up for confusion/disappointment. It is also a very large hotel,( like sister property, Grand Waliea) so must need to have conventions to be profitable. We really loved the Wright's restaurant; grill and pool cafes were also good. Our maid did a great job, so I hope she got the extra we were charged each day.( I left more...) Attention to detail: our heat wasn't functioning and it was dealt with very quickly by two pleasant fellows. We were given a late check out at 2pm with no extra charges. They let us park our rented motorcycle in the valet lot. ( self parking is a a pain, as mentioned earlier by others) The carpeting in the room had a few spots, but it took me two days to notice...sheets, towels, robes were excellent and i loved the desert flower shampoo etc. Occasionally there was uncaring, lackluster service, but it was the exception, not the rule. (Phoenix has really low unemployment.)The pool outside our windown was pretty noisy one day with high energy team building stuff....so was glad I was not napping! Concierge staff were great - helping us get to the wonderous Barrio Cafe, Le Grande Orange Grocery, and Desert Botanical Garden. Also loved the area of the Biltmore - there were actually mature neighborhood trees being nurtured! All in all, the Biltmore made giant, overbuilding Phoenix a good place to visit. It's expensive, but then it is an iconic property with its Frank Lloyd Wright influences and interesting history.

name: The Westin Detroit Metropolitan Airport
title: “Overnight Delay at DTW wound up being a Delight”
text: Equipment delays by the airline caused me to miss my connecting flight. Though I was given a voucher for another hotel, I chose the convenience of the Westin DTW Airport. I was pretty grumpy about missing my flight, but the hotel experience made the delay a delight. The staff at check-in was friendly and helpful. The hotel lobby was gorgeous and my room incredibly nice and comfortable. And quiet - no evidence that the hotel is in the middle of a major airport. While the quality of the food at the bar was only so-so, the service was quick and friendly. The next morning, I got up, checked out easily and was on my way to my destination through the hotel-only airport security line.

name: Renaissance Charlotte Suites
title: “Great hotel suites and restaurant!”
text: We went to Carowinds (this hotel is 10 min. away) and decided to stay here. It looks like an Embassy suites, so nothing like a typical Renaissance. The breakfast buffet is great, and includes waffles and omelets to order for $14. The bar is next to check in, so it's not in a private area, which disappointed me. The photos do not depict the hotel decor and set up, but it was fine. I have really high standards, and was a tad disappointed with the beds (hard!), and the room could use some repairs (bathroom ceiling suffered water damage, maybe?). But the staff was great, and the food at dinner was SO good! I had the porkchops, and they were definitely prepared by a good chef. My husband had the short ribs, and he said they were really good and tender. We had the hummus which was homemade and the calamari appetizers, and both were great. I only speak of this in the review because oftentimes hotel restaurants tend to let me down, but this one stood up to my challenge! I will definitely stay here again, as the suites were awesome for our kids-one is a teen and the other is 6.

name: Arizona Biltmore
title: “Glad I Wasn't Paying For It”
text:
My stay was on someone else's dime; I was here for a conference in April. Landscape is very appealing. Loved the chairs scattered about. The main pool is fair. It was difficult to find empty pool lounge chairs. Enjoyed the salsa-making demo in the pool area. The resort has many activities scheduled, but no one tells you about them! We found out about them on our last day there.. what a waste. I think the rooms are overpriced if they're in the high $200s per night. 
Don't bother eating at the bistro. The meal was mediocre, and the service was horrible. We stood at the door for more than 5 minutes before anyone greeted us, then we waited another 5 minutes before a table was cleaned (there were many dirty tables).

name: Arizona Biltmore
title: “something missing in a Resort”
text:
took mom after a cancer treatment to relax. 
I experienced alot of staff wanting to enter the room at random times during our stay. One was the day of our checkout at 9am while we were eating breakfast. The staff opened the door and wanted to know when we were going to checkout then left.
I also realized when I got home that one of the sale robes that I got from dillards was not in my suitcase. I called the resort within 5 hours and was told by security that no one has checked into the room and they would look for the robe. they returned saying that it was not in lost and found or in the room when they checked.
Every year mom and I go to local resorts in Arizona because of the discounts in the summer. I would have a very difficult time getting mom to go back to this place because of the inability to trust the staff. 
I believe this place to be very beautiful and it is, but this is a resort and 
my 75% $10.00 shower robe should not have been that much of a valuable item to not offer to replace; it still had the tags on it. (went and got another one the next day)
should you give this place another chance....yes... since our stay in the summer of 2004 I understand that it is now under new management. Employee honesty is something earned with time and hard to find. If you stay here you will enjoy the events and some wonderful staff BUT make sure you keep an eye on your valuable and not so valuable things. And remember to take everything with you!!!

name: Arizona Biltmore
title: “Not as nice as expected”
text: Not as nice as expected. Hard to find room/cottage - terrible directions from staff, did not help me with my bags. Roaches in bathroom - I know its the desert, but yuck!

name: The Westin Book Cadillac Detroit
title: “Downtown Detroit's best hotel has some issues to address”
text:
I recently stayed at the Westin Book Cadillac for a night when I was in Detroit.
I have wanted to stay there since the hotel was re-opened last year, but hadn’t had a real chance until now. (In the past, I’ve often stayed at the Westin in Southfield, which is considerably cheaper though isn’t in a great location for downtown business travelers.)
The Westin Book Cadillac is probably the best non-casino hotel in downtown Detroit. The only real non-casino competition comes from the Marriott Renaissance Center. 
The location is superb for anyone with a reason to be downtown. While Detroit is steadily improving, there are still drawbacks with being downtown. Namely, the lack of any real shopping -- you’ve got to head out to the suburbs. And what is downtown -- with the exception of Greektown and the bars -- closes around 5 o’clock when the workers start leaving for the suburbs. Nevertheless, I spent several hours walking around the vicinity of the hotel, taking in the sights, the architecture and the feel of a large city. I’ve been to Detroit a lot in the past, but never as a tourist. This was eye-opening, as you could really spend a day taking in the museums (namely the Detroit Institute of Arts) and the sights of Detroit. Still Detroit does have downsides and unfortunately you always have to be keep your guard up, especially when walking around at night or walking back to the hotel from a sporting event. 
But back to hotel itself.
The Westin Book Cadillac is what you would expect. There’s valet parking, a concierge, several restaurants, a wonderful spa, a gift shop, ballrooms, room service, a pool, fitness center and more. The offerings are what you would expect for a hotel of this class. Speaking of parking, I would avoid the valet parking and use the public parking garage around the corner (it’s where they valet park). You’ll save money and won’t have to worry about the hassle of valet. 
The rooms are contemporary, rather spacious -- especially the bathrooms (I’ve stayed in rooms the size of my bathroom while in Europe) and feature an amazing large, flat-screen television. The beds were comfortable. The public spaces are a mixture of classic and contemporary designs, are well lit and very clean. I encountered many staff members, who warmly greeted me with a “hello" when passing. 
I did find some of the service and offerings to be substandard for this class of hotel. For starters, the internet is rather expensive -- it should be free -- and business center isn’t complimentary. Also, the check-in wasn’t what I expected. The front desk clerk didn’t welcome me to the hotel or even say “hello.” She asked for my last name and credit card and then proceeded to give me my room key before telling me where the elevators were located. I also asked the concierge for a walking map of the area, which she provided though I thought she might follow-up with a logical question about what I wanted to see or do. In past experience, a good concierge will ask guests if there is anything in particular they want to see or do. 
Upon entering my room, I went to take a bath and discovered a large amount of body hair, including what appeared to be pubic hair, on the bathroom floor. I called down to the front desk and asked for the manager-on-duty. He immediately offered me a new room and within about 15 minutes I was moved to a slightly larger room down the hall. A couple of hours later, I returned to my new room and found a bottle of wine, sparkling water and a plate of fruit with a handwritten note from the manager-on-duty. This was very considerate of him. He told me to contact him if there was anything else he could do. So I took him up on his offer and asked him to take care of a spa service I used. (I went there after not having taken the bath I wanted.) I assume the manager took care of this, though I never heard back from him despite me sending a follow-up e-mail message. 
I was also a little disappointed with the complimentary toiletries. While I understand the hotel had several available upon request, a hotel of this class should offer more than hand lotion, shampoo and conditioner in each room. For a hotel such as the Westin Book Cadillac, I would expect a shoe mint, mouthwash and maybe a sewing kit. I also read the in-room directory and saw a complimentary turndown service, but this wasn’t until 10 o’clock at night. I doubt few guests know of this, and it should be a standard offering. I was also surprised there wasn’t a telephone directory or a Bible in the nightstand. I think this is the first hotel without a Bible that I have ever stayed at. Other downsides were a lack of towels (only two small towels and two medium size towels are provided), which is an issue if you’re traveling with a spouse and a kid. There was also only one bathrobe, which doesn’t make sense if there’s two guests in the room. 
My biggest disappointment was the horrible service at 24 Grille, where I ate dinner. I had a wonderful meal -- the food was amazing, but the service was horrendous. After being seated, I waited 10 minutes for my waiter to come over while other tables -- seated after me -- were immediately served by their waiter. I can only assume this is because I was alone and the waiter didn’t think he would get a big tip from a lone diner. 
After ordering a starter and an entrée, I never saw my waiter again until I asked for the bill. He never asked how my meal was or if I needed anything else. To the restaurant’s credit, the young gentleman serving water was very nice and kept coming over to refill my glass. I also waited approximately 15 minutes for my entrée to be brought over. I know it’s difficult to time to service of multiple courses to the exact moment, but this is an unusually large gap -- especially when the waiter never came a single time to ask if I wanted more dinner bread or a glass of wine to pass the time. The service was really disappointing because Grill 24 is rather expensive even by hotel standards. (The other restaurant is more up-market and even more expensive.) 
In all, the Westin Book Cadillac is fine hotel with a few issues to address. If management is reading this, the lack of complimentary internet is probably No. 1 on my list of complaints -- outside of the lousy restaurant service. The lack of toiletries, the low number of towels or the lack of a second bathrobe can all be easily remedied. 
If you’re going to be in downtown Detroit, there’s no better choice than the Westin Book Cadillac. 
However, those who find themselves in the suburbs shopping -- or those on a budget -- may want to consider the Westin in Southfield. It’s in an excellent neutral location for those wanting to shop at both Somerset in Troy or Twelve Oaks in Novi, while also visiting Detroit for sporting or entertainment events. And it offers many of the same services and amenities as the Westin Book Cadillac without the high price.

name: Drury Inn & Suites Charlotte North
title: “Wonderful stay. Would certainly recommend”
text:
I wanted to check out local apartments in the area as I am going to move to Charlotte soon. This hotel is comfortably located nearby several apartment communities. So, that was a bug plus for me. The cleanliness was impressive in the room. I stayed there for just one night, but was able to enjoy their evening kickback breakfast. But needless to say, their morning breakfast was the highlight. Various selections were available. The staff serving the guests had all smiling faces. Hotel Manager personally came to each and every table and asked if the guests liked the breakfast and their stay.
Overall, a pleasant stay and would certainly recommend to anyone.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Hotel Detroit-Dearborn
title: “Best staff. Best service.”
text:
I have stayed at this particular Doubletree 5 times in the last 6 years. Everytime I notice the high quality of the staff. They are always friendly, accomodating and helpful. The hotel is clean with a very nice lobby. The restaurant is good and there are several places to eat nearby.
The security is excellent. On my last visit, my 4 year daughter had an accident and required medical attention. The security staff were very responsive. They gave me written directions to the nearby hospital and checked on us when we returned. The hotel contacted me a week later just to see if she was OK.
Overall a great staff at a great hotel. If you can't decide where to stay in the area, this is the place!

name: Renaissance Charlotte SouthPark Hotel
title: “Great hotel with excellent service”
text: My husband and I stayed one Sat night just for a night away. I had previously stayed here on business (the room and the service was great then but the hotel was under renovation at the time). I was very impressed by the results of the renovation in the lobby, restaurant, etc. The staff was very kind and helpful. The room is as nice as you expect with a Renaissance. Free parking is available in a parking garage connected to the hotel (valet parking for a fee is also available). The hotel is within walking distance to a number of restaurants in Piedmont Row (you could also walk if you needed to the Southpark Mall but you'd have to cross a pretty busy road). We enjoyed our short getaway and will return again next time we're in the area.

name: Drury Inn & Suites Charlotte North
title: “Nice on Drury!”
text:
We stayed here on the first and last nights of a visit to see our grand-daughther! The rooms were excellent and it was a nice place to "recover" from the flight and prepare for leaving!
The staff were excellent - my wife's bag was delayed and the staff looked after it while we were out at dinner. Also our flight from Charlotte was later in the day and they let us stay around for a while which really helped out!
Zapata's mexican restaurant is a fave from when we lived in Charlotte (just across the road, also there is a nice walk round the lake.

name: The Westin Detroit Metropolitan Airport
title: “Love it”
text:
I always stay at the airport before flying on a trip/vacation.
I live about an hour or so from the airport, so it's nice for the early flights.
I always book a 4 star hotel on Hotwire.com and the only 4 star in the DTW vicinity is the Westin. I usually get it for half price or better. The hotel itself is very limited in terms of having convenient amenities, but I usually get there late and just crash before my flight. The beds are comfortable, and I always sleep great. You barely hear airport traffic or other sounds from within the terminal. 
Always a good experience.

name: The Ritz-Carlton, Charlotte
title: “This was the best hotel/experience we have ever had!”
text:
We travel a lot and in our opinion this was our favorite place to stay of all time. We got a parlor suite, at around $600 a night, however you get what you pay for!! The rooms are a great size, master bath very nice. The bed, sheets, pillows first class all the way...best night sleep in a hotel ever. Will probably start using the Ritz for our hotel rooms now, because of this experience
Thank you

name: The Westin Book Cadillac Detroit
title: “BEST HOTEL FOR HUNDREDS OF MILES”
text:
This, by far, blows any other Detroit hotel out of the water. Impeccable service, amazing historic building, wonderful views. I originally booked my stay at a different hotel - which ended up being a HUGE disaster. The Westin was so gracious and even upgraded my room to try and make my stay in Detroit as pleasant as possible. I simply can't say enough about this place. I think the staff made all the difference. I also hear it's the only hotel in Detroit with a door man and 24hr valet service.
A+++
The only place I will ever stay when in Detroit.

Address: '530 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd'
name: Hampton Inn Charlotte - Uptown
title: “The Best Hampton We've ever stayed in!”
text: From parking to check in everything was great. Roon clean, 1st class. Shuttle available to take you to over 40 places to eat, Service Just Top Notch. Front desk crew couldn't have been nicer.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Hotel Detroit-Dearborn
title: “Sehr gut”
text: Dies ist das zweite Mal, dass ich in die Doubletree by Hilton stayd in Detroit-Dearborn. Der Service war ebenso hervorragend wie die erste Zeit. Das Zimmer ist gut und sauber. Schade, dass die Nachbarschaft ziemlich schlecht ist, nur an der Autobahn und in einem viel weniger als eindrucksvoller Lage. Das Hotel ist zwar ganz nett, ich glaube, es ist ein wenig überteuert.

name: Hampton Inn and Suites Charlotte Airport
title: “Great Park n Fly”
text:
This is an excellent choice for your park n fly in Charlotte. Clean, roomy, friendly, and prompt shuttle to the airport which is only about a mile away. Beds are very comfy, really nice big shower, and everything you could need including a microwave and fridge. Great breakfast included and they will even provide to - go bags. Leave your car and get shuttled right to you check in counter...perfect. Also, prompt pick up. They even provided much needed water bottles when they picked us up.
Tip...not a lot of restaurants nearby, but what they don't tell you is there's a restaurant in the Holiday Inn next door. You can walk to it and have a decent meal and drinks.

name: The Ritz-Carlton, Charlotte
title: “More Boutique Feel than Ritz”
text:
This hotel reminds me more of a Boutique Hotel than a Ritz. It's VERY nice with a great indoor pool which is needed for the EXTREME temp shifts. Plus GREAT pool food service.
Rooms very comfortable, roomier than most Ritz Carlton rooms in Big cities. Very well thought out rooms which makes the rooms perfect. They have drawers for unpacking...something that to many hotels have stopped doing.
Not specific to the Ritz Charlotte, more to downtown Charlotte---they need to get later hours on nights of special events. When a Coldplay concert let out at 11PM most restaurants were closed,or closing. NOT good for downtown Charlotte guests.
Special NOTE of thanks to guest services manager, Christian Jaquier, he makes hospitality perfect!

name: Hyatt Place Charlotte Airport/Tyvola Road
title: “Great Hotel - Great Staff”
text:
I booked this hotel for one night just because it was cheap. I was really surprised at how big the room was and how nice it was. The staff was excellent and went way out of their way to be helpful. I will be staying at Hyatt Place hotels in the future!!
The only negative was the bathroom tile floor was cracked and broken and had caulking that needed to be replaced.

name: Aloft Charlotte Ballantyne
title: “Very fun weekend at Aloft!”
text:
I found a great deal on this hotel online (40% off second night), and I had wanted to try out this hotel because of its contemporary design. My friend and I went to Charlotte for a Girls' Weekend. This place ended up being a perfect fit for us. We both loved the design of the hotel. Clean lines, modern look, etc. 
Hugh at the front desk was very friendly and helpful and went out of his way to help us find a karaoke bar. The linens were nice, especially the fluffy towels. The hotel was having a "Spring Fling" Party the night we checked in, so it was fun to have a party atmosphere with live music, lots of people, etc. They even had a photo booth set up with props, so we got to take some funny pictures, which was fun. 
We also like the fact that the hotel was close to a lot of shopping and restaurants.
The negatives for us were: No free breakfast. They do have a few items for sale near the front desk, but not much selection and overpriced. The shower was low-pressure, so I didn't feel "clean" afterwards. My bed was on the hard side, but my friend said hers was fine, so it could just be I'm used to sleeping on a softer bed. 
This would not be the type of place I would go with my family of 5, but for a Girls' Weekend it was perfect. I would definitely stay again.

Address: '530 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd'
name: Hampton Inn Charlotte - Uptown
title: “Hamton inn einfach super”
text:
Wir waren vier tage in diesem hotel,sehr sauber freundlich und die haben super betten,und tolle bettwäsche.sehr freundliches personal.
immer wieder.sauberes badezimmer und handtücher.toles personal hat uns die koffer ausgeladen und ins zimmer bebracht,hat geholfen für restaurants und stadtkarte.
bei fragen sofort da und geholfen.

name: Dunhill Hotel
title: “A warm and wonderful place.”
text: The Dunhill Hotel, was the friendliest and warmist hotel i've ever stayed in. The staff were fantastic, they talked to you like friends rather than guests. With warmth and interest. I wouldn't stay anywhere else. It was a home away from home, but without all the work. Very personnal and lovely.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “No Disappointments Here!!!”
text:
This was our fourth and last hotel of an 8 day trip and it was the best. Everything was absolutely perfect. They offer complimentary wine in the beautiful lobby from 5-6 each evening, the location is great and the rooms are lovely. The entire staff was most attentive and everything went smoothly. Not only would we stay there again, we had not heard of Kimpton Hotels (which they are a part of) and so we
would definitely consider trying some of the other hotels they own -- which are supposedly all unique.

name: Super 8 Meacham / North Fort Worth
title: “Nice place to stay”
text:
Hotel was clean, staff pleasant and helpful. Bed was kinda hard. Nice quiet location. We checked out intending to move on but after a day of site seeing, we decided to stay one more night. Very accommodating, they even gave us our same room.
I will say the walls are pretty thin. Lots of noise and some sort of banshie type wailing a couple of times during our second night. First night was quiet.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Fort Worth Downtown/Blackstone
title: “Perfect location, helpful staff!”
text: I stayed at the Courtyard Marriott to host a friend's party after my home became unavailable at the last minute. They were able to reserve me a room with a great view and the location couldn't have been better! The staff was also very friendly and helpful, loaning us supplies to help set up for the party. Couldn't have asked for a better experience. Hotel is currently under construction but it's obviously they've made great efforts to ensure cleanliness is still a priority.

name: The Ballantyne Hotel and Lodge
title: “Nice resort, close to great shopping”
text:
The Ballantyne Hotel & Lodge Charlotte, North Carolina
http://www.theballantynehotel.com/ 
The Ballantyne Hotel & Lodge (one of Starwood Luxury Collection) is located just 20 minutes from Charlotte-Douglas Airport and downtown Charlotte. This place is an ideal venue for meetings, weddings and social occasions. 
The hotel includes an 18-hole golf course, Gallery Restaurant and Spa, complete with a fitness facility with personal training classes and indoor and outdoor pools. The hotel also offers wine tastings of the finest wines bi-monthly on Saturdays at 6pm throughout the summer in Gallery Bar.
The hotel is within 18 miles of downtown Charlotte and the SouthPark Mall (my favourite shopping place) featuring Neiman Marcus, Tiffany, Nordstrom, etc.

name: Hampton Inn and Suites Charlotte Airport
title: “Wonderful Wedding Night”
text: My wife and I stayed here on our wedding night because they offered the opportunity for us to leave our car there while we were on our honeymoon. First off, our first impression was "This place is awesome!" Check in was very quick and our room was much better than we had anticipated. Everything was great, the bed, bath, television, all of it. At first we noticed the sounds of the planes leaving the airport but soon neither of us were aware of the fly overs. The next morning we had breakfast and both of us were full by the time we left to catch our plane. The shuttle to the airport was nice and quick, much faster than trying to drive there ourselves. When we arrived back from our Honeymoon all we had to do is call Hampton and they picked us up, drove us back to our car, and we were back to reality. Our car was safe while we were away, this is a wonderful service to utilize if you are flying out of Charlotte. We have already decided that if we are ever flying out of Charlotte again this will be the only place we'll stay.

name: Dalworth Inn
title: “Don't Stay Here!!”
text:
This place is DISCUSTING!! Live and dead bugs in your room. Dirty linens. Sticky carpet. Broken furniture. Ripped shower curtain. Broken and filthy air conditioner. 
If I hadn't been desperate for a place to stay at 2:00am I would have checked out as soon as I walked in!!! 
I didn't sleep much because I kept jumping out of bed because I kept feeling things crawling on me. I checked in at about 2am and I set my alarm for 5:00am to get the hell out of there!! 
I didn't even go anywhere eles in the motel, I was too scared to find out what eles I might see at the Motel Hell!
DONT STAY HERE!!!

name: Days Inn Fort Worth West
title: “Share a room with crickets”
text: I know it's not all the motel's fault, but we recently stayed at this location and were overrun by crickets. I am not kidding but the crickets are of plague proportions right out of the Bible. We killed at least 35 in our room and they kept coming. Also, I guess the housekeeper must of thought we were hungry as they left some leftover potato chip crumbs all over the floor. I know I'm trying to be funny, but in all seriousness this was one of the worst motels I've ever stayed at. Our wakeup call was about 15 minutes late. The shower did not work properly either. Also, I've stayed in smoking rooms before (all was available for our stay), but this one smelled like a tobacco barn. I've stayed at hundreds of cheap motels over the years and certainly do not have the highest of standards, but this was terrible. We will definitely find another motel to stay at in Ft. Worth on our next visit. You should too.

name: Sheraton Fort Worth Hotel and Spa
title: “Outstanding Service Sheraton Fort Worth”
text: I stayed at this Sheraton for a business meeting June 18-23, 2012 and the service was outstanding! I especially want to mention Charles Hequet from the restaurant/lounge. Charles took care of our entire team of folks daily and always had smile and friendly word for us. He is a wonderful representative for Sheraton!

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Fantastic”
text: This Hotel was fantastic, we had a room with a view of Alcatraz. The beds were comfortable and everything was very well presented. Would definatly go back again.

name: BEST WESTERN Inn Fort Worth
title: “Nothing Special, But Clean And Comfortable.”
text: This is our second stay here, mainly because it is close to our son's house. This is a run of the mill average motel, with nothing special. The rooms are clean, the staff is friendly, the breakfasts are adequate. If you want the Ritz, this is not it, but if you just need a clean place for a night or two, this place will work well. I will say that on both of our stays, there have been mechanical issues with either the air conditioner ( on our first stay ) or the ice machines. There was only one ice machine in service for the entire motel. Needless to say, there was very little ice available.

name: Residence Inn Fort Worth University Drive/River Plaza
title: “good location, dated but spacious suites”
text:
I stayed here one night with my four kids ages 8-14 for an academic competition at TCU. Having read the negative reviews on TA, I was nervous about what our 2 bedroom suite would be like, but our rooms were fine--not as nice as most Residence Inns we have stayed at, but not the worst. Carpets are a bit worn, furnishings are a bit dated, but there is plenty of space, and everything was clean. Having 2 bathrooms is great, counter space was fine, having a desk in the master bedroom was nice. We did not use the kitchenette, but we enjoyed using the table for board games. The TV was fine, and my 14 year old slept well on the sleeper sofa. Beds were comfortable, and we all slept from about 1030pm-830am. We had requested a quiet room, and were given an upstairs suite by the river path-no one heard any street noise. The free WiFi worked well. Fitness center is small, but we didn't need it.
 Service at check-in was friendly & quick. Basketballs are available to check out. Breakfast was nice, about average for Residence Inn, and better than most places-hot eggs, spicy potatoes with onions, sausage, tortillas, Canadian bacon, bacon, pancakes, and oatmeal were available along with the usual cold cereal, yogurt, continental items. There were fresh blueberries, strawberry sauce, chocolate chips, and pecans along with the usual pancake/oatmeal toppings, plus two types of salsa & cheese for the eggs. There was plenty of space to eat.
 Price was reasonable for a good location in a major city. This location was cheaper than the cultural district one, plus we needed the sleeper sofa. The drive to TCU was very short, and the zoo was a short walk away. We ate a nice dinner at Blue Mesa Grill just across the street, and there were several other nonchain restaurants. We ate lunch at Panera, also across the street. The Stockyards were a 12 minute drive away, so we visited them before the competition. We would stay here again if we need to visit TCU.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Ft. Worth Burleson
title: “Good average stay, but not much more.”
text:
We have stayed here a few times in last four years, and twice recently.
Location is a block from freeway and convenient to a huge number of well known stores and restaurants. This Hampton is about 4 yrs old and is in good to average condition for that age. Some noise thru walls/floor from others walking/stomping in adjacent rooms.
Breakfast juices were tasteless and watered down on our last 2 visits. Our room's toilet had a very noisy internal leak/drip due to a worn flapper valve & its internal pull chain fell off inside the tank when we jiggled it to try to stop the dripping noises.

name: Microtel Inn & Suites by Wyndham Ft. Worth North/At Fossil Creek
title: “Good time”
text: Very nice and clean room. The service is very good. Got a great night sleep thank you again. The rooms where very clean and the bed was very restful. The staff was very helpful in telling and finding restuarents.

name: Drury Inn & Suites Charlotte Northlake
title: “Immaculate”
text: This is the top-rated hotel in Charlotte for a reason. Clean! Super friendly! Airy! Comfortable! Light! The staff was so helpful, the food so good. When I go back to Charlotte, it will be to stay here.

name: Hotel Trinity InnSuites Fort Worth / DFW
title: “Stay Away! Never Again!”
text: Front desk staff was rude. Made me wait until she finished counting change for the shift change. Room was not ready and when the call came to tell her the room was ready she didn't answer the phone (multi-tasking is not her thing). The hotel room (all suites) is an old Ramada with some new paint and carpet. The rooms were stale, baseboards pulling away from the wall and two buttons were missing for the in-room jacuzzi. There was broken glass in the parking lot, looked like it came from a car window, on the day we arrived and still was there when we left. We didn't go the happy hour but did go to the breakfast buffet. My wife loves fruit and it was mentioned on the motels website - the fruit was fruit loops and cut up oranges. We were so glad we only booked the room for one night. Never again!

name: Country Inn & Suites Fort Worth
title: “Ideal location for visiting the Fort Worth Stockyards”
text: We arrived into DFW, picked up a hire car and drove straight to the hotel - not at all difficult to locate even in the dark and after a long flight from LHR. Made to feel very welcome. Great room with two queen beds, quiet and comfortable. Excellent complimentary breakfast. Only a few minutes drive to the Stockyards where there's easy parking - we of course went to see the cattle drive - then in the evening we used the free shuttle bus to and from Billy Bob's Texas, an excellent service. We wouldn't hesitate to return to this hotel.

name: Staybridge Suites Charlotte Ballantyne
title: “Great hotel, hope to back soon!!”
text: I was put here for my new job and can't thank them enough. It has an indoor pool, a gym with more than a treadmill or two, it actually had a universal machine, free weights and a stepper along with a couple treadmills. Breakfast is served evryday and has everything anyone would want, meat, eggs, cereal, oatmeal, waffles, coffee, juice, ETC.. Also Tuesday through Thursday was free beer, wine and food, which included, salad, pasta, tacos, soup, sandwiches and a couple other items. The rooms are spacious with a private bathroom for each room and a common room with a TV, couch, table, full size fridge, ove, stovetop and microwave. It also has a putting green in the back of the place. This hotel is one of the best I've been in and hope my company puts me back here when I return to the area. The only negatives were the heat pump outside my window was loud and the scrambled eggs were a little under temp when they were served, but bear in mind they were already cooked, they just needed to heat up a little more. Other than that, I would definately recommend this hotel.

name: Hilton Charlotte University Place
title: “Typical Hilton, very nice”
text: we really enjoyed our stay at this hotel. the room was spacious and the staff was very friendly. the room had huge window with natural light and a view of water. it had a nice flat screen tv for my husband to watch basketball. it was a typical hilton with no free breakfast. we didnt eat at the restaurant so i dont know how their food is. there are a lot of restaurants near- qdoba, melting pot, thai, buffalo wild wing, total wine (not a restaurant, i know). the bed and pillows were really comfy.

name: Renaissance Charlotte Suites
title: “An Excellent Business Hotel”
text:
We stayed here at the beginning and end of a trip to DC. We left our car in the hotel parking lot and took the shuttle to and from the airport. We spent two nights at the hotel.
The hotel is in a business park and is a handsome building with nicely landscaped grounds. Check in was effortless and friendly. Our suite was roomy, clean and comfortable. We heard a bit of noise from the room next door but it ended after only a few minutes.
We did not eat in the restaurant but did have a drink in the lobby bar. Very nice experience, sitting in the atrium lobby sipping a drink and enjoying the company of your fellow traveller. 
The only problems we encountered was a bedroom TV that did not work our first night and no soap the other night. In both cases the problems were quickly remedied.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Perfect stay”
text:
Had a perfect stay at the Chancellor. Location is right in the middle of everything. Staff VERY helpful and very friendly.
Rooms are small, but still sufficient. And I prefer to use the bathroom by myself, not at the same time with my partner. For one occupant at a time there is plenty of room in the bathroom. 
Didn't miss air condition at all, there is a fan which was not even needed at the time of my stay. Open window during night....and as to the street noise: well, you choose the location (heart of the city), so how come people still expect no street sounds??
The pillow service was a very nice touch! They offer about 10 different pillows to choose from.....so take your pick.
I had had the package that included parking. Sutter garage is very close and once you have reached the garage they park your car for you.... 
Would definitely stay at the Chancellor again! 
Xenia from Germany.

name: Hampton Inn Charlotte - South Park
title: “Great stay would recommend to others”
text: Very nice hotel in quiet location. Were checked in by a wonderfully trained and professional staff person. Stayed in room 627 which faced the shopping community and outside water fountain. Would give all 5 stars if these small issues were not present. The shower did not have a round extended bar so it felt cramped and there were signs of age such as chipping areas, the mattress was a bit uncomfortable, and the breakfast area was not well equipped. There were a few hairs in the shower area as well, but must say the room otherwise was cleaned with care. Loved the staff, pool, location, fireplace, high ceilings, etc. Will be back and would recommend to friends and family.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Charlotte Matthews
title: “One of the Nicest”
text: This property was great! The staff was engaging, professional, friendly and genuinely seemed to enjoy their work. The property was nicely appointed and squeaky clean. The breakfast was varied and well stocked with tasty and healthy items. The room was large and very clean. The beds were comfortable. Next time I am in town, I will stay here.

name: Drury Inn & Suites Charlotte Northlake
title: “great room, service, food for the price!”
text: Nice hotel for the price. We walked to the mall, had easy access to I-77, about 15 min from downtown, nice free food and alcohol in the evening. We ate the free stuff, then split a late dinner to save money. Room was clean, staff was friendly. Nice pool and hot tub.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Perfect start to our Honeymoon!!!”
text:
What can I say, 5 stars easy. Coming from Scotland my new wife and I arrived tired but very happy at the door. Being our first time in the US we weren't to sure about tipping and forgot the Doorman after he'd taken our bags out of the boot and passed them to a bellboy. Caught up with later to say a proper thanks.
First impressions were wonderful decor is bright and welcoming with a roaring fire in the lobby under the wonderful clock. This is where they have nightly wine tasting, apparently a different winery every month.
We were only staying here for the first three nights of our honeymoon, but oh how we wish we could of stayed longer.
Fantastic location and great staff made everything so good. We especially would like to thank Lane one of the Concierges, she was absolutely brilliant and helped me organise several little surprises for my new wife even before we got there.
Also little touches like the leopard skin style dressing gowns/house coats?? and the umbrella in the room which you can buy if you want were things we'd love to see in the UK.
Room was spacious and looked out on the trolley turnaround and we could even see one end of the GG Bridge. Bed was delightful, so comfortable it was hard to get out of it.
Finally thanks to the Argonaut for even providing lovely Scottish rain for us for our stay??? We'd of loved California sunshine but who cares when you can stay in a place like this??

name: Drury Inn & Suites Charlotte Northlake
title: “nice hotel”
text: I found this to be a very nice hotel - staff was great, and I love the unlimited soda and popcorn. The 'free dinner' turns out to be a blessing and a curse - it's great to have it available, but then you tend to eat it, and it's not the most gourmet experience (hot dogs, chicken nuggets, iceberg salad, chili etc). Breakfast is very good. Workout room is adequate. I would stay here again.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Ft. Worth-North at Fossil Creek
title: “Quiet, clean, and comfortable--what more could you want?”
text: I took my husband and son and his wife and 2 small children to a race at the Texas Motor Speedway. I was reluctant to book at this hotel because it was right on the freeway (i.e., conveniently located) and I was concerned about the traffic noise. What a pleasant surprise we experienced! This hotel has quality double-paned windows and NO NOISE could be heard whatsoever from the busy traffic just outside our window. The walls of the hotel are very insulated and we could not hear our neighbors or their TV or even their small dog. The doors of each room have a closer that shuts the door softly so you don't hear doors slamming all night long. The bed was very comfortable and the sheets and blankets were clean and freshly laundered. The bathroom was very roomy and well appointed. All of the rooms are 2-rooms (or more) suites with a full kitchen including a microwave, 2-burner stove, dishwasher, disposal, and refrigerator. Plus a free breakfast 7 days a week and dinner Monday-Thursday. We have stayed at fancier places and paid a LOT more money for them, but we have not been more comfortable or welcomed any more than we were here.

name: Argonaut Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “nice location, nice rooms”
text: I would have given this hotel 5 stars except that the walls are a little thin and we could hear music and tv from the next room. Other than that, the location, people working there and the room were excellent. Free internet access in the lobby. We had a package for parking($36 a night), free breakfast in the Blue Mermaid Restaurant downstairs, free cable car pass for 1 day and Pier 39 fun book. Great package. I always have to look for a parking package because SF parking rates are outrageous. I would stay here again. This is the best hotel in the Fisherman's Wharf area.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Ft. Worth-North at Fossil Creek
title: “Super service at Homewood Suites @ Fossil Creek”
text: Could not have stayed at a better place. Superior service, beautiful hotel with excellent staff, breakfast area and food were wonderful and their presentation first rate.

name: Marriott Hotel & Golf Club at Champions Circle
title: “Outstanding!!!”
text: Just a wonderful place!. I had a golf course view and even in February, the view was wonderful. The hotel has great grounds, super rooms and, with booking through Priceline, super rates.!!! Very efficient checkin, super water pressure in the shower, pillow top beds with lots of pillows... I found nothing not to just love at Champions Circle, other than paying for internet access...I just don't understand it... oh well.

name: Hilton Charlotte University Place
title: “Comfortable Hotel, Great Price”
text:
This was a very nice, very comfortable hotel. However, for a Hilton, there were cosmetic issues that I would not have expected such as peeling wallpaper, gaps between the ceiling and wall, stained carpets, etc. However, they were obviously just cosmetic, the room was very clean.
We got the room from Priceline.com for only $45/night and were very happy with the value. When in Charlotte again, we will definitely cross our fingers that we can get the Hilton from Priceline.com again.
