It's fairly tough to drive to the front. It appears that the architects failed to allow enough room for cars, taxis and the like in front so it's always chaotic.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites El Paso East
title: “Nice rooms and good priced.”
text:
We stayed here for one night in summer 2009 on our way crossing the US. We looked around for a good priced Hotel and compared. In the end this place offered the best value.
It was quite cheap (65$ including tax) and was very safe. Even it is close to the Interstate the rooms are pretty quiet. But because of the Interstate it means you can get anywhere pretty fast. Walmart, a huge shopping Mall and a nice Texas Roadhouse are close by.
Check-in was fast and friendly. The rooms are clean and well sized. It did come with some extra chair (comfy), TV, fridge and microwave. The bed was big and comfy too. From our room you even could see Mexico.... was nice especially at night....seeing the lights from Mexico.
We really had a good stay here and were happy with the value we got for our money. We would stay here again.
Wanna know more about my trips? Click on my profile or visit:
route66traveler.jimdo.com

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites El Paso East
title: “Clean Rooms and Comfortable Beds”
text: Stayed here for the Sun Bowl. Clean Rooms and Comfortable Beds. Cheap rate off of hotwire. Free Breakfast(no waffle maker). I would give it a higher rating but when we arrived at 10 PM after a long flight, there was a problem with hotwire's credit card and the clerk gave me a number to call and wouldn't check me in until I resolved the problem. She should have called hotwire and resolved it herself (seeing that the hotel is charging hotwire's credit card) or let me check in and resolve it the following morning.

name: Hampton Inn El Paso-Airport
title: “Great airport hotel”
text: I had an early flight out of El Paso, so checked Trip Advisor and decided to stay at the Hampton Inn. They have an airport shuttle service that operates 24 hrs a day. Extremely nice room! Although they do not have a restaurant, they do offer snacks for sale in their "food pantry". I was also told there is a nice restaurant in the Holiday Inn next door. Whenever I find myself needing a room in El Paso, I will be staying at this hotel.

name: Doubletree Hotel El Paso Downtown/City Center
title: “Loved it”
text: Booked this hotel as a spare of the moment thing, a website said the check in age is 18 (I'm 19 so I said okay great!) Well, we called after we booked it and they said that the age limit is 21 but that since we already booked it would be okay. So we arrive and they have no problems checking us in, gave us a fresh warm cookie! What other hotel does that?! We called the front desk and asked how ordering pizza would work (the elevators are key operated) and they helped us out. Spent the night watching tv on the nice tv they provided, only complaint is that our bathroom door didnt shut all the way it. Other than that the hotel was nice, friendly and helpful. The room was decorated nicely and there were plenty of things around for us to walk around and do and the scenery! Pretty! And the beds were comfortable, I slept like a baby.

name: Hilton Garden Inn El Paso
title: “El Paso's Finest”
text:
I chose this hotel due to its high ranking and enthusiastic feedback. I was not disappointed. This hotel is, in my own opinion, El Paso's finest. The front desk staff were professional and courteous. They made every attempt to make you feel welcome and at home and I was greeted with a genuine and true smile whenever I walked past the front desk.
The rooms were terrific. They were spacious and had a very comfortable bed and a large flat screen TV. I was very impressed with this hotel's cleanliness and wide range of facilities. A business center is located in the lobby for those that need to go on the internet or print and copy something. 
The location is excellent too. Mesa Street is nearby and has many eating establishments, stores, and a Starbucks just a short walk away. 
I can't find anything at fault about this hotel. It has easily become my favorite place to stay in El Paso. Well done Hilton Garden Inn, you have hit a home run in El Paso.

name: BEST WESTERN Sunland Park Inn
title: “Terrible!”
text: What a dive! $79.00 per night? Filthy, room smelled bad. I would not recommend this hotel. Not up to the standards of any other best western Ive ever stayed at.

name: Microtel Inn & Suites by Wyndham El Paso West
title: “stained sheets and unclean”
text: tried 3 rooms, yellow and brown stains on all the sheets, stains on pillows, hairs in beds, hairs on floors of bathrooms. If you can get past these. the $66 price for two beds might be acceptable. But the signs at the side entrances that say, not responsible for theft and vandalism makes you wonder, given the vacant land adjacent to the parking. And I didn't see any cameras that may deter criminals.

name: La Quinta Inn El Paso - Airport
title: “Muy comodo y limpio.”
text: Las habitaciones son limpias, comodas las camas y el personal muy accesible. El desayuno es bueno, aunque le faltan los huevos cosidos y los waffles de otros hoteles La Quinta a los que he llegado. Esta bien ubicado (frente al freeway hay un centro comercial y el aeropuerto esta a 15 minutos) El servicio de shuttle es rapido. El precio es bueno si reservas por hoteles.com

name: El Paso West Travelodge
title: “Relaxing night”
text: My wife and I stayed overnight here after the second day of our Texas road trip. This Travelodge was a great place to stay at a very reasonable price. The manager was friendly and helpful, the room was clean and comfortable, best of all the place was quiet. Especially compared to the previous night at a noisy, cheap Motel 6. Would stay here again anytime, and will do so on the return trip.

name: Holiday Inn El Paso-Airport I-10
title: “spacious rooms and great ammenities”
text: I personally loved the service at this hotel. The rooms are spacious and clean. We had a king-bed room. It had a nice sized bathroom, flat screen TV, nicely furnished and spacious! It was an awesome experience! Check-in was easy. My kids loved the pool. The staff were all friendly, always had a great smile and offered to help. I will definitely stay here again!

name: La Quinta Inn El Paso West
title: “non smoking rooms”
text: I asked for a non smoking room, 1st floor, overlooking the pool. I got a non smoking room that smell like someone had just smoke a pack of cigs. the oder was so strong that i left the door open ( in 38 degree weather) to get rid of the oder and that did not work. One bed had fresh linen, the other bed linen had the heavy smoke oder. i spoke to the desk help when i checked out. I will stay there again, but i will check my non smoking room before i sign my contract.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Muy céntrico”
text:
Estuvimos 4 noches y lo mejo,r sin duda, es la situación. Está muy céntrico y cerca de todos los medios de transporte.
En cuanto al hotel en si, lo encontramos bastante normal. Habitaciones actualizadas pero bastante pequeñas. En nuestro caso, las ventanas daban a la parte de atrás de algunos edificios y el ruido de los aparatos de ventilación nos molestaba durante la noche.
El servicio, correcto.
En cuanto al precio nos pareció un poco caro por lo que obtuvivos pero estuvimos en agosto y seguro que los precios durante el resto de año son más asequibles. Al final pagas por la situción en el centro de San Francisco (los hoteles de alrededor tienen precios aún más altos, aunque también son de más categoría).

name: Holiday Inn El Paso-Sunland & I-10 W.
title: “Great staff, odd layout of hotel”
text:
The staff was very friendly and helpful. They should train other hotels in "hospitality". Lobby was nice and updated, exercise room was spacious with good equipment, lobby bar was comfortable. The layout of the hotel is a little odd with multiple buildings and somewhat of a maze to find the stairs to the second floor and then to find your room. 
The rooms appeared to have been remodeled and current. I would stay here again.

name: Chase Suite Hotel El Paso
title: “Nice, but....”
text:
I would have rated this hotel excellent except that I was put in a smoking room with a queen size bed when I had reserved a non-smoking room with a king size bed. When I questioned the staff about it they said that non-smoking rooms and bed sizes were "requests" not reservations. 
There were many other people here that I spoke with that had the same problem. It is obvious that the hotel is not managing their smoking and non-smoking rooms. 
This is an excellent hotel if you are TDY at Ft Bliss. Each room has a full kitchen, so you don't have to go out to dinner every night. The hotel has free cocktails and snack food Monday through Thursday. 
The hotel rooms need to be updated. They aren't spotless, but pretty close.
Once again, if you are going to be TDY at Ft Bliss, this is the place to stay.

name: La Quinta Inn El Paso West
title: “Clean, safe place to stay”
text: Nice clean rooms. Place seemed safe. Cracker Barrell right next door!

name: Camino Real El Paso
title: “Just okay”
text:
The hotel sits in the heart of downtown El Paso. It has a parking garage that you can use for just $5/day which we considered a plus. The lobby bar is impressive and the buidling itself unique and historic. The A/C worked well and the beds were comfortable. 
The rooms were not very nice ... stained carpet, old TVs, loud A/C. The bathroom was not very clean or inviting. Hairs on the floor and in the tub and the tile floor was chipped and stained with grime. 
The onsite restaurant was fine, the bar prices were reasonable, vending machine prices were really cheap. The breakfast buffet was good.
Overall for the price we paid, it was okay. If we had paid alot, I would have given it a rating of 2.

name: Camino Real El Paso
title: “Please read the whole review!”
text: You pull up and it looks like the set of some movie where there's no one left on earth. Then you go in the lobby and it looks like the day after an estate sale and the only thing left are things that are nailed down. But when you get to the front desk and talk to the friendly staff (as in Will), the reasons to turn around start disappearing. You go on up to the room that badly needs remodeling and updating so you decide to go have a drink in the bar with the famous Tiffany dome. All you can focus on is the tacky chrome chairs but again, that goes away after you talk to the outgoing young man behind the bar. The restaurant is closed, there's no one in the cafe and we take that as a bad sign so we walk across the street for dinner. So why stay? Because if you don't, these gems will disappear and the only choice will be the aesthetic chains that are the fast foods of spending the night travels. It takes a little more time to get off of I-10 and yes, downtown El Paso is DEE-PRESS-ING but, the rooms are clean, the rates are very good, and the staff is so professional and friendly. It's not their fault the Camino Real corporation isn't keeping it up and taking pride in this historical gem.

name: Red Roof Inn - El Paso East
title: “Good trip, thanks mister Dean”
text: I'm pretty new at hotels because I'm not on hotels much, but sometimes when you need a place to stay, its good to know you got a good place looking out for you. First thing I always notice is the refrigerated air conditioning, which was an A+ from the start. Rooms looked classy, made you feel like you're something really special there. One of the really convenient parts is that the parking isn't jammed packed, so there was definitely enough parking spots close to my room and a couple to spare. Since I'm not big on knowing on what services hotels provided, I went to the front and Dean was there to help me out. Seems like the big guy has been around long enough to know alot about hotels, services, and how I could take advantage of the catering. Made me feel like real royalty when I was there, guess that's part of the service while you're there. Long story short, if I ever need a place to stay, I'll definitely stay at the red roof again. Also the TV was good, but I'm not big on watching TV, at least its good to know that its there. All in all, I had a good visit. Thanks!

name: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham - El Paso
title: “Concerns/Pluses”
text:
My busband, Ramon, booked the hotel stay for me, spouse Josephine and my daughter Debbie Fiske. We were extremely pleased w/ the location close to airport(flew in and would drive next morning to Ruidoso).
Concerns: The towels were old and stained. The fitness room(used by my daughter, who is a gym instructor) equipment was dated, also the pictures on wall('80s hair style and work out clothes ) There were no hand towels nor paper towels available, nor water available. 
On the plus side: The breakfast was excellent! Mexican breakfast food, yogurt, cereal, bagels, etc. a very good balance.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites El Paso West
title: “Great hotel!”
text: Clean ,comfortable hotel. Room has a microwave and fridge. The only complaint I have is that the front desk woman was not the friendliest. They do have free wi-fi,free parking and free hot breakfast with cheese omelettes,pastries,juices,fruit,bacon,etc. If you stay in El Paso,I think the newer ,nicer side of town is the west side. This hotel is sort of on the outskirts of El Paso,and there was a new shopping center or outlet close by.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites El Paso West
title: “Great stay!”
text: Was relocated from another Hilton property in El Paso and found a room here. The suites are as good as I have ever stayed. Very clean (albeit the property is only 4 months old). The breakfast are just OK. The front desk could not have been more helpful (especially Christine)

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “The price is right!”
text:
After we paid $60 dollers a night for 4 nights in mid July 04 I checked this site and thought there must be two hotels of this name and we had paid for a dud !!
To be honest we visited the City last summer and knew the location but where still worried there had been a mistake with the price , but no. This is an excellent hotel no matter which part of the service you look at, the rooms, staff, public areas even the normally surly reception staff where up-beat, friendly and helpful.
I would have no problem in recommending this property, we paid $280 a night for a suite in a Hyatt in San Diego and as nice as it was the Chancellor was better.

name: Camino Real El Paso
title: “Reasonable for the money and if you want to stay downtown”
text: First, the hotel was in the perfect location for us because we were going to eat dinner downtown and go to the Plaza Theatre (directly across the street) for a show Saturday Night. At check in the lady at the front desk, while very pleasant, was all alone and not very efficient. We had a minor issue with the rate and reservation but it was resolved. The room (King bed) was large and the furniture was a bit above average. Interestingly, not a single piece of art on the wall. Yes, the TV was very old but did not matter as we were not there to watch TV. The bathroom was below average and definitely could be updated but everything worked. The main restaurant and bar area were popular. All in all, for the rate we paid and the fact all of our activities were downtown, I would stay there again if we need to be downtown.

name: Wyndham El Paso Airport
title: “Clean Rooms, Concierge Level A Must!!”
text: I was amazed at the size of the rooms. Separate living area, desk and mini bar with refrigerator PLUS the bedroom with king size bed and balcony overlooking the pool. Extremely clean. Conveniently located next to the airport and you don't realize it. You hardly ever hear the planes take off and land. Very nice size pool with cabana area. The slide is awesome for children. I look forward to my next stay in El Paso. The two computers in the lobby with internet service is a nice feature. Thanks goes out to each employee for all the dedicated hard work each day.

name: Embassy Suites Columbus - Airport
title: “weekend at COSI”
text: It's a clean, kid friendly hotel. The kids enjoyed the pool and the manager's reception. We had dinner at the hotel restaurant and the service was awful and the food was not much better. Overall the hotel is very nice, I would order pizza or go out for dinner though

name: Hyatt Place Columbus/OSU
title: “Hyatt Place was wonderful !!!”
text: Everything we experienced while @ this hotel was wonderful. Our check-in was fast & easy, the lady checking us in asked about our preferences & each request was met. It was an added blessing to have the free parking garage within a few steps. I appreciated the fact that it was offered @ no charge esp. in Columbus. Our room was larger than expected with a huge TV and separate sitting area. It more than met our expectations. We decided to go for a swim & noticed the towels in the swim area were gone so we walked to the front desk & one of the ladies IMMEDIATELY got fresh towels for us. We were surprised because normally it takes a while to see results. Being so close to Ohio State University they had been extremely busy with lots of different athletes staying there using the facilities. We mentioned the indoor pool was a little chilly & she turned up the heat for us. The complimentary breakfast was superb. We had the sausage gravy w/biscuits, fresh fruit, yogurt and coffee. The gravy was so tasty. It was all really good & we left stuffed. Overall, it was wonderful. The hotel is close to everything & we were able to do a lot while we were there . We highly recommend this hotel. It was extremely clean, comfortable & just really a nice place to stay. The customer service is beyond compare & made our stay even more enjoyable :-)

name: Embassy Suites Columbus - Airport
title: “Close to excellent, but not quite there.....”
text:
My husband and I recently stayed at the Embassy Suites by the Columbus Airport. Below are the pros and cons of our stay:
Pros:
~Newly built hotel
~Very spacious rooms
~Very clean rooms
~Nice large LCD TVs in living room and bedroom
~Very spacious bathroom including a spacious stand-up shower
~Very friendly staff
~Room Service (dinner) was very good
~Comfortable couch for lounging
~Quiet (hardly noticed any airplane noise)
~Ample parking
Cons:
~Bed was a little too firm (for us anyway)
~Room service failed to pick up our dishes from our dinner room service order (even though a hotel staff member placed a bill under our door sometime during the night). What was very disturbing was that the next morning, it was apparent that someone had rummaged through our dirty dishes looking for food. One can only assume that a transient or a drunk guest was responsible. Had room service picked up our dishes in a timely manner, this never would have happened.
~Location of hotel is convenient to the airport, but not in a good neighborhood
~Toilet in room is very loud when flushed. We could hear flushing from rooms above and rooms beside us. 
~The buffet breakfast was very disappointing. We arrived when it opened (730a). While there was plenty to choose from, the food was lukewarm at best (some was just cold); the bacon was not cooked thoroughly; the danishes were still partially frozen; etc. Breakfast at McDonalds would have been better than this. 
Overall, the hotel's pros outweigh the cons; however, if the hotel wants to retain its four-diamond status, they need to step it up a little in the breakfast and the room service areas.

name: Microtel Inn & Suites by Wyndham El Paso Airport
title: “Ask for the quiet side of the hotel”
text: We have stayed at other Microtels so we were prepared for the small room. This one is convenient to the Airport but we were glad that we had our GPS to guide us the the hotel. Our room was on the side next to the street instead of the side next to the neighboring hotel. There was alot of loud street/car noise during the night due to the closeness to the street. Other than that it wa fine.

name: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham - El Paso
title: “I just don't like this place...but...”
text:
Well I hate to say it but I will more than likely stay @ Hawthorn again just because of it's location and it meets the per diem for the area for my company. 
The positive thing is they do have a pretty nice free breakfast. It is very good.
The negatives - this place is outdated - and not clean. 
I noticed new bedding like that is going to help the place look "new"?
The shower (to me) is just nasty....with rusty faucets...and the bottom of the shower is just gross.
This is a convenient place. I usually travel to El Paso by myself and this is close to work. The only good thing about staying at this hotel is that there is 2 resturants in the parking lot (Applebees & Cattle Baron's). 
I don't like this place...but I don't have many choices due to cost restraints.
Oh and the walls must be super thin because you can hear the person in the next room coughing and the person upstairs doing jumping jacks I assume.

name: Red Roof Inn - El Paso East
title: “Great People”
text: I have been staying at this hotel for the past six years. All the people working there are great, they make sure that in that are no problems with the room and if there is anything wrong they make it wright. I would recamend this hotel to anyone out in that are to stay with them.

name: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham - El Paso
title: “Peaceful, well landscaped hotel”
text:
I very much enjoyed my stay at the Hawthorne. I particularly liked the workout area and pool. The pool courtyard was tropically landscaped and pleasing to be in and look at. My room was a pool courtyard view room which gave the appearance of being in a high class resort. 
The hotel was quiet and well kept. My only complaint was that the internet access was down one evening. The breakfast was delicious.
If you stay here, try the Cattle Baron restaurant right across the parking lot. The food was fantastic and reasonably priced. Also, FIND Carlos and Mickeys. I can't remember their address but it's only a couple miles away. They had amazing Mexican food. The Sopapia desert was particularly excellent.

name: Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham - El Paso
title: “Hawthorne was great”
text: My visit to the Hawthorne was pleasurable, compared to recent reviewer's comments. It was not the nicest hotel room, but I found it clean, and responsive to any of my needs, such as a refrigerator n my room (I didn't have a suite.) Internet was free, and the breakfast was one of the better ones for a hotel... eggs, bacon, refried beans, potatoes, cereal, fruit, yogurt, etc. And it was good! There was a "happy hour" in the evening. They also have shuttle service. I did not see ANY bugs of ANY kind. I would return to this hotel.

name: Hilton Columbus/Polaris
title: “Nice hotel”
text: The Polaris Hilton room was large. The room was also very clean. Nice sized bathroom. If you are looking for a nice place to stay this would a good choice.

name: Sleep Inn at Court Square
title: “Great find”
text: I extended a business trip by a day to see some of the city and needed a nice, but inexpensive play to stay. The front desk staff were very helpful and I enjoyed being on the trolley line. It's much quieter than the hotel I stayed at a block away from Beale street. The free breakfast was huge and there was plenty to eat even for a picky eater like me.

name: SpringHill Suites Memphis East / Galleria
title: “Great Service”
text:
Good Evening
Once again the SpringHill Suites by Marriott, with Naomi Herring, Asst. General Manager, her staff and host of housekeepers made our stay a pleasure. They were always willing and ready to accommodate us with whatever we needed. The rooms were furnished with a refrigerator, microwave, sink, desk and queen sofa sleeper. The rooms were clean and updated. 
 Special Thanks to Billy, Cassandra, Tonya and Donna (housekeeping) and the rest of the staff for greeting us with a smile each time our paths crossed. The coffee and breakfast was fresh and hot at all times. 
The location was great and close to all the attractions were we interested in. (shopping, food)
In the future, when selecting a hotel we will consider SpringHill Suites by Marriott our host hotel. 
Thank You for quality service.

name: BEST WESTERN Galleria Inn and Suites
title: “Very Good place”
text: We stayed here on the way back home. Staff was very friendly, breakfast was very good, everything was very neat and clean in this hotel. It is an older hotel and the rooms are showing some wear and tear but I felt very comfortable in the room. Everything is very clean and well maintained, no worries there. We had a double room with a tiny kitchenette attached so we sat and ate our dinner in the room, which was treat after so many days on the road. I also thought their breakfast to be one of the best we had at any of our hotel stays so far-nice continental breakfast. Great coffee! Highly recommend!

name: Four Points by Sheraton Memphis East
title: “Nice and clean”
text:
Hi, I used to stay at the Four Points almost on a weekly basis until they nixed the points and cash availability, as a platinum member who has stayed in a lot of SPG properties I bring out the following points
PROS
The rooms are comparable in size to the Four Points brand
The rooms are always neat and clean and there is a empty refrigerator in every room
The staff is extremely friendly and helpful 
CONS
Tough to get to with a car and impossible by foot (not their fault)
Very small lobby and no bar to socialize
I would highly recommend this hotel for anybody coming into town with a car who wants a nice clean quiet hotel, however if you like to socialize or catch a drink before you go to sleep, you can stay at the Hilton or the DoubleTree down the road for almost the same price

name: Holiday Inn Univ of Memphis
title: “Great place”
text: Friendly staff, spacious rooms, well kept hotel inside and out. Nice neighborhood also. Good value for the location.

name: Days Inn Memphis at Graceland
title: “Good Deal For The Price ...”
text:
Loved that This hotel was just a short walk to Graceland!
The price was about $35 less per night than Heartbreak Hotel Down the block.
Our Only complaint was of the 3 In house Elvis Movie channels Provided Only 1 of them worked.

name: Sleep Inn at Court Square
title: “Nice, clean, great location”
text: Stayed for one night traveling thru town & wanted to hit Beale Street. Hotel was convenient and breakfast was great. Parking was available on site. Just missing a pool. Staff was friendly and very helpful.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Memphis East
title: “Nice hotel”
text:
Nice hotel property. Good breakfast. Clean rooms. Friendly staff. Difficult highway access.
Good location near many good restaurants.

name: Comfort Inn Downtown
title: “Greatest staff ever”
text: My family reunion was from July 26-29, 2012. I arrived that Wednesday and may I say the staff was courteous, friendly and a true pleasure. The location was perfect one can walk to Beale Street, Civil Rights Museum, stores and the view was excellent. Swimming on the roof outside was a true treat. Bonus free breakfast with my favorite waffles. Nice variety of food. During times when they say customer service is failing the hotel staff here makes one believe it has come back. Great job kudos to everyone. Thank you for making my reunion a success.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Memphis Primacy Parkway
title: “One of the Best Hotels of our Trip”
text: What a find. This hotel is modern, features large, comfortable rooms and is convenient to the Memphis area. We liked it so much that we spent a second night. It is outside the city, which some may find to be inconvenient, but we had no problem getting around.

name: BEST WESTERN Galleria Inn and Suites
title: “Average hotel...”
text: Average hotel, looks like they upgraded recently but the room still looks a little run down. Bathroom needs renovation. AC was so loud and the room still felt sticky after it was on high for a while. Okay for one night. Should be closer to like $60-$70 bux a night. Breakfast was okay. Attendant during breakfast was very nice & helpful. Served its purpose...decent nights sleep, in safe area.

name: SpringHill Suites Memphis Downtown
title: “Great location on trolley line, reasonably priced”
text:
This property is your cookie cutter springhill suites. Feels like it was recently renovated, all the usual amenities are present - the lobby has a nice little bar and seating area (first time I'd seen a bar that was staffed with bartender at a springhill suites). 
Note if you drive: google maps takes you some weird backwards way down an alley to find the entrance. Ask to hotel for better directions. 
 Valet and self parking have exact same price, by the way. Only one valet so you may have to wait awhile to find him. 
Our room was in the connected historical building which made it a little inconvenient to walk to/from the front entrance (up an elevator, down a hall to a hidden elevator, up again and down more halls to my room). Given that our building was 100 years old I was hoping for some charm but you really just get basic normal modern insides, except for some squeaky hallway floors. Room itself was fine - typical. Not much to complain about except the sink area for getting ready (two people can't fit at same time) and the complete lack of a full length mirror. 
Also our room was right outside the housekeeping closet and you could easily hear their hallway conversations. further, the doors slam pretty loudly so get a room away from the stairs, which lots of people took to avoid the slow elevators - resulting in lots of slamming doors from the stairwell. 
One warning: we had gone to breakfast and returned to our room, forgetting to latch the door from the inside. Sure enough, in walks a housekeeper without so much as a knock, even though the do not disturb sign was on the door. She was all the way through the living room before she realized we were inside, or even looked for that matter, which implied (to me anyway) that this is a regular habit. 
Front desk staff were friendly but busy many times - had to wait to speak to them every time we needed anything (they were always on the phone or dealing with another guest in front of us). 
Overall decent value - I may go back, due to convenient location on Main St. Trolley line and walking distance to Beale St. but there are about 3 other similar quality properties right next door that may be less likely to invade your room.

name: The Westin Seattle
title: “Updated and renovated rooms but slow wifi and bad Plat bennies”
text:
As a SPG Platinum, I recently stayed here for 2 nights. 
Location
The location is excellent. It's in the downtown core and everything is within walking distance. The "Two Towers" can be seen at a distance so it's fairly easy to spot driving into downtown. Lots of restaurant choices are nearby with a Bartell's and McD's both less than a block away. 
Parking
Driving down 5th, there was a parkade that advertised "Westin". However, be warned as this isn't the Westin hotel but a building named the Westin. The Westin parkade is right beside the lobby entrance on 6th. If you it's open, you can save a few bucks by doing the self-park. It's super convenient and there's an elevator that takes you to the bottom and into the lobby entrance. I checked, and there are in-out privileges. For a few $ more, you can get the valet parking. Overall, this is Seattle downtown and parking is extortionate - $41 for self-park and $44 for valet.
Check-in
First off, the person manning the SPG Gold/Plat desk was pretty rude. At first, he asked me to wait as his computer wasn't working. Fine, I waited. Then he started helping another lady who walked by and when I mentioned I was next in line, he didn't seem to care. 
My actual front desk agent was a younger Asian lady who was excellent. I had been pre-upgraded to a suite for my 2nd day but not my first. After a bit of checking with the manager, she snagged me a suite for the entire stay. She even helped me store all my luggage and items I bought while my wife and I went out for dinner. 
Room
The room I received was an accessible suite in the North Tower. The suite itself (as the entire hotel) was been recently renovated. There were really no issues with the suite and it was very, very spacious. The only issue I had was with the bathroom - but this was a direct result of my choice of an accessible suite. The shower wasn't enclosed and water would get everywhere. In other accessible suites I've had in the past, there was at least a curtain to help stop the splashing but not here. 
The room wifi was incredibly slow as only 802.11g (not n) was offered. For an entire day, I think the wifi charge would have been $19 or something. Ridiculous, considering the awful speeds I was getting. 
Platinum bennies
Ok, I got my suite. My internet charges are comped. I had a package sent to the hotel and even those delivery charges were comped. What wasn't kosher was the free continental breakfast. There is no way to upgrade from a very meager offering and the front desk person said she wasn't aware when I mentioned the Westin Bellevue and W have this practice. To top it off, she mentioned the restaurant doesn't offer a buffet - which is completely false. No, it isn't just her as there have been many reports of this Westin really lacking in the Platinum breakfast area. I chose 500 points instead but would have much preferred a breakfast that was upgradable.
Final verdict
The Westin used to be a tired, old hotel in great need of a renovation. Well, that renovation happened and the rooms now are excellent. However, this hotel needs to update their tech infrastructure as Wifi G speeds are unacceptable considering the ridiculous prices charged. The service, for the large part, was excellent with the sole exception of an uninterested and rude front desk agent manning the SPG Gold/Plat desk. Lastly, the Westin would have won a few more notches upward if they had offered a decent continental breakfast that was upgradable. 
Would I return? Actually, I'd look hard at the Sheraton Seattle (Pike Tower). I do prefer this hotel to the W and the Four Points. If the price was right, then yes, I'd return.

name: SpringHill Suites Seattle Downtown/South Lake Union
title: “Great place and great value”
text: This is the second time our group of 4 stays here while on business in Seattle. The location is not too bad, just a 15-20 minute walk from the business center. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The service is great - helped us out a couple of times with checking luggage in and out and getting us a cab. The hot breakfast in the morning is a great convenience prior to heading to business. The price per room per night is great if you don't mind walking a bit.

name: Renaissance Seattle Hotel
title: “Great service, nice room”
text:
We stayed for one night as part of the King Tut package which was a great deal. Our room was clean, nicely decorated and the bedding was very soft. Renovated recently I'm sure and done so well.
The hotel bar is great and a wonderful people watching spot. The concierge and front desk staff were helpful and friendly and our requested turn-down service was completed.
It is a busy hotel so you can wait a long time for elevators and it is not located right in the heart of the other hotels and close to the highway. Still it was very quiet - we were on the 7th floor and didn't hear any outside noise.
No pool - as an FYI.

name: Warwick Seattle Hotel
title: “Bummed”
text: We have not stayed at the Warwick in 3-4 years. We remember it being a really nice hotel. We did a bid on Priceline for a 3 1/2 star hotel and the Warwick was our winner. This is NOT a 3 1/2 star hotel anymore. The first room we were placed had such a bad mattress that we could see the dents just by looking at it. They placed us in another room with a beautiful view of a cement wall of the next store parking garage. I could actually almost touch the cement wall plus very little light entered the room. Fortunately we were so busy in Seattle we did not spend much time in the room but it was not I repeat a 3 1/2 star hotel more like a 2 star. Rooms really need to be updated to be competitive very worn looking. To bad it used to be a cool hotel.

name: The Peabody Memphis
title: “Great location”
text: I stayed at the Peabody during Elvis week although I was there for a business trip. I stayed on the 8th floor in a corner room which was spacious and I was pleasantly surprised by the toiletries (Gilchrist and Soames) and soap in the shape of a duck. The room had a good Internet connection for both my laptop and iPhone and was quiet except for the last night when my neighbor seemed to be rearranging the contents of a closet. I did not hear any traffic noise. I also had a good view of the fountain for the marching of the ducks on my last day there. It was a unique experience and added charm to my stay. The location is superb; there are great restaurants just a ten minute walk away. Ask the concierge for recommendations. Everything he picked was excellent.

name: Belltown Inn
title: “3 at best”
text:
Parking awkward
Staff only just friendly enough, not friendly, simply acceptable
Room moderate, clean enough, but a bit tired
Noisy at night from courtyard -was warm and no A/C, so had to sleep with window open - fountain and people below took some getting used to
Location pretty good and price pretty good
I guess it is what it is

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Memphis East-Sycamore View
title: “great place to stay”
text: the hotel was great. the staff was very helpful in everyway. the room was clean, and in excellent condition. the breakfast was great. i would recommend others to stay at this hotel.

name: The Westin Seattle
title: “This place has it all”
text: It's wonderful, whether on vacation or on business, to find a hotel that is run professionally from the reservations to the departure. I had the joy of staying here. The location is wonderful for sight seeing, shopping, and dining. The check-in was quick and gave me the feeling of really being welcome. The rest of the staff were of the same quality. The pool and exercise areas were clean and had plenty of towels. Special honors go to the concierge staff. They are TOPS with suggestions, and answers to even the most mundane questions. Judy was especially helpful and always smiling even though it seemed that she slept under the desk. As you can tell from my prior travels, I am not a newby. If you are going to stay in Seattle, this is the place.

name: Embassy Suites Memphis
title: “Great Hotel”
text: This is the first time that I've stayed at an Embassy Suites and I absolutely loved it. The room was nice and spacious and the staff was wonderful! Everyone was so friendly!

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Executive Inn
title: “Great Place to stay”
text:
Beautiful views of the space needle - especially at night so if you like photography ask for a room with a view. The staff are great and the local restuarant is excellent.
Secure parking is a plus. Free wi-fi - my only issue was waking at 4 am to do a conference call and I could not find the internet password - called down to the front desk and the man on duty would not give it to me - he insisited I come down to get it in person - I tried to convince him that at 4 am I was not dressed but he claimed it was policy that guests come down to collect the password at the desk ....so I got dressed and went downstairs to get it.
Ridiculous and I was seriously irritated ! 
Anyway I spoke with the day staff and they seemed shocked - that is not hotel policy! 
Keep the code safe!

name: Doubletree by Hilton Seattle Airport
title: “Decent enough for the $$$”
text:
We stayed here for a few nights last weekend, booked on expedia's "surprise me" plan so we were committed. 
The room was fairly musty and probably was a smoking room in the past. Internet was and up-charge, and I gave up on ever getting a coffee in lobby in the mornings as the singly staffed coffee bar was always backed up.
The two good things I can say about the place is at least the bed was comfortable and the airplane noise was surprisingly quiet for being so close to the airport.
Oh yeah, one other good thing... It's right by the Cedarbrook Lodge (where we wanted to stay) which has a fantastic restaurant, the Copperleaf. One of the BEST meals we've had in a while.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Executive Inn
title: “Location is fantastic for seeing Seattle at its best.”
text: Don't judge by the outside appearance. Clean rooms and great service. Space needle and all Seattle central within one block. Monorail is also a block away. Plan on staying here many times while heading out on Alaska cruise. Cannot wait to come back!

name: Doubletree by Hilton Seattle Airport
title: “Bad idea on changing Diamond member breakfast”
text: So as a10-year Hilton Honor Diamond Member, "continental breakfast" is included. At virtually 100% of Hilton properties this means a "real" breakfast -- a hot, sit-down (almost always buffet) breakfast. Not here. At this property it means an $8 voucher for the Expresso Cafe. Continental breakfast by definition is AT LEAST coffee, muffin/bread/roll, and juice. To most "nicer" hotels (anything not a motel) it includes fruit and oatmeal and at "finer" hotels like true Hiltons, Waldorfs, and Conrads, it includes all breakfast items. The basic coffee, bread, and juice at the Expresso Cafe cannot be had for close to $8. We were told this change in policy came from the Operations Manager. Bad operations decision.....especially for repeat Diamond corporate customers. On matter of principle and not hunger, we will not go back and will not recommend to colleagues who travel to the SeaTac area often.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Seattle Downtown
title: “Very clean and comforatable”
text: Convenient location. This hotel was exceptionally clean. The bed was very comfortable. My room was very quiet and no outside noise could be heard. The breakfast was above average. High speed internet was good. Lots of good restaurants nearby. The $15 to park seemed a bit high.

name: Renaissance Seattle Hotel
title: “Great place to stay to explore Seattle”
text: We had excellent service and a comfortable/clean room at the Renaissance Seattle Hotel. We were on the eastern side of the hotel, but we were on a higher floor, so there was no problem with noise. The hotel had a room available for us to check in early, which was wonderful. The location is a convenient walk to many attractions in Seattle.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Downtown Seattle Center
title: “Remodeled Very Nicely”
text: The newly remodeled Four Points is nicer than other Starwood properties I've stayed at. The rooms were spacious and nicely decorated. The lobby, bar, restaurant, and especially the patio are all very nice. We had great service from the bar while spending an evening on the patio in front of the fireplace. It is a short walk to the Seattle Center. Closer than you would think. Walk about 6 blocks west of the hotel and there are several restaurants. At first we weren't sure of the area but it was very safe. The Gates foundation was right around the corner. We booked our room two days before we left and got a great rate.

name: SpringHill Suites Seattle Downtown/South Lake Union
title: “Further out but a very friendly staff”
text:
I selected this hotel for it's location close to a relative's apartment, not as a downtown hotel. We arrived about 1:00 pm and had requested an early check in. The room was available for us. If travelling with others and wanting a suite, I will warn you that there were no doors to close off the bedroom or the sink/vanity area of the bathroom. The shower/toilet area has a door but is small, so its is not a good set up if you need privacy. 
The staff was very friendly. Grab the business card for the shuttle when you check in. We had no problems when we called about 30 minutes beforehand but other people who just showed up found the shuttle to be full. The breakfast was the typical set up and runs for a fairly short time span so it was very busy, lines for the waffle maker as noted. I also liked having the business center available since I was traveling without a laptop but it did seem to typically have people waiting to use the two computers. We did walk from my relatives place back to the hotel late at night. Twice we (2 women) had homeless people asking for money but didn't feel unsafe.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Seattle Downtown
title: “Meh”
text:
I've stayed at this Hampton Inn quite a few times now. Pretty much every time I'm in Seattle for business I stay here because it fits right in with what my company will pay for a hotel. It's not an awful hotel as it has the usual Hampton Inn amenities but it's also not a great hotel for a few reasons. The first reason is that they have rooms literally right at the street level. As I'm writing this review there is a tour bus of teenagers exiting a bus right outside my room. Not the best way to end an evening when you'd like to get some sleep, and definitely no privacy. Second, as others have said, it's a hike to get from parking to the front desk. That wouldn't be so bad if there was actually parking that would fit a modern small to midsize car. I'm not exaggerating when I write that only Smart cars will fit in their parking garage. And it's such a deal for $15/night to park (why not just build it in to the room rate?).
It's not a bad hotel due to the proximity to I-5 and there are a few things nearby to try for restaurants but it definitely isn't the most happening neighborhood. And especially be careful when asking for a room as you are either right on top of the street (as I am), staring at HVAC units (the last trip), or getting a bird's eye view of the 7-11 behind the hotel (my first visit). I have yet to have a great room that has any privacy and I get the feeling that being a Hilton Honors member means absolutely nothing to this Hampton Inn.
This hotel is fine but I definitely wouldn't book it if you want a place where you can relax and get some work done in your room.

name: W Seattle
title: “Visually Appealing but Nothing Else”
text:
Beyond the great location and its trendy decor but failed to deliver when it came to the basics. 
The good: The room was nice and clean as expected. Location was perfect. Parking was easy. Staff was quick and responsive.
The bad: 
- Coffee tasted like ashtray. Not just the complimentary one in the lobby but also the $5/cup one when you order in the lobby. Save your taste buds the torture and go to Starbucks across the street.
- Ordered two chicken noodle soups via room service. Tasted like someone poured hot water in a bowl and threw some leftover chicken and a few pastas in. Super bland, don't order it.
- Be careful where you sit when ordering from the happy hour menu. If you sit in the lobby, you may find a happy hour menu in front of you but be warned this is only valid within the restaurant/bar area. The staff didn't inform us of this when we ordered even though we were clearly ordering off the happy hour menu.

name: Renaissance Seattle Hotel
title: “Very nice place, very nice location, but......”
text: Exactly what you would expect from a high end Marriott hotel. I didn't use many of the amenities so I can't comment on those. However, overall, it was quite a good experience. The service was good and rooms were compfortable.

name: BEST WESTERN Airport Executel
title: “Curtains did not close or block street lights!”
text: Staff are friendly and helpful. I am in my room right now with my husband and daughter who are both fast asleep. The problem is that the thicker curtains do not close or cover the window and they are only for show. The street lights are shining into my room directly in my face through the flimsy sheers. I am in room number 153. I like to face the side the window is on while sleeping and for this reason I will have a very uncomfortable and disruptive sleep. I Can't do much about it at this time since I'm exhausted and the rest of my family is sound asleep. Rooms are kind of small but they are clean. I'm not happy that the hotel is too cheap to have curtains that close all the way! Wifi is too slow here and my emails take forever to open and send.

name: SpringHill Suites Seattle Downtown/South Lake Union
title: “Great Value in Central Town Location With Many Amenities”
text:
This review combines two stays, a year apart, because TripAdvisor does not allow more than one post. Most of my reviews are preceded by counsel for third-party (e.g. Priceline) guests. That counsel has been omitted here.
APRIL 2010 PLUS: Room refrigerator had been preset at a reasonable level. Hot water ran quickly. Large, very spacious room with separate living and sleeping sections. Separate bath and vanity area. MINUS: heat and cool control easy to find on wall, but with print on controls so tiny it is barely legible. A wall sign would help. System works well but is very slow to respond. Very centrally located; hourly shuttle and nearly public transportation makes moving about easy. Suggestion: tip the shuttle drivers; they can be very helpful. Avoid a car--and if you have guests, use inexpensive self-pay lot next door or street parking--street free after 6 and on weekends, as all over Seattle. Breakfast space becomes a kitchen for lunch and dinner, but there were so few customers that it can be difficult to get attention. Front desk interaction is necessary for small purchases and is always busy with counseling about how-to-get-where. Polite but can involve long, long waits. Help yourself when possible.
APRIL 2009 PLUS: Breakfast buffet: hot eggs and meats, yogurts in two sizes and including low-carb, breads, muffins, make-own waffles, hard eggs, potatoes, hot oatmeal and toppings, cold cereals and juices; excellent coffee/tea in breakfast room and lobby (24 hours). Totally non-smoking, like all Marriotts. Open business center with two-computers and a printer for each, off lobby. Flawless free wired and wireless internet in rooms, wireless in lobby. Newspaper outside door on weekdays, in lobby on weekends. Inside pool and hot tub. Free access to huge 24-hour fitness across the street. Starbucks (closed weekends) across the street. Walk to midtown or downtown or Pike Market; hotel provides by-reservation shuttle on the hour with stops at Westlake Center, Space Needle, Convention Center. The giant, rally giant flagship REI and upscale shops (and BLIX, probably one of Seattle’s best spa spaces) one block walk. Public transportation on Denny (#8 bus) runs between Cap Hill and Queen Anne, past Seattle Center. Valet parking only, with modest rates for short-term visitors, $20 overnight. Recent (fabulous) lobby, breakfast room and bar renovation. Exceptionally helpful and friendly employees. Quiet despite extreme proximity to freeway. Coin laundry with several machines for guests, 2nd floor; $1 each wash and dry when I was there. Priceline 2.5 or 3-star, South Lake Union, $65-72 in winter/spring (desk was quoting $109 to walk-ins one day of my stay); higher in summer/fall. Hotel is owned by a TX company but Marriott-branded; in most of these hotels, Marriott provides management training and staff is well-trained. 
MINUS: Constant traffic on Yale Avenue can make vehicle exit risky and difficult. At all costs avoid driving at commuter hours (morning or 3-6). Valet and front desk folks will make route suggestions. Starbucks closed on weekends. Unclear how to retrieve messages from room telephone. Breakfast room can be very crowded; to avoid this go early, and avoid late hours. Room refrigerator not easily set and was extremely cold; it froze fruit, water and flowers! Ample hot water but slow to run hot (3-4 minutes late at night; most hotels are instant-hot)

name: Doubletree by Hilton Seattle Airport
title: “Consistent Quality. . . Great Service”
text:
Hilton and Doubletree have provided an excellent example of their brand with this hotel. The check-in was the fastest I have ever experienced and the cookies don't hurt. The pre-printed name on my key envelope was a simple and noticed touch.
The room felt huge and very clean. The bathroom products and towels were exquisite. The big screen LCD TV was definitely in HD and had tons of channels. The balcony was a nice touch. Tried the pool out and found it perfect for a quick, refreshing dip.
The shuttle to SEA at 4:45AM was very convenient and super quick. Our shuttle was packed with flight crews and it was a good sign seeing them in a good, rested mood. Those guys know hotels.
We didn't try the restaurant, mainly because we fell in love with the Denny's across the street. Highly recommended Doubletree.

name: Renaissance Seattle Hotel
title: “Great staff and above average food. Rooms an issue”
text:
Okay full disclosure. I am a Marriott point addict. Not so much for vacations or leisure but as someone who travels 130 days a year I tend to go out of my way to stay at Marriotts. Thus when coming to Seattle for a conference I chose the Renaissance as it was the nearest Marriott property to the convention center ...a short 6 blocks downhill and a very long 6 blocks back up 
Rooms. 
Sadly the one thing that is an issue Rooms are okay but on the smaller side. Too much furniture jammed into them and bathrooms are small and not very well appointed. It's clean and it's okay but it needs a bit of a rethink in terms of layout. Secondly and worse is lack of sound proofing. I had a a connecting room door and could literally here everything going on next door. Literally my neighbors calls to his wife and I didn't need to turn on my tv since I could hear his as if we were sharing a room. He wasn't particularly loud talker it's just clear that no sound proofing was evident. Luckily he checked out after one day but it really would make me think twice about staying here again. Which is too bad because the public areas are lovely, modern comfortable and well designed. The service was great friendly compotent and knowledgeable. 
I ate a few lunches in the restaurant and the food was very good with lots of local ingredient s and very fresh...but still the small rooms, tiny bathrooms and complete lack of sound proofing make me think you should try the Marriott Seattle waterfront instead. Or there is always the four seasons !

name: W Seattle
title: “Wow - This place blows. Save yourself.”
text:
I stay in downtown Seattle every week. Mostly at the Grand Hyatt and the Hyatt at Olive 8. Trust me. Those properties are WAY better. This place is horrible. tiny rooms, I get a fantastic view of the parking garage so when cars have their headlights on you get wonderful night lights. (They offered a free movie to cover it, but I mean. who watches movies when on business travel)
So here's the thing. I'm not familiar with SPG, but apparently there is this green program where they don't clean your rooms or give you new shampoo. Anyways - I declined it on check-in. But for whatever reason, they kept it on. When you work late on business travel, the last thing you want to do is to come back to a room that has no new towels, shampoo or just basic house keeping. Am I a little messy? yes. but..that's the point of staying in a hotel for business travel. You can focus on why you are in the city in the first place. 
When I went to complain, I got about lukewarm support and even challenges to my complaints. 
Just do yourself a favor, don't stay here for work. The W's are cool and chic...but not very helpful for a good nights rest.

name: SpringHill Suites Seattle Downtown/South Lake Union
title: “One of the best”
text: This is one of the best hotels I have stayed in for a long while. The hotel offers a very friendly and fast check-in. The rooms are great, TV, fridge, microwave, sleeping and sitting area, a nice bathroom with separated area for the shower and bathtub. It was extremely clean, absolutely no mould around the tile in the bath. The breakfast which is included in the rate is excellent. From waffles, to saussage, eggs, potatoes, pastry, breads, cereal, even oatmeal, fruit, juice and coffee. I was extremely impress with this hotel. Also free wifi in the rooms and lobby. There is a small bar in the lobby also a restaurant that serves dinner. It is about a 10 minute walk to downtown, there is a 24 hour fitness center across the street, other than that not much in the immediate area.

name: SpringHill Suites Seattle Downtown/South Lake Union
title: “Great hotel for family”
text: My husband and I traveled to Seattle in the beginning of September over Labor Day weekend with our 5 year old daughter and 4 month old son. It was his first ever trip and it was great! The room was spacious and accommodated the 4 of us and all our gear. I wouldn't call it a real "suite", though, since there was no wall dividing the bedroom area and the living area, just a quarter-wall, but it worked for us since we wanted our daughter sleeping close by. Breakfast was great in the morning. The location wasn't bad, close to all the major attractions. They did have a shuttle that brought guests to some of the attractions but unfortunately it brought us to the Space Needle and didn't pick us up! We had booked the shuttle back but the driver had apparently forgotten about us. We waited for about 45 minutes and called the hotel, who paid for us to get a cab ride back. Other than this it was a great place to stay at a reasonable price.

name: SpringHill Suites Seattle Downtown/South Lake Union
title: “Far Out”
text:
My wife and I decided to take a vacation to Seattle. Apparently, the entire population of North America had the same idea. The closest I could get to downtown was this SpringHill Suites. I wish we'd just chosen another city or another time.
The "suite" was small, as with all such hotels of this sort, but was clean. As other reviewers have pointed out, there was some noise. The breakfast was excellent. The bed was hard as a rock and the pillows were abominable--even the replacements we asked them to give us. Free internet access was nice. 
Our main problem--it was a half- to three-quarter mile walk to any really decent restaurant. And the walk led through a questionable neighborhood. I was negatively impressed by the location, and would not stay here again.
Oh, yes. We had a car (parked at $20 per night), but parking in downtown Seattle is a proble,, and quite expensive.

name: Hilton Seattle Airport & Conference Center
title: “memorable”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Seattle Hilton (Airport) in June, using it as a launch for the beginning of our 25th anniversary cruise. We were pleasantly surprised at the beauty of the gardens, and the spaciousness of the rooms. We expected little from a airport hotel, and were delighted with our stay there. One of the little touchs that I particularly liked, was a huge glass modern art decanter filled with water, ice and lemons adjacent to the registration desk. It looked so refreshing and welcomed us in the most beautiful way.

name: The Peabody Memphis
title: “Don't get an adjoining room.”
text:
My husband and I went to Memphis for a weekend trip to see a concert at the Orpheum. We decided to stay in the downtown area, so we got a room for the weekend at The Peabody. We got the Bed & Breakfast package. It was Mother's Day weekend. We got in our room in the afternoon on Friday. The room seemed nice and quiet. We noticed we had an adjoining room door. We didn't hear anything, so we hoped for the best. We went out for supper and walked around Beale Street. Got back to the room and kept hearing the guy next door (adjoining room) yelling. He apparently was watching the Memphis Grizzlies basketball game and every time they scored, he yelled, "Booom!".
We luckily had a sound machine and got to sleep in between the Booms. The next day we left and did some sightseeing downtown and came back in the afternoon. We couldn't hear anybody at this time, but before we left for supper and the concert, we heard several women talking and laughing. It seemed as if they were almost in the same room with us. We got back late from the concert and they were still having a good time. We used our sound machine again and finally got to sleep.
I don't know if it was the thinness of the walls or the door, but it wasn't a pleasant experience. The room on the other side of us, we never heard anything. So, I can only assume the door wasn't insulated enough between the two rooms.
The room seemed nice, but upon further "inspection" we noticed an extension cord that was behind the bed and used for several lamps in front of the window. The bathroom was small with hardly any counter space. There was limited space to put your toiletry case on as well.
The bed & breakfast package came with breakfast in their restaurant for the buffet. The breakfast was great and the service (once you got in) was excellent. Unfortunately, the ladies at the hostess station seemed to have no clue. They were the ones busing tables and seating people. It seemed as if they were short staffed, but then again it also appeared as if this was normal. I will give them the benefit of the doubt, so maybe they didn't staff enough for the holiday weekend.
The ducks are okay to stay and watch, but not worth the wait. There was a crown starting at 30 minutes before the time for the ducks to arrive. The guy who takes care of the ducks started with his story about 20 minutes before. Then it took forever for the elevator to finally get there with the ducks, promptly at 11 AM. They quickly walked the red carpet to the fountain. Very hard to see them with all the kids and people around, much less get a photo of them as the waddle the red carpet. Once you see it, it's not worth seeing again.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Seattle Airport
title: “Convenient lovely hotel”
text: We stayed at the Doubletree on the backend of our Aslaskan cruise. We just needed one night and wanted something close to the airport. This is a very nice hotel with an excellent shuttle service. The room was large and clean. The bathroom was very large, but had a bathtub instead of just a shower which we didn't care for. Had a little trouble with the faucet in the tub, but not enough to call them. We used the shuttle a total of four times in our short stay. We were able to use the train service from the airport to downtown and Pike's Market. All in all, it was very convenient. The only negative was the restaurant in the hotel. We thought it was very expensive for what you got for food and cocktails. We had also eaten twice at the restaurant in the Maxwell Hotel and it was much better and more moderately priced. However, other than the restaurant the hotel was very good.

name: Comfort Inn Downtown
title: “the best hotel downtown”
text: this hotel is close to all the action downtown. the reception staff a really friendly. there's 24 security. rooms are big and clean. there's free internet access in reception. if you need a cab anywhere they will be happy to call jim who is a really friendly and helpful cab driver. this is the best of the best in this price range.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Executive Inn
title: “shower stall unclean”
text: bathroom shower stall hadn't been cleaned and the walls were COVERED with another woman's hair during our stay on Sept. 12 and 13. Yuch!

name: Hotel Max
title: “VERY clean, awesome bed”
text:
Can't say enough good things about this hotel. Super clean, comfy bed, staff very professional and helpful, centrally located (can walk to so many things), modern decor. I know some people have complained about the tiny rooms and bathrooms. That didn't really bother me and my partner, but then again, we don't have kids and we're used to living in small spaces. 
Will definitely stay again when we go back to Seattle.

name: Comfort Inn Downtown
title: “Dont stay here!”
text: Just returned from a fantastic time in fabulous Memphis with no thanks to the awful Comfort Inn. The reception/breakfast area is pokey and dated. The room was in dire need of renovation. The carpet was threadbare and you wouldn't walk on it in your bare feet in a fit as it looked and felt filthy. The funiture has seen better days but not in this century. The breakfast was disgusting. We checked out after one night and moved to the thousand times more superior Peabody. The location of the Comfort Inn is fine if you want to visit Mud Island or the Pyramid but it is a 15 minute walk to Beale Street. Wouldn't reccommend this hotel to my worst enemy.

name: Renaissance Seattle Hotel
title: “Disappointed in Seattle”
text: We got a last minute deal at this 4 star hotel, and while the room itself was very nice, we were not very satisfied with our experience. It was a bit of a walk from the downtown core, the hotel parking costs were double that of a 3 1/2 star hotel, and there was an extra charge for wifi in our room. It was a busy weekend, and it took forever to get anywhere in the elevators (there are 6) due to long waits for an elevator, then to multiple stops on each trip. In addition, our car had to be valet-parked offsite as it was "overheight" (it was over 6'2"), and they left it on the street outside the hotel entrance for over 5 hours at night as they were "very busy" and "hadn't had time to take it" over to to other garage. IT only got moved after we brought it to their attention. We won't be going back to this hotel, as we have stayed just as nice rooms in Seattle for the same price with a more suitable slate of options.

name: Hotel Max
title: “Artistic hotel in good location”
text:
This hip hotel is located conveniently near Westlake station and the monorail terminal which takes you to the space needle. We found Seattle relatively small anyway, and it was no problem walking to pike place market or space needle from the hotel.
Yes, the rooms are small (queen: 190-230 sq. ft / 18-21 sq. m). They say that they have many different room layouts. We didn't carry excessive baggage with us, so this wasn't really an issue.
The room was clean and the bed was really comfy. They have different pillows available you could order to your room.
Staff in the lobby was very friendly, but couldn't give us proficient information about the usual tourist questions. The price was also a bit high, especially considering the small room. But it was a pleasant stay, so we can't really complain and would stay there again any time.

name: Hotel Max
title: “Boutique in Seattle”
text: The property was great, centrally located and walking distance to the light rail and Pike Place Market. We had a ton of great restaurants in the area to choose from. The room was a good size, had a pillow and spiritual texts menu. The bathroom was a little small but had a tub and a shower, separate water closet. The electronic key card was of Nirvana and the decor in the hotel was modern. I enjoyed the stay and would stay again next time in Seattle.

name: Renaissance Seattle Hotel
title: “Not bad”
text: It is what it is. I guess for near $300 a night (after the taxes and valet charges catch up with you) you would at least get some WiFi included with your stay. Not to mention that when you pull up the valet would be there to actually get your car, take your gas and there wouldn't be only two people to check in a crowd of thirty. The rooms are nice, clean, and stocked. There was a mini-fridge that did not charge you each time you opened it. Very easy access to the freeway, so this would be a good stop on your way north to Canada.

name: Days Inn Seattle North
title: “Way better than we ever expected”
text: Rooms were clean, well maintained. Can't beat the price. Service was excellant. Well recommended, will stay there again next time. Pleasantly surprized in all categories.

name: Seattle Pacific Hotel
title: “Awful”
text: Booked by mistake. We thought it was a different property. What a disaster. This place is the definition of a dump. Dirty, beat up, broken furniture, doors are not secure, mold in shower, plumbing is terrible, parking terrible, i can keep on going but if you stay there, check out. Service is terrible. It is a crime that this place is open let alone charges $100 nightly.

name: The Westin Seattle
title: “Superb hotel in Downtown Seattle”
text:
Great hotel for shopping and close to the famous Pike Pier fish market. Hotel very spacious and clean and the staff were very helpful..We stayed at this hotel prior to going on a cruise and the staff were genuinely pleased that you were having a nice time and very helpful when we were asking questions about the area...The hotel is very close to everything that you would require from a stop over, but would also be a great place to stay for more than the 2 days that we were there.
 Nice restaurant and bar facilities although I personally thought a bit expensive..No need to worry about that though as loads of restaurants and bars in close walking distance

name: Hilton Seattle Airport & Conference Center
title: “Great stay with a few little annoyances.”
text:
In general, I've found that hotels which house airline crews are comfortable and reasonably priced. So, when i saw a Japanese airline crew at the check in desk, I was set for a comfortable room and a great meal. But my personal opinion of this property is somewhat mixed. 
As others have commented, Spencers, the hotel's restaurant, is more a big, noisy community tavern than a place to have a quiet meal. Whether it is expensive or not is beside the point. I find the place offputting. And from from the number of room service trays in the hallways, I'd say others probably agreed with me.
Another issue I had was the walk to the parking garage. Okay, I'll be 66 next birthday, but I'm in pretty good shape. I found that once on the main floor, the walk to the garage was at least a city-block. Picture the hotel as the shape of a shoe box. My room was at the front of the box. The parking structure was out the back of the box and in another buildng that faces a street a block away. Granted they do valet parking. But if what you remember about the property is the long, long walk to the parking garage, then the property can't possibly be five star.
I will say I had a comfortable room. And in response to the reviewer who complained about the housekeeping, I find that hard to believe. I got two to three knocks on my door in the morning with offers to clean my room. This is *with* my 'Do Not Disturb' sign posted on my doorknob. 
Perhaps the maids can't read? No matter -- better clean than dirty.
As I say, my room was comfortable and at night I slept like a baby. There was a strong Wifi signal and I moved some gigantic graphics files -- whatever the cost -- so I feel I got my money's worth from the hotel's Internet. I also met some really nice people here who I exchanged business cards with. I guess that's what you *really* expect from a hotel.

name: Comfort Inn & Suites Seattle
title: “Enjoyed our stay at the Comfort Inn”
text:
When looking for a good hotel, without paying an arm and a leg we chose the Comfort Inn on Aurora Ave (about $100.00 a night, before taxes, etc.) It is an easy drive to and from the airport on Route 99 - in fact, it only took us about 30 minutes to get to the airport for a 9 AM flight when we left. 
The front desk staff was great, we had a quick check-in and the room was better-than-average. The room was clean and neat both times we stayed there. As it turns out, we booked it for our first and last night in WA. 
They also had a great breakfast buffet! We will likely return when visiting in the future.

name: Renaissance Seattle Hotel
title: “Small beds but GREAT Concierge service !”
text: I was in Seattle with my family for a couple of days and stayed 3 nights at the Renaissance in a double beds bedroom. The bed are too small and very bouncy ... it was not the best sleep we had ! But the location is great and the concierges are super nice and efficient. We had to book tickets to Vancouver, to find a restaurant, to have our rental car repaired and the concierges (Lucy, fred and Beth) helped us A LOT, always with a big smile and a lot of energy ! Will I coe back ? Certainly : you feel in a great hotel when you find such a great service !

name: Renaissance Seattle Hotel
title: “Good location. Small rooms”
text: The hotel was fine. Nothing special and we had a less than lovely view of the highway. The hotel staff were very nice and I love that the provide Aveda products!. My only complaint is that the room was very cramped.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Seattle Airport
title: “Very nice property”
text: Friendly staff, top notch decor and facilities, and great proximity to Sea-Tac. I always try and stay here when passing through Seattle.

name: Motel 6 Seattle Sea-Tac Airport South
title: “Sheeeeeeeesh”
text: My wife and I stayed here for a high school basketball tourney.Check in was fine....... until they lost our reservations.Upon arriving we had to pay $8.00 more than agreed......I was alittle upset but very tired,so I went ahead and payed. About 2:AM the police had to break up a fight in the room across the way from ours.....think I'll stay somewhere else next year............

name: The Westin Seattle
title: “What a Veiw!”
text: Stayed here with some SPG points back in Nov. Was a great place. A bit older but with nice rooms. Our view was on the Space Needle. Loved it. The location is pretty good and within walking distance of most things. I'd recommend a high floor. The front desk staff was very friendly.

name: The Westin Seattle
title: “A great business trip”
text:
The Westin is a very elegant modern hotel at one edge of the CBD in Seattle. My room was very large with a huge king sized bed and decent bathroom. 
Television reception was not perfect - not digital quality! - and was interested as ever in advertisements in America - a prize on one morning call in show was an all expenses paid trip to New York including free colonoscopy !!! Oh brave new world that has such people in it!
Very relaxing place to be. Good view across the city. Think you probably need to be higher than level 20 to get picturesque views of the sound.
Really good for access to the metro back to the airport. Couldnt face making conversation with a Slavic driver in a town car for 30 minutes so had an entertaining 40 minute ride interacting with the locals :)
[... no-one seemed in need of a colonoscopy, so I didn't use that opening line.]

name: Seattle Pacific Hotel
title: “a solid DON'T STAY HERE!! Please don't make this to yourself...”
text:
I deserved it because I had the chance to read many bad reviews about this place... the factor was the price, but the place is not that cheap either, for what you have to go through.
Just few facts:
We arrived there to find out we had no reservation (?!?). Many minutes later, the reservation "re-appeared". Not sure what happeded.
Next morning, we wanted to have breakfast (included) but only some apples, bread and muffins were served. I asked one guy at the frontdesk about butter but he responded: "no butter, no"... I guess he doesn't speak English.
Later, at 11:00 we got a phone call from frontdesk "Hey, you staying? if not, checkout, 11:00 o'clock, bye" -- hehe, wow. And it doesn't end there, 'cause 10 min later one guy knocked the door and walked in when I opended... hahaha... wow! my girldfriend was so upset she got into the bathroom to avoid the guy.
the guy checked for the TV remote, check on the fridge and even look over the sheets of the bed (can you believe it? and we were still there!!)
So, if you are staying in Downton Seattle, I recommend going to The Moore (european style, but closer to downtown) or pay a few more bucks and stay at the Travelers Inn or Days Inn, not this pseudo-hotel... you don't deserve this.

name: Hotel Seattle
title: “Old and Rundown”
text: The location was pretty nice, although it was on a steep hill. The TV was very old. We had problems with the heater in our room and had to bang on it a lot. We stayed here for a night and then moved to the Comfort Inn by the airport. It was too expensive to stay here for the value of the hotel.

name: Hotel Max
title: “Great location, chic, but "European" sized rooms :)”
text:
Hotel Max is in a good location, right downtown in just a few minutes from Pike Place Market, great restaurants, etc. It's got a cool rock/music theme, and is a good value.
Just be aware, the hotel is a boutique hotel, and has a bit of European sizing, i.e. smaller than Americans may be used to. Depending on the floor you're on, you might have a very, very small bathroom. I was on the 5th floor, but my colleagues on 9th and 10th floors said their bathrooms were small, but not quite as small as mine.
All in all, good price, good location, just be prepared for smaller dimensions.

name: Econo Lodge SeaTac Airport
title: “disgusting dirt bag hotel complete with trashy fight out front at 2am!”
text:
my husband and I stayed here for 1 night and we were just looking for a cheap place to sleep before we flew out of SeaTac the next day. well, "cheap" comes in every form here. from the creepy guy sitting at the computer all night long looking up naughty websites, to the arguing couple out front at 2am that led to the police showing up... 
the "free" breakfast is just cereal and coffee, the jacuzzi is smaller than a bathtub and we didn't go in it in fear of catching some kind of rash, and the gym facilites is just an exercise bike.
this place smelled bad and was so dirty, i couldn't wait for morning to come. we vowed to each other that we will never ever stay at a place like this again. 
on the other hand, the guy at the front desk was very nice and helpful, and the rest of the staff was ok too. they probably feel really bad for the people that decide to stay there!

name: Seattle Pacific Hotel
title: “A good value for $69”
text: My family (of 3) stayed at the Vagabond in late June 2004 and found it a decent place for the price. The tub was peeling because a former owner had painted it, but otherwise everything worked. The air conditioning unit drowned out the street noises, so we had no trouble sleeping. There was some confusion about the price, since the phone reservation people quoted me a price of $69 and the receptionist had it as $79, but the night clerk was able to fix the problem. The location was near public transportation and three blocks from the Space Needle. We spent most of our time outside the hotel, so we didn't care what the hall carpet looked like. With other hotels downtown starting at $125 and up, we thought we got what we paid for.

name: Warwick Seattle Hotel
title: “Really bad”
text: My wife and I had prepaid for two nights and after the first we gave up and moved out. What a dump, I can not believe they had such dirty carpets and threadbare linen, on the bed, they even had holes in them. To be honest, until they completely remodel the place I would not recommend anyone staying there. We didn't even care we had to pay again at a different hotel. Just as long as we were not staying there.

name: Warwick Seattle Hotel
title: “Walking distance to Pike's and decent.”
text:
However--- they were doing massive construction and woke me up at 7am every morning. Not exactly how I wanted to spend my vacation. I called the front desk to see if they had earplugs.... they did not....and didn't seem to care about my lack of a good night's sleep. 
Other than that...it is a decent hotel. Nothing fancy or special.

name: Executive Hotel Pacific
title: “Good Value/Location”
text:
