WHY I CHOSE THIS HOTEL: location (proximity to business destination); price (I work at a non-profit); positive reviews.
ABOUT ME: Beyond the basics, the main things I look for in a hotel are clean rooms and reliable Internet access; don't need much else.
THE BAD: 
Upon check-in, the front desk person had difficulties pulling up my reservation because the online-reservation system will occasionally sort the guest names by Prefix instead of the person's name--they couldn't find me under Smith or John, but rather "Mister." They finally figured it out, but FYI.
The Elevators: I stayed four nights. During that time, one day the elevators seemed sluggish and we had to try a couple times to close the doors and go. One evening *both* elevators were stalled at the lobby. Several other guests, a hotel staff member, and I tried repeatedly to get it to go, but were unsuccessful. I ended up taking the 6 flights of stairs to my room that night. It definitely is an intermittent problem, but you might want to request a lower-floor room just in case.
The Internet: was spotty. I was able to connect simply enough, but kept getting dropped intermittently.
No In-Room Desk: instead, one of the bedside tables had a circular glass top and power outlets. I tried sitting at this table using the chair and ottoman available but it was an ergonomic nightmare for me. This coupled with the WiFi issues made it more difficult to work in-room.
THE GOOD:
Service Staff: Every person I encountered was friendly and helpful.
Room: Although the building is a bit older than some, the rooms were serviceable and clean. Bed was comfy; A/C controls worked; quick and ample hot water. Rooms tend to the smaller side. I had a room with one double bed and found it plenty big for me, but a couple with more than 1 bag each might be a bit of a squeeze.
Price: Hard to beat that for the location.
Location: Within walking distance of Pike Place Market, Seattle Art Museum, the Central Library, Pioneer Square; a short bus or cab ride to many other attractions. 3 blocks to the University Street light rail station (which costs $2.75 for a one-way trip to the airport). Very convenient.
Wine Tasting: I was a bit dubious when the Web site promoted daily "hosted complimentary evening wine receptions" but it turned out to be a nice way to unwind and meet fellow guests.
VERDICT: I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again if traveling solo or as a couple for leisure. I would *consider* staying again for business, but with revised expectations about working in-room.

name: Travelodge Seattle by the Space Needle
title: “Good value for great location.”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Travelodge by the Space Needle at the end of October. The room was clean and the staff was friendly. The walls are pretty thin though, so if you're a light sleeper ear plugs are handy! Free breakfast was decent.

name: BEST WESTERN Airport Executel
title: “Dingy and Depressing”
text: I never expect luxury accommodations at airport motels, but this place was the pits! As soon as we drove up to the place, we knew it was a mistake. The halls were dark and musty. The rooms were sorely in need of updating and also had a musty odor. The mattress was old and uncomfortable, too. The high speed internet access in the room didn't work, and the staff was no help in resolving the issue. If you have any alternatives, stay somewhere else.

name: Seattle Pacific Hotel
title: “Terrible! Use at own risk!”
text: We stayed here in June '03. It was terrible. The room was dirty and grungy looking with all the tile and tub in the bathroom painted and peeling badly. I wouldn't let my daughter have a bath in it! The breakfast was nothing more than day-old pastries, if you could actually get any. The staff would only put out a few dozen and when gone.. oh well. The pool was terrible as well, tiles missing and dirty. When we checked in they also tries to pull a fast one as well. We booked and payed in full through Expedia. They tried to make us pay again. Thank goodness I had a printed confirmation showing it was paid in full. I would defeinitely say this place is a use at your own risk!

name: Travelodge Seattle by the Space Needle
title: “NOt the best room”
text:
2 things : the bathroom door was practically touching the bed which wasn't too nice considering it's a room that's supposed to accommodate up to 5 people. And if anyone needed to use the bathroom at night they had to snug right up to the bed to get to it and disturb the person trying to sleep.
Put some curtains on the windows!

name: Travelodge Seattle by the Space Needle
title: “Travelodge stay”
text:
I was unhappy with the cleanliness of my room. When I arrived in my room the trash had not been taken out, and the shower appeared to have not been cleaned. 
I was also disappointed with the lack of vegan options at breakfast. Even just offering soy milk would be great.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Seattle Downtown / Lake Union
title: “It's a place to sleep.”
text:
The rooms and hotel are a bit outdated. The bed was pretty hard for me - although I've read complaints that they were too soft. 
Service at the front desk was mediocre, and it was hard to get the attendant's attention - even with few people around. 
The breakfast buffet was good...typical Marriott quality. No complaints there. I think this is a great hotel for people on business trips, but nothing more than that since its so far away from the city.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Seattle Downtown / Lake Union
title: “Good Overnight in Seattle”
text: We needed a quick place to stay on our way to our cruise. The Courtyard Marriott, despite expensive parking ($20, but self-park with ins-and-outs, which was great), was just right. Clean room and perfectly located. Unfortunately, there was a great deal of street noise, so it's a good thing I was exhausted.

name: Hotel Max
title: “Excellent hotel for winter travels”
text: We've stayed at Hotel Max five or six times and always a treat. Beds and pillows are so comfortable. Always clean, location is superb for shopping, love the happy hour at the restaruant next door. And they always have a great winter special. I would highly recomend to another single/couple staying in downtown Seattle.

name: Travelodge Seattle University
title: “Not worth it...”
text: We stayed here for a college visit to UDub.... the location was great...right next to campus. However, that is where the greatness ends! The price was way too high for this place. The website for the Travelodge advertises that it is a non-smoking facility, however, we walked into the hallway and there was a strong smell of smoke throughout the building. As we continued down the hall, we could smell the cleaning chemicals that were used for the rooms and it was almost unbearable. The floors were disgusting and looked like they hadn't been replaced since the place opened! The room was ok... floor was still gross and the room was very outdated.... big spider on ceiling and just run-down looking but it wasn't super dirty or anything. After staying in the room for a few minutes we actually decided to leave and get another hotel in Bellevue... worth it!!! I must say the cleaning staff was very nice and concerned about how the room presented and even offered to help us load our car as we were leaving. This place just ins't worth the price!

name: Hilton Seattle
title: “Perfect business hotel!”
text: The hotel is centrally located and a typical Hilton business hotel. The Top of the Hilton was nice with great view and food.

name: Red Roof Inn Seattle Airport - SEATAC
title: “Outstanding Customer Service”
text: I arranged for my adult age daughter to stay here after a very late flight arrival from Alaska. Even after several changes needed to be made due to a missed flight - the staff at this hotel were very accomodating and when she finally arrived, the shuttle picked her up promptly and she settled in quickly and comfortably. I asked for a recomendation for limo service on the day of departure to transport my daughter to her final destination and "Seattle Metro" - (Rick) was the hotels' choice. This proved to be a "God Send" as Rick personally stayed in touch with me during the several day process of my daughters' arrival to Seattle and her ultimate departure. Rick actually called me when she did not initially arrive, (even before my daughter called) which allowed me more time to assist in re-booking her flight. Rick assisted my daughter with her luggage and called me again once she had arrived at her destination, to assure me she had arrived safely. The staff at the hotel were fabulous as well - Sean specifically at the front desk remained patient and processed my numerous telephone calls to the hotel, with friendly and efficient service. Thank you to all the folks at this hotel and to Rick with Seattle Metro Transportation Services for your assistance. Although I have not mentioned this, my daughter was very ill and was to be admitted to a nearby hospital, making this ordeal so very stressful on our family ( we live thousands of miles away ) Your caring and efficient customer service, made this situation so very much easier. THANK YOU !

name: The Peabody Memphis
title: “Loved the feel of a "classic hotel"”
text:
The room was extremely spacious with a king size bed, a full size couch, dress, two armchairs end table, desk and coffee table and walk-in closet. And there was still lots of room to move around! Very quiet, lots of towels.
If you want to watch the marching ducks, a good place to see them march is from the mezzanine if you can't get a view by the fountain.
The lobby bar is outrageously expensive($15 martini and $9 beer) and the service was terrible. In addition, it is very crowded and the acoustics make it loud.
There is a mandatory $11.95 daily service charge which makes your internet connection "free".

name: Red Roof Inn Seattle Airport - SEATAC
title: “Reasonable, friendly, clean”
text: We stayed here both before our early flight to Europe and again on the way back. Among our fellow guests, we noticed, were other senior travellers as well as young families who have also discovered this hotel. Its location is very near the airport, and free shuttle service is available every 20 minutes. Since we look for good value and basic comfort in our accommodations when we travel rather than glamour, this hotel filled the bill. We asked the friendly staff person at the desk for a room on the top floor since we had read in other reviews that this hotel can be noisy, and we received a spacious room with a huge bathroom in a quiet corner of the building. The room was clean and the beds were comfortable. Travellers should be aware, however, that this hotel has no restaurant. But there is a international chain restaurant just down the street with great food and terrific deals for breakfast. Coffee is available in the lobby area downstairs for those who need a kickstart before heading for the restaurant. The first night of our stay, we took advantage of the SoundTansit light rail from the station located down the street to explore downtown Seattle. The ride into the heart of the city on this sleek, fast rail system was fun and took us right into the heart of the city.

name: The Peabody Memphis
title: “the Peabody made our Memphis trip perfect”
text:
our trip to Memphis was to visit Graceland and we stayed at the Peabody hotel on 7/10/10 for three nights, we arrived at the Peabody early and was very pleased that our room was ready for us, check in was very quick and the staff were friendly and polite. the lobby is so beautiful and the ducks in the fountain are amazing, on arrival at our room we were a bit shocked to find we were right next to the elevator and my husband is a very light sleeper i thought we might have problems but we said we would see how noisy it was the first night and if it was a problem we would ask if we could move, we didn't need to i think because the bed was so comfy my husband slept like a log and he never heard a thing. the rooms were lovely and it was just a pleasure to stay here. we had our breakfast in the restaurant in the hotel and that was very good too,all the hotel staff were lovely, especially the night bell man who when i couldn't sleep and went to sit outside in the early hours he stood with me and chatted and i felt very safe, i wish i had asked him his name so i could let the hotel manager know because during our three night stay i saw how hard he worked and how polite he was to the guests he really is a credit to the Peabody hotel.
 Graceland was amazing and we also booked a trip to tupelo to Elvis's birthplace, we booked with mikes Memphis tours and he picked us up from the Peabody and we spent the day with mike and his partner sue they took us around the birthplace and loads of other places that were important in Elvis's life, we had a lovely day with them and mike and Sue's knowledge on Elvis was amazing. i would recommend the Peabody hotel to everyone it made our holiday special and hope one day we will be able to return.

name: Holiday Inn Express Seattle City Center
title: “perfect location”
text: Stayed overnight on the 4th floor before going on a cruise. Beautiful view of the Space Needle where we walked tthe next day. Friendly staff and ok breakfast. Used Seattle Best Car Service from airport to hotel then to pier then back to airport for a package price. Good deal!

name: Hotel Nexus Seattle
title: “Excellent customer service and a great room!”
text: I walked up to the front desk after driving for three hours to Seattle and was in a lousy mood but was soon put at ease by the staff when I was given excellent customer service. I am a student and needed a great deal on a room and the guy at the front desk told me that he could give me a discounted rate and offered me coffee, which made me very happy. I found the room to be clean and the beds very comfortable. I will definitely be staying there again the next time I am in town.

name: Red Roof Inn Seattle Airport - SEATAC
title: “Good but can be best...”
text:
Room and other services are good,.
Problems with internet connection..worst speed ever...Complained to staff but they had no solution.
So if you need good internet dnt come otherwise its a good choice...

name: Travelodge Seattle by the Space Needle
title: “Pretty good stay, ok rooms, a bit pricey but good location”
text: The room and hotel was pretty dated but.. beds were comfy. Close to space needle we walked easily there. We even walked down to the piers but it was a hike back. Breakfast was really good but tight room. Igot a room with a fridge but it didnt work. The one thing the beds are super high and I have a toddler who fell out of bed in the middle of the night. It was kind of scary not sure why they are so high.

name: Holiday Inn Express Seattle City Center
title: “Clean spacious room with decent breakfast”
text: Stayed for two nights with extended family, with young kids. The room was spacious. The bathroom was clean. Breakfast was decent. The breakfast room has two attendants at all time, so the food was always well stocked. The location of the hotel was great. We walked to the Space Needle. There's also a Walgreens close by, so it was very convenience. I would definitely stay here again.

name: W Seattle
title: “Great Location, fantastic service, can't wait to return”
text:
Stayed at the W from Aug 2 - 5th, 2009. Could not find anything to fault with this trendy hotel in a great location. Easy to walk everywher. Very quiet, had a 'wonderful" room on the 19th floor. No waiting for elevators, newspaper daily, very comfortable room with roomy sofa under window. DVD player, ipod dock, great bed, small fridge containing minibar.
All staff were incredibly helpful and friendly. Concierge right by the elevator always ready to answer questions or help plan sightseeing etc.
We did not dine at the hotel, lots of available options nearby from fine dining to casual breakfast places. 
Very trendy front desk and lobby / living room area. Elevators had great music, hallways are dimly lit, a good idea seems to keep noise down in the hallways. 
All in all a very memorable trip, can't wait to stay at the "W" again !

name: Sixth Avenue Inn
title: “Glorified parking lot”
text:
Because there wasso much to see and do in Seattle, this place really was just a great place to park our car. Convenient to Pike's Place and restaurants, this hotel is a little expensive to use only for sleeping!
The staff was friendly and helpful and the room was clean, if tiny! McDonald's is right next door for a quick breakfast.

name: Quality Inn & Suites Seattle
title: “Would go back again”
text:
We had a great stay at the quality inn.
What I noticed about it is that it has taken all previous reviews into account and the hotel is being refurbished. The lift is being replaced and the corridors are being painted. So at the moment they dont look the best but that did not bother us.
The rooms were really clean and perfect for our overnight trip. Breakfast in the morning was included but finished a bit early for our liken at 9:30am.
Staff were so friendly and helpful, and assisted us in any questions we had.
The heated pool/hot tub area is lovely and there was nothing better than coming home after walking around seattle and relaxing in them. (open until midnight)
Location is the best thing about this hotel and it is so close to everything especially the Space Needle.
All in all a great stay and fantasic value for money.

name: Quality Inn & Suites Seattle
title: “Update to hotel”
text:
Stayed at the Quality Inn on John Street - Seattle Center. The hotel is what you are paying for which means the following to me. Good price for the other hotels in the area. Towels that are a bit scratchy & rough. Lower grade bed, but good clean sheets. Here are the positives: Great location to Space Needle (3 blocks), Excellent help from the front desk - thanks Chris, good location to rental car locations if needed, standard, but filing free breakfast bar, low cost for parking for other hotels in the area, fridge & microwave in the room, two good grocery stores within 1-2 blocks, overall good price for budget.
Lows: Hotel carpet is worn, not a lot of sit down places to eat nearby, yes- the elevators are slow, but your on vacation, budget hotel as stated above.

name: Inn at Queen Anne
title: “The Service is amazing!”
text: We had friends recommend the Inn at Queen Anne and we were not disappointed. We went for just a few days to celebrate my husband's birthday-and at first the Inn isn't awe-inspiring. It used to be an old apartment complex so the building is rather post-WWII drab. The rooms are rustic, the bathroom fixtures antique-ey, our room had a small kitchenette with an ancient stove. Ancient in a GOOD way though, everything worked really well-hot water, all electric-it was a neat touch feeling like we were stepping back in time. I realized how terrific this place was when I asked at the front desk for an iron and a hair dryer. Literally two minutes later, there was a parade of employees carrying all of the requested items to our room and installing them, making sure everything was *perfect*. We felt like royalty! The next day was more of the same level of service. That morning we requested the complimentary shuttle to the pier so we could take the ferry over to Bainsbridge. The lady behind the desk apologized and said the car had just left and wouldn't return for at least 30 minutes. She asked if we could wait (we couldn't) so she gave us cab fare from the drawer, and called us a cab! The cab was there within 5 min. and we had free fare and tip. Amazing. Last but not least, the Inn is super close to EVERYTHING...we could walk to the Space Needle, EMP, record store (really cool, eclectic record store a block away), bars, restaurants, etc. We both loved our stay there and will definitely revisit next time we're in the Emerald City!

name: Quality Inn & Suites Seattle
title: “NOT SO Quality Inn”
text:
This hotel offers a cruise and park special - 238 dollars, excellent package considering they include up to 2 weeks parking and the shuttle back and forth to the ship. We stayed at the Maxwell for three nights before moving here so we were a little spoiled. As we were already in town and were told that the parking was limited we arrived early. Rooms were not available so we waited in the lobby. The lobby area is run down, outdated and dirty. Our room 219 was ready at about 1:30 which was fine - it is a very busy hotel. We took the elevator up - slow and creaky! Room 219 was disgusting, the carpets filthy and badly stained. I quickly looked down the hall at some other rooms, as they were being cleaned, and went back to the front desk. I asked the women for another room at the other end of the hall. She asked if the room had been cleaned and I said yes but that it was still disgusting and I was not about to sleep in it. She moved us to another room that was a bit better. The hotel has great potential ! Good location, indoor pool and work out room. Large breakfast area and parts of it have been updated. They need to update, clean and get new furniture for the lobby. The rooms and hallways all need to be completely refurbished. The elevators also need to be updated - they literally creek and are very slow. Stairs are easily accessible, but when you have several suitcases an elevator is necessary. They have laundry facilities but when we used the dryer it ruined two white shirts , they came out covered in grease!!
For Seattle this is the best cruise and park package available but if I weren't going to use that particular package I would recommend you go somewhere else until this place cleans up its act!

name: Quality Inn & Suites Seattle
title: “Good value hotel--location, breakfast and clean!!”
text:
We were happy with our recent stay here. Yes, the rooms are small. Yes, the bathrooms are even smaller. But the shower was great, hot water, nice and clean. Everything was clean. 
The elevators are slow, and old, but there are stairs...and the parking is FREE!! We walked everywhere we needed to go, the location was great. Cant complain for the price we paid.
Pillows are tiny though--I mean 2 together are the size of a standard pillow. Take your own.
Breakfast was impressive, there were many choices and it was great (and also FREE!)
Swimming pool was great, a few broken tiles here and there, but nothing horrible. We enjoyed it.
All in all, well worth it. We would stay there again-- I would rather stay here for a reasonable rate, and be able to walk everywhere then have to drive into the city and park downtown everyday!
PS-my recommendation would depend who I was referring, if you want a 4 or 5 star hotel this is not for you. If you want a budget hotel that is affordable, clean and in a good location then this is the hotel for you!

name: Warwick Seattle Hotel
title: “Needs a rennovation”
text:
I am glad I got a discount. The room was clean, but nothing special. In fact the bathroom showed a bit of wear. The size and amenities were no different from a good Best Western. Just as noisy too. Maybe that is why there is a discount.
The service was average.
However, there is a good advantage to this hotel if you have a car. You can park your car yourself and save money doing without valet service. If you approach from Lenora St, however, you have to make two lefts to get to the garage which is to the left of the lobby.
The location is great for Belltown, the Federal Courthouse and the town's retail core.

name: Sixth Avenue Inn
title: “Why the extra charge?”
text: I was fairly satisfied with my stay at the motel--nothing fancy but OK for the pr;ice. The bathroom was really small but the room size was OK and the bed comfy. When I got home, however, I had an email from my credit card with a $25.00 (extra) charge from the motel -- itemized as SIxth Ave. Inn --Restaurant. We didn't ever step foot in the restaurant, never ordered any room service or anything else from there, so why the charge ? I immediately contacted the Inn (by email) asking about it and haven't heard a thing back yet (and it has been over a week now). This has changed my opinion of the place from OK to POOR. Maybe this review will get me an answer.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Seattle Airport
title: “Great hotel very close to the airport and car rental”
text: A good value hotel near the airport and car rental though parking isn't cheap. Staff are helpful. And also they give away good cookies to hotel guests.

name: Hotel Max
title: “Stayed here almost two weeks in November - very restful.”
text:
The Hotel Max has taken an older property and provided a fun flair. The doormen and front desk are very friendly and willing to help. The rooms are a tad small, but for business travel that is alright. The biggest drawback I saw was the manual thermostat on the heating/cooling unit. I would have preferred a wall-mount thermostat.
The Internet quality was average. VPN was sometimes difficult due to latency from their Internet provider.

name: Inn at Queen Anne
title: “Two Thumbs Down”
text:
What a disappointment. This might be fine for the leisure traveler but it's not recommended for the business traveler. 
1. Parking is hit-or-miss. You have to pull up at the curb, go in, and see if they have parking available. If not, you may park on the street at a meter overnight or in a pay lot "within a few blocks of the hotel". 
2. There is no elevator and no mention of this on their website or when you call to make a reservation. 
3. Only "special" rooms have Internet access (this is Seattle!) Again, this is not mentioned anywhere on their website or when I *specifically* asked for the difference in room types. 
4. Rooms are small but servicable. Nothing to write home about. No irons/boards in the room. No coffee service. 
5. No one available to check me out at 6:30am. I left early to try to get to an Internet cafe the desk clerk told me opened at 6am. Uh, it opened at 7:00 and I had to be on my way across town at a meeting by then. 
If I were a leisure traveler, none of this would have bothered me quite so much but as a business traveler, no thanks. You definitely get what you pay for. I doubt I'll be back.

name: Sixth Avenue Inn
title: “I'm Jazzed About This Place”
text: I booked this hotel because of the fact it is across the street from a Jazz Club. I was in town to see Dr John for two nights and you can’t beat the safety and convenience of just having to cross the street to your hotel at night. My room was on the 4th floor and faced the Jazz Club. The Strip Club is on the next block over on the back side of the hotel. But! Don’t think this is a bad area, it is not. The hotel is also surrounded by coffee shops, a salon, McDonalds, Westin Hotel, and office buildings. I am sorry, but I really think too big of a deal is made of the Strip Club being around. From what I saw of Seattle most of downtown was “mixed”. There were Fancy Joints mixed with “sketchy” joints in many areas. I had no problem with the area this hotel is located in. There are bus stops right close. It is true that there is traffic going by. I expect this in a city, so no big deal. I arrived very early and was met with very friendly and helpful service and was checked in right way. I was happy with my room and the view. The bed was comfy, but could have used a “comforter” blanket. I never even had to touch the air-conditioned/heater because it felt just right as it was. I made good use of the microwave/fridge and everything was clean and in good working order. I did not find my room to be “dated” so not sure what other people are expecting. I noticed the tub had a low side so it would be easy to get in/out if you had any mobility issues. Shampoo ect comes from a dispenser and it works just fine. I left a note for the maid to leave me a few extra sugar/coffee mate and she left me plenty. I find some places think a “few” means “one” so I always appreciate when they don’t try and be Stingy with the stuff. There was a restaurant in the hotel that I did not try but I did look over the menu and it seemed to be at a fair price. I think the location of this hotel is great. I walked everywhere to and from it. There isn’t even a need to ride the monorail to the Space Needle if you don’t want to. Another great thing about its location was that it is right next to a Drop off/Pickup location (The Westin) for the Cheap Airport shuttle so you can choose an affordable way to/from airport and only have to cross the street to catch it. They have a secure place to keep your luggage after checkout if you need it. I’d stay here again. My Room was Clean and Comfy, Location was perfect for me, I found the staff Helpful, Happy and Friendly and… really it’s hard to find better than that.

name: Radisson Hotel Seattle Airport
title: “Professional and Clean”
text: The public areas and staff here are brisk, a little cool but efficient, and lend a reassuring competence to the experience. There is no cookie at check-in and no attempt to make you feel that you have "come home," but we are usually arriving late in the evening and leaving early, so it fits fine. Excellent beds, clean bathrooms, and an outstanding breakfast menu. They do have a fine buffet breakfast, but if you have the time to sit and order from the menu, it's worth it--they don't really want you to do that; supplying the buffet keeps the staff busy, but hey, maybe I want my eggs a special way or to experience the original menu items. We walk from the airport to the hotel--takes about 8 minutes, and they do have a prompt shuttle. All-in-all, this place meets our traveling needs four times a year, and we have always been satisfied.

name: Red Roof Inn Seattle Airport - SEATAC
title: “Never Again”
text: We stayed in this hotel in July of 2006 and we will never do it again. Our non-smoking room smelled of smoke worse than the smoking room our travelling companions had, the halls and elevator were filthy and we had several hundred dollars worth of shoes taken from our locked vehicle. There are no signs posted and their corporate offices refused to reimburse us because they do not consider the area high risk despite information to the contrary.

name: Red Lion Hotel on Fifth Avenue Seattle
title: “Better than I expected and a great location”
text:
Stayed here one night on business. Grabbed the room last minute, it was only $70 for a queen. I was expecting it to be of quality inn standard. The parking area is fairly small and I an extra $32 so factor that in.
The check in process was a little more cumbersome than your usual hotel these days.
The elevator is a little dated so I was pleasantly surprised once I reached my room. The room had a great view, was newly renovated, had great furnishings and was very clean!
I have stayed at 1000 and Pan Pacific for 5 times the rate and will definitely think about the Red Lion in the future, the location is perfect for access to downtown. I honestly think its the best value.

name: Mediterranean Inn
title: “Amazing view from the rooftop sundeck!”
text: The view from the room, well that was ONLY the space needle, but the deck was 360. A glass of wine at night, full moon, space needle, beautiful and very romantic. Coffee on the deck in the morning, what a great way to wake up. No crowds, plenty of chairs. On to the room, comfortable, clean, kitchenette, comfortable bed, no complaints. Very nice business center, which we used several times. Convenient location to public transportation, small grocery stores for breakfast items, liquor stores, shopping. There two days, never used a cab. We walked to the needle, pikes market, restaurants along the water, state ferry, etc. Price, about $95 dollars. Would stay there again.

name: Holiday Inn Seattle
title: “It's Clean, friendly but...”
text: After arriving at the hotel with a 7 hour drive behind us we were exhausted ! The check-in was fast and the front desk staff was THE BEST I have ever dealt with ! They were awesome ! We got the parking pass and directions to the garage, ok Big trucks don't fit ! So they give us directions to a lot nearby. OK so truck is aways away & not that secured. Up to our room, WOW it is nicely decorated, super clean , modern with everything you could ever ask for. All is well until we try & sleep. The A/C fan was very noisey, the matress was so hard , I was beside myself to go to sleep, then it started ! We must have had the " River dancers" in the room above us , I guess the floors have no insulation at all ? Then the alarm clock went off ! Should have checked it before I went to bed. So, it is a good place but it maybe not the most restful.

name: BEST WESTERN Loyal Inn
title: “Good location for walking, driving or public transit”
text: Room was spacious and quiet. Bed was comfortable. Windows have sheer curtains only, allowing the early summer morning light to penetrate the room. Staff was friendly and helpful. The large, square sink mitigated splashes on the bathroom counter. The hotel does have a coin laundromat. This is not mentioned on their website or in the room directory. The hotel is two blocks to the free bus zone. Easy walk to Space Needle. We walked the nine blocks to Pike Market without a problem. A cab ride to Columbia Center/Pioneer Square is $8. We used the Budget car rental station two blocks away to rent a car for sightseeing outside of downtown. There is a $2 city tax on the $10 per day parking fee.

name: Coast Gateway Hotel
title: “Everything was great!”
text: Right from the cheerful and helpful shuttle drivers (Especially the gentleman on the late night shift), to the rooms, cleanliness, quietness, front desk staff, ease of printing our boarding passes, free wi-fi, and great breakfast (Loved the waffle maker!) we can find nothing to complain about!

name: Renaissance Seattle Hotel
title: “Good price but ...”
text:
My wife and I spent a night at the hotel in October 2003. I got a package deal ($139) that included parking ($19) and breakfast ($20). 
The rate was pretty good considering what was included and the location of the hotel (downtown Seattle). We could easily walk to the shopping district (6 blocks), and take the monorail from downtown to the Space Needle etc.
Unfortunately, we have numerous little issues with the hotel and its staff. At check-in I asked for a quiet room that would not face the freeway (hotel was right next to the freeway, which might also explained a bit lower rate compared to other similar hotels). After we declined an offer to pay extra to get a room that face the waterfront, we were assured that our room would not face the freeway. Also, we were informed that even if our room would have faced the freeway we would not noticed it because the rooms are so quite (more on this later). 
Then I asked about the free breakfast whether it is a buffet or something else. The person at the check-in did not know basically anything about the breakfast. He had no idea whether a buffet breakfast was going to be served or not. Finally he gave us a breakfast coupon, which according to him would give us 20 dollars off from any breakfast we would like to have. Obviously he had never read the coupon because it said that it would be good for a breakfast buffet for 2.
So, we got a room on the 21st floor. Not only did the room face the freeway, but it was right by the elevators. I wonder where I room would have been, had I not asked for a quiet room!? By the way, you can easily hear the noise from the freeway even up to the 21st floor. We had hard time sleeping because of the noise.
We also decided to have dinner at the hotel's restaurant on the 28th floor. That did not go well either. First, we were completely ignored for at least 10 minutes. We considered walking out just before somebody finally came to take our orders. I had chicken which was good, however the potatoes were raw. My wife has salmon, which turned out to be completely raw inside. She had to send it back.
Service at the breakfast was not any better, although the food was good. I asked for tea, and got one cup and a promise that I would get a pot of tea. The pot never showed up. Neither did the glasses of orange juice that we ordered.
The only good thing about this hotel is the price considering its location (close to downtown). However, make sure that you get a room that does not face the freeway, or otherwise your room can be really noisy.
Overall, in my opinion this hotel does not deserve 4 stars. We are not going to stay at the hotel again. I am willing to pay another 50 dollars or so per night to try another nearby hotel, such as Sheraton.

name: Coast Gateway Hotel
title: “Very convenient, friendly driver, clean room!”
text:
I had arrived late at Seatac to wait overnight for an early flight home. The shuttle arrived promptly, had a very friendly and helpful driver. Check-in was quick and efficient by a very hard working woman at the front desk who was checking people in, coordinating pickups and a few other tasks at the same time. The room was clean, quiet and comfortable. Breakfast is avaialble starting at 5 , a big help for those with early flights and the same friendly driver was there to take me back for the quick ride to the airport.
The team seemed to have their act together for this type of stay..

name: Holiday Inn Seattle
title: “Best value of Money”
text: I really enjoyed my stay at the Holiday Inn. It is just a little walk into the heart of downtown(about 10 minutes), so it was a great way to start your day before grabbing your first cup of coffee. Super easy hotel to find, quick walk to the Light Rail, a few minute walk to downtown to all the restuarants

name: The Peabody Memphis
title: “Really marvelous!”
text:
I had two French exchange students as my guests at the Peabody. They were enchanted by the ducks, of course, as anyone would be! 
The quick check-in was a happy surprise. Elegant and immaculate room. The beds are heavenly! The staff is very friendly and helpful.
Only room for improvement is signage. We parked in the self-parking garage, and spent too much time wandering around trying to find the lobby.

name: Embassy Suites Seattle - Tacoma International Airport
title: “Beautiful Room!”
text: We were very nervous about staying at this hotel after reading some less-than-positive reviews avbout it online, but we ended up taking a wrong turn from the airport and ended up away from the Holiday Inn Express. It was 11pm, and we were exhausted, so we decided to take our chances. We needed a room big enough for us and our three children so Embassy Suites are a good fit for us. Our room looked like it had recently been remodeled. It was very clean, and modern, with new bedding with the triple-sheeting like Holiday Inn Express does, and all of us loved it. There was a table that could be pulled out from the wall that all of us could sit at and eat our fast-food meal we brought with us. We did not have to pay for parking, as someone else posted. Our college daughter had a paper due that she had to turn in, so she went and used the business center downstairs and got her work submitted. The next day the front desk person gave us an easy-to-follow map that had directions to IKEA and the mall on it, so we were off! We were very glad we took our chances on this hotel-we were not disappointed!

name: BEST WESTERN Loyal Inn
title: “Better than I expected; great location.”
text: I stayed in a "better than basic" king room (I forget the moniker; it was on the 4th floor). The room was very large, nicely appointed & clean. King bed, desk with nice desk chair, overstuffed chair with side table. double sinks, huge closet, safe, fridge, microvave, coffeemaker, wet bar sink. Staff very accomodating, security guard after 10 PM (for smokers who must be outside). 2 blocks walk to Whole Foods (great take out if you want it). Breakfast Serve-yourself typically OK. The hotel is very green -- recycle bin in every room (yeah!), breakfast served on china. 15 minute walk to Seattle Center (Space Needle & more); about 20 minutes to downtown Westlake station (where the light rail will take you to the airport for $2.75). Should I go to Seattle again, I'll stay at the Loyal.

name: Quality Inn & Suites Seattle
title: “Sehr gute Lage da nah am Space Needle”
text: Das Hotel ist für ein Stadthotel gut, zentrale Lage, saubere Zimmer, sehr gutes Frühstück. Zimmer sind recht klein, typisch für Stadthotels. Kurze Wege zum Space Needle, was richtig gut ist! (ca. 10 Min). Parken sogar ohne Gebühr. Man kann auch gut zu Fuß nach downtown, ist nicht zu weit! Alternativ kann man auch die am Space Needle sich befindende Monorail nutzen, die schnell in downtown ist.

name: W Seattle
title: “Decent... but no "W"ow”
text: I just returned from a 3-night business trip at the W Seattle. The hotel is located in a fabulous downtown location at 4th & Seneca with easy (less than 6 blocks) walking access to shopping, restaurants, and Pike’s Place Market. My room was larger than in other W’s I have recently stayed and equipped in typical W style…comfy bed, hip furniture, and a neutral (tans & grey) palette. The lighting in the bathroom was minimal, yielding a pretty dark bathroom (especially over the shower and commode). Toiletries are “Bliss” brand and smell good! The overall hotel service was fair (efficient but not overly courteous check-in, prompt room service, awful valet, & good housekeeping). Less attitude than some W’s and more than others. Overall, it’s a good hotel. I paid $345/night, which makes me question the value proposition given the vast array of great Seattle options. I personally prefer the adjacent Fairmont and the nearby Grand Hyatt.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Seattle Airport
title: “Old Doubletree in Seattle”
text: Yes the Hotel is very handy to the Airport, which was great, & it was priced competitively. BUT it looks very old, out dated. My Duvet & furnishings in my room looked very used & the room itself was miles away from the lobby - thought I was staying in Seattle not Las Vegas! I travel every 2wks & spend many a night in a hotel room. The staff were helpful but I wouldn’t stay here again.

name: Hotel Max
title: “Hotel Max is very cool”
text: We really liked Hotel Max - the look is different and fun and our stay was really very pleasant. I heard about how some of the rooms were smaller but I asked for a larger room if possible and I got one. At the same time when I called they offered to move our travelling companions to the same floor (if possible) and it was done. The doorman that first day was really nice and helpful. I'm from the south so I'm used to more open friendly types but I did notice Seattle was not exactly like that - nice, but not overly friendly so it may seem to some people that they are a bit cold - I think it is just a different culture. The only complaint I had was that when I called to ask them the best way to get to the airport they stated a cab or town car. I wish they had mentioned that there is a really reasonable Downtown/Airport bus as well - we could have saved some money as the cab drive was about $40 but the shuttle would have been $22 for two people. Other then that I would totally recommend this place - it was a good value in a very convenient location with a certain cool ambience.

name: W Seattle
title: “Brrrrrrrrrrrrrrr Where is my coat?!!”
text: I need to give this hotel a good rating because it was clean, attractive and convenient. However, it wasn't for us. It was a little to "cold" and I don't mean the temperature. With exception of the valet guys, who were very friendly, everyone else acted as if they were doing us a favor by being there. We prefer a little warmer and cozy setting so we won't be back. Now the Willows Lodge...that is a great place!!!!!

name: Executive Hotel Pacific
title: “Charged twice, concierge made me feel unwelcomed!!”
text: I arrived in the late morning hours knowing I wouldnt be able to check in, but was told that I could leave my bags before I could checkin. When I arrived with my bags the concierge was telling other guests about how soon they could possibly check in to the hotel. I stayed around ok with what he had said because all I wanted to do was drop off my bags so I could tour seattle. The conciege greeted me with "Did you not hear what I said, or should I repeat myself to you?!" That was such a warm greeting. After a few minutes of explaining to the guy that I just wanted to drop off my bags and I knew it was early to checkin, he finally took my bags from me. After a few hours I returned and checked in to the room and went to the concierge to retrieve my bags. And once again I was greeted with another warm welcome of "Where is your baggage claim ticket?" I told him that he never gave me one and he gave me an attitude about how he does his job properly and he doesnt need me to tell him different. He never gave me a baggage ticket. Then he expected a tip from me after he did get my bags for me. I just walked away. Enough of the Concierge. The room was good, other than the outlet that I wanted to plug my laptop in, it wasnt connected to the wall at all. I thought that could be a fire threat to the hotel. The rest of my stay went good, the AC worked and the room was exactly what I needed. After my stay, I went to check my bank account and the hotel had charged me twice for my stay. When I called the hotel they told me that they would refund one night to my card and it would take 3-5 business days. The hotel put me in a huge hole for the rest of my vacation. This hotel caused me to depend on others to support me for my trip. They ended up making me feel like a homeless man. So after the 2 things that I have mentioned, this hotel is terrible and I have no intentions of ever recommending this hotel to any of my family and friends who travel to seattle often.

name: Hotel Max
title: “Just So So”
text: I think the hotel is over priced and well not really that great. The location is pretty good and the rooms clean, they give that little funk appeal but soooo small. I really would rather stay at Hotel 1000 or the W for pretty much the same price. I would stay again only if rate were much less. I will say that the service is very good though. Nice friendly and helpful staff. I am a resort owner in a tourist town and we charge 450 for our largest room with 2 bedrooms, 2 bath, jacuzzi , fireplace, 42 inch plasmas and they are on the water so just found it hard to pay that much for just and average place.

name: Coast Gateway Hotel
title: “Very good experience!”
text: Stayed on a weekday in a superior room (at AAA rate). Bed was very comfortable, bath was clean, towels & robes thick, refrigerator. Overall, very clean and well maintained room. Hotel borders the runway, but with soudproofing the airport traffic wasn't a bother at all--actually pretty neat to have a front row view of gates A13 & A14! Front desk staff was friendly and courteous.

name: Red Lion Hotel on Fifth Avenue Seattle
title: “Location, location, location”
text: The hotel's location is right in the downtown area, closed to Pike Public Market. Room is excellent, front desk service is excellent. We came early in the morning, around 10 a.m. just get off from cruise, immediately provided with a room and we did not have to wait until check in time. Pike Public Market is within short 4 blocks walking distance. Shopping centers and light rail to the airport is about 2 blocks from the hotel.

name: Radisson Hotel Seattle Airport
title: “Stay and Fly”
text:
We booked this Hotel on a "reverse fly and park" deal. We parked our car then flew to NC for Christmas. When we returned we stayed at the hotel one night before returning home. This Hotel is very accommodating and staff was extremely helpful. The rooms are very nice, roomy and comfortable. They have sleep number beds - but the jury is still out on exactly how comfortable they really are as compared to higher-end mattresses. I read one review where the person was up all night listening to the sound of the sleep number bed's motor. Although we heard our neighbor's bed "once" I am convinced that it would not have kept us awake or woke us up.
Linens are super nice, bath towels new and large. Location is outstanding - right across from the Airport and their shuttle service is convenient. I think they have fridges on request. They have a restaurant and bar but we got in late and left early so we did not utilize either one. If your flying out of Seattle and need a convenient place to park and a nice hotel to say in - this is the place for you.

name: Hotel Max
title: “Stay somewhere else”
text:
I travel quite a bit for business, but consider myself to be 'hip and knowledgeable'.
People have described this as an 'artsy' hotel, but I would describe it as more alternative than anything. Yes, there are paintings in the room of local and up and coming artists, and each door has its own artist covering of a painting or print. All for supporting local artists, they lose the hospitality aspect of being a hotel. 
The majority of rooms are SMALL. One bed and a desk, and you have to shimmy by them to get through. The closet is a half closet where clothes hang sideways. There is no place to open an ironing board.
Here are some more drawbacks:
-It's loud! The walls are paper thin, I heard every word of a conversation in the room beside me. If you have a room on the Stewart side of the street, say goodbye to sleeping.
-The gym is the size of a closet, forget about stretching. There are two treadmills, two ellepticals and one bench with free weights. They don't clean the area or supply enough towels.
-The restaurant is absolutely ridiculous. There was a group of us for breakfast, we forewarned them to be prepared. I waited 1 hour for my breakfast after ordering it 3 times, dirty silverware, a server who had no idea what was going on.
-I called the front desk just to be transferred to another room 3 times, each time I was put on hold after my request and not transferred. Ok so they were busy...but how long does it take to transfer a phone call!??!?
-The wireless internet was nearly impossible to use, and the elevators were so slow!
-More than once I waited for an elevator only to have it open and see the cleaning staff with their back to the door having a conversation. So that's why I waited for one of the TWO elevators for so long! One of them was on hold due to a social conversation!
The good stuff:
-comfortable beds and linens
Sorry but I cannot recommend this to anyone, other than a deaf mute artist who has a need for a personal vibrator kit (it's part of the mini-bar). Oh and they don't need to room service or to work out.

name: Radisson Hotel Seattle Airport
title: “Huge room 10 mins walk from Light Rail and Terminal”
text:
One of the nicest hotel airport rooms I've ever stayed in: huge, with massive desk space, excellent king-size bed, nice quality sheets, pillows, and duvet, large bathroom. Couldn't believe it was actually an airport hotel. Only negative: strange hydraulic whine noise every few minutes really disturbing -- I guess it must have been the elevator which was nearby, but I've never heard one that sounded that much like a whiney foghorn! I was staying there as I had an ealry morning (5 am!) departure, and the noise seemed to stop late-ish... but still, if I stay there again I'll request a room far from the elevator. In a similar vein, the window wasn't properly closed and the aircon controls were hard to find (hidden behind curtains) so I would have had a less stuffy and less noisy room if I'd worked all that out a bit earlier.
Room service speedy and tasty.
You really can walk there from the Light Rail station at SeaTac in about 7 mins with wheeled luggage. You could also walk to the Terminal if you wanted, it would take just a bit longer. There is a free shuttle (which I took in the morning, feeling so exhausted with such an early start) but it is a small minivan and only runs every hour and half-hour, so be forewarned.
Wacky positive: the bath soap bar (no shower gel, which initially irritated me!) is beautifully aromatic (coconut? cinnamon? strange but nice, whatever it was) and is shaped with little bumpy bits as a circulation massager. Hard to describe but really great! (I did say it was wacky....)
All in all a pleasant surprise -- highly recommendable as long as you're not near the lift, get the window closed, and enjoy your shower!

name: Mediterranean Inn
title: “Good Value”
text:
Was looking for a decent and reasonable place to stay, close to Key Arena. The price was right and you can't get any closer to the venue. The rooms are older but clean. The location is great as after the concert, there are several decent pubs for a late night drink and meal within 1-2 blocks. The room pictures on their website are pretty much accurate, but maybe not quite as bright, but still pretty good. The only thing was the heating was left on when we arrived and it was a little uncomfortable upon arrival. Didn't see any A/C controls so I am not sure about hot summer nights.
Overall good value and have no problem recommending this hotel.

name: Red Lion Hotel on Fifth Avenue Seattle
title: “Came home with bed bug bites”
text: Okay hotel but got home with 6 bed bug bites and only stayed in the room one night, room #614. Be cautious.

name: Warwick Seattle Hotel
title: “Nice Hotel and Service, but . . . .”
text:
My husband and I decided to plan a trip with my cousin and her husband. They had stayed at the Warwick many years ago and loves the space needle view. So, we booked both of our rooms at the Warwick for a three night stay. 
Upon arrival, my cousin told me, don't expect a huge lobby or check in counter. Boy was she right!! The lobby area is very small but cozy. Check in/out, question desk and concierge are all at one desk that is about 15 feet long. You feel so cramped if you are getting information and there are two people waiting behind you!! But, very good service. The manager who checked us in gave us coupon books, maps, anything that was going to help us around the city. That was very nice!
The room was clean and looked nice. Until we went into the restroom. It was clean, very small, but clean but looked like a fist was coming through the ceiling. It was very weird! Also, in the shower, there was a cover that looked as if it was ready to fall off. 
We paid for the upgaded view of the space needle. We were told we'd be able to see it from our bed. Well, that was false. In order to see the needle, you had to stand in the corner and look at it or open the slider to see it. It was ok though. 
We read some reviews about the pool being kind of dingy and dark, but nice once you were in the water. So we tried it out. It is in the basement, but the elevator takes you right there. The first thing you notice when you walk in is the stench of chlorine. It smelled so bad. We decided to muddle through and went in the pool. The temp was nice, but we then opted for the spa. From the steam and the chlorine, both my husband and I had to leave because our eyes were burning and watering so bad. We told the front desk and a lady responded with "how do you expect us to keep it clean?" 
Overall, it was nice, but we probably won't stay there again. We found a hotel a few blocks closer to all of the shopping that was way nicer and cleaner and had cheaper rates. I think we will give it a try next time.

name: W Seattle
title: “Good stay”
text: In many ways, very much the "W" experience: decor, vibe, service... which is a compliment. Though the lobby area is quite small, still very functional and service is very attentive and helpful. Unlike other W's, the elevators are quick! Gym is incredibly small and claustrophobic. Location is excellent - close to all the shops and Pike's Place Market. Good, reliable stay with excellent service

name: Executive Hotel Pacific
title: “great location”
text: currently staying at the hotel. despite the few negative reviews, this is a very nice hotel! I asked for a complimentary upgrade but john (who checked us in 3/10) said he didnt know how and was afraid to, so we are spending an extra $10 a nite. so far, other than that, very nice!

name: Quality Inn & Suites Seattle
title: “okay but needs upgrading”
text:
My family and I stayed here for 2 nights, we got the big family suite on the fifth floor. Definitely not worth over $260 a night but with 6 people to divide with, it made it "ok" We heard plenty of comments from people in the elevator ride up that we were LUCKY we weren't on the second floor because the rooms were horrible. 
Because they were busy we had to move into another suite the second night. The second suite was a little more run down than the first one. They definitely NEED to steam clean the carpets or get new carpet it was pretty gross. I would not walk without shoes in the room. Air conditioning wasn't the greatest but was manageable. 
Nice size family rooms, but we probably won't go back. Would rather spend a little more money for something nicer and more updated...After all I am on holidays

name: Red Roof Inn Seattle Airport - SEATAC
title: “Good hotel for the price”
text: This hotel was a decent hotel for the price. The only problem we experienced was being able to hear the next room's TV and it wasn't on a show that I would want children to hear. Wasn't bothered by airplane noise, just the TV in the next room. Just be sure to BRING EARPLUGS. Even with the thin walls, I would stay again. Hotel staff said there will be a $5 Million dollar renovation in Nov 06, so I hope the prices don't go up.

name: Travelodge Seattle by the Space Needle
title: “beware of extra charges”
text: we have stayed here several times in the past. it's an ok hotel with decent rooms and a good breakfast. was somewhat upset by a new (1/09 so they said) $10 per day parking fee. reserved on the travelodge.com site so nomention was made of the parking fee (seems like they could get their website to include things like that). don't like extra fees that aren't included in the quoted reservation price. so, stay here but beware.

name: The Westin Seattle
title: “A friendly and helpful staff, a good location but strange dining choces.”
text:
I stayed in the Wesin Seattle for three nighs in mid-april whil attending an annual meeting in the Washington Convention Center. As a state employee I got a very good rate, much cheaper than the convetion rate at the other hotels. the Westin is well located in downtown Seattle: it is near the monorail station, the the light rail station and it was but a short walk to the convention center. Many restaurants, stores are nearby and the Pike Street Market is about a 15 miniute walk
 The hotel has two circular towers and I liked being close to the elevator. rooms are well designed but a bit worn in some areas. Hotel staff is friendly and very helpful. The concierge staff is particularly good.. 
 A strange thing about this hotel - a four star residence, are its dining choices. There are two restaurants: one is open for breakfast and lunch and the other for dinnner. However, the breakfast place is a cafeteria (which is not mentioned in the hotel web site). The food is ok - good bakery items, and reasonably priced but the place fills up quickly and sometimes there is no place to sit. The young staff are great but they need more help. I did not eat in the dinner restaurant and it did not seem that busy..

name: Hotel Max
title: “The Seattle Hotel Max”
text: From everything I saw on the website for this hotel I thought it was going to be a nice stay. However, once we arrived to the hotel I was surprised at a few things. First was the size of the room and bathroom. This is one of the few times I’ve run into having a 3x3 foot shower in a hotel in the states. This is normally something done in small hotels in London or Paris but not common for Seattle. The rooms was also not much larger then the bed with windows that haven’t been updated for at least 50 years. Each unit has its own in window air conditioner which was appreciated. Also the rooms had very little sound proofing between each room which allowed us to hear everything the neighbors did through the night. For the price there are much better places to stay in Seattle. I would not recommend this hotel to a friend or visit it again.

name: W Seattle
title: “Consistent Property, Eltie Minded!”
text:
Ahh The W Seattle! I am a SPG Plat member and "W The Card holder. Lately when in Seattle on business I have been staying at the HYATT downtown, but because of a convention at that property I was back at my old stomping grounds THE W.
Once a flagship of THE W chain, she is showing a little bit of wear and tear here and there. 
The Staff was great as expected except the concierge, who was was a bit too impressed with himself.
The hallways/elevators are very dimly lit, with a sexy ambiance, this hotel is for the movers and shakers, the style makers, or people who think they have style! I personally love it.
Once inside the rooms you have the wonderful signature W Beds which are quite simply amazing. One of the most comfortable beds you will experience. Mod decor abounds in the rooms with great flat screen TVs and a well appointed bathroom. All of the Bathroom products are provided by BLISS Spa's and you will want to take home the face wash and body lotion, they are that good!
My only complaint (and to some this may be a plus) is that it is difficult to get the rooms dark. When I am in Seattle I work late and sleep in, I am usually upgraded to a Corner King room which has amazing views but is difficult to darken, especially when I want to sleep in.
The blinds are a so-so at best shutters that just don't block sunlight (reason why I have been over at The Hyatt lately instead).
The restaurant /room service is amazing and the bar is great. Last year Quentin Tarantino was at the bar with a lady friend having a drink on a Thursday night! (I don't spot too many celebrities in my hotel travels)
No coffee makers in the rooms (urghh pet peeve!) I like to make a cup of coffee without having to go downstairs for the free coffee or order a $16 small pot from room service.
Overall though it is a wonderful property with a great location and good staff, on the trendy, high-end side of things so if you are stuffy and grumpy or like to get to bed very early, try the Fairmont next door (which has the best Oysters and Salmon in Seattle at the restaurant "Shucker's" on their ground floor.) But if you want to stay with the fashionista boutique brigade, give it a go!!!!

name: Holiday Inn Express Seattle City Center
title: “Think I would pass”
text: Although the price was good (for Seattle), the room needed a good cleaning and updating. We have stayed at Holiday Inn Express that have the comfortable beds with new bedding, this one was disappointing. The toilet was plugged when we got into the room, there was a bag of food left in the microwave, the carpet was dirty, the curtains had a big stain on them and the blankets also had stains. The room had a busy freeway right out front, so I would suggest earplugs. We typically stay at holiday inn express because you know what you can expect but think I would pass on staying at this one again. On the upside, the staff was very friendly and we did have a good view of the space needle.

name: The Peabody Memphis
title: “Grand Old Place”
text: Rooms were nice and classic and the location is perfect to take in the best Memphis has to offer. Staff were friendly and helpful but the bathrooms are a little small.

name: Executive Hotel Pacific
title: “Convenient, comfortable, helpful staff”
text: I would highly recommend this hotel - it's close to Pike Place Market, great eats and all the city has to offer.

name: Inn at Queen Anne
title: “The worst hotel experience I've ever had. Stay Away!”
text: I warn you of booking this hotel for your next visit to Seattle. Although nicely located, we encountered hostile, terribly rude and unattentive staff. We had a bee infestation in our room. Staff is not knowledgeable about their own services or city. At one point, we were told to go out and purchase our own iron, since the one's they had were all taken for the evening (we had asked ahead of time if we should have reserved it and they said no). To add insult to injury, they incorrectly charged us by adding on an unauthrized upgrade. The hotel has tainted our experience in lovely Seattle and I can assure you that I have traveled the world and have yet to stay at such a terribly organized and run establishment.

name: The Peabody Memphis
title: “Entenhausen in Memphis!”
text: Das legendäre Peabody Hotel rühmt sich als Luxus-Herberge und ist ohne Zweifel sehenswert und sehr gediegen. Bekannt sind die in der Lobby in einem Brunnen schwimmenden Enten und die Show, welche jeden Morgen um 11:00 Uhr und am Nachmittag um 17:00 Uhr mit dem Federvieh veranstaltet wird. Sollte man sich unbedingt anschauen, wenn man schon in der Nähe ist. Allerdings muss man sich schon recht früh in der Lobby einfinden, damit man noch ein gutes Plätzchen erwischt. Das Hotel ist um diese Zeit wirklich gerammelt voll.

name: Moore Hotel
title: “Value for Location”
text: The Moore is the best price for the location. It is no frills, clean and quiet. There was no closet in the room, so if you have clothes you wish to hang this may be an inconvenience. I did not inquire with the front desk if an iron or hair dryer were available. If these are a necessity you should check with them before booking. The cozy cafe they run is a great place to start the day.

name: Inn at Queen Anne
title: “Queen Ann Hotel- molto fumo e niente arrosto”
text:
Le camere che ci sono state assegnate al secondo piano dell'ala destra dell'hotel sono in condizioni fatiscenti e presentano una pulizia generale non adeguata agli standard degli altri hotel e motel visitati con rate allineati.
In particolare la camera del mio amico presentava le lenzuola sporche e piene di peli e capelli. la mia camera aveva invece il rubinetto della vasca rotto con perdita di acqua calda continua e rumorosa.
Il frigorifero alloggiato nella camera emetteva un rumore elevato che mi ha costretto a spegnerlo (e quindi a renderlo inutilizzabile). L'aria condizionata presentava una griglia sporca di polvere (oltre ad essere molto rumorosa) che mi ha impedito di utilizzarla. La cucina presente all'interno della stanza era fatiscente e non adeguata a standard igenici moderni.
Il letto cigolava e aveva il materasso cedevole.
L'unica nota positiva è stata la posizione dell'Hotel in una zona relativamente tranquilla e vicina alla monorail dello space neddle con la quale si raggiungiungeva velocemente il centro città.
In ultima analisi sconsiglio vivamente di utilizzare quest'albergo, suggerendo di trovare sistemazioni alternative anche se più scomode dal punto di vista logistico o più care, a patto che forniscano un livello di pulizia e decenza adeguata

name: Moore Hotel
title: “Older hotel has character, but lacks modern conveniences”
text: If you looking for a clean hotel significantly less expensive than most others in downtown Seattle, the Moore is a good choice. We went in late September so the outside air temperature was in the low 70's. We were able to cool our room by opening the window, but this let in considerable traffic noise which doesn't let up all night. Don't know what a person would do if the outside temps were hot. The rooms are quite small and there is only one tiny elevator serving the entire hotel. If your expectations are for a 19th century hotel experience, you will be just fine.

name: Radisson Hotel Seattle Airport
title: “nice, but don't wait for the shuttle”
text: After coming in from Florida and calling 3 times for a shuttle pick-up, it arrived 45 minutes later. It would have been much easier just to drag the luggage down across the street to the hotel in about 5 minutes. Room on the 7th floor was smokey, night manager very helpful and changed our room immediately to a nonsmoking floor. Housekeeping did a good job, front desk helpful, halls showing definite signs of wear. Room itself was quite nice (king), sleep number beds overrated, but for $45 on Priceline, can't complain!

name: Executive Hotel Pacific
title: “Fantastic place to sleep and travel about Downtown”
text: Fantastic location for those who want to be close to Pike Place and the waterfront. Staff was very helpful and knoweldgeable about the area. Would stay again there again. Room was on the small side but clean.

name: Red Lion Hotel Seattle Airport
title: “Excellent pre-flight hotel stay”
text: I've stayed at this Red Lion several times over the past couple of years, the night before an early morning flight. Each time the staff & facilities have been top notch. Their excellent hotel/parking packages make an out-of-town get-away out of SeaTac airport affordable.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Seattle Sea-Tac
title: “Great value”
text: Found the La Quinta to be clean, the location very convenient, the staff helpful, and our room to be a good value for the cost. We will definitely stay there again.

name: Sixth Avenue Inn
title: “Good little hotel for the price...”
text: The Sixth Avenue Inn was a good deal for the happening downtown Seattle area. It is within walking distance of almost anything you would want to see or do making it safe to party without worrying about who is going to drive. The rooms are incredibly outdated but if you can see past the decor, this is your hotel. The bells and whistles are kept to a minimum, which may be why the price is lower than some of the larger hotels. The restaurant on the lower level is a cool spot to grab a bite and drinks. The ambiance on the bar side is is a lot like the bar in the movie National Lampoon's Vacation. Dark yet comfortable. If the fire is not lit, ask them to...it makes it so much better for late night drinks. Be sure to leave extra time when checking out as a lot of people tend to leave around the same time and the one person behind the desk gets busy fast.

name: Red Lion Hotel Seattle Airport
title: “A very good airport hotel choice.”
text:
This is my second stay here. The first time I was travelling alone, and I felt safe and taken care of so I came back again.
This is an older hotel, but the room was spotless and the bed was very comfortable. The AC was quiet and worked perfectly. We found the room on the top floor quiet and the wifi worked perfectly. We did hear some noise in the morning - but nothing you don't hear at any other hotel (doors closing when guests leave, etc). The airport noise was barely noticeable. We had a great night's sleep.
My only very minor complaint was that the bathroom floor was a bit slippery after the first person showered. We put a towel on the floor and it was fine. I think the floor had just been polished.
The staff was friendly, check in and out was fast and efficient, and the restaurant recommendation was appreciated.
It's also very convenient to the airport. I won't hesitate to recommend this hotel to my friends, and will stay there next time I'm in town.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Seattle Sea-Tac
title: “Good service, decent rooms and price”
text:
We stayed in the La Quinta in in Seattle, near the airport, and it served our need well. The front desk staff was very friendly and kind. There is a complimentary breakfast available and no additional charge for parking. My only concern was that the toilet seat wouldn't stay up in our room, but I informed the front desk of that when we checked out and I am confident that they addressed the problem.
The pool is outdoors, which doesn't bother me, but I figured that it is with mentioning, since I heard someone ask where the indoor pool was located (there is not indoor pool). 
There is a shuttle to the airport, which I believe starts at 4:39 am.

name: Moore Hotel
title: “Location, location, location...”
text: We were going to spend only 5 days in Seattle so wanted to be somewhere centrally located and at the same time not too expensive. The Moore Hotel offered us exactly what we were looking for. It is only a couple of blocks away from Pike Market, downtown, and the waterfront, within reach of the Space Needle, a 6 minute walk from the Light Rail which takes you straight to Sea-Tac, not to mention so many other attractions. The rooms are simple and clean, housecleaning is very good, but the hotel is old and has no ac. There's only one ice machine on the second floor so that is a bit of an inconvenience. The first two nights, we had a room right by the shared washrooms (we took a room with a private bath) so we had to endure door banging all night. We complained to the front desk and were promptly given a room further off so we were quite satisfied. The staff was polite, helpful, and knowledgeable. I definitely recommend this unpretentious hotel for all those who have no intention of renting a car during their stay in Seattle. It is in a great location.

name: Mediterranean Inn
title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: This hotel is located very close to the Seattle Center, Space Needle, Pike Place Market, and other attractions. The staff at the hotel was very accommodating, rooms very clean and nicely furnished, with wonderful views of the city. Parking was affordable and other means of transportation were very convenient. A Safeway Grocery store is convenient as well as a Starbucks Coffee shop outside the lobby. The front desk manager, Sheila, was very helpful, knowledgeable, and congenial. I would definitely recommend this hotel to others. We stayed here prior to and following our Alaska cruise and it was convenient to the port.

name: The Edgewater Hotel Seattle
title: “Most Amazing Room & Wedding”
text: We had our wedding at The Edgewater in October 2011 and it was the best experience we could have asked for! The Olympic Ballroom is the most beautiful space and the terrace was such a wonderful added bonus for our cocktail hour. We were also upgraded (surprise!!) to the penthouse suite for our wedding night's stay and were blown away with the gesture and amazing water view accommodations! We will be back year after year and maybe one day in the future we can book that penthouse suite and relive the magic of that night!

name: Hotel Max
title: “Traumbetten - nicht "sleepless in Seattle"”
text:
Toll gelegen, mitten im Zentrum. Vom Hotel aus sind alle Sehenswürdigkeiten zu Fuss erreichbar. Die Monorailstation liegt zwei Blocks um die Ecke. Damit kommt man locker zur Space-Needle (Fernsehturm). 
Kein Frühstück! Wie überall in den Staaten gibt's kein Frühstück, das mit unserem vergleichbar wäre... andere Länder, andere Sitten. Dafür gibt's gleich mehrere Star Bucks in der Nähe. Das muss wohl reichen. Gleich hinter dem Hotel gibt's eine tolle Bar mit Nacht-Menue. (Besonders günstig, wenn man links, auf der Bar-Seite isst).
Die Zimmer sind geräumig, mit sehr grossem Flat-Screen; extra Bad und WC. Herausragend ist dieses Hotel jedoch für seine Komfort-Betten. Selten in einem Hotel so gut geschlafen. Zum Innenhof gab's ein Ventilationsgeräusch, mit dem man leben muss...
Mit der Rezeption hatten wir nicht viel zu tun, da der Schlüssel eine Magnetkarte ist und man so nicht dauernd zur Rezeption gehen muss.
Preis-Leistung: trotz der guten Betten und der hervorragenden Lage: etwas teuer... Wir hatten online ein Package mit Virgin Air gebucht (von San Franciso-Seattle und zurück); das hat sich gelohnt, günstiger Flug)

name: BEST WESTERN Loyal Inn
title: “Great choice”
text: My wife and I chose this Best Western after quite a bit of research. We were looking for something near or in downtown with free parking and air conditioning since she's pregnant and it was hot. The location was very good (close to the Space Needle and Seattle offers free bus rides in downtown area), the free wireless was nice, and the continental breakfast is pretty impressive. The room is spacious enough, the bed was fairly comfortable with good pillows, and the shower had hot water and good pressure. The only complaints I might have had would be the front desk; aside from John C. they weren't much help. Much of the front desk staff consisted of young people who mean well enough but don't have the social skills or confidence to answer good tourist questions. Also, I had to negotiate for free parking since I was told that was offered over the phone. They were nice and cooperative about the parking issue. On the whole, this is a great value -- we get up and get going and this place offers what one needs to do that for a good, big city price. On a side note, we found the Golden Singha Thai restaurant on Cedar (short walk towards central downtown and the Needle) to be excellent food for $8 (dinner).

name: Hotel Max
title: “Nous n y retournerons ps”
text: En depit d un accueil excellent, nous n avons pas apprecie cet hotel : notre chambre etait situee a un angle de l hotel, donnant sur 2 rues et par consequent etait extremement bruyante; par ailleurs, cette chambre etait si exiguee qu il fallait fermer la porte de la salle de bain pour pouvoir ouvrir celle du placard de l entree. Nous avions a peine assez de place pour nos bagages.

name: The Edgewater Hotel Seattle
title: “Another Great Stay”
text:
If you can stay anywhere in downtown Seattle, I highly recommend the Edgewater. I've stay here often and have never been disappointed. If the weather is awful as it usually is the city side is just fine - if by chance the sun shines try to get a west facing waterside room. Yes, it is a little pricey, but convenient to Pike Place market, Bell Town and if your healthy you can walk to any of Seattles offerings. I'll be back, hope to see you there.
Rich

name: The Westin Memphis Beale Street
title: “Great stay, Great location”
text:
This hotel was the perfect location for our stay. It was clean, the staff was friendly and helpful. Didn't have a have any problems with getting our room cleaned on a daily basis. Smelled clean and fresh each time we walked through the door. Quite and pleasantly comfort. The beds are to dream for, would love to have one at home. Love the separate shower. This stay was more than I expected. Beale Street is just steps away. 
Tip: Unless you plan to buy the snacks from the refrigerator or the snack tray, Do NOT touch. If you do touch the snacks, you have 30 seconds to put it back. They have weight sensors and the signal goes straight to the front desk.

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton Hotel Seattle Airport - Southcenter
title: “Great Getaway Property”
text:
I booked this property for 2 reasons. 1) The price of admission was very good and 2) they are the only Doubletree/Hilton in the Seattle airport area that offers full breakfast to Diamond members. 
I met my sister there for a weekend of shopping and a visit to our grandmother. This place was a great score for all of our objectives. Nestled into a great area filled with shopping and food, it is also very close to the Seattle airport. We ventured into the downtown area with a very quick drive on I-5 to visit the market and also had easy access to get out of town to the south for our visit with grandma. 
The property has the look and feel of a former Embassy Suites. The room had great flat screen TVs in both the front room with the couch and desk as well as within the bedroom. The shower had AWESOME water pressure which is a huge plus for me. Parking was ample and places to eat were numerous within walking distance.
