I used the fitness center and found the equipment to be the newest, most advanced cardio equipment I have used in any hotels. Excellent! There were several treadmills, ellipticals, free weights and several weight machines for use. Balls, mats and everything you could need for a great workout.
The free diamond breakfast was great and everything I expected from a Hilton/Doubletree breakfast from a food perspective. The service was sketchy in the breakfast both days trying to get more coffee, cream, etc. They were not busy, just not paying attention.
If there is a downside to this property,we did not find it. I would stay here again in a heartbeat.

name: Homewood Suites Seattle-Downtown
title: “Great value for money”
text: Stayed here for one night en route from Vancouver. Very impressed with the friendly attention from all employees at this hotel from the room attendants to the Manager on duty. Very good value for money as full buffet breakfast is included in the tariff as well as beer/wine and small evening meal. The room we were given was clean, large, very well appointed, and extremely comfortable. Earlier in the month stayed for five nights at the Homewood Suites in Pike Street but would recommend the Downtown suites first if friendliness and attention is important to you.

name: Silver Cloud Hotel Stadium
title: “Location Location Location”
text:
Wow, I've been going to Seahawks and Mariners games for years and haven't ever stayed here. I've been missing out.
This place is perfect for attending a game. Parking is only 22 for valet, rooms are large and clean and the restaurant and bar are awesome.

name: Sixth Avenue Inn
title: “Sixth Ave inn is economy only... not a Boutique hotel...”
text:
The hotel had some decent ratings, but when we drove up, I was a little taken back. It looks like any Motel 6/Rodeway Inn along any major interstate. The rooms all back up to 6th ave and it looks really cheap and dirty as you walk up. On the plus, the staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The room, as prior reviews described, were small at best. I had no problems with the room size, since that is what i expected. The Bed, however, was like sleeping on a plywood deck and that coupled with the street noise, made sleeping a challenge. 
ok, so much for the bad. 
like i said, the staff was nice, and the location was central to most anything in the area we wanted to see such as the space needle, pike st. market.
If this motel were charging $59 a night, i would think it was a solid value and worth staying at, but at $120+ a night, it is a poor value in my book.
I would not stay there again, and my wife was really pleased that we only spent one night there before we went on to Vancouver.

name: Homewood Suites Seattle - Tacoma Airport / Tukwila
title: “They treated me well.”
text:
I was traveling for business, and staying for 2 months. The staff treated me very well during my extended stay. The hotel offers a great shuttle service. They were able to get me to my training, local shopping and food. 
The front desk staff of Melissa, Shemekia and Mike were a great help to me. They gave me a few great options for food and entertainment. Mike even was able to get me signed up for the Hilton Honors program.
All in all this was a great place. If I am every back to the Seattle area, I will choose to stay here again.

name: Red Lion Hotel on Fifth Avenue Seattle
title: “Great hotel in a great location!”
text: We stayed here for our first trip to Seattle. We were in town to catch a cruise ship to Alaska. This hotel is very nice and the staff were all extremely helpful. We had baggage shipped via Fedex to the hotel before our arrival and they took care of it until we arrived. The hotel is a short walk from Pike Place Market, which is awesome, and a longer walk to most of downtown Seattle's attractions. Next time I am in Seattle, I will definitely be staying here again

name: Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Its Hard Finding Consitencey”
text:
The hotel has the potential to be great but someone needs to secretly monitor them because it seems that they easily drop the ball in places
The towels feel like sandpaper. Not good when you are paying almost $300 per night.
I recommend the jacuzzi, but don't take the one with the gum wad stuck to the wall.
The rooms need to be carefully cleaned, and not just superficially. 
The bell desk has a Eric who is very helpful in answering destination questions, as well as Pete at the front desk.
Location is perfect. Near great restaurants, shopping. Pikes is a short walk and the monorail is across the street which takes you right to the Space Needle
Jenna is another pleasant person to deal with at the front desk.
The hotel can be great. It just needs some monitoring

name: Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Great Place to Stay!”
text: Hotel is clean with nicely updated rooms in a neat historic building. Exceptional staff. Great location. Most comfortable bed and best sleep I had all year, in a summer filled with travel. I will stay in the Roosevelt the next time I visit Seattle!

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton Hotel Seattle Airport - Southcenter
title: “Looking forward to another stay”
text: We enjoyed our first visit to this hotel. The shuttle driver was professional and competent. The hotel landscaping was fresh and pretty. The front desk staff were helpful, friendly, and professional. The lobby and reception areas were nicely decorated, clean, and easy to navigate. Our room was well-appointed, quiet, and a great value for the money. Their Crabtree and Evelyn toiletries smelled so good that we tracked down a Crabtree and Evelyn store elsewhere on our trip and purchased more. The hotel is within walking distance of the Southcenter Mall and a number of restaurants. We'd stay here again in a minute.

name: The Westin Seattle
title: “The rooms are outdated, but the views and...”
text: The rooms are outdated, but the views and the service were awesome! Would stay here again.

name: Crowne Plaza Seattle Downtown Area
title: “Great View”
text: We had a room on the 29th floor and loved the view. You could see the Space Needle, the Pike Place Market sign and the sound. Our suite had plenty of room and the service was great.

name: Crowne Plaza Seattle Downtown Area
title: “Average”
text: Very average property. Nothing special. Great location. Dated, so dated. The Club floor - only the name. So on)

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton Hotel Seattle Airport - Southcenter
title: “Early flight”
text: Very nice hotel. Stayed here New Year's eve to get our son off to the airport early the next day. Quiet and very close to South Center Mall and many restaurants. Enjoyed the morning breakfast buffet.

name: Courtyard Seattle Downtown/Pioneer Square
title: “Great Downtown Hotel”
text:
I stayed in the Courtyard Marriot on a weekend stay in Seattle. It was a cozy hotel with all amenities (including free Wi-Fi). The Hotel was conveniently located 1 block from the Light Rail so it was easy access from the ariport. It was also conveniently located next to Pioneer Square and not far from Park Place Market.
We had a view of the Bay on the 14 floor which was great and we were lucky to be in Seattle when it was sunny. The Bed was very comfortable and the room was clean.

name: The Westin Memphis Beale Street
title: “Great service! Great location! And awesome beds and showers :-)”
text:
From the time we got to this location I felt great about it. The staff at the front desk were so very accommodating and helpful. We got there a bit early for check in but we gave our phone number checked in our bags and were able to walk around and explore while our room got readied. As soon as it was all set we got a call that we are welcome to come back and check into the room. 
The location is just GREAT! It's just around the corner from Beal St. So you are very much in walking distance of all the fun but just far enough that there is NO noise in your room. We got a small snack/meal for a dinner treat one evening and it was very fast, delisiouse and well presented. 
We w
Really fell in love with Westin properties and will look for them on our future trips.

name: Silver Cloud Hotel Stadium
title: “2.5 star posing as a 3.5 star”
text: this hotel is definitely NOT a 3.5 star hotel. it's more like a 2.5 star hotel posing at a 3.5 star. it is not in a nice part of downtown, it's about 8 minute drive to the nice part. you cannot walk to it. you cannot walk in the area period, there's no restaurants within walking distance either and the staff is immature and unprofessional. there was hair on our pillowcase and once we uncovered the top comforter off the bed, the sheets were not tucked in and crisp at all, they barely made the bed and the sheets did not smell clean. there was a stain on the sofa chair. to top it off there was a gentleman checking in with a prostitute. it was obvious from her appearance he had picked her up from the side of the road. she was groping him right in the lobby at the front desk - ew! it made me wonder what kind of things go on in this hotel?

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton Hotel Seattle Airport - Southcenter
title: “DoubleTree by Hilton Seattle Airport, SeaTac, Washington, United States”
text: Went to Seattle on a shopping trip and stayed here for one night. It's about a 15 minute drive to downtown Seattle and close to Westfield, Mall. Great reception, friendly,helpful staff. Check in was quick and we were treated to warm, chocolate chip cookies, they even asked how many we wanted! The room was clean and large and even though we were on the first floor facing the front of the hotel/parking lot there were trees/shrubs planted in front of the deck to give the illusion of green space, large deck too. The beds were very comfortable. There was a beautiful, large outdoor pool with lots of deck space for sunning and a small hot tub. We didn't check out the fitness room but it looks okay on the webpage. I would recommend this hotel. Also, if you go on a shopping excursion check out Nordstrum Rack, about 5 mins from the hotel and try Elliott's in Seattle for dinner, on the waterfront, excellent!

name: Sheraton Seattle Hotel
title: “Great Location, friendly staff but paper thin walls!!”
text: Great location without any views. Close to everything and the staff were all great!! Did not enough the noisy rooms. I could hear the person upstairs to next door talking and using the toilet. Wouldn't spend the money again.

name: Moore Hotel
title: “good first impression of Seattle”
text:
Great central location. We could not get wifi in the room but it was available in the lobby. 
My only quibbble was the elevator which you would not call a modern or high speed elevator. However I was rarely inconvenienced by the elevator during our four day stay. Would deifintely go back.

name: Sheraton Seattle Hotel
title: “Beautiful Lobby and Comfy Beds!”
text:
I was in Seattle for a conference and found a great deal on this room. We walked in and were completely impressed by the lobby! The room had a wonderful view of downtown and the beds were very comfy. I wish we had been able to spend more time there - it had a great location with excellent shopping all around!
The only downside was the parking: either $30 valet or $22 at a garage 3 blocks away. But, I guess that happens in Downtown!

name: MarQueen Hotel
title: “Ask for room 111!”
text: The Marqueen is a lovely hotel in a great area of Seattle. Room 111 is huge, with a little sitting room and a roomy kitchen. Was a bit concerned as there is not an elevator in the hotel but it seems to only have two floors and ours was on the 1st so there was no problem. The staff was friendly and accommodating. Being Seattle, there is a great indy coffee shop connected to the hotel, which is a a real bonus!

name: Red Lion Hotel Seattle Airport
title: “It's a Dump...and $150”
text: I always thought Red Lions had a good reputaion and have had good experiences...this one was different. We got in about 10 PM - the gal checking us in was really nice. The halls really smelled like old smoke enouph that we were worried our room would reek too - luckily it did not.The room was actually OK..but old pieces and parts and A/C didn't work. The place needs updating very low ceilings and the outside is beat up. We missed our departure and need a late checkout..we asked if we could have a little more time - and the gal at the counter (the one with light brown hair in a bun in morning) wouldn't even look up at was very blunt and mean about having to be out at noon, because a number of people were to check-in..and- that we "had the right" to hang out in the lobby or connecting coffee shop. I understand - but the housekeepers had already cleaned a number of rooms so that wasn't the issue...and she wasn't letting people check-in anyway we heard her tell people not until 3PM---so we hung out in lobby with all our Hawaii luggage for an hour until our ride came. We won't stay at Red Lion SeaTac again.. All for $150.00

name: Red Lion Hotel Seattle Airport
title: “Comfortable and Convenient”
text: Red Lion Hotel Seattle Airport is just as it says; right across the street from SeaTac. Very convenient accomodation for air travelers. Yet from inside my hotel room, I noticed no airport noise. Rooms are spacious, clean and comfortable. Hotel staff polite and helpful. Very affordable value in comparison to similar area hotels. I will definately make this my future hotel of choice when traveling to Seattle.

name: Red Lion Hotel Seattle Airport
title: “About what you'd expect from an airport hotel”
text:
This was my first time seeing or staying at this hotel. I have to say I was pretty shocked upon pulling up in the parking lot...the hotel could best be called orange. WOW. I was a little nervous about what the inside would be like, but was pleasantly surprised. It had typical decor, amenities and rooms. 
I stay at Red Lion hotels pretty often and have found there to be a range of what they offer. I would say this one falls right in the middle. There were no glaring flaws (carpets were clean, room was average size, decor was farily modern) or amazing features (parking was outside, view was parking lot). 
We didn't eat at the restaurant which was in the parking lot, outside the hotel, so I can't weigh in on that. There was very little plane noise throughout the night, but I could hear some in the morning. But considering that this hotel is literally across the street from the airport, so that's to be expected. I was a little disapointed that I was charged $10 for outdoor, self parking. Perhaps this is an airport hotel standard.
All in all, it was about what I would expect from an airport hotel...close, convenient, and reasonably priced.

name: Moore Hotel
title: “Old school charm for a great price AND a great location”
text:
Two blocks from Pike Place Market, you'll find this little gem. And for $100/night (for a Thursday) in this area of Seattle, you'll have a hard time beating the price. 
This is a renovated original building, complete with real keys (versus the plastic variety). I felt like I was in an old movie when I walked off the closet sized elevator, down the hallway. It's not one of those all frills included hotels, but you will get clean linens, and basic toiletries, and excellent guest service. The bathrooms have claw foot tubs, and although the shower head was a little low for my height, the charm of the room itself made up for it. I rated the sleep quality as average related to the box spring mattress, but the room itself (on the 7th floor) was quiet.
The location and the charm are two of the best features of the Moore Hotel. As long as their prices and service continue, I would pick this hotel again.

name: Crowne Plaza Seattle Downtown Area
title: “Comfortable but not exceptional”
text: We stayed at the CP for 6 nights. The rooms were adequate and clean but nothing out of the ordinary. The bed however was very comfortable and I loved the pillows! We were on the 15th floor and the traffic noise was loud. I've read reviews from others who received some type of comfort package with earplugs and sleep masks but we did not get anything like that. I found the hotel staff to be pleasant and helpful although housekeeping was somewhat lacking as my coffee and supplies weren't refilled every day and I had to ask for them at the front desk. The lobby was okay but it was small and I do prefer larger ones. I also wish there had been coffee available in the lobby as I've found in many other hotels. We were not happy that there was an added charge for wireless access as the room cost was high enough. The location was great and we were able to walk to almost everything although some streets are very steep! We were in Seattle for a convention and the hall was just a short walk through the park. We took the light rail from the airport and the train station was just a few blocks away so we were able to save on the cost of taxis. There are a lot of restuarants within walking distance also but check them out as some are very pricey!

name: Sheraton Seattle Hotel
title: “Great Location - but expensive”
text: I stayed here for three nights. Its used a lot for buisness so expect to see lots of buisness people. Overall its nice and the location is excellent. One down side is it is a little on the pricey side for what you get in your room. I would stay there again.

name: Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Supurb Location!”
text: My wife and I stayed here recently for our first time. Check-in was easy, and its location is the best. Right in the middle of downtown Seattle's business, shopping and dining area. You can walk to most attractions from here. Great little bar attatched to the premises also. We got a very nice corner room on the 8th floor. It appeared to be one of the larger rooms, according to the floor diagram. The bed itself was very comfortable. If your a light sleeper, request a higher floor due to the early morning street activity. I had ear plugs, and my wife sleeps soundly, so it wasn't much of an issue for us.

name: Sheraton Seattle Hotel
title: “Centrally Located Hotel in Downtown”
text: Overall I was happy with the hotel and most of the staff were friendly. We did have some not so pleasant service in the bar area with staff members standing around complaining about customers. And, the maid service wasn't so thorough. But, the location was great. Walking distance to just about everything we wanted to do. The beds were comfortable and we had all the basics we needed. Wifi in the room is not included ($10.95 per night) and parking (around $40 per night) was quite expensive. The valets however were very quick.

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton Hotel Seattle Airport - Southcenter
title: “Less than okay”
text:
We stayed at the Doubletree Suites the night before a flight out of Sea-Tac. We booked to leave our vehicle there for the duration of our trip. If you want to do this don't pay the extra $20 I did to keep your vehicle here. They just tell you to park anywhere in their lot and don't ask for your vehicle license number. However, I wouldn't do the "park and fly" here again since my vehicle got broken into while we were on vacation.
We were disappointed with the room. It started when we first walked into the room. It had the smell of stale cigarette smoke even though it was supposedly a non-smoking room. The bathroom was microscopic and the fan didn't work well enough to make it anything less than a humid pit. The rest of the room was okay but it had a very 80s feel to it and the rooms are very small. Not exactly what I expected from reading the other reviews. Our room also had a lovely view of the HVACs on the roof of the conference area of the hotel. We got to hear the drone of those HVACs all night long.
On the plus, the shuttle to the airport and the pickup on the return was excellent. However, I've learned my lesson about "park and fly" near Sea-Tac. Next time we'll park at a secure lot near the airport.

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton Hotel Seattle Airport - Southcenter
title: “Pretty Decent Hotel”
text: This was our first trip to Seattle. We decided to stay outside the city because we had friends who lived nearby in Kent and we wanted to make it convenient for them. Good choice! The hotel is right next to a large shopping center and there were numerous restaurants within walking distance. Doubletree prooved to be an ideal central location. The city proper was 20 minutes away and we could also take a short trip south to Tacoma and Bremerton. As for our room, it was huge. It was also very clean and quiet. Aside for th front desk employees who weren't very friendly, we had no complaints. We would definitely stay there again.

name: Courtyard Seattle Downtown/Pioneer Square
title: “Ottimo per soggiorno di lavoro”
text: Una settimana di lavoro a Seattle alloggio in questo ottimo hotel in downtown a 2 minuti fermata metro e in pieno centro con maggiori attrazioni raggiungibili a piedi. Pulizia perfetta, camere molto belle, piccolo bar collegato per snack e drinks

name: Moore Hotel
title: “Perfect when seeing a show, close to the Market.”
text: Excellent price for the location, just blocks away from the the Market. The room had everything you need, and parking was very reasonable with the hotel discount. Very convenient walking next door for the wshow at the theater, and the hotel was quiet. Just wish there was more water pressure in the shower and Internet access in the room.

name: Mediterranean Inn
title: “Highly recommend it”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights and it was the perfect location to explore Seattle. We walked to all the main attractions, Space Needle, Experience Music Project, Pike Place Market etc. The location is also close to lots of smaller shops and eateries. The view from the roof terrace was fantastic, take your breakfast up there and enjoy! The room was spacious with great coffee.

name: Red Lion Hotel Seattle Airport
title: “Not Really a Red Lion but still OK”
text: The Red Lion, hurriedly converted from a West Coast when we came, looked overdue for renovation. Our room had some paint peeling, but the restaurant was good and the lobby nice enough. Our building was unfortunately separated from the main, but by only a few feet. The location was good, especially for the excellent Museum of Flight, but the property really felt like the decent West Coast hotels rather than the added luxury you expect from Red Lion. This was in March 2003

name: Marriott Waterfront Seattle
title: “Never again”
text: I am a real Marriott fan and I have stayed at this hotel several times before without incident but this time was a disaster. There were dirty room service dishes (not mine) in the hallway for days, even after I complained several time. My room was not serviced ("The housekeeper for this room is new and must have forgotten" was the response I got). My car was not brought up when I called the valet (he said no one "told him" to bring it up). And when I asked the front desk attendant for the name of the GM, he said he didn't know who the GM was. Really??? You don't know your boss' name? Although they were ALL very apologetic, this was just a service nightmare. In all fairness, I have written the GM but have not heard back yet as it is too soon. But there were just too many problems and I expect more from a Marriott.

name: The Edgewater Hotel Seattle
title: “Unforgettable, romantic stay”
text:
Edgewater is built out onto a pier, so it really is over the water. The rooms are lodge decor, with a cozy fireplace. If you upgrade to the nicest rooms, be aware that the higher room numbers are out farther, are completely unobstructed. And you should upgrade because the views are amazing. Plus the soaking tub was lovely, as was the newly decorated bathroom. The room decor could use some upgrading--the bedspreads are in need of a change. 
Absolutely do eat at the restaurant--great food, beautiful decor, right on the water. And we enjoyed the nightclub afterward, which had good live entertainment. Breakfast was great too.
The one negative? No free internet which drives my husband nuts.

name: Silver Cloud Hotel - Broadway
title: “Another nice Silver Cloud but I prefer their Stadium location”
text: I love the Silver Cloud hotels. Each is unique and the design is modern and clean. I stayed here b/c Stadium was booked. It is everything that Silver Cloud is except for the location. Not much around and being near "Pill Hill" you may get woken up by the occasional ambulance rushing to the nearby hospital. The free shuttle around town is a great feature of this hotel chain. All in all though a very nice place and the price at $129 cannot be beat for the quality.

name: Residence Inn Seattle Downtown/Lake Union
title: “Great Location with beautiful views and delicious restaurants in walking distance”
text:
I am a huge Marriott fan. I have been platinum with this hotel chain for 4 years and have stayed at Residence Inns all over the country- this one was definitely up to the Marriott hotel standards.
The rooms are very spacious and up-to-date. I stayed in a two-bedroom suite with my co-worker. We both had a king sized bed, bathroom and plenty of space to ourselves. The shared kitchen was perfect along with a balcony in the living room area. Unfortunately there is no oven, but there is a stovetop, microwave and a community grill downstairs. 
Within walking distance you can find some great local restaurants! There is sushi, seafood and a variety of other restaurants directly across from the hotel, not to mention a ton of others within a half mile walk.
If you are coming from the airport, you can get here on the public transportation. Catch the metro from the airport, take it to the end of the line (under Nordstrom), catch the trolley line and ride it to the end (in front of the hotel). It takes about 45 minutes from the airport to the front door of the Residence Inn! If you are driving, the hotel is right off of the highway. Parking is expensive- $23 a day in the garage underneath. But you can park behind the hotel on the street for a 10 hour maximum at $1.50 an hour OR for free after 6pm until 8am, which gives another option, especially if you are working in the area.
I will say that if I were paying for the hotel room myself I would probably not stay here due to the high prices. Luckily I am in Seattle for business and my company pays for hotels. So my review is based on amenities and location alone, not factoring in the room rate.
***There is currently (Sept. 2012) road construction, which causes a few detours around the hotel. It is not a huge problem but just be aware of this***

name: Mediterranean Inn
title: “Really poor quality--A very bad stay.”
text: I'm not so sure why so many people rate the Mediterranean Inn as well as they do. This is one of those hotels that's all about show and very little about quality. I chose to stay at the hotel because of the generally positive feedback from TripAdvisor and the overall appearance of the hotel based on the pictures I had seen. But upon arrival, it was obvious that the hotel would be lacking. Generally unlean, tacky decor, and the bare minimum of comforts define the hotel. I've stayed in many Best Westerns that are superior in these regards. Our room was tiny and bed uncomfortable and overly springy, with old and dirty looking sheets. The window was tiny, and despite what you see in the pictures, there are no balconies--just made to look that way. Our refrigerator didn' t work, there was no air conditioning, and despite a temperate 70 degree day in Seattle, the whole place managed to be stuffy and uncomfortable. One of the elevators was broken the whole stay as well. The staff were generally unconcerned about things and there never seemed to be enough of them to handle things properly. The price is less than many other quality hotels in Seattle, but don't make the mistake of comparing this hotel to anything nice. Compare it to a Best Western or Ramada Inn, and you'll still be far happier at one of those.

name: Homewood Suites Seattle Convention Center Pike Street
title: “The place to stay in Seattle - location, friendly, comfy, highly recommend”
text:
This was a terrific place to stay for so many reasons.
Location: easy walking distance (well, as easy as it can be in Seattle) to the Convention Center, Pike Market, the monorail & train... it's got a great location.
Friendly: Everyone, all the time. An easy 5 out of 5!
Comfy: Great room, VERY comfy bed, kitchenette (great for leftovers!) our room had a small but very cool balcony. Clean, well-furnished, free internet - Room: easy 5 out of 5.
Food: Free breakfast which was really well done. Never too crowded, good selection of hot and cold food. Reception (dinner) in the evening - also well done!
Extras: car rental in house (this was great since we were there on the weekend and decided to rent one day). 
Highly recommended! We would stay here again without looking anywhere else.

name: Ace Hotel
title: “A hidden bathroom & great staff!”
text:
Unlike a lot of other people, I'd never heard of "Ace" so when I arrived I was very surprised. The entrance was nothing like most hotels and when you get to reception there's a beautiful wooden table with a fish tank next to it. Your room even has a real key. 
The hotel is small and I wasn't aware that not all rooms have bathrooms. My room had a bathroom but it took me a few minutes to find it. Why? Because it was behind a large revolving mirror wall! Very cool. The room wasn't huge but had a king size bed, desk, tv, stainless steel sink and open shower. Plus two very cozy robes. 
What I liked the most was the staff. They were very nice and very helpful in guiding me around the city and suggesting restaurants to try. 
The location is perfect and while the price wasn't exactly cheap, it wasn't much different from the neighboring hotels. Plus, you get a unique experience.

name: Roosevelt Hotel
title: “Location, location, location”
text: This was our second trip to Seattle w/in the last year. The first time we stayed at the Mayflower & would have done so again but for a friend’s recommendation to try the Roosevelt. We prefer boutique hotels to the big chains. The Roosevelt offered a senior rate which was an excellent value. The location was great – across the street from Pacific Place and an easy walk to Pike’s Place Market (my favorite go-to in Seattle). My room overlooked the street and I thought noise from traffic & the restaurant below (Von's) would be an issue but it wasn't at all. Overall I would rate this hotel better than average in most respects; front desk & concierge staff were friendly and helpful. This was our second trip to Seattle w/in the last year. The first time we stayed at the Mayflower & would have done so again but for a friend’s recommendation to try the Roosevelt. We took advantage of the senior rate which was an excellent value. The location was great – across the street from Pacific Place mall and an easy walk to Pike's and other attractions. Enjoyed the use of the robe & slippers but would've also liked an in-room safe. Overall I would rate this hotel better than average in most respects. We found the front desk & concierge staff to be friendly and helpful.

name: Hotel Deca, Seattle
title: “Consistantly Interesting”
text:
I stayed at the Dec recently and found it to be an interesting Art Deco styled place to stay. When I got there I realized that I had stayed in the same hotel (under a different owner) about 20 years ago. It was interesting then and remains so now. 
The decor is not typical chain hotel the only really odd thing about the place is the barn of a bar in the basement.
I'd stay again.

name: The Westin Memphis Beale Street
title: “Sweet Spot for Rock, Soul, and Memphis”
text: The new Westin Memphis Beale Street is seamlessly integrated into the burgeoning Center City Commission's hot, up-and-coming downtown Memphis. Located on a block that makes it neighbors with Morgan Freeman, Gibson guitars, the Rock n Soul Museum, FedEx Forum, and the world-famous Beale Street, you could not ask for a better location and value during your visit to Memphis. You'll find the staff to be incredibly helpful, friendly, and knowledgeable about their city--as are most Memphians. You'll be within walking distance of some of the city's greatest spots, including the National Civil Rights Museum. Rooms are spacious and comfortable, clean and new. The lobby is peacefully modern, impeccably kept, and the fitness facilities are above and beyond those you'd find in comparable hotels. The only drawback was arriving on the night of an event at the FedEx Forum; I had to park a few blocks away. From that point forward, there was easy parking in the garage next door.

name: The Westin Memphis Beale Street
title: “Not What We Expected”
text:
My husband, children and I decided to take a weekend trip to Memphis to tour Graceland and chose the Westin because of it's location and the fact that it was such a new property. Through confirmation emails from the hotel, they invited you to relax, unwind and feel rejuvenated. Well, upon arriving Saturday night at approximately 6:00, I was told that no rooms were ready......"We had a full house last night." I'm thinking, "Isn't check out at 12:00 and check in at 3:00?". For once, I arrive at a hotel past the check in time, only to be told that the rooms were not ready! Strike #1.
So my family and I sit, exhausted from a 5 hour trip, in the lobby with all of our luggage waiting on the push cart. There was a group of women in the lounge also waiting with all of their luggage, and they said they had been waiting for two hours. Luckily for us, we only waited about 20 minutes or so. So up to the room we go.
The room was very nice and we decided to order a movie and turn in early for the big day at Graceland tomorrow. Well, our room was on the 7th floor facing Beale Street. We were directly behind Silky O'Sullivans and there was a band playing. I am a fan of live music, but I was tired and really wanted to relax. The band was SO loud, that I felt like I was in the courtyard with them. I decide to call the front desk to see if they had any sort of white noise maker, and was told this: "Turn up your TV". Well, needless to say, that did not sit well with me. So, until about 3:00 a.m., I listened to Jungle Boogie, Mustang Sally, etc. All while attempting to get some sleep. Strike #2.
The next morning, we left and went to Graceland. Great time and well worth the trip. Well, when we got back to the Westin at about 3:00 that evening, we entered our room in hopes of feeling "refreshed and rejuvenated" and to our dismay, housekeeping had not even been by. So I called the front desk and they said they would get back with me. They never did. Strike #3, you're out. So we left in disgust and walked down Beale Street. Once we made it back to our room, at about 7:30, the room finally had been tended to. 
There were positives about the Westin: The Daily Grill had an excellent breakfast menu and the food was delicious. The wait staff was friendly, too. Also, Joan, the concierge was very helpful and sympathetic to my "issues" I had during my stay. My suggestion to anyone considering staying here would be to not bring any young children (mine were 8 and 5 ), and also don't stay here if you want to relax. Even though it was a beautiful hotel, it's more appropriate for those wanting to enjoy the night life. At least be sure and request a room on the opposite side of Beale Street.

name: Sheraton Seattle Hotel
title: “Nice place for a stop over”
text: We stayed here for one night while waiting to board our cruise to Alaska. We stayed on the 15th floor In a King room. Managed to get a great deal on this room through Priceline. It is very close to Pikes Place Market (about 3 blocks) as well as down town. The room itself was very nice, clean and had a good size bathroom. Parking is expensive though , about 30 dollars or so. The cruise parking area was also closeby. If you stay here try for a high room as the view lower is not as good.

name: Homewood Suites Seattle Convention Center Pike Street
title: “family welcoming atmosphere”
text: Rooms and suites very spacious and comfortable. Breakfast terrific for a family. Location is awesome! Staff extremely alert and freindly.

name: Mediterranean Inn
title: “Excellently located hotel with great service and rooms!”
text:
Located in great section of the downtown area, lots of excellent restaurants, bars, clubs, and pubs! Space Needle and many other things in close walking distance! 
Excellent service with a great little room!

name: Hotel Deca, Seattle
title: “Not at all what they make it out to be”
text: We stayed at the Hotel Deca so we could park our vehicle while we did the Alaska Cruise and stayed at the Hotel on the day we returned. Although all the arrangements had been made, when we arrived, the staff didn't have a clue what we were talking about. We were supposed to be shuttled to the port and the shuttle was not available, even though it was prearranged, so the manager took us herself. On our return from the cruise, we took a taxi to avoid having shuttle issues again and when we arrived at the hotel to drop our luggage, since our room was not ready that early, we requested a shuttle to take us into the city. You guessed it, the shuttle would not be available till after 3, so again we took a taxi. The staff just didn't seem to know what was going on and we didn't get anything that we had booked. Didn't get the right room, didn't get the shuttle, the beds have feathers in the mattress that stick in to you, and had plumbing problems to top it all off. Would not recommend this hotel.

name: Residence Inn Seattle Downtown/Lake Union
title: “Stay at Residence Inn”
text: We recently stayed at The Residence Inn at Lake Union/Seattle, WA. What attracted us to this hotel was the fact that they have two bedroom suites which others say they have but don't. The pictures of the room online also looked as though they have been recently renovated. We were traveling with two children as well. Overall this was a great hotel. They had a very nice complimentary breakfast every day with a nice variety. Three evenings they also had a light dinner, that our children enjoyed. The pool was nice and they have a seperate 3 foot pool for small children. This hotel was probably one of the most pet friendly hotels that I have ever seen. It actually seemed like my family was in the minority with out a pet. My only complaint was that our furniture in our living room (although newer) was very worn especially the chair. And there was a big stain in the middle of our carpet. Also the mattresses were horribly soft. I eventually got semi used to it. The kitchen was very nice and very nice to have a full size frig and microwave to cook some things for our children. Would definitely stay there again. Great location to get to airport, downtown, and suburbs. I did a lot of research on a room for a family of 5 staying for a week and The Residence Inn was definately the best game in town.

name: Silver Cloud Hotel - Broadway
title: “Good location. Nice functional hotel. Nothing too fancy. Good place to stay if you're visiting the medical centers”
text: We stayed here for one night, prior to taking the Amtrak Cascades from Seattle to Vancouver. The hotel is nice and clean. It is very functional, and the staff is efficient and friendly. Location was good for us, as we visited some family living nearby. It's a popular hotel for people visiting the medical facilities located nearby. Although it is a bit out of the way from downtown, the shuttle service was prompt and accomodating. We booked this hotel through Hotwire. Got a good price. We'd stay here again.

name: Residence Inn Seattle Downtown/Lake Union
title: “Great room and very comfortable.”
text: I was so happy to be able to stay here as the location was pretty great. It was right next to a trolley stop, although the trip there from the airport (without a car) was a little trickier. The room was beautiful and the bed was super comfortable. The customer service was excellent as well, and the breakfast was fine for a hotel. I would definitely stay there again!

name: Residence Inn Seattle Downtown/Lake Union
title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: My family stayed here Oct 6-10. It is the perfect place to stay especially for a family with children. The staff was freindly and helpful. The beds were comfortable. Hot breakfast was served every morning and was delishous. Having the streetcar right outside the hotel was great also for getting downtown. $2.50 for an adult. I would defineately stay here again!

name: SpringHill Suites Memphis Downtown
title: “Good location - bad management”
text:
This hotel, while perfectly located on Main Street, really could use a management change.
We stayed here over the extended 3 day weekend surrounding Labor Day. 1st note: finding the entrance with GPS is misleading. Address is Main Street - but you have to enter off of Court because Main Street is closed to vehicular traffic.
MARRIOTT'S FAULT: We checked in on the late side of Friday (after 9:00 pm). Service at the front desk was slow, slow, slow...did I mention they were slow? We went up to the room and discovered that the A/C unit - while functional - made a horrible rattle. I fudged with it for a while, attempting to squelch the noise, and discovered it was probably reported by some other weary traveler on a prior stay. I'm guessing hotel management / maintenance crew "fixed" the previuosly reported rattle by re-attaching the cover with packing tape - which had, by now, dislodged and was just hanging - not functional at all. We called the front desk - only to find out that, because of the late hour, nobody was available to remedy the situation until the next day (a Saturday? yeah right!). I ended up stuffing a pillow under the cover to prop it into place which made the rattle much less noticable. Unpacking is always the first thing I do. My husband gets the top drawer, I get the middle drawer, and our 7 year old gets the bottom drawer. I couldn't open the bottom two...they were off track or broken or both. In fact, once I managed to make an opening in the middle drawer large enough to get my hand into, I couldn't get it closed again. The suites do have a sitting area - with a large desk with drawers so we tried to get our things into that storage space. You guess it. They were broken as well. At that point, we just started looking for broken items to make a list for the maintenance crew that had been promised to us for a Saturday visit. The towel shelf over the toilet was barely hanging on -...we were actually afraid it would fall on our head while - well you get it. Plus, regular maintenance items were certainly lacking such as caulking around the tub and toilet. 
My 7 year old always swims in the morning, before we go out, and we figured (prior to booking) that an outdoor pool, in Memphis, in the dog days of summer would be okay. Besides it was a "heated" pool. Nope. In fact, the gentleman cleaning the pool (bless his sweet heart) indicated that the heater had been broken for "a lawwwwnnnggg time". His words (and inflection), not mine. It was a COLD pool even in the heat of the midday because the area is in the shadow of the tall building surrounding the hotel. 
Breakfasts were nicely done, in an area larger than other similarly priced Marriott properties, but the hard-working staff could not keep up with the crowd and supplies. The food rations seemed to be quite limited (running out of waffle batter, meat, eggs, and juices before the scheduled end to the service). Perhaps the management could have added staff / supplies for a holiday weekend? Oh, and Marriott - please make sure that hotel staff knows a little about replenishing toner cartridges in your business center printers...
NOT MARRIOTT'S FAULT: - The location of the hotel - on the aforementioned closed to vehicular traffic Main Street - is well-intentioned. I think that being on the long stretch of the public trolley line (with a stop right outside the hotel) and with the quaintly decorated stream of horse-drawn carriages clip clopping right outside was probably a good move on the part of Marriott. Having said that, Memphis has done nothing to keep a good impression in the minds of travelers. It looked good on the surface, and in on line photos - but once we walked down Main Streeet toward the Music Festival (another Labor Day weekend draw) we couldn't help but notice the boarded-up, barred windows, and trash laden benches, sidewalks, and alleys. Sorry- Memphis...you need to do better if you want to keep people in those hotel rooms.
I understand, from my husband's follow up call with Marriott corporate management that they are aware of issues at this hotel and are, in fact, at the time I am writing this review - making drastic changes to the staff management here.
It'll be a long time before we go back to this Spring Hill Suites. Sad to say, too, that my family will probably not go back to Memphis either. It really is not too much to expect for a city to welcome visitors with clean streets and safe environments to entice them to want to come again and again. NEVER again, for us.

name: Marriott Waterfront Seattle
title: “Great Stay at this Marriott property”
text:
March, 2009. I had the opportunity to spend three nights at the Seattle Marriott Waterfront hotel when business required me to be in the area and I was to bring a friend. The hotel is on Alaskan Way, about a quarter mile below Pike Public Market. I used the hotel's recommended private car service from SeaTac airport. Excellent driver/operator. This was my first stay at this hotel. Last year when in Seattle I stayed at the Grand Hyatt on Pine street.
Check-in was smoothand We received King rooms as guaranteed. Our room was on the Concierge level # and offered a great view of the Emerald City. The rate was below $130.00 per night, using the AAA discount. 
Our room, was very comfortable and nicely decorated. The bed was ultra comfortable. Both feather and foam pillows were available. Lighting in the room was very good with lamps on both sides of the bed, on the desk, and a floor lamp. The work desk was okay and the office-style chair functional and comfortable. The room had a a comfortable arm chair. We asked for a microwave.
The TV was had a lot of cable channels as well as a wide selection of pay-per-view movies. I looked at some previews and costs per movie seemed to be between $12 and $15. High-speed Internet service had a charge of $9.95 per day. .
The bathroom was clean. Lighting was good, the towels were plentiful, and the shower worked well – immediate hot water with plenty of pressure. Bath amenities include shampoo, conditioner, lotion, and mouthwash.
The concierge lounge was a couple of doors down the hall. The high tables and counters make it easy to use a laptop. There is complimentary wired internet service. I did not notice if there is Wi-Fi service or not. In the evening, the concierge lounge offered a hot appetizer, a variety of cheese and crackers, fruit and drinks. The breakfast buffet featured scrambled eggs, hot oatmeal, and all the other things you would expect on a breakfast buffet.
The hotel public areas were clean and well-kept, but could use an updating to the style of the rooms. 
The hotel has a small outdoor swimming pool and hydrotherapy spa. There is also a sauna and steam room accessible from the pool area. My friend used the gym and she told me it was well equipped.
There is one restaurant the hotel and several restaurants within few minutes and 10 minute walk from the hotel. We had breakfast several times in the onsite restaurant and food was good and service was great. I will stay at the Seattle Marriott if I can get a good again. Just outside the hotel is elevator and stairs that take you up near Pike's Market. The stairs is a bit of climbing but if you're in shape there is no problem. The staff were friendly and helpful. I highly recommend this property if one want a property a bit away from the hustle of downtown.

name: MarQueen Hotel
title: “Still very good”
text: Just spent five days with family at the Marqueen. Great location, great hotel. Comfortable beds, very spacious, the kitchen (even a table!) and sitting room perfect for a long stay. Staff excellent, great value. Highly recommended!

name: Moore Hotel
title: “Loved The Moore”
text:
My husband & I stayed at The Moore 6/9/07 & 6/17/07 (before & after a cruise). On our first stay we arrived before check in, but when the desk clerk heard our story about being stranded by the airport shuttle in the rain without our suitcases & not knowing where we were, he volunteered to find us a room we could check into early. The room was VERY clean & I thought it was alot larger than some newer hotel rooms. The tub is old, so it was huge! You can lay down in it. The bed was comfortable.Our rooms had recently been redone. In the morning we asked the desk clerk were we could catch a cab to the terminal, she said have a seat and I'll call you one. Did'nt expect this much service for the price.
On our second stay we arrived very early, 8:30(cruise ships are in at 6AM). The clerk stored our bags for us & told us that check in wasn't until 3PM but that we would probably be tired by than & to come back around noon & she would have a room for us. She did!
Both rooms we had were near the elevator, it didn't bother us at all. We delt with 3-4 different front desk employees, all were more than friendly and very helpful. We did see some homeless in the area, but no one bothered us. TWO blocks from Pike's Market & walking distance to the water, Seattle Center, the monorail & more! This was a bargin of a lifetime. 
About a block away is the Virginia Inn. We had a great dinner there on our first night. Lowell's in the market is really good for breakfast (ate there both mornings). Met friends there our first day for lunch, the clam chowder is horrible. Ivars on the water has the best clam chowder I have ever had.(Had this the second time thru Seattle)
Another great bargin. The double decker (narrated) bus tour.. $18. per person, good for 2 days. Ride it all around, get off when you want ,sightsee, walk around..get back on when the next bus comes thru..do it again,all over town. Stops about 3 blks. from the Moore. You can buy yor tickets from the driver.

name: Homewood Suites Seattle Convention Center Pike Street
title: “Good value, location and price”
text:
Rooms are a good size with a kitchenette, living room, bedroom and bathroom. I enjoyed the extra space which is good when you are away from home for several days. 
The free breakfast is limited in choice but it is free.

name: Ace Hotel
title: “Expect the worst”
text: A change of plans had us cancel our stay at the Ace Hotel. When we called to cancel - a week before our cancelled trip, we got a cancellation number. A month later, $240.57 (Canadian) had been charged on our credit card but we have since trashed the cancellation record. Given, we should have kept the number but the manager had been unhelpful, unsympathetic and snobby! Shame on them for being in the service industry. For $240.57, they have lost not only my business, but also of my colleagues and friends.

name: Hotel Deca, Seattle
title: “Art Deco Deca”
text: Super friendly staff, very helpful and genuine. The hotel felt safe, and secure. (I've stayed in some that dont give you that vibe!) Awesome renos and keeping with the retro feel. Convenient access to the I-5 which was great!

name: Days Inn Memphis at Graceland
title: “OK to visit Graceland”
text:
If you are planning on visiting Graceland then stay here otherwise look around for something else, we were there when the Christmas lights were on at Graceland just over the road and we could see them from our room, that was great, rooms are in need of refurbishment and modernising but for one night OK, walk to the Graceland tour office in
a couple of minutes, breakfast fine and staff helpful. The swimming
pool is something of a landmark as it is guitar shaped all be it only four strings!! Elvis would turn in his grave, thats if hes there, why is his name spelt wrongly on his gravestone??

name: Silver Cloud Hotel - Broadway
title: “Perfect Location, Excellent Service”
text: First time staying in a Silver Cloud Hotel ( frankly never heard of the chain) Very Very Very happy with the entire stay. Excellent service from Paul at the front desk. Nice room, Clean and comfortable. Perfect location. Very close to all Seallte attractions, but just outside. Great walking, very safe neighborhood

name: Grand Hyatt Seattle
title: “I LOVE THIS HOTEL”
text:
There - I said it. I love this hotel. Everything about it makes me want to go back. Location was superb. Love how the taxi sweeps in off the street. Very effortless check in. Beautiful lobby to walk into. Room on the 23rd floor had fantastic cityscape views all across downtown Seattle. The bathroom was very big, very bright, very modern with super touches such as dimmer switches for the bath area. At last an individual shower area. 
We had pre dinner drinks and breakfast in the Ruth's Chris Steakhouse which doubles as the hotel dining facility. It has an excellent wine list and the steaks looked fantastic.
All in all. i don't think i will even consider any other hotel in Seattle for next year's trip.

name: Homewood Suites Seattle Convention Center Pike Street
title: “Like home!”
text: Homewood is always the best for extended stays. This location has great service and a wonderful location. Excellent weekday receptions. Salmon and cocktails are on the menus. Decent daily breakfast and clean comfortable rooms.

name: Homewood Suites Seattle Convention Center Pike Street
title: “A great set up, much better than the standard conference hotel”
text: Stayed at Homewood Suites while at a recent conference at the convention centre. I found the set up really convenient and really liked not constantly having to eat out. The suites all have some cooking facilities and a breakfast buffet is provided included in the price. On weekday evenings there is also a light evening meal including wine or beer provided free of charge. The food is not cordon bleu but the breakfast had enough variety to make most people happy. The staff were extremely helpful and friendly and rooms were of a good standard. The only downside was freeway noise - ear plugs are provided though! Although Homewood is part of the Hilton group the experience was very different from the standard Hilton city-centre hotel experience, service was better and I didn't feel like they were going to try and charge me extra every time I moved a muscle.

name: Crowne Plaza Seattle Downtown Area
title: “Avoid Crowne Plaza”
text: Although the location is pretty good, the overall service was horrible. The woman at the hotel reception was curt. When we got to our room we had two double beds. We called down to see if we could switch rooms to either one queen or king and the operator said no because we booked through priceline. The room was a nice size...of course it was, it had two beds. The heater was a bit smelly. The bathroom smelled like mildew, and it was difficult to find accurate water temperature on the shower. Overall, I would avoid this hotel.

name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Hip but elegant”
text: We truly enjoyed our stay in this lovely old hotel in downtown Seattle. The hotel is excellently located in an area that by bus, taxi or metro lets one enjoy all of the city. The Saturday morning market was totally awesome, to repeat an often used phrase but it describes thus place to a T.

name: Hyatt At Olive 8
title: “Sleepless in Seattle”
text:
Wonderful hotel in a very convenient location. Short walk to monorail and Pike Market. We stayed in a corner King---the room was immense with great views, very contemporary look, gorgeous bath amenities. The entire staff could not have been more cordial--Special kudos to Sarah at the desk and the concierge for his restaurant recommendation(Blue Acre--Fabulous!)
Dallas Cowboys also stayed while we were there. If and when we return to Seattle, we will definitely book here. A totally marvelous experience!

name: Grand Hyatt Seattle
title: “What you expect”
text: I stayed in this hotel for business and got everything I would have expected from a place with Hyatt's reputation. The service was very friendly and attentive, there was great choice and again service for breakfast and the room had everything I needed. Hotel of choice for work trips to Seattle!

name: Silver Cloud Inn - Lake Union
title: “Fantastic Value!”
text: Wow; huge selection at the free breakfast with hit and cold foods, a free shuttle to the main city attractions and a great room with Aveda toiletries. We saved a bundle of cash and aggravation. Great front desk staff and shuttle drivers made our stay very enjoyable. Will recommend this stay to all our friends and family!

name: Watertown Hotel Seattle
title: “Outstanding in every way!”
text:
Very Comfortable! Excellent quality! This hotel is almost like being at home. Very Comfortable Rooms! I almost never sleep well in a hotel the first night. I slept great!
Very Quiet even though my room overlooked the street. The staff is very friendly and they know the area! The complimentary breakfast is very high quality.

name: Watertown Hotel Seattle
title: “I definitely will be back”
text: Watertown Hotel is very conviently located next to the University of Washington Campus. I was visiting my son in Phinney ridge and this was the closet best place with the most ammenities I could find. The rooms are super clean and very modern. A euro feel. Best of all it is 100 % non smoking! I love the fact that they have a free shuttle to downtown and provide free bikes to ride on. I love this hotel!

name: The Paramount Hotel
title: “Fit for a Queen or King”
text:
My stay at the Paramount hotel was an awesome experience. Though we arrived early before check-in, they allowed us to hold our luggage in a safe location while we explored the downtown area as our room was being prepped for us. The hotel is just a short stroll to the Pike market place and other great locations. If you are a coffee lover like me, you will also enjoy the fact that there is coffee shops just about on every street corner. No joke!
The beds were comfy, room was nice and had a great view. White robes were also included! The hotel staff were beyond helpful and courteous.
Only flaw was the parking charge each night and if we needed to get something from the car had to check in with the staff to get access. Overall, it was a great stay!

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Pioneer Square Hotel
title: “Excellent Place to stay”
text:
This was an excellent place to stay
- Very courteous,accomodating & helpful staff
- Clean and nice rooms
- very nice breakfast to start the day
The construction does not bother at all..closeby to Pike street or Amtrak station !!
We loved the stay !!!

name: Hyatt At Olive 8
title: “Excellent hotel, service, location....and green to boot!”
text: This is my second stay at the Hyatt at Olive 8. I had stayed here a year or two ago. Great rooms, great room service, great location (minutes to public transport and shopping). The place to stay if you want to be green!

name: Homewood Suites Seattle Convention Center Pike Street
title: “disappointing experience”
text: We booked this hotel for its location downtown. Parking was $25 extra. The valet was hurried and rude. Our tv didn't work which they did fix when asked. Our phone never worked. Loud sirens were heard outside as was the tv of our neighbor - not ideal with a baby. We missed the free breakfast because it closed at 10am on a Sunday, for crying out loud! We arrived at 10:02 and everything was packed up and gone - so obviously they started clearing it out before 10am. We were not warned about breakfast times by check-in staff. Because they only had a few rooms left, we spent about $300 with taxes for a one night stay. Needless to say, I expect a lot more for that price: very disappointing and will not return.

name: Silver Cloud Inn - Lake Union
title: “Top Choice.”
text:
The Silver Cloud at Lake Union is an excellent hotel for leisure travelers and very good for business folks. It is on the northern edge of downtown Seattle, a little too far from the CBD to walk to a meeting, but close enough to be convenient to the entertainment areas. Seattle Centre is an easy walk. Walking in Seattle has never felt unsafe. The location makes the Silver Cloud feel a little less harried than other hotels right in the core. We've seen a couple reviews mention that dining is hard to find in the hotel's neighbourhood. Not true. There at least 7-8 restaurants within a 10 minute walk. Most of them across the street from the Cloud, on the lake shore. 
The front desk staff are almost always welcoming and enthusiastic. Occasionally though, the check-in crew will turn a little less welcoming when the room has been booked through Priceline or one of the other discount sites. Upgrading to a lake view room when a booking is done outside the Silver Cloud system can be a challenge.
A lot of good stuff is included in your room rate; 24 hour indoor pool/hot tub, shuttle to or from different spots downtown (take it to the baseball/football/soccer game and walk back along the water), a decent breakfast in a nice room, and free parking. This may be the only hotel in downtown Seattle that charges less than $25 a night for parking. 
The rooms are large, with a fridge, desk and a great television. Everything is always spotlessly clean throughout the property. Aveda products in the bathroom. The lake view rooms with 2 queens come with Juliet balconies but the king rooms do not. 
You are not likely to be disappointed if you stay here.

Address: '700 3rd Ave (corner of Third and Cherry - hotel entrance on Cherry Street)'
name: The Arctic Club Seattle - a DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel
title: “very nice”
text:
stayed here on the first night of our honeymoon before heading to vancouver island. when the staff found out about this, they sent up some chocolate covered strawberries which were absolutely delicious!!
the hotel is "old world" decor style--classy and clean.

name: Silver Cloud Inn - Lake Union
title: “Excellent”
text: Stayed only one night. My wife and I had an appointment nearby and we were taking the Victoria Clipper the next day and so we stayed at this hotel. Absolutely no regrets. As soon as we checked in we left our bags in the room and went back downstairs to take the free shuttle to Pike Place Market. The shuttle also goes to Pioneer Square and the Space Needle. When we called to be picked up again, the shuttle was back at the drop off point in less than 10 minutes. The room was clean and comfortable. I would definitely stay here again.

name: Hyatt Place Seattle/Downtown
title: “A Gem!”
text: With such glowing reviews of this hotel, I was actually hesitant to try, for fear of disappointment! However, due to a family funeral, this was the hotel reserved for everyone. What a gem. The lobby was welcoming, the rooms nice and yes, the breakfast is as what everyone is raving about. I could not believe the quality and selection of the breakfast. Three kinds of skillet breakfast sandwiches, waffles, and the usual complement of cereal, breads, pastries, etc. The fruits were fresh and sweet. No rubbery fake scrambled eggs here! Walgreen's is right across the street for bottled water, snacks, forgotten toiletry items, and yes, an extra suitcase for over zealous shopping. The shuttle is a nice benefit, since downtown parking is often so expensive and hard to find. The cons would be the $20 daily parking rate, and for my trip, it was a bit hard to navigate to the freeways due to the construction. But those would not be deal breakers. Will definitely stay here again should I travel to Seattle in the future. In fact, I will now search out other Hyatt Place in other locations I travel to.

name: Marriott Waterfront Seattle
title: “Tolle Lage mit kleinen Schönheitsfehlern”
text: Das Marriott liegt super in der Nähe des Kreuzfahrtanlegers, aber auch fußläufig zum Pike Place Market und zur Innenstadt. Perfekt auch für alle, die ein Motorrad über EagleRider gemietet haben oder mieten wollen: das Stadt-Büro ist im Hotel! Das Hotel ist modern. Die Ausstattung der Zimmer wie üblich bei diesen Ketten. Nichts , was man kritisieren kann - außer einer lärmenden Klimaanlage, die sich auch nicht abstellen läßt! Also nichts für sensible Menschen, die ihren Schlaf brauchen.

name: Silver Cloud Inn - Lake Union
title: “Perfect stay in this Hotel”
text: We stayed in this delightful Hotel. Who provide wonderful stay, friendly service and an extraordinary breakfast. The room was beautiful, sunny and clean, and we were made to feel at home at all times. It’s a breath of fresh air because of the stunning landscape outside with beautiful flowers. Overall, I would thoroughly recommend this hotel.

name: Grand Hyatt Seattle
title: “Top-notch, beautiful hotel and very relaxing!”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Grand Hyatt in March 2012 for a 3 day trip to Seattle. This hotel is in a great location, close to restaurants and shopping and of course, Starbucks! There is a Starbucks attached to the hotel. The monorail is only about a block away which is a great way to get over to the Space Needle and EMP. The rooms in this hotel are so beautiful and very comfortable. I loved the wall to wall windows overlooking the city. Our room had a lovely sitting room with TV, couch, and desk. The bathroom was UNREAL with a deep soaking tub (we bought some bubble bath at the mall across the street so we could try it out and it was heavenly!) and large glass shower. This hotel has all of the amenities. We tried room service and the food was delicious, the staff polite and friendly. The concierge outside was very helpful with tips and hailing cabs. We would love to stay here again on our next trip to this beautiful city!!

name: The Westin Seattle
title: “Not the quality you might expect”
text: We booked a weekend stay at the Westin Seattle thinking that, being a Westin it would be clean and comfortable and the service would be good. We were quite wrong. This hotel is well below what I expect from a Westin. I'm not a normal complainer but at almost $300 a night you expect certain things, cleanliness being one of them. While the hotel is in a good location we had the following problems with the hotel. The white bed sheets has stains on them, the floors were dirty, the maids don't seem to vacuum the floors, the service was very slow. I had dropped some crumbs on the floor in the morning and figured it would get cleaned up by the maid when we got back at the end of the day. Not so. We got some wine to celebrate one night and called down for a corkscrew. We got it, 1.5 hours later. The last annoyance was the lack of a free internet kiosk. I know I should have brought my laptop but do you have to nickel and dime me at $12 an hour just to check my emails? This Westin is in trouble because there are plenty of other options for hotels in that price range. I certainly won't be back.

name: The Westin Seattle
title: “Great hotel!”
text: This is a great hotel and especially at the low, low price of $139.00 from Priceline in the summer on a weekend. I was a bit reluctant because when you book on Priceline you don't know the hotel until you have basically paid a non-refundable night(s). Also since I think it rated at only 3.5 stars I was wondering if it would be up to my neat freak standards. YES, it was! The staff was very attentive and handed me water bottles the minute I walked in after my morning runs. They also had small pocket laminated running route maps at the concierge desk. The concierge knew everything! Pool is a little on the stuffy, chlorinated side since it is inside but still nice. Our room had the most wonderful view of the city, harbor and space needle. I think it was the best view at the hotel, room 4632. Our room was immaculate and we loved the in-room Starbucks coffee and tea. I really can't think of any negatives about our stay at the Westin. It is also perfectly located. We walked to Whole Foods and bought food to go since we have young kids and the hotel even brought up a mini-frig at our request at no charge.

name: Hotel Deca, Seattle
title: “Terrific Hotel in the U District”
text: We stayed here on the last weekend of the Seattle International Film Fest since all three of the movies we were seeing were playing at the Neptune Theater kitty-corner from the Deca. The decor throughout is very well done and upkeep/cleanliness was good. Although the room was small, the unusual shape, smart furnishings and large sunny bay window made it seem more spacious and on the whole it was very comfortable. The bathroom was tiny, but well renovated. The free parking in a lot just outside was great. Staff friendly, helpful and sincerely cheerful. My only gripe (except for the scratchy TP in the bathroom) was room service quit at 1000 on a Saturday night - no cold sandwiches, salads, snack - nada. Would definitely recommend to colleagues and friends.

Address: '700 3rd Ave (corner of Third and Cherry - hotel entrance on Cherry Street)'
name: The Arctic Club Seattle - a DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel
title: “One of the coolest hotels around...”
text: Unbelievable charming remodeled historic hotel in the heart of downtown. Feels like you are stepping back in time to the early 20th century, yet the hotels has all the modern conveniences of today (hard to even tell is part of the Hilton chain). Accommodating staff, comfortable rooms (some may think they are a little on the small side compared to chain hotels but they are plenty big enough). Nice upscale bar (Polar Bar) in back of lobby the serves small bites, and just about any drink you can imagine. June restaurant is attached to hotel, did not eat there but looked amazing. Great downtown location, can walk to just about anywhere. Would be great hotel for romantic getaway, special occasion, etc. When you have a choice to stay at someplace like this among all of the other cookie cutter chains, why not? Will definitely be back to this place!

name: Silver Cloud Inn - Lake Union
title: “Great Pick!”
text: Chose this hotel based on other reviews and they were right on. Very helpful staff. Jay upon check-in suggested an upgrade to water view and it was well worth it. The view of the lake including boats and water planes was great. The hotel is clean, rooms are spacious. One of the best features is the free shuttle to downtown attractions. The drivers were informative. We never waited more than 15 minutes for a ride. Another feature is the breakfast. It takes place in a large sunny room overlooking the lake. Unlike other hotels, they use dinnerware and silverware...no plastic or paper. It was well stocked with numerous choices. Parking was also included in enclosed garage.The location is within a good proximity to downtown. We were able to walk to the Needle and downtown, but as I mentioned the shuttle is always available. Great choice for value and a quality hotel.

Address: '700 3rd Ave (corner of Third and Cherry - hotel entrance on Cherry Street)'
name: The Arctic Club Seattle - a DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel
title: “Good value hotel”
text: We stayed for three nights and found this to be a good value, well located hotel. Room was comfortable, and service friendly. Lovely "Club" style bar & lounge which is good for a nightcap. Bus is just outside the door, and there is a good selection of restaurants and bars just down the street. Only downside was difficulty in getting a taxi one morning. The front desk had booked one for us and called again after 15 mins, but none appeared so we ended up just catching a bus! Staff mentioned that many taxi drivers don't know the hotel.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Seattle Downtown
title: “Nice place!”
text: Found this place on line, after weeks of searching hotels in downtown that weren't $450. We were so pleased! Especially loving their 1 pm check out time. Great beds, nice leather recliner--tv was smaller. Pet friendly. There was construction next door, but it did not disturb our sleep at all in the early morning. There are 10 parking spots right by the door if you are lucky enough to score one--tight squeeze for our SUV. The regular parking lot is around the block, and it was blocked by a truck--so they let us park right outside the door, until the truck left. Nice shower, pet friendly-- quick jaunt to the market, downtown, art museum, and Dick's drive in on Capitol HIll (which they nicely gave us directions for.) Room was quiet and nice ammenitites.

Address: '700 3rd Ave (corner of Third and Cherry - hotel entrance on Cherry Street)'
name: The Arctic Club Seattle - a DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel
title: “A Lovely, Historic Property”
text: First the down side. It's located several blocks off the beaten path in downtown and close to what is a changing area somewhat fraught with urban challenges. Get used to frequent police sirens and ambulences sent to pick up stabbing victims a few blocks away. Most of the crime is related to homelessness, poverty and alcohol and drug use and not aimed at tourists or residents. Seattle has always had a plethora of Native America, African-American and other street people. The economy isn't helping. So, with that out of the way, let me state that this is a lovely, well-maintained property. The building's history is fascinating, as are some of the decor items used throughout that were part of the original property. Front desk, valet and room service staff were, for the most part, professional, warm and responsive. Rooms are varied in layout, but well appointed and extremely comfortable. Nice big bathrooms make up for somewhat smaller rooms, but it makes for a very nice stay. The main part of downtown is a pleasant 10 minute walk away, along with Pikes Place and other tourist areas. Seattle is a great walking city so take advantage of it. Your body will thank you!

name: The Westin Seattle
title: “Creepy and Old”
text:
I recently stayed 4 nights at the Westin on business. It was a dismal experience. The room was dark, creepy and old. It was also pretty small and the bed was a murphy style that flipped down from the wall. One plus: the fabulous view.
I had breakfast in the casual eatery each morning and found it to be overpriced...a egg mcmuffin style sandwich and a bottle of water ran $13. Room service was even pricier, the one meal I ordered was bland and tasteless and ended up costing $42. 
The worst part about my stay was while I was waiting for room service. I get a call telling me to open my door and when I do, I find another door has been closed, thereby locking my room and the room next to me off from the elevator vestibule and hallway. It was not just closed, but locked witha deadblot, and the top latch thrown, too. This caught me completely off guard and when I opened it the room service attendant could tell I was flustered. I asked who closed and locked that door and he was as dumbfounded as me. All he could come up with was that the person in the room next to me had closed it perhaps to make it quieter....why the Westin even has doors like that is beyond me. 
I spent the rest of the night uneasy.

Address: '700 3rd Ave (corner of Third and Cherry - hotel entrance on Cherry Street)'
name: The Arctic Club Seattle - a DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel
title: “Great”
text: Friendly helpful beautiful elegant walk to link, Pike place and stores

name: The Westin Seattle
title: “Loved the Towers”
text: My husband and I stayed at The Westin Seattle for five days in April. We were in town for a convention with a group of fifteen. Eleven of us managed to book rooms in the Towers, and we all had a great experience. The rooms were beautiful... albeit we had an awesome view of Elliot Bay from the 31st floor. Housekeeping was prompt and maticulate. My only complaints were; 1. The room layout prevented access to the chest of drawers, as upon opening the drawers, the bed was in the way and niether piece of furniture wanted to move, and 2. I would suggest not eating in the hotel. There is much better food to be found elsewhere at more reasonable prices.

name: Cedarbrook Lodge
title: “Gorgeous”
text: Was overnighting for a work function here at this beautiful lodge. I've stayed at numerous hotels on the main strip and never knew this was so close to the airport!! What a hidden gem! And all the employees were outstanding!! Rooms aren't huge but the amenities more than make up for it. Deep soaking tubs, nice gym, and a quaint little lounge. It was like we had driven into the mountains and were staying at a ski lodge. Will definitely recommend this hotel and will try to make this my first choice when I stay in Seattle. Outstanding job!

name: Hotel Andra
title: “Outstanding customer service!”
text: My wife and I had a wonderful stay at Hotel Andra during my wife's birthday. We brought our dog to the hotel, and the staff were extremely friendly and accommodating. My wife was recovering from a broken foot, and when the elevators were down on Saturday night due to a fire alarm (which forced her to take the stairs), the staff brought up a gift of chocolates and a birthday card afterwards to say sorry and to make us feel more at home! The entire staff was extremely customer focused, from the housekeepers, front desk staff, bellmen, and valet. Everyone put forward their absolute best effort. By far one of the best hotel services I've ever had!

name: Hotel Deca, Seattle
title: “Paper thin walls, dirty floors, dicey neighborhood at night.”
text:
I was woken by people talking while waiting for the elevator and could hear person next door move their shower curtain! 
Bathroom smelled like a wet sweatsock after I showered. And then, I stepped on what I hope to god was a crumbled chocolate cookie left by a previous occupant near the base of the bed. Gross. 
The neighborhood by day is fine, but at night, its scary. I stepped out for a bite and saw a guy cleaning his crack pipe and got offered drugs twice, all within 2 blocks of the hotel.
The lobby looks cool, but don't read a book by the cover.

name: Hotel Deca, Seattle
title: “a pleasant experience for UW visitors”
text: Only stayed two nights as in transit to cruise. Found the hotel clean and welcoming with decent breakfast on offer. Shuttle was helpful for getting into Seattle downtown as is a little isolated from the trouristy areas. Very good if wanting to be near the university.

name: Sheraton Seattle Hotel
title: “Great location, beautiful hotel!”
text: This hotel was central to everything downtown Seattle. I walked to Pike's Place Market every morning, and it was just a short cab ride to the Space Needle and Union Square. My room was spacious and clean. The bed was comfortable. The staff was friendly. I would definitely stay at this hotel if I were to return to Seattle.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Pioneer Square Hotel
title: “Great location and staff, very clean well kept”
text: A great hotel in wonderful condition. Very nice staff. Walking distance to many nice restaurants and shops. It was great to have two single beds.

name: The Sorrento Hotel
title: “Great Staff”
text: We booked the Sorrento directly through the hotel website. Got an excellent price for our 3 night stay. The staff was great, starting off with the concierge who let us know before we arrived that a hotel car was available to pick us up at the ferry, saving us the cost of a taxi.
