Very friendly and helpful front desk staff made sure everything was satisfactory. We were upgraded to a suite which was a nice perk. Some minor quibbles: like in many other old hotels, the bathroom was small; we were on the second floor above the entrance and noise and unwanted light were problems (we had to keep the bathroom door closed to keep out light but were unable to close the drapes in the bedroom) and there is an underlying odour (more in the halls, less in the rooms). Overall an excellent stay, however.

name: The Sorrento Hotel
title: “Can't wait to come back”
text: My wife and I just pent 4 nights at this beautiful hotel. The service was very friendly and accommodating. We had a junior suite that was perfect in size, comfort and decorating. I highly recommend this hotel. The food at the Hunt Club was very good and we ate at the bar as the restaurant was empty.

name: University Inn Seattle
title: “Nice view”
text: I've just returned from staying here for 5 days on business.This hotel offered a nice continental breakfast each day. They had waffle irons to make homemade waffles and feel a little less like being away from home. The woman overseeing the breakfast was so sweet and friendly each morning. They also had a mid day snack daily and it also was quite a selection. The front lobby has a dish of candies and was sampled on many occasions. The room was enjoyable with a refigerator and microwave. It had a wonderful triangular window extending past the edge of the building allowing for a great view to look out upon the city.

name: Mayflower Park
title: “"Mad Men"-Era Historical Property: You Give Up Some Contemporary Amenities”
text:
When you walk in, you see old photos of the place, in its hey-day, I would imagine. It's got a couple of shiny brass plaques attesting to the property's official "historical building" status. So I am sure this review will not sit right with the kinds of travelers who love older properties and historical places, like old-timey inns and "charming" B and Bs, and so on. So let me say the nice things: You couldn't be in a better location in downtown Seattle. Perfect for going anywhere on foot. Pikes Place is nearby, and you pass excellent retail places, like Columbia, where we often buy travel clothing. Public transportation is everywhere. The concierge office is great. They lent us two day-passes to the Seattle Art Center. Wow, what a nice perk. We were also upgraded, at no expense, into a large queen "deluxe" room, and it was nice to have the extra square footage for a few nights, to say nothing of the one of the three windows that looked out over the beautiful tree-filled park that has the Occupy Movement and a convenient Starbucks. The upper lobby was very plush, and a nice place for us to cool our heels after we checked out but before we went to the airport later that night. We were offered food and drink service while we sat up there--very nice. The property has an adjoining restaurant and lounge. We hit the lounge for lunch and evening drinks: good service, nice draft selection, good reds. 
All right, that said, the hotel's weak Wifi is not up to the task. It was down three times in three days, mostly an hour or so each morning. Of course, they blamed Comcast, but it doesn't take an IT specialist to know that their arcane password-protected system is at fault. They deliver a paper newspaper to your door??? Just a waste of money, like the old peoples' television, which we never watch. The bathroom has shampoo, conditioner, and body lotion in pint-sized vats with squirters that are mounted to the wall like its a YMCA gym. Guess it saves them money so they can deliver a newspaper I throw away. The hard bed was a queen-sized bed!!! Hello!!! All this square footage and a little bed-for-one-person. The room was crowded with dated furniture like a hoarder lived there. I had to move everything back against the walls so it resembled a flea market with some room for foot traffic. Housekeeping, I am sad to say (and I tipped every morning), didn't do that great of a job. The stupid hotel landline rang THREE times when we were there. I had to unplug it. The room is filled with really dated stuff: lots of old brass fixtures, a two-prong (i.e., 1980s) electrical strip along the floor that is inadequate for powering cell phones and devices, and old curtains and light shades. There must have been 15 pieces of ad copy paperwork and laminated trifolds on the flat surfaces, when we checked in. Clutter! We piled them up so they were not in the way on one of the several pieces of furniture we never were going to use anyway. Like visiting an elderly aunt who was falling behind on the renovation she did thirty years ago. While we were there, the staff ran some sort of training crew around our floor noisily, and a room across the hall was being worked on equally noisily for one entire day. The workout room has old equipment. The elliptical didn't work, the two treadmills needed replacement, and they had no bathroom. Two yoga mats--always a nice sign in any hotel--were on the floor being walked on by the few of us who were using the equipment: UNSANITARY; no one is going to use them, people! (There is a good yoga place across the street, BTW.) To their credit, they did provide Purell and cleaning wipes. Room service was expensive and not all that good. It wasn't cheap. We paid over two hundred bucks a night. For that money, I would either expect a bit more or be willing to pay a little more to get what I need. I like to visit charming places, not stay in them. So I wouldn't recommend the Mayflower Park to other travelers, unless you were like the friendly dude in the museum who said he and his wife would come into Seattle, from where they lived in the 'burbs, and stay at the Mayflower Park to enjoy its historical ambience for a Saturday night to enjoy the city. There are three or four good modern hotels within a block or so for travelers who carry iPads and devices/phones and so on. Look near the convention center, around the corner for them. Please, if you are hotel management, don't reply to this.

name: The Maxwell Hotel Seattle
title: “Top Notice Hotel”
text:
We spent one night at the Maxwell and wished we could have stayed there for the rest of our trip. The room was clean, large, and most of all extremely comfortable. The service was friendly and helpful from check-in to check-out – and we arrived at 9:30am off a cruise ship. They offered to hold our luggage, and gave us a wonderful map of the area. Short walk to Seattle Center and the Monorail to downtown made the location excellent for sightseeing in those two areas. We were renting a car the day we checked out and they helped us out by having the shuttle driver take us and our luggage to the rental car location – after holding our luggage the whole day after we had checked out. 
The lack of a hotel and area directory was a little odd to us but when we inquired we were told to just ask as many questions as we had and they would help us out – which they did.
Overall, this is one of the nicest hotels we have stayed in and I would highly recommend it for your visit to Seattle Center and downtown.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Seattle
title: “The best in Town”
text: I have been visiting Seattle several times a year for over 25 years and the Four Seasons is the best hotel in town by a huge margin

name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Unbelievable service, stellar accomodations”
text: I checked into the Vintage Park for a weekend conference at a nearby hotel. The level of quality and service was head and shoulders above at the Vintage! I was delighted by the hot chocolate that was waiting each afternoon, and the evening wine tastings were relaxing. The staff was the friendliest I've encountered in some time. The room was clean, and the bed was soft and really comfortable. I can't think of a single thing I would change about my trip. I will absolutely stay at the Vintage on every trip to Seattle, no questions asked.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Seattle
title: “Great for business and leisure travelers”
text:
Stayed at the wonderful four seasons for 3 nights for work and sightseeing. 
I've stayed at many different four seasons properties across the globe and this one is better than the average four seasons. 
The service is great. The front desk and lobby staff are super friendly and go out of their way to helpful. They made great restaurant recommendations (metropolitan grill was my fav) and assisted us in storing/refrigerating some food we purchased at nearby Pike market. 
The location is great - very close to the famous pike market and acquarium (great for kids). Seattle is a terrific walking city with lots of shopping choices and we found the four seasons to be a great home base to see everything. 
The room was very high quality and modern. Love the in mirror tv. Always appreciate the turn down service with complimentsry bottles of water. The housekeeping staff was invisible yet they always cleaned our room whenever we left the room, which is the way it should be. Had a nice view of the water from our room. Very nice room overall. 
The fitness center has pretty new equipment but not much choice. Nice views of the water from the treadmill. Pool was closed, outside only and pretty small. The spa was pleasant, and massage was good like most other four seasons spas. The locker room was a bit disappointing - small with a steam room but no sauna or whirlpool. 
Wifi Internet worked well but was expensive. Tv choices were great - even had nfl network. Had breakfast one morning and it was uneventful as the food was very average - you're better off walking to a nearby diner. 
Overall I would definitely recommend the four seasons Seattle to anyone traveling to Seattle for work or fun.

name: Hotel 1000
title: “Great location, comfy stay”
text:
our stay to seattle was brief but the hotel staff was so accommodating and welcoming. i'm from l.a. and the staff there would have been obnoxious, stuck up and rude. no such thing here, just friendly and genuine.
the hotel room was spacious and comfy. modern but warm feeling. hotel tub was relaxing but the water from the ceiling was weird. would have liked a bigger shower/rainwater shower head but overall the bathroom had a luxurious, spa feel. morton brown amenities, yes please!
the location couldn't have been better to explore all seattle had to offer. pike place, seattle center, pioneer square. close to the light rail, waterfront. excellent place to tour around.
the hotel gym was a bit small and crowded on a monday morning but the equipment was good and varied enough.

name: Hotel Andra
title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text:
We like staying in Suites and the Suite here was fabulous. Very nicely furnished & large. The bedding and Towels are of very good quality.
The staff very friendly especially the concierge Lorraine. I had asked for a Sunday newspaper that they were all out of because it was Monday and they went to another hotel and got one for me. Very impressed.

name: The Sorrento Hotel
title: “Obviously heading back to Seattle VERY soon!”
text: I’m not really a review person, but I felt compelled to write one for the Sorrento because frankly I hope they open one in every city around the globe! Even though there is much to explore in Seattle, I had a hard time leaving the cozy lobby of the Sorrento. With it's soft lighting and comfy couches, it’s easy to find yourself still by the fire- hours later-listening to someone playing the baby grand while sipping a glass of wine. My room was extremely spacious with big windows that you can actually open to get some fresh air, the bed was like a thick puffy cloud, and there were many tasty treats in the room. I'm looking forward to my return to the Sorrento Hotel very soon!

name: Alexis Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “GREAT EXPERIENCE!”
text: Met my wife here for a couple days while briefly home from deployment. The staff was incredibly gracious and even upgraded our room. The hotel is in a great location, within walking distance to the Public Market and many bars/eateries. The decor was very classy and the hotel was well maintained. We had drinks in the bar a couple times and ate brunch in the restaurant. Also excellent. Would not hesitate to recommend this property to our friends and will definitely stay again. Keep up the great work!

name: Hotel Deca, Seattle
title: “The good and the not so good”
text: We stayed at the University Tower Hotel for 3 nights. The rooms are a bit small and the bathrooms have no place to put anything, we ended up using the bottom of the side table in the actual room. The rooms are decorated very nicely and the price was great, but the area was not good for walking around (at least for us 'oldies'). One street over are restaurants but more of a younger person's type area, we stuck out like a sore thumb. There is a shopping area about 10 minutes away that had restaurants and was the saving grace for places to eat for us. The deluxe continental breakfast was the best part, tons of pastrys, fruit, breads, cereals, muffins, hard boiled eggs, juices, you name it. You could be there a week and not eat the same thing every day. Our maid service was awful and we even tipped!! Forgot coffee two days in a row, did not vacuum where needed....just not great. So, the good and the not so good......

name: The Sorrento Hotel
title: “Classic old hotel”
text: Loved our stay-- service was excellent, got upgraded to a suite for a very reasonable price, room was huge and bed was unbelievably comfortable. Only issue was with the temperature in the room-- couldn't ever get it quite warm enough. Shower was lukewarm as well. Not enough to stop me from returning, though!

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Pioneer Square Hotel
title: “Perfect Location, Great Hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Best Western Pioneer Square for 2 nights prior to our Alaskan cruise. This was a family reunion of sorts, and the hotel was wonderful in working with us to get 6 rooms with the set up needed for each family and all together on one floor of the hotel. Hotel staff VERY nice to work with.
This is a perfect location for walking around downtown Seattle and the waterfront. Very easy walking to Pike Street Market, the waterfront, etc. Hotel very kindly arranged taxi van service for all of us on the morning we needed to get to the pier with all of our luggage.
Rooms are small compared to some other hotels, but VERY clean and nice. Free continental breakfast was nice. There was juice, coffee, cereals, milk, danish, bagels, toast, boiled eggs, etc.
Great price and great location, we will stay here on our next trip to Seattle.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Seattle
title: “Highly recommended”
text: excellent hotel and services, would highly recommend.

name: Grand Hyatt Seattle
title: “Amazing hotel in excellent location”
text: We arrived early and they let us into our room right away. Awesome. THe hotel is in a perfect location. Many places are within walking distance (Pikes Place, City Center Pioneer Square) and if you rather take public transportation then you are in luck because it is right by the light link, monorail busses etc. The bathroom was massive and they had a nice tub. The hotel restaurant has a delicious homemade granola and yogurt for breakfast that I would recommend.

name: The Sorrento Hotel
title: “It is a gem and we will be back!”
text: This is a true find in any city! The service is exceptional. Talk about a five star performance! It is a true boutique hotel! It is comfortable and historic. What a great place....and it is a return trip for us.

name: Cedarbrook Lodge
title: “great place to stay”
text: We recently stayed at this property, rooms are quiet, pillow selection is great, we had our Standard Poodle with us, plenty of space to go for a walk.

name: The Maxwell Hotel Seattle
title: “Max out your visit to Seattle stay at the Maxwell!”
text:
Great hotel near the Space Needle and Monorail to downtown. Also easy access to Pike market with free hotel shuttle.
Large and comfy rooms with fridge and microwave and Coffee machine well supplied even popcorn all complimentary as is coffee and cakes in lobby during the afternoon. Light rail from airport to Mono rail is best value if you arrive in working hours.

name: Hyatt At Olive 8
title: “Elegant & Environmentally Conscious”
text: The excellent service started with a phone call to the hotel during which I was given several options for traveling from the airport to Hyatt at Olive 8. Each day, the friendly service of the concierge and other staff made our stay at this LEED-certified hotel well worth our investment, and the proximity to great restaurants and attractions was another selling point. We were able to walk to almost all the attractions and venues we wanted to see.

name: The Maxwell Hotel Seattle
title: “Comfortable and pleasant stay!”
text: Wonderful stay! Loved the rooms and the staff was so helpful and professional. The rooms are modern and spacious. Not your average hotel room, in a good way!

name: Hotel Andra
title: “Excellent hotel very nice staff”
text: The hotel Andra is a cosy modern boutique hotel in a perfect location for exploring downtown Seattle.All of the staff are wonderful lola is a must for breakfast ans serious pie across the street is a must for dinner. I will be staying at this hotel on my next trip to Seattle

name: Hyatt At Olive 8
title: “Great Staff. Great Rooms. Great Location.”
text:
I had the chance to compare this Hyatt to the Grand Hyatt, because we checked in here the day we checked out of the Grand. Just like the Grand, I have nothing but good things to say about this place.
As the name says, it is on Olive and 8 so it is about 1/2 a block away from the Grand. It is very much centrally located, which made it easy to walk everywhere- Belltown, Pioneeer Square, Pike Place, etc.
I do have to say that while I prefer the rooms at the Grand Hyatt, the rooms here are also amazing. The room we got may have been smaller than the one we got at the Grand, but everything is still top-notch. Everything - furniture, fixtures, fittings, electronics, etc - is very clean and modern; the bathroom is nice and spacious (although smaller than the one at the Grand and only had a shower/tub combo); and the bed is heavenly comfortable. 
I will say, though, that the staff here seemed a lot friendlier and accommodating than those at the Grand (I never thought the service could be surpassed there, but I guess I was wrong). Despite the fact that we made our booking through Priceline, our riff-raff status did not seem to matter to the staff because we were treated so very well and were made to feel truly welcome and appreciated as guests. The service provided by everyone - from front desk to housekeeping to the bar staff - was just impeccable. 
Just to niggle at a couple of things because that is what I do: in-room wifi is not free, which bugs me in this day and age, and parking is expensive ($38, valet only, but on par with what is offered in the area, and one can always self-park at the 7th and Pike Garage for $30/24 hours). 
Still, Hyatt at Olive 8 gets a 4.5* rating from me, which I will round up to a 5 because of the AMAZING staff.

name: Cedarbrook Lodge
title: “Still one of the best in Seattle”
text:
Had dinner at Copperleaf this recent stay, lives up to the hype - great food and service - nice wine list. Very few tables available each night - so reservations are recommended. 
Highly reco Cedarbrook Lodge.

name: Grand Hyatt Seattle
title: “A wonderful retreat”
text: I recently stayed here for a conference I attended. The hotel hotel had a low key and simple feel to it. I loved my room. The bed was comfortable and I thought the electronic shades were great. The bathroom was the best part. It was huge..almost half the size of the suite. It had an inviting soaking tub with some cool fixtures and a huge mirror over the tub. The shower separate and rather large. I loved the rooms and would highly recommend this hotel.

name: Silver Cloud Inn - Lake Union
title: “Excellent”
text:
I stayed here in the beginning of November. I had read reviews and
chose to stay and see for myself. It was everything I had read. The
free shuttle, the free continental breakfast was amazing. The rooms were clean, big and comfortable. Our room had a view of the lake and the Space Needle. I would recommend this hotel to all travelers in the 
Seattle area. The staff was friendly and very accomodating.

name: Hyatt At Olive 8
title: “Trendy Hotel in a Perfect Location!”
text:
My husband and I spent our 15th anniversary in Seattle and this hotel was great. The decor is super trendy, which was fun, but not really a big deal for us. We loved the super quick check-in at the kiosk, because you never really know if you're going to have a friendly employee or not. The room was large and very nice. We had a view of the Paramount which was fun watching people flock to see Mary Poppins. 
We had drinks in the bar, and the waitresses were very friendly. We walked all over downtown, shopping, eating and sightseeing, and to be able to come right back to the hotel was wonderful. The valet guys had our car ready in minutes. And although parking is crazy expensive, it is, afterall, Seattle.

name: Hotel Deca, Seattle
title: “Deca is a delight!”
text:
Props to Priceline for turning me onto this great boutique hotel. I got a great rate on a wonderful hotel in a nice location. 
I reserved a room with a king, but when I checked in they didn't have one available. As a result, I was upgraded to a suite with two queen beds. It was a great room and I have zero complaints. Staff is very friendly and quick to respond to any requests; I forgot a toothbrush (doh!) and one was brought to me within minutes. 
Parking, internet access and breakfast are complimentary. The wifi connection is available throughout the hotel, which makes sitting in front of the fireplace in their gorgeous lobby to catch up on work a nice option.

name: The Sorrento Hotel
title: “Luxury, Service and Location all in one”
text: Stayed at the Sorrento for the first time after moving away from Seattle 10 years and after never stepping foot in the door while residing in the city but had always heard glowing reviews of it. Was immediately taken aback by the generosity of the staff who were very friendly and immediately offered a room upgrade. Upon entering the room i found out why this hotel was given such high marks, separate sitting area with couch and desk, the most comfortable down-filled bed, large marble bathroom with excellent toiletries. We were most pleased. It is a little stretch for walking down to Pike's Market unless you happen to be in tiptop shape as Seattle is very hilly. The breakfast was excellent also and plus they have a nice happy hour in the lobby with the fireplaces glowing which can be handy during the wet weather that may great you while in Seattle.

name: University Inn Seattle
title: “Very Happy with stay”
text:
We didn't have reservations and were given a room with 2 queen beds, we called and requested a room with a king bed and couch. The staff was very friendly and polite about our request. We were given another room which was perfect for us. The rooms were spotless and comfortable. There are a LOT of pillows on the very comfortable bed, white ones being feather and beige ones being foam, really nice to have so many. 
If you put your order in before midnight, you get breakfast brought to your room between 8 and 10 AM. We forgot to put our room # on the menu choices and when I called to see when breakfast was coming, a polite clerk named Terrell immediately got our breakfast delivered just as ordered- yummy blueberry waffles, scrambled eggs, sausage, yogurt, coffee, all for free with the room. 
We would definately stay there again.
By the way, the hotel on the block before this wanted $60 more for their rooms and we had a great view of Mount Ranier, which the other place didn't.

name: Hotel 1000
title: “Great Location in Downtown Seattle”
text:
This is a boutique hotel, very trendy with excellent rooms. Very quite.
Pros: 
Excellent location in Downtown Seattle (near Public Market and Pike St.)
Big room with a gorgeous bathroom.
Cons: Although the staff was correct, they only seem to be helpful when you ask about info repeatedly.
Tip: The hotel restaurant is very, very good. Amazing juices!

name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “The HVP is a Diamond among hotels in Seattle”
text: On your way to the HVP you will pass breathtaking views of Mt Ranier and the Pugent Sound. Another thing you will notice is all the mega-chain hotels that are big and tall enough to offer a great view. You wont find the HVP soaring in the sky like the Crowne Plaza or the Sheraton but that is what makes this boutique hotel one of Seattle's BEST kept secrets!! Upon arrival I was greated by two or three excited and ready to help Bellmen. The hotel itself is a "vintage" 11 story brick structure smack in the heart of the city surrounded by beautiful parks and cute shops and restaurants. The location is the absolute best, about 4 or 5 blocks to anything you would ever want: The waterfront, The market, Pacific Place, The monirail, Public library, and more. I had booked a double-double room but that turned out to be too close to the elevator for comfort. I spoke with the front desk and I was upgraded with a smile to a double-delux. The beds were so comfortable it seemed and if I had never left home. Internet is complimentary and the beautiful high-tech public library is accross the street if you need anything further. I arranged a trip to Boeing Feild through the Hotel and everything was smooth and ontime. No problems with anything, I had a great experience!

name: Hotel 1000
title: “Great Boutique Hotel”
text: We really enjoyed our stay here. The location is great for walking and exploring downtown Seattle, and the rooms were very comfortable and luxurious. Highly recommended!

name: Grand Hyatt Seattle
title: “It was off the hook!”
text:
I thought this hotel was a dream.The hotel was clean and it made you feel at home.I also brought my boyfriend along and he loved the hotel.The people who work there were very nice and accomodating to us!
I stayed a week and it was the most exhilerating experience at a hotel.

name: Hyatt At Olive 8
title: “Beautiful, modern hotel with great location!”
text:
We stayed here on a leisure visit to Seattle. The Paramount theater is just a block away. The hotel was very modern, well appointed and spotless. The room was typical size, but the ameneties were great. The bathroom was very well appointed. The bed was very comfortable. Highly recommend this facility!
Only issue: Internet charge. They should include regular access with room rate...add charge for high speed.

name: Hotel Andra
title: “Poor Management and Customer Service”
text:
Key points are below:
• When I booked the hotel (months ago and upon recommendation from a loyal hotel customer), I requested a early check-in on 9/3 because I knew we would need to get in early (climbed Rainier and was heading to Seattle early on Saturday)
• When I called on Saturday morning to confirm the early check-in, there was no record of my request but I was told we could likely get in between 1-2
• We arrived at 1:30 and the room was not available – we went to get lunch and was told that we would receive a call as soon as the room was ready
• We never received a call and when we arrived at 7 pm that night, the luggage had not been taken to the room
• After waiting for the luggage to make its way to the room, my friend went to start getting ready and found someone else’s luggage in our room (our luggage had been taken to the wrong room and we had someone else’s stuff in ours)
• We had to wait another 15 minutes to get our luggage and we were late to plans because of it
• When I talked to Carmen, the Manager on duty, and expressed my concerns – she was nice and understanding and committed to giving us a free night’s stay AND breakfast for the four adults staying in the room every morning of our stay
• Sunday morning, when we sat down at the restaurant next door to enjoy our breakfast, we were told she had not honored her agreement
• I talked to Isaac and he said he would only give TWO of the four breakfast for one morning (totally different from what Carmen committed to)
• Isaac was unprofessional and did not appear to care that we had already wasted time and energy on a stay that was terrible
I could go on and on about Carmen and Isaac and their treatment of customers, but overall, wanted to share this feedback and make you aware of how unpleasant an experience it was when we were all trying to enjoy our Rainier celebration in Seattle. It is very unfortunate.

name: The Maxwell Hotel Seattle
title: “very pleasant stay”
text: room was big, very clean and spacious. so was the bathroom. stuff was very helpful and hospitable. complimentary little cupcakes in the afternoon, at the lobby, gave a nice touch. very close to the space needle and the park, lots of small good restaurant ( a great little Thai place down the street, 5 min. walk is especially good) and a superb supermarket near by make it a perfect location.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Seattle
title: “Typical Four Seasons”
text: Just returned today from a 4 night stay in Seattle at the Four Seasons. The service is typical Four Seasons, always there when you need them, with few flaws. The only complaint is the shower water pressure. I felt it was low, but my partner thought it was perfect. The bathroom is huge, with one of the deepest tubs I've ever seen in a hotel. The bathroom mirror has a television built into it. Great idea! Lights are on dimmers in every room. The view of Puget Sound was perfect. The front desk staff addressed me by name every time I passed the desk, and always with a smile. The business center was spotlessly clean, and offered new computers and printers. We did not eat at ART, but would like to next time. The hotel location could not have been better.

name: Alexis Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great location!”
text: Hotel is perfectly located on 1st Ave, convenient to Pike Market, Pioneer square and a light rail station. The room I stayed in was small, but was fine for me traveling solo. No view, other than the building next to me and the street. The hotel was quiet and the staff was pleasant enough, I had to ask for a map that the couple in front of me were offered. Nice touches like free happy hour with wine every afternoon. Overall a very pleasant stay, in a unique hotel. Note: the doors to the rooms are very heavy!

name: Silver Cloud Inn - Lake Union
title: “Great Location and Service”
text: The hotel staff graciously and immediately accommodated our requests for a crib and for an extended stay due to a late flight. The hotel room was larger than expected and included the two queen beds, a sofa bed, large desk with comfortable desk chair, microwave and refrigerator. The room was spotless and well maintained throughout our stay. The free shuttle, WiFi internet access, business center and parking were used daily and greatly appreciated, as was the morning breakfast service in the large, beautiful rooms overlooking the waterfront. Overall, a great visit and one we would look forward to repeating.

name: Hyatt At Olive 8
title: “Loved it!”
text: Hotel was clean, beautifully decorated, friendly staff and all! Visited Seattle for a Conference and this hotel is a short two block walk to the convention center. We used the Downtown Shuttle Service to and from the airport and was very pleased with them as well. I enjoyed my stay at the Olive 8!! Hotel was EXCELLENT!

name: The Paramount Hotel
title: “Great hotel, great location, great price”
text:
This hotel is in a great location right in the heart of downtown. It is within walking distance of Pike's Place market, the waterfront, the monorail to the space needle, the convention center and shopping. If you need a cab there are plenty to catch. 
The hotel itself is newly remodeled with a contemporary decor. It is done very nicely, comfortable and not imposing like some of big name hotels. The rooms are of average size and the beds are very comfortable. Room includes free wireless internet service, mini bar, coffee service although a great Starbucks right around the corner. The staff was very friendly and helpful. There is a nice restaurant/bar on the first floor which has happy hour every night from 9-12pm. It attracts quite a crowd and is a fun place to gather with friends. 
In summary I would recommend this hotel fo either tourists or business travelers. It offers great value for the money.

name: Hyatt Place Seattle/Downtown
title: “Great Hotel”
text: Good location, just 10 minutes walk to the Seattle needle, Pacific Science Centre and the Experience Music Project. Free continental breakfast, free internet and free shuttle to take you anywhere within 1 mile of the hotel. Very friendly and helpful staff. Would certainly stay here again.

name: Mayflower Park
title: “Location, service large rooms”
text: My wife and i stayed here October 14th and 15th. The room was very well apointed and large, more like a suite. Bed room and sitting room could be divided. Price was very fair. Service was excellent and the location can't be beat.

name: The Maxwell Hotel Seattle
title: “Nice rooms, service could be better”
text:
The Maxwell has nice, clean, good sized rooms. No complaints there.
I found the service left a bit to be desired however. On check in at 1pm, we were flatly told that check in was 3pm. I appreciate that 3pm is the check in time. However most places are generally a bit flexible about check in time. Maybe they were 100% booked the previous night, but it would have been nice to have that communicated. We don't usually show up early for check in, but find that good hotels are generally accommodating on the odd occasion this happens.
There was also another strange guy working the desk at various times who was a bit creepy.
All that said, as other reviews note here, the rooms at the Maxwell are high standard and good value.

name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Staff at Hotel Vintage Park”
text: We only stayed one night at Hotel Vintage Park, but in that short time I was extremely impressed with the helpfulness of the staff. The coffee service in the morning and wine service in the evening in the cozy lobby were nice touches. The room was unique and comfortable, however the bathroom was very small. All in all, this was a nice hotel.

name: The Fairmont Olympic Seattle
title: “A Holiday Treat”
text:
Christmas is coming, time to head to the Fairmont Olympic. My husband and I have an awesome tradition of staying at the Olympic (which is what it was called long ago, we still call it that) during Christmas time. The fragrance of the looming Christmas tree in the lobby brings Christmas on in our first breath. Then we venture around the lobby to check out the gingerbread house which sits near the entrance to the grand Garden Court dining room. Eventually, we head upstairs to check out the Teddy Bear Suite and watch the children (young and old) marvel at the wonder of this marvelous suite which is now overrun with teddy's, big and small, and beautiful decorations.
A coffee or a cocktail (depending on the time of day) while sitting in the lobby is a must-do. Just sit and watch people and enjoy this lovely and iconic Seattle landmark. And the rooms! Well, they never disappoint. We can't wait to get there and always dread leaving. Unless, of course, it's to go shopping in Seattle and then return with our shopping bags AND then back to those lobby chairs for that beverage of choice.
See you in a few weeks, Olympic!

name: Hotel 1000
title: “Treated like Royalty that is also your best friend”
text: It's hard to know how it can be done better than what we experienced at this hotel, which will be our one and only for every Seattle stay from now on. We were treated with the kindness and warmth like a best friend, but with the detailed spoiled treatment that I assume Royalty enjoys. We've traveled a lot, including all the "top" hotels in Seattle, and have extensively traveled back East, Europe, Asia and the best of S. America and I can't say I've had a better experience than the treatment, professionalism and warmth of the staff here. The hotel was chic and spotless but the care left all the attitude that comes with this kind of environs at the curb. The king suite was luxurious, though on the small side by square footage but the use of space, the view, and all the conveniences afforded by location, an always ready to please staff, a complimentary hotel car (though it was busy one time we wanted to be driven and so took a cab), made up for the square footage shortage.

name: Cedarbrook Lodge
title: “Absolutely superb. Well worthy of its high ranking”
text:
This is a great hotel. OK it is a little pricey compared to others locally. But having said that we chose the Doubletree a couple of weeks later and whilst we saved a small amount the service was awful.
Fabulous personal service beginning with the airport pick-up. Lovely room and the common areas are fantastic. Really peaceful location despite its close proximity to the airport. Good breakfast choices and the bar area is very welcoming with great wine and food selections.
Another plus is the drop off and pick up at the Light Rail station.
Overall I would rank it as excellent.

name: Cedarbrook Lodge
title: “Great Hotel”
text: Found this really nice lodge/hotel near Sea-Tac Airport. We shared room with the other couple (2 beds). Bathroom was really clean, room was very reasonable size. I definitely loved the bed and pillow. It was so comfortable we took naps everyday. The hotel provides daily continental breakfast which was delicious. Fresh bagels and bread everyday with fresh fruits. Oatmeals, cereal, and also fresh smoked salmon. I made myself smoked salmon bagel every morning along with my world famous starbucks coffee. Yum! The hotel lobby/rest area also provides bottled water, chips, yogurt, string cheese, and wait for it... Haagan daz ice cream!!!!! What's there not to like about this hotel? Free hotel parking, free snacks, and free breakfast. The hotel is like 5 mins away from the airport, about 15-20 mins from downtown Seattle. I would definitely come back and stay here again.

name: Grand Hyatt Seattle
title: “Beautiful rooms”
text: We stayed at the Hyatt for 4 days during a conference. The room was one of the best we have had. It was spacious, well appointed and had a glorious view over Seattle (24th floor). But what we really loved was the bathroom that was also large and comfortable with both a shower and bath. Would definitely revist this hotel.

name: The Fairmont Olympic Seattle
title: “Very nice hotel!”
text: Me and my friends stayed here while attending a convention because it was very close by and we got a deal through the convention. We had a great stay and the staff were very friendly, there were always staff around to help. The room was also very clean and nice. The only thing we didn't like was the beds were kind of small, which was fine for me and my bf but not so much for our other two friends. Also stuff was kind of expensive but that is to be expected when staying at a nicer hotel. I was really glad to have stayed here though and be in such a cool building, i would stay here again!

name: Hotel Andra
title: “Perfectly beautiful, comfortable, pleasant -- hard to go home”
text: My husband and I stayed at Hotel Andra for a week in early July -- a return trip for him, first for me -- and we could not have been happier. The staff were cheerful, helpful, and really seemed to care about our experience. Room was small but very comfortable -- beautiful bathroom -- we slept very well in the deliciously appointed bed. The lobby and public areas are beautifully decorated and felt like our living room, a lovely extension of our room. Good location, funky interesting neighborhood, close (but not too) to Pike St. We ordered dinner from room service the night we arrived and were not terribly impressed, but breakfast the next morning in the restaurant was spectacular. We subsequently discovered the bakery across the street offers many of the same things (ah, the homemade English muffins!) for mornings when we wanted to grab and go. (We were also regulars at the bakery for the delicious desserts.) It was a blissful week. My husband had stayed here previously during a business trip and insisted I come back with him for a romantic vacation. Seattle is great, well worth visiting, but the Hotel Andra is a destination in itself.

name: Mayflower Park
title: “A fabulous find!”
text: The best hotel in Seattle, in my opinion. Beautiful and clean, great service and ammenities and best of all... within walking distance to EVERYTHING (shopping, monorail, restaurants, Pike Place Market, Pioneer Square... you name it!) I will definitely stay here again and I have been telling all my friends about it! As a local doing a downtown romantic weekend getaway... this hotel was PERFECT!

name: River Inn of Harbor Town
title: “A highlight of our Memphis visit”
text:
We treated ourselves to two nice hotels on our recent 2 week trip along the Mississippi River, the River Inn being one of them. We were not disappointed! The rooms are beautiful, the service outstanding and the breakfast that is included is wonderful! We asked for a river view room which we were provided. Since this was our first time in the area it was great to see the barges moving along the river.
The hotel is in a quiet area not too far from downtown and Beale street, but far enough. It is a very walkable area and trolleys to town run nearby. Taxis seemed plentiful.
Highly recommend!

name: Hotel Andra
title: “Loved it but not sure if we would spend the money again.”
text: We loved the location of the Andra-it was central to everything in Seattle and in what appeared to be the safest part of town. The rooms were well appointed with a modern but homey décor, and the bed was incredibly comfortable. Our room had a beautiful view of Space Needle. In spite of the fact that I loved returning to the soothing atmosphere of the lobby and room every day, I’m not sure if I would spend the money to stay there again. There were too many down sides for us. The A/C was VERY loud, waking me up with almost every click on/off. The room was TINY- maybe 9x9, and full of furniture (a bar, a desk and two end tables), with no place to unpack clothes other than a closet. It was tough to negotiate having two suitcases in such a small space. The BIG turn off came when I attempted to arrange a taxi to take me to airport. I was told (by two different front desk workers, at two different times) that they could arrange a Town Car for me for only $40. I refused explaining that a taxi is cheaper and they actually disagreed, although the $32 fare is clearly visible on all taxi doors. I have the money to spend but don’t appreciate being ripped off. Since it was our first trip to Seattle, I am happy we stayed there but now that we know the lay of the land, we will probably stay elsewhere when we return.

name: Pan Pacific Seattle
title: “surprisingly great”
text: had a friend suggest this newer hotel, and was so glad I took the advice. loved the asian design that went into the room, and the view to the north was really cool. some convenient spots close-by makes this a great idea for short business trips and quick travel hops.

name: The Maxwell Hotel Seattle
title: “A true delight”
text: Maxwell staff are very friendly, helpful and efficient. Regrettably no breakfast capability at the hotel but there are endless options outside the hotel within a few minutes walk. Rooms are spacious and clean and the afternoon bottomless coffee pot and cup cakes is a welcome pleasure when returning from a long day enjoying Seattle. Downtown Seattle and the Pike Market are easily walkable (about 20 minutes) and the hotel fits neatly into the $32 fixed price taxi ride to and from the airport.

name: Mayflower Park
title: “Great place--good value”
text: Front desk was very friendly even though I arrived after midnight. Accommodations were comfortable and clean. I would stay here again the next time I go to Seattle.

name: Cedarbrook Lodge
title: “An airport oasis”
text: Fabulous northwest lodge feel in a secluded airport neighborhood. Had dinner in the lounge. Bryce provided exceptional service and great humor. This is a special spot, I really mean it.

name: Grand Hyatt Seattle
title: “First Class Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Grand Hyatt on business for 5 nights in October 2006. My family came with me for two of the days and at check-in they easily upgraded me to a corner suite for a few dollars more.
Check-in was one of the smoothest and friendliest I have ever experienced. The clerk called me in my room a few minutes later to see if everything was okay.
The rooms are great, the corner suites are very nice with an entrance and sitting room well separated from the bedroom by a long hallway.
Why didn't I give the Grand Hyatt 5 stars?
1) The only food in the hotel is a Ruth's Chris and while they serve breakfast, it is at Ruth's Chris prices. 
2) In-room housekeeping during my stay was minimal at best. Some days they didn't even replace the dirty wine glasses or drinking glasses. They would also missed dirty towels on the floor.
I expected a bit more in these areas from a hotel of this class.

name: Cedarbrook Lodge
title: “What an amazing place to stay!”
text: We stayed here for two nights and enjoyed every minute of it. Our room was very comfortable and super clean with no problems. Excellent "healthy"complimentary breakfast was a great treat. The staff were nice and professional people. In my opinion this hotel should be rated higher. You don't need to think twice before booking this wonderful hotel.

name: River Inn of Harbor Town
title: “The best hotel we stayed at in the USA”
text:
From the moment I booked the River Inn, I knew we would have good service. We were in Memphis for my husband's 50th Birthday so I wanted it to be special. Nataly in the front office answered all my queries, even helping with a birthday cake. The Inn is situated a few kilometres outside Memphis town, right on the banks of the Mississippi. There is plenty of parking in a nice quiet part of the Memphis, away from the razzle dazzle of Beale Street. Our room was equisite, with it's four poster bed, big fluffy duvet, divine pillows, chocolates and port with the bed turndown, and view of the river from our room. We had a guest office on our floor which was always empty so excellent to catch up with the family via the Internet. 
Happy hour on the terrace was nice, with local and imported wines, softdrink and nibblies available. The view from the terrace of the magical Missisippi 'rolling along' was one I'll never forget. 
But it was the breakfast that blew us away. Freshly squeezed juice, pancakes to die for, perfectly cooked bacon and eggs and the best coffee in the USA - all with 6 star service. I've lost the name of the gentleman who waited our table but his wonderful Southern manners and service should be used as an example of customer service perfection in textbooks.
I wasn't a huge fan of Memphis, with the exception of Gracelands, but I would go back to the River Inn in a heart beat. We saw it in a book of the best boutique hotels in the world, and it deserves to be there. Take a bow, River Inn.

name: Holiday Inn Express Boston
title: “Great Park n Fly Location”
text: This is in a great location and it's a great hotel too..the staff tries VERY hard to get things right! Very easy to find, I90 to I93 southbound, exit 18 continue on service road to hotel on the right, after the shopping plaza (great Olive Garden within walking distance from the hotel)... Complimentary shuttle from and to airport... Great breakfast, very comfortable bed, nice room with flat screen TV, great wifi Internet, nice fitness center... Very courteous customer service, free parking with parking pass and free shuttle back to the hotel. A great place to stay IF you are in the right room. Be sure to ask for a room in a quiet location. Do NOT let them put you in any room over-looking the parking lot...especially on a week-end night as there is a possibility that party goers will congregate outside the side entrance and make LOTS of noise before getting in their cars and departing the premises. The hotel will make amends and does TRY to get them off the premises. Unfortunately, some people never grow up and never respect other peoples rights to privacy. Very easy to get to Trinity Church, Boston Library and Prudential Center on a Sunday with your own car and a GPS unit. Would I stay here again? Of course!

name: Holiday Inn Express Boston
title: “Difficult to get to”
text:
It is right on the freeway frontage road but very confusing to get to. I wasn't the only one. Others commented as the were checking in. Check in was easy and friendly. Heftiest goodie bag for Priority members I've seen. There is a comp shuttle that will take you to the subway station but it is only a 5-8 minute walk.
Room was clean and well maintained but there was some freeway noise at night.
Large uncovered parking lot to leave your car and take the subway in to the city.

name: Grand Hyatt Seattle
title: “Great hotel, great service!”
text: The Grand Hyatt Seattle is one of the best hotels I have ever stayed at, from the doorbells to the electric drapes, to the great service, all 5 stars. I really like the wood and natural tones, defiantly worth the money. The 721 Pine Restaurant is good, a little pricey, but still good. The views of the city and Puget Sound are amazing. The Grand Hyatt Seattle is a hotel I would recommend to anyone!

name: The Edgewater Hotel Seattle
title: “A nice surprise”
text:
The website for this place doesn't do it's justice. I was a little bit afraid that this hotel would be for old folks but I was wrong. It's actually very refreshingly hip, yet cozy and has the personality that larger chain hotels lack incredibly. The staff here was also very personable and "human". The lounge called "67" is very cool for drinks or food anytime. There are seats right next to the water and it was very chic. I could imagine some great nightlife here during the right time. 
We stayed on the first floor with a balcony and a fire place. It was great, except that you can hear the water lapping up against the walls at night. Maybe it would have been better if I stayed on the upper floors. Also, we had some trouble with the fire place but I'm sure if we stayed there longer, we would have got the hang of it. Also, we could hear people walking in the room above us at night, so that was a disruption.
Overall though, I would stay there again and am really glad we went there.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown
title: “Pleasant stay”
text: We visited Boston for a wedding and stayed at this hotel for a few days. We needed some business services urgently when we first arrived and the personnel at the desk went out of their way to help us. The building itself is older, but clean. Rooms were comfortable. We enjoyed being able to walk everywhere in the downtown area. I would not hesitate to stay here again. There is a fitness center with a pool attached to the hotel, we did not have time to use either.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown
title: “super comfy beds”
text:
we arrived at Boston at mid afternoon, and the room was waiting for us. It was a medium to big room size, with a comfy and big bathroom. Air conditiong worked fantastic and the location was great. Near a T station ( china town ) but also near good great localitons, as the park, china town, and the beginning of Boston trail ( that we did ) . 
But what I remember the room for was the comfy bed. Pretty big bed, but not enormous, and the softest comfortable mattress I ever slept in. really great beds. We didn't need any assistance from staff but they were nice and the chocolate complimentary cookie that they gave you was good.
Breakfast was not included but you have plenty of places in a few minutes walking distances, plenty of starbacks and dunkin donuts, and if you're looking for great coffee try Boston Coffee company, delicious, strong, and good.

name: Holiday Inn Express Boston
title: “Most reasonably priced hotel in Boston”
text: My husband and I have stayed in this hotel a few times. Though not the fanciest hotel, we love the fact that we can walk the 5 or so miles to Fenway. It is clean and the staff is very accomodating. My only complaint is that the fan in the bathroom was noisy and went on automatically when you turned the light on and we tried to keep the light off as much as possible. We've stayed in pricier hotels which charged for internet and breakfast and these are both included. Will stay there again.

name: Hotel 1000
title: “Wonderful location and amazing view.”
text: From the moment I checked in I liked this place. They informed me about a promotion with Alaska Airlines where I would get miles for my stay. The front desk made sure I knew where everything was located in the hotel and the room. Well, all I can say is I was floored. The best room in Seattle. Corner view HUGE bathtub with a water view. Great hotel and part of the AMEX Platinum hotels so you can get the room upgrade and free breakfast for two.

name: Beacon Hill Hotel and Bistro
title: “comfy, friendly hotel in a great neighborhood”
text: I stayed for one night prior to a conference. The staff is personable and professional. The food was very good. My room was small, but I expected that and it was fine. The neighborhood is historical and quaint. The hotel is close to the Boston Common. There is a Starbucks and a CVS nearby, but the stores are predominantly boutiques and non-chain cafes, etc. I gave 4 "dots" for sleep quality because the garbage trucks show up on Charles Street in the dead of night, but I am a light sleeper anyway. I would go back in a heartbeat.

name: Grand Hyatt Seattle
title: “Great Location”
text: Great Room at good price, a little understaffed at the front desk.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Boston Crosstown Center
title: “Loved this hotel!”
text: Very clean hotel with very friendly staff!! I admit there are a lot of sirens, but we kept the fan going continuous on the air unit in the room and this helped, plus they have ear plugs available in the room if needed. There is a shuttle available to the airport and hospital, however, if they aren't busy they will take you to other areas. We were able to get a ride to the TD Garden and even picked up after the game!! We loved the driver Justin, he was so helpful!!! We took the silver line transit to the Boston common area for a whopping $6.00, and boy was it a cultural experience for our teenagers! A cab from the Quincy Market area, or even Newberry street ran between 11-15 dollars back to the hotel. We had pizza delivered to the room from Rome(?) pizza and it was excellent, and very reasonable!! We would definitely stay here again!! The breakfast provided was excellent, with a nice open large area for seating! The kids were disappointed to discover that the are not cookies available at all times. We were informed that they put those out at a couple different times. There was also complimentary evening food available but we were never there at those times to take advantage of that service.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown
title: “Consistently good hotel”
text:
Stay here a lot on business. Nice rooms, good 
Location. Only one small issue. I get room service a lot and realize it is usually a rip off but it works for me when I don't want to go out. I ordered a burger, nothing special. Came with soggy fries. Here is the issue, with service fee and tip, 26 bucks. Burger was marginal at best. Their room service menu was one of the highest I have seen. Other than that, good choice. Right next tothe tufts "t" stop.

name: Beacon Hill Hotel and Bistro
title: “Lovely hotel, but don't order the duck!”
text: A wonderful boutique hotel in a super area in Boston. Rooms are a bit small, and slightly noisy at times (from the street), but it is a fantastic place to stay for location and service. It has an excellent restaurant attached, which provides an extensive breakfast menu (included in room charge). Evening menu is great, seems to be well subscribed to by local residents. But don't order the duck - it's a bit anaemic, leading to a rather bland dining experience - though other meals, chicken/steak/fish are much better( based on one meal experience only!) Would definitely stay here again. (Also has free internet access........!)

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton - Boston
title: “Pleasant place to stay in . . .”
text:
1. Location: Not great - unless you drive - as it is not near a subway station (20 mins' walk), Harvard Square (20 - 30 mins' walk), supermarket / convenience store (10 mins' walk). However, this place is nice as it is away from hustle and bustle. Also, being sited along the river means that it affords a gorgeous view. On the plus side, it is about 15 mins' away from airport.
2. Staff: Helpful, and generally, polite and welcoming.
3. Rooms: Good sized. Comfortable beds and rooms. 2 TVs: in living area and bedroom, with many cable channels. Aircon / heater available. Comfortable bathrooms.
4. Amenities: Good enough fitness room. Heated pool, although a bit small.
5. Other: Shuttle service, regular, and to 4 different parts of Boston downtown or Harvard Square. Great to overcome limitations of location.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Boston Crosstown Center
title: “Great rooms and location for Boston Medical Center/other Boston hospitals”
text: This hotel gives deep discounts for families needing to stay visiting someone in the nearby hospitals. Apparently they reserve rooms for such purpose so that even if the Hampton Inn website says they are full, it is worth calling directly for availability. Breakfast is included. Self-parking is only $10 a day and you can come and go as often as you please. The room was spacious, immaculately clean with a very nice bathroom.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown
title: “Not Good”
text: This is a good spot only if you need the medical center next door. While it is next to the T it is the orange line which is pretty limited. Rooms are old, you have to go to the second floor to check in and get elevators to the rooms. We called the front desk several times with no answer after many, many rings. It needs to be renovated badly/, shortly after check-in a man came to work on the restroom. The drain in the tub/shower would not staye up and had to be propped up for the water to drain. Good for a budget but go somewhere else if you can.

name: Grand Hyatt Seattle
title: “Toplage”
text: Wir hatten eine Suite im 19. Stock mit prachtvoller Aussicht bis hin zum Meer. Das Hotel war perfekt sauber und das Badezimmer sehr gross für ein Stadhotel mit Dusche und Wanne. Das Personal war überdurchschnittlich freundlich und hilfsbereit. wir fanden es einzig etwas seltsam, dass auch Aussenstehende ungehindert Zugang auf die Etagen hatten.

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Great hotel in a great city”
text:
I was in town for a conference (at another hotel) but selected Sheraton because I had accumulated enough SPG points for a free night. Sheraton was promoting their Club Lounge so I gave it a try. I was NOT disappointed. We were given a room on the 29th floor overlooking the Charles River. The Club Lounge was open all day with snacks and drinks and even included breakfast and (heavy) hors d'oeuvres each day.
The hotel is in a great location: walking distance of Fenway and several “T” stops (a must when in Boston).

name: Pan Pacific Seattle
title: “A Great Respite”
text: The Pan Pacific Seattle took very good care of us. The place is very comfortable, in a good location on the edge of downtown near Seattle Center. Having Starbucks and Whole Foods within the building (outside entrances, however) was a big plus, too.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Boston Crosstown Center
title: “Top Notch”
text:
I stayed at this hotel while my husband was at Brigham & Women's Hospital for a procedure. I was very happy with everything. The breakfast was terrific (the cooking staff works really hard), the rooms and beds were lovely and well cleaned each day. I never had a problem with the shuttle and took it back and forth 15 days in a row.
Lots of people stay here whose loved ones are in the hospital, so the staff is especially nice. They are well trained to deal with these type of guests and were so helpful.
I consider myself a person who has high standards and would highly recommend this hotel.

name: Hotel 140
title: “Quality Hotel, Excellent Price Point”
text: When I visit Boston, I always stay here. Best Value in Back Bay, and the quality is unmatched. The staff is always friendly, courteous and helpful. I have stayed here about 10 times, and I have never had a bad experience. It's right next to Back Bay station, which is super convenient.

name: Pan Pacific Seattle
title: “Not quite in the premier league”
text: As urban hotels go, this is functional enough. Room decor is safe and bland. Beds comfortable. Baths are spacious but the sliding window over the tub opening to the bedroom creates some awkward sight lines as w.c. is not walled off as in many hotels these days. While the manager claimed the hotel had the fastest wi-fi in Seattle, our connection was fitful throughout a three-day weekend and not up to video, which has become my litmus test for in-room broadband these days. TV has some overly complicated remote controls on the interactive menu and it's hard to navigate the movie and other entertainment choices. Retail outlets in same complex as hotel are a plus.

name: The Fairmont Olympic Seattle
title: “top of the line”
text: we stayed and enjoyed, service was above and beyond. if you are a novice traveler, it's nice to have know that that some places are just outstanding, when we travel back to seattle, it's the only place we will stay

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “The do it yourself hotel, don't go”
text:
I was really disappointed with this hotel
Rooms booked and we turned up but on arriving in our car at the front door of the hotel the portering team could not recognise a customer and family wanting some help with their luggage.
The hotel was very busy, is that not their business, and we waited 90 minutes before we took two rooms 11 floors apart
One was the "unlucky for some room". Next to the lift. We did not sleep well.
An early departure was badly handled by the hotel. We had to get our own taxis from around the corner.
To be honest I have never been at a hotel with such a poor front door.

name: Hyatt Regency Boston
title: “Not worth the price”
text:
Elegant design, modern amenities and good location.
Extraordinarily pleasant service.
However, for $300 a night even in Boston one would expect: a real lobby where one can have meetings, breakfast served on time, an exercise room where all the equipment works and climate controls that one can reach without moving a lamp. At the Hyatt, you get none of these.

name: Cedarbrook Lodge
title: “Excellent Hotel & Restaurant”
text:
We've planned to visit the Hotel Restaurant. After knowing it's located inside a hotel, we did the hotel search & were happy to find out it was the #1 Hotel on tripadvisor, which we've always trusted. Since we didn't need to start our days early, we reckoned it's okay that we'd need to commune for 20 mins. every morning to Bellevue, which was our purpose of visit.
Check-in was speedy & professional. The 2 front-receptionist were extremely smart and caring. They even knew we made reservation at the Restaurant, which I booked via Opentable.
Dinner was excellent. We tried their "Earth Day" tasting menu @$49 + $30 for wine-pairing.
The Hotel "Living Room" has an abundant supply of complimentary water, chips, chocolate, cheese string, yugurt, and Haagen-daz ice-cream.
Bathroom amenities were of good quality and environmental-friendly. My only dislike was the bed was too soft, and the air-con slightly blew on my face.
The complimentary breakfast, though lacking variety, was delicious, including bread, bagel, muffin, cereal, salmon, salami, etc.
We absolutely enjoyed our stay, and will definitely consider this Hotel again.

name: Alexis Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text: I've stayed at this hotel three times on business. The location is perfect for a stay in downtown Seattle. It’s about 3 blocks from Pike’s Market, 2 blocks from the museum and a short stroll down to the waterfront. The rooms are classic Kimpton, comfortable bed with eclectic furnishings and all the amenities that you may need. The staff is very friendly, if not a bit slow (I blame that on the computer systems though). The Bookstore is a wonderful and quite place to stop in for food and a drink, the staff there are very friendly as well. The Library is their other restaurant, the service is very slow but the food is fantastic.

name: Hilton Boston Downtown / Financial District
title: “Great Location in Boston”
text: Ideally located close to the waterfront, central historic areas, Quincy Markets, the airport & Amtrak Sth Station. Paid $50 for an upgrade and ended up with a huge corner suite with 2 rooms which was useful for us. Room was very clean and all amenities were of high quality. The bed was super comfortable which meant a first good nights sleep following jetlag and poor sleep the night before in LA. Must have's: Samual Adams Seasonal (beer) at the bar at the eastern end of Quincy markets (near all the food) and lobster bisque at Chart House close by on the waterfront.

name: Hotel 1000
title: “One of my top-rated hotels ever!”
text:
I'm a complete hotel snob after having been subjected to too many highway motels on childhood road trips - call it my form of adolescent rebellion, but since I was old enough to book my own trips, I've never been able to deal with anything less than a 4* hotel. That being said, I do try to find the best deal possible, and have been lucky enough to have stayed in some gorgeous rooms at great prices over the years. Hotel 1000, though, tops the list. 
My husband and I were heading down to Seattle for a concert and wanted someplace chic, comfortable and close to the venue. After reading Hotel 1000's reviews, there was no question as to where we'd be staying. We booked their most basic room for $225/night, which turned out to anything but basic. The bathroom was incredibly large, with a shower, 2-person ceiling-filled tub, and wonderful amenities, including a loofah sponge. The room itself was massive (we were in a corner room, slightly larger than the regular basic rooms, I believe), with an incredibly comfortable bed. Turndown service left little chocolates on the pillow, we very much enjoyed the French press-brewed Starbucks coffee, and the robes were simply sumptuous. Free wifi and VOIP calls are a nice touch and would make this a perfect place for an extended business stay.
Beyond the room, the hotel itself is very nice - intimate and very stylish. There's delicious complementary strawberry lemonade in the lobby, a treat almost as sweet as the staff. I have never yet encountered a staff as gracious and helpful as Hotel 1000's - from the valets who greeted us (and happily retrieved some items we had left in the car when we called down), to the concierge and front desk staff, everyone we encountered was having a great time doing their jobs - their pride in their place of work certainly shows.
A fabulous stay, and I don't think I could stay anywhere else in Seattle after having experienced Hotel 1000!

name: Holiday Inn Express Boston
title: “Cheating with the room type”
text: We stayed 1 night there, I booked and paid in advance for 2 rooms with 2 double beds, and requested connecting rooms since we have teenagers, the ladies at the front desk were very nice AT the beginning, she said the connecting rooms are not avaialable, the best they can do is next or across, with queen or 2 doubles. I picked 2 rooms next to each, and thought they are 2 doubles (my mistake), then I realized I misunderstood. So, I went down and ask to change to the room across (politely), which was empty and have 2 doubles. One of the lady said they already told me there is no 2 doubles available, which I'm sure one choice was 1 queen and 2 doubles. Anyway, her face turned mean & sound nasty, and found a room on the other floor, I told her I need them on the same floor and close to each other, she said nothing is available, so I stay with the queen rooms. I mentioned to her, I booked and paid for the rooms with 2 doubles, which costs more than the single queen room, and she said that is no guarantee. I was so disappointed and would like to share this to everyone. This is the wrost Holiday Inn Express I've ever stayed with.

name: Alexis Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Magnificent, Delightful Hotel”
text: Very fussy ex-meeting planner ... LOVED this hotel. From check-in to check-out, they did everything right. I had read on this forum that it can be noisy, so I requested a quiet room, and got one of the best hotel rooms of my entire life. The bathroom was triple the size of mine at home. The bedding was the highest quality; Aveda amenities; spa on premises; cute little bistro too; free pint of Haagen Daz coupon upon check-in was a nice touch. The hotel really is a work of art -- it's everywhere. To a person, every single staff person I encountered seemed to want only to exceed my expectations. And they love pets and welcome them warmly with a cute sign in the lobby. Terrific, helpful concierge. Perfect location right by the waterfront -- most downtown Seattle hotels were several blocks up. Unfortunately for them, there is big construction going on directly across the street of the front of the hotel, so be sure to request a room facing the opposite direction. This hotel was a dream. I didn't want to leave. Truly one of the very best hotel experiences of my life, and I have stayed at hundreds of hotels thru my work.

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton - Boston
title: “Nice room, nice staff”
text: The room exceeded our expectations. We had a king suite, which was very large with a separate living room. The cookies at check in were such a nice touch! The staff was also good, and having and indoor pool and hottub is a definite plus!!! The only downside is the location... unless you want to be in the Harvard Area. Harvard was a short walk, but downtown and most of the dining/attractions are an expensive cab ride away.

name: Alexis Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great time at the Alexis”
text: We just returned from Seattle. I chose the Alexis based on the location, free wine tasting (my sister loved that part) and Fodor's. Good thing I didn't read the review about the bed bugs because I would have passed on a wonderful hotel. Our suite was huge with a very comfortable bed and large sitting area. The staff is excellent. The watercolor postcards in the lobby from 5-6 p.m. was alot of fun. My 12 year old was happily entertained as the rest of us chatted . One night an artist showed up and did quick sketches of all of us. FREE! We tipped but still it was a very nice touch. This hotel is very much for people that don't like cookie cutter hotels. I'm a four star type and I was pleased.

name: Cedarbrook Lodge
title: “Great lodge/retreat, wonderful restaurant”
text: We took advantage of a Valentine's Day package for a room and prix-fixe dinner. The room was a bit small, but there are wonderful common areas in the buildings with snacks, water, couches, fireplaces, and a TV. What a great place to relax! The restaurant is a must, simply a delight! The ambience is a mid-90's lodge, in wonderful condition, with lots of amenities. Just around the corner from SEA, but very quiet. Not the cheapest, but among the very best!

name: Hotel 140
title: “Very Disappointing”
text: Very disappointing experience with this hotel and their management. We made a reservation to stay at this hotel. They charged my credit card in full upfront, which was surprising to me because it was not made clear that they would do so when I was making the reservation online. Four days before we left for our trip, my husband broke his foot and we were no longer able to travel across the country to Boston. I called the hotel immediately and spoke to a very nice front desk representative who said that because of the circumstances, I would be refunded within 48 hours. However, 48 hours went by and I was not refunded a cent. I left message after message trying to reach the sales coordinator and the manager. Three weeks later, they finally returned one of my calls and told me that there was nothing that they could do. Poor hospitality, horrible business ethics, and all around terrible experience. We will choose to take our business elsewhere next time we go to Boston. Disappointing.

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton - Boston
title: “Good Hotel for the Money”
text:
My husband and I stayed July 4th weekend to attend a Red Sox game. The hotel was very nice and the little bar/restaurant was very nice. We had a quick lunch and a couple of drinks there and enjoyed it. Our room was clean (although there was a stain on the carpet) and very roomy. Perfect to spread out and relax. The bed was so comfortable you melted right into it. It was nice to have a refrigerator and microwave so you could birng your own snacks and drinks to have in the hotel. Our room was on a corner overlooking the Charles River so it was very nice to look out the large windows and watch the world go by.
Keep in mind the hotel is not really near anything, so a car is a must. But with the easy parking in the garage, it really wasn't a problem.
We did have the brunch on Sunday in the larger restaurant. The food was very good, but the set up was a bit strange. The people waiting in line for the special order items were right in front of the items for the ready made buffet. The staff was refilling the buffet items and the customers could not access the other food items because the staff was in the way. Not very conducive to getting everybody in and out of line quickly.
All in all, it was a good place to stay for the price. I would return again.

name: Hotel 1000
title: “Nearly perfect - nearly”
text:
We stayed at the hotel for our anniversay and prior to attending a Seahawks game. What the hotel has control over, it delivers with excellence.
Hotel parking is valet only and the valet is quick and polite. The lobby is not large, but very stylish. Front desk staff was extremely cordial and eager to assist. The room was immaculately clean and well appointed, with a good selection of complimentary starbucks coffee and tazo teas. The mini bar could have used some chocolate for my late night chocolate craving, but $4 for a microbrew is very reasonable. 
The bed was heavenly and a delight to sink into. I thought the pillows at the Bellagio were the best, but these were at least equal. The bath room is delightful and stylish, love the loofah in the bath, the fresh-fagranced toilletries and soft robes. 
Our room was on floor 8, with a peekaboo view of the ferries crossing the Sound as the sun set behind the Olympic Mountains. Very nice. The manager had left us complimentary champagne and strawberries and an anniversary card, which was enjoyed and appreciated.
But the only thing that detracted from our stay was the street noise. I would stay here again, but I offer a word of caution about the potential for noise. When the bars close, it can be loud.

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Great location very convenient”
text: We went with the whole family and the stayed in the North Tower (newly renovated, not sure what the South tower is like though). The room was a good size but the bathroom was a bit small. The staff were extremely friendly and the service was great, the room was very clean. The hotel is conveniently attached to the Prudential Center which has quite a few restaurant options as well as a food court, the stores though are more high end and pricey. The location is central and it is a short walk to downtown. Wireless internet is only free in the lobby and is $12.95 per device per day in the room (though they had a $5.95 special at the time) which is quite pricey.

name: Pan Pacific Seattle
title: “FANTASTIC VALUE FOR A MOST COMFORTABLE STAY WITH WONDERFUL SERVICE”
text:
My husband and I were going onto a cruise on which we were going to spoil ourselves and so wanted somewhere to stay prior to that departure that spoilt us. I found the hotel and obtained a brilliant rom price from hotels.com. This hotel had all the things we were looking for... easy access to the local attractions and downtown shopping...affordable luxury.. an extremely clean room and bathroom suite... a most comfortable large bed... and excellent service from all the staff. The breakfast, although at an exra cost was superb. The extra bonus was having a Starbucks coffee house adjoining the hotel which opened at 0530 am and so despite having the facility of a coffee machine ( unfortunately not a kettle for hot water for TEA) in the room, my husband delighted in going next door to Starbucks ! The two restaurants adjacent to the hotel were both easy to access and very reasonably priced for an evening meal. Another bonus was the amazing food hall which was situated underneath the hotel, which povided, in additional to the normal groceries, fresh fruit and veg, an amazing bakery offering a selection of homemade cakes, a hot and cold takeaway meals service that would meet anyone's requirements, and an extra facility providing a variety of beverage.
We need more of this chain throughout the US !!!!!!

name: The Edgewater Hotel Seattle
title: “original,pero vivió mejores tiempos”
text:
Su ubicación es muy original:situado encima de unos pilones dentro del agua.Tuvo famosos alojados en sus habitaciones: Beatles ,Ray Charles,Suprems,Rolling Stones,Led Z.,Roy Orbison ,etc.Está claro que eso fue hace mucho,mucho tiempo,(las fotos colgadas en los espacios comunes,así lo demuestran).no creo que ahora pasaran del hall.
La habitación era ruidosa,estábamos a 200m de las vías del tren,su único "encanto" radicaba en una chimenea de" mentirijillas",osea, de gas .
El bar y restaurante decorados con originalidad, pero como el resto,viejos y descuidados. Cenamos y desayunamos correctamente,(caro)
Aunque no está lejos del centro ,como está a nivel del agua hay unas" buenas cuestas "para subir:llegas arriba sin aliento.
!ATENCIÓN parejas con niños! Nosotros estábamos en un 2º piso y las ventanas se abrían completamente y su altura nos llegaba por las rodillas(muy bajas),Había una buena caída y en la zona de descanso del Hall lo mismo,pero éstas daban directamente al agua: de hecho había una abierta .Me pareció increíble este fallo en las medidas de seguridad.(Se supone que en Estados Unidos son muy cuidadosos con estos temas)

name: Hyatt Regency Boston
title: “Great hotel at a great price!”
text:
I went on hotwire.com and found a great rate at this hotel. Of course with hotwire you don't know the name of the hotel until after you book it.
Beautiful hotel! Nice big rooms! CLEAN! Located right in Downtown Crossing close to everything. I travel to Boston many times on business and I will definitely stay here again!!

name: Mayflower Park
title: “Great location and service”
text:
