We had not been to Seattle in a few years and we wanted to find an nice hotel in downtown that was reasonably priced. The Mayflower Park met all these criteria. So we took Amtrak from Portland to Seattle (a great ride in both directions) and checked in at the Mayflower.
When we checked in, the front desk got us a very quiet room that actually had two separate bathrooms (it was nice to be able to spread out). The service was excellent throughout and we got some good tips from the concierge on what to do and where to eat.
The location was excellent, a few blocks away from the Pike Street Market and right at the termini of both the monorail and the new streetcar to Lake Union. In addition, downtown buses are free so we only needed a taxi once (after a tiring day and evening on the waterfront).

name: Hotel Andra
title: “Great location, nice hotel”
text: Hotel Andrea is conveniently located only a few blocks from the wharf and a few blocks from the convention center, which made it ideal for my business stay. I had dinner at the hotel restaurant and it was nice. I got in very late and had some appetizers and wine at the bar. The staff were friendly and offered to put me somewhere with a power outlet so I could work. The room was also lovely with a full length mirror. The bed was comfortable and the rooms were quiet - so basically everything a business traveller needs. I had high speed Internet and an iron at my disposal, so all in all I was pleased. I'd definitely go back.

name: River Inn of Harbor Town
title: “Perfect Hotel - the best in Memphis”
text:
The River Inn was the most wonderful place to stay. We chose this hotel over the Peabody hoping for more exclusive, personable service and we were not dissapointed.
The rooms were gorgeous, the staff were amazing (hello Shannon & Patrick!) the breakfast was superb and all the little touches (port & chocolates at bedtime!) made this a very memorable trip.
Yes its a 10 minute walk to main street and one that you might not want to do at night, but a cheap cab is always available.
Definitely definitely recommend - and hopefully we will be able to visit again soon.

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Great location”
text:
We're a family of four and our two boys prefer sleeping in their own bed whenever possible. The hotel was great to accomodate our request, and put us in a handicap room because the normal rooms would be too small to fit 2 rollaway beds. It worked out fine for space, and handicap rooms are corner suites so the views are excellent.
The hotel's location was perfect, since it's right in the Prudential shopping center area where were lots of shops and restaurants. Its also very close to the Prudential stop on the "T". The T is Boston's subway system and is a handy way to get to the airport or to other places in town.
This hotel is a business hotel that goes out of its way to help families, but is ideal for the business traveller who would normally travel alone or with one other person.

name: Hilton Boston Downtown / Financial District
title: “No No No”
text:
I picked the hotel for the location is great - close to the aquarium - walking distance to fanueil hall, etc....BUT the hotel missed a key ingredient in any hotel renovation - soundproofing. 
I will caveat this saying that I have lived in NYC and we arenot sensitive to noises from outside, upstairs neighbors, etc. 
We were awoken at 1am by the nightclub outside (Across the street), the music was literally shaking us in our bed. Had we not been with the baby (who, thankfully, slept through this) we would have moved rooms that instant. We also had lots of noise through the walls and the ceilings - far too much for a hotel of this quality. I'll go back to the Copley Hotels next time...they are much, much better, Hilton, Westin, Marriott...even if I have a farther walk to things. 
Just a really disappointing trip (with little sleep) because the hotel seems really nice, and, like I said, in a great location
Upon checkout, they did apologize for the situation...but they MUST know this is a recurring issue with that side of the hotel...they did comp our breakfast room service, which was OK because at that point what could they do? But how can we move a room at 1am with an infant!?!

name: DoubleTree Suites by Hilton - Boston
title: “Great Value at the Doubletree Suites”
text:
I stayed at the Doubletree for one night and was very satisfied with the experience. We got a great rate thru Priceline.com so that made it even better. Our room was on an 'executive' floor so I'm not sure what the difference was. 
Upon entry, you are in the 'living' area which had a pull out bed and a good size flat screen TV. The bathroom was average but featured Neutrogena products and good fluffy towels. The bedroom had a king size bed that was very comfortable with many pillows and nice quality bed linens. The bedroom had a smaller TV. Our room looked out over the Charles River. The room was very clean and bright, with new modern furnishings. 
The location was excellent for driving in from the airport, very easy to access from the highway. Also, the garage and valet allowed in-and-out parking for one rate. The hotel is a bit removed from the 'action' of Boston, and since we were only there for one night we did not use the shuttle service. Our walk to Harvard Square took about 25 minutes. We had a drink in the sports bar, but otherwise did not dine or use any of the hotels other amenities. 
I was very happy with the room considering I got what I feel to be a bargain ($98 per night including tax). My stay the previous week in Boston at another hotel was double the price and the room was tiny! 
Overall, I think the Doubletree is an excellent quality hotel and would definitely stay there again.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown
title: “$13 for WiFi”
text: Unreasonable to charge for WiFi in 2010. Free in the lobby and $13 in the room.

name: The Fairmont Olympic Seattle
title: “Excellent hotel”
text: We stayed for three nights at the end of May on vacation. I had found a promotional rate through Orbitz that made the price reasonable,considering how expensive is Seattle. I did not find anything about this hotel that I can complaint about, it was simply excellent in all ways. The staff was very professional and helpfull, specially at the spa and concierge. the room was extremely well appointed, best bedding I ever experienced in a hotel, and the pillows were feather, the expensive ones. Robes and slippers, umbrella in the closet, along with the customary. a scale in the bathroom to see the damage done to the waistline. Make-up mirrors in the bathroom, extra thick towels, top end toilettries, everthing you would expect and require for a place that claims five stars. The spa facilities were top notch, along with the pool area and locker room. they provided complementary coffe, bottled water, apples, and papers at the spa/pol, so you could sit at the adjacent terrace and relax reading the papers (NY Times, USA Today and local), go for a soak and then change. All kind of tolettries available in the locker room, not just your shaving cream and cheap cologne. robes and slippers there too! The location is excellent, downtown, and one block from the skytrain station on Third Ave. This leaves you a twenty minute ride to the Seattle-Tacoma airport, extremely convenient if you are a mere pedestrian, which is highly recomended in Seattle. If you need transportation to visit something out of town, you can rent a car there, but ditch the rental immediately inSeattle and use the Skytrain!! the bars was excellent, with a nice happy hour and their food, starters, were pretty good. I will return again if money is no object!!!!!!!

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Excellent service”
text: We upgraded to Club level, and enjoyed a healthful and tasty breakfast, excellent snacks in the lounge, and friendly service from everyone. This was a stay for a conference, and the service to conference attendees was also superb.

name: Holiday Inn Express Boston
title: “Come ce l'aspettavamo”
text: Camere non tanto grandi ma pulite, bagno piccolo. Frigorifero e micoonde in camera. Colazione vicino alla reception con pavimento e moquette luridi, scarsa la qualità, tutto confezionato, sempre uguale ogni giorno e con poco assortimento. Pomeriggio alle 18 biscotti scaldati offerti ogni giorno. Posizione: fuori dal centro ma relativamente vicino alla fermata della motro S.Andrew (10 minuti buoni a piedi), vicino all'autostrada (si sente il rumore dalle camere) e ad un centro commerciale. Zona squallida ma tranquilla. Con un albergo più vicino al centro o in centro non c'è bisogno di usare la metro perchè Boston si gira benissimo a piedi. Personale molto cordiale e disponibile. Uso del pc gratuito e connessione wi fi. Ho prenotato tardi e mi sono dovuta accontentare di ciò che ho trovato disponibile ma non ci tornerei.

name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great location!”
text: A great place to stay to walk and see the city life of Seattle

name: Hyatt Regency Boston
title: “Good location for business and for tourism”
text: Was only here one night and enjoyed my stay. The check-in was speedy (3PM) and the two check-in agents were extremely nice and funny. The room was spacious - bathroom door could have been nicer (it would not stay open and needed a good painting). The bed was comfy and I love the pillows. We had drinks at the bar and the server was very friendly. The location after dark is pretty deserted but we cabbed it back from dinner and didn't have any problems. We also cabbed it to/from Logan with ease. I'd stay here again.

name: The Maxwell Hotel Seattle
title: “Best Location in Seattle”
text: The Maxwell is on the border between tourist area and Queen Anne neighborhood. So from the hotel you are a walk from museums, the waterfront, and tourist sites and a beautiful hilly neighborhood with charming houses and great views and neighborhood restaurants. We went to the Seattle Art Museum and waterfront one day, but then ate at neighborhood spots. We also went for walks just up the hill and around Queen Anne just looking at the houses and stopping to look at the views of Mt. Rainer on one side, and the mountain range on the other side. The hotel made a major mistake in our booking - we had signed up for a package that included a 2 hour cruise of the lake, and when we got there they had not purchased the cruise tickets and could not get us onto another. BUT, the way they handled it was inpeccable and left us feeling initially disappointed, of course, but no lasting pain. The manager came up to the room immediately in person, with a bottle of champagne, to personnaly appologize and offered to comp one night of hotel plus arrange for a lovely brunch (on them) on the waterfront the next day. I think the in-person apology and quick response and rearrangement plus the comped night were as good a response as one could hope for, and we appreciated them. Anyone can make a mistake, and they dealt with it very well. If you were booking a package, I would confirm and reconfirm. The Maxwell has hardwood floors which initially sounded good, but actually is a little hard on the feet after a day of walking on pavement. Beds VERY comfortable, nice bathroom with excellent lighting, quiet despite busy neighborhood, free parking. Front desk staff other than the manager were clueless - asked for several tips about the neighborhood and none of them knew anything about the neighborhood. Japanese restaurant? Had to look it up but there was a great one just down the street whcih we found. Desert at night? No clue but there was a coffee and pastry shop right down the street which we found. What restaurants and stores were at the top of the hill? No clue but we walked up and found great stuff. So don't count on the front desk people. If Melonie the Manager is there, she's the only one who knows what's what. Swimming pool and fitness room were small but perfectly adequate, and all machines worked.

name: Hotel 1000
title: “Great Downtown hotel...”
text:
Great downtown location... good for both business and leisure travelers. Just blocks away from Pikes Place and the Seattle Art Museum. Top service - very helpful staff. I cannot think of one thing to complain about... even the chocolates on the bed in the evening were great.
We were a bit concerned that the noise would be bad since it was in a popular area; however, this was not a problem even in our room overlooking 1st Avenue (great view from our room on the 8th floor). We were there for 5 nights and only one night (Saturday) did we notice a bit of traffic noise (it seemed like there were a few loud motorcycles cruising around the area... the sound of their engines made it into the room) - possibly the rooms on the other side of the hotel would have no traffic noise.

name: The Edgewater Hotel Seattle
title: “fantastic, romantic, Alaskan Lodge on the water, perfect, great bargain”
text: No bad view. beautiful Lobby. Great vews from the bar area. would hands down stay here again.

name: Hotel 140
title: “Our stay in Boston”
text: We found this hotel by accident on the internet and have been very pleased with the quality of the hotel. The staff were extremely friendly and met all our needs. We will definitely stay here again and will recommend to our friends coming to Boston.

name: Hilton Boston Downtown / Financial District
title: “Hilton gave us a wonderful anniversary weekend in Boston!”
text:
The Hilton Boston was in a great location; we took the train into North station, which turned out to be a very walkable district to the hotel. We were greeted at the front desk by a very friendly and helpful young woman; when we booked the hotel we told them that we were celebrating our anniversary; to oujr surprise when we checked in we found out that they had upgraded us to a huge, beautiful suite! The suite was incredible, beautiful and clean. The bedding was extremely comfortable and great quality. On top of the suite upgrade, they also threw in a buffet breakfast for both mornings, which was quite good.
Faneuil Hall was less than 5 walking minutes away; the 'T' was a couple of blocks. We had great weather so spent the weekend walking to most parts of Boston, and taking the 'T' when we got tired. It was a great weekend at a fabulous hotel in a great location.
Things we liked least about the hotel were quite minor; 2 of the lamps in the room had dead lightbulbs, and there could have been better lighting in the living room. The bathroom was quite small for the size and luxury of the suite. Also, no free wireless internet in the room were a definite negative.
Things we liked the most were the location, friendliness and quality of the hotel.

name: Mayflower Park
title: “Great Boutique Hotel!!!!”
text:
Great hotel with excellent staff!! Friendly and efficient front desk. 
Called to confirm reservation and Reservations Clerk was extremely nice. Hotel matched rate found on internet. Room was beautifully decorated with Boutique feel. Andaluca (sp?) was Yummy! Full Breakfast for our kids under 10 was free, Olivers' Lounge had the BEST martinis. 
Could not have asked for better location... we walked to pretty much EVERY attraction. DEFINITELY would stay again. Can't say enough!

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Roundhouse Suites
title: “Excellent staff, best ever, clean room, nothing was any trouble”
text:
Excellent stay, the reception staff especially Orlando was very helpful. Rooms were clean, free internet, free shuttle bus, free cookeis, free ice, free b'fast. What a bargain!! even had a bath.
Alittle noisy but I asked for a room at the back and I found it okay. Very reasonably priced. I recommend to anyone, close to the convention centre. Thank you again for a great stay, I would come back when next in Boston!!

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Good Location, Average Hotel”
text:
My fiance and I stayed for one night on New Year's Eve. The location of the hotel is its main appeal; a great base of operations to explore Boston and Cambridge either on foot or the T. The room was clean and tidy. Everything one would expect in hotel in this range.
Check in was a bit of a cluster. NYE is probably one of their busiest nights, but a little better organization would go a long way. I, like many others, had other plans for the 45 minutes I spent in the unmarked line for Sheraton Preferred Guests. The receptionist did make an exception for me, which was appreciated, but a better system would help.
In the elevator I spoke to a guest who stated he was there for a friend's 1200 person NYE party in a ballroom, which raised a little concern for late night noise. While there were several 'amateurs' in the lobby early in the evening, the security did start checking room keys at the elevators before 8PM. By the time we returned to the room at the end of the night, there was no loud party/noise issues at all.
We did eat at the hotel restaurant, Sidebar, which was the highlight of our stay. Waiter Jimmy was one of the best I've ever had. Thorough, timely, and genuine. No problem to get a table for 7 on short notice. Food was good and fairly priced.

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “A typical convention hotel”
text: We stayed here during a 5 day conference in January and were underwhelmed. There is no refrigerator in the room. The king bed mattress was lumpy with a "hole"on one side and a "shelf" on the other side. The bathroom is small and the toilet is noisy. We kept the bathroom door shut to minimize sounds from the neighboring bathroom. The TV has över 20 channels". 20 oz soda bottles cost $2.25 in the vending machine on the floor. On the plus side, it was easy to control room temperature and the heating system was silent. The pillows were soft and comfortable, and the wait for elevators was reasonable. One day when I returned at 3:30 pm to the room, it was not yet made up. I called guest services and someone was sent to make up the room within 20 minutes.

name: Hotel Andra
title: “I really enjoyed it.”
text:
I have recently returned from the Hotel Andra and can say that I was pleased with my experience. The room we had was lovely and the people who served the hotel were very accomodating. We had breakfast @ Lola twice and the food was absolutely delicious! 
The location of the Hotel is perfect. I would stay there again!

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown
title: “Great Value - book through the 'go boston' website!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel 31 March - 3 April 2006 and found it fantastic value for money. The location is great if you don't mind a walk - it took us about 15 minutes to get to Quincy Market - which I think is quite reasonable.
We stayed as a family of 4 in the one room - spacious enough and very comfortable. There was no view - and I don't think you would get a good view from any of the rooms as it is only 5 levels high and not in a particularly scenic location.
The staff were courteous and efficient. We were given late check out on asking.
We booked the hotel through the 'go boston' website for one night, and then paid a discounted rate for the subsequent nights. On check in we had 2 adult and 2 children's 'go boston' cards for one day and two nights trolley bus tour - these would cost almost £150 if we were buying them and so worked out to be a fantastic deal.
The only disappointment was the car booked to return us to the airport via the concierge (Thomas)- we paid over the odds for the convenience - yet got a surly and unfriendly driver who virtually threw us out of the van when we got there - a distinct difference from our wonderfully friendly welcome by the Bostonions.

name: Hilton Boston Downtown / Financial District
title: “Nice find in Boston”
text: After reading past reviews, I wasn't quite sure what I was going to encounter during my stay at the Hilton Boston Financial District. I must say, I was very pleased with both the hotel and the staff. The room was large (sometimes unusual in big city hotels built in the 1920's) and very comfortable. My one complaint was the distance from the TV to the bed--the old style tv made it difficult to watch tv from anywhere but the chair, unless you wanted to crank up the volume. The bed was delightfully comfortable. And housekeeping was great. The staff was friendly, yet very professional.

name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A Great Hotel”
text: We stayed here in March as we were on a Hockey tour. The Hotel is literally opposite the Arena so was a perfect location for us as we had two matches to go to in the four days we were there. Also it is right next to China Town (which is nothing to write home about) and also it is not to far from all the tourist attractions. The cost was a little high at $217 per night but the hotel, location and amenities were worth it to us. The Hotel's restaurant we only ate once in as food was really expensive, but very good. Another nice touch was the wine receptions every evening, which were free receptions for those staying at the hotel. The bathroom needed updating but was perfectly usable and the min bar has to be seen to be believed. All in all I would recommend this hotel.

name: Bulfinch Hotel Boston
title: “Pass on this one...”
text: I stayed at this hotel on my last trip to Boston... and have stayed there 4 previous times. Extremely disappointed this time. They eliminated their "frequent guest" program but I guess never notified any of the "guests" of this program... I was told that they were purchased by another hotel chain and they did away with it. Strike One. Oh, and when i called to confirm reservation and to get a reduction in rate, I asked about the program and was told that they would take care of me ... I guess they lied. Strike Two. Room rates were more than double the previous trip and was told that they rooms were under renovation because of the new owner. When I checked in, I asked for an updated room and was told "they haven't renovated any yet... just new TVs". Another lie?? Strike Three. I also noticed white stains on the brown blanket over the bed... quite a few of them... Looks like housekeeping is really lax on doing it's job... I'm now officially done with this place.

name: Hyatt Regency Boston
title: “unsatisfactory”
text: It"s not 4 stars hotel: not friendly stuff, very noisy aircondition in the room, not working hair dryer, not quility food., the lockers without keys in the swimming pool .

name: Boston Common Hotel and Conference Center
title: “Great location”
text:
Our stay was great! Air conditioning was working very well, we had plenty of fluffy towels and cleaning ladies did a great job through our stay of 4 days. 
Internet is free, but only accessible inside common areas (lobby and 5th floor's breakfast area).
The location is GREAT: a short walk from Copley square and even shorter walk to Back Bay metro station.
I dare add that some employees at front desk should work a little on their welcoming skills... when I arrived and asked where and how we could pay for parking, the lady "aswered" with a condescending tone. Bad days happen in any job, but it's kind of disappointing when you're a customer paying a few hundred dollars for a stay! Anyways, later on, another collegue explained clearly where the parking office was. The fare is only 23$/day!

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Great stay at Sheraton & visiting Boston”
text: The Sheraton was wonderful, best thing was the location, right near the Tube with access to everywhere. The room was fine, the bedding was luxurious, we slept like angels. Everyone very helpful. There is a food court next door in the Prudential Center which was great for really economical meals. Our favorite restaurant was Charley's on Newbury Street. Attractions - first day walked most the Freedom Trail, we loved all the history. Recommend watching the 3 DVD series Liberty on the American Revolution, available thru Netflix. MFA Museum of Fine Arts wonderful, also enjoyed JFK museum & Boston Public Library (awesome building, great murals), last day we went to Bunker Hill & USS Constitution, both very interesting.

name: Pan Pacific Seattle
title: “Great experience”
text: The hotel was great. The location above a Whole Foods is terrific. It is a bit of a walk to the waterfront but Seattle is safe and clean. Room was clean and the soaking tub very nice. Sheets, towels and room above average for a good value. Also quiet and good service.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown
title: “Conveniente y muy buena atención”
text: La habitación era amplia, limpia, ajustada al precio. Hotel silencioso y cerca de las atracciones de la ciudad. Bien localizado. Lo recomiendo. El personal muy amistoso y cortés.

name: Howard Johnson Inn Fenway Park Boston
title: “NEEDS HELP”
text: Not that this is a terrible hotel it is just old and beaten up. the rooms appeared to be clean, and the neighborhood is a bar and college area if that's what you want. parking in the lot $20.00, not bad but certainly not great

name: Ramada Inn Boston
title: “Nice place to stay”
text: Good quality for the money. It was a nightmare to drive to. One bonus was a shuttle service to the train station which was a fast trip to the sights of Boston. Internet service was poor.

name: Hyatt Regency Boston
title: “Perfect location!”
text: Everything about this place is perfect! It's within walking distance to everything, or a very short cab ride, or the train is steps away... eveything we wanted to see in Boston was so close! The room was so comfortable and very clean. The staff was extremely friendly and accomodating! I really cannot say enough good about this hotel!

name: The Fairmont Olympic Seattle
title: “Excellent Service”
text: This is a beautiful hotel with service you will not find elsewhere. My personal favorite is the way the bellmen welcome you back every time you leave and return to the hotel. It's such a nice gesture to say "welcome back" and always put a smile on my face. The Concierge was extremely helpful with restaurant suggestions and handling the reservations. The room we had was a Deluxe King and I thought it was plenty big with a nice bathroom (although I would have preferred to have had a separate shower and bath instead of a bath/shower combination). The cleaning women cleaned the room very well each day and there is turndown service each night. Also each night they leave a card with the next day's weather forecast (which I found very helpful in planning the next day's wardrobe selection). In the morning, there is a newspaper delivered. There are no "views" from this hotel, but what you're paying for is the service. I would recommend the hotel to those who enjoy high quality service.

name: The Fairmont Olympic Seattle
title: “elegance and impeccable service!!”
text:
I was a little worried having read some reviews before staying here. The hotel has some worn items, but the service and care of its staff more than compensated for any worn carpet I saw. My in-laws and I stayed here on the night of July 4th. We arrived around 9:30AM from our cruise ship and they let us check in at that very moment, no added fees. My mother-in-law and I took High Tea at the Georgian. It was excellent and we were not rushed, but were encouraged to linger. 
Upon check-in, we were given a little bag of toys (very cheap made in China), but a nice thought and a card to order complimentary cookies and milk from room service for our 2 year-old. 
Both rooms were huge!! Ours was so large, and allowed plenty of room for our portable crib. The draperies were a little dated, but lovely as they were trimmed with bullion fringe.
We learned from an employee that the Georgian Room is about to be renovated-a shame, I liked the green upholstery. Everything is very elegantly decorated, but the bath faucets and fixtures show their age.
The hotel was lovely, one of the finest that I have ever stayed in while in a large city. Some things are worn, but I am sure that renovations are soon to follow. Never once did I see anything dirty or grimy, everything was neat and clean in our room. My overall opinion of the Fairmont is a high opinion of a classic hotel that knows customer service and care. Try not to be in a rush, be nice to the staff (anywhere you go), even if it takes a little more time. Many of the Fairmont’s staff are international and are sincere about guests' concerns. I would jump at the chance to stay at the Fairmont again and am blessed to have gotten such a great room at such a great rate for this trip.
TEA at the Georgian Room
Our waiter suggested I try the 1907 Fairmont blend tea-a wise decision. He was very nice and helpful. His name was Quoc (Asian guy). Another waiter was Alvis (Eastern European?) Both were humorous and answered any questions we had about the hotel or food, all-the-while remaining very professional. One could tell they enjoyed their work. 
The decor of the 2 chandeliers (8 feet high each), green furniture and creamy walls was soothing. It is not the fanciest hotel that I have taken tea in before, but the food was superb and again the wait staffs made it seem grander than the Palm Court Tea experience that I had in San Fran. The Wait staff was horribly snobbish there!
At many other high teas I have had, the chef brings in certain finished pastries, etc. The waiters explained that the only items not made on the premises are bread and crackers. All pastries are made there and also supplied to their little patisserie.
The food was great, but the service by our two waiters as mentioned above was probably the best service I have ever had in North America and Europe!

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Good location”
text: Recently stayed for 3 nights in Sheraton on first ever visit to Boston. Couldn't believe how expensive the hotels were in the city , but got a very good rate through Hotwire. Hotel is well situated , being only a few minutes walk to Boylston St , with its many bars/restaurants and the popular shopping area of Newbury St . The room in North Tower was small but adequate , with coffee making facility , hairdryer and safe. The bathroom was very small , but bed was extremely comfortable , one of the nicest i've ever slept in . The hotel has nice pool and workout area on 5th floor and also outdoor area adjacent to pool with sun loungers . Complimentary internet access is available in foyer. No complaints about hotel and very good value for price we paid , but not for price that hotel were quoting on their website.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Boston Garden
title: “What do you compromise on, for value?”
text:
This hotel is located close to the north end and all that is offered here...and that is quite a lot; little Italy, historical monuments and the Freedom Trail - well worth it. 
Although the rooms are really quite spacious and if you use them as we did, you can overlook some things - the slightly dated decor, dirty looking carpets and a rough looking location. 
As a value for money sleeping place it is ideal.

name: Comfort Inn - Boston
title: “If you like noise, this (DIS-) Comfort Inn is the place for you.”
text:
THE GOOD: Hotel shuttle service was very good -- friendly drivers picked us up from our ship when it docked and also took us several times to the nearby "T" station. Also good: our room was spacious and the breakfasts were good.
THE BAD: Because of the overpriced Boston hotels, we had to find a somewhat less expensive place to stay outside the city, which led us to stay at this Inn where: the breakfast nook was chaotic every morning and the food, once gone, was not replaced; the toilet in our room didn't flush properly; and, in an era of large screen HD TV, we had, instead, a 25" TV with a "fuzzy" picture.
THE UGLY: The NOISE factor was incredible! Usually when you make advance reservations with a hotel and you request a quiet room, you get a room in the back, away from any traffic. We got a room in the back, alright -- right next to commuter trains that rumbled noisily by our room about every 20 minutes until very late at night, then started up again at 5 a.m.. This noise was made even worse by a loud air conditioning unit; by noisy neighbors who talked loudly in the hallway around 1 a.m and just as loudly in their room until about 2 a.m.; by next door plumbing noises (shower and toilet); and by an early morning garbage truck emptying a dumpster. Most inexcusable of all were the noisy maids who hung out at a storage closet across from our room.. Several times every morning they were talking and laughing very loudly with one another, at length, and even yelled at each other down the hallway.
BOTTOM LINE: If you can't get a good night's sleep, it"s not worth staying at a hotel like this despite its more positive amenities.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Roundhouse Suites
title: “Very good do not let area mislead you”
text:
The area is not the best. South end of Boston.
The hotel has been renovated. 
We had a suite, 2 televsions, free parking and breakfast for $109.
Shuttle to the downtown in 15 minutes. 
Very good pick for anyone staying in Boston.

name: Onyx Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Average at best”
text: Nice room no views but very expensive bar was always empty breakfast average with reluctent staff I feel there is better for the price. reasonable situation

name: Comfort Inn - Boston
title: “Nice Hotel, very expensive in this time of the year”
text:
Me and my girlfriend decided to take a trip to Boston and it was a pretty spontaneous decision. Did not book a hotel. Thought we could find one cheap and fast when we get there. MAJOR MISTAKE. Do not go to Boston before you make a hotel reservation. It was a nightmare. All the hotels were booked. One taxi driver told us that the Comfort Inn might have rooms. Guess what ? They had only one room left (that's what they said) and charged us something like 240 USD for one night :). That is a lot for a three star hotel. Maybe the season was pretty busy, but still 240 USD :) for a Comfort Inn. We did not have any choice cause it was already passing midnight so we paid the price.
The room was OK, nice view of downtown Boston from distance. Location is good if you are with a car, next to a major highway. Breakfast was also OK, typical 100 USD per room per night hotel breakfast but not for 240 :D. Would never make that mistake again to go on a trip without booking in advance. I had my lesson.

name: Comfort Inn - Boston
title: “Disappointed”
text:
I was disappointed in my selection of a hotel. I used priceline to get a good deal on a hotel and entered in I was willing to stay in South Boston and this hotel came up. It lists its address as Boston but it's actually located in Dorchester (a Boston suburb). Their website said that the local T station was only 1.5 miles away but it's actually 2.1 miles by foot or car (read the small print). We arrived at 10 a.m. on a Saturday and was hoping to take the shuttle to the T station to catch the T into Boston. We waited for 10 minutes and when the shuttle arrived it said it only had 2 available seats. Well there were 20 people waiting. The driver said the next shuttle would be in 20 minutes and again would only fit 12 people. The shuttles service both the Comfort Inn and the Ramada. So when it looked like we would never get to the station before noon I asked the man at the front desk how far the T station was and if it was walkable (keep in mind I have small children who were with me). He said it was only about 3/4 of a mile down the road and it was walkable. So we decided to walk. Well it was quite a long walk and when I clocked it with my car the next day I found out it was actually 2.1 miles away and the walk involved walking through parking lots (again I have small children). Needless to say we ended up driving into Boston every day since the shuttle service was a nightmare, not convenient at all. 
The hotel is also not located in a great place. When you check in they give you a hand out that says they have had recent car break-ins and to remove all electronics from your vehicle. They even go as far to say to clean the area were your GPS suctions onto your window so the potential thief doesn't realize you have a GPS. It surely didn't leave us with the warm and fuzzys. 
The train also runs directly behind the hotel so avoid getting a room on the backside of the hotel. We stayed in one on the front side facing the parking lot so I'm not sure how much the train is heard from within one of the backside rooms. 
It's a very small hotel with not a lot of amenities. I surely didn't pay a lot but I guess sometimes you get what you pay for.

name: Hyatt Regency Boston
title: “Hyatt - Skip It WIth Family”
text:
We bboked room online and requested two double beds- After valet parking the car we were informed at check in that we now were in a king room. We left the confirmation in the car (already parked). We were told to produce proof of reservation or move- "they were busy and we were holding them up"- We went back to the car and got the reservation confirmation- were then told the hotel was sold out. The front desk staff was rude, lied to us and accused us of using a third party to book our room- (not sure of the meaning of this). 
This is a fine hotel for a business travler but not for a family - Look at other options and avoid this property if you can.

name: Holiday Inn Boston at Beacon Hill
title: “WOW, top notch hotel and service.”
text:
Let me first start off by saying that I have stayed in many hotels in my 30 years.
I want to thank the staff at the Holiday Inn as I found them to be top notch and address any issue that came up very fast and with complete professionalism. 
I found the hotel to be in a very very good spot and close to pretty much everything Boston has to offer. There are so many great restaurants, pubs, and coffee shops close by. Charles street is just up the road and offers so much. I can not say enough about the location
The hotel was very clean, and offered everything a good hotel should. The pool was very nice, clean and had a life guard which is hotels tend to skimp on. The pool area was well used. I do think the hotel should look into a bit more workout equipment but I am sure they will in time. 
as many people on here have complained, I did not find any issues with the current renos interfering with our experience. 
I will 100% without a doubt stay at this hotel again in the future as I fell in love with Boston and want to return very soon.
I huge thanks for the staff for making this stay one I won't forget. Thank you. 
Ryan and Melissa

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “GOOD LOCATION, AVERAGE ROOMS, AVERAGE SERVICE.”
text:
We went on a 2 week vacation to Boston and wanted to stay at a central location since we were going to visit all the local attractions.This Sheraton hotel in Boston is located perfectly because you can walk to Fenway Park; you have access to a mall from the 2nd floor of the hotel; you can walk to take boat tours; etc., etc. Everything is easily accessible from this hotel. But, we found out that there are several other similar hotels located in the same area, and some of them might be a little less expensive.... so we might stay somewhere else next time.
Our room was average/comfortable, but the bathroom was really small! We were on the 12th floor. We did get the WORST view we have ever gotten from any hotel! It was this brown structure, we found out it was the back wall of the mall. For an expensive hotel we were surprised that the coffee maker had one creamer and one sugar and there was no mini bar! Not the best Sheraton we have stayed at. This hotel is REALLY busy all the time. Because of this, there are people in the lobby and in the entrance at all times! Several times the doorman was not able to get us a taxi because he would be overwhelmed with other guests. Luckily there are always taxis parked a block away, so we could just walk and flag them down ourselves.
They have good room service and the concierge is very helpful. Their bar is well stocked and they have good service.
Overall, it was a very good experience and we would stay at this hotel again.
**********************************************************************************************

name: Hyatt Regency Boston
title: “home away from home”
text: I spent 4 nights at the Hyatt Downtown and thought it was great. The doorman was right there to carry my luggage all the way from the street to the lobby and asked if I would need it brought to my room. Great start! The reason for the two sets of elevators is for security purposes. The hotel wants to see who is coming and going to the rooms. One night I had to show my key to get on the second set of elevators to the rooms. This is a good thing. Check in was very pleasant and professional. I got the room through Priceline so I was expecting a view of the alley but what a pleasant surprise when I got a room on the 20th floor with a tremendous view of the financial district and the inner harbor islands. It was very nice and I was really happy to have it. The bed was super comfortable, the bathroom was fully stocked with products (even toothpaste). The best part of the hotel though is the gym. While not everyone looks for this when they travel, if you like to work out this gym had everything! This hotel was very nice. I would definitely go back.

name: Copley House
title: “Beautiful neighborhood, great value”
text: This hotel is in a fabulous section of Boston. It is just blocks from the Prudential Center, Newbury Street, and very short walk to two different T stops, (Prudential on green line, and Back Bay on Orange line). In a quiet neighborhood of beautiful brownstones and a walking path to that orange line stop, it is a very safe area. We were warmly greeted and treated well at check in. We had a studio in the building on Newton St, which was very quiet. The room was small, but very clean and we really enjoyed having a kitchen. There were many wonderful resturants nearby on Tremont St. and a huge grocery at the Prudential complex. My traveling companion and I thought that this was a great value and we would recommend this hotel to our friends and will stay there again when visiting Boston.

name: Comfort Inn - Boston
title: “Good value for the money”
text:
We stayed 4 nights at this hotel and except for one night , had an enjoyable stay. The night in question was due to a large group of about 25 - 30 teenagers who checked in late and were loud, continuously knocking at each others' rooms, stomping and yelling the length of the hallways. Called the front desk to request that the group's chaperones be notified to settle their people down. Said they would but basically nothing changed till well past. midnight .
That aside, unless you want to pay $350+ for a downtown hotel, this is a very good option. They provide a free shuttle to and from the airport. We waited an acceptable 20 minutes, after our call, for our pickup. The pickup location was across the immediate departure area of the airport and easy to find. We were joining a cruise and they also provided a free scheduled drop off to the cruise terminal. The hotel is located about three subway stops from the center of Boston and they also provide a shuttle to and from the Metro or "T" station. This shuttle runs about every 30 minutes but of particular note, the van can carry only about 20 people and serves not only the Comfort Inn but the Ramada Inn and as a consequence can fill quite quickly. There were a few occasions where people could not get on and had to wait 30 minutes for the next pickup with no assurance that they would be able to get on the next one. Think some kind of sign up system is needed.
The rooms were clean and functional and unlike some other reviewers we didn't find traffic noise or any other external noises to be any problem at all, and we had a room facing the road. 
The free breakfast was very good and the selection was more than adequate. The immediate area does not have too many options for resturants. There is a resturant attached to a hotel (think it was a Ramada Inn) - the food was so so, but like some other reviewer mentioned, the service was abysmally slow. Eat in town before you return to the hotel unless you have time to burn. A sandwich shop, a Dunking Doughnut resturant and Bowling Alley Pizza place are closeby. There is also a large super market across the street with an attached deli. You can access the market through an overhead pedestrian walkway or a crosswalk with a traffic light immediately to the left and infront of the hotel.

Address: '240 Mount Vernon Street at Bayside Center'
name: DoubleTree Club by Hilton Hotel Boston Bayside
title: “Nice stay in South Boston”
text:
We booked two rooms at the DoubleTree to attend our daughter's graduation at UMASS Boston, which is also located near the Bayside Expo. 
The room was spacious, clean and the staff courteous. Our room consisted of a comfortable king-size bed, desk, and a comfortable chair. The bathroom was clean and spacious. The room was also equipped with a small refrigerator.
The downstairs lobby, included a small bar area with seating for about 20 people. Adjacent to that was a seating for about 40 people to eat from the small "self-service" cafe where you can purchase sandwiches from a limited menu. The staff here was slow and not very courteous.
There was a $10 daily charge to park and wifi was available for free in the lobby (if you asked), but only available for a fee in rooms.
The location is a bit out of the way, but there is a T-Stop nearby.
Overall we would stay here again.

name: Holiday Inn Boston at Beacon Hill
title: “Great location for vacation”
text: This Holiday Inn's location is great for a vacation in Boston. It was close to many restaurants on Charles St., as well as to Boston Commons, the Esplande along the Charles River, and sites on the Freedom Trail. The MGH Redline metro stop is also very close to the hotel. The hotel itself was clean and the staff was friendly. The rooms were quiet; we did not hear any other guests even though the hotel was full during our visit. The pool was closed during our visit; a memo said it was closed indefinitely.

name: Bulfinch Hotel Boston
title: “A European-style, boutique hotel”
text: My daughter and I stayed at the Bulfinch while we were in Boston visiting colleges. It is centrally located and close to the subway. We had planned to stay two nights, but our flight was cancelled and when I called ahead to say we would be a day late they were very accommodating and didn't charge us for the first night, despite their cancellation policy. When we arrived the next morning, the valet was very helpful in showing us how to get to the subway and where we were going. We knew we'd have to share a king-sized bed, since they don't seem to have rooms with two beds, but the room itself was very comfortable and the bathroom quite large, perhaps because we got a handicapped-accessible room. The decor was very modern and the bed very comfortable. I found everyone to be helpful and had no qualms with the location, despite the fact that we were two women traveling alone. If my daughter goes to school in Boston, I look forward to staying at the Bulfinch again.

name: The Fairmont Olympic Seattle
title: “Worth every penny – a fantastic stay”
text: My fiancée and I were very happy with our stay at the Fairmont Olympic. In town for a friend’s wedding, everything was handled with the high level of service that I have come to expect from the Fairmont chain. Location is central, easy walking distance to most of the main Seattle attractions. The property itself is beautiful, a hotel with all of the old detail that takes you back in time. The lobby is phenomenal and has both a restaurant and a bar with ample seating. Once upstairs, we were amazed at the size of our room. Truly living in the lap of luxury for the weekend.

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “I have a feeling that management was not listening.”
text:
We stayed at the Sheraton Boston Hotel from July 28th to July 30th for a medical conference. We arrived at the front door after battling Boston traffic with lots of suitcases. Normally I am happy to carry my own luggage, but I would have been grateful for some assistance. None was to be found. No one greeted us on arrival or offered us assistance. So, we needed to drag six items to the front desk. I have stayed at many large city hotels and find it unusual that nobody was on duty to help us; especially on Friday afternoon. As a matter of fact, I saw no bell hops in the hotel. Is this no longer a service that Sheraton offers?
The room itself was very nice, very roomy with a wonderful view. However, when I went into the bathroom I noticed that there was a leak from around the bathtub faucet. This must have been going on for a long time because there was a water stain. I immediately notfied the front desk, and they sent someone up to repair it while we were away. The "repair" consisted of tightening the handles with brute force, making it very difficult for me to use the shower. I complained to the front desk no less than three times during my stay. I will give high marks to the desk personnel for their concern. They did offer me one day of free internet and $50 off my hotel bill.
That was not my concern, I was not really inconvenienced. In an age when all hotels have cards in the bathrooms stating that they are "Committed to saving resources", I am disturbed that the Boston Sheraton Hotel would not take a few moments to repair the leak, stop the flow of water, and save thousands of gallons of water!

name: Holiday Inn Boston at Beacon Hill
title: “Good location for a nice hotel”
text:
I got this hotel through Priceline ($240 / night, which was $30 cheaper than anything else I could find for >3 stars). The location is the best part about this hotel. It is a 5 min walk from the nearest T station and the Charles River Esplanade and Longfellow Bridge. And right at the foot of Beacon Hill, which means you can enjoy the quaint, historic neighbourhood easily. There are several places to eat nearby. 
As others have said, the hotel is under renovations but it didn't inconvenience us in any way. Breakfast was not included and so we just went to the Au Bon Pain which is right in front of the hotel and got a much cheaper breakfast. The rooms were comfortable, clean and basically what you'd expect at a Holiday Inn. The bathroom doors were frosted glass, (what's up with that, our new york hotel was the same!) and although you can't really see through it, not very private. I didn't mind too much, I've lived with my husband long enough :) But I'm glad I wasn't sharing with a friend.
Oh one other note of caution - this location is near multiple hospitals. Which means siren blasting ambulances go by. As soon as we got to our room, 3 or 4 of the went by in a short period and it was *loud* in the room. Fortunately we weren't ever disturbed at night (it was peaceful, not even much street noise although we were only on the 4th floor). But I imagine that's a matter of luck.
Wireless was complimentary but so poor that we had to give up on it.
Overall, good for its price and location.

name: Comfort Inn - Boston
title: “Sencillo y limpio, cerca del Aeropuerto”
text:
Es un hotel situado un poco lejos de todo, pero por ello disponen de un servicio de Shuttle gratuito al aeropuerto, donde puedes enlanzar con la red de metro de Boston.
Las habitaciones son amplias y limpias, y el precio (95.-€ por tres personas) es adecuado.
Tienen un desayuno mínimo gratuito, pero suficiente para hacer un café y una pasta por la mañana..
Hay bastante personal hispano, y los que no, siempre chapurrean algunas palabras en español.
Es estilo un Ibis europeo.

name: Comfort Inn - Boston
title: “Immer wieder !”
text: Dieses Hotel/Motel liegt etwas außerhalb von Boston. Problem? Nein, denn erstens ist das Parken frei, ansonsten fährt alle halbe Std. ein Shuttle zur U-Bahn, Fahrtdauer ca. 10 min, und dann 4 Stationen mit der U-Bahn und man ist mitten im Zentrum von Boston. Suuuper. Die Zimmer sind hell, freundlich und sauber, Internet ist schnell und kostenlos (WLAN). Das Frühstück ist amerikanisch, aber von überraschend guter Qualität. Für dortige Verhältnisse. Das Personal ist sehr freundlich,kompetent sowie sehr hilfsbereit.

name: Ramada Inn Boston
title: “Just as I expected”
text:
I am still here so I reserve the right to revise or amend my opinion. Every traveler has his or her own personal experiences good and bad. This is mine so far:
Check in was fast, room was clean and bed comfy. I am here so I do not have to commute to the hospital where my wife is for a few days. The shuttle to the train is great and on time. I drove to the hospital before checking in and Boston traffic is tough so I am avoiding that with the shuttle and the train.
Breakfast is decent and loved the waffles.
WiFi worked great, I am using it right now in fact.
The biggest negative is trying to find the hotel. If you do not have a GPS good luck.
Some complained of cleanliness issues but there is no problem here for me but I did not get under the bed or search for mice poops. I might after reading one review.
The rate is the best in Boston. You can find upscale hotels but be prepared to drop another hundred bucks a night at least. 
If things go down hill I will revise my comments but soon I will be off to make my own waffles.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Logan Airport
title: “Awsome”
text: this is one of the best hotels I've stayed at, very clean, loved the pool and hot tub, my kids had a blast, breakfast was AWSOME, even though I had to pay for mine (kids eat free), so worth it!

name: The Fairmont Olympic Seattle
title: “Traumhaftes Hotel”
text:
Vom Empfang an fühlten wir uns in diesem Haus sehr wohl. Das Personal war sehr zugewandt: Viele sprachen uns schon nach ein paar Stunden mit Namen an, nachdem sie sich nach der Aussprache erkundigt hatten.
Das Zimmer (De Luxe Doppelzimmer) war wunderbar, ein echter Luxus: Kleines Wohnzimmer und großes Schlafzimmer, kleiner Ankleideraum, hübsches Bad. Topzustand, tadellos sauber.
Der Zimmerservice war exzellent, auch die servierten Speisen.
Das Frühstück war luxuriös. Köstliches Buffet oder à la carte. Obst sehr schön angerichtet, eindrucksvoll die tiefroten und gelben Kirschen in zylindrischen Gläsern. Auch hier sehr persönlicher Service. 
Der Concierge war effektiv. Unternehmungen wurden hervorragend gebucht.
Alles in allem: Ein Hotel, das den Abschied schwer macht und zum Wiederkommen einlädt.

name: Courtyard Boston Downtown / Tremont
title: “Please do not spend your night here on weekends/festivities”
text:
This hotel should not be under Marriott portfolio, it's probably one of the worst night spent into a hotel and it's very sad to say that because it's extremely well located, it allows you to visit Boston by walk and right in front of the hotel you have the stop of one of the trolleys that ride all around the city.
So overall we can say great location during the day and strategic for visiting the city; but during the night it's another story!! A Night club is right attached to the hotel, you also have a direct access from the lounge and you can hear the music from the 15th floor! 
Security seems not existing and rooms (old and not in really nice shape) are not soundproof at all so you can hear everything from corridors to next room.

name: Ramada Inn Boston
title: “ramanda”
text: was a good place too stay, its a wee bit out of the town on the train.

name: Courtyard Boston-South Boston
title: “COMODO”
text: Camere spaziose e confortevoli; ottima soluzione per famiglie di 4 persone (la camera con 2 queen bed è molto conveniente). Piscina disponibile, anche se piccola. Lo shuttle gratuito dall'albergo porta direttamente alla fermata della metropolitana (anche al ritorno) in 10 minuti. Breakfast ottimo e a prezzi accettabili (US$ 11 per adulti - US$ 7 per i bambini). Dintorni un po' tristi, con ristoranti e centro commerciale a 5 min. a piedi. Senz'altro consigliabile. Prezzo solo camera, senza breakfast, US$ 209 + tax.

name: Hyatt Regency Boston
title: “Good stay but noisy”
text:
Great looking hotel, though rather confusing lobby. Good location. Great views of the River, if you get a river view room (I had booked a river view room, but they gave me a non-view room without warning - when I brought it to their attention they reduced my rate to the regular room for the first night, and then I moved the second night)
The big caveat being that the central well of the hotel transmits a lot of noise, and this hotel tends to host noisy conventions. So get a room that is away from the central well, and definitely not near the elevators.
Otherwise the service is good, restaurant is average, beds are great. Would recommend.

name: Boston Hotel Buckminster
title: “Historic building, clean rooms and superb location!”
text: This is a beautiful, old hotel in the heart of Fenway park district. We stayed here one night and went to see the parks and the Gardner museum the next day. Parking was very reasonably priced ($28 overnight until check-out) and right next to the hotel. The staff was friendly and the building and room were gorgeous. That being said, it is an OLD building so it won't have the fancy, modern look that some people prefer. Also, the hot water took quite a bit of time to make it to our room - we had to run the tap for about 15 minutes to get it flowing at first. But the staff said that was normal and were very helpful about it. I also really appreciated the microwave and mini-fridge in the room. The Buckminster is a slice of history in an area that is gentrifying quickly - I recommend a stay at this wonderful hotel.

name: Onyx Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “I thought the place was great for young couples”
text:
We stayed at the Onyx hotel over the Feb 5, 2010 weekend. I thought the room was small, but well spaced, with a comfortable size bathroom. We went with another couple and they gave us the corner rooms which aloud us to lock the outer doors, while keeping our inner doors open for easy passage.
On the second night as we came into our room, we smelled smoke coming from one of the vents, as neither of us are smokers, we immediately reported this to the front desk, and advised them of our concern, as well as concerned for being charged.
They sent someone up to examin the issue, and felt it was nothing serious.
After reading some posts I am slightly concerned that they may try and charge us for this, but I feel reasonable good that this wont happen.
I don't believe there is a deep cleaning scam as I don't see how it would benefit employees. Maybe the hotel itself. But as an employee if you are asked to do this, which it is illegal, that would be a great lawsuit for them.
Anyways assuming over the next week, we do not get charged for the deep cleaning, then I will certainly go back.

name: Courtyard Boston Downtown / Tremont
title: “No way, too expensive and not at all rest-material”
text:
Whenever I go on a business trip I chose a hotel to sleep and rest in. This one was offered by the show I was attending but it was horrible. 
I thought "Marriott means good quality" but absolutely not. First, we arrived very late [past midnight] and when we got to our room it was two doubles, so we called in and asked for a king size [i went with my husband] and they moved us [which was ok] BUT the real problem began... it was IMPOSSIBLE to sleep!!!!!! 
There were compressors buzzing the WHOLE night!! I had an early meeting at the show and didn't sleep AT ALL!!!!!!! We asked to be moved from the room but they told us next morning they would, and they gave us the SMALLEST room ever.
I would NEVER EVER book this hotel again... the room was small, the towels were old and seemed dirty, the bathroom had mold - VERY OLD very ugly 
It was a horrible experience.. i thank god it was just for 2 nights..

name: BEST WESTERN University Hotel-Boston/Brighton
title: “Great tourist value”
text: We booked the Best Western Terrace Inn as a $99.per night special from a GO Boston card I ordered online through their tourism dept. I called a few days in advance to reserve; it really was only $99. per night. It was right on the green line, although almost at the outside edge, near Boston Univ. West. But in 25 min., you were downtown! No driving! Free parking, okay rooms, free "expanded" continental breakfast (waffles, cereal, fruit, etc. A wonderful Spanish restaurant was around the corner. Friendly staff. For the price, we were able to stay an extra day! The Marriot at the Embarcadero charges $40. per day just to park!

name: Boston Hotel Buckminster
title: “Good hotel which is well located”
text: I wasn't expecing much from this hotel but I was pleasently surprised. I booked a twin room and it turned out to have it's own living room which came in handy as we needed to add an extra bed which the staff were very helpful with. Also the location is good, it's 5 mins from Fenway park which is good for baseball fans. Also it's only about a 15 min walk into the main bar / restaurant street and this is an easy and pleasent walk. I really enjoyed boston and am thinking of going back and would stay at the Buckminster again. It's a good hotel which offers value for money. Breakfast is very basic though.

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Definently be back”
text: We just got back today from a weekend getaway to Boston. We drove 4 hours from upstate New York and stayed at the Sheraton Boston Hotel. The hotel was easy to find right off of I-90, pretty much 2 turns and you're there. Valet parking for the car (valet parking was a bit much, $44 per day) and quick check in. The rooms were clean and in very good shape. The area it's in is very nice. The Prudential center is hooked up to the hotel which made it nice for shopping or eating. There is a full 24 hour grocery store right around the corner with all the wine, beer or liquor you want. The best part was the subway was at the end of the block, and you had to walk by the Cheesecake Factory to get there! I would absolutely recommend this hotel for it's location and easy access. Everything you would need is right there.

name: Boston Hotel Buckminster
title: “Beware... Mattress equals a backache !!”
text:
I stayed at the famous Buckminster Hotel in the past, I love the history of the Hotel, the fact that it faces the "Green Monsta" at Fenway Park, if requested as we did. Yes, there is a bit of street noise...you are real close to Boston University. Ther area is goregeous... Public garden down the street etc ...
The room? ok .... very clean, kitchenette, 2 t.v's. The problem? Well, the bed sagged in the middle and was intolerable. It was noticed about 3 am as we were woken with unreal back pain. I brought this to the attention of the clerk the next morning. her response? " Well, we are replacing the mattresses room by room. My reply " So, at that reat, it will be 2013 until all rooms are done ?" Well, her look alone could have killed.
My next comment was " I'm going to trip advisor to notify others of the lousy mattresses." Her reply" You gotta do whatcha gotta do"
Well... there ya go ... lousy RERPONSE !!
The hotel is nice, clean. The location is great.
The matresses suck and they DO NOT APOLOGIZE FOR THAT ... NOT EVEN CLOSE !!

name: Constitution Inn
title: “This place is a dump.”
text: We were initially assigned to a top floor with a sloped ceiling. Since we're both very tall we requested a change. The second room was not the best, but better. After dropping our bags off we took the shuttle downtown for a bite to eat. Upon returning and getting ready for bed, I notice that the sheets had hair on them. Upon further examination there was also pubic hair on the sheets. I called the front desk to complain and the matter was immediately addressed, but the fact that I had to deal with this was horrible. Later that night the latch on the toilet broke. We had to open the top and pull the chain to flush it. We decided to wait till morning to report it because we already felt like we were trouble makers. We did so lst thing the next morning and it turned into a nightmare. The maintenance worker was late to work and when he did come he told the front desk it would be another hour. I was later told that he had to go and buy a part to fix it. To be fair we were offered another room (dingy and facing a brick wall) which we declined and offered an additional nights stay for free. Honestly, I wouldn't stay there again if it were free for a month. The place needs a major upgrade and little things like finger prints on the elevator walls made it feel dumpy and dirty. On top of that it's some kind of shelter/residence for families. I couldn't get the full story about this, but it was absoulutey the worst place I've stayed in my life. If we didn't have basketball tickets I would have checked out immediately. NEVER AGAIN.

name: Onyx Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Onyx was fab”
text: We made our first trip in to Boston in July and stayed at the Onyx - we were not disappointed! The staff was wonderful, as was our room. We were in town for the Eagles at the TD Banknorth and the location was excellent - we were a stone's throw from the Arena. Everyone was so friendly, it was incredible. Our room was beautifully appointed and our floor was very quiet. We enjoyed a wonderful stay at the Onyx and would definitely recommend it to anyone staying in Boston. We will most certainly stay again and are looking forward to returning.

name: The Fairmont Olympic Seattle
title: “Luxury Lodging”
text: From the start it was apparent that the employees were friendly and attentive. We were amazed at the professionalism of every member of the hotel staff. The rooms were spacious and up to date. Overall a very relaxing stay at a wonderful hotel.

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Great hotel!”
text: We found a great deal for this hotel. The location was good. The rooms were very clean and nice. Elevators were really fast. The staff was nice including the concierge. It is attached to the Prudential Center with plenty of shopping. Great place to stay while in Boston!

name: Bulfinch Hotel Boston
title: “A New Gem in Boston”
text:
I stayed here over the weekend. The rooms are compact but well decorated and designed; my room had a spacious bathroom with a large shower stall. The decor is modern and not overdone.
The only criticism I can make is that the vending/ice machines had not been installed on my floor yet. 
The price ($154) was well worth it in my opinion. The hotel is only 3 short blocks from North Station; you can walk to the station in under 3 minutes. Fanueil Hall is a 5-8 minute walk.

name: Hilton Boston Logan Airport
title: “AMAZING HOTEL”
text:
I was in Boston for one night and I am so glad I stayed here. The staff was excellent!! Everyone was so professional and it made me feel at home. The rooms were spotless, and all the public areas were immaculate. It is great to see such a big hotel being kept after so well.
I also ate in their restaurant, Connolley's. The food was fantastic and the service was great. All around this hotel certainly deserves a 5-rating. There is no other hotel I would rather stay in Boston than this one!

name: Milner Hotel
title: “No Room, Even with Confirmation”
text: Arrived around 8pm with confirmation number in hand, and were told that our "reservation had been cancelled". And, that they were booked and could not accomodate us. And, made very little effort to try to help us find a room in a supposedly "all booked" city. Milnor claimed that Hotels.com cancelled our reservation, but we have no record of that. Terribly disappointed. Looked old and dumpy, anyway, so it was probably for the best.

name: Hyatt Regency Boston
title: “Hyatt Great Experience Once Again.”
text: We completed our stay yesterday and were very happy once again. We stayed at this hotel two times prior to this trip. The staff from the manager Kristy Cotton to the housekeeping staff and everyone in between were courteous and helpful. The hotel is located in a good spot with the t stops, shopping, and the Market close to the hotel. The hotel has beautiful old oil paintings in antique frames, waterford lighting fixtures that lend an elegeant flair to the hotel. Room service was prompt, very courteous and the food was good and hot. The restaurant Avenue One was great quality food at a fair price with excellent, excellent attentive service(Jason I had to mention you.) The pool area is a big hit with our kids, unfortunately this time we hit a snafu with the pool being closed for part of our stay due to the inconsideration of a parent of a child using it. The beds are heavenly, the rooms are very clean and spacious. Parking is expensive, but isn't it expensive EVERYWHERE in Boston? The hotel concierge is excellent and patient. Everyone of their staff took the time to explain different attractions and directions to me. The front desk staff bent over backwards for us(Natalie and Lisa we must mention you too,). I would stay at this hotel in the future once again without hesitation.

name: Boston Marriott Copley Place
title: “Comfortable, good location”
text: It is a great hotel, well located, with nice views of the city. The beds are so so cosy that you get great sleep! There is a Starbucks downstairs what is very convenient as breakfast is not included. A good option in Boston

name: Embassy Suites Boston Logan Airport
title: “Pool and restaurant were highlights of the trip”
text:
Our suite was nicely laid out and clean. The pull-out couch was average, not great but provided a decent night's sleep and having the door between rooms was useful as one of our party had a 4 am departure and didn't need to wake the others to get out.
The pool and hot tub were clean, well lit and pleasant. The water in the pool wasn't as disgustingly warm as hotel pools often are, so it was quite refreshing.
The restaurant was certainly the most special thing for us. We were exhausted from a very long day of appointments, athletics and sightseeing, so got dinner at the hotel restaurant just to avoid having to drive, and we were very happily surprised. We had not one but two attentive servers who took our orders quickly and with a really pleasant attitude. The seafood pasta (which all three of our party ordered) was ample, fresh and delicious. The weekend up to that point had been characterized by mediocre food and indifferent service at other places in Boston (including our hotel the night before) so we were thrilled with the experience at the Embassy Suites.
The shuttle bus to the airport was great as well, for the above-mentioned 4am departure. It runs every 15 minutes round-the-clock so no need to even reserve it! I highly recommend this place for a restful night before a flight. I only wish I could have stuck around for the breakfast...

name: The Inn at Longwood Medical
title: “Game night stay”
text: We stayed overnight here after a Red Sox game and I have to say that this hotel is one of the cleanest hotel I have ever been in. The staff was extremely friendly and courteous and I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone staying in the area, you definitely will not be disappointed.

name: Boston Marriott Copley Place
title: “Great Location and excellent hotel”
text:
Usual high standards from the Marriott, great location for down down, parks, theatres, bars, restaurants and the harbour.
Standard rooms have 2 double beds with all the usual things you'd find in an Amarican hotel room ie tv with many channels, ac, desk and chair, iron & ironing board etc
Hotel has a great sports bar which is alway busy and a quieter bar where you can relax. Food in the restaurant is good and reasonably priced or if you prefere a short walk on to Broylsdon St or Nwebury street for a great choice of bars and restaurants.
Hotel has a good gym with many machines and fre weights and ihas an ndoor pool area.
Hotel is very close to the T (underground train) which is cheap, safe and reliable.
Free wifi in reception.

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Great Service”
text: Stayed here on a business trip for 4 nights. However, as a package deal internet was free but I wasn't able to connect it from my room but was able to connect from the lobby. Other than that, everything else went very smoothly and didn't have any issues.

name: The Inn at Longwood Medical
title: “Bachelor Party”
text: Bunch of us stayed downtown the night of our buddy's bachelor party. It's actually the second time I've stayed at this hotel (despite living in area) and genuinely have no complaints. The staff was always professional and very service oriented. The location is perfect for getting anywhere in the city and the accomodations are superior for the price. Highly recommended.

name: Hyatt Regency Boston
title: “Mitten in der City”
text:
Vor allem die Lage ist das überzeugende Argument des Hyatt Regency Boston.
Viele Geschäfte, Restaurants, Boston Common, Market Street, Long Warf, Aquarium, Beacon Hill, etc sind in wenigen Gehminuten erreichbar.Zur sehr schönen Newburry Street geht man durch den Park in ca 15 Min.Das Hotel entspricht nicht dem Standard den ich von einem Hyatt Regency erwarte und kenne.Trotzdem ist alles gepflegt, sauber und gut ausgestattet.Die Angestellten sind alle sehr freundlich und kompetent.Das Frühstücksbuffet ist sehr abwechslungsreich und qualitativ sehr gut.Als Alternative empfehle ich die Brueggers Bagel Bakery 5 Min vom Hotel entfernt.

name: Hilton Boston Logan Airport
title: “Convenient Airport Hotel, standard hilton fare, nothing exception, solid.”
text: As far as airport hotels go, this is definitely a solid top notch, as a general hotel for Boston, it's a good 3* in my view. The room was spacious, however didn't receive a suite upgrade even though i was only there for 10 hours and there were suites available and i checked in around 11pm. The room was nice and comfortable. With a lazy chair and view of the airport, Nice and quiet. They observed my request for a quiet room away from elevator. The breakfast service in the lobby was lack luster, and the food average for hilton standards. I ended up having to go to the desk to get my check! The gym was superb, with a pool and jacuzzi - love it. This hotel will now be my preferred choice when travelling from logan and avoiding the commuter traffic in the mornings. The gym and pool and jacuzzi cap it off. Appreciate if they treated diamonds better with an upgrade. Had to pay $25 for breakfast downstairs as diamond! And the bellboy was grumpy i had to leave my extra luggage for 3 days whilst i travelled inter-state. And said it wasn't allowed but grudginly accepted. The checkout lady was very nice and checkin was superfast. Overall I'd give this property a 3-3.5 if it was off airport, but because it's connected to the airport (the only in logan) the great gym, efficient desk agents, i will score it a 4. Appreciate if the hotel could start upgrading diamonds to suites if available... then upon my next stay they will definitely get a 5, if not, my review will be a 3, it should be offered if available! We will see... ;-) it is quite pricey, but this is Boston.

Address: '240 Mount Vernon Street at Bayside Center'
name: DoubleTree Club by Hilton Hotel Boston Bayside
title: “Doubletree club by Hilton hôtel Boston bayside”
text:
Hôtel et chambre de bon standing, agréable, dommage que le wifi et le parking ne soient pas compris dans le prix de la chambre,le petit déjeuner est moyen. l hôtel est excentré, mais le métro est vraiment a 2mn a pied de l'hôtel et c'est très pratique, il vaut mieux ne pas aller a Boston en voiture le prix des parkings est très élevé en général 10$ l'heure, Boston n'est pas une très grande ville la visite est facilement faisable à pied.
Nous recommandons donc cet hôtel à ceux pour qui ne tiennent pas particulièrement a être en centre ville.

name: Boston Marriott Copley Place
title: “Couldn't have chosen a better hotel!”
text: Stayed at the Boston Marriott Copley hotel for four days in August, 2012. Hotel is easily accessible, wonderfully situated. Attached to Prudential Center shopping, within walking distance of Boston Public Library (must see), Trinity Church and the snazzy shopping/dining district of Newberry Street, the hotel couldn't have been better. Staff was extremely accommodating and concierge knowledgable. I was traveling alone with my 17 year old daughter, so I wanted a place where I would feel safe! Walked into the Prudential center for a lovely Sunday mass at the chapel within the shopping center. Hotel is also within walking distance of Northeastern University (reason for our visit) and the Museum of Fine Arts. Accommodations in the room itself were just wonderful . . . fluffy down comforters provided wonderful night's sleep. The hotel is spanking clean, restaurants within for breakfast, Starbucks on the second floor and other great dining right there. Also, Shaw's supermarket is directly across the street for water, Dunkin Donuts coffee and, if you would like, breakfast items. Great muffins!!!! All in all, a terrific Boston visit.

name: Onyx Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Very Pleasant Stay”
text: We stayed at the Onyx Hotel September 23 - 26, 2004 and had a wonderful stay. The free continental breakfast and wine tastings were a real treat. The Onyx is on the same street as Au Bon Pain - great for coffee in the morning, several pubs and sports bars. It is also only two blocks from the North End T station - very convenient. The rooms were stylish, new and clean. I loved the bed with its goose down comforter--it was sooo comfortable. Overall a great stay at a great price (through Travelocity). The only reason I gave this hotel four out of five stars was that its not closer to the tourist attractions like Fanueil Hall and Freedom Trail, however is within walking distance of the North End.

name: W Boston
title: “Room not cleaned at all”
text: The staff were nice, opened doors, smiled but when my room was not cleaned at 7pm I got upset- the hotel is gorgeous but the maid service is subpar( there were room service dishes outside our room until 6:30pm from morning and as mentioned our room was never cleaned.

name: W Boston
title: “On the expensive side but cleanliness, hipness and location are all included.”
text: Stayed here 5 or more times. Always consistent W quality in rooms, staff, etc. Walk to everything in Boston. High energy as expected from W, but no complaints.

name: Taj Boston
title: “Absolute best location and service!”
text:
The staff at the Taj Boston are among the most helpful and courteous of any hotel in America. This is the "Old" Ritz-Carlton, located just across from the Boston Public Garden and right on Newbury Street. The Taj management has maintained the charm of the original building but greatly improved a few things, like housekeeping, updated interiors of rooms and added authentic Indian ovens & chefs for some delicious Indian food. The Chicken Pot Pie is still on the menu, for those like me who have grown up eating it here.
The feeling upon arrival is one of sincere welcome. The size of the hotel is large enough to employ a depth of staff and management but the feel is intimate. A great contrast to other Luxury hotels in Boston (others have the feel of an airport terminal or convention building to me). 
The Taj Bar is superb! It is like an English smoking room (no smoking, of course) with a nice selection of sandwiches and full courses. Breakfast in it is buffet ("All proper Englishman serve themselves breakfast"). The waitstaff are wonderful.
