When I am out of town, I like to view my dogs on a web cam. I had difficulty doing this on the computers in the Business Center (brand new Macs & an HP - huge screens & printers that work, by the way). Although it was late at night, an IT person was summoned and arrived about 40 seconds later. As soon as I explained my problem, he had downloaded and installed the software needed and we were both viewing my miniature Dachshunds frolicking happily at home. What wonderful service!
Of all the areas of the hotel that are truly outstanding is housekeeping. Perhaps one of the most under-appreciated areas because if it is adequate, no one complains that much and if it is good, it is expected. However, when it is absolutely outstanding it should be noted. In an older building like this one, there are many areas that require additional attention and it is much more difficult to keep things going perfectly. They do it here. Every single crystal on every light fixture is clean and polished; I cannot get my own housekeeper to get this done in my home! There is not a speck of dust anywhere. When this was the Ritz-Carlton, I always noticed dust in the vents and on top of the light bulbs in the lamps, and all the light fixtures had a covering of dust - as I live in a building of the same era, I know how difficult it is to keep dust from gathering. So I decided to inspect the rooms more closely. Not one speck of dust - anywhere. This makes for a much better air quality and cuts down on a lot of allergies. Hotels that say it cannot be done are wrong: somehow they got it done here.
Also, the bathrooms are recently redone on a beautiful beige stone with top of the line fixtures. The make up mirrors and all amenities are first class.
Room service is prompt and good. 
Bed and bath linens are first class. 
For a stay in Boston, this is my #1 recommendation for a Luxury Hotel.
NOTE: Just as in all buildings of this era in Boston, your iPhone will not work when in the hotel. It is the same in the salons and shops along Newbury Street. There is internet access both in the rooms and in the top of the line Business Center, and your iPhone will work for email, messaging, etc., just not phone calls.

name: Hilton Boston Downtown / Financial District
title: “Great service " by request"”
text: Couldn't praise service of Wyndham by Request manager enough. I had a need to aquire stair access as I don't like lifts and was e-mailed personally on more than one occasion and asssured that this would not be a problem. The hotel is beautiful, central and the service is special. Thanks for making an apprehensive stay wonderful!!

name: The Inn at Longwood Medical
title: “Reservation Process”
text: I have stayed there before and It was great when you need to be close to Beth Israel or Boston Children's Medical. Staff is very Friendly especially Jose the Bell/ Travel person. However, the reason for this post is that I need to return with my Dad who has Alzheimers and I needed a room on the same, floor. Noah, the reservation agent listened to what I was saying and even though I say this all the time I travel, I did not expect he responce I got. He validated my concern and said he would make sure that we had ajoining rooms so that I did not need to worry. It was a great expirience and I feel Noah went out of his way to make sure I was safe and my Dad would be safe as well. I would highly recommmend this hotel to anyone. I feel comfortable there and the satff is truly genuine and unique. Cheers

name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport
title: “Great service at a great location”
text:
Our first impression was of the fantastic harbor view. Our room was very good though it had an airport view. There was no problem with airport noise. The restaurant had excellent food (try the chowder and the lobster omelet). There is access to a water taxi that will bring you to the North End for a great price.
The best part is the service. The staff consistently went out of the way to ensure that we were happy. They are the biggest reason for the great review!

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “Good business hotel in a convenient location”
text:
Stayed here for 3 days and had no complaints - the room size is fine, the room service quick and overall pretty good, the staff friendly and helpful. The location is not central BUT the next train station is across the street, the tour bus stops right in front of the hotel, the Convention center is next door, and the airport shuttle leaves across the street as well (Silver line bus). 
From here you can walk to many places, if the weather permits. Also, dining options are close-by or can be reached in a short time.

name: Taj Boston
title: “Conveniently Located Boutique Style Hotel”
text: This hotel is well located just south of the Boston Common and close to the Back Bay area. The welcome from the desk seemed genuine and friendly and all staff showed a frienly and corteouse manner. Extras such as chocolates every night made it even more special. The room was well furnished and extremely comfortable. Only negataive was the room looked out over other hotel rooms. Ate at the hotel restaurant and found it excellent, great food and excellent service. The Cheers bar is only 200 metres away and is worth a visit if you were a fan.

name: Holiday Inn Boston at Beacon Hill
title: “Ottima scelta per visitare Boston!”
text:
Questo hotel a Beacon Hill è un ottimo punto di partenza per la visita della stupenda città di Boston! Da qui, a piedi potete praticamente arrivare in qualsiasi punto della città oppure prendere la metropolitana nella vicina stazione.
Se siete in macchina preparatevi a una botta da 50 dollari al giorno per il parcheggio, infatti l'hotel è a due passi dall'ospedale, immaginate voi il traffico.
Le stanze sono comunque insonorizzate e abbastanza grandi, preferite magari 2 letti queen.
Bello il bagno con vasca e doccia. Pulizia buona.
WiFi gratuito e veloce, personale cordiale.
Se prenotato con buon anticipo potrete strappare un buon prezzo, comunque molto alto, come in tutte le grandi città della East Coast.

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “Very nice hotel!!”
text: This hotel is a very nice property to stay. It is very close to the World Trade Center station (5 minute walk) of the transit system so makes getting around Boston very convienent. Highly suggest getting a Charlie pass and get around on transit system - one cab ride will be more than the $15 7-day pass! Downside is that it is away from any restaurants and the main downtown areas, but a quick transit ride and 10 minute walk will get you to downtown. I would recommend this hotel to anyone.

name: Boston Marriott Copley Place
title: “Modern hotel, great location.”
text: Travelled to Boston for a weekend break and stayed in the Marriott in Copley Place, had a very nice stay. Hotel staff extremely friendly and very willing to help with any enquiry, always said hello and good morning etc. The room was very spacious and modern, bed was amazingly comfortable and the room seemed to of had a recent refurbishment. Bathroom also very nice, clean and spacious with towels and toiletries provided. The hotel's facilities are also fantastic, the pool/gym area was very clean and up to date, there was a fantastic view over the city from the pool/gym area. Hotel is situated right next to a mall which is connected to the hotel and there is also a mall opposite which is connected via walkway bridge. The hotel has its own Starbucks which was great for a quick breakfast before exploring. Transport links are very close by and easy to get to, nearest subway is a 2 minute walk away and hotel is a short walk into Copley Square. Would definately recommend this hotel, very relaxing stay :)

name: Hilton Boston Back Bay
title: “Excellent hotel in the Back Bay”
text:
This hotel is located in the most perfect spot! Very short walk to Fenway Park, parking garage is right across the street and the hop on hop off trolly stops at this hotel! In addition, a short stroll to Boylston St and many, many great resturants and shopping!
The hotel is very clean and quiet. The health club and pool is outstanding. There is a Starbucks located inside the hotel and the hotel makes available everyday fresh lemon and water as well as fresh oranges and water to help quench your thirst!
Staff is very friendly and helpful. When I go back to Boston, I will stay here again, no question. Try to get a room on the upper floors, awesome views of the Charles River and Fenway Park!

name: Hilton Boston Back Bay
title: “It was alright”
text: When I checked in the last behind the desk didn't even smile. She did not look happy to be here. I ordered room service and guy that brought it up was really nice. However the chicken wings were under cooked and it made me very sick. So do not order the chicken wings. My boyfriend. Went for a walk to see if that would help my stomach, which it did but my phone died in the middle of the walk. When I got back to the hotel I asked for a charger. Maria at the desk said they didn't have any iPhone chargers but she would let me use her personal one. She is the saving grace for this hotel! That made my night.

name: W Boston
title: “Quite Expensive for 'Just Ok'”
text: We recently styaed one night at the W, after attending a private party at the hotel. The party planners and the staff were amazing but the room and the hotel are not as nice as others in the same area. The lobby is very small and underwhelming for the calibre of hotel. Most of the space is dominated by the bar/nightclub which was a zoo after dark. The check in desks seem like an afterthought, tucked in behind the club. The room was fine except for the lighting. The lighting in the bathroom was almost nonexistent and when we returned to the room after the party at 1am, only one of the bathroom lights came on. When we checked out, I was told that we were doing the lights "wrong" and that we must not have had the master switch on. That would have been impossible since the one dim light in the middle of bathroom came on, but none of the others. Anyway, the bed was comfy and the Bliss bath products are awesome but the hotel on the whole is just not worth the cost. If you're going to spend that kind of money in Boston, go around the corner to the Ritz or to the Four Seasons.

name: Taj Boston
title: “Very pleasant stay”
text:
Just returned from a 4 night city break in Boston, staying at the Taj, we were a bit sceptical about the Taj given some of the recent more negative reviews on TA.
In Summery
Location is great
We had no problems checking in
Staff were attentive without being overbearing
Room was very large, with a good size bathroom, if a little dated in it's decoration, YES our view was not great, but we dont spend our days staring out of the bedroom window! We ate in the bar and took tea at 4 o'clock (we are afterall ENGLISH) also in the bar, can have no complaints.
Overall a positive experience for us.

name: Onyx Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Me encantó el hotel, pero sobretodo el servicio !!”
text: Me encantó el Onyx hotel desde que lo ví por primera vez en internet, decidimos quedarnos ahí y fué una experiencia maravillosa !! por otras críticas ( aquí en tripadvisor ) supe que los cuartos eran muy pequeños y no se equivocaron !! jajaja pero suficientes para nosotros dos ! Las personas en el Front Desk no pudieron ser más amables en todo momento ... eso fue lo mejor !!

name: The Midtown Hotel
title: “Loved the Midtown”
text: Just back from Boston, stayed at the Midtown for 9 nights I could not fault it. The rooms are clean, the beds are very comfortable,plenty space in the room, asked for a room at the back and it was very quiet. The staff were helpful at all times. Its in a great location, there are three T stations nearby.The nearest for breakfast is Thorntons. Its ok , got sick of all the eggs on the menu.Plenty restaurants within 10 mins walk on Newbury Street and visit Uno on Boylston Street for dinner.

name: Taj Boston
title: “Nice but no free Internet”
text: I could not give more than three stars because it makes me crazy when hotels charge for the Internet. Our room was spacious, comfortable, and clean and the bed was excellent. The location is great right near shopping and the commons.

name: Hilton Boston Back Bay
title: “Good value, good area”
text:
Ive stayed in a variety of hotels in Boston, and this is a good one I would return to. Its fairly generic, could use some updating in the common areas but its very comfortable and standard comfortable Hilton quality. Its very near the convention center, backbay, the malls (prudential) and good and $$ dining on Newbury st. The windows open a little as well, which is nice if you want some good fresh Beantown air. I had a high room so noise was no issue. Not sure what the lower floors would be like. Good view!
If you dont want to hit the ample fitness room, go for a run to Cambridge and backbay. You'll be happy. Enjoy Boston

name: Onyx Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Wonderful hotel”
text:
My husband & I spent Thanksgiving Weekend at the Onyx Hotel. We were very pleased with every aspect of the hotel. The service was wonderful.
The staff was very helpful & accommodating. The room was very comfortable especially the bed. We took advantage of the free breakfast.
There were more than enough food choices. The only disadvantage (which I understand is common in Boston) is that the parking was expensive and offsite. When we wanted out car we had to call the bellstaff to get it for us.
They did not keep us waiting but we found it inconvenient to say the least.
Location was good for the T and shopping mall was a short drive away.
Do not hesitate to stay at the Onyx. You won't be disappointed.

name: Onyx Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Hip and Cool”
text:
I stayed at the Onyx during a week-long vacation to the Boston area. 
It is a very hip hotel. Walking into the lobby, there's a dj spinning in the bar-area, adding a fun atmosphere to the place. 
The rooms are modern and very clean. They are a little small, but when you're in a place like Boston, you're not doing much in there except sleeping. It is also very quiet. My room was near the elevator and I never heard it.
The service was fantastic. The front desk staff was especially friendly and helpful. I would definitely stay there again.

name: Boston Hotel Buckminster
title: “Hervorragend”
text: Ein schönes Hotel in verkehrstechnisch guter Lage (Hihgway, U-Bahn) zu einem annehmbaren Preis. Direkt neben dem Baseballstadion. Wir hatten eine Suite mit Kingsizebett, einfaches, ausreichendes kontinentales Frühstück und einen super freundlichen und hilfsbereiten Service. Dose Bier kann man im China Restaurant bekommen, sonst in MA schwierig.

name: Boston Hotel Buckminster
title: “Due giorni a Boston”
text: Un buon hotel con stanze spaziose e prezzi accessibili a Boston. Non vicinissimo al centro ma ben servito dalla metropolitana e posizionato in una zona molto tranquilla. Di buona qualità e varia la colazione.

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “A Great Stay”
text: Our stay in Boston was awesome and this hotel was the icing on the cake. We spent 4 nights here. Although this hotel is not exactly on the water, you can see the beautiful view of the harbor from your window. The first thing you notice when you walk in is the aroma of the hotel, it's delish. I wish I could bottle it up and take it home. Check in was quick and accurate. Room service was prompt and accurate. The room was spacious and very clean. We had no problems whatsoever. The drawback to this hotel as for many in the area, parking is outrageous $40+/night. One would think, as a guest you would get a discount. If it all possible take public transportation, its very fast and easy to understand.

name: Hilton Boston Downtown / Financial District
title: “Fun time”
text:
We stayed at the Wyndham Feb 13-15. Had a great time!! The Concerige was great and more than helpful!! The room was clean and great view!! 
Great location for Quincy Market and the harbor! Would stay again!!

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “Great place to stay”
text:
Spent 4 nights there this week and it was very nice. Had a convention in the center and it was a quick walk through the sky bridge attaching both buildings. I had the top floor (16th) so the views of the city and the sunsets were very nice. 
The Westin is close enough to the city but a short taxi or subway away. Fanuiel Hall was $7.80 taxi (no tip). Went to Fenway for about $20. The Silver line for the subway is just a short walk over the bridge. 
Rooms were good and I always sleep well on their beds. 
If you eat at hotel, don't bother with the MJ O'Connor's. You can do a short walk to the waterfront for much better places. 
If you want really BAD service, eat at the Birch Bar which is the lobby bar. I had dinner one day and lunch another. Different bartenders and servers each time but just as horrible each time. The best was actually room service which pleasantly surprised me. Very efficient and friendly. I had the pan seared salmon with porcini mushrooms and it was excellent. 
I am SPG Gold so I always enjoy the Westin chain and this was no exception.

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Great Hotel with a Beautiful View”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Sheraton in mid-September and we loved it. We caught the red-eye from LA to Boston so when we got to the hotel at 7:00 AM we planned on just dropping off our bags but they gave us a room early which meant we could relax a little before sightseeing. To top it off, our room even had a beautiful view of the Charles River and MIT.
We like to walk so it didn't seem to far from the old historic part of the town or Harvard University. That being said, if you don't like to walk the subway stop is right around the corner and that is really easy to use, even to the airport or train station.
Also we booked this room though HotWire and got this as the 3 1/2 Star selection for Back Bay.
The only negative expierence we had with the hotel was with the employees at Starbucks (located in the lobby) who were rude and tried to overcharge us (twice).

name: Milner Hotel
title: “Me encanto este hotel, muy calido y el desayuno excelente”
text: Me gusto mucho, no hay lujo, el desayuno muy bueno, esta muy bien ubicado, el personal excelente, el precio me resulto bueno, las habitaciones son chicas ,pero muy limpias, verdaderamente falta donde colocar las maletas, pero yo sigo diciendo que me gusto muchooooooooo

name: Holiday Inn Boston at Beacon Hill
title: “You really can't ask for a better location.”
text:
First, this is a Holiday Inn. Don't book a room here expecting the Omni or the W. The rooms are standard, clean, comfortable, and what you would expect for the price point and franchise. I got a reasonable rate on Priceline, even though I booked last minute and on a holiday weekend. The front desk service was great, the valet just as good. The rooms were nothing particularly special, but they were just fine.
I will say, however, the location can't be beat. You're walking distance to Faneuil Hall, a string of (touristy) pubs, Boston Common, State House, Old State House, North End ... the list goes on. You're also very close to two T stops, so you can get to further distances easily (we were in town for a Red Sox game, and this location couldn't have been better for a quick trip to the ballpark).
Overall, we were very happy with our experience here. There were signs in the elevator that suggest a renovation is in progress, so you may stay with an even nicer hotel depending on when you go :)

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “Boston Westin Waterfront - superb”
text: A fabulous stay at this hotel - staff was excellent in accommodating all our needs. Staff went above and beyond to insure that our requests were handled in a timely fashion. I have never stayed at a hotel where EVERY employee was pleasant and helpful.

name: Chandler Inn
title: “Beautiful Neighbourhood Hotel”
text: Lovely updated hotel in beautiful Boston Back Bay area. Minutes walk to Back Bay T station. Surrounded by dozens of fabulous restaurants. Rooms are small but nicely updated. Beds where very comfortable. Staff was helpful and friendly. Definitely would recommend this hotel to friends.

name: Onyx Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “the onyx is great”
text: We stayed at the Onyx for 2 nights. It was perfect ;our room was immaculate,very quiet, spotlessly clean,with a very comfortable bed.But the main plus point was the staff. Nothing was too much trouble for them, and their courtesy, cheerfulness, and efficiency was the best we have ever encountered.We had come from the UK and only had a two night trip, so every minute counted,and the Onyx ensured that it was well worth it.If you are visiting Boston, don't waste time looking at alternatives. This hotel has an excellent position,wonderful rooms, and above all a staff who convince you that you really matter.It wasn't just one or two of them; they were all superb.We are planning our return trip!

name: Hilton Boston Logan Airport
title: “great location to airport”
text: I stayed here with carvan tours and enjoulyed the convenant location to the airport. But there isnt anyrhing else around. Also the bar/restaurant was high and the food wasnt good. We undoubtably was a bother to the waitress to show up.

name: Hilton Boston Downtown / Financial District
title: “Enjoyed the Wyndham”
text: We spent four nights at the Wyndham. Had a lovely big room. Corner view with a plethora of windows. Comfy bed. High floor as asked for in Wyndham by Request. Tea and Coffee a in room a lovely change from most American hotels. Bar was nice. Friendly service. Check in courteous and efficient, just what you neeed after a seven hour flight. Brilliant location. Perfect for an early morning walk to the sea. Please please eat and drink at Mr Dooleys bar next door. Truly superb. A proper Irish bar. Really enjoyed everything about Boston.

name: Chandler Inn
title: “Quite good, didn't disappoint”
text:
Everything was clean, orderly and didn't run into any problems during my 5 nights stay at the Chandler. Yes, the rooms aren't that big but not too cramped that it would've bothered me. The room was clean, the bed was good and didn't hear any noise from the outside throughout my stay.
There's absolutely no common space at the hotel. The rooms don't quite live up to their description on the hotel's website and neither would I call this a "boutique" hotel.
Location is excellent considering the price (and taking into account Boston prices). A short walking distance to the Back Bay station for the T and trains - and not that bad even to downtown or Fenway.
All in all a good experience. Wouldn't quite agree with the 5-star reviews but definitely a solid 4.

name: Chandler Inn
title: “Chandler is great!”
text: Our room was crisp and clean. Modern furnishings, flat screen tv, very comfortable. The bathroom, albeit brand New, is quite small...not an issue for us but may be an issue if a visitor is accustomed to spacious hotel bathrooms. Staff was welcoming and gracious. Walking distance to Tremont and great restaurants. Plenty of offsite parking. Would definitely stay again.

name: The Inn at Longwood Medical
title: “Affordable and close to Fenway and Boston, worth the trip.”
text: We have stayed at this hotel many times for 3-4 times each year when seeing a Red Sox game. For Boston, this hotel is very affordable and close to Fenway and a nice walk to downtown Boston. The staff are always friendly and helpful. check in and check out are also hastle free. I would recommend to anyone.

name: Taj Boston
title: “Thank goodness for James in Concierge”
text:
Having stayed at the Four Season each time we have visted Boston we decided to try the Taj. It is located in a superb location, across the street from Boston Common and centrally located to shops, dining, Fenway and downtown. The hotel was nice and the staff accommodating but I would definitely not rate this a five star hotel! We arrived at 6 a.m. and there was no bellhop or valet at the front door. I don't mind bringing my own luggage in by any means but when you claim to be a five star hotel there should be someone there to greet the guests. This has been my past experience. The young lady at the desk was great and got us settled in our rooms. When we arrived in our room, we did not have a dresser. We were staying for a week and this was unacceptable. I went downstairs and requested a dresser and she stated they would call engineering and deliver one within 30 minutes. 
 Unfortunately, our non-smoking room definitely had a smoker in it prior to our visit. When I went down to the front desk they did tell me they were a non-smoking hotel, which I know, but that certainly does not mean everyone follows the room. My husband, who is severely allergic to smoke and has suffers from asthma, smelled it as soon as he walked in the room. After speaking with a second person, he apologized and did acknowledge that it happens sometimes and some guests don't mind paying the 250 room charge to have the convenience of smoking in their rooms. His solution? Although he was very kind, he offered to have the draperies and carpet steam cleaned, chairs swapped, an air filtration unit and all the linens removed. Smoke sticks to everything- even walls. I told him we would like to change rooms event if it meant us been charged more for an upgrade. He stated there were no rooms available for the next three days and this was the best they could do. This seemed like a lot of work and knowing how much my husband suffers with allergies knew this would be unacceptable. This is where James in concierge comes in. 
He had been working on something for us and I mentioned this to him. He said he would see what he could do and left to speak to a manager. When he returned he told us our room had been changed and they would send a bellhop right away to help move the luggage. I was very grateful!
In addition, James was extremely helpful the entire week with car rental (had the car dropped off and picked up at the hotel), restaurant reservations, tickets and more (took care of billing errors after our stay!). He was a pleasure to work with!
As far as rooms, they are decorated very nice but I will say the same thing a number of reviewers have commented on- the carpets in the rooms are absolutely filthy! There were 3 rooms between friends and family (not including the room we had for 2 hours) and they were all pretty disgusting. You absolutely have to upgrade or you will end up with the view our friends had - staring into rooftop, air conditioning units and windows. I The staff was fine but had it not been for James in Concierge, our hotel stay would have been miserable. Would I stay here again? It would not be my first choice but I would sure miss James!

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “Great location and historic hotel”
text:
I stayed @ The Park Plaza 3 days ago. I loved the stuff. Valet parking was a bit expensif. When We pulled in we were welcomed by Khalid he was nice an curtious. Room service was ok. Overall i would recomend this hotel to my friends.
Jen

name: Hilton Boston Logan Airport
title: “Excellent Airport Hotel”
text: Very convenient to the terminals (either walking or by shuttle), the views from my room were fantastic, the people were always nice and helpful, the morning breakfast was great. Very good experience.

name: Boston Marriott Copley Place
title: “Great family vaca.”
text: I went with my husband and 2 sons, 10 months old and 10 years old. It was perfect! The staff were friendly and accomidating and the room was clean and comfortable. There is so much to do within walk or taxi.

name: W Boston
title: “We wouldn't know...”
text: I had booked a room here back in October on Expedia when my friend qualified for the Boston marathon. My husband and I were looking forward to staying at this hotel for months. We frequently stay at W's and are also starwood preferred guests. We arrived at 3:15 pm, parked the car and went to check in. As soon as I gave the girl at the welcome desk my name, she quickly said "excuse me" and ducked into the back room. I knew that wasn't a good sign! A moment later she returned with a manager who claimed she had been trying to contact me all morning. She told us the hotel was full and they would be sending us to stay at the Westin hotel, 1.5 miles down the road. We were so confused and couldn't believe this was happening. We had a reservation, we were 15 minutes past when check in began, it just didn't make sense. My only guess is that if you book using a third party, you are at the hotels mercy. But I have NEVER heard of such a thing happening, and we were really disappointed. They comped our room at the Westin, but we were 1.5 miles out of the city and had to take cabs EVERYWHERE. We were really upset about what this W hotel did. So lesson learned make sure you book directly with the hotel you are staying at, otherwise you might find yourself shut out even when you have a reservation. So disappointed W Boston!

name: Courtyard Boston Downtown / Tremont
title: “a last resort, unless you want to be close to theaters”
text:
I stayed here on a business trip because there was a huge conference in town and - literally - every other hotel in the area was booked. It was adequate, but I'd only stay here again in similar last-resort circumstances. The location is horrible unless you are going to the theaters - in an up-and-coming area that isn't quite there yet, with hit-and-miss blocks (some feeling rather deserted and sketchy). I didn't have any problem with noise, but it was a Tuesday night and they put me on the top floor facing away from the street. Check-in was pretty good.
The lobby is very pretty - the hotel clearly has some historical legacy - but had a musty natural gas smell. The room was garishly decorated (reds, blues and yellows, with mostly reds) and had very cheap linens. My room was a perfectly decent size - again, perhaps because it was on a higher floor?
The biggest problem I had was with getting a cab - following tips from other reviews, I called downstairs to the bell desk 15 minutes before I needed to leave in the morning, in order to make certain a cab would be there. The phone rang several times, and was finally answered by the front desk. I asked if they would make sure a cab was available for me in 15 minutes, and was told that several cabs were downstairs right then and that they would make certain that there was a cab for me. I went downstairs less than 10 minutes later - no cabs, and when I found a bellman, he obviously had no idea that I had called or talked with the front desk. I waited outside for almost 15 minutes while he tried to find a cab - because of the hotel's location, there aren't many cabs driving by - and finally jumped in a livery car who offered to drive me for a higher price. I ended up late to my meeting because of the poor hotel location and bell/front desk incompetence.

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “nice hotel”
text: We recently stayed at the Boston Park Plaza while in town for the Yankees Red Sox baseball games. The hotel was nice, within walking distance to many great locations in Boston. When we checked in the process was quick and efficient. We had a coupon for a free upgrade so we were given a room on the 15th floor. The room was quaint, but served its purpose. The bathroom was nice, small though. The only downside to the room was the air conditioning. The lowest we could put it on was 64 and it never really cooled down. The parking was valet and a little pricey. We went to the Hotel Bar on Saturday night after the game, it was good, quick and friendly service. The breakfast that was offered on the Tower floor was a different story. There was one young lady working on both days and she didn't have any help. It was busy on Sunday with many families coming in. She tried her best but there was a mess at almost all the tables and the food was almost out of everything. On Monday we thought it might be a little better, but again the poor girl was all by herslef and got crushed with all the people. Finally two guys in suits came to help her but it was very poor, they should have more staff. We would stay here again but a little pricey.

name: Hilton Boston Back Bay
title: “Convenient, clean, and not ridiculously priced”
text: We were in town for a family event and stayed at the Hilton Back Bay with several other family members. The hotel itself is newly remodeled and has nice facilities overall. My only real complaint would be that the elevators can be rather slow and the breakfast at the hotel restaurant is very overpriced. On the positive side, the location can't be beat.

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “Older But Incredibly Convenient”
text: I was completely overwhelmed by the number of areas/places to stay when looking for a hotel for our first trip to Boston, so thankfully my neighbor recommended Boston Park Plaza. You can tell it was once a very grand hotel and has a beautiful lobby. It has been kept up, but the rooms are configured a little strangely. It looks like they eliminated full bathrooms and have replaced them with the smallest shower I have honestly ever seen. I opted for the deluxe room for our family of 4 to be sure we had enough room, but it probably wasn't necessary. The pricing was on the low side for a nice convenient place. Since we weren't in the hotel room that much, the fully functional bathroom and the very comfortable beds were perfect for us. The hotel was really convenient to the Duck tours, the Freedom Trail, lots of restaurants (many were more expensive than we were looking for but we recommend M.J. O'Connors Irish Pub right outside the hotel). And more important than I understood before getting to Boston, the hotel is right across the street from a T stop (Boston's subway), so we were able to take it quickly to the Bunker Hill Memorial and Little Italy (in the north side), to see the Boston Pops one night, and just in case we were too tired to walk back to the hotel after a long day. Just as an aside, if you have never been to Boston it is a very safe feeling city, so I don't think you can really go wrong if you stay in any of the historic areas.

name: Courtyard Boston Downtown / Tremont
title: “Great stay!”
text: After reading reviews of this hotel, I was a little hesitant about staying here. But how wrong the prior reviews were! We had a great time at this hotel. Because there were 5 in our party, we were given a handicapped accessible room. The room was very large with an even larger bathroom. We were on the 10th floor, and aside from an occasional siren (the New England Medical Center is across the street), it was very quiet. The staff couldn't have been nicer and even brought me a fan for the room after they had turned the heat on. The orange line T stop is across the street, or you could walk a few blocks to the green line. There is a great pizza place a block up, and a Dunkin Donuts another block from that. The hotel offered breakfast at a reasonable price even though we didn't take advantage of it. I am a travel agent and paid travel agent rates, but even if I weren't, I would still spend the money to stay here. You can't beat the location or the service!

name: Renaissance Boston Waterfront Hotel
title: “Fancy hotel.....”
text: Fancy hotel, location was convenient to local attractions but not as close as some other places I've stayed. The view was decent, lots of construction and a somewhat obstructed harbor view. The beds were like a cloud. Decent sized room and ample bathroom. Not quite as fancy or large rooms as some other 4.5 or 5 stars I've stayed at in Boston. However, I'm aware I'm just splitting hairs at this point. This place is like out of a magazine. The lobby is so fancy, that I honestly felt awkward walking through it in sneakers. Seriously. Close to Jerry Remy's which is a fun place to eat. Legal Test Kitchen literally footsteps away. Everything in this part of town is so clean it looks like you could eat right off the sidewalk (I didn't, in case you were wondering.)

name: Constitution Inn
title: “Bad Experience”
text: Government discount was nice. Hotel was clean. Staff not overly friendly but found that in other areas of Boston as well. Our rental car was broken into overnight however and it was one of several. Boston police officer that responded didn't even carry forms to fill out a report and was not interested to investigate the other cars damaged as well. Sorry Boston, but you are on our least favorite city and the low part of our trip.

name: Courtyard Boston Downtown / Tremont
title: “Nice hotel, good location, but noisy”
text: Just stayed here while at a nearby conference. They are STILL renovating the lobby, although our newly renovated room was very nice and comfy. I disagree that the location is "dicey" - it's great being so close to Chinatown AND you are smack in the middle of the Theater district, with LOTS of great restaurants very close by. HOWEVER, the hotel room was VERY noisy, what with all the theater crowds and traffic right outside - all night you could hear honking, sirens, crowd noise (from the nightclub downstairs)- they really need to do some extra insulation to block out the noise because it sounds like all that is coming from RIGHT outside your window even on the 12th floor. The other issue I had is that the bathrooms were tiny, with absolutely NO counter in the bathroom (only a pedestal sink...I HATE putting my stuff on the back of the toilet!). However, the staff was VERY nice, coffee in the lobbby in the morning, cookies in the afternoon, FREE high speed internet access, right across from the T-station (although that entrance is NOT always open!) as well as close by to all the theaters, so all in alll it wasn't a bad stay....

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Very good value for money and perfect location.”
text:
We stayed here as it was our first trip to Boston and did not want to be too far out of the city. After reading some of the reviews we were a bit nervous about staying here. However we found the staff to be friendly, the rooms big, especially the bed and to be in great walking distance from the centre of Boston. We would definitely recommend staying here again. The only minor downside and this is the case with most hotels near the city, you have to pay for parking which is $38 for 24 hrs. But there is another car park about 2 mins drive from the hotel which cost $33. The plus of the $38 car park is that you could walk straight from the car park into the hotel lifts to the reception desk. 
We really enjoyed walking the FreedomTrail - a good way to explore the city for first timers. We also went to the Legal Seafood Restaurant - a bit pricey but definitely worth it, it was gorgeous.

name: Boston Marriott Copley Place
title: “Great location and Facilities”
text: This is a great location. The second floor flows directly into a shopping center on the same side of the street and the Prudential Center (across the street) is accessible via an enclosed aerial walkway. There is a very busy Starbucks on the second floor and a large supermarket across the street. There is a T station close by. The rooms are spacious and equipped with refrigerators and are up to the usual high Marriott standard.

name: Renaissance Boston Waterfront Hotel
title: “First Class”
text: This hotel is really beautiful. It is right next to all of the pier activities and restaurants. Within walking distance to the main part of the city as well. Boston is beautiful and this hotel was nicer than the apartment I live in. Spacious, clean, well maintained rooms with shampoo and conditioner from Aveda (nice touch). All staff members were very nice and helpful. This is the only hotel I have ranked with five stars. Can't go wrong here. Only minor complaint is that I could hear my neighbor's door slam at all hours of the night and early morning, but as with any large hotel this is normal.

name: The Midtown Hotel
title: “Hotel buono, in ottima posizione”
text: Sono stato al Midtown Hotel durante il mio ultimo soggiorno a Boston. L'hotel offre servizi nella media, è adatto a persone non troppo esigenti che vogliono utilizzare l'hotel solo come base di appoggio per un viaggio turistico. Le stanze sono comunque molto grandi e hanno tutto ciò di cui si ha bisogno. La posizione è veramente ottima, a due passi dalla fermata della Metro e nel bel quartiere di Prudential. Le camere sono pulite, anche se soprattutto i bagni avrebbero bisogno di una ristrutturazione. In definitiva è un hotel che offre il giusto dei servizi, a prezzi davvero ottimi. Se tornerò a Boston per turismo sicuramente prenderò in considerazione l'ipotesi di tornare qui!

name: Boston Marriott Copley Place
title: “Good Hynes convention site”
text:
As a 24 year elite member of Marriott I have been in a lot of Marriott Hotels around the globe. I had never stayed in this hotel, so this is my first impression. I was put on the Concierge level. One very big gripe I have when a hotel has a lot of convention guests like me during this visit, is that they close the Concierge Lounge and all services associated with it from FridY pm until SundY pm. We are business people at a convention. We are paying the rate, but not getting the service we are paying for. I could care less about the fact the wonderful personnel who take care of the Congierge Lounge need a break on weekend. Use it to train others. The least you can do is to open it and allow access to coffee and soda pop and water. Is that too much to ask, cheap hotel owners?
Now that that's over, know that the location is superb, particularly for shopping and getting to the Hynes without going out in the elements.
The fitness, swimming,spa area has been renovated and is greAt. The rooms are just OK and haven' changed much in the last decade. One of my other peeve is the lack ofnsheets and blankets. You get a comforter which seems to work very well for my spouse, but I have to throw it off as being too hot about 4 times a night. That is why I really stay away when I am alone on trips from Marriott's and got to the lower brands, as they are more comfortable regarding bedding for men who tend to have a very different temperature desire when sleeping.

name: Boston Marriott Copley Place
title: “Average in the heart of Boston”
text:
Copley is the most touristy spot of Boston. With that said, of the myriad of hotels around the Copley area, the choices are abundant. The location of the Boston Marriott Copley Place has been it's prime reason for being filled with guests day 365 days of the year. It's connected to the Prudential building at Copley Place and the the Westin Plaza. It's right smack on Copley where it's a short stroll to most of the best places to see in Boston. The T is right at it's front and back. And even on a day when the weather is at it's worst, you can always run home to the Boston Marriott at Copley because it's so accessible to wherever you're coming from. So that's the good side.
Now the down side. If there's a pet peeve I have, it's carpeting in a room that doesn't offer complimentary slippers. It's unhygienic to have a room covered in dark-colored wall to wall carpeting and there are no complimentary slippers. You can't see all that murk, mug and dirt covering the floor. While I understand they vacuum the carpets each day, it's still not good to have the floor covered with carpets unless you're offering slippers.
There are no added bathroom amenities. With all the other hotels offering better amenities, it's sad that the Marriott has simply Body and Bath lotion, shampoo, conditioner and soap. 
This is also the first time that I've stayed in a hotel that has an envelope in the room for maid service. While it may not be mandatory, it's such a turn off that even the maids require a tip nowadays. Leaving an envelope in the room for tips for a job that is part of the job description is bad taste.
The concierge is cold. Very very cold. They're not the kind of people you would want to ask for help or directions or anything at all. To say they are "impersonal" is being kind. The hotel should be more family and tourist friendly. But you won't get much help from them.
Internet connection is $12.95 a day and they offer no packages for 3 or 5 or 7 days usages. Unless I was living inside the hotel room, this is a complete rip-off! Many hotels all over the world offer internet service for FREE nowadays. The hotel is expensive enough as it is and charging for added internet connection for a few hours at this rate is outrageous. 
Finally, Marriott should strip down the pictures it posts about hotel rooms. Don't get deceived. This is NOT what the rooms look like. They are old, weary and are (I believe) being renovated still. The elevators are enough proof as to the age and state of the hotel. It's too bad that a hotel in this location with this name, sadly has not lived up to expectations.

name: Chandler Inn
title: “Very good accomodations and Amenities”
text:
Loved the Hotel, though there was a strange smell along the corridors, probably humidaty. Nothing that a 5m with the windows opened didn't resolve. Staff very frinedly and helpfull, all was very clean. Free WiFi.
Surely we'll come back.

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “what a surprise”
text: What a surprise the Sheraton was after reading some of the reviews. it would appear there is a massive difference in the rooms, the South tower being the best. Check in was very efficient and the room was lovely, very large with the most comfortable beds ever. The hotel as stated is in a fantastic location and the Wrentham Village outlet is well worth a visit for bargain shopping ( the bus picks up outside). The hotel bar is a little pricey ( not helped by the current dollar rate) but is a nice place to relax after a busy day shopping. There is a number of restaurants close by. A cab from the airport to the hotel can be cheaper than the shuttles depending what time of the day you go. If it is not rush hour it is just under $30.

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “I have expected more for the money.!”
text:
First time in Boston, didn't know the areas, booked a hotel first in the worst part of city (Malden)Decided to pay even more for a better area and hotel. Not knowing that beside the location this hotel was even worse with aminities, you pay extra for Wifi in the room, no refrig or mini bar no microwave in the room.
On top of that the mattress was bulged in the middle and stained, my disc problems got even worse, and I end up laying on the floor. There was no ventilator in the bathroom, the color is peeling off in the room and bathroom. I have asked for a better room, with the better mattress, or chane of the mattress. I was giving an option of lower level room, even worse, good that I have checked the room before moving my stuff with my back pain etc. Not worth for the money.

name: Hilton Boston Back Bay
title: “Convenient to Northeastern University”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for just a night when we took Marshall to his freshman orientation at Northeastern. This hotel is nicely located just a few blocks away from the campus, so it was an ideal location for us. You can walk to the Fens and Fenway Park, as well as the restaurants on Boylston and Newbury streets.
This hotel is pretty standard for a Hilton. Biggest complaints about the hotel are small bathroom and no free wifi in the room (they do have computers downstairs in the lobby though). We were hoping for an early check-in and left our bags with the hotel, along with our cell phone number, but they never called us. Wound up checking in at the usual time. Hope that's not an indication of what service is like at this hotel, as given its location, we'll probably wind up staying here a number of times over the next few years.

name: Hilton Boston Back Bay
title: “Great location”
text: Loved the location.could walk to Fenway. Subway was conveniet. Their breakfast was very good. Their staff was very helpful. First time to Boston and would definitely go back here

name: Hilton Boston Logan Airport
title: “A little soul-less but not bad”
text:
I stayed here for three nights to attend a nearby conference. The shuttle picked me up from Logan about 20 minutes after I called which sounds like a long time but the traffic between the hotel and shuttle pick-up area is very congested. I used the free shuttle frequently to get to the subway. It was convenient but many of the drivers drove very aggressively with jack-rabbit starts and hard braking.
Check-in was fine. Overall, the hotel felt a little empty, personality-wise. The executive lounge's evening hors d'oeuvres were mostly fried bits and raw vegetables with standard cheeses. Breakfast had no hot choices which makes it less appealing than a Hampton Inn. It would be nice if this Hilton upgraded the food choices in the executive lounge to match some other Hilton lounges.
The room was acceptable and clean. Nothing special but nothing terrible. 
There were wonderful views of the harbor and airport. As others have mentioned, you hear no airport noise at all from the room.
One tip is to buy a $15 weekly subway pass. It saves a lot of money and is very convenient. The workers at the subway station are helpful and polite.

name: Hilton Boston Logan Airport
title: “Great Location, Nice Hotel. Expensive, However.”
text:
There's a skywalk that connects this hotel with the terminal, which means you can sleep somewhat later than usual before catching an early plane. I stayed at this hotel on a nice day in May, but I can see how it would be terrific in bad weather for avoiding taking a cab (or rental car) into snarled highway/airport traffic.
This place is expensive, though, with a base rate (before taxes) of $319 for the lowest-priced room.

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Boston Hotel”
text:
Just returned from a short trip (4 nights) to Boston. We were delighted with the location of the Sheraton/Boston and its comfortable room, 8th floor north tower. Being attached to the Prudential shopping mall made it very safe and convenient for me to shop while my husband was otherwise occupied. 
Concierge was terrific. That department simply made our stay the best.............
California travelers

name: Hilton Boston Logan Airport
title: “Convenient & comfortable!”
text: Landed at Logan and walked across the bridge to the hotel. Incredibly convenient (although the walk from Terminal E to the bridge is a decent hike with luggage) - but within 10 minutes, I was checked in and up in my room. Great room, good pub in the lobby, and service staff were incredibly friendly. Would definitely stay there again!

name: The Midtown Hotel
title: “assolutamente da consigliare!”
text:
In pieno centro a Boston (Back Bay) camere grandi e spaziose (il bagno abb piccolo, ma funzionale) e pulite
insomma è un due stelle, ma assolutamente ottimo..magari nn per un viaggio di nozze, ma per turisti è assolutamente perfetto (anche il prezzo)
aggiungo che il personale è davvero gentilissimo!

name: Grand Hyatt Seattle
title: “The best I have ever stayed at!!”
text: My husband and I stayed here for 4 nights during our honeymoon the week after Christmas. The service, hotel and everything was exceptional! We decided to valet our car because the self park had no in and out privelages and the valet staff were very friendly and helpful! The staff greeted us every time they saw us and our room was beautiful, clean and more than we expected! The bathroom was huge and the black out drapes were great! I would recommend this hotel to anyone, especially couples and honeymooners! It is also very close to a lot of shopping (Pacific Place, Westlake center, etc) We had a great time and we will definitely come back to stay here again and again!!

name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport
title: “Handy refuge”
text:
My first stay in an "airport hotel" so have nothing to compare against but here are some thoughts on the Harborside in general.
Location
Quick courtesy shuttle ride away from Logan airport. Pickup seems on the slow side. I had to wait 20 mins at Logan and 30 mins at the Airport Underground/Subway station. The City is reachable by water shuttle (didn't try this) or Underground/Subway (+ car/taxi of course). 
The hotel
Rooms are enormous and include a decent sized desk. Beds very comfortable. Bathroom fixtures and fittings looked distinctly tired in my room e.g. chipped bath enamel. Decor overall pretty netural - mainly beige. Boston views available at extra cost, otherwise you get the airport - but soundproofing must be top notch as I didn't hear a thing.
Catering
Didn't try the restaurant but it does have an incredible view of the city. Room service is prompt, varied choice and good quality. No obvious labelling of vegetarian and other special diet options on the menu that I could see.
Staff
Definitely the Harborside's strong point. Staff are friendly and willing to go to considerable lengths to help - even on Xmas Eve!
Overall
I wouldn't recommend the Harborside for a long stay or for making a number of trips to central Boston locations but for one night either side of a flight it is fine

name: Club Quarters Boston
title: “Amazing Stay”
text: First off the location of the hotel was perfect. No rental car was needed because I stayed a walk away from everything. The espresso machine was a life saver, saved me a trip to Starbucks plus it was free! Not to mention Mr. Arthur the hotel manager was very helpful. He made the stay so much easier. with insightful tips on good eats and drinks.

name: Inn at the Market
title: “quality and location”
text: spent a couple of nights here with my husband while enjoying a long weekend away. we both really loved the location of the inn at the market. it is close to all of what is "happening" in seattle. the water view is lovely, the beds comfy, the staff was always smiling, pleasant and helpful. there is no doubt that we would stay here again the next time we travel to seattle which hopefully will be sooner than later.

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Sheraton Boston”
text: I stay at the Sheraton Boston very regularly with work and i think it's a lovely hotel. The rooms are usually very nice and the beds are amazing. The staff are helpful and i find the Starbucks in the lobby and the free internet computers very handy. The hotel is comunicated to the Prudential shopping centre which is also linked to the Copley shopping centre so you don't have to go outside for anything, which is handy in the snowy winters. The location is excellent, with lots of restaurants and shops at its doorstep and the famous Newbury street one block away where you can find some of Boston's best boutiques, bars and restaurants. If you are visiting Boston don't hesitate and stay here, you'll have everything you want at hand.

name: W Boston
title: “Stadt Hotel”
text: Das Hotel ist neu und liegt im Theater District. Obwohl es an einer stark befahrenen Strasse liegt, hört man den Strassenlärm nicht im Zimmer. In kurzer Fussdistanz sind viele Sehenswürdigkeiten erreichbar. Restaurants und Bars hat es auch in unmittelbarer Nähe. Die Zimmer sind grosszügig und modern eingerichtet und erfüllen einen höheren Standard. Schade ist nur, dass WiFi kostenpflichtig ist.

name: Chandler Inn
title: “Average, ok location”
text: The room was average, with a decently sized bed and a clean washroom. It is comparable to, e.g., a Travel Lodge or a Holiday Inn; there was nothing terribly special OR objectionable about the hotel because it had functional decor and decent service.

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “Awesome Westin”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for only one night on a day trip into Boston.
The hotel is so big and the rooms are really spacious. The staff are very helpful and there's a bar in the lobby with seating area which is a great way to start the night with a few drinks before heading out.
The bathroom is one of the cleanest bathrooms I've ever seen. The shower has two heads and the soap products are not harsh for your skin at all!
The bed was really comfy, best night sleep!
Can't complain about this hotel at all.

name: Hilton Boston Back Bay
title: “Great location”
text: Had a great experience at this hotel. The room was clean and quiet. The location was excellent. Very close to public transportation, trolly stops, sites and attractions all within walking distance.

name: Sheraton Seattle Hotel
title: “excellent hotel stay for $79 on Priceline! what a deal.....”
text:
We stayed overnight in Seattle after a spring cruise up the coast and wanted a hotel that we could walk to everything, do a little sightseeing and find some good restaurants. We like boutique type hotels, (Love Kimptons) and were looking at the nice variety of those in Seattle. Decided to do some bidding on Priceline and ended up here.
The hotel's location is wonderful. Very close to everything. Lot's of wonderful shopping around. a few blocks up from Pike's Place Market where we took the food tour from Savor Seattle which was fun. 
The Hotel is clean, the lobby spacious and well decorated, large and spacious. Big couches, fire place, big easy chairs and free wi-fi.
There is a pool and jacuzzi on the 35th floor. Indoor. The gym is also up there. Very nice.
Try priceline for a great deal!

name: Renaissance Boston Waterfront Hotel
title: “Customer service was lacking but hotel was nice”
text:
This hotel is great in that it has a great location-walking distance to restaurants and the stops for the sightseeing tours. The rooms were clean, the beds comfortable and the amenities were fine. My only complaint was the customer service. The doormen/bellmen who stand at the curb did not greet us once during our entire stay. No one offered to help us with our bags-from the bell men to the front desk. 
The front desk always had many desk clerks available but none seemed to excited to help us. Smiles were infrequent. On one day we asked to borrow an umbrella and the desk clerk told us there would be a $40 charge for the umbrella until we returned it. This wouldn't have been as irritating if the umbrella hadn't been a complete piece of garbage. She only offered us one umbrella even though there were too of us and then told us that we probably didn't need it because it was not currently raining. I am glad I didn't listen to her because there was a torrential downpour a few hours later and it drizzled the entire day. That being said-the umbrella still wasn't all that helpful. It was a piece of junk and kept turning inside out with the wind. We bought a second umbrella from the drug store.
We stayed here for 3 days, 2 nights and with the exception of the concierge who was very friendly and knowledgeable-the staff at this hotel is not friendly or helpful. I would not stay here again for this reason. The hotel itself is fine though.Also-the brand of shampoo/lotion they use which is Aveda is horrible and smells like garbage and patchouli.

name: Hilton Boston Back Bay
title: “Very understaffed and eating there made us sick”
text: Very understaffed and eating there made us sick, sometimes the front desk was unattended for up to ten minutes....I thought a hotel was opne 24 hours. Also,,,we became ill after eating at the restaraunt. Then we had to wait 45 minutes for security(apparently only one security person works each shift we were told) to do a food poisoning report.

name: Inn at the Market
title: “Fantastic!”
text: My husband and I stayed here with another couple to go to the Madonna concert. The hotel is right in front of the Pike Market sign as you are headed down the hill into the market. We got a city view room and our friends got a sea view room. The view of the bay was fantastic, right over their viewing deck out past pike. The courtyard area you walk into to get to the hotel makes the experience even better as you know you are in Seattle but there is this quietness in there that is fantastic. The food at their little restaurant was great. The rooms were very clean. I would absolutely stay there again..and plan on coming back really soon!

name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport
Renaissance Boston Waterfront Hotel
title: “Beautiful Hotel and Convenient Location”
text: Great spot to get into the city, near a T stop and a short walk to the water.

name: Club Quarters Boston
title: “Perfect hotel for Boston Marathon!”
text:
There is only one downside staying at the Club Quarters in Boston. Its the elevators. They are so slow you wouldnt believe it before you experience them =)
Other than that - perfect. Very serviceminded. They also have elephant and castle pub next to it so you can eat breakfast, lunch, dinner and drink lot of good beer!
Its also very close to downtown and the shuttlebusses that shuttle you to the Boston Marathon start. Next time I visit boston I will stay at same hotel!

name: Taj Boston
title: “Gutes Hotel mit kleinen Extras”
text:
Das Taj Boston ist super zentral gelegen. Es liegt nicht nur an der zentralen Einkaufsmeile sondern auch gegenüber dem "Commons Park". Die Zimmer sind angenehm gross und sehr sauber. Wie man es von einem 5 Sterne Haus auch erwartet. Die Extras wie der Downturning Service, eine extrem hilfreicher Concierge sowie das excellent Frühstück machen einen Aufenthalt unvergesslich.
Als grosses - einziges Minus - muss jedoch erwähnt werden, dass das Taj nicht über einen Swimmingpool oder einen Wellnessbereich verfügt. Einzig ein grosses gut eingerichtetes - modernes Gym steht zur Verfügung.

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “Nice, clean and comfortable.”
text: I came up to Boston to see a Yankees vs Red Sox game and stayed at this Hotel. I got a good deal by paying in full up front to get a 10% discount. The hotel was very big, clean, modern and comfortable. The only downside was that it was not walking distance to Quincy Market, but only a 5 min cab ride. They had underground parking that was safe and close. It is a convention center hotel but suited my needs being that my stay was only one night.

name: Charlesmark Hotel
title: “Great Value!”
text: This quaint hotel combines the best of European styling and feel with American comfort. All of that at the perfect location in downtown Boston.

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “Greatest Boston Experience Ever”
text: Upon arrival my wife & I were greeted with a courteous staff, friendly smiles and a warm charm not always found up north. The Concierge Theresa Finnegan assisted me before we even arrived with rental car info, parking, destinations and answered every question I had with patience and a smile. The hotel was beautiful, clean and very professionally run and so convenient to everything in Boston. I highly recommend the Weston Boston Waterfront and can only hope the next time we're there that Theresa is still part of the staff.

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “Disappointed”
text: I have stayed at the Park Plaza four or five times usually when attending a conference held there. My rooms have always been fine. Not big but very adequate and looking out on the street. Once I was even upgraded without request to the floor which had continental breakfast. This past week, I stayed for two nights while attending a conference and was very disappointed for several reasons. The first, is that the room I was given was really cramped. There was not enough room to fit a table if I wanted to order room service meals. The shower stall was so small that I bumped the sides. There was a little appendage to the stall so that the shower curtain would prevent water from hitting the floor. The room looked out on the inside of the hotel and I knew that the hotel was far from full. The TV channel guide was inaccurate and the hotel no longer had pay for view movies. I tried to call room service and twice and got no answer. The directions for making a long distance call were inaccurate and when I finally got room service the directions that they gave were incorrect also. When I checked in I asked if there were any room discounts left for the conference and was told that I would have to call myself to ask. I wasn't really expecting one since I was asking so late but how hard was it for the desk person to call and ask? In the future I will find another place to stay.

name: Sheraton Boston Hotel
title: “Ottimo se scontato”
text: Noi abbiamo prenotato con Hotwire e per quello che abbiamo pagato e` stato sicuramente un affare. L'abergo ha i difetti degli alberghi "per congressi": camere un po piccole e servizio in camera non velocissimo (la cassaforte non funzionava ed abbiamo aspettato un po' per sistemarla). WiFi in camera solo a pagamento (lo sapevamo) ma gratis e discreta nell'ingresso; collegamento con il Prudential Center e la metro interno (abbiamo avuto una giornata di forte pioggia e vento e quindi e` stato apprezzato), ottimo il servizio degli ascensori e dell'assistenza bagagli. Non abbiamo usufruito dello sconto per la colazione in quanto iscritti al Club Sheraton perche` i posti nelle vicinanze (non solo al Prudential) erano comunque validi e piu` economici

name: Club Quarters Boston
title: “Luxury at afforadable prices!”
text: We had a great experience with the Club Quarters Boston. We arrived a little earlier than planned and they already had our room ready. The room was clean, well maintained and felt modern and fresh. It was a good size, had a quiet (and working) temperature system that kept us comfy the whole time. The whole atmosphere of the hotel was luxurious. The bathroom needed some re-grouting but it too was clean. Our bed was HUGE (i think they pushed two twins together since there was an uncomfortable seam in the middle) but we slept great. I loved the filtered water stations - WAY better than the nasty ice and tap water at other hotels. I didn't realize until we were checking out that we we could have had pieces of exercise equipment brought to the room! I would have done that. We were just a short walk from TD Garden, Quincy Market, Boston Common and a hundred other amazing things. The service was impeccable. I'm sorry we didn't get a chance to eat at the pub downstairs cause it looked like a neat place. When we checked out they offered to hold our bags for a few hours - which was extremely helpful so we weren't stuck lugging our heavy bags around Quincy Market. We WILL DEFINITELY be staying here again and I will be recommending this place to everyone I know looking for a place to stay. Thank you for making our weekend getaway perfect and stress free.

name: Renaissance Boston Waterfront Hotel
title: “Good business hotel in the Seaport District”
text:
As stated, the Renaissance Boston Waterfront Hotel is located in Boston's Seaport District, which can be somewhat of a hike to the more touristy areas of Boston. This hotel caters primarily to groups and convention business, is located right next to the Boston convention center and a short cab ride from Logan. The quality of the property is above average, with spacious clean guest rooms, expansive lobby, bar / restaurant and business center amenities. The service however was rather spotty in areas (front desk, valet and phone). This could be due to the hotel catering primarily to corporate guests, but a friendly smile and welcome from the valet wouldn't have hurt. A quick call on the "Let us serve you" phone button rang for what must have been 5 times, and my request got a "yeah no problem *click*". Not exactly what I am use to from Marriott branded hotels. Also, the addition of a Spa would be a nice perk for the hotel. Overall though I was satisfied with my stay, and would stay there again if attending a convention or corporate function.
Quick dining tip, the Legal Sea Foods next to the hotel is outstanding - stop by and check it out if staying in the area.

name: Ritz-Carlton Boston Common
title: “Great Location, Good Service but average hotel”
text: Booked three nights for work at the Ritz-Carlton for myself and customers. The location near the commons was great and short walk in the morning to local shops and coffee. The Concierage was very good and over all service was good.. The hotel overall was just not that nice or exquisite for the price.. An average bar, foyer, rooms, hallways,etc.. So, for the money these areas should have been nicer... Will stay at the Wharf the next time.

name: The Westin Copley Place
title: “Excellent location, nice large rooms but small bathrooms”
text: The Westinghouse Copley place is not as luxurious as other Westins I have visited. The rooms are large (try and opt for a corner suite), with nice big windows and incredible comfy beds. The bathroom in the junior suite was very very small for such a large room. Breakfast is average. I would expect a much bigger more varied buffet for the size of hotel, that said there is an option to order a la carte which was very good. The location is fantastic. Very close to new berry street which is very nice and short walk to the common, opera house etc. it's also right opposite back bay station and also has two very nice malls attached should you wish to shop. I wouldn't pay more than $250 to stay here as you may find better more affordable options nearby. My friends were staying in the Lenox hotel which is two minutes walk away. They really liked it and got a fantastic pre pay rate online. The Lenox offers a much less corporate feel if that's what you are looking for.

name: The Westin Copley Place
title: “Good Location”
text:
I was there for a sales meeting. The location is excellent. We were able to use the shopping tunnels to have lunch. My room had a great view of the river.. My room was clean.
The staff was friendly and helpful.

name: InterContinental Boston
title: “Great location!”
text:
Though we only stayed in this hotel one night, we would definitely return when in Boston. The location is superb...two blocks from South Station in the heart of the Financial district. Very close to the Aquarium, North End, Fanuiel Hall and Haymarket Square.
The rooms are quite spacious, the bathroom huge with plenty of towels. We found it immaculately clean. The corridors have many twist and turns, so you could have difficulty finding your room, but they are very quiet.
The lobby is large, with two or three restaurants to choose from. There is a lovely area out back to sit and enjoy the sunny weather and great views of Boston Harbor.
I would highly recommend this hotel.

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “A wonderful vacation”
text: Theresa Finnegan did a wonderful job helping us with a mini vacation. She was the finest conciege that we have dealt with in a long time. Her patience and suggestions were invaluable to our wonderful time in Boston.

name: The Westin Copley Place
title: “Enforced vacation ala: Hurricane Sandy”
text:
We were in Boston for a wedding and then planned to spend one extra day in the city before flying home on Monday Oct. 29th.. But Hurricane Sandy changed 
everyone's plans. We are so saddened by what Hurricane Sandy has done to the East Coast. We are thankful that our family & friends are safe and unharmed and we do keep the many who are effected in our thoughts. 
The Westin Copley Plaza really stepped up with unexpected rooms being cancelled and others being extended due to travel conditions. The front desk staff, especially Sarah, were very helpful as we juggled rooms for ourselves and adult children. We were able to use a reduced rate (hurricane rate) and our SPG points to stay an additional 4 days for 2 different reservations. Westin made the best of a bad situation for all of us.

name: Charlesmark Hotel
title: “Best Location & Best Price Hotel in Boston!”
text:
The CharlesMark Hotel, a charming boutique hotel, is located in the heart of the Back Bay and costs a fraction of the price of other hotels. Right out the CharlesMark front door brings you to some of the best shops and restaurants on Boylston and Newbury Streets; there's Copley Square, Trinity Church, and the park at Copley Square; and across the street is the Boston Public Library. The CharlesMark has a better location than both the Westin or Copley Marriott hotels and costs a fraction of the price. The rooms are cozy and incredibly well-organized and nicely designed.
The staff is very friendly and helpful, and they let you in on all the "secrets" of enjoying Boston like a Bostonian, rather than steering you to over-priced tourist traps like other hotels. Staying at the CharlesMark makes you feel like a Bostonian (even though you're stay is temporary). Be warned though, the CharlesMark makes Boston so inviting and wonderful you might be tempted to move there! Basically, the CharlesMark is just a whole heck of a lot friendlier and more personal than other hotels.
Did I mention there's a great lounge downstairs? Well, yes, there is! The street-level lounge is cheery and well-lighted during the day (and includes a wonderul little outdoor patio with tables and chairs). In the morning the lounge hosts a FREE help-yourself continental breakfast of bagels and cream cheese, muffins, toast, fresh fruit, coffee, juice, etc. and basically has the pleasant ambience of a European pensione. In the afternnon it's a perfect place to come back and have a cool drink on the patio before heading to your room. At night the lounge becomes a hip Back Bay neighborhood place to have a drink at night. It's the perfect combination --- hip, friendly, and not loud at all (the lounge was active the nights we stayed, but when we got to our room, we didn't hear a thing and it was as quiet as a cabin in Vermont!).
And are you interested in the Boston Marathon? The CharlesMark is is situated exactly at the Boston Marathon finish line! What could be more convenient to runners and their families and spectators than that?!
All in all, the CharlesMark is a unique blend of charm, friendliness, utility, convenience, great location, and cost effectiveness. My only hesitation in publishing my review is that I don't want the hotel to be booked the next time I call to stay there --- and believe me, the next time we go to Boston, we'll be staying at the CharlesMark!
Vive la CharlesMark!

name: Renaissance Boston Waterfront Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text:
What a great location - only a few minutes from the airport by Silverline, and a 15 minute walk to Boston's sights.
Ask for a room on a high floor with harbour view - even if, like me, you booked with Priceline. I paid only $80 per night for a weekend stay - you can't get a cheap motel for that!
The room was very comfortable - and Starbucks internet password worked on the 17th floor in my room too!
I will definitely return!

name: Revere Hotel Boston Common
title: “Great location at a great price”
text: A short weekend trip. Amazing location close to shopping, commons, and nightlife. Interiors seemed to be updated recently. Chic boutique feel with great spa quality products. If I return to Boston I would easily choose to stay here again.

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “Very classy, not expensive, good location”
text: The Silver line bus from the airport stops 2 minutes from the hotel. Very new, very classy. Upgraded our room for a higher floor with big windows for free. Starbucks coffee in the room. Nice, new, designed rooms. Very good gym with treadmills and pool for free. Downtown is in 15 minutes walking distance but the bus is at the corner. The staff is helpful and polite. Try the Barking crab near the hotel!

name: Club Quarters Boston
title: “Good location, poor service”
text: I booked thru a company website and was not aware that by having my aunt meet me in town and stay with me we would be charged additional fees. I'm not sure what the fees were for. The king sizez bed I reserved isn't what I got so I ended up sleeping on an awful pull out bed. The soap, coffee, towels, wash cloths that were used were never replaced. The location was nice, but for the price of this room I would have been much better off staying in a Sheraton or Westin. I tried to send an email to their customer service, but couldnt find an email address on their site. Maybe they don't want to hear about their bad service??

name: Hilton Boston Logan Airport
title: “Noise insulation excellent from airport, not good from neighbours”
text: The hotel is very convenient for the airport but it is quicker to walk than to use the hotel shuttle. Bed was really comfortable and clean. Sound insulation from the airport is excellent but non-existent from next room: from the sound point of view there was no wall between the rooms. The price to pay for the sound insulation from the airport is that the windows do not open and the air conditioning in the room is quite crude: if it is on, the bed is in a draft.

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Boston Harbor on Tudor Wharf
title: “Sleepezee in Boston”
text:
This was our first experience of a Residence Inn and it won't (hopefully!) be our last.
As others have said this hotel is ideally placed for those who are in Boston to site see and especially for those who don't mind a little walking. Approx 20 mins to City centre. This property is actually on the famous 'Freedom Trail' and also has quick access to the water taxi for a novel way to access the City sites. Very comfortable beds and slept as we wouild at home. We had a small 'problemette' with our first room ( not really the hotels fault) which was immediately resolved by the helpful front desk staff who offered a change of room even though the hotel was very full.(Thank you Dottie!) 
Shame about the 'non green' plastic eating kit for meals - but hey the breakfast was included so what the ............we are on holiday!

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “Incredible...the best hotel in the city!”
text:
I have stayed in many hotels, and I have to say this one is top notch. I can not say one negative thing about this hotel.
Our holiday party was awesome! The room, the food, the service were all A+. Tom Carter was an awesome bartender, so outgoing, friendly, and efficient! Thank you for such a great job. We will defininitely be having our holiday party here next year, and want Tom to be our bartender again! Thanks again for such a memorable experience!

name: Club Quarters Boston
title: “Very convenient, very nicely done”
text: This is located right in the middle of Boston's financial district and pretty near Chinatown and the Fanueil Hall marketplace - we walked without any problems. The hotel itself is very well maintained, comfortable and quiet.

name: The Westin Copley Place
title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: Although I only had 2 days here at the Westin copley, the 2 days were fab! The valet guys were so nice to me... and very attentive, After I checked in I went up to my room I had reserved on of the Jr suites, newly renovated with the "Heavenly bed" with a panaramic veiw of the Charles river..... need I say more! I was able to shop at a very near by farmers market and walked everywere loved it!! The hotel work out room was great I walked by it and thought it was nice.lol but went to the bar in the hotel called BAR 10, bartender was very nice and suggested there chowder....... best chowda eva!!!! Will be going back this october for fall leaves crispy weather and another fabulous stay at the Westin... cant wait....

name: Newbury Guest House
title: “Dont expect Victorian charm”
