text: The Newbury is in a fantastic location and is good value for money but dont expect a quaint new england B&B experience. The rooms are functional but basic - no luxurious touches and the common areas are again functional. The breakfast was certainly decent and the staff were efficient and friendly.

name: Newbury Guest House
title: “Skip breakfast and you'll be fine”
text:
We arrived at Boston after many hours of flight, and we got a wet welcome from the heavens. Doesn't really sound like a great start to a trip, but I must say, once the cab reached the Hotel area things started to look up. The near by streets are beautiful. Newbury Street itself is filled with small shops and some restaurants as well. Other streets near the hotel are just full of atmosphere of old. 
The room itself was nice, we opted for the mid-sized room, good enough for most couples, nice to be in, and clean. Shower could use better water pressure.
Many people addressed the breakfast issue in their comment, we found it not worth the bother. 10 min' walk should get you a number of better alternatives. It's a bit of a pity, the meal is set up in what later in the day is used as a restaurant, so we really expected more.
Apart from the breakfast problem the place is great for tourists, staff was helpful and friendly as well.
I would definitely consider staying there again.

name: Copley Square Hotel
title: “Copley Hotel”
text: Amazing service at this boutique hotel. Leslie who greeted us as check in, exceeded all expectations by offering to upgrade our rooms, making reservations for both nights at great restaurants while bringing us complimentary wine upon check in. She really made us feel welcome. Rooms are quaint, tastefully decorated and comfortable. On top of all of this, the location is perfect for exploring the city! I will definitely stay here next time I visit.

name: The Westin Copley Place
title: “Good Hotel Value”
text: The Westin is a good deal for a good hotel in a good location. We had a room on the 27th floor overlooking the Charles River and points SE for $275 a night. Can't beat it, and the Sorrellina Italian restaurant is dorectly across the street. The mall attched to the hotel has all of the top designer stores in it. If there's such a thing as a "one-stop-shopping" venue this is it.

name: Hilton Boston Back Bay
title: “No soundproofing”
text: We were very disappointed with our experience here. We only got about 2 hours sleep because the walls and windows of the room were not soundproofed at all! We could hear every word of everyone going by our room, and the incessant scraping of sidewalk ice in the morning sounded as if it were in our room (and we were on the 7th floor!). Add to that the $38 valet parking which didn't even get our car into a covered garage (there was snow and ice all over our car, and the windows had been given only a perfunctory brushing), and we will not be staying here again, nor recommending it to anyone.

name: Ritz-Carlton Boston Common
title: “Amazing”
text: We had the best stay here. The staff from the door to cleaning staff were superb. All friendly and would do anything to help. We had a fantastic one bedroom suite that was luxury. The club access is well worth getting with great food and drink. Also giving access to the fitness club on 4th floor that has to be seen/used to be believed. The staff in club level there are excellent providing so much help and advice that helped make are stay in Boston a very good one. We found the location great as well. Easy access to everywhere. ould recommend to anyone to stay here.

name: Sheraton Seattle Hotel
title: “Had my Wedding Here”
text:
My wife and I got married here back on Labor day September 4, 2006.
I will just start by a couple quick comments on the wedding then get back to the rooms and facilities.
Our wedding was perfect and we couldn't have asked for anything better. The hotel staff was extremely friendly and helpful and the ballrooms were gorgeous.
Back to the review, The construction at that point didn't effect us for the most part. The front of the hotel was being worked on but the main entrance was still open. I was in a standard room the first night. Nothing special really except for the great Sheraton beds which are to die for. 
The pool was average as well and the gym was nothing to write home about. I would expect a little more from the Sheraton chain in regards to these areas. The hallways and lobby are very nice and extremely clean.
The suite we stayed in on our wedding night was very outdated. Run down furniture, old time TV (with a VCR no less). It was very clean and we had the staff's full attention but they should really modernize some of the rooms, especially the suites.

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “Too many negatives though location is great.”
text: The location is outstanding. Not much else is good about this place. The rooms are refurbished historical but still very tired looking. Most importantly, the walls are paper thin! We had to listen to every conversation and every amorous adventure of the neighbors on both sides of our room. Really! I do NOT recommend.

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Boston Harbor on Tudor Wharf
title: “The Most Accommodating, Helpful & Pleasant Staff - Thanks, Dottie!”
text: Our room was immaculate, comfortable & the view was amazing. We were celebrating our anniversary and since we have some food allergies, we consulted Dottie and were so pleased with her recommendation - we ate there twice! Dottie made us feel like we were old friends. She remembered our names, remembered our anniversary, remembered what we did for the day, remembered what we were doing tomorrow and made sure our cab was there when we needed it. We were having a great weekend but Dottie made it a wonderful weekend. I'd go back again in a heartbeat!

name: Charlesmark Hotel
title: “Excellent value, excellent service”
text:
For a 3-day conference at Hynes Convention center, I turned to TripAdvisor to find a hotel nearby that would fit the budget of my employer. I contacted the Charlesmark directly and made a reservation, which was confirmed promptly by e-mail and gave directions to the municipal parking lot where they've arranged a $20 discounted rate, much better than the Prudential Center's $36 a night. 
On arrival in Boston I parked my car, then stopped in at the Charlesmark on the way to the Hynes and left my bag. When I returned that night, my bag had already been nicely placed in my room. While the room was not large, it was quiet, the contemporary decor was attractive and the space well utilized. Bottles of water were left in the room each day at no charge, there was a stereo, video player, cable TV, and a huge full length mirror. Two computer stations with internet are available in the downstairs lounge. In the morning, there are newspapers, juice, coffee, fruit, bagels and so on, all included in the room rate. Coffee and pretzel-type snacks are available throughout the day. The staff was quite helpful and I was very pleased with the hotel. 
Those traveling for pleasure might want to ask about room views--my room had a very limited rear view, which was fine for me, but might not work for everyone. This is a nice area for visitors, with plenty of shopping and restaurants nearby on Boylston Street and in the Prudential Center Mall. It's an easy walk to Newbury Street and to the Boston Common, there's a Shaw's Supermarket nearby , and a Green Line subway stop on the corner.

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Truely Wonderful Hotel”
text:
I recently stayed at the Hotel Omniparker for 4 nights whilst on a mini trip to America that took in New York, Boston and Saratoga. 
The hotel is located in a great part of Boston just up from the common and Beacon Hill, both must see areas of the city which makes it an ideal base for your stay in Boston. You are 10 minutes away from the Famous Quincy Market and the Marina both which are must see during your visit. The Cheers Bar and surrounding Beacon Hill area are both 10 minute walks away and access to other areas of the city via subways are easily accessible from the hotel.
The rooms are well furnished and quite a decent size for an ageing hotel. Do not let the work ageing deter you from choosing this hotel however, the age gives it plenty of character and the rooms are very well maintained and comfortable. The service is impeccable and I have to say was by far the best I received during my trip. The hotel concierge were excellent and extremely helpful, arranged tickets for the baseball and also assisted with our travel plans for Saratoga. 
I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone and will stay again if I am in the Boston area.

name: Millennium Bostonian Hotel
title: “Enjoyable!”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights at the end of our trip to New Hampshire, I wanted to be close to the airport for our departure. We loved the location the view from our windows :-) I think it's a bit overpriced for what you get, but I have come to realize that most hotels really over rate their value. Having to pay for wireless internet is a bit ridiculous considering how much the rooms cost.

name: Revere Hotel Boston Common
title: “Let's imagine: welcome with a glass of champagne”
text: Great location, huge lobby when you arrive.... And a glass of Champagne. That's our experience when we arrived in Revere. It's correct that there are also bad sides: check-in was slow (new staff ... But Champagne helps), carpet smells in the corridor (is that the glue due to refurbishment?) and the swiming pool is not the most fantastic yiu've ever seen. For the rest: great location, nice staff, easy to find bikes nearby and metro.

name: Revere Hotel Boston Common
title: “we enjoyed our stay”
text:
The hotel is in a great location. It is really close to Boston Common which makes it easy for touring (by walking) around the historical parts of Boston, getting to the subway system and gaining quick access to the highway. 
The beds and pillows were comfortable, the rooms were nice and clean, the Skoah bath products are lovely and can be purchased at the front desk.
The pool contained way TOO MUCH chlorine. After I returned home, I noticed a review from the weeks before my stay that noted the pool was not clean...maybe someone tried (too hard) to clean it between our stays? The hallway also had an odour of vomit during the 2 nights we were there...really not an inconvenience since we were in the hallway a minimal amount of time but something we all noted.
As other reviews have indicated, the elevators are slow and the card-keys a bit finicky but were nothing more than an expected peculiarity.

name: Millennium Bostonian Hotel
title: “Great hotel and lovely staff.”
text: Arrived at hotel having booked a twin room for 1 night through Octopus travel for myself and my daughter. Reception advised that only a King room was available and Octopus cannot book twin rooms online, they had apparently had this problem with Octopus in the past. However, as the hotel was full we accepted the King room and the hotel were going to take it up with Octous Travel and arrange to add a roll-up bed. The room was huge, very clean with a beautiful walk-in shower. Even although it was not their mistake, the receptionist was very good arranged a late checkout for the next day and provided vouchers for free breakfast for us both. The location of the hotel is great and would definitely recommend it.

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Please reconsider staying elsewhere”
text: Stayed here one (thank goodness) night and was most underwhelmed. Any semblance of manners was fabricated by the staff. Elevators were so crowded that they vibrated up and down the entire ride. Our room was the size of most walk-in closets, the shower curtain was moldy and the view looked toward a wall of a vacated building covered with black soot and rotted window sills. We were supposed to have received a king or 2 queens and were given a double. Honestly, this lovely city is overflowing with options for travelers. Walk through the lobby here to take in the history of the place and then continue walking right out the other door. Omni, very poor job with this property. You need to initiate some charm school classes with your gruff staff, and work to ensure that they understand how reservation systems work.

name: Ritz-Carlton Boston Common
title: “Staff Friendly, But, rooms not pleasing”
text:
Let me start off by saying that I usually stay in 5-10 different hotels a year, and am a Silver VIP member with the Hilton HHonors program.
I stayed in the Ritz Boston Common for New Years Eve 2005, on the Club Floor, with a Partial Boston Common view. My room rate was $499 plus tax.
Rooms:
The room was average, on the smaller side, however the bathroom was beautiful, with a shower, seperate tub, and marble galore. The room was clean, however there was a long hair in the tub, which I didn't bother calling about, since I didn't plan on using the tub anyways. The beds were comfortable, however I have stayed in Ramadas that had better pillows. 
Staff:
Almost every staff member that I encountered was friendly and helpful, and did almost anything to get my requests, and also remembered me, and welcomed be back, whenever I would reenter. 
Dining:
I can only comment on room service, which was beyond execptional, when my I returned to my room at 3am, and was hungry. They were able to make up a fresh fruit plate, and a cesar salad (Which was excellent) in less than 30 minutes. Also, the Private club lounge had some excellent food options throughout my stay, and the staff there was very friendly.
Overall Opinion:
I would definately NOT stay here again based on the rooms, however I would recommend coming back for the staff.

name: The Westin Copley Place
title: “Great location for our first trip to Boston”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Westin from 14-17 June. The location was perfect and we were able to walk to just about every place we wanted to go. The room was nice and the hotel was exactly what we wanted for our stay.

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Boston Harbor on Tudor Wharf
title: “Schöne Aussicht auf den Jachthafen”
text: In Laufentfernung zum Zentrum, mit gut ausgestatteter Küche und reichhaltigem Frühstücksbuffet haben wir unseren Aufenthalt in Boston genossen. Die Angestellten waren sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit. Das Ausziehsofa war zum Schlafen sehr unbequem. Unsere Kinder mußten dort schlafen, da für einen Erwachsenen mit höherem Gewicht die Spiralen zu sehr in den Rücken drückten. Für 4 war auch der Esstisch zu klein und es gab nur zwei Essstühle plus ein Schreibtischstuhl. Kinder zahlen nichts extra, aber wenn nicht alle sitzen können, ist das schon etwas blöd. Trotzdem hat der Pool und das wirklich sehr reichhaltige Buffet uns entschädigt und wir waren recht zufrieden. Sich selber kochen zu können finden wir immer hilfreich. Läden gibt es in Laufentfernung. Zum Zentrum (Quincy Market) läuft man etwa 15 Minuten. Es gibt auch eine Busverbindung über die Brücke - wir sind aber immer gelaufen (trotz Blizzard), da die Wartezeit auf den nächsten Bus länger als die Laufzeit war. Der Busplan von Boston ist etwas schwieriger zu verstehen als der Subwayplan. Mit etwas Einlesezeit versteht man es aber und beim Bus sieht man viel.

name: Copley Square Hotel
title: “Nice but not a Four Star hotel”
text: My husband and I stayed a The Copley Hotel for one night. The room was too small for two average-size adults to stay in for more than a day. The bathroom was so small we had to step into the bathtub to make enough room for the door to shut and there was no where to set toiletries. I have read other reviews comparing the room size and price to New York hotels, but let's face it, it's not New York. We have stayed in a number of hotels in the Copley Square area and found many other hotels for the same price or less, with larger rooms and significantly more amenities. Although the staff was very nice, the common areas nicely decorated and the rooms clean, we will not be returning given the other options in the area.

name: Revere Hotel Boston Common
title: “Revere Hotel”
text: Very upscale with great views....has a balcony to look out onto Boston. Rooms recently re-done and extremely nice...staff very helpful......

name: Inn at the Market
title: “seattle sights with a special friend”
text: an old and dear friend was in washington for a visit.....I wanted to show her the sights in seattle and I chose this lovely inn. it was lovely in everyway. the staff was friendly and the room comfortable and beautiful. everything was at our fingertips .....it was perfection.

name: Sheraton Seattle Hotel
title: “Customer service is TERRIBLE!”
text: The valets just stand around and stare at you instead of getting your keys or asking if you need help. The hotel charged 40 dollars of food to my room when i never got rom service and they charged 3 movies instead of 2. Since they said they couldnt do anything they said I had to call accounting.....Why do I need to call when it was not my mistake!!

name: Charlesmark Hotel
title: “Awesome”
text: Stayed five nights for a conference at the local convention center...Not only is Charlesmark in an excellent part of Boston close to incredible shopping, but the layout is pretty cool....Had drinks in the lobby and shopped until I dropped at Newbury Street and Copley Place...Room was tiny but I was traveling single so it was OK...Loved the bathroom with the speakers piping satellite music in...The shower was gorgeous....Garbage truck woke me up in the wee hours but I feel back asleep.

name: The Westin Copley Place
title: “nice stay for the right price”
text: Stayed here for two nights thru the memorial day weekend. Stayed in a junior sweet for about $250. per night, which I thought was a good price. The room is roomier than a standard room, it had two queen beds and a pull out sofa which was suprisingly very comfortable. Had a total of four in the room. They gave me the harbor view which I would not pay extra for, because the actual harbor is miles in the distance so don't waste the extra $. opt for the standard city view which has nice views of anywhere in the city. The cordless phone next to bed did not work, called hotel for 2 days to repair it..still not done when we checked out. And the house cleaning never dusted light stand in between the two beds before we arrived and for the next two days...hmmmm? Be very carefull of the snack bar in your rooms because they are on sensors and if you touch one of the items, even if you didnt remove it they will automatically charge your room, so dont forget to check your bill very carefully. Very courteous front desk and concierge. Breakfast is very expensive $15 - $17. for basic egg dishes etc....but hey your on vaca. i guess...right? The hotel is at the Copley Mall and about 1 block from Newbury st. I would absolutely stay here again for the right price. Also water pipes noisy when other guests where showering, I think it was the room above?

name: Charlesmark Hotel
title: “Not Perfect”
text:
My wife and I booked a larger room ,which was attractively decorated, if rather dark .Despite the higher price of the room,I was surprised to find that it had no windows to the outside.As mentioned by another correspondent, the room smelt musty.
Breakfast was described as " continental",but it was not clear to us ,with the cramped arrangements and limited variety ,which continent was being referred to.
Overall, I was disappointed at the value for money,which might have been better with a better room.The location was good.

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Old, Historic Hotel. Nice but not my cup of Tea!”
text: This hotel is historic, has a stunning entry, wonderful staff, but not for me. I am a new, modern, smell of air freshener hotel girl. If you love history and can't get enough at a museum then sleeping here would be for you. Rooms are very small but you are in Boston why would you want to be in your room. The heat/air system was loud and turned off and on all night. I saw every hour on the clock (garbage trucks pick up at 5am). The staff was great, a few native Bostonians that I love. Love you Seamus!! So convienent to all the great historic spots. Boston Cream Pie..YUM!

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “Good Price, Nice Stay”
text:
My wife and I decided on a whim to have dinner (Petit Robert Bistro in Kenmore Square)in Boston last Saturday, so, being an SPG member and looking for points, I looked up rates at all Boston-area Starwood properties - Found a deluxe king room here at the Westin Waterfront for under $160 !
 The hotel's very easy to find from the highway, and the T's right across the street. (Took the Silver Line to South Station, hopped on the Red Line to Park St, picked up the Green there - Not exactly rocket science, and it took about a half hour).
 We found the decor in the lobby to be very pleasant and relaxing, and enjoyed the "white tea" scent piped in. At check in, we were asked whether we would prefer a higher or lower floor, which I though was very nice, and, after expressing our preference for a high floor, were given a room on the 8th, an SPG member floor. 
 The room was modern and comfortable, and we didn't have any problems with noise from other guests like some previous reviewers, even though the hotel was fairly full this weekend.
 After dinner across town, we stopped at City Bar off the lobby - Nice vibe, good drinks, not too crazy-priced. It was fun to compare this location to the other City Bar we know, at the Lenox in Back Bay - That one was a little more "happening", I guess, with more apparent locals, as opposed to the mix of conference types, etc here.
 So all in all, we got a good deal, had no problems, found nothing to prevent us from considering this hotel one of our Boston options.

name: Sheraton Seattle Hotel
title: “Goods and Bads”
text:
I stayed at the Sheraton for four days in May 2005. 
The goods: 
Location: Great. Walking distance to almost everything you'd want to see in the downtown area.
Rooms: Really nice. Light soothing decor. Very comfortable bed with a variety of pillows. coffee maker. 
Concierge: Very helpful
The bads:
Elevators: -- not enough and very slow
Coffee shop: -- ridiculously expensive. There is a $20 breakfast buffet that didn't look spectacular. I only wanted oatmeal, juice and coffee so ordered from the menu. The bill was still $20.
Desk staff: Well -- After being notified by phone message at 5:00p.m.on Friday night that a fax was waiting for me at the front desk (the business center was closed), when I went to get it, the staff couldn't find it after 15 minutes of searching. I told the desk person to find it and I would pick it up after dinner. At 9 p.m. I asked again. After 20 minutes the desk person said, that must have been a duplicate message and there was no fax. I said I doubted that and said that I was expecting a fax. I asked that the fax, when found, be delivered to my room. At 10:00 p.m. the fax was slipped under my door. It had actually been received at the hotel at 10:00a.m. on Thursday morning -- 36 hours before I received it. As it was after business hours there was nothing I could do about the important message that needed a timely response. I complained to the manager on duty the next morning and she did apologize and she credited $75 against my hotel bill. That did not compensate for the cost to me because I couldn't respond to the fax. 
Would I stay there again -- Maybe. It was better and less expensive than the W Hotel, where I stayed a couple of years ago.

name: Millennium Bostonian Hotel
title: “Fabulous!!”
text: My husband and I planned a trip to Boston for our 25th Wedding Anniversary. Finally decided upon the Millenium and thank heavens we did. Upon check-in I mentioned the reason for our visit, and would an room upgrade be possible, to which the reply was "yes". We were given a large, beautiful room with a working wood burning fireplace (yes, a real fireplace, not gas), unbelievable king bed, and the largest bathroom I've ever seen in a hotel. After check-in we decided to walk around the city and upon our return we discovered a chilled bottle of champage, chocolate covered strawberries and a very thoughtful note from the staff. The hotel is in an excellent location across from Faneuil Hall and outstanding staff. We will definitely return!!

name: Inn at the Market
title: “I won't stay anywhere else!!”
text: My husband and I stayed for an over night get away. Wonderful view of the bay. Super comfy bed. Restaurants are amazing. Super yummy French food at Marche and the Eggs Benedict from Bacco amazing, soo good for breakfast. Great boutiques to shop in. You wouldn't have to leave the hotel if you didn't need to. AMAZING. AMAZING. AMAZING!!!

name: The Fairmont Copley Plaza, Boston
title: “Not worth the price premium you pay at the Fairmont.”
text: The bathroom was not clean at this hotel. For the prices they charge the value just was not there. The Lennox Hotel in Boston is a better hotel with better service for much less money. I would not stay at the Fairmont when I return to Boston.

name: Club Quarters Boston
title: “Get what you pay for...would stay again for the right price”
text: Great location. 4 minute walk to Faneuil Hall area. You aren't going to find many hotels that are 2 blocks from Faneuil Hall and under $100. I paid $90 per night for labor day weekend. I got what I paid for...but all of the travel website should reconsider the 3 star rating. Very outdated hotel...a bit of a dirty atmosphere(probably because of the style it is decorated in)...not unbearable. The front desk clerks were not very friendly. The rooms were a lot better than I expected for the price. They had a queen bed, a table with 2 chairs, a fridge, microwave, and sink. The bathroom was small but did the job. The linens were pretty gross. They definitely should bring some new towels into the rotation. They also only prepare the room for 1 person...this is probably because club quarters hotels are made for business travelers, who are typically alone. A call to the front desk will get you some extra towels. I would definitely stay again for $100 or under. I am shocked that this hotel usually goes for $160 per night(over priced) but all of the other hotels in the same area were quite a bit more. So if its a cheap room that you need...definitely do priceline.com and search the downtown/charlestown area...you might get lucky.

name: Omni Parker House
title: “A piece of history in the heart of the city!”
text:
My wife and I have just returned to England after a great holiday in the US which included 2 nights stay at the Omni Parker in Boston. I had been looking forward to staying here for months as I had read about all the history of the hotel and had seen wonderful pictures of the interior. I had also been in contact with Joseph Tyler the concierge for a few months and he is a wonderful ambassador the hotel and could not be more helpful, he really helped us have a great wedding anniversary. I had read previous comments about the rooms and had asked prior to arrival for a room with a view away from the lifts. The location of the hotel does not give it great views but the staff did the best they could and we were happy. I had also read about the size of the rooms and we were therefore prepared for them to be on the smaller side. Our room was perfectly adequate but yes it was a little tight, however if you want the character of America's oldest running hotel with all its old world charm and furnishing, you cannot expect a large modern room. Our room had everything in it that we wanted and was maintained well and the bed was a good size and comfortable. We did not eat in the hotel as the restaurant standard and therefore the price was higher than what we wanted, but there are some good eating establishments a stones throw from the hotel. We were very pleased with this hotel and you need to decide whether you want the old world charm and sophistication of the way it is because I for one would not want to see it ripped apart for modernisation, there are plenty of other hotels if this is what you want.
It is situated right on the freedom trail and is not far from anywhere in the city. I would definately recommend it to anyone and I would suggest getting in touch with them in advance with any requests. Thanks again to all at the hotel for giving us a truly memorable stay with particular thanks to Joseph.

name: Boston Marriott Long Wharf
title: “Very expensive, but charming!”
text: I extended my business travel and my husband joined me for a long weekend. The staff are very professional and helpful. Like others said, location is everything. We returned the rental car as it wasn't needed at all - and parking was $46 per day. We did the hop-on/hop-off trolley and saw the sites over 3 days' time. It really wasn't enough to absorb this beautiful and historical city! Access to the concierge lounge was so worth it! We asked for a small refrigerator in our room so we could store water and some food -- we had just come from a Residence Inn so we had quite a bit that we didn't want to throw out. They brought up the crudiest looking thing and stuck it right in the middle of our entrance/foyer - LOL. (We moved it.) There is a "cooler" in each room (not really a fridge) which is a nice touch. Our bed was a bit lumpy, but the linens were luxurious. We were in room 165 and had a front-row seat to the busy sidewalks (fun people-watching) and the beautiful skyline! Our housekeeper was the best! We tipped her well and she gave us extra chocolates and towels! Breakfast on Saturday was $50 for 2 for the buffet - very good food but a bit expensive.

name: Sheraton Seattle Hotel
title: “Classy, Clean and Cordial”
text: I really enjoyed my stay at Seattle Sheraton. I Hotwired the room and asked for the $30 upgrade to the Club Level. The rooms were immaculate and well appointed. The business services available inthe room made for a seamless business experience. The staff was extremely nice and efficient. The breakfast on the 32nd floor Club Room was more than enough. Fresh fruit, good coffee and nice ambience. The location is minutes away from Pikes market. The workout facility is ample and up to date. The massage services are very good, professional and well priced at $75 for an hour. I would absolutely return.

name: The Fairmont Copley Plaza, Boston
title: “The best of the best”
text: The hotel is beautiful and is located in an excellent and accessible to central Boston area. The location really encourages walking and touring. The hotel has everything you could desire especially on the Gold floor level. The meals and snacks are fantastic and the service is always superior. Though costly, the stay is worth every cent. The stay really makes you feel like you are someone special.

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “Fantastic”
text:
I got a fantastic deal on this hotel from otel.com (It was a secret hotel, that I managed to work out, that cost £290 for 5 nights!), but was quite unsure if to book it due to the reviews I had read, but I am glad that I did. 
Even though this hotel is out of the city centre I must admit that it did not cause any inconvenience to our stay. The transport links in Boston are fantastic and with the T stop being just over the road it was so easy to get to any area in a few minutes. Cabs were also rather cheap, it only cost us $5 - $8 to get from Copley and Downtown back to the hotel. We have stayed in central Boston previously and I must say that staying by the Waterfront was no problem at all, if anything it was rather relaxing as there were no busy street sounds when trying to sleep. There is also a plentiful supply of cabs outside the hotel and the Boston tour bus comes to the hotel reception.
In all the hotel was very nice. The room was large, clean and very comfortable. We also found the staff very nice and friendly, check in was quick and easy and check out was made even better as they allowed us to delay check out until 5pm! We also found Teresa on the service desk very helpful, she managed to put us in touch with a really cheap and convenient way to get out to the Outlet Village and provided us with take away menus when we wanted a night in after all the shopping we had done in the day had worn us out.

name: Millennium Bostonian Hotel
title: “Bags stolen. No apology from hotel.”
text:
What would otherwise have been a good stay turned into a nightmare when I realized that $400 worth of shopping was stolen from my valet parked car.
I was encouraged to leave my car in valet parking by the door man who said paying $40 per night was worth it because of the safety factor. I parked it with them over 2 nights $80). After we checked out and loaded up our car we drove off not even thinking to check through our stuff in the car. Only when we arrived at the next destination a couple hours away did we realize that the bags had been pinched. I was apalled that even after alerting the hotel they provided no apology and totally feeble compensation. They did not even offer to take off the cost of the parking. Their solution was to fob me off to the valet company and leave them to solve it..... I was shocked at the Bostonian's unprofessionalism and careless manner dealing with this. Thumbs down!
You would never find this at a true world class hotel.

name: Charlesmark Hotel
title: “buono!”
text: hotel in ottima posizione, su una delle strade principali; personale della reception cortese e disponibile. Bel bagno e bella doccia. Unica nota negativa la colazione: troppo poco fornita la colazione con solo un po' di succo, caffè e due pezzi di pane. Prezzo forse troppo elevato!

name: Club Quarters Boston
title: “ottima scelta!”
text:
Questo hotel si trova nella zona finanziaria di Boston, ma in 10 min a piedi il centro è raggiunto. L'hotel,anche se maggiormente utilizzato da persone che viaggiano per motivi di lavoro, è curato in ogni particolare.
L'accoglienza del cliente è molto sbrigativa e veloce, probabilmente dato dal fatto che i maggiori clienti sono business-man, ma se oserete fare qualche domanda in più, il personale si rivelerà molto attento e cordiale.
Stanze non grandissime ma accessoriate di tutto punto, così come il bagno.
Se decidete si soggiornare qualke giorno a Boston, questo è il posto ideale!!
Boston è stupenda...vale veramente la pena vederla!!

name: Sheraton Seattle Hotel
title: “Tolle Lage für Convention Center aber Bar schliest früh & wenig gemütlich”
text: Das SHERATON entspricht dem üblichen Standard dieser Kette. Die Lage ist aber sowohl für CC als auch für die "Erkundung" von Seattle wirklich gut. Die Zimmer sind US-üblich geräumig aber etwas abgewohnt. Die Hotelbar hat wenig Charme und um Mitternacht ist spätestens Zapfenstreich. Da habe ich in USA schon deutlich bessere Hotelbars erlebt wie z.B. WILSHIRE GRAND in LA.

name: Boston Marriott Copley Place
title: “Pretty Good”
text:
I booked the Marriott through Priceline, and stayed there for two nights, having spent three nights at the Westin.
Upon check in at the Marriott I was greeted by a very friendly receptionist. However I was disappointed that they did not have details of my Elite Rewards status, and therefore they had not guaranteed my king bed request. Therefore I had to have a twin room, which while not a problem, was disappointing.
My room was nice, more than adequate, but nothing out of the ordinary. I felt that everything was very 'uniform' at the Marriott.
A highlight of my stay was being able to use the Club Lounge on the Concierge Floor. As I travel alone and often stay in large business hotels, it is nice to know that there is a friendly face who will always remember your name. Beatrix was a prime example of this. Unfortunately I had to leave earlier than expected, and did not get the chance to thank her for all her assistance during my stay, so if anyone visits the Marriott, please search her out!
Whilst I would give this hotel four stars, I would not say that it is at the better end of this market. They miss the little touches that make a hotel more enticing. I was also surprised that when I requested a travel adaptor (mine had disappeared between New York and Boston!) all they were able to offer me was one from the hotel shop ... for $30! I went over the road to Walgreens and picked one up for $12!
Overall, a hotel of a solid standard. However, if you are looking for somewhere that bit more special, go to the Westin.

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Delightful hotel!”
text: Great location in the historic district. Not your typical business traveler hotel--which is a big plus! Rooms are small but adequate. There was noise from other guests in the hallway, but the hotel's ambience outshines the noise level!

name: Inn at the Market
title: “Short Stays in the heart of The Pike Place Market, Seattle”
text: Last week we had the occasion to stay in Seattle for two non-consecutive nights and chose to stay each night at the Inn at the Market. What a delight - everything about those stays. The staff is wonderful, from the moment you hand your car off to the bell staff for valet parking, until you get in the car to leave. The rooms are great. This time we stayed on the City side, but have stayed on the Market/Puget Sound side in the past. In either case, the rooms are great. If you do not want room service, there are dozens of places to eat in the Market, and some that are absolutely first class. A great stay.

name: Copley Square Hotel
title: “Nice hotel - but misleading reservation”
text: The hotel was nice - very modern and posh. We booked the family suite and it was perfect if you are traveling with children. The bathroom was ridiculously small (seriously, the one on our cruise ship was larger) but ok - and we were expecting that from other reviews. What upset me most was that when I booked I was told I would have a free breakfast with my package - I even confirmed this on the phone with reservations but when I arrived there was "nor record" of a free breakfast. After arguing with the front desk - they sent me coupons for one day - not the three days we were staying and made it clear that they didn't believe us but were doing this to shut us up. I really don't appreciate being mislead and I REALLY don't appreciate the front desk people insinuating that I was lying. The entire thing ruined an otherwise pleasant stay and left such a poor taste that we will never stay there again. There are too many other options for excellent hotels in the area...

name: Club Quarters Boston
title: “Posizione comoda e Hotel elegante”
text: Abbiamo soggiornato 2 notti, la posizione e' perfetta in pieno centro a Boston (zona Downtown), dalla quale si potevano raggiungere a piedi i piu' interessanti punti della citta'. Camera pulitissima ed elegante, letto comodissimo. L'hotel appare anche adatto per una clientela business. Piu' caro rispetto ad un b&b ma comunque conveniente. Parcheggio non comodo se arrivate in auto in quanto l'Hotel si trova in zona a traffico limitato.

name: The Back Bay Hotel
title: “A week at this hotel and we thought of it as home”
text:
This hotel was a great base for our sight seeing and shopping around Boston. The location was within walking distance to all the main attractions as well as having a number of T stops near by if you were going a bit further. 
The staff were friendly and helpful and house keeping was completed to an excellent standard. When we first arrived the fridge in our room did not seem to be working so someone was sent up to look at it and the arrived within minutes which was excellent! It must have been unplugged by a previous guest.
The furnishings in the room were to a high standard with marble tops and dark wood. The room was kept well stocked with toiletries and plenty of stationary. They fridge came in handy since there was not hot drinks in the room, you get complimentary bottled water, so we stocked the fridge with iced tea also. The picture quality of the tv was not great, but we are used to HD at home and this tv wasn't, although saying that I think it still could have been better. 
We had an excellent wifi signal in our room throughout the 7 nights which helped us plan our activities for the days ahead as well as keeping in touch with family and friends. 
We always intended to try out the bar or restaurant but our days sight seeing ended quite late so we ate elsewhere, but the bar seemed nice and even had a bigger crowd on week nights that I would have expected meaning there was a nice atmosphere, possibly due to different conferences the hotel seemed to be hosting.
I would have liked a seating area in the room with a small table, there may not have been room for this though. There was a desk chair at one side of the bed where my boyfriend would sit and I would sit at the other in a soft chair or on the bed. This wouldn't put me off returning.

name: The Westin Copley Place
title: “Excellent services and wonderful stay at Westin Copley”
text: Staying with Westin Copley is the best choice - it makes my first journey in Boston after the horrible long flight from Hong Kong wonderful, comfortable and warm (esp. in this winter time)seriously! It locates at the center of the city while everywhere is just a walking distance - make my life easier and convenient (no kidding). I will definitely tell my friends/ colleagues to stay with Westin Copley if they are planning to Boston!

name: InterContinental Boston
title: “Very pleased”
text: We booked this last minute on a third party website so got it at a rock-bottom price. We didn't know what the hotel was until we had paid, but we couldn't afford it if it were full price. We were very happy with our choice! The service was outstanding. They went out of their way to accomodate us, even though we paid a pittance of the full rate. Our room wasn't ready so they gave us a suite with a view of the water! They made up two extra beds for the kids, looked after our stuff when we checked out, marking our daughter's violin as fragile, and all the staff were helpful and polite. The room was nicely decorated, the lobby and bar were humming, and it is in a fairly central location. The concierge was very informative and gave us maps and all kinds of information about the subway and the Freedom Trail, as well as restaurant tips, etc... A great Boston choice, I highly recommend it.

name: InterContinental Boston
title: “Hope You Don't Have A Problem”
text:
During our stay in August 2010 the hotel experienced a fire which in their defence was not a predictable event. But after being evacuated for more than twelve hours from our rooms with little or no communication from the hotel ,the hotel next door offered us in to stay in their ballroom.Once we were allowed back into our rooms the following morning we were once again evacuated due to a fire. This time the duration was possibility one hour.
After numerous complaints to the management the best we could recoup financially from the hotel was reimbursement for the night we were unable to use our room.
They would not entertain any additional compensation for our inconvenience even though it cause us to cancel some events that we had scheduled for our visit.
In closing, don't have any problems that may require assistance with from the hotel.

name: Copley Square Hotel
title: “Boutique hotel at the heart of Boston”
text: Booked into there for three week via Expedia. Location is excellent. Shopping at Newbury and the surrounding areas. Lots of photo taking opportunities as well with all the historical buildings nearby. Get as high a level as possible as the noise from the bar and disco can be loud. Would recommend a better variety of room service dinner.

name: Harborside Inn
title: “3 great days in Boston”
text: 2 yrs ago, we stayed at the Marriott Custom House around the corner, which is a 5 star condo, but we did not want to pay their steep prices nor need such luxury. Someone cued us in about Harborside Inn, so imagine our delight to find a vacancy here! Took the Blue-Line subway from Logan Airport to the Aquarium Stop (2nd stop) and the exit to Quincy Market side which put us at the front door of the Harborside Inn! Only $2.50/person. You get on the free shuttle from the airport to the subway stop; then it was a mere 10 minutes from Airport to Harborside Inn. What a delightful surprise not to pay $20-25 for a cab. The hotel clerks are low-keyed, helpful, kind. Our room on the 8th floor, city view was quiet and roomy, with a safe & frig. The construction in the lobby was not noisy nor bothersome. This was the perfect location for our goals of walking to the Italian North End to eat at Al Dente's, where we had heavenly Veal Valdestona with artichokes, proscuitto & mushrooms one day, & Regina's pizza for lunch the next day. In the opposite direction, but also a 10 minute walk, was James Hook's Lobster Shack where we had Maine Lobster rolls 3x, including one packed for our flight lunch. Best deal for $13, recommended by the Trolley ticket man 2 yrs ago. This Maine style roll is with mayo, and chock full of lobster - no fillers. Only 3 small tables inside and some picnic tables outside. It's basically a friendly seafood market, but perfect for a quick inside sit-down or carry out. We were disappointed with Yankee Lobster Shack for dinner - 10 min. further along Northern Ave. The clam chowder was too sweet. Tasted like corn water was used in the soup base & the boiled lobster was overcooked. Prices ok, but we like more ambience for dinner. Took a cab there at 5:30 pm which cost $13 because of the heavy traffic. Only $6-$7 when no traffic. Quincy Mkt & Fanuiel Hall is across from Harborside Inn too, but been there, done that. Chose to explore other areas instead. Bought a subway pass for 1 week for $18 and explored Newbury St., one day and Copley Square another day. Walked 15-20 min to Atlantic Wharf where we took the Architectural Society's Harbor Cruise for $20 each as senior citizens. Other Harbor Tours end in Sept., but this particular cruise was still operating the 1st week of October. Call them to confirm. We had a beautiful sunny day for it. Narrated by an architect who made it so thoroughly interesting. By the way we could not get a Senior Charlie Pass on the MBTA bus/subway system because we are not Massachusetts residents, but the week's pass was worth it for the convenience. Harborside would be our choice again in Boston. Starbucks is 2 short blocks away; full convenience store is next door. Many coffee shops & convenience stores within short walking distance. The Frommer's Guide in the room for borrowing (or be charged for, if you keep it) recommends the Legal Seafoods a block away, which we didn't get to. The frig was handy to store our lobster rolls packed by James Hook's in plastic container the day before for our morning flight. Boston is a great walking town! Enjoyed our 3 day mini-vacation due to the convenient location of Harborside. 10 minutes to the North End or Seaport Blvd Bridge where Hook's Shack is located.

name: Millennium Bostonian Hotel
title: “Location that cannot be beat”
text: We stayed at the Bostonian Sept. 13-Sept. 16, 2007. The hotel is in need of renovation, which according to signs inside the hotel, will commence in early 2008. I, however, am willing to overlook some stained carpet and outdated decor for an absolutely outstanding location. Being across the street from Fanueil Hall and Quincy Market, on the doorstep of the North End and dozens of great italian restaurants, a five-minute walk to the waterfront and aquarium are more important to me than high-end design. The staff was very friendly. I called housekeeping twice (once for a pair of scissors and once from more decaf coffee) and both times there was a knock at our door in less than 5 minutes. Our room would not win any awards for high style, but it was large and clean. When this place is renovated, it will be THE place to stay in Boston.

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “Ok, but could have been better”
text: This hotel is in a convenient location in the Back Bay area. The lobby is beautiful. I didn't try the restaurant or room service. My single room was small and a little cramped with a small double bed, hardly any closet space and a cramped shower with no tub. The bathroom had hardly any counter space for toiletries, makeup, etc. The shower spray was very powerful, however; I ended up with a huge puddle of water all over the tile floor whenever I used it. Also, there were no available outlets in the room, so I had to unplug a lamp to charge my cell phone. I was told when I checked in that there were no king beds available. I had a choice between the small single room or a room with two double beds. I was alone, so I chose the single room. Had I known how small it was, I would have picked the room with two double beds. I know the hotel was busy and there was a convention being hosted there, but I still find it hard to believe that in a place that size they didn't have any larger single rooms available. Maybe the receptionist gave me a limited choice because I booked the room for a reduced rate on hotwire. Anyway, I was a little disappointed. I expected more from a 3.5 star hotel. By the way, bring your laptop if you need internet access. It's free in your room, but they charge for it in the business center. I wouldn't stay here a second time. There are better options in the Back Bay area for the price.

name: Boston Marriott Long Wharf
title: “Meh”
text: The Long Wharf Marriott was fine but not as good as expected and not nearly as nice as the Marriott in Quincy, which is lovely and very friendly and costs much less. The location is awesome; it wasn't hard to find things to do locally. But I concur with another reviewer that the hotel is shabby around the edges. Our fan also didn't work in our bathroom. We were told they would send someone right up. No, they did not. It seemed like a policy response, with the appearance of prompt service without the reality of prompt service. I also agree that the pool is shockingly small. I doubt that we will go back. Given the number of families there with little kids, and the price point, you would think they would have some sort of fun free extras for kids. I would say it is a charm-free hotel with one exception: they do have an awesome concierge who got us Red Sox tickets at the last minute on opening day. He was fantastic. The people in the restaurant were also quite nice. Great potential.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square
title: “Disappointed with room and quality”
text:
Wanted a reasonably priced hotel for 2 nights and selected the Courtyard in Copely Square because I regularly stay at Marriott properties for business.
Had a late check-in at around 1am and hotel did not have a room prepared according to my normal requests with regard to extra towels and a refrigerator. Front desk did arrange to have a fridge brought up but do not want to have to wait for this in the middle of the night.
Room was tiny for two people and associated luggage. Room was also a little tired with dirty marks and worn surfaces/edges everywhere. 
Small and cramped bathroom. 
Have stayed at many (10+) Courtyard properties and this one is nowhere close to the quality of most. Was happy to move on.

name: Fairmont Battery Wharf
title: “great location, great hospitality”
text: We had no idea what we were in for when we booked our one night at this hotel. As we were travelling to Nantucket we needed a hotel relatively close to Logan but did not want to be at the airport. As frequent guests at other Fairmont hotels we decided to try it out and it was far beyond our expectations! We booked a "gold" club room and found it was in a separate building away from the other parts of the hotel. We were warmly greeted and escorted to our room by one of the reception staff who explained the door key system and introduced us to the features of our room.She even suggested that we really should partake in an Italian Festival taking place that evening on Commercial Street. We did and it was wonderful, we had the best Italian food of our lives and enjoyed the celebration very much. I asked about running and was directed to the "Harbour Walk" which was a good run along the wharfs and jetties. We made use of the "club room" both for refreshment and breakfast and welcomed the personal service of the attendants. All in all it was a great place for two weary travellers to relax and enjoy North Boston.

name: The Fairmont Copley Plaza, Boston
title: “Elegant With Issues”
text:
Like the Englishman, upon being asked by his waiter at the club, "How is your boiled egg?", replied, "Parts of it are quite good", so I have some difficulty rating The Fairmont Copley Plaza Boston.
Should you be a member of the Fairmont's President's Club, the doorman will greet you by your name when you arrive at the curb of the front door. Your car will be stored for $42.00/day. You will receive free internet service, or if not a member you will pay a hefty daily fee for it. 
The hotel is under renovation. I don't think my room had been renovated yet. The window could not be opened for fresh air. The edges of the doors had chipped paint. The bed, sheets, blanket, and pillows were excellent. The closet very large. The furnishings elegant, with two electric outlets right there on the desk, for charging my half-dozen battery driven devices.
The bathroom had issues. The shower curtain was on a narrow track, hard to pull around the tub and too short. The toilet was located so close to the wall that it was difficult to use, especially with the toilet paper holder occupying the space where one's right leg is located.
It takes a while to get hot water.
The desk phone did not work, but the one at the bed did. The desk clock did not work either; it runs on batteries, though maintenance assured me it did not. The down light to call the elevator on the fourth floor was out. You just don't put your room card in the slot to call the elevator, but must withdraw it do activate the elevator. Details, details.
Prior to sleep, I requested additional pillows from the front desk; they arrived twenty minutes later. 
No Sunday paper brought to room or available at front desk; you can buy one in the gift shop. 
There's a bottle of water in the room, with a tag around the neck of the bottle, declaring its price is $7.00.
I miss the iconic Brass Rail Bar off the lobby! It's no longer there.

name: The Fairmont Copley Plaza, Boston
title: “Fairmont Copley unlikely to disappoint”
text: Beautiful old hotel well positioned in Boston; rooms are old as to be expected and the floor-boards creak overhead; service is not the best I have experienced but this seems to be one of the best hotels in Boston otherwise; tip generously or invoke the wrath of the service staff!

name: The Back Bay Hotel
title: “Great Stay!”
text: Stayed here for 3 nights in September! Nice clean and modern touches! Front desk was very friendly and helpful! Large room and super big bathroom! Room service from the Domestic staff was just perfect! Enjoyed "Cuffes Bar" (The hotel was a former Police station!) Had a Gaelic flavor to the place, which was just great! Great location to the main shopping and commerce area of the City! "Free coffee" in your room in the morning, which was the perfect start to your day! Served up a great breakfast and the staff were excellent! A little pricey but worth it! Would definitely recommend this hotel for a stay!!

name: The Langham, Boston
title: “Location, ++++”
text:
Stayed here for three nights for a family gathering recently. From checking in, with very good counter staff, to check out, everything was just right and very efficient. Breakfast was a treat with a great room and service.Lovely pool area, absolutely spotless and very friendly and helpful staff, even at 6 a.m.!. Some renovation was in progress but was very well managed with extra guides to see us to our rooms when we returned late and found the access to the regular lifts unavailable.But no problem, there was an alternative lift nearby, well done Managers,Marcus always around keeping an eye on everything too.
Bowler hatted doorman really earned respect for his service during a severe thunderstorm when taxis were scarce for a while, with large umbrella at the ready to protect from the downpour and calling in extra cabs for us. 
If you want a perfect location for sightseeing, shopping or strolling around Boston this is it.

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “Average Hotel In An Unbeatable Location”
text: The hotel has a fascinating history and the communal areas are comfortable and stylish. The rooms are decent quality but cleaning standards could be higher; if you move any fixtures then you'll likely find a layer of dust. Room service is pricey and the food served is pretty poor but the main resteraunt does offer tastier dishes. Some of the service leaves a little to be desired: reception and resteraunt staff are friendly enough but we found both the bellhops and the doormen surprisingly rude on several occassions. The location is however simply unbeatable, with the subway on your doorstep meaning most of Boston is only 10mins away.

name: Harborside Inn
title: “Great Location!”
text:
The location was fabulous. We rode the blue line from the airport to the aquarium stop, got off and had a little trouble finding the hotel because it was behind the entrance to the subway across the street. A quick walk across the street and we were there. Our room wasn't ready but they stored our bags and we took off to see the Freedom Trail. We were about two blocks away from Quincy Market where we ate most of our meals. Also about a 20minute walk from the Italian section where we had a great dinner. A few blocks in the other direction put us at the aquarium and the ferry that we took to Salem.
The hotel room was small but very clean. The bathroom was newly remodeled. The room had a free in-room safe, free wifi, refrigerator, and a nice flat screen tv. Coffee was free in the hotel and there was a dunkin donuts nearby for breakfast.
We stayed in one of the atrium rooms so we had absolutely no street noise. The atrium is more like a domed small space between buildings. Some sunlight came in but not a lot. We weren't there much during the day anyway.
There was nothing fancy but it was exactly what we wanted. The hotel staff was very good and stored our bags again after we checked out.

name: Boston Marriott Long Wharf
title: “Great Location - Great Stay”
text: This was our first time staying at the Marriott Long Wharf and we made a great decision. From the moment we arrived, we felt welcomed by the friendly and helpful staff. We were able to check in early and were happy to find out that our room was ready. This was a great help b/c we were able to park our car and put our bags in our room. The staff (the helpful friendly doormen, everyone at the front desk, the man who brought the rollaway bed to our room, the wait staff) were all terrific. The hotel lobby is beautiful - our room was very clean and quiet. The only complaints we had, were the pillows weren't the greatest; the windows were pretty grimey (despite the great view); the breakfast buffet wasn't refilled very well. That may sound petty, but when your kids are hungry and you want to get your day started so you can get to the musuems, it can be frustrating to wait for eggs, and pancakes. The food was very good though. The hotel's location was really great - walking distance to the Aquarium, Quincy Market and the North End. We look forward to coming back to stay.

name: Fairmont Battery Wharf
title: “Great time”
text:
Family took a quick trip to Boston staying 1 night at the Fairmont Long Warf. Hotel is in great location, our room at excellent view across harbor to Bunker Hill and USS Constitution. Hotel was very clean and staff was friendly. We parked 2 minutes away at parking lot toward quincy market, saved $17 for overnight parking. First checked in and drop off luggage then went up the street to park. 
We would definitely go back.

name: InterContinental Boston
title: “Contemporary, Clean, City Hotel”
text: There was very little not to like about the InterContinental Hotel in Boston. It's an imposing new glass structure on the border of the seaport and business districts. It has an entrance on the busy Atlantic Avenue just a few shirt blocks away from South Station, and in partial view of the harbor and channel. The rear entrance is directly on the channel, with beautiful views of the water, federal court house, and children's museum. On the rear patio, there are relaxing places to sit with music and a outdoor bar. The hotel's interior design is contemporary and bright, not stuffy or gawdy. The registration desk could've used a third person, but the line still moved quickly. Bell hops were very helpful. We valed-parked the car at the hotel entrance. To retrieve the car, it was necessary to take a separate elevator to the underground garage and office, which was a little strange, but not that inconvenient. Parking was expensive, but not terrible compared to city hotels. The hotel common spaces were extremely clean and comfortable, as were the banquet areas. Hotel staff, including security guards, managers, bell hops, and room service attendants were all very pleasant. The rooms were a decent size. We had a view of the building under construction next door, as well as a sliver of the channel and Atlantic Avenue. In a nice twist, the bathroom is about as big as the rest of the room. There is a full glass shower, as well as a tub. Very spacious. One interesting feature is a window between the bathroom and the rest of the room. It can be slid closed, but light can shine through at night if someone is in the bathroom. Not a big deal. the room had a huge flat screen tv, plenty of drawers and closet space, a desk, and several chairs. It was a very comfortable, beautiful room. The mattress was not as comfy as I would've expected, but the pillows were nice. I think the best elements of this hotel are its proximity to South Station, the business district, and Quincy Market/North End; its contemporary design and appeal; and its cleanliness.

name: Harborside Inn
title: “Tremendous value for the location!”
text:
This is a somewhat bare-bones, nicely decorated hotel near Fanuel Hall, the waterfornt and "hop-on-hop-off" tours. For the location, the price was fantastic! I went to Boston in December of 2010. The hotel is a renovated mill or industrial building. Lobby is small and cramped, but well decorated. Staff was young and quite casual. A little disappointing, but once I had my room key, I didn't care.
My room was confortable and stylishly decorated. The bathroom is quite modern. Liked the hotel and would recommend it for a short stay, in spite of the front desk staff.

name: The Fairmont Copley Plaza, Boston
title: “Nice Location”
text:
First, before you stay at any Fairmont Hotel, join their rewards program. Access to a fantastic lounge in each hotel AND free internet.
Pluses:
1. Location
2. Staff
3. Lounge/Gold Room is fantastic; great breakfasts and snacks all day (please don't forget to tip here,,,,I really hate when people get waited on hand and foot and can't scrape together a couple of bucks for the staff in the lounge).
4. Beautiful historical building. I had an excellent room. It was spotless and cleaned nicely each of the 4 days I was here. Robes in rooms, safe, and I had a coffee pot (not sure why everyone else said they didn't have one???)
5. Umbrella in the room. Living in Portland, I appreciate that kind of stuff on the road.
6. Oak Room Wedge Salad. YUM.
7. Catie the dog. Made me miss my lil 4 legged pal :(.
Minuses:
1. Thin walls. I heard my neighbor all night long. And, I heard him press snooze about 10 times in the mornings. I was millimeters from going to knock on his door and go female on him. You are not at home buddy. Wake up.
2. Fitness room. Its a total joke. 2 treadmills and 2 ellipticals. In a walk in closet with some weights. You get a guy in their who takes garlic supplements, and sweats profusely, and you will gag on your towel. The nearby options are ridiculously overpriced. For a business traveler like myself, I expect high end hotels to have nicer fitness facilities,,,,,particularly if you have a lot of meetings on sight. And, because its sandwiched between sleeping rooms, you cannot get in there until 6:00am.

name: The Westin Copley Place
title: “Perfect!”
text: This is my favorite place to stay whenever I'm in Boston for business or pleasure. The beds are extremely comfy, the rooms are clean, and I love the complimentary bath soaps (odd thing to look forward to, I know). The staff can be a little snooby sometimes, but nothing outrageous. Wonderful location, and if you don't feel like wandering out of the hotel for food, there are plenty of options in the lobby. There's even a walkway to the Copley square mall, so you don't have to venture outside on blustery days - more dining options and things to do -bonus!

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “Sehr gutes Hotel, leider etwas abseits vom Stadtkern”
text:
Das Hotel ist für ein US Hotel durchaus mit europäischem 5* Niveau vergleichbar. Die Zimmer sind modern und geräumig und der Service ist zuvorkommend.
Lediglich die Lage im Business Destrict ist für´s Sightseeing nicht ganz perfekt, da man in die Stadtmitte doch eine ganze Weile laufen muss, wenn man kein Taxi nehmen will.

name: Harborside Inn
title: “First time to Boston - Excellent Hotel”
text: We stayed for two nights in Boston on July 3 and 4th. The hotel was very easy to find off the highway. Very nice staff, even called a great little bakery for me to make sure it was open on the holiday. The rooms were different that the usual bland hotel room, with a wonderful old brick wall behind the bed. Bedside lamps with dimmer switches were excellent. Super clean room with a great bathroom. The towels were fresh, white, white, white and very soft. The bed was one of the most comfortable we have slept in at any hotel. Loved the convenience of the location. We could walk to any part of the city we wanted to see. This hotel is a great little secret that we will definitely return to.

name: Millennium Bostonian Hotel
title: “Great hotel, Great Location!”
text:
We have just arrived back from a four night stay in Boston at the Millenium Hotel. In all we were very pleased with the hotel. We had a lovely big room on the seventh floor with a balcony and sofa and a separate dressing area. The view on this side of the hotel was not fantastic as it overlooked what is left of the Big Dig however it was quiet. Service was very good and rooms were cleaned thoroughly every day. Having read previous reviews some customers have commented on decor and carpets etc - while it may be quite chintzy in places I dont go on holiday to check out the standard of the carpets as I have more important things to do like enjoy myself!!
Lounge was very nice altho drinks were a bit pricey and the one morning we had breakfast at the hotel the pancakes were off ( very disappointed - I had flown the Atlantic for genuine pancakes with maple syrup!!!)
Location is fab - Quincy mkt and Faneuil Hall over the road and T station within 5 mins walk.
Did all the tourist stuff - best bits observation deck at Prudential tower, Freedom trail, Sunday brunch at Joels bar on Newbury Street and tickets for Blue Man Group at the Charles Playhouse.
Very safe city to walk in and much friendlier then NYC.

name: The Westin Boston Waterfront
title: “bien mais des surplus et un peu loin du centre”
text: L'hotel est parfait, le service correct , par contre, il est un peu loin du centre et a part la navette qui vous y dépose, ça fait une petite trotte; compter 10$ si on veut prendre un taxi. Autre désagrément et pas des moindres : les facturations supplémentaires du bussiness center : 6$ le 1/4 heure de connexion internet. 9$ pour recevoir un paquet ( même si on est dans la chambre à l'attendre). .2 timbres sont vendus dans un petit emballage avec 1$ de surcout pour 0.98$ ; etc...il vaut mieux apporter son laptop.

name: The Fairmont Copley Plaza, Boston
title: “Friendly and elegant, but expensive and dated”
text: I stayed here for business one evening in August. It is a beautiful hotel, but it felt dated and a little worn around the edges. The staff was very kind, welcoming and upgraded my room without my asking and for no additional charge. The room itself was very spacious and lovely. The hallways felt like an old Ivy League dorm hallway and the workout room seemed to be a tiny afterthought. I also had dinner in the hotel's Oak Room, which has both a dining area and a bar with a display of fresh fish. The bar was friendly and the food pretty good. A little pricey for what you get. I would stay here again, because the room was great and the service excellent, but for the price, I would look around at other options as well, as it's not a terrific value.

name: The Liberty Hotel
title: “Not just a hotel - an experience”
text:
We just got back from a 1 night stay at The Liberty Hotel and everything about the stay was fantastic - the service, the room, the magnificent lobby. But what separates great hotels is to take a hotel stay and turn it into a memorable experience - and the Liberty delivered.
We were greeted with a glass of champagne at check in and then handed an invitation to "Cocktails with Calvin" (for being Starwood Platinum member). We made our way to the catwalk bar area at 7pm and had a blast - sharing food, laughs and cocktails with Guest Experience Director - Calvin, Rooms Manager - Brian and a few other guests. They then made us reservations nearby for dinner at Toscano. Upon returning to the hotel at 10pm, the weekly Thursday night fashion show was just getting underway in the lobby. 
The entire staff is topnotch and clearly cares about service - from doorman, to valet to front desk, even the restaurant hostess who got us free cups of coffee (since we missed the 7-9am free lobby coffee).
This is the top spot and only hotel in Boston for anyone who is looking for a fun filled 5 star experience. Book a room here and enjoy!

name: Inn at the Market
title: “Excellent stay in the heart of the city”
text:
We stayed at the IATM twice on our recent holiday to the USA, on arrival & on our last night.
We arrived at the hotel much earlier than check in time but this wasn't an issue, although our room wasn't quite ready, the receptionist took our mobile number & promised to call us as soon as the room became available, the concierge took care of our luggage and that left us free to stretch our legs, explore and grab a coffee after enduring a 10 hour flight to Seattle. 
We were in our city view room within the hour & were not disappointed, clean, bright, spacious & wonderful comfy king size bed. After a couple of hours rest, we popped out & bought a bottle of wine and sat enjoying the uninterrupted views of Elliott Bay from the terrace (this is such a bonus). At the end of the evening we returned to our room and housekeeping had replaced the towels, turned down our bed and left us a couple of chocolates, this was a lovely gesture.
When we returned to the hotel for our last night we had chosen a room with water view, given that the terrace is available to enjoy the water view, we felt this was an over indulgence, as the room itself (apart from the view) offered nothing more than the city view room, just we payed an extra $76 dollars for the priviledge.
All the staff were extremely helpful and nothing was too much trouble for them, if we returned to Seattle we'd certainly consider staying here again.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square
title: “Great Location, Huge Room”
text: It doesn't look like much from the outside, and the lobby's small... but the room had 2 queen beds and was huge! Very comfortable beds - with great big quilts and lots of pillows! Public parking was across the street. Breakfast was good too. By the way, we had a phenomenal rate - only $99. What a deal! I'd definitely recommend... especially if you're on a budget.

name: The Fairmont Copley Plaza, Boston
title: “great looking but lacking good service”
text: found other peoples' stuff under the bed - very dirty under tv table even had old traces of food. very noisy out side of room did not sleep through any of the four nights, trucks, buses, garbage trucks throughout the night. staff was very stuffy- unless you flashed a lot of money. not a good stay. the building is very pretty and very old that was the nicest thing of the stay. very over priced at over $400 per night - not even a doughnut for breakfast.

name: Fairmont Battery Wharf
title: “Polite service but I don't understand people's awe of this place?!”
text:
As I sit here writing this I am still puzzled about this property. I am wondering whether I am not sophisticated enough to appreciate it's allure? I'll try my best to explain:
Despite having to wait a half hour+ to check into our room, the staff was very polite though they should have offered us free breakfast for the inconvenience. (Check in time is 3. We arrived at 3:15 and the room wasn't ready until 3:50). We were not wowed, at all, with the atmosphere of the lobby. It felt very cold and corporate. The hotel has rooms in different buildings and feels disconnected. It reminded me of being on a business trip and staying in a business owned, tiny condo. Our room was small, impersonal, and although the hotel is fairly new, it still felt worn. We got to the room to discover there was no bath tub - a huge disappointment for me. When we asked the front desk we were told that most rooms do not have tubs and it would have been an extra $300 to get a suite which had one!! Also the room was really small. I know we were in a city but it still felt unusually cramped. The rooms did have robes but they were thin, scratchy and unappealing. The best part of the hotel was the bedding. The sheets had lots of threads and the mattress and pillows were yummy. In summary from the reviews I read I was expecting something like the W in NYC...no such luck.

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Beautiful .....wouldn't stay anywhere else”
text:
I am so shocked by some of the previous reviews for this hotel, it's so sad that the hotel is run down for the small bathrooms and old decor. It's an old hotel, the oldest in Boston I believe, people must realise that it has probably had the bathrooms added in later years hence the space, but perfectly adequate I have to add. The decor is in keeping with hotel, we had all mod cons flat screen TV and the most amazing bed, best couple of nights sleep I've had for ages, you had to actually climb up onto it it was so sumptuous.
Also the hotel staff were all really friendly and made our stay wonderful, even the guys outside on the street and we hadn't even tipped them when we arrived.
We also ate in Parkers restaurant which unbeknown to us was where JFK proposed to Jackie, food was very good but large portions. Great breakfast with a choice of buffet or menu, for a couple of dollars more the buffet was great with unlimited juice and coffee and the chef cooked omellettes to order. 
This hotel is in the perfect location, near shops and restaurants and the freedom trail starts right outside the hotel. Lots of historic buildings all around and the park just minutes away.The stop for the trolley tour is just up the hill so perfect for everything. Just one piece of advice if you go to visit old Ironsides in the dockyard you need photo ID to be allowed on.
 I did join the loyalty scheme before we went and we were given a top floor room with choice of free drinks in the morning.
We were travelling from Boston to New hampshire to go skiing and the staff were very helpful with information and there even is an Omni hotel up in the white mountains which looks fantastic. 
If we visit Boston again we will be sure to stay at the Omni Parker House, thanks to the wonderful team for such a pleasant stay and making us feel welcome on our first visit to Boston

name: Millennium Bostonian Hotel
title: “Dingy”
text: This hotel experience was horrible for what you pay for. Expecting a pleasant Valentines Day weekend, We were very displeased to walk into a lobby that smelled like the streets of South Boston after the St Patricks Day Parade. After locating the 2x2 window that the Front desk is in we made our way up to the room. The carpets have not been replaced since the building went up, the bed spread and curtains were as dirty as the lobby smelled, the chipped walls and peelling wallpaper added the worn look that unfortunately we were not looking for. THe room was furnished nicely and the pillows were comfortable, but I forgot my slippers so walking on the floor had to be done with caution.

name: Inn at the Market
title: “Great hotel in a perfect location”
text:
We stayed in the Inn at the start of a 3 week vacation and it was probably the best hotel we stayed in. The loaction in the heart of Pike Place market is fantastic for the first time visitor, and we've never had so much great fresh food on our doorstep before. The reception area was warm, peacefull and welcoming, and always had bowl of fresh cookies out every afternoon. 
The hotel isnt a moden statement of cutting edge design, but it fits in perfectly with its surrounding, and has a sophisticated, relaxing, and friendly ambiance. We did have a problem overly loud air conditioning in the room, but this was our only issue. Other than that the rooms were spacious, well designed, had great views, and were an unexpected highlight.

name: Harborside Inn
title: “Fantastic Boston Getaway”
text: We went to Boston for my 30th birthday and found this hotel online. I was nervous because some of the reviews stated there was rude staff and it was noisy. We found the exact opposite! The staff were very friendly and helpful the entire weekend. We stayed in a City View room and it was quiet for a city like Boston. We were able to walk to everything we wnated to do and the Market is directly across the street. I would most definitely stay here again and recommend it to other travelers!

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Very pleasant stay”
text: Great hotel in central position. Good facilities, nice restaurant but expensive. Staff excellent. Rooms a little tired and small.

name: InterContinental Boston
title: “Great hotel, bad location”
text: Hubby and I went to Boston to attend a jazz fest and just to get away from it all (if you know what I Mean!) location of this hotel was quite a distance from most points of interest so we rented a car instead of high taxi rates. Beautiful hotel, most of the service was great, did have a problem with the bar staff, which was resolved by bar manager. Suggested positive patron interaction program to alleviate this in the future. Food was expensive and not up to par for cost. Best things about hotel; bathroom impeccable with a great soaking tub and walk-in shower, toiletries not used as left behind a negative smell. The outside harbour area was perfect. We took our late night brandy there every evening and it proved to be very romantic!

name: Fairmont Battery Wharf
title: “Nice-but didn't feel like a Fairmont”
text: Arrived here after spending 2 days at the Four Seasons. I wanted to experience a water location to get a different Boston feel. The hotel is very nice and new. The room is very modern and well appointed. However, I was not overly impressed with the staff.
