Except for one very enthusiastic lady at the front desk, the staff seemed didn't seem very engaged or professional to me. This was not the level of service or vibe I was expecting from a Fairmont. I was surpised to find that I felt isolated on Battery Wharf. The North End is right at your doorstep and the Aquarium along with the closest subway stop is about a 10 minute walk. I just felt disconnected from the city. A very nice hotel but a little different than I was expecting.

name: Ames - A Morgans Original
title: “Great Hotel!”
text: We had a great stay at this hotel. Very modern and walking distance to everything. There is a subway stop just behind the hotel but we didn't use it as everything is so close. The room was a good size and very nice and bathroom modern and clean. The staff were friendly and provided great tips for places to eat. I would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to stay in Boston.

name: The Back Bay Hotel
title: “Lovely Hotel”
text: Had a lovely stay at this hotel. Great location. Friendly and helpful staff. Definitely worth staying here.

name: InterContinental Boston
title: “Fabulous Stay”
text:
We live locally in MA and decided to make a get-away trip to Boston. Using Priceline to book a room, we landed at the InterContinental Boston. The location was perfect, as it was walking distance to the subway, waterfront, downtown, and the Water Taxi to Charlestown. We got into Boston early on Saturday to secure a room. We requested a room facing the city and had no problem getting one. The hotel staff was very accommodating and curious. The room was nicely furnished and very clean. We didn't use the hotel restaurants or the pool/spa/fitness center. 
Couple Notes:
* The rooms facing the city are across from the Boston Fire/Ambulance Dept, which blows their sirens every time they enter/leave the firehouse. It could be disturbing.
* The RumBa hotel bar is a very popular place on the weekend. It was impossible to get seat in the bar and we had to wait a long time to get a drink. They also played the music very very loud. It's not a place to get a quiet drink on the weekend!
* The Sushi-Teq bar/restaurant had patio seating outside earlier in the evening, but we didn't make use of it. It was very elegant and quiet outside.

name: The Langham, Boston
title: “Small but clean room”
text:
The Langham has a great location with a few minutes easy walk from South Station and many of the sites along the Freedom Trail, including Faneuil Hall and Boston Common. It is in the financial district and near the Aquarium and Children's Museum. I stayed in a very small classic room with a nice bathroom. It was right at the elevators which was noisy especially in the evening and early morning. The room was clean, with a large flat-screen TV with amble stations, mini-bar, large closet and queen bed. The bed was comfortable but the pillows were very compressible and uncomfortable. Nightly turn-down service with chocolates, robes and slippers was a nice touch as were the nice toiletries from the hotel spa. Unfortunately, there was a very strong perfume smell in the bathroom and room which caused headaches and allergies. The wireless internet ($12/day) was very slow and inconsistent making it difficult to use. The hotel has a restaurant and a nice gym, indoor pool and spa. The gym had a nice selection of cardio equipment overlooking the pool as well as a weights area. 
Overall, the Langham is very nice and in a great location.

name: The Liberty Hotel
title: “Perfect!”
text: What a unique, memorable, nostalgic place! Everything from the exterior to the interior was incredible. The history of the place is both sad and intriguing. Clink was great. Rooms/service/food was phenomenal. There isn't even a need to go out at night to find nightlife, because on the weekend the place is hoppin'. Definitely worth checking out!

name: InterContinental Boston
title: “Loved this hotel!”
text: We booked this hotel through Hotwire, and loved it. I didn't mind that they charged for internet as we travel with a laptop and a broadband card, and our own small coffeepot: most high end hotels don't provide a coffeepot. I loved the details in the hotel: the doorbell for the room, the 'do not disturb' that was controlled inside the room [ever stayed somewhere that a kid put their sign on your room for kicks???} and just the lovely decor. We had a corner room with a great view; I didn't feel as though they discriminated against us because of getting the room on Hotwire; and the room was huge. I've stayed in places where the whole room was smaller than the Intercontinental's bathroom! We didn't eat in the hotel restaurants but they looked great. The short walk to the T was a great feature, as we don't keep a rental car when visiting Boston.

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Disappointed, but got it for a bargain”
text:
I managed to snag a great deal at this place last year from December 29-Jan 2nd, for $99/night. I'd never been to Boston and I was a member at Omni so I figured what the hell.
This hotel is part of all kinds of historical events and facts: it's one of the oldest hotels in America (of course, haunted too), it's where the Boston Creme Pie was invented and it's where JFK proposed to Jackie (awwwww).
The place is as grand as its history and is in a pretty good location. Right across from city hall and the commons, right on the Freedom Trail and about a ten minute walk from all of the North End restaurants.
Though the service is friendly and the hotel is aesthetically pleasing, I didn't find the atmosphere to be very nice. It's loaded with sloshed old people and weird out-of-towner-amateur-historians. As a 23 year-old, this is a little disconcerting, especially since we had to spend a lot of time there due to all the sleety, snowy icy mess outside. I took off a star because our room was dreadfully small and the walls were pretty thin. We didn't hear people having sex (this time) but we could hear everyone else's tv's. A second star was taken off because there was no wifi in the room even though we were select guests and receive free wifi. There was nothing they could do about it, apparently.
Still, this is a great hotel to start with and in a way better location than a lot of the other places I found and if I got a good deal, I'd probably stay here again.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square
title: “Hidden "gem". location and staff, enough said.”
text:
Frequently travel to Boston for work. Prior to my recent two night stay, I had never used this hotel. Moving forward- I'll only stay here.
Location- perfect nook right in the heart of the city. So surprised at proximity to just about everything Boston has to offer. 
Staff- They don't make them like this anymore
Added bonus: complimentary beer (good beer!), upon returning from a long work day. It's the little touches as such that put it in my category of a "gem".

name: The Langham, Boston
title: “Best Hotel!”
text: My husband and I stayed here for two nights (Sept. 22-23) and had the best stay. Everyone that worked at the hotel was professional and eager to make our stay as enjoyable as possible. The hotel is beautiful and our room (basic queen) was so cozy and roomy, I didn't want to leave it. I had requested a higher floor and we were placed on the top floor, which was nice. The hotel has an awesome bar/restaurant, BOND, which is really cool and cozy. The location of the hotel is PERFECT. I knew very little about Boston and I feel so lucky to have chosen this hotel. It was within walking distance to everything and only a few short blocks from Quincy Market where all the shops and restaurants are. If you book a room here, you will not be disappointed.

name: InterContinental Boston
title: “Nice notel. Great location”
text:
We really liked this hotel. We got a great deal direct from the hotel website. The room we had was massive and the bathroom was amazing. Although I really did not like the sliding window between the bathroom and bedroom ..... but that was just me.
The location was great. South station is only a few mins walk away from the hotel. In the other direction, you have a 10 min walk to the restaurants down at the aquarium.

name: The Langham, Boston
title: “Decent, but impersonal. And it needs some expenditure to bring it to par with competitors.”
text:
We stayed for two nights in October 2010. This hotel is handsome indeed, but has a more business-type feel to it than the likes of Back Bay Hotel or the Lenox.
Location:
- Well-located for business travellers due to its close proximity to pretty much every financial institution in Boston, a bit less attractive for Newbury St addicts. Although, keep in mind Boston is very walkable. If you shun the hotel restaurant for breakfast on weekend, you'll have a problem - there is a dearth of good options in that area. It is also not heavy on dinner choices (yes, Ruth's is close by), but you may walk to Chinatown for reasonable food (10-15mins).
Room:
- Superior King in our case. No surprises here for that category, although we wondered about the clunky CRT TV. No flatscreens in a 4-star hotel? It worked perfectly well, but it made me wonder the owner's willingness to cough up the capital expenditure to maintain such a huge outfit. They seem to have corrected it by now, still half a decade after most competitors.
- On the more important issue of cleanliness, we could not fault it. 
- Size was generous, both for the living area and the bath. The most striking feature were the huge windows, which opened the view over Post Office square towards some of the imposing (for Boston..) skyscrapers, which made a memorable impression at night.
Service
- Check-in/out was efficient; retrieving our bags from the storage room took a while, but overall everything seemed professional.
- Staff (both for room service and cleaning) was very friendly, which didn't do much to change the slightly impersonal feel of the place, however.
Overall Impression
- While there weren't any hiccups during our stay we came away unimpressed. Maybe the Langham appeals to the slightly "mature" traveller (we are in our early 30s); the atmosphere was more Old England than New England. Walking the corridors I thought it's a tad more stuffy than elegant or even luxurious, but of course that is a matter of personal taste. Objectively, it is a decent downtown option, not fancy but solid. It is just that you'll likely find better for pretty much the same price. 
Still, there seems to have been some upgrade going on (flatscreens..), so if you like the location, it is solid enough to at least give it a try.

name: Seaport Boston Hotel
title: “Excellent hotel in every way”
text: We were not disappointed with this excellent hotel when we stayed there in August. Lovely rooms, great view, easy to get to (there is an airport bus which drops you right outside and is free at arrivals), first class concierge and delicious breakfasts. The reception staff could not do enough for us from printing out emails to booking a restaurant, organising tours, the lot. Waiting staff in the restaurant were delightful and efficient. Happy to recommend and even more happy to return there in the future.

name: Inn at the Market
title: “Great Location and Great Place to Stay!!”
text: You can't beat this location, just a few feet from Pike's Market. It was pouring down rain during our stay so being close to the Market and all the attractions was fantastic. The hotel was very nice, clean rooms, great views. Would love to come back and stay here again.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square
title: “Possibly the cleanest, friendliest, most comfortable hotel I've experienced”
text:
I have just completed an eight night stay at this hotel. This was my first time in Boston (which I loved) and I am so pleased I chose this hotel. The first thing I always look for in a room is how clean it is. This room was spotless and was kept that way through the whole week. The staff who work here are first class.....I am not usually gushing in praise when I write reviews, but if a team do their job better than anyone else then they deserve the praise.
Some notes on the practical points....
The room was a fairly average room size. Not huge but more than adequate.
The internet from the room worked well. I also used the computer and printer in the lounge to print off my boarding passes for the trip home.
The bed was excellent and I think that because the room was also quiet (despite the hotel being full) I had the best sleep in a hotel I have ever had.
The bathroom was nice and included a bath....how much can you say about a bathroom?
I had breakfast in the dining room most mornings. This was OK. Not a lot of variety , though. Eggs, sausages, bacon, toast or you could have cereals or make a waffle.
I was able to leave my bags there after checkout which was very handy given I had a late flight out.
It also had the subway very close and was within easy walking distance to the theatre district, the symphony hall, the Boston Common and transport centre.
If I am fortunate enough to go to Boston again this is where I will stay. Loved it!
I would have no hesitation in recommending this

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Very disappointing”
text:
Straight the the points... Dirty sheets (!), peeling wallpaper, chipped paint, fruitflies all over the room(!), poorly positioned bathroom shelving (my toothbrush went into the toilet!). No mouthwash. No fridge. Loud annoying AC. And best of all, I was late for my meeting because the stupid shower didn't work. Just dribbled water on me.
This is an Omni??
I stayed here for a convention on Sep12. They may have given me a rarely-used room (maybe it was a handicap room?), but it doesn't excuse the conditions. I let them know about it and while the did fix the shower, making it barely usable instead of non-functioning... they didn't address the other items at all.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square
title: “Great Stay”
text: This Marriott was a great hotel. The front desk staff was very helpful. They even made us a reservation at a restaurant and we did not have to wait to be seated. They also gave us suggestions about where to go out to eat, bars and shopping. The room was very spacious and clean. I would recommend this hotel to anyone.

name: Nine Zero Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Location, location, location!”
text: The Nine Zero has a great location, nice view, and an interesting contemporary decor. We got a clean and spacious corner room (805). They offer a happy hour with surprisingly pretty good wine @ 5pm. The room temperature did not go lower than 72 even though the thermostat would go down to 62. My guess is that the a/c does not have the adequate capacity for the room. Bed and pillows are fine (could be better), perhaps is about time to get new ones. Not too bad but if you want a cool room to sleep this particular one would not do it. We had breakfast at their restaurant one morning and the food was simply ok. Spent $38 for breakfast for ONE person including tax and tip! We did not have a car so did not have to worry about parking. If you are thinking about renting a car in Boston, think again, it is almost impossible to find a parking spot without paying a fortune. I would definitely stay here again and skip their restaurant.

name: Mandarin Oriental, Boston
title: “Great Location but Some Service Issues”
text:
The Location is amazing-best place in Boston
Great Restaurants within the Hotel--all have excellent food!!
The Spa is amazing--a must!!!
Rooms are very nice--comfortable--well appointed. Rain shower are fantastic but read below.
However, there were several service issues that you would not expect at a Mandarin Oriental. When we checked in the front desk person asked us if we would like to have a welcome drink sent to our room as is done at MO hotels. They forgot to send it. When I told the staff that we are going out and that they had forgotten to send the drinks he apologized and promised to send it in the evening. They forgot again. That evening when I took a shower I noticed the shower pressure was very weak. I asked if someone could take a look at the shower. Engineering came up right away. They recommended that we change our room since it will take a while to fix. We stopped by the front desk to check about moving our room and they wanted to put us in a smaller room on a lower floor. So we decided to stay in our original room since engineering made a temporary fix. Two days later the handle to our shower fell off in the shower while housekeeping was cleaning the room. Instead of having it fixed they simply left the handle on the bathroom counter. We had also gone out and purchased sparking water bottles for each of our bedsides. Housekeeping would take both bottles and put them up on the bar each day rather than leaving them on each side of the bed. So we would not know which bottle was who's. 
This is a great hotel and we would definitely go back. Hopefully the service hiccups will be fixed next time.

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Worst Hotel Experience of my life!”
text: Not only is this hotel grossly overpriced, they could care less about you as a guest! I used their Valet service during my stay in September 2011 and my vehicle was damaged by their company. They decided to forge the valet ticket saying the damage already existed on my car which is a complete lie! When i gave them my car, there was not damage, and when I get it back there is damage? And they refuse to pay for the repair??? This is NOT the way to run a hotel. I will NEVER stay at another Omni hotel and I will make sure my friends and everyone I talk to knows about this terrible experience with them.

name: Nine Zero Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Classy, Elegant Hotel”
text: My daughter and I stayed overnight at the hotel. I was greeted by a very friendly check-in gal, who just happened to be a UNLV Graduate (Go REBELS) like myself. We got there 3 hours before check-in time and I thought we would only be able to leave our luggage, but we were able to get right into room, drop off our luggage and go sight-seeing. The room was large, very comfortable king-size bed, large bathroom (even a robe for you if you need one), large LED flatscreen, loaded bar and snacks, and even a radio that you could attach an Ipod too. The hotel is in a great location: A less then 5-minute walk from the Park St. T; the Boston Common, the wharf, Quincy Market, etc. We had breakfast at the hotel, and although a little pricey, the portions were very generous, and the service impeccable. The entire hotel has this very hip-classy vibe to it, and the staff were all very friendly and helpful. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone visiting the Boston area.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square
title: “octoberfest!”
text: Stayed at this hotel on their Sam Adams getaway package and it was awesome! Rate included 6 beers, some souvenirs and breakfast. Staff was great - room was bigger then I thought considering it's a downtown hotel. I already have my reservation to go back for the tree lighting in faneul hall

name: Boston Marriott Long Wharf
title: “Good central location”
text: On stopovers on my way to or from Europe, I usually stay either here or the Hilton at the airport. The Long Whart is getting a little long in the tooth and could stand some rennovations, but still it is a competent hotel only a few yards from the most "high value" sites in Boston. The cab ride from the airport to the hotel has gone up considerably over the years but it's good if you are "on your way through" and have a little time to do some sightseeing.

name: The Liberty Hotel
title: “Great soundproof rooms, large clean bathrm, and friendly check-in, but loud foyer parties, even on the weeknight”
text:
I've stayed in October 2010 and in spring of 2010 (I think it was April or May). Both times, the check-in staff were friendly and helpful and answered all my questions. Both times I arrived on a weekend evening to a loud party happening in the foyer. I actually had to yell at the check-in staff in between pauses for music but eventually got my questions across. Upon arrival at the room, both times, the room was spacious, away from the elevator, and with soundproof walls. I was actually surprised the first time to find out that we had neighbours beside us. Would definitely recommend both restaurants - Italian specialty for brunch was nicer than normal and about $30 per person. Dinner we had one night at the restaurant on the 3rd floor and that was delicious and the service was excellenet. Dinner was about $180 for two with a bottle of wine. We both had an appetizer and a main course and a coffee / tea for dessert. Tip was extra and we paid that in cash.
I had friends come to pick me up twice. parking is an issue, but they let them wait in the roundabout for me. Also, upon being dropped off at night. There is usually a huge crowd outside trying to get as near to the outdoor heaters as possible. They don't part to allow you entrance into the hotel and the valet and concierge do not ask them to part to allow ease of entry. I think this part could be improved. They should add an extra covered area to the side for the people waiting for rides/friends or wanting to smoke. There should be no obstructions for patrons wanting to enter the hotel. Someone told me that this happens often as the The Liberty is a "trendy" place to be for dinner and "hot spot" for night life. 10 years ago, this would have been great for me. Now it's just annoying when you've been on a plane / airport for a few hours and just want to get your travel portion over and done with as quickly and quietly as possible. 
Except for the entrance way pile up at nights (yes - even on weeknights), I loved the hotel, it's staff and it's more than ample and clean bathrooms. I love their towels.

name: Inn at the Market
title: “The Benchmark for quality and service”
text: We have just stayed four nights at The Inn at the Market hotel in Seattle and can do nothing but highly recommend it to other travellers. We had a partial water view room that overlooked the patio area and water, which we booked via the Internet. The room was large, spotlessly clean as was the bathroom and the hotel generally. Any question or request made to the hotel reception staff was dealt with efficiently and all in a warm and friendly manner. The hotel is located just metres away from the Pike Market and Aquarium, and the water front activities in general. Being an avid tea drinker I find that you can not make tea in a coffee pot and when I requested a kettle it was delivered virtually before I hung up the phone. Guests are invited to use the patio area, and to even take snacks, food and drink up to the patio. The hotel uses Bacco Restaraunt for breakfast in room service, which we did not use as in room service, but we did have breakfast there on our last day and it was very good value for money and excellent food. If/when we return to Seattle we will definitely be staying at Inn at the Market.

name: The Langham, Boston
title: “Best hotel in the city”
text: If you like to be catered to and treated like a VIP this is the hotel for you. From the minute the doorman greets you till the time you check out the staff makes you feel special. For a special weekend or just a visit to the city this is the place to stay. We have been back once or twice a year for the past 5 years and never had a complaint. They get ***** 5 stars from us...

name: The Langham, Boston
title: “Great location and staff”
text:
We had three nights at the Langham as the final stage of two weeks in NYS and Massachussets.
When we arrived the reception staff looked after the children while we returned our hire car.
The concierge organised whale watching trips for us and were happy to advise us on places to go and eat.
One evening, on our way out for dinner, our daughter was crying because she had lost a toy. The reception staff were very concerned for her. When we returned to our room we found a tray with milk, lemonade and an enormous plate of cookies had been left for her. 
We didn't use any of the hotel facilities as we were only there a short time but we fell in love with Boston and when we return for a longer visit in 2012 the Langham will be our preferred hotel.

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Comfortable, Clean, Extremely Convenient”
text: Excellent Back Bay location: Prudential "T" station just steps from entrance and across street from Prudential Center restaurants & shops. Twenty minute walk to Fenway. In-house restaurant fare is good/not great but all hotel/restaurant staff friendly, responsive, and kid-friendly. Rooms stylish, well-maintained, clean and comfortable. Roof-top pool great place to cool off.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square
title: “Great location, great service, tiny room”
text: We just stayed here for 4 nights for leisure. The plus - the service was great and the location was excellent. We could walk to many attractions. There is also a grocery store across the street (Shaws), which was great for stocking up on snacks and drinks. They provide an in room cooler, but did bring us a refrigerator upon request. The only minus is that the rooms were so tiny - the smallest I have ever stayed in. But it is fine if you are just in the room for sleeping. The black out curtians worked well and I got some great sleep here.

name: InterContinental Boston
title: “Awesome hotel”
text: We got this hotel for $120 on Priceline on July 4, which is a great deal. The hotel opened only 3 months ago, so everything is brand new. The employees are all very friendly and helpful and the room was great. The bed was very comfortable. The shower was great and separate from the tub area. There was a sliding window by the bed to look into the bathroom area. Flat screen tv with many channels. The fitness area was great for a hotel, but the pool area was very limited and there were only a couple of chairs to sit on. Also, it is a lap pool, but it is only 3 ft deep, hardly deep enough to do laps and there were unsupervised kids all over the pool, preventing anyone trying to actually do laps from swimming. Valet parking is a bit pricey, $39 for 24 hrs, but that's to be expected in a city. If you do go, check out Fajitas & Ritas Mexican restaurant near Boston Commons. There is also a restaurant you can walk to that's two blocks away, the Barking Crab, which is awesome. Overall, a very nice hotel.

name: Boston Marriott Long Wharf
title: “Great service and location”
text: We were very happy with the parking and service. The staff were very educated about the area and offered to help with everything. We were able to check in early and leave our car there until 6:00 p.m. the following day. The location was perfect, the T and aquarium are right next to the hotel. Quincy Market is across the street. The room was clean and nicely setup. We have two small children and the pool was a nice treat. Our only compliant was the noise level from the hallway during the night. We were woken up several times by other loud guests returning from a night of partying.

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Location for the Freedom trail is perfect!”
text: The staff of the hotel was very accomodating and gracious. Had a wonderful 2 night stay on my own. As a woman traveling on my own, I felt very safe. The room was clean, the bed linens plush and the housekeeping staff very prompt. Rooms are a bit small but have all amenities. The location on the Freedom Trail was a great surprise to me. I was able to dash out for a few hours of sightseeing and shopping and it was all close by,

name: The Liberty Hotel
title: “Best Hotel I've ever stayed at!”
text:
This is a truly stunning hotel! Words cannot do justice to this place. Of all the hotels I''ve ever stayed at, this tops the list.
During the booking process, I had a few preliminary queries which Jackie dealt with using great proficciency. Upon arrival at the hotel, you are made feel like royalty. The doorman was very welcomming and polite. On entering the hotel, the wow factor kicks in. 
The reception atrium is stunning and is a fantastic transformation of this former prison. Dakota checked me in and was exceptionally friendly and welcoming. He assisted me with all my queries (as it was my first time in Boston, I had many!). 
The room was amazing. The view over the river and the city is second to none. The pros in the room included the very comfortable bed, oversized bath, separate large shower, very extensive minibar, molton brown products, excellent phone system that has links to weather, flight information, news etc. A separate mention must go to the complimentary wifi access. It is a complete rip off the way other hotels charge for internet usage. So well done to the Liberty for not ripping us off by charging! 
Other attractions in the hotel include a well equipped gym, a funky and very buzzing atmosphere in the trendiest lobby I have ever seen. The bar is hopping from about 8 onwards and because it is in the lobby, it adds to the atmosphere of the atrium. 
I had dinner in the restaurant at the bar which was a fun dining experience. A very very friendly waitress gave me great recommendations including a cosmo made from cucumber pulp! Delicious. 
The concierge (from Wexford) was wonderful to deal and made some great recommendations for breakfast, sightseeing and many other wonderful things. 
The Liberty made my stay in Boston perfect. I would have no hesitation at recommending this hotel and cannot wait to return

name: The Langham, Boston
title: “Major Disappointment”
text:
I just spent one evening (Sat 13th) at the Langham and was very unimpressed by the hotel itself and the service provided.
This was a valentines day getaway with the g/f. Trip was booked through hotwire so I didn't know what I was getting but the rate for a 4.5 star hotel was very good. Unfortunately The Langham is at best a 4 star and probably closer to a 3.5 star hotel even without any issues.
Prior to arriving I called the concierge to order the "rose petal turn down service" I explained to the concierge that this was a surprise for my g/f and that we would be going to dinner at 8:30 so they could come anytime after that.
Upon arrival the hotel is very unimpressive at first glance. I expect a very nice foyer for a 4.5 star hotel. The foyer to the Langham looks more like a Holiday Inn. Low ceilings and nothing eye catching whatsoever.
Check=in moved briskly and the front desk was very courteous and did take the time to explain where the restaurants, fitness center and other services can be found. I thought this was a very nice touch.
The room itself was average for Boston. I did get one of the worst rooms available, I guess that happens when you book through a discount site. The queen bed was fairly stiff but not horrible. The room itself was furnished in an older style. The furnishings were OK but nothing special and the TV was below average for even a 4 star hotel.
The room amenities were quite nice, particularly the robe and toiletries. 
So far I would have been satisfied if this was a 3.5-4 star hotel, but this was clearly not a 4.5 star hotel.
After settling in we decided to go to Bond for a pre-dinner drink and app. WOW is the first word that comes to mind when you see this place. It is a really spectacular lounge with the huge chandeliers, low slung seating and beautiful mirror back bar. Unfortunately this luxury comes with a price and that price is steep if you want one of their signature cocktails. We did enjoy the two martini's we had but I'm not sure they were worth $14. As for the apps, they were also pricey but they were worth every penny. We shared the fried calamari with thai chili sauce and lobster pot pie. Both were simply outstanding dishes. The Calamari were quite large, cooked perfectly and accompanied by a sauce that was the perfect blend of tangy, sweet and spicy. The Lobster pot pie was equally outstanding, large chunks of lobster were combined with potatoes and chantrelle mushrooms. 
After our $90 pre-dinner drinks and apps we headed up to the room to get ready for dinner. At 8:00 PM we got a knock at our door, luckily I answered the door and the g/f was busy getting ready so she didn't hear me ask the hotel staffer to come back after 8:30 for the turndown service. Had she answered the door the surprise would have been blown.
After a wonderful dinner we head back to the room to put our leftovers in the fridge before going back to Bond for a night cap. It was around 10PM and I was a bit surprised that the rose petal turn down hadn't happened yet. Still being V-days weekend, I assumed they were busy and would get to us eventually.
After a few more martini's we head up to the room a little after midnight, sadly still no roses. Guess the surprise is now on me.
Things only got worse as I tried to sleep with what sounded like a train station running underneath our hotel room. I know other people complained about the sound but I really didn't think it would bother me. Again joke's on me, it was horrible and only the booze helped me fall asleep.
Checkout the next morning went smooth and they did apologize twice for missing the turn down (though on V-day weekend, forgetting roses isn't really acceptable).
Outside of Bond, nothing stands out at the Langham which makes it critically important that they nail all the little details. Unfortunately, for me at least, they failed miserably.
Overall this is at best a 4 star hotel, if you go there expecting something akin to the Park Plaza Hotel (in a worse location) you should be satisfied. If you go there expecting the Boston Harbor Hotel, you will be disappointed like I was.

name: The Westin Copley Place
title: “Nice Hotel”
text: Very nice hotel, located in downtown at Boston. Just a little expensive, but a good service. They have many events, I went to the Biomedical Conferences 2010.

name: The Westin Copley Place
title: “Very Beautiful hotel but located away from the spot light.”
text: This is a very beautiful hotel. The room service was very good. The hotel is very clean. My wife and I stayed here for the Red Sox game at Fenway. It is located at the very end of Huntington Ave and is not near any of the restaurants or Fenway. It is a good location for access to the Mass Pike. There is no on street parking in the area but it's like this any where in Boston. I think the parking rate was like $35 a night. The Hotel food was average but the lunch menu was very minimal at the best. It's definitely nicer then some of the other hotels that are closer to Fenway.

name: The Liberty Hotel
title: “Superb”
text:
The hotel is lovely and the food is outstanding. Try the flatbreads and the mozzarella apps - unusual and tasty. Great for Techies; young and old. Great nightlife, but the rooms are quiet. Bloody Mary bar is a must if you are a fan. ALL the restaurants were great. Could have eaten in the City, but chose to eat at the hotel and we were not disappointed. 
Great view, wonderful beds, luxe baths. Loved it and will return.
Highly recommend. But be aware - it is a bit on the pricey side. We felt it was worth the splurge.

name: The Inn At St Botolph
title: “Great Room, Great Location”
text: We stayed in Room 301 (deluxe 1 bedroom suite). The room was spacious, clean and well equiped, and great value for money). We loved the check-in system (key pad coded for both main entrance, and room), and the privacy that it gave us. We also enjoyed the extensive channel options on both of the TV's. The hotel is on a quiet street, yet only 100 yards from the Prudential Centre and the T. Also, for sports fans, a short walk to Fenway.

name: Marriott's Custom House
title: “Small children love the Custom House!”
text:
We stayed at the Custom House from June 29th to July 3rd, 2008. I can't say enough great things about this place. If you can spend the money, stay here with small children! Paid $329 per night on Priceline last -minute for a 1 bedroom suite. Arrived and got a 19th floor harborview 1 bedroom suite which was amazing. 1st time in Boston, traveling with 9 mo old and 4 yr old. Perfect location - Faneuil Hall/Quincy Marketplace, Aquarium/Imax, horsedrawn charriages, trolley and boat tours all within 1-2 blocks. Little Italy, parks with playgrounds within 5 minute walk. Boston Common within 10-12 minutes. T (subway) station and a 24 hr market right out the front door - don't even need to cross the street. 
Game room with ping pong, air hockey, video games and even a train table (4 yo was in heaven - but BYOT - bring your own trains) on the 24th floor. 26th floor has an observation deck with amazing 360 degree views of city, harbor, accessible ONLY to hotel guests - another awesome perk. Game room has vending machines for snacks and several washers and dryers. Laundry was free to guests and room includes one package of Tide, can buy more at front desk. We did laundry while 4yo played trains! For those without small kids, every evening offered an interesting speaker - wish we could have attended. 
Downside - breakfast not included, but is offered for a small fee on 1st floor daily. No hotel restaurant, but Faneuil Hall has dozens of restaurants in and out of its food court one-half block away. 
One tip - best place for baby food and diapers was Rite-aid several blocks away across from City Hall - rest of food could be found at the 24 hr market outside the hotel. Rooms clean enough that I let our 9 mo old crawl on the floor, which I rarely do. Finally, the hotel has their own off-street court for unloading, so no rushed frenzy to load/unload the car and all your stuff with small kids - plenty of space and didn't feel rushed even in peak travel season. Enjoy- this place is wonderful!

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Excellent Location, Comfortable Stay”
text:
Excellent location in the heart of Boston, across from the magnificent Prudential Center, close to Boston's Northeastern University, Berkley College of Music, Boston University, and MFA. Elegant and very comfortable accomodations. Room lacks from a bit of space in the double room. I personally don't like the A/C systems that are set to AUTO... so in the middle of the night it shuts down and room gets warm... and this was during Thanksgiving weekend 2011. 
Excellent service overall. A give it a 4.5.

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Rooftop pool - wow!”
text:
We've been to Boston a few times and stayed in a variety of four star hotels. Really rated the Colonnade Hotel. It seemed less touristy than most. I think it is probably used more by business men/women and not used by the main tour organisers. That could explain the good value at weekends. 
Good service, friendly and relaxed. Decent beds/bedding and everything worked. Brasserie Jo great for casual meal and had a nice laid-back atmosphere - just like Boston.
The rooftop swimming pool and bar was a great hit with all the family. A brilliant place to chill out after a day of sightseeing. Views over reflecting pool etc. pretty special too.
Can't wait to go back!

name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square
title: “Excelente zona”
text: Muy buen hotel para familias en una inmejorable zona. Las habitaciones son cómódas y con buen servicio de limpieza. El personal muy amable. Frente al hotel está el Prudential Center Plaza, que es un centro comercial con buenas tiendas y restaurantes. A la espalda del hotel está la zona de Back Bay que está poblada de tiendas y restaurantes. Lo recomiendo 100%.

name: The Langham, Boston
title: “wonderful stay”
text: Enjoyed a four day stay at the Langham. The staff was lovely - doormen even remembered our name. The spa was great - brand new and the pool and hot tub were great. We had a corner room, 801 with two double beds and a couch as well - very large room with a nice view of the park. Only would change the restaurante as was a bit pricey for the food quality but overall a great stay.

name: Ames - A Morgans Original
title: “Lungo il Freedom Trail”
text: Localizzato nel restaurato Ames Building, interessante edificio storico all'incrocio di Court St e Washington St, è arredato con mobili di design con piacevole contrasto con la struttura dell'edificio. Abbiamo soggiornato in questo hotel per tre giorni prima di iniziare in auto il nostro giro nel New England. É un hotel frequentato sia da turisti che da professionisti delle banche di Downtown. Il nostro giudizio é positivo per i servizi offerti, per il veloce check in e out e l'abbondante colazione. Per i turisti è possibile utilizzare gratuitamente biciclette dell'hotel. Ottima opportunitá che ci ha permesso di scoprire Boston in modo insolito. Da consigliare.

name: Inn at the Market
title: “Lovely hotel, superb location”
text:
Stayed for 5 nights in this hotel having booked it for our city break to Seattle after having read the good reviews on Tripadvisor. The reviews hardly did the hotel justice which was just about perfect in every way. The room was spacious and spotlessly clean, the view from the hotel deck over the Puget Sound was just breathtaking and the staff could not have been of more help. However the best bit about the hotel was its location "in the Market". It was ideally placed for Pike Place Market, shopping, various other attractions and a whole host of excellent restaurants.
I would definitely recommend this hotel and will stay there again if we ever return to Seattle

name: The Back Bay Hotel
title: “Chic hotel in great location”
text: Nice place to stay-got a great deal on a special from another site. Contemporary decor, clean, nicely done.

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Colonnade Hotel in Boston made my trip so wonderful!!”
text: The Colonnade Hotel in Boston is a wonderful hotel. It is very well situated in Back Bay, near all the action but also near some beautiful residential neighbourhoods. The hotel is modern, very clean and the all staff from the doormen to the cleaning staff and best of all the concierge were very friendly and did their best to make my trip better than I had expected. Jerry Good, the unbelievable concierge, truly went out of his way to arrange reservations and even had a surprise waiting for my daughter and myself at one of the best restaurants. This was supposed to have been just a nice 4 day trip for my daughter and myself but, in large part to the satff at The Colonnade, it was a trip to remember!! Thank you Colonnade!

name: Marriott's Custom House
title: “I feel like i'm home”
text:
Custom House Marriott is the best hotel for any one travelling to Boston! Whether you are a business traveller or vacation with your family, the hotel offers very spacious rooms (size of a small 1 bedroom appartment, with a separate bathroom, bedroom and livingroom/kitchen). The rooms are very clean. With 2 TVs we were able to enjoy our TV shows while the kids watched their show in the other room. 
Hotel also contains:
- Gym
- Washing machines 
- Play room (pool table and video games)
The hotel is close to restaurants, pubs, tourist attractions and great shopping. 
I travel to Boston very often and I love staying at this hotel.

name: The Fairmont Copley Plaza, Boston
title: “Great Location-Average Hotel”
text: Stayed at this hotel for 3 days with teenage son recently. It is very well located in central Copley square, only 1 block each from both the Green and Orange lines of the "T". I should add that the subway is the best way to get around Boston. Anyone willing to compete with the aggressive drivers is nuts. The hotel is old and ornate, with a beautiful lobby, but it's aging and the Deluxe room we had was a little tired and faded. The bathroom was small with a door that would not fully close and the walk in closet had a defective light that they could not fix. The hotel was busy and noisy with lots going on like meetings, proms, etc. so be prepared. I also thought the staff, particularly the concierges were not that friendly or extremely helpful. The hotel has one very formal restaurant and no casual coffee shop, so we ended up having breakfast at a Starbucks on the corner. Bottom line: We paid a discounted corporate rate so I was happy with the value received. But I would fell differently if I had paid the rack rate.

name: Ames - A Morgans Original
title: “Bel hôtel bien placé et personnel serviable.”
text:
Hôtel idéalement situé (à 2 pas du city hall). La décoration est moderne et agréable.
Ma chambre était relativement spacieuse, fonctionnelle et au goût du jour (cependant un peu sombre). 
Le personnel est très accueillant, sympathique et serviable. Je confirme l'efficacité et la gentillesse de Nina Sweet. 
Le restaurant est bon mais un peu cher.

name: The Liberty Hotel
title: “Pure Luxury”
text:
Our fifth stay was as fantastic as our first stay in this superb hotel, which is a brilliant and award winning makeover from Boston's notorious old Charles Street Jail (which was Court-ordered to close several decades ago because of overcrowding).
The comfort of the rooms, world class quality of the food outlets, and especially the excellent level of personal service will continue to bring us back to the Liberty Hotel again and again.

name: Nine Zero Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Simply great”
text: We have stayed twice at this hotel over the course of 5 years and enjoyed it tremendously both times. It is a very stylish, and comfortable hotel. The rooms are modern, cozy and quiet. The staff is attentive, and the location is just perfect. There is a very popular wine happy hour in the lounge, from which you can overlook Tremont Street. Perfect for a pleasant stay in Boston!

name: Harborside Inn
title: “Fantastic Hotel - Will stay again!!!”
text: What a great place! located near everything you want and need to see in Boston. Lovely old charm, wonderful & helpful staff, very comfortable & clean rooms with all the nice amenities! Computers for guest use in the lobby. 24hr coffee/tea in lobby as well. Comfy big chairs and couches to read the morning paper in the lobby. We walked to Fanuiel Hall, super Pubs, restaurants, historic sights, the harbor, took the subway to Harvard, walked to Beacon Hill, Newberry, the Commons. Our favorite area was the North End...only 15 min walk from the Hotel. LOVE the coffees and pastries at Mike's and Modern Pastry too. the BEST ever!! Such a friendly city....this Hotel is not to be missed. You do not need a car or a taxi. You are in the heart of this lovely historic city!!!!! I highly suggest you stay nowhere else! did I mention the hotel rate is cheaper than most? can't beat it!

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “Great for conferences”
text:
I was pretty worried what my conference was going to be like. Some of the reviews across the internet expressed pretty negative opinions about the Boston Park Plaza. 
This place is great for conferences. The facilities are more than adequate. The staff gets the job done without being obtrusive. The location allows many options for meals and other outings. There is a great park not even a block away.
I would definitely stay here again and would recommend the Boston Park Plaza for any business conference.

name: enVision Hotel Boston
title: “Loud and disappointing stay”
text:
We arrived in Boston on August 22nd for our one night stay ~ we had booked online with hte hotel as they had a decent promotion on and although it was out of the way of downtown Boston we were there to see a Red Sox game so its walking proximity to there was our deciding factor. We got there easily on public transit, area seems a bit sketchy but we were only there one night so it was fine and we didnt encounter any issues that way.
The Good:
Hotel was lovely ~ clean fresh staff was friendly and helpful upon check in even printing us out walking directions to Fenway form the Hotel.
Room was big and clean and everything we needed was there ~ no complaints on appearance.
The Bad:
We were in an underground room ~ OMG LOUD LOUD LOUD ~ no sleep ~ clanking and shaking all night/into the morning I have never experienced anything like that at all in a hotel EVER!!!! I have no idea what it was or why as when we went to check out in the morning and I complained I was met with "oh thats too bad Im sorry ~ then presented my bill ~ I said is there no one we can tlak to abolut this? She said not really sorry. 
HORRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE~~~ Even an explanation at that point would have been nice but I got nothing ~ I much rather would have paid more to stay somewhere where I could have slept!
My only other caution is that there is nothing in the way of amenities for food and drink after hours which although wouldnt be a deciding factor for us would have been nice to know upon booking as we were starving after the game got back to the hotel and realized there were no food options for us close by at all!!
If you want to keep return clientelle i would suggest that you A) stop putting people below ground and B) address their concerns upon checkout

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “Ideal in every way”
text: I hve recently returned from a third stay at The Lenox in Boston, Boston is a vibrant, interesting and civilised city and The Lenox is ideally positioned to enjoy every aspect of the place. We walked to the river, for a pleasant stroll before unpacking. There are two huge malls a few minutes walk from the hotel, Boston Library is almost next door, the subway station is closer still and there is a massive supermarket nearby too. The welcome upon arrival is warm; the staff are exceptionally helpful and friendly and can provide any information needed to enhance once's stay. The rooms are comfortable and the reception areas particularly pleasant. We will be back.

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “Poor hotel”
text:
I must say this among the worst hotel to stay. They charged me USD 320 per day without breakfast and were poor in all sence. Smallest room size as if you are staying in a store. I would rate this hotel as one hotel which is just charging for its location. Guys please do not stay here. Only good thing was breakfast which they charges USD 26 separately apart from this it is all [--].
Television remote not working... enter the room and you end up lying on the small 4*6 bed not even double bed, old building at a great location.

name: Nine Zero Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Modern, but very comfortable.”
text:
We booked this hotel for four nights. We arrived there a bit early but could check in straight away, we were given breakfast vouchers which we were not expecting. The receptionist came around to the front of the desk to show us where the lifts were, which was a nice touch, and told us that wine was served between 5.00 and 6.00pm every day in the reception area.
The room was excellent, lovely large bed with feather pillows, I was a bit worried as the interior is very modern, but all the furniture was very comfortable, including two lovely armchairs in the bedroom. The only downside was that we didn't have a view, but there again we were out every day.
We went down to the reception area at 5.00pm and had more than one glass of wine! a very nice touch.
Benjamin the "bellboy" was more than helpful, he really couldn't do enough, he would suggest where to go and eat and he always asked us if we had enjoyed our day. Would we stay there again, definately.

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Extreamly nice hotel”
text: Great location, luxurious and overall very nice hotel with extreamly helpful and friendly staff. Room was big and beds very comfortable. Internet access possible through the flat screen TV in the room. To mention somtething that could be improved, it would be the sound/noise isolation of the door to the hallway.

name: The Fairmont Copley Plaza, Boston
title: “A fantastic business experience...”
text: From top to bottom, this hotel is the perfect location for conventions. Ideally placed, grand, and more than hospitable for not only transient guests but for the business world as well. I recommend this hotel for either.

name: Inn at the Market
title: “Excellent location for Pike Place Market”
text:
We stayed for three nights as part of our Silver Wedding Anniversary trip around the West Coast. The hotel had kindly left a card and chocolate covered strawberries in our room, which was a lovely gesture.
The hotel is only a couple of minutes walk from Pike Place Market, one of the best markets I've ever seen and made me wish we had such quality markets in England.
The hotel reception staff and the valet staff were very helpful and their welcome was very warm, which is unusual for large hotels.
I wouldn't hesitate to recommend Inn at the Market as a great place to stay.

name: Boston Marriott Copley Place
title: “great hotel”
text:
Stayed at the Marriott Copley Place for a weekend recently and was very impressed. The room was clean ( and I am very picky about cleanliness at hotels) and everything worked properly. The view was great and the bedding is very nice with washable duvets. My children enjoyed the swimming pool, which was nice and warm and not too crowded. The restaurant was good for the breakfast buffet. Location was very close to shopping via covered walkways and also close to T stops and Boston Common and area restaurants.
I would definitely stay here again while in Boston.

name: Inn at the Market
title: “Great place to stay in Seattle”
text: Inn at the Market is a wonderful place to stay in Seattle. The expense is a bit more then I usually spend but it was worth it because the hotel is located right next to Pike's Place Market. The view can't be beat in all Seattle. There's a wonderful balcony to watch a romantic sunset. When checking in at the hotel my husband and I were pleasantly surprised to receive a room upgrade to a suite. Since we were celebrating our anniversary it made the stay that much more special. I only wish we were able to stay a little longer then planned. The bed was very comfortable due to the quality of the mattress. I wanted to take it home with me. The front desk staff were very helpful in making a dinner recommendation and reservation for us. Again we were surprised when we were greeted at the restaurant (Cutter's) with ribbon decorations and a candle on the table. The hotel treated us to an appetizer also. We felt like VIPs. I recommend the Inn at the Market for a romantic getaway in an exciting city.

name: Harborside Inn
title: “Great location!!”
text:
This was our first trip to Boston, to celebrate our 22nd wedding anniversary and we had enjoyable stay at the Haborside Inn of Boston. It doesn't have all fancy amenities as the other major hotels. But if your looking for quiet and romantic weekend this is the place to stay. This hotel is in a perfect location and within minutes of everything, like subway, Quincy Market and Faneuil Hall. The staff was nice and helpful and the rooms were comfortable and clean. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone. We would stay there again.
Regards,
CTP

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Boston in style”
text:
Our stay at Omni Parker House just place us in a relax ambiance after our stay in N.Y.
Luxure, attention service, good restaurant in the hôtel and near by.
Just on the other side of the street, you'll find the best steak house on the East side of Norh America. No, I'm not joking, go and try RUTH'S CHRIS STEAK HOUSE. It worth the detour.

name: Harborside Inn
title: “no frills,immaculate room, shabby furniture in lobby”
text: the location was perfect to sites and the T. the staff was courteous and very helpful, however ,there was no one to help with our luggage checking in or out. the room was rather small but immaculate.the furniture in the lobby was frayed and really needed to be replaced. we went to the marriott long wharf ,had a delicious breakfast ,and decided to cool off there in their beautiful lobby for a few hours. that worked for us.

name: Omni Parker House
title: “A good hotel, well positioned for the historic sights.”
text:
An old, formal hotel in appearance but with high standards and good quality service.
Well positioned in the centre of the city and close to most of the historic sights.
Good service but a little expensive for extras not pre booked, for example breakfast and meals.

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “Fabulous hotel, great location and service”
text: Second time we stayed here and the Lenox is as fabulous as we remembered it from last year. The rooms were large and light, beds were comfortable, and the service impeccable. My only complaint is the lack of hot water /coffee pot in the rooms as is common in many hotels these days. I look forward to my next trip to Boston, where we will stay here again.

name: The Westin Copley Place
title: “The Wonderful Westin”
text:
My finace (now husband) was traveling to Boston on business so I joined him on his trip. We now live in Boston, but at the time of our stay at the Westin, we were living in Tampa FL. 
The staff at the Westin are very helpful and professional. As Starwoods Preferred Guests we were upgraded to to a spacious junior suite with many windows and, as in all Westins, the Heavenly Bed.
The location of the Copley Westin is perfect. The hotel is connected to the Copley Mall, an upscale mall with almost every high-end shop your heart could desire. It's just two blocks from Newbury street which is lined with many boutique shops and great dining. Boylston St also has many options for high end dining. There are two T (train) stops within two blocks of the hotel (Copley-Green Line and Back Bay-Orange Line). 
I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Boston. I've also heard great things about the new Westin on the waterfront, but I personally think the Copley location is accesible to more attactions.

name: The Westin Copley Place
title: “Just as a Westin should be”
text:
The Westin Copley is as a Westin should be. The room was clean and spacious, and the bed was as adverstised -- Heavenly. And although I didn't get a room with the view of the Charles River, the Boston night lights were so mesmerizing that I actually left the drapes open during my sleeps.
The location of the hotel is fabulous as busy Boylston Street is literally a block away and trendy Newbury Street is not that much farther. And even though I was in Boston the week it faced its coldest tempreatures this winter, I still managed to walk from the hotel to "Cheers" on Beacon Street, which is on the outskirts of Beacon Hill.
Boston looks like it has plenty of nice, upscale hotels throughout Copley Plaza and other downtown "districts" that might be worth a stay also. However, if I go back to Boston again, I'd stay at the Westin Copley again.

name: Inn at the Market
title: “Loved the Inn at the Market”
text: We just returned from a week in Seattle and chose the Inn at the Market and are very happy we did. We had a water view room and we were on the top floor. The views of Elliott Bay were breathtaking. From our room we could watch the market wake up every morning, the ferry crossings and the cruise ships. The inn is beautifully furnished, well appointed and the staff was very friendly. We did not rent a car for the trip, but wanted a car for one day to go to Mount Rainier. Just asked at teh front desk and the car was delivered right to the inn for us and picked up when we were back from our day trip. You are in walking distance to Pioneer Square, downtown shopping, the market, the piers for any water trips and lots of great restaurants. The inn has three restaurants as well. There is a rooftop garden with chairs for relaxing with your morning coffee or an afternoon glass of wine. We felt the inn to be the perfect choice for us and would definitely stay there again the ext time we are in Seattle.

name: Nine Zero Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Dissapointed.”
text: A bath couldn't be filled with water in my room because a plug didn't work. It is very relacxing time for me to take a bath. Called and asked the front desk, there was no apology with insincere talk. It was very dissapointing. Can I stay 4 more nights here?

name: Boston Marriott Copley Place
title: “Attractive hotel in great location”
text:
The Marriot Boston is a nice hotel in a super location. Being centered in Copley, you can access some of Boston's best attractions and shopping without stepping outside! The Marriot is directly connected to both the Copley Place Mall and Prudential Center Mall. Copley Place offers upscale shopping, various dining options, and a movie theater; Prudential Center also offers an array of stores, a food court, multiple restaurants (from fast food to fine dining), the Prudential Observatory, and functional stops such as the Post Office, banks, and Shaws Supermarket. The lobby in the Marriot Boston is one of its finest features. Several floors, all open for viewing above and below, are connected by escalators, thus avoiding a wait to access main floors. 
Glass chandaleirs and opulent lighting abound in this hotel. The hotel boasts a number of restaurants, and a bar with regular entertainment and music. The lobby is spacious and there is a lot of seating. There is a pool and health club, and room service is available. All of the rooms have nice views, and I recommend asking for a corner room on a high floor, for the best views and most space. Parking is expensive and located in the Copley Mall's parking garage. I havent stayed in this hotel for a couple of years now, but for the most part, enjoyed my visits. However, I did have a few complaints. I've always stayed there during the winter when the heat was on, and in many rooms and hospitality suites, noticed a strange, musty odor when the blower turned on. I am not aware of whether this has been resolved or not. The rooms were a bit on the small side, and were kind of stuffy. The bathrooms were somewhat run-down, though not falling apart, I expected a bit more for my money. The service was not terrific, nor was it terrible. The staff often seemed overwhelmed at busy times, and were not always able to answer my questions or requests. One of the few times I decided to try valet parking, I ended up having to wait over 20 minutes for my vehicle despite calling ahead. No pets are allowed, which presents an issue for me while travelling. The elevators are tough - long waits are common, and "getting lucky" (waiting less than 7-10 min at busy times for that magical "ding" on your floor) has been a joke between the guests each time I've stayed there. The verdict? 
It's a nice hotel business travelers especially might find fufills their needs, or those who mainly want prime location and spend minimal time in their rooms would enjoy it- but there are others I like better for my own business or recreational purposes. It's very pretty in the common areas, but this can be enjoyed by simply walking through on the way to the malls, or dining at the restaurants or bar.

name: The Back Bay Hotel
title: “The Best Hotel in Boston!!!”
text: I can't say enough how amazing this hotel is. My wife and I have stayed here every year we go to Boston for a getaway. The staff amazing, the food excellent and the rooms spotless. You will not be disappointed. Even better the last time we stayed was our anniversary and the hotel matched the price from a year earlier ($295 for a corner room). Now that's class!!!

name: Nine Zero Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A fantastic hotel -great service.”
text: We are currently enjoying a 5 night break at the 90 zero and have been greatly impressed by the quality of the room.The staff have been very helpful and friendly the one hour wine session from 5.00-6,00 p.m is a welcome relief from all the activities which can be found close by.The free internet for kimpton in touch members is also much appreciated.On arrival in our room we found a bottle of bubbly and six strawberries dipped in chocolate -a welcome touch even though our 30 anniversary, isn't till tomorrow,The concergie staff have been great in securing dining reservations.The whole of Boston is taken up by the marathon but I certainly intend to visit the city again and enjoy the hospitality of this great hotel found in a great location.

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Pleasant stay at the Colonnade”
text:
Our family stayed at the Colonnade overnight. Overall, it was a pleasant stay, no glitches. The location is super-convenient, right next to shopping and transportation. My wife and kids enjoyed their breakfast at Jo's. Their pancakes were very good!
Self park was easy and convenient right next to the hotel. The hotel personnel were all pleasant and helpful.
The hallways were a bit too dark for me. Also, there truly was a musty, but mild odor along the corridors, similar to what I've read in previous reviews. This did not affect our stay in any way, though.

name: Nine Zero Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Perfect”
text: From the location to the service to the plush beds and floor to ceiling windows. Don't stay anywhere else in Boston.

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Convenient location, great staff.”
text:
Nice hotel, great staff. For a big hotel I was impressed with how clean the room was and the staff were very responsive even though there seemed to be people coming and going constantly at the front desk. The hotel is directly across the street from a mall, with several convenient food options. There is a T stop right on the corner so getting anywhere in Boston is really easy. I definitely agree with several other reviews on here that the internet connection is horribly slow. To get work done I actually ended up across the street at the Barnes and Nobel.
The fitness facilities were great. It rained most of my trip so I was not able to run outside and ended up in the fitness center most days. There are two full rows of cardio machines, several weight machines, and an open floor area for stretching or working with free weights. I was impressed.
The room was clean and the bed comfortable with plenty of extra pillows. The room did have a bit of a musty smell to it, but opening the window to let in some fresh air solved this problem. It is a bit pricy, which seems to be the norm in Boston, but it is possible to find less expensive and comperable places if you look early enough.

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “I enjoyed the hotel”
text: Given the reviews and my own prior experience, it was with some trepidation that I booked a double room at the BPP Hotel. I have heard the rooms were small and shabby. But the price and location could not be beat so I booked it. Besides, who spends time in the room on a trip to Boston? It's a party town. In the event, my room was spacious, clean and quiet. I recommend getting a double. The lobby was beautiful and the bar/restaurant is a nice place to meet for drinks before getting the night started. The location is really the best quality. It is surrounded by the wonderful restaurants and shopping of Boston's Back Bay and South End. It is also close to the Public Garden and Commons making for a nice walk over to Beacon Hill and the Waterfront. The staff was a little aloof, but proficient at what they did. The housekeeping staff however was very gracious and did a nice efficient job. Overall, a very nice stay.

name: Motel 6 Memphis - Graceland
title: “Stay away!!!”
text:
I only needed a place to nap after a flight and before the next leg of my trip. I was told the airport shuttle comes every few minutes, but none came so I called the hotel. They said there is no regular schedule for the shuttle, but they would send it over to pick me up. When it arrived, a very nice driver apologized for no air conditioning in the van - it was broken. But he assured me this was much safer than the van that had AC - that one had no brakes! When I went to get out of the van, the door would not open. He said it was damaged in the last crash it had...he was able to pry it open from the outside! 
Lobby was clean and nice. Went to my first floor room which had an awful smell and the gold bedspreads looked dirty. Pulled the bedspread down and found clean but scratchy sheets. I slept anyway. It was daytime (thank God!) When I woke up, I went to take a shower and found that there was a bar of soap but no shampoo. There was toilet paper but no tissues in the room. I checked the housekeeping cart in the hall - no shamppoo. I went to the front desk, and the girl seemed surprised that I needed shampoo. She rooted around and found some in the back room. I had not eaten all day and looked for the vending machines. Soda machine had only soda - water was empty - and snack machine was out of order. Not exactly the type of neighborhood you would walk around looking for the 7-11, so I had nothing to eat. I don't know that I could have eaten in that room anyway. Filthy hotel, lousy place to stay.

name: Hampton Inn Memphis-Walnut Grove/Baptist Hospital East
title: “Clean, Safe Location, Family Friendly”
text: Met up with family for a weekend of shopping at Memphis and stayed at this Hampton for 2 nights. I have never had a bad experience with Hampton/Hilton. The staff was friendly and helpful, the rooms were clean, beds very comfortable, good wifi, and the rooms although a somewhat older hotel, the rooms were fairly updated. I had never stayed in Memphis and wanted a safe location. This location is on the East side of Memphis next to the Baptist Hospital, and very safe. Quiet tucked away hotel. It is very close to I-240 and I-40 and near many good shopping centers. The value was great! I pre-paid and the room rate was around $60 a night. If going back to Memphis I will definitely stay here again.

name: Hampton Inn Memphis - Southwind
title: “Be sure to get a refurbished room”
text: Booked a king suite but the 2 rooms were separated by a long, very narrow hall and both rooms were very dark. The sofa bed was old, dirty and impossible to sleep on as there was a bar that jutted through the middle of the thin mattress. We put the mattress on the floor and looked up to see the ceiling fan caked with dust and the walls from fan height to the ceiling also filled with the dust that was flung off the fan. Needless to say, we did not use the fan. Do to the lateness, we spent the night but requested a change first thing in the morning. When we showed the head of housekeeping the fan and dust, she shrugged her shoulders and said it was difficult to clean them because they needed maintenance to provide a ladder. (I didn't tell her how I clean my fan at home with a step ladder and a simple extended brush especially made for high ceiling fans. The thickness of dust we could see from the floor meant no one had cleaned this particular fan in years.) To their credit, we were given a refurbished room that was cleaner and they correctly adjusted our bill. However, the TVs are still very old, the bathrooms had holes or stains in the grout around the tub and all the fixtures are old.

name: Hampton Inn Memphis-Poplar
title: “Wonderful service, great Breakfasts!”
text: Stayed here to attend the tennis tournaments at the Morgan Keegan Racquet Club and everything was as good as I would expect and to meet famous tennis players staying there also, was a hugh plus ! Service was great and the only thing that could be improved upon is to have maids that speak English. The ones I tried to deal with could NOT ! It was impossible to communicate unless you played charades ! Not fun at all ! They also knock on your doors early to see if you are checking out ! ! ! Yet can't answer a question !

name: Comfort Suites I-240 East-Airport
title: “decent older hotel”
text:
reception personnel were friendly and helpful; a sour smell was present in the bathroom & staff quickly responded and replaced the shower curtain and cleaned the bathroom floor (hmm). a washer & dryer were available (thank god!) since we were on our last set of clean clothes and had several days of visiting in memphis.
word of warning to men: the commode was low to the floor and the bowl was shallow, so men watch the "jewels" lest they fall into the water.

name: Hilton Memphis
title: “Decent price, good eateries nearby”
text: My brother and I stayed here for a convention. It was clean, quiet and near good eateries. Staff was friendly, free parking, and thought the room/view was above average. I would recommend this hotel to businessmen and leisure travelers alike. The price was unbeatable and less then many lower level chains that I have reviewed on here as well.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Memphis
title: “Average”
text: Checked in late evening, room was clean and nice, loved the toiletries. No continental breakfast (and couldn't find those cookies, either...) so ate a $$$ breakfast in the Lynchburg Lounge. Never needed any services so can't comment on that.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Memphis
title: “Basic But Overall Clean”
text:
Staff was very friendly and helpful. The hotel lobby is very small and not many table for breakfast. Breakfast area is one of the smallest I have ever been in. However, the choices were normal and good. Stayed in a King room. The room was Very small and basic. Sheets were a little rough. Overall the hotel was clean yet simple. Quick one night stay...this is the place. More than one night....Maybe look into another option. Pricing was under $100 which is the max. I would pay for that area and this particular hotel.
But Again....Very Friendly Staff and Serves the one night business trip purpose.

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Great accommodations and fantastic staff”
text: Our room was very nice and spacious. We had a family of four and had plenty of space. Every staff member was extremely polite and helpful. The concierge service was one of the best I have experienced. Location was great - we walked to Fenway, Newbury St and the Bostom Common. Took the subway downtown and to Cambridge. I would definitely stay here again.

name: BEST WESTERN Suites
title: “Worst Hotel of the Trip”
text:
On a trip by car from Washington DC to Memphis, we stayed at eight different Best Western motels and hotels. This was by far the worst of the lot. We had booked in advance and stood to lose our deposit otherwise we would probably have gone elsewhere having been greeted by the depressing reception area, overpowering smell of cooking curry and having to ring a bell several times to get any attention from a reluctant receptionist. The elevator was scruffy, but to be fair the room was clean and well-enough appointed, although at lunch time curry fumes percolated up from the reception area below.
Breakfast was minimal in a very small room. Another guest said "Best Western should be ashamed of this place!" There was no coffee. Vigorous ringing of the bell eventually secured the attention of the reluctant receptionist, who said that it might take some time.
Do not be fooled by the blandishments in the advert which state that the location provides easy access for the sights of Memphis. It is 10 miles out of the city along a very congested freeway.

name: Super 8 Memphis Airport East
title: “OK except for one important thing”
text: I would have given three stars as the room and bathroom were clean and big, couch, table, desk and TV, internet and coffee maker. Unfortunately, the sheets weren't clean enough, as shades of old stains were visible in different places and I didn't feel confortable. The location is probably convenient for those who are just passing and stopping by, pretty close to the airport but far from anything else. Located on a kind of highway there are no shops and restaurant on walking distance, so you'd need a car. There are two or three vending machines in the lobby, but water was sold out and hasn't been supplied during my two days stay. However the staff was kind and helpful. The breakfast very basic. I think most of the customers are passing travelers and lorry drivers. It was very cheap, but, as I didn't have a car, I spent what i saved in taxis. If just as me you don't have a car and you are interested in visiting Graceland and/or the city centre I would recommend to stay downtown (Beale street). Consider that if you intend to visit the SUN Studios (walking distance from Beale St.) you can get a free ride from there to Graceland and return (check the website http://www.sunstudio.com/).

name: Hampton Inn Memphis-Poplar
title: “Comfortable place to stay”
text: I was pleased with the overall quality of the hotel. It was a decent price for a decent hotel. Nothing too exciting, but good.

name: Hampton Inn Memphis-Poplar
title: “great place to stay”
text:
This was a great place to stay. I have family in Memphis, and each time I return to visit I've found it increasingly difficult to find reasonable lodging in a safe part of town for a reasonable price. I've stayed in all types of chains all over town and have paid money in several different price ranges. To me this hotel, while definitely not the least expensive, was the best value I've foud for the money, and just happens to be centrally located enough to be convenient to almost everything.
The room was spectacular (the beds are the best). It was very clean and comfortable. I didn't hear the train even without earplugs. Nice pool for the kids. The carpets were worn in the halls, but the room carpeting wasn't (nor was it dirty).
I think this is my new home away from home while in Memphis!

name: Real Value Inn
title: “Pay the extra money”
text: Visiting for the first time ,my cousin and I came just to visit Graceland and when picking this motel the pictures ,and information didn't seem so bad,but when we checked in we had no idea what we were getting ourselves into ,the place was horrible I would never ever recommend this place ,it's in the seediest part of east Memphis ,next to a run down boarded up strip joint ,walls in bathroom were disgusting,blood stained sheets ,didn't really sleep under sheets ,and the people coming in and out of there I really unsafe but we went out and came back and just stayed inside after 6pm way before dark cause we wouldn't want to try to venture out in that neighborhood, I've stayed at plenty of motels and this was absolutely the worst in my life ,we had called for a cab and we waited along time I guess they saw where the pick up was and didn't want to go out there because of the area,but we did get a guy who was just so helpful we called him to take us to Graceland and back and he was so great to us.

name: Union Express
title: “They need to shut this place down.....”
text: This is the worst place to stay the rooms are terrible, the workers r rude.. I can't believe this dump, the hot water didn't work, they had no towels, besides the one they had stuffed in the hole in the wall where it look like it was water damage and they had to cut a hole in the wall, they had so many bugs, and had the to charge $90 for the room, but I should have followed my first mind and looked at the room before I paid, cause once I paid for it and when in the room I said hell no went to tell them I didn't want the the room. The guy tell me there is no refunds and he had to go cause he was the housekeeper, maintenance, customer service, and the pool guy and he didn't have time to deal with this..... Really WTH... NEVER AGAIN IT NEED TO BURN TO THE GROUND......

name: Hilton Memphis
title: “Nice place with thin walls”
text: I stayed at this hotel because it was one of the only ones in East Memphis that had a free shuttle to the airport. The rate was nice but the walls were super thin. They were very busy with some type of family reunion or conference and every time they came to their room, I could hear everything, so it was very hard to relax.
