On the other hand, the breakfast was great. I would stay here again, but I wouldn't stay on the first floor.

name: Super 8 Memphis / Downtown / Graceland Area
title: “Quick and Easily Cheaper”
text: Hotel is off the beaten path, but the rate was appealing. shuttle service better than local cabs and public transportation. staff quite knowledgeleable and pleasant.

name: Artisan Hotel Memphis
title: “Unauthorized Charges!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text: My boyfriend and I were looking for a classy hotel to stay in near Beale Street for our vacation to the Memphis in May Festival. We came across the Artisan Hotel and thought that the pictures looked nice so we booked the hotel. Well when we checked in we expected the lavish rooms that they have pictured on the website...but that was not what we got. Also we had to give a credit card for a $50.00 hold just in case we damage something...which was understandable. Well I gave the man that checked us in one of my Visa cards that I keep spare cash on to use for the hold. Come to find out he not only charged my card $50 but also he charge my card $137.06, for what nobody could tell me. So when I got to use my card it gets declined at Walgreen's. So that puts a damper on our trip on top of the fact that the rooms look like Super 8 with a comtemperary sink in the bathroom, instead of the lush pictures that they display on the website. Actually the guy that checked us in said he was giving us one of the newly renovated rooms...go figure that. So I go to the front desk about the $137.06 charge and they say that it will be released at the same time the $50 will be released when we checked out. Well long story short...we checked out Sunday, it is now Wednesday and no money has been credited to my account and my bank is actually showing that they collected on the $50 damages charge!!!! If you are going to Memphis there are plenty more nicer hotels to stay at besides the Artisan and my boyfriend and I are definately not staying there ever again!!!

name: Hilton Memphis
title: “Nice Hotel!”
text: I am a diamond member and found this jem in Memphis. Nice suite beautiful wall to wall windows, I will stay here from now on on my buisness trips to Memphis.

name: Hilton Memphis
title: “Eugene the Bellman was AWESOME!”
text: Our company recently held a conference at this Hilton. I asked the Bellman, Eugene, to unload 19 huge heavy boxes from 2 trucks and take them to our registration area. Temps were high 90s....poor guy got sweaty and dirty, and had to make about 7 or 8 trips, but he never complained. The smile never left his face and he came back regularly to see if I needed anything. I have never experienced service this nice. Eugene is a HUGE asset to this hotel! When you're there, seek him out! I was so impressed with him that I even found the General Manager and the Hotel Manager to personally sing his praises!

name: Seaport Boston Hotel
title: “Excellent Business Class Luxury”
text:
I stayed at The Seaport last August for seven nights as the hotel was ideally located for the live concerts at The Bank of America Pavilion which I was attending. The neighborhood is quiet but boasts several small restaurants and bars within walking distance. Transfers from Logan airport take approximately 15 minutes.
The large rooms have good facilities and the hotel itself has an excellent business centre. Staff are friendly, efficient and very helpful. I was fortunate to secure a room during 'low' season for £65 a night through Hotels.com as on a subsequent visit in December the room rate was twice the price!
The hotel obviously attracts many businessmen due to it's location south of the financial district. There are better located tourist hotels in the city but for me, The Seaport ticked all the boxes. Excellent Business Class Luxury . .. occasionally at an affordable price.

name: Scottish Inn Memphis Airport
title: “Horrible experience”
text:
I booked the hotel through Expedia. When we arrived at the hotel, they were posting a lower rate in front; however, when we went to the front desk, the front desk lady quoted us a much higher price and said that the rate we booked online was not real. What's the point of making a reservation online if they don't honor the rate?
The place looked dirty and smelled like cigarettes, and the lady was plain rude. When we asked about the cheaper price posted out front, she said it was only valid for truck drivers (the sign didn't say that). What blatant false advertisement! When we said we'd like to go around other places to see if they had better rate, she kept yelling, "Go! go! you won't find anything better!", but meanwhile kept the door locked (it was relatively late at night) so we couldn't head out.
We left and actually found a better (cleaner, friendlier, cheaper) place down the road, but in general it was just a horrible experience--and we didn't even stay there!

name: Elvis Presley's Heartbreak Hotel
title: “Terrible!”
text:
Don't bother staying here!!!!
The beds very uncomfortable, room is very dated, very noisy a/c, they say they provide free wifi (when booking) but when you get there they say oh the signal isn't very strong, which meant it will work for maybe 5 min then drop out, the gym is so small & has nothing to offer, the walls are paper thin so every time someone is talking in the hall you can hear everything & also when they leave their room the door closing shakes the wall, the staff are rude & not friendly tried to not give us our discount for the Elvis Insider because i dindt have my card when i checked in, so we had to talk to the manager, & the elevator was broke down so we had to use a very slow service elevator further down, i definitely won't be back to stay here. I think maybe the Days in might be better.
 For the kind of money they charge they provide nothing in return. Honestly don't waist your money on a bad hotel.

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Great hotel in downtown Boston”
text:
I recently tagged along with my wife on her business trip, and we were lucky enough to stay at the Colonnade Hotel. The location was perfect for my day excursions while she was down at the Convention Center, with the green line right outside the front door, which couldn't be more convenient. Not only that but on the one day it was rain/snowing, there is a huge shopping center with tons of restaurants and shops to kill some time or drop some money. 
The check in was pretty quick and painless, and the rooms were a very decent size, looks to be recently renovated, and very clean. The staff was accommodating and friendly. The star of the staff, has to be Norman at the bell stand; courteous, friendly and extremely helpful.
We didn’t get the chance to have dinner at the hotel’s restaurant but on one of the days my wife was at her conference, I ventured down for a solo lunch. If you go you have to try the French Onion Soup. UNBELEIVABLE! Maybe the best I have ever had.
Next time we stay in Boston, I would definitely stay again at the Colonnade Hotel. Great staff, location, food, and comfortable and clean rooms. Keep up the good work, Colonnade !!

name: Fairfield Inn Memphis I-240 & Perkins
title: “Very impressed.”
text: The staff was very friendly and helpful. Had a very comfortable clean room. Nice breakfast variety. Only thing that I didn't like was it was not close to tourist attractions but it was near lots of restaurants and plenty shopping. Would definitely stay there again if in that area.

name: Artisan Hotel Memphis
title: “Go To The Artisan Hotel In Memphis TN, It Is Beautiful”
text: The Artisan Hotel in Memphis TN is a nice soothing and relaxing place. We visited Memphis TN by way of VA During the American Idol Weekend. The Artisan was the best stay ever. They available rooms and made us feel special as guest and good rates. In my book that means a lot. So visit the Artisan Hotel, enjoy the lounge, pool and good food. 1837 Union Avenue Memphis TN. 38104 901 278 4100

name: Super 8 Memphis / Downtown / Graceland Area
title: “OMG dont stay here”
text: we checked in around 8pm. There was blood on the door jam into the bathroom, mold on the ceiling, an abandoned building in the back, and rat traps on the balcony. The response from the front desk, when we told them about the smeared blood in the room: "housekeeping has gone home for the day." W etried a different room-this room had a hole cut into the wall, the baseboards were missing, mold on the ceiling. We checked out. we were afraid to leave our car in the parking lot, and our luggage in the room during the day. We found a Days Inn for the same price on the east side of Memphis that was totally fine.

name: Holiday Inn Select Memphis - Downtown (Beale Street)
title: “Very tired”
text: Hotel has a good location in Memphis and is handy for Beale Street. However, the whole place is in dire need of a revamp. Very old and tired decor. Breakfast was pretty grim but charmingly served. In fact all the staff were good and helpful but the building is depressing.

name: Red Roof Inn Memphis East
title: “Unrenovated Room”
text: I got an excellent price on this room and knew the area well, so we decided to stay for a few nights. Turns out, we only stayed one night, and that was because we arrived so late at night. We were told that we would get a renovated room, but when we arrived, it seems they gave that room away even though I called to confirm (probably due to our late check in). The walls were thin, we could hear noise in the next room. The carpets looked worn, but the worst thing that happened was seeing a brownish stain on the comforter of the bed, which also had some holes in it. The sheets were fine, but we didn't feel comfortable at all. I wrote the manager explaining what happened and he did write back right away apologizing for our bad experience and saying he examined the room and that the hotel was currently being renovated. There might be some good rooms after the renovation. Location is good, next to Cracker Barrel.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Memphis Airport
title: “Average Courtyard, close to airport and Medtronic”
text:
Location: I was traveling for Medtronic an able to walk next door for my meetings, literally next door. The airport is about 5-10 minutes away, but the rental car location is even closer. No restaurants nearby - just a Subway.
The hotel is in a business park, nothing glamorous at all. 
Room: My room had a parking lot view and was a little smaller than most Courtyards. Very nice bed and TV. Mini fridge, coffee, and full plug-in hairdryer (nice). There was a couch and table and a work desk. I got a strong WI-fi signal and that was free. I was in 159 and got the Medtronic rate - I mention this because I actually had to prove that I was there for them. It saved me $45 per night. 
Bathroom: strong shower, separate room from sink. Again a little small it fine for one person. 
All very clean. 
Gym: let's call it a room with a treadmill, elliptical, a bench and tweets of dumbbells (15 & 20).
Whirpool is inside next to gym - windows to gym & business area. 
Pool is outside and pretty nice - closes at 11pm. 
Business area had about 5 computers and was open in the lobby. 
Breakfast: good buffet, several hot and cold voices, eggs, sausage and gravy, waffles, cereal, fruit, etc. Service there was awesome - they GET business travel and were super quick. 
I'd recommend for Medtronic, may look elsewhere for airport, definitely go downtown otherwise if I return.

name: Omni Parker House
title: “great location”
text: Great location..close to everything in downtown Boston. Our kids loved staying in a real "haunted" hotel! Right in the heart of downtown...lots of history to explore!

name: Vista Inn Motel Downtown Memphis
title: “Good value and clean”
text: This was a good value for the locaton. The room was clean and decent for the price. We could walk to Beale St and not worry about where the car was parked. The staff was friendly and offered assistance without us asking for any. We will stay here again.

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Had a fabulous visit to Boston!”
text: The Colonnade Hotel is beautiful, in a great location, and has a fabulous restaurant. The rooms are luxuriously appointed, immaculate & very comfortable. The staff is very committed to the comfort of their guests, and are all very friendly & accommodating. I will definitely stay at this hotel again!

name: Elvis Presley's Heartbreak Hotel
title: “I wish we had stayed at the Peabody”
text:
Being used to 4 and 5 star resorts, we knew this would not be deluxe, but unfortunately there is nothing deluxe near Graceland, as surprising as that may be. I would advise folks to stay downtown and shuttle to Graceland and be nearer the other Memphis attractions.
We did have a two room suite...the bed and shower were good. The ac and bathroom fan were SO loud...an in the wall ac unit that blew on us. Room was musty and felt damp. Breakfast included was ordinary at best. Fellow travelers felt the same way. A plus was the dining room/lounge area that had a. Ar and played Elvis movies all day. Also Elvis movies in room. The advertised wifi had poor connectivity that made it useless...they did have two computers in the lobby with free Internet for guest use.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Gen X Inn
title: “Good location for us”
text:
We stayed one night at the Peabody which was wonderful but the Best Western offered free parking and is also near enough to downtown to be on the trolley line! We are not late night people so safety was not an issue for us. 
There is a generous size refrigerator in the room which was clean and pleasant. No issues with noise or anything else!

name: Homewood Suites Memphis - Hacks Cross
title: “Excellent”
text: Employees are Great!!!!! A + in service.. Had a great time at the 5:00pm free food and beers!!! The employees very friendly. I will stay again without hesitation. Great job!!!! Rooms are very comfortable. Plenty of stores and restaurants around area. Overall, great hotel!!!

name: Homewood Suites Memphis - Hacks Cross
title: “Great staff”
text:
I have stayed at the Homewood Suites a number of times on business and I'm always impressed with the friendly and responsive staff. The room are comfortable and there is a good breakfast selection. There is also a really great outdoor pool.
If youare coming as a tourist you really need a car as it's out of town.

name: Vista Inn Motel Downtown Memphis
title: “Horrible!!!”
text: This is literally the worst place I have ever stayed in (including hostels in Europe). The reason we booked this place was because of its location, and it was cheap compared to other hotels in the area...DON'T BE FOOLED! I had read all of the reviews and thought, "Why not?" It is much more worth your time and money to stay somewhere else. When I called, I was told that the place had just been renovated. Now, if they did indeed fix things, the owners used garage sale furtinure or stuff from the dump. Our TV did not have a power button or a remote to use. The sink did not have a drain, the carpet was coming up around the edges, there were holes in the walls, there were holes in the furtinure, and there was MOLD in the shower. The towels were paper thin and the beds were lumpy. They advertised having free wi-fi, irons, and ironing boards, but I found none of these things. We attempted to stick it out not wanting to waste 75$, but there were people fighting and slamming doors at the motel not to mention the horrible traffic right outside (which I know they had no control over). At midnight we left and went to another hotel which was MUCH better. When we left, I stopped to talk to person working, and he was really rude about the thing - tried to deny that there was fighting going on etc... I will never stay here again, and I wouldn't recommend this place to my worst enemy.

name: Boston Harbor Hotel
title: “Boston Harbor Hotel: "Wicked Awesome"”
text:
If you want to stay at a true 5 star hotel, this is it! from the arched promenade to the elegant views of both the city and Boston Harbor, this is the place to be! Walking distance to Faneuil Hall, The Aquarium and downtown Boston. The customer service is top notch and the indoor pool is great for both adults and kids. There is a great spa as well as well as an eucalyptus steam room. Depending on the time of year, you can stay at the hotel, attend some of the local festivities and then return and wind down at the lobby bar. Each room comes with complimentary Fuji water bottles which is nice; I don't mind tap but this is a nice treat. 
For families, it's close to the Childrens Museum, Aquarium and to the "T". 
There are great deals as well; just check on-line. Keep in mind that the hotel is considered in the city so parking is at a premium and you will pay about $40.00 a day. The hotel has specials that include parking as well so that's always a nice plus.
Being from NY Yankee fan, giving such a great review of something in Boston was difficult but it's well deserved!

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Great hotel !!”
text: We arrived in Boston on July 4th for a two week art class only to discover that our original accomodations were under construction and created a very unhealthy environment. We called the Colonade on July 5 and spoke to Jill, one of their very friendly and helpful reservation agents. After explaining our dilemma and the fact that we would need two connecting rooms for the duration of our visit, Jill worked wonders for us. She was able to arrange the rooms and an American Express deal that included breakfast and other amenities. Our stay was wonderful. From the doorman to check in, concierge, housekeeping, and the delicious breakfast and engaging staff in the dining room, we were constantly pleased with the friendliness and efficiency of these employees. The rooms were spacious and the pillows and mattresses were beyond comfortable. And, we could not have asked for a better location. With the Prudentai Shops and restaurants across the street, and the T Line right outside the door, we were able to easily discover the joys of this lovely city. We plan on returning to Boston frequently in the next few months, and staying the Hotel Colonnade will definately be our top priority!!

name: Nine Zero Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Luxurious Hotel w/ prime location and friendly staff”
text:
Pros:
- prime location
- free evening wine hour 
- friendly staff
- surprise treats from the concierge for our special occasion
- pet-friendly
- environmentally conscious
Cons:
- tub draining problem (details below)
- very expensive 
- street parking is difficult to find in that area
Details:
STAFF: We were greeted with a smile from the friendly Gabriella at the front desk. We stayed here for our 7 year anniversary. Since it was a special occasion, she also gave us champagne at check-in. When we arrived to our room, we found that Thomas, our concierge, had spoiled us with a bottle of champagne and chocolate-covered strawberries and a signed note from the staff. What a delightful surprise! 
LOCATION: The location is prime! Right across from part of the Freedom Trail, a block from Boston Commons, and the State house. KO prime is the steakhouse right next door (although we didn't get to try it). There's also a movie theater just down the street.
ROOMS: Bed was super comfortable. No complaints there. I love the fact that they have recycling in the rooms. I also love the fact that they are pet-friendly. There was a yappy little dog in the room right next to us, but we were hardly in our rooms and I love dogs. However, just a warning for those that aren't pet-lovers The only problem that we had was that our tub didn't drain well. By the time that I finished showering, the water had reached my ankles. I never complained during my stay. When I filled out a survey after we left and discussed that, I got an email immediately apologizing and letting us know that they would get right on fixing that. 
PERKS: They also have a free wine hour everyday from 5-6 for guests. Great chance to unwind right before heading out to dinner. 
EXPENSE: The price will most likely prevent us from going back unless it's for a special occasion. 
OVERALL: Loved this place! Would recommend it to a friend, but would warn them about the price.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Boston
title: “Don't miss this hotel”
text: Truly a marvelous hotel. Rooms are quiet even when overlooking the Public Garden or Commons. The rooms are spacious, airy, and extremely comfortable. The staff is excellent, offering good advice on the City and how to best experience it. Real value for the money in terms of a great time made even better by great staff.

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Memphis
title: “Nice Hotel, But Some Down Sides”
text:
The room was OK apart from being on the Freeway side. This means 24 hour noise.
The Shuttle downtown is good and the drivers and the valet guys are really nice. 
The bar was Ok, but the welcome could have been much warmer. On the other hand the reception staff were very good. Get the Shuttle back at night. The walk isn't far, but you pass a number of interesting characters on the way if you choose to walk and the area is pretty quiet otherwise at night.

name: Nine Zero Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Absolutely great place to stay in heart of Boston”
text: Just spent 3 nights at Nine Zero with my husband and teenager. We loved the place, cannot say enough good things about it. Friendly, helpful staff,comfortable beds, quiet room, never heard a sound from any of the other rooms. Great location, can walk to Faneuil Hall, the Commons, Freedom Trail. Afternoon wine hour is wonderful amenity. We also thought the fitness center was well-equipped, better than your typical hotel. Overall, very pleased!

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “Look no further - Perfection”
text:
We stayed at the Lenox Hotel for four days - 12th June 2012, and from the moment we were collected from the Airport by Gurgen, we knew we had made the right choice. He was extremely courtious, pleasent and made us feel extremely welcome.
On arrival at the hotel every member of staff from the doorman, bell-boys, house keeping to the receptionist's - everyone had a smile and made us feel as if we were the only guests at the hotel. Nothing was too much trouble and our up-grade to a suite was the icing on the cake, as we were staying at the hotel for my mothers birthday. "Perfect".
The room was absolutely beautiful, large, clean, bright, tidy and the beds were soo' comfortable - made us feel as thought we were in a Country Hotel and not a hotel in the middle of Boston. The position of the hotel was an excellent location for the hop-on-hop-off bus tours, tourist attractions, subway, restuarants and shops galore all just a stones throw away. They even have an in-house resturant. In the mornings coffee/tea are supplied in the lobby and there is fruit on the desk for you to help yourself - an added bonus if you are up and about early. They also supply cold drinks in the lobby in the afternoons.
Kristie at the concierge desk was fab, everyday she would give us directions to the places we wanted to go with a smile and some hints along the way. Everyone at the desk could not have been more helpful.
The hotel even supplied us with umbrella's as it rained non-stop on our first day in Boston which was really nice to have and did not stop us from venturing out. 
From start to finish staying at the Lenox Hotel was an experience we will not forget and would certainly stay there again.
Oh by the way, the chocolates they left on the bed with the turn down service was just a extra
bonus we loved.
Thanks to everyone at "The Lenox" - you are definately one in a million.

name: Holiday Inn Select Memphis - Downtown (Beale Street)
title: “Great location”
text: Stayed here with my wife 16 to 18 Feb 2012. Great location just round the corner from Beale Street.I couldnt fault the hotel. We didnt eat there but every bar in Beale Street serves food. If you want a great steak ask for the Butchers Shop. 2H ueys2 just opposite good for burgers etc. This area is all about music and drinking. Have a good time.

name: The Back Bay Hotel
title: “Very nice hotel”
text:
Stayed here in during the Boston marathon for convenience to finish line area. Excellent choice. Room was not ready on our arrival. They offered another room but lady at check-in recommended to wait for our room since it was a corner room. Wait was worth it. Nice large room on 8th floor on corner. Large bathroom - shower only. I would have preferred a tub after the marathon. Very clean and nice amenities. Free fridge and free espresso. 
Room service VERY overpriced, poor quality food. Breakfast buffet downstairs much better. Had dinner one night, good food, but also rather pricey for small portions. 
Exceptional service attitude by all employees - bell men, reception area, concierge, maids, room service.
Nice bar areas. Lively crowd. Overall very good experience.

name: The Fairmont Copley Plaza, Boston
title: “Disappointed - luxury must mean few amenities”
text: Okay, first the good - the "deluxe" room I had was quite large, including the bathroom, and the bed was the best I have slept on in some time. The bathrobes were also a nice touch, and my view of Copley Square was fantastic. Now the bad: there were no rooms available when I arrived around noon - I know checkin at most hotels isn't until 3:00 or so but 99.9% of the time they have rooms available; I was able to check into Nine Zero at 10:30 a.m. when I stayed there. So I kept checking in (they did offer to call my cell phone but I didn't think it would be that long) and finally at 3:00 I was told a room was ready; however when I got up to the room housekeeping was still in there so I had to go back to the lobby and wait another 15 minutes. There is no coffee in the room; minor, I know but most hotels have free coffee. They offered to bring a coffee machine with the "set-up" to your room for $10 plus taxes, etc. I also didn't receive a newspaper even though when I made my reservation through the Fairmont site they asked what type of paper I wanted (national or local). For those of you who don't wash your face in the shower, the sink in the bathroom is an adventure to use (don't bump your head!) and for a hotel that has great views, I don't understand why the chair is situated on the opposite side of the room by the door; I'd rather sit in a chair by the window so I can enjoy the view. The lobby is not set up right to me; the only place for people to sit is on the opposite side of checkin near a reception room and if there is an event going on (as there was on the day I stayed) you have to hear the noise from the room. Finally, a treat for me is to order room service breakfast; don't bother. Two eggs, toast, ham, coffee and juice (no mention of potatoes on the menu I had) for $21 plus room service fee, gratuity, taxes, etc. which by my calculations would bring the total close to $30! A big disappointment and I would not likely stay there again, even with the reduced rate I paid.

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “Good hotel but time for a change?”
text: I have stayed at the Lenox several times over the past few years - the last time was in March. Until my last visit I would have rated this hotel with 5 stars, but my last visit was not as enjoyable as other previous visits. The positives highlighted by other reviewers are entirely accurate e.g. great location surrounded by a multitude of shops, restaurants and bars to suit all budgets, warm courteous staff, and lovely decor. However my last trip was spoiled by noise. The first night the neighbours played very loud music which was quickly sorted by the management with a complimentary breakfast as an apology. My stay coincided with the unseasonal hot weather, and my room was opposite the ice machine. All through the following nights I was woken with the noise of ice hitting ice buckets. In addition to this noise, the air conditioning unit also made sleeping difficult...not just mine, but the noise from the unit in the room next door also kept me awake. In fairness this was the first time I noticed excessive noise in the hotel, however no matter how lovely a room is (and they are lovely), the main priority should be a good nights sleep? Another thing which I was not happy about was that the concierge charged me $60 for my transfer back to the airport, when we paid $40 three months previously. I may return to the Lenox in the future, but have booked another hotel for my next visit to Boston in December.

name: Nine Zero Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Wonderful stay”
text:
Hmm...not sure what the below reviewer expected, maybe a clown for a concierge to entertain his son, perhaps? For the rest of us who weren't born with a silver spoon but still enjoy the finer things in life without feeling entitled, it is a fantastic hotel.
Room and hotel are very nicely decorated, and service was fantastic. No stuffy employees here, everyone we met with or even simply passed by always greeted us with a smile and a hello.
We fully agree with prior reviewers that the beds are super comfy and the shower head/water pressure is wonderful. Our room, on the 11th floor, was also very quiet.
The hotel does have a wine reception in the evenings. We forgot about it, and therefore missed it, but when we came down at the very end of it on Sat. night everyone who took part seemed to be having a great time.
The location of this hotel was the best. Basically right across from Boston Common, short walk to everything such as Faneuil Hall, North End, Theatre District, and just a 3-min walk from the Park Street T-stop on both the red & green lines.
I did sign up for the no-cost Kimpton InTouch membership ahead of time, had no problem with the wi-fi in our room, and when we returned from dinner the first evening we had a welcome card with a certificate to "raid the mini-bar," up to two items totaling $10. We ended up not taking advantage of this, but it was a wonderful touch!
We would certainly stay again for our next weekend trip into Boston!

name: XV Beacon
title: “XV Beacon, A Perfect Experience!”
text: My husband and I travelled from Brookline to Boston (about 5 minutes by car) to spend our wedding anniversary at XV Beacon and dine at Moo. To say that is was perfect is an understatement! We were very impressed at the service and attention that the staff provided. I am interior designer and I was drooling over the decor, sexy, masculine and understated. The restaurant was amazing, I am still craving those truffle fries! Really it couldn't have been better! I cannot wait to go again, hopefully for a longer stay;)

name: The Back Bay Hotel
title: “Service, Staff & Facilities way beyond expectations”
text:
This is an extraordinary hotel. From the moment you arrive the staff are so welcoming and helpful - they are genuine and sincere and really want to do their best to make you enjoy your stay. The rooms are gorgeous with beautiful furnishings and well appointed bathrooms. Breakfast is fantastic - great buffet or choose from a la carte - again the staff are brilliant. Having stayed at many different hotels throughout America and Canada myself and my husband both felt we had found a real gem of a hotel. The bar had a good buzz to it in the evenings - it seems to be well frequented by locals. 
The hotel's location is really great, easy walking distance to Copley Square and the Prudential Shopping Mall. Lots of restaurants etc nearby. 
We know without doubt that we'll be staying at this hotel and will be recommending it to anyone we know who is looking for a hotel to stay in when visiting Boston.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Boston
title: “The For Seasons is top of the line.”
text: Overall, the nicest hotel I ever stayed at. When I arrived it was raining however the hotel was warm and cozy inside. All the employees were friendly and accomodating. I used the spa one day and the female attendant eas most helpful. When I asked for a robe she was right there to provide me with one and also a pair of slippers. I have no complaints with your hotel. Thank you.

name: Holiday Inn Select Memphis - Downtown (Beale Street)
title: “Great location Great hotel just the wrong weekend!”
text: We arrived on a Saturday (7-23) and experienced the same group of college kids!! We were up most of the night with a party outside our room. Security was there met of the night as well. If they have a policy against groups of that nature they surely didn't enforce it! With 2 small children on a road trip across the south a good night's sleep is important. We found everything else to be PERFECT!! I would recommend and stay again....well, minus the Sigma Chi fraternity and their girlfriends!

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Memphis
title: “Showing a little age and could use a cleaning”
text:
Got this on priceline for a steal so I have no reason to complain too much. Only stayed 1 night.
Positives: Great front desk staff, very comfortable beds, pretty nice bedrooms and lobby. Super nice shuttle driver.
Negatives: Not very clean bedroom, hair on bed and floor, make up on one of the pillow cases, Very small bathroom that smelled like mold. On the end of main street are still close to the trolly but after dark kind of seems a little scary. Did not complain about the cleaniness so do not know how they would have reacted.

name: Harborside Inn
title: “Great location but too noisy”
text: Opted to stay in the Harborside following a visit throughout New England. Primary location, easy to find even in a rental car. Great location for sightseeing in Boston - Have stayed in Back Bay before, and downtown location is far better. Room was adequate for our needs and array of restaurants and bars nearby meant eating was not a problem. Main and major drawback is the noise levels. Currently the 'Big Dig' occupies much of the Bayside area and work at night means that, having opted for the more expensive townview rooms, noise levels were high. This disturbed our sleep to a great extent and I would recommend for this reason alone that either an inside room, or an alternative hotel is sought. The hotel was busy although the staff were sufficiently attentive and available.

name: The Back Bay Hotel
title: “OUtstanding!”
text:
I can't say enough good things about this hotel! The staff is lovely, the rooms are well done and (most important to me) unbelievably clean and well maintained. Not one detail has been overlooked in the fabulous restoration of this former police station. 
My daughter hopes to go to college in Boston and if she does, we're staying here whenever we visit her.

name: Harborside Inn
title: “Muy buena ubicacion, tranquilo, comodo”
text:
Hotel muy comodo con buena ubicacion muy cerca del Freedom trail, y de centros nocturnos, Faneuil Hill, etc, limpio muy tranquilo, 
Internet free en habitacion, cafe gratis en el looby
Tv con cable con amplia programacion
Falencias: no tener cafetera en la habitacion ni heladera

name: Boston Harbor Hotel
title: “Excellent Hotel, Great Location”
text: I had a very enjoyable stay here this past week. Rooms were spotless and service was second to none. Room price was a little high but you get every penny of what you pay for. I will stay here every time I visit Boston.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Memphis Downtown
title: “Nice hotel with great location...just little things kept from a "5"”
text: Location, location, location! We picked this hotel because we like Hiltons and this one has a great location just blocks away from Beale Street. It was also the most reasonably priced and for a good-sized room. Parking was pricey ($21) but it seems typical of downtown Memphis hotels. The great thing was, the places we wanted to go to we either walked or took the trolley. Check-in was smooth, and the staff was friendly. The room was clean and nicely furnished, but there was a weird drop ceiling in the entry by the bathroom that was in serious need of repair. It was also noisy, and the door didn't quite meet the floor. But the staff was great and very accommodating despite a tragic domestic dispute that occurred while we stayed there. We would likely stay there again but with the hopes the corporation would put some money into repairs.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Boston
title: “Lovely hotel, lovely location”
text: This is a lovely hotel in a lovely location, and it is worth paying for a Garden view room. We particularly appreciated the fitness room / pool overlooking the Garden where coffee, fresh fruit and newspapers were available every morning, and water flavored with fresh fruit and/or green vegetables was available all day. Also, fresh apples are available everywhere at all times of the day. We were very grateful for the excellent breakfast we were served in the Bristol Lounge even though it was lunch-time. Finally, when we did have a problem, it was addressed in a more than satisfactory manner. This is a tranquil oasis.

name: Nine Zero Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great facilities. Terrific location. Good price.”
text: This is a cool boutique style hotel. Very attractive facilities and rooms. Excellent location for walking the historic trail. Friendly complimentary wine-beer reception in early evening. We would definitely stay here again and recommend it to all.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Boston
title: “Wonderful experience!”
text: Perfect location and service that exceeds all expectations. We will never stay anywhere else when visiting Boston. Thank you for making our anniversary the perfect weekend.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Memphis Downtown
title: “Nice Property, Great Location”
text: We stayed three nights over Thanksgiving. We were very comfortable in the room and customer service was good, including valet. There is only valet parking which was really ok with us. A couple blocks to Beale Street, and nice shops and restaurants in the downtown area. I really didn't appreciate the TGI Friday's in the hotel. Service, what service and food just medicore. But with so many choices with in three blocks of hotel you should check out the possibilities. I enjoyed window shopping at The Peabody while my husband enjoyed the poker table at Tunica Horseshoe Casino. Will be writing on the Restaurant experiences in that category.

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “Love the Lenox!”
text:
I booked this hotel after reading all the great reviews, but I was still wary that somehow it wouldn't be so great. Well, it was that great! Everyone on staff seemed genuinely pleased to see you and help you--their service was truly outstanding. Front desk checked us in quickly, and my daughter got a stuffed animal. They have a plate of cookies out every evening, which helped hold us til dinner. Complimentary coffee and tea is available in the lobby every morning, and one blustery afternoon there was hot chocolate out for everyone--very welcome.
We had a queen/queen junior suite which is in a corner and apparently a larger room than the standard room. We thought it was spacious, with lots of room for the family to spread out. Nice high ceilings and a non-working fireplace. Beds were comfortable, thick curtains kept the light out in the morning. Even though we were on the 6th floor I only heard street noise once in three nights. I agree with others that the concierge was really helpful, with suggestions for breakfast and dinner when asked. They even loaned us umbrellas when it started raining as we were headed out for the day.
The location of the hotel is very convenient for shopping, dining, and touring. One block from Newbury Street, a block or two from two fancy malls, and not too far from the Public Gardens and the super fancy shopping nearby. We walked from the North End back to the hotel (with stops along the way) without a problem.
The only negative about the hotel is the cost to park your car--that added a lot to the cost of staying there. However, this was offset by the discount we got through a special offer they were running on TripAdvisor! And to reiterate what everyone says about the great customer service--when I tried to book the special offer online, the room type we wanted didn't show up. So I called the hotel directly and the woman helping me said no problem, I'll give you that discount on the room you want! 
Loved the hotel, would most certainly stay there again!

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “Great experience”
text: Wonderful service, particularly kind to my children. Breakfast oatmeal not so good but would return, great choice

name: Memphis Marriott Downtown
title: “Adequate Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Marriot in Sept. The staff was wonderful. We even were able to get early checkin. The housekeeping was good. No problems with getting the room cleaned. The beds were comfortable. The hotel is located on the cable car line. We could just hop on and take the cable car to Beale street. We would stay here again.

name: Memphis Marriott Downtown
title: “Awesome!”
text: Came to Memphis for the Labor Day weekend and the Marriott was thee perfect hotel. The trolly picks up right in front of the hotel. The upper deck right off the pool is super nice! The hotel staff was so nice and helpful! Will diffently stay there again!

name: Omni Parker House
title: “over priced and poor rooms”
text: We were really disappointed with our stay at the Omni Parker Hotel. At first glance when we walked into the lobby - it looked very impressive. However, on entering our room (which we had paid a significant amount for) - it was tiny, with a window view of a brick wall, a small double bed, small bathroom with poor shower. Internet connection was $6.95 for 15mins, rather than complimentary. Overall, it was no way near the class of the Lenox Hotel which I stayed in last year (for less money!).

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “You get what you pay for”
text: The hotel lobby is beautiful. The location is superb. The price was great. We Hotwired it and got a deal. It was recently remodled in 2005 and at first glance the room seemed great. We had read some of the reviews and thought that we had made a mistake. As we looked closer we saw that the carpet had stains in it, the bathroom floor had a permanent dirty look too it, the carpet was pealing up in one corner and when I tried to unplug the coffee pot to use the iron the entire socket came out of the wall. This is by no means a 4 star hotel. I will say the staff was nice and professional. We did not asked to be moved, so who's to say if all the rooms were as bad. I would just note that you get what you pay. If the finer things aren't what you're looking for, this is a cheap place to sleep that's close to all the sites.

name: Holiday Inn Select Memphis - Downtown (Beale Street)
title: “Good location but lazy housekeeping staff!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights in mid-October. The hotel was easy to get to from the I40. On arrival the elevator from the carpark down to the lobby was not working so we had to drag our bags down the stairs. Check-in was quick and efficient. we had a room on the 12th floor looking out over The Peabody hotel. Everything had been refurbished but I agree with other reviewers that close to the elevators there was a weird musty smell. Our room smelled fine and apart from the splatters of paint on the furniture it looked o.k. The (Beale street) tag is a little misleading - it's only a 4 min walk away but it's on Union street not Beale! Was an easy walk to the baseball stadium, Beale street and The Rendevous restaurant (best for BBQ!) is literally in an alley behind the hotel so location wise it's great. Our biggest disappointment was the housekeeping. The 1st morning we were there we left at 10am and removed the privacy tag from the front of the door to inside our room. After coming back from Graceland (you HAVE to go!) at 6pm we saw that the tag was back on the front of the door. We thought it weird and sure enough when we opened it up the tag on the back of the door was gone and the room was not cleaned. The housekeeping staff obviously didn't want to clean our room so opened the door and moved the tag from the back to the outside! On the plus side when I rang the front desk they immediately apologised and offered us free drinks as way of compensation. The other good part is that they have a computer in the lobby that people can use for printing boarding passes etc.
I didn't really feel we had got good value for money with the hotel (we paid $179 a night) - yes the location was great but it wasn't worth that much.

name: Nine Zero Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Clean, comfortable, peaceful rooms! Great location!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for my husband's 40th birthday. We were very pleased with our stay! The hotel staff even delivered chocolates and a card for my husband. The bed was extremely comfortable and the room was very clean and quiet. We had a great night's sleep. 
The hotel is in a great location. We had dinner at Ruth's Chris and walked to the restaurant. 
I agree with the poster about the charge for parking, but I've found that is typical Boston Hotel parking fees.
This hotel was a great escape and I would stay here again!

name: Memphis Marriott Downtown
title: “Typical convention center hotel”
text:
Typical convention center hotel. Everything cost. Parking $18. 
No comp breakfast. Nothing within 3 block but trolley is close by. 
Service slow but friendly. Food is good but expensive. Conference food good.

name: Memphis Marriott Downtown
title: “Good Location, not worth the price”
text: My husband and I decided to take a weekend trip in Memphis. We chose this hotel because of its location to Beale St and access to the Trolly. The rooms are nice and clean. However, for the price of the room, I expected better service. First, they do not prorate the parking. We arrived at 8pm and had to valet park because the self park was full. Despite arriving so late, we were still charged a full day for parking. The hotel does not offer a continental breakfast. Our first morning, we received good service and decent food. On the second morning, we ate the breakfast buffet. The server did not even visit our table. We each fixed our plate (separately) and then had to stop a server to ask for drinks. When he returned he only poured drinks for my husband. I had to ask him to return to pour my coffee. We then had to flag down another server to ask for our check when we were done. The food was luke warm and definitely not at a safe temperature. The scrambled eggs were very runny, like they weren't done. The hotel has an indoor pool, but it is not heated and was so cold we couldn't even swim in it. At the end of the trip, we decided that it would have been better to book a room at a mid-rate hotel and drive to all the attractions. The convenience of the location to downtown and the trolly was not worth the price of the hotel.

name: Hotel Commonwealth
title: “Taking Customer Satisfaction to a New Level”
text: I have stayed at many 5 star hotels but Hotel Commonwealth has taken customer service to a new level. They were attentive to our needs sending directions to our destination to our room, without me asking for them. They noticed our interest in baseball and one doorman gave my husband a commemorative baseball pin just by noticing his Chicago Cubs jersey. The rooms were clean, spacious, and the aIr conditioining was just perfect. The front desk personnel were very helpful and friendly. Their location was perfect for us.

name: Holiday Inn Select Memphis - Downtown (Beale Street)
title: “Not Good”
text:
This hotel has rude staff, dirty rooms and if your room faces the Peabody hotel, lots of noise all night.
We didn't seem to have to wait long for a lift but I would recommend parking on level 3 and walking up to level 4 as suggested in other reviews.
The hotel needs complete modernisation. The rooms are dark and feel unclean, quite disgusting.
On the plus side the location is good for all the Beale Street attractions.
Would I stay in this hotel again?? NO WAY.

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Fabulous Hotel in the Best Location”
text: The staff at the hotel was very professional and helpful. Whenever we needed anything they were there immediately. They suggested great restaurants and made the reservations for us. The rooms were excellent and very clean with a great view. The Colonnade made our visit to Boston wonderful!

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Good Experience”
text: Loved the Quiet. Food was great.

name: Hotel Commonwealth
title: “Favorite Boston hotel”
text: Always wonderful to return to this fabulous first class hotel. It is truly outstanding in every way.

name: Boston Harbor Hotel
title: “Convenient to Logan Airport and Faneuil Hall”
text: This is a very nice property. I stayed here for a conference and was given a room overlooking the water (I belong to the frequent guest club that the hotel belongs to) and the room was clean, very comforatable and nicely decorated. I appreciated the long hallway from the door to the sleeping area since it blocked some noise. I must say though that the plumbing from adjoining or nearby rooms was a little on the loud side. The staff I interacted with were very professional, helpful and pleasant. It is convenient to Faneuil Hall, but perhaps not readily apparent becasue of the various streets to be crossed to get there - it isn't particularly scenic out front of the hotel. But, Boston is small and a lot is walkable, or reachable in short order by cab. I would stay at this property again.

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “Close to downtown and near the Boston Common”
text:
After reading all of the lukewarm reviews, I was a little wary about staying at the Park Plaza. However, after arriving, I was pleasantly surprised by how friendly everyone was and how nice the room looked. It isn't the largest room I've stayed in, but I would say that for the price (went through Priceline) I was happy with what I got. It was clean, the room service is 24 hrs and there is a very nice bar (whiskey park) downstairs. The airconditioning was very weak but considering the fact that I got a view of the city from my room (I was on the 14th floor) I was satisfied. The shower is very nice and if you ask for a queen, they are very accomodating.
I would recommend anyone staying there (esp. if you get it for a pretty good price...)

name: Memphis Marriott Downtown
title: “Not at all what I expected”
text: We stayed at this hotel for the Memphis St. Jude Marathon weekend. This is a big deal with a lot of people in town and all of the hotels downtown had been booked for months. This hotel was not at all prepared for the crowds which I do not understand at all. The event happens every year and is capped at a certain number of participants, so the crowds are not unexpected. There were no towels ready (we were told they were still in the dryer). Our room was never cleaned while we were there and we had to call and request towels more than once. The first time I called I was told it would take "a really long time" to receive the towels and it was 9:00 p.m., so I requested that we get them in the morning. I was assured that that would be no problem. We did not receive towels in the morning. After the run, our room was not cleaned and we still had no towels (after running a half marathon, believe me, you need towels!). That's when I was told that they didn't have any and that they were still in the dryer. Really? This is the Marriott, not a Motel 6. I expect the room to be cleaned and there to be towels. They did eventually bring towels but never cleaned the room, emptied the trash or brought us more toilet paper or toiletries. Again, if this were a 1 or 2 star hotel, I would be more understanding but I have honestly had better luck with 1 or 2 star hotels than this one. Also, there was a guy in the elevator scamming people for money at 5:30 in the morning. The valet parking was a mess and no one there was at all helpful. The website says that parking is $18 but valet parking was $20 and when we asked about it beforehand, we were told it was $18. Just all around, not very helpful or friendly for the type of hotel this is supposed to be. If I am ever back for this run, I definitely won't stay here.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Memphis Downtown
title: “Zentrale Lage in Memphis”
text: Gute zentrale Lage in Memphis (eine Block von Beale Street entfernt). Die Zimmer sind schon etwas älter aber grosszügig. Die Straße ist zwar stark befahren, doch uns hat das nicht gestört. Als Willkommensgeschenk gab es einen warmen Cookie. Sehr lecker. An der Rezeption waren die Damen nett und hilfsbereit. Allerdings war das Parken mit 22 $ wirklich sehr teuer. Durch Priceline war es für uns eine ideal Übernachtungsmöglichkeit. Ach ja der Aussenpool ist eher klein.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton Memphis Downtown
title: “Good location, but rather tired.”
text: Just stayed for 3 nights. Good central location, but the basic rooms are small and the decor was rather tired. No alternative to valet parking was offered and at $20 a night this is robbery!

name: Boston Harbor Hotel
title: “Good For Business”
text:
I found the hotel very comfortable and ideal as a venue for meetings and for access to other parts of the city.
The room was very spacious with a view over the harbour.
The price was reasonable considering the location and convenience.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Memphis-Shady Grove Road
title: “Clean, quiet, helpful and friendly!”
text: Great hotel. I've stayed at this hotel twice, one trip being for two weeks. The staff are consistently helpful and friendly, doing anything they can to meet your needs. The hotel lobby space is well lit, relaxing and inviting for breakfast or to have a change of scenery during the day/evening. The rooms are clean - housekeeping does a great job every day of cleaning the room and working around my mess that I've left behind each day. Great hotel and I highly recommend it!

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Fantastic Hotel and PERFECT wedding event location!”
text:
We chose the Colonnade Hotel as the location for our wedding reception and couldn't have been happier with our selection. Not only could our guests not stop talking about the excellent accommodations and service at the hotel, but the event itself was perfect. The examples of the Colonnade's exceptional attention to detail and all the "special" things the hotel did are so numerous, we've had to categorize and summarize them below:
1. Event Selection/Planning: The wedding packages offered are terrific. They include everything you could hope for and don't nickel and dime you. The Event Planning Staff is very knowledgeable and was willing to accommodate any special and/or unique requests we had. We spent 9 months planning the event with the coordinator and felt the entire time that every aspect/detail/concern was addressed and covered by the event coordinator and banquet manager. They were available at all hours, even giving us their home email address.
2. Hotel Location: Perfect location! It is right downtown in Copley, feet away from the Prudential Center with a T stop right in front of the Hotel. There are multiple restaurants (local and national chains, fine dining, quick eats, and even a sports restaurant), a 24 hour grocery store and a 7-11 all within 100 yards. The Trolley Tour pickup and Duck Tour are across the street. 
3. Hotel grounds/rooms/amenities: The Colonnade sparkles with class and resonates with elegance. The rooms were recently remodeled and look modern and sharp; flat screen TVs, iPod docking stations, marble sinks, and modern fixtures. The rooftop pool is a MUST-SEE. It has awesome views of the city (including Fenway Park). The restaurant (Brassiere Jo) is top-notch, with excellent food and a terrific Belgian beer selection.
4. Hotel Staff: Everyone (Myself, my wife, our wedding guests staying at the hotel) were treated like royalty. No request was too small and everyone was made to feel accommodated and welcomed. The staff seemed to know all our wedding guests by name and treated them with 5 star professionalism. Multiple examples of "above and beyond" service, for example:
- Special amenities left in our parents rooms.
- Very early check-in for some of our guests who arrived early due to incoming flights.
- My friend forgot to pack his suit jacket and the Concierge gave my friend his own personal jacket to wear for the wedding (literally giving him the "shirt" off his back).
5. The Wedding: If you are having an event in Boston (Business, weddings, large party) you should seriously consider the Colonnade. The staff, food, roof-top pool cocktail hour, & reception hall all served to make our wedding a classy, elegant, and uniquely memorable event. Our guests said we could have stopped after the cocktail hour and it would have been better than any other wedding they attended. The food astonished everyone. Everything from the stationary displays to the passed hors d'oeuvres to the dinner itself met and could beat the standards of any 5-star restaurant. The chef personally came out to check on the food and the entire wait staff knew every detail of the dishes prepared. The hotel wedding coordinator and banquet manager were there every step of the way, ensuring not one detail was missed. The front desk manager and hotel staff could not have been more professional and accommodating. Everyone exceeded our highest expectations.
To summarize - we would recommend this hotel for any of your needs whether vacation, business, or major events. We plan to celebrate our anniversary here for many years to come.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Memphis-Shady Grove Road
title: “Employees are Fantastic !!!!”
text: The employees of this Hampton made this stay great for me. The front desk always had someone there and they were always friendly and not too busy to see to my needs. The shuttle driver (Fred) is a huge assett to this hotel. The hotel itself is a little dated but kept very clean and presentable. My suite was very clean, comfy and accomadating.

name: Staybridge Suites Memphis - Poplar Ave East
title: “Weekend stay in Memphis”
text: our stay in Memphis was very relaxing and enjoyable. The hotel location was close to everythign we need and wanted to go. Breakfast was great and the pool was clean and refreshing.

name: Staybridge Suites Memphis - Poplar Ave East
title: “Clean, nice, and friendly”
text:
Hotel rooms are not exactly on my list of favorite things, but Staybridge Suites in Memphis proved to be one of the cleanest, nicest, and friendliest hotels that I have ever stayed in. The room was kept just like I keep my home which allowed me to relax and enjoy my stay. I could not have asked for more friendly service from everyone who worked there from the desk clerk to the cleaning staff. Mr. Curtis Hynes made sure my family had everything they needed and provided us with a pleasant smile and friendly conversation. Next trip, I will look for the Staybridge name!
Thank you Staybridge Memphis!

name: Hilton Columbus/Polaris
title: “Staff was excellent”
text: I locked my keys in my car. I wasn't even staying in the hotel - I was just attending a conference there. The assistant manager called AAA and used her personal account with them. She took care of meeting them in the parking lot and getting my keys while another kind polite staff member took my wife and I in the hotel shuttle to get lunch. When we were done with lunch, my keys were ready at the desk. They completely changed my day!

name: Holiday Inn Hotel & Suites Memphis-Wolfchase Galleria
title: “Very nice”
text: I was in Memphis for an one night stay and the Holiday Inn Hotel & Suites was recommended by a relative. It was a little pricey but very nice accomodations. I was told by a clerk that the building is three years old but is in "like new" condition. Rooms were clean and comfortable and had all the essentials in the bath. Though I didn't choose to use it, there is a full service restaurant with a breakfast buffet available. I would definately stay here again.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Memphis Wolfchase
title: “Slightly better than before.”
text: The breakfast was much better than before more hot items to choose. The place is very clean and orderly. Nice quiet rooms. The only thing that we saw this time was the couch was in need of cleaning and the desk chair needed replaced. Their networking for TV could use an update. No internet in the rooms.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Memphis-Shady Grove Road
title: “Outsourced hotel reservations are good argument for “Inn sourcing"”
text:
Outsourcing is a way of life for vacationers. Despite the brouhaha regarding the export of American jobs, most of us have come to accept it as a generally seamless way of trip planning. But my recent experience of making a simple change to hotel reservations demonstrates the old adage about sausage making: you don’t want to see what goes on behind the scenes. The following is completely true, except I’ll use only first name initials. 
My brother is preparing to get married in Memphis. His wedding planner funneled guests to the Hampton Inn Memphis (Shady Grove) for reservations. The rate and location were great. So great, in fact, that about a month after I originally booked my stay there, I decided to celebrate my own anniversary in Memphis and arrive a couple of days early and stay at the same hotel.
That’s when the seamlessness of outsourcing began to unravel. I called the Hampton Inn where we’ll be staying. T picked up and politely told me she was switching me over to reservations desk. I soon learned that the “desk” was in the Philippines, where E answered. E extended my stay two days as I wanted, but only after putting me on hold twice for a total of over 25 minutes (my phone records bear this out). The only problem was that, in the process, he bumped my entire rate up about $21 per night.
Why the increased rate? E attributed the mistake to someone else whose name he eagerly volunteered: M. M is in Dallas, but E could not contact M again, due “system limitations,” so he did the next best thing. He transferred me to B, whom he said was in Memphis. B’s is the only name I’m suspect about, because I was told that no one at the Memphis hotel goes by the name of B.
 Who told me that? L. L is a housekeeper at the hotel, and she picked up the telephone “in order to help out the front desk” she informed. Ours was actually a pleasant conversation. L is a good listener, and sympathized with me after realizing that I had been on the telephone holding for 33 minutes. But L could only put me in contact with someone else. T.
Remember her? T was the first person I had spoken with, over half an hour ago. T assured me of one thing. She was busy booking a large group and couldn’t speak with me. But, strangely enough, she breathlessly offered to put me in contact the staff person in charge of weddings. Fearing the advent of another trip through the maze, I fortunately remembered the name of an onsite manager, M. I asked for him.
To say M was pleasantly efficient is an understatement. He made excuses for being overworked. He did not claim that the mix-up in my rates was due to anyone in the Philippines, Dallas…or even at the Memphis hotel’s front desk. He made the booking change, locked me in at the original rate, and wished me a great day and safe arrival. In essence, M brought about a new concept that I’ll call “inn sourcing”. Just as my hour long globetrotting call made a 360? return to the front desk, perhaps the “seamless” outsourcing concept should be rethought. M was the best argument of “Inn Sourcing” I had seen in a long time. © 08/30/2010 D.

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Memphis
title: “Très bonne option pas trop chère pour Memphis”
text:
Nous étions trois à nous partager une chambre lors de notre séjour au Crowne Plaza. L'hôtel est très facile à trouver en voiture, juste à la sortie de l'autoroute. Néanmoins Beale Street n'est pas très éloignée, environ 15-20 minutes à pieds (à faire de jour, on nous a déconseillé de le faire de nuit). Le personnel était très accueillant et agréable, ils ont même un service de voiturier gratuit qui dépose les clients dans les lieux touristiques de la ville pendant la journée. La chambre était spacieuse et confortable, bien qu'il manquait quand même quelques petits détails pour un hôtel qui se veut de ce niveau (peu de produits offerts dans la salle de bains, minibar vide...). Il n'y a pas de coffre dans la chambre, néanmoins il est possible de laisser ses objets de valeurs dans un coffre à la réception. 
Le buffet du petit déjeuner était passable, pratiquement aucun fruits... Nous y avons passé deux nuits et dans l'ensemble le service n'était pas si mal.

name: Hyatt Place Wolfchase Galleria
title: “Very Refreshing, Modern, and Clean”
text: We were impressed with the nice rooms and wonderful decor throughout the hotel. Rooms were very comfortable. Continental breakfast wasn't your average breakfast. We enjoyed our stay. Walked to Joe's Crab Shack.

name: Hilton Columbus/Polaris
title: “Ottimo albergo”
text:
Ho soggiornato in questo albergo per quasi una settimana durante un viaggio di affari. Ottime stanze, letto molto confortevole, ambiente silenzioso e rilassante. Alcune note: in bagno un'ottima e ampia doccia ma, purtroppo, solo fissa. Macchina per caffè "all'americana" a disposizione. La cassaforte non funzionava (anche se non ho riscontrato alcun problema in merito a sicurezza). Camera molto ampia ed estremamente confortevole. WiFi disponibile for free. Colazione veramente ottima sia per quanto riguarda brioches, ed espresso che per quanto riguarda continental breakfast (mai mangiato del bacon così croccante!). 
inoltre, la vicinanza al centro commerciale e ad un cospicuo numero di ristoranti tranquillamente raggiungibili con una breve passeggiata dal retro dell'hotel, permette di passare la serata in modo rilassante dopo una lunga giornata di lavoro.
Splendida la procedura di check-out che non avevo mai trovato altrove: alle 6.00 di mattina dell'ultimo giorno la fattura ti arriva da sotto la fessura della porta, senza disturbarti. Se è tutto OK per fare check-out è sufficiente premere un tasto specifico disponibile sull'apparecchio telefonico della stanza. Tutto qui. Non serve presentarsi per l'ennesima volta alla reception. Grandioso, no?

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “Loved the Park Plaza”
text:
My husband and I booked a room at the Park Plaza through priceline for $60 a night (our stay was in early Jan.) and I was thrilled until I read the reviews on this site and others. I called and requested a king non-smoking room before we left but being the pessimist I am, I knew we were going to be in for a terrible three nights. 
Upon arrival we were thoroughly impressed by the lobby and the manners of the staff, and after seeing our room we were impressed with it also. We must have had a remodeled room because it was extremely nicely decorated and the bed was comfortable and yes, a king. Very nice linens. No offensive odors or stains at all. Fresh paint and new carpet. The room and the bathroom were both on the smaller side but by no means intolerable. The shower had been recently remodeled and it was clean and there were two showerheads with great pressure. There was a digital thermostat in the room and you could open our window with no problems at all. Also - we had two phones - a cordless and one with a cord, and high speed internet connection. Large tv too. The closet was a normal sized closet - not a walk in or anything but more than enough for our needs. Oh and I loved the free shampoo and soap - the smell was wonderful. We had no complaints the entire time. Upon returning to our room every afternoon it had been cleaned and re-stocked. They also have a free business center open 24 hours which is nice. 
By the way we were on the 21st floor - and the halls were wide, clean, recently remodeled, and well lit. I looked on a few other floors just to see if any of those were different and they all looked the same. I would recommend, even at a higher price than we paid, and I would stay there again.
Oh and I forgot - the location only added to the Park Plaza. We didn't have a car in Boston and the nearest T station is about a block away, so that was very convenient. It is also surrounded by restaurants and shops and Boston Common and the public gardens are right around the corner. 
I can't think of anything else, I just know that I was very pleasantly surprised that no part of the hotel that I saw was dark or dingy or stinky, and everyone was very polite and helpful. My only regret is that I never ate at Finale, though we did eat at the Irish pub one night (can't remember the name) and the food was great.

name: Hyatt Place Wolfchase Galleria
title: “Nice, clean, large, room.”
text: The hotel was very nice. Rooms were spacious, with a refrigerator and sitting area. Ours had two beds, and a pull-out sofa in the sitting area. Definitely need a car to get to downtown Memphis, but within walking distance of shopping mall and restaurants. Hotel staff was responsive to any questions we had. Breakfast included. About a 20 minute ride to Memphis airport. Arranged for Memphis City Tour bus tp pick us up at hotel for a half day tour, and they brought us back afterward.

name: Elvis Presley's Heartbreak Hotel
title: “heartbreak heaven”
text:
we were delighted with Heartbreak hotel,it was everything we 
wanted,friendly staff,big room,with 2 TVs,continental breakfast
and plenty of it.And not far from Gracelands,so we could go when we wanted.the meditation garden is open every morning, free entry 7,30 to 8,30.it made our stay complete.ideal for Elvis fans.

name: Nine Zero Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Best in Boston”
text: L'albergo più bello in cui siamo stati in luna di miele: sito in pieno centro città, camere dal design fantastico e staff di prim'ordine. Tutto perfetto e trattamento molto amichevole. Chi visita questa meravigliosa città deve per forza provare il Nine Zero. Per il resto del nord America c'è sempre un Kimpton a disposizione...

name: Rodeway Inn Memphis
title: “Pay the extra $20 and stay in town”
text:
Firstly; the rooms. They were massive and had some new furnishings, so we were pretty happy with that. We were unhappy with the poor wireless connection and pair of grimy tweezers we found near the bathroom sink when we first arrived.
Secondly; location. It's a dump of an area and walking around, particularly at night, is not recommended. It's also a good 40 minute power walk to Beale St.
Thirdly; breakfast. It was the worst breakfast offering I'd ever seen. It was as though the hoteliers had gone to a nearby liquor store and grabbed the only food items available, and stocked those for the breakfast. In other words, it was long-life (or stale) muffins/pastries/bread and old fruit.
Finally; management. This is where it really falls apart. Prior to my arrival, I contacted the hotel and asked them how I arrange my airport transfers. They said to call the hotel once I had landed and I would be picked up. If only it turned out that easy. I rang the hotel and the staff member who answered spoke basic English (at best), and told me to wait "outside" the airport. Of course, I had no idea where to wait, having never visited Memphis before, and after about 45 minutes of futile follow-up conversations with the hotel the van finally arrived. It was very frustrating.
The language barrier was a problem many more times during our stay, for example, when trying to redeem the hotel's award points and asking simple things like directions around town. I don't think the staff's level of English was sufficient enough for them to be operating a hotel.
I would also advise them to do something about the smell in the lobby. It is a pungent curry smell, which shouldn't greet guests every time they enter.
Overall, we thought we'd save a few dollars staying here, but we ended up spending just as much on cabs getting downtown.
Admittedly, the rooms were comfortable, but that's not enough to salvage our opinion of the Rodeway Inn.

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “Good service, small rooms”
text: The service and location were perfect. The room and bathroom were small. Our family of four had a hard time with the tiny bathroom.

name: Memphis Marriott Downtown
title: “"Will not Hesitate to Return"”
text:
"Will make the same Choice Again"
The room was lovely, well laid out and very clean. The bed was very comfortable and the linen was crisp and inviting. The bathroom was also very clean with everything necessary in it. Guest amenities were luxurious and very adequate. The of Memphis from my room was very relaxing. Breakfast was rich. The downside is that i had to pay for the internet, which i think for a hotel of that size, price and quality should be complimentary. All-in-all it is obvious that somebody is paying attention to the hotel.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Memphis East
title: “viva la musica....”
text: Bell'albergo, consigliato a che si muove in macchina, perchè non centrale ma facilmente raggiungibile. Ottime le stanze, comodissimi i letti e buona anche la pulizia delle camere. Colazione molto abbondante e caffè (americano) sempre dispinibile.

name: Staybridge Suites Memphis - Poplar Ave East
title: “The Ideal Hotel for Business stay”
text:
I have been at this hotel for almost four months while working in Memphis. The room I have is great; a small apartment type suite with a seperate bedroom and living area with kitchen. This has been good as I work in my hotel room during the day. I have been able to utilize the business offices and the front desk personnel have been very helpful with getting faxes sent and taking messages. The hotel is located in a quiet out of the way area just off the main road into the downtown area. There are great locations for walking, biking or jogging around the hotel. Great restaurants are located very close by. 
The staff at the hotel -- front desk personnel, housekeeping and the food staff are personable, engaging and work very hard to make your stay as perfect as possible. They all are willing to go that extra mile to get you what you need.
If you are looking for a comfortable place to stay for a long or short term visit to the Memphis area, I highly recommend this hotel.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “Super Hotel direkt am Union Square”
text: Dieses Hotel ist wirklich sehr für Leute zu empfehlen, die ein Paar nette Tage in San Francisco verbringen wollen. Wir haben es zu zweit für 3 Übernachtungen gebucht. Queensizebed, Flachbildfernseher, Ankleideschrank, Fenster zum Union Square. Direkt vor dem Hotel hält die Cable Car und die Haltestelle für den SightSeeing Bus ist auch direkt am Union Square. Das Frühstück im Hotel haben wir nicht getestet, hätte man aber auch vor Ort noch buchen können.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Memphis - Beale Street
title: “Clean hotel convenient to action”
text: We just stayed one night between Xmas and New Year. We had two couples in two rooms. We were upgraded to executive rooms upon check in and really appreciated the extra room. The rooms were both clean and we enjoyed the stay. Two dings were 1. Housekeeping knocked on the door at 8:15 to clean the room and considering we were checkingout at 11 and had a late night on Beale St. It was a little early. 2. The breakfast was not very good and the area it was served in was nowhere near big enough for the number of guests. There was a line to use the small toaster and there were people waiting for tables. On the plus side the b-fast staff were helpful and hustling, they were just overburdened.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
title: “hotel agréable et bien situé”
text: bon hotel très bien situé et agréable, simple avec chambre confortable. sdb un peu désuète et petite mais propre. un petit dej (non compris) de bonne qualité. hotel calme et literie confortable.

name: Camino Real El Paso
title: “USBC Bowlers stay here, you won't be sorry”
text: Just got back from National's. Although our bowling wasn't good the visit to ElPaso was fabulous. The hotel staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome and take care of our needs. The shuttle drivers are eager to please and the hotel restaurant food is so good and priced right there is no need to go else where. The servers go out of their way to meet your requests. The people on the streets were very polite and we even took a ride on the public bus where the daily people were eager to engage in conversation and welcome us to El Paso. Just a walk across the street to bowl and walking to fast foods if that's your choice. It truly was a wonderful experience. I want to go back !! Barbara

name: Colonnade Hotel
title: “Bellissimo e confortevole”
text: Hotel ottimo da tutti i punti di vista: pulizia, servizi in camera, posizione. Si trova davanti alla fermata della metro che porta in centro a Boston. Siamo arrivati in macchina e abbiamo parcheggiato di fianco all'hotel nel parcheggio coperto.La camera era ampia, molto pulita, silenziosa, moderna e confortevole. Vicino si trova il ristorante/bar dell'hotel, in cui abbiamo cenato bene la prima sera. Lo consiglio a tutti

name: Embassy Suites Columbus - Airport
title: “Great Hotel, clean, quiet and NEW”
text: Not sure how old this hotel is, but it looks brand new. Rooms are well appointed, clean, and nicely furnished. Manager's reception was nice. Business center was nice, fitness center was nice. No bad comments.

name: Hampton Inn and Suites Columbus Downtown
title: “Good but not Great”
text:
In town on business, this was my first stay at a Hampton Inn. I didn't choose the hotel - and didn't pay for it either. The hotel is located right downtown across from the convention center and adjacent to the Short North entertainment/arts district. 
I pulled up and found that the only hotel parking is valet. The valet parking fee is $21 a night with in/out privileges. My arrival was around 5:30pm and the two valets were hustling. There were three cars ahead of me and I was told to park along the street and they'd move my car inside soon. I left the keys with the valet and grabbed my briefcase and bag out of the trunk. I've valet parked many times and never had a problem. I usually throw my valet key in my briefcase before heading out but this time I forgot and that was a bit of a problem. I walked inside and there was a small line at front desk as the two agents processed guests. Of course, as usual, one of the guests had some sort of issue which tied things up for everyone else. 
When they got to me it took about thirty seconds for them to take an imprint, make a key and give me an internet passcode. Upstairs I found a rather pleasant and comfortable room - nicer than I had expected. The bed was comfortable with a nice white comforter on top and I slept very well. 
The tv is in a cabinet - not a plasma - but the channel selection was impressive. I had wanted to watch a program that night on BBC American and figured I'd be out of luck. But sure enough, they had BBC American on the system with about 80 other channels. Not bad. 
I walked a block up High Street and had a drink and dinner at the Hyde Park Steak House - and noted there is a Starbucks just a block further up. 
Coming back to the hotel - a couple of hours later - the message light on the phone was lit. I called and got a message from the front desk asking if I had the keys to my car. Ugh. I put on my coat and headed back outside to find my year old Volvo still sitting where I'd left it - unlocked yet being watched by the valet staff. What happened?
