The valets said they couldn't find my keys. I specifically told the one valet I handed my keys to that I had to ask him to unlock the back doors to grab a bag. I think this jarred his memory but still no keys. I asked to see their key box to figure out if I could find my keys. Opening it up, I found another set that looked identical, but were for another car. I asked what they were going to do, especially since I had a 9am meeting across town and didn't want my car sitting outside all night - unlocked. They said they would look through the other cars and see if they could find the keys. 
I went back upstairs to try and relax. No point in hanging out or getting mad - and hoped for the best. If nothing else, I'd have to call Volvo Assist in the morning and see if the local dealer could get me a spare key made. An hour later I decided to go back down stairs to check on the situation. Walking outside, I found the hotel garage door closed and my car was no where to be found. I knocked on the valet door. They had found the keys [in another car] and my car was safe and parked in the garage. Finally, some peace. What ticked me off was the valets had told the front desk to call me and let me know; but the call never came through. 
The next morning I left and the car was brought up with no problems. I checked out and the door man was very friendly and positive. I headed to my meeting and that was that. 
Towards the end of the day, it was clear that driving three hours home was a bad idea. It was snowing, roads were icy and the thought of heading east into the mountains starting at 8pm didn't appeal. So, I stayed again. I checked their online site and it said no rooms available. I called and the front desk said they had one room left. I took it; showed up and was again in my room in about sixty seconds. The valet was very pleasant and considering the weather, I decided to walk up to Hyde Park for a late dinner at the bar. I ended up sleeping late - undisturbed - and checked out at 11:30am Saturday morning. 
All in all, not a bad stay. If I hadn't had the missing car key concerns, I'd up the review. But despite the frustration with valet, I'd return here. The rooms were clean, comfortable and the staff friendly and helpful.

name: Rodeway Inn & Suites
title: “WORST EXPERIENCE IN BALTIMORE”
text:
Terrible hotel. Booked on line. When checking i requested for a AAA discount.Was told i could get management discount and agreed. It was a trick, they put me in a king bedroom and charged me for it!
When i protested, management was rude and flatly refused tom refund my money. I ended up paying more than I would have paid before the "discount"
Rooms were dirty and we could not get an extra towel.
I would greatly discourage anybody to stay here.
peter
north carolina
PS: I am a regular visitor to Baltimore and have stayed in five good hotels after this trip

name: Days Inn Inner Harbor
title: “Best Facility and Location for Price”
text: The hotel was clean, the location was superb and the price was phenomenal. The walls seemed very thin so you could hear almost everything others were doing. Aside from that the stay was great.

name: Hampton Inn and Suites Columbus Downtown
title: “Hampton Inn Downtown a Pleasant Surprise”
text:
I stayed here two nights in December 2006 on a business trip. As soon as I entered the lobby, I knew this was not your average Hampton Inn. I don't stay in Hamptons very often, and was not sure what to expect. I was very pleased. This is a very upscale version, closer to Hilton. Staff was very attentive, courteous, and helpful, good business center, valet parking was nice. Rooms were nicely appointed, everything looked new, free breakfast was good (seemed to be a more extensive breakfast selection than an average Hampton). My room had both soft and firm pillows.
The location is great, right across the street from the convention center. But my favorite amenity is the fact that the hotel is located about a block from Martini, one of Cameron Mitchell's restaurants and one of my favorites in Columbus.
If you are looking for a new hotel in the downtown Columbus area, this is a safe bet.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Baltimore Downtown/Inner Harbor
title: “Nice hotel, but I was expecting more”
text:
Last time I stayed in Bmore, it was at the Residence Inn about a half mile up the harbor. I wanted to stay here, but was turned off by the location, as it seemed far off the inner harbor. This was well before I knew Harbor East existed. Anyway, I finally got my chance to stay, and found myself wishing I had stayed at the RI.
The location is great; right off the freeway, walking distance to Little Italy (terrible food - dont waste your $), Harbor East & the rest of the Inner Harbor. There's valet parking for $30something a night I believe & you can also brave parking on the streets behind the hotel for free.
This place passes all the surface test, nice lobby, cool brick building, etc. Unfort., when you whittle down deeper, you expose the flaws of the hotel. Not to say that theyre major flaws, just annoyances.
First- I know its a green hotel, but the lighting in the hotel is abysmal. In your room, you have to go through twenty lights to get your room to have sufficient light. You may ask, why not just open the curtains? Well in a perfect world that would be wonderful, but when you're on the first floor & you have a sidewalk right outside your window, that becomes an issue. But on the lights issue, how is it more eco friendly to have 10 dim lights on as opposed to one or two brighter ones? Seems counter productive to me.
Room placement- Being on the first floor by a sidewalk, certainly had plenty of um.... shall I call them disadvantages. First off, the nieghborhood behind the hotel looks like it should be nice. Nice colonial style townhomes... but here's the kicker. Who knows who lives in them. My first day - when I still had the blinds open- I witnessed a person finish up his hard day at "work" and come back home to his townhouse. His work was begging for money on a street corner. I watched him come walking up his stoop, take off his "homeless attire" which underneath revealed normal clothes, then go inside.... wow! Anyway, two nights later I'm trying to get in a power nap and I hear some homeless guy yelling in the street & comes violently knocking on my window. Fantastic! That just happened to be the night that I parked my car on the street by my room.
Another fun caveat of the rooms is the lack of cell coverage. Both sprint & verizon; neither could hold a call longer than 15 seconds, if I was even able to recieve a call!
This is sounding wayyyy to negative. This place really is a nice hotel, just dont stay on the first floor! Also, dont try to deal with the housekeepers.My personal favorite gem of this trip was my first day there, I'm getting ready to shower after sitting in traffic for 4 hours coming down from NJ only to find no shampoo! The housekeeper is next door, here is our exchange
me: do you have any shampoo, there is none in my room
housekeeper (hk): no!
me: what do you mean no? no you dont have any on you?
hk: no! no shampoo in hotel.
me: what, youre telling me that there is no shampoo in the hotel?
hk: no, no shampoo in the hotel.
me: donde esta el shampoo?
hk: no, no shampoo
I immediately went into my room & called the front desk, thinking that this was some bizarre "green hotel" thing. Either that or the housekeeper was on something. Yes there was shampoo in the hotel and someone immediately brought it to me. Seriously, that was the most bizarre thing that I have encountered at a hotel in quite sometime. I was waiting for the hidden cameras to come out and tell me that I'm on some game show.
Even though I've only harped on the bad, this really IS a nice hotel! Seriously, the location couldnt be beat & the staff (minus the housekeeper) were all great. Its just that when compared to the Residence on Light St, I enjoyed my time there much more for some reason.

name: Rodeway Inn & Suites
title: “Horrible nightmare”
text: First of all let me say the staff is very friendly. We were shown to our room. It was clean but very small. When we opened the door the door hit the bed so tells you how tiny it is. It had a very odd smell to the room. My kids went to turn on the bedside lamp and desk lamps and they didn't turn on. The overhead light was an annoying fluorescent light. Then my son decided to watch some tv while I was trying to figure out how to get to where we were going. The tv didn't work...why?? Because they unplug every thing in the room. We had to crawl under the desk to plug all cords in. The desk chair felt wet and slimy and the cords were greasy as well. My son sat in chair to watch tv ( not desk chair) and said it felt wet and weird as well. I have a special needs child and he didn't feel comfortable here at all. He was paranoid that smoke detector was sitting on the floor with NO battery. Went we went to bed the traffic from the busy highway was so loud I sat and looked at the wall all night. Had less than 3 hrs. I will say the beds were comfortable. Took shower the next morning in the huge bathroom and whatever they clean the floors with is some seriously heavy duty wax. I warned my boys about it because even with standing on towels they slid out from under you. My poor 12 yr old lost balance and came within inches of busting his head off sink. Breakfast was decent I liked the fact you could make your own belgian waffles. I got excited when I saw fresh fruit till I realized it was dusty wax decoration. The floors in the room where food is as well was so waxy that the chair slid while sitting in it. The price was great but I could have paid $20 more and stayed somewhere much nicer. Will never stay there again.

name: Hotel Brexton
title: “I could have stayed for a week!”
text:
Two nights was not enough for me in this elegant hotel, an historic building which was recently re-purposed (it's first life was as a hotel!)
I met 4 or 5 front desk people - they were all so friendly and helpful.
The common spaces - even the elevator - are quirky; my room was long, lean and beautiful, with 4 windows over looking a little garden and out to the neighborhood; my bathroom in a turreted space - a remarkable architectural and design feat.
The bed was so comfy and the pillows fantastic; the space was quiet and serene.
Self serve breakfast was simple and ample; coffee maker in the room with real coffee - a plus for me.
The location could not be better; my morning walk thru this beautiful neighborhood to the Inner Harbor was just far enough, the Homewood campus of Hopkins less than a 5 minute drive; 10 minutes to the Visionary Arts Museum and Federal Hill; easy access to major highways.
I can't wait to go back!

name: Rodeway Inn & Suites
title: “Nice and Clean Motel With Cheap Price Ranges in the Area!!!!”
text: I was there in Baltimore for my business purpose with my colleagues..We were looking for a nice place which can fit into our budget...We found this motel meeting all our needs...They provides refrigerator in the rooms..Nice and clean rooms...daily room service and free internet service...Last but the most important the price ranges are quite cheap compare to some hotel in the area....15-20 mins from baltimore downtown...Hotel is managed by one family...this family maintain this motel pretty good..Definetley recommand this motel..

name: Admiral Fell Inn
title: “A Great Place to Stay”
text:
We had a wonderful stay @ the Admiral Fell Inn. The front desk staff (especially Hakeem) went out of their way to provide everything we needed for a great experience.
The Harbor Night package was an excellent value & saved us alot of money during the course of our visit.
We also loved that the hotel is pet-friendly (regardless of pet size) & our "dogter" received lots of attention as we passed thru the lobby.
We will definitely return!

name: Americas Best Value Inn
title: “gutes Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis, aber LAUT”
text: positiv: - alles dabei, was man für diesen Preis erwartet - kostenfreies Parken - kostenfreies I-Net (Wifi) - jeden Tag für geputzt - Kühlschrank, Kaffeemaschine - Fernseher mit 70 Sendern - in der Nähe Tankstelle, McDonalds negativ: - aufgrund naher Lage zur Interstate 95 viel Verkehrslärm - bis Downtown ca. 6 Meilen über schlechte Straßen und durch gefährlich anmutende Gebiete - Frühstück nur amerikanisch süß - Kaffee, Milch, süße Bagels, Frischkäse, Marmelade, Juice, Kellogs (aber steht ja schon vorher fest)

name: Hotel Brexton
title: “So much more characterful than the big corporates”
text:
I chose Hotel Brexton as an alternative to the big corporate hotels near the harbour side and I'm so glad I did. I was in Baltimore for a meeting at the Convention Centre which was a pleasant 25 minute walk away. My room was comfy, clean and characterful, the breakfasts were more than adequate but what made my stay a 5 star experience was the professional and friendly staff...all very personable and helpful. 
The hotel is in a quiet neighbourhood, the rooms are spacious and overall I think Hotel Brexton represents very good value for money.

name: Radisson Plaza Lord Baltimore
title: “We must have been lucky!!!”
text: My husband made reservations at this hotel without consulting me. Before we left for our trip to Baltimore Labor Day weekend for the Baltimore Grand Prix, I read the reviews. I was horrified and afraid to stay at the Radisson. I tried to find another hotel, but everything was booked because of the festivities. So I prepared myself for the worse and was so stressed out by the time we arrived on Friday (we booked a three night stay). Now, keep in mind, this hotel is a "HISTORIC HOTEL" and listed in the historical catalog for hotels. "Historic" means "old". That much I expected and did not mind. We were pleasantly greeted by the door staff, as well as the front desk. Very, very nice people, especially Casey! The lobby and rest of hotel was as expected and very nice, in my opinion, as I like historic architecture. The elevators were very slow, however, but acceptable. We booked a King bed room on the Plaza level (17th floor), with free breakfast and cocktail hour in the evenings. Our room was beautiful! It must have been renovated. We had a corner room and plenty of sunshine (although, the windows were very dirty). Pleasant decor and clean. Everything worked and the furniture was old but in good condition. The sleep number mattress must have been new because it was extremely comfortable and the remote worked fine in order to adjust the firmness. The bathroom was immaculate!!! Modern and clean, no bugs, no hair and plenty of hot water. Also an abundant supply of toiletries (shampoo, conditioner, body lotion, great soaps, body gel, shower cap, cotton swabs, etc.. Hair dryer worked great. Great shower head, great water pressure, and shower curtain was not a problem. Ok, so maybe an old style Philips TV in the sleeping area, but it was big enough, and we got 28 channels including HBO and the reception was fine! Housekeeping was great. Our room was cleaned everyday and linens were crisp and clean, and the towels smelled fresh. They were not the softest towels, but just fine for us. Every staff person we came in contact with was extremely pleasant and made us feel special!! There was traffic noise, but your are staying in the CITY!!! So what do you expect!! The breakfast was ok with enough choices to nibble on. The cocktail hour was nice, with beer, wine and beverages and good appetizers!! The only MINOR complaint is the hallways to our room were smelly--like old carpet smell and stale cirgarette smell--but if they installed automatic air fresheners in the hallways, it would probably resolve that issue. All in all, we had a great experience and plan on staying here next year for the Grand Prix as well!!! (Just going to make sure we get that same exact room!!!!) I feel bad for all you folks that had a terrible experience, but I am sure glad we were not one of them!!!

name: BEST WESTERN Plus Envy Hotel
title: “Modern and Clean”
text:
This hotel was central and modern. Our room was large and nicely decorated. The bed was comfortable with nice linen and everything was spotless. Service was good on the front desk. Breakfast wasn't anything special and they need to ensure that items remain topped up for those guests coming later as when went there was no milk, sausage or orange juice. This was resolved quickly on request though. 
I don't have any complaints about the location. Yes, it is at a bus stop. Yes, there were a few 'characters' around but it was not threatening in any way and I felt safe at all times. People were friendly and helpful and I would have no hesitation about staying here again.

name: Quality Inn Downtown Baltimore
title: “Served its purpose...”
text:
My friends and I spent one night at the Quality Inn Downtown Batimore because we were attending something at the Convention Center. The hotel said it was .3 miles away, but it was a little further walk. As previously stated, parking is not on-site, but 15.00 a day is reasonable in a major city, you need to carry your belongings a block.
 All the staff I encountered were very friendly during our stay. The room was clean but small. We had a room with two queen beds and you could barely move the chair at the desk. The bathroom was a decent size though. The beds were comfortable. The free wi-fi worked fine in our room. The TV on the other hand did not carry ESPN which was not good. Very limited channels on TV. Not too many places to eat directly around the hotel, but you could walk down towards Pratt Street as there are many places down there.
 The continental breakfast the next day was bare bones. Toast, cereal, and bagels. It was fine. Overall, the staff was nice, the location was ok, and the room was ok. We stayed at another hotel that weekend (booking issues) and liked it better. I would stay here again, but look elsewhere first.

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Baltimore Downtown/Inner Harbor
title: “Good value for the price”
text: We just got back from our stay at this hotel. Couple of drawbacks: The shower is very nice, I thought there was plenty of water pressure (unlike the other reviewer), but there is no shower curtain, only a partial glass partition. My husband splashed the water around and got it all over the bathroom floor. Other drawback is that there is one elevator to serve about 30 rooms per floor for 4 floors (5 story hotel). We had to wait a long time for the elevator for breakfast and to check out. The $27/day for valet is actually not that steep compared to other hotels in the area. Great location, about 1 mile walk to the stadium and to Camden Yards. My favorite was the hair dryer in the room. They provide a very powerful and compact hair dryer in the room.

name: Elvis Presley's Heartbreak Hotel
title: “Heartbreak Hotel totally gets you in the Elvis spirit!”
text: I, like the person before me that wrote a review, am glad I didn't let the negative comments sway me. We had an absolutely wonderful time. All of the staff that we dealt with at the hotel bent over backwards to be friendly and helpful. There is alot to do within walking distance and Beale Street is a short distance away. Our room was very nice and clean. You really start to get into the Elvis spirit as soon as you walk in the lobby. The complimentary continental breakfast was plus too!

name: Americas Best Value Inn
title: “The staff was so polite!”
text: My family and I stayed here for 2 nights so my son could have medical tests at John Hopkins. It was cheap and convenient to the downtown. After my sons test he vomited all over the floor in the lobby and one of the staff members rushed right over to help. He was so sweet and cleaned it right up. They were so helpful and we were able to rest quietly. It wasn't the most modern in the rooms, but the fridge was a great plus. I would definately recommend this hotel!

name: Americas Best Value Inn
title: “Very good accomodations, location and price.”
text: I have stayed at this hotel at least 6-7 times. It is my first choice of hotel when I travel to Baltimore. Hotel is conveniently located near the interstate and downtown inner harbor. There is a large supermarket, a small shopping center and several fast food restaurants located one minute from this hotel. I stopped staying in the pricey downtown hotels because this hotel is "better" and much less expensive. The continential breakfast is so-so but there is free parking and smoking rooms are available. Caution, book early as this is a popular hotel and rooms sometimes sell out quickly. This is "my" hotel wheneven I travel to Baltimore. I have recommended this hotel to many friends and family members.

name: BEST WESTERN Baltimore West
title: “Bed Bugs”
text: The pictures look great but the rooms are not up to par with the pictures. My mom was attacked at 5AM by bed bugs. The shower had mold on the was walls and the tub was dirty. I would never recommend this hotel. Run

name: Elvis Presley's Heartbreak Hotel
title: “The Heartbreak Hotel Experience”
text: If you are an Elvis fan you must stay at the Heartbreak Hotel and share in the Elvis experience! From the moment you enter the lobby to you get to the room it's a blast from the past! Elvis is everywhere! I really enjoyed my stay there and if I had the chance would go back in a heartbeat! The rooms where nicely decorated and clean. Everything you needed on a trip! Staff was very friendly and accomendating. Only problem was with the shuttle service....one night we waited on Beale St in the pouring rain for over an hour for the shuttle to come. We called the hotel several times and asked if they had any information on where the driver was,we also asked it we could take a taxi back at their expence and their answer was NO. Otherwise, we had a great time! You have to see it to believe it!!! They have kept the King alive!!!

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Baltimore
title: “Good choice for business, but could be better”
text:
Hilton generally offers excellent service and a fairly good value, especially in today's hotel market that has adopted the philosophy of offering less for the same price. However, the Homewood Suites offers quite a bit for the money, especially considering it shares a building with the Hilton Garden Inn. The most surprising aspect of this hybrid hotel is that both the Garden Inn and Homewood were avaialble at the same rate. I chose Homewood for the free breakfast, free dinner, free wireless internet and larger room.
The room was excellent -- very spacious and clean. The televisions worked nicely and offered a decent channel lineup. Some people complain about the exhaust vent in the bathroom that does not turn off and makes quite a bit of noise. I usually sleep with a white noise machine running, so I actually liked this. It definitely helps at night with some of the local traffic outside the window. The bed is comfortable and the linens, towels and kitchen area is very clean and nice. My only complaints for the room were a backed-up shower drain and a slight ammonia smell (think cat litterbox) from the tub which never seemed to be a problem (the smell only, of course) when actually using the shower. If it was, I would have requested a room change.
Service was very good -- the staff gives taxi vouchers for travel to Johns Hopkins. I needed these each day so I could travel to the campus for business. The staff was very friendly but I did not rate them a 5 only because I requested my shower drain to be addressed the next day while I was away and it was not done. I had to get service upon returning to the room, which is when I wanted to use the shower. The service was complete in about 20 minutes, but the front desk staff fumbled that one.
Breakfast is just ok. The offerings aren't great in terms of variety and quantity. You get scrambled eggs (which are dry and not very tasty), sausage, bacon and cereal. The waffle iron is a great feature but they consistently ran out of fruit and had little to no yogurt. If I were managing this hotel, I would offer the Homewood room for a slightly higher rate and give their guests free breakfast at the main restaurant which offers an omelet stand. The free breakfast in the Homewood lodge just isn't great. I didn't try any of the free dinners but it seemed more like a cafeteria-style offering, with the exception of the free draft beer and wine (a nice touch).
The main reasons I recommend this hotel: location and gym option. The hotel partners with a local health club to give you access to a REAL facility while you are a guest. You will not find a closet gym with one treadmill and a pair of 10-lb dumbbells. Excellent gym option here, which was very important to me. The hotel's location is great, right on the Inner Harbor and within walking distance of a Whole Foods Market (very important to me) and a 24-hr CVS. It's also very convenient to the JHU campus, especially with the taxi voucher .
Overall, the Homewood is a good choice. I will stay here again if I travel to this part of Baltimore for business, but I will likely opt for the $10 restaurant breakfast vs. the free Homewood Lodge breakfast in the future.

name: Admiral Fell Inn
title: “Admiral Fell Inn ~ SIMPLY AMAZING”
text:
On our first trip to Baltimore my husband and I booked a room at the Admrial Fell Inn, not only did we absolutely fall in love with the entire place and the professional staff but we can not wait to book another trip there.... hopefully it will be SOON! 
The amenities were wonderful, the rooms were immaculate and clean, the beds were cozy and heavenly, the atmosphere was romantic and nostalgic, the location was superb, the staff were courteous, humorous, helpful, and extremely professional, the overall feel of the place was quaint yet regal. I can NOT rave enough about this hotel. 
They offer free activities, including wine and chocolate... as if that were not enough there are evening receptions with light snacks followed by a ghost tour! My husband and I had a fabulous time and truly cannot wait to visit this hotel again! EVERYTHING about the place was WONDERFUL! 
Sincerely~
Fell Inn love with Admiral Fell Inn
Heather and Mike

name: Brookshire Suites
title: “Fantastic!”
text: Very welcoming, staff was very nice, the manager made sure everyone was pleased during breakfast time and socialized with the costumers. The rooms were very clean one of the best I have seen. And the view we got from our room was beautiful. Great hotel. Highly recommend it.

name: Elvis Presley's Heartbreak Hotel
title: “génial!”
text: un must pour les fans, l'hôtel est juste à côté de Graceland et on s'y trouve plongé dans le monde d'Elvis car les clients sont tous fans, grande chambre avec tv, belle salle de bain, petit salon attenant et kitchenette avec frigo, café, micro ondes, déco Elvis dans tout l'hôtel, grand lit confortable, propre, personnel très serviable, bar et resto sympa avec écran géant at film et concerts d'elvis, petit déjeuner gratuit en buffet,vafé disponible toute la journée, internet gratuit (petit débit), shuttle gratuit pour aéroport, shuttle payant pour aller à Beale street, sun studio, rock'n roll museum toutes les heures bref rien à dire nous y retournerons avec grand plaisir

name: Days Inn Inner Harbor
title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: Very good location, within walking distance of Camden Yards, Inner Harbor and many restaurants and shops. Lobby is small but attractive. Only had breakfast in the restaurant but was very good. Check in was slow on a very busy saturday afternoon. Parking is expensive but convenient except for when there is an Oriole's game. The parking garage is open to everyone looking for a place to park for the game. We drove to the B & O RR museum on Sunday morning and when we returned to the hotel we could not get into the garage because it was full so we drove over to the Inner Harbor and parked there. Wouldn't have minded except we had all ready paid to park in the garage next to the hotel and then had to pay to park at the Inner Harbor which we had planned to walk to. I gave the room an average rating because our room was next door to a maintenance room which made our room narrow and tight spacewise.

name: Radisson Plaza Lord Baltimore
title: “Good experience this time”
text:
This is the second time I've stayed at the Radisson Plaza Lord Baltimore. We stay in Baltimore periodically to see our son so I usually book where I can get the best deal (Baltimore hotels are notoriously expensive in the inner harbor area). The first time we stayed here we had a cavernous room but thought the furnishings were a little dingy. I was tempted to to back with an incredible special rate that included parking at the nearby deck, and it was a very pleasant experience this time.
The service at the front desk and in the bar was truly excellent. We had a surprisingly good early supper in the bar area that hit the spot. Our room was small but clean, although there was a big stain on the carpet. We had a Sleep Number bed, which should have been a plus but I'm not a big fan because I can't ever find a comfortable setting.
Just a reminder that this is an old hotel--my husband stayed here on a school trip 45 years ago! Having now stayed there twice, my sense is that the rooms may be a little uneven in quality and size. Our stay there was very short this time so I did not check out all the amenities, but it suited us very well for this visit.

name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Baltimore
title: “Great Stay!”
text:
My husband and I stayed in Homewood Suites during a corporate event in Baltimore. We really enjoyed our stay in the hotel. 
Our room was very clean, but for a new hotel, the living room furniture and comforter seemed worn. Also, the fan in the bathroom runs constantly (no off switch) so we had to cover it with a piece of paper to soften the noise. The bed was very comfortable though and the shower stayed hot and had good pressure. We were on the top floor and had an excellent view of the statue in the round-a-bout below and of the harbor. The room was plenty big enough and the TV is very large. We only stayed one night, but it would have been comfortable for a longer stay. 
Breakfast was good, they had a fairly wide selection of hot and cold choices and everything we had tasted good.
The hotel's location is great, we were within walking distance to Pier 5 that had a lot of great attractions, bars, and restaurants and access to the water taxi and aquarium.
Service was great, everyone was very helpful and kind.

name: Madison Hotel
title: “A wonderful stay...”
text:
We just returned from a stay at the lovely Madison Hotel... what a treat! Everything was really wonderful from the time we pulled up to the front door. This hotel is dedicated to making their guests feel welcome and the staff were superb, friendly and helpful at every turn. 
The rooms were small but very clean and well appointed. 
The shower in the room was larger than most although there was no bathtub.
We enjoyed a truly 5 star meal at the restaurant in the hotel called "Bistro 83" ... and be sure you try the "Wedding Cake" martini!!! We were impressed with the food, the service, the atmosphere... everything!
The fitness center and swimming pool were very clean, well kept and not crowded - the little touches at this hotel are what make it special, like fresh fruit and bottled water for those using the gym.
The continental breakfast was very good and, again, the hotel made you feel like it wasn't a regular continenal breakfast by using fine linens on the tables, silverware and higher quality breakfast foods with more variety. I HIGHLY recommend a visit to the Madison Hotel - you won't be disappointed.

name: Hotel Brexton
title: “AN Incredible experience”
text:
I was planning a weekend getaway for my wife and I, and did quite a research on all the hotels in the Innner Harbour area. I didnt want your typical "CHAIN" hotel so ran into a blog for Hotel Brexton. Read more and more reviews and thought "wow" this has got to be the place. My wife loves "antiqey/modern" furniture type and I thought this would be a perfect place. Long story short, she was aurprised when we drove up to the hotel as she didnt know where i was taking her, but her face lif up the instant we walked in. From a friendly front desk to an incredible looking room, our stay was nothing but wonderful/short but we have promised ourself well be back in the future.
SIncere thanks to Paul the manager and his staff for wonderful hospitqlity and for making our anniversary a special one and thank you for the Bottle of champagne. CLASS ACT
We highly reccomend this hotel to anyone.

name: Days Inn Inner Harbor
title: “Days inn at the inner harbor in baltimore”
text: The hotel was very clean and the staff was wonderfully helpful. The location is excellent with the convention center and Inner Harbor a few minutes walk away. Guest laundry on site is basic but perfectly functional. We would definitely stay here again and feel confident that we would enjoy the same level of comfort, welcome, and convenience.

name: Radisson Plaza Lord Baltimore
title: “The staff were full of smiles!”
text: Our room was on the 12th floor and had no problems with it. It took us a few minutes to get the hang of the air number bed. I still prefer my memory foam bed at home.The staff at the desk that night was Lisa & Daniel. Both were smiling and friendly. They answered our questions and gave us maps of the area. We added a night because of Lisa's friendly manor. The breakfast in the hotel was very good and the waitress,Ivori,was on top of her game. The ladies in the coffee shop were very friendly too. The only problem we had was how far the parking garage was from the hotel. Like any big city at night be aware of your surroundings. This beautiful hotel made Baltimore a great vacation city.

name: Days Inn Baltimore
title: “This hotel is dated, smelly and and in need of an overhaul.”
text: If you want cheap then this is it but if you want cleanliness then look somewhere else. Terrible odors and outdated decor. A little scary for me. Dont know how I made it through the night.

name: Tremont Suites Hotel and Grand Historic Venue
title: “Comfortable suite, attentive staff - we really enjoyed our stay.”
text: For my annual business conference, my husband and I enjoyed a 4-night stay in a spacious, updated suite with a full kitchen and a very comfy bed. The suite was clean and quiet and did I say, spacious. All of the staff--room service, front desk, at Tug's restaurant and especially the Deli were friendly and very customer service-oriented. It was warm in Baltimore, yet the room temp was just right. Just a little frustrated that one of the treadmills and a television was not working in the exercise room. A big plus was the meeting rooms for the conference. This hotel is connected to a former historic temple--our meeting rooms were beautiful--architecture, wood work, art work, exquisite carpeting.

name: Admiral Fell Inn
title: “Historic hotel with a great location”
text: My husband is a US Merchant Marine, and I usually pick him up and/or drop him off at the port of Baltimore. When we stay in Baltimore, we check into this hotel. It has a quiet elegance, and the location is great for walking around the Fell's Point area of Baltimore. On my recent visit, I did opt for the jacuzzi room and I would not do that again. For one thing it was only slightly bigger than my tub at home, and another thing the water from the shower did not drain quickly so after taking a shower, well the thought of sitting in the tub lost its appeal. Two other things of note, if you valet park your vehicle, the valet leaves at 10:00PM. When I had to get my car later than that, I had to get the key card for the garage form the front desk and walk 2 blocks to a closed garage. I was not happy doing this , but luckily my car was on the ground floor. Upon my return, I parked on the street as the meters do not go into effect until 10:00 AM. The Inn also charges a fee for $9.95, to cover internet, phone use, a gym pass, and a shuttle. We did use the shuttle which was convenient. The staff was helpful and friendly, and as I said the location makes its a great restaurant/bar/shopping/museum place.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Baltimore Downtown / Inner Harbor
title: “Great customer service”
text: Stayed one Friday night in January. Gave us a traditional room that had a balcony with nice city view- that was an unexpected pleasant surprise. Front desk was very pleasant. Bartender was happy to serve us drinks at 10:55 even though she was closing up at 11pm. Hotel was not crowded and they had no problem giving us a late check out. Breakfast buffet for 10.95 was reasonable for the food choices (including made to order eggs and waffles) and the service was great there too. Walking distance to restaurants and a nice spa.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Baltimore North
title: “What a great hotel.”
text:
I traveled down to Baltimore with a group of friends from Massachusetts. 
We booked two rooms, and were able to get them moved to the smoking area and still have then next to each other. The staff was more than accommodating, even with a late check-in for the evening.
The rooms themselves were excellent. Clean and more than enough towels and such for our entire party.
I enjoy La Quinta, and this stay really made me realize that you get a great deal for what you pay for. I stayed at another hotel (Super 8) later in the weekend and it actually cost more, and was not nearly as large nor as nice. 
I can't say enough about how I love to travel, and I love the ability to rely on La Quinta to have a great spot to land whenever I'm out and about.

name: Brookshire Suites
title: “Do Not Stay Here!”
text: We used Trip Advisor to pick this place that we stayed in May 13-16. If it was just that we had no A/C for our stay, I would not say anything but conditions were awful. No literature is given to you upon check-in or in the rooms and no mention was made of their Cloud Nine continental breakfast nor their happy hour (without booze since they lost their liquor license). The remotes do not work for the TV's in the rooms, so we had to change channels using the TV. Also note that this big city hotel only has 25 channels to choose from and 4 of them are ESPN channels. We tried to use the ATM in the lobby and that did not work. Wi-Fi is an issue here, but again the front desk clerk failed to tell us they also have a wired connection in the room. The maid failed to leave extra toilet paper in our room so we called down at 3 P.M. to request some. At 4:30, we called again and they assured us some would be sent up. We returned after seeing the Yankees/Orioles game, and there still was no toilet paper so I had to go to the front desk to get some. I sat one day and complained to the manager and he failed to call me back to notify me he was crediting my bill, which they did eventually do. The final calamity happened overnight on our final night there when the pipes burst and knocked out all hot water to the hotel so we could not get a shower. Next up, I tried to get a luggage cart for our stuff, and all were being used. I guess everyone was leaving as fast as they could!

name: Madison Hotel
title: “Beautiful boutique hotel-much better than Peabody”
text: The Madison is a classy alternative to the overhyped Peabody. King suites are well appointed with Gilchrist & Soames amenities, Frette bath robes, and a small kitchenette area. Our suite overlooked the Mississippi River. Beds/linens are ultra comfortable. Room was spacious, and very quiet. Most floors have only 8 rooms. Bathroom is large enough to park a car. Room service menu, while not bad by any means, is not anything to get very excited about. OK for a late night snack. Great location, within walking distance to any Beale Street locale. Staff was very accomodating to all our needs. Comparable to the Waldorf Towers in NYC.

name: Baltimore Marriott Inner Harbor at Camden Yards
title: “Great staff, great accommodations”
text: An excellent value for the weekend rate we paid. Great for coming into town and taking in a show or event. What impressed me the most was the friendly and helpful staff: from the bell staff, bar and restaurant staff, housekeeping and front desk, everyone went out of their way to make my family feel welcome and at home. The average-size room was clean and comfortable, and the entire hotel was well maintained. We'll stay there again on our next visit to Baltimore.

name: Madison Hotel
title: “Great Choice!”
text: Much better and more updated hotel compared to the Peabody! It is much more comfortable and fun than the Peabody. Finding a newspaper around there is like finding a needle in a haystack though!

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Baltimore Inner Harbor
title: “Could Not Ask for More!”
text: All of the positive reviews of this place are pretty much spot on what we received when we stayed at the Hampton Inn - Inner Harbor. For me who had never been to Baltimore, I chose this place based on the location and price and hoped for the best. The Hampton Inn did not disappoint. After an exhausting eight hour drive, we were greeted by the friendliest hotel manager that I had ever had the pleasure to meet. He allowed us to check in earlier, handed out maps and pointed out spots of interest, fantastic for someone that had never been to the city before. Our check-in was quick and trouble free and the manager insisted that if there was anything that we needed, we shouldn't hesitate to get in touch with him directly. Major points for that. Our room was on the sixth floor, and only a short walk from the elevator. The room itself was a good size, more than ample space for the king sized bed a nice seating area next to the windows and a desk. The bathroom was massive. The cleanliness is the upmost importance to me when staying at a home away from home and this place did not disappoint. The place was spotless. Linens were clean and crisp, plenty of towels and complimentary soaps and lotions. The flat panel tv was great and the free HBO was a treat as it was the season finale of True Blood! There was also free Wifi available, great for checking email or tooling around online. The room was quiet, and the bed was soft and comfortable. If you're going for the view, this might not be the place as our room overlooked the building across the street that may or may not have been slated for demolition. This view was easily rectified by closing the blinds. The proximity of this hotel to all the activities, dining and entertainment of the Inner Harbor are what puts the Hampton Inn head and shoulders above the rest. With a quick five minute walk you were in the heart of it all. We chose to take the MARC train to DC one of the days of our stay and we were only a ten minute walk from the Camden Yards Station, meaning our car could stay parked in the lot. The parking is a big hefty at $29/day but its the price you pay to stay in any area that doesn't allow the luxury of its own on-site lot. The free breakfast each morning was a great selection of bread products, make your own waffles, bacon, sausage, eggs or omelets, fruit, cereal, juice and coffee. A great addition for those traveling on a budget. Overall, we had a fantastic stay and I would definitely be back again. This hotel hit all of the bars that I set : cleanliness, friendliness of staff, location and value. I could not be happier!

name: Courtyard by Marriott Baltimore Downtown / Inner Harbor
title: “Convenient, Quiet, Clean”
text: Wanted a place near, but not at, the event I was attending. This was great, good wireless connection, quiet room close to the bustle of the Inner Harbor. Greatl little pizza/cafe adjacent with outdoor dining.Would stay there again.

name: Sheraton Baltimore City Center Hotel
title: “Pick a different hotel.”
text: Not a fan of Sheraton and this hotel reinforced my beliefs. This hotel has over 1,000 rooms and only ever has one person working behind the desk, even during check in and out times. Ask for the North Tower if you must stay here; the South Tower rooms suffered water damage during Hurricane Sandy. They automatically add valet parking to your bill whether or not you have a car, necessitating waiting in the line at the front desk for a correction.

name: Mount Vernon Hotel
title: “It was just okay”
text: We were in town for an event and decided to stay overnight as opposed to drive home late. Although, relatively old, the hotel has been maintained nicely. We thought the sleep was comfortable and the room was spacious enough... About the size you would expect for a basic room with two queen beds. The staff was friendly and helpful. The free breakfast was sufficient and tasty. The problems... 1) thankfully it wasn't a really cold night. The heat never came on. When I inquired, I was told that the heat is automatically regulated by the building and that it had not switched on but would be soon. We never felt the heat. 2) the parking was less than desirable. There are only 30 spots for the 100+ rooms. I guess it is understandable being that the building was built during a time when there weren't thousands of cars on the road. Alternate parking is across the street but get there early as it closes. As I mentioned, we were in town for an event and therefore, made it back to the hotel after 9pm. The garage parking was closed. We had to park almost two blocks away. 3) older hotel, loud plumbing. Our neighbors were up early, therefore, so were we. Despite all of this, the location is great. There are some really good food options in the area.

name: Sheraton Baltimore City Center Hotel
title: “Excellent Service”
text: I had my wedding at the Sheraton Baltimore City Center hotel and it was the best decision I ever made. As a busy physician, time management is important to me. The sales manager, Vaneska, was so helpful in helping me plan my special day that I did not even need a wedding planner!Vaneska went out of her way to make sure my table settings, flowers, and decorations were in order. The food & drinks were also great. In addition, the proximity and easy acessabilty of the hotel to the Amtrak Penn station as well as the BWI airport made travelling easy for my out-of town guest. Finally, it was a plus that the hotel was slightly removed from the hustle & bustle of the busy inner harbor...yet just a walking distance away if a guest felt like taking it in. I highly recommend this hotel for your stay or your event ;o) - Abi

name: Radisson Hotel at Cross Keys
title: “Excellent hotel, good value, wonderful staff”
text: Stayed at this property because of electrical outage in our area. Relatives from out of town had stayed here and were pleased. The hotel staff was very welcoming, sympathetic and understanding. The room was large and had a private enclosed patio with a lounge, 2 chairs and a table. The beds were extremely comfortable. Only down side is that the tv is older and the bathrooms are older. However, ammenities are fine and shower pressure is wonderful.

name: Radisson Hotel at Cross Keys
title: “Agree with dated rooms, great staff!”
text: It's always a tad uncomfortable to stay at a hotel that's near a major medical center. This hotel is very near John Hopkins medical center so many guests seem to be there for treatment or medical appointments. I was in the area for work and this was the most convenient hotel. The facility and rooms are dated apart from the sleep number bed which was very comfortable. If there were options, I'm not sure I'd choose this hotel. But the staff was very pleasant and helpful. I had forgotten a charger for my phone and a staff member offered to share his to help me out. The restaurant was closed while I was there but you could get food in the lounge.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Baltimore Inner Harbor
title: “The friendliest, most helpful staff”
text: This hotel is clean and the rooms are spacious. The breakfast is very good, and there are different selections on different days. The best things about it is the staff. Everyone is friendly and helpful, and they make sure that any issues you have are addressed. It is an easy walk to the harbor, the convention center or Camden Yards.

name: Brookshire Suites
title: “Small, quaint and very nice.”
text: Excellent location, good value. Room size is fine, but very small bathrooms. Ian was very helpful at the front desk.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Baltimore Downtown / Inner Harbor
title: “Baltimore stay in Inner Harbor”
text: Clean, friendly and very convenient to Inner Harbor attractions.

name: Sheraton Baltimore City Center Hotel
title: “Excellent Customer Service”
text: The entire staff was friendy and helpful. Dhafi and the other valet team members were awesome getting me in and out. The Club Lounge is wonderful and Larhonda Wilson makes you feel like you are at home. She always went out of her way to make sure I had everything I wanted and could ever ask for! Overall, A+++!!!

name: Renaissance Baltimore Harborplace Hotel
title: “Fit for Everyone”
text: My wife and I were concerned when we checked in for a Saturday night stay. We came to Baltimore to have dinner with friends and enjoy the Baltimore Harbor. But when we entered the hotel, we saw that it was the headquarters for a bunch of athletic teams in town for a softball tournament. They tend to be late-night, room-hopping party animals. Then too, we saw by signs in the lobby that the hotel was hosting the graduation party for one of the city's high schools. Oh boy. I told my wife we might end up driving home to get some sleep that night. But I expressed my concerns to the lady behind the counter and she said "not to worry." We ended up with a beautiful room (I had a low, pre-paid rate that didn't promise me anything but a bed to sleep on) on a quiet floor and with the exception of all the excitement in the lobby, we would have thought we had the hotel to ourselves.

name: Hilton Baltimore
title: “Great service”
text:
We recently stayed at this hotel the night before a very special occasion (I had my US citizenship ceremony next morning). The front office manager had found out about it (I suspect my friend called ahead), so we had a bottle of wine and chocolates in the room when we arrived, and the greatest view of the Inner Harbor. We frequently stay at Hilton hotels, but this time we couldn't have wished for a better night. The staff was very friendly, including the lobby bar and restaurant. All areas are very clean and I'd go back there just to work out at the hotel gym again - one can't get a better view than this, overlooking the Orioles baseball stadium. 
Special thanks to FO manager John Gilligan!

name: Hilton Baltimore
title: “A great place to stay.”
text:
I have been a regular business guest at the Hilton Baltimore for one year now and highly recommend it. The lobby is inviting, clean and spacious. Many guests gravitate 
to the lobby and enjoy the comfort of the sofas while enjoying a drink and surfing the net. The rooms are very clean, always with new linen, bright, reasonably spacious and have flat screen TVs. Ask front desk for a ball park view and if they can they will help!
The restaurant menu is unfortunately limited in choices, however the half chicken or Flat Iron Steak or eggs Benedict with crab cakes are my favorites.
The majority of the staff treated me very, very well and management was always there to ensure things ran smoothly.
If you have free time ask the concierge for information about the Circulator Bus. The Orange Stop is right in front of the Hotel Lobby.
Albert.

name: Radisson Plaza Lord Baltimore
title: “Cheap hotel, inconvenient parking”
text:
Good:
- Free internet is great, could even stream videos
- Staff is very friendly and supportive
- Room is big, nice and clean
- Sleep number bed is a nice toy, but it's not very comfy
Bad:
- When i just came to the hotel - I could not find a place to leave the car and go to the reception - there is a tiny spot that is always taken by some other clients.
- To get to the parking - you need to make a big circle (a guy at the front door said "Baltimore is a one-way city").
- Parking is $15 and across the street - not very convenient, valet parking is $30
- Saw a big rat right at the parking garage
- When I came to my room - it was freesing - heating was broken. They fixed it in 10 minutes after I talked to the guy on reception though
- Phone buttons were not working
- TV in the room is very old and not working well
- Do not go on the streets in the night time - it's kinds scary out there

name: Holiday Inn Express Baltimore-Downtown
title: “Loved this place!”
text: We had never been to Baltimore before and were to meet friends there for a long weekend. We had no idea where to begin for a hotel search. They were there on business so their room was already booked. We couldn't afford to stay where they were so I went to hotwire. We were set up at the Holiday Inn Express on North Gay St which is only a few blocks from the Inner Harbor area. We were close enough to walk to the Inner Harbor area within 10 minutes but far enough away to get away from the city distractions. This building is an old bank converted to a hotel. It is a lovely hotel with the original mail chutes still there. The main check-in desk, lobby area, lounge area, breakfast area are all in the huge downstairs with high ceilings and large pillars. Very attractively decorated. The continental breakfast area is spacious enough that you don't have to "wait in line" for anything. There is lots of seating areas from small tables to lounge type chairs. Our room was a corner room with windows facing 2 different streets. There were many windows that were quite large and gave us a beautiful view of the city from a couple of different angles. The room was perfect with the standard 2 beds, 2 easy chairs, table, large screen TV. It was much more spacious than most hotels we've stayed in. The bathroom had a large sinktop area with lots of room to put everything. All of the furniture was a dark cherry finish. There was also a small refrigerator and microwave between the bathroom and sleeping area. The ice machines were stationed at convenient locations on each floor. We didn't have to go up or down stairs to get ice like some other places. The hotel staff that we interacted with was all friendly, courteous, and knowledgeable about the area. This hotel also has its own parking lot and you get a pass to park free when you pay for your room. Our friends were staying in a hotel that was much more expensive but we all agreed that our room was much nicer than theirs. I would definately recommend this hotel to anyone and I would not hesitate to stay here again.

name: Renaissance Baltimore Harborplace Hotel
title: “Thieves in this hotel- Do not stay here!”
text: I stayed in this hotel for a regional meeting with my company. Upon returning to my room in the evening, all but a few items had been stolen from my room. I called security and they promised me that they will do a full investigation and get to the bottom of who entered my room and who stole my stuff. Well, Here we are a week later and the claims adjustor from Marriott/Renaissance just called me and said that they have no proof that their employees stole my items and the state statute says they have no liability for my items. She even had the gall to tell me that I should have put my items in the hotel safe. They stole my car keys, house keys, ID, credit cards backpack and clothes. Based on the morons that ran security at this hotel, its clearly an inside job. they have no surveillance cameras except in the common areas and the hotel is connected to a mall where anyone can wander in from. Stay away from this hotel. Criminals are in cahoots with the employees there and neither you or your stuff is safe in this hotel.

name: Holiday Inn Express Baltimore at the Stadiums
title: “Great if you are going to the Ravens game.”
text: This hotel was perfect for going to the game. Check in was a breeze, the room clean and comfy. You can walk to the game or the festivities at the game. After the game walk back to the hotel have a rest and head out on the shuttle to the inner harbour for dinner. Lots of restaurants and shops. Only problem was breakfast isn't until 730 and no early togo bags for those with early flights home.

name: Brookshire Suites
title: “Wouldn't stay anywhere else”
text: Beautiful clean room, excellent staff who go above and beyond. Full Breakfast and a happy hour you won't find anywhere else. Very satisfied and would highly recommend!!!

name: Hyatt Regency Baltimore
title: “Don't listen to those old bad review-its great!”
text: I don't know what was going on in 2006 but most of the bad reviews are really old. We stayed at the club level and it was really pretty quite great. The club room was open every time I tried to go in, even 630am breakfast (smoked salmon, fresh berries and fruits and cheeses, quite the spread). The room was roomy and clean, and the bathroom isn't the typical closet. The location was great-right across the street from the inner harbour with lots of shopping and eats. The staff was great and when I had a broken hair dryer they had a new one to me quick-at 6am. Overall a great experience-and i travel a LOT

name: Brookshire Suites
title: “Great location in great city.”
text: Enjoyed the location more than anything, but the rooms were very, very quiet. Beds were great. Slept well.

name: Hyatt Regency Baltimore
title: “Nice and modern Hyatt on the Inner Harbor”
text:
I really enjoyed my stay at the Hyatt Regency in Baltimore. I booked through hotwire and got a great deal. The hotel was in an excellent (albeit touristy) location on the inner-harbor and was definitely a great deal considering how little we paid through hotwire.
Compliments:
- The lobby, elevators, and overall hotel amenities: modern, clean, very spacious (loved the views from elevator!)
- My room was very nice and modern with gorgeous views of harbor
- The hotel bar (bistro 335 I think) was great with decent (and not too pricey) wine selection
- Starbucks on second floor – very much appreciated!
- The front desk, housekeeping, and concierge were excellent on Friday and Saturday night: super-accommodating, friendly, helpful, etc.
- The location: one of the only hotels actually on the inner-harbor and also really convenient to everything central in Baltimore
Complaints:
- The bed: teeeeny pillows, and no inner sheet, just a tucked in (tiny!) sheet covering mattress, which would not stay on! waking up on a hotel mattress is not pleasant.
- The front desk, housekeeping, and concierge on Sunday night were awful! (Didn’t clean room until asked twice; concierge had no recommendations for a nice Italian restaurant (weird); front desk seemed to be always vacant, ...) It seemed like the great staff went home Sunday night and a terrible staff filled-in! I understand Sunday is a less busy night but we are paying the same rate so I expect the same service....
- Internet and parking were really pricey... although somewhat expected from big, corporate hotel in decent sized city
Anyway, overall I would recommend this hotel if you are looking to stay at a modern, big hotel on the inner harbor. I'd consider staying there again if I was in Baltimore.

name: Hyatt Regency Baltimore
title: “The 2007 renovation didn't last long . . .”
text: A tired, worn-out convention hotel that has seen better days. Even a stay on the Club floor was disappointing. The rooms are cramped, the hallways noisy, and the service is almost non-existent. Almost 5 hours to get the room made up (5 hours after a call requesting the service, that is); a Club room that ran out of amenites every day of our stay, and was often not re-stocked; and generally unengaged staff for whatever else one might need. The 2007 renovation changed the colors and the carpets, perhaps, but this aging hotel needed a good deal more to be competitive in the Inner Harbor market.

name: Hilton Baltimore
title: “Great place to stay - did not disappoint.”
text: Stayed here for 4 nights for a work trip. Room was nice, clean. Deck beside workout area with view of stadium & Orioles game was nice for entertaining clients who were baseball fans. 18th fl lounge was well stocked each morning with a nice variety of fruit, pastries and beverages. The bar area was pleasant (though slightly lacking in beer selection).

name: Admiral Fell Inn
title: “Hotel is run by a bunch of cheats!”
text:
The hotel tried to charge me a 9.95/day destination fee when I checked in. I explained that since I used priceline, my reservation was paid in full. After a 45 minute argument, they clerk informed me that he would waive the fee for me as a 1 time courtesy. 
2 weeks later I see the fee show up on my credit card statement!! Calling the hotel resulted in claims that they'd never waive the fee and I must be lying. I'm filing a dispute with my credit card company.
This hotel matched a 3 star bid on priceline in the fells point area. I strongly recommend that you do not use priceline in this area as you may get this hotel, and who knows what they'll try and tack on your bill!

name: Sheraton Baltimore City Center Hotel
title: “Great stay!”
text: Got a great deal on priceline for 2 night stay on St Patrick's Day weekend. My wife's sister from Brazil was visiting with us for the month and we decided to go to Baltimore for a fun weekend out. The staff members were very friendly and helpful. When we checked in, they had us set up for a King bed. As tempting as that was, I asked if they had a room available with 2 beds. The guy at the front desk (I forget his name, sorry) upgraded us to a corner deluxe room, which was very spacious with two beds and lots of windows. The only reason I didn't give this hotel 5 out of 5 is because of the steep parking fee ($22 a day), which is normal for downtown in any city, and also you could hear a lot of noise coming from the street at night. Not located in the nicest part of town either, but still close to the harbor and power plant live, which is what we came for. All things considered, it was a great stay and I would hope to get this hotel again if bidding the Baltimore Inner Harbor area.

name: Sheraton Inner Harbor Hotel
title: “Perfect Location”
text: I love the fact that this hotel is walking distance to the harbor where tons of restaurants and shopping is located. I went for a walk after work every night and always founf something to do. The bar at the hotel was just enought for nightcap. The entire staff at the hotel was very friendly and tries to make you feel at home. The fitness room has new machines and it also has a seperate weight training room. Parking garage is great and easy to find spots, I parked right by the entrance every night I was there(4 nights).

name: Holiday Inn Inner Harbor
title: “Wonderful Staff”
text: Stayed at this hotel with my family to see the Orioles Game. Great location! Walking distance to everything that you would need. Only a couple blocks from Camden Yards and about a 10 min walk to Inner Harbor. The rooms were very clean and the staff was excellent. I will definitely stay at this hotel again!

name: Hilton Garden Inn Baltimore Inner Harbor
title: “Nice HGI with a great location”
text: Rooms here are fairly standard HGI rooms and the Internet access is pretty good. The location is really nice for Inner harbor access, with lots of good restaurants in the immediate area. The work-out facility is first rate, since the HGI has worked a deal with the gym next door, guests have free access to a full service gym with very easy access. The breakfast buffet was the standard HGI setup. Parking is a bit problematic. I used the valet parking, which was adequate.

name: Admiral Fell Inn
title: “horrible”
text:
If you stay here you will be treated like DIRT from the desk clerks, you will get double billed on your credit card, and this hotel will charge an extra $9.95 as a destination fee which is not tax and is probably illegal. 
NEVER AGAIN.

name: Holiday Inn Inner Harbor
title: “Not for long stays...”
text: This hotel is a great location from the Inner Harbor, but for $250/night it was very over priced for the riom accomendtions. I stayed here for 2wks for work and the room was a standard room u would get from a $99/night hotel. Every other day my room key got deactivated and there is only one laundry room on the 3rd floor, out of 11 floors. Which includes 2 washers and 2 dryers (and not even the new nice ones). Service was always with a smile, but if you have time to search for a better hotel, I suggest u do that. And search out prior reviews this is DEFINITELY not a 5-star hotel!!

name: Radisson Plaza Lord Baltimore
title: “Absolutely Wonderful!”
text: Upon entering the hotel the first thing you notice is the luxurious decor and inviting lobby. Just beyond the lobby is a rather small but very quaint bar area, perfect for a nightcap or a quiet game of cards. When we got to our room we were very impressed with the linens and the overall upkeep of the room. It was gorgeous to say the least, with a nice view of the courtyard across the street. An added bonus was the Sleep Number bed that was in our room, although my husband loved it, I couldn't seem to find "my number". The hotel is a short walk to Inner Harbor and there is a very convienient walkway (Charles St. Skywalk) that leads there if you choose not to dodge traffic. The restaurant at the hotel is also spectacular, the Short Ribs are out of this world! The only downside to staying in this hotel is the parking (they charge twenty-five dollars for valet) luckily we were able to find parking for six dollars a day just a few blocks away. Overall this hotel is definitely a great place to stay.

name: Sheraton Baltimore City Center Hotel
title: “Great for leisure travel!”
text: I stayed here as a side trip to a college reunion in Annapolis. My fiancee has never been to Baltimore, so we took advantage of this hotel's excellent location to see Baltimore. It is a block away from a public-transit hub, including the light-rail line to BWI and various bus lines to major attractions not already within walking distance (e.g. Fell's Point). Found this hotel on Hotwire & got a great rate. Service was prompt and friendly. Can't beat the free Internet. Only downside is that its restaurant is overpriced for breakfast

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Hotel & Conference Center
title: “Clean & Comfortable”
text: I am skeptical of any hotel in the Baltimore area, but this one was clean and very comfortable. The bed spreads could use updating and the front desk staff was not particularly nice, but I did not have to interact with them much. The breakfast was decent, not the best I've had. On weekdays there was an omelet station, which was a nice treat. The hotel looked big, but felt small. I would stay here again when visiting Baltimore. You definitely need a car to visit any attractions.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Hotel & Conference Center
title: “A lot of bang for cheap price.”
text: I stayed here for a night with couples. We went to the inner harbor and came back to just sleep. Beds were comfty, clean, and quiet. I have to say the man up front Kal was so helpful with every request I had. If you need to get things done ask for him! He made personal calls all night for my late transportation needs! Complimentary breakfast was good for being free. The Waffle machine was a hit =)

name: Radisson Plaza Lord Baltimore
title: “Decent Downtown Hotel Made Better by Comparison”
text:
I stayed at the "Lord Baltimore" for six nights last week. As I checked into the hotel and first occupied my room, I was thinking I'd be giving the hotel an average rating, but during the stay I became more impressed. First off, if you've stayed at a Radisson in San Diego or Boston (any major tourist destination), there are newer, nicer Radissons out there. Having said that, in comparison the the other hotels right downtown, like the Wyndham directly across the street, the Radisson is nicer. 
I booked my reservation online and went with the "Plaza Club" special. This included private access to the club level (club level floors require special key access), as well as a continental breakfast (nothing remarkable), and "happy hour" from 6-7:30p. This cocktail hour, which was included in the special was actually nice, because hors d'oeuvres were offered, as were complimentary beer and wine (and there were no enforced limits on the drinks). While I was there, the cocktail hour-and-a-half was popular, and usually attended by about 6-15 guests, also there for some conference. The room I stayed in included a "comfort select" bed, which might explain the complaint someone made a couple reviews back. Although I didn't care for the feature, you could adjust the bed's firmness using an attached remote. Since the bed included dual zones, I can imagine a "hump" could be created by setting one side soft and the other hard. Otherwise the room was adequate, I could adjust the heat to my liking, the linens were fresh, there were no offensive odors, and wireless internet was complimentary on the "club level". The hotel still displayed some signs of design eras gone by though (probably from before it was a Radisson), like the huge setee in the lobby, but again, even with some 70's kitsch, this was still better. For example, some peers staying at the Wyndham across the street complained about long elevator waits (I think there were only two or three; Radisson has 5), they ran out of TP at one point! (they were comp'd with drinks), and no wireless internet access in the rooms. I found the Radisson staff to be generally nice and helpful. For the coffee drinkers there's a Starbucks in the lower level, and the Lord Baltimore Grill was fair to middlin' full service restaurant with dialy buffet that also provides room service. I got a really good burger with curly fries there for lunch one day, but didn't like the french onion or crab soups. In the end, a generally decent hotel, made even better by comparison.

name: Four Points by Sheraton BWI Airport
title: “Excellent Hotel Experience!”
text: This place was great, the service was outstanding. I have stayed at dozens of hotels over the past 20+ years and this place had the best service I have ever experienced. We went to the area to visit DC and Baltimore for the first time, and this was the right place to stay. Although the highway system is a little confusing, it's easy to find by following the BWI signs. The shuttle was prompt and took us to the airport train station where we were able to ride the MARC train into the centrally located DC Union Station. Because it's on TSA property, the hotel area feels alot safer than most DC area hotels, and safety was a primary concern. When I checked in, I was assigned the wrong room, which was too small for my family. When I inquired about it, the front desk upgraded us to a larger room without question. Beware that for some rooms, the airplanes take off just a few hundred yards outside the window. We stayed in one of those rooms but it's really not that loud (my kids and I thought it was cool). We didn't try the restaurant (expensive high end food), and there are no restaurants withing walking distance, but the front desk has printed directions for other restaurants. Free parking very close to the hotel entrance. We will definately stay there again next time we visit the DC/Baltimore area. We found a gem.

name: Sheraton Inner Harbor Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text: Service was great throughout the hotel. There were smiling faces at the front desk, in the restaurant, and in the guest hallways and public areas. The room was very clean and comfortable. The Sheraton bed is the most comfortable of all hotel brand bedding. The location is perfect for business or pleasure with the Inner Harbor in walking distance. Any restaurant of choice is available in the Harbor. The stadiums for both football and baseball are seen from the guestroom windows.

name: Sheraton Baltimore City Center Hotel
title: “OK hotel in downtown Baltimore”
text:
The Sheraton City Center is just an average hotel in downtown Baltimore with two separate towers (north and south). There are numerous nearby high rises that tend to block any sort of view (Inner Harbor, etc.), including the Raddison that is right across the street (and connected by a ramp above street level).
Our room on the 18th floor was a corner unit with a king bed. The duvet was crazy heavy, to the point that it was dragged off the bed by it's own weight during the night. A small but clean bathroom, a desk with an office chair, a flat-screen TV, mini-fridge with nothing in it, an awkwardly placed closet, and a comfortable bed completed the room, but no extra pillows or a blanket (to use instead of the duvet).
When I was there the hotel was experiencing a "internet is down" situation that made it impossible to access the web from the computers in the Business Center. After trying several times to access the internet in order to print out boarding passes for the next days flight, I made my way to the front desk, who then told me about the (apparent) hotel-wide internet blackout. Once I explained what I wanted to do, they directed me to the Concierge computer and let me use that. While it took a while to get the printing done (wait in line again, then tell front desk folks that the printing wasn't working, then have them futz around and confer with each other), the staff did make it happen. Eventually.
Bottom line is that this is a reasonable choice in a reasonably convenient hotel, if you find a rate that is to your liking.

name: Four Points by Sheraton BWI Airport
title: “Very comfortable”
text: At the last minute, I decided to stay here the night before my 6 am flight and to park my car here for the duration of my trip. Good decision! Though I had booked an ordinary king room, at checkin I was upgraded to a large, executive room. It was vast. There were two soft chairs, a sofa, and a desk the size of an aircraft carrier. The bed was reasonably comfy (thin pillows--you may have to pile them up), the bathroom was attractive and spotless, and the toiletries were good quality. Although the airport and parking garage are literally next door, noise was not a problem. The bad news was that I was only there to catch a few hours' sleep, so had no real chance to enjoy the big TV or sofa. Service was good; checkin was a little slow because there were several guests ahead of me, but the upgrade more than made up for that. Shuttle service both ways was flawless and courteous. I may be back if my plans call for an early-morning flight.

name: Admiral Fell Inn
title: “Romance at Home”
text:
I have lived in Baltimore all my life and did not know this wonderful place was here. I was given as an employee of Johns Hopkins and thought this would great for my anniversary. My husband and I had a very nice, intimate dinner. Our room was absolutely beautiful. The staff was friendly and very helpful.
We are going to make it a habit of going often.

name: Mount Vernon Hotel
title: “Nice Hotel - Go Tigers!”
text: After reading all the negatives reviews, I was expecting the worst! Hotel and staff was clean, friendly, helpful. Decent price for location. Used the light rail, two blocks down, to get to Camden Yards, $6.00 round trip. Couldn't get a cab.

name: Brookshire Suites
title: “A/C was broke everyday we stayed except the last. Check A/C before going!!!!”
text: My wife and I decided to stay here for our honeymoon. The service itself was great but the hotel could you some updates. First when we got there I knew there was going to be a problem because the room wasn't cold but and the air was on. It was blowing somewhat hot air. I thought it just needed some time but unfortunately it didn't work out that way. We stayed 3 nights 4 days. (M thru Th) and every night it was 85 to 90 in our room except for real late the 3rd night and we didn't care because we were leaving the next day. On tuesday the only thing they could do was give us a fan to push HOT air around THANKS FOR NOTHING. I was really looking forward to the hotel but this put a damper on our honeymoon. They did not bother to reduce our rate which I felt was appropriate. I would not recommend this hotel unless they are little better with their service if something does break. I fully understand things break but they should have taken care of there customers better.

name: Pier 5 Hotel
title: “Rooms very overpriced, but great staff and wonderful breakfast buffet”
text:
I had first learned about this hotel from Groupon, but they had offered only a 2-night-stay (which we can never take), so I had to let that go. But when Sniqueaway came out with an offer to stay for one night, I grabbed it! 
The pictures online of the building looked great, directly at the waterfront in the inner harbour of Baltimore.
We arrove on a Wedneday afternoon and were greeted very nicely by Kyle (I believe) at the front desk. We checked in without any issues, were even handed a 25 $ voucher towards breakfast for the next morning! That had not been mentioned by Sniqueaway, so that was a nice surprise!
We had booked a room for 199 $ with a king bed and harbour view. Now we did have a view into the harbour - when we looked out to the right over the lower roofs beneath our 3rd floor window. And we had a king bed as announced.
But it was really only a very small standard room. The ceiling was constructed very interestingly (see pictures), it was going up high and looked very nice. But it only made the room bigger in an optical way, the ground size of the room stayed the same.
On the door I had seen the floor map of the whole floor, and there I saw that our room (305) was like a handtowel (a small rectangular), and nearby were much bigger rooms.
I would not say anything if we hadn't paid 199 $ for this. Usually I am paying less for a suite in a Kimpton hotel (by using deals)! And the 199 $ was a deal price by Sniqueaway! 
I looked up the rack rate online, and I saw the regular rate for our small room was 299 $ per night midweek. That is really too much!! And Hubby said he also found we have paid too much, even with that Snq coupon.
At least we got that 25 $ voucher for breakfast, and that was really really great! We had the choice between a continental buffet (all you can eat) for 11.99 $ per person and a warm breakfast (eggs etc) for about 15 $ per person. We were standing in front of the buffet and the decision was easy, as it looked really wonderful.
Pastries, breads, bagels, boiled eggs, fresh fruits and berries, joghurt, various juices, cereals, granola and much more that I am now forgetting. We really ate the money's worth to get ahead of the price, as we had paid too much for our small room. We were helped by Bill who was very friendly, just like all staff members we met. 
Kyle (front desk) had borrowed us an umbrella when we went out in the pouring rain for dinner the night before. Alexandra at the front desk helped me out with some key issues, and the maid gave me another bottle of (free) Voss water. 
The lobby was decorated very tastefully with beautiful furniture. I liked the open style, how you look down onto the lobby when you come out of your room. The architecture was really interesting in this building.
