But the bath room was unimpressive, I am afraid! Tub and shower combo, this American insult of a bathroom, I still can't believe this whenever I am seeing that. You can bathe 2 small children in that, but not an adult, and definitely not 2 adults.
But even worse was the toilet design! Not only was the toilet right there by that joke of a tub, it also had the paper roll BEHIND the toilet at the wall. So you had to get yourself some paper rolled down and ripped before you sat down! In my age (48) I don't always have that time anymore, so even when you rush to the toilet and make it in time, then your spouse has to come in and get you some toilet paper fom the roll behind you. Or you stand up and drip into your underwear while you turn around and roll down some paper. Not good either way!
The counter which held the ONE SINK was very big, and it could have easily held 2 sinks. I don't know why they did it like that, I thought that was wasted this way. There was also a hair dryer hanging in a bag from the bathroom door, also we had a safe in the closet plus a (tiny) robe (yes one robe, not two). 
We had free internet access, so we had brought our laptop along, which we have set up on the desk between the bed and the window. It worked fine. So I watched a german TV show online while Hubby watched some CCN news on the TV at the wall.
Another nice thing was that the window actually opened! After the terrible rain on Wednesday night we awoke to a blue sky next morning with warm temperatures. It was March 1st and it felt like May 1st! We opened the window and enjoyed the fresh air. Glad that we could shut off the climate machine, because that was very loud. But at least it worked.
I should also mention that they offer valet parking, but right before you get to the hotel you can self park in 2 various public places for $22 per 24 hours. I don't know what valet parking would have been, but I am sure it would have been more.
Hubby loved the alarm clock, it looked just like the one I had in the early 70s, but besides ringing it could also say "Good Morning" when you shut it off. He would have bought that right away if that had been offered! There was a second clock standing in the shelf across the room, I think it was also a CD player. We haven't touched it, as we stayed only for one night, but it is a nice thing to have.
I am sure this hotel has reallly nice rooms and suites, but considering our handtowel sized room was $ 299 ($199 with Snq), you can imagine you would pay the amount of your monthly mortgage payment for one night in a suite there. I have no idea why they believe these prices are adequate. I can get a Spa room or even a suite in a Kimpton hotel for less than this Pier 5 Hotel is asking for a very small standard room. 
Unless we can find an incredible deal for this hotel (and not just $100 off), we will stay at the Monaco (Kimpton) next time. I have actually already booked our 2 next Baltimore stays there.

name: Brookshire Suites
title: “The hotel Manager was Great”
text: The room were smaller than expected for the price but my family and I had an incident where our car was broken into while in the hotel's valet parking and the hotel manager Travis was great and I loved the way he handled the situation.

name: Brookshire Suites
title: “Cozy and comfortable with a warm, welcoming staff!”
text: Brookshire Suites is a smaller hotel with personal touches. You do not feel like a number when you enter the hotel lobby to check in. We were greeted warmly and told about the amenities offered. The beds were plush and very comfortable. We felt safe and relaxed. Our sons were there for hospital tests, so a shuttle service took them from the hotel directly to Johns Hopkins Hospital. The Cloud Room on the top floor had a wonderful breakfast, and there is coffee and tea available at all hours for guests. We plan to return to Baltimore and we will definitely stay here again!

name: Home2 Suites by Hilton Baltimore Downtown
title: “Home2Suites by Hilton.”
text: A great place to stay for business or pleasure. Stayed with family. A " flat hotel " as known in Europe. Friendly staff, valet parking ( perhaps pricey at $ 25 ). Breakfast bar, which forces us to get off bed as it closes at 09.00 am.

name: Sheraton Baltimore City Center Hotel
title: “NOT good enough”
text: Stayed here for a Yankee/Orioles game (one night). Got the room through Priceline.com for less than half of the hotel's price. Not worth the $ I spent at all! The room was small, the carpet was stained, there were stains on the bathroom wall and the glass shelves in the room were dusty and the bed squeeked. The TV stopped working at 2am and i had to mess with the plugs to get it to work again. The blue rugs heading to the South Tower elevators was musty. Perhaps the Priceline customers get the older, dirtier rooms? Once leaving the hotel walk with crowds..one wrong turn and there are dozens of beggars and "low brow" people. A bottle of soda in the shop in the lobby is $2.. At 2am, I had a blistering headache and no help from the hotel staff other than to send me to a 7-11 in the neighborhood- I stayed put. There was a nice view of the stadium but thats the only ammenity in this hotel,

name: Sheraton Baltimore City Center Hotel
title: “Caveat Emptor”
text: I picked this hotel from the available properties which we're offered up for a convention my wife and I we're attending in Baltimore. It was one of the more moderately priced options in the selection, so I decided to give it a try. Stayed there three nights and would not recommend this hotel to anyone. The location is ok with respect to access to the convention center and the inner harbor (if you don't mind the pan handlers), however, the hotel itself is old, rundown and in desperate need of a remodel. The hallways are dingy and dark, and the room didn't even have a lounge chair......either you sit at the desk or on the bed. As for the elevator, it was always crowded and utterly filthy, with no evidence of regular cleaning.......and this is significant because I had to use the elevator frequently to get my room key card reprogramed when it failed to work (and yes I kept it away from my cell phone and all magnetic devices). Lastly, there was the parking. The hotel lot was full, so I learned that I could either use the valet (@$35.00 a night) or park it in a nearby lot. Naturally, I chose the self park option ($ 19) and upon checkout , found that the hotel erroneously billed me for valet! I could go on, but what is the point?......caveat emptor.

name: Brookshire Suites
title: “The most rest I've had in along time.”
text: I loved the room. It was very spacious and clean. The bathroom was huge and clean. the beds were soft, but firm that gave us a goodnight sleep. I believe that this will be my first choice to stay when I come to the Baltimore area.

name: Sheraton Inner Harbor Hotel
title: “awsome hotel manager -kind, charitable ,concerned about the community”
text:
I had a concern for a family member who had to drive her gr-daughter to outpatient chemotherapy at a local hospital 4 days a week from the Eastern Shore,Maryland to Baltimore. An idea came to me to contact the Sheraton hotel Inner Harbor and ask if they were able to donate a few night stays for my cousin and her gr daughter during the time of the chemo sessions. I was pleased to get a positive response from the hotel manager and that he was able to help them. This helped me to regain faith in humanity and the corporate world.
Thank you again to that hotel manager at the Sheraton Inner Harbor. You know who you are.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Hotel & Conference Center
title: “Most friendly, hospitable and clean”
text:
Was a very rewarding experience to stay at the Best Western on
Mc'Donnell Street in Baltimore.
VERY clean, MOST hospitable and a great deal for the rate.Great
location right at the I-95 making accessibility to anwhere very easy.
Would HIGHLY recommend.

name: Royal Sonesta Harbor Court Baltimore
title: “A Work In-progress”
text: My wife and I stayed here for the Sailabration as the hotel is a short walk to Baltimore's Inner Harbor. This hotel was recently taken over by new owners and it is clear they have not gotten around to renovating the property yet. The old-style fake gold/brass look is everywhere and in need of replacing as its flaking or worn off in places. Our room had chipped and worn-out furniture, dirty air vents (see pictures), and pealing paint. One bright spot is the small restaurant, which served outstanding food with great service! We were there for a Sunday brunch and it was 4-stars. The lounge was also very nice although over-priced for drinks. My advice if you book here: make sure to ask if the room they are putting you in has been renovated yet. If not, book one of the many other fine inner harbor hotels.

name: Home2 Suites by Hilton Baltimore Downtown
title: “Worth a Try....”
text: My husband and I just spent three nights at this Hotel. Our purpose for visiting Baltimore was an appointment at Johns Hopkins Hospital. We found the hotel staff to be excellent at this location. Latika saved our butts from having to pay for 2 nights of parking. She is an excellent example of the staff at Home 2 Suites. Nick, the manager, is very hands on and totally credits his staff for their great ratings. We found the location to be perfect for us. Affordable, courteous staff in a great location. Out car wouldn't start when we were ready to leave, and we couldn't have gotten more help from the guys in valet parking..... They deserve a pat on the back for helping us out of a terrible situation. We would stay here again and highly suggest you give this hotel and it's "great" staff a chance. The rooms were nicely furnished and very cozy! The price, compared to the rest of Baltimore, was just right. Thank you all for a great stay! We also love that they are pet friendly, altough we didn't have a pet. This hotel is a little bit Boutique and a little bit Long-term Home. Excellent!

name: Hampton Inn Baltimore-Downtown-Convention Center
title: “Very CLEAN and CONVENIENT”
text:
We traveled to Baltimore for the Brooks Robinson statue dedication on September 29th 2012 and stayed the night at the Hampton Inn for another game on Sunday. I have traveled to many places and this is the cleanest hotel I have ever been to. The hotel was completely booked and we arrived right at check in. The valet guys were fantastic! Yes, paying to park is $29.00 which is a little steep, but these boys hustle and I was very impressed with them, leading me to tip 3 different times. Although the hotel was booked and check in time can be hectic, I only waited a few minutes. June, from the front desk seemed a little stressed at first but she loosened up a bit and was quite pleasant. She also called our room to see if we were happy with it. The condition of this room was amazing. I have been to many hotels and timeshares. THIS WAS THE CLEANEST ROOM I HAVE EVER STAYED IN!!! 
The walk to the park is one minute. If you are disabled, this is the perfect place to be. Three bars are connected to the hotel. So if you want to have a few beers and walk up to your room, it is perfect. On a side note: The staff and the people at the bars are a good crowd and quite friendly. You won't feel unsafe if you are a peaceful person. Being a police officer, I don't like to be in the wrong kind of crowd. I HIGHLY SUGGEST STAYING HERE!!! GO ORIOLES!!!!! WE MADE THE PLAYOFFS!!

name: Home2 Suites by Hilton Baltimore Downtown
title: “I loved my stay”
text: My girlfriend booked a room at this hotel and Unadus really helped us within the city and recommended a great diner

name: Home2 Suites by Hilton Baltimore Downtown
title: “Home2 Suites by Hilton® Baltimore Downtown”
text: Conveniently located in downtown Baltimore, the Home2 Suites by Hilton® Baltimore Downtown is nestled on a small, quiet street close to great local restaurants and bars. Near Mercy Hospital, Baltimore International Airport(BWI) and several major office buildings, Home2 Suites Baltimore Downtown is also close to museums and major attractions such as Inner Harbor, Maryland Science Center and the National Aquarium. Such a great price and includes breakfast. Linita and Lakia

name: The Back Bay Hotel
title: “Great hotel”
text:
My wife and I stayed 4 nights at the Jury's, everything was great. 
The service was exceptional (especially Heather the concierge, who advised us on the best places to go to). 
We had room 738 a corner room over looking the street, the room was very large for a city centre hotel. The room was very clean and the bed was one of the most comfortable that we have ever slept in.
I would recommend this hotel to everyone wanting to visit Boston.
If you get a chance go to Grill 23 across the road from the hotel, best steaks you will ever have.

name: Henderson's Wharf Inn
title: “Recent Stay”
text: We just got back from an overnight getaway to Baltimore and the Henderson's Wharf. This was our first stay at the inn and everything was perfect. The front desk staff was excellent. We had a harbor view room which was just that, you could not get a better view. The bed was comfy and the room was very nicely decorated. Parking was in a safe gated lot located next to the inn. We will be back.

name: Renaissance Baltimore Harborplace Hotel
title: “Not too impressed”
text:
Fabulous hotel interior however came short for its guestrooms... unless you stayed in the presidential suite, I suppose. The price I paid for that room could have gotten me a suite at another Marriott location. 
But I do recomment its Window restaurant where the breakfast was satisfying.

name: Brookshire Suites
title: “Incredible Hotel!”
text: We were pleasantly surprised at the accomodations we experienced at the Brookshire Suites. The staff is exceptional, very attentive. The rooms were immaculate and very large! We had a fantastic view of the harbor from our room. Very centrally located to all activities. Parking seemed a little high ($33) but all in all, we would DEFINETELY stay here again.

name: Hampton Inn Baltimore-Downtown-Convention Center
title: “Friendly and Convenient!”
text: I recently stayed at the Hampton while in town for a national competition with students. It is directly across the street from Camden Yards! Even though we were there for competition, the crowds were really mellow, even after winning the game. The fireworks woke me up one night, but were over quickly. There are many attractions within walking distance and lots of choices for dining - from the hot dogs on the street to more expensive steaks and seafood. Everyone was so friendly. They even allowed our group to check out in the morning, compete all day, and come back to get our luggage from storage that night. I would definitely stay there again, and the next time, I hope I actually get to see a game!

name: Baltimore Marriott Waterfront
title: “Excellent location, prime views”
text: Stayed here twice over the last month and this is an excellent choice for Baltimore Inner Harbor. The harbor views are stunning, especially from the higher floors. In addition the hotel is in great shape; they are well staffed and very attentive...rooms are standard for a higher end Marriott, but view and location make it a winner. Easy access to everything in Inner Harbor and Little Italy is within walking distance as well.

name: Pier 5 Hotel
title: “Spectacular view, but not much else....”
text:
After years of visiting the Baltimore Inner Harbor, my girlfriend and I decided that we needed to make the Pier 5 Hotel our next weekend getaway. We booked a 3 night stay October 8th - 11th. Arrived Friday early evening and were greeted by a cheerful front-end staff, and a happy hour that helped put us in a great mood for the weekend. Our room #204 was a corner suite, with a fantastic view of the harbor. 
Unfortunately, that's about all the positive to report. Our suite was in desperate need of renovation. The bathroom has less than adequate lighting, and the height of the countertop makes one feel as though you were a professional basketball player (I am just under 6 feet tall). 
The first evening uncovered a mattress that has seen better days, and an in-wall air conditioning unit that woke us each time it came on throughout the evening. The fact that the AC unit is 3 feet from the bed obviously did not help matters. 
Breakfast at Pizzazz in the lobby gets a thumbs down. The restaurant lacks organization. Upon seating, we noticed that our tablecloth was dirty. We give credit to the waiter for sensing our displeasure and immediately moving us to another table. Unfortunately, the second was as dirty as the first. Eggs came out of the kitchen, but toaster was on the buffet counter. Coffee urn was empty when we were seated, and took forever to refill (No, it was not crowded). You leave this restaurant feeling awfully confused. 
If you choose to eat lunch or dinner at one of the restaurants located off the lobby of the hotel, I strongly urge that you confirm your reservation with the restaurant directly. It would be prudent for a hotel to advise their guests if a restaurant will be closed for a private function, which neither the hotel nor the restaurant felt was important when they closed at 4pm Sunday for a wedding reception.
Telephone service is horrendous. You have no choice but to dial 0 from your room for any needs. The inadequacy of this phone system was never more apparent than Monday at checkout. We tried for 15 minutes to call for a bellhop. Phone rang, no one answered. Finally we carried 6 bags out to the valet without any assistance from an employee. 
Save your money. This location leaves a lot to be desired.

name: Royal Sonesta Harbor Court Baltimore
title: “Grand Hotel”
text: Just stayed at the InterContinental for the first time. It is a magnificent hotel. From check in to check out everything was fabulous. The staff is truly dedicated to the comfort and pleasure of its guests. This hotel is a true jewel on the Baltimore harbor.

name: Hilton Baltimore
title: “Good Beginning”
text:
New hotel just opened last week. They were still experiencing some of the glitches involved in opening a new hotel, hence the 4 rating instead of 5 but overall a good experience. A few nice touches:
1) Some of the rooms overlook Camden Park. You can actually see the interior of the Stadium from your room and with binoculars you might be able to watch the game.
2) The interior of the rooms have a new style desk with a "sub" computer desk underneath, to allow easier use of your laptop. I also enjoyed the interior room furnishing which were comfy.
3) The new flat screen TVs offer a wonderful selection of entertainment - more than movies and the usual TV selections.
4) The fitness center is wonderful for on the road fitness. 10 Treadmills, 7 Ellipticals, 3 Bikes, weights and 7 or 8 other pieces of equipment - all to be used while overlooking an enviable great view right into Camden Park and home plate! The center also includes a full sauna, full swimming pool and jacuzzi and an outdoor patio (which also overlooks Camden Park). Tip: Make sure you bring your earplugs to plug into the entertainment center equipment.
The staff clearly is well trained and they are working hard to show it! 
It is a new downtown hotel so expect to pay for parking and the newness of the hotel and it's amenities - but a good start for a convention hotel.

name: Memphis Marriott Downtown
title: “Rooms average/location average”
text:
I stayed here for a conference in January. The rooms were allright--one of those places where at first glance, it looks really nice, but then when you look closer, you realize the curtains are dirty, the lampshade is ripped, the toilet makes weird noises, and there's hair on the bathroom floor.
The hotel itself isn't around a lot in terms of walking distance. During a weekday evening, all the restaurants nearby are closed, so you'll have to take a trolley to get somewhere. However, the trolley is very nice and convenient. It's $1 each way and stops right outside the hotel. It will take you to Beale street, about a 7 minute ride. You can buy passes for the trolley in the gift shop of the hotel.
If you are coming for a conference, look out. The place is absolutel confusing. At one point, I missed a symposium b/c I just couldn't find it. You had to go up several escalators down a few more and around and around to go from one room to the next. It took us so long to find the registration that we gave up at one point. Everyone was wondering around like "do you know how to get to...." Very confusing.
There are a few shuttles that will take you places from the hotel.I did a trip to graceland. With the shuttle and admittance to graceland, it was $30. We upgraded and did the extra plane and cars museum for another $10. They also have ashuttle that will take you to a casino which is about a half hour away.
There is no wireless in the rooms. They have a cord you can use to plug your laptop in. It costs $10 a day and goes from noon to noon. Watch out--they charged me for two days when I only used it for one.
There is also a business center, which is just two computers and a hookup where you can use on or two laptops for free. Of couse, it was always taken so don't plan on getting online much here.
Overall, it was an okay stay. For the price, I would have expected a litle bit more

name: The Back Bay Hotel
title: “A home from home in Back Bay.”
text:
My wife and I stayed at Jurys from July 1st through July 8th.
The whole experience was excellent.
Everybody at the hotel from doorman - front desk - concierges - cleaning staff were marvellous and couldnt have done more to ensure our stay was absolutely spot on.
The hotel is ideally placed a short walk away from most things you want to see. Anything you are not sure about - then have a chat with any of the concierges - nothing seems too much trouble.
Our room - a corner king executive - was large, bright and airy.
Beds were very comfortable - and each night - as one would expect in a hotel of this standard - the sheets were turned down and the obligatory chocolates left on the pillow - still a nice touch though.
I hired the coffee maker for the week and I am glad i did. Each day the tray was replenished witha selection of coffees and tea, and fresh milk and cream left in the fridge together with water bottles. I would recommend that anyone staying here hire the coffee makers - its $27 dollars for the week or £14 .
I dont see what the fuss about hiring them is - I have never stayed anywhere in America except smaller backwood places where there has been any kind of brewing facility in the room , and certainly never seen one in any city hotels.
We had the feeling whilst we were there that everyone genuinely wanted us to be there and we were made very welcome . We will certainly go back should we ever return to Boston . For me its a no brainer to stay anywhere else.
This is a very good hotel with a laid back cosy atmosphere - not like many hotels of this standard which can be a bit stuffy and staid.
Places we ate at and thought OK
Joes - Hamburgers and american fare
Laurel Grill - next to hotel - good food and very reasonable
California Pizza - OK for quick meals
Changs Chinese Bistro - reasonable standards , good value.
Rock Bottom Beer Company - American - OK - cheap !
Maggianos Little Italy - Excellent - cheap !
All the above are in easy walking distance of the hotel and whilst they are probably not in the good food guide to Boston a la this forum - they will stand muster with most eating establishments for good reasonably priced meals - buts its all a matter of choice and opinion. All I can say is we found them OK.
Things I can recommend to do
Duck Tour
Sky Walk
Whale Watch
Harbour Tour
Charlestown and Bunker Hill
Things i wouldnt recommend
Wrentham Village
Cape Cod Excursion - Gray line
Spirit Cruise.
All in all a wonderful stay in a wonderful hotel in a wonderful city
Pity about British Airways - but thats another story.

name: Sheraton Inner Harbor Hotel
title: “Hoodwinked at the Sheraton Inner Habor Hotel”
text:
My husband and I were looking for a quick getaway, when we made the reservations we requested a room with a Harbor View. We were assured we had a Harbor View room when we confirmed our reservation the day before we checked in. Upon arrival we waited on a long line to check in and once we were finally at the desk we noticed problem # 1, the clerk at the desk was very dry, he seemed half dead. We told him we rec'd a ticket to park in the hotel garage, he advised us parking will be $20 per day whether we move the car or not, problem # 2. This was rather upsetting since we were already spending over $500 for a 2 night stay. 
We get to our room pull back the curtain, and proceeded to climb over the chair and table w/lamp to get a distorted view of the Inner Harbor. Please note we had an awesome view of the Hyatt's pool and tennis court, meanwhile we paid for a harbor view. We went back downstairs to speak to the clerk that checked us in to request our room to be changed. He told us they were booked and for us to call the front desk in the morning to see if "a better room" becomes available. My husband told him we paid for a harbor view and wanted to speak with the manager. The manager promptly addressed us and took us to see a room that had a "better view of the harbor" but the room had a queen size fold out bed that was very low to the ground, that would have been perfect for a teenager. We expressed to her how displeased we were and although she was nice and apologized she didn't offer to take anything off of the bill. 
We left the Sheraton and walked across the street to the Hyatt to check availability, since it was the July 4th holiday weekend they were completely booked. Upon returning to the Sheraton we noticed the night shift had just clocked in so we went back to the front desk and expressed how unhappy we were and how we were assured we would receive a harbor view room when we made the reservations and confirmed and paid extra $$ for it but instead we paid extra money to see the Hyatt's pool and tennis court. The clerk was very understanding and gave us a credit of almost $50, which just about covered parking. 
If your looking for a CLEAN hotel with a LOVELY view of the Hyatt this is definitely the place to stay !!

name: Pier 5 Hotel
title: “Great location and so pet friendly!!”
text: Thank you Pier Five....great location on the water and great staff. From the wonderful valet team to the front desk team, we all enjoyed our stay!!! Jill and Empress were fun to talk with. They offered ideas for city visiting. The entire staff treated our pup so special! We had a standard room and were very happy. It faced the street but was very quiet. The room was a great size and we had no complaints at all. We LOVED the receptions offered by Admiral Fells and Pier 5. Pier 5 had "crabby night" on Friday. We could bring the pup and enjoy crab roll ups and drinks. The Fells property had a reception with cheese and drinks and then a ghost tour through the property provided by Allison....very good and she was very informative. Can't wait to go back in the fall...Thank you all for making our pups first "vacation" so special!!!

name: Pier 5 Hotel
title: “Great location does not make up for poor quality of room."”
text:
We had high expectations, but were very disappointed with the condition of the room. It turns out that a “standard” room does not include an arm chair and coffee table, just a big empty space where they would have been located. The worst part was a very loud A/C that kept cycling on/off—it did not have a “fan-on” setting with the A/C (i.e., fan on, but A/C off)—which made sleep impossible. Other problems: wobbly desk chair, ripped curtain, squeaky bathroom door, no cuts, and clogged bathtub. Cheap motels have better rooms. Without a harbor view, you should save your money and go elsewhere.
Good points: location (but can be noisy with concert shell and Inner Harbor noise), free Wi-Fi, and they nicely agreed to cancel & refund my second night.

name: Sheraton Inner Harbor Hotel
title: “Mediocre charm in Charm City”
text:
Problems: 1. It took 20 minutes to check in, with a trainee who hadn't been trained to apologize for the delay.
2. One lamp in the room did not work.
3. The coffee maker was not placed near an outlet, so it had to be moved.
4. What's with hotels taking out the sodas/liquor in the in-room refrigerators these days? 
5. This almost had me move out. There was a USED, still slightly-damp, face cloth hanging over the shower curtain. Admittedly, I'm not the greatest housekeeper, but this was below even my standards.
6. $15 cash to park for the baseball game, but $18 to park overnight.
Good stuff: 1. Great view of the harbor.
2. Lots of pillows on a very comfortable bed.
3. Price was okay (on line deal). At least it's close to the Inner Harbor and the stadiums.

name: Baltimore Marriott Waterfront
title: “Nice View and Rooms”
text: I went for a bachelorette weekend to Baltmore and stayed here. The view was nice and the rooms were well appointed. Very comfortable beds and sheets. It was a little on the pricer side but you get what you pay for and I would stay here again if i'm ever in the Baltimore. Also not too far of a walk to very good restaurants and bars.

name: Baltimore Marriott Waterfront
title: “Amazing Views”
text: Welcomed by valets and always had a bottle of water for us when we went out. Within walking distance to anything in the Inner Harbor and that is why we stayed. Booked deluxe oversized room with exclusive views...and it was both. Amazing Corner suite with views looking out of inner harbour and down to the inner harbour itself, large hallway talking you to washroom and large sitting area and then to the area with the bed. Ate dinner and breakfast downstairs, the bar for dinner and restaurant for breakfast. Busy bar service was still great and the food was good as well. Same for the breakfast, large serving as well.

name: Sleep Inn & Suites Downtown Inner Harbor
title: “Awesome Hotel - Clean and Great Service”
text: I stayed at the Downtown Inner Harbor hotel prior to going on a cruise. The manager Abraham was most accomodating to help us make our cruise transfers to and from the port. The rooms were very clean and comfortable. It is within walking distance to the Inner Harbor area. I strongley recommend the hotel for any stay in Baltimore Md. Make sure you use the stay and ride program for any cruise holiday, it will save you money!!!!

name: Baltimore Marriott Waterfront
title: “Beautiful hotel, beautiful harbor view, excellent service”
text: The hotel and staff are excellent! The property is located near the National Aquarium, the historic power plant building, and the Baltimore World Trade Center. It is at the opposite end of the inner harbor from Camden Yards and M&T Bank Stadium. All of the attractions of the inner harbor are within walking distance, young children may get a little tired if the walk is to a ballgame. The hotel property is relatively new and very clean, the rooms have adequate space, are well-appointed and very comfortable. The harbor view is beautiful, the best views are from the higher rooms. Our only sampling of the restaurant was the breakfast buffet and it was well done. The common areas have high ceilings, marble floors and well-crafted trimwork. There are several "parlors" on the lobby level, reminding you of a classic grand hotel.

name: Royal Sonesta Harbor Court Baltimore
title: “Excellent Location, Great Rooms”
text: My boyfriend and I enjoyed a weekend stay. The hotel is in an excellent location., directly across the street from the Inner Harbor. The staff was polite and we had a beautiful courtyard view room.

name: The Back Bay Hotel
title: “Great Hotel”
text: We were doing a 5 city holiday in the USA and Canada, Boston and Jurys was the first chose. I booked this hotel through expedia, which was excellent, it gave me all the infomation I required to made a good decision to book this hotel. This room was with 2 queen beds and of very good standard, although the view was not good (this did not bother either of us as the exploration of Boston was the proirity) the room was very clean and tidy and housekeeping was excellent. The beds were very confortable and the bathroom was of good standard. The staff were kind and friendly and the Cuffs bar downstairs at the hotel was good. The hotel was in an excellent location to explore Boston (which to me is a good walking city) and if I did return back to Boston I would stay at this hotel again. very good keep up the good work.

name: Residence Inn Memphis Downtown
title: “fabulous hospitality and comfort”
text:
I traveled alone for the first time and couldn't have had a better time or selected a better hotel for me. The staff was exceptionally receptive and helpful and the hotel was nicely appointed and located in the center of the activity. I had a corner room with extra windows and a side view of the Mississippi River.....all of the appliances in the kitchen appeared new and everything worked. Although the staff offered to shop for me, I would have preferred easy access to a supermarket. Without a car, it was a long walk to carry groceries back to the hotel.
The breakfasts served at the Residence were really wonderul.....hot and cold buffet tables and everything was fresh including the fruit. Complimentary buffets were served in the evening as well and one could easily take dinner there at no cost.
I would return to this hotel and to Memphis in a New York minute.

name: Brookshire Suites
title: “Breakfast with Bite a hit with the kids!!”
text: I loved the character breakfast on Saturday Morning. The kids absolutely loved " Mr. Bite"!!!! I didn't think I would be able to take them anywhere but Disney World, but with Mr. Bite there we can vacation in Baltimore instead! Hey, its cheaper and we had a really great stay at the Brookshire Suites!

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Baltimore Downtown/Inner Harbor
title: “Great Hotel”
text: Great hotel for extended stay. Rooms were comfortable and clean. Staff was friendly and helpful. Enjoyed very much the afternoon cocktails. Only con: no on-site parking. Fine if you are traveling by taxi.

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “Location”
text:
Lo mejor del hotel es la localizacion, a una cuadra del parque y de la calle Newbury con tiendas y restaurantes. El hotel es viejo y necesita una renovacion, los cuartos son pequeños al igual que los baños, pero la localizacion ayuda.
El personal amable, el restaurant tiene un buen buffet y tambien hay un bar en la noche.
Si buscas un hotel bien ubicado para caminar por las zonas turisticas es muy buena opcion

name: Drury Inn Denver East
title: “Like Drury Inns!”
text: We always try to stay at Drury properties when traveling! Always can depend on a clean room, however this one wasn't the best in that regard. The halls and elevator were in need of a good vacumning. We didn't arrive early enough for the Kickback treats and drinks!!! We did enjoy the breakfast however before we hit the road early in the morning! The staff is always so polite and nice!!! I left my paperback in the room and realized it after we left. I called the hotel and after several conversations with the staff, it was located and they sent it to me within a week. Thank you so much!

name: Monaco Baltimore, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Best of the Best!”
text: My husband and I spent four nights at the Monaco Baltimore, and we had an incredible stay. We came to Baltimore for a surprise birthday trip for my husband, and the hotel upgraded our room to a King Deluxe and also welcomed us with champagne and chocolate covered strawberries. The architecture of the old B&O Railroad headquarters is magnificent. The service throughout the stay was top notch, the staff was very responsive, the room was very large with high ceilings, and we had a soaking whirlpool tub, double sink and large shower in the bathroom. The location is within walking distance of the Inner Harbor and Camden Yards. We are already talking about staying there for our next visit to Baltimore.

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Denver
title: “Great Service, Easy Location, Comfortable Rooms”
text:
If you are looking for a hip hotel in downtown, this is not your place...if your are looking for an easy, great location hotel with chill and nice staff than this is your place!! 
Kelly checked us in at the front desk and was great, and we asked a lot of her. We had people meeting us and she was really patient, she even gave directions to a severally lost friend!!
She offered a ton of great tips for Denver, fabulous!! 
The rooms were clean and comfortable, not huge, but room enough. Getting around downtown was easy...but the service was the best. Thanks for being so helpful Kelly and Sunny!!

name: Drury Inn Denver East
title: “Partisan TV in the breakfast room - never again”
text: I will not stay there again. The hotel was clean and the amenities and furnishings adequate. My husband has often stayed there on business, leaving too early for the breakfast. So we stayed there as a family on vacation. The breakfast was sumptuous, but the room crowded, the coffee lousy, the scrambled eggs seemingly not from eggs in the shell, and too long a line to wait one's turn at the 2 waffle makers. The deal breaker for us was a big flat-screen television blasting Fox News. Why would a hotel force partisan broadcasting - whether right-wing or left-wing - on its guests? In addition Fox News shows more smut than any other news network (always under the pretext of protesting the smut, but they show plenty of it) and I do not allow my children to watch such things.

name: Valli-Hi Motor Hotel
title: “RUN AWAY!”
text:
This is the place for Meth.
The entire hotel and its staff are trailer trash..and I used to live there. So I believe that I'm over qualified for this review.
Did I mention the meth users and dealers?! Just ask at the front desk they will hook you up..
Get a room and score some meth and the TB is for free!
JUST SAY NO AND DRIVE AWAY!
Thanks for your time
 Jack

name: Valli-Hi Motor Hotel
title: “bloss nicht dort übernachten”
text:
das schlimmste Motel, wo ich jemals übernachtet habe:
-keine Handtücher (erst auf mehrmalige Reklamation hin brachte man welche in mein Zimmer, die aber dunkelgrau statt weiß waren- man sagte mir aber das käme vom Wäschetrockner!?)
das Zimmer war unglaublich schmutzig (ich glaube nicht, daß man dort jemals Staub gesaugt hat) und roch unangenehm im Zimmer
-in den Fliesen im Bad waren riesige Löcher (bzw. haben ganz gefehlt)
-es gab keine richtigen Eingangstüren (nur Glasschiebetüren zum Hof hin)
-es war sehr laut, weil die Wände sehr dünn waren

name: Days Inn Central
title: “Never for woman !”
text:
I don't recommend for ladies who travel by herself. 
The people who work at front desk are VERY customer careful, but the guests are very, very weird !
The first night, there was a couple having a argument outside the room about midnight. The night after, a guy was listen a music from his car to loud !
I've heard from local people that is a striper house near by and some people use go to this hotel to doing drugs.
I did not feel safe enough, all night concerned, lots of noises get myself scare all the time.
Even the hotel is close to Downtown, the employees are very friendly, the price is about half than Downtown hotels, not sure if I’ll back to.

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Denver
title: “Excellent”
text: Enjoyed my stay at the Crowne Plaza...attentive staff...good restaurant...convenient location. Would stay again!

name: Drury Inn Denver East
title: “Fantastic bargain”
text: What a pleasant surprise. Never stayed at a Drury before, but it was fantastic - great rooms, very clean. Internet availability in the lobby. Free soda fountain all day. Big breakfast, free alcoholic beverages each evening with pizza, nachos, baked potatoes, salad - amazing bargain!!!

name: Howard Johnson Inn Denver
title: “Checked in... Didn't stay!”
text: I booked this hotel with hotels.com. I tried 3 different rooms!!! I was traveling with my 4 small children...Did not stay here. First of all, advertised check-in time was 3pm. I arrived at 3:30, and they had no rooms ready for me. The first room they did offer, was extremely dirty, holes in the curtains, a large patch of the ceiling over the beds looked like it was detached and ready to fall in at any moment, and where the smoke detector was supposed to be, there were just wires hanging out of the wall. So, I asked for a better room. The second room, the electronic lock was jammed and we could not get the door to unlock. The front desk person looked on her computer and could not figure out what the problem was (thank goodness we were outside the room, and not inside). So, we tried a third room (supposedly one of the nicer rooms). It was a little better, but was still dirty, holes in the curtains, and the smoke detector didn't work. Even if it was dead batteries, there's no excuse. People's lives depend on that LITTLE thing. So, I requested yet a different room. . they said they did not have one available. So, needless to say, I requested a refund on the room from hotels.com, and found one on my own.

name: Loews Denver Hotel
title: “Ok hotel, a bit outdated. Slow internet connection. Great Service.”
text: I stayed here for a Convention. Service is quite good, they have a free shuttle service that can take you to close distrance places. The hotel is far from downtown, close to Cherry Creek Mall; nothing good close.

name: Days Inn Central
title: “The Downtown Slums”
text: Our stay at the Days Inn on Federal Boulevard was horrible. We booked through hotels(-) The first room we had we were moved from because 10 minutes playing on the floor caused the kids to come up covered in black sooty type stuff. We were moved to a new room only to discover a more horrendous scene. One of the electrical outlets was broken and had white powder on the floor where you could see it had been shorting and sparking. The bathroom had mold all over from the ceiling to the floor. The kids still came up with black stuff on them after playing on the floor. Furniture was broken and the paint and construction was in great disrepair. When the Days Inn refused to refund us our money so we could go somewhere else, we contacted the Denver DA's office. Also, we were unable to get ahold of hotels.com to try to resolve the issues we had with a place that was deeply misrepresented on their site. Every time we wrote or called, we were unable to get ahold of a person or were hung up on. I do not advise using hotels(-) or Days Inn in any city. We contacted Days Inn's corporate headquarters only to be told that they could not help us and that we would need to take any concerns we had about our stay to the management of that specific Days Inn. The Denver DA's office gets a 110% as they promised they would not give us the run around like the hotel and hotel reps had. (And they didn't.)

name: Jet Hotel
title: “Horrible”
text: The only positive thing I will say is great location. I was embarrassed to be seen coming in and out of this hotel. The carpet was torn and severely stained. Bed was broken probably because this should be or is a rent the room by the hour hotel. The hallways were dark I didn't feel safe. The blind fell off the door to the balcony and balcony is a loose term. I put the blind up myself. There was no lighting around the sink the bulbs were blown. Furniture was an after thought and not an attempt at modern decor as stated in another review. On a Tuesday night the music cranked up at about 9:30pm and didn't stop till around 3:00am it shook the already broken bed. This hotel is a club with a hook up joint upstairs. I packed and left early the next morning. Would have left before that but other hotels were booked with business conference. Oh the two staff members I saw we're nice. I wouldn't have been surprised to see a chalk outline of a body or prostitutes.

name: Henderson's Wharf Inn
title: “Understated, pleasant, very comfortable”
text: I live just outside Baltimore; decided to spend the night in Baltimore as a splurge after an important day in the city. This was my second stay at this hotel. Great service, small hotel, very very comfortable rooms. My first stay was an interior room looking out on the courtyard; my second was a water view. I'm not sure that the steep price increase for the water view is worth it, because the interior room was equally well-appointed and cozy. In any case, the whole property is underpriced for what you get. The breakfast spread is spectacular and varied, with wicker trays for you to take your selection back to your room. My favorite hotel recently.

name: The Back Bay Hotel
title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text:
This is an excellent hotel located beside John Hancock Tower. This former Boston Police Headquarters was opened in June '04 and the staff are amongst the most pleasant you will find in any American property. Rooms are an adequate size and very well designed with in room safe and ironing facilities. Bathrooms are modern and of a great standard. All rooms offer free WiFi facilities.
The bar on the ground floor is excellent, altho can be quite crowded at night as it has an outside patio area for the smokers!!!.
Overall, one of the nicest, happiest hotels you're likely to experience in North America with staff that really make you feel at home.

name: Renaissance Denver Hotel
title: “Had a great time!”
text:
My hubby and I decided to take a staycation in our hometown of Denver. We live down in the southern burbs and rarely get out towards the Stapleton area, and we wanted to visit the Bass Pro Shop, so we decided to stay at this hotel. The Lobby area of the hotel is very nice, decorated in various lovely colors. The lobby is a large, very tall Atrium with the rooms facing out towards the courtyard.
My husband is a Marriott Rewards member, so we were upgraded to a room on the concierge level, floor 12. The room was very nice, the room had nice furniture and a nice west facing view of the mountains. Thanks to all the great Tripadvisor members who commented on the train whistle that kept them up, we mentioned this when checking in, and evidently if you are facing west (which is the best view of the Mountains anyway) you don't hear it as well. I didn't hear it all! The room had a nice balcony, which since it is still winter we didn't use, but it would be great in the spring and summer. The room was very clean and the bathroom nice and well appointed with Aveda products which I love.
We wanted to eat over at the Northfield shopping area which is where Bass Pro Shop is located and the hotel has a shuttle which drove us there and then returned at 10:30 pm to pick us up. That was nice as it allowed us to have a some drinks and not having to worry about driving. That was nice. There is a small but nice bar in the lobby of the atrium and evidently an Italian restaurant at the hotel, but we did not eat there. 
Our stay here was very nice, and I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone wishing to stay in the Stapleton area of Denver. It would be nice for someone also going to or leaving the airport even though it is a little ways away from DIA. Thank you, we will return!

name: Denver's Best Inn and Suites
title: “Not worth the savings! And not worth five minutes of your time.”
text:
Never again will I reserve a room here. The room was filthy (although the sheets did appear clean) everything else was noticeably dirty. My mom cut her leg on the bed, the area of town was sketchy, nothing about this hotel was worth a cheaper room. 
We checked out immediately and did NOT stay more than five minutes!

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Denver
title: “Exceptionally Friendly Staff”
text: The staff was so friendly and helpful every step of the way from reservations to check in to lost and found even after the trip that I found it important to write a review...something I have never done before. I would highly recommend this hotel. The buffet breakfast was very good, the wait staff exceptional, and the location is perfect with just a very short walk for those wanting to partake in downtown activities such as the Convention Center, Performing Arts Center, State Capitol, free 16th Street Mall ride, B-Cycle bike sharing locations, etc., etc.

name: Henderson's Wharf Inn
title: “Wonderful service, view and location”
text: I came to Baltimore with my teenage son to look at Johns Hopkins University. What an unexpected delight and surprise. After driving in the rain for what seemed like forevever from Washington DC after taking two college tours, we checked into our harbor view room. It was spacious and well appointed with a complimentary bottle of wine as well. The front staff was friendly, courteous and very helpful. They had menus from the local restaurants along with a map of how to get there. The breakfast bar consisted of fresh pineapple, strawberries, blueberries, cantelope and honewdew. What a treat and the coffe was perfect. I will definitely stay here again when we are in Baltimore and I would reccomennd this well run establishment to any and everyone.

name: The Back Bay Hotel
title: “Excellent hotel and staff”
text:
I would really have to struggle long and hard to find anything wrong with this hotel. We were shown up to our wonderful room and our bags followed. The bed was huge, comfortable and the pillows fantastic.
Champagne and chocolate covered strawberries awaited us as requested. The CD player was on and further CDs were offered. Three telephones, TV, safe, iron, bathrobes, hairdryer and the lovely toiletries. Even an umbrella in the closet for wet days! The view, from the seventh floor, was fantastic. Every evening the bed was turned down for us. 
The hotel has internet access freely available as well as wireless and wire access in all rooms.
The staff were all highly trained and so considerate of their guests. They enquired on a regular basis if they could help us and offered suggestions for excursions. The concierge was especially helpful with car and restaurant bookings and directions.
The General Manager was a very friendly Dublin man whom we made a point to speak to congratulate him on the fine restoration of the building and the excellent staff. It is an hotel where everyone from the doorman to the General Manager were all glad that you were staying with them.
Breakfast in the Stanhope Grill is wonderful. Do not pass on the buffet. This is THE breakfast. You just cannot eat after it until evening! It really sets you up for a day touring Boston.
We had dinner in the bar on Easter Sunday and were looked after wonderfully by Kahela ( I hope I have spelt her name right). Her friendly smiling, chatty manner made us feel right at home. She treated us like welcome friends every night we went in. She typified the manner and style of all the hotel’s staff towards us. A marvellous group of people. Well done Stephen for training them so well in customer care.
We had dinner in the Stanhope Grill and the food was just great. The craic in Cuffs bar was great. I just loved sitting there and listening to the enjoyment of so many people and engaging in my favourite pastime – people watching. A REAL Irish bar – just don’t run out of Guinness again!!
The location of the hotel is just right. One direction is Boston Common and the other is Copley Place and Newbury Street, another and you are at the Prudential Centre. Hard Rock Cafe is just around the corner as is Back Bay train station.
This is an hotel in a million. Perhaps I should not tell anyone about it so that I can always get in when I return, but I promised Stephen the manager I would tell everyone how good it is and how satisfied we both were with our stay. Do go there – it is well worth it.

name: Comfort Inn Downtown
title: “Comfortable stay”
text: We traveled to Denver for a meeting, went early to enjoy Denver. Got hotel room through the convention housing center. Since we had stayed in this hotel in the past and liked it we were happy to get a room there. Very convenient to the center of town, to the 16th street mall and the buses there, plenty of restaurants, shops, museums. Also had a shuttle bus to the convention center from this hotel - very convenient. The convention center is actually within walking distance. Hotel is comfortable, convenient free breakfast, Internet access is free. Fitness center available, but too busy to use on this trip. Husband came with me, but it was my meeting.

name: The Burnsley All Suite Hotel
title: “Fantastic!”
text:
I was looking for a nice hotel at a decent price near downtown during the World Series. For 170$ a night I found the Burnsley and I couldn't have been happier.
The suite was more an apartment than a suite: kitchen, bathroom, very large living room with round table that sits 6 people, sofa, two tv's, nice king size bed, and a nice balcony with fantastic views fo the city and the Rocky Mountains.
Very clean, bathroom a bit old but in good shape, staff corteous, free covered parking on site.
I'll definitely make the Burnsley my first choice when returning to Denver.

name: The Burnsley All Suite Hotel
title: “You Take the Good, You Take the Bad...”
text: The Burnsley is a few blocks southeast of the Capitol, which puts it in walking distance to the Civic Center, but not to other popular tourist areas like LoDo or Cherry Creek. Nonetheless, I got a great online rate (gov't ID) and parking was free, so I decided to give it a try. The lobby of the hotel is quite sophisticated, but the glamour ends there. It is a converted apartment building, and the hallways and other main areas (other than those in the lobby or on the mezzanine) are very outdated (1970s wallpaper). Our suite was indeed spacious and had a very nice view of the Capitol. It was also pretty clean, although there was some mold in the shower soap dish. My major problem with this place is that the decor is so outdated and the furnishings are tattered; the carpet was old and worn; the living room sofa literally had stuffing coming out of it in some spots. I don't understand why this place was recommended in my guidebook. I'll say one very positive thing, though: the bed and pillows were fabulous--the best that I have ever slept on in a hotel! Nonetheless, I think some major renovations are required.

name: Denver Marriott City Center
title: “Trains loud, nice location”
text: Stayed for business and it is nice location to the convention center and 16th street mall. Clean hotel and friendly staff. Rooms were small and we had to listen to the train whistles and bells every 5 minutes. It can be tough to sleep through the noise if you are a light sleeper.

name: Denver Marriott City Center
title: “Great Service”
text: I spent one week at this location and had no problems with anything. Rooms were clean and well kept. Beds were very nice and easy to sleep on. The 17th floor has an outstanding concierge lounge also with great service and an honor bar. Indoor pool was nice and well maintained. This hotel is close to everything and within walking distance to everything. there is no on site parking and its 30 bucks a day for valet services. Valet's were very helpful an on average takes 10 to 15 minutes to get your car ready for pick up. A Starbucks is in the lobby and a small store with everything.

name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Denver
title: “Good spot to stay in Denver”
text: Only complaint was a garbage smell in 18th floor hallway otherwise the stay was perfect. Centrally located to freeways, food, shopping and attractions

name: La Quinta Inn Denver Cherry Creek
title: “Good quality”
text: This hotel offers a nice and quiet place to rest in denver. It is really close to DU and several movie theaters. I would stay here when friends came from out of state to visit. It is not 5 star quality but is clean, comfortable, and affordable. Its a little far from Downtown if you are looking to have fun in Lodo or on Cap hill. If you want to be closer to the downtown denver nightlife i suggest the LaQuinta off of park avenue. This is a good location if you have business to attend to in the cherry creek area.

name: Ramada Denver Midtown
title: “Für das Geld okay”
text: Zustand des Hotels ist jetzt nicht der beste ( Beschädigte Möbel, ältere Einrichtung, 1 von 4 Lampen ging nicht), aber es ist sauber. Bad mit Badewanne hat mir gut gefallen. Internet und Frühstück umsonst fand ich super. Personal ist zwar nicht super freundlich, hilft aber trotzdem weiter. Meinen Urlaub würde ich nicht da verbringen wollen, aber für Geschäftsreise ist es völlig in Ordnung gewesen. Zur Innenstadt ist es nicht weit und man kann entweder den kostenlosen Hotelshuttel benutzen, Bus (1.75 Dollar) oder Taxi (8 Dollar) oder man läuft so ca. halbe Stunde.

name: Best Western Plus Denver International Airport Inn & Suites
title: “airport pickup”
text: This is a great location for airport convenience. We have used their shuttles to and from the airport, and they are so helpful. The location also provides park and ride, which always reduces our parking costs, even if you cannot get a discounted rate using the park and ride.

name: Best Western Plus Denver International Airport Inn & Suites
title: “Great Place To Stay”
text: I've stayed here a few times and always a pleasure. They have well lit and clean rooms, breakfast area is well maintained and stocked. The shuttle service to the Denver Airport is fast and dependable. No complaints here.

name: Best Western Plus Denver International Airport Inn & Suites
title: “Great find for travels”
text: The Denver Best Western Plus Hotel was very convenient and cost-effective for my husband and me as we began a 9 day rail vacation in Canada. We are residents of Fort Collins and drove to Denver for our flight into Calgary. We knew that construction was making travel to DIA challenging so leaving our car off-airport was especially attractive. The complimentary parking for the duration of our trip and the free shuttle to the airport made things very easy. In addition, the hotel is very nicely appointed, clean and attractive. Staff was very friendly and a breakfast bag to take with us as we were leaving before the buffet breakfast was served was such a nice surprise. Kudos all around! We will use this hotel again and will tell our friends of our experience.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Memphis - Beale Street
title: “Great location!”
text:
This was a really nice hotel... like some of the previous reviews stated, the music from Beale St was quite loud, but we enjoyed it. We stayed in one of the rooms with a balcony and it would have been perfect if the view hadn't been of the Hooter's restaurant down below. 
Parking is a little expensive at $15/night but it's very convenient and the parking rates are expected in a downtown area. 
Great breakfast and wonderful staff!

name: Monaco Baltimore, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “I'll Never Stay Anywhere Else Again”
text:
The Monaco in Baltimore exceeded every expectation, and went above the already-excellent standard that Kimpton Hotels always live up to.
The property is gorgeous: the building is breathtaking, with special details in numerous places. The fitness center is well above what most boutique hotels offer. My room furnishings, floor plan (I was in a large corner suite overlooking Charles St.) and bathroom were phenomenal - including the deepest bathtub I have ever seen! 
The staff members were also tremendously welcoming and helpful: from the time I got out of the cab until I departed the next morning they went beyond all necessity to ensure I was comfortable and happy. From being greeted with a glass of wine, to being handed a jogging map of the city upon check-in, they paid attention to the things that matter to me. The GM is certainly running this place well.
I can't wait to go back, but this time for fun instead of work!

name: Ramada Inn Downtown Denver
title: “Anual Meeting”
text: I was in town to anual meeting in Nephrology. It´s a cleaner hotel, confy enough and placed a few minutes from convention center by taxi. A two blocks from McDonalds and others fast foods. Very cool for a short stay or a business stay. The hotel was in price range at location and didn´t expect so much. Shuttle service was good and reliable.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Denver Southeast
title: “Conveniently located”
text: I was able to book two nights through a discount website for $31 per night; including taxes and fees of $16.03 it came to $78.03, which I think makes it an excellent value for a nice hotel. It is an older property, but I feel it has been well maintained. It is located just off of I-25 on Hampden Road, which is a nice location near a residential neighborhood. I didn't try the restaurant, instead I visited a Whole Foods located just a few blocks away, where you can eat in-store or do takeout. There is an attractive outdoor pool that I didn't try, and a comfortably-heated indoor pool that I did try and liked. There is also an indoor spa and fitness center just off the indoor pool. The layout of the hotel is a little confusing as it is built on a hill, but they provide a map. As someone else mentioned, several of the first-floor rooms have outside access, which would be handy if you don't want to navigate the hallways. There is a covered parking garage which allows you to keep your car out of the hot sun, which I appreciated. When I stayed, the only wireless high-speed internet access was available in the lobby. However, in each room they offer free high-speed internet using an ethernet plug on the desk. Cables are stored in the closet. I have stayed here before and will do so again.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Memphis - Beale Street
title: “Location, Location, Location”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights and had a great time. Hotel was clean, staff was excellent, free breakfast, but the location was the best. The hotel is right next to Beale Street, Peabody Place (restaurants, cinema, and a few stores), FedEx Forum (Memphis Grizzlies), and also very close to the Gibson Factory, the minor league baseball stadium, and The Peabody Hotel.
Only issue is the noise when trying to sleep, but what can you expect when you are right next to Beale Street. 
I'd reco anyone to stay at this hotel. Price is a little high, but figure in the lack in needing cab fare or a rental car (charge is $12/day for parking) and it should even out.

name: Henderson's Wharf Inn
title: “The best of Baltimore!”
text: My husband and I stayed here one night last week. After reading the reviews, I was excited to see how the hotel measured up. It was fantastic! The rooms are beautifully furnished in such a way to maintain the historic feel of the hotel. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Breakfast was wonderful. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone staying in Baltimore. We can't wait to return!

name: Four Points by Sheraton Denver Southeast
title: “Awful”
text: With a Marriot name you would expect at the very least business quality. Not So. This is by far the worst Marriot we have ever been to. We also paid well over $100 to stay at a 30 year old dump! Everything is extremely dated and worn out. The staff were fine, but the rooms are horrible! Tiny beds with worn out furniture and linens scuffed up walls etc.. the list goes on. Also not safe for small children, balconies that appear to not meet safety regulations. Stay away from this one. There is a better Marriot 10 minutes south off the same freeway. Wish we had stayed there! Also do not believe the new pictures on the Marriot website they are so far from the truth its pathetic!!!!!

name: Residence Inn Memphis Downtown
title: “Fabulous friendly staff”
text: Stayed 3 nights here in July 2008. Great welcome and very courteous smiling staff throughout. Good position for all the sights, but we were not really ready for the inner city emptiness in Memphis. Great restaurant "Mcewens" next door. Basic breakfast but bonus of 2 free dinners during the week. Music scene is fun, and this hotel is a great base, nice and relaxing at the end of a hard day.

name: Residence Inn Memphis Downtown
title: “Loved It”
text:
I stayed at the Residence Inn Monroe Ave ,Downtown Memphis.
26th-29th June 2008
I was very nervous having booked on the internet(Hotels.com).
When we arrived we were greeted by friendly staff,Hughie at the reception soon made us feel welecome.The rooms were great,breakfast lovely,location brilliant,and we had a great stay here and I will recommend to my family and friends.Tom Newquay,Cornwall,UK

name: Embassy Suites Denver - Southeast
title: “Typical Embassy Suites in most respects”
text:
I just spent 3 nights at this Embassy Suites. It seems to be typical of the chain, although it smelled like smoking is allowed on one side of the 7th floor. The odor didn't get to my room, but walking past that area could be problematic if you are hyper sensitive. 
The room was fine, although the mattress was somewhat soft. One of my pet peeves is shower/bath fixtures that are loose or don't work quite right. That is not a problem here. All of the bathroom fixtures seemed to be fairly new. I always had hot water in the morning, even with a fairly full hotel. The sink area in the bathroom itself is small, but there is another sink in the bedroom. There are 2 TVs, but neither is a flatscreen. In fact, the TV in the bar/restaurant was also old and outdated. Nothing HiDef in this hotel. Channel selection in the rooms is limited. 
I had two evening meals in the restaurant. They were ok. Other dining options in the area are limited, with only a Qdoba and a McDonalds within walking distance. There is a Whole Foods grocery store across the street. I didn't have a chance to "explore" the immediate area so I can't tell you if there are other dining options available. 
Two of the attractions of an Embassy Suites are the free breakfast and the evening "Manager's Reception". The lines for this breakfast were long, but they moved quickly. If you don't want eggs, there are fruit and cereal. The "Manager's Reception" is in the bar/restaurant area. Your choice of libations is limited. In other words, you can only have one brand of beer or the "cheap stuff" if you are having a cocktail. I don't know what the wine offering is. But the price is right during the reception, and there are servers if you don't want to stand in line. 
The facility itself seems kind of gloomy. One of the elevators is out of service, and the other 3 are somewhat slow. The staff was helpful and, for the most part, friendly. I don't know that this hotel would be my first choice for a stay, primarily because of location, but if my work were to be in the area again, I wouldn't turn it down. 
Almost forgot: the air conditioning ran all of the time. I don't think the temperature controls are accurate. What the control said was 67 seemed to be warmer than that. I had to set the temperature to 65. I couldn't leave the window open because the outside spotlights seemed to be directed right at my room. Not really, but they are very bright.

name: Denver Marriott Tech Center
title: “Rude front desk person”
text: Front desk guy was rude. His name badge showed, he is from KY and also he is the supervisor for the night shift. Bad /rude behavior. I lost all my pleasure of stay after his talk. I am not going to come back. Bad customer service.

name: Fairfield Inn Denver Cherry Creek
title: “No frills, good value”
text: This is a no frills hotel, with a small lobby with a cozy fireplace, small (but clean) rooms, nice bathroom. Odd numbered rooms have mountain views. Somewhat difficult to get in and out of the building and parking lot which is under the building (but parking is free!), and the hotel is in a very congested area. We stayed on an upper floor, but could still hear the traffic noise below. Also walls are very thin and at times you can clearly hear conversations in neighboring rooms. This hotel is centrally located, near all shopping and restaurants. Free wi-fi a plus. Front desk clerk was very nice and friendly, all staff were really exceptional, very helpful and outgoing. Breakfast was basic-bagels, muffins, etc. but nice to have available. There is a small fitness room with minimal equipment. If you are just looking for a decent, clean and inexpensive place to stay, you will be satisfied with your stay here.

name: Embassy Suites Denver - Southeast
title: “Wireless Internet cost $8.95/night/device”
text:
We stayed one night and checked out to move to another Hilton Property because I was disappointed with the wireless internet policy. I knew that internet access cost $9/day and I was fine with that, but it turns out that it is $9/day/device and we have two laptops and two iPads that we needed to use during our visit.
Other than that, the breakfast was good, the room was fine, and the staff was friendly.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Denver Hotel
title: “Reasonable stay”
text: I found that the rooms weren't that bad, but it seemed a bit pricey compared to other places I have been to on my trip.

name: Days Inn & Suites DIA-Denver International Airport
title: “Perfect for a one night business trip”
text: Although the exterior of this Days Inn seems fairly new, the room appeared very dated based on the furnishings and decor. However, being that I was traveling as a single male guest for one night, this did not bother me, was just an observation. The front desk was very helpful, checked me in quickly and efficiently and the price was terrific. The room was clean and the a/c worked perfectly. The bathroom was a wee bit small, but very clean and the shower nice and hot. I was literally at this hotel for less than 10 hours and for what I needed (a bed, a shower and close to DIA) it couldn't be beat. The only negative I would point out is the tiny parking lot. I had to parallel park on an adjacent empty street, but apparently this is status quo for the area...really not a big deal, but if I had a complaint, that would be the only one.

name: Hotel VQ
title: “Quality staff, friendly, clean and comfortable”
text: I have frequented this Hotel on a monthly basis for the past three years and have always found the rooms and banqurt facilities to be clean and the staff Rachel Taylor,Linda Talbott and the banquet staff Juan and Inira to be very accomidating of our wishes. The view and location are great and access from I-25 is very easy. As for their banquet menues the food is great and the presentations appealing to the eye and to the pallet.

name: Comfort Suites Denver International Airport
title: “Get Internet Rate not the Rate at the Dexk”
text: The stay was just ok! The front desk was helpful. The hotel computer was not working at arrival. I probably killed about 7 "bugs" in my restroom. The breakfast was good, bacon, eggs, juice, biscuits, etc.

name: Microtel Inn by Wyndham Denver
title: “Not very clean but free shuttle”
text:
I stayed here on an overnight stop between flights back to Scotland 
- Positives
Free Courtesy shuttle pick from the airport and return the next day was prompt and the drivers were friendly 
The continental breakfast was better than expected - coffee- tea - bagels - fruit - etc 
There is a great diner about 100 yards away get the Pie :)
Good value for 1 night and Airport stop over
- Negatives
- One of the blankest was stained
- A few tiles in the Bathroom were cracked
-The hotel in general was a bit dirty and needed some serious updating
I think with a bit of TLC this Hotel could be brought back up to a much better standard. There seems to be a lack of attention to the general cleanliness of the hotel a shame really.

name: Monaco Baltimore, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “great location, flawless stay”
text: this hotel is conveniently located a few short blocks from the convention centre as well as the inner harbour. some reviews commented on the safety concerns after-dark, but we did not experience any problems (and we walked everywhere). all staff were fantastic, including doormen, room service and housekeeping - friendly and very accommodating! across the street are coffee shops, and up the road is a superb little grocery store. easy to walk to countless restaurants - but don't forget the B&O Brasserie onsite! the only improvement i would suggest is a vending machine for water - other than the wet bar, you would have to order room-service for it...is an inconvenience. oh yes, very noisy air conditioning system in the room - but given the fact that it was pretty warm and humid during our stay - it was still very much appreciated!

name: The Timbers Hotel
title: “great hotel”
text: We got back to Canada a week ago from Denver Colorado. Our first time there. Went to the Dever Stock Show and Rodeo. Our friends were staying at this hotel, and had stayed there before. We really enjoyed the hotel. No problem with anything. I didn't eat in the restuarant, but our friends did, and they said it was excellent. The kitchenette was great. Room service excellent. The shuttle ran us to the mall, the stock show, rodeo etc., picked us up when we dropped off our rental car and took us to the airport. We tipped each time, as the service was complimentary. would definitely recommend this hotel. Great price with the group rate.

name: Denver Marriott City Center
title: “Adequate”
text:
Rooms were adequate and what I expect in a hotel that serves large number of patrons attending conferences. Everything in the room was nice from the television to the beds, however, the size of the room was cramped. The hotel staff was very good and always trying to assist you with any need. The hotel and rooms were very clean and well taken care of. The location is great for the conference center and the surrounding area has lots of entertainment and shopping options. 
On the down side the rooms was loud. The a/c sounded like a bus driving through your room. We could hear a noise from somewhere that we finally decided was the elevators going up and down. This was not too much of a bother but something you could hear in the quite of the night. The room doors seem to have a closing mechanism that causes them to slam. You could hear every neighboring room shut the door when they returned home. This is particularly a bother on the weekends when some people are returning form the bars at 2 and 3 am. This was so bad on Saturday night that we had to call down to the desk and have security come up and stop the partying that was going on a few rooms away. It was not that you could hear the what was going on in the room, but every time someone would go in or out of the room the door would slam. 
Overall I would not write this hotel off my list of places to stay, but I would not necessarily say that the next time I am in Denver I will automatically stay there either.

name: Holiday Inn Select Denver - Cherry Creek
title: “It's not as bad as the other reviews say”
text: Overall nice hotel for the $50 priceline bid, and worty of being 3-star. Biggest problem - stuck in a smoking room on a smoking floor. Once the elevator doors opened, it was so smokey in the hallway that I felt like I was walking through a chimney. The room was, however, free of smoke smell. Shower temperature also goes from perfect down to luke warm every couple of minutes. Lobby/lounge had a warm atmosphere. Internet, Parking, and Newspaper were all free, unlike the Hyatt I stayed at the week before. Strip club across the street did not interfere by noise or any other aspect. Shopping very convenient also across the street. Very suburban-like setting.

name: Denver Marriott Tech Center
title: “Big hotel in the Mile High City”
text:
Like some of the other reviewers, I also got this hotel via Priceline. The value is excellent. 
This is a big hotel. I had a room in the North tower. This meant a 2 minute walk from the lobby to the elevator. The furnishings in the lobby are nice enough but they'll probably need to be renovated in the next 2 years. The hotel has the "Colorado Lodge feel" that you'd expect from a Denver hotel. 
My room was clean and well appointed. The bed was comfortable I liked having the refrigerator. The downside was no wireless internet and I hate paying for the internet. This really is something that should be included these days. 
Being an elite member, I had access to the concierge lounge. This was very nice as there was breakfast and dinner. Also, they had a nice Starbuck's coffee machine in the room. Nice to have in the morning! 
I didn't get a chance to eat at the restaurants or use the fitness center but I heard good things. 
Overall, I'd stay here again if I could get a nice rate on Priceline. I'm not sure I could be talked into the regular rate, which was over $200 at the time I booked.

name: Sheraton Denver Downtown Hotel
title: “Mega-hotel, but personal service”
text:
Because I called ahead, my room was ready for an 8 am check-in. Rooms, especially in The Towers, are lovely with all the amenities. Great location, right on the 16th Street Mall and lots of dining options in the hotel and nearby.
I was attending a conference and the meeting spaces were gigantic and the A/V staff very helpful.

name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Denver Hotel
title: “friendly & helpfull staff, clean & attractive Bestwestern Denver Hotel”
text:
Very Nice experience & Best Western Denver Hotel.
Marianna helped with public transportation to denver downtown and local restuarants.
Roy the Front Manager is very help in organizing trips to local attractions and shuttle service.
Jacquie helped us out since she is denver resident.

name: Ramada Inn Downtown Denver
title: “Good Cheap Hotel Downtown”
text: I stayed here in February 2005. I chose it because of the price and the location. It's about a mile from the Capitol and is cheaper than anything else in the area. Granted, like the others say, the neighborhood can be a bit sketchy (I was panhandled upon walking 2 blocks west). It has a post office, liquor store, and bodega across the street. The Mexican Restaurant kitchen was closed for repairs when I was there, but the bar was open. The restaurant staff was friendly. The room and the hotel were very clean. There were kids playing in the hot tub, but I didn't investigate its cleanliness myself. Hotel staff was courteous and professional. Bottom line: if you're looking for a cheap but clean hotel in downtown Denver and don't mind an occasional panhandler, don't hesitate to stay here.

name: The Westin Denver Downtown
title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: Perfectly located right in the downtown area within walking distance of many great restaurants, shops, bars, etc... The service was great and all of the employees were professional and courteous. The room was very nice and comfortable. Overall a great stay.

name: Ramada Inn Downtown Denver
title: “Gutes Hotel in fast perfekter Lage”
text:
Dieses Hotel bietet Zimmer in tollem Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis.
Es ist ca. 10 Gehminuten vom Stadtkern entfernt und besticht durch seinen Western-Stil.
Frühstück und Abendessen kann man extra im hoteleigenen Restaurant dazuwählen.
Außerdem bieten ein kleiner Pool und Fitnessraum Sportmöglichkeiten. 
Große Stadtparks, Golfplätze und Zoo sind ebenfalls schnell zu erreichen.
Alles in allem bietet diese Hotel ein guten Ausgangspunkt für Leute, die gerne mehr von der Stadt sehen und denen es nichts ausmacht, ein bißchen laufen zu müssen !

name: Ramada Inn Downtown Denver
title: “Impossibile dormire”
text:
