L'hotel è vetusto, ma almeno due camere, la mia e quella di altri dueamici, avevano "vista sul sistema di condizionamento dell'hotel" con un rumore infernale che ci ha impedito di dormire tutta la notte.
Comunque l'hotel è sconsigliabile, malgrado la vicinanza al centro.

name: Hyatt Regency Denver Tech Center
title: “doesn't live up to the "regency" name”
text:
Typically when you hear of a Hyatt Regency you immediately expect a bit more. Not at this place. It's very grand when you walk in the front door but that's about it. The hotel is very old looking and dated. 70's mustard colored walls, carpet and curtains in the rooms. For this being in the DTC area, I'd expect them to more tech friendly. If you have electronics, bring your own power supply. I had to unplug the lamp just so I could charge my laptop and phone at the same time. The remote and keyboard for the tv is more of a pain than anything. The remote has a roller ball mouse on it which is great in theory but not if it doesn't work! I had to carry around the remote AND keyboard just to watch the tv. The deadbolt to my door didn't work and it looks like they may know that so there was an old chain slide lock added on. The air in my room also didn't work. Besides the fact that it didn't work, my corner room was so small I had to move the desk to get the chair out to get to the AC unit to adjust the temperature. If there is more than one person in your party, the corner room is probably not going to work for you. In addition, there was rust in the shower and some strange white stuff all over the bathroom walls.
The room service choices were also very few and poor. I think the condition of the hotel is reflected in the questionably low price per night for this place.
I've stayed at the Hyatt Place hotels also and I think that was much more of a value. Because this has the name "regency" that's evidently the ok to charge you extra for everything. $5 bottle water, you have to pay to park, pay for wireless internet, etc. If you're a business traveler, ask about the "business plan" upon checkin. It's $25 and includes parking, breakfast, internet, water and dry cleaning.
I also didn't like the fact that once you're actually a guest and park in the parking garage you essentially have to use the back door to get to the elevators and parking garage. You're never acknowledged by the staff because no one sees you coming or going (also a safety issue). 
I was less than impressed with this hotel. I stayed at a Hilton Garden Inn the night after my stay here and I was 100x more impressed with that hotel than this Hyatt Regency. It's way overdue for a complete makeover.

name: Inn at Cherry Creek
title: “A pleasant surprise”
text: My mom booked this room for us, as she had an art show in walking distance from this place. This was my first stay here and I loved it. My fiancé was in love with the beds as they were so comfortable. They had nice little touches and amenities everywhere. The coolest experience was, I mentioned I liked this painting they had hung out back. The manager was so nice that on my birthday, he gave it to me. He also came out when we having breakfast to see how our stay was and if there was anything else we could do. Two thumbs up David (that's the manager)!

name: The Westin Denver Downtown
title: “Very nice stay”
text: This hotel was wonderful in many ways. First, it is conveniently located downtown and within walking distance of many of the restaurants and bars in the downtown area. We were impressed with the size of the rooms. The room size made it much easier to travel with our two children. We were also impressed with the friendliness of the staff. Most of them really went out of their way to assist us with anything that we needed during our stay. Steve, their head concierge, was very helpful. We loved the rooftop pool and gym. The only thing that we could think of to improve is how some of the rooms seemed to be a bit worn out. It seemed like the hotel is still in a transition to become a Westin.

name: Super 8 Denver - Airport
title: “Suite-sized room”
text:
Close to DIA, right on Tower Road with eateries and such to help unwind, this motel was far more than I expected for a Super 8. The room was Large! Comfortable, easy to move around in, with a King sized bed that was soft yet firm. Clean, no repairs needed. Mini fridge, coffee, nice bathroom, comfortable couch, perfect-sized television. 
Didn't get to try the restaurant as I had an early flight, so I made do with a quick bite from the Continental breakfast made available.

name: Residence Inn Denver Downtown
title: “This Place Has Bed Bugs - Stay Away!!!”
text: I stayed in this hotel for one month and on the 9th day of my stay, I woke up with bed bug bites all over my body, including my face and neck. I went into work (at a dermatology clinic) that day and asked some of the residents to confirm that the lesions did indeed resemble insect bites. When I got home that day, I removed the sheets from my bed and saw a bed bug (I knew it was a bed bug since I am in medical school and I have studied pictures of bed bugs). I asked to change rooms and I received no apology and had to move rooms by myself. I left the pillow I had brought from home in the first room since it could have been infested, but the next day after I get back from washing all of my clothes, I found it in my new room - the staff had brought it to me even after they should have known the other room was infested. I woke up in my new room with more bites and I had to move rooms again. After all of this, the hotel still denies that there are bed bugs in the hotel and refuses to even compensate me for my dry cleaning bill (which was necessary to prevent the bugs from coming home with me in any potentially infested clothing). They disrespected me in front of other guests and insinuated that I was making the whole thing up despite the blistering red welts all over my arms, hands, face and neck. There is a fundamental lack of knowledge and respect for the decency of a fellow human-being by every staff member I encountered while at this hotel.

name: Hyatt Regency Denver Tech Center
title: “Good place to stay”
text:
I stayed at the Hyatt Regency Tech Center on a fun trip with my son recently. It was a perfectly good hotel for our purposes and I would recommend it to anyone and would happily stay there again on another trip to Denver, despite having a few issues with the property.
The hotel was nice and clean and in a good location if you do not have to go downtown. Traffic was relatively light in the area (we were there over a holiday weekend; since this is primarily a business district, I imagine it is busier during the week) and there were plenty of restaurants within driving distance. The Tech Center area is a pleasant business park area that is well-maintained and clean. The hotel had a decent (but pricey) breakfast and a nice indoor pool and hot tub (very clean and well-kept). The bed was very comfortable.
There were a few downsides during our trip. First, the walls seemed to be somewhat thin as there was a group of spanish-speaking people that were up late talking loudly one night and I could hear everything they said (but not understand it!). I almost called the front desk, but they finally quieted down about 11:30 p.m.
Also, the staff failed to clean our room one day. We left the room about 10:30 a.m., and did not come back until 6:30 p.m., so they had plenty of time and there was not a sign on the door telling them not to disturb. So, I was disappointed in that. 
Finally, when I made my reservation with Hyatt, I bought an upgrade package that included breakfast, parking and internet. Before I bought it, I called Hyatt's customer service to make sure it would include breakfast for both me and my son. They told me that my son would be able to eat free, so it would not be a problem. But, when I arrived at the hotel, they told me that only kids under 5 eat free. My son is 10, so he was not free. When I politely explained the situation to the front desk personnel, and that I had been told something different by Hyatt customer service, they offered no apology or even a token gesture to make up for it. In my opinion, a top-notch property tries to at least offer a token gesture. Especially since I am a Hyatt Gold Club member. But, nope, nothing from them for this misinformation. 
But, those negatives aside, the property itself is nice and the staff were generally courteous, so I would recommend it.

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Best historic hotel in Boston! (and a tip for better service)”
text:
After quickly scanning the reviews of this hotel, I cannot imagine where the negative reviewer from Dublin stayed. I have stayed at most of the old hotels in Boston (Lenox, Park Plaza, etc.) and this was the best!
BIGGEST TIP: Sign up for Omni's "Select Guest" program. It's free and you'd be an idiot not to sign up. By doing so, you get to check out late (as late as 5PM!!), free room service drinks and a paper in the morning, and other small things that makes the entire experience worthwhile.
The room was nice and was a good size. Try the Deluxe rooms as they are not much more money and provide you with more space. The staff was so very nice. My wife and I arrived at 12:30AM after our flight was delayed. We checked in quickly, were greeted with smiles and quickly made it up to our room. We ordered room service (24 hours) and it came in about 5 minutes! The food by the way was the best for room service I have ever had.
Overall, we had a great vacation. Oh! Their gym is great:pretty sizable and a number of machines, weights, etc. 
Only negatives: Their gift shop is being remodeled so it is currently in a temporary location. That and the bar, despite it's history closes at 12am on weekends...at a hotel I found this a little strange. But this was such a minor problem, it did not make one difference to our trip.
Don't forget to try the Parker House Rolls!

name: Hyatt Regency Denver Tech Center
title: “Would use again”
text: I would highly recommend this hotel. We stayed for two nights with a "pick your perk" option. This meant free parking and $20a day off food and drinks. Room was clean and bed very comfortable. Food inthe bar was good and buffet breakfast was of a good standard with lots of options. A good location to explore denver and golden without breaking the bank.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Denver - Aurora
title: “Bed Bugs!!! Don't stay here!”
text:
The area where this hotel is located (in a business park) is scary if you arrive or depart after dark. When you walk into the hotel you think it is wonderful. Well, when you walk in, it IS beautiful. However, when you get to your room things take a turn for the worse. The "suite" is a stock hotel room. Nothing fancy..very dry and business looking. 
I stayed at this hotel on the second floor, right off the elevator on Oct 8th, 2006. It was horrible! When we walked into the room it had a pungent sweet odor--- little did I know that the smell was being emitted by bed bugs who would soon bite me as I hopped into bed after a long drive in the pouring rain from Northern Colorado! The bathroom looked like it has not been cleaned. There were marks on the floor that looked like something of wet dirty feet. The toilet is white so you definitely saw the huge green snot that was dried onto the toilet seat. There were no sheets, blankets or pillowcases for the sofa bed, and in the bedroom there was a half full water bottle on the night table behind the lamp. As I climbed into bed and started to drift off to sleep, I began to itch. Little did I know my bed and the bed next to mine was infested with bed bugs! I had welts all over my body including my face and head. At 3am after sitting in the chair at the desk and contimplating about going to the front desk, I began moving both matresses on the beds and in between the mattress and boxspring I found dead bed bug carcasses and egg sacks. DISGUSTING! The people I was with went to management and told them about this issue. All they asked was if we wanted to move to a different room. HELL NO! WE WANTED OUT! So, we demanded that they not charge us for the room and thankfully they didn't. We left and on the way out the lady at the desk called out "Sorry for the inconvienience!" Real nice!!!!!! HORRIBLE! DON'T STAY HERE! If you want a nice hotel stay at the Staybridge Suites in Lone Tree or Cherry Creek! They are wonderful!

name: Residence Inn Denver Downtown
title: “I will never stay here again...”
text: Terrible experience. The room was FILTHY! There were dead bugs on all the window sills, the room hadn't been properly dusted in months. There were two inches of dust, popcorn kernels, and garbage in the air conditioning vents. The bathtub wouldn't drain. We contacted the front desk about the filth and when nothing was resolved by the next day, we notified them again. We were then directed to the manager Marcus and he blew us off. He told us, "It can't be that bad." The garbage from housekeeping sat in the courtyard area for two days before it was picked up. This is an old facility. It needs some serious renovating. I have stayed at hotels that have a bigger hot tub than the swimming pool was there. I will have to say the breakfast was excellent as well as the complimentary shuttle downtown. I cannot recommend this facility at all. We ended up across the street at a Hampton Inn. Cheaper and brand new.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Denver - Aurora
title: “Für so viel geld könnte der Service besser sein”
text: Die Embassy Suites in Denver sind ein großes modernes Hotel in der Nähe des Flughafens. Die Zimmer sind alle rund um eine Art Innenhof angeordnet, was das Haus etwas hellhörig macht. Das Personal war recht freundlich, aber man bekommt keinen 4 Sterne Service. Die Zimmer sind recht groß und bieten einen gewissen Komfort. Es handelt sich um Suites mit kleiner Küche/Wohnbereich und einem separaten Schlafraum. Als wir am Ende zu hause unsere Kreditkartenabrechnung checken, hatten wir nur leider für das Zimmer zwei mal bezahlt, und hatten erst Mühen das Geld wieder zu bekommen, weil wir angeblich ein paar Dinge im Zimmer gelassen haben und sie dachten, dass wir wieder kommen, wir hatten aber ausgecheckt. So was geht meiner Meinung nach nicht in einem Hotel der Hilton Gruppe.

name: Quality Inn & Suites Denver International Airport
title: “Très bon rapport qualité prix”
text:
Nous sommes arrivés à l'aéroport de Denver le soir et nous y avons séjourné une nuit avant de partir vers les Rockies. L'accueil est bien. Les chambres sont confortables, spacieuses, et propres. Petit souci d'insonorisation mais bon cela reste acceptable. Le petit déjeuner est correct mais difficile pour nous européens. C'est un petit déjeuner simple, typiquement américain (oeufs, hamburgers, bacon, céreales, bagels, donuts, gaufres...) mais nous n'avons pas mal mangé. 
En conclusion 62 euros pour un nuit petit déjeuner compris reste vraiment intéressant !!! A recommander !!!

name: Pier 5 Hotel
title: “Very nice staff, enjoyed the hotel”
text:
We really enjoyed our stay here. I was nervous after reading some reviews that said the hotel was in disrepair, etc. but we were pleasantly surprised.
I booked a one night wine package over the phone with the hotel. After I called I saw on their website that there was a promotion for a $25 gas card if you booked a package. The agent added it to my res. I also inquired about free parking for harbor magic members (I joined online) and she said I could not get that b/c I was getting the gas card. I said fine but when we checked in I asked again regarding free parking and the front desk agent gave it to us happily, they also gave us the gas card and a $50 voucher toward our next stay. We were upgraded to a suite b/c the hotel was sold out. Room was very nice, walls are thin so you hear a lot of doors slamming but that was just in the morning. A/C was also rather loud but not awful. 
Great location, didn't have to take the car out at all and had a really nice dinner at Sabatinos in Little Italy. 
I'd go back to Pier 5 again, staff was really nice.

name: Hampton Inn Baltimore-Downtown-Convention Center
title: “Had a Great Stay at the Hampton”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at this hotel last weekend and had a fabulous experience. We were attending an event at the Geppi Museum and booked the hotel rather than driving back to DC that night. It was well worth the excursion. The room was large and very comfortable. We had plenty of room to both get ready for the formal affair and relax after. The staff were courteous. The pool, while smallish, was clean, refreshing, and uncrowded- the first night we had the area to ourselves with just the lifeguard (very polite and helpful). Breakfast was more than substantial, as always with Hampton, and they had many options. The decor is very modern and new, not at all what we had expected and a very pleasant surprise. While we did not have much of a view at all, the room still had plenty of natural light, easily blocked out with the black-out drapes. The hotel is also very convenient to Pickles and other traditional sports bars in downtown. Every part of our stay was wonderful and we will certainly go back for a casual retreat.

name: Super 8 Denver - Airport
title: “Kind of just 'ok'”
text: We were given perhaps the largest hotel room ever on the ground floor. Initial response was 'wow'. Huge room, bed and jet bathtub (in the bedroom, not the bathroom). On closer inspection though I was a little disappointed with the quality of the room. The carpet was ripped and where the tiles around the bathtub were cracked, they'd added pieces of carpet over the corner. I have no major complaints, I just wasn't wowed by it. It was generally quite clean, but could do with a bit of an update. It's in a remote place with a group of other hotels and the dining choices are limited. We tried to eat in diner/bar place which appeared to be closed permanently across the road. We ended up in a Village Inn which was adequate because it was across the road, but not our first choice for great dining. The breakfast was ok - standard Holiday Inn. The staff were friendly and efficient. There was a self service shop with basic goods and snacks which was very useful and the shuttle to the airport was timely and efficient.

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “One of our best stays EVER !!”
text: Lets start with the only negative of the whole weekend, we tried to eat late Friday night at the Solas irish Pub and after 20 minutes of sitting at a table, never saw a waiter or was even acknowledged by a staff member, so we got up left (again no acknowledgement) and walked across the lobby to City Table and had a wonderful time. other than that, this may be the best place we have ever stayed ( and we travel ALOT), every and I do mean EVERY employee here wants nothing more than to serve you in the best way possible. No request is too much and all the little touches are unbelievable, from the staff at the door to greet you ,to leaving a hand written birthday note and bottle of wine for my wife's birthday, to the poor gentleman that came to our room twice to help us with our fireplace fire, everyone had a smile on and seemed generally happy to be working here. The rooms are a perfect mix of century old luxury and modern day innovation. While the bathrooms are on the small side, i will totally accept that for the GIANT corner fireplace room we had !! Two employees need to be singled out Christine the bartender at City Table (see seperate review) and Nina at the conceirge desk, no request was to great for Nina, she will go way, way out of her way to help you. I can honestly say we will NEVER stay anywhere else while in Boston. thank you to all the staff for making my wife's birthday so special.

name: Royal Sonesta Harbor Court Baltimore
title: “Some good to say, but more bad”
text:
Stayed at this hotel overnight for an Orioles game. We had a courtyard room and though the decor was a bit dark and tired (needs updating), the room itself was nicely sized and so was the bathroom. On arrival one light in the bathroom was out.
This hotel looks as though it needs a thorough cleaning. Nearly every door on our floor was severely marred on the bottom one foot from shoes, carts or whatever. Looked horrible. Stains on the curtains in our room also.
Breakfast was good, but when they ask if you want coffee and juice, be careful -- the small glass of juice cost $4.50! The restaurant used for breakfast also needed some deep cleaning. We sat next to the windows - unfortunately we had to look at the air vents at the bottom of the windows and they were totally littered with dust, small dirt and other stuff. Just did not look clean and made you wonder how clean the other places were that were out of public view. Small hair found underneath the scrambled eggs after my wife ate half of them. The hotel took off the cost of the meal, as they should have.
I would not recommend this hotel -- there are too many others that are newer, cleaner and doing a better job. The owners need to invest in this hotel if they want to keep up -- needs updating and cleaning.

name: Royal Sonesta Harbor Court Baltimore
title: “Above and beyond”
text:
This hotel has the best view of the inner harbor one can find. The minute you walk into the hotel you can tell this is a special place. 
I was assigned an upgraded view room due to my platinum status. I must of by luck been assigned the one room that was not up to par (some issues). Without asking I was moved to a huge mini suite and the room I left was placed out of order. Once you walk in and see this hotel you will know my experience with a sup par room was not the norm. When in baltimore stay here, 
especially on weekends when it cost a few bucks more than the Holiday Inn.

name: Embassy Suites Denver-International Airport
title: “Comfortable and Convenient Stay”
text: My husband and I stayed at this convenient Embassy Suites after our late afternoon flight before heading for the mountains the following day. Every aspect of this hotel met our needs and expectations. After a quick dinner at the nearby Ruby Tuesday's, we settled into our very comfortable room with a great view of the lights of Denver. The free breakfast the next morning included our favorite custom omelettes with many other selections available. Our stay here was the perfect beginning to a wonderful vacation week in Colorado.

name: Doubletree by Hilton Hotel Denver
title: “Wonderful big rooms”
text: great big rooms at a low price. Large hotel. Great pool. Nice balconies.

name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers
title: “Absolutely the worst!!!!”
text: I blocked a set of rooms, about 16 in all, for an event in the city and I am terribly embarassed that I subjected my guests to this horribly maintained hotel. Don't be mislead by its exterior and lobby: the halls and rooms are filthy, extremely dusty, rooms are small, toilets backed up - 2 of my guest required plumbing help at 2 in the morning, service is slow, doors don't work- 1 guest was locked in the room and could not get out, bathroom fixtures fell on another guest, holes in walls, etc...I can go on and on. It should be sued for misrepresentation and false advertisement as a 4 star hotel. There are a lot of other hotel in Boston at the same price that is much better maintained.

name: The Westin Denver Downtown
title: “Nickel & Diming”
text:
$10 per day for WiFi in your room, $1.50 for a local 30 second telephone call, $60 for regular bacon & egg room service breakfast for two. $13 for a Manahattan. Poor selection of TV channels unless you want to pay extra.
We booked our room through Hotwire (which probably indicates that they are struggling) and we were reminded by the staff of this on several occasions - should you expect less service when you book through Hotwire?
Visitors to Denver should know that the cost of getting from the airport to Downtown is close to $100 so booking a hotel with a free shuttle is definitely a plus - Westin doesn't provide any help in this respect.
On the plus side the Hotel does give you the option of opting out of housekeeping in return for a $5 voucher which is a good green gesture though I'm sure the value of not having to launder towels, make beds and vacuum exceeds $5 to Westin.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Denver Tech Center
title: “Great rooms”
text: The room I stayed in had a full kitchen which was perfect for a long stay. The full fridge and microwave came were useful specially if you would like to have a cup of tea in the comfort of your room. The staff were attentive and very nice. There are plenty of resturants and coffee shops within walking distance.

name: The Curtis
title: “Interesting and fun, but better options are out there”
text:
I had a 1 night stay-over in Denver so figured I would try the Curtis hotel. I had read mixed reviews so wanted to give it a try for myself. Here's the breakdown:
Pros:
- Interesting, modern decor (each floor has a different theme)
- Location
- Service - best I've had in Denver!
- Breakfast buffet - also hard to beat for hotels at this level...service at breakfast was also stellar
- Gym - quite large and plenty of options for working out
- Parking - a bit pricy, but they do have parking, which is hard to come by downtown
- Bar scene - VERY vibrant, modern and with lots of options
- Accepts gov't rate
Cons:
- Rooms were small...especially the bathrooms
- A bit noisy...mainly from the hallways
Although I laid out many more pros then cons, these cons are significant. Being I was just overnighting in Denver, it wasn't that bad. But had I stayed here for a longer business or pleasure trip, these cons would have grown more troublesome. All in all, not a bad place and well worth staying for fun, but I would go elsewhere for longer stays (i.e. Embassy Suites Downtown or the Four Seasons)

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Denver Downtown
title: “good location”
text: We stayed for just one night after a trip in to the rockies,it was a good choice in a good location.It was a clean large room, and the pool and spa were very welcome after a long drive! We walked into and back from mall street and felt very safe. We would definitely stay here again.

name: Hyatt Regency Denver Tech Center
title: “Away from it..”
text:
I have stayed at the Hyatt DTC several times. I have enjoyed it to the local attractions. There is also the Bellevue Train Station if you wish to ride the light-rail to the attractions such as the 16th St. Mall or the Pepsi Center and Coors Field. You could walk to the station, but it is about a 2 mile walk. 
The staff at the hotel are very pleasant. The only issue I had was in regards to the size of the beds. This last time, I took my family of 4 - 2 kids aged 5 and 10. The beds were full size and rather small to comfortably sleep 1 adult and 1 child. I called for a cot and they said they could only provide a cot in rooms with the king size bed due to fire code. This didn't make a whole lot of sense considering the room with the 2 beds was larger than the room with the king sized bed.
We were charged $5.00 for parking which I consider very reasonable. 
The pool is chock full of kids and very noisy. It is not a place where adults can relax. Just keep this in mind.
The sports bar on the 2nd level is okay. It was an okay place to get an afternoon bite to eat or an evening cocktail, but nothing to write home about.
If you don't mind being away from the hustle and bustle of the city and driving to reach the attractions, then you will be okay staying here. If you like the feel of being in the middle of it all, then I would suggest staying downtown. The other nice thing about the Hyatt DTC is that during the weekend the streets around the area are practically deserted due to it being a business area. Also, there is wonderful breakfast dining at The Original Pancake House which is within walking distance.

name: Embassy Suites Denver-International Airport
title: “Embassy Suites has Our Attention”
text: Recently stayed here through a friend's reward points due to a flight cancellation. Rewards were honored no problem and service and hospitality was top notch. We managed to arrive at the end of the Manager's Reception and the bartender was very attentive. Cooked-to-Order omelets was great. Needless to say we'll be looking into Embassy Suites for our future travel stays.

name: The Curtis
title: “Trying to be groovey and hitting the mark for the most part.”
text: I was attending a long conference at the Convention Center and stayed six nights at the Curtis. Architecturally boring building sauced up by some whimsical touches inside and a front desk and bell staff that bends over backward for guests. Whimsy continues onto guest floors and luckily stays in the halls. The king corner room I had on the dancing floor (each floor themed) was large and light, good bed, bath on the small side, no closet - just a small armoire. Three star view. The housekeeper could have used a swifter - I ended up dusting on day three. HVAC was great. Water was perfect temps always. Amazing location for visitors to downtown Denver. Honestly, I was excited to stay at a Hipster hotel and was a tad disappointed by the hype vs. reality. Not at all the higher end feel of other Doubletree boutiques, like in Chicago. Restaurant was great and room service prompt, friendly, and yummy. Pass on the crab cake Benedict. Not good.

name: Fairfield Inn Denver Airport
title: “This is an excellent Fairfield Inn; I would return”
text: I was here for a short overnight to catch an early flight from DEN the next morning. The room was very clean, very well appointed, and a notch above the Fairfields I've stayed at before. The staff were extremely friendly and helpful, arranging two shuttles, giving advice on which to take, and specially going out of their way the next early morning to get me and the other shuttle riders a hot cup of coffee at 330 am. And the hotel was under the limit of my hotel allowance!

name: Baymont Inn and Suites Denver International Airport
title: “nice stay”
text:
Very nice girl@front desk 10/24/12@ 3pm
nice shuttle driver good location always stay there on way to airport

name: Grand Hyatt Denver Downtown
title: “Factor in cost of expensive parking if you book this hotel.”
text: This hotel is overpriced. Not to mention the valet is $28/day & the only other parking options are no less than $10/day. I think hotels should have free parking for guests, not so at the Grand Hyatt Denver. The pool was cold, kids were dissapointed they couldn't swim. The restaurand had a tasty breakfast, and our server was very friendly, so that was nice. One block from 16th street mall, also nice. Hotel Bartender seemed annoyed when we ordered drinks (I think she was closing down, but it was only 10pm on a Friday night...). Won't stay @ this hotel again. Not sure what makes it a four star hotel.

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “Wonderful”
text: A real gem and a very relaxing hotel to stay at with a welcoming fire in the lobby, I wish more hotels were like this. Traditional elegant décor, excellent friendly and professional staff. I will definitely stay here again when visiting Boston.

name: The Curtis
title: “The Curtis is an amazing place to host a wedding reception!”
text: Me and my husband were married on Sept. 1 and hosted our reception at the Curtis. Sarah Morris, their wedding coordinator, helped us every step of the way – even during the reception itself. Coming from a customer service background, we were very impressed with the attention we received. Everyone who attended our wedding keeps telling us how much fun they had – the Curtis is amazing!

name: Hilton Garden Inn Denver Cherry Creek
title: “Nice contemporary style property”
text: We stayed at this property on our way home from the mountains back to KC. Another great Hilton property. This hotel had beautiful contemporary rooms and very comfortable beds. Although there is construction going on we were very pleased with the valet service offered to mitigate any inconvenience. The pool is a bit small but the fitness room was nice and I imagine for the typical business traveler the pool would be satisfactory.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Denver Cherry Creek
title: “Coughlin / Katers Wedding”
text:
My son's wedding was June 15, 2012. Hotel was Amazing!!!! Elegant, classy, and just absolutely magnificent! All our guests for the wedding were very impressed. Service was excellent and the morning buffet was something to see, so impressive! Dan at the frontdesk was a hoot. Loved his sense of humor and his professionalism. He made the experience there comfortable. Can't say enough. So happy for my son and his wife that they picked this hotel for their guests to stay at. Just a lovely experience had by all. Also thank you to Mike for his help in scheduling this event and putting up with me, the groom's mom. 
Huge Thank You!
Nancy Katers
Green Bay, WI

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Great!!!”
text:
Recently had a few days at the Omni and it was wonderful. We'd booked a European room with an online deal that meant it was only $66 a night. 
The bed was comfortable with plenty of pillows, and after a long flight (and going from freezing temperatures in the UK to 23C in Boston in November!) the shower and air con were more than wonderful. 
Location-wise it was ideal and the bar served the strongest gin and tonic I've ever had! Despite being young and a bit scruffy the staff treated us with the utmost courtesy and were nothing but helpful. I'd be back like a shot and have already told friends and family about it.

name: Grand Hyatt Denver Downtown
title: “Pleasant, clean, safe”
text:
Stayed 3 nights and enjoyed it. Front desk and concierge staff were excellent, friendly and helpful. Room was great, large, clean and nice bed.
The only complaint was the $9.99 for wireless....

name: Embassy Suites Denver-International Airport
title: “Clean, spacious rooms perfect for family with kids.”
text:
We needed a fridge for our baby's milk bottles and a microwave to heat them and they had this in a clean, modern kitchenette counter area. My 10 yr. old loved having two rooms and the view out the inside window to the hallway and atrium.
We requested a crib in the room which we had to call and remind staff but then the crib was delivered w/in 5 minutes. We had a rental car so we didn't have to worry about shuttles. Check in was quick and staff was courteous. We ate supper at one of the restaurants located around the corner and had the FREE breakfast buffet downstairs in the morning. Great food and lots of it. Perfect selection for adults and little children.
Swam in the pool twice. Wish it was warmer, but it was clean and the setting was nice.
We loved being able to cozy up on the couch and watch a Christmas movie while the baby went to bed before the rest of us.
OH, and we viewed a beautiful sunset out the bedroom window.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Denver-Speer Boulevard
title: “Good stay”
text: We stayed here for the Denver Broncos game. The room was clean, had a suite and it was very quiet being on the second floor and completely full. The beds were very comfortable. It was also very close to the stadium, about a 15min walk if you take the fenced walk way near the freeway. (safe, beautiful walk at night with the lighted skyline) We did not try the breakfast since we were meeting up with family, but it smelt wonderful and the coffee was yummy. I would stay here again, very nice experience.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Denver-Speer Boulevard
title: “Family Vacation”
text: We stayed here during our recent family vacation to Denver. It was in a good location, easy access to the Interstate and close to the Bronco stadium. I felt the room was very nice and clean. The free breakfast in the morning was good but typical. My daughters felt the beds were uncomfortable but I didn't mind them. My only complaints would be the parking is poor. Very limited unless you want to park up the hill in a seperate location. Also, the swimming pool is in the basement. Very dismal and "spooky" as my daughter called it so she chose not to swim which is usually what she looks forward to. However, I felt the price was reasonable and the decor was new so I wouldn't mind staying here again.

name: The Westin Denver Downtown
title: “Great loacation, comfortable hotel”
text:
I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone. The service from the moment we checked in, until we left was superb! The room was very large and the beds were extremely comfortable. I had my best sleep in years. We were a little bit worried when we saw that our room was right across from the elevator, but the noise level was very low. I know this sounds crazy, but the curtains in the room were fantastic! They were the kind that kept the light out, so even at like 9am in the morning it still looked like it was the middle of the night in the room. 
The pool area was very nice, it was a bit crowded in the afternoon, they ran out of chairs, so we had to put our towels on the ground. It was a very hot day, so there was a very pleasant hotel staffer that walked around every fifteen minutes or so and gave us water, and kept coming around and refilling our water and making sure that we had ice. The view from the pool deck was nice, you could see the mountains. 
The hotel was in a great location and was close to great restaurants and the capital building and very close to Coors Field, which we went to one night to watch our beloved Cubbies. 
If I had any complaints and these are very minor, it would be that the hotel bar was only open until midnight and that the Starbucks on the lower level was very small and didn't carry alot of pastries. There was a Starbucks about a block away near the 16th St Mall which was bigger and carried a lot more things, so we ended up going there instead. 
Also in the business center, the internet was not free, which was not a big deal, but it would have been nice to have free internet access. 
All in all, a very pleasant experience!

name: Baymont Inn and Suites Denver International Airport
title: “Handy for the Airport and Denver”
text: Stayed here as both the first and last hotel on a 3 week trip. A good hotel - reasonably priced with everything you need in an airport hotel. The room was spacious and comfortable. The swimming pool was good - although a little cold. The hotel is convenient for several near by restaurants. What's not to like? The only downside the hotel shuttle didn't display its name - it was showing only The Quality Inn so we waited longer than we needed to.

name: Baltimore Marriott Waterfront
title: “Good performer, but generic in feel and operation”
text: We usually stay at old-world grand dame hotels, so this recent addition to the inner harbor was a departure for us. We stayed for a weekend during the Grand Prix event. Food is plain and unremarkable. Lobby and public areas are generic Marriott style. The same carpet and bland gift shop you see in all the others. The view is wonderful. This is probably the most expensive place in town, but is really a good, bland business hotel.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Denver Airport DIA
title: “Convenient airport stay”
text:
We found this hotel very convenient, clean, and comfortable. We needed to print boarding passes and the hotel staff were helpful in pointing out the best computer to use for that purpose. It is located across the street from a decent restaurant and, of course, close to the airport for an early morning departure. 
Mary from California

name: Baymont Inn and Suites Denver International Airport
title: “Pleasant and enjoyable airport hotel convenience”
text: Great location for airport convenience! It was a nice relaxing place after a long day of travel and business. Restaurants in walking distance with the mountains on the horizon to enjoy on your walk.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Denver-Speer Boulevard
title: “The best hotel of our three week holiday”
text:
This is by far the best hotel of our three week holiday in Wyoming, Montana and Colorado, the room is spacious and the beds are so comfortable, the breakfast is different every day and lots to choose from, but best thing of all is the staff they couldn't be more helpful.
I would recommend this hotel to everyone.

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “attentive, thoughtful service”
text:
One might wonder how I could write a review of a hotel I have not yet arrived at... I am writing this early, pre-stay review in response to service received a week prior to my visit that is totally and completely in keeping with all of the accolades this hotel has received (and as I now know, deserved).
I sent a quick e-mail to the Chief Concierge, Keith Loveless in advance of our stay since our son has some medical issues that require a little extra help / attention (refrigeration for meds, storage for wheelchair, etc.). "LoveLESS" is the wrong name for this guy because he's shown us nothing but!!
His thoughtful attention to our issues leaves me looking even more forward to our little getaway and stay at The Lenox Hotel.
Post visit review to follow....
-Jen Portnoy
www.hopeforjavier.org

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Denver-Speer Boulevard
title: “Enjoyed the stay”
text: My second stay & I booked this hotel for a five day business trip to downtown Denver. The hotel is new & the staff is very friendly. My room was very nice & quiet with great beds. I liked the free parking. There were two elevators & for a small hotel this was wonderful. No wait for the elevator. The service was of a personal touch & I saw the same faces every day at the desk which was nice. This hotel is going to be my choice for all future stays in Denver downtown.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Denver Airport DIA
title: “Nice place near the airport”
text:
Our second stay here. Clean and comfortable. It's a high volume hotel near the airport, so it shows a little wear and tear, but it's clean and comfortable, and reasonably priced.
Front desk is efficient and pleasant. They have a computer and printer you can print your boarding passes on in the lobby. Breakfast layout in the morning is nothing special but you can grab a bite before you fly and not have to hunt something down in the airport.

name: The Brown Palace Hotel and Spa
title: “This hotel just gets better and better”
text:
We have lived in the Denver area all of our lives and over the years we have spent occasional nights at the Brown Palace for special occasions such as New Years Eve, birthdays, anniversaries 
This latest stay was by far the very best of all!!
The room was one of the nicest yet. Quiet, spacious, and very well decorated!
The art work on the walls was very interesting and tasteful. The bed was sooooo comfortable
Brunch in the hotel the next morning was by far the best brunch I have ever had. Make reservations early since they book up quickly 
I would give this hotel a double thumbs up

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “Beautiful Hotel, great service”
text: My teenage daughter and I stayed at the Lenox for 4 nights while visiting Boston. We initally were placed in a small room with a King size bed in the back of the hotel but were moved to a much nicer and larger room with double beds and a view upon request. The room was older but elegant with a chandelier and nice amenities as well as view. The staff were exceptional - with a personal touch. They answered all questions and greeted you upon arrival and departure from the lobby; the concierge was also helpful. The location was very nice, just one block away from all the shops on Newburry street and within walking distance of many restaurants and sights to see. Out of five hotels we stayed at on our travels this summer, the Lenox was defintely the nicest. We also got a good price through booking during an advertised special on Travelzoo; the staff still treated us with the same courtesy as all the other guests.

name: Staybridge Suites Denver International Airport
title: “Nothing Impressive”
text:
While my recent stay was okay...it seemed to be run of the mill Staybridge. Nothing to brag about...
That's too bad, because I did have a complaint. The wireless service was terrible. Slow and unresponsive. I know I wasn't the only person to complain. I heard other guest with similar issues.
This is really too bad. It can make or break a stay when you are on business.

name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Denver Gateway Park
title: “Clean”
text: This was a very clean hotel only being 7 months old. It was a bit scarey as of the part of town it is in. A bit uncomfortable for a single female. Rooms were very clean cold from all the tile. Value is exactly what you pay for. Down side as I was leaving the next morning one of the cleaning gals was moping/sweeping the front entry way, the water quickly turned to ice, which made it tricky walking outside of the hotel to your car. A bit scarey.

name: The Westin Denver Downtown
title: “Very Nice”
text:
Stayed one night in July after a backpacking trip.
Overall an excellent property. Very clean, bed was super-comfy, room was spacious and pleasant. Bathrooms and products therein very good. Staff were friendly and accomodating.
The price was a bit high I thought, and the doors could use a bit more soundproofing (or maybe just fit better). But those are my only complaints, and neither are big ones.
Highly recommended.

name: Grand Hyatt Denver Downtown
title: “Great hotel.”
text: Beautiful, convenient to the happenings of downtown Denver. right near the 16th street mall. Several great restaurants nearby. Would highly recommend Marlowe's. Awesome grilled pear salad! Just an all around classy hotel.

name: Omni Parker House
title: “Hotel con encanto”
text: Hotel histórico, bonito, no defrauda, salvo las habitaciones que son algo estrechas

name: Hyatt Regency Denver At Colorado Convention Center
title: “Right in the heart of old downtown”
text: Big beautiful lobby, very much a convention type hotel. Multiple bars and restaurant /coffee shop in the lobby. Striking vibrant art. Rooms are very sterile and boringly conventional. Nice toiletries.

name: The Westin Denver Downtown
title: “Great Room”
text: The room was awesome. Very tastefully decorated. Only stayed for one night and was perfect location to walk to Coors Field. Only drawback was the price of parking. I was under the impression that parking was included....if so, I had no proof of that. Parking attendant wouldn't let me exit until I paid $13 !!

name: Hilton Garden Inn Denver Downtown
title: “Great Mile High Stay!”
text: This is overdue, but a well deserved rating of a great downtown Denver hotel. Stayed here over Christmas, visiting family for the holidays. We were lucky enough to get a 12th floor room with a great view, overlooking the Convention Center, with Invesco Field in the near distance, and the mountains in the far distance. The staff was great, from the moment we checked in right through check out. A minor phone problem on Christmas Day was quickly resolved (10 minutes), otherwise a flwaless stay. Nice pool, fitness center, and restaurant... easy walking distance (2 blocks) to the 16th Street Mall, and very easy access to I-25 and local sites. Booked online at a terrific rate ($94 / night). Valet parking is not cheap (was $26, going up to $28 on 1/2/11 I think), but either you take you chances at a remote lot or risk getting a ticket / towed (downtown parking restrictions starting Sunday nights through Friday nights)...it did give some peace of mind and we never waited more than 2 minutes for our car. If you want a downtown spot that is clean, reasonable (if you rate-shop), and offers a great staff, look no further. Would DEFINITELY stay here again. Thanks HGI, you guys rock!

name: Grand Hyatt Denver Downtown
title: “Great Location”
text:
We booked this room on Priceline through "name your own price", so we had no clue what hotel we would end up at. Overall we were very pleased with the Grand Hyatt. It is a very snazzy hotel, VERY clean, comfy beds, great bathroom, and awesome views. Although we didn't use them, we checked out the fitness room and pool area. They seemed really nice-although the outdoor hottub was out of order. I find it amusing and irritating that at plush hotels you have to pay for so many extras. They do not have free wi-fi, you have to purchase it for $9.99 a day. Valet parking is $26 a day, otherwise you can use the parking garage that is attached to the building, but be prepared to pay at least $7 every time you come and go. We are from a smaller city so we are not used to haivng to pay to park. The location is perfect for wandering around downtown. It's within walking distance of the 16th Street Mall, many restaurants and bars, and several other attractions. 
Overall this hotel gets a thumbs up, I'm just glad I booked through priceline and only paid about $70 a night (plus parking and internet)!

name: Hotel Monaco Denver - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Can't wait to go back”
text: Had a wonderful romantic evening. Hotel Monaco exceeded our expectations, from the accomodations to the Aveda Spa, the weekend. It was fantastic. Can't wait to return.

name: The Oxford Hotel
title: “Immaculate and friendly!”
text: From check in to check out - the Oxford staff made me feel welcome. Service was top notch - especially being dropped off at the convention center every morning. The room was absolutely immaculate upon my return each evening. I very highly recommend The Oxford as a cozy and personable alternative to the "big" hotels in Denver.

name: Hyatt Regency Denver At Colorado Convention Center
title: “Great hotel!”
text: We stayed here for two nights. Great location as you can walk to all the great touristy things. Very clean and welcoming room! Extremely friendly staff. Would definitely stay here again. Elegant, trendy, and sophisticated hotel for both business guests and leisure travelers.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Denver Downtown
title: “Clean, friendly and still new”
text:
I stayed at Hilton Garden Inn Downtown Denver for one night on my way to the Rocky Mountains National Park. Everyone from the valet parking staff to the janitors was really friendly and accommodating. I was allowed an early check-in, which was nice after a 10-hour flight.
The room was clean and still pretty much in a new condition. The bathroom was spotless. Not much of a view (my room was overlooking the Hyatt parking carage), but I wasn't there for the view anyway.
The working desk was good-sized and the ergonomic chair was just great. I tend to do lots of post-processing for photos in hotels, and I really hate it when they give you tiny desks with terrible chairs. None of those problems here. I also liked the room equipment: HD flat-screen TV and iPod-ready alarm clock.
In-room safe would be a nice addition, though. I didn't feel comfortable leaving my laptops etc. to the room when popping out for a moment, but didn't feel like going through the hassle to check the stuff to the front desk safe, as I was going to be out only for about 30 minutes or so.
Having to use the valet parking ($25 + tip) is a bit irritating, but I guess that's what you have to do in downtown locations.
If I need a place to stay in downtown Denver again, I'll most likely return here.

name: Baymont Inn and Suites Denver International Airport
title: “Perfect place for easy access to the airport”
text: I arrived in Denver a day early for a ski trip. The complimentary shuttle was reliable and the hotel was clean. The room was as good as advertised and the bed was super comfortable. The staff was very accommodating and the woman who checked me in asked my preference about a first floor room or higher. The continental breakfast was decent and the waffle maker was a nice touch. I would definitely stay there again if the opportunity arose.

name: Warwick Denver Hotel
title: “Room was nice; paying for internet is ridiculous”
text: The room was very nice and very large. Almost every amenity was included -- except of course Internet which is still considered non-essential by "nice" hotels. This is extremely annoying. Another annoying thing was that I was forced to wait over 20 minutes to check-in because of some complicated situation with the previous guest and the fact that the other was "in training" and so could not lift a finger. An apology was given, but it was perfunctory and given while the clerk typed.

name: Baymont Inn and Suites Denver International Airport
title: “Stay and park for the airport”
text: I stayed one night before I caught a plane the next morning for an 18 day trip. Check in was fast, the room was pleasant and everything in working order. Breakfast was okay with quite a few different choices including eggs and bacon, fruit, cereals, and breads. I planned to leave my car for the duration of my trip and thought I would have to pay extra because I would be gone more that 2 weeks. I was pleasantly surprised when I was not charged for those extra days. The shuttle was a little late leaving for the airport and when I arrived back in Denver, I called in and had to wait about 20-25 minutes for the pick-up but they told me to stay inside and just go out after 20 minutes. The driver came exactly when expected and my car was just as I left it 18 days earlier.

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “cheap and old”
text: yes location is perfefct however the hotel is old, floors look like an hospital ward!! Bathroomss really old and in need of urgent renovation. We had a corner room, fireplace could not be lit. Clean was not spotless. Receptionist are really unfriendly however the concierge was excellent. There is no lobby. Never again!

name: Baymont Inn and Suites Denver International Airport
title: “Perfect location to airport”
text:
Perfect location when need a place close to the airport. We stayed there after flying into Denver and visiting Boulder for a day before traveling further around in Colorado.
Nice breakfast and clean room.

name: Grand Hyatt Denver Downtown
title: “Im Herzen von Old Denver”
text:
Das Grand Hyatt (vormals Hyatt Regency) ist noch immer eine Klasse für sich. Das Hotel liegt im alten Downtown und bietet die Möglichkeit für eine Altstadterkundung zu Fuß, zu den weiter ntfernten Zielen ist es mit dem Auto auch jeweils nur ein paar Minuten.
Das Hotel verfügt über eine ausgezeichnetes restaurant und eine sehr angenehme Lounge.
Das Personal ist freundlich und hilfsbereit. Die Zimmer sind modern, aber bequem und geräumig.

name: The Curtis
title: “Fun, funky and very comfortable”
text:
My husband and I booked into The Curtis Hotel for 3 days using Hilton Honors points. This is not your usual Doubletree Hotel. The hotel is themed: 'pop culture' a mix from the mid to late 20th century. Each of the 16 floors are 'themed'. For example we were put on the 13th floor. As the elevator door opens, there is a recording of Jack Nicholson's voice 'here's Johnny' from his role in the movie 'The Shining'. A movie still of Jack Nicholson when he says that line is framed on the wall. Decorations on that floor are from the scary genre.
We had a king bed room in the corner of the building which offered two windows. One of the windows looked out on the mountains ringing Denver. Quite a view. The room was clean, spacious and very comfortable, with a small flat screen TV opposite the bed and a refrigerator.
A shout out to Lainey, one of the registration staff who was so very friendly, helpful and upbeat, as we found all the young staff to be. Our room included breakfast buffet in their restaurant 'The Office'. The buffet had a good selection of hot and cold breakfast foods. If it is not included in your room rate, it would be pricey, around $15.00+ per person.
The hotel is across the street from the Denver Performing Arts Complex, a block from the Convention Center, and two blocks from the 16th Street Mall. We found it a perfect location fro exploring Denver, a beautiful city.
We turned in our rental car when we arrived in Denver. Parking can be pricey, about $24+ a day in the garage adjacent to the hotel.

name: The Curtis
title: “Great location, service and atmosphere”
text: This was our second stay at the Curtis because we have found the service to be impeccable (from front desk and maid service to bell hops and parking attendants) and the location can't be beat. Additionally, the rooms are VERY CLEAN and the walls must be pretty thick because we weren't disturbed at all (and the hotel was fully booked). I love the decor at the Curtis, it's a fun atmosphere for vacation and I'm sure business travelers will appreciate a change of scenery from the typical "hotel room"

name: JW Marriott Denver Cherry Creek
title: “Great place to stay in good neighbourhood”
text: We stayed here as part of our road show and I must say that I really enjoyed it. The reception staff, bell hops and the constant presence at the front door was noticeable. Second Home Bar is amazingly popular and attracts a nice crowd. Beds very comfy and linen beautiful. We had a brief but great time

name: Baltimore Marriott Waterfront
title: “Beware of Valet Parking!”
text: This hotel is very good, right in the middle of everything so you do not have to move your car. As Platinum Mariott Members we've been to more than a few Mariotts this year and we chose valet parking because we felt there would be a certain degree of security and care for our new vehicle. Unfortunately, here it was not the case and it wasn't until we got home from our 5 day stay that we found a heavy ding in the rear passenger door - obviously from another vehicle's door having been slammed into ours. We also noticed that a better ink pen that we keep in the console was taken as well. (We never used our car during the stay so this was not a accident on our part.) We continued to store our car in valet and at $32 per day we expected better. Too bad....but we still enjoyed everything else this hotel had to offer and will certainly visit again - we just won't let them touch our car!

name: The Brown Palace Hotel and Spa
title: “Amazing experience!”
text: My husband and I always try to do something special and different for out anniversary. This is our 22nd anniversary and we chose the Brown Palace on the advice of a relative. We would not ususally chose an option like this, but were overwhelmed by the customer service, amazing attention to detail, fabulous original antique fixtures at every turn. I am not a history buff but thoroughly enjoyed the history at this landmark hotel. The staff is so friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable. For some reason I thought the experience would be pretentious, but I couldn't have been more WRONG. Just good old fashioned and sincere customer service. We will definitely spend more honeymoons here, and recommend the Brown Palace for anyone wanting to be pampered, spoiled and treated like the royalty that has graced its doors.

name: Magnolia Hotel Denver
title: “Very loud”
text: Poor design...very loud voices coming from valet area. Staff useless. Well, not useless, but ineffectual as they are guests having a smoke and perhaps another drink? So we were told. Happened more than once. Will not be back.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Denver Downtown
title: “great location”
text: We stayed at this hotel and had no problems. Good location, good bars, good food. Go to Biker Jims Gourmet sausage stand , he has raindeer, elk, rattlesnake sausage. Good stuff. Walking distance to Coors Field, all the local brewhouses. Very comfortable beds and rooms. Will stay here again when we go back.....and free coffee in Lobby...

name: Warwick Denver Hotel
title: “Wonderful Hotel, Great Restaurant, Friendly People”
text: My wife and I recently spent 4 days at the Warwick while we relaxed and took in the city of Denver. The location is an easy walk to the 16th Street Mall and access to all of downtown yet the hotel has an uptown feel. Lovely outside patio dining overlooks a park across the street. All of the staff were exceedingly friendly and helpful. We had several meals in the restaurant and they were outstanding. I never thought I cared much for bread pudding until I had it here. Fortunately, I had it the first day so I was able to order it twice more before we departed. Very nice fitness room. Good Value. The Warwick will be home for us when we visit Denver.

name: The Oxford Hotel
title: “Absolutely Love the Oxford”
text: I love to stay here when I travel through Denver. The rooms are marvelously appointed and service is impeccable. A town car will take you anywhere in the downtown area. Not for folks who like the modern or minimalist aesthetic.

name: Hotel Monaco Denver - a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Had a wonderful time!”
text: Stayed here with my wife celebrating a special getaway. We had a great time, staff was friendly and Panzaon was excellent. Also got a chance to meet their General Manager during wine hour. He told me about some local options to see and do beyond the usual tourist traps. Was a treat, felt like I was an insider. Apparently lots of the staff have some secret local recommendations, so be sure to ask.

name: Residence Inn Denver City Center
title: “Fantastic hotel with great customer service in Denver”
text: My husband raved about this hotel for our entire holiday. Our room had a partial view of the city and was clean with modern furnishings, and the kitchenette and full sized fridge was a lovely bonus. The hotel's outside hottub overlooked the streets below and was another plus for us. On our arrival, we were told our hotel package included both buffet-style dinner and breakfast with lots of variety, although I found some of the dishes a bit hit and miss. However, the selling point of this hotel was the service from all of the hotel staff we came into contact with - nothing was a drama and that really made our stay here memorable.

name: Warwick Denver Hotel
title: “Mostly great - until we were harrassed.”
text:
We met friends here for our annual weekend in Downtown Denver to relax and catch up together. i felt the service was incredible the moment we arrived. Our bellboy was very attentive - even checking the weather while we checked in as I asked if it was to snow or not. He also was wonderful enough to see we did not have a wine opener in our room (was in the locked mini-bar) so he got us one and ran it up to us. We stayed in a jr. suite and it was quite spacious and nice. 
Some weirdness after that though ----- housekeeping knocked on our door asking what we needed. nothing - we hadn't called. that was weird. 
We enjoyed a drink downstairs at Happy Hour and found the atmosphere fun. We had to go up to the bar to get some attention though ---- and then it was non-stop service. :)
We returned after dinner (at the Samba Room) to relax and visit with a bottle of wine. Security knocked on our door saying there was a complaint about our noise. um - what? we were sitting, no music, no tv - just talking. Told him we were NOT loud, they repeated they had received a complaint and left. Then a bit later the night manager came to the door, warning us it was our 2nd noise warning and another would require us to leave the hotel. We asked if she heard us while out in the hall and she refused to answer, just to say "I am not here to debate the noise level". she was very rude and talked to us like we were children. Even telling our friend, who answered the door in her robe and explained she is in the bed, falling asleep, while the other 3 of us were visiting. If she didn't find it loud - how could someone else? Our friend is currently fighting cancer with chemo treatments. the manager then told our friend she "could not talk to her like that, she was an employee." oy vey! what about the paying patron? The manager then pulled out some line that all registered guests have to be in their own rooms by 10 pm and non-registered guests must leave.
yeah --- ruined the whole night for us!
In fact we even switched to our room across the hall and with our TV on, we couldn't even hear it in the hallway. How did anyone hear anything? I am guessing thru the glass to the balcony or the vent.
Breakfast downstairs the next morning was nice and the same nice service we'd had before the night before in our room.
Our friends left that day while my husband and I stayed for another night. We had no complaints the rest of the weekend.
It is a tad farther from the rest of downtown, but easy enough to walk down to 16th street and catch the shuttle. Too seedy to walk back at night though, so we did cab it back.

name: Sheraton Denver Downtown Hotel
title: “Beautiful place to stay”
text: This was our first time staying at the Sheraton. The first room we were in was REALLY small. It was just one king bed and hardly any room to move. I called the front desk and asked to be changed to a bigger room as we had a toddler with our own pack and play. They sent someone up and we moved to a HUGE room on the other side (its a divided hotel) . The walk was a ways with our bags, but not a huge deal. The room was wonderful. We spent sometime in the hotel bar, the bartender was awesome. One thing though is I got charged 2 different prices for martinis, I called the front desk and they did revise that. I would definitely stay here again, very upscale and clean. Right on the 16th Street Mall.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Denver Downtown
title: “Good Hotel but not worth the price”
text:
I am spending my last of 3 nights at this property. I had originally been booked for 4 nights at a rate of $179/night, I had to change my arrival date by 1 day and I was stuck with some sort of Junior Suite at $289/night. I was annoyed as it was a huge price difference for one less night-Iwasn't adding nights. And I didn't need a 2 room suite for 1 person. So however, I need to rate my experience based on $289 a night.
I didn't use the sitting room at all, but there was a second bathroom off it which if I were with family would have been great. The king size bed was comfy and I like that the internet hookup was close to the bed so I could sit there and work rather than at the desk. 
Fresh chocolate chip cookies available each night at the front desk were nice, as was complimentary hot beverages each morning from 6am-10am.
Location as described by others was great. I loved being on the 16th Street Mall and went from one end to the other. I never felt unsafe as a woman alone and walked around in daylight and night. It is a very crowded area and many singles were around.
For the negatives, for nearly $300 per night I thought that the hotel info binder in the room should be clean and free of the previous guests food and candy debris (it was not). The coffee cups for the in room coffee maker were stained and chipped. The TV Cable lacked many channels that I consider basic-Bravo, Food Network, Comedy Central etc. 1 remote for 2 tvs (I didn't need two, but had I...), the tub had a broken drain cover so you had to adjust it to keep the tub from filling with water during your shower. As you can see all managable but you can't charge that price without fixing those things. Lastly, the hot tub and excercise room is being renovated but no word of that on their website. I found out after toting my workout clothes and swimsuit for no reason upon checkin. That was disappointing.

name: Sheraton Denver Downtown Hotel
title: “Consistently Good.”
text: I've stayed here on a number of occasions over the past eighteen months and have found the experience to be consistently satisfactory, despite the disruption from renovations. However, what really sets it apart is the genuine service culture among employees, consistently excellent in my experience, and adding a lot of character to the hotel. Now that the rooms have been returned to a good standard, it's a great place to stay if you want a downtown location.

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “Comfortable, well-appointed but small!”
text:
I stayed here for one night.  I definitely got one of the smaller standard rooms - the bathrom was shall, we say "European" sized - shower stall and there was virtually no counter space on the bathroom. But I got one of the smaller rooms.
 But the bed was comfortable and the service was professional.  The room was well appointed, with some modern conveniences - flat screen tv, Bose iPod dock and an alarm clock.  Good location to Back Bay, close to Newbury street shopping.  Overall, would definitely recommend, and it seems to be pretty good value for the money (even if it was on my employer's dime!).

name: JW Marriott Denver Cherry Creek
title: “Great relaxing get-away... Fun Hotel Bar!!!”
text: Went to Denver just to get away and enjoy "Restaurant Week" and it was great! Super-clean hotel with an excellent staff. Complimentary cocktails and appetizers in the Concierge Lounge is a HUGE plus, too. Mountain view is worth it, if you can get it... Easy walking distance to great restaurants like Houston's, Cherry Creek Grill, and Elway's makes it a great location. Plenty of shopping close by as well. We ate at "Second Home" in the hotel and really loved it... My wife forgot a tote bag in the closet with cash in the top of it, and it was promptly turned in to the front desk after check-out. We picked it up the next day with everything there.

name: Hyatt Regency Denver At Colorado Convention Center
title: “Beautiful hotel and great location”
text: I stayed here for a conference and received an upgrade to a suite when my room was not available upon arrival. The suite was truly spectacular, and I slept really well throughout my stay. I was able to run directly from the hotel to nearby parks safely and easily. A great stay.

name: Hyatt Regency Denver At Colorado Convention Center
title: “Just so so”
text: As a Hyatt hotel, I expected more than was offered. The lobby was nice and the rooms were just okay. I was surprised to see that no refrigrator was in the room. There was also no extra ammenities in the bathroom, such as shower cap, q-tips, etc. Just shampoo and cream rinse. I think I just expected more since it was a Hyatt and such a large hotel.

name: Magnolia Hotel Denver
title: “Perfect!!!”
text: Great!! Loved the unique yet updated feel of the hotel. Staff was friendly from valet service to showing us things to do around the city. Valet is totally worth it, can go in and out. Bed was great, bathtub big, we requested a nice view and got the top floor w a sweeping view. Loved the free beer and wine happy hour and milk and cookies were yummy as well. Wish they were warm or that they had a microwave to warm them in. They let us check in early which was awesome for us!!! Walked to Wykoop Brewery---FANTASTIC-- beer and food. Then walked to REI and back. They have a b-cycle program where you get a free bike or can pay for a day. I read the book in our room for tourist ideas, ended up doing some pretty cool things!

name: Four Seasons Hotel Denver
title: “Great Hotel”
text: This is a great hotel , it's in a nice area of downtown Denver, has a great view and the rooms are over the top great! When staying in Denver you most stay here! I can wait to stay again. I will be trying out the spa on my next visit.

name: Homewood Suites Denver International Airport
title: “... simply ... THANKS !”
text:
As a weekly business traveler I stay in many hotels in many classes in many brands - sometimes for several days and sometimes for extended stays. I feel compelled to write to say thanks for your truly genuine and gracious hospitalty. To all the staff a the Denver Homewood - thanks! At the risk of leaving someone out, Thanks Aaron, Abigail. Angie, Carlos, Margot, Krista, Melissa, The drivers, Room Attendants, the Food service staff, and Hector, who all consistantly strive to make mundane business travel a little more home-like in a clean, friendlyand safe facility. (Sorry if I left anyone out). From day one, they made me feel welcome. 
If you are staying in the Denver International Airport Area, my recommendation is the Homewood Suites. It is a tremendous Price/Value/Service stay. 
Warm regards,
Gerry M.

name: Hyatt Regency Denver At Colorado Convention Center
title: “Modern hotel with great amenities and a convenient location”
text:
We really enjoyed our stay at the Hyatt Regency. The lobby is impressive and there is a beautiful bar/restaurant on the 27th floor with amazing views of the mountains and city. We loved watching the sunset from up there. Our room was clean and modern. The doors are quite heavy though, so expect some slamming in the middle of the night or morning from other people. This is not the hotel's fault, however you may want to ask for a room away from the elevators or at end of hall to minimize it.
The location is perfect for exploring Denver. You are one block away from the 16th street mall, close to the Capitol buildings, and if you're after a Rockies Game or want to get to the LoDo area, it's a ten minute walk or you can hop on the free shuttle that is a block away and goes up and down the 16th street mall
We have stayed in a number of hotels in downtown Denver and this is our favorite so far.

name: The Westin Georgetown, Washington D.C.
title: “Great stay at the Westin!!”
text: Every year, my family makes our annual traditional Christmas trip to D.C. to shop in Georgetown, see the White House Christmas Tree, have dinner at the Old Ebbitt Grill and end up at the Downtown DC Holiday Market located on the sidewalk of F Street, NW between 7th and 9th Streets, in front of the Smithsonian American Art Museum and National Portrait Gallery. We try to stay at different hotels, mostly SPG properties. The Westin in our opinion rated as one of our top 2 stays over the past years. The location was great for everything we wanted to do. We drove our vehicle into DC and the GPS was accurate getting us to the hotel. Once at the hotel the 2 front doorman (Deenny & Amadou) could not have been any nicer helping us with our bags and joking around with our kids. They made you feel as if you were coming home. Once we unloaded we used self parking which was half a block away and was $34.00 USD for overnight parking (cheapest around the area). We have a Suburban which fit in the underground lot. Even better the elevator in the parking garage was connected to the hotel and puts you right in the lobby. When we checked in, the front desk staff especially Sloan, could not have been more pleasant and accommodating and were very expedient. The rooms were very clean, updated and spacious for all of us. We did not eat at the hotel or use the room service so I can't comment on that. The walk to Georgetown was a quick 7 minutes, .5 miles out the front door and directly down M Street where there was everything you could want from food to pharmacies. Getting over to the White House to see the tree and have dinner was a 10-15 minute cab ride at a cost between $10-12.00 USD. The Westin staff could not have been more accommadating, friendly and helpful. I would highly recommend staying there with the family and will return next year.

name: Hyatt Regency Denver At Colorado Convention Center
title: “excellent and centrally located too”
text: this hotel is of a high standard, the staff really do address you by name and thus it all feels so much more personal than you might expect from such a large hotel. The accommodation was of course clean and very comfortable - the large TV was great too. All the food we had was of good standard and value. the hotel was ideally situated near to the free downtown shuttle service so it was possible to get around really easily, its not too far from the airport and is covered by regular airport shuttle services.

name: Residence Inn Denver City Center
title: “Really enjoyed this hotel”
text:
Our suite was a complete apartment with full kitchen, separate living room and separate bedroom. The lavatory and bathe were also in a separate room. The dressing table and sink were off the bedroom. Ample closet space was across from the sink. Plenty of hangars. There is an iron and ironing board and hair dryer also. The bed was very comfortable and had an ample supply of pillows and the european type spread and cover. Two night stands with variable bright lights on two large end tables with three large drawers each. There is a large TV on a three drawer dresser in a corner of the bedroom. Nice big roomy room. Window looked out over the downtown.
The living room has a flat screen TV. business desk with executive chair and internet hookups. There is a fold out couch and an overstuffed sitting chair with a side table and a floor lamp. Enjoyed sitting comfortably and reading the paper,which was delivered daily, with a hot,fresh brewed cup of coffee.
The kitchen is set up for four persons with all the kitchen needs.
The entry is very attractive and all staff are very people friendly. We had two minor repair needs and they were both answered within minutes. Front desk is knowledgeable of the surrounding city.
The refrigerator supplys ice so there is no hunting the hallways.
Extra coffee and popcorn are available at the front desk. 
The included breakfast is equivalent to a buffett. There is fresh batter for waffles as well. The eating area is as large and comfortable as any restaurant .There are three large TVs going constanly which is a bit disconcerting since they are on different channels. There are two computers for guest usage. A gas burning fire place with huge overstuffed chair is another place to drink your coffee and read any of the three available papers.

name: Hyatt Regency Denver At Colorado Convention Center
title: “Very clean, comfortable room!!!”
text:
Overall, this hotel was great! From check-in to check-out, everyone was so friendly & courteous. The room was spacious, the bed was comfy, the bathroom was large and the shower had great water pressure. There were only two things we didn't like about the hotel. The pool was rather small & with a convention in town, it was difficult to find space to swim/relax in the tiny indoor pool without being splashed by a bunch of kids. The second was that the soap provided by the hotel smelled bad & reminded me of a portable potty. I had to go to Walgreen's and buy a bar of Dove soap because I couldn't stand bathing with the one provided. 
The hotel is in a great location with respect to the convention center (1 block away) and the 16th Street mall (1 block).

name: Rouge, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Cute hotel with good service in a decent location”
text:
I stayed at the hotel with my family for 3 days, and I really liked the hotel. To be honest, the hotel is nothing fancy, but it had everything that made our stay pleasant.
The rooms are pretty spacious and the beds comfortable, the staff is very friendly and always quick to help out in whichever way is needed, they have iHome devices to charge iPhones etc., a neat minibar with some exotic choices. You can pour free herbal tea/lemonade in the afternoons, and on some days even have a free wine tasting in the (small) lobby. There is a nice small hotel bar as well.
To be fair, some of the amenities offered aren't that exciting. The gym is in the basement and pretty bad as far as gym goes. It's tiny and besides a couple of treadmills only has a few free weights. The breakfast which is offered isn't particularly exciting either, but considering that you are so close to many coffee houses & restaurants this wasn't really a big concern. The bathrooms in the rooms are clean and work well, but are very tiny. This didn't bother me, but bothered my wife. My requirements for a bathroom are that it's clean and works, all of which applied.
