My wife has higher standards, I believe she is only satisfied if a bathroom has at least 800 square feet and a whirlpool :-).
So in summary it's not a Ritz Carlton, but for the price we got we felt that we got a good value and had a pleasant experience. And yes, there is a lot of red; the hotel used to be an apartment building from what I understand.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington, DC Downtown
title: “Conveniently located, reasonably priced hotel”
text:
I recently stayed overnight in the DC Hilton Garden Inn. I selected the hotel because it was well-located and less expensive than other hotels in the area. With that context, it very much met my expectations. 
My room, on the 11th floor, faced an interior space -- no view but fairly quiet for a room in the heart of the city. The location directly accross the street from the Metro was also a plus. The room was reasonably large, with a good size desk, firm king bed, good lighting, fast (and free) wifi, as well as a hard-wired internet connection on the desk, and multiple electrical outlets in the base of lamps on both the desk and night tables -- in other words, just about everything one needs on a business trip. The only negatives were that the HVAC fan was a bit noisy, the water pressure in the shower anemic, and the towels a bit skimpy; given the price point, however, none of this was out of the ordinary.

name: The Westin Georgetown, Washington D.C.
title: “good location for visiting GWU”
text:
Stayed here for a weekend in september with my son looking at colleges.
Nice area with the fairmont across the street and the ritz a block east.
Ordered room service with a very limited menu. Not sure if this will change after the lobby restaurant is finished its renovation..
we had to pay $10 day for internet but i overheard others say theirs was free.
Parking is $40 night with no in/out.
Instead you can go up a block to N street and park on the street in front of a school for the weekend.
There is a deli across the street where you can sit and get an omelet or bagel if you don't want the $8 bagel at the hotel .
I think Westin has great beds and linens for the price. We paid $150/nt for 2 double beds.
If you want to ride a city share bike, there is a rack right in front of the fairmont.

name: The Brown Palace Hotel and Spa
title: “Stepping back in Time”
text: We loved our three nights at the Brown Palace. We found an excellent deal on Hotels.com for a Top of the Brown room. It was very roomy, the bed was really comfortable and the marble and granite bathroom was all class. The staff was excellent. Hopefully, one day we'll be back!

name: The Westin Georgetown, Washington D.C.
title: “College Visit”
text:
For the purpose of being located near the Universities we wanted to visit, the hotel is great. The front desk staff is friendly and courteous. The rooms are clean and modern. 
 However:
The valet service is lacking in professionalism. 
A dinner reservation we had made before our arrival with the concierge could not be located when we needed the information regarding time and location. The restaurant that was then suggested did not match what we had asked for.
The room I was given had a view of roof tops, air vents, air conditioners and satellite dishes. 
The breakfast buffet was lacking some basics usually found at buffet, such as oatmeal.
We had asked for connected or adjacent rooms and upon check in the staff was surprised with that request. We were accommodated with rooms in the same corridor after some time.
For a Starwood Hotel where I have a SPG membership and have had some great experiences in other cities. I was disappointed.

name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center
title: “great weekend”
text: This hotel is fantastic. Great location for the Wells Fargo Theater to see Il Divo. room was beautiful with a great view, lovely lobby and terrific staff. wonderful full breakfast. we were able to walk to Elways at the Ritz for dinner. will use this hotel again for sure when going to the theater in Denver. especially liked that you needed your room key to access the elevator, very secure.

name: The Ritz-Carlton, Georgetown
title: “Beautiful Hotel, Our Room Needed Some Updates”
text: We enjoyed our stay at the Ritz Carlton, we were upgraded to a suite upon arrival which was a nice surprise. The staff was friendly and helpful. There was complimentary bottled water available in the lobby, in the guest rooms and in the exercise room. There were a couple of negatives, the hotel has a dark interior with low lighting which is nice in some respects but our room did not have suffient lighting for getting ready. The exercise room was not up to the usual Ritz Carlton standards. The hallways were very warm, but the guest room was well air conditioned. If we had paid the full price for our guest room, I would have been a bit disappointed. Overall we liked the hotel and we will stay there again.

name: The Ritz-Carlton, Georgetown
title: “Loved it”
text:
Stayed two nights at the hotel for a conference. This is definitely a pricey experience, but as all costs were included, this was the hotel of choice. The rooms are beautifully decorated and comfortable, the beds had down comforters. The bathroom was to die for - marble tile, separate tub and glass shower, very chic and elegant.
The staff of the hotel were wonderful and friendly, and accomodated every request.
The only complaint would be the construction noise from the health club, but as I was at a conference all day, the annoyance was minimal.

name: Homewood Suites Denver International Airport
title: “Perfect!”
text: I travel frequently and I have yet to find a hotel that offers true overall excellence. This hotel will not disappoint the business or leisure traveler. The breakfast and dinner put them in a class all by themselves! Perfect!

name: The Westin Georgetown, Washington D.C.
title: “Small rooms, so-so service, they should be so much better!”
text: For a Westin that charges so much better, they should be so much better! The hotel is very well located in Georgetown (actually West End), easy to get everywhere, easy access to the Metro and great to walk just about everywhere. The rooms are small and poorly fitted. No closets, just an armoire. Newly done bathrooms with terrible shower heads, a soaking tub (for one only) and very limited space. What's with the hotels these days...no towel racks! The room was so small that the chair hardly fit. The coffee maker was on the desk. I had to request turn down service and every request I had, I had to make each and every day. I asked for extra decaf coffee, extra towels and I had to call each day to remind them. Don't they note a guest's requests?? The WiFi charges are rediculous! For what you pay for a room, they have to nickel and dime you for everything...very annoying! Oh, and the towels are like sandpaper! Come on, this is a Westin, where is the service???

name: The Westin Georgetown, Washington D.C.
title: “Fresh, sunny room”
text: I really enjoyed my stay at this hotel. Everything fresh and immaculate. Loved the bathtub and comfy bed. After finding out our anniversary was that weekend, the manager send us a nice note with chocolate covered strawberries! Nice location - close to Georgetown and Dupont Circle. My minor complaint was tht Wi-Fi was not free. Otherwise, lovely hotel!

name: AKA White House
title: “Location, Location, Location and quite comfortable too:)”
text: 8 easy transportation days due to the location near 2 Metro stops. 7 restful nights too. The 2 bd was modern, clean and well equipped. The roof top area was perfect for a relaxing conversation out doors just steps away. We had very little interaction with the staff, but each encounter was professional and helpful. Thank you to all of you at AKA, we will most certainly stay here again :) Only recommendation for coffee drinkers; The coffee maker provided is nice and programmable for a fresh, hot morning cup, but you need to bring your coffee, filters and fixings unless you want to go downstairs before caffeinating. :)

name: Residence Inn Washington, DC/Capitol
title: “Good value for money”
text:
The hotel is very clean and pleasant with specious rooms.
It is conveniently located 1.5 blocks from a metro station and 5 minutes' walk from the national mall.
However, there are no real restaurants in walking distance.
The breakfast is OK, not more.
The staff is friendly.
Overall good value for money.

name: The Ritz-Carlton, Washington DC
title: “A Comfortable Luxury Hotel in Uptown Washington DC that simply says "enjoy the moment"”
text:
The Ritz Carlton, Washington DC is located in Uptown Washington DC, just north of Washington Circle Park and within walking distance to trendy Georgetown and Dupont Circle.
The hotel's location, in a residential portion of Washington, lends to the overall tranquility that the hotel offers. Besides focusing on customer service, the Ritz Carlton Washington DC serves to provide quiet relief from the daily demands of Washington. The rooms are adequately appointed but are far from being luxurious. The rooms are quiet, which removes some of the accommodations' inadequacies, such as the lack of complementary in-room internet services. Instead the Ritz Carlton offers mini-bars in each room, which is something that few seasoned business persons are seeking when planning an extended business stay. All-in-all the Ritz Carlton Washington DC is a comfortable stay in Uptown Washington, without presenting an overly pretentious tone that some similar luxury hotels seem to exhibit. The Ritz-Carlton Washington DC appears to be seeking to offer a 'home away from home", with just a bit more added to make one's stay a little more memorable, such as their afternoon side table setting of self-serve coffee and freshly baked cookies ... that presents a very civilized and acceptable way to express the thoughts that we each need to take some "time-out" of our daily schedule and just "enjoy the moment", with a simple cup of good coffee and a delicious cookie.

name: Savoy Suites Hotel
title: “Best Value In DC”
text: Savoy Suites is fantastic! Great location, great service, and great value. Rooms are spacious, clean and comfortable. The restaurant is top-notch. The people who work here will make you feel right at home. Tiffany is a front desk super-star, and Hanin is one of the best bartenders in DC. If you are planning to be in the area, you would be silly to stay anywhere else.

name: Hyatt Regency Denver At Colorado Convention Center
title: “Good luck with your reservation and watch your cash around employees”
text: Reserved a king size mountain view room two months prior to our stay for an annual conference. Ended up with two double beds overlooking a construction site with a wonderful view of smog over south Denver. So much for mountains. The final straw that made us decide to cancel our stay and leave the conference early was the fact that a bar waitress tried to stiff us for $5.00 on a $10.00 bar tab when we paid cash. When I approached the bar manager about it, I was basically called a liar until I pointed out the two witnesses to the chain of events that were sitting at my table. Eugene, the bar manager, reluctantly remitted $5.00 back to us. I will not stay at a Hyatt again - anywhere, and further, when we have our regional conference in April, I will tell all 350 attendees the story and recommend that they stay somewhere other than Hyatts as well.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Management GREAT in the Storm but Front Desk needs MAJOR "Climate Change" !”
text:
As it happened, the timing of our most recent repeat visit to the Omni Shoreham was not ideal - Washington D.C. was hit by "Superstorm Sandy" a few days after our arrival. But Hotel Manager Allan Codore + his managerial colleagues pulled-out all the stops to look after their guests, with severely depleted staff resources - more on that later.
Tempted though we might be, it would be unfair to judge this impressive, expensive, historic hotel by the largely dysfunctional Front Desk. On our arrival day, we were too early to get into our room straightaway, so we came back in late afternoon. Accompanied by our personable Porter (Joe) we tried to gain entry to our allocated room, but couldn't. Joe used his "master" keycard, only to discover the room was already occupied - first major screw-up ! We were given an alternative, hoping that was the end of our problems - it wasn't. Four days into our advance-booked weeklong stay, we returned from some sightseeing to discover we were "locked out" - Room keycards clearly not programmed correctly ! We also had difficulty getting the correct "Guest Welcome Pack", got inaccurate replies to some queries to Front Desk, had problems getting our preferred newspaper, and had to argue over a wrongly allocated "Room Service Charge" before we left. Not impressive !!
In noting these unpardonable failures on the part of particular Front Desk staff, we must also acknowledge that a young Floridian, Emily, was excellent in her Front Desk role, showing great patience & helpfulness, and we were also impressed by her colleague Natalie. But as for the other people....
"Sandy" hit the area two days before our planned departure. With transport shut down, and dangerous conditions outdoors, the Omni was missing over 50 staff. Allan & company jumped to the rescue - maintaining basic housekeeping and other essential services & most noticeably serving dinner (we would argue that the Dining Room ran better than ever that night because the mainly manager Servers were clearly focussed on taking and delivering food orders !) Well done the management team ! (they probably hadn't time to notice their laudable performance coincided with an anniversary of the hotel's official opening).
For fear it might appear that we didn't notice other "positives" during our somewhat fraught stay, we must commend the consistently helpful Concierge staff, and of course the outstanding service Hassan & his team delivered in the "Marquee Lounge". Oh, and we definitely have to give a second mention to that wonderful character Joe, who having retrieved a messy "welcome to your room" on our arrival, conducted us off the premises with humour and efficiency !
[By the way, some of the "pluses" of the Omni Shoreham's neighbourhood include "Open City" - a friendly good-value cafe / diner - and a very convenient station for the safe, clean & efficient Washington Metro]

name: Rouge, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Good hotel for the price”
text: Stayed here for a quick weekend visit to DC. The hotel is very good for the price point. It's like your average, standard Sheraton or Marriott, just with some more flair--red walls, cool lamps, funky wallpaper, etc. They are targeting the 20-30s crowd, so wouldn't recommend for older travelers. Parts of the room are kind of worn--the bathroom is on the older side.

name: AKA White House
title: “Beautiful, spacious and convenient”
text: We stayed at AKA White House as part of a family east coast vacation. There were 5 of us - 5 big adults. This accommodation is actually a lovely 2 bedroom 2-bath apartment which was a lot more enjoyable for 5 nights that hotel rooms would have been. It's a great location - the White House is right out the door, 2 blocks away. The interior decor is modern, restful, and stylish. All areas of the hotel are immaculately clean. The fully equipped kitchen makes it easy to save on meals. There is a comfortable living room with flat screen tv, and also flat screens in both bedrooms. We benefited from the washer and dryer to get ready for the next leg of the trip. The front desk staff was unfailingly helpful and pleasant. Light continental breakfast is served in the pleasant lounge on the first floor. The metro stop is just 5 minutes away. The only small negatives I saw is that the staff in the breakfast room does not seem to have the same great customer service attitude as the front desk - kind of sullen and slow, standing and watching as items ran low and were used up before reluctantly replenishing. . Also the hotel is in a business district; we felt completely safe, but stores and restaurants are not plentiful - although they are there. Unfortunately, the deli on the first floor on the hotel, Heidi's, did not seem that good in our opinion. Overall, tho, we loved it and would definitely stay there again.

name: Residence Inn Washington, DC/Capitol
title: “Nice Hotel for Families”
text: Stayed 2 nights in May for a family trip to DC. Location is safe, but not a lot of options for dining. Smithsonian is easily walkable, even for 6 - 10 year olds. We had a 2 bedroom room which was perfect, quiet and clean. Breakfast was great, with lots of food available.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Washington, D.C.
title: “Perfect Stay during the DC Mix Weekend”
text: We stayed at Embassy Suites for the Labor Day Weekend for the Annual DC Mix Party Weekend. The Hotel could not have been more perfect. From the complimentary breakfast to the Managers Reception, everything was great and the friendly smiles at both the front desk and in the food service area was more than welcome. The actual Suite upgrade that I booked was super spacious, and actually had a sink and mirror inside of the bedroom,which I thought was a SUPER idea!!! The living room area had a huge table, and the TV's in both the bedroom and living room were large enough. The beds slept VERY comfortable and front desk was able to recommend great delivery in the afternoon for a local shop that had great pasta! And we went to the restaurant downstairs in the Hotel for Dinner. It was AWESOME!!! The waiter was very attentive, recommended a great white wine, and made sure we were ok with our food choices. And the FOOD-Amazing!!!! It was a great complement to the hotel, and they even allowed us to place the dinner order on our Hotel bill, even though they are separate from the hotel.It would be a shame to stay at the Hotel and NOT eat dinner at the restaurant downstairs at least once, that's how good the food and service was. Overall, I would definitely return to the hotel on my next visit to DC!

name: Hotel Lombardy
title: “Old World Charm”
text: We loved the charm of this non-chain hotel. The personnel were very pleasant and attentive. The location is very close to two Metro stations. There are a lot of restaurants to choose from and the Founding Farmers restaurant was great for breakfast. There is a Whole Foods Grocery close by for added convenience, which also has excellent meal choices. Loved the free Washington Post and bottles of water every night!

name: Embassy Suites Washington-Convention Center
title: “Great Hotel and a Great Happy Hour!”
text: Had a great time at this hotel. My trip was especially made great by Maria (cleaning staff on 5th floor) and Terry (one of the greeters)!

name: Residence Inn Washington, DC/Capitol
title: “Quintessential customer service”
text: Enroute to DC, I had managed to lose my credit card and my phone. Upon arriving at the hotel the desk clerk was able to check me into my room early and provided a free upgrade stating "hopefully this will help make your day a little better". The hotel was extremely clean and the beds were comfortable. My only complaint is that the fan would kick on during the night and make a horrible vibrating noise. One night it actually kept me up throughout the night. They sent an engineer to check into it the next morning. And, although it did occur again the next couple of nights, the noise level seemed less and it didn't occur quite as frequent. I'm thinking we just had a bad room, which was also the reason it was so easy to get into. Anyway, our stay was pleasant. Only recommendation is that the hotel offer additional services, such as shuttle and money services. The desk clerk and manager went out of their way to assist me with some travel needs, but were limited in what they could do - to no fault of their own and not for a lack of trying.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington, DC Downtown
title: “Excellence!”
text: This hotel is spotless, well managed, and close to everything. The rooms are flawless with adjustable beds, microwaves, refrigerators and flat screen TV's. Friendly staff is ready to help with any questions you might have. The White House is only three blocks away, well within walking distance, and cab fare to major points of interest (National Mall, the Smithsonian, the Washington and Lincoln Memorials) is less than $10. The Washington DC room tax rate is substantial, so be prepared to pay $250 per night and a 14.5% tax on top of that. The room rate is priced accordingly though, because comparable hotels would command a price of $300 per night. The only (minor) complaint that I would have with this hotel is the bar - it's really just a small bar serving only odd-ball beers (No Heineken or Bud Light - Pabst Blue Ribbon) and they close early, but they are able to make any mixed drink and the prices are great. In summary, I would recommend the Hilltop Garden Inn to anyone looking for value at a perfect locale. I give this hotel a 5 out of 5 stars.

name: Savoy Suites Hotel
title: “Visiting a Sleeping Giant”
text:
There are some giants better observed while they are sleeping: teething toddlers and wild tigers, are two which immediately come to mind. After our trip to D.C., this city has been added to this list.
 My daughter is planning on attending a university "back East". We are from Central California and decided to take advantage of the 24 hour period before the university's Open House by visiting as many states, or in the case of D.C, districts, as we could ( Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and New York---were all toured, loved, and photographed with great relish).
 Our plane landed in Richmond, Virginia at midnight. We rented a car and proceeded to head to our first leg of the trip: Washington, D.C.
 To make sure we did not lose our room, we called the Savoy to let them know we would NOT be arriving until 3 a.m. Always call the hotel when you are going to be checking in at an irregular time.
 We drove on unfamiliar freeways, surprised by the frequent changes in the speed limit.
 When we arrived in D.C., we were stunned at the feeling of reverence we experienced just by gazing at the Pentagon (which I was glad to see seemed to have curtains in the windows--this added a feminine touch to the military facility), the Lincoln Memorial, Washington Monument, U.S. Capitol Building, National Archives, and Jefferson Memorial.
 These alabaster edifices, stripped of tourists, politicians, honking horns, and whirring vehicles were perfect under the gentle Autumn sky. In fact, I would not want to see them any other way.
 As we were the only moving vehicle on the streets, we took advantage of the opportunity to hop out and take some photographs with these spectacular buildings in the background. I am sure we looked a bit suspicious to the security guards in the area, but they must have deemed us harmless in the end, because we were not pulled over or questioned.
 We rolled down the windows and breathed in the crisp October air as we drove along the Potomac and then wound our way up M street to Wisconsin, where the Savoy is located.
 Since we were so late, the outside doors were locked. But upon seeing me, the attendant unlocked them and let me in.
 Being the very last to check-in, we got the only parking spot left in the basement garage. This proved to be too much for our West Coast parking skills...our rental car hit a post (hey, it was in the blind-spot) and we ended up duct-taping our right brake light back together and taking advantage of the rental insurance we had purchased for the vehicle).
 The room was clean, contemporary, and fairly quiet (being in the heart of Georgetown). We could hear large trucks throughout the night...but we were so exhausted...we did not care.
 Savoy Suites Hotel is ideally located for the shop-a-holic ( M Street is divine!). Since there is a garage, small as it may be, it's great for the car-renting tourist.
 We scored a fantastic deal on our room, considering we stayed on a weekend. 
 This hotel definitely got our "Thelma and Louise", mother-daughter adventure off to a great start.
 I

name: Mandarin Oriental, Washington D.C.
title: “Mandarin brand is amazing!”
text:
I have stayed at many Mandarin Oriental hotel's across the US and have never had a bad experience. Everything from check in to check out is always perfect. Impeccable service, great restaurants and amazingly clean and neat. The Mandarin in DC continued to impress. They remember your name at check in and always offer you a bottle of water. The room had tranquil music playing and a welcome note with a snack which was nice. It was clean and the turndown service was great - left robe, slippers and shoe shine box by the bed each night. The lobby bar/restaurant was a great place for a lite bite and a few drinks. The service there was great. 
I have stayed here a few times and its been great every time. Its the first choice for me when I am traveling for business to any city but also highly recommend for personal use - its worth the $$$.

name: The Brown Palace Hotel and Spa
title: “Treated like Royalty at the Brown Palace!”
text:
A day and night to remember! From the moment I pulled the car up and was greeted by the doorman until I left the next day after breakfast I was treated like Royalty. All the staff from the turn down service to the person who cleared the table at dinner, had a smile, Good Morning, Good Evening, Happy New Year, are you enjoying your stay, may I help you! 
The afternoon tea in the lobby was delicious-not only from a taste standpoint, but from an experience standpoint. The Palace Arms restaurant had impeccable service, food and wine. A definite place to have dinner again.
In fact, the overnight event was so amazing, my sister and I plan to make it an annual event!

name: Mandarin Oriental, Washington D.C.
title: “Very nice, great views, but not very close to things”
text:
This hotel is very nice. The rooms are very nice, the beds super comfortable, and the bathrooms are awesome. We spent one day seeing the memorials, leaving the hotel on foot, and returning 4 hours later. A long walk but very nice on a warm day. There are no stores other than a CVS within a 1/2 mile radius.
Overall, we had a great stay and would return. Staff was very helpful and friendly. The only things which were disappointing are the following (but we admit these are minor):
Swimming Pool - only luke warm.... I expected warmer. No hot tub, which was disappointing.
Fitness Room - asked us to leave because my 11-year-old children were not allowed, even though we were exercising together and using the equipment responsibly.
Room -- no coffee pot, have to order always from room service.
Mini-bar -- no wine, had to always order from room service.

name: Hyatt Regency Denver At Colorado Convention Center
title: “Could have been cleaner, nice location for convention”
text:
This stay was very average for the Hyatt. The checking-in process was amazingly easy (all online); however, there was a line almost to the door during the busy times in the afternoon. Obviously, there are some staffing issues that need to be addressed. The hotel is very busy during my stay; there were at least three other meetings besides my own. 
Room service was quick and friendly, but I have to agree with the other reviewers who state the food is awful. I ate other food provided by the hotel during my meeting and found it to be equally mediocre. On the plus side, the coffee shop does a wonderful latte, and the staff there was excellent.
My room needed a new shower curtain (many rust stains) and the shower vent needed a thorough cleaning (caked with dust). I requested this be done after the first night, but it was never done. We also had to request for tolietries to be replaced which is a huge pet peeve of mine. Why is this so hard for housekeeping staff to do especially when there is a $5 tip sitting next to the empty bottles?
The bed was average. I liked the flat screen TV and the desk set up in the room. It was great for our laptop and eating room service.
The location is the main appeal of this hotel. I was so happy to be staying close by when I was hobbling along in high heels. It is a short walk to the 16th St mall and all the other fun downtown sights.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington, DC Downtown
title: “Wonderful experience”
text: My husband and I stayed here recently and had a great experience. The service was truly efficient and everyone is helpful. The location is good, about a 1.5 mile walk to the museum mall. There are also breakfast places, bars, etc. locally. They have fresh cookies in the lobby and there is free coffee/tea in the morning. The hair dryer they provide is weak, ladies you may want to bring your own. Overall we would definitely stay again!

name: Four Seasons Hotel Denver
title: “Not what I would expect from Four Seasons...”
text:
We came into town to visit family for the holidays, but took a night to meet some old friends at the Four Seasons. From the start it was a bit of an odd experience. The front desk was nice, but had to do a lot of "checking with the manager". They made a point of telling us that the pool was outside, but it was heated. Then when we went to look at the pool, we were greeted with a sign stating that the pool was closed for ice around the pool deck. It seemed that maybe one could use a shovel or salt to make a path the 15 feet to the hot tub, but no. Then the bar was perplexing. Our first waitress before dinner was very attentive, but the second waitress later that night, not so much.
The next morning was the really damper on the experience. When we went to leave in the morning the valet brought our friends' car to the door. Unfortunately, it arrived with a HUGE dent in the side. Apparently, the valet the night before had crashed the car returning it to the garage. These things happen, but they did not seem to handle this the way a hotel of this quality should. Not very remorseful. It seems they should bend over backwards to make the customer feel better about the situation, but that didn't seem the case. It wasn't my car, but I left feeling bad about the whole stay. 
The hotel's insurance will cover it and they offered him a $100 to spend in the restaurant, which seemed little consolation for the hours of time and trouble they will have dealing with their mistake. Also, they still had the $29 dollar valet charge on the bill. He asked to have that removed, which they did, but that seemed like a no-brainer for them to have done prior to printing the bill. 
Anyhow, it's a nice building, but they need to invest in some salt and customer service training.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Great stay...great people”
text: We will be back. When we arrived our kids were given a goody bag and when we returned from dinner cookies and milk had been delivered for them. Exceptional staff that is very attentive. One block to the Metro makes this a great place to stay with the family while visiting the sites.

name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center
title: “Wow, what outstanding service!”
text: I could not have been more impressed with my stay at this hotel in Denver. It was right downtown and near everything you could want to do which made going to and from the hotel very convenient. I will be staying here whenever I come back. JM

name: The Westin Georgetown, Washington D.C.
title: “Great place - my second home”
text: I love this place. I travel here very often for work and I feel as though it is my second home sometimes. I am ALWAYS greeted by the most friendly and attentive door men (Amadau and Deenny) They always have a smile for me and help me with my bags. I look forward to returning to the hotel to see their happy faces. The staff is all very attentive and always remember me. Very clean and located right by Gtown for good dinners.

name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center
title: “Outstanding hotel”
text:
Of all the Embassy Suites Hotels I have stayed in, this property is at the top. The only other property that comes close is the Embassy Suites hotel in Seaside, California.
The facilities are extraordinary. The staff is extremely courteous and will go out of their way to help you. Houskeeping is wonderful, the breakfasts are as always, great from A to Z. Their Restaurant was a wonderful surprise. The foos is exceptional for Embassy, the ambiance is good and presentation is excellent. I stgayed there for ten days in December and enjoyed myself every day. The facilities such as pool, fitness and bisiness center are very accessable and professional or in the case od the pool, fun. Valet service is outstanding. They remember your name after a day or two. In fact that also applies foe front desk staff. They had an incredible 4 course christmas dinner at $35 and it was well worth every penny. This is the place to stay for fun, culture at the performing arts center accross the street or shopping along the 16th street mall, unique experience in itself. It does not get any better then this hotel for the money.A little luxury, security, and so much more.

name: Washington Plaza
title: “Great stay”
text: Kids loved the pool after a long day's site seeing. Clean hotel. Nicely refurbished, rooms of a good standard. Food ok. Great location for us on our first visit to see all the sights. Walked everwhere. Would def stay again.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Relaxing atmosphere with loud room air conditioner unit”
text: The hotel is relaxing with large rooms and plenty of shops with amenities. I found the staff willing to answer questions and provide information on near by restaurants and entertainment. I attended a four day business conference at the hotel. I enjoyed the spacious accommodations and nearby attractions.Great experience for me but some of the conference attendees had complaints about unclean rooms and bed linen. I would say check your pillows before laying down for the night. One conference attendee complained of blood found on her bed and pillow. The hotel was very accommodating by changing the linen and pillows and sending up a huge fruit tray as a measure of forgiveness. Overall my room was clean although it smelled of a peculiar odor, I brought an air freshener but it did not help. Please be reminded the air conditioner units are located inside the room and can be a little noisy at times.The restaurant in the hotel is pricey but there is a restaurant across the street that is reasonable and the food is really good.

name: Rouge, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great experience!!!”
text: I was so unure about this hotel judging from the outside but inside its so nice. The red floors were spic n span..the staff was supa nice and it was so modern with the art and red decor. Supa supa clean! The rooms look way better in person. I had the deluxe room and it is by far the best room I ever stayed in..bed was sooo comfy and the room n bathroom was clean. I'm coming back soon..loved it

name: Washington Plaza
title: “intensive tourism”
text:
I stayed for 4 nights in Washington Plaza with the main aim to visit Washington intensively. I made a good choice, (thanks to other reviews read here!). the hotel is within 15mins walk from the White House and once you get there, you get everywhere! 
The room was nice but I noticed the same as in the previous hotel in Washington: the phonetic isolation between bathrooms is not good because you can hear your neighbours taking their shower or flushing the toilets.. 
I did not have time to use the pool or fitness room (though too small to my taste).
the hotel's restaurant was very good. I ate there twice and the food was close to the French cuisine. 
Staff was very nice and helped me with the few questions that I had, nothing to complain!

name: Hyatt Regency Denver At Colorado Convention Center
title: “Excelente ubicación”
text:
Fui en viaje de negocios para asistir a una convención en el Colorado CC, que se encuentra justo atrás del hotel, por lo que es una inmejorable ubicación.
El hotel es muy agradable, limpio y funcional a un precio razonable.
Altamente recomendable.

name: Hotel Lombardy
title: “Great value, great service”
text: On every occasion I've stayed at the Lombardy, I've been impressed by the staff - evidently proud and happy to be here, courteous, personable and informative, they make a stay here stand out. Rooms are large and well-appointed, there's free and fast wifi, it's minutes away from the World Bank, and 2-3 blocks from the metro. The Venetian Bar is comfortable, albeit the loud jazz sometimes can be less than relaxing. Hard to beat.

name: Savoy Suites Hotel
title: “great sleep on a great bed”
text: Good location-walking distance to good shopping. Easy to catch buses to go wherever. Whole foods was a few minutes walk away. Very quiet room at the end of the hall away from elevators. Hotel was undergoing some reno at the time but this was not intrusive. Very friendly/helpful staff. Best rate was had online.

name: The Westin Georgetown, Washington D.C.
title: “Beautiful hotel in a quiet location”
text:
I had an excellent Westin stay at this hotel. The rooms were large with high ceilings. The bathroom was enormous and had both a shower and bathtub. Beds/linens/bath products were all usual high quality Westin. The lobby was typical understated Westin, which is a good thing. I found the lounge to be tasteful and very refined. I only had the breakfast buffet. While not cheap, I found it to be an acceptable value. 
 This hotel is a nice choice if you're not accustomed to city sounds. The neighborhood is very quiet, and I slept just as well as when I'm in the quiet suburbs. It's not close to the metro, but an easy 5 block walk. 
 The staff here is excellent. The "main" concierge is Friday-Sunday I believe. I was in contact with him over email several weeks before my visit. Jeffery was very helpful and communicative. The service is typical excellent Westin. Clean rooms etc etc. 
 Overall the value for my rate was excellent, however rates here vary wildly. If you can get one of their cheaper rates for your stay, it's a top notch value. If you don't mind being a bit of a walk from the metro, and want a nice quiet neighborhood, this is definitely a great place to stay. This was my first trip to DC and The Westin-Georgetown helped make it a wonderful trip. I look forward to returning and would recommend it to friends.

name: The Westin Georgetown, Washington D.C.
title: “This hotel feels like my home away from home!”
text: I particularly want to commend one of the doormen, Deenny, and one of the woman at the front desk, Katherine. Both of them are fantastic!

name: Savoy Suites Hotel
title: “Great views, great beds, great weekend.”
text: This past March was our second stay at Savoy Suites, this time with another couple to celebrate two March birthdays. The hotel is up on a hill on Wisconsin Ave. and both times we stayed there we had wonderful views. (In March we looked out of our window and realized that we could see the spires of the National Cathedral beyond the nearby trees.) If you're fond of Georgetown, the location is great: a couple of blocks from Whole Foods, Pearson's Wines and our favorite barbecue place. Up hill is the Cathedral and down takes you into the heart of G'town and M Street. The beds are wonderful, the rooms are large and well lit, the parking is convenient and every staff person we encountered was friendly and helpful. On an earlier stay during warm weather we had drinks out on the patio while listening to a jazz pianist. My wife and I enjoyed this hotel more than most we have stayed at in G'town and we will be staying there again.

name: Mandarin Oriental, Washington D.C.
title: “Excellent place to stay for the Cherry Blossom Festival”
text: The location of the hotel is perfect. From the front doors you can see the Washington Memorial as well as the White House. It's walking distance from the museums (the Holocaust Museums is only 3 blocks away and the hotel gives you complimentary admission tickets). Also, there is a small foot bridge that takes you to the basin where you can even walk to the other monuments. The staff is exemplary and made our weekend relaxing and enjoyable. Will definitely come back here next year for the Cherry Blossom Festival.

name: Hotel Lombardy
title: “Great Value and Location”
text: We are in the middle of our 7 day stay and I am very pleased with this hotel. It is an old building that has been keep up and has some personality. I asked the hotel to give us a nice room because this was my son’s first trip to DC and the hotel upgraded us to a King Suite with the view of the little park across the street. We took the Metro from Reagan Airport to the Farragut West stop for $1.70 and was only 2 ½ blocks from the hotel. Note: the hotel is really on I street at Pennsylvania ave. We have used the Metro to go everywhere in DC with little cost and trouble. It took a couple of times to get used to it. Note: there are token machines at every stop, get a $10 or $20 worth depending on how long you are staying. Back to the hotel… there is everything to eat with in ½ block from $40 a plate to $6 Johnny Rockets. There is a TGIF Friday’s on the corner and a CVS Pharmacy 1 block away for snacks and stuff. Across the street there is a small mall made out of the old buildings and has a few nice shops (girl shops, nothing for us boys). There is also a couple of nice small pubs to get a drink and pub meal. I can go on and on but the short is I would recommend this hotel.

name: Washington Marriott Wardman Park
title: “Vast, well run hotel”
text: This vast hotel sits on a slight hill just by the Woodley Park/Zoo DC Metro station. It has a large number of room spread over three low towers. It does a lot of conference and event trade, yet manages to absorb it all easily. The rooms, which seem to have been refurbished recently, are up to the usual comfort level and palette you would expect from a Marriott - ochres, gold, pale blues. The bathrooms are a little on the small side. There is a wide choice of bars and restaurants. The hotel is very convenient for getting around the sights of Washington from the Metro station or take the Circulator bus to Adams Morgan. Pedestrian access could be easier; it's a steepish walk up, specially with bags. Depending which way your room looks you might get a nice view of the Washington Monument or of the National Cathedral. Shirts cost $8.50 to launder.

name: Embassy Suites Washington-Convention Center
title: “Kid Friendly, Adults--Trying”
text: This is a great hotel for families, and it was as crowded as the Air and Space museum on Memorial Day weekend. By 8:00 AM, the line to get a simple breakfast was 30 minutes long, and it was hard to find a table. Kids seemed to love it--but for adults wanting a relaxing start of the day, it's best to have breakfast somewhere else. Same for the evening happy hour--long wait lines. Rooms are good--plenty of room and a comfortable bed. The staff is absolutely the most friendly and helpful I've ever seen in the US--and I travel extensively and worldwide on business. Only a small hotel in Romania I've visited beats them for friendliness. I would not stay here again, but I would recommend it for families with children.

name: Club Quarters
title: “Excellent for a quick stay!”
text: Had a late concert at Constitution Hall. Excellent spot to stay to avoid the travel back home. Very small room, but it was clean and worked well for the short stay. We were totally able to walk to the venue. Good times.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Washington DC-Northeast
title: “Too far away, limited shuttle service, nowhere to anywhere nearby”
text: Overall this was ok. The neighborhood is rough and there are no decent restaurants anywhere. There is a shuttle to union station some hours of the day but it was often full. Breakfast buffet was typical HIE fare.

name: BEST WESTERN Georgetown Hotel & Suites
title: “Peaceful”
text: This hotel is a quiet, pleasant, clean place to stay after the exercise of seeing Washington DC. The room we had was nicely arranged and large enough. It is a few blocks from Metro, has nice restaurants close by, and is within walking distance of the Potomac. The mall area and other tourist attractions can be quickly reached by bus and Metro. If possible, don't take a car because parking is $25.00 a night. The management were friendly and helpful.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington, DC Downtown
title: “Excellent hotel, great service! Would go back...”
text: This hotel is well kept, and is extremely close to the Red line Metro. Although the neighborhood seems to be moving in the right direction, some surrounding areas are still a bit "seedy." The staff was great, my room was clean, and everyone I encountered was extrememly friendly. I would stay there again! Local supermarket and small restaurants are adjacent to this hotel. Overnight parking was $30, a little pricey though....

name: Embassy Suites Washington-Convention Center
title: “A+ Friendly Staff”
text: Arrived on mega bus early and the Friendly staff allowed us to check in early.Nice clean room,and the best free complimentary breakfast i have ever seen.also they checked our backpacks the next morning so we could go sightseeing without carrying our bags until we left that night on the bus. also we had dinner there before we left and was very good,next time i stay in DC this will be my first choice.

name: Embassy Suites Washington-Convention Center
title: “Great location for a weekend stay.”
text: We just decided to go to DC for the weekend with the kids. We spent a lot of time out seeing the sights, but when we were in the hotel it was great. The morning breakfasts were a hit with the kids; the happy hour was a hit with the parents. The people at the front desk were extremely helpful. There was a problem with the room's temperature and the staff fixed it immediately. They even left an apology note and chocolate hammers as a treat for the kids. Thanks for a great visit.

name: BEST WESTERN Georgetown Hotel & Suites
title: “A nice place to stay for familes at an affordable price.”
text: I would highly recommend this hotel for people looking for affordable accomodations. It was clean, the staff was very nice, and it was close to the Metro and DC. We could walk to Georgetown and the Lincoln memorial. We didn't like our initial room and had no problem switching to another room more to our liking. Parking was across the street at the Ritz Carlton garage. The only real problem we had was with the hot water pressure in the shower, but this was minor. They also had a continental breakfast. All in all, for the money, this is a good choice.

name: Washington Marriott
title: “We loved this hotel...it was just like home!”
text: My son and I recently stayed for four overnights at the Washington Marriott Hotel for the National Campaign to End Violence (Do the Write Thing Challenge). We were super impressed with the quality and service that this hotel provided. From the moment that we arrived, we were treated with dignity and respect. Our guest room was impeccably maintained and had comfortable beds and excellent personalized climate-contolled air-conditioning. We enjoyed wonderful breakfasts, provided by the Do the Write Thing Committee almost every day that we were there. I also enjoyed one of the most wonderful bacon cheeseburgers in the Atrium Restaurant as well as a wonderful breakfast at the Atrium with my son on our last day. The entire staff at the Marriott Washington from the receptionists to the bell staff to housekeeping to the Atrium staff were pleasant and helpful whenever we needed assistance. On our last day, I inadvertently overtipped the bell staff and he being an extremely honest man ran after the taxi and returned part of the tip. What a man of integrity to look out for another traveler's welfare. If he hadn't, we would have been short for our taxi cab's tip. We cannot say again what a wonderful place the Washington Marriott is...we would definately like to visit again. Thanks for treating us like family!

name: Kellogg Conference Hotel at Gallaudet University
title: “Excellent Customer Service”
text: Stayed here for a weekend college visit with my daughter. Evening check-in was professional and efficient with a phone call to our room to make sure we were satisfied. The organic toiletries were a pleasant surprise. Beds were very comfortable with premium bedding (very high on my priority list). Staff was knowledgable of the area and able to provide pertinent tips on both walking and accessing the Metro. The shuttle to Union Station is a big bonus. We did not take advantage of the on-site Bistro or restaraunt but it deserves mentioning as well. The only reason this was not a perfect stay was the disruptive group of children on our floor the last night that took about two hours to correct (after multiple complaints by patrons). It is very likely that we would stay here again regardless of the reason we're in DC!!

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington, DC Downtown
title: “Wonderful Hotel for the Weekend Tourist”
text: The hotel is very close to the White House, Smithsonian and monuments of Washington, DC. The staff was very friendly and accomodating. We all (spouse, two friends and myself) very much enjoyed the restaurant. The buffet breakfast was an excellent deal and the service was always tops. Our evening drinks and dinner were equally enjoyable, especially the waitstaff. Our thanks to everyone at the hotel for making our weekend trip a delightful time.

name: Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill
title: “Could be better.”
text: The staff is great and friendly. For all other points, I agreed with all recent posts. They could do better if invest a little in renovation and take away all these stupid small extra charges: Internet ($11) definetly can be free, breakfast ($21 for buffet) can be cheaper and parking at $45 is way to high. Some advise regarding parking, if you do not mind to walk for 5 min. find a spot at the Union Statation, it is only $22 for 24 hours vs $45 at the hotel. Keep in mind, you can leave you car at the hotel until 5 pm on the check out day.

name: Rouge, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Decent hotel for a visit to the museum centre that is Washington D.C.”
text: The value for money for this hotel is probably the best thing about it. The room we were given was huge although it was quite a weird set out - there was a huge space of nothing - perhaps it used to be a kitchenette and has recently been remodelled. The service in the bar area was pretty slow. The location is not ideal - although is still walking distance from the main monuments. We had a problem finding anywhere for breakfast as we were walking to the monuments so it may be a good idea to eat at the hotel. It is in a very quiet area of D.C. There are areas close by for resturants. The staff couldn't recommend any restaurants to us so luckily we had read up on some places to go local to the hotel. Washington DC is of course an amazing city - full of history, museums and monuments. Loved the city!

name: Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill
title: “Very Average”
text:
Location is good if you need to be near the Capitol Building,other than that I have very little positives to add.
The hotel is in need of a refurbishment,It is looking very dated ,the carpets in the hallways are from another era,If they wait a little long enough they probably will become fashonable !
Our bathroom was clean,However had a very stale water smell that would not go away.
It is a shame that I can find few positives ,The staff were all friendly.
Value for money was poor,everything was an extra and we left feeling that we could have received a better experience elsewhere ?

name: BEST WESTERN Georgetown Hotel & Suites
title: “Family vacation, June 9-16, 2007”
text:
Our extended family of 6 stayed in two suites; we were comfortable with the size of the rooms. The hotel staff was very friendly. The hotel was clean (non-smoking!), but the paint and wall paper were a little faded/worn. The queen-sized beds were very comfortable (seemed new) but the sofa and sofa bed were worn and not-so-comfortable. The continental breakfast was pretty good - cold cereal, oatmeal, boiled eggs, muffins/bagels/pastry, fresh fruit, juice and coffee/tea/cocoa. The frigde/micro were handy; we saved money by not having to eat all of our meals out. Trader Joe's is just a few blocks away for groceries. Well-situated between two metro stops. Parking two blocks over at the Ritz-Carlton, but may be able to find street parking on weekends. 
As for sight-seeing; try to get advance tickets for timed entry ahead of time to popular sites (Holocaust Museum, Bureau of Engraving & Printing). Also, contact your representatives for other sites besides the Capitol and White House; we did not find out until too late that we could have gotten them for the Supreme Court and National Archives; ask about anything else you may be interested in; apparently these are not well-published - we were using several guidebooks and the official websites even!

name: DoubleTree Hotel Washington DC
title: “More than a port in a storm!”
text:
In any ordinary time, I would have been happy to write a great review of the DoubleTree on Rhode Island Ave. Catering (from what I could gather) to business people and tourists, the hotel and restaurant are much nicer than the usual tourist hotel. Big rooms (esp. for a city), lovely and clean, a top-notch restaurant that uses local ingredients, and a friendly and helpful staff--that would have earned 5 stars in my book any time!
But last week, along with many of the hotel's guests were trapped by Hurricane Sandy. It was an inconvenient and sometimes scary time, but the hotel staff rose to occasion. I can only imagine what was going on behind the scenes to ensure that our rooms were clean and fresh, our omelets made, and our drinks poured. But service continued at a high level. I hope the Hilton organization realizes how lucky they are to have such a dedicated crew.

name: Four Points by Sheraton
title: “Friendly and functional”
text:
I arrived at the hotel by taxi from Dulles which cost USD70. 
The check-in and greeting were excellent. I recall that 'Sharon' did an excellent job of checking me in and making sure i received the SPG benefits to which I was entitled.
The bed was comfortable and everything functional.
I did spend some time in the gym. The treadmill was good quality which I enjoyed.
All up, a pleasant stay, friendly and functional staff. I would stay here again.
I should add that the downtown location isn't excellent for tourists.

name: Rouge, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Huge rooms in a cute hotel”
text:
Super clean, quirky hotel with huge rooms and amazingly friendly front desk staff. Great location, HUGE rooms. Tiny bathroom, but I don't hang out in bathrooms so I didn't mind. Bar and restaurant on-site. Free internet ( a must these days as far as I am concerned- don't nickle and dime me for WiFi! Very good value overall! 
Recycling bin in my room- YAY! Seemingly genuine concern for the environment. OPERABLE WINDOWS! Thank god for that, since my thermostat didn't work (room stayed at a stable 72 degrees even when I tried to turn the heat down to 65. I didn't bother calling the front desk to get it working since with my window open it was a fine temp (room 807 in case the manager wants to fix the problem before summer).
Like most hotels, the gym here is sad with only a few machines, but they have yoga mats and weights and exercise balls, which I broguht up to my room for a workout which was perfect. You can also run safely outside as many locals do.
Great place for travellers looking for something different from a cookie-cutter Marriot. Very pet-friendly too.

name: BEST WESTERN Georgetown Hotel & Suites
title: “Great location; Great for families”
text:
Just returned from a 5 day, 4 night stay at the hotel. We were there with our 2 kids to do the D.C. tourist thing. 
The room had ample space and we didn't feel like we were living on top of eachother for 5 days. The room amenities (mini-fridge, microwave) helped us store our drinks, etc. for our daily outings. Breakfast saved us money and was a great start to our days. The location, whether walking or subwaying around to the sights was about as central as you can get. The price was right and, all in all, good value for money and a great place for families.

name: Club Quarters
title: “Nice, But Not For Tall Travelers”
text:
As noted in the other reviews, this is a good hotel for business travelers. It is clean and well-located. The rooms, although small, are adequate for one person. BUT the beds are not large enough for a tall person (5'10" or taller). Even though beds are described as "queen" size, they seem to be smaller than normal doubles. I found my feet hanging off the edge -- and I'm only 6 feet tall! 
Also, there is a noisy demolition project next door at this time (early Dec. 2006).

name: Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill
title: “Not what I expected”
text: Our stay was adequate at this hotel. I was disappointed there was not a couch or fridge in our room like advertised. We took our children & the pool always crowded. Then we found out there were people from other hotels using it.

name: Washington Marriott Wardman Park
title: “rude front desk”
text:
arrived at noon,told would get phone at 4 when rooms ready, did not happen, returned at 4:30 and told "some people don't follow the rules and leave on time". Not my problem!! Asked for 2 really nice quiet rooms, got ice machine outside and door, and hair in tub.When I followed the rules and asked for late checkout due to my daughter's graduation the next day, I was DENIED!
In this very large hotel, the 2 rooms i occupied were needed the as soon as i checked out.
Please spend your money elsewhere ,even if you have to spend more. Only pros are convenience to metro many restaurants

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington, DC Downtown
title: “adequate”
text: this hotel has a pretty good location. was able to walk almost everywhere. was lied to about purchasing hop on hop off tickets-was told I could only buy them at hotel and not on the bus,. pretty shadey. starbucks nearby. good bed, nice tv small bathroom. free internet always a plus. somewhat noisey typical city sirens all night. traffic is horrendous. metro across the street. don;t pay more than $199.

name: Hotel Lombardy
title: “a quaint charm”
text:
Years ago we stayed at Hotel Lombardy several times and it hasn't changed. Yes, it's an older hotel; the elevator is "quaint" but the property is maintained and the staff is generally courteous and helpful. The rooms are very clean, the beds comfortable and AC works - and we were there in very hot, humid weather!!! It has a little pub and restaurant, though we did not dine there. There are a couple of decent restaurants in the neighborhood.
It's near George Washington University. We like the location, only several blocks to Potomac Park and the west end of the Mall where the impressive memorials are located (except for the hideous WWII memorial).
The young, inexperienced manager did change our front room, after some quibbling, to one further "inside" the hotel. I always request a quiet room and the sirens on the intersection of 
I St., Pennsylvania Ave. and 21 St. were intolerable. He tried to dissuade me by saying that this front room was a "view room" !
Of the intersection!? Anyway, yes, I would stay there again, sans view!

name: Days Inn Connecticut Ave.
title: “Good Place to Stay in NW DC”
text: I needed a hotel room the night movers cleared out my apartment in Cleveland Park, north of the National Zoo. The Days Inn is only one Metro stop away, and is really the only option, short of bed and breakfasts, in that neighborhood... and a good optioin too. There are restaurants and stores right across Connecticut Ave., or down the street. I will definitely stay there again if I need to return to DC.

name: Four Points by Sheraton
title: “Great location”
text:
My favourite thing about this hotel was the staff. They were all lovely and very helpful, and that makes such a huge difference in a city you’re not familiar with. Barbara in reception was particularly good.
As for the hotel itself, well, it’s a little run down. In our room there were issues with the air conditioning (sorted swiftly once reported) and one of the bathroom taps. The room was a good size and clean, but the décor was a bit blah and it didn’t have any feeling of plushness.
That said, this isn’t an expensive hotel, and the location was really handy. It’s a little long but comfortable walk to the National Mall, there is a subway station handy and there were a good number of restaurants and bars nearby.
If you’re looking for somewhere fairly comfortable and conveniently located to shower and sleep that won’t break the bank, Four Points is definitely worth a look-in.

name: Washington Marriott Wardman Park
title: “Quiet, clean, large hotel”
text:
We stayed here one night in May and booked through priceline so our rate was quite good. The size of the hotel reminds me of those big Vegas properties but I didn't think it was overwhelming or particularly confusing. The hotel seemed a little out of the way for major attractions but there is a convenient metro station down the small hill from the hotel. The staff is professional but not overly friendly or helpful. We were disappointed to be given 2 double beds when we wanted one bed and have always been accommodated by other hotels in DC (we travel to DC about 4 times a year).
The room was clean and comfortable, and very quiet. We were in the old section, Wardman Tower. We booked a very basic room and it was really nothing special. Had we paid the nightly rate on their website we would have felt we did not get our money's worth. 
Wifi is not free, and the valet parking is on the expensive side but the service was very quick.
We didn't eat at the hotel but noticed a very long line at the small take-out mart in the lobby in the morning.
I would stay here again only if I couldn't get a better rate elsewhere.

name: Four Points by Sheraton
title: “We really enjoyed ourselves.”
text: The employees were wonderful!!! The were helpful and polite. Check in, check out, room service, cleaning and service all went perfectly.

name: Embassy Suites Washington-Convention Center
title: “BIGGEST SCAM IN THE WORLD, BEWARE OF THIS HOTEL”
text:
Upon arrival we were told the room we had reserved was unavaiable. We were given a very small room which we quickly discovered had no heat. There were noisy parties going on the floor we had been given. Instead of upgrading us we were kept in that room.
The scamms started immediately; We purchased items from the store inside the hotel and the person at the counter did not give the proper change for a 20 dollar bill. She shorted us 10 dollars and then acted as is she did not understand when this was brought to her atention. She finally gave the correct change after we had to insist she shorted us-nice try...
The maid did not clean the room one day and she just happened to show up when we were in the room and gave us a story about having to leave for a family emergency. The entire story seems to look as if she was looking for a tip. She made it a point to tell us she would not be back the next day to make sure we left the tip. We had snacks missing and that also seemed odd. 
My wife got food poisining and had to go to the hospital. Unk if it was a result of the food from this hotel, however, it happened shortly after we arrived. 
The most scary was the last day. We made arraingements with the Washington Flier Taxi Service for pickup to the airport. When we went to the lobby the Bell Hop ask if we were waiting for a taxi. When we told him the company we were waiting for he told us they were outside and the driver was in the bathroom. When the driver came out we were assisted to his unmarked taxi and the Bell Hop assisted us with the bags. (We made it very clear we were waiting for a specific company-he insisted the cab we were getting in was the correct one). Once inside we noticed there was no meeter and no markings on the taxi. We told the driver to stop and he got angry with us asking if we had already paid for the other company. We luckly insisted upon getting out because who knows where we would have ended up or what amount we would have had to pay. The cab driver and the Bell Hop clearly knew each other and this was clearly a scam. We should have read the other Trip Advisor reviiew listed in September section. 
The hotel is clearly lacking ethical management. We would never stay there again. This hotel was outright scarry to stay at. Poor customer service, and extremely disappointing for an Embassy Suites....

name: Mandarin Oriental, Washington D.C.
title: “Fantastic Location”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Mandarin for business for 3 days. We did not pay for it, but I know that it was very pricey. I don't know that we would go out of our way to stay here again because it was very expensive. Having said that, it was incredibly nice. We were especially impressed with the quality of customer service all the way from the bellboys to the concierge. They always made us feel very regal and special.
Our rooms were very comfortable. We had a corner room that had a nice amount of space in it. I found it strange that at this price range they had mediocre TVs. Also odd, the room did come with a coffee pot. This is something I thought most all hotels offered. Another inconvience (depends on how you look at it) was that they did not ice on the floors. You had to call down for it.
The location of the hotel is phenomenal. You are on the waterfront and also very conveniently located to a metro station which allows you to get anywhere you need to go. You can also get to the heart of DC for about 6.00 cab ride or walk 15 minutes to the mall area with the Smithsonians and Washington Monument. All very convenient from here

name: Rouge, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great room, great location, great rate”
text:
Hotel Rouge is about 3 blocks east of DuPont Circle, 7 blocks north of the White House - superb location. The hotel itself is very swanky (red drapes and carpet, zebra patterns on cushions) and has a euro feel. Even if you're not into that type of thing, not to worry - the hotel staff was great, the room was spacious and quiet, the shower was hot and powerful, and the price for the location was amazing. We paid about $160 before tax, plus $30 to park. You may find a better rate in the 'burbs, but then you've gotta find a way into town, fight traffic, and pay about the same to park - plus you've wasted valuable time that you could spend enjoying DC.
If you find a comparable room in a comparable location at a better rate, take it. Otherwise, book Hotel Rouge today.

name: The Latham Hotel
title: “Great hotel in a great part of D.C.”
text: Me & my fiance went to D.C. for 4 nights. We pricelined a hotel and got this hotel, never hearing of it before we checked the reviews and googled alot to learn about it. We got the executive suite, it was a really nice room, had a sitting room, nice size bathroom and nice bedroom, 2 tv's in the room. The only problem we had was that the cable went out in the room the 2nd day we were they and they were unable to fix it, so they upgraded us at no charge to us to the best room in the hotel on the 10th floor with a corner room with windows on both sides and also gave us a portable fridge in the room too. They really went out of their way for us, they did great. The rooms were great & clean, the bathroom was so nice, and the location was unbelievable. There was so much to do in the area and it was just a short cab ride to all the historic sites. We loved this hotel and would definitely visit again.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington, DC Downtown
title: “Warm Cookies waiting for you each night.”
text:
Reallly small cozy hotel downtown...with warm cookies that were always waiting for us...we had an ongoing joke with the front desk...when we'd come in...they would say we kept these cookies waiting just for you...they were warm chocolate chip cookies...it was a good way to end our day.
Our room was quiet and clean...late one night we heard lots of noise down on the street...it was an alley...we called the front desk...and within minutes it was quiet again...we never heard anymore noise after that night. 
Found the CVS...good find...just down the street...cheaper to get snacks and supplies here...the DC store is more like a grocery store.
Across from the hotel there is a restaurant and the underground train....since everything downtown closes around 4pm...we got salads and fruit from the restaurant and keep it in our fridge.
We were two ladies out in DC...so we took caution, since it was downtown...but having the train just across the street made it an easy run into our hotel at night. 
My suggestion to you...is to find the restaurants and the attractions you want to go to and plan your day....everything opens and closes at different times...you need to get tickets far in advance for some attractions....some places you can only get to one way...so make sure you have all your ducks in a row....it sucks to get almost there...only to find out you missed the last bus by just minutes.
Wear wore comfy shoes...cause you never know...one day we figured out we had walked over 5 miles. 
Best place to eat..."Old Ebbitt Grill"...great crab cakes and burgers.
Best view to have a drink..."Sky Terrace" at the Hotel Washington.

name: The Embassy Row Hotel
title: “Small but comfortable”
text:
We stayed at the Embassy Row Hotel November 9-11,2011. The hotel was well described in TA reviews and we took advantage of other travelers insights. 
The location was terrific. A safe area, with a short walk to the Metro and lively night scene (DuPont has a variety of bars and restaurants of all types). 
Check-in was quick and easy. As recommended, we stayed in a non-smoking room on the 4th floor, well away from the smoking rooms on the 6th floor. The room was small, but clean and comfortable. Free wireless was a plus. They offer a continental breakfast which featured bagels, fruit, fruit bars and cerial. Not much of a choice if you are on a diet though. 
The downside was no onsite restaurant or bar (when you did not want to head out late night) and valet parking, which costs $40 for a day/night.
All-in-all I would stay here again. We did not mind the small rooms as it was expected.

name: Washington Marriott Wardman Park
title: “Decent value for Washington DC”
text: Decent room that you can probably get at value price. Very nice staff, but huge hotel and very busy with many outside events. Expensive to park if you have a car. Otherwise, great access to Metro and can walk to zoo, restaurants and nice neighborhoods.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington, DC Downtown
title: “Hilton Garden Inn- Where are the Restaurants?”
text:
My wife and I booked this hotel for a small getaway weekend before the holidays. I have never been to D.C. so we thought this would be the perfect weekend. 
The Hilton Garden Inn is located right across from the Metro, which is very convenient. We took the Metro back to the airport for $2.00. From the airport it was 16.00 for a cab. Take the Metro right from the airport! I was worried (chicken) to take the the Metro from the airport when we arrived but don't it's so easy and the attendants in the booth are very nice and are very nice about telling you which train to take if you have any doubt. Anyways, once you exit the Metro, Hilton Garden Inn is right across the street. 
The hotel is nice when you walk in, checked-in in less than 5 minutes and in my room less than 10 minutes after arriving. When we opened the door to our room they had some classical music playing softly. We had a king-sized bed which was comfortable. Sheets were clean, but had one or two stains of lipstick (not my wife's color) or could have been blood? But they were changed as well as the mattress sheet the next day. I was too tired to complain after walking the National Mall and it really didn't bother me, I just switched the sheet around. The A/C unit kicked on by itself even though it was switched off! We think room 807 is haunted!
The room was a pretty big room. It had a microwave, refrigerator, LCD television, basic channels. There are really no restaurants within walking distance except for an over priced Italian Restaurant named Tuscana (For pizza hut personal pan-sized pizza and two soups I paid $32.00), some other restaurants that closed early and I never saw anyone in them anyway. As a matter of fact everything closes early. There was a McDonald's a block a way behind the Hilton. Quick walk but the McDonald's is full of homeless people. Don't eat there just order and take it back to your room. It bothered me a little because some had a few screws missing and they were really dirty. I lost my appetite trying to have breakfast one of the days. There is a CVS down the street, my advice buy some snacks and take them back to your room. I did notice a little noise from the room next door, they had a child but it was tolerable.
Room service would have been good but the Quesadilla did not taste good at all. My wife hated it and when I tasted it the beans tasted somewhat "mechanical." If you know what I mean. Mobley burger was good. We paid $59.00 for a burger, bad tasting quesadilla, two sodas, and a dessert. They do have these delicious cookies in the lobby that are free to guests. Very good. There was a place called the Corner Bakery, south of the Hilton go there for breakfast. Inexpensive and it is very good.
Overall this hotel is in a great location for the Metro, and the sights are within walking distance. Five-minute walk and you're at the White House. A 10-minute Metro ride and you're at the Arlington Cemetery. Take advantage of the Metro, it even drops you off right in the middle of all the smithsonian museums. We would go back to the Hilton Garden Inn, for the money ($99/night) and great location.

name: Four Points by Sheraton
title: “Don't use the "preferred guest" floor”
text:
The highest floor in this hotel is the 9th floor, reserved for their "preferred guests". That floor is directly under the roof and it seems the entire floor vibrates to the tunes of the air handling system that must be mounted on top of that floor. I stayed in this property in FEB 2012 - I cannot tell if they had a mechanical failure or if this is the normal state of affairs, but one thing is sure: The entire floor is far too noisy. I asked to change rooms but none of the two rooms I inspected was really quiet. One room was simply noisier than the other. 
Overall, the rooms are very small, somewhat run-down and with an absolutely unattractive and dull "decor". I cannot say anything particularly positive about this hotel. 
In summary, I put a noise protector into my ears and made it through the night. I will definitely not come back to this property again.

name: Rouge, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Stay at the Rouge”
text:
Just got back from a 2 day stay at the Rouge. It was the first boutique hotel that I have stayed at and I was impressed. The staff was helpful and there was a free happy hour of Red Stripe beer and red wine that I enjoyed. The two bed room I stayed in was very spacious. The location is good. Only a 5-10 minute walk from the Dupont Circle area and a 10-15 min walk from Adams-Morgan. 
The only problem I had was that a mouse appeared in my room on our last day. Due to the cold weather and the placement of food in the room, this cannot be avoided. I alert the staff to the problem and they took care of it immediately..

name: Quality Inn Washington
title: “Poor location but nice rooms.”
text:
We stayed here for four nights in March 2011. The rooms were clean and had all the standard amenities of a budget hotel, plus free cable TV and free WiFi. Our room contained a king size bed which was incredibly comfortable. The staff were friendly as well.
The location of this hotel is not the best; it is quite a dodgy area and we definitely did not feel safe enough to walk around at night. Also, on the Friday night some guests in other rooms decided to have a party in the parking lot, right outside our room (this continued past 2:00am). I think in this case the staff should have asked them to return to their rooms or leave. All other nights, though, we did not experience any noise issues.
I would recommend this hotel only if you have a car or do not mind taking taxis into town. (From there to the National Mall is approximately a 60 minute walk.)

name: Howard Johnson Express Inn - Washington
title: “Pure fright”
text:
My boyfriend and I needed a place to stay for one night after a late concert in DC. We wanted someplace clean and safe and were not looking for any frills. Although we knew the street was not in the best area, we figured the HoJo had a decent enough reputation to suffice for one night, and the price was great. After our experience, I can say that it is worth it to pay more to stay in a decent area.
The only reason this hotel rated a two out of five is that the room seemed clean. Everything else was a disaster. We walked downtown after checking in and passed dozens of homeless people begging for change. The walk is not something I would ever do again as it led through dangerous looking and dark parts of town. We returned to the hotel that evening, and at 5:30 a.m. were awoken by a loud banging on the door. We were terrified, and upon looking through the peephole saw a large, man standing there swaying and looking incoherent. He continued to bang on the door foor the next five minutes. We shouted at him to leave and finally he did. It occurred to us (in our half asleep state) to call the police, but we figured the man would be long gone by the time they arrived. The rest of the night we tossed and turned unable/afraid to fall asleep.
The next morning we went to put our luggage in the car and noticed glass all over the ground next to the driver's side door. I remarked that we were lucky it was not our car that was broken into. Unfortunately, I spoke too soon because when I went to open the passenger's door, the window was completely smashed out. The stereo was ripped out and several personal items were stolen (including a GPS system which we should have never left there in the first place.) This, in combination with the last night's door pounding, left me feeling terrified and angry, and I went to alert the desk clerk while my boyfriend called the cops. When I told the clerk what had happened, he didn't even bat an eye as he told me this type of thing was common, "especially at this time of year." (Apparently the thief was Christmas shopping in our car?) I told him it would have been nice to have been made aware of this little issue before we checked in.
Hopefully this review will alert anyone else looking to save a few bucks in DC and steer them away from this hotel. My new outlook is that DC is outrageously expensive, whatever way you look at it, so, eat fast food or take the Metro to save money, but don't skimp on hotel prices as they indicate safety. The DC police later told my boyfriend that car break ins are common at hotels all over the city except in paid hotel parking garages. Pay the bit extra to help guarantee your safety, especially if you have children!

name: The Allen Lee
