title: “You get what you pay for”
text: The Allen Lee is a cheap hotel in the heart of Washington, DC. It is not at all fancy and is a little run down, but it is in a safe neighborhood and the folks at the desk are nice. If you are looking for a place to sleep while exploring, stay here. My wife was concerned that I would bring bed bugs back. Didn't happen.

name: Comfort Inn & Suites New York Avenue
title: “not centrally located”
text:
The Comfort Inn New York Avenue offers clean and spacious rooms and a good breakfast buffet, but the hotel is not centrally located and there is no public transport available near the hotel.
We had to catch a flight late at night and asked the lady at the reception in the evening to call a taxi for 3 a.m. When we were ready for departure there was no taxi waiting for us and the guy at the reception didn't help us to get a taxi at all. We had to stand in the rain in the front of the hotel to flag down a taxi. Finally we reached the airport at the last minute.
I wouldn't stay at the Comfort Inn New York Avenue again.

name: Four Points by Sheraton
title: “Nice hotel with great Front desk staff”
text: I came down to visit some friends and go to a concert at the 9:30 club. The staff was really nice, my room was great (it was right near the hotel bar, but it was still nice and quiet). The parking was a little pricy, but it is DC....

name: Embassy Suites Washington-Convention Center
title: “Great place for families at a decent price”
text:
We stayed here in early March-a larger corner suite room that accommodated my husband and me, plus mother in law and 2 young kids (ages 4 and 7). I highly recommend this as a choice for DC if you have a young family and don't mind a short cab ride or healthy walk to the Mall and other locales in DC. We ate dinner our first night at Capital City Brewing Co, which was fine. Other nights, we ordered in pizza at the hotel from a local chain they recommended (great price, fast delivery), and still another, we went out to Hard Rock , which is a crowd pleaser when you have little ones.
The free breakfast was very convenient and I never waited more than 5 minutes for a custom omelet, or in the buffet line that served hot, fresh food. The staff was constantly watchful of food running out and replaced empty bins immediately with new ones.
Pool is on the smaller side but the plus side is-it's shallow for little ones ( just a bit over 3 feet deep) all the way across. Even with 5 other kids in the pool from another family we did not feel crowded out at all. Towels everywhere and staff nearby to check in on things. Exercise room-didn't use but looked very clean and was used by other patrons.
Manager reception was adequate--snacks were of the popcorn/chips and salsa variety, but drinks and service were plentiful.
There is apparently a laundry facility onsite that I never searched for, but heard about from the man who works in the gift shop. They sell tiny bottles of Tide in the gift shop.
Housekeeping and room service were excellent. We asked for an extra towel and the maid brought up 4. Bell caps and other service reps were knowledgeable and helpful. 
My only "con" is that there really wasn't a convenient drugstore nearby, where we could purchase snacks and drinks. Perhaps I was not completely aware of what was around us in that area, though, since we literally spent most of our days touring and were never back at the hotel except at night. Speaking of night, we did not feel threatened walking around the hotel vicinity with our kids and stroller in the evenings. We come from a large city, so are mindful of our surroundings. But you'll be fine in this neighborhood. 
One key piece of info: a hotel staff person told us the White House was a quick 2-block walk. Well, it wasn't. It was more like 15 minutes briskly, and 6-7 blocks plus. If you are headed to an early morning White House tour, give yourself plenty of time, because it is a hike, and you should allow enough time to find the correct entrance for tours as well as clear the proper security checkpoints.

name: Mandarin Oriental, Washington D.C.
title: “SUPER!”
text: Mandarin Oriental odwiedzi?am z kole?ank? w maju 2011. Hotel ?wietny, obs?uga bardzo mi?a i wsz?dzie blisko w mie?cie. Room service, pokoje, spa bez zarzutu. Widok ?wietny, ogród hotelowy, w restauracji ?wietne jedzenie.

name: Motel 6 Washington DC
title: “stay at your peril!”
text:
I would advise anyone considering staying in this Motel 6 to seriously reconsider.
I gave my credit card and driver's license to the desk when I checked in. My driver's license was returned to me, but not my credit card. Unfortunately for me, I didn't notice this oversight.
The next day, I went to the front desk to book another night but couldn't find my credit card. The person at the desk said that her coworker was supposed to return it to me. But he hadn't!
By that time, my credit card had been fraudulently used several times.
I can't say who was responsible for the theft and use of my credit card. The police are investigating. But I believe that there are some serious discrepancies in the motel's internal investigation of the incident.
I would never stay at the Motel 6 again!

name: Comfort Inn & Suites New York Avenue
title: “Not as expected”
text: The shuttle didn't run to Union Station daily as advertised, which is a problem as taxis don't normally come by. There were no restaurants or fast food places adjacent to the hotel as described. Upon checkout there was an additional $9.95 on the bill,( which was removed). The front desk was not knowledgeable or helpful.

name: The Latham Hotel
title: “Pleasant stay”
text:
First, thanks to Trip Advisor for providing these forums. I had an “Independence Room” on the 9th floor, 917 to be exact. I got a very good rate on a travel web site and paid $119. I found the room comfy and clean. The bathroom was a little on the small side but fixtures and tiling were in good condition. The A/C unit was on the verge of being too loud so I turned it off at night and opened the windows. The weather was amenable and I was delighted I could actually open the windows. 
There is no concierge and the front desk staff were friendly albeit inaccurate with some information. I was given bad information about metro transport. Fortunately, I had access to the internet and verified before I left my room. Speaking of internet, I was told by the front desk that the WiFi rates were for 24 hour cumulative usage. It was not. The rate is 10.95 for a 24 hour day. I was surprised that any hotel actually charges for Internet access at all. For the standard rates they charge they need to get with it!! 
Getting back to transportation, please check out the web sites for the DC Circulator buses and Washington DC Hop Stop. These should provide you with a good basis for getting around. Also, the DC Circulator bus advertises an “every 10 min” schedule. This was not the case, it was more like 20 – 35 min. Too bad, otherwise it is a great service. 
As other reviews state, the location is great. Enjoy the Canal/towpath directly behind the hotel. It is a lovely rustic and historic walkway. 
In the food category, I can tell you I enjoyed a Crab Cake for lunch at Clyde’s located up a ways on M Street. I also enjoyed Seafood Curry across the street at Miss Saigon. Le Madeleine which is located in front of the hotel was a pass as far as I am concerned. The “French Breakfast” of Scrambled Eggs, Bacon, Potato and Croissant was overpriced and COLD. Literally, it was stone cold. Eeesh. Oh, and don’t ask for anything besides scrambled eggs – they don’t do anything else. Bon Appetit

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington, DC Downtown
title: “Awesome Location”
text: This hotel has the perfect location, right across the street from the Metro Stop and just a couple blocks from the White House. The room was spacious and clean. Breakfast the next morning was a perfect start to the day. I would definately stay here again.

name: The Westin Georgetown, Washington D.C.
title: “Eine exzellente Unterkunft für alle Unternehmungen in Washington”
text: Das Hotelpersonal war sehr um das Woahl der Gäste bemüht. Obwohl wir drei Stunden vor derCheck-In Zeit da waren, bekamen wir problemlos unsere Zimmer. Diese waren geräumig, sehr sauber und mit allem ausgestattet was der Reisende braucht. Dur<ch die hervorragegende Lage in der Nähe der Metro Station Foggy Bottom waren wir innerhalb kurzer Zeit vom Flughafen in der Unterkunft. The Mall ist zu Fuß in zwanzig Minuten zu erreichen. Eine Unterkunft, die wir immer wählen würden wenn wir in Washington sind.

name: Capitol Skyline Hotel
title: “Not living up to expectations”
text:
We actually did not choose this hotel as we joined friends who had selected it.
We did however read the reviews that appear to be mixed.
Black is not my color and certainly not for decorating a hotel.
The rooms did look like they were restored, but not by a company that deserves a recommendation. The bathroom was remodelled with a nice granite counter, nice floor tiles, nice wall tiles and a very modern toilet. But they forgot to replace the bathtub and the wall paper! So the bathtub got a coat of enaimel paint appried by a person who forgot to do a proper priming, so it was peeling.
The rest of the room was also remodelled with a very nice and extremely comfortable bed and nice carpet, but rather than removing the wallpaper the renovator desided to paint it a very dark grey and use black California style blinds.
The "designer" is not my style and rarely would you see a hotel that gives such a somber impression, so I do agree with the reviewers who described the atmosphere as dungeon like.
But having said that, the beds were the most comfortable ones you can get in a hotel.
We had booked till the 1st November, so instead of sightseeing that Monday and Tuesday, we ended up watching the news about the huricane in the room.
Neither of us had ever encoutered a hurricane before, so on Sunday Morning I did go to the front dest for advice. They detailed to me the precousions they were planning and assured us that they would do their very best to deal with any possible emergency like back-up generators, food and water.
So if you plan to spend all your time sightseeing to get back to the hotel ready to collapse, this could be a good hotel for an excellent sleep. But if you end up spending a lot of time in the hotel, and have similar decorating taste as I, I would wait till they get a new decorator.

name: Windsor Park Hotel
title: “Budget Traveler Price, Great location”
text:
Windsor Park hotel is in an excellent location and within walking distance to the Zoo, 2 metro stops, and Adams Morgan. It is a place to rest at night. Right across from the Chinese Embassy, once a parking spot is located, a traveler can enjoy walking and the metro to all of the DC metro destinations.
The rooms are dated and could use a renovation - especially the bathroom and the mattress. Since we drove to DC, I packed extra pillows and I was happy we made this decision. There is free wireless internet in the location - so it is very helpful.
The hotel is for a budget traveler that prefers to spend their money on attractions and food - not on a place to sleep and rest. Some of the staff is helpful and others are not - so it is hit or miss.

name: Windsor Inn
title: “Set Your Expectations”
text:
If you come to this property with your expectations properly set, your stay will be great.
The rooms are small, they're dated, and the breakfast sucks - but the location and the price are great. And the front desk help (where to eat, how to catch the bus, etc) is excellent.
The bed was small (an old fashioned double - does anyone sleep in those anymore?) but comfortable. The hotel/B&B was relatively quiet, but it's location is excellent. Great access to transit, walking distance to the White House and The Mall, and a few blocks to the Metro. Restaurants everywhere - most within a block or two.
We stayed in a private room with ensuite bathroom downstairs (below street level).
Overall, I'd come back!

name: Channel Inn Hotel
title: “A place to stay but not much more - rather disgusting...”
text:
The Hotel is located off the main areas of DC and is not convenient to Metro or anything else other than the wharf... The wharf fish market is an interesting place to see but nothing I would look forward to on a vacation and the location makes its a poor choice for business unless you have a car, order a taxi in plenty of time to get where you are going.
No free shuttle anywhere.
First impressions... Not the worst place I have ever stayed but probably the second worst I have stayed in the USA.....
Dingy, old, dirty, dank, drab, smelly... I am referring to the staff, lobby, restaurant, bar, entrance, everything!
Uncaring service. Staff that do not know what is going on, do not communicate and do not seem to care what is going on around them.
There are a few staff that really try hard and go the extra mile for guests but none are at the front desk!
The pool is something out of the 1950's and is right on the main road outside the hotel and ringed by a tall steal security fence that makes you feel like you are in a cage...
The one good point is the view of the Potomac off the bar, restaurant and some of the rooms on the back of the hotel. Quite nice and the patio outside is probably comfortable in the Summer or Spring.
If you like the stuff above then you will love the bar full of 40's - 60's men and women that crowd in to listen to old Motown and other unknown funk music from the 60's and 70's...
Hint: get the staff to bring you a clean sheet to put down on the bed and use your own covers and pillow!!!

name: Georgetown University Hotel and Conference Center
title: “Great Beds - not so great staff”
text: We stayed at the hotel as it had been reserved for us for business purposes. I had stayed there before and had been disappointed by the attitude of some of the desk staff. This was to be the case again. On checking in it seemed as if the girl on the desk was doing us a favour. I asked if a package had been left at reception for me to collect and was told 'no' (it had been). The room size was adequate but small. The bed was one of the most comfortable I have slept in. The bathroom and vanity area was poorly lit and badly designed. Car parking is an extortionate $25 for 24 hours and was made worse by the fact that I parked at midnight and left just before 6am.

name: The Latham Hotel
title: “nice but not luxury”
text:
The Latham is a nice hotel but not a luxury one and it is too expensive for its amenities.
the best thing is its location and the location on site of the restaurant Citronelle.
the rooms are indeed small but they are comfortable. the toiletries are very nice too but robes would be nice.

name: The Latham Hotel
title: “Not what I expected”
text:
I expected a little more than what I received. Let me begin by saying
that the staff is EXTREMELY helpful and supportive, but the hotel is definitely not what I hoped. The first room that we were given was really nice (despite the small bed), but the heat did not work properly. The weekend of this trip was an extremely cold spring one. Fortunately, we were promptly moved to another room; one that overlooked the pool. Unfortunately, the pool was cover by a blue tarp
and the room open to the outside and not a hallway. The door to the room would not close completely (it closed, but the door and the frame was ajar). We used a towel to keep the cold air out and placed the sitting chair against it so I would feel safe. The handset for the telephone did not work, but we were able to have it fixed very quickly. I suppose I could have requested another room, but i didn't know what to expect from another room. I also did not feel up to riding around DC looking for another hotel. 
I don't think I will used this hotel again.

name: Rouge, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
Nous avons passés 3 nuits a l'Hotel Rouge. Personnel très compétent et aux petits soins pour nous y compris le directeur.
Et ce qui ne gate rien le directeur et un réceptionniste parlent parfaitement français.
Une anecdote: à notre départ, la navette attendue pour nous rendre à Dulles Airport ne s'est pas présentée. Le réceptionniste nous a proposé sans hésiter de nous emmener avec une voiture de l'hotel sans bourse délier ( 45minutes de route)

name: Channel Inn Hotel
title: “Better than expected”
text:
As someone else said, you get what you pay for! The hotel is a bit rough round the edges and the manager is lacking in customer care skills, but the rest of the staff we encountered were pleasant and friendly, they even let us watch tennis on the telly in the bar despite being a football match on! 
Rooms are spacious and clean, if in need of a bit of refurbishment. Air con worked, and there were lots of channels available on the TVs. We never got a view of the marina, so never used the balcony. The shower was very poor, very low pressure unless you left it cold. 
We never ate in the restaurant. Breakfast was reasonably priced and ample choice in the coffee shop in the hotel. 
Location is ideal for metro (1 minute walk) where there is a Safeway as well as a choice of places to eat. We ate in the nearby 'Philips' restaurant where there was lots of choice, including fresh seafood and crab. The pool was closed as it is out of season, but is beside the road, so would not have used it anyway.
Okay for a couple of days, but would not have wanted to stay any longer. Value for money.

name: Four Points by Sheraton
title: “No disasters, but nothing to write home about.”
text: A big negative for this hotel was the noisy air conditioner unit. I cranked the room down to about 63 degrees and then turned it off, as my only hope at sleeping. The first night it took me until 3 am to work out that you have to turn it off BOTH at the wall thermostat and on the A/C unit itself. The lobby has quite possibly the ugliest furniture I've ever seen. (I admit I'm style challenged so I asked my sister for an opinion too, and she just snickered). People who were attempting to sit and chat in the lobby seemed profoundly uncomfortable. The restaurant was pleasant, with a good menu and not overpriced. As others have noted, it's pretty odd to have WIRED internet access anymore at a hotel. Mine flaked out a lot as I moved my laptop around the room; the ethernet cable was a bit "worn," it seems. (It's just as well: had it been functional on my first night here, I would have given a 1-star rating because I was so annoyed by the A/C). Location was good enough but nothing to write home about; staff were pleasant and competent but again nothing special. I disliked the barrage of questions on checking in ("Are you a rewards member? Do you want to be a rewards member? Can we have your email address?" No. No. and No. Please just check me in.). As a final comment, I was dismayed to find that the hotel charges $2.00 to make a toll-free (1-800-) calling card call. Really, that's as bad as charging for internet access... just chintzy and inappropriate.

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Georgetown
title: “Confortable hotel”
text: We recently stayed for three nights at the Holiday Inn Georgetown in room 503. The room was confortable, the staff helpful and friendly and the hotel is in a great location. We will certainly be staying at the Holiday Inn Georgetown on future visits to Washington ,D.C.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington, DC Downtown
title: “Lo standard Hilton ad un buon prezzo”
text: Abbiamo utilizzato questo hotel nel nostro soggiorno di vacanza a Washington. La scelta è stata fatta in base al prezzo (molto conveniente, probabilmente perchè abbiamo soggiornato durante il week end) e Alla posizione vicina ad una fermata della metro. La camera era davvero molto ampia e spaziosa e il servizio ottimo. Tra l'altro gli ospiti possono accedere gratuitamente alla piscina interna ed al centro benessere. Lato negativo è che di fronte c'è una discoteca all'aperto e il sabato sera la musica ad alto volume disturba il sonno. Per quanto riguarda il quartiere, non si può dire che sia bellissimo e ottimamente frequentato, ma la vicinanza alla fermata alla metro rende questo hotel comodo per spostarsi in città durante il giorno. l'unico consiglio è quello di non rientrare troppo tardi la notte con mezzi diversi dal taxi.

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Georgetown
title: “A good, typical Holiday Inn”
text:
We stayed in this Hotel for what turned out to be six nights in July 2012. It was pretty much what you would expect from a Holiday Inn. Average, no frills, ok quality.
Our room was clean and comfortable. All the Staff we came in contact with were very helpful and cheerful. Especially the Reception and Bar Staff. The Reception Staff helped us out when we asked for a different room (no reason other than we decided we preferred a King bed rather than two doubles as was previously given to us). We also asked for a higher floor and they obliged. The Bar Staff were chatty and friendly and we felt welcomed into the Bar. The Bar itself, we found was a little odd. We couldn't put our finger on why, but decided that it looked a little like a play area rather than a bar because of the decor, but that was a minor thing and we enjoyed a drink or two in there after a long day sight-seeing. The food in the bar (we ate one evening) was very good. The breakfast buffet was average and ok.
The Hotel had a bit of a Business feel about it. There was a conference on, so it may have been because of that. The pool (which we didn't use) looked a bit scruffy but was better than nothing.
The Hotel is close to Bus stops, so getting about is cheap and easy. 
There are a couple of reasonable Restaurants and a Supermarket within walking distance, but that is about it. Everything is a bus/taxi ride away even down to the main part of Georgetown, but we didn't find that a problem as the buses were cheap and we also discovered the circular bus and the open top bus both dropped us in the vicinity we needed to be to get back to the Hotel. 
Overall, I would recommend this Hotel for a basic, reasonably priced, friendly, no frills stay.

name: Georgetown University Hotel and Conference Center
title: “perfect hotel for college visit”
text: Wednesday- Saturday stay to bring student home from DC program, have one day to relax, and visit GU.. We traveled without a car, did not do any sight seeing in DC. I was a bit concerned after reading some reviews, but I had none of the problems discussed in reviews. Air conditioning was great and it was very hot during my stay. We traveled with Ipad/iphone so did not have to pay for internet. We experience some chains still charge for internet, though it seems unreasonable.... Hotel has a printer for boarding passes, one located at front desk, another hidden away in the the business center located off the main lobby in the conference area... We booked through the hotel website, so paid the normal AAA rate. Had a nice view of campus from 5th floor room. Very comfortable, clean, updated room. It was easy to get a cab or car service from hotel. taxi stand directly outside hotel. The car service hotel arranged to Dulles was about the same rate ($65) 2 passengers would pay for a shuttle. Taxi i took from Reagan Airport to hotel was $18. Also used car service for event in Arlington. Driver was a pleasure and she made the ride much more interesting than the typical cab driver. GU Shuttle located just down a block from the hotel, we never used it, but seemed to be very popular. It was not obvious to me initially, but you could reach the student center (food court, bookstore, cafe, market) directly from the hotel lobby, never having to go outside.This was very useful considering the hot temperatures outside. Small student market for snacks, fruit,water, and priced at the normal rate. Across a path from the hotel the Epicurean Dining was perfect for dinner/takeout (salad, pizza, sushi, etc). Much better quality/atmosphere than expected from a college food court. We did not use Faculty Club Restaurant (located in the hotel's conference area), buffet opened for lunch and dinner. Noticed a "free" self service laundry room, on the 5th floor, though we did not use.. Hotel provided newspapers in the lobby and it seemed that apples where at the front desk in the morning.The hotel staff was very helpful, I asked lots of questions about walking directions since I initially had no idea where I was in relation to the campus and downtown. It would have been more helpful if they just offered the maps originally, but I guess they incorrectly assumed I knew where I was going. Very easy walk to downtown. Less than 15 minutes to Georgetown shopping area.Highlights from downtown: "old stone house" historic sight, Georgetown cupcakes ( pre-noon lines seemed shorter), Dean and Delucca market, experiencing the old townhomes/cobblestones walkways.

name: Channel Inn Hotel
title: “Decent...not Great!”
text: Hotel is a bit run down, but for the price that I paid, I didn't expect much. The staff I thought were pretty pleasant! My original room was really hot, even with the AC on. I asked for a different room which they let me choose between two other rooms. The key didn't work, so the maintenance man, Luis, was nice enough to walk us up and even changed a light bulb that was out. The decor is out of date, no fridge and small TV, Housekeeping was AWESOME and kept the room clean and very friendly. We did order room service which was good, but the restaurant was overpriced and gross. Always a taxi outside waiting and close to everything. The pool was nice too! If you are on a budget, this would be a good choice. If you have a bit more extra funds to spend on a hotel, I wouldn't choose this place.

name: Capitol Skyline Hotel
title: “Was a nice stay.”
text:
The hotel is situated within walking distance to the Captiol and other famous sights. Moreover you can use a restaurant, a small fitness room and a pool. My room was comfortable and had enough space - HBO is also available. The reception is friendly and helps asap. Sadly there is no late check-out available. Youhave to check-out by noon or pay $75 extra. But you can leave you bags in a secured room until you have to go to the airport. 
At daylight I felt safe, however the taxi driver did not recommended me to enter the area behind the hotel. Moreover, the famous Georgetown district is far away. If you are looking for a hotel in the better parts of Washington try something north of the Capital Mall. But on the other hand the way to the Airport (DCA or IAD) is shorter and a taxi drive from DCA usually just costs around $15. The only thing that really bothered me was the slowest WiFi, I've ever seen in my life since the 1990 - 56kBit! - Skype is impossible to be used.
I would come back, if I get a another chance to visit DC.
Thank you.
CF

name: L'Enfant Plaza Hotel
title: “Great location, decent hotel, kind of 70ish urban renewel architecture”
text: L'Enfant Plaza hotel is in a great location - right on top of a metro stop and food court and just a brief walk to the Mall, the Smithsonian Museums, the monuments, the Capital, etc. As for the hotel itself - the rooms are large and fine and the beds are comfortable. Otherwise the furnishings and the design are pretty average - no flat screen tvs, bathroom fixtures and design dated, colors and wallpaper reflecting a bygone age, and the hallways frankly are kind of like long caverns. Pool a nice touch but health club and other hotel facilities nothing to write home about. The food was pretty good except I felt the breakfast buffet was kind of lacking and overpriced (it was actually included in our room rate, but I certainly wouldn't pay the going rate for it) A decent place to stay but wouldn't choose it for a special occasion.

name: Days Inn Connecticut Ave.
title: “Si tienen un presupuesto con holgura, no vayan a este hotel”
text: La primera impresión cuando uno llega a este hotel, es la de que llegó a un hotel de clase turista pleno. La entrada es muy fea, un tapete feo con apariencia de viejo y la recepción igual. Al tomar el elevador, el piso esta en muy mal estado, se siente sucio. Ya en piso 5 donde me hospede habitación 508, el olor a mugre y sucio de los corredores es impresionante. Las puertas de las habitación son de madera pero se ven muy viejas. Cuando entré a mi habitación encuentro que es amplia, pero de nuevo la misma sensación de suciedad en pisos y tapetes. El WiFi funciona bien. El baño, con ducha y tina, se ve viejo. En resumen, si bien pude dormir y no tuve ningún contratiempo, es un hotel regular. La ubicación no es mala, la zona es segura pero no se esta tan cerca de las zonas bonitas de Washington DC. Un taxi desde el hotel al Dupont circle cuesta alrededor de 10 dólares y a la calle M en Gerorgetown, alrededor de 16 dólares.

name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center
title: “Pet-Friendly, But Dark & Dismal”
text:
On a road trip, we stopped to visit family in DC for a few nights and the Westin City Center was one of the few hotels in the area that would allow us to stay with our dog (a 60lb husky). This hotel is extremely pet friendly and we were not given any funny looks or hassled about our dog's size or breed. Other hotels have very strict weight policies and sometimes won't allow huskies (not sure why). The staff was friendly to us and we were greeted promptly when we arrived to check-in. I have no complaints about the service.
But, the room and hotel itself was just dark and depressing. Maybe other rooms in the hotel have windows, but the pet room we were given just looked out at the hotel lobby area and other rooms in the building. There were no windows, so I felt like we were stuck in a cave. It was clean enough, but not spotless. The decor was outdated as well. It felt more like a Hampton Inn than most Westins I have stayed in previously. Valet is the only option for parking (no self-park) and was expensive - I believe $20 to $30/day. 
I wouldn't complain about the decor, how dark the room was, or the cleanliness if I weren't paying well over $200/night, plus a daily pet fee, plus valet, plus taxes. For a place that totaled nearly $300 night when all was said and done, this was a MASSIVE disappointment. I know DC is expensive and it's par for the course in the city, but there must be a better value.

name: Harrington Hotel
title: “Cockroach surprise”
text:
Overall the staff seem very helpful/pleasant. We arrived early and they immediately offered to mind our bags until we checked in.
Unfortunately, once we got to our hotel room, there was a cockroach on the wall.
When we notified staff, they quickly came to remove it (he actually stamped on it) - then we were moved to a different room.
A peaceful sleep wasn't possible after the cockroach experience though.
It is also quite noisy, neighbours and outside noises.

name: Channel Inn Hotel
title: “Wonderful Balcony View, Cranky Front Desk Staff”
text:
Myself and three friends stayed here for the Reason Rally (March 2012). 
About our room: Our balcony looked out over the water, and we could see ships cruising by all day, it was beautiful. The rest of the room was average, which is perfect for me. There were no towels when we first got our room, though they fixed that quickly. There was no coffeepot, just as a warning to those that are in dire need of morning caffeine. There is a Pepsi machine as well as an ice machine down the hall. The decor is outdated but neat and clean.
About the restaurant: The restaurant served a cafeteria-style breakfast, and was reasonably priced and tasty.
About the staff: The man I first dealt with to see if we could check in early was rude, didn't speak much, and just shook his head and glared a lot. He was also there a few hours later when we did check in, and he was rude to a few others in line. I chose to check in with another man who was behind the counter at the time, and he was quite nice. The girl I checked out with was also friendly.
About parking: Parking was free, and in a garage on the lower level of the hotel. As an added benefit, they let us park there before check-in, and they let us stay parked after check-out while we explored the city.
About the location: The hotel is a short walk from the National Mall, where our event was. We also hit a few museums, the botanical garden, and the capital and never needed any transportation. I wouldn't recommend walking for anyone who gets tired easy, or has small children though.
Overall I liked the hotel experience. I would recommend this for the price to anyone traveling for fun and on a budget, but not to anyone who expects a modern hotel with many amenities.

name: DoubleTree Suites Washington, DC
title: “What a DUMP ... Don't stay here!!”
text: Booked a week's stay at this hotel and would have checked out immediately if it had not been 11 pm when we arrived and if our packed itinerary would have allowed the time to find a better alternative hotel. From the moment we checked in, everything we expect from a Hilton brand hotel was missing or lacking. You do NOT get the Hilton experience at this hotel. I'm a HHonors Gold member and have stayed in Hiltons across the US and the world and this was not what I expected. Here's what you get when you stay at the Doubtree Suites in Washington DC ... 1) you will not be greated when you come and go 2) expect to wait a half hour in the middle of the night for a key to your room because the front desk staff does not make you a key nor have a master to to readily get you in your room (this happened to us) 3) expect to get put into a ground level floor when you are a women traveling with a child even though you asked to be put into a higher floor for safety concerns (your concerns will not be acknowledged) 4) expect a non-working toilet 4) expect a kitche that is not functional. No oven and one small pot to use on the burner 5) expect mediocre housecleaning 6) expect an extremely small pool 7) expect very limited dining options in the area 8) do not expect assistance from the hotel staff (they did not know the difference between Georgetown and George Washington Universities (but other guests were helpful in getting us around) 9) expect popcorn ceilings in your room 10) expect a bed where you roll to the middle (not upgraded beds like you get in most Hilton hotels). This hotel does not meet Hilton standards and the Hilton corporation should come take a stay to see this. We asked for the General Manager to contact us and he never did! We posted on the HHonors Facebook page and was told to expect an email (which we never got). We were extremely disappointed and never got any satisfaction. Do not stay here!!!

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Georgetown
title: “The room was not clean.”
text: The room was not clean. There were spots on the mirror in the bathroom that should have been wiped. The same with the bathtub. I tried to connect my phone charger to an outlet behind a chair, and there was accumulated dust that had not been taken care of in a long time. Then I surveyed the room more carefully and there was dust in every corner. The same with the two chairs by the round table. They have not been vacuumed in a long time. Again, in the corners where the seat meets the back of the chair.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington, DC Downtown
title: “Sehr ordentliches Preis-Leistungsverhältnis”
text: Sehr gute Lage zu Institutionen, Sewhenswürdigkeiten und ÖPNV! AC nervig da nicht abzustellen. Insgesammt aber ein Angebot das in anderen Hotels der Stadt deutlich teurer verkauft wird. Somit mein aktueller Washingtontipp!

name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center
title: “Noisy room next door”
text: Good area. Very nice Westin hotel as far as layout and bar/restaurant but the room was so noisy form the neighbors just watching tv and speaking to each other in a normal voice. So bottom line for a Westin not comfortable.

name: Windsor Inn
title: “NO VISITES ESTE HOTEL”
text: En este Hotel te engañan, te mienten y te Roban. Fui del 27 al 29 de abril por dos noches pagados en hoteles.com y despues de llegar a mi casa me doy cuenta que me cargaron una noche extra por salir a las 6 de la tarde, cuando en realidad sali a las 6 de la manana en vuelo de regreso a Tampa, y aun esta en investigacion por American Express, pues ellos no quieren hacer la devolcion, ademas las habitaciones sucias y rotas

name: Channel Inn Hotel
title: “They don't care!!!”
text: Have you ever stayed in a hotel that didn't have a newspaper free or for sale. These people didn't know where we could even buy one, let alone care. The lady's that worked there seemed to care. Other wise they didn't give a *&$#@

name: Georgetown Inn
title: “Excellent”
text: Charming hotel with friendly and helpful staff, excellent location. Our room was spacious and comfortable. Circulator bus to downtown stops literally outside the front door. Hotel restaurant good with other good options across the street. Neighbourhood was picturesque with lots of older homes and felt very safe.

name: Capitol Skyline Hotel
title: “Excellent - ticks all the boxes”
text: I was so impressed on arriving at the hotel that I immediately booked another night. The room was majestic to say the least and I was amazed at it because of the low price. The staff could not have been more helpful throughout my stay and I am surprised that the rating for this hotel is not higher. I initially got a cab here but soon realised that the nearest Metro station was only a 5 minute walk away so I used this from then on. The hotel itself is only a short walk to the Capitol building and the walk was a pleasant one. All in all I was delighte with my stay here and would have no hesitation in recommending it.

name: Melrose Hotel, Washington DC
title: “Very Nice For Business Travelers”
text: Stayed here for a business meeting. Close to Foggy Bottom Metro. Rooms very comfortable.

name: Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill
title: “Some good, some not so good...”
text:
I stayed here for one night on my own and my husband joined me for a conference the next few days. The good--the lobby is bright and airy, I found the check-in staff very professional and accommodating. I found the room with the king bed spacious. The hotel restaurant staff were accommodating and the maid helpful.
The bad--There were many families with children in the hotel over the weekend and I was bothered by doors opening and closing as well as people talking in the halls past 10 p.m. The rooms were not well insulated enough to prevent being disturbed by the noise. The internet is not free here.
The ugly--About 2 a.m. on Sunday I was awakened by--the fire alarm. All guests were instructed to evacuate the building. After a while we were allowed to return and learned not only that someone had pulled the fire alarm, but that this is not unusual.
Overall, I think this hotel wants to be a business hotel, but really lowers their rates to get the families in on the weekends. It doesn't seem set up to appropriately accommodate families.

name: L'Enfant Plaza Hotel
title: “L'Enfant Plaza Hotel and American Grill”
text:
First, the hotel - The hotel is fine except for charging $10.95/day for internet service. I think it is unreasonable for ANY hotel to charge for internet service. I called the 'assistant manager' and requested the internet to be free and was told that was not possible. I then went to the business center, where the internet is free IF you use their computer, and made a reservation for the Residence Inn three blocks away (free internet, breakfast, manager's reception and Marriott points). I then talked to the front desk employee who in turn talked to his manager. They would give me the internet service for $5. Needless to say, I am changing hotels tomorrow. This hotel is not so wonderful that I'm willing to pay $55 for internet service for the week.
As for the American Grill restaurant, I usually don't eat at hotel restaurants, but I didn't want to go in search of food for dinner. I'm glad I ate at the hotel this time. The American Grill may have served me the best meal that I've ever had! Cast Iron Seared Beef Tenderloin grilled to 'medium' perfection, huge tender chunks of Alaskan King Crab, garlic horseradish cream, asparagus, crispy potato cake. With the Caesar's salad and delicious bread basket (and a beer), it was absolutely worth the $48 price tag for one person. The wait staff also followed up frequently (but not annoyingly so) to see that I had everything I needed.

name: Harrington Hotel
title: “All factors considered, not bad”
text:
The Harrington is steps away from everything worth seeing, this is the most important part (for my husband and I, anyway). If you are looking for a spa-like retreat, this hotel is not for you. 
The hotel is old and run-down (some might find this charming?), but the staff is cheerful and helpful. Because of its central location, book early - we stayed there at the end of May 2011 and there were at least 2 large groups of teenagers staying there (we're talking 60-75 people per group) and the hotel was booked solid.
Our small queen room faced a brick wall (it was on the inside of the building, on the 9th floor) but we did not hear a sound from the busy streets below (this was a common complaint we overheard from other guests - the hotel is at a very busy intersection in Washington DC's business district)
There is no parking on the premises, their parking garage is about two blocks away, a brisk 5 minute walk from the hotel; they charge $15 per day. It is best to park the car and walk, as almost everything you want is very close by, including shopping, restaurants, coffee shops and monuments.
There are two restaurants downstairs, one a breakfast place (which we did not visit) and sports bars with mediocre food, tired wait staff and $12 pitchers of beer.
We would definitely stay here again, you can't beat that location!

name: Melrose Hotel, Washington DC
title: “What Happened to You Get what you pay for?”
text:
I stayed at this hotel because my company recommended it. Pros- rooms are a good size with couch and two chairs,a and separate work space. Cons- limited cable channels, older hotel with dated decor. 
I had to call front desk staff several times because there was no information in the room about the hotel. No gift shop or place to get bottled water, snacks etc. Main restaurant closed. 
I have stayed at much nicer hotels with more amenities for less money

name: Channel Inn Hotel
title: “I would rather be smacked in the nuts with a sledgehammer than ever stay at that sploogerific dump again”
text:
Had to do a two week stint at the Washington Navy Yard -- usually get berthing at the Navy Lodge in Anacostia (not so good) or at Bolling AFB (nice!). For some reason there was nothing available, so I was told to get a hotel in town. It's not far from the Yard, so I chose the Channel Inn. 
A grievous error on so many grounds. First, the place is in A SLUM, no two ways about it. I'm from the Bronx and even I was uneasy in that hood. Second, the place is filthy, top to bottom. Third, the staff is so rude, it's unbelievable. 
The place blows syphilitic goats.

name: DoubleTree Suites Washington, DC
title: “Roomy, Reasonable, Rooftop Pool, Best Location”
text: I have been staying in the area since my son started GWU. We've had all good experiences but I would have to say that the value of the Doubletree Suites is superior. The location makes it work. The pool was a real perk as it was very hot the first day i arrived. It's a small pool but the water was clean and refreshing and I was the only person swimming. I felt very relaxed watching the planes flying overhead while enjoying a dip. The staff was friendly and helpful. I would definitely stay here again as I said, it is the best value in town. I did not even need all the amenities the suite offered. I was by myself but if you're bringing kids or family members, it gives lots of room to spread out.

name: Harrington Hotel
title: “Great location, old world charm rooms”
text:
The best location one can get (5 minutes walk from the mall, 2 mins from FBI Edgar Hoover building, 10 minutes from the white house) for this price in Washington. Rooms have old world charm (and some of the bathroom walls and bathtubs show that!). Air con was good, rooms large with tv (no fridge or tea-coffee... ;-( ) 
They serve a very good and filling buffet continental breakfast at the restaurant below for 11 dollars. There is also a 24 hour Mc Donalds closeby - but why would you want to poison yourselves with that, huh?
The wireless internet is not so good - signal is poor in many rooms.
Also, some single rooms are really tiny. The reception is very helpful. The rooms are all well decorated - the colours adn tapestries give you a feel of living in a historical place (it IS hundred years old!)

name: Capitol Skyline Hotel
title: “excellent service!”
text: service staff were the friendliest and most helpful i've met in a long time. always ready to lend a hand, provide guidance and suggestions and very warm to guests!

name: Melrose Hotel, Washington DC
title: “tired hotel”
text: soggy beds, dirty rooms, poor service, bad food, expensive do not go there !!!

name: Four Points by Sheraton
title: “Not fancy but really nice”
text: The hotel looks small (small lobby for instance), but it is also modern and clean. The staff is very nice and helpful. The swimming pool on the rooftop is a bit disappointing: quite small and the air (yes, the air, not the water) is totally overheated (in summer !). The hotel is also very well located. The rooms are small but quite nice.

name: Harrington Hotel
title: “Much better than I expected!”
text: After reading some negative reviews I wasn't sure what to expect but luckily we booked a room anyway and were very pleased. Yes, it's an older building but I think that added to its charm. The room was very clean and cleaned well every day (3 night stay). Everyone working there was very friendly and helpful. The Hotel was full for the Cherry Blossom Festival yet we didn't hear any noise from the rooms nearby or in the halls. We had 2 windows, one in the bedroom and one in the bath. Lots of natural light if desired. Parking is extremely reasonable and you can't ask for a better location! The nearest Metro station is only 2 blocks away and many of the sights are in walking distance. We'd be happy to stay at the Harrington next time in D.C.

name: The Churchill Hotel
title: “Pleasant Historic Hotel Currently In Midst of Renovations”
text: I always enjoy staying at the Churchill as it is so comfortable an environment and feels like an apartment (as it once was) rather than a hotel room. It is definitely an older hotel but management is constantly maintaining and replacing, as they are doing now, and it does not feel run down, dirty or tired. I also like the location since it is so near transportation and outstanding food options. A great hotel for a DC experience.

name: Capitol Skyline Hotel
title: “A good place to stay in DC”
text: We spent 3 days in this hotel, it was pretty close to tourist attractions, there was a free shuttle to Capitol, musuems,etc. The breakfast was awsome and it was included in the price, rooms and bathrooms were pretty clean. The only problem was our room was facing a busy street so a lot of noise and sirens. In general we liked it.

name: Courtyard Washington, DC / U.S. Capitol
title: “Location a minus”
text:
Overall an okay place to stay depending on what you're looking for. The hotel is new and clean. Rooms were small, comfortable. We asked to move to a different location as we were next to the elevator and our second room was larger. Staff was accomodating in this and most respects. Service with breakfast was a bit slow and heard several complaints from folks. 
I'd stay here if I were traveling alone or on business. Also would probably be a good, inexpensive place to stay with children. It's easy to get on the subway (<1 block) and minutes to Union Station, Capital, etc. 
We were there with parents celebrating a special weekend, so not the ideal location as not much in the surrounding area within walking distance to see/do/eat. There's definitely not much in terms of dining located nearby. You pretty much need to take the subway for any dining or nightlife. Basically, the hotel's a good place to crash but has not real ambiance. 
Definitely don't wait on a cab from the hotel or you will be waiting for 30-45 minutes. Take the train 1 stop to Union and catch a cab there. A bit of a disappointment that it's difficult to get a cab from the hotel. 
Agree with reviewers that would not venture out into the surrounding communities, but felt safe walking between the subway & hotel.

name: Channel Inn Hotel
title: “lots of potential, lost every opportunity”
text: My stay was so disappointing. The location was so pretty but the hotel is falling apart. The carpets are bumpy and filfthy. The bedspread had a cigarette burn in it. The pillows are flat and the sheets on the bed didn't even fit the mattress. The staff at the desk were indifferent. The coffee house was crummmy and the food totally unimaginative. No one at this hotel has made any effort to make it nice. Sorry to say.

name: Harrington Hotel
title: “Extremely Convient, Great Price but....”
text: You have to be willing to remember that this hotel is just a place to sleep. For the price, and DC is EXPENSIVE, it was a steal. This place is really old, that's probably it's biggest problem. There is a horrible smell in the lobby like everyone says, but it's only in the lobby. Everything else in the hotel is adequate. It's very basic, the room kind of reminded me of an old roadside motel. But it wasn't frightening. I won't give you scary warnings of "stay away!!!" But keep your expectations low. As for its location, I don't think you can beat it. Two blocks from the center of the Mall, surrounded by restaurants and other sights, is pretty ideal. So keep your sense of humor and remember that you're probably there to see DC not to spend your days in a hotel room.

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Capitol
title: “A terrible place to stay.”
text: As long as you never have to speak to the staff, are not in your room from 6-9 PM, and don't mind a semi dilapidated room, it is probably an OK place to stay. The staff is not only rude, but the manager just keeps telling me he doesn't know what happened so he can't address it. The mini fridge doesn't work. The handle to the closet was busted. And from 6-9 PM they have extremely loud live music blasting from one of the hotel restaurants. The incessant thumping is intolerable. Only after repeated complaints was I offered another room, and by then it was late the last night of my stay. All the staff and manager would say to me over and over was "I apologize, but there is nothing I can do." One last thing. The room service is overpriced and well below average. Buffalo wings were undercooked and bloody.

name: W Washington DC
title: “Ok but not great”
text: Great location but misses the mark for a Starwood property. We were offered paper deliver for our 5 days here. Did we ever receive a paper in the morning, NO. One morning the concierge went and retrieved a ppaper for us, after we called, the we gave up. J&G steakhouse/ restaurant in the hotel is a must miss. Terrible service, wait for dinner, food doesn't match up to the chefs typical high quality food. The positives are the location, Starwood points, and the rooftop lounge. Otherwise I suggest another hotel.

name: Georgetown Suites
title: “I would stay here again, again, and again!”
text:
I was a little concerned about booking this hotel after reading tripadvisor reviews. However, I am so glad we did! It is in the best area of Georgetown. You are one block from M street. The hotel was easy to get in and out of with the car on the narrow streets. We parked and walked or used the metro. We stayed here for 3 days. I book on Internet and got a great rate that included parking, breakfast and Internet. We had a studio for the 3 of us which was very roomy. We did not use the cooking facilities, but it was nice to have a refrigerator for water bottles. 
The room was SUPER clean. The decor was a little outdated, but the cleanliness made up for it. Upon check out the hotel did bill be 30.00 per day for pakring, however, when I questioned them, they removed it quickly. 
The breakfast was your standard continental. They did have a nice variety of breads, muffins, scones. Howver, the selection changed everyday. So, the cranberry ornage bread that I loved the first day, I did not see again. They also had sausage and bacon biscuits that you could heat up in the microwave. My daughter tried one and liked it well enough. 
Hotel is about a 20 minute walk to Foggy Bottom metro. But it was an enjoyable walk. 
I would stay here again! The walk along the canal is amazing. 
Almost forgot to mention the air conditioning that people complained about.....our air worked most of the time. We left one day and came back to a stifling room. My husband messed with the thermostat and the air came back on. It would work for a few hours and then go out again. This was not a problem if we were in the room. During the night it always went out. One night we slept without covers because it was so hot. However, after that, my husband got up in the middle of the night a couple of times and messed with thermostat and it came back on. A little nuisance but since it did turn back on with some help we never bothered to complain. 
We were on the second floor and there was a street lamp right outside our window that shined directly in! We had room darkening curtains that helped a lot! I would request a room away from that lamp though.

name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center
title: “Nice return visit”
text:
Concierge Lynn Jason is outstanding. We returned for another visit following our April, 2010 visit because of her. 
The hotel rooms are starting to show wear. No more turn down service.
As a SPG member we were upgraded to an outside room. Very Nice.
Room was not vacuumed as well as it could have been. Hallway wasn't vacuumed either.
Asked for feather free pillows. Very lumpy, Not foam. Do not know what they were.

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Capitol
title: “Clean But Dated /Convenient Location”
text:
Really great location near Capital Hill and 1 block from the Metro(L'Enfant Station) that will take you anywhere in the city AND a quick 10 minute subwayride to Regan Natl Airport. Also 1/2 block from the suburban train station. Friendly staff too. Otherwise average experience, clean,
but rooms are from the Farris Bueller era.

name: W Washington DC
title: “Falls short considering price”
text: I give it an average grade when putting in the mix with all hotels. For high end properties, I would drop one mark and list it as poor. Yes, it's very slick looking and tres chic on the surface. Bed is very comfortable, linens are great and I liked the shower, front desk staff helpful. Hotel lacks the little things that make it above average for a business traveler. Shouldn't have to crawl on my knees to find a plug for my laptop or cell phone charger (or an iron). Would a cup of good coffee in the room be too much to ask for? There is a card that says a coffee maker is available, just call down or come fetch a cup of complimentary coffee in the the lobby. Please don't make me do that. And if you're a tea or decaf drinker -- now you have to beg for a cup of that from someone in the lobby as it's not part of the set up (and they returned to tell my husband decaf was unavailable). Seems like in their quest for a spare, uncluttered look, they forego some of those extras. Rooms are geared the same way. Their cutesy stuff takes up too much of the premium real estate on desk tops. Give me enough room to put out my laptop and work without having to pile up other stuff and rearrange. At their rates, I expect a little more. Bottom line -- the W sacrifices services to guests so they can have a hotel that projects their branded look.

name: Harrington Hotel
title: “close to everything!!”
text: Initially our group of 6 had rented a brownstone, but being in a shady part of town, we decided not to stay there and found the Harrington in the yellow pages. They had a room available that would sleep six, almost impossible to find in a hotel, without paying a fortune. The staff was really nice and helpful. Anything we asked for we received. I needed to print our boarding passes before leaving and was able to since there was a computer room with a printer guests could use. The hotel is old, but it was actually a nice change, it definitely has character. There is a large refrigerator in the room, which was nice. The location was awesome!! Like three blocks from everything!! White House, National Mall and one block from Metro Center Station. No problem with noise at night, but the city noises wake you early in the am, which wasn't a problem since we were up early to sightsee anyway. If you don't mind staying in a place that isn't brand new, spotless and fancy, this is a great place, great price.

name: Washington Marriott Wardman Park
title: “Great room, horrible business center”
text:
The room was great - newly renovated (as is much of the hotel, reportedly), comfortable, everything worked fine and was clean. No minibar, for some reason - the space where it would be was empty. 
For $400 a night (paid for by work, but still), I would have expected free wi-fi in the rooms - and really, all over the hotel. No such luck. They charged $10 (I think) if you access the internet in your room. So I figured I'd try their business center. Very hard to locate, and I could hardly believe my eyes when I finally found it. A row of maybe 6 computers, none of which connected successfully to the printer. Not a soul around to help. An internet charge of $6 for 20 minutes. And the weirdest thing of all - instead of regular Windows or some other normal operating system, all the computers were outfitted with some weird system called iBahn, which was very constraining and difficult to navigate (for example, when I tried to access an attachment to an email - I imagine it's still there on the computer, but I could not for the life of me figure out how to delete it - and I'm not a computer imbecile!).
I hosted a work event there for 75 people - it went fine, and the food and service were good. It was near impossible to figure out the billing, but they let us hold the event.
When all was said and done, nice place to sleep, but not worth the high price tag.

name: Melrose Hotel, Washington DC
title: “disappointing”
text: I was very disappointed with the hotel. It had a 4 star rating and but there is no way it was actually 4 star. The hallways, rooms, and bathrooms were dated. There was nothing particularly redeeming about the hotel except for its proximity to the GWU metro station. The area the hotel is in is very nice though. I wouldnt recommend the hotel and definitely wouldnt stay there again.

name: Hamilton Crowne Plaza Hotel
title: “Appears too be under New Management..”
text:
Stayed here for the third (3rd) time the forth (4th) of July week. I will only say that it appeared under a different Management then previous visits. This is obvious in the service, throughout the facility. Mainly in the restaurant area. Ate there the first (1st) night and opted for other options the remainder of the trip. The food was "DEAD" (i.e. without any love) on arrival to the table. 
I hope the new management gets it's hands around this area, quickly.. Love the location but, the optics of the lack of Service Concerns with management, troubles me in this economy.

name: L'Enfant Plaza Hotel
title: “Nothing spectacular, but the location makes it worth while”
text: We spent June 30th thru July 6th, over the 4th of July. The price and location make it worthwhile. Although the cost of parking our car seemed outlandish to us, when averaged in with the cost of the room it was still more affordable than anything else in the Capitol hill area. The front desk was very friendly during check-in. I wish we had taken other reviewers advice and not eaten in the bar, mainly because cokes were in bottles rather than fountain drinks, so we were billed for each of our son's refills, which got expensive real quick. The beer selection was abysmal. At least the staff were pleasant there as well. The TV channel selection in both the 'brewpub' and the room were a joke, but we weren't in Washington DC to watch TV. The elevators from the hotel to the mall below and the metro were slow and crowded. And most of the restaurants in the food court between the mall and the metro were closed over the weekend - not sure if it was because it was the weekend or due to ongoing renovations, but it was a disadvantage. The room itself was nothing stellar, but neither was it horrible. It probably could use a renovation. Whomever was responsible for picking up room services was lax, trays stayed in the hallways for hours. One huge plus is the proximity of this hotel to the metro. We were able to get to restaurants and to a National's baseball game quickly and without hassle with the hotel right over the metro.

name: Harrington Hotel
title: “Convenient and Inexpensive”
text: I frequently work at the National Archives in DC and a number of years ago my wife and I discovered the Harrington. It is the most convenient hotel without spending a fortune you can find in downtown Washington. A short block north of Pennsylvania Avenue, it is the ideal place for people on a budget and for people who are satisifed with a clean comfortable room and no great aminities. It's old (but always being improved) but clean with a two places to eat at the site (Harry's and Harriet's). It's often filled with groups but of the many times I've stayed there, I've never found that a problem. In fact, my wife & I have often enjoyed meeting the young people who are there on school trips from all over the world. I have recommended the Harrington to numerous other people - many genealogists such as myself to work at the Archives - and they all agree as to its convenience and affordability.

name: Georgetown Suites
title: “Family Holiday”
text:
WOW!!! Great hotel in a Great location!!!!!! 
I stayed there a few weeks ago with my wife and 11 month old baby daughter. It's a 15 minute walk to the subway. Rooms were great, service was great, location was great... Everything was great... The staff were a little too professional in my opinion. Not as relaxed and happy and bubbly as other places I visited in the US. BUT hey, I can't fault them for that. They were spot on with everything and extremely helpful whenever I asked a question... 
This place and the staff are FANTASTIC for those visiting DC... Everything about this place was excellent and I highly recommend this to anyone visiting DC. I WILL stay there again next time I visit DC. My only regret is we didn't stay there longer.

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Capitol
title: “Excellent hotel for a family to stay in”
text: Excellent and obviously recently refurbished hotel. The staff were very helpful and the rooms were spacious and clean. It is sooooo centrally located, with the air & space museum only 5 mins walk away, capital hill 15mins, metro 5 mins and the shuttle bus to Dulles airport 5 mins(to Hazy museum if you loved the air & space museum - is a must!). Also, the head office of NASA is around the corner (hidden of course) and a supermarket 15 mins walk away. For dinner at night it is a little isolated, but we could eat in the restaurant - it had fancy as well as plain type food. The food was excellent and kids ate free! Take-away was also an option.

name: Melrose Hotel, Washington DC
title: “Absolute Dump!!”
text: This hotel is seriously like a hostel. The staff is not friendly nor helpful at all. The room had a very funky odor that you immediately smelled once you opened the door. The furniture was old and the room was very dated and worn. The towels were old and the shower curtain had mold on it. The desk chair was stained and not sturdy. The pillows were fiber and extremely flat. The restaurant buffet and breakfast is absolutely gross for the price and the service is very very poor. I complained upon checkout and not much was really done about it nor did I feel they even cared.

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Capitol
title: “Close to the National Air and Space Museum”
text: I'm in the hotel right now and have been here 4 nights. I was surprised when I checked in because I'll be here for 10 nights they told me that if I checked out early I'd have a $100 fee. I've spent more nights in hotels than I care to. This hotel is average to worn condition, but the people are friendly and it's within walking distance of the Capitol and the National Mall. L'enfant Plaza Metro Station is a block away I always get turned around in there and never know which exit to take. There's a nice Safeway one metro stop away at Waterfront, and there's a CVS Pharmacy very close by, a Quiznos, and a McDonalds. I haven't tried the restaurant in the hotel. The bar was really loud on Wednesday and it's right there in the lobby. When I arrived there were a lot of people in power wheelchairs - I spoke to their group leader or guide - he said they were there to support disabled people living on their own and to not be forced into care facilities or something like that. This group seemed to be doing okay with this hotel. I washed a load of jeans that I bought at Macy's Metro Center and the laundry room is decently equipped but a few of the machines were out of order. The concierge desk guy is probably in the wrong job and the reason I say that is he's not really talkative. The gift shop is a packed little store and a little odd to navigate through. The business center is well equipped, and it was busy Friday afternoon with people checking in online and printing boarding passes. The room is worn, the desk chair has the arm covering peeled off on the left arm, and the furniture is ding'd and scratched and old. The TV is nice, the satellite service messes up sometimes but that may have been the weather. I have a courtyard view which is quiet. The shower has a good flow and the water temp is steady. The bed is very comfortable. The rooms heat and A/C unit is right next to the desk which makes it uncomfortable to work at the desk. The rooms ethernet cable connecton didn't work so I'm left to use the unsecured wireless connection which I'm uncomfortable about. I called their internet support and they worked with me a lot about the internet connection and they came to the conclusion that the modem is bad, but I haven't asked the front desk about it yet. Unsecured wireless is not good - I was just briefed at work about how bad it is to use unsecured wireless. The room has a small fridge which is convenient for cold drinks and left overs. Overall it's a decent place for the price, but if you're a picky person there's a lot you could complain about if you choose to.

name: Washington Marriott Wardman Park
title: “Great Marriott bargain in DC”
text: Found an excellent bargain through Priceline.Com and was given the Marriott Wardman Park in the Dupont Circle/Adams Morgan area of Washington DC. Excellent location just 1 Metro stop north of Dupont Circle right at the entrance to the hotel. Everything you expect from a Marriott (very clean/well appointed room, great linens, and VERY comfortable bed). Hotel is under some major remodeling/construction, but definately worth the stay for a very reasonable price.

name: Hamilton Crowne Plaza Hotel
title: “Nice stay and great service”
text: I'm from Maryland but stayed at the Crowne Plaza to avoid multiple drives for some events I was attending in DC. The staff was very friendly and helpful. My room was on the 11th floor and had a great city view. Prior to arriving I had read several reviews stating that the hotel was older but my room was really nice and well maintained. The hotel is centrally located with metro access within a block - note that overnight parking is very difficult to find on the weekends ( I had to pay $44 (with fee) for valet). The do have a Starbucks and a restaurant onsite and there are multiple food options in the area. Overall, I would definitely recommend this hotel if you are headed to DC.

name: Melrose Hotel, Washington DC
title: “Great value and great location”
text:
I stayed at the Melrose over the Memorial holiday. Based on some reviews I was a little nervous. I was looking for and got a great deal (especially for DC) on the hotel website...$88/nite for the king. Everyone I dealt with was nice and not over attentive.
The room was great (and they should buy some new pillows) but I was very comfortable. I had a chair w/ ottoman and a loveseat and refrigerator. It's not luxurious but a steal at the price. There was no problem with early check-in and they held my bags after check out. I did not eat at restaurant or drink at the bar. The bar looked comfortable though.
Great access to public transportation. Easy walk to Georgtown shopping and restaurants. Ask for nearby food stores for snacking.

name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center
Capitol Skyline Hotel
title: “Bellissime stanze ma posizione scomoda”
text: Siamo stati in questo hotel solo due notti. Da fuori non è granchè, un casermone di cemento. Le stanze però sono enormi e pulite. La cabina armadio è grande quasi quanto tutta la stanza del nostro hotel a NY. Il letto sarebbe bastato per 6 persone!! E' situato appena fuori dal centro di Washington, dalle finestre si vede la cupola del Campidoglio. La metropolitana non è vicinissima ma l'hotel offre un servizio gratuito di navetta che porta sia alla fermata della metro che in altre zone del centro. Funziona solo in andata, per il ritorno consiglio vivamente il taxi, da qualsiasi punto del centro bastano 7-8 dollari per tornare in albergo. Portatevi sempre dietro l'indirizzo perchè un paio di taxisti non lo conoscevano. La zona attorno all'albergo è tutta in costruzione (palazzi per uffici), tra qualche anno penso che sarà in una posizione ottima per viaggi di lavoro. Colazione: 18$ in hotel oppure McDonalds a 150 mt.

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Central / White House
title: “Nice place to stay. Good rooms.”
text:
The hotel is a little too far away from the metro (during hot wheater). The rooms are excelent. Great beds Bathroom is not big, but good. 
The people at the reception are no rocketscientists. I speak rather good English, but have to ask all the time everything twice. 
The lobby needs a quick make over. It is really old fashioned. The elevators are a real drama. 
The people at the restaurant need a course for better service.

name: L'Enfant Plaza Hotel
title: “Would stay here again!”
text:
We booked this hotel due to location and proximity to the sights we wanted to see while we were visiting Washington. We flew into Ronald Reagan Airport and took the Metro to the L'enfant Plaza Stop.
From that point we had a little issue getting to the hotel as there are no signs. I called the front desk and got bad directions and it took us about 45 minutes to find the hotel from that point. The only bad thing about this is there were 6 adults and 2 children and we had lots of luggage and strollers to lug around. If you book this hotel, please make sure to get directions to the lobby before you get off the metro (we figured out if you took the exit that had the astronaut with the dog it led you right up to the lobby)
After we finally found the hotel, things were great. Staff was nice and courteous. There are a few places to eat and shop under the hotel (a cvs, a mcdonalds and a few various other restaurants) but the hours are funny, so just shop in the morning before you go and leave stuff in your room. We asked for a refrigerator, which they gladly provided upon arrival and even had connecting rooms, which was great for the kids to go visit their grandparents.
The hotel has a Starbucks (once again only open in the morning) and a restaurant downstairs (not sure of the hours). But food was decent. VERY EXPENSIVE though, (one bottle of Corona and two cans of coke set us back $16) so if you can help it, shop at the CVS downstairs. 
The pool looked very nice, however we did not take advantage of it, because the pool is open from 10 a.m to 8 pm with a lifeguard on duty, and our hours were slightly different.
The proximity is within 2 blocks (long blocks) to the Smithsonian Castle and right through there is the Mall.
We flew in, but if you drive in, parking is $42 per night, which is pricey, but you are staying right in the heart of Washington D.C. We visited Capitol Hill, the Zoo and the main attractions and spent less then $10 per person on our Metro Cards, which is a bonus of staying here.
Overall, it is an older hotel, but I would stay here again in a second, if I got a chance. The rooms were clean and stayed cool, despite the heat outside. The beds were comfortable, even though they were full size, were long.
Overall, I would say this is a great place to stay and would stay there again.

name: Grand Hyatt Washington
title: “Location, location, location”
text: Nice rooms with comfortable beds, even nicer suites if you splurge. The metro goes right into the hotel - so convenient! Front desk agents very friendly and efficient. Very nice lounge with food and drinks for those who have access. Great restaurants around the location.

name: The Churchill Hotel
title: “I sad dissapointment”
text:
My wife and I had stayed here last year and as a result of that experience I booked a room at the Churchill for 5 nights. This is a very old hotel and as such one expects bumps in the floor and the odd 400 year old settling issue. I was however very dissapointed at the band aid maintenance going on in this hotel and I felt the maintenance staff was not taking on the responsibilty of maintaining a national treasure. Tiles on the floor were loose on the my bathroom floor without any grout and the smell of rotting wood was very noticable. The wall paper looked like it had been applied by a 14 year and the way the room had been painted numerous time relayed to me a lack of repect for this historic hotel. During my visit I had the oportunity to see and overhear some of the instructions passed out to various staff as to how to deal with ongoing maintenance issues at the hotel. Myself, being a project manager, some of those folks would no longer have employement with this hotel.
I am from the West Coast of Canada and we do not have buildings of this age. However I can assure you we do not treat our heritage with such disrespect and negligence. I will not stay at the Churchill again, but I feel a temendous sadness for the way this piece of American heritage is being treated.

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Capitol
title: “LOCATION!!”
text: Just a block from the Air & Space Museum and close to the mall. Easy walking to just about every DC attaction. Hotel is clean. Pool is great for cooling off on a hot day although not very luxurious. Breakfast buffett is good and very convenient. Bar/restaurant is okay and nice place to unwind. Starbucks in the lobby is a plus. Taxi's always available, never a wait. You do get a little noise from the train track that is nearby but the location is worth it. One block to L'enfant Plaza Metro stop.

name: Harrington Hotel
title: “Tourist Hotel Character”
text: As a regular at tourist hotels in America and Britain, I liked this place. Most hotels frown on a family of five and make us feel like we had "one too many." Here, our spacious room was set up for five. It was quiet. We slept all night. We walked to all the attractions. The price was half that of its neighbors. But like any old tourist hotel, it has character and you need it too. Roll with the quirks, and both your feet and pocketbook will thank you.

name: Georgetown Suites
title: “Great location but lacking hospitality”
text: Family of 4 with a 17yr old & 7yr old so I always book in advance & pay up front to get a King suite with a sofa bed NON smoking, with that said this is how it went. Called ahead an hour before arrival so everything would be ready for faster check in, I was told we were booked for the other building across the street but she would let them know we were on our way. When we arrived front desk clerk was not notified so here goes the 30 min wait checking us in “ Oh I’m sorry we don’t seem to have the room you wanted but we do have a smoking Queen suite” I said no I paid in advance for a NON smoking King suite over a month ago why don’t I have the room I paid for?? I can’t put a 7yr old girl with her 17 yr old brother on a sofa bed he would kill me. We get a King so she sleeps with us and her brother gets the sofa bed. We had been driving in the rain for 12 hrs and we just wanted to relax. After the front desk clerk called her manager at the other building they decided to accommodate us with a Non smoking Queen & a roll away bed but they said they wouldn’t charge for the roll away. Ya Think!! It took them 1 ½ hrs to bring us the roll away after my husband called the front desk twice to remind them. On a good note even though the rooms are very outdated they are clean large suites with a kitchen, dining area & living room. The queen size bedroom with one night stand & no windows was small and odd. We were on the 4th floor room 403 with a nice view of the court yard and houses next to the hotel. The location of the hotel is wonderful, you can walk to restaurants and shops all over M street. The only other thing would be the garage, it’s a tight squeeze but they did let us keep are car there till 3PM on the day we checked out so that was cool. Overall I just wished we had the room I paid for that was updated and maybe some protein at breakfast all pastries, yogurt, & bagels. Some hotels go out of their way to make you happy and some just don’t care.

name: W Washington DC
title: “there are + and -”
text:
first the "+": the views from the 10th floor was awesome. the location next to the white house and the easy walk to the national mall were a blessing.
the service was incredibly good as well. staff is very responsive. a member brought my email to me when i could not print it out due to a business center printer issue. she had me email it to her and it took all of 5 minutes..good job.. the food in the restraunt was great, especailly breakfast. the bed was comfortable and you sleep like a baby..we were warned about the noise but it was not noticable, maybe we were on the north end of the building and the noise is on the south end. try the giner margaritas and the ginger sodas it is a house recipe and the giner is made from scratch.
now the "-": wife complained there was not enough light to do her makeup..and very little sink space , this was a better room (deluxe) for a solo business traveler not a couple, the worst thing was the shower.. it is rromy and thw water pressure and volume are excellent but the floor is slippery and i mean slippery. it is dangerous. when you open the door it knocks the towels off the wall hanger onto the usually wet floor from water leaking out of the shower door. we had to call for toilet paper on 3 different days. they left only one roll with no back up. it may seem more of an annoyance but i could not get change for a 100 dollar bill at the desk on 4 different days at different times. weird. they sent me to the bar twice and they couldnt do it either since the guy didnt have a register key.. weird..

name: The Churchill Hotel
