title: “Excellent location in Washington DC”
text:
Have just returned from 5 night stay at the Hotel Churchill, nr Dupont Circle. Despite some negative reviews on Trip Advisor, we decided to go ahead and book and were extremely pleased both with the hotel accommodation and helpfulness of the staff. The rooms are larger than usual city-size rooms and had nice seating area with sofa, lamp and fridge, which meant that we had somewhere to relax in our room when we were too tired to go out again in the evening after walking all day long. Everything was provided, including iron and ironing board in room, fridge and flat screen tvs. We found free internet access in adjoining bar extremly useful and always managed to find a free computer when we wanted it. Didn't have breakfast in hotel as quite expensive, but found plenty of places on our walks to have something to eat.
Hotel in excellent area, with beautiful streets just behind it with some lovely character buildings, including houses where Hilary Clinton and Ted Kennedy reside. Well worth walking round if you are interested in architecture. Several Embassies in surrounding roads as well. Dupont Circle about a 5 - 10 minute walk away. Quite scruffy, but plenty of places to eat and handy for metro system.
Lots to see in Washington and many things, such as Museums and National Botanical Gardens, are free! Easy to walk to historic Georgetown from hotel - lots of good shops there, places to eat and, again, interesting to explore back streets there with beautiful characterful properties.
To sum up, for us the Churchill Hotel was an excellent place to stay and we loved the location. Washington itself is a great city to visit with lots to do.

name: Harrington Hotel
title: “For Washington DC $$, its a good bargain”
text:
We stayed the week before Easter and had a great experience. Our room was more than adequate, since we were rarely there for more than a few hours a day. The room was cleaned every day, with fresh towels. The bed was comfortable. For two people, we had plenty of room (12x12), with a decent sized closet. Ask for a mini frig before you show up. It was nice to be able to relax with something cold in your room after a long day of sight-seeing. Plus it is nice to be able to store left-overs from the night before. The temperature was just right, thus we did not need to worry about heat or air conditioning, and can't comment on that aspect of the hotel. Sure the place is old, but it shows its age well.
It has to be one of the most convienent places to stay. Not only easy walking distance to the mall, but a whole slew of bus stops to anywhere in the city within a one block radius, and 2 blocks from the metro. There is absolutely no need for a car if you don't plan to travel outside the DC area.
The morning breakfast place in the hotel is very convenient, with lots of freshly made hot meal choices. We always showed up early to "beat the rush", that was never all that crowded anyway. It was just a bit on the pricey side, but not outrageous considering the convenience.
The attached lunch and dinner restaurant was always crowded, including the outside seating. We never tried it, had too many other "fancy eating places" to go to.
Considering the next least expensive place we found while researching downtown hotels averaged $175, the $99 price tag was a real bargain for what you got. I would have no qualms about staying here again.
On another subject: I have to say that we had a great experience with all the workers who make things go in Washington DC. Everyone we had contact with, from the bus drivers, hotel staff, wait staff, museum staff, everyone, all these people were considerate, friendly and helpful. Washington DC is a unique American city that everyone must experience at least once.

name: Washington Hilton
title: “Just What I Needed”
text: We had a White House tour planned and wanted to be able to walk over there, so this was a convenient location. The room was spacious, comfortable bed - only downside is there is a wi-fi charge for the room. Parking is expensive, but I purchased a package that included the parking fee plus the breakfast buffet the next morning - and we felt that was fair. I would stay there again.

name: W Washington DC
title: “Great Location, excellent service”
text:
I was in DC for some business meetings and chose the W because I could walk to a few of the appointments. The location couldn't have been better. When I checked in, the front desk agent was very friendly. She asked for my SPG status and then helped find a nice view for me. Nice touch. The doorman was great, every time I walked in and out, he was engaged and helpful. Confirmed my directions a couple times as well, really good service.
My room was pretty small, not sure if that's standard, but definitely one fo the smaller Starwood rooms I've ever been in. The desk was useable for laptops and the internet speed was fast. The bathroom was fairly large compared to the rest of the room. The closet was not designed well as you have to stand in front of the toilet to open it. Very strange, definitely a design flaw as there is nowhere to put your suitcase when unpacking except back around the corner in the bedroom. Shower was a good size.
Overall, it was a great stay, if you can past the small room. If not for that, it would have been a 5.

name: Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill
title: “Hôtel à Washington près de Union Station & Capitol”
text: Chic et confortable. Hall de l'hôtel spectaculaire. Hôtel très bien situé. La propreté de la salle de bain laissait à désirer. Stationnement très dispendieux en surplus du prix de la chambre. Extra pour avoir l'internet dans la chambre.

name: Melrose Hotel, Washington DC
title: “Consistently excellent”
text:
We stayed at the Melrose several times during our visits to Washington, DC and every time it's been a no-headache, comfortable stay. 
The location is great, it's steps away from Georgetown shopping area, metro, and walking distance to all the sites of interest as well as the hiking trails along the river. 
The service is always consistently polite with all our requests satisfied promptly. The service is not intrusive but extremely effective, which is awesome if you want to feel more like at home. We never had problems with the rooms, our requested king size non-smoking always available upon the check-in even late at night. 
The rooms are clean and are furnished in more of the 'traditional european style' than modern. If you are looking for a swanky Kimpton type of property or a W type this is not it. It's comfortable, the rooms are a good size and it's QUIET despite the fact that there are some busy streets around. Never a problem with the noise from neighbors or parties or traffic at least during our stays. The beds are fairly comfortable although the matresses and pillows are old. The only complaint I have is that they don't have down/feather pillows - which is something I always expect a 4 star property would have. But they always get us down pillows upon request, only once we had to wait for 1 night as they had none available since we checked in very late. 
If you are looking for a comfortable no-nonsense reasonably priced accommodations in the middle of the great location then this is definitely the choice. I've stayed at many hotels in DC including Westins (both embassy row and westin grand), some boutique Kimpton properties, Marriotts and Sheratons outside of the city but Melrose was really the only hotel where I had a NO HEADACHE stay consistently. We never had problems with the bills, checking in or out, getting the room we want, noise, attitude problems from staff, inedequate housekeeping etc. I think the management of this place definitely knows what they are doing. If this place only had updated the rooms with newer beds I would not even consider staying anywhere else.

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Central / White House
title: “Very Good Value for Downtown DC”
text: We stayed for the Easter Holiday in DC. The hotel was well situated, anything closer to the Mall would be two to three times the price. The room was exceptionally clean and the beds were INCREDIBLY comfortable. Same with the pillows!!! Since we normally only sleep and shower at hotels when we travel, I don't need tons of amenities and prefer a lower price to tons of extras. This hotel fit the bill perfectly. The staff was courteous and helpful, the restaurant clean and well priced and our room was perfect for what we paid. A taxi to the corner where the Washington Monument is only cost us $7 mid morning, less than it would cost for 4 passes on the Metro.

name: Renaissance Washington, DC Dupont Circle Hotel
title: “Very comfortable and convenient”
text: We picked this hotel because of its proximity to DuPont Circle for a two night stay. Despite its name it is a few blocks away but the neighbourhood is lovely. The staff are very professional and helpful. Our room was spacious and quiet. The hotel seemed much more personal thn it's size would suggest.

name: Harrington Hotel
title: “Location...it's a dump”
text:
After traveling many hours and arriving during a storm, we had no choice but to check in. The lobby had a strong smell of I don't know what. The walk to parking is a long 4 blocks. The room was not clean, needed to be vacumed, and was really old. My 8 year old pointed to the smoke detector and asked what it was...... One of the beds stunk and was rendered useless. Needless to say we checked out first thing. 
I was not expecting a four star but based on reviews I did expect hospitalitiy, I saw none. I called a number at dcrooms, found in AAA books, and was checked into a gorgeous hotel, closer to the sites, for $20 more a night

name: The Churchill Hotel
title: “A Great Deal - Really”
text:
This hotel is absolutely fine for a weekend stay in DC. It's pretty close to Dupont Circle and the metro - lots of restaurants and shops and you are pretty much in the center of the city. I won’t lie, there are definitely some small problems with the hotel (i.e. most of the power outlets in the room didn't work) but there are lots of pluses too- very comfortable bed, HUGE room (we asked for an upgrade to a jr. suite) and the great price. We got it on priceline for $75 a night. You cannot stay in a good area of DC for $75. For that price, I'll deal with the lack of working outlets. And the noise from Connecticut Avenue is really not that bad. Anyone who lives in a city will not be bothered by it. 
The staff was very sweet and very helpful, slow yes, but you could tell they were trying. Whatever we asked for was done within a few minutes. If you are just using it as a place to stop over, change and sleep, you'll be find at this hotel. If you are looking for a luxurious romantic stop, then i'd say look elsewhere.

name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center
title: “great breakfast, clean rooms”
text: This is a solid, reliable chain hotel right across from the convention center. The rooms are exactly as expected, clean... though the amenities (shampoo etc) were not particularly good the coffee was better than general. I would like to reiterate the much touted breakfast.. the short order chef on duty when we were there (Ryan) did a grand job of making omelets and like all the staff was cheery, positive and made the stay very pleasant

name: Capital Hilton
title: “V. pleasant weekend stay with family”
text: Our family of three had a very nice stay this past weekend. We had booked a room on the Executive Level but when we checked in there was not a room available. Without skipping a beat, the desk manager gave us floor access AND free wifi for our stay. I can't imagine the 10th floor rooms were any nicer than huge room we had on the 9th. Lounge access was great and the croissants at breakfast tasted like they were made in house--very tasty. Super location for the monuments, White House and Smithsonian museums. Will stay here again.

name: The Henley Park Hotel
title: “Lovely Hotel in a GREAT LOCATION!”
text: There is no doubt that the location of this hotel is great! We had a room on the 5th floor over looking 10th St, I was expecting more noise based on the reviews that I had read prior. It was actually quiet for a large city. The bed was very comfortable...with lots of pillows! The room was VERY clean. The staff was very helpful and the bar and restaurant (although pricey) were very good (We only had dinner and dessert). The bartender makes great cocktails. The nightly water is a nice touch, especially when you have been doing a lot of walking. Overall a wonderful experience.

name: Harrington Hotel
title: “Pretty Good Place to Stay: Coupons Will Make It A Lot Cheaper”
text: Hello, I just returned today from a vacation in the D.C. area. I spent 3 nights here at the Harrington this week. Back in this hotel's prime, it was probably a very expensive, luxourious place to stay. It was built a while back, and still has an interesting vintage look to it. I liked staying here, and probably would again. If you do stay here you must get a coupon to lower your room rate. On the back of my door, it said my room was around $120 a night, but I got it for $85 and a day of free parking with a coupon out of one of those visitors guides that have coupons and advertisements. The best offer I found was $80 with parking in the Traveler Discount Guide (traveldiscountguide.com), and you can print it online at roomsaver.com The hotel was very clean and had full cable with many channels. The hotel has a very good location that is within walking distance of many attractions. My room had a nice view of the street and came with a coffee pot and refridgerator. The only downside to this hotel is it's age and a few things look like they could use renovation, but it is still a nice place to stay in Washington.

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Capitol
title: “Good service...room needs some updating.”
text:
The hotel is in an excellent location for visiting the smithsonian museums and the Capitol building. It's also a block away from a metro subway stop, L'Enfant Plaza, which has four lines I believe.
The staff are polite and efficient. The hotel has two restaurants, a Starbucks, and a deli of sorts. There's also a gift shop with some snacks, cigarettes, soda, etc.
The only criticism i have is the room needs a bit of refurbishment. The arms of the desk chair were worn out and small pieces would come off when you touched it. The wallpaper in the shower was a little rough.
Overall a good stay.

name: The Churchill Hotel
title: “prima hotel”
text: Lekkere bedden. Grote douchekop. Heerlijk ontbijt en starbuckskoffie. Locatie prima, 10 min van metro dupont-cirkel af. Goede buurt. Makkelijk een taxi te pakken vanaf daar (die overigens heel goed betaalbaar zijn).

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Central / White House
title: “great location, nice hotel”
text: I went to the Holiday inn central in september 2002. The location is perfect: near the White House, not far from the Mall. We did all the visits by foot. Even if Washington DC is well known for its criminalty, we didn't feel unsafe in this hotel. The rooms are spacious with a big bathroom; the staff is nice. There's a big swimming pool on the roof but it closed the day we arrived... If I was going back to Washington DC, I would choose this hotel every times.

name: Comfort Inn Downtown DC / Convention Center
title: “qualità/prezzo”
text:
il personale è stato disponibile in quanto siamo arrivati prima dell'ora del check in e abbiamo potuto mettere temporaneamente le valigie in uno stanzino.
la camera era per 4 persone e per fortuna eravamo solo in 3 in quanto è un po' piccola.
la colazione viene servita in una stanza molto grande ed è molto varia.
unica nota negativa dell'hotel:la posizione; a pochi passi dall'hotel c'è la stazione dei vigili del fuoco e di notte le sirene si sentono molto,a causa della mancanza di doppi vetri incamera.

name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center
title: “Stay here when in Denver!”
text: Spent one nt at the ES convention center while in Denver. Great downtown location. Nice spacious suites. Mod metro atmosphere. Looks brand new. Hotel appeared to be filled to capacity so the manager's cocktail hr was a bit of a mob scene - but, what what do you expect when you are giving out free drinks & nibbles? The breakfast selections were impressive. Kudos to the staff - especially the valets and reception. We didn't have a car to park, but the valets got us taxis and info about the city. They were all so friendly and personable. When we had a last minute change in our travel plans and were looking for something to do in Denver for a couple of hours, the guy in reception (didn't catch his name) tried to get us in at the last minute to the US Mint. When that didn't work, he came up with a couple of alternatives and explained the best way to get to the attractions. Very helpful. Would definately stay here again.

name: Grand Hyatt Washington
title: “great location and people”
text: I have stayed here many times and always had a good stay. So easy to get to from the airport and great staff. The food is great and always served with a smile.

name: Washington Hilton
title: “A cavernous Hilton with some history”
text:
First the history - It was at the lower south entrance to this hotel that John Hinckley shot Ronald Reagan. For some reason, it's not the most prominent thing in this hotel's advertising plan....
The rooms are Hilton standard, which means adequate for the business traveler though not plush. Hilton's standards are fairly high, and just about any Hilton I'd rank would get at least a Very Good rating (though I've made exceptions), and this is in that category.
But if you're not here for one of the vast number of conferences this hotel hosts, then there are probably better choices. It's not really near the main tourist action in this town (though if you learn how to use the Metro, and you should in this city, getting around is fairly easy; this hotel is a few blocks uphill from the Dupont Circle Metro). The place is big, awkwardly so in my opinion, and it's hard to navigate if you are a business traveler trying to find the room in which your meeting is being held. It's also not particularly quiet, though I've never had too much trouble sleeping here in a number of visits.
In short, it has the quality you'd expect of a Hilton, but is really nothing special. You won't at all mind staying there, but the visit may not be memorable.

name: Comfort Inn Downtown DC / Convention Center
title: “Solides Hotel aber Lage nicht optimal”
text: Ich war mit meiner Freundin 5 Tage dort. Das Hotel macht einen gepflegten Eindruck. Wir hatten ein Doppelzimmer mit zwei Queenbetten. Es hat schöne Möbel mit dunklem Furnier. Es gibt ein paar Abnutzungserscheinungen wie einen Fleck auf dem Teppich und der Gleichen aber man kann ja nicht nach jedem Gast renovieren. Das Bad ist ausreichend groß und es gibt einen großen Waschtisch mit genug Ablageplatz. Die Dusche funktioniert tadellos. Die Fenster kann man nicht öffen aber es gibt ein kleines Klimagerät, das jedoch recht laut ist. Wir haben es nur eingeschaltet wenn wir nicht da waren. Der Internetzugang über WLAN funktionierte zuerst leider nur sehr unzuverlässig. Auf Nachfrage erklärte man mir es gäbe Probleme durch das Erdbeben und den Sturm im August 2011. Offenbar wurde eine provisorische Lösung verwendet. An unserem letzen Tag funktionierte wieder der normale Zugang der dann auch stabil lief. Das Frühstück ist kostenlos und für amerikanische Verhältnisse überdurchschnittlich. Es gibt nicht nur Toast und Bagel plus Cornflakes sondern auch warme Sachen wie Rührei, Speck oder Würstchen und Waffeln zum selbst backen. Der Frühstücksraum ist sehr gemütlich eingerichtet und nie überfüllt. Wie in den USA offenbar üblich gibt es jedoch nur Einweggeschirr. Die Lage ist nicht schlecht aber auch nicht optimal. Die Metrostationen sind etwa 800 bis 1000 Meter entfernt was natürlich machbar ist aber auch nicht wirklich ein Katzensprung. Richtige Restaurants in der Umgebung gibt es nicht sehr viele und davon waren die meisten entweder nicht unsere Preisklasse oder nicht unser Geschmack. Es gibt zwar sehr viele Snackläden für Sandwiches und der gleichen bei denen wir uns dann meistens versorgt haben, diese haben jedoch oft schon ab 20:00 Uhr geschlossen. Für sonstigen Bedarf gibt es jedoch eine Drogerie mit 24 Stundenbetrieb gleich um die Ecke. In der Lobby kann man sich auch jeder Zeit Kaffe, Tee und Wasser kostenlos holen. Insgesamt kann ich das Hotel schon weiterempfehlen wenn man mit ein paar Einschränkungen leben kann oder eh lieber nochmal mit der Metro auswärts zum Essen fahren möchte.

name: Capital Hilton
title: “Location couldn't be better!”
text: We just stayed at the Capitol Hilton and we did too find the hotel dated but it is a historic hotel so what do you expected but they seem to be working on it. We were able to get a smoking room which we did appreciate. Our room was a nice size. It had a wet bar area but wish it had a refrigerator. I like that the bathroom sink was outside the tub and toilet area but wish that room was bigger. A nice touch was the light above the tub. A light was out in the bathroom and a handle on the door was broken. We told our housekeeper and it was fixed by the time we got back from breakfast. The location was the best ... 2 blocks from the Metro and close to the White House. We weren't able to get the breakfast plan don't ask me why but that there was a Corner Bakery around the corner a couple of blocks ... very good but closed on Sundays. Good restaurants in the area.

name: Harrington Hotel
title: “Touristenhotel wie aus dem Bilderbuch”
text:
Ich bin voll und ganz mit diesem Hotel zufrieden. Der Service war mehr als nur gut, die Zimmer waren geräumig und sauber. Ausserdem war es leise, d.h. der Straßenlärm drang nicht zu uns durch, obwohl wir uns nur im zweiten Stock befanden. Die Lage des Hotels ist traumhaft, fast jede Sehenswürdigkeit ist zu Fuß erreichbar und andernfalls gibt es viele U-Bahnstationen in der Nähe... 
Ich war mehr als nur begeistert von diesem Hotel und würde es definitiv als erste Wahl für einen Sightseeingurlaub in Washington DC sehen...

name: Comfort Inn Downtown DC / Convention Center
title: “Its OK”
text:
I spent a week at this property in mid-July, and here are my observations. The hotel is located in a transitional area in downtown DC. The adjoining neighborhood looks sad and depressing, but it is relatively safe. I did A LOT of walking that week so I became very familiar with the vicinity.
The hotel has a very small lobby, and the sitting area reminds me of a living room, which doesn't take a lot of people to fill the room up. The exercise room (adjacent to the lobby) consists of a treadmill and a TV. I didn't see it used while I was there.
If you have a laptop, bring it. I noticed a lot of people who didn't bring theirs surfing the net in the business center, which is right off the lobby. The hotel having complimentary wireless was definately helpful.
There is no on-site parking; cars are secured at a property up the street, so its not as simple as running downstairs and driving out. The staff is attentive and urges guests to allow 15 minutes or so to retrieve your vehicle. There is some parking around the hotel, but it is not recommended.
The rooms themselves are spacious, and I like how the bathrooms are situated.
There is a 24 hour CVS pharmacy about three blocks up the street.
The staff I encountered were very helpful and accomodating, but remember that this is a Comfort Inn, and not the Hyatt.
I believe that the ice machines and soda machines are on different floors, be sure to find out at check-in which one is on your floor. 
I had a few minor problems (no hot water; TV stopped working), but all in all it is an okay.
The convention center is about a 10 minute walk, and I walked to the White House in about 35 minutes.

name: Georgetown Suites
title: “lunghissimo soggiorno”
text: sono stato ospite del GT per quasi un anno ed è stata veramente un'esperienza positivissima, lo consiglio a tutti

name: The Brown Palace Hotel and Spa
title: “Très spacieux, hall magnifique”
text: Nous y avons passé une nuit, chambre très spacieuse, confortable et très propre. Hall impressionnant. Petit déjeuner à la carte parfait. Service top.

name: L'Enfant Plaza Hotel
title: “Faded Hotel But Good Location”
text:
I was in town for a business meeting and stayed here one night. It was my first experience with this hotel (I used to live in DC and have been a frequent visitor for many years).
The location of L'Enfant Plaza is good, particularly for tourists and the hotel is connected to the underground Metro stop, which is very convenient. Check in was cold but OK (the unsmiling and brusque clerk seemed displeased to be working); check out, by contrast, was fast and friendly. The room was clean enough but the furniture obviously needs to be replaced (a few holes in upholstery, faded fabrics, worn carpeting, scratched wood). None of these problems was terrible and none was noticeable at first glance. The strangest wear was in the bathroom's ceramic tile floor. The area in front of the sink had two, dinner plate-size gray spots that were permanently worn into the white tile surface. A smaller circle was in front of the bathtub. When I turned on the bathroom light, I first thought that something was casting a shadow on the floor. It is the weirdest wear pattern I have ever seen anywhere.
The hotel generally is in need of an overall freshening. If you can get an inexpensive room rate as I did, L'Enfant Plaza would be a good choice. Just don't go there expecting the same quality accommodations that are available elsewhere in DC. L'Enfant Plaza has in-room wireless internet but they still charge $10 plus tax daily fee for it, a needless irritant at a time when even roadside motels offer free wireless.

name: Renaissance Washington, DC Dupont Circle Hotel
title: “Why does such a nice place chintz on the Internet?”
text: The staff were all very nice and the room was great, but I resented paying $16 a day for Internet. For cryin' out loud, the local burger shop offers free Wi-Fi, and a $300/day hotel charges extra for it?

name: L'Enfant Plaza Hotel
title: “Location is everything”
text:
Has gotten some poor reviews I see. I discussed with the hotel. They are planning to continue upgrades through 2009. Our bed very comfortable and current, furniture recently reupholstered. Yes, wallpaper and TV needs next upgrade. TV reception extremely poor so I called desk. They apologized and said they had workmen there for the last 2 days to resolve problems. Bathroom not granite but very adequate and clean. I think all rooms have balcony. Mine did. There are views of Potomac or semi-monuments views (request nicely in advance would be a good idea as there is a charge if you "demand" monument view). Facing the front is best for noise prevention. If you ask, they have coffee makers (saves long lines and cost of Starbuck in lobby) and hand creme during very dry Winter cold. Floors 12-15 have their own elevator to save wait time. Staff very helpful. Valet park at $30.00 only choice.
However, the absolute BEST of the hotel is location, location. It is over a main Metro stop, large shopping area and food court. A very short walk to Smithsonian and in a safe appearing business area..

name: Washington Hilton
title: “Really good hotel”
text: This was my favorite of the Hiltons on the trip. The rooms are large, comfortable and some have excellent views of Washington. Significantly better food - breakfast was wonderful, there is free wi-fi. I'd stay here again in the next trip.

name: Washington Hilton
title: “Not a value for money Hotel!”
text:
Recently renovated hotel with a $120m budget. Very swanky from the exterior & lobby! 
But missed critical details like quality of the mattress & coffee maker. 
Even the shower was below par. I have a better shower at my University apartment!

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Washington, D.C.
title: “Typical Embassy Suites Needs Some Management Focus”
text:
This Embassy Suites property is typical for this Hilton brand. One's rating of the location, as is the case for any hotel, is in the eye of the beholder, depending on why one is in DC. I would typify the location as not very close to any one thing, but reasonably close to a lot of things. Going north on 22nd, one is in a pleasant residential neighborhood, with Dupont Circle and the Dupont Circle Metro about 10-15 minutes away walking. Going south on 22nd, one is on M street, which, moving to the West, takes one by the swank hotels that claim to be but are not in Georgetown, and then in Georgetown itself. The Mall is walkable to the South. Going East on M or L reaches a lot of potential destinations. 
Like most Embassy Suites, the character of this hotel changes vastly from weekend/Holiday to weekday. During the week it is typically business-oriented with the usual business type travelers. One is likely to see business meetings or gatherings taking place in the spread out lobby, and all is low key and under control. On weekends/holidays, the hotel turns into more of a zoo, as families quite reasonably descend upon the hotel en masse because the suites provide an excellent way to house vacationing families and the rates are discounted. Thus, one is likely to see many, many families and children running around loudly, much longer lines at the "manager's reception" (more on that below) and the free breakfast. Whether this is a plus or a minus depends on your view of families and children. 
As I have seen at other Embassy Suites, the "manager's reception" has gone cheap, with a few desultory bowls of chips and party mix and maybe some celery sticks. No attempt to spend more and make this more of a broad offering of appetizers, etc. 
The staff at the front desk admits that hotel parking is a structural issue. The small garage under the hotel has only room for about 100 cars, so you can be frozen out and forced to use the parking garage down the street at the Ritz Carlton if it is full. Even if you get one of the coveted spaces below for $30 a night, you may end up not being able to find a space, or having to park in an aisle, etc. 
The front desk staff at this property is not as uniformly trained in superb customer service and customer engagement as is the case elsewhere, meaning that your interaction is a crap shoot depending on the personality of the person you get. On at least one occasion in our recent stay, the person at the front desk was condescening and not friendly. More management attention is warranted on this front. 
Inexplicably, the soaring interior lobby is kept dark during the day and at night; management has made the decision to keep many of the interior lights off. For breakfast, they turn them on. 
The exercise room is pretty good for this type of property, with enough treadmills and weights, and one universal weight machine.

name: Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Excellent Hotel in excellent location”
text: Checkin was quick and easy. The room was recently remodeled and was clean, fresh and very spacious. The beds were comfortable and linens fresh and new. The hotel is two blocks from Chinatown and there are plenty of food options. METRO is also a few blocks away. Very pleased with this hotel and would definitely stay there again.

name: Courtyard Washington Capitol Hill/Navy Yard
title: “brand new hotel very convenient to Metro”
text:
I stayed at the Courtyard Navy Yard for four nights in May 2006. This hotel is brand new and my room was immaculate. I was on one of the upper floors in the corner room (the outside glass sort of wraps around the edge of the hotel). The room was spotless, and with all the amenities you could want including wide- screen LCD TV, free broadband, good-sized bathroom, ironing board, hair dryer, and lots of lighting options. Room service is not available after 10pm, but there is a simple, decent, breakfast buffet and even a little "snack market" next to the registration desk. It's basically a hotel designed for business travelers, but it's new and definitely NOT some dump!
The staff was also very friendly and helpful. The only thing keeping me from giving 5 stars is the location. True, it is close to the Metro, which is a good thing, but that's about it. There is virtually nothing else to do in the immediate area. There is a lot of construction going on with new office complexes springing up, but there is is nothing within walking distance of the hotel right now except a CVS pharmacy. The entrance to the Navy Yard Metro station (green line) is on the next block. If you are a business traveler, I highly recommend the Courtyard Navy Yard if all you need is a nice, clean place to sleep or work and don't care about being within walking distance to everything.
Overall I was pleased and would stay here again if I was in DC on business. For siteseeing it's a bit out of the way but not much. The fact that the place is new and the staff friendly makes all the difference.

name: Grand Hyatt Washington
title: “Nice place”
text:
I think the best thing about the hotel is the location. It's in china town in the midst of many restaurants, bars, some museums and some shops. It's also just blocks from the Verizon Center. 
The hotel itself is nice but I think average for a Hyatt. The rooms are clean but fairly basic. Staff is on the curt side. 
It's not a bad place to stay at all but the rooms won't wow you or anything. Not a bad value for the right price and again, good location. Starbucks downstairs in the lobby for those that need a kick in the morning!

name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Perfect location to explore DC!”
text:
The Mayflower Renaissance is a beautiful hotel and centrally located. It's about 15 min walk to the Washington Monument and 10 min to Dupont Circle. The hotel is on a subway "Red Line" at Farragut North station. 
I got room 901, a cozy and quiet corner unit. The room was clean with a comfy king-size bed and a flat-screen TV. The bathroom was well appointed. Every morning I enjoyed going to Paul Bakery for breakfast. On a lazy night, I ordered a delivery from Meiwah and the food was fantastic.
The Internet was expensive, $12.95 per day. In this day and age, it's hard to believe that some establishments are still charging for the Internet. Remember to check the statement at check out, I had an extra one day charge for the internet. 
Like:
- Location
- Friendly staff
Dislike:
- Expensive Internet
- No safety box in the room
- Low water pressure

name: State Plaza Hotel
title: “Superb!”
text:
I don't have a bad word to say about my stay at this hotel. If I were to have a complaint, it would be that my flat is barely larger than the room I was given!
More space than I could have asked for. Friendly staff. They even offered to charge my phone at reception because I had failed to find an adaptor plug for my UK phone.
Thank you State Plaza! I'll be back.

name: Capital Hilton
title: “Reliable”
text:
This hotel is fine. Nice clean room with a small loveseat. Free wifi in the lobby, you can pay for itin the room - would be nice to have it free in the room. Great gym and spa. Eating choices in the hotel were all very high, but there were affordable places within walking distance to eat. E had rented a car and found it difficult many times to reach the valet to bring the car out. We also felt it was an annoyance to them to bring the car out unless we were checking out.
The location is convenient and we got a good rate on Hotwire so we stayed for a night.

name: L'Enfant Plaza Hotel
title: “very nice, good price”
text:
First I'll tell you the good points about this hotel. This is the closest hotel to the smithsonian. We walked everywhere with our 8 year old and he did fine. This hotel has a great indoor pool. It was really large and the kids had a ball at the end of the day, it does close at 8pm, so take note. The rooms were very spacious, we had a rollaway ($20 a night) and it wasn't cramped a bit. The beds were very comfortable with a down comforter. The toiletries were Rusk products, very nice. the lobby was really nice. The staff was very nice.
Bad points. It is an older hotel that has not been 100% kept up. Yes, you can see wallpaper tears here and there. Tile cracks here and there. It's not terrible. Also, there are no restaurants in the area. There is a food court underneath the hotel, but it's closed by around 6pm.
While the hotel did have some upkeep issues, I'm really picky and it didn't bother me. The hotel was very clean, the carpet and floors were all clean, everything smelled clean. The bathroom had a lot of marble, the bedding was new and tasteful.
We only paid $99 a night which included valet parking.
Also, I prefer this area. We've stayed at the Embassy Suites Convention Ctr and the Hyatt downtown and both locations were a bit scary at night. Many homeless people at that end of town. The L'enfant plaza seemed to be a safer area and it was well lit.
The hotel restaurant was pricey. We ate almost every meal there. It was fine, just a bit pricey.

name: Washington Hilton
title: “Great Hotel”
text: My husband and I stayed here for the first leg of our Honeymoon. Beautiful Hotel, rooms were a great size and very comfortable. Great location, within walking distance to all Washingtons Fab sights. Tour Bus stopped right outside the hotel which was very convenient.. Would recommend this hotel.

name: W Washington DC
title: “Great Stay”
text:
Great Night at the W
My boys came up from Blacksburg, Virginia to celebrate my promotion at
a prominent company in the D.C metropolitan area. I got a room at the
W for the weekend so we can party and not worry about having to go all
the way back to Virginia.
We hit the town, a couple of bars and some lounges and decided to come
back to the hotel and came to the hotel for our reservation at the
rooftop terrace. The music was good and the view was GREAT! My boys
were yelling “Obama” as if he were going to come out of the White
house and wave back. Krystle, our server was amazing and had some
funky earrings on that made our night. Great server, if you go to the
POV rooftop make sure you ask for her.
All in all we had a great night. Thanks The W and Krystle

name: Grand Hyatt Washington
title: “Convenient location for tourists!”
text:
For genuine tourists, driving in Washington DC is a nightmare. The location of the Grand Hyatt Washington DC is excellent because it is attached to the Metro Center station. Tourists can easily go to different places simply by Metro plus some walking. One can even go to Mount Vernon (the old residence of George Washington) in Virginia, by Metro and bus.
The hotel is just two blocks or so away from the Ford's Theater (where Lincoln was shot) and Chinatown. Ford's Theater is a place where all tourists should go, in my opinion. Chinatown is a place where reasonable-priced and ok food can be found in addition to a store where one can buy some beer or liquor and bring back to the hotel for consumption later. 
However Metro cannot get to all tourist spots in Washington DC. The Tourmobile can be supplemented as another vehicle for tourists. A problem for the Grand Hyatt is that it is not close to any Tourmobile stops.

name: Renaissance Washington, DC Dupont Circle Hotel
title: “Fabulous! Modern, sophisticated and comfortable”
text: Our company just used this site for a conference. The hotel itself was beautiful - smaller, with a modern, sleek look and comfortable feel. The staff was friendly, helpful and always available. We really enjoyed our stay and felt we received exceptional treatment by every member of the hotel team. We've already booked another workshop there for the fall. Highly recommend!

name: Washington Hilton
title: “Location exellent but infrastructre substandard for a Hilton.”
text: Great location for sightseeing, close to Dupont Circle metro. Service in the hotel was good, breakfast is pricey but awesome. I especially appreciated the mint-flavored ice water that was provided in the lobby. Still, the infrastructure was a bit disappointing for a Hilton: while the lobby, restaurants and pool were nice, the room itself was substandard: the tub in the room did not drain, the closet door would not close, there was no WIFI possibility in the room, just internet with a cord and the ice machine closest to our room did not work, had to go to a different floor to get it. I was given a break on the bill when I complained, but would rather have had a room in good order.

name: Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Pleasant comfortable hotel for business travel”
text: The hotel is clean and comfortable with a modern feel and appealing decor. The rooms are quite small, but adequate and comfortable. Traveling for business, it was fine, if I was traveling with family, it would have been much too small. Food was really good for hotel standards, and staff was more than accommodating and friendly. I'm rarely disappointed with a Marriott hotel, and this was definitely up to standards.

name: Renaissance Washington, DC Dupont Circle Hotel
title: “nice hotel, great location”
text: Booked on priceline for $88 a night. We got three rooms for a family event. We were traveling with a small baby, so after reading on TripAdvisor that the rooms were small, we called ahead and asked for a bigger room. They upgraded two of the rooms, and even provided two small, empty refridgerators free of charge. However, we couldnt fit our pack n play (crib) in the room, we ended up setting it up in the bathroom. The location was the best I've ever stayed in Washington, we could walk to the Mall in about 15 minutes, or take the metro. The conceirge was really helpful, provided us with maps and advice. It was a nice, quiet, clean hotel and I couldnt ask for anything more at that price.

name: State Plaza Hotel
title: “Great spot for GWU Commencement”
text: I chose this hotel because of its location right in the middle of George Washington University. I was there for my daughter's graduation, and the State Plaza was a perfect base of operations. The staff was very friendly and helpful, and the room was large and very nice. Having a kitchen area with refrigerator was handy. One minor complaint: the one day we were gone from 8 am to 4:30 pm, the maid arrived to make up the room at 4:35! I would definitely recommend this hotel.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Good hotel, rooms a little sparce”
text: Service was excellent and the hotel shared facilities (lobby, gym), were excellent. The rooms, while big and clean, were a little sparse. Also, the hotel is loud - not that the clientele is rowdy, but the doors and walls are thin so you hear your fellow guests.

name: The Henley Park Hotel
title: “Not Bad!!!”
text: The first day was a bit awkward as the desk clerk hit my charge card for excess charges which caused a decline but aside from that our stay was good. The staff was attentive and immediately sought to help with any questions of small problems. There were no big problems. The hotel is next to construction but again not a problem when your inside. There is quite a bit of street noise. Probably the only negative. Our room was as offered and was very comfortable. Our maidservice was wonderful and the room looked great every time we came in from sightseeing. The bellmen were helpful and did every thing they could to make our stay good. By the way this is a beautiful medieval decor. These folks know how to run a class Hotel. We've travelled a lot and were quite impressed by this little jewel. My wife thinks this is not as glowing a review as the hotel deserves. All in all a great hotel.

name: Hamilton Crowne Plaza Hotel
title: “Wonderful Service!”
text: I just came back from a 3 night stay at the Crowne Plaza. I was very pleased with the accomodations. My room was very clean and nicely decorated though it was a little small. The room was enabled for wireless internet access. I asked at check in for a quiet room and it certainly was quiet. I never even heard other guests going into and out of their rooms! The staff at this hotel are very pleasant and attentive! Two things I was not pleased with were the elevators (they are very small - 8 person capacity-and very slow) and the fact that Ice/Vending machines are only on the odd numbered floors. Overall, I would certainly stay here again and, yes, would recommend it to others.

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Capitol
title: “We really liked this hotel”
text:
The hotel is ideally situated to see the majority of sites. The staff were helpful. The reception was bright and cheerful and the bedroom was well decorated. The only downside was the very limited menu in the restaurant however the bar offered varied light meals but was packed every night. We got this booking at an extremely good rate from TravelRepublic.co.uk and have yet to see it beaten. Would definitely return to this hotel.
H Rayner 
Kent UK

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Beautiful Historic Hotel with a 21st Century Touch!”
text:
I stayed here during a US Department of Education conference and paid the government rate of $183 per night. 
The hotel was absolutely beautiful. I liked that each room was just a little different in its layout and design. It gave it character. The bar was lovely. Dark wood panelling lined the walls. A very classic, rich look. 
I only had one breakfast at the restaurant. It was a $20 buffet with fresh fruit, made to order omlets, meats, etc. 
There IS free wifi if you sign up for their select guest loyalty program. That also gets you a free beverage delivered each morning: coffee, juice, tea, etc. they so have in room coffee makers. 
Across the street is a great little restaurant called Open City. Give it a try!

name: Hamilton Crowne Plaza Hotel
title: “Perfect”
text: Great Hotel, Great Staff, Wonderful Price, Could not ask for anything more when it comes to all around service and satisfaction.

name: The Eldon Luxury Suites
title: “Not Perfect But Great Value!”
text:
I highly recommend this hotel but there are a few little things that bothered me. 
Note: This hotel does not have a restaurant or bar on premise - it offers a small breakfast and not much more. Also, all the room's floors are stone - no carpets. I did not mind but you might.
GREAT:
Very reasonable price. Great bang for the buck
Nice, huge rooms
Kitchen is well appointed
Incredibly comfortable bed
Bathroom is really fancy with an incredible shower
Free WiFi 
Many closets and storage, especially for hanging up clothing
DirecTV has many, many channels
Continental breakfast offered cold/hot cereals, breads, pastries, hot drinks, and OJ - for only $5!!
REALLY BOTHERED ME
No TV in bedroom. 
Bedroom desk was very small and the chair stunk. They really need a proper chair with wheels and a high, adjustable seat/back.
OTHER CRITIQUES
Bathroom only had one small hook to hang towels. I had to hang my second one on top of the bathroom door.
Bedroom closet was huge but shelves were 1/2 as deep as the closet. 
Living room furniture was sparse
They charged me for my complete stay the day after checking in. Hmm....

name: The Eldon Luxury Suites
title: “lost booking”
text: I booked the Eldon via Expedia and when I arrived at the hotel, they informed me that they were overbooked and didn't have a room for me for two nights. The owner also manages two really low quality hotels 10 blocks away and offered to send me there for two nights and then have me return back to the Eldon for the rest of my stay. How bad does someone's IT infrastructure need to be in order for them to make this mistake? When I arrived back at the Eldon two days later, I reminded the management that the rate at other hotel (the Windsor) was half of the Eldon and that I should be discounted accordingly. The manager told me that because the reservation was already paid for, there was nothings she could do!! I've yet to checkout and really fight for the partial refund, but I don't see how they could justify not yielding it. The facilities themselves are really really nice. Everything is covered in marble and wood. The bathroom has designer fixtures and nice Japanese six-way shower

name: Homewood Suites Washington, DC
title: “Lovely and close to white house”
text: I absolutely loved my stay here. The rooms were great with a full size fridge and a comfy king size bed. The staff was helpful and attentive. Sierra was deff the best employee we met up with here for checkin in. Will be staying here again next trip!

name: L'Enfant Plaza Hotel
title: “Good experience for us”
text:
We had a 4 night stay at this hotel and had a good time.
Service was very good. On early arrival they said we would need to wait for a room but before we finished checking in one became available.
We got some very nice help with our questions about travel and attractions.
It is so very convenient to everything.
Room appeared clean.Some hanging cracked wall paper in the bathroom ceiling but otherwise good shape. Prompt maid service. no long waits for elevator.
Restaurants are OK but not great for the prices.
Foggy Bottom bar was all smoking area.Would have been good to have a no smoke area too.
We would recommend this hotel and would stay again if in the area.

name: Homewood Suites Washington, DC
title: “Could use an upgrade”
text: I stayed here for a few night while in business in DC. The hotel was nice enough, but could use an update. I found the decor to be old and dated. I've stayed in some really nice Homewood Suites such as the one in Baltimore, and this one is not up to that one's standard.

name: Washington Plaza
title: “Single mom with 11 year old son love DC!”
text: The outdoor pool was fabulous! Very refreshing after touring the sites and museums all day. Pool staff was very friendly and courteous. Rooms were clean and our room had a view of the pool. Closest metro is .3 miles away. Bring your walking shoes! Make sure you have a safe in your room because some of the rooms don't have them. Complimentary bottled water each evening was great too. I got a king superior room for 129$ a night so for location, amenities and value, I think this place is great. Next door is the Donovan House that has a rooftop pool and loud music. Bring earplugs if you are a light sleeper - Thomas circle had lots of traffic 24/7!

name: Holiday Inn Washington - Capitol
title: “A very well run,located and maintained hotel. This Holiday Inn is a pleasure!!”
text:
The Holiday Inn Capitol certainly has a lot going for it. After staying in a wonderful hotel in NYC for a few days (Affinia 50--highly recommended), my brother and I thought we would be taking a huge step down in quality etc...not so. 
The Room--a pretty spacious one compared to many, with a good tv (remote worked well, sound good, loads of channels), two very comfortable beds with a pillow menu (very Affinia mind you), great air conditioning-though the unit looks old, it's controlled from a modern digital wall unit and can make the room absolutely freezing or roasting, very useful. The bathroom is spacious and, most importantly, clean with a very nice powerful shower and nice soaps too. Maid service was very efficient and cleaned the room thoroughly. It was great to see not just a mini fridge, but a full fridge in the room, with nothing in it, no overpriced alcohol or anything!! 
Though one could hear some noise out in the corridor or from other rooms during the day, at night the hotel is silent, like from about 8pm, great for a good night's sleep. There wasn't a safe in our room but the ones beside/behind reception were useful, and the number of front desk staff meant I never had to wait for more than a minute to access it before going out.
The Hotel: a modern, spacious lobby with all the usual stuff plus a lot of more unusual stuff too. The hotel has a Starbucks right off the lobby which is very usual, a gift shop/general shop open to 10pm daily, two restaurants and a deli style place. The business center, open 24 hours and only accessible with a room key, offers free, yes free, internet and printers etc.Though it's sometimes busy due to this fact, not paying or having to get a prepaid card or whatever was very refreshing.
Restaurants nearby include Quiznos, Mcdonalds, Wall Street Deli, and a Vie de France, and there is a CVS right beside the hotel for fridge supplies. It's true that there aren't many great restaurants near the hotel but taxis, right outside, are very cheap for most destinations as they work by zone fees, not meters.
I recommend Charlie Palmer Steak (1st and Constitution) for a great night...quiet, great service, great food, reasonable prices.
The location of the hotel for sightseeing is great, steps to the Mall, Capitol etc, and L'Enfant Plaza station (the biggest metro station by line number) is great for Archives, White House, Spy Museum, Holocaust Museum, and it's two steps away.
We never used the pool on the roof but many others seemed to enjoy it, though I understand it's not too deep.
The hotel , interestingly, has guest laundry facilities on the second floor, i.e. dryers and washers, which are cheap, secure and very useful if you would rather not use the hotel's laundry service.We used both and obviously one was much cheaper (hotel service was $70, guest ones $3).
We didn't eat in the restaurants, we prefer to leave the hotel at night, but they looked nice and not overly expensive and the Pizza Hut pizzas offered in the Shuttle Express Deli were popular.LIve jazz was very popular in the 21st Amendment Bar and Grill when it was on.
Free USA Today was a nice touch too. Ice, soda on every floor.
Overall, the Holiday Inn Capitol served us very well.For the rate we got via hotel's website, our stay were above expectations.The rooms were nice, clean and well air conditioned, the hotel was in a great location and had above average amenities. If you want a pleasant stay along with a location set up for sightseeing and more sightseeing, then I'd go with this place. Yea the Willard looked nice, but huge credit card bills aren't and they may not have a pillow menu.

name: L'Enfant Plaza Hotel
title: “Wonderful location, needs a makeover.”
text: I attended a holiday ball the was held at Loews L'Enfant and the location is wonderful. Walked a flight a stairs beneath the hotel lobby to access the metro which is very convenient. Great location in relation to sightseeing, Smithsonian is a short walk away. The room was a nice size but the furniture was worn and stained. The thermostat had a high, medium, low setting dial and the air was cool or cold even. I decided to use the extra blanket and forego heat all together. The shower head was very old and hard to move to adjust the flow of water. Loews could use a major makeover with furniture and fixtures. After reading other reviews I was a little hesitant about staying there but they gave a discount rate for guests attending the ball. I would stay there again if for nothing more then how close it is to the museums and metro access.

name: The Eldon Luxury Suites
title: “Luxury in a convenient location near convention center”
text: Very large, clean suites and nicely appointed kitchen and bath were more like a small apartment than a hotel suite. Friendly folks at the front desk made great restaurant recommendations (based on what I asked for) and gladly handled cab requests. Walking distance to many places I needed to go; short cab ride to the rest. Hallways were a bit noisy due to the hard surfaces: maybe some soudnproofing around the doors would help. I can't wait to go back, and take my wife with me. She'll love it.

name: State Plaza Hotel
title: “Great place for family reunion”
text: Family reunion held here. Professional and friendly staff. Good location. Kithen well stocked. We had more family than anticipated. The staff bent over backwards to accomodate our needs -- even cooking additional food at the banquet. The rooms were clean, the kitchen well stocked. There were restaurants, museums, subway within walking distance and city bus service close to the hotel. Great place for a family reunion.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Washington, D.C.
title: “Would absolutely stay here again.”
text: Hotel staff, especially those at the front desk, were friendly and helpful. We arrived in Washington VERY early on a Friday (January 14th) morning for a three night stay, expecting to have to wait until 3:00 P.M. to check in. Not so - the front desk staff were able to get us into a suite right away. Perfect after a long journey. The hotel is well-situated for touring the major sights, either walking or using the metro. The breakfast is a great way to start each day, and we encountered no lines at all. The evening reception is a perfect way to wind down after a long day of touring. The one drawback, which I have seen mentioned a few times, is the charge for internet access. On the other hand, access to the internet probably would have interfered with getting the most out of a three day stay. All in all, I cannot say enough good about this hotel, and I would absolutely stay there again.

name: Washington Hilton
title: “NEVER USE VALET PARKING”
text:
For a $37 fee of Valet Parking, I figure I will get my car in a reasonable amount of time. NO....NOT EVER CLOSE!!!!!!! On May 13, I had a important meeting at 9 am. I figured giving myself 1 hour and 30 minutes was good enough because it's only 10 miles away from this hotel. I was in the lobby of the hotel at 7:45 and the valet service could not get my car to me until 8:35...a 50 minute wait. This is just unacceptable for a 4 star hotel charging me $37 dollars. It was clear to me that other guests waited just as long as me that morning.
Rooms are smaller than usual but clean. If you are looking for a quite hotel with quality service, go somewhere else.

name: Capital Hilton
title: “Got excellent price @ Hotwire.com”
text: Great hotel, highly recommended. Extremely close to the White House, about a half-mile walk.

name: State Plaza Hotel
title: “Good value hotel in the city centre”
text:
The location of this hotel was perfect for us as we had a young family and no vehicle. The rooms were clean and tidy and the little kitchen was a boon for breakfasts and making hot snacks. Couple of small signs of wear and tear (which made it feel like being at home). Easy walk to the Lincoln Memorial and the White House and close to a couple of useful bus routes. Not too close to many resteraunts but we made sure we ate before we got back rather than going out seperately in the evening. 
Liked the fact that you were not plagued by bell hops, but the staff reacted well when my room key failed and on the occassion I mucked up the safety lock box in the room sending people along to assist in just a few minutes (apparently the room keys are occassionally wiped by security scanners when you visit Washington museums...) .
I would certainly recommend this hotel and would stay again. Prefered staying here to the hotels further up near Dupont and Northwards.

name: Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Helpful & Honest Housekeeping Staff!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for one night this fall. The hotel is within walking distance to many tourist sites and so it's good option for a vacation stay. The rooms are pretty standard but comfortable. I didn't like the entrance/ driveway set-up. It's all driveway and you have to dodge cars and valets to get into the main entrance. There is also a pretty hefty charge for the wireless internet in-room access.
But I was quite impressed by the housekeeping staff. I left my i=pod charging cord plugged into the wall and not only did they find it, they mailed it back to me! Yeah!!!

name: Capital Hilton
title: “TERRIBLE SERVICE”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights as part of our honeymoon, checking in on a Friday around 6pm, was effortless, and pleasoon aftersant enough, given the 14th floor with a queen bed which was terrible it sank in the middle. The bell boy arrived shorly after we got to our room but he was an elderly gentleman and struggled to even lift the bags off the trolly, but he tried his best.
After getting our room sorted we went for a walk to the White House which is only a short 5 min. walk, and got a quicky meal.
After the second day of sight seeing we returned to the Hotel and went to the bar for a couple of quiet drinks, and were served by a pleasant young Lady, but soon after a middle aged guy with glasses, i think his name was Paolo ??? could be wrong because he never got close enough to see his name tag, well i will tell you this guy has the personality of a BRICK, with a bad attitude, with service to match, he doesnt belong in a Hilton Hotel any where, which made us retire to our room. 
Beware of paying extra for the executive floor for the weekend, they advertise that you can get snacks and alcoholic drinks in an honesty bar. WRONG !!!!!!! What they DO NOT tell you that this is only available Monday thru to Thursdays. They also advertise a Concierge is available in the executive lounge daily......... WRONG !!!!!!!!!! i rang the concierge downstairs and got put thru to the front desk and was asked to hold.......... i did...........for 15mins !!!!!!!!!! so i went downstairs........ no one available to answer my questions.... 
Definately not in the usual Hilton class, the Hotel itself looks nice, the room was adequate, however the amenities were not replaced. 
Overall this Hotel is a big disappointment and we would not recommend this place at all.

name: Washington Plaza
title: “Central and great staff”
text:
For no reason we were upgraded which we didn't complain about, we were given a corner room which had ample room with a view out to Thomas Circle.
It is a casual 10-15min walk to the National Mall which is great. The walk was safe and is close to many dining options. We were also close to Chinatown which is where you can see the Wizards play for very little $.
Overall the staff were more than helpful, location and room were excellent, only negative is that the large outside pool is seasonal and was closed during our visit.

name: Washington Plaza
title: “Great except for the internet access”
text:
Before I get into what I like about this hotel, let me tell you the one thing I didn't like - the internet provided. The hotel provides free wireless internet (it is no longer $10/night as some of the reviews here indicate), and also provides wired internet if you bring your own ethernet cable or buy one from the front desk. I went wireless, and had two problems with it. First, the signal was not very strong - this may have been because my room was at the very edge of the building, I'm not sure. But more importantly, and bizarrely, the internet was filtered, and some perfectly innocuous websites were being blocked. I couldn't access Flickr, the popular photo sharing site, which was blocked as a "music download site," and many Youtube videos would also not display. I have never stayed at a hotel that filtered its internet before, so I found it very odd and inconvenient (as I wished to upload some photos I had taken).
But now, on to the good. I found the staff to be very professional and kind, and having someone there just to open the door for you was nice in the cold. I was permitted to check-in immediately upon my arrival even though I arrived about an hour before check-in officially began.
The room I stayed in featured two queen beds and was plenty big enough for me. There was no couch, and only a single desk with one chair, which may annoy some. I felt like half the bed was covered with some very plump pillows! There was a large-screen flat screen television with a moderate selection of channels. The alarm clock seemed designed to be as easy to operate as possible - nice for a hotel! The room had a digital thermostat and very responsive heater. The curtains covering the windows blocked out essentially all the city light if closed.
The bathroom was also fine, with the shower in particular being quite wonderful. The sink was outside the bathroom.
Outside the hotel, the nearest Metro station is something like 4 blocks away. Unfortunately you have to walk around Thomas Circle to get there, which is a bit annoying since there is a lot of traffic and the traffic lights, if they are synced at all, aren't synced with pedestrians in mind. There is a CVS approximately directly across from the hotel, and plenty of restaurants nearby.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Our DC Home-Away-From-Home”
text:
The first TripAdvisor review that I wrote (December 2006) was for the Omni Shoreham. We’ve probably have stayed at the Omni about a dozen times over this five year period (the last time this past August, to see the MLK Jr. Memorial and during Hurricane Irene). I can safely say that my wife and I now consider the Omni to be our Washington, DC, home-away-from-home. We’ve stayed at quite a few other DC hotels over the years, as we visit Washington on a fairly regular basis. And when we do stay at the other hotels, we end up asking ourselves ‘why didn’t we stay at the Omni?’
For us, the Omni just feels ‘right’: it’s close to the Metro, the ambiance is great, the rooms (especially the larger suites, which we stay in when the price is right) are comfortable, there are lots of good restaurants nearby, and the staff has always been top-notch. And the free wifi is nice as is the complimentary (for Select Guest members) morning coffee delivered to our room.
We’re visiting DC again in November and yes, we’ll be staying at the Omni.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Washington, D.C.
title: “Great Place to stay with family”
text: Great rooms and breakfast. Merely wish the parking garage cost less & the pool was larger. We have stayed three times in this hotel. The friends we recommended it to have repeated their visit as well.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Washington, D.C.
title: “unbeatable!”
text: One of the best hotels when you are traveling with kids. Spacious rooms, Friendly staff, everyone goes out of their way to make your stay enjoyable. Free breakfast and complimentary drinks are a treat! Great location as well....

name: Beacon Hotel & Corporate Quarters
title: “Spectacular”
text: Our recent stay was most enjoyable, noy only for the accommodations, but also for the attention to detail from all the staff. Kingsley, our desk clerk was most solicitous of our needs. The hotel was clean, bright and with many amenities that made us feel at home.We will certainly stay here again,

name: Capital Hilton
title: “Remodeled Rooms = Great Stay”
text: My Family and I stayed here in April and had a great time. We stayed on the 11th floor, Executive Floor, which was just remodeled. The rooms were clean, new, and extremely comfortable. We were able to get a good deal along with a AAA discount. The executive floor saved us time and money with the included breakfast. I belong to Hilton HHonors and my membership included free access to the gym. It was one of the best in the area. They are remodeling from the top down, so try to keep this in mind when booking. The Capital Hilton is very close to two metro stations and walking distance to the White House.

name: Capital Hilton
title: “thin walls made it hard to sleep”
text: Because of the design of the hotel, we could hear the person next door urinating while we were trying to get to sleep. The hotel should take the time to reduce noise when they do their renovations. Even a quiet TV next door could be heard loud and clear. Don't stay here if you'd like a good night's sleep. V E R Y soft mattress.

name: Grand Hyatt Washington
title: “Planning a reunion...Beware”
text: Had our class reunion here....The room was small......The Food we had as part of our reunion was terrible....They ran out of food...closed it up early....CHARGED OUTRAGEOUS PRICES FOR DRINKS...THEY EVEN TRIED TO CHARGE ME 5.50 FOR A GLASS OF WATER WHICH IS AGAINST THE LAW TO CHARGE FOR A GLASS OF WATER. 10.50 FOR A TINY MIXED DRINK WITH GENERIC LIGUOR. Everyone oomplAined about it...I did not see too many people drinking...You would think that if they would lower the price of the drinks somewhat..they would sell more...another example of corporate greed........I will never stay here if I ever came to DC.....Greed is rampant here in DC

name: Homewood Suites Washington, DC
title: “Would DEFINITELY recommend!!!”
text: My sister and I took a last minute trip to D.C. to use our grandparents tickets to the NCAA hockey tourney after our grandpa was too sick to travel. We stayed there for two days and couldn't have been happier with the service. The hotel staff was extremely nice, and very helpful when it came to switching the reservations into my name, etc. It all went very smoothly, and they were very kind. The room was very clean, and comfortable. The beds were fantastic! The duvet covers were magnificent. We still talk about how nice our room was and how great the beds and covers were! The room was great, the staff is great, the food was delicious! It is also very close to a lot of the landmarks we went to! I would recommend Homewood Suites to anyone going to D.C.

name: Morrison-Clark Historic Inn
title: “Perfect Inner City Get a way!”
text: This hotel is a cross between a traditional hotel and a beautiful home. It is an oasis in downtown DC, peaceful and beautiful. When I sat on the front porch I felt at ease. The hotel is surrounded by beautiful gardens and trees - like a house. I got to look out on busy DC and yet feel sheltered from downtown DC at the same time. The beds were extremely comfortable. The room was charming. The staff were very friendly. I would go back and stay in a heart beat. The only thing I would change is the lobby and stairway carpeting needs a good cleaning or replacement - it was getting dingy. It was clean but it was looking worn and dingy. Also, there was a small amount of dry rot on the balcony connected to my room. This is to be expected in a building of this age. It didn't affect the safty of the balcony, it just cryed out for attention. This is a fantastic hotel!

name: Embassy Suites Chevy Chase Pavilion
title: “Nice location”
text:
This hotel was in a great location in reference to the Metro and has some great restaurants in the area. There were a couple of days of our week long vacation where we wanted to turn in early but the noise from the construction was a little too much to do that. The parking garage was under construction too which made it difficult to get out at times. I felt that with causing that much trouble with trying to obtain the car, the parking cost should have been canceled or should have at least been reduced.
The Manager’s reception each evening was very nice and it was fun to have board games to play. The breakfast each morning was delicious. The pool was a little too cold for my taste, but it didn’t bother my 10 year old son. It did feel as though there were ice cubes dumped in there to cool it off.
We didn't care too much for the pillows on the bed. As soon as you lay your head on them, all of the fluff went away. I like my pillow to be a little stiffer. Great time at this hotel overall though.

name: Embassy Suites Chevy Chase Pavilion
title: “Thank You Embassy Suites”
text: After reading some of the reviews I was a little worried about the hotel, but we were so happy with everything about Embassy Suites Chevy Chase. THe staff was exceptional and went out of their way to help with anything! Every person we encountered from the front desk, breakfast staff, or housekeeping were wonderful. The room was beautiful and breakfast was great. Don't be scared off by the construction, we didn't hear much of anything and really if you are in DC how much time are you going to spend in your room. I can't wait to go back and see the finished product but the hotel is great even with all this going on. I have never stayed in another hotel where the customer service was so great! The metro stop in the hotel is convenient and easy to navigate.

name: Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Renaissance Hotel-- eeeh not fabulous”
text:
I consider Renaissance Hotels to be an upgrade from the regular Marriotts-- not so. This one has a new fabulous lobby. Workers not super helpful. We are Gold Elite Rewards members and the "upgrade" to our room was a joke. We were "upgraded to a 4th floor room with 2 double beds. Very small. Stained bed skirts and carpet. Not so sure what they were planning to put us in originally. Aveda toiletries were microscopic and not generous. No fan in bathroom. Bathroom had toilet, sink and tub/shower all behind the same door. Marriott site states "Concierge Lounge serves continental breakfast, hors d'oeuvres in the evening and beverages all day" They closed after b/fast on friday never to open for the entire weekend. The workers in the club level were aggressively patroling the "honor" bar and were not so friendly with the children in our group. The club level drinks start at $5 for a beer and go up from there. No pool at this location. Health club will not admit under 18. 
Not super friendly for families with kids. Would not recommend.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Awesome”
text: We recently stayed at the Omni for a friend's wedding. Having previously explained to their loyalty abassador that I was also meeting my daughter and son-in-law who reside on the West Coast and had not seen for quite a while, she seemed to go out of her way to make the stay special. The room overlooked the beautiful gardens. We were even able to see the wedding rehearsal. The service the entire weeked was wonderful. Beverages of our choice were delivered to our room each morning with no charge as a Select member. We had turn down service each evening. The food for both the reception and dinnner was delicious! The location near the metro was excellent. There are many different types of restaurants located within just a few blocks. A wonderful trip!!

name: State Plaza Hotel
title: “Good option for family travel”
text:
The hotel was very nice and clean. I got a very good deal from Orbitz, much cheaper than other travel search engines and the hotel website. Actually, we had a small apartment, with kitchen and fridge.
There is a CVS next door, where you can buy sandwiches and drinks. This is good, because there are not many restaurants in the area. For lunch/dinner, you can walk towards 21st St. and G St. (GW University). There is a bar/restaurant with good atmosphere, and not too expensive. Otherwise, you can order in, they will give you some menus at the front desk.
The location is very good for tourists. It is a few blocks from the White House, the Lincoln Memorial and the Obelisk.
The only con I found is that the hotel is a bit noisy (we were on the 1st floor, on the walkway). I think most people are doing business and they get up very early.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Washington, D.C.
title: “Good value Hotel, Family oriented”
text:
We stayed there 3 nights with two teenagers, one 14, one 16. The rooms are spaciuos and clean, and our room had two queen beds and a pull-out sofa - perfect for 4. 
Pluses - Reasonable rates include cooked to order breakfast and happy hour. Food and drink was good but not great - which was expected for free service
Staff was friendly, the hotel is in good area for dining with both family and upscale adult choices close at hand - McD's, Subway, Bertucci's, Calif Pizza Kitchen, etc.
Cons - Its a good 4-5 block walk to Metro, you have to take Metro to really see any sites
There were a lot of families and children in the pool, at breakfast, etc. If you've got no patience for kids, its not the right place to be, at least during summer break.
There is a charge for internet and parking, although internet kiosks are available in the lobby.
Overall, its a busy hotel with lots of families - no different than found in many vacation destinations. Good value and service made our's a good stay, and this hotel did a great job filling that niche.

name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Girlfriends trip”
text: Had the best time at the Mayflower with my girlfriends. The hotel was AMAZING and the staff was even better. I definetly plan on going back to DC and I will stay no other place then the MAYFLOWER. Centrally located and the rooms are a great size. Make sure you say how to Roni at the concierge's desk( he is MR. personality).

name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center
title: “I want to go back to Courtyard by Marriott”
text:
The front desk staff (David King and Yael) were awesome! They were friendly and really made me feel welcome. While my room wasn't quite ready (I was early) I had a great lunch at Gordon Biersch (adjacent to the hotel) and when finished with the fantastic lunch, my room was ready and waiting!
The room was spacious, clean, and quiet. Totally impressed with this hotel, and I want to go back to Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center. Close to the metro and wonderful sites!

name: Washington Plaza
title: “You've got to be kidding”
text:
We are here now. This was the last room available in the heart of DC for this week. Forget the condition of the hotel, it gets much worse. After three attempts to get extra blankets for my family, we froze the first night here. There is no Concierge that I can tell. Yesterday, I sat at the bar during happy hour and was approached by 3 gay men. Plus, the drinks consist entirely of ice. The worst was last night, at the restaurant, the waiter tried to shake me down because he felt a 17% tip was inadequate.
The hotel is just now focusing on service. I'll change my rating after my stay if it gets better.

name: The River Inn
title: “OK...but a bit tired.”
text:
The River Inn is fine if you set your expectations to a barely 3 star hotel. The location is ok (near the Kennedy Center and Georgetown), the staff is friendly (if not a bit inept) and the price is right. The big sticking point is the room itself. They are like studio apartments (full kitchen included) that need a renovation. The leather (naugahyde?) headboards are peeling and worn, the lighting is minimal and the rooms are in need of better lighting. Also, little things get annoying after the first day (no ramp to the front door so you bump your bags down the steps, the elevator can be painfully slow, the wifi is spotty, the business/fitness center is a joke). 
Would I stay here again? Probably, since options are limited in this area. Do I love it? No, not really.

name: Homewood Suites Washington, DC
title: “Good hotel, but bring your walking shoes, really!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel and the trip can best be described in 3 sections. The hotel, transportation, and the sites.
THE HOTEL & ROOM
Along the lines of the other comments, the hotel and room was nice. There is a lot of construction in DC and I don't think the hotel is older than 5 years. The room had new towels, sheets, kitchen appliances and furniture. The breakfast was ok, not mamas cooking but a few scrambled eggs, wheat cereal, yogurt, and skim milk will do. We didn’t use the gym. The staff is very helpful especially for getting change for transportation.
TRANSPPROTATION
This hotel is located away for the busy areas. There are a lot of apartments and town homes in the area. That’s great, but getting around is tuff. Forget the cabs if you are on a budget. I'll report later. We took the bus @ $1.25 per trip. We took the bus a lot since the train (Metro) is no shorter than 3 blocks away in any direction.
