The bus stop is 1 block down from Thomas Square on 15th street. Look for the CVS. As with any bus, there are those who don’t talk and have no smell, and then there are others. Deal with it or walk. We did some of that at first, but DC is no London. The blocks are long. The wait may be 10 minutes, but it will save your feet for shopping.We didn’t want to walk all dressed up for dinner, so we took a cab. The cab ride from the airport across the river was $14.00, the cab ride to Georgia Browns, only 4 blocks away was $8 bucks. Nuff said.
THE SITES
We saw a lot of stuff. Worth the trip at least once.The library of congress is nice, but dont expect to see any books! You will need tickets for most places. Get up early for all the tours, arriving about 6:30 am should do it. We ate at Georgia Brown for dinner and gess what. Get there early too! 
Overall the stay was good. I'm a little tired from all the walking.
Enjoy

name: Morrison-Clark Historic Inn
title: “Comfortable and Accomodating”
text: We stayed here for a weekend getaway. The staff was really nice. When we left our gloves in the car, which was in valet, they had no problem retrieving them for us. They gave great recommendations for night life and transportation. The rooms were very clean and comfortable. However, the space was a bit small. The location is good, and it's easy to get anywhere in DC. Overall, we really enjoyed our stay.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Beautiful”
text: enjoyed Omni Shoreham. Room clean and request for extra towels was promptly filled. Would stay there again if I have a choice.

name: JW Marriott Washington DC
title: “Great central location”
text: Great, central location when taking the family to DC - less than 2 blocks to a couple of different Metro stops and only a few blocks from several Smithsonian museums including the American History Museum, Natural History Museum and the National Gallery of Art. Right around the corner from the White House and Treasury and plenty of great restaurants in the area. It is not the least expensive hotel by any stretch (valet parking is $45 + tax - I recommend parking at DCA for $20/night and taking the Metro in town - we saved nearly $100 doing this) but the location can't be beat. Pool is indoors but worked well for the family and the fitness center is well equipped and good size. Staff could not have been nicer. Worth paying a little more for a city view otherwise you are staring at bricks and the view, especially from the higher floors is magnifcent

name: Washington Plaza
title: “Avoid it!”
text:
Thank goodness I only stayed one night. Not worth the money. My room smell terrible. Non-smoking areas are a joke.
The curtains and the carpet were DISGUSTING.
Do not be fooled by the good-looking lobby. This hotel needs to undergo major renovations...
The only positive thing is that is well located, but there are a lot of other hotels in the same area.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Luxury surroundings and attentive service at the Shoreham”
text: My partner and I stayed at the Omni Shoreham over Labor Day weekend 2010 for a "staycation," staying close to home, and seeing all the tourist sites we've never visited before. I found an excellent deal online, and booked a room. There were some complications with the initial reservation, but they were eventually sorted out completely by the front desk staff when we arrived. Our room had a king-sized bed, and a good-sized living room, with a sofa, table and chairs, desk, and dresser with TV. We were happy to find two cold bottles of water in the fridge. I joined the Omni "Select Guest" program before making the reservation, and this was a good idea; it brought with it free WiFi in our room (usually $9.99/day), and two free beverages per person in the mornings delivered to the room. Two different concierges were helpful on two different days, helping us print out tickets for the Old Town Trolley tour, and recommending local restaurants. We enjoyed the pool and the poolside service, and found the gym to have everything we needed and wanted, including fresh ice water, towels, and high-quality machines, and additional workout supplies. Overall, our stay was excellent, and we were very pleased with the staff's positive attitude and attentive service.

name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Historic DC Hotel. Two Great Stays Here.”
text: I stayed at the Mayflower for the second time recently when I was in DC for a weekend getaway. If you arrive during times of heavy traffic (which seems to be always in DC), expect to get honked at a time or two as you wait for the valet to get to you. After that, your worries are over. The hotel is beautiful, and the staff was so friendly and helpful. I got the room on priceline.com, and didn't expect to get the best room. However, I got a room on the top floor that was really nice. The girl at the front desk was particularly nice, and welcomed me to the Mayflower despite the fact that I probably booked the room for considerably less than most of the other guests. The door staff can catch a cab for you in no time so I would not at all recommend driving your own vehicle around DC. Traffic is terrible, and parking can be brutal. Also, there is a Metro station within 2 blocks of the hotel that makes catching the train overly simple. I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at the Mayflower, and look forward to staying there again.

name: Embassy Suites Chevy Chase Pavilion
title: “Excellent choice for family vacation”
text: Spent four nights at the Embassy Suites Chevy Chase Pavilion with spouse and three kids (18, 15 & 11) while seeing the sights of DC. The thing we all most appreciated about this hotel -- especially after a full day of touring -- was the VERY convenient access to the Metro (located in lower level of hotel property). As a family of five, we appreciated the spacious two-room suite that included a sofa sleeper. Beds could have been firmer (sagged a little toward the middle). The bar area in the room offered a second sink and mirror which was helpful for getting ready every morning. Fridge came in handy for our leftover cheesecake from the Cheesecake Factory Restaurant adjacent to the hotel. As at other Embassy Suites we've stayed at, breakfast was always plentiful -- and complimentary! Pool, hot tub and workout facility met our expectations. We had an upper floor room so were not affected by noise from outside traffic or 3rd floor breakfast area. Front desk staff was always friendly and helpful. One tip: if parking in the pavilion's ramp, park near the "hotel" elevator (rather than the "shops" or "office" elevator). We parked near and used the "office" elevator and had to take two elevators to get to the lobby. Not a big deal, just a little confusing at first. Bottom line: every member of the family agreed they'd want to stay here again if ever back in the area.

name: JW Marriott Washington DC
title: “Excellent for sightseeing base”
text:
We got a 'deal' on the hotel over Memorial Day weekend. Still more expensive than other choices but in the end I was very pleased. We paid a bit extra for a room with a view out onto the Plaza - something I'm usually opposed to spending money on. This was our kids' first trip to DC and I think they really enjoyed looking out over the City. One night it was a bit noisy as there was some kind of party going on in the plaza but it was over by 10 pm. 
The room was nicely decorated, updated and comfortable. Everything was clean.The only strange thing was that there were neither towel racks nor a fan in the bathroom. Parents beware - the mini bar is one with the automatic sensor so if you move something you will be charged! 
We paid to have breakfast included with the room price and that was well worth it. The buffet breakfast had a great selection every day - fresh waffles and omelettes, and the usual cereals, eggs, muffins etc. Definitely worth it for a family of 4. We ate dinner here one night and it wasn't anything exceptional and was priced for the convenience. I will say that the dining room staff was exceptionally friendly.
We used the pool every afternoon for a mid-day break and never found it crowded at that time even though it is a bit small. The one evening we went it was packed. There is a nice small courtyard adjacent to the pool with table and chairs for those who would rather lounge outside. 
The metro is about a block away and you can walk to the Mall. We used the metro pretty much only to get to a few places such as the zoo.
I have no complaints and would stay there again. Definitely recommended for a home base for a family sightseeing in DC.

name: Beacon Hotel & Corporate Quarters
title: “Great value!”
text:
We stayed for 3 nights a this hotel which was a very nice surprise regarding value for money!!
The room had an very big and comfortable bed, the bathroom was very clean and the room was spacious.
The standard of the room was very good - no flaws at all.
We has hoped to try the sky-bar but unfortunately it closed early or was occupied.
Will definately stay there again if i can find the same price again (225 USD per night)!

name: Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Right next to Convention Center!”
text: Easy walk across the street to the Convention Center. Starbucks in lobby. Breakfast buffet was great in the mornings. Room was very clean, bed was comfortable, nicely decorated, flat screen tv. Some front desk clerks had attitude...but Concierge & bell staff was wonderful. No pool, and no business center closest is at a Fed-Ex down the street, not in the hotel. Would stay again if in town for a convention (not in the nicest part of town), but if in DC for fun/tourist stuff would not stay there, Georgetown is much nicer and safer.

name: The River Inn
title: “Nice Stay! Awesome location! They could improve sleep quality.”
text:
They gave us a Potomac 1 bedroom suite instead of the regular room that was on our reservation. This was GREAT! The room was VERY big and had a nice view of Potomac River. The room was very well furnitured and the bathroom was very clean. Wi-Fi worked but they could improve the signal strengh.
Breakfast was included. It's not an excellent breakfast but it is good enough if you are staying for a few days. They had the same food every day.
There was a very comfortable KING bed in the room and a VERY UNCOMFORTABLE sofa bed in the living room. You should really think about this if you are an adult. The 
sleep quality is very bad at the sofa bed!
Restaurant staff could be a little bit more pleasant.
Despites all that it is a nice hotel close to all attractions and to the subway!

name: Beacon Hotel & Corporate Quarters
title: “Overpriced, noisy”
text:
Located on Rhode Island Ave. at the intersection of Massachusetts Ave., this hotel has heavy street traffic and considerable street noise. It is convenient to Dupont Circle (3-4 blocks away), but other hotels are equally convenient, quieter, and better priced. 
The lobby is tiny, with guests crowded into a small space for check in and check out, and the elevators compete with the same space. There are only 2 elevators to service multiple stores, and when I stayed there in June 2007 only one was working. I stayed on the 4th floor and used the stairs because I got tired of waiting for the elevator. 
The adjoining restaurant is very expensive for the food served. Much better restaurants can be found 4-5 blocks up 17th Street, and much better pricing.

name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Overall, a decent stay.”
text: The Mayflower Rennaisance is no doubt a beautiful historic hotel and overall, we enjoyed our stay there. We were, however, disappointed when upon after first full day of touring around D.C., we came back to a room where the beds hadn't been made, towels hadn't been changed, coffee hadn't been replaced, etc. Bottom line, our room wasn't touched. We were also billed over hundred dollars by Renaissance for what should have been redeemed Marriott points. The location is great and the staff is extremely friendly and helpful.

name: Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Fantastic Stay!!”
text: My wife and I stayed a week at the Renaissance in June, 2008 on a sightseeing tour of Washington DC. If I could think of anything negative at all to say it would be that there was a lot of noise from the street below our room from traffic. Every other aspect of our stay was fantastic. The room was exceptionally clean and well appointed. The housekeeping staff did a great job every day. Every single employee was cheerful and friendly. They all greeted us each time we came and went with a smile and a hello. They were all helpful and made it seem as though we were sincerely appreciated. There were 3 metro stations within 3 blocks of the hotel, all within an easy 5 minute walk. There were many restaurants nearby and a movie theatre about 4 blocks away in China Town. The hotel is located close to all the major museums and the national mall. Only 5 blocks from the White House. Parking was 22 dollars per day. We never moved our car all week. The concierge was friendly and very helpful. All the things I had read about the hotel being located in a bad neighborhood was totally wrong. We walked all over the neighborhood both day and night and never once felt uneasy or nervous about our safety. We saw about 3 homeless folks at different times in doorways asleep, but there were police everywhere. There are tons of business people walking the sidewalks all the time and we felt quite safe. All in all we were well pleased and would reccomend the Renaissance to anyone wishing to stay in Downtown DC.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Seamless Service in beautiful property”
text:
Incredible service starting as soon as we approached the hotel. We arrived via a west coast red eye flight and the hotel was kind enough to provide us a very early in check in.
Very nice with the daily wake up coffee tray delivered to your door. For a few bucks they'll add a bagel or muffin.
The room was nice and spacious with a comfortable king bed. 
The pool and grounds made it feel like a resort and was a great reprieve from the heat and bustle of the city. 
The staff here were very helpful, kind and friendly. We really enjoyed our stay.

name: Beacon Hotel & Corporate Quarters
title: “Waited ONE HOUR for two pillows!!!!!!!”
text: My husband and I traveled from NJ to DC for his friends birthday celebration. We left NJ late Friday night and arrived at the Beacon Hotel around 11:30 p.m. Upon our arrival we realized that the room was smaller than we anticipated and more importantly after suchna long drive only had two pillows on the bed. I called down the front desk and requested two pillows, about 30 minutes later a Mr. James showed up to our room with one pillow and argued with my husband that we only requested one pillow. My husband made two trips down to the front desk after driving for 4 hours that night. We had to wait another 30 minutes for the other pillow. I complained on our last day and the acting manager Paul's only exlaination was that Mr. James works for an out side company. I was not please at all. My next time in DC I will stay at the Doubletree down the block. If you do decide to stay here be careful of the bathtub....I almost fell when trying to get out...You need assitance because it built higher than usual.

name: Morrison-Clark Historic Inn
title: “Diamond in the city”
text: I'm a native Washingtonian but have never heard of or seen this hotel before. It was a nice change from other hotels I've stayed in with a quiet court yard, fire place in the lobby area and over all quiet area. It seems like it can be a Bed-n-Breakfast but its not.

name: Beacon Hotel & Corporate Quarters
title: “The Stay was fine but the staff needs to go”
text: To the very rude staff of the Beacon please make sure the people your talking rudely about over something that was very much your fault, are not fluent in the language you are insulting them. I have never in my life had to deal with such a unprofessional staff before. Just goes to show you, you could pay good money to stay in a nice hotel but the untrained and hostile staff erase everything good. At the same time I dont think that the GM cares alot either my email expalaning what happened has gone without response.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “A luxurious experience”
text:
A really nice hotel, with a stunning lobby. Excellent facilities, including the pool. Was there for a workshop/conference and this was an ideal venue.
The best thing of all was the reasonable price and great quality of the 'eat all u can' buffet and the menu in the hotel restaurant. 
Only issue was being a few miles away from downtown, but on reflection that was no bad thing :-)
The hotel staff were really helpful

name: Embassy Suites Chevy Chase Pavilion
title: “Good hotel for family....”
text: We really liked this hotel. I chose it because of the reviews AND because it is sooooo close to the metro. Loved the morning breakfast and the evening reception. Always plenty of food! Very kid friendly hotel. It's a bit outdated and the beds were a bit mushy, but I would stay here again in a heartbeat. Next to a mall too. The worst thing was, there is only 1 washer and 1 dryer in the whole hotel!!! I couldn't believe this!

name: Grand Hyatt Washington
title: “a great stay for a 60th birthday surprise”
text:
We stayed at the Grand Hyatt on Aug 10th and had a superb stay. The room was fabulous, super clean, nicely decorated and comfortable. We're not accustomed to staying in business type hotels and really enjoyed the posh room. For us, it's posh. :-) I mentioned that one of us was celebrating a big 60th birthday and was quite surprised when we came back to the room after a day of sightseeing to find a piece of thick, chocolate cake, decorated with "Happy B" in chocolate on the side of the plate, goblets, a bottle of bubbly in an ice bucket and a birthday card. The Birthday Boy (should I say "man" since he turned 60?) was thrilled!
It was a GREAT surprise and I couldn't have asked for more. I scoured the internet for ages trying to decide which special hotel to book for his birthday. I wanted something really nice or something really different. He didn't know which one I had booked and was surprised when we arrived by Metro. 
The next morning we went down for the complimentary breakfast buffet. I wasn't expecting much since reading some grumblings here but was surprised by the spectacle of a breakfast buffet. There was a beautiful, eye-catching display of hot foods, fruit, fresh juices on ice and sweets. We were quite taken with the variety of the hot items. It's a big breakfast buffet and everything was delicious. Of course, the "Birthday Boy' (also known as the one with a great fondness for food) loved it. 
Lucky for us, DC had Restaurant Week that week and we enjoyed TenPenh, DC Grill and Cordoroy. That's a lot of heavy duty eating for a 2-day/1-night stay! We loved DC Grill the best and the Birthday Boy thinks the hotel breakfast buffet is right up there too.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center
title: “Great location and value”
text:
My husband and I stayed here two nights during the Blizzard of '09. The location is great. Within walking distance to National Mall, White House, monuments, Chinatown, and many more. We were given a room on the 8th floor looking out to the Spy Museum and the Holiday Market. Room is spacious if strangely configured. The sink is outside the bathroom, which I personally don't like. The room and the hotel were clean. My only gripe is that the room furnishings looked cheap, the closet door did not close and TV had a very limited number of free channels. Normally I would not care about the TV, but this time we had to spend moret ime in the room since it was snowing outside and the entire DC was closed. The staff frienfdy but a little slow. Could be because they had only essential staff due to the snow.
All in all, this was a great value for $98/night (AAA rate)

name: The Normandy Hotel
title: “Good, but room for improvement”
text:
This hotel is fairly small compared to what I usually stay in, however it is clean and I didn't have any real problems with the staff. My issue would be that a towel I took with me was taken from the room, I assume that it was an innocent mistake by the hotel cleaning staff (ie. they thought that it was one of their own) so as soon as I realised I e mailed the hotel but they couldn't find it - I didn't even get much of an apology either. A towel is a towel and not a big deal, but it does concern me that if they can take that what else can they take..
The rooms are of a fair size, I stayed in a twin room and it was plently big enough, the room comfortably fitted in two double beds. 
The location was a bit of out the way but we knew that and do not mind walking and so we often walked to the white house / monument although getting a cab would not have been difficult. The food at the sister hotel (Jurys Washington) was very nice and that hotel looked a lot more upmarket than the Normandy Inn.
I would return to the Normandy Inn again BUT I would make sure that all of my stuff was looked away in a suitcase whenever I wasn't in the room and that I did not take anything of great value to me.

name: State Plaza Hotel
title: “Stay away from this hotel”
text: I encourage everyone to stay away from this hotel. The service is terrible. One of their valet parking workers gave me my car back with 2 feet long scraping on the rear door along with a big dent. When I reported the damage to them the administration resorted to procrastination tactics and after two weeks of waiting they informed me that their insurance company would not cover the damage. I am still fighting it, and will do my best to get them to pay for what they have done to my car. What upsets me the most is that the valet driver did not acknowledge the accident and deliberately attempted to conceal it from me. Moreover, the hotel administration added more insults to the injury by evading being held accountable. So, my advice to all of you to is to find a different hotel that really value their guests and take care of their properties. This one has failed miserably in all these basic services.

name: Washington Plaza
title: “Komfortables Hotel für wenig Geld, etwas außerhalb”
text:
Das Hotel liegt mehrere Blocks von der nächsten Metro entfernt. Das ist aber kein Problem. Von dort ist man innerhalb von maximal 10 Minuten in der Innenstadt bzw. bei allen touristischen Zielen.
Das Zimmer, das wir hatten, war sehr komfortabel, fast schon luxoriös. Wir haben uns insgesamt sehr wohl gefühlt. Der Service Desk und auch alle anderen Mitarbeiter waren stets äußerst freundlich und hilfsbereit.
Laut einem Reiseführer (Marco Polo?), liegt das Hotel gerade noch in einem Bereich, den man angeblich als Touri meiden sollte, aber davon haben wir nichts gemerkt.
In weniger als 5 Minuten erreicht man einen CVS Store (Apotheke/Supermarkt). Auch diverse Restaurants sind fussläufig erreichbar.
Alles in allem würden wir hier wieder bleiben und können das Hotel uneingeschränkt weiterempfehlen.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center
title: “great value and location”
text: reasonable rate for family of four (approx. $149) in a great location. Room was very comfortable and clean. In room internet was a little slow, but this was not our priority. Several convenient stores located near hotel for family snacks and quick meals ( CVS, subway, bread/bagel store). One week day there was a farmers market a few blocks from the hotel (maybe it was Thursday?) Great location, easy to walk to most sights.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center
title: “Second Stay - Nice perks”
text: This is my second time to stay in this Courtyard, It's location is perfect to visit many historic sites and it's in an interesting historic building. Beds were good, and I liked that the sink in our room was separated from the other part of the bathroom because I was sharing a room with a colleague. The last time I was in this hotel there was a restaurant in the lower level, but there is now more of a snack bar and a business center...and this is fine. On this trip the doorman offered small cold water bottles when we left the room (and it was very hot) and this was very much appreciated!! Also, in the afternoon there were snacks and drinks in the lobby for those staying at the hotel...a very nice perk!

name: The Normandy Hotel
title: “Nice but...”
text:
The staff was very friendly and helpful. The hotel appeared to be well kept. The location is great; I was able to order Chinese and have it delivered to my room.
We discovered the only problem with the hotel after we were about to check out. Our carpet was filthy. The carpet was dark colored and we were not able to see the dirt during out stay(in room 403). We later saw that after my 1 yr old nice had been crawling on the floor her pink clothes were ruined. When I got back home my white socks were filthy. I thought the dirt may have come from the airport when I took off my shoes, I rationalized. But that was not the case. It was the hotel. Don't accept room 403.

name: Grand Hyatt Washington
title: “Very Swank”
text:
Very upscale hotel. Great for tourist as the hotel is connected to the Metro through the Metro Center stop. I was there for a business conference. I was very impressed. Expect to pay for pool use and wireless internet. A little pricy, but I guess you have to expect that in DC.
Very clean, up-to-date rooms and public areas. I would definitely stay here again (if I got a good deal on the room!).

name: Grand Hyatt Washington
title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
Just got back from a 4 night stay at this hotel. I got a $139 a night rate for all nights except the last night which was $319. 
The price included a free breakfast buffet for every morning of our stay. The buffet included things like fresh fruit, smoothies in shot glasses, scrambled eggs, potatoes, sticky buns on Sunday, bagels, toast, sausage, bacon, oatmeal, grits, juices, etc. There were enough choices to make anybody happy. It was nice and convenient. 
Our room was clean and the bed and pillows were extremely comfortable. I believe the pillows were down pillows because your head just melted into the pillows. The bathroom was not huge but was not tiny, it was a good size. The bathtub was a very nice size as well. The room had a full size ironing board and iron and a mini bar. We had a king bed, and two large sized chairs, desk, and large 4 drawer dresser. The only thing I didn't like about the room was that it seemed damp in there for some reason. We were on the eleventh floor with a view of the atrium and there was absolutely no noise to keep us awake at night. We had HBO in our room which was nice to watch a free movie in the evening as we drifted off to sleep. 
The Metro Center station is a short indoor walk via connecting hallways. We took the Metro back to the airport when we left via the blue line called Franconia. If we had known how to use the Metro at the time, we would have taken the Metro to the hotel when we got there as well. 
The health club next door had a pool that we were allowed to use for free. The ladies' locker room and the mens' locker room have a tiny sauna which felt very relaxing and soothing after getting out of the chilly pool. 
The hotel has a sports bar called Grand Slam that was nice to sit and have a few drinks or a meal. 
The cleaning staff always seemed to clean our room at the perfect time while we were gone as we were in and out of our room throughout the day so that was nice.
Hard Rock Cafe, ESPN Zone, Capitol Brewing Company, and China Town were all within very easy walking distance for a nice meal. 
Ford's Theater is right down the street. The International Spy Museaum if very close by. Also, we walked to the White House from the hotel on our first night. 
This is a nice hotel in a great location and I would definitely stay there again.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center
title: “Good Value for Location”
text: Nothing fancy about this hotel, but clean, comfortable, friendly staff and a great location for the price. Could walk to Nat'l Archives, and "Mall" easily, steps from Spy Museum. Friends of ours stayed in a boutique hotel just two blocks away for 2 nights for the price of our 3 nights here. Same size room, just a little less flare at the Courtyard. Breakfast buffet was ok, but for just a few dollars more go to the Hotel Monaco (two blocks) for excellent brunch with tasty Bloody Mary's.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Great home base for visit to DC”
text: We had a fantastic stay at the Omni Shoreham. It is located just steps from the Metro and has several dining options around the corner (recommendation: avoid all three of the Indian restaurants - all bad). The hotel is from the 1930's, but the service is 2010. Very good communication leading to stay, including option to check in ahead of time. Be sure to sign up for their frequent stay club ahead of time and you will receive even better treatment, including free wi-fi and hot beverages to your door. Our rooms were tremendous, overlooking the park and with a balcony. Given that it's an old hotel, I am sure rooms vary. Very good deals if you can find a week where hotel is not taken up by meetings. We paid a very low rate through hotel web site that included parking and free breakfast (Zoo Package). Big thumbs up.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Wonderful stay!”
text: My husband & I spent 3 nights here & it was wonderful! It is basically located just across the street from the Metro station which was VERY convenient! We never even needed a rental car. This hotel is very beautiful and a very friendly staff. We had a buffet breakfast each morning that was GREAT, we never needed anything to eat before dinner! We will stay here again if the opportunity arises!

name: The Normandy Hotel
title: “Great Hotel and Reasonable”
text: After searching dozens of hotels, I settled for this hotel after reading reviews from Trip Advisor. We loved this hotel. It was small, intimate and cozy. The hotel is on a residential street of beautiful homes and embassies . The service was excellent. The walk of 8-10 minutes to tons of restaurants was easy and a great trendy part of the City -- Dupont Circle. If your energetic - the walk from the White House (25 mins) takes you past Felines Basement and many shops and restaurants. I would stay there again.

name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “would not suggest staying at this hotel”
text: I had a very disturbing experience staying at this very old and run down hotel. The air conditioning is very loud and ruins any sort of peace and quiet in the room. The room itself is old and in need of repairs. I felt like it was pulling teeth to get any sort of assistance while staying there. To get extra towels or having a maid to come in to make up your room in the morning was like pulling teeth. Forget about receiving a turn down in the evening, it just doesn't happen. The location is alright but not great. It is still a distance to get to any good restaurants. I would definitely say go find a more accomodating hotel when staying in Dc this one is not worth wasting your time and money at.

name: The River Inn
title: “Has character and space!”
text:
I came to DC on business last week, and this was the hotel 'assigned' to us. I got a corner suite with the kitchen and three separate rooms. The furniture are rustic Italian-styled (so I am told) and the room had a retro feel. The televisions were first rate with huge selection; the one in the living room had a DVD player...great for the CD collection I happened to bring! Convenience to the metro was great; try the Aroma Indian Restaurant on I street, about 5 blocks away! 
I should also mention that through some mixup (on our end, probably), I was listed to come in a day earlier than I did, so they listed me as a no-show for the first day. But, they had no problem taking that extra day off when I checked out. 
I was asked to come back next year to perform the same duties, so I will gently "prod" the travel folks to choose this hotel again next year! Great!!

name: The Fairfax at Embassy Row, a Starwood Luxury Collection Hotel
title: “nice hotel , great location”
text:
We stayed here recently and really liked it. We got a very good deal on Hotwire , but I would recommend traveling to the area when the congress is not in session , since most places will decrease their prices. It is conveniently located just 2 blocks from Dupont circle metro station. This is a historic building, recently rennonvated, well kept and nicely old style decorated. We had a decent size room which was very clean with very soft linens. Decoration was old style and victorian . Hotel staff were really polite and helpful. Business center was okay with 2 PCs and a printer. 
We didn't try the restaurants on site and I cannot comment on them. The only really negative point was thin walls ! I travel a lot and have never experienced such thin walls even in cheap motels ! The noise from next door is easily in your ears ! First night people next door were really noisy, but we were lucky that they checked out the next day ! 
But this was such a charming place that I cannot remove a star for this problem ! 
I would stay here again if get a good deal again. Great place .

name: St. Gregory Hotel & Suites
title: “A great location for business or pleasure with the greatest staff”
text: From the time we entered the hotel we were made to feel at home From a one night stay to a longer term stay the hotel and staff at St Gregory are the best in Washington DC

name: State Plaza Hotel
title: “Outstanding stay for your money!”
text: I picked this hotel on line for our trip. Our High school band was coming to march in the Memorial Day Parade. Right in the heart of DC, walking distance to alot of sites or the metro stop a few blocks away. The staff was courteous and friendly. Saved my parents on parking, told them street parking was free when they came. Beds were awesome (better than the Double tree in Crystal City that our band stayed at). Although my friends said the breakfast buffet was very exspensive. They would not do it again, eat their, but overall very satisfied. Would recommend this hotel to anyone. Kuddos!!!!

name: Washington Hilton
title: “Hotel confortevole, colazione ottima”
text: hotel rinnovato da poco, quindi le camere e i bagni erano molto carini e puliti. Colazione impeccabile, mai mangiate delle "scrambled eggs" così buone! la zona è tranquilla, ma basta allontanarsi di poco e si arriva alla discutibile DuPont Circle che è frequentata, soprattutto nelle ore serali, da tipi poco raccomandabili. in generale, il mio giudizio è positivo

name: Washington Plaza
title: “Y aller sans hésiter !!!”
text:
Nous avons passé 2 jours au Washington Plaza avec mon conjoint et ce fut un séjour extra!
Nous sommes arrivés à 13h alors que le check in avait lieu à 15h et la chambre était déjà prête! On a donc pu poser nos valises et partir visiter.
L'hôtel est très bien situé, à 10 minutes à pieds de la Maison Blanche.
De retour à l'hôtel en fin d'après-midi, nous avons pu profiter de la piscine et du bar de la piscine. C'est fantastique de pouvoir faire cela en plein coeur de la ville !
La chambre est très spacieuse, la literie très confortable et c'est très propre.
Le petit déjeuner est très bon et pas très cher.
Seul petit bémol (oui il en faut bien un) le restaurant n'est pas génial...il doit y en avoir de meilleurs dans DC.

name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Centrally Located”
text: We enjoyed this centrally located hotel. Elevators were fast, doormen were helpful in getting taxi's fast, concierge very helpful w/metro directions, making restaurant reservations for us & just helping with general information. Our room was on 3rd floor overlooking a quiet side street so we slept GREAT!!! We would stay here again.

name: Washington Hilton
title: “Wie zu erwarten gute Qualitaet”
text:
Der Aufenthalt im Hilton wird mir lange in guter Erinnerung bleiben. Die Betten waren sehr gemuetlich, das Bad sowie das Zimmer geräumig und schön eingerichtet. Der Service war gut und es war nichts zu bemaengeln.
Bis zur naechsten U-Bahn Station läuft man ca fuenf Minuten. von daher ist sie Lage nicht perfekt aber durchaus gut.
Das weisse haus ist zu Fuß in etwa 20 Minuten zu erreichen.

name: Grand Hyatt Washington
title: “Awesome value--great location”
text: I don't understand any of the negative reviews as I thought this hotel was wonderful, especially for the $99 rate I paid! 10 min walk to the Mall and all the sites. Room was clean, comfortable, updated. Staff was helpful and even received a 50% coupon for the breakfast buffet. When I come to DC again, I would definitely stay here, especially if the rate remains low. In DC it's hard to find an affordable NICE hotel so the Grand Hyatt ranks high on my list!

name: Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “i really liked staying here”
text: overall this hotel is a nice one. its in a great spot. Everything is walking distance from the hotel. The concierge staff are very helpful. The only thing is it doesn't have is a pool... but you know thats not always a necessity.

name: The Fairfax at Embassy Row, a Starwood Luxury Collection Hotel
title: “If you can nab a stay at this hotel at a discount, DO IT!”
text: Lovely hotel conveniently located within one block of Dupont Circle Metro. I loved the fact that they didn't charge for business center access, and the in house hotel gym is at least decent (small, but everything was fairly modern and in working order). Rooms are a bit dated, but I felt that it was a great deal for the price. Lounge and restaurant both top notch.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Excellent”
text:
This was the second time I have stayed at the Omni Shoreham. It is such a beautiful hotel and didn't disappoint. The first time I stayed in 2009 the foyer displayed absolutely beautiful long stem roses. This time it was decorated in wonderful Xmas decorations.
The rooms are good with very comfortable beds and the room service was good. I had a problem with my suitcase lock and the maintenance man was there in a jiffy to fix it for me.
There is a wonderful bar at the front of the hotel which has a very welcoming feeling to it. I even met a lady who lives over the road who has made this bar her local place for a drink at the end of the day.
Job well done Omni Shoreham for a fabulous hotel.

name: The Eldon Luxury Suites
title: “Geheimtipp in Washingotn D.C. - klasse Suitenhotel zu super Preisen”
text: Wir waren hier auf unserem ersten Trip in den USA für 2 Tage und das Eldon ist wirklich ausßergewöhnlich. Für den Preis wirklich ein super tolles Hitel mit extrem großem Hauptzimmer mit schöner offener Küche und sämtlichen Annehmlichkeiten, die man sich vorstellen kann. Das Bad und das Bett sind vom Allerfeinsten und man fühlt sich rundum wohl. Ein richtig guter Geheimtipp. Parkplatz wird nachts abgeschlossen und die Lage ist wirklich sehr gut. MIt einem kurzen Fußmarsch ist man direkt im Zentrum und bei allen Sehenswürdigkeiten. Das Personal ist nicht übertrieben nett, aber man wird stets gegrüßt und freundlich willkommen geheißen. Das typische amerikanische Frühstück mit Toast und Muffins ist auch inklusive und es gibt leckeren Orangensaft. Wir waren wirklcih rundum zufrieden, vor allem für den extrem guten Preis.

name: Beacon Hotel & Corporate Quarters
title: “Lovely hotel in a great position. Very accomodating staff.”
text: We stayed here for four days, two of them by ourselves before meeting up with friends. The hotel was centrally located for sightseeing and the staff were very helpful in accomodating our needs.

name: State Plaza Hotel
title: “Great Hotel for the Money”
text:
To all those who said this hotel was too far from the metro and from the National Mall........you are some lazy people. The location was great. 1/2 mile to the National Mall and Metro is not that far. I was also a little weary because several reviews complained about the Hotel staff being rude. Everyone we dealt with was wonderful. Answered all our questions, gave us recommendations on where to eat, ect. The hotel is older and could use some updates, but for the money you spend, it's a great deal!
Another bonus is that we got one of the suites even though we paid for a regular room. The suite had a full kitchen which was great!

name: Beacon Hotel & Corporate Quarters
title: “excellent efficient friendly service”
text: The staff is exemplary and the facilities are comfortable yet classy

name: Washington Plaza
title: “Great Place to Stay; Close to Monuments and Museums”
text:
We enjoyed our stay at Washington Plaza for many reasons:
- We booked (2) adjoining Superior Double rooms - these rooms had a locked, private, foyer-like double door, then each of our rooms had its own locked door. So, at times we kept the foyer-like double door locked and our (2) doors open so the family could come and go as they pleased.
- The Staff was friendly and helpful. Requested and received at no charge (2) small refrigerators. 
- The rooms were very clean and the beds were very comfortable.
- Newly installed, in-room, 4-digit code safe - large enough for a laptop.
- Coffee Maker. 
- Bath & Body Works Toiletries.
- Well maintained and relaxing outdoor Pool with a Lifeguard, Lounge Chairs/Pillows & Towels. Open from 9:00 am to 9:00 pm.
 - Saw Servers walking by with delicious looking Desserts & Frozen Drinks from the outdoor Bar.
- Walked approx. 1/4 mi. to McPherson Metro Station and purchased the "Rail Short Trip Pass" for $30.35 per person - good for 7 days. We took the Metro to all Museums, Monuments, Archives, Arlington Cemetery, Ford's Theatre, The Washington National's Baseball Stadium & The National Zoo.
- Washington Plaza (WP) is also within walking distance of some nice casual restaurants including City Buffet - a Chinese Buffet, and Pizza Authentica - both were clean & tasty.
- WP also within walking distance of a 24 hr. CVS Pharmacy. 
- Considering DC is a city, use good judgment and remain on your guard, just know that we never felt threatened or unsafe in this NW part of DC.
- $26.00 per night, underground, come-and-go-as-many-times-as-you-please or Valet (for a little more $) Parking. 
- See my TripAdvisor Review BEFORE you take a Tour with "OnBoard Tours".
- I would definitely recommend this hotel to others.

name: Washington Hilton
title: “Hotel da business”
text:
Ho soggiornato per lavoro, per essere molto grande offre un buon standard qualitativo. Buono e veloce il Chek in, la camera ampia, così come il bagno dove c'era una bella e ampia linea di cortesia inoltre la camera godeva una bella vista; nota negativa la moquette.
Buona la colazione con una ampia scelta, belle e funzionanti le sale riunioni, bellissima la sala plenaria. Hotel un po' lontano dal centro ma comunque in generale buono.

name: Washington Plaza
title: “Location is great, but it's the pool area that makes this hotel.”
text:
Stay here if for no other reason than the pool area.
After staying in New York with no place to really relax at the end of the day (we certainly couldn't relax in our cracker box hotel room), we decided that the next time we visited a large city we would stay in a hotel with a pool area. The Washington Plaza definitely fit the bill. After a long day of sight seeing and museum visiting, it was heaven to return to the Plaza, change into our swimming suites, and head down to the pool. After ordering a meal at the outdoor section of the hotel's restaurant (excellent food and service, by the way), we took a quick dip while waiting for the food to arrive, then sat down to enjoy our meal and drinks. Afterward, we would relax in some of the numerous lounge chairs, listening to soft music from the restaurant, the sound of the traffic from Thomas Circle reminding us we were in the heart of a major metropolis, yet safely dimmed by plants, trees, and neatly painted retaining wall. It truly was our oasis in Washington DC.
The rooms were always clean, as were the rest of the areas of the hotel.
The location of the hotel was excellent. Only six blocks north (a fifteen minute walk, all down hill) of the Washington Monument. The hotel is located on Thomas Circle, an attractive traffic circle with two beautiful stone churches.
The rooms we stayed in were modern and well appointed, if not overly large in size.
Service was excellent throughout our stay (though Jasmine at the front desk could take a step or two down from her high horse).
Value; well, what can you say. You're staying in a luxury hotel in the heart of Washington DC, so don't expect a "deal". But in our opinion the cost was well worth it in every respect.
The sleep quality was very good. Though we could hear doors closing from the hall, we never heard a sound from other rooms through the walls of our room.
What we liked the least: the elevators seemed a bit slow at times.
What we liked best: did I mention the pool area?

name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center
title: “Great Location!”
text: My husband and I decided on a quick trip to DC for the weekend. We chose this hotel because of it's proximity to the Metro Station, Smithsonians, restaurants and the Mall. I requested an early check-in since our flight arrived at 7am into Reagan. Took the yellow line straight to Gallery Place/Chinatown station...got to the Courtyard before 8am! Checked in at the hotel and they were able to get us our room. Room was on the 10th (top) floor. It was quite small and did not have a view of anything (unless you consider the space between 2 buildings a view.) It didn't matter to us. It was very clean, quiet, comfortable bed and just what we needed. We were not in the room much anyway. Everyone was very friendly. Very convenient (few blocks) to the Mall and the Smithsonians. Some of the best restaurants were in this area too. We would definitely stay here again!

name: The Fairfax at Embassy Row, a Starwood Luxury Collection Hotel
title: “elegant”
text: The Fairfax is an elegant old hotel that has been renovated to perfection. The service is excellent, rooms are clean and comfortable and the bed is outstanding. My only complaint is that the room is on the small side for the price and a lot of light leaks in around the door.

name: Washington Plaza
title: “OK, mehr aber auch nicht”
text:
Wir hatten ein bisschen Pech, dass genau vor unserem Fenster die Klimaanlage (Gebläse) war. Zimmer auf der Rückseite des zweiten Stocks also besser vermeiden.
Der Service war gut, die Aussatttung der Zimmer für amerik. Verhältnisse eher spärlich. Das Preis-Leistungsverhältnis ist gut.

name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Did not like The Renaissance Mayflower Hotel”
text: The location of the location of the hotel was perfect. Its very convenient to get food or walk to The White House. When I arrived to the hotel, I was greeted with warm welcome by the bell boy. The lobby was nice but the light setting was a little dim/dark. The hotel is big with long hallways. I dont like the setup of the floor. It seem pretty creepy to me. The long hallways, rooms on each side, dim lights and mirrors on the end of the hallways. They put me on the corner room of the floor. I had to walk from corner-end of the hallway to the middle of the floor to get to the elevator.

name: Washington Marriott at Metro Center
title: “Had a great weekend”
text: Everything was perfect. Staff, food, service, everything. Can't complain. I really like the location, it's close to everything, in special to Macy's which is right across from the building. I was surprised with the food, really good presentation and flavor.

name: L'Enfant Plaza Hotel
title: “Gutes Hotel direkt bei den DC Highlights”
text: Gutes Hotel welches in direkter Fußgänger-Nähe zu den wichtigste Attraktionen von DC liegt - in 5 Minuten steht man Mitten auf der Mall. Pool auf dem Dach war eine Attraktion für die Kids.

name: One Washington Circle Hotel
title: “Excellent service... except for bellboy”
text:
One Washington Circle Hotel is a very comfortable hotel and it is amazingly well located within the DC Area if you're in town for business. It's rates are quite reasonable, when compared with others nearby.
Internet access is free and of very high speed, both through cable and wifi.
Service is great and the crew are very kind. The only setback I found was litte help from the bellboys which for some unexplainable reason wouldn't help me with my luggage when arriving / departing. Best I could get from them was a door open.
I stayed twice through a business trip. The rooms where very comfortable. Some plumbing work was done during my second stay, management was careful enought as to notify me of this through a letter but luckily there were no problems for me and water never ran out.
The in house CityBistro has excellent food. Be aware though that room service ends early so if you're in the mood for a midnight meal, you're gonna have to order in.

name: JW Marriott Washington DC
title: “Accommodating and suitable”
text: Location good , Shop next door for groceries etc very handy worth big points if staying a few days , don't need a car , the touring redline buses stop there. Which are a perfect way to see Washington highly recommend. There are two Red line companies one has just bought the other line so you can get on any but they do have different stops be ware..one free washing machine on level 3 it's at the very end of corridor...could be a cue . wifi downstairs only

name: St. Gregory Hotel & Suites
title: “Not worth the money, how did they get 4 stars???”
text: The staff was incoherent at best! They set the tone for what would be a terrible weekend at an overpriced, poorly run, impostor of a 4 star hotel!

name: Homewood Suites Washington, DC
title: “Great service and value for money”
text: very comfortable hotel clean and well equipped room at an extremely reasonable rate, the reception staff could not have been more helpful and polite, warm friendly welcome and justly proud of their hotel. The location is actually not as bad as some reviewers have suggested, we walked to all the main tourist attractions from the hotel quite comfortably and then got the metro back to the nearest stop. Also some people have said the breakfast room was crowded which it was at peak times but thats because it was such a superb breakfast offering everything you could want and constantly being topped up, we didnt need to eat lunch! Fab stay, thank you to all the staff.

name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Nettes old fashion Hotel im Herzen Washingtons”
text:
Das Mayflower hat den Charm von einem alten Grand Hotel. Es ist sehr "old fashion" was seinen Charme ausmacht. Schöner Eingangsbereich mit großen Kristalllüstern, nettes Personal. 
Mein Zimmer war leider sehr klein und auch nicht mehr das frisch Renovierteste, aber es war sauber. Das Badezimmer war auch schon ziemlich in die Jahre gekommen und könnte eine Renovierung gebrauchen, aber ebenfalls sauber.
Das Hotel an sich liegt "mittendrin". Alle Sehenswürdigkeiten können gut zu Fuß erreicht werden. Am Weißen Haus ist man innerhalb von 10-15 Minuten zu Fuß. 
Viele schöne kleine Restaurants und Geschäfte sind ebenfalls zu Fuß zu erreichen. Die Metro und Bushaltestellen, quasi direkt von der Tür.

name: Residence Inn Washington DC / Vermont Ave.
title: “Good location, but needs some refreshing”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel many times over the last 5 years, as it's close to a client's office I visit 4-5 times per year. This hotel used to be my first choice. It is now becoming my last choice. Marriott needs to invest in this property and update it both cosmetically as well as with better HVAC and plumbing.
Location: Close proximitey to major attactions like the White House. Easy 4 block walk to the metro. Many excellent restaurants within an easy walk. 
Staff: Always extremely friendly and helpful. Usually able to accomodate an early check in. 
Rooms: Here's where the problems begin. I have stayed on every floor of this hotel. One is not better than the other. The matresses are uncomfortable. One side is extremely worn, so you roll from one side of the bed to the other. They need better mattresses or to rotate their mattresses for more even wear. In my last few stays the sheets and towels had holes in them from wear. Also, were very rough in texture. In more rooms than not, pipes frequently rattle and you can hear water running in the walls, ofent loud enough to prevent a good night's sleep. Finally, the AC is VERY loud and in some rooms blows directly onto the bed.
Breakfast room: Generally clean and has a good selection of breakfast items. I do not usually have dinner here, unless it's poor weather. Have enjoyed the manager reception on occasion.

name: Hampton Inn Washington, DC-Convention Center
title: “Convenient location with several dining options”
text: Enjoyed a one day visit within walking distance of several restaurants, attractions and the convention center. Friendly and helpful bellman and breakfast area staff. Hotel was clean with rooms well supplied with towels, etc. Comfortable beds, reasonable price. Parking a little high at $34 pls $6 tax.

name: Residence Inn Washington DC / Vermont Ave.
title: “Good location. Within walking distance to places of interest in Washington DC.”
text:
This is my second time in this hotel. Both instances were for work. It's the preferred lodging by our office since it's very near the location where the activities are to be held.
In both instances, the room I had were big and comfortable. The rooms and the common areas are well lit and clean. The staff are friendly and helpful. While its a bit pricey, the property is located in the part of the city that is accessible to various places of interest - the White House, the Capitol, Georgetown, The Mall, the Smithsonian, the World Bank and others. If you are fond of walking, as I am, all these places are accessible by walking from this hotel. Just bring comfortable shoes and hydrate often especially during the summer.

name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel
title: “Mehr Schein als Sein”
text:
Die Empfangshalle ist sehr beeindruckend, und einzelne Zimmer ebenfalls, obwohl es bei der Zimmergröße, obwohl es die selbe Preiskategorie ist, große Unterschiede in der Ausstattung (Möbel) und Größe gibt. Die Zimmer zur Straße sind sehr laut. Die amerkanischen Betten sind ein Traum, sehr weich, viel Kissen, aber diese Qualität gibt es auch in anderen Hotels. Hervorzuheben ist das freundliche Servicepersonal und die gute Lage. Das weiße Haus und diverse Sehenswürdigkeiten können zu Fuß erreicht werden.
Dringend Empfehlung für alle Businessreisende: Wintersachen mitbringen. Die Räume sind totatl unterkühlt.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “luxury on the go”
text: My husband and I just completed a 4 night stay here and we absoutly loved it! The staff was friendly and helpful, especially the head bellman, Elliott. Always ready to help get a taxi for you ro anything else needed. Our room was a cornor room with 3 windows. It was spacious and comfortable. The decor was beautiful. Be sure to join the Select Guest program. This allows free internet and 2 morning beverages. The morning bevereages were brought up and at appointed time asked each day. The location is near a Metro stop and lots of restaurants. Open City Cafe is across the street, for breakfast, lunch or dinner. Also 1 block over on Conn. Ave. Woodley Cafe is good for Lunch or dinner. We would definately stay here again!

name: Washington Court Hotel on Capitol Hill
title: “Overpriced for the lack of amenities”
text:
For full disclosure, I was not paying for this hotel myself, it was a business trip. But, that being said, these were my issues: WiFi cost $10 per 24 hours! and on top of that, it was very slow. I couldn't watch hulu without it buffering every 10 seconds, so eventually I gave up. Also, the continental breakfast cost $15. This included bagels, pastries, oatmeal, and fruit. Hot food cost $5 more. Third, there was no safe in the room, and no fridge either. I have never been in a modern hotel that did not have a safe in-room. 
I think that this hotel has inflated prices because they know most clients are businesspeople who will be charging it on expense accounts anyway. But still, I was underwhelmed for the price range.

name: George Washington University Inn
title: “Felt like we were returning home instead of a hotel...”
text: Stayed here while visiting colleges with my son. GWU Inn felt lke we were returning home instead of staying in a hotel. Location was perfect, near Foggy Bottom Metro, close to Whole Foods, great restaurants, Starbucks , quiet residential location, friendly doormen. My king sized bed was extremely comfortable and my son said sofa bed was comfortable too. Only problem was the refrigerator in our kitchenette didn't close. I would recommend this hotel.

name: Capital Hilton
title: “Great Location - Everything Else Simply Average”
text:
My wife and I chose the Capital Hilton based upon its location - for that, we were extremely pleased. For visiting the many monuments, museums, and historic locations in D.C., the location of this hotel is great. However, the hotel is in great need of an update. Our room was supposed to be a non-smoking room and while I am sure no one had smoked in this room recently, there was a distinct smell of smoke in the room - I am sure the room used to be a smoking room at one point in time. Unfortunately, we were told there were no other rooms we could be moved to and considering my wife is a Hilton Diamond member, I would hope we would have been moved to a better room if one were available. In addition, the bed was extremely uncomfortable and was well past its prime. It sagged considerably in the middle, provided little support, and if you sat on any edge of the bed it felt as if the top part of the mattress sunk to the point it was touching the bottom part of the mattress.
I give the hotel an overall rating of 3 based solely upon the location. I would not recommend this hotel to others even with the great location because there are other hotels in the immediate area that are newer and nicer. With an update to the interiors of the rooms, including new beds and removal of the smokey smell from rooms that were previously smoking rooms, this would be a great hotel. Until that happens, the Capital Hilton is merely average especially considering the room rate that is currently charged.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Washington, D.C.
title: “Fantastic, just fantastic!!”
text: Stayed here for 3 night with my wife our baby & my in-laws. Cant say enough good things about it, the rooms were great, the hotel lobby itself was beautifuil with a waterfall built inside!! The complementry breakfast was great, there was SO much verity that no one could say they dont have this or that. The staff was excellent and very accomodating. Would stay here again.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Washington, D.C.
title: “Great Family Hotel”
text:
This Hotel is perfect for a family. The kids LOVED having their own LCD Flat screen TV, the indoor pool, the pancakes,etc at breakfast and the snacks and sodas during the managers cocktail hour. All of our friends at other hotels came by and swam at ours. The adults will also love the privacy the two bedroom suite offers, the made to order breakfast with cappucino or mocha coffee and the cocktail hour(I had a martini every night after our full days!)
It is situated exactly between the Foggy Bottom and Dupont Circle metro stops, within walking distance to Georgetown and surrounded by many good and varied restaurants.

name: Donovan House - A Kimpton Hotel
title: “Coolest Shower Ever”
text: Stayed in DC for a conference and chose this hotel rather than the conference site . . . what a great move! The room was perfectly comfortable for one or two, super comfy bed and plenty of closet and drawer space for clothes. Really nice soaps and toiletries, and a hair dryer that actually WORKED! Amazing! The best feature, however, was the walk-in shower that physically stood in the middle of the room inside an opaque cylindrical structure. Totally fun. My only complaint is that the robes and towels smelled very faintly of hospital antiseptic - never had that happen before. And when I ordered room service, they neglected to inform me of the size of the portions, which ended up in me way over-ordering. Nevertheless, it's a great location and I would return again for sure!

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “excelent hotel”
text:
we habe been there for weekend 17-20/04 .The hotel is very big great location near metro station ( red line). The room was very big The staff was very helpfull.
The only problem that we have is The bill that they charged us with parking when we didn't have any car but they fix it immediatly.

name: Donovan House - A Kimpton Hotel
title: “Zentan Restaurant is Excellent”
text: My husband and I went to DC for my birthday in mid-July 2012. The hotel was nice, but the restaurant and staff really made our stay memorable. The bar staff, including Shiloh, Ram and Edwin were amazing! Making awesome cocktails, surprising me with little birthday treats all weekend and providing lots of suggestions to make our trip fun. And the food was spectacular from the singapore slaw to the bowls of noodles, this place is really really worth a trip.

name: Residence Inn Washington/Dupont Circle
title: “Excellent DC choice”
text: We have stayed at the hotel for 4 nights. DC best location, hotel room is specious and very comfortable, stuff very attentive. Breakfast is just ok, vegetables would be nice upgrade.

name: Embassy Suites Hotel Washington, D.C.
title: “Excelente hotel...volveré”
text:
El hotel tiene muy buena ubicación a 10 min. de Dupont Circle. Las habitaciones grandes y limpias. Cuentan con horno microonda y minibar, por si uno se quiere abastecer de algunas cosas y hay un CVS y Wallgreens en la esquina. El personal siempre muy amable y dispuesto a ayudar en lo que se necesitara. 
Business center, siempre accesible y cómodo. 
El desayuno muy rico y las recepciones en la tarde espectaculares.
Un hotel para volver!!

name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Washington, DC / Downtown
title: “Mostly good”
text: Having been to this hotel before in it's previous life and recalling the neighborhood, I was leary to return. The hotel and the neighborhood have changed for the better. Much better. The hotel sits at the edge of D.C.'s Chinatown and is attractively decorated with a decidedly Chinese motif. The rooms are efficient, quiet and comfortable but beware, the rooms are tiny. If you're familiar with the average size of rooms in New York, you'll know what I mean. Fine if you're a single traveler but cramped otherwise. Enjoying the free breakfast can be a challenge if the hotel is near capacity as it was on my stay. Lots of tourists with kids trying to navigate the small breakfast area and jockey for a table was frustrating. Service staff was fantastic. Friendly and professional. Overall a B+ stay and I'd return.

name: The River Inn
title: “A Great Option on a Quiet Street!”
text:
I have stayed at the River Inn several times on business and have been very well taken care of every time. The staff has always been courteous and helpful and the rooms are very clean, comfortable and well appointed. Located on 25th Street just in from K, the hotel is very quiet, well insulated from the city noise and bustling traffic.
The small kitchenettes, while nothing too fancy, allow me to cook a little dinner if I'm on an extended stay. That said, I usually opt to go out. The hotel is an easy walk from dozens of solid dining options in Georgetown and Foggy Bottom and the restaurant in the lobby, DISH, is excellent and also provides room service! 
The River Inn is also just a walk from the monuments - closest are the Lincoln Memorial and the Vietnam Veterans Memorial. On several mornings, I've pulled on my running shoes and headed for jog along the reflecting pool. Great way to start my day.
All told, I definitely recommend the River Inn!

name: Residence Inn Washington/Dupont Circle
title: “Great location”
text: I periodically visit DC on business, and keep trying various locations (Dupont, Crystal City, Key Bridge area, downtown) to see what might be best whenever I can bring my family back for a vacation. I've stayed twice in the Dupont Circle area and love it. Hotel is 2 blocks from Dupont. Dupont Circle itself is a big grassy area with a fountain in the middle and sidewalks & benches all around. Immediately surrounding it are a zillion restaurants (no chains), a CVS Pharmacy, bookstores, etc. In the evening people stroll about and congregate on sidewalks, performers play music, families push baby strollers, young women are able to walk alone (safe), etc. The Metro is perhaps a 3 block walk from the hotel, so you don't need to rent a car if you fly into National (Metro-served) and plan to just see DC city sites. Get a Metro map online to decide if you need a car. Parking is expensive at any DC hotel ($23/day here), so be forewarned. Hotel staff were all very friendly, they took care of a minor maintenance item in my room immediately, bed was great, kitchen area welcome/useful, breakfast welcome and good. Mimi's Restaurant right outside front entrance good - welcome when it rained one night. Room not luxury, views are of city area around it. Don't be put off by that picture of the hotel - yes it looks like that, but is set in an area of numerous unique/older houses - not gross high rises like Crystal City or Key Bridge area. I recommend this place.

name: Capitol Hill Hotel
title: “Reasonable hotel in a very good location”
text: If you are looking for a moderate hotel in the Capitol Hill area, this is a very good choice. I didn't want expensive luxury, and I did want convenient access by taxi to Union Station. Capitol Hill Suites is a good combination of reasonable price for a fairly generous space plus an easy walk to the Capitol grounds and that end of the Mall, also across the street from the Library of Congress (ideal for someone working there for a few days). A little bit shabby but not bad, with a kitchenette. Not a lot of extra service, but a pleasant staff and acceptable breakfast.

name: Donovan House - A Kimpton Hotel
title: “Loved IT!!!!”
text:
We loved our stay at the Donovan. The room was very spacious and well furnished in a modern style. The Frette Linens were a pleasent surprise.
All the major sights were in walking distances if you like to walk. If not, well located near a subway. The area had a lot of restaurants for the evening and the one in the hotel was excellant for both breakfast and dinner. The coffee in the morning was a treat as well as the free happy hour in the lobby. The pool was perfect for a quick dip after a day of sightseeing and at night transforms into a stylish bar perfect for an after dinner drink. The staff was very nice at all times

name: The River Inn
title: “It was Awful!”
text: Well...when we got there...no one was at front desk to help us...phone was ringing off the hook...finally a young lady came back 22 minutes later to help us...we ask for a king..go to suite and it was a double...she stated they oversold the hotel on kings and i was "out of luck"...but I could "try back in the morning". I asked to speak to Front Office Manager.....I got him by phone...he was so unhelpful...I travel alot...but was unimpressed...the website does not describe this hotel the way it is..the staff was not friendly..i asked for directions twice...both times I was directed to a "cabby" as they referred to them..it was aweful! BEWARE!

name: George Washington University Inn
title: “Convenience Trumps Amenities”
text:
I chose the GWU Inn based on the Trip Advisor reviews I read that stressed the convenience. We lived on the Metro during our four day visit, so being a block from the Foggy Bottom/GWU Metro stop was a huge bonus. We were also checking out GWU with our teenaged daughter, so we could get a sense of the neighborhood and the students living around us. The GWU Inn rooms were very nice - super clean and everything was comfortable - especially the beds. However, I agree with the comments on the soundproofing - my daughter was awakened in the middle of the night by a very noisy neighbor and could hear everything said. My only other complaint is that the front desk staff didn't seem to have a clue regarding directions or restaurant recommendations. I also thought that a boutique hotel like this would have complimentary coffee/tea in the lobby. Oh, well, just a thought for management! Also, breakfast was actually quite good and a great value at $6.50 per person (fruit, yogurts, cereals, OJ, coffee, home-baked - I think - banana nut bread, bagels and toast). Plenty to start your day with (apparently there are packages you can buy that includes breakfast, but when I researched the price per night, it didn't make sense to buy the package). Also, one morning, the restaurant was almost out of food at 8:45pm and they tried to tell us to go eat somewhere else. The waiter was quite flustered and ultimately we were able to get enough to eat, but I thought that indicated poor planning by someone.
Overall, I really recommend this hotel, esp. for its proximity to the Metro station, 15 minute walk to Georgetown, 10 minute walk to Kennedy Center. Last tip: There's a 7-11 up the street if you forget your toothbrush :)

name: Washington Court Hotel on Capitol Hill
title: “great business expectations ... unfulfilled”
text:
Had great expectations about this hotel, much of which was bolstered by the reviews of my fellow Trip Advisors below. However, although the hotel may be great for the pleasure or vacation traveler -- the location alone really is very good -- for the business traveler, which I am, it is very disappointing. Those who are planning workshops, conventions, or other business meetings need to take a good, critical look at this hotel before paying to have it held there.
The staff were not particularly friendly nor helpful. In fact, almost without exception they seemed bored and indifferent to my needs as a business traveler. Check in was mechanical and I may as well have been talking to a robot (anyone know the meaning of the word "hospitality" or, dare I say it, "welcome"?) 
The room was adequate enough. I had a corner room, which blocked out some of the noise my fellow convention attendees complained about -- includng hearing people in the room next door and conversations in the corridor. But, the decor and appointments were slightly below average and the bed was decidedly uncomfortable (for me) due to the far-too-soft pillows, on/in which I felt I was suffocating all night.
The meeting rooms were terrible. I brought with me my own mobile wifi because it's imperative (and I think this is true for many business travelers) to stay connected and online. And, I'm not talking just about email, but to be able to find information relevant to the topics being discussed and to do more investigation and reading makes for a richer conference or workshop experience. My wifi did not work, however! -- nor did the hotel wifi in the meeting rooms in which I was in. Nor, as the final straw, did my phone get reception in those meeting rooms!
Then there's the business office. I was surprised NOT to see a huge photo of Gordon Gekko from Wall Street fame smiling down at us with the caption, "Greed is Good." The reason? Can't do a single thing -- not print, not copy, not access the internet -- without sliding the trusty credit card through the slot a $9.50 a pop. I had one page to print -- an invitation slip that would enable me access to a session I needed to attend. 
There was no way I was going to pay $9.50 to print one page. When I asked the front desk about this, I was first told that they were unable to help me. On appeal to reason (I mean, come on ... $9.50 to print ONE page?!) they relented and permitted me to email them the document. As the only place the wifi seemed to work reliably was in the lobby, I was able to do this from the lobby area.
One final thing about the meeting rooms and technology: In all the meeting rooms I went to, I counted a total of four available power outlets. This, in rooms that could hold 80 people. Four? With laptops and ipads and phones to charge/connect? Ridiculous! I even asked if there could be a power-strip provided that might enable a few more people to use the technology they'd brought with them -- and not risk draining the batteries for these long, extended sessions -- and was told that my request could not be accommodated.
Really? Well, all I can say is yes, indeed: The Washington Court Hotel will not be accommodating me in the future. At all. Ever.

name: The River Inn
title: “hotel river inn washington”
text: hotel bon, mais qualité de l'accueil laisse vraiment à désirer. Etions là durant l'ouragan irena; aucune aide du personnel, l'ambassade cherche à nous joindre, on ne passe pas les communications!!! on ne nous en prévient même pas c'est la débrouille, mais aucune sollicitude. Dommage pour l'image du pays quand on est étranger....

name: George Washington University Inn
title: “Great Location, Okay Rooms, Mediocre Service”
text:
I stayed at this hotel because I attended a two-day orientation session at GWU. This hotel was so close and I got quite a good rate through the school. I did have a little trouble finding the place, it is nestled in between residential homes & apartment buildings and the sign is pretty tiny. But it was within a block and a half from the metro and even less to campus.
The room was plenty big, with two double beds, a desk, a separate room for the microwave & fridge, and a tiny bathroom. The bathroom shelf was annoying (as other reviewers have said) because it would not fit any of my toiletries. Water pressure was good, the towels were amazing, and I liked they offered free shoe shine service (although I never used it).
The best part about the room - the bed! It was so comfortable, moreso than even my own at home. One of the best I've slept on while away from home. The worst part (besides the tiny bathroom) - the maid service. They didn't replace any of the toiletries during my four night stay, forgot to clean the coffee pot and replace the coffee a couple of other days, and didn't bother to do more than make the beds and take out the trash and towels. Very disappointing. The view out my window was lovely at night, I could see the Kennedy Center all lit up down the street. Lovely!
All in all, when I go back to GWU I will likely stay at this hotel because of the amazing discount the university offered me. But if I were paying over $200 a night I'd move out of the district to Alexandria or Arlington and get a much nicer hotel for the price.

name: George Washington University Inn
title: “Very Pleasant”
text: We stayed at this wonderful older hotel for 6 nights in October of 2005. We had a spacious corner suite with fully equipped kitchenette (frig, sink, stovetop, microwave, dishes, etc.). Although the furniture was somewhat worn, we were very comfortable. Lots of closet space, 2 TV's, and triple sheets on a nice firm mattress. Excellent, helpful staff that were polite and helpful without "butt kissing". The location is excellent just a short walk from the University and Metro station. The restaurant on the ground floor serves some of the best Italian food we've ever eaten and there is also a TGI Friday's a few blocks away and a little place called Lindy's that serves the best hamburgers ever. The breakfast offerings at the hotel are limited but convenient (expensive for eggs and toast). Overall, a very pleasant stay at very reasonable rates (average about $200 per nite). We will stay here again. FYI- a supermarket, liquor store and pharmacy are located just a few blocks away at the WAtergate complex.

name: Washington Court Hotel on Capitol Hill
title: “Beautiful hotel, awesome location, excellent service”
text: This hotel has all the bells and whistles....it's in a great location. Walk out the front door of the hotel and the Capitol is right there. It's very convenient to the metro; about a 7 minute walk to Union Station. We didn't eat there but did go across the street to the Billy Goat Tavern. They serve breakfast and lunch for sure. Don't know about dinner but they do have a full bar. The hotel is pricey though as far as room service and wi-fi although we did not use either. They were very professional and went out of their way to be accomodating. They allowed us to keep our luggage there until well after we checked out.

name: The Liaison Capitol Hill, An Affinia Hotel
title: “The Liaison Capitol Hill is THE place to stay while in DC.”
text: The Liaison Capitol Hill is THE place to stay while in DC. I doubt that you could find a nicer place to stay... from the friendly door men, the helpful concierge staff, the desk staff and housekeeping. The location is wonderful for walking to Union Station, the Capitol and the mall for the many attractions and museums. The entire staff made us feel welcome and pampered. I look forward to our next stay with Liaison.

name: Capital Hilton
title: “Nice Lobby, Below Average Hotel”
text: Besides a great lobby, the hotel was otherwise disappointing. My room was dirty and the overall service was below average . I pre-ordered breakfast the night before my departure and the hotel failed to deliver it. When I called to complain they said there was nothing they could do and I would have to wait 30-40 minutes if I still wanted it. Next time I'm in D.C., I'll try another option.

name: JW Marriott Washington DC
title: “Good location but not sure it's worth it”
text: We booked this hotel well in advance based on reviews we read on this website. I was excited to be so close to the action & we were definitely not disappointed. As another reviewer said, if you have young children (ours are aged 4 & 5), the distances are still misleading and they were tired after walking to the Monument & the Natural History Museum. Location is everything but I probably would not stay here again. The rooms were overpriced for what we got. We arrived just before 5 pm and our hotel rooms (we had 3) were not ready. The woman at the desk was unfriendly & unhelpful and after a day of traveling and dealing with DC traffic on a Sunday afternoon, I was extremely disappointed. She was the only person we dealt with during our 2-night stay that wasn't helpful but it was a really bad first impression. Considering the price of the room, you have to use the lobby to access free wi-fi which is a real inconvenience & parking adds to the cost at about $40/night. The sounds from the hall are noticeable since there are large spaces under the doors (you can actually see feet walking by) and while the hotel looks newly renovated, it still feels dated. The view from our room was awesome (Monument) and the pool was OK (take advantage of the free fruit - especially if you're there on Sunday when everything closes early). Nothing too exciting and I was expecting much better. The best part? Location. The worst part? Cost, disinterested staff, cold pool & did I mention cost?

name: The River Inn
title: “Excellent”
text:
Parfait , Cette hotel est situé à coté du quartier de Georgetown .
