Ideal pour une famille de 4 personnes . Excellent rapport qualité/prix . Grande chambre avec cuisine equipée ,belle salle de bain . Tres confortable , beaucoup de charme . Personnel tres souriant et tres disponible .

name: JW Marriott Washington DC
title: “Great experience”
text:
We stayed at the JW over the New year. Although there was little going on in DC, we managed to have an enjoyable and very comfortable stay. Our room was a suite... which was exceptionally large, and beautifully decorated. The view from the room and the shared balcony was awe-insipring!
We found the hotel to be very clean, the staff helpful, and the location excellent. We would definitely stay here again.

name: Capitol Hill Hotel
title: “Walk To The Marine Barracks"”
text: The location allows you to walk to the "Marine Barracks, 8th & I Sts." for the summer Friday nite "Evening Parade" and dinner at the fine restaurants on the way. Room was quiet, clean and bed was just right. Plenty of space in room, a refrigerater with a freezer that works. "Continental" breakfast was more than enough choices as well as not crowded, but we had to walk to a different bldg. Not a problem in nice weather. Downside was $35.84/nite valet parking with no alternate choices. Though prompt service was noted. Decor is somewhat dark and shows wear, but well kept and excellent front desk service. Price was an excellent value and directly behind "Library of Congress" bldg, in a residential neighborhood. Upon leaving, noted a diner right up the street for add'l meals. Internet at 2 desks in lobby, always occupied by guests.

name: Hampton Inn Washington, DC-Convention Center
title: “DC gem!!!”
text: Four of us girlfriends headed off to Washington to see GLEE at the verizon center. We pulled right into the valet parking and took our bags and a nice gentlemen wisked the car away to the deck below. Upon checking in the front desk clerk was so accomodating and everything was so easy. She let us split our bill four ways (unheard of) and offered maps, restaurants suggestions, etc. We returned at 11:00pm and were immediately asked if we enjoyed our concert. The next morning we had a lovely breakfast with a hostess that was like a ray of sunshine. The rooms were comfortable and so were the beds. Don't miss this one.

name: St. Gregory Hotel & Suites
title: “OK but not worth a top rating”
text:
Staff and service: very friendly and helpful.
Room: suite with kitchen (handy for a family but not for business travel); clean but long/narrow and and very dimly lit.
Exercise room: very small but adequate.
Neighborhood: a business region; seemingly safe but the streets are virtually empty at night.
Bottom line: OK if you need to be in this region of D.C., but there are much better hotels and locations in the capital.

name: Washington Marriott at Metro Center
title: “Very Nice Hotel with Great SErvice”
text:
Nice hotel with helpful and friendly staff. Restaurant is very very good which frankly surprised me. Breakfast was included and was a very nice buffet with homemade waffles and omelets, etc. Several blocks from museums but further from the monuments. With young children, walking could be a problem, although the hotel is right at a metro stop.
Pool and hot tub are very small but adequate for kids. Gym is very nice.
No complaints here and pleasantly surprised at how good the restaurant

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington DC/US Capitol
title: “One of the best I've ever stayed at”
text: I travel about 2.5 weeks per month and am a faithful Hilton Honors member, and this one deserves mention. Picked this one because of its AAA price and general proximity tocapital bldgs. Rooms were outstanding, and hospitality of all staff was extraordinary, vrom the maid who helped me get in the room, to the maintenance guy who volunteered to increase the water pressure in my room, to the restaurant mgr who let me use a table for a business mtg through breakfast and into lunch. The only negative is how the bathroom doors are positioned and if not shut, swing open to the walkway. (Count on hitting it late at night if you don't turn a light on.) All an all, a GREAT Hilton property.

name: Washington Marriott at Metro Center
title: “Great Location, clean and fresh room”
text:
Good Marriott - clean, updated rooms & lobby. Starbuck in lobby and other restaurants including COSI (sandwich/salad) very close by. Check in easy and left keys for the late arriving members of our group. No issues with room. Manuel was very helpful offering directions, and holding bags on our final day!
Second time stayed here and for about $200 a great value with access to Washington sites and offices. Took train to city, but I know they have parking or parking in the area.

name: The Liaison Capitol Hill, An Affinia Hotel
title: “Lovely!”
text: We stayed here for one night to see Washington while we were in New York but I would have stayed a lot longer if I'd known how nice it is. The place was modern and spotless, the staff were so friendly and it was very close to the railway station and places to eat. Perfect! The staff were very helpful with our queries on tours etc.

name: Capital Hilton
title: “Bom hotel”
text: gostei do hotel. Tem bom atendimento, organizado e limpo. Os funcionários muito gentis e educados. O café da manhã é caro, melhor opção próxima é o Starbuck. Pontos turísticos muito próximos para fazer a pé. Cuidado com taxis, eles dão a maior volta para chegar no mesmo lugar. Metrô a 2 quarteirões, fácil de entender. ônibus também de fácil acesso. Recomendo para quem quer conhecer Washington.

name: Madera, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Horrible service. Internet problems. Slow service. Go elsewhere!”
text: I chose this hotel for a business trip and was very disappointed. Service is slow and beyond horrible. The front desk staff doesn't seem well trained. Internet didn't work in my room (508) and they left me waiting for almost an hour without a call back or solution. Restaurant is closed for two weeks due to renovations and there are few options close by. I'll never come back here.

name: The Liaison Capitol Hill, An Affinia Hotel
title: “Nice room, but heavily scented”
text:
I like the Liaison Capitol Hill Hotel, but I am only giving it three stars, because it gave me a headache. While I am not allergic, exactly, to scents and perfumes, they do on occasion give me a terrific headache. My room at the Liaison had some sort of air freshener whose scent was cloying and inescapable, and inevitably gave me a headache. It might be a feature that others like, but I couldn't get away from it, and it made me feel sick. Disappointingly, the room has beautiful huge windows, but they are sealed shut, so I could not air out the room that way. I probably should have called the front desk to ask them if the scent came from some sort of plug-in (as was the case my hotel room in Italy), which would have been easily fixed, but for some stupid reason, I never did. 
Had the hotel been unscented, I would have liked it a lot. It is the first place I have stayed where there was a pillow menu, and as ridiculous as this seems, nevertheless I could not resist trying one. There was a buckwheat pillow, various down or hypoallergenic options, and a magnetic pillow that is supposed to help with stress and knotty muscles. This is the one I requested. Turns out I was so exhausted by the time I got back for bed that I didn't even use the thing. The substantial pile of the pillows already on the bed was just fine, and the bed itself was pretty heavenly. It had a firm mattress, good smelling clean sheets, and a nice down comforter that would have been especially perfect if I had been able to open the window to catch the breezes of an early fall night. (Yes, I'm mad about the windows! It's such a waste, especially when you can see that they used to open, and the latches have been removed.) 
Others have said that the hotel's bathrooms are tiny, and they are not ample, it's true. However, as I don't spent a lot of time in the bathroom, I didn't care. What I do care about is that this is the first place I have stayed where they don't use those insanely wasteful individual bottles of shampoo, conditioner and shower gel. Instead, there are full size bottles with pump dispensers on the shower wall, and I could not be more thrilled about that. I didn’t recognize the brand, but having used it, I ended up clean and smelled good, so that worked well enough for me.
There is also decent Lavazza coffee to make in your little individual coffee maker in the morning. Sadly, there is no liquid creamer, only packets of that nasty cancer-inducing non diary powder. There's no mini bar, but a ton of Fiji water, in case you are thirsty. Be warned it will cost you handsomely if you break one of those open, but at least they warn you what the price will be. 
There are always a few hotel features that I don't check out, but feel I should mention. In this case, that would be the rooftop pool, which sadly had just closed for the season. It is possible that, from the roof, you might get a pretty spectacular view of the Capitol building, but if not, it's only a couple of block walk to get that lovely view. The Liaison would be a great place to stay for anyone who had business on the Hill, but there is not a terrible lot going on in the area at night. The hotel does have a restaurant which appeared pretty popular, called Art & Soul. There is also a horrible looking soulless Hyatt across the street, which probably has a restaurant or two in there as well. 
The last couple of things I will mention abut the Liaison is that every staff member I interacted with was a delight, and the valet parking, should you have the misfortune of needing it, is punishingly expensive a $48 per night. Ouch! Street parking in this area might not be too difficult, but it's probably a bad idea. Better just to leave the car at home if you can, and rely on DCs Metro system (the Liaison is very close to the red line Union Station stop), so you can use that $48 to buy yourself a nice dinner instead!

name: JW Marriott Washington DC
title: “BEST HOTEL YET!!!!!!!”
text: What can I say this hotel it is in a great location in a great city. The hotel was awsome from the moment i arrived - had a great room overlooking the Washington Monument and the Lincoln Memorial. It was great rooms well furnished, bathroom was huge, beds were plush and great, restaurant was fantastic especially breakfast. Staff were fantastic especially the concierge desk nothing was too much for them.

name: Capitol Hill Hotel
title: “EXCELLENT HOTEL, QUIET, CLEAN, FRENDLY, CLOSE TO EVERYTHING.”
text:
I couldent have happyer with the CAPITOL HILL SUITES i am only sorry our stay was only for five days, its a short walk from the capitol building in a nice quiet place close to some bars, shops, and resterants. i whould stay there again in a heart beat. 10 out of 10.
i couldent thank the people ENOUGH that maid our stay so memorable.

name: Capitol Hill Hotel
title: “Great value”
text: Quiet little hotel at the junction of parliament area and surburbia. Only one block from Metro stop, it was easy to find. We were in a room in the building beside the main one, where the free breakfast was held every morning. Room big in size, with little separate dining room, kitchette, walk in wardrobe and bathroom. Free wifi in all rooms - what a pleasant surprise! Free breakfast was continental, bagels were yummy! Considering we paid AU$100 per night, it was great value! One reception staff was rude however when on departure we asked whether they sold stamps - she made a grunt as if we were troubling her, and when we then told her we needed to send a postcard internationally, she unpleasantly denied having any international stamps. Good impression of the hotel with a slightly bad ending.

name: Washington Marriott at Metro Center
title: “Great Location”
text: Well the location is great because you can either catch the metro right outside or you can walk!!! we walked to K &14th two nights with no problem, Thw White House and the Washington Monument and ChinaTown!!! The beds were so comfy and the fitness center is nice too!! They give you fresh fruit in there and water! I loved the sauna and the jacuzzi too!! They also have a happy hour DAILY from 4-7 and $3 WINGS!!!! The faculty was soooo nice! The bell men, the bartender and the front desk ppl...Even random ppl who were just walking! The maids did a good job too but like any other hotel they only clean comforters like once every so often bc I had the same lil stain on my bed but they were good about every thing else! Its right downtown by the grand Hyatt...The only thing that was crazy was parking but thats downtown DC for ya!!! I got a deal for $65 a night and I feel that was the best deal in all of downtown!! So my stay I cant complain...only downers were they had no robes but other than that i loved it!!

name: Madera, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Excellent Staff, Fabulous Location”
text: I've stayed at the Hotel Madera many times and never been disappointed. The staff--especially Michelle O.--is fabulous. Attentive, friendly and accommodating. The location is terrific--very close to Dupont Circle and Metro stop, but quiet neighborhood. Restaurant is excellent and late afternoon wine (complimentary) is a nice perk. Rooms are very clean and beautifully furnished. I highly recommend the Hotel Madera. Kudos to the staff for their excellent work!

name: The Liaison Capitol Hill, An Affinia Hotel
title: “Good Experiece Overall”
text:
Everyone has their own opinion in a place so there will always be good reviews and bad ones. Overall my review on this is very good.
Pros-
It's right next to the Capitol building and the train station. It's very clean and the staff is all pretty nice for the most part. The pool area happens to be decent. If you're into very modern New York City style hotels then you'll love this place. It's not too far of a walk from 7th where all the restaurants and pretty much where the nightlife is if you're tempted to go to a bar.
Cons- 
It is a walk of you want to go to the center of everything like memorials or the white house, but taxi cabs are very easy to come by! 
My biggest complaint is the parking! It's a rip off they charge you $48 per night. If you don't mind walking two blocks up from the train station part your car there!!! It's only $22 for every 24 hours. I stayed 2 nights and paid $44 saved myself $52 on this trip! 
Other then the parking, stay here you won't be disappointed!

name: Hampton Inn Washington, DC-Convention Center
title: “Great hotel - poor breakfast!”
text:
I stayed here for a business trip in June 2010. It made a nice change for me to stay in a smaller-scale chain hotel rather than one of the usual chain "behemoths" like Hilton or Renaissance!
Staff:
I only spoke to the reception staff and bellboy (didn't have my room cleaned) during my stay, and everyone was helpful and friendly.
Room:
My room was clean, spacious and cool (very welcome because it was very hot and humid outside). There was free internet access throughout the hotel - very cool!
Free breakfast:
Hampton Inn make a big deal of their free breakfast deal, but to be honest if you are looking to save money and get a free brekkie, you are better off finding a cheaper hotel and going to a cafe. The quality of the breakfast buffet is dreadful. Dubious-looking omelettes, suspicious gravy and salty processed meats were standard fare most days. There were also cereals, fruit and so on, but I was after a little more.
Location:
Within easy walking distance of Chinatown metro, lots of restaurants/bars etc. Good for seeing DC if you are there for that, and very close to the convention center.
Other:
There are only 2 lifts in the hotel for approx 250 rooms, and both are very slow, so you will spend quite a bit of time waiting for the lift to arrive!
There is a very small gym in the hotel (a few cardio machines and some dumbbells only) and a pool+jacuzzi, but I didn't use any of these facilities.

name: Phoenix Park Hotel
title: “Great location, lots of charm”
text: This hotel is very conveniently located for sightseeing, right beside Union Station. Everything works fine....elevators, shower, toilet, lighting etc., Flat screen TV in room, free wifi, fastest room-service I've ever come across (15 minutes) and a great, cheerful Irish Pub downstairs if you fancy turning some strangers into friends. The AC in the room was a bit tricky to find the right temp but otherwise the room was a decent size and they had that very nice touch, a warm and comfy bathrobe. Found the coffee pot dirty and the grounds bag from the previous occupant still in the hopper. Garbage cans being collected in the lane outside woke me at 4AM...not good....would ask at reception for a room away from the rear or side of the hotel. Reception staff were polite and friendly, also the bartenders, also the servers. Limo driver who got me to the airport raved about the owner's generosity to his employees. Good to hear, would probably stay again....in a different room at the front.

name: Phoenix Park Hotel
title: “The Right Place”
text: We have travelled around the world on a tight budget and found the Phoenix Park to be one of the best vaules. We spent a week there over New Year's. The staff were friendly and helpful. The room was clean and comfortable. The area felt safe and accessible. We took the Megabus to Washington and it dropped us off at Union Station, almost across the street. Because the Mall and Capital are within easy walking distance and the Union Station Metro is right there, we felt in the centre of everything -there was no need for a car or the cost of parking. The restaurants in the area were on the high side but there were some delis in the neighbourhood, a little grocery store not far off and, of course, the food court at Union Station. The Phoenix Park may not have the five star ameneties of a resort but then, we came to see Washington, not to swim.

name: Capitol Hill Hotel
title: “CHS was a wonderful place to stay in a great location”
text: While my husband did research at the Library of Congress (only steps away), I easily visited my senator, observed both the Senate and House in action, and took in some sites I'd missed on other trips (like the Newseum). We parked at Union Station to save a little money, and that worked fine; it's only a few blocks away, We loved being in a quiet neighborhood, got great rates via the hotel Internet specials, and loved having a Continental breakfast available each morning. .

name: The Liaison Capitol Hill, An Affinia Hotel
title: “Service and Location were Outstanding”
text: Old hotel with a great makeover. Designer did a great job. Location for first time visitors is impossible to match in price range. (proximity to Amtrak, Capitol, museums-all walking) Special Thanks to Jay C at the rooftop for the company , service , and recommendations. Lincoln's Waffle House- great!

name: Avenue Suites Georgetown
title: “Great location, room, price, service”
text: We had a wonderful four-day stay at the Avenue Suites. Our suite was very roomy, clean and comfortable for three adults. The location near the subway stop and George Washington University, in a beatiful, vibrant Georgetown neighborhood was terrific. We were within an easy walk of many restaurants. And the service from all the staff was impeccable. The price was very reasonable for the size of the room and the amenities. (Don't tell them!)

name: The Dupont Circle Hotel
title: “Oh well...”
text:
We stayed there twice this summer and our experience is mixed at best. The rooms are nicely appointed but rather small and the side towards Kraemer books gets a lot of sun. Unfortunately, the staff does not always keep the aircon running at the necessary temp/fan speed and so when we occupied our room the temp inside was upwards of 80 degree. Even after 1 hour that had not changed much. It took many calls and staff was not responsive at all until I got really upset and threatened to leave and find another place to stay. Finally a technician (very nice guy) turned up and had to perform a fix. Breakfast is normally not included, only a la carte and pricy for the selection and quality offered.
On our second stay a couple of weeks later we had a problem with our reservation. Again, the fron desk staff was overwhelmed by this issue and referred us to the Guest Relation Manager. The way we were approached and the way our issue was handled was poor at best and unprofessional at worst. I was made feel as if I was pretending to have a reservation (and was told they were fully booked), then - after I showed them my confirmed booking on my cell phone- I was told that my travel agent had not send the reservation, when I called my agent, they told me that the reservation had gone through and was confirmed and the guest relation manager kept disappearing w/o communicating to us - just interrupting my phone call with the travel agent that she refused to call herself. Instead of helping to solve the problem and staying with us, she attended to other front desk business etc. It was rather uncomfortable to be in that lobby and having to fix this. When fixed an apology was not forthcoming right away! Later that day we got a nice note and were offered a sign of good will for the inconvenience. Check-out in both stays took for ever, so allow extra time! But this booking incident together with the experience the first time have me believe that the hotel is badly managed and staff is not really customer focused but company and self-interst focused.
If you are young the bar is hoping at night and you might like that, but for older folks like me it is much too loud (having horrible accoustics with noise dampening materials) and does not allow for a pleasant environment.
If you are not used to city living, beware of the early morning noise from the garbage trucks that takes over from 6am onwards...
The saving grace is that the rates are ok and that the hotel is truly centally located (being close to the red line metro) and the availability of concierge parking (pricy!).

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington DC/US Capitol
title: “Fabulous!!!!”
text:
I stayed here about 2 weeks ago. The service was impeccable!!! I was lost, called
the hotel and the gentleman stayed on the phone with me until I made it to the hotel!
The rooms were fabulous! The neighborhood was great!! This is my hotel choice while in DC!!

name: Helix, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Descent choice, central location.”
text:
The decor of the hotel is very cool as it was in other Kimpton Hotels I stayed. But what matters is your room. Our room was fairly good size with a couch and large screen tv. Bed was comfortable. Overall, it was a pretty good choice for the price we paid.
I recommend not eating breakfast at the hotel since there are better choices nearby.

name: Avenue Suites Georgetown
title: “Excellent place to stay while visiting DC”
text: I was at this hotel for the memorial weekend with my family and we loved it. I was traveling with my autistic son and got to the hotel way before check in time on Saturday morning and they totally accommodated me to get into a room before check in time so my son could unwind a bit before we started our day. The staff was great and always helpful and friendly. The rooms were very clean and plenty of room in them.Even though you have a full kitchen they offer a very nice continental breakfast.The hotel is right in the middle of everything. Just missing a pool but otherwise very satisfied. Will definitely stay her again.

name: Hampton Inn Washington, DC-Convention Center
title: “Great Experience !!!”
text: Great location to everything.. Great breakfast in the am and a very friendly staff. The rate to stay was awesome especially for such a nice hotel. I definitely recommend this hotel and I will stay again!

name: Monaco Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Good Hotel, Great Location!”
text:
This was our first stay in a Kimpton hotel and the experience was a pleasant surprise. I felt like we paid a very good nightly rate ($140/night), but what killed us was valet parking at $40/night. Despite that, everything else lived up to the reviews. 
We stayed on the 3rd floor in a queen deluxe room overlooking the Spy Museum. The room seemed cozy at first glance, but then I looked up. These are probably the highest ceilings I've seen in a hotel room. The huge windows and high ceilings made the room feel airy. The room is clean. Housekeeping and the hotel staff did not disappoint. I especially was surpised at how many times the front desk called to check up on us. After a long day of sightseeing, the beds were as comfy as can be. I absolutely loved the long, majestic hallways on the floor. 
On top of all the great amenities of Monaco, the best was the location! Penn Quarter is lively and filled with great restaurants. It's also a couple blocks from the National Mall where we spent the majority of our visit. The hotel is mere steps away from the Gallery Place/Chinatown rail station so we were able to hop on the train and go.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington DC/US Capitol
title: “Nice place with loads of potential”
text: Our family of four stayed here for three nights in mid-June. The property had been open for less than two months, we were told, and was very pretty inside. Pluses were the staff - very friendly and helpful, the close metro (Florida/NY Ave. Red Line stop is less than a block away), the restaurant was tasty - we had all breakfasts there and one dinner. Minuses were the staff - when we first arrived, the valet handed my husband a baggage cart and he had to load it himself and take into the elevators and to our room. Housekeeping was sketchy at times - we were not given enough towels, our trash was not emptied one day (banana peel in it - yucky smell), and then the next day it was emptied without a replacement trash bag put in. Dirty glasses were left in the bathroom, and all of my toiletries out on the bathroom counter were scooped up and dumped into one of our overnight bags that was sitting there. The pool area is pleasant, but the water was too cold for my kids to swim in. Rooms have microwaves and small fridges - great for storing things purchased at the grocery store right next door. There is also a CVS right across the street. We ate at Roti (a couple doors down - yummy Mediterranean) and had large, yummy glasses of wine at the coffee house in the same block. There aren't many other dining choices within walking distance, so we hopped on the Metro and went one stop to Union Station where we found awesome Asian food. I think the staff issues are simply a training curve - a lot of new people working there, and the valet who got our car when we were leaving packed everything we brought out for us! Our greatest disappointment was with access to the laundry room. When we arrived, there was sign on the door stating that it was closed for servicing - turns out the company who owns the machines had not come to remove the money from them and they were full. We were told it would be taken care of the next day. And the next day it was the same story. Next day, the same story. The front desk offered to let us us the Hilton machines but required two people to be in the room to make sure no one got hurt. We have two small children - we could not leave them alone, so this was not an option. I would definitely stay here again because it is so easy to get into the city for sightseeing.

name: Hampton Inn Washington, DC-Convention Center
title: “Great Beds !”
text:
I have stayed in many VERY Nice Hotels in DC, but this one for the price is GREAT. Good location, Clean rooms, Good price on parking, Friendly Staff, Great Breakfast, Free Web and GREAT BEDS
With tons of Pillows !!!

name: Madera, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A pleasant surprise”
text: I was pleasantly surprised. My first visit to a Kimpton Hotel. It was clear that management has thought through what they are offering and there are a few welcome unconventional offerings that made it seem as if they cared. Went here because my usual DC hotels (Lombardy and Carlyle Suites) were charging over $300/night while this was much closer to $200. The staff were friendly and competent, the room was spacious and modern, great location just off Dupont Circle. I liked the accompanying Firefly restaurant where the food was definitely good, although prices a little high to use consistently.

name: Hampton Inn Washington, DC-Convention Center
title: “Savvy traveler's hotel”
text: I used this hotel in this early spring because of good reviews of TripAdvisor. This hotel was spacious, new, clean, comfortable and not so expensive. And one of the good things is the location was just half block from (long distance) bus station (we used bus service from NYC) and close to Chinatown which we later found a good small inexpensive Chinese restaurant in the area. The lobby had coffee and tea/hot chocolate service 24 hrs, and we enjoyed the hot drinks when we came back from outside. Even I knew the area is not dangerous, I was wondering how is the neighborhood's safeness around there. Because I brought my three young daughters (10, 9, 7 yrs old). After I arrived I found that It was not good neighborhood before, but it is fine now. It was safe even I took the daughters for dinner after 8PM. One thing I had bad experience with this hotel was my daughters used TV game and the hotel charged a lot. (It looks their record is not reliable.) I learned a lesson.

name: Madera, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Tremendous experience. We will stay at the Madera again.”
text: The Hotel staff...and I mean all of them...were truly accomodating, cheerful and helpful as were all of the Firefly restaurant staff. A thoroughly enjoyable experience all the way around.

name: Washington Court Hotel on Capitol Hill
title: “We had a great stay”
text:
Frist let me say that we got a great package with this hotel from Priceline and the cost is a big factor whenever I look at value. If I had paid full price I'm sure I could think of things to find fault with.
That said, we spent 4 nights here and were very pleased with our stay and would love to get a package like this again in the future. We were in D.C. to sightsee and didn't spend much time in the hotel other then to sleep and get ready for the new day. My wife had breakfast there each morning and felt the service was slow and the price high but this is Washington D.C and that seems to be the rule everywhere we went. 
By the end of our stay they were having trouble with two of there there elevators which slowed us down a little but really not much of a problem. The business center charges $7 to use the computer so we printed our bording passes at the airport instead.
We stayed in room #1218 which has a view of the Capital dome over the roof tops. The room was always spotless and was a very nice room althought I am sure if you looked hard enough you could find something wrong with it. There is noise from the fire station on the street below but we didn't find it a problem. The cable TV wasn't all that great but we there to see the sights and spent litte time watching TV. The bathroom was also very nice with a good tub/shower, lots of towels and the like.
There is a small store for snacks and drinks on the street next to the fire station. The door men were very good and cabs seem to always be there waiting. A ride to National airport cost us $17.
There are two subway stations, each about three blocks in either direction from the hotel and not a bad walk for us. We thought the subway system was great but you do need to learn how the system works to make the most of it.
We did see some homeless people in the area by the hotel but only a few and never had any problem with them.
The front desk staff did seem a little on edge but we didn't have any problems with them. Everyone we came in contact with on the hotel staff treated us well.
We were happy with our stay and if we find a package like this in the future we will be staying at this hotel again.

name: Capitol Hill Hotel
title: “avoid at all costs!!”
text: I visited this hotel on the web numerous times, and boy was I fooled. I traveled with my husband & 3 kids for a weekend in March. After confirming my reservation and the type of room I requested, which was one with 2 queen beds and a pullout before we arrived, we were very suprised when we arrived to find our room had 1 king bed. We were informed by management that a reservation just makes sure you have a room, not the room that was requested. After my husband argued with the manager, we were finally given the room we requested. There was no apology from the manager or concessions made for their error. The place was musty and moldy smelling. Supplies like drinking cups were nonexsistent. Only good thing was location.

name: One Washington Circle Hotel
title: “hotel one washington circle”
text:
hotel très bien situé, à deux pas de la station de metro "foggy bottom" qui vous emmene dans tout Washington pour moins de 2 dollars le trajet.
Les chambres sont spacieuses et très calmes.
Un "open top tour bus" s'arrête au pieds de l'hotel, cela peut être pratique...
J'y retournerai sans hésiter

name: Phoenix Park Hotel
title: “Wonderful Hotel, great staff, treat you like family”
text: Stayed at hotel on anniversary trip to DC. Very near Union Station so no need for cab. Front Desk person, Liz Mitchell heard it was anniversary and upgraded us to suite for a small fee. What a great room with kitchenette, dining room and fireplace living room. Staff gave great help on transport around DC, Dining and discounts. this will be our DC headquarters from now on.

name: Washington Court Hotel on Capitol Hill
title: “Good hotel, great value and location”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Washington Court Hotel with our 5 month old son. It was our first family vacation, and we couldn't have been happier with the hotel. It's certainly not a high end destination - everything feels slightly aged - and the service is good but not exceptional. But the price, $139 a night for a Deluxe King, was the best we could find, and the location was ideal for two new parents to walk around town. The staff was always helpful and friendly, and the room was large and comfortable. We felt safe in the neighborhood (yes, the homeless gather around Union Station, but we never felt threatened), and happily wandered to Union Station a number of evenings for dinner.
We'd highly recommend the hotel to friends and family, and will stay there again for our next trip to DC.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Amazing Hotel - Go There”
text: Forget the Capitol, the White House, the Monuments & Memorials, it's worth visiting Washington just to stay at the Omni. It's definitely the best hotel I've ever stayed in - and considering it's dirt cheap (from th UK at least), that's pretty amazing. Rooms are opulent, and the staff make you feel like Royalty - but it's by no means stuffy or exculsive in the bad sense of the word. You may think there's no more to say - but wait - the buffet breakfasts are absolutely out of this world.

name: Carlyle Suites Hotel
title: “Decent hotel, Perfect location.”
text:
The Carlye Suites has been my home away from home on dozens of occasions. 
I must say that the location cannot be beat! It is in the heart of the best neighborhood in Washington, and just a short walk from everything good about DC! 
Overall, the hotel is clean, but perhaps not as modern as major hotel brand. It's "ART DECO" from the lobby and common areas to the rooms. 
All rooms have refrigerators, and most have full kitchenette facilities! This is a GREAT thing to have for simple preparations-- however some guest ruin it by attempting to cook a steak dinner or a fry happy breakfast that permeates and lingers in the room for the next guest. 
Book away from rooms ending in 22,24,26,28.... they are cracker box small... and in the hallway that connects the two buildings. 
I don't think you will be disappointed in this hotel... they try! And will do their best to make you feel at home!
The internet-- while generally reliable-- is a pain because it signs you out every time you close your computer or your phone falls to sleep! But it's free!

name: The Dupont Circle Hotel
title: “Great Location”
text:
The Dupont at the Circle worked out great for me. It was close to the business I had to do. The room was comfortable, free internet, nice bar down stairs.
The bathroom was clean and quite stylish, European feel. It had a great walking in stone shower but no bath tub.
My only regret is that I was there alone. I would have been a lot more fun if my wife had been able to join me.

name: The St. Regis Washington, D.C.
title: “First class.... exactly what I expected.”
text: Stayed for two nights on business. This was my second stay at this hotel. I didn't get upgraded this time but that is not guaranteed. Doorman, valet, and reception were all very professional, efficient and friendly. The room was well appointed and extremely comfortable...even if it was somewhat on the smaller side. This is becoming one of my favorite DC hotels.

name: Helix, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Funky nice hotel with pleasant staff”
text: You could play basketball in the main room, but the bathroom is claustrophobic. Other than that, excellent experience.

name: The Madison
title: “DH&R conference”
text: I stay in Madison Hotel for annual Engineers Conference. The hotel is absolutely beautiful.The location is very good for center city downtown. The staff is very helpful. This hotel is close to the DCA airport, only a short cab ride and it is also close to many attractions of an historic significance and to the White House. The are well kept.

name: Willard InterContinental Washington
title: “Well appointed and comfortable”
text:
The staff, from registration to bellhop to valet went above and beyond. They were courteous and assisted in any way they could. When my husband talked to the manager about being billed $10 a night for EACH device we own (Two personal laptops, One iPad, One work laptop), he graciously reduced the cost. THAT's great customer service. Housekeeping took special care when I was working in the room and even asked if they should come back later to vacuum. 
The bed was super comfortable. The two chairs (easy chair and desk chair) were not only comfortable but allowed me to get a LOT of work done. 
It's located right near the White house and the Hop on Hop off bus route! I was able to get tons of work done AND take a tour of the city as well.

name: Helix, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Started well but declined”
text: The room was impressive. Signed up to the Kimpton In Touch - benefits include free internet, free continental breakfast, free nightly cocktail - thought it would be great stay. It declined slowly over the week. Cocktail requested was a Bloody Mary - pretty basic cocktail. Was told they don't make those. Rang room service one night - no answer. Needed to print - had to use the business center - $7.95/15min and then $0.80 for a b/w page. Also, I was rung one morning to question the 'do not disturb' sign I had on the door - doesn't ringing someone equate to disturbing them ? Other than these faults it was a good stay.

name: The Dupont Circle Hotel
title: “5 Wonderful Days”
text:
I stayed in this hotel for 5 days with my Husband. It was my first time in America. I found the hotel to be excellent, from when we arrived at the door, to the ever so pleasant Door man who throughout our stay was always smiling. Reception was very professional. The room was spotless and very warm. Bar Service was excellent, tables cleared straight away. Restaurant food was excellent and the service second to none. 
All in all this is one of the best hotels I have ever stayed in and would highly recommend it.
Only downside would be that I would have loved a window in the room that open a little for some fresh air.

name: Topaz, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Clean, quiet hotel with friendly staff”
text: In typical Kimpton style, this hotel shines as a customer-focused choice for the business or leisure travel. It is within 10 minutes walking distance of the Farragut and Dupont circle metro stops, and although its not as close as some would like, in nice weather, it is a comfortable walk in a nice part of town. The hotel staff were very helpful as well. It is a bit loud in the back rooms on Monday early mornings when the trash is being picked up but over the week, the noise on Monday was an exeption to the rest of the week. Will definately stay here again.

name: Hampton Inn Washington, DC-Convention Center
title: “Hotel Hampton Inn- Washington”
text: Hotel molto bello, nuovissimo; stanza spaziosa, con frigo e microonde (inaspettatamente), confortevole. Posizione un pò scomoda per visitare il centro di Washington, ma se la giornata è bella e si ha voglia di fare due passi, in 15 minuti si arriva al Mall.

name: Omni Shoreham Hotel
title: “Zeer compleet, luxe hotel”
text: Zeer compleet, luxe hotel. De kamers zijn net gerenoveerd, met LCD flatscreen TV en WIFI internet. Hotel inrichting zo net voor de kerst is adembenemend. Het ontbijt is zeer uitgebreid, luxe en goede service

name: Madera, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great hotel!”
text: We try to stay at Kimpton hotels whenever possible. Got a fabulous rate of $70/night via Priceline. The staff was attentive, helpful, and friendly. The room (#409) was very spacious, though it did not have a balcony. The toilet and shower are in one room, the sink in another area. The bathing area was a little tight, but certainly manageable.

name: The Dupont Circle Hotel
title: “Trendy, great for solo travelers!”
text:
I had to stay an extra day in DC for work and ended up having to change to this hotel. (The one I was staying at was booked.) I had to walk through Dupont Circle and was surprised by all the homeless people playing checkers. I loved the location with so many places to eat around it and even a bookstore nearby! The first floor is a very busy place and I got lost a couple of times trying to find a door or an elevator. However, the man at the front desk was very helpful and I didn't feel rushed while checking in.
My room was incredible! Probably the best room I've ever stayed at. (I'm a HHonors member.) The bathroom was the best part - heated floors, open layout (I could watch TV from the shower) and loved the shutters on the windows. However, if there's someone else in the room, the open layout may bother them if they want to sleep in while the other person is in the shower. Also, the shutters do not shut out all the light, so if you want it pitch dark in your room you won't get it here. 
Flat screen TV on the wall, bed was super comfortable and the neighbors were quiet. I got a great night of sleep. I wish I had stayed there for my entire trip!

name: Madera, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “It all comes together at Madera”
text:
I just returned from a six-day trip to Washington, D.C. where I stayed at the Hotel Madera in Dupont Circle. Here's my take on this boutique chain hotel.
Cleanliness-Very clean. I saw no insects, cobwebs or dust on the furniture. The only thing I did notice, and only when I looked up close, was some writing on the wall in my hotel room. I could tell there had been efforts to clean it. They just couldn't get it all out.
Service-VERY friendly folks at the front desk. They always said hello and goodbye to guests. One thing though: the day I checked in, I was offered a hand with my luggage, which I declined because I didn't need it. The morning I checked out, however, I had more bags and I wasn't offered a hand to get out of the door. I wasn't peeved, but it would have been nice. You say, "Well, you should have asked." I say, in the hospitality industry, a guest shouldn't have to ask for something as basic as holding the door open.
Location-Dupont Circle is a busy residential/business area. There are plenty of sit-down restaurants there. But there weren't any fast food or takeout joints, which was inconvenient for me because I like to grab-and-go and eat in my hotel room. But there is a post office, a Fed Ex center, a Bank of America and a CVS all within walking distance. Plus, the Dupont Circle station is just two blocks away from the hotel. 
Value-I signed up for Kimpton Hotel's free membership program before booking. This allowed me to take advantage of their price-matching deal. I saw a deluxe king room for $181.50/night on Hotels.com. I called Kimpton and told them. So, instead of paying $216/night by booking with Kimpton, they knocked their price down to $181/night and I booked directly with the hotel, which is what I prefer. 
Rooms-I liked my room, which was on the top floor. It definitely had a wow factor to it. The bathroom was tiny, with just a toilet and bathtub in it. But the vanity and sink were in a separate area in front of the BIG closet. I also had a balcony, which I never used. Being a Kimpton member gave me free WiFi for my entire stay. It was pretty fast, and I never got booted off. It's an unsecure network though, so make sure all your firewalls and such are working. 
What else can I say? The hotel was very quiet and I only saw a handful of guests while I was there. Apparently, they also take pets. I never went to the Firefly restaurant, which always seemed busy during happy hour, or ordered room service because it was expensive and I was traveling on a budget. 
Also, the pillows on my bed had feathers. I don't think I've ever used feather pillows before. I mention this because I noticed during my stay that a couple of little scratches and a small rash appeared on my face while staying at the hotel. I don't quite know where they came from. All I know is I didn't have them before my stay at the Madera. My only guess is that I might have had a reaction to the pillows. If you've got sensitive skin, you may want to request foam pillows instead.
All in all, it was a great place to stay, and I highly recommend it.

name: Carlyle Suites Hotel
title: “Awesome service !”
text: Just spent a week in D.C. and stayed at the Carlyle. I can't say enough for the wonderful service there, especially Simon and Abou at the front desk. On checking in we were switched to a different room (I am a light sleeper) without a moment's hesitation. We received very good suggestions for places to eat and any request was handled quickly & cheerfully. The room was clean (wonderful bed), the location is great for touring Washington & the staff greeted you warmly each day on our return. I'll definitely stay again when in the area.

name: The Madison
title: “Nicely Done”
text: The hotel is extremely well appointed from a design standpoint and perhaps more importantly the level of service matches! I marveled at the creativity the Federalist has put into their drink menus, offerings are impressive featuring herbs, spices, and fresh made purees – try the Five Ri! The menu matches the expectations set forth by the cocktails, the steak was well prepared and matched anything you could find in a higher end steakhouse. Food staff throughout the hotel was eager to please and well versed in menu items and preparation. Location is central to all major sites and you would be hard pressed to find a location with such charm and personal service.

name: The Liaison Capitol Hill, An Affinia Hotel
title: “Excellent staff made the trip”
text:
I stayed here as part of a block of rooms (for a wedding) during the first full weekend in January. While most of the people in the block were placed on a floor with a lot of noise, I lucklily was placed on a lower floor, and I didn't find much issue with it. My room seemed like it was newly renovated-- very clean and stylish. There was a chaise lounge chair that was perfect for a nap!
I have to say that the staff at the front desk were really excellent. Van checked me in, and he was very friendly and helpful. Devin was also at the front desk during most of my stay, and he was super helpful as well on a number of occassions. These two really made a regular hotel stay into a great customer service experience.
I liked the location too-- it was within walking distance to the Capitol, the mall, museums, and monuments. It's not too far from Reagan airport (about $16 taxi trip), and it was close to the wedding ceremony/reception. If you're a Capitol Hill bride looking for a hotel for your guests, I would recommend it. I had a great stay.

name: Monaco Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Hip and Friendly and Happening”
text: My wife and I spent one night for a quickie DC trip. The hotel staff was amazing and accommodating—from the front desk to the Bellmen and valets. The lobby and bar was amiably packed with locals and tourists, drinking adult beverages and having a good time. Even though the hotel was at capacity due to a few weddings, it all worked. Our room was hotel modern: flat screen, IPod, wired and well appointed. The location is DC perfect, across from an art museum and the Verizon center eating and shopping district. A fun, convenient place. Highly recommended.

name: Madera, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great location”
text: DuPont Circle is the place to be - close to the metro and in a semi-residential, therefore quiet neighborhood. We were offered a large corner room (804) with 2 Queen beds and a balconey - handy for checking the weather each day before venturing out. Using AAA membership we got the price down from $340 to $199. My advice would be to look for their bargin times of the year and jump on their Christmas rate of $98/night. We had to cancel our Christmas holiday plans and rebook at a peak time for the area - Cherry Blossom season. Nicer weather, but twice the expense. We checked out the other Klimpton property nearby, Topaz Hotel, and found Madera to be superior.

name: JW Marriott Washington DC
title: “excelente!”
text:
[--]
o hotel e show, porem na diaria nao esta incluso o cafe da manha! pelo preco acho q nao custava oferecer essa cortesia!

name: The Dupont Circle Hotel
title: “DC trade show”
text:
I spent a very hot weekend in DC for the Fancy Food Show.
The Dupont Circle Hotel was great.
From the moment I arrived at reception I was greeted by a wonderful young lady who grew up in Boston near me and could not do enough for me. The room was really nice with all of the amenitys that I could possible want. Everything was very clean. Plenty of room for 1 or 2 people. Bathroom was interesting with an open shower like in Europe. Very comfortable bed and large flat screen TV. I used the business center for checking my emails and printing off my return boarding pass. Very convenient.
Hotel location is in a great area with lots of good restaurants and close to the Metro. I look forward to staying there again.

name: The Fairmont Washington DC
title: “Excellent stay- stands out in DC.”
text:
I was in DC and a little hesitant to stay this far off the mall. The hotel is very close to Georgetown- not really walkable to the sites of Washington. However, it is still in a great area with access to trails, shopping- anything you need. 
DC is a tough market because hotels are always very expensive. You can easily pay 200-400 and end up in a very average hotel room. In the Fairmont's case, however, there was no doubt that this was a luxury hotel.
Service was perfect from the moment I exited the car. Throughout my stay, the staff continually exceeded my expectations. They have a program called Fairmont Gold that is free to join and customizes your experience further- even down to the paper you receive in the morning. 
I was very happy with the room assignment despite not having a view. Because it is in a population dense neighborhood, there are buildings very close. Your best bet is likely an interior courtyard view- mine looked across an alley into another building despite being on the 9th (of 10 floor). The room amenities were incredible. All the little things like a suit rack, shoe horn, gently dimming reading lights, the finest toiletries- nothing was spared.
The fitness center was great as well. It is a fitness club so there are more than just the regular guests there. That means there is also a lot more equipment than you'd normally expect. 
I was there for a meeting and the meeting space was great. It even made the washed up vitriol of the politicians we heard somewhat more bearable!
I'd love to stay here again on my next visit. It is probably better for business than families due to the fact that it is a little distance from the mall.

name: Park Hyatt Washington
title: “The Park Hyatt should have been so much better”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel before and in the past this hotel was much better. This last weekend I was in a room with a shared door. The room next door was having a loud party all night. All the noise came through the door and you could hear everything. The front desk said they would handle the situation and did not. Needless to say it was not a good night. After finally getting to sleep at 3 pm the trash truck woke me up at five. In addition, this room had an extemely hard mattress and poor pillows. On the positive side this hotel has a nice workout facility, excellent location and great bar. 
 This stay should have been so much more. When I checked out the front desk said the general manager would contact me. This has not happened.

name: Topaz, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Get Away”
text: We really enjoyed our stay at the Topaz. The location was perfect, close to everything yet tucked away in a quiet neighborhood. The room was spacious, comfortable, and very nice with many unexpected extras. I wish we didn't have such a busy evening planned and just spent more time in the room. It was the quietest city hotel I've stayed in. We didn't hear any street sounds or noise from other rooms. Staff was very friendly and helpful. We ended up eating dinner in the hotel restaurant as it was so convenient. My husband and the burger and yucca fries and I had the tuna steak sandwich and yucca fries. They were both amazing and I think I'd go back just for that meal. Our stay at the Topaz really made a rare night away for my husband and me into something extra special. We will definitely be back.

name: Four Seasons Washington D.C.
title: “Fabulous!”
text: Great location, great lobby, great hotel room with great mattresses, great bathroom with separate stalls for bathroom and shower and a terrific grand tub! Everything was elegant and impeccably spotless. An oasis of calm! Have fun and worth the plunge! Wish we could have stayed longer.

name: Madera, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Madera As Good as Reviewed”
text:
I did lots of research when looking for a place to stay in DC for our family vacation and I was thrilled to find that Hotel Madera was as good as its reviews suggested. The staff was exceptional, the room very quiet and clean, and the location near the metro proved invaluable. We were there during the heat wave and I can't tell you how welcome the milk and cookies were when we got back to the hotel late one night.
Unfortunately, our car was damaged in the parking garage. As I am writing this I am just beginning to sort this out with insurance and the hotel but my first conversation with the Madera staff about the problem was very reassuring. It is obvious that the service doesn't end when you walk out the front door.

name: Helix, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Perfect Location, Pretty Perfect Hotel”
text: This was my first visit to the hotel and I was really impressed with just about everything. The location is absolutely perfect with so many great restaurants and bars within just a couple blocks. There is a really nice Whole Foods as well that is one block away, which is great if you want to grab a snack on your way back to your room. The hotel is convenient to both Dupont Circle (less than a ten minute walk) as well as the U Street Corridor, which boasts a lot of great restaurants as well. The rooms are different than most hotels, with the focus here being on more modern and fun elements. The service was impeccable and the complimentary wine every evening in the lobby was an enjoyable delight. Best of all, this hotel (like all Kimpton hotels) is super dog friendly, which makes it so easy to travel with your additional family members. I would highly recommend staying at the Helix next time your travels require a trip to DC!

name: The Liaison Capitol Hill, An Affinia Hotel
title: “Spectacular stay! Amazing staff! I would definitely stay here again!”
text: We had a great time here! Beautiful modern hotel, great restaurant, friendly helpful staff, lovely rooftop pool and close to all the sights! We will definitely stay here again!

name: The Fairmont Washington DC
title: “Such a classy place!”
text:
I joined my husband for a business trip to Washington DC.He had stayed at the Fairmont before and was very satisfied.This time we were upgraded to the Golden Conscierge Floor.The hotel is well situated,convenient.The reception area and the lounge/bar are very nice.
Our room was impeccable,the GC Floor breakfast and free internet loung facility a plus.
The reception staff and the conscierge service both at the reception and the GC Floor were excellent.Definitely going back!

name: The Jefferson, Washington DC
title: “A true gem, and a great home base for a DC family vacation”
text:
It would be difficult to imagine a better home base in the heart of DC for us and our three kids. Every member of the staff (admin, dining, concierge, cleaning) was attentive, cheerful, and prompt with service. The location was great - we walked to all the big DC sites - White House, museums, monuments, Capitol, and it's only a block to the Metro (Red Line), but it was QUIET - just far enough away from the nighttime sirens you hear in hotels right on the Mall/Commons/Lafayette Square.
The Plume is exquisite (get the kids room service and treat yourself to a spectacular experience there), and breakfast at the Greenhouse was a treat for the whole family, but equally as important to us were the variety of dining options in a 2-block radius of the hotel, including family dining (ex. PJ Clarke's), quick sandwich places, and healthy organic options.
The hotel is distinctive, from the decor and authentic Jefferson artifacts to the mini-library in the room. If you're bringing kids, you'll be happy to know they have Wii/Gamecube/Xbox options for the room.
Bathroom was luxurious - and if you are a neat freak, this is your place. Unequivocally the cleanest hotel we have ever stayed in.
It's not inexpensive by any stretch, but we felt it was worth every penny. A true gem.

name: Helix, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “fun hotel”
text:
this a colorful little hotel in Washington DC. the overall ambiance is very tasteful, bright and appealing. 
staff is courteous and helpful. rooms are functional, clean and amenities are very good but the rooms are small. 
it is not the best location to be in Washington DC but once you are inside the hotel you will not regret having chosen the hotel. 
the bar is good and so is food. the bubbly hour is very relaxing and great way to unwind after a hectic day.

name: Madera, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Strangest rooms I've stayed in since 1995”
text:
You'll never forget your room at this apartment building converted into a hotel. I stayed in two rooms during a recent trip and each one had its quirks. 
The handicapped room had no closet, just a hanging bar for clothes below (my) waist height in the bathroom. The double queen sized beds left little space for maneuver around the room and both I and a guest were kneecapped by one of the bed. There was an entire room attached to my room that was EMPTY - not a stick of furniture or a closet. This was probably once a kitchenette, judging by the power hookups along the wall. The bathroom's hand held shower sprayer would not stay on the sliding hook apparatus, leading me to switch rooms.
My second room still had no closet, just a higher and longer clothes bar running along the wall that separated the room from the bathroom area. There was no safe in this room, and when I called the desk on this, a safe was toted up to my room and put (unsecured) on a shelf. I guess they figure that anyone running through the lobby with one of these 2'x2'x2' metal boxes would attract attention, and that's how they would protect your valuables. The staff person who brought the safe box up agreed that it would be a good idea to fasten these to something in the room and said that management "was looking into it."
On the plus side, I liked the high speed internet that was included in the room rate. And the linens, towels, and toiletries were all excellent.

name: Hotel George, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “DC stop on way down to OuterBanks”
text:
Friendly staff that was so helpful and pleasant - the open wine tasting each evening was a great touch - very good with our dogs and for those without dogs you are not overwhelmed by those traveling with their pets. 
Staff were helpful with directions and very attentive to any questions / needs we had.
Stayed in another Kimpton Hotel in Baltimore on our return trip from the Outerbanks and had a very good experience their as well. 
We will be a return guest and will recommend to our friends.

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Fabulous experience!”
text: My significant other and I just spent a Saturday night here over Thanksgiving. It was his birthday which I mentioned upon booking and check-in. We're also Kimpton members and had a great AAA rate. They upgraded us to a spa/exercise room which was so much fun. The whirlpool tub is designed for two and was spacious, clean and worked superbly. There was an elliptical machine in its own roomy nook. We were treated to champagne and chocolate covered strawberries for the birthday celebration. The room was very spacious with a great bed. People really attended the happy hour for wine, hot toddies and hors d'oeuvres and to verying degrees to meet one another. The staff were to a person exceptionally hospitable. When we came downstairs on Sunday morning and they were out of newspapers they bopped right out and bought additional ones, handing us ours at our breakfast table. The location is great between the metro and all that the Dupont Circle area has to offer. We were able to park for free on a neighboring street. High honors to Kimpton. I have stayed in their hotels now in Chicago, San Fran, New York City and DC and they never disappoint.

name: Helix, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Always Excellent!”
text: Because my partner and I travel with our two dogs, I stay in Kimpton Hotels whenever possible. Their services are awesome. Hotel Helix is no exception.

name: Hotel George, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Hotel”
text: We had a great stay at Hotel George in Washington, DC. Great location.....friendly staff......and great rooms.

name: Madera, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Härligt hotell på gångavstånd till det mesta!”
text: Lite dyrt, men trivdes jättebra på det här hotellet, stannade bara en natt men hann se mycket av DC eftersom det var gångavstånd till det mesta, annars ligger tunnelbanan just om hörnet. Utmärkt service, perfekt att det gick att lämna in bilen på hotellets parkering (extra kost).

name: Sofitel Washington DC
title: “Close to the White House, great hotel”
text: I stayed here for 2 nights while on a business trip. Hotel staff was very friendly and the room was extremely comfortable, large and quiet. I enjoyed coming back to my room after a long day of meetings to find the lights dimmed, classical music playing, and bottles of water. In the mornings, the hotel provides complimentary coffee and tea in the bar/restaurant area off the main lobby.

name: The Dupont Circle Hotel
title: “Save yourself some stress ... don't bother!”
text:
Aside from the location, this hotel has nothing going for it! We were greeted gruffly by the reception clerk who then rapidly fired off a tirade of instructions abouth the hotel, none of which we could remember or were documented anywhere in our room. The concierge was friendly, but never there when you needed him - we waited 40 minutes for someone to even acknowledge us at the desk to make a tour booking. 
Room was comfortable and at first look, it does look nice, but it all ends there. We stayed for 4 nights in Room 201 from 15 Nov. After the first night, not one toiletry item was restocked - not even toilet paper! I had to call reception to ask for soap and a shower cap and despite them advising it "would be sent straight up", I waited 45 minutes and even then they did not get it right. After 3 visits to my room and a claim they did not know what I meant, I finally received some soap. The next day I left a note for housekeeping requesting they restock ALL items we had used - this was a pretty clear request. Again, nothing was restocked, so I called reception again to request a shower cap and shower gel where I received a very rude response that "it should be there", and technically, if housekeeping had done their job it should have been! I then had to explain that we had not had any items replaced for 2 days and I thought this was a basic and simple request. The housekeeping staff obviously decided they would be smart and delivered to me a huge bag filled with all toiletry items EXCEPT the ones I had requested, so I again called for what I needed ... I think you're getting the picture. What makes this worse is that my husband and I stayed here with friends who kept telling us every day that their toiletry items were being replaced, even the ones they were not using!! They were staying on the same floor but at the other end of the floor and obviously had housekeeping staff who cared about the guest comfort.
The room itself was incredibly noisy. The street below is horrendous and there is NO insulation from noise. There are no curtains and the shutters did not close enough to darken the room. So if you want sleep, avoid this hotel.
The locatioin is great - ony two blocks to the Metro and an abundance of restaurants ... but that's all I can say on the positive side.
On checking out I was asked how our stay was and I responed it was "fair". When asked why I explained my story and was haned a card with details of the Operations manager and TripAdvisor. The reception clerk recommended I write a review and that the Manager would respond. I could not actually believe that there was no apology, but the hotel's own staff suggested I should write a poor review ... so here it is! I'm not sure if I will get a response as it doesn;t help me after I have left ... I just would have liked some assistance at the time. All I hope is that my experience helps others NOT stay here!

name: Willard InterContinental Washington
title: “Would go back in a heart beat!”
text:
Loved it Loved it!! We had just left a timeshare with the grandchildren and we (the grandparents) stayed in the Williard, while the kids stayed elsewhere and we met daily. First of all, the lobby is breathe taking, our room was super and perfect size (king bed) and staff was terrific.
It was very clean. We purchased it with the breakfast package which was well worth it. Your choice of buffet or off the menu. The hotel is alongside the treasury building, you can walk 1/2 block and be in front of the White House, across the street from the Mall, and a little bit of a further walk to the museums. It was perfect !
If I had to think of a negative it would be that in the bathroom there was no place to hang a toiletry bag other than the hook behind the door which was for your towel. The sink top was also a bit small with tow of us and toiletries. But I could live with that! If we go back to DC will stay there again.

name: Monaco Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Location - Great Staff”
text: Stayed at the Hotel Monaco for 7 nights and it was fantastic. The location is superb. Just across the street from Metro and mere blocks from the Mall. Great Dining options very close by and great resturaunt - Poste on site. The building is great - old Post Office building renovated into boutique Hotel. Best part about the whole stay - however - was the staff. Great recommendations for dining - great happy hour - and just plain great service - especially from weekend front desk manager, Jason. Will stay at the Monaco again on my next trip to DC - nothing in DC comes close to beating the location and service.

name: Four Seasons Washington D.C.
title: “Perfect business hotel. Not cheap, but worth it”
text: Flawless comfort and tranquility in a big city. Not cheap, but worth it

name: Carlyle Suites Hotel
title: “Great for a group event”
text: My organization stayed at the Carlyle Suites Hotel for our annual board meeting in DC. Sales and Catering Manager JoAnn Sipe was super helpful arranging our rooms, and flexible with changes to our group size. The hotel is great. Very nice and at a reasonable rate. We particularly like that each room has a small kitchen, which is great for people like me who are picky about food, and like to start the day with breakfast in the room. We've stayed at the Carlyle two years in a row now, and look forward to coming back next year.

name: Park Hyatt Washington
title: “Good DC Choice”
text: With many different options in DC the Park Hyatt is a good choice. The location is great being near both DuPont Circle and Georgetown and not far from K Street and the museums. The decor is modern and fresh and the room was designed well with a spacious bathroom and living area. Service was good but not great but overall the hotel exceeded my expectations. Also the Park Hyatt is a good value compared to the Ritz or Four Seasons in Georgetown. I liked this hotel and would return.

name: Willard InterContinental Washington
title: “Great Hotel, Great Location, Good but not great service”
text: On the whole, I think we got what we paid for. The hotel location was wonderful. There were many great restaurants within a block. Easy access to almost all attractions. In my opinion the only drawback was very good and friendly, but not exceptional service. The concierge is exceptionally busy and it takes an act of congress to see him. In four days we were unable to have a good discussion with him because people were lined up to see him and I was always at the end of the line. We were able to get a phone call through and he did take care of us, but the office is obviously understaffed. Upon arrival we had to unload our own bags from the cab and got 1/2 way up the stairs before the bell staff assisted our family of 3. On other occasions, they were superb. I would reccommend staying here, but not if you are use to Four Seasons or Ritz style service. However, the room was beautiful, updated, large and overall value was very good..

name: The Madison
title: “Great service”
text: The staff are incredible and provide very high quality service, which helps this place overcome some of it's negatives. The rooms are nice, but pretty small, and it seems a bit worn in places, which then seem to show shoddy attempts at hiding it. Overall when I was comparing it to similarly-priced hotels, I couldn't help but think the others might have been a better experience. It's a nice, comfortable hotel, but I really felt like I overpaid. The staff were by far the best part of the experience.

name: Hotel Teatro
title: “Really enjoyable hotel”
text: We have just come back from 1 week holiday (to celebrate our 13th wedding anniversary) in Denver from the UK (My wife is English and I’m French). We chose the Teatro Hotel based on the Trip Advisor reviews. I must say we were not disappointed. 3 weeks prior to the trip I got some great advice from Carolyn and Torie (Hotel concierges) about best places to eat and visit (they booked us a table at Second Home for our wedding anniversary which was a GREAT restaurant!). The room was very nice (a bit of street noise but nothing that we couldn’t cope with) and the bed was amazingly comfortable (2nd best mattress in a hotel after the Four Season in Paris). The car service is an absolute must-The staff operating it are courteous and extremely professional-they did their utmost to be of assistance and it saved us a fortune in taxi fare. We also had a great time at the bar (Al was a great barman). The only slight disappointment was that on our arrival (past midnight as our plane was delayed by 4 hours) we found a bottle of fizzy alcohol and some biscuits which we thought was a lovely gesture for our wedding anniversary-it’s only when I read the card the next day that we discovered that it was meant for guests who were attending a big wedding and were staying at the hotel (told reception the next day who sent someone to take everything way). All in all an excellent stay!

name: Sofitel Washington DC
title: “Luxurious accomodations, impeccable service, great location: worth it!”
text: I recently stayed at the Sofitel for a four-day conference and it was one of the finest hotels I've ever visited. The Sofitel was a luxurious, comfortable hotel in a great location with impeccable, attentive service. The catered French menus for all the conference meals were absolutely delicious and generous. The meeting rooms were beautiful and just the right size for this group of about 100-120 attendees. My fellow conference guests only wished there was an accessible stairway from the first floor conference room to the second level meeting rooms, as the elevators became really congested between sessions. I thought it was a worthy value for the price, and will gladly return.

name: The Dupont Circle Hotel
title: “Spacious rooms, great location, reasonable value.”
text: What is now the Dupont has been through many personality changes. Now entirely renovated in early 21st century style it's not hugely expensive by DC standards and ideally located for the metro and a huge collection of restaurants. Reception staff were very friendly, public areas and rooms were spotlessly clean, and there is little traffic noise despite the building being on a triangle of land backing onto a traffic circle. Some questionable room decor choices though. The espresso-color stained light wood furniture does not stand up well to hotel use (every scratch and ding shows) and the shallow bathroom sinks are trendy but guaranteed to splash water in every direction.

name: The Liaison Capitol Hill, An Affinia Hotel
title: “This hotel is a "rare" find”
text: Not since we stayed in the old Shoreham in the 1970's have we found a hotel as uniquely suited for business travel. Service is attentive, amenities top notch; certainly the restaurant is one of the best I've eaten in. The basic room we stayed in was somewhat on the small side, but the beds were something you dream of when on the road. The other "plus" for me was the location; it's proximity to the Capitol and Union Station. Definitely top of my list for DC travel

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “More than what we needed!”
text:
We arrived at Hotel Palomar after coming from New York, we arrived at 5pm and could see that the lobby was really busy, not really understanding what was going on we checked in and were told that between 5pm - 6pm they have wine and nibbles for all guest to enjoy and communicate with other guests. We just had a 3 hours train ride from NY so this was perfect! There was a choice of white and red wine, there were olives and crackers to nibble on too. A lovely jesture from the hotel, and this is every night. 
The hotel allows pets, which i love and throughly enjoyed seeing all the different dogs going in and out the elevator. 
The hotel is large, it is situated on a side street away from the main dupont circle area, it is close to the metro and about 40-50 minutes walk to The Mall/lincoln memorial/capital building etc. We walked to these every day, and some twice as we went back to the IMAX in the national History museum one night, so don't be concerned that it may look out of the way. That said, 50 minutes there, 50 minutes back plus all day walking around the more meant we were exhausted, but the hotel has plasters!!! much needed. 
We had a package with continental breakfast, which consisted of toast, croissants, porridge, tea, coffee, fruit juice, cakes and fruit. This was plenty compared to what we usually eat and available until 10am, so more relaxing that NY. 
The room that we stayed in was on the 3rd floor, it was quiet, so very comfortable, spacious and welcoming. We didn't have a view, but we didn't need one. We had just spend the past few days in NY and needed a relaxing break and this hotel gave it to us. It was extremly clean, Aveda hair and body products in the bathroom, replaced daily if you have used a drop. Being typically british we asked reception for tea making facilities and 5 minutes later they were being delivered with fresh milk. 
There is a mini bar, but you have to pay for items naturally so we didn't ask for the key for this. There is a safe in the room and there are gowns and slippers. The bed was massive, so many pillows and duvets and sheets. We went in February so needed a nice warm room and this was great. The hotel is very large, but you don't really notice the other guests until the wine and nibble hour, it is very quiet. There is a pool but we didn't get to view this seeing as it was February. 
We got this hotel at a brilliant rate with Virgin.com and after turning up, i am sure a mistake was made as we should have paid way more than what we did. 
All staff were more than accomodating, the doorman were very helpful and friendly. 
We thoroughly enjoyed our trip to Washington and our stay at Hotel Palomar, i wouldn't hesitate to stay here again.

name: Hotel George, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great hotel”
text: The staff, room, and location of this hotel is excellent. I will stay here again when I need to return to Washington DC. On top of that they offer free parking for hybrid vehicles!

name: Monaco Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Awful service, do not stay at Hotel Monaco”
text:
My group of three adults was genuinely looking forward to our stay at Kimpton's Hotel Monaco in Washington, DC but we were greeted by stress and left our stay (early) stressed. They overbooked the hotel and when we arrived they made our group of 3 adults stay in a small room with one queen-size bed. This is unacceptable. We then had to argue to get them to deliver a roll-out bed. The room was then even smaller, with three adults' things, we were very uncomfortable. They refused to transfer us to a room with two beds even though we were booked for 3 nights. When we left early after the second night they attempted to charge us an extra $100 for leaving early. Unbelievable! We had already paid for our entire trip, they could sell their room twice and they try to give us a penalty charge!?!? After yet another argument they waived the fee for leaving early. 
I recommend saving over $100 a night and staying at an economy hotel if Hotel Monaco is an option. The service will likely be better and the space and comfort level will be the same.
What a let down. I haven't encountered horrible service such as that from the Hotel Monaco staff anywhere before. Don't stay there.

name: Hotel George, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A lovely hotel”
text:
I always to stay at the George when I'm in DC. The rooms are really nice: great sheets and bathrooms. The staff is extremely responsive. And if you're a Kimpton in touch person, which is free to join, you get free Internet and a $10 credit for the minibar.
