The best rooms are the ones ending in, say 03 to 08: those are the rooms looking out over E Street. Some of the other rooms can be a little dark, but if you want quiet might be a tad better.
The hotel restaurNt, Bistro Bis, is phenomenal, especially for a power breakfast.
I would stay at the George always, if J could, but I've never seen a hotel where the room rates vary so dramatically.

name: Carlyle Suites Hotel
title: “Great location, Nice room”
text:
Location is great (close to Dupont Circle) and the staff were very professional and friendly.
The room I stayed was nice, clean and big. Recommended for couples or families.
Regarding the interior, some doors and bathroom items looked outdated or cheap, which I didn't expect from the room rates. 
If you're not too picky about the details, I think it's quite a nice hotel.

name: Park Hyatt Washington
title: “Excellent”
text:
Little to say beyond the other five star reviews: excellent service, palatial bathrooms, and well appointed rooms and public areas. All the staff is particularly warm. Breakfast at the Blue Duck Tavern is a must - their eggs are the freshest and best tasting I have ever tried.
Problems - On my last stay I booked a Park Suite and was given one on the top floor that had an odd layout and seemed less than the advertised 1060 sq. feet. It also lacked a work desk, which was particularly irritating on a work trip, and the A/C occasionally shut off for a few minutes to blow hot humid air. Next time I'll request another room if this occurs.
Overall, however, this will be my hotel of choice for most business trips to DC, except for the times I have business very close to the St. Regis.

name: Willard InterContinental Washington
title: “Very comfortable and clean”
text:
I stayed at the Willard Intercontinental in DC for one night/two days this summer on a business trip. I chose this hotel because it was basically located across from the Ronald Reagan Conference Center where I had business. 
They were able to let me check in way early, which was awesome, and it's located within walking distance to quite a few site-seeing/touristy things, so I was able to spend some of my free time as a tourist. 
All of my dealings with the staff were great, from check in to storing and then retrieving my bag upon checkout on my 2nd day.
The room was very comfortable, clean and quiet, and I have to admit, very large and spacious for a standard king hotel room these days.
I would totally stay here again if visiting DC for either leisure or business again.

name: Hotel George, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Lovely Boutique Hotel Convenient to Capitol and Smithsonian”
text: This is a nice hotel in a great location for sight seeing. The hotel is quirky and modern with a friendly professional staff. We had a lovely room facing E street with big windows that let in a lot of light. It gave the room the feel of a guest room of a private home instead of a hotel room. It was well appointed with nice furnishings, a safe, a mini bar and a spacious bath. I had a problem with the promo "park and play" rate I booked the room under when I checked in, but manager, Michael Love, quickly and professionally set things right. It is an easy walk to the Capitol, Library of Congress and the Smithsonian. There is a Starbucks around the corner. If you are headed towards the theater district at night a pied, you may want to walk down towards the mall and then head down to 7th because there is a homeless shelter on 2nd Ave and lots of characters hanging around. I did not feel concerned at all during daylight, but I would feel uncomfortable walking by after dark. However, the whole thing could easily be averted just walking down a block and around it.

name: Hotel Teatro
title: “Great Job”
text: Everyone at The Hotel Teatro did a wonderful job. My wife and I had an excellent time. Mr. Andrew Solanyk, an employee, even loaned me his personal cufflinks for a shirt I wanted to wear.....above and beyond. Thank you.

name: The Madison
title: “Not what it used to be!”
text: I've stayed at the Madison several times over the past three years and always enjoyed the room, staff and location. This last visit may well be my last. I was taken to one room that overwhelmingly smelled of smoke and they quickly moved me to another room that at least did not smell. There is construction going on on one side of the hotel closing their popular bar and restaurant that we were not informed about and the noise started by 8am on a weekend morning. Additionally, the room was not clean with obvious stains on the bathroom walls and an overall shabby appearance. The location is superb and the staff was helpful, but the hotel is beginning to look rundown. There are too many other choices in D.C. than to settle for the Madison's disrepair.

name: Sofitel Washington DC
title: “Excellent service and terrific location!”
text: I was here on business recently. The service was excellent--from the woman who welcomed me to the concierge that gave me an umbrella because of overcast skies to the person who delivered my breakfast. The rooms are well appointed and the bathroom is great--very large with a separate tub and shower. The shower has a rain shower head and the toiletries were L'Occitane. The rooms were a little on the small side and you have to pay for wifi--in a nice hotel I think that comes off as a cheap step--otherwise I would have given 5 stars. The location is great--very close to the White House and the monuments and near to some very good restaurants. I would stay here again.

name: The Madison
title: “Awesome”
text: This was such a plush hotel...Beautiful and some homey...The beds and linens were so awesome. The location was fabulous so close to the White House and close to the metro. Every trip back to DC we will stay here. 1 thing, the breakfast was not the best and was very expensive. Eat elsewhere!

name: The Madison
title: “Excellent location, superb staff”
text: I really have nothing bad to say about this hotel except that the AC unit was a little dated and did not totally keep up with the extreme heat Washington faced during our stay. The staff was great, the rooms were clean and nice and we really enjoyed the lobby wine parties. This hotel has a nice gym with plenty of selection when it comes to the machines. We would certainly stay here again.

name: The Dupont Circle Hotel
title: “Never again!”
text: The hotel front desk was so unorganized! Asked for the manager and they said we are all managers, what? Need to go for more training! Don't leave any change laying around because it will dissappear! Told the front desk about it and he never flinched , like it happens often. If you want to leave a tip for the housekeeping staff it is not until you check out. No bathroom privacy..whatever happened to doors on bathrooms? The only thing positive was the comfy bed and the door staff.

name: Willard InterContinental Washington
title: “Unpretentious service in luxurious hotel with a perfect tourist location”
text:
Despite a few service blemishes, the hotel is historic, glamorous, the location is perfect and probably the best spot in the city for tourists wanting to visit the monuments and museums along The Mall each day. The public areas are over-the-top, decadently beautiful with custom-loomed carpets, marble pillars, gold moldings, red velvet, etc.
Especially given the discounted rate currently available, (about $400/night prepaid on Expedia with buffet breakfast for 2 given as a $50 daily credit) we would absolutely choose this hotel again. 
Service was blissfully unpretentious. Front desk is efficient and courteous. They did make an error on checkout, did not see my $2,400 prepay. This was (with some difficulty figuring out on their part) corrected when I quesioned it. Bellhops expect tips when luggage brought into the lobby and then again when they bring it to the room. Unlike other 5-star hotels I have been in, bellhops blatantly push for tips. Housekeeping always greeted us and were eager to please.
Service is excellent but not impeccable. We did not have a nightly turn-down service, nor was a paper delivered to our room, it was kept in a stack near the elevator. I believe these may be available in a higher room stay level. Restaurant service friendly but again not top drawer (in the breakfast buffet, they take your dirty utensils off your plate and put it back on the table when you go for more food rather than give you a new one for instance). Phone service is excellent, they answer you promptly by name (pronounced correctly!).
We had a deluxe room #731 overlooking the courtyard. Room was very large, quiet, fairly clean, and the bathrooms wonderfully clean. Mattresses were good, but not of Westin/Four Seasons quality. Plenty of towels (including wash cloths!) were always provided. However, they never vacuumed under the beds or bureaus...we know this because on our last day, we checked under the beds to make sure we didn't miss anything; there were plenty of large dust balls and a pair of sandals from some previous guests! There were a few minor things not in working order...the tv speaker in the bathrooms was pulled out of the wall, and the clock-radio iPhone plug did not work. The digital tv is amazingly slow turning it on and froze once, but turning it off and back on fixed it.
We made almost no use of the concierge, as the recommended DC restaurants are consistent across Fodors, Frommers, Lonely Planet, etc so check these sites online. The Old Ebbitt Grill is one block in back of the hotel, across from the White House, was a great inexpensive place for a meal with decent quality food.
Note that the famous restaurant "The Willard Room" is now closed, the room is available for business and party rentals only. They have replaced it with a casual french-style "Cafe du Parc" on the side of the hotel which was warm and nice, had a nice seating area in front of the hotel during the day. The breakfast buffet ($25) is here, was decent but never varied during the 6 days we were here.
The only minor inconvenience that really mattered was the Prime Minister of Iraq, Maliki, was staying in the hotel while we were there. It is a bit inconvenient as extra precautions are taken, more so than with other world leaders. There were secret service men in the lobby, on every floor, the rear street, rear hotel entrance, and rear elevator were blocked for his use. Karzai, the Afghan president also stays at this hotel with similar precautions we were told.
All of these minor inconveniences pale in comparison to the perfect location for tourists visiting the main sites along The Mall. The location is a few blocks closer to The Mall than even the Hay Adams. The Marriott was directly across the street, but it did not look like a 5-star hotel.

name: Sofitel Washington DC
title: “holiday visit”
text: decor is good, upholstery excellent, customer service is appalling

name: Hotel Teatro
title: “Wonderful Service!”
text: My boyfriend and I booked this hotel to celebrate New Year's Eve downtown... and we loved every minute of it. The location is great!!! Just a few blocks from both the light rail and 16th street mall, not to mention the fact that it is right by all the theaters! The room was very clean and well decorated. The bathroom was wonderful with a large soaking tub and a rain shower. It was definitely a nice place to stay. However the best part of this hotel is definitely the service. From the moment we walked in to the moment we left I felt like the staff treated us as if we were royalty. Everyone was polite and always smiling, and there to help us with anything... even the cleaning lady voluntarily helped us open our door, and did so with a smile! The best employee by far though was Adam. He delivered our room service breakfast. It really seemed like he loved his job! He made conversation with us, and was just really nice. When we were checking out he walked by, and recognized us by name, and proceeded to talk to us and made sure everything turned out alright! I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone that enjoys good service!

name: Hotel Teatro
title: “Worth the $$”
text:
Booked for a 4 night stay as part of an 18 day trip around Colorado, based on TA advice and a cracking deal through a hotel room website. Stayed in Superior King Size room on 8th floor.
The staff could not be more helpful or polite. I was most impressed with how they went out of their way to help.
Great location - Downtown/LoDo on the door step - as was 16th St.
Went to the Broncos match - far better to walk - across the Uni grounds - just 30 minutes.
The bed was so comfortable - great accomodation.
I would agree with another TA review - the rooms needed far more drawers for clothing - and the towel rails need to be near the sinks in the bathroom.
All in all, a great hotel!

name: Helix, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Enjoyable experience”
text: Very unique hotel although much smaller than pictures reflect. The room itself was good size though, and very clean and comfortable. The staff seemed helpful, but not overly accomodating. For those of you unfamiliar with the DC area, the closest metro stations at McPhearson and Dupont, are quite a hike away. I know it says 5-6 blocks, but I don't understand how they measure "blocks" in DC! Plan your day wisely and it shouldn't be an issue. The free happy hour was wonderful and much appreciated after a long day of sightseeing. One more word of warning: this is a local hot spot for the bar and can get pretty rowdy on the weekends. If you're not into the late night noise, ask for a room that faces the opposite direction of the outdoor patio. You'll sleep much better! All in all, a good experience especially if you are traveling with pets.

name: The Dupont Circle Hotel
title: “Very Nice”
text: Check inn was easy. All of the staff I encountered were extremely polite. The location was good. The Dupont Circle Metro Station is close (use Q street). The room was very clean. The bed was extremely comfortable. The free wireless internet worked well. The room was quiet except for a little street noise. This was not really a problem. The bathroom was nice. Some have complained about the configuration of the shower. This isn't really a problem if you direct the shower head properly. We did not use the restaurant but did use the bar which was good. I would return.

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “Good value (last time I stayed)”
text: Bostn hotels are implasuably expensive. The Lenox has a certain charm, the rooms are small but nicely done. Really central location. A better bet forthe money that the Marriot or Sheraton. If I go back on business I'll stay there again.

name: Magnolia Hotel Denver
title: “Overnight trip”
text: Excellent location, comfortable and just right for us. Hotel shuttle took us to a local resturant for a wedding reception which made life easy on us since we didn't know the location.

name: Monaco Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Superb hotel in a great location”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Monaco over Christmas while visiting relatives in the DC area. I chose the hotel for its location, which was within walking distance of the Smithsonian museums and White House, and across the street from a Metro station. The hotel was gorgeous, very European in feeling. Our room was large enough to be quite comfortable and had amenities such as free internet, plush bathrobes, and cd player. The staff was super-friendly and helpful. Room service was prompt and the food was excellent; I want their grilled-cheese sandwich recipe!

name: Hotel Teatro
title: “Lovely Botique Hotel”
text:
We live about 50 miles from Denver and chose this hotel for a birthday celebration, particularly because we wanted a smaller boutique hotel with high service standards.
The location is good as it is near the performing arts center, the 16th street mall and all of the downtown activities.
The check-in area is rather simple and non-descript. We had a small suite with a bedroom, living room and two full baths. The bed was very comfortable, the room appointments were lovely and the room was very clean. The bathroom was good sized, with a nice size soaking tub and a separate shower with a rainfall shower head (which I love) and great tile and counter tops with terrific toiletry amenities.
There was a printer/fax/copier in the room although we hadn't taken a computer with us as we were trying to "not work" for a day.
The concierge was great. Very responsive, helpful and pleasant. The staff were very attentive. They managed to find my husband a stocking hat (still with the tags on it) at 7:30 p.m. on a Sunday evening, as we were going on a horse drawn carriage ride and he hade forgotten his hat. We found the bell staff, housekeeping and front desk staff to deliver a high level of service.
Downsides: The room we had, on the 5th floor, had a brick wall for a view and there was some type of drilling going on during the afternoon. It didn't bother us much and didn't last long. Since we were there for a birthday celebration, we had planned on ordering dessert when we returned after dinner. The menu said room service was served until 10 p.m. We called at 9:30 p.m. and they could not provide the dessert we had chosen as the "kitchen was closing." They offered an alternative, which I presumed would have been served warm (a chocolate molten cupcake) but it was quite cold. They did comp the dessert but we would have preferred to pay for the one we had selected. Our breakfast was also delivered 15 minutes after the requested time, which we confirmed the evening before.
Overall we found the hotel to be of high quality and we would stay here again based on the quality of the staff, the well appointed rooms and the location. Room Service could use a little work but it isn't enough of a drawback to take away from the excellant service provided by the rest of the staff.

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “Superb Hotel”
text:
What can I say? The Lenox is a beautiful hotel in every way. The rooms are spacious, comfortable and elegant. The view out over Boston from our 10th floor room was spectacular. 
Beds (2 doubles!!) were big and really comfortable, the bathroom was clean and had fresh flowers on our arrival and we had a small sofa which was great to lie on and look at the city after a day of walking!
The hotel has 2 bars that offer the chance to relax no matter your mood. City Bar is more "cool" and chilled out, whereas Solas next door offers a good traditional Irish bar with a great pint of Sam Adams!!
The Lenox has a really traditional feel (from the ceiling chandeliers to the cotton bags with your morning newspaper), whilst still being modern (from the data points in the room to the wall mounted TVs in the lobby toilets!!) This hotel manages to make you feel special, and it has a prime location in this wonderful city.

name: The Liaison Capitol Hill, An Affinia Hotel
title: “Incredible Experience Here!!”
text: I stayed here in December during a trip to DC for work, going off a colleague's advice. Glad I took him up on it- the place was very cool; very nicely done. Great location, excelent amenities (I only wish it was summer so i could have gone out to the pool, which looks amazing), amazing staff, and a fastastic overall vibe to the place. I would definitely come back here for all of my DC travel, and would highly recommend this hotel for the positive experince i had here.

name: Magnolia Hotel Denver
title: “Great little boutique hotel downtown! Great buffet breakfast!”
text: We would definitely stay here again. The hotel is beautiful inside. The valet Parker's are great!

name: Carlyle Suites Hotel
title: “The Carlyle was great!”
text:
This was our first visit to the DC area and we had a wonderful time. The weather was hot but we enjoyed our stay just the same. The hotel was excellent. The service was superior and so was the the condition of the hotel. I don't recall his name, but the manager was so nice to us. We felt very welcome the minute we walked into their door. I would reccomend this hotel to anyone I know coming to the DC area. Thanks for making our family vaction extra special.
Sincerely,
Stacy Lindsley

name: Helix, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great fun at Hotel Helix”
text:
I was booked into the Hotel Helix by someone handling my business arrangements, someone living in the area who said she thought I'd appreciate a hotel a little out of the ordinary and standard -- and I absolutely loved the Austin Powers retro look of the lobby and my room and the music playing in the lobby. A younger friend going to graduate school in DC came to visit, and he thought it was the perfect hotel for me, too: funky yet filled with all the comforts and amenities one would expect at a hotel -- comfy bed with a trompe l'oeil backdrop of a surfer on the entire wall, bright oranges and yellows and greens to the color scheme but somehow not disturbingly glaring, television midway on a kitchy pole stand with good reception and sound, good quality toiletries and water pressure and temperature in the bathroom area with a bright orange sink, coffee maker. I also appreciated and attended the free champagne "happy hour" each evening.
I appreciated not being in not just a carbon copy chain hotel where all the majority of the hotels and noise were. I enjoyed walking to the White House area, to the International Spy Museum, to the Smithsonian American Art Museum, etc. Not far, but not for those unaccustomed to walking. Great restaurant a block or so away, convenient corner store for buying snacks or soft drinks for the room. I didn't find the neighborhood overly sketchy as some other reviewers had, but then I'm a born-and-raised big-city person.

name: Magnolia Hotel Denver
title: “This is our favorite place to stay in Denver. The rooms and all the staff are wonderful.”
text: This is the best place to stay in downtown Denver. Everything about it is awesome.

name: Park Hyatt Washington
title: “Expensive, but refined”
text: I stayed at this property for two nights recently on a business trip and was impressed with the level of refinement. The staff were courteous, attentive and knowledgeable - a rare feat it seems these days. The rooms elegant, simple, luxurious and quite comfortable. I agree that the rooms are pricey, but this hotel is a great choice for business travelers.

name: Monaco Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “DC Monaco Outstanding”
text:
I read with interest the reviews criticizing the Monaco, since I had stayed there several times with no problems. When I stayed at the Monaco again this week, I was especially attentive for the supposed small rooms, noisey doors, dampness, and the other negative things I had read on this site. Once again, my stay was excellent. Big, clean, nicely furnished room with high ceilings. Wonderful decor. The wide and open hallways with curtains feel like a Persian castle. The restaurant has excellent reasonably priced food, and the bar is big and hopping.
My only complaint -- contruction on side streets keeps taxis away. At 6:00 am I had to wait 15 minutes before a cab came by.
By way of comparison, I stayed at the trendy "W" hotel on Lex in New York last week and it was not even in the same league as the DC Monaco.

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Pleasant stay”
text:
I spent one night in the Palomar as I was attending my cousin's wedding there. I had a nice, clean comfortable room on the 4th floor with only one problem. I had requested an early check in time of 11am because I was attending a 2pm wedding and was not able to get a room until the standard 3pm check in time. I ended up getting ready for the wedding in family member's rooms that had checked in the night before.
I had to catch a plane the next morning and it was easy to get shuttle service to pick me up from there. I was also pleasantly surprised when I visited the Business Center and realized the Palomar provides free printing of airline boarding passes. Not all hotels offer this so that was nice! Pets are permitted to stay in this hotel so if you want a pet free room you need to make a point to request that. I don't have pet allergies but I just didn't want to sleep in a bed where someone else's dog or cat might have spent the night.

name: Hotel George, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Wonderful!”
text: We visited DC this weekend for business...combined with a couples get away! It was exactly what we were looking for! Great location, reasonable price, clean! We chose the Hotel because of the wonderful reviews and they were correct! My favorite thing about the place was the wonderful shower! Mega water pressure from a great shower head and wonderful shampoo, conditioner and body wash which reminded me exactly of the most expensive ones we enountered at a Caribbean spa! Staff was polite and helpful. Within 2 blocks of Union Station and super reasonable! Can't say enough good things!

name: The Lenox Hotel
title: “il materasso più' comodo mai provato!”
text: Consigliatoci da amici residenti a Boston, questo hotel ha delle camere spaziose e molto curate. Il materasso era comodissimo e il bagno tenuto molto bene. Ottimo anche il servizio del personale. Il classico hotel americano di alto servizio e professionalita', a prezzi abbastanza modici per la qualità'... Se torniamo a Boston, sappiamo dove andare, CONSIGLIATISSIMO!

name: Topaz, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Most comfortable bed ever”
text:
Stayed for three nights last weekend. Pluses: Excellent location, attractive, large room and the most comfortable bed, pillows, sheets, and comforter of any hotel I've ever stayed at. Despite my complaints, I would definitely consider staying there again.
Minuses: There aren't many places for breakfast close by and there is a limited, expensive breakfast menu at the hotel. There is wireless Internet access, and they offer the use of a bridge device if you don't have a wireless card, but it took two calls and almost 2 hours for them to bring it and then it didn't work, so we had to wait for the next morning to replace it. We received someone else's bill on the second day, and there was an erroneous charge on the final bill. The accounting system seems a bit sloppy, and the people at the front desk, while pleasant, don't seem to care very much.

name: The Fairmont Washington DC
title: “Impressive Service and Quality”
text: Went for a anniversary celebration and the frontdesk went way out of his way to ensure my expectations were met. The room was well appointed and the view grandiose. It was an enjoyable stay and my disapointment was returning to work the following Monday.

name: Hotel Commonwealth
title: “Wicked awesome at it's best!”
text: I have nothing negative to say about this hotel or my experience staying there. Rather, it exceeded my expectations. Staff were friendly and helpful. The room and bedding was devine. We will stay here again.

name: Country Inn & Suites By Carlson, Denver International Airport
title: “Good for families”
text:
We stayed here for two nights recently. This hotel simply has everything you could ask for. We were very impressed with our stay and will definitely be staying here again if ever in Denver.
you can find many restaurants nearby.

name: Hotel George, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Hooray for our neighborhood hotel!”
text: The Hotel George is located in the Capitol Hill neighborhood where we live. We have always appreciated having a top-notch hotel nearby as it's a convenient place for family to stay and we very much enjoy the hotel's restaurant, Bistro Bis. Yesterday we discovered how truly wonderful it is to have the Hotel George nearby. Our neighborhood suffered a major power outage during a heat wave. With temperatures indoors reaching the mid-80s we were eager to find a place to stay for the night. The Hotel George came to the rescue and offered rooms to neighborhood residents at a very steep discount. What fantastic customer service! Kudos to Kimpton.

name: Sofitel Washington DC
title: “Solidly satisfying”
text: My wife and I spent nine nights at the Sofitel Layfayette Square recently, enjoyed it, and would return. While the hotel didn't elicit a "wow" as it has for some, it deserves four stars if only for the staff's performance and the sleep-inducing mattress. Even more impressive than the staff's friendliness was their rare-for-any-hotel prompt reaction to a request. Another armchair? Done. Fix a poorly draining shower? Done. More hangers? Right away. Our "luxury king" room (812) was roomy and satisfyingly quiet. A better view would have been a plus, but those are in short supply in downtown hotels. Maybe on a higher floor? The shower was the water-saving type, so you have to give credit even while wishing they might have cheated just a little. The closet is cramped for two persons, and we're tight packers. But these are quibbles, and overall the Sofitel's location was perfect for us, their service and attitude were exceptional, and we give it a thumbs-up. Tip: If you don't like a duvet when you sleep -- remember, this is a very French hotel -- just ask for regular sheets. They'll be on your bed when you return.

name: Helix, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Chambre vieillissante, personnel désagréable”
text: Des l'arrivée les ennuis ont commencé : la chambre n'était pas prete, il a fallu attendre avec de nombreuses autres personnes... Arrivée dans la chambre très forte odeur d'urine dans la salle de bain, la gouvernante vient vérifier et nous change de chambre. Cette chambre, comme la précédente, était vraiment "en fin de vie", mobilier abimé, et taché, rideaux manquants Cet hôtel se veut au top, il le fut à l'ouverture, j'y avais passé deux nuits il y a 5 ans et tout était parfait. Aucun des personnels croisés dans les couloirs et ascenceurs de l'hotel n'a daigné répondre à nos bonjours... Par contre si vous venez avec un chien vous serez bien reçu : gamelle de croquette et eau dès l'entrée (mais pas pour le voyageur qui attend sa chambre), panier à chien dans la chambre (ce qui explique cette délicate odeur qui émane de la moquette). Ce n'est pas parce que le mobilier se veut design (bcp d'articles viennent d'IKEA) qu'il peut encore prétendre à être "classe". Un seul bon point : c'était mon anniversaire et j'ai eu un plateau de fruits et un bouteille de vin mousseux dans ma chambre, mais cela n'a pas effacé mon désapointement face à la mauvais qualité des prestations....

name: Hotel George, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “A gracious staff and a beautiful hotel in a convenient location.......”
text:
My room was comfortable and quiet, most welcome after a full day of sight-seeing with
energetic children. Hotel George has a sophisticated restaurant and bar for adults, and
the station is nearby with lots of kid food. Most of all, I liked the friendly staff led by
concierge Michael Love. They provided service, conversation and treats for the children.
My son, the children and I had three rooms. We felt so at home that it was hard to leave.
We walked to the National Gallery, the Newseum, the Building Museum while a quick
cab ride took us to the Washington and Lincoln Memorials, The International Spy Museum and the Museum of Air and Space. I liked Hotel George so much that I would
stay there again without consulting any other hotels!

name: Carlyle Suites Hotel
title: “Hidden art-deco gem in DC.”
text: I lived in this neighborhood for 10yrs and stayed at the Carlyle Suites on three occassions. It was consistently outstanding all three times. You feel like you're in South Beach. It's super clean; the staff is pleasant; the rooms are updated and modern with TempurPedic beds. It is also in the heart of the nightlife as it's between the trendy neighborhoods of Dupont Circle, Logan Circle, U Street, Adams Morgan and Downtown is also walkable. The Sunday brunch is great too. I also like the fact that their toilletries are green. On one stay, we had our two 100 dogs as we were between settleing homes. They were more than happy to let us keep our dogs. And to top it off, the price is usually cheaper than most of the sterile chains. I recommend this hotel to all my friends and family who visit DC.

name: The Hay-Adams
title: “Beautiful hotel, great restaurant”
text: Stayed for 3 nights, beautiful hotel, though the rooms are small. Exceptional service from arrival to departure, without exception. The bar on the lower level was always so crowded we never used it, but the restaurant is among the best in Washington: exceptional food, service, and atmosphere (for some reason it is closed for dinner on Staurdays).

name: The Liaison Capitol Hill, An Affinia Hotel
title: “Tolle Lage beim Capitol”
text: Das Liaison Capitol Hotel liegt nahe dem kleinen Park beim Capitol. das Frühstück ist gut und man hat 3 Wahlmöglichkeiten- alle drei sehr gut, nur bei einem längeren Aufenthalt könnte es langweilig werden. das Zimmer war groß und gut ausgestattet. das Bad hingegen war schon etwas klein. Auch zum Kongress kann man zu Fuß gehen, etwa in 10-15 min..Auf dem 10. Stock ist ein traumhaftes Pool mit guter Aussicht!!

name: Magnolia Hotel Denver
title: “Excellent location and very accommodating staff!”
text:
Our room was clean, comfortable but nothing fancy. It was somewhat small, but handled the needs for 2 adults in town for a wedding well. We are allergic to feathers so in advance we asked for hypoallergenic accommodations. To our delight, the room was made up and held for our arrival. This is quite rare in the hotel industry. 
Usually when we arrive at a hotel, even though we have asked for hypoallergic accommodations in advance, we will get a room where all they have done is take the feather pillows and duvet from a pre-made bed and replace them with synthetics. So when we arrive and explain that NO FEATHERS can EVER be in contact with the linens, the beds have to be stripped and remade. We feel embarrassed asking for perfectly nice bed(s) to be remade; this is a waste of resources and energy, and we can't unpack for at least an hour after we arrive. 
 Thank you, Magnolia, for taking good care of us!

name: The Hay-Adams
title: “Elegant First Class Old World Charm!”
text: My husband and I had the great fortune of staying at the Hay Adams during the cherry blossom festival in DC two years ago. The hotel brings you back to another era. I felt like we were staying in a bedroom in the Chateau of Versaille in Paris! It was absolutely magnificent. This hotel has a very rich feel about it. I will say that driving up in a normal car when every one else was driving a Porsche or luxury vehicle was a bit uncomfortable, but once inside it was wonderful. The crowd tends to be more senior so we did feel like we were the youngest people there, but it really did not bother us. I would love to go back. (May just leave the car at home)!

name: The Hay-Adams
title: “The standard for old-world service”
text: I stayed here recently on a business trip and was simply blown away by the outstanding service. The room was nicely updated without losing its charm. Food was expensive (no more than any other hotel, as an aside) in room service but quite good. Bed and pillows were outstanding and unlike many other hotesl I have stayed at on business--actually helped me sleep!

name: The Liaison Capitol Hill, An Affinia Hotel
title: “Tolle Lage, nur wenige Gehminuten zum Capitol. Sehr sehr in die Jahre gekommen (sehr veraltet).”
text:
Tolle Lage, da das Hotel nur sehr wenige Gehminuten zum Capitol entfernt liegt. Das sogenannte "Moderne" Hotel ist sehr in die Jahre gekommen. Total veraltet und nicht sauber. Im ersten Zimmer gab es Probleme mit der Klimaanlage. Sie war dermassen laut, dass ein Schlafen unmöglich war. Überhaupt kein erholsamer Schlaf war möglich. Mitten in der Nacht haben wir dann ein zweites Zimmer bezogen. Keine Besserung. Leider war ein drittes Zimmer nicht möglich zu beziehen, laut Manager. Zur Problemlösung hatte er uns dann Ohrstöpsel gereicht! Service war in Amerika üblich, total oberflächlich ok. Fazit: sehr veraltetes Hotel, zu laute Zimmer, unrein.
Die Rooftopbar ist schön, aber leider reicht dies nicht um so ein Hotel gut zu bewerten.

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Not up to the usual Kimpton service”
text: I love the Kimptons and was looking forward to staying here again. But something was amiss here. The rooms are great, I and love the location. I was there for three nights and throughout my stay, the staff seemed tired and overwhelmed. There was also a disconnect in the restaurant. I received a meal that was either different than what I ordered or completely different than what was on the menu three times.

name: Hotel George, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great hotel and great value!”
text:
Located near the Union Station/Metro and The Capital, we were extremely pleased we chose this gem of a hotel! The front desk was very friendly and helpful - even suggested dining options (other than their expensive in-house restaurant). 
By joining the 'Kimpton Club' online for free, we got free internet, $10 from the minibar and our checkout extended late. The room was small but tastefully decorated with excellent linens in the bath and on the bed. Pillows and bedding top notch also....
The surrounding area was a little sketchy but the nearby (more expensive) Hyatt is even closer to the local 'men's shelter' - we never had problems walking, even at night and used the local Metro, Circulator Bus, cabs and our feet!
Great value - we'd stay again in an instant!

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great hotel let down by the reception service.”
text:
My fiancé and I, stayed at the Palomar for 3 nights during the end of December. After a long coach trip from NYC and arriving in the evening we were extremely tired and just wanted to check into our hotel quickly and go to our room to rest.
Unfortunately we had misplaced our hotel voucher but thought that would be no problem as we would be on the central reservation system. This was not the case. When I was asked if I could retrieve this on my email, I asked politely if I could use their PC to do so. I was told yes there was a $5 charge to do so! Considering we were about to check in and were paying guests, we thought this was extremely rude. Luckily a manager said we could use the PC for free and found our reservation had been put under a misspelt name (their fault) for which no apology was offered. While we were looking for the confirmation, we were told that they had found our booking but it was for the wrong dates! Finally, after printing out our confirmation online we were able to check in and get our room key. 
Other than the view, the hotel room was great! Very spacious and comfortable! Perfect for either a vacation or work stay and the hotel has a brilliant location. The housekeeping and breakfast staff were great as well.
Unfortunately, after a nice stay, we were again let down by the reception staff upon checkout. Their unfriendly attitude and general coldness to guests left a bad impression with us.

name: Hotel Commonwealth
title: “An enjoyable gem”
text: We quite enjoyed staying at this hotel in Boston, the accomodations were large, clean and the staff, very helpful and friendly. It is one street away from Newport St, the main shopping area and right beside the T.

name: Magnolia Hotel Denver
title: “Great place for a Denver stopover”
text: Really good location in the centre of the city and very close to the 16th St shopping district. Clean, modern and stylish. Free happy hour drink on arrival is a nice touch. Very good breakfast. Quiet rooms.

name: Country Inn & Suites By Carlson, Denver International Airport
title: “First-rate accommodations”
text: Outstanding front-desk personnel; comfortable, spacious and clean room; excellent amenities. Well worth the $$.

name: Carlyle Suites Hotel
title: “Zwischen Baustelle und Müllabfuhr”
text:
Dieses Hotel befindet sich zur Zeit im Umbau, d.h. Eingangshalle ist eine Baustelle. Unser Zimmer hat die ganze Nacht wie eine Großküche gerochen. Man hatte das Gefühl, dass der Küchenabzug direkt in unser Zimmer geleitet wurde. :-(
Morgens um 7 Uhr wurden wir von der Baustelle nebenan geweckt. 
Dieses Hotel ist schlecht und teuer!!!!!!!

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Beautiful hotel, AWESOME staff!!!”
text:
I originally booked my room through travelocity, looking for a hotel in DuPont Circle with at least a 4 star rating. The Palomar was booked for me at random, so I looked it up online. I read a few reviews, and somehow got the impression that it was mainly a chick hotel, (A lot of "girls night out" stories on here *cringe*), and my IMMEDIATE visual impression were the hot pink cylinder pillows on the bed. Not such a big deal, but there it is. Either way, I found out that I had to stay earlier and leave later and decided to call the hotel directly. Clayton was very helpful with modifying my booking and was kind enough to match the rate that Travelocity quoted to me. 
I checked in Saturday night and Diedra was my guest service agent/night auditor. She made sure that I felt welcomed, while being HILARIOUS! It was my first stay there and Diedra gave me the best REAL first impression and it helped set the tone for the rest of my stay. Lizann was also great about following up and maintaining a consistent level of service.
I didn't get to go out very much because of a heavy workload so housekeeping didn't get a chance to clean up; Not their fault that I'm a hermit, so I just wanted towels refreshed. I called down and spoke to Lizann again, who went the extra mile. Not only did she have the towels replaced but as much of my room amenities as possible, from glasses to minibar to sundry items, all in a timely fashion. ALL the staff were friendly!
I used to work in the hotel industry for a few years in numerous capacities including reservations, guest services, and even night auditor, so I go out of my way not to be a bother. It was nice that despite me not asking for much they anticipated what I COULD need and offered it. The complimentary amenities that came with my stay are great, but it's the people that truly make the experience.
I wish the Palomar staff a Happy New Year, and look forward to seeing them again soon!

name: Hotel Commonwealth
title: “One of the Best Hotels in Boston”
text: I stayed at Hotel Commonwealth for a few days leading up to the Memorial Day weekend in 2011. Prior to our arrival a reservation agent, Emily Cormier, was kind enough to e-mail a map of the subway system for our convenience. Upon our arrival, we had an excellent experience with the hotel staff. We arrived around 11pm and were promptly greeted and offered bottled water. We stayed in a deluxe queen room with a Fenway Park view. The room was clean and very spacious. There was free high speed internet which definitely was a bonus. The bathroom was well apportioned. The location of the hotel is ideal. You're within walking distance of Fenway Park, Prudential Center, and other sites. Plus, Kenmore station is adjacent to the hotel which is very convenient for traveling throughout Boston. The hotel restaurants were fabulous. The Eastern Standard's breakfast is a good option. Also, you want to have at least one meal at the Island Creek Oyster Bar. The service there was first rate. Hotel Commonwealth is a great option if you are visiting Boston.

name: Country Inn & Suites By Carlson, Denver International Airport
title: “Outstanding Guest Service”
text: Our stay at this hotel was a real treat! Every single staff member was courteous and went out of their way to make us feel welcome. Mon - Thurs the management team held a reception where they offered complimentary beverages (adult ones too!) and appetizers. The ambience and generosity was outstanding. Not evry often in my travels do I find a location where guests are spending time on the front porch of the hotel in rocking chairs and enjoying each others' company. This was a great experience for all of my team

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great Rooms, great location, but service can improve”
text:
I generally think that Kimpton Group offers a much better and more interesting experience than the rest of the big chains like Hilton, Mariott, Hyatt, Westin, etc....at a better or comparable price. The decor is usually quirkier, bordering on boutique, and there are nice unique touches if you take the trouble to sign up as a Kimpton Club member...worth doing and no extra cost . 
The Palomar DC is probably the weakest of all my experiences so far ( I have stayed in Kimpton Hotels in San Francisco twice, in Chicago, and in New York all of which I loved), mostly because the service was so-so. I had 3 nights there recently- two in October and one in November. The rooms were great ( tiny things didn't work during my October stay, like the Hair Dryer) and check-in and check-out was efficient though ordinary, but it was the service at their Urbana Restaurant that let the brand down....on both visits. It was simply underwhelming and perfunctory. Seems the hotel attracts a bit of a yuppie set who likes to drink and then get rowdy to the point of oblivion on how it impacts other guests. This results in other guests not getting much attention, waiting excessively long for a simple order. During October, the room adjacent to mine was occupied by what seemed to be a hen's party with 20 people in the room and very loud partying way past midnight ( I finally complained to reception at 1 am and whilst security gave the girls the message to zip it up seeing there had already been earlier complaints, it had no impact and the hotel had seemingly no desire to act nor could they offer me an alternate room)

name: Hotel George, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Great location, hotel with a difference”
text:
This hotel is very well located and within easy walking distance of Union station with its various restaurants and cafes. The Capital. and several museums are also near by and the tour buses all leave from the station, so a perfect location for sightseeing stays. If you are sick of the same old faceless Hotel this place, although not outstanding, offers spacious clean rooms decorated with a twist as well as friendly front desk staff. The bar and restaurant were over priced as to be expected in Hotels but offered a pleasant place to relax and unwind for the price tag. We all enjoyed our stay.
Do not use the Hotel car Park, park right across the street for half the price!

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “not what I was hoping for”
text:
I have stayed at many Kimpton hotels on the west coast and Chicago so I was really looking forward to my stay in Washington DC but was very disappointed. The reason I like the Kimptons is the boutique feeling and the quality of the rooms. When we arrived Sunday afternoon the lobby was crazy busy I was wondering if there had been a convention it was so busy. I noticed a lot of guests with dogs, some guests actually had 2 dogs. I was not aware this hotel allowed dogs. The room was very cookie cutter nothing special at all and in fact there was very bad water pressure in the bathroom and when we mentioned it to the front desk they told us that many guests have complained about that - so why hasn't it been addressed??? Another nice touch at Kimpton Hotels is wine tasting in the evening but the problem at this hotel is that is so crowded there was no where to sit and enjoy a glass of wine unless you wanted to stand in the area where check in /check out was, not very relaxing.
I did find the staff to be very friendly and nice. The location to Dupont Circle is great. Just not the standard I am used to from Kimpton.

name: Country Inn & Suites By Carlson, Denver International Airport
title: “Wonderful place to stay arriving by plane or car”
text: The hotel staff in the evening were very helpful, cheery and were team leaders as they helped one another; besides being helpful to us. The rooms were clean, spotless, and roomy. Bed was adequate due to the quality of the room furnishings, we expected more. However, we slept very well. The continental breakfast goes beyond being adequate. It was delicious and the help was always there to clean tables and see that supplies were available. You were not hungry when you left the breakfast area. The lobby is clean and very friendly looking. Over all our experience here was fantastic. I would highly recommend it to everyone. The price was a bit on the high middle range; but we were not disappointed by the price as our stay was well worth the price. They have elevators to reach the top floors so that is very helpful to any handicap person not able to do stairs.

name: Sofitel Washington DC
title: “Roomy”
text:
I cannot say enough about the space in the standard guestrooms. The bedroom is separated from the bathroom with an entryway and closet. The bathroom has a European-style tub and separate shower and plenty of room. The bedroom is spacy and comfortable, but the position of the tv is strange, making it difficult to stay in bed and watch. 
The Sofitel has a self-service business center just off the lobby that was fully stocked with updated computers and printers. This would meet needs for most any business situation, although it is somewhat cramped. There are only 3 workstations, so it could easily become overwhelmed during a convention.
It is hard to do breakfast for under $25, and the options are more suited for European travelers. Rice and tomatoes would not be my first choice, but they turned out halfway decent for breakfast. 
Overall, a pleasant stay with much more good than bad.

name: Hotel Commonwealth
title: “Very worthy of your Business”
text: The front door staff was awesome. The front desk staff was efficient. The rooms are really nice and the bathrooms very spacious. The water pressure in the shower was the best I have experienced in Boston. My only complaint is that they do not have an On Demand video system. Rather you have to call the Concierage and order off a list of available DVD's. We chose 7 DVD's we were interested in and turned out that none were available. Not a smart system for an otherwise top notch hotel.

name: Sofitel Washington DC
title: “There is a reason this is Number One”
text: I only get to D.C. a couple of times a year. I go on holiday weekends when hotel room offers are at their lowest, which is why I can afford to stay at the Sofitel, which is consistently rated No.1. It is a pricey hotel, but offers excellent values when Congress is not in session and the town is quiet. The front desk staff manages to remember me when I return, after months, and thousands of visitors in between, I get a big welcoming smile ... and they have actually read, and respond to, the requests I have made about accommodations. I like a quiet room, far from elevators ... and they bend over backwards to see that I get one each time. For a solo, older, woman traveler, this bit of friendliness & consideration is Gold. Would that all hotels could remember that personal service results in good business. And even old ladies spend real money. I was especially looked after by Evette, and wish to extend thanks. She really does the most professional job at a front desk I have ever encountered; and I travel a lot. Everyone was helpful and friendly as well. My only complaint about this hotel, and it is a consistent one ... is a wish for better light to read by in bed. This time I noticed the bulb in the light over the bed was much brighter than in the past, so someone is listening ... but it was strangely only turned on and off from outside the room. Go figure. All is as well at the Sofitel as one can expect in a good hotel. Actually, better.

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “I said we'd be back and we were and I'll say it again...wonderful”
text: This hotel just goes above and beyond. This was our second stay. This time we had our two dogs with us and it was such a pleasure to be able to stay in such a beautiful room with lots of space for my family of 4 and 2 dogs. The beds are comfortable and the perks of being a kimpton member are so nice. The staff is professional and friendly from house keeping, to valet, to front desk to the restaurant staff. I also am very impressed by the attention to detail the staff pays and accountablilty to comments (not that I have ever had a negative one). Just a pleasure, on the pricey side but they back up and make sure you get your money's worth. Will absolutely stay again and again.

name: Hotel Commonwealth
title: “Awesome staff that aims to please!”
text: We stayed at the Hotel Commonwealth as our son was going to a summer study program in Boston. Wow, everything about this hotel was top-notch, from the service, cleanliness of rooms and the amazing view of Fenway Park. They really go out of their way to make sure your stay in Boston is a memorable experience. We'd highly recommend this hotel!

name: Hotel Commonwealth
title: “Fantastic Stay!”
text: Sad to say, we are flying back from Boston as I type this review. Our stay at Hotel Commonwealth was exemplary. As others have stated, the staff is all very attentive. We had a "junior suite". Aside from a shower that had the force of a fire hose (seriously) the room was amazing! Super quiet and comfortable, especially the bed which I never wanted to get out of. Also worth noting: the drinks next door at the Eastern Standard are amazing and the hotel is very convenient to the Kenmore T-Stop (Green Line) and Fenway Park.

name: Sofitel Washington DC
title: “A perfect stay......”
text: From start to finish, our stay was perfect. It actually began earlier by asking and being granted early check in. This allowed us to settle in and then out to see the city. We stopped at Le Bar for a drink after checking in, chatted with the congenial bartender and staff - about 10 min later we are surprised with a special anniversary dessert! (the reason for our stay) The room and each staff member we spoke with made our stay very special. We will surely visit the Sofitel again!

name: Sofitel Washington DC
title: “probably the best hotel in dc”
text:
I can agree with the other visitors below that everything in this hotel is just great : room, bed, bathroom, personnel, food in bar and breakfast at Ici (OK, it's expensive, but it has superb quality has a fantastic atmosphere, and the most friendly and helpful waiters... plus in the area i didn't see decent breakfast alternatives). Location is also good, though the area is a bit sterile.
One flaw: during our first night construction work started on the opposite building around 2 am. the noise was unsupportable. the reception desk agent was not able to give us another room as the system was out. next day they apologized that they were not aware of these works, if not they would have given us another room when checking in. also received e-mailed apologies from general manager. "chapeau" for this.
bottom-line: can't wait to be back in washington and to stay at the sofitel.

name: Hotel Commonwealth
title: “First rate service”
text:
First of all the location of the Hotel couldn't have been more perfect as we had tickets to Fenway Park to see a game on Sunday. Not only was the proximity so close to Fenway Park but, the hotel staff assisted us in choosing seats and helped us buy tickets to the game before we even arrived at the Hotel and had them at the Hotel for pick-up.
On our late arrival, we were surprised by having our room upgraded to your brand new suite. The suite was beautifully decorated and was equipped with a gas fireplace and a flat screen televsion. The cleanliness was par non and the attention to details from the cookies in our room to the gorgeously folded washroom towels and washcloths were nice touches.
Our rest that evening was wonderful. The bed and the bedding in the bedroom were so comfortable.
In the morning, I called the front desk to purchase 2 hotel robes and I was surprised at how quickly the matter was handled and the robes were delivered to my room. The Manager was kind enough to give me two complimentary umbrella's as I had also asked to purchase two umbrella's.
My family was celebrating my husband's 53rd Birthday and the Commonwealth Hotel and staff made it a Birthday to remember. 
We will highly recommend this Hotel to others and would definitely consider staying again. 
Thank you,
Tina Manousos

name: Hotel Commonwealth
title: “Hakuna Matata!”
text:
From the moment I stepped into this hotel I knew I made the right choice. The entire staff was always ready to meet my request and with a smile that was genuine! The hotel far exceeded my expectations. I travel to Boston quite often and I have never stayed here before but decided to give it a try. Josh handled my reservation. Of course I had my list of what I wanted the room to be like. It was exactly how I wanted it and then some. Right down to a bottle of NY water! Nice touch Josh! (knowing I was from NY) It just made me smile. At that moment, I knew my stay was just going to be fabulous and it was just that. 
They even had an umbrella in the closet so I wasn't caught off guard with a downpour!
The Hotel Commonwealth is definitely worth the price if you want no worries.

name: Magnolia Hotel Denver
title: “Go Rockies. A wonderful place to stay in downtown Denver.”
text: From the moment we drove into the entryway staff was there to assist. They were friendly and helpful. The complimentary breakfast buffet was very good. The room was spotless, but the bed was bouncy and the room temperature could not be adjusted to be cool enough for a good sleep. A great value.

name: Magnolia Hotel Denver
title: “Best of the West”
text:
Magnolia was the best hotel we stayed in during our trip out West.
The staff could not have been nicer, from the reception to the valets.
Great complimentary breakfast, cookies at night and managers reception in the evening.
Beds were deliciously comfy. Bathrooms were spotless with great toiletries.

name: Hotel Commonwealth
title: “Exceeded our expectations!”
text: While visiting our daughter at college, we decided to splurge at the Hotel Commonwealth. From the second the door was opened to us until we left the next day, every detail exceeded our expectations for an absolutely beautiful stay. We ate both lunch AND dinner at Eastern Standard and now have a new favorite in Boston!

name: Hotel Commonwealth
title: “A great hotel with a surprisingly large room”
text:
I had a very short stay at Hotel Commonwealth, just one night, but will definitely return on my next trip to Boston. The room was large with a desk and sitting area. Also a large bathroom with separated toilet room within the bathroom. Check-in and check-out was quick and easy, staff was friendly and accommodating and the room was very clean and comfortable. I loved the crisp white linens on the bed and the mattress was superb. The room was very quiet given that it faced a busy street. I enjoyed an excellent meal at the adjoining restaurant, Eastern Standard. 
After my one night here, I went to Cape Cod. When I returned to Boston I stayed at another hotel and the room there was tiny and dark, so I appreciated the size of the room at Hotel Commonwealth and wished I had booked the remainder of my stay here.

name: Magnolia Hotel Denver
title: “Good amenities and centrally located.”
text: The breakfasts and night-time cookies were great. The only thing missing is airline miles.

name: Magnolia Hotel Denver
title: “Truly a wonderful experience.”
text: We sure did enjoy our stay at the Magnolia. We were only there for one night and we wish that we had been able to stay for another one. The staff was very nice and extremely helpful. Our room was plenty big, and we loved the living area with the kitchen and fireplace, it was worth the upgrade. The complimentary beverages in the evening and the cookies at night were a great touch. Everything was really wonderful from the time we walked through the doors (which were always opened for us by staff) and we will definitely stay there again next time we're in the Denver area.

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Our FAVORITE DC hotel in every single way”
text:
Hotel Palomar, right off of Dupont Circle, in DC is our FAVORITE hotel. I'll start by saying that Palomar is a Kimpton Hotel and we've had great experiences with all Kimpton hotels that we've stayed at (including nearby Hotel Palomar in Arlington which is also amazing). Each time that we've visited has been worth RAVING about and while we have tried other DC hotels that were very nice, none compared to Palomar.
LOCATION:
Dupont Circle is THE place to be in DC. We have stayed in other DC neighborhoods but ended up coming back to Dupont Circle because everything that we like to do is either a short walk , metro ride or drive away. Georgetown shopping is a 5-10 minute drive west on P street, the National Zoo, Adams Morgan and Embassy Row are a quick ride up Connecticut Ave, and Capitol Hill, The White House, and all of the monuments and museums at the National Mall are also a short drive away. All are also very easily accessible via Metro. Dupont Circle is a beautiful, clean neighborhood - very romantic to walk around at night and FULL of amazing places to eat.
Now onto Hotel Palomar - 
As soon as you walk into the very chic lobby you get a feel of luxury but not in a stuffy or impersonal sense. Gorgeous marble is everywhere, a warm fireplace with cozy seating invites you to stay and enjoy a glass of wine or lemonade and all of the hotel staff are very helpful and welcoming. Front desk staff are always helpful and personable - making check-in and -out a quick and pleasant process and making sure that you have everything you need. They always ask about the reason for your visit and go as far as to suggest activities appropriate to the reason for your stay. 
While you can tell that the hotel is in an older renovated building, it has all of the charm and character of historical DC with all of the chic decor and amenities that you would expect of a new build. The ENTIRE hotel is always impeccably clean. The rooms are very comfortable and you have everything you would ever want - multiple pillows custom fit to your preferences, plush robes, complimentary umbrella to use during your stay, spacious closest, plush carpet, luxurious bed linens wrapped around the MOST comfortable hotel mattresses that I've ever slept in, flat-panel TV, spacious work/desk space, beautiful bathrooms with spacious vanities and luxury bath products and the list goes on and on. Even staying in their basic room offers a luxurious, spacious and relaxing environment.
The fitness center is small but sufficient for a quick morning workout and complete with complimentary granny smith apples and headphones if you forget to pack yours. While I didn't get to go to the pool, it looks beautiful and lots of people were outside in the 100 degree weather enjoying the lounge chairs and covered bed-style cabanas. 
In my opinion, the nightly rate may be on the higher-end compared with other DC hotels in the same class, you get soooo much for your money. All of the small touches set Palomar apart from other hotels in the city and make Kimpton hotels our favorites. Complimentary refreshments are served throughout the day in the lobby ranging from morning coffee and tea to the afternoon wine hour. Hotel staff makes sure that they cater to the individual and make sure that your stay is very special and comfortable - we informed the person making our reservation that we were going to be in town to celebrate our anniversary and we were greeted at check-in with wishes of a happy anniversary and there were rose petals on the bed when we walked into the room. bedding and pillows can always be adjusted to fit your preferences and if you forget to pack anything, hotel staff always does their best to make sure you have when you need. 
Palomar is also eco- and pet-friendly.
Lastly I just want to commend Kimpton for building and managing amazing hotels. White Palomar is our favorite, we have had similar experiences at other Kimpton Hotels. Do yourself a favor a become a Kimpton inTouch member for extra perks (like free wireless internet access and complimentary mini-bar items) at all of their hotels across the country.

name: Magnolia Hotel Denver
title: “Great amenities if you have time to use them.”
text: As with any downtown hotel, getting there is half the challenge. Location is great, near everything. Check-in was smooth, the room was spacious and clean. We were a little concerned that our room was right next to the elevator, but we never heard it! If you have time, you must take advantaqge of all the "freebies". There is a beer and wine reception, cookies and milk, and a breakfast buffet. I would definitely stay there again!

name: Magnolia Hotel Denver
title: “Best Hotel in Denver! Awesome Staff, Great Rooms, CLEAN!”
text: Denver's Best Cozy Hot Spot! Great Location. Rooms are Clean, Trendy and Roomy. Staff is Awesome, very attentive :)

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Excellent stay at the Hotel Palomar in Washington, D.C.”
text: We arrived after a long drive to find that our reservation had been cancelled for some reason, luckily I had my confirmation number with me, but they had a room for us and were very apologetic and gracious about it. The room was huge and very nicely furnished, it was contemporary in style and very attractive. We liked the amenities, the emphasis on art in the common areas and the rooms, we had dinner in their restaurant which was excellent. All of the staff were pleasant and accommodating. I would stay here again in a heartbeat!

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Best Hotel Visit in DC”
text: I've stayed in dozens of hotels in the DC-area, and enjoyed the Palomar the most. It's a gorgeous building in a great location -- the atmosphere is open, relaxed, and elegant. When we checked in, the concierge was very kind -- and even upgraded us to an executive room (even though we'd booked on hotwire and were technically speaking low on the tourist totem pole). He also gave us chits for a complimentary glass of house wine in the lovely hotel bar, since we'd missed the afternoon wine service. The room itself was big enough to do cartwheels in, very nicely furnished and spotless, with a nice view of P street. (And finally -- a hotel with TWO bathrobes in the closet!) Morning coffee was delicious (served in the lobby and with a free copy of the Financial Times). Everything you could want in a hotel -- nothing more, nothing less.

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Overpriced with noisy rooms”
text: The Hotel Palomar is a sufficiently nice, luxurious hotel. Well-equipped rooms, good staff, great location. The only problem is the out-of-line price and the incredibly noisy rooms. I stayed up half the night because I could hear every coming and going in the hallway, not to mention the overactive maid staff starting their work early in the morning. It's not the best experience to only sleep half the night and then wake up and find a bill for $399 for a single night.

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Così così”
text: A fine settembre, con mio marito, abbiamo pernottato per due notti in questo Hotel, l'unico dei 4 dove abbiamo soggiornato negli Stati Uniti, con moquette. Entrando in camera si sentiva uno strano odore. Avevamo la prima colazione compresa nel prezzo, assolutamente immangiabile, c'era un grande tavolo in una sala semi buia con pane e brioche, purtroppo c'erano grandi contenitori di marmellata e burro da dove tutti attingevano con un cucchiaio e dove ci parlavano sopra. Sconsiglio di avere la colazione compresa, meglio pagarla extra e farsi portare qualcosa dalla cucina

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Top-Hotel in Washington”
text: Ausgezeichnete Lage in der Nähe der Metrostation Dupont Circle (red line, Direktverbindung zur Union Station) und Busstationen (z.B. nach Georgetown). Sehr gutes in-house Restaurant. Zimmer sehr gross (auch für eine Einzelnutzung), sauber und hell. Freundliches Personal. Gratis Kaffee und Tee in der Lobby. Sehr gutes Preis/Leistungs-Verhältnis.

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “Superhotel Superlage”
text:
Anlässlich einer Geschäftsreise waren wir das 2. Mal im Hotel Palomar in Washington.
Die Zimmer sind sehr großzügig, sehr sauber und besonders Geschmackvoll eingerichtet.
Besonders schätzten wir die tägliche open wine bar in der Lobby, die sich ausgezeichnet eignet um auch mit anderen Gästen des Hauses ins Gespräch zu kommen. Dem Hotel angegliedert ist ein sehr gutes und nettes Restaurant und eine sensationelle Bar die abends von einem jungen internationalen Publikum aus der Umgebung besucht wird. Hier kommt die Nähe zum Dupont Circle und den vielen Botschaften voll zum Tragen. Wenn wir wieder mal in Washington sind, werden wir auf alle Fälle wieder im Palomar sein!

name: Palomar Washington DC, a Kimpton Hotel
title: “excellent”
text:
un excellent hotel 4 *, pour un prix raisonnable. un valet pour la voiture qui va la parquer .déjeuner au choix en supplément, carte variée.
le soir, bar musical,dans lequel on peut grignoter des petits plats qui ne sont heureusement pas des hamburgers.
avec en face, un excellent resto, avec de la cuisine internationale de bon niveau.
Une chambre moderne luxueuse en parfait état, bien insonirisée (à l'arrière en tout cas)et moins chère que les hotels concurrents.
A quelques minutes de la maison blanche.
